title: [Aiter][ROCm] RMSNormGated+GroupedQuantFP8 fusion
author: tpopp
body:
This PR adds a compilation fusion pass (AiterRMSNormGatedFp8GroupQuantPattern) that fuses the decomposed RMSNormGated + reshape + group FP8 quantization sequence into a single AITER Triton kernel call (fused_rms_gated_fp8_group_quant). This pattern appears in GatedDeltaNetAttention layers (e.g., Qwen3-Next) where each attention head's output goes through gated RMS normalization, is reshaped back to the full hidden dimension, and then group-quantized to FP8 before the output projection linear layer.

Results:
a 9us set of 2 kernels can be combined to 4.5us. In the case of Qwen3Next, this can be a 1-3% improvement depending on how small the workload is (concurrency 1 vs 128).

  Motivation

  In models using GatedDeltaNetAttention (such as Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8), the output path of each attention block performs:
  1. RMSNormGated on per-head tensors (N*H, D) with a gating tensor
  2. Reshape to (N, H*D)
  3. Group FP8 quantization with GroupShape(1, 128)

  These three operations decompose into many elementwise and reduction kernels when torch.compile lowers them. By matching this pattern in the FX graph and replacing it with a single fused Triton kernel from AITER, we eliminate multiple GPU kernel launches and intermediate memory traffic.


  Changes
• Register rocm_aiter_fused_rms_gated_fp8_group_quant custom op wrapping aiter.ops.triton.quant.fused_rms_gated_fp8_group_quant
  • Add rocm_aiter_ops.are_gdn_triton_kernels_available() — checks whether the required AITER Triton kernels (causal_conv1d_update_single_token, gated_delta_net) are importable, allowing graceful fallback on older AITER builds that lack the GDN kernels
  • rocm_aiter_fusion.py: Add AiterRMSNormGatedFp8GroupQuantPattern that matches the decomposed norm→reshape→quant graph and replaces it with the fused op. Add _fold_consecutive_reshapes pre-processing pass (needed because make_fx faithfully
    records chained reshapes that must be folded for the pattern to match). Dynamically infer num_heads/head_dim from GatedDeltaNetAttention layers via static_forward_context. Gate the pattern on are_gdn_triton_kernels_available()
  • matcher_utils.py: Add MatcherRMSNormGated pattern tracer that traces RMSNormGated.forward_static for use in pm.register_replacement. Extend MatcherQuantFP8 to support Triton-based quant op matching
  • layernorm.py: Extract RMSNormGated.forward_static as a @staticmethod so both forward_native and the matcher can share the same pure-PyTorch implementation. forward_native delegates to it
  • test_fusion.py: Add unit tests (TestGatedModel) for the fusion pattern covering positive match cases (aiter quant, non-aiter quant, per-token dynamic) and negative cases (wrong group shape, per-tensor quant)


  AITER Dependency

  The fused Triton kernel (fused_rms_gated_fp8_group_quant) is provided by ROCm/aiter#2423 (​https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2423​) ("[Triton] optimized decode kernels for Qwen3-Next model"). The fusion pass is gated behind  rocm_aiter_ops.are_gdn_triton_kernels_available(), so it is a no-op on AITER versions that do not include this PR.


  Benchmark Results

  Setup:
  • Model: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8, TP=1
  • GPU: AMD MI355x (gfx950), single GPU
  • Base image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly (vLLM v0.19.2rc1) with AITER rebuilt from aiter:main + PR #2423
  • Attention backend: ROCM_AITER_FA
  • Compilation: cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, custom_ops=["-rms_norm", "-silu_and_mul", "+quant_fp8"], pass_config={"fuse_norm_quant": true}
  • Benchmark command: vllm bench serve --dataset_name random --random_input_len 1024 --random_output_len 1024 --max_concurrency 4 --num_prompts 32 --num_warmups 4 --seed 1 --temperature 0 --ignore_eos

  Pattern matching verification:
  • With fusion: RocmAiterRMSNormQuantFusionPass replaced 5 patterns (1+2+2 across repeated-layer subgraphs — the 4 additional matches are from AiterRMSNormGatedFp8GroupQuantPattern)
  • Without fusion (pattern commented out): replaced 1 pattern (only the existing non-gated AiterRMSNormDynamicQuantPattern)

  Throughput (ISL=1024, OSL=1024, concurrency=4):

  ┌─────────────────────────────────┬─────────────┬──────────┬───────┐
  │ Metric                          │ With Fusion │ Baseline │ Delta │
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────┼──────────┼───────┤
  │ Output token throughput (tok/s) │ 467.05      │ 456.52   │ +2.3% │
  │ Total token throughput (tok/s)  │ 934.11      │ 913.04   │ +2.3% │
  │ Mean TPOT (ms)                  │ 8.44        │ 8.66     │ −2.5% │
  │ P99 TPOT (ms)                   │ 8.67        │ 8.98     │ −3.5% │
  │ Mean E2EL (ms)                  │ 8,769       │ 8,971    │ −2.3% │
  └─────────────────────────────────┴─────────────┴──────────┴───────┘

  Accuracy (lm_eval, gsm8k, 5-shot):

  ┌──────────────────┬────────────────┬────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┐
  │ Filter           │ With Fusion    │ Baseline       │ Delta                       │
  ├──────────────────┼────────────────┼────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
  │ flexible-extract │ 0.8605 ±0.0095 │ 0.8506 ±0.0098 │ +0.0099 (within error bars) │
  │ strict-match     │ 0.8089 ±0.0108 │ 0.8097 ±0.0108 │ −0.0008 (within error bars) │
  └──────────────────┴────────────────┴────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘

  Accuracy is statistically identical — the fusion is numerically safe.


  Test plan

  • [x] Unit tests: pytest tests/compile/passes/test_fusion.py -k "gated" — positive and negative pattern match cases
  • [x] lm_eval --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 — accuracy unchanged vs. baseline
  • [x] vllm bench serve — throughput improved ~2.3%, TPOT improved ~2.5%
  • [x] Verified graceful no-op when AITER lacks GDN kernels (are_gdn_triton_kernels_available() == False)

title: [Aiter][ROCm] gdn_linear_attn kernel fusion
author: tpopp
body:
Overview:
This change merges various triton compiled kernels into single kernels. For all backends, triton kernels are merged into one. For AITER, the triton kernels are further merged into optimized kernels for AMD.

Fusions remove 20-26us in launch overhead per layer (36 GDN layers and 12 attention layers per decode step) which corresponds to 5-8% improvements in TPOT and throughput depending on workload size and input/output size rations.

 Summary

  This PR integrates AITER's optimized Triton kernels into the GatedDeltaNetAttention decode path and restructures the forward pass to reduce overhead. When running on ROCm with AITER enabled, decode-only batches use fused Triton kernels for the
  convolution update, gating + delta rule update, and QKV rearrangement, replacing multiple individual PyTorch operations with fewer, more efficient kernel launches. The prefill and speculative-decode paths are factored out of the decode-only hot
  path to keep the CUDA-graphed decode region lean.


  Changes

  • Import and gate AITER Triton kernels at module level (gdn_linear_attn.py): Import causal_conv1d_update_single_token, fused_reshape_causal_conv1d_update_single_token, and fused_rearrange_sigmoid_gated_delta_rule from AITER behind a
    GDN_AITER_TRITON_AVAILABLE flag that checks rocm_aiter_ops.are_gdn_triton_kernels_available(). This avoids per-call import overhead and gracefully falls back on systems without these kernels.


  • Add _forward_core_decode_fast (gdn_linear_attn.py): A new decode fast-path method that uses the AITER Triton kernels for:
    • Fused reshape + causal conv1d single-token update (replacing separate reshape, conv1d, and state update operations)
    • Fused rearrange + sigmoid gating + delta rule state update (replacing separate sigmoid, gating, rearrangement, and recurrence operations)


  • Restructure forward (gdn_linear_attn.py): When AITER fast-path kernels are available, the forward method packs QKV and Z together, passes them through a prepare_gdn_attention_core_inputs compiled helper for prefill, and routes decode-only
    batches to the new _forward_core_decode_fast. The prefill and speculative-decode logic is factored out of the decode-only branch to minimize the CUDA-graphed region.


  • Pass core_attn_out into chunk kernels (chunk.py, chunk_o.py): Thread an optional core_attn_out tensor through the chunked GDN kernel pipeline so that prefill output can be written directly into the pre-allocated output buffer, eliminating a
    separate copy.


  • Add are_gdn_triton_kernels_available() (_aiter_ops.py): Centralized check for the optional AITER Triton kernels (conv1d single-token, gated delta net). Returns False on older AITER builds that lack these modules.


  AITER Dependency

  The AITER Triton kernels used in this PR are provided by ROCm/aiter#2423 (​https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2423​) ("[Triton] optimized decode kernels for Qwen3-Next model"). The fast-path is gated behind
  rocm_aiter_ops.are_gdn_triton_kernels_available(), so it is a no-op on AITER versions that do not include this PR — the existing decode path is used as-is.


  Benchmark Results

  Setup:
  • Model: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8, TP=1
  • GPU: AMD MI355x (gfx950), single GPU
  • Base image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly (vLLM v0.19.2rc1) with AITER rebuilt from aiter:main + ROCm/aiter#2423 (​https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2423​)
  • Attention backend: ROCM_AITER_FA
  • Compilation: cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, custom_ops=["-rms_norm", "-silu_and_mul", "+quant_fp8"], pass_config={"fuse_norm_quant": true}
  • Benchmark: vllm bench serve --dataset_name random --random_input_len 1024 --random_output_len 1024 --max_concurrency 4 --num_prompts 32 --num_warmups 4 --seed 1 --temperature 0 --ignore_eos
  • Accuracy: lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 against the running server
  • Baseline: same image and configuration without this PR applied

  Throughput (ISL=1024, OSL=1024, concurrency=4):

  ┌─────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │ Metric                          │ Baseline │ With PR │ Delta │
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ Output token throughput (tok/s) │ 456.52   │ 482.55  │ +5.7% │
  │ Total token throughput (tok/s)  │ 913.04   │ 965.09  │ +5.7% │
  │ Mean TPOT (ms)                  │ 8.66     │ 8.15    │ −5.9% │
  │ P99 TPOT (ms)                   │ 8.98     │ 8.28    │ −7.8% │
  │ Mean E2EL (ms)                  │ 8,971    │ 8,488   │ −5.4% │
  └─────────────────────────────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────┘

  Accuracy (lm_eval, gsm8k, 5-shot):

  ┌──────────────────┬────────────────┬────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┐
  │ Filter           │ Baseline       │ With PR        │ Delta                       │
  ├──────────────────┼────────────────┼────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
  │ flexible-extract │ 0.8506 ±0.0098 │ 0.8605 ±0.0095 │ +0.0099 (within error bars) │
  │ strict-match     │ 0.8097 ±0.0108 │ 0.8203 ±0.0106 │ +0.0106 (within error bars) │
  └──────────────────┴────────────────┴────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘

  Accuracy is statistically identical — all deltas are within the standard error bounds.


  Test plan

  • [x] vllm bench serve — 5.7% output throughput improvement, 5.9% TPOT reduction
  • [x] lm_eval --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 — accuracy unchanged vs. baseline (within stderr)
  • [x] Server starts and serves requests correctly with ROCM_AITER_FA attention backend
  • [x] Verified graceful fallback when AITER lacks GDN kernels (GDN_AITER_TRITON_AVAILABLE == False)
  • [x] torch.profiler trace generated and inspected for correct kernel dispatch

title: [GDN] Enable FI Blackwell GDN prefill kernel
author: arpera
body:
~## IMPORTANT!!!~
~This PR MUST be merged after this change https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3155 is merged in Flashinfer and vLLM starts to use this FI version. There is a bug in GDN implementation in FI.~

## Purpose

Enable FlashInfer's new Blackwell (SM100) CuTe-DSL GDN prefill kernel ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3001](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3001)) by default in vLLM.
The same PR [Add FlashInfer prefill support for SM100+](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22921) in sqlang just in case.

On Blackwell the dispatcher in `ChunkGatedDeltaRule.__init__` now routes GDN prefill to FlashInfer when all of the following hold (logged once at init):

* `requested in ["flashinfer", "auto"]`;
* `platform == cuda`;
* one of:
  * Hopper (SM90) — no further constraints (pre-existing path, unchanged);
  * Blackwell (SM10.x) with `head_k_dim == 128`, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13` installed, `cuda_runtime >= 13`.

Otherwise we stay on the Triton/FLA path.

## Test Result

Hardware: 8xB200

### Functional

**e2e gsm8k**:

```
# Server
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
    --port 8000 -tp 1 -pp 1 -dp 8 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --language-model-only \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --stream-interval 100 \
    --gdn-prefill-backend {triton,flashinfer}
    
# Client
python3 tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py
```

| Backend | Accuracy | Invalid Rate | Tokens/sec |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Triton | 0.873 | 0.027 | 1,290 |
| FlashInfer Blackwell | **0.874** | **0.024** | **1,611** |

Accuracy remains the same, no degradation.

title: [Bugfix] Fix max_num_batched_token not captured in cuda graph
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose Currently, cuda graph capture sizes only include batch size that land on multiples of 8 or 16. When `max_num_batched_tokens` is not a multiple of the stride, it won't be captured. title: [Bench] Forward --seed to CustomDataset and CustomMMDataset shuffle
author: Aktsvigun
body:
## Summary

`get_samples` in `vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py` passes `random_seed=args.seed` to `RandomDataset` and every HuggingFace-family dataset branch, but omits it when instantiating `CustomDataset` and `CustomMMDataset`. Both classes run `random.seed(self.random_seed)` followed by `random.shuffle(self.data)` during load, so the omission leaves their shuffle hardcoded to `DEFAULT_SEED=0` regardless of what the user passes for `--seed`.

**User-visible symptom.** `vllm bench serve --dataset-name custom --dataset-path X.jsonl --num-prompts N --seed Y` picks the same N rows from `X.jsonl` on every run, no matter how `Y` varies. That breaks the natural use of `--seed` to draw different prompt subsets across repeat benchmarks (for example, to bust KV-cache across runs when profiling a served endpoint against a large prompt corpus).

## Fix

Two call sites in the `get_samples` function gain `random_seed=args.seed`:

- `custom` branch (around line 1805)
- `custom_mm` branch (around line 1818)

This mirrors the pattern already in place for the HF-family branches a few lines below (`random_seed=args.seed` at ~lines 1975–2076). Six lines added, two removed.

## Test plan

Added `tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py`:

- `test_custom_dataset_seed_propagates` — with a 60-row fixture and `num_prompts=30`, different `--seed` values must produce different subsets. **Fails without this patch and passes with it** (verified locally by stashing the fix, running the test, then popping the stash).
- `test_custom_dataset_same_seed_is_deterministic` — same `--seed` must reproduce the same subset.

Run command:

\`\`\`
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py -v
\`\`\`

Result locally: both tests pass after the fix.

## Duplicate-work check

- \`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "random_seed CustomDataset in:title,body"\` — no matches.
- \`gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "custom dataset seed shuffle in:title,body"\` — no related matches.

## Scope notes

- `SonnetDataset` (same function, line 1831) has the same omission but is marked deprecated with a `DeprecationWarning` at the class definition. Left unchanged; happy to include it if maintainers prefer.
- `SpecBench` and `SpeedBench` subclass `CustomDataset` and are dispatched through the `custom` branch, so they inherit the fix without further changes.

title: [Bugfix][Gemma 4] Clamp soft-token estimate to max_soft_tokens
author: hnt2601
body:
## Summary

For extreme-aspect-ratio images (e.g. `3x900`), the prompt-side `Gemma4ProcessingInfo._compute_num_soft_tokens` returned more soft tokens than the HF Gemma 4 image processor's vision tower actually emits (which is capped at `max_soft_tokens`). The mismatch crashed `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` mid-forward and propagated `ValueError` out of `EngineCore.step()` with:

```
Attempted to assign 280 multimodal tokens to 289 placeholders
```

This PR fixes the bug by clamping the prompt-side estimator to `max_soft_tokens` so the placeholder count always matches what the encoder will emit, and adds a small typed-exception layer in the Gemma 4 model so a future engine-layer change can classify this failure mode without parsing free-form `ValueError` messages.

## Root cause

`Gemma4ProcessingInfo._compute_num_soft_tokens` computes target H/W via `max(unit, floor(dim * scale / unit) * unit)`. For very thin or very tall images the `max(unit, …)` floor clamps one dimension up to `unit`, while the other scales freely. After dividing by `patch_size**2 * pooling_kernel_size**2`, the result can exceed `max_soft_tokens`.

Concrete repro for `image_height=3, image_width=900, max_soft_tokens=280, patch_size=14, pooling_kernel_size=2`:

- `scale ≈ 9.02`
- `target_h = 28` (floor would give 0; `max(unit=28, …)` lifts it)
- `target_w = 8092`
- `num_patches = (28 // 14) * (8092 // 14) = 1156`
- `soft_tokens = 1156 // 4 = 289`

The HF Gemma 4 image processor caps its vision-tower output at `max_soft_tokens = 280`, so the prompt has 289 image placeholders but only 280 embeddings to fill them.

## Changes

### 1. Clamp at the prompt-side estimator (the fix)

`Gemma4ProcessingInfo._compute_num_soft_tokens` now returns `min(num_patches // (pooling_kernel_size**2), max_soft_tokens)`. Strict tightening of an existing upper bound: any caller that previously got a value ≤ `max_soft_tokens` is unaffected; any caller that got a value > `max_soft_tokens` was already producing a hard crash downstream.

### 2. Typed exception for the count mismatch (defense in depth)

Adds `Gemma4MultimodalPlaceholderMismatch(ValueError)` and a small `_count_multimodal_embedding_rows` helper to `gemma4_mm.py`, and an explicit count check at the top of `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.embed_input_ids`:

```python
expected = int(is_multimodal.sum().item())
actual = _count_multimodal_embedding_rows(multimodal_embeddings)
if actual != expected:
    raise Gemma4MultimodalPlaceholderMismatch(
        actual=actual, expected=expected
    )
```

The clamp above means this branch should not fire under normal operation. It exists so that any future regression reintroducing a count mismatch raises a *typed* `ValueError` subclass with structured `actual` / `expected` attributes — instead of the generic `ValueError` that `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` raises after a failing `inputs_embeds[is_multimodal] = mm_embeds_flat` index-put. Subclassing `ValueError` keeps existing `except ValueError` handlers working unchanged.

Note: the exception is not yet caught at the engine layer — that hardening is a separate follow-up. Until then, the failure mode for a count mismatch is the same as before, but the offending case is identifiable without string matching on the error message.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Open PRs touching `gemma4` / `multimodal` were checked:

- **#40599** — `[MM][Gemma4] Support max_soft_tokens="auto"`. Adds
  an auto-mode that *selects* `max_soft_tokens` per image; orthogonal
  to the prompt-side estimator over-shooting whatever cap is set.
- **#40347** — `[Bugfix][Gemma4] Fix vision fp16 overflow causing
  <pad> output`. Different bug (numerical overflow), different layer.
- **#40464** — `gemma4: batch multimodal vision processing`.
  Performance work; does not touch the soft-token arithmetic.
- **#40281** — `Fix gemma4 core: quantized inference + gguf
  loading + fused moe gelu_tanh`. Unrelated to multimodal.
- **#39073, #38891** — RMSNorm validation, per-layer attention
  backend. Unrelated.

No open PR addresses the placeholder/encoder soft-token count
mismatch.

## Test plan

New tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py`
run without loading the real Gemma 4 weights (uses `MagicMock` for
`get_hf_config()`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py -v
```

| Test | Pins |
| --- | --- |
| `test_compute_num_soft_tokens_does_not_exceed_max_soft_tokens` (4 cases) | the clamp — production repro `(900,3,280)`, swapped `(3,900,280)`, video-frame budget `(900,3,70)`, high cap `(4000,2,1120)` |
| `test_gemma4_multimodal_placeholder_mismatch_is_value_error` | exception subclasses `ValueError` (preserves `except ValueError` call sites) |
| `test_gemma4_multimodal_placeholder_mismatch_carries_counts` | `actual` / `expected` attributes + message contains both counts |
| `test_gemma4_multimodal_placeholder_mismatch_requires_kwargs` | constructor is keyword-only |
| `test_count_multimodal_embedding_rows` (4 cases) | helper handles tensor, list, tuple, and empty inputs |

All pass locally on Python 3.12 in a `uv` venv.

## Backwards compatibility

- `min(…, max_soft_tokens)` is a strict tightening of an existing upper bound; no public API surface changes.
- `Gemma4MultimodalPlaceholderMismatch` is a new public name in `vllm.model_executor.models.gemma4_mm`. Subclasses `ValueError`, so any caller using `except ValueError` continues to catch it.
- `_count_multimodal_embedding_rows` is module-private (leading underscore).

body:
flashinfer <= 0.6.8.post1 ships no SM110 MoE cubins. On SM110 the SM100 artifact is reused at runtime and the TMA-WS dispatcher picks tile `256x256x128` which has no SM100 registration, raising `Unsupported tile shape config 256256128 for MoE gemm` at `moe_gemm_template_dispatch_tma_ws.h:486` when running Nemotron-H unquantized BF16 MoE. Drop SM110 from the `FlashInferExperts` whitelist so the oracle falls back to Triton, analogous to #39825 for SM121.

Surfaced by #36286 which migrated unquantized MoE to the full oracle flow: the oracle now auto-picks FlashInfer CUTLASS whenever `_supports_current_device` returns True, rather than requiring `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP16=1` as an opt-in. The SM110 gap was latent before; it now triggers by default on Thor.

Tracked at https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3134 . Remove once SM110 MoE cubins ship.

## Test plan

Before (Thor SM110, `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16`): EngineCore crashes with `Unsupported tile shape config 256256128 for MoE gemm`.

After: the unquantized MoE falls back to Triton and the server starts.

title: [EPLB] Fix replica selection bias in fused_moe router
author: arpera
body:
## Purpose

Current replica selection in the EPLB fused-MoE router distributes tokens unevenly across replicas of the same logical expert. Switching to a different hashing implementation fixes this.

## Test Result

### Functional

Hardware: B200

Added `test_eplb_map_hot_expert_replica_balance` as a regression check: it fails on the pre-fix commit and passes with this fix.

```
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -v
```

Result: **496 passed**.

### Performance

Hardware: 8xB200

I experimented with eplb setting 8 additional slots per rank using Qwen3.5-A17B NVFP4 DP8 with EP. Then I measured ratio of workload between ranks as `max/mean` where `max` is the maximum number of tokens one of the ranks processed on one step, `mean` is a mean value of processed tokens by all ranks.

Before this hash change I had average ratio `1.2`, where imbalance between the same replicas in some cases was more than `90%`, but after this change imbalance decreased a lot to `1.07`.

title: [Kernel][Helion] Optimize Helion config parsing latency
author: gmagogsfm
body:
This PR optimizes Helion compilation time.

Previously config picking is not cached, so every cuda graph capture size (per num_token) needs to go through all stored configs for matching, and each matching requires expensive RegEx operations due to free-form string-based config key.

Two improvements are made:
- Replace regex-based config key parsing with structured dict config keys.  eliminating the per-call regex overhead 
- Deserializes keys once on load and passes parsed dicts to kernel pick_config functions with caching enabled, so for different shapes config parsing doesn't need to be done repeatedly


Benchmark: 80,000 calls to `pick_config` with 300 config keys, 8 different input shapes. Measured on NVIDIA H100.

| Approach | us/call | Speedup |
|---|---|---|
| Old (regex, no cache) | 1289 | 1.0× |
| New (CaseKey, no cache) | 46 | 28× |
| New (CaseKey, cached) | 1.8 | 719× |

title: [Bugfix] Size FlashInfer NVLink MNNVL workspace to EP group
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Summary
Fix `FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager` and `FlashInferNVLinkTwoSidedManager` so the MNNVL workspace is sized to the EP group instead of the DP group.

In both managers, the flashinfer-allocated workspace tensor's leading dimension is determined by the comm_backend's group size (via `MnnvlMemory.set_comm_from_config` -> `comm_backend.Split(...)` -> `Get_size`; vLLM's `CustomCommunicator.Split` is a no-op that returns `self`), while the kernel-side dimension comes from the manager's view of the EP group:

- One-sided (`MoeAlltoAll` + `moe_a2a_get_workspace_size_per_rank`): kernel asserts `workspace.size(0) == moe_ep_size`, where `moe_ep_size = self.world_size`.
- Two-sided (`MnnvlMoe.get_moe_workspaces`): workspace stride is sized to `mapping.tp_size`, which is set to `self.world_size` in this manager.

Both paths previously wired `CustomCommunicator(get_dp_group().cpu_group)`, sizing the workspace to the DP group. Whenever `dp_size != ep_size` -- i.e. the standard TP>1 + DP>1 EP configuration -- the two dimensions disagree (the one-sided kernel asserts on first dispatch; the two-sided allocation is similarly mismatched, presumably hidden today because typical two-sided users run TP=1, where DP == EP).

These managers only ever live on the EP `CudaCommunicator` (gated on `is_ep_communicator and data_parallel_size > 1` in [`base_device_communicator.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py)), so `self.cpu_group` is the EP group by construction (size = `DP * PCP * TP`) and matches the kernels' expectation for any combination of DP / PCP / TP.

## Why this is not a duplicate
Searched open PRs on `vllm-project/vllm` for `FlashInferNVLinkOneSided`, `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, `MnnvlConfig`, and `all2all.py + MnnvlConfig` -- no open PR addresses this bug.

## Test plan
Reproduced and verified end-to-end with the configuration that originally hit the assertion (TP=2, DP=4, EP, hybrid LB on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4):

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --language-model-only \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    -tp 2 \
    -dp 4 \
    -ep \
    --max-model-len 118400 \
    --data-parallel-size-local 2 \
    --data-parallel-address ${master_addr} \
    --data-parallel-rpc-port ${master_port} \
    --data-parallel-start-rank ${start_rank} \
    --data-parallel-hybrid-lb \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --attention_config.disable_flashinfer_prefill false \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --all2all-backend {flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided, flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided}
```

- **Before the fix:** the `workspace.size(0) == moe_ep_size` assertion fires inside the flashinfer one-sided and two-sided NVLink kernel on the first dispatch.
- **After the fix:** server initializes and serves requests successfully.

## AI assistance
This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the configuration above to verify the fix end-to-end.

title: [KV Transfer] Add MooncakeStoreConnector for KV cache offloading via Mooncake distributed store
author: LCAIZJ
body:
## Summary

Add `MooncakeStoreConnector`, a new KV connector that uses [MooncakeDistributedStore](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake) as a shared KV cache pool. Unlike the existing `MooncakeConnector` (which does direct point-to-point KV transfer between prefiller and decoder), `MooncakeStoreConnector` offloads KV cache to an external distributed store, enabling:

  - **CPU/Disk offloading**: Extend effective KV cache capacity by offloading to CPU memory or SSD via Mooncake's transfer engine.
  - **Hash-based prefix caching across instances**: Multiple vLLM instances share cached KV blocks through the store using block-hash deduplication.
  - **Flexible deployment**: Works as a single-node KV cache extension (`kv_both`), or in disaggregated prefill-decode setups (`kv_producer` / `kv_consumer`).

  ## Architecture

  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/
  ├── init.py
  ├── mooncake_store_connector.py   # Main connector (scheduler/worker dispatch)
  ├── mooncake_store_scheduler.py   # Scheduler-side: prefix lookup, metadata building
  ├── mooncake_store_worker.py      # Worker-side: background send/recv threads, buffer registration
  └── mooncake_store_data.py        # Shared data structures (ReqMeta, ChunkedTokenDatabase, etc.)

  - **Scheduler side** (`MooncakeStoreScheduler`): Queries external prefix cache hits via ZMQ IPC (`LookupKeyClient` ↔ `LookupKeyServer`), builds per-step connector metadata with load/save specs.
  - **Worker side** (`MooncakeStoreWorker`): Registers GPU KV cache buffers with the Mooncake store, spawns background `KVCacheStoreSendingThread` / `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread` for async put/get. Supports stride-based layout detection for both FlashAttn (K/V-first) and FlashInfer (blocks-first) cache formats.
  - **Disk offload**: Optional disk offloading with budget-aware batch splitting to avoid staging-buffer exhaustion.

  ## Files changed (10 files, +2966 lines)

  | File | Description |
  |------|-------------|
  | `vllm/.../mooncake/store/mooncake_store_connector.py` | Main connector class, role-based dispatch |
  | `vllm/.../mooncake/store/mooncake_store_scheduler.py` | Scheduler logic, ZMQ lookup client |
  | `vllm/.../mooncake/store/mooncake_store_worker.py` | Worker logic, background transfer threads |
  | `vllm/.../mooncake/store/mooncake_store_data.py` | Shared data structures |
  | `vllm/.../mooncake/store/__init__.py` | Package init |
  | `vllm/.../mooncake/mooncake_utils.py` | Add `get_mooncake_dp_engine_index()` helper |
  | `vllm/.../kv_connector/factory.py` | Register `MooncakeStoreConnector` |
  | `tests/.../test_mooncake_store_connector.py` | Unit tests for connector/scheduler |
  | `tests/.../test_mooncake_store_worker.py` | Unit tests for worker/threads |
  | `docs/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage.md` | Usage documentation |

  ## Usage

  ```bash
  # Single-node CPU offloading
  MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH=mooncake_config.json \
  vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
      --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}'

  # Disaggregated prefill-decode
  # Prefiller:
  vllm serve ... --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer"}'
  # Decoder:
  vllm serve ... --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"}'

  See docs/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage.md for full setup instructions.

  Test plan

  - Unit tests pass: pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -v
  - Ruff lint and format checks pass
  - Integration test with Mooncake master + single-node offloading (manual, requires mooncake-transfer-engine)
  - Multi-node disaggregated prefill-decode test (manual, requires RDMA/TCP cluster)
```

  ## Related

RFC：https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38474
Mooncake project: https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake

title: [Kernel] Marlin MoE: include SM 12.x in default arch list
author: tonyliu312
body:
## Purpose

On SM 12.x (RTX 50-series, NVIDIA GB10 / DGX Spark), the Marlin and Marlin-MoE kernels are currently *missing* from the compiled `_C.so` / `_moe_C.abi3.so`. The driver tries to JIT-promote the `8.0+PTX` fallback to SM 12.x, and Marlin-MoE silently produces wrong outputs (V4-Flash MoE decode emits gibberish, while the same model on Hopper produces coherent text).

This PR adds `12.0;12.1` to `MARLIN_ARCHS`, `MARLIN_BF16_ARCHS`, and `MARLIN_MOE_ARCHS` in `CMakeLists.txt` so native sm_120/sm_121 cubins are emitted.

The fp8 sibling lists (`MARLIN_FP8_ARCHS`, `MARLIN_MOE_FP8_ARCHS`) already include `8.9;12.0;12.1`, so the precedent and CTK support for SM 12.x in this file is well established. This change just extends the same coverage to the BF16/FP16 paths.

## Test Plan

1. Rebuild vLLM on a GB10 / DGX Spark host with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1`.
2. Verify Marlin-MoE cubins are emitted natively (no PTX JIT fallback).
3. Run V4-Flash decode against the rebuilt wheel; compare output coherence and steady-state throughput against an unpatched baseline.

## Test Result

**Cubin verification (after rebuild):**

```
$ cuobjdump --list-elf $VLLM/_moe_C.abi3.so | grep -c sm_121
22
$ cuobjdump --list-elf $VLLM/_moe_C.abi3.so | grep -c sm_120
22
```

(Was `0` on both before this patch — only PTX entries.)

**End-to-end model output (V4-Flash, dual DGX Spark, TP=2, single request, max_tokens=80):**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Output | gibberish tokens (e.g. repeating punctuation, stale shards) | `"Silver light spills down — / A hare pounds rice in the dark, / Watching all the world."` |
| Steady throughput | n/a (corrupt output) | 6.28 t/s |

## Notes

- Hardware tested: GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121), pair-wise TP=2 over Spectrum-X.
- No code path changes — only CUDA arch list extension. Existing 8.0/9.0 builds are untouched.
- The MoE Marlin kernel itself already builds cleanly for sm_120/sm_121 with CTK 12.6+; this PR just stops excluding those arches from the build matrix.

## Related

Relates to ongoing SM 12.x enablement work:
- Refs #40760 (zyongye SM120 attention path)
- Refs #40860 (ivanium SM120 build matrix tweaks)
- Refs #40899 (jasl ds4-sm120 — separate scope: DeepSeek-V4 SM12 fused kernels)

## Checklist

- [x] Tested on real hardware (GB10 / DGX Spark, sm_121)
- [x] No other paths regressed (sm_80 / sm_90 builds untouched)
- [x] Commit signed-off (DCO)
- [ ] CI passes (will be confirmed once submitted)

title: [ROCm][Kernel] Add HybridW4A16LinearKernel: Triton prefill + HIP skinny decode
author: mgehre-amd
body:
Add a hybrid W4A16 linear kernel for ROCm gfx11/gfx12 that routes between two GEMM implementations based on batch size:
- M <= 5: HIP wvSplitK_int4_g skinny GEMM (optimized for single-token decode)
- M > 5: Triton fused dequant GEMM (optimized for prefill/batched inference)

Both paths share a single weight tensor in the AWQ-style packed shuffle layout [N, K//8]. Supports both symmetric (uint4b8, bias=8) and asymmetric (uint4, per-group zero-points) quantization with group sizes 32, 64 or 128.

The Triton kernel includes tuned tile-size heuristics for gfx1151 (Strix Halo, RDNA 3.5) and gfx1201 (RDNA 4) based on real weight shapes from Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.1-8B-AWQ, plus shape-specific overrides.

The HIP skinny decode kernel uses a marlin-style magic-number dequantization trick for bf16 models, avoiding an expensive fp32 round-trip on gfx1151.

title: [ROCm][perf] Use workspace manager for sparse indexer allocations
author: tuukkjs
body:
## Purpose

Replace dynamic per-call allocations in the ROCm sparse attention indexer with workspace manager allocations.

The sparse attention indexer uses temporary buffers in both prefill and decode: `k_fp8` / `k_scale` in prefill and decode logits buffers in `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`. These buffers are runtime scratch space, and their sizes vary with request shape, batch size, and speculative decoding state. They are a good fit for `WorkspaceManager`, which is already used elsewhere in vLLM to reserve and reuse bounded scratch buffers instead of relying on repeated hot-path PyTorch allocator calls.

This PR is primarily an allocator robustness and consistency change:

- It avoids repeated dynamic `torch.empty` / `torch.full` allocations in the ROCm sparse indexer hot path.
- It makes the ROCm sparse prefill behavior match the existing CUDA sparse indexer pattern, where temporary buffers are workspace-managed.
- It lets profiling reserve the required scratch size up front, so later execution reuses the profiled workspace instead of growing allocator state unexpectedly.

Earlier validation of the stale predecessor PR showed plain-image failures under sustained MTP load, including memory access faults and `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. On the current nightly stack used for the tests, that exact MTP=2 failure no longer reproduces reliably in the plain image. Therefore this PR can not be said to fix MTP=2 crash that occured eariler. The argument for PR is that sparse-indexer scratch allocations should be workspace-managed on ROCm for the same reason they are workspace-managed elsewhere: bounded scratch reuse, less allocator churn, and lower risk of fragmentation or late hot-path allocation surprises.

This continues the work of stale PR #38704 by @gronsti-amd, rebased onto current `main`. AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Solution

- **Prefill path:** Replace per-chunk `torch.empty` allocations for `k_fp8` and `k_scale` with a single `workspace_manager.get_simultaneous()` allocation, slicing the workspace views per chunk.
- **Decode path:** Allocate the temporary decode logits buffer from `WorkspaceManager` and pass it to the existing AITER paged-MQA logits kernels.
- **Memory profiling path:** Reserve workspace for the prefill and decode buffer sizes in the real implementation's early-exit path, while keeping the fake implementation compatible with FakeTensor mode during `torch.compile`.

## Test Plan

**Environment:**

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-f6490a28413526adefae8dd7af32906d060e0436`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2`
- Hardware: 8x MI355X, TP=8
- Attention backend: `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`

**Four experiments were run for validation:**

1. **No MTP (baseline):** Verifies the workspace manager changes do not regress the non-speculative decoding path.
2. **MTP=1 (1 speculative token):** Validates workspace-managed allocations under MTP with a single draft token.
3. **MTP=2 (2 speculative tokens):** Validates workspace-managed allocations under MTP with two draft tokens.
4. **MTP=3 (3 speculative tokens):** Validates workspace-managed allocations under MTP with three draft tokens.

**Server command:**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --seed 4321 \
    --dtype auto \

(The `--speculative-config` argument is omitted for the no-MTP baseline, and `N` is 1, 2, or 3 for the MTP experiments.)

title: [DSv4] Use `cvt` PTX for FP32->FP4 conversion
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Purpose

Currently FP4 quantization logic for `_fused_indexer_q_rope_mxfp4_kernel()` and `_fused_kv_compress_norm_rope_insert_indexer_mxfp4_attn()` does a linear search, which is inefficient, and more importantly, does not do round-to-nearest-even correctly. This PR switches to inline PTX `cvt.rn.satfinite.e2m1x2.f32` which is cleaner and should be faster too.

## Test Plan

title: [Model Runner V2] Apply synthetic mode to probabilistic rejection sampler
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# Context
Per-position acceptance rates were recently added in [this PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40662), adding support for both MRV1 and MRV2. However, MRV2 currently uses [a separate path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0dc7a0f368a3f212d37e39ba4dd7b682e378fe2/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py#L140-L152) for synthetic rejection sampling, which is not ideal because synthetic acceptance rates should closely approximate actual rejection sampling.

# This PR
I apply the synthetic mode in the probabilistic rejection sampling kernels. This involved pass the synthetic conditional rates to `_probabilistic_rejection_kernel` (now renamed to `_rejection_kernel`). If non-None, the draft token is accepted with the conditional probability of that given step. Note that the kernel still loads target/draft logits, sum-exponentials, etc, even if unused to closely match the performance of actual rejection sampling.

Other notable changes:
- Deleted `synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py`, not used anymore.
- Renamed `probabilistic_rejection_sampler_utils.py` to `rejection_sampler_utils.py`, as well as removed `probabilistic` prefix from all methods within. That prefix was leftover from when the rejection sample method was either "probabilistic", "strict", or "synthetic". Now it's just either "standard" or "synthetic".
- Added test cases for synthetic rejection sampling to `test_rejection_sampler_utils.py`.

# Tests
## Automatic

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Avoid per-step numpy allocation in prepare_next_t…
author: wangluochao902
body:
## Description

### Purpose
Remove an unnecessary `np.array()` allocation that runs every decode step in the speculative decoding path.

### Background

After the target model produces sampled tokens, the drafter needs the **next token ID** for each request to start drafting. There are two cases:

1. **Normal request**: The next token is the last sampled token from the target model
2. **Discarded request** (e.g., chunked prefill not yet finished): No token was sampled, so we fall back to looking up the token from the request's history

`prepare_next_token_ids_padded` computes the "backup" token IDs for case 2, then a Triton kernel picks between case 1 and case 2 for each request.

### Example

Suppose we have 3 requests:

```
Request A: "The cat sat on the" → sampled [mat]     (normal)
Request B: "Hello world"        → sampled []         (discarded — still prefilling)
Request C: "Once upon a"        → sampled [time]     (normal)

num_tokens_no_spec = [6, 2, 4]
```

We need backup token IDs (the last committed token for each request):
```
Request A: token at position 5 (= 6-1) → "the"
Request B: token at position 1 (= 2-1) → "world"
Request C: token at position 3 (= 4-1) → "a"
```

The Triton kernel later picks: A→"mat" (sampled), B→"world" (backup), C→"time" (sampled).

### Problem

The current code builds these backup IDs via a list comprehension + `np.array()`:

```python
seq_lens_list = (gpu_input_batch.num_tokens_no_spec[:num_reqs] - 1).tolist()
self.backup_next_token_ids.np[:num_reqs] = np.array(
    [requests[gpu_input_batch.req_ids[i]].get_token_id(seq_lens_list[i])
     for i in range(num_reqs)],
    dtype=np.int32,
)
```

Every decode step this:
1. Creates a Python list via `.tolist()`
2. Creates another Python list via the list comprehension
3. Allocates a new numpy array via `np.array()`
4. Copies into the pre-allocated pinned buffer

Steps 1–3 are unnecessary since we already have a pre-allocated `CpuGpuBuffer`.

### Fix

Write directly into the pre-allocated pinned buffer:

```python
_backup_np = self.backup_next_token_ids.np
_nts = gpu_input_batch.num_tokens_no_spec
for i in range(num_reqs):
    _backup_np[i] = requests[
        gpu_input_batch.req_ids[i]
    ].get_token_id(_nts[i] - 1)
```

No temporary list, no `np.array()` allocation. Each value is written directly into the pinned buffer. Typical batch sizes in spec decode are 1–16 requests, so the loop is trivially fast.

This applies to all speculative decoding methods (Eagle, MTP, DFlash, draft_model) since `prepare_next_token_ids_padded` is on `SpecDecodeBaseProposer`.

### Test Plan

```bash
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-speculator.eagle3","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_tensor_parallel_size":1}'

vllm bench serve \
    --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
    --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions \
    --dataset-name sonnet --dataset-path sonnet.txt \
    --sonnet-input-len 4096 --sonnet-output-len 512 --sonnet-prefix-len 0 \
    --num-prompts 200 --max-concurrency 1 \
    --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 42
```

### Test Results

Llama-3.1-8B + Eagle3 (TP=4, num_speculative_tokens=3, H200, 3×100 prompts, max-concurrency 1):

| | Mean TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| Before (3 runs avg) | 2.60 | 3.24 |
| After (3 runs avg) | 2.58 | 2.94 |
| **Improvement** | **0.8%** | **9.3%** |

The P99 improvement comes from eliminating occasional Python GC pauses triggered by the per-step `np.array()` allocation.

title: [Kernel][MoE] Support GELU on TRT-LLM NvFP4 fused MoE for Gemma4
author: juhi10071998
body: ## Summary Enables `MoEActivation.GELU` (gated GELU, GeGLU) on the FlashInfer TRT-LLM NvFP4 MoE backend (`TrtLlmNvFp4Experts*` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py`). The GPU kernel and the dispatcher already support GeGLU end-to-end — only the Python allow-list and assertions were gating it out. This is also the first kernel-level test for the TRT-LLM × NvFP4 intersection in vLLM — sibling backends (CUTLASS NvFP4 in test_flashinfer_moe.py) and sibling quants (TRT-LLM FP8 in test_flashinfer.py) had tests, but the specific kernel and quant scheme this PR enables had no coverage. The swizzle-flag fix in make_test_quant_config was a latent test-infra bug that surfaced on the first attempt to drive this kernel through the standard test helpers. **Motivation:** Gemma4 MoE blocks use gated GELU. Without this change, vLLM falls through to `Marlin` kernel when running quantized Gemma4 on Blackwell. Builds on #39510, whose non-aligned `intermediate_size` weight padding is exercised by the new test at Gemma4's `(64, 704, 4096)` shape. ## Changes | File | Change | |---|---| | `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py` | Add `MoEActivation.GELU` to `_supports_activation` and to the modular/monolithic `apply()` allow-list assertions. | | `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py` | Add an `is_nvfp4_scale_swizzled` parameter (default `True`, preserves existing callers) to `make_test_quant_config`, forwarded to FusedMoEQuantConfig.make`. | | `tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py` | **New file.** Kernel test exercising SiLU, RELU², and GELU at three shapes including Gemma4's `(intermediate_size=704, hidden=4096)`. | The test-helper change is needed because the FlashInfer TRT-LLM kernel rejects swizzled (padded) input quant scales — its `numel`-based vec_size derivation requires `numel == M*K/16`. Production code already does the right thing in `oracle/nvfp4.py:458`; the test helper hardcoded the swizzled default, leaving the kernel untestable through `make_test_quant_config`. ## Test plan Ran on a Blackwell (SM100) box with FlashInfer-python 0.6.8.post1 and flashinfer-cubin 0.6.8.post1. ` python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py --timeout=1200 ` **Result: 8 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.** All three GELU rows pass, including Gemma4's `(64, 704, 4096)`. The skip is `RELU2_NO_MUL @ (64, 704, 4096)` — FlashInfer's `trtllm_batched_gemm_runner` raises *"No valid config found for the given problem shape"* for non-gated RELU² at non-256-aligned `intermediate_size`. Verified pre-existing on `main` without this PR's changes; Does not affect Gemma4 enablement (Gemma4 uses gated GELU, not non-gated RELU²). will raise an issue in Flashinfer, but not blocking this PR. The monolithic path (`TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsMonolithic`) is gated identically to the modular path. End-to-end coverage in this PR is on the modular path (which is what Gemma4's multi-GPU expert-parallel deployments use). The monolithic path was verified by probing `flashinfer.fused_moe.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` directly with `activation_type=Geglu`; the kernel accepts the call. Both entry points share the same FlashInfer kernel family for the underlying compute. ## Note- - No production code changes for the swizzle issue. The oracle already sets the right flag in production. - No GPU code changes — the kernel always supported GeGLU. - No new dependencies, no FlashInfer version bump, no new dispatch paths. - The monolithic path is gated identically to the modular path. The new test exercises the modular path end-to-end (the path Gemma4's expected multi-GPU-EP deployments use). Also, when can the PR be picked in vllm latest image along with PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39510 ## TL;DR vLLM's Python allow-list rejected gated GELU on the TRT-LLM NvFP4 MoE backend, even though the underlying FlashInfer kernel supports it. This PR extends the allow-list to include MoEActivation.GELU (3 lines trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py). It also adds the first kernel-level test for TRT-LLM × NvFP4, which surfaced and fixes a latent test-helper bug around NvFP4 scale layout.

title: [ROCm][CI] Extended Fused MoE and FP8 MoE test support
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
This PR makes the fused MoE layer test matrix usable on ROCm/MI355 by fixing the real ModelOpt FP8/FP4 failures it exposes and by making distributed subcase failures visible to pytest.

Key changes:

- Propagate fused MoE distributed subcase failures back to the parent pytest process instead of allowing child-rank failures to print as failed subcases while the parent test reports `PASSED`.
- Allow `modelopt_fp4` MoE test configs on gfx950 alongside the existing SM100 path, where native or emulated NVFP4 execution is available.
- Use the existing NVFP4 reference quantization path to create packed FP4 test weights on ROCm, since `ops.scaled_fp4_quant` is not available there.
- Keep NVFP4 emulation lookup tensors on the same device as the packed FP4 input during dequantization.
- Preserve reduced ModelOpt FP8 tensor-wise MoE activation scales as backend-neutral 0-D tensors, reshaping them only at the Triton launch boundary so FlashInfer retains its scalar ABI while Triton receives a loadable pointer.
- Gate the experimental MoRI fused MoE layer matrix behind `VLLM_TEST_ENABLE_MORI_MOE_LAYER=1`; when enabled, the test sets the AITER fused MoE env requirements and disables AITER shared expert fusion.
- Enable the modular OAI Triton MoE test on CUDA-like platforms and pad MXFP4 test weights/inputs to the CDNA4 scale-layout alignment on ROCm while slicing outputs back to the original test shape.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used to analyze the CI and review feedback and to prepare the changes.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix]: dynamically align BLOCK_DMODEL with Lv in MLA decode kernel
author: vllmellm
body: ## Purpose Fixes #40966 This PR resolves a Triton compilation error, `ValueError('Cannot make_shape_compatible: incompatible dimensions at index 1: 256 and 512')` occurring in MLA-based models Mistral-Small on ROCm. **Key Changes:** **Dynamic Dimension Alignment:** Updated the triton_decode_attention kernel to align BLOCK_DMODEL with the local latent rank (Lv) instead of the total head dimension (Lk) when is_mla=True. This ensures shape compatibility for tl.dot operations. **Regression-Free Generalization:** Replaced hardcoded dimension checks with generalized next_power_of_2 logic, supporting a wider range of MLA configurations while maintaining compatibility with DeepSeek-V3/V3.1. **Hardware Tuning:** Optimized the BLOCK size to 16 for HIP/ROCm (MI300X) to balance shared memory pressure. ## Test Plan 1. Comprehensive Regression Testing (MLA Models): Verify that the dynamic alignment logic maintains stability and accuracy across various MLA-based architectures. - Models: DeepSeek-V3.1 (TP4), DeepSeek-V2-Lite (TP2), and Kimi-K2.5 (TP8). - Evaluation: Compare GSM8K accuracy (LM-Eval) and serving throughput/latency against the original hardcoded kernel. 2. Bugfix Verification (Mistral-Small): Confirm the fix resolves the compilation crash on ROCm. - Models: Mistral-Small-2403 (TP2). - Evaluation: E2E serving and accuracy benchmark. ## Test Result 1. LMEval Accuracy Comparison (No Regression) The fix resolves the Mistral-Small crash while maintaining consistent accuracy across all tested MLA models. Notably, the DeepSeek-V2-Lite results align perfectly with existing community benchmarks. 2. Benchmark Serving Performance Beyond fixing the crash, the dynamic alignment of BLOCK_DMODEL significantly improves Time to First Token (TTFT) on ROCm by optimizing memory access patterns. Serving benchmarks show no performance regression in throughput, and all models benefit from lower initial latency.

title: Defer flashinfer cubin download to avoid ~2.5 GB (decompressed) layer duplication
author: benoittgt
body:
Defer `flashinfer download-cubin` to after all pip installs, eliminating ~2.5 GB of cross-layer file duplication in the Docker image.

## Purpose

While looking at reducing image size with `Dive` and Claude Opus, I find few things. Here is the first one;

Running `flashinfer download-cubin` in the flashinfer-jit-cache install layer (L586) writes ~10,600 precompiled cubin files into the `flashinfer_cubin` package directory. When the vLLM wheel is installed later (L644), it resolves `flashinfer-python` and `flashinfer-cubin` as transitive dependencies (via `pyproject.toml` dynamic deps -> `setup.py` -> `requirements/cuda.txt`), touching/reinstalling those packages. The overlay filesystem keeps the original cubins from the earlier layer as **dead weight** even though they are fully shadowed.

[Dive](https://github.com/wagoodman/dive) analysis of the published `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.16.0` image (26.29 GB, efficiency 95.1%) confirms 2,452 MB of duplication across 10,598 flashinfer cubin/header files, each appearing in exactly two layers.

The fix moves only the cubin download to after the last pip install (EP kernels). The `flashinfer-jit-cache` pip install stays in its original layer to preserve Docker build cache behavior. No packages are added or removed; the image produces the same runtime environment.

## Test Plan

1. Build the image with and without the patch: `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t vllm-openai .`
2. Compare image sizes with `docker images` and confirm a ~2.5 GB reduction.
3. Run [Dive](https://github.com/wagoodman/dive) on both images (`dive vllm-openai`) and verify that `flashinfer_cubin` files no longer appear duplicated across layers (count should be 1 instead of 2).
4. Start the server with a model and confirm vLLM serves inference requests normally, including FlashInfer attention backend.

## Test Result

Not yet tested on a full build (requires CUDA build environment). The change is a pure layer reordering: same `flashinfer show-config && flashinfer download-cubin` commands, same packages, just executed after the last pip install instead of before. Dive data from the current `v0.16.0` image confirms the duplication mechanism and the expected savings.

Duplication data extracted from the published image:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total image size | 26.29 GB |
| Inefficient bytes | 2,566 MB |
| flashinfer_cubin duplication | 2,452 MB (10,598 files, each in 2 layers) |
| Expected savings | ~2.5 GB |

title: Fix static actorder handling for compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE
author: ZewenShen-Cohere
body:
## Purpose

Fix compressed-tensors WNA16 Marlin MoE handling for checkpoints with `actorder=static`.
`ActivationOrdering.STATIC` is equivalent to weight-order/no runtime `g_idx`, but the previous logic treated any truthy `actorder` as grouped actorder. This caused `w2` scales to be loaded full on every TP rank and made the Marlin kernel infer the wrong group size.

## Details

For `actorder=static`, `w2` scales should be sharded with the TP partition, and `is_k_full` should remain true.
Before this fix, a `tp=2`, `group_size=32` Qwen3-A3B W4A16 checkpoint failed during startup because the kernel inferred:
```text
size_k = 384, num_groups = 24, effective group_size = 16
```
which is not a valid Marlin WNA16 MoE configuration. This leads to the following error message during initialization:
```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Invalid thread config: thread_m_blocks = 4, thread_k = -1, thread_n = -1, num_threads = -1 for MKN = [65536, 384, 2048] and num_bits = 4, group_size = 16, has_act_order = 0, is_k_full = 0, has_zp = 0, is_zp_float = 0, max_shared_mem = 232448', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
```

This PR also adds validation that static group-scale WNA16 MoE shards are aligned to group_size, so unsupported TP layouts fail early with a clear error instead of producing a later CUDA/kernel failure.

## Test Plan

- [x] Confirm that the [Qwen3-A3B W4A16 GPTQ GS32 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/zshen-cohere/Qwen3-30B-A3B-INT4A16-GPTQ-GS32) (obtained from llm-compressor using gptq+static actorder) doesn't load without my fix, and loads after my fix.

title: [Perf] Optimize `AllPool.forward` by slicing first, 51% faster in the method level benchmark
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

Part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35631

## Test

### Acc

Covered in current CI

### Perf

```bash
import gc
import statistics
import time

import numpy as np
import torch

from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.pooler.tokwise.methods import AllPool
from vllm.pooling_params import PoolingParams
from vllm.v1.pool.metadata import PoolingMetadata, PoolingStates

DEVICE = "cuda:0"
DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
HIDDEN_SIZE = 4096

FULL_LENGTHS = [128] * 64
# FULL_LENGTHS = [32 + (i * 17) % 224 for i in range(64)]  # varying-length case
SUBGROUP_OFFSET = 16
SUBGROUP_SIZE = 32

WARMUP = 500
ITERS = 4000
REPEATS = 5


def build_metadata(device: torch.device) -> PoolingMetadata:
    tasks = ["classify"] * len(FULL_LENGTHS)
    for i in range(SUBGROUP_OFFSET, SUBGROUP_OFFSET + SUBGROUP_SIZE):
        tasks[i] = "token_classify"

    metadata = PoolingMetadata(
        prompt_lens=torch.tensor(FULL_LENGTHS, dtype=torch.int32),
        prompt_token_ids=None,
        prompt_token_ids_cpu=None,
        pooling_params=[PoolingParams(task=t) for t in tasks],
        pooling_states=[PoolingStates() for _ in tasks],
    )

    query_start_loc_gpu = torch.tensor(
        [0] + list(np.cumsum(FULL_LENGTHS)),
        dtype=torch.int32,
        device=device,
    )
    metadata.build_pooling_cursor(
        np.asarray(FULL_LENGTHS, dtype=np.int32),
        seq_lens_cpu=metadata.prompt_lens,
        device=device,
        query_start_loc_gpu=query_start_loc_gpu,
    )
    return metadata[SUBGROUP_OFFSET:SUBGROUP_OFFSET + SUBGROUP_SIZE]


def measure_us(pooler: AllPool, hidden_states: torch.Tensor, metadata: PoolingMetadata):
    samples = []
    for _ in range(REPEATS):
        for _ in range(WARMUP):
            pooler(hidden_states, metadata)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

        # Use wall time, not CUDA events: current AllPool.forward may include
        # host-visible sync via .tolist() / .item().
        gc.disable()
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(ITERS):
            pooler(hidden_states, metadata)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        t1 = time.perf_counter()
        gc.enable()

        samples.append((t1 - t0) * 1e6 / ITERS)
    return samples


def main():
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise SystemExit("CUDA is not available")

    device = torch.device(DEVICE)
    hidden_states = torch.randn(
        sum(FULL_LENGTHS),
        HIDDEN_SIZE,
        device=device,
        dtype=DTYPE,
    )

    cfg = VllmConfig()
    cfg.scheduler_config.enable_chunked_prefill = False

    with set_current_vllm_config(cfg):
        pooler = AllPool()
        metadata = build_metadata(device)

        out = pooler(hidden_states, metadata)
        assert len(out) == SUBGROUP_SIZE
        assert sum(x.shape[0] for x in out) == sum(
            FULL_LENGTHS[SUBGROUP_OFFSET:SUBGROUP_OFFSET + SUBGROUP_SIZE]
        )

        samples = measure_us(pooler, hidden_states, metadata)

    print(f"AllPool.forward median: {statistics.median(samples):.2f} us")
    print(f"runs: {[round(x, 2) for x in samples]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

runs: [39.67, 39.65, 39.72, 39.59, 39.47]
```

Main

title: [Bugfix] Use enable_sm120_family for per-tensor FP8 CUTLASS kernels on SM12.1
author: j9smith
body:
## Purpose

Fix per-tensor FP8 CUTLASS kernels failing on SM 12.1 devices (e.g., NVIDIA GB10). 

The `cutlass_3x_gemm_sm120` and `cutlass_3x_gemm_sm120_custom` structs use `enable_sm120_only` which guards on `__CUDA_ARCH == 1200`. On SM 12.1 (`__CUDA_ARCH__ == 1210`), this causes a kernel trap and surfaces as `cutlass_gemm_caller Error Internal`. 

The fix replaces `enable_sm120_only` with `enable_sm120_family` (which checks `>= 1200 && <1300`) in two files:
- `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm.cuh`
- `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_sm120_fp8_dispatch.cuh`

The blockwise FP8 path (`scaled_mm_blockwise_sm120_fp8_dispatch.cuh`) already uses `enable_sm120_family` so the precedent is set. There are no other occurrences of `enable_sm120_only` in the codebase as far as I can see. 

This PR fixes #40758.

## Test Plan
This is a two line change replacing an architecture guard and so no new tests are required. Existing `test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py` FP8 tests cover this codepath on SM 12.x hardware.

## Test Result
Pending CI. 

All FP8 CUTLASS tests pass on SM 12.0 (RTX 5060 Ti):
`pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py -v -k "fp8"`

title: [Bugfix][Hybrid][NemotronH] Fix mamba_cache_mode=all + speculative decoding crash
author: roikoren755
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the chain of three bugs reported in #39809 that crash NemotronH (and other hybrid Mamba2) models when prefix caching `all` mode is combined with speculative decoding.

This PR also reverts the temporary workaround merged in #40454.

### Evaluation

Verified end-to-end with `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super using a shared few-shot prefix to exercise the cache. The full `(PC-off, PC-align, PC-all) × (CUDA graphs, --enforce-eager)` matrix all land at ~92% accuracy, confirming `PC all + SpecDec` is correctness-equivalent to the existing baselines. The logs also show a prefix cache hit rate of around 75%, for both `align` and `all` modes.

### Solution overview

The three issues share a root cause: in `mamba_cache_mode='all'` + spec decode the kernel reads/writes `1 + num_speculative_blocks` consecutive state slots per request, but the surrounding bookkeeping treated the block table and per-request indices as if no speculative slots were reserved. Concretely:

1. `state_indices_tensor_d` is now sized to `cdiv(max_model_len, block_size) + num_speculative_blocks` so each request's block table addresses every slot the kernel actually touches. `MambaSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes` and the `mamba_get_block_table_tensor` docstring updated to match.
2. The persistent `block_idx_last_*` buffers used during CUDA graph capture are now padded to `num_reqs` (matching how the kernel indexes them) instead of `num_decode_tokens`.
3. When fewer drafts are accepted than scheduled, the next step's read anchor must point to the slot the previous step actually wrote — `(num_computed - 1) // block_size` no longer matches because `num_computed` reflects only accepted tokens. Tracked per request in `mamba_state_idx` and plumbed to the kernel as `block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step`.

## Test Plan

Two new regression tests added `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py`:
- test_state_indices_tensor_d_includes_num_speculative_blocks
- test_block_idx_cudagraph_capture_padded_by_num_reqs

Both fail on main without this PR and pass with it.

End-to-end reproducer from #39809 on a 4×GB200 host:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode all \
--trust-remote-code \
--tensor-parallel-size 4 \
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
```

Sent the same long prompt twice and observed vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 2 passed, 0 failed.

```
tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py::test_state_indices_tensor_d_includes_num_speculative_blocks PASSED
tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py::test_block_idx_cudagraph_capture_padded_by_num_reqs PASSED
```

Without the fix:
- test_state_indices_tensor_d_includes_num_speculative_blocks fails with
`assert torch.Size([4, 16]) == (4, 18)`.
- test_block_idx_cudagraph_capture_padded_by_num_reqs fails with
`assert torch.Size([4]) == (3,)`.

E2E: server starts cleanly, completions are factually correct, no crash. With duplicate sends of a >4224-token prompt, `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` increments as expected (8448 cached tokens / 10926 prompt tokens, i.e. 2 full Mamba blocks worth on the second request).

title: [Bugfix][KV Transfer] Reject NixlConnector + expandable_segments:True
author: esmeetu
body:
## Purpose

`NixlConnector` pins the KV cache via `ibv_reg_mr` once at startup. When `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`, PyTorch's CUDA VMM allocator can later remap KV cache virtual addresses to different physical pages — leaving the registered IB `rkey` pointing at stale physical pages.

The two settings are fundamentally incompatible: `ibv_reg_mr` expects stable physical mappings for the lifetime of the MR, while `expandable_segments` explicitly trades that guarantee for memory-pool flexibility.

In practice this combination silently corrupts inter-node KV transfers and only surfaces at the first request, with errors like:

- `IBV_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR (synd 0x13 vend 0x88 hw_synd 0/0)` on the decode side
- `makeXferReq: remote agent '<uuid>' was invalidated in between prepXferDlist and this call`
- `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` / `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` / `NIXL_ERR_CANCELED`
- 0 Gbps RDMA traffic despite NIXL appearing healthy at startup; benchmark stalls indefinitely

The prefill side shows **zero errors** because the allocator misbehavior happens at the CUDA VMM layer below NIXL's awareness. Diagnosing this from the symptom is hours of work; preventing the misconfiguration up front is one `if`.

This change validates the combination at config-load time in `KVTransferConfig.__post_init__` and fails fast with an actionable error.

This affects only `NixlConnector` — other connectors do not pin GPU memory through `ibv_reg_mr`, so the same env var is harmless for them and is left untouched.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py -v
```

Adds three cases covering:
1. `NixlConnector` + `expandable_segments:True` → raises with a clear message
2. `NixlConnector` + `expandable_segments:False` (or other allocator config) → allowed
3. Non-NIXL connector + `expandable_segments:True` → unaffected

## Test Result

Before this change, a real GB200 NVL72 1P/1D run with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` on the prefill side accepts the config, allocates and registers KV memory, then produces 66 NIXL transfer failures at the first request and the benchmark hangs at 12/320 progress. Removing `expandable_segments:True` (the only change) fixes it: 0 NIXL errors, benchmark progresses normally to 132/320 within ~2 minutes.

After this change, the same misconfiguration is rejected at startup with:

```
ValueError: NixlConnector is incompatible with PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True. PyTorch's CUDA VMM allocator can remap KV cache virtual addresses to different physical pages, invalidating the IB memory regions registered by NIXL. Unset expandable_segments:True (or remove it from PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF).
```

title: [Bugfix][KV Transfer][NIXL] Notify P node on pre-admission rejection to free stranded KV blocks
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where prefill KV blocks on the **P (prefill) node** are stranded for up to `VLLM_NIXL_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (default 480s) when the **D (decode) node** rejects an incoming request *before* it is admitted to the engine scheduler.

When a request that carries KV-transfer params (`do_remote_prefill=True`, `remote_block_ids`, `remote_engine_id`, etc.) is rejected on D for reasons like:

- Render / chat-template error
- Model existence check failure (`_check_model`)
- Input validation error
- Engine errored
- Beam-search-with-stream rejection
- `previous_response_id` not found (responses API)

…D never opens a NIXL transfer for it, so P never receives the implicit "transfer complete → free blocks" signal. The blocks linger until the abort timeout fires.

This PR adds an explicit early-rejection notification:

1. The OpenAI-compatible serving layer (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `responses`) calls `engine_client.notify_kv_transfer_request_rejected(...)` on every pre-admission rejection path that has `kv_transfer_params.do_remote_prefill=True`.
2. `AsyncLLM` → `EngineCoreClient` (in-process / sync MP / async MP / DPLB-async MP) → `EngineCore` → `Scheduler` → `KVConnectorBase_V1.request_rejected_before_admission(...)`.
3. `NixlConnectorScheduler` recognizes the params and enqueues an empty `_reqs_need_recv` entry. On the next scheduler tick the worker side issues the notification that releases the remote blocks. To make sure that tick actually happens when D has no other in-flight work, `Scheduler.has_requests()` now also reports pending connector metadata.
4. `MultiConnector` fans out to its child connectors and accepts the first one that recognizes the params.
5. `DPLBAsyncMPClient` broadcasts the notification to all local DP engines when no `data_parallel_rank` header is present (the rejection happens before admission, so the request isn't yet tracked in `reqs_in_flight`).

The `_reqs_need_recv` value type changed from `(Request, BlockIds)` to `(dict[str, Any], BlockIds)` because pre-admission rejections do not have a `Request` object — only the raw `kv_transfer_params` dict — and that's all the existing code on the `_build_kv_connector_meta` side actually consumed (`req.kv_transfer_params`).

If `do_remote_prefill` is set but the required `remote_*` metadata is incomplete, the connector logs a warning and returns False (no-op) rather than guessing.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

I checked open PRs and issues with searches like `stranded prefill`, `stranded KV blocks rejected NIXL`, `request_rejected_before_admission`, `kv_transfer_params reject`, and `decode reject prefill`. The closest matches are:

- **#38027 [Nixl][PD] Lease renewal TTL KV blocks on P** — bounds stranding via heartbeat-based TTL refresh. Complementary, not a duplicate: it shortens the window for crashes / disconnects, but pre-admission rejections still need an explicit "this transfer will never start" signal so blocks free *immediately* instead of after the (shortened) lease.
- **#35764 [Feat][NIXL] Add KV lease refresh mechanism** — same area, same rationale as #38027.
- **#41237 [Bugfix][KV Transfer] Reject NixlConnector + expandable_segments:True** — unrelated config-validation fix.

No existing PR covers the rejected-before-admission notification path.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests added:
  - `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_rejected_remote_prefill_request_enqueues_empty_recv` — verifies the connector enqueues an empty recv with the original `remote_*` params and `Scheduler.has_requests()` flips True until the tick flushes it.
  - `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_rejected_remote_prefill_request_missing_metadata_is_ignored` — verifies the connector no-ops (and does not mutate `do_remote_prefill`) when required `remote_*` fields are missing.
  - `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py::test_request_rejected_before_admission_uses_first_accepting_connector` — verifies short-circuit fan-out behavior in `MultiConnector`.
- [x] Local: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -v` — 76 passed, 2 skipped, 1 unrelated failure (`test_multi_example_connector_consistency`, which fails on `OSError: gated repo meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` — unrelated to this change).
- [x] Pre-commit hooks staged / will run on push.
- [ ] Reviewer should confirm behavior end-to-end on a P/D NIXL deployment by sending an oversized prompt (or one whose chat template fails) carrying `kv_transfer_params.do_remote_prefill=True` and observing that the P-side block usage drops immediately rather than after `VLLM_NIXL_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with assistance from Claude (Anthropic). I (the human submitter) reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, and can defend the design end-to-end.

This updates the EAGLE3 acceptance length regression test to use ROCm backend auto-selection instead of hard-selecting attention backends. The Qwen3-VL FP8 MoE case is limited to ROCm TP4 and enables expert parallelism to avoid the unsupported block-FP8 TP shard shape. title: [ROCm][CI] Fix NIXL spec-decode acceptance startup and diagnostics
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Use `ATTENTION_BACKEND=ROCM_ATTN` override in AMD Buildkite for the NIXL speculative-decoding acceptance test.
- Make the NIXL spec-decode integration script fail fast when a server process exits before readiness instead of polling for the full timeout.
- Pin this integration test path to `127.0.0.1` and set `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST` explicitly so HTTP, proxy traffic, and NIXL side-channel metadata use the same loopback address family.
- Improve NIXL KV-cache registration diagnostics when a tensor does not match the expected block dimension, including layer name, shape, stride, backend list, KV layout, and topology mode.

## Scope Notes

1. HTTP readiness is not enough for NIXL. The failing logs showed `/v1/completions` returning 200, then decode later timing out in `_nixl_handshake()` while waiting for prefill metadata on the side-channel socket. The new readiness check sends the same NIXL `get_meta_msg` request over ZMQ that decode needs, so the test does not start until the side channel is actually answering.

2. `localhost` can resolve through IPv6 while the proxy path is already intentionally bound to `127.0.0.1` for CI. This test now uses `127.0.0.1` consistently and passes that host into the Python test for proxy and metrics access.

cc @kenroche

title: [Perf] Warmup forward_native sampler kernel
author: arpera
body:
## Purpose

The default-on FlashInfer top-k/top-p sampler from #40376 exposed a warmup gap in `_dummy_sampler_run`: the existing dummy call uses `generators={}`, which under the new default routes through `flashinfer_sample` and leaves the `forward_native` Triton fallback path JIT-cold. That fallback is taken at runtime whenever a request has a seed (`SamplingMetadata.generators` non-empty), so the first such request pays ~1s of JIT cost on its first sampling step.

This makes `tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py::test_multi_abort` fail on main: the test seeds every request and aborts after `asyncio.sleep(0.5)`, asserting `> 0` generated tokens — the JIT slowdown pushes the first decode past the abort window. #41316 was opened to revert #40376 over this; this PR removes the underlying gap without reverting. The V2 model runner already covers the equivalent in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py` (`SamplingParams.for_sampler_warmup`); V1 was missing it.

## Test Result

### Functional

Hardware: 1xB200

**`tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py::test_multi_abort`:**

```
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py::test_multi_abort -v
```

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Before fix, default (`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1`)             | 2/2 FAIL |
| Before fix, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`                       | 2/2 PASS |
| Before fix, default + `asyncio.sleep` raised from `0.5` to `2.0`  | 2/2 PASS |
| **After fix, default**                                            | **2/2 PASS** |

The bisect isolates the regression to cold-start of the `forward_native` Triton sampling kernels: a longer sleep masks it, and this fix pays it at engine init time instead.

title: [Nixl][PD] Lease renewal TTL KV blocks on P
author: NickLucche
body:
This PR implements a KV Cache lease renewal mechanism for optimizing the time of remote blocks retention.
The effort is described in more details here https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i-O6kqY7WfF1lPyyftRpCQt5fwnFYIEDZKCxyB51Sjg/edit?usp=sharing.

TL;DR: `VLLM_NIXL_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` single timeout is too simple and leads to P holding requests for too long when D crashes. 
We need a more dynamic TTL “lease renewal” system that minimizes the time blocks are stranded on P.
At the same time, we also need a way for D to extend TTL of requests blocks in P that are currently in the waiting queue.
This ensures traffic surges on D do not lead to blocks “early-free” due to congestion

## Test with

```
 --kv-transfer-config '{
