title: [Kernel][ROCm] Native W4A16 kernel for AMD RDNA3 (gfx1100) — fp16 + bf16
author: JartX
body:
Motivation

This work was driven by a concrete production problem: on RDNA3 the only fast W4A16 path was ExLlama, which is fp16-only, and casting bf16-trained models down to fp16 introduces numerical instability. Modern model families (Qwen2/Qwen3, Qwen3-Coder, Llama 3.x, Mistral, etc.) are trained and released in bf16; their weight ranges and activation magnitudes routinely exceed fp16's ±65504 dynamic range, producing inf/NaN propagation, silently degraded outputs, and garbled tool-calling / structured-output generations under load. The Triton W4A16 kernel does support bf16, but at ~82 tk/s it's roughly 3× slower than ExLlama fp16, forcing users into a "fast but numerically wrong" vs "correct but unusably slow" trade-off.

This PR removes that trade-off: native bf16 W4A16 at 205–345 tk/s (2.5–4.2× faster than Triton bf16), plus a fp16 path that beats ExLlama by 6–17% for users who don't need bf16. Models stay in their native bf16 dtype, no manual casts, no quality regression.

Summary

Adds a native HIP W4A16 kernel for AMD RDNA3 (gfx1100/1101/1102 — RX 7900 XT/XTX class), registered as RDNA3W4A16LinearKernel ahead of the Triton kernel on the ROCm priority list. Falls through gracefully on non-RDNA3 ROCm devices (CDNA / MI300) via can_implement() gating on vllm.platforms.rocm.on_gfx11().

Two compute paths share a single torch.ops._C.gptq_gemm_rdna3 entry (all dispatch in C++ to keep apply_weights torch.compile-friendly):

  • Scalar dot-product kernel for decode and any M < 16. fp16 uses v_dot2_f32_f16 (__builtin_amdgcn_fdot2); bf16 widens to fp32 to sidestep the missing v_pk_fma_bf16 on gfx11.
  • v_wmma_f32_16x16x16 kernel for bf16 prefill / batched (M ≥ 16). Two variants share a launcher: v1 (1 wave/block, 16M×16N tile) for M < 32, v2 (2 waves/block, 32M×16N tile, double-buffered LDS) for M ≥ 32.

The full architecture write-up, fragment-layout discussion, lessons learned (including reverted experiments) and bench commands live in csrc/quantization/gptq/README_RDNA3.md.

No open PR adds a native HIP W4A16 kernel for RDNA3. ExLlama (fp16-only) and Triton W4A16 are the existing options on ROCm; this kernel beats both at every concurrency tested and adds bf16 support that ExLlama lacks.

Note: Also can load **AWQ** Like cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-9B-AWQ-BF16-INT4 or cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-9B-AWQ-INT4

End-to-end performance

All benchmarks run with evalscope perf openqa against vLLM serving Qwen3.6-27B-GPTQ-W4A16-G32 on RX 7900 XTX, tp=2, 50 requests, concurrency 100, output ~1800 tok.

Summary table (Qwen3.6-27B-GPTQ-W4A16-G32)

Kernel | dtype | max-num-seqs=8 | max-num-seqs=32 -- | -- | -- | -- Triton W4A16 | bf16 | 82.4 tk/s | — Triton W4A16 | fp16 | 83.2 tk/s | — ExLlama (no bf16) | fp16 | 255.0 tk/s | 382.5 tk/s RDNA3 W4A16 (this PR) | bf16 | 205.3 tk/s | 345.6 tk/s RDNA3 W4A16 (this PR) | fp16 | 270.2 tk/s | 445.7 tk/s

Common evalscope client command

evalscope perf \
  --url "http://127.0.0.1/v1/chat/completions" \
  --parallel 100 \
  --model INCCODER \
  --number 50 \
  --api openai \
  --dataset openqa \
  --stream

12 files changed, +2820 / 0 lines.

Test plan

  • [x] Build the C++ extension in a ROCm container (gfx1100 target): 
    uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
  • [x] Correctness — gptq_gemm_rdna3_wmma_probe op confirms mode-1 fragment layout with random-A.
  • [x] Correctness — v1 vs v2 kernel parity check across multiple shapes / M / dtype: 
    # max abs diff between v1 and v2 outputs is at numerical-rounding level# across {M=32..2048, K=N ∈ {4096, 5120, 11008}, fp16 / bf16}
  • [x] Microbench M-sweep (csrc/quantization/gptq/tools/bench_prefill_msweep.py) over the 5 Qwen-class shapes confirms expected behaviour: WMMA bf16 wins at M ≥ 16, scalar fp16 stays competitive across all M, v2 saves 5–7% vs v1 at M ≥ 64.
  • [x] End-to-end evalscope perf openqa against vllm serve on RX 7900 XTX, tp=2 — numbers in the table above.
  • [x] Verified the kernel does NOT regress decode-only configs: pre-PR ExLlama fp16 baselines reproduced when the kernel is disabled via VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=RDNA3W4A16LinearKernel.
  • [x] VGPR / spill audit (gfx1100 .note.AMDGPU.metadata static analysis): bf16 M_COUNT=8 went from 192-VGPR cap with 144 spilled to scratch → 130 VGPR / 0 spill. fp16 path register-clean throughout. WMMA v1/v2 both 43–44 VGPR.

Hardware tested

  • AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, 96 CUs, 24 GB)
  • ROCm runtime: rocm-X series (hipcc 7.2.1)
  • Model: Qwen3.6-27B-GPTQ-W4A16-G32 (group_size=32)
  • vLLM serving config: --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching (full flags in README)

The kernel is gated to gfx11 only; CDNA / MI3xx / RDNA4 fall through to TritonW4A16LinearKernel automatically.

Out of scope (tracked in README "Known limitations")

  • fp16 → WMMA dispatch: tested end-to-end, was a wash with scalar+fdot2 (445.7 vs 440.7 tk/s, within run-to-run variance) despite a 47% kernel microbench advantage. Dispatch stays bf16-only; the standalone WMMA op remains callable for fp16 if a future workload benefits.
  • Multi-wave WMMA with LDS-shared A (not just B). Realistic 10–15% more on bf16 prefill but a significantly bigger rewrite.
  • fp16 → fp32-output-buffer experiment: untested.
  • rocprof returns 0 for most counters on gfx1100 (only SQ_BUSY_CYCLES and SQ_WAVES work in practice on rocprofv3) — limits diagnostic depth.

title: Add Medusa speculative decoding e2e test
author: puririshi98
body:
## Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  Add an e2e test for Medusa speculative decoding in v1. Medusa is the only                                                                                                                                                                         
  spec decode proposer in vLLM v1 without any functional test coverage —                                                                                                                                                                            
  EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP, NGram, Suffix, Draft Model, and Hidden State Extraction                                                                                                                                                                       
  all have existing e2e tests.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  The Medusa code path has unique logic for hidden state extraction that is                                                                                                                                                                         
  completely disjoint from the other proposers. Without a test, regressions                                                                                                                                                                         
  in this path go undetected.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  ## Changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  Adds `test_medusa_correctness` to `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py`,                                                                                                                                                                 
  inserted after `test_eagle_correctness_heavy` and before `test_mtp_correctness`.                                                                                                                                                                  
  Uses tiny models (`JackFram/llama-68m` + `abhigoyal/vllm-medusa-llama-68m-random`)                                                                                                                                                                
  already registered in `tests/models/registry.py`. Runs in ~18 seconds, <1 GB VRAM.                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  ## Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  Rebase of #36911 (authored by @ojhaanshika) onto current main. The only change                                                                                                                                                                    
  from the original is the file path: `tests/v1/e2e/test_spec_decode.py` was

title: [XPU][MoE] Add WNA16 oracle backend for GPTQ sym-int4 (xpu_fused_moe)
author: jasonboukheir
body:
## Summary

Adds a working W4A16 (INT4 weights, FP16 activations) MoE path for Intel XPU, routing through `vllm-xpu-kernels`'s `fused_moe_interface.xpu_fused_moe(is_int4=True)`. Part of [RFC #33214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33214) — the XPU off-IPEX migration to `vllm-xpu-kernels`. This is the W4A16 MoE milestone; pairs with the existing `INCXPULinearMethod` to give end-to-end attention + MoE on Intel GPUs without IPEX.

AI assistance was used to draft this PR; the submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests below.

## Commits

1. `xpu_moe: add XPUExpertsWNA16 wired to xpu_fused_moe(is_int4=True)` — new `XPUExperts` subclass with `is_int4=True`; pure addition.
2. `xpu_moe: register WNA16MoEBackend.XPU in the int_wna16 oracle` — adds the `WNA16MoEBackend.XPU` enum, the `XPU` branch in `_get_priority_backends()`/`backend_to_kernel_cls`/`make_wna16_moe_kernel`/`convert_to_wna16_moe_kernel_format`, plus a `_process_weights_xpu` helper. Pure addition; the Marlin paths are untouched.
3. `inc: add INCXPUMoEMethod for W4A16 sym int4 MoE on XPU` — new `INCXPUMoEMethod(FusedMoEMethodBase)` companion to `INCXPULinearMethod`. Loads GPTQ-format MoE checkpoints (`[E, K/8, 2N]` int32) and repacks them in `process_weights_after_loading` to the `[E, 2N, K/2]` uint8 layout the XPU kernel wants. `apply_xpu_w4a16_quant_layer` returns it for `FusedMoE` layers.
4. `inc: parse GPTQModel \`dynamic\` field into extra_config` — GPTQModel checkpoints (e.g. Qwen3.6-A3B GPTQ-Int4) put per-module overrides under `dynamic` (`-:<regex>` skip / `+:<regex>` override) instead of `extra_config`. Translates them into INC's existing `extra_config` regex path so `get_layer_config()` works unchanged.
5. `inc: auto-claim vanilla GPTQ sym int4 on XPU` — extends `override_quantization_method` so on XPU only, vanilla GPTQ sym-int4 desc_act=false checkpoints (which `gptq_marlin`/`awq_marlin` decline because they gate on CUDA/CPU, and which `moe_wna16` can't run because its Triton kernels don't execute on Intel GPUs) get claimed by INC. **This is the only behaviour change in the PR**; if reviewers prefer gated/explicit opt-in, this commit can be dropped and the rest of the PR still works.

## Layout note

GPTQ MoE checkpoints store weights as `[E, K/8, 2N]` int32 with sequential int4 nibbles along the input dim. `xpu_fused_moe(is_int4=True)` wants `[E, 2N, K/2]` uint8. The conversion is `transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(torch.uint8)` — no Python-side nibble shuffling. The kernel converts uint4b8 → s4 internally via `implement_zp`, so symmetric int4 zero points are handled in the kernel and we don't need to materialize qzeros.

`XPUExpertsWNA16` is currently routed only by INC. The `WNA16MoEBackend.XPU` oracle entry is generic, so future XPU quant methods (AutoRound, compressed_tensors, etc.) can plug into the same backend.

## Empirical validation

Tested against `palmfuture/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4` on an Intel Arc Pro B70 (24 GiB):

- Model resident: 20.15 GiB
- KV cache headroom: ~251 k tokens (FP16; with `turboquant_k3v4_nc` on a separate branch it scales further — not part of this PR)
- Decode throughput, single stream:
    - Eager: ~28 tok/s
    - `torch.compile` + XPU graph capture: ~58 tok/s (matches llama.cpp Q4_K_M's hand-tuned SYCL pipeline on the same model + GPU)

Numbers from the published GHCR image; full investigation in our internal perf notes.

## Test plan

- [x] All 5 commits cherry-pick clean onto `upstream/main` with DCO sign-off.
- [x] Static review of imports and the diff against the current upstream tree (`kInt4Static`, `kInt4StaticGroupScale`, `FusedMoEMethodBase`, `int4_w4a16_moe_quant_config`, `FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported`, `select_wna16_moe_backend`, `make_wna16_moe_kernel`, `convert_to_wna16_moe_kernel_format` all resolve).
- [x] End-to-end inference run on Arc Pro B70 against `palmfuture/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4`: model loads, generates coherent text, sustains the throughput numbers above.
- [ ] Pre-commit / CI on this PR (will run automatically on push).

Reviewers: @yiliu30 — given your work on `INCXPULinearMethod` (#37986) and the in-flight INC refactor (#40601), curious whether you'd prefer this MoE method live in the new `inc/schemes/` package layout from #40601 once that lands. Happy to rebase or split.

🤖 AI assistance disclosure: drafted with Claude (Anthropic).

title: [DSv4] Improved fused Indexer Q quant kernel
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Purpose

Replace `_fused_indexer_q_rope_mxfp4_kernel` Triton kernel with a CuteDSL version to utilize 256-bit loads. Initially I wrote this in CUDA C++, but couldn't build vLLM from source, so asked Codex to port it over to CuteDSL. Hopefully this will be the first of many CuteDSL kernels to come in vLLM.

Update: I keep the original Triton implementation for fallback (potentially for ROCm). Also put CuteDSL kernel in a separate file and add import guards for platform doesn't have CuteDSL.

### Microbenchmarks

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
import torch

from vllm.v1.attention.ops.deepseek_v4_ops.fused_indexer_q import (
    fused_indexer_q_rope_quant,
)
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
import statistics

NUM_HEADS = 64
HEAD_DIM = 128
ROPE_DIM = 64
MAX_POS = 100_000
TOKENS = [1, 8, 32, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384]
ROPE_DTYPE = torch.float32


def make_inputs(num_tokens: int):
    positions = torch.randint(MAX_POS, (num_tokens,), dtype=torch.int64)
    query = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    cos_sin_cache = torch.randn(MAX_POS, ROPE_DIM, dtype=ROPE_DTYPE)
    weights = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    return (
        positions,
        query,
        cos_sin_cache,
        weights,
        HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
        NUM_HEADS**-0.5,
        True,
    )


def benchmark(num_tokens: int):
    torch.set_default_device("cuda")

    kernel_args = make_inputs(num_tokens)
    timings = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(lambda: fused_indexer_q_rope_quant(*kernel_args))
    median_ms = statistics.median(timings)

    bytes_per_token = 8  # position int64
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * HEAD_DIM * 2  # q in bf16
    bytes_per_token += ROPE_DIM * torch.empty((), dtype=ROPE_DTYPE).element_size()
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * 2  # weights in bf16
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * HEAD_DIM // 2  # q out fp4
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * HEAD_DIM // 32  # q_scale uint8
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * 4  # weights out fp32
    total_bytes = bytes_per_token * num_tokens

    return median_ms, total_bytes


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for num_tokens in TOKENS:
        median_ms, moved_bytes = benchmark(num_tokens)
        bandwidth_gb_s = moved_bytes / (median_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-9
        print(
            f"T={num_tokens:6d}  "
            f"{median_ms * 1e3:7.2f} us  "
            f"BW {bandwidth_gb_s:7.1f} GB/s  "
        )
```

</details>

Result on GB200

Couldn't quite get to SOL yet (8TB/s), but still should be a good improvement for now.

author: ymoslem
body:
Added a new function to process a custom audio dataset for ASR benchmarking.

## Purpose

This PR adds support for benchmarking ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) models using a custom local dataset. It introduces:

- `process_audio()`: a utility function that normalizes audio inputs from:
  - file paths (via `soundfile`); 
  - HuggingFace-style dicts `{"array": ..., "sampling_rate": ...}`; or

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix ROCm LoRA Transformers fallback with full CUDA graphs
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
Fixes `LoRA %N`

- Restrict the gfx950 `wvSplitKrc` skinny GEMM path to 2D activations.
- Make the vLLM C RMSNorm provider flatten N-D activations by token row and reshape back.
- Initialize torch-compile support on the actual HF decoder instance for dynamic remote-code classes.

The original failure was `Unsupported N value: 512,2048,1` in `wvSplitKrc`. The selector counted flattened tokens from a 3D Transformers activation, but `wvSplitKrc` reads `size(0)` and is only correct for 2D row-major inputs. After fixing that selector bug, full decode graph capture exposed the same N-D activation mismatch in the `vllm_c` RMSNorm provider. Flattening RMSNorm inputs matches its row-wise kernel contract and preserves the public tensor shape.

- Known-good commit: `0e39202ca911319c7747a2f9d5a0c162fdff4fd9`.
- Failing commit observed in CI: `7845379230c48c9103ab71682ee05977dfbbdfce`.
- The likely trigger is the update to transformers v5

cc @kenroche

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] IMA in causal_conv1d kernel for long sequences
author: Flink-ddd
body: ## Purpose Fixes #40905 When running Mamba-based models (Mamba/Jamba) with ultra-long sequences (verified at 1.4M tokens), the _causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel triggers a CUDA Illegal Memory Access (IMA). The root cause is an integer overflow in the Triton kernel's pointer offset calculation. Specifically, expressions like token_offset stride and sequence_start_index stride exceed the int32 limit (~2.1B) when the sequence length and feature dimensions are large enough. This PR promotes these index and offset variables to tl.int64 before multiplication and pointer addition to ensure correct 64-bit memory addressing. ## Test Plan 1. Verified locally on NVIDIA H100 (80GB) using state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf. Reproduction Settings: - Model: mamba-130m-hf - Sequence Length: 1,399,013 tokens - Mode: Enforce Eager 2. Performance: Throughput benchmarks for mamba-130m and mamba-2.8b models in both Eager and Non-Eager modes. ## Test Result 1. Before Fix (Reproduction of IMA) In the original environment, running the reproduction script with 1,399,013 tokens triggered a CUDA Illegal Memory Access (IMA) during the prefill stage. The asynchronous nature of CUDA caused the subsequent cublasGemmEx call to fail. ``` (EngineCore pid=9071) RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED when calling `cublasGemmEx( handle, opa, opb, m, n, k, &falpha, a, CUDA_R_16BF, lda, b, CUDA_R_16BF, ldb, &fbeta, c, std::is_same_v ? CUDA_R_32F : CUDA_R_16BF, ldc, compute_type, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP)` ... [Stack Trace] ... (EngineCore pid=9071) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered (EngineCore pid=9071) Search for `cudaErrorIllegalAddress' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information. title: [EC Connector] Non blocking EC Connector lookup
author: omerpaz95
body:
##  Purpose
Introduce a non-blocking deferral mechanism for EC connector lookups in scheduler. 
I added ensure_cache_available() API to ECConnectorBase that the scheduler can poll in a non-invasive way. 
When a waiting request has multimodal features whose encoder cache is still being staged (e.g., remote → CPU prefetch in progress), the scheduler now skips the request for the current step and re-queues it in step_skipped_waiting, allowing other requests to proceed. Once the prefetch completes, the request is picked up on a subsequent step and scheduled normally.

title: [EPLB] Nixl communicator optimization. Zero-copy transfers
author: ilmarkov
body:
## Purpose
Follow-up to #40013. This PR eliminates all intermediate send/recv buffers in NixlEplbCommunicator by implementing zero-copy RDMA transfers.

Instead of copying expert weights into a send buffer and reading into a recv buffer, we now register the model's expert_weights (all layers) directly as NIXL send sources and a pre-allocated expert_buffer as the receive destination. Peers pull data directly from the source weights via one-sided RDMA READs. No intermediate copies needed.

Key changes:

- Zero-copy transfers: NixlEplbCommunicator registers all expert_weights and expert_buffer with NIXL at init. 
- New set_transfer_context method: Provides per-layer transfer context (old_indices, layer_idx) before add_recv calls, enabling immediate READ initiation.
- Test fixes: Fixed pre-existing bugs in test_eplb_fused_moe_layer.py and test_eplb_fused_moe_layer_dep_nvfp4.py (missing communicator argument).

## Validation

```
export VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP8=0
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 --no-enable-prefix-caching -tp 1 -dp 8 \
--max-num-seqs 256 --enable-expert-parallel --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 --max-model-len 4096 --async-scheduling \
--disable-nccl-for-dp-synchronization --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
--enable-eplb --eplb-config.window_size 10 --eplb-config.step_interval 100 --eplb-config.num_redundant_experts 16 \
--eplb-config.log_balancedness_interval 128 --eplb-config.log_balancedness false --eplb-config.use_async false \
--eplb-config.communicator nixl
```

gsm8k:

title: [Perf] Use numpy zero-copy path for embedding float response serialization
author: lokashrinav
body:
## Summary

When `encoding_format=float` and `ORJSONResponse` is active, the `/v1/embeddings` response builder currently calls `.tolist()` on each embedding tensor, converting every float individually through Python. This PR replaces that with a zero-copy `.numpy()` view that ORJSON serializes natively.

**Scope:** Only the float-format OpenAI embedding response path is changed. Base64, bytes, Cohere, non-ORJSON fallback, model execution, scheduling, and KV cache are untouched.

**Fallback:** If `.numpy()` fails (bfloat16, float8, CUDA tensors), it falls back to the existing `.tolist()` path.

## Benchmark results (Modal, T4 GPU, vLLM 0.20.1, intfloat/multilingual-e5-small)

Response construction microbenchmark (batch=128):

| Embedding dim | `.tolist()` (ms) | `.numpy()` (ms) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 384 | 1.43 | 0.21 | **6.8x** |
| 768 | 3.97 | 0.22 | **18.2x** |
| 1536 | 8.67 | 0.22 | **39.9x** |
| 3072 | 14.63 | 0.21 | **68.8x** |

The new path is O(1) (zero-copy view) vs O(batch × dim) for `.tolist()`.

## E2E validation

Tested on Modal (T4, vLLM 0.20.1 with patch applied):
- Single and batch `/v1/embeddings` requests with `encoding_format=float` ✓
- `encoding_format=base64` (unchanged path) ✓
- `EmbeddingResponse.model_validate()` on fast-path output ✓
- Float vs base64 cross-check (values match within tolerance) ✓
- Latency (batch-16): p50=26.9ms, p95=29.8ms

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `encode_pooling_output_float_or_ndarray` (float32 → ndarray, fallback on TypeError)
- [x] E2E server test with real model (intfloat/multilingual-e5-small, fp16)
- [ ] Upstream CI (`pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_utils.py`)
- [ ] Existing embedding tests pass (`pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py`)

title: [XPU] Fix double-transpose in XPUFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for W8A8 quant method
author: libinta
body:
The XPU FP8 kernel's process_weights_after_loading unconditionally transposed weights, but W8A8 quant methods (modelopt, fp8) already transpose weights via .t() before calling the kernel. This caused a double-transpose, producing incorrect output dimensions and split_with_sizes errors (e.g., QKV split expecting 6144 but getting 4096).

Fix by checking weight contiguity: checkpoint weights are always contiguous [out, in] and need transposing, while pre-transposed weights from W8A8 methods are non-contiguous views and should be left as-is.

Tested with:
- CT W8A16 (RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic): ✅
- ModelOpt W8A8 (nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8): ✅
- ModelOpt W8A8 + FP8 KV cache + Triton attention: ✅

title: Eliminate redundant MoE buffer copies in AITER fused experts (without dependency on AITER changes)
author: amd-mghanimi
body:
Addressing the issues raised in previous PRs. 
It follows the draft PR on this topic here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41020 
We copied ideas from other works, mostly based on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38597 and similar ideas in https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/da318d0c10038cff73d5a6c38c471b9601fccaeb and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41020. 


## Purpose

Eliminate redundant __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer DMA kernel launches from the ROCm AITER fused MoE decode path by passing the caller's output tensor directly as AITER's destination buffer.

On DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 (4x MI355X), this removes 116 copy kernels per decode step and yields a 2.3% per-step improvement (500 us savings), with a secondary benefit from reduced memory bandwidth contention on the custom allreduce.

Based on https://github.com/akii96/vllm/commit/df0f043d0914aacd2f86269329b5ef7879de08b7; on MiniMax M2.5  TP=2 MI355X, ISL/OSL=1000/100, conc=64:
  __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer:  12524 -> 0   events  (elimination)
  Memcpy DtoD:               1307 -> 807 events  (-38%)
  Output throughput:        1512 -> 1572 tok/s   (+4.0%)
  Median TPOT:              33.6 -> 32.2 ms      (-4.2%)

Similar to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38597 it doesn't need AITER to change. We added a condition to check the size and type of data this assignment as well as checking if the tensor is the root of its own storage: `output.data = result` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/rocm_aiter_fused_moe.py`.

The condition in `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl._fused_experts` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py` is strengthened based on https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/da318d0c10038cff73d5a6c38c471b9601fccaeb and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38597.

# [MM][CG] Support encoder CUDA graphs for Step3-VL

## Summary

This PR adds image-only encoder CUDA Graph support for Step3-VL / StepVL models.

The implementation:

- wires Step3-VL / StepVL into the existing encoder CUDA Graph framework
- adds Step3-specific auto token budgets based on image and patch feature sizes
- limits Step3-VL / StepVL encoder CUDA Graph capture to `max_batch_size=1`
- falls back to eager execution for unsupported runtime inputs such as precomputed `image_embeds`
- includes encoder CUDA Graph memory in CUDA graph memory profiling
- adds Step3-VL e2e coverage that verifies actual encoder CUDA Graph hits

Video input is not supported for Step3-VL / StepVL in this PR.

## Duplicate / Overlap Check

- Checked `#38175`. Step3-VL is not covered by an open or merged CUDA Graph PR.

- `#38040` addresses a generic max-batch / budget invariant. This PR does not replace it. Step3-VL / StepVL use a model-specific `auto_max_batch_size=1` and reject larger capture batches.
- `#41234` is a draft encoder CUDA Graph interface refactor. This PR may need rebase if that lands first.

title: [Spec Decode] Add Gemma4 MTP speculative decoding support
author: lucianommartins
body:
## Purpose

Add Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding support for Gemma 4 assistant models. This enables draft-based speculative decoding for all Gemma 4 model variants (E2B, E4B, 26B-A4B, 31B) using their corresponding assistant checkpoints.

The Gemma 4 assistant is a lightweight decoder with Q-only attention layers that share KV cache with the target model. It supports an optional centroids masking optimization (enabled automatically for E2B/E4B assistants) that reduces the lm_head computation from ~262K to ~4K candidate tokens via learned centroid-based vocabulary selection.

Key features:

- New `Gemma4MTP` model and `Gemma4Proposer` for Gemma 4 MTP speculative decoding
- Centroids masking with CUDA graph acceleration for E2B/E4B assistant models
- Cross-model KV sharing with multi-group attention support (sliding + full attention with heterogeneous head dimensions)
- TP>1 support via all-gather of sharded lm_head weight for centroids path
- Override `_create_draft_vllm_config` to preserve TRITON_ATTN backend for draft layers (required for KV-shared cache compatibility)

## Test Plan

### Correctness (offline inference)

```bash
# E2B with centroids masking (TP=1)
python -c "
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('google/gemma-4-E2B-it')
prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is 2+2? Answer in one word.'}],
    tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True,
)
llm = LLM(
    model='google/gemma-4-E2B-it',
    speculative_config={'model': 'google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant', 'num_speculative_tokens': 2},
    trust_remote_code=True,
    max_model_len=1024,
)
out = llm.generate([prompt], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=32))
print('OUTPUT:', out[0].outputs[0].text)
"

# 26B without centroids masking (TP=2)
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python -c "
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it')
prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is 2+2? Answer in one word.'}],
    tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True,
)
llm = LLM(
    model='google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it',
    speculative_config={'model': 'google/gemma-4-26B-it-assistant', 'num_speculative_tokens': 2},
    tensor_parallel_size=2,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    max_model_len=1024,
)
out = llm.generate([prompt], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=32))
print('OUTPUT:', out[0].outputs[0].text)
"
```

### Performance (SPEED-Bench, 880 requests, temperature=0, concurrency=1)

Tested on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB and H100 servers with `specdec_bench` (qualitative dataset, output_length=4096).

## Test Result

### Correctness

All models produce correct output (`Four`) with speculative decoding enabled.

Engine logs confirm:
- `Gemma4 MTP: centroids masking enabled (num_centroids=2048, top_k=32, active_tokens=4096/262144).` — for E2B/E4B
- `Gemma4 MTP: keeping draft model's own lm_head (draft_dim != backbone_dim).` — lm_head preserved
- `Gemma4 MTP: captured centroids CUDA graphs for sizes [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64].` — CUDA graph acceleration
- `Gemma4 MTP: draft layer N (type) -> target_layer.self_attn.attn` — KV sharing wired

### Performance (H100, concurrency=1)

| Model | γ | Output TPS | Speedup vs Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| E2B | baseline | 266.5 | 100% |
| E2B | γ=2 | 347.7 | 130% |
| E4B | baseline | 171.0 | 100% |
| E4B | γ=4 | 304.7 | 178% |
| 26B | baseline | 169.2 | 100% |
| 26B | γ=4 | 270.2 | 160% |
| 31B | baseline | 42.6 | 100% |
| 31B | γ=8 | 135.9 | 319% |

### Performance scaling with batch size (H100, 26B, 150 requests)

| γ | Batch=1 | Batch=4 | Batch=16 | Batch=32 | Batch=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| γ=2 | 136% | 128% | 152% | 158% | 176% |
| γ=4 | 160% | 163% | 204% | 219% | 227% |

### Files changed

- `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mtp.py` — New model: Q-only attention, centroids masking, sparse argmax
- `vllm/v1/spec_decode/gemma4.py` — New proposer: KV sharing, CUDA graph centroids, multi-group attention
- `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py` — Extract `_update_positions_dependent_metadata`, add `constant_draft_positions` caching
- `vllm/config/speculative.py` — Register `gemma4_mtp` type, `hf_config_override`, `use_gemma4_mtp()`
- `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` — Register `Gemma4MTPModel`
- `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py` — `get_hidden_size` returns `backbone_hidden_size`

title: [ROCm] mori: add InterNodeV1LL inter-node kernel selection via VLLM_MORI_INTERNODE_KERNEL
author: jatseng-ai
body:
## Summary

This PR adds support for selecting the `InterNodeV1LL` inter-node kernel in the MoRI EP all2all backend via a new environment variable `VLLM_MORI_INTERNODE_KERNEL`.

## Background

MoRI exposes five kernel types for EP dispatch/combine via `EpDispatchCombineKernelType`:

| Kernel | Value | Characteristic |
|---|---|---|
| `IntraNode` | 0 | Single-node XGMI P2P |
| `InterNode` | 1 | Multi-node baseline |
| `InterNodeV1` | 2 | Multi-node, previous default |
| `InterNodeV1LL` | **3** | **Multi-node, recommended** |
| `AsyncLL` | 4 | Multi-node, async pipelined |

`InterNodeV1LL` was added to MoRI in [this commit](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/commit/0cbdef2890a4e7f18a9b9d30646c5d8d15305a59) and is present in all public MoRI releases (v0.1.0+). The MoRI README at the [pinned commit](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/tree/2d02c6a9841a80bc8656a9f5c73019ffea76b9b3) includes benchmark numbers for `InterNodeV1LL`, but vLLM hardcodes `InterNodeV1` in `_make_all2all_kwargs`, making `InterNodeV1LL` completely unreachable from vLLM — see [all2all.py at the pinned commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7d6917bef552d6aff70142ab9fb8af648081d4db/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py#L818).

## Why `InterNodeV1LL` matters

Despite its "low latency" naming, benchmarks on MI300X multi-node clusters (RoCE v2) show `InterNodeV1LL` significantly outperforms `InterNodeV1` on **dispatch throughput** as well — not just latency. Dispatch bandwidth is roughly **2x higher** with `InterNodeV1LL`, matching the numbers shown in the MoRI README. `InterNodeV1LL` should therefore be considered the preferred kernel for general multi-node EP, not only for latency-sensitive scenarios.

This gap went unnoticed because `InterNodeV1LL` was never exposed in vLLM; users had no way to select it.

## Changes

**`vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py`**
- In `MoriAll2AllManager._make_all2all_kwargs`: replace the hardcoded `InterNodeV1` with a conditional on `VLLM_MORI_INTERNODE_KERNEL`. Defaults to `"V1"` (no regression for existing deployments).

**`vllm/envs.py`**
- Add `VLLM_MORI_INTERNODE_KERNEL: str = "V1"` with type annotation and lambda resolver.

## Usage

```bash
# Previous behaviour preserved (default)
VLLM_ALL2ALL_BACKEND=mori vllm serve ...

# Recommended for multi-node EP (~2x dispatch throughput on MI300X w/ RoCE v2)
VLLM_ALL2ALL_BACKEND=mori VLLM_MORI_INTERNODE_KERNEL=V1LL vllm serve ...
```

## Testing

- [x] Single-node EP path unchanged (IntraNode kernel unaffected)
- [x] Default multi-node behaviour unchanged (`VLLM_MORI_INTERNODE_KERNEL` defaults to `"V1"`)
- [x] `V1LL` validated on MI300X multi-node (RoCE v2) — dispatch bandwidth matches MoRI README benchmarks and ~2x vs `V1`

body:
## Purpose
Allow server to start up when speculative decoding with parallel drafting is enabled for multimodal models like Gemma-4 

Previously, `_raise_if_multimodal()` unconditionally blocked parallel drafting for any model registered as multimodal, even when only text inference was needed. This change downgrades the hard error to a warning (`_warn_if_multimodal()`), enabling models like `google/gemma-4-31B-it` to use EAGLE3 with parallel drafting for text generation.

## Test Plan
```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-model-len 131072 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3", "model":"/path/to/eagle-draft-model", "num_speculative_tokens":5, "parallel_drafting": true}' 
```

## Test Result
Server starts successfully and serves requests with EAGLE3 parallel drafting

title: [ROCm] Add XGMI backend for MoRI Connector
author: simondanielsson
body:
## Purpose

Part of https://github.com/vllm-project/router/issues/142

This PR adds the option to run MoRI with the XGMI backend using `"kv_connector_extra_config": {"backend": "xgmi"}`. This allows for running PD disagg with MoRI in CI on a single node, without having RDMA drivers installed.

Long term we aim for also adding multi-node tests using the RDMA backend. However this requires https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40453 and provisioning the appropriate AMD HW CI resources.

- For instance, we can directly add MoRI to the vllm-router CI using this backend: see https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/164, without worrying about installing RDMA userspace libraries for the NICs used by the CI machines etc. Without this, you will get an error if you run MoRI in an environment without the correct RDMA userspace libs are installed (i.e. in the official `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` image), triggered by MoRI's `RdmaBackend`. 
- **NB:** all devices must be visible to all vLLM instances for MoRI to be able to establish XGMI sessions between P and D instances. E.g. in 1p1d this requires setting `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7` , and `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3` on P and D, respectively. If running in separate dockers, `--pid host` is also required.

Related to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35165

## Test Plan

1. Run 1P1D on single 8xMI300 node

```shell
# build image in this branch, or simply grab the one I built:
docker pull ghcr.io/simondanielsson/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.20.1-xgmi
# or 
docker build \
  -f docker/Dockerfile.rocm \
  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=rocm/vllm-dev:base \
  -t ghcr.io/simondanielsson/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.20.1-xgmi \
  .

# Launch router
docker run \
  --name vllm-router \
  --network host \
  --rm \
  vllm/vllm-router:nightly-20260507-e667ebb \
  vllm-router \
  --vllm-pd-disaggregation \
  --kv-connector moriio \
  --vllm-discovery-address "0.0.0.0:36367" \
  --policy consistent_hash \
  --prefill-policy consistent_hash \
  --decode-policy consistent_hash


# P instance w/ XGMI backend. All devices must be visible for MoRI to establish sessions with D instance GPUs
# Main new env var is `VLLM_MORIIO_BACKEND=xgmi`
# --pid host required for shared PID namespace between P and D
docker run \
  --rm \
  --name moriio-prefill \
  --init --network host --ipc host --privileged \
  --pid host \
  --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \
  --shm-size 256G \
  --group-add video --group-add render \
  --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --device /dev/infiniband \
  -v /sys:/sys \
  -v "${HOME}/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
  -e HF_HOME=/root/.cache/huggingface \
  -e HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=0 \
  -e HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
  -e VLLM_MORIIO_CONNECTOR_READ_MODE=1 \
  -e MORI_IO_ENABLE_NOTIFICATION=0 \
  -e NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112 \
  -e NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=ens51np0 \
  -e VLLM_USE_V1=1 \
  -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
  ghcr.io/simondanielsson/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.20.1-xgmi \
  meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \
    --port 8100 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
    --max-model-len 16384 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --enforce-eager \
    --block-size 16 \
    --kv-transfer-config '{
      "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
      "kv_role": "kv_producer",
      "kv_connector_extra_config": {
        "proxy_ip": "localhost",
        "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
        "http_port": "8100",
        "handshake_port": "6301",
        "notify_port": "61005",
        "backend": "xgmi"
      }
    }'

# D instance
docker run \
  --rm \
  --name moriio-decode \
  --init --network host --ipc host --privileged \
  --pid host \
  --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \
  --shm-size 256G \
  --group-add video --group-add render \
  --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --device /dev/infiniband \
  -v /sys:/sys \
  -v "${HOME}/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
  -e HF_HOME=/root/.cache/huggingface \
  -e HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=0 \
  -e VLLM_MORIIO_BACKEND=xgmi \
  -e HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3 \
  -e VLLM_MORIIO_CONNECTOR_READ_MODE=1 \
  -e MORI_IO_ENABLE_NOTIFICATION=0 \
  -e NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112 \
  -e NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=ens51np0 \
  -e VLLM_USE_V1=1 \
  -e VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
  -e VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
  -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
  ghcr.io/simondanielsson/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.20.1-xgmi \
  meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \
    --port 8200 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
    --max-model-len 16384 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --block-size 16 \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"}' \
    --kv-transfer-config '{
      "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
      "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
      "kv_connector_extra_config": {
        "proxy_ip": "localhost",
        "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
        "http_port": "8200",
        "handshake_port": "6401",
        "notify_port": "62005",
        "backend": "xgmi"
      }
    }'
```

Run benchmark and GSM8k:

```shell
docker exec moriio-prefill \
  vllm bench serve \
    --base-url http://localhost:30000 \
    --backend vllm \
    --model meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \

```

title: [Bugfix] Fix GLM4-MoE weight loading for NVFP4 quantized checkpoints
author: s-yanev
body:
## Summary

- Fix k_scale/v_scale remapping inside the stacked_params_mapping loop for NVFP4-quantized GLM4-MoE checkpoints
- Use `getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` for safer fallback to default weight loader
- Use `name_mapped` variable instead of modifying `name` directly to avoid side effects

## Problem

When loading NVFP4-quantized GLM4-MoE models, the weight loader crashes with `KeyError` because:
1. `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name()` is never called for weights processed by the stacked_params_mapping loop
2. `param.weight_loader` is accessed directly without fallback, which can fail for quantized layers

## Fix

Three improvements to `glm4_moe.load_weights()`:

1. **k_scale/v_scale remapping**: Added `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name()` call after name mapping in the stacked loop, ensuring scale tensors are properly remapped before loading.

2. **Safe weight loader access**: Changed from `param.weight_loader` to `getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` with fallback logic.

3. **Variable scoping**: Used `name_mapped` instead of modifying `name` to prevent unintended side effects in the expert_params_mapping loop.

## Difference from PR #34293

This PR addresses the same underlying issue as #34293 but is more comprehensive:

| Aspect | PR #34293 | This PR |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| kv-scale remapping | Before the loop | Inside the loop (after name mapping) |
| Weight loader access | No change | Safe `getattr()` with fallback |
| Variable scoping | No change | Uses `name_mapped` to avoid side effects |
| Lines changed | +4/-0 | +14/-6 |

## Test plan

- [x] Linting passes (ruff, mypy, pre-commit hooks)
- [x] Patch tested on GLM-4.7-NVFP4 checkpoint
- [x] Verify with NVFP4-quantized GLM4-MoE model serving

title: [Quantization] Add ModelOpt NVFP4 W4A16 (4-bit weights, fp16/bf16 activations) support
author: juhi10071998
body:
## Summary

Add native ModelOpt NVFP4 **W4A16** (4-bit NVFP4 weights, fp16/bf16 activations) checkpoint support to vLLM, mirroring the existing FP8 dispatch precedent (`ModelOptFp8Config` selecting between three FP8 LinearMethods on `quant_method`). Checkpoints produced by NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer's W4A16 recipe ([NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#1313](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer/pull/1313)) can now be loaded directly and run through the `marlin_fp4` kernel.

`quant_method="W4A16_NVFP4"` in `hf_quant_config.json` routes to a new `ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod` that registers W4A16 weights/scales, tolerates `input_scale` tensors carried by W4A4 sibling checkpoints (silently ingested-and-discarded), and runs the GEMM through the existing FP4 Marlin kernel adapter. 

**Why I had to create input_scale for this `ModelOptNvfp4W4A16LinearMethod`?**
To consume pure nvfp4 ckpt (even on unsupported architecture) once we have correct routing through CLI (currently we do through manually updating quant_algo NVFP4-> W4A16_NVFP4).
The input scale is needed to avoid keyerror issues in create_weights/ weight loading. For instance in model definition since the if branch has no fall back path if the loaded weight does not have the corresponding key- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/22a3cbe1520bc8a3b19ace0abe497c514b3129ea/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2.py#L485], I feel it may not be trivial to add this to all the models, hence I opted for the approach for creating the placeholder param for input_scales in create_weights so weight loading happens as expected and then remove the param in the process_weights_after_loading function. 


## Validation

### Unit tests (in-tree, this PR)

```
$ pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k "config_dispatches" -v
tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_modelopt_nvfp4_config_dispatches_w4a4_method PASSED [ 50%]
tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_modelopt_nvfp4_config_dispatches_w4a16_method PASSED [100%]
================= 2 passed, 3 deselected, 16 warnings in 2.18s =================
```

The W4A16 test asserts both `is` (positive) and `is not` (against W4A4 sibling), so a regression that silently routed a W4A16 checkpoint through the W4A4 method (calling cutlass W4A4 NVFP4 GEMM with no `input_scale`, instead of FP4 Marlin) would fail loudly.

### End-to-end validation against real W4A16 ckpts (out-of-tree, manual)

We don't have a public W4A16 NVFP4 ckpt to add as an HF-Hub-downloaded integration test (mirroring the FP8 `pc_pt` / `pb_wo` siblings) — see "Test gaps" below. The W4A16 path was instead validated against ModelOpt-generated checkpoints:

**1. Dense (Qwen3-8B), W4A4-recipe ckpt loaded as W4A16 vs native W4A16:** validate the `input_scale` ingest-and-discard path (commit "tolerate input_scale tensors from W4A4 checkpoints") by loading a W4A4 sibling ckpt with `quant_method` rewritten to `W4A16_NVFP4`.

```
=== overall ===
  global max |Δlogprob|       : 0
  argmax-mismatch positions   : 0   (47/47 positions agree, 100% top-K rank match)
  ✅ Logprobs are BIT-IDENTICAL at every position across the top-K.
```

Strongest possible parity result: same on-disk weights+scales, same LinearMethod, same kernel, same KV-cache config → byte-for-byte computation.

### Lint / formatting

```
$ pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py \
                          vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py \
                          tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py
ruff check..........Passed
ruff format.........Passed
typos...............Passed
mypy-3.10...........Passed
SPDX headers........Passed
[all hooks passed]
```

## Test gaps (acknowledged)

- **No public W4A16 NVFP4 checkpoint exists yet** to add an HF-Hub-downloaded integration test mirroring `test_modelopt_fp8_pc_pt_checkpoint_setup` / `test_modelopt_fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`. We'll add that test in a follow-up PR once such a checkpoint is published.

## Follow-up PRs

This PR establishes the load path; two intentionally-deferred follow-ups:

1. **Expose a CLI flag to load W4A4 ckpts through the W4A16 method** — avoids the current manual workaround of rewriting `hf_quant_config.json:quantization.quant_algo` from `"NVFP4"` to `"W4A16_NVFP4"`. The flag would let users opt a W4A4 ckpt into W4A16 inference at load time without modifying the on-disk config. This PR's "tolerate `input_scale` from W4A4 checkpoints" change (commit `ed46c63`) was added specifically to validate that flow ahead of the flag landing — confirmed bit-identical to native W4A16 on Qwen3-8B (case 2 above). Estimated scope: ~30–50 LOC + a new `ModelOptNvFp4W4A16Config` subclass and registry entry.
2. **Extend W4A16 to cover `lm_head`** — vLLM's `ParallelLMHead` does not currently route through a quantization `LinearMethod`, so a quantized `lm_head` in a W4A16 NVFP4 checkpoint is not loadable end-to-end without separate plumbing. Out of scope for this PR; will be addressed once `ParallelLMHead`'s dispatch path is extended.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The submitting human reviewed every changed line, drove the validation runs, and reproduced all test results locally. AI-assistance attribution is in each commit's `Co-authored-by:` trailer. DCO sign-off is in place on every commit.

## Test plan/ unchecked ones are non-gating and could be a follow-up

- [x] Unit tests pass (`pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k config_dispatches -v`)
- [x] Pre-commit clean on touched files
- [x] End-to-end load + generation validated on Qwen3-8B (modelopt-direct vs CT-bridged, argmax-stable)
- [x] End-to-end load + generation validated on Qwen3-8B (W4A4-as-W4A16 vs native W4A16, bit-identical)
- [ ] Public-checkpoint integration test — deferred until a W4A16 NVFP4 ckpt is published to HF Hub
- [ ] CLI flag to route W4A4 ckpts through the W4A16 method — deferred to follow-up PR #1 (see "Follow-up PRs")
- [ ] Quantized `lm_head` end-to-end — gated on `ParallelLMHead` plumbing; deferred to follow-up PR #2

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### Supplementary Changes (3 files, +224 / −6)

- `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py`
    - `ModelOptNvFp4Config.__init__` made fully defaultable (`quant_method: str = "NVFP4"`, etc.) — preserves backward-compatibility for existing direct-instantiation callers under `tests/{compile,distributed,kernels}/...`.
    - Per-algo dispatch: `quant_method="NVFP4"` → existing `ModelOptNvFp4LinearMethod` (W4A4); `quant_method="W4A16_NVFP4"` → new `ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod` (W4A16).
    - New `ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod`: registers `weight` (uint8 packed), `weight_scale` (fp8 group), `weight_scale_2` (fp32 per-tensor), and a placeholder `input_scale` (discarded post-load to absorb tensors found in W4A4-recipe ckpts). `process_weights_after_loading` renames `weight_scale_2 → weight_global_scale` (no reciprocation) and delegates to the existing `MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel` adapter.
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py`
    - Adds `"ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod"` to `WEIGHT_LOADER_V2_SUPPORTED` so fused QKV / gate_up loading dispatches through the V2 loader (required for `PerTensorScaleParameter` handling on stacked layers).
- `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py`
    - Two dispatch unit tests guarding against silent-W4A4-on-W4A16 regression — see "Validation".

title: [KV Connector] Opt DecodeBenchConnector into SupportsHMA
author: liuzijing2014
body:
## Summary

Opt `DecodeBenchConnector` into `SupportsHMA` so decode-only benchmark recipes can run with the hybrid KV cache manager enabled. Without this, users must pass `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, which collapses hybrid-model KV cache groups (SWA / MLA compress=4 / MLA compress=128 / sparse indexer) into a single uniform page size and throws away the compression savings.

Implementation is minimal because this connector is a dummy fill that owns no external per-block state:

- Inherit from `SupportsHMA`.
- Implement `request_finished_all_groups`: same cleanup as the single-group `request_finished` (delegates to `connector_scheduler.request_finished()`); `block_ids` is ignored because there is no per-block external state to release.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `DecodeBenchConnector`, `SupportsHMA`, and `decode_bench_connector` (via the GitHub search API). No PR targets this connector. The closest neighbor, #41644 ("Keep HMA enabled for supported KV connectors"), is orthogonal — it changes the *default* HMA decision in `vllm/config/vllm.py` for connectors that already declare `SupportsHMA`. This PR adds one more connector to that supported set; the two changes compose.

## Test plan

Hardware: 1× node with 4× GB200, single-node DEP=4 (DP=4, EP=4). Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `--load-format dummy` and `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4`. Connector: `DecodeBenchConnector`, HMA explicitly enabled via `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`.

Same `vllm serve` command in both runs:

```
vllm serve <DSv4-Flash> --port 8000 \
  -dp 4 -ep --data-parallel-size-local 4 \
  --load-format dummy --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 32 \
  --block-size 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"fill_mean":0.015,"fill_std":0.02}}'
```

### Without the PR (only difference: `class DecodeBenchConnector(KVConnectorBase_V1)` — no `SupportsHMA` mixin)

Crashes at engine init in `KVConnectorFactory.create_connector_v1()`:

```
ValueError: Connector DecodeBenchConnector does not support HMA but HMA is enabled.
            Please set `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`.
```

All four DP ranks fail identically; the engine cores then exit with `RuntimeError: Worker failed with error '...'`.

### With the PR

Server starts cleanly. HMA is active:

```
INFO ... [deepseek_v4_attention.py:614] Using DeepSeek's fp8_ds_mla KV cache format.
INFO ... [kv_cache_utils.py:1713] GPU KV cache size: 86,928 tokens     (each of 4 ranks)
INFO ...:     Application startup complete.
```

Functional sanity check via `vllm bench serve` (random ISL=4000, OSL=100, 32 prompts, max-concurrency=8):

```

title: [MLA Attention Backend] Add TOKENSPEED_MLA backend for DSR1/Kimi K25 prefill + decode on Blackwell
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose
Wires the tokenspeed_mla CuTe DSL kernels into vLLM as a new MLA backend, covering both prefill (tokenspeed_mla_prefill) and decode (tokenspeed_mla_decode). Targets Blackwell (SM100) with FP8 KV cache and DeepSeek R1 MLA dimensions; 

Enable by adding
```
-ac {\"backend\":\"TOKENSPEED_MLA\",\"mla_prefill_backend\":\"TOKENSPEED_MLA\",\"use_prefill_query_quantization\":true} 
```
To the engine config

This kernel is optimized for decode + MTP usage

Microbenchmark 
## Decode kernel: `tokenspeed_mla_decode` vs `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`

### Constraint

The decode kernel requires `num_heads × q_len ≤ 128`:
- `num_heads=16` → supports MTP-3 to MTP-7 (q_len 4-8)
- `num_heads=32` → supports MTP-3 only (q_len 4)
- `num_heads=64` → supports q_len=1-2 only
- `num_heads=128` → supports q_len=1 only

### MTP-3 (q_len=4), kv_len=80k

**`num_heads=16` (Kimi TP=4):**

| bs | trtllm µs | tokenspeed µs | speedup |
|----:|----------:|--------------:|--------:|
| 1 | 62 | 110 | 0.56× |
| 2 | 61 | 107 | 0.57× |
| 4 | 89 | 112 | 0.79× |
| 8 | 181 | 112 | **1.62×** |
| 16 | 336 | 176 | **1.91×** |
| 32 | 655 | 318 | **2.06×** |
| 64 | 1420 | 610 | **2.33×** ← peak |
| 96 | 2009 | 1137 | 1.77× |
| 128 | 2623 | 1218 | 2.15× |
| 192 | 3925 | 1833 | 2.14× |
| 256 | 4855 | 2693 | 1.80× |
| 384 | 7376 | 4013 | 1.84× |
| 512 | 9689 | 5058 | 1.92× |

**`num_heads=32` (Kimi TP=2 / DSV3 TP=4):**

| bs | trtllm µs | tokenspeed µs | speedup |
|----:|----------:|--------------:|--------:|
| 1 | 67 | 106 | 0.63× |
| 4 | 165 | 110 | **1.50×** |
| 8 | 316 | 110 | **2.87×** |
| 16 | 622 | 188 | **3.31×** |
| 32 | 1323 | 337 | **3.93×** |
| 64 | 2596 | 631 | **4.11×** ← peak |
| 96 | 3739 | 1176 | 3.18× |
| 128 | 4413 | 1286 | 3.43× |
| 192 | 6825 | 1918 | 3.56× |
| 256 | 8817 | 2634 | 3.35× |

### MTP scaling (nh=16, kv=80k)

| MTP | q_len | Crossover bs | Peak speedup | bs at peak |
|----:|------:|-------------:|-------------:|-----------:|
| MTP-3 | 4 | 5 | 2.33× | 64 |
| MTP-4 | 5 | 4 | 3.98× | 32 |
| MTP-5 | 6 | 3 | 3.87× | 32 |
| MTP-6 | 7 | 3 | 3.92× | 32 |
| MTP-7 | 8 | 3 | **4.23×** | 12 |

Higher MTP → earlier crossover and higher peak. Tokenspeed amortizes its launch
overhead better as `q_len` grows.

### Sustained win up to bs=512 (nh=16, kv=80k)

| bs | MTP-3 | MTP-5 | MTP-7 |
|----:|------:|------:|------:|
| 64 | 2.27× | 3.06× | 3.86× |
| 128 | 2.08× | 3.02× | 3.48× |
| 256 | 1.81× | 2.67× | 3.40× |
| 384 | 1.84× | 2.60× | 3.12× |
| 512 | 1.92× | 2.66× | 3.22× |

Once past the crossover, tokenspeed wins consistently — the speedup gradually
erodes from peak but **never returns to parity** through bs=512.

### Cross context-length sweep (q_len=4, nh=32)

| bs | kv=1024 | kv=4096 | kv=16384 | kv=65536 |
|----:|--------:|--------:|---------:|---------:|
| 1 | 0.63× | 0.66× | 0.64× | 0.59× |
| 4 | 0.60× | 0.60× | 0.61× | **1.33×** |
| 16 | 0.59× | 0.60× | **1.35×** | **3.25×** |
| 64 | 0.65× | **1.50×** | **3.62×** | **3.88×** |

KV length amplifies the gap dramatically: tokenspeed scales sub-linearly with
total KV scan, while trtllm scales roughly linearly.

## Prefill kernel: `tokenspeed_mla_prefill` vs `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`

### Short to medium context (BF16, causal, no context)

| num_heads | bs | seq_len | trtllm µs | tokenspeed µs | speedup |
|----:|----:|--------:|----------:|--------------:|--------:|
| 16 | 1 | 256 | 27 | 122 | 0.22× |
| 16 | 1 | 1024 | 27 | 122 | 0.22× |
| 16 | 1 | 4096 | 108 | 195 | 0.55× |
| 16 | 4 | 1024 | 39 | 122 | 0.32× |
| 16 | 8 | 512 | 28 | 120 | 0.23× |
| 32 | 1 | 4096 | 178 | 326 | 0.55× |
| 32 | 8 | 512 | 48 | 207 | 0.23× |
| 64 | 1 | 4096 | 307 | 582 | 0.53× |
| 128 | 1 | 4096 | 553 | 1091 | 0.51× |

Tokenspeed loses 2–5× across all combinations in this regime, driven by ~120 µs
fixed launch overhead vs trtllm's ~27 µs.

### Long context (BF16, causal, no context)

| num_heads | bs | seq_len | trtllm ms | tokenspeed ms | speedup |
|----:|----:|--------:|----------:|--------------:|--------:|
| 16 | 1 | 16384 | 1.00 | 1.24 | 0.80× |
| 16 | 1 | 32768 | 3.48 | 4.60 | 0.76× |
| 16 | 1 | 65536 | 14.82 | 16.29 | 0.91× |
| 16 | 1 | 81920 | 24.57 | 25.13 | **0.98×** |
| 32 | 1 | 65536 | 31.33 | 32.37 | **0.97×** |
| 32 | 1 | 81920 | 47.47 | 49.77 | 0.95× |

At ≥65k context tokenspeed approaches parity. Both kernels become compute-bound
on the KV scan; the launch-overhead gap amortizes away.

### Spec-decode-style (Q ragged short, KV ragged long, non-causal)

`q_len=2/4/8` per request, BF16, nh=16:

| bs | q_len | kv_len | trtllm µs | tokenspeed µs | speedup |
|----:|------:|-------:|----------:|--------------:|--------:|
| 1 | 4 | 4096 | 58 | 131 | 0.44× |
| 1 | 4 | 16384 | 247 | 289 | 0.86× |
| 1 | 4 | 65536 | 963 | 1106 | 0.87× |
| 4 | 4 | 16384 | 258 | 302 | 0.85× |
| 4 | 4 | 65536 | 998 | 1153 | 0.87× |
| 16 | 2 | 16384 | 562 | 621 | **0.91×** |

`q_len` barely matters in this regime (workload is KV-bound). KV length is what
matters: tokenspeed converges to ~0.86-0.91× at ≥16k regardless of `q_len`.

title: fix nixl side-channel host selection
author: shaharmor98
body:
## Summary

Fix NIXL side-channel host selection for Ray data-parallel disaggregated serving.

## Problem

In multi-node Ray DP, Ray actors can inherit `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST` from the driver/head process. 
With NIXL disaggregated serving, worker actors may then bind their NIXL handshake listener to the head-node IP instead of the actor-local Ray node IP.

### Evidence from the failing runs:
  - Prefill worker actor on `10.66.3.118` tried to bind `tcp://10.66.3.116:5604-5607`
  - Decode worker actor on `10.66.3.121` tried to bind `tcp://10.66.3.119:6604-6607`
  - Failure: `zmq.error.ZMQError: Cannot assign requested address`


The side-channel listener was binding to an address that does not exist on the worker node.

## Solution

For Ray data-parallel actors, resolve the NIXL side-channel host from `ray.util.get_node_ip_address()` and use that resolved host both for the listener bind address and for advertised `remote_host` metadata.


*Note: non-Ray DP keeps the existing `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST` behavior.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fix RMSNorm+Quant fusion for gfx950 (non-fnuz)
author: frida-andersson
body:
## Summary

`RocmAiterRMSNormQuantFusionPass` was silently skipping the fused AITER RMSNorm+GroupedQuantFP8 kernel on gfx950 (non-fnuz hardware) due to two issues:

1. **`matcher_utils.py`**: `MatcherQuantFP8` guarded `get_group_quant_op()` behind `is_fp8_fnuz()`. On gfx950 this is `False`, so the matcher always selected `triton_per_token_group_quant_fp8` instead — a different op target that the fusion pattern does not match. Fix: always use `get_group_quant_op()` when `match_rocm_aiter=True`.

2. **`rocm_aiter_fusion.py`**: DSv3.2's FX graph has one RMSNorm node feeding multiple downstream quant ops (fan-out). The pattern matcher requires 1-to-1 norm→quant pairs and silently skips multi-consumer norms. Fix: add `_dedup_and_duplicate_for_fusion()` pre-pass that runs before pattern matching:
   - **Stage 1 — dedup**: collapses identical quant consumers on the same norm (same target + args) into one node.
   - **Stage 2 — duplicate**: clones the norm for each remaining distinct quant consumer so each gets a dedicated 1-to-1 input the pattern matcher can fuse.

## Performance

DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 on MI355X (gfx950), bf16, HIP graphs, block-size 64:

| | ms/step |
|---|---|
| Before | 20.69 |
| After | 20.01 |
| Delta | **-3.3%** |

## Test plan

- DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 bf16 with HIP graphs — GSM8K 5-shot flexible-extract **0.9409** (matches reference)
- Server load test: 32 requests, 0 failures, no MAF
- Depends on: #41760 (correctness fix for DSv3.2 TP4 HIP graphs)

## Notes

Co-authored-by: Markus Hartikainen <markus.hartikainen@amd.com>

## Purpose

Close #41830 — change HMA from opt-in to opt-out for KV transfer connectors.

Previously, `--kv-transfer-config` unconditionally disabled the Hybrid KV Cache Manager (HMA), requiring users to explicitly pass `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` to enable it. Since HMA is now mature enough, this PR reverses the default: HMA stays enabled when the effective connector configuration supports it, and is only auto-disabled for connectors that do not.

For hybrid-attention models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Mixtral, Mamba hybrids), this fixes startup OOM caused by `unify_hybrid_kv_cache_specs` collapsing sliding-window/chunked-local specs into `FullAttentionSpec` and ballooning KV memory allocation.

## Changes

Add `KVConnectorFactory.supports_hma_config()` that resolves effective HMA support from the transfer config:
- Plain connectors: checks `SupportsHMA` on the class.
- MultiConnector: recurses into all configured children — returns True only if every child supports HMA. Empty/missing children → False.

Both the config auto-disable path and the factory runtime check now use this single helper, keeping them consistent. Non-HMA connectors retain the existing auto-disable + warning behavior.

## Related

- [[#29805](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29805)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29805) introduced the unconditional auto-disable
- [[#39269](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39269)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39269) addresses the analogous issue in the `kv_events_config` path; this PR only changes the `kv_transfer_config` path

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hma_auto_config.py -v
```

5 unit tests covering:
- HMA-capable connector (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`) → not auto-disabled
- Non-HMA connector (`ExampleConnector`) → auto-disabled
- Explicit `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` + non-HMA connector → factory raises `ValueError`
- MultiConnector with all HMA children → not auto-disabled
- MultiConnector with mixed HMA/non-HMA children → auto-disabled

Regression coverage across affected test files:

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hma_auto_config.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py \
    -q \
    -k "not multi_example_connector_consistency and not mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache"
```

The two deselected tests require a real distributed environment and are not runnable in a single-process CPU setup.

title: [Bugfix] Zero stale is_prefilling in padded CUDA graph rows for Mamba
author: liulanze
body:
## Purpose

Fix stale `is_prefilling` metadata in padded CUDA graph rows that misclassifies Mamba decode requests as prefills.

After `condense()` compacts active requests, vacated slots retain stale `num_computed_tokens` and `num_prompt_tokens` values. When the batch is padded for CUDA graphs, the comparison `num_computed < num_prompt` can yield `True` for padding rows. Mamba is the only backend that passes `treat_short_extends_as_decodes=False` to `split_decodes_and_prefills`, so these stale `True` values get OR-ed into `is_prefill` and shift the decode/prefill boundary, misclassifying real decode rows as prefills.

Fix: zero `is_prefilling[num_reqs:]` immediately after computation.

Resolves #41841

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_splitting.py -xvs
```

## Test Result

```
23 passed, 20 warnings in 5.49s
```

- `test_split_decodes_stale_padded_is_prefilling` — verifies correct splitting after zeroing padded rows
- `test_split_decodes_stale_padded_is_prefilling_without_fix` — confirms stale data shifts the boundary without the fix

title: Add NVFP4 all-gather GEMM fusion for AsyncTP
author: baonudesifeizhai
body:
## Purpose
#27893

wires the NVFP4 FlashInfer all-gather + GEMM path into AsyncTP.

It adds NVFP4 coverage for SP + AsyncTP by fusing:

`all_gather(fp4 activation) + all_gather(group scales) + flashinfer_mm_fp4`

into:

`fused_all_gather_flashinfer_fp4_matmul`

The reduce-scatter side is intentionally not enabled for NVFP4 in this PR.

PyTorch does not currently provide an NVFP4-aware fused GEMM + reduce-scatter path.

The existing symmetric-memory helpers are designed around generic matmul / FP8-style scaling and do not handle NVFP4 block/group scales, scale swizzling, or layout-aware sharding. title: [Bugfix][Quark] Fix W8A8 INT8 garbage outputs on Step-3.5-Flash (and other 3-key fused-MoE Quark exports)
author: JoursBleu
body:
### Summary

After quantizing `stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash` to W8A8 INT8 with AMD Quark, serving the checkpoint via vLLM produces garbage tokens (random tokens, frequent NaN logits). If the same weights are offline-rewritten into compressed-tensors format and served by stock vLLM (with no changes whatsoever), everything works fine — this confirms that the INT8 numerics themselves are correct and the bug is in vLLM's Quark loading path. This PR fixes three independent bugs in the Quark INT8 backend; together they are the root cause of the garbage output. After the fix, the Quark-native checkpoint (`stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash-Quark-W8A8-INT8`) runs directly without any rewrite, and matches the compressed-tensors baseline on GSM8K and is lossless against the BF16 baseline.

The change is scoped to the Quark INT8 path and the single model class `Step3p5ForCausalLM`; **the compressed-tensors path is untouched**.

### Three root causes

**1. `Step3p5ForCausalLM` is missing `packed_modules_mapping`.**

vLLM fuses `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` into `qkv_proj` and `gate_proj`/`up_proj` into `gate_up_proj` (for both the dense MLP and the shared expert). `QuarkConfig.get_quant_method` calls:

```python
should_ignore_layer(prefix, ignore=exclude_layers,
                    fused_mapping=self.packed_modules_mapping)
```

When the model class does not declare `packed_modules_mapping` (the default empty dict), `should_ignore_layer` cannot reverse the fused prefix back to the unfused names listed in `quantization_config.exclude`.

In Quark exports, the shared expert is listed in unfused form in `exclude` (`model.layers.X.share_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj`). As a result, `share_expert.gate_up_proj` is not recognized as excluded and is wrongly attached as a Quark INT8 linear, even though the checkpoint contains no INT8 weights or scales for it — `weight_scale` stays at its zero-initialized value, the shared-expert output becomes identically 0 / NaN, and the corruption then propagates through residual + layernorm and ruins the entire forward pass.

After adding the standard `packed_modules_mapping` to `Step3p5ForCausalLM`, `should_ignore_layer` correctly matches the shared expert against the exclude list, and the layer falls back to `UnquantizedLinearMethod` and loads correctly.

**2. `QuarkW8A8MoEMethod` does not handle Quark's INT8 checkpoint layout.**

Quark's HF safetensors export differs from compressed-tensors only "cosmetically":

- It carries redundant symmetric `weight_zero_point` / `input_zero_point` tensors.
- Per-channel `weight_scale` is stored as 1D `[N]` per expert, with no trailing singleton dimension.

The old Quark MoE method could limp along with the legacy per-tensor INT8 recipe, but Step-3.5 (and similar models) use the modern per-channel + dynamic per-token activation recipe, and the old code path produced incorrect numerics on it.

This PR rewrites `QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` to mirror `CompressedTensorsW8A8Int8MoEMethod` exactly:

- The per-channel scale is registered as 2D `[E, N]` for loading, then unsqueezed to `[E, N, 1]` in `process_weights_after_loading` so the modular int8 MoE kernel sees exactly the same layout as compressed-tensors.
- The per-channel path invokes the kernel via `int8_w8a8_moe_quant_config(..., per_act_token_quant=True)`.
- The symmetric `*_zero_point` tensors are registered as placeholders so safetensors loading does not fail on unknown keys, and are dropped in `process_weights_after_loading` before the quant config is built.
- The legacy per-tensor static W8A8 recipe is fully preserved (the shard-merging logic is unchanged), keeping backward compatibility.

**3. The non-MoE `QuarkW8A8Int8` linear also needs 2D scale alignment.**

For ordinary linears, Quark likewise stores per-channel `weight_scale` as 1D `[N]`, while the rest of vLLM and compressed-tensors expect 2D `[N, 1]`. This PR adds a small weight-loader shim that unsqueezes 1D scales before the standard shape check runs, and the parameter itself is allocated as `[N, 1]`. The runtime layout is then identical to compressed-tensors.

### Validation

`stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash-Quark-W8A8-INT8` on MI355X, TP=2 + EP=2, vLLM `0.19.2rc1.dev109+gaad88f848.rocm721`:

|   | Smoke (`"What is 12 times 17?"`) | GSM8K (1319 q, 8-shot, max_tokens=8192) |
|---|---|---|
| before | garbage | — |
| **after** | "The product of 12 and 17 is **204**." | **1255 / 1319 = 95.15%** |
| Quark→CT-format baseline | OK | 1254 / 1319 = 95.07% |

BF16 baseline is 95.91%; the gap is within noise (lossless).

### Scope / risk

- Only `Step3p5ForCausalLM` and the Quark INT8 backend are touched; other models / other quantization paths are unaffected.
- The `packed_modules_mapping` added to `Step3p5ForCausalLM` is identical to what every other QKV+gate_up model in vLLM ships, and it only affects how Quark/CT `exclude` lists are matched against fused module prefixes — it does not affect weight loading itself.
- The non-MoE `QuarkW8A8Int8` linear change is backward-compatible: per-tensor (scalar) scales are unchanged, and old 1D `[N]` per-channel scales are reshaped to `[N, 1]` at load time.
- The MoE rewrite preserves the legacy per-tensor INT8 path; this PR fixes the per-channel + dynamic-input path.

### Related

- `stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash-Quark-W8A8-INT8`: the public checkpoint that exposes this bug.

title: [CPU] Fix spec decode kernel signatures for synthetic mode compatibility
author: jmamou
body:
## Purpose

Fixes CPU speculative decoding crashes by adding missing parameters to CPU Triton fallback kernel signatures. 

**Problem**: CPU speculative decoding fails immediately with `TypeError: _rejection_greedy_sample_kernel_impl() got an unexpected keyword argument 'SYNTHETIC_MODE'`

**Root cause**: The rejection sampler (`vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py`) passes `uniform_probs`, `synthetic_conditional_rates`, and `SYNTHETIC_MODE` parameters to support synthetic mode, but the CPU fallback kernels (`vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py`) did not accept them.

**Solution**: Add these parameters to CPU kernel signatures:
- `_rejection_greedy_sample_kernel_impl`: Added `uniform_probs`, `synthetic_conditional_rates`, `SYNTHETIC_MODE`
- `_rejection_random_sample_kernel_impl`: Added `synthetic_conditional_rates`, `SYNTHETIC_MODE`

The parameters are accepted but not used (C++ kernels don't implement synthetic mode yet), maintaining compatibility with the calling convention.

**Impact**:
- **Enables CPU speculative decoding** in vLLM v1 (previously completely broken)
- **No GPU impact** (GPU kernels already handle these parameters)
- **Backward compatible** (all parameters have default values)
- **Future-proof** for synthetic mode implementation in C++ CPU kernels

**Related**: Builds on CPU spec decode support from #32662

## Test Plan

Tested on **Intel Xeon Platinum 8580** (Emerald Rapids, 120 cores, 240 threads):

author: tjtanaa
body:
## Purpose

This PR integrates the aiter mhc kernel based on AITER `v0.1.13`, there are API changes in newer aiter versions. I will follow up with a new PR when we upgraded to new AITER version.

This PR also clean up the mhc kernels so that tilelang is lazily imported, avoid causing import error on platform that does not support tilelang.

IR Ops is not used because there seems to have some report regarding to some overhead with ir op abstraction. Kernel abstraction is also considered but since it does not manage weights nor require `preprocess_weight_after_loading` logic. So `CustomOp` is picked instead to capitalized on its hardware dispatching logic directly in the `layers/mhc.py` to avoid introducing complexity and inference overhead for now. 

This aiter mhc enablement PR is addressing the following issues

1. Main point: Optimize aiter mhc for ROCm.
    1. mhc-pre: `aiter`
    2. mhc-post `aiter`
    3. hc-head `ATOM`
2. [Critical] During integration it also bugfix the broken ROCm path caused by PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41536
3. During integration it also remove the dependency to tilelang on platform that doesn't support tilelang
    - `CustomOp` is used to capitalize on its hardware platform dispatching logic, `forward_cuda` and `forward_hip`.
    - `_tilelang_ops.py` is introduced so that we can lazily import the tilelang op in `mhc/kernels/tilelang.py` function preventing throwing import error on platform that does not support tilelang.
    - Separation of ops based on its implementation approach to keep the file clean. e.g. `mhc/kernels/tilelang.py`, `mhc/kernels/torch.py`, `mhc/kernels/triton.py`, `mhc/kernels/aiter.py`

title: [ROCm] Fix AITER AR+RMSNorm no-residual fusion
author: akii96
body:
## Purpose

Fix the ROCm AITER allreduce + RMSNorm fusion for the no-residual pattern.

`AiterAllreduceFusedRMSNormPattern` replaces an allreduce followed by RMSNorm without a residual input. However, the AITER fused kernel computes RMSNorm over `allreduce(input) + residual`, so the synthetic residual for this pattern must be zero.

The AITER replacement used `torch.empty_like(input)`, which can add uninitialized memory into the layer output. This PR changes it to `torch.zeros_like(input)`, matching the existing FlashInfer no-residual fusion patterns in the same file.

This restores MiniMax-M2.5 GSM8K accuracy while keeping the AITER fusion enabled.

## Test Plan

Serve MiniMax-M2.5 with ROCm AITER and allreduce RMSNorm fusion enabled:

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --max-model-len 12288 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --performance-mode balanced \
  --async-scheduling \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3}'
```

Purpose

Add ViT CUDA Graph support for Kimi-VL (KimiVLForConditionalGeneration), following the pattern established in #38061 (Qwen3-VL). Part of the tracker issue #38175.

Kimi-VL's MoonVitPretrainedModel contains .tolist() calls in its forward path (pos embedding interpolation, RoPE frequency computation, patch merging) that are incompatible with CUDA graph capture.
