title: Remove unnecessary `load_weights` methods
author: hmellor
body:
This PR adds missing functionality to `AutoWeightsLoader` which allows us to delete the `load_weights` method boilerplate from 41 architectures in vLLM. Every one of these architectures can automatically load:

- GPTQ checkpoints with correct bias skipping
- FP8 checkpoints with various scale formats
- Checkpoints with fused or sharded `qkv_proj`/`gate_up_proj` weights

---

The specific changes are:
- Enables `MergedColumnParallelLinear` and `QKVParallelLinear` to load themselves from fused or unfused checkpoints without any special logic provided that the checkpoint weights are mapped correctly
  - The mappings for `qkv_proj` look like this, which maps checkpoint name to a shard in `QKVParallelLinear`:
    ```py
    hf_to_vllm_mapper = WeightsMapper(
      orig_to_new_substr={
          # weight_name: (param_name, shard_id)
          ".q_proj": (".qkv_proj", "q"),
          ".k_proj": (".qkv_proj", "k"),
          ".v_proj": (".qkv_proj", "v"),
      }
    )
    ```
  - The mappings for `gate_up_proj` look like this, which maps checkpoint name to a shard in `MergedColumnParallelLinear`:
    ```py
    hf_to_vllm_mapper = WeightsMapper(
        orig_to_new_substr={
            # weight_name: (param_name, shard_id)
            ".gate_proj": (".gate_up_proj", "0"),
            ".up_proj": (".gate_up_proj", "1"),
        }
    )
    ```
- When LoRA manager and quant config use the mapper, we provide a `get_unfused_mapper` method as this is what these features are expecting
- Add unexpected GPTQ bias skipping to `AutoWeightsLoader`

---

This change actually found a latent bug in the layerwise online-quantization accounting:

  1. `Fp8OnlineLinearMethod.create_weights` calls `initialize_online_processing(layer)`, which snapshots `load_numel_total = get_layer_size(layer)` and wraps the weight loaders of tensors that exist at that moment. But `ColumnParallelLinear.__init__` registers `self.bias` after `create_weights` returns — so the bias was excluded from the expected total and its loader never wrapped.
  2. For OPT (qkv biases), the counter therefore hits the weight-only total at the last weight shard, and `_layerwise_process` finalizes the layer before the q bias arrives: it materializes the meta weight, replays the buffered shards, quantizes, and runs the Marlin prep — which permutes the bias for the kernel epilogue and replaces the param with a bare `Parameter`.
  3. The trailing q-bias load then hits that post-processed param (no `output_dim`, shape [2304] vs [768]) → the assert in `QKVParallelLinear.weight_loader`.

On main, OPT's old dict-based loader held a stale `params_dict` snapshot, so the late bias write went into the dead pre-Marlin tensor — silent corruption that the test never caught (it only checks dtypes, explicitly not accuracy). The branch's delegation path fetches the live param at load time, which turned the silent bug into a crash.

title: [Bugfix] OffloadingConnector: respect skip_reading_prefix_cache flag
author: littlecircle0730
body:
## Purpose
Fix #44585

`OffloadingConnectorScheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens()` was ignoring
`request.skip_reading_prefix_cache` and querying the CPU offload cache
unconditionally. This caused requests that explicitly opted out of prefix
cache reads (e.g. those with `prompt_logprobs` set, or
`skip_reading_prefix_cache=True`) to silently load KV blocks from CPU
anyway, returning incorrect `prompt_logprobs` results and masking the
intended full-recompute behavior.

The fix mirrors the existing guard already present in
`KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks()`: add an early return of `(0, False)`
when `request.skip_reading_prefix_cache is True`, so the external CPU
lookup is completely skipped.

This PR is not duplicating any existing open PR (checked via
`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "44585 in:body"`).

## Test Plan
```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -v
```

Added test_skip_reading_prefix_cache to verify:
1. A block is stored in CPU offload cache via a normal request
2. A second request with identical tokens and skip_reading_prefix_cache=True is sent
3. No blocks are loaded from CPU (expected_loaded=())
4. manager.lookup is never called (the external lookup is fully skipped)

Both async_scheduling=True and async_scheduling=False are covered via @pytest.mark.parametrize.

## Test Result
53 passed, 18 warnings in 30.03s
All pre-existing tests pass with no regressions.

title: [Bugfix] Mamba CPU Offloading
author: varun-sundar-rabindranath
body:
## Purpose
CPUOffloading + Mamba models + cache-mode "align" : Compared to cold outputs (don't hit the CPU), this combination yields incorrect results for cache'd prompts that end exactly at the offloaded block boundaries. 

When at block boundaries, the Offloading code path treats MambaSpec like sliding-window attention and returns hit-tokens that are not multiples of mamba cache size. This is incorrect.  
The "CPU cache stores" are triggered at offload block boundaries. Mamba has only a single state, and at block boundaries it is the state of the last token in the block. When the prompt is exactly at the boundary, The CPU offload should not load the cached block. This is because we'd use that state to recompute the last token and this is problematic as there is only one KV value and that is for the last token already. 

This PR drops the `max_hit_tokens` to cache boundary when a MambaSpec is detected. 

## Test Plan
Add unit test 

## Test Result
Unit tests passes on the PR

following is the output of the Falcon model when prompts are exactly at block boundaries -- 
The outputs are the same for a cold run on both `main` and `PR`:

```

`PR - CPU Hit Run`: same as cold run

```

When prompts end mid-block -- both `main` and `PR` are correct.

title: [ASR] Optimize CPU preproc to get 2.5x RTFx via multi-threading
author: ekagra-ranjan
body:
Currently, vLLM ASR's CPU preprocessing like audio loading and RMS chunking is a synchronous code which blocks the main eventloop of FastAPI server which leads to serial execution instead of batched processing. This bottleneck becomes much more painful when the system is processing [long audio ](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44587). Under high concurrency, it also leads to timeouts in `health/` endpoint which makes it difficult to identify faulty nodes and makes auto scaling aggressive.

This PR unblocks the CPU preproc sync processing by offloading them to a ThreadPool executor which frees the main eventloop of asyncio to keep running the server while the background thread load audio arrays and do the RMS chunk split. 
* This optimization leads to 2.5x higher RTFx throughput for `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`
* It also unblocks the `health/` endpoint and we see the latency go from 25s -> 0.06ms

Adds `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_PREPROCESS_WORKERS` as an env variable.

Cmd for running benchmark (after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44587 is merged)
```
MODEL_ID=openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo
vllm serve $MODEL_ID --trust-remote-code
```

Long audio
```
MAX_CONCURRENCY=128
NUM_PROMPTS=128

time vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-audio \
  --endpoint /v1/audio/transcriptions \
  --dataset-name hf \
  --dataset-path ArtificialAnalysis/Earnings22-Cleaned-AA \
  --hf-split test \
  --num-prompts ${NUM_PROMPTS} \
  --ready-check-timeout-sec 600 \
  --save-result \
  --save-detailed \
  --result-filename asr-bench.json \
  --max-concurrency ${MAX_CONCURRENCY}
```

On 1xH100:
* w/o this PR -> RTFx: 735, Benchmark duration 201.75    
* this PR 
  * **2 threads RTFx: 1890 , Benchmark duration 78.45**
  * 1 thread RTFx: 1335.05
  * 4 thread RTFx: 1739.89
  * 8 thread RTFx: 1272.91
  * 16 thread RTFx: 1292.97 
* 250% gain with 2 thread

Short audio (>80% samples are <10s)
```
MAX_CONCURRENCY=500
NUM_PROMPTS=128

time vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-audio \
  --endpoint /v1/audio/transcriptions \
  --dataset-name hf \
  --dataset-path D4nt3/esb-datasets-earnings22-validation-tiny-filtered \
  --hf-split validation \
  --num-prompts ${NUM_PROMPTS} \
  --ready-check-timeout-sec 600 \
  --save-result \
  --save-detailed \
  --result-filename asr-bench.json \
  --max-concurrency ${MAX_CONCURRENCY}
```

On 1xH100:
* w/o this PR -> RTFx: 600.885
* this PR -> RTFx: 591.7725
* 1.5% drop

However if we start vllm server with `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_PREPROCESS_WORKERS=1` then we get 1.7% higher RTFx

### Test
`test_long_audio_wer_correctness` introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44587 passes and will gate this codepath on CI. That test is long audio + BS>1 + multi-threading + RMS chunk and is fast since that dataset is just 37MB so good for CI.

title: [PD][Bugfix] Fix KV Cache sharing with HMA
author: NickLucche
body:
HMA is now the default way to serve models even when a connector is provided as of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41847.

Unfortunately we missed covering an important feature that is layers that share the same KV cache tensor, which currently crashes on main when attempting to fetch the corresponding `layer_spec`.
The fix is straightforward, as we ensure that layers that do not need a kv cache are not present in the kv_cache_spec at setup time
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3da29aa4a5509b068d378bd8aedbe4837cecf6a6/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L7441-L7459 

All we have to do in the PD connector is skip registration for those layers, like we did before supporting HMA.

title: Speed up docs build
author: hmellor
body:
In my local the combination of these changes reduces the build time from 376s to 275s. This is a ~27% decrease which will noticeably improve build and queue times in CI.

The performance affecting changes are:

- Exclude vendored HF processor & config classes from API reference - these model specific classes are not important to include in the API reference
- Removing `separate_signature` and `show_signature_annotations` - this is more similar to the PyTorch docs
- Adding `doscstring_section_style: list` - simpler to generate than tables, also more similar to the PyTorch docs

Other changes:

- Add `parameter_headings` so that docs readers can get anchor links directly to function parameters so they can be more specific when referencing our docs
- Remove outdated protobuf exclusions now that we have removed vendored gRPC code
- Replace all Sphinx/Numpy style docstring formatting with Google style to be consistent with the rest of the codebase
- Add a note to `AGENTS.md` to tell future agents to use Google style

<details>
<summary>Perf benchmarking script </summary>
```
import os                                                                                                                                                                                                        
import time                                                                                                                                                                                                      
from statistics import mean                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
import vllm                                                                                                                                                                                                      
import vllm._custom_ops                                                                                                                                                                                          
import torch                                                                                                                                                                                                     
import torch.nn.functional as F                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
print(hasattr(torch.ops, "_C"))                                                                                                                                                                                  
print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, "gelu_tanh_and_mul"))                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
def bench_once(fn, x, out=None, iters=200, warmup=50):                                                                                                                                                           
    for _ in range(warmup):                                                                                                                                                                                      
        if out is None:                                                                                                                                                                                          
            fn(x)                                                                                                                                                                                                
        else:                                                                                                                                                                                                    
            fn(out, x)                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    times = []                                                                                                                                                                                                   
    for _ in range(iters):                                                                                                                                                                                       
        t0 = time.perf_counter()                                                                                                                                                                                 
        if out is None:                                                                                                                                                                                          
            y = fn(x)                                                                                                                                                                                            
        else:                                                                                                                                                                                                    
            fn(out, x)                                                                                                                                                                                           
            y = out                                                                                                                                                                                              
        t1 = time.perf_counter()                                                                                                                                                                                 
        times.append(t1 - t0)                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    return y, times                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
def fmt_result(name, x, times):                                                                                                                                                                                  
    avg_s = mean(times)                                                                                                                                                                                          
    elems_per_s = x.numel() / avg_s                                                                                                                                                                              
    gib_per_s = (x.numel() * x.element_size()) / avg_s / (1024 ** 3)                                                                                                                                             
    print(                                                                                                                                                                                                       
        f"{name:20s}  avg={avg_s * 1e3:8.3f} ms  "                                                                                                                                                               
        f"throughput={elems_per_s / 1e6:10.3f} Melem/s  "                                                                                                                                          
        f"input_bw={gib_per_s:8.3f} GiB/s"
    )

def main():
    torch.set_grad_enabled(False)
    torch.set_num_threads(int(os.environ.get("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")))
    device = "cpu"

    # Try a few representative sizes.
    cases = [
        (4096, 4096),
        (8192, 4096),
        (16384, 4096),
    ]
    dtypes = [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16]

    for dtype in dtypes:
        print(f"===== dtype={dtype} =====")
        for rows, cols in cases:
            x = torch.randn(rows, cols, dtype=dtype, device=device).contiguous()
            out = torch.empty_like(x)

            ref, t_ref = bench_once(
                lambda t: F.gelu(t, approximate="tanh"),
                x,
            )
            ker, t_ker = bench_once(
                torch.ops._C.gelu_tanh,
                x,
                out=out,
            )

            torch.testing.assert_close(
                ker.float(),
                ref.float(),
                rtol=1e-2 if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 1e-4,
                atol=1e-2 if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 1e-5,
            )

            print(f"shape=({rows}, {cols})")
            fmt_result("F.gelu(tanh)", x, t_ref)
            fmt_result("torch.ops._C.gelu_tanh", x, t_ker)
            print(f"speedup: {mean(t_ref) / mean(t_ker):8.3f}x")
            print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with torch.inference_mode():
        main()

```

title: [Bugfix] Add X-Session-ID from conversation_id in multi-turn benchmark
author: tykow
body:
Set X-Session-ID in send_request when conversation_id is present. Keep the header unset when conversation_id is not provided.

Co-authored-by: GitHub Copilot


## Purpose

Set the `X-Session-ID` HTTP header from `conversation_id` in the multi-turn benchmark client (`send_request`) when a `conversation_id` is present. The header is left unset when no `conversation_id` is provided, preserving existing behavior.

This enables session affinity when the benchmark runs behind the vLLM Router. The router's `consistent_hash` policy extracts its routing key using a hash-key priority list in which `X-Session-ID` is the highest-priority key. Sending it keeps all turns of a conversation on the same worker, maximizing KV-cache reuse for multi-turn workloads.

Reference: https://github.com/vllm-project/router/blob/main/docs/load_balancing/README.md#hash-key-priority

Related (not duplicate):
- #44516 adds api_key and generic custom headers; this PR specifically derives `X-Session-ID` from each request's `conversation_id`.
- #43756 makes the `conversation_id` payload field opt-in; this PR concerns the routing header, not the payload field.

## Test Plan

1. Static check: confirm the modified file has no lint/type errors.
2. Manual header verification: point the benchmark at a local mock/echo endpoint and confirm requests with a `conversation_id` include `X-Session-ID`, while requests without one omit it.
3. (Optional, with router) Run `vllm-router --policy consistent_hash` with 2+ workers, run the multi-turn benchmark, and confirm same-`conversation_id` turns route to the same worker via router logs.

Command:
```bash
python benchmarks/multi_turn/benchmark_serving_multi_turn.py \
  -i <input.json> -m <model> --url http://router:8000
```

## Test Result

- Modified file passes editor diagnostics with no errors.
- Requests carry `X-Session-ID: <conversation_id>` when a conversation id is set; header is absent otherwise.

title: [NVFP4][Emulation] Fuse NVFP4 weight dequantization with compute in triton kernel for w13/w2 MOE MLP linears
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
## Purpose

On platforms without native NVFP4 hardware support (e.g. AMD MI350), NVFP4 MoE weights are currently dequantized for MOE emulation in BF16.

The previous implementation from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35737 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40033 dequantized the full weight tensors `w13` and `w2`, including ALL experts, before calling the standard Triton MoE GEMM kernel through `TritonExperts.apply`, materializing large intermediate BF16 tensors and adding memory bandwidth pressure.

## Implementation

This PR introduces a fused Triton kernel (`fused_moe_nvfp4_emulation_kernel`) that performs NVFP4 weight dequantization inline with the GEMM compute for both `w13` and `w2` MoE MLP linears. Each packed uint8 byte (two FP4 values) is loaded once, dequantized and immediately consumed by `tl.dot`, thus:

1. eliminating the need to materialize full dequantized weight tensors in HBM,
2. dequantizing only the experts hit through `expert_ids`, similar to [`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1c23c4203007d16d96b1f07847f5bf1b663ad0d7/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L59) currently used for w4a16 models on Instinct MI3xx (e.g. `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`)

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix mHC fused-RMSNorm big-fuse miscompile for hidden_size != 4096
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

`mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` (the RMSNorm-fused mHC pre big-fuse used
by DeepSeek-V4 when `norm_weight` is supplied) pipelines its fused-RMSNorm pass
at `num_stages=3`. Combined with the loop-carried `sumsq` reduction and the
persistent `output_shared` staging buffer written at per-iteration offsets, the
TileLang software pipeliner miscompiles the loop. The result is **silently wrong
`layer_input`** for every hidden size except 4096:

| hidden_size | trip count (`H // 1024`) | result vs fp32 reference |
|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 2 | **NaN** |
| 3072 | 3 | **NaN** |
| 4096 | 4 | correct (1.66e-3) |
| 5120 | 5 | 0.55 |
| 6144 | 6 | 0.23 |
| 7168 (DSv4) | 7 | 0.17 |
| 8192 | 8 | 0.36 |

It is occupancy-dependent (at H=7168 it is correct for ≤256 tokens, breaks at
≥512) and slightly non-deterministic run-to-run — the signature of a pipeline
prologue/epilogue codegen issue, not an arithmetic one. The path was evidently
only validated at `hidden_size=4096`.

## Fix

Drop the fused-RMSNorm pass to `num_stages=2`, matching the correct no-norm
sibling kernel `mhc_pre_big_fuse_tilelang` (which already uses depth 2). One line.

Root cause is in the pipeliner, not the algorithm: forcing the no-norm kernel
(no loop-carried state) to `num_stages=3` stays correct, so depth-3 alone is
fine — it only breaks when combined with the loop-carried reduction + persistent
shared buffer. Depth-2 handles that combination correctly.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open mHC PRs (#42735 bf16 shared staging, #44144 XPU fused_post_pre,
#43950 ROCm aiter default, #42893 / #41834 DSv4 platform fixes). None touch the
`num_stages` / fused-norm correctness. #42735 is a separate float32→bf16 staging
perf change and already uses `num_stages=2` in its variants.

## Test

Verified on GB200 (CUDA 13, TileLang) against an fp32 RMSNorm reference built on
top of the existing `mhc_pre_ref` in `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`:

- Before: `hidden_size` 2048/3072 → NaN; 5120/6144/7168/8192 → rel-err 0.17–0.55; only 4096 correct.
- After: all hidden sizes 2048–8192 match to ~1.6e-3 (bf16 floor), deterministic, across token counts 1..16384.
- Full op path `torch.ops.vllm.mhc_pre_tilelang(..., norm_weight, norm_eps)` (deep_gemm + kernel) at H=3072/7168: 1.67e-3, all finite.
- The non-fused paths (`mhc_pre`, `mhc_post`) are unchanged and unaffected.

> AI assistance (Claude) was used to diagnose and write this change; the author reviewed every line and ran the verification above.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Qwen3.5-FP8 nightly fail. Guard fused_add_rms_norm input/weight dtype mismatch in RMSNorm + quant fusion
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Summary

The nightly [LM Eval Qwen3.5 Models (B200) — ci build #70074](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/70074#019e9470-dfa7-479f-b6aa-b78bcddcd4c7) job started failing on `main`, a regression introduced by #42646 "[perf] Add gemma RMS AR fusion". The RMSNorm + quant fusion's dtype guard only inspected `rms_norm` nodes, not `fused_add_rms_norm` nodes, so a `GemmaRMSNorm` (used by Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next) producing a bf16 input with an fp32 weight got fused into `rms_norm_per_block_quant`, which aborts with `weight.scalar_type() == input.scalar_type()`. This crashes Qwen3.5-FP8 (block-FP8) at engine startup. This PR extends the guard to also cover `fused_add_rms_norm`.

## Root cause

`#42646` changed `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_native` to emit `ir.ops.fused_add_rms_norm(x, residual, weight, eps)` for the residual path, where `weight = self.weight.float() + 1.0` is fp32 while `x`/`residual` are bf16. The fusion's `_rms_input_weight_dtype_match` extra-check only looked at `vllm_ir.rms_norm` nodes and returned `True` for `fused_add_rms_norm` matches, so the fused-add patterns fused despite the dtype mismatch and emitted a `weight=fp32 / input=bf16` call into the strict block-FP8 kernel.

## Fix

Extend `_rms_input_weight_dtype_match` to also handle `fused_add_rms_norm` nodes (input is `args[0]`, weight is `args[2]`), so a dtype mismatch now correctly skips the fusion and falls back to the unfused path — consistent with the existing behavior for plain `rms_norm`.

## Test plan

- `pytest -s -v tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/models-qwen35-blackwell.txt -k Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8-DEP2` passed

title: [PERF] [Qwen3.5] Split mixed prefill+decode batches: route decodes to the recurrent kernel
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
# Description

This PR has 3 changes:

1. **Main: split mixed prefill+decode batches** (see below).
2. **Add MTP eval** config for Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4.
3. **Rename** `fast_kernel` → `aiter_kernel` (`fast_kernel` was too general).

## Problem

GDN attention ran **all** non-spec tokens through `chunk_gated_delta_rule`. Each decode becomes its own chunk padded to `FLA_CHUNK_SIZE=64`, so `D` decodes cost `D` near-empty 64-token chunks of wasted work. The ratio looks like this:

| Case | Kernel | Median (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| A. prefill 8192 | CuteDSL chunk | 464.1 |
| B. decode 953 | fused_sigmoid | 1843.7 |
| Sum | | 2370.8 |
| C. mixed unified (953+7239 → chunk) | CuteDSL chunk | 4361.6 |

With this PR:

| Case | Kernel | Median (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| split (pre+dec, this change) | CuteDSL + fused_sigmoid | 2256.5 |

PS: MTP already goes through this path.

## Solution

When a non-spec batch mixes prefills and decodes, peel the decode front-slice off to the recurrent update kernel `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` and run only the prefill tail through the chunk kernel. The metadata builder rebases chunk metadata to the prefill-only tail; outputs are stitched back in decode-first order.

## Tests

- `test_gdn_forward_core_split.py::test_forward_core_split_matches_unified`: split path matches the unified chunk-only path on `core_attn_out` and SSM-state. **8/8 passed** on B200 (bf16/fp32 × mixed-batch shapes).
- GSM8K (1319 q, 5-shot, B200):

| Model | Threshold | Measured | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 0.84 ± 0.03 | 0.8499 | ✅ |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 | 0.79 ± 0.03 | 0.7953 | ✅ |
| nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.8863 | ✅ |

## Performance

Kernel microbench (B200, cold-L2 CUPTI, 397B-A17B-NVFP4, mixed 953 decodes + 7239 prefill): unified chunk 4361 µs → split 2256 µs, **1.93× speedup** (1.88–2.17× across configs).

End-to-end (8×B200, DP=8+EP, ISL=8192/OSL=256, conc=2048, steady-state):

Server:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800 VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=5.0 \
  vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
    --port 8000 -tp 1 -pp 1 -dp 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --language-model-only --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching --stream-interval=100
```

Client:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm --model nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
  --port 8000 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --dataset-name random --random-input 8192 --random-output 256 \
  --max-concurrency 2048 --num-prompt 2048 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0.0
```

| Metric | Baseline (unified) | With split | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s | 131,976 | **164,156** | **+24.4%** |

title: [Bugfix] Canonicalize FP8 weight layout to (K, N) at the source
author: mgoin
body:
## Summary

Fixes #44110 at the root cause, as an alternative to #44113.

`MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.process_weights_after_loading` previously
tried to detect whether its incoming weight was `(N, K)` or `(K, N)` and
transpose accordingly. The shape-based heuristic was a no-op when
`N == K`, silently corrupting square layers. #44113 swaps the heuristic
from shape to `is_contiguous()`, but that just trades one fragile
implicit contract in the kernel for another.

The real issue is that the kernel boundary has no agreed-on layout:
- `CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` expects `(K, N)` and does not transpose.
- `ModelOptFp8{,PcPt}LinearMethod` already pre-transposes to `(K, N)`.
- `Fp8LinearMethod` (non-marlin), `Fp8OnlineLinearMethod` (non-marlin) pre-transpose to `(K, N)`.
- `Fp8LinearMethod` (use_marlin) and `CompressedTensorsW8A16Fp8` skip the transpose and let Marlin guess.

This PR makes every FP8 linear caller canonicalize to `(K, N)` before
delegating, and removes the detection heuristic from Marlin entirely.
This is the canonicalization step that the TODO referenced in #33314
was asking for, scoped to the FP8 paths that share this kernel.

### Changes

- `Fp8LinearMethod` (use_marlin, non-block): transpose before delegating.
- `Fp8OnlineLinearMethod`: collapse the marlin/non-marlin branches into a single transpose + delegate.
- `CompressedTensorsW8A16Fp8` (non-block): transpose before delegating.
- `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`: drop the conditional transpose from the non-block branch.

Net diff: 3 files, +11 / -29.

### Why this is preferable to #44113

- Removes the implicit "kernel detects layout from weight metadata" contract entirely.
- Makes the FP8 callers consistent with each other and with the Cutlass kernel's existing expectation.
- The `is_contiguous()` switch in #44113 still breaks if any future caller pre-transposes and then calls `.contiguous()`, or loads a checkpoint that happens to land non-contiguous.

## Test plan

- [x] Square (N==K, 4096×4096) regression case verified end-to-end on A40 (sm_86) with `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1`, both the checkpoint-layout path (CompressedTensors-style) and the pre-transposed path (ModelOpt-style). Relative error < 0.005 in all cases.
- [x] Non-square shapes (1024×4096, 4096×12800) verified for both paths.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files — all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, etc.).
- [ ] Existing `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py` and `tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py` runs in CI.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to draft the change; I (mgoin) reviewed and tested every line.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: [KV Connector] Mooncake store: prefix-cache retention interval for sparse attention
author: ivanium
body:
Follow-up of #43447.

## Summary

Adds prefix-cache retention support to the Mooncake KV store's `store_mask`, so the store writes exactly the blocks a future local prefix-cache hit can actually consume — and no more.

Previously `store_mask` computed a per-lcm-region template (via a dummy-hash pass through `find_longest_cache_hit`) and tiled it across the request. This refactor instead reuses the engine's own `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.reachable_block_mask`, the same logic the local prefix cache uses to decide block reachability. As a result:

- For full-attention groups the mask is unchanged (every chunk is stored).
- For sparse / sliding-window-attention (SWA) groups, the retained tail blocks now honor `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL`. Instead of keeping an SWA tail at *every* lcm boundary, the store keeps one tail per `retention_interval`-token segment, plus the latest replay-boundary tail derived from the request's prompt length (`num_prompt_tokens`). This significantly reduces store writes for sparse-attention models (e.g. DSV4-style SWA checkpointing) while preserving cache-hit reachability.

`num_prompt_tokens` is plumbed from the request tracker (`prefill_end_tokens`) through `ReqMeta` into the sending thread so the coordinator can compute the replay boundary.

## Behavior

- `retention_interval=None` (default): keeps the SWA tail at every lcm boundary — matches prior behavior.
- `retention_interval=K`: keeps one SWA tail per K-token segment.
- `retention_interval=0`: drops all segment tails; only the latest replay boundary (capped at `num_prompt-1`, aligned down to lcm) is retained.

Configured via the existing `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` env var, mirroring vLLM core's `KVCacheCoordinator.retention_interval`.

## Testing

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py -q
# 26 passed
```

Added 4 new tests covering the dense default, interval-based sparsification, the `retention_interval=0` replay-only case, and coexistence of segment + replay tails. Lint clean (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy`).

## Notes

- Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses Mooncake store retention; searched `vllm-project/vllm` open PRs for "mooncake store retention" and this branch head.
- AI assistance was used in preparing this change; the human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Prevent cuMemcpyBatchAsync segfault with MTP and KV offloading
author: JOSH1024
body:
**Bug:** 
Currently, vLLM crashes with a `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` segfault when using native KV offloading (`--kv-offloading-backend native`) alongside MTP speculative decoding on long contexts.

**Root cause:** 
I found that the `OffloadingConnectorScheduler` was accidentally including EAGLE/MTP draft-attention groups in both the load and store scheduling paths. Since these draft groups don't have stable block hashes and use tiny `gpu_block_size` values, it caused a massive miscalculation (`num_gpu_blocks = cdiv(420K, small_size) = 105022`). This resulted in an out-of-bounds GPU block index that triggered a silent, hard-to-debug CUDA segfault in `swap_blocks_batch`.

**Fix:** 
- Added an `is_eagle_group` flag to `GroupOffloadConfig` so we can easily spot these groups.
- Updated the scheduler to skip eagle groups entirely in all load/store scheduling loops. 
- As a defense-in-depth measure, I also added a pre-DMA bounds check in `gpu_worker.py`. This ensures that if any out-of-bounds block ID ever slips through in the future, it safely throws a clear Python `RuntimeError` instead of a silent CUDA segfault.

**Accountability:**
I used some AI assistance to help me track down the root cause and write the patches, but I have manually reviewed every changed line to ensure it's correct. I am relying on the GitHub CI to run the full Linux suite since I am developing on Windows.

**Testing:**
Verified the fix locally via a custom standalone regression test suite (8 passing tests ):
- Confirmed `is_eagle_group` correctly populates and defaults to `False` (preserving backward compatibility).
- Verified the load path (`update_state_after_alloc`) and store path (`_build_store_jobs`) appropriately skip MTP groups and correctly return `group_sizes=0` and `block_indices=0`.
- Verified the defense-in-depth bounds check safely catches out-of-bounds IDs before triggering the CUDA call.

Closes #44780

title: [Kernel][Perf] Tune fused_moe FP8 config for Qwen3-Next-80B tp=4 on H100 (+25% at batch 96-512)
author: qyYue1389
body:
## Purpose

Add a tuned Triton fused_moe config for `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8` on a single NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 with tp=4 and FP8 w8a8 blockwise quantization (`block_shape=[128, 128]`)

Qwen3-Next-80B has `num_experts=512`, `num_experts_per_tok=10`, `moe_intermediate_size=512`. With tp=4 this gives the kernel shape `E=512, N=128`. The current `get_default_config` in `fused_moe.py` is ~25% slower than the tuned configuration for the batch_size range that dominates production serving 

The file contains 5 batch-size keys (`96, 128, 256, 512, 1024`) for which the tuned config beats the default by >=5%. Other batch sizes fall back to `get_default_config` via the existing vllm fallback path

## Test plan

Tuned with `benchmark_moe.py --tune` on a single H100 80GB HBM3 (precompiled vLLM cu128 + torch 2.11.0+cu128 + triton 3.6.0)

## Test Result
 
Tuning walked 10,368 valid configurations across 18 batch sizes (`{1,2,4,8,16,24,32,48,64,96,128,256,512,1024,1536,2048,3072,4096}`), total wall time 77 minutes.

After tuning, the file was copied into the configs/ directory and the benchmark re-run for all 18 batch sizes. Per-batch-size median kernel time:

| batch_size | baseline (us) | tuned (us) | speedup |
|-----------:|--------------:|-----------:|--------:|
| 1     | 29.45  | 29.26  | +0.6%   |
| 2     | 30.35  | 30.13  | +0.7%   |
| 4     | 36.38  | 35.24  | +3.2%   |
| 8     | 54.81  | 54.93  | -0.2%   |
| 16    | 80.74  | 79.29  | +1.8%   |
| 24    | 95.90  | 96.65  | -0.8%   |
| 32    | 111.83 | 109.90 | +1.8%   |
| 48    | 140.51 | 140.38 | +0.1%   |
| 64    | 152.18 | 151.30 | +0.6%   |
| **96**   | **215.09** | **171.56** | **+25.4%** |
| **128**  | **229.10** | **183.06** | **+25.1%** |
| **256**  | **248.41** | **199.60** | **+24.5%** |
| **512**  | **262.77** | **217.58** | **+20.8%** |
| **1024** | **290.12** | **268.59** | **+8.0%**  |
| 1536  | 318.21 | 317.86 | +0.1%   |
| 2048  | 345.23 | 344.86 | +0.1%   |
| 3072  | 429.06 | 429.53 | -0.1%   |
| 4096  | 568.93 | 567.50 | +0.3%   |

The JSON ships only the bolded 5 keys (`96, 128, 256, 512, 1024`). Batch sizes outside this range fall back to `get_default_config`, which my benchmark shows is within 1% of the tuned config

The wins on the kept keys are primarily driven by `GROUP_SIZE_M=64` (vs `get_default_config`, `GROUP_SIZE_M=32`), which gives a more L2-cache friendly tile traversal order for `E=512, N=128, FP8` workload

The closest H100 PR is #35808 (`E=256,N=512` on H100), which is in different shape. Recent tuned-config PRs #44273 / #44152 / #44553 all target H20, not H100. No open or merged PR addresses
`E=512,N=128` FP8 blockwise on H100.

## Reproduction commands

```bash
# Baseline (move the new JSON aside first to force the default config)
mv vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/E=512,N=128,device_name=NVIDIA_H100_80GB_HBM3,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json /tmp/
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
    -tp 4 --dtype fp8_w8a8 \
    --batch-size 1 2 4 8 16 24 32 48 64 96 128 256 512 1024 1536 2048 3072 4096

# Tuned (restore the JSON)
mv /tmp/E=512,N=128,device_name=NVIDIA_H100_80GB_HBM3,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json \
   vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
    -tp 4 --dtype fp8_w8a8 \
    --batch-size 1 2 4 8 16 24 32 48 64 96 128 256 512 1024 1536 2048 3072 4096
```

title: [Frontend][Core] Add release_kv_cache_memory() API
author: andakai
body:
## Motivation

Sleep level 2 releases KV cache memory, but it also discards model weights. This
is unnecessarily expensive when a framework only needs temporary GPU headroom
while keeping the same model instance resident.

One concrete use case is model weight update in RL training. The workaround in
[verl#7373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7373) uses
`sleep(level=2)` followed by `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` before updating the
standalone model. Releasing only the KV cache reduces peak GPU memory and can
avoid OOM during the update, without discarding and remapping weights.

## Summary

This PR adds `release_kv_cache_memory()` as a dedicated KV-only partial-sleep
operation. It discards KV cache allocations, keeps model weights resident, and
pauses scheduling until the released memory is restored with the existing
`wake_up()` API.

## Implementation

### Call flow

The offline and server entry points converge on the same engine path:

```text
LLM.release_kv_cache_memory() -> LLMEngine ---------\
                                                       -> EngineCore
POST /release_kv_cache_memory -> EngineClient ------/       |
                                                             v
                                      Executor.discard(("kv_cache",))
                                                             |
                                                             v
                                               Worker -> SleepModeBackend
                                                             |
                                                             v
                                           CuMem/XPU allocator.discard(tags)
```

`EngineCore` first pauses the scheduler and clears the prefix cache. Depending
on the selected pause mode, it either handles existing requests immediately or
waits for in-flight requests to finish before asking all workers to discard KV
cache allocations. The scheduler remains paused after release; a discard
failure also fails closed instead of resuming scheduling with potentially
partially unmapped memory.

At allocator level, only mapped allocations tagged `kv_cache` are unmapped and
released, without a CPU backup. Per-allocation mapping state prevents duplicate
unmap or map operations when release, sleep, and wake-up calls are mixed.

### Interaction with sleep levels

`release_kv_cache_memory()` is treated as a KV-only partial sleep. A later
`sleep(1)` or `sleep(2)` can upgrade that state to a full sleep:

| Current state | Operation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fully awake | `release_kv_cache_memory()` | KV cache discarded, weights resident, scheduler paused |
| KV-only sleeping | `sleep(1)` | Weights offloaded, KV cache remains discarded |
| KV-only sleeping | `sleep(2)` | Weights discarded, KV cache remains discarded |
| KV-only sleeping | `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` | KV cache remapped and scheduling resumed |
| Full sleep | `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` | Only KV cache remapped; weights remain sleeping and scheduling stays paused |
| Full sleep | `wake_up()` | All allocations restored and scheduling resumed |

The executor tracks the exact internal state with `sleeping_tags`. Scheduling
is resumed only after no sleeping tags remain.

### Logging and observability

This PR reuses the existing sleep-state logger instead of adding a dedicated
`kv_cache_released` Prometheus state. After KV release, the existing metrics
report `awake=0`, `weights_offloaded=0`, and `discard_all=0`: the engine is not
available for scheduling, but it is not in sleep level 1 or 2. The precise
resource state remains available internally through `sleeping_tags`.

There is currently no requirement to monitor KV-only release separately. If
that becomes useful, a dedicated Prometheus state and its transition logic can
be added in a follow-up change.

## Scope

The public API intentionally supports only KV cache release. Existing sleep
levels already cover the other current cases:

- `sleep(1)` offloads weights and discards KV cache memory.
- `sleep(2)` discards all managed GPU memory.

A generic public tag API would also need to define whether each tag is discarded
or offloaded, increasing the API surface and overlapping with existing sleep
semantics. More fine-grained public memory management can be discussed when a
concrete additional use case appears; the internal `discard(tags)` path remains
extensible.

## Related work

- [vLLM#42658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42658) explores generic
  tag-level sleep management. This PR instead provides a smaller, explicit
  end-to-end API for the known KV-only use case.
- [vLLM#46438](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46438) contains related
  allocator-level selective-discard work.
- [verl#7373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7373) demonstrates the
  downstream model-update use case and its current sleep/wake workaround.

This PR does not duplicate the generic public API proposed in #42658; its scope
and semantics are intentionally narrower.

## Tests

Local validation used an Enroot container on one NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3
and Torch 2.13.0+cu130. The PR Python source was tested with the image's
precompiled native libraries (vLLM distribution 0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py \
  -k "kv_cache_release_rejects_unsafe_state or pause_synchronizes_device" \
  -v -o addopts=""
```

Result: **5 passed**. Rejection coverage checks an unpaused scheduler, pending
requests, and pending batches independently, with no cache reset or discard on
failure. Removing each guard in memory caused its corresponding test to fail.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py \
  -k release_kv_cache_memory_preserves_generation \
  -x -v -o addopts="" --timeout=600
```

Result: **2 passed**. Real Qwen3-0.6B generation covers rejection without a pause,
KV-only release/wake-up, and release followed by full level-1 sleep/wake-up.
Checks use process-local mapped memory and compare greedy token IDs before and
after restoration.

```bash
pre-commit run --files tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py
```

Result: all applicable hooks passed.

The test revision changes no production behavior; no additional model
benchmark was run beyond the generation-equivalence checks above.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to review the implementation, revise and validate the tests,
and draft this description.
The submitter reviewed the resulting changes and test scope.

title: [ROCm][gpt-oss] Pass GateMode.INTERLEAVE for MXFP4 W4A16 fused MoE
author: Rohan138
body:
## Summary

title: [ROCm][DSv4][Perf] Flash-decode split-K decode attention kernel
author: Fangzhou-Ai

## Purpose
This PR optimizes the DeepSeek-V4 sparse **decode** attention path on ROCm (`_sparse_attn_decode_ragged_kernel`), which is GPU-occupancy-bound at small batch sizes: DSV4's 16 TP-local heads collapse to a single head-block, so the whole decode runs on just `batch` workgroups and leaves most of a 256-CU gfx950 device idle (latency flat at ~277us across batch 4 to 128). title: [Bugfix] Lazily import the humming quantization backend
author: mgoin
body:
## Summary

The quantization registry eagerly imports every backend, including `humming`. Importing `humming` has import-time side effects, so this happens for every quantized model even when humming isn't used (see #44904).

This adds a small lazy facade at `vllm/utils/humming.py` and routes all humming access through it, so the package is only imported when a humming layer is actually used. New humming symbols are added with a single entry in the facade's `_EXPORTS` dict.

## Test

```
$ python -c "from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import get_quantization_config; get_quantization_config('humming'); import sys; print('humming' in sys.modules)"
False
```

Verified `humming` stays out of `sys.modules` after resolving the registry entry, and loads on first actual symbol use. `ruff check` passes on all touched files.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change.

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Add store group semantics
author: bitborne
body:
## Purpose

Mooncake added optional grouped object semantics in kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2180, motivated by the group-semantics discussion in kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2127. vLLM's MooncakeStoreConnector currently writes each physical Mooncake object independently, even when multiple physical objects belong to the same logical vLLM KV cache entry.

This PR adds an opt-in vLLM-side integration so related Mooncake objects can carry a shared logical group id. This lets Mooncake apply group-aware metadata routing, lease refresh, and eviction behavior without changing vLLM's generic KV connector interfaces or the default Mooncake write path.

The implementation follows the same high-level semantics as the SGLang adaptation in sgl-project/sglang#26574, adapted to vLLM's MooncakeStore key layout.

### Modifications

- Add runtime capability detection for `ReplicateConfig.group_ids`.
- Add an opt-in Mooncake connector extra config:

```json
{
  "enable_group_semantics": true
}
```

- Keep the default behavior unchanged. When the flag is disabled, vLLM still calls the existing `batch_put_from_multi_buffers(keys, addrs, sizes, replicate_config)` path without setting `group_ids`.
- When the flag is enabled and the installed Mooncake package supports `group_ids`, set `replicate_config.group_ids` with one group id per object passed to `batch_put_from_multi_buffers`.
- Fall back to the existing write path when running against older Mooncake packages that do not expose `ReplicateConfig.group_ids`.
- Use vLLM's logical KV cache identity as the Mooncake group boundary:

```text
vllm-mooncake-store:{model}@pcp{pcp_rank}@dcp{dcp_rank}@group:{kv_cache_group}@{chunk_hash}
```

- Preserve physical object keys unchanged. Physical keys still include `tp_rank` and `pp_rank`.
- Exclude physical `tp_rank` and `pp_rank` from the Mooncake group id so physical shards of the same logical KV cache entry can be grouped together.
- Preserve vLLM KV cache group identity in the group id, so different KV cache groups do not collapse into the same Mooncake group.
- Keep existing-object filtering aligned with Mooncake's batch API requirement: `len(group_ids) == len(keys)` after filtering out already-existing objects.

### Duplicate-work check

This is not duplicating an existing vLLM PR. I checked open PRs with:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "2127 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Mooncake group semantics"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "ReplicateConfig group_ids"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "MooncakeStoreConnector group"
```

The broad `MooncakeStoreConnector group` search only returned unrelated PRs.

### AI assistance

This PR includes AI-assisted code and test changes. I reviewed the changed lines and validated the behavior with the tests below.

## Test Plan

Run the MooncakeStoreConnector worker unit tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -q
```

Run lint and formatting checks for the touched files:

```bash
.venv/bin/ruff check --output-format github \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py
```

```bash
.venv/bin/ruff format --check \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py
```

The unit tests cover:

- group semantics disabled: existing behavior remains unchanged
- older Mooncake package without `ReplicateConfig.group_ids`: fallback path
- `ReplicateConfig.group_ids` detection through class and instance attributes
- group id generation from logical KV cache identity
- physical `tp_rank` / `pp_rank` excluded from group id
- physical object key layout preserved
- multiple memory segments per object
- multiple vLLM KV cache groups
- existing-object filtering keeps `keys` and `group_ids` aligned

title: [Security] Fix info disclosure via int32 truncation in GGUF dequantize kernels
author: jperezdealgaba
body:
## Purpose

Fix an information disclosure vulnerability caused by integer truncation in GGUF dequantize kernels (csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/gguf/).

The to_cuda_ggml_t function pointer typedef declares its element count parameter k as int (32-bit). When a GGUF model has weight tensor dimensions whose product exceeds INT_MAX (e.g. a 65536x65536 matrix), the int64_t product m * n is silently truncated to int at the call site. The CUDA kernel then processes only the truncated number of elements. Since output tensors are allocated with torch::empty (uninitialized memory), the unfilled portion retains stale GPU memory which — in multi-tenant inference deployments — may contain tensor data from other users' requests.

Changes:

- Widen k from int to int64_t in the to_cuda_ggml_t typedef (ggml-common.h) and all 18 dequantize function signatures in dequantize.cuh
- Widen the dequantize_block kernel's index arithmetic to int64_t to match
- Widen col, batch, vecs, and padded local variables in gguf_kernel.cu from int to int64_t to prevent the same class of truncation in the matmul and MoE paths
- Defense-in-depth: zero-initialize all output tensors via torch::stable::fill_(Y, 0.0) in ggml_dequantize, ggml_mul_mat_vec_a8, ggml_mul_mat_a8, and ggml_moe_a8, so that even if a future truncation bug occurs, stale GPU memory is never exposed

## Test Plan

```
# Build and verify compilation succeeds
python setup.py build_ext --inplace
# Run existing GGUF tests to verify no regression
python -m pytest tests/ -k "gguf" -v
```

The type change from int to int64_t is ABI-compatible and all downstream call sites already pass int64_t values (e.g. m * n in ggml_dequantize). The fix eliminates the silent truncation at the function pointer boundary.

## Test Result

- All existing GGUF kernel call sites pass int64_t values — the widened signatures eliminate the implicit narrowing conversion
- clang-format passes on all changed files
- ggml_moe_a8_vec already used fill_(Y, 0.0) — the other four functions now match

title: [CPU] Skip Triton kernel monkey-patches when Triton-CPU is available
author: jmamou
body:
## Purpose

When Triton-CPU is installed and active (the default in x86 Docker images since 0.22.0), the `@triton.jit` kernels in `rejection_sampler.py`, `block_table.py`, and `llm_base_proposer.py` can run natively on CPU — but they fail to compile due to int32/int64 type mismatches that Triton-CPU's stricter compiler catches.

This PR:
1. **Fixes the type mismatches** in 5 Triton kernels by replacing `0` (int32) with `tl.zeros([], dtype=tl.int64)` in conditional branches where the else-path produces int64 from `tl.load()`. This is backward-compatible with CUDA Triton.
2. **Skips the C++ monkey-patches** when `HAS_TRITON` is True (i.e., Triton-CPU backend is detected), letting native Triton kernels execute directly. The C++ fallback implementations remain for environments without Triton-CPU.

### Kernels fixed
- `expand_kernel`
- `rejection_greedy_sample_kernel`
- `rejection_random_sample_kernel`
- `sample_recovered_tokens_kernel`
- `eagle_prepare_inputs_padded_kernel`

### Root cause
Triton-CPU requires type consistency across if/else branches:
```python
# BEFORE (fails on Triton-CPU):
start_idx = 0 if req_idx == 0 else tl.load(ptr + req_idx - 1)
#           ^^^ int32                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ int64

# AFTER (works on both CUDA and CPU Triton):
start_idx = tl.zeros([], dtype=tl.int64) if req_idx == 0 else tl.load(ptr + req_idx - 1)
```

Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42638#issuecomment-4656481736

## Test plan

- [x] All 5 fixed kernels compile and produce correct results on Triton-CPU (tested in `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.22.0` Docker image)
- [x] `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel` already works on Triton-CPU (no fix needed)
- [ ] Verify SD inference end-to-end on x86 CPU Docker image (Triton-CPU present)
- [ ] Verify no regression on GPU CI (type fix is backward-compatible)

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output][Spec Decode] Advance grammar across reasoning boundary
author: yuyue0225sc
body:
### Purpose

Fixes #43388. Fixes #48228. Fixes #34650.

Under async scheduling + speculative decoding + a Qwen-style reasoning parser, `should_advance` in `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py` silently fails for JSON/regex/choice constraints. Two distinct bugs interact:

**Bug 1: the delta window misses the marker.** The delta window computed from `num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders` skips `</think>` whenever some drafts are rejected, because the placeholder count stays greater than zero. As a result `reasoning_ended` never flips, the grammar is never enforced, and the output contains Markdown fences or arbitrary prose.

**Bug 2: post-marker tokens never reach the FSM.** Even after `reasoning_ended` flips, the post-marker content tokens produced in the marker step never enter the grammar FSM. On the next step the bitmask is prepared with the grammar at its initial state, the model emits the opening token again, and `response_format=json_object` returns `{{...}` content — HTTP 200, but the body fails to parse on the client (the exact symptom reported in #48228).

This PR closes the inter-step state leak in `should_advance`. The sibling intra-step bitmask leak in `grammar_bitmask` was fixed by #44297 (merged); the patch sites are independent, and together they cover the full reasoning → content boundary under async + speculative decoding.

### Design

One unified boundary path for **all** constraint types (final shape reached through review with @yzong-rh):

1. `should_advance` accepts an optional `new_token_ids` argument from the scheduler call site and uses it as the exact delta window (fixes Bug 1). The two draft-validation call sites keep the placeholder fallback; their behavior is unchanged.
2. At the boundary, `should_advance` records `reasoning_end_token_index` and returns `True` for every constraint type. The scheduler then uses `trim_reasoning_for_advance()` + `accept_tokens()` to advance only the verified post-marker suffix (fixes Bug 2). `should_advance` no longer mutates the grammar — it only updates reasoning-boundary state and decides whether the scheduler should advance.

Earlier revisions used a conservative inline drain for JSON/regex/choice (advance inside `should_advance`, return `False`) while `STRUCTURAL_TAG` under spec decode used the scheduler's trim-and-advance path — two paths for the same boundary. The final revision removes that split: post-marker positions inside a speculative window are already constrained by `grammar_bitmask`, and rejection sampling prevents grammar-invalid drafts from being committed, so the committed suffix reaching `accept_tokens` is grammar-valid. Net effect on vLLM-side complexity: no per-constraint-type branching, no grammar side effects outside the scheduler, and a single boundary mechanism that any future backend-side delegation would migrate as one unit.

One intentional semantics change: an `accept_tokens` rejection at the boundary (not expected in the normal flow, per the invariant above) now terminates the request through the scheduler's standard error path instead of warn-and-continue, matching the existing non-reasoning path.

### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- #36138 (merged) fixed the spec-decode × structured-output bypass for single-token markers, but its placeholder math underflows past the marker under async scheduling + draft rejection (Bug 1) — #43388 still reproduced on Qwen3.5 + MTP.
- #43526 (closed) took the same first step but was closed by its author because post-marker tokens in the same batch were left unobserved by the FSM; this PR closes that gap.
- #43424 (open) targets multi-token markers (gpt-oss Harmony) via a different code path (`precommit_filter_tokens`); the scopes are complementary and can land in either order.

### Test Plan

Regression cases in `tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py`:

- `test_should_advance_uses_new_token_ids_when_provided` — Bug 1: the reasoner sees the exact multi-token delta rather than the placeholder-derived window.
- `test_should_advance_without_new_token_ids_falls_back` — backward compat for the no-arg call sites.
- `test_should_advance_trims_reasoning_prefix_for_json` — Bug 2: the boundary step records `reasoning_end_token_index`, returns `True`, and `trim_reasoning_for_advance` yields only the post-marker suffix.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/structured_output/ -v
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py -v
```

### Test Result

Re-verified on the current branch (merged with latest main), 8× H20, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, `--reasoning-parser qwen3`:

- `json_object`, MTP k=4 (the #43388 scenario): **50/50** requests returned clean JSON. Baseline on main without this fix: 7/50 ok (86% failure — Markdown fences + leading garbage).
- Strict tool calling / `STRUCTURAL_TAG`, MTP k=1 (the #44006 scenario): **50/50** valid `tool_calls`, 0 HTTP 500 — confirms the unified path does not regress #44297.
- Unit: `tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py` — 11 passed.

Independent verification on other hardware:

- @estrella159 applied https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44297 + this PR on vLLM 0.24.0 (Blackwell sm120), 8 launches per arm, 24 distinct prompts per launch:
Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 (dense): strict-JSON validity 14.12/24 to 23.38/24 (paired p=0.0078). The patched MTP-on arm is statistically indistinguishable from MTP-off (23.25/24, p=1.0), i.e. the fix restores MTP-on to the MTP-off baseline.
Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (MoE): 12.75/24 to 20.25/24 (paired p=0.0078). A residual gap to the MTP-off baseline remains (23.75/24, p=0.0078), attributable to a grammar-level whitespace-liveness hazard that spec-decode amplifies on this architecture.
- @stefanwichmann cherry-picked this PR on GB10 (DGX Spark), `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8`, across 5 fresh engine starts: 10/10 valid JSON with MTP re-enabled, doubled-brace output gone ([#48228 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48228)).
- @Mazyod  reproduced on google/gemma-4-E2B-it + MTP (num_speculative_tokens=2, L4, strict json_schema): JSON corruption at concurrency 8/16/24/32 went from 75%/100%/96%/91% baseline to 0% at every level with this PR, confirming both the should_advance and scheduler changes are required — first verification on a non-Qwen model family.
- @cresslank  independently validated `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` with DSpark spec
  decode (Blackwell, async scheduling) — first run through DeepSeek's DSpark path
  rather than the MTP configs above, confirming the shared accept-side fix holds
  regardless of speculation method. Stock **7/20** → this PR **20/20** (matching
  speculation-off), plus **120/120** on a prompt-diverse liveness run, 0 boundary
  corruption; failures were malformed exactly at the reasoning→grammar transition.

<details>
<summary>E2E reproducer (server command + 50-trial classification client)</summary>

Server:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":4}' \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --enable-log-requests \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
  --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager \
  --port 8000
```

Client sends 50 requests asking for a JSON object describing Seoul, with `response_format={"type":"json_object"}` and `enable_thinking=true`, without forbidding Markdown (so the model falls back to its training-time formatting habit). Each response is classified as `ok` (raw JSON, parses, has required keys), `markdown_fence`, `leading_garbage`, `bad_json`, etc.

````python
import json, os, re, time
from collections import Counter
from openai import APIStatusError, OpenAI

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("VLLM_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1")
MODEL = os.environ.get("VLLM_MODEL", "qwen3.5-35b-a3b")
TRIALS = int(os.environ.get("TRIALS", "50"))

MESSAGES = [{"role": "user", "content": "Give me a JSON object describing Seoul, with keys city, country, and population."}]
REQUIRED_KEYS = ("city", "country", "population")

def classify(content):
    if not content or not content.strip():
        return "empty", ""
    raw = content
    s = content.strip()
    if s.startswith("```"):
        return "markdown_fence", s[:120]
    if raw[0] != "{":
        return "leading_garbage", repr(raw[:40])
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", s, re.DOTALL)
    if not m:
        return "no_json", repr(s[:80])
    if m.group(0) != s:
        return "prose_wrapped", s[:120]
    try:
        obj = json.loads(s)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        return "bad_json", str(e)
    for k in REQUIRED_KEYS:
        if k not in obj:
            return "bad_json", "missing " + repr(k)
    return "ok", json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False)[:120]

def main():
    client = OpenAI(base_url=BASE_URL, api_key="EMPTY", max_retries=0, timeout=120.0)
    counts = Counter()
    t0 = time.time()
    print("target:", BASE_URL, "model:", MODEL, "trials:", TRIALS)
    for i in range(1, TRIALS + 1):
        try:
            r = client.chat.completions.create(
                model=MODEL, messages=MESSAGES,
                response_format={"type": "json_object"},
                extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}},
                temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=4096,
            )
            kind, detail = classify(r.choices[0].message.content or "")
        except APIStatusError as e:
            kind, detail = "http_error", "HTTP " + str(e.status_code)
        except Exception as e:
            kind, detail = "client_error", type(e).__name__
        counts[kind] += 1
        print("[%3d/%d] %-20s %s" % (i, TRIALS, kind, detail), flush=True)
    print("\nsummary (%.1fs):" % (time.time() - t0))
    for k, n in counts.most_common():
        print("  %-20s %d" % (k, n))
    bug = counts["markdown_fence"] + counts["prose_wrapped"] + counts["no_json"] + counts["bad_json"] + counts["leading_garbage"]
    print("\nFAIL %d/%d" % (bug, TRIALS) if bug else "\nPASS %d/%d" % (counts["ok"], TRIALS))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````

</details>

title: [Perf][ROCm] Fix GDN KKT warmup regression on RDNA by avoiding fp32 tl.dot
author: nemanjaudovic
body:
## Purpose
After this PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42076, during running of Qwen3.5-9B model that uses GDN triton kernel on RDNA GPUs, warmup time went from ~150s to ~2400s. The problem was that operands of tl.dot() were casted to fp32, so that operation lowered to software fp32 matmul instead of wmma instuction.
These changes are modifying kernel only for RDNA GPUs, while they are untouched for all other GPUs.

## Test Plan
Tests were performed on qwen3.5-9b model. After proposed changes are applied warmup time goes back to ~150s. 
Also, tests on gsm8k benchmark were done, and correctness is preserved on RDNA GPUs, while kernel is untouched for all other GPUs. 
After detailed testing of IRs and compilation times for each stage, regression happens in amdgcn stage where the difference is about 190x.

title: [EPLB] Enable nixl eplb communicator for elastic ep
author: ilmarkov
body:
## Purpose
Enable `NixlEplbCommunicator` for elastic EP, allowing async EPLB during elastic scale-up/down.

**Key changes:**
1. Drain-before-scale. Consume all pending async transfers before groups are replaced. Wait for all layers to finish rather than stop in the middle to avoid cross-rank and cross-thread races.
2. Start async thread after scale-up on new workers.
3. Deferred NIXL remote setup. Postpone collective metadata
   exchange to first `set_transfer_context()` to avoid deadlocks.
4. Replace `monitored_barrier`  with `all_reduce` + `wait(timeout)` for stateless groups in Nixl EPLB communicator.
5. Prefer NIXL in  auto-selection for all EP modes.


## Test Plan
`tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py`. Test params tuned  (`step_interval=10`, `window_size=5`) to actually trigger EPLB.
- `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` — new
  `test_nixl_deferred_init` verifying the deferred-init path  end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Voxtral realtime: fix boot OOM and engine crash at max_model_len
author: damienlaine
body:
Fixes for Voxtral realtime, all in the model and the realtime entrypoint. The unbounded-duration part is #45833 (stacked).

### Update 2026-10-05

Reworked after @andylolu2's review: no core changes anymore. Scheduler, runner and output_processor changes dropped (#58942 covers ERROR/ABORT, #42502 the generic scheduler guard).

### Fixes

- **Boot OOM (#38233)**: profiling runs one audio item of `max_model_len` tokens. With the default `max_model_len` (131072) that OOMs at boot on 16 GB. New `VoxtralRealtimeProcessingInfo`: the profiling audio is the largest streaming chunk (the prefix, 39 tokens), `{"audio": 1}` per update. The item size stays `max_model_len` because it also sizes the encoder cache: a paused session keeps its last chunk cached until it resumes, and a cache sized to one chunk deadlocks concurrent sessions (0/12 at `--max-num-batched-tokens 256`).
- **Engine crash at `max_model_len`**: a streaming session reaching the limit kills the EngineCore (`illegal memory access`) and every other session with it. `VoxtralRealtimeBuffer` now counts submitted tokens and ends the stream before `max_model_len`, so the session finishes normally.
- **WebSocket disconnect**: cancelling the generation task doesn't abort the engine request, the slot stays held. Cleanup now aborts it.

### Tests

RTX 4090 Laptop 16 GB, `--hf-overrides` sliding window 256, PIECEWISE:

- `--max-model-len 131072`: main OOMs during profiling, this PR boots.
- concurrent realtime streams: same transcripts, throughput and memory as with the previous runner change, no OOM. 12 sessions at `--max-num-batched-tokens 256`: 12/12, same as main.
- `--max-model-len 512`, 70 s streams over websocket: streams stop at the cap, client gets `transcription.done`, next session OK.

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py -k max_model_len   # 2 passed
```

`test_voxtral_realtime_generator_max_model_len` fails with `EngineDeadError` without the buffer cap.

AI-assisted; reviewed and tested by me.

title: Stop setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES internally in vLLM, add device_ids arg
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
This PR changes the way vLLM interacts with the `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (CVD) environment variable:
* With this PR vLLM no longer sets CVD to control which GPU a worker uses
* This PR adds a `--device-ids` argument so that users don't need to set 

This has a few benefits:
* vLLM currently does not support the UUID format for device IDs which is problematic for using it with MIG (should fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32569)
* There is currently no way to use external DP load balancing with DeepGEMM MegaMoE, because setting CVD for each individual rank isolates GPUs and prevents NCCL from initializing (fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44556)

One thing this implies is that we need to decouple the concept of "local rank" from "device id" inside of vLLM, so there are a lot of changes caused by that.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA] Add AITER FlashAttention MLA prefill backend (`ROCM_AITER_FA`)
author: xaguilar-amd
body:
## Summary

Adds an AITER-backed MLA prefill backend that calls `aiter.flash_attn_varlen_func`
directly instead of falling back to the upstream CK-tile FlashAttention path on ROCm.

It dispatches the fast `aiter::fmha_fwd_*` kernel on gfx950 and, unlike the CK
fallback, needs **no V padding** (native qk=192 / v=128 head dims) and returns
`softmax_lse` already shaped `(nheads, total_q)` (**no LSE transpose**). This is the
fp16/bf16 generic-varlen prefill path; it is auto-selected on gfx950 and transparently
falls back to `FLASH_ATTN` everywhere else.

Applies to all MLA models on gfx950 (DeepSeek V3/R1, Kimi-K2, …); validated on
`amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4-AttnFP8` and `deepseek-ai/Deepseek-V3`.

## What changed

- **New** `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/aiter_flash_attn.py` —
  `AiterFlashAttnPrefillBackend` (`get_name() == "ROCM_AITER_FA"`), implementing
  `run_prefill_new_tokens` (causal) and `run_prefill_context_chunk` (unmasked).
- **`registry.py`** — registers the `ROCM_AITER_FA` enum member.
- **`selector.py`** — on ROCm, prefers `[ROCM_AITER_FA, FLASH_ATTN]`.

## Selection & gating

- Auto-selected only when **all** hold: `current_platform.is_rocm()`, `on_gfx950()`,
  `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, and `aiter.flash_attn_varlen_func` is importable.
- `validate_configuration` filters it out on non-gfx950 / aiter-missing hosts, so those
  fall back to `FLASH_ATTN` with no behavior change.
- Precision follows the inherited `supported_dtypes = [float16, bfloat16]` 
- Can be forced explicitly via `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'`.

## Performance

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Don't reject fp8_e5m2 KV cache for non-fp8 quantized checkpoints
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

Closes #39137.

`_init_kv_cache_quant` rejects `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2` for every quantized checkpoint with "fp8_e5m2 kv-cache is not supported with fp8 checkpoints". But weight-only checkpoints (INT4/INT8 compressed-tensors, AWQ, GPTQ) carry no fp8 KV scales and are not fp8. On Ampere, where `fp8_e5m2` is the only fp8 KV cache dtype that runs at all (`fp8_e4m3` is unsupported by the hardware), this makes fp8 KV cache unreachable for every weight-quantized model.

The gate now fires only when the checkpoint actually stores fp8 KV scales. A compressed-tensors checkpoint does so only when it declares a `kv_cache_scheme`; weight-only ones declare none. Genuine fp8 checkpoints (including compressed-tensors fp8-KV) stay rejected, so a class-only whitelist or a blanket compressed-tensors exemption would be wrong.

This deliberately leaves the separate query-quant `fp8_e5m2` assert in `Attention.forward` alone. On Ampere, allowing it there only moves the crash into `reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash`, since the query-quant path uses e4m3, which Triton does not support on SM 8.x.

<details><summary>Related PRs</summary>

- #39195 (closed): narrowed the gate to `BaseKVCacheMethod`, which does not help because `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod` is itself a subclass.
- #39255 (open): exempts all compressed-tensors by class and also patches the query-quant assert, which only moves the Ampere crash deeper as above.

</details>

## Test Plan

Reproduce with a weight-only W4A16 compressed-tensors checkpoint (no `kv_cache_scheme`) and `fp8_e5m2` KV cache. The gate is a checkpoint-config check, so it fires identically on any CUDA device; the logs below are from an RTX 4090 (SM 8.9), and the fix was first validated on an A800 (SM 8.0), the Ampere case the Purpose describes.

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="nm-testing/tinyllama-oneshot-w4a16-channel-v2",  # weight-only W4A16, no kv_cache_scheme
    kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e5m2",
    max_model_len=2048,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
    enforce_eager=True,
)
out = llm.generate("The capital of France is", SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
print(out[0].outputs[0].text)
```

Equivalent server: `vllm serve nm-testing/tinyllama-oneshot-w4a16-channel-v2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2`

## Test Result

Same model, command, and environment for both runs; the only difference is the gate in `_init_kv_cache_quant`.

**Before (main):** engine core init fails at the gate, matching the report.
