title: [Bugfix][Test] Fix test_flashinfer_cutlass_mxfp4_fused_moe on sm90 (stale weight/scale interleave)
author: wentian-byte
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the stale weight/scale preparation in `test_flashinfer_cutlass_mxfp4_fused_moe`, which fails on Hopper (sm90) with ~89% mismatch (vs the 0.2 threshold).

Closes #46585.

## Root cause

The test prepared inputs for the SM90 mixed-input cutlass MoE GEMM (`cutlass_fused_moe(use_w4_group_scaling=True)`) with:
- a hand-rolled `_interleave_scales_lastdim_by4` for scales, and
- **no interleave at all** for the packed 4-bit weights.

The SM90 mixed-dtype GEMM expects weights/scales in a specific interleaved layout; without it the FP4→BF16 LUT reads bytes from the wrong positions for any `K > 128`, so the kernel output diverges from the dequantized reference. The kernel itself is correct — the test was stale.

(Thanks to the maintainer who diagnosed this in #46585 and pointed at the right helpers.)

## Fix

Use flashinfer's dedicated helpers to prepare inputs, matching what the kernel expects:
- `interleave_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm(w, quant_type="fp4")` for `fc1`/`fc2` weights
- `interleave_moe_scales_for_sm90_mixed_gemm(s)` for the block scales

and drop the now-unused `_interleave_scales_lastdim_by4` helper.

## Test

Verified on 1×H20 (sm90, flashinfer 0.6.12): `test_flashinfer_cutlass_mxfp4_fused_moe` goes from **1 failed (89% mismatch)** to **8 passed** (all parametrizations).

title: [Attention] Support NVFP4 KV cache on SM8x and SM12x with FlashInfer
author: lesj0610
body:
## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` has a paged KV write path only on SM100, where trtllm-gen provides the native store, so the dtype cannot be used on SM8x or SM12x at all.

On SM8x and SM12x this writes the cache with FlashInfer's `nvfp4_quantize_append_paged_kv_cache_with_slot_mapping` and reads it back with the native fa2 prefill and decode wrappers, so no kernel change is needed. On SM12x, NVFP4 groups use the native decode wrapper instead of XQA and capture only single-token decode graphs, as on SM8x. One helper carves each page into its K and V halves for NHD and HND and leaves the data/scale split to the existing `nvfp4_split_data_scale`; SM100 builds its views through the same helper and keeps its trtllm-gen kernels. The query and output stay in model dtype on the fa2 path, so q_scale is not applied and no FP8 staging buffer is allocated. Both FlashInfer entry points are in the pinned 0.7.0, so no version bump is needed. On the sm_80 host used for validation, KV cache capacity went from 1,446,932 to 4,805,405 tokens (3.32x).

On these GPUs two combinations are refused in `supports_combination`, so the server stops at backend selection before the weights load: head_size 64, where fa2 prefill misreads NVFP4 by 10 to 15 percent once it picks the 128-row query tile (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5965, reproduced on sm_80 too), and attention sinks, since the sink prefill wrapper cannot read the block scales (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5966). flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6024 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6021 fix these but are not merged yet, so both refusals stay until the fixes ship in a FlashInfer release and the pin moves. DCP is refused in the metadata builder, because `supports_combination` does not see it. Scale-search variants such as `nvfp4_4over6` stay SM100-only because the slot-mapping writer has no scale search yet; once FlashInfer's writer supports it, enabling them here is a two- or three-line change.

`#46329`, `#54772` and `#56550` also target SM12x; this path needs no CUDA kernel or XQA change. RFC `#47684` tracks the wider work.

I used Codex and Claude while implementing and preparing this PR. I reviewed the final diff and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -k nvfp4
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
vllm serve <Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B|Qwen/Qwen3-4B> --attention-backend FLASHINFER --kv-cache-dtype <auto|nvfp4> --max-model-len 4096 --port 8131
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 100 --port 8131
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --attention-backend FLASHINFER --kv-cache-dtype <auto|nvfp4> --max-model-len 128K --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --enable-chunked-prefill --reasoning-parser qwen3 --port 8099
python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py --port 8099 --num-samples 30 --needles 2 4 8 --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --seed 42 --concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

The GPU test writes through `do_kv_cache_update()` on all four block-compact layouts, dequantizes what the slot-mapping writer stored through the same views, and checks it against the input and that the neighbouring layer stays untouched. The read path is covered by the evals below. pre-commit passes.

mgoin ran this on SM121 with the stock `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` wheel; the results are in the comments. On sm_80 with the same stock wheel at `9adf229fb5`, the four nvfp4 tests pass, `openai/gpt-oss-20b` with an NVFP4 cache stops in 45 s with the head_size 64 reason, and GSM8K with the FLASHINFER backend for both dtypes gives:

| Model | Questions | bf16 KV | nvfp4 KV |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 100, two runs | 0.350, 0.350 | 0.170, 0.130 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | all 1319 | 0.384 | 0.174 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-4B (32 query / 8 KV heads) | 100, two runs | 0.920, 0.910 | 0.880, 0.880 |

MRCR on Qwen3.5-4B, 30 samples across needles 2/4/8 with prompts of 16,626 to 33,231 tokens, measured on an earlier, larger revision of this PR:

| KV dtype | Match ratio | Prefix hit rate | n2 | n4 | n8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| auto | 0.8523 | 1.0000 | 0.9949 | 0.7987 | 0.7633 |
| nvfp4 | 0.8452 | 0.9667 | 0.8951 | 0.8773 | 0.7633 |

SM100 now builds its views through the shared helper. For LBHNC and BLHNC, the two layouts SM100 accepts, they match the previous views on CPU whenever the cache has more than one block; SM100 itself was not run. SM86, SM89, SM120 and performance are untested.

title: [Bugfix][KV offload] Store interior chunk-boundary blocks under MTP/Eagle
author: drakosha
body:
## Summary

Fixes #46971.

With MTP/Eagle speculative decoding, `OffloadingConnector` stored KV to CPU but
prefix reuse almost never hit: re-sending an evicted long prompt recomputed the
whole prefill instead of loading it from CPU, and `External prefix cache hit
rate` stayed at 0%.

`_build_store_jobs` computes `num_blocks` twice. The key-collection loop applies
the Eagle trailing-block exclusion (`num_blocks - 1`), but the job-build loop
recomputes `num_blocks` without it and advances `next_stored_block_idx` to that
larger value (`advance_stored_idx` has the same omission). So the excluded
trailing block of every chunked-prefill chunk is jumped over and never stored —
offloaded block 31, 63, 95, … with an 8192-token chunk and 256-token blocks.
`_maximal_prefix_lookup` stops at the first gap, capping reuse at the first
chunk.

This pulls the exclusion into a single `storable_blocks()` helper used in all
three places, so only the one genuinely-volatile tail block of the range is held
back (the invariant #44784 added) and interior blocks store normally.

## Test

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py` — full
offloading-connector scheduler suite plus a new `test_multichunk_store_no_interior_holes`
that drives a >1-chunk prefill and asserts the stored blocks are contiguous (no
boundary gap). The new test fails on the current code (gap at block 249) and
passes with the fix; the existing 78 tests still pass (80 passed total).

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
# 80 passed
```

Verified end to end on GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse MLA), TP4 + DCP4,
fp8_ds_mla, MTP, CPU offload. Prime a 200k prompt, evict it, re-send:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| re-send TTFT | 47.7 s (recompute) | 0.5 s |
| reloaded from CPU | 0.42 GiB | 10.9 GiB |
| `offload_hit` tokens | 7680 (30 blocks) | 199424 (780/781 blocks) |

Output is unchanged: on a deterministic prompt the greedy continuation served
from offload reload matches both a fresh prefill and a GPU-prefix-cache hit token
for token, and the volatile tail block is still excluded.

## Notes

Checked open/closed issues and PRs before filing — no existing fix; nearest PRs
(#46960, #46139, #46082, #39021) touch other paths. AI assistance was used to
investigate the bug and prepare this change; every line was reviewed.

title: [Bugfix] Capture final-layer aux hidden state in deepseek_v2 backbone
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose
The `deepseek_v2` backbone captures EAGLE3 / `extract_hidden_states` aux hidden states only at decoder-layer *inputs* (ids `0..num_hidden_layers-1`), so an aux id equal to `num_hidden_layers` — the final layer's output — is silently dropped, returning one fewer hidden state than configured. This makes deepseek_v2-family models (DeepSeek V2/V3, GLM-MoE, Kimi, …) unusable as aux-hidden-state targets whenever the final-layer state is requested.

This captures the final layer's output as well, mirroring the `llama` backbone. It is a no-op when no aux hidden-state layers are set, so normal inference is unaffected.

## Test
With a deepseek_v2-family target (GLM-MoE) and `eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids` that include the final layer, the model previously returned N-1 hidden states (RuntimeError on the consumer's fixed-size buffer). With this change it returns all N requested aux hidden states.

title: [ROCm][DeepEP] Stabilize high-throughput DBO for DP+EP
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
This fixes ROCm DeepEP high-throughput DBO accuracy for DP+EP without skipping the backend. The failing local repro was `test_dbo_dp_ep_gsm8k[deepep_high_throughput]`, where GSM8K accuracy dropped below the test threshold. DeepEP high-throughput uses Buffer-owned communication state. Under DBO on ROCm, overlapping ubatches can reuse that communication workspace before the previous dispatch/combine has finished. Two other ROCm-specific interactions made the failure easier to hit: async scheduling and DBO CU partitioning.

Proposed changes:
- Disable auto async scheduling for `ROCm + DeepEP high-throughput + DBO`; explicit async scheduling now fails fast for that unsupported combination.
- For the same combination, set DBO communication CUs/SMS to `0` so DBO does not partition CUs away from the DeepEP HT kernels.
- Synchronize after DeepEP HT `dispatch` and `combine` when DBO is enabled on ROCm so the next ubatch cannot reuse Buffer-owned communication workspace too early.
- Add focused unit coverage for DBO threshold behavior and the ROCm DeepEP HT CU-partition guard.

This keeps `deepep_high_throughput` active. It does not skip the test, does not fall back to another all2all backend, and does not change DeepEP low-latency behavior.

title: [Spec][V2] Support MTP speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism
author: eastwood-c
body:
## Purpose

MTP speculative decoding does not work under pipeline parallelism on the V2 model runner. #50514
landed the generic PP spec-decode transport; this PR covers the MTP-specific gaps that remain on
the PP>1 path.

**Depends on #55745** — a one-line `record_stream` guard in #50514's `broadcast_drafts`, without
which this path trips a device-side `IndexKernel` assert under async launches. It is the bottom
commit here and can be dropped once #55745 merges.

**1. MTP drafters do not implement `SupportsPP`.** The engine refuses to build the draft at all:
```
NotImplementedError: Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model.
Supported models implement the `SupportsPP` interface.   [DeepSeekMTPModel]
```
The draft runs only on the last PP stage, so it never consumes PP intermediate tensors, but the
interface still requires the `make_empty_intermediate_tensors` factory. Applied to `DeepSeekMTP`
and `Qwen3_5MTP`. Mirrors #39704 for the V1 runner.

**2. Qwen3.5/3.6 MTP draft head skips its `fc` projection.** It branched on `is_first_rank`, which
is False on the last PP stage where the drafter is built. The head then fell through to the
intermediate-tensor path with nothing to read (~1% acceptance). Now branches on
`intermediate_tensors is None`, which is equivalent for a pipelined module and correct for a
whole-drafter-on-one-rank module. @hackxixi suggested this as the general rule for draft heads.

**3. DeepSeek MTP does not load its own `embed_tokens`.** A checkpoint storing it as one top-level
tied weight has no spec layer to rewrite from. The loader dropped it, and the draft embedded with
uninitialised weights. Under PP the target's copy is a `PPMissingLayer` on the draft's stage, so it
cannot borrow the target's. Per-spec-layer checkpoints are unaffected.

**4. `DeepseekV32MTP` carries neither of the above.** It was forked out of `DeepSeekMTP` after this
branch first added `SupportsPP`, and took neither that nor the `embed_tokens` load.
`speculative.py` routes `deepseek_v32` and `glm_moe_dsa` there, so this is the GLM-5.2 and
DeepSeek-V3.2 path. Missing `SupportsPP` raises the error above; the missing `embed_tokens` load is
silent — the engine serves correct output, because rejected drafts are discarded, and only
acceptance shows it: 32.69% against 93.51% once the weight loads. Both restored on the nvidia and
amd variants.

**5. Stale `topk_indices_buffer` in sparse MLA backends.** `LLMBaseProposer.load_model` repoints
the draft's indexers at the target's buffer, but that runs after the backend impls snapshot it in
`__init__`. Its `named_modules()` walk reaches the indexer but not the impls, which are plain
`AttentionImplBase` objects. The impls then read a buffer nothing writes: garbage DSA attention and
degenerate drafts.

A `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` mixin now resolves the buffer per read, so `forward_mqa` is unchanged
and every `SparseMLACommonImpl` subclass is covered, including `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90`. The
three impls that are not subclasses (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120`, `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse`,
`xpu_mla_sparse`) use the same mixin. An explicit assignment still supersedes the indexer, which is
how skip-topk layers and the proposer's module walk set it. The mixin is in
`sparse_mla_attention.py`, not `v1/attention/backend.py`: every consumer is sparse MLA, and the
four span two bases whose only shared ancestor is `AttentionImplBase`.

`DeepseekV32Model` (nvidia) held the buffer in a local, so the proposer's sharing block never ran
for DSA at all. It is now exposed on the model, as the ROCm variant already does.

**6. Draft MM embedding gather on ranks without an encoder runner.** `ModelState.encoder_runner`
exists only on the first PP rank, so a multimodal-capable MTP drafter died in warmup on the last:
```
AttributeError: 'MambaHybridModelState' object has no attribute 'encoder_runner'
```
Later ranks have no cached embeddings to gather. `Qwen3_5MTP` is the first in-tree draft that is
both `SupportsPP` and `SupportsMultiModal`.

## Not duplicating existing work

- #50514 provides the PP draft-token transport. The earlier revision of this PR carried its own
  version; that is dropped. The only change here to `v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py` is #55745's guard.
- #53408, #54635, #55081 (@JasonKeyiL) implement `SupportsPP` on other MTP families; neither
  `deepseek_mtp.py` nor `qwen3_5_mtp.py` is touched by any of them. #55081 overlaps fix 4's
  `SupportsPP` half, which can be dropped if it merges first.
- #54709 (qwen4_exp draft head) is the same bug as fix 2 and takes the same one-liner; left out to
  keep this focused.

## Test Plan

```
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
```

New unit tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` cover fix 5: the repointed-buffer
regression itself, explicit assignment superseding the indexer, and the subclass family.

## Test Result

```
# 1x H200 NVL (SM 9.0)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_mask.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py    -> 186 passed, 616 skipped
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py                        -> 4 passed
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_mtp_parallel_load.py      -> 5 passed, 1 skipped
pytest tests/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py \
  tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py          -> 57 passed, 1 skipped
pre-commit run --files <12 changed>                            -> passed
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <12 changed> --hook-stage manual -> passed
```

Skips are capability and dtype gates (SM 10.x, `fp8_ds_mla`/`nvfp4_ds_mla`, FA4, `block_size=32`),
not this change.

### Acceptance

GSM8K, first 200 prompts, greedy, `max_tokens=512`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, async launches,
measured on this branch. `mean_acceptance_length` as defined in
`tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/`.

title: [Spec Decode] DSpark
author: benchislett
body:
## Purpose Adds support for [DSpark](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark) speculative decoding, using both DeepSeek-V4 DSpark models as well as [DeepSeek-trained Qwen3-DSpark](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7) models. ## Design DSpark uses non-causal sliding-window attention. To implement this, instead of manually reimplementing the MLA attention, we instead utilize the existing SparseMLA backends with an expanded topk size, in which the queries all include _each other_ in their topk indices, independent of causality. This implements exactly-correct attention with respect to causality (see test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py) while also minimizing changes to the KV cache utilities and allowing reuse of existing, efficient sparse attention kernels. For CUDA Graphs, we capture the full DFlash backbone and autoregressive sampling loop in a single graph. This decreases host and kernel launch overhead. ## Testing I ran GSM8k at high concurrency, with and without prefix caching (and num_fewshot high enough to trigger prefix cache hits), and got good scores with DSV4-Pro + DSpark. I ran multiple categories of SPEED-Bench at BS32 + BS8 + BS1, with and without thinking enabled, with CUDA graphs + prefix caching enabled. Performance is strong: At BS1 with 7 draft tokens, the verification is ~11-13ms, DFlash backbone is 0.6ms, and autoregressive sampling is another ~0.6ms. E2E step time on 8xB300 is ~14ms; with ALs of ~5, that works out to >350 TPS (observed on speed-bench coding + no-thinking). May improve further once probabilistic drafting stabilizes (see below). Comprehensive evaluation and detailed benchmarking to follow. ### Example Commands
Launch commands

```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative_config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}' vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --speculative_config '{"method":"dspark","model":"deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7","num_speculative_tokens":7, "attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}' ```

Benchmark Commands

```bash vllm bench serve --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path . --speed-bench-category "coding" --num-prompts -1 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-shuffle --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0 --speed-bench-output-len 2048 --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --skip-chat-template vllm bench serve --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path . --speed-bench-category "roleplay" --num-prompts -1 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-shuffle --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0 --speed-bench-output-len 2048 --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --skip-chat-template vllm bench serve --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path . --speed-bench-category "coding" --num-prompts -1 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-shuffle --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0 --speed-bench-output-len 2048 --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --skip-chat-template --extra-body '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":"true"}}' vllm bench serve --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path . --speed-bench-category "roleplay" --num-prompts -1 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-shuffle --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0 --speed-bench-output-len 2048 --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --skip-chat-template --extra-body '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":"true"}}' python3 vllm/tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 5 python3 vllm/tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 50 ```

### Performance Disclaimers: - Only TP, no EP or DP. So high-end is not accurate (bs >= 64 tend to use DP) - Only 8 gpus, so y-axis is normalized a bit unfairly - Forced AL per-method + per-draft-length, calibrated on speed-bench category average, thinking on, temp 1. See above. - DSpark vs MTP gap at BS1 widens approx +7% if using coding-category ALs. And even more if using thinking-off and/or low temperature. - No dynamic scheduling (see below) ## Known Issues - ~Probabilistic drafting runs but leads to correctness issues; the completions slowly degrade into junk/loops and acceptance rates are inflated. I suspect a subtle issue with how we are running rejection sampling. For whatever reason, GSM8k still passes -- more comprehensive evaluation is needed for final verification.~ - - ~Lead: looking into NaN sanitization as a few ops have some dummy torch.empty inputs that might be corrupting the draft logits.~ - - ~Lead: Seems like DSV4-Pro + MTP + Probabilistic is also giving some bad outputs. Dense-model scenario seems to work fine with DSpark + Probabilistic. Investigating.~ - - Solved, two bugs. d0d2c854443729af4eea364b491d01e434791393 and 54b454fa99e15f96155f0995756216341f22fb10 - ~Dense-model (Qwen3) DSpark is having some IMA when using CUDA graphs. I likely missed a buffer somewhere, and will debug promptly~ seems fixed by rebasing to latest main and using FLASH_ATTN backend. Further evals ongoing ## Scope - dynamic drafting and confidence-based scheduling are out-of-scope for this PR. Track DSD here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45953, and we will unify with DSpark in a follow-up work - Gemma4-DSpark is left for follow-up as it has its own arch (cannot reuse the Qwen3 DFlash) and I'm not sure we'll want to support it just for DeepSeek's checkpoint. It'll probably be easier just to train a DSpark for the Qwen3 arch and reuse the current implementation.

title: [NIXL] Avoid reading expired blocks in bidirectional turn-2 read
author: tomerg-nvidia
body:
## Purpose
Currently with the multi-turn bidirectional mode, the nixl connector can result with garbage reads on turn 2 (P reading from D). This is because D sets a constant TTL for the blocks which is not extended by the heartbeat like the P TTL. When the blocks are expired they can be reused for other requests. The problem is that subsequent turns don't have a way to tell that the blocks on D are no longer valid and should not be read.

This change adds the following functionality:
1. D adds its timestamp to the handshake (Bumps `NIXL_CONNECTOR_VERSION` 4 -> 5)
2. P calculates a time offset with D
3. D submits the blocks expiration time in the `kv_transfer_params`
4. If P sees that the blocks are about to become invalid (or already have been), it declines the request

## Test Plan
Manually tested by creating P and D with `"bidirectional_kv_xfer":true`, waiting the timeout between initial request and followup while issuing many other requests.

Added unit tests to see that the request is declined when it should.

## Test Result

With the changes the right kv blocks are read and the chat continues normally, before them the second turn response was garbage.

All added tests are passing

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Track allocated block IDs when num_external_tokens is 0
author: linshi-w
body:
Fixes #46951.
 
  update_state_after_alloc() returns early when num_external_tokens == 0 without recording allocated block IDs in _current_batch_allocated_block_ids.
  Blocks allocated by other async connectors (via MultiConnector) are invisible to re-allocation detection — pending store jobs won't be flushed if those blocks are reused.

title: Remove more unnecessary `load_weights` methods
author: hmellor
body:
- `FusedMoE` now takes `ckpt_names` instead of `expert_mapping` and stores them individually in `RoutedExperts`
- `RoutedExperts.load_weights` then calls `RoutedExperts.get_expert_mapping` which uses these names to construct the expert mappings on the fly
- `RoutedExperts.load_weights` now handles checkponts like Qwen3 VL MoE where the fused expert weights may be transposed
- `RoutedExperts.load_weights` now breaks the inner loop early if fused weights have been used, the same weight will never be used to load fused and unfused parameters
- `FusedMoEWithLoRA` now tells `RoutedExperts` what the LoRA base layer prefix is so `RoutedExperts` no longer needs to examine the whole model to know if LoRA is being used
- `get_moe_expert_mapping` now checks all modules and returns from (in order of priority):
  - mapping from explicit `get_expert_mapping` defined in model
  - `RoutedExperts.get_expert_mapping`
- This means that it's no longer necessary to define `get_expert_mapping` on a model class as the only two consumers (LoRA and bitsandbytes) use `get_moe_expert_mapping` which will always be able to get it from the `RoutedExperts`

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix LSE log-base mismatch in DCP + FlashInfer MLA decode
author: GirasoleY
body:
## Purpose

FlashInfer's trtllm-gen MLA decode kernel returns LSE in **log2** (per flashinfer's own reference at `flashinfer/trace/templates/attention.py:81`: `logsumexp / log(2.0)`), but `MLAAttention`'s DCP combine in `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py` hard-codes `is_lse_base_on_e=True` when calling `cp_lse_ag_out_rs` / `dcp_a2a_lse_reduce`, asserting natural log. The mismatch makes the per-shard re-weighting use the wrong base when combining DCP partial attention outputs, producing incorrect softmax denominators and corrupted attention values.

This is the residual bug after #43729 ("Support DCP with FlashInfer MLA") merged: that PR wired LSE *return* through `FlashInferMLAImpl` (so DCP combine now runs), but left the combine assuming natural-log LSE.

**Symptom** on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 + FP8 KV + DCP=4 + `FLASHINFER_MLA`:
- Same prompt sent twice within one run produces different argmax tokens at 24/32 positions (vs ~4/32 noise floor on the no-DCP baseline with the same backend).
- Argmax tokens diverge from the no-DCP baseline on every test prompt.
- `TRITON_MLA`, FlashAttention MLA, FlashMLA, and Cutlass MLA are unaffected — their kernels emit LSE in natural log, matching the old hard-coded assumption.

**Fix:** declare each backend's LSE base as a capability flag (`lse_base_on_e`) on `AttentionImplBase` (default `True` / natural log), override it to `False` on `FlashInferMLAImpl`, and thread it through the DCP combine. The kernels already support both bases natively via their `IS_BASE_E` constexpr (`tl.exp/tl.log` vs `tl.exp2/tl.log2`), so there is no FP multiply or rounding loss — and adding another log2-emitting backend later is a one-line `ClassVar` instead of a call-site edit.

## Not a duplicate

- **#43729** (merged) added FlashInfer MLA + DCP support and the LSE-return plumbing, but not this log-base reconciliation.
- **#47074** ("Use larger workspace size for Flashinfer MLA LSE") touches the same file but fixes an orthogonal issue — a `trtllm_gen_softmax_workspace` allocation overflow — not the LSE base. The two are complementary.

## Test Plan & Results

Verified end-to-end on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 + DCP=4 + FP8 KV (Blackwell GB200) against a TEP4 (no DCP, same FlashInfer backend) baseline:

- **5-prompt greedy-decode refcomp** (max_tokens=32, top_p=1): **0 token mismatches** after fix vs `28+24+24+4+0` before; within-run stability `24/32 → 5/32` (matches baseline `4/32`).
- **5-shot GSM8K** (full 1319-problem set): baseline `0.9356 / 0.9363` vs DCP4-FI `0.9363 / 0.9371` (flexible / strict) — delta `+0.07% / +0.08%`, well under run-to-run variance.

Kernel-level equivalence test added (`tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py` was part of the original branch; this PR contains the core fix — happy to fold the test/CI-trigger commits back in if reviewers prefer).

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to diagnose and patch this issue end-to-end. The submitting author has reviewed every changed line.

title: [Perf] Use blocking CUDA events to avoid busy polling cuda driver lock
author: GirasoleY
body:
## Summary

When async scheduling is enabled, the per-step CUDA-event syncs default to spin-wait events that busy-poll the CUDA driver lock. Under per-step TP collective contention the main-thread spin can balloon on a *rotating* rank, making it arrive late at the eager `cross_device_reduce` all-reduce while the other ranks spin-wait on it — the occasional "long all-reduce" straggle. This makes those events **blocking (sleep)** instead, for both model runners:

- **V1** (`gpu_model_runner.py`): `prepare_inputs_event` — the load-bearing one, synchronized on the main thread every step in `synchronize_input_prep()` — plus the two `async_copy_ready_event` copies.
- **V2** (`gpu/async_utils.py` ×2, `gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`): `copy_event`. Note V2 has no per-step main-thread input-prep event, so there is no `prepare_inputs_event` analogue — this is the async-copy consistency fix only.

## Why `torch.get_device_module().Event(blocking=True)`

- **Not** `torch.cuda.Event(...)` — the `check-torch-cuda-call` lint (RFC #30679) forbids it.
- **Not** `torch.Event(blocking=True)` — that **silently ignores the blocking flag on CUDA** (verified no-op: cpu/wall = 1.0, still spins).
- `torch.get_device_module().Event(blocking=True)` is device-agnostic (passes the lint) and yields a *real* blocking event on CUDA. On CUDA it resolves to `torch.cuda.Event`, so it is the **identical event object**; the extra `get_device_module()` lookup is **~74 ns/call** (measured) — negligible.

## Results

**TP=4 MoE decode (the target case):** eager `cross_device_reduce` **p99 11.9 ms → 0.5 ms** (max 21 → 2.9 ms) at matched batch; py-spy confirms the main thread no longer stalls in `synchronize_input_prep`.

**Low-contention no-regression (Qwen3.5-0.8B, TP=1, 8k/1k, same-node controlled):** blocking is neutral-to-slightly-*faster* than spin (TPOT p50 spin 2.095 ms → cuda 2.008 ms / gdm 2.047 ms). `torch.cuda.Event` vs `get_device_module()` head-to-head on one node are within noise (+1.9%, ~1σ, n=3) — equivalent, exactly as the 74 ns lookup predicts.

Happy to gate this behind a flag if maintainers would rather not change the default spin-wait behavior.

title: [Bugfix] [Gemma4] Fix Gemma4 MTP draft model layers ignoring quant_config
author: ayush1399
body:
## Purpose

This PR fixes quantization support for the Gemma4 Eagle (MTP) draft model in speculative decoding. Previously, all layers in the Gemma4 MTP draft model were hardcoded to `quant_config=None`, causing quantized draft checkpoints to silently load incorrectly and produce 0% draft token acceptance.

This PR addresses the following:

- Use `get_draft_quant_config` in `Gemma4MultiTokenPredictor` and `Gemma4MTP` to obtain the draft model's quantization config.
- Propagate `quant_config` to all layers previously hardcoded to `None`: `q_proj`, `o_proj`, and `Attention` in `Gemma4MTPAttention`; the MLP in `Gemma4MTPDecoderLayer`; and `embed_tokens`, `pre_projection`, `post_projection`, and all decoder layers in `Gemma4MultiTokenPredictor`.
- Fix `Gemma4MultiTokenPredictor` incorrectly sourcing `quant_config` from `vllm_config.quant_config` (the target model's config) instead of the draft model's config.
- Fix `lm_head` in `Gemma4MTP` to receive the draft model's `quant_config`.

## Test Plan

Tested with a quantized Gemma4 31B target model with a quantized Gemma4 MTP draft model using
FP8 block quantization. Both checkpoints were quantized using the vLLM Project's LLM Compressor library.

Non-quantized models work exactly the same as before (no changes to behavior).

- Tests verify `get_draft_quant_config()` is used in place of `vllm_config.quant_config`

title: [Bench][BugFix] Fix empty decoder prompt for Cohere ASR in throughput benchmark
author: mganczarenko
body:
## Purpose

  Fix `ASRDataset.sample()` raising `"The decoder prompt cannot be empty"` when
  benchmarking Cohere ASR models (e.g. `CohereLabs/cohere-transcribe-03-2026`).

  `ASRDataset.sample()` previously only built a decoder prompt for OpenAI/Whisper
  tokenizers, falling back to `prompt = ""` for all others. `CohereAsrTokenizer`
  sets `skip_decoder_start_token=True` and does not override
  `skip_prompt_length_check`, so the empty prompt is rejected at inference time.

  **Fix:** detect `CohereAsrTokenizer` by class name (primary path — robust to
  local checkpoint paths) with a `name_or_path.lower()` fallback, and supply
  the English transcription control-token sequence the model requires.

  No existing PR addresses this specific issue. Related but distinct: #39259
  (Cohere ASR librosa import error — different failure mode).

title: [Bugfix] compressed-tensors: allow int8 grouped WNA16 MoE on Marlin
author: joerowell
body:
The num_bits==8 branch of CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod asserted group_size == -1, rejecting int8 experts quantized with a group size (e.g. group_size=128) even though Marlin supports them: uint8b128 is a supported quant type and MARLIN_SUPPORTED_GROUP_SIZES includes 128, and check_moe_marlin_supports_layer already admits group_size in {-1,32,64,128} (so the method is selected and then asserts against itself).

The assert isn't needed, and crucially, it unblocks mixed-precision INT models (such as `poolside/Laguna-XS.2-INT4`, which has INT4 & INT8 layers).

title: [Perf][MoE] Write FlashInfer combine into final output
author: samnordmann
body:
## Summary

Pass vLLM's preallocated MoE output tensor to FlashInfer one-sided combine,
removing the temporary combine output and subsequent `output.copy_()`.

Requires FlashInfer PR: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3776

## Performance

Nemotron Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4, one GB200 node (4 gpus), TP1/DP4/EP4, FlashInfer
one-sided, ISL/OSL 50000/2048, concurrency 16:

| | Baseline | Direct output | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput | 470.26 tok/s | 481.14 tok/s | **+2.31%** |
| Mean TPOT | 27.418 ms | 26.567 ms | **-3.10%** |

TTFT showed no statistically resolved change: 13.45 → 13.62 s nominally (+1.27%), while the four paired wave deltas ranged from -21.3% to +32.2%. Pending more perf data.


### Relation to #44452
This is a narrower alternative, not the same implementation. #44452 changes
the output-ownership contract across all modular MoE backends. This PR keeps
the existing contract and changes only FlashInfer one-sided by letting its
combine kernel write into the already-owned vLLM output buffer.

## Validation

- Nemotron Ultra NVFP4 end-to-end A/B reported above.
- `ruff check vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided.py`
- `ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided.py`

AI assistance was used to develop and benchmark this change.

title: [Kernel][XPU] Tensor-descriptor operand loads for Triton W8A8 scaled_mm
author: oonyshch
body:
### Two changes to the compressed-tensors W8A8 INT8 linear path.

1. Tensor-descriptor operand loads for `scaled_mm_kernel`
2. Enables that path on XPU at all.

### Per-kernel microbenchmark:

B70, int8 in / bf16 out, device self-time via torch.profiler: TD reduces self-time by 89-99% across M in {1, 64, 256} and K=N in {4096, 8192}, with max|plain - TD| = 0.0.

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, n=200:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TD off | 0.800 +/- 0.028 | 0.720 +/- 0.032 |
| TD on | 0.790 +/- 0.029 | 0.710 +/- 0.032 |

Both match the checkpoint's expected gsm8k range, which also confirms the new XPU dispatch path is numerically fine.

### Performance

1x Arc Pro B70, `neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8`, `--linear-backend triton --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching`, seed 42, `random` 1024-in/128-out. Only `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` differs between arms; 500/30/60 requests completed, 0 failed.

| | TD off | TD on | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| saturation output tok/s | 32.93 | 78.93 | +139.7% |
| saturation median TTFT | 956.5 s | 402.6 s | -57.9% |
| saturation median TPOT | 3318 ms | 1406 ms | -57.6% |
| concurrency 1 median TTFT / TPOT | 3142 ms / 273.0 ms | 1304 ms / 60.7 ms | -58.5% / -77.8% |
| concurrency 8 median TTFT / TPOT | 11155 ms / 396.6 ms | 4521 ms / 110.6 ms | -59.5% / -72.1% |

Checkpoint weights are stored transposed (`w_q.t()`, strides `(1, K)`), so the descriptor path also covers that orientation; without it the gate rejects every real layer and TD is never reached.

### Notes

- Stacks with the tensor-descriptor work under RFC #42545; gated by the consolidated `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` (auto-on for XPU, opt-in elsewhere).

title: [Spec Decode][DSpark] Add Gemma4-12B DSpark draft model
author: HangruiCao2000
body:
## Summary

Adds **DSpark** (semi-autoregressive block speculative decoding, built on #46995) for **Gemma4-12B**, for the `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7` checkpoint. Following the Laguna DFlash review, this is a **thin subclass reuse** of the existing stacks, not a standalone model.

## Design
- **`Gemma4DSparkModel(DFlashQwen3Model)`** — inherits the fused context-KV precompute. Gemma4's `attention_k_eq_v` is isolated behind the `_build_context_kv_buffers` / `_project_context_kv` hooks: project once through `k_proj` for all layers; **K** gets `k_norm` + RoPE downstream, **V = `v_norm`(same projection)** (no RoPE, no separate `v_proj`). Only `forward` (sandwich norms + `layer_scalar`) and `embed_input_ids` (`sqrt(hidden)` scaling) are overridden.
- **`Gemma4DSparkForCausalLM(Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM)`** — inherits the DSpark speculator contract (Markov head, `combine_hidden_states`, precompute delegation, `compute_logits`); overrides only the self-contained-checkpoint setup + flat weight loader.
- Attention / decoder-layer / MLP reuse the native Gemma4 MTP draft (`Gemma4MTPAttention` / `Gemma4MTPDecoderLayer` / `Gemma4MLP`).

## Changes (5 files, +408)
- `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_dspark.py` (new)
- `registry.py`: register `Gemma4DSparkModel`
- `config/speculative.py`: detect `method=dspark`, normalize `target_layer_ids` / `block_size`
- `tests/models/registry.py`: `Gemma4DSparkModel` example → `test_can_initialize` builds the draft over the base classes (**catches base-class API drift**)

title: [Distributed] Default FlashInfer allreduce to mnnvl on single node
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

The single-node default for the FlashInfer fused allreduce backend was pinned
to `trtllm` to work around an `mnnvl` cudagraph capture/replay hang
(#35772). That hang was root-caused and fixed upstream in FlashInfer
([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3304](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3304),
released in `>= 0.6.12`; vLLM currently pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.13`), so
the workaround is no longer needed.

This PR makes `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=auto` select `mnnvl` for both
single- and multi-node setups, giving a single uniform backend and resolving
the long-standing "switch back to auto when the issue is resolved" TODO in
`_resolve_fi_ar_backend`.

## Behavior

- `auto` + multi-node → `mnnvl` (unchanged; `trtllm` has no multi-node support).
- `auto` + single-node → `mnnvl` (**changed** from `trtllm`).
- Explicit `trtllm` / `mnnvl` → respected (unchanged).

### NVSwitch fallback

`mnnvl` requires NVSwitch multicast. On single-node topologies without it
(NVLink-bridge / PCIe), the mnnvl workspace cannot be created. Previously
`trtllm` (IPC P2P) was always used there. To avoid regressing those setups
from fused allreduce to plain NCCL, `auto` now falls back to `trtllm` when the
single-node `mnnvl` workspace fails to initialize, so fused allreduce stays
enabled. Multi-node and explicit selections keep their existing behavior.

## Test Plan / Results

Hardware: single node, 4× NVIDIA GB200 (SM100, NVSwitch fabric),
FlashInfer 0.6.12 (contains the fix).

Existing fused-allreduce pass test, which spawns TP=2 and exercises the
`mnnvl` cudagraph capture/replay path that previously hung:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py -k "mnnvl" -q
```

Result: `10 passed, 14 deselected in 382.43s` — no hang.

Backend-resolution unit check (mocked node count):

| env | nodes | resolved |
|-----|-------|----------|
| auto | 1 | `('mnnvl', fallback=True)` |
| auto | 2 | `('mnnvl', fallback=False)` |
| trtllm | 1 | `('trtllm', fallback=False)` |
| mnnvl | 1 | `('mnnvl', fallback=False)` |

Lint: `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, etc.) passes.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs (`flashinfer allreduce backend mnnvl`, `35772 in:body`); no
open PR changes the single-node auto backend default. Existing related PRs
(#40970 benchmark fix, #39758 quant-fusion perf, #38136 multi-node selection)
do not touch this default.

## Known tradeoff

For quantized models on a single node, quant fusion (FP8/FP4) still requires
`trtllm` (`get_fi_ar_quant_workspace`). With non-quant patterns now on `mnnvl`,
such models may allocate both an `mnnvl` and a `trtllm` workspace rather than
sharing one. This is a deliberate tradeoff for the uniform/default `mnnvl`
path; reviewers who prefer to avoid it could instead keep `trtllm` when a quant
fusion pattern is present.

---

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate the upstream fix, implement the
change, and run the test above. A human maintainer has reviewed every changed
line.

title: [BugFix][Spec Decode] Compact shared topk indices buffer after first MTP draft step
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# Context
Deepseek-style topk index selection for MTP has a bug during proposal stage when the topk indices are shared among all MTP draft step forward passes. After the first draft step, `set_skip_topk` is called on the MTP model to force the remaining draft steps to reuse the same topk indices values (held within `topk_indices_buffer` of the attention module). The issue is that the first draft forward pass will fill the `topk_indices_buffer` tensor with the per-request, multi-token, bonus + accepted tokens. So they are laid out like:
```
a0, a1, a2, a3, b0, b1, b2, b3, c0, c1, c2, c3, ...
```
with a total of `num_tokens = num_reqs * (1 + num_spec_tokens))` rows.

But the remaining `num_spec_tokens - 1` draft steps are expecting a layout of:
```
a3, b3, c3, ...
``` 
with a total of `num_tokens = num_reqs`. Consequently, they use the wrong topk indices, potentially from other requests. The draft tokens becomes lower quality, and acceptance rates drop.

# This PR
Fixes the above issue by compacting the topk indices for the last query token of each request, so that they are contiguous at the front of the buffer.

# Validation
**Server**
```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4 \
  -tp 4 \
  -O3 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=False \
  --speculative_config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "full_decode_only", "mode": 0}'
```

**Bench**
```
vllm-bench \
    --model $MODEL \
    --backend openai-chat \
    --dataset-name speed-bench \
    --speed-bench-config throughput_16k \
    --speed-bench-max-input-len 10240 \
    --speed-bench-category low_entropy \
    --request-rate inf \
    --max-concurrency 32 \
    --num-prompts 256 \
    --output-len 2048 \
    --ignore-eos \
    --temperature 1.0 \
    --percentile-metrics "ttft,tpot,itl,e2el" \
    --result-dir ~/dev \
    --save-result
```

**Results**
Metric | index sharing = True, main | index sharing = True, #47238
-- | -- | --
Request throughput (req/s) | 0.74 | 0.79
Output token throughput (tok/s) | 1517.50 | 1625.59

title: Fixes non-coalesced HBM access in marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_kernel_awq
author: flutist
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes non-coalesced HBM access in `marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_kernel_awq` (AWQ int4-fp8 weight preprocessing kernel, model-load cold path).

### Problem
Original thread mapping used `threadIdx.x` for the row dimension:
```cpp
qweight[(blockIdx.x * 32 + threadIdx.x) * size_n / 8 + blockIdx.y]
```
Adjacent threads (tidx 0..31) read elements strided by `size_n/8` int32 words — non-coalesced, ~12.5% sector utilization on large matrices.

### Fix
Remap `threadIdx.x` to the column dimension (stride 1, fully coalesced):
```cpp
int col = blockIdx.y * 32 + threadIdx.x;
if (col >= size_n / 8) return;
int32_t val = qweight[blockIdx.x * (size_n / 8) + col];
```
- Grid: `dim3 blocks(size_k, (size_n / 8 + 31) / 32)`, `blockIdx.x` indexes rows directly
- Alignment relaxed from implicit `size_n % 256` to explicit `size_n % 8` + tail boundary check

### Coverage equivalence
Old: `(row=bx*32+tidx, col=by)`; New: `(row=bx, col=by*32+tidx)` — same `[0,size_k) × [0,size_n/8)` element space, each processed exactly once, logically equivalent.

## Why is this not duplicating an existing PR?
Searched open PRs/issues for "marlin preprocess" and coalesced-access fixes on this kernel; found only general marlin performance discussions, no PR addressing the non-coalesced thread mapping in `marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_kernel_awq`.

## Test commands and results

### Correctness
```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py::test_marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_awq \
       tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py::test_marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_without_zp -v
```
Both pass.

### Performance
```bash
python -c "
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
k,n,g = 16384,16384,128
qw = torch.randint(0,2**31,(k,n//8),dtype=torch.int32,device='cuda')
qz = torch.randint(0,16,(k//g,n//8),dtype=torch.int32,device='cuda')
for _ in range(5): ops.marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess(qw,qz)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
s,e = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
s.record()
for _ in range(50): ops.marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess(qw,qz)
e.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f'{s.elapsed_time(e)/50*1e3:.1f} us/iter')
"
```
- Before: 1291.1 us/iter
- After: 581.9 us/iter
- Speedup: **2.22x**

Control: the unchanged `without_zp` kernel path shows no regression (557.7 → 557.4 us/iter, within noise), confirming measurement stability.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Reserve the KV null block when validating max_model_len
author: 92hyungjun
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #35541 (still not fully resolved).

That issue was previously addressed by #41069, which made the startup capacity check account for `num_gpu_blocks_override`. However, #41069 validates against the **total** block count, so the exact-boundary case — where the KV cache holds exactly as many blocks as a `max_model_len` request needs — still passes at startup and then hangs at runtime. It also only covers the override path, not `kv_cache_memory_bytes` or profiled memory. This PR completes the fix.

`BlockPool` permanently reserves one block as the null block, so only `num_gpu_blocks - 1` blocks are usable for requests (`BlockPool.get_usage()` already subtracts it). But the startup check (`_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` in `get_kv_cache_configs`) compares `max_model_len` against the **total** block count. A config with exactly `ceil(max_model_len / block_size)` blocks passes the check (it logs `Maximum concurrency for <max_model_len> tokens per request: 1.00x`) but is one usable block short at runtime, so a request can never be scheduled and the engine hangs (0 tok/s).

### When it happens

All sources of the block count flow into the same check, so any can hit the boundary:

- `num_gpu_blocks_override = N` with `max_model_len == N * block_size`
- `kv_cache_memory_bytes` sized to exactly `N` blocks
- `gpu_memory_utilization` (including the default) when the profiled block count equals `ceil(max_model_len / block_size)` — uncommon (auto-profiling usually leaves head-room), but the same bug.

### Why it hangs

With `block_size=16`, 50 total blocks -> 49 usable (784 tokens), and `max_model_len=800` (needs 50 blocks):

1. Startup: needed = 50, total = 50 -> the check passes.
2. A prompt fits in the 49 usable blocks and starts decoding.
3. When the length crosses 784 tokens it needs a 50th block; only 49 are usable, so `allocate_slots()` returns `None`.
4. The request is preempted, `num_computed_tokens` reset to 0, and requeued.
5. It is re-admitted, needs the same 50 blocks, and fails again. Nothing is running to preempt and there is no infeasibility guard, so it retries identically every step.
6. `running == 0`, `waiting >= 1`, `scheduled_tokens == 0` every step -> 0 tok/s.

### Reproduction (current `main`)

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

# 50 total KV blocks -> BlockPool reserves 1 null block -> 49 usable = 784 tokens.
# max_model_len=800 needs ceil(800/16)=50 blocks: the check counts the 50 total
# blocks and passes, but only 49 are usable.
llm = LLM(
    model="facebook/opt-125m",
    load_format="dummy",
    block_size=16,
    num_gpu_blocks_override=50,
    max_model_len=800,
)
sp = SamplingParams(max_tokens=40, ignore_eos=True)
llm.generate({"prompt_token_ids": list(range(1, 771))}, sp)
# current main: hangs forever. With this PR: raises ValueError at startup.
```

## The fix

In `get_kv_cache_configs`, reserve one block (the null block) in the capacity used by the admission check and auto-fit, while allocation keeps using the full memory. Since all sources of the block count funnel into `available_memory`, this covers `num_gpu_blocks_override`, `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, and profiled memory with one change, and keeps auto-fit consistent with the check.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k reserves_null_block
```

Plus the reproduction above.

## Test Result

- Reproduction — before: hangs at 0 tok/s; after: raises at startup with `ValueError: ... max seq len (800) ... estimated maximum model length is 784` (= 49 usable blocks × 16).
- New unit tests cover the boundary for both the override and the memory-derived paths; related `test_kv_cache_utils.py` tests pass with no regressions.

## Not a duplicate

#41069 (merged) is override-only and validates against the total block count, leaving the null-block boundary unfixed. #35542 (an earlier, unmerged attempt) added a separate override-only check. This PR fixes the shared capacity accounting for all sources of the block count.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and draft this change; all changed lines were reviewed and the tests were run locally as described above.

title: [Bugfix] Guard CUDA-only rms_norm_per_block_quant in FUSED_OPS for non-CUDA builds
author: tsvikas
body:
## Purpose

`FUSED_OPS` in `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rms_quant_fusion.py` dereferences `torch.ops._C.rms_norm_per_block_quant.default` at **import time**, but that is a CUDA-only custom op. On builds where it is not registered (e.g. `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=tpu`), merely importing this module raises `AttributeError`. Because the module is imported by `pass_manager` and several sibling fusion passes, this breaks importing models that pull this path (surfaced building MiniMax-M3 on TPU).

## Fix

Guard the four `rms_norm_per_block_quant` entries behind `hasattr(torch.ops._C, "rms_norm_per_block_quant")`, mirroring the existing `per_token_group_fp8_quant` / `scaled_fp4_quant` guards a few lines above for `QUANT_OPS`. On CUDA the op is present, so all four entries are populated exactly as before — no behavior change.

## Test Plan / Result

On a `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=tpu` build, `import vllm.compilation.passes.fusion.rms_quant_fusion` (and importing a model that pulls it) no longer raises `AttributeError`. On CUDA, `FUSED_OPS` is unchanged.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and validated the behavior end-to-end; the change is a minimal import guard mirroring the existing `per_token_group_fp8_quant` pattern in the same file. Attribution is included as a `Co-authored-by:` commit trailer.

title: [Bugfix] Don't read KV cache past `seq_len` in triton paged attn kernels
author: njhill
body:
The Triton unified_attention and ROCm paged-decode kernels load KV cache slots beyond seq_len (the unwritten tail of the last partial block) and rely on the score mask to drop them. That is unsafe when the tail is non-finite: masked positions get softmax weight 0, but 0 * NaN = NaN still poisons the output. In `compute_tile_loop_bounds` the causal-derived `max_seq_prefix_len` can additionally overshoot seq_len for non-causal (cross-)attention, widening the over-read.

- `triton_attention_helpers.compute_tile_loop_bounds`: clamp the non-causal / mixed / prefix branch to exactly `seq_len`.
- `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.kernel_paged_attention_2d`: bound the K/V loads to `seq_len` (other=0.0), matching the score mask.

Surfaced as Whisper cross-attention emitting garbage on ROCm once MRV2 made it the default model runner. The over-read only affects output when the unwritten tail is non-finite (NaN under MRV2 on ROCm; harmless zero under MRV1 and on CUDA via 0 * 0). Freed KV blocks are never re-zeroed, so correctness relies on never reading past seq_len. MRV2 (unlike MRV1) runs a dummy warmup forward; for encoder-decoder it has no encoder input, so cross-attn attends to zero keys - an empty softmax that yields NaN on the ROCm kernel - and that NaN lands in the block tails the first real request reuses. The fix is correct regardless, since reading beyond seq_len is never valid.

I will open a separate PR to improve the MRV2 warmup in encoder-decoder case.

Claude was used to help find this!

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Apply SWA lookup mask before hashing/key build
author: zhewenl
body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeStoreWorker._lookup_full` builds its prefix-lookup candidate keys with
`for chunk_id, h in enumerate(group_hashes)`. Because `group_hashes` is a
`Sequence`, that iteration performs a per-chunk `__getitem__` — a `memoryview`
slice plus a `BlockHash` allocation — for **every** chunk, including the
sparse-attention (SWA) chunks that `lookup_mask` discards one line later.

On DeepSeek-V4-style hybrid configs (small SWA `block_size` over a long
context) the masked-out chunks are the large majority of the scan, so almost
all of that per-chunk allocation is wasted work on the hot lookup path.

This PR reorders the loop to check the mask **before** touching `group_hashes`,
indexing it only for chunks that survive the mask:

- `max_chunks = min(len(group_hashes), cdiv(token_len, spec_block_size))`
- `for chunk_id in range(mask_limit): if masked: continue; h = group_hashes[chunk_id]`

The output is unchanged: `cdiv(token_len, block_size)` reproduces the previous
`start_idx >= token_len` break, and `min(max_chunks, len(mask))` reproduces the
previous `chunk_id >= len(mask)` guard. Only the wasted allocations for masked
chunks are removed.

## Results

Validated on the **exact code in this PR** (a clean checkout of upstream `main` +
this change), DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 2-node, hybrid full-MLA + 4 SWA groups, long-context
workload. Two back-to-back runs — one with the old `enumerate` loop, one with this
PR — at a **matched candidate-key count** (~17.6k keys/lookup, within 0.3%), so the
phases are directly comparable. Worker-side per-`lookup()` timing, lookup-weighted
across DP ranks:

| phase | before (`enumerate`) | after (this PR) | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| candidate key build | 39.3 ms (53%) | 16.2 ms (37%) | **−59%** |
| total `lookup()` | 73.5 ms | 43.1 ms | **−41%** |
| exists / mask-build / find-hit | 5.2 / 4.5 / 2.3 ms | 5.1 / 4.5 / 2.3 ms | flat |

The `exists`, mask-build, and `find_longest_cache_hit` phases are unchanged — the
only thing removed is the per-masked-chunk `BlockHash` allocation — confirming the
speedup comes solely from not materializing hashes for chunks the mask discards.
Keys sent and hit results are identical. The benefit scales with mask sparsity, so
it is largest exactly where the scan is most expensive (small SWA block sizes /
long contexts).

## Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs touching the Mooncake store connector (`gh pr list --repo
vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "mooncake lookup" / "mooncake swa" /
"mooncake key"`). None modify the `_lookup_full` candidate-key loop; the closest
(#45503) is an unrelated LookupKeyServer teardown fix. #45969 (compact keys +
zero-copy wire) optimized key *size* and the scheduler↔worker wire format, not
the worker's per-chunk candidate scan, so this is complementary.

## Test

Adds a focused unit test, `test_lookup_applies_swa_mask_before_accessing_hashes`,
that records which block-hash indices are accessed before the store RPC and
asserts only the reachable boundaries are touched (masked SWA chunks are
skipped) — i.e. it guards the "mask before access" property, not just output.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -q
# 74 passed
```

AI assistance was used for this change (profiling, the loop rewrite, the test,
and this PR text). The performance numbers are from real GB200 runs. The human
submitter has reviewed every changed line and will own review follow-ups.

title: [BugFix] Fix ModelOpt mixed-precision quantization for sparse `quantized_layers` configs.
author: danielafrimi
body:
Fix ModelOpt mixed-precision dispatch so missing sibling layers do not inherit
quantization from unrelated siblings.

The previous fallback could see one quantized layer under a parent, e.g. `o_proj`,
and incorrectly apply the same quantization to a missing sibling like `qkv_proj`.
This is unsafe for sparse mixed FP8/NVFP4 configs.

Now we only infer quantization for known packed projections:
`qkv_proj <- q_proj/k_proj/v_proj` and `gate_up_proj <- gate_proj/up_proj`.


For Nemotron Super NVFP4, the config is sparse and mixed precision.

title: [Model Runner V2][MTP] Share topk index buffer between draft steps
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# Context
Deepseek-style topk index selection for MTP has a bug during proposal stage when the topk indices are shared among all MTP draft step forward passes. After the first draft step, `set_skip_topk` is called on the MTP model to force the remaining draft steps to reuse the same topk indices values (held within `topk_indices_buffer` of the attention module).

This feature was introduce in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44420 for Model Runner V1.

# This PR
Enable this feature for Model Runner V2. I didn't want to leak model-specific optimizations into `AutoRegressiveSpeculator`, so i introduced a callback pattern. New optimizations/features that need to run at specific points during the `propose` operation can inherit from this class and override whatever methods are needed.

```
class AutoRegressiveSpeculatorCallbacks(Protocol):
    def on_prefill_begin(self) -> None: ...
    def on_prefill_end(self, last_token_indices: torch.Tensor) -> None: ...
    def on_multi_step_decode_begin(self) -> None: ...
    def on_multi_step_decode_end(self) -> None: ...
```

The topk indexer sharing feature registers itself after `MTPSpeculator` loads its draft model. After determining whether the draft model is a MTP model that can do index sharing AND index sharing is enabled, it is added to the list of callback classes for the auto regressive speculator to call during prefill begin/end and multi step decode begin/end.

# Benchmarks
**Server**
```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4 \
  -tp 4 \
  -O3 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \

  --speculative_config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "full_decode_only", "mode": 0}'
```

**Bench**
```

title: [CI/Build][AMD] Fix ROCm OOM in eagle_correctness_heavy by reserving CUDA graph memory
author: peizhang56
body:
## Purpose

test_eagle_correctness_heavy builds a reference engine and a speculative engine back to back in one process, and its parametrized cases run sequentially. On the AMD "V1 e2e (4 GPUs)" step the TRITON_ATTN Llama-4-Scout cases (llama4_eagle, llama4_eagle_mm) aborted at engine init with HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES ("Available Free mem : 0 MB") right after CUDA graph capture, while the same model passed on ROCM_AITER_FA.

There are two independent problems, both fixed here:

1. Lazy VRAM reclaim between engines. ROCm frees VRAM lazily, so after cleanup_dist_env_and_memory() the next engine can start memory profiling while the previous engine's VRAM is still resident, read inflated free memory, and size the KV pool too large. Fixed by a wait_for_rocm_memory_to_settle() barrier after each engine teardown so the next engine profiles against a clean device (reuses the existing helper; no-op off ROCm).

2. CUDA graph capture memory not reserved on ROCm (root cause of the remaining OOM). The memory profiler skipped CUDA graph profiling on ROCm (#36720), so the KV cache was sized as if capture were free; capture then had to fit in the (1 - gpu_memory_utilization) slack, and when the fixed capture cost exceeded that slack, startup OOMed. #36720 skipped ROCm because torch.cuda.mem_get_info() and graph_pool_handle() produced incorrect/negative estimates. Both causes are gone: #44825 moved the profiler to torch.accelerator.get_memory_info (reliable on ROCm, already used by the AMD-CI mem tests), and graph_pool_handle resolves to the same torch.cuda handle the live capture path already uses on ROCm. So this re-enables CUDA graph memory profiling on ROCm; XPU stays excluded (#39977).

This supersedes the earlier per-model gpu_memory_utilization=0.85 override (addressing @AndreasKaratzas's review): the profiler now reserves capture memory automatically, which is portable across GPU sizes (a fixed byte cost, not a utilization ratio that maps to different absolute headroom on MI300 vs MI325). The override is removed in this PR.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to diagnose and implement this change. Not a duplicate: no open PR re-enables ROCm CUDA graph memory profiling (#46932 fixes negative estimates on NVIDIA unified-memory GPUs, a different platform and failure mode).

## Test Plan

```
pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py -k "eagle_correctness_heavy"
```

Hardware: AMD MI300 (gfx942), 4 GPUs, TP=4. Run with `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`. Reproduced with the `TRITON_ATTN` cases run back to back (the CI ordering that failed).

## Test Result

Before: the two `TRITON_ATTN` heavy cases fail during engine init:

```
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES: ... Available Free mem : 0 MB
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError'
FAILED v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py::test_eagle_correctness_heavy[TRITON_ATTN-llama4_eagle]
FAILED v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py::test_eagle_correctness_heavy[TRITON_ATTN-llama4_eagle_mm]
```

After: both cases pass back to back, and the barrier drains VRAM to ~0.28 GiB on all 4 GPUs before each subsequent engine starts:

```
Done waiting for stable free GPU memory on devices devices=[0, 1, 2, 3] ... dur_s=5.10
================= 2 passed, 16 warnings in 2110.20s (0:35:10) =================
```

No `HSA_STATUS_ERROR` occurred in the passing run.

title: [Bugfix][Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Fix int32 offset overflow in block verification kernels
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

`_compute_cumulative_log_p_kernel` and `_compute_local_residual_mass_kernel` (used when `rejection_sample_method="block"`) multiply int32 logit/request-state indices by vocab-scale strides before int64 promotion. With a GLM-scale vocab (~155k tokens) the byte offset wraps once `logit_idx * vocab >= 2**31` (`logit_idx >= ~13.8k`, reachable with large `max_num_seqs` × `1 + num_speculative_tokens`), or once `req_state_idx * num_speculative_steps * vocab >= 2**31` for the draft-logits buffer. Block verification then reads out-of-bounds logits for requests late in the batch, corrupting acceptance decisions (or crashing with an illegal memory access).

The sibling kernels (`_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel`, `_rejection_kernel`, `_resample_kernel`) already promote these indices to int64 (#46560 fixed the same class of bug in the sampler kernels); this brings the two remaining block-verification kernels in line.

Found while auditing the V2 spec-decode sampling path for #47239 (not the cause of that issue — this path requires the non-default `rejection_sample_method="block"`).

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

`gh pr list --search "rejection sampler overflow"` / `"block verification int32"` — no open PR touches these kernels or this overflow.

## Test Plan

New GPU regression test `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py`: runs one request through `rejection_sample(use_block_verification=True)` alone at index 0, then again placed past the int32 overflow threshold (target-side `logit_idx=15000` with V=155264, and draft-side `req_state_idx=8000` with k=2), asserting identical outputs. Each case allocates ~5 GiB.

## Test Result

```
$ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py -q   # GB200
2 passed

# with the kernel fix reverted (git stash), same test:
2 failed, 2 errors   # CUDA illegal access / output mismatch from wrapped offsets
```

Pre-commit (ruff, mypy) passes on changed files.

## AI assistance disclosure

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [perf]Add fused Kimi image preprocessing
author: Kevin-XiongC
body: ## Summary This PR adds a fused CPU image preprocessing path for Kimi-K2.5/K2.6 vision chunks. - Adds `KimiK25FusedVisionProcessor`, a vLLM-local processor that preserves the Kimi NaViT resize/token semantics while fusing padding, normalization, and patchification through numba. - Uses the fused processor automatically when numba is available. - Falls back to the remote HF image processor when numba is unavailable. - Uses a small `uint8 -> normalized float32` lookup table in the fused kernel to avoid repeating the normalization arithmetic for every pixel. ## Benchmark Benchmarked on an x86 host with 192 visible CPUs using synthetic RGB inputs. Benchmark script: https://gist.github.com/Kevin-XiongC/601fa73e2ed45709981ff9f5f482d9d1 Case: ```text 8 x 2048x2048 images warmup=3 iters=20 ``` With `NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=192` and OpenCV threads set to 192: ```text origin processor: mean 1315.969 ms, p50 1324.421 ms, p90 1337.793 ms, p99 1338.415 ms PIL resize + formula fused: mean 207.421 ms, p50 194.645 ms, p90 265.659 ms, p99 273.600 ms PIL resize + LUT fused: mean 189.631 ms, p50 179.403 ms, p90 243.703 ms, p99 250.829 ms OpenCV resize + LUT fused: mean 128.490 ms, p50 107.043 ms, p90 181.956 ms, p99 188.809 ms ``` Observed speedups: ```text PIL LUT fused vs PIL formula fused: 1.094x PIL LUT fused vs origin: 6.940x OpenCV LUT fused vs origin: 10.242x ``` The LUT path is numerically aligned with the formula-based fused path: ```text formula_lut_grid_equal=True formula_lut_max_abs_diff=0.00000006 formula_lut_allclose_1e-6=True ``` OpenCV resize was faster in these benchmarks, but it is not used in this PR because its bicubic output does not numerically match the current PIL bicubic output: ```text grid_equal=True pixel_max_abs_diff=0.50980389 pixel_mean_abs_diff=0.08271982 pixel_allclose_1e-5=False ``` This PR uses the PIL resize path to preserve existing preprocessing semantics and only fuses the CPU operations after resize. ## TEST

title: [ROCm] Enable DeepSeek-V4 DSpark speculative decoding on AMD (MI350X / MI355X, gfx950)
author: larryli2-amd
body:
## Summary

DSpark speculative decoding for **DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T)** was previously **NVIDIA-only** in vLLM:
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/__init__.py` sets `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM = None` on ROCm, so
`--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark",...}'` fails at model-load time on AMD GPUs.

This PR enables DSpark on ROCm by porting the draft model to the AMD subpackage and wiring the two
pieces the draft depends on that were missing on the AMD path (the EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state interface
on the target model, and the non-causal sliding-window-attention ragged-buffer sizing). The base
DeepSeek-V4 model, the ROCm sparse-MLA / sparse-SWA backends, and the MHC
`aiter`/`triton` kernels already existed on ROCm — DSpark reuses all of them, so this is a wiring
port, not new kernel work.

Model: [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark)

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/__init__.py` | Un-stub the ROCm branch: import `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` from `.amd.dspark` instead of setting it to `None`. |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py` *(new)* | ROCm port of `nvidia/dspark.py`: imports the AMD `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`, routes the MHC head through the `HCHeadOp` / `MHCPostOp` CustomOp dispatchers (aiter/tilelang/triton) instead of the NVIDIA-only tilelang kernels, gates the trailing `mhc_post` on `use_fused_mhc`, and drops the mega-MoE weight path (absent in `amd/model.py`). |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py` | Add the EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state interface (`EagleModelMixin` on the inner model, `SupportsEagle3` on `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`) and collect mean-pooled aux hidden states at the DSpark target layers in `forward`. DSpark consumes target layers `dspark_target_layer_ids = [58, 59, 60]`; this is the same mechanism EAGLE3/DFlash use to hand intermediate hidden states to a draft model. |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py` | Size the ROCm sparse-SWA ragged buffer for the non-causal (DSpark draft) index width. See below. |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | Reject `num_speculative_tokens < dspark_block_size` for `method="dspark"` with a clear error (DSpark is a semi-autoregressive block drafter, so sub-block speculative lengths are unsupported). |
| `tests/models/test_registry.py` | `DSparkDraftModel` is now supported on ROCm too; the registry-import test previously skipped it on all non-CUDA platforms. Skip only on platforms where it is still stubbed (i.e. not CUDA and not ROCm). |

### Why the sparse-SWA ragged-buffer change is required

`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder` allocated its persistent ragged index buffer for the
**causal** window width only (`max_tokens * window_size`) and passed `window_size` as the
max-entries-per-row to `_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers`. DSpark's **non-causal** draft widens each
token's SWA index list to `noncausal_index_width = cdiv(window_size + num_speculative_tokens, 128) * 128`,
so the actual `nnz` overflows the buffer and crashes with e.g. `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a
(896) must match the size of tensor b (1792) at non-singleton dimension 0`.

The non-causal path was never exercised on ROCm before (its only user, DSpark, was stubbed), which is
why this was latent. The fix is backward-compatible: for the non-DSpark/causal path
`noncausal_index_width == 0`, so `max(window_size, noncausal_index_width) == window_size` and
`base.decode_swa_indices.shape[-1] == window_size` — i.e. a no-op for the existing base path, and
correct for DSpark.

## Results (8× AMD MI350X, gfx950)

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-09663abde0f50944a8d5ea30120666024b503faa` (vLLM `0.23.1rc1.dev714+g09663abde`)
- Recipe: InferenceX `dsv4-fp4-mi355x-vllm` (TP=8, `--moe-backend aiter`, FP8 KV cache, full CUDA graph `mode:3 FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`)
- Workload: `ISL/OSL = 1024/1024`, `--ignore-eos` (fixed 1024 output tokens/request), greedy
- The DeepSeek-V4-Pro checkpoint is mixed precision: FP4 (MXFP4) MoE experts + FP8 block-scaled dense/attention + FP8 (`fp8_ds_mla`) KV cache.

### Throughput @ concurrency = 8

| Config | Output tok/s **per GPU** | TPOT (ms) | Speedup vs baseline | Mean acceptance length | Avg draft acceptance | Per-position acceptance |
|--------|--------------------------|-----------|---------------------|------------------------|----------------------|-------------------------|
| **STP baseline** (no draft) | 32.6 | 29.7 | 1.00× | — | — | — |
| **DSpark** `num_speculative_tokens=6` | **51.9** | **17.9** | **1.59×** | **2.94** | 32.4% | `0.819 / 0.403 / 0.247 / 0.193 / 0.158 / 0.122` |

TPOT speedup vs baseline: DSpark n=6 = 1.66×.

**Quality:** on a fixed 10-prompt set (raw `/v1/completions`, temperature 0), STP and DSpark n=6
produce matching, correct answers. Re-running the DSpark n=6 config directly from this PR's committed
code reproduces the throughput (~52 tok/s/GPU, within run-to-run variance).

## Reproduction

All commands run inside the ROCm container. Environment: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.

### 1. Serve

**STP baseline (no speculative decoding):**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark --port 8000 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --trust-remote-code --moe-backend aiter \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'
```

**DSpark** — add (`num_speculative_tokens=6` was the best-performing value in testing):

```bash
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'
```

### 2. Benchmark (InferenceX `benchmark_serving.py`)

```bash
# from InferenceX/utils/bench_serving/
python3 benchmark_serving.py \
    --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark --backend vllm \
    --base-url http://0.0.0.0:8000 \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.8 \
    --num-prompts 80 --max-concurrency 8 \
    --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \
    --num-warmups 16 \
    --percentile-metrics 'ttft,tpot,itl,e2el' \
    --save-result --trust-remote-code
```

- `num-prompts = 10 × max-concurrency`, `num-warmups = 2 × max-concurrency` (InferenceX convention).
- **For the DSpark runs, add `--use-chat-template --dsv4`.** Spec-decode acceptance
  degrades on raw random tokens; the DeepSeek-V4 chat encoding is required for meaningful acceptance
  numbers (matches the InferenceX spec-decoding recipes).
- Output-throughput-per-GPU = `output_throughput / tensor_parallel_size`.

### 3. Acceptance metrics

```bash
curl -s http://0.0.0.0:8000/metrics | grep -E 'spec_decode_num_(drafts_total|draft_tokens_total|accepted_tokens_total|accepted_tokens_per_pos_total)'
```

- Mean acceptance length = `1 + accepted_tokens_total / drafts_total`
- Per-position acceptance rate = `accepted_tokens_per_pos_total[i] / drafts_total`

## Note: known limitation

Greedy DSpark occasionally produces intermittent, prompt/run-dependent garbled output (not tied to a
specific `num_speculative_tokens`). Root-causing this is left as a follow-up.

## Caveats

- Validated on **MI350X**; the InferenceX reference recipe targets **MI355X** (same gfx950 family,
  higher clocks/TDP), so absolute throughput may differ. STP vs DSpark were all measured on
  the same hardware and image, so the relative speedups are directly comparable.
- Measured with the pinned nightly image above; the InferenceX recipe pins `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.22.0`.

title: [MoE] FI autotuning: max bucket = max token count [e.g. `DP_size*MNBT`]
author: netanel-haber
body:
vLLM does not pass `tune_max_num_tokens` to FlashInfer’s BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 TRT-LLM MoE kernels. FlashInfer therefore ends autotuning at its default maximum bucket of 8192. This can be too low. The estimated maximum token count is: `DP size * max_num_batched_tokens` Larger inputs still run, but use a tactic tuned for a smaller bucket. This PR passes that estimate to FlashInfer while keeping 8192 as the minimum tuning range. MXFP4 is unchanged to keep this PR focused. ### Representative result: +2.62% output TPS Nemotron Ultra NVFP4, DP=4, TP=1, EP, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, concurrency 128: - Before: 21 buckets ending at 8192. - After: 23 buckets ending at 32768, adding 16384 and 32768. | Metric | Before (n=3) | After (n=4) | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output TPS | 1706.8 ± 2.1 | 1751.5 ± 3.8 | +2.62% | | TTFT (ms) | 30188.1 ± 283.2 | 29250.8 ± 126.1 | -3.10% |
Benchmark details **Environment:** 4× NVIDIA GB200 GPUs, FlashInfer v0.6.13. Server: ```bash vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 -dp 4 -tp 1 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-flashinfer-autotune ``` Benchmark: ```bash # Avoid vLLM DP load-balancer noise by routing directly to DP ranks. haproxy -f <(echo $'listen x\n mode http\n bind 127.0.0.1:8001-8004\n http-request set-header X-data-parallel-rank %[dst_port,sub(8001)]\n server x 127.0.0.1:8000') & aiperf profile --url http://127.0.0.1:8001 --url http://127.0.0.1:8002 --url http://127.0.0.1:8003 --url http://127.0.0.1:8004 --num-requests 256 --concurrency 128 --endpoint-type completions --streaming --isl 50000 --osl 2048 ```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Add missing draft_id_to_target_id to DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM
author: Laurent-Zhang
body:
## What this PR does

Fixes #47418

`DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` is a full-vocab draft model (draft ids are target ids, no d2t remapping). However, `DSparkSpeculator.load_draft_model` accesses `model.draft_id_to_target_id` unconditionally, causing an `AttributeError` when running DeepSeek-V4-Flash with DSpark.

### Root Cause

In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py:86`:
```python
if self.draft_logits is not None and model.draft_id_to_target_id is not None:
```

This line assumes the draft model has a `draft_id_to_target_id` attribute, but `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` doesn't define it.

### Fix

Add `draft_id_to_target_id = None` as a class attribute to `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, consistent with:
- The full-vocab identity mapping already implemented in `map_draft_to_target()` (returns draft_ids directly)
- The pattern used in `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` (which sets it to `None` when draft_vocab == target_vocab)

### Testing

The fix is minimal and follows the existing pattern. The check `model.draft_id_to_target_id is not None` will now correctly evaluate to `False`, skipping the d2t scatter logic that isn't needed for full-vocab drafts.
