title: [Bugfix] Fix pooled Whisper encoder sliding-window kernel size
author: njhill
body:
The causal Whisper encoder pools `block_pool_size` encoder tokens per KV block, so its `SlidingWindowSpec.sliding_window` is expressed in pooled units for the KV cache manager. The attention kernel, however, reads its window from the same spec field but runs on the `block_pool_size`x-expanded (unpooled) sequence, so it interpreted the pooled window as an unpooled one and attended to `block_pool_size`x too few tokens.

This was latent until #47071 scaled `sliding_window` down into pooled units (to stop over-reserving KV blocks): that scaling also shrank the kernel window `block_pool_size`x, truncating the encoder's effective context and changing Voxtral Realtime transcriptions (test_realtime_validation failure).

Fix by decoupling the two consumers: keep the pooled window (plus a one-block eviction margin) for the manager's retention/reservation, and pass the model's real unpooled window through to the block-pooling builder so the kernel attends over the correct range.

Fixes the CI failure on main: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/75877#019f2067-ce90-4ce8-ba8c-e54c54dae0c4

cc @andylolu2

title: [BugFix] Fix ModelOpt quantization inference for fused siblings
author: jasonlizhengjian
body:
## Summary

Fix ModelOpt mixed-precision dispatch so unlisted fused projections remain unquantized.

This removes the generic parent-sibling fallback from `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig._resolve_quant_algo` and adds explicit `packed_modules_mapping` declarations to the NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 causal and conditional model classes. Explicit packed mappings preserve MiniMax `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj` dispatch without inferring quantization for unrelated or intentionally unquantized siblings.

Fixes #47241.
Follow-up to #46756.

## Root cause

Qwen3.6 stores GDN `in_proj_a` and `in_proj_b` as BF16 tensors without quantization scales, while vLLM fuses them into `in_proj_ba`.

The parent-prefix fallback added by #46756 observed that the other direct `linear_attn` children were FP8 and incorrectly classified the unlisted `in_proj_ba` as FP8. The loader then copied BF16 checkpoint tensors into FP8 parameters while the expected scale placeholders had no checkpoint values. Shapes still matched, so loading completed, but recurrent attention state and logits were corrupted.

## Why this is not duplicate work

#47354 guards the fallback with `packed_modules_mapping`. That fixes unregistered siblings such as Nemotron Mamba `conv1d` and `norm`, but Qwen's unquantized `in_proj_ba` is itself a registered packed module, so the guarded fallback still classifies it as FP8.

This PR removes the unsafe inference entirely and makes the original MiniMax requirement explicit in the NVIDIA model classes. Resolution therefore succeeds only when declared packed shards are present and agree on their quantization algorithm.

## Validation

- B300 SXM6 AC, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, deterministic prompts with `temperature=0` and `enable_thinking=false`:
  - Before: both prompts emitted token `248050` (`<|box_end|>`) repeatedly.
  - After: France prompt returned `Paris`; `2+2` returned `4`.
- B300 focused ModelOpt mixed-precision tests: `6 passed`.
- After rebasing onto current `main`, CPU-safe resolver regression tests: `4 passed`.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py`: all applicable hooks passed.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with root-cause analysis, implementation, and test execution. The human submitter reviewed the complete diff and validation results.

title: [Bugfix] Recycle post-final-norm hidden in GLM MTP (single norm)
author: zhou9402
body:
The compile-free DeepseekV32 MTP draft layer returned the pre-final-norm hidden as both the draft-logits hidden and the recycled previous_hidden_states. Recycling the pre-final-norm hidden mismatches the draft model's hnorm and drops MTP acceptance; the reference deepseek_mtp.py (PR #45895) recycles the post-final-norm hidden.

Fix by computing the post-final-norm hidden once -- fusing the residual-add into the final RMSNorm (fused_add_rms_norm) -- and returning it for both tuple positions. compute_logits then applies the LM head only (no second RMSNorm), so the norm count is unchanged (one per draft step per layer) while the recycled hidden is now correctly post-norm.

The tuple return is understood by both the V2 speculator (isinstance-tuple check in autoregressive/speculator.py) and the legacy proposer (model_returns_tuple() is True for the DeepSeekMTPModel architecture used by GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2). SharedHead and the proposer contracts are unchanged.

title: [1/N][Feat][Perf] Add new warmup infrastructure for JITs
author: LopezCastroRoberto
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a shared warmup infrastructure for JIT kernels in vLLM.

The goal is to provide a standard, extensible way for kernels from different JIT backends, including Triton, CuTeDSL, TileLang, and potential future DSLs, to expose the set of specializations that should be compiled during engine startup.

This is not intended to be a one-off warmup path for a specific kernel. Instead, it defines a kernel-owned contract where each warmable kernel describes its own compile keys, dispatch logic, warmup search space, and compile-only entry point.

## Motivation

vLLM increasingly relies on JIT-generated kernels from multiple DSLs. Today, warming these kernels is difficult to standardize because each backend exposes different runtime and compilation APIs. This PR starts building a common infrastructure with several goals:

- Create shared JIT warmup infrastructure for all JIT backends in vLLM.
- Keep warmup definitions close to the kernels that own the specialization logic, making the system easier to review and maintain.
- Warm up actual compile keys instead of running representative non-key inputs, such as token sizes, and hoping they map to all required specializations. That mapping is not always obvious or guaranteed, so warmup should target the compile-key space directly.
- Use Python AST dispatch tracing to derive compile-key search spaces from normal Python `dispatch(...)` methods, avoiding duplicated hand-written warmup logic.
- Support compile-only warmup APIs, avoiding dummy runtime launches and dummy tensor allocation. Dummy runs can be expensive and may have side effects; each DSL should expose fake tensor/spec descriptors suitable for compilation only.
- Define a standard interface for new contributors (and potentially third-party libraries) to expose warmup metadata: compile keys, representative warmup keys, and a compile-only API.

## Warmup Contract

Each warmable kernel should expose a small wrapper object near the kernel's normal runtime entry point.

The wrapper owns:

- A frozen `CompileKey` dataclass with the fields that identify one compiled specialization.
- A `dispatch(...)` method that maps normal dispatch arguments to `CompileKey`.
- A `get_warmup_keys(...)` method that returns representative keys to compile.
- A `compile(compile_key)` method that compiles one key.

Proposed shape:

```python
class MyKernel(VllmJitKernel["MyKernel.CompileKey"]):

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class CompileKey:
        BLOCK_SIZE: int

    @staticmethod
    def kernel(...):
        ...

    def dispatch(self, *, num_tokens: int) -> CompileKey:
        return self.CompileKey(BLOCK_SIZE= ...)

    def get_warmup_keys(self, vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> list[CompileKey]:
        ...

    def compile(self, compile_key: CompileKey) -> None:
        ...

    def __call__(self, ...):
        compile_key = self.dispatch(...)
        ...

MY_KERNEL = MyKernel()
```

CompileKey must be hashable. `get_warmup_keys(...)` should deduplicate keys before returning them if multiple representative inputs map to the same compiled specialization.

## Initial Coverage

This PR adds initial coverage examples for both Triton and CuTeDSL kernels.

These examples are meant to validate the proposed infrastructure across different JIT backends and show how new kernels can adopt the same contract while still using backend-specific compile-only APIs.

Initial examples include:

- Sparse MLA Triton warmup paths.
- FA4 MLA CuTeDSL warmup path.

The intention is not to migrate every existing warmup in this PR, but to establish a shared infrastructure after review.

## TODO
- [ ] Add/expand contributor documentation.
- [ ] Longer-term: migrate all existing warmups in vLLM into this shared system.

title: [Bugfix] Initialize draft CUDA-graph keys for the native draft_model proposer
author: avalliappan-nvidia
body:
### Problem
When speculative decoding uses the native **`draft_model`** method (`method="draft_model"`), the draft
model runs **eager** every step — no CUDA-graph replay — even though its PIECEWISE graphs are captured
during `dummy_run`. The engine captures the draft graph but never dispatches to it, so each draft forward
is launch-bound (hundreds of thousands of `cudaLaunchKernel` calls) and can cost **more than a full dense
verify**, making `draft_model` self-speculative decoding net-negative.

### Root cause
`GPUModelRunner._check_and_update_cudagraph_mode()` initializes the **drafter's** cudagraph-dispatcher
keys only for the EAGLE / extract-hidden-states paths:

```python
# Initialize drafter's cudagraph dispatcher if using spec decode.
if self.speculative_config and (
    self.speculative_config.use_eagle()
    or self.speculative_config.uses_extract_hidden_states()
):
    assert isinstance(self.drafter, EagleProposer | DFlashProposer
                      | ExtractHiddenStatesProposer | Gemma4Proposer)
    self.drafter.initialize_cudagraph_keys(cudagraph_mode)
```

`uses_draft_model()` is excluded, so for `method="draft_model"` the drafter's `keys_initialized` stays
`False`, and `CUDAGraphDispatcher.dispatch()` returns `CUDAGraphMode.NONE` (eager) for every draft step.
This is inconsistent with every sibling gate in the same file, which already include `uses_draft_model()`
(drafter construction, attention-backend init, padded-drafter-batch, post-forward hidden-states gate).

### Fix
Add `uses_draft_model()` to the drafter keys-init gate and `DraftModelProposer` to the assert:

```python
if self.speculative_config and (
    self.speculative_config.use_eagle()
    or self.speculative_config.uses_draft_model()          # <-- ADD
    or self.speculative_config.uses_extract_hidden_states()
):
    assert isinstance(self.drafter, EagleProposer | DFlashProposer | DraftModelProposer
                      | ExtractHiddenStatesProposer | Gemma4Proposer)   # <-- add DraftModelProposer
    self.drafter.initialize_cudagraph_keys(cudagraph_mode)
```

The draft's PIECEWISE graphs are already captured (the capture block already includes
`uses_draft_model()`); this only enables dispatch to them. No new capture, no accuracy change.

### Impact
Because the drafter's cudagraph keys are never initialized, the draft model runs **eager** every step, so
each draft forward is launch-bound (an nsys trace of the pre-fix path shows a per-step `cudaLaunchKernel`
storm). After the fix, the draft forward is dispatched to its already-captured PIECEWISE graph, removing
that per-step launch overhead. Acceptance length is unchanged (identical tokens), so the entire effect is
per-draft-step latency: without graph replay the draft step can cost more than the target verify, which
makes `draft_model` self-speculation net-negative; with replay it becomes a net speedup.

### Test plan
- [x] Fix ported function-level off current `main`.
- [x] `pre-commit` (ruff / ruff-format / mypy / typos / SPDX) clean on the changed files.
- [ ] Sanity e2e (reviewer/CI): `draft_model` spec decode produces identical tokens vs eager-draft
      (accuracy unchanged) and the draft step is graph-replayed (no per-step launch storm).

### AI assistance disclosure
This change was drafted with AI assistance (Cursor / Claude), per the contributing guide's "AI Assisted
Contributions" policy. All changed lines were reviewed and validated end-to-end by the author. Attribution
is included via a `Co-authored-by: Claude` commit trailer.

title: [Perf] Optimize `fused_topk_bias` for DSv4, 1.5~2x kernel performance improvement
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

Part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45861

~Originally when `hash_indices_table` is None we will do a redundant `input_tokens.to(dtype=indices_type)` which can be removed.~

We make the conversion inside the kernel to improve performance

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Performance using this AI generated script:

<details>

```py

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.fused_topk_bias_router import (
    fused_topk_bias,
)


def time_cuda(fn, warmup=20, iters=100):
    for _ in range(warmup):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(iters):
        fn()
    end.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) / iters


def main():
    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA is required"
    torch.manual_seed(0)

    vocab_size = 163840
    num_experts = 512
    topk = 8
    hidden_size = 1
    dtype = torch.bfloat16
    indices_type = torch.int32
    device = "cuda"

    hash_table_long = torch.randint(
        0, num_experts, (vocab_size, topk), dtype=torch.long, device=device
    )
    hash_table_int = hash_table_long.to(torch.int32)

    def route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids, table):
        return fused_topk_bias(
            hidden_states=hidden_states,
            gating_output=gating_output,
            scoring_func="sqrtsoftplus",
            e_score_correction_bias=None,
            topk=topk,
            renormalize=True,
            indices_type=indices_type,
            input_tokens=input_ids,
            hash_indices_table=table,
        )

    def old_python_cast(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids):
        input_ids = input_ids.to(indices_type)
        table = hash_table_long.to(indices_type)
        return route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids, table)

    print("device:", torch.cuda.get_device_name())
    print(
        f"vocab={vocab_size} experts={num_experts} topk={topk} "
        f"table_int64={hash_table_long.numel() * hash_table_long.element_size() / 1e6:.2f}MB"
    )
    print("times are ms/forward")

    for num_tokens in (128, 512, 2048, 8192):
        hidden_states = torch.empty(
            (num_tokens, hidden_size), dtype=dtype, device=device
        )
        gating_output = torch.randn(
            (num_tokens, num_experts), dtype=dtype, device=device
        )
        input_ids_long = torch.randint(
            0, vocab_size, (num_tokens,), dtype=torch.long, device=device
        )
        input_ids_int = input_ids_long.to(torch.int32)

        new_w, new_ids = route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_long,
                               hash_table_long)
        ref_w, ref_ids = route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_int,
                               hash_table_int)
        torch.testing.assert_close(new_ids, ref_ids, atol=0, rtol=0)
        torch.testing.assert_close(new_w, ref_w, atol=2e-2, rtol=1e-2)

        current = time_cuda(
            lambda: route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_long,
                          hash_table_long)
        )
        old = time_cuda(
            lambda: old_python_cast(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_long)
        )
        precast = time_cuda(
            lambda: route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_int,
                          hash_table_int)
        )
        print(
            f"M={num_tokens:5d}: current_mixed={current:.4f}  "
            f"old_python_cast={old:.4f}  precast_int32={precast:.4f}  "
            f"speedup={old / current:.2f}x"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

</details>


And we get

```bash
M=  128: current_mixed=0.0163  old_python_cast=0.0311  precast_int32=0.0157  speedup=1.91x
M=  512: current_mixed=0.0158  old_python_cast=0.0316  precast_int32=0.0159  speedup=2.01x
M= 2048: current_mixed=0.0162  old_python_cast=0.0308  precast_int32=0.0156  speedup=1.91x
M= 8192: current_mixed=0.0195  old_python_cast=0.0313  precast_int32=0.0194  speedup=1.61x
```

title: [Bugfix] Fix PD disagg + MTP correctness for Qwen3.5(GDN)
author: andakai
body:
## Problem

`Qwen3.5-0.8B` with `MTP=1` can lose GSM8K accuracy under PD disaggregation when concurrency is greater than 1 and default cudagraph is enabled. The issue was reproduced with both Mooncake and NIXL.

Trigger pattern:

- model: `Qwen3.5-0.8B`
- hybrid/GDN state model
- PD disaggregation
- MTP/spec decode enabled, `num_speculative_tokens=1`
- TP=1
- concurrent requests, so decode can batch normal running requests with a newly handed-off request
- default cudagraph enabled

| Connector | Config | Accuracy |
|---|---|---:|
| Mooncake | before fix, 4P4D | `0.153904` |
| NIXL | before fix, 4P4D | `0.185747` |

## Root Cause

**On the decode worker, a newly handed-off GDN request will not have completed the last prompt token**, because the decode worker still needs to forward the prompt tail token `x_N` to advance GDN state to `h(N)`.

So in D instance:
```text
num_computed_tokens = num_prompt_tokens - 1
state = h(N-1)
```

In the previous version, D instance will go into this branch, because its `num_new_tokens=1`. **However, this is actually the prompt tail token, so this prefill token will go into the decode.**
```
if (
    (self.num_spec_tokens > 0 and self.dynamic_sd_lookup is None)
    and num_new_tokens == 1
    and num_computed_tokens >= request.num_prompt_tokens
    and (scheduled_running_reqs and not prefill_scheduled)
):
    num_new_tokens = 1 + self.num_spec_tokens
```

Old scheduler logic could still pad this boundary step as MTP decode:

```text
input = [xN, -1]
query_len = 1 + mtp_tokens
```

The input assembly kernel will execute the decode rewrite in `_combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens_kernel`

```python
if NUM_NEW_SAMPLED_TOKENS > 0:
  # Write the last sampled token ID to input_ids.
  last_token_id = tl.load(last_sampled_tokens_ptr + req_state_idx)
  tl.store(input_ids_ptr + query_end - num_logits, last_token_id)
```

For normal decode this is correct,  this is used to write the previously sampled/accepted token into the decode input slot for the next forward pass, **and the model should consume the last generated token, not another prompt token**. In this PD+GDN situation, it is the previous computed token, `x(N-1)`. So the prompt tail `xN` is overwritten before GDN forward, and the recurrent state advances from the wrong token.

This explains the accuracy collapse: once GDN state is corrupted at the PD handoff boundary, later generation follows the wrong state trajectory.

## Fix

Only schedule MTP padding for a request after its prompt has completed locally. In this way, the last token in D instance will be treated as a prefill token and does not overwrite `xN`.

```diff
 if (
     (self.num_spec_tokens > 0 and self.dynamic_sd_lookup is None)
     and num_new_tokens == 1
+    and num_computed_tokens >= request.num_prompt_tokens
     and (scheduled_running_reqs and not prefill_scheduled)
 ):
     num_new_tokens = 1 + self.num_spec_tokens
```



## Validation

All accuracy numbers below use `Qwen3.5-0.8B`, GSM8K full set, 5-shot, `max_tokens=256`, `MTP=1`, `TP=1`. Use default config.

| Connector | Config | Accuracy |
|---|---|---:|
| Mooncake | before fix, 4P4D | `0.153904` |
| Mooncake | after fix, 4P4D | `0.321456` |
| NIXL | before fix, 4P4D | `0.185747` |
| NIXL | after fix, 4P4D | `0.323730` |

This is close to the standalone accuracy.

author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

So we save two additional copy from CPU to GPU

## Test

### Acc

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash   --trust-remote-code   --kv-cache-dtype fp8   --block-size 256   --enable-expert-parallel   --tensor-parallel-size 4   --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True   --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe   --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4   --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4   --enable-auto-tool-choice   --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --port9256
```

```bash
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9522|±  |0.0059|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9530|±  |0.0058|
```

### Perf

Running this AI-generated microbenchmark Script

<details>

```py
import gc
import statistics
import time

import numpy as np
import torch

from vllm.utils.torch_utils import np_to_pinned_tensor

WARMUP_ITERS = 100
CASES = [
    ("decode bs32", 32, 1, 0, 5000),
    ("decode bs256", 256, 1, 0, 3000),
    ("decode bs512", 512, 1, 0, 2000),
    ("mixed/short prefill 512 tok", 32, 16, 0, 2000),
    ("prefill 4096 tok", 64, 64, 0, 1000),
    ("prefill 8192 tok + cg pad", 128, 64, 128, 800),
]


def make_query_start_loc(num_reqs: int, query_len: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    query_lens = torch.full((num_reqs,), query_len, dtype=torch.int32)
    query_start_loc = torch.empty(num_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
    query_start_loc[0] = 0
    torch.cumsum(query_lens, dim=0, out=query_start_loc[1:])
    return query_start_loc


def old_three_builds(
    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    num_reqs: int,
    num_actual_tokens: int,
    buffers: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Old path: Sparse MLA, SWA, and Compressor each build the mapping."""
    buf_mla, buf_swa, buf_compressor = buffers

    starts = np.asarray(query_start_loc, dtype=np.int32)
    lens_np = np.diff(starts)
    req_id_per_token = np.repeat(np.arange(lens_np.shape[0], dtype=np.int32), lens_np)
    mapped_tokens = req_id_per_token.shape[0]
    buf_mla[:mapped_tokens].copy_(
        np_to_pinned_tensor(req_id_per_token), non_blocking=True
    )
    if mapped_tokens < num_actual_tokens:
        buf_mla[mapped_tokens:num_actual_tokens].zero_()

    query_lens = query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]
    req_ids = torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(num_reqs), query_lens).pin_memory()
    buf_swa[: req_ids.shape[0]].copy_(req_ids, non_blocking=True)

    query_lens = query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]
    req_ids = torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(num_reqs), query_lens).pin_memory()
    buf_compressor[: req_ids.shape[0]].copy_(req_ids, non_blocking=True)

    return (
        buf_mla[:num_actual_tokens],
        buf_swa[: req_ids.shape[0]],
        buf_compressor[: req_ids.shape[0]],
    )


def cached_three_builds(
    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    num_reqs: int,
    num_actual_tokens: int,
    buffers: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """New path: build once, then reuse cached tensor views."""
    del num_reqs
    buf = buffers[0]

    starts = np.asarray(query_start_loc, dtype=np.int32)
    lens_np = np.diff(starts)
    token_to_req = np.repeat(np.arange(lens_np.shape[0], dtype=np.int32), lens_np)
    mapped_tokens = token_to_req.shape[0]
    buf[:mapped_tokens].copy_(np_to_pinned_tensor(token_to_req), non_blocking=True)
    if mapped_tokens < num_actual_tokens:
        buf[mapped_tokens:num_actual_tokens].zero_()

    cached = buf[: max(mapped_tokens, num_actual_tokens)]
    out = cached[:num_actual_tokens]
    return out, out, out


def bench(
    fn,
    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    num_reqs: int,
    num_actual_tokens: int,
    buffers: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
    iters: int,
) -> float:
    gc.disable()
    for _ in range(WARMUP_ITERS):
        fn(query_start_loc, num_reqs, num_actual_tokens, buffers)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    samples_ns = []
    for _ in range(iters):
        start_ns = time.perf_counter_ns()
        fn(query_start_loc, num_reqs, num_actual_tokens, buffers)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        samples_ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - start_ns)
    gc.enable()
    return statistics.median(samples_ns) / 1e3


def main() -> None:
    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "This benchmark requires CUDA."
    device = torch.device("cuda")
    print(f"device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(device)}")
    print(
        f"{'case':<28} {'old_med_us':>11} {'new_med_us':>11} "
        f"{'speedup':>8} {'saved_us':>10}"
    )

    for name, num_reqs, query_len, pad_tokens, iters in CASES:
        query_start_loc = make_query_start_loc(num_reqs, query_len)
        num_actual_tokens = int(query_start_loc[-1].item()) + pad_tokens
        capacity = num_actual_tokens + 16
        buffers = tuple(
            torch.empty(capacity, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) for _ in range(3)
        )

        old_us = bench(
            old_three_builds,
            query_start_loc,
            num_reqs,
            num_actual_tokens,
            buffers,
            iters,
        )
        new_us = bench(
            cached_three_builds,
            query_start_loc,
            num_reqs,
            num_actual_tokens,
            buffers,
            iters,
        )
        print(
            f"{name:<28} {old_us:11.2f} {new_us:11.2f} "
            f"{old_us / new_us:8.2f} {old_us - new_us:10.2f}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

title: [Bugfix][KV-transfer] MoRIIO: retry RDMA send-queue-full backpressure instead of failing the read
author: edwinlim0919
body:
## Purpose

At high concurrency the per-QP RDMA send queue fills up. `read_remote_data` posts the READ **synchronously**, but the mori executor joins its worker before returning and marks the status on the calling thread, so a send-queue-full rejection comes back as a `Failed()` status immediately.

That `Failed()` status was then treated as a failed transfer. `get_finished` notifies the prefill to release its blocks and drops the request, which stalls and is aborted by timeout. Under sustained multi-decode / MTP RDMA load this kills requests that would have succeeded **milliseconds later**, once the separate CQ-poll thread drains completions and frees SQ depth.

## Fix

Detect the transient SQ-full status (`_is_sq_full_status`: `Failed()` and `"SQ full"` in the message) and **back off + re-post** the READ, bounded by `transfer_timeout`, instead of letting the transient rejection abort the request.

- No self-deadlock: the SQ drain runs off-thread.
- The reserve is all-or-nothing, so nothing is posted on a rejected attempt.
- On a genuinely sustained overload past the deadline, the failed status is stored and `get_finished` handles it non-fatally as before (notify prefill + drop). Behaviour for non-SQ-full statuses is unchanged.

+48 / −3, one file (`moriio_connector.py`).

## Validation

Validated on 2-node MI300X (gfx942): before this change, high-concurrency disaggregated P/D runs stalled/hung on SQ-full backpressure; after, they run clean at the concurrency levels used for our InferenceX submission.

## AI assistance

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and is responsible for the change end-to-end.

title: [Minimax-M3] Using tok_sparse_select from MSA instead of triton kernels
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

Replace the two per-path Triton top-k implementations in the MiniMax-M3 MSA (SM100/Blackwell) indexer with a **single MSA `sparse_topk_select`** over one unified score buffer shared by decode and prefill.

**Before**, the MSA indexer ran two independent top-k paths:
- **decode** → Triton fused `minimax_m3_index_decode` (block-score + split-K top-k) writing `topk_indices_buffer[:, :nd]`
- **prefill** → fmha_sm100 `OnlyScore` → Triton `minimax_m3_index_topk` writing `topk_indices_buffer[:, nd:]`

**After**, both sides only compute **block scores** into one token-major unified buffer `[total_q, H, max_k_tiles]`, then a single `fmha_sm100.sparse_topk_select` selects the top-k for the whole batch (decode `[:nd]` + prefill `[nd:]`) in one call:
- decode scores via the new score-only `minimax_m3_index_decode_score` (split-K, cudagraph-safe) into `unified[:nd]` (transposed strided view; the kernel writes by strides);
- prefill scores via fmha `OnlyScore`, writing `max_score` **straight into** `unified[nd:]` (stride-aware, no copy — the plan's `max_k_tiles` is forced to the buffer's tile dim so the shapes match exactly);
- one `sparse_topk_select` (THK layout, no transpose) writes the selected block ids into the shared `topk_indices_buffer`, bounding each row by its causal page count and force-including the init/local blocks.

### Supporting changes
- **Split `minimax_m3_index_decode`** into `minimax_m3_index_decode_score` (score-only; new `score_out` writes into a shared buffer) plus the existing fused wrapper (now calls the score fn then the top-k, and gains an optional `score_out`).
- **Drop the `-1` sentinel from the sparse-attention kernels.** `sparse_topk_select` does not pad selections with `-1`, so `_gqa_sparse_fwd_kernel` / `_gqa_sparse_decode_kernel` now derive the valid block count directly from the causal sequence position (`min(max_topk, cdiv(kv_len, block))`) instead of counting `topk_idx >= 0`. The `BLOCK_SIZE_T` constexpr and the sentinel load are removed.
- **Token-major `topk_indices_buffer`** `[total_q, num_index_heads, topk]` (was head-major `[H, total_q, topk]`) to match `sparse_topk_select`'s native `[token, head, topk]` output; the attend slices tokens on dim 0 then transposes to `[H, tokens, topk]` (`sparse_attention_msa.py`).
- **`num_valid_pages_buffer`** — a stable per-token causal page-count buffer (`cdiv(pos+1, 128)`) in the indexer metadata, feeding `sparse_topk_select`'s `force_end_blocks` + out-of-range clamp; kept at a stable address for cudagraph replay.
- **Bump the MSA (`fmha_sm100`) pin** to `0a2e5cc` for the `sparse_topk_select` entry point.

Net effect: one top-k kernel instead of two, less shared-buffer plumbing, and a single MSA select path for both prefill and decode.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py -v
```
Run on SM100 / Blackwell. `test_msa_indexer_impl_matches_triton` is the key correctness gate — it runs the refactored MSA unified-score + `sparse_topk_select` path and the Triton indexer on the same mixed decode+prefill batch and asserts identical top-k selections.

`test_decode_index_topk_fp8` was updated for the refactored `minimax_m3_index_decode` signature: fp8 QK is computed unscaled, so the reference matmul drops `sm_scale`, and `max_decode_query_len` is passed through.

Plus e2e GPQA eval against a MiniMax-M3 server on the MSA indexer backend.

## Test Result

Local run on Blackwell: **51 passed**, including the modified `test_decode_index_topk_fp8[*]`. The 2 `test_msa_indexer_impl_matches_triton[*]` cases error in this environment inside `create_vllm_config` on a gated-repo HF download (`meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B`, 401) — before any indexer code runs — so they need an HF-authenticated host to execute; not a code failure.

End to end GSM8K score passed 

<!-- Submitter to paste the full pytest output (incl. parity test on an HF-authed host) and GPQA before/after numbers. -->

title: [KVConnector] Guard lmcache_mp_connector state transition with num_external_tokens
author: Alex-ai-future
body:
## Purpose

When `lmcache_mp_connector` is used as a non-chosen sub-connector in
MultiConnector, it receives `update_state_after_alloc` with
`num_external_tokens=0`.

The connector's state machine uses `needs_retrieve()` (which checks
`num_lmcache_hit_blocks > num_vllm_hit_blocks`) to decide whether to
load, but this does not account for being non-chosen. When LMCache has
cached data but another connector was chosen, the state machine
incorrectly transitions to `WAITING_FOR_LOAD` and creates retrieve tasks.
Additionally, lookup locks are not released (lock leak until TTL expiry).

**Fix:** Add `and num_external_tokens > 0` to the `condition` variable.
This forces `condition=False` for non-chosen connectors, so the existing
`if not condition:` branch correctly transitions to READY and releases
all lookup locks.

Ref: #46865 (MultiConnector real blocks), #47294 (wrong fix direction)

## Changes

**`lmcache_mp_connector.py`**: 
```python
# Before
condition = tracker.needs_retrieve()

# After
condition = tracker.needs_retrieve() and num_external_tokens > 0
```

## Logical Correctness

The fix ensures correct behavior across all scenarios:

### Scenario 1: Non-chosen connector (the bug being fixed)
- **Input**: `num_external_tokens = 0`, `num_lmcache_hit_blocks > 0`
- **Before fix**: `condition = True` → incorrectly enters `WAITING_FOR_LOAD`, partial lock release
- **After fix**: `condition = False` → correctly enters `READY`, all locks released ✅

### Scenario 2: Chosen connector (unchanged)
- **Input**: `num_external_tokens > 0`, `num_lmcache_hit_blocks > 0`
- **Before fix**: `condition = True` → enters `WAITING_FOR_LOAD`
- **After fix**: `condition = True` → enters `WAITING_FOR_LOAD` (unchanged) ✅

### Scenario 3: Cold request (unchanged)
- **Input**: `num_external_tokens = 0`, `num_lmcache_hit_blocks = 0`
- **Before fix**: `condition = False` → enters `READY`
- **After fix**: `condition = False` → enters `READY` (unchanged) ✅

## Why This Fix is Correct

**Key insight**: `num_external_tokens` semantically means "how many tokens 
this connector needs to load". When `num_external_tokens == 0`, it means 
"this connector doesn't need to load anything", so:

1. **Block tracking (store path) remains unaffected** — executes unconditionally
2. **State transition** — goes directly to `READY` (no need to wait for load)
3. **Lock release** — all lookup locks are freed (since none will be used)

The fix is minimal (one line), surgical, and preserves all existing behavior
for chosen connectors and cold requests.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Verify the fix doesn't break existing functionality
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/ -v
```

## Test Result

Manual verification confirms the logical correctness across all three scenarios
described above.

title: [CI] Bump `huggingface-hub` from `v1.10.2` to `v1.22.0`
author: hmellor
body:
This release includes https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/pull/4394: 

> `snapshot_download` now caches a repository's file listing on disk under a new `trees/` folder, so re-downloading a commit that's already cached costs a single network call — resolving the branch or tag to a commit hash — instead of one metadata request per file. The listing is immutable per commit and shared by both `snapshot_download` and `hf_hub_download`; for Xet-enabled files it also skips the per-file HEAD `/resolve` request entirely, rebuilding the metadata from the cached listing. As a deliberate side effect of the completeness check, when the Hub can't be reached and the local snapshot is missing requested files, `snapshot_download` now raises `IncompleteSnapshotError` instead of silently returning a partial folder.

title: [ROCm] Disable persistent sparse-MLA kernel for chunked-prefill continuations
author: Rohan138
body:
# [ROCm] Disable persistent sparse-MLA kernel for chunked-prefill continuations

## Summary
Fixes #47042. GLM-4.6/4.5 / DeepSeek-V3.2-style sparse-MLA (DSA) models on ROCm
produce correct output up to ~20K tokens and then collapse into repetition /
garbage at longer contexts.

Root cause: the AITER **persistent MLA work-stealing kernel**
(`get_mla_metadata_v1` + the `work_meta_data` persistent path in
`aiter.mla.mla_decode_fwd`, enabled unconditionally for the sparse-MLA backend
in #41990) is **numerically wrong for multi-token (prefill) batches**. The
per-token error is small in isolation, but chunked prefill runs a request
through several forward passes and the error **compounds** through the KV cache
across passes/layers until long-context decode collapses.

This is why the failure is gated on **chunk count**, not context length:

| max-num-batched-tokens | 20K prompt | chunks | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8192 | 22K tok | 3 | garbage (0/10 needles) |
| 12288 | 22K tok | 2 | correct |
| 21504 | 22K tok | 2 | correct |
| 12288 | 33K tok | 3 | garbage |

The persistent kernel is correct for **pure decode** (`qseqlen==1`) and for
**fresh single-chunk prefills**. This patch gates it on batch shape: it falls
back to the (correct) non-persistent split-KV path whenever any request in the
batch is a chunked-prefill *continuation* — i.e. it has more than one query
token this step *and* part of its context was already computed in an earlier
chunk (`seq_len > query_len`). Decode and single-chunk prefills keep the
persistent performance path, so there is no decode throughput regression.

## Why this is not a duplicate
- #47404 ("Synchronize sparse MLA metadata before graph replay") touches the
  same file but fixes a *different* bug: a stale-metadata race during CUDA-graph
  replay. The bug here is a **numerical correctness** bug in the kernel itself —
  it reproduces with `--enforce-eager` / `-cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE` (no graph
  replay), so metadata-ordering is not involved.
- #41973 / #41990 is the feature that *enabled* the persistent path (the source
  of this regression), not a fix.
- No open PR references #47042.

## Isolated (kernel-only) reproduction
A standalone script (no vLLM/model) builds a sparse-MLA batch, regenerates the
persistent metadata via `get_mla_metadata_v1`, and compares the persistent
kernel and the non-persistent kernel against a torch fp32 reference:

```
N=  1 (decode):        persistent max_relerr=0.000   non-persistent=0.000  -> OK
N=512 (prefill batch): persistent max_relerr=7.15    non-persistent=0.108  -> PERSISTENT WRONG
```

The non-persistent kernel matches the fp32 reference tightly everywhere; the
persistent kernel is correct for decode-shaped batches but produces large
errors for prefill-shaped batches. (The underlying kernel bug is also worth an
AITER-side fix; this PR is the vLLM-side mitigation.)

## Testing (MI355X / gfx950, TP8, GLM-FP8, vLLM nightly + aiter 0.1.16.post2)
Needle-in-a-haystack via raw `/v1/completions`, greedy, `max-num-batched-tokens
8192` (default small chunk), cudagraph/torch.compile **enabled**:

| context | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2K  | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| 20K | **0/10 (garbage)** | 10/10 |
| 40K | garbage | 10/10 |

No accuracy regression on short context:
`lm_eval gsm8k --num_fewshot 20` (concurrency 256): **0.944 flexible / 0.945
strict** exact_match, unchanged vs baseline (decode path is untouched).

## Notes
- Python-only change; behavior differs only on ROCm sparse-MLA (`glm_moe_dsa` /
  DeepSeek-V3.2 indexer) backends.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and draft this change; a human
  author owns and has validated it.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`
  should be run before submission.

title: [Bugfix] Zero new KV blocks for quantized + sliding-window hybrid caches
author: EdalatiAli
body:
## Purpose

A hybrid KV cache that quantizes full-attention layers but keeps sliding-window layers in higher precision (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers sliding_window`) produces **NaN / all-zero output** once the input exceeds the sliding window. Uniform fp8 and bf16 are fine; only the hybrid combo fails (seen on Blackwell + FlashInfer).

## Root cause

Attention groups share one block pool. The sliding-window group frees blocks mid-request; those pages get reallocated to the fp8 group and read back including slots not written this step. As bf16 that leftover is harmless
garbage, but as **fp8 it decodes to NaN/Inf** and corrupts attention. The existing zeroing guard (`needs_kv_cache_zeroing`) was gated only on Mamba (#35219), so this config was left exposed.

## Fix

Extend `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` to also fire for block-dropping attention (sliding-window / chunked-local) + quantized (FP8/NVFP4) KV cache:

```python
needs_kv_cache_zeroing = has_mamba_layers or (has_block_dropping_layers and has_quantized_kv_cache)
```

Uniform / unquantized caches stay `False` → zero overhead.

## Test Plan
- Run RULER (`niah_single_1`) evals on `CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-w4a4` with various kv cache quantization options, before and after the fix.
- Here are the repro steps on B200, FlashInfer backend, `lm-eval-harness` 0.4.x.

Serve the hybrid config:

```bash
vllm serve CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-w4a4 \
  --tool-call-parser cohere_command4 --reasoning-parser cohere_command4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers sliding_window
```

2. Run the needle eval (repeat with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` alone, and with no
`--kv-cache-dtype` flag for the bf16 reference):

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,model=CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-w4a4,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False" \
  --tasks niah_single_1 \
  --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[4096,32768,131072],"tokenizer":"CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-w4a4"}' \
  --gen_kwargs "temperature=0.9,top_p=0.95,repetition_penalty=1.04" \
  --trust_remote_code
```

## Test Result

| KV cache config             | 4K    | 32K   | 132K   |
| --------------------------- | --------- | --------- | --------- |
| bf16 (reference)            | 0.994     | 0.388     | 0.556     |
| fp8 uniform                 | 0.994     | 0.376     | 0.462     |
| fp8 + skip-SWA **w/o fix**  | **0.002** | **0.000** | **0.002** |
| fp8 + skip-SWA **with fix** | **0.990** | **0.376** | **0.520** |

title: [Rust Frontend] [Perf] Avoid extra copies for multimodal tensors
author: reidliu41
body:
## Purpose
  Multimodal requests with inline tensor payloads can carry large byte buffers,
  such as image `pixel_values`. The Rust frontend previously copied those bytes
  in two avoidable places before sending the request to engine:

  1. `lower_text_request` cloned `request.mm_features` into `GenerateRequest`.
  2. `WireArrayData::RawView` cloned the raw tensor bytes while building an owned
     MessagePack ext value.

  The change removes both extra copies:

  - Move `mm_features` into `GenerateRequest` with `take()`. The retained
    response-side `TextRequest` no longer keeps `mm_features`, matching the
    current response decoding path.
  - Serialize `RawView` MessagePack ext values from borrowed bytes while keeping
    the exact existing wire format.

  For multimodal requests with large tensor payloads, this avoids repeated large
  buffer allocations and copies on the Rust frontend path, reducing per-request
  CPU work and transient memory pressure without changing engine behavior or the
  wire format.

## Test Plan

```

  cargo clippy -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-text --all-targets
```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Trim token_ids/logprobs left past a stop string under speculative decoding
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

With `ngram` speculative decoding, a single decode step can accept several tokens at once. When a stop string completes in the middle of that accepted batch, V1 truncates `output_text` to the stop boundary but leaves the tokens generated after the stop in `RequestOutput.outputs[0].token_ids`. When logprobs are requested, those past-stop token logprobs are returned as well.

The root cause is that incremental detokenization appends the whole accepted token batch before stop-string evaluation. The stop-string helper returns a character truncation point, so text gets trimmed but the token ids and per-step logprobs are not mapped back to the stop boundary.

This records the text start offset for each newly accepted token, drops tokens whose text starts after the matched stop string, and propagates the dropped-token count so the per-step `new_token_ids` and `new_logprobs` are trimmed consistently for streaming, non-streaming, and logprobs outputs. It only applies when EngineCore has not already ended the step on a stop token, preserving the existing stop-token termination behavior.

## Test Plan

I ran a real `LLM(...)` reproduction with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `ngram` speculative decoding, `temperature=0`, `stop=[" ha ha ha"]`, and `logprobs=2`. The upstream main check reproduces the leak because the speculative path returns six generated token ids and six logprobs while the non-spec baseline returns three; this branch passes with both paths returning three.

I also ran the focused detokenizer regression file, the existing min-tokens detokenizer file, and scoped pre-commit hooks for the three changed Python files.

## Test Result

The real-engine reproduction shows the baseline/spec mismatch on main and `PASS fixed behavior` on this branch. In the failing main run, both `include_stop_str_in_output` modes return correct text and `finish_reason="stop"`, but the speculative output leaks `[6386, 6386, 6386]` past the stop boundary.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end reproduction</summary>

Hardware: one NVIDIA RTX 4090. Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` cached locally at `/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-0.6B`. Settings: `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, `enforce_eager=True`, `temperature=0`, `stop=[" ha ha ha"]`, `include_stop_str_in_output` tested both ways, `logprobs=2`, `ngram` speculative config `{"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 6, "prompt_lookup_min": 1, "prompt_lookup_max": 4}`.

`sd_stop_boundary_probe.py`:

```python
import argparse
import gc
import json
import os

import torch

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL", "ERROR")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS", "1")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


PROMPT = "ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha"
STOP = " ha ha ha"


def build_llm(model: str, speculative: bool) -> LLM:
    spec = None
    if speculative:
        spec = {
            "method": "ngram",
            "num_speculative_tokens": 6,
            "prompt_lookup_min": 1,
            "prompt_lookup_max": 4,
        }
    return LLM(
        model=model,
        max_model_len=2048,
        max_num_seqs=4,
        max_num_batched_tokens=256,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.25,
        enforce_eager=True,
        speculative_config=spec,
    )


def cleanup_llm(llm: LLM) -> None:
    del llm
    gc.collect()
    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()


def run_case(llm: LLM, include_stop: bool, logprobs: int | None) -> dict:
    params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=16,
        stop=[STOP],
        include_stop_str_in_output=include_stop,
        skip_special_tokens=False,
        logprobs=logprobs,
    )
    output = llm.generate([PROMPT], params, use_tqdm=False)[0].outputs[0]
    result = {
        "text": output.text,
        "token_ids": list(output.token_ids),
        "finish_reason": output.finish_reason,
        "stop_reason": output.stop_reason,
    }
    if logprobs is not None:
        result["logprobs_len"] = len(output.logprobs or [])
    return result


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--expect", choices=["match", "leak"], required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--logprobs", type=int, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    baseline = build_llm(args.model, speculative=False)
    baseline_rows = {
        mode: run_case(baseline, mode == "include", args.logprobs)
        for mode in ("exclude", "include")
    }
    cleanup_llm(baseline)

    speculative = build_llm(args.model, speculative=True)
    spec_rows = {
        mode: run_case(speculative, mode == "include", args.logprobs)
        for mode in ("exclude", "include")
    }
    cleanup_llm(speculative)

    payload = {"baseline": baseline_rows, "spec": spec_rows}
    print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))

    matches = all(
        spec_rows[mode]["token_ids"] == baseline_rows[mode]["token_ids"]
        for mode in ("exclude", "include")
    )
    logprobs_match = True
    if args.logprobs is not None:
        logprobs_match = all(
            spec_rows[mode]["logprobs_len"]
            == baseline_rows[mode]["logprobs_len"]
            == len(spec_rows[mode]["token_ids"])
            for mode in ("exclude", "include")
        )

    if args.expect == "match" and matches and logprobs_match:
        print("PASS fixed behavior")
        return 0
    if args.expect == "leak" and not matches:
        print("PASS leak reproduced")
        return 0

    print(
        "FAIL",
        json.dumps(
            {
                "expect": args.expect,
                "token_ids_match": matches,
                "logprobs_match": logprobs_match,
            },
            indent=2,
        ),
    )
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

title: [MM][CG] Support ViT full CUDA graph for Idefics3 and SmolVLM
author: CHIPMUNK-T0T
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds ViT encoder CUDA Graph support for Idefics3 / SmolVLM as part of #38175.

Idefics3 computes vision position IDs from the patch attention mask during the encoder forward pass. To make the encoder compatible with CUDA Graph capture, this PR precomputes the position IDs and passes them as fixed graph inputs.

Changes:
- Implement `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for `Idefics3ForConditionalGeneration`
- Add CUDA Graph capture/replay using `pixel_values`, `pixel_attention_mask`, and `position_ids`
- Expose position-ID computation from `Idefics2VisionEmbeddings`
- Add SmolVLM coverage to `test_vit_cudagraph.py`

I checked #38175 and open PRs and found no existing PR covering Idefics3 / SmolVLM encoder CUDA Graph support.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Test Plan

Targeted test:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_vit_cudagraph_image -q -k idefics3
```

Also ran:

* Ruff on the changed Python files
* Python syntax checks
* Diff whitespace check
* A small end-to-end latency benchmark with encoder CUDA Graph disabled/enabled

## Test Result

* Targeted CUDA Graph test: `1 passed, 13 deselected`
* Ruff: passed
* Python syntax checks: passed
* Diff whitespace check: passed

### Benchmark

Environment:

* GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 12GB
* Model: `HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct`
* Input: 1 generated 512×512 image + fixed prompt
* Batch size: 1
* `max_tokens=1`
* Warmup: 5 runs
* Measured: 30 runs

title: [Bugfix][OpenAI] Respect allowed_token_ids in beam search
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

OpenAI-compatible completion requests already accept `allowed_token_ids`, and the normal sampling path respects it. The beam-search path dropped that field while building `BeamSearchParams`, then ranked candidates from per-step logprobs that can include tokens outside the sampling mask, so a valid request could return HTTP 200 with forbidden `token_ids`.

This keeps `allowed_token_ids` on `BeamSearchParams`, forwards it from both completion and chat completion requests, and filters beam candidates before ranking. Small allowlists use `logprob_token_ids` so beam search can score the exact allowed set; the shared offline beam path also intersects request allowlists with structured-output grammar allowlists.

## Test Plan

I ran a real OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` reproduction on Qwen3-0.6B with `allowed_token_ids=[43096]`, where token 43096 decodes to `" banana"`. I ran the same server/client on current main, on this branch, and after reverting this branch diff, then ran ruff on the changed runtime files.

## Test Result

On main, the beam request returned forbidden token 12095 (`" Paris"`) while the normal sampling control returned allowed token 43096 (`" banana"`). On this branch, beam and sampling both returned token 43096; after reverting this branch diff, beam returned token 12095 again.

title: Bump flashinfer version to 0.6.14
author: AmeenP
body:
## Purpose

Pick up flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3615, which fixes the multi-CTA radix top-k sampler stream hang (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3610): the kernel's epilogue resets the software barrier's arrival counter with no sync against peer CTAs still polling it, so a peer can spin forever and permanently wedge the stream (GPU pinned at 100% util / low power, no Xid, engine frozen). 0.6.14 is the first release containing the fix; current pin (0.6.13) is affected.

Originally reported on SM120/SM121 (#43885, worked around by #44405), but it is not Blackwell-specific — we hit it in production on H100 serving Qwen models (top_k+top_p are Qwen's defaults, so every request launches this kernel) and can reproduce on Hopper: a `__nanosleep` widening the `wait_ge` poll gap wedges 0.6.11.post2/0.6.13-era kernels on the first launch, while a #3615 backport survives 50k launches under the same perturbation. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43885#issuecomment-4888293062.

With this in, the SM120/121 default-off from #44405 can be revisited.

## Test Plan

Version bump only (same file set as #46683). Wheels verified available: `flashinfer-python`/`flashinfer-cubin` 0.6.14 on PyPI, `flashinfer-jit-cache` 0.6.14+cu130 on https://flashinfer.ai/whl.

Fix validated at the kernel level on H100: stock kernel + widened barrier-poll window = deterministic wedge on first launch; 0.6.14's reset scheme under identical conditions = 50k launches clean with bit-identical top-k masks.

## Test Result

See above.

title: [KV Offload] Split tiering_lookup_delay into sync/async histograms
author: Srinivasoo7
body:
## Summary

Splits the planned `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_lookup_delay_seconds` metric into two histograms on `TieringOffloadingManager`:

- `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_lookup_sync_delay_seconds` : cost of a single secondary-tier lookup call.
- `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_lookup_async_delay_seconds` : total time a request's lookup stays deferred across a tier promotion, from the first RETRY until it resolves (or the request finishes without resolving).

This mirrors the sync/async split already used for the connector-level lookup delay metric (`_ConnectorMetricName.LOOKUP_SYNC_DELAY` / `LOOKUP_ASYNC_DELAY` in `scheduler.py`), applied at the `TieringOffloadingManager` level since `scheduler.py` is generic across any `OffloadingManager` and has no notion of tiers.


## Implementation

- `TieringOffloadingMetrics.LOOKUP_SYNC_DELAY` / `LOOKUP_ASYNC_DELAY`: new metric names in `tiering/base.py`.
- `TieringOffloadingSpec.build_metric_definitions`: registers both as histograms with bucket boundaries copied from the connector-level equivalents.
- `TieringOffloadingManager`:
  - `RequestState.secondary_lookup_start_time`: per-request deferred-lookup timer, `None` when no secondary lookup is pending.
  - `lookup()`: records sync delay on every call that reaches the secondary-tier loop; starts the async timer on the first RETRY for a request; flushes the async delay once resolved, either by a later lookup hitting the primary tier directly (the promotion completed) or by the secondary-tier loop reaching a definitive MISS.
  - `_maybe_finalize_request`: flushes any still-pending async delay if the request finishes before its deferred lookup ever resolves.
  - `get_stats()`: aggregates the buffered manager-level histogram observations into the returned stats alongside the per-tier stats.

# Related/References

Checked against the open PRs tracking RFC #44008 (Table 2): `#47413`, `#46019`, `#47235` : none of these touch `TieringOffloadingManager.lookup()` or its lookup-delay metric.


**Note:**

This branch is built on top of #45958 , which introduces the connector-level sync/async pattern this PR mirrors. Until
#45958 merges, the diff against `main` will include its changes too, the actual new content here is limited to the 4 files under
`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/` and the corresponding test file. 
Happy to rebase onto `main` once #45958 lands.

title: [Frontend] Overlap preprocessing and computation for pooling models offline inference
author: noooop
body:
## TL;DR - Use multithreading to accelerate preprocessing. You can specify the number of threads using renderer_num_workers. - Tiling to overlap preprocessing and computation for pooling models offline inference. - Sadly, because of the GIL, multithreading can only speed up the tokenizer and can hardly accelerate multimodal preprocessing at all. We are looking for ways to use multiprocessing to speed up multimodal preprocessing. ## How This Works: To implement `Overlap preprocessing and computation for pooling models offline inference`, we have redesigned the interface of `PoolingIOProcessor`. (We apologize for the breaking changes involved.) The new workflow proceeds as follows: 1. **Request generation** – `io_processor.get_request_factory_offline` splits an input batch into individual requests and returns a `request_factory` function. This function is a `RequestGenerator`, and each element it yields is suitable as input to the `render` method. 2. **Preprocessing** – `io_processor.render` consumes those generated elements and produces `PoolingEngineInput` objects, which are ready to be fed into the inference engine. 3. **Multithreaded acceleration** – We call `self._executor.map(io_processor.render, request_factory())` to parallelize the preprocessing step across multiple threads, significantly speeding it up. 4. **Overlapping with computation** – Inside `_run_tiling_engine`, we maintain at most `max_num_seqs * 2` requests in the core to keep it fully saturated. That is, we preprocess only a small portion of requests and then start the engine running, this allows us to overlap preprocessing with the computation, which is especially beneficial for offline inference of pooling models. ## Purpose Currently, offline inference for pooling models does not employ multithreaded preprocessing, and GPU work only begins after preprocessing has finished for all inputs—this is highly inefficient. Sadly, preprocessing time currently grows with input length, even though the data will be truncated to a small prompt size afterward. This results in a typical embedding working flow—such as preprocessing a wiki page containing hundreds of thousands of tokens and then truncating it to 512 tokens—taking an incredibly long time. We currently do not have a better truncation method that would make preprocessing take a reasonable amount of time—specifically, a method where the preprocessing time depends on the truncation length rather than the input length. However, we can speed things up as much as possible using multithreading, as well as tiling to overlap preprocessing and computation. ``` import time from vllm import LLM llm = LLM(model="BAAI/bge-m3", runner="pooling", max_num_seqs=8, renderer_num_workers=8) prompt = "hello " n_prompt = 100 for n in range(4, 18): n = 2 ** n prompts = [prompt * n] * n_prompt start = time.perf_counter() llm.embed(prompts, tokenization_kwargs={ "truncate_prompt_tokens": 512 }, use_tqdm=False) end = time.perf_counter() elapsed_time = end - start print(n, elapsed_time) ``` | prompt len | main | renderer_num_workers=1 | renderer_num_workers=2 | renderer_num_workers=4 | renderer_num_workers=8 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 16 | 0.054 | 0.050 | 0.051 | 0.051 | 0.051 | | 32 | 0.069 | 0.064 | 0.065 | 0.066 | 0.066 | | 64 | 0.103 | 0.095 | 0.094 | 0.092 | 0.095 | | 128 | 0.162 | 0.149 | 0.153 | 0.152 | 0.155 | | 256 | 0.282 | 0.253 | 0.250 | 0.250 | 0.249 | | 512 | 0.324 | 0.250 | 0.250 | 0.251 | 0.250 | | 1024 | 0.377 | 0.255 | 0.255 | 0.251 | 0.253 | | 2048 | 0.499 | 0.260 | 0.256 | 0.256 | 0.257 | | 4096 | 0.756 | 0.464 | 0.261 | 0.255 | 0.257 | | 8192 | 1.278 | 0.912 | 0.470 | 0.263 | 0.266 | | 16384 | 2.371 | 1.822 | 0.924 | 0.473 | 0.286 | | 32768 | 4.690 | 3.655 | 1.854 | 0.955 | 0.574 | | 65536 | 9.868 | 7.343 | 3.762 | 2.075 | 1.287 | | 131072 | 24.418 | 15.665 | 8.601 | 4.688 | 2.872 | 1. The total time scales down almost linearly with an increase in the number of renderer workers. 2. When preprocessing takes less time than computation (~0.250 here), the preprocessing overhead can be almost entirely overlapped. Fixes #45733 #41390 This idea originated from #28458 Address https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41678#issuecomment-4787577629 ## Test Plan keep ci green ## Test Result ---

title: [MRV2][Performance] Skip no-op FP32 logits materialization
author: jesse996
body:
## Purpose

MRV2 currently materializes the logits tensor as FP32 before applying sampling parameters, even when every active request is a no-op: temperature is 0 or 1, top-k equals the vocabulary size, top-p is 1, min-p is 0, and there are no penalties, logit biases, or bad words.

The Gumbel sampling kernel already converts loaded logits to FP32 in registers. This PR adds a no-op fast path that returns the original logits tensor and preserves the existing FP32 path whenever any active request needs logits processing.

For batch size 128 and vocabulary size 151,936, the fast path avoids materializing a 74.2 MiB FP32 tensor per decoding step, along with the associated copy kernel and memory traffic.


## Test Result

title: [ROCm][Perf] DSv4 two-stage compressor kernel for HCA prefill
author: kliuae
body:
## Purpose
This PR adds a two-stage Triton implementation to the DeepSeek-V4 compressor for the prefill path in head_dim=512, cr>=128 to improve TTFT.

On upstream ROCm, the single pass compressor-norm-rope-cache fusion is dispatched one workgroup per token. In HCA where compress ratio is 128, only workgroups that live on the CR boundary (positions % 128 == 0) execute on 128x512 grids, and the others early exit. During perfill, the number of boundaries per step is `num_prefill_tokens / cr`, and for a 8192-token chunk, that leaves 8192/128=64 CUs in action, leaving most of the CUs unoccupied (e.g. 256 total CUs on MI355).

Following the strategy in CuTeDSL CUDA kernel, this PR breaks this path into two stages/kernels:
- Compress: this is the more compute-demanding stage. Instead of compressing the 128 rows for all heads in one single program, split workloads along the head dimension so that each program computes only a `head_dim / num_splits` slice of the output, and more programs can be spawned to fill the CUs. As the weighted sum is independent for each column, he split is exact and no cross-workgroup reduction is needed.
- Finalize: the remaining norm-rope-cache ops. As the workload is serial but light, this uses the original one-program-per-boundary dispatch strategy.

The number of splits for the first stage is sized to target `num_splits ~= num_CUs / num_cr_boundaries` to saturate the CUs. The two stage split is enabled for prefill whose workloads benefit more from filling the occupancy. In prefill-heavy workloads, this brings ~3-4% reduction in TTFT.

title: [ROCm][KVConnector][MoRI-IO] Fix WRITE-mode remote-TP rank collapse (#46332 follow-up)
author: avininjamay8
body:
## Purpose

 In WRITE mode, each prefill TP rank must target the correct decode TP rank for KV transfer. #46332 introduced heterogeneous TP support, requiring the prefill to query the decode's TP size (remote_tp_size) from the proxy to compute the correct target rank. The rank mapping reads peer TP size from kv_transfer_params, but the proxy sets remote_tp_size not tp_size. The old code read tp_size which was never set, defaulting to 1. This caused all 8 prefill TP ranks to fan into decode rank 0, leaving 7/8 of the decode KV cache unwritten and accuracy collapsing to near zero in WRITE mode. READ mode was unaffected.

**Changes**

- moriio_common.py - read remote_tp_size (falling back to tp_size, then 0) when building transfer params.
- moriio_connector.py - treat remote_tp_size <= 0 as homogeneous TP (use local world_size) instead of collapsing to rank 0.

## Test Plan

MoRIIO connector over RoCE RDMA fabric, 1P1D WRITE mode (`read_mode: false`), nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`.

### Homogeneous TP8 — MI350X

Serve DeepSeek-V3 1P1D, prefill TP8 / decode TP8.

  ```bash
  # PREFILL — TP8
  vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V3 \
      --host $PREFILL_IP --port 8100 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
      --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager \
      --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"proxy_ip":"$PREFILL_IP","proxy_ping_port":"36367",
        "http_port":"8100","handshake_port":"6301","notify_port":"61005","read_mode":false}}'                                          
  # DECODE — TP8
  vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V3 \
      --host $DECODE_IP --port 8200 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.7 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --trust-remote-code \
      --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"proxy_ip":"$PREFILL_IP","proxy_ping_port":"36367",                                                       "http_port":"8200","handshake_port":"6301","notify_port":"61005","read_mode":false}}'
```

### Heterogeneous TP (prefill TP4 / decode TP8) — MI300X

Serve DeepSeek-V3 1P1D, prefill TP4 / decode TP8.

  ```bash
  # PREFILL — TP4
  vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V3 \
      --host $PREFILL_IP --port 8100 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
      --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager \
      --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"proxy_ip":"$PREFILL_IP","proxy_ping_port":"36367",
        "http_port":"8100","handshake_port":"6301","notify_port":"61005","read_mode":false}}'

  # DECODE — TP8
  vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V3 \
      --host $DECODE_IP --port 8200 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.7 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --trust-remote-code \
      --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"proxy_ip":"$PREFILL_IP","proxy_ping_port":"36367",
        "http_port":"8200","handshake_port":"6301","notify_port":"61005","read_mode":false}}' 
``` 

Also verified Homogeous TP on MI300.

### GSM8K Evaluation

  ```bash
  lm_eval --model local-completions \
      --tasks gsm8k \
      --model_args
  model=/models/DeepSeek-V3,base_url=http://$PREFILL_IP:10001/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \      --limit 250
```

## Test Result

### Accuracy Results (GSM8K, flexible-extract)

  ```
  Config                                    Platform   Without fix   With fix
  ----------------------------------------  --------   -----------   --------
  1P1D homogeneous TP8                       MI350X         ~0.00      0.944
  1P1D heterogeneous (prefill TP4/dec TP8)   MI300X         ~0.00      0.95
  ``` 

Also validated on: DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4, Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4 (1P1D and 2P2D TP8).

title: [Core] Preserve Marconi caching with selective hybrid cache retention
author: njhill
body:
The [Marconi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19379) paper was implemented in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37898, which enables caching of mamba state for shared prefixes in "align" mode.

This PR extends the shared prefix boundary caching to the retention-interval sparse caching added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43447 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45845 for both mamba states and SWA.

In particular it means we can set retention interval = 0 for optimal long-context/agent session caching and also benefit from implicitly cached system prompt.

title: [Bugfix] Fix handling 5D KV cache in kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive
author: dsocek
body:
## PR Purpose

Fixes `IndexError` in `kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive()` for 5D blocks-first KV caches.

`kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive()` (added in #30275) permutes a received KV cache from HND to NHD layout. It assumes the cache is 4D. But since #42095 is recently merged, non-MLA backends allocate a 5D cache `(num_blocks, 2, block_size, H, D)`. This causes the following error:

```bash
IndexError: index_copy_(): Source dimensionality (4), destination dimensionality (5)
```
(This was also flagged as future work in #37943)

### Fix
Use a 5D-aware `inv_order` when the cache is 5D (while 4D path remains unchanged)

## Test Plan
Quick test with:
```bash
DECODER_KV_LAYOUT=NHD DECODER_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN \
bash tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh
```

## Test Result
Before: `IndexError`
After: **pass**

title: [Spec Decode] DSpark confidence-scheduled verification
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
Adaptively sizes the DSpark draft-verification budget from per-request confidence instead of always verifying every drafted token. Motivation: fixed-k speculation collapses at high concurrency — once the GPU saturates, verifying 7 drafts per request burns more compute than the accepted tokens return, dropping **below** non-speculative decoding (see table). ## Design - A Triton kernel ranks draft slots by survival probability (cumprod of per-position confidence) and admits the prefix maximizing estimated accepted tokens per millisecond. - Step costs come from curves profiled with dummy steps at startup: a step function at/below the cudagraph capture limit (padding is physical), linear interpolation above it. - Batch-level budget sizing runs on CPU from double-buffered *stale* confidences (no sync); per-request allocation runs on GPU from live values. - Per-request confidence is smoothed with an EMA (`adaptive_verification_ema_alpha`, default 0.8 — measured bias-zero crossing across batch sizes). - Decode cudagraphs become varlen: captured on the token grid, dispatched via `max_query_len`, every captured slot non-empty. Requires `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, which the DSV4 backends report on SM100. ## Results DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, TP=4, SM100 (B300), `speed_bench` 256 prompts, 512 output tokens; throughput measured at `32881ec177`; subsequent HEAD commits are audit fixes off the captured-graph hot path (decode `max_q_len` sourcing, CPU upper-bound restoration, non-adaptive request-ordering revert to main), accuracy re-validated at HEAD. Output tok/s: Adaptive matches fixed-k within ±3% at c≤64 and preserves the spec-decode win at high concurrency where fixed-k goes underwater (at c=256, fixed 7-token is 33% *below* no-spec). Acceptance length falls from ~3.9 to 3.5 at c=256 — the budget deliberately trims drafts as verification tokens become expensive. Note: the no-spec arm ran with a co-tenant job on the other half of the node; its numbers are directionally correct but modestly depressed. Adaptive/fixed arms ran on an idle node. Accuracy (re-measured at HEAD after the audit fixes below): GSM8K **0.945** (c=16) / **0.951** (c=64), 0 invalid (bar 0.84); MTBench **80/80** completed, completions manually checked for repetition/degeneration — none found.
Reproduction commands **Server** (all measurements; ablations via the noted config deltas): ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \ --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 8192 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --block-size 256 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 \ --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark","attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' ``` - fixed 7-token baseline: `"enable_adaptive_verification":false` - no-spec baseline: omit `--speculative-config` **Benchmark harness** — `vllm bench serve` (the Python implementation; the CLI falls back to it automatically when the optional Rust `vllm-rs` binary is absent). If your install ships a Rust binary that rejects any flag below, invoke the Python implementation directly — still repo-only: ```bash python -c 'from vllm.benchmarks.serve import add_cli_args, main from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser p = FlexibleArgumentParser(); add_cli_args(p); main(p.parse_args())' ``` **GSM8K** (in-tree runner; 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0): ```bash python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 \ --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 16 # and 64 ``` **MTBench coherence** (80 prompts, temperature 1; inspect the saved completions for repetition/degeneration, not just the completion count): ```bash vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model dspark-full \ --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --dataset-name hf --dataset-path philschmid/mt-bench \ --num-prompts 80 --no-oversample --hf-output-len 256 \ --max-concurrency 16 --request-rate inf --temperature 1 \ --save-result --save-detailed ``` **Throughput sweep** (per concurrency; one warmup pass at `--speed-bench-output-len 256 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 32` first): ```bash for c in 1 16 32 64 128 256; do vllm bench serve \ --backend openai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \ --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model dspark-full \ --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path \ --speed-bench-dataset-subset qualitative \ --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle --temperature 1.0 \ --speed-bench-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency $c \ --save-result --result-filename adaptive_on_c${c}.json done ``` `--disable-shuffle` plus the fixed prompt set gives every arm identical prompts in identical order; `output_throughput` from the result JSON is the tok/s reported above. The prompt set is an internal speed-bench "qualitative" subset; any fixed prompt set of comparable length distribution reproduces the relative behavior, e.g. `--dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512`.
## Limitations - Output logprobs are rejected when confidence-based verification is enabled (verification compacts logits after the forward pass). - Non-SM100 falls back to PIECEWISE decode graphs: correct, but without the varlen-FULL-graph throughput win. ## Tests ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py tests/v1/cudagraph/ -q ``` All pass; full pre-commit green. GSM8K eval config added at `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-confidence-TP4.yaml`. ## Not a duplicate Canonical PR for DSpark confidence-based verification; no other open PR touches adaptive draft budgeting. --- AI assistance was used for this change (see commit trailers). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Quantization] Bound peak memory when repacking FP4 MoE weights for Marlin
author: joerowell
body:
## Purpose
The FP4 MoE Marlin prep functions repack each expert's weight into a Python list and torch.cat the list into the final [E, ...] tensor. At the cat, the per-expert list and the concatenated result are both live, transiently holding ~2x the repacked weight footprint. For large MoE checkpoints on unified-memory devices (e.g. GB10 where "GPU" memory is shared host DRAM) this spike can exhaust the box during model load.

Fill a preallocated [E, ...] output expert-by-expert instead. Output is byte-identical to the cat; only the intermediate allocation changes. Applied to the weight repack in prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin, prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin, and prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin (the memory-dominant path; scales/bias are much smaller and left unchanged).



## Test Plan
If existing tests pass, this change should be safe.

Tested manually with `vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b --moe-backend marlin`

title: [CPU] fixes heterogeneous NIXL KV transfer into CPU_ATTN decode workers
author: sihancx
body:
## Purpose

fix heterogeneous NIXL KV transfer into CPU_ATTN decode workers, and resolve Prefill(XPU) -> Decode(CPU) accuracy issue.

The accuracy issue was fixed earlier in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38935. However after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44393 , the layout was changed again. This PR fixes the issue.

## Test Plan

Prefill (XPU) -> Decode (CPU) accuracy is validated locally

in prefill xpu container

```bash
export VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=debug
export UCX_TLS=ze_ipc,ze_copy,self,tcp
export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=4
export model_name=Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
export tp_size=1

# prefill (XPU)
VLLM_USE_V1=1 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=localhost VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5577 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=1 vllm serve $model_name -tp $tp_size --host localhost --port 8100 --seed 42 --enforce-eager --dtype float16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_buffer_device":"cpu", "kv_connector_extra_config":{"enforce_handshake_compat": false}}' --max-model-len 8192 --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching &
# proxy
python3 /workspace/vllm/tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py --prefiller-host localhost --prefiller-port 8100 --decoder-host localhost --decoder-port 8200 --host localhost --port 8300

```

```bash

export UCX_TLS=ze_ipc,ze_copy,self,tcp
export model_name=Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
```
