title: [ROCm][CI][MoE] Fix double-transpose of fused w3 expert weights
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a crash when loading fused MoE expert weights whose checkpoint stores the
`gate_up_proj` tensor in a transposed layout (e.g.
`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`).

In `RoutedExperts.load_weights`, a single fused checkpoint tensor
(`gate_up_proj`) is matched **twice** by the expert mapping — once for `w1` and
once for `w3`. The transpose reassigned the outer-loop `loaded_weight`, so the
`w3` iteration saw the tensor **already transposed** by the `w1` iteration and
transposed it a second time. For block-scale tensors (`gate_up_proj_scale_inv`)
this made `chunk(2, dim=1)` split the hidden-block dimension instead of the
intermediate-block dimension, producing shards of the wrong size and crashing
weight loading:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (6) must match the size of tensor b (8)
at non-singleton dimension 0
```

The plain weight survived by luck (after the first transpose its last dim equals
`hidden`, so the second transpose is skipped), but the block scale did not.

Fix: use a per-iteration local variable so the transpose never mutates the shared
`loaded_weight`. Both `w1` and `w3` now start from the original tensor, making
them symmetric.

The `w2` (down_proj) branch matches only once and the non-fused path is
untouched, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_length.py -k "qwen3-30b-moe-vl-eagle3"
```

## Test Result

On ROCm (MI300, gfx942) the target FP8 MoE model now loads and the `tp1`
case passes end-to-end (including the acceptance-length assertions):

```
test_eagle3_acceptance_length[auto-tp1-3-qwen3-30b-moe-vl-eagle3] PASSED
```
---

- [x] Root cause identified (shared `loaded_weight` mutated across w1/w3).
- [x] `w2` and non-fused paths verified unchanged (no regression).
- [ ] (CI) Validate on the ROCm CI lane.

title: [Kernel][ROCm][Perf] FlyDSL decode-attention kernel for 4-bit TurboQuant KV cache
author: aditi-amd
body: ## Purpose This PR upstreams the FlyDSL TurboQuant 4-bit KV-cache decode kernel developed and optimized by the AMD team. For background on the TurboQuant algorithm and its role in agentic vLLM serving, see our blog write-up [TurboQuant blog] (https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/artificial-intelligence/turboquant-vllm-agentic/README.html) This PR adds a custom FlyDSL TurboQuant 4-bit KV-cache decode kernel for ROCm / MI355X (gfx950) as an opt-in alternative to the default vLLM TurboQuant Triton decode, for its supported profile: 1. KV cache quantized to 4-bit (MSE-key centroids + 4-bit value), HEAD_SIZE=128 2. GQA group ∈ {8, 16} → canonical tq_decode kernel 3. GQA group == 6 → tq_decode_gqa6 sibling kernel (MiniMax-M2.5) 4. arch == gfx950 ( gfx950 / CDNA4; the kernel uses CDNA4-only intrinsics and is tuned and validated there) Selection is automatic (no env flag): on gfx950 with 4-bit TurboQuant KV and FlyDSL importable, eligible decode layers route to the FlyDSL kernel via capability gating (on_gfx950()). Layers with unsupported shapes — or all layers if FlyDSL isn't importable — fall back to the SoA Triton TurboQuant decode. ## Test Plan 1. Kernel correctness (unit test): tests/kernels/turboquant/test_flydsl_turboquant_decode.py validates the flydsl decode kernel against a pure-PyTorch fp32 attention oracle built from the known dequantized KV values (both sides see identical quantized data; only bf16-vs-fp32 accumulation differs). Parametrized over batch × seq-len × {GQA-8, GQA-16, GQA-6} × block-size {16, 32}. Skips cleanly off ROCm/gfx950 or when FlyDSL is not importable. 2. Accuracy (GSM8K, full 1319-sample test set) on MiniMax-M2.5 and Qwen3-32B: bf16 baseline vs TQ44v4. 3. End-to-end perf runs: identical server + bench config, only the KV-cache dtype / decode kernel differs per leg. ## Test Result ### Accuracy — GSM8K (exact match, 1319 samples) | Model | BF16 | FlyDSL TQ44 | |---|---|---|---| | MiniMax-M2.5 | 88.17 | 87.95 (−0.22) | | Qwen3-32B | 95.45 | 95.15 (−0.30) | Accuracy is neutral (within ~0.4pp of BF16 across both models). ### Perf — MiniMax-M2.5, 32K in / 1K out, TP=2, C=64, N=80, MI355X The middle leg is the existing default vLLM TurboQuant 4-bit decode. TQ44 FlyDSL is +7% over BF16 and ~4.1× the default TurboQuant decode at 4-bit KV. ## Recommended serve command ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 # keep the fast aiter CK fused-MoE vllm serve --port 8000 \ --tensor-parallel-size=2 --enable-expert-parallel \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 34816 \ --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc --block-size=32 \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-log-requests \ --trust-remote-code --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' ``` Bench (identical for every leg): ```bash vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \ --endpoint /v1/completions --model --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \ --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 80 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \ --num-warmups 8 --seed 42 ```

title: [Bugfix] Allow non-contiguous query in FlashInfer FP8 query quantization
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
Fix #47905 

## Purpose

Fix an `AssertionError` in the FlashInfer attention backend when running models that slice their query from a fused QKV projection (e.g. Nemotron) with FP8 KV cache.

#43232 moved the query→FP8 quantization inline into `FlashInferImpl.maybe_quant_query`, guarded by `assert query.is_contiguous()`. Models such as Nemotron produce their query via `q, k, v = qkv.split(...)`, which returns a **view** into the fused QKV tensor. That view has a token-dim stride equal to the full QKV width, so the query is non-contiguous and trips the assert on the native FlashInfer FP8 prefill/decode path:

```
File ".../flashinfer.py", line 1587, in maybe_quant_query
    assert query.is_contiguous()
AssertionError
```

The assert is over-strict. Both `query.view(num_tokens, num_heads * head_size)` and the `scaled_fp8_quant` kernel only require that the per-token `(num_heads, head_size)` block is contiguous — the token-dim stride is free (the kernel reads it from `stride(-2)` and only requires `stride(-1) == 1`). This PR replaces the contiguity assert with that precise precondition (`query.stride(2) == 1 and query.stride(1) == head_size`), keeping the existing zero-copy `view` path.

This is not a duplicate: no open PR addresses the FlashInfer FP8 query-quantization contiguity assertion. It is a follow-up bugfix to #43232.

## Test Plan

Repro: serve a Nemotron model with `--attention-backend FLASHINFER --kv-cache-dtype fp8` (previously raised `AssertionError` in `maybe_quant_query`; also reported on Nemotron + FlashInfer FP8 outside PD-disagg).

- [x] Nemotron + FlashInfer + FP8 KV cache serves without the assertion.
- [x] Existing FlashInfer FP8 paths (contiguous query) unchanged.

## Test Result

Confirmed working

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to diagnose and draft this change.

title: fix: hash speculative draft model config
author: alexeldeib
body:
## Purpose

AOT compilation cache keys include VllmConfig.compute_hash(), which delegates to SpeculativeConfig.compute_hash(). For DFlash and related aux-hidden-state methods, the speculative hash only distinguished whether aux states were used and which aux layer IDs were returned.

That is insufficient when two deployments share an AOT cache root but use different draft model configs with the same aux layer IDs. The second deployment can load an AOT artifact compiled for the first draft model, even though the compiled graph shape contract belongs to a different draft backbone.

Include draft_model_config.compute_hash() whenever aux-hidden-state speculative decoding uses a draft model. Keep the existing layer-id factor so configs that share the same draft model but request different aux states still hash separately.

## Test Plan

~Add a focused regression test covering two DFlash-like configs with identical aux layer IDs but different draft model hashes.~ removed per feedback

## Test Result

Avoids collision between two incompatible models on the cache key. This solves a real-world serving issue where the drafters have slightly different architectures but attempt to reuse the cache leading to assertion errors on code paths like this qwen3_dflash.py -> flash_attn.py -> vllm_flash_attn/cute/interface.py
```
assert k.shape == (num_pages, page_size, num_head_kv, head_dim)
```

Running either model independently with a clean cache works, making the fingerprint fully unique solves the collision.

title: [Spec Decode] Support hybrid (SWA + full attention) DFlash drafters
author: mgoin
body:
Enables DFlash drafters that mix sliding-window and full-attention layers (e.g. z-lab/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DFlash) on the V2 model runner, by giving each KV cache group its own causal attention metadata so the sliding-window layers run causal and the full-attention layers non-causal.

Also fixes lm_head sharing when the target is a *ForConditionalGeneration model: the head is nested under get_language_model(), so the draft was keeping its zero-initialized head. This affects DFlash, DSpark, and EAGLE/MTP.

Depends on #45207 and #47698 for GDN/mamba target support.

Validated on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + z-lab/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DFlash: GSM8K acceptance length ~5 at 7 speculative tokens.

title: [Tests][Spec Decode] Add gemma4 MTP acceptance rates test
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# This PR
Gemma4 MTP is lacking acceptance tests for both MRV1 and MRV2. I generalized the existing `test_dflash_acceptance_rates` test into `test_acceptance_rates` and extended it to test dflash (Qwen/Qwen3-8B + z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16) and gemma4 MTP (google/gemma-4-E4B-it + google/gemma-4-E4B-it-assistant). The test iterates over the specified datasets in `expected_acceptance_lengths`, runs the eval, and verifies that the acceptance length approximately matches what was expected. The test allows specifying a different set of datasets/acceptance lenghts per base/draft model pair.

Google didn't publish acceptance rates for the gemma4 draft models, so I just used the MRV1 implementation as a baseline. Fortunately, the MRV1 and MRV2 acceptance lengths match exactly across gsm8k, humaneval, and mt-bench.

While trying to enable these tests, I noticed and fixes these issues:
1. MRV1's Gemma4 MTP had a startup issue because #43957 added an embedding-dim equality guard to `_maybe_share_embeddings` in llm_base_proposer.py, but Gemma4 MTP intentionally shares dim-mismatched embeddings. Added a `_maybe_share_embeddings` override in gemma4.py.

3. In the case of probabilistic rejection sampling (using draft logits), the gumbel sample positions weren't being updated for the last N - 1 draft steps. Although KV positions shouldn't be updated, the gumbel sample positions should be.

title: [EC Connector] P2P NIXL + CPU EC Connector
author: omerpaz95
body:
## Purpose
This PR extends ECCPUConnector to support P2P EC sharing based on NIXL. [The original PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42998) was split into two parts; [The first part](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47423) is a standalone CPU-based offloading EC connector, and this PR is an extension of it, allowing CPU-offloaded EC cache to be shared between vLLM instances via NIXL.
The control plane is ZMQ (consumer DEALER → producer ROUTER) carrying msgpack XferReq / XferAck.
**Dependencies:**
- [EC Transfer Params](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42433)
- [CPU OffloadingEC Connector](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47423)

## Logic

- **Producer scheduler.** Binds a ZMQ ROUTER. A single router thread owns the socket, ingests `XferReq` frames, validates `mm_hash` presence in  `_local_encodings` (NACK queued otherwise), pins the matching block indices in the CPU mmap region, and posts an async NIXL `WRITE` directly to the consumer's pre-registered destination blocks (In the consumer's CPU mmap region). 
Completions are polled on every router-loop iteration via `_sweep_completions`, which unpins blocks and emits `XferAck(ok=True/false)`. 
Two-phase bookkeeping (`_pending_save` → `_local_encodings`) prevents serving  pre-`save_caches` garbage: a freshly allocated block range only becomes serveable on the next `build_connector_meta` step, by which point the worker's `save_caches` has finished and synchronized.
- **Producer worker.** `save_caches` copies `encoder_cache[mm_hash]` →  `mmap[block_indices]` on a dedicated copy stream and CPU-syncs before returning, so the bytes are coherent for the scheduler's NIXL reads.
- **Consumer scheduler.** Lazy DEALER pool keyed by `(host, port)` with  ZMTP heartbeat + per-DEALER monitor sockets subscribed to  `EVENT_DISCONNECTED`. `ensure_cache_available(request)` allocates  blocks for unseen `mm_hash`es from `request.ec_transfer_params`,  sends `XferReq`, and returns `pending=True` until ack arrives. A  `_loaded` mmap cache keeps completed transfer blocks alive for local re-copy on subsequent requests (`_pending_reload`), avoiding the producer round-trip when possible.
- **Consumer worker.** `start_load_caches` copies `mmap[block_indices]` → `encoder_cache[mm_hash]` on a dedicated copy stream.
- **Failure path.** Producer-side NACK (unknown `mm_hash`, compat hash mismatch, evicted) → consumer frees blocks and falls through to local encode. Producer disconnect → ZMTP heartbeat fires  `EVENT_DISCONNECTED` within `HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` (4s); `on_peer_down` evicts the peer, removes the NIXL agent, and tombstones in-flight entries so stalled requests fall back cleanly.

## End-to-End Architecture

```
                      ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │  External caller (orchestrator +     │
                      │  request router, out of scope here)  │
                      │                                      │
                      └─┬──▲────────────────────────┬────────┘
                        │  │                        │
                   HTTP │  │ HTTP response body     │  HTTP req w/
                    req │  │ carries top-level      │  ec_transfer_params
                 (OpenAI│  │ ec_transfer_params     │  in extra_args
                  + b64 │  │                        │
                  +     │  │                        │
                  max=1)│  │                        │
                        ▼  │                        ▼
         ┌──────────────┬──┴──────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────┐
         │ Producer vLLM              │    │ Consumer vLLM            │
         │ ec_role=ec_producer        │    │ ec_role=ec_consumer      │
         │ mm_encoder_only=true       │    │                          │
         │                            │    │                          │
         │ Scheduler                  │    │ Scheduler                │
         │ ├─ ECSharedRegion          │    │ ├─ ECSharedRegion        │
         │ │    (mmap, NIXL-reg,      │    │ │    (mmap, NIXL-reg,    │
         │ │     alloc/free/pin)      │    │ │     alloc/free)        │
         │ ├─ _local_encodings:       │    │ ├─ _remote_encodings:    │
         │ │    mm_hash →             │    │ │    mm_hash →           │
         │ │    block_indices         │    │ │    block_indices       │
         │ ├─ NIXL agent              │    │ ├─ _ready: arrived       │
         │ ├─ ZMQ ROUTER              │    │ │    mm_hashes           │
         │ │   (VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL) │    │ ├─ NIXL agent            │
         │ ├─ router thread           │    │ ├─ peer pool:            │
         │ └─ in-flight xfers         │    │ │    (host,port) →       │
         │                            │    │ │    (DEALER,agent,md)   │
         │ Worker                     │    │ └─ ensure_cache_         │
         │ └─ save_caches:            │    │    available(request)    │
         │    GPU → mmap              │    │                          │
         │    at block_indices        │    │ Worker                   │
         │    from metadata           │    │ └─ start_load_caches:    │
         │                            │    │    mmap → GPU            │
         │ request_finished() emits   │    │    at block_indices      │
         │ ec_transfer_params         │    │    from metadata         │
         │ in response body           │    │                          │
         └──────────┬─────────────────┘    └──────────┬───────────────┘
                    │                                 │
                    │   ROUTER ← ZMQ DEALER           │
                    │   XferReq / XferAck             │
                    │  ◄───────────────────────────── │
                    │                                 │
                    │   NIXL WRITE                    │
                    │   mmap → remote mmap            │
                    │  ──────────────────────────────►│
                    └────────────────────────────────►│
```

## Lifecycle (cold path)

1. Caller dispatches request to producer. Producer runs with `--mm-encoder-only`.
2. Producer scheduler `build_connector_meta` allocates blocks for the newly-scheduled `mm_hash`, parks them in `_pending_save`, emits `meta.saves[mm_hash] = block_indices`.
3. Producer worker's `save_caches` copies GPU → mmap at those indices, synchronizes the copy stream.
4. Next step's `build_connector_meta` promotes `_pending_save` →  `_local_encodings`. Producer's `request_finished` returns `ec_transfer_params = {mm_hash: {peer_host, peer_port, size_bytes, nixl_agent_metadata_b64}}` in the response body.
5. Caller forwards the original request to a consumer with `sampling_params.extra_args["ec_transfer_params"]` populated from (4).
6. Consumer scheduler `ensure_cache_available` allocates blocks, opens a ZMQ DEALER to the producer (cached in the peer pool), `add_remote_agent`s the producer's NIXL identity, and sends `XferReq` over the DEALER.
7. Producer router thread receives `XferReq` over the ZMQ ROUTER, pins blocks, posts NIXL `WRITE` to consumer's `dst_block_indices`. On `check_xfer_state == DONE`, sends `XferAck(ok=True)` and unpins.
8. Consumer `_drain_acks` consumes the ack, moves `mm_hash` to `_ready`. Next `build_connector_meta` adds it to `meta.loads` and moves blocks to `_loaded`. Worker copies mmap → GPU on its dedicated stream.
9. Subsequent requests for the same `mm_hash` re-serve via local mmap → GPU re-copy (`_pending_reload`), no producer round-trip (until evicted when the CPU mmap region is full - FIFO policy).

## Configuration

All knobs in `ec_connector_extra_config`.

| Field | Scope | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--mm-encoder-only` (existing) | producer, required | `False` | Skip the LM entirely; only the vision encoder runs. |
| `ec_connector_extra_config.num_ec_blocks` | both | `80000` | Block count in the mmap region on each side. |
| `VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST` (env) | producer | pod IP | ZMQ ROUTER bind host. |
| `VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT` (env) | producer | — | ZMQ ROUTER bind port; advertised to caller in response's `peer_port`. |

Consumer needs no static peer config — every value to reach a producer arrives per-request via `ec_transfer_params`.

## Testing plan

- **Unit** (`tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/`): `test_metadata.py` (msgpack round-trip, compat hash factors); `test_scheduler.py` (~10 tests covering producer + consumer branches: alloc/send, idempotency, ack success/failure, peer-pool invalidation, router-thread WRITE/NACK, concurrent xfers per `mm_hash`, `request_finished` shape);
  `test_worker.py` (3 tests for save/load copy paths);
  `test_ec_shared_region.py`, `test_utils.py`, `test_common.py`
- **Run command:**
  ```bash
  python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/ -v
  ```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Restrict embedding-width share guard to EAGLE drafts
author: evantakahashi
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #47794 — Gemma4 MTP fails engine initialization on nightly with a linear shape mismatch (`[s47, 3840] x [5632, 1024]`).

Root cause: #43957 added an embedding-width guard to `_maybe_share_embeddings` that disables target↔draft embedding sharing when the widths differ. That is correct for EAGLE drafts, which consume `input_embeds` in their decoder layers at their own hidden size (the `Eagle3MiniMaxM2` XPU case #43957 fixed). It is wrong for MTP drafts: Gemma4 MTP's `pre_projection` is built as `Linear(2 * backbone_hidden_size, hidden_size)` and its draft-width `embed_tokens` exists only to populate the tied draft-dim `lm_head` — `gemma4_mtp.py` explicitly documents that sharing replaces it with the backbone-width table. With sharing disabled, the concat width becomes `1024 + 2816 = 3840` instead of `2816 + 2816 = 5632`, crashing at init.

Fix: apply the width guard only to EAGLE drafts, keyed on the `has_own_embed_tokens` attribute — the existing EAGLE/MTP discriminator in this method. MTP drafts return to unconditional sharing (pre-#43957 behavior); the #43957 EAGLE behavior is preserved.

## Relationship to existing PRs

I claimed #47794 in the issue at 04:13 UTC with this diagnosis and fix plan ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47794#issuecomment-4900048127)); #47833 was opened at 07:17 UTC without engaging that claim. Beyond the overlap, this PR adds runtime verification driving the real `Gemma4MTP` module (see below), which #47833 notes it could not do, plus an additional MTP dims-match regression case. Happy to consolidate whichever way maintainers prefer.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_share_embeddings.py -v
```

Runtime A/B verification (CPU, no GPU needed): instantiated the real `Gemma4MTP` module (0 decoder layers, draft width 8, backbone width 32) plus a target with a backbone-width embedding table, ran the real `SpecDecodeBaseProposer._maybe_share_embeddings`, then the real `Gemma4MTP.forward` — the exact seam that crashed in the issue.

## Test Result

- On `main` (unfixed): new test `test_mtp_shares_embeddings_when_dims_differ` FAILS; runtime harness reports `embeddings shared: False` and forward crashes with `mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (4x40 and 64x8)` — the scaled analogue of the issue's `3840 x 5632` mismatch.
- With this PR: all 4 tests PASS; harness reports `embeddings shared: True`, `forward OK: draft_hidden=(4, 8) backbone_hidden=(4, 32)`, and the tied draft-dim `lm_head` is left intact.
- EAGLE regression coverage: dims-differ stays unshared (#43957 behavior), dims-match shares.
- `pre-commit` (ruff check/format, mypy hook, typos) passes on changed files.
- Not run: end-to-end GPU serve with the 26B checkpoint (no hardware) — @realmorita, could you confirm on your setup?

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the analysis, fix, tests, and verification; submitted after human review.

title: Support DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark NVFP4 with emulation kernel
author: jimmy-adams
body:
## Purpose

Add support for DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark mixed-quantized checkpoints, where different parts of the model may use different quantization layouts, including per-block FP8 linear layers and NVFP4 MoE experts.

This PR focuses on the Quark/DeepSeek-V4 model-side pieces needed to correctly identify and load these mixed-quantized checkpoints. It avoids changing generic weight-loading behavior and keeps DeepSeek-V4-specific mappings out of the base `QuarkConfig`.

## Main Changes

- Add a dedicated `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` scheme for Quark per-block FP8 weights.
  - Keeps the existing `QuarkW8A8Fp8` path focused on per-tensor/per-channel FP8.
  - Derives activation group size from `block_size[1]` instead of hardcoding it independently.
  - Requires per-block FP8 configs to provide `block_size`.

- Move DeepSeek-V4-specific fused module mappings to the DeepSeek-V4 AMD model path.
  - Handles mappings such as `gate_up_proj -> [w1, w3]` and `fused_wqa_wkv -> [wq_a, wkv]` without injecting architecture-specific knowledge into generic `QuarkConfig`.

- Add DeepSeek-V4 AMD checkpoint name handling for scale tensors.
  - Supports checkpoint/vLLM parameter naming differences needed by the mixed Quark layout.

- Align Quark NVFP4 MoE fused `w13` global-scale handling with existing NVFP4 MoE implementations.
  - When `w1/w3` global scales differ, warn and use the `w1` scale for fused `w13`, matching the existing ModelOpt and compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE convention.
  - This avoids introducing a new `max(w1, w3)` scale-selection policy in this PR.

- Keep generic loader behavior unchanged.
  - The previous diagnostic/debug changes to `parameter.py` were reverted.
  - The PR no longer modifies generic weight-loader logic.

## Out of Scope

- This PR does not introduce a new generic NVFP4 scale-selection policy.
- This PR does not claim full E2E coverage for a future Quark-exported per-block FP8 checkpoint until such a checkpoint is available.
- Broader refactoring of shared NVFP4 MoE scale handling can be done in a separate follow-up PR.

- Inspect DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint tensor shapes and quantization configs.

title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3][Spec Decode] Support speculative decode with AITER sparse PA
author: tanpinsiang
body:
## Summary

This PR enables MiniMax-M3 speculative decode on the ROCm AITER sparse paged-attention path introduced in #47287.

The core change maps flattened speculative decode rows back to their request-local query positions:

```text
req_id = row // decode_query_len
local_q = row % decode_query_len
query_abs_pos = seq_lens[req_id] - decode_query_len + local_q
```

Then it reuses the existing prefill sparse block-table builder to produce one compact page-16 AITER table row per query token.

No new Triton/Gluon attention kernel is added. The existing `decode_query_len == 1` fast path is preserved.

## What Changed

- Add `minimax_m3_build_sparse_block_table_decode`.
- Remove the AITER sparse-PA `decode_query_len != 1` rejection.
- Pass `decode_query_len` into the internal AITER sparse decode adapter.
- Add ROCm coverage for speculative sparse block-table mapping.
- Harden sparse block-table generation for padded/empty decode rows, including the existing non-spec decode path under FULL cudagraph padding.

## Why

#47287 adds the AITER sparse PA path but keeps speculative decode unsupported. That blocks MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3/MTP from using the same sparse-PA fast path.

This PR closes that gap with minimal plumbing:
- spec decode reuses the existing sparse table builder;
- single-token decode behavior remains unchanged;
- padding behavior is covered explicitly.

## Scope

This is ROCm/MiniMax-M3-specific and internal to the AITER sparse PA path.

This PR does not change:
- the non-AITER sparse attention path;
- NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 behavior;
- the AITER attention kernel itself;
- public user-facing configuration.

- **Hardware**: AMD Instinct MI355X

title: [ROCm] Remove redundant AITER fused_qk_rmsnorm probe (avoids config-time HIP init)
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

`enable_mla_dual_rms_norm_fusion` probed AITER (`check_aiter_fused_qk_rmsnorm`)
while building the `VllmConfig` in the **parent** process. That probe imports
`aiter`, which initializes the HIP context and forces the multiprocessing start
method to `spawn`. When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, this breaks any flow that
relies on `fork` — e.g. in-process registration of an out-of-tree model.

It reproduces as a ROCm-only failure of
`test_extract_hidden_states_with_predictable_dummy_model` (the test registers an
out-of-tree `PredictableLlamaForCausalLM` in-process and explicitly requests
`fork`):

```
ValueError: Model architectures ['PredictableLlamaForCausalLM'] are not supported
```

The same test passes on CUDA — the root cause is ROCm/AITER specific.

Instead of guarding non-MLA models, this PR **removes the redundant probe
entirely** (and a dead legacy fallback).

## Root cause

The test requests `fork` so the engine-core child inherits the in-process
registration:

```python
monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD", "fork")
```

With `fork` the child inherits the registration and works. With `spawn` the
child re-imports vLLM from scratch, the registry is empty, and the architecture
is "not supported".

vLLM force-overrides `fork` → `spawn` whenever the accelerator (HIP/CUDA)
context is already initialized in the parent (`_maybe_force_spawn`):

```
system_utils.py:157 We must use the `spawn` ... Reasons: CUDA is initialized
```

On ROCm with AITER enabled (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`), the HIP context gets
initialized in the parent during config construction, via this chain:

```
LLM() -> create_engine_config -> VllmConfig.__post_init__
  -> _apply_optimization_level_defaults
    -> enable_mla_dual_rms_norm_fusion            (vllm/config/vllm.py)
      -> check_aiter_fused_qk_rmsnorm             (vllm/_aiter_ops.py)
        -> from aiter.ops... import ...           # imports the aiter package
          -> aiter/.../arch_info.py
             triton...get_current_target().arch
               -> torch.cuda.current_device()     # initializes HIP
```

So merely building the config imported `aiter` to probe an MLA-only fusion
kernel — for **every** model, including non-MLA models like this Llama test —
and that import initialized HIP in the parent, forcing `spawn` and breaking the
test.

The probe was also **redundant**: on the pinned AITER (`v0.1.16.post3`) the
`fused_qk_rmsnorm` kernel is always present (it has shipped since ~`0.1.14`), so
`check_aiter_fused_qk_rmsnorm()` always returned `True`.

## Behavior / risk

- The MLA dual RMSNorm fusion pass is a graph pattern-matcher that only matches
  MLA q/kv dual-RMSNorm ops, so it is a **no-op for non-MLA models**. Gating it
  on `is_enabled()` alone is therefore safe.
- No `aiter` import at config time → the parent stays HIP-clean → `fork` is
  preserved.
- **MLA models** (`use_mla=True`): fusion still applies exactly as before
  (verified by the unit test).
- No functional regression; the change only removes an unnecessary parent-side
  HIP initialization and dead fallback code.

## Test Plan

Reproduced locally on MI300 (ROCm), inside the dev container:

```bash
# 1) Reproduce the bug (AITER enabled + fork)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/extract_hidden_states_integration/test_extraction.py::test_extract_hidden_states_with_predictable_dummy_model

# 2) CI-faithful run (spawn, no AITER)
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
pytest -v -s v1/kv_connector/extract_hidden_states_integration

# 3) MLA fusion still works
pytest -v -s tests/compile/passes/test_fuse_mla_dual_rms_norm.py
```

## Test Result

- **Before the fix** (with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`): parent imports `aiter` →
  HIP init → `spawn` override → `PredictableLlamaForCausalLM ... not supported`
  (**FAILED**).
- **After the fix**: parent stays HIP-clean, `fork` is used, test **passes**.
- `tests/compile/passes/test_fuse_mla_dual_rms_norm.py`: **2 passed**
  (bf16 + fp8 per-token) — MLA fusion unchanged.
- CI-faithful extract group (spawn, no AITER): **3 passed**.

title: [Perf][V1] Skip LRU hash-split in free_blocks when prefix caching is off
author: adobrzyn
body:
## Purpose

`BlockPool.free_blocks()` runs once per engine step. Since #42656 it always
partitions freed blocks into `blocks_with_hash` / `blocks_without_hash` (two
list builds + a per-block `block_hash is None` branch) and issues **two** queue
ops (`prepend_n` + `append_n`).

When prefix caching is **disabled** (`enable_caching=False`), no block ever
carries a hash, so `blocks_with_hash` is always empty and the partition is a
pure no-op that only adds CPU work on the hot path. Because `free_blocks()` is
called every step, on short decode steps (small models and/or low batch sizes,
where model-forward time is small) this fixed per-step overhead is a
measurable fraction of the step and reduces decode throughput.

This PR adds an early single-pass path in `free_blocks()` when
`enable_caching` is `False`, restoring the pre-#42656 behavior for that case.
When prefix caching is **enabled**, the #42656 LRU-ordering logic is unchanged.

## Correctness

With `enable_caching=False` every freed block already went into
`blocks_without_hash` and was `prepend_n`'d; the APC hash table is never
consulted in this mode, so free-list ordering does not affect cache-hit
behavior and the single-pass `append_n` is behavior-equivalent (identical
ref-count decrement and `ref_cnt == 0 and not is_null` freeing condition).
With `enable_caching=True` the code path is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit run --all-files` on the changed file (ruff-check + ruff-format pass).
- Serving benchmark on a decode-bound single-instance config (dense model,
  FP8, prefix caching off, 4096-in / 1024-out, max-concurrency 8): output-token
  throughput recovered ~3.5% and median TPOT dropped correspondingly vs.
  unpatched, matching the throughput of the commit immediately before #42656.
- No change in the `enable_caching=True` path.

## Test Result

Decode-bound benchmark, prefix caching off: ~734 -> ~760 tok/s (2 runs),
median TPOT ~10.5 -> ~10.1 ms. Bisect isolated the origin to #42656 by direct
parent/child comparison (parent GOOD vs #42656 BAD).

## Notes

- Not a duplicate: current `main` still carries the #42656 two-list split
  unchanged; no open PR addresses this per-step overhead (searched
  `free_blocks`, `block_pool` perf). This only restores the fast path for the
  `enable_caching=False` case and does not alter #42656's LRU improvement for
  prefix caching.
- AI assistance was used to bisect and draft this change; the submitter has
  reviewed every line and run the checks above.

title: [Kernel] ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs for faster Mamba2 standard decode
author: Johnny-Liou
body:
## Background

This is the first sub-PR split out from the large draft PR [#47576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47576), which presents the full ReplaySSM design across Mamba2 and Gated DeltaNet for both standard and speculative decode. To keep review tractable, this PR lands only the first stage, Mamba2 standard decode. ReplaySSM caches recent SSM inputs instead of writing the recurrent state back to HBM on every step. It is a collaboration between [Dao AI Lab](https://dao-lab.ai) and NVIDIA, and the full derivation and figures are in the [blog post](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/). AI assistance was used for parts of this work, and the authors have reviewed every changed line.

## Core concept

SSM decode is memory-bound. Each step loads and stores a `(nheads, d, n)` recurrent state, and that per-step state store dominates HBM traffic. ReplaySSM keeps a small ring buffer of recent inputs together with a periodic checkpoint state. On most steps it reads the decode output directly from the checkpoint plus the buffer, without materializing the full state, and it writes the full state back only on periodic flushes, once every `L` steps, where `L` is the buffer length. On the non-flush steps the per-step state store becomes a small input append, which roughly **halves** the dominant traffic.

The baseline only becomes bandwidth-bound at large batch. The table below reports the DRAM bandwidth the baseline `selective_state_update` reaches, as a percentage of peak, at the tuned config and measured in isolation.

| bs | H100 fp32 | H100 fp16 | B300 fp32 | B300 fp16 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 21.6% | 13.3% | 9.3% | 4.5% |
| 8 | 63.3% | 43.3% | 32.9% | 24.0% |
| 32 | 80.3% | 74.3% | 65.0% | 45.0% |
| 128 | 84.2% | 82.2% | 81.7% | 72.5% |
| 256 | 84.5% | 83.7% | 84.5% | 78.4% |
| 512 | 84.6% | 84.0% | 85.6% | 81.3% |

At small batch the per-request state footprint is tiny and the launch grid is small, so too few memory transactions are in flight to cover HBM latency, and the kernel is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound. In a hybrid model the small-batch step is also dominated by the MLP layers, not the SSM layers. Small batch is therefore not the target regime. **ReplaySSM targets serving batch**, where the SSM kernel saturates HBM and the per-step state store is the bottleneck.

## What this PR adds

Everything here is opt-in. With the feature off, the decode path is byte-for-byte the baseline.

- The Mamba2 output-only decode kernel `selective_state_update_replayssm_output_only`, plus its hardware-keyed launch-config helper.
- Two config flags, both default off. `--use-replayssm` turns on Mamba2 standard cached decode, and `--replayssm-buffer-len` sets the history buffer length `L` (default 16).
- Integration. The Mamba2 mixer dispatches to the kernel under the flag, the Mamba attention metadata builder carries the per-row ring cursor and flush flag, and the state-shape calculator sizes the extra caches on the paged state. The conv path reuses vLLM's `causal_conv1d_update` unchanged.

The feature requires `--mamba-cache-mode none`, and it covers standard (non-speculative) decode only.

## Design notes

### Paged cache layout

The input ring caches (`x`, `dt`, `B`) and the checkpoint state live inside the paged KV block, appended as extra tensors on the baseline `(conv, ssm)` state. They stay live across decode steps, the checkpoint until the next flush and the ring across many steps, so they must sit in HBM between kernel launches. Appending them onto the paged state reuses vLLM's per-request block allocation and block-table indexing directly. The output read vector (Mamba2 `C`) is never cached; it comes from the current step's activations.

### CUDA graphs and continuous batching

Whether a row flushes is per-row runtime data. Under continuous batching the rows in one captured batch sit at different buffer positions, so `is_flush` varies across the batch and cannot be a compile-time constant, even for standard decode. The kernel takes `is_flush` as a per-row input and branches on it inside the kernel, so one captured graph per batch size covers both the non-flush and the flush rows. The write position is `decode_step mod L`, computed on the host each step from scheduler token counts and copied to the device asynchronously, so no device-to-host sync is needed.

## Results

Two models are evaluated, Nemotron-3-Nano-4B (BF16) on one H100 and Nemotron-3-Super-120B (NVFP4) on one B300, at buffer length 16 with fp32 and fp16 SSM state, greedy, and CUDA graphs on. End-to-end numbers are produced with `benchmarks/replayssm/e2e_decode_speedup.py`.

> [!NOTE]
> **Baselines.** Speedups are reported against two baselines of vLLM's `selective_state_update` decode kernel:
> - **Tuned baseline** — a per-shape tuned launch config (the bundled JSON for the nearest shape). This is the honest, primary results.
> - **Default baseline** — the shipped default launch config.
>
> In the speedup tables every cell is written as `tuned (default)`, e.g. `1.52x (1.55x)`: the primary number is the speedup vs the **tuned** baseline, and the number in parentheses is the speedup vs the **default** baseline.

### End-to-end speedup

Whole-model per-step speedup. Each cell is `tuned (default)`, e.g. `1.52x (1.55x)` (see the baselines note above; the parenthetical number is vs the default baseline).

| bs | H100 fp32 | H100 fp16 | B300 fp32 | B300 fp16 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.98x (0.98x) | 0.98x (0.98x) | 0.96x (0.96x) | 0.96x (0.95x) |
| 8 | 1.03x (1.05x) | 1.00x (1.06x) | 1.01x (1.01x) | 0.98x (0.98x) |
| 32 | 1.16x (1.18x) | 1.07x (1.24x) | 1.06x (1.09x) | 1.00x (1.03x) |
| 128 | 1.38x (1.40x) | 1.21x (1.57x) | 1.24x (1.30x) | 1.04x (1.07x) |
| 256 | 1.47x (1.49x) | 1.26x (1.74x) | 1.42x (1.48x) | 1.06x (1.12x) |
| 512 | 1.52x (1.55x) | 1.30x (1.86x) | 1.72x (1.75x) | 1.11x (1.17x) |

ReplaySSM wins most at serving batch, where the SSM layers take a growing share of the step, and stays roughly break-even at bs 1 to 8. The large H100 fp16 default-baseline numbers (in parentheses) come from the poor shipped fp16 default, so the primary vs-tuned number is the honest figure.

### Kernel-level speedup

Isolated per-kernel CUDA-time speedup, cold L2. Each cell is `tuned (default)`, e.g. `1.80x (1.89x)` (the parenthetical number is vs the default baseline).

| bs | H100 fp32 | H100 fp16 | B300 fp32 | B300 fp16 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.73x (0.80x) | 0.58x (0.88x) | 0.41x (0.44x) | 0.44x (0.42x) |
| 8 | 1.36x (1.39x) | 1.09x (1.76x) | 1.02x (1.21x) | 0.83x (0.99x) |
| 32 | 1.69x (1.72x) | 1.40x (2.39x) | 1.20x (1.39x) | 1.00x (1.19x) |
| 128 | 1.78x (1.84x) | 1.56x (2.74x) | 1.46x (1.68x) | 1.22x (1.44x) |
| 256 | 1.81x (1.89x) | 1.57x (2.74x) | 1.53x (1.75x) | 1.26x (1.51x) |
| 512 | 1.80x (1.89x) | 1.62x (2.85x) | 1.56x (1.77x) | 1.30x (1.55x) |

The kernel speedup rises with batch and saturates around bs 128 to 256. The whole-model B300 numbers above run higher than a naive Amdahl estimate from these isolated numbers, for the power reason described next.

### Bandwidth and B300 power

Per-kernel DRAM utilization at bs512, as a percentage of peak. The decoupled kernel spends most steps on the non-flush (nf) branch and one step in `L` on the flush branch.

| cell | baseline | decoupled nf | decoupled flush |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 fp32 | 84.7% | 85.6% | 80.7% |
| H100 fp16 | 84.1% | 79.9% | 78.2% |
| B300 fp32 | 85.6% | 77.3% | 69.8% |
| B300 fp16 | 82.5% | 61.9% | 58.4% |

On B300, and especially at fp16, the kernel sits below the baseline ceiling because the flush reconstruction dot caps the flush-branch bandwidth. Splitting the decode kernel into two, one for the non-flush branch and one for the flush branch, raises bandwidth utilization substantially. Under CUDA graphs that split forces two launches per step, and the double-launch overhead hurts on Hopper but pays off on Blackwell. A Blackwell-specific split kernel is planned as a follow-up.

B300 also shows a power effect. The baseline draws more power than ReplaySSM and throttles its SM clock under the enforced cap, which costs bandwidth. In the full model this makes the fp32 baseline about 1.6x slower than in kernel-level isolation, while ReplaySSM keeps full clock. A higher power cap would likely close this gap.

### Buffer length

Isolated per-kernel speedup vs the tuned baseline. Each cell lists buffer length `L` = 8 / 16 / 32, with the best of the three in bold.

| model | bs 8 | bs 32 | bs 256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nano-4B (H100) fp32 | 1.34x / **1.37x** / 1.22x | 1.63x / **1.69x** / 1.50x | 1.74x / **1.80x** / 1.60x |
| Nano-4B (H100) fp16 | 1.04x / **1.09x** / 0.98x | 1.27x / **1.40x** / 1.22x | 1.43x / **1.56x** / 1.38x |
| Super-120B (B300) fp32 | 0.99x / **1.01x** / 0.97x | 1.16x / **1.20x** / 1.15x | 1.48x / **1.53x** / 1.49x |
| Super-120B (B300) fp16 | 0.83x / **0.84x** / 0.81x | 0.99x / **1.01x** / 0.95x | 1.21x / **1.26x** / 1.20x |

Speedup is bell-shaped in buffer length, trading flush frequency against per-step traffic. `L=16` is best in every entry and is the shipped default.

## Tests

Correctness is checked at three levels, all on Mamba2.

Per-step kernel correctness lives in `tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py`. Every decode step is checked against an exact fp32 reference and against the baseline decode kernel, over multi-flush sequences, across six state and activation precision combinations, the production model geometries, buffer lengths 1/4/16, the `z` gate, and continuous batching with per-row buffer positions and null-padded slots. The file also includes a tensor-parallel head-shard equivalence check, that one monolithic run equals concatenating the independent per-rank shards. Tolerances are near-exact at fp32 (rtol 1e-4, atol 1e-3), tight enough to catch a TF32 matmul-precision regression, and looser at bf16 and fp16 where rounding dominates.

Prefill and decode equivalence lives in `tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_prefill_decode_equivalence_mamba2.py`. Because the SSM recurrence is path-independent, the chunked prefill path and step-by-step decode must give the same per-position outputs and final state, and both are anchored on the exact recurrence.

Engine-level parity lives in `tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py`. It compares the baseline (feature off) against ReplaySSM (feature on) with greedy decode and `check_logprobs_close` on Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, at TP1 and, under `@multi_gpu_test`, at TP2.

```
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_prefill_decode_equivalence_mamba2.py \
       tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py -q
```

## Duplicate check

This PR is split from the large draft PR [#47576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47576), which stays open as the full design. Related prior PRs we are aware of:

- [#43102](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43102) and [#43439](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43439), earlier PRs from our collaborator on the same ReplaySSM effort. This is the newer, more complete version.
- [#46239](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46239), opened by another contributor based on our original fork. We have since made substantial changes, intend to land the feature ourselves, and have notified the author.

## Out of scope

- Stochastic rounding for fp16 state on Blackwell, which is the baseline's own fp16 precision option.
- The further precision benefit of ReplaySSM. Because the checkpoint is written back only on flushes, a low-precision checkpoint is quantized far less often than under the per-step baseline store. Quantifying this is still in progress.
- A two-kernel split of the decode kernel that raises Blackwell bandwidth utilization. It adds a second CUDA-graph launch per step, which pays off on Blackwell but not on Hopper, so it is planned as a Blackwell-specific follow-up.
- Speculative decode and GDN, which land in later sub-PRs.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Let pooling chunked prefill use full context
author: TommyTranX
body:
## Summary

- Fix a V1 scheduler liveness bug for pooling requests with chunked prefill.
- Pooling runners emit an output from the final prefill hidden state and do not append a sampled token, but the scheduler reserved one context slot for every non-diffusion request.
- When a pooling prompt length equaled `max_model_len`, the first chunk could run, the next running-step schedule would stop one token early, and the request could no longer make progress.
- Reserve zero sampled-token slots for pooling runners so the final prefill chunk can reach `max_model_len` and emit the pooling output.

Fixes #47971, Fixes #24704, Fixes #55427

## Duplicate-work check

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search 'repo:vllm-project/vllm 47971 in:body'` returned no open PRs.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search 'repo:vllm-project/vllm 24704 in:body'` returned no open PRs.
- A root-cause search for pooling + chunked prefill + max_model_len did not find an overlapping open scheduler fix.

## Tests

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_pooling_chunked_prefill_can_finish_at_max_model_len -q`
- [x] `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py`
- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_is_chunked_prefill_supported -q` was attempted locally, but this macOS environment failed unrelated teardown with `Allocator for mps is not a DeviceAllocator`, and one model-inspection case also lacked `compressed_tensors`.

## Model evals

Not run. This is a scheduler liveness fix for pooling request progress and does not change model outputs when the request already finishes.

## Assistance

OpenAI Codex assistance was used to investigate the scheduler liveness issue, implement the fix, and add the regression test. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines and test results.

title: [ROCm] Fused Shared Expert Support for AMD Quark DeepSeek-V4 Model Checkpoints
author: ColinZ22
body:
## Purpose

Enable serving AMD Quark DeepSeek-V4-MXFP4 checkpoints (AMD-Quark quantized, allowing MXFP4 shared expert fusion) in vLLM. The runtime layout implemented in this PR reuses the existing deepseek_v4_fp8 path.

## Changes

**`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/quant_config.py`**

- `DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method` now also claims `quant_method="quark"` for `model_type=deepseek_v4`, guarded by `_is_quark_mxfp4_ocp` so **only** MXFP4 exports are rerouted. Other Quark DSV4 checkpoints (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4) fall through to the generic `QuarkConfig` path untouched.
- `from_config` translates the nested Quark schema into the flat FP8 keys `Fp8Config.from_config` expects.

**`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`**

- Weights mapper handles the AMD `.weight_scale` to `.weight_scale_inv` naming for FP8 attention/linear scales (checkpoint uses `.weight_scale`; the block-FP8 param registers `.weight_scale_inv`). Expert/shared-expert `w{1,2,3}.weight_scale` are left untouched for the MXFP4 loader.
- MXFP4 shared-expert fusion: the shared expert is loaded as an appended routed-expert slot and runs through the same MXFP4 grouped GEMM as the routed experts. Required to run with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`.

Note: a related PR #47972 targets NVFP4 DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints via the **generic Quark path** (per-block FP8 in `QuarkConfig`, NVFP4 emulation). This PR targets MXFP4 checkpoints via the existing `deepseek_v4_fp8` reroute. An override guard is added so the two do not collide.

## Test plan

Launch (ROCm, gfx950, TP=4):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

Launch with MTP speculative decoding (adds `--speculative-config`; `num_speculative_tokens` <= `num_nextn_predict_lay
ers`):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "deepseek_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

GSM8K 8-shot (`lm_eval`, `num_concurrent=128`):

| Checkpoint | flexible-extract | strict-match |

title: [Bugfix] Use int8 workspace for FlashInfer MLA decode
author: njhill
body:
FlashInfer's CuteDSL MLA-decode tactic requires an int8 workspace_buffer, but vLLM allocated it as uint8. The trtllm-gen path (used for normal inference) views the buffer as uint8, so the mismatch is invisible until the FlashInfer autotuner enumerates the CuteDSL tactic. Model Runner V2's warmup autotunes trtllm_batch_decode_mla, so once V2 became the default runner for MoE models it hit `workspace_buffer must be torch.int8`, crashing every DeepSeek MLA test on Blackwell (#46646). Model Runner V1 never tunes that op, which is why it was unaffected.

int8 is accepted by every tactic (trtllm-gen still views it as uint8), so allocate both the dense and sparse FlashInfer MLA workspaces as int8. Add a regression test that drives the decode under the FlashInfer autotuner with vLLM's workspace buffer.

With help from Claude.

title: [DSv4] Remove sparse-MLA q-head padding for FlashInfer >=0.6.14
author: majunze2001
body:
## Purpose

Remove the query-head padding in the DeepSeek V4 FlashInfer sparse-MLA
attention layers. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3545 relaxes the
`trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` guard to accept `h_q ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}`
on **both** the SM100 and SM120 decode paths (previously only `{64, 128}`).

Before this, vLLM padded the per-rank head count up to the nearest kernel-supported
value — SM100 (`DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttention`) to `{64, 128}` and SM120
(`DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention`) to `{16, 32, 64, 128}` — which wasted compute
on high tensor-parallel sizes (e.g. on SM100 the padded head count for TP4/TP8/TP16
was always 64: 32→64, 16→64, 8→64). Both classes now delegate to a shared
`_pad_to_supported_q_heads` helper and use the native head count for the usual TP
sizes; only exotic sub-8 per-rank counts (TP > 16) are still rounded up to 8.

For DeepSeek V4 (128 attention heads), TP 1/2/4/8/16 → 128/64/32/16/8, all of which
now pass through unpadded.

## Dependency: pending #47669

This change is **runtime-gated on flashinfer ≥ 0.6.14** and should merge after
(or stacked on) #47669 ("Bump flashinfer version to 0.6.14"). The repo currently
pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.13`, whose kernel still enforces
`num_heads ∈ {64, 128}`; merging this before the bump would regress SM100
TP4/TP8/TP16 with `ValueError: Expected 64 or 128 query heads`. This PR deliberately
does **not** touch the version pins — that is #47669's job.

- Version bump PR: #47669
- Upstream flashinfer change that unlocks the head counts: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3545 (first released in flashinfer 0.6.14)

## Not a duplicate

Per the contribution checks, no open PR modifies `get_padded_num_q_heads` or the
sparse-MLA head padding. #47669 only bumps the flashinfer version (for an unrelated
top-k sampler hang fix) and does not remove the padding. Other open DSv4 PRs cover
ROCm functional fixes, SM12x enablement, KV-cache dtype selection, and workspace
bounds — none touch this code path.

## Test Plan

- Lint/type: `pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`
  (ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy).
- Verify the kernel guard in the installed flashinfer 0.6.14 actually accepts the
  wider head-count set on both decode paths.
- Unit-level check of the new `_pad_to_supported_q_heads` mapping for realistic and
  edge-case head counts.

## Test Result

- `pre-commit` hooks (ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy-3.10) pass on the changed file.
- Against `flashinfer==0.6.14`, both validators in `flashinfer/mla/_core.py` accept
  `{8, 16, 32, 64, 128}`: the SM100 `seq_lens`/`cum_seq_lens_q` path and the SM120
  `swa_topk_lens`/`extra_sparse_indices` path (error message "for SM120 DSv4").
- `_pad_to_supported_q_heads` mapping:
  - TP1→128, TP2→64, TP4→32, TP8→16, TP16→8 (all unpadded).
  - `num_heads=4` → 8 (sub-8 still rounded up); `num_heads=256` → `ValueError`.


## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter has
reviewed every changed line and is responsible for defending the change and running
the hardware-dependent evaluation.

title: [BugFix][Mooncake] Use global data_parallel_index for the DP engine index
author: ivanium
body:
## Purpose

`get_mooncake_dp_engine_index` asserted `data_parallel_rank_local is not None` under external/hybrid DP LB. This crashes on headless wide-TP follower nodes: they go through `run_headless` → `MultiprocExecutor` directly, which never populates `data_parallel_rank_local`.

Preferring `data_parallel_rank_local` was also inconsistent: for a replica launched with `--data-parallel-rank N` (N > 0), head-node processes computed `rank_local = 0` while follower-node workers would compute the global index N, so TP ranks of the same replica disagreed on their DP index.

Fix: use `parallel_config.data_parallel_index` unconditionally. It is populated in every launch path (`ParallelConfig.__post_init__`, `run_engine_core`, Ray actor), is identical on head and follower nodes, and unlike `data_parallel_rank` is not reset to 0 for dense-model DP engines. That reduces the helper to a one-line accessor, so it is inlined at its two call sites (`MooncakeStoreWorker.__init__`, `get_zmq_rpc_path_lookup`) and removed; the lookup IPC path stays unique per node since co-located engines have distinct global indices.

## Duplicate check

No open PR touches this helper (searched `mooncake dp index`, `get_mooncake_dp_engine_index`, `mooncake wide TP`, `data_parallel_rank_local mooncake`; open Mooncake PRs #47317 / #41093 are unrelated).

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) via commit hooks.
- Wide-TP (multi-node TP, headless followers) × DP deployment with MooncakeStoreConnector, which crashed on the assert before this change.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py` (monkeypatch replaced by `data_parallel_index=0` on the fake parallel_config).

## Test Result

Wide-TP DP serving comes up and serves traffic; previously every follower node died at engine init with `AssertionError` in `get_mooncake_dp_engine_index`. No model-output/accuracy impact (side-channel identity only).

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change; the diff was reviewed and the deployment validated by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix eagle3 first-layer qkv_proj prefix for quantized drafts
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Purpose

The EAGLE3 first decoder layer overrides `self.self_attn.qkv_proj` but builds it with `prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "qkv_proj")`, yielding `…layers.0.qkv_proj` instead of the canonical `…layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj`. For a quantized draft, the quant config matches its `exclude_modules` against this prefix — the missing `.self_attn` segment lets the excluded attention get quantized, and the `2 * hidden_size` first-layer qkv weight then fails to load (shape assert in `load_qkv_weight`). This blocks serving any quantized (e.g. NVFP4) EAGLE3 draft. No-op for non-quantized drafts.

```python
-            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "qkv_proj"),
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "self_attn.qkv_proj"),
```

## Test Plan

Tested with MiniMax-M3 + [`Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3); GSM8K accuracy and speculative acceptance rates both unaffected by this change.

For quantized draft model like https://huggingface.co/Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA-NVFP4 verified that it is now loaded correctly according to the quantization config:
```

"quantization_config": {
...
},
"ignore": [
  "embed_tokens",
  "fc",
  "self_attn",
  "lm_head"
],
...
}


```

title: Optimize ppc64le vLLM runtime image size
author: puneetsharma21
body:
> **Note:** This PR is an improved and generalized evolution of [vllm-project/vllm#46017](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46017), introducing dynamic PyTorch companion version derivation, repository-safe dependency resolution, and multi-version vLLM support alongside the container footprint optimizations.

### Summary
Optimize the vLLM Docker build and runtime container image for Power (`ppc64le`) architecture by:
1. Dynamically deriving compatible companion package versions (`torchvision`, `torchaudio`, and `openssl-devel`) to future-proof builds across multiple vLLM and PyTorch releases.
2. Cleaning up build-time dependencies, Python caches, and unneeded build tools to significantly reduce the final container image footprint.
3. Aligning multi-stage Docker builds to eliminate duplicate package installations and redundant layer executions.

---

### Changes

#### 1. Dynamic Dependency & Version Resolution (`docker/build_vllm_ppc64le.sh`)
- **Automated PyTorch Companion Derivation:** Replaced static version matrices with arithmetic derivation for `torchvision` (`0.(minor+15).patch`) and decoupled `torchaudio` (`2.(minor-2).patch` for $\ge$2.13), enabling out-of-the-box support for past, current, and future PyTorch/vLLM releases without manual script modification.
- **Repository-Safe OpenSSL Resolution:** Dynamically inspects the installed `openssl-libs` version via `rpm -q` to install the exact matching `openssl-devel` package, preventing build breaks during upstream UBI repository sync windows.
- **Robust Source Fallback:** Preserves DevPI pre-built wheel priority while cleanly falling back to source compilation for `torch`, `torchvision`, `torchaudio`, and `xgrammar` when wheel mirrors are unavailable.

#### 2. Image Optimization & Footprint Reduction (`docker/Dockerfile.ppc64le`)
- **Build Artifact & Tooling Cleanup:** Uninstalls build-only tools (`cmake`, `meson-python`, `maturin`, `scikit-build-core`, `nanobind`, `cython`, etc.) from the virtual environment before final stage hand-off.
- **Cache & Test Suite Pruning:** Strips `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`, `*.pyo`, static archives (`libxgrammar.a`), and packaged unit test directories (`/site-packages/*/tests`) from `/opt/vllm`.
- **Deduplication:** Removed redundant runtime package installations (`util-linux`, duplicate `ARG PYTHON_VERSION`) and cleaned up Dockerfile line continuations.

---

### Benefits
- **Future-Proof Builds:** Eliminates maintenance overhead of updating static version mappings when bumping PyTorch versions.
- **Reduced Image Size:** Lowers total image size, decreasing storage and bandwidth requirements.
- **Faster Pull & Startup:** Speeds up container deployment times in Kubernetes/OpenShift environments.
- **No Runtime Impact:** Retains full inference functionality, CPU acceleration (Power10 SIMD/MMA), and standard entrypoints.

---

### Testing & Validation
- [x] **vLLM Compatibility Range:** Validated and tested end-to-end across vLLM versions from **0.25 to 0.31.0**.
- [x] **PyTorch Dependency Resolution:** Verified `docker/build_vllm_ppc64le.sh` accurately resolves matching `torchvision` and `torchaudio` companion versions for PyTorch 2.10, 2.11, 2.13, and newer releases.
- [x] **Package Dependency Resolution:** Verified `microdnf` cleanly resolves system dependencies across UBI 9 base images without package conflict.
- [x] **Build & Runtime:** Built image on `ppc64le` environment (`podman build -f docker/Dockerfile.ppc64le .`), confirmed the container starts cleanly with `vllm serve`, and validated model loading and inference.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offloading] Fix stale transfer_jobs after reset_cache + harden job completion
author: Alex-ai-future
body:
## Purpose

Fix a bug in `reset_cache()` where `transfer_jobs` for active (unfinished) requests was not cleared.

### Bug

`reset_cache()` discards in-flight jobs (`_jobs.clear()`) and sets `_stale_job_threshold` to filter stale worker completions. However, it did not clear `transfer_jobs` for surviving requests. Since stale job_ids are filtered by `_stale_job_threshold` and never reach the completion handler, they can never be removed from `transfer_jobs` through the normal completion path.

This causes permanent request deferral:

1. `transfer_jobs` retains stale job_ids
2. `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` checks `if req_status.transfer_jobs:` → returns `None`
3. Scheduler moves request to `step_skipped_waiting` every step
4. Request is permanently stuck — never scheduled, never completes

### Fix

Add `status.transfer_jobs.clear()` in `reset_cache()` for surviving (active) requests.

## Test Result

- pre-commit hooks pass
- All 87 existing tests in `test_scheduler.py` pass

Part of KV Offloading roadmap (#33689)

title: [Perf][Hybrid] Vectorize _copy_mamba_state_block to uint64 for temporal
author: fuscof-ibm
body:
## Purpose

PR [#40172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40172) introduced the [postprocess_mamba_fused_kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0d12618e98ff2d21d36081e0e9b4eb23573b6d38/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py#L133) in MRV1 to copy states in hybrid models when prefix caching is enabled in align mode (and under MTP). Every accepted draft step that crosses a block boundary triggers a full sweep of `(num_reqs × total_states)` state copies — for Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B that's 24 linear-attention layers × (conv + temporal) = 48 state copies per accepted step, ~2 MiB temporal + ~80 KiB conv per block. Temporal states are 20–30× the size of conv states and dominate the copy size.

A later PR [#42406](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42406) refactored the kernel to reuse the copy mechanism, now delegated to the [_copy_mamba_state_block](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0d12618e98ff2d21d36081e0e9b4eb23573b6d38/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py#L27) to support align mode prefix caching in MRv2.

The current copy body issues **1-byte loads and stores** and it is not capable of exploiting the hardware leaving most HBM bandwidth on the floor: the kernel tops out at ~62 % of HBM3 peak on H100 and ~33 % of HBM3e peak on GB200.

This PR switches the temporal-state copy to **`uint64` loads/stores** (8× wider transactions per instruction). 
bf16/fp16/fp32 temporal states with contiguous inner dims are 8-byte aligned, therefore we can issue `uint64` loads/store. To make every issued address safe by construction, `MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext` now asserts at setup that the temporal-state base pointer and per-block stride are both 8-byte aligned; so the assert is a cheap guardrail rather than a fallback path. The conv path is untouched.

Net effect: the kernel becomes HBM-bandwidth-bound — ~82–84 % of peak on H100 from `reqs≥16` and up to ~74 % on GB200 from `reqs≥32`. For smaller number of requests (`reqs=1–8`) is up to ~5.9–6.5× on both H100 and GB200.

End-to-end on GB200 with MTP this shows up as **+0.75 % / +2.97 % / +1.48 %** output throughput and correspondingly lower median and P99 TPOT at concurrencies 32 / 64 / 128, with MTP acceptance unchanged.

## Test Plan

### Microbenchmark

Developed a microbenchmark harness [bench_copy_mamba_state_block.py](https://github.com/fuscof-ibm/vllm/blob/postprocess_benchmark/bench_copy_mamba_state_block.py),
which isolates `_copy_mamba_state_block` behind a minimal Triton wrapper launched at
the production grid (num_reqs, 48) using Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B's real state layout
(24 linear layers × conv+temporal, tp=1, num_spec=2),
with each request assigned distinct src/dst block ids so L2 can't mask DRAM traffic.

Each request corresponds to 49.88 MiB of copies: 24 temporal (float32) and 24 SD conv (bfloat16).

We sweep the num_req to `{1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128}` using two GPU architectures:

- H100 (HBM3, ~3.35 TB/s peak)
- GB200 (HBM3e, ~8 TB/s peak)

### End-to-end serving

`vllm bench serve` against `vllm serve` with MTP and prefix caching enabled (which exercises the state copies):

```bash
vllm serve \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \
    -tp 1 -pp 1 -dp 1 \
    --language-model-only \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_next_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \
    --enable-prefix-caching
```

Benchmark workload:

```
    vllm bench serve \
        --dataset-name random \
        --seed 42 \
        --temperature 0 \
        --random-input-len "$INPUT_LEN" \
        --random-output-len "$OUTPUT_LEN" \
        --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" \
        --request-rate inf \
        --max-concurrency "$conc" \
        --ignore-eos \
        --percentile-metrics "ttft,tpot,itl,e2el" \
        --metric-percentiles "50,90,99"
```

Workload: `--dataset-name random`, `INPUT_LEN=500`, `OUTPUT_LEN=5330`, `NUM_PROMPTS=500`.

The workload is chosen to exercise the `_copy_mamba_state_block` which happens when a block is crossed.
For Qwen3.5-9B the block size is 533. The output length is chosen to be 10x the block size.

Hardware: NVIDIA GB200. Concurrency sweep `{32, 64, 128}`. At each concurrency we ran the benchmark **4 times per branch and discarded the 1st run** to strip warmup/JIT effects; reported numbers aggregate the remaining 3 runs, with std devs computed as sample std dev (n−1).

Branches compared:

- `main` — [`4e5ca89c`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/4e5ca89cfe98121642d76b40e32a006f4d0fbf3b)
- `postprocess_vectorize` — [`9256ed051`](https://github.com/fuscof-ibm/vllm/commit/9256ed051e0034ca261718cdf8e0663711f9d7d2)

## Test Result

Microbenchmarks raw results 

[microbenchmark_h100.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29842159/microbenchmark_h100.md)
[microbenchmark_gb200.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29842160/microbenchmark_gb200.md)

E2E raw results:

[final_results_gb200_128.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29842174/final_results_gb200_128.txt)
[final_results_gb200_32.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29842175/final_results_gb200_32.txt)
[final_results_gb200_64.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29842177/final_results_gb200_64.txt)


### Microbenchmark — kernel throughput

**H100 (HBM3, ~3.35 TB/s peak):**

| reqs | MAIN (GB/s) | PR (GB/s) | Gain | MAIN % peak | PR % peak |
|-----:|------------:|----------:|-----:|------------:|----------:|
| 1    | 108.6       | 641.0     | **5.90×** | 3.2%   | 19.1% |
| 4    | 388.9       | 1846.5    | **4.75×** | 11.6%  | 55.1% |
| 8    | 712.3       | 2472.6    | **3.47×** | 21.3%  | 73.8% |
| 16   | 1260.7      | 2799.2    | **2.22×** | 37.6%  | **83.6%** |

| 128  | 2086.3      | 2822.9    | **1.35×** | 62.3%  | **84.3%** |

PR saturates HBM from `reqs≥16` (~82–84% of peak). MAIN caps at 62% of peak.

**GB200 (HBM3e, ~8 TB/s peak):**

| reqs | MAIN (GB/s) | PR (GB/s) | Gain | MAIN % peak | PR % peak |
|-----:|------------:|----------:|-----:|------------:|----------:|
| 1    | 73.8        | 479.4     | **6.50×** | 0.9%   | 6.0%  |
| 4    | 280.1       | 1640.6    | **5.86×** | 3.5%   | 20.5% |
| 8    | 547.9       | 3050.0    | **5.57×** | 6.8%   | 38.1% |
| 16   | 1019.2      | 4737.9    | **4.65×** | 12.7%  | 59.2% |
| 32   | 1730.0      | 5900.6    | **3.41×** | 21.6%  | **73.8%** |
| 64   | 2065.9      | 5165.9    | **2.50×** | 25.8%  | 64.6% |
| 128  | 2606.3      | 5788.0    | **2.22×** | 32.6%  | 72.4% |

PR reaches ~74% of peak at `reqs=32`. MAIN caps at 33% of peak.

### Microbenchmark — kernel latency

**H100 (avg kernel latency, µs):**

| reqs | MAIN | PR | Speedup | Absolute saving |
|-----:|-----:|---:|--------:|----------------:|
| 1    | 963.25  | 163.18  | **5.90×** | −800.1 µs |
| 4    | 1075.78 | 226.58  | **4.75×** | −849.2 µs |
| 8    | 1174.75 | 338.41  | **3.47×** | −836.3 µs |
| 16   | 1327.50 | 597.85  | **2.22×** | −729.7 µs |
| 32   | 1760.57 | 1221.86 | **1.44×** | −538.7 µs |
| 64   | 3613.88 | 2390.06 | **1.51×** | −1223.8 µs |
| 128  | 6417.25 | 4742.66 | **1.35×** | −1674.6 µs |

A near-constant ~800 µs saving at low `reqs` (fixed overhead removed), growing to ~1.7 ms at `reqs=128` as the workload becomes bandwidth-heavy.

**GB200 (avg kernel latency, µs):**

| reqs | MAIN | PR | Speedup | Absolute saving |
|-----:|-----:|---:|--------:|----------------:|
| 1    | 1417.62 | 218.20  | **6.50×** | −1199.4 µs |
| 4    | 1493.72 | 255.02  | **5.86×** | −1238.7 µs |
| 8    | 1527.27 | 274.35  | **5.57×** | −1252.9 µs |
| 16   | 1642.00 | 353.22  | **4.65×** | −1288.8 µs |

| 64   | 3240.21 | 1295.81 | **2.50×** | −1944.4 µs |
| 128  | 5136.81 | 2313.11 | **2.22×** | −2823.7 µs |

Absolute saving grows monotonically with `reqs` (1.20 → 2.82 ms).

**Cross-platform takeaways:**

- Low-`reqs` (`reqs=1–8`)  uplift is **~5.9–6.5× on both GPUs** : sub-350 µs on PR vs 0.96–1.53 ms on MAIN.
- PR saturates H100 HBM at `reqs≥16` (~84% peak); on GB200 it reaches ~74% at `reqs=32`.


### End-to-end serving (GB200)

Steady-state:

| Metric | Branch | conc=32 | conc=64 | conc=128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output tok/s | main | 7278.1 ± 15.0 | 11350.0 ± 32.2 | 15127.7 ± 111.6 |
| Output tok/s | PR   | 7333.1 ± 15.4 | 11686.7 ± 14.3 | 15351.5 ± 44.1 |

| Median TPOT (ms) | main | 4.267 ± 0.012 | 5.453 ± 0.032 | 8.100 ± 0.079 |
| Median TPOT (ms) | PR   | 4.230 ± 0.000 | 5.233 ± 0.035 | 7.993 ± 0.035 |
| Δ median TPOT    |      | **−0.87 %** | **−4.03 %** | **−1.32 %** |
| Median ITL (ms)  | main | 11.687 ± 0.006 | 14.810 ± 0.079 | 22.900 ± 0.062 |
| Median ITL (ms)  | PR   | 11.580 ± 0.017 | 14.467 ± 0.021 | 22.683 ± 0.049 |
| Δ median ITL     |      | **−0.92 %** | **−2.32 %** | **−0.95 %** |
| Acceptance rate (%) | main | 98.63 ± 0.05 | 98.26 ± 0.35 | 98.46 ± 0.31 |
| Acceptance rate (%) | PR   | 98.66 ± 0.08 | 98.59 ± 0.10 | 98.68 ± 0.06 |

P99 tails:

| P99 metric | Branch | conc=32 | conc=64 | conc=128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TPOT (ms) | main | 4.98 ± 0.03 | 6.70 ± 0.08 | 9.59 ± 0.17 |
| TPOT (ms) | PR   | 4.94 ± 0.07 | 6.45 ± 0.11 | 9.40 ± 0.05 |
| Δ P99 TPOT |     | **−0.80 %** | **−3.73 %** | **−1.98 %** |
| ITL (ms)  | main | 77.15 ± 0.16 | 80.57 ± 0.17 | 88.10 ± 1.23 |
| ITL (ms)  | PR   | 76.97 ± 0.21 | 79.53 ± 0.52 | 87.75 ± 0.77 |
| Δ P99 ITL  |     | **−0.23 %** | **−1.29 %** | **−0.40 %** |
<!--
| E2EL (ms) | main | 26728 ± 227 | 35903 ± 400 | 51639 ± 844 |
| E2EL (ms) | PR   | 26436 ± 328 | 34561 ± 640 | 50599 ± 197 |
| TTFT (ms) | main | 434 ± 16 | 956 ± 391 | 1721 ± 518 |
| TTFT (ms) | PR   | 847 ± 754 | 1046 ± 553 | 1432 ± 23 |
-->

**Analysis.**

- Throughput and per-token latency improve at every concurrency, with deltas well outside 1σ:
    - `conc=32`: +0.75 % throughput, ~0.9 % lower median TPOT
    - `conc=64`: +2.97 % throughput, ~4.0 % lower median TPOT
    - `conc=128`: +1.48 % throughput, ~1.3 % lower median TPOT
- Gains peak at `conc=64`. At `conc=32` the step is still GPU-idle-bound so a faster kernel moves the wall clock only slightly; at `conc=128` the GPU is closer to saturation so the copy is a smaller share of the step. Mid-concurrency is where this kernel is on the critical path.
- **Speculative decoding is unaffected.** Acceptance rates and per-position acceptance are indistinguishable between branches (all ~98.5–98.7 %). The speedup is pure kernel time, not a change in draft/verify behavior.

<!--
- P99 TPOT / E2EL tails improve proportionally to the medians (−0.8 % / −3.7 % / −2.0 % for P99 TPOT at conc 32 / 64 / 128; −1.1 % / −3.7 % / −2.0 % for P99 E2EL). At `conc=64` and `conc=128` the P99 improvements exceed 1σ.
- P99 ITL barely moves. These spikes (77–88 ms) are dominated by rare CUDA-graph / eviction events rather than this copy, so vectorization has no purchase on them — as expected.
- P99 TTFT is inconclusive: TTFT is prefill-dominated and shouldn't be affected by this change in either direction. Run-to-run variance on both branches is large (σ from ~15 to ~750 ms); the apparent regression at `conc=32` on the PR branch (847 ± 754 ms vs 434 ± 16 ms) is driven by a single outlier run and is not signal.
-->

### Summary

`_copy_mamba_state_block` goes from ~33 % to ~73% of HBM peak in GB200 and from ~62% to ~85% of HBM peak in the H100. On both H100 and GB200 there for the low request range there is a substantial speedup in kernel latency:   **~5.9–6.5× speedup** for `reqs=1` and **~3.5x - 5.6x** for `reqs=8` for H100 and GB200 respectively.

End-to-end on GB200 with MTP speculative decoding this shows up as **+0.75 % / +2.97 % / +1.48 %** output throughput and correspondingly lower median and P99 TPOT at concurrencies 32 / 64 / 128. 

MTP acceptance is unaffected as expected.


PR [#40172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40172) introduced the kernel and PR [#42406](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42406) refactored dispatch; this PR is the first change to widen the temporal load/store transactions.

title: [KV Offloading] Per-request tier filtering with TierFilter/TierMatcher
author: ronensc
body:
## Purpose

Adds per-request tier filtering to KV cache offloading.
Requests can specify which secondary tiers to load from via `kv_transfer_params["kv_load_tiers"]`, filtering by medium and locality.

See detailed design discussion: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48123#issuecomment-4979058299


Key changes:
- `Medium` enum: `CPU`/`STORAGE` (coarse granularity, both FS and OBJ → STORAGE)
- `TierMatcher(NamedTuple)` with optional `medium` and `locality` fields
- `TierFilter` with `allows()` — applied to secondary tiers only (primary always participates)
- `_parse_tier_filter()` validates request params with warning logging
- `MEDIUM_STORAGE` wire constant in `kv_events.py` (replaces `MEDIUM_FS`/`MEDIUM_OBJ`)
- `Locality` enum on `SecondaryTierManager` base class

Design decisions (confirmed by reviewers):
- Filter gates secondary tiers only; primary always participates (it's the promotion target)
- `None` on tier side = "unconstrained" (passes any filter) — supports P2P tiers with dynamic locality
- `None` on matcher side = "match anything"


## Test Plan
```
pytest -v tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ \
          tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
          tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py \
          tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result
```
437 passed, 17 warnings in 183.26s (0:03:03) 
```
