title: [Build] Fix DeepEP CUDA driver stub linking
author: khluu
body:
## Summary

- discover the CUDA toolkit's `libcuda.so` driver stub before building DeepEP
- prepend its architecture-specific directory to `LIBRARY_PATH`
- fail early with a clear message if the toolkit stub is missing

## Root cause

#45321 updated the pinned DeepEP revision to `d4f41e4e93`. That DeepEP revision adds `-lcuda` when linking its extension, but the manylinux wheel builders do not contain a real NVIDIA driver library in their normal linker search path.

The first observed failure was earlier in compilation because the manylinux headers did not define `SYS_pidfd_open` and `SYS_pidfd_getfd`. #49814 supplied those definitions and allowed all DeepEP sources to compile, but it did not change the final linker search path. The build then advanced to the final link and failed with `ld: cannot find -lcuda`.

This change links against the CUDA toolkit's driver stub during wheel construction. The stub is used only at link time; the built extension resolves the real NVIDIA driver library at runtime.

## Duplicate-work check

I searched open vLLM PRs for `49814`, `DeepEP libcuda wheel`, and `DeepEP CUDA stub`, and open issues for `DeepEP libcuda wheel`. No open PR or issue addresses this release-wheel linker failure. The nearest search results concern unrelated DeepSeek model support.

## Validation

- `bash -n tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh`
- `shellcheck tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh`
- synthetic symlinked `CUDA_HOME` fixture covering architecture-specific `targets/*/lib/stubs/libcuda.so` discovery
- repository commit hooks, including shell lint, Docker dependency graph validation, and DCO sign-off
- [`release-v2` build #4388](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/4388), commit `1fca23e6bdf531c8ea71d95e6bd90f841990ae84`:
  - [CUDA 13 x86_64 wheel](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/4388#019fa7ad-53f3-4a62-b796-46cb28c019cc): passed, exit 0; built the DeepEP wheel and full vLLM wheel
  - [CUDA 13 aarch64 wheel](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/4388#019fa7ad-53f1-47b7-b9d2-96ff7c358d1b): passed, exit 0; built the DeepEP wheel and full vLLM wheel

Model evaluation is not applicable because this changes only the build-time linker search path and does not change model output or serving behavior.

title: [Kernel][CI] `--jit-monitor-mode error` e2e tests for kernel warmup infra
author: NickLucche
body:
This PR actions this comment https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47456#issuecomment-5068299757 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47456) as part of the broader effort of getting JITs under control with a proper warmup framework.

It does 3 things:
 - centralizes existing jit tests into a separate directory
 - separates tests into a new buildkite job for better parallelization as well as tracking in PRs
 - adds an e2e test for specific models which runs with `--jit-monitor-mode error`

In particular the latter purposely **only loads a subset of dummy layers** of the whole model, to keep test fast and footprint minimal.
All we aim to test here is that the paths the various blocks repeateadly call in the forwad are correctly precompiled, so we don't need to execute all blocks, but rather make sure different kernel groups are present (FA/MoE..).

title: [chore] clean-up weight prepack for INT8 MoE
author: fadara01
body:
## Purpose

This aims to simplify / fix the weight prepack path for INT8 MoE.

Currently, weight prepack is owned by the MoE Backend (not by the MoE kernel), this is problematic because:
- in CPU, we have a single MoE backend, but multiple kernels (for AArch64, x86). As a result, choosing the correct packing function requires: (1) selecting CPU packing function for the CPU MoE backend (2) inside the CPU packing function, you need to select the ISA specific packing function. This will keep getting more convoluted as new backends and kernels are added.
- the current flow does not match the `FusedMoEExperts` API, which exposes a `process_weights_after_loading` to abstract away the complexity in the first point.

This PR makes the MoE kernel own weight prepack utilising `process_weights_after_loading`, in line with other quantized MoE code paths like `CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod`

This should not change behaviour for GPU backends like triton or humming because they don't implement a prepacking method.

title: [CPU] Migrate unquantized MoE to the modular-kernel experts structure
author: bigPYJ1151
body:
## Purpose

The unquantized (BF16/FP16/FP32) CPU MoE was the last unquantized backend still on the
legacy monolithic path. `oracle/unquantized.py` short-circuited before backend selection
with `# TODO: migrate to MK structure`, and `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` carried three CPU
escape hatches (`is_monolithic`, a bespoke `process_weights_after_loading` branch, and a
bespoke `apply_monolithic` branch) to keep it alive. Every *quantized* CPU MoE path had
already moved to `experts/cpu_moe.py` as `FusedMoEExpertsMonolithic` subclasses.

Inside `CPUFusedMOE`, three unrelated implementations were entangled behind a
`self.forward_method` attribute and a single `check_grouped_gemm` if-ladder. A fourth,
`SGLFusedMOE`, sat behind `VLLM_CPU_SGL_KERNEL`, handled SILU only, and is superseded by
the grouped-gemm kernels.

This PR replaces all of that with three decoupled `FusedMoEExpertsMonolithic` subclasses
in `experts/cpu_moe.py`, selected by the oracle like every other backend:

| Class | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `X86CPUUnquantizedExperts` | AMX / vector grouped gemm — the **only** x86 implementation |
| `ArmCPUUnquantizedExperts` | NEON grouped gemm |
| `TorchCPUUnquantizedExperts` | per-expert torch/oneDNN loop, non-x86 only |

Behaviour changes worth reviewer attention:

- **x86 always uses grouped gemm.** The torch loop is no longer reachable there. One shape
  genuinely cannot use it — `swigluoai`'s interleaved gate/up layout with a per-partition
  intermediate size that is not a multiple of 32, which zero-padding cannot fix — and that
  now raises with a message suggesting a different `--tensor-parallel-size`. Previously
  this raised on AMX hosts but silently fell back to the much slower torch loop on
  non-AMX x86.
- **FP16/FP32 on AMX-capable hosts is fixed.** `check_grouped_gemm` used to *raise* for
  non-BF16 dtypes whenever AMX was present; it now selects the vector kernel, which
  already handled those dtypes on non-AMX x86.
- **`SGLFusedMOE` and the `VLLM_CPU_SGL_KERNEL` MoE gate are removed.** The env var still
  applies to linear layers (`layers/utils.py`, `kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cpu.py`) and is
  unchanged there; the doc entry is reworded accordingly.

Routing behaviour is deliberately **unchanged**. The monolithic `apply()` signature cannot
carry `custom_routing_function` / `scoring_func` / `renormalize`, so the experts capture
them off the layer in `process_weights_after_loading` and call the same `select_experts()`
as before. Without this, grouped-topk (DeepSeek), sigmoid scoring, and custom-routing
models (gemma4, phimoe, cohere2, llama4, interns1_pro, transformers/moe) would have
regressed on CPU.

`grouped_topk` / `select_experts` move next to their callers and
`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/cpu_fused_moe.py` is deleted.

### Not duplicating an existing PR

No open PR migrates the unquantized CPU MoE to the modular-kernel experts structure. The
`#37753` oracle-refactor PRs (#44231, #44562, #37776, #46901) migrate the oracle ABC and
other quant schemes, not this backend. Textual overlap that will need a rebase by whoever
lands second:

- #43653 adds SWIGLUSTEP/RELU2 activations to the deleted `cpu_fused_moe.py`; the feature
  would move into `_CPU_MOE_ACT_FN` in `experts/cpu_moe.py`.
- #45480 patches the same deleted file.
- #48430 adds a regression test to `tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py` and would
  need its import repointed at `experts.cpu_moe`.
- #47778 (CPU MoE DP/EP) and #50116 (INT8 prepack cleanup) touch `experts/cpu_moe.py` but
  not the unquantized path.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -x -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py
pytest -x -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Output-identity checks against `main`, greedy decoding, identical prompts:

- `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, TP=4 via `vllm serve` + `curl` — exercises the padding path
  (`moe_intermediate_size=704`, `704 // 4 == 176` → padded to 192) *and* a
  `custom_routing_function`, i.e. the two things most likely to regress.

Serving benchmark per `docs`/CPU practice:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct --dtype=bfloat16 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 4096 --port 8000

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random --num-prompts=32 --random-input-len=1024 \
  --random-output-len=256 --request-rate=inf --num-warmups=32 \
  --temperature=0 --ignore-eos --port=8000
```

## Test Result

Unit tests (Intel x86, AMX-capable):

```

tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py . 152 passed

title: [Bugfix] Don't transpose fused MoE quantization scales in `RoutedExperts.load_weights`
author: hmellor
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a regression from #47058 that breaks loading of fused, per-channel-quantized
MoE checkpoints with TP > 1.

`RoutedExperts.load_weights` normalises the orientation of fused expert tensors so
that checkpoints storing them either way (e.g. Qwen3 VL MoE) load correctly. It
identified fused tensors by rank alone and then transposed by testing for the
*absence* of the hidden dim:

```python
is_fused = loaded_weight.dim() == 3
...
if fused_weight.shape[-1] != unpadded_hidden:   # w1/w3
    fused_weight = fused_weight.transpose(-1, -2)
```

Any 3D tensor with no hidden dim satisfies that condition, so auxiliary
quantization tensors were transposed too. For a fused per-channel scale
`[E, 2 * I, 1]`, the check sees `1 != hidden_size` and produces `[E, 1, 2 * I]`.
The subsequent `chunk(2, dim=1)` / `unbind()` / TP-shard chain then operates on
the wrong axis, and `loaded_weight.shape[shard_dim] // tp_size` collapses to `0`:

```
RuntimeError: output with shape [0, 1] doesn't match the broadcast shape [0, 2048]
```

Block scales `[E, 2 * I / block, H / block]` were mis-transposed by the same check.

## Fix

Extract the orientation logic into `RoutedExperts._orient_fused_weight` and only
transpose when the hidden dim is *definitively* on the wrong axis:

```python
if (
    fused_weight.shape[hidden_axis] != unpadded_hidden
    and fused_weight.shape[intermediate_axis] == unpadded_hidden
):
    return fused_weight.transpose(-1, -2)
return fused_weight
```

This is a strict narrowing of the previous condition, so transposed checkpoints
still normalise and standard checkpoints are still left alone; tensors with no
hidden dim now fall through untouched. Requiring both clauses (rather than just
`shape[intermediate_axis] == unpadded_hidden`) preserves the old behaviour when
both axes happen to equal `hidden_size`.

The scale now follows the expected path for a `[E=256, I=1024, H=3072]` model at
TP=4: `[256, 2048, 1]` -> chunk -> `[256, 1024, 1]` -> unbind -> `[1024, 1]` ->
shard -> `[256, 1]`, matching the `[256, 1]` destination slice.

### Known limitation

A checkpoint that is *both* transposed and block-quantized still cannot be
resolved, since neither axis of `[E, 2 * I / block, H / block]` matches
`hidden_size`. That is not decidable from shape alone and would need
quantization-config-driven layout metadata. No known checkpoint is affected, and
the previous code was strictly worse here (it transposed every block scale).

## Not a duplicate

Checked for existing work before opening:

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "RoutedExperts fused transpose scale"` — no results
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "per-channel scale moe load_weights"` — no results

## Test Plan

Added `TestOrientFusedWeight` to `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py`,
covering both orientations for w13 and w2, the `[E, 2 * I, 1]` per-channel scale
regression (including the resulting `chunk`), the w2 per-channel scale, and a
block scale. The per-channel cases fail on `main` and pass with this change.

## Test Result

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py -q
36 passed, 16 warnings in 4.53s
```

`pre-commit run` passes on the changed files, including `mypy-3.10`.

**Model evaluation is still outstanding.** This change affects weight loading, so
it needs an end-to-end load of an affected checkpoint (e.g. `Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-W8A8`
at TP=4) plus eval numbers. I will add those to this PR before it is merged.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). I have reviewed every
changed line and run the tests above.

title: [KV Connector] Fix NIXL mamba state pairing for multi-slot block tables
author: njhill
body:
The NIXL P/D transfer pairs SSM state blocks positionally and assumes a request's mamba group resolves to a single local state block. That only holds for the mamba_block_size = max_model_len default WITHOUT speculative decoding. With a speculative config, mamba managers co-allocate num_speculative_blocks trailing scratch slots on every request, and with mamba prefix caching the block list is additionally a multi-slot table: "align" mode holds null-block placeholders for slots whose state migrated forward, "all" mode holds a state per block position. Neither placeholders nor scratch slots hold transferable state, yet both participated in the pairing (the scheduler-side #46694 computed-tokens clip covers AttentionSpec groups only, so mamba lists always leave P raw):

- spec on both P and D: equal-length lists pair positionally, so P's stale scratch bytes are RDMA'd over D's zero-initialized scratch slots;
- spec on P only: the single-local-block rule reads the remote tail, loading D's state from P's last scratch slot instead of the state-bearing slot (silent state corruption);
- align mode: the generic head-clip could pair D's state-bearing block against a P-side placeholder, or the transfer tripped the single-local-block assertion.

Fix the pairing contract at both levels:

- Scheduler: at every block-id exchange point (pull/push, recv and send sides), strip the trailing speculative slots from SSM groups, and in single-state cache modes ("none"/"align") reduce the group to the running state slot — everything before it is a null placeholder or the previous step's superseded state, both of which could otherwise be paired against the real state. Exchanged lists are then 1:1 between P and D. "all" mode keeps its remaining slots, placeholders included, so they stay position-indexed.
- Worker: replace the single-local-block assertion in _apply_prefix_caching with alignment over the min count, which now only applies to "all" mode's multi-slot lists — a longer remote list carries earlier positions covered by a local prefix hit (read its tail), while a longer local list holds the position D recomputes itself, which receives no remote state. A larger local excess than that one position means the lists are not position-aligned, and asserts rather than transferring state into the wrong slots.

Claude was used for this.

title: [CI][NIXL] Fix flaky DP+EP test port conflict
author: divakar-amd
body:
This PR fixes flaky NIXL accuracy test timeout in DP+EP mode by setting `VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT` for the decode instance.

Without this PR, the DP_EP case for decode instance has tendency to fall into race-condition as the ports are not explicitly set for this case. They might end up inheriting the same fixed base port and might compete with the prefill instance's port range.

Fix: Set `VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT` instead of `VLLM_PORT` for DP mode. This reserves a port range for DP process group coordination. This allows each EngineCore to independently allocate other ports and isolates decode's DP ports from prefill's ports.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix NaN handling in rejection sampler tl.argmax
author: gabriel-peracio
body:
## Summary

`tl.argmax` on an all-NaN block returns an out-of-range block index (pointing into the padded region beyond `num_blocks - 1`). That index is used to load from the local-argmax tensor, producing an out-of-bounds read and an illegal memory access downstream in the rejection sampler.

Two kernels in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py` are affected:

- `_compute_global_target_argmax` — `tl.argmax(local_max)` at line 111, result used to index `target_local_argmax_ptr` at line 113.
- `_insert_resampled_kernel` — `tl.argmax(resampled_local_max)` at line 852, result used to index `resampled_local_argmax_ptr` at line 854.

When all values in the (padded) block dimension are NaN — reachable via NaN target logits — `tl.argmax` does not guarantee an in-range result. The loaded garbage index then propagates into subsequent gathers/stores, surfacing as an illegal memory access.

**Fix:** in both kernels, map NaN to `-inf` via `tl.where` before `tl.argmax`, and clamp the resulting block index to `num_blocks - 1` with `tl.minimum` as a defensive bound. Two small, surgical changes; no behavior change for non-NaN inputs.

## Symptom / reproduction

Observed as an illegal memory access during speculative-decoding warmup (DSpark) when serving Kimi-K3 on 8xB300 with TP=8. Confirmed the root cause with a standalone Triton repro on an RTX 4090:

```python
import torch, triton, triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def k(out_ptr, NUM_BLOCKS: tl.constexpr, PAD: tl.constexpr):
    blocks = tl.arange(0, PAD)
    vals = tl.full((PAD,), float("nan"), tl.float32)
    vals = tl.where(blocks < NUM_BLOCKS, vals, float("-inf"))
    idx = tl.argmax(vals, axis=0)
    tl.store(out_ptr, idx)

out = torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
k[(1,)](out, NUM_BLOCKS=4, PAD=8)
print(out.item())  # unpatched: 8 (out of range); with NaN->-inf + clamp: in [0, 3]
```

On the all-NaN input, unpatched `tl.argmax` returns `idx == num_blocks` (out of range); with the NaN→-inf mapping plus clamp the index stays in range.

## Validation

- Standalone Triton repro (RTX 4090): patched kernel returns an in-range index on all-NaN input; unpatched does not.
- Full vLLM server on 8xB300, TP=8, Kimi-K3 with DSpark speculative decoding: server boots through warmup (previously IMA), generates coherent output, acceptance length 2.5, conc=1 throughput 110–116 tok/s (+58% vs no-spec).

## Disclosure

- AI assistance (Kimi K3) was used in developing this fix. A human engineer (Gabriel Peracio, Parasail) reviewed every changed line and validated the fix on hardware as described above.
- Checked for duplicates before opening: no open PR or issue covers `tl.argmax`/NaN out-of-bounds in the rejection sampler (`rejection_sampler_utils.py`).

title: [ROCm][Perf] Extend QK-norm/RoPE/KV-cache fusion to MRoPE
author: vorapolsiloai
body:
## Summary

Extend the existing `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` to support Qwen3-VL 3D MRoPE. For eligible decode ranges, it replaces two Q/K RMSNorm launches, MRoPE, and the unified FP8 KV-cache update with one AITER attention-prologue kernel: **three fewer GPU launches per layer**.

This is a model-agnostic compile-pass integration: it removes the earlier Qwen3-specific flag/wrapper and uses the existing O2/O3 pass controls. Unsupported configurations stay on the unfused path.

![Before and after GPU trace: separate operations fused into one AITER kernel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vorapolsiloai/vllm/93e5d01e7e12610a3ae8371801aae2036342ff16/pr-assets/vllm-50212-before-after.png)

## Review guide

1. `matcher_utils.py` and `qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`: match 3D MRoPE and emit the fused replacement.
2. `_aiter_ops.py`, `attention/backend.py`, and `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py`: capability gate and backend-owned kernel dispatch/cache handling.
3. `rotary_embedding/mrope.py`: expose MRoPE as a matchable custom op on HIP only.
4. `attention.py`: keep scalar Quark query scales per-tensor unless per-head scaling is explicitly enabled. This fixes TP4/TP8 when one KV head is local to each rank.
5. `test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`: correctness, rejection, layout, version-gate, and TP regressions.

## Safety and compatibility

- Only ROCm AITER unified decoder attention opts in; other backends reject by default.
- CUDA/XPU MRoPE behavior is unchanged.
- Fusion is rejected for observable rotated K, unsupported dimensions/layouts, unsupported AITER builds, and ranges above the existing 256-token limit.
- Full/partial rotary, NeoX/GPT-J pairing, interleaved/non-interleaved MRoPE, and LBHNC/LBNHC/LHBNC cache layouts are covered.
- Opaque `LayerName` patterns are registered once on torch >= 2.11 to avoid duplicate wildcard patterns.

### AITER requirement

Requires a build containing the strided KV-cache fix from [AITER #4531](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4531) ([`b0cc5392`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/b0cc5392dd838a4bec46a5553e7fbeed60218ab5)); the first containing tag is [`v0.1.20.dev1`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/tree/v0.1.20.dev1). Builds known not to contain it (`v0.1.20.dev0`, `v0.1.20`, and `v0.1.20.post1`) cleanly fall back to the unfused path.

## Validation

- Full ROCm compile-pass sweep: **1,020 passed** with the AITER #4531 source.
- Final scalar-query-scale regression: **3/3 passed** for TP2 `(32, 2)`, TP4 `(16, 1)`, and TP8 `(8, 1)` local `(Q heads, KV heads)`.
- Real serving compilation fused all expected layers: **48** for Qwen3-VL-30B TP1 and **94 per rank** for Qwen3-VL-235B TP2/TP4.
- Steady-state Kineto traces confirm one fused call per eligible layer and a net reduction of three launches. Large-prefill ranges remain unfused as intended.
- Ruff, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Performance

MI355X (`gfx950`), 8,192 input / 1,024 output tokens, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, paired fusion OFF/ON runs:

| Model | TP | MC | Output tok/s OFF | Output tok/s ON | Throughput | Mean TPOT OFF -> ON | TPOT |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Qwen3-VL-30B FP8 | 1 | 4 | 538.78 | 623.68 | **+15.76%** | 7.16 -> 6.15 ms | **-14.22%** |
| Qwen3-VL-30B FP8 | 1 | 64 | 2,660.65 | 2,786.82 | **+4.74%** | 22.11 -> 21.06 ms | **-4.72%** |
| Qwen3-VL-30B FP8 | 1 | 256 | 3,556.08 | 3,580.08 | **+0.67%** | 64.58 -> 64.08 ms | **-0.78%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 2 | 4 | 274.39 | 304.65 | **+11.03%** | 13.42 -> 11.99 ms | **-10.66%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 2 | 64 | 1,344.76 | 1,366.77 | **+1.64%** | 43.51 -> 42.82 ms | **-1.59%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 2 | 256 | 1,981.63 | 1,992.43 | **+0.54%** | 113.88 -> 112.99 ms | **-0.78%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 4 | 4 | 306.59 | 341.66 | **+11.44%** | 11.93 -> 10.59 ms | **-11.25%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 4 | 64 | 1,888.43 | 1,985.68 | **+5.15%** | 30.58 -> 29.14 ms | **-4.74%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 4 | 256 | 3,087.00 | 3,132.56 | **+1.48%** | 72.50 -> 71.33 ms | **-1.61%** |

All nine measured point estimates improve. The small high-concurrency deltas require repeated runs before claiming statistical significance. TP8 has targeted correctness coverage but was not rerun end-to-end because the eighth GPU was unavailable.

title: [Bug-fix] Fix MoE fused sum row offsets
author: happyyzy
body:
Resolves https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47281

`moe_fused_mul_sum` indexes `inputs` by:

```python
inputs[offs_m, :, offs_k]
```

where the row stride is:

```text
stride_m = top_k * hidden_size
```

The old kernel kept `offs_m` as int32, so `offs_m * stride_m` can overflow before pointer arithmetic.

This only reproduces on the larger Qwen3.5 shape because the max row offset crosses int32:

```text
INT32_MAX = 2,147,483,647
```

DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP=4:

```text
inputs.shape = (32768, 6, 4096)
stride_m = 6 * 4096 = 24576
max row offset = 32767 * 24576 = 805,281,792
OK
```

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, DP=8:

```text
inputs.shape = (65536, 8, 2048)
stride_m = 8 * 2048 = 16384
max row offset = 65535 * 16384 = 1,073,725,440
OK
```

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, DP=8:

```text
inputs.shape = (65536, 10, 4096)
stride_m = 10 * 4096 = 40960
max row offset = 65535 * 40960 = 2,684,313,600
OVERFLOW
```

Overflow starts at row:

```text
ceil(2^31 / 40960) = 52429
```

So the 35B and DeepSeek-V4 shapes stay below int32 range, while the 397B shape overflows and can produce an invalid global-memory address. This patch casts `offs_m` to int64 before row-offset arithmetic.

title: [Perf][CUDA] Programmatic dependent launch for the DSA decode kernels
author: zhou9402
body:
## What this does

Chain the DSA decode kernels with programmatic dependent launch so back-to-back
small kernels overlap their launch latency:

- the fused norm/rope and fused-q Triton kernels get a `USE_PDL` constexpr with
  `gdc_wait()` / `gdc_launch_dependents()`, launched with `launch_pdl`
- the NVFP4 quant kernels switch to `cudaLaunchKernelEx` with programmatic stream
  serialization, guarded on `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900` and `sm_version >= 90`

Gated at runtime on `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`, so it is a no-op
where PDL is unavailable.

Touches the same region of `deepseek_v32/nvidia/kernels.py` as #49792 — whichever
merges second needs a rebase. Keep the `@torch.compiler.assume_constant_result`
decorator on `_is_arch_support_pdl` when resolving it: the shared decorator line
sits above the conflict marker, so a naive "take both sides" drops it.

Part of the #48597 re-split — see that PR for the tracker and merge order.

## Benchmark

8×B300 TP8, `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, MTP=5, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, fp8 KV
cache, 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, concurrency 1, 64 prompts.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve $MODEL --served-model-name glm-5.2 \
  -tp 8 --port 8300 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --kernel-config '{"ir_op_priority":{"rms_norm":["vllm_c","native"],"fused_add_rms_norm":["vllm_c","native"]},"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}'
```

| | output tok/s | total tok/s | median TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` (torch-compiled, verified: 16 Dynamo transforms) | 446.7 | 4019.8 | 1.94 ms |
| this PR alone | 459.2 | 4132.5 | 1.88 ms |
| full series | 542.5 | 4882.7 | 1.56 ms |

The `main` and per-PR rows are from the original session on one build. The
`full series` row was re-measured on 2026-07-30 with all six branches
cherry-picked onto `main` @ `48a077e4cf`, same node, dataset and server flags;
`main` was not re-run on that newer base, so the two are separate sessions
rather than one back-to-back delta.

> The prompts come from a low-entropy synthetic dataset, so MTP acceptance sits
> near the ceiling (~5.98 of 6 draft tokens accepted, >99%). Real traffic accepts
> far less, so these absolute throughput numbers are optimistic; the comparison
> between rows is still apples-to-apples since every row uses the same dataset and
> the same acceptance rate.

`lm_eval gsm8k` 5-shot on the full series: 0.9393 flexible / 0.9386 strict.
Re-measured 2026-07-30 with `tests/evals/gsm8k` (500 questions, 5-shot): 0.950,
no invalid responses; MTP acceptance length 5.97.
`pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py` → 100 passed
(241 passed on the 2026-07-30 re-run, which picks up the new GLM-5.2 cases).

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the split and the benchmarks; every changed line has been reviewed.

title: [PD][PushConnector] Record last activity of remotes to allow clean up of stale ones
author: NickLucche
body:
Part of the stability enhancement efforts described here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48633.

The PushConnector currently inherits all the logic from `base_worker.py` necessary to clean up old/stale remotes data structures here and prevent cpu leak (more info here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44424).
It is not tapping into that workflow though as the connector itself isn't recording time of last activity for each remote it receives a message from.

This PR allows the PushConnector to start tracking remote engine TTLs, thus enabling periodic clean up of stale ones.

title: [Hardware][AMD] Enable fused bf16→fp32 router GEMM on ROCm
author: mpashkovskii
body:
## Purpose

This pull request addresses issue #50267 by enabling fused bf16→fp32 GEMM operations on AMD ROCm hardware for MoE router gates.

## Problem Statement

The MoE router gate requires `out_dtype=torch.float32` for the `grouped_topk` operation. However, on ROCm, the fused fp32-output GEMM implementation was gated exclusively to CUDA platforms. This caused a fallback to bf16 GEMM followed by a separate cast operation, creating a standalone "bf16→fp32 copy kernel" visible in performance traces between the router GEMM and `grouped_topk` for every MoE layer on each decode step.

## Solution

The changes enable hipBLASLt's `out_dtype` epilogue support (analogous to CUDA's cuBLAS capability) by modifying `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/gate_linear.py`:

- Adds ROCm as an alternative condition for `allow_cublas_router_gemm` when: no bias exists, weights are bf16, and output is fp32
- Updates both `__init__` and `set_out_dtype` methods to ensure consistency
- The fused tier now executes on ROCm, folding the fp32 cast into the GEMM epilogue

## Impact Assessment

**CUDA:** No changes; the condition uses `current_platform.is_rocm()`, which evaluates false on CUDA.

**Correctness:** Verified on gfx942 hardware; results match fp32 reference within ~6e-5 tolerance.

**Scope:** Router gate only; expert GEMMs and other fp32 operations remain unaffected.

## Performance Results

Benchmarked on ROCm (gfx942) using the online serving benchmark: baseline vs. fused, 3 seeds each (123 / 456 / 789), max concurrency 4, 40 requests per run (40960 input + 40960 generated tokens). All runs completed 40/40 successful with 0 failures.

Averaged across the 3 seeds:

| Metric                    | Baseline | Fused (this PR) | Δ              |
|---------------------------|----------|-----------------|----------------|
| Benchmark duration (s)    | 343.18   | 337.69          | −5.5 s (−1.6%) |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 119.35   | 121.29          | +1.9 (+1.6%)   |
| Total throughput (tok/s)  | 238.71   | 242.59          | +3.9 (+1.6%)   |
| Mean TPOT (ms)            | 32.87    | 32.34           | −0.53 (−1.6%)  |
| Mean ITL (ms)             | 32.87    | 32.34           | −0.53 (−1.6%)  |
| Mean TTFT (ms)            | 689.65   | 688.97          | ≈flat (−0.1%)  |

**Interpretation:** Folding the fp32 cast into the router GEMM epilogue removes a per-MoE-layer, per-decode-step conversion kernel from the critical path. The decode-path metrics (TPOT, ITL, output throughput) all improve by a consistent ~1.6%, while TTFT is unchanged as expected since prefill is not dominated by that per-step kernel. Variance across seeds is small (throughput within ±0.2 tok/s, TPOT within ±0.07 ms), so the improvement is stable and above noise, if modest.

## Testing Plan

- Confirm the standalone `bfloat16tofloat32_copy_kernel` is absent from ROCm traces
- Validate router logits match previous behavior within tolerance
- Unit tests added for the modification
speedup_claims: TPOT, ITL, output throughput) all improve by a consistent ~1.6%

speedup_evidence.claim: TPOT, ITL, output throughput) all improve by a consistent ~1.6%

title: [Bugfix] Fix speculative decoding for short_conv (LFM2) models
author: zwischenraum
body:
## Purpose

Supersedes #44296 (rebased onto main with the original commit and authorship preserved — thanks @Tonoken3); that PR has had failing pre-commit since opening and merge conflicts since July 6 with no author activity, so this revives it to make the merge cheap.

Speculative decoding (ngram, EAGLE-3, any method) on `short_conv` (LFM2 / LFM2.5) targets silently corrupts output at the first rejected token: attention KV rolls back, but the conv sliding window retains rejected-token activations. `mamba2` / GDN already handle this via the spec-aware `causal_conv1d_update` path; `short_conv` was never wired in:

1. `MambaStateShapeCalculator.short_conv_state_shape` sizes the conv state `conv_kernel - 1` (no `num_spec`), so there is no room to roll the window back (mirror: `mamba2_state_shape` adds `num_spec`).
2. `GPUModelRunner._build_attn_group_metadata` never injects `num_accepted_tokens` for `ShortConvAttentionMetadataBuilder`, so the layer never sees the accepted-token counts.

Changes vs #44296: rebased onto current main, fixed the mypy failure that blocked its pre-commit (`assert state_indices_tensor_d is not None`), added a regression test for the spec-widened conv state shape.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

#44296 is this fix (red CI + conflicts + stale for 8 weeks; original commit and authorship preserved here). #50146 bundles a rebase of the same target-side fix with 6 further drafter-side changes across 9 files and depends on other open PRs; this PR is the minimal, independently mergeable target-side correctness fix for released models.

## Test plan

- `pre-commit run` (incl. mypy-3.10): pass.
- New `tests/kernels/mamba/test_short_conv_state_shape.py`: pass.
- E2E (we are the model vendor — Liquid AI serving team; LFM2.5-230M fine-tune + trained EAGLE-3 drafter with ~0.9/step acceptance, ROCm MI325X, v0.26.0 + this patch): without the fix, low-concurrency spec decode diverges after the first rejection (doubled/fused tokens, occasionally flipped outputs; under default cudagraphs it degrades to garbage from ~token 2). With it, `--enforce-eager`, `PIECEWISE`, and default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` all produce identical, correct output on fixed-seed content probes.

AI assistance was used to rebase, fix, and validate this change; I reviewed every changed line and am accountable for it.

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Don't stop an encoder-instance request before its images are encoded
author: gty111
body:
## Problem

On an EPD encoder instance a request can be marked finished **before its
multi-modal items are encoded**.

Under sync scheduling this is silent: no embedding reaches the EC connector, the
decode instance re-encodes locally, and the client still gets a successful
completion.

**Under async scheduling it kills the engine.** The fabricated token decrements
`num_output_placeholders` for a request that never had a placeholder, so
`AsyncScheduler._update_request_with_output` trips
`assert request.num_output_placeholders >= 0` and `EngineCore` dies with
`EngineDeadError`. (Same counter as #48245, reached by a different path — that
fix covered the preemption rollback, not this one.)

## Root cause

The encoder instance signals "this request is done here" with a fabricated
token, and relies on the proxy's `max_tokens: 1` to turn it into a stop:

```python
sampled_token_ids: list[list[int]] = [[0] for _ in req_ids]
```

`[0]` is a legal token, not an empty list. Three defaults line up:

1. The example proxy sends `max_tokens: 1` to the encoder instance.
2. When the encoder cache has no room for an item,
   `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` truncates `num_new_tokens` to the text before
   the image and **still schedules the request**, with an empty
   `scheduled_encoder_inputs` (the caller only skips it when
   `num_new_tokens == 0`).
3. The encoder instance's early return doesn't sample, so it never builds
   `discard_request_mask` — the mask that normally clears sampled tokens for
   chunked-prefill requests that aren't on their last chunk.

`update_from_output` has no in-flight-prefill guard of its own; it relies on the
runner returning an empty list. So the token is appended, `check_stop` sees
`num_output_tokens (1) >= max_tokens (1)`, and the request ends with its prompt
only partly consumed.

## Fix

Stop fabricating tokens; let the scheduler own the stop decision.

- `make_empty_encoder_model_runner_output` emits no tokens at all.
- `Scheduler.update_from_output` finishes an encoder-instance request once its
  prompt is consumed:

  ```python
  elif (
      self.is_encoder_only
      and request.num_computed_tokens >= request.num_prompt_tokens
  ):
      request.status = RequestStatus.FINISHED_STOPPED
      stopped = True
  ```

- The example proxy no longer sends `max_tokens: 1`; completion no longer
  depends on it.

"Prompt consumed" is the correct predicate because `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs`
never schedules tokens past an unadmitted multi-modal item, so a consumed prompt
implies every item in it was encoded or cache-served.

The decision belongs in the scheduler rather than the worker: it already advances
`num_computed_tokens` at schedule time, whereas the two GPU runners keep request
state in different shapes (`dict[str, CachedRequestState]` vs. the V2 runner's
SoA `RequestState`), so a worker-side predicate would have to be written twice
and kept in sync. The helper's signature is unchanged, so both runners work as-is.
The new branch sits after the pooling stop and is only reached when the step
produced no sampled token, so any path that does return real tokens keeps its
existing behaviour.

**Behaviour change:** an encoder-instance response now carries 0 completion
tokens with `finish_reason: "stop"` (previously 1 bogus token and
`finish_reason: "length"`). The example proxy only checks the HTTP status.

## Tests

Two regression tests in the existing scheduler suite: with the encoder cache
exhausted the request must not finish and must produce no output token; once
space is restored the encoder input is scheduled and only then does the request
finish. The unblocked path must still complete in one step, with no output token.
Both use `max_tokens=16` so they assert on encoding progress rather than on the
`max_tokens: 1` cap.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k encoder_instance -v
# 2 passed, 137 deselected
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q
# 139 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit -q
# 133 passed
```

Dropping only the `num_computed_tokens >= num_prompt_tokens` guard (finishing
unconditionally) fails the first test and leaves the second passing, so the test
discriminates on behaviour, not on the code shape.

---

- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

title: [Kernel][Model] Optimize FA4 mm_prefix range lookup
author: vhagor
body:
# [Kernel][Model] Gemma4: optimize FA4 mm_prefix range lookup and CuTe JIT stability

## Motivation

Gemma4 multimodal models can use FA4 as the backend for all layers, so that both
sliding-attention layers (`head_dim=256`) and global/full layers
(`global_head_dim=512`) use one attention backend. This is required for the
vision `mm_prefix` / PrefixLM bidirectional mask path, and avoids mixing
FlashAttention and Triton attention implementations within the same model.

For video prompts, however, the current FA4 `mm_prefix` implementation scales
poorly when the number of multimodal ranges varies across requests and batches.
In Gemma4 video workloads each frame commonly contributes one range, so batches
may see `max_ranges` values such as 1, 8, 16, 32, 46, or 64 over time.

This is not limited to applications that pre-extract frames outside vLLM. The
native vLLM video ingestion path can also produce variable frame counts. Raw
video inputs are decoded by `VideoMediaIO` / `VideoBackend`, which uniformly
samples up to `num_frames` frames (`32` by default). Long videos usually become
32 sampled frames, but shorter clips, failed frame recovery, JPEG-frame
sequences, multiple videos in one prompt, mixed image+video prompts, or
request-level `media_io_kwargs` such as `fps`, `num_frames=-1`, or a larger
`num_frames` can all change the final number of frames in a batch.

Gemma4 does not have a native video tower in vLLM. After video loading, each
sampled frame is processed as an image and the video placeholder is expanded as:

```text
mm:ss <boi> <|video|>*N <eoi> mm:ss <boi> <|video|>*N <eoi> ...
```

Only the `<|video|>` soft-token positions are marked as multimodal embeddings;
the timestamp, `<boi>`, and `<eoi>` tokens are not. Therefore
`PlaceholderRange.extract_embeds_range()` splits one video into one
bidirectional `mm_prefix` range per frame rather than one range for the whole
video. With default raw video loading, one video typically contributes between
1 and 32 ranges. With multiple videos, mixed images, or caller-provided frame
sequences, the range count can be higher and more variable.

## Problem

The current FA4 `mm_prefix` mask_mod receives a padded tensor of shape
`(batch, max_ranges, 2)` and scans every range for every Q x K score:

```python
for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(max_ranges):
    r_start, r_end = ranges[b, i]
    keep = keep | (q_in_range & k_in_range)
```

This creates two performance problems:

1. `max_ranges` is baked into the CuTe JIT specialization via
   `cutlass.range_constexpr(max_ranges)`. Different video frame counts can
   produce different FA4 compile keys and trigger repeated cold JIT compiles.
2. Even when the kernel is already compiled, the mask work is
   `O(max_ranges)` per score. A request with many frames increases the work for
   every request in the same batch because the tensor is padded to the batch
   maximum.

For Gemma4 video prefill with FA4 and vision `mm_prefix`, this hurts both cold
start and steady state. The GPU can sit idle while CuTe compiles a new
specialization, and the compiled kernel still pays for the range scan on every
masked score.

The old mask work scales roughly as:

```text
sliding_layers * num_heads * L^2 * batch_max_ranges
```

The `batch_max_ranges` term comes from scanning all padded ranges in the
mask_mod. The proposed range-id path keeps the same dense Q x K mask surface,
but each lookup is constant time:

```text
sliding_layers * num_heads * L^2
```

There is a metadata precompute step to allocate and fill the
`(batch, max_seq_len)` range-id tensor:

```text
batch_size * max_seq_len + total_mm_tokens
```

That work happens outside the FA4 score loop. The hot FA4 mask path no longer
scales with the largest frame count in the batch.

## Proposed change

Move range membership lookup from the FA4 mask inner loop into metadata
precomputation:

- Build a per-token range-id tensor with shape `(batch, max_seq_len)`.
- Fill non-mm tokens with `-1`.
- Assign each multimodal range a request-local integer id.
- In the FA4 mask_mod, replace the loop over `max_ranges` with:

```python
q_id = range_ids[b, q_abs]
k_id = range_ids[b, kv_idx]
mm = (q_id >= 0) & (q_id == k_id)
keep = causal_window_keep | mm
```

For Gemma4 sliding layers that clamp the bidirectional block to the sliding
window, keep the existing `(query_abs - kv_idx) < sliding_window` condition on
the `mm` branch.

This preserves the non-overlapping range semantics of the existing
start/end-list implementation while making lookup `O(1)` and removing
`max_ranges` from the FA4 mask_mod compile key.

The complexity reduction is part of the fix, not just a cache workaround. It
removes the range loop from the innermost Q x K masking path, so the FA4 mask
cost no longer scales with the batch's largest video frame count.

## Measured results

The numbers below were measured with the latest vLLM version on one H100 GPU,
using Gemma 4 31B in BF16. The benchmark used FA4 with vision
`mm_prefix`.

This was a pooling embedding workload, not a generation benchmark. That matches
the production use case for this branch, where serving returns pooled scores
rather than generated text. QPS means completed pooling embedding requests per
second.

Workload shape:

- 1000 real requests stress test at concurrency 32.
- Each request has one video and text, in `text + video` order.
- Video frame count varies between 8 and 64 frames, with an average of 48.
- Each frame is 360 x 640.
- The text part averages 885 tokens.

| Path | QPS |
| --- | ---: |
| Existing FA4 `mm_prefix` range scan with CuTe JIT | 0.103 |
| Existing FA4 `mm_prefix` range scan without CuTe JIT | 0.678 |
| FA4 with per-token range ids | 1.307 |
| Triton reference path | 0.743 |

This is a +92.8% QPS improvement over the existing FA4 path and makes FA4 faster
than the Triton comparison path under the same workload.

The gain comes from both parts of the change:

- avoiding repeated FA4 CuTe recompilation when `max_ranges` changes;
- replacing the per-score scan over all padded ranges with an `O(1)` range-id
  equality check.

Correctness checks from the same setup:

- outputs matched bit-exact between old FA4 and range-id FA4.
- Mean absolute difference versus the reference path was about 0.00646, in the
  same range as the historical FA4/Triton difference.

## Implementation sketch

Files touched:

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py`
  - Add `compute_mm_prefix_range_id_tensor(...)`.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`
  - Store `mm_prefix_range_id_tensor` in `FlashAttentionMetadata`.
  - Build the range-id tensor from `CommonAttentionMetadata.mm_req_doc_ranges`.
  - Pass the range-id tensor to FA4 as `aux_tensors`.
  - Remove `max_ranges` from `_make_mm_prefix_mask_mod(...)`.
  - Use `q_id == k_id` instead of scanning range start/end pairs.
- `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py`
  - Clear the new FA metadata field on full-attention layers, matching the
    existing Gemma4 `mm_prefix` cleanup.

The Triton attention path can continue using the existing
`(batch, max_ranges, 2)` tensor. This change only optimizes the FA4 path.

## Test result

Unit / local:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix_range_id.py -v
# 4 passed, 14 warnings in 0.85s

git diff --check -- \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix_range_id.py
# passed
```

## Duplicate-work check

Searched for existing and open work around:

- Gemma4 FA4 `mm_prefix`
- `mm_prefix` range lookup
- `range_constexpr(max_ranges)`
- `compute_mm_prefix_range_id_tensor`
- FA4 Gemma4 video performance

Related existing work covers FA4 enablement, Gemma4 bidirectional vision
attention, correctness fixes for FA4 `mm_prefix`, FA4 FP8 KV cache work, and
text-only backend selection. The duplicate-work check did not find an existing
PR or issue that removes the FA4 `max_ranges` specialization or replaces the
in-kernel range scan with a per-token range-id lookup.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to analyze the current implementation and prepare this
issue draft.

title: [BugFix] Fix P/D preemption race condition
author: njhill
body:
There is a small race condition with P/D and async scheduling, where a prefill request can be preempted during it's final (possible only) step. The scheduler logic currently allows such requests to complete normally because for most purposes they are finished (final output token generated and returned). They just get removed from the waiting queue.

However at this point, their kv blocks have been purged and so async kv-consuming connectors (prefill side) will see an empty list of blocks when their `request_finished()` is called.

One possibility is to have the connector fail the request in this case so that the router will retry it (since it shoud happen pretty rarely).

This PR attempts to fix it internally - when such preemptions happen in cases that there's a connector that _requires_ generated kv, it will discard the last token so that the request will be requeued/computed.

A new `requires_kv_delivery` property to control this behavior is added that connectors can override - since it doesn't make sense to recompute for offloading connectors that are just caching for possible later reuse. It defaults to `True` only for producing connectors.

---

**Note:** This replaces https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48141 which had some gaps and needed to be reworked following https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48245. Thanks to @Dao007forever, @ivanium and @liuzijing2014 for help with this!

Claude was used to help with this PR.

title: [DSv4 Perf] Remove redundant full kernel for dsv4, 1.88x kernel performance improvement
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

Part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45861

Passing an out tensor to avoid additional `torch.full` kernel call

## Test

Covered in unit tests

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
import gc
import statistics
import time
from collections.abc import Callable

import torch

from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.common.ops.cache_utils import (
    combine_topk_swa_indices,
)

# Fixed production-like C128A prefill configuration.
NUM_TOKENS = 8192
MAX_MODEL_LEN = 1_048_576
COMPRESS_RATIO = 128
WINDOW_SIZE = 128
TOPK_WIDTH = MAX_MODEL_LEN // COMPRESS_RATIO
COMBINED_TOPK = (
    (TOPK_WIDTH + WINDOW_SIZE + 127) // 128 * 128
)

# Timing configuration.  The first calls compile/warm the Triton kernel and are
# deliberately excluded.  Rounds alternate provider order to reduce bias.
WARMUP_ITERS = 5
ITERS_PER_ROUND = 20
NUM_ROUNDS = 5

Provider = Callable[[], tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]


def make_inputs() -> tuple[
    torch.Tensor,
    torch.Tensor,
    torch.Tensor,
    torch.Tensor,
]:
    """Create the metadata seen by one fresh 8192-token C128A prefill."""
    device = torch.device("cuda")

    # C128A reserves MAX_MODEL_LEN / COMPRESS_RATIO columns.  For an 8192-token
    # prompt only the first 64 can be valid, so leave the unused tail untouched.
    topk_indices = torch.empty(
        (NUM_TOKENS, TOPK_WIDTH), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
    )
    valid_topk = NUM_TOKENS // COMPRESS_RATIO
    topk_indices[:, :valid_topk] = torch.arange(
        valid_topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
    )

    query_start_loc = torch.tensor(
        [0, NUM_TOKENS], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
    )
    seq_lens = torch.tensor([NUM_TOKENS], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    gather_lens = torch.tensor(
        [min(NUM_TOKENS, WINDOW_SIZE)], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
    )
    return topk_indices, query_start_loc, seq_lens, gather_lens


def measure_batch(provider: Provider) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Return average (GPU event ms, synchronized wall-clock ms) per call."""
    start_event = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    end_event = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)

    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    wall_start = time.perf_counter()
    start_event.record()
    for _ in range(ITERS_PER_ROUND):
        result = provider()
        # Drop the old-path output immediately, matching its temporary lifetime
        # in _forward_prefill and allowing normal CUDA allocator reuse.
        del result
    end_event.record()
    end_event.synchronize()
    wall_end = time.perf_counter()

    return (
        start_event.elapsed_time(end_event) / ITERS_PER_ROUND,
        (wall_end - wall_start) * 1000 / ITERS_PER_ROUND,
    )


def report(
    before_gpu: list[float],
    after_gpu: list[float],
    before_wall: list[float],
    after_wall: list[float],
) -> None:
    before_gpu_ms = statistics.median(before_gpu)
    after_gpu_ms = statistics.median(after_gpu)
    before_wall_ms = statistics.median(before_wall)
    after_wall_ms = statistics.median(after_wall)

    gpu_speedup = before_gpu_ms / after_gpu_ms
    wall_speedup = before_wall_ms / after_wall_ms
    gpu_reduction = (1.0 - after_gpu_ms / before_gpu_ms) * 100
    wall_reduction = (1.0 - after_wall_ms / before_wall_ms) * 100

    print("\nResults (median of per-round averages)")
    print("-" * 72)
    print(f"{'Provider':<12} {'GPU latency':>16} {'Wall latency':>16}")
    print(f"{'before':<12} {before_gpu_ms:>13.3f} ms {before_wall_ms:>13.3f} ms")
    print(f"{'after':<12} {after_gpu_ms:>13.3f} ms {after_wall_ms:>13.3f} ms")
    print("-" * 72)
    print(f"GPU:  {gpu_speedup:.2f}x speedup, {gpu_reduction:.1f}% lower latency")
    print(f"Wall: {wall_speedup:.2f}x speedup, {wall_reduction:.1f}% lower latency")
    print(
        "\nThis is the combine-index micro-operation speedup, not full-model "
        "prefill speedup."
    )


@torch.inference_mode()
def main() -> None:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("This benchmark requires a CUDA GPU")

    torch.cuda.set_device(0)
    topk_indices, query_start_loc, seq_lens, gather_lens = make_inputs()

    compressed_len = NUM_TOKENS // COMPRESS_RATIO
    n = compressed_len
    m = n + WINDOW_SIZE

    workspace_indices = torch.empty(
        (NUM_TOKENS, COMBINED_TOPK), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
    )
    workspace_lens = torch.empty(NUM_TOKENS, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

    def before() -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        return combine_topk_swa_indices(
            topk_indices,
            query_start_loc,
            seq_lens,
            gather_lens,
            WINDOW_SIZE,
            COMPRESS_RATIO,
            TOPK_WIDTH,
            m,
            n,
        )

    def after() -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        return combine_topk_swa_indices(
            topk_indices,
            query_start_loc,
            seq_lens,
            gather_lens,
            WINDOW_SIZE,
            COMPRESS_RATIO,
            TOPK_WIDTH,
            m,
            n,
            out=(workspace_indices, workspace_lens),
        )

    print("DSv4 C128A prefill combine-index microbenchmark")
    print("=" * 72)
    print(f"GPU:                 {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")
    print(f"Prompt tokens:       {NUM_TOKENS}")
    print(f"Maximum model len:   {MAX_MODEL_LEN}")
    print(f"C128A index width:   {TOPK_WIDTH}")
    print(f"Combined width:      {COMBINED_TOPK}")
    print(
        "Output buffer:       "
        f"{NUM_TOKENS * COMBINED_TOPK * torch.int32.itemsize / 2**20:.1f} MiB"
    )
    print(
        f"Timing:              {NUM_ROUNDS} rounds x {ITERS_PER_ROUND} calls"
    )

    # Compile both paths and stabilize allocator/workspace state.
    for provider in (before, after):
        for _ in range(WARMUP_ITERS):
            result = provider()
            del result
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

    # The new path intentionally leaves padding uninitialized.  Compare only
    # lengths and valid entries, which are the values consumed by FlashMLA.
    reference_indices, reference_lens = before()
    actual_indices, actual_lens = after()
    torch.testing.assert_close(reference_lens, actual_lens, rtol=0, atol=0)
    sample_rows = (127, NUM_TOKENS // 2, NUM_TOKENS - 1)
    sample_lens = actual_lens[list(sample_rows)].cpu().tolist()
    for row, length in zip(sample_rows, sample_lens):
        torch.testing.assert_close(
            reference_indices[row, :length],
            actual_indices[row, :length],
            rtol=0,
            atol=0,
        )
    del reference_indices, reference_lens, actual_indices, actual_lens
    gc.collect()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    print("Correctness check:   passed (lengths and sampled valid entries)")

    samples: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]] = {
        "before": [],
        "after": [],
    }
    for round_idx in range(NUM_ROUNDS):
        order = (("before", before), ("after", after))
        if round_idx % 2:
            order = tuple(reversed(order))
        for name, provider in order:
            samples[name].append(measure_batch(provider))

    report(
        [sample[0] for sample in samples["before"]],
        [sample[0] for sample in samples["after"]],
        [sample[1] for sample in samples["before"]],
        [sample[1] for sample in samples["after"]],
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

And we get

title: [DSv4 Perf] Fix redundant memory allocation and copy for dsv4 pp buffer, 448 MiB GPU memory saved
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

We do `torch.empty` and `copy` in pp last rank even if there is no mtp enabled, this PR fixes the issue,

## Test

Perf gain can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

import torch

HIDDEN_SIZE = 7168
HC_MULT = 4
MAX_NUM_TOKENS = 8192
NUM_WARMUPS = 20
NUM_REPEATS = 1000
TOKEN_COUNTS = (1, 8, 32, 128, 512, 2048, 8192)


def main() -> None:
    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA is required"

    hidden_states = torch.empty(
        MAX_NUM_TOKENS,
        HC_MULT,
        HIDDEN_SIZE,
        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device="cuda",
    )
    mtp_hidden_buffer = torch.empty(
        MAX_NUM_TOKENS,
        HC_MULT * HIDDEN_SIZE,
        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device="cuda",
    )

    buffer_mib = mtp_hidden_buffer.nbytes / 2**20
    print(f"GPU: {torch.cuda.get_device_name()}")
    print(f"MTP buffer: {buffer_mib:.1f} MiB")
    print("tokens\tcopy size\tcopy latency")

    for num_tokens in TOKEN_COUNTS:
        src = hidden_states[:num_tokens].flatten(1)
        dst = mtp_hidden_buffer[:num_tokens]

        for _ in range(NUM_WARMUPS):
            dst.copy_(src)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        start.record()
        for _ in range(NUM_REPEATS):

        copy_mib = src.nbytes / 2**20
        print(f"{num_tokens}\t{copy_mib:.3f} MiB\t{latency_us:.3f} us")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

title: [PD][Bugfix] Rebase KV lease deadlines onto worker clock
author: njhill
body:
`pull_scheduler.request_finished` stamps `reqs_to_send` deadlines with the **scheduler process's** `time.perf_counter()`; `base_worker` expires them against **each worker's own** `perf_counter`. perf_counter epochs are process-local — across nodes they differ by boot-time deltas, so on a multi-node prefill deployment the second node's effective TTL is `ttl − (node clock-epoch gap)`, which can be near zero or negative.

Premature release marks blocks reusable while the remote read is pending — the read then pulls whatever now occupies those blocks: silent accuracy corruption because the *arriving* data is wrong.

**Fix**: ship the scheduler's clock in `NixlConnectorMetadata.scheduler_clock` and have workers rebase the remaining TTL onto their own clock at registration (broadcast latency only lengthens the lease — the safe direction). Applied to pull and push workers; the D-side turn-2 `blocks_expiry_time` path (which already does clock-offset estimation) is untouched.

This PR was originally authored by @esmeetu and Claude.

title: [Perf] Skip detokenization in offline beam search
author: samuelkim7
body:
## What & why

Follow-up to #46422, which skipped detokenization in online beam search and noted the offline path has the identical pattern.

Offline beam search asks for `logprobs = 2 * beam_width` on every internal per-step request. The engine detokenizes all of those token ids into strings on every step, but beam search never reads them. It ranks beams by `cum_logprob` and decodes the final text itself. This PR sets `detokenize=False` on the two internal `SamplingParams`, same as #46422 did for the online path.

As with #46422, the per-step `Logprob` entries in the returned sequences no longer carry `decoded_token` strings. Final output text is unchanged.

## Benchmark

A100, Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B (same model as #46422), offline `LLM.beam_search`, 8 prompts of 256 tokens, 32 output tokens, temperature 0, `enforce_eager`. One arm per process. Output token ids are sha256-compared across arms as a hard gate.

| beam width | wall clock (before → after) | speedup | outputs identical |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 2.67s → 2.13s | 1.25x | yes |
| 8 | 3.58s → 2.71s | 1.32x | yes |
| 20 | 9.41s → 6.61s | 1.42x | yes |

The win grows with beam width, matching the O(beam_width) per-step cost #46422 measured on the online path (1.80x at width 20 there; eager mode inflates the per-step GPU time here, so these numbers are conservative).

## Correctness

Output token ids are bit-identical between arms at all three beam widths on the A100 run (sha256 gate). I also verified output equality on CPU (TinyLlama-1.1B, beam widths 4 and 8, 3 interleaved rounds each). The existing `tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py` suite covers the offline path against HF reference outputs in CI.

## Duplicate check

No open PR applies this to the offline path. #47630 touches the same file for `allowed_token_ids` handling and does not conflict with this change.

Done with Claude Code assistance, mostly on the benchmark harness and runs. I reviewed the change and validated the results.

title: [BugFix] Scope divergent hybrid cache hits to capable connectors
author: ivanium
body:
## Summary

- Gate divergent per-group local cache hits behind a connector capability.
- Opt NIXL in and keep unknown/store-style connectors on the common local hit.
- Enable the capability for MultiConnector only when every child supports it.
- Reconcile divergent partial hits before external lookup.

## Why

Per-group hybrid cache hits rely on the connector restoring missing Mamba state. Applying that policy to every connector can report a full-attention hit without a valid state at the resume boundary.

This is not a duplicate of #46455 or #48195: those target the original divergence handling addressed by #48425. This follow-up defines a conservative connector contract on current `main` and covers partial divergent hits.

title: [Perf][Sparse MLA] Drop the atomic contention in the index remap
author: njhill
body:
The sparse-MLA index remap splits each 2048-wide row into 16 column tiles. On the valid-count path every tile atomic-adds into the same per-row counter, so the row total is built under 16-way contention -- and the DCP compaction path uses that same counter as an atomic slot allocator.

Counting is the only reason the tiles need to talk to each other. Give one program the whole row instead: the count becomes an in-register reduction plus a plain store, the compaction base is statically 0, and the counter buffer no longer needs zero-initialization. Rows without a count keep the 16-tile layout, where there is nothing to contend on.

Measured on GB200 inside a CUDA graph -- decode runs under graphs, so the launcher overhead is captured once and only the kernel work is timed. Per-call, previous kernel -> this one:

```
                              1 token        256 tokens    1024 tokens
  index_topk 512  ( 4 tiles)  2.50->1.67us   4.06->1.84us   5.50->2.54us
  index_topk 2048 (16 tiles)  3.02->1.83us   5.65->2.20us  12.22->3.84us
```
That is 1.50x-3.18x, and the gain widens with the tile count -- 16 tiles pull away from 4 as the batch grows, which is the contention signature. The remap runs once per attention layer per decode step, so for a 78-layer index_topk=2048 model this is ~93us/step at one token and ~270us/step at 256.

This path is used by the sparse-MLA backends that request valid counts (flashmla, flashinfer, flashattn, xpu, rocm_aiter). DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA does its own index handling and is unaffected.

Bit-exact: 1728 randomized A/B configurations (token counts 1-1024, invalid fractions 0-100%, out-of-bounds block ids, DCP sizes 2/4 with interleave 1/64) match the previous implementation exactly -- the compaction prefix additionally becomes deterministically in-order, where before its order was unspecified.

Idea from https://asari.ai/blog/inference-optimization. @AsariAI other PRs are very welcome!

title: [Bugfix] Fix stale latent MoE residual pointer in CUDA graphs
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose
Fix a bug in Latent MoE runner where CUDA graphs hold stale pointers which can be freed by eager execution, causing illegal memory access.

Current code:
```
def _get_zero_residual(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        numel = hidden_states.numel()
        buf = getattr(self, "_zero_residual", None)
        if (
            buf is None
            or buf.dtype != hidden_states.dtype
            or buf.device != hidden_states.device
            or buf.numel() < numel
        ):
            buf = torch.zeros(
                numel, dtype=hidden_states.dtype, device=hidden_states.device
            )
            self._zero_residual = buf
        return buf[:numel].view_as(hidden_states)
```

`buf` is allocated outside graph capture, and can be reassigned when a larger hidden states tensor requires a larger buffer in eager execution. Thus, the cuda graphs still point to the stale memory address, resulting in illegal memory access when memory pressure is high.

The PR fixes it by allocating a static buffer using `max_num_tokens` to eliminate stale memory caused by reassignment.

## Test Plan
Tested that before the change, workloads hits `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` consistently. With the patch, the issue is gone.

## Test Result

title: [CPU] Bump up CPU kernels to latest version
author: bigPYJ1151
body:
## Purpose

Sync `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/` from sglang (`sgl-kernel/csrc/cpu`) to latest upstream `main`, reconciling vLLM-specific patches layered on since the last bump (#41924): MXFP4 W4A16 MoE, AMX GDN dispatch, ISA-portability BLAS fallback, RISC-V scalar/RVV support, chunked-prefill `has_initial_state` fix, DFlash speculative decoding, and batched spec-decode conv-state updates. Also rejects one upstream regression found during merge (a broken `TORCH_CHECK` for MXFP4 scale validation that would have silently weakened a size check).

Adopts SGLang's new pooled-state-indexing `chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu` signature for GDN prefill: the CPU GDN path now reads/writes the pooled `ssm_state` buffer directly via `initial_state_indices` instead of gathering a local copy first, avoiding an extra copy per prefill call. Made the kernel read `initial_state`'s actual `stride(0)` at runtime (mirroring `conv.cpp`'s `conv_state_slot_stride`) instead of assuming a fully packed layout, since pool buffers can be padded per slot (e.g. Qwen3.5's Mamba cache-align mode).

Not a duplicate of any open PR — searched `gh pr list` for sgl-kernel/CPU-kernel-bump related terms, no matches.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to fetch/diff upstream sglang, reconcile merge conflicts against vLLM-specific patches, and run the validation below. All changes were reviewed and tested by the submitting human.

## Test Plan

- Build: `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python3 setup.py develop` (`_C`, `_C_AVX512`, `_C_AVX2` targets)
- Correctness: `tests/quantization/test_cpu_wna16.py` / `test_cpu_w8a8.py` model list (12 models covering AWQ/GPTQ/compressed-tensors W4A16, FP8 W8A16 dense/MoE, MXFP4, INT8 W8A8 MoE) via offline inference, before vs. after this change
- `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`: multi-sequence prefill, prefix-cache reuse (`has_initial_state=True` path)
- `vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve` before/after on 4 models (w8a8, w4a16, FP8 MoE, Qwen3.5)
- `lm_eval` GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot, chat template, `max_model_len=16384`, `max_gen_toks=8192`) on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, before vs. after

## Test Result

- Build succeeds cleanly on all three CPU ISA targets.
- All 12 quantization models produce coherent output; 10/12 byte-identical to the pre-bump baseline under greedy decoding, 2 diverge after the first token (`gpt-oss-20b` MXFP4, `Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4`) consistent with quantized-kernel numerics shifting a near-tied argmax, not a functional break.
- Qwen3.5 GDN: coherent generation across fresh-state and prefix-cache-reuse prefill paths.
- Serving benchmarks: throughput/latency within noise (±3%) for the three MoE GEMM paths (w8a8, w4a16, FP8); Qwen3.5 GDN path improved 3-8% across throughput/TTFT/TPOT from the pooled-gather optimization.
- GSM8K: before `0.795/0.785` (flexible/strict exact_match), after `0.835/0.795` — within one standard error, no regression.

title: [Core] Fix ValueError on KV load failure with a hybrid KV cache
author: kebe7jun
body:
## Purpose
`_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` unpacks `get_block_ids()` -- which
returns one block-id list per KV cache group -- into a single name:

    # TODO (davidb): add support for hybrid memory allocator
    (req_block_ids,) = self.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)

so the first reported invalid block on a hybrid (Mamba/SSM plus attention)
model raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)` inside the
scheduler. Nothing catches it, so EngineCore calls `_send_engine_dead()` and
exits: one recoverable read failure takes down every request on the instance,
not just the one that failed.

A hybrid model's groups sit on different block grids, so the same block index
means a different token position in each and there is no single longest valid
prefix to truncate at. Rather than build a block-level answer for that -- per-
block error handling is being removed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42461 -- affected hybrid requests
recompute in full, which is the granularity that replacement moves to anyway.
Single-group models keep the existing block-level truncation untouched.

Blocks are still added to `marked_invalid_block_ids` so a request sharing one
of them is rescheduled as before.

The null block needs excluding on this path. In Mamba `align` mode a group's
block list is mostly the shared null block -- a 9-chunk request looks like
`[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 10]`, only the aligned snapshot is backed -- so
without the guard a reported null block would restart unrelated requests, and
`blocks_to_evict` would collect a block that belongs to no request.

## Test Plan

Use Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B (TP=2, 4 KV cache groups).

And also: `pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py`

title: [EPD] Remove duplicate image preprocessing in EPD and enable preprocess on GPU
author: gty111
body: ## Problem Two separate costs in an EPD deployment. **The decode instance redoes work the encoder already did.** The encoder instance runs the full HF image transform to produce the embedding; the decode instance then runs the identical transform over the same pixels. It does not need the result — the embedding already reaches it out of band through the EC connector, and the only thing it still needs from the pixels is the patch grid that sizes the placeholder range. At 2048² that duplicated transform costs ~66 ms per request, on top of shipping it 3.36 MB of base64 it has no use for. The encoder can simply hand the grid over instead. **The transform runs on CPU, and it is slow there.** It is a resize / normalize / patchify over several megabytes of pixels. Timing the HF `image_processor` alone, per image: | image | patches | CPU | GPU | speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 256² | 256 | 5.34 ms | 0.62 ms | 8.6× | | 512² | 1024 | 4.95 ms | 0.76 ms | 6.5× | | 1024² | 4096 | 5.85 ms | 1.45 ms | 4.0× | | 1536² | 9216 | 8.66 ms | 2.63 ms | 3.3× | | 2048² | 16384 | 11.46 ms | 4.32 ms | 2.7× | | 3072² | 36864 | 22.61 ms | 12.15 ms | 1.9× | | 4096² | 65536 | 40.48 ms | 17.88 ms | 2.3× | An encoder instance has the capacity to spare — it allocates no KV cache, so frontend work does not compete with a language model. Running on device also removes the copy back to host memory that `pixel_values` currently needs in order to cross the IPC boundary. ## Changes Two independent optimisations, cumulative in effect. ### 1. Send the grid out of band `ECExampleConnector` gains a `request_finished` override that reports each item's `mm_hash` and the `*_grid_thw` its processor produced, through the existing `ec_transfer_params` channel. The proxy replaces the image part with a metadata reference: ```python { "type": "image_embeds", "image_embeds": {"image_grid_thw": _b64_tensor(grid)}, "uuid": item_uuid, } ``` The grid comes from the side that computed it; the proxy never re-derives it. `Qwen2VLMultiModalDataParser` has to accept an item carrying only the grid, so it now asks `MultiModalDataParser.embedding_required_fields`, which drops the embeds key only when embeddings genuinely arrive out of band. The gate is a derived flag `MultiModalConfig.mm_embeds_out_of_band`, resolved to true **exactly on EC consumers** and not exposed on the CLI — everywhere else a request that forgets its embeddings keeps failing fast with the original error. `BaseProcessingInfo.build_data_parser` stamps it onto whatever parser the model returned, so the six existing construction sites are untouched. ### 2. Preprocess on the encoder's GPU New `--mm-processor-device={auto,cpu,cuda}`. `auto` picks the accelerator only when both hold: - the instance is an EC producer and not a consumer — no decoder, no KV cache, so frontend work does not compete with the language model; - `mm_tensor_ipc == torch_shm` — other transports serialise host bytes, so the result would be copied back and that copy costs more than it saves. Otherwise `cpu`, with a log line explaining why. `InputProcessingContext` passes `device="cuda"` to the HF processor (fast processors accept it; PIL-backed ones drop it via `get_allowed_kwarg_only_overrides`) and skips the copy back to host when the transport can carry device tensors, so `pixel_values` crosses by CUDA IPC. Two supporting fixes this exposed: `reduce_data` now skips pinning when the batch is already on device (`pin_memory()` rejects device tensors and previously killed the engine with `cannot pin 'CUDABFloat16Type'`), and `_postprocess_output` keeps tensors on device only under `torch_shm`. ## Results `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` (bf16 MoE), 2048² images, 1592 requests per configuration, median of three runs. Encoder on GPU0, decode on GPU1, `ECExampleConnector` over local disk. Output token throughput (tok/s), with the ratio against baseline: | configuration | c=1 | c=2 | c=4 | c=8 | c=16 | c=32 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 83.2 | 139.0 | 214.2 | 310.9 | 412.1 | 499.5 | | grid out of band | 109.1 | 171.6 | 262.6 | 380.3 | 485.6 | 597.0 | | + GPU preprocess | 117.0 | 169.6 | 270.0 | 378.0 | 491.1 | 616.0 | | **ratio, grid** | 1.31 | 1.23 | 1.23 | 1.22 | 1.18 | 1.20 | | **ratio, + GPU** | 1.41 | 1.22 | 1.26 | 1.22 | 1.19 | 1.23 | **Change 1 is a uniform win**: throughput 1.18–1.31×, TTFT 0.66–0.83×, end-to-end 0.76–0.86×, at every level. Proxy stage timing attributes it to the decode instance no longer running the transform nor receiving 3.36 MB of base64 per image; the bookkeeping the proxy takes on costs 0.66 ms. **Change 2 is a latency win, not a throughput win.** Over change 1 it is flat within run-to-run spread across c=2…c=16, ahead only at c=1 and c=32. What it consistently improves is TTFT (lower at five of six levels) and TPOT at c=32, 22.9 ms against 25.7 — matching what it removes, a 50 MB `pixel_values` round trip through host memory: movement on the critical path, not throughput-limiting compute. Full data and measurement caveats are in the report attached to this PR.

title: [Model] Fused mm preprocess normalisation on the Device
author: noooop
body:
## Purpose

This is one of my favorite CV tricks.

1. When normalize is computed on the GPU, it can be fused into subsequent operators, or even if left unfused, it takes almost no time.
2. Currently, image data transmission from the entrypoint to the engine core and then to the GPU uses uint8, rather than the model dtype bf16, and is only converted to bf16 on the GPU before entering input normal.

Moreover, this can be applied to all vision models.

### Speedup mm preprocess

title: [Model Runner V2] batch-sharded sample
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# Summary
Currently before sampling, the full target logits are materialized, allocating memory of size `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size)`. This PR reduces that per-step memory allocation by a factor of `1/P` during tensor parallelism by sharding the logits and sampler inputs along the batch dimension, and sampling in parallel on a subset of the batch.

Sharding the sampler inputs (`InputBatch`) was straightforward, and is handled by `BatchSharder.shard_sampler_inputs`. Requests are assigned to ranks by partitioning the request state index mapping (using `idx_mapping % tp_size`) in a deterministic way. From there, we derive the new sharded input batch CPU arrays & GPU tensors for the local rank, based on the requests that it "owns".

Sharding the logits along the batch dimension is accomplished by having the model compute logits for only its slice of the vocab size by implementing the `compute_logits_local` method. After that, each rank has a `[num_tokens, vocab_size // P]` slice of the full logits. However, instead of all-gathering to get the full `[num_tokens, vocab_size]`, we instead all-to-all along the batch dimension, so that each rank ends up with `[num_tokens // P, vocab_size]`.

In summary, this PR (1) reduces peak target logits memory from `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size)` => `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size / P)`, and (2) parallelizes the sampling operation, which can be particularly beneficial for TPOT whenever heavy sampling operations (e.g. top-k, top-p, block verification, etc) are performed. No changes had to be made to the `Sampler` or `RejectionSampler` because they work perfectly fine with smaller batch sizes as long as we shard the `InputBatch` properly, which we do.

NOTE: A big motivation for this PR is to enable sharding of the draft logits. The cached draft logits from the speculator forward pass(es) are preallocated in memory for the worst case, with a size of `O(max_num_reqs * num_spec_tokens * vocab_size)`. We can reduce that by a factor of `1/P` as well, but sharded sampling is a prerequisite.

author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose
Fixes two FP8-related issues in the current ROCm DeepEP pin:

1. On FP8 e4m3fn-based platforms (gfx950) on the current pin, the low-latency FP8 kernels were using an incorrect FP8 e4m3fnuz max of `240.0` instead of `448.0` because of a missing macro guard.

https://github.com/ROCm/DeepEP/pull/17 addressed both issues. It allows a pluggable e4m3fnuz max by command line, which we use during the ROCm DeepEP build in the vLLM container.

This PR is not a duplicate of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50145, which addresses the same tests but erroneously loosens tolerances instead of fixing the root cause.
