title: [Core] Update PyTorch to 2.14.0, torchvision to 0.29.0, triton to 3.8.0 (release channel)
author: atalman
body:
## Purpose

Update the PyTorch ecosystem to **2.14.0**, resolving wheels from the **release** channel:

- `torch`: → **2.14.0**
- `torchvision`: → **0.29.0**
- `triton`: **3.8.0** (unchanged — current for 2.14.0)
- `torchaudio`: **2.11.0** (unchanged — newest published on every channel)

CUDA stays on **cu130**.

This PR originally targeted the 2.14.0 release candidate on the test channel. That premise has
expired: **2.14.0 went GA on 2026-09-02 and 2.14.1 on 2026-09-30**, both published to the release
index. Continuing to pin an RC from `whl/test/` would ship a version that is two releases stale.

### Verified availability on the release channel before pinning

| Artifact | `whl/cu130` | `whl/cpu` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `torch==2.14.0` | present (`2.14.0`, `2.14.0+cu130`) | present |
| `torchvision==0.29.0` | present (`0.29.0`, `0.29.0+cu130`) | present |
| `torchaudio==2.11.0` | present | present |
| `triton==3.8.0` | present | n/a |
| `torchao==0.18.0` | present | n/a |

`torch==2.14.0` is also on PyPI.


| Removed | File |
| --- | --- |
| `ENV UV_NO_CACHE=1` | `docker/Dockerfile.cpu` |
| `--no-cache` on the image build | `.buildkite/image_build/image_build_cpu.sh` |
| `--no-cache` on the test build | `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-cpu-test.sh` |
| test-channel `--extra-index-url` | `tests/standalone_tests/python_only_compile.sh` |

Dropping the two `--no-cache` flags restores CPU image layer caching, which the comments noted had
been disabled at a measured cost (build 84705: 28 cached layers, zero torch downloads).

## Deliberately unchanged

**`.buildkite/scripts/check-ray-compatibility.sh`** already offers the resolver both the stable and
the test channel and lets `uv --index-strategy unsafe-best-match` pick. It resolves 2.14.1 from
stable today and still works for a future RC, so it needs no edit.

**The CPU shard timeouts in `.buildkite/hardware_tests/cpu.yaml`** (50m → 90m, 90m → 120m) are a
*different* workaround: torch 2.14 made CPU model-execution shards up to ~6.6x slower, tracked by
[pytorch/pytorch#193951](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/193951). That issue is now closed
as completed, so by its own comment these are revertable — but the timings in the comment were
measured against the RC and there is no 2.14.1 measurement yet. Left in place deliberately: a
too-generous limit costs nothing, a too-tight one kills a shard mid-run. Worth one measured run
before reverting, as a follow-up.

## CI status

Triage of the last full run ([build 91655](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91655)) is in a
comment below: 14 blocking failures, of which 2 are plausible torch regressions — an NVFP4
divergence that matches the already-filed
[pytorch/test-infra#8785](https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/8785), and a ROCm
`vllm._deepselect_C` extension build failure. The rest are pre-existing on `main`, infrastructure,
or flake-shaped. That run was against 2.14.0 from the test channel; it will need a re-run on these
pins.

title: speculative decoding under tensor parallelism (TP>1) , workspace creation select max hidden dim of target and draft model
author: khushali9
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #52023
With draft_model speculative decoding under tensor parallelism (TP>1), the engine crashes at init when the draft model's hidden_size is larger than the target model's(TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace sized from target only).

I kept logs and [seongyun](https://github.com/seongyun1104) help me run it on H100 and we confirmed workspace creation happens in eager and init does have draft model' config. 

My fix is simple, it just checks max for both model and picks the max hidden dim. 

## Test Plan
[seongyun](https://github.com/seongyun1104) to run this on H100 and confirm it does not crash. 
**A/B/C Matrix commands** 

The A/B/C matrix (the e2e validation) — the three serve commands:

 A — the crash (must now succeed): TP=2, draft wider
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","model":"Qwen/Qwen3-4B","num_speculative_tokens":1}'

B — regression check: same but TP=1
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","model":"Qwen/Qwen3-4B","num_speculative_tokens":1}'

C — regression check: TP=2, draft narrower
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","num_speculative_tokens":1}'


## Test Result
**A/B/C matrix Run**
Ran the A/B/C matrix on this PR head (b1d2ef5) on 2×H100 (SXM), TP=2. All three serve, and no arm logs a workspace validation error. I added a one-line trace at the sizing site (_fused_ar_workspace_hidden_dim) to show the width the pass builds with.

A — repro (draft wider than target): Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B (hidden 2048) + draft Qwen/Qwen3-4B (hidden 2560). The target model's fusion pass now builds the shared workspace at the draft width on both TP ranks:

[VERIFY52193] workspace_hidden_dim=2560 target=2048
[VERIFY52193] workspace_hidden_dim=2560 target=2048
Without the max(...), that pass sizes the workspace from the target (2048) only, so the draft's 2560-wide forward hits 2560 exceeds ... 2048 ([#52023](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52023)). With the fix the server reaches Application startup complete and a completion request returns normally.

B — regression (draft narrower than target): Qwen/Qwen3-4B (2560) + draft Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (1024). Serves normally; workspace stays target-sized (no inflation).

C — no speculative decoding: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B alone. Serves normally; max() is a no-op (draft_model_config is None).

ARM A: PASS   ARM B: PASS   ARM C: PASS
grep -c "Workspace validation failed" arm_{A,B,C}.log  ->  0  0  0

title: [Kernel] Add FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP8 linear backend
author: seonjinn
body:
## Purpose

FlashInfer exposes a TensorRT-LLM backend for dense MXFP8 GEMM, but vLLM's
`flashinfer_trtllm` linear selector currently covers NVFP4 only. This change
adds `FlashInferTrtllmMxfp8LinearKernel`, which can be selected with:

```text
--linear-backend flashinfer_trtllm
```


The kernel prepares TensorRT-LLM weight and scale layouts once after weight
loading. At runtime it quantizes BF16 activations with the 8x4 scale layout,
calls FlashInfer's TensorRT-LLM MXFP8 GEMM, and slices the physically padded
output back to its logical width before adding bias.

The kernel is the last CUDA entry in the MXFP8 priority list, so existing
kernels retain their normal priority. Explicit `flashinfer_trtllm` selection
filters the list to this kernel. This PR does not add tactic hints, MoE kernel
changes, or the high-M 128x4 activation-scale path.

No matching open PR was found with the searches `MXFP8 TRTLLM linear` and
`mm_mxfp8 trtllm`. The closest merged implementations are the NVFP4 TRTLLM
linear backend (#39129) and the MXFP8 CuTeDSL linear backend (#46393). Open PR
#52016 adds the independent B12X CuTeDSL package for SM120/SM121 and does not
expose FlashInfer's TensorRT-LLM MXFP8 runner.

## Test Result

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/kernels/quantization \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_trtllm_linear.py -q

1 passed
```

```text
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  docs/features/quantization/modelopt.md \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_trtllm_linear.py \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/flashinfer.py

All hooks passed
```

The GB200 test passed five real-GPU cases: three numerical shapes with M=1,
7, and 128, custom-op checks, and CUDA Graph capture and replay. The N=130
cases cover physical output padding and slicing. The run used commit
`37d19a7edd7559c3f8da24703d53feea198f96b4` and FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3,

title: [ROCm][DSV4][Perf] Optimize Triton sparse-MLA decode on gfx950
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## Summary

Optimize the existing in-tree Triton DeepSeek-V4 sparse-MLA decode path for
gfx950/MI355X.

The change adds a dedicated gfx950 partial kernel, workload-aware split
selection, graph-safe adaptive work selection, and gfx950-only cp-gather
de-specialization. It adds no AITER/Gluon runtime dependency or implementation
switch; corrected AITER/Gluon is used only as a performance comparator.

The PR remains draft while refreshed CI runs and the human submitter completes
the final line-by-line review.

## gfx950-only scope

All new runtime behavior is explicitly gated by `_ON_GFX950`:

- the specialized sparse-decode partial kernel and up-to-32 split policy;
- adaptive captured-graph split selection and narrowed ragged views;
- direct BF16 output;
- the compressed-cache NaN-free fast path; and
- cp-gather token/batch de-specialization.

gfx942 retains its existing 1-16 split selector, partial/ragged kernels,
cp-gather specialization, reducer behavior, and output path. A read-only gfx942
AOT audit found byte-identical HSACO text versus the clean baseline.

## Design

The gfx950 kernel:

- combines 448 NoPE and 64 RoPE dimensions for one 512-wide QK dot;
- uses four 128-wide PV accumulators to avoid spilling;
- processes main/SWA work in guarded BK32 tiles;
- peels full 64-entry compressed-cache groups into two ordered BK32 updates;
- preserves masked tails, attention sinks, and invalid-index semantics; and
- uses a fixed captured maximum grid while choosing live per-row work.

The split selector targets device occupancy, caps short workloads at four
splits, and uses up to 32 splits for low-batch long-context rows.

Compressed-cache scrub elision requires an explicit, false-by-default
provenance bit. On gfx950, both writers cap UE8M0 codes at 254 and canonicalize
RoPE NaNs. Main-cache values are still scrubbed, invalid indices contribute
zero probability, and cache block address multiplication uses int64.

## Performance

### Kernel acceptance

On one 256-CU MI355X, the exact 40-shape matrix
`T={1,2,4,8,16,32,48,64} x context={4K,32K,100K,500K,1M}` passed eager and
warmed-graph correctness and the `<=1.03` performance gate:

| Comparator | Accepted shapes | Worst measured ratio |
|---|---:|---:|
| Clean in-tree Triton | 40/40 | 1.000000 |
| Corrected AITER/Gluon | 40/40 | 1.023918 |

All 1,920 correctness comparisons passed with `atol=rtol=0.02`.

The final source-only cleanup was rechecked on four representative graph
shapes. Outputs were bitwise identical, p50 changed by -0.15% to +0.18%, and
the S8/S32 executable text and resource usage were unchanged.

### Canonical 8k/1k serving A/B

Configuration: 8x MI355X, TP8/DP1, concurrency 64, prefix caching disabled,
128 warmups followed by 640 scored requests, and fresh isolated compile caches.
The reference used the exact old sparse-decode source plus the same cp-gather
fix as the candidate. Input/output length arrays were byte-identical.

| Metric | Old sparse + common cp fix | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 1,155.242 tok/s | **1,187.054 tok/s** | **+2.754%** |
| Duration | 510.652 s | **496.967 s** | **-2.680%** |
| Median TTFT | 451.565 ms | **445.356 ms** | **-1.375%** |
| P90 TTFT | **1,508.041 ms** | 1,569.744 ms | +4.092% |
| P99 TTFT | 21,089.724 ms | **19,419.572 ms** | **-7.919%** |
| P99.9 TTFT | 25,961.827 ms | **24,709.868 ms** | **-4.822%** |

Both arms completed all requests without errors, preemption, or prefix-cache
activity. Every reported P99/P99.9 latency improved; P90 TTFT was the sole
regressed percentile. This is a positive paired no-regression result, not a
claim of statistical consistency from one run per arm.

Full results and methodology are in the
[8k/1k follow-up comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52212#issuecomment-5304874641).

## Validation

```bash
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -vv

ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k 'cp_gather_despecialized or gfx950_compressed_cache or \
      indexer_gather_accepts_upper_bound_output' -vv

pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

Results on the current head: 57 attention tests passed, four focused
compressor/cp tests passed, all changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, and
Python 3.12 mypy passed.

A full GSM8K run on the preceding pure-Triton source completed all 1,319
examples with strict accuracy 0.960576 and flexible accuracy 0.959818.

## Duplicate-work check

Issue #41820 and open PRs were checked for `41820 in:body` and
`DSV4 sparse MLA Triton`. No open PR duplicates this change. #50566 focuses on
reusable split-K scratch and output-copy removal; #51714 adds an optional
external AITER/Gluon path. This PR instead optimizes the default in-tree Triton
implementation on gfx950.

## AI assistance and accountability

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, test development,
benchmarking, auditing, and drafting. The human submitter remains responsible
for reviewing every changed line, understanding and defending the change,
rerunning the relevant tests, and completing final CI review.

title: Promote `prefix_cache_retention_interval` to an argument and change the default to 0
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
`VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` was added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43447, and allows control over the frequency of caching blocks for SWA and SSM models.

When setting this value to zero, vLLM retains only the latest replayable prompt boundary, and when setting it to a positive integer N, vLLM retains every N tokens.

This has become an extremely important setting especially for agentic workloads, so this PR upgrades it to an argument rather than an environment variable.

In addition, it now defaults to `0` rather than `None`, so that we avoid caching useless blocks. Marconi-style cache retention guarantees that we still retain the system prompt.

title: [Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Adaptive Verification without a confidence head
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# Context Currently, adaptive verification (AV) is only enabled for DSpark speculators that have a confidence head. This PR enables it for ALL draft-model-based speculator types (MTP, EAGLE3, DFlash 1&2), including DSpark when a confidence head is not available. NOTE: The attention backend(s) of the base model must still support variable length verification, which is the existing prerequisite for DSpark AV. This PR depends on #52992, which extends that support to the backends used here (Inkling sconv / rel-attention, FLASH_ATTN, FLASH_ATTN_MLA). All benchmarks below were captured with it applied. # This PR This PR implements an online acceptance estimator that learns to predict acceptance probabilities for draft tokens using the draft's logits. AV now works for DFlash, DFlash2, MTP, and any other draft-model speculator, provided that the attention backend(s) of the base model supports variable length verification. The feature used is `logit(q_max)`, the log-odds of the draft distribution's most likely token. # Results Summary AV OFF vs ON for three drafters that previously could not use AV, plus DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark run with the estimator and, as a reference, with its trained confidence head. Four datasets (speed-bench 2k low-entropy, speed-bench 2k high-entropy, humaneval, mt-bench), temp 1.0 / top-p 0.95, concurrency 64, ≤2K in / 2K out, natural EOS. Mean throughput gain with AV on: **+18.5%** MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash, **+18.1%** Inkling-NVFP4 + MTP8, **+14.6%** Muse-Glimmer-30B + DFlash2. Every dataset improves, with the largest gains on speed-bench high-entropy (**+34.0%** on MiMo, **+32.3%** on Inkling), where drafts most overrun acceptance. AV beats fixed verification at the same speculative length on every dataset, but a smaller fixed length can still beat it at specific concurrencies. The Pareto curves below compare AV at the max speculative length against a sweep of fixed lengths. **DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark:** the estimator and the trained confidence head are roughly on par at every measured concurrency. **MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash** (no confidence head): AV is on the throughput–interactivity frontier at 5 of 7 concurrencies. GSM8K accuracy is unchanged with AV on (pooled −0.08pp over 5,276 paired questions, McNemar p = 0.77; see [Accuracy](#gsm8k-accuracy-eval--av-off-vs-on)). # How it works For each drafted token the estimator fits a per-position logistic regression ``` p_accept(k) = sigmoid(w * logit(q_max) + b[k]) ``` where `q_max` is the draft model's probability of its most likely token, `w` is a slope shared across draft positions, and `b[k]` is a per-position intercept. Both are refit continuously during serving. **Prediction happens during draft sampling.** `sample_draft` already materializes the draft logits in order to draw a token, so the estimator scores the same rows in the same pass. Every draft-model speculator routes through that one call site, which is why MTP, DFlash and EAGLE3 need no speculator changes. Only DFlash2, which samples through a selector walk rather than `sample_draft`, scores at its own equivalent point. The probability is written into two index spaces at once: the persistent request-state slot, where the next step's refit will find it alongside the label the target eventually produces, and the current batch position, which is what AV indexes by. Keeping both avoids a reorder later, since the batch is compacted between the two uses. **Trimming reuses the existing AV path unchanged.** The estimator only supplies the per-position probabilities that DSpark's confidence head previously supplied. `record_confidences` publishes them and starts an async device-to-host copy, `get_num_tokens` sizes the global draft budget on CPU from the landed copy, and `_assign_draft_token_budget` ranks every `(request, step)` slot on device by its **survival probability** (the running product of that request's per-position confidences) admitting the globally best `draft_budget` slots. Because survival only decreases along a request, a global top-k always admits a prefix of each request's drafts, so `compact_batch` and `reallocate_drafts` can shorten the verification batch without any per-request bookkeeping. **Per step**, `propose()` folds the previous step's drafts (now graded accepted or rejected by the target) into IRLS sufficient statistics, and every `REFIT_INTERVAL` steps solves for new coefficients. Because the slope is shared by all draft positions, the information matrix is an arrowhead and the solve collapses to a scalar equation, so no per-position matrix inverse is needed. **Updates are damped by sample count.** Newton steps are scaled by `n / (n + DAMPING_OBSERVATIONS)`, but the slope and the intercepts count different things. The slope learns from every position, so it is damped by the round's total across all of them and is effectively undamped at serving batch sizes. Each intercept is damped by its own position's count, and observations thin out with depth because a deep position only exists when the shallower ones were accepted and admitted, so deeper `b[k]` move more conservatively, and a position nobody reached in a round has `n = 0` and holds still. **Shared slope, per-position intercepts.** Sharing one slope across positions costs almost nothing (0.0002 AUC, 0.0003 log-loss) and keeps deep positions usable: they see too few labels per round to fit two parameters each, but an intercept alone is well determined. # Why `logit(q_max)` Candidate features were compared on three metrics: - **AUC** measures discrimination: the probability that a random accepted draft scores above a random rejected one (0.5 = chance). - **log-loss** is the mean negative log-likelihood of the predicted probability. It rewards calibration and penalizes confident mistakes. - **ECE** measures calibration: predictions are binned, and each bin's mean prediction is compared with its observed acceptance frequency, weighted by bin occupancy. Held-out scores on ~4.5M labeled drafts from DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark, collected without AV (temp 1.0, top-p 0.95, concurrency 64; SPEED-Bench 2k low/high-entropy, GSM8K, HumanEval, MT-Bench). The last two rows are references, not fitted features. | feature | lossless | AUC ↑ | log-loss ↓ | ECE ↓ | |---|---|---|---|---| | `log(q_max)` | yes | 0.8069 | 0.4813 | 0.0592 | | `log(q_max) - log(q_2nd)` (top-2 margin) | yes | 0.8156 | 0.4437 | 0.0105 | | `H(q)` (entropy) | yes | 0.8321 | 0.4577 | 0.0638 | | `-log(-log(q_max))` | yes | 0.8336 | 0.4289 | 0.0103 | | **`logit(q_max)` (shipped)** | **yes** | **0.8336** | **0.4284** | **0.0100** | | `logit(q_sampled)` | **no** | 0.8553 | 0.4040 | 0.0152 | | `-log(-log(q_sampled))` | **no** | 0.8554 | 0.4075 | 0.0193 | | *`q_max` used directly as the probability (no fit)* | *yes* | *0.8259* | *0.4880* | *0.0736* | | *trained confidence head* | *yes* | *0.8191* | *0.4449* | *0.0052* | ### Takeaways: - **Losslessness rules out `q_sampled`.** The `q_sampled` features rank best, about 0.022 AUC above the best lossless feature, but they score the token the drafter actually drew. Trimming on them makes the decision to verify position `i` depend on `x_i` itself, so the drafts that survive trimming are no longer distributed as `q`, while rejection sampling still corrects with `min(1, p/q)`. The output distribution tilts toward the drafter's confident tokens. For example, with vocabulary `[a, b]`, `p = [0.5, 0.5]`, `q = [0.2, 0.8]`, and trimming when `q(x) < 0.5`, the output is `a` with probability 0.4 instead of 0.5. `q_max` depends only on the draft distribution, so the trim decision is fixed before `x_i` is drawn and the sampler's precondition holds. Under greedy drafting, the drawn token is the argmax, so the two features are identical. - **The fit is what provides calibration.** Used directly, as EAGLE-2 does when ranking its draft tree, raw `q_max` already ranks drafts better than the trained head (0.8259 vs 0.8191 AUC). But it is overconfident: its mean prediction is 0.784 against an observed acceptance rate of 0.723, and its ECE is 7× the fitted estimator's. AV's budget decision sums these probabilities against a measured cost table, so it needs calibrated values. Fitting on the target's accept/reject decisions provides them, and the result holds when scored prequentially, with each prediction using only coefficients fit on earlier steps, as in serving (ECE 0.0105). - **Discrimination is not calibration.** Entropy ranks nearly as well as `logit(q_max)` (0.8321 vs 0.8336 AUC) but is far worse calibrated (ECE 0.0638 vs 0.0100). Among the lossless features, `logit(q_max)` matches or beats every other fitted feature on all three metrics, needs no extra vocab pass (unlike the top-2 margin), and shares the log-odds scale of the quantity it predicts. ## Versus a trained confidence head DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark ships a trained confidence head, so it serves as the baseline. On the same held-out drafts: | | AUC ↑ | log-loss ↓ | ECE ↓ | |---|---|---|---| | estimator, `logit(q_max)` | **0.8336** | **0.4284** | 0.0100 | | trained confidence head | 0.8191 | 0.4449 | **0.0052** | The estimator ranks drafts better, and the head is slightly better calibrated, with no trained weights needed for the estimator. The ranking advantage comes from deeper positions: the head leads at the first draft position, and the estimator leads from the second onward, by up to 0.08 AUC at the deepest. Excluding the first position, the two are nearly tied on calibration (ECE 0.0103 vs 0.0090). Since survival is a running product, the first position is rarely the one trimmed, so the estimator is strongest where trimming actually happens. End to end, with probabilistic drafting and AV on in both arms (full tables under Benchmarks): | | estimator vs head | |---|---| | tok/s | +2.1% | | median TPOT | −3.9% | | accepted/drafted | +4.70pp (4 of 4 datasets) | The estimator matches the trained head without needing one. ## Fitted coefficients across models | model | nspec | slope `w` | `w` sd | intercept `b[0]` | |---|---|---|---|---| | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark | 5 | 0.5013 | 0.0250 | +0.279 | | MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash | 8 | 0.5197 | 0.0415 | −1.000 | | Inkling-NVFP4 + MTP8 | 8 | 0.5859 | 0.0349 | −0.572 | | Muse-Glimmer-30B + DFlash2 | 7 | 0.4450 | 0.0323 | +0.167 | Online coefficients averaged over refits during probabilistic serving; `w` sd is the refit-to-refit standard deviation. The first-position intercept `b[0]` is shown because it is comparable across draft depths, unlike the mean over positions. The slope is stable within a model pair but differs across pairs (0.45 to 0.59). The intercepts absorb workload difficulty: fitting DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark separately on each of five datasets, `w` stays between 0.51 and 0.55, while `b[0]` ranges from +0.61 to −0.09 and correlates with mean draft entropy at r = −0.89. # GSM8K Accuracy Eval - AV OFF vs ON Paired design: same 1319 GSM8K questions and the same per-request seed in both arms, temp 1.0 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20, concurrency 64, 4096-token cap, natural EOS. Pairing lets McNemar's exact test run on the discordant answers, which is far more sensitive at n=1319 than comparing two independent accuracy rates. | model | draft depth | n | AV off | AV on | delta | discordant (off-only/on-only) | McNemar p | degenerate off/on | refits | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark | 5 | 1319 | 93.93% | 93.40% | -0.53pp | 26 / 19 | 0.371 | 0 / 0 | 16 | | Muse-Glimmer-30B + DFlash2 | 7 | 1319 | 96.29% | 96.21% | -0.08pp | 11 / 10 | 1.000 | 0 / 0 | 7 | | Inkling-NVFP4 + MTP8 | 8 | 1319 | 95.98% | 95.83% | -0.15pp | 6 / 4 | 0.754 | 0 / 0 | 24 | | MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash | 8 | 1319 | 95.83% | 96.29% | +0.45pp | 11 / 17 | 0.345 | 0 / 0 | 20 | | **POOLED (all four)** | | **5276** | **95.51%** | **95.43%** | **-0.08pp** | **54 / 50** | **0.769** | **0 / 0** | | No significant change in accuracy from enabling AV with the acceptance estimator. # Benchmarks ## MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash — AV OFF vs ON 4xGB200 TP4, nspec 8, probabilistic drafting, temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95, concurrency 64, <=2K in / 2K out, natural EOS, FLASH_ATTN pinned on the draft in both arms. | dataset | tok/s OFF -> ON | Δtok/s | noise | median TPOT ms | ΔTPOT | accept len | Δ accepted/drafted | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | speed-bench 2k low-entropy | 4053 -> 4735 | **+16.8%** | 1.6% | 14.64 -> 12.52 | **-14.5%** | 3.41 -> 3.12 | -3.69pp | | speed-bench 2k high-entropy | 2497 -> 3347 | **+34.0%** | 0.8% | 24.95 -> 18.66 | **-25.2%** | 1.92 -> 1.78 | -1.89pp | | gsm8k | 3992 -> 4836 | **+21.2%** | 10.2% | 10.16 -> 8.54 | **-16.0%** | 5.11 -> 4.87 | -2.99pp | | humaneval | 4366 -> 4760 | **+9.0%** | 8.2% | 9.96 -> 8.59 | **-13.8%** | 4.20 -> 3.74 | -5.79pp | | mt-bench | 2752 -> 3136 | **+14.0%** | 3.9% | 11.64 -> 10.21 | **-12.3%** | 3.19 -> 2.92 | -3.33pp | | **mean** | | **+19.0%** | | | **-16.4%** | | **-3.54pp** |
Full per-arm metrics — median TTFT / TPOT / ITL, acceptance, generated tokens | dataset | arm | tok/s p1/p2 | spread | TTFT ms | TPOT ms | ITL ms | accept len | accept rate | gen tokens | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | speed-bench 2k low-entropy | OFF | 4021 / 4086 | 1.6% | 190 | 14.64 | 43.5 | 3.41 | 30.1% | 799250 | | speed-bench 2k low-entropy | ON | 4755 / 4715 | 0.8% | 159 | 12.52 | 32.0 | 3.12 | 26.4% | 793318 | | speed-bench 2k high-entropy | OFF | 2496 / 2498 | 0.1% | 189 | 24.95 | 43.1 | 1.92 | 11.6% | 814976 | | speed-bench 2k high-entropy | ON | 3334 / 3360 | 0.8% | 150 | 18.66 | 28.6 | 1.78 | 9.7% | 816026 | | gsm8k | OFF | 4186 / 3798 | 10.2% | 197 | 10.16 | 49.0 | 5.11 | 51.3% | 66898 | | gsm8k | ON | 4967 / 4704 | 5.6% | 155 | 8.54 | 38.8 | 4.87 | 48.3% | 66671 | | humaneval | OFF | 4460 / 4272 | 4.4% | 163 | 9.96 | 42.6 | 4.20 | 40.0% | 116190 | | humaneval | ON | 4572 / 4948 | 8.2% | 134 | 8.59 | 31.0 | 3.74 | 34.2% | 122601 | | mt-bench | OFF | 2802 / 2701 | 3.7% | 362 | 11.64 | 40.4 | 3.19 | 27.3% | 62204 | | mt-bench | ON | 3077 / 3196 | 3.9% | 350 | 10.21 | 30.3 | 2.92 | 23.9% | 59546 |
humaneval's +9.0% sits close to its own 8.2% noise floor, and its arms differ by 5.5% in generated tokens, so TPOT (-13.8%) is the more reliable signal on that row. ## Inkling-NVFP4 + MTP8 — AV OFF vs ON 4xGB200 TP4, MTP with 8 speculative tokens (`num_nextn_predict_layers: 8`, so this is the multi-module MTP path), temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95, concurrency 64, <=2K in / 2K out, natural EOS. title: [Feature] Support batch invariance on ROCm
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` makes a request's output independent of what else is in the batch. On ROCm the
mode set the flag and then ran ordinary kernels, and the determinism suite skipped itself, so nothing
noticed. This PR makes the mode work on gfx90a, gfx942 and gfx950 and runs the suite there. It builds on #58623
(custom all-reduce under batch invariance).

1. **`[Quantization] Fix FP8 GEMM paths that batch invariance relies on`**
   - `triton_scaled_mm` adds the bias in fp32 before the cast, as CUTLASS does, and no longer raises
     `UnboundLocalError` with `use_heuristic=False`.
   - `TritonFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, a scaled-mm linear kernel over `triton_scaled_mm` (per-tensor or
     per-token activations; per-tensor, per-channel or per-token weights), forced under batch invariance on
     ROCm. The block-scaled path takes `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`. Both warn when they override
     `--linear-backend` and raise, as NVFP4 does, if they can't implement the layer.
   - `fp8_scaled_mm_is_batch_invariant()`: the kernel is CUTLASS or Triton **and** the activation scale
     is static or per-token. It replaces the `isinstance(..., CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel)` checks in
     `Fp8LinearMethod.apply()` and the online per-tensor and PTPC paths.
   - Block FP8 skips the tuned config lookup under batch invariance.
   - `ocp_mx_emulation_moe` passes the checkpoint's static `a2_scale` (w_mxfp4_a_fp8 only) instead of `None`,
     which fell back to a dynamic per-tensor amax.
2. **`[ROCm][Core] Batch-invariant inference on gfx942 and gfx950`**
   - The persistent-matmul overrides on ROCm (sharing the SM80 branch), plus `mm.out`/`addmm.out`/`bmm.out`.
   - On ROCm, floating-point all-reduces the custom kernel declines, and floating-point reduce-scatters, take
     an all-gather (all-to-all) plus a fixed-order sum.
   - `+rms_norm` is forced into `custom_ops` under batch invariance on ROCm.
   - The AITER MX linear/MoE kernels pin their split-K or decline, the MXFP4 asm preshuffle path (which
     splits K) is skipped, and the skinny GEMMs are turned off.
   - MLA prefill: no `num_splits` on ROCm's `flash_attn_varlen_func`, and `ROCM_AITER_FA` is refused,
     whether auto-selected or explicitly selected.
3. **`[CI][ROCm] Run the determinism suite on gfx942 and gfx950`**
   - A ROCm entry in `DEVICE_BACKENDS`; the RMSNorm, online, NVFP4, LoRA-shrink and VLM tests un-skip
     on ROCm.
   - AMD mirrors for the Batch Invariance steps (A100 → MI250, H100 → MI300, B200 → MI355), running the
     same tests with `TRITON_ATTN` where the NVIDIA command selects `FLASH_ATTN`.
   - An optional distributed step (4×H100, mirrored on 4×MI300), running the E2E tests at TP=4 (with and without custom
     all-reduce) and at DP=4 with expert parallelism.

## Not ROCm-specific

- **`.out` overloads.** Inductor calls `extern_kernels.mm(..., out=buf)`, which bypassed the
  batch-invariant `mm`/`addmm`/`bmm`.
- **`torch.bmm`** is no longer rebound to the Python kernel. The `aten::bmm` registration covers it, as
  it does `mm` and `addmm`, and the rebinding broke `torch.bmm` on CPU tensors (as #60037 proposed).
- **Softmax** ignored `_softmax`'s `half_to_float` flag, so `torch.softmax(fp16, dtype=torch.float32)` returned
  fp16 (the bug #55249 also fixes).
- **Dynamic per-tensor FP8.** The scale is an amax over the whole batch, so no direct FP8 GEMM can be
  invariant with it; it keeps the BF16 fallback on every platform.
- **Block FP8.** Tuned tables change `BLOCK_SIZE_K` with M on 13 tables across 6 devices.
- **#58510's block32 MXFP8 GEMM** picks split-K by M; it now declines.

## Notable decisions

- **The all-reduce fallback stays, as a ROCm backstop.** #58623 removes the size threshold, but
  `should_custom_ar` still declines on dtype, byte alignment, contiguity, world size or a disabled custom
  AR, and on ROCm the next stop is RCCL. Integer all-reduces and reduce-scatters stay on RCCL, since
  integer sums are exact in any order.
- **Reduce-scatter.** Turning off SP/async TP under batch invariance (#56377) does not cover the
  model-level reduce-scatters: the MoE combine (`reduce_scatterv`) with DP>1 and EP, and SP MoE. On ROCm
  both go through all-to-all plus a fixed-order sum, ahead of the AITER reduce-scatter. RCCL
  `reduce(root=0)` (#45683's path) was measured batch variant at 4 ranks.
- **`ROCM_AITER_FA` MLA prefill is refused under batch invariance.** It is batch variant at kernel
  level: a 3.5k–6k-token sequence prefilled alone differs from the same sequence packed with others.
- **`+rms_norm` on ROCm.** With `custom_ops` at its compile default, `RMSNorm` runs `forward_native`, so
  `rms_norm_batch_invariant` is never reached, and Inductor lowers it to a reduction whose block size it
  picks by benchmarking at first launch. Forced on ROCm only; #60074 should address this on every platform.
  On an earlier ROCm image, DeepSeek-V2-Lite was not repeatable run to run (needle test 0/5), and 5/5 with
  the fix.
- **Scope.** The mode refuses known-incompatible configurations (sparse MLA, attention backends and MoE
  experts that don't declare support) and forces known-invariant implementations where one exists. It can't
  be swept against every kernel and flag in one PR, and AITER is invariant for some kernels and not others,
  so there is no blanket switch.

## Test plan

8× MI355 (gfx950), ROCm base image (torch 2.13, triton 3.8, aiter 0.1.24), compile cache disabled, the
CI commands run from `tests/`. The kernel rows were rerun on the final commit, the E2E and 4-GPU rows on the
previous revision; CI below covers the final commit.

| command | GPUs | result |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 7 passed, 1 skipped |
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_rms_norm_batch_invariant.py` | 1 | 475 passed |
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_lora_shrink_batch_invariant.py` | 1 | 6 passed |
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance_vlm.py` | 1 | 5 passed |
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py` | 1 | 29 passed, 8 skipped |
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_cutlass_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 81 passed, 120 skipped (CUTLASS-only) |
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_nvfp4_batch_invariant.py` | 1 | 1 passed |
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_mx_linear_batch_invariant.py` | 1 | 14 passed |
| `pytest v1/determinism/test_online_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 1 passed |
| needle, `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat -k TRITON_MLA` | 1 | 2 passed |
| needle, `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-FP8 -k TRITON_ATTN` | 1 | 2 passed |
| `pytest kernels/quantization/test_triton_scaled_mm.py` | 1 | 125 passed |
| TP=4: `bs1_vs_bsN or without_batch_invariance_should_fail` | 4 | 3 passed |
| TP=4, custom AR disabled (every all-reduce on the fallback): `bs1_vs_bsN` | 4 | 2 passed |
| TP=4 needle (all-reduces up to 45 MiB, chunked) | 4 | 2 passed |
| DP=4 + EP, OLMoE, online (reduce-scatter in the MoE combine) | 4 | 1 passed |

Upstream CI on this commit: [ci 93945](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93945) — every Batch
Invariance step passes: A100/H100/B200 and the 4-GPU H100 step on NVIDIA, their MI250/MI300/MI355 mirrors
and the 4-GPU MI300 step on AMD. The only failures are Ascend NPU and MI300 Quantization Shard 1
(`AXK1Config.scoring_func`), both failing on main too. Also green on the ROCm 10 image
([amd-ci 14415](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14415), built from `Dockerfile.rock`), including the
[MI300 Quantized Models step](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14415#01a12365-94c6-4db7-976c-1b25a98df658),
whose gpt-oss W-MXFP4-A-FP8 gsm8k check runs the emulation MoE.

Each new test fails with its fix reverted, one line at a time:
- FP8 scale predicate: 16 fail; Triton kernel excluded: 82 fail.
- Block-FP8 default config: fails (BI off differs by 323 elements, asserted in the test).
- `triton_scaled_mm` bias order: 4 fail; `use_heuristic`: 2 fail.
- MXFP4: without the split-K pin the three Triton shapes fail; without the asm-preshuffle gate
  `(8192, 14336, asm)` fails (row 0 changes at M = 9 … 2048).
- Each `.out` registration: its own case fails.
- `+rms_norm` (earlier image): the DSV2 needle test goes from 5/5 to 0/5.
- All-reduce fallback replaced by RCCL: TP=4 bs1-vs-bsN fails 32/32.
- Reduce-scatter routed back to upstream: DP=4 EP fails.

`pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passes, and each commit passes on its own.

## AI assistance

Written with AI assistance (Claude). Every line has been reviewed by the submitter, who can defend the
change end to end.

## Related PRs

- #58623 (merged): custom all-reduce under batch invariance. This PR builds on it.
- #55249: the same softmax `half_to_float` fix.
- #60074: pins Inductor kernel configs under batch invariance; the same root cause as `+rms_norm`, on every platform.
- #60047, #59952: also change `batch_invariant.py`'s matmul registrations and `matmul_persistent`. #60047 and #59985
  (keeps `GateLinear` off its specialized tiers) cover the MoE router's fp32-output GEMM (`mm.dtype`), which this
  PR doesn't.
- #57092: online FP8 MoE batch invariance; touches the same FP8 apply paths.
- #55958: refuses batch-invariant mode on unsupported platforms; ROCm should be in its supported set.
- #57042: the two-stage custom all-reduce rank-order change, split out of an earlier revision of this PR; left to that PR.

title: [Bugfix] Widen flashinfer.comm import guard so a failed import doesn't abort engine startup
author: shanjiaz
body:
## Purpose

The optional `flashinfer.comm` import in `allreduce_rms_fusion.py` is guarded by
`except ImportError`, so any other exception during import aborts `EngineCore` startup.
Hit with `flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3` on Python 3.11, which raises `TypeError` at
import time — killing startup on a `tp_size=1` run with `fuse_allreduce_rms: False`.

Widen the guard to `except Exception` and log a warning, so a broken flashinfer disables
the fusion pass instead of failing startup.

## Test Plan

Python 3.11:

```bash
uv pip install "flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3"
python -c "import vllm.compilation.passes.fusion.allreduce_rms_fusion as m; print(m.flashinfer_comm)"
```

## Test Result

Before: `TypeError: type 'array.array' is not subscriptable`, raised out of the module.

After:

```
WARNING [allreduce_rms_fusion.py:97] Failed to import flashinfer.comm; disabling allreduce fusion.
None
```

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results

title: [Feature][DSpark]: Logprobs adaptive verification
author: therealnaveenkamal
body:
Solves #51873 

## Purpose

Lifts the restriction blocking logprobs with enable_adaptive_verification, implementing the TODO from #47808.

Adaptive verification assigns per-request draft counts on device; the CPU-side `cu_num_logits_np` only holds an evenly-distributed stand-in. Using it as `cu_num_generated_tokens` would misassign logprob rows across requests. Instead, the rejection sampler now attaches the device `cu_num_logits`. The tensor rides along on the existing async D2H copy in AsyncOutput and is materialized as a list in tolists() after the copy event.

## Test Plan

title: [ROCm][Quantization] Support AMD Quark per-block FP8 for fused MoE layers
author: jimmy-adams
body:
## Purpose

#47972 added per-block (128x128) FP8 for Quark **linear** layers, but
`QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` still rejects the qscheme, so a Quark checkpoint whose routed
experts are quantized per-block loads every linear layer and then fails:

```
ValueError: For FP8 Fused MoE layers, only per-tensor and per-channel scales for
weights and activations are supported. Found per_block, per_group
```

## Changes

`QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` now accepts `per_block`, following the `BLOCK` strategy of
`CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`. The per-tensor and per-channel paths are untouched;
only the scale layout differs.

- `create_weights` allocates the weight scales on the 128x128 block grid and tags them
  with `FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported.BLOCK`, so `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` shards them
  by block rather than by row.
- The scales are registered as `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale`, the names Quark
  exports, so loading them needs no model-specific checkpoint mapping.
- `__init__` reads `block_size` from the weight config and requires dynamic activation
  quantization, rejecting a static input scale.
- `block_shape` is threaded through `_setup_kernel` and `get_fused_moe_quant_config` into
  `make_fp8_moe_quant_config`, which picks the block-scaled backend.

The fused-MoE block-alignment check was byte-identical in the FP8, compressed-tensors and
Quark implementations, so it now lives next to its linear counterpart in `fp8_utils` as
`validate_fp8_block_shape_moe`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k per_block
```

## Test Result

The unit tests above report `8 passed, 35 deselected`, covering the four new MoE tests and
the per-block linear tests from #47972.

End to end on 1x MI355X (gfx950), serving `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` re-quantized with AMD Quark
into an NVFP4 backbone with a per-block FP8 MTP layer, at TP=1 with
`num_speculative_tokens=1`:

- The drafter's `mlp.experts.routed_experts` binds `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` and loads
  without any model-specific weight mapping, on the TRITON FP8 MoE backend.
- Its scales are sharded on the block grid, giving `w13_weight_scale (256, 8, 16)` and
  `w2_weight_scale (256, 16, 4)` for `weight_block_size=[128, 128]`.
- `Avg Draft acceptance rate` averages 94.2%, which a scale or layout mismatch would drive
  towards 0.

Accuracy on that same run, `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot over the full 1319 questions with the
drafter enabled and thinking disabled in the chat template:

| Filter | exact_match |
| --- | --- |
| flexible-extract | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 |
| strict-match | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 |

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DSpark: inherit the target's attention backend when the speculative config names none
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

`load_dspark_model` passes `backend=speculative_config.attention_backend` when
building the draft's config. That field is `None` unless the user names a backend
inside `--speculative-config`, and `None` re-runs backend auto-selection rather
than meaning "same as target" — so an explicitly pinned target backend is silently
discarded and the draft can pick a different attention class.

On DeepSeek V4 with `--attention-config.backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, the
target builds `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttention` (plain 512B KV row) while the
draft falls back to `DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention`, whose `__init__` rewrites the
shared `cache_config.cache_dtype` to `fp8_ds_mla`. The SWA cache is then allocated
at 584B/token but still reshaped at `head_dim`, on every rank at first forward:

```
RuntimeError: shape '[-1, 64, 512]' is invalid for input of size 4176917504
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py, in _fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert
```

`4176917504 = 111754 * 64 * 584`, the `fp8_ds_mla` geometry. Fall back to the
target's backend when the speculative config names none; an explicit
`attention_backend` still wins.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- **#40611** (open) lets the draft *deliberately differ* from the target. This
  fixes the *fallback* when nothing is specified; the explicit override still wins.
- **#51538** / **#51042** fix a different DSV4 + DSpark defect (`decode_swa_indices`
  width). Independent of this one and deliberately not included.

Each masks the other, verified on one config (DSV4-Pro-0813, TP8 × 2 GB300,
`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, DSpark k=7):

| fixes | result |
| --- | --- |
| neither | `shape '[-1, 64, 512]'` invalid (this bug) |
| this PR | passes, then fails in #51538's path: `shape '[7, 128]'` invalid |
| #51538 | `shape '[-1, 64, 512]'` invalid again (this bug) |
| both | engine initializes and serves |

## Test plan

`pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py` → **2 passed**.
`pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py` → all pass
(incl. mypy, ruff).

## Model evaluation

aime25, 4 epochs (n=120), temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95, thinking on,
`max_tokens=150000`, DSV4-Pro-0813 on TP8 × 2 GB300, same tree throughout.
DSpark rows need #51538 applied too, since both are required to start:

| configuration | exact_match | pass@4 | errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, no spec | 1.0000 | 1.0 | 0 |
| `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` + DSpark | 0.9917 | 1.0 | 0 |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` + DSpark (n=360) | 0.9778 | 1.0 | 0 |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, no spec (n=360) | 0.9944 | 1.0 | 0 |

Mean acceptance length 3.16 at full concurrency. The DSpark row's single miss is a
`length` truncation on the one AIME problem that runs long in every configuration
tested, with no repetition loop. No unfixed baseline: the configuration cannot
start without this fix.

## AI assistance

This work was produced with AI assistance. The submitter has reviewed every changed
line, and the tests and evaluations above were executed on the hardware described.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable fused KDA decode on gfx942 (MI325X)
author: mpashkovskii
body:
## Purpose

PR #50654 added the fused Kimi-K3 KDA decode kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu`), but gated it to gfx950 (MI355X) in two places, so it never activates on gfx942 (MI325X):

- **Build gate** — `CMakeLists.txt` filtered the HIP source to `gfx950` only, so the kernel was not compiled and `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` (and therefore `torch.ops._C.fused_kda_decode`) was never defined on a gfx942-only build.
- **Runtime gate** — `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py` ended with `return on_gfx950()`.

This change extends both gates to gfx942 as well, so MI325X can take the fused decode path instead of falling back to the three-launch Triton path.

The kernel body is unchanged. It uses only CDNA-common primitives — wave64, DPP row/quad permutes (`quad_perm`, `row_half_mirror`, `row_mirror`), `__builtin_nontemporal_load/store`, and bf16 intrinsics — with no MFMA / FP8 / gfx950-only paths, so no source-level changes are required for gfx942. LDS use is ~2.8 KiB/block and register pressure ~130 VGPR, both well within CDNA3 limits.

## Changes

- `CMakeLists.txt`: HIP arch filter `gfx950` -> `gfx942|gfx950` (and comment).
- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py`: gate `on_gfx950()` -> `on_gfx950() or on_gfx942()`.
- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`: extend the module skip guard from gfx950 to gfx942 / gfx950 so the correctness suite runs on MI325X.

All other backends and the CUDA path are unchanged; the shape/dtype/head-count guards in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` are unchanged.

## Performance

The kernel-level win is large, but the end-to-end win on MI325X is currently small: the Kimi-K3 decode step is dominated by the MXFP4 MoE (int4) and the MLA attention plus the TP8 collectives, which dwarf the KDA linear-attention block. The fusion removes ~66 us of per-layer kernel time (mostly launch overhead), but that is a small fraction of today's total per-token cost. It should become more visible once #50817 (MXFP4 MoE Triton a16w4 for gfx942) lands and shrinks the dominant MoE cost — the fixed KDA saving then represents a larger share of a smaller decode step.

### End-to-end (tp8, 256-in / 256-out, max-concurrency 4)

| Metric | Triton fallback | Fused KDA | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 425.95 | 422.66 | -0.77% |
| P99 TPOT (ms) | 427.64 | 424.19 | -0.81% |
| Output tok/s | 9.29 | 9.36 | +0.75% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 1577.24 | 1574.03 | -0.20% (flat) |

TTFT is unchanged, as expected for a decode-only kernel.

### Per-layer kernel sequence (torch profiler medians, us)

Baseline runs the KDA decode as ~16 separate kernels per layer — the conv1d update, the recurrent delta-rule step, and the gated output RMSNorm decomposed into a chain of launch-overhead-bound (~4 us floor) elementwise ops. Fused collapses all of them into a single kernel:

| # | Baseline kernel | us | Fused kernel | us |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | _causal_conv1d_update_kernel | 5.01 | kda_decode_fusion_kernel<true, 12, true, true, true> | 7.77 |
| 2 | fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode_kernel | 6.45 | | |
| 3 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.37 | | |
| 4 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.41 | | |
| 5 | pow (tensor, scalar) | 4.41 | | |
| 6 | reduce Mean | 5.01 | | |
| 7 | add | 4.45 | | |
| 8 | rsqrt | 4.37 | | |
| 9 | mul | 4.21 | | |
| 10 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.17 | | |
| 11 | mul | 4.21 | | |
| 12 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.45 | | |
| 13 | sigmoid | 5.05 | | |
| 14 | mul | 4.33 | | |
| 15 | float32->bfloat16 copy | 4.49 | | |
| 16 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.57 | | |
| | **total (16 kernels)** | **~73.96** | **total (1 kernel)** | **7.77** |

~9.5x less kernel time for the KDA decode block (~74 -> 7.8 us/layer). The `12` template arg is 12 heads/rank (96 KDA heads at TP8). Across the model's KDA layers (~69 per the kernel header) that is ~4.6 ms/token of raw kernel time removed, in the same ballpark as the ~3.3 ms/token TPOT drop measured above (the remainder overlaps with other work).

## Not a duplicate


- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA decode gfx942"`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_kda_decode MI325"`

## Test Plan

Run on an MI325X (gfx942) box after building with gfx942 in the arch list:

1. Build compiles the kernel and registers the op: `python -c "import torch, vllm; print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, 'fused_kda_decode'))"` -> expect `True`.
2. Kernel correctness: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -v`
3. Model accuracy (output-affecting change) — serve Kimi-K3 on MI325X and run gsm8k, compared against the Triton fallback path: `make gsm8k`
4. Decode latency / throughput before vs after (fused vs Triton fallback): `make bench-kda-mi325`

## Test Result


- Op registered: **True** on the gfx942 build (`hasattr(torch.ops._C, "fused_kda_decode")`); the fused kernel appears in the trace (see Performance).
- Latency/throughput: **-0.77% mean TPOT**, +0.75% output tok/s
- gsm8k (fused vs Triton): **parity** — both 1.00 exact_match on flexible-extract and strict-match (5-shot, limit=100, stderr 0). The fused kernel matches the Triton fallback exactly.
- `test_amd_kda_decode.py`: **12/12 passed** on MI325X (gfx942) — fused output matches the Triton reference across heads {12, 24, 96} x tokens {1, 7, 128}, plus the null-slot, no-output-norm, and padding edge cases.

## Checklist

- [x] Compiles for gfx942 (kernel present in the .so with gfx942 codegen)
- [x] `test_amd_kda_decode.py` passes on MI325X (12/12)
- [x] gsm8k parity with the Triton path
- [x] AI assistance used (see below)

## AI assistance

This change was drafted with AI assistance (Claude). A human must review every line and run the build, tests, and eval on MI325X hardware before merge; the correctness and accuracy results above are not yet filled in.

title: [Perf][Nemotron] Skip redundant latent-MoE all-reduce at TP>1 (~13% decode win)
author: ECMGit
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

**Nemotron-3 decode regressed ~14% between v0.26.0 and v0.27.x at TP>1. This PR restores it.** The mechanism is generic but `NemotronH` is the only model that opts in, so it is the only one whose behaviour changes. No existing issue found.

| tp4, concurrency 1, inter-token latency | v0.26.0 | v0.27.1 | + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Super 120B-A12B BF16 (n=4/arm) | 4.07 ms | 4.64 ms (**+13.8%**) | **4.08 ms** (+0.15%) |
| Ultra 550B-A55B NVFP4 | 6.86 ms† | 7.21 ms | **6.79 ms** (−5.8% same-node) |

† cross-node, directional only — see Test Result.

### Root cause

[`_maybe_reduce_routed_output_before_transform()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L434-L453) (added in v0.27.0rc1) all-reduces the routed output in latent space before the transform is applied, and [the combined output is all-reduced again](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L455-L495) on the late path ([call site](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L742-L749)).
So **every latent-MoE layer at TP>1 or EP>1 issues two tensor-parallel all-reduces per token instead of one.** The function does not exist in v0.26.0.
`NemotronH` is hit because it passes [`fc2_latent_proj` as its `routed_output_transform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L226).

### The fix

Adds an opt-in `reduce_commutative` attribute, **defaulting to `False` so every model that does not set it is byte-for-byte unchanged.**
`NemotronH` sets it when the transform is bias-free **and** unquantised — then `sum_r W x_r == W sum_r x_r`, so reducing once *after* the transform is equivalent and costs one collective instead of two.
Quantisation is judged from the **constructed layer**, not the model-wide `quant_config`: ModelOpt excludes the latent projections, so a quantised Nemotron-3 checkpoint has `quant_config != None` yet still gets an `UnquantizedLinearMethod` here. Testing the model-wide config would disable this on exactly the quantised checkpoints where the regression is largest.

**Kimi K3 is unchanged.** Its [`KimiRoutedOutputTransform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py#L295-L302) wraps an `RMSNorm`, never sets the flag, and keeps both collectives.

<details>
<summary>Interactions checked, and the alternative considered</summary>

- [`skip_final_all_reduce`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L468-L473) asserts against [`_fused_output_is_reduced`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L403-L408), a combine-kernel property this PR does not touch.
- For `NemotronH`, `reduce_results` defaults to `True` — the [`reduce_results=False`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L180) nearby is on *shared_experts*, not the FusedMoE — so the late all-reduce always fires.
- Runtime check on Ultra NVFP4: `quant_config=ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` (non-None) while `fc2_latent_proj.quant_method=UnquantizedLinearMethod`, confirming the layer-level test is the correct one.
- Alternative: [`LatentMoERunner`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py#L52) already fuses to one collective, but it now lives under `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` (moved by [#50678](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50678)) and reads [`transform.norm`/`up_proj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py#L216-L224), which `NemotronH` does not have. Happy to go that way if preferred.

</details>

## Test Plan

4x GB300 (sm_103), stock upstream containers `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0` and `:v0.27.1`, no NCCL env overrides. Public checkpoints [Super BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16) and [Ultra NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4). Every flag exists in both releases, so arms differ only by vLLM version; the `+ this PR` arms patch the same container in place.

```bash
vllm serve <ckpt> --served-model-name nemotron --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 2200 --max-num-seqs 128 \
    --attention-backend FLASHINFER --trust-remote-code --enable-prefix-caching \
    --mamba-cache-mode align --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 16384

aiperf profile --url localhost:8000 --model nemotron --tokenizer <ckpt> \
    --endpoint-type completions --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --streaming \
    --extra-inputs "min_tokens:1000" --extra-inputs "max_tokens:1000" \
    --extra-inputs "ignore_eos:true" --synthetic-input-tokens-mean 1000 \
    --output-tokens-mean 1000 --concurrency $C --request-count $((5*C)) --warmup-request-count 1

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 \
    --model_args model=nemotron,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=<ckpt>
```

## Test Result

### Super BF16, tp4, c=1 — four samples per arm, two server loads each

| arm | ITL (ms) | n | spread | tok/s per user |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.26.0 | 4.07 | 4 | 0.03 | 245.56 |
| v0.27.1 | **4.64** | 4 | 0.02 | 215.73 |
| + this PR | **4.08** | 4 | 0.01 | 245.21 |

Regression **+13.8% ITL / −12.2% tok/s**; with this PR **+0.15% vs v0.26.0**. The v0.26.0 and patched arms ran on *different* nodes and still agree to 0.15%.

### Concurrency sweep, Super BF16 (single run per point)

| ITL (ms) | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.26.0 | 4.08 | 6.23 | 9.88 | 12.18 |
| v0.27.1 | 4.60 | 6.63 | 10.39 | 13.09 |
| + this PR | **4.07** | **6.11** | **9.88** | **12.21** |

Restored at every concurrency. The win shrinks as batch grows — at small batch the collectives are latency-bound so their *count* dominates; at large batch they are bandwidth-bound and the surviving reduce (4096-wide) exceeds the removed one (1024-wide). Not a trade-off at any measured point.

### Ultra NVFP4, tp4, c=1 — confirms the fix on a quantised checkpoint

| arm | ITL (ms) | n | tok/s per user | vs v0.26.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.26.0 | 6.86 | 3 | 145.68 | — |
| v0.27.1 | 7.21 | 2 | 138.71 | +5.0% |
| + this PR | **6.79** | 3 | **147.22** | **−1.1%** |

**v0.27.1 → +this PR is same-node, same-container: −5.8% ITL / +6.1% tok/s.** That is the quantitative claim here.
Read the v0.26.0 row directionally: it is cross-node, and this checkpoint shows ~8% node-to-node variation (v0.27.1 stock measured 7.78 and 7.20 ms on two nodes, stable within each, identical clock/power caps — likely co-tenancy on the 72-GPU chassis). Super BF16 has no such issue, reproducing to 0.03 ms across four nodes.

### Controls

| control | result |
|---|---|
| tp1 negative control (early reduce is TP-gated) | 6.22 vs 6.20 ms, **−0.3% — no difference** |
| node-to-node variation, Super BF16 | 4.63 vs 4.60 ms, **0.65%** |

### Accuracy — gsm8k, 5-shot, greedy, tp4, full 1319 questions

| checkpoint | arm | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| Super BF16 | v0.27.1 | 0.9310 ± 0.0070 | 0.9181 ± 0.0076 |
| Super BF16 | + this PR | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 | 0.9166 ± 0.0076 |
| Ultra NVFP4 | v0.27.1 | 0.9363 ± 0.0067 | 0.9340 ± 0.0068 |
| Ultra NVFP4 | + this PR | 0.9431 ± 0.0064 | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 |

All four deltas within one standard error. Bitwise identity is not expected — moving the all-reduce past a linear map changes float summation order. The Ultra pair covers the quantised case this PR newly enables.

title: [CI] Shard Quantization job into 4 parallel shards (≤30 min target)
author: khluu
body:
## What
Shard the long-pole `Quantization` CI job (single job, ~71–75 min wall in build #83851; 90-day 68/73/75 min) into 4 parallel Buildkite shards so each shard lands ≤30 min. Rebased onto current `main`, preserving the live `device`/`key`/V2 env/torchao 0.17+CUDA13 pin and the `-k 'not test_compressed_tensors_w4a8_fp8'` selection.

## How
- `parallelism: 4` on the `Quantization` step + pytest-shard (`--shard-id=$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB --num-shards=$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB_COUNT`), mirroring the existing `Kernels Quantization Test %N` pattern. No test files moved — shards are disjoint slices of `tests/quantization/` chosen by pytest-shard at collection time.
- Label → `Quantization %N`; per-shard `timeout_in_minutes` lowered 75 → 40. `key: quantization` unchanged so targeted `VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS` launches keep working.

## Validation — targeted build #83897 (only `quantization` + image-build dep, head `579902220`, terminal green)
Per-shard wall (4 shards): **17.03 / 13.43 / 10.52 / 23.10 min** — all four **< 30 min** (max 23.10, ~7 min headroom). min/median/max = 10.52 / 15.23 / 23.10 min. **3.075× critical-path speedup** vs the 71m01s single-job baseline. Sum = 64.07 GPU-min (−6.9 vs the single baseline run → within run-to-run variance; the split does not inflate GPU-minutes).

**Coverage — exact node-ID union.** Shard manifests report 139 / 142 / 115 / 140 selected node IDs; all pairwise intersections are 0 and the union = 536, exactly matching the `collected 537 items / 1 deselected / 2 skipped / 536 selected` line (the single deselection is the intended `-k` filter). No test is dropped or double-run.

**Overhead (Kevin's Q2).** Fixed per-shard repeated cost = job wall − pytest runtime (container/setup re-pay + teardown): **0.90–1.04 min/shard**. That ~1 min/shard is the only thing the split re-pays; cached wheels keep the torchao/conch installs cheap.

## Why 4 shards
~71 min single-job wall with ~1 min/shard fixed overhead → 4-way lands the worst shard at 23.1 min, comfortably ≤30 with headroom for the 68–75 min spread and pytest-shard's nodeid-hash imbalance. 5 shards were unnecessary.

Part of the CI-overhaul sharding pass, one PR per long-pole job.
