title: [Kernel] Add NVFP4 support to the torch linear backend
author: mlazos
body:
## Purpose

Extend the existing `torch` linear backend to ModelOpt W4A4 NVFP4 models on
SM10x (Blackwell).

The adapter reuses vLLM's NVFP4 quantization and layout utilities, calls native
`torch._scaled_mm`, applies the ModelOpt global dequantization scale and bias,
and lets `torch.compile`/TorchInductor select an enabled scaled-GEMM backend.
Existing optimized `auto` candidates retain priority; Torch is placed
immediately before emulation and can be selected explicitly with
`--linear-backend torch`.

This does not add or change a custom operator, schema, meta function, or C++
signature, so the custom-op `torch.library.opcheck()` requirements do not
apply.

## Relationship to #36721

This PR references and overlaps #36721, which first proposed an NVFP4
`torch._scaled_mm` backend. It is submitted as a successor/alternative
for review because #36721 is currently several months behind `main`, marked
`needs-rebase`, and its current diff includes unrelated dependency-file changes
from old merges.

The concrete delta here is:

- a clean three-file change on current `main`;
- integration with the shared `--linear-backend torch` registry rather than
  the former NVFP4-specific environment-variable path;
- current weight/activation padding and swizzled-scale layout handling;
- coverage through the existing eager/compiled NVFP4 model test matrix; and
- paired B200 measurements against current FlashInfer CuTeDSL, including its
  normal heuristic and explicitly autotuned tactics.

If maintainers prefer updating #36721 in place, this branch and its results can
be folded into that PR rather than merged independently.

## PyTorch dependency

The vLLM adapter uses native `torch._scaled_mm` and has no dependency on a
vLLM-specific custom operator. The NVGEMM performance configuration measured
below depends on a separate, not-yet-upstream TorchInductor/CuTeDSL stack. The
adapter remains useful with any scaled-GEMM implementation selected by the
installed PyTorch build.

## Test plan and results

- Rebasing onto current `main` produced no conflicts.
- `pre-commit run --files ...`: passed all applicable hooks, including Ruff,
  formatting, mypy, SPDX, configuration, and import checks.
- A supplemental kernel-level smoke sweep compared Torch and vLLM CUTLASS
  directly on the same randomly generated BF16 inputs while varying M over
  `{1, 10, 32, 128, 150}`, covering single-token decode, batched decode, and
  padded/non-padded row counts. Every case passed
  `torch.allclose(atol=0.1, rtol=0.1)`. These tolerances match vLLM's existing
  NVFP4 kernel correctness test in
  `tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_nvfp4_scaled_mm.py`; the observed
  maximum absolute difference of 0.5 occurred within the combined
  `atol + rtol * abs(reference)` bound. This is supplemental to the exact
  200-example checkpoint-level comparison below.
- With the final native output-scale path and candidate policy, all four Qwen
  projection shapes at M in `{8, 32, 128}` were bit-exact between
  TorchInductor NVGEMM, FlashInfer CuTeDSL, and vLLM CUTLASS: zero differing
  BF16 elements across all 12 cases.
- Actual-checkpoint validation passed with the official
  `nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4` revision
  `bdb54e24298451af785c0ac63c1b485e9b7400a2`. On 200 GSM8K questions
  (five-shot, greedy, 256-token limit), Torch/NVGEMM and vLLM CUTLASS produced
  identical token IDs and text on all 200 examples. Both scored 68.5%
  (137/200), with the same single max-token-limit invalid response. This used
  vLLM's standard prompt builder and scorer from
  `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`.

## End-to-end performance

Environment: GB200 GPU 0, FlashInfer 0.6.17 (`a0a6b019`), 32 input tokens,
128 output tokens, 10 warmups, 30 timed iterations, dummy weights, `-O2`, a
static compile/CUDA-graph size equal to batch size, and detokenization disabled.
These are full prefill-plus-decode latency results from unmodified
`vllm bench latency`; local scripts only orchestrated runs and parsed its JSON.

Torch used NVGEMM with its final scoped candidate policy. FlashInfer's
heuristic column used its normal analytical selection; the tuned column used
vLLM's standard `--enable-flashinfer-autotune` warmup with `mm_fp4` tuning
enabled. Because clocks could not be locked, the table reports paired medians
and uses conservative Torch measurements.

| model | batch | Torch median | FI heuristic | tuned FI | result vs tuned FI |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-32B-FP4 | 8 | **860.692 ms** | 900.905 ms | 880.618 ms | Torch +2.26% |
| Qwen3-32B-FP4 | 32 | **905.629 ms** | 945.227 ms | 942.995 ms | Torch +3.96% |
| Qwen3-32B-FP4 | 128 | **1035.426 ms** | 1128.631 ms | 1050.884 ms | Torch +1.47% |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4 | 8 | **344.201 ms** | 368.667 ms | 357.500 ms | Torch +3.72% |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4 | 32 | **366.533 ms** | 382.388 ms | 377.934 ms | Torch +3.02% |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4 | 128 | **440.583 ms** | 456.486 ms | 448.309 ms | Torch +1.72% |

The Llama B128 cold sample was an obvious shared-machine outlier, so the slower
of two stable cache-hit medians is reported. The second was 427.245 ms.

### Autotuning and startup

| model | batch | Torch candidate timing | Torch cold compile / init | Torch cache-hit compile / init |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen | 8 | 57.64 s | 142.62 / 156.33 s | 0.42 / 24.12 s |
| Qwen | 32 | 46.57 s | 131.45 / 143.87 s | 0.54 / 25.55 s |
| Qwen | 128 | 65.97 s | 150.63 / 162.30 s | 0.36 / 24.74 s |
| Llama | 8 | 59.51 s | 109.57 / 121.34 s | 0.43 / 24.66 s |
| Llama | 32 | 46.80 s | 97.10 / 108.95 s | 0.33 / 21.12 s |
| Llama | 128 | 71.38 s | 121.05 / 133.82 s | 0.36-0.46 / 26.02-26.53 s |

Default heuristic FlashInfer had the lowest cold initialization, approximately
52-97 seconds, but lost all six steady-state comparisons. Tuned FlashInfer
initialized in approximately 52-102 seconds when compiled tactics were already
available and approximately 8-12 seconds when fully cached. Its first empty
Qwen JIT workspace required 162.99 seconds of tactic work and 310.98 seconds of
total initialization. Torch candidate selection was persistent-cacheable and
did not repeat on the cache-hit runs above.

## Caveats

- GPU clocks could not be locked; paired back-to-back medians are used.
- Dummy weights validate shapes, dispatch, and performance, not model quality.
- Results cover two dense ModelOpt NVFP4 models at one input/output length, not
  MoE or broad production shape coverage.
- The local installed FlashInfer attention stack produced incoherent output
  across Torch, CUTLASS, FlashInfer, and emulation linear backends. Accuracy
  validation therefore used Triton attention with BF16 KV cache for both
  compared linear backends, isolating the Torch-versus-CUTLASS linear path.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR includes code and text developed with OpenAI Codex assistance. The
human author is reviewing the full diff and validating behavior, accuracy, and
performance end to end before marking the PR ready for review.

---

- [x] Purpose and relationship to prior work are documented.
- [x] Test commands and current results are documented.
- [x] Batch-size 8/32/128 benchmarks are reported for two models.
- [x] Kernel-level accuracy is validated against two independent backends.
- [x] Complete checkpoint-level quality evaluation.
- [x] No separate docs page is needed: this extends the documented `torch`
  value of `--linear-backend` without adding a CLI option.

title: [KV Connector] Support MooncakeStore with hybrid DCP prefix caching
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose

This PR enables `MooncakeStoreConnector` for mamba hybrid models (e.g., kimi k3) using decode context parallelism (DCP) and fixes a bug where incorrect load keys are constructed under fine-grained prefix hits, causing KV load failures.

### Failure Example

Consider Kimi-K3 with DCP 8 + DSpark and `--prefix-match-unit 128`:

- **Attention block span under DCP:** 1,536 × 8 = 12,288 tokens
- **Mamba block span:** 1,536 tokens
- **Prefix-match unit:** 128 tokens

Reproduction steps:
1. Send a 15,000-token prompt.
2. Clear GPU local cache.
3. Send the same prompt again.

#### Cache blocks stored and keys:

| KV group | Stored state | Store-key hash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full attention | First physical block through 12,288 | `H_12288` |
| Full attention | Second physical block valid through 14,848 | `H_14848` |
| Mamba | Checkpoint at 13,824 | `H_13824` |
| Mamba | Partial state at 14,848 | `H_14848` |

#### Lookup

1. Attention matches its second physical block under `H_14848`.
3. EAGLE rewinds one 128-token unit, reducing the candidate hit length to 14,720.
4. Mamba has no checkpoint at 14,720, so it falls back to `H_13824`.
5. All groups converge to a safe `hit_length = 13,824`.

The existing load path derives the key for a group's partially reused physical block from `hit_length`. As a result, it requested `H_13824` for the attention block, even though that physical block was stored under `H_14848`. Mooncake therefore returned `-704` because the derived key did not exist.

This PR fixes this load failure by recording the precise token boundaries for partial cache store so that subsequent load requests can use the correct load key.

## Test Plan
- Mooncake store unit tests
- E2E Kimi k3 accuracy with dspark and mooncake

## Test Result
- Validated Kimi k3 DCP + dspark produces coherent results with mooncake external cache hits by clearing GPU local cache.
- Validate the same workload which causes `-704` load failure now passes with the fix.

title: [Core][KV Connector] Start async KV loads after the forward launch when no sync loads are scheduled
author: GirasoleY
body:
## Purpose

In scaled P/D setups, decode workers spend significant host time posting NIXL pull requests: e.g. ~5 ms for 9 remote KV requests fanned out across TP8 (= 72 NIXL handles), with occasional spikes to ~48 ms. The expensive part is synchronous descriptor construction (`make_prepped_xfer()` + `transfer()`), which used to run in `pre_forward()` and therefore delayed the GPU model forward.

This PR defers `start_load_kv()` until **after** the current step's forward has been launched whenever the step has no synchronous KV loads, so the host-side load submission overlaps with GPU compute. It trades a negligible TTFT increase for a shorter TPOT.

### How it works

- The scheduler already knows per request whether its connector load is synchronous (`load_async=False`, i.e. the KV is consumed by the current step) or asynchronous. It now aggregates this into a new `SchedulerOutput.has_sync_kv_loads` flag (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, `vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py`).
- On the worker side, both connector call sites honor the flag:
  - `ActiveKVConnector` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/kv_connector.py`): `pre_forward()` calls `start_load_kv()` immediately only when `has_sync_kv_loads` is set; otherwise it marks the load start pending and `post_forward()` runs it after the forward launch. The `no_forward` path still starts any deferred load exactly once.
  - `KVConnectorModelRunnerMixin._get_kv_connector_output()` (`vllm/v1/worker/kv_connector_model_runner_mixin.py`): same ordering — sync loads run before the yield, async loads run in the `finally` after the forward launch, still ordered after any in-flight KV block zeroing.
- No config opt-in: the behavior is automatic. Steps that schedule a synchronous load keep the existing pre-forward ordering; steps with only async loads (or a mix — mixed steps conservatively keep the pre-forward path) benefit from the overlap.

### Connector rework

Because `start_load_kv()` / `wait_for_save()` now reliably run after the forward launch, connectors no longer need the `get_finished()` workaround to get compute/I-O overlap:

- **Mooncake store connector** (`mooncake/store/connector.py`, `mooncake/store/worker.py`): load and store submission moved out of `get_finished()` into real `start_load_kv()` and `wait_for_save()` implementations; `get_finished()` now only reports completed send/recv request IDs.
- **Simple CPU offload connector** (`simple_cpu_offload_connector.py`, `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py`): same move — loads are launched in `start_load_kv()`, stores in `wait_for_save()` (still gated on a compute-done event for the GPU→CPU direction, see #45704 / #39306); `get_finished()` only tracks completed transfer events.
- **LMCache connector** (`lmcache_connector.py`, `lmcache_integration/vllm_v1_adapter.py`): the per-step layerwise state (`current_layer`, `layerwise_retrievers`) was reset in `start_load_kv()`, but the layerwise hooks fire during every forward once metadata is bound — including before a deferred load start. The reset moves to a new `bind_connector_metadata()` hook, with a compat fallback for LMCache engines that predate the hook.
- `KVConnectorBase.start_load_kv()` docstring updated to document the new ordering contract (`kv_connector/v1/base.py`).

### Duplicate-work check

The closest open work is #45211, which offloads NIXL READ submission to a dedicated reader thread and introduces cross-thread queue/locking ownership. This PR is materially different and smaller: it creates no thread and no concurrent connector-state access; posting remains synchronous on the model-runner thread but occurs after the current model forward is enqueued. Searches for deferred `start_load_kv()` / `post_forward()` ordering found no equivalent open PR.

AI assistance was used for trace analysis, implementation support, tests, and preparation of this draft. The author will review the exact public diff before marking it ready for review.

## Test Plan

New/updated unit tests:

- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_has_sync_kv_loads` — covers async-only, sync-only, and mixed steps.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kv_connector.py` (new) — asserts `pre_forward` / `post_forward` / `no_forward` ordering of `start_load_kv` vs `wait_for_save` for both values of `has_sync_kv_loads`.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py` — updated to assert async loads start after the layer hooks rather than assuming the old pre-forward order.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py`, `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py` — updated for the `start_load_kv` / `wait_for_save` split (stores still gated on the compute-done event, loads are not).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_simple_cpu_offload.py` — asserts a remote-prefill (async) load step reports `has_sync_kv_loads == False`.

End-to-end: two-node P/D setup with Qwen3-0.6B, one TP1 producer and one TP1 decoder, 1,319 GSM8K prompts at concurrency 64:

| Metric | Control A2 | Deferred B | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT | 14,471.9 ms | 14,481.5 ms | +9.6 ms (+0.07%) |
| TPOT | 4.940 ms/token | 4.697 ms/token | -0.243 ms (-4.92%) |
| ITL | 4.939 ms/token | 4.701 ms/token | -0.239 ms (-4.83%) |
| E2E | 15,077.9 ms | 15,053.3 ms | -24.6 ms (-0.16%) |

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Reapply group geometry for FlashAttention metadata
author: mgoin
body:
## Summary

Reapply #53002 after it was temporarily reverted in #51718 to unblock the KV-cache layout refactor.

FlashAttention metadata builders use their own attention group as the source of truth for geometry:

- query heads come from the registered attention layers
- KV heads and head size come from the group's `AttentionSpec`
- DFlash shallow-copies `VllmConfig` only to override causality, avoiding validator re-entry

This prevents FA3 AOT scheduler metadata from being planned with target-model shapes when a draft model has a different GQA ratio. It also supports attention layers such as Inkling that expose `num_heads` directly without an `impl` wrapper.

The code is behaviorally unchanged from the reviewed and merged #53002; the only reapplication conflict was the reorganized imports from #51718.

## Why this is not duplicate work

#53002 was merged and then explicitly reverted by commit `e1ae59cfef91` inside #51718 as a stacking workaround. @njhill requested that the fix be reopened after #51718 landed.

The older open drafts #39775 and #50694 target pre-current-main speculative-decoding structure and carry broader schema/routing changes. This patch uses current main's existing per-group layer and KV-spec geometry instead.

Addresses #50851.

## Validation

title: [Feature][Spec] Support disabling trailing prefix-cache block dropping
author: ZeldaHuang
body:
## Purpose
Add an opt-in `disable_eagle_block_drop` speculative-decoding option for
EAGLE-family methods, including dSpark. When enabled, vLLM keeps the trailing
prefix-cache block instead of conservatively dropping it after speculative-model
prefill.

This does not bypass target-model verification. The option can change which
draft tokens are proposed and therefore may affect speculative-token acceptance
rates, but accepted output tokens are still verified by the target model.

## Test Plan

Run an A/B prefix-cache benchmark with the following configuration:

- 2 nodes x 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, tensor parallel size 8
- `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` MXFP4 weights
- [`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark)
- 7 speculative tokens, greedy draft sampling, and `FLASHINFER_MLA`
- 12,288-token shared prefix, 256-token suffix, 160 requests, and concurrency 16

Run the following command on both nodes. Set `NODE_RANK=0` on the API node and
`NODE_RANK=1` on the worker node; only the worker uses `--headless`.

```bash
NODE_RANK=${NODE_RANK:?set NODE_RANK to 0 or 1}
MASTER_ADDR=${MASTER_ADDR:?set MASTER_ADDR to the rank-0 host}
HEADLESS=()
(( NODE_RANK > 0 )) && HEADLESS=(--headless)

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --nnodes 2 \
  --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$MASTER_ADDR" \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --moe-backend auto \
  --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER"}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA","draft_sample_method":"greedy","disable_eagle_block_drop":true}' \
  --enforce-eager \
  "${HEADLESS[@]}"
```

For the default baseline, use the same command but omit
`"disable_eagle_block_drop": true`.

After resetting the prefix cache, send one untimed request to populate the
12,288-token shared prefix, capture the Prometheus counters, and then run the
timed benchmark:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://${MASTER_ADDR}:8000 \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tokenizer moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --num-prompts 160 \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 12288 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 256 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 1 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 1 \
  --disable-shuffle \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 16 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

The shared prefix is aligned to Kimi-K3's 1,536-token Mamba state interval.
With the default behavior, the final aligned block is dropped, so each timed
request re-computes 1,536 additional prompt tokens.

For acceptance rate, run a second A/B on the complete GSM8K test split. The
official `openai/gsm8k` test parquet was exported one-to-one to ShareGPT JSON
because the runtime image does not include the optional Hugging Face `datasets`
dependency. Both variants use all 1,319 questions in the same order, a maximum
output length of 256, concurrency 16, temperature 0, and EOS handling enabled.
Run one untimed request before capturing the Prometheus counters, then run:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://${MASTER_ADDR}:8000 \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tokenizer moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name sharegpt \
  --dataset-path gsm8k-test-sharegpt.json \
  --sharegpt-output-len 256 \
  --num-prompts 1319 \
  --no-oversample \
  --disable-shuffle \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 16 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```


## Test Result


All timed prefix-cache requests succeeded (`160/160`) in both variants.

| Metric | Default drop | `disable_eagle_block_drop=true` | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cached tokens per request | 10,752 | 12,288 | +1,536 |
| Locally computed tokens per request | 1,792 | 256 | -1,536 |
| Total cached tokens | 1,720,320 | 1,966,080 | +245,760 |
| Total locally computed tokens | 286,720 | 40,960 | -245,760 |
| Request throughput | 12.720 req/s | 25.556 req/s | +100.91% |
| Mean TTFT | 1,222.00 ms | 604.88 ms | -50.50% |
| P50 TTFT | 1,225.40 ms | 566.73 ms | -53.75% |
| P90 TTFT | 1,227.04 ms | 746.72 ms | -39.14% |

All GSM8K requests also succeeded (`1,319/1,319`) in both variants. Timed-pass
Prometheus counter deltas matched the benchmark summary:

| GSM8K metric | Default drop | `disable_eagle_block_drop=true` | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Draft steps | 84,278 | 84,436 | +158 |
| Draft tokens | 589,946 | 591,052 | +1,106 |
| Accepted tokens | 239,307 | 240,658 | +1,351 |
| Acceptance rate | 40.564% | 40.717% | +0.153 pp (+0.376% relative) |
| Mean acceptance length | 3.84 | 3.85 | +0.01 |

No acceptance-rate regression was observed on the complete GSM8K test split;
the no-drop variant increased acceptance by 0.153 percentage points. GSM8K's
independent prompts produced a 0% prefix-cache hit rate, so this result checks
for a general acceptance regression rather than the long-prefix cache-hit path.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.

</details>

title: [Kimi K3][Kernel] Support DS conv-state layout in fused KDA decode kernel
author: gcanlin
body:
## Summary

The fused KDA decode kernel (`ops.fused_kda_decode`) previously required the SD conv-state cache layout, so any deployment that pins `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS` — required for NIXL point-to-point state transfer in P/D-disaggregated serving — silently bypassed the fused path and fell back to the multi-op Triton decode chain for all 69 KDA layers of the model.

This PR supports both physical cache layouts by dispatching to separate SD- and DS-specialized fused-kernel instantiations. Keeping each layout's address calculation compile-time constant avoids the extra integer instructions and register pressure caused by runtime inner strides. Both layouts now use the fused path (in-proj GEMM → fused KDA decode → out-proj GEMM per layer and step), and numerics are bit-identical for identical inputs.

Update (head `0e67480f`): per review feedback, the layout specialization is now expressed as two integer conv-state inner strides (channel, tap) as non-type template parameters instead of a layout enum. The generated device code is unchanged — see the parity data below.

## Motivation

- Deployment reality: production K3 serving pins `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS` (NIXL PD transfer), and several recent fixes treat DS as the supported production layout. Under DS, the fused kernel was never used.
- Measured cost of the fallback chain on B200 (TP8 shape, H_local=12, K=V=128): 1.16-1.58x slower than the fused kernel depending on batch, plus ~3x launch count in the per-layer decode chain (8-9 vs 3 kernels).

## Performance

### DS specialized fused path vs Triton fallback

B200, CUDA graph replay, `H_local=12`, `K=V=128`, 50 warmup iterations, and 300 measured iterations. Values are the average of two median runs. The fallback uses the Triton gated RMSNorm kernel rather than its eager PyTorch decomposition.

| Decode batch size | Triton fallback (us) | Specialized fused (us) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 9.170 | 5.500 | 1.67x |
| 8 | 10.480 | 5.610 | 1.87x |
| 32 | 16.865 | 9.170 | 1.84x |
| 64 | 24.920 | 16.000 | 1.56x |
| 128 | 50.625 | 35.195 | 1.44x |
| 256 | 90.890 | 71.075 | 1.28x |
| 512 | 171.455 | 140.055 | 1.22x |

### SD regression and DS specialization check

B200, CUDA graph replay, `H_local=12`, `K=V=128`, 50 warmup iterations, and 300 measured iterations. Values are the average of two median runs with reversed execution order, using binaries produced by the same build tree.

| Decode batch size | SD baseline | SD dynamic strides | SD regression | SD specialized | SD vs. baseline | DS dynamic strides | DS specialized | DS improvement |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.250 us | 5.400 us | +2.86% | 5.250 us | 0.00% | 5.530 us | 5.490 us | 0.72% |
| 8 | 5.340 us | 5.460 us | +2.25% | 5.340 us | 0.00% | 5.790 us | 5.610 us | 3.11% |
| 32 | 8.850 us | 8.960 us | +1.24% | 8.850 us | 0.00% | 9.285 us | 9.170 us | 1.24% |
| 64 | 15.670 us | 16.475 us | +5.14% | 15.670 us | 0.00% | 16.815 us | 16.000 us | 4.85% |
| 128 | 35.570 us | 39.670 us | +11.53% | 35.570 us | 0.00% | 39.515 us | 35.190 us | 10.95% |
| 256 | 71.675 us | 76.245 us | +6.38% | 71.650 us | -0.03% | 75.905 us | 71.150 us | 6.26% |
| 512 | 140.925 us | 149.695 us | +6.22% | 140.945 us | +0.01% | 148.600 us | 140.030 us | 5.77% |
| **Geometric mean** | — | — | **+5.04%** | — | **-0.00%** | — | — | **4.75%** |

Compile-time specialization fully recovers the original SD performance and improves DS performance by up to **10.95%**. For the representative H_local=12 kernel, runtime strides increase register use from 64 to 72 registers per thread, while both specialized variants use 64. The additional kernel instances increase the extension binary by 392 KB (0.95%).

### Stride-NTTP parity check (review feedback, head `0e67480f`)

The layout enum was replaced by two integer strides as template parameters, per review feedback. The layout is still detected at launch from the conv_state strides and resolved inside the head-count dispatch (SD = `<1, 3 * H * 128>`, DS = `<kConvWidth - 1, 1>`), so both strides remain compile-time constants.

Codegen parity proof: a normalized `cuobjdump` comparison of all 128 `kda_decode_fusion_many_heads_kernel` instantiations in `_C_stable_libtorch` shows **bit-identical SASS** between the enum version and this rewrite (identical REG/STACK/SHARED, zero spills), so measured performance is identical by construction.

B200, CUDA graph replay, `H_local=12`, `K=V=128`, 50 warmup / 300 measured iterations, fused-path per-layer latency:

| Decode batch size | SD enum (us) | SD stride-NTTP (us) | Delta | DS enum (us) | DS stride-NTTP (us) | Delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.02 | 4.99 | -0.6% | 5.25 | 5.25 | 0.0% |
| 8 | 5.31 | 5.31 | 0.0% | 5.58 | 5.58 | 0.0% |
| 32 | 8.82 | 8.82 | 0.0% | 9.16 | 9.16 | 0.0% |
| 64 | 15.64 | 15.66 | +0.1% | 15.98 | 15.98 | 0.0% |
| 128 | 35.38 | 35.37 | -0.03% | 35.07 | 35.04 | -0.09% |

Production-shaped check (69 per-layer state buffer sets, B=128, DS): 37.04 us/layer fused vs 49.33 us/layer Triton chain (1.33x).

An earlier stride-NTTP attempt was measured to regress 7-18%, but that attempt bundled unrelated changes; this clean rewrite matches the enum version exactly.

### E2E: 2 nodes x 8xB200, TP8+PP2, FP8 KV cache, DS layout, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` cudagraphs

`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 128 input / 512 output tokens,
128 requests, max-concurrency 64, temperature 0, and no profiler. Each side used
one full-load pilot followed by two measured runs. Both sides used the same vLLM
nightly image (`sha256:95bed119f39e...`); the candidate overlaid this PR at
commit `40459de9d3`. The current head `0e67480f` emits bit-identical kernel SASS (verified above), so these numbers carry over; a fresh E2E run on it will follow.

| Metric | Baseline (fallback chain) | This PR (fused kernel) | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 2069.73 tok/s | 2149.26 tok/s | **+3.84%** |
| Total token throughput | 2587.16 tok/s | 2686.57 tok/s | **+3.84%** |
| Benchmark duration | 31.66 s | 30.49 s | **-3.70%** |
| Mean TPOT | 29.73 ms | 28.59 ms | **-3.84%** |
| Median TPOT | 29.99 ms | 28.77 ms | **-4.08%** |
| Mean ITL | 29.68 ms | 28.54 ms | **-3.84%** |
| Mean TTFT | 632.44 ms | 629.93 ms | -0.40% |
| Median TTFT | 614.08 ms | 614.34 ms | +0.04% |

Every measured run completed all 128 requests with zero failures. The
output-throughput spread was 0.46% for the baseline and 0.53% for this PR, so
the 3.84% improvement is well above the observed run-to-run variation. Both
nodes logged `Fused KDA decode kernel (conv+KDA+norm) is enabled.` for the
candidate, with no errors or runtime JIT-compilation warnings.

Acc:

```
| Tasks | Version | Filter           | n-shot | Metric       |   |  Value |   |     Stderr |
| ----- | ------: | ---------------- | -----: | ------------ | - | -----: | - | ---------: |
| gsm8k |       3 | flexible-extract |      5 | exact\_match | ↑ | 0.9689 | ± |     0.0048 |
|       |         | strict-match     |      5 | exact\_match | ↑ | 0.9697 | ± |     0.0047 |
```

### Kernel trace verification

With the DS layout pinned, the patched serving stack runs `kda_decode_fusion_many_heads_kernel` for every KDA decode layer (5076 calls in the profiled window, 7.2us/call average, 1.26% of window kernel time); the decode-side `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel`, `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` triton kernels and the separate gated-norm kernel disappear from the decode hot path (prefill-only `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` and FlashKDA prefill remain, as intended). In the baseline trace the fallback trio costs ~3.5% of kernel time.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py -k test_fused_kda_decode_correctness -v
```

`10 passed, 51 deselected`; the targeted cases cover both SD and DS layouts, H=12/24/48/96, output normalization, and lower-bound decay. Re-run at head `0e67480f` (stride-NTTP rewrite): `10 passed, 51 deselected`.

Server (as used for the E2E numbers above):

```bash
# on two 8xB200 nodes (rank0/rank1)
VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS vllm serve /path/to/Kimi-K3 \
  --served-model-name Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.84 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1} --master-addr <rank0-ip> --master-port 29512 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \

```

title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 token offset overflow in fused SiLU block quant
author: canlahlah
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53390.

`silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` used a 32-bit `token_idx` when computing
global input and output row offsets. For sufficiently large token batches,
`token_idx * (2 * hidden_size)` overflowed `INT32_MAX`, wrapped the input
pointer, and caused an illegal CUDA memory access.

Widen `token_idx` to `int64_t`, matching the sibling activation kernels. This
keeps the row-offset arithmetic in 64 bits without widening unrelated
thread, group, or dimension indices.

Add a focused regression test at the first overflowing token count. The test
launches the standalone op, synchronizes to surface CUDA faults, and compares
the previously overflowing final row with the same input processed by a safe
one-token invocation.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR references #53390. A keyword search for
`silu_and_mul_per_block_quant overflow` found no open PR addressing this
integer-overflow bug. The open Triton implementation PR #39641 concerns a
different feature and does not fix this CUDA kernel's row addressing.

## Test plan

Completed locally:

```text
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

Completed on RunPod:

```text
CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_silu_mul_block_quant.py::test_silu_block_quant_int32_offset_overflow \
  -v -s
```

With the kernel source restored from `upstream/main`, the test fails at CUDA
synchronization as expected:

```text
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

With this PR applied, the identical command passes:

```text
1 passed, 14 warnings in 3.07s
```

The full affected kernel test file also passes:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_silu_mul_block_quant.py \
  -v

331 passed, 14 warnings in 148.16s (0:02:28)
```

Model evaluation is not applicable: this changes pointer-index width only and
does not alter model numerics for previously valid offsets.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to inspect the affected kernels and precedent fixes,
refine the implementation scope, and review the regression test. The human
contributor reviewed every changed line and is responsible for running the GPU
validation and defending the change end-to-end.

title: [Perf] Split xdrope_positions H2D copy into per-row transfers
author: JasonKeyiL
body:
## Summary

PR #51841 identified a subtle host-run-ahead killer: `copy_(..., non_blocking=True)` on a **strided view of a pinned buffer** silently falls back to a pageable intermediate, and pageable H2D synchronizes the stream regardless of `non_blocking`. That PR fixed `mrope_positions`. Eight lines below the fix, `xdrope_positions` has the identical setup and the identical bug.

Layout is the same:

```python
# gpu_model_runner.py, buffer allocation
self.mrope_positions  = self._make_buffer((3, self.max_num_tokens + 1), ...)
self.xdrope_positions = self._make_buffer((self.uses_xdrope_dim, self.max_num_tokens + 1), ...)
```

Both use the trailing `+1` column to stay non-contiguous for `torch.compile`, so `cpu[:, :N]` is a strided view of the pinned staging area.

Before:

```python
elif self.uses_xdrope_dim > 0:
    self.xdrope_positions.gpu[:, :total_num_scheduled_tokens].copy_(
        self.xdrope_positions.cpu[:, :total_num_scheduled_tokens],
        non_blocking=True,
    )
```

After (same shape as the `mrope_positions` fix in #51841):

```python
elif self.uses_xdrope_dim > 0:
    for row in range(self.xdrope_positions.gpu.shape[0]):
        self.xdrope_positions.gpu[row, :total_num_scheduled_tokens].copy_(
            self.xdrope_positions.cpu[row, :total_num_scheduled_tokens],
            non_blocking=True,
        )
```

Each row is contiguous within the pinned allocation, so the transfer stays on the pinned-async path.

## Scope

- Only affects models that opt into XD-RoPE (`uses_xdrope_dim > 0`) — HunYuan-VL is the current in-tree consumer.
- No API change, no behavior change for non-XD-RoPE models.
- Mirrors an already-merged fix; there is no new pattern to review.

## Test plan

- [x] `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` — all hooks pass (ruff / mypy-3.10 / typos / DCO / SPDX).
- [ ] `nsys` before/after on HunYuan-VL to confirm the H2D block disappears the same way it did for mrope in #51841 — I don't have HunYuan-VL local; happy to attach a trace if someone with the model can run it, or I'll pull one on cloud.

## Related

- #51841 — the original mrope fix and full explanation of the pinned/strided/pageable interaction.
- #43107 — `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK` CI infrastructure that motivated this line of work.

AI assistance was used to locate the missing counterpart to #51841's mrope fix; every changed line was reviewed and the buffer-layout equivalence to `mrope_positions` was verified.

title: [Feature] Add first-class KV hints request envelope for programmatic KV management
author: karen-sy
body:
## Purpose

Please see RFC #53421 for context and related works.

This PR introduces a first-class, orchestrator-agnostic `KvHints` request envelope for vLLM V1. It:

- Defines typed `KvHintsEnvelope` and `KvHintAction` representations in Python and Rust.
- Propagates optional hints through `AsyncLLM`, `EngineCoreRequest`, and the scheduler `Request`.
- Propagates hints through the native Rust `GenerateRequest` path.
- Preserves Python/Rust MessagePack wire compatibility.
- Exposes a public HTTP/gRPC field.

This PR establishes the envelope and request plumbing only. It does not define or execute individual KV-hint actions. However, it establishes KVCR (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53624) as a possible secondary tier KV manager which can natively ingest this KV hint envelope contract and own the definition/execution of supported KV-hint actions.

## Test Plan

title: [Bugfix] Keep grid dims for XD-RoPE models on a prefix-cache hit
author: drakosha
body:
## Purpose

HunyuanOCR (any XD-RoPE model) takes the whole server down on the second request whose prompt hits the prefix cache:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 1755, in _init_xdrope_positions
  req_state.xdrope_positions = xdrope_model.get_xdrope_input_positions(...)
File "vllm/model_executor/models/hunyuan_vision.py", line 865, in get_xdrope_input_positions
  t, h, w = image_grid_thw[image_index]
IndexError: list index out of range
```

`EngineCore encountered a fatal error` follows and the API server shuts down, so one bad request ends the process.

### Root cause

`strip_covered_mm_data()` drops the tensor data of multimodal items whose placeholder span is fully inside the prefix-cache-covered region. Its own docstring names the exception:

> M-RoPE models are the exception: the worker computes positions for the whole prompt from the CPU-side metadata fields (e.g. grid dims), so those are kept.

XD-RoPE models compute positions the same way (`get_xdrope_input_positions()` reads `image_grid_thw`), but the scheduler only ever passes `uses_mrope`. So for HunyuanVL the grid dims are stripped, `MultiModalFeatureSpec.gather_kwargs()` skips the feature because its data is `None`, and `image_grid_thw` arrives empty while `prompt_token_ids` still contains the `image_start` token. The loop runs over `image_start_indices` and indexes past the end.

Instrumented `get_xdrope_input_positions()` on two identical requests, printing what actually arrives:

```
XDROPE-DBG starts=1 grids=1 features=1 data_none=0   <- first request, ok
XDROPE-DBG starts=1 grids=0 features=1 data_none=1   <- prefix-cache hit, IndexError
```

`image_grid_thw` is already marked `keep_on_cpu=True` in `hunyuan_vision.py`, so nothing else is needed: the metadata just has to survive the strip.

### Fix

Extend the existing exception to XD-RoPE: `strip_covered_mm_data()` takes `uses_xdrope`, `NewRequestData.from_request()` passes it through, and the scheduler derives it from `model_config.uses_xdrope_dim > 0`.

## Test Plan

**Minimal reproducer** (a blank image is enough, the trigger is the repeated prompt):

```bash
vllm serve tencent/HunyuanOCR --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 16384
python repro.py    # sends the same image+prompt three times
```

```python
import base64, io, json, urllib.request
from PIL import Image
buf = io.BytesIO(); Image.new("RGB", (320, 120), "white").save(buf, "PNG")
b = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()
for i in range(3):
    body = {"model": "tencent/HunyuanOCR", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 16,
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64," + b}},
                {"type": "text", "text": "What is in the image?"}]}]}
    req = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions",
                                 json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120)); print(i, "ok")
    except Exception as ex: print(i, type(ex).__name__, str(ex)[:70])
```

Unit test: `tests/v1/core/test_output.py::test_strip_covered_mm_data_xdrope`, mirroring the existing M-RoPE case.

## Test Result

Same image, same commit, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.10 --max-model-len 16384`, H200:

| | request 0 | request 1 | request 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | ok | HTTP 500, EngineCore dead | connection refused |
| after | ok | ok | ok |

Real workload: reading a document page as 52 separate crops through one server (many crops share a size, so their prompts are token-identical) went from dying on crop 10 to all 52 completing.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` also avoids the crash, which is what pinned the cause.

## Note on #50429

#50429 fixes a different `IndexError` at the same line (duplicate `image_start` tokens) and is not a fix for this one. Its loop change from `range(len(image_start_indices))` to `range(num_images)` would make this path silently skip the XD-RoPE computation when `num_images == 0` and leave plain `arange` positions for the image tokens, turning a crash into wrong output. Worth landing both: that PR guards the token-count side, this one keeps the grid dims from being stripped in the first place.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Only create draft_id_to_target_id when draft vocab differs
author: drslark
body:
## Purpose

We found a bug that makes full-vocab EAGLE3 drafters (`draft_vocab_size == target vocab_size`, e.g. `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA` and `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-Eagle3`) run a redundant vocab-remapping step after the lm_head, degrading decode performance with no effect on the output.

`compute_logits` in `llama_eagle3.py` has a fast path and a slow path. Full-vocab drafts were meant to take the fast path, but erroneously they never do. On H20, the slow path's `logits_new[:, targets] = logits` is `5x` slower than a plain copy:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle3.py::Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM
def compute_logits(self, hidden_states):
    logits = self.logits_processor(self.lm_head, hidden_states)
    if self.draft_id_to_target_id is None:
        # full-vocab draft: logits are already in target vocab space
        return logits

    # reduced-vocab draft: scatter into target vocab space
    base = torch.arange(self.config.draft_vocab_size, device=logits.device)
    targets = base + self.draft_id_to_target_id
    logits_new = logits.new_full(
        (logits.shape[0], self.config.vocab_size), float("-inf")
    )
    logits_new[:, targets] = logits
    return logits_new
```

In `__init__`, even when `draft_vocab_size == target vocab_size`, the parameter is still initialized — it is never `None`, so the slow path is always taken:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle3.py::Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM
def __init__(self, ...):
    ...
    self.draft_id_to_target_id = nn.Parameter(
        torch.zeros(self.config.draft_vocab_size, dtype=torch.long),
        requires_grad=False,
    )
    ...
```

After reading https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/18488 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/18909, we believe full-vocab drafts were always meant to take the fast path.

This is corroborated by `qwen3_dspark.py` and `qwen3_dflash.py`, which already handle it correctly:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dspark.py::Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM
def __init__(self, ...):
    ...
    target_vocab_size = vllm_config.model_config.get_vocab_size()
    if self.config.draft_vocab_size != target_vocab_size:
        self.draft_id_to_target_id = nn.Parameter(
            torch.zeros(self.config.draft_vocab_size, dtype=torch.long),
            requires_grad=False,
        )
    else:
        self.draft_id_to_target_id = None
    ...
```

So we follow dspark/dflash: create the parameter only when the draft vocab differs. Full-vocab drafts then take the `is None` fast path and return the lm_head logits as-is (bit-identical); reduced-vocab drafts are unaffected.

## Test Plan

1. Added a print to the slow path of `compute_logits` and ran a full-vocab EAGLE3 draft, before and after the change.
2. Added a unit test for the conditional: `pytest tests/model_executor/test_eagle_quantization.py -k d2t -v`
3. End-to-end speculative-decoding acceptance run on an H20 GPU with `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-Eagle3` (`num_speculative_tokens=3`), using 80 MT-Bench prompts passed through the chat template, before and after the change, measuring the acceptance rate.

## Test Result

1. Before the change, the print fires on every call; after the change, it never fires — the slow path is confirmed not taken, and the slow operation is avoided.
2. The unit test passes; the two full-vocab cases fail on unpatched code, so it guards the regression.
3. Before the change:

   ```
   total_num_output_tokens: 20480
   num_drafts: 12294
   num_draft_tokens: 36882
   num_accepted_tokens: 8171
   mean acceptance length: 1.66
   --------------------------------------------------
   acceptance at token 0: 0.41
   acceptance at token 1: 0.18
   acceptance at token 2: 0.08
   ```

   After the change:

   ```
   total_num_output_tokens: 20480
   num_drafts: 12294
   num_draft_tokens: 36882
   num_accepted_tokens: 8171
   mean acceptance length: 1.66
   --------------------------------------------------
   acceptance at token 0: 0.41
   acceptance at token 1: 0.18
   acceptance at token 2: 0.08
   ```

   Every counter matches exactly across both runs, confirming the change is output-neutral for full-vocab drafts.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code, GLM-5.3) and reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Model] Fix KV cache layout and optimize Dots3 NOTE Omni encoders
author: KurodaKanbei
body:
## Purpose

This PR improves the correctness and efficiency of Dots3 NOTE Omni inference.

The changes include:

- Force the Dots3 NOTE padded sparse attention backend to use the `BLHNC` KV-cache layout so mixed DSA/MLA/SWA cache page sizes are represented correctly.
- Optimize the vision encoder by:
  - preparing sequence metadata once per forward pass;
  - keeping grid metadata on CPU to avoid unnecessary device synchronization;
  - precomputing RoPE cosine and sine tensors once for all vision layers;
  - skipping redundant `nn.Linear` initialization before checkpoint loading.
- Optimize the audio encoder by:
  - batching log-Mel spectrogram computation;
  - batching audio segments across inputs;
  - limiting each speech encoder micro-batch to 16 segments to control temporary memory usage.

These are internal model implementation changes and do not modify the user-facing API or model configuration.

This PR does not duplicate existing work: no existing PR covers the same combination of the Dots3 NOTE KV-cache layout fix and vision/audio encoder optimizations.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the implementation. The submitter reviewed every changed line and validated the behavior end to end.

title: [Core] Enhance cpu<->gpu sync checking to include paged async copies
author: njhill
body:
The CPU<->GPU sync checking added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44800 / https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43107 makes use of pytorch's `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode` function.

However this does not catch stalls due to "non-blocking" tensor copies to or from non-pinned host memory, where an implicit copy is made to a staging buffer. This also includes copies from pinned tensors which have non-dense layouts.

This PR extends the sync checking mode by monkeypatching the relevant pytorch methods to check for this.

title: [Bugfix][Models] Register sleep-managed runtime buffers
author: Ronald1995
body:
## Purpose

Part of #53343. Split from #53344.

Level-2 sleep discards weight-tagged allocations and reloads parameters. Plain model tensor attributes are neither checkpoint parameters nor discoverable through `named_buffers`, so their semantic values can be lost even though their virtual addresses remain stable.

## Changes

Register static runtime tensors as non-persistent model buffers for:

- Gemma3n runtime scales;
- Conformer relative positional encodings;
- Voxtral mel filters;
- ERNIE 4.5 VL visual-token tensor caches.

The buffers remain excluded from `state_dict` while participating in the existing level-2 sleep buffer save/restore path.

Adds an allocation-level level-2 reproducer and a parameterized end-to-end regression test covering every model changed by this PR through its real top-level model:

- FireRedASR2 for the shared Conformer encoder;
- Gemma3n;
- Voxtral;
- ERNIE 4.5 VL.

Each case runs `generate`, locates the target runtime tensors by model type and `getattr`, saves their values and addresses, saves the dummy model parameters, enters level-2 sleep, wakes the weight mappings normally, reloads the parameters, wakes the KV cache, and runs `generate` again. The snapshot helper deliberately does not use `named_buffers`, so the same test can run on both the pre-fix and post-fix branches.

The FireRedASR2 Hugging Face override is invoked more than once during config loading and can receive a generic `PreTrainedConfig` without the repository-specific `audio_encoder_conf` extension. The test now creates the complete minimal encoder configuration when that field is absent instead of unconditionally updating it.

No test-side memory poisoning is performed; the test exercises the real physical-page contents returned by the CUDA driver. It verifies immediately after weights wake-up that every target tensor keeps both its value and virtual address, then verifies that generated tokens and selected-token logprobs are unchanged.

OpenPangu and the Static Sink Attention issues exposed by its test have been moved to follow-up PR #53696.

## Dependency

Independent. Can merge directly into `main`. PR #53696 depends on this PR for the shared sleep-mode test framework.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_sleep_mode_tensor_ownership.py
pytest -q tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py -k level2_discards
```

Changed files pass Ruff, `git diff --check`, and Python compilation. The end-to-end cases require a supported Linux CUDA runtime; the configured remote CUDA development container was unavailable during this update. The local Python test environment is also missing the repository's `tblib` dependency, so executable pytest coverage is left to CI.

title: BugFix(PCP): use persistent input buffers for PIECEWISE CUDA graphs
author: pisceskkk
body:
## Summary

Fix PIECEWISE CUDA graph execution with PCP by using persistent PCP input buffers during graph capture and sizing graph dispatch from the largest real rank-local PCP batch before padding.

## Implementation

- Decoder graph capture now uses `PCPManager.input_buffers` when PCP is active, ensuring capture and runtime partitioning share persistent `input_ids`, `positions`, and `is_padding` buffers.
- `GPUModelRunner` obtains the graph dispatch size from `PCPManager.get_num_tokens_for_dispatch()`.
- The CUDA graph dispatcher selects the smallest captured token size covering that rank-local maximum.
- The selected `BatchExecutionDescriptor.num_tokens` is passed to PCP partitioning as `padded_num_tokens`, which determines rank-local gather-index and mask capacity.
- A shared `_iter_rank_chunks()` implements rank chunking for both dispatch-size calculation and segment construction.
- PCP raises `ValueError` when `padded_num_tokens` is smaller than the largest rank-local batch.

Representative dispatch mappings:

| Workload | Global tokens | Rank-local maximum | Capture size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PCP2 prefill | 8 | 4 | 4 |
| PCP2 prefill | 7 | 4 | 4 |
| PCP2, 3 decodes | 3 | 3 | 4 |
| PCP2, 3 decodes + prefill | 11 | 7 | 8 |
| PCP4, 2 decodes + prefill | 11 | 5 | 8 |

## Validation configuration

- NVIDIA H20 GPUs
- GLM-4.7-Flash
- TP1 + PCP4 + EP4

title: [Performance] Optimize Dots3 NOTE runtime
author: KurodaKanbei
body:
## Purpose

This PR optimizes the Dots3 NOTE runtime paths for both the language model and vision encoder.

The main changes are:

- Enable Model Runner V2 by default for `Dots3NoteForCausalLM`.
- Capture the MTP speculator prefill and decode paths with CUDA Graphs under Model Runner V2.
- Fuse the MTP embedding lookup with the embedding/hidden-state RMSNorm path when the vocabulary is replicated.
- Enable uniform-batch CUDA Graph support for the custom MLA metadata builder.
- Share the dense MLP weight-padding implementation between the backbone and MTP weight loaders.
- Reuse a single vision RMSNorm implementation.
- Replace direct fallback messages with `warning_once` logging.

These changes preserve the existing model behavior and weight-loading format.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/attention.py \
  vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/model.py \
  vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/mtp.py \
  vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/vision.py \
  vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/vision_attention.py
```

Additional validation included:

- Python compilation checks for the modified modules.
- Numerical checks for the fused embedding/RMSNorm paths.
- Full-graph TorchInductor compilation of the fused operations.
- End-to-end startup and inference with an FP8 Dots3 NOTE checkpoint on H100 GPUs using DP + EP and MTP.
- Verification that `Dots3NoteForCausalLM` selects Model Runner V2 by default.
- Verification that CUDA Graph capture completes for the target model and MTP speculator prefill/decode paths.
- Torch profiling covering one prefill iteration and ten decode iterations after warmup and JIT compilation.
- End-to-end multimodal evaluation with image inputs.

## Test Result

- All relevant pre-commit checks passed.
- The fused embedding/RMSNorm implementations matched the reference outputs.
- The backbone and MTP paths compiled successfully with TorchInductor.
- The service log confirmed `Using V2 Model Runner`.
- Target-model and MTP speculator CUDA Graph capture completed successfully.
- No unexpected graph breaks, eager fallbacks, unsupported-operation warnings, or recompilations were observed in the compiled backbone and MTP regions.
- The FP8 service started successfully on H100 GPUs with DP + EP and MTP enabled.

The compiled runtime benchmark improved output throughput by approximately 9.47% and reduced latency by approximately 8.68%.

On the single-request profiling workload with 512 input tokens and 64 output tokens, enabling Model Runner V2 produced the following additional improvements:

- Average GPU decode-step duration decreased from 22.34 ms to 18.92 ms.
- Average worker `execute_context` duration decreased from 12.50 ms to 7.61 ms.

The remaining graph-external GPU work was limited to the LM head and sampling/metadata operations, totaling approximately 0.57 ms per steady-state decode interval.

title: [Kimi-K3][Perf] Prefetch ll_bf16 router weights for M=1
author: mingg26
body:
## Purpose

Reduce the Kimi-K3 single-token AttnRes-to-router latency by loading the first
`ll_bf16` router-weight tiles before the incoming PDL wait.

The optimized kernel is selected from the runtime `M` shape:

- `M == 1`: use the weight-prefetch PDL specialization;
- every other `M`: use the original `ll_bf16` kernel unchanged.

The earlier AttnRes and latent-MoE-tail changes have been removed. AttnRes is
now provided by #54261, which is included in the rebased `main` base.

## Duplicate-work check

Open-PR searches for `ll_bf16 PDL` and `router weight prefetch` found no PR
implementing this optimization. This PR is intentionally limited to the
`ll_bf16` shape dispatch and does not duplicate #54261.

## Implementation

- Add an optional dot-product path that preloads the first eight static
  weight tiles before `griddepcontrol_wait()`.
- Keep separate compiled-kernel caches for the original and prefetch variants.
- Dispatch the prefetch variant only for `hidden_states.shape[0] == 1`.
- Add a unit test covering the `M=1` versus `M>1` dispatch boundary.

## Validation

Hardware: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, CUDA graph, cold L2, SM clock locked at 1980 MHz
for performance measurements.

Tests:

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py -v`
  - `136 passed`
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files ...`
  - passed
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-format --files ...`
  - passed
- Incremental `_C_stable_libtorch` build and install against rebased `main`
  - passed

The full kernel suite covers dot-product and split-K shapes, single-token
production shapes, numerical edge cases, deterministic output, CUDA graphs,
and dispatch/cache behavior.

## Performance

Timed region: merged native AttnRes followed by `ll_bf16`, including the PDL
handoff. L2 is flushed before the graph replay; AttnRes then produces the
activation consumed by `ll_bf16`.

For `M=1`, `N in {256, 384, 896}`, and AttnRes block counts `{1, 4, 8}`, all
nine tested production combinations were neutral or faster:

- median speedup range: `+0.26%` to `+20.13%`;
- mean speedup range: `+2.20%` to `+19.05%`;
- `M=1, N=896, blocks=8`: `16.288 us -> 14.240 us` median (`+14.38%`).

A forced prefetch run at `M=4, N=896, blocks=8` regressed from
`16.288 us -> 16.320 us` median (`-0.20%`) and `-1.30%` by mean. Therefore the
production dispatch deliberately keeps the specialization at `M == 1`.

No model-output evaluation was needed because this changes kernel scheduling,
not the mathematical operation; the full numerical suite passed. The previous
TP8 serving result from the broader pre-cleanup diff is not claimed here.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for diff cleanup, rebase support, test execution, and
benchmark analysis. The human submitter must review every changed line and be
able to defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Test][Qwen3-VL] Cover compiled DeepStack input contract
author: maithilijoshi20
body:
## Summary

Adds a regression test for the Qwen3-VL DeepStack input contract when the decoder is compiled.

#43617 fixed a correctness problem where compile warmup could call the decoder with `deepstack_input_embeds=None`. That lets the compiled graph specialize to the no-DeepStack path, so a later multimodal request can ignore real DeepStack features. The fix keeps the argument present and uses zero-backed tensors when there is no payload.

This test covers that sequence:

1. Run the compiled decoder with an empty, zero-backed DeepStack payload.
2. Add a known nonzero payload.
3. Verify that the next compiled call uses it.

It fails if the old `num_tokens == 0` early return is brought back.

## Scope

This PR does not fix #53516. That report shows a task-specific quality difference when the old guard is restored, but restoring it also reintroduces the compiled-graph correctness bug fixed by #43617. The test here protects the stable input contract while the underlying quality question is investigated separately.

## Related work

- #43617 introduced the stable zero-backed tensor contract.
- #49397 keeps that contract for vision-enabled models while skipping DeepStack buffers when the vision tower itself is unavailable.

## Testing

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/compile/test_deepstack_input_contract.py -q` `1 passed`
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_vl_mrope.py -q` `96 passed`
- `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check tests/compile/test_deepstack_input_contract.py` passed
- `.venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check tests/compile/test_deepstack_input_contract.py` passed

I also ran Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct on the public `stop_sign` and `cherry_blossom` assets. With the stable tensor contract, compiled and eager runs produced the same text. Restoring the old guard changed both outputs, including the reported people count for `stop_sign`.

title: [Kimi K3][Kernel] Enable low-latency decode GEMM dispatch on SM100
author: gcanlin
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

The Kimi-K3 BF16 decode GEMM selector (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py`) is gated behind `_is_sm103()` with a single table measured on B300, so on **B200 (SM100)** every decode projection falls back to cuBLAS — even though neither backend is SM103-specific (the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM has no arch gate; `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` only requires SM90+).

This PR adds a separately measured SM100 table (`KIMI_K3_PROJECTIONS_SM100`, 24 shapes) and routes by compute capability. Because winner sets genuinely differ between the two parts — in backend, in covered token counts, and sometimes in which CuTe config wins — the tables are not merged into one. Only the two runtime entry points (`try_low_latency_gemm`, `enable_kimi_k3_low_latency_gemm`) route per capability; `select_kimi_k3_backend` keeps reading the SM103 table, so existing selector behavior/tests are untouched. No change on B300.

### Why not simply reuse the SM103 table on SM100

Measured answer (per-cell three-way, B200, CUDA-graph replay, all candidates numerically validated vs cuBLAS first):

| shape | M | cuBLAS | SM103 tuned cfg | best fresh cfg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7168x8448 | 1 | 26.19 | **20.81** | 22.60 |
| 20480x7168 | 1 | 51.28 | **43.05** | 44.01 |
| 40960x7168 | 2 | 96.37 | **83.66** | 86.03 |
| 3072x7168 | 1 | 10.26 | 6.16 | 6.17 (same cfg) |
| 3584x7168 | 1 | 12.31 | 8.21 | 8.21 (same cfg) |
| 6288x7168 | 2 | 14.42 | 18.44 | – |
| 16896x7168 | 1 | 40.57 | 36.87 | **35.71** |

Reusing outright would *both* leave wins on the table (several shapes) *and* regress known cells (6288x7168 M2..4 routes a config that loses to cuBLAS on B200; 3584x7168 wants a different backend: dsv3 on B300, CuTe M1..3 on B200; 7168x384 wins on neither). Instead each SM100 entry takes the better of the two measured candidates, and the TP16 shapes gained B200 coverage along the way (768x7168 +40–59%, 1152x1536 +60%, 3216x7168 +50%, 4224x7168 +33%).

### Relationship to #53202

flashinfer `mm_bf16(backend="auto")` was measured as a fourth candidate on every cell: on SM100 it does **not** reach the tuned entries (at most +4% vs cuBLAS), i.e. the hand-tuned tables are not redundant with it on this part — the missing SM100 perf-parity evidence that #53202's "Known gaps" section asks for before dropping the tables.

## Benchmarks

Kernel-level: B200 (SM100), CUDA-graph replay (matching the production decode mode), numeric check vs cuBLAS per candidate, same ≥5% inclusion threshold as the SM103 table. Wins up to **+60%** (q_b_proj 2304×1536, M=8); lm_head 40960×7168 **+25%** at M=1.

E2E: Kimi-K3 on 16×B200, TP8×PP2, final merged table (`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, in=1024/out=256, `--ignore-eos`; gains concentrate at low concurrency because c=64 moves decode batches past the M=1..16 dispatch range):

| concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | this PR (tok/s) | Δ throughput | Δ mean ITL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1  | 88.0   | 96.6   | **+9.8%** | **−10.1%** |
| 4  | 293.7  | 299.7  | **+2.0%** | **−4.0%** |
| 16 | 789.3  | 805.4  | **+2.0%** | −1.2% |
| 64 | 1683.8 | 1682.6 | −0.1%     | +0.0% (noise) |

Accuracy (lm-eval-harness GSM8K, full test set 1319 samples, 5-shot, temperature=0, seed=0, against the TP8×PP2 B200 server running this PR) — exact-match on par with the stock image:

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9750|±  |0.0043|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9757|±  |0.0042|
```

(lm-eval-harness `local-chat-completions`, `--apply_chat_template`, gen kwargs `temperature=0.0`, `max_tokens=1500`, `until=["Question:", "</s>", "<|im_end|>"]`.)

## How was this patch tested

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k "sm100 or table or selector or instantiation or build_plan or installation"
```

**20 new SM100 tests** (`EXPECTED_SELECTIONS_SM100` selector table, table↔plan consistency, capability routing via `_low_latency_table`) plus the dsv3 instantiation check now spans both tables; `test_installation_requires_bf16_sm103` pins the full capability probe so it stays hardware-independent. All pass on B200.

Known follow-ups (not in this PR): CuTe config sweep for remaining borderline cells; `routed_expert_up_proj` (7168,3584) residual-path configs for SM100 (not measured); dsv3 variants of the TP16 shapes not measured on B200.

title: [XPU] Ensure unquantized linear weight is N-contiguous
author: zufangzhu
body:
- The XPU unquantized GEMM path uses torch.nn.functional.linear, which performs better when the (N, K) weight is N-contiguous.  
- Keep the weight layout bydefault due to the "non-deterministic constructs such as atomic operations" in oneDNN matmul   . But add VLLM_XPU_FORCE_N_CONTIG_WEIGHT to force relayout weight for performance opt. 

## Tests
Qwen3-8B linear shapes, bfloat16, TP=1. Speedup = `t(default K-contig) / t(N-contig)`;
**> 1 means the relayout is faster**.

| Layer (K, N) | K vs N | B60 decode (M=32) | B60 prefill (M=256) | B70 decode (M=32) | B70 prefill (M=256) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qkv_proj` (4096, 6144) | K < N | **0.46** | 0.73 | 0.98 | 1.01 |
| `gate_up_proj` (4096, 24576) | K < N | **0.54** | 0.92 | 0.99 | 1.05 |
| `o_proj` (4096, 4096) | K = N | 0.98 | 1.03 | 1.03 | 1.65 |
| `down_proj` (12288, 4096) | K > N | 1.11 | **2.00** | 1.06 | **1.68** |

The `K > N` guard is what makes this safe: on B60, K < N weights lose up to ~2x in the
decode regime; on B70 they are merely neutral. `K > N` is the only condition that wins
on both SKUs and is independent of `M` — which matters because the weight layout is
fixed once at load time and cannot be re-selected per forward, while `M` is dynamic.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse SWA q/kv RMSNorm and q FP8 group quant for DeepSeek-V4
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Purpose On the ROCm path of DeepSeek-V4, every decode step's SWA token-insertion pipeline runs: 1. vLLM's Triton `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` (norms the q-lora and kv latents to bf16). 2. aiter per-1x128 dynamic quant of the bf16 q-lora (input quant of the block-scaled FP8 `wq_b` GEMM). 3. the same quant a second time in the indexer's `wq_b`, which shares the q-lora with the attention layer. This PR replaces 1+2 with a single aiter HIP kernel (`fused_qk_rmsnorm_group_quant`): it RMSNorms both latents (fp32 accumulate) and quantizes the q latent (per-1x128, fp32 scales) in one pass, so: - the hot path drops from 2 kernel launches to 1. - the bf16 q-lora write+read round-trip disappears; quantization now reads the fp32 accumulator directly (single rounding, equivalent-or-better precision). - the attention `wq_b` and the indexer `wq_b` both consume the pre-quantized `(qr_fp8, qr_scale)` pair and skip their own input quant (removes a third quant launch on the long-context path). - kv stays bf16 and feeds the existing fused insert kernel (`fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert`) unchanged. > [!NOTE] > The change is scoped to the ROCm/AITER path and does not change the CUDA or XPU implementations. --- **Before fusing** (4µs 839ns + 4µs 719ns + 4µs 719ns = 14 µs 277 ns): **After fusing** (4µs 919ns, **2.90x** faster): ## Test Plan - Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload. - Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset. ## Test Result > [!NOTE] > The tests below are executed on AMD MI350X GPU, so the performance could be slightly lower than the MI355X baseline, so I verified this PR with an A/B test compared with vLLM `main` on the same machine. ### Benchmark Concurrency | Version | Output token throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | 1 | Main | 56.29 | — | 418.93 | — | 17.33 | — | 1 | This PR | 56.70 | 0.73% ↑ | 462.05 | 10.29% ↑ | 17.16 | 0.98% ↓ | 4 | Main | 181.61 | — | 514.31 | — | 20.95 | — | 4 | This PR | 182.49 | 0.48% ↑ | 517.49 | 0.62% ↑ | 20.84 | 0.53% ↓ | 16 | Main | 530.80 | — | 806.76 | — | 28.30 | — | 16 | This PR | 535.25 | 0.84% ↑ | 808.93 | 0.27% ↑ | 28.05 | 0.88% ↓ | 64 | Main | 1062.02 | — | 1780.55 | — | 57.27 | — | 64 | This PR | 1067.39 | 0.51% ↑ | 1778.38 | 0.12% ↓ | 56.98 | 0.51% ↓ | ### Accuracy Test Full GSM8K evaluation on this change (1,319 examples): |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9431|± |0.0064| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9431|± |0.0064| Both results exceed the required 94% threshold. ---

title: [Core][Feat] Pluggable KVCacheConfigBuilder for platform/model-specific KV cache planning
author: wangxiyuan
body: RFC: #62100 ## Purpose Follow-up to #42309. vLLM picks the KV cache grouping of every model with one heuristic in core (`get_kv_cache_groups()`). New hybrid models, drafters, cache precisions and platforms keep needing plans that this heuristic does not give, so each new model changes core, and vllm-ascend monkey-patches core planning to use its own DSV4 plan. This PR adds an **experimental** pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder`. Core keeps one planning flow and checks every plan. A platform selects a builder that decides grouping and placement, and a model can return its own groups. The interfaces can change, in particular when #61452 changes the KV cache group data structure. ## Changes - **`KVCacheConfigBuilder`** (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_config_builder.py`) with two decisions: `get_kv_cache_groups(vllm_config, kv_cache_spec)` and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, num_blocks)`. A platform selects the class with `Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls`; the default is `DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder`. - **Core owns the planning flow.** `get_kv_cache_configs` is a core function, not a builder method: merge specs, group, check, project onto PP stages, apply the block-count override, auto-fit and admission, place, and converge ranks. Platforms make only the two decisions above. - **Bytes per block come from the builder's placement.** Core places one block and reads its single device backing, so a platform with its own placement does not compute memory separately. A placement with several device allocations overrides the private, transitional `_get_pool_bytes_per_block` (until worker-driven allocation, #42449). - **Model-owned grouping.** A model class can implement `SupportsKVCacheGrouping.get_kv_cache_groups` (a classmethod). Priority: a platform builder that overrides grouping (it reaches the model hook only through `super()`), then the model hook, then the default heuristic. - **Every grouping is checked**, from any source, on the planning path and both profiling paths: each layer is in exactly one group. - **Profiling** passes `num_blocks` directly instead of temporarily setting `num_gpu_blocks_override`. Bug fixes: - PP projection now keeps `host_resident`, `role` and `enable_kv_transfer` on partially projected groups. - `num_gpu_blocks_override` no longer inflates the one-block probe (it gave `500 * C` instead of `C` bytes per block). - HiSparse keeps the direct bytes computation, because probing its placement would size the host pool before auto-fit. A model hook combined with HiSparse raises a clear error. ## Users - vllm-ascend#18359 moves the Ascend plans into an `AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder` and removes most of its planning patches. - wangxiyuan/vllm#2 (stacked on this PR): model hooks for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Kimi-K3 (Kimi-K3 + DSpark: 5 groups instead of 20), and golden grouping plans per model. Not a duplicate: #58638 (#58207, #58380) improves the default heuristic for drafters. That work is complementary; this PR adds the extension point and does not change the default grouping. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py ``` ## Test Result 83 passed (head `6283b0aca3`, GB200 node). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. The authors reviewed every changed line. Co-Authored-By: Yifan Qiao Co-Authored-By: Mengqing Cao Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

title: [Perf][Kernel] Initialize NVFP4 padding in quant kernel
author: LopezCastroRoberto
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #49775 and #45739.

#45739 used a separate `torch.zeros` allocation to initialize padded NVFP4 scales. This PR moves the required initialization into the CUDA quantization kernel, allowing the wrapper to safely use `torch.empty` and avoid the extra zero-fill launch.

It also:

- Preserves a specialized fast path for unpadded output.
- Retains programmatic dependent launch support.
- Adds sentinel-based regression coverage for padded rows and columns.

This does not duplicate #47587, which covers FlashInfer’s TRT-LLM 8x4 layout. This PR targets vLLM’s built-in 128x4 swizzled kernel.

## Test Result

Validated on NVIDIA B300 with CUDA 13.4 (`sm_103a`):

title: [Distributed] Add opt-in FlashInfer PCIe IPC all-reduce backend
author: lucifer1004
body:
# [Distributed] Add opt-in FlashInfer PCIe IPC all-reduce backend

## Purpose

On PCIe-only multi-GPU boxes (e.g. RTX 6000 Pro, SM120 — no NVLink), the default
NCCL RING_LL all-reduce dominates small-message decode collectives. This PR adds
an opt-in `flashinfer-ipc` custom all-reduce backend that rides FlashInfer's
single-node IPC symmetric-memory implementation (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4393):

- `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER_PCIE_IPC=1` selects it, mirroring the existing
  `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` / `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM` env-based
  backend selection; NCCL behavior is unchanged unless the env is set (off by
  default).
- Graph warmup prepares all capture buckets on every rank before capture, and
  the autotune warmup window is kept rank-symmetric so no rank can fall back to
  NCCL mid-capture while another stays in IPC.
- Safe dispatch: falls back to the existing custom all-reduce / NCCL path when
  the IPC buffer cannot be allocated or the message shape is unsupported.
- Lifecycle: registers/frees IPC buffers with the communicator lifecycle.

## Relationship to existing work

- #47979 (our earlier SM120 PCIe serving stack PR) covers PCIe-safe comms via
  symmetric memory in general; this PR is the FlashInfer IPC backend split out
  as a standalone, self-contained piece. It does not duplicate #50941
  (hierarchical island-aware allreduce, a different algorithm) or #52555
  (custom-AR max-size tuning for TP=2, orthogonal knob).

## Test plan

- `pytest tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_pcie_ipc_all_reduce.py` — 8 passed
  (buffer lifecycle, dispatch fallback, capture-bucket preparation).
- `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD` — all hooks pass
  (ruff, mypy-3.10, etc.).
- E2E on 4x RTX 6000 Pro (SM120), DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP4 serving with
  DSpark: server bring-up, CUDA-graph capture, and generation all pass with the
  backend enabled.

## Notes

AI assistance (Kimi Code / OpenAI Codex) was used in preparing this change;
every line was reviewed and tested by the submitting human.

title: [XPU] Route grouped_topk to the fused _moe_C kernel on XPU
author: mfylcek
body:
## Purpose

vllm-xpu-kernels ships a fused grouped_topk (noaux_tc) kernel registered into the same `_moe_C::grouped_topk` op that CUDA uses, but both gates guarding it test `is_cuda()`, so XPU always fell back to the eager decomposition.

This PR routes grouped_topk to the fused _moe_C kernel on XPU and registers a fake (meta) implementation for _moe_C::grouped_topk, which previously had only device kernels and no meta kernel, so torch.compile could not trace through it resulting in graph breaks (not XPU-specific — adding the meta implementation helps on CUDA too).

Affects: every DeepSeek-V3-style (noaux_tc) MoE model — DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2.6, Trinity-Nano, Ling/Bailing, GLM-4.5, Longcat-Flash
