title: [Metrics][KV Offload] Fill vllm:kv_offload_config_info with the CPU cache capacity
author: amirfr3
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

GPU KV-cache capacity is observable. `num_gpu_blocks` and `kv_cache_size_tokens`
are labels on `vllm:cache_config_info`. The CPU offload tier exports only usage
(`vllm:kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` and the read/write variants) and no
capacity. The size is not recoverable externally either, because it depends on
`blocks_per_chunk`, page alignment, and whether a replicated layout deduplicates
the per-worker copies. All three are connector-internal.

This PR fills `vllm:kv_offload_config_info` with the CPU cache facts. The gauge,
the label rendering and the emission call come from #56867, the generic
config-info PR. The CPU side adds four labels:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cpu_num_chunks` | Chunk slots in the tier. Chunks, not GPU blocks. |
| `cpu_blocks_per_chunk` | GPU blocks in one chunk: the chunk-to-block conversion factor. |
| `cpu_kv_cache_size_bytes` | Size of the tier in bytes: `cpu_num_chunks` times the page-aligned bytes of one chunk. |
| `cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens` | KV tokens the tier holds for requests of `max_model_len` tokens. It is computed like the GPU `kv_cache_size_tokens`. |

No name carries a tier index, so a CPU fact reads the same under
`CPUOffloadingSpec` and under `TieringOffloadingSpec`. The gauge is per engine.
Sum across the `engine` label for the instance total. The Info shape is the
extensible container the reviewers of #49307 asked for.

### `cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens`

The tier is content-addressed (`OffloadKey = block_hash + group_idx`), so there is
no per-request allocation to divide by, and no analogue of the GPU
`max_concurrency`. The token capacity depends on the request length. The label
fixes the length at `max_model_len`, as the GPU `kv_cache_size_tokens` does:

```
chunks_per_request       = sum over groups of min(cdiv(max_model_len, tokens_per_chunk), cap)
cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens = num_chunks * max_model_len // chunks_per_request
```

Both `tokens_per_chunk` and `cap` are per group. `tokens_per_chunk` is
`blocks_per_chunk * tokens_per_block` of that group. `cap` is the chunks of that
group the tier keeps for one request: `None` for attention that reaches back
without a bound, `cdiv(window, tokens_per_chunk)` for a sliding window, and 1 for
Mamba. A capped group holds a fixed number of chunks however long the request
grows.

Two values cross the `OffloadingConfig` boundary for this:
`OffloadingGroupConfig.sliding_window_size_in_chunks` and
`OffloadingModelConfig.max_model_len`. `build_offloading_config` computes the first
one with `get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks`. The connector scheduler now reads the
same field, so the value has one source. Both new fields have a default, so a
spec that does not read them does not change.

`None` covers two cases: a `max_model_len` of 0, and no KV cache group at all. Zero
chunks reports `0`, not `None`, because zero slots hold exactly zero tokens.

`CPUOffloadingInfo.from_config(config, num_chunks, kv_bytes_per_chunk)` builds the
labels. The CPU spec builds it once as `cpu_info`, and passes it to the manager
as the last keyword argument `info`. `TieringOffloadingSpec` inherits `cpu_info`
and passes it to its primary tier.

### Why this estimate

The GPU side answers the same question in the same three steps.
`get_kv_cache_capacity` (`kv_cache_utils.py:2291`) builds `kv_cache_size_tokens`
like this:

```
num_blocks_per_request = sum over groups of cdiv(max_memory_usage_bytes, page_size_bytes)
max_concurrency        = num_blocks / num_blocks_per_request
kv_cache_size_tokens   = int(max_concurrency * max_model_len)
```

Sum the per-request cost over the groups, divide the pool by that sum, multiply by
the request length. The formula above does the same, with chunks in place of blocks.

The per-group cap matches too. `SlidingWindowSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes` calls
`max_admission_blocks_per_request`, which bounds a windowed group by its window
(`kv_cache_interface.py:716`). `MambaSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes` charges one page
for each request in the default cache mode (`kv_cache_interface.py:922`).

Both numbers report an upper bound, because both assume that every request reaches
`max_model_len`. An operator reads the two side by side.

### Worked examples

Every number below is pinned in `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_capacity.py`.
`held` is `min(cdiv(max_model_len, tokens_per_chunk), cap)`.

**Qwen3-8B**, TP 2, 1 full group, `tokens_per_chunk` 256, 4500 slots,
`max_model_len` 36864: `chunks_per_request = 144`, and `4500 * 36864 // 144 = 1152000`.

**gemma-3-27b-it**, TP 2, 1 full group and 6 sliding-window groups, window 1024
tokens, so `cap` is 4. `tokens_per_chunk` 256, 4000 slots, `max_model_len` 36864:

| Groups | cap | cdiv(36864, 256) | held | subtotal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 full | None | 144 | 144 | 144 |
| 6 SWA | 4 | 144 | 4 | 24 |

`chunks_per_request = 168`, and `4000 * 36864 // 168 = 877714`.

**granite-4.0-h-small**, TP 2, 1 full group and 9 Mamba groups, `tokens_per_chunk`
528, 8000 slots, `max_model_len` 36864:

| Groups | cap | cdiv(36864, 528) | held | subtotal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 full | None | 70 | 70 | 70 |
| 9 Mamba | 1 | 70 | 1 | 9 |

`chunks_per_request = 79`, and `8000 * 36864 // 79 = 3733063`.

**A hybrid with one group of each kind**, `tokens_per_chunk` 256, 4000 slots,
`max_model_len` 36864, window 1024 tokens: `chunks_per_request = 144 + 4 + 1 = 149`,
and `4000 * 36864 // 149 = 989637`. If all three groups grew with the request, the
answer would be 341333. The caps carry most of the number on a hybrid model.

### Relation to #56867, #49307 and #51615

**#56867** adds `vllm:kv_offload_config_info` and the mechanism that fills it, with
no real value behind it. This PR supplies the CPU values. #56867 has landed
(`775fefa804`), and this branch is rebased on top of it through current `main`.

**#49307 (@yanburman)** became this same metric after review (@orozery: bundle
static tier information into one Info metric following `vllm:cache_config_info`),
emitted once at engine startup. That needed a new public `get_config_info()`
connector API, an `EngineCoreReadyResponse` field, a runtime-populated
`KVTransferConfig` side-channel and a `record_config_info()` chain. All of those
edit code outside `kv_offload/` and `offloading/`, which reviewers objected to.
**#51615 (@nilig, draft)** emits `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_capacity_tokens` through the
existing connector-stats path.

This PR takes the metric shape of #49307 and the emission mechanism of #51615. The
cost is that the metric is absent (no series, never `0`) until the first scheduler
step.

## Test Plan

- **Unit tests** - 15 new test functions, over four sections of the change.

    - **The capacity arithmetic** - `test_capacity.py` calls
      `CPUOffloadingInfo.from_config` and covers the four model shapes above, a
      pure-Mamba model, an empty tier, and the two cases with no token scale.
    - **The tier sizing** - the labels of a real `CPUOffloadingSpec` report the
      numbers the spec resolved, under tensor parallel, under a replicated
      layout, and with a second group that shares the slots.
    - **The config boundary** - `build_offloading_config` fills the two new
      fields, `sliding_window_size_in_chunks` on the group and `max_model_len` on
      the model.
    - **The tiering pass-through** - the primary tier reports the four labels
      on the `0:primary` series, the tiering spec gives it `cpu_info`, and the
      tiering spec declares exactly the names the manager fills.

    Files: `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_capacity.py` is new and holds 2 (11 cases).
    `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py` holds 10,
    `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py` holds 2, and
    `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py` holds 1.
    `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py` gains no test. Its
    drift guard now pins the four CPU names next to the secondary tier names.
    `test_scheduler.py` only gives its mock group the new field.

    ```bash
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload \
      tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector \
      --ignore=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_offload_integrity.py -q
    ```

- **Lint** - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`.

- **Documentation** - `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md` adds three rows to the
  "Info Metric Labels" table of #56867, one for each new label.

- **Model evaluations: not applicable.** Metrics only. The PR touches no scheduling,
  no KV-cache placement, no transfer behavior and no model output.

- **GPU and data-parallel sanity runs** - four servers on the pokprod cluster, one
  H100 80 GB per engine: the merge base and this branch with `Qwen3-8B` as an
  A/B pair, then this branch with `TieringOffloadingSpec` and the `example`
  secondary tier (`Qwen3-0.6B`), with `--data-parallel-size 2` (`Qwen3-0.6B`),
  and with `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, a model with sliding-window and full-attention
  layers. Each server answers 96 completion requests in three rounds.

- **Not verified.** A real hybrid Mamba model stays untested.

## Test Result

At `87e4b690cf`, on macOS (no CUDA, no `/dev/shm`):

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_config`, `test_factory`, `test_capacity`, `test_tiering_offloading`, `test_scheduler` | `626 passed, 1 skipped` |
| Full offload suites (command above) | `1341 passed, 86 failed, 16 skipped` |
| Same suites at the previous branch tip | `1353 passed, 86 failed, 16 skipped` |

- The same 86 tests fail before and after. All are in `cpu/test_gpu_worker.py` (32)
  and `cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py` (54), which need CUDA and `/dev/shm`.
- The pass count is 12 lower only because the PR removed the old capacity tests.
- `test_offload_integrity.py` is excluded. It cannot import `StoreTrigger`, which
  also fails without this PR's changes.
- The skipped test in `test_factory.py`
  (`test_tiering_spec_passes_the_cpu_facts_to_the_primary_tier`) needs `/dev/shm`,
  so it runs in CI.

**GPU runs**, on the pokprod cluster, one H100 80 GB per engine, at `87e4b690cf`.
The image is a nightly build of an ancestor of the merge base. The package tree
holds the exact merge-base checkout, and the branch files sit on top of it. A
server of the merge base runs as the control.

The control and this branch, `Qwen3-8B`, `cpu_bytes_to_use` of 10 GiB,
`blocks_per_chunk` of 4, `max_model_len` 8192: the same store counter
(44694503424 bytes), the same query counter (306541), the same round-3 texts
(32 of 32), and no server errors on either side. The PR changes no transfer
behavior.

The labels, each equal to the value computed by hand from the model shape:

| Server | `cpu_num_chunks` | `cpu_blocks_per_chunk` | `cpu_kv_cache_size_bytes` | `cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B, 10 GiB, 4 blocks/chunk | 1137 | 4 | 10730078208 | 72768 |
| Qwen3-0.6B, tiering, 2 GiB, block 16 | 1170 | 1 | 2146959360 | 18720 |
| Qwen3-0.6B, DP 2, 2 GiB, 4 blocks/chunk | 292 | 4 | 2143289344 | 18688 |
| gpt-oss-20b, 10 GiB, 4 blocks/chunk | 6826 | 4 | 10736369664 | 430143 |

- Qwen3-8B: 2 × 2 bytes × 36 layers × 8 KV heads × 128 head dim × 16 tokens per
  block × 4 blocks per chunk.
- The tiering server also publishes the `1:example` series with
  `example_info="67"` and an empty value on every CPU label.
- Both data-parallel engines report the same labels, each sized from the full

title: [NIXL][PCP] Report replicated-PCP ranks > 0 as done sending instead of hiding them
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Purpose

With replicated KV under PCP only PCP rank 0 takes part in NIXL transfers, so `NixlConnector` on ranks > 0 cleared `done_sending` and `get_finished_count()` was lowered to `TP x PP` so the scheduler only waited for rank 0.

That breaks as soon as `NixlConnector` is wrapped in a `MultiConnector` with a sibling that saves on every rank (e.g. `OffloadingConnector`):

- `MultiConnector.get_finished_count()` returns `None` when any child returns `None`, so the `KVOutputAggregator` expects `world_size` finishes per request;
- `MultiConnector` records an extra async save per request and only reports it finished once *every* child on that worker has — and NIXL on ranks > 0 never does.

Requests therefore never finish sending, their blocks are never freed and the prefill engine stalls at `Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: N reqs` with the KV cache full. Observed with GLM-5.2-FP8 PCP8 prefill, `MultiConnector = NixlConnector(kv_producer) + OffloadingConnector(TieringOffloadingSpec)`: 14/35 requests completed at concurrency 16, then nothing.

Fix: ranks > 0 report the requests they are asked to send as finished as soon as the connector metadata arrives, and `get_finished_count()` is back to `world_size`. Rank 0 still reports only when the consumer has read the blocks, so the aggregate completes exactly when it did before.

## Test Plan

title: [Kernel] Fuse DeepEP-v2 decode globalize+align into one launch
author: elvircrn
body:
Fuses the DeepEP-v2 INDEXED cudagraph-decode metadata chain (`_globalize_recv_topk_idx` + `moe_align_block_size` + `count_and_sort_expert_tokens`) into a single CUDA launch for the Humming path.

`recv_topk_idx` holds **local** expert ids; the kernel bins by local id (align/sort) while writing back the global id, and reads `num_recv` on-device from `psum[-1]` so it is CUDA-graph safe. Sizing by local (not global) experts shrinks the sentinel/`expert_ids` region by ~`ep_size` under EP. The fused kernel also produces the optional scatter index used by Humming for larger EP batches.

The fused path is selected for CUDA Humming INDEXED experts when DeepEP-v2 defers globalization during CUDA-graph decode. Other paths keep the standalone globalization and alignment behavior.

## Numbers

H200, EP32, INDEXED decode — fused vs the 3-kernel chain, measured before the October 6 rebase:

| tokens | speedup |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1.23x |
| 8 | 1.14x |
| 32 | 1.16x |
| 64 | 1.36x |
| 128 | 1.67x |
| 256 (n=8192) | 2.01x |

## Testing

After the October 12 rebase onto upstream commit `c599b5971`: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the six changed Python files; Apple `clang-format` 21 `--dry-run --Werror` passed on the changed CUDA/C++ files; `git diff --check` passed. `git range-diff` confirmed that the functional patch is unchanged apart from adapting paths to upstream's new `csrc/moe` layout. CI then found a stale `libtorch_stable/torch_utils.h` include in the moved CUDA source; commit `52d7e1c15` changes it to `torch_utils.h`, matching the other MoE CUDA files. The corrected include and formatting were checked locally, but the CUDA build needs to rerun in CI. The pinned `clang-format` and mypy hooks passed on the prior October 7 base but were not rerun here. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_globalize_align_block_size.py -v` could not run on the macOS rebase host. The test includes correctness cases for the optional scatter index.

Pending on CUDA hardware: `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` rebuild, the pytest run, and a model evaluation (for example gsm8k) with the fused path active. The kernel originated from a validated standalone prototype; the measurements above have not been repeated on the rebased code.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate — no open PR fused this chain when the PR was created (`gh pr list --search "globalize align"`).
- AI assistance (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex) was used. Human review of the rebase resolution and GPU validation are pending.

## Purpose
Add fused CPU sampling kernels (Gumbel-max + greedy argmax) to replace the expensive default random sampling pipeline (softmax → exponential → div → argmax) on CPU backends.

title: [Benchmark] Warn on warm prefix cache for random serve runs
author: zupengwang
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52884.

`RandomDataset` is deterministic for a fixed `--seed`. Repeating the same
`vllm bench serve` workload against a server with a warm prefix cache can
therefore reuse most prompt tokens and materially inflate the reported
throughput.

This PR:

- reads the exact prefix-cache query and hit counters immediately before and
  after the timed benchmark, aggregating counters across engine labels;
- warns when a random-dataset run observes a prefix-cache hit rate of at least
  1%;
- skips the warning when metrics are unavailable, counters reset, or the
  dataset is not random; and
- documents how to reset the cache, vary `--seed`, or use
  `vllm bench sweep serve` for parameter sweeps.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR currently references #52884. #46938 is
complementary: it reports prefix-cache hit rate in benchmark output, while this
PR detects a deterministic random-dataset measurement hazard and gives users
actionable guidance. This PR does not add or change benchmark result fields.

## Test Plan

- `pytest -q tests/benchmarks/test_serve_warm_prefix_cache.py`
- `git diff --check`
- Repository pre-commit hooks for Ruff, formatting, Markdown, spelling, SPDX,
  and mypy.
- End-to-end RTX 4090 run with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, 128 random
  requests, 1024 input tokens, 64 output tokens, concurrency 32, and seed 0:
  run the same workload twice against one prefix-caching server, then reset the
  prefix cache and run it once more.

## Test Result

- Unit test: `8 passed, 14 warnings in 2.69s`.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `typos`,
  `check-spdx-header`, and `mypy-3.10`: passed.
- Cold E2E run: 0 / 131072 prefix-cache hits, 15.027 requests/s,
  16349.78 tokens/s, and 1014.26 ms mean TTFT.
- Repeated warm run: 129024 / 131072 hits (98.44%), 29.783 requests/s,
  32403.75 tokens/s, and 107.44 ms mean TTFT. The patched client emitted the
  expected `98.4% prefix cache hit rate` warning. Request throughput increased
  by about 1.98x, reproducing the measurement hazard.
- After `POST /reset_prefix_cache` returned `{"success":true}`, the next run
  had a +131072 query delta, zero hit delta, and emitted no warm-cache warning.

The GPU E2E was run on base `080a66a69`. The branch was then fast-forwarded to
`8d301f075`; the intervening upstream commits did not touch these files, the
reviewed file hashes remained unchanged, and the unit test was rerun on the
current base. A full CUDA source rebuild was not run because this change only
touches Python, tests, and documentation, and the RTX 4090 node does not have
`nvcc` installed.

No model implementation or model output behavior changes, so model evaluation
is not applicable.

This change was developed with AI assistance. The human author reviewed every
changed line and reviewed the test and benchmark evidence above before
authorizing this Draft PR.

title: [Elastic EP] Support Model Runner V2
author: almogtavor
body:
## Summary

Support Elastic Expert Parallel scaling with Model Runner V2.

MRV2 now uses a correctness-first scaling sequence:

```text
prepare while serving
-> close admission
-> drain already-admitted requests
-> commit the topology change
-> reopen admission on success
```

The implementation:

- Removes the user-facing reserved warmup slot configuration and its HBM cost.
- Restores full scheduler and request-state capacity.
- Makes MRV2 drain before Elastic EP commit while preserving MRV1 behavior.
- Rejects new requests inside `check_admission` while scaling and registers every parallel-sampling child before the first engine send so a drain sees the whole fanout; existing streaming continuations may finish during drain.
- Keeps drain failures recoverable by reopening admission.
- Fails closed on commit failure because distributed topology may be partially mutated; commit remains one-shot.
- Isolates MRV2 warmup request state, redirects block-table writes to the null block, suppresses EPLB during warmup, and restores state afterward.
- Preserves dynamic DP rank/size behavior, EPLB registration/mapping updates, deferred async EPLB handling, and CUDA graph release.

## Validation

- Local focused admission/drain suite after the lock removal: `52 passed`.
- OpenShift CUDA environment, before the lock removal: admission plus MRV2 serving-state tests: `55 passed`.
- H100 serving-state tests, before the warmup context manager moved to `EPLBController`: `3 passed`.
- Ruff formatting and mypy 3.10: passed.
- Full 4-GPU Elastic EP integration was attempted with NIXL and Ray 2.56.1. The test reached model download but was blocked by the OpenShift `/workspace` PVC quota (`Errno 122: Disk quota exceeded`), after the initial Ray PATH issue was resolved.
- 4-GPU validation of the current revision is pending because cluster access is unavailable.

## Scope

This PR intentionally does not add commit retries or recovery semantics after a potentially partial distributed topology mutation. The existing Elastic EP fault-tolerance behavior is unchanged.

AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Enable a4w4 flydsl kernels for KimiK3
author: ppalanga
body:
## Summary

- When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1` (the existing Kimi-K3 recipe toggle), route SiTU MXFP4 routed experts through AITER's **a4w4** flydsl kernels (`afp4_wfp4_fp4`, `fp4q`) instead of the previous **a8w4** path (`afp8_wfp4_fp8`, `fp8q`, `_gui_` interleave).
- vLLM sets `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=1` at init and clears any legacy `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` override (AITER checks A8W4 first, so leaving it set would still pick afp8).
- SiTUv2 gate/up weights use the **separated** layout to match ATOM kernel selection.

No new env flags; the existing recipe variable keeps its name for compatibility.

## AITER requirement

This path needs [ROCm/aiter#4463](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4463) (first tagged in **AITER v0.1.20**): `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4` dispatch plus `kimik3_a4w4_{un,}tuned_fmoe.csv`. vLLM `main` already pins `AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.21.post1`, which includes that PR.

On AITER **v0.1.19** (this PR's original docker pin), a4w4 still launches `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` but logs **heuristic FlyDSL fallback** because the tuned CSV rows are missing. That is not the tuned a4w4 config from #4463.

## Motivation

Trace comparison on Kimi-K3 / MI355X shows vLLM dispatching `mfma_moe1_silu_mul_afp8_wfp4_fp8_*_gui_xcd4_*` while ATOM uses `mfma_moe1_silu_mul_afp4_wfp4_fp4_*_situv2_*`. AITER supports a4w4 via `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4` in #4463; vLLM previously wired the recipe toggle to a8w4. Open PR #50813 adds explicit opt-in a8w4 for Quark checkpoints — this change makes a4w4 the default for the existing SiTUv2 recipe path.

## Results

GSM8K (Kimi-K3 MXFP4, MI355X, TP=8, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1`, greedy 5-shot, full test split `n=1319`):

| Filter | Metric | This PR (a4w4) | Prior a8w4 recipe |
|---|---|---|---|
| strict-match | exact_match | **0.9659 ± 0.005** | 0.9666 |
| flexible-extract | exact_match | **0.9659 ± 0.005** | 0.9666 |

No accuracy regression (within stderr). Decode dispatch used `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` (fp4 activations); no `afp8` / `_gui_` kernels.

`niah_single_2` at 32k (`n=20`): **1.0** on both a4w4 and a8w4.

8k ISL / 1k OSL serving on AITER **without** #4463 tuned CSVs (heuristic a4w4 vs tuned a8w4) is a wash (~0.5% at conc 4/8). Isolated kernel timings in AITER #4463 show a4w4 ahead of a8w4 once the tuned rows are present.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k situv2` on gfx950
- [x] Serve Kimi-K3 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1`; confirm a4w4 FlyDSL (`afp4_wfp4_bf16`, not `afp8` / `fp8q` / `_gui_`)
- [ ] Confirm **tuned** a4w4 configs (`using 2stage`, no `heuristic FlyDSL fallback`) on AITER >= v0.1.20
- [ ] Do **not** set `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1` in launch scripts (overrides a4w4)
- [x] GSM8K vs prior a8w4 baseline (see Results)
- [x] `niah_single_2` vs prior a8w4
- [ ] 8k/1k serving A/B on AITER with #4463 tuned CSVs
- [ ] Verify cudagraph correctness under full decode (SiTUv2 a4w4 flydsl path, distinct from generic `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` cudagraph issue in #44988)

title: [Kimi K3 Perf] Optimize `eh_proj` linear calculation, 12.9 ~ 25.2% kernel performance improvement
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

Enabling m=1 and m=2 for low latency gemm

Originally we use `nn.Linear`, it is not `LinearBase`, so won't work in `enable_kimi_k3_low_latency_gemm`

Now we enable it

## Test

Acc covered in current unit tests

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
"""Sweep cuBLAS vs CuTe for the Kimi-K3 MTP eh_proj."""

import statistics

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.cute_dsl.skinny_gemm import (
    SkinnyGemmConfig,
    shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm,
)

N = 7168
K = 14336
MS = range(1, 17)
REPEATS = 9
REPLAYS = 200

# block_size, outputs_per_block, k_unroll, vector_width
CANDIDATES = (
    (32, 4, 4, 8),
    (32, 8, 4, 8),
    (64, 2, 1, 8),
    (64, 4, 1, 8),
    (64, 4, 2, 8),
    (64, 8, 2, 8),
    (128, 2, 1, 8),
    (128, 4, 1, 8),
    (128, 4, 2, 8),
    (224, 2, 2, 8),
    (224, 4, 2, 8),
    (224, 7, 2, 8),
    (224, 4, 4, 8),
    (256, 2, 2, 8),
    (256, 4, 2, 8),
    (256, 7, 2, 8),
    (448, 2, 2, 8),
    (448, 4, 2, 8),
)


def configs(m: int) -> list[SkinnyGemmConfig]:
    result = [SkinnyGemmConfig(m, *candidate) for candidate in CANDIDATES]
    if m == 1:
        result.append(SkinnyGemmConfig(1, 256, 2, vector_width=4, static_k=K))
    return result


def benchmark(call, weights: list[torch.Tensor]) -> float:
    for weight in weights:
        call(weight)
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()

    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        for weight in weights:
            call(weight)
    for _ in range(10):
        graph.replay()
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()

    samples = []
    for _ in range(REPEATS):
        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        start.record()
        for _ in range(REPLAYS):
            graph.replay()
        end.record()
        end.synchronize()
        samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / (REPLAYS * len(weights)))
    return statistics.median(samples)


@torch.inference_mode()
def main() -> None:
    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(0)
    print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), torch.cuda.get_device_capability())
    print(" M | cuBLAS(us) | CuTe(us) | gain(%) | best config")
    print("---|------------|----------|---------|------------")

    for m in MS:
        torch.manual_seed(m)
        x = torch.randn(m, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        weights = [
            torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) for _ in range(2)
        ]
        reference = torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weights[0])
        cublas_us = benchmark(
            lambda weight, x=x: torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight), weights
        )

        best_us = float("inf")
        best_config = None
        for config in configs(m):
            output = shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm(x, weights[0], config)
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                output.float(), reference.float(), rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-1
            )
            latency = benchmark(
                lambda weight, config=config, x=x: shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm(
                    x, weight, config
                ),
                weights,
            )
            if latency < best_us:
                best_us, best_config = latency, config

        gain = (cublas_us - best_us) / cublas_us * 100
        print(
            f"{m:2d} | {cublas_us:10.3f} | {best_us:8.3f} | {gain:7.1f} | {best_config}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Cache the Mamba state at the block-grid position of EAGLE resume
author: akshaver
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the second of the two EAGLE + `--mamba-cache-mode align` prefix-cache defects pinned
by #52371.

Full attention hits at a position it holds a key for. EAGLE prunes one hash unit off that
candidate and drops it. The Mamba group materializes state only on its own block grid, so
nothing exists at the resulting position and the hit floors back to the previous block
boundary.

Commit 1 covers the case where the shared prefix runs to the end of the producer's prompt.
When it ends earlier — a system prompt followed by a per-request suffix, the deployed shape
— the producer's tail sits over tokens no sibling shares, so a check-point there is
unreachable. The sibling stops at the last shared boundary and EAGLE drops one hash unit
below it. That position is already recorded: `request.shared_prefix_boundary`, set by
`get_computed_blocks` to the longest single-group hit.

Commit 2 is two parts:
- `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` ends a chunk at the junction **as observed** rather
  than floored to the block grid, which rounds the resume point away. Past the prompt it
  falls back to the block-floored stop — the manager writes nothing there, but stock still
  check-points at the block boundary, so dropping the stop would lose a snapshot.
- `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` accepts the junction in addition to the prompt
  tail, bounded to the prompt chunk being computed.

Commit 3 removes a mooncake connector change introduced in Commit 1, deferring solving 
disag so a follow-on PR.

## Details

The junction stop is the *earliest* mandatory stop, so it **replaces** the block-boundary
stop — a junction the manager then refuses leaves less cached than not splitting at all.
`KVCacheManager` therefore computes one predicate both sides read:

| condition | why |
| --- | --- |
| EAGLE annotated on the model | the manager takes the drop *per KV cache group*, the scheduler flag is model-wide; derived separately they disagree on any annotated model |
| fine-grained partial hash hits on | requires `--prefix-match-unit`. Under `align`, `_align_hybrid_block_size` raises the attention block to the Mamba page and then sets `mamba_block_size = block_size`, so both groups share one block size and the GCD that feeds `hash_block_size` equals the scheduler block — nothing to look an entry up with |
| no multi-module MTP | `cache_blocks` then hands the manager `num_computed - num_reprefillable`, not the chunk end, so the position published is not the one held |

**Rejected alternative.** Shifting the cacheable grid to `k*block - hash`. That poisons the
cache — slot `p` would hold state after `(p+1)*block - hash` tokens while `cache_blocks`
publishes it as `(p+1)*block`.

## Opt-in, default off

`--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` (`CacheConfig.enable_mamba_fine_grained_prefix_cache`).
Off, the junction stays block-floored and only the prompt tail is registered — the behaviour
of commit 1 alone, pinned by `test_disabled_by_default`. The field is in `compute_hash`'s
ignored factors, so it does not perturb the compiled-graph cache.

## Test Plan

```bash
uv run pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/ tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
              tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py \
              tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py -q
uv run pytest tests/v1/core/ -q     # baseline-differenced against main
```

## Test Result

- Targeted suites: **229 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full `tests/v1/core/`: identical failure set to `main` — **0 new, 0 fixed**.
- Every condition in the new production code is mutation-covered:

| mutation | tests that fail |
| --- | --- |
| manager stops accepting the junction | 5 |
| scheduler reverts to block-flooring the junction | 4 |
| flag propagated without the narrowing conditions | 2 |
| multi-module MTP exclusion dropped | 2 |
| past-the-prompt stop dropped instead of falling back | 1 |
| prompt bound dropped | 1 |

- `test_scheduler_never_stops_where_the_manager_refuses` sweeps the armed
  (block, hash, prompt_len) space: without the manager's acceptance clause, 10 of 15 armed
  configs split at a junction the manager then refuses.

- Per edited tests `test_prefix_caching.py::test_hybrid_local_kv_retention_mtp_reuses_latest_boundary` and `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py::test_unaligned_resume_never_runs_past_its_block`, the boundary changed which required adjusting the pinned boundary.

## Reuse Pareto

The quantity this change moves is prefix-cache **hit length**; TTFT and throughput are
downstream of it. Measured exactly by driving the real `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split`
and the real `KVCacheManager`, at the geometry `align` mode actually serves — attention
block **equals** mamba block, hash unit = `prefix_match_unit`. Figure and the 84-config
grid it plots are attached in a comment below.

- **0 of 84 configs where enabling the flag reduces reuse.**
- The saving is a **constant `block − hash_unit` tokens per request**, independent of where
  the shared prefix ends. The *ratio* therefore tracks how much other uncached work a
  request has, and how large the served block is. At the ATHENA workload (57,600 shared,
  6,400 suffix, hash unit 64):

  | served block | uncached prefill off → on | ratio |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 2,048 | 8,704 → 6,720 | 1.30 |
  | 4,224 | 13,312 → 9,152 | 1.45 |
  | 8,448 | 21,760 → 13,376 | 1.63 |

  Across suffix lengths at block 4,224: 2.32x at 400 tokens, 1.96x at 1,600, 1.45x at
  6,400, 1.15x at 25,600. Read the served `block_size` off a server startup log to pick the
  right row — the *shape* holds for every block size, only the magnitude moves.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used (Claude Code), including adversarial review passes that removed a
dead code path and two silent cache-reuse regressions from earlier drafts of this change.
Every changed line was reviewed by me and the commands above were run locally.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Don't pad spec decode up to `max_model_len`
author: njhill
body:
The uniform spec-decode padding applied to single-token decodes in the waiting loop allowed `num_computed_tokens` to land exactly on `max_model_len`. The running loop's `max_model_len` cap subtracts the tokens the step will sample, so it then goes negative, and with async scheduling the request is scheduled again before the output that would stop it: `num_scheduled_tokens` is negative and the model runner crashes in np.repeat.

Only pad when there is room for the padded chunk plus the sampled token(s), and schedule the single real token un-padded otherwise (breaking out of the waiting loop instead would starve the request, which can never make progress, and head-of-line block the queue).

Also propagate `create_scheduler(max_model_len=...)` to ModelConfig in the core scheduler test utils, since the scheduler reads model_config.max_model_len, matching the kv_connector test utils.

This PR replaces similar fix PRs https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50342 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53812.

Thanks to @sungsooha and @yifjiang for those.

title: [Spec Decode][ROCm] Add FLy: entropy-gated deferred verification for draft-model speculative decoding
author: eecspan
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds [FLy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22972), an opt-in, lossy speculative verification policy, with support for both ModelRunner V1 and ModelRunner V2.

Standard verification stops at the first rejected draft token. FLy can accept an isolated rejection when the target entropy is high and the next `W` draft tokens all pass native verification. It needs no additional checkpoint or target forward pass. FLy does not preserve the target distribution and may reduce output quality; standard verification remains the default.

## Results at a glance

- **MRV2:** four recent models using DSpark/MTP, evaluated on AMD MI355X and NVIDIA B300. Across batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64, FLy improves decode throughput over Standard SD at all 48 model/platform/batch points: **1.055x–1.310x on AMD** and **1.041x–1.273x on NVIDIA**.
- **MRV2 quality:** Target / Standard SD / FLy comparisons on GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, and GPQA-Diamond. Minimum measured accuracy retention relative to Target is **96.43% on AMD** and **96.30% on NVIDIA**, both one-question differences on AIME25. These are single-pass measurements, not a quality guarantee.
- **V1:** the existing four target/draft pairs across ten benchmarks show **1.067x–1.938x** throughput versus Standard SD on AMD MI355X. Additional NVIDIA and non-zero-temperature results are retained below.

## Implementation

FLy changes verification decisions, using the native acceptance rule for each sampling mode: token equality for greedy target sampling, target-only acceptance for greedy drafting with random target sampling, or probability-ratio acceptance for probabilistic drafting.

A rejected position is eligible only when its draft token is not masked by target constraints, its top-k target entropy meets the threshold, and a full window of `W` subsequent draft tokens passes native verification. Another rejection within that window rejects the original position; a short trailing window is not deferred.

- **MRV1:** a pre-pass overrides the target argmax or uniform sample consumed by the existing acceptance kernels. The random path checks positive target and draft probability before forcing acceptance. Softmax is computed once and reused.
- **MRV2:** the rejection kernel tracks a pending rejection and commits the window only after all `W` native acceptances. Failed windows recover at the original rejected position, preserving that position's argmax or probability-normalization statistics.

Entropy is computed from processed target scores as `-sum(p * log(p))` over the largest `fly_entropy_top_k` probabilities, without renormalizing that subset. The default top-k is 3. This is the implementation's top-k gate, rather than the paper's full-vocabulary normalized entropy.

Configuration validates the window and logs a one-time lossy-method warning. Probabilistic drafting retains draft probabilities for FLy. The V1 pre-pass uses int64 vocabulary-offset arithmetic to avoid overflow on large batches.

This PR also rejects `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` together with `use_local_argmax_reduction=True`: the local-argmax path otherwise bypasses vocabulary intersection and token-ID mapping. This validation applies to all verification methods. FLy-specific entropy and acceptance work runs only when explicitly enabled.

## Usage

```python
from vllm import LLM

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "draft_model",
        "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 8,
        "rejection_sample_method": "fly",
        "fly_window_size": 6,
        "fly_entropy_threshold": 0.3,
        "fly_entropy_top_k": 3,
    },
)
```

`fly_window_size` defaults to `min(6, num_speculative_tokens - 1)`. FLy requires at least two speculative tokens and a window smaller than that count. `fly_entropy_top_k` must be positive and is capped at the vocabulary size.

FLy supports heterogeneous vocabularies through the existing token mapping with greedy drafting. The proposer allowlist has been removed; `extract_hidden_states` is explicitly rejected because it does not perform speculative verification.

Standalone `draft_model` proposing uses MRV1. MRV2 supports FLy with its supported proposers, including MTP and DSpark as evaluated below. FLy does not force a fallback to MRV1. The MRV2 measurements use `fly_window_size=2`, as specified in their setup.

## ModelRunner V2 evaluation

All runs use ModelRunner V2 and the models' native speculative heads. Draft sampling is greedy. FLy uses `window=2`, a default entropy threshold of `0.3`, and entropy top-k `3`.

Target-only (`T`) is the primary quality reference, while Standard SD (`SD`) is included as a sanity baseline. `FLy−T` is the absolute accuracy difference, and retention is `FLy correct / Target correct`.

| Model | Speculative method | K | AMD MI355X TP | NVIDIA B300 TP | Reasoning effort |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | DSpark | 7 | 4 | 2 | `high` |
| Qwen3.8-27B | MTP | 3 | 2 | 1 | `xhigh` |
| GLM-5.2-FP8 | MTP | 5 | 4 | 4 | `max` |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 | MTP | 8 | 2 | 1 | thinking enabled |

title: [Attention][DCP] Use FlashInfer native CP for MLA decode
author: GirasoleY
body:
## Summary

FlashInfer 0.6.17 exposes native context-parallel masking through CuTeDSL MLA decode kernel. This PR adds MLA DCP support through FlashInfer (limit to cuteDSL path only)

### Relationship to existing work

This is not a duplicate of the existing speculative/DCP PRs:

- #52188 added vLLM's DSpark/DCP slot mapping and draft metadata. This PR uses that plumbing; it does not reimplement it.
- #53139 removed the legacy manual FlashInfer DSpark/DCP flattening. This PR does not restore that workaround; it uses FlashInfer's native CP mask.
- #48392 covers dense GQA/MHA DFlash/DSpark DCP, whereas this change is for the MLA backend.
- #52990 migrates FlashInfer MLA to the unified API but does not forward or enable native CP semantics. If it lands first, the call-site rebase should be mechanical.

I also searched open vLLM PRs for `causal_seqlens_kv_global` and the native FlashInfer MLA CP arguments and found no overlapping integration.

## Test

Kimi-K3 DCP8-DCP8 P/D w/ EAGLE3:

- DeepSWE full113: 113/113 trials completed, 77/113 passed (68.14%), zero evaluator errors and zero retries;
- weighted EAGLE acceptance: 53.52%;

title: [Bugfix] Revert renderer warmup overlap to avoid fork deadlock
author: khluu
body:
## Summary

Reverts #52764, restoring synchronous multimodal renderer warmup after engine-core initialization.

## Why

Main build #85765 reproduced the same startup hang in exact H200 and MI300 `multi-modal-models-standard-4-other-whisper` jobs:

- H200: `test_moss_audio_generation_smoke` resolved `MossAudioModel`, then made no progress until the 75-minute job timeout.
- MI300: the same test hit its 25-minute timeout. The captured stack shows the renderer warmup worker inside Whisper spectrogram preprocessing while the main thread is inside `multiprocessing.popen_fork` launching engine-core processes.

That is the unsafe overlap introduced by #52764: a live Python background thread is doing multimodal processor work while engine-core initialization forks. The current merge (#53396) is not the culprit; its exact PR-head build #85744 passed both H200 and MI300 mirrors.

## Validation

- `python3 -m compileall` on the changed runtime files
- `ruff check`
- `ruff format --check`
- `typos`

The repository-wide pre-commit bootstrap is currently blocked on this host because a hook environment uses Python 3.9 while the pinned mypy 1.20.2 requires Python >=3.10. Exact H200 and MI300 Buildkite jobs are required before merge.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Fused kernels for KDA prefill reland
author: kliuae
body:
## Purpose
#52606 added a KDA prefill fusion path for ROCm's gfx950, but was reverted in #53294 as its builds failed on gfx90a. This PR adds back the fused path, and guards the kernel builds on gfx950. This PR also adds a few optimizations to further improve the prefill performance, achieving ~5% TTFT reduction compared to the original triton path of the KDA prefill chain.

The bulk of the design follows #52606 in fusing KDA prefill ops into two groups: **"prologue"** that handles the (pre-)processing leading up to the recurrent update, and **"recurrence"** that adopts a two-pass strategy, walking the state update in each group of chunks first from uninitialized states and then from the correct initial states, with a scan in between to work out the true initial states of each groups.

This PR additionally incorporates the following on top of the original kernels:
- The recurrence stage reads from and writes to the recurrent state paged cache directly. While the old path using dense `initial_state`/`final_state` still functions, `state_cache` and `state_indices` can be optionally piped into the kernel and is set as default for the fused path. This fuses the gather/scatter into this kernel, eliminating the need for `gather_initial_state` and the final scatter in the fused path.
- The recurrent state update is further split into two, along the state's K dimension and the chunk's tokens. Two waves now handles their separate halves of each block, and communicate their intermediates through LDS for their reduction. This improves occupancy of CUs.
- Checkpoint state, indices, and offsets are exported from the kernel interface. This can allow the fused path to resume from a mamba block boundary rather than recomputing when it's adopted for ROCm.

An additional engine argument option `--kda-prefill-backend=fused` is added to enable this fused path, and it's set as the default when it is supported.

## Test Plan

Unit tests for the fused kernels
lm_eval with gsm8k on MI355X

Server command
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --load-format auto \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --kda-prefill-backend auto  # "auto" = "triton" for main; "fused" for the PR branch
```

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix GraniteMoeHybrid per-expert quantized weight loading
author: Priyjain-amd
body:
Quantized GraniteMoeHybrid checkpoints with one tensor per expert fail with KeyError: 'layers.0.block_sparse_moe.experts.w2_weight'.

The FusedMoE/MoERunner refactor (#41184) moved expert parameters into a RoutedExperts submodule, but get_expert_mapping() still returns the pre-refactor experts.w13_/w2_ prefixes, so _load_quant_expert() looks up a name missing the routed_experts level.

Pass the mapped name through maybe_remap_moe_expert_param_name(), which only rewrites known expert suffixes present in params_dict, leaving other layouts unaffected.

Issue resolve: #54047

body:
## Purpose

Tune hopper low latency gemm kernel

## Test

Acc covered in current unit tests

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
from statistics import geometric_mean

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia import low_latency_gemm as gemm
from vllm.triton_utils import triton

COPIES = 8  # Distinct weights approximate different model layers.
WARMUP = 20
REPETITIONS = 100
TOKENS = range(1, 3)


def bench_graph(fn) -> float:
    """Return microseconds per GEMM, with graph launch cost amortized."""
    outputs = fn()
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        outputs = fn()
    latency_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(
        graph.replay,
        warmup=WARMUP,
        rep=REPETITIONS,
        return_mode="median",
    )
    del outputs
    return latency_ms * 1000 / COPIES


def run_plan(plan, x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    output = gemm._run_plan(plan, x, weight)
    return F.linear(x, weight) if output is None else output


def main() -> None:
    capability = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()
    if capability != (9, 0):
        raise RuntimeError(f"This benchmark requires Hopper (SM90), got {capability}")

    print(f"GPU: {torch.cuda.get_device_name()} {capability}")
    print("       N      K   M  backend          before_us   after_us  speedup")

    selected_speedups = []
    for (n, k), spec in gemm.KIMI_K3_PROJECTIONS_SM90.items():
        weights = [
            torch.empty((n, k), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
            for _ in range(COPIES)
        ]
        plan = gemm._build_plan(spec)

        for m in TOKENS:
            x = torch.empty((m, k), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
            backend = plan[m][0] if m in plan else "cuBLAS fallback"

            before_us = bench_graph(
                lambda x=x, weights=weights: [F.linear(x, w) for w in weights]
            )
            after_us = bench_graph(
                lambda plan=plan, x=x, weights=weights: [
                    run_plan(plan, x, w) for w in weights
                ]
            )
            speedup = before_us / after_us
            if m in plan:
                selected_speedups.append(speedup)

            print(
                f"{n:8d} {k:6d} {m:3d}  {backend:15s} "
                f"{before_us:10.2f} {after_us:10.2f} {speedup:8.2f}x"
            )

        weights.clear()
        torch.accelerator.empty_cache()

    print(
        f"Selected points: {len(selected_speedups)}, "
        f"geomean {geometric_mean(selected_speedups):.2f}x, "
        f"min {min(selected_speedups):.2f}x, max {max(selected_speedups):.2f}x"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

title: [Bugfix] Format kernel-import errors eagerly so warning_once does not retain them
author: zwang86
body:
FIX #54096

## Purpose

`logger.warning_once` caches its arguments forever (`lru_cache`). The kernel import fallbacks passed the live `ImportError` as a lazy format argument, so the cache retained the exception — and through `__traceback__` every frame and local on the raising path. `import_kernels` runs inside `LLM.__init__`, so on platforms without compiled `vllm._C` kernels the pinned locals included the `LLM` instance under construction: it could never be garbage collected, its EngineCore subprocess only exited with the interpreter, and on accelerator plugins the device stayed held by the leaked engine. Each exception instance was also a distinct cache key, defeating the once-deduplication.

Per review feedback, this fixes the specific call sites and nothing else: format the exception eagerly at the five kernel import sites (`repr(e)` with `%s` renders byte-identical output to the previous `%r` of the live exception). No logger changes, no new tests.

## Test Plan

Block the `vllm._C` import with a meta-path finder, keep a weakref to the raised exception, call `Platform.import_kernels()` twice, then `gc.collect()`:

```python
import gc, sys, weakref
from vllm.platforms.interface import Platform

class TrackedError(ModuleNotFoundError):  # plain ModuleNotFoundError is not weakref-able
    pass

refs = []
class Blocker:
    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
        if name in ("vllm._C", "vllm._moe_C_stable_libtorch"):
            e = TrackedError(f"No module named '{name}'")
            refs.append(weakref.ref(e))
            raise e
        return None

for m in ("vllm._C", "vllm._moe_C_stable_libtorch"):
    sys.modules.pop(m, None)
sys.meta_path.insert(0, Blocker())

Platform.import_kernels()
Platform.import_kernels()  # second call: shows dedup behavior
gc.collect()
print("exception retained after gc:", any(r() is not None for r in refs))
```

## Test Result

Output before this fix (main):

```text
WARNING 09-14 21:12:50 [interface.py:368] Failed to import from vllm._C: TrackedError("No module named 'vllm._C'")
WARNING 09-14 21:12:50 [interface.py:368] Failed to import from vllm._C: TrackedError("No module named 'vllm._C'")
exception retained after gc: True
```

The warning fires on every call ("once" is defeated because each exception instance is a new cache key), and the exception is retained forever with its traceback.

Output after this fix:

```text
WARNING 09-14 21:10:57 [interface.py:368] Failed to import from vllm._C: TrackedError("No module named 'vllm._C'")
exception retained after gc: False
```

The warning text is byte-identical, fires once, and nothing is retained.

End-to-end: on a Neuron (OOT platform) stack with this fix applied, `del llm` shuts the EngineCore down within 2s; previously the engine survived until interpreter exit and held the device.

title: [MoE][DeepEPV2] Add PaddedStandard activation format
author: bnellnm
body:
## Motivation

`DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize` hands the experts an activation tensor whose **row count is an upper bound rather than the exact token count**, so some rows are inactive padding. The shape is still 2D `(num_tokens, hidden_dim)` — the padding is in the token dimension; nothing is padded along `E`. It arises because the number of tokens a rank receives after dispatch is data-dependent and not knowable on the host without a device sync, from two sources:

- **decode / cudagraph mode** — the recv buffer is sized to the worst case (`R * num_max_tokens_per_rank`); only the `[0, num_recv_tokens)` prefix is written and the tail is left **uninitialized**.
- **prefill mode** — tokens are grouped per-expert and each expert's block is padded up to `expert_alignment`; those gaps are zeroed.

Inactive rows are signalled by setting all of their `topk_ids` slots to `-1`, and `ExpertTokensMetadata.psum_recv_per_rank` carries the real/padding boundary on device (reading it host-side would break CUDA-graph capture).

Previously this was hidden behind the generic `Standard` activation format, so experts had no way to know their input might contain such rows. Kernels that *can* skip padding couldn't opt in, and kernels that *can't* handle it had no way to reject the layout. That is a correctness issue, not just a missed optimization: the decode-mode tail is uninitialized, so an expert that builds routing by scanning every row can read garbage that aliases a valid expert id and corrupt real tokens.

This PR introduces a distinct `PaddedStandard` activation format so that the padding contract is communicated explicitly from the prepare/finalize stage to the experts, and only experts that actually support padded input are selected.

## Design

`PaddedStandard` is modeled as a **superset** of `Standard`: a padding-aware kernel treats unpadded input as the zero-padding case, so it accepts both formats, while a `Standard`-only kernel accepts only `Standard`.
`BatchedExperts` remains a disjoint format.

Declaring `PaddedStandard` is a contract: the kernel must either skip inactive rows or produce results for them that are safe to discard, and must honor the `-1` markers rather than trusting row contents.

Rather than have each experts kernel enumerate a list of accepted formats, every kernel declares a single `activation_format()` and the superset relation is expressed by one directional helper on the enum:

```python                                                                                                                              
class FusedMoEActivationFormat(Enum):                                                                                                  
    Standard = ("standard",)                                                                                                           
    BatchedExperts = ("batched_experts",)                                                                                              
    PaddedStandard = ("padded_standard",)                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                       
    def is_superset(self, pf_format: "FusedMoEActivationFormat") -> bool:                                                              
        """Whether this (experts) format is a superset of `pf_format`, i.e. an                                                         
        experts kernel declaring `self` can consume activations produced by a                                                          
        prepare/finalize step in `pf_format`."""                                                                                       
        if self == pf_format:                                                                                                          
            return True                                                                                                                
        return (                                                                                                                       
            self == FusedMoEActivationFormat.PaddedStandard                                                                            
            and pf_format == FusedMoEActivationFormat.Standard                                                                         
        )                                                                                                                              
```                                                                                                                                    

The relation is directional and used as `expert_format.is_superset(pf_format)` everywhere: the experts format (`self`) must be a superset of the prepare/finalize format (the argument).

## What changed

### New activation format
- Added `FusedMoEActivationFormat.PaddedStandard` and the `is_superset()` relation (`modular_kernel.py`).
- `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize.activation_format` now reports `PaddedStandard` instead of `Standard` (`prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py`).

### Experts declare a single activation format
- `FusedMoEExperts.activation_format() -> FusedMoEActivationFormat` (kept single-valued; no list). Experts that support padded input declare `PaddedStandard`:
  - `DeepGemmFP4Experts` (Blackwell only)
  - `HummingIndexedExperts`
  - `TrtLlmMxfp4Mxfp8ExpertsModular` (mxfp4+mxfp8)
  - `TrtLlmBf16ExpertsModular` and `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular` — the TRTLLM-Gen
    kernels skip padding rows at tile granularity (only the modular variants;
    the monolithic classes stay `Standard`).
- All other experts declare their single existing format (`Standard` or `BatchedExperts`).

### TRTLLM mxfp4 expert split
- `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` was split into `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModularBase` + two subclasses, because only the mxfp4+mxfp8 variant supports `PaddedStandard`. `_supports_quant_scheme` was moved down into the subclasses/monolithic class accordingly.

### Format-compatibility checks go through `is_superset`
- `FusedMoEExperts.is_supported_config`: `cls.activation_format().is_superset(activation_format)`.
- `FusedMoEKernel._post_init_setup`: asserts `fused_experts.activation_format().is_superset(prepare_finalize.activation_format)`.
- Test tooling `modular_kernel_tools/common.py` validity check uses the same relation instead of format equality.

### Batched detection uses an `is_batched` property
- `BatchedExperts` is disjoint, so instead of raw `== BatchedExperts` comparisons
  there is a `FusedMoEActivationFormat.is_batched` property that encapsulates the
  single legitimate identity check. All batched-detection sites (`__init__`
  validation, `HummingExpertsBase.is_batched`, cutlass `use_batched_format`,
  `FusedMoEConfig.use_batched_activation_format`, the oracle backend-remap
  branches, and `mk_objects.py`) use `<format>.is_batched`.

### Centralized format selection
- Added `FusedMoEConfig.activation_format` property that resolves the all2all format once: `BatchedExperts` for DeepEP-LL / NIXL-EP / `batched_triton`, `PaddedStandard` for DeepEP V2, else `Standard`.
- Moved `use_batched_activation_format` from `FusedMoEParallelConfig` to `FusedMoEConfig` (now defined in terms of `activation_format`).
- All per-dtype oracle selectors (`fp8`, `int8`, `int_wna16`, `mxfp4`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`, `unquantized`, `w4a8`, `w4a8_int8`, `humming_utils`) now use `config.activation_format` instead of each re-deriving the batched/standard branch.
- Fixed a latent bug in `oracle/fp8.py`: the explicit-DeepGEMM branch tested `== Standard` (which would misroute a `PaddedStandard` config to `BATCHED_DEEPGEMM`); it now tests `== BatchedExperts`.

### `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` can reach `DeepGemmFP4Experts`
The method picked its `FusedMoEExperts` class from a hardcoded if-chain
(`CutlassExpertsMxfp4._supports_current_device()` → `is_xpu()` → Marlin) that never
consulted `activation_format`, so on SM100 it always chose `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`
(`Standard`) and `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize` tripped the assert in
`modular_kernel.py`. `--moe-backend=deep_gemm` now joins `b12x` in deferring to
`select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, which is format-aware:

```python                                                                                                                              
if moe.moe_backend == "b12x" or moe.moe_backend == "deep_gemm":                                                                        
    self.mxfp4_backend, experts_cls = select_mxfp4_moe_backend(moe)                                                                    
```                                                                                                                                    

`process_weights_after_loading` gains the matching `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` branch.
`DeepGemmFP4Experts` has no `process_weights_after_loading` of its own, so without it
the DeepGEMM scale packing never ran and the weights fell through the `else`
catch-all into `prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin`.

Selection is unchanged for every other `--moe-backend` value, including `auto`: the
CUTLASS / XPU / Marlin chain is untouched. This is deliberately the narrow fix —
routing the remaining mxfp4 call sites (`inc_mxfp4_moe.py`, `quark_moe.py`) through
the oracle, and teaching the oracle about `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`, is a follow-up PR.

## Testing

### New tests

- Padding test for deep_gemm in `test_deepgemm.py`
- `test_trtllm_bf16_moe_padding_robust` — padding-robustness: poison the padding
  (NaN in the workspace arena / in the inactive rows of a hand-built `PaddedStandard`
  buffer whose `topk_ids` are `-1`) and assert the valid outputs stay finite and are
  bit-identical to a clean-padding run.
  These prove padding is excluded from results, **not** physical compute-skipping:
  MoE rows are independent in the token dimension and TRTLLM activation quant is
  per-row, so skipping and compute-then-discard give identical valid outputs. The
  compute-savings of tile/block-granularity skipping is a benchmark concern, not a
  pytest assertion.
- Updated `test_deepep_v2_moe.py` to only use experts that support the new format.

### Results

Run on 8× B200 (SM100), FlashInfer 0.6.18, CUDA 13.0:

```                                                                                                                                    
tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py                         20 passed                                                                   
tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_bf16_moe.py                   5 passed                                                                   
tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py (full matrix)      18 passed                                                                   
tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py    25 passed                                                                   
tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py                 1 passed                                                                   
tests/quantization/test_auto_round.py         97 passed, 5 failed                                                                      
```                                                                                                                                    

The 5 `test_auto_round.py` failures are all `test_auto_round_model` end-to-end engine
starts and fail identically on an unmodified tree: this checkout's compiled `_C`
extension is stale relative to the Python wrappers (`_C::gptq_marlin_repack()`
signature mismatch; `Failed to initialize MXFP4 GEMM: status=7` /
`Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 700` from `cutlass_mxfp4_group_mm`). Not
related to this change.

Tolerances in `test_deepep_v2_moe.py` are now scaled to the magnitude of the
reference output (`_scaled_tolerances`) rather than fixed. The output std grows
with the accumulation length, so a fixed `atol` was both too tight at the largest
shape — `(222, 1024, 2048)` fp8 failed with 25/454656 elements just over `6e-2`,
the tail of a smooth error distribution rather than any real defect — and far too
loose at the smallest. Measured `max_err/std` is stable per dtype across every
MNK (bf16 ≤ 0.06, fp8 ≤ 0.33), so the fraction is set per dtype with ~2x headroom.
This tightens the small shapes substantially (bf16 `(1, 256, 256)`: `atol` 1e-1 →
~2e-3) while removing the large-shape false failure.

`test_deepep_v2_moe.py` now pairs DeepEP V2 only with padding-aware TRTLLM experts
(`flashinfer_trtllm` for bf16, `trtllm_fp8` for fp8); the `flashinfer_cutlass`
(`Standard`) path was dropped since it cannot consume the padded layout under the
`is_superset` gate.

Local-run caveat: on a single-node NVLink box DeepEP v2 needs `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`,
because it otherwise requires NCCL GIN/RDMA for `num_ranks > 1` and
`ncclDevCommCreate` fails. Multi-node genuinely needs GIN — do not set this
globally in CI.

### Model evals

gsm8k, 1319 questions, 5-shot, DP=4 + `--enable-expert-parallel                                                                        
--all2all-backend deepep_v2`, no `--enforce-eager` (eager mode never populates
`psum_recv_per_rank`, so the padded decode layout under test would not appear).
`tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor-dp-ep/config-b200-deepep-v2.txt`:

| model | experts | measured | threshold |                                                                                             
| --- | --- | --- | --- |                                                                                                              
| `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` | `TrtLlmBf16ExpertsModular` | 0.8893 | 0.88 |                                                                  
| `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8` | `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular` | 0.8954 | 0.88 |                                                
| `nm-testing/Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4A16` | `DeepGemmFP4Experts` (psum) | 0.8196 | 0.79 |                                                  

The mxfp4 row sits below the 0.88 W4A16 baseline because `--moe-backend=deep_gemm`
forces `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` activations, not because of padding: the same backend
without EP or DeepEP scores 0.8059, i.e. slightly *lower* than the padded EP run.

Backend selection was confirmed on the mxfp4 run rather than assumed — the server log
shows `Using 'DEEPGEMM_MXFP4' Mxfp4 MoE backend` / `Using DeepGemmFP4Experts` paired
with `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize`. Before the `deep_gemm` routing fix this exact
configuration hit the activation-format assert in `modular_kernel.py`.

Not covered: `tests/evals/gpt_oss/configs/gpt-oss-20b-sm100-fi-mxfp4-mxfp8-trtllm-deepep-v2.yaml`.
gpt-oss's hidden size 2880 is rounded up to 3072 by
`DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize.maybe_roundup_layer_hidden_size` (2880 × bf16 = 5760 B →
6144 B transfer atom), but `modular_kernel.py:1526` allocates the finalize output as
`torch.empty_like(hidden_states)` at the unpadded 2880, so `output.copy_(combined_x)`
gets a 2880↔3072 shape conflict. That allocation does not honor the padded-output
contract the model side already assumes (`gpt_oss.py:415` slices
`self.experts(...)[:, : self.hidden_size]`). Separately,
`tests/evals/gpt_oss/test_gpqa_correctness.py:128` hardcodes `--enforce-eager`, which
leaves `psum_recv_per_rank` unpopulated, so this config could not exercise decode
padding even if it started.

## Notes
- AI assistance was used in preparing this change (tests + comments).
- Not a duplicate: introduces a new activation-format category rather than modifying existing dispatch behavior; no open PR adds a padded standard MoE format.

title: [Kernel] Fall back from persistent top-k on low-shared-memory GPUs
author: lucamotz
body:
## Purpose

`persistent_topk` can require more cooperative CTAs than the device can keep
resident for a long row. The existing dispatcher falls back to `FilteredTopK`
in that case, but `FilteredTopK` requires at least 128 KiB of opt-in shared
memory. On GPUs below that limit, the dispatcher raises instead and terminates
EngineCore.

This change routes only that oversubscribed, sub-128-KiB branch to vLLM's
existing `top_k_per_row_decode` implementation. It preserves the current
persistent path when the cooperative launch fits and the current
`FilteredTopK` fallback on devices that can provide its shared-memory
requirement.

The fallback derives `next_n` from the existing lengths tensor:
one-dimensional lengths retain ordinary decode semantics, while
two-dimensional lengths retain the per-step MTP layout.

Related upstream report (exact failure comment):
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45317#issuecomment-4757201334

Focused root-cause report:
https://github.com/jasl/vllm/issues/21

### Existing work considered

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834 carries a much broader SM12x
  model-enablement branch and an alternative low-shared-memory implementation.
  That branch forces a custom single-CTA noncooperative persistent kernel for
  all sub-128-KiB devices. This PR changes only the already-failing
  oversubscribed dispatcher branch, applies independently to current `main`,
  and reuses an existing generic vLLM operation. It adds no product-name,
  compute-capability, or SM-count gate.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52149 addresses candidate-buffer
  overflow and exact rescanning inside `persistent_topk`. It does not change
  the low-shared-memory oversubscription branch in `topk.cu`; the failure mode
  and implementation are separate.

## Test Plan

On current upstream `main` (`de9250ac9e9b249133fff14e15d9248a1ebbcdb8`):

```bash
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
python -c 'import ast, pathlib; ast.parse(pathlib.Path("tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py").read_text())'
python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py \
  -k persistent_topk_falls_back_on_low_smem_device
```

The focused pytest was subsequently run from the exact PR-head test file in
an isolated container on each of two independent GB10 devices. The container
used the qualified vLLM build containing the patch-identical compiled
operator; no production image layer was modified.

## Test Result

- The patch replayed cleanly onto current `main`.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Python syntax check for `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`: passed with
  Python 3.14.5.
- Stable patch ID:
  `4d3b6dd0d58156fdf5447374c85e68e14cd6bf68`.

GPU/build validation was performed on vLLM
`487ecf187d3dfe74d2cf6119a92881dba403c219` with the identical patch
(SHA-256 `b932ec3812541b99049ad27182172fe495054e47c2e4ae97b314e78206acf450`):

- The patched ARM64/CUDA 13 build compiled all 80 CUDA objects, including
  `topk.cu`, and linked the stable libtorch extension.
- A standalone regression covering the same low-shared-memory cases passed
  independently on two NVIDIA GB10 GPUs (SM 12.1, 48 SMs, 101,376 bytes
  opt-in shared memory): `next_n` 1 and 2, `top_k=512`, `seq_len=32769`,
  stride 3,574,656. Returned index sets matched `torch.topk`.
- The exact focused upstream pytest selection passed independently on both
  GB10 devices: `2 passed, 187 deselected` per device, covering `next_n=1`
  and `next_n=2`. The PR-head test file SHA-256 was
  `fd2c8075f50e5c332f2b0f5d00430df57562fe2cc63506383c345efb16c64352`.

### Redacted two-GB10 integration evidence

This is downstream integration evidence, not a claim that this patch alone
enables GLM-5.3.

The final qualified TP2 endpoint uses `max_model_len=491520`, full concurrency
2, FP8 KV cache, eager execution, Marlin MoE, and MTP5:

- `/health` returned 200 and the exact served alias was `glm-5.3-flash`.
- The engine reported 1,047,552 KV tokens, or 2.13x full-length concurrency.
- Both exact ranks remained alive after every request.
- A 50,019-token prompt plus 64 generated tokens crossed the former roughly
  24K--40K crash wall and returned HTTP 200.
- Two concurrent near-limit requests, each with 480,024 prompt tokens plus 32
  generated tokens, both returned HTTP 200.
- A bounded simultaneous-decode c2 run measured 18.715 tokens/s median per
  stream and 31.350 tokens/s aggregate. MTP5 accepted 167 of 450 draft tokens
  during that batch (37.11%).
- The post-test scan found no new persistent-top-k, CUDA, EngineCore, NaN,
  invalid-index, collective, or fatal signature on either rank.

A separate `max_model_len=524288` canary is deliberately not presented as the
final qualified endpoint. It passed a bounded c1 request with 500,020 prompt
tokens plus 32 generated tokens, but exposed only 986,530 KV tokens (1.88x at
524,288), so it did not satisfy the full-length c2 capacity gate. The
491,520-token configuration above is the live-qualified result.

Private hostnames, container names, filesystem paths, environment files,
credentials, rollback locations, and raw logs are intentionally omitted.

### Scope and caveats

- The CUDA build and live endpoint were qualified at `487ecf187`; current
  `main` has passed apply/static checks but has not yet been rebuilt on GB10.
- This patch does not add GLM-5.3 model support. That work is tracked in
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53906.
- Native SM120/SM121 `512+0` NoPE sparse-MLA kernels, the `(32, 2176)` dispatch
  specialization, FP8 packed-KV behavior inside those kernels, and their
  low-shared-memory tile selection are FlashInfer-owned and intentionally not
  included here.
- GLM-dependent vLLM follow-ups remain separate from this generic PR.

### AI assistance disclosure

This change and PR description were prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The
human submitter reviewed the changed lines and is responsible for the
implementation and reported evidence.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, including related reports.
- [x] The test plan, including the focused CUDA command.
- [x] The test results and limitations.
- [x] Documentation impact considered; no user-facing documentation is needed
  for this kernel dispatch fallback.
</details>

title: [Bugfix] Remove race in fused groupwise RMSNorm quantization
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Fix three flaky fused quantized RMSNorm failures observed in the H200 kernel CI job:
https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/85850#01a04456-3602-4e62-b405-0c986c85cdc3

The two group-64 scale failures were caused by a real shared-memory race in `warpReduceMaxSpecialized`. Each reduction stage read values written by other lanes in the preceding stage without synchronization. CUDA racecheck reported thousands of hazards for the failing specialization.

Replace that reduction with a register-based warp shuffle and write only the final lane-0 result back to shared memory. This supports both CUDA warp-32 and ROCm wave-32/wave-64 paths and also handles groups with more or fewer contributors than the warp width.

The remaining CUDA BF16 per-token FP8 case had bit-identical scales and one isolated output differing by exactly one E4M3 ULP out of 2,103,296 values. Keep scale comparison strict, but permit a bounded number of isolated one-ULP output differences for this specific CUDA/BF16/per-token/FP8 configuration.

## Why this is not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `fused quant layernorm`, `rms_norm_per_block_quant`, and `warpReduceMaxSpecialized`. No open PR addresses this reduction race or the per-token assertion.

The nearest open work is materially different:

- #45770 adds mixed input/weight dtype support.
- #49639 restores the scalar RMSNorm intermediate rounding boundary.
- #37196 refactors older static quantization kernels.

None changes `quantization/fused_kernels/layernorm_utils.cuh` or removes this shared-memory hazard.

## Performance

Direct H200 measurements timed the full fused op with preallocated outputs. Cold-L2 results used explicit L2 flushing; hot results used ten kernels per CUDA graph replay. Builds were alternated new/old/new or old/new/old to control for drift.

| BF16 + residual case | Cold L2, old -> new | Hot CUDA graph, old -> new |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2048x1024, group-64 INT8 | 22.82 -> 19.39 us (**15.0% faster**) | 17.81 -> 14.36 us (**19.3% faster**) |
| 2048x1024, group-64 FP8 | 24.48 -> 20.96 us (**14.4% faster**) | 19.68 -> 16.16 us (**17.9% faster**) |
| 2048x1024, group-128 FP8 | 22.50 -> 20.03 us (**11.0% faster**) | 17.67 -> 15.16 us (**14.2% faster**) |
| 1x1024, group-64 FP8 | 7.84 -> 7.84 us (no change) | 4.13 -> 4.01 us (**2.9% faster**) |
| 1x5120, group-64 FP8 | 12.45 -> 12.03 us (**3.3% faster**) | 7.77 -> 7.28 us (**6.3% faster**) |
| 1x5120, group-128 FP8 | 11.74 -> 11.52 us (**1.9% faster**) | 7.05 -> 6.77 us (**4.0% faster**) |

CUPTI Python was unavailable locally, so the FlashInfer benchmark helper used its CUDA-event/CUDA-graph fallback.

## Model evaluation

A seeded two-layer `Qwen2ForCausalLM` model-output equivalence check replaced all five RMSNorm outputs with FP8 group quantize/dequantize results and compared the unfused reference against this fused kernel over an 8x32 token batch:

| Group size | Token logits | Top-1 agreement | Max / mean abs logit diff | Mean cosine | Repeat deterministic |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 256 | 100% | 0 / 0 | 1.0 | yes, bitwise |
| 128 | 256 | 100% | 0 / 0 | 1.0 | yes, bitwise |

## Test plan and results

CUDA incremental build:

```bash
cmake --build --preset release --target install
```

Passed.

Original three failing cases:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  'tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py::test_rms_norm[False-cuda:0-0-dtype0-True-2048x1024-int8-group-64-tma-0-scale-ub-False]' \
  'tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py::test_rms_norm[False-cuda:0-0-dtype0-True-2048x1024-float8_e4m3fn-group-64-tma-0-scale-ub-False]' \
  'tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py::test_rms_norm[True-cuda:0-0-dtype0-True-2048x1027-float8_e4m3fn-per-token-tma-0-scale-ub-False]'
```

Result: `3 passed, 14 warnings`.

Additional correctness coverage:

- FP8 group-64 at 1x5120: passed.
- INT8 group-128 at 1x5120: passed.
- 100 repeated 2048x1024 group-64 scale comparisons across INT8 and FP8: all bitwise deterministic.

CUDA racecheck covered both the original group-64 specialization and wider group-64/group-128 configurations:

```text
RACECHECK SUMMARY: 0 hazards displayed (0 errors, 0 warnings)
```

Before this change, the original specialization reported four warning classes and thousands of hazards.

Applicable repository hooks:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/fused_kernels/layernorm_utils.cuh \
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py
```

All passed.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with diagnosis, implementation, racecheck analysis, benchmarking, model-output evaluation, test execution, and drafting this description. I reviewed every changed line and verified the commands and results above.
