title: [Bugfix] Account for client queue time in serve benchmarks
author: maithilijoshi20
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54101.

With `--max-concurrency`, a request can spend time waiting for the benchmark client semaphore before its timer starts. This PR records that wait separately as client-side queue time, while keeping `start_time` unchanged for throughput calculations.
The benchmark output now reports queue-inclusive E2EL summaries and percentiles, and includes per-request `queue_times` in the generation and pooling JSON results.

## Example Output

For a finite-rate run where the concurrency cap creates client-side backpressure, selecting the new percentile metrics adds these sections to the console output:

```text
-------------- Client-side Queueing --------------
Mean Client Queue Time (ms):             1424.50
Median Client Queue Time (ms):           1424.50
P99 Client Queue Time (ms):              2820.51
------- Queue-inclusive End-to-end Latency -------
Mean E2EL incl. Client Queue (ms):        1924.50
```

title: [Bugfix] Keep the Moondream3 MoE all-reduce out of the fused-path try
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Purpose

`Moondream3TextMoE.forward` wrapped **both** the fused expert kernel and the
tensor-parallel all-reduce that follows it in a single `try/except
(NotImplementedError, RuntimeError)`:

```python
try:
    out = fused_experts(...)
    out = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(out)   # <-- inside the try
    return out
except (NotImplementedError, RuntimeError) as exc:
    self._use_fused_moe = False
    ...
# fallback Python expert loop
out = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(out)       # <-- all-reduces again
```

A `RuntimeError` raised by the **collective itself** was therefore caught and
treated as a fused-kernel failure. That rank disabled the fused path, ran the
Python expert loop, and issued a *second* all-reduce, while every peer issued
one. The tensor-parallel group desyncs and wedges permanently: all ranks stay
alive, no traceback is produced, and the job only ends when a test or step
timeout fires.

Note the failure is specific to the collective raising. If `fused_experts`
itself raises, both the old and new code all-reduce exactly once — that path
was never broken, which is why this went unnoticed.

This is a latent bug in the model, not a regression from any recent PR. It
became reachable on ROCm when #53183 ("[Model Runner V2] Use MRV2 for all
models by default") removed the `is_moe` gate from
`_is_default_v2_model_runner_model()`. `Moondream3ForCausalLM` declares
`moe_num_experts = 64`, is absent from the old
`DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES` allowlist, and is not in
`ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES`, so it moved from MRV1 to MRV2 on ROCm.

### Fix

Narrow the `try` to the expert computation and all-reduce exactly once at the
end of `forward`, on every path. The fallback loop moves into `_expert_loop`,
which returns this rank's partial output and does not communicate. A failing
collective now propagates instead of being retried.

## Test Plan

New CPU-only unit tests in
`tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3_moe.py`, marked
`pytest.mark.cpu_test`, running under a single-rank gloo TP group. They pin the
invariant that makes the bug impossible: **exactly one all-reduce per forward,
on every path.**

- `test_expert_loop_all_reduces_once` — Python fallback path
- `test_fused_path_all_reduces_once` — fused kernel path
- `test_all_reduce_failure_is_not_retried` — **the regression guard**: a
  collective that raises must propagate, not trigger a second collective
- `test_fallback_after_fused_failure_all_reduces_once[RuntimeError,
  NotImplementedError]` — fused failure still all-reduces once, and so does the
  next forward once the fused path is disabled

The router is stubbed so the test does not depend on platform-specific
`ReplicatedLinear` weight post-processing.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3_moe.py -v
```

## Test Result

```
test_expert_loop_all_reduces_once                                PASSED
test_fused_path_all_reduces_once                                 PASSED
test_all_reduce_failure_is_not_retried                           PASSED
test_fallback_after_fused_failure_all_reduces_once[exc0]         PASSED
test_fallback_after_fused_failure_all_reduces_once[exc1]         PASSED
5 passed in 4.69s
```

title: [Hy4] support Hy4-preview model
author: thisjiang
body:
## Purpose

# Hy4 preview Usage Guide

  Hy4 preview is Tencent Hy's new-generation open-source Mixture-of-Experts language
  model. Its backbone has 770B total parameters with 49B activated per token across
  78 layers. The first layer uses a dense FFN; the other 77 layers use 256 routed
  experts (top-8) and 1 shared expert. A native MTP layer adds 10B total parameters
  (0.7B activated) for speculative decoding.

  On the architecture side, inspired by DeepSeek and GLM, the attention module employs Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention (Gated DSA) with IndexCache for cross-layer sparse index reuse. The residual pathway uses iHC (identity Hyper-Connections) to expand inter-layer information flow.

  ## vLLM Setup

  Choose one of the following setup methods.

  ### Using Docker

  ```bash
  docker run --gpus all \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    --ipc=host \
    -e VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1 \
    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
    vllm/vllm-openai:hy4-preview tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
      --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
      --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
      --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
      --enable-auto-tool-choice \
      --port 8000 \
      --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  Build vLLM from source:

  ```bash
  uv venv --python 3.12 --seed --managed-python
  source .venv/bin/activate
  git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
  cd vllm
  uv pip install --editable . --torch-backend=auto
  ```

  ## vLLM Deployment

  Start the FP8 model with MTP enabled:

  ```bash
  export VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1

  vllm serve tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
    --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  ## OpenAI Client Example

  Tencent recommends `temperature=0.9` and `top_p=1.0`. Reasoning defaults to
  `high`, which is suitable for math, coding, and other complex tasks.

  ```python
  from openai import OpenAI

  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

  response = client.chat.completions.create(
      model="hy4-preview",
      messages=[
          {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"},
      ],
      temperature=0.9,
      top_p=1.0,
  )
  output_msg = response.choices[0].message
  print(output_msg.reasoning_content)  # chain-of-thought
  print(output_msg.content)             # final answer
  ```

  For a direct response without deep reasoning, pass `reasoning_effort="no_think"`:

  ```python
  response = client.chat.completions.create(
      model="hy4-preview",
      messages=[
          {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"},
      ],
      temperature=0.9,
      top_p=1.0,
      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "no_think"}},
  )
  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
  ```

  ### cURL Usage

  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
      "model": "hy4-preview",
      "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"}
      ],
      "temperature": 0.9,
      "top_p": 1.0
    }'
  ```

  ## References

  - [Hugging Face: Hy4 preview](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-preview)
  - [Hugging Face: Hy4 preview-FP8](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8)
  - [ModelScope: Hy4 preview](https://modelscope.cn/models/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-preview)
  - [GitHub: Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-preview](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-preview)
  - [GitCode: Hy4 preview](https://ai.gitcode.com/tencent_hunyuan/Hy4-preview)
  - [CNB: Hy4 preview](https://cnb.cool/ai-models/tencent/Hy4-preview)
  - [AngelSlim quantization toolkit](https://github.com/tencent/AngelSlim)

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark no longer drop the last prefix-cache block (mamba align context recompute)
author: Ledgero
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #53477. DFlash and DSpark preserve the target KV cache and do not require the EAGLE-style trailing prefix-cache block drop. Scoping that drop correctly restores reusable Mamba checkpoints in `--mamba-cache-mode align` and prevents full-context recomputation on subsequent replies.

## Claims

- DFlash/DSpark no longer drop the last prefix-cache block solely because `SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle()` also matches those methods.
- Existing EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP behavior is unchanged, including the `disable_eagle_block_drop` opt-out and its warning.
- `use_eagle()` remains unchanged for encoder shift, lookahead budgeting, and other existing specification-decoding behavior.

## Validation

Local reproduction (2x L40S, vLLM 0.26.0 layout, Qwen3.5-4B hybrid target + Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash draft, three-turn conversation with a shared 30x system prefix):

| Configuration | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| DFlash + mamba align | `cached=[0, 0, 0]` (full recompute every turn) | `[0, 560, 560]` |
| DFlash + mamba all | `[0, 0, 0]` | `[0, 560, 560]` |
| no spec + align/all | `[0, 1056, 1136]` | unchanged |
| MTP + align | no regression observed | no regression observed |

Acceptance comparison against upstream main, using the same models, seed, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=128`, warmed prefix cache, and the V2 runner:

| Method | Prompts | Baseline rate / length | This PR rate / length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DFlash | 32 | 0.14804 / 3.36859 | 0.15199 / 3.43189 |
| DSpark | 128 | 0.34399 / 3.40794 | 0.34512 / 3.41582 |

Targeted tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_eagle_block_drop_can_be_disabled_without_disabling_eagle -q
# 8 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py -q
# 46 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q -k mamba_align
# 2 passed, 229 deselected

.venv/bin/ruff check vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
git diff --check
```

Independent validations since opening:

- dtandersen: Intel Arc B70, Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 + DFlash2 - token corruption with prefix caching resolved.
- vedcsolution: 4x DGX Spark GB10 (TP4), GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2 - identical-request prefix hits `0/12,552` to `4,608`, TTFT `3.9s` to `1.55s`; an extra KDA over-truncation was also fixed (69-scenario tool-call suite `89` to `91`).
- positive666 closed #54041 as superseded by this PR after validating both approaches.

## Details

### Root cause

`SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle()` is a broad predicate for speculative decoding that reads target hidden states, and it intentionally matches `eagle`, `eagle3`, `mtp`, `dflash`, and `dspark`. #53388 derived `use_eagle_block_drop()` from that broad predicate.

EAGLE-style drafters construct a position's draft KV from the target hidden state **and the next token**. DFlash/DSpark construct it from the target hidden state alone. Therefore only EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP need the trailing EAGLE block drop; both DFlash and DSpark preserve the target KV cache.

For a prompt shorter than two Mamba blocks, the spurious back-off produced this sequence:

1. `last_cache_position == 0`, so the prompt was a single chunk ending off the Mamba block grid.
2. Mamba align mode only materializes a reusable recurrent state at a block-aligned chunk end.
3. `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` converged the next turn's hit to zero, causing full-context recomputation.

### Implementation

- `vllm/config/speculative.py`: add `needs_eagle_block_drop()` for the precise EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP capability, and compose `use_eagle_block_drop()` from it plus `disable_eagle_block_drop`.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: reuse `needs_eagle_block_drop()` in the warning condition. The existing split back-off, `KVCacheManager(use_eagle=...)`, offloading, and Mooncake paths now receive `False` for DFlash/DSpark without changing `use_eagle()`.
- `tests/test_config.py`: parameterize the existing config test over EAGLE3/MTP (drop) and DFlash/DSpark (no drop), both with the opt-out enabled and disabled.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: set the now-separate `use_eagle_block_drop` scheduler value in the Mamba-align EAGLE fixture.

The change is limited to the prefix-cache trailing-block policy. EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP retain the previous default behavior, and the existing explicit opt-out remains available.

### Related work and duplication

No open PR addresses #53477. Related work includes #53388 (merged opt-out for EAGLE trailing-block dropping), #30877 (Mamba align prefix caching), #42971, and #44082. None previously corrected the DFlash/DSpark classification.

title: [Kimi-K3][Kernel] Optimize the low-M fused latent MoE tail
author: zyongye
body:
## Summary

This PR reduces the SM100 Kimi-K3 latent-MoE decode tail latency for low token counts while preserving the existing operator structure. Deferred BF16 top-16 finalization, routed AllReduce, RMSNorm, and shared-expert ReduceScatter remain fused in one CuTe DSL collective kernel; the following rank-sharded up-projection and Lamport consumer are made cheaper and are launched earlier with PDL.

The production path remains valid for `M <= 16` (and the existing larger capacities). The most aggressive static SIMT up-projection is deliberately limited to `M <= 5`; measurements show that the dynamic WGMMA path wins again from `M=6` onward.

## Optimization details

### 1. Specialize BF16 top-16 finalization inside the fused collective

The Kimi-K3 route contract on current `main` is BF16 top-16. The specialized path assigns one 16-byte latent fragment to each thread and uses inline PTX to:

- load all 16 route indices and 16 BF16 route weights with wide vector loads;
- predicate invalid/dropped routes before gathering their GEMM2 fragments;
- accumulate weighted BF16 inputs directly into eight FP32 registers with `fma.rn.f32.bf16`;
- round to packed BF16 once, immediately before NVLS publication.

This removes scalar metadata traffic and compiler-generated BF16-to-FP32 conversion sequences from the hot loop. FP32 is used for arithmetic accumulation, not for the communication buffers: multicast, Lamport storage, and the collective's configured internal wire format remain BF16 (`fp32_internal=False`).

### 2. Compact the fused collective's low-M launch

For the TP8 Kimi-K3 shape (`latent=3584`, `hidden=7168`), `M=1..4` now uses a seven-CTA cluster with 64 threads per CTA and exact one-cluster-per-token ownership. `M=1` gets its own specialization; `M=2..4` share the four-token specialization. The shared ReduceScatter uses one compact role instead of launching redundant destination roles.

The routed and shared roles call `griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()` immediately after publishing the data required by the successor. This lets the up-projection grid become resident while the collective completes its remaining reduction, normalization, flag rotation, and cleanup. The general schedule is retained for `M >= 5`, including multi-wave Lamport generation handling.

### 3. Use a one-pass skinny BF16 up-projection for `M <= 5`

The static SIMT kernel now uses:

- 224 threads per CTA;
- two output columns per CTA;
- 16 BF16 values (32 bytes) per thread;
- one K tile for `K=3584`;
- explicit `fma.rn.f32.bf16` into FP32 accumulators;
- a checked 32-byte alignment contract.

Compared with the prior eight-output/eight-BF16 geometry, this trades more output CTAs for a shorter, single-pass inner loop. The production WGMMA cluster shape remains `(1, 8)`; this PR does not change the dynamic GEMM cluster. The measured crossover keeps the static path at `M <= 5`: at `M=6` static/dynamic were `5.478/5.629 us`, but by `M=8` they were `7.193/5.794 us`, and the gap continued to grow through `M=16`.

### 4. Right-size and overlap the Lamport consumer

The copy/reset grid is selected at runtime as:

```text
min(32, ceil((M * 7168 / 8) / 128)) CTAs
```

For `M=1`, this is exactly seven 128-thread CTAs covering the 896 16-byte fragments, instead of 32 x 224 = 7,168 launched threads. Each polling iteration copies a ready fragment and resets its sentinel in the same pass. Because the Lamport marker itself is the data-readiness contract, the consumer no longer waits for ordinary producer-grid completion before polling, and it publishes its own PDL launch point early.

## Performance

Measured on 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (driver 580.126.09), TP8, Kimi-K3 dimensions, BF16 tail inputs, and CUDA Graph replay. Isolated GEMV measurements rotate weights through a working set larger than L2. Values are medians.

| M=1 measurement | Before | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Exposed collective -> skinny GEMV -> Lamport chain in the packed Nsight trace | 12.096 us | 9.056 us | -25.1% |
| Skinny GEMV, rotating weights | 2.84-2.92 us | 2.51-2.52 us | -11% to -14% |
| Lamport copy/reset, standalone | ~4.77 us | ~1.25 us | -73.8% |
| Lamport copy/reset under packed overlap | ~4.77 us | ~1.95 us | -59.1% |

The decomposition shows that launch right-sizing of the Lamport consumer is the largest direct kernel reduction. In paired whole-tail replays holding the collective and copy fixed, the GEMV geometry reduced `16.512 -> 16.224 us` (~0.29 us). Moving the PDL point early reduced `16.576 -> 16.224 us` (~0.35 us).

The slowest-rank CUDA-event whole-tail sweep for `M=1..16` was effectively flat because that metric includes cross-rank graph scheduling and hides producer/consumer overlap; for example, `M=1` was `16.384 -> 16.352 us`. The 3.04 us improvement above is the exposed three-kernel critical chain in Nsight, excluding the region overlapped with its predecessor.

## Accuracy

### Kernel parity

The TP8 distributed tests compare the fused result with PyTorch collectives, RMSNorm, linear projection, and final add using `atol=8e-2`, `rtol=3e-2`:

- finalized input: `M = 1, 5, 8, 16, 33, 65, 5`, including two token waves, mailbox reuse, and CUDA Graph replay;
- deferred top-8 input: `M = 1, 5, 16, 33, 65`;
- specialized BF16 top-16 input: `M = 1, 2, 4, 5, 16`, including an invalid/dropped route and CUDA Graph replay.

All comparisons passed. The machine has eight GPUs, so the distributed TP16 pytest was not run; local TP16-shard up-projection parity passed during kernel tuning.

### Full-model evaluation

The modified production service was evaluated with `lm-eval 0.4.12` on the complete GSM8K v3 test split: 1,319/1,319 samples, 5-shot multi-turn chat-template prompting, greedy decoding, and seed 2026.

| Task | Filter | Correct | Exact match | Stderr |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K v3 | strict-match | 1267 / 1319 | 0.9606 | 0.0054 |
| GSM8K v3 | flexible-extract | 1273 / 1319 | 0.9651 | 0.0051 |

Serving used TP8, MXFP4 MoE, FP8 KV cache, a 16,384-token context limit, and 64 concurrent evaluation requests. No requests failed or retried.

Current `upstream/main` at `c01b50e390` has an unrelated Kimi-K3 startup issue where `_KimiK3LowLatencyApply` does not initialize the base method's `_gemm_impl`. For this evaluation only, startup used a local, uncommitted `super().__init__()` workaround. It does not touch the latent tail and was removed before the branch was pushed; it is not present in this PR.

## Tests run

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/latent_moe_tail/allreduce_rmsnorm_reduce_scatter_early_exit.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/latent_moe_tail/fused_add_multicast_skinny_gemm.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/latent_moe_tail/lamport_copy.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/latent_moe_tail/primitives.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/latent_moe_tail.py
# all hooks passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py \
  -k 'tp8_matches_native_path or deferred_finalize_matches_finalized' -v
# 2 passed, 2 deselected

.venv/bin/lm_eval run \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1/chat/completions,tokenizer=/path/to/Kimi-K3,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,trust_remote_code=true,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,timeout=900,max_gen_toks=1500,max_length=16384 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --fewshot_as_multiturn true --log_samples --seed 2026
# 1319/1319 samples; strict 0.9606, flexible 0.9651
```

## Duplicate-work check

No issue number was provided, so there is no issue-number-specific PR query. Keyword searches found no PR implementing this low-M path.

- #53556 targets a different execution path: it moves BF16 shared-expert work into DeepGEMM MegaMoE, removes the standalone shared reduction, and optimizes the published-shared tail at `M=32/64`. This PR keeps the modular MXFP4 tail structure and optimizes its existing fused finalize + routed AR/RMSNorm + shared RS chain at `M=1..16`.
- #53202 changes the default unquantized BF16 linear implementation. The skinny kernel here is not that linear method: it fuses the shared-shard add, TP-local up-projection, and NVLS multicast publication.

## Contribution notes

AI assistance was used during implementation, source comparison, benchmarking, testing, and preparation of this PR description. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand and defend the change end-to-end, and verify the reported commands and results before submission.

title: [Feature][EPD] Support dynamic EPD (EC-connector) proxy
author: gty111
body:
## Purpose

Add launcher-managed dynamic instance registration to the existing EPD example
proxy while preserving its static URL configuration mode.

An external launcher can register ready instances over HTTP as `encode`,
`prefill`, `decode`, or `prefill_decode`. The registered roles determine the
topology:

- `encode` + `prefill_decode` for E+PD
- `encode` + `prefill` + `decode` for E+P+D

The proxy rejects mixing combined PD instances with standalone P/D instances.
A standalone decode instance is routable only while a healthy prefill instance
is available.

This change is confined to the example proxy, its launch scripts, documentation,
and tests. It does not add worker registration threads or change vLLM's EC
connector configuration.

## Usage

Start the proxy in dynamic mode with an admin key:

```bash
export ADMIN_API_KEY="your-admin-key"
python examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py \
  --port 8000 --dynamic-registration
```

After an instance is ready, register its reachable HTTP endpoint:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body http://proxy-host:8000/instances \
  -H "X-API-Key: $ADMIN_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"role":"encode","url":"http://e-host:8001"}'

curl --fail-with-body http://proxy-host:8000/instances \
  -H "X-API-Key: $ADMIN_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"role":"prefill_decode","url":"http://pd-host:8002"}'
```

POST and DELETE operations on `/instances` require `X-API-Key`. GET can be used
to inspect the registry. Registration is idempotent, and launchers must
re-register instances after a proxy restart.

For Example and NIXL EC connectors, no additional registration fields are
needed. For Mooncake, the launcher also supplies the EC consumer's fixed
TP-rank-0 control addresses and DP size:

```json
{
  "role": "prefill_decode",
  "url": "http://pd-host:8002",
  "dp_size": 2,
  "ec_zmq_addrs": ["tcp://pd-host:19019", "tcp://pd-host:19021"]
}
```

The proxy keeps the selected consumer replica and its control address together
for the encoder push and inference request.

The `disagg_1e1pd_example.sh` and `disagg_1e1p1d_example.sh` scripts support this
mode through `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION=1` and `ADMIN_API_KEY`; static routing remains
the default.

## Availability behavior

- Periodic health probes stop routing to an instance after the configured
  consecutive-failure threshold.
- Recovered instances rejoin automatically.
- Unreachable instances are evicted after `--evicted-ttl` unless it is `0`.
- Explicit removal stops new routing without changing already selected routes.
- Probe interval, timeout, failure threshold, and eviction TTL are configurable.

## Validation

Model evaluation (earlier revision):

```bash
CONCURRENCY=1 REPEAT=1 MAX_MODEL_LEN=16384 \
  bash tests/v1/ec_connector/integration/run_epd_mooncake_ec_full_pipeline.sh
```

Qwen2.5-VL-3B with Mooncake TCP and CUDA graphs enabled: single-image,
two-image, and repeated-image responses matched the colocated baseline (3/3).
This E2E/model evaluation has not been rerun on the current revision.

## Duplicate-work check

No other open PR found by searches for dynamic EPD registration or EPD proxy
implements launcher-managed HTTP instance registration. Related open PRs cover
documentation, proxy bug fixes, transfer lifecycle, or EC connectors rather
than this registry and routing behavior.

AI assistance was used. The submitter reviewed the changes and validation
results.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Route the fused shared-expert gate GEMM through the platform dispatcher
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose

When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` is on, `MoERunner` concatenates the router gate and the shared-expert gate into a single `[num_experts + num_shared, hidden]` weight and computes the combined logits with a bare `F.linear`. The un-fused `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` branch immediately below it calls `self.gate(hidden_states)`, a `ReplicatedLinear` whose `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` goes through `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()`.

The problem is that FSE silently replaced ROCm's skinny-GEMM kernels with Tensile `Cijk_*` kernels firing once per MoE layer
per decode step. Those kernels cost 110.6 ms per 100 decode steps where the skinny path does the same GEMM in 55.6 ms, a nearly 2x regression on this GEMM.

This PR routes the fused path through `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` as well.
* On ROCm that reaches `rocm_unquantized_gemm`, matching the un-fused path; 
* On every other platform `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` returns `F.linear`, so the change is a no-op there.


Beyond the immediate win, this also puts the fused gate back onto the path that can reach AITER's tuned GEMM at all. `F.linear` goes straight to rocBLAS and never consults AITER for tuned kernels. After this change the GEMMs flow through `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` into `aiter.tuned_gemm.mm`, and any tuned configuration AITER ships for this shape is picked up automatically with no further vLLM change.


## Test Plan

Models
* `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` -> `Quark-MXFP4`: publicly available, for baseline 
* `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-MoE-MXFP4` -> `MoE-MXFP4`: custom checkpoint enabling FP4-quantized fused shared experts

All runs on MI355X (gfx950), TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, AITER attention, `--ignore-eos`, identical seeds on both arms; the arms differ only by this patch.

**Kernel-level.** PyTorch profiler traces over a decode-only window, comparing per-kernel time before and after.

**Serving throughput and latency.** 

| ISL | OSL | Max concurrency | Prompts |
|-----|-----|-----------------|---------|
| 1024 | 1024 | 4 | 32 |
| 1024 | 1024 | 8 | 64 |
| 1024 | 1024 | 16 | 96 |
| 1024 | 1024 | 32 | 128 |
| 1024 | 1024 | 128 | 384 |

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 5-shot, three arms -- `Quark-MXFP4` with FSE off, `MoE-MXFP4` with FSE off, `MoE-MXFP4` with FSE on -- to keep the checkpoint change separate from the fused-shared-experts change.

## Test Result

### Kernels

Decode-only trace at conc=4; ms per 100 decode steps:

| Arm | Total | wvSplitK | Tensile `Cijk_*` |
|-----|-------|----------|------------------|
| Fused shared experts off | 1807.5 | 330.4 | 0.0 |
| Fused shared experts on, before this PR | 1419.8 | 275.2 | 110.6 |
| Fused shared experts on, with this PR | 1368.9 | 330.8 | 0.0 |

The `Cijk_*` kernels disappear and total wvSplitK time returns to the un-fused level (330.8 against 330.4), which confirms the fused 513-wide gate is no more expensive than the 512-wide router gate it replaces. Net recovery is about 51 ms per 100 decode steps.

### Serving benchmarks

Median of three runs per case for the patched arm, one run per case for the baseline. Each cell is `before → after (change)`; higher is better for throughput, lower for latency.

| ISL | OSL | Conc | Prompts | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean E2EL (ms) |
|-----|-----|------|---------|--------------|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| 1024 | 1024 | 4 | 32 | 279.6 → 289.4 (+3.5%) | 177.1 → 179.1 (+1.1%) | 13.78 → 13.29 (-3.5%) | 13,445.7 → 12,988.4 (-3.4%) |
| 1024 | 1024 | 8 | 64 | 414.7 → 415.6 (+0.2%) | 214.4 → 215.3 (+0.4%) | 17.74 → 17.74 (-0.0%) | 16,860.0 → 16,860.3 (+0.0%) |
| 1024 | 1024 | 16 | 96 | 687.6 → 687.5 (-0.0%) | 284.0 → 283.5 (-0.2%) | 21.02 → 21.06 (+0.2%) | 22,840.0 → 22,894.9 (+0.2%) |
| 1024 | 1024 | 32 | 128 | 976.1 → 972.5 (-0.4%) | 411.5 → 445.7 (+8.3%) | 28.17 → 28.40 (+0.8%) | 29,632.2 → 29,870.6 (+0.8%) |
| 1024 | 1024 | 128 | 384 | 2,178.8 → 2,165.4 (-0.6%) | 1,298.6 → 1,295.7 (-0.2%) | 49.72 → 50.25 (+1.1%) | 51,305.5 → 51,752.2 (+0.9%) |

Geometric mean output throughput over the five cases: **+0.5%**. 

`rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` only selects the wvSplitK skinny kernels when the token count is at most 5. At concurrency 4 the decode batch stays inside that window, which is where the +3.5% comes from. Above it, the call falls through to `aiter.tuned_gemm.mm`, whose tuned table has no entry for the 513-wide fused gate, so the lookup misses and AITER circles back to its default `torch` solution -- the same rocBLAS kernel the previous `F.linear` used. Performance above that boundary is therefore unchanged by construction, and the flat rows are the expected result rather than a regression.

That gap is on the ROCm/AITER side, not in vLLM. Tuning the shape offline (N=513, K=8192, bf16, on gfx950) shows the fallback is leaving performance on the table at every batch size tested, at no cost in accuracy (error ratio 0.0 for every selected kernel):

| Tokens | rocBLAS fallback | Best available (hipBLASLt) | Speedup |
|--------|------------------|----------------------------|---------|
| 8 | 12.10 µs | 8.85 µs | 1.37x |
| 16 | 11.63 µs | 8.75 µs | 1.33x |
| 64 | 12.53 µs | 11.08 µs | 1.13x |
| 256 | 15.36 µs | 14.28 µs | 1.07x |
| 1024 | 28.86 µs | 23.25 µs | 1.24x |
| 8192 | 108.18 µs | 89.66 µs | 1.21x |

Closing that gap belongs in AITER, as tuned configurations for the fused gate width and, potentially, relaxed shape constraints. This PR is the prerequisite for any of it reaching the fused path: as long as the gate went through `F.linear`, AITER was never consulted for this GEMM at all. Once those configurations land, the fused gate picks them up with no further vLLM changes.

### GSM8K

5-shot, 1319 problems, `lm_eval` with `tensor_parallel_size=8`, `max_gen_toks=2048`, seed 4321.

| Arm | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|-----|------------------|--------------|
| Quark-MXFP4, fused shared experts off | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 |
| MoE-MXFP4, fused shared experts off | 0.9310 ± 0.0070 | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 |
| MoE-MXFP4, fused shared experts on | 0.9280 ± 0.0071 | 0.9280 ± 0.0071 |
| MoE-MXFP4, fused shared experts on, with this PR | 0.9227 ± 0.0074 | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 |

All four arms are statistically indistinguishable; the widest gap, between the Quark-MXFP4 reference and this PR, is 1.1 standard errors of the difference. The second arm isolates the checkpoint change (shared expert pre-quantized to MXFP4) from fusion itself, so the third is attributable to fusion alone, and the fourth to this patch alone.

---

title: [Kernel] Make prefix-prefill tiling independent of the KV page size
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Purpose

Hybrid mamba + full-attention models are given an attention page sized to match
the mamba page (544, 1040, 1056, ...), a multiple of the kernel alignment rather
than a power of two. `context_attention_fwd` keyed its tile sizes off that,
collapsing `BLOCK_M`/`BLOCK_N` from 128/64 down to 32/32.

That collapse is vestigial. It landed in #31380, the same commit that introduced
`PHYSICAL_BLOCK_SIZE` so page addressing would stop riding on the tile width.
Since then `_paged_kv_cache_offsets` resolves each context token individually, so
a tile may straddle a page; and `BLOCK_M` (query rows) and `BLOCK_N`
(current-chunk KV columns) never index the paged cache at all. Neither tile can
depend on the page being a power of two.

Power-of-two pages already selected 128/64 and are byte-for-byte unaffected.

The context tile width (`TRITON_BLOCK_SIZE`) is deliberately left at 32. Sweeping
it showed the best value depends on both page size and `head_size` — 32 wins when
it divides the page (544 = 32x17, 1056 = 32x33), 64/128 win when it does not
(1040 = 16x65) — which wants an autotuner rather than a new constant.

## Test Plan

Correctness is checked against an fp32 reference built by gathering K/V out of
the paged cache, rather than against the stock kernel, so "differs from before"
is distinguishable from "wrong". The harness is validated by a negative control
that forces the pre-#31380 addressing and must be flagged.

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py -k qwen3_nonstandard
```

`test_qwen3_nonstandard_block_size` is extended from one shape to three, adding
`head_size` 256 with pages 1040 and 1056 (Qwen3.5-MoE / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next),
where the query tile is the dominant consumer of registers.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2, torch 2.12, triton 3.7.1.

Full file, run on this branch and on an unmodified `origin/main` worktree:
**8 failed, 184 passed, 224 skipped** on both, with an identical failure set. All
8 pre-existing failures are in `chunked_prefill_paged_decode` at `head_size` 128
/ `num_queries_per_kv` 1 and are untouched by this change. The extended
`qwen3_nonstandard` selection is 12 passed.

Randomized correctness: 600 ragged batches across pages 128/512/544/1040/1056/
2048, `head_size` 64/128/256, MQA and GQA, sliding window, non-causal, and the
`k=None` cache-sourced path. Max abs deviation from the fp32 reference is
identical before and after the change in every case. 200 repeats are bitwise
identical, and re-checking after compiling 27 tile configs in-process rules out a
JIT-cache effect.

Kernel time, `triton.testing.do_bench`, interleaved A/B in one process, spread
across repeats <= 1.4%:

| shape | page 544, head_size 128 | page 1040, head_size 256 |
|---|---|---|
| 8192q + 0ctx | 1.370 -> 0.644 ms (2.13x) | 1.112 -> 0.720 ms (1.54x) |
| 4096q + 4096ctx | 2.247 -> 0.876 ms (2.56x) | 1.836 -> 1.068 ms (1.72x) |
| 2048q + 6144ctx | 2.638 -> 0.959 ms (2.75x) | 2.218 -> 1.291 ms (1.72x) |
| 512q + 8192ctx | 3.202 -> 1.151 ms (2.78x) | 2.779 -> 1.642 ms (1.69x) |
| ragged batch | 6.033 -> 2.484 ms (2.43x) | 5.639 -> 3.744 ms (1.51x) |

On accuracy: the change alters bf16 accumulation order, so outputs shift within
bf16 noise. What is verified is that the deviation from an fp32 reference is
*unchanged* by this patch on every shape tested above, i.e. the new tiling is no
further from exact arithmetic than the old one. An end-to-end model eval has not
been run yet; happy to add one if reviewers want it beyond the kernel-level
evidence.

## Not a duplicate

- No open PR touches `prefix_prefill` tiling.
- #53383 also edits `prefix_prefill.py` but adds a separate route for short-query
  / long-context (spec-decode verify) and explicitly leaves `_fwd_kernel` alone.
  Textual overlap in `context_attention_fwd` is possible; the changes are
  independent.
- #38454 is test-only.
- #35923 and #38454 concern whether hybrid non-standard block sizes *run*, not
  how they are tiled.

## Notes for reviewers

- The non-power-of-two page is produced in `Platform.check_and_update_config`,
  which is platform-agnostic, so CUDA hybrid models were taking the 32/32
  collapse too and should see the same benefit. The extended test keeps the
  pre-existing ROCm-only skip; dropping it would widen coverage but I have only
  validated on gfx950.
- Separately noticed and *not* addressed here: the context loop's block-table
  load is unmasked, which is only safe while `query_len >= BLOCK_SIZE`. The
  values are always correct (the lanes are dropped by the K/V mask), but the
  address can leave the row. Both fixes I tried (masking, clamping) cost 5-12%,
  apparently by defeating scalarization of that load, so this deserves its own
  change rather than being folded into a perf PR.

AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Structured Output] Let terminal grammars stop under min_tokens (II)
author: arpera
body:
## Purpose

min_tokens can force structured-output requests to sample outside the grammar after a short schema reaches its terminal state. For schemas such as {"type":"boolean"}, {"enum":["a"]}, or {"type":"null"}, the grammar's only legal continuation after the value is EOS. min_tokens then masks EOS because the request has not reached the requested minimum length, leaving no legal token.

This PR was created as a continuation of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47489 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49521 to fix the issue reported also here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53665.
Also this PR fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51299 since the fix is in the same code area.

Moreover the issue with min_tokens + structured-output constraints is even worse. It can also be reproduced with any "semantic masking" logit processor like structured outputs, allowed_token_ids, min_tokens, bad_words that can mask out all token_ids (all logits are -inf). See original [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47489#issuecomment-5062309103). This PR does not try to fix all the other logit processors, only focusing for now on min_tokens + structured output. Full fix requires larger refactor and is left for future attempts.

## Test Plan

<details>
<summary>Repro for PR #47489 for both MRV1 and MRV2 ([original gist](https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/40200cc3831c38f9e79b44182328c08b))</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Repro for min_tokens + terminal structured-output schemas (#47489)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import cleanup_dist_env_and_memory
from vllm.sampling_params import StructuredOutputsParams


def run(llm: LLM, label: str, schema: dict, min_tokens: int) -> None:
    params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0.0,
        min_tokens=min_tokens,
        max_tokens=40,
        structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json=json.dumps(schema)),
    )
    output = llm.generate(["Answer:"], params, use_tqdm=False)[0].outputs[0]
    print(
        label,
        repr(output.text),
        len(output.token_ids),
        output.token_ids,
        output.finish_reason,
        output.stop_reason,
    )


def run_cases(llm: LLM, runner_label: str) -> None:
    cases = [
        ("control-bool", {"type": "boolean"}, 0),
        ("min-bool", {"type": "boolean"}, 20),
        ("min-enum", {"enum": ["a"]}, 20),
        ("min-null", {"type": "null"}, 30),
    ]
    for name, schema, min_tokens in cases:
        run(llm, f"{runner_label}/{name}", schema, min_tokens)


def main() -> None:
    for use_v2 in (False, True):
        runner_label = "v2" if use_v2 else "v1"
        os.environ["VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER"] = "1" if use_v2 else "0"
        print(f"=== Model runner {runner_label.upper()} ===")
        llm = LLM(
            model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
            enforce_eager=True,
            gpu_memory_utilization=0.30,
            max_model_len=512,
            structured_outputs_config={"backend": "xgrammar"},
        )
        try:
            run_cases(llm, runner_label)
        finally:
            del llm
            cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
</details>

**PASSED**

```python
# hangs forever before this PR

             SamplingParams(max_tokens=500, min_tokens=500, ignore_eos=True))
```

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Fix MXFP8 startup crash on layers below mm_mxfp8 shape limits
author: samuelkim7
body:
## Purpose

`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --quantization mxfp8` dies in the profile run on a B200 with `AssertionError: mm_mxfp8 requires N >= 128, got N=32`. The layer is the GDN `in_proj_ba` (weight 32 x 1024). The larger Qwen3.5 sizes and Qwen3-Next have N=64 or N=96 there, so the whole family fails to start with online MXFP8.

`FlashInferCutlassMxfp8LinearKernel` and `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel` return `True` from `can_implement` for every layer. The `mm_mxfp8` shape limits (N >= 128, K >= 128, K % 32 == 0) are only asserts inside `apply_weights`, so on SM100 a layer below the limits is still selected instead of falling through to Marlin.

`Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig` gains a two-element `(N, K)` `weight_shape`, and the two FlashInfer kernels share a shape validator called by `can_implement`. CUTLASS adds its SM12x-specific alignment check. The compressed-tensors, INC and online MXFP8 schemes select the kernel in `create_weights` instead of `__init__`, the per-layer pattern `Fp8LinearMethod` already uses. ModelOpt already selects in `create_weights` since #49381, so there this PR forwards the weight shape and extracts the trailing `(N, K)` dimensions at the BMM re-selection call site. No kernel code changes.

From @stecasta's review: on SM12x the CUTLASS kernel also rejects N % 32 != 0, and `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel.can_implement` now rejects N <= 0, K <= 0 and K % 32 != 0.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_kernel_selection.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py tests/model_executor/kernels/test_b12x_linear.py tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_amd_ops.py tests/quantization/test_auto_round.py -k "mxfp8 or inc or selection or b12x or minimax"
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_tile_padding.py -k test_mxfp8_marlin_padded_round_trip  # GPU
```

On a B200 I ran `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B", quantization="mxfp8")` on `main` and with this patch applied, then generated 8 tokens.

## Test result

The first two commands give 164 passed and 11 skipped on CPU, on the rebased branch (main 54020c3c3e). On an L4 and an RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), the third passes for all five shapes, including the new (32, 256), (96, 256) and (130, 256). `pre-commit run` is clean on the changed files. The B200 run below is from the original base d1922cb5a; the rebase changed no kernel code.

B200, vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev49+gd1922cb5a, FlashInfer 0.6.17, CUDA 13.0:

| arm | startup | MXFP8 kernels selected | output for "The capital of France is" |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | fails in `profile_run` after 52 s: `AssertionError: mm_mxfp8 requires N >= 128, got N=32` | `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel` | none |
| this PR | ok | `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel`, `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel` | ` Paris.` |

`in_proj_ba` is the only quantized linear in this model with N < 128, so it is the layer Marlin took (padded to N=64, the log shows the Marlin padding warning). Every other layer still gets the FlashInfer kernel.

title: [ROCm] Expose kFp8DynamicTokenSym on AITER PTPC linears
author: rebklee
body:
## Purpose
`FP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` already no-ops in-kernel quant on a matching `QuantizedActivation`. The AITER PTPC kernels never exposed `input_quant_key()`, so `expose_input_quant_key` left the layer unmarked and producers could not skip `dynamic_per_token_scaled_quant`.

Return `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` from `input_quant_key()` on the AITER PTPC kernels (AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel, AiterPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel, AiterHipbMMPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel).

`Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` and `QuarkW8A8Fp8` call `expose_input_quant_key` after kernel init.

Not a duplicate. [#44260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44260) landed the QuantizedActivation contract and CUDA static-FP8 consumers; AITER PTPC kernels still return None, so expose_input_quant_key never marks the layer. [#44132](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44132) added Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod without that call. [#33773](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33773) landed the GEMMs, not the fusion key.

title: [Kernel] Warm up Qwen GDN gated RMSNorm
author: zupengwang
body:
## Purpose

Refs #49349.

Qwen3.5's GDN output projection calls the FLA `layer_norm_fwd_kernel` through
`RMSNormGated`. With cold Triton/vLLM caches, the first real request compiled
this specialization after the JIT monitor became active:

```text
ACTIVATION='silu', BLOCK_N=128, HAS_BIAS=False, HAS_Z=True,
IS_RMS_NORM=True, N=128, NORM_BEFORE_GATE=True, ROWS_PER_BLOCK=4,
X/Y/W/Z='*bf16'
```

This PR moves that compilation into startup warmup by:

- adding a shared `VllmJitKernel` wrapper for the FLA layer-norm forward kernel;
- using the same compile-key dispatch contract for runtime execution and
  compile-only warmup;
- enumerating the `M` specialization and `ROWS_PER_BLOCK` keys implied by the
  configured token limit and TP-local Qwen value-head count; and
- registering the Qwen GDN gated RMSNorm configuration with its actual dtypes,
  head dimension, activation, and gate ordering.

The warmup uses `TritonWarmupTensor` descriptors and does not allocate or launch
dummy inference tensors.

This does not duplicate #51134, which removes an obsolete FlashInfer startup
warning but does not warm this Triton kernel. It also does not overlap #50279,

title: [Kimi-K3] Add FlashInfer speculative KDA backend
author: djmmoss
body:
## Purpose

Integrate FlashInfer's packed fused KDA kernel into Kimi-K3 speculative decode.
For supported pure speculative-decode batches, this replaces separate short
convolution, recurrent KDA, and gated normalization launches with
`flashinfer.packed_fused_kda_decode`. Unsupported configurations and mixed
batches retain the existing vLLM paths.

The backend defaults to `auto` and can be forced with
`additional_config.kda_spec_decode_backend={native,flashinfer}`. Eligibility is
fail-closed: the FlashInfer API, SM100-family CUDA, supported Kimi-K3 shapes and
dtypes, a bounded gate, the SD convolution-cache layout, and RecoverSSM being
disabled are all required. The recurrent state may be float32 or bfloat16;
bfloat16 needs flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5503.

No competing open PR implementing this packed FlashInfer speculative-KDA path
was found. #53525 optimizes the native single-token PDL path and does not
overlap this integration.

AI assistance was used in developing this contribution.

## Test Plan

```text
pytest -q tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py
```

The tests cover backend selection and fallback, cache-layout rejection, the
production `_forward` integration for float32 and bfloat16 recurrent state,
cache/state parity with the composed reference, null speculative rows,
accepted-token updates, and dynamic CUDA Graph metadata.

## Test Result

On one NVIDIA B300 (SM103), vLLM `2d50faf829` with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5503
(`1e381ec10`):

```text
111 passed, 7 skipped
```

The 7 skips are existing single-token FlashInfer decode cases (DS conv layout,
unfused output norm).

### Real-model evaluation

The native and FlashInfer backends were evaluated on eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs
with `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` revision `a590ce090c` and the
`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` draft model revision `cf6b824462` using six draft
tokens. Both runs used vLLM head `3324e3c7e3`, FlashInfer head `609ec78b49`,
temperature 0, and seed 42.

| Evaluation | Native | FlashInfer | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 questions | 94.693%, 153.1 s | 95.299%, 142.2 s | +0.607 percentage points; 1.077x lower wall time |
| OCRBench, 1,000 questions | 908 and 905 | 906 | FlashInfer is within the native repeat range |

For GSM8K, 1,283/1,319 extracted answers matched between backends. A full
FlashInfer repeat produced the exact same response checksum and completed in
141.1 s. OCRBench's native responses and score varied across two concurrent
runs, so its latency is not used to claim a backend speedup; FlashInfer's score
falls inside the observed native 905-908 range.

### Synthetic serving performance

An eight-B300 synthetic Kimi-K3/DSpark A/B (six draft tokens, 8K input, 1K
output) matched the baseline checksum. Total output throughput versus the
native backend:

| Recurrent state | c=1 | c=4 | c=8 | c=16 | c=32 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| float32 (default) | +2.63% | +2.54% | +3.29% | +1.76% | +1.75% |
| bfloat16 (`--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16`) | +5.55% | +4.45% | +2.98% | +0.98% | +1.34% |

The bfloat16 row used this branch at `2d50faf829` with
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5503; both backends ran with bfloat16 state and
produced the same checksum.

title: [Kimi-K3][Perf] Make native CUDA AttnRes the SM100 default
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

Make the native CUDA Kimi-K3 AttnRes implementation the default for dense
`hidden_size=7168` inputs on SM100.

This PR:

- extends the existing register/TMEM kernel to cover block counts 0 through 8,
  optional prefix addition, optional output normalization, and block-bank
  writes;
- uses the existing source-chunk schedule for all supported block counts,
  while preserving a compile-time-folded common path;
- makes output normalization a compile-time specialization so the disabled
  path elides its shared-memory buffer, barrier, and arithmetic;
- delays the PDL wait until the first producer-dependent prefix or delta TMA
  for every native shape and triggers dependents after the producer TMAs;
- retains Triton as the fallback for unsupported devices and non-dense row
  layouts; and
- adds a reproducible CUDA-versus-Triton kernel benchmark.

Duplicate-work check: the author of #53524 coordinated moving its AttnRes PDL
handoff into this integrated change; that PR's remaining distinct scope is its
C=1 MoE/router work. #50760 changes warmup profiles only. Neither otherwise
extends the native kernel to all Kimi-K3 AttnRes call variants.

## Performance

Measured on GPU 7, an NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, with PyTorch 2.13.0 and CUDA 13.0.
Times are median microseconds; lower is better.

| Tokens | Blocks | Triton | CUDA | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0 | 8.19 | 8.19 | 1.00x |
| 1 | 1 | 10.24 | 8.19 | 1.25x |
| 1 | 4 | 12.29 | 8.22 | 1.49x |
| 1 | 8 | 14.34 | 10.24 | 1.40x |
| 4096 | 8 | 204.77 | 122.88 | 1.67x |
| 8192 | 8 | 395.30 | 229.44 | 1.72x |

For the measured `M <= 16` cases with one or more block rows, CUDA was 1.20x
to 1.49x faster than Triton. The zero-block path tied Triton at 8.19 us.

In a captured single-token CUDA graph, profiler device rows for the CUDA
kernel were 3.67, 4.44, and 5.48 us for 1, 4, and 8 block rows. Full graph
replay medians were 8.03, 10.05, and 10.05 us, respectively.

The no-output-normalization specialization was neutral for the measured
`M <= 16` cases and up to 4.6% faster for larger measured shapes. For example,
the 8-block, M=1024 case improved from 40.86 to 38.98 us.

## Test Plan

```bash
cmake --build cmake-build-release --target _C_stable_libtorch
cmake --install cmake-build-release --component _C_stable_libtorch

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_attn_res.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_aux_attn_res_stream.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py -q

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_attn_res.py \
  --num-tokens 1 16 1024 4096 8192 \
  --num-blocks 0 1 4 8 --warmup-ms 50 --repeat-ms 200

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_attn_res.py \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/attn_res_kernel.cu \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/ops.h \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/torch_bindings.cpp \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_attn_res.py \
  vllm/_custom_ops.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/attn_res.py
```

## Test Result

- Incremental CUDA build: passed.
- Focused Kimi-K3 suite: 34 passed, 9 platform skips.
- Benchmark reference checks for 0, 1, 4, and 8 blocks: passed.
- All pre-commit hooks on changed files: passed.
- Model evaluation: run on the full Kimi-K3 checkpoint across five serving
  configurations; see Model Evaluation below. Kernel outputs and in-place
  mutations are additionally checked against the PyTorch reference across all
  block counts and fused variants.

## Model Evaluation

Full `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (MXFP4) on GB300 (SM100), vLLM
`0.17.2rc1.dev5039+g73b83949f`, across five serving configurations. GSM8K is
5-shot via `/v1/completions` (temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95); OCRBench is
multimodal chat with thinking effort high (temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0).
Reported scores are GSM8K strict-match exact match and OCRBench Final Score
Norm.

| Config | Topology | GSM8K | OCRBench | Request errors |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP8 | TP8 | 95.53% (n=1319) | 89.3 (893/1000) | 0 |
| TEP8 | TP8 + EP | 97.27% (n=1319) | 89.3 (893/1000) | 0 |
| DEP16 | TP1 x DP16 x EP16 | 95.98% (n=1319) | 89.2 (892/1000) | 0 |
| TP8, `--max-num-seqs 16` | TP8, eval concurrency 8 | 96.36% (n=1319) | n/a | 0 |
| TP8, serial | TP8, eval concurrency 1 | 99.60% (n=250) | n/a | 0 |

No accuracy regression. GSM8K spans 95.5% to 97.3% across topologies, which is
within run-to-run variance for temperature-0.6 sampling (roughly +/-0.5 point
standard error at n=1319). OCRBench agrees to within 0.1 point across the three
multimodal configurations.

The two low-concurrency rows are the most direct check on this change: they
hold decode batches at 1 to 16 tokens, the small-batch regime this PR moves
from Triton onto the native kernel. The serial row's 99.60% reflects its
250-sample subset rather than a topology difference -- scoring the TP8 run's
own outputs on those identical 250 items gives 98.80%, a two-item difference.

benchmarking, testing, and PR preparation. This PR is left as a draft until the

change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix Mooncake physical-block transfer length
author: zhewenl
body:
## What and why

Mooncake can silently corrupt attention KV data when the scheduler logical block size is larger than the attention kernel physical block size.

For Kimi-K3, one 768-token logical attention block expands into twelve 64-token kernel block IDs. Mooncake expands the IDs correctly, but previously attached the full logical `page_size_bytes` of 884,736 bytes to every physical-block descriptor even though the physical stride is 73,728 bytes. Adjacent descriptors therefore overlap by 12x and overwrite neighboring blocks under concurrency.

This is a vLLM transfer-metadata bug, not a Mooncake TransferEngine or deployment-environment issue.

## Changes

- Divide contiguous `AttentionSpec` transfer length by `physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block` after logical block IDs are expanded.
- Reject any descriptor whose transfer length exceeds the physical block stride.
- Add a focused ratio-greater-than-one registration regression test.
- Correct an existing mixed MLA/Eagle test fixture whose mock tensor stride was smaller than its declared cache-spec page.

This PR intentionally does not include unrelated Mamba slot handling, hybrid/heterogeneous-TP planning, producer or consumer synchronization fences, debug logging, or Mooncake TransferEngine workarounds.

## Relation to existing work

- #46334 identified the logical-versus-physical block-size problem, but it is closed and unmerged and used a block-folding approach.
- #46807 merged logical-ID expansion for Mooncake. This PR keeps that expansion and fixes the missing per-physical-block descriptor-length conversion.
- The fix is generic to contiguous `AttentionSpec` layouts with a logical-to-physical ratio greater than one; it is not limited to Kimi-K3 or MLA by model name.

## Validation

Unit tests on the PR parent:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py

38 passed
```

Kimi-K3 Mooncake PD, TP8 producer to TP8 consumer, GB300, runtime logical block 768 and physical kernel block 64:

- GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1,319 examples, concurrency 64
- flexible-extract: **0.9659**
- strict-match: **0.9659**
- request errors: **0**
- Mooncake transfer failures: **0**
- Mooncake receive failures: **0**

This matches the NIXL baseline of approximately 0.97 and the prior full-patch run of 0.9666.

## AI assistance

Codex was used during root-cause analysis, test authoring, patch minimization, and validation. The author reviewed the changed lines and ran the reported unit and model evaluations.

title: [Attention][DCP] Enable FlashInfer MLA for DSpark drafting
author: GirasoleY
body:
## Summary

- Recompute rank-local DCP sequence lengths from the draft model's current global sequence lengths before every shared draft metadata build.
- Share that metadata plumbing across EAGLE, MTP, DFlash, and DSpark, removing DFlash's duplicate preparation.
- Keep causal target MLA layers and non-causal DSpark draft layers in separate KV-cache groups by requiring the group to agree on `non_causal_multi_token_decode`.
- Advertise FlashInfer MLA support for non-causal multi-token DCP drafting.
- Repeat global causal sequence boundaries when non-causal DSpark blocks are flattened into single-token decode rows.
- Add focused metadata and backend regressions.

## Motivation

DSpark needs two complementary pieces for FlashInfer MLA under DCP:

1. Draft attention must recompute rank-local sequence lengths from its own current global sequence lengths. Reusing target-local lengths is not sufficient because draft steps advance or rewind `input_buffers.seq_lens` after sampling and rejection.
2. FlashInfer's non-causal DSpark path flattens each query block into independent decode rows. Under DCP, the local block table and sequence lengths were expanded, but the global causal boundaries were not, leaving the native CP kernel with mismatched batch geometry.

The cache-group merge also used `any(non_causal_multi_token_decode)`, which could promote a causal target group to the draft's non-causal behavior. Requiring agreement keeps target and draft groups distinct.

Putting rank-local preparation in the shared draft metadata builder also fixes the same missing plumbing for EAGLE and MTP while preserving existing DFlash behavior.

## Tests

Passed:

- 12 focused B300 unit tests covering FlashInfer MLA DCP metadata/backend behavior
- pre-commit/static validation before the conflict-free rebase
- `uvx --offline ruff check` on all eight changed Python files after combining the commits
- `uvx --offline ruff format --check`
- `python3 -m py_compile`
- `git diff --check`

End-to-end Kimi-K3 DSpark+DCP evaluation is pending because the available dev GPUs were occupied.

## Relationship to existing work

- Builds on causal native FlashInfer MLA DCP support from #54012.
- Independent of the scheduler/verifier/full-CUDA-graph fixes in #54102.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to compare k3-dev with current upstream, trace the shared draft metadata paths, isolate the backend-independent and FlashInfer-specific pieces, write the initial patches/tests, and run validation. The submitter will review every changed line and complete end-to-end evaluation.

title: [Bugfix][Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Decouple the draft's gumbel noise stream from the target's
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# Context
Picking up the work from #47386. During target verification, the Gumbel noise used to re-sample a rejected draft token is drawn from the same Philox offset as the noise that produced that draft token (the same seed, pos), so byte-identical noise. Conditioned on the proposal winning the argmax, the other tokens' Gumbels are truncated below that max, most tightly for the tokens the draft ranked highest, but lost (high-q loser tokens generally have smaller noise, because otherwise they would have won), so the residual under-weights exactly those tokens and the output distribution is no longer the target's.

This affects `draft_sample_method="probabilistic"` only. Under the default greedy, `draft_logits` is None, the draft never calls `gumbel_sample`, and there is no shared noise vector.

# This PR
Adds a salt (1 << 30) to the offset of the draft's Philox stream, decoupling the draft's Gumbel noise from the target's. Verification is a probability-ratio test against the cached draft distribution rather than a Gumbel coupling, so nothing depends on the two streams matching.

Also refactors how the speculators compute the position used as the sampling-stream index, so each site states its own convention instead of relying on an implicit +1 inside sample_draft. This incidentally fixes a second latent issue: the sampling position was previously derived from a buffer clamped at max_model_len, so near the context limit two consecutive draft steps could reuse one noise vector. It is now tracked unclamped.

# Tests
```
gdelfin@gb200-rack1-18:~/vllm$ python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py::test_gumbel_drafted_rejection_sample_is_unbiased -q
Running 2 items in this shard
..                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          [100%]
2 passed in 2.96s

gdelfin@gb200-rack1-18:~/vllm$ python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py::test_drafting_uses_a_separate_noise_stream -q
Running 1 items in this shard
.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           [100%]
1 passed in 3.92s
```

— 2K in / 2K out, 512 prompts, 64 warmups, concurrency 64, `temperature=1.0 top_p=0.95 top_k=20`.
All runs use `draft_sample_method: probabilistic` (the salt is a no-op under the default `greedy`,
where the draft never calls `gumbel_sample`). 4× GB200, TP4 except Gemma 4 (TP1).
Baseline `de9250ac9e` → this PR `1529dd5363`.

| Model | N | Output tok/s | Acceptance length | Acceptance rate % | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) |
|:--|--:|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Stop offloading the final sampled token's KV slot
author: almogtavor
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54193.

`_build_store_jobs` lets a finished request offload up to `req.num_tokens`. The last of those tokens has no KV of its own because it was produced by the forward pass at the position before it and the request ends before any pass covers its own slot. The last position with KV that anything wrote is therefore `num_tokens - 1` and a finish landing on a block boundary hands the offload tier a full block whose final slot sits past that point.

Offloaded blocks are keyed by a hash of their token ids and every id involved is legitimate. A later request that replays the same tokens in normal multi-turn chat will therefore match the hash and load the bad block. In the reproduction below the GPU prefix cache commits one block where the offload path stored two.

Under speculative decoding the junk is dangerous since Spec decode proposes several draft tokens, runs them all through the model, then throws away the rejected ones. Slot 3 that was never written for that token (although we generated the [0,1,2,3] tokens), can hold the KV of the first rejected draft. It’s a KV vector for a token that vllm decided not to keep, but downstream it looks legitimate.
The cache key is a hash of [a, b, c, EOS] so later request that happens to start with those same four tokens gets a hit and loads the poisoned block, so the model attends to a token that wasnt accepted.

## Fix

`num_tokens_after_batch = max(req.num_prompt_tokens, req.num_tokens - 1)` in the finished branch.

I compared that against `num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders`, the confirmed-token formula used by both `AsyncScheduler._update_request_with_output` and `simple_kv_offload`. One H100 running Qwen3-30B-A3B-W4A16 with 11 finished requests observed per configuration:

| configuration | confirmed-token formula matched `num_tokens - 1` | `max()` changed the answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sync, no spec decode | 11/11 | never |
| async, no spec decode | 11/11 | never |
| sync, ngram spec decode | 5/11 | never |
| async, ngram_gpu spec decode | 11/11 | never |

The confirmed-token formula runs ahead by up to `num_speculative_tokens` under synchronous speculative decoding because `num_computed_tokens` counts the whole scheduled batch before rejected drafts are rolled back. Logged cases had `num_computed_tokens` at 28 and 60 and 98 where `num_tokens - 1` was 27 and 57 and 95. The `max()` suggested in the issue applies only to a request that finishes without generating anything and nothing reaches this branch in that state because aborted requests take the branch above it and pooling requests finish in the same step they prefill so they take the running branch instead. A pooling probe of 12 requests saw none arrive here. The `max()` therefore never changed an answer but it costs nothing and covers the case if a future caller does reach it.

#48596 added this branch so that the block completed at finish would stop being skipped. Skipping it is the correct behaviour and the branch still runs for every other block so the worker side fence fix from that PR is untouched.

## Reproduction

CPU only. A 7-token prompt finishing on a block boundary has the GPU prefix cache committing 1 block while the offload path stores 2. A second request whose prompt is the first request's full token stream including EOS then gets content-hash hits on both.

## Measured on one H100

Qwen3-30B-A3B-W4A16 with `offload_prompt_only: false` because the default of true clamps the watermark down to the prompt and hides this branch completely.

A request finishing at exactly 64 tokens was snapshotted at the step before it finished and again at the step it finished. Slot 63 of its last GPU block was bit identical across that final forward pass and held all zeros while slot 62 went from zero to a norm of 526. The store job emitted at that same step copied that GPU block to the offload tier.

A later request whose prompt starts with those 64 tokens then loaded the block back into fresh GPU blocks. Position 63 came back all zeros while its fifteen neighbours ranged from 506 to 538 so the model decoded while attending to an empty slot.

Changing the one line to `num_tokens - 1` stops that store job. The same later request recomputes the block instead and position 63 comes back at 520.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector -q
```

`241 passed, 2 skipped`. Three tests encoded the old watermark and now assert the corrected contract, with `test_last_block_offloaded_at_request_finish` renamed to `test_final_sampled_token_does_not_complete_an_offloaded_block`. Running those tests against unfixed source gives `4 failed, 237 passed, 2 skipped`.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` at v0.14.0 pass on both changed files. No model eval because the measurement above reads the KV cache directly and is exact where sampled output on this mixture of experts model drifts between runs of identical code.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR touches this branch.

title: [Perf] Pin CPU tensors before non_blocking H2D in three MM paths
author: JasonKeyiL

author: JasonKeyiL

title: [Bugfix] Gate sm_100-only kernel tests on the capability family, not >=
author: bojiang3
body:
## Summary

`has_device_capability(100)` is a `>=` test, so a device reporting capability 12.1 satisfies it. Tests that guard sm_100-only kernels with it therefore **run** on consumer and workstation Blackwell, where those kernels do not exist, and fail instead of skipping.

`is_device_capability_family(100)` is the check these guards want. Its docstring states the difference:

> Returns True if the device capability is any `<major>.x`. Mirrors CUDA 13 'family' architecture semantics (e.g. 10.x, 11.x, 12.x).

`test_cutlass_mla_decode.py` already uses it at line 39; this makes the rest of that file, and the sibling MoE tests, consistent.

## Verification

Measured on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), before → after:

| test file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `test_cutlass_mla_decode.py` | 49 failed | 49 skipped |
| `test_cutedsl_moe.py` | 1 failed | 1 skipped |
| `test_trtllm_bf16_moe.py` | 1 failed | 1 skipped |
| `test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py` | 1 failed | 1 skipped |
| `test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py` | 1 failed | 1 skipped |

## These were genuine absences, not hidden defects

Skipping a test can hide a real bug, so each guard here was checked against what the failure actually was:

* `_C::sm100_cutlass_mla_get_workspace_size` — `NotImplementedError`, no implementation registered for this device
* `test_cutedsl_moe` — the kernel itself reports `['sm_100', 'sm_103'] are the only supported SM versions`
* the three TRT-LLM paths — abort inside `TrtllmGenBatchedGemmRunner`

Only guards whose kernel is genuinely sm_100-family-only are changed. Other tests that fail on this hardware for numerical or unrelated reasons are deliberately left alone — those need their own investigation, not a skip.

## Why this wasn't caught in CI

vLLM's CI does not run on consumer or workstation Blackwell, so `>=` and family checks are indistinguishable there: every device that satisfies one satisfies the other.

title: [KV Connector] Support heterogeneous TP sharing for hybrid KV cache in Mooncake Store
author: chengy-sysu
body:
## Dependency

Depends on #53129.

This is a follow-up PR that extends the heterogeneous TP Store layout
introduced in #53129 to unified hybrid KV caches. Please review the
Hybrid-specific commits after #53129. The dependency changes will
disappear from this PR diff after #53129 merges and this branch is
rebased onto upstream `main`.

Merge order:

1. #53129
2. This PR

## Purpose

This PR extends heterogeneous-TP sharing in `MooncakeStoreConnector` from a
single Full Attention cache group to unified Hybrid KV cache allocations. vLLM
instances whose local TP sizes divide a common Store TP size can share the same
Attention KV and Mamba/GDN state through Mooncake Store. Sharing endpoints use
the same PP size.

Hybrid KV cache adds three challenges beyond Full Attention:

- Attention KV grows by token, while Mamba/GDN groups store complete recurrent
  checkpoints with different TP replication rules;
- vLLM aligns Attention pages with Mamba/GDN state pages, so the local page size
  can change with TP size even when two endpoints use the same model;
- prefix reuse must intersect the available boundaries of every cache group,
  while Decode writeback may advance each group at a different rate.

This PR builds on the common Store TP layout from #53129 and represents each
cache group in a stable Store namespace. Attention uses TP-independent Store
chunks, while Mamba/GDN uses complete state checkpoints. These Store boundaries
are independent of the endpoint's local Hybrid page allocation.

### Unified Hybrid Store layout

Each cache group creates its Store layout from its `KVCacheSpec`:

- Attention groups divide global KV head slots into the fixed Store TP shards;
- MQA and replicated GQA use their physical head-slot count for Store sharding;
- Mamba/GDN groups store complete convolution and recurrent state units and
  map replicated local units to their Store shards;
- `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` is unwrapped before the group layout is planned;
- each group namespace includes its Store value format and schema fingerprint.

`StoreLayout` owns tensor interpretation, shard mapping, buffer spans, and Store
keys. The worker executes the resulting descriptors through a common path.

### Attention layouts

The heterogeneous Store path supports the backend-native LBHNC, BLHNC, LHBNC,
BHLNC, LBNHC, and BLNHC cache layouts.

- LBHNC, BLHNC, LHBNC, and BHLNC are normalized to the same head-major Store
  value order;
- LBNHC and BLNHC are normalized to the same token-major Store value order;
- endpoints whose local layouts produce the same Store value order share one
  namespace;
- head-major and token-major Store values remain isolated by their schema.

### Store chunks and local Hybrid pages

`store_chunk_size` defines the stable number of tokens represented by one
Attention Store object. A local Attention page can contain multiple Store
chunks. The connector reads and writes those chunks through tensor-offset
descriptors, so endpoints can share Store objects when their local Hybrid page
sizes differ.

Hybrid heterogeneous-TP sharing requires the same explicit
`--prefix-match-unit` on every endpoint. The connector uses that prefix-hash
boundary as `store_chunk_size` when no Store-specific value is configured. An
explicit larger `store_chunk_size` may reduce Store object and metadata
overhead:

```json
{
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
        "store_tp_size": 4,
        "store_chunk_size": 400,
        "save_decode_cache": true
    }
}
```

The configured value must be a multiple of `prefix_match_unit`, align with
every stored state, and divide the local Attention page. Invalid or
incompatible configurations use the isolated rank-local Store namespace.

### Hybrid lookup and Decode writeback

Hybrid prefix lookup intersects the availability of all required cache groups
at each reusable boundary. Attention chunks may be stored before the next full
Hybrid checkpoint. Mamba/GDN entries remain complete state snapshots at their
reusable boundaries, so lookup exposes a longer prefix only after every group
required at that boundary is present.

Decode offloading tracks acknowledged progress per cache group. Attention can
advance independently while a Mamba/GDN group waits for its next complete
checkpoint. A failed PUT retries from the earliest unacknowledged offset for
that group. Partial physical cache blocks are stored from their copy-on-write
handoff sources, allowing a hash-aligned Store chunk to be written before its
larger local page is complete.

Scheduler Store-job boundaries, prefix-hash boundaries, local cache pages, and
KV-event block boundaries are resolved independently. KV events continue to
describe the scheduler's logical block chain while Store jobs operate on the
finer Hybrid checkpoint when required.

### Supported scope

Shared endpoints satisfy the compatibility requirements from #53129 and the
following Hybrid constraints:

- Store TP size is greater than or equal to local TP size and divisible by it;
- all sharing endpoints use the same Store TP size and PP size;
- Attention head slots and Store shards have an integral divisible mapping;
- cache groups use supported Attention specs or `MambaSpec`, including
  supported `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` wrappers;
- Mamba/GDN convolution state uses DS or SD layout; sharing endpoints use the
  same layout;
- PCP and DCP are disabled;
- cross-layer KV blocks are disabled.

Endpoints outside this scope retain the existing rank-local behavior.

This PR updates the Mooncake Store Connector documentation and adds regression
coverage for:

- mixed Attention and Mamba/GDN cache groups;
- per-group TP replication and Store-shard ownership;
- all six backend-native Attention cache layouts;
- head-major and token-major Store schema normalization;
- TP-independent Store chunk selection and explicit `store_chunk_size`;
- Hybrid local pages containing multiple Store chunks;
- partial-tail PUT and GET from copy-on-write cache blocks;
- per-group acknowledged Store progress and PUT retries;
- prefix lookup across cache groups with different reusable boundaries;
- scheduler Store-job, prefix-hash, and KV-event boundary separation;
- rank-local fallback for unsupported or incompatible configurations.

## Related Issues and PRs

- Issue #45036 tracks the Mooncake Store Connector roadmap, including Decode
  KV PUT and heterogeneous GQA/TP sharing. This PR extends that work to Hybrid
  KV cache allocations with divisible TP sizes.
- PR #52466 added Decode KV offloading to Mooncake Store consumers. This PR
  applies the same consumer writeback lifecycle independently across Hybrid
  cache groups.
- PR #53129 introduces the common Store TP layout for Full Attention KV cache.
  This PR uses that layout as its base and extends the Store planning,
  namespace, lookup, and writeback paths to Hybrid KV cache.
- PR #53078 adds heterogeneous-TP support for Hybrid GDN/Mamba models to
  `MooncakeConnector` direct P/D transfer. This PR targets persistent and
  reusable KV objects in `MooncakeStoreConnector`, including prefix lookup and
  Decode writeback through a shared Store pool.

## Test Plan

### Unit and static checks

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  docs/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage.md \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_layout.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/data.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/ssm_conv_transfer_utils.py

python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_layout.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py
```

### RDMA cluster tests

Reusable E2E test code:
