title: [Docker] Compile Python bytecode at image build time
author: matteso1
body:
## Purpose

Fresh containers compile thousands of Python files during startup. This PR sets `UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1` in eight Dockerfiles, moving that work into image construction through uv's existing option.

## Current CI (September 24)

[CI 91034](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034) is running on `da0a5f6ed074`. The [H100 fault-tolerance job](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034#01a0d50c-2031-49c0-ba53-07b204574241) now passes both tests with #58593 included. The nightly dependency check also [passed its one retry](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034#01a0d546-42ce-499d-8f60-5ba7cfd9fac9), after SQLAlchemy's compatible wheel became available.

The [structured-output failure](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034#01a0d50c-202c-4b63-9825-46865a4c852a) repeats with the same parameter and output on main [91027](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91027) and [91036](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91036). B200 Mooncake already has an [automatic retry](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034#01a0d550-1a3d-44f0-b04a-721008e9d67b) queued. [AMD 13576](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13576) timed out after slow checkpoint loading; its later stall remains unexplained. That native job consumes a wheel built before the changed final-image stage. Other jobs are still running.

The diff remains eight ENV lines plus one blank line. Pre-commit and paired Linux CPU Dockerfile definition checks pass, with the same two existing warnings as main. The head is unchanged while this run finishes.

## Results

### Matched build, delivery, and serving

I built `470fe3942ecdb889b2f3c0b57ace4b09d61dd103` with and without the CUDA Dockerfile ENV line (`vllm-openai`, CUDA sm_89, Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, uv 0.12.10). Source, interpreter, 244 Python distributions, 26,734 Python files, native payloads, and non-bytecode site-packages bytes matched. Each observation pulled from a loopback registry into an empty Docker store, then served local/offline Qwen3-0.6B through the first correct HTTP completion on one RTX 4090 Laptop with a four-CPU quota.

| Artifact | Compressed runtime layers | Median pull to correct response |
|---|---:|---:|
| Control, gzip | 8,511,741,380 bytes | 155.7265 s |
| Bytecode, gzip | 8,664,824,384 bytes | 144.5137 s |

The bytecode image adds 153,083,004 compressed bytes (+1.7985%). Its median paired saving is **15.3606 s**, n=3 pairs, and all three pairs improved. Five independent next-token checks and four-request bursts passed per activation with matching choices and usage. Candidate import compiled zero source files; control import compiled 5,257. Bypassing candidate caches restored 5,478 compilations.

### Native serving attribution

In a separate installed vLLM 0.28.0 experiment, the same 8.85 GB of Python and shared-object files were 100% page-resident before every start. First-correct-response medians were **57.0394 s without bytecode and 47.6911 s with it**, with a **10.1300 s median paired saving**, n=3 pairs; all pairs and output checks passed. The measured startup saving includes avoided compilation, cache-file work, and normal parent/child reuse. It is not entirely compiler CPU. [Protocol, observations, and limits](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55422#issuecomment-5608794542).

### Direct compiler reproduction

The exact 5,118-file import corpus, 78.60 MB and about 2.16 million source lines, was read into memory and compiled without execution or bytecode writes. Native CPython 3.12.3 took **6.3033 s median**, n=3 whole-corpus passes. A real uncached serving-CLI import took 12.2019 s with 6.9880 s inside 5,118 compiler calls; cached import took 5.0095 s and made zero compiler calls. Source hashes and 196 package versions match the resident-page study, but the Python binary build changed, so absolute times are not interchangeable. To reproduce without vLLM or a GPU, invoke `compile(source_bytes, filename, "exec", dont_inherit=True, optimize=0)` over the recorded trace paths in a fresh `python3.12 -I -S -B` process after preloading the sources.

### Inclusive import roots

Fresh-process medians below use fully resident source/native pages, n=3 paired runs per root. Rows include transitive imports and are **not additive**. Paired-saving medians need not equal differences of arm medians.

| Entry point | No bytecode | Bytecode | Median paired saving |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `import torch` | 2.1306 s | 0.8025 s | 1.3281 s |
| `import transformers` | 1.2943 s | 0.6760 s | 0.6018 s |
| `import vllm` | 6.7075 s | 2.1068 s | 4.6007 s |
| `import vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve` | 12.2659 s | 5.0198 s | 7.2461 s |

In this vLLM 0.28.0 environment (Torch 2.13.0, Transformers 5.17.0), bare Torch did not load Dynamo, Inductor, or SymPy; importing vLLM loaded all three. Bare Transformers did not load Torch. One eager path is the Inductor patch in `vllm.env_override`. Dependency-file ownership therefore does not tell us which entry point introduces the import cost.

### Bytecode portability

Pure-Python timestamp and checked-hash caches created on macOS ARM64, CPython 3.12.13 loaded unchanged on Linux x86-64, CPython 3.12.3 with source compilation blocked. Both used cache tag `cpython-312` and magic `cb0d0d0a`; all nine reuse and validation cases matched their expected outcomes. [Python documents compiled modules as architecture-independent](https://docs.python.org/3.12/tutorial/modules.html#compiled-python-files), with compatible interpreter format still required. The image pins its Python/native platform; the PR compiles within that build path and retains source. This fixture is not a full cross-platform vLLM deployment.

### Known caveats

uv [recommends bytecode compilation for production images](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker/#compiling-bytecode), trading build work and image size for startup time. The upstream issues I found concern [reproducible cache/image bytes](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/129724) and [compilation hangs under affected QEMU-user setups](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/6105). I reproduced the former on Mac CPython 3.12.13: identical source and checked-hash headers produced different serialized bytes depending on compilation order, but equal decoded code objects and correct execution. We should not claim reproducible image digests. The QEMU report concerns the build environment; native CUDA validation does not qualify emulated builds. No cache-format or concurrency workaround is added by this PR.

<details>
<summary>Secondary observations, reproduction details, and limits</summary>

Native serving pairs, without/with bytecode: 54.7488/44.6188 s, 57.0394/47.6911 s, and 60.6387/48.4054 s. Its separate September 9 CLI trace measured 8.1962 s in 5,118 source-compilation calls. The September 15 preloaded direct-compile passes were 6.2461, 6.3033 and 6.3194 s; their Python 3.12.3 build is newer, despite matching source hashes and package versions.

Separate diagnostic import-root traces measured compiler time/source files as Torch 1.3441 s/871, Transformers 0.6780 s/398, vLLM 4.7605 s/2,293 and serving CLI 7.5139 s/5,118. These hooked traces are excluded from the uninstrumented root medians above. The cached serving trace made zero compiler calls. Within the uncached CLI trace, exclusive compiler costs by source-file owner were Torch 2.852 s, SymPy 1.032 s, Transformers 0.498 s and vLLM 0.431 s, plus other dependencies. These are compiler timings, not inclusive package-import durations.

The earlier unchanged-runtime mechanism fixture used the published vLLM 0.28.0 image plus `python3 -m compileall -q -j 8 /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages`. With image and model present, medians were 63.967 s control and 51.953 s bytecode, with a 12.014 s median paired saving, n=5. With the image absent and model present, loopback pull-through-response medians were 145.041 s and 134.109 s, with a 10.337 s median paired saving, n=3. Its added gzip layer was 153,159,438 bytes. This fixture isolates the mechanism but is not a matched full build of this PR.

Exact-head paired pull-through-response observations were 149.8156/134.4550 s, 155.7265/144.5137 s, and 162.3850/146.2806 s for control/bytecode. Host source pages were warm or uncontrolled in that experiment. The same bytecode artifact exported with the separate opt-in zstd change was 17.7633% smaller than control and saved 37.7032 s median paired, but those combined numbers include both changes and are not this PR's isolated effect.

The full-build recipes shared one recorded host-network preparation because the rig lacks `docker0`. The first control build failed in 1.32 s before installation; no timed cell was affected. Build durations, 688.83 s control and 629.16 s candidate, are not a matched build-time comparison. In the older delivery fixture, one post-timing mount cleanup failed after the clock and functional checks; that observation was retained without replacement and cleanup was resolved before continuing. The resident-page study retained two excluded preparation attempts and corrected a TCP cleanup probe before its six measured cells. The import-root study's first preparation reached 98.0101% residency and timed no imports; equal mmap page touches then produced 100% residency without relaxing the gate.

These are one-host medians with local models, no Internet transfer, warm or controlled pages as stated, and no p95 or throughput claim. They do not validate missing-model startup, every accelerator image, published multi-platform size, slow links, fleets, pip installs, or the earlier A10/Qwen3-8B baseline. Normal source-backed loader validation has limits: a corrupt marshalled body can fail without source fallback, and timestamp caches can accept changed same-size/same-mtime source. uv initially compiled only the reinstalled vLLM distribution in the package study, so the ENV line alone does not prove complete cache coverage for every image variant.

</details>

Related to #48193. An open-PR title search for bytecode on September 15 returned only this PR. AI assistance was used for implementation, experiment tooling, and analysis.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Fix KDA projection overlap on Hopper
author: chengchengpei
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55350.

Kimi-K3's low-token-count TP8 KDA projection-overlap path fails during CUDA
graph profiling on H100/SM90a. Two independent incompatibilities are involved:

1. the skinny N/K kernels unconditionally emit PTX `fma.f32.bf16`, which
   requires SM100 or newer and fails libNVVM compilation for `sm_90a`; and
2. FlashInfer's `cute-dsl` QKVG backend rejects SM90 during backend validation.

PR #55108 avoids the failure by disabling KDA projection overlap on Hopper.
This PR keeps the overlap structure enabled while selecting architecture-safe
operations.

## Implementation

- **SM100 and newer:** retain the existing mixed-precision BF16 FMA path.
- **SM90:** convert BF16 operands to FP32 and use FP32 FMA in the skinny N/K
  kernels.
- **SM100 and SM103 QKVG:** retain FlashInfer `cute-dsl` with PDL.
- **Other capabilities, including SM90:** use `torch.mm` for QKVG while keeping
  the concurrent F_A/beta and F_B projection branch.

The architecture check follows the PTX ISA requirement that
`fma.f32.{f16/bf16}` requires `sm_100` or higher. SM100 and SM103 behavior is
otherwise unchanged.

## Test plan and results

### Focused source checks

- `ruff format --check`: passed
- `ruff check`: passed
- Python compilation: passed
- capability and QKVG backend-selection tests: passed locally

### H100 single-GPU compile and correctness preflight

Tested with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`, so the projection-overlap path executed:

- skinny N and K kernels compiled for rows 2 through 14;
- CUDA-graph capture and replay passed for rows 2, 8, and 14;
- complete overlapped projection passed for rows 3 and 14;
- complete overlap also passed under CUDA-graph replay for row 14;
- the selected H100 QKVG backend was `torch.mm`; and
- projection overlap remained enabled.

Numerical comparison against FP32 references:

- portable skinny N/K kernels: maximum absolute error
  `1.220703125e-4`;
- complete-overlap QKVG `torch.mm` branch: maximum absolute error
  `4.8828125e-4`; and
- minimum observed cosine similarity: greater than `0.9999998`.

The larger QKVG value is from the `torch.mm` branch, not the portable skinny
FMA implementation.

### Four-node H100 end-to-end check

An integration image based on main commit `e962733e` plus this PR and #53948
was tested on 32 x H100 with TP8/PP4, CUDA graphs, BF16 activations, MXFP4
weights, and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`:

- the server completed CUDA-graph profiling and started successfully;
- 4,000/4,000 OpenAI-compatible requests succeeded;
- all responses returned HTTP 200 with the expected prompt and completion-token
  counts; and
- output throughput was 3,437.1 tokens/s across the deployment.

This end-to-end result is a startup, correctness, and regression check rather
than an isolated performance comparison because the image also contained the
unrelated PP prototype from #53948. A matched comparison against #55108's
full-disable approach remains useful follow-up work for quantifying the benefit
of preserving overlap on Hopper.

title: [Bugfix][Model][Spec Decode] Defer disposable GLM MTP head
author: lucamotz
body:
## Summary

- defer the GLM MTP `ParallelLMHead` that `load_eagle_model()` replaces with the target model's head
- keep `SharedHead`'s default behavior unchanged for other MTP models
- verify the quantized placeholder is not allocated

GLM MTP constructs a per-layer `ParallelLMHead` that `load_eagle_model()` replaces with the target model's head. That temporary head caused the load-time memory peak this PR originally addressed. #52501 subsequently initialized unloaded ModelOpt NVFP4 `weight_scale` parameters to a NaN sentinel and added a check that rejects an unoverwritten sentinel during quantization processing. Because the disposable head has no checkpoint scales to load, draft loading now fails inside `get_model()`, before `load_eagle_model()` can replace it.

Fixes #57532.

## Validation

- `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -q --tb=short` (`3 passed`)
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` (passed)
- DGX Spark, 2 nodes / TP=2, GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4, MTP=3, 8K validation context:
  - main at validation time (`4c6c1a40b3`) fails while loading the draft: `NVFP4 weight_scale for layer 'parallel_lm_head' was never loaded (still NaN)`
  - the same build with only #52501 reverted reaches ready state and serves the expected model alias
  - this PR (`67e55792ff`) reaches ready state, returns HTTP 200 from `/health`, serves `glm-5.3-flash`, and completes a deterministic short request with MTP active (96 draft tokens, 44 accepted)

Hardware validation used `67e55792ff`. The identical patch was subsequently rebased onto `44dd18fe0b` as `5517abf8da`; the focused tests and pre-commit passed again after rebase.

This PR predates #57532; duplicate searches found no competing fix.

AI assistance was used to rebase the change, run validation, and draft this description. Every changed line and the validation results were reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire Mamba states across null gaps
author: lucamotz
body:

Fix align-mode Mamba retirement stopping at null gaps and leaking older states. Track the retired prefix to avoid rescanning it.

title: [Bugfix] Defer adaptive verification until after kernel warmup
author: khluu
body:
The B200 LM Eval Spec Decode lane fails during DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark startup. The full log from [main build 87376](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87376#01a07028-57a6-4e1f-9e5e-8d39298b7cb4) reaches `AdaptiveVerificationManager.get_num_tokens` from `warmup_kernels` and asserts because `cost_tables` is still `None`.

`GPUWorker.compile_or_warm_up_model` deliberately runs kernel warmup before `capture_model`. Adaptive cost calibration happens inside `capture_model`, so the warmup's synthetic speculative decode steps cannot use calibrated budgets yet. Temporarily suspend the runner's adaptive manager during kernel warmup, exercising fixed draft counts, and restore it in `finally` for graph capture and serving. Keep adaptive verification enabled for actual requests.

Duplicate checks: no open PR matches `cost_tables warmup`. #54065 changes calibration batch shapes, and #52233 caches calibrated profiles; neither fixes this pre-calibration warmup call.

Validation on Linux with PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu:
```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py -q
```
**11 passed, 26 skipped** (GPU-only cases). New tests cover restoring the same uncalibrated manager on both successful warmup and exceptions. All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

B200 model evaluation remains required: run the exact LM Eval Spec Decode lane and verify DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-confidence-TEP4 startup and GSM8K accuracy. No GPU or model-evaluation success is claimed yet.

title: [Bugfix] Exclude DP token padding from draft attention metadata
author: khluu
body:
DeepSeek-V3.2 DP8 + EP + MTP crashes when DP ranks have unequal request counts. A rank with 12 requests receives model inputs padded to 13 tokens; the sparse indexer then fails with `shape '[12, -1, 64, 128]' is invalid for input of size 106496`. This is confirmed in [main build 87584](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87584#01a07dad-00e7-4a29-9abe-6cdc65c9100f). The subsequent GSM8K result of 0.0000 reflects the engine failure.

Autoregressive draft decode produces one query per request. Use the descriptor's request count, falling back to the actual local request count, for the attention token count in both ordinary and fused multi-step decode. Preserve padded model inputs/collective sizes and FULL graph request padding.

Validation:
- The exact [H200 large-model job in build 87389](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87389#01a0712c-2e18-480d-bda7-dfac8725ed44) passed all **6 evaluations** on implementation commit `39ba6cbae8e1`. DeepSeek-V3.2-DP scored **0.9568**, above its **0.8700** lower bound.
- After merging main and removing the added regression test, unused imports caused pre-commit to fail. Those imports are now removed. `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle_draft_attn_metadata.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh targeted H200 validation for current head `c34119ecbe4d` is [build 87771](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87771). Its result is pending; the older passing run above is not represented as current-head validation.

Duplicate checks found no competing PR for the one-query-per-request draft-decode metadata mismatch. Related #53660, #54102, and #53577 address draft prefill, verifier residual padding, and DSpark PP respectively. This PR updates the existing fix rather than introducing a second implementation.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and validation.

title: [Fast Start] Support fp4
author: liusy58
body:
## Purpose

Extend weight-cache IPC loading (`--load-format ipc_cache`) to support FP4 models (NVFP4 and MXFP4). Previously only unquantized and FP8 weights could be shared through the IPC weight cache. This lets FP4 models such as `Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` and `Kimi-K3` load their weights via the daemon without re-quantizing on each rank.

## Test Plan

Qwen3

```bash

export MODEL=/mnt/minecraft/model/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3

SOCK_DIR=/home/liusy/vllm/.vscode/sock
cd /home/liusy/vllm
mkdir -p "$SOCK_DIR"

# Drop any previous (possibly hung) daemon and stale sockets so the new ranks
# bind cleanly and free the GPU memory the old ranks still hold.
pkill -f "weight_cache.daemon" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 2
rm -f "$SOCK_DIR"/*.sock

python -u -m vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --weight-cache-socket-dir "$SOCK_DIR"
```

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Recover locally invalidated pull peer metadata
author: xijiaat
body:
## Summary

Recover a pull peer whose **local NIXL metadata is missing while Prefill is still alive with the same engine ID**. Without recovery, vLLM's cached `_remote_agents` entry and prepared dlists can keep subsequent requests on the stale path.

A receive failure schedules a descriptor-free `check_remote_metadata(agent)` check. This queries **local metadata existence, not peer health**. Only confirmed absence makes the peer eligible for recovery; a transfer error or probe exception alone does not.

## Implementation

- Track failed and locally invalid peers in `NixlBaseConnectorWorker`. One `_cleanup_remote_engines()` pass handles both replacement and invalidation, reusing `_cleanup_remote_engine()` to release resources.
- Defer probes and cleanup while background handshakes are pending. For invalid peers, reject new reads and wait for all existing receive handles to settle before cleanup. Replacement cleanup retains its existing queued-request guard.
- Clear recovery state in the shared per-engine cleanup, including TTL eviction and shutdown. A peer that is both replaced and invalidated is cleaned once; the replacement's address mapping is preserved.
- Route new and handshake-ready requests through the pull worker's existing read entry point. After cleanup, a fresh request re-handshakes the unchanged engine ID and uses newly prepared descriptors. Failed requests are **not replayed with old remote block IDs**.

The production changes are in `nixl/base_worker.py` and `nixl/pull_worker.py`. Recovery remains **pull-only**, with an explicit push-mode TODO. There is no new router API, configuration, or metadata probe on successful transfers.

Following Yannik's review, tests reuse `TestPeerReplacement` and `FakeNixlWrapper` instead of a separate hand-built recovery fixture. The existing receive/HMA fixtures and push test stub initialize the new fields. Nick Hill's read/handshake simplification is retained with authorship preserved.

## Related Work and Scope

Related to #49238. This is a follow-up to merged #50047, not another replacement detector:

| Change | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| #50047 | A new engine ID is confirmed at the same address. |
| This PR | The engine ID is unchanged, but NIXL has lost the decoder's local peer metadata. |

Both now use one base-worker cleanup pass, rather than separate replacement and recovery passes. The scope split was discussed in [#50047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50047#issuecomment-5629552908).

#52232 addresses HMA failure propagation and is **not included here**. Recovering future requests does not by itself guarantee that the failed HMA request returns an error instead of invalid output. TTL policy and the native UCX race discussed in NIXL #1987 are also outside this patch's scope.

Stuck reads or handshakes defer recovery; this patch does not forcibly release active resources. Native cleanup exceptions propagate rather than being swallowed. Recovery is not a claim that every UCX failure is recoverable.

## Validation

### Refactor and CI

| Check | Result and revision scope |
| --- | --- |
| Local source-AST/mock regressions after the refactor and September 29 main merge | 32 passed: 20 previous recovery cases plus 12 existing receive-lifecycle cases. These external harnesses are not full-import vLLM tests. |
| Old-fixture negative control | The same 12 receive-lifecycle cases fail with the original missing-field fixtures. |
| Recorded-main behavioral negative control | 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passing controls. |
| Local pre-commit, including Ruff and mypy; `git diff --check` | Passed on the September 29 merged revision. |
| [Buildkite #91865](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91865), September 29 merged revision | NVIDIA KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**; AMD KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**. The overall build reports "passed and blocked"; not every defined pipeline job was executed. |
| [Subsequent automatic main merge](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8aba1056b6b811b4770fd6bba860b54835c84ca6), September 30 | Pre-commit and DCO passed. No full Buildkite result is attached to this new head at the time of this update; #91865 tested the preceding revision. |

The failures in earlier CI #91736 were missing recovery fields in fixtures that bypass the worker constructor. Those fixtures are now initialized, and the subsequent KV Connector shards pass.

Regression coverage includes confirmed-missing versus healthy/probe-error cases, same-ID re-handshake with fresh descriptors, pending-handshake gating, sibling-handle drain ordering, new-read rejection, healthy-peer isolation, replacement/invalidation overlap, notify-only requests, expiry accounting, cleanup exceptions, TTL eviction, and shutdown.

Local full-import pytest collection was blocked by missing `tblib` and the incomplete vLLM runtime environment; the 32 local cases are not a substitute for CI. There is **no new native NIXL/GPU or model-serving evaluation of the refactored revision**. Historical experiments below remain evidence only for their stated revisions and configurations.

### Reproduction Commands

From a vLLM checkout with the repository's test dependencies installed:

```bash
# Focused replacement and local-invalidation coverage.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -k TestPeerReplacement -v --tb=short

# Broader connector CPU regression suite.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -v --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

These commands select the current tests; they are not presented as the exact Buildkite shard commands. The old `-k peer_recovery` selector no longer describes the consolidated tests.

<details>
<summary>Historical native and serving evidence, before the current refactor</summary>

### September 23 H20 validation

Full vLLM Python imports in isolated H20 containers: **357 selected CPU tests passed**, including 18 recovery cases; the corresponding main-only selection passed 339. Eight selected baseline cases produced 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passes.

Real NIXL/UCX probes passed with 1 MiB CPU and GPU buffers. With the peer still alive, the probe deliberately removed local metadata, observed the stale-read failure, invoked patched cleanup, and explicitly reloaded the same agent's metadata for a byte-checked read. Healthy-peer reads continued working. Automatic re-handshake was covered separately by pytest.

Runtime: NIXL 1.4.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3. The rebased Python source used native extensions from the existing vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9` image, not a fresh CUDA build of main. No weights were loaded for this validation. This is not a model-serving, natural-disconnect, or NVLink/RDMA validation of the current revision.

[Exact commands, full selected logs, and native probe](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/34c74ce35e1f68958e5881a1907bf84d).

### Original TP1 P/D serving experiment

The original implementation was tested with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, NIXL 1.3.2, fp8 HMA KV, eager mode, `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy`, and the existing TP1 packed-layout fix. With no active reads, a controlled hook removed only Decode's local remote metadata, retaining the Python cache. A real stale read failed with `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`; fresh requests automatically re-handshook the unchanged Prefill engine ID and returned the expected short answers.

The **recovery-only failed request still emitted 32 invalid tokens**. Adding #52232 and an API terminal-error follow-up produced a passing 10-request scenario: two normal controls, four controlled failures across Chat/Completion and streaming/non-streaming, and four fresh Chat recoveries. The failed requests emitted no generated content. This combined result must not be attributed to the recovery-only diff. Attribution for the HMA change belongs to Tyler Michael Smith.

The original recovery-only CPU selections passed 353 distinct cases across two runs. The combined recovery/HMA/API experiment passed 425 selected tests, not 425 tests of this standalone patch. Full original logs retain earlier failures and an independently wrong pre-injection arithmetic control.

This is controlled failure-path evidence, not general accuracy, natural transport-failure reproduction, multi-rank native-race coverage, or a guarantee of production readiness.

[Selected raw logs, response bodies/SSE, commands and patches](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/a975858a507d6c45fd394b3675cc0ab9). Internal addresses and paths are anonymized. The HMA/API evidence is also reported in [#52232](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52232#issuecomment-5552174526).

### Maintainer simplification

Nick Hill's [simplification](https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/7dc2a0eb49dbc62fdfc329885e663a672160cdec) was incorporated with authorship and sign-off preserved. It reuses main's in-flight-transfer guard rather than a second request-to-engine map: receive metadata remains available until the handles settle. The subsequent refactor retains that approach and moves cleanup into the base worker as suggested by Yannik Hinteregger.

</details>

## AI Assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, and this report. The human submitter reviewed and approved the original contribution; subsequent compatibility adaptations remain subject to human review. Historical results and limited failure-path tests are not claims of comprehensive model evaluation or production readiness.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Preserve target parallel config (DCP) for DSpark
author: starkwj
body:
## Purpose

Fix Kimi-K3 startup with DSpark when decode context parallelism (DCP) is enabled.

#50514 changed `load_dspark_model` to use `speculative_config.draft_parallel_config` instead of target's `parallel_config` when constructing the draft `VllmConfig`.
However, `speculative_config.draft_parallel_config` only copies a subset of the target parallel settings and leaves DCP fields at their defaults (dcp=1) (in function `create_draft_parallel_config`).
Thus, when launching models (e.g, Kimi-K3) with DCP and DSpark, the DSpark failed to inherit the DCP settings, and results in assertion failure.

```shell
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py", line 299, in create_metada
ta_builders
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]     builder_cls(
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla.py", l
ine 141, in __init__
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]     super().__init__(
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.p
y", line 2376, in __init__
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]     assert isinstance(self.dcp_manager, MLADCPManager)
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055] AssertionError
```

#50514 only changes this behavior for DSpark (not DFlash/Eagle).
Thus, this PR is a quick "revert" fix for DSpark, and retaining the setting `PP=1` in #50514.
This PR does not fix by modifying `create_draft_parallel_config`, as it may affect other drafters' behavior.
And according to RFC #53673, more refactor for decoupling target and draft parallel config may be required.


## Test Plan

Launch Kimi-K3 with DCP 8 and DSpark (Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark).

## Test Result

Succeed to start Kimi-K3 with DCP and DSpark.

title: [Perf] Fix TRTLLM ragged prefill perf regression
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose
There is a perf regression in flashinfer TRTLLM ragged prefill, as described in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4928. This PR fixes it by skipping the checks inside the kernel call, avoiding the CUDA synchronization, and instead do the checks at the MLA Prefill metadata preparation so it is done once per forward instead of inside every kernel call.

Fixed ISL=8k OSL=128 Throughput

|           4 | 14,544 |    14,829 (+2.0%) |   14,918 (+2.6%) |

title: [Bugfix] Bound GDN speculative decode query widths
author: DimensionSTP
body:
## Overview

Keep oversized profiling rows out of GDN's bounded speculative state layout. This follows merged #56531, whose shared routing implementation is already in main.

I utilized AI tools to assist in refining the implementation, executing tests, and analyzing logs.

## Claims

- Require a decode row's query width to fit within `num_speculative_tokens + 1`, addressing the profiling failure reported by @okorzh-amd.
- Keep valid zero-draft and boundary-length rows on the speculative path.
- Add one small regression in the existing worker test file, as requested in review.

## Validation

On upstream main `4187ade7b87e` without the bound, the retained regression fails: query widths `[12, 8, 1]` with seven speculative tokens produce `[0, 0, 0]` instead of `[-1, 0, 0]`. It passes with the bound.

The official worker/GDN CPU suites pass: 74 passed, 3 platform skips. All applicable project checks pass, including Ruff, spelling, mypy for Python 3.10-3.13, and test-to-Buildkite wiring.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_zero_draft_spec_rows.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py

pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py
```

This update only reduces tests. Production code is unchanged from published `a1f1e1b7`. Earlier CUDA validation remains recorded in the PR history; this revision does not claim a new GPU or full-model E2E run.

The original reporter [confirmed that the change works in E2E tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55504#discussion_r4212822637). That is external confirmation, not an AMD run performed locally for this PR.

## Details

With seven speculative tokens, the state-index table has eight columns. Unflagged 12-token profiling rows were classified as speculative even though they exceed that layout. The inclusive width bound fixes this without requiring query length to equal the supplied draft count plus one, which would break adaptive verification.

The only production change is this bound in `MambaHybridModelState.prepare_attn()`. Existing upstream comments and inline routing are retained. The regression reuses the existing worker helpers. The added kernel coverage has been removed, leaving a two-file diff with one new test and no new helper, kernel, backend default, or public configuration.

#59824 carries this dependency as a separate backport. Landing the width bound through #55504 would let that PR use it from main.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Make streaming TTFT/E2E latency accounting consistent across endpoints
author: surajm20061998
body:
## Purpose

`vllm/benchmarks/serve.py` derives TPOT from the end of the request:

```python
latency_minus_ttft = outputs[i].latency - outputs[i].ttft
tpot = latency_minus_ttft / (output_len - 1)
```

For that to mean "average inter-token latency", `latency - ttft` has to equal
`sum(itl)`. Today it does not, and it fails differently per endpoint, so E2EL
and TPOT are not comparable between an `openai` run and an `openai-chat` run.

Two independent causes:

**1. TTFT is read off a second clock call (`/v1/completions`).**

```python
timestamp = time.perf_counter()          # chunk arrival; seeds the ITL chain
if not first_chunk_received:
    first_chunk_received = True
    ttft = time.perf_counter() - st      # a different, later reading
    output.ttft = ttft
...
most_recent_timestamp = timestamp        # the earlier reading
```

TTFT is measured from one reading while the ITL chain continues from another,
so `latency - ttft` comes up short by the gap between the two calls.
`async_request_openai_chat_completions` and `async_request_openai_audio` already
do the right thing (`output.ttft = timestamp - st`), so this aligns completions
with its siblings rather than introducing a new convention.

**2. The trailing `usage` chunk extends E2E latency (chat and audio).**

`vllm bench serve` always sends `stream_options.include_usage`, so every stream
ends with a choice-less `usage` chunk after the last token. In chat and audio,
`most_recent_timestamp = timestamp` sits *outside* the `if choices:` branch, so
that trailer advances the end of the request; `output.latency` therefore runs
past the final token. `async_request_openai_completions` updates it *inside*
the branch and stops at the last token. `serve.py` assigns
`e2els.append(outputs[i].latency)` directly, so this lands in reported E2EL and
TPOT.

I fixed it in the direction that stops at the last token, because the
alternative — having completions also count the usage chunk — would break the
identity on *both* endpoints instead of fixing it: the usage gap appears in
`latency` but never in any `itl`. The loop already refuses to let the `[DONE]`
sentinel move the clock; the usage chunk is the same category of non-token
trailer.

`benchmarks/backend_request_func.py` carries the same two defects and is still
imported by `benchmark_prefix_caching.py` and
`benchmark_serving_structured_output.py`, so it gets the identical hunks (plus
the same one-line TTFT fix in `async_request_tgi`). Happy to split that file
into its own PR if you'd rather keep this one to `vllm/benchmarks/`.

### Magnitude — deliberately not overstated

This is a correctness and cross-endpoint-comparability fix, **not** a
performance claim. `chat_completion/serving.py` yields the usage chunk
immediately after the final content chunk in the same generator with no engine
await between, so in normal operation the error is tens of microseconds — I
measured ~24 µs on a 200 ms request, about 0.01%. The gap is not bounded by
anything, though: it is whatever separates two SSE writes, which on a saturated
client event loop is not guaranteed to stay small.

The lasting value is the test: `endpoint_request_func.py` currently has no test
coverage of its timing accounting at all, so nothing was stopping this from
drifting further.

## Not a duplicate

Per `AGENTS.md` I checked:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "endpoint_request_func"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "backend_request_func"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "usage chunk latency"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "benchmark ttft latency"
```

The only open PRs in this area are **#42661** and **#46652**, which both address
a *different* bug: servers batching multiple tokens into one SSE chunk, making
ITL per-chunk rather than per-token. Neither touches which clock reading TTFT
uses, nor where the request is considered to end. They are complementary — with
either merged, `sum(itl)` still spans the same decode window, so the identity
asserted here continues to hold.

#46652 also adds `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func.py`; this PR adds
`test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, so there is no filename collision, and
the two suites could be folded together later if that is preferred.

## Test Plan

New: `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, parametrized over
all three streaming request functions (completions, chat, audio). CPU-only — no
GPU, model, or socket; the request functions are driven against a fake session.

The exactness tests substitute a **scripted clock** that advances by a fixed
tick on every read. What a code path observes then depends only on how many
times it reads the clock, so a stray or misattributed read shows up as a whole
tick of drift instead of sub-microsecond jitter. That makes the assertions
exact and free of timing flakiness.

1. `test_decode_span_identity_is_exact` — `(latency - ttft) - sum(itl) == 0`.
2. `test_trailing_usage_chunk_does_not_extend_latency` — E2E latency stops at
   the final token.
3. `test_decode_span_identity_holds_with_real_clock` — same identity against the
   real clock with real inter-chunk gaps.
4. `test_usage_only_stream_is_not_reported_as_success` — a stream with no token
   chunk fails rather than reporting a zero-duration success. The residual differences out the same
   recorded timestamps, so jitter cancels and only float rounding remains; the
   1 µs bound is ample rather than tight.

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_audio_dataset.py -v   # sibling suite, same module
pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py \
    benchmarks/backend_request_func.py \
    tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py
```

## Test Result

On unpatched `main` (f4eccda), the new tests fail with the defects visible as
whole ticks of the scripted clock — negative for the extra TTFT read, positive
for the counted usage chunk:

```
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[completions]
  AssertionError: completions: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = -1.0
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[chat]
  AssertionError: chat: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = 1.0
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[audio]
  AssertionError: audio: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = 1.0
8 failed, 1 passed
```

With the fix applied:

```
tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py 12 passed
tests/benchmarks/test_audio_dataset.py                 8 passed   (no regression)
(20 passed total)
```

Reverting only the two source files and re-running reproduces the 8 failures,
confirming the tests actually exercise the fix.

Independently, driving the unpatched request functions against a local SSE
server over a real socket, residual `(latency - ttft) - sum(itl)`:

| scenario | completions | chat |
|---|---|---|
| usage chunk emitted immediately (realistic) | −0.35 µs | +24.09 µs |
| usage chunk delayed 30 ms (mechanism probe) | −0.32 µs | **+31 473 µs** |

The probe isolates the mechanism: a 30 ms delay before the usage chunk moves
chat's residual by ~30 ms and leaves completions flat. After the fix, all four
cells are 0.00 µs.

`pre-commit` / `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean on all three files.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This changes only how the **benchmark client** measures latency
on the wire. No engine, scheduler, sampling, or serving path is touched, so
model outputs and accuracy are unaffected.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance. I have reviewed every changed
line, run the tests above myself, and can defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Kernel] Add fused MoE tuned config for E=256,N=512 on NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe
author: bakiburakogun
body:
## Purpose

Add a tuned fused-MoE Triton kernel configuration for **NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe** covering the Qwen3.5-122B-A10B MoE shapes at tensor parallel size 2 in bfloat16:

- `E=256` experts, `moe_intermediate_size=1024`, so `N=512` per rank at TP=2
- file: `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_A100_80GB_PCIe.json`

There is currently no A100 entry for this shape (H100/H20 exist), so A100 PCIe deployments fall back to the default heuristic config.

## Test Plan

Generated with the standard tuning script on an 8x A100 80GB PCIe host (no NVLink), vLLM v0.28.0 image, Ray workers over all 8 GPUs:

```bash
python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B --tp-size 2 --dtype auto --tune --trust-remote-code
```

Then compared default vs. tuned kernel time on one GPU with the same script in benchmark mode (`--batch-size 1 4 16 64 256 1024 4096`), the tuned run pointing `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` at the generated file.

## Test Result

Kernel time from `benchmark_moe.py` (bf16, TP=2 shapes, one A100 80GB PCIe, vLLM v0.28.0, Triton 3.7.1):

| batch size | default config (us) | tuned config (us) | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 73.35 | 67.54 | -7.9% |
| 4 | 206.86 | 200.41 | -3.1% |
| 16 | 606.49 | 589.62 | -2.8% |
| 64 | 1270.50 | 1238.59 | -2.5% |
| 256 | 1607.70 | 1468.64 | -8.6% |
| 1024 | 2102.24 | 1694.01 | -19.4% |
| 4096 | 3300.12 | 2719.18 | -17.6% |

Every measured batch size improves; the largest gains are at the prefill-sized batches (1024 and 4096, about 18-19% faster), the decode-sized batches gain 2-9%.

Full tuning run took 10292 s (about 2 h 51 min) across 8 GPUs.

Sanity: the file loads with `json.load`, keys are the batch sizes produced by the tuner, and vLLM picks it up at startup (`Using configuration from .../E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_A100_80GB_PCIe.json for MoE layer`).

title: [Refactor][ROCm] Migrate the RDNA3 W4A16 MoE to the oracle/experts pa…
author: JartX
body:
## Purpose

This is the follow-up refactor @BowenBao asked for when the RDNA3 W4A16 MoE kernel landed in #44075: the kernel is no longer wired in through its own quant-method class, it is now a normal oracle backend with an experts class, like every other WNA16 backend. Tracked in #44460, part of #37753. It was blocked on #44570, which is merged.

In short:

- `WNA16MoEBackend.RDNA3` + `Rdna3WNA16Experts`, selected by the oracle
- weight prep moved next to the other `_process_weights_*` handlers
- `rocm_moe_rdna.py` and `compressed_tensors_moe_wna16_rdna3.py` deleted, along with the inline dispatch in `compressed_tensors_moe.py`
- `--moe-backend rdna3` now works to force it

The HIP kernel and its tests are untouched — this is dispatch plumbing only.

It also fixes a crash: `RoutedExperts` decides whether to pass `intermediate_size_full` by class name, and our subclass was not on that list, so W4A16 MoE models currently fail to load on gfx1100 with `KeyError: 'intermediate_size_full'`. Going back to the parent class fixes it. No gfx1100 CI, so nobody noticed.

Three intentional behaviour changes: asymmetric checkpoints now fall back to Triton (the kernel synthesizes symmetric zero points, so it was silently ignoring theirs), LoRA falls back to Triton instead of dropping the delta, and the activation now honours the swiglu clamp/alpha/beta.

No other open PR does this — #43389 / #52970 are Triton rewrites, #46676 is MXFP4, #49321 is expert offload.

## Test Plan

2× RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), TP2, CUDA graphs on, `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-W4A16-G32` (compressed-tensors int4, group 32, symmetric).

```bash
vllm serve /models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-W4A16-G32 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 8 --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --served-model-name M35 --port 8001

# GSM8K: 200 problems, 8 concurrent, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95, max_tokens 640

pytest -q tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py
pytest -q tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_compile_guards.py
pytest -q tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py
```

## Test Result

| dispatch | GSM8K (n=200) | generation throughput @ 8 concurrent |
|---|---|---|
| before | 185/200 = 92.5% | 385–394 tok/s |
| after | 187/200 = 93.5% | ~385 tok/s |

Two problems apart, about one standard error — the same, as expected for a dispatch change. Throughput unchanged. (The "before" run needed the class-name list patched locally, otherwise the model does not load.)

The server picks the right path:

```
Using 'RDNA3' WNA16 MoE backend.
Using Rdna3WNA16Experts
```

Tests on gfx1100: 97 passed (MoE kernel), 19 passed / 9 skipped (compile guards, skips are the non-gfx1100 cases), 13 passed / 5 skipped (oracle). `pre-commit run` clean, mypy included.

---

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache][MLA] Align packed block strides for V3.2 sparse MLA
author: 200lz
body:
## Purpose

V3.2 sparse MLA did not publish the physical block-stride alignment its selected kernel requires. This PR sets the existing `block_stride_alignment` contract at the producer, lifts the field to `KVCacheSpec`, and lets the allocator consume it without an MLA type check. HiSparse hot-page and stride constraints are combined in one LCM so sequential rounding cannot invalidate the first constraint.

The requirement is selected by backend and cache format. Flattened-row paths, including FlashInfer sparse, share their predicate with warmup. SM100 FlashMLA paged FP8/NVFP4 additionally require independent native TMA alignment (`fp8_ds_mla`: 656 bytes; `nvfp4_ds_mla`: 352 bytes), without flattened-row warmup. Existing BLHNC/BLNHC support is retained.

This adopts LucasWilkinson’s minimized suggestion in 200lz/vllm#1: six files, +187/-27, including compact alignment/merge tests and the existing producer/allocator/binder contract test. Layout gating/threading, admission/auto-fit rewrites, and HiSparse PP capacity work are outside this PR.

## Scope and validation

This complements #56254’s existing alignment propagation and pool rounding by supplying the missing V3.2 producer requirement; upstream #53781 already fixed the fused-writer issue. Those changes are not duplicated here.

CPU validation on exact suggestion `1d45dcafade7903237c627d941fda7df26341d76`: **258 passed, 41 skipped**. A clean temporary merge with main `79468c20ef23227d4e051f807e10fd54fb24e24f` passed **265 tests, 45 skipped**. The PR branch itself was not merged with main.

```bash
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \

  tests/v1/engine/test_init_error_messaging.py \

ruff check <changed files>

git diff --check

```

All static checks passed on both trees, including default mypy 3.10 and explicit mypy 3.12. CUDA cases and the CUDA-only sparse-backend module were skipped on the CPU host.

The retained producer/native-TMA logic and sparse layout test are unchanged from the earlier B200-validated revision. That work reproduced the FP8 TMA assertion before correction and passed the packed FP8/NVFP4/backend cases afterward; the broader earlier B200 bundle had 182 passes. Those historical results support the retained contracts, not the removed PP/admission fixes or a new full-runtime validation on current main. No new GPU run was required.

[stu-cao previously reported qualitative GB200 NVLink NIXL transfer improvement](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55528#issuecomment-5628968592); no numerical speedup is claimed. Production MTP/DFlash2 correctness, acceptance, and long-context behavior still require retesting. No production model-quality evaluation is claimed.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Enable NIXL telemetry for the OBJ tier
author: zupengwang
body:
## Purpose

The OBJ secondary tier reads NIXL transfer telemetry for every successful store or load, but creates its agent with telemetry capture disabled by default. Without `NIXL_TELEMETRY_ENABLE`, a completed transfer raises `nixlNoTelemetryError` before releasing its handles or reporting the job result.

Enable telemetry capture when constructing the OBJ agent. Make the existing mock respect the disabled default, and extend the store/load roundtrip test to check transfer timing and completion bookkeeping.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-09-06 found no open PR implementing this fix. Searches covered OBJ telemetry, objectstore, `capture_telemetry`, and `nixlNoTelemetryError`. The open backpressure PR #50045 touches OBJ constructor plumbing but does not enable telemetry. The telemetry read was introduced by #48798.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change.

## Test Plan

Tested against upstream `808f8cd3ac6751278d8b7be97f6fde5295ca4653` on Linux with Python 3.12.13 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. The isolated checkout imports its own upstream Python source and reuses dependencies and binary extensions from an existing vLLM 0.28.0 installation.

```bash
# Original implementation with the regression test changes.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py -k test_store_then_load_roundtrip --timeout=60

# Fixed implementation.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py --timeout=60
```

Supplemental validation used the full OBJ manager with native NIXL 1.3.2, its OBJ plugin, and a loopback Moto S3 service. `NIXL_TELEMETRY_ENABLE` was unset. The check stores two CPU blocks, clears their buffer, loads them, and compares the restored bytes and job results.

## Test Result

- Baseline regression: 1 failed, 37 deselected; failure occurs at the telemetry read.
- Fixed OBJ and adjacent tiering suites: 124 passed.
- Native OBJ baseline: both S3 writes succeeded, then `NIXL_ERR_NO_TELEMETRY` prevented completion and left one tracked transfer.
- Native OBJ with the fix: store and load succeeded with transfer timing, restored bytes matched, and completed transfers were removed and reported once.
- Ruff check/format, typos, mypy for Python 3.10–3.13, and applicable repository validation hooks passed individually on the two changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- The bulk pre-commit run timed out after 120 seconds while installing the unrelated Actionlint environment. All 15 applicable checks were subsequently run individually using the unmodified repository configuration.
- CPU validation only; CUDA remained uninitialized. No model serving, GPU, production S3, or performance benchmark was run.

title: [Docker] Use zstd for CI images and offer a Docker Hub variant
author: matteso1
body:
The ordinary CUDA CI image now exports zstd level 3 under the existing ECR commit tag that test runners consume. Standard Docker Hub tags retain their separate gzip release path, and the CUDA 13.0 amd64 release action also publishes a separately tagged `-zstd` variant from an immutable release-image digest by default. The requested test script has been removed.

The CI change applies to the ordinary `test-ci` build. CPU/Arm builds and the separate Torch-nightly builder retain their existing paths. The public release variant stays separately tagged because ordinary pulls do not provide a reliable same-tag gzip fallback for unsupported zstd consumers.

## Measurement

Earlier matched images on one RTX 4090 Laptop rig, Qwen3-0.6B, four-CPU quota, local registry and three fresh-store runs per arm:

| Image | Compressed bytes | Median pull to first correct response |
|---|---:|---:|
| Bytecode, gzip | 8,664,824,384 | 144.51 s |
| Same image, zstd level 3 | 6,999,776,144 | 118.02 s |

The zstd image is 19.2% smaller, with a 22.19-second median paired saving. Paired savings differ from subtracting the arm medians. This is the earlier same-host local-registry experiment, not a measurement of production ECR or Internet delivery.

## Validation

Merged current main and passed applicable pre-commit hooks, including ShellCheck and Buildkite configuration checks. The actual ci-infra consumers select the unchanged ECR commit tag, so no separate runner tag change is needed.

[CI build 89441](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89441#01a0abf5-32fd-4467-8e35-6e8b54bc6ce9) exported the `69f15d2e2e0137af8d0b10a693af28e54e907fb3` image with 44 zstd layers. An independent registry read verified its manifest and both commit labels. I then pulled Linux amd64 digest `sha256:81fe52601ccf6c61d8824016483e81fd24244491211cf4973b285fda6d4408d2` on my rig: Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and vLLM imports passed, followed by a small CUDA matrix multiplication on the selected RTX 4090 Laptop. The temporary container/image reference were removed and the existing snapshot workload was preserved. The CI exporter and zstd export helper are unchanged by the default-publication update. Mac and Linux command-spy checks passed for all release targets and export-failure cleanup; the normal gzip calls are preserved. Repository hooks passed. These orchestration checks did not publish images.

This is a published-image Docker/CUDA check, not full model-serving or cross-consumer qualification. Build 89441 was started manually without PR association, so normal PR CI is still needed. The earlier tiny-fixture harness failure and the corrected preflight-script attempt remain in the experiment record.

title: [Perf] Fuse DeepEncoder relative bias in Triton attention
author: Levius-Fubuki
body:
## Purpose

DeepEncoder relative attention currently expands decomposed height and width
terms into a dense `[B, heads, HW, HW]` bias before SDPA. Its 64x64 global
attention therefore materializes a 384 MiB BF16 temporary.

This PR adds a dedicated Triton forward kernel that evaluates both relative
terms while streaming key/value tiles through online softmax:

```text
before: rel_h + rel_w -> dense 4D bias -> SDPA
after:  compact rel_h/rel_w -> fused Triton attention
```

The Triton path is limited to the production DeepEncoder global-attention
configuration on CUDA: FP16/BF16 with head dimension 64. Window attention,
CPU, unsupported dtypes, and unsupported head dimensions retain the existing
SDPA path. The implementation does not use FlexAttention or `torch.compile`.

## Test Plan

### Regression tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/multimodal/test_deepencoder.py

source /etc/network_turbo
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_ocr.py
```

Results:

```text
16 passed
6 passed
```

The focused suite covers FP16/BF16 numerical equivalence on square and
non-square grids, partial tiles, CPU fallback, mixed-device input rejection,
global/window dispatch, exact benchmark repeat counts, and CUDA Graph
capture/replay at 14x14 and 64x64.

The two upstream DeepSeek-OCR cases in
`tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py` remain skipped by
their existing markers (`2 skipped, 26 deselected`).

### Changed-file checks

```bash
ruff check \
  vllm/model_executor/models/deepencoder.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/test_deepencoder.py \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_deepencoder_rel_pos_attention.py

ruff format --check \
  vllm/model_executor/models/deepencoder.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/test_deepencoder.py \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_deepencoder_rel_pos_attention.py
```

`ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, Python bytecode compilation, and
`git diff --check` pass. The full pre-commit wrapper could not finish its first
actionlint environment installation on the test server; the Python hooks that
apply to these files were run directly from the pinned hook environments.

### RTX 4090 microbenchmark

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_deepencoder_rel_pos_attention.py \
  --implementation production \
  --shapes global \
  --warmup 10 --repeats 50 \
  --output production-global.json
```

Hardware/software: NVIDIA RTX 4090, CUDA 13.2, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132,
Triton 3.7.1, BF16. Results are medians of 50 interleaved samples.

| Scope | Path | p50 (ms) | Incremental peak allocation (MiB) | Max abs error |
|:---|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| attention operator | Dense SDPA | 1.1453 | 390 | reference |
| attention operator | Triton | 0.5478 | 6 | 9.77e-4 |
| full `RelPosAttention` | Dense SDPA | 1.5667 | 426 | reference |
| full `RelPosAttention` | Triton | 0.9820 | 42 | 4.88e-4 |

The independent recheck reduced operator latency by 52.2% and full-layer
latency by 37.3%, while both measurements saved exactly 384 MiB of incremental
peak allocation. Reference and candidate both pass CUDA Graph capture/replay.

The previous FlexAttention candidate measured 1.4469 ms for the full layer on
the same GPU. The Triton revision is about 32.1% lower than that result and has
no per-process `torch.compile` dependency.

### DeepSeek-OCR end-to-end correctness

I ran `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR` with a deterministic 1024x1024 OCR image,
greedy decoding, and `enforce_eager=True`. The base reference and Triton
candidate generated exactly the same 21 token IDs and decoded text.

## Limitations

These are isolated DeepEncoder attention results from one RTX 4090, not an
end-to-end serving throughput claim or a performance claim for other GPU
architectures. The optimized path is forward-only and intentionally limited to
CUDA FP16/BF16 with head dimension 64; other configurations use SDPA.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during implementation, testing, benchmarking, and PR
drafting. The human contributor reviewed and takes responsibility for the
change and evidence.

title: [Bugfix] Fix NVFP4 fused SiLU+mul scale allocation and global scale direction
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

Fix two independent bugs in the manual SiLU+NVFP4 fusion producer (`_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_dynamic`, introduced in #51415) that break the `(B200) Kernels Shard 2` lane on main (builds [87376](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87376), [87450](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87450), [87460](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87460)): `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in `vllm::silu_mul_cvt_fp16_to_fp4<__nv_bfloat16, false>` for both `test_nvfp4[flashinfer_cutlass-*]` variants.

**Bug 1 — scale buffer under-allocation (the IMA).** The producer allocated the swizzled block-scale tensor as `(M, ceil(N/64)*4)` fp8 = `M*N/16` bytes, but the kernel writes the tensor-core swizzled SF layout `[numMTiles, numKTiles, 32, 4, 4]`, which requires `round_up(M,128) * round_up(N/16,4)` bytes. For M=1, N=14336 (Llama-3.1-8B intermediate size): 896 bytes allocated vs 114688 written. The OOB writes usually land inside a mapped caching-allocator segment and silently corrupt neighboring tensors (wrong text output in eager mode); when they escape the segment they produce the CI IMA. Fix: allocate the padded swizzled shape, mirroring `create_fp4_scale_tensor`.

**Bug 2 — global scale direction (wrong output once the crash is fixed).** The producer passed `input_global_scale`, but the consumer GEMM's `alpha = input_global_scale * weight_global_scale` only cancels when the activation was quantized with the inverse scale, as the unfused `scaled_fp4_quant` path does (`layer.input_global_scale_inv`). With the wrong direction the GEMM input is off by `input_global_scale^2`. Fix: pass `input_global_scale_inv`.

Existing tests could not catch either bug: the kernel test takes its buffer from `scaled_fp4_quant` (correctly padded) and only uses shapes with `M % 128 == 0` (where both size formulas coincide); the manual-fusion test used `num_tokens=128` and `input_global_scale=1.0` (its own inverse).

## Relation to existing PRs (duplicate-work check)

Searched open PRs for `nvfp4 silu`, `silu_and_mul_nvfp4`, `nvfp4 illegal memory`, `fused_act_quant`:

- #55456 fixes bug 1 with the same approach (reusing the canonical padded allocator) but is a **draft with no Blackwell hardware validation** ("B200 access was unavailable"), and explicitly does not touch bug 2.
- #55505 fixes bug 2 as a side effect of a **larger `InputQuantScales` contract refactor** (8 files), also without SM100+ validation.

This PR is the materially different **minimal combined fix**: both one-paragraph fixes plus regression tests, validated end-to-end on GB200 hardware. It is intended as a fast CI-stopgap; either of the above PRs can land instead and this one can be closed. @khluu and @jjjxia are credited as co-authors since their PRs identified/fixed the same bugs independently.

## Test Plan / Results (GB200, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130)

Kernel + fusion unit tests (on this PR's base, `f43ef1531d`):

```
python -m pytest tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py
=> 54 passed
```

`compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`, direct `torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` call, M=1, N=1048576:
- old allocation: `Invalid __global__ write of size 1` in `silu_mul_cvt_fp16_to_fp4<__nv_bfloat16, false>`, 4132865 bytes past a 65536-byte allocation (same kernel as the CI core dumps);
- fixed allocation: `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`, and dequantized output matches the unfused `scaled_fp4_quant` reference at M in {1, 8, 127}, N=14336.

Model evaluation (the exact CI-failing cases, on GB200):

```
python -m pytest tests/models/quantization/test_nvfp4.py \
  -k 'test_nvfp4 and flashinfer_cutlass'
=> 2 passed   # both variants, previously IMA during warmup
```

pre-commit (ruff check/format, mypy 3.10, sign-off): all pass.

## AI assistance

Kimi Code (Moonshot AI) performed the investigation, implementation, and validation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

Co-authored-by: khluu <khluu000@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: jiahao <jxia77@terpmail.umd.edu>

## CI wiring (so the regression actually runs)

The regression tests only help if CI runs them; verification of the job wiring on main:

- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py` — already run by `(B200) Kernels Shard %N` (shard 0). ✅
- `tests/models/quantization/test_nvfp4.py` — already run by `(B200) Kernels Shard %N` (shard 1; the lane that fails on main). ✅
- `tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py` — **was not collected by any job** (the `(B200) Fusion and Compile` job runs only `test_fusion_attn.py`, `test_mla_attn_quant_fusion.py`, `test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py`, and `distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py`). This PR wires it into that job (B200 hardware, required by its NVFP4 cases) and adds `vllm/model_executor/layers/fusion/`, `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/fp4/`, and the two NVFP4 test files to the relevant jobs' `source_file_dependencies` so future changes to the producer/kernel trigger these lanes.

title: [Bugfix] Make KV cache and MFU log lines backend-neutral
author: Ianniu123
body:
## Purpose

Three log lines hardcode `"GPU"` regardless of the active backend, which is misleading on
the CPU backend (and on XPU/NPU). This addresses items 1–3 of #55614.

The label is now derived from `device_config.device_type`, which is already resolved at
config construction and available at every call site — no new imports.

**CUDA and ROCm output is unchanged**: `device_type == "cuda"` yields the same `"GPU"`
literal as before, and ROCm reports `device_type == "cuda"` as well.

| site | before | after (CPU backend) |
|---|---|---|
| `v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` | `GPU KV cache size: …` | `CPU KV cache size: …` |
| `v1/metrics/loggers.py` (x2) | `GPU KV cache usage: …` | `CPU KV cache usage: …` |
| `v1/metrics/perf.py` | `MFU: … TF/s/GPU … GB/s/GPU` | `MFU: … TF/s/device … GB/s/device` |

The MFU line is a unit rather than a device label — the underlying calculation divides by
`tp_size`/`pp_size`, i.e. it is a per-rank rate — so `/device` is used instead of a
platform-derived name.

## Scope

Item 4 of the issue (renaming the exported Prometheus metrics
`vllm:estimated_flops_per_gpu_total`, `…_read_bytes_per_gpu_total`,
`…_write_bytes_per_gpu_total`) is **deliberately not included**. Those are public metric
names and renaming them breaks existing scrapers and needs a maintainer decision on a
deprecation/alias path. Happy to follow up separately if wanted.

## Test Plan

Built the CPU backend from source on x86 (AVX2) and captured the three log lines with the
change reverted and applied, on the same machine and same commit:

```bash
FILES="vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py"

git checkout HEAD~1 -- $FILES
vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --enable-mfu-metrics 2>&1 | tee /tmp/cpu-before.log

git checkout HEAD -- $FILES
vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --enable-mfu-metrics 2>&1 | tee /tmp/cpu-after.log
```

## Test Result

**Before** (CPU backend, `device_config=cpu`):

```
INFO [kv_cache_utils.py:2312] GPU KV cache size: 242,688 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 2,048 tokens per request: 118.50x
INFO [loggers.py:310] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.2 tokens/s, ... GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
INFO [perf.py:1529] Engine 000: MFU: 0.0 TF/s/GPU 0.9 GB/s/GPU
```

**After** (same machine, same commit, change applied):

```
INFO [kv_cache_utils.py:2313] CPU KV cache size: 243,456 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 2,048 tokens per request: 118.88x
INFO [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.2 tokens/s, ... CPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
INFO [perf.py:1529] Engine 000: MFU: 0.0 TF/s/device 0.9 GB/s/device
```

CUDA was not exercised at runtime. The CUDA path is unchanged by construction:
`device_type == "cuda"` selects the literal `"GPU"`, which is what the strings hardcoded
previously, so there is no CUDA-specific branch that could regress.

title: [FlashInfer] Migrate autotune warmup to flashinfer.autotune_v2 managed cache
author: YangXu1990uiuc
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Use FlashInfer's managed autotune cache for eligible single-rank deployments, with shared v1/v2 warmup execution. Multi-rank deployments retain upstream's legacy cache synchronization; enabling managed tuning there remains a separate release/pin/validation step after the now-merged [FlashInfer #6185](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6185).

## Claims

- Automatically select managed v2 when both APIs are present and the deployment is single-rank, single-node, PP=1 and non-elastic.
- Preserve #57635's per-rank legacy files, group-wide cache validation and PP stage-specific tuning groups. Multi-rank managed tuning remains disabled until a released FlashInfer fix is pinned and validated.
- Share generic warmup execution, including HiSparse, ReplaySSM and Kimi, and preserve the MRv2 sparse warmup route. Retain main's speculative-drafter bucket coverage and `round_up=True`; follow main's removal of the separate BF16-only pass.

This is a cache-lifecycle migration, with no claim of universal deadlock prevention, zero warm-start profiling or improved serving throughput.

## Validation

Current head: `adbbc10e0702`. Python source is unchanged from `081e81bca1e7`, which passed **78 targeted CPU warmup tests** and all six PR-file pre-commit checks, including mypy. The documentation-only follow-ups also pass applicable pre-commit checks. User documentation now lists only the vLLM cache override and its managed/legacy defaults.

The branch pins Torch **2.14.0** and FlashInfer **0.7.2**. Local CPU checks used Torch 2.13.0 / FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 plus Humming 0.1.17; the 0.7.2 managed API and cache defaults were checked against release source. These checks do not validate the new GPU dependency stack. Hosted CI for this head is pending.

**Historical GPU evidence:** source `1fee4445c116`, based on main `276fbcff2717`, passed **9/9 GPU lifecycle cases** and [Buildkite #94030](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94030). GPU/model results below have not been rerun on the current head and dependency pin. The existing Model Executor CI step includes the targeted warmup suite.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Targeted warmup suite | 78 passed; eligibility, lifecycle/cleanup, per-rank/PP persistence, inconsistent/partial caches, sparse MRv1/MRv2 routes |
| Changed-file pre-commit and mypy | Passed for all six PR files on `081e81bca1e7`, including the standard Python 3.11-targeting mypy hook |
| B200 TP1, Qwen3-8B-FP8 | Managed cold/warm and same-runtime legacy control: 3/3 passed |
| B200 TP2+EP, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP4, FlashInfer CUTLASS | Main control plus PR cold/warm/partial-cache recovery: 4/4 passed on the retained legacy path |
| B200 PP2, Qwen3-8B-FP8 | Legacy cold/warm: 2/2 passed |
| Managed warm-cache reuse | 40 winners plus manifest unchanged; no new successful profiling observed at the post-init snapshot |
| Full GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, 256 output tokens | Managed warm: 1143/1319 (86.66%); same-runtime legacy: 1157/1319 (87.72%) |

GSM8K difference: **-1.06 percentage points**, approximate paired 95% interval **[-2.41, +0.28]** points. This is one pair of runs and does not establish accuracy equivalence or a stable regression. Selected-token logprobs were finite. No serving-performance claim is made.

Historical GPU runtime: B200, Model Runner v2, Torch 2.13.0, FlashInfer Python/cubin `0.7.0.post1`, matching JIT cache `0.7.0.post1+cu130`. The complete PR Python source was overlaid on native wheel `187a0eb98aa4`; native/build/dependency paths match, but this is not a native rebuild. Engine runs used `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. These are offline `LLM.generate` tests, not HTTP-serving benchmarks. Multi-rank **managed** tuning remains disabled and is not covered by these legacy fallback results.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
pre-commit run --files docs/usage/security.md \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_autotune_cache.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py vllm/utils/flashinfer.py
```

The refreshed CPU check used `PYTHONPATH` pointing to an isolated `humming-kernels==0.1.17` installation. To reproduce the historical GPU results, use the GPU-validated source, native wheel and FlashInfer versions above, with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, and a fresh `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` for cold startup; reuse it for warm startup.

```python
llm = LLM(
    model="nvidia/Qwen3-8B-FP8",
    revision="2cebc4c89e25abc17668c81b01dceaf3d8b914d5",
    tensor_parallel_size=1,
    max_model_len=4096, max_num_batched_tokens=512, max_num_seqs=16,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.7, seed=0,
    kernel_config={"enable_flashinfer_autotune": True, "moe_backend": "auto"},
    compilation_config={"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]},
)
```

Evaluate with `tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval._build_gsm8k_prompts(1319, 5)`, `SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=256, seed=42, stop=["Question", "Assistant:", "<|separator|>"])`, and the suite's `_score_gsm8k`. The legacy control uses a separate cache root and an external worker extension that replaces only `vllm.utils.flashinfer.has_flashinfer_autotune_v2` with `lambda: False` before initialization.

For TP2+EP, use `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP4`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`, `enable_expert_parallel=True`, and `moe_backend="flashinfer_cutlass"`; for PP2, use the FP8 model with `pipeline_parallel_size=2`. The partial-cache test removes only rank 1's persisted legacy file between runs and verifies coordinated recovery and rank-local persistence. Worker snapshots record path selection and cache state; they are not per-call kernel traces.

</details>

## Details

Measurement-policy experiments are tracked separately in [draft #61403](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61403). It adds explicit eager/graph measurement controls and reports three independent B200 tuning rounds plus model evaluations; this cache migration retains the existing measurement defaults and can land independently.

**Mixed cache hits can hang before finalization.** A partial rank-specific cache, or another publisher between rank lookups, can make one rank skip profiling while another enters timing collectives. A final barrier/reload cannot repair that mismatch. [FlashInfer #6185](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6185), merged October 16, coordinates the pre-profiling hit decision in the library. The single-rank gate here avoids enabling this distributed managed-cache path on the current pin. Re-enabling it requires a library release, a pin update and validation; PP, multi-node and Elastic EP retain additional constraints.

`VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` controls placement; FlashInfer owns managed entry/environment identity. Independently tuning deployments should use separate roots. Legacy persistence retains `autotune_configs_dp<dp>_rank<rank>.json` and group-coordinated load success.

SM120 sparse-MLA CPB/crossover calibration is a separate cache under `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DIR`; managed winner reload does not distribute its file or install its process-local state. The reporter supplied a private-API-based patch; supported calibration distribution and affected-hardware validation remain separate follow-up work. Some non-default per-op measurement policies also re-profile on warm starts.

This updates the existing migration, incorporates YangXu1990uiuc/vllm#1, and preserves the merged #57635. The open cache-only startup/search-strategy work addresses different behavior. FlashInfer #3573 handles EP/DP-aware profiling and final synchronization, not the pre-profiling hit decision. All conversation/review pages were revisited under the PR checklist. AI assistance was used for review, implementation and validation; the human submitter remains responsible for the contribution.
