title: [Quantization] Layer re-quantization for linear layers through online quantization API (MXFP8 -> FP8 PTPC showcase)
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
Detailed RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59062

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Purpose

This PR allows re-quantizing linear layers to a different precision using online quantization API, as long as the `dequantize_weight` method for relevant `LinearMethodBase` subclass is implemented.

Similar features have been requested previously in specialized cases:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51274

and this feature exists on sglang side https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28291 / https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29328.

Addresses the third item of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167. This PR is adapted from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427, co-authored by @tanpinsiang.

This change lets `--quantization-config.linear fp8_per_channel` convert selected serialized ModelOpt MXFP8 linears to FP8 PTPC at load time.

The original checkpoint quantization config remains responsible for unselected linears and MoE.

The composition is handled by the existing `resolve_quant_method`, so model implementations continue to receive their original checkpoint quantization config type.

Quantization methods expose an optional `dequantize_weight` method, that:

- raises `NotImplementedError` by default, or
- dequantizes the quant method weights if implemented.

This draft implements it only for `ModelOptMxFp8LinearMethod`.

Such `dequantize_weight` methods implementation can be shared across model producers (quark, modelopt, compressed-tensors, etc.) based on weight quant key, no model producer-specific code should be required.

## Test Plan

```bash
vllm serve mmangkad/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-MXFP8 --quantization-config.linear "fp8_per_channel"
```

or

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --linear-backend auto \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --language-model-only \
  --quantization-config.linear fp8_per_channel
```

`pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py-s -vvvvv`

## Test Result

Unit test passing, end-to-end eval to be added.

title: [Quantization] Enable shared expert fusion compatibility with online `shared_expert` quantization (showcase: along Quark MXFP4 routed experts)
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Purpose

This PR enables compatibility of online `shared_expert` quantization with fused shared expert optimization. As an example, it implements it for for `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod` (and `INCMxfp4MoEMethod` to showcase extensibility, possibly to be removed).

The main idea is that given https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f27ae25473af7520dde3f8b9e0705041940be0c9/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L168-L180 `self.shared_expert = Qwen3NextMLP` is not defined when using `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, we use weight loading in the `RoutedExperts` to capture the shared expert weight loading, quantize it there, and copy the quantized shared expert into the correct quantized fused expert slot.

The original `quant_method` is preserved (e.g. `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod`).

This PR does NOT implement `experts` + `shared_expert` joint online quantization + fusion. `experts` is expected to be already quantized in this PR (loaded through `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod`/`INCMxfp4MoEMethod`)

Main design goal is to be as much as possible quant method agnostic.

We also preserve quant config compatibility checks for fused shared expert, that could be extended to accommodate new precisions e.g. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53161

## Test Plan

Testing:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES="6,7" \
vllm serve \
    amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_expert*": "mxfp4"}' \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2
```

`pytest tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py -s -vvvvv`

## Test Result

Displayed to user: `(EngineCore pid=27900) INFO 08-17 10:29:41 [base_loader.py:109] Quantized 80 layers of types: mlp.shared_expert.down_proj: 40 (from linear: QuantSpec(weight=QuantKey(dtype=torch.uint8, scale=ScaleDesc(dtype=torch.uint8, static=True, group_shape=GroupShape(row=1, col=32)), scale2=None, symmetric=True), activation=None)); mlp.shared_expert.gate_up_proj: 40 (from linear: QuantSpec(weight=QuantKey(dtype=torch.uint8, scale=ScaleDesc(dtype=torch.uint8, static=True, group_shape=GroupShape(row=1, col=32)), scale2=None, symmetric=True), activation=None))`

title: [Mamba] Unify FI ReplaySSM STP/MTP/Prefix Caching Lifecycle
author: askliar
body:
## Summary

Adds FlashInfer ReplaySSM prefix caching in `align` mode, including MTP, for Model Runners V1 and V2.
Replay rings remain inside Mamba pages.

- Preserves live state and cached prefixes across partial acceptance, preemption, and request reordering.
- Batches lifecycle work across cache groups and keeps V1 accepted-token counts on the GPU.
- Fixes Mamba page alignment and checkpoint publication before block release.

[Usage, MTP example, and supported configurations](https://github.com/askliar/vllm/blob/d9cd1fd1fcfc5a08d14ff29ba7439f76ad42d628/docs/features/automatic_prefix_caching.md#flashinfer-replayssm).

## Performance

### ReplaySSM OFF → ON

**Super 3, one GB300, TP1, V2, FP32 SSM state, CUDA graphs, no prefix caching.**
Uses the [paper workloads](https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM/tree/73a9592e9d8a2268620e8883a82f5cec7442ed36/benchmarks/replayssm) with current FlashInfer.
Standard decoding generates 1,000 tokens from a short prompt. Natural MTP3 generates 256 tokens per GSM8K question.
Results average two repetitions per mode in OFF/ON/ON/OFF order.

| Workload | Batch | OFF output TPS | ON output TPS | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | 10,950 | 24,037 | **2.20×** |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | 9,516 | 19,217 | **2.02×** |
| Standard decoding | 256 | 11,412 | 14,631 | **1.28×** |

Output TPS includes prefill and complete generation. MTP gains include higher admission:

| Workload | Peak concurrent decoding, OFF → ON | Per-request decode TPS, OFF → ON |
|---|---:|---:|
| MTP3, batch 512 | **219 → 512** | 61.99 → 59.93 |
| MTP3, batch 256 | **221 → 256** | 60.81 → 97.98 |
| Standard, batch 256 | 256 → 256 | 45.01 → 57.89 |

Concurrent decoding is measured from overlapping request timestamps. Per-request decode TPS is the reciprocal mean time per output token.
All 16 Super runs completed with zero preemptions.

### ReplaySSM OFF → ON with prefix caching

**Same TP1 paper workloads, with prefix caching enabled in both modes.**
Uses Super 3 on one GB300, V2, FP32 SSM state, stock FlashInfer, and normal CUDA graphs.
Each run seeds the exact prompt batch before timing. Results average two runs per mode in OFF/ON/ON/OFF order.

| Workload | Per-request decode TPS, OFF → ON | Decode change | Total output TPS, OFF → ON | Requests with prefix hits, OFF → ON |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MTP3, batch 256 | 60.21 → **91.12** | **+51.3%** | 8,747 → **18,043** | 0 → **256** |
| Standard, batch 256 | 43.88 → **54.56** | **+24.3%** | 11,047 → **13,670** | 256 → 256 |
| MTP3, batch 512 | 60.83 → 57.15 | −6.1% | 10,266 → **20,384** | 0 → 0 |

- **Standard, batch 256:** both modes reuse 13 prompt tokens per request, with zero preemptions.
- **MTP3, batch 256:** ON reuses 19,683 prompt tokens per run with zero preemptions. OFF has no hits and 2–4 preemptions.
- **MTP3, batch 512:** neither mode records prefix hits. ON improves total throughput while decoding more requests together, but per-request decode slows.

Per-request decode TPS is the reciprocal mean time per output token. Total output TPS includes prefill and complete generation.
All 16 prefix-enabled runs completed. These results demonstrate prefix reuse at batch 256.
Gains include differences in cache retention and preemption.

### Prefix caching OFF → ON

**Super 3, four GB300 GPUs, TP4, V2, FP16 SSM state, concurrency one, CUDA graphs.**
ReplaySSM is enabled in both modes.
Workload: 51,200 shared tokens, then 20 turns with 2,048 new input tokens and 1,024 output tokens.
MTP uses three drafts and synthetic acceptance length 3.1151. Values average two repetitions per mode.

| Metric | Prefix OFF | Prefix ON | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| E2E output TPS | 304.76 | 518.88 | **+70.26%** |
| Decode TPS | 589.38 | 611.60 | **+3.77%** |
| Time to first token, mean repeat median | 1,658.9 ms | 249.8 ms | **−84.94%** |

Each ON run records **1,513,680 prefix-hit tokens**. Measurements include first-use checkpoint-store compilation.

### Comparison with main

Same TP4 workload, ReplaySSM enabled, prefix caching disabled.

| Comparison | Main | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| STP decode TPS, identical saved tuning | 239.77 | 239.65 | −0.05% |
| MTP decode TPS | 577.02 | 587.76 | +1.86% |
| MTP E2E output TPS | 303.20 | 301.58 | −0.54% |

## Validation

Manual GB300 validation:

- **71 component tests passed**, with one expected missing-provider skip.
- **17 E2E test identities passed** across tested revisions, covering FP16 TP2 MTP, prefix reuse, preemption, and partial acceptance.
- **Hooks and DCO passed** on `d9cd1fd1fc`; [hosted pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40393393118).

title: [Feat][Frontend] Add Watchdog for Engine and Worker Monitoring
author: wenjinhust
body:
## Purpose

 Fixes RFC [#56816 ](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56816)

  Add a watchdog mechanism to vLLM V1 to automatically capture all-thread stack
  traces when the engine or worker process stops making progress, making it easier
  to diagnose hangs and deadlocks.

  - **New `vllm/utils/watch_dog.py`**: introduces the `WatchDog` class. A background
    daemon thread monitors a heartbeat (`feed()`); if the heartbeat is not refreshed
    within a timeout (default 300s, checked every 10s), it dumps the stack traces of
    all threads via `faulthandler` into a per-process log file
    (`VLLM_STACK_DUMP_for_<name>_<pid>.log`). Repeated timeouts without an intervening
    feed are logged only once. Provides `feed()` / `dump_stack()` / `start()` /
    `stop()` and a process-wide singleton `get_watch_dog()`.
  - **EngineCoreProc**: creates and starts a watchdog named `engine` after startup and
    feeds it while processing the input queue and before each engine step. The input
    queue `get()` now uses `timeout=5` so the loop stays responsive while preserving
    the original blocking semantics. The shutdown signal handler dumps all thread
    stacks for diagnosis.
  - **WorkerProc** (multiproc executor): likewise creates and starts a watchdog named
    `worker` and feeds it before executing every worker method; its signal handler
    dumps all thread stacks.


  ## Test Plan & Result

### Test Qwen3-8B by TP 1:

- Launch vllm:

title: [Bugfix][Core] Preserve speculative metrics when coalescing outputs
author: git-jxj
body:
## Overview

Preserve terminal per-request speculative-decoding metrics when a slow DELTA consumer coalesces request outputs.

## Claims

- Keep `CompletionOutput.spec_decode_metrics` from the terminal chunk when merging it with earlier chunks, without changing generated tokens or text.

## Validation

The regression fails on baseline `f0c44cc7d5` with `spec_decode_metrics=None`. The regression, collector/sampling-mask tests, and upstream pooling-error regressions pass: **12 passed, 40 deselected**.

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_outputs.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -k 'request_output or collector or sampling_mask or specialized_pooling_outputs'
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --hook-stage manual --files vllm/outputs.py tests/test_outputs.py
```

All applicable changed-file manual hooks pass, including mypy for Python 3.10–3.13. The human submitter confirmed review of every changed line and personally passing the relevant tests. The unchanged tree at `19660d2a6e` was independently revalidated on the node before this update.

Real GPU validation used Qwen3-0.6B on an RTX 5060 Ti, n-gram speculation with three draft tokens, DELTA output, and a consumer sleeping three seconds between chunks:

| Configuration | Baseline `f0c44cc7d5` | Updated `19660d2a6e` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Terminal speculative metrics | Lost (`None`) | All **93 draft / 77 accepted tokens** retained |
| Generated output | 128 tokens | Identical 128 token IDs and text |

This exercised the real AsyncLLM serving engine with checkout Python source and existing precompiled native extensions (`0.28.1rc1.dev396+g9cd956c7e`), using MRV1 and the PyTorch sampler. HTTP API behavior and rebuilt native extensions were not tested. Current-head `pre-run-check` stops before upstream pre-commit at the contributor authorization gate; upstream CI has not run.

<details>
<summary>GPU reproducer configuration</summary>

Use a local Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, and `.venv/bin/python` with the following AsyncLLM reproducer. The baseline returns `None`; the fix returns the engine's terminal metrics.

```python
import asyncio
from vllm import AsyncEngineArgs, SamplingParams
from vllm.sampling_params import RequestOutputKind
from vllm.v1.engine.async_llm import AsyncLLM

async def main():
    engine = AsyncLLM.from_engine_args(AsyncEngineArgs(
        model="/path/to/Qwen3-0.6B", dtype="bfloat16",
        max_model_len=512, max_num_seqs=1, max_num_batched_tokens=512,
        kv_cache_memory_bytes=256 * 1024 * 1024,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.25, enforce_eager=True,
        enable_prefix_caching=False, disable_log_stats=True,
        speculative_config={"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
                            "prompt_lookup_min": 1, "prompt_lookup_max": 3},
        per_request_spec_decode_metrics="summary",
    ))
    prompt = ("<|im_start|>user\n/no_think\n"
              "Repeat the phrase red blue green fifty times, separated by spaces. "
              "Output only the repeated words.\n<|im_end|>\n"
              "<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n")
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128, ignore_eos=True,
                            output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA)
    try:
        async for output in engine.generate(prompt, params, request_id="slow-delta"):
            if output.finished:
                print(output.outputs[0].spec_decode_metrics)
            else:
                await asyncio.sleep(3)
    finally:
        engine.shutdown(timeout=10)

asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

## Details

`RequestOutput.add(aggregate=True)` appends token data and copies finish state, but misses `spec_decode_metrics`, which is populated only on the terminal completion. Copy its non-null value in that existing aggregation path.

Rebased onto `f0c44cc7d5`, preserving upstream #58975 pooling-error regressions and the sampling-mask behavior from #55935. This PR addresses the remaining terminal-metrics loss. Checked against subsequent main `8442117446`: relevant output/engine/test code is unchanged, and an offline merge is clean with the identical two-file patch. Earlier open-PR searches found no other matching aggregation-metrics fix; #55935 covers the separate sampling-mask behavior.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Validate SWA coverage at unaligned cache-hit boundaries
author: xijiaat
body:
## Purpose

Prevent an offload cache hit from passing lookup when it lacks an SWA chunk
that GPU block allocation will require. With mixed cache-group granularities,
the common hit boundary can fall inside an SWA CPU chunk. The fixed suffix
window then misses a required chunk on the left, causing
`CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_load()` to assert.

For example, with a 3904-token hit, a 128-token window, 64-token GPU blocks and
256-token CPU chunks, lookup checks chunk 15 but allocation needs chunks 14
and 15. This reproduces without concurrent eviction or transport failure.

Compute the first lookup window from the actual hit boundary, and use the same
coverage when checking in-flight loads. Missing coverage is rejected before
allocation; pending coverage defers. Earlier chunk-aligned candidates retain
their existing window size. Store behavior, transfer code, and the CPU cache
assertion are unchanged. No new configuration or public API.

Related #54914: the assertion matches, but this does not establish the cause of
that historical incident. Duplicate checks found no matching open fix.
#52287 preserves store-side EAGLE replay windows; #55118 concerns verified
full-attention EAGLE tail handling. This patch validates load coverage even
when entries are already absent, including without EAGLE.
#55168 changes a different connector (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`) under DCP;
this fix is for `OffloadingConnector` and reproduces with world size 1.

## Tests

The CPU runs used pinned main Python sources with a process-local import

title: [Spec Decode] Add NVFP4 DSpark gathered top-k projection
author: askliar
body:
## Motivation

DSpark's Markov head computes the draft correction by selecting rows from its W2 projection. With a quantized W2 Markov head, those rows are stored as packed NVFP4 values plus per-group/global scales, so they cannot be indexed and used as ordinary dense weights. The selected rows must be gathered and dequantized before the correction matmul.

This is required to run `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark`, whose Markov head is quantized. Without this path, draft top-k either cannot run or falls back to an incompatible dense-weight assumption.

## What changed

- Retain packed NVFP4 W2 weights and scales after ModelOpt loading when DSpark draft top-k is enabled.
- Add a Triton gathered-row dequantization and bias kernel for CUDA BF16.
- Preserve the dequantize/scatter fallback for CPU and CUDA FP16/W4A16 paths.
- Add focused parity coverage for the gathered NVFP4 path.

## Showcase

Matched Nemotron 3.5 Lightning run with DL=5, synthetic AL=3.3, natural routing, ISL=34,817, OSL=1,024, concurrency 1, and 5 measured requests:

| Temperature | Top-k | TPS/user | Global TPS | Observed AL | Avg OSL |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T=0 | 512 | 135.337 | 128.986 | 3.5168 | 864.06 |
| T=0 | Off | 130.861 | 124.296 | 3.4944 | 872.42 |
| T=1 | 512 | 133.502 | 126.880 | 3.4628 | 857.34 |
| T=1 | Off | 128.542 | 121.981 | 3.4275 | 873.52 |

Top-k off versus top-k=512:

- T=0: -3.31% TPS/user, -3.64% global TPS, -0.0224 AL
- T=1: -3.72% TPS/user, -3.86% global TPS, -0.0353 AL

Both configurations completed 2 warmups and 5/5 measured requests with zero errors; observed synthetic acceptance length was 3.2636 in both runs.

## Validation

- `python3 -m compileall -q` on all changed Python files
- `git diff --check`
- Direct CUDA gathered-kernel parity passed for batches 1, 2, 4, and 8.

title: [Perf][GDN] Enable the FlashInfer GDN prefill kernel on SM12x
author: stecasta
body:
## Purpose

FlashInfer's GDN prefill kernel is never used on SM12x, so consumer and SoC Blackwell (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, DGX Spark GB10) silently runs the Triton/FLA fallback for every linear-attention layer. On Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 that is 3 of every 4 layers.

`_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend()` only sets `supports_flashinfer` for SM90 or the SM10x family, so SM12x falls through to `return backend, "triton"`.

The gate is now stale.. It was written in #40717 (merged 2026-05-20) to enable FlashInfer's **SM100** kernel. FlashInfer's **SM120** CuTe-DSL delta rule prefill kernel landed later, in [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3479](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3479) (merged 2026-06-17), and nothing revisited the gate afterwards. FlashInfer ships and tests it: `flashinfer/gdn_kernels/delta_rule_dsl/delta_rule_sm120.py` is on main, `gdn_prefill.py` imports `chunk_gated_delta_rule_sm120` and `cp_delta_rule_dsl_sm120`, and `tests/gdn/test_prefill_delta_rule.py` guards with *"Skip test if not SM90, SM100, or SM12x (with CUDA 13+) architecture."*

## Fix

Add an SM12x branch using the same conditions as the SM10x one (`head_k_dim == 128`, CUDA >= 13), which match what FlashInfer's own GDN prefill test requires.


## Test Result

Kernel A/B on DGX Spark GB10 (SM121), vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c`, FlashInfer 0.6.18, both arms in one process on one node. Baseline is `vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.chunk_gated_delta_rule`, which is what this gate currently selects. FlashInfer is invoked exactly as `fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule()` does it (l2norm, squeeze, `exp(g)`, fp32 state). Geometry from `Qwen3.8-27B`: `linear_num_key_heads=16`, `linear_num_value_heads=48`, `linear_key_head_dim=128`.

| seqlen | FLA/Triton | FlashInfer | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 1.166 ms | 0.305 ms | 3.83x |
| 2048 | 2.333 ms | 0.569 ms | 4.10x |
| 4096 | 4.581 ms | 1.056 ms | 4.34x |
| 8192 | 9.084 ms | 2.008 ms | 4.52x |

### Numerical agreement

Same setup, comparing output and `final_state` against the Triton/FLA path. GDN state layout has been a correctness trap before (the `final_state` transpose issue found on B300 during #40717 review, and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3155), so `final_state` is checked explicitly, including varlen batches.

| seq_lens | out max abs | out rel | state max abs | state rel |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [1024] | 0.00098 | 0.0118 | 0.00438 | 0.0042 |
| [2048] | 0.00098 | 0.0107 | 0.00421 | 0.0059 |
| [4096] | 0.00098 | 0.0084 | 0.00425 | 0.0055 |
| [256, 256] | 0.00073 | 0.0085 | 0.00477 | 0.0057 |
| [64, 128, 512] | 0.00098 | 0.0122 | 0.00451 | 0.0046 |
| [2048, 2048] | 0.00098 | 0.0084 | 0.00429 | 0.0055 |

All within bf16 tolerance, and `final_state` agrees, so the transpose trap does not apply on this path. Device reported `cc (12, 1)`, CUDA runtime 13.0, so both gate conditions hold.

### End-to-end serving

vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c`, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 with DFlash2 `num_speculative_tokens=7`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, TP1. Both arms use the same container image except for this patch. Acceptance length is forced (`synthetic_acceptance_length=5.695`, measured 5.72) so the two arms decode identical token counts and the comparison isolates prefill.

RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q (SM120), 32768-token shared prefix plus ISL 2048 / OSL 256, prefix caching enabled, measured hit rate 82.5%, `Usage Prompt Tokens` 34868:

| | Triton/FLA | FlashInfer | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT, concurrency 1 | 1061.44 ms | 1008.68 ms | 5.0% |
| TTFT, concurrency 4 | 3767.81 ms | 3518.07 ms | 6.6% |
| Request latency, c1 | 2151.66 ms | 2089.85 ms | 2.9% |
| Request latency, c4 | 5137.93 ms | 4860.53 ms | 5.4% |
| Output throughput, c1 | 118.79 tok/s | 122.23 tok/s | 2.9% |
| Output throughput, c4 | 199.20 tok/s | 209.55 tok/s | 5.2% |

DGX Spark GB10 (SM121), ISL 32768 with prefix caching disabled so every request computes all 32768 tokens:

| | Triton/FLA | FlashInfer | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT, concurrency 1 | 17972.22 ms | 16679.82 ms | 7.2% |
| TTFT, concurrency 4 | 26348.74 ms | 24400.14 ms | 7.4% |
| Request latency, c1 | 23235.23 ms | 21932.34 ms | 5.6% |
| Request latency, c4 | 78354.18 ms | 73463.86 ms | 6.2% |
| Output throughput, c1 | 11.01 tok/s | 11.67 tok/s | 6.0% |
| Output throughput, c4 | 13.03 tok/s | 13.87 tok/s | 6.4% |

The relative gain is similar across the two shapes because GDN prefill and the layers it competes with are both linear in sequence length, so the ratio is largely length invariant. What changes is the absolute saving: 52.8 ms of TTFT at ISL 2048 computed, against 1292.4 ms at ISL 32768 computed, tracking the roughly 17x difference in computed tokens.

Backend selection was confirmed from the server log on both architectures rather than inferred, with the baseline logging `Using Triton/FLA GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, head_k_dim=128)` and the patched build logging `Using FlashInfer GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, head_k_dim=128)`.

## Why this is not a duplicate

I ran the checks in AGENTS.md. Nothing open widens this gate. #38315 optimises the Triton `chunk_gated_delta_rule` path this change routes around, and is complementary. #36414 proposed a PyTorch GDN fallback for SM12.0+ and was closed. #43273 added the in-tree SM100 CuteDSL kernel, which this does not touch.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to author this change. I have reviewed every changed line, ran the benchmarks above myself, and can defend the design.

title: [XPU] Wire up SYCL apply_rotary_emb kernel in ApplyRotaryEmb
author: mganczarenko
body:
## Purpose

  `ApplyRotaryEmb.forward_cuda` imports `vllm.vllm_flash_attn.layers.rotary`, a CUDA-only
  module, so there is no `forward_xpu` override and every XPU call falls back to the CustomOp
  default `forward_native` (~8 elementwise kernels). `vllm_xpu_kernels` — already a pinned
  dependency (`requirements/xpu.txt`) — ships a SYCL `apply_rotary_emb` kernel that vLLM never
  calls. This adds an 11-line `forward_xpu` wiring it up, following the same per-backend pattern
  already used by `forward_cuda`/`forward_hip` in this class.


  ## Test Plan

  `pytest tests/kernels/core/test_apply_rotary_emb.py -v` on XPU hardware — 3 new XPU-gated
  cases (text / GPT-J interleaved / partial-rotary) comparing `forward_xpu` against
  `forward_native` bit-exact (`atol=0, rtol=0`).

  Additional correctness sweep across 12 shapes (vision + text, both RoPE styles, partial
  rotary), calling the real `forward_xpu`/CustomOp dispatch path (not the raw kernel).

  End-to-end check on GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking (vision-heavy multimodal, eager mode, 4 images @
  1024px, 5 iterations), comparing wall-clock and output text SHA-256 before/after.

  ## Test Result

  `test_apply_rotary_emb.py`: 3 new cases pass; 4 pre-existing CUDA-only dispatch tests correctly
  skip on XPU.

  12-shape correctness sweep: maxerr 0.0 in all 12 cases.

  GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking E2E: median latency 2.5414s -> 2.4794s (1.025x). Output text SHA-256
  identical between unpatched and patched arms across all 5 iterations — no behavior change
  beyond speed. RoPE is a small fraction of this model's device time, so the wall-clock win here
  is modest; the kernel-level win (measured separately, not included in this PR) is larger and
  should generalize better on RoPE-heavier models.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Decode hot-path cleanups: strided KDA recurrent inputs, NoPE MQA query without concat, no duplicate router GEMM
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

Three small, independent decode hot-path cleanups found while profiling GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, FP8, TP4 on 4x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`):

1. **KDA decode: read token-strided q/k/v/beta in `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`.** The decode path hands the recurrent kernel column slices of the merged `q|k|v` conv output and of the fused `qkvbfg_a` projection (beta); `fused_recurrent_kda` made each contiguous, i.e. 4 copy kernels per KDA layer per step (34 layers; ~11 us/layer at 64 requests, ~0.4 ms/step). The Triton kernel now takes explicit token strides; contiguous callers are unchanged. The stride check is pure integer arithmetic (no views) because the KDA forward is a CUDA-graph break and runs eagerly.
2. **MLA: write the absorbed MQA query token-major and skip the empty RoPE concat.** Without head padding the W_UK bmm now writes into a `(B, N, L)` buffer through a transposed `out` view (verified: one GEMM kernel, no copy, identical result). For NoPE models (`qk_rope_head_dim == 0`) the FlashInfer sparse backend then uses `ql_nope` directly instead of `torch.cat` with a zero-width `q_pe`, which took the slow `CatArrayBatchedCopy` path (13.7 us/layer at 256 decode tokens, ~0.75 ms/layer per 16k-token prefill chunk).
3. **Glm5NextMoE: do not compute the router logits twice.** `MoERunner` holds the gate (passed via `FusedMoEFactory`) and recomputes the logits (`moe_runner.py:897`), so the gate GEMM in `Glm5NextMoE.forward` was wasted (two bf16->fp32 GEMMs + reductions per MoE layer). Follows `DeepseekV2MoE` and passes a placeholder.

## Test Plan

- Unit / kernel tests listed under "Tests" below.
- Serving benchmark, all builds back-to-back in one session on 4x GB300 (SM100), TP4, prefix caching disabled:
  ```bash
  vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 4 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE \
    --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model glm53-flash --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 \
    --ignore-eos --seed 0 --random-input-len <in> --random-output-len <out> --max-concurrency <c> \
    --num-prompts <n> --num-warmups <c> --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
  ```
  Points: 1k/512 at c=1/64/256; prefill-only 8x2048, 2x8192, 8x32768, 2x65536; 32k/256 at c=16. The prefix-cache hit rate in the server log was checked to be 0.0% for every run.
- Accuracy per build: `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0`

## Test Result

### Performance of this PR alone

main `156050598` vs main + this PR, 4x GB300, TP4, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, **prefix caching disabled** (hit rate 0.0% checked in the server log), `vllm bench serve` random dataset with warmups, both servers run back-to-back in the same session. Decode tok/s is the steady-state window value (full concurrency); TPOT is the per-request median.

| point | metric | main | +#55736 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1k/512 c=1 | decode tok/s | 144 | 146 | +1.8% |
| 1k/512 c=1 | median TPOT ms | 6.57 | 6.46 | -1.7% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | decode tok/s | 2964 | 3090 | +4.3% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | median TPOT ms | 20.02 | 19.26 | -3.8% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | decode tok/s | 7147 | 7367 | +3.1% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | median TPOT ms | 33.87 | 32.87 | -3.0% |
| prefill 8x2048 | mean TTFT ms | 461 | 449 | -2.5% |
| prefill 2x8192 | mean TTFT ms | 389 | 380 | -2.4% |
| prefill 8x32768 | mean TTFT ms | 5258 | 5108 | -2.8% |
| prefill 2x65536 | mean TTFT ms | 2738 | 2661 | -2.8% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | decode tok/s | 287 | 296 | +3.1% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | mean TTFT ms | 3883 | 3835 | -1.2% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | median TPOT ms | 41.34 | 40.10 | -3.0% |

Decode: +3-4% tok/s (−3-4% TPOT) at c=64, c=256 and in the 32k-context point, −1.7% TPOT at c=1 (host-bound). Prefill: a consistent −2.5-2.8% TTFT on all four points

### Accuracy (per build, same session)

Each rung of the ablation was also evaluated on its own: **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, lm_eval `local-completions`)

| build | gsm8k flexible-extract % | gsm8k strict-match % |
|---|---|---|
| main | 93.33 ± 0.69 | 93.10 ± 0.70 | 
| +#55736 | 93.03 ± 0.70 | 92.95 ± 0.71 |

## Duplicate-work check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_recurrent_kda stride"`, `"MoERunner gate router_logits Glm5Next"`, `"GLM-5.3-Flash prefill"`: no open PR covers these (the open GLM-5.3-Flash PRs #54951 / #55222 / #55385 / #55543 touch the indexer prefill sharding, SM90 sparse-MLA dtypes and the SM90 FA/FlashMLA wiring).

## Tests

- `pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (new; fp32 PyTorch reference for plain and spec-decode shapes, strided-vs-contiguous bit-identity, unaddressable layouts rejected): 6 passed.
- bmm into a transposed `out`: max diff 0.0 vs `bmm().transpose()`, profiler shows a single `nvjet` kernel.
- `pre-commit run ruff-check / ruff-format` on the changed files: passed.
- e2e: serving smoke (chat sanity); prompt-logprob A/B on real 4k/12k/30k/60k prompts vs main is within ~1-2.5x the main-vs-main run-to-run noise floor with identical next tokens; **gsm8k 1319 questions (5-shot, greedy): main 93.03% ± 0.70, full series 92.65% ± 0.72** (5 questions, < 1σ; measured on the three PRs together).

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Use FlashKDA for KDA chunked prefill (1.7-3.8x faster than the Triton chunk path)
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

Use **FlashKDA** (`vllm._flashkda_C`, already built and used by Kimi-K3) for GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA chunked prefill instead of the ~15-kernel Triton `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` path.

FlashKDA implements the same bounded-gate KDA recurrence GLM-5.3-Flash uses (`lower_bound * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (g + dt_bias))`, in-kernel q/k l2norm, raw beta logits), so it is a drop-in. On GB300 per KDA layer (H=16/rank, D=128, `bench/flashkda_vs_chunk.py`):

| shape | Triton chunk path | FlashKDA |
|---|---|---|
| 8 x 2048 tokens | 183 us | 49 us |
| 4 x 8192 | 555 us | 146 us |
| 1 x 16384 | 1371 us | 787 us |

Selection: automatic when supported (SM90/SM10x/SM12x, bf16, head_dim 128, bounded gate); `additional_config.kda_prefill_backend = triton` keeps the old path (`flashkda` forces it). The output is written straight into the layer buffer (no merge copy) and the pre-sigmoid beta cast is not needed on this path. Spec-decode tokens themselves keep the Triton recurrent kernel (`num_accepted_tokens` rollback); in a step that carries both, FlashKDA runs the prefill segment into a workspace buffer and the outputs are scattered back by `non_spec_token_indx` / `spec_token_indx` (same scheme as the Kimi-K3 KDA layer; the merge writes straight into `core_attn_out`).

## Test Plan

- Unit / kernel tests listed under "Tests" below.
- Serving benchmark, all builds back-to-back in one session on 4x GB300 (SM100), TP4, prefix caching disabled:
  ```bash
  vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 4 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE \
    --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model glm53-flash --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 \
    --ignore-eos --seed 0 --random-input-len <in> --random-output-len <out> --max-concurrency <c> \
    --num-prompts <n> --num-warmups <c> --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
  ```
  0 prefix-cache hit rate in the server log was checked to be 0.0% for every run.
- Accuracy per build: `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0` (1319 questions), prompt-logprob agreement on real 4k/12k/30k/60k prompts vs main, and a 36-needle retrieval set at 6k/16k/30k (greedy, `reasoning_effort=low`), repeated 3x on main / +#55736 / full stack.

## Test Result

### Performance of this PR alone

Measured on top of #55736 (main + #55736) vs the same + this PR, 4x GB300, TP4, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, **prefix caching disabled** (hit rate 0.0% checked in the server log), `vllm bench serve` random dataset with warmups, back-to-back in the same session. #55736 only touches decode, so this is the effect of FlashKDA on an otherwise-main prefill path. Decode tok/s is the steady-state window value; TPOT is the per-request median.

| point | metric | +#55736 | +#55736 +#55737 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 8x2048 | mean TTFT ms | 449 | 395 | -12.2% |
| prefill 2x8192 | mean TTFT ms | 380 | 330 | -13.2% |
| prefill 8x32768 | mean TTFT ms | 5108 | 4693 | -8.1% |
| prefill 2x65536 | mean TTFT ms | 2661 | 2450 | -7.9% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | decode tok/s | 296 | 316 | +6.6% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | mean TTFT ms | 3835 | 3642 | -5.0% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | median TPOT ms | 40.10 | 37.50 | -6.5% |
| 1k/512 c=1 | decode tok/s | 146 | 147 | +0.7% |
| 1k/512 c=1 | median TPOT ms | 6.46 | 6.47 | +0.2% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | decode tok/s | 3090 | 3132 | +1.4% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | median TPOT ms | 19.26 | 19.24 | -0.1% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | decode tok/s | 7367 | 7717 | +4.7% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | median TPOT ms | 32.87 | 31.30 | -4.8% |

### With speculative decoding (MTP k=1)

Same build, same settings plus `--speculative-config.method=mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens=1`, `kda_prefill_backend=triton` vs `flashkda`, back-to-back. Random-dataset acceptance is ~1.2 tokens/step, so absolute decode numbers are low; the comparison is what matters. Whole-run throughput (the steady-state window accounting is off under spec decode).

| point | metric | MTP k=1 + Triton KDA prefill  | MTP k=1 + FlashKDA |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 8x2048 | mean TTFT ms | 464 | 423 (-8.8%) |
| prefill 2x8192 | mean TTFT ms | 390 | 360 (-7.7%) |
| 32k/256 c=16 | decode tok/s | 260 | 284 (+9.5%) |
| 32k/256 c=16 | mean TTFT ms | 2623 | 2479 (-5.5%) |
| 32k/256 c=16 | median TPOT ms | 52.09 | 47.86 (-8.1%) |
| 1k/512 c=64 | decode tok/s | 2003 | 2130 (+6.3%) |
| 1k/512 c=64 | median TPOT ms | 30.00 | 27.56 (-8.1%) |
| 1k/512 c=256 | decode tok/s | 3697 | 4116 (+11.3%) |
| 1k/512 c=256 | median TPOT ms | 67.96 | 60.53 (-10.9%) |

### Accuracy (per build, same session)

Each rung of the ablation was also evaluated on its own: **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, lm_eval `local-completions`

| build | gsm8k flexible-extract % | gsm8k strict-match % |
|---|---|---|
| main | 93.33 ± 0.69 | 93.10 ± 0.70 |
| +#55736 +#55737 | 93.25 ± 0.69 | 93.18 ± 0.69 |


## Duplicate-work check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "GLM-5.3-Flash FlashKDA"` / `"glm5next KDA"`: no open PR wires FlashKDA for GLM-5.3-Flash (#55224 is the KDA conv weight refit fix).
- vllm-project/vllm#55364 (FlashInfer KDA kernels) is Kimi-K3 only (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/...`) and adds a `--kda-prefill-backend` engine arg; this PR touches only `vllm/models/glm5next/...`. Once #55364 lands, the `additional_config.kda_prefill_backend` knob here should move to that arg.

## Tests

- `bench/kda_numerics.py`: FlashKDA vs the naive recurrent reference (from `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py`) mean|Δ| 2e-5, max 4.8e-4 on outputs, same as the Triton chunk path vs the reference (T=48, 2 sequences, lower_bound -5). Note the Triton chunk path writes its output into `v`'s buffer, so the comparison clones `v`.
- `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py -k flashkda`: 2 passed (extension sanity).
- e2e: chat sanity; prompt-logprob A/B vs main within ~1-2.5x the main-vs-main noise floor with identical next tokens; **gsm8k 1319 questions (5-shot, greedy): main 93.03% ± 0.70, full series 92.65% ± 0.72** (measured on the three PRs together).
- `pre-commit run ruff-check / ruff-format`: passed.

## Notes for review

- FlashKDA hardcodes dense q/k/v strides, so the three `.contiguous()` copies of the conv-output slices remain (~115 us/layer per 16k chunk); a follow-up could run the short conv per q/k/v into separate buffers.
- AI assistance: developed with Claude and reviewed by the submitter

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Dense/masked-MHA sparse prefill for the NoPE (256, 0, 256) layout + skip the NoPE K concat
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

On main, GLM-5.3-Flash's MLA layout (qk_nope 256, qk_rope 0, v 256) is unknown to the FlashAttention prefill backend and to the masked-MHA allow-list, so `MLACommonImpl` logs `No MLA prefill backend supports this model` and **every prefill token goes through the per-token top-k MQA kernel**. Profiling shows that kernel is KV-gather bound at the HBM roofline: 5.9 ms/layer per 16k-token chunk, and still 1.6 ms/layer for 8x2048 where dense MHA needs ~0.2 ms.

Three commits:
1. **Register the (256, 0, 256) dims with `FlashAttnPrefillBackend`** (7 lines). Same lines as in the SM90 wiring PR vllm-project/vllm#55385; kept separate so it can be dropped once that lands. This alone gives the dense-MHA prefill path for sequences ≤ index_topk (2048).
2. **Masked-MHA allow-list**: `_is_masked_mha_available` only knew (128, 512, 128, 64, 128) and (64, 512, 192, 64, 256); GLM-5.3-Flash is (64, 512, 256, 0, 256). The kernels are identical for qk_head_dim 256 / v 256, so sequences between 2k and the existing FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE thresholds (36k at TP4, 64k at TP8) now use FA4 masked MHA instead of the per-token top-k MQA kernel.
3. **NoPE K concat**: `_concat_k_nope_k_pe` returns `k_nope` directly when there is no RoPE part instead of allocating and copying a same-sized tensor (134 MB/layer per 16k chunk).

## Test Plan

- Unit / kernel tests listed under "Tests" below.
- Serving benchmark, all builds back-to-back in one session on 4x GB300 (SM100), TP4, prefix caching disabled:
  ```bash
  vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 4 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE \
    --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model glm53-flash --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 \
    --ignore-eos --seed 0 --random-input-len <in> --random-output-len <out> --max-concurrency <c> \
    --num-prompts <n> --num-warmups <c> --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
  ```
 0 prefix-cache hit 
- Accuracy per build: `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0` (1319 questions)

## Test Result

### Performance of this PR alone

Measured on top of #55736 + #55737 (main + #55736 + #55737) vs the same + this PR, 4x GB300, TP4, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, **prefix caching disabled** (hit rate 0.0% checked in the server log), `vllm bench serve` random dataset with warmups, back-to-back in the same session. Decode tok/s is the steady-state window value; TPOT is the per-request median.

| point | metric | +#55736 +#55737 | +#55736 +#55737 +#55738 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 8x2048 | mean TTFT ms | 395 | 361 | -8.5% |
| prefill 2x8192 | mean TTFT ms | 330 | 315 | -4.6% |
| prefill 8x32768 | mean TTFT ms | 4693 | 4347 | -7.4% |
| prefill 2x65536 | mean TTFT ms | 2450 | 2365 | -3.5% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | decode tok/s | 316 | 322 | +1.9% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | mean TTFT ms | 3642 | 3482 | -4.4% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | median TPOT ms | 37.50 | 36.97 | -1.4% |
| 1k/512 c=1 | decode tok/s | 147 | 147 | -0.2% |
| 1k/512 c=1 | median TPOT ms | 6.47 | 6.49 | +0.3% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | decode tok/s | 3132 | 3133 | +0.0% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | median TPOT ms | 19.24 | 19.09 | -0.8% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | decode tok/s | 7717 | 7755 | +0.5% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | median TPOT ms | 31.30 | 31.29 | -0.0% |

Prefill up to the masked-MHA threshold (≤ 36k at TP4): −8.5% TTFT for 8x2048 (dense MHA), −7.4% for 8x32k (masked MHA), −4.4% TTFT in the 32k-context serving point. 2x8192 shows −4.6%, but that 16-request point has a ~4% run-to-run noise floor (last column of the ablation below), so treat it as indicative only. 64k prompts are above the threshold and stay on the sparse kernel; the −3.5% there (0.0% noise floor) is the K-concat removal alone. Decode is unchanged (±0.8%).


### Accuracy (per build, same session)

Each rung of the ablation was also evaluated on its own: **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, lm_eval `local-completions`), **prompt-logprob agreement** on real 4k/12k/30k/60k prompts (mean |Δ logprob| per token vs the main build; the "main again" row is the run-to-run noise floor of this FP8 model), and a **needle-in-a-haystack** retrieval set (12 codes per length at 6k/16k/30k tokens, greedy, `reasoning_effort=low`), which exercises the 2k-36k prefill range where #55738 switches kernels.

| build | gsm8k flexible-extract % | gsm8k strict-match % |
|---|---|---|
| main | 93.33 ± 0.69 | 93.10 ± 0.70 |
| +#55736 +#55737 +#55738 | 93.10 ± 0.70 | 93.10 ± 0.70 |


### Caveat: runtime JIT

The first request in each new sequence-length bucket JIT-compiles the FA4 CuTeDSL `mask_mod` variant (`BlackwellFusedMultiHeadAttentionForward`) plus the Triton `_scatter_topk_single_req_kernel` (~7 s each; `jit_monitor` warns). `FA4MLAPrefillKernel.get_warmup_keys` does not cover mask_mod, so this is a pre-existing gap for every masked-MHA model; a warmup for the masked variants should be a follow-up before relying on this in production.

## Duplicate-work check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "NoPE masked MHA 256"` / `"GLM-5.3-Flash prefill"`: #55385 covers the FA dims (commit 1 here is the same 7 lines); #54951 / #55222 / #55543 touch the indexer prefill sharding, the indexer workspace and SM90 fp8 KV. None adds the masked-MHA layout or the K-concat skip.
- vllm-project/vllm#53969 / #55277 add NoPE support to the SM120 FlashInfer sparse backend only (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py`); no overlap with the masked-MHA allow-list or the K-concat skip.

## Tests

- New unit tests (all pass on GB300, 14 cases):
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness[glm53_flash_nope_hd256_v256-*]`: dense MHA, masked MHA and masked MHA with chunked context for the NoPE `(64, 256, 0, 256)` layout against the per-token SDPA reference.
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_is_masked_mha_available_model_dims`: allow-list accepts the DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5 and NoPE GLM-5.3-Flash geometries and rejects quantized KV, FA3, `(256, 64, 256)` and a different head count.
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py::TestBackendValidation::test_flash_attn_accepts_glm53_flash_nope_dimensions`: `FlashAttnPrefillBackend.validate_configuration` accepts `(256, 0, 256)` and still rejects `(256, 64, 256)`.
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_concat_k_nope_k_pe_matches_torch_cat[rope|nope]`: `_concat_k_nope_k_pe` equals `torch.cat` of `k_nope` and the broadcast `k_pe`; with no RoPE part it returns `k_nope` itself (same `data_ptr`).
- `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`, `tests/kernels/test_glm5next_kda_recurrent_strided.py` unaffected; prompt-logprob A/B on real 4k/12k/30k/60k prompts vs main: mean|Δ| 0.06-0.12 vs a main-vs-main noise floor of 0.04-0.11 (≈2.5x at 4k where dense/masked MHA replaces the sparse kernel), identical next tokens; **gsm8k 1319 questions (5-shot, greedy): main 93.03% ± 0.70, full series 92.65% ± 0.72** (measured on the three PRs together).
- `pre-commit run ruff-check / ruff-format`: passed.
- AI assistance: developed with Claude Fable 5.1 and reviewed by the submitter; profiling notes and raw benchmark logs available on request.

## Notes for review

title: [Core] Default prefix_cache_retention_interval to dense for Mamba + EAGLE
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

#52216 promoted `prefix_cache_retention_interval` to an argument and changed the default from `None` (dense) to `0` (sparse: keep only the latest replay boundary). This default is unfriendly to Mamba + EAGLE: with sparse retention, only the latest replay boundary keeps a Mamba state checkpoint, and EAGLE additionally drops the tail block from prefix-cache hits, leaving Mamba checkpoints largely unreachable — prefix caching never hits for the Mamba cache group (see #53504 for a production report of 0 hit tokens).

This PR keeps the public argument unchanged (`int | None`, default `0`) and only changes how an **unset** value is resolved: `EngineArgs.prefix_cache_retention_interval` now defaults to a private sentinel (or the deprecated `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` env var when set), so `create_engine_config` can tell an unset value apart from an explicit one and resolve it once the model and speculative-decoding configurations are known:

- Mamba model (`has_inner_state`) + EAGLE-style speculative decoding (`use_eagle()`) -> `None` (dense checkpoints, the pre-#52216 behavior)
- everything else -> `0` (unchanged from #52216)

Explicitly configured values are always respected: `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 0/N/None` and the deprecated env var all override the resolution.

Only `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` is touched on the product side; `CacheConfig`, `VllmConfig`, and the CLI surface are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: open PRs in this area (#54713, #53479, #55403) change retention/blocking *mechanics* for Mamba under EAGLE; none restore the pre-#52216 dense default for this combination.

## Test Plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_config_utils.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q -k "retention or mamba"
```

## Test Result

132 passed + 27 passed. New parametrized test `test_prefix_cache_retention_interval_default_resolution` covers: unset -> dense for Mamba+EAGLE, unset -> 0 for Mamba w/o EAGLE / EAGLE w/o Mamba / plain models, explicit `0`/`None`/`64` respected, CLI default remains the unset sentinel, and the deprecated env var path. `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files (ruff, mypy, etc.). `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py` has 11 failures on this machine, all from GPU OOM / HF 403s (real-model GPU tests), unrelated to this change.

---

title: [Frontend][RL] Track HTTP weight operation outcomes and concurrency
author: Ronald1995
body:
## Purpose

Weight sync is on the critical path of every RL step, but the frontend exposes no signal for how long each weight-transfer operation takes or whether one is stuck. The generic HTTP metrics already count every weight route by status (`http_requests_total{handler,status}`), but their per-handler histogram tops out at 1 s, and nothing is recorded until a request completes, so a hung NCCL transfer is invisible.

This PR adds two metrics, with the same names, labels and buckets in the Python and Rust frontends:

| Metric | Type | Labels |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vllm:rl_weight_update_operation_duration_seconds` | Histogram, buckets 0.01–600 s | `operation` |
| `vllm:rl_weight_update_operations_in_flight` | Gauge (`livesum` in multiprocess mode) | `operation` |

| Endpoint | `operation` |
| --- | --- |
| `/init_weight_transfer_engine` | `init` |
| `/start_weight_update` | `start` |
| `/start_draft_weight_update` | `start_draft` |
| `/update_weights` | `update` (one per chunk when packed) |
| `/finish_weight_update` | `finish` (includes the optional version update) |

- Each route wraps only its engine call, so requests rejected by validation are not recorded.
- The in-flight gauge is released and the duration observed on success, error and cancellation. Python uses a context manager; Rust uses a guard dropped at the end of the handler.
- Python collectors are created lazily on the default registry, after multiprocess Prometheus setup.
- No request counter is added: `http_requests_total` already covers counts and status. This matches the sleep-mode metrics in #52864.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_rl_weight_operation_metrics.py
pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/test_weight_operation_metrics.py  # 1 GPU
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-metrics weight_operation
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-server --lib weight_transfer
```

- E2E (1 GPU): a real `vllm serve --api-server-count 2` with the IPC weight-transfer backend. An HF trainer runs eight full syncs over HTTP. `/metrics` must report the exact summed duration counts per operation and zero in-flight, and the multiprocess files must show both API servers recorded, so the counts are cross-process sums.
- Multiprocess (CPU): two real processes each hold an operation open; the registry that `/metrics` serves (`get_prometheus_registry()`) reports in-flight 2, then 0 and two duration samples after both finish. Fails if `livesum` is dropped.
- Cancellation (CPU): cancelling a route task while the engine call is pending releases in-flight and still observes the duration. Fails if the recorder only handles `Exception`.
- Also (CPU): recorder success/exception paths, each of the five routes, rejected input records nothing, lazy registration on the default registry.
- Rust: the recorder guard tracks in-flight and duration; the HTTP lifecycle test checks `update`/`finish` duration counts and in-flight; invalid payloads record no duration.

## Test Result

- Python unit: 11 passed. E2E: 1 passed on GB200.
- Rust: `vllm-metrics` 1 passed, `vllm-server` weight_transfer routes 3 passed.
- pre-commit (ruff, mypy, rustfmt, typos, test tethering) clean.
- No model output path changes, so no accuracy eval.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bench] Save server queue time and TTFT in detailed results
author: lzzzzzc
body:
## Purpose
PR #46768 added server-side per-request timing metrics to OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Completions responses. However, `vllm bench serve` discarded these metrics and only retained client-observed timing data.

This PR preserves two server-side metrics in detailed benchmark results:

- `server_queue_times`: time spent waiting in the server scheduler queue.
- `server_ttfts`: time from scheduling to first-token generation.

Both values are converted from milliseconds to seconds to match the existing per-request benchmark arrays. Missing values are represented as `null` while preserving request-index alignment. Both arrays are omitted if neither metric is available for any request, or if --save-detailed is not enabled.

The implementation supports both the Python benchmark client and the Rust benchmark client used with `VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1`. Documentation is updated to distinguish these values from the client-side `queue_times` and `ttfts`.

This PR focuses on server-side queue time and TTFT to help **distinguish scheduler waiting time from time to first-token generation**. I’m happy to include the remaining per-request metrics if maintainers prefer a broader scope.

There is no associated issue. This is a follow-up integration to #46768.

I searched open PRs for `server_queue_times`, `server_ttfts`, and the combination of `enable-per-request-metrics` with `save-detailed`, and found no existing PR implementing this behavior.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used during implementation. I reviewed every changed line and can explain and maintain the change.

## Test Plan

- Verify that both Python Chat Completions and Completions clients extract metrics from the final streaming usage chunk.
- Verify millisecond-to-second conversion, zero-valued metrics, unavailable values, and per-request array alignment.
- Verify equivalent result serialization in the Rust benchmark client.
- Run the targeted Python and Rust tests.
- Run a Python end-to-end smoke test against a live `/v1/completions` endpoint
  and inspect the saved detailed JSON.


## Test Result

### Python targeted tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v
```

Result: **27 passed, 14 warnings**. This includes the existing timing tests and the migrated server metrics tests.

### Rust targeted tests

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked -p vllm-bench server_metrics
```

Result: **5 passed, 0 failed**.

### Lint checks

Pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Python E2E smoke test

Behavior change:

- Before: detailed benchmark results did not contain server-side queue time
  or TTFT.
- After: detailed results include `server_queue_times` and `server_ttfts`
  when these metrics are available.

The smoke test was run on the modified version using
`gemma-4-E2B-it`, with `--enable-per-request-metrics`
enabled on the server:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --model /path/to/gemma-4-E2B-it \
  --dataset-name custom \
  --dataset-path toolagent_3k.jsonl \
  --num-prompts 3 \
  --disable-shuffle \
  --custom-output-len=-1 \
  --request-rate 0.6 \
  --save-result \
  --save-detailed \
  --result-dir results \
  --result-filename gemma4_server_metrics_smoke_3.json
```

Results:

- 3 successful requests, 0 failures.
- Both server timing arrays were present in the saved detailed JSON.
- Each array contained 3 non-null, non-negative values and matched the
  length of the existing per-request arrays.

Saved values, in seconds (rounded for readability):

```json
{
  "ttfts": [0.820385, 0.774362, 4.330024],
  "server_queue_times": [0.000060141, 0.000023473, 0.000028463],
  "server_ttfts": [0.709359, 0.729975, 4.277035]
}
```

This E2E run covers the Python client and `/v1/completions` endpoint.
Chat Completions and Rust behavior are covered by the targeted tests above.

title: [Perf] Use UVA-backed contents for MRV2 apply_write
author: bjf-frz
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
  PLEASE FILL IN THE PR DESCRIPTION HERE ENSURING ALL CHECKLIST ITEMS (AT THE BOTTOM) HAVE BEEN CONSIDERED.

  ## Purpose

  In MRV2, `StagedWriteTensor.apply_write()` unconditionally copies staged contents to GPU memory via H2D before the Triton kernel writes them to the target, even when the target is UVA-backed.

  This change selects the contents staging location based on the target: GPU-backed targets retain the existing H2D path, while UVA-backed targets use pinned UVA buffers directly. This avoids the temporary GPU contents buffer and explicit H2D copy for UVA-backed targets.

The implementation reuses the existing UvaBufferPool, treating size as the initial capacity. Each slot grows along dimension 0 when needed, preserving trailing dimensions, and is reused when its capacity is sufficient. Growth fills the new buffer with the current contents without copying previous contents. Existing zero initialization, round-robin slot selection, and caller-managed GPU reader lifetime requirements remain unchanged.

  ## Test Plan

• - Hardware: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, single GPU; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0; PyTorch CPU threads: 1.

  - vLLM base commit: 392db567b260cb4d1e5f91547b65d527038fe641.
    - Candidate: 60ab6783a8.
    - All variants share precompiled extensions from 86484465153f08f4523d8be964fd6309146eab09.

  - Measurement boundary: Device synchronization before and after apply_write(); exclude the initial synchronization, stage_write(), and initial pool construction. In model runs, measure only all_token_ids.apply_write() after warmup.

  - Comparison: Original H2D staging versus growable, reusable UVA contents. GSM8K additionally tests an experimental per-call UVA allocation variant, not included in this PR.

  - Cases:
    - Correctness: GPU/UVA targets, multiple dtypes and input types, 1D/2D pool inputs, growth/reuse, in-flight readers, and copy_to_gpu() compatibility.
    - Generation: Compare token IDs on four requests using Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4.
    - Microbenchmark: int32 contents, 1/16/64 write segments; reuse and first-use growth from 64 to 262,144 elements; boundary growth at 1,024→1,025, 16,384→16,385, and
    262,144→262,145. 100 samples per variant per case, three runs, alternating A/B order.
    - GSM8K: Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, TP=1, MRV2; 1,319 warmup requests followed by 1,319 test requests. Max model length/batched tokens: 8,192; max sequences: 64; GPU memory
    utilization: 0.35; prefix caching disabled; seed: 42. Three runs per variant with rotated order; verify equal staged write segments and elements.

  ## Test Result

  Scenario definitions:

  - Steady-state reuse: Fill an existing buffer with sufficient capacity; no allocation.
  - First-use growth: Grow a slot from its initial one-element capacity to fit the contents. Initial pool construction is outside the timer; this is not a cold-start measurement.
  - Growth: Exceed an existing slot's capacity, e.g. 1,024→1,025 allocates capacity 2,048. Fill current contents without copying old contents.
  - GSM8K: Measure all_token_ids.apply_write() during model execution, including growth calls.

  Element counts describe flattened contents, not target capacity. Microbenchmark rows use 16 write segments and one CPU thread. Each reported statistic is the median of three per-run statistics.

  | Test | Scenario / contents elements | H2D | UVA contents | Speedup | Time reduction |
  |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Microbenchmark | Steady-state reuse / 64 | 34.35 μs | 27.37 μs | 1.26× | 20.3% |
  | Microbenchmark | Steady-state reuse / 1,024 | 66.64 μs | 41.27 μs | 1.61× | 38.1% |

  | Microbenchmark | Steady-state reuse / 262,144 | 8.727 ms | 4.450 ms | 1.96× | 49.0% |
  | Microbenchmark | First-use growth / 64 | 34.16 μs | 34.81 μs | 0.98× | -1.9% |
  | Microbenchmark | First-use growth / 1,024 | 66.03 μs | 48.74 μs | 1.35× | 26.2% |
  | Microbenchmark | First-use growth / 16,384 | 582.47 μs | 311.08 μs | 1.87× | 46.6% |
  | Microbenchmark | First-use growth / 262,144 | 8.833 ms | 4.472 ms | 1.98× | 49.4% |
  | Microbenchmark | Growth / 1,024→1,025 | 66.37 μs | 49.33 μs | 1.35× | 25.7% |

title: [Perf][Attention][MiniMax-M3] Select CUTLASS MSA by EAGLE3 decode shape
author: anish-shanbhag
body:
## Overview

Select the MiniMax-M3 CUTLASS MSA decode path using measured SM103 EAGLE3
crossover points instead of a fixed batch-16 gate. The current patch is
model-local and keeps the original floor for unmeasured shapes and
architectures.

No other open PR changes this decode dispatch gate; #60684 changes prefill
query quantization and does not overlap this work.

## Claims in the current patch

- On SM103 with decode query lengths 1–8 and measured rank-local 64/4, 32/2,
  or 16/1 query/KV heads, use CUTLASS once
  `batch_size * decode_query_len * num_q_heads >= 1024`.
- Keep the existing batch-16 floor for query lengths 9–32, SM100, and unknown
  head geometries.
- Preserve all existing kernel constraints: explicit CUTLASS selection, FP8
  E4M3 KV cache, supported head geometry, page size 128, top-k 16, supported
  query length, and the planner row bound.
- Allow deployments to override the automatic crossover with the model-local
  `VLLM_MINIMAX_M3_MSA_CUTLASS_MIN_BATCH`; unset uses the automatic policy,
  and setting the integer to 16 restores the original floor.

## Validation

Full `pr-checklist` audit: [read the condensed report](https://gist.github.com/anish-shanbhag/e87258c8b3d501ac34195d91335ff1cb).

### Current PR refresh (2026-10-08)

- Added the review update as a fast-forward commit; no existing commits were
  rewritten.
- Removed the global `envs.py` registration and `tests/test_envs.py` changes.
  The final PR changes only the MiniMax MSA implementation and its existing
  kernel test.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/sparse_attention_msa.py`:
  passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, and
  forbidden-import checks.
- CPU-safe direct checks: seven dispatch cases and two model-local override
  cases passed. `git diff --check` also passed.
- The local host does not have the PyTorch/CUDA test runtime, so the existing
  GB300 correctness and benchmark results below remain the GPU validation.

### Original query-length-4 GB300 evidence

The isolated benchmark used one NVIDIA GB300, EAGLE3 query length 4, FP8 E4M3
KV cache, 16 selected pages per token/KV head, CUDA graph replay, 30 warmups,
300 iterations, and five trials. It covered request batches 1/2/4/8/16, 8K
and 200K cached contexts, TP1/TP2/TP4, and concurrent DEP2/DEP4 ranks.

| Local heads | Batch 4 | Batch 8 | Batch 16 | First measured win | Query-head rows at win |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64/4 | 1.069x | 1.545x | 1.875x | 4 | 1,024 |
| 32/2 | 0.800x | 1.100x | 1.642x | 8 | 1,024 |
| 16/1 | 0.600x | 0.800x | 1.099x | 16 | 1,024 |

These conservative ratios charge CUTLASS for standalone BF16-to-FP8 query
quantization. All 130 rank-level CUTLASS-versus-Triton comparisons passed at
`atol=0.02`, `rtol=0.02`; maximum absolute error was `0.00006104`. The
focused GB300 kernel suite reported `41 passed` in 237.40 seconds, and the
focused environment suite reported `9 passed`.

### Query-length 1–8 follow-up (2026-10-08)

A second GB300 microbenchmark swept decode query lengths 1–8, TP1/TP2/TP4,
request batches 1/2/3/4/6/8/12/16/24/32/48/64, and cached contexts 8,192 and
200,064. It used interleaved CUDA-graph replay with the same 30 warmups, 300
iterations, and five trials. Query lengths 1/2/4/8 fit the rule; 3/5/6/7 were
held out. All 1,344 rank-level comparisons passed correctness at
`atol=rtol=0.02`; maximum absolute error was `0.00430298`.

The safe direct-kernel crossover is the first measured batch for which every
larger measured batch wins at both context lengths:

| Decode query length | TP1 / 64 Q heads | TP2 / 32 Q heads | TP4 / 16 Q heads |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 12 | 24 | 48 |
| 2 | 6 | 12 | 24 |
| 3 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| 4 | 3 | 6 | 12 |
| 5 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
| 6 | 2 | 4 | 6 |
| 7 | 2 | 3 | 6 |
| 8 | 2 | 3 | 6 |

The follow-up image (vLLM 0.25.0) first won at 768 query-head rows for query
length 4. The newer vLLM 0.28.1rc1 benchmark used only power-of-two batches,
so its first measured win at 1,024 rows did not test 768. At the shared 512-
and 1,024-row points, the two datasets agree to rounding (approximately
0.889x/0.800x and 1.222x/1.099x for direct/conservative speedup). This is not
evidence of a version shift, but the matching-version evidence does not resolve
the intermediate boundary. The merge-safe rule is therefore the conservative,
directly measured newer-image boundary:

```python
query_head_rows = batch_size * decode_query_len * num_q_heads
if 1 <= decode_query_len <= 8 and measured_head_geometry:
    automatic_min_batch = ceil_div(1024, decode_query_len * num_q_heads)
else:
    automatic_min_batch = 16
use_cutlass = batch_size >= automatic_min_batch
```

The 1,024-row rule produced zero false-positive CUTLASS regressions across all
576 new aggregated cases. It left 61 direct-kernel wins unselected on the
older image, an intentional conservative trade-off. This supports replacing
the `decode_query_len == 4` special case and three head-geometry entries with a
single query-head-row threshold, while retaining every existing capability,
dtype, head, page-size, top-k, maximum-query-length, and maximum-row guard.
Query lengths 9–32 retain the existing batch-16 floor rather than extrapolating
beyond the measured sweep. Unknown head geometries also retain 16.

The selected region has clear margin: among all 318 selected cases, the minimum
direct-kernel speedup was 1.221x and the minimum quantization-inclusive speedup
was 1.098x. The 24 cases at exactly 1,024 rows measured 1.221–1.223x direct and
1.098–1.101x with standalone quantization. Median per-case trial CV at the
boundary was 0.020% for Triton and 0.019% for the conservative CUTLASS path;
the maximum CVs were 0.199% and 0.063%, respectively.

The current commit implements the conservative 1,024 query-head-row rule for
query lengths 1–8. The 768-row rule remains a later candidate, but it should be
adopted only after measuring that intermediate point on the same vLLM build
used by the PR.

Complete tables, all trial JSON/CSV artifacts, methodology, and runnable
benchmark/analysis scripts are in the [benchmark Gist](https://gist.github.com/anish-shanbhag/3ce54e7314995b38b22612ab0100b260).

Matched MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 disaggregated EAGLE3 runs of the original fixed-16
policy versus an earlier blanket batch-4 experiment showed approximately
+3–5% p90 per-user output-token rate and +1–2.5% total TPS/GPU. That experiment
supports the opportunity but does not isolate the final dispatch policy; the
microbenchmarks above provide the shape-specific evidence.

## Details

### Root cause and implementation

The existing metadata builder used a fixed `batch_size >= 16` dispatch gate,
so common EAGLE3 verification steps fell back to Triton even when CUTLASS was
faster. A blanket lower floor is unsafe because tensor parallelism changes
rank-local query/KV head geometry and therefore the crossover. The current
model-local helper selects a conservative floor from query length, device
capability, and head geometry. The metadata builder resolves the optional
environment override once at initialization and passes it to the existing
dispatch predicate.

### Design fit and trade-offs

The implementation stays within MiniMax-M3's NVIDIA sparse-attention path and
does not change shared scheduler, model-runner, or KV-cache interfaces. The
automatic speedup is deliberately limited to the measured SM103 EAGLE3
query-length and head-geometry region; all other shapes keep the prior
batch-16 behavior.

## Checklist

- [x] Change is model-local and does not add complexity to shared core components.
- [x] Dispatch boundaries have targeted regression coverage; the integer
  override remains a model-local rollback.
- [x] Existing CUDA correctness and benchmark evidence exercises the changed path.
- [x] Query lengths 1–8 now have a genuine CUTLASS-versus-Triton microbenchmark.
- [x] Current lint, typing, test-tethering, and CPU-safe checks pass after rebasing.
- [x] Performance scope, fallback behavior, version calibration, and end-to-end limitations are explicit.
- [x] Commits are signed off and include AI-assistance attribution.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change, benchmark support, rebase, and PR refresh used OpenAI Codex. The
human submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line,
reproducing GPU validation as needed, and defending the implementation and
evidence end to end.

title: [Nixl] Separate transport-failure metrics from KV expiry
author: NickLucche
body:
Splits NIXL connector failure reporting into two signals: a grouped **transport-failure counter** for sporadic lower-transport-layer events (or link issues), and a separate KV-expiry counter carrying the autoscaler signal.

## Motivation

Every NIXL connector failure currently funnels into a single `num_failed_transfers` counter, and several failure paths are not counted at all. That conflates two signals that mean very different things operationally:

- **Transport failures** — a UCX transfer that failed mid-flight, a handshake that did not complete, a `send_notif` that could not be posted. These are sporadic events rooted in the lower transport layer; when they spike, the thing to investigate is the network, not the deployment.
- **KV expiry** — the prefiller's lease on a request's KV blocks ran out before the decoder read them. This is not a transport problem; it is actionable input for the autoscaler and for lease tuning (`kv_lease_duration` too short, or scale-down too aggressive).

The old behavior was at its worst on the pull worker's turn-2 path: a request whose KV had simply expired was recorded as a *failed transfer*, polluting the transport counter with autoscaler signal.

## What changes

| Signal | Covers |
|---|---|
| `vllm:nixl_num_failed_transfers` / CLI `Num failed transfers` | transfers + handshakes + failed `send_notif` — the sporadic transport class |
| `vllm:nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs` / CLI `Num KV expired reqs` | KV expiry only — the autoscaler signal |

- KV expiry is no longer counted as a transfer failure. The turn-2 expiry path records `num_kv_expired_reqs` and reports it separately.
- Handshake failures are now counted. Two paths previously logged without recording anything: the `handshake_setup_failed` callback and the push-side `push_handshake_failed` handler.
- Failed notifications are folded into the transport counter: a `send_notif` failure has the same sporadic lower-transport-layer causes as a failed transfer. The separate `vllm:nixl_num_failed_notifications` counter and CLI field are removed.
- Closed two previously uncounted failure paths found while tracing notifications:
  - pull-side MLA multi-rank `send_notif` calls were unguarded, so a failure propagated as an unhandled exception. They now log `notification_failed` and record the metric.
  - push-side PUSH_REG `send_notif` failures were logged but neither counted nor reflected in request state. They now record the failure and mark the request failed, matching the adjacent no-agents path.
- `reduce()` reports failure counts in both branches, so failures now also surface in the periodic `KV Transfer metrics` log line, not only via Prometheus.
- Docs: the metrics reference in `nixl_connector_usage.md` is updated with the two-signal grouping and its rationale.

Raw per-category keys (`num_failed_transfers`, `num_failed_handshakes`, `num_failed_notifications`) are still recorded internally, so re-splitting the reporting later is a small change.

## Testing

New coverage: stats grouping (`test_kv_connector_stats_failure_grouping`), Prometheus grouping (`test_nixl_prom_metrics_group_handshake_with_transfer_failures`), handshake-failure metrics in both push and pull suites, and turn-2 gate tests asserting KV expiry records no transport failure.

```
pre-commit run --files <changed files>          # ruff, mypy-3.10, markdownlint all pass
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k "stats or prom or handshake"    # 8 passed
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py                              # 43 passed
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -k stats                         # 14 passed
python -m pytest "tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py::test_turn2_deadline_gate" \
       "tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py::test_turn2_full_prefix_hit_with_expired_deadline_skips_gate" \
                                                                                                     # 5 passed
```

The dist_init-heavy suites abort locally after several tests per process (torch.distributed teardown, reproduces on a clean checkout), hence the targeted runs above.

title: [Bugfix] Fix FlashInfer KV sharing with omitted K/V
author: lzzzzzc
body:
This is a narrow forward fix for the FlashInfer regression covered by #55789,
preserving #54917 instead of reverting it.



## Purpose

[#54917](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54917) avoids computing K/V projections for Gemma4 KV-sharing layers and invokes attention with `key=None` and `value=None`. FlashInfer still sliced these tensors unconditionally while removing CUDA Graph padding, causing startup to fail with:
```text
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```
This PR fixes the FlashInfer handling of omitted K/V tensors while keeping the common non-DCP path free of additional Python branches and tensor slices.K/V are sliced only at the DCP prefill call site, where they are actually consumed. KV-sharing DCP prefill remains unsupported and is rejected with a clear error.

This PR also removes the uninitialized placeholder K/V tensors from `gemma4_mtp`. Gemma4 MTP KV-sharing layers now pass `None` for K/V, matching the target model and the existing attention-layer contract. This avoids an allocation on every draft-layer forward and prevents DCP prefill from silently consuming uninitialized placeholder tensors.

The shared abstract attention interface remains unchanged.

## Test Plan
- Verify Gemma4 E2B mixed FlashAttention 2 / FlashInfer startup, CUDA Graph
  capture, and generation.
- Run Gemma4 E2B GSM8K correctness evaluation without MTP.
- Run Gemma4 E2B GSM8K correctness evaluation with the Gemma4 MTP assistant.
- Run formatting and static type checks on the changed files.

## Test Result

### Gemma4 mixed-backend regression
Tested google/gemma-4-E2B-it on an RTX 3090 with the following backend
selection:
- Sliding-window attention: FlashAttention 2
- Full attention: FlashInfer

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/vllm serve <local-gemma-4-E2B-it-path> \
  --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \
  --attention-config \
  '{"backend":"FLASHINFER","backend_per_kind":{"sliding_window":"FLASH_ATTN"},"flash_attn_version":2}'
```

Observed:
- Both FlashAttention 2 and FlashInfer were selected.
- PIECEWISE and FULL CUDA Graph capture completed successfully.
- The API server reached Application startup complete.
- A greedy Chat Completions request completed successfully and returned the
  expected answer (Paris).
- The previous NoneType slicing failure did not occur.

### Gemma4 model correctness

Ran GSM8K 5-shot evaluation against the Gemma4 E2B mixed-backend
server:

- `flexible-extract exact_match`: `0.6535 ± 0.0131`
- `strict-match exact_match`: `0.4898 ± 0.0138`
- Reference strict-match accuracy: `0.485`
- Minimum accepted with existing tolerance: `0.435`

The evaluation passed without an observable accuracy regression.

### Gemma4 MTP mixed-backend evaluation

Configuration:

- Target: `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`
- Assistant: `google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant`
- Sliding-window attention: FlashAttention 2
- Full attention: FlashInfer
- Speculative tokens: 1

```bash
# server 
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 vllm serve /path/to/models/gemma-4-E2B-it \
  --port 8192 \
  --served-model-name google/gemma-4-E2B-it \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --language-model-only \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","model":"/home/lzc/models/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER","backend_per_kind":{"sliding_window":"FLASH_ATTN"},"flash_attn_version":2}'

# client

LMEVAL_LOG_LEVEL=INFO \
python -m lm_eval run \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=google/gemma-4-E2B-it,base_url=http://localhost:8192/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenizer=/path/to/models/gemma-4-E2B-it,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,trust_remote_code=True" \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --apply_chat_template
```

|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.6550|±  |0.0131|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.4829|±  |0.0138|

The strict-match result is consistent with the existing 0.485 reference.

## Duplicate-work check

This PR addresses the same regression as #55871, which proposed passing placeholder K/V tensors from Gemma4 and was closed without merging. This PR instead allows FlashInfer to accept omitted K/V tensors and read from the shared KV cache directly. #55789, the fallback revert, was also closed without merging.

every changed line and can explain and maintain the change.
