title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][MoE] Avoid uninitialized EPLB state in DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark drafter
author: luoyuctl
body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark startup when EPLB is enabled for the target model.

The target and DSpark draft use different routed-expert topologies (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash target: 384 routed experts; DSpark drafter: 128). When target-model EPLB is enabled, the draft routers inherit `enable_eplb=True`, but the drafter is not registered with a compatible EPLB model state. Its router-level `EplbLayerState` therefore never receives `expert_load_view` / logical-to-physical mappings and profiling fails with:

```text
ValueError: EPLB requires expert_load_view != None
```

## Fix

- Keep EPLB enabled for the target model.
- Apply the override in the shared `load_dspark_model()` path while constructing the draft `ParallelConfig`.
- Use shallow config `replace()` calls only; do not deep-copy the full `VllmConfig` after target-model construction.
- Disable draft EPLB, redundant experts, and elastic EP atomically in the same `ParallelConfig` replacement.
- Preserve the target config and shared runtime/compilation state.
- Add a focused regression test for atomic target/draft parallel-config isolation.

This intentionally disables EPLB for DSpark draft models while leaving target EPLB unchanged. Full heterogeneous target/draft EPLB support belongs in the EPLB multi-model machinery and should be handled separately.

## Validation

Focused regression test:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py
# 1 passed
```

Revalidated on the original 8x NVIDIA H20 environment:

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- TP8 / EP8
- NVIDIA driver: 595.58.03
- CUDA: 13.2
- Target EPLB enabled
- DSpark speculative decoding enabled with 5 draft tokens

Observed after the patch:

```text
Using ['PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends for group 'eplb:0'
EPLB is disabled for the DSpark draft model. EPLB remains enabled for the target model.
EPLB is enabled for MoE part of model /models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
Initialized EPLB communicator: NixlEplbCommunicator.
DSpark draft model loaded: 97 params
Rearranged experts (profile) in 1.09 s.
OpenAI server is ready to accept requests
```

A real completion request succeeded with speculative decoding active:

```text
vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total 5
vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total 25
vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total 16
```

No `deepcopy`/pickling, EPLB-state, CUDA, or EngineCore errors occurred.

For transparency, the H20 runtime validation used the production DeepSeek image with this loader change backported rather than a full binary rebuild of the PR head. The focused regression test was run against the PR implementation.

Model-evaluation impact: not applicable to model numerics or output semantics; this only changes the draft parallel configuration used during DSpark model construction.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open vLLM PRs for `DSpark EPLB DeepSeek V4.1`, `expert_load_view DSpark`, and `expert_load_view EPLB speculative`; no other open PR addresses this startup failure. Issue #50576 concerns SM8x/Ampere DSpark support and is unrelated. Related precedent: #25311 added multi-model EPLB support for MoE speculative models with compatible expert topology.

## Trade-off

The DSpark draft MoE does not receive EPLB balancing with this workaround. The target model remains EPLB-enabled, preserving the primary EPLB benefit while avoiding the startup correctness failure.

## AI Assistance

OpenAI ChatGPT assisted with root-cause analysis, patch drafting, regression-test drafting, and PR text refinement. The submitter supplied the production H20 reproduction environment and failure logs, reviewed every changed line, ran the focused test, and performed the H20 validation described above. AI assistance is also recorded in the commit trailers.

title: Revert "[CI][XPU] Disable model runner V2 for XPU quantization test for some partially pre-quantized models"
author: chaojun-zhang
body:
This reverts #56179.

**The problem**

`test_online_quantization_loads_real_weights[...tinysmokeqwen3moe-W4A16...]` hangs on XPU CI. `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod.create_weights()` (pre-#54809) always registers 4 g_idx-related `nn.Parameter`s, even for checkpoints (like this one) with no actorder/g_idx data — leaving them uninitialized.

**Verified on real XPU hardware**

Re-registering just these 4 parameters reproduces the hang; removing them fixes it. On XPU, `_process_weights_xpu()` never touches g_idx at all, so these parameters stay untouched throughout loading.

**Why not on CUDA**

On CUDA (Marlin backend), `process_weights_after_loading()` reads and replaces the g_idx parameter even for non-actorder checkpoints, so it doesn't stay untouched the way it does on XPU.

**Fixing PR**

#54809 removes GPTQ actorder support and, as part of that, deletes this unconditional registration. 

**Why this revert**

#54809 already fixes this on `main`, so #56179's `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` workaround is no longer needed.

title: [Proposal][HiSparse] Simplify cache initialization and block-size resolution
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
Proposal against #53781, targeting `feat/hisparse-mla-decode-main` at e995b60e3f.

HiSparse currently carries backend block-size capabilities through `MLAAttentionSpec` so the scheduler-side layout planner can resolve cache geometry. Resolve that geometry while the worker still has the selected attention and indexer backends instead. For example, a configured 256-token block with 64-token-only kernels produces 64-token specs before layout planning.

- Remove `supported_kernel_block_sizes` from the spec and its `customize_spec` plumbing. Keep `get_kv_cache_spec` to one HiSparse helper call.
- Reuse main's existing `select_common_block_size`, removing the extra constraints helper and reverting the `MultipleOf` dataclass change. Condense its candidate selection and proof comment while preserving the preference for the manager size, then the largest compatible divisor.
- Replace the allocator's storage-pointer dictionary with a single `HiSparseHostPool`, preserving explicit CUDA registration and the existing cleanup path.
- Keep host allocation and view construction in HiSparse, passing only device tensors to the shared allocator. This removes the shared allocator's host callback and placement branching. Including the selector simplification, `worker/utils.py` against main is +36/-25.
- Move shared request-state and prefill-staging allocation into runtime initialization so cache binding only wires existing storage and block tables.

The common-size compatibility check remains. Non-HiSparse specs retain their existing block sizes.

### Relationship to other work

Checked #53781's discussion, open PRs mentioning `53781`, open HiSparse block-size PRs, and PRs targeting this base. #56008 proposes block-pool placement metadata and #56109 proposes evictable resident pages; this proposal instead addresses worker initialization and removes backend capability data from cache specs. It is intended to be merged or cherry-picked into #53781, not to replace it.

### Validation

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  -q -k 'hisparse or allocate or (select_common_block_size and not rocm)'
```

23 passed (the invocation also included `tests/v1/worker/test_kv_cache_allocation_scope.py`, whose scope tests were deselected). Separately, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_kv_cache_allocation_scope.py -q`: 4 passed. Covers common-size selection, mixed exact/multiple constraints, incompatible backends, non-HiSparse behavior, layout geometry, and connector behavior. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed on the changed files; `git diff --check` passed.

An earlier broader CPU-only run of `test_attn_utils.py` and `test_kv_cache_utils.py` had 121 passes and 11 failures: nine copy tests require CUDA-backed pinned memory and two pipeline-parallel configuration tests require visible GPUs. That run used `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''`.

GPU/model evaluation: not run. This is an initialization refactor with no intended output change, but end-to-end HiSparse validation remains pending.

title: [bug-fix] Fix KV block leak with fault tolerance enabled in P/D disaggregation
author: tiankaijin
body:
## Purpose

Extend the fault tolerance (FT) framework (#44428) to prefill/decode (P/D) disaggregated deployments. When KV transfer is enabled, a worker failure currently causes two problems:

1. **KV transfer progress loss.** When `_model_forward` raises, the exception path discards the `kv_connector_output`, so `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` / `invalid_block_ids` for in-flight transfers are lost. After `retry` recovery, the scheduler's KV transfer bookkeeping no longer matches the actual connector state, and requests can hang or leak KV blocks.

2. **Response queue residue.** In the executor's `get_response`, the first `FAILURE` response raises immediately, without dequeuing the remaining workers' responses. The stale responses left in the MQs are then consumed by the *next* RPC call, corrupting subsequent steps.

Key design:

- **Preserve KV state on failure**: a failed worker's `kv_connector_output` is extracted before the exception is shipped, carried via a new `ExceptionWithKVConnectorOutput` / `ResponseStatus.FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT` status, and deferred into the executor's `KVOutputAggregator`
- **Drain-then-raise**: `get_response` always dequeues **all** workers' responses before raising (this covers all collective RPCs, not just `execute_model`), so no residue is left in the response queues
- **Defer-and-replay**: `KVOutputAggregator.ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs` stashes salvaged outputs; they are replayed through the normal `aggregate()` loop at the next successful step, so pending transfers are correctly reported without any special-case merging logic. Salvaged `kv_cache_events` are dropped (see Details)
- **Consume, don't drop**: on recovery, `EngineCoreSentinel` drains the batch queue and consumes each future's `kv_connector_output` (worker-side connectors use get-and-clear semantics) instead of clearing the queue wholesale
- **No new control flow**: everything rides the existing response MQ, batch queue, and `KVOutputAggregator` mechanisms

### Details

1. **Async output extraction.** `get_kv_connector_output()` is added to `AsyncModelRunnerOutput` and its implementations (v1 GPU runner, v2 `AsyncOutput` / `AsyncPoolingOutput`). In `WorkerProc.enqueue_output`, when `get_output()` raises, the pending `kv_connector_output` is extracted and shipped to the executor as `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT`.

2. **Drain-then-raise in the executor.** In `get_response`, a `FAILURE` / `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT` no longer raises immediately. All workers' responses are dequeued; KV connector outputs (explicit or embedded in successful responses) are stashed via `KVOutputAggregator.ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs`, and only then is the error raised. Stale exception responses from other ranks are dropped. When FT is disabled or the executor has already failed, the original raise-immediately behavior is preserved.

3. **Defer-and-replay in the aggregator.** Salvaged outputs are stashed by `ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs` and replayed through the normal aggregation loop at the next successful `aggregate()` call, so `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` / `failed_recving` / `invalid_block_ids` and worker metadata are preserved exactly as if they had arrived late. Salvaged `kv_cache_events` are dropped at stash time: a dropped event only costs a cache miss until its blocks are stored again, while replaying them could perturb the surviving workers' event quorum (e.g. overshooting LMCache's `count == num_workers` exact-match threshold). `aggregate()` itself is unchanged.

4. **Batch queue drain on recovery.** `EngineCoreSentinel` now drains the batch queue instead of `clear()`ing it: each pending future's `kv_connector_output` is consumed and applied via `scheduler.update_from_output(SchedulerOutput.make_empty(), ModelRunnerOutput.with_kv_conn_output_only(...))` (KV transfer state only -- the rest of the model output is not applied to avoid corrupting scheduler state mid-recovery).

## Test Plan

Unit tests added in this PR:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
    tests/v1/executor/test_executor.py \
    tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_engine_core_sentinel.py -v
```

- `test_output_aggregator.py`: replay of salvaged transfer fields, completion of recv votes, and salvaged event votes never entering the quorum (LMCache exact-match and Mooncake `>=` semantics, including late-live-vote cases)
- `test_executor.py`: drain-then-raise behavior of `get_response` under `FAILURE` / `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT`
- `test_engine_core_sentinel.py`: batch queue drain surfaces `kv_connector_output` and drops failed futures

CI wiring: `.buildkite/test_areas/fault_tolerance.yaml` now runs the sentinel test in the FT pipeline, and `source_file_dependencies` covers `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/` and `vllm/v1/executor/` so aggregator/executor-only changes trigger it.

Manual verification:

**Model**: Qwen3-30B-A3B
**Configuration**: 1 prefill (kv_producer) + 1 decode (kv_consumer), MooncakeConnector, fault tolerance enabled

### Launching the cluster

Each instance runs as a separate `vllm serve` process.

**Prefill instance (producer)** -- GPU 0, port 8010:

```bash
VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
vllm serve <MODEL> \
    --port 8010 \
    --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer"}' \
    --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30 \
    --enable-fault-tolerance \
    --fault-tolerance-config '{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 500}'
```

**Decode instance (consumer)** -- GPU 1, port 8020:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \
vllm serve <MODEL> \
    --port 8020 \
    --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}' \
    --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30 \
    --enable-fault-tolerance \
    --fault-tolerance-config '{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 500}'
```

**Proxy** (routes requests between P and D instances):

```bash
python3 examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
    --prefill http://0.0.0.0:8010 8998 \
    --decode http://0.0.0.0:8020 \
    --port 8000
```

### Simulating faults

To simulate a device-side failure on the decode instance, inject a `RuntimeError` in the forward path, raising at a chosen step on the target rank:

```python
# Fault injection: raise at specific steps
if step_count in [250, 5000]:
    raise RuntimeError("FAULT INJECTION: exception in forward path")
```

### Sending inference requests

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model": "<MODEL>", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 128}'
```

### Querying FT status and issuing recovery

```bash
# Query engine status (one per instance port):
curl -s http://localhost:8010/fault_tolerance/status
curl -s http://localhost:8020/fault_tolerance/status

# Issue retry to both instances after both become unhealthy:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8010/fault_tolerance/apply \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"instruction": "retry", "params": {"timeout": 120}}'
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8020/fault_tolerance/apply \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"instruction": "retry", "params": {"timeout": 120}}'
```

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix AITER preshuffled FP8 block-scale kernel
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose

This PR fixes breakages in MLA models on ROCm.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51692 added AiterPreshuffledFp8BlockScaledMMKernel first in the ROCm block-scaled priority list, so DeepSeek-V4/V3/Kimi-K2/many MLA models select it. Four things there lead to incorrect results:
- It reads the activation scale as column-major, while pre-quantizing callers emit row-major scales. Both unfortunately have the same shape `(M, N // 32)`
- The kernel B-preshuffles the weight after loading, and models like DS V4 on ROCm shuffle `fused_wqa_wkv`, `wo_b` and `gate_up_proj` again.
- `wo_a` is a BMM layer whose weight is read by the model directly rather than through the linear kernel, so preshuffling it corrupts the output projection.
- `kv_b_proj` is read by MLA via `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` to build `W_UK` and `W_UV`, so preshuffling it leads to incorrect construction.

In particular, DS V3/R1 is fine at TP1/TP2 but gives incorrect results at TP4/TP8, and Kimi K2 is fine at TP1 but gives incorrect results at TP>2. The general rule here is whether AITER FP8 block-scaled GEMM has tuning entries for the problematic matrices and preshuffle them. The PR tested DS V3 at TP1/DP8, so did not run into the regime where output was corrupt.

DS V4 cannot start on ROCm at all because its `_wq_b_proj` hits `apply_block_scaled_mm` and raises `NotImplementedError`, on top of the other correctness issues mentioned above.

## Test Plan
Test DeepSeek V4 TP8, DeepSeek V3 TP8 gsm8k after the fixes above. The former is also tested as part of the LM Eval (Large Models) test group in AMD CI.

## Test Result
DeepSeek V4 and V3 TP8 gsm8k recover from 0 to 0.9568 and 0.9458 respectively.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.

author: 0z5a
body:
Replace the DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark context insertion call's unused query allocation and query work with a KV-only wrapper. Dispatch the existing CUDA KV math with zero query heads for packed uint8 `fp8_ds_mla`, BF16 and ordinary FP8 e4m3fn caches. Keep projection, `kv_norm`, scheduling and acceptance logic unchanged. Validate device/dtype/layout inputs and preserve padded page strides.

**Rebase validation (2026-09-14):** current head `17127220492339af2d5969003633a7ddbdaf5c45` is based on `main` at `dbf49dad11e30ec5d464be74b715a9a9e31c2c5a`. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Cap DFlash/DSpark profiling query batch
author: wangyicong52
body:
Fixes #56443.

## Root Cause
The memory-profiling dummy run can hand-build max_num_seqs requests without applying the scheduler's speculative query-token budget. For DSpark/DFlash, each request can require num_query_per_req draft query rows.
For example, with max_num_seqs=512, max_num_batched_tokens=2048, and DSpark K=5, the profiling path asks the speculator for 512 * 5 = 2560 query rows while its input buffers are sized for 2048 rows, so DSpark can read _anchor_idx past input_ids and later surface CUDA IndexKernel/device-side assert errors.

## Changes
Cap the initial dummy/profile draft-generation pass to the largest complete set of query blocks that fits the speculator input buffer, preserve the full target-context and sampler projection for memory profiling, and fail early with a clear ValueError if a real query batch exceeds the input buffer.

Other profiling dummy runs, including FlashInfer autotune, build target attention metadata and cannot use the initial skip-attention shortcut. Add a default no-op speculator hook that lets DFlash-family speculators cap the dummy request count before GPUModelRunner builds those synthetic batches. This does not affect real serving requests or other speculator implementations.

## Existing PRs

#53970 addresses the same `max_num_seqs * parallel-draft query width > max_num_batched_tokens` failure condition with a broader capacity-based fix: it raises `max_num_batched_tokens` to cover the worst-case parallel-draft batch and enlarges the DFlash input buffers. This PR instead leaves the configured target token budget unchanged and caps only synthetic profiling batches to the existing speculator capacity. It covers both the initial skip-attention memory profile and full-attention profiling dummy runs such as FlashInfer autotune, and adds a fail-fast check if a real serving batch violates the scheduler invariant already established by #51256. The approaches are alternatives for the startup crash, but differ in scope and memory/scheduling impact.

#53080 separates target and draft scheduler budgets, but it does not constrain model-runner-generated profiling batches that bypass normal scheduler admission. #53577 covers broader DSpark/PP and padded graph safety work, but it has no matching profile query-buffer cap. #55133 and #56387 address different DSpark failure modes.

## Test Plan

### Common Configuration

- Hardware: 4x NVIDIA H20
- Tensor parallel size: 4
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909`
- CUDA graph mode: `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

```bash
vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --moe-backend auto \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","draft_sample_method":"greedy","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2

FlashInfer autotune was left enabled by default.

```bash
vllm serve /data00/models/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8001 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"/data00/models/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Qwen3-8B + DFlash

FlashInfer autotune was left enabled by default.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8001 \
  --served-model-name qwen3-8b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":16}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

## Test Result

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Without this PR, startup fails during memory profiling before the API server becomes ready:

```text
/__w/pytorch/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernel.cu:111: operator(): block: [0,0,0], thread: [...] Assertion `-sizes[i] <= index && index < sizes[i] && "index out of bounds"` failed.
RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED when calling `cublasGemmEx(...)`
EngineCore failed to start.
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

With this PR, the service completed profiling, KV cache creation, CUDA graph capture, and API startup. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the logs contained none of the failure signatures above.

### Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2

Without this PR, startup fails during the initial memory profile. DFlash2 tries to process 128 requests with query width 8, requiring 1024 query rows while its input buffer contains only 512 rows. The logs show:

```text
IndexKernel.cu:111: Assertion `... index out of bounds` failed.
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
EngineCore failed to start.
```

With this PR, both the initial memory profile and the default FlashInfer autotune completed, followed by KV cache creation, target/DFlash2 CUDA graph capture, and API startup. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. A 128-concurrency run completed 128/128 requests and generated 2812 completion tokens. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the startup/request logs contained no CUDA, EngineCore, traceback, `ValueError`, or HTTP 500 failure signatures.

### Qwen3-8B + DFlash

Without this PR, the initial memory-profile phase completes, but the default FlashInfer autotune dummy run uses 64 requests with query width 17, requiring 1088 query rows while the input buffer contains only 512 rows. The workers fail with:

```text
CUDA error (.../flash_fwd_launch_template.h:199): an illegal memory access was encountered
EngineCore failed to start.
```

With this PR, the initial profile, default FlashInfer autotune, KV cache creation, target/DFlash CUDA graph capture, and API startup all completed. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. A 64-concurrency run completed 64/64 requests and generated 2048 completion tokens. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the startup/request logs contained no CUDA, EngineCore, traceback, `ValueError`, or HTTP 500 failure signatures.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Encoder prefill attention on gfx1151: split-D head dims, alignment hint, launch config
author: roberteg16
body:
## Summary

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py` is the **encoder** attention kernel — ViT towers via the mm-encoder backend, the encoder branches of `TRITON_ATTN` and `ROCM_ATTN`, and `mimo_v2_omni`'s visual attention. (The paged LLM prefill path imports a same-named `context_attention_fwd` from `prefix_prefill.py`; that is a different module and is untouched here.)

It pads the head-dim tile to `next_power_of_2(head_dim)`, which wastes most of the matmul on the non-power-of-2 head dims vision towers use, and the KV tile #58225 picks for RDNA is still wider than those shapes want. On gfx1151 this is worth **2.19x** on the head_dim=72 kernel and takes Gemma3-4B's TTFT down **21%**.

Everything is inside one `if on_gfx1151()` in `context_attention_fwd` that only overrides launch values. Every other part keeps today's behaviour exactly: the launch arguments are computed as they are now, and only reassigned inside that branch.

```python
    BLOCK_DMODEL = triton.next_power_of_2(Lk)
    BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL = 0
    HEAD_STRIDE_ALIGNED_8 = False

    if on_gfx1151() and q.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
        main = BLOCK_DMODEL // 2
        tail = max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(Lk - main))
        if Lk != BLOCK_DMODEL and main + tail < BLOCK_DMODEL:
            BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL = main, tail

        HEAD_STRIDE_ALIGNED_8 = ...   # from the real strides of Q/K/V/O

        if HEAD_STRIDE_ALIGNED_8 and (BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL) == (64, 16):
            BLOCK_N, num_warps = 16, 4
```

Exactly **one** existing line in the wrapper changes (`BLOCK_DMODEL=` in the launch). Four more change in `_fwd_kernel`, hoisting the head-axis offsets into locals so the alignment hint has something to annotate. Everything else is additive, and the new path is constexpr dead code when `BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL == 0`.

## Commits

| commit | what it does |
|---|---|
| `[ROCm] Split the head-dim block for non-power-of-2 head dims on gfx1151` | Covers the head dim as a power-of-2 main block plus a power-of-2 tail (72 → 64+16 = 80) behind a new constexpr `BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL`; a tail of 0 reproduces the single-block kernel exactly. Skipped where it would not narrow the extent — 112 would be 64+64, the same 128 lanes for 12% more time. |
| `[ROCm] Narrow the KV tile for the 64 + 16 head dims on gfx1151` | Two things, and only one is about the tile. The `tl.multiple_of` hint on the head-axis offsets keeps the D-contiguous loads vectorized at `head_dim=72`, where the head stride is 8 mod 16 and Triton will not infer the alignment; it is set from the real strides and is unconditional. The narrow tile (`BLOCK_N=16`, 4 warps) is then taken only where that hint is active. |

## Performance

Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), against `upstream/main` which already includes #58225. Each pass checks out every point in turn and tables are the median of 3 such passes; spread is ±1% or better except where noted.

**Kernel** — `context_attention_fwd`, B=1, S=3520, H=16, bf16, non-causal, ms/call:

| head_dim | upstream | `+split` | `+narrow tile & hint` | total |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.727 | 1.745 (0.99x) | 1.741 (1.00x) | 0.99x |
| 72 | 4.842 | 2.524 (**1.92x**) | 2.213 (**1.14x**) | **2.19x** |
| 80 | 3.511 ±8% | 2.938 (**1.20x**) | 2.347 (**1.25x**) | **1.50x** |
| 96 | 3.578 | 3.222 (**1.11x**) | 3.230 (1.00x) | **1.11x** |
| 128 | 3.892 | 3.898 (1.00x) | 3.902 (1.00x) | 1.00x |
| 256 | 13.746 | 13.744 (1.00x) | 13.748 (1.00x) | 1.00x |

**The hint is unconditional; the tile is what depends on it.** At every head dim whose stride is already 16-byte aligned the hint is a tautology the compiler had anyway, and it measures exactly that. Each head dim on the tile it is given, median of 4 interleaved passes, ms/call:

| head_dim | no hint | with hint | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.814 | 1.813 | 1.00x |
| 72 | 2.887 | 2.302 | **1.25x** |
| 80 | 2.322 | 2.325 | 1.00x |
| 96 | 3.204 | 3.203 | 1.00x |
| 128 | 3.871 | 3.885 | 1.00x |
| 256 | 13.556 | 13.563 | 1.00x |

Only `head_dim=72`, the one that is 8 mod 16, learns anything from it. The narrow tile is the part that needs it: with vectorized loads `BLOCK_N=16` and 4 warps are worth 1.25x at both 72 (2.895 → 2.293) and 80 (2.924 → 2.331), but without them they are a regression — at `head_dim=72` with scalar loads the narrow tile runs 2.676 ms against 2.449 for the tile #58225 picks. Hence `if HEAD_STRIDE_ALIGNED_8 and ...`: a `head_dim` of 72 in a view whose head stride is padded keeps the wider tile.

**End to end** — TTFT, single 1920x1080 image, `max_tokens=1`, prefix caching and the multimodal processor cache disabled and a different image per repetition so every call really re-runs the vision tower. Median of 5, ms:

| model | ViT head_dim | upstream | `+split` | `+narrow tile & hint` | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `gemma-3-4b-it-quantized.w4a16` (SigLIP) | 72 | 442.8 | 362.2 (**−18.2%**) | 350.8 (−3.1%) | **−20.8%** |
| `Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` | 80 | 1946.7 | 1934.4 (−0.6%) | 1907.1 (−1.4%) | **−2.0%** |

## Why these values

Against #58225's tile, median of 5 interleaved passes at S=3520:

| head_dim | split | #58225 tile | `BLOCK_N=16`, 4 warps | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | (64, 0) | 1.818 | 1.943 | 0.94x |
| 72 | (64, 16) | 2.909 | 2.309 | **1.26x** |
| 80 | (64, 16) | 2.934 | 2.341 | **1.25x** |
| 88 | (64, 32) | 3.202 | 3.350 | 0.96x |
| 96 | (64, 32) | 3.225 | 3.385 | 0.95x |
| 112 | (128, 0) | 3.672 | 8.009 | 0.46x |
| 128 | (128, 0) | 3.896 | 9.236 | 0.42x |

Hence the narrower tile is taken exactly for the 64 + 16 dims. No `waves_per_eu` override helped anywhere, so none is set, and `BLOCK_M` keeps the generic selection.

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_vit_prefill_attn.py` is added so this is reproducible; it launches `_fwd_kernel` directly so `--bm/--bn/--nw/--ns/--we` are honoured.

```
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_vit_prefill_attn.py --seq 3520 --heads 16 --head-dim 72 \
    --backend TRITON_ATTN --bm 128 --bn 16 --nw 4
```

## Testing

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_prefill_attention.py   128 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                            clean (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, SPDX)
```

The existing correctness tests only covered `head_dim` 128; they now also run 64, 72, 80 and 96, which between them exercise both tail widths the kernel can emit (72 and 80 split as 64+16, 96 as 64+32). 

## Not a duplicate

This builds on #58225, which caps `BLOCK_N` at 32 for all of RDNA3/RDNA4 and already covers head dims 96 and up on gfx1151 — which is why nothing is claimed there. What is left is the 64 + 16 dims, where the tile wants to be narrower still and the head dim needs the split in the first place.

#56232, #56253 and #56276 tune `triton_unified_attention.py` (decoder prefill/decode) — the same argument applied to the other attention kernel, no file overlap. Encoder attention reaches this kernel under both `ROCM_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`, so #56232's backend reordering does not change whether this applies.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). Every line was reviewed by the submitter, and the measurements above were run and checked by hand.

title: [httpx migration] Import httpx from huggingface_hub
author: Wauplin
body:
_(disclaimer: maintainer of huggingface_hub here :hugs: )_

Direct `httpx` imports will break when `huggingface_hub` migrates to `httpx2`. Import through `huggingface_hub.utils` instead, using the compatibility export shipped in `huggingface_hub` 1.31.0. Goal is to make vLLM compatible with both huggingface_hub 1.x and 2.x when the switch to `httpx2` happens.

Related: https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/pull/4803 and https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/issues/4802.

`huggingface_hub` is bumped to `>= 1.31.0` (the release the re-export landed in). The `logging.getLogger("httpx")` silencing in `vllm/logger.py` is extended to `httpx2`, which logs under its own name. title: [Perf][Kernel] Integrate DeepSelect TopK for the DSA sparse indexer
author: ZJY0516
body:
## What

Integrate [DeepSeek DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect) (MIT) — a high-performance TopK kernel library for DeepSeek Sparse Attention — into vLLM via CMake FetchContent, and make **every** decode top-k implementation on the DSA sparse indexer path explicitly selectable, with a measured auto heuristic on top.

- New `vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py`: the indexer's decode top-k stage. Hosts every backend entry point (DeepSelect, cooperative, persistent, per_row, FlashInfer ragged, torch reference) and `SparseIndexerTopk`, an `nn.Module` that resolves and runs one per step. `SparseAttnIndexer` just calls `SparseIndexerTopk()(...)`.
- New `KernelConfig.sparse_indexer_topk_backend` (`--sparse-indexer-topk-backend`): `auto` (default) / `deep_select` / `cooperative` / `persistent` / `per_row` / `flashinfer` / `torch`. Explicit values fail fast with the specific unmet constraint.
- Per-row `seq_lens` map directly onto DeepSelect's `end` parameter; output is written into the preallocated `topk_indices` buffer (CUDA-graph safe; the test below captures and replays every backend).


## Why not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for "DeepSelect" and "topk kernel sparse": no PR integrates DeepSelect. Related but different work: #56346 (sampled filtering inside persistent top-k), #48726 (a custom fused LiteTopk kernel), #55872 (deterministic FlashInfer top-k). This PR vendors DeepSeek's kernels unchanged and adds a shape-based dispatch, rather than modifying existing kernels.

## Performance (NVIDIA GB200, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUPTI timing, CUDA graph replay, cold L2)

Shapes from the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Lightning Indexer (`index_topk=512`; indexer "vocab" = KV context length). Scope of this PR is the sparse indexer only.

fp32 (vLLM's indexer logits), CUDA graph replay, vs the **pre-PR auto pick** for each shape (persistent for bs>64, cooperative for bs<=64), plus the other candidates:

| shape | DeepSelect | persistent (pre-PR default, bs>64) | cooperative (pre-PR default, bs<=64) | per_row | FlashInfer ragged | torch.topk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bs=256, kv=1M | **191us** (5.6 TB/s) | 616us | n/a (>64 rows) | 613us | 595us | 2878us |
| bs=64, kv=1M | **88us** | 303us | 132us | 206us | 206us | 905us |
| bs=8, kv=1M | 85us | 180us | **40us** (auto keeps cooperative) | 89us | 95us | 194us |

bf16 (DeepSelect's native dtype; vLLM's fp32 kernels don't apply), eager microbench: bs=256, kv=1M: **119us** (4.5 TB/s) vs FlashInfer 529us vs torch.topk 1855us.

## Tests

All in `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`:

- `test_deep_select_topk` / `test_deep_select_topk_preallocated_output` — wrapper correctness (fp32/bf16, variable per-row `end`, -1 fill, NaN-filled dirty tail proving the kernel never reads past `end`, preallocated strided output buffer).
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_topk_explicit_backends` — every explicit backend x next_n {1,4}: per-row length restriction, -1 fill, set/value equality vs torch.topk.
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_topk_short_seq_lens` — seq_len < next_n with spec decode: derived row ends clamp at 0 (matching the reference kernels' `max(0, ...)`); negative ends would be OOB for the ragged kernels.
- `test_sparse_indexer_topk_backend_resolution` — pins the auto chain (unchanged from main) and the fail-fast errors of every explicit backend.

Full file: 42/42 topk-related cases pass on GB200; `pre-commit run` on all touched files passes.

## Model eval

  - GSM8K flexible：0.9333
  - strict match：0.9325

## Notes / open questions

- Blackwell-only for now: DeepSelect upstream compiles sm_100a/sm_103a only.
- DeepSelect's sampling top-k (fp32, vocab 129280) also beats torch/FlashInfer at large batch — left for a follow-up, this PR is sparse-indexer only.
- AI assistance: this PR was implemented with AI assistance (Kimi Code); I have reviewed the changes and run the tests above.

title: [Kernel][Perf][Quantization] Fix odd-row performance cliff in per-token-group quantization
author: ayush1399
body:
## Purpose

Avoid the odd-row performance cliff in per-token-group 8-bit quantization while preserving the existing launch policy for even row counts.

We identified this while investigating unexpectedly poor TPOT (time per output token) with Gemma 4 31B FP8 at TP8 on H100. The reproduction traced about 35 ms of extra time in a 13,359-token prefill forward pass to activation quantization, enough to erase the roughly 30 ms saved by FP8 GEMMs. At TP8, the down-projection input has width 2688: odd row counts launch 16-thread blocks and make quantization roughly 4× slower than the neighboring even case. The width-5376 inputs also take a roughly 2× slower path.

The current heuristic selects one group per block when the total group count is odd, launching only 16 threads. This change selects block geometry using the next even row count, then uses ceil-div and bounds checks for the actual groups. No tensors are padded or copied. All threads still participate in block and PDL synchronization, and the bounds check is compiled out for full blocks.

Quantization arithmetic and scale layouts are unchanged. The helper serves both FP8 and INT8, so both receive regression coverage. The separate packed kernel is unchanged.

### Related work

[#55330](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55330) takes a different approach: a register-resident kernel with fixed 256-thread launches for eligible inputs. This change retains the shared-memory kernel and its existing even-row policy, including support for FP32 inputs and group size 64. The approaches may be complementary, with this policy improving the shared-memory fallback.

## Performance

The H100 measurements below confirm the kernel improvement at the Gemma TP8 down-projection shape. End-to-end TP8 TPOT has not yet been remeasured with this patch.

Kernel latency in microseconds, measured with CUPTI and CUDA graphs. BF16 input, FP8 output, group size 128, column-major FP32 scales with UE8M0 rounding. Results are medians of three rounds of 30 samples; cold runs flush L2 outside the timed kernel.

| GPU | M × K | Hot before → after | Cold before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | 32767 × 128 | 41.76 → 10.45 | 41.86 → 12.48 |
| H100 | 32768 × 128 | 10.46 → 10.43 | 12.35 → 12.35 |
| H100 | 65537 × 128 | 81.18 → 41.82 | 81.22 → 41.86 |
| H100 | 13359 × 2688 | 339.63 → 81.46 | 339.63 → 83.38 |
| GB10 | 32767 × 128 | 49.23 → 20.93 | 85.98 → 89.10 |
| GB10 | 32768 × 128 | 20.80 → 20.82 | 87.14 → 86.62 |
| GB10 | 65537 × 128 | 108.24 → 67.47 | 146.27 → 145.66 |
| GB10 | 13359 × 2688 | 517.30 → 487.12 | 541.51 → 516.96 |

**H100:** The final production-source comparison covers 18 shapes, with geometric-mean latency reductions of 39.5% hot and 38.0% cold. An earlier 259-shape policy prototype also covered the broader matrix: all 112 odd shapes were within 2.9% hot and 4.2% cold of the next-even control. That prototype always enabled the guard for odd rows; the final patch omits it when no tail exists.

**GB10:** Across 182 general shapes, the geometric-mean latency reduction is 6.7% hot and 0.2% cold. Even-row performance remains essentially unchanged. Across 91 odd/next-even pairs, geometric-mean latency differs by less than 0.4%.

Clocks were not locked on either GPU. The H100 and GB10 aggregate matrices differ, so their averages are not a direct GPU comparison. H200, B200, B300, and ROCm were not tested.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing FP8 and INT8 tests with empty inputs, odd tails, FP16/BF16/FP32 inputs, group sizes 64/128, and supported scale layouts.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_per_token_group_quant_fp8 \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_per_token_group_quant_int8

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/fp8/per_token_group_quant.cu \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py
```

## Test Result

- Isolated production-source tests: **678 passed** on both H100 and GB10.
- GB10 Compute Sanitizer memcheck and synccheck: **zero errors**.
- GB10 validation reports **678 passed** with the rebuilt extension. Its command ledger names `test_utils.py` rather than the test file above; the recorded command needs reconciliation.
- Final production-source benchmarks produced byte-identical quantized outputs and identical scales against baseline on all **18 H100 shapes** and **194 GB10 shapes**.
- Repository hooks passed.
- GB10 Gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block loaded and generated the expected response to a deterministic text prompt through the modified quantizer. This was a serving smoke test; a broader model accuracy evaluation has not been run.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Ignore pending chunks in invalid sliding windows
author: jacklin78911-collab
body:
## Purpose

A pending CPU KV write can unnecessarily defer a request even when an earlier sliding window is ready to load. For a two-chunk window, `[HIT, HIT, MISS, HIT_PENDING]` currently returns `None`: the reverse scan keeps the pending flag after the miss has already ruled out that incomplete suffix. The core scheduler therefore submits no load for the ready prefix.

Track pending writes within the current consecutive window and clear that state when a miss invalidates the window. A pending chunk inside a usable window still defers lookup, and `RETRY` retains its existing conservative behavior. No timeout, transfer ownership, or external API changes are introduced.

## Why this is not duplicate work

I checked #49829 and #53087 discussions and searched open PRs for `_sliding_window_lookup`, `HIT_PENDING gap`, and related offload/window/defer terms on 2026-09-11. #53087 addresses bounded waits, #53330 addresses P2P supply/demand coverage, and #51787 addresses cache recency. This change fixes the stale pending flag for an already-invalid sliding window. It does not claim to fix the production stalls reported in #49829 or an underlying stalled transfer.

## Test Plan

The regressions fail against the unchanged base: the scanner returns `None`, and the real core scheduler plus CPU manager submits zero loads. With the fix, both synchronous and asynchronous scheduling load the earlier prefix and resume the remaining prompt while the unrelated CPU write is still pending.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py -q --disable-warnings

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result

Tested on base `22258a26bc090bccf5473cf681bbe9bac41bd035` plus this patch. The two test files pass: **249 passed** in 81.88 seconds. Pre-commit passes, including the configured mypy check, and `git diff --check` is clean.

GPU output check: a two-layer Gemma2 with dummy weights, BF16, and native CPU KV offload on an RTX 4060 Laptop. After warming the earlier window and clearing the GPU prefix cache, the backend lookup boundary is made to report a missing chunk followed by a pending chunk. The actual CPU/GPU worker reloads 32 prefix tokens, and all 8 generated tokens match the reference run. This is a controlled output-consistency check, not a trained-model accuracy evaluation, real stalled-copy experiment, or throughput/TTFT benchmark.

Local environment: Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Transformers 5.17.0, current Python source plus precompiled extensions. This is not an exact-commit source build; standard CI with the main branch's PyTorch 2.13.0 dependency remains necessary. The optional DeepGEMM extension was unavailable due to local ABI mismatch; the exercised model uses FlashAttention 2.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, test execution, and drafting. The submitting human has reviewed the change. The test results reported above were run by Codex.

title: [Core] Extensible KV cache
author: njhill
body:
## Overview

Size the KV cache from the GPU memory actually free after CUDA graph capture and warmup, instead of from a pre-capture profiling estimate. The cache's address range is reserved up front with the driver's virtual memory API, and physical memory is mapped into it only once the final size is known. Enabled by default on CUDA and ROCm with the V2 model runner.

Productization of @zhuohan123's demonstration in #47363; replaces #50779.

### Background

The KV cache has to exist before CUDA graph capture, because captured graphs bake in its addresses. So today it is sized from a profiling run that happens before capture and warmup, and everything allocated after that has to be guessed:
- **CUDA graph memory** is either ignored or estimated with a throwaway capture pass, which costs startup time.
- **Warmup and runtime transients** that profiling doesn't exercise, such as attention workspaces, sampler and logprobs buffers, and spec-decode drafts, are covered only by slack.

That slack is the `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92` default: 8% of the device, about 15 GiB of a 192 GiB GPU, left idle to absorb estimation error. When the estimate is too optimistic, the engine runs out of memory at runtime anyway.

### Extensible KV cache

The full KV cache capacity is reserved as virtual address space, with no physical memory behind it. Only the blocks that capture and warmup actually touch are backed with physical pages. After warmup, each worker measures the memory that is really free and the transient peaks it really saw. The engine then commits the final block count in one step, by mapping more physical memory into the same reserved range.

Addresses never move, so the layer views and the already-captured CUDA graphs stay valid. The cache is sized from measurement rather than from an estimate, so the default can use the whole device, keeping a measured transient reserve plus a margin.

## Claims

- **Larger KV cache by default:** 4–10% more KV cache tokens (4.9–11.3 GiB per GPU) across eight models on GB200, most of them 7–10%. The gain comes from no longer needing the 8% slack. At an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92`, the cache comes out 1–4% *smaller* than today's. It subtracts the CUDA graph and warmup memory it actually measured, which today's path leaves the slack to absorb.
- **Faster engine startup:** no throwaway CUDA graph capture pass to estimate graph memory. Engine init time, excluding weight loading, falls 21–34% (5–34 s); end-to-end startup falls 6–18%.
- **No tuning `gpu_memory_utilization` to avoid OOMs:** the cache size follows what the model, graphs and warmup actually use. The utilization setting remains a cap for sharing a GPU.
- Works with sleep mode, CUDA graphs, spec decode, hybrid models, TP/PP/DP, and the KV connectors listed under "Compatibility". Where a configuration can't use it, it falls back to today's estimate-based sizing automatically. An explicit `--enable-extensible-kv-cache` there is an error.

## Validation

- Capacity and startup benchmarks: see "Results" below.
- Unit tests:
  - `tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py`
  - `tests/utils_/test_vmm_driver.py`
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py`
  - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py`
  - `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py`
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`
- End-to-end: greedy outputs match with the feature on and off, and before and after sleep/wake.
- NIXL P/D accuracy on GB200; on ROCm, with patched UCX and ROCr (see "Compatibility").

## Results

GB200 (189 GiB per GPU), default settings otherwise. Each start is a fresh process.
- **Variants:**
  - **off:** `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`, i.e. today's sizing with the default `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92`.
  - **on:** this PR's defaults.
- **Method:**
  - One unmeasured warm-up start per variant, to populate the torch.compile, JIT and weight page caches.
  - Then three interleaved off/on pairs; medians are reported.
  - Weights load from a warm page cache, so end-to-end times are faster than a cold start. Weight loading is identical between variants.

**KV cache capacity per GPU**

| Model | TP | off | on | Gain | Tokens | on, at 0.92 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 1 | 150.2 GiB | 161.6 GiB | +11.3 GiB | +7.5% | −0.6% |
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 | 1 | 147.3 GiB | 157.4 GiB | +10.1 GiB | +6.8% | −1.4% |
| Qwen3-32B | 1 | 103.1 GiB | 113.0 GiB | +9.9 GiB | +9.5% | −1.9% |
| gpt-oss-20b | 1 | 150.5 GiB | 161.0 GiB | +10.5 GiB | +7.0% | −0.9% |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 1 | 97.6 GiB | 106.2 GiB | +8.6 GiB | +8.8% | −2.3% |
| MiniMax-M2.7 | 4 | 109.7 GiB | 118.4 GiB | +8.7 GiB | +7.9% | −1.3% |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | 4 | 108.1 GiB | 117.1 GiB | +9.0 GiB | +8.2% | −1.5% |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 4 | 119.9 GiB | 124.9 GiB | +4.9 GiB | +4.1% | −3.7% |

- **"on, at 0.92"** is the extensible cache at an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92`, compared with off. The cache comes out slightly smaller there because it subtracts the CUDA graph and warmup memory it measured, which today's sizing leaves to the slack.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash gains least** because its CUDA graphs and workspaces need about 15 GiB per GPU after warmup. Today's sizing leaves almost all of that to the 8% slack, so the slack was mostly in use already.

**Startup time** (median of 3)

| Model | TP | Engine init, off | Engine init, on | Change | End-to-end, off | End-to-end, on | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 1 | 17.7 s | 12.5 s | −5.2 s (−29%) | 50.0 s | 40.9 s | −9.1 s (−18%) |
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 | 1 | 20.1 s | 13.7 s | −6.3 s (−32%) | 51.7 s | 44.7 s | −7.0 s (−14%) |
| Qwen3-32B | 1 | 30.7 s | 21.6 s | −9.1 s (−30%) | 80.9 s | 71.4 s | −9.5 s (−12%) |
| gpt-oss-20b | 1 | 19.2 s | 13.8 s | −5.3 s (−28%) | 47.2 s | 42.2 s | −5.0 s (−11%) |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 1 | 53.3 s | 42.4 s | −11.0 s (−21%) | 119.7 s | 109.4 s | −10.4 s (−9%) |
| MiniMax-M2.7 | 4 | 55.9 s | 38.3 s | −17.6 s (−31%) | 146.9 s | 137.4 s | −9.4 s (−6%) |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | 4 | 76.1 s | 50.1 s | −26.0 s (−34%) | 173.8 s | 144.2 s | −29.6 s (−17%) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 4 | 112.2 s | 77.9 s | −34.2 s (−30%) | 192.2 s | 174.2 s | −18.0 s (−9%) |

- **Engine init** is the logged "init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model)" time, which excludes weight loading.
- **End-to-end** runs from process start until `LLM()` returns.
- **Spread:** engine init varied by about 1–2 s within a variant, and every on start was faster than every off start.
- **Where the time goes:** most of the saving is the throwaway CUDA graph capture pass that today's sizing runs to estimate graph memory. The actual capture takes the same time in both variants.
- **TP4 runs loaded checkpoints lazily** (`safetensors_load_strategy="lazy"`). The automatic background prefetch from Lustre intermittently hung multi-rank loading, independently of this change. MiniMax-M2.7's off starts used the prefetch, so its end-to-end comparison mixes the two loading modes.

<!-- TODO: H200 -->

## Details

### Implementation

- **`ExtensibleTensor`** (`vllm/utils/extensible_tensor.py`, `vllm/utils/vmm_driver.py`):
  - A tensor over a reserved virtual address range, exposed to torch through DLPack.
  - Its segments are backed with physical memory on demand, in driver-granule chunks; newly committed blocks are zeroed.
  - Uses the CUDA (`cuMem*`) and HIP (`hipMem*`) VMM APIs through ctypes.
  - A startup probe falls back to estimate-based sizing where the driver lacks VMM support, or where a HIP runtime has the `hipMemSetAccess` defect.
- **`ExtensibleKVCache`** (`vllm/v1/worker/extensible_kv_cache.py`):
  - Plugs into `allocate_kv_cache` as an allocator hook. It reserves the capacity from the profiled budget and splits it into per-layer (or per-tensor) segments, so kernels and layer views are unchanged.
  - Before capture, only the null block is backed. Warmup commits the blocks it addresses.
- **Sizing** (`gpu_worker._measure_kv_cache_blocks`, `kv_cache_planning.finalize_extensible_kv_cache`):
  - After warmup, each worker reports how many blocks fit. That is its budget less two things:
    - the measured transient peak: the larger of the profiling peak and the warmup peak;
    - a margin of `max(1 GiB, 0.75 × transient peak)`.
  - The engine takes the minimum across workers, and across DP engines, which step in lockstep. It then shrinks the configs and issues one `extend_kv_cache` RPC.
  - Warmup gains a full-budget prefill step and a prompt-logprobs chunk, so their peaks are measured rather than estimated. For MLA models it also runs a prefill over one chunked-context workspace of cached context, which measures MLA's context up-projection for prefix cache hits.
  - With the feature on and `gpu_memory_utilization` unset, the utilization defaults to 1.0; otherwise it stays 0.92. The CUDA graph memory profiling pass is skipped.
- **Sleep mode:** sleep, and `release_kv_cache_memory()`, unmap the physical pages; wake remaps them at the same addresses.
- **Weight updates** (`reload_weights`, weight-transfer sessions): a layerwise update needs transient memory that warmup can't measure, at its peak a few times the largest layer's checkpoint-format size. Before any weight changes, the worker checks free memory against that estimate:
  - If short after a pause that cleared the KV cache (the default RL weight-update flow), it releases the cache's physical memory for the update and remaps it afterwards. Nothing is reserved in normal serving.
  - Otherwise a reload fails before loading if even the largest layer can't fit, and warns if only the estimate doesn't.
- **KV connectors:**
  - The worker-side connector is created after the final extend, so it registers the final memory.
  - Under a connector, segment boundaries are aligned to the driver granule, so RDMA registrations never span physical chunks.
- **Consistency:** every worker and every DP engine agrees on whether the feature is on and on the warmup block count, so they warm up the same steps.

### Compatibility

| Not supported | Behavior | What enabling it would need |
|---|---|---|
| Platforms other than CUDA/ROCm | Off | A `VmmDriver` per platform. XPU looks feasible: Level Zero has all the VMM primitives, but the calls need PyTorch's SYCL context (a small C++ op), and PyTorch's XPU DLPack import would need to accept the mapped pointer. |
| V1 model runner | Off | Only the V2 runner is wired up. Not planned, since V1 is deprecated. |
| `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, `num_gpu_blocks_override` | Off; error if requested | Nothing: an explicit size makes measured sizing moot. |
| HiSparse | Off | HiSparse allocates its own KV cache. It would need to allocate through the extensible allocator hook. |
| Elastic EP | Off | Scale-up launches skip warmup and reuse the profiled size. New ranks would need to adopt the running engines' committed block count. |
| `LMCacheMPConnector` | Off | It shares the cache through legacy CUDA IPC, which can't export VMM memory. Needs POSIX-fd exportable allocations, LMCache's VMM IPC wrapper (`VmmCudaIPCWrapper` / `resolve_kv_wrapper_factory`) in `wrap_kv_caches`, and handling of tensors that span segments. |
| Connectors with `custom_mem_pool` (Mooncake NVLink/BAREX) | Off | The cache must come from the connector's pool. The pool would need to supply physical allocations that can be mapped into the reserved range. |
| ROCm with NIXL, Mooncake or MoRIIO | Off | UCX and ROCr can't yet register or share HIP VMM memory. Fixed upstream in openucx/ucx#12137–#12140 and ROCm/rocm-systems#13989. Once those reach the ROCm image, drop the gate and allocate exportable (POSIX-fd) memory, which is ready in a follow-up commit. |
| HIP runtimes before TheRock 7.12 | Off (probed) | Fixed upstream by ROCm/rocm-systems#2451. Nothing needed on the vLLM side. |
| Models without a KV cache | Off | Nothing to size. |
| Weight reloads without a cache-clearing pause (e.g. `reload_weights` called directly while serving) | On; the reload needs headroom from `gpu_memory_utilization`. Without it the reload warns and may run out of memory, or fails before loading when even the largest layer can't fit | Release only the cache blocks that are free: commit in finer physical chunks, and have the scheduler set aside a range of free block ids for the reload. Chunked MoE weight processing would also shrink what a reload needs. |

---

Claude was used extensively to help with this.

title: [Model Runner V2] Support custom logits processors
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

Add support for custom logits processors to Model Runner V2, mirroring the V1 feature with V2's batch model (#47172).

- a new `LogitsProcessor` ABC under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logits_processor/` with a single `add_request()` lifecycle keyed by the persistent slot index — no BatchUpdate ledger and no removal hook (V2 slots are never moved and freed slots are never indexed, so add-side overwrite is sufficient)
- `LogitsProcRequestState`, a narrow frozen struct passed to `__init__` that exposes only the fields a processor may read (token history, device, max_num_reqs, vocab_size), so `RequestState` stays out of the interface
- `LogitsContext`, the per-step batch layout passed to `apply()` — V2 reorders and expands logits rows every step, so a row is not a request
- a V2-own loader that validates entrypoint plugins and FQCNs against the V2 interface at load time, rejecting V1-interface processors with a clear error instead of crashing mid-sampling
- adoption of the interface by the built-in sampler states (logit bias, penalties, bad words): `add_request() -> bool` is OR-ed into `needs_logits_processing`, and `apply_staged_writes()` is the optional per-step flush hook for host-staged writes
- removes "custom logits processors" from the V2-unsupported gate: they no longer force a silent fallback to the V1 runner (or a hard error when V2 is forced)
- ports V1's `validate_params` to the V2 interface as an optional classmethod, dispatched at request admission by the active model runner: V1 keeps the existing path byte for byte, V2 runs the new entry

No behavior change for the pre-existing sampling stages; their pipeline order is unchanged. Custom processors run after the built-in stages and before thinking-budget forcing and temperature.

Documents the MRV2 logits processor interface in `docs/features/custom_logitsprocs.md`.

## Duplicate work check

#47585 adapts the V1 interface via a bridge: it diffs the row→request assignment every step to synthesize V1 `BatchUpdate` events, and mirrors output tokens on CPU from the AsyncOutput D2H copy. That doesn't fit MRV2:

1. **MRV2 has no BatchUpdate.** V1 needs the added/removed/moved ledger only because its batch indices compact and move; MRV2 slots are persistent and never moved. The bridge re-derives via per-step diffs what the runner already knows — a synthetic event stream instead of real lifecycle calls.
2. **The persistent batch model differs.** MRV2 reorders logits rows every step and expands them under speculative decoding (a row is not a request). The bridge assumes V1's row==request semantics, pays a per-step CPU diff + D2H sync to reconstruct state MRV2 already keeps on-device, and cannot represent draft rows — so it inherits V1's "no custom processors under spec decode" restriction, which MRV2-native processors don't have.
3. The bridge keeps V1's runtime costs (per-step diffing, CPU token mirrors, argmax-invariance routing) instead of exploiting MRV2's strengths (stable slots, on-device token history, admission gating via `add_request()`'s return).

This PR therefore implements a V2-native interface and rejects V1-interface processors at load time with a clear error, rather than wrapping them.

## Test Plan

- New CPU-only loader tests (`tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py`): V1-interface rejection via class object / FQCN / entrypoint, non-type and unimportable FQCNs, pooling-model rejection, load order, `validate_params` admission behavior.
- New GPU integration test (`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py`): a recording custom processor driven through `Sampler` — hook order, logits modification, pipeline position (post-bias, pre-temperature).
- New regressions: custom processor's `add_request()` return gating `needs_logits_processing`; slot reuse clearing bad-words state; custom LPs absent from the V2-unsupported gate (`tests/test_config.py`); `verify()` stays runner-agnostic (`tests/test_sampling_params.py`).
- Adapted existing suites: logit bias, bad words, sampler flags, thinking budget.
- E2E on NVIDIA GB200 with Qwen/Qwen3-8B: `vllm serve` with a target-token custom processor (correctness: forced output matches the target token exactly; untouched requests unaffected), `vllm bench serve` baseline vs loaded-processor throughput, and startup rejection of a V1-interface processor.

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logit_bias.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_bad_words.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py \
    tests/test_config.py::test_v2_model_runner_supports_custom_logits_processors \
    tests/test_sampling_params.py::test_verify_leaves_logits_processors_to_admission -v
```

## Test Result

- Units: 50 passed on NVIDIA GB200.
- E2E (Qwen3-8B, MRV2): serve with the custom processor starts under the V2 runner with no fallback; forced requests emit exactly the target token, plain requests unaffected; a V1-interface processor is rejected at engine init with a clear error.

Bench on GB200 (`vllm bench serve`, random 128/128, 256 prompts, concurrency 32, warmup + median of 7 runs). The processor is loaded but no request activates it:

| Config | Output token/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Delta v. baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 7,081 | 71.5 | 3.98 | 0.0% |
| Custom LP loaded | 7,074 | 71.7 | 3.98 | -0.1% (within run-to-run noise) |

`pre-commit run` green on all changed files; mypy 3.10–3.13 green.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>
