title: [MM][V2] Enable encoder-only ViT CUDA graph capture
author: jiangkuaixue123
body:
## Purpose

Enable vision encoder CUDA graph capture for ModelRunnerV2 encoder-only instances. #49852 added encoder graph support to the ordinary V2 GPUModelRunner, but MMEncoderModelRunner overrides `capture_model` with an immediate return, so E-only instances do not capture those graphs.

Call the existing EncoderRunner capture path from the E-only runner, with GC handling, capture-memory accounting, and workspace locking. Reuse existing budget selection, replay, eager fallback, output copies, and EC transfer. The feature remains opt-in, independent of decoder graph mode, and disabled by `enforce_eager`.

Add E-only configuration/lifecycle/model tests, Mooncake graph-hit assertions, and CI configuration. **The attention-padding zero-initialization workaround, its capture context, and its dedicated padding regression test have been removed.** The production change is confined to MMEncoderModelRunner; this PR does not change attention kernels or default backend selection.

## Known FA backend issue and backend validation

The separate NaN issue is tracked in #57136. With the workaround disabled, H20 / Qwen2.5-VL-3B / BF16 / head_dim=80 / TP=1 testing of nine encoder graph budgets sharing one pool produced:

| Actual encoder backend | 1196-token image replaying budget 2048 | V-padding NaN injection into a single attention call |
|---|---|---|
| FLASH_ATTN, FA3 | All-NaN graph output; eager finite | Valid output becomes NaN in eager and graph |
| FLASH_ATTN, FA4 | All-NaN graph output; eager finite | Valid output becomes NaN in eager and graph |
| TRITON_ATTN | Finite; maximum difference from its eager reference = 0 | Valid output remains finite and matches reference |
| FLASHINFER (cuDNN) | Finite; maximum difference from its eager reference = 0 | Valid output remains finite and matches reference |

Backend/version selection was inspected on the actual attention layers; there was no silent fallback. Each backend ran three small -> large -> small sequences, with nine graph hits and zero misses. Tail-injection tests covered capacity/active lengths 256/128 and 2048/1196, using fixed atol=rtol=0.016 against unpadded FP32 SDPA. FLASHINFER used its required offset metadata and interleaved QKV layout. All backends leave some output padding unwritten, but only FA3/FA4 propagated V-tail NaNs in these tests. The complete full-model propagation chain and interface-contract responsibility remain under investigation in #57136.

**FLASHINFER and Triton did not reproduce this issue in the tested configuration; this is not a universal guarantee across models and shapes. FA3/FA4 remain affected in that configuration, and this PR does not fix or close #57136.** All E-only model test cases (Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, and Qwen3.5) select FLASHINFER. Mooncake CI selects TRITON_ATTN. Users can set `--mm-encoder-attn-backend TRITON_ATTN` or `FLASHINFER` when using encoder graphs on supported configurations; the integration script exposes `E_MM_ENCODER_ATTN_BACKEND`.

Environment: NVIDIA H20-3e, driver 580.105.08, Python 3.12, Torch 2.13.0+cu132; FLASHINFER 0.6.17, cuDNN package 9.20.0.48. Model revision: 66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3. Backend comparisons used 53a766fd7d with the workaround disabled before worker initialization; the final change removes that workaround entirely. Existing precompiled extensions were reused. Multi-GPU, V1, RDMA, LoRA, and broad model-quality benchmarks were not evaluated in this follow-up. No performance improvement is claimed.

## Test Plan

```bash
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_worker_ec_connector.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py \
  -k 'eonly and (qwen2_5_vl or qwen3_vl)' -v -s
```

## Test Result

Code validation revision 05c72d0cf9: pre-commit (including shellcheck and documentation checks) and manual mypy-3.12 passed. H20 rerun on this revision: combined attention/encoder/EC suites **132 passed, 14 skipped** (27.85s; ROCm/AITER-only skips). Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL E-only tests using TRITON_ATTN: **2 passed** (123.19s), covering images, video, budget fallback, and retained-output integrity. The backend comparisons above were completed without the workaround. The updated Mooncake CI backend configuration has not yet been run end-to-end on this revision; earlier EPD results with the workaround are not presented as validation of this final version.

The subsequent documentation-only commit 31993e3013 removes all changes to `docs/features/disagg_encoder.md`; its pre-commit checks passed. Production code and tests are unchanged from the validated revision above.

## Duplicate-work checks and human review

Open PR searches for E-only/encoder-only graphs, encoder cudagraph, and padding NaNs found no competing E-only capture implementation. #49852 is the merged infrastructure reused here. #55929 addresses input normalization; #52230 addresses V1 non-first PP ranks. The independent FA NaN issue is tracked in #57136 rather than fixed in this PR.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, testing, and review. This PR remains a draft pending the human submitter's required review and test confirmation:

- [ ] Human submitter reviewed every changed line and understands the change end-to-end.
- [ ] Human submitter ran the relevant tests.



### E-only model test backend follow-up

All three parameterized E-only model test cases now use FLASHINFER. The H20 FLASHINFER rerun described below covers Qwen2.5-VL; Qwen3-VL and Qwen3.5 await validation with this backend. Buildkite 89352 failed that case with TRITON_ATTN on H200 MIG (finite outputs, but maximum absolute difference 3.40625). On H20 at the same cc04b48770 source revision, the isolated test passed with TRITON_ATTN and with a test-only FLASHINFER override: 1 passed in 88.82s and 57.55s respectively, both with maximum absolute error 0, seven graph hits and one fallback. These durations include startup and are not a backend performance comparison. Pre-commit passed for the committed backend change; the new CI result remains pending.

title: [Perf][Engram] Serialize offloaded lookups and pack host tables into huge pages
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

Two CPU-offloaded Engram lookups ran on separate streams and interfered with main-stream decoder work. Use one model-owned stream and a completion event per layer, so the lookups take turns instead of jointly starving decoder compute of SMs, and the first consumer waits only for its own lookup.

For private CPU-offloaded tables, `thp_packing` allocates weights and scales in one anonymous mapping that requests transparent huge pages (`MADV_HUGEPAGE`), prefaults it, and registers it with CUDA. Before prefaulting, the cached pages of the local checkpoint snapshot are released (`posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)`) so the kernel can find contiguous physical memory; after weight loading refills that cache, it is released again and one `MADV_COLLAPSE` is attempted. Huge pages are best effort: any failure falls back to ordinary Torch pinned memory or keeps the existing pages with a warning, and correctness never depends on them. Small tables, DP shared storage, the lookup kernel and the SM/2 background grid are unchanged.

Why the page-cache release and the post-load collapse are kept: measured on one GB200 NUMA node (441 GiB) with 250 GiB of small-page anonymous memory resident and the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint in the page cache, allocating a 25 GiB table:

| Step | Huge-page coverage |
|---|---|
| prefault, no fadvise | 12-22% |
| fadvise before prefault | 66% |
| + post-load fadvise + `MADV_COLLAPSE` | 100% |
| post-load collapse without fadvise | `ENOMEM`, unchanged |

`EngramConfig.thp_packing` defaults to `False`; set `--engram-config '{"thp_packing": true}'` to enable it. Page allocation follows the host's THP policy; the code does not change system settings.

Duplicate-work check (2026-09-15): [#56436](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56436) controls overlap eligibility; [#56757](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56757) uses file-backed tables. Neither serializes the offloaded lookups on a single model-owned stream nor implements this registered THP allocation path.

## Test plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py \
  tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/test_config.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/config/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py
git diff --check
```

## Test result

- `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`: 86 passed, 1 skipped (GB200). New guards: packed storage and its pinned fallback give exact lookup rows; a passed-in stream is the lookup stream; consuming one layer does not wait for a later layer's lookup on the shared stream (fails with the previous stream-wide `wait_stream`).
- `tests/test_config.py -k engram`: 40 passed; `tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py`: 23 passed, 2 skipped.
- Pre-commit, `mypy-3.12`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Model evaluation

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.12 (all 1319 problems, five-shot chat, greedy, 1024 output tokens, seed 123) on 4xGB200, TP4, eager, checkpoint `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash@dba1be0a`:

| `thp_packing` | Accuracy |
| --- | --- |
| OFF | 96.51% (1273/1319) |
| ON | 96.59% (1274/1319) |

The ON run had all 8 tables fully huge-page backed (192 GiB, 100% coverage, no fallback). The two-problem delta is within run-to-run noise; THP packing changes only how table memory is backed, not its contents.

## Performance

E2E average TTFT (ms, lower is better), same serving config for all three variants. A = independent lookup streams + pinned tables; B = one serialized model-owned stream + pinned tables; C = serialized stream + THP-packed tables (this PR).

| Input / concurrency | A | B | C | C vs A | C vs B |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8K / 1 | 230.88 | 237.16 | 229.53 | -0.58% | -3.22% |
| 8K / 32 | 1642.64 | 1617.62 | 1595.97 | -2.84% | -1.34% |
| 32K / 1 | 891.66 | 887.84 | 886.45 | -0.58% | -0.16% |
| 32K / 32 | 5160.91 | 5128.07 | 5104.18 | -1.10% | -0.47% |

C is fastest in every configuration; the gain grows with concurrency at 8K input (up to -2.84% vs A, -3.22% vs B at the opposite ends of the matrix).

Kernel-level comparison of the lookup itself (SM/2 background grid, one DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 shard: 96,002,653 rows x 256 fp8 + ue8m0 scales, ~24.8 GiB host table, CUPTI timing with CUDA graphs and cold L2, mean of 20 reps with rotated measurement order, THP coverage 97.4%):

| tokens / lookup | THP (us) | 64K pinned (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2.68 | 2.69 | 1.00x |
| 32 | 3.28 | 3.35 | 1.02x |
| 512 | 8.56 | 11.24 | 1.31x |
| 2048 | 28.30 | 34.26 | 1.21x |
| 8192 | 102.32 | 264.58 | 2.59x |
| 32768 | 392.51 | 3947.99 | 10.06x |

THP is at parity for decode-sized lookups and increasingly faster beyond 512 tokens: the 64 KiB baseline collapses to ~13 GB/s at 32K tokens from GPU MMU TLB thrash (unstable across runs, 2.8-41x), while THP sustains ~134 GB/s of host read bandwidth. An ablation with mmap+cudaHostRegister but no huge pages matched cudaHostAlloc at every size, so the difference comes from the page size alone, not the allocation path.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and this draft. Human review of every changed line and independent execution of relevant tests are required before submission.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix EAGLE and dense draft startup with EP
author: kyleliang-nv
body:
## Purpose

After #55914, pairing an EP-enabled MoE target with a dense EAGLE, EAGLE3, or independent draft model fails during configuration validation:

```text
Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled.
```

Pass the final draft `ModelConfig`, after draft architecture overrides, to `create_draft_parallel_config`. Disable inherited EP only when that config reports a dense draft through `ModelConfig.is_moe`, the same classification used by the existing validator. MoE drafts, including DeepSeek V4 MTP and DSpark, continue to inherit target EP. Target EP and target/draft TP settings remain unchanged.

The new `draft_model_config` argument is optional. Existing two-argument calls, or calls that explicitly pass `None`, retain the previous EP inheritance. The normal configuration-construction path always supplies the final draft config. This preserves helper-call compatibility; it does not infer draft density or fix existing validation failures for callers that omit model information.

## Test Plan

The regression constructs real `ModelConfig` and `SpeculativeConfig` objects from small local configuration files, exercising architecture conversion and production validation without mocks or model weights. Its 24 cases cover dense independent/EAGLE/EAGLE3 drafts and MoE independent/MTP/DSpark drafts, target EP on/off, and matching target/draft TP sizes of 1 and 2.

Four additional compatibility cases cover omitted and explicit-`None` draft model configs, each with target EP on/off.

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py tests/test_config.py
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k 'draft_inherits_ep_only_for_moe or draft_parallel_config_preserves_ep_without_model' -v
```

## Test Result

Rebased without conflicts onto public `main` at `fc8132a5e523294ea69decb5e7cbf50e9d3e135e` on 2026-09-16. The three existing patches are unchanged by the rebase.

- Pre-commit: passed.
- On the rebased head `a2e2e9035de0e81252cda7164198c4d2f5230a9d`: 28 passed.
- Before replacing the required boolean argument with the optional model config, all four new compatibility cases failed with `TypeError`.
- Negative control: keeping the optional helper and EP guard but omitting the draft config at the production call site caused 6 expert-count validation failures and 22 passes. The failures were dense independent/EAGLE/EAGLE3 drafts with target EP enabled. This confirms the configuration-level tests catch a missing call-site update even when the compatibility tests pass.
- On the earlier head `e679fb51c48b62b83920a24ea733bd4b3efb6cbe`, repeated the negative control using an in-process wrapper that deliberately omits the draft model config when calling the real helper: the same 6 dense-draft/target-EP cases failed with expert-count validation errors, and 22 passed. The on-disk source was unchanged.
- Full inference and model accuracy evaluations were not run; these tests cover configuration construction and validation only.

## Related work

This PR overlaps #56933, which addresses the same regression. Following review, this PR adopts the same backward-compatible optional-model-config interface, with an explicit legacy fallback and real configuration-construction regression coverage. These are alternative fixes, not dependencies; maintainers can select or consolidate the overlapping changes. #35143 addresses a separate dense-draft DP synchronization optimization.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the regression, implement the change, and prepare tests. Test commands, results, and validation limits are documented above.

title: [Model][DSv4.1] FlashMLA mega attention and the NVFP4 compressed KV cache
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

Supersedes #56344, which closed when its base branch `dsv41-optimized` was deleted.

FlashMLA's mega-attention kernel does Q RoPE, sparse attention, the output's inverse RoPE and its FP8 cast in one launch, writing straight into the buffer `wo_a` consumes. It arrives as `FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend` (`FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`) with its own attention layer, plus the V4.1 NVFP4 compressed KV record that only this kernel can read — and, as of this revision, **it is the SM100 default** rather than an opt-in backend.

Rebased onto current `main`, which now includes #56441 (KV-only DSpark context insertion); that PR touched the same translation unit and its interaction with this one is described under *Rebase onto #56441* below.

## The interface capability the base layer acts on

`accepts_unnormed_unroped_query` — the attention kernel applies the Q norm and RoPE itself and reads Q in its own chunk-interleaved layout, so the layer's fused KV insert reduces to a zero-pad of Q to the kernel's head count, and to nothing at all once the shard is already that wide.

The output side needs no flag: the mega layer's `_alloc_attn_out` / `_o_proj` pair speaks `QuantizedActivation` where every other layer speaks bf16 and rotates in `_o_proj`. An earlier revision of this PR declared a second capability, `produces_inv_roped_quantized_output`; it had no reader — the dispatch is the override pair — so it is gone.

## Q reaches the kernel through the existing fused op, not a new one

Rather than a separate Triton pad kernel, `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert` gains two independent knobs:

- `apply_q_rope` — rotate Q as well; KV is always rotated. A runtime argument, on the `kv_mxfp8` precedent.
- `is_q_interleaved` — read and write Q in the mega layout (32 chunks of `[heads, 16]` per token), which moves the padding heads to the tail of every head-dim chunk. A template parameter, because it selects the address arithmetic.

They are orthogonal, and that is tested. A lane owns dims `[16l, 16l+16)` of its head in **either** layout — only the address differs — so the per-head RMSNorm and the GPT-J RoPE are equally valid interleaved. `test_q_interleaved_is_orthogonal_to_norm_and_rope` pins it over all eight of (16, 64 heads) × (norm on/off) × (RoPE on/off): the head-major result permuted into the interleaved layout must equal the interleaved path on a permuted input, bit for bit, with the KV cache byte-identical so the Q layout cannot leak into the KV half. An earlier revision conflated the two into one flag on the mistaken belief that the layout made RoPE ill-defined; that test fails against the conflated form.

`q_head_padded = 0` additionally asks for the KV insert alone, which is what TP1 wants — its 64 live heads are already the kernel's head count, so no Q pass is scheduled at all.

## One buffer pair per step

The output travels as a `QuantizedActivation` (`kMxfp8Dynamic`: fp8 e4m3 data, packed-ue8m0 MN-major scales). FlashMLA's fused ops take caller-provided `out_fp8` / `out_sf`, so a single buffer pair covers a whole step: the prefill chunks and the decode segment fill disjoint token ranges, and one `fp8_einsum` over all N tokens replaces one call per segment. The scale buffer's head-dim stride is `ceil4(N)` — both what the kernel requires of a caller buffer and what DeepGEMM expects for that N.

`wq_b` rows and `wo_a` columns are permuted once at load into the kernel's chunk-interleaved layouts, so the surrounding GEMMs speak them directly rather than shuffling per step. DSpark's draft layers are ordinary `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`s and therefore take the engine-wide backend, so they owe the same post-load permutation; `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading` now runs it, where before it finalized only MoE weights and every draft forward hit the layer's own guard.

## NVFP4 compressed cache

`nvfp4_ds_mla` now means the V4.1 MXFP8 sliding-window record beside a 288 B NVFP4 compressed record (256 B of e2m1 pairs, then 32 e4m3 scales of 16 dims). It rides the byte-width dispatch the fp8 records already use, so `rope_quant_insert` and `dequantize_and_gather_k_cache` pick it up with no call-site change; CuteDSL has no fp4 gather, so that record takes Triton.

This is the format the reference implementation itself stores: `inference/model.py` quantizes the compressed latent with `fp4_act_quant(latent, 16, True, scale_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)` — group 16, e4m3 scales. `fp8_ds_mla` is *more* precise than the reference on that cache, not less.

Each layer declares the packed record its kernel prefers, and an unspecific `--kv-cache-dtype` resolves to it:

| layer | `auto` / `fp8` | explicit `fp8_ds_mla` | explicit `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
|---|---|---|---|
| mega attention | `nvfp4_ds_mla` | `fp8_ds_mla` | `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` | `fp8_ds_mla` | `fp8_ds_mla` | rejected by the backend |
| plain-row (FlashInfer) | `fp8` | — | `ValueError` |

## Default backend on SM100

An unspecified `--attention_config.backend` now resolves to `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` on SM100. The layer answers `is_available_for()` rather than letting the selector guess, because `__init__` raises on topologies the kernel cannot serve — it is SM100 only, it needs `WV_GROUP_SIZE` heads per `wo_a` group, and a build may not carry the kernel at all. On a 64-head model that admits TP1 through TP8 and declines TP16 (4 local heads), which falls through to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` instead of failing at startup.

The default is chosen for TP1's win plus the 45%-smaller compressed record, **not** for a uniform speedup — see the table below, where TP2 through TP8 are a wash. Set `--attention_config.backend=FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` to get the previous path.

## Performance

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`, one GB300, CUDA graphs on, counting every per-step op each path runs (topk_swa=128, topk_extra=512, NVFP4 compressed cache), as mega / `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` microseconds on a 64-head model:

```
  s_q                    1      32     128     256     512
  TP1 (64 live heads)  29/29   31/31   31/40   53/72   96/140    up to 1.45x
  TP2 (32 live)        29/29   31/30   35/35   61/63  110/119
  TP4 (16 live)        29/29   31/29   34/34   59/58  109/109
  TP8 (8 live)         29/29   31/29   33/33   59/57  107/104
```

The decisive variable is live heads over padded heads, not batch size: the kernel absorbs the inverse RoPE and the FP8 cast, whose cost scales with *live* heads, while its own cost scales with *padded* heads — always 64, since FlashMLA's FP8 decode takes only `h_q` in {64, 128}. So TP1 wins and TP2 down cancel to within a few percent. There is no batch size at which falling back pays, so there is no minimum-token threshold and no fallback path to maintain.

An earlier revision of this table also charged the mega arm for a separate Q-pad kernel "that the split-KV path gets for free"; that is no longer true — the pad is now inside the same fused insert both paths run, and at TP1 it is skipped entirely.

These are decode numbers; **prefill is unmeasured**. Measure under CUDA graphs — in eager mode launch overhead swamps both paths and overstates the fused one several-fold.

## Accuracy: measured end to end, with DSpark

The earlier revision listed accuracy as not covered. It now is. Both arms on one GB300, TP4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` at pinned snapshot `517ef625`, identical eval config, DSpark k=5 with **real** rejection sampling (`rejection_sample_method=synthetic` deliberately absent, so acceptance measures the draft rather than echoing the config). The two recipes differ by exactly one engine flag.

| | mega attention (NVFP4) | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` (fp8_ds_mla) | history band |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k flexible / strict | **0.9318** / 0.9318 | 0.9265 / 0.9265 | median 0.9287, IQR 0.9265–0.9318 |
| gpqa_diamond exact / pass@4 | **0.9053** / 0.9545 | 0.9066 / 0.9545 | median 0.9040, IQR 0.8990–0.9141 |
| draft acceptance gpqa | 0.4376 (len 3.188) | 0.4341 (len 3.171) | |
| draft acceptance gsm8k | 0.4957 (len 3.479) | 0.4945 (len 3.473) | |

All four scores land inside their interquartile range, and the two arms agree within sampling noise (gsm8k 0.53 pt, gpqa 0.13 pt; gpqa is n=198 at temperature 1.0, so one question is ~0.5 pt). **The fused kernel and the 45%-smaller compressed record cost nothing measurable in accuracy.**

Draft acceptance is the more sensitive check, because it reads draft-versus-target agreement directly: all four figures span 0.4341–0.4376 on gpqa and 0.4945–0.4957 on gsm8k, and they also reproduce the pre-rebase run to three decimals.

Scores were validated before being quoted: `num_request_errors: 0` on every eval, step durations plausible (530/114 s and 519/113 s), gsm8k > gpqa cross-task ordering, flexible − strict gap exactly 0.0000, and truncation of 3/792 gpqa and 1/1319 gsm8k rows so that answered-only accuracy tracks the headline (mega 0.9087 / 0.9332; sparse 0.9100 / 0.9279). GSM8K runs `api_type: completions` 5-shot greedy, so it bypasses the chat template and is not the deployed serving path; GPQA runs the deployed chat path with thinking on and the `deepseek_v41` reasoning parser.

## Rebase onto #56441

#56441 added a KV-only context-insert op to the same translation unit. Two of its call sites needed updating for this series and **git reported no conflict on either**, because neither side edited those lines — they would have surfaced only at compile time: `launchFusedDeepseekV4Templated` gains a template parameter (`is_q_interleaved`) and a runtime one (`apply_q_rope`), and the KV-only op calls it. Both are fixed at the call site, with a comment noting that zero query heads means no Q slot is scheduled so neither knob is reachable there.

The two series had also independently arrived at the same `kNumHeadsQPadded == 0` grid fix (I contributed it to #56441 during review); it collapsed to one.

## Test Plan & Result

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py \
       tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
       tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py \
       tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py \
       tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py     # 522 passed, 17 skipped
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                    # all hooks pass
```

The last two suites are there because the op this PR changes is also called by the **DSv4.0** paths (`deepseek_v4/attention.py`, its dspark, xpu); the two new parameters are defaulted so those call sites still bind, which is worth testing rather than assuming.

New tests cover the NVFP4 record byte-exactly against a reference quantizer derived from FlashMLA's `tests/quant.py` (scales exact, values within half an e2m1 step, untouched rows and page padding preserved), an insert→gather round trip, the `wq_b` / `wo_a` permutations against a reference that permutes the activation instead, the interleaved Q pad (live elements bit-exact, padding heads zero, both grid variants, and the KV-insert-only launch), the norm/RoPE orthogonality described above, and graph-replay coverage that a captured insert refills its allocated Q buffer over changed input.

## Not duplicating

#56893 (merged) landed the V4.1 MXFP8 KV record this builds on. #56344 is the earlier flag-gated form of this same integration and is closed. #56441 (merged) added a KV-only wrapper op in the same files; disjoint in intent, and the interaction is described above.

## Not yet covered

- **Prefill perf is unmeasured** — every number above is decode.
- **Non-SM100 arches** are untouched by design; the kernel has no SM90 instantiation and the default declines there.
- Two commits in this series do not build standalone (a call-site fix landed one commit later than the parameter it fixes), which matters only for `git bisect` across the series, not for the tip or a squash-merge.

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Expose transfer stats via Prometheus
author: CAICAIIs
body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeConnector` collects per-transfer stats but never exports them: it does not override `KVConnectorBase_V1.build_prom_metrics`, which returns `None`, so the stats only reach the periodic `KV Transfer metrics: ...` log line. `mooncake/stats.py` carried a `TODO(mooncake-stats)` for exactly this.

This adds `MooncakePromMetrics` and wires it through `MooncakeConnector.build_prom_metrics`: histograms `vllm:mooncake_xfer_time_seconds`, `vllm:mooncake_bytes_transferred`, `vllm:mooncake_num_descriptors`, and counters `vllm:mooncake_num_failed_transfers`, `vllm:mooncake_num_failed_recvs`, `vllm:mooncake_num_kv_expired_reqs`, all with the standard `model_name`/`engine` labels. Mooncake is push-based, so the histograms are only populated on the prefiller instance.

It also fixes a latent crash: `MultiKVConnectorPromMetrics.observe` asserts that every connector id in the stats payload has registered metrics, and `MultiConnector` only registers sub-connectors whose `build_prom_metrics` returns non-`None`. With `MooncakeConnector` inside a `MultiConnector`, the first stats report therefore raised `AssertionError` in the stats logger.

`observe()` indexes the stats snapshot directly, the way the stats containers themselves read `data`, so a renamed stats key surfaces as a `KeyError` rather than silently reporting zeros.

## Changes

- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/stats.py`: add `MooncakePromMetrics` and the bucket edges it publishes; drop the TODO
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py`: add `MooncakeConnector.build_prom_metrics`
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py`: cover the wiring and the exported series
- `docs/features/mooncake_connector_usage.md`: document the new metrics

No wiring is needed elsewhere: `KVConnectorProm` resolves the class through `connector_cls.build_prom_metrics(...)`, and `MultiConnector` delegates to each sub-connector.

Sharing the plumbing that `NixlPromMetrics` duplicates is left to a separate PR, as requested in review.

## Duplicate-work check

Supersedes #50374, which attempted the same change, was blocked on pre-commit, and was no longer being worked on. Metric names, buckets and attribute layout are unchanged from it, so dashboards written against it keep working.

## Test Plan

- Run applicable pre-commit hooks on the changed files.
- Run the metrics tests, plus the neighbouring suites that exercise the same hierarchy:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_metrics.py
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -k prom
```

- Check the connector against a pristine tree at the same base commit:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py -v
```

## Test Result

- Pre-commit hooks on the changed files: passed (ruff check, ruff format, typos, markdownlint-cli2, mypy 3.10, SPDX headers, lazy imports, forbidden imports).
- `test_mooncake_stats.py`: **20 passed**; `offloading_connector/test_metrics.py`: **22 passed**; `test_multi_connector.py -k prom`: **1 passed**.
- `test_mooncake_connector.py`: **45 passed, 2 failed**. Both failures reproduce identically on a pristine tree at the same base commit, so they are artifacts of the test environment rather than regressions.
- The new tests assert exported samples through `REGISTRY.get_sample_value(...)` — series names, labels, bucket edges and values — rather than fake metric objects, and feed `observe()` a snapshot produced by the real `MooncakeKVConnectorStats` so the declared keys are pinned to the connector rather than restated in the test.

This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed line by line by the submitter.

title: [CI] Fix NIXL push worker test stub after failure deferral

title: [DSpark] Support pipeline-parallel targets in aggregated serving
author: lucifer1004
body:
## What

DSpark on a pipeline-parallel target in aggregated (non-PD) serving. The drafter runs wholly on the last PP stage; this PR makes that work correctly:

- **Draft broadcast across stages**: the last stage's speculator proposes drafts, but earlier stages need them for the next verification step. The last rank now broadcasts the fresh drafts on the PP group (`PPHandler.broadcast_drafts`), and the broadcast is gated out of the no-op second call site when a speculator ran (double-posting misaligned the recv FIFO and hung the pipeline).
- **Warmup**: the deferred PP post-update triton kernel never runs during warmup steps on non-last ranks; its first mid-serving compile would deadlock against the in-flight NCCL broadcast. `warmup_pp_decode_update` compiles it during capture, and the sampled-token broadcast is disabled for the warmup window.
- **Draft embedding under PP**: the drafter aliases the target's embedding table, which #50514 retains on the last PP stage when speculative decoding is active. (An earlier revision of this PR loaded a separate drafter copy; dropped per review.)
- **Padded graph batch safety**: the DFlash prepare-inputs kernel clears `input_ids`/`positions` and sets `is_padding` on CUDA-graph padding rows, and the DSv4 top-k router zeroes padded-row selections instead of reading uninitialized state.

## Not a duplicate

Split from #53577 (reviewer request): this PR is the aggregated-serving half; the PD prefill + KV-transfer half follows separately.

## Tests

- New/extended: `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py`.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py -q` → 1686 passed, 6 skipped.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py -q` → 34 passed.

## Model evaluation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0731) DSpark K=5, IFB PP2×TP2, GSM8K strict-match: **0.9484** (1319 samples; an earlier revision measured 0.9545 — both within noise of the target-only arm). Spec decode mean acceptance length 4.38.

Kimi-K3 DSpark IFB PP relies on the TritonMLA causal multi-token fix from #51065 (merged; included in this branch's base). Smoke-verified on SM120 (PP2×TP4): coherent outputs with healthy per-position draft acceptance (144/96/55/31/22/17/12/6 over K=8).

AI assistance was used in preparing this PR.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Integrate Mega-mHC from DeepGEMM for DeepSeek V4.1  (reopen of #56255)
author: Juntian777
body:
## Summary

- Reopen [vLLM #56255](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56255) (closed unmerged), rebased on the [#56876](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56876) base (`1b5a7abb58`) with the model path retargeted to `deepseek_v41`.
- Keep the original implementation commit separate from the follow-up adaptation; its elfutils dependency is already in the base.
- Preserve the current TileLang fused path for auxiliary capture and unsupported inputs, and preserve Engram injection order.
- Pin the #56876 vLLM DeepGEMM fork at `ad1f1726` (2.8.0), including its SM90/SM120 support and API fixes.

## Why this is not a duplicate

#56255 was closed without merging; this PR reopens that work. Open-PR searches show no competing Mega-mHC integration. [#56611](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56611) fuses TileLang statistics with attention/FFN instead; this change uses DeepGEMM Mega-mHC fusion. Dependency changes intentionally reuse #56876 rather than re-opening them.

## Benchmarks

Single GB200, H=5120 / 7168, `hc_mult=4`, BF16, 20 Sinkhorn iterations. Full post + delayed-pre + RMSNorm chain. CUPTI full-stage spans over CUDA graph replays, cold L2, 10 warmup + 100 samples per variant in forward/reverse (ABCCBA) order. Setup, JIT, and host allocation excluded; CPU launch overhead is outside the measured spans.

### E2E Benchmarks

GB200 TP4, official DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `fp8_ds_mla`, no speculative decoding, `max-model-len=40960`. Same local source (`e7fcd569dd`) and dependencies; TileLang uses the existing fused-op worker hook, and #56611 Overlap is ported onto this base with TP4 enabled.

`vllm bench serve`: exactly 8192/32768 input + 1024 output tokens, seed 0, temperature 0, one warmup, ignore EOS, prefix caching disabled. C1: 20 requests/case; C32: 64. All **504 requests** completed with exact token counts.

Latencies are in ms. **Δ is relative to TileLang**, shown as mean TPOT / output throughput; negative TPOT and positive throughput are better.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Keep batch x heads out of gridDim.z in the GLM-5.3-Flash fused recurrent KDA kernel
author: NolenLiang
body:
## Purpose

Fix a start-up crash of GLM-5.3-Flash in data-parallel deployments (TP=1 per rank): `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` was launched with `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)`, and with 64 KDA value heads on one GPU the first CUDA-graph capture batch of 1024 sequences needs `1024 * 64 = 65536` programs — one over the CUDA `gridDim.z` limit of 65535 — so the launch fails with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument` and `--data-parallel-size 4` (with or without EP) cannot start. TP4 (16 heads per rank) is unaffected.

The kernel now carries `N * HV` in `gridDim.x` (limit 2^31-1) with the `program_id` mapping swapped accordingly. Scope (narrowed in review): only the NVIDIA GLM-5.3-Flash copy under `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/third_party/kda/` (`kernels.py`, `fused_recurrent.py`) and its test are changed. The same `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)` pattern exists in the AMD GLM copy and in `third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/{fused_recurrent,fused_sigmoid_gating,kda}.py`; those are intentionally left unchanged here (no AMD reproduction available; the shared kernels serve other models and need their own validation) and are candidates for separate follow-up. The packed-decode kernel in the same GLM file already guarded this case (`split_batch_head_grid = B * HV > 65535`). The narrowed change serves every GLM-5.3-Flash TP configuration; the failure itself needs TP=1 per rank (DP) at the default capture sizes.

Fixes #56973

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched vllm-project/vllm open and closed PRs and issues (GitHub search, 2026-09-13 and 2026-09-15) for `fused_recurrent_kda`, `gridDim.z`, `65535`, `invalid argument` + GLM-5.3-Flash / KDA / DP: no report of this crash and no PR touching the launch grid of `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`; the only related guard is the existing `split_batch_head_grid` check in the packed-decode kernel of the same file.

## Test Plan

- Regression case added to the existing `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (`test_fused_recurrent_kda_more_than_65535_programs`, parametrized 1024×64 and 2048×48 (sequence, head) programs with head dim 16): the full batch must be bitwise identical to the same batch run in two halves. It fails on the unpatched kernel with the Triton launch error and passes with this change.
- Existing test that exercises the changed kernel: `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (NVIDIA glm5next `fused_recurrent_kda`). The flash-linear-attention and AMD copies are no longer touched by this PR.

## Test commands run and results

On 4× GB200 (SM100), 2026-09-11 nightly image, the changed kernel files mounted over the installed package (`/tmp/t` holds a copy of `tests/` so `import vllm` resolves to the installed package):

```
pip install tblib
python3 -m pytest -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py
python3 -m pytest -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py \
    tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py tests/kernels/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py \
    tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py
```

- `test_kda_recurrent.py` with the new case: stock kernel — 2 failed (the two new parametrizations, `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`), 6 passed; patched kernel — 8 passed.
- The six files (before the new case was added): 197 passed / 7 skipped on stock, 197 passed / 7 skipped with the fix.
- Bitwise equivalence stock vs patched on identical inputs (plain-decode calls at 16, 1024, 4096 and 64000 programs; spec-decode-style calls with 2-D state indices and `num_accepted_tokens` at T=4 and T=6): outputs and state updates `torch.equal`; both deterministic run to run. On the crashing shape (1024 × 64) the patched output equals a reference assembled from two stock half-batches, bitwise.
- End to end: `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel` starts, captures its graphs and serves an 8k-in/1k-out sweep at concurrency 1–128; TP4 with the patch reproduces stock TP4 throughput (169.6 vs 169.1 tok/s at c=1, 1898.6 vs 1897.4 at c=32); gsm8k 5-shot greedy on the patched DP4+EP server 0.927 vs 0.934 for stock TP4 (paired exact McNemar p = 0.29 on the 57 discordant questions).
- 2026-09-21, after narrowing — kernel regression test only (the TP4 / DP4+EP serving runs and the gsm8k evaluation above were done before the narrowing and were not repeated, since the NVIDIA GLM kernel files are unchanged by it): same image and procedure, with only the two NVIDIA GLM kernel files copied over the installed package; the three shared flash-linear-attention wrappers were left as installed (their `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)` lines checked present by grep). Stock: 2 failed / 6 passed in `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (the two > 65535-program cases, `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`); with the two files: 8 passed.

## Model evaluation

gsm8k, lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13, 5-shot, greedy, one prompt per request, all 1319 questions: patched DP4 + EP server 0.927 (1223 correct) vs stock TP4 0.934 (1232 correct); paired exact McNemar on the 57 discordant questions p = 0.29 (no detectable difference; the kernel outputs themselves are bitwise identical to stock where stock can run).

## AI assistance

This change was developed with an AI assistant (Claude); the author reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements above.

title: [Spec Decode][Model] Support DFlash2 draft models with GLM-5.3-Flash
author: Dovis01
body:
## Summary

`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` is the block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter published for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. On current `main` the pair cannot be served: `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2",...}'` fails during startup, and fixing one failure exposes the next. This PR makes the combination start and serve on NVIDIA (8x H100, TP8 + EP), adds unit coverage for the two non-model changes, and reports a throughput sweep against the existing MTP path. No kernels, defaults, or MTP behaviour are changed.

The three blockers on `main` (9d4d9aa5bc), in the order they surface:

| # | Stage | Error on `main` | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | draft model load | `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface` | `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (the architecture the DFlash2 checkpoint targets) do not declare `SupportsEagle3`, and `Glm5NextModel` is not an `EagleModelMixin`, so the DFlash speculator cannot register its aux hidden-state layers (`target_layer_ids + 1 = [6, 15, 25, 34, 43]`). |
| 2 | KV cache init | `NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.` | `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` bails out as soon as a non-MLA attention layer (the draft's sliding-window GQA layers) is present, so the generic page unifier runs on a spec set it cannot unify (MLA 655,360 B, indexer 21,120 B and draft 163,840 B pages at block_size 640). |
| 3 | config | `ValueError: Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled` | `create_draft_parallel_config` copies `enable_expert_parallel` from the MoE target onto the dense drafter (introduced by #55914 for the DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE drafter). |

### Changes

- **`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py` (aux hidden-state capture).** `Glm5NextModel` becomes an `EagleModelMixin`; `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` declare `SupportsEagle3`. The tensor handed to the drafter is not `hidden_states + residual`: GLM-5.3-Flash layers run mHC with 4 residual streams and defer each layer's `hc_post` into the next layer's fused post+pre kernel, so at a layer boundary `residual` is the widened `(T, 4 * hidden)` stream (a naive `hidden + residual` fails with `The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1`) and `hidden_states` alone is the raw layer output. `_aux_hidden_state()` completes the deferred `hc_post` through a dedicated `MHCPostOp` and contracts the streams back to `hidden_size` with `hc_contract`, which is the quantity SGLang's `_prepare_aux_hidden_state` feeds DFlash2. The capture is read-only: the layer loop keeps consuming the original `(hidden_states, residual, post, comb)` tuple. Non-mHC layer boundaries already carry the summed stream in `hidden_states` and are returned as-is. When any aux layer is requested, `forward` returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)`; otherwise the return type is unchanged.

### Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate check run on 2026-09-15)

Searches: `gh pr list --state open --search "dflash glm"`, `"GLM-5.3 speculative draft"`, `"create_draft_parallel_config"`, `"enable_expert_parallel draft model"`, `gh pr list --state all --search "dflash"`, `gh issue list --search "GLM-5.3-Flash dflash"`.

- #55682 (Leoyzen, open) implements the aux capture with the same semantics (materialize `hc_post`, then `hc_contract`, at the layer boundary) and adds a CPU unit suite for it. It intentionally leaves the KV-cache layout to a companion change (its description notes the draft sliding-window groups still need one); on the configuration tested here (TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, H100) `main` + an aux-capture-only change still fails at blocker 2. The `model.py` change here is functionally equivalent for GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC boundaries; if #55682 lands first, this PR rebases onto it and drops its `model.py` hunk.
- #55423 (zixi-qi, draft, needs-rebase) covers aux capture plus a KV layout, but with a different layout design: the draft's sliding-window layers are re-blocked to the MLA block size, padded to the MLA page and aliased into the target's MLA slots (no extra bytes per block; `is_eagle_group` follows `use_eagle_block_drop()`; tested with `disable_eagle_block_drop=true`). This PR keeps the draft in a separate region with its native page instead; it is simpler and needs no block-drop override, but it costs KV capacity (numbers below). The two are alternative designs for reviewers to choose between.
- #56933 (hnt2601, opened 2026-09-15) is the same EP-inheritance fix with a different signature (`draft_model_config: ModelConfig | None`). If it merges first, this PR drops the `speculative.py` hunk.
- #55219 (ivanium, draft) removes the GLM-specific layout in favour of the generic packed layout; if that lands, the `kv_cache_utils.py` part of this PR is superseded.
- #54451 (ROCm: glm5next lacks `SupportsEagle3`) is the ROCm counterpart of blocker 1; this PR only touches the NVIDIA model file.

No open PR makes `GLM-5.3-Flash + GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` start on `main` end to end; this one does, and the parts overlapping with #55682 and #56933 are flagged above for rebasing.

Due to discussion for kv cache allocation,  this PR just submits the main support in advance.

## Previous full supported performance

**Setup.** 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 535.154.05), TP8 + EP, torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Python 3.12, vLLM `main` 9d4d9aa5bc + this branch, V2 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Target `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-model-len 131072`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). Draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window layers, sliding window 2048, block_size 8). Auto-selected attention backends: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (target), FLASH_ATTN (draft).

**Workload.** 16 fixed prompts (code and prose), greedy (`temperature=0`), `max_tokens=512`, `/v1/chat/completions`. Single stream = 4 sequential prompts after 2 warm-ups; concurrency N = N simultaneous requests (prompts cycled). Aggregate output tok/s, per-request median tok/s in parentheses. `k` = `num_speculative_tokens`, "FA" / "FI" = FlashAttention / FlashInfer draft attention, the number in the config column is `--max-num-seqs`.

| Config | Single stream | Conc 8 | Conc 32 | Conc 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16, FA, 48 | 178.7 | 848.5 (118.3) | 707.3 (23.1) | - |
| DFlash2 k=8, FA, 48 | 202.1 | 987.7 (136.3) | 2652.5 (94.5) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FA, 48 | 218.5 | 1064.5 (145.2) | 2844.3 (101.2) | - |
| DFlash2 k=4, FA, 48 | 220.3 | 1051.3 (148.0) | 2751.6 (98.8) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FI, 48 | 202.1 | 1021.0 (141.1) | 2578.8 (95.1) | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 1) | **223.0** | **1074.0 (145.2)** | **2850.7 (103.9)** | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 2) | **225.5** | - | **2923.6 (106.7)** | **4269.3 (77.5)** |
| MTP k=5, 96 (baseline) | 160.7 | 853.7 (117.3) | 2377.0 (84.0) | 3721.3 (66.7) |

Acceptance, aggregated from every `SpecDecoding metrics` log line of each run:

| Config | Mean acceptance length | Draft acceptance rate | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16 | 3.63 | 16.5% | 0.75, 0.54, 0.39, 0.28, 0.20, 0.14, 0.10, 0.08, 0.05, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.006, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001 |
| DFlash2 k=8 | 3.33 | 29.1% | 0.75, 0.53, 0.36, 0.25, 0.18, 0.12, 0.08, 0.06 |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 3.31 | 38.5% | 0.77, 0.55, 0.39, 0.28, 0.19, 0.13 |
| DFlash2 k=4 | 3.00 | 49.9% | 0.78, 0.56, 0.39, 0.27 |
| MTP k=5 | 3.13 | 42.7% | 0.81, 0.57, 0.37, 0.23, 0.15 |

Takeaways:

- `num_speculative_tokens` is the dominant knob. Acceptance decays to ~0 beyond position 8 (the drafter's block_size), so k=16 pays a 17-token verify per step for the same ~3.3-3.6 accepted tokens; going to k=6 raises conc-32 throughput from 707 to 2924 tok/s (4.1x). k=4..6 is the sweet spot on this workload, k=8 is slightly worse.
- Against MTP k=5 at identical settings, DFlash2 k=6 is faster at every concurrency: +40% single stream, +26% at 8, +23% at 32, +15% at 64.
- FlashInfer as the draft attention backend is 7-9% slower than the auto-selected FlashAttention.
- `--max-num-seqs 96` vs 48: +2-3%, no preemption at concurrency 64.

**KV cache capacity (cost of the separate draft region).**

| Config | Available KV memory | KV capacity | Max concurrency at 131072 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP k=5 | 23.61 GiB | 1,802,673 tokens | 13.75x |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 23.49 GiB | 1,358,649 tokens | 10.37x |

Per block (block_size 640) the target uses 11 x 655,360 B MLA pages plus 11 x 21,120 B indexer pages (kpool tails aliased into them); the draft adds 5 x 163,840 B pages and its own per-request block demand to the group-aware capacity estimate, hence 24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory. #55423's slot-aliasing design avoids this at the price of re-blocking the draft to the MLA page; that is the main trade-off between the two PRs. At `--max-num-seqs 96` this still leaves ~14k tokens per sequence.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group "tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters" -v

# Lint and types
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py

# Serve (8x H100)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-num-seqs 96 --max-model-len 131072 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":6}'
# MTP baseline: same command with --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

# Tool-calling E2E: 8 scenarios against /v1/chat/completions (auto / required / named tool_choice, zero-arg tool, no tools, thinking off, streaming, multi-turn), see Test Result
# Throughput sweep: 16 prompts, greedy, max_tokens=512, single stream + concurrency {8,32} / {32,64}; per-config server relaunch with the speculative-config JSON above
# Accuracy
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** `3 passed` (the kv-cache test and both parametrizations of the config test).

**pre-commit.** All hooks pass on the five changed files, including `mypy-3.10` (the follow-up commit fixes a `dict` invariance error in `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next`).

**Startup.** Each blocker above was hit and cleared in turn on this branch; the final configuration loads the draft (5 layers, `Overriding draft model max model len from 1048576 to 131072`), builds the KV cache (`GPU KV cache size: 1,358,649 tokens`), captures CUDA graphs and serves.

**Tool-calling E2E** against the running DFlash2 server (`--tool-call-parser glm47`, `--reasoning-parser glm45`): 8/8 pass, zero FSM or CUDA errors in the server log. Repeated after each sweep configuration with the same result.

| Scenario | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| auto tool call | `tool_choice=auto`, one `<tool_call>` parsed into `tool_calls`, arguments valid JSON | PASS |
| required tool call | `tool_choice=required` forces a call | PASS |
| named tool call | `tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}` picks the named tool | PASS |
| named zero-argument tool | tool without parameters yields `arguments == "{}"` | PASS |
| no tools, plain chat | no tool schema, ordinary completion, no stray tags | PASS |
| thinking off | `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` with tools | PASS |
| streaming tool call | `stream=true`, deltas reassemble to a valid call | PASS |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back, second assistant turn answers from it | PASS |

**GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, `--max-concurrency 1 --request-timeout-seconds 7200`; the default 600 s timeout acts as a global deadline at concurrency 1 and truncates the run).**

| Server | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target only (no speculative config), same machine and flags | 0.931 | 0.0% | 121,390 | 1195 s | 101.6 |
| DFlash2 k=6 (this PR) | 0.939 | 0.0% | 123,732 | 607 s | 203.8 |

The two accuracies differ by 0.8 points (about 10 of 1319 questions), inside the run-to-run spread of this greedy-but-nondeterministic stack (see below); output-token counts match within 2%. DFlash2 delivers the same accuracy at 2.0x the single-stream decode speed.

**Greedy output determinism.** Exact token-level lossless verification is not possible on this stack: with `temperature=0` the same server produces different continuations run to run (16 sweep prompts, 512 tokens, sequential, prompt already cached): target-only 0/16 identical across three runs (median common prefix 272-306 characters before the first divergence), DFlash2 k=6 0/16 identical across three runs (median 237-306), and DFlash2 vs target-only 0/16 identical (median 222-237). The run-to-run spread of the target alone is the same size as the DFlash2-vs-target spread, so the divergence comes from the fp8 MoE + EP numerics of the target (near-tie argmax flips), not from the speculative path; the GSM8K parity above (0.919 vs 0.911) is the meaningful losslessness check.

**Pre-existing crash observed while testing, not introduced by this PR (#55626).** Any step that co-schedules a ~600+ token prefill with a speculative verify step, or a burst of a dozen ~630-token prefills, kills the engine with an asynchronous CUDA fault. It reproduces identically with MTP, whose KV layout on this branch is byte-for-byte the `main` layout, so it is a property of the target's FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA path with speculative decoding, matching the traceback location and the FlashInfer core dump posted in #55626.

| Run | Speculative config | Load | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | DFlash2 k=6 | `gsm8k_eval.py` unbounded (100 in flight): 12 prefills of 618-645 tokens in one step, 7578 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, all 8 workers, reproduced 3/3 |
| A' | DFlash2 k=6, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | same | fault attributed to FlashInfer `BatchMLAPagedAttentionSM90` in the target's `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py::forward_mqa` (`Failed to run MLA, error: an illegal memory access was encountered`) |
| B | DFlash2 k=6 | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 661-token prefill + one 7-token verify step | `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` (sticky error surfacing in the next GEMM) |
| C | MTP k=5 (main layout) | unbounded: 7 prefills, 4518 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` |
| D | MTP k=5 (main layout) | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 637-token prefill + one 6-token verify step | `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered`, surfacing at `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py:350 _kv_lens_host` (the same frame as in #55626) |

The throughput sweep and the tool-calling E2E never hit it because their concurrent prompts are short (~30 tokens) and their long prompts run one at a time; GSM8K was therefore run at `--max-concurrency 1`. Prefix caching is not involved (`prefix_cache_stats ... hits=0` in every crash dump).

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- #55626 (above) affects every speculative configuration of GLM-5.3-Flash on SM90 and needs a separate fix; the DFlash2 path inherits it.
- The separate draft region costs KV capacity relative to the slot-aliasing design in #55423 (24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory); the two designs should be reconciled in review.
- Aux hidden states are not all-gathered under sequence parallelism (`compilation_config.pass_config.enable_sp`); the tested configuration runs with compilation mode NONE, where SP is off. Pipeline parallelism is already gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash and was not exercised.
- Tested with greedy sampling for throughput and the default sampling of the tool-calling scripts; `disable_eagle_block_drop` was left at its default.
- Only the NVIDIA model file is changed; the ROCm copy (#54451) is not addressed.

title: [Feature] Per-row candidate IDs for prefill token scoring (M2 of #56860)
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

M2 of #56860, following #54335. `SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids` becomes per row: one candidate list per scored causal prompt row, so an on-policy distillation teacher scores each response position against the student's own top-K.

- **Input**: an integer array `[num_rows, num_ids]` (or nested lists), `-1` padding shorter rows. Row `j` scores prompt token `prompt_logprob_start + j + 1`; the row count must equal `prompt_len - 1 - prompt_logprob_start`.
- **Output**: unchanged shape, `[num_rows, num_ids]` float32; padded entries are `-inf`, as decode-side `logprob_token_ids` pads.

This replaces the request-wise form; the same IDs at every row is a tiled array.

## Design

- **Array, not nested lists.** The table is normalized once in `verify()` (before the processor's deepcopy) to C-contiguous `int32`, like the runner's other token ID buffers, and travels on the existing zero-copy ndarray path. Measured against an all-`list[list[int]]` prototype: 4000 × 64 costs +5 ms vs +105 ms, 4000 × 1024 +9 ms vs +1.6 s.
- **JSON.** The field is `Annotated[np.ndarray, GetPydanticSchema(... list[list[StrictInt]])]`; `PydanticMsgspecMixin` now keeps `Annotated` metadata (`include_extras=True`). `SamplingParams` is the mixin's only user and no other field's schema changes.
- **Validation.** `verify()` checks shape, width (`--max-logprobs`) and a `max_model_len` row bound before padding, then vocabulary; admission checks the exact row count against the prompt.
- **Worker.** The table is sliced per prefill chunk by absolute prompt row; `-1` is clamped for the gather and masked to `-inf` at emit; state is freed once scores are emitted.
- **Rust frontend** (`/inference/v1/generate`): parses `Vec<Vec<i32>>`, applies the same checks in the same order, and sends an `int32` ndarray (aux frame when large). The checks are required there: engine-core does not re-validate.

## Test Plan

GB200, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` with this branch overlaid, `vllm-rs` built from this branch.

- `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k prompt_logprob_token_ids`, `test_logprobs_processor.py`, `test_trace_replay_params.py`: 6 passed. The chunked-prefill + preemption test uses distinct candidates per row and checks them against an unchunked run and same-run `prompt_logprobs`.
- `test_serving_tokens.py::test_generate_prompt_token_id_logprobs`, Python and Rust frontends: passed.
- `vllm serve` (Qwen3-0.6B, chunked prefill at 64 tokens), 36 cases per frontend: sparse ragged rows checked entry by entry against `prompt_logprobs` top-20 (up to 1500 rows, ~15k entries, exact match), empty rows, width and row-count bounds, out-of-vocab and non-integer elements, streaming, concurrency. Both frontends accept and reject the same requests and return byte-identical matrices.
- `cargo test` (engine-core-client, text, llm, server), `cargo clippy --workspace`, `pre-commit`: pass.

## Test Result

Qwen3-8B, TP=1, 8192-token prompt, `max_tokens=1`, `int32` array input; median of 15 interleaved pairs against a ~108 ms baseline:

| rows × ids | 1000 × 64 | 4000 × 64 | 4000 × 1024 | `prompt_logprobs=0` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| added | +1 ms | +5 ms | +9 ms | +65 ms |

For 4000 rows the GPU side is ~5 ms regardless of width: the extra `lm_head` over the scored rows (~3.4 ms) and the full-vocab log-softmax (~1.4 ms). Nested-list input is slower (Python object copies); the docs recommend `int32` arrays.

## AI assistance

Implemented with Claude Code; every line reviewed by the submitter. Not a duplicate: #56860 tracks the design and #54335 is M1; no other open PR implements per-row prefill candidates.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Add per-tensor FP8 W8A16 kernel to fix Ministral crash on CPU
author: bigPYJ1151
body:
## Summary

- Add `CPUFp8PerTensorScaledMMLinearKernel`, a per-tensor FP8 W8A16 CPU kernel
  built on the existing AMX block-scaled kernel. `PerTensorTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`
  was the only per-tensor FP8 CPU kernel available and wasn't wired up for
  AMX-capable CPUs, crashing on load of fp8-quantized `PixtralForConditionalGeneration`
  models (e.g. Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512).
- CI: match the wrapped `RuntimeError("Cannot find any model weights with ...")`
  that `default_loader.py` raises for a partial HF cache snapshot, so the CPU
  CI offline→online retry fallback actually triggers for that cache-miss shape.
- CI: mount `~/.cache/vllm` (in addition to the already-mounted `~/.cache/huggingface`)
  so multimodal test fixtures (`VideoAsset`, `ImageAsset`, `AudioAsset`, which
  download into `VLLM_ASSETS_CACHE`) persist across CPU CI container lifetimes
  instead of being re-fetched, and falling back online, on every run.

The two CI fixes were found while chasing recurring CPU CI flakiness during
verification of the kernel fix above (Buildkite builds #89028 and #89045).

## Test plan

- `python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_cpu_fp8_scaled_mm.py -v`
  → 80 passed (covers both the new per-tensor kernel and the underlying
  block-scaled kernel it reuses, including the N-not-a-multiple-of-32 rejection path).
- CI script changes verified with `bash -n` and against the actual failing
  Buildkite logs they target: #89028 (CPU multi-modal tests re-fetching video
  assets every run) and #89045 (CPU spec-decode failing outright on a partial
  weight-file cache instead of retrying online).

title: [Perf][Attention] Source Triton metadata builder geometry from kv_cache_spec
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Overview

`TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder` is built per KV-cache group but sizes its 3D-kernel threshold and split-K scratch from the model-wide KV head count and head dim, so on heterogeneous models such as Gemma 4 decode stays on the slower 2D kernel; this PR reads both from the group's `kv_cache_spec`, as `FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder` already does (#42650 did the same for `num_heads_q`).

`unified_attention` takes the 2D grid's `num_kv_heads` from `k.shape[2]`, the group's own count. On `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` the full-attention group has 2 KV heads against a model-wide 8, so `seq_threshold_3D` is `128 // 8 = 16` instead of `128 // 2 = 64`: at batch 24 the grid is 48 blocks, below `MIN_LAUNCH_GRID_SIZE_2D = 128`, yet the builder stays on 2D. The sliding groups size `softmax_segm_output` for head dim 512 instead of 256.

The buffer uses `head_size`, the stride `unified_attention` applies (`next_power_of_2(q.shape[2])`); `head_size_v` belongs to the DiffKV path, which re-sizes its own buffer. Switching kernel changes the bf16 reduction order, so generated text can differ. Where the spec matches the model-global values, nothing changes.

#54191 changes `num_heads_kv` only. #57409 changes `headdim` only, inside a DFlash change. This PR does both, and the new tests fail on either half alone. #47520 rescales the grid-size target and keeps the divisor, so it composes with this.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 full-attention decode at batches 24–64 moves from the 2D to the 3D kernel: **+66%** at batch 24 (506 µs → 172 µs) and **+36%** at batch 64 on MI325X. Batches that keep their kernel are flat.
- On vLLM v0.29.0 (MI355X), `vllm bench serve` of gemma-4 at 32K input and concurrency 24 gives **+6.7%** total tok/s and **−11.5%** median TPOT, with TTFT flat. Not re-taken on this `main`.
- GSM8K strict-match on that build goes from **0.4155 to 0.4511**; a repeated base run is bit-identical.
- Affected locally: gemma-4-26B-A4B and gemma-4-31B, which `Gemma4Config` forces onto `TRITON_ATTN` on ROCm. Homogeneous models are unchanged.

## Validation

Base is `main@7128f568ac`; the patched arm adds only this diff.

| tree | Triton cases in `test_group_head_counts.py` |
|---|---|
| `main` | 3 failed |
| `num_heads_kv` only (#54191) | 2 failed: geometry, scratch stride |
| `headdim = head_size_v` | 1 failed: scratch stride |
| threshold capped before the capture snap | 1 failed: snaps to 48, not 64 |
| this PR | 4 passed, 12 skipped |

`test_triton_attn_metadata_builder.py` and `test_triton_attn_segments.py` pass 44/44 on both arms. One new case uses an off-grid `max_num_seqs=50`, where the threshold snaps to a capture size (64) before `max_num_seqs` caps the scratch rows.

Kernel, MI325X, `unified_attention` at the full-attention group shape (16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 512, block 16, ctx 4096, decode), median of five `do_bench` repeats, both run orders within 0.5 points:

| batch | main | this PR | gain |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---:|
| 8 / 16 | 3D | 3D | −0.1% / −0.3% |
| 24 | 2D | **3D** | **+66%** |
| 32 | 2D | **3D** | **+63%** |
| 48 / 50 | 2D | **3D** | **+49% / +48%** |
| 64 | 2D | **3D** | **+36%** |
| 96 | 2D | 2D | ~0 |

Outputs match exactly where the kernel is unchanged, and to 2.8e-3 relative L2 where it switches.

Serve on v0.29.0 (`98dff2a81d`), MI355X, six interleaved pairs, 32K input / 256 output, concurrency 24:

| metric | base | patched | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 25835 | 27574 | **+6.7%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 65.18 | 57.68 | **−11.5%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 13823 | 13793 | −0.2% |

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, `seed=1234`:

| comparison | identical text | strict-match |
|---|---:|---|
| base vs base | 100% | 0.4155 → 0.4155 |
| base vs base at `max_num_seqs=128` | 4.6% | 0.4155 → 0.4314 |
| base vs this PR | 12.7% | 0.4155 → 0.4511 |
| Qwen3-8B (never builds this) | 99.9% | 0.8726 → 0.8726 |

`main` alone at a different `max_num_seqs` already changes 95% of generations: the 2D/3D boundary is batch-dependent, and this PR moves it.

## Details

Of 17 local checkpoints, only Gemma 4 reaches this builder without an explicit backend selection; the others, forced onto it, match `main` in every builder field. Under full graph capture with an off-grid `max_num_seqs=50`, batches 49–50 pad to 56 tokens and stay on 2D on both arms; that sizing comes from `main`.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: widen skinny GEMM LDS activation loads to b128
author: roberteg16
body:
## Summary

The `wvSplitK` int4 skinny GEMM stages activations into LDS as `s[k_ + K * n]` and reads them back per row. `K` is a runtime value, so the compiler cannot prove the per-row offset `K*n` is 16-element aligned and falls back to paired `ds_load_2addr_b32`/`b64` for the higher rows. But `K` is a multiple of `A_CHUNK` and so is `k_`, so `s[k_ + K * n]` is in fact `sizeof(bigTypeA)`-aligned for every row — annotating the read lets the compiler widen all activation rows to `ds_load_b128`.

That invariant was implicit: `A_CHUNK` is a template argument pinned to 16 by the launch macro, and the host only checks `K % 16 == 0`. The k-loop already relies on it too, since it consumes whole `A_CHUNK` chunks. The host check now uses a shared `kInt4KAlign` constant, each kernel does `static_assert(kInt4KAlign % A_CHUNK == 0)`, and the LDS buffer is declared `alignas(sizeof(bigTypeA))`, so raising `A_CHUNK` fails to build until `kInt4KAlign` is raised with it.

This is a compiler-visibility argument rather than an architectural one, so it is not gated on a specific gfx target. The global fallback read in the medium kernel is deliberately left untouched: `A[]`'s base alignment is not guaranteed there.

LDS load instructions across all int4 instantiations, gfx1151 with ROCm 10.2, counted by disassembling the gfx1151 device image out of the built `_rocm_C.abi3.so`:

| | `ds_load_b128` | `ds_load_2addr_b32` | `ds_load_2addr_b64` | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 6864 | 3744 | 624 | 11232 |
| after | 9360 | 0 | 0 | 9360 |

`N=1` and `N=2` were already fully widened by this compiler and come out byte-identical; the change is confined to `N=3,4,5`.

## Measurements

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_gemm.py`, `--group-size 128`, batch 4, median of 3 passes, TFLOP/s, symmetric / asymmetric:

| K x N | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2048x2048 | 2.501 / 2.020 | 2.929 / 2.316 | **+17.1% / +14.6%** |
| 2560x2560 | 3.040 / 2.853 | 3.392 / 3.038 | **+11.6% / +6.5%** |
| 8192x2048 | 2.218 / 1.645 | 2.276 / 1.743 | +2.6% / +6.0% |
| 2560x3840 | 3.834 / 3.402 | 3.877 / 3.510 | +1.1% / +3.2% |
| 2048x6144 | 3.301 / 3.122 | 3.275 / 3.077 | -0.8% / -1.4% |
| 2048x16384 | 3.258 / 3.162 | 3.272 / 3.164 | +0.4% / +0.1% |
| 2560x19456 | 3.361 / 3.334 | 3.369 / 3.321 | +0.2% / -0.4% |

The win concentrates on small `out_features`, where the kernel is bound by the LDS read rather than by the weight stream. Batch 1 and 2 are flat everywhere, which is exactly what the instruction counts predict. Only shapes that actually reach the HIP skinny path (`M <= 5` and `K*M <= 32768`) are listed; the rest route to Triton and are unaffected.

Reproducing the asymmetric column needs #57004, without which the benchmark's `hybrid-w4a16-zp` provider raises.

## Model evaluation

GSM8K on gfx1151, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42. `max_num_seqs=4` so every decode step runs the `N=3,4` instantiations this change touches (`max_num_seqs=1` would only exercise the unchanged `N=1` path):

```bash
lm_eval --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=<model>,max_model_len=4096,max_num_seqs=4,dtype=float16,gpu_memory_utilization=0.75,enforce_eager=False,seed=42 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 42
```

| model | filter | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` | strict-match | 0.8582 ± 0.0096 | 0.8590 ± 0.0096 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` | flexible-extract | 0.8613 ± 0.0095 | 0.8620 ± 0.0095 |

Qwen3-8B-AWQ differs by a single question, well inside one stderr. Average output throughput over the eval run is flat (20.9 vs 20.6 tok/s).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py` on gfx1151: 84 passed.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` passes, clang-format included.
- [x] ISA verified by disassembling the built device image and counting LDS opcodes per instantiation; the `static_assert`/`alignas` hardening leaves it byte-identical.
- [x] With the launch macro set to `A_CHUNK=32`, the build fails on the `static_assert` in both kernels, and succeeds again once `kInt4KAlign` is raised to 32.
- [x] GSM8K 5-shot on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ`: accuracy matches the baseline (see above).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change, as required by `AGENTS.md`. Not a duplicate: the only other open PR touching `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` is #56301, which changes host-side weight row-stride padding and does not touch the LDS activation reads.
