title: [Kernel] Accumulate ranks in absolute order in 2-stage custom all-reduce
author: mosafariuk
body:
## Purpose

`cross_device_reduce_2stage` rotates the rank pointers, so each partition's owner starts its sum at its own rank. `cross_device_reduce_1stage` sums ranks in absolute order `0..N-1`. Both reduce through the same `packed_reduce`, which accumulates into float32 (`csrc/custom_collective_common.cuh:87`, `:323-330`). When those partial sums round, the two kernels can return different bits for the same all-reduce — and the choice between them is made by message size (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:298-307`: 1-stage below 512 KiB at ≤4 ranks and 256 KiB at ≤8, 2-stage above).

(Line numbers are at main `b49c921a27`, this PR's base; the comment added here shifts the `.cuh` ones after line 47 by 2 on this branch.)

The rotation also makes 2-stage output depend on the total tensor size, even with no switch between kernels. This was independently measured by @curvedinf ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57042#issuecomment-5686335910)). `part = size / ngpus` moves the ownership boundaries whenever the size changes (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:38-40`), and each owner starts its sum at its own rank (`:45-48`). In their on-GPU in-vitro run of the unmodified kernels at 4 ranks and fp32, 14.86% of the elements of a 1664×5120 tensor differ bitwise from the same rows of its 2048×5120 parent. Both sizes are above the 512 KiB threshold, so this comes from a chunked-prefill geometry change alone. The 1-stage control on the same data is bit-identical, which pins the cause to the rotation this PR removes.

This PR makes the 2-stage kernel read the rank pointers in absolute order, so both kernels produce identical bits whichever one the heuristic selects, and 2-stage output no longer depends on the tensor size. The direction was proposed by @sfeng33 in the review of #50505; this is that change, split out and self-contained against main. cc @sfeng33

**The change** is one line in `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh`: `ptrs[i] = (const P*)_dp->ptrs[target]` → `_dp->ptrs[i]`.

Only `ptrs` loses the rotation. `tmps[i]` must keep it: `tmp_out = tmps[0]` has to be the rank's own scratch buffer, and the stage-2 gather indexes `tmps` with the same `(rank + i)` rotation. De-rotating both would make every rank write its stage-1 results into rank 0's scratch region. The code comment records this.

**Why the kernels then agree bit-for-bit.** For every element, both compute `downcast(((up(x0) + up(x1)) + ...) + up(xN-1))` through the same float32 accumulator. There are no partial sums on the 2-stage path: each partition's owner computes the full N-term sum, and stage 2 only copies already-downcast values. Once the order matches, every operation matches.

**Effect outside batch invariance.** This changes 2-stage output bit patterns for all runs, not only under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. Before and after, each result sums the same terms through the same float32 accumulator; only the order of the additions differs. How often bits actually change depends on the data and dtype: in the CPU emulation below, plain random fp16/bf16 inputs changed no elements and fp32 inputs changed ~32% (31.28% on GPU in @curvedinf's run, below). No existing test asserts bit-exact 2-stage output: the custom all-reduce tests either run at TP=2, which always selects 1-stage, or force 1-stage (`test_custom_allreduce_chunked`), and the bit-exact all-gather/reduce-scatter tests never dispatch `allreduce()`.

**Prior art, and why this is a separate PR.** #52231 by @mawong-amd already contains this same one-line change, with `ptrs` de-rotated and `tmps` kept rotated. It is part of a 36-file PR adding batch invariance on ROCm, which describes the change as making 2-stage batch-invariant and keeps that path disabled on CUDA pending tuning. This PR splits out only the kernel line, with a 4-rank differential test, so it can be reviewed and land on its own. If #52231 lands first, this PR reduces to the test. cc @mawong-amd

#56358 also targets fixed-order TP reduction, but through an opt-in Python gather-and-sum path (`VLLM_TP_FIXED_ORDER_ALLREDUCE`); it doesn't touch this kernel. Relationship to #50505: complementary. This PR makes kernel *selection* irrelevant to the bits; #50505 keeps *backend* selection (custom vs NCCL) batch-independent. Whichever lands second should drop #50505's force-1-stage gate.

## Test Plan

New test `test_one_and_two_stage_allreduce_bitwise_identical` in `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`. No NVIDIA CI job runs this file: the `:nvidia: (A100) Distributed` step it is declared in is no longer emitted, because the A100 fleet is retired. Its AMD mirror, `:amd: (MI355) Distributed`, still runs it on 4× MI355. The mirror inherits `optional: true`, so it runs only when someone unblocks it (`Run :amd: (MI355) Distributed` in build #93586).

- 4 ranks. It forces each kernel in turn with `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=1stage|2stage` (read on every `allreduce()` call, `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:271`) over the same per-rank inputs, and asserts bitwise-identical outputs.
- fp16 / bf16 / fp32 × 4 sizes, from 16,336 B to 4,194,224 B. The sizes straddle the 512 KiB threshold, and three leave an uneven last partition.
- Adversarial inputs: each element holds `+B`, `-B` and small terms below float32's resolution at `B`, in a random rank order. Ordinary random fp16/bf16 data almost never detects a change of order, because its float32 partial sums are almost always exact (see the emulation below).
- Both forced kernels must also return the exact sum on integer inputs. The existing custom all-reduce tests run at TP=2 or force 1-stage, so none of them reaches 2-stage.
- Why 4 ranks: at 2 the rotation only turns `a+b` into `b+a`, which is commutative, so no 2-rank run can tell the orders apart.
- Skips cleanly with fewer than 4 GPUs, without the custom all-reduce ops, or without full NVLink (custom all-reduce disables itself above 2 PCIe-only ranks).

## Test Result

**4-rank GPU differential: run on 4× MI355.** @mawong-amd ran it on 4× MI355 (gfx950, XGMI) with this PR rebased onto main ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57042#pullrequestreview-5454848047)). The test passes on this branch, and against main's kernel it fails with `fp16, 16336 bytes: 2-stage differs from 1-stage in 5113/8168 elements`.

It has not been run on NVIDIA. It needs 4 GPUs with NVLink all-to-all; to reproduce there, the test should **fail** against main's kernel and **pass** on this branch:

```bash
TEST=tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
git fetch https://github.com/mosafariuk/vllm.git rankorder-2stage
# main's kernel (this PR's base; a precompiled build is enough, since main's kernel is unchanged):
git checkout b49c921a27083c25c16f308be1326055dbc87bbf && VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .
git checkout d7f127882cd37a5f57f313493a7498688f5457b8 -- "$TEST"
pytest -rA "$TEST" -k one_and_two_stage   # expect FAILED: "... 2-stage differs from 1-stage in N/M elements"
# this branch (kernel change, needs a source build):
git checkout d7f127882cd37a5f57f313493a7498688f5457b8 && uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
pytest -rA "$TEST" -k one_and_two_stage   # expect PASSED
```

Other runs:

Independent in-vitro run by @curvedinf on an AMD gfx1100 ([comment with harness and logs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57042#issuecomment-5686335910)). It used the unmodified kernel headers from main `241e9391e`; `custom_all_reduce.cuh` and `custom_collective_common.cuh` there are byte-identical to this PR's original base `2983fc6286`. Main has since added only an unrelated `mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter` declaration to `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. Four logical ranks are staged sequentially on one GPU with the barrier flags pre-armed. That exercises the kernels' arithmetic (pointer order and partition ownership), but not IPC, NVLink, or this PR's pytest test. Inputs are `N(0,1)·(0.1 + 0.05·rank)`:

| comparison, 4 ranks | fp32 | bf16 |
|---|---|---|
| 1-stage vs 2-stage, same 2048×5120 data | 31.28% of elements differ | 0 |
| 2-stage at 1664×5120 vs the same rows at 2048×5120 | 14.86% | 0 |
| control: 1-stage at 1664 vs 2048 | 0 | 0 |

With this PR's line applied to the harness's header copy, all fp32 rows are reported as 0. The attached logs cover the unmodified runs. A CPU emulation of the same geometry, with a different RNG, gives 30.9% and 14.7%. 34.6% of the smaller tensor's elements change owner between the two sizes.

CPU, full test file (run before the rebase; line numbers and skip counts differ at the current head):
```
$ pytest -rA -v tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
SKIPPED [4] tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py:217: Not enough GPUs to run the test.
SKIPPED [1] tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py:312: Not enough GPUs to run the test.
================== 11 passed, 5 skipped, 14 warnings in 6.35s ==================
```

4× A100-SXM4-40GB without NVLink (`nvidia-smi topo -m` shows every pair as `NODE`), with a wheel built from this branch before the rebase — the skip path on real hardware:
```
is_fully_connected(0..3): False
SKIPPED [1] tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py:320: Custom all-reduce needs fully connected GPUs above 2 ranks.
================ 1 skipped, 15 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.45s ================
```

CPU emulation of `packed_reduce`'s float32 accumulation (emulated, not GPU). For each element, 1-stage order vs the unpatched 2-stage owner-rotated order, downcast and compared bitwise at 4 ranks:

| inputs | fp16 | bf16 | fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| this test's adversarial inputs, all 4 sizes | 62.5–62.6% of elements differ | 62.4–62.5% | 61.8–62.5% |
| plain `randn` | **0** differ | **0** differ | ~32% |

Partition owner 0 differs in 0% of elements, as expected (its order already matches); owners 1–3 differ in ~83%. The plain-`randn` row is why the test uses adversarial inputs. The fp16/bf16 zeros are structural at 4 ranks, not luck. Those terms carry 11 or 8 significant bits, so float32's 24-bit accumulator adds them exactly unless their magnitudes differ by roughly 2^11–2^14 or more. The rare rounding that remains is erased by the downcast: in an emulation with @curvedinf's input distribution, 480 of 10.5M 1-stage bf16 sums round in float32, and 0 bits differ between orders after the downcast. For realistic data the practical impact is on fp32 all-reduces. fp16/bf16 bits change mainly for inputs like this test's cancellation.

`pre-commit run --files csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`: all applicable hooks passed (ruff check/format, clang-format, typos, mypy, SPDX).

No model evaluation was run. The change only reorders a float32 accumulation of the same terms, so outputs can differ at the bit level but not in expected accuracy. Happy to run an lm-eval comparison if reviewers want one.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Import full blocks without tail prefill on D
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse currently rejects host imports whose computed-token count is not block aligned. This draft explores an alternative to #56946: receive the full final block and restore its contents into one writable GPU page, so a successful NIXL full-prompt import resumes with a single-token forward instead of prefilling the unaligned tail on D.

The idea is that we want to avoid having to run prefill on D, however short they might be (<block_size here), with north star being deploying D with decode-only CG (aligned with rest of cases).

### NIXL analogy: transfer capacity is not sequence length

NIXL already transfers physical blocks containing partially filled prompt tails. Moving the unused bytes does not make them computed tokens. HiSparse can use the same distinction:

| For a 32,019-token prompt, block size 128 | This approach |
| --- | --- |
| Real imported tokens | 32,019 |
| Host blocks received | 251 |
| Physical capacity | 32,128 token slots |
| Unused tail capacity ("holes") | 109 token slots |
| Prompt work on D after a full import | The usual last-token replay for logits |

The holes are unused rows within the request's final host block. They do not change token positions or sequence length, and generation fills them at their normal offsets. P does not compute dummy padding tokens. No sub-block allocator or NIXL wire-protocol change is required.

### Implementation and tradeoff

- Reserve one writable resident page for the final imported block, including aligned prompts whose last token is replayed.
- After a successful external receive, enqueue a full-page host-to-device restore on every TP rank. Copies run on the compute stream before the forward/CUDA-graph replay.
- Retain both endpoints until every participating worker completes its copy. Avoid publishing an uninitialized resident copy to prefix-cache users, and keep an incomplete host page unsealed.
- Register a completed, valid restored GPU page for later prefix hits only after all workers finish. Pending restores remain hidden, and incomplete pages and aborted requests are excluded. This incorporates [NickLucche/vllm#12](https://github.com/NickLucche/vllm/pull/12).
- Continue using the existing row-mirror and page-sealing paths for newly generated KV.

Compared with #56946, this transfers the final block and pays for one page of H2D copying per layer/rank rather than recomputing up to `block_size - 1` prompt tokens. It also reserves a resident tail page for aligned imports. The unused host rows are ordinary tail capacity, not extra logical tokens or permanent gaps between prompt and output. No performance improvement has been measured.

The intended benefit is to keep successful full-prompt P/D handoffs on single-token execution, compatible with decode-only graph capture. This is not a guarantee that D can never prefill: cache misses, failed transfers, preemption, or partial external hits can still require recomputation.

### Related work

Checked #56699 and its comments, open PRs mentioning it, and open PRs matching HiSparse import, landing, tail, partial, full block, and tail restore.

- #56946 addresses the same admission failure by rounding the imported prefix down and prefilling the remainder locally. This draft is the explicitly requested alternative that retains all real prompt KV and changes tail residency instead.
- The notify-only read and empty-region shape fixes are reused verbatim from #56946 (originally #55398). They prevent empty local destinations from entering region expansion when P and D have different cache-group layouts. They are independent of tail policy; empty receives notify P, and report `finished_recving` only when `awaiting_kvs=True`.
- #55398 chooses direct GPU landing for imported history when capacity permits. This draft preserves host landing and restores only the final page.
- #56109 concerns broader pool/residency management. This draft uses the current pool model.

Related to the deployment discussion in #56699; this does not claim to fix that issue's CUDA launch failure or establish end-to-end P/D correctness.

## Test Plan

Exercise aligned, unaligned, and sub-block imports; last-token resumption; partial-page publication; multi-worker completion and abort lifetime; and tail-copy contents on both host-writer and non-writer ranks.

Before marking ready, run real NIXL P/D on NVIDIA GPUs with decode-only graphs, check generated-token/logprob parity against the prefiller reference, and exercise page-boundary crossing, eviction/preemption, and concurrent traffic. Heterogeneous TP/DCP coverage remains pending.

## Test Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py \
  -k 'hisparse or connector_completes_partial_prefix' -q
```

**99 passed, 2 skipped, 117 deselected** on macOS. The two skipped cases require CUDA. Commit-time pre-commit hooks passed, including the configured mypy hook.

Rerun after integrating #12 and rebasing onto `upstream/main` at `fc8132a5e5`: **99 passed, 2 skipped, 117 deselected**. The existing import test now checks that one worker completion does not publish the GPU copy and that full completion publishes aligned tails. Pre-commit hooks passed across all PR files. GPU/model validation of the combined change remains pending.

Additional existing empty-receive checks after restoring those two NIXL hunks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k empty_recv_is_reported_only_when_awaited -q
```

**4 passed, 130 deselected** on macOS. The separate completion-time positional group-pairing workaround reported by the GPU investigation is not included in this draft.

After rebasing onto `upstream/main` (`c6fa1f05d1`, including #57027), fixed the H200 CI failure in `test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore[offload]`: the sync checker reports the tail copy as potentially synchronous because PyTorch does not recognize the host pool's external `cudaHostRegister` registration. A narrow `gpu_sync_allowed()` scope covers that copy; the transfer and stream ordering are unchanged. The existing CUDA tail-restore test now allocates the host pool through the production registration path and enables strict sync checking.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k empty_recv_is_reported_only_when_awaited -q
```

Post-rebase results on macOS: **88 passed, 2 CUDA cases skipped** and **4 passed**, respectively. Pre-commit hooks passed across all PR files. The CUDA regression and failing GPU e2e test still require the new CI run.

**Model evaluation / GPU serving: not run.** This is a draft for design review, published at the submitter's explicit request without waiting for GPU testing. No accuracy, graph-replay, throughput, or latency claim is made.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, tests, and this description. Human line-by-line review and human-run GPU validation remain pending before this draft is ready for merge.

title: [Bugfix] Fix incorrect Mamba block allocation estimate that prevents request admission
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose
It is found for Kimi K3, a long request can be rejected admission when loading prefix cache from external KV storage (e.g., Mooncake) and get stuck in the waiting queue forever, causing entire system to stall. Investigation shows the bug is in Mamba's block allocation estimation call `get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, which incorrectly calculates the physical blocks needed for such requests, potentially a regression caused by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53614

Stall reproduction on 8 x B300:
```
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
export WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0
export MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH=mooncake_config.json
export VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=50052
export MC_ENABLE_DEST_DEVICE_AFFINITY=1

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
    --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --prefix-match-unit 128 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --max-cudagraph-capture-size 2048 \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":0}' \
    --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA \
    --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \
    --language-model-only \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"load_async":true,"lookup_async":true,"enable_cross_layers_blocks":false}}'
```

Sending a 1M-length request, clear the GPU local kv cache, and send the same request again causes the entire system to stall as the request fails the admission gate.

## Test Plan
Added unit test that checks equality of estimated blocks vs actual allocated blocks for mamba in `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, existing main fail the tests while the branch passes.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Honor dynamic K in autoregressive speculators, 1.2~1.3x kernel perf improvement
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

MRV2 did not propagate `SchedulerOutput.num_spec_tokens_to_schedule` to autoregressive speculators, causing unnecessary draft forwards and stale draft tokens.

This PR fixes the issue

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
from functools import partial
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch
import triton

from vllm.v1.spec_decode.dynamic.utils import build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.autoregressive.speculator import (
    AutoRegressiveSpeculator,
)

MAX_K = 5
MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 48
HIDDEN_SIZE = 4096
NUM_REQS = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 48)
DYNAMIC_K_SCHEDULE = [(1, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, 3)]


class SyntheticSpeculator(AutoRegressiveSpeculator):
    """MRV2 proposer whose model forward is replaced by a matmul."""

    def load_draft_model(self, target_model, target_attn_layer_names):
        raise NotImplementedError("This benchmark does not load a model")

    def __init__(self, device: torch.device) -> None:
        # Deliberately skip the real constructor: it allocates model-related state.
        self.num_speculative_steps = MAX_K
        self.max_num_reqs = MAX_BATCH_SIZE
        self.max_model_len = 8192
        self.dp_size = 1
        self.dp_rank = 0
        self.pcp_manager = None
        self.eplb_state = None
        self.use_fused_multi_step_decode = True
        self.prefill_cudagraph_manager = None
        self.decode_cudagraph_manager = None
        self.speculative_config = SimpleNamespace(
            uses_dynamic_speculative_decoding=lambda: True,
        )

        self.input_buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device)
        self.hidden_states = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.last_token_indices = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )
        self.current_draft_step = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
        self.sample_src_positions = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )
        self.idx_mapping = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
        self.temperature = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device=device)
        self.seeds = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
        self.draft_tokens = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_K, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )

        self.weight = torch.randn(
            HIDDEN_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.src = torch.randn(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.dst = torch.empty_like(self.src)
        self.count_steps = False
        self.steps = 0

    def _synthetic_forward(self, num_tokens: int) -> None:
        torch.mm(self.src[:num_tokens], self.weight, out=self.dst[:num_tokens])
        self.src, self.dst = self.dst, self.src
        if self.count_steps:
            self.steps += 1

    def _prefill(self, num_reqs: int, num_tokens: int, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        self._synthetic_forward(num_tokens)
        self.draft_tokens[:num_reqs, 0].zero_()

    def _generate_draft(
        self, num_reqs: int, num_tokens_padded: int, *args, **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        self._synthetic_forward(num_tokens_padded)


def count_forwards(speculator: SyntheticSpeculator, run) -> int:
    speculator.steps = 0
    speculator.count_steps = True
    run()
    speculator.count_steps = False
    return speculator.steps


def main() -> None:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("CUDA is required")

    device = torch.device("cuda")
    speculator = SyntheticSpeculator(device)
    target_buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device)
    target_hidden_states = torch.randn_like(speculator.hidden_states)
    temperature = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device=device)
    seeds = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    last_sampled = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    dense_schedule = build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup(
        DYNAMIC_K_SCHEDULE,
        vllm_max_batch_size=MAX_BATCH_SIZE,
        vllm_num_speculative_tokens=MAX_K,
    )

    print("batch  sched_k  buggy_ms  fixed_ms  speedup  forwards(buggy->fixed)")
    for num_reqs in NUM_REQS:
        batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_reqs, target_buffers)
        common_args = dict(
            input_batch=batch,
            attn_metadata={},
            slot_mappings={},
            last_hidden_states=target_hidden_states[:num_reqs],
            aux_hidden_states=None,
            num_sampled=torch.ones(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
            num_rejected=torch.zeros(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
            last_sampled=last_sampled,
            next_prefill_tokens=target_buffers.input_ids,
            temperature=temperature,
            seeds=seeds,
            dummy_run=True,
            skip_attn_for_dummy_run=True,
            is_profile=True,
        )
        dynamic_k = dense_schedule[num_reqs]

        # Buggy: model_runner omitted runtime K, so propose() used max K=5.
        buggy = partial(speculator.propose, **common_args)
        # Fixed: model_runner passes the scheduler-selected runtime K=3.
        fixed = partial(
            speculator.propose,
            **common_args,
            num_speculative_tokens=dynamic_k,
        )

        buggy_steps = count_forwards(speculator, buggy)
        fixed_steps = count_forwards(speculator, fixed)
        assert dynamic_k == 3
        assert buggy_steps == MAX_K
        assert fixed_steps == dynamic_k

        buggy_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(buggy)
        fixed_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(fixed)
        print(
            f"{num_reqs:>5}  {dynamic_k:>7}  {buggy_ms:>8.3f}  "
            f"{fixed_ms:>8.3f}  {buggy_ms / fixed_ms:>7.3f}x  "
            f"{buggy_steps}->{fixed_steps}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

And we can get

```bash
batch  sched_k  buggy_ms  fixed_ms  speedup  forwards(buggy->fixed)
    1        3     0.151     0.115    1.306x  5->3
    2        3     0.148     0.115    1.286x  5->3
    4        3     0.149     0.115    1.298x  5->3
    8        3     0.148     0.115    1.282x  5->3
   16        3     0.151     0.115    1.315x  5->3
   32        3     0.150     0.114    1.306x  5->3
   48        3     0.149     0.115    1.287x  5->3
```

title: [Attention] Add UltraQuant 4-bit KV cache backend (FlyDSL D=256)
author: aditi-amd
body: ## Purpose Adds an `ultraquant_4bit` KV-cache dtype for long-context / agentic serving, where the KV cache is the limiter. UltraQuant stores the cache at 4 bits, FP4 E2M1 codes with UE8M0 (power-of-two) per-group-32 scales, and Hadamard-rotated keys, giving **~2× KV density over fp8**, so more concurrency fits before eviction and decode stays memory-efficient under load. Decode runs on a FlyDSL `D=256` kernel for GQA group sizes **{6, 8, 16}**, with a Triton unified-attention fallback and numerical reference paths. ## Design - New `UltraQuantAttentionImpl`, a standalone subclass of `TurboQuantAttentionImpl`. - `TurboQuantAttentionBackend.get_impl_cls()` dispatches to the UQ impl on the `ultraquant_4bit` cache dtype. - New ops under `vllm/v1/attention/ops/ultraquant/` (FP4/UE8M0 format, Hadamard store, dequant, Triton unified attention, reference) and the FlyDSL D=256 decode kernel/launcher. ## Test Plan - **Unit tests** (`tests/kernels/ultraquant/`): store, dequant, decode, and FlyDSL-vs-reference numerical checks, plus config. - **Serve smokes**: Qwen3.8 (GQA-16, TP=8) and Qwen3.6-27B (GQA-6, TP=2), confirming FlyDSL dispatch (no Triton fallback) and coherent output. - **Accuracy** (KV format is the only variable; sampling fixed): GPQA-Diamond. - **Performance**: SemiAnalysis-style 262K-token agentic replay, throughput/latency and peak KV utilization across concurrency. ## Usage Enable the 4-bit KV cache with `--kv-cache-dtype ultraquant_4bit` (D=256, GQA {6,8,16}): vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-MXFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \ --kv-cache-dtype ultraquant_4bit \ --max-model-len 163840 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --trust-remote-code The 4-bit KV cache composes with MXFP4 weights. Decode auto-dispatches to the FlyDSL D=256 kernel (gfx950), otherwise it falls back to Triton unified attention. All accuracy/perf runs use the sampling settings recommended in the model's Hugging Face card (Qwen3.8: `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20`). ## Test Results **Accuracy — GPQA-Diamond, mean over multiple seeds.** UltraQuant is at parity with the fp8 (KV8) baseline — in fact marginally ahead on the mean. The decode kernel is numerically exact, so per-seed differences are sampling variance (the arms trade places seed to seed). | Model | UltraQuant 4-bit (mean) | KV8 fp8 (mean) | |---|---|---| | Qwen3.8 | **93.27%** | 92.42% | | Qwen3.6-27B | **86.87%** | 85.61% | **Performance: throughput–latency Pareto (262K-token requests, MI355X):** Qwen3.8 (GQA-16, TP=8). UQ and KV8 track together at low concurrency; UQ pulls ahead from **C=32** onward. KV8 saturates its cache at **C=38 (100%, evicting)** and throughput collapses, while UQ is still at ~44% cache and keeps scaling. | Concurrency | UQ tok/s | KV8 tok/s | Δ | UQ peak KV | KV8 peak KV | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8 | 193.9 | 199.4 | −2.7% | 8.2% | 14.1% | | 16 | 280.2 | 288.0 | −2.7% | 17.4% | 32.0% | | 32 | 374.0 | 363.1 | +3.0% | 35.1% | 66.3% | | 36 | 398.9 | 299.6 | +33.1% | 39.7% | 82.4% | | 38 | 414.6 | 225.4 | +84.0% | 44.2% | **100.0%** | | 42 | 430.7 | 114.7 | +275% | 45.4% | 99.9% | --- UQ first wins at **C=32 before any eviction** (KV8 only 66% cache), and the gap widens sharply once KV8 hits the eviction wall at C=38. Qwen3.6-27B (GQA-6, TP=2). Same shape; UQ wins even before KV8 evicts at C=42 UQ delivers +9% throughput at lower ITL while KV8 is only ~39% cache. UQ peak KV is ~half of KV8 at every point. | Concurrency | UQ tok/s | KV8 tok/s | Δ | UQ peak KV | KV8 peak KV | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8 | 268.3 | 271.8 | −1.3% | 4.8% | 8.4% | | 16 | 383.3 | 391.4 | −2.1% | 9.7% | 15.2% | | 32 | 519.9 | 529.5 | −1.8% | 17.6% | 32.1% | | 34 | 545.1 | 537.6 | +1.4% | 19.0% | 31.8% | | 42 | 592.0 | 543.1 | +9.0% | 22.6% | 38.7% | ## Notes - Requires a FlyDSL-capable ROCm build (gfx950) for the D=256 decode kernel; falls back to Triton unified attention otherwise. - Benchmark figures were measured across differing vLLM / AITER / FlyDSL bases, so absolute throughput/latency (and the 8-bit baseline) are indicative rather than bit-identical across environments; the accuracy and relative UQ-vs-KV8 trends are the takeaway. ## References [UltraQuant 4bit KV](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20474)

title: [Bugfix] Fix np.float64 leaking into the KV transfer metrics log
author: NickLucche
body:
The KV transfer metrics log line currently shows raw numpy scalar reprs when the stats come from a connector inside a MultiConnector:

```
(APIServer pid=3547631) INFO 09-15 19:44:52 [metrics.py:107] KV Transfer metrics: NixlPullConnector={'Num successful transfers': 8, 'Avg xfer time (ms)': np.float64(2.338), 'P90 xfer time (ms)': 2.772, 'Avg post time (ms)': np.float64(1.111), 'P90 post time (ms)': 1.88, 'Avg MB per transfer': np.float64(25.441), 'Throughput (MB/s)': np.float64(10883.285), 'Avg number of descriptors': np.float64(133.5)}
```

The single-connector path was fine because the log line formats each value with an f-string (`str()`), which renders `np.float64` as a plain number. With a MultiConnector, `reduce()` returns a nested dict and the whole dict gets rendered with `str()`, which formats every value with `repr()` — and numpy 2 renders `repr(np.float64(2.338))` as `np.float64(2.338)`.

The fix is to have the nixl/mooncake/hf3fs `reduce()` implementations return plain Python scalars via `.item()`, which is what their `dict[str, int | float]` annotation already promised. After the fix the same line reads:

```
KV Transfer metrics: NixlPullConnector={'Num successful transfers': 8, 'Avg xfer time (ms)': 2.338, 'P90 xfer time (ms)': 2.772, 'Avg post time (ms)': 1.111, 'P90 post time (ms)': 1.88, 'Avg MB per transfer': 25.441, 'Throughput (MB/s)': 10883.285, 'Avg number of descriptors': 133.5}
```

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] AMD-Quark mixed-precision DeepSeek-V4.1 support
author: xiao-llm
body:
## Purpose

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` does not load today. It is a **mixed-precision** AMD-Quark export — MXFP4 experts, but 226 per-layer attention specs in MXFP8:

| | scheme |
|---|---|
| `global_quant_config` | `fp4` / `per_group` / `group_size=32` / `e8m0` |
| `layer_quant_config` (226 entries) | `fp8_e4m3` / `per_block` / `block_size=[32,32]` / `float8_e8m0fnu` |

Four independent bugs block it. Each one assumes DeepSeek **V4**'s `128x128` block geometry, or the DeepSeek-native scale naming.

| # | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | All 226 per-layer specs silently discarded | Decline mixed-precision Quark exports, let `QuarkConfig` take them |
| 2 | `NotImplementedError: No quark compatible scheme was found.` | New `QuarkW8A8Mxfp8` scheme |
| 3 | Attention shards silently fall back to global MXFP4 | Expose the VL wrapper's mappings as class attributes |
| 4 | Engram scale tensor never routed | Add a `weight_scale$` mapper rule |

### 1. The V4.1 config claims the checkpoint, then throws the specs away

`DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method` accepts any Quark export whose *global* scheme is MXFP4 — this one qualifies. But `from_config` then rewrites the config into a single global FP8 scheme with `weight_block_size = [128, 128]`, discarding all 226 per-layer specs. `get_quant_method` then gates its MXFP8 path on `weight_block_size == [32, 32]`,
which that rewrite has just made unreachable.

**Fix:** a Quark export carrying `layer_quant_config` is mixed precision by definition, so decline it and let `QuarkConfig` handle it.

### 2. QuarkConfig has no scheme for 32×32 per-block FP8

`_is_fp8_w8a8` only accepts per-block FP8 at `[128, 128]` (V4 geometry), and the OCP-MX matchers only accept 1-D `per_group` weights. A 32×32 per-block e8m0 weight matches neither, so dispatch raises.

**Fix:** extend `QuarkOCP_MX` to handle MXFP8 as a first-class OCP-MX dtype. `mxfp8_e4m3` is added to `_WEIGHT_QUANT_KEY_MAP` / `_ACTIVATION_QUANT_KEY_MAP`, a normalizer (`ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows()`) accepts both config dialects, and `QuarkOCP_MX` gains an unpacked MXFP8 branch with 3-way `packed_factor` (`1` for mxfp8, `2` for mxfp4, `8/6` for mxfp6).

The only difference from canonical 1-D MXFP8 is scale layout. MXFP8 carries one e8m0 value per weight *row* per 32-element group; Quark's `block_size=[R, 32]` carries one per *R* rows. The loader expands each scale row:

```python
loaded_weight.view(torch.uint8).repeat_interleave(rows, dim=0)
```

At `R == 1` the two layouts coincide and expansion is a no-op. The kernel is the shared `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel()` — the same one compressed-tensors and INC MXFP8 schemes use. Existing 128×128 per-block FP8 keeps
`QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`, asserted in the new tests.

This also fixes a latent dispatch inconsistency: `get_quant_method()` and `get_quant_method_target()` now agree on MXFP8 layers, since both walk the same `QuarkOCP_MX` matcher chain.

Both MXFP8 config dialects are accepted:

| | Shape A (canonical MX) | Shape B (DeepSeek-V4.1) |
|---|---|---|
| `dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| shape | `qscheme=per_group`, `group_size=32` | `qscheme=per_block`, `block_size=[32,32]` |
| scale | `scale_format="e8m0"` | `scale_type="float8_e8m0fnu"` |
| `scale_block_rows` (R) | 1 | 32 |

### 3. The VL wrapper hides its module mappings from the quant config

`configure_quant_config` reads `hf_to_vllm_mapper` and `packed_modules_mapping` off the **class**, before `__init__` runs.
`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` (vision variant) defined neither at class level, only as instance attributes. So per-layer keys naming `layers.N.attn.wq_a` never matched the runtime `language_model.model.layers.N.attn.wq_a`, and every
attention shard silently fell back to the global MXFP4 spec.

**Fix:** expose both as class attributes, with the prefix rules shared via one module-level constant so they cannot drift.

### 4. The engram scale name

Quark spells it `engram.embed.weight_scale`. The mapper's rules match `\.scale$` — a literal `.scale` suffix — so the rule never fires.

**Fix:** add an explicit `weight_scale$` rule alongside the existing one.

## Scope

ROCm/AMD path only (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`). The `nvidia/` twins have the same shape for items 3 and 4, but this PR deliberately leaves them alone — only the AMD path has been validated on hardware.

## Test Plan

**Quark dispatch tests (`test_quark.py`):**

- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_2d_block` — a 32×32 per-block e8m0 linear dispatches to `QuarkOCP_MX` with `scale_block_rows == 32`; experts still fall through to the global MXFP4 spec; 128×128 per-block FP8 still gets
  `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_canonical` — canonical 1-D per-group MXFP8 (Shape A) dispatches to `QuarkOCP_MX` with `scale_block_rows == 1`; `get_quant_method` / `get_quant_method_target` agree.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_moe_raises` — MXFP8 experts raise `NotImplementedError`.
- `test_quark_override_delegates_to_quark_config` — all `quant_method=="quark"` configs (MXFP4, MXFP8, mixed, etc.) return `None` from  `DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method`, confirming delegation to `QuarkConfig`. Parametrized over V4 and V4.1 model types (10 cases).

**FP8 / DeepSeek-V4.1 tests (`test_fp8.py`):**

- `test_deepseek_v41_declines_mixed_precision_quark_config`
- `test_deepseek_v41_vl_exposes_quant_mappings_on_class`
- `test_deepseek_v41_engram_scale_accepts_quark_name`

## Test Result

**0 new code failures.** 

### End-to-end

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` (48 shards, 475 GB) on 4x MI355X at TP=4: all shards load in 74.5 s, MXFP8 attention resolves to `QuarkOCP_MX` via the `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`, and the model is coherent.

GSM8K accuracy (1319 problems, greedy, seed=42, 8-shot)
| Config | flexible-extract | strict-match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MXFP4 | 92.34% ± 0.73 | 92.42% ± 0.73 |
| Base FP8 | 92.87% ± 0.71 | 92.95% ± 0.71 |

Hardware: 4x MI355X (gfx950/CDNA4), TP=4.

title: [ROCm][CI] Enable AITER FP8/unquantized cases in modular-kernel sweep + fix MoRI per-tensor FP8 dispatch
author: divakar-amd
body:
This is step 1 ("FP8/unquantized case identification") of the plan in #54966; the MXFP4 config/weight-conversion work needs gfx950 hardware and will follow separately.

### What

`AiterExperts` in the modular-kernel combinations sweep (`tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`) was only reachable indirectly through the general quant-config cross-product, with no assertion that the exercised `(weight_key, activation_key)` pair is one it actually declares supported. The harness also hardcoded `torch.float8_e4m3fn` everywhere, which on FNUZ FP8 platforms (gfx94x / MI300):

- unconditionally skipped this whole test file (`current_platform.is_fp8_fnuz()` module-level guard), so none of these cases had ever run on MI300/MI200-class hardware
- registered `AiterExperts` under `fp8_types` only, silently excluding the fully-unquantized `(None, None)` scheme it also supports

### Changes

- `mk_objects.py` / `common.py`: use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` / `is_fp8()` instead of the hardcoded `torch.float8_e4m3fn` literal (no-op on CUDA/gfx950, where `fp8_dtype()` returns the same literal); register `AiterExperts` under `common_float_types` (was `fp8_types`) so `(None, None)` is actually generated.
- `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: drop the module-level FNUZ skip; add `assert_aiter_quant_scheme_case()` to make the exercised `(weight_key, activation_key)` pair explicit and assert `AiterExperts._supports_quant_scheme()` agrees — gated on `fused_experts_type.__name__ == "AiterExperts"`, so no other backend is affected.

### Additional Fix: MoRI Missing Per-Tensor FP8 Dispatch

Broadening quant-config coverage also exposed a real bug (distinct from #57029): `MoriPrepareAndFinalize.prepare()` only quantized activations for block-quantized/per-token FP8, so per-tensor FP8 configs fell through to unquantized dispatch while weights stayed FP8, which surfaced downstream as a misleading `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4b8` Triton assertion.
Fixed in: (a.) `all2all_utils.py`: extend `use_fp8_dispatch`/`scale_dim` to `is_per_tensor` (b,) `mori.py`: add the per-tensor quant branch, broadcasting the scalar scale to `[num_tokens, 1]` since MoRI's dispatch reads scales via a raw pointer
Fixes: 
`test_modular_kernel_combinations_multigpu[... quant_config15-MoriPrepareAndFinalize-TritonExperts-2]`

### Pre-existing bug surfaced

Running on MI300 (gfx942) for the first time (previously skipped at module-level) reproduced a deterministic HIP `illegal memory access` for every `AiterExperts` × `{DeepEPHTPrepareAndFinalize, MoriPrepareAndFinalize}` combination at `world_size=2`, including the plain unquantized case. Filed as #57029 with a full repro; this PR adds a scoped skip referencing it so CI doesn't regress on this newly-exercised combination. Not fixed here.

### Test plan

On MI300 (gfx942, FNUZ FP8), 
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -sv tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py
```
All 6 target `(weight_key, activation_key)` pairs from #54966 (5 FP8 + `(None, None)`) verified individually, each triggering the new assertion. Confirmed the FNUZ-skip removal doesn't affect CUDA/gfx950, and that the DeepEP-HT/Mori skip actually suppresses the crash (ran that node id before/after).

### AI assistance disclosure

Portions of this change (diagnosis, harness edits, and the new AITER test infra) were developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). All changes were reviewed and the tests above were run and verified by me on MI300 hardware.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][PD] Align region-mapped pulls across logical block sizes
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

Fix a NIXL pull that can silently load the wrong prompt pages when P and D allocate KV differently. The motivating setup has **plain NIXL on P and NIXL + HiSparse on D**, with **`--block-size 128` on both servers**.

The same command-line block size does not guarantee the same allocation. A logical block is the unit the scheduler allocates; a physical page is the unit used by the attention kernel and transfer. With a kernel that requires 64-token pages, plain P can keep 128-token logical blocks and split each into two physical pages. HiSparse's setup on D resolves its MLA scheduler blocks to the native 64-token size directly. That produces this geometry in the affected path:

| | Command-line block size | Scheduler's logical block | Physical/kernel page |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P: plain NIXL, HiSparse disabled | 128 | 128 | 64 |
| D: NIXL + HiSparse | 128 | 64 | 64 |

For a **160-token prompt**, P must allocate two logical blocks: capacity for 256 tokens, or **four physical pages**. D needs only **three physical pages**. Let `A` and `B` each hold 64 tokens, and `C` hold the remaining 32:

```text
P advertises:       [ A | B | C | unused ]
D has space for:    [   |   |   ]

Current selection:  [ B | C | unused ]  <- last three producer pages
Correct selection:  [ A | B | C ]
```

Logical-to-physical expansion already happens. The mistake comes afterward: the region-based suffix matcher assumes that any extra pages on P represent a prefix D has already cached. Here the extra page is unused capacity at the end, so that assumption shifts the whole transfer. If D has actually cached `A`, the remaining transfer should select `B, C`; the old logic selects `C, unused`.

**The fix selects pages by token position.** Pass the producer's existing `remote_num_tokens` through to the worker, combine it with each destination group's cached-prefix offset, and select the corresponding physical pages. Whole-page transfers remain: `C` is transferred with its unused rows, but the entirely unused fourth page does not shift the selection. This adds no prefill on D.

**HiSparse also exposes a separate assumption at transfer completion.** P can keep main KV and indexer KV in one merged cache group. D separates host KV and GPU indexer KV into different groups, so NIXL uses *regions* to match the corresponding memory buffers. The old `get_transfer_results()` still pairs groups by position. Looking up P's group 1 for D's group 1 can fail because P has only group 0, or pair the wrong blocks when the index exists.

Completion now uses the region read plan. The worker records `region_blocks_to_zero`: whole destination pages that were allocated but excluded from the read. For example, in the reverse allocation geometry, D may reserve four pages while P supplies three:

```text
D after the read:   [ A | B | C | untouched ]
D after completion:[ A | B | C | zeroed    ]
```

For two example regions with destination IDs `[10, 11, 12, 13]` and `[20, 21, 22, 23]`, receiving three pages into each produces a cleanup plan of `[[13], [23]]`. Completion clears page 13 only in its region and page 23 only in its region, then skips the old positional group processing.

This plan is local to one request on the receiving worker. `None` means use the existing completion path; empty per-region lists mean a region-mapped read with nothing to zero. In the original P-four-pages/D-three-pages example, D receives all its pages, so there is **no zeroing**. The plan does not include cached prefix pages or unused rows within the transferred partial page. It is discarded with the request's receive metadata; failed reads skip this cleanup.

Scope: pure MLA region pulls with equal physical page sizes, DCP=1, and one cache-group owner per region. Heterogeneous logical geometry without the required metadata or with shared-group regions is rejected. Existing homogeneous fallback behavior remains.

**Dependency:** the empty-receive fixes belong to #57049 (also present in #56946, originally from #55398). They are excluded from this PR, which will be rebased after that prerequisite lands. #57049's HiSparse tail-import policy remains separate from this transfer-alignment fix.

Duplicate checks included related issue #57019, its comments, and open PR searches for that issue, NIXL logical/physical geometry, and region padding. #57027 fixes layer binding offsets. #55374 introduces broader piecewise token-window loading in the ordinary group-based pull/push paths; its current diff does not wire that through the region-based path introduced by #53780. This PR addresses that region path without adding the piecewise-loading API.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, and validation. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the changed lines and validating the patched GPU deployment. GPU accuracy validation remains pending.


## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -m cpu_test -q

uv run --no-project pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/metadata.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py
```

GPU follow-up: apply this fix alongside #57049 and #57027, restore block size 128, and repeat the same 100-question GSM8K sample with the same model, prompt/scoring settings, and concurrency 10. A full matched evaluation remains pending.

## Test Result

- CPU suite: **91 passed, 1 deselected**. Includes real receive-path page expansion and descriptor selection with transport mocked, producer/consumer padding, unequal per-region cache hits, and completion zeroing across strided layer views.
- Negative control: restoring main's mapping methods in memory makes the 160-token regression fail on the source descriptors: `[21, 22, 23, 121, 122, 123]` versus `[20, 21, 22, 120, 121, 122]`.

title: [Benchmark] Retire stale benchmarks and consolidate RMSNorm
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Retire the legacy CUTLASS benchmark directory and its stale pickle-import exceptions, remove the hashing profiler that still searches for the removed `hash_of_block` function, and consolidate plain/residual RMSNorm benchmarking in the IR harness.

The standalone RMSNorm script is replaced by the shared shape grid for `rms_norm` and `fused_add_rms_norm`; `--ops rms_norm` selects both. This uses the registered IR providers and retires the standalone FlashInfer comparison. Overall: 3 added lines, 780 removed.

Duplicate check: no open PR addresses these removals or consolidation. Searched `cutlass_benchmarks`, `benchmark_hashing`, and `benchmark_rmsnorm`; #44381 concerns CUDA launch checks and only references the old script in its test plan.

AI assistance was used for this change and validation.

## Test Plan

- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files benchmarks/kernels/ir/shapes.py tools/pre_commit/check_forbidden_imports.py`
- `git diff --check`
- `chg run -g=1 --timeout 10m -- .venv/bin/python /tmp/vllm_rmsnorm_ir_smoke.py`

## Test Result

All checks passed. On one reserved NVIDIA B300, the smoke script checked native and vLLM implementations for both operations using FP16/BF16/FP32, 1/64 tokens, and hidden size 4096: 24 correctness checks passed. Both eager and CUDA-graph benchmark runs generated valid timing CSVs. No remaining references to the removed scripts were found.

Model evaluation: not applicable; this changes benchmark scripts and lint exceptions only.

<details>
<summary>RMSNorm smoke script (save to /tmp/vllm_rmsnorm_ir_smoke.py and run from the repository root)</summary>

```python
import csv
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))

import torch

from benchmarks.kernels.ir import bench_ir_ops as bench
from tests.ir.ir_test_utils import assert_close, clone_args

torch.manual_seed(0)
torch.set_default_device("cuda")
print(f"Device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name()}", flush=True)

for name in ("rms_norm", "fused_add_rms_norm"):
    cases = [
        case
        for case in bench.SHAPE_CONFIGS[name]
        if case["num_tokens"] in (1, 64) and case["hidden_size"] == 4096
    ]
    assert len(cases) == 6
    bench.SHAPE_CONFIGS[name] = cases
    op = bench.IrOp.registry[name]
    checks = 0
    for case in cases:
        args = op.generate_inputs(**case)
        expected = op.impls["native"].impl_fn(*clone_args(args))
        for impl in op.impls.values():
            if impl.supported and impl.supports_args(*args):
                assert_close(op, impl.impl_fn(*clone_args(args)), expected)
                checks += 1
    print(f"{name}: {checks} correctness checks passed", flush=True)

for mode in ("graph", "eager"):
    output_dir = Path(f"/tmp/vllm-rmsnorm-ir-smoke-{mode}")
    sys.argv = [
        "bench_ir_ops.py", "--ops", "rms_norm", "--warmup", "5", "--rep", "10",
        "--save-path", str(output_dir),
    ]
    if mode == "eager":
        sys.argv.append("--no-cuda-graph")
    bench.main()
    for name in ("rms_norm", "fused_add_rms_norm"):
        with (output_dir / f"{name}_detail.csv").open() as f:
            rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
        assert len(rows) == 6
        for row in rows:
            for field in ("native (us)", "vllm_c (us)"):
                assert math.isfinite(float(row[field])) and float(row[field]) > 0
    print(f"{mode}: both RMSNorm operations produced valid timing CSVs", flush=True)
```

</details>

title: [Bugfix] Make online FP8 MoE experts batch-invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
author: ybwbqg9379
body:
Fixes #57016

## Purpose

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a MoE model served with `--quantization fp8` (online per-tensor FP8, Triton experts) still produces output that depends on which other requests share its batch: greedy tokens flip within the first ~10 positions and prefix-cached K/V differs depending on who wrote it. Dense layers are invariant; only the experts are not.

Two things were wrong:

1. `Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod` (and `Fp8MoEMethod` for FP8-serialized per-tensor checkpoints with dynamic activations) quantize the expert inputs with one dynamic scale over the whole activation tensor (`kFp8DynamicTensorSym`), i.e. the max over every token of every co-batched request. Under batch-invariant mode this PR selects `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` and passes `per_act_token_quant=True`, mirroring what `Fp8LinearMethod` already does for dense layers.
2. Switching to per-token activations exposed a latent launcher bug: `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` passed `stride_bse=0` for 1-D `[E]` weight scales (and `stride_bsn=1` for the singleton dim of `[E, 1, 1]`), so the kernel's `per_channel_quant` branch read expert 0's scale for every expert or indexed past the buffer. The combination tests already skipped "per-tensor weights + per-token activations" for the Triton experts as NYI, although `TritonExperts._supports_quant_scheme` advertises the pair. This PR passes the expert stride unconditionally and broadcasts singleton scale dims, and narrows the NYI gate to the still-unsupported "per-channel weights + per-tensor activations" case so the combination suite covers the fixed pair.

The bf16 Triton expert path is already invariant on `main` (`get_default_config`/`get_moe_configs` pin the tile config under the flag); the reporter's bf16 mismatch was on 0.27.1.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_online_fp8_moe_logprobs_bitwise_bs1_vs_bsN` (granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct, `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`, greedy, BS=1 vs BS=8 bitwise tokens+logprobs). Fails on `main`, passes with this PR.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: the per-tensor-weight + per-token-activation FP8 config is no longer skipped for `TritonExperts` / `BatchedTritonExperts` / `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts`.
- Reporter's reproducer (co-batch and writer-suffix modes) against a running server.
- Kernel check: `fused_experts` vs `tests.kernels.utils.torch_experts`, E=32, N=1024, K=2048, M=128, topk=4, per-tensor `[E,1,1]` weight scales: max abs err 0.010 with per-tensor activations, 0.003 with per-token activations (before the launcher fix the per-token case returned values in the thousands).
- Existing suites: `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py::test_fused_moe`, pre-commit, `mypy-3.12`.

Hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), WSL2, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The modular kernel combination suite itself does not run on this WSL2 machine (spawned worker fails with `CUDA error: invalid resource handle` on unmodified `main` too), so that part relies on CI and on the independent H20 run linked below.

## Test Result

- Reporter's probe, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 --quantization fp8`, before: A-alone vs A-with-B first token flip at 11 (logprob gap 0.166), warm-vs-cold flip at 11 (gap 0.347). After: every comparison identical, both rounds.
- gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` (tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py): default (no flag) 34.1%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on `main` 34.3%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with this PR 32.7%. Per-token activation quantization is strictly finer than per-tensor, and the kernel-level error is lower, so the small delta is sampling noise from a 1B model.
- New e2e test: PASS with the PR, FAIL on `main` ("logprobs are not bitwise equal between BS=1 and BS=8; max abs diff 2.2e-01").
- Independent cross-architecture validation by @CarrotSwordsman on H20 (sm_90, real Linux GPU, driver 535), [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57092#issuecomment-5730213177): the same e2e test FAILS on a clean 0.28.0+cu129 wheel (max abs diff 2.8e-01) and PASSES with this PR's files applied, reproducing and eliminating the #57016 symptom on Hopper. Their `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` run on the patched wheel was 8 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped, the two failures being `deep_gemm`'s `NVCC >= 12.3` assert in a container pinned to 12.1. As they note, that suite does not discriminate against a release wheel (the pre-PR NYI skip is not present there to be removed), so the e2e pair is the evidence in that setup.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` (non-DeepGEMM): 164 passed, 20 skipped. `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k test_fused_moe`: 241 passed. pre-commit and `mypy-3.12` clean on all changed files.

> Note: since #53585, online per-tensor FP8 is selected with `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`; commands above that use `--quantization fp8` predate that change.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #57016 (checked with `gh pr list --search "57016 in:body"` and by searching open PRs for "batch invariant moe"); #55881 is the XPU MoE variant and does not touch the CUDA Triton path or FP8 activation quantization.

title: [Perf][EPD] Batch image requests per encoder
author: gty111
body:
## Summary

Batch **proxy-to-encoder HTTP requests**: instead of sending one request per image, the proxy groups images from the same user request assigned to the same E instance into a single multi-image request. Per-image round-robin assignment and parallel requests to different E instances are preserved. Audio/video remain unbatched; no new configuration is added.

Return item positions in EC metadata so the proxy can map each result back to the original image, including repeated images and processing-derived hashes. This changes request fan-out in the proxy, not encoder compute batching; no scheduler or model-runner changes.

## Results

Same-node A/B: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B BF16, 4E+4PD on two GB200 nodes, Mooncake RDMA, MRv2, concurrency 96, CUDA graphs up to 16384 tokens, no eager. Each arm: 200 warmup requests, then 2 × 1200 MUIRBench requests with structured choice.

| Metric | Baseline | Batched | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean throughput | 90.22 req/s | 96.34 req/s | +6.8% |
| Mean latency | 1035.7 ms | 975.2 ms | -5.8% |
| P99 latency | 3036.0 ms | 2862.8 ms | -5.7% |
| Accuracy | 58.92% | 59.33% | +0.42 pp |

E subrequests per round: 4924 → 3878 (-21.2%). All requests succeeded without proxy retries. No accuracy regression observed; this is a two-round comparison, not a claim of improved model accuracy. Both arms use the same worker metadata addition and differ only in the proxy.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/{test_epd_proxy_retry,test_epd_proxy_round_robin,test_ec_example_connector}.py -q
```

58 passed; pre-commit passed. Covers repeated images, derived hashes, raw-media mode, metadata ordering and HTTP retries.

Checked #52409 and open PRs for encoder batching/fan-out; no duplicate found. #54176 concerns dynamic registration, not request batching.

AI assistance was used. Draft pending human review.

title: [Perf] Optimize Molmo2 pooling preparation
author: Levius-Fubuki
body:
### Purpose

Molmo2 pooling currently materializes a tiled batch-index tensor and uses
multi-dimensional advanced indexing before masking invalid patches and reducing
the attention query.

This change keeps the implementation in native PyTorch while reducing that
overhead. It flattens the batch-local patch indices into global row indices,
uses `torch.index_select` for the gather, masks invalid entries in place, and
performs the existing sum/mean query reduction without changing the subsequent
attention, projection, or token filtering behavior.

No Triton kernel or custom-op dispatch is added, so there is no extra JIT
startup cost or platform-specific fallback path.

### Tests and validation

Pooling coverage is consolidated into the existing
`tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_molmo2.py` suite. Two parametrized
cases exercise `Molmo2VisionBackbone.forward` with lightweight substitutes
for the encoder and learned layers, checking masked and ordinary means,
partially/all-invalid groups, repeated indices, cross-batch indexing, attention
masks, and invalid-group filtering against explicit expected values.

The standalone 228-line pooling test file and benchmark script have been
removed. The pooling implementation is unchanged by this review follow-up.

Agent-run on macOS 15.1 ARM64, Python 3.12.13 and PyTorch 2.14.0, from the
PR worktree using the parent checkout's virtual environment:

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 ../../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_molmo2.py
# 7 passed; one existing warning about missing vllm._version

../../.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_molmo2.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/molmo2.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy

git diff --check
# Passed
```

The suite uses the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker because these CPU
unit tests do not initialize distributed or accelerator state. Without it,
the existing processing tests triggered a macOS/PyTorch
`empty_host_cache` teardown crash in the local environment.

### RTX 4090 Microbenchmark (historical)

The script is preserved at [the pre-follow-up commit](https://github.com/Levius-Fubuki/vllm/blob/e26ed1564398652949f446d78fa252eac26b40a2/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_molmo2_pooling.py); the command below refers to that version. These measurements were not rerun for this test-only follow-up.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_molmo2_pooling.py \
  --batch-sizes 1 2 \
  --dtypes float16 bfloat16 \
  --warmup 50 --repeats 200 --trials 10
```

Hardware/software: NVIDIA RTX 4090, PyTorch 2.12.1+cu130, Triton 3.7.1.

The benchmark compares the exact upstream native preparation path against the
optimized native helper. Across 24 image/video rows, every measured case
improved. The geometric-mean speedup was 1.29x, with a range of 1.06x--1.50x.

| B | kind | dtype | groups | Upstream median / IQR (us) | Optimized median / IQR (us) | Speedup |
|---:|:---|:---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | image K=4 | FP16 | 550 | 165.55 / 0.17 | 118.42 / 0.34 | 1.40x |
| 1 | video K=9 | FP16 | 256 | 175.82 / 13.33 | 117.49 / 0.82 | 1.50x |
| 1 | video K=9 | BF16 | 4096 | 991.10 / 0.44 | 927.38 / 0.53 | 1.07x |
| 2 | video K=9 | FP16 | 4096 | 1954.28 / 5.32 | 1830.80 / 0.18 | 1.07x |


### Limitations

The performance measurements isolate pooling preparation rather than full-model
end-to-end latency. This follow-up was validated against the PR source with local
Python dependencies and no built vLLM native extensions. CUDA tests, full-model
evaluation and benchmarks were not rerun; GPU evidence above is historical.
The new validation results are agent-run, not human-run.

### AI assistance

AI assistance was used during implementation, testing, benchmarking, review,
and PR drafting. I reviewed and take responsibility for the change and
evidence.

title: [Perf][MRV2] Share token-to-request mappings across KV cache groups
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

`build_attn_metadata()` creates one `CommonAttentionMetadata` per KV cache group, and each group lazily launches its own token-to-request mapping kernel — even though every group in the same call sees identical query boundaries and token padding. A DeepSeek V4.1 spec-decode trace shows 6 mapping launches in target prep and 3 in draft prep per step, all computing the same mapping.

## Change

Share one mapping across KV cache groups within a single `build_attn_metadata()` call (+3 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py`):

- A per-call local cache is threaded through each group's `CommonAttentionMetadata` (`_token_to_req_indices_cache`).
- The first group that needs the mapping builds it into its existing persistent buffer; later groups reuse that tensor instead of launching the kernel again.
- The cache lives only for the duration of one call, so target/draft prep stay isolated and each step recomputes from fresh inputs — no cross-step state, safe under CUDA-graph replay.

Builds on merged #56562 (Triton mapping kernel) by removing repeat launches across groups. Dup checks: searched open PRs for `token_to_req_indices`, `"metadata" "KV" "share"`, `56562 in:body` — none. Related but distinct: #56996, #41834.

## Test Plan

GB200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py
git diff --check
```

## Test Result

- 30 passed, 1 failed — the failure (`test_indexer_builder_deepseek_v4_compressed_slot_mapping_uses_num_states`) needs access to the gated HF repo `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` (401 in this environment); unrelated to this change.
- Mapping launches: target **6 → 1**, draft **3 → 1**; total kernel launches 30 → 25 and 12 → 10

### Metadata-builder benchmark

The benchmark calls the real SWA, MLA, indexer, and compressor builders through `build_attn_metadata()`, approximating the trace's launch pattern: target prep uses six KV groups with six query tokens per request, draft prep three noncausal SWA groups with five; context 8,192, SWA window 128, block size 128, persistent token capacity 16,384.

Measured quantity is **host wall time per `build_attn_metadata()` call** (builder Python + kernel submission; input prep and compilation excluded). 100 warmup calls, then 12 rounds × 200 calls alternating baseline/candidate; medians of per-round averages, no profiler, GC disabled during timing, GPU clocks not locked.

| Batch | Builder suite | Before (µs) | After (µs) | Saved (µs) | Reduction |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Target | 1261.14 | 1120.84 | 140.30 | 11.12% |
| 1 | Draft | 484.71 | 425.06 | 59.66 | 12.31% |
| 16 | Target | 1237.62 | 1100.57 | 137.05 | 11.07% |
| 16 | Draft | 469.18 | 415.60 | 53.57 | 11.42% |
| 128 | Target | 1242.93 | 1102.52 | 140.41 | 11.30% |
| 128 | Draft | 482.71 | 426.00 | 56.72 | 11.75% |

At batch 1 the target+draft host medians sum to **1.746 → 1.546 ms**, i.e. **0.20 ms saved per step** of metadata building. GPU-side span (CUPTI, CUDA-graph replay, cold L2, median of 4×100 replays): target 66.7 → 58.0 µs, draft 27.7 → 24.1 µs.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex implemented the change and ran the reported checks under the submitter's direction; human review of every changed line and human-run validation remain required.

title: [BugFix][KV Connector] Fix Deadlock with KVConnector + MTP under KV Pressure
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
## Purpose

Scheduler can deadlock under KV memory pressure with MTP + KV connector --- encountered in production deployment of GLM5.2

### Example

- 2 requests A (needs 4 blocks + 1 for mtp), B (needs 3 blocks + 1 for mtp)
- Total blocks 7

#### Step 1 — A and B arrive and get added to `skipped_waiting` queue

A is admitted (4 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`
B is admitted (3 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`

- result: 
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

#### Step 2 — A's transfer lands. 

Schedule the `skipped_waiting` queue first. Peek `skipped_waiting` → A.

`_is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS)` is True → `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request(A)` succeeds → `A.status=WAITING` 

Then, schedule A. Need to allocate for the MTP blocks [these are only allocated after async load]. We need 1 block, but there is 0 left. `allocate_slots` returns None and we `break` (end attempting to schedule.

- result:
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

As we can see, the queues are in the same state as before this step, and will continue to be in this state (trying to schedule A, asking to allocate blocks) forever.

#### Step 3 onward — Same cycle

Peek `skipped_waiting` → still A, now status WAITING. _is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING) is False, so no promotion branch; straight to allocation; fails; break. Spin forever.

## Root Cause

Async KV load is allocated without lookahead slots (see `limit_lookahead_tokens`), and `_request_remaining_blocks()` -- which backs the `_inflight_prefill_reserved_blocks()` admission gate -- does not count them either. 

Then, after the `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV` is done, we ask `allocate_slots()` for the lookahead margin on top ---> if this block is not available, we `break` --- with this request at the front of the `skipped_waiting` queue. If no requests are running, then no new blocks come free and we deadlock in this loop

**So there is a mismatch in the blocks reserved and what is actually needed to start running**

## Test Plan

- unit test
- reproducer (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57104#issuecomment-5701283900)

## Test Result

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Avoid triton recompiles in the acceptance estimator
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
## Context
Triton keys its compilation cache on whether each int scalar is 1 and whether it is 16-divisible, so the number of tokens/reqs args re-key as the batch size changes at runtime, causing stalls.

## Summary

| kernel | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `_accumulate_kernel` | 14 | 1 |
| `_local_max_sumexp_kernel` | 3 | 1 |

title: [Bugfix][ModelLoader] Make enable_weights_track check quantized layers
author: siliangchen-amd
body:
## Purpose

`enable_weights_track` is meant to catch weights a checkpoint did not provide, but it exempts every parameter of any layer whose quant method defines `process_weights_after_loading`. `QuantizeMethodBase` defines it, so that is every linear, MoE and embedding layer, quantized or not. On a quantized model the opt-in check therefore never fires: a block-FP8 checkpoint missing a `weight_scale_inv` loads and serves garbage.

- For quantized models, where the flag is opt-in, only KV-cache quantization parameters, empty placeholders, fbgemm_fp8's config-built `input_scale_ub` and online-quantization parameters stay exempt. The check now also reaches the model's unquantized layers, such as a vision tower. Unquantized models, where the check is on by default, are unchanged.
- `MoERunner.load_weights` now prefixes `routed_experts.`, so the names it returns match the registered parameters; otherwise every expert weight is reported as missing once the check is on.

## Related PRs

- #41086 added `enable_weights_track` together with the module-wide exemption narrowed here.
- #35074 tracked quantized models by default and was reverted the same day (#35309); the false positives reported against it (#35299, #35305) were GPTQ/AWQ MoE `g_idx` parameters, which vLLM no longer registers. Here quantized models stay opt-in; the KV-cache exemption follows #35074 and the empty-placeholder one #35299.
- #34930 (open) tracks quantized models by default with a warning and keeps the current exemption. It changes when the check runs, this PR what it checks; both edit `track_weights_loading`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py`: three new cases, each failing if its part of the change is reverted. They run in CI's Model Executor job.
- Load one checkpoint or more per quantization format with `--model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_weights_track": true}'`, intact and with one tensor removed.

## Test Result

All with the flag on.

End to end on MI325X, DeepSeek on 8x MI300X; measured on earlier revisions of this PR, which exempted fewer parameters, the intact checkpoints on vLLM 0.27.1 with the change applied.

| checkpoint | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 repack, `attn.wo_a` block scale missing in all 43 layers | boots, serves, gsm8k 0.00 | refuses to load, names the 43 `wo_a.weight_scale_inv` |
| same repack with `wo_a` in `ignored_layers` (its correct config) | boots | boots, gsm8k 1.00 (50 samples) |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 with one `weight_scale_inv` removed | boots, outputs garbage | refuses to load, names that parameter |
| intact: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8, Qwen3-14B-FP8, gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4), Qwen3-30B-A3B (bf16) | boots | boots |

Load check on main with this PR on MI300X, running vLLM's loader up to and including the check, with no inference. Every checkpoint below loads intact. With the listed tensor removed from a `down_proj` or `o_proj`, unless named otherwise, the load is refused and names exactly that parameter; main accepts all of them. Main checks 11–28% of these checkpoints' parameters and this PR 63–100%; the rest are KV-cache quantization parameters, empty placeholders and fbgemm's `input_scale_ub`.

| format | checkpoints | tensor removed |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 (block), Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct-FP8 (static), Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-KV | `weight_scale_inv`, `input_scale` |
| compressed-tensors | Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct FP8-dynamic and W8A8, Qwen3-0.6B W4A16, Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8-dynamic and AWQ-4bit (MoE) | `weight_scale`, `weight_packed` |
| AWQ, GPTQ | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct AWQ and GPTQ-Int4, Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 (MoE) | `qweight` |
| ModelOpt, Quark | Qwen3-8B-FP8 (ModelOpt), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct PTPC (Quark) | `input_scale`, `weight_scale` |
| fbgemm_fp8 | Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct FBGEMM | `weight_scale` |
| vision-language | Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-FP8, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct FP8-dynamic | a weight scale; vision-tower `attn.proj.bias` |
| MTP draft | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 | `o_proj.weight_scale_inv`; `fc.weight`; `lm_head.weight` |

Online fp8 on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct loads and stays exempt. A missing shard of a fused parameter (one of q/k/v or gate/up, or one expert) is still not detected, as on main, because the fused parameter is reported loaded.

`test_registry.py`: 9 passed. `models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_mla` and `lora/test_sequence_classification.py`, which failed in this PR's first CI run, pass locally.

AI-assisted (Claude); I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom) while optimizing DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix MLA RoPE fused-kernel tests for TheRock image
author: mawong-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
The `Core Operations Kernels` test group fails on TheRock image (see [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12914/list?sid=01a09eed-c3fc-4155-8ae7-ad55792cdc2c&open=false)). This has been root-caused to the Triton 3.8 upgrade.
Specifically, in the computation of RoPE, we compute terms similar to  `x * cos - y * sin`. In Triton 3.7, the LLVM backend lowers to `FMA_F16(x, cos, MUL_F16(-y, sin))`, which is the same as the HIP reference fused kernel. However, in Triton 3.8, the LLVM backend instead lowers to `FMA_F16(-y, sin, MUL_F16(x, cos))`.
In short, the LLVM backend makes a different choice for which product to pre-round to F16 in the fused multiply-add. This pre-rounding can lead to a 1 ULP difference (wrt the product) compared to a hypothetical reference which does all the arithmetic in FP32 before rounding to F16 once at the end.
Thus, the 2 choices of which product to pre-round can lead to differ by up to 2 ULP wrt `max(abs(x * cos), abs(-y * sin))`. The current tolerances do not adequately capture the subtleties in this regime, which is partly why the tolerances for this test have been adjusted at least 3 separate times (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51083, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46409, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32408).

## Purpose
This PR reworks and unifies the tolerances for this test for half-precision dtypes on ROCm.
Specifically, for the non-RoPE portions of the tensors, we compare to the references using default `atol` and `rtol`. For the RoPE portions of the tensors, we now have a 2 part test:

1. Compare to the references using default `atol` and `rtol`. The number of failing elements must not exceed 0.01 (for bf16) or 0.0001 (for fp16) of all elements.
2. For all failing elements, check that they differ from the reference elements by up to 2 ULP wrt the relevant products (e.g. `max(abs(x * cos), abs(-y * sin), abs(-x * sin), abs(y * cos))` for non-Neox-style RoPE).

## Test Plan
For ROCm 10:
Run the Core Operations Kernels test group on AMD CI [with this fix](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002/list) applied vs [without this fix](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13000/list).

For ROCm 7.2:
Run the Core Operations Kernels test group as part of CI on this PR.

## Test Result
The Core Operations Kernels test group is fixed on ROCm 10, and there are no test regressions on both ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10.

- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
