title: [CI] Split LM Eval TurboQuant KV Cache into per-config jobs
author: Thangnguyenvn98
body:
## What

`LM Eval TurboQuant KV Cache` runs four GSM8K accuracy evals — one per kv-cache-dtype config — serially in a single H200 MIG job measuring 39–51m of pytest against a 55m timeout. This replaces it with four content-named jobs, one config each, so the timeline and job names say exactly what ran. Same per-config split as the merged `(H200) LM Eval Large Models` change (#57965).

## Old

```text
tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/
└── models-turboquant.txt        # 4 configs, one job: 39–51m pytest, timeout 55m
```

## New

```text
lm-eval-turboquant-k8v4    (H200 MIG 18GB) LM Eval TurboQuant k8v4    models-turboquant-k8v4.txt
lm-eval-turboquant-t4nc    (H200 MIG 18GB) LM Eval TurboQuant t4nc    models-turboquant-t4nc.txt
lm-eval-turboquant-k3v4nc  (H200 MIG 18GB) LM Eval TurboQuant k3v4nc  models-turboquant-k3v4nc.txt
lm-eval-turboquant-t3nc    (H200 MIG 18GB) LM Eval TurboQuant t3nc    models-turboquant-t3nc.txt
```

Old → new key: `lm-eval-turboquant-kv-cache` → the four `lm-eval-turboquant-*` keys. `models-turboquant.txt` is removed; the four YAML configs are untouched, each in exactly one list. Timeout drops 55 → 30 (~1.7× the slowest measured config).

## Notes

- **Same cases, unchanged configs.** The four `Qwen3-4B-TQ-*.yaml` configs are not modified; coverage is 4/4 configs exactly once, verified locally. `models-turboquant.txt`'s only CI consumer was this job.
- **Per-config jobs over `parallelism: 4`.** An earlier revision of this PR used shard-N list files; revised to named per-config jobs to match #57965 — timeline-readable names and per-config flake isolation (retrying one config no longer re-runs the other three), at the cost of four block/job entries instead of one job with replicas.
- **Resource note:** the four MIG jobs can run concurrently; each still fits a single MIG slice.
- No AMD mirror exists on this step and `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` is untouched; only the TurboQuant lane changes.

## Validation

Scoped build [#89258](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89258) measured the four configs individually (12.4–15.9m pytest, 14.4–17.2m wall each, all green) — those per-config durations carry over unchanged since the configs and commands are identical; only the job boundary moved. A fresh scoped build on the revised head is linked in the comments.

Checks run locally: `yaml.safe_load` on the edited pipeline YAML; a script verifying each list file resolves to an existing config and that the four TurboQuant configs are claimed exactly once (matching the old `models-turboquant.txt`); no remaining references to the old key or list file. `pytest --collect-only` is not runnable locally (no GPU/torch env); the scoped build exercises all four jobs.

## Contribution checklist

- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this job or these configs (searched `turboquant`, `lm eval shard`, and this branch name).
- This change is AI-assisted (noted per the contribution policy); commit trailers carry the attribution.

title: [Perf][GDN] Scatter mixed speculative outputs into the caller buffer
author: tripathiarpan20
body:
## Purpose

Mixed speculative/non-speculative Qwen GDN batches currently allocate `merged_out`, scatter both output partitions into it, and copy the complete tensor into `core_attn_out`. This change scatters directly into the caller's buffer, removing one output-sized allocation and the final full-output copy while preserving token order, buffer aliases, and padding rows.

The opportunity was identified while reviewing a submission to a [Pareton AI inference-optimization campaign](https://www.pareton.ai/dashboard/campaigns/7e0462e4-5806-44ac-9f5b-af0542a4bb86). [Pareton AI](https://github.com/Pareton-ai/pareton/blob/main/README.md) evaluates inference patches against pinned vLLM baselines, using reproducible builds and the same sampled workload for contenders within each round. This PR extracts a small, generally applicable improvement from that work for upstream review. Campaign-level results are not presented as measurements of this isolated change.

Co-authored with @xavierlyu and @Danbog32.

### Change

- Write speculative and non-speculative outputs into `core_attn_out` with two `index_copy_` operations along the token dimension.
- Remove the temporary merge allocation and subsequent copy.

Recurrent computation and state updates are unchanged. The optimization applies when speculative and non-speculative outputs coexist; it does not improve paths that bypass this merge. The allocation removed contains `num_actual_tokens × value_heads × value_head_dim` elements.

### Related work

Open-PR searches and diff inspection on September 16, 2026 found no matching change:

- [#57039](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57039) reuses FlashInfer prefill output buffers for non-speculative batches; its diff retains the mixed speculative merge changed here.
- [#54612](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54612) and [#55260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55260) optimize packed QKV, metadata, and projections without removing this temporary.
- [#50233](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50233) overlaps non-speculative decode/prefill execution; its current diff does not remove the mixed speculative output merge.
- [#50172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50172) and [#55504](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55504) address caching and state recovery rather than this output assembly.

Searches included `GDN scatter`, `GDN stride`, `GDN metadata`, `GDN copy`, `"merged_out"`, and `"GDN" "output" "copy"`.

## Test Plan

Tested September 16, 2026 against vLLM base `0f8fa53acf43a9a6a7a1f7e6b196950c78cd6d7a`, with the production change at commit `5fe281e336f8f25aab2f89cf85c211bf83594551`. The production GDN module in the current PR is byte-for-byte identical to the measured version (SHA-256 `187a368baca93a1d9920d44477c297855413acf7608ace2873ea24b6ff62b21f`). Both serving variants used the wheel built from that exact base. The baseline GDN module matched the repository source byte-for-byte; the patched arm replaced only that module. Native binaries, dependencies, model weights, inputs, and launch settings were identical.

Static hooks ran on macOS ARM64 with Python 3.12.6. The repository tests, GPU component checks, and serving measurements ran on the VM below.

### Test VM and model

| Component | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| GPU | 1 × NVIDIA H100 PCIe, 81,559 MiB reported memory, 310 W power limit, MIG disabled |
| CPU / RAM | 20 vCPUs, Intel Xeon Platinum 8352Y @ 2.20 GHz; approximately 125 GiB RAM; container quota 20 CPU cores and 123 GiB memory |
| OS / driver | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux 6.8.0-90-generic, NVIDIA driver 580.126.09 |
| Runtime | Python 3.12.3; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; CUDA runtime 13.0; Triton 3.7.1; FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 |
| vLLM | 0.29.1rc1.dev194+g0f8fa53ac; V1 model runner; default compilation and full/piecewise CUDA graphs enabled |
| Model | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, revision `851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a`, BF16, TP=1, text-only inputs |
| GDN / speculative decoding | 24 GDN layers, 32 value heads × 128 dimensions; Triton prefill; MTP with 3 speculative tokens |

This model was selected because its GDN and native MTP paths exercise the mixed speculative/non-speculative merge on one H100. This is a separate upstream validation workload, not a reproduction of the original Pareton campaign score.

### Correctness checks

The [validation bundle](https://github.com/tripathiarpan20/vllm/raw/9055cd31883f61361aa80817f86a734301d8368a/gpu-validation.tar.gz) supplies the supplementary harnesses, fixed workload, raw results, and reproduction instructions.

The supplementary real-kernel harness executes the actual baseline and patched `_forward_core` methods with real metadata construction, convolution, and GDN kernels. Its matrix uses two speculative sequences with query length 4 and two non-speculative sequences with lengths 1 and 1/65/257, BF16 activations, BF16/FP32 recurrent states, and contiguous/strided destinations. It is a component test with supplied weights and states, not a full model accuracy benchmark.

The repository tests are reproducible from the checkout with the matching CUDA runtime and test dependencies:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py

pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py
```

### Serving benchmark protocol

A fixed manifest contains **64 requests** in the same order for both variants: 16 at each input/output token pair of **256/64, 768/128, 1,536/192, and 3,072/256**. Prompt token IDs are saved rather than retokenized between runs. Requests use greedy sampling, seed 42, and `ignore_eos=true` to keep output work fixed. The manifest SHA-256 is `6b5f1be99c276edc155ba269973ad3302c5f85706b4e2eb1d76e3b5a7aaa08c1`.

Each sweep submits the manifest in waves of **1, 4, 8, 16, or 32 concurrent requests**, waiting for each wave to finish. These are client batch sizes; vLLM determines internal token batches. There are four independent server sessions in **baseline → patched → patched → baseline** order, with two measured sweeps per session: **four repetitions and 256 requests per variant/batch size**. The client runs on the same VM over loopback. Startup/compilation and a 32-request warmup with 16 output tokens per request are excluded; the prefix cache is reset before each measured repetition/batch-size cell. There is no simultaneous competing GPU benchmark.

TTFT is measured from client request submission to the first token-bearing response. The table reports the **worst per-run p99 across the four repetitions**, calculated over the 64 requests in each run with NumPy's linear percentile interpolation. Throughput is all generated tokens divided by wall-clock time for the complete 64-request sweep, including waiting for each wave; the report gives the median and min–max range of four observations. No failed or slow measured samples are removed.

Both arms use these serving settings with the pinned model snapshot:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  vllm serve /path/to/pinned/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --served-model-name qwen-gdn --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --seed 42 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --gdn-prefill-backend triton --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --generation-config vllm --language-model-only
```

The measured runs additionally enable the development cache-reset/profiling endpoints and configure the Torch profiler; the profiler is inactive throughout timing. A separate untimed eight-request baseline profile captured **336 `index_copy_` calls into `[1, N, 32, 128]` merge tensors: 168 mixed GDN merges across seven scheduler steps and 24 GDN layers**. This confirms that the model workload reaches the branch changed by the PR. Batch 1 is a useful control because one request cannot create a mixed speculative/non-speculative sequence batch.

## Test Result

### Correctness and static checks

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing fused sigmoid/GDN recurrent-kernel suite | **18 CUDA cases passed** in the recorded H100 run |
| Supplementary real-kernel mixed-batch comparison | **12 passed**, exact baseline/patched output, convolution-state, and recurrent-state equality |
| CUDA graph replay in those 12 component cases | Exact match to eager execution in both variants; padding and unused strided storage preserved |
| Isolated old/new CUDA output-assembly comparison | **12 passed**, covering BF16/FP32, contiguous/strided output, and 32/256/4,096 tokens; graph replay checked |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks on the production GDN file | Passed, including Ruff, formatting, typos, default mypy, and repository checks |
| Explicit Python 3.12 mypy, Python compilation, patch whitespace | Passed |

The archived 26-test log also includes eight mocked assembly cases that were removed from this PR during review. They are excluded from the 18-case result above. This PR adds no new tests; the supplementary real-kernel comparisons and model measurements provide the change-specific validation.

### Isolated output-assembly timing

CUDA-event medians, 25 warmup calls and 50 repetitions of 20 merges; BF16 contiguous output with 32 value heads × 128 dimensions. Each row reports one GDN layer's merge. The full matrix also includes FP32 and strided storage. These are component timings, not end-to-end speedups.

| Tokens | Temporary removed | Eager baseline → patched (µs) | CUDA graph baseline → patched (µs) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32 | 0.25 MiB | 35.05 → 17.95 | 6.59 → 5.33 |
| 256 | 2 MiB | 36.71 → 18.55 | 8.92 → 7.05 |
| 4,096 | 32 MiB | 109.37 → 75.60 | 102.74 → 71.61 |

The 4,096-token case measures a larger tensor than the serving test’s 1,024-token scheduling budget. The direct merge was faster in these isolated measurements; serving results below determine the observed model-level impact.

### Time to first token

All **2,560/2,560 requests succeeded**, generating **409,600 output tokens** across both variants.

| Client batch | Baseline worst p99 TTFT (ms) | Patched worst p99 TTFT (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 265.0 | 275.6 |
| 4 | 627.9 | 545.5 |
| 8 | 1193.1 | 1021.9 |
| 16 | 2189.6 | 2416.2 |
| 32 | 4369.7 | 4793.1 |

### Serving throughput and speculative acceptance

| Client batch | Baseline output tok/s, median [min–max] | Patched output tok/s, median [min–max] | Median change | Draft acceptance baseline → patched |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 250.0 [249.2–251.4] | 250.8 [249.0–251.7] | +0.32% | 67.02% → 67.02% |
| 4 | 472.7 [457.0–479.7] | 491.2 [484.0–494.2] | +3.92% | 67.33% → 67.34% |
| 8 | 673.9 [633.8–685.9] | 701.5 [691.0–705.3] | +4.10% | 67.20% → 67.20% |
| 16 | 838.2 [822.9–854.0] | 829.7 [781.2–870.1] | -1.01% | 66.16% → 66.16% |
| 32 | 963.9 [955.8–972.1] | 959.5 [877.8–990.7] | -0.46% | 65.49% → 65.49% |

Draft acceptance is accepted draft tokens divided by proposed draft tokens, from per-cell Prometheus counter deltas. It is not an accuracy score.

### Compilation and warmup observations

The server logs report the following startup timings. Compilation time is the engine's reported compilation component; JIT kernel warmup is reported separately. These phases are excluded from throughput and TTFT measurements.

| Session, in execution order | Reported compilation (s) | JIT kernel warmup (s) | CUDA graph capture (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline-a | 0.65 | 115.79 | 4 |
| patched-a | 14.49 | 0.84 | 4 |
| patched-b | 0.53 | 0.81 | 3 |
| baseline-b | 13.97 | 0.92 | 4 |

Compilation caches were shared across sessions and were not reset for a controlled cold-compilation comparison. Both baseline-a and patched-b loaded cached AOT artifacts for the main and MTP models; patched-a and baseline-b performed a main-model Dynamo/compile pass while reusing the MTP artifact. The first session also incurred substantially more JIT kernel warmup. These observations document startup behavior, but do not establish a compilation-time improvement or regression from the patch. No Triton JIT-compilation warnings occurred during measured serving.

### Generated-output comparison

Every comparison uses the first baseline sweep at the same client batch size as its reference. The following counts require the **entire generated token-ID sequence** to match for a request. Baseline repeats provide a control for run-to-run variation.

| Client batch | Exact matches in other baseline sweeps | Exact matches in patched sweeps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 192/192 | 256/256 |
| 4 | 186/192 | 250/256 |
| 8 | 191/192 | 256/256 |
| 16 | 192/192 | 256/256 |
| 32 | 192/192 | 256/256 |

Greedy token IDs varied for some requests even between unmodified baseline sweeps. Accordingly, this serving comparison does not establish bitwise model-output equivalence or task accuracy. The direct baseline/patched GDN component comparisons above matched outputs and states exactly.

### Interpretation and limits

The isolated merge is faster and removes the expected temporary allocation. In the serving test, median output throughput changed by **+3.92% at client batch 4** and **+4.10% at batch 8**, while batch 16 was **−1.01%** and batch 32 was **−0.46%**. Batch 1, which does not exercise the mixed-sequence merge, changed by **+0.32%**. These are observed differences from four measurements per configuration, not a general speedup guarantee; the full ranges above show the variation, including slower patched runs at larger batches.

Worst per-run p99 TTFT decreased from **627.9 to 545.5 ms at batch 4** and **1,193.1 to 1,021.9 ms at batch 8**, but increased from **2,189.6 to 2,416.2 ms at batch 16** and **4,369.7 to 4,793.1 ms at batch 32**. The results therefore show a workload-dependent serving benefit, with higher observed tail latency at the larger batch sizes. Compilation timings have different cache histories and should not be used to attribute a startup-time change to this patch.

All four sessions used the expected source hashes and the same input-manifest hash. Server logs contained no Triton JIT-compilation warnings after measurement began. The benchmark server processes were stopped after the final run. The [GPU validation archive](https://github.com/tripathiarpan20/vllm/raw/9055cd31883f61361aa80817f86a734301d8368a/gpu-validation.tar.gz) contains the exact workload, harnesses, raw request timings/token IDs, counter snapshots, server logs, environment versions, trace, and checksums.

These results cover one H100 PCIe, one model revision, one serving configuration, and a finite synthetic workload. They do not establish task accuracy or performance on other GPUs/models. The source change removes only the mixed-output allocation/copy; unrelated Pareton campaign optimizations are absent from both serving arms.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, and validation support.

---
<details>
<summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary>

- [x] Purpose and distinction from related work described.
- [x] Test commands and benchmark protocol provided.
- [x] Correctness and before/after performance results included.
- [x] Documentation impact considered: no public API or configuration changes.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Stop sleep(level=2) from zeroing compressed-tensors KV scales
author: AlanFokCo
body:
## Purpose

`sleep(level=2)` zeroes the calibrated KV-cache scales of compressed-tensors
KV-FP8 checkpoints, so the first request after a weights-only reload — the shape an
RL weight-sync uses — returns **NaN logprobs and a wrong first token**.

Level 2 discards the weights allocation without keeping a copy, and the only
generic safety net is the `named_buffers()` snapshot in `Worker.sleep()` /
`Worker.wake_up()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:253`, `:291`) — that file has no
`named_parameters` walk. `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading()`
rebinds `_q_scale`/`_k_scale`/`_v_scale` onto the `nn.Parameter` placeholders,
moving those names out of `_buffers`, so the snapshot never sees them and they come
back as blank pages reading `0.0`. `_prob_scale`, never rebound, survives — that
asymmetry pinpoints the cause, and every other KV-cache quant method is unaffected
because it `.copy_()`s into the existing buffer (`kv_cache.py:152/156/157/195`).

**Fix (+10/−3, one file):** `register_buffer()` the three scales — the form
`set_default_quant_scales(register_buffer=True)` created them in
(`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:129-135`). `register_buffer()`
rather than `.copy_()` because ATTN_HEAD loads `num_kv_heads` scales into a buffer
created 0-dim; `persistent=True` because `sharded_state_loader.py:162` needs the
keys. Shape, dtype, device, virtual address and the `state_dict` key set are
unchanged (measured: same keys, shapes and dtypes, 0 pointer moves). The single exit
covers TENSOR and ATTN_HEAD by measurement, MLA and the draft model statically (same
`_init_kv_cache_quant`, same buffers snapshotted) — we have not run MLA or
spec-decode.

We fixed the quant method rather than the snapshot because compressed-tensors is the
only one that breaks that buffer invariant; a worker-level `named_parameters()` net
would also cover the W8A8 case below, but it carries a host-memory cost and a policy
question, so it belongs in its own change.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs/issues for compressed-tensors KV scales, `sleep(level=2)`,
`_q/_k/_v_scale`, the `named_buffers` snapshot and `register_buffer`: nothing open
addresses this. Nearest hits #38975 (`_prob_scale_float` sync, no sleep involved)
and #55206 (release pinned host memory after `wake_up`). Related RFCs #48310, #48312.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py -k compressed_tensors_kv_scale
cd tests && VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s basic_correctness/test_mem.py
```

New case `test_deep_sleep_fp8_kvcache_compressed_tensors_kv_scale`, above the two
`…_mrv1` cases (the second builds its engine in the pytest parent and leaves its 0.9
KV pool mapped there, which a fork inherits). It asserts registration form, non-zero
values, exact equality with the pre-sleep copies, and greedy output/logprob parity
against a never-slept control, plus a `sleep(level=1)` negative control and an
anti-vacuity probe that the weights really were discarded and reloaded. Red arm =
revert only the fix. Exact equality is deliberate: an injected 4.657e-09
perturbation of these scales flipped a greedy decision at token 10.

Checkpoint `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor` (static
`kv_cache_scheme`, so the scales are genuinely calibrated; already used by
`tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py`). Measured floor 2.46 + 0.69 GiB, so
`gpu_memory_utilization=0.6` fits the `h200_18gb` slice this file runs on — no
`large_gpu_mark`, **not skipped in CI**.

## Test result (H20)

| arm | rc | result |
|---|---|---|
| pristine tree | **1** | `1 failed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 16.37s` — assertion names all 66 lost scales |
| with this fix | **0** | `1 passed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 23.18s` |
| with this fix, 10.8 GiB budget (≡ 18 GiB slice @ util 0.6) | **0** | `1 passed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 22.16s` |
| whole file as CI invokes it | **0** | `14 passed, 41 warnings in 221.09s` |

With the fix, output is **bit-exact against the never-slept control** (36/36 rounds,
324-tensor census 0 zeroed / 0 pointer moves), the noise floor is 0, and
`sleep(level=1)` is a clean negative control. Lint on the two changed files:
`ruff check` / `ruff format --diff` / `py_compile` clean and
`pre-commit run --files <both>` 13 Passed / 0 Failed — including
`check-forbidden-imports`, which is why the test resolves the hub id with the shared
`hf_api()` helper.

<details>
<summary>Full characterization on the 8B checkpoint (96/96 scales, NaN logprobs, FLASHINFER, CUDA graphs, TP=2, ATTN_HEAD)</summary>

8B `nm-testing/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-KV-FP8-tensor-static_minmax`, greedy with
logprobs: unfixed, **96/96** parameter-form scales read back `0.0` while **0/32**
buffer-form did and all 34,560 logprobs are NaN; with the fix, **36/36 rounds
bit-exact** vs the reload-only control, 324-tensor census 0 zeroed / 0 pointer
moves. Noise floor 0 (no-sleep reload 36/36 bit-exact; 22 pre-sleep references
across 22 processes identical); `sleep(level=1)` clean (0/128 changed). FLASHINFER
reproduces it identically, so it is not backend-specific; with CUDA graphs on, wake
re-captures nothing; at TP=2 exactly those 96 names flip form; ATTN_HEAD (`[8,1,1]`)
covered; old-format `quant_method="fp8"` unaffected at these scales.

</details>

## Model evaluation

GSM8K, full 1319-question test set, vLLM's own harness
(`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` — `_build_gsm8k_prompts` / `get_answer_value` /
`_score_gsm8k`; 5-shot, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, seed 0) on
`nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor` with
`kv_cache_dtype=fp8`:

| arm | accuracy | invalid | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — never slept | 2.65% (35/1319) | 0.6% | — |
| B — level=2 → wake(weights) → weights-only reload → wake(kv_cache), **with fix** | 2.65% (35/1319) | 0.6% | **1319/1319 byte-identical output** |
| C — same sequence, **without fix** | **0.00% (0/1319)** | **100%** | 0/1319 |

Absolute accuracy is low because TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat is weak at 5-shot GSM8K; the
signal is that B reproduces A byte-for-byte while C collapses (all 66
`_q/_k/_v_scale` read back `0.0`, every response runs to `max_tokens`, most decoding
to an empty string). Both sleeping arms assert the weights pool really was discarded
and the reload really restored 135 parameters bit-exactly, so the delta can only
come from the scales. A 500-question subset gave the same picture (500/500).

## Scope

The documented level-2 recovery -- `collective_rpc("reload_weights")` -- self-heals, and
this PR does not claim otherwise: the layerwise path re-creates the `k_scale`/`v_scale`
placeholders before replaying the checkpoint, so `process_weights_after_loading()` runs
again (measured: green with and without the fix). What does not self-heal is anything
that skips it: `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` with no reload at all,
`reload_weights(is_checkpoint_format=False)` (the kernel-format branch, `param.copy_()`
only, next to the `# TODO: buffers?`), and a third-party `model.load_weights()`. There
the `named_buffers()` snapshot is the only net, which is the level-2 contract in
`docs/features/sleep_mode.md` ("the model's buffers are kept in CPU") and the invariant
`test_static_model_tensors_survive_level2_restore` asserts at the same point. Measured
matrix and the exact reason a plain reload cannot restore them: follow-up comment.

## Platforms

Verified on CUDA/H20 only. The AMD mirror of `basic_correctness` collects this test
(`requires_fp8` is true on CDNA, sleep mode is available on MI3xx) and two assertions are
platform-sensitive: `discarded["all_zero"]`, which relies on the driver handing back zeroed
pages, and the bit-exact logprob comparison. If the mirror goes red we will relax those two
(tolerance / platform guard) and keep the buffer-form assertion, which is the point of the test.

## Not covered (disclosed)

- W8A8 `weight_scale` / `input_scale` are `nn.Parameter` too and are lost by the
  same mechanism: on `neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV`, **449 of 580**
  censused tensors read back `0.0` after level=2 + a weights-only reload (256
  weight/input scales, 129 weights, 64 norms), while its 128 KV/attention scales are
  buffers and survive. Needs the worker-level net above — separate change.
- The test pins `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, like the two adjacent `…_mrv1` cases.
  Both runners share `Worker.sleep()` and `_sleep_saved_buffers`, but we have not
  measured the V2 runner and do not claim it here.
- TP=2 shows a pre-existing per-engine output bimodality (2 of 24 snapshots; same
  signature with `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, also in the unfixed control arm) —
  unrelated to sleep or to this patch.

title: [MM][Mistral] Add compile support for Pixtral vision encoders
author: jzakrzew
body:
## Purpose
Add `compile_mm_encoder` support for both Pixtral vision encoder implementations:

- `PixtralForConditionalGeneration`, including Mistral-format Mistral 3 models.
- The Hugging Face Pixtral encoder used by `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`.

The change applies `support_torch_compile` to the transformer blocks in both implementations and marks the token, rotary embedding, and packed-sequence dimensions as dynamic.

The feature remains gated behind `compile_mm_encoder`, which is disabled by default.

### Performance results
Note: the results are only about GPU kernel time. Total E2E runtime improves much less, even with Cuda graphs from #56277, because apply_hf_processor is the main bottleneck now.

Profiling was performed on an NVIDIA GB200 system using the same 16-image BF16 capture before and after enabling compilation. 
Total GPU kernel time decreased by **42%**, from **1173.6 ms to 676.8 ms**, corresponding to a **1.73x speedup**.

The improvement came from eliminating or fusing much of execution overhead:

| Kernel category | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FlashAttention | 273 ms | 273 ms | 0% |
| GEMM | 272 ms | 272 ms | 0% |
| Elementwise operations | 368 ms | 11 ms | 97% |
| SiLU | 121 ms | 44 ms | 64% |
| Concat | 96 ms | 0.3 ms | >99% |


  ### CUDA-graph compatibility

  This work is complementary to #56277, which adds Pixtral encoder CUDA-graph support. It does not duplicate or modify that implementation.

  The CUDA-graph PR’s pixtral.py and mistral3.py changes apply cleanly over this change. Its packed encoder forwards continue to use the unchanged transformer interface. Encoder CUDA-graph capture also performs an eager warmup before capture,
  allowing the transformer blocks to compile first.

  A combined compile_mm_encoder=True plus cudagraph_mm_encoder=True integration test should be added once #56277 is merged.

## Test Plan
Exercise both encoder implementations with compilation enabled and disabled:

- Mistral-format `PixtralForConditionalGeneration`
- Hugging Face `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`

The test uses dummy weights and verifies that the compilation counter increases only when `compile_mm_encoder` is enabled.

## Test Result

```console
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/compile/fullgraph/test_multimodal_compile.py \
  -k pixtral_compilation -vv -s

4 passed, 4 deselected
```

title: [KV Cache] GLM-5.3-Flash: use the generic packed KV layout; CircularBufferSpec tail with speculative ring slots
author: andakai
body:
## Purpose

Move kernel block splitting from the block table into each attention group. Previously `BlockTable` split every manager block for the whole KV cache group (`kernel_block_sizes`). All backends in a group had to share one kernel block size, block tables and slot mappings were at kernel granularity, and packed (block-outermost) caches could not be split at all, since other layers' pages sit between a layer's blocks. Now block tables stay at manager granularity, and each `AttentionGroup` maps manager blocks to the kernel blocks its own backend needs.

On top of this, GLM-5.3-Flash moves to the generic packed KV layout, and its model-specific KV code is removed.

## Design

### Kernel block mapping

**Choosing the kernel block size**
- `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` picks a size per KV cache group with `select_common_block_size(manager, backends, specs)`. Packed groups keep the manager block size and are never split group-wide.
- Each `AttentionGroup` then picks its own size for its backend and spec. It sets `kernel_block_size` only when that is smaller than the manager block.

**Mapping block tables**
- The group maps manager block `b` to kernel blocks `b * stride + j` (`j < block_size / kernel_block_size`).
  - `stride` is the number of kernel blocks per manager block.
  - For packed caches it is the packed block stride in kernel blocks.
- The mapped table is persistent and preallocated per ubatch, so CUDA graphs capture a stable buffer.
- Mapping happens inside `build_metadata`, `build_metadata_for_cudagraph_capture` and `build_metadata_for_drafting`. All runners and drafters (V1/MRv2, EAGLE, Gemma4, Step3.5, DFlash) go through these. Fused multi-step draft decode re-maps before replaying a FULL graph.
- `BlockTable`/`InputBatch` (V1 and MRv2) drop `kernel_block_sizes`. Slot mappings, CP and DFlash stay at manager granularity.

**Mapping KV views**
- When KV caches are bound, each group views its cache in kernel blocks. Packed caches use `as_strided` with the packed block stride.
- Only compressed caches (`tokens_per_state > 1`) may be split this way, because their write slots come from the mapped block table. Token and pooled caches are written through manager-block slot mappings, so they are rejected.
- The KV block zeroer maps the views back to manager blocks.

**Alignment**
- `block_stride_alignment` accepts `MultipleOf(n)`, meaning whole kernel blocks of up to `n` tokens, so a packed block always splits into whole kernel blocks.
- Fixed-size backends get it automatically; sparse MLA backends set their own in `customize_spec`.
- Bytes per block: block-outermost layouts round to the lcm of all alignments; layer-outermost layouts pad each layer's page separately.

**Consumers:** NIXL, Mooncake and HiSparse pick kernel block sizes the same way as the worker.

### GLM-5.3-Flash

- Uses the packed `BLHNC` layout. Removed its custom groups, byte layout, `KpoolTailSpec` and `storage_block_size`.
- The kpool indexer is a compressed spec whose backend declares DeepGEMM page sizes (32/64; 64 on SM120). The tail is a `CircularBufferSpec` ring of `kpool + num_speculative_tokens`.
- FlashMLA fp8 on SM90 reads 64-token pages over flat rows, so packed blocks need not be split.

**Example** (GLM-5.3-Flash on H200, manager block = 640 tokens, `index_kpool = 4`):

| Attention group | States per manager block | Kernel block | Kernel blocks per manager block |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sparse MLA (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`) | 640 | 640 (no split) | 1 |
| kpool indexer (`tokens_per_state = 4`) | 160 | 32 (DeepGEMM page) | 5 |

For a request with manager block table `[7, 2]`:
- **Sparse MLA** builds its metadata from `[7, 2]` unchanged.
- **The indexer group** maps it to `[7·S, …, 7·S+4, 2·S, …, 2·S+4]`, where `S` is the stride between manager blocks in kernel blocks:
  - In a plain (layer-outermost) cache, `S = 5`, giving `[35..39, 10..14]`.
  - In the packed `BLHNC` cache, each manager block also holds the other layers' pages, so `S` is the packed block size divided by the indexer's 32-state page. `MultipleOf` alignment keeps that an integer.

The scheduler, slot mappings and other groups never see kernel blocks. On main, the whole group had to share one kernel block size, so the indexer needed the GLM-only `storage_block_size` workaround instead.

## Test Result

Each cell is GSM8K / GPQA Diamond / acceptance length; no request errors.

| Platform | Model / backend | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | GLM `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, MTP5 | 0.9280 / 0.7323 / 4.73 | 0.9333 / 0.7374 / 4.73 |
| GB200 | DSv4.1 default, DSpark5 | 0.9257 / 0.8384 / 4.08 | 0.9261 / 0.8460 / 4.01 |
| H200 | GLM `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` | — | 0.9386 / 0.7323 / 4.78 |
| H200 | GLM `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` + `fp8_ds_mla` (GSM8K / accept) | 0.9325 / 3.937 | 0.9348 / 3.930 |
| H200 | DSv4.1 default | — | 0.9272 / 0.8535 / 4.05 |
| MI350X | GLM `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` | 0.9211 / 0.6768 / 3.33 | 0.9191 / 0.6835 / 4.82 |
| MI350X | DSv4.1 default | 0.9272 / 0.8333 / 4.03 | 0.9303 / 0.8535 / 3.94 |

- **Prefix caching:** mid-block hits give byte-identical outputs to main.
- **NIXL 1P1D:** GLM 0.9401, DSv4.1 0.9265, 0 failed transfers.
- **Mooncake P/D:** GLM 0.9136.

Performance, PR vs main (medians, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64):

| Platform | Model / workload | Output throughput | TTFT p50 | TPOT p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | GLM 4K/1K | −0.1% / +3.5% / +0.3% | −3.4% / −4.6% / +0.7% | −1.9% / +0.7% / −1.5% |
| GB200 | GLM 32K/1K | +0.0% / +1.8% / +0.5% | −0.3% / −0.1% / −1.9% | −0.8% / −5.7% / −2.0% |
| GB200 | GLM sonnet | +4.3% / +0.7% / +0.2% | −21.2% / +0.5% / −24.8% | +2.2% / −0.1% / −1.4% |
| GB200 | DSv4.1 4K/1K | −0.1% / −1.4% / +1.7% | +0.0% / +0.3% / +0.3% | −7.0% / +0.6% / −1.4% |
| H200 | GLM 4K/1K | +6.0% / +2.4% / +1.6% | +0.2% / −3.0% / −0.3% | −3.3% / +2.0% / −3.5% |
| H200 | GLM sonnet | +11.2% / −1.6% / +1.2% | −3.6% / −2.4% / −1.5% | −2.0% / +6.4% / −0.6% |
| H200 | DSv4.1 4K/1K | +6.2% / +1.9% / +0.5% | +6.0% / −3.6% / +0.2% | −14.6% / −1.3% / −0.5% |
| MI350X | GLM 4K/1K (random) | −8.6% / −9.9% / −9.2% | +0.3% / −0.2% / −0.5% | +7.8% / +3.3% / +4.3% |
| MI350X | GLM sonnet | +3.3% / +8.8% / +8.7% | +2.5% / +0.2% / +2.7% | −4.3% / −7.9% / −7.6% |
| MI350X | DSv4.1 4K/1K | +1.3% / −3.2% / −0.3% | −2.9% / −4.7% / −0.9% | +1.7% / +4.8% / −0.4% |

title: [XPU] Dispatch nn.LayerNorm to fused SYCL kernel via CustomOp
author: mganczarenko
body:
## Purpose

  vllm-xpu-kernels exposes fused SYCL kernels for standard (non-RMS) LayerNorm ([vllm-xpu-kernels#577](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/577)) - `layer_norm`, `fused_add_layer_norm`, `nemotron_layer_norm`, `fused_add_nemotron_layer_norm` - but nothing in vLLM dispatched to them yet. Every model with a bare
  `nn.LayerNorm` fell back to torch-xpu-ops' generic kernel on XPU.

  - Adds `StandardLayerNorm`, a `CustomOp` (registered `"layer_norm"`) - drop-in for a bare `nn.LayerNorm`, dispatching via `forward_native`/`forward_cuda`/`forward_xpu`, matching `RMSNorm`/`GemmaRMSNorm` in the same file.
  - Reworks `NemotronLayerNorm1P` (Nemotron's "+1 to weights" variant) from an `nn.LayerNorm` subclass into a `CustomOp` sibling (`"nemotron_layer_norm"`); its XPU path also dispatches the fused-residual-add kernel when a residual is present.
  - Wires both into GPT-2, GPT-J, OPT, SigLIP (PaliGemma's vision tower), and Nemotron.
  - Adds `replace_layernorm_class` (`transformers/utils.py`), matching `replace_linear_class`/`replace_conv_class`/`replace_embedding_class`, so the Transformers modeling backend's generic recursive module-replace picks this up too - covers StarCoder2-style models with no dedicated vLLM model file.
  - Kernel calls are wrapped as real `torch.ops.vllm.xpu_*` custom ops (`_xpu_ops.py`, via `direct_register_custom_op`), the same way `GemmaRMSNorm` wraps its kernel - compile-safe by construction, gated only by the standard `CustomOp` `+`/`-custom_ops` toggle.
  - Every dispatch path is `hasattr(torch.ops._C, ...)`-guarded and falls back to native `F.layer_norm` when the op isn't present - currently a no-op everywhere, since no `vllm-xpu-kernels` release yet contains #577 (just merged) and `requirements/xpu.txt`'s pin predates it.

  ## Test Plan

  - `ruff check`, `ruff format`, full `pre-commit` (incl. `mypy`) on every touched file.
  - Kernel correctness on Intel B70 hardware: parametrized cases across hidden sizes (incl. non-power-of-2), bf16/fp16, weight/bias/weight_bias combinations, plus fused-add cases, for both `layer_norm` and `nemotron_layer_norm`/`fused_add_nemotron_layer_norm`, checked against a plain-PyTorch fp32 reference.
  - End-to-end serve (`--enforce-eager`) on the same hardware, per affected model.
  - End-to-end performance via the official `vllm bench serve`/`throughput`/`latency`, baseline vs patched, N=3 median.
  - Not yet added: a correctness test in the repo (`tests/kernels/core/test_layernorm.py` covers `RMSNorm`/`GemmaRMSNorm`, nothing exercised plain LayerNorm before this PR). Not yet done: lm_eval accuracy check for any affected model. A reproducible kernel-level benchmark (`benchmark/benchmark_layer_norm.py`) is already
  committed on the vllm-xpu-kernels PR itself.

  ## Test Result

  **Correctness:** 64 parametrized cases + 2 fused-add cases, all pass vs plain-PyTorch fp32 reference.

  **Kernel microbenchmark** (native `F.layer_norm` vs SYCL, bf16, hidden_size=4096):

  | tokens | native | SYCL | speedup |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 8.35us | 3.60us | 2.32x |
  | 128 | 9.63us | 3.70us | 2.60x |
  | 512 | 28.20us | 5.90us | 4.78x |
  | 1024 | 51.73us | 10.83us | 4.78x (peak) |
  | 2048 | 103.91us | 56.61us | 1.84x |

  **End-to-end serve:** GPT-J, GPT-2, OPT-125m, Nemotron/Minitron-8B, PaliGemma (SigLIP), and StarCoder2-3B all served and generated correctly with `--enforce-eager`; SYCL dispatch confirmed firing inside the real engine, not just via a direct standalone op call.

  **End-to-end performance:**

  | Model | Path | Throughput | Latency | Serve |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | GPT-2-124M | direct swap | **+9.1%** | -9.5% (faster) | **+5.3%** |
  | OPT-125M | direct swap | **+9.2%** | -1.2% (faster) | **+9.4%** |
  | GPT-J-405M | direct swap | **+6.1%** | -4.4% (faster) | **+9.2%** |
  | StarCoder2-3B | generic swap | +1.0% | -1.2% (faster) | +1.3% |
  | Minitron-8B (Nemotron) | direct swap | +0.8% | -0.9% (faster) | +0.5% |


  **Caveat:** the above was measured against an earlier revision of this dispatch code (direct `torch.ops._C.*` calls, gated by `torch.compiler.is_compiling()`). This PR wraps those same calls through `torch.ops.vllm.xpu_*` instead, for `torch.compile` safety - a thin pass-through to the identical kernel call, so behavior should
  be unchanged, but hasn't itself been re-run on hardware.

title: [Quantization] Select per-token NVFP4 MoE backends explicitly
author: S1ro1
body:
## Purpose

Online `nvfp4_per_token` previously advertised the ordinary NVFP4 activation scheme even though execution uses per-token scales. This could select an incompatible backend. One-sided dispatch also sized its buffer for packed FP4 although the per-token path sends unpacked activations and quantizes inside the expert kernel.

- Add `kNvfp4DynamicToken` and use it for online NVFP4 MoE selection.
- Declare TRTLLM support and size modular expert workspaces for unpacked inputs.
- Size one-sided communication buffers with an optional `input_dtype` override. An explicit BF16/FP16 dtype reserves `hidden_dim * input_dtype.itemsize` activation bytes and zero scale bytes; `None` preserves quant-config-based sizing. Per-token NVFP4 supplies `moe_config.in_dtype`. This supports deferred quantization without relying on another BF16 layer enlarging the shared buffer.
- Cover both packed/deferred dispatch sizing, including BF16/FP16 dtype overrides and early rejection of FP32, FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2, and INT8 overrides. FlashInfer’s per-token NVFP4 quantizer accepts only BF16/FP16 activations; its FP32 per-token scales do not imply FP32 activation support.

Depends on #57091 and must merge after it. All Marlin capability changes belong to that PR's generic activation contract; there is no Marlin diff here. CuTe-DSL per-token support remains in #50030. The per-token backend-contract tests were removed from this PR because they need #57091; they should return with it.

## Validation

Latest sizing and dtype-validation changes:

- `uv run --no-sync --project /home/matej/prime-rl-stack-clean python /home/matej/prime-rl/outputs/glm53-rl-startup/20260922/nvfp4-one-sided/run_pr_tests.py` — **8 passed, 50 deselected**. The wrapper runs `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k nvfp4_one_sided -q --tb=short` against this checkout, with existing compiled CUDA extensions and isolated test dependencies. Both per-token modes with BF16/FP16 input dtypes and rejection of four unsupported override dtypes are covered. FP16 acceptance is checked at the configuration/quantizer-contract level; the GPU communication check below uses BF16.
- `uv run --no-sync --project /home/matej/prime-rl-stack-clean pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/all2all_utils.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py tests/quantization/test_online.py` — passed, including Ruff and mypy. Commit hooks also passed.
- Isolated two-B300-GPU check: `uv run --no-sync --project /home/matej/prime-rl-stack-clean torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 /home/matej/prime-rl/outputs/glm53-rl-startup/20260922/nvfp4-one-sided/gpu_dispatch_check.py` — FlashInfer one-sided BF16 dispatch/combine using this checkout's dtype override, hidden size 6144, capacity 320, batches of 1/96/320 tokens per rank, three repetitions each. **All 9 round trips matched the original input exactly**; no BF16 model layer or manager growth was used to provision the buffer. The initial harness incorrectly assumed token order is preserved during dispatch; the corrected check compares dispatched value multisets per source rank and requires exact original token order/values after combine.

These checks validate configuration and GPU communication, not full-model numerical accuracy. No full-model evaluation was rerun for this update, and the live GLM-5.3 RL deployment remains on its previous wheel.

Prior validation, before the sizing update: 30 configuration tests passed with prerequisite #57091 applied. Historical single-GPU and DP2/EP2 TRTLLM comparisons were reported for the original implementation; those were not rerun here.

## Non-duplicate and assistance

This updates the existing backend-selection fix split from #50030 at maintainers' request, rather than opening a competing implementation. #57091 owns the prerequisite Marlin activation-contract changes.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used. The submitting human must review every changed line, run the relevant tests, and defend the change.

title: [Bugfix][PP][Spec Decode] MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 aux-state relay at PP > 1 and per-stage FlashInfer autotune
author: venkywonka
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enables EAGLE3 for MiniMax-M3 (NVIDIA model file) at PP > 1 on Model Runner V2, and scopes FlashInfer autotune to each PP stage's TP group, fixing a startup deadlock. Builds on #50514 (PP aux-state relay), changes the autotune sync from #50892, supersedes #57198.

Motivation: MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 PP2/TP4 + EAGLE3 serving on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (also needs #59081, which supersedes #47665). No performance claim; the speedup there comes from split-K admission (#45450 / #52879 / #56148).

## Claims

1. **MiniMax-M3 + EAGLE3 runs at PP > 1.** Base rejects it at load (`ValueError: ... does not support eagle3 with pipeline parallelism`). The drafter then gets all aux states every step; acceptance length and GSM8K match TP8.
2. **FlashInfer autotune no longer deadlocks at PP > 1** when stages tune different shapes. Each stage tunes within its TP group and writes `<cache>_tp_<ranks>.json`. PP = 1 is unchanged.

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` + `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3`, offline `LLM`, greedy, cold autotune. Both arms: vLLM 213c379 + FP8 Triton-indexer enablement (as in #47665; needed on SM120) + #56148's Triton-attention guard hunks (not its split-K path). Arms differ only in this PR's files as of 4683f1e3 (since then: `kernel_warmup.py` comments only; extractor hunk dropped).

| Config | Aux relay (steps) | Mean AL | GSM8K-200 spec / no-spec | Stage cache entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | – | 3.471 | 94.5 / 94.5 | unchanged |
| PP2/TP4 | 4600/4600 | 3.460, 3.449, 3.452 | 95.5 / 95.5 | 140 / 80 |
| PP3/TP2 | 7200/7200 | 3.469 | 94.0 / – | 140 / 80 / 80 |

Main engine args (PP2/TP4):
```text
-tp 4 -pp 2 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend marlin --max-model-len 65536 --language-model-only
--max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 12 --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95
--disable-custom-all-reduce --enable-prefix-caching --seed 0
--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3","num_speculative_tokens":3,
  "draft_tensor_parallel_size":4,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
```

**Base** (same image, base files):
- With these args: the `ValueError` on all 8 ranks.
- Without `--speculative-config`: hangs in autotune; `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'` avoids it. PR `model.py` with base `kernel_warmup.py` + EAGLE3 hangs too (both changes needed).
- Non-spec PP2/TP4 (autotune off, 16 prompts, two setups): identical greedy outputs 2–3/16 PR vs base, 2–5/16 PR vs PR (mean hidden cosine .95–.97): no detectable PR effect.

**Non-MiniMax, H200:** Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 bf16 PP2/TP2, PR vs base: both start; PR writes per-stage caches; GSM8K-200 96.0 vs 95.5 (default MoE, 0 tuned entries), 95.5 vs 94.0 (`flashinfer_cutlass`, 44 entries/stage): equivalent.

@SloptimistPrime reported the autotune fix on 6x GB10 (SM121), TP2/PP3 (#57198); their test commit 1291f3fe is not included.

**CPU tests and lint:**
```bash

  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py
# 17 passed (11 added). Production files reverted: 8 of the 11 fail

pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files $(git diff --name-only 5c3b61e9)
# all pass, incl. mypy 3.10-3.13 and test tethering
```

## Details

**Root cause, autotune.** Since #50892 all ranks sync over the world group (cache broadcast, barrier, per-tactic all-reduce). PP stages can tune different shapes (140 vs 80 `mxfp8_gemm` entries), so PP0 waits on a collective PP1 never joins. Fix: at PP > 1, leader, broadcast, barrier, timing average and cache file use the stage's TP group.

**Root cause, MiniMax-M3.** No #50514 opt-in; taps used stage-local layer indices. Fix: set `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp` and use the `EagleModelMixin` helpers (global indices, pack local / collect upstream taps), like Llama, Qwen2, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3. Tap 0 aliases `residual`, which fused add-RMSNorm updates in place, so it is cloned when layer 0 is a tap (any PP size; CPU-tested; GPU runs above use taps 2/30/57).

title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: speed up skinny GEMM decode, including speculative batches
author: roberteg16
body:
## Summary

Tunes the W4A16 skinny GEMM decode path on gfx115x, and stops routing deep-K decode shapes away from it.

The kernel compiles for gfx11 and gfx12, and everything here was measured on gfx1151, so **every commit gates itself to gfx115x** -- the tuning and the routing alike. Off gfx115x the kernel runs exactly as it does today: the K * N bound stays at 1.2x LDS, the chunked path never launches, every tuple takes the checked K loop, the zero point keeps its own pass over the unpacked values, and the dispatch keeps its current tuples. The Python side gets an `on_gfx115x()` platform helper so the layer routes to match the C++ host check.

Eight commits, each measured against its parent on gfx1151 / ROCm 10.2, median of 3 passes:

| commit | what | effect |
|---|---|---|
| test coverage | asymmetric path and batch 4/5 at the op level | — |
| K loop | instantiate the whole-block loop without the bound check | mean **+18.9%**, 44 of 46 cells |
| zero point | fold it into the fp16 dequant constants | up to **+28.8%** at batch 1, asymmetric |
| group stride | scale and zero-point rows get their own row stride, HIP and Triton | — |
| LDS bound | stop rejecting K * N past the LDS budget | **+67% / +90%** on the shape that crosses it |
| chunked K | walk K in LDS-sized chunks so every activation row stays in LDS | **+30.5% / +51.7%** at batch 4, deep K |
| dispatch rules | avoid trimming wave slots, widen loads for deep-K batch 1 | **+9.4% to +16.3%** |
| LDS band | store the chunked activation band piece-major, conflict-free | **+1.9%** mean on chunked shapes |

## Results

The GEMM shapes a `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` decode step issues, at group size 32 and asymmetric, driven through `rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply` so the HIP/Triton routing is the production one. Percentages are bytes moved over elapsed time against 230 GB/s of practical board bandwidth. Median of 3 passes against `main`.

| Workload | Shape (M×K) | Kernel | main | this branch | Gain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Decode, N=1 | 43008×5376 | sml | 634.8 µs — 92% | 499.2 µs — 116% ⁽¹⁾ | **−21.4%** |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×21504 | sml | 360.7 µs — 81% | 325.5 µs — 89% | −9.8% |
| Decode, N=1 | 16384×5376 | sml | 266.7 µs — 83% | 242.1 µs — 92% | −9.2% |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×8192 | sml | 144.0 µs — 77% | 129.9 µs — 85% | −9.8% |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×16384 | sml | 296.0 µs — 75% | 263.8 µs — 84% | **−10.9%** |
| Decode, N=1 | 20480×5376 | sml | 334.8 µs — 83% | 303.5 µs — 91% | −9.3% |
| Spec decode, N=2 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 474.9 µs — 61% | 313.8 µs — 93% | **−33.9%** |
| Spec decode, N=2 | 5376×16384 | sml | 295.3 µs — 75% | 264.1 µs — 84% | **−10.6%** |
| Spec decode, N=3 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 498.7 µs — 58% | 315.3 µs — 92% | **−36.8%** |
| Spec decode, N=3 | 5376×16384 | Triton → chunked | 728.0 µs — 30% | 259.5 µs — 86% | **−64.4%** |
| Spec decode, N=4 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 499.2 µs — 58% | 316.0 µs — 92% | **−36.7%** |
| Spec decode, N=4 | 5376×16384 | Triton → chunked | 743.4 µs — 30% | 256.1 µs — 87% | **−65.6%** |

The speculative-decode rows carry the routing change: today any shape with K * batch past the LDS budget goes to the Triton prefill kernel, which at N=3 and K=16384 runs at 30% of bandwidth. Run-to-run spread is under 4% on every cell except that one, where it is 7.6%; the effect there is an order larger.

⁽¹⁾ Above 100% because the denominator charges scales and zero points to DRAM; for this shape that working set is 18 MB and fits the 32 MB MALL. The weight stream alone is 115.6 MB in 499.2 µs, 232 GB/s, which is the board's practical ceiling.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42, on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` with `max_num_seqs=4`:

| | main | this branch |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| strict-match | 0.8582259287338894 | 0.8582259287338894 |
| flexible-extract | 0.8612585291887794 | 0.8612585291887794 |

Identical to the last digit, so every one of the 1319 answers matches. `max_num_seqs=4` is load-bearing: Qwen3-8B has K = 4096 and K = 12288, so at batch 1 nothing crosses the LDS budget and none of the routing changes engage. At batch 4 the down projection gives K * N = 49152, which goes to Triton today and stays on the chunked path here -- the eval runs straight through the largest behavioural change in the series and produces the same output.

The deep-K tuple is not covered by this eval, and cannot be by any Qwen3-8B: it needs K divisible by 8192, and this model has neither. It is covered at the op level instead, by test cases at K = 8192 and K = 16384.

## End to end

`cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` served on gfx1151, 328 in / 256 out, 10 prompts each carrying one 640×480 image, batch 1:

| | main | this branch | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TPOT** | 120.7 ms | **107.4 ms** | **−11.0%** |
| **Decode throughput** | 7.65 tok/s | **8.49 tok/s** | **+11.0%** |
| End-to-end latency | 33.47 s | 30.15 s | −9.9% |
| TTFT | 2691 ms | 2762 ms | +2.6% |

TTFT is prefill. Routing there is unchanged, and the Triton kernel's arithmetic is too, but its scale and zero-point addressing now goes through a row stride instead of assuming K / group_size; for a contiguous tensor that stride is the same value and the generated code is unchanged.

This understates the series: at batch 1 on an AWQ checkpoint the chunked path, the wave-packing rule and the deep-K tuple all stay inactive, so the number above comes from the first four commits alone. The last three target speculative decoding and deep-K projections, which this configuration does not exercise.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py` on gfx1151: 197 passed. Cases added for the deep-K instantiations, for each batch that reaches the chunked path, for a K that crosses a chunk boundary with a ragged tail, and for group size 32 where one unrolled step spans exactly one scale group.
- [x] `pre-commit run` clean on every touched file, clang-format included.
- [x] End to end served on gfx1151 with an image workload, `main` against this branch.
- [x] GSM8K 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42 on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ`: identical to the last digit.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change, as required by `AGENTS.md`. Not a duplicate: the only other open PR touching `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` is #57015, which adds an alignment hint to the activation load in the compute body and changes neither the K loop, the dequant path nor the dispatch.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Remove MegaMoE padding and shared padding workaround
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

Remove unnecessary MegaMoE intermediate-width padding for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and revert the production workaround added in #56568. Routed and shared experts both retain the checkpoint width of 2304, so native shared-expert fusion remains enabled without padding either to 2560.

The bundled DeepGEMM uses `layout::Data(..., false)` for activation-scale rows in `include/deep_gemm/layout/mega_moe.cuh`; the old 16-byte TMA-row alignment rationale no longer applies. The existing runtime check still requires intermediate dimensions divisible by 128.

This removes 10% of the intermediate dimension used by the padded expert GEMMs and avoids the separate padded shared-weight copies introduced by #56568. Fusion keeps its existing eligibility checks and disable flag. A bare revert of #56568 would leave routed padding in place and disable V4.1 shared fusion again, so this change removes both together.

Retain the useful regression coverage from #56568, now checking exact checkpoint-shaped weight/scale preservation, native-width shared fusion, buffer reuse, and repeated finalization.

Related: #56217. Duplicate checks covered its issue/comments, open PRs mentioning #56217/#56568, and MegaMoE/shared-expert/padding searches. #56568 is already merged; this replaces its padding workaround. #54049 targets FlashInfer CuteDSL, #55275 adds GLM adapters, #40833 integrates a general fused-MoE backend, and #56697 targets SM90 Marlin. None removes this native DeepGEMM model-path padding.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py --hook-stage manual
```

Also compare this implementation directly with upstream `42919b49c5` on four GB200 GPUs using identical random expert weights, inputs, routes, and routing weights: hidden size 5120, intermediate width 2304 versus 2560, 384 experts, top-6, token counts 1/8/32/128/1024/2048, shared fusion both disabled and enabled. For the reference, upstream itself pads the native checkpoint-shaped shared weights.

## Test Result

Focused suite: **30 passed** on GB200.
Four-GPU operator comparison against upstream `42919b49c5`: **48/48 comparisons have exactly zero output error**, including all shared-fusion cases. Shared-expert outputs have nonzero contribution. Candidate commit: `21cda373e8`.
Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy 3.10, and explicit mypy 3.12 passed.

Previously completed real-weight model evaluation used this exact production model file with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/EP4. Full GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.12, five-shot multi-turn chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, 1024 output tokens, seed 123:

| Configuration | Correct / 1319 | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Auto-MoE/FlashMLA FP8-indexer baseline, three runs | 1270–1274 | 96.2851–96.5883% |
| Native-width MegaMoE/FlashMLA FP8 indexer | 1271 | 96.3609% |
| Combined optimized configuration, MXFP4 sparse indexer | 1266 | 95.9818% |

These are prior model-path validation results, not a newly measured isolated comparison against current upstream with #56568. The combined configuration includes separate attention/indexer optimizations. No new end-to-end speedup over #56568 is claimed here.

Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. Woosuk Kwon authorized submission after the prepared diff and validation results were presented for review.

title: [Core] Model console logging as CLI configuration
author: markmc
body:
Addresses #57200.

Adds a typed `LoggingConfig` to `VllmConfig` with three initial fields:

- `configure_logging`
- `log_level`
- `pylogging_config_file`

The complete object can be supplied as `--logging-config` JSON or with dotted arguments such as `--logging-config.log_level DEBUG`. `--log-level` is a convenience override for `log_level`, while the pre-existing `--log-config-file` is retained as a legacy override for `pylogging_config_file`.

The same model is available through serve YAML and Python configuration. `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING`, `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL`, and `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` remain as compatibility defaults. Explicit CLI and YAML configuration takes precedence, and the convenience/legacy CLI arguments override their matching `--logging-config` fields.

The resolved configuration is applied after argument parsing and propagated through `VllmConfig` to Uvicorn and API, engine, coordinator, and worker processes. This fixes the asymmetry where a CLI-supplied `--log-config-file` configured Uvicorn but arrived too late for vLLM's already-initialized root logger. Code that previously inspected `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL` directly now uses the effective logger level.

The existing default text output and custom Python `dictConfig` behavior are preserved. Tests cover JSON and dotted CLI forms, CLI/YAML/environment precedence, post-import reconfiguration, custom configuration files, and spawned-process propagation.

title: [CI] Ignore ruff D209, rejoin the docstrings it split, and silence incompatible-rule warnings
author: hmellor
body:
## Purpose

`pre-commit run --all-files` currently fails on `main` (`1085b64425`): three docstrings landed alongside #52136, which selected the whole `pydocstyle` `D` family, so `ruff check` flags them for D209 (`new-line-after-last-paragraph`).

This PR drops D209 rather than reformatting them, and undoes the reformatting the rule already caused.

D209 only moves the closing `"""` of a multi-line docstring onto a line of its own. That costs a line of pure punctuation and buys no readability. Note the repo already ignores D205, so a summary is allowed to run straight into its body with no blank line; enforcing closing-quote placement while ignoring the separator that actually carries meaning is an odd pair of choices.

Three commits:

1. **Ignore D209** — one line in `pyproject.toml`. Fixes `main`.
2. **Rejoin the docstrings D209 split** — 2085 closing quotes go back onto their last content line, recovering the 2085 lines the rule cost when #52136 landed.
3. **Silence ruff's incompatible-rule warnings** — selecting the whole `D` family pulls in two mutually exclusive pairs, so every ruff invocation printed:

   ```
   warning: `incorrect-blank-line-before-class` (D203) and `no-blank-line-before-class` (D211) are incompatible. Ignoring `incorrect-blank-line-before-class`.
   warning: `multi-line-summary-first-line` (D212) and `multi-line-summary-second-line` (D213) are incompatible. Ignoring `multi-line-summary-second-line`.
   ```

   Ruff was already resolving both pairs on its own, keeping D211 and D212. Ignoring D203 and D213 explicitly pins that same choice, so the warnings go away and `ruff check --statistics` output is byte-identical before and after.

The sweep is deliberately scoped. It matches against #52136's own diff, so it only touches docstrings *that commit* split; the ~6900 docstrings whose authors had already put the closing quotes on their own line are left exactly as they are. An unscoped join would have hit 8972 docstrings across 2484 files, which is a restyle rather than a revert.

Worth flagging for reviewers: nothing enforces the joined style going forward, since ruff has no inverse of D209. Ignoring the rule stops it *forcing* the split; it will not stop new code drifting back to it.

## Test Result

```
pre-commit run --all-files
```

All hooks pass. Specifically on the 692 swept files:

- `ruff check` and `ruff format` are stable — no hook modified a single swept file.
- All 692 files compile (`py_compile`).
- Every docstring's `inspect.cleandoc()` text is byte-identical before and after the sweep (verified programmatically across all 692 files): 0 content mismatches. The change is whitespace-only.

A full `pre-commit run --all-files` is now also warning-free.

Docstring formatting only, so no model eval applies.

Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "D209 docstring ruff"` and `--search "pydocstyle"` both return nothing.

AI assistance was used to produce this change; the sweep was script-generated and I have reviewed the script, the scoping, and the verification output.

title: [Perf][Pooling] Avoid blocking seq_lens GPU-to-CPU copy for pooling in FlashInfer metadata builder
author: frankwang28
body:
## Purpose
FlashInfer's metadata builder needs per-request sequence lengths on the CPU to plan paged KV metadata. For V2 model runner, `seq_lens` live on the GPU, so the builder fetches them with `common_attn_metadata.seq_lens.cpu()`. For pooling models this copy is avoidable; pooling models have no speculative tokens, so `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` maintained by the model runner is exact, not optimistic. The pooling runner already relies on this (`pooling_runner.py`: ["Pooling has no speculative tokens, so this CPU upper bound is exact"](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pool/pooling_runner.py#L142)). 

This results in a measured performance boost of about 1.35%.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Reduce CUDA graph divergences
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose
This PR cuts down on some ROCm-specific divergences that have now outlived their use. This serves as a cleaner base for the ModelRunner V2 default enablement on ROCm (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56360).

1. Reverts https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48526, which performed graph capture profiling on the current stream rather than a new side stream on other platforms after a performance regression was observed. The reason given then was that a side-stream "shifts the KV/activation buffers' physical placement and slows every bandwidth-bound decode kernel ~20%"; this is not correct.
The true reason is due to a latent runtime defect involving long cross-stream waits which was subsequently fixed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53712 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55099. In particular, the revert is now measured to be performance neutral rather than incurring a 20% slowdown.

2. Reverts #55095's DS V4 fallback on ROCm to `CudaGraphMode.NONE` if MRV2 is enabled. The justification given was #52644, but it no longer applied on `main`, so DS V4 was suffering an unnecessary performance degradation on ROCm with MRV2 enabled.

3. Gate `compile_or_warm_up_model`'s `torch.compile` specialization warmups not only on whether the compilation mode is `VLLM_COMPILE` but also on whether there's even a torch.compile'd submodule.

## Test Plan
Full `gsm8k` was run on DS V4 before/after these changes (2 in particular), on both ModelRunner V1 and V2, and accuracies between 0.954-0.972 were observed.
Performance was measured on TP8, concurrencies 1, 8, 32, 128, 256, 8K/1K, on DS V4 and Qwen-3.5-35B after these changes, and found to be the same (within noise).

Main and AMD CI will also be run on this PR. 

## Test Result
There are no new regressions in CI.

title: [A2A] Allow EPLB + SharedExpert Overlap + DeepEPv2
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
## Purpose

Allow shared expert overlap when EPLB is enabled with the `deepep_v2` all2all backend, by adding `deepep_v2` to `_EPLB_OVERLAP_SAFE_BACKENDS`. This follows #50569, which made the same exemption for `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` after validating it.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR touches `_EPLB_OVERLAP_SAFE_BACKENDS` for `deepep_v2`. Sequence-parallel support for `deepep_v2` is a separate PR (#57210); it was applied locally only for the SP runs below. When SP is active, `_disable_shared_experts_overlap` returns early, so this change only affects TP=1 deployments.

## Test Plan

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`
- Hardware: 8×H200, single node
- Backend: `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`
- Execution: `--enforce-eager` (see note on CUDA graphs below)
- Environment: `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`, because the node has no InfiniBand NICs. vLLM's `_check_gin_support` does not honor `EP_DISABLE_GIN`, so the GIN query was skipped locally (after the communicator-init probe). That change is not part of this PR.
- EPLB: async (the default), rebalancing aggressively so experts move many times during each eval:

```bash
EP_DISABLE_GIN=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"use_async": true, "window_size": 50, "step_interval": 100, "num_redundant_experts": 4}' \
  --all2all-backend deepep_v2 --enforce-eager \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 2048

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --num-questions 1319
```

- SP runs: same command with `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2` and #57210 applied. The logs confirm `sp_size=2`.
- Baseline (overlap off): same command with this PR's one-line change reverted.

## Test Result

GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot. Each accuracy is from a separate eval run against the same server.

| Config | EPLB | Shared expert overlap | GSM8K accuracy | Async rebalances |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 (**this PR**) | async | on | 0.353 / 0.353 / 0.346 | 52 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 (baseline, PR reverted) | async | off | 0.349 / 0.346 / 0.354 | 52 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 | off | on | 0.352 | – |
| TP=2, DP=2, EP=4 (SP, #57210) | off | off (SP disables it) | 0.350 / 0.356 / 0.349 | 0 |
| TP=2, DP=2, EP=4 (SP, #57210) | async | off (SP disables it) | 0.357 / 0.351 / 0.359 | 51 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4, `allgather_reducescatter` (reference) | off | – | 0.361 | – |

Enabling overlap with async EPLB on `deepep_v2` shows no accuracy change against the baseline, and there were no errors or hangs across 52 rebalances. SP combined with async EPLB on `deepep_v2` also works as expected.

**Known issue, unrelated to this PR:** with `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1` on this node, `deepep_v2` produces garbage output (GSM8K 0.000) whenever CUDA graphs are enabled. This happens with or without EPLB, and with the shared experts stream on or off. Eager mode is correct, so all results above use `--enforce-eager`. This will be tracked separately.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to run the validation and draft this description. I have reviewed the change and the results.

title: [CI] Split (H200 MIG 35GB) Spec Decode Speculators + MTP into 4 named jobs
author: Thangnguyenvn98
body:
## What

Split the `spec-decode-speculators-mtp` job (Spec Decode Speculators + MTP) into four named jobs that each run whole directories. `mtp/test_mtp.py` (6 cases, ~32m of pytest) splits into per-model content folders sharing a `_correctness.py` helper. The job's p50 is ~42m against a 50m timeout; after the split the slowest job runs ~12.4m of pytest, and each job's timeout drops to 30m.

## Old

```
tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/
├── mtp/
│   └── test_mtp.py            # test_mtp_correctness[mimo|deepseek|qwen3_5-hybrid|gemma4-e4b]
│                              # + test_mtp_rejected_placeholders_match_greedy_token_ids[…]  ~32m
└── speculators/
    └── test_speculators.py    # test_speculators_model_integration[llama3|qwen3]           ~8m
```

`pytest v1/e2e/spec_decode/speculators/` + `pytest v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/`, one job, key `spec-decode-speculators-mtp`.

## New

```
tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/
├── mtp/
│   ├── _correctness.py                                  # shared test body, never collected
│   ├── gemma4/test_mtp.py           # test_mtp_correctness[gemma4-e4b]            ~9.6m
│   ├── deepseek/test_mtp.py         # test_mtp_correctness[deepseek]              ~7.6m
│   ├── mimo/test_mtp.py             # test_mtp_correctness[mimo]                  ~5.0m
│   └── qwen3_5/                     # same model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base
│       ├── test_mtp.py              # test_mtp_correctness[qwen3_5-hybrid]        ~4.4m
│       └── test_rejected_placeholders.py  # both cudagraph modes                 ~4.8m
└── speculators/                     # unchanged                                   ~9.4m
```

Four named jobs, one replica each, whole-directory commands only:

| key | job label (H200 MIG 35GB) | coverage | pytest |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec-decode-speculators` | Spec Decode Speculators | `speculators/` | ~9.4m |
| `spec-decode-mtp-qwen3-5` | Spec Decode MTP Qwen3.5 | `mtp/qwen3_5/` | ~9.2m |
| `spec-decode-mtp-gemma4` | Spec Decode MTP Gemma4 | `mtp/gemma4/` | ~9.6m |
| `spec-decode-mtp-deepseek-mimo` | Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo | `mtp/deepseek/`, `mtp/mimo/` | ~12.4m |

The old key `spec-decode-speculators-mtp` is removed; nothing else referenced it (no `depends_on` or coverage-check consumers).

## Notes

- Node IDs are unchanged modulo the path prefix — same test names and parametrize ids (`mtp/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_correctness[mimo]` → `mtp/mimo/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_correctness[mimo]`), so per-test history carries over. `_correctness.py` holds the shared MTP correctness body and matches no collection pattern.
- Durations are pytest times from recent `main` runs of this job and from build 90275. Jobs with two directories run them as separate pytest invocations, preserving the old job's per-suite process isolation.
- Each MI300 mirror runs its job's whole directories as a single replica (no `parallelism` to inherit). Its own per-case timings keep the slowest mirror job well inside the new 40m mirror timeout (was 75m).
- The B200 nightly step and the legacy `test-amd.yaml` copies keep running `pytest v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/`, which still collects the new subfolders whole — unchanged. Deferred: the sibling Eagle `-k` splits and the acceptance-nightly `--deselect` partitioning stay filter-based; out of scope here.

## Expected runtime and overhead (predictions)

Per-directory pytest times are measured in build [90275](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90275) (previous grouping; see the [validation comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57237#issuecomment-5765646057)); the regrouped rows are predictions from those numbers plus the ~1.4m/job setup measured there.

| job | pytest | est. running wall | est. non-pytest overhead |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speculators | ~9.4m | ~11m | ~1.4m |
| MTP Qwen3.5 | ~9.2m | ~11m | ~1.4m |
| MTP Gemma4 | ~9.6m | ~11m | ~1.4m (measured) |
| MTP DeepSeek + MiMo | ~12.4m | ~14m | ~1.4m (measured) |

Baseline: 1 job, 47.4m wall on a recent `main` run. After: ~47m total worker-minutes, still four jobs → **~0 extra worker-minutes**, inside the ≤20 aggregate budget. Slowest job ~12.4m pytest, inside the ≤20m target. `qwen3_5/` holds both Qwen3.5 tests (same model), so each job is one model family and the four land at ~9–12m.

## AI assistance & verification

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi Code); a human reviewed the diff. No existing PR covers this restructure (checked open PRs for spec_decode sharding).

Verification run locally:
- `pre-commit run` on all changed files — passed (ruff, mypy, SPDX, Buildkite step-key check).
- `pytest --collect-only`-equivalent AST check: the six parametrized node IDs are identical before/after modulo the path prefix; `_correctness.py` collects nothing.
- `tools/check_area_test_coverage.py --tree tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode .buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml` — no violations reference the new steps or folders (all reported violations pre-date this change and belong to the Eagle `-k` jobs and acceptance nightly).
- GPU validation: scoped CI build to follow as a comment.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix Nixl+Offloading PD edge cases on TheRock image
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose
This PR fixes two issues observed on the (MI300) MultiConnector (Nixl+Offloading) PD edge cases test group on TheRock image (observed [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13000/list?sid=01a0a804-5e41-45dc-81bc-82b154c38890&tab=output) and [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002/list?sid=01a0a870-9608-4b69-970f-f7eb2ea5138f&tab=output)).

1. There is plenty of spam of the form `ucp_worker.c:3328 UCX  DATA  arm iface 0x39efd290 returned Success`. Resolved by bumping the AINIC version up to match what's currently in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`, per the previous updates in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54112 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56459.

2. `test_prefill_cpu_offload_after_gpu_eviction` fails the direct output match test. This was root-caused to slight (reasonable) numerical differences in the prefix cache hot vs cold path. See for instance the following issues:
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33123
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/5543#issuecomment-4625222702
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54490
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42699

This is compounded by the particular eviction prompt here being an open-ended exposition with many plausible continuations. In particular, the next-token logprobs were measured:
- ROCm 10:  ' However' -2.2956 / ' In' -3.3581   → margin 0.0625
- ROCm 7.2:  exact tie above on a cold cache     → margin 0.0000

i.e. almost or exactly tied between the top 2 candidates. The two observed diverging CI continuations (' The development...' vs ' The field...') are exactly the tied top-2 candidates.
Prefix-caching hit in this case legitimately shifts logits by ~0.005–0.06. This is measured to be backend-independent (triton 0.06, AITER 0.074). A 0.0625 margin sits inside that noise floor, so a hot-vs-cold shift can flip the argmax and cause direct text-matching to fail.
Fix: For direct text-matching to be reliable here (insensitive to small reasonable numerical divergences), the continuation has to be reliable i.e. not invite open-ended drift. Appending a sentence to count to 5000 ensures this while still preserving the spirit of the test. In particular, the exact eviction prompt is irrelevant, and slight numerical differences between the prefix cache hot-vs-cold paths are not what is under test here.
 
## Test Plan
All NixlConnector tests were run [before](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002) and [after](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13014) this PR on ROCm 10 and it was found to fix the failing test group and remove the UCX clutter while not causing any test regressions.

Main and AMD CI will also run on this PR on ROCm 7.2 to verify it causes no new regressions both on the AMD and Nvidia code paths.

## Test Result
All NixlConnector tests pass on ROCm 10 without clutter, and there are no new regressions on ROCm 7.2 and on CUDA.
