title: [Core] structured generation mode for DiffusionGemma model (Jev-like)
author: mmastrac
body:
## Prerequisite PRs A few PRs that can go in on their own merits were split out: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57414: hand out stashed logprobs only on the committing step (bug fix) - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57416: give a prefill-only batch the model state's number of logit rows (perf) - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57417: honor logprob_token_ids on the converging step (feature parity w/autoregressive) - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57462: type cast error if dynamo falls back to eager mid-run (bugfix) - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57589: fix multimodal support in DiffusionGemma (bugfix) ## Purpose DiffusionGemma (and likely other models in vLLM) contains all of the necessary components to build a Jev-like model that provides structured answers with bounded choices. By fixing canvas positions in the given structured output format, you can ask the model to provide a token and logprobs (from which a client derives entropy) that can be used to determine the models most likely answer and its confidence in that answer. If entropy does not pass a given threshold, you can perform additional sampling to determine agreement between runs and therefore the actual confidence of the model's answer. This PR contains a prototype example server for serving the `/v1/systemone` endpoint. It does not implement a standard endpoint in vLLM. The model is sufficiently powerful to work with _any_ structured output that follows one limitation: the token choices _must_ be a single token, so that the canvas itself does not shift. The requesting client can always translate multi-token options into single token options, however (ie: "moderation_spam" -> "A"). The choices are always laid out in a system prompt and the model correctly diffuses single-token-slot answers (or makes a guess and flags it with uncertainty). Why do we require the token IDs in the request? Currently we provide the token slot positions that are unfixed for the model to choose and this allows the two to be matched more accurately. A followup PR will likely add a template syntax. The model, using this framework, can answer yes/no ("noul" in Jev parlance), scale, or multiple choice questions, and provides its certainty and error bars with the answer. The only missing pieces for this to work in vLLM today are in this PR: - A way to pre-seed the canvas with the fixed tokens - A way to send read-only requests that emit the argmax canvas on the converging step and skip the commit forward (logprobs come from that step at temperature 1) - A way to limit the number of steps run (we only want the first step) - A bugfix for two parallel DiffusionGemma generations that stomp on each other in lockstep: two concurrent requests with logprobs on where one converges in the same step another commits loses its stash and the request fails with HTTP 500 "list index out of range". This PR currently contains the machinery to make this model work and a sample interposer server is included to demonstrate end-to-end functionality that is sufficient to serve traffic at reasonable scale. | field | type | validation | effect | |---|---|---|---| | `diffusion_seed_canvas` | `list[int]`, exactly the request's canvas width | ids in `[0, vocab)`, length checked against `diffusion_canvas_length`, else the served `--diffusion-config` | replaces the random canvas after prefill | | `diffusion_max_steps` | `int >= 1` | clamped to `max_denoising_steps` | denoise steps before the canvas is emitted | | `diffusion_pinned` | `list[int]` of canvas positions | needs a `diffusion_seed_canvas`; positions must lie inside the request's canvas | held at their seed value on every denoise step, and their self-conditioning soft embed is zeroed, so a read past one step denoises the canvas the request seeded instead of one the model rewrote | | `diffusion_read_only` | `bool` (the OpenAI server delivers JSON booleans in `vllm_xargs` as 0/1, which is accepted) | caps `max_tokens` at the canvas, sets `ignore_eos` | emit on the converging step, skip the commit forward, temperature-1 logprobs | | `diffusion_canvas_length` | `int`, 1 to the served `canvas_length` | validated in `verify`; the seed must be this long | the request runs on a canvas this wide: the scheduler schedules this many draft tokens and the sampler tiles the read at this width, so a short schema on a wide server costs the same as on a server of its own width | | `logprob_token_ids` (a request field, not in `vllm_xargs`) | `list[int]`, up to 128 | existing vLLM validation | exact logprobs for those ids at every canvas position. The sampler now honors it on the converging step, so a read asks for its label ids instead of hoping they rank in the top-k (with 26 options only 1-8 did) | Example request: ``` { "model": "dgemma", "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "Answer a fixed set of questions about the state ... Question urgent: ...\n yes\n no\n..."}, {"role": "user", "content": "{\"ticket\": \"Since this morning the dashboard shows a blank page after login...\"}"} ], "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}, "max_tokens": 17, "logprobs": true, "top_logprobs": 20, "return_tokens_as_token_ids": true, "vllm_xargs": { "diffusion_seed_canvas": [100, 45518, 107, 101, 148436, 236787, 71203, 107, 36164, 236787, 9950, 107, 66387, 236787, 236743, 189012, 106, 0, 0, "... 64 ids total"], "diffusion_max_steps": 1, "diffusion_read_only": true } } ``` ## Example Queries These are _raw_ example queries passed to the model: ``` Answer a fixed set of questions about the state the user provides. Each question lists its allowed answers; reply with exactly one label per question. You are reviewing a user post on a community forum. Question violates: Does the post break the community rules? yes no Question category: Which rule does it come closest to breaking? A: none B: spam (unsolicited promotion) C: harassment (targets a person or group) D: self_harm Question severity: How severe is it? 1: none 2: mild 3: serious 4: critical Reply with one line per question, in this order, formatted as "id: label". ``` Answer template (@ standing in for a noised slot): ``` <|channel>thought\nviolates: @\ncategory: @\nseverity: @ ``` Seeded canvas: ``` [100, 45518, 107, 101, 51584, 1090, 236787, 58369, 107, 10618, 236787, 13112, 107, 127243, 236787, 236743, 144194, 106, 0, 0, ... 0] pos 7: violates <- 58369 (' Mell') pos 11: category <- 13112 (' laugh') pos 16: severity <- 144194 ('اهرة') ``` ## Test Plan Run locally on a DGX spark, with a concurrency sweep to ensure it scales and does not corrupt parallel generations. ``` pytest tests/test_sampling_params.py tests/v1/sample/test_diffusion_gemma_reads.py ``` Run with: ``` vllm serve nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4 --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 32}' --max-logprobs 32 --enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --max-num-seqs 32 python examples/features/structured_diffusion/structured_server.py --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8000 --tokenizer nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4 --canvas 32 ``` ## Test Result Hardware: 1 DGX Spark, sole active GPU process. Setup: read-only single reads, 32-row canvas, three decisions per request, cache-busted state with the schema prefix cached Results: 1-way 8.7 req/s at 0.12 s, 32-way 54.0 req/s at 0.58 s, about 162 decisions/s. Using a sample request/response corpus to determine, from a mock support request, the urgency, tone and routing of an outage report, we get the correct variable number of samples per request (the auto policy re-reads only when the first read is uncertain): H1: is the first read's entropy per question over the top-20 logprobs (note that reads=4 when H1>0.1) ``` == samples=auto outage 527ms reads=4 title: [Metrics][KV Offload] Add Prometheus metrics for SimpleCPUOffloadConnector
author: mevince
body:
## Purpose

Exposes `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` telemetry through the existing `KVConnectorStats` pipeline, the same contract the offloading connector, NIXL, and mooncake follow. Scheduler-side only; the transfer path is untouched. The manager already tracks every quantity involved.

Five series under `vllm:simple_kv_offload_*`, drained once per engine step:

- `save_outcomes_total{outcome}`: store decisions as interval deltas, `stored` or one of `dropped_cpu_full`, `dropped_request_gone`, `dropped_null_block`, `dropped_not_hashed`, `skipped_already_cached`, `skipped_in_flight`
- `load_blocks_total`: KV blocks restored to GPU from the offload pool when loads finish; prefill work avoided through offload cache hits
- `used_blocks`: pool blocks pinned by in-flight transfers or cache hits. Warm but evictable cached blocks don't count; `info`'s `capacity_blocks` gives the pool size
- `pending_store_blocks`: blocks in queued, issued, or abandoned stores. If it grows without coming down, a transfer is stuck
- `info{backend,page_cache,lazy_offload,capacity_blocks}`: config fingerprint, value always 1

Because the stats flow through `KVConnectorStats`, the per-step CLI log picks them up too (via `reduce()`; the constant info gauge is skipped there).

One behavior change: `reset()` now seeds the fresh `BoundaryStoreStats` with outcomes counted since the last drain, so the new counter doesn't lose a window that straddles a cache reset (e.g. a LoRA unload mid-interval). `get_boundary_store_stats()` right after a reset reports that carried window instead of zero. The accessor is diagnostics-only; nothing in the control flow reads it.

## Related work

Not a duplicate of #41790: that PR instruments the worker-side DMA copy path (transfer bytes, DMA-only timing from pooled CUDA events, transfer-size histograms) on the generic offloading stats transport. This PR adds scheduler-side logical block counters through the connector's own `KVConnectorStats` pipeline; the transfer path is untouched. The two measure different layers — DMA transfer cost there, store admission and load effectiveness here — and the only overlap is a pool-utilization gauge exposed under a different name.

## What each metric is for

- `save_outcomes_total{outcome}`: classifies every eager-mode store decision, and is the first place to look when the cache hit rate drops. `dropped_cpu_full` means KV was lost because the pool was full. `dropped_request_gone` means the request finished or was preempted before the hand-off was processed. `dropped_not_hashed` points at hashing config. `skipped_already_cached` and `skipped_in_flight` mean the content is already stored or a store for it is in flight.
- `load_blocks_total`: KV blocks restored to GPU from the offload pool when loads finish, i.e. prefill work a request did not have to redo. Flat while traffic is flowing means data is stored but never matched, which points at hashing or prefixes.
- `used_blocks`: pool blocks currently pinned by in-flight transfers or cache hits. `dropped_cpu_full` starts exactly when this gauge reaches `capacity_blocks`, so alerting below the ceiling warns before data is lost. Evictable cached blocks are not counted because they are reclaimed on demand.
- `pending_store_blocks`: store backlog. Normal behavior is spikes that return to ~0 as stores finish. A value that keeps growing means a stuck transfer. Stuck stores also hold pool blocks, so this is the first warning before `used_blocks` fills and `dropped_cpu_full` starts.
- `info`: config context for the other metrics. `capacity_blocks` is the ceiling for `used_blocks`. `backend` tells you whether to read a growing backlog as disk latency or memory bandwidth. `lazy_offload=true` explains why `save_outcomes_total` reports nothing: it only classifies eager-mode stores.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/ \
  "tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_scheduler_kv_connector_stats" -q
```

## Test Result

111 passed, 2 skipped, including the 20 tests in `test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py`.

AI assistance: used for implementation and validation. Human review and ownership remain with the submitter.

title: [Spec Decode] Enable Gemma4 DSpark adaptive verification with FlashInfer
author: zixi-qi
body: ## Purpose Enable Gemma4 DSpark adaptive verification with FlashInfer TRTLLM-GEN, building on #52157 (#51871): graph-safe variable-length decode, trained confidence-head loading, graph-cache separation, and RoPE config normalization. Adaptive verification replays FULL decode CUDA graphs in which each request has 1 to 1 + k query tokens, read from the device `query_start_loc` (k = `num_speculative_tokens`). On `main` it requires every target builder to report `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, which also promises graphs for mixed prefill/decode batches. FlashInfer's TRTLLM-GEN path can replay variable-length decode batches but not mixed ones, so, per review, this PR declares that capability separately instead of adding an enum member: - **`AttentionCGSupport` is unchanged.** - **New builder classmethod** `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len(vllm_config, kv_cache_spec) -> int | None`: the largest per-request query length L for which one FULL cudagraph replays any decode batch with 1 to L query tokens per request. It returns `None` for `ALWAYS` builders, which replay any batch, and for builders without variable-length support. | Builder | `get_cudagraph_support()` | `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len()` | Adaptive verification | |---|---|---|---| | `ALWAYS` builders (FA3, Triton, FlexAttention, Kimi-K3 KDA, FlashInfer MLA, ...) | `ALWAYS` | `None` | supported | | FlashInfer with its TRTLLM-GEN varlen path active (adaptive verification on, SM100 family, no DCP) | `UNIFORM_BATCH` | `1 + k` | supported (needs at least `1 + k`) | | FlashInfer otherwise, and other builders below `ALWAYS` | unchanged | `None` | not supported | - **Readers.** Adaptive verification is the only reader: every target builder must report `ALWAYS` or a bound of at least `1 + k`. CUDA graph mode resolution and capture are unchanged. - **Batches with a prefill no longer replay varlen decode graphs.** Dispatch matched those graphs on `max(num_scheduled_tokens)` alone, so decodes plus a prefill chunk of at most `1 + k` tokens replayed a decode graph. That is harmless for FlashInfer and FlashInfer MLA, which run short prefills on their decode kernels, but not for Kimi-K3's KDA builder (`ALWAYS` since #52988): it classifies rows by request state and does not restage its graph buffers when a prefill row is present. The runner now passes `max_query_len=None` for any batch with a prefill. - **Decode width on model runner V2.** Six copies of `1 + (2 if parallel_drafting else 1) * k` now share `max_decode_query_len()`. The 2× covers model runner V1's parallel drafter only, so on V2 the spec-as-decode width is `1 + k`, and DFlash/DSpark prefill chunks of `k + 2` to `2k + 1` tokens take the prefill kernel. Not a duplicate: #53929 proposes a `VARLEN_DECODE` member to enable adaptive DSpark verification for Qwen GDN; under this design GDN would override `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len()` instead. ## Test Plan On one GB300, BF16, model runner V2, rebased on `9ef37771be` (includes #52988): ```bash pre-commit run --files pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \ tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py \ tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \ tests/test_config.py tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py ``` The full list, 31 files, also covers the linear-attention, chunked-local, DCP, batch splitting and reordering, Gemma4 model and TRTLLM-GEN varlen kernel suites. End to end, Gemma4-12B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7` K=7, comparing this revision with the previous one: - GSM8K, 50 questions, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, fixed and adaptive verification. - A mix of 4 long generations and 40 prompts of 2 to 7 tokens under adaptive verification, `max_num_seqs=8`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, so that verification rows and short prefills share steps. Full GSM8K, all 1,319 test questions, 5-shot raw completions, temperature 0 / seed 0, 512-token cap, pretrained Gemma4-12B, BF16 TP1 (measured on the first revision; the captured graphs are unchanged since): | Mode | Correct / total | Accuracy | | --- | ---: | ---: | | No speculation | 822 / 1,319 | 62.32% | | DSpark K=7 | 828 / 1,319 | 62.77% | | DSpark K=7 + adaptive | 826 / 1,319 | 62.62% | Adaptive versus fixed: −0.15 percentage points (two questions), exact paired McNemar p=0.868. All 3,957 requests completed with no preemptions or request errors. ## Test Result - **Lint:** pre-commit and mypy 3.12 pass. - **Tests:** 3,201 pass. The 9 failures are all accounted for: - 6 DCP distributed tests in `tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py` and 2 tests on gated `meta-llama` repos also fail on the previous revision. - One fp8 `TRTLLM_RAGGED` `small_decode` case in `test_mla_backends.py` passed 3/3 on rerun on both revisions. - **Short-prefill mix:** the previous revision replayed the varlen decode graph for all 31 steps that paired verification rows with a prefill of at most 7 tokens. This revision runs all 32 such steps piecewise, and decode-only steps still replay FULL graphs. 36 of 44 completions are token-identical; the other 8 diverge at greedy near-ties, and within a single run the same prompt also yields both variants depending on its batch. - **GSM8K:** captured FULL graphs are identical to the previous revision (fixed 2 + 32, adaptive 2 + 35). Accuracy is 25/50 fixed and 24/50 adaptive, against 24/50 and 24/50; 47/50 and 50/50 answers are identical. ## Perf Benchmark No speculation vs DSpark K=7 vs DSpark K=7 with adaptive verification, Gemma4-12B with `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7`, one GB300, TP1, BF16 (first revision): AI assistance was used (OpenAI Codex and Claude Code). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Bugfix] Honor skip_reading_prefix_cache for KV connector hits
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

`skip_reading_prefix_cache` (#28194) means "compute every prompt token in this request". `SamplingParams` sets it for `prompt_logprobs` and `PoolingParams` for the token-level tasks (`token_embed`, `token_classify`, `plugin`), because a prefix served from cache has no logits or hidden states for those rows; callers may also set it explicitly. Today it only gates the local prefix cache (`KVCacheManager`). The scheduler adopts a KV connector's `get_num_new_matched_tokens` result unconditionally, so honoring the flag has been left to each connector: `OffloadingConnector` (#44592) and `SimpleCPUOffload` (#54998) got individual fixes, while NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake and MoRIIO do not check it (`grep skip_reading_prefix_cache` over `kv_connector/v1/` finds only the two offload connectors).

Consequences with the remaining connectors:

- A `prompt_logprobs` request whose prefix is served remotely (LMCache, Mooncake) skips those rows silently. `LogprobsProcessor._update_prompt_logprobs` appends per received chunk with no placeholder, so the returned list is shorter and its indices no longer line up with prompt positions.
- In P/D disaggregation the decode engine gets the whole prompt from the connector, ships an unfilled `LogprobsTensors` and crashes with `OverflowError` (#50792; #50795 patches that symptom in the runner by not shipping the tensor).

This PR fixes it where the decision is made: the scheduler discards the connector hit when the request sets the flag (4 lines), so the flag holds for every connector, present and future, exactly as it does for the local cache. The request still computes and stores its KV as usual; only its read is skipped, which is what the two in-tree offload connectors already do.

Relation to #50795: that PR keeps the remote hit and returns no prompt logprobs for the request; this one recomputes the prompt on the decode side and returns correct prompt logprobs, at the cost of that request's prefill. NIXL's decode side already handles `num_external_tokens == 0` as a full local hit and notifies the prefill side to free its blocks (`pull_scheduler.py`, "If remote_blocks and num_external_tokens = 0 ..."), so nothing leaks. Happy to reduce this to the runner-side guard if maintainers prefer that trade-off; the two are complementary rather than conflicting.

Found while auditing #54335 (fixed-token prefill scoring), which also sets the flag and needs every prompt row; that PR will depend on this one.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_kv_connector_honors_skip_reading_prefix_cache`: with the mock connector reporting a 32-token hit, a plain request schedules 32 of its 64 tokens while a `prompt_logprobs` request schedules all 64.
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "skip_reading_prefix_cache or kv_connector_basic"`: 3 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passes.

## Test Result

The new test fails on `main` (the `prompt_logprobs` request schedules 32 tokens) and passes with this change. No GPU path is touched.

## AI assistance

Implemented with Claude Code; every line reviewed by the submitter. Not a duplicate: #50795 addresses the same symptom in the runner rather than the flag; no open PR changes the scheduler's connector-hit handling (`gh pr list --search "skip_reading_prefix_cache"`).

title: [Perf][Model] Qwen4Exp QSA: sm_90 tuning table for _select_config
author: ShuoleiWang
body:
## Purpose

Retune one kernel's launch parameters for sm_90 (H100/H200/H20): `_qsa_sparse_paged_gqa_splitk_kernel`, the Triton split-K kernel that runs the sparse attention of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's QSA layers over the 2048 selected tokens per query. Its tile width, split count and warps per CTA come from `_select_config()` in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa.py`, a table tuned on GB300 (#55557 added an sm_120 table beside it). Measured on H20, the GB300 entries are the wrong geometry in most decode regions, so this PR adds `_select_sm90_config()` in the same shape as the sm_120 helper. Besides that nothing else changes. Regions where the default entry is already fastest return `None` and keep it.

Each row below is one region of `_select_config`'s key, `base_programs = query rows × kv_heads per rank` (at TP8 with MTP3 that is 4 × concurrency, so the second column shows which serving points land in the region). "GB300 entry" is what runs today, "sm_90 entry" what this PR selects on H100/H200/H20; a tuple is (BLOCK_N, target_splits, num_warps). "Latency" is the change in this kernel's time per call when switching from the GB300 entry to the sm_90 entry, measured on one H20 (attention + split-K merge + fused output gate, CUDA-graph replay, median of 3 interleaved orders × 9 replays, hot and L2-evicted), at the three head geometries group 3 / 6 / 12 = query heads per kv head at TP8 / TP4 / TP1-2. Negative is faster.

bf16 K/V cache:

| `base_programs` | TP8 + MTP3 | GB300 entry | sm_90 entry | latency, group 3 / 6 / 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≤ 24 | C1 – C6 | (32, 64, 4) | (64, 64, 2) | −11 % / −12 % / −14 % at 4 rows, −12 % / −19 % / −21 % at 16 rows |
| 25 … 32 | C7 – C8 | (32, 16, 1) | (64, 64, 2) | −7 % / −7 % / ±0 |
| 33 … 64 | C9 – C16 | (32, 8, 1) | (32, 16, 1) | −8 % / −6 % / −4 % |
| 65 … 128 | C17 – C32 | (32, 4, 1) | (32, 8, 1) | −14 % / −13 % / −9 % |
| 129 … 256 | C33 – C64 | (32, 8, 1) | unchanged | best candidate within 3 % of the default |
| 257 … 512 | C65 – C128 | (64, 4, 2) | (32, 4, 1) | −13 % / −12 % / −4 % |
| 513 … 2048 | C129 – C512 | (64, 1, 2) | (32, 4, 1) | −18 % / not measured / −1 % |
| > 2048 | prefill | (32, 1, 1) prefill, (64, 1, 2) decode | unchanged | prefill entry re-confirmed (8 neighbours slower); decode entry not measured |

fp8 K/V cache (the path added by #55557):

| `base_programs` | TP8 + MTP3 | GB300 entry | sm_90 entry | latency, group 3 / 6 / 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≤ 24 | C1 – C6 | (32, 64, 4) | (64, 64, 2) | −8 % / −8 % / −20 % at 4 rows, −15 % / −18 % / −22 % at 16 rows |
| 25 … 32 | C7 – C8 | (32, 16, 1) | unchanged | default is fastest (best candidate +8 … +18 %) |
| 33 … 256 | C9 – C64 | (32, 8, 1) / (32, 4, 1) / (32, 8, 1) | unchanged | default is fastest at group 3 (candidates −1 … +3 %); groups 6 / 12 not measured |
| 257 … 512 | C65 – C128 | (64, 4, 2) | (32, 4, 1) | −43 % / −43 % / −31 % |
| 513 … 2048 | C129 – C512 | (64, 1, 2) | (32, 4, 1) | −53 % / −45 % / −43 % |
| > 2048 | prefill | same as bf16 | unchanged | not measured |

Why: at small `base_programs` the kernel hands tiles to split programs stride-wise, so (32, 64, 4) leaves one program with a two-tile tail (65 tiles over 64 splits) that the launch waits for, whereas a 64-wide tile gives 33 tiles over 33 splits, one per program. From a few hundred programs up the kernel is gather-bound and wants resident CTAs: BLOCK_N 64 needs 68–76 KB of shared memory per CTA (3 CTAs/SM) against 35–41 KB for BLOCK_N 32 with one warp (6 CTAs/SM). With fp8 the in-kernel dequant adds per-tile work, which is why the 64-wide entries lose almost half the time there.

No region regresses beyond run-to-run noise on any geometry; every candidate passed the FP32 reference at `rtol=atol=2e-2`. This kernel is 3–9 % of a decode step on this model, so end-to-end throughput moves by well under 1 % with bf16 caches; with fp8 caches the change is about 6 % of a C128 decode step. All measurements are H20; H100/H200 were not available. `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py` (added here) re-measures one shape in about 10 s, so a maintainer can check the direction there:

```bash
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 128 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 [--kv-dtype fp8]
```

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "<q>"` for `qsa select_config`, `qsa sm90`, `qsa hopper`, `qsa H20`, `qwen4_exp sparse attention tuning`: no open PR touches the sm_90 entries of this table. The open QSA PRs are #55430 (tile-union prefill kernel on SM121) and #55122 (deterministic persistent top-k), both orthogonal; #55557 (merged) added the sm_120 table this PR sits next to.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -k "select_config_regions or sm90_"
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 128 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 --candidates 64,4,2 32,8,1 32,6,1
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 1 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 --candidates 32,64,4 64,64,2
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 128 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 --kv-dtype fp8 --candidates 64,4,2 32,6,1
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 4 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 --kv-dtype fp8 --candidates 32,64,4 64,64,4
```

In addition, on 8× H20 (TP8/EP8, MTP3, bf16 K/V, `--cudagraph-capture-sizes 1 4 16 64 256 512`), stock vs this PR: server start and graph capture, `vllm bench serve` random 8k-in/1k-out at C1 (8 prompts) and C128 (256 prompts), greedy generations with `logprobs` on 16 prompts, and GSM8K through lm-evaluation-harness (0-shot chat template, greedy, first 300 problems, identical prompts on both servers).

## Test Result

Unit tests (H20, main `fc8132a5` tree):

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `-k "select_config_regions or sm90_"` | 11 passed |
| whole file | 83 passed, 0 failed |

Sweep script (H20; `current` is the entry this PR selects):

| shape | K/V | this PR | GB300 entry | GB300 vs this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 rows, group 3 | bf16 | (32, 4, 1) 343 µs | (64, 4, 2) 387 µs | +13 % |
| 4 rows, group 3 | bf16 | (64, 64, 2) 12.6 µs | (32, 64, 4) 14.9 µs | +18 % hot / +10 % L2-evicted |
| 512 rows, group 3 | fp8 | (32, 4, 1) 330 µs | (64, 4, 2) 577 µs | +75 % |
| 16 rows, group 3 | fp8 | (64, 64, 2) 24.5 µs | (32, 64, 4) 29.1 µs | +18 % |

Serving (8× H20, bf16 K/V; one launch per arm, so the tok/s differences are within the 1–3 % stock-vs-stock drift of this box and only show the absence of a regression):

| point | stock | this PR | failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1, 8 prompts | 263.6 tok/s | 259.1 tok/s | 0 / 0 |
| C128, 256 prompts | 1649.0 tok/s | 1674.8 tok/s | 0 / 0 |

Both servers captured every PIECEWISE and FULL graph size. The patched server's Triton cache holds only the (1 warp, N32) and (2 warps, N64) attention specializations; the stock one also has (4 warps, N32), i.e. the sm_90 table is the one running.

Model evaluation. The split count changes the split-K reduction order, so greedy outputs diverge from stock at near-ties: at every divergence the top-1/top-2 margin is 0–0.75 logprob (0–6 bf16 ULPs) and the other arm's token is inside the top-5; 12 of 16 chat prompts have bit-identical first-token top-5 logprobs.

| GSM8K, 0-shot chat, greedy, 300 problems | flexible-extract exact match |
|---|---|
| stock | 85.0 % ± 2.1 |
| this PR | 86.3 % ± 2.0 |

## AI assistance

Claude were used for the implementation, benchmark scripts and this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

title: [Bugfix] Isolate supplemental FlashInfer BF16 autotuning
author: jiahanc
body:
## Purpose

The supplemental 32-token FlashInfer BF16 warmup currently applies its bounded `tuning_buckets` to every operation in the dummy run. An MXFP8 drafter GEMM with M=40 can consequently inherit the BF16 bucket cap and reuse a low-M tactic that does not support its input.

Run this supplemental pass after the full-model autotune context exits. Only `flashinfer_bf16_mm` enables tuning and installs the BF16 buckets; other operations execute using their normal cache lookup or fallback. Preserve the existing token-count helper's default behavior while excluding the supplemental BF16 pass from the full-op loop. Deferred-MoE tuning retains its own pass even when its token limit is also 32. Skip-op controls, HiSparse skip-attention, distributed tuning and cache persistence remain in effect.

This isolates the BF16 supplemental pass; it does not change the bucket policy of full-model/deferred-MoE passes or provide a general cached-tactic validity fix. Related: #50572, #55377 and https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5269.

Duplicate-work checks found no equivalent isolation fix. #54524 changes default BF16 backend selection, while #55671 migrates autotune cache persistence; neither isolates the supplemental BF16 tuning context.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/utils/flashinfer.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
```

Existing repository pytest targets (not added or modified by this PR; the full pytest run was not completed):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/kernels/test_flashinfer_bf16_gemm.py -q
```

## Test Result

- The two modified files passed Ruff, formatting and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13 in a clean tracked-files snapshot. `git diff --check` passed. Repository-wide pre-commit also reports pre-existing EC connector docstring/formatting issues; those unrelated files are intentionally unchanged by this PR.

**Single-GPU validation on PR head `16964585e3`:** NVIDIA B200, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CuTe DSL 4.7.0, FlashInfer source at `d3ad3b1387078a61f846df91e07bbdad8fb70df6`. Standalone probes execute the changed vLLM source functions with real FlashInfer autotuning and CUDA kernels, bypassing unrelated vLLM package imports. These are local validation scripts, not committed tests in this PR. The results below are from those probes, not from the repository pytest command above.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| BF16 supplemental tuning | Exactly `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`; M=32 numerical comparison passed. The existing vLLM BF16 eligibility predicate accepts M=32 and rejects M=33/8192 for this CuTeDSL path. |
| MXFP8 full warmup | Completed all 21 buckets through M=8192. At `(M,N,K)=(8192,1792,5120)`, the selected tactic produced finite output with cosine similarity **0.99930** against the PyTorch reference. |
| MXFP8 inside the BF16-only pass | M=8192 remained mapped to bucket **8192**, reused the same winning tactic with autotuning disabled, and retained cosine similarity **0.99930**. It did not inherit the BF16 cap of 32. |

Separate checks passed for existing token-count behavior, skip-op propagation and exception-state restoration. The earlier M=40 scope check also confirmed that MXFP8 maps to bucket 64 during the BF16-only pass.

Full pytest collection was blocked by missing `tblib` in the available environment. The probes are not a full vLLM pytest run. End-to-end serving/model evaluation has not been run.

title: [XPU] limit FA kernel block size to multipleOf 64
author: yma11
body:
## Purpose
On XPU platform, `flash_attn_varlen_func` prefers `block_size` multipleOf 64 from performance perspective and we originally respect it by adding path in [`get_preferred_block_size`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L323). But as introduction of [`prepare_kernel_block_size`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L458), the final kernel block size changes to small numbers such as 16, 32 which are not actually preferred ones on XPU platform. This PR enforces the preference and adds warning if final kernel block size is not as expected.

Take `Microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct` for example, #53007 caused final kernel_block_size changed to `16` from previous `64`, as it picks primary block size for SWA layers which changes KV cache Spec info. XPU will follow the `prepare_kernel_block_size` flow but inject specific logic like [update_block_size_for_backend](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/platforms/xpu.py#L425), [get_preferred_block_size](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L373), and here `get_preferred_kernel_block_size`.

## Test Plan
```
python3 examples/basic/offline_inference/generate.py --model Microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct  --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 --trust_remote_code 
```

## Test Result
previous without `multipleOf[64]` limitation, it will use kernel block-size `16`:

**Note that if user explicitly sets block size using `--block-size 16`, it will be respected and warning will be printed.**

title: [torch.compile] Canonicalize functionalized split slices for fusion pa…
author: laithsakka
body:
### Purpose
PyTorch 2.15 changed functionalization replay for multi-output views in [pytorch/pytorch#194037](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/194037). Individual split_with_sizes outputs are now regenerated as contiguous slice nodes.

This graph change prevented vLLM passes that expect a canonical split_with_sizes plus getitem representation from matching. It caused:

1. QKNormRoPEFusionPass to report norm_rope_fusion=0 instead of 6.
2. ScatterSplitReplacementPass to leave two slice_scatter operations in the graph.

### This PR 
Extend SplitCoalescingPass to convert complete, contiguous, unit-step slice partitions into one split_with_sizes node with indexed getitem users.

The rewrite is deliberately conservative. It requires concrete bounds, positive widths, full dimension coverage, compatible tensor metadata, and no gaps or overlaps. 

## Fix existing 
This PR also fixes an existing SplitCoalescingPass correctness bug. Previously, two split_with_sizes nodes were considered duplicates when they had the same input and split sizes, even if they split different dimensions:
```
split_with_sizes(x, [4, 4], dim=0)
split_with_sizes(x, [4, 4], dim=1)
```
The pass could incorrectly replace one with the other. The updated coalescing identity includes the normalized split dimension, so only semantically equivalent splits are merged. The new regression test verifies that splits on different dimensions remain separate.

### Test Plan
python -m ruff format --check \
  vllm/compilation/passes/utility/split_coalescing.py \
  tests/compile/passes/test_split_coalescing.py

python -m ruff check \
  vllm/compilation/passes/utility/split_coalescing.py \
  tests/compile/passes/test_split_coalescing.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/passes/test_split_coalescing.py \
  tests/compile/passes/test_scatter_split_replace.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/passes/test_qk_norm_rope_fusion.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python -m pytest -q \
  'tests/compile/fusions_e2e/test_tp1_quant.py::test_tp1_fp8_fusions[inductor_partition-+quant_fp8,-rms_norm-6-TRITON_ATTN-Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-<lambda>-model_kwargs1-<lambda>-False]'
### Test Result
Before:
```
norm_rope_fusion expected: [6], found: [0]
```
```
test_scatter_split_replace[float16]:
assert op_count(aten.slice_scatter.default) == 0
found: 2
```
```
test_scatter_split_replace[bfloat16]:
assert op_count(aten.slice_scatter.default) == 0
found: 2
After:
```
all pass after

author: liusy58
body:
## Purpose

Under `--load-format ipc_cache`, the MTP draft model was not served by the weight cache daemon: the engine either reloaded it from disk or sent it to the target daemon with a mismatching fingerprint.

The launcher now starts a second daemon group for the MTP draft, with its own cache key, sockets (`*_draft0.sock`) and rendezvous port (`--weight-cache-draft-master-port`). On the engine side, get_draft_load_config routes an MTP draft to that group and lets other draft types (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark) fall back to disk. Only MTP drafts are cached; the draft must use the target's TP size.

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache][GLM-5.3-Flash] Disable slot mapping kernel for the kpool tail buffer
author: simondanielsson
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57227.

GLM-5.3-Flash crashes with MAF when sending 500k ISL prompts.  This is caused by out of bounds indexing in the default `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` applied to the Kpool tail buffer. The kpool tail buffer has a fixed size for each request and anyway uses its own slot mapping kernel `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping`, and hence should not use the default kernel.

**Alternatively: make KpoolTailSpec inherit from CircularBufferSpec instead of the SW spec.**

## Why

The KpoolTailSpec is a ring buffer with one block per requests, and is addressed by `pos % kpool` (bounded). The generic slot mapping kernel `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` addresses by `pos // kernel_block_size` (unbounded), and it's used to be enabled for all kv specs except for `CircularBufferSpec`. 

#53781 refactored what kv specs should use this generic slot mapping kernel to instead those specs declaring `uses_slot_mapping: true`. However, KpoolTailSpec inherits from SW and not the circular buffer spec, meaning it still deemed to use the generic slot mapping kernel even though it's a ring buffer. Since that kernels addressing grows unbounded with sequence length (`pos // kernel_block_size`) while the actual KpoolTail buffer is fixed in size, this eventually triggered a MAF at long enough requests.

This PR fixes is it by excluding not using this generic slot mapping kernel for KpoolTailSpec. Instead it just relies on its tailored `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` inside the metadata builder.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Register int8 scaled_mm as a custom op
author: limkcreply
body:
### What is wrong

`TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` calls `triton_scaled_mm` directly at line 134. That function is plain Python. It picks a tile shape from `triton.next_power_of_2(M)`, does some reshapes and asserts, then launches a Triton kernel.

There is no custom op wrapper around it, so dynamo and inductor trace straight into all of that. The fp8 block scaled path a few lines below in the same file does have one, registered as `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm_func`. So fp8 is opaque to the compiler and int8 is not.

### What it costs

Measured on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, Strix Halo), vLLM 0.28.0 built for ROCm 7.2. One linear layer at the fused gate_up shape N=34816 K=5120, one token of decode so M=1:

```
eager, called directly              1.321 ms    134.9 GB/s
torch.compile, called directly     38.072 ms      4.7 GB/s
torch.compile, through a custom op  1.314 ms    135.6 GB/s
```

End to end on a Qwen3.5 27B model quantized to int8 w8a8 with AMD Quark. Same server flags both runs, default cudagraph mode, the patch is the only difference:

```
                  single stream    4 concurrent
before             2.17 tok/s        8.40 tok/s
after              5.15 tok/s       19.37 tok/s
```

Three runs each way. Before: 59.10, 59.09, 59.11 seconds. After: 24.88, 24.86, 24.88 seconds.

The same model in bf16 is not affected either way, 4.10 tok/s compiled against 4.04 eager, so this is specific to the int8 path.

No setting recovers it. `--enforce-eager` is the only mitigation and it still lands at 5.02 tok/s, below the patched number, and it turns off compilation for the rest of the model.

### The fix

Register `int8_scaled_mm_func` with a fake impl and call that from `apply_weights`. This mirrors what `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm_func` already does a few lines below.

Output is unchanged. `torch.allclose` against the unpatched kernel passes at rtol 1e-2 atol 1e-2, and generation on the 27B model reads the same as before.

### Testing notes

I only have gfx1151, so that is the only hardware this was measured on. On CUDA the cutlass int8 kernel is normally picked ahead of the Triton one, so fewer users reach this path there and I could not measure it. The change is platform neutral. It adds a wrapper and does not touch the kernel or the tile selection.

This is int8 w8a8 only. AWQ, GPTQ and compressed-tensors W4A16 go through Marlin, `awq_triton` or `wNa16` and are untouched.

### Repro without a large model

```python
import torch
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.triton_scaled_mm import triton_scaled_mm

N, K = 34816, 5120
w = torch.randint(-127, 127, (K, N), dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
ws = torch.rand(N, 1, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
x = torch.randint(-127, 127, (1, K), dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
xs = torch.rand(1, 1, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")

c = torch.compile(triton_scaled_mm, dynamic=True, fullgraph=True)
c(x, w, xs, ws, torch.bfloat16, None)
```

Time the compiled call against the plain one. On gfx1151 the compiled one is about 29 times slower.

title: [Bugfix] Max-load throughput cliff when `max_num_seqs` is not a multiple of 8
author: andylolu2
body:
## Why

By default, cudagraphs are captured in (mostly) multiples of 8. When `max_num_seqs` is not set to a multiple of 8, it has the unfortunate side effect that the last bucket of batch sizes doesn't fall into a FULL cuda graph. For example, with `max_num_seqs=100` (and no spec decode), we get:

| Num decodes | Cudagraph mode |
|---|---:|
| 95 | FULL |
| 96 | FULL |
| 97 | PIECEWISE |
| 98 | PIECEWISE |
| 99 | PIECEWISE |
| 100 | PIECEWISE |

This is quite bad practically, because servers can get stuck in the slow PIECEWISE mode when it's overloaded (num_running_reqs = max_num_seqs).

In a TP4/B200 reproduction this was not a small boundary effect: batch 97 started behind batch 96 and progressively slowed over a 2,000-token decode, eventually falling below 1,000 tok/s/server. Adding the legal FULL-100 shape removed the cliff.

## Fix

This is actually already correctly handled when spec decode is turned on by #50488, but not when spec dec is off. The fix is to simply piggy-back off the PR's changes: when the inferred default is used without speculative decoding, add `max_num_seqs` as the widest uniform-decode shape if it fits under the existing capture ceiling:

```python
elif max_num_seqs <= max_cudagraph_capture_size:
    uniform_decode_sizes = [max_num_seqs]
```

For the example above, the ladder becomes:

```text
..., 88, 96, 100, 104, 112, ...
```

The unchanged graph manager then produces FULL descriptors through 100, while later sizes remain PIECEWISE-only.

## Benchmark evidence

The reproducer used [Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603) with TP4 on B200, `max_num_seqs=100`, logprobs enabled, 2,000 generated tokens, and a production-shaped prompt distribution with roughly equal mass around 8k, 16k, 32k, 64k, and 127k input tokens.

| Batch | Before | With FULL 100 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 96 | 3,753 tok/s | 3,760.78 tok/s |
| 97 | 1,523 tok/s | **3,876.85 tok/s** |

Batch 97 improved 2.55× (+154.6%) and became comparable to batch 96. Before the fix its server-throughput windows decayed from 2,922 tok/s near output token 302 to 829 tok/s in the final window. After the fix they stayed flat at 3,923, 3,890, 3,862, and 3,824 tok/s. Total time fell from 129.72 s to 52.41 s.

An Nsight trace showed that the PIECEWISE path accumulated tensor-parallel rank drift: attention remained around 0.58 ms, while graph-launch gaps grew from about 0.69 ms to 5.5 ms and MNNVL all-reduce wait medians grew from about 10 µs to 3.6–4.7 ms. This PR avoids that path for a legal decode batch; it does not attempt to independently repair PIECEWISE rank drift.

## Test results

```text
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/test_config.py \
  -k default_cudagraph_capture_size_respects_platform_ceiling
11 passed, 61 deselected

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  -k 'uniform_decode_pads_up_to_full_graph or uniform_decode_exact_match_is_not_over_padded or uniform_decode_beyond_capture_ladder_falls_back or divisor_query_len_dispatch_is_unchanged'
6 passed, 5 deselected

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/vllm.py tests/compile/test_config.py
all hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and repository checks
```

Revert check: with the production hunk reverted while retaining the new test, both cases fail (`2 failed`): neither 100 nor 101 is present in the inferred capture sizes.

No model evaluation was run because this changes only which execution graph serves an already-valid shape; model operations and outputs are unchanged.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `max_num_seqs`, `cudagraph`, `capture sizes`, `off-stride`, and `uniform decode`. The nearby work addresses different contracts:

- #50488 introduced `uniform_decode_sizes` for speculative decoding and deliberately kept non-speculative defaults unchanged. This PR closes that remaining non-speculative boundary hole using its abstraction.
- #37865 appends `max_cudagraph_capture_size`; here that value is 200, so it still does not add the required 100-request boundary.
- #55004 covers uniform decode under an explicitly configured scalar maximum, primarily with speculative decoding. This PR changes only the inferred default and leaves explicit configuration untouched.
- #53407 lets a uniform decode pad to a wider compatible FULL graph, but it requires such a graph to exist. In this case 104 requests exceeds the scheduler limit, so there is no compatible FULL graph until 100 is captured.
- #56136 concerns candidate ladders for multiple dynamic-speculation query lengths, not the non-speculative capture set.
- #54352 is a draft auto-revert for the memory regression caused when #50488 raised capture ceilings. This patch never raises the ceiling and adds only a shape already below it.

No open PR covers an off-stride, non-speculative `max_num_seqs` boundary.

## Reviewer guide

- `vllm/config/vllm.py`: the two-line behavior change reuses the uniform-decode capture-size path; the nearby comment is updated to match its broadened scope.
- `tests/compile/test_config.py`: one new parameter exercises the existing capture-boundary contract at `max_num_seqs=100`.

There are no moves, generated files, or mechanical propagation changes.

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation, patch, tests, duplicate-work audit, and PR write-up. I reviewed every changed line and the benchmark evidence before submission.

title: [CI] Make ci-clean-log.sh portable to macOS/BSD sed
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

`.buildkite/scripts/ci-clean-log.sh` (used by `ci-fetch-log.sh` to strip timestamps/ANSI codes from CI logs) used GNU-only `sed` invocations:
- `-i` with no backup suffix
- `-r` for extended regex

On macOS (BSD `sed`), `sed -i` requires a backup-suffix argument and ERE is enabled with `-E`, so the script failed with `sed: invalid command code` and `ci-fetch-log.sh` could not clean logs locally. This PR detects GNU vs BSD `sed` once and routes all in-place edits through a `sedi` wrapper that supplies the correct `-i` form and ERE flag for each platform.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Checked open PRs/issues for `ci-clean-log`, `sed`, and `ci-fetch-log`; no existing PR addresses the GNU/BSD portability of this script.

## Test plan / commands run

- Verified the cleaned output on a synthetic log containing all three target patterns (ISO timestamp, `ESC _bk;t=… BEL` marker, ANSI color codes) — all stripped, exit 0, on macOS BSD sed.
- Verified the previously-broken stdout path now works: `ci-fetch-log.sh 89402 <job_uuid> -` produced output with zero remaining `_bk;t=` markers.
- `pre-commit run` (shellcheck) passes on the changed file.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code), surfaced during a CI flakiness investigation that used `ci-fetch-log.sh` to read failing-attempt logs on macOS.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Release consumed MRV2 CPU inputs
author: Sy0307
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Release consumed request-local CPU multimodal payloads from MRV2 workers while requests are still decoding. This extends #52041's prefix-hit stripping to inputs that actually reached a worker, while retaining EngineCore replay data and GPU embeddings.

## Claims

- Release each occurrence only after its placeholder range is confirmed consumed; exclude in-flight prefill, unconfirmed output placeholders and inputs being encoded in the same step.
- Restore payloads when KV-load rollback schedules encoding again, including inputs initially stripped by a prefix hit. Preemption and streaming request installation rebuild tracking.
- Keep SHM processor-cache descriptors on their existing ACK protocol. MRV1 and encoder embedding eviction are unchanged.

## Validation

Code baseline: `2f1041e8dd05415d9984d0a83ad957d54a049eb4`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused scheduler regressions | 8 passed |
| Entire `test_encoder_runner.py` | 25 passed |
| Qwen3-VL live-generation regression, unchanged main | Fails: worker still holds the image payload after three steps while the request is alive |
| Same real-model regression, this patch | Passes: payload released, request completes 16 output tokens |
| Changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX and CI tethering | Passed |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

CPU commands:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k cpu_encoder_input -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py -q
```

`--confcutdir` is only for the local macOS environment. Expanded scheduler/output testing had the same two unrelated failures on both arms: missing root `caplog_vllm` fixture and the local no-Triton fallback rejecting async MRV1+PP. The original main had 255 passes; the initial patch had 260 passes, and the three subsequent parameter cases passed separately.

Real-model reproducer on one H200:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_memory_leak.py -k consumed_cpu_inputs -v -s
```

Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, greedy, eager. Both arms used Torch 2.14.0, Transformers 5.20.2 and FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1. The native wheel is `921ed7fa1`; its only difference from the tested main is `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml`, so runtime and native sources match. `VLLM_MODEL_REDIRECT_PATH` pointed the existing model name at the local weight snapshot.

The GPU regression uses the real LLM entry point and the worker's actual EncoderCache, and is selected by the existing Multimodal Models Standard 4 job. Scheduler regressions exercise real constructors, scheduled outputs, forced preemption and invalid-block rollback. Worker tests verify storage reclamation, independent ownership and restored inputs reaching `EncoderRunner.prepare_mm_inputs`.

TP=2 integration checks also used Qwen3-VL on physical H200 GPUs 2/3, with the tensor arena enabled, processor caching disabled, prefix caching enabled, and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:

| Live request at step 4 | Main | This patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1024px image, below the arena threshold | Both workers retain approximately 6 MiB of inputs | Both workers drop their inputs |
| 1536px image, confirmed arena allocation | Both workers retain approximately 13.5 MiB; slot readers remain unacknowledged | Both workers drop their inputs; a fully acknowledged, reusable slot is observed before request completion |

Each arm completed a first request and a repeated-prefix request with 32 output tokens each. Token IDs matched exactly across main/patch in both image-size cases; cancellation cleared request-local cache entries. These are small deterministic comparisons, not a full quality evaluation. Slot snapshots are asynchronous; the memory figures describe each worker's payload references, not additive physical-memory savings. Cancellation may still leave short-lived references outside EncoderCache.

The node could not initialize NVLS multicast, including on main; both TP2 arms ran with `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`. Existing fallback all-reduce paths were used without changing vLLM code. No GPU synchronization error was raised. Physical GPUs 4/5 were excluded throughout.

Current-revision host-memory A/B (Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, MRV2, TP=2, physical H200 GPUs 0/2): 16 distinct 1536px image requests arriving in two waves of 8, each generating 128 tokens. Each configuration/arm had two independent engine starts with reversed arm order on the second start, one warmup and three formal rounds per start. PSS sums the driver/EngineCore and its worker process tree, avoiding shared-page double counting. Means below use snapshots with all 16 requests alive and each having generated at least 8, 32 and 64 tokens.

| Configuration | Main decode PSS | Patch decode PSS | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default 4 GiB LRU processor cache, arena off | 6.950 GiB | 6.567 GiB | 393.0 MiB / 5.52% |
| Processor cache off, arena off | 6.733 GiB | 6.303 GiB | 440.7 MiB / 6.39% |
| Processor cache off, arena on | 8.493 GiB | 8.131 GiB | 370.1 MiB / 4.26% |

Worker request-cache input references fell from approximately 216 MiB per rank to zero in all cases. With the arena enabled, slot-exhaustion fallbacks fell from 8 to 0 per round; all 8 slots became reusable while requests were still alive. The arena's 2 GiB pinned mapping remains allocated, so this is slot reuse, not unmapping the arena. In this small workload, the arena's fixed mapping also makes its absolute PSS larger than the arena-off configuration.

Corresponding output token IDs matched for all 576 formal requests across the three configurations, with 128 tokens per request. The two independent-start PSS reductions with default LRU caching were 402.0 and 383.9 MiB. These are workload-specific decode-residency measurements, not universal percentages or exact prefill peaks. The driver and EngineCore share a process in this harness; workers use the real multiprocess TP executor. Configuration: eager, max model length 4096, batched tokens 2048, sequences 16, GPU memory utilization 0.20, seed 0, prefix caching enabled with distinct inputs, NVLS disabled equally on both arms, and GPU sync checking enabled. No allocator trimming or production-code instrumentation was used. EngineCore replay inputs and its LRU cache are still retained.

No throughput speedup or full accuracy result is claimed for this revision. KV-load failure restoration is covered by CPU scheduler/worker tests, not a distributed KV-transfer model run.

## Details

A single `SchedulerOutput.encoder_input_updates` map carries payload replacement by request ID and input index: `None` releases an input; a payload restores it. An index has one update per step, avoiding separate restore/free ordering. The scheduler tracks only remaining releasable inputs and stops scanning once none remain.

Workers apply updates after request installation and RoPE position initialization. Replacing entries in a worker-owned list preserves EngineCore's original feature objects, including with the uniprocess executor. The same placeholder metadata remains available for embedding gathering and PrefixLM ranges.

Related work and scope:

- #52041/#53456 handle stripping before initial position computation. This patch releases after that initialization and does not change their metadata rules.
- #54994 preserves SHM address references; those descriptors remain excluded here.
- #51207 shares transport storage. It does not release request-local references, and its slots cannot be reused until their storage references are dropped. This PR adds no COW or other transport.
- #62834 checks remote encoder embedding readiness during EPD replay; it does not restore a local worker's raw inputs for re-encoding.
- Open #50871 clears EngineCore inputs for resumable sessions. This patch requires retained EngineCore payloads for rollback; combining the two requires an explicit replay policy.
- #56813 caches position ranges, which this patch does not change; #56826/#62850 optimize other cache cleanup. None implements this running-request payload lifecycle.

No user-facing configuration or behavior contract is added, so no separate design document is introduced. AI assistance was used for implementation, upstream comparison, review and validation.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** One request-local lifecycle change; reuses executor transport and preserves replay ownership.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** CPU regressions and a real-model base-fail/patch-pass reproducer; remaining coverage limits are explicit.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Changed-file checks pass; no unrelated transport or API abstraction.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, duplicate checks, validation and limitations updated.

title: [ROCm][CI] Adapt MoE tests to the triton_kernels 3.8 API
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose

#55934 bumped `ROCM_TRITON_KERNELS_COMMIT` in `Dockerfile.rock` to the `3.8.x` branch. The library code was updated to dispatch on `get_triton_kernels_version()`, but the two MoE test modules were not, and fail against 3.8 in four ways:

  - `matmul_ogs` -> `matmul` and `matmul_ogs_details` -> `matmul_details`, imported at module scope, so collection dies with `ModuleNotFoundError` and takes out every `MoE Kernels` shard on MI300 and MI355.
  - `PrecisionConfig.weight_scale` -> `b_mx_scale`/`b_microblock_size`; 3.8 rejects the old keyword outright.
  - `make_default_matmul_mxfp4_w_layout` and its scale counterpart return a `layout` instance rather than a `(layout, opts)` pair, so unpacking raises `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable StridedLayout object`.
  - gather/scatter indices are plain tensors, so `.src_indx`/`.dst_indx` raise `AttributeError`.

## Fixes
- Dispatch the imports on `get_triton_kernels_version()`, exactly as `config.py`, `oracle/mxfp4.py` and `mxfp4_utils.py` already do.
- Route the `PrecisionConfig` weight-scale kwargs through a shared helper: `_mx_scale_kwargs` is promoted from `oracle/mxfp4.py` to a public mx_scale_kwargs` in `mxfp4_utils.py`, beside its existing read-side twin `weight_mx_scale`, so the tests are not reaching into a private helper. `oracle/mxfp4.py` imports it under the old private name, leaving its six call sites untouched.
- Add `mxfp4_w_layouts()` to the MoE tests' own `utils.py` and use it from both modules, so the layout dispatch lives in one place rather than being duplicated.
- Skip `test_routing_data_from_sparse_topk_parity` on 3.8. There `routing_data_from_sparse_topk` simply forwards to `make_routing_data`, so the test would be vacuously comparing a function against itself. This mirrors the existing 3.5.1 skip.


## Test Plan
AMD CI is run against this PR on both [ROCm 7.2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13107) and [ROCm 10](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13103), paying attention to the previously failing `MoE Kernels` test groups on both MI300X and MI355X and the MI355X `FP8 MoE Kernels` test group.

## Test Result
The test groups now pass, and there are no new regressions.

title: [Model] Use upstream GLM-5.3 and Qwen4-Exp configs and processor
author: hmellor
body:
## Purpose

Transformers ships `glm5_next` as of **v5.16.1** and `qwen4_exp` as of **v5.16.0**, so the vendored copies can go. Raises the `transformers` floor in `requirements/common.txt` from `>= 5.10.4` to `>= 5.16.1` — CI already pins `transformers==5.16.1` exactly in `requirements/test/{cuda,rocm,xpu}.in`, so this only makes the declared minimum match what is already tested.

Removed:

- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/glm5_next.py` (420 lines)
- `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/glm5next.py` (953 lines)
- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/qwen4_exp.py`
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/config.py`

Net **-1961 lines**.

### Not a straight deletion

The upstream classes are not drop-in replacements, so the model code moves to their spellings:

| vLLM read | upstream ships |
|---|---|
| `mla_nope` | `mla_use_nope` |
| `num_experts_per_token` | `num_experts_per_tok` |
| `moe_renormalize` | `norm_topk_prob` |
| `mhc_num_residual_streams` | `hc_mult` |
| `mhc_sinkhorn_iterations` | `hc_sinkhorn_iters` |

`is_moe` / `is_kda_layer` / `is_linear_attn` now derive from `layer_types`, and text-level reads go through `hf_text_config` now that the top-level config no longer mirrors its `text_config` via `__getattribute__`.

I verified the rename table by loading the real `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` `config.json` through upstream's `Glm5NextConfig` and diffing the resolved attribute surface against every attribute the model tree reads.

### Behaviour deliberately preserved

Three things in the vendored code were intentional divergences, not schema, and are kept with their explanations:

1. **Vision `rms_norm_eps` stays 1e-6.** The checkpoint ships 1e-5 and upstream honours it; the vendored config force-overrode it because 1e-5 "produces repetitive/degraded image descriptions". Now a named constant at its single call site.
2. **The frame sampler moves to `Glm5NextVideoBackend._sample_frame_indices`**, its only consumer, rather than being replaced by upstream's `sample_frames`. See the open question below — this one is worth a second look.
3. **The `NotImplementedError` guards** for config options this implementation lacks move into `_validate_supported_config`, called from `Glm5NextModel.__init__`.

Three GLM-5.3 values have no source in either the checkpoint or the upstream config, so they become named constants rather than silently-missing attributes: `mhc_tau` (0.05), `mhc_post_mult_value` (2.0), `logit_scale` (1.0).

### Hybrid layer accounting

Both vendored configs supplied a `layers_block_type` property that mapped their sparse-attention layer type onto `"attention"`. Without it, `ModelConfig.get_num_layers_by_block_type` falls through to its `layer_types` branch, which only recognised `"full_attention"` — so both models would have counted **zero** attention layers. It now counts `deepseek_sparse_attention` and `qwen_sparse_attention` too, which is what both properties did.

`_get_full_attention_layer_indices` in the turboquant config has the same blind spot, but it already checks `layer_types` first and so is unchanged by this PR. Flagging it as a separate pre-existing issue rather than widening scope here.

### Open question: the frame sampler

This PR keeps vLLM's own frame sampler, but I am not confident that is the right call and would like a view on it.

The sampler's docstring justifies diverging from the reference implementation by noting that the linspace variant "cost 4 points on video grounding evals". That comment describes only the **short-clip** branch (`total_frames < extract_t`), which requires `fps < 2`; I could not construct a case where that branch differs from upstream at all.

The branch that does differ is the common one, for an unrelated reason: vLLM walks at `1/(temporal_patch_size * target_fps)` (0.25s), collecting ~2x the candidates, then re-spreads them with `linspace`. Upstream walks at `1/target_fps` (0.5s) and keeps its picks. Over a sweep of realistic sources, **38/53 cases differ** — same frame counts, different indices:

| case | vLLM | upstream |
|---|---|---|
| 30s @30fps | `0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 76, 91, 106` | `0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105` |
| 3 frames @2fps | `0, 1, 2, 2` | `0, 1` |

vLLM's spacing drifts off the target fps and short sources pick up a duplicated tail frame from the odd-parity pad. There is also no consistency argument for keeping our own: `create_hf_metadata` sets `do_sample_frames = len(valid_frame_indices) == source.total_frames_num`, so whenever the backend sub-samples the processor is told not to re-sample, and the backend's choice is authoritative either way.

So switching to upstream's `sample_frames` would delete the last vendored piece and looks more correct on the merits — but it changes frame selection for nearly every video, so it needs a video eval that I could not run. Keeping ours (what this PR does) preserves exactly what ships today at no eval cost. Happy to switch if a reviewer with a GPU wants to take the eval.

### Dropped code left over from Qwen3-Next — please sanity-check

`Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer` selected between a MoE block and a dense `Qwen3NextMLP`:

```python
mlp_only_layers = getattr(config, "mlp_only_layers", [])
num_experts = getattr(config, "num_experts", 0) or 0
absolute_layer_id = self.layer_idx + 1
is_moe_layer = self.layer_idx not in mlp_only_layers and (
    num_experts > 0 and absolute_layer_id % config.decoder_sparse_step == 0
)
```

This is a verbatim lift of `qwen3_next.py:479-485`, which arrived with the original support PR (#53896) — Qwen4Exp derives from Qwen3-Next and still subclasses `Qwen3NextAttention` and `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`. `decoder_sparse_step` and `mlp_only_layers` are Qwen3-Next concepts; upstream's `Qwen4ExpTextConfig` declares neither, and neither appears anywhere in `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` or `...-FP8`. They only resolved because the vendored config subclassed `Qwen3NextConfig` and inherited them, which is why nothing ever flagged the branch as dead.

Evaluating the original expression against both checkpoints with the old vendored config gives `is_moe_layer` **True for 48/48 layers**, no dense layers: with `mlp_only_layers=[]`, `num_experts=512` and `decoder_sparse_step=1` it reduces to `True` for any layer index. So this PR builds the MoE block unconditionally and drops the branch, its guards and the `Qwen3NextMLP` import (`-38/+6`).

Worth a second opinion, since it is a deletion rather than a rename: a hypothetical future checkpoint setting `mlp_only_layers` or `decoder_sparse_step` would previously have been honoured and now would not. Upstream's `qwen4_exp` has no dense path at all (neither key appears in the model, and `validate_architecture` requires `num_experts > 0`), so such a checkpoint would not load in transformers either — which is why I think dropping it is right. Happy to restore it as `getattr(config, "decoder_sparse_step", 1)` with only the dead `else` removed if a reviewer would rather keep the guard.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_config.py \
       tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py \
       tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py \
       tests/multimodal/test_video.py \
       tests/test_config.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Also ran a differential check of the vendored vs upstream `smart_resize` across an 8232-point grid of sizes, frame counts and token budgets, since upstream denominates its bounds in vision tokens where the vendored one took raw pixels.

Every suite was run on this branch **and** on the base commit in a second worktree, because this machine has pre-existing video-codec failures.

| the four files above | 24 failed, 433 passed, 18 skipped | 24 failed, **430** passed, 18 skipped |

**Identical failure sets.** The −3 passed is exactly accounted for: 7 removed cases that tested the vendored config's own behaviour, 4 added for the relocated layer-type accounting. The 24 pre-existing failures are macOS video-codec and unrelated `test_vllm_config_defaults` / `test_ir_op_priority_ctx` cases, all failing identically at the base commit.

`smart_resize` differential: **8232/8232 agree, 0 mismatches.**

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files, including `mypy`.

Both public checkpoints were loaded through the upstream config classes to check the ported attribute surface directly, rather than inferring it:

- `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`: **37/39** attributes the model tree reads resolve; the two that do not are `decoder_sparse_step` and `intermediate_size`, both discussed above.
- `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`: every renamed field resolves to the expected value, and the three with no source anywhere are the named constants above.

|---|---|---|---|

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix DCP pulls across MLA cache regions
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
When prefill and decode use different cache-group layouts, as with a HiSparse decoder, NIXL matches their KV blocks by memory region. That receive path currently assumes a single source rank and fails when a DCP prefiller supplies multiple ranks.

Create a read for each source rank using the existing region mapping. For each region, reuse `_apply_dcp_prefix_caching` to select the pages owned by that rank and skip the decoder's cached prefix. Bound the reads by the sequence length and zero any remaining allocation padding. The ordinary DCP path stays unchanged. Requires unshared MLA regions with matching logical/kernel page sizes.

Independent of #55398's GPU-landing feature; #57077 covers DCP1 only.

### Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -m cpu_test -q
```
