title: [Perf] Remove CPU-GPU sync in heterogeneous vocabulary speculative decoding
author: MichaelLapshin
body: ## Purpose Remove a CPU-GPU synchronization between target and draft model execution phases during speculative decoding. This occurs specifically when heterogeneous vocabulary is used. The CPU-GPU synchronization point prevents the engine from enqueuing more draft-model CUDA kernels asynchronously during the target model's execution. So the CPU kernel launch rate becomes a bottleneck given a sufficiently small draft model decoding time. **NSYS profiling**. Notice the async compute and GPU activity drops to ~0% between target and draft model execution for a decode step. ## Test Plan **Correctness test**. These new unit tests ensure that the output of the vocabulary mapping functions return the correct token ids. ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_vocab_mapping.py -k "test_map_target_to_draft_ids or test_map_draft_to_target_ids" ``` **Performance test**. Run the following script for both this branch and main to compare the performance difference. Draft tokens are all synthetically rejected to avoid non-deterministic behaviour. ``` vllm bench throughput \ --model \ --speculative-config '{ "method": "draft_model", "model": "", "num_speculative_tokens": 8, "rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 1.0, "parallel_drafting": , "use_heterogeneous_vocab": true }' \ --num-warmups 1 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --random-input-len 128 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --num-prompts 1 ``` ## Test Result ### Correctness test The unit tests passed. ### Performance test Throughput was evaluated on a RTX 6000 Ada Generation GPU and Intel Xeon E5-2640v3 CPU. #### Vanilla speculative decoding (batch size: 1, speculative tokens: 4, parallel drafting: false, 'use_heterogeneous_vocab': true) target model | draft model | old decode throughput | new decode throughput | speedup -- | -- | -- | -- | -- Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 21.33 tps | 25.74 tps | +20.7% Qwen/Qwen3-4B | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 24.08 tps | 25.03 tps | +3.9% Qwen/Qwen3-8B | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 18.92 tps | 26.01 tps | +37.5% Qwen/Qwen3-14B | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 15.47 tps | 26.15 tps | +69.0% #### Parallel Draft (PARD) speculative decoding (batch size: 1, speculative tokens: 8, parallel drafting: true, 'use_heterogeneous_vocab': true) target model | draft model | old decode throughput | new decode throughput | speedup -- | -- | -- | -- | -- Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B | amd/PARD-Qwen2.5-0.5B | 39.93 tps | 57.02 tps | +42.8% Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B | amd/PARD-Qwen2.5-0.5B | 30.50 tps | 52.31 tps | +71.5% Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B | amd/PARD-Qwen2.5-0.5B | 20.60 tps | 28.78 tps | +39.7% ### NSYS Profiling Notice the removal of this synchronization point improves the GPU and async compute activity, and the throughput for the draft model.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable layer-aware CSA2 multi-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Purpose DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has three attention layer shapes: full CSA2 layers (2/8/14/20) run SWA + compressor + indexer and build a new global KV cache with their own Top-K indices; reindex CSA2 layers (24/28/32/36) run SWA + indexer only, re-scoring Top-K over an earlier layer's global KV cache; all other layers are dense or pure SWA. The shared v4.1 pipeline overlaps the full CSA2 layers with **three** fork/join pairs per step (input projections; Q/SWA-insert vs compressor; indexer vs cache-insert) and the reindex layers with one. On ROCm each fork/join is a HIP event pair per side stream, so the multi-stream launch cost outweighs the overlap benefit there. --- This PR gives the ROCm attention layer a layer-type-aware scheme with exactly one fork/join per step: **Full CSA2 layers (`_forward_csa2_full`)**: one 3-stream fork right after the input norm. - default stream: fused wqa+wkv → q/kv split+norm → wq_b → fused qnorm/RoPE/SWA-insert; - aux stream 0: the compressor chain (kv_score GEMM → save/compress/norm → RoPE-quant cache insert); - aux stream 1: indexer `weights_proj`. After the single join, the indexer K write (`_produce_k`, whose `wk` consumes the aux-0 latent) and the query path (`forward_q`, whose wq_b consumes the default-stream qr) run serially, followed by the indexer op and sparse MLA. **Reindex CSA2 layers (`_forward_csa2_reindex`)**: the input projections run serially first (the query path consumes qr, so overlapping the weight projection is not worth it), then one 2-stream fork overlaps the SWA q path with the indexer query path. **Dense layers**: fully serial (`aux_stream_list` disabled). --- A new shared helper `execute_in_parallel_default_first` (in `vllm/utils/multi_stream_utils.py`) mirrors `execute_in_parallel` but enqueues the default chain before the aux chains — the default chain is the longest, so starting it first shortens the step tail while the aux streams still only wait on the pre-fork default-stream work. The fork is gated exactly like the shipped v4.0 multi-stream gate (#51794/#56853): it only runs where the fork/join becomes static graph edges (inside capture, or with non-dict metadata such as the profile run); everywhere else — including MRV1, which keeps its wide eager region (#51430) — the layer falls back to the fully sequential base pipeline. The CUDA/NVIDIA path is untouched except for a behavior-neutral base refactor: the v4.1 indexer's query path is extracted into `DeepseekV4Indexer.forward_q`, still driven unchanged by the base `forward` (`_produce_k` keeps its private name). This is not a duplicate of #51794/#56853, which cover v4.0: v4.1-flash has a different topology (the indexer derives K from the kv-source compressor's latent, with no indexer-local compressor), so the overlap must differ per layer type. ## Trace Comparison (Take conc=4 as an example) **With regard to CSA2 layers with compressor and indexer (layer_id=2/8/14/20):** Before: > The default NV path launches multi-stream 3 times per layer, which is inefficient on ROCm path (multi-stream cost > overlap benefit). After (**20.76%** faster than the old pattern): --- **With regard to CSA2 layers only with indexer (layer_id=24/28/32/36):** Before: > No need to overlap indexer weight projection, since the benefit (4 μs) < the multi-stream cost (5 μs + 6 μs = 11 μs). Instead, we prefer to overlap SWA process and indexer process. After (**11.90%** faster than the old pattern): ## Test Plan Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload with server launch commands below: ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 GPU_COUNT=4 export HF_HOME=/shared/models vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8333 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --moe-backend aiter \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log \ --no-swa-bounded-replay \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \ 2>&1 | tee "${OUTDIR}/server.log" ``` Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000,tokenized_requests=False \ --batch_size auto \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log ``` > [!NOTE] > All tests based on latest `nightly-rocm100` image. ## Test Result ### Benchmark By the way, note that the e2e benefit could be small, since there are onlt **8** layers that we can optimize (overlap), while other layers always execute serially. | Conc | Version | Output token throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change | | ---: | :------ | ------------------------------: | :-----: | -------------: | :------: | -------------: | :-----: | | 1 | main | 114.47 | — | 392.61 | — | 8.32 | — | | 1 | this PR | 117.28 | 2.45% ↑ | 266.06 | 32.23% ↓ | 8.25 | 0.84% ↓ | | 4 | main | 381.72 | — | 348.33 | — | 9.86 | — | | 4 | this PR | 386.47 | 1.24% ↑ | 331.76 | 4.76% ↓ | 9.76 | 1.01% ↓ | | 16 | main | 1018.13 | — | 496.96 | — | 14.73 | — | | 16 | this PR | 1018.69 | 0.06% ↑ | 495.02 | 0.39% ↓ | 14.73 | 0.00% | | 64 | main | 1912.44 | — | 1165.33 | — | 31.71 | — | | 64 | this PR | 1920.10 | 0.40% ↑ | 1160.00 | 0.46% ↓ | 31.59 | 0.38% ↓ | In summary, the performance data indicates that this PR provides consistent throughput gains and latency reductions without introducing a regression in the tested metrics. The most noticeable benefit is at low concurrency, while at higher concurrency (conc=16 and 64) the changes are comparatively small, suggesting that the optimization has limited additional impact once the system becomes heavily loaded. ### Accuracy Test Main: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| This PR: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9371|± |0.0067| ---

title: [Perf] Give a prefill-only batch the model state's number of logit rows
author: mmastrac
body:
## Purpose

Performance win: a prefill-only batch in a diffusion model (no draft tokens scheduled) hands every request one logit row regardless of what the model state says it samples per step.

DiffusionGemma's prefill step never reads them so every prefill has to take an unnecessary full pass over the 262144-row vocabulary matrix, about an extra 8.8 ms on a GB10.

Split out of #57250.

## Test plan

Hardware: 1 DGX Spark.

Model: `nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4`

Serve with: `--diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 32}' --max-logprobs 32 --enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling`, before/after patch (or torch profiler)

## Test Results

Before/after with the model runner swapped and nothing else changed:

median read | time
-|-
before, one row per request	| 116.5 ms 
 after	| 106.9 ms 

Before: `compute_logits` runs on every DiffusionGemma prefill step, ~8.8 ms per prefill in the torch profile.

After: no logits pass on prefill steps, decode steps unchanged, 32-way concurrency sweep with logprobs passes. Autoregressive models unchanged and take the same branch with one row per request, as before.

title: [Kernel][MiniMax-M3] Add Triton query-tiled sparse prefill tuned on Hopper
author: NVShreyas
body:
## Purpose

MiniMax-M3 sparse prefill currently launches one Triton program per query token. Adjacent queries often select overlapping sparse KV blocks, so this PR adds an opt-in query-tiled kernel that:

- groups adjacent queries into one program,
- enumerates the distinct union of their selected blocks,
- loads each union K/V block once, and
- gates each block by per-query membership and causality.

Hopper selects the tiled prefill kernel automatically; other CUDA architectures continue to use the generic scalar kernel. The decode kernel now validates persistent top-k block IDs before dereferencing the block table, which makes mixed chunked-prefill/prefix-reuse batches safe.

This is not a duplicate of the open MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention work:

- #52963 targets ROCm/gfx950.
- #55372 targets query-tiled verify-decode attention, while this PR targets prefill.

AI assistance was used to implement, test, benchmark, and prepare this change. The human submitter reviewed the complete diff and approved submission.

## Test Plan

Correctness (H100 Buildkite):

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py
```

The one-off microbenchmark harness is not included in the tree. The H200 matrix covers the original scalar, standalone tiled, and PR implementations; tile sizes 1/2/4/8/16/32; six prefill geometries; BF16 and FP8 KV; and 16/8/0 shared selections out of top-k 16.

## Test Result

### Correctness

title: [Core][Kernel] Share persistent workspaces for Marlin and Humming
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Co-authored by: ErinYin <liang.yin@daocloud.io>

Humming grouped MoE currently retains permutation scratch in every layer, so its persistent memory grows with the number of layers. Marlin lock buffers are also owned by individual layers or kernels, tying their lifetime to weight preparation and reload.

This PR gives both resources a shared owner in `WorkspaceManager`:

- Add `get_persistent_resource(key, factory)` for objects with stable storage and `get_persistent(...)` for fixed-shape tensors. Resources are cached separately for each `(ubatch, lane)` and must exist before workspace locking.
- Share compatible Humming `MoEPermuteScratch` objects across sequential layers. Compatibility includes capacity, routing dimensions, device, hidden size, and dtype.
- Acquire Marlin locks at execution time, with separate buffers for concurrent CUDA streams as well as ubatches and lanes. Zero-initialize once; successful Marlin calls restore their counters to zero.
- Resolve dense Marlin workspace lookup inside a runtime custom op so `torch.compile` does not trace execution-context selection.
- Preserve standalone allocation when no workspace manager exists and support explicit Marlin workspaces.

### Relationship to existing work

This combines the direction of #50626 and #56764 with a general resource API. #50626 is the earlier tensor-only Marlin implementation; #56764 adds a Humming-specific cache and accessor to `WorkspaceManager`. Here, the manager handles resource lifetime and execution-slot isolation, while each backend defines its own resource and compatibility key. The intent is to consolidate both changes around that shared API.

Addresses the memory issue in #56759 and relates to the runtime-storage ownership discussion in #48312. Searches for those issues and for `marlin workspace`, `workspace persistent`, and `humming scratch` found the related PRs above; the distinction is the combined, backend-independent resource API.

#55105 remains complementary: its dispatch-capacity and runtime-dtype fixes can feed into the shared scratch accessor, while its activation-buffer fixes stay in Humming. Those fixes are not included here.

## Test Plan

Tests cover resource reuse and locking, standalone fallback, isolation across execution slots and CUDA streams, weight-preparation behavior, and compiled Marlin execution. Permutation tests compare outputs with and without persistent scratch; CUDA graph tests change inputs, routing, and graph sizes to detect stale metadata or aliasing.

Latest targeted runs on NVIDIA B300:

```bash
# 488 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  -k 'permute or humming or workspace or persistent' --timeout=180 -q

# 20 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_scratch_isolated_across_execution_slots \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py --timeout=180 -q

# 1 passed; run with FlashInfer 0.6.17 pinned via PYTHONPATH
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_scratch_reused_across_graph_sizes \
  --timeout=180 -q

# 112 passed, 13 skipped
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_tile_padding.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
  -k 'marlin or workspace' --timeout=180 -q

# 1 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py -k persistent_locks -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run
git diff --check
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, and repository checks.

Before publication, the commit was rebased onto `f3aa88d230`. The only conflict was an obsolete Marlin workspace docstring; the implementation was preserved. Hooks passed again, followed by **60 passed** in this focused run (FlashInfer 0.6.17 pinned via `PYTHONPATH`):

```bash
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py \
  -k 'persistent or humming or scratch or marlin_prepare_layer or marlin_post_load or marlin_workspace' \
  --timeout=180 -q
```

## Test Result

### Humming memory

Before the rebase, compared clean base `35dc273072ff133743bc5fcfa306bf030fa8730b` with this change using the same compiled extensions and dependency versions. Model: `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`, revision `a1ff8c8967426709e5528307c14c52c17616b008` (40 MoE layers, hidden size 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8).

Configuration: one B300, TP=1/DP=1, BF16, Humming for linear and MoE, **`VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped`**. Worker probes confirmed all 40 layers used `HummingGroupedExperts`. Fixed 8 GiB KV cache, max model length 8192, max sequences 32, async scheduling disabled, seed 0, V2 runner, compilation and CUDA graphs enabled with capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.17.

Live PyTorch GPU allocation immediately after initialization, in GiB (2^30 bytes):

| Max batched tokens | Before | After | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2048 | 33.412 | 30.953 | **2.459** |
| 8192 | 41.352 | 31.516 | **9.836** |

The number of scratch objects falls from 40 to 1. At 8192 tokens, their storage falls from 10330.684 MiB to 258.267 MiB: **97.5% less scratch memory**. Each distinct configuration or concurrently active execution slot still needs separate storage. Fixing the KV-cache budget keeps vLLM from consuming the saving as a larger KV cache.

The 8192-token pair ran sequentially on the same reserved GPU, with fresh processes. The 2048-token baseline and repeated full baseline used another B300 of the same model. These measurements do not establish a latency improvement.

### Model evaluation

Full GSM8K with the grouped Humming configuration above, 1319 questions, five shots, greedy sampling, and a 256-output-token limit, using the repository's GSM8K prompt/scoring helpers:

| Run | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 1208/1319 | 91.58% | 1 |
| After | 1203/1319 | 91.21% | 1 |
| Before, repeated control | 1201/1319 | 91.05% | 1 |

The candidate falls within the observed baseline accuracy range. This does **not** establish bitwise equivalence or rule out a causal accuracy effect: 690/1319 token sequences match between before/after, while only 669/1319 match between the two unmodified baseline runs. Repeated greedy requests also vary on both versions, including after prefix-cache resets; the cause remains unresolved.

Marlin additionally passed the repository GSM8K serving evaluation on 128 questions with five shots: **119/128 (92.97%), zero invalid answers**, using the same model with both backends set to Marlin, max sequences 16, max batched tokens 2048, and graph sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]`.

### Remaining validation

No H200 or end-to-end distributed DeepEP v2/HT/LL, DBO, or DSpark serving run was performed. Expert-map and execution-slot tests cover local behavior and do not substitute for those runs. The model evaluation uses BF16/SILU and does not cover the FP8/SITU cases discussed in #55105.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing, and drafting this PR.

title: [Kernel][DSV4.1] Fuse MXFP8 wo_b GEMM with sequence-parallel reduce-scatter
author: gcanlin
body:
## Purpose

Under sequence parallel, DeepSeek-V4.1's `wo_b` runs as an MXFP8 row-parallel GEMM followed by a TP reduce-scatter: two kernels and one HBM round trip per layer. This PR fuses them with the SM100 GEMM-RS kernel. It builds on @gau-nernst's MXFP8 support for the Kimi-K3 GEMM-RS/AR kernel (the first five commits), moves that kernel to `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/cute_dsl/gemm_rs_ar.py` so both models share one workspace, init gate, warmup, test and benchmark, and binds V4.1's `wo_b` to it behind `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1` (default off; this single flag replaces `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_RS` and gates the Kimi-K3 RS path too — `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_AR` is unchanged). The decoder layer skips its own `sp_reduce_scatter` when bound; RS zero-fills output rows beyond M for callers that pass an unpadded token count. Requires SM100, BF16 model dtype, sequence parallel, TP in 2..16, and FlashInfer CUTLASS or CuTe-DSL MXFP8 weights (what `linear_backend=auto` selects); anything else falls back with a warning.

No open PR fuses the V4.1 `wo_b` reduce-scatter: #57257 changes the SP all-gather side and #54151 is Kimi-K3 AG-GEMM.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/test_gemm_rs_ar.py  # 2 GPUs: bf16, flashinfer_cutlass, flashinfer_cutedsl
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -- benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py \
    --model deepseek_v41 --backend flashinfer_cutedsl --m 128 192 256 384 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 16384
```

### Deploy

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 2026
```

Baseline: the same command with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=0` (main's `wo_b` path).

### Benchmark

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 2026 --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 96 --num-warmups 8
```

GSM8K: lm-eval 0.4.12, `gsm8k` 5-shot chat (`--apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn`, thinking off), greedy, 1024 max tokens, all 1319 questions.

## Test Result

4xB200, TP4 + EP4 with MegaMoE (sequence parallel), FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, no speculative decoding. Kernel test: 3 passed.

Operator level (`benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py`), TP4, `wo_b` shape N=5120 with K=2048 per rank, MXFP8 CuTe-DSL layout, activation quantization included in both candidates, CUDA graphs, median over 40 samples of the slowest rank. The baseline is the model's unfused path with vLLM's own collective dispatch (custom Lamport reduce-scatter for small messages, NCCL above its size cap):

| M | vLLM linear + `sp_reduce_scatter` (us) | GEMM-RS (us) | latency |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 26.6 | 29.2 | +9.7% |
| 512 | 36.9 | 38.9 | +5.6% |
| 1024 | 48.0 | 47.1 | -2.0% |
| 2048 | 100.9 | 63.5 | -37.1% |
| 4096 | 141.8 | 96.3 | -32.1% |
| 8192 | 226.8 | 162.8 | -28.2% |
| 16384 | 428.5 | 289.2 | -32.5% |

The fused kernel wins from about 1024 tokens; below that vLLM's Lamport reduce-scatter is faster than the fused kernel's fixed flag/exit handshake. Without speculative decoding, decode batches (at most `max_num_seqs` tokens) never reach the fused path and prefill chunks are large, so serving only sees the winning region.

Torch profiler, one 8192-token prefill step on rank 0: the 40 NCCL reduce-scatter launches (9.1 ms) and 40 `wo_b` GEMMs (2.8 ms) are replaced by 40 fused launches (6.6 ms); GPU busy time per step drops from 127.1 ms to 118.1 ms (-7.1%).

Online serving, `bench serve` with fixed-length random requests, mean of two runs per arm (arms off, on, on, off with a fresh server each), zero preemptions:

| workload | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TTFT (ms) | mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c16 | 1697.8 -> 1708.0 (+0.6%) | 15279.8 -> 15371.6 (+0.6%) | 1050.5 -> 1038.5 (-1.1%) | 8.40 -> 8.36 (-0.5%) |
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c32 | 2592.0 -> 2668.2 (+2.9%) | 23328.4 -> 24014.2 (+2.9%) | 1565.3 -> 1512.5 (-3.4%) | 10.82 -> 10.51 (-2.9%) |
| 1024 in / 2048 out, c32 | 3178.2 -> 3324.3 (+4.6%) | 4767.4 -> 4986.5 (+4.6%) | 771.4 -> 767.5 (-0.5%) | 9.75 -> 9.27 (-5.0%) |

Run-to-run spread: baseline runs differ by 0.5% (c16), 5.4% (c32) and 16% (1k/2k); fused runs by 0.1%, 1.7% and 7%. The c16 change is within drift; c32 is at its edge with every percentile improving (p99 TTFT 4760 -> 3610 ms); the 1k/2k row is not resolved by two runs.

GSM8K, same server config:

| metric | off | on | paired changes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| flexible-extract | 95.98% (+-0.54) | 96.29% (+-0.52) | 10 became correct, 6 became wrong |
| strict-match | 79.45% (+-1.11) | 78.70% (+-1.13) | 30 became correct, 40 became wrong |

Both within one standard error; 417 of 1319 generations are byte-identical, the rest differ in BF16 partial rounding order between the fused FP32 multicast reduction and NCCL's ring.

Not measured: speculative decoding (decode batches near 192 tokens would also take the fused path) and TP8. The `off` arm runs this branch with the flag unset rather than a separate main checkout; the earlier commits only touch Kimi-K3 and `cute_utils`, so V4.1's `wo_b` path is main's.

AI assistance was used (Claude Code) for the V4.1 integration, the kernel relocation and driving the benchmarks; every changed line and result was reviewed by the author.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Fix FlashInfer DSpark non-causal attention
author: WoosukKwon
body:
DSpark's non-causal draft window has 133 valid keys at draft length 5, padded to 256 indices. The DSV4.1 FlashInfer integration passed the padded width as the active sparse length, so padding entered softmax normalization. A constant-value reference expecting 1 returned 0.51953125 (133/256). Short contexts also inherited causal visibility from the launcher's per-request query positions.

Use the valid SWA length, retaining FlashInfer's required 128-column minimum, and present each draft query with the full non-causal sequence length. Prepare the per-token active lengths and sequence lengths once in the metadata builder, using persistent buffers refreshed before FULL CUDA graph replay and shared across layers. Singleton query/output views remove the need to construct query offsets in each layer. This changes vLLM metadata only; no FlashInfer source changes or new Triton kernel are needed. The two int32 buffers use 8 bytes per configured maximum batched token per builder (64 KiB at capacity 8192).

Validation on 4× GB200 with FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`), DSpark length 5 and full decode graphs. DEP4 uses MegaMoE/adaptive verification; TP4 uses auto MoE/fixed verification.

Full GSM8K: 1,319 identical 5-shot chat prompts per pair, greedy, seed 123, thinking off, 1,024-token output cap. Accuracy below uses flexible extraction.

| Configuration | Acceptance before → fixed (including bonus) | GSM8K before → fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DEP4 | 3.1823 → **3.8248** (+20.2%) | 1268 → 1271 / 1319 (96.13% → 96.36%) |
| TP4 | 3.2075 → **3.8879** (+21.2%) | 1266 → 1263 / 1319 (95.98% → 95.75%) |

All 1,319 requests completed in each fixed run, with no errors or empty responses. DEP had no capped outputs; TP had one (versus zero before). Strict extraction: DEP 1042 → 1042; TP 1060 → 1049. These evaluations establish acceptance recovery, not exact greedy-output equivalence or an accuracy improvement. MegaAttention measured 3.8437 acceptance on the DEP cohort. These are short-context results, not 100K-context throughput measurements.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py \
  -k test_dsv41_flashinfer_dspark_window_matches_reference -q -rs
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py
```

The original 12 regression cases failed before the correctness fix. All 12 expanded cases pass with persistent metadata: BF16/FP8, 16/64 heads, short/long windows, mixed query lengths, padding, and CUDA graph replay after Q/KV and visible-length updates, with unchanged buffer addresses. Attention outputs are bitwise identical to the initial correctness fix across eight FP8 shapes (16/64 heads, batch 1/8/32/128). Nine full draft-forward runs have zero observed eager/graph, changed-input, restored-input and post-replay error. Pre-commit checks pass. Validation ran on the optimization worktree; all three changed files are identical in this isolated PR branch. The GSM8K results above evaluate the correctness fix; the metadata refactor was validated by parity and replay checks, without repeating the full accuracy runs.

Metadata-refactor performance on GB200 ×4, relative to the initial correctness fix: synthetic weights and 102,400 KV tokens/request, draft length 5, TP auto MoE / DEP MegaMoE. Medians of five distributed-MAX samples, 20 graph replays/sample after 3 seconds of warmup; each comparison uses the same runner and repeats one endpoint to expose order effects.

| Workload | Initial fix (µs) | Prepared metadata (µs) | Draft-forward result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| TP4 B1 | 403 / 425 | 366 | 9–14% lower latency |
| DEP4 B8 | 703 / 691 | 669 | 3–5% lower latency |
| DEP4 B128 | 1370 | 1431 / 1327 | Inconclusive |

The forward boundary excludes metadata preparation, LM head, scheduler and sampling; these are not serving-throughput gains. Preparation costs 3.9–8.5 µs per build in a separate CUPTI/CUDA-graph/cold-L2 microbenchmark and is shared across layers. Exact commands and raw results are archived locally under `/home/woosuk/.cache/v41-dspark-opt/metadata-opt/metadata-paired-002-*`; the microbenchmark results are in `prepared-results.json`.

Duplicate check: searched open DSpark/FlashInfer, acceptance, noncausal sparse, and padding PRs. #52499 and #57292 address SM120 routing/page geometry; #54834 addresses dense FlashInfer cache-layout resolution; #55692 addresses block-table bounds. None fixes the SM100 DSV4.1 non-causal active lengths and visibility corrected here.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Reuse the decode topk ragged metadata across layers
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body: ## Purpose `_forward_decode` rebuilds the ragged form of the topk indices on every compressed layer. The pack is a pure function of the shared `topk_indices_buffer`, which only `index_source_layer_ids` write, plus per-step metadata (`token_to_req_indices`, the block table, `is_valid_token`). The one per-layer term is `compress_ratio`, which divides the block size. So the layers between two index sources all rebuild the same thing. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `compress_ratios` has 38 layers with a compressed cache and `index_source_layer_ids` has 8 entries, giving 38 rebuilds per decode step for 8 distinct results — a 4.8x redundancy. A 10-step decode trace on MI355X (TP4, rank 0) confirms the count and the cost: | kernel | total | calls | per call | |---|---|---|---| | `_pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel` | 1678.1 us | 380 | 4.42 us | | `_compute_topk_lens_kernel` | 1546.0 us | 380 | 4.07 us | 380 = 38 layers x 10 steps. Together they are 2.2% of all kernel time, ~322 us and 76 launches per step. ## What changes The index source memoizes the pack and the layers below it read through, keyed by compress ratio since that is the only per-layer term. Consumers resolve their source once in `__init__` through `static_forward_context`, the same way the layer already resolves its compressed-KV source, and raise the same `NotImplementedError` if a PP split lands inside an index-sharing group. Invalidation is structural rather than versioned: the source clears its own entry when it runs, and it always runs before the layers that consume its indices, so a step cannot read the previous step's pack. Prefill is untouched. Expected effect: 8 rebuilds per step instead of 38, ~255 us and 60 launches per step of GPU work removed, ~1.8% of decode GPU time on this model. ## Not a duplicate Searched open PRs for the neighbouring work: - #56638 re-enables the fused `combine_topk_swa_indices` kernel. Same file, but the mixed-prefill index combine, not the decode pack. - #57282 adds an opt-in HIP decode kernel. It consumes this metadata; it does not change how often it is built. - #57109 and #54394 touch the indexer that produces the indices, upstream of the pack. None of them change the per-layer rebuild. ## Test plan - `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X: a 10-step decode capture to confirm the rebuild count drops to one per index source, and GSM8K for accuracy parity. The change is a pure memoization, so parity is the bar. ## Test results Unit tests, on the branch, MI355X: ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q 68 passed in 75.03s ``` Decode capture, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X, 10 engine steps at concurrency 1, fp8 KV, MTP spec decode. Per-step kernel time, mean over the four TP ranks: | kernel | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `_pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel` | 173.1 us | 38.0 us | | `_compute_topk_lens_kernel` | 158.4 us | 34.1 us | | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` (untouched) | 201.6 us | 206.5 us | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` (untouched) | 218.7 us | 224.1 us | Launches fall from 380 to 80 per 10 steps, i.e. exactly the 8 per step the 8 index sources predict, and the untouched kernels stay put. Net 250.2 us per step against the 255 us the trace analysis predicted. Accuracy, GSM8K 5-shot, 400 questions, greedy, concurrency 32, spec decode off so that generations are model-faithful: | build | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | main | 0.9025 | 0.0% | | this PR | 0.9025 | 0.0% | Note this stack is not run-to-run deterministic: `main` compared against itself disagrees token-for-token on 3 of 6 fixed greedy prompts, so parity is established statistically rather than by diffing outputs. ## What is not measured End-to-end interactivity, which this PR does not claim. Paired step-time samples on MI355X (TP4, MTP spec decode, profiler off, three 25 s samples per point, `main` and the patched build loaded side by side on opposite GPU halves) do not resolve a change of this size. The patched side here carries this change together with #57435: | concurrency | main | patched | delta | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 45.57 +/- 1.24 ms/step | 46.15 +/- 1.21 | +1.28% | | 32 | 44.65 +/- 0.21 ms/step | 44.41 +/- 0.08 | -0.54% | Acceptance was identical at 3.533 tokens per step, so the comparison is fair. The concurrency-32 point moves the right way and is by far the tighter of the two, but three samples cannot separate a sub-1% effect from this spread, and the concurrency-1 spread is larger than the effect being looked for. With spec decode off the loop is outright host-bound -- 12.61 +/- 0.00 ms per step, with the A/B at -0.01% and 0.00% -- so removed GPU work simply lands in host slack. The claim here is therefore the kernel-level saving above, not an ITL number. --- AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every line, ran the tests and evals above myself, and am responsible for it.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Fuse the inverse RoPE into the sparse decode reduce
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body: ## Purpose The ROCm sparse decode writes the attention output twice. The reduce kernel combines the split-K partials and stores `[T, H, 512]`, and then `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` reads that whole tensor back, rotates the trailing 64 rope lanes and writes it out again — a full round trip per layer, for an epilogue on data the reduce already held in registers. From a 10-step decode trace on MI355X (TP4, rank 0): | kernel | total | calls | share of kernel time | |---|---|---|---| | `_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_partial_kernel` | 4707.3 us | 430 | 3.24% | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` | 2214.2 us | 430 | 1.52% | | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` | 1965.5 us | 430 | 1.35% | 430 = 43 layers x 10 steps: every layer pays it, sliding-window and MTP layers included. FlashMLA's mega-attention kernel already folds this rotation and the FP8 cast into its epilogue on SM100 — `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` describes exactly that — and the layer interface for it is platform-generic (`_alloc_attn_out` / `_o_proj`, `accepts_unnormed_unroped_query`). The ROCm Triton path just never took it. ## What changes The reduce gained an optional inverse-RoPE epilogue. Reshaping the combined row into adjacent pairs puts the rope lanes in the last 32 of 256 pairs, so giving the NoPE pairs cos=1 and sin=0 lets one expression cover the whole row with no branch and no second pass: ```python even, odd = tl.split(tl.reshape(out, (BLOCK_H, COMB_DIM // 2, 2))) out = tl.reshape(tl.join(even * cos + odd * sin, odd * cos - even * sin), ...) ``` Which rows still owe a rotation depends on the batch: the reduce rotates the decode rows it produces, prefill rows have no such epilogue, and a decode path that does not fuse (for instance the opt-in HIP kernel in #57282) rotates nothing. `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` reports how many leading rows it rotated and `forward_mqa` pays the standalone pass for the rest, in place. On a decode-only step that leaves nothing to do, so the kernel does not launch at all rather than being replaced by a copy. That bookkeeping belongs in the eager attention segment specifically, not in `_o_proj`. An earlier revision of this PR handed the row count to `_o_proj`, which runs inside the compiled region; since vLLM compiles with `skip_all_guards_unsafe`, the Python int froze at its trace-time value and rows ended up rotated zero or two times. GSM8K fell to 0.087 against a 0.902 baseline with fluent output and no error of any kind. The lane arithmetic was correct throughout, so no kernel-level test caught it -- only the eval did. Two side effects worth noting: the rotation now happens on the fp32 accumulator rather than the already-rounded bf16 output, dropping a rounding step, and the NoPE lanes come through bit-exact (x1.0 + 0.0). Expected effect: ~196 us and 43 launches per step removed, ~1.35% of decode GPU time on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. ## Not a duplicate - #54894 fuses inverse RoPE with group quantization via AITER's `inverse_rope_group_quant` — different model (`deepseek_v4`), different mechanism, and it keeps the rotation as its own pass. This removes the pass. The two are compatible in direction: if the V4.1 ROCm path later adopts an FP8 `wo_a`, the natural next step is emitting the FP8 cast from this same epilogue, which is what the SM100 kernel does. - #57282 adds an opt-in HIP decode kernel for a specific batch range and falls through to this Triton path otherwise; the two compose, and the rotated-row count above is what keeps them honest. - #56720 and #56342 touch other kernels in the same file, not the reduce. ## Test results Unit tests, on the branch, MI355X: ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py \ tests/kernels/attention/test_dsv41_rocm_fused_inv_rope.py -q 69 passed in 38.64s ``` Kernel equivalence, MI355X: running the real decode kernels fused, then unfused followed by `_fused_inverse_rope_gptj`, on identical inputs. NoPE lanes are bit-exact and rope lanes agree to bf16 rounding at every shape tried -- `(queries, heads)` of (2, 3), (1, 128), (8, 128), (32, 128): | | max abs diff | |---|---| | NoPE lanes | 0.0 (32 queries: 4.9e-4) | | rope lanes | <= 2.0e-3, against \|rope\| up to 0.29 | Decode capture, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X, 10 engine steps at concurrency 1, MTP spec decode. Per-step kernel time, mean over the four TP ranks: | kernel | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` | 201.6 us | 0.0 us (430 launches -> 0) | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` | 218.7 us | 227.0 us | The pass disappears on decode-only steps and the reduce absorbs it for 8.3 us, so 193 us per step net, against the 196 us the trace analysis predicted. Accuracy, GSM8K 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 32 score remains the same --- AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every line, ran the tests and evals above myself, and am responsible for it.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Preserve logprobs across streaming continuations
author: i-m-aditya
body:
## Problem

When a resumable streaming request finishes one chunk while its continuation
is already queued, the continuation can replace `request.sampling_params`
before the scheduler packages the completed chunk's logprobs.

If chunk A requests logprobs and chunk B does not, chunk A's final output loses
its logprob payload. The result incorrectly depends on whether the continuation
arrived before or after chunk A's final model output.

## Solution

Snapshot the finishing chunk's sampling parameters before handling the stop and
possible streaming continuation. Use that snapshot when extracting logprobs for
the completed output.

Added a scheduler regression test that covers both continuation arrival orders
and verifies the exact logprob payload remains attached to the finishing chunk.

## Tests

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -v`
- `.venv/bin/ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`
- `.venv/bin/ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`
- `git diff --check`
- `pre-commit` hooks

## Duplicate work

Searched open pull requests for scheduler, streaming, logprobs, and `new_logprobs`; no matching open PR was found.

title: [ROCm][CI] Query HIP device memory for test GPU teardown waits.
author: sheralskumar
body:
## Purpose 
- PR 1 to enable MI355 DPX jobs
- On ROCm, measure GPU teardown / idle memory with `torch.cuda.mem_get_info` (HIP logical devices) instead of amdsmi physical indices.
- Raise ROCm teardown headroom to 4 GiB to match known driver/runtime residency.
- Stop remapping HfRunner memory checks through `get_physical_device_indices` on paths that now use HIP devices.

## Why
amdsmi on DPX `gpu-0` reports the parent MI350 card (~288 GiB) and includes the sibling partition's VRAM, so `_wait_for_gpu_memory_release` false-fails. HIP is partition-scoped (~144 GiB NPS2).

## Test Plan
- [ ] `tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_remote_vllm_server.py`
- [ ] DPX: teardown wait sees partition memory, not parent-card memory
- [ ] Existing AMD CI (`vllm/amd-ci`) does not regress on SPX/MI300

title: [ROCm][DSv4][Perf] Fuse the inverse RoPE into the sparse decode reduce
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4 shares the ROCm sparse decode kernels with V4.1, so the reduce
epilogue added in #57435 applies here with no kernel work at all — only the
call site has to opt in. On decode-only steps the standalone
`_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` stops launching entirely; on V4.1 that measured
201.6 us per step against 8.3 us added to the reduce, for 193 us net.

#57435 has since merged, so this is no longer stacked: the epilogue, the
`inverse_rope` switch on `rocm_inv_rope_einsum`, and the
`rocm_inverse_rope_rows_` helper are all on main. What is left here is 27 lines
in one file.

## What changes

`_forward_decode` passes the positions and the cos/sin cache into
`rocm_sparse_attn_decode`, so the rotation happens on the fp32 accumulators in
the reduce rather than in a separate pass over the already-rounded bf16 output,
and `_o_proj` no longer rotates.

Which rows still owe a rotation is batch-dependent — the reduce rotates the
decode rows it produced, prefill rows have none, and a decode path that does
not fuse rotates nothing — so `forward_mqa` settles it from the count the
decode reports, in the eager attention segment. That placement is the point:
vLLM compiles with `skip_all_guards_unsafe`, so the same value read from inside
the compiled `_o_proj` freezes at its trace-time value. In #57435 that mistake
cost 0.087 GSM8K against a 0.902 baseline, with fluent output and no error.

One thing V4 has that V4.1 does not: the FP8 `wo_a` path from #54894, whose
`inverse_rope_group_quant` rotates while it quantizes. Fusing there would
rotate twice, so the fusion is gated on `self._wo_a_fp8_weight is None` — which
is exactly the condition under which `_o_proj` takes the BF16 einsum branch
that stops rotating. When the FP8 path is active the decode is handed no
positions, returns a rotated count of 0, the settle pass is skipped, and the
path is left byte-identical to today. The gate is a load-time constant, not a
batch-dependent one, so reading it here raises none of the tracing concerns
above.

## Not a duplicate

- #57435 is the same optimization for `deepseek_v41` and was the parent of this
  branch; it has merged. The V4.1 call site cannot cover V4: they are separate
  attention classes in separate files.
- #57078 tiles the standalone inverse-RoPE kernel for sparse prefill. The two
  compose rather than collide: this PR removes the pass on decode-only steps
  and leaves prefill rows going through that same kernel, which #57078 makes
  faster.
- #54894 moved `wo_a` to an FP8 output projection in this same `_o_proj` and
  has landed. The textual conflict predicted here is resolved, and the
  correctness interaction it created is handled by the gate described above.

## Test plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py`
- A fused-vs-unfused A/B of the real decode kernels on MI355X.
- A DeepSeek-V4 serving eval. **Not yet run — this is why the PR is a draft.**

## Test results

Unit tests, on the branch, MI355X:

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q
74 passed in 65.82s
```

Kernel equivalence, MI355X: the real decode kernels run fused, then unfused
followed by `_fused_inverse_rope_gptj`, on identical inputs, at V4's head dims
(nope 448, rope 64). NoPE lanes are bit-exact and rope lanes agree to bf16
rounding at every shape tried — `(queries, heads)` of (2, 3), (1, 128),
(8, 128), (32, 128):

| | max abs diff |
|---|---|
| NoPE lanes | 0.0 (32 queries: 4.9e-4) |
| rope lanes | <= 2.0e-3, against \|rope\| up to 0.29 |

The kernel-level evidence for the epilogue itself, including the decode trace
and the GSM8K parity runs, is in #57435, and those kernels are untouched here.

## What is not measured

**No DeepSeek-V4 model has been run end to end on this branch.** The V4.1
sibling was validated with GSM8K at 1319 questions (0.918 against a 0.901
baseline) and a decode trace, but that exercises the V4.1 call site, not this
one. What supports this change is the shared kernels plus reading the V4 path:
`forward_mqa` is the sole attention entry point for
`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention` (`forward_mha` is not implemented for these
model classes, so `sparse_mla_force_mqa` does not route around it), decode rows
occupy the leading rows of the output buffer, and the base class slices
`o_padded[:, :n_local_heads, :]` before `_o_proj`, which is exactly the region
rotated here.

The FP8 `wo_a` gate is likewise unmeasured on a real V4 checkpoint. It is
argued from the code — no positions in means a rotated count of 0 out, and the
settle pass is skipped — rather than from a run on FP8 weights.

That reasoning is not a substitute for an eval, and the V4.1 experience is the
reason to say so plainly: the failure mode of getting this wrong is fluent
output with wrong answers and no error anywhere. A V4 eval, on both the BF16
and FP8 `wo_a` paths, should gate this leaving draft.

---

AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every line, ran
the tests above myself, and am responsible for it.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Retain offload event metadata through batch translation
author: karya0
body:
## Purpose

`OffloadingEventsTracker` caches a `BlockStored` payload per offload key and drops it when the key's last residency goes away. The drop happened inline in `_take_removed_event`, so within a single `take_events` batch a removal could delete the payload that a *later* event in that same batch still needed — a primary removal preceding a queued secondary (KVCR) store. That store then fell back to the placeholder payload, publishing an event with no block hashes and no token ids.

Fix: collect the removed keys during the batch and drop their payloads once, after every event in the batch has had a chance to register its residencies.

Scope: this does not address a store that only completes in a later batch; that needs the in-flight store set and is left for a follow-up.

Not a duplicate of #52103, which touches the same files to add request provenance to stored events.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py
```

`test_primary_removal_preserves_metadata_for_same_batch_kvcr_store` is added to the existing suite, parametrized over the secondary removal landing in the same batch or the next one. It asserts the store keeps its full payload, and that the payload is still dropped once no residency remains.

## Test Result

```
25 passed, 14 warnings in 18.96s
```

Both parametrizations fail with the fix reverted and pass with it applied. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, ruff format, mypy).

No model evaluation: this changes only the KV-event payload published to external consumers, not the offload data path or any generated output.

AI assistance was used for this change; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Kernel][Perf] Add sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50) tuned configs for batch-invariant persistent matmul
author: LioEinaudi
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #53247 (Ada/Hopper tables) and #53649 (Blackwell SM100 table). Compute capability 12.x — Blackwell workstation/consumer parts such as RTX PRO 6000 and the RTX 50 series — had no entry in `_get_tuned_matmul_arch_family`, so under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` every linear layer on these GPUs ran the batch-invariant persistent matmul with the default `128x128x64 / 8 warps / 3 stages` config.

This PR adds an `sm120` family with tuned configs for the 15 TP=1 GEMM shapes of Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B (`gate_up_proj`, `down_proj`, `qkv_proj`, `lm_head`, `o_proj`), and maps `major == 12` to it. Same structure and invariance rule as the existing families: **one `BLOCK_K` per (N, K) shape**, so every row keeps the same K-reduction order regardless of M, with `BLOCK_M / BLOCK_N / num_warps / num_stages` selected per M bucket.

## Method

Same sweep as #53247, run on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 188 SMs, driver 580.159.04), vLLM main @ f3aa88d2, torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1:

- per shape: 3 `BLOCK_K` x 4 `BLOCK_M` x 4 `BLOCK_N` x 2 warps x 4 stages = 384 configs x 10 M values (1 ... 2048), CUDA-event timed against the current default config and cuBLAS (`torch.mm`);
- `BLOCK_K` chosen shape-wide by a decode-weighted score, then the best config per M bucket under that `BLOCK_K`;
- gate: for every shape, the selected configs must be `allclose` to an fp32 reference and the rows for M = 1 must be **bitwise identical** to the same rows computed at M = 8 / 32 / 256 / 2048 (sha256 of the row bytes). All 15 shapes green.

## Kernel-level results (p50, tuned vs current default; geomean over M buckets)

| model | shape | N | K | BLOCK_K | decode (M<=64) | all M | max | min (M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B | gate_up_proj | 12288 | 2048 | 64 | 5.68x | 2.90x | 6.44x | 1.01x (1024) |
| Qwen3-1.7B | down_proj | 2048 | 6144 | 64 | 4.16x | 2.77x | 4.24x | 1.00x (1024) |
| Qwen3-1.7B | qkv_proj | 4096 | 2048 | 128 | 2.16x | 1.64x | 2.40x | 0.90x (2048) |
| Qwen3-1.7B | lm_head | 151936 | 2048 | 64 | 1.84x | 1.44x | 2.17x | 1.00x (1024) |
| Qwen3-1.7B | o_proj | 2048 | 2048 | 32 | 1.58x | 1.42x | 1.66x | 0.95x (1024) |
| Qwen3-4B | gate_up_proj | 19456 | 2560 | 64 | 8.03x | 3.50x | 9.76x | 1.00x (256) |
| Qwen3-4B | down_proj | 2560 | 9728 | 128 | 5.92x | 3.16x | 6.50x | 0.79x (1024) |
| Qwen3-4B | qkv_proj | 6144 | 2560 | 64 | 3.65x | 2.23x | 4.22x | 1.00x (256) |
| Qwen3-4B | lm_head | 151936 | 2560 | 64 | 1.54x | 1.30x | 1.73x | 1.00x (256) |
| Qwen3-4B | o_proj | 2560 | 4096 | 128 | 2.95x | 2.14x | 3.11x | 0.88x (1024) |
| Qwen3-8B | gate_up_proj | 24576 | 4096 | 64 | 2.48x | 1.74x | 2.75x | 0.99x (2048) |
| Qwen3-8B | down_proj | 4096 | 12288 | 128 | 5.50x | 2.82x | 6.99x | 0.78x (2048) |
| Qwen3-8B | qkv_proj | 6144 | 4096 | 64 | 4.97x | 2.69x | 5.66x | 1.00x (256) |
| Qwen3-8B | lm_head | 151936 | 4096 | 64 | 1.30x | 1.18x | 1.35x | 1.00x (512) |
| Qwen3-8B | o_proj | 4096 | 4096 | 128 | 3.28x | 2.14x | 3.54x | 0.89x (2048) |

The regressions below 1.0x are all at M >= 512 (prefill-sized batches) on `down_proj` / `o_proj` / `qkv_proj` and are the cost of the shape-wide `BLOCK_K` chosen for decode; the same trade-off exists in the Ada/Hopper/SM100 tables. Full per-M tables (cuBLAS / default / tuned p50 for every shape) are attached as `kernel_before_after.csv` per model.

## Test Plan

- Kernel sweep + bitwise gates as above (`correctness_gates.json`, all green).
- `tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py` on the branch on an RTX PRO 6000 (the tuned-M-bucket test picks up the new family automatically via `_get_tuned_matmul_arch_family`).
- End to end, same format as #53649: `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm bench latency --model <m>` (defaults: input 32 / output 128 / batch 8, decode-heavy) and a prefill-heavy variant (input 1024 / output 32 / batch 8), each for BI=0, BI=1 with the previous default configs, and BI=1 with this PR, on the same GPU.

## Test Result

Hardware: one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 96 GB, PCIe), driver 580.159.04; vLLM main @ f3aa88d2 + this PR (branch head c24692b8), torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1; `vllm bench latency --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10`, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0`. "default" = the same tree with `batch_invariant_configs.py` reverted to `origin/main` (no sm120 family), measured in the same job on the same GPU.

**Decode-heavy (bench latency defaults: input 32 / output 128 / batch 8), avg latency in seconds**

| model | BI=0 | BI=1 default configs | BI=1 this PR | change | BI tax before -> after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B | 0.4802 | 1.5916 | **1.4301** | -10.1% | 3.31x -> 2.98x |
| Qwen3-4B | 0.9382 | 2.9861 | **2.3562** | -21.1% | 3.18x -> 2.51x |
| Qwen3-8B | 1.5150 | 4.1242 | **3.4510** | -16.3% | 2.72x -> 2.28x |

**Prefill-heavy (input 1024 / output 32 / batch 8)**

| model | BI=0 | BI=1 default configs | BI=1 this PR | change | BI tax before -> after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B | 0.2233 | 0.5064 | **0.4708** | -7.0% | 2.27x -> 2.11x |
| Qwen3-4B | 0.4536 | 0.9798 | **0.8337** | -14.9% | 2.16x -> 1.84x |

title: [Perf][Attention] Reduce GLM sparse MLA preparation overhead
author: GirasoleY
body:
## Purpose

Reduce query packing and sparse-index preparation overhead around FlashInfer NoPE MLA attention.

The three commits:

1. Reuse a contiguous NoPE query when its rotary tail is empty, avoiding a redundant `torch.cat` before FP8 quantization. Preserve concatenation for nonempty rotary dimensions and strided queries.
2. Use one padded remap program per query for counted sparse capacities up to 4096. Initialize padding and reduce valid counts inside the remap kernel, removing separate fills and atomic accumulation. Preserve larger tiled cases and reusable buffers. Name the device entry point `sparse_mla_index_remap_kernel` for trace attribution.
3. Simplify empty-query handling: fuse dummy-entry preparation and safe-length calculation while preserving raw counts; skip preparation and masking for resident TP; mask only LSE for DCP and let its existing merge suppress zero-weight outputs, including NaNs. Preserve PyTorch output masking for HiSparse without LSE. There is no custom output-zeroing kernel.

Duplicate-work checks found no matching open PR. Related PRs #54258 (separate ROCm remap kernel), #38354 (DeepSeek pre-attention GEMM/RoPE fusion), and #57161 (GLM kpool/indexer scheduling) address different kernels or stages. No existing issue is being claimed or closed.

## Correctness

Prior TP validation on the experiment stack used GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8+EP8, all custom ops enabled, eager execution, no prefix cache, and exactly 32768 input tokens with either 1 or 16 generated tokens. Across 12 repeatability requests, all 8976 sparse-layer calls across eight ranks had positive valid counts (minimum 1). A direct full-shape FP8 attention comparison at 32768 queries × 8 heads × 512 dimensions, capacity 2176, matched the previous implementation bit for bit.

## Performance

Controlled end-to-end comparison on four GB300 GPUs, TP4+EP4, eager, `custom_ops=["all"]`, no prefix cache, no speculative decoding, and FP8 E4M3 KV cache. The actual upstream PR model stayed loaded while an idle-worker extension switched only the three preparation changes to their PR-base implementations. All four ranks verified the implementation selection. Compatible prebuilt extensions were reused.

Both implementations were warmed, then measured in four alternating baseline/PR and PR/baseline rounds with five matched samples per workload per round (20 pairs each). Each request had exactly 32768 input tokens, with a 32768-token prefill scheduling limit. Prefill generated one token; decode generated 128 tokens. These are client-observed serving latencies.

| Metric | PR base | PR | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32K prefill TTFT, median | 518.25 ms | 507.61 ms | 2.05% |
| Decode inter-token latency, median | 122.85 ms/token | 120.77 ms/token | 1.70% |

All 20 pairs improved for each workload. Per-round median reductions ranged from 1.78–2.27% for prefill and 1.21–1.98% for decode. These measurements apply to eager TP4 execution; CUDA-graph decode and other parallel configurations were not measured in this comparison.

Earlier isolated measurements on the same GB300 GPU, using CUDA graph replay and the median of five samples with 40 repetitions/sample:

| Operation | Before | Optimized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Remap including initialization | 531.90 µs | 282.93 µs |
| Safe lengths and dummy entry | 12.32 µs | 4.12 µs |

Shape: 32768 queries × 8 heads × 512 dimensions, capacity 2176. These are preparation microbenchmarks from the experiment stack. Resident TP now skips safe-length preparation entirely. Earlier tracing also confirmed removal of all 11 redundant query concatenations. The final upstream revision has not been reprofiled; the controlled end-to-end results above are separate from these older microbenchmarks. Measurements of the removed output-zeroing kernel are excluded.

title: [Perf][KV Offload] Publish async lookup results per request group
author: Alex-ai-future
body:
## Overview

`AsyncLookupManager` batches each scheduler step's tier-existence probes, then checks request groups sequentially on its worker. This change publishes a request group's result as soon as that group's lookup finishes, so completed groups no longer wait for later groups before the scheduler can use their results.

## Claims

- A completed group can resolve at the next scheduler drain even while later groups are still being checked; a HIT can therefore become eligible to start promotion earlier.
- The worker remains FIFO and single-threaded. Each group's `batch_lookup()` must finish before its results are published; lookup verdicts and promotion policy are unchanged.
- Results remain grouped by `req_id`; this does not publish a partially consumed group.

## Validation

### Tests

The following results were recorded on PR commit `b117dd93`, before merging the latest `main` and before this test-only cleanup. They have not been rerun on the current PR head.

The current test diff keeps the blocked-group publication and lazy-iterator atomicity cases, folds FIFO ordering into the blocked-group test, and removes a standalone exception case already covered by the existing iterator-failure test.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py -q
# 22 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py -q
# 82 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py -q
# 54 passed
```

### FS lookup timing replay

A scheduler-timing replay compared pre-PR aggregate publication with this PR's per-group publication while keeping submission at step end. It used the current `FsAsyncLookupManager`, the repository's `fs_io_C` batch lookup implementation, and existing files sharded 256 per directory. The model-execution windows were simulated as 5 ms or 20 ms sleeps; all keys were hits. `HIT step` is the first simulated scheduler step where a request group returned HIT and could initiate promotion.

The table reports step-1 HIT fraction and mean/median first-HIT step across request groups and measured runs. Brackets give the minimum and maximum observed first-HIT step. Sample counts are per configuration; 16K configurations used 10 runs, most 64K configurations used 4 runs, and 64 groups at 5 ms used 10 runs.

| Keys | Groups × keys/group | Step | Runs | Pre-PR: Step-1 HIT | Pre-PR: mean / median HIT step [range] | This PR: Step-1 HIT | This PR: mean / median HIT step [range] |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16K | 16 × 1,024 | 5 ms | 10 | 0% | 12.50 / 13.0 [9–14] | 0% | 6.51 / 6.5 [2–13] |
| 16K | 16 × 1,024 | 20 ms | 10 | 0% | 3.70 / 4.0 [3–4] | 23% [19–25] | 2.20 / 2.0 [1–4] |
| 16K | 64 × 256 | 5 ms | 10 | 0% | 12.50 / 12.0 [10–15] | 0% [0–2] | 6.82 / 7.0 [1–16] |
| 16K | 64 × 256 | 20 ms | 10 | 0% | 3.40 / 3.0 [3–4] | 26% [22–30] | 2.17 / 2.0 [1–4] |
| 64K | 16 × 4,096 | 5 ms | 4 | 0% | 37.75 / 38.5 [35–39] | 0% | 19.77 / 20.5 [5–32] |
| 64K | 16 × 4,096 | 20 ms | 4 | 0% | 12.00 / 12.0 [11–13] | 0% | 6.55 / 7.0 [2–11] |
| 64K | 64 × 1,024 | 5 ms | 10 | 0% | 41.10 / 41.0 [38–44] | 0% | 22.10 / 22.5 [3–40] |
| 64K | 64 × 1,024 | 20 ms | 4 | 0% | 12.00 / 12.0 [12–12] | 0% | 7.27 / 7.0 [2–12] |

The mean reflects aggregate waiting across groups; the median reflects a typical group's wait. The ranges show that some groups still resolve much later than the typical group.

This replay isolates result-publication timing; it does not run the full scheduler, allocate primary-tier slots, or execute promotion transfers. Its step duration is simulated, so these results are directional and are not a serving-throughput claim. Absolute wall-clock timings varied. The scratch replay harness is not part of this PR.

No model evaluation was run because this change affects lookup-result publication timing, not model outputs or accuracy. No end-to-end serving benchmark was run.

## Details

The worker still receives the step's accumulated keys at `flush()` and groups them by `req_id`. Previously, it collected results from every group and posted one combined result batch after the last group completed. The new code posts each group's results immediately after fully consuming that group's `batch_lookup()` output. This removes the result-publication wait between independent groups; it does not start the worker earlier or parallelize the group lookups.

I found no open PR for this exact result-publication change. Related #61292 moves Mooncake connector lookups to the input thread, and #62615 protects primary-tier hits during promotion; both address different paths. #23622 is a non-merge PoC for different connector lookup semantics.

AI assistance was used. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing and defending the change.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Address kpool tail blocks by the padded indexer stride in the NVIDIA prefill seed kernel
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

Fix silent indexer-cache corruption for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA: the kpool prefill tail-seed kernel addresses tail blocks with a dense stride while the tail cache is stored with the indexer's padded block stride.

**How the tail cache is laid out.** `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` pads the `KpoolTailSpec` page to the indexer page (`page_size_padded = idx_page`; 38016 B for the default `block_size=1152`: 288 pool rows x 132 B), and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places every indexer layer's tail tensor at the *same offset* as that layer's indexer tensor with `block_stride = idx_page`. Tail block `b` is therefore the first 2048 B (`[2, kpool=4, 128]` bf16) of indexer block `b`; the two never collide because both groups draw distinct block ids from one pool. `create_kv_cache_views` builds the view with `as_strided`, so `tail_kv_cache.stride(0) == 19008` elements instead of the dense 1024.

**The bug.** `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py` computed

```python
base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM   # dense 2048 B block stride
```

so for every prefill it (a) left the request's own tail block unseeded and (b) wrote 2048 B of raw bf16 K / gate rows at byte `blk * 2048` of the layer's indexer region, i.e. into indexer block `blk * 2048 // 38016` at offset `blk * 2048 % 38016` — fp8 key rows or the fp32 scale region of whatever request owns that block. The decode kernel (`TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS` / `KPOOL_HEAD`) and the AMD seed kernel already address the tail through `stride(0)` / `stride(1)`; only the NVIDIA seed kernel did not, and the existing regression test for exactly this layout was `skipif(not is_rocm)`.

**Why it shows up as "the cached system prompt is broken".** Only indexer blocks with id below `num_blocks * 2048 / 38016` (~5% of the pool) can be hit, and those are the ids handed out first after startup, i.e. the blocks of the first prefix-cached prompt, typically a long-lived system prompt. Every later request whose tail block id falls in `[19, ~19 * k]` overwrites part of that prompt's indexer blocks `1..k`; prefix-cached blocks are never recomputed, so the damage persists and accumulates, on every TP rank identically. The MLA KV itself is untouched (all writes stay inside the layer's indexer region), so the effect is a corrupted sparse top-k selection for any context longer than `index_topk` (2048). The predicted signature is therefore: with prefix caching on, requests that hit a long-lived cached prompt degrade over time while the same prompt sent with a `cache_salt` (fresh, high block ids) stays correct even on repeated cache hits, and all TP ranks are affected identically. The reproduction below confirms exactly this.

**Fix.** Pass `TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS = tail.stride(0)` and `KPOOL_HEAD = tail.stride(1)` to the NVIDIA seed kernel (same as the AMD kernel), assert the expected view layout in `kpool_seed_tail_cache`, and run `test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride` on every platform.

**Origin.** The tail cache has aliased the indexer tensor with a padded, strided view since the tail spec was introduced on the GLM-5.3-Flash development branch (07-28); the prefill seed was a torch fancy-index scatter (`tail[block_ids, 0, offsets] = k`, stride-correct) until it was replaced by this Triton kernel with dense addressing (08-17, "perf: indexer eager path tail seed and scatter"). The kernel reached main unchanged with #53906 and is unchanged in the current main, so every NVIDIA build since #53906 is affected.

**Not a duplicate.** #56059 adds a `NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS` out-of-range guard to the same kernel for a ROCm fault (#56037); it does not change the addressing, and the two changes compose. No other open PR touches the NVIDIA seed kernel's addressing.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py -q
```

Kernel-level repro (SM103): build the runtime tail view with `create_kv_cache_views(KpoolTailSpec(block_size=4, num_kv_heads=2, head_size=128, dtype=bf16, page_size_padded=38016), ...)` over a sentinel-filled 256 x 38016 B buffer, seed one 6-token request whose tail block is 200 (and 18), then inspect which bytes changed.

End-to-end byte-level probe (GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on 4 x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `enforce_eager`, prefix caching on, `num_gpu_blocks_override=800` so the block pool wraps every ~130 requests): an offline `LLM` serves a 14.5k-token system prompt of 420 "vault -> access code" records, then `collective_rpc` snapshots the indexer K cache pages and the tail cache of the prompt's blocks on rank 0. Eight rounds of 50 unrelated filler prompts (200-2000 tokens each) follow; after every round one lookup question re-hits the cached prompt (keeping it hot in the LRU) and the cached pages are diffed against the snapshot taken right after the first request. Finally seven lookup questions are asked against the hot cached prompt. Same script, same seed, on main and on this branch.

Request-level reproduction against a running server (OpenAI API only, no GPU introspection): same 14.5k-token registry prompt, 7 lookup questions, then batches of 100 unrelated filler prompts (150-1500 tokens, unique prefixes, concurrency 16) each followed by the 7 lookups (cache hit), then the same prompt with `cache_salt` twice. Server: main, TP4, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `enforce_eager`, `--num-gpu-blocks-override 800` so the block pool cycles quickly (with the default pool the same script needs several thousand fillers).

## Test Result

Kernel-level repro, tail view `stride = (19008, 512, 128, 1)` elements:

| kernel | tail block | own tail block seeded | bytes written (layer indexer region) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 200 | no (still sentinel) | `[409600, 411648)` = indexer block 10, fp8 rows 230..245 |
| main | 18 | no | `[36864, 38912)` = indexer block 0 scale region + block 1 rows 0..6 |
| this PR | 200 | yes | `[7603200, 7605248)` = block 200, bytes 0..2048 |
| this PR | 18 | yes | `[684288, 686336)` = block 18, bytes 0..2048 |

`pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py`: on main the un-skipped `test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride` fails (`tail[3, 0, 2]` is still the sentinel); with this PR 29 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only preshuffle test).

End-to-end probe. Runtime views match the analysis: indexer `k_cache` `[7200, 32, 132]` uint8 stride `(4224, 132, 1)` (800 blocks x 9 DeepGEMM pages) and `tail_cache` `[800, 2, 4, 128]` bf16 stride `(19008, 512, 128, 1)` share one `data_ptr`. The system prompt occupies indexer blocks 1..13; the 38 fully cached pages of blocks 1..5 were watched.

| filler requests since the prompt was cached | main: cached pages modified | main: bytes modified | main: re-hit lookup | this PR: pages modified | this PR: re-hit lookup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 16 / 38 | 18.4 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 100 | 21 / 38 | 28.6 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 150 | 21 / 38 | 36.7 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 200 | 24 / 38 | 41.6 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 250 | 25 / 38 | 45.7 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 300 | 25 / 38 | 47.8 KB | no code | 0 | correct |
| 350 | 27 / 38 | 58.0 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 400 | 30 / 38 | 64.1 KB | no code | 0 | correct |

Final seven lookups against the hot cached prompt: main 1/7 correct, with garbled answers such as `vault harbor-harbor-7` and `raven-saffron-203? No, wait`; this PR 7/7 correct. The modified regions on main are contiguous 2048 B runs (e.g. page 9 offsets 0..2816), i.e. one misplaced tail seed per filler request, and on main the very first request already writes 2048 B into indexer block 0 (the null block); neither happens with this PR. In a shorter server-based run on main (default pool of 9259 blocks, only 120 fillers, no wrap-around) the cached prompt was still answered correctly, which is consistent with the sparse per-request damage: each filler misplaces one 2048 B chunk, so a hot prompt degrades as the free list keeps cycling through the low block ids, while a `cache_salt` copy of the prompt (fresh, high block ids) is never hit.

Request-level reproduction on main (correct lookups out of 7; `/metrics` confirmed 96768/101978 prompt tokens served from the prefix cache in every re-hit pass):

| pass | correct |
|---|---|
| fresh prefill | 7 |
| cache hit, before fillers | 7 |
| cache hit after 100 / 200 / 300 / 400 / 500 / 600 fillers | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| same prompt with `cache_salt` (fresh blocks) | 7 |
| salted prompt again (cache hit) | 7 |

After the fillers the model no longer even reads the question correctly (`vault velvet-tundra-143` for `velvet-tundra-67`, `they haven't specified which vault`, `the human turn is empty`): the cached prompt is unusable while the salted copy of the very same prompt is fine.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and the patch; every changed line was reviewed and the tests above were run by the submitter.
