title: [ROCm] Capture CUDA graphs with expandable segments off for AITER all-reduce
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Purpose

With `expandable_segments:True`, the caching allocator hands out VMM-backed pointers, which `hipIpcGetMemHandle` cannot export. AITER's custom all-reduce therefore stages every all-reduce captured in a CUDA graph through a device-to-device copy.

The activations feeding those all-reduces are allocated inside graph capture from the graph's private pool. Turning expandable segments off for the duration of `graph_capture()` makes them exportable, so AITER takes its registered, copy-free path. Weights, KV cache and allocations made outside `graph_capture()` keep expandable segments.

No flag. It applies automatically on ROCm when the TP group's AITER custom all-reduce registers graph buffers (`AiterCustomAllreduce.registers_graph_buffers`). That needs vLLM not to have turned registration off (the cuMem graph pool), the communicator to be enabled, a non-gfx1250 GPU, and AITER's public `defers_capture_registration` class marker. The marker means AITER takes the registration decision when capture begins; it was added in ROCm/aiter#5799 and first released in v0.1.26.

It is skipped when the DP group also runs AITER collectives. Under DP+EP the MoE combine reduce-scatters a persistent workspace allocated before capture, which the registered path cannot export.

Nothing changes on AITER before v0.1.26 (vLLM pins v0.1.26 since #62486), without AITER custom all-reduce, with the cuMem graph pool, on gfx1250, or when expandable segments are already off.

`non_expandable_allocations()` (`vllm/device_allocator/alloc_conf.py`) flips only that field of the live allocator config and restores the full string on exit, including on error. It uses the same read/flip/restore pattern as `CuMemAllocator.use_memory_pool`.

## Test Plan

- `pytest -v -s tests/device_allocator`
- `pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_custom_ar.py` (2 GPUs; runs in the existing AMD CI step)
- Before/after kernel trace: rocprofv3 `--kernel-trace` on Qwen3-0.6B TP2 decode with cudagraphs, per decode graph replay per rank.
- MI355X, image `nightly-rocm100-77154ca6` with this PR's `vllm/` diff applied. AITER is either v0.1.25 + the ROCm/aiter#5799 diff (Python-only; real v0.1.26 adds only gfx1250 symm_mem and `gemma_norm`, the capture path is identical) or stock v0.1.25. All runs use `PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` unless noted.
  - Gate: Qwen3-0.6B(-FP8, `fuse_allreduce_rms`) at TP1 and TP2, with AITER custom AR on and off, and with expandable segments off.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8 (no mono decode, DSpark k=6 synthetic AL 3.87) with and without SWA bounded replay. Decode benchmark: random 1024 in / 256 out at concurrency 1 and 8.

## Test Result

- `tests/device_allocator`: 31 passed (30 on main).
- `tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_custom_ar.py` on MI355X:
  - `test_aiter_defers_capture_registration` checks that AITER still exposes the marker the gate relies on.
  - `test_rocm_aiter_custom_allreduce_skips_copy_with_expandable_segments` runs on 2 GPUs. It turns `expandable_segments` on, then asserts that inside `graph_capture()` AITER takes the registered path (input bound directly, no staging copy). It also checks the all-reduce result after replay and that expandable segments are restored.
  - Results: all pass with #5799. With the guard forced off, the second test fails. On AITER without #5799, the marker test fails and the GPU test is skipped.
- Before/after trace (Qwen3-0.6B TP2, `expandable_segments:True`; "before" is AITER v0.1.25 = copy-in), per decode graph replay per rank. The counts are identical on both ranks and over all 63 decode steps:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| AITER all-reduce kernels | 57 | 57 |
| `__amd_rocclr_copyBuffer` (staging copy) | 58 | 1 |
| copyBuffer immediately before an all-reduce | 57 | 0 |
| kernels in the replay | 396 | 339 |

  The one remaining copyBuffer is the FULL graph's output copy. Greedy outputs are identical. Unprofiled decode step: 1.29 → 1.20 ms at batch 1 (−7%) and 1.46 → 1.35 ms at batch 4 (−8%). The raw traces are attached in the review thread.
- Gate behaviour:

| Config | Guard | AITER capture path |
|---|---|---|
| TP2, AITER with #5799 | on | registered on every rank |
| TP2, AITER with #5799, expandable off | on (no-op) | registered |
| TP2, stock AITER v0.1.25 | off | copy-in |
| TP1 | off | no AITER all-reduce |
| TP2, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0` | off | vLLM's own custom all-reduce, which fails under expandable segments with or without this PR |

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8 with expandable segments on, measured over one serving run per arm:
  - With SWA bounded replay on, every rank takes the registered path, including in the decoder-replay graphs: 48 lines across 8 ranks, no errors.
  - Decode step vs copy-in (stock v0.1.25): -2.9% at c1 (8.79 vs 9.05 ms) and -1.5% at c8 (11.72 vs 11.90 ms).
  - With replay off, two runs per arm: -2.6% at c1 and -2.0% at c8. That matches running with expandable segments off.
  - Cost: graph pool +0.4-0.5 GiB per GPU, the same as with expandable segments off. KV cache -0.2% (-0.26% with replay on).
- Kimi-K3 8x MI355X MTP K=4 (earlier revision, same mechanism), TPOT P50 at 8k c1 / 8k c8:
  - expandable on: 6.29 / 11.73 ms
  - expandable on with the guard: 6.02 / 11.46 ms
  - expandable off: 6.03 / 11.46 ms

title: [Bugfix][DBO] Fix DeepEP low-latency profiling crash with DP+EP+DBO
author: micah-wil
body:
## Summary
`tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py::test_dbo_dp_ep_gsm8k[deepep_low_latency]` started crashing at engine init (memory profiling) on ROCm (MI300X) with DP+EP+DBO.

Root cause: after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/5607, in the V1 `GPUModelRunner._dummy_run`, the MoE padding mask (`is_padding`) was computed **after** `num_tokens_padded` had been shrunk to a single microbatch for DBO forward-context bookkeeping. The mask only spanned one microbatch, so the DBO ubatch wrapper sliced an out-of-range (empty) mask for the trailing microbatch. That desynchronized the DeepEP low-latency combine across the two microbatches and crashed with:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'recv_hook'
ValueError: torch.cat(): expected a non-empty list of Tensors
```

## Fix
- Compute `is_padding` against the **full** padded token count, before the single-ubatch adjustment, so every microbatch gets a correctly sized mask.
- Route the dummy tokens through the experts during a **profile** run (instead of masking them all as padding), mirroring the ModelRunner V2 behavior so MoE memory is measured and the MoE kernels are exercised.

## Test
Verified on MI300X (2x, DP=2, EP, DBO, DeepEP built from ROCm/DeepEP):
- `test_dbo_dp_ep_gsm8k[deepep_low_latency]` -> PASSED

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix MiMo-V2.5 fused fp8 qkv_proj sharding (pre-shard count is num_key_value_heads; MTP path too)
author: vllmellm
body:
## Purpose

`XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` cannot load on current main at any TP size. 

Currently with TP4, on mi355x/mi300x we will hit this error.

```
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py", line 527, in _shard_fp8_qkv_proj
    w_g_dequant = w_g * s_g_expanded
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1856) must match the size of tensor b (1792) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

This is not platform specific, so every platform that runs this checkpoint is affected.

The root cause is, the checkpoint's fused `qkv_proj` is pre-sharded at `ckpt_tp = config.num_key_value_heads` (4 here), each chunk holding `[Q_c | K_c | V_c]` with its own fp8 block scales, while `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` (#45200) assumes one chunk per KV head. The assumption holds for Pro (8 KV heads / 8 chunks) and for V2.5's GA layers (4/4) — those load fine today — but not for the SWA layers: 8 KV heads over 4 chunks, so each chunk carries two KV heads.

Concretely, for `model.layers.1.self_attn.qkv_proj`:
- weight `(14848, 4096)` = 4 chunks of 3072 Q + 384 K + 256 V = **3712** rows = **29** blocks exactly
- `weight_scale_inv` `(116, 32)` = **4 × 29**; the one-per-KV-head reading expects 8 × 15 = 120 and per-group-floor 112, so the loader's `116 // 8 = 14` expands to 1792 rows vs the 1856-row slice

For GA layers (`(13568, 108)`, chunks of 3392 = 3072+192+128) and Pro (`(27136, 216)`, 8 chunks of 3392) the pre-shard count happens to equal the KV-head count, which is why SWA breaks. 

## Change

1. `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` takes `ckpt_tp` (= `config.num_key_value_heads`, i.e. the number of ranks the checkpoint was pre-sharded into — 4 for MiMo-V2.5, 8 for Pro) and derives the chunk geometry from the layer's own heads/dims.
   - `tp_size == ckpt_tp` → plain chunk of weight and scales (the chunk already is `[Q_r|K_r|V_r]`; scale rows line up with `ceil(rows/128)`);
   - otherwise gather each rank's Q/K/V head rows from the chunks that hold them, dequantize with the per-chunk scale mapping `(row // rows_per_chunk) * ceil(rows_per_chunk/128) + (row % rows_per_chunk) // 128`, reorder and requantize (zero-padding the 26.5-block tail, since `scaled_quantize` needs full blocks);
   - a scale tensor matching neither the per-chunk nor a continuous grid now raises instead of being dequantized with the wrong scale.
2. TP > `num_kv_heads` (GA layers at TP=8) via KV replication, the same convention `QKVParallelLinear` uses for split checkpoints: rank *r* owns KV head `r // (tp_size // num_kv_heads)`, so each Q head stays with the KV head it attends to.
3. `mimo_v2_mtp.py`: the MTP draft loader sharded the fused qkv with a plain `chunk(tp_size)` for weight *and* scales. At TP=4 that is correct by coincidence, at TP=8 the scale chunks come out `[15]*7 + [11]` against a 15-row parameter (rank 7 asserts in `default_weight_loader`) and mid-block ranks take a neighbouring block's scale. It now buffers weight + `weight_scale_inv` per layer and shards them through `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` with `ckpt_tp = config.num_key_value_heads`; non-fp8 fused checkpoints keep the old path.
4. added `tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py`: new CPU-only unit test. It builds GA, SWA and Pro checkpoints in the export's chunk layout with known fp32 weights and asserts, for TP = 1, 2, 4, 8, that every rank's dequantized rows match an independent reference; that tp_size == ckpt_tp returns the checkpoint chunk unchanged; and that reading the SWA scales as one slice per KV head is detectably wrong (relL2 > 5x tolerance). 

For reference, #53242 fixes only the SWA symptom (global row map — exact for SWA, but it mis-scales 62.7% of GA rows and would mis-scale 81.4% of Pro's), and #46755 adds the TP > `num_kv_heads` case with per-KV-head scale arithmetic, which for V2.5's MTP tensors would compute `116 // 8 = 14` and break TP=4 spec decode that works today. 

## Test Plan

Non-spec, the reported configuration (TP=4) and TP=8 + EP:

```bash
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len auto --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo

vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len auto --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo
```

Spec decode (MTP), both TP sizes:

```bash
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len auto --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mimo_v2_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo
```

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template
```

## Test Result

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm serve ... --tensor-parallel-size 4` | crash at load | **Server started, with sensible output** |
| TP=8 (w/wo EP) | `AssertionError: TP size must evenly split the number of KV heads` | **Server started, with sensible output** |
| TP=4 + MTP spec (`num_speculative_tokens=1`) | crash at load | loads, draft acceptance **~95%** |
| TP=8 + (w/wo) EP + MTP spec | crash at load | **loads, draft acceptance 20703/21660 = 95.6%** |
| GSM8K (TP=2/4/8) | n/a (never loaded) | ** around 0.9704 flex / 0.9712 strict ± 0.005** |
| real tensors at TP=4 (GA, SWA, MTP), relL2 vs independent reference | crash | **0.0000** (pure chunk); TP=1/2 ≤ 0.011; TP=8 GA 0.0000, SWA 0.008-0.011 |
| TP=2 end-to-end | crash | *Server started, with sensible output** |
| synthetic GA/SWA/Pro checkpoints, TP 1/2/4/8 | crash / assert | 0.026-0.028 (fp8 round-trip floor) |
| old reading (`ckpt_tp = num_kv_heads`) on SWA | — | detectably wrong: relL2 1.05 |

---

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Fail streams that end in a server error event
author: tevinshi2015
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`vllm bench serve` counts a request as successful when any token arrived, even if the stream then ends in a server error event. This fails those requests in the completions, chat and audio backends, in both `vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py` and the standalone `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py`.

Benchmark client only: no model, kernel or serving path is touched.

## Claims

- A stream that delivers tokens and then an `error` event is reported as failed, with the server's error object in `output.error`. Partial `generated_text` is kept for `--save-detailed`.
- The server's error takes precedence over "Never received a valid chunk to calculate TTFT", which names a symptom rather than the cause.
- Under a mid-run EngineCore kill at concurrency 64, the unpatched report overstates completed requests by 22% and output throughput by 14%, and understates mean E2EL by 8%.

## Validation

Unit (no GPU), at the rebased head `4a4eb4257`, on base `76c6f3f2a`. `test_error_event_stream_is_not_reported_as_success` and its legacy counterpart stream two tokens, then the error envelope, then `[DONE]`, over all three streaming endpoints.

```bash
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -k error_event
```

| Sources | Result |
|---|---|
| Base `76c6f3f2a` (new tests only) | 6 failed, each `AssertionError: assert not True` on `output.success` |
| This PR | 6 passed |
| This PR, full `test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py` + `test_responses_request_func.py` | 74 passed |

Those pytest runs used `--noconftest` in a CPU-only environment. `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files <changed>` passes, including mypy.

End-to-end on one RTX 3060 (clocks locked), Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, `vllm bench serve --save-detailed`, random 512-token prompts, 128 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`; `kill -9` on EngineCore 20 s into the run. Measured at the original commit, before the rebase. Classifying one unpatched run's own requests by token count, at concurrency 64:

| Reported by the benchmark | Reported | Complete requests only | Error |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| completed | 274 | 225 | **+22%** |
| mean E2EL | 2,566 ms | 2,790 ms | 8% too fast |
| output tokens | 32,684 | 28,800 | +3,884 partial tokens |
| output throughput | 2,745 tok/s | 2,418 tok/s | **+14%** |

49 of the 274 "successful" requests (18%) never produced their 128 tokens; their counts run 1-127, median 121, so they do not stand out by eye. With the fix, the same fault reports 221 completed, all complete, and each failed request carries the server's error object.

Only a request that has already streamed a token and then receives the error event is miscounted, so the effect scales with in-flight streams at the fault: 49 at concurrency 64, 1-4 at concurrency 16.

Independent validation at the earlier commit `1e74a69c7`: [regression corpus](https://github.com/k21993/benchmark-stream-audit) from a comment on this PR.

No `RemoteOpenAIServer` regression test is added: a real server cannot deterministically emit this event mid-stream without fault injection, so the tests drive the real request functions over the existing fake session, and the end-to-end run above covers the real failure.

**Model evaluation:** not applicable; this only changes how the benchmark client classifies a response.

## Details

**Root cause.** A generation that fails after the response has started cannot change the HTTP 200 already sent, so the stream generators report the failure in-band:

```text
data: {"error": {"message": "EngineCore encountered an issue. ...", "type": "InternalServerError", "param": null, "code": 500}}
data: [DONE]
```

The clients read only `choices` and `usage`, so the truncated request joins `completed`, its partial tokens join `total_output` and `output_throughput`, and its short end-to-end time joins the E2EL statistics. The report is biased in the optimistic direction exactly when the server is failing.

**Design.** The same envelope is emitted for a dead engine, a failed tool parser and a generation error, so the fix keys on the `error` object rather than on one cause. It uses the same `stream_error` shape as the Responses backend.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched the PRs touching these files:
- #54708 (merged) fails streams with no token chunk; a stream that produces tokens and then fails still counted as a success.
- #55508 (merged) fixed TTFT/E2E latency accounting; it does not look at error events.
- #54628 (merged) handles error events for the Responses backend only.
- #62341 (merged) filters content-free chat chunks; this PR is rebased on it and keeps `_choice_has_streamed_output`.
- #64143 (open) changes SSE data-field parsing, not failure classification; it touches the same file, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

**Follow-up.** The Rust bench client (`rust/src/bench/src/backends/openai_completions.rs`, `openai_chat.rs`) has the same gap and is left out to keep this change in one language. #59736 covers token-less streams there, not this case. I can send it separately or fold it in here.

**How this was found.** While `SIGKILL`ing EngineCore under load to compare what each observer reports, requests in flight at the fault ended with HTTP 200 after 1-116 of their 128 tokens.

---

title: [Perf][ROCm] Add a ROCm path for Hy4 and compile the backbone
author: akii96
body:
## Summary - Adds `vllm/models/hy_v4/amd/`, so ROCm no longer runs the NVIDIA backbone directly, matching the layout every other model in `vllm/models/` already has. - Gives the ROCm backbone `@support_torch_compile`. Without it, vLLM silently resolved `cudagraph_mode` to `NONE` and served the whole 78-layer model eager. - Restores cudagraph capture on ROCm: **13x lower decode latency** (311.7 → 23.8 ms TPOT) in the default cudagraph mode, plus a regression test so this cannot silently return. ## Motivation `hy_v4` was the only model under `vllm/models/` without an `amd/` path, so ROCm ran the NVIDIA backbone directly. This adds one, matching `minimax_m3`, `kimi_k3` and others, and gives subsequent ROCm kernel work somewhere to land. `nvidia/model.py` is untouched; the draft head has no ROCm implementation yet and still resolves to `nvidia/mtp.py`. Prior to this PR the shared NVIDIA backbone had no `@support_torch_compile`, which on ROCm showed up in the server startup logs as: ``` WARNING [vllm.py] `torch.compile` is turned on, but the model tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 does not support it. WARNING [compilation.py] Cudagraph mode PIECEWISE requires piecewise capture, but the loaded model provides neither a compiled submodule nor breakable CUDA graphs. Overriding to NONE. WARNING [model_runner.py] Skipping encoder and decoder CUDA graph capture. ``` Both cudagraph paths were affected: explicit `PIECEWISE` had no compiled submodule to attach to and was overridden to `NONE`, while the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` fell through `without_piecewise()` to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, which dies at capture on gfx942. ## Results 8×MI325X (gfx942), TP8, `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8`, Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly@sha256:f169e8df365b5112a1e6500543e13d8161374277c22c94d8ed60817324c101e1` | cudagraph mode | TPOT | output tok/s | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | `NONE` -> eager fallback, before this PR | 311.7 ms | 3.2 | 1.0x | | `PIECEWISE` -> explicit | 80.6 ms | 12.4 | 3.9x | | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` -> default | **23.8 ms** | **42.1** | **13.1x** | After the fix the default resolves to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and captures both passes (57 FULL + 106 PIECEWISE) with no downgrade. ## Correctness - `tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py`: 6/6 passed. They run a toy Hy4 (2 layers, dummy weights), so they check wiring rather than model quality - The model produces coherent output on ordinary reasoning and arithmetic prompts, with correct answers and clean stop behaviour. | max_gen_toks | GPQA-Diamond (flexible-extract) | correct | blanks | blank acc | non-blank acc | |--------------|---------------------------------|---------|------------|-----------|------------------| | 32k | 79.80% ± 2.86 | 158/198 | 26 (13.1%) | 0/26 (0%) | 91.86% (158/172) | | 64k | 85.35% ± 2.52 | 169/198 | 5 (2.5%) | 0/5 (0%) | 87.56% (169/193) | In the table above A "blank" is a response where the model exhausted its generation budget mid-reasoning and never emitted a final answer choice, so the harness scores it wrong; raising max_gen_toks from 32k to 64k cuts these from 13.1% to 2.5% and accounts for the entire +5.6-point gain, since accuracy on responses that actually completed is statistically unchanged (91.9% vs 87.6%, overlapping at ±2.9/±2.5). The new test runs `VLLM_COMPILE` + `PIECEWISE` and asserts the backbone reaches the compiler and that graphs are actually captured. Existing ROCm coverage pins compilation mode to `NONE`, so it could not observe this.
Serving command ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \ HF_HUB_CACHE=/data/hf_home \ vllm serve tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --port 8000 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-model-len 65536 \ --reasoning-parser hy_v4 ``` The `PIECEWISE` row adds `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'` to the same command.

title: [Perf][Frontend] Offload streaming derender detokenization
author: KEYS-A15
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57350.

The plain streaming chat and completion derender paths currently `call _detokenize_delta()` synchronously from the FastAPI event-loop thread. Under concurrent streaming workloads, this can serialize derender processing and delay unrelated asynchronous work.

This PR:

- Creates an asynchronous wrapper around `_detokenize_delta()` using the renderer's existing shared executor.
- Awaits that wrapper from both `derender_chat_stream()` and derender_completion_stream().
- `Keeps _detokenize_delta()` synchronous for code already executing within the renderer executor.
- Adds regression coverage verifying that both streaming paths execute detokenization on the configured renderer executor rather than the event-loop thread.
- Streaming derender suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `60 passed, 1 xfailed` (an upstream test marked as an expected failure)

I searched open PRs by issue number and behavior keywords. #50550 modifies the streaming reasoning/tool-parser path, while this PR targets the plain incremental-detokenization path. The distinction and proposed executor boundary were confirmed in #57350 before implementation.

This changes execution placement only. It does not change tokenization semantics, stream-state handling, output ordering, model execution, or the public API.

**AI disclosure:** This PR includes code developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex during implementation, test design, and review. I reviewed and understood every changed line and ran all tests listed below.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
```

The focused regression test was also run before and after the production change. It exercises both public streaming methods and compares the detokenization thread with the event-loop thread and the configured executor worker.

The performance workload used 20 concurrent streams with 2,048 one-token chunks per stream, for 40,960 derender requests per run. Tokenization probes using a 1,537-token prompt were issued every 250 ms while derender was under load. Each configuration was run three times, and the table reports the median of the per-run measurements.

The benchmark compared `upstream/main` at `6dc34b6334` with this PR at `a1de8533fe`, using `--renderer-num-workers` values of 1 and 4.

## Test Result

- Streaming derender suite: `61 passed, 1 xfailed`
- The expected failure is an existing parser-path case tracked by #55195.
- Ruff formatting and linting: passed.
- Mypy and all other applicable pre-commit hooks: passed.
- Focused regression before the fix: both chat and completion cases failed because detokenization ran on the event-loop thread.
- Focused regression after the fix: both cases passed and ran on the configured renderer executor.

### Concurrent streaming benchmark

| Workers | Version         | Throughput (tok/s) | Derender p50 | Derender p99 | Cadence p50 | Cadence p99 | In-load tokenize p50 | In-load tokenize p99 |
| ------: | --------------- | -----------------: | -----------: | -----------: | ----------: | ----------: | -------------------: | -------------------: |
|       1 | `upstream/main` |            1120.04 |     7.318 ms |    93.818 ms |    7.316 ms |   93.826 ms |            26.974 ms |           104.076 ms |
|       1 | This PR         |            1118.19 |     7.131 ms |    96.195 ms |    7.131 ms |   96.202 ms |            23.564 ms |           102.095 ms |
|       4 | `upstream/main` |            1098.88 |     7.179 ms |   101.206 ms |    7.178 ms |  101.215 ms |            25.042 ms |           107.417 ms |
|       4 | This PR         |            1112.55 |     7.061 ms |   101.228 ms |    7.061 ms |  101.226 ms |            27.383 ms |           131.855 ms |

With one renderer worker, throughput was effectively unchanged (`-0.2%`), median derender latency improved slightly, and in-load tokenization did not regress. With four workers, throughput improved by `1.2%`, median derender latency improved by `1.6%`, and derender and cadence p99 remained effectively unchanged.

The four-worker in-load tokenization p99 median was higher for this PR, although the individual-run ranges overlapped substantially (`93.87–129.97 ms` upstream and `105.89–134.84 ms` for this PR). This may indicate renderer-pool contention or normal tail-latency variance; the benchmark does not distinguish between them. The results show no material derender throughput or cadence regression from the additional executor hop.

No model evaluation was run because this change does not affect model execution, sampling, token selection, or generated output.

title: [MM][Mistral3] Image preprocessing optimization
author: jzakrzew
body:
## Purpose
Reduce CPU time spent preprocessing images for HF-format Mistral 3 models.

This PR applies two optimizations:

  - On Transformers 5.15 and newer, call PixtralProcessor without dummy text. Image-only calls are supported there, so tokenizing generated [IMG] placeholders is unnecessary. Older Transformers versions retain the existing path.
- Use vLLM's fused mm preprocess normalization on device (introduced in #50411)

### Performance
Skipping generated `[IMG]` text reduces median renderer latency from 75.1 to
69.0 ms for one image (**8.2%**) and from 310.9 to 284.0 ms for four images
(**8.7%**).

Moving rescaling and normalization to the model executor shortens the renderer's
critical path. Resizing remains in the renderer.

```text
Before: renderer: resize + normalize → executor: H2D normalized bfloat16
After:  renderer: resize + raw uint8 → executor: H2D raw uint8 + normalize
```

Setup:

- Model: `mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503`
- Input: random RGB PIL images at the default 1540x1540 size
- CPU: Intel Core i9-10920X
- Torch intra-op threads: 1, matching vLLM renderer/steady-state serving
- Transformers 5.16.1, PyTorch 2.13.0
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (CUDA 13.0)
- vLLM commit `391adf89a7`
- 5 warmup iterations followed by 40 measured iterations
- Configurations alternated during measurement
- Reported values are median latency
- Multimodal processor cache disabled


| Process and stage | 1 image before | 1 image after | 4 images before | 4 images after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Renderer: resize and prepare pixels | 68.3 ms (resize + CPU normalize) | **11.7 ms** (resize + raw `uint8`) | 232.4 ms (resize + CPU normalize) | **45.2 ms** (resize + raw `uint8`) |
| Executor: transfer and normalize pixels | 1.768 ms (H2D `bfloat16`) | **1.265 ms** (H2D `uint8` + GPU normalize) | 7.044 ms (H2D `bfloat16`) | **5.031 ms** (H2D `uint8` + GPU normalize) |


## Test Plan
The tests verify:

- `FusedInputNorm` matches the Hugging Face Pixtral normalization result.
- Mistral 3 returns raw `uint8` pixel values when GPU-side normalization is enabled, and normalized values when it is disabled.
- Use of the standard `PixtralProcessor` through the Mistral 3 processing stack.

## Test Result

```console
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py \
  tests/models/test_vision.py -q

38 passed, 8 skipped, 16 warnings in 34.88s
```

## Duplicate-work check
I found no open PR that implements either optimization.

title: [Perf][GLM] Fuse the kpool tail slot mapping into one Triton kernel
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA models keep a one-block-per-request circular tail cache (kpool). Every decode step — twice per step with MTP, once for the target model and once for the drafter — `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder.build()` maps each token to its request's tail ring with a chain of small torch ops (`arange` + `searchsorted` + `clamp` + `index_select` + `remainder` + `copy_`): 12 kernel launches and ~250 us of CPU enqueue time per build.

This PR replaces the chain with a single Triton kernel driven directly by `query_start_loc`, including the CUDA-graph padding rows. The CPU-tensor path keeps the torch implementation, and the emitted values are bit-identical to it.

With #57317 the generic `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` no longer runs for `KpoolTailSpec`, so `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` is now the only slot-mapping path for the tail group — this fusion covers all of it. It composes with #57477 (the seed-kernel stride fix): this PR only produces the logical slot ids (`block * kpool + pos % kpool`) that consumers decompose with `// kpool` / `% kpool`; physical addressing of the padded tail view is untouched, and the kernel reads the block table through its real `stride(0)`.

Not a duplicate: #56562 covers the sparse-indexer decode expansion and the token→request mapping (an earlier revision of this PR had similar pieces and was rescoped); #57161 reworks the kpool *compress* kernel and #57458 the NoPE query packing — neither touches the tail slot mapping.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py
```

E2E setup: 4x GB300 (SM103), TP4, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`, V2 model runner; `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos`, two runs per build, base = `42a33039eb`.

## Test Result

- `test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`: 17 passed — 4 new CUDA cases check the Triton path against the torch reference, including tokens past the last request boundary, CUDA-graph padding rows, and a non-contiguous (strided-view) block table.
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py` + `test_indexer_native_next_n.py`: 16 passed.
- Bit-exact vs the torch formulation → no output-affecting change, so no separate model eval was run.

Micro (`compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping`, kpool=4, GB300; CPU = enqueue time without sync, GPU = profiler device time):

| shape | torch CPU | this PR CPU | torch GPU | this PR GPU | launches |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode bs=1 (2 tok, MTP k=1) | 157 us | 38 us | 18.2 us | 1.5 us | 12 -> 1 |
| decode bs=16 (32 tok) | 266 us | 35 us | — | — | 12 -> 1 |
| decode bs=64 (128 tok) | 259 us | 34 us | — | — | 12 -> 1 |

| prefill 2x8192 | 243 us | 32 us | — | — | 12 -> 1 |

E2E (8k in / 1k out, output tok/s, two runs per build):

| point | main | +this PR | Δ (avg) | main run-to-run noise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | 220.1 / 215.3 | 229.0 / 228.7 | +5.1% | ±2.2% |
| c=16 | 1359.8 / 1433.0 | 1461.9 / 1397.8 | +2.4% | ±5.4% |

Median TPOT deltas are within noise at every point (-0.6% to +2.7%). The c=1 throughput ordering was consistent across both pairs of runs (and c=1 mean TPOT was 4.19 ms on both PR runs vs 4.37/4.47 ms on main), but with n=2 per build this sits at the edge of the noise floor. The durable claim is the removed per-step CPU work (~0.44 ms/step with MTP: two builds x ~220 us) and 11 fewer launches per build, which async scheduling largely overlaps on this hardware.

title: [EPLB] Add EPLB support to dspark draft models (DeepSeekV4)
author: ilmarkov
body:
## Purpose
Enable EPLB for DSpark draft models on DeepSeek V4.

DSpark MoE drafters now implement MixtureOfExperts, so EPLB can register and rebalance draft experts alongside the target model when using --enable-eplb with DSpark speculative decoding. 

Dsv4.1 Dspark draft is not supported because EPLB requires target and draft models have the same number of routed experts.
Add logging of draft models to distinguish eplb run of target and draft models.

- Other DSpark drafts (Qwen3, Gemma4, K3 MLA) — dense drafts with no MoE layers; EPLB on the draft is N/A. If the target is MoE, existing target-side EPLB is unchanged.
- DSV4 DSpark on AMD/XPU those platforms don’t yet expose MixtureOfExperts on the target path either.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Add AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill backend
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose

Add `aiter_flydsl` as an opt-in GDN prefill backend on ROCm. Supported BF16 GDN layers with 128-dimensional key and value heads route through AITER's optimized VK implementation with both the fused FlyDSL prepare stage and FlyDSL K5 enabled; unsupported platforms, shapes, dtypes, and older AITER builds retain the Triton/FLA path.

This requires the AITER APIs from ROCm/aiter#4532, ROCm/aiter#4598, ROCm/aiter#4694, ROCm/aiter#4732, and the prepare-kernel fix in ROCm/aiter#4952; all merged.

## Test Plan

**Hardware:** 8x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3
**Model:** `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, BF16 GDN, FP8 KV cache

* **Kernel case:** Added `test_aiter_flydsl_prefill_matches_triton_reference`: packed sequences `[70, 130]`, BF16 Q/K/V, FP32 state, 128-dim heads, GQA ratio 2, run on device and compared against the *same* AITER entry point with `use_chunk_flydsl`/`use_prepare_flydsl` off. Using that as the reference means the two calls differ only in the kernels this backend exists to select. Verified passing on MI355X (gfx950).
* **Reference:** AITER `chunk_gated_delta_rule_opt_vk` with Triton prepare and Triton VK K5
* **Unit tests:** `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py`, pruned to the cases that guard correctness:
  * `test_aiter_flydsl_prefill_matches_triton_reference[fp32_state|bf16_state]` — the numerical check. Packed sequences `[70, 130]` (both span several 64-token chunks and end in a partial one), BF16 Q/K/V, 128-dim heads, GQA ratio 2, run on device against the *same* AITER entry point with `use_chunk_flydsl`/`use_prepare_flydsl` off, so the two calls differ only in the kernels this backend selects. Parametrized over the SSM state dtype because `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` can make it FP32 or BF16 and the backend forwards `initial_state.dtype` to AITER; it also asserts the final state comes back in that dtype, since it is written back into the cache.
  * `test_resolve_aiter_flydsl_gdn_prefill_backend` — the shape/dtype gate. FlyDSL is only taken for BF16 with 128/128 key/value heads; any other combination must stay on Triton rather than reach kernels that don't support it.
  * `test_kda_style_model_cannot_select_flydsl` — Kimi K3 KDA shares this layer but builds its own chunk metadata, which the FlyDSL path skips. This pins that the resolver turns it down before that mismatch can happen.
  * `test_explicit_aiter_flydsl_fails_closed[kernels_missing|not_rocm]` — an explicit `aiter_flydsl` request on a build without the kernels, or off ROCm, raises instead of silently running Triton and reporting the run as FlyDSL.

## Test Result

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement get_top_tokens() on the ROCm DeepSeek V4 MTP drafter
author: BaoYunkai
body:
## Purpose

Enabling `speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` with a `deepseek_v4` draft model **fails
engine startup** rather than falling back to the full-vocab path:

```
ValueError: use_local_argmax_reduction is enabled but draft model DeepSeekV4MTP
does not implement get_top_tokens().
```

Both opt-in sites probe the draft model with `hasattr(model, "get_top_tokens")` and raise when it
is missing (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:1606`,
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py:387`), and `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictor` implements
only `compute_logits`. So the flag is a trap for every `deepseek_v4` checkpoint: it does not run
slower, it does not start.

`model_type: deepseek_v4` is rewritten to `DeepSeekV4MTPModel` by its own branch in
`SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`, which the registry resolves to the per-platform
`DeepSeekV4MTP`, so the generic MTP drafter fix in #56995 does not reach it.

**Fix.** Forward to `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` from both the predictor and the wrapper in
the ROCm implementation (`amd/mtp.py`), mirroring the `compute_logits` pair already in the file.
The `nvidia` and `xpu` drafters are not changed: this was verified on MI355X only, so they are
left to a follow-up that can be tested on that hardware.

V4 reaches its LM head through `hc_head` over the `(T, hc_mult, D)` residual and then the shared
head's RMSNorm, unlike V3 (`shared_head` alone) and V3.2 (an already-normed hidden state). Running
a different transform returns a *different draft token* instead of failing, so that transform is
factored into `_pre_head()` and shared by `compute_logits` and `get_top_tokens` rather than written
twice.

`use_local_argmax_reduction` defaults to `False` and gates every call site, so the default path is
unchanged.

## Test Plan

Hardware: MI355X (`gfx950`), HIP 7.2.53211, torch 2.11.0. Measurements ran against a substrate
built from upstream `releases/v0.27.1` (the sha the host's build names) plus that build's compiled
extensions; in the region this PR touches, v0.27.1 and `main` differ only in how the shared-head
RMSNorm kernel is re-exported, so the arms transfer. The two arms are one tree differing in exactly
one file (`diff -r`).

1. **Unit tests** (added, ROCm only; the module skips before importing the ROCm drafter elsewhere):
   `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dsv4_mtp_local_argmax.py`, asserting that the token
   `get_top_tokens` selects carries the row maximum of the full-vocab logits. Re-run on a v0.30.0
   substrate after rebasing onto current `main`.
2. **Falsifiability**: the same tests run against the merge base, and against two deliberately
   wrong implementations — the shared-head RMSNorm dropped, and `hc_head` dropped.
3. **Micro, TP=2**: both arms as methods on the same predictor over a real TP process group with
   the real `hc_head` op, RMSNorm kernel, `ParallelLMHead` and `LogitsProcessor`, swept over draft
   batch. Four pairs per point, pair 0 discarded, arm order alternated.
4. **e2e, TP=2**: `vllm bench serve` on `DSV4-base-tpl`, fp8 KV cache, 1024 in / 512 out, 300
   prompts, `--max-concurrency 68`. Four interleaved pairs, pair 0 discarded.
5. **GSM8K A/B**: `lm_eval --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, greedy, all 1319 items,
   `enable_prefix_caching=False`, per-sample logging, **with a base-repeat control** (`base2`, a
   second run of the same build) so the noise floor is measured rather than assumed.

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** 3 passed. All 3 fail on the merge base. Dropping the shared-head RMSNorm fails 2 of
3; dropping `hc_head` fails 2 of 3. The norm gain is `normal_(1.0, 0.5)` and the `hc_head`
scale/base are non-trivial on purpose: an argmax is invariant to RMSNorm's per-row rescale, so a
default all-ones weight could not detect a skipped norm at all.

**Micro (TP=2).** This is a trade-off with a crossover, not a uniform win, so the crossover and the
absolute per-step cost matter more than any median over the sweep:

| shape | crossover (draft batch) | worst cost below | best saving above |
|---|---|---|---|
| hidden 4096, vocab 129280 | 36 → 44 | bs=6: +80.8 µs/step (−42.7 %) | bs=1028: −2496.6 µs/step (+80.1 %) |
| hidden 7168, vocab 129280 | 12 → 20 | bs=6: +29.6 µs/step (−12.4 %) | bs=1028: −2511.1 µs/step (+71.9 %) |

**Token agreement is 1.0000 at all 32 swept points**, on both the selected index and the selected
logit value. The crossover had to be recomputed for V4 rather than carried over from #56995's V3
numbers, and it differs between the two V4 shapes.

**e2e (TP=2, concurrency 68, above the crossover).** No change in either direction:

| metric | base | patched | pairwise median | pairwise range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s | 1935.13 | 1929.16 | −0.17 % | −0.92 … +1.26 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 31.25 | 31.22 | +0.55 % | −0.73 … +0.62 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 30.37 | 30.48 | −0.07 % | −1.72 … +0.89 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 584.73 | 588.33 | −1.11 % | −1.59 … −0.33 % |
| Acceptance length | 1.31 | 1.31 | −0.11 % | −1.08 … +0.67 % |

That is the expected result, and it is worth stating why rather than leaving it to be read as a
disappointment: the micro saving at the batch this run reached is 84.7 µs, while the measured
engine step is 40.83 ms (mean TPOT 31.25 ms × acceptance length 1.31), so the predicted e2e effect
is **+0.21 %** — an order of magnitude below the pair-to-pair spread. The e2e arm can show that
nothing regressed; it cannot resolve the win. Pair 0, had it been kept, would have read +8.41 %,
because the base arm alone rose from 1775.6 to 1935.1 tok/s between pair 0 and pair 1 on AITER JIT
warmup. Unchanged acceptance length is the e2e-level statement that the draft tokens did not
change.

**GSM8K (1319 items, 5-shot, greedy).**

| arm | strict | flexible |
|---|---|---|
| base | 0.9515 ± 0.0059 | 0.9507 ± 0.0060 |
| base2 (same build, control) | 0.9522 ± 0.0059 | 0.9530 ± 0.0058 |
| patched | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | 0.9492 ± 0.0060 |

Effect (base → patched) is −0.0015 strict against a noise floor (base → base2) of +0.0008; both are
well inside the ±0.0059 stderr. Per-sample agreement is the sharper test and needs the same
control: base vs base2 produce identical text on **36.5 %** of items, base vs patched on **36.0 %**
— indistinguishable. Same-verdict rates are 98.1 % and 98.2 %. Two runs of one build already
disagree on most generations because vLLM's batching makes bf16 reductions batch-shape dependent,
so without the control column the 64 % of differing prompts would read as a regression. Claim: no
measurable accuracy change on GSM8K within the base-repeat noise floor — not bit-exactness.

**Not covered.** GSM8K exercises one shape of one path and says nothing about long context,
sampling or multi-turn.

---

AI assistance: the patch, its tests and the measurements above were produced with Claude via

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Avoid receive reports for notification-only requests
author: NickLucche
body:
A notif-only decode request (abort/full prefix cache hit) can still need to notify the prefiller to release KV. 
If that notification's handshake fails, NIXL reports a failed receive for a request the scheduler has already removed, crashing EngineCore. 
See "CI issue example" for how this relates to [Buildkite 89597](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89597/list?jid=01a0aefa-3c19-4a8d-b721-4199af7bf4d8&tab=output).

Keep notification-only entries out of receive tracking. This also covers full local prefix hits, where the KV is already local and the scheduler never waits for a receive. Producer notification is still attempted, but its failure no longer reports a receive failure or completion. 

Actual receives retain both signals: completion is needed to release blocks under `fail` or resume scheduling under `recompute`.

## Cancellation example

1. Prefiller P has computed KV for request A.
2. Decoder D cancels A before scheduling it. D removes A from the scheduler, but queues a notification telling P to release its KV. This has `awaiting_kvs=False` and no local receive blocks.
3. The worker attempts the handshake needed to notify P. The handshake fails—for example, because of a block-size mismatch.
4. Before the fix: A was registered as a receive, so the worker reports both `failed_recving={A}` and `finished_recving={A}`. The scheduler processes the completion, cannot find A, and crashes.
5. After the fix: A isn’t registered as a receive. The notification is still attempted and its failure logged, but no receive failure or completion reaches the scheduler.

## CI issue example

In [Buildkite 89597](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89597/list?jid=01a0aefa-3c19-4a8d-b721-4199af7bf4d8&tab=output), a four-block KV receive fails because of the 1920/1024 block-size mismatch (_expected_ for SSMs has block size is tp dependent). 

While returning the generation error, D's serving wrapper submits a separate cleanup request with `abort_immediately=True` and the same producer KV reference. 

That request never runs inference: it only tells P to release its KV. Its handshake hits the same mismatch, and NIXL reports a failed receive for a request already removed from the scheduler, crashing EngineCore.

1. P computes KV for request A. D's attempt to receive it fails; A finishes with an error.
2. D's serving error-cleanup wrapper submits a separate request B with `abort_immediately=True`, carrying A's producer KV reference.
3. The engine immediately aborts B. The connector queues an empty receive solely to notify P to release its blocks: `awaiting_kvs=False`, no local receive blocks. B is removed from the scheduler.
4. B's notification handshake hits the same block-size mismatch. Before the fix, the worker reports `failed_recving={B}` and `finished_recving={B}`; the scheduler cannot find B and crashes.
5. After the fix, B is not tracked as a receive. Notification is still attempted and its failure logged, but no receive failure or completion reaches the scheduler.

cc @njhill @jyizheng since you guys introduced `awaiting_kvs` 

### On Buildkite

The Buildkite adjustment is orthogonal, included in this PR to unblock the release: set both Kimi DP/EP block sizes to 2048 to avoid the 1920/1024 handshake mismatch

title: [Perf] Use breakable CUDA graphs (no torch.compile) by default under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT so the tuned matmul configs see the runtime M
author: LioEinaudi
body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` routes every linear layer through the batch-invariant persistent Triton matmul, which picks its tile config from a per-architecture table keyed by `(N, K)` and an **M bucket** (#53247 Ada/Hopper, #53649 SM100, #57456 SM120). On the default `torch.compile` path that lookup (`_get_matmul_config`, called from `matmul_persistent`) runs while Dynamo traces the model with the compile-time dummy M, and the selected `BLOCK_M / BLOCK_N / num_warps / num_stages` are frozen in the graph. Every decode step therefore runs with the largest bucket's configs (#54243): on RTX PRO 6000 that is 3-6x slower per GEMM than the `M <= 8` configs the tables were tuned for, and it is where essentially all of the remaining batch-invariance overhead goes ([profile](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54243#issuecomment-5723774275)).

Without `torch.compile` the lookup executes at CUDA graph capture time with each capture size's real M, and the tables work as intended. This PR makes batch-invariant mode default to that path via the existing breakable CUDA graph mechanism (#42304, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`), following the same opt-in pattern as `default_breakable_cudagraph_architectures`. It is in line with moving models off `torch.compile` (as suggested in #54503) and needs no change to the matmul or the tables.

## Changes

- `vllm/config/vllm.py`: `_maybe_enable_breakable_cudagraph` also auto-enables breakable CUDA graphs when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the platform is CUDA, the model is bf16 and unquantized, `enforce_eager` is off, sequence parallelism / async TP were not explicitly enabled (they are `torch.compile` passes), and at least one of the per-rank `(N, K)` shapes of the linear layers inside the compiled forward (qkv_proj / o_proj / gate_up_proj / down_proj, derived from `ModelConfig` + TP size; `lm_head` runs in `compute_logits()` outside the compiled graph and does not count) is a key of the device's tuned table. Only when the user did not set `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` themselves; `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` opts out (old behaviour). Logged once.
- `tests/test_config.py`: one parametrized config-level test (`test_batch_invariant_breakable_cudagraph`, 11 cases: on; BI off; explicit opt-out; eager; SP enabled; fp16; quantized; untuned shapes; TP=4 per-rank hit; list-valued `intermediate_size`; no table).
- `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`: one item under "Implementation Details".

No change for `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`, ROCm/XPU, devices without a tuned table, or models whose shapes / dtype the table does not cover (those keep `torch.compile`, since `_get_matmul_config` would fall back to the default config anyway).

## Test Plan

Hardware: one node with RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 96 GB, PCIe), driver 580.159.04; torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1; `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`. The latency numbers below were taken with this PR's first commit on main @ dbf4b89cf2 and the gsm8k numbers (in the comments) at 05fba88af; both trees carried the sm_120 table from #57456, which has since been merged. The gate changes in later commits do not alter the runtime path for these models (their qkv / gate_up / down shapes are in the table), and the final head was re-checked on the same GPU (unit tests + Qwen3-1.7B decode: 0.524 s auto-enabled vs 1.480 s with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`).

Same protocol as #53649 / #57456, all runs in one job on the same GPU per model:

```bash
# BI=1, this PR (breakable CUDA graphs auto-enabled)
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10                                   # decode-heavy (defaults: input 32 / output 128 / batch 8)
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10 --input-len 1024 --output-len 32 --batch-size 8   # prefill-heavy
# BI=1, opt-out on this PR (== previous behaviour, torch.compile path)
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10
# BI=1 on main (same commands, main checkout) and BI=0 reference
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0 vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10
```
Same for `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, plus `-tp 2` on Qwen3-8B.

Correctness / invariance on this PR:

```bash
pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k breakable
pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py
pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "bs1_vs_bsN and (FLASH_ATTN or TRITON_ATTN)"
VLLM_NEEDLE_TRIALS=3 VLLM_NEEDLE_BATCH_SIZE=64 pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "needle and FLASH_ATTN"
```

## Test Result

All numbers from one job, one GPU per model, `vllm bench latency --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10`, avg latency in seconds. "main" = main @ dbf4b89cf2 (+ #57456's table); "this PR, opt-out" = this PR with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, i.e. the previous behaviour on the same tree. Every "this PR" run logged `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1: auto-enabling VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 ...` and ran with `CompilationMode.NONE`; every other run ran with `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`.

**Decode-heavy (input 32 / output 128 / batch 8)**

| model | BI=0 | BI=1 main | BI=1 this PR, opt-out | BI=1 this PR | change vs main | BI overhead main -> this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B | 0.4849 | 1.4305 | 1.4303 | **0.5211** | -63.6% | 2.95x -> 1.07x |
| Qwen3-4B | 0.9366 | 2.3578 | 2.3159 | **0.9797** | -58.4% | 2.52x -> 1.05x |
| Qwen3-8B | 1.5175 | 3.4567 | 3.4408 | **1.5818** | -54.2% | 2.28x -> 1.04x |

**Prefill-heavy (input 1024 / output 32 / batch 8)**

| model | BI=0 | BI=1 main | BI=1 this PR, opt-out | BI=1 this PR | change vs main | BI overhead main -> this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B | 0.2236 | 0.4674 | 0.4692 | **0.2590** | -44.6% | 2.09x -> 1.16x |
| Qwen3-4B | 0.4530 | 0.8095 | 0.8098 | **0.5024** | -37.9% | 1.79x -> 1.11x |
| Qwen3-8B | 0.7928 | 1.2641 | 1.2640 | **0.8254** | -34.7% | 1.59x -> 1.04x |

**TP=2, Qwen3-8B, decode-heavy, BI=1:** main 2.9336 s, this PR opt-out 2.9958 s, this PR 2.8955 s (-1.3%). No gain is expected here because the sm_120 table only has the TP=1 shapes (per-rank shapes fall back to the default config), and there is no regression.

The remaining 4-16% over BI=0 is the batch-invariant kernels themselves plus the Inductor fusions given up by not compiling (with BI=0 the same breakable path costs 2-6% on these workloads, measured in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54243#issuecomment-5723774275). Kernel-level, the persistent matmul is at cuBLAS parity for decode on this path (370 ms vs 388 ms of GEMM time over 128 decode steps of Qwen3-1.7B, vs 1349 ms with the frozen bucket; same comment).

Tests on this PR (+ #57456's table), same GPU type:

```
$ pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k breakable
29 passed, 367 deselected, 14 warnings in 9.11s
$ pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py

$ VLLM_NEEDLE_TRIALS=3 VLLM_NEEDLE_BATCH_SIZE=64 pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "needle and FLASH_ATTN"
```

The generation tests above run the auto-enabled path (re-running the `bs1_vs_bsN and TRITON_ATTN` pair with `pytest -s` shows the auto-enable log line and both engines starting with `CompilationMode.NONE` / `Breakable CUDA graph enabled`).

Plus a TP=2 bitwise check on this PR (Qwen3-1.7B, 64 prompts x 24 greedy tokens, sampled-token logprobs compared bitwise: single-request vs batched and repeat vs repeat, prefix caching off): 0 / 1536 mismatches in all four comparisons, with the auto-enable log line present.

title: [ROCm][CI] Expand single-GPU coverage on MI355 DPX
author: sheralskumar
body:
Move selected single-GPU CI coverage to MI355 DPX through Buildkite YAML changes only, with legacy DPX jobs grouped under their MI355 sections. Keep general suites that were returned to MI300 on that queue in both main and legacy CI.

| Source queue | Main-CI suites moved | Main-CI shards moved |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `mi300_1` | 30/51 (58.8%) | 41/80 (51.3%) |
| `mi355_1` | 44/53 (83.0%) | 62/78 (79.5%) |

Quantization (including GPTQ) and Model Executor (including tensorizer) remain off DPX. Their main-CI AMD mirrors run on `mi300_1`; legacy coverage retains `mi300_1` plus the existing full-card `mi355_1` Quantization jobs. These suites retain their normal assertions and failure reporting.

General LM Eval Small Models, MoE Kernels, Quantization Kernels, and Core Operation Kernels run on MI300 in both pipelines. The legacy labels and hardware selectors match that queue. Their commands, shard counts, timeouts, and failure policies are preserved. Dedicated DPX jobs cover native quantization, FP4/INT4 MoE, and the small gfx950 evaluation model list.

The resulting main pipeline contains 77 DPX groups / 106 shards; the legacy pipeline contains 74 DPX groups / 110 shards. All 225 legacy groups are retained, including the incoming full-card DSv4-Flash disaggregated and TurboQuant t3nc jobs.

The supporting Python, shell, and model-list changes are in [#58244](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58244). This split avoids duplicating those changes across the two PRs. **Merge #58244 first**: the YAML references its new `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/models-gfx950-small.txt` and relies on its supporting fixes.

The MI355 DPX Fullgraph job temporarily sets `TORCHINDUCTOR_PRECOMPILATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0` to avoid the concurrent Triton LLVM codegen/LLD race seen in [Buildkite #90998](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90998#01a0d46e-00d5-4a44-b7eb-1f683ecc6d4b). The failure is `GCNRegPressure.cpp:524: Assertion 'MRI && "call reset first"' failed`. This disables background precompilation while keeping compilation and autotuning enabled; cold compilation may take longer. Remove the workaround once the ROCm Triton pin includes [triton-lang/triton#11567](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11567).

Validation:

- After merging `origin/main` at `4f72bd0152`, applicable pre-commit hooks passed for all 25 YAML paths in the PR, including Buildkite step keys and test tethering. Command: `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -z | xargs -0 /app/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files`. `git diff --check` also passed.
- All 25 changed YAML files parsed with duplicate-key rejection; the PR contains only YAML changes relative to the merged main. Runtime code, tests, and scripts match incoming main.
- Before this main merge, rendered main-CI PR and main-branch pipelines using ci-infra `dd8242b2`, with external Docker-cache lookups stubbed. Both passed generated step-key, queue, and GPU-resource checks.
- Before this main merge, rendered legacy pipelines with the production MiniJinja CLI version `2.3.1` for `amdproduction`, `amdgfx942nightly`, `amdgfx950nightly`, `amdmi300`, and `amdmi355`. All five passed generated step-key, queue, and GPU-resource checks, including single-partition DPX requests without an extra GPU claim.
- Semantic comparison after the merge confirmed all 223 pre-merge legacy groups remain, with only the incoming Helion dependency path correction; both new jobs exactly match main. The merged pipeline has 225 legacy groups. DPX routing, MI300 exclusions, Torchrun timeouts of 55 minutes, and Hybrid SSM timeouts of 80 minutes are preserved.
- Local workaround smoke test: `TORCHINDUCTOR_PRECOMPILATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s 'tests/compile/fullgraph/test_full_graph.py::test_custom_compile_config[compilation_config1-RedHatAI/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic-model_kwargs1]'` passed in 137.79 seconds with fresh Triton/Inductor/vLLM caches. This ran on local vLLM `310f15d354`, stock Triton `3.7.1+gitf0b55c07`, and a full-card MI355. Logs confirmed 16 background-precompile bypasses, 16 autotuning passes, and four generated outputs.
- The complete GPU CI group and DPX model evaluations have not been rerun; the local smoke test does not establish DPX runtime correctness or full-group timing. #58244 must land first to supply the referenced gfx950 model list.

The CI changes, merge conflict resolution, validation, and description were AI-assisted with Codex.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Overlap mHC coefficients for small TP batches
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

Overlap shifted mHC coefficient generation with attention/FFN on small batches. The decoder keeps one post/pre path: the existing mHC dispatcher
selects overlap or native execution, while the decoder joins the coefficient
stream before consuming its outputs.

`supports_mhc_overlap` in `.ops.mhc` requires SM100/DeepGEMM, no ubatching,
and compatible projection dimensions: hidden width divisible by 64, and
`hc_mult * (hc_mult + 2)` a positive multiple of 8 no greater than 32.
The exact H5120/hc4 restrictions and helper assertion are removed.
Compatible tensor/data/pipeline/expert-parallel configurations, attention backends,
and LoRA configurations use the same token cutoff, without a separate performance
allowlist. Larger batches, draft layers, and piecewise/breakable graphs retain
native execution. The cutoff is generalized from the TP4 measurements below;
those measurements do not establish a gain for every newly enabled configuration.

The cutoff is **16 tokens**, based on same-instance paired full-forward
measurements with matching tuned GEMM tactics (three samples per arm):

| Tokens | Native ms | Overlap ms | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.763 | 4.692 | 1.49% |
| 6 | 6.204 | 5.929 | 4.42% |
| 8 | 6.644 | 6.360 | 4.28% |
| 12 | 7.408 | 7.292 | 1.57% |
| 16 | 7.966 | 7.877 | 1.12% |
| 24 | 9.153 | 9.365 | -2.31% |
| 48 | 11.915 | 12.040 | -1.05% |
| 96 | 15.292 | 15.247 | 0.29% |
| 192 | 18.820 | 18.977 | -0.84% |
| 252 | 20.040 | 20.230 | -0.95% |

All samples are retained; the 24/48-token overlap arms contain outliers
(SD 0.390/0.388 ms). Larger shapes show no reliable useful gain, so keep native
execution there. Selection uses the captured token shape, never actual KV
length. Split-kernel warmup is bounded by the same cutoff.

## Validation

Based on main `17e50b9b76`. Latest validation: **79 GPU tests pass**, covering
exact output parity and changed-input CUDA graph replay across `(hidden_size,
hc_mult)` = `(4096, 2)`, `(5120, 4)`, `(7168, 4)`, plus decoder/reference parity
and graph/batch fallbacks. Pre-commit passes.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'overlap_preserves_outputs or decoder_mixes_match_torch' -q -rs
```

Only transient input/scratch tensors (`x`, `mix`, `sqr`) need side-stream allocator
recording. The model retains weights, and callers retain coefficient outputs
until joining the side stream; the helper documents that ownership requirement.

Model/performance measurements below are prior results, not reruns on the new
main base or measurements of every newly enabled configuration.

Measured on GB200×4, model revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`,
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, TP4, DSpark fixed length 5, and synthetic 100K ±5% KV.
These are fixed-forward GPU latencies; no default-O2 piecewise-serving gain is
claimed. The prior ten-sample native/automatic pair measured 6.206→5.932 ms (4.42%).

The refactored commit's three-sample same-instance native/automatic comparison
measures **6.210→5.928 ms (4.55%)**, with identical inputs, KV and tuned GEMM
tactics. Automatic selection activates all 40 target layers. Both arms have
finite outputs and zero eager/graph, changed-input and restored-input replay
errors. Replay checks do not assert native/overlap full-model bitwise parity.

Prior matched real-weight GSM8K: 1271→1268/1319 (96.36→96.13%; 7 improve, 10 regress).
DSpark acceptance length 3.870→3.874. Local FP64 and serialized/async checks support
the numerical change; full-model hidden states are rounding-sensitive. The
refactor preserves the evaluated kernel math and launch order, so this accuracy
evaluation is reused. Prior same-instance allocator peaks increased 16 MiB allocated
and 74 MiB reserved per rank; this is not a serving-capacity measurement.

The projection-width limit of 32 follows DeepGEMM's device-side output-swizzle
constraint. Newly enabled dimensions have correctness coverage, not additional
end-to-end performance measurements.

## Final-head validation (2026-09-21)

Exact head `479b025e45`, GB200×4, pinned model revision above, TP4 **without
DSpark or all-reduce+mHC fusion**, FlashInfer FP8 attention/MXFP4 sparse indexer.
Baseline uses the same head with overlap disabled before loading.

| Metric | Overlap disabled | Enabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Forward-only, KV8704 | 4.727 /4.730 ms (before/after) | 4.657 ms (−1.5%) |
| Real8K/1K C1 mean TPOT | 5.013 ms | 4.992 ms (−0.4%) |
| Median ITL | 5.011 ms | 4.974 ms |
| P99 ITL | 5.228 ms | 6.049 ms |
| Full GSM8K flexible extraction | 1266/1319 (95.98%) | 1271/1319 (96.36%) |

Forward harness: same initialized synthetic weights/KV, five samples ×20
CUDA-graph replays after5s warmup per arm; slowest-rank GPU time, excluding
lm_head/sampling/scheduler/HTTP. All arms pass finite-output and changed-input
replay checks (zero replay error). This is not cross-arm bitwise parity.

Serving: ten exact8192-input/1024-output requests per arm, greedy, C1, two
warmups; FULL_DECODE_ONLY with eager prefill. All requests succeed; candidate
tail bursts in2/10 requests mean this is not a strong serving-speed claim.
GSM8K: lm-eval0.4.12, five-shot chat, greedy, seed123, C8, max output1024;
matching prompts/targets,10 improve and5 regress, strict formatting79.68% both.

**Warmup caveat:** initial overlap-disabled GSM8K reproduced cached FlashInfer
CuTe tactic compilation under strict JIT monitoring. Final arms use identical
startup-only cached-tactic and DeepGEMM split warmup from the existing fix in
#57643, plus identical pinned tactics. Zero monitored runtime JIT afterward;
these workarounds are not part of this PR. No claim of stock-stack zero JIT or
coverage of every newly enabled topology/backend. The79 focused GPU tests
above validate the exact head.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found for shifted mHC coefficient/sublayer overlap. #52725 concerns
XPU norm fusion; #42735 changes BF16 shared staging in the older mHC kernel;
#56761 changes GLM JIT warmup; #51802 registers NVIDIA V4 warmup variants.
None implements this scheduling change.

AI assistance was used to implement, benchmark and test this change.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Optimize MegaMoE staging and NVFP4 cache gathers
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

Reduce DeepSeek V4.1 MegaMoE/MegaAttention prefill overhead: tile multiple tokens
per MegaMoE staging program for sufficiently large inputs, and size the NVFP4
gather grid by request count and output capacity. Keep conservative launch
choices for small inputs. Both transformations preserve the existing arithmetic
and add no persistent buffers.

Dispatch uses eight-token staging tiles from 64 tokens, otherwise one token.
On GB200 at H5120, forced eight-token tiles regress 2–16-token kernels, tie at
32, and improve from 64 onward (both scale layouts):

| Tokens | Native staging us | Eight-token tile us |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 2.400 | 2.752 |
| 32 | 2.880 | 2.816 |
| 64 | 3.328 | 3.136 |
| 128 | 4.672 | 3.296 |
| 8192 | 175.616 | 32.416 |
| 16384 | 348.993 | 60.736 |

NVFP4 gathers retain 128 workers for short rows and chunks of >=16 requests.
Otherwise use `min(2048 // num_reqs, max(128, compressed_capacity))` workers.
At 100K gathered rows, 1/2/4/8-request kernel latency falls by 88%/76%/50%/18%;
16/32 requests are unchanged. The caller passes a view of the compressed region
so SWA workspace does not inflate its capacity. No allocation, device-to-host
synchronization or actual-KV decode dispatch is added.

Kernel sweeps use CUPTI, CUDA graphs and cold L2, checking bitwise equality
before timing. Final branch boundary/stride checks are recorded below.

## Performance and validation

GB200×4, DEP4/MegaMoE/MegaAttention, model revision
`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1.
Earlier paired ten-sample fixed-forward confirmations with matching tuned GEMMs:

| Workload per DP rank | Baseline ms | Candidate ms | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Q16K, KV100K | 415.559 | 400.955 | 3.51% |
| B31Q1 + B1Q8K, KV100K | 224.438 | 207.711 | 7.45% |

Mixed baseline SD 9.124 ms versus candidate 0.697 ms; all samples retained.
The earlier three-sample mixed screen improved 6.14%. B8Q2K improves 1.73%;
decode/draft are essentially unchanged. No new model or workspace buffers.
These are synthetic fixed-forward GPU timings, not serving throughput.

Matched full real-weight GSM8K: 1272→1271 /1319 (96.44→96.36% flexible extraction;
7 improve, 8 regress). DSpark acceptance length 3.8281→3.8289. Real-prefill
traces confirm both changed paths execute. Both accuracy arms carry the separate
sparse-remap correctness guard, which is not included in this PR.

GPU validation at `e2a2356a6229`: **29 staging tests and 24 gather tests pass**.
The gather cases cover 1/8/32 requests, 70/128/129/2051 rows, partial gathers,
non-contiguous request strides, untouched bounds, and CUDA-graph replay after
changing lengths in persistent buffers.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py \
  -k 'fused_input_staging or stages_shared_scale_tma_layout' -q -rs
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k v41_nvfp4_gather_matches_insert -q -rs
```

All pre-commit hooks pass. The follow-up removes only benchmark scripts;
production code and correctness tests retain the validated contents. Final dispatched-kernel checks preserve short gathers
and small staging inputs. At H5120/N64, the final staging comparison is
3.360→3.264 us; the gain near the boundary is modest. At H7168/N64,
3.712→3.168 us supports the same cutoff. Large-input gains remain intact.
The earlier real-weight quality evaluation is reused: this dispatch refinement
preserves the evaluated arithmetic; the narrower view changes launch bounds only.

Validation commit `e2a2356a6229` full-model checks pass with finite outputs and zero
eager/graph, changed-input and restored-input replay errors:

- Q16K: 400.490 ms (three samples), consistent with the earlier confirmation.
- DEP B32 adaptive verification, draft length 5 and seeded lengths 1–6:
  112 total tokens; same-instance original/automatic staging measures
  **18.310→18.285 ms (0.14%)**, with matched inputs, KV and GEMM tactics.
  A post-timing trace confirms all 40 staging calls: summed kernel time
  144.00→112.16 us; MegaMoE time remains 11.703 ms in both arms.

An earlier unpaired B32 check measured 30.287 ms with high spread. It is retained
as an unexplained slow run, not used to estimate the staging effect. The paired
check above isolates staging and does not reproduce that regression. Compilation
is excluded from timing and guarded against during timed work.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found for tiled DeepSeek MegaMoE staging or CUDA NVFP4 gather sizing.
#56720 sizes a ROCm FP8 gather grid and explicitly preserves CUDA dispatch;
this change targets the separate CUDA NVFP4 branch. #43592 targets MiniMax-M2
prepared-input fusion rather than this DeepSeek staging kernel. #55109 fixes
block-table strides; #57489 adds gfx950 FP4 attention. Neither implements these
CUDA launch heuristics.

AI assistance was used to implement, benchmark and test this change.

title: [DFlash] Capture the context K/V precompute in the draft CUDA graph
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

Even when the query forward replays a FULL CUDA graph, the DFlash/DSpark draft step still runs the context K/V precompute (`precompute_and_store_context_kv`) eagerly outside the graph, because the number of context tokens varies from step to step.

This PR captures the context K/V precompute ahead of the query forward in the draft's FULL decode graph. Each graph stores one full verify of context rows per request; rows past the batch are padded with `PAD_SLOT_ID` so they write no K/V, and any prefill context beyond the graph's rows is stored eagerly before replay. The precompute has no host syncs, so every DFlash drafter captures it. The draft attention metadata build stays eager, as before.


## Validation

Capturing the context K/V precompute must not change the speculator's proposals. The checks below therefore compare acceptance and accuracy between this branch's parent commit (`c723a831a8`) and `d8de1d3a2f`, and serving performance against current main, with everything else held fixed.

### Setup

- **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).
- **Speculative decoding:** DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and full decode CUDA graphs.
- **Topologies:**
  - **DEP4:** MegaMoE backend with adaptive verification.
  - **TP4:** auto MoE backend with fixed verification.

### Acceptance and GSM8K accuracy

Each pair runs the full GSM8K test set (1,319 identical 5-shot completion prompts) with greedy decoding, concurrency 32, a 1,024-token output cap, and strict answer extraction.

Acceptance length is read from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over the whole run for DEP4. For TP4, it is aggregated from the engine's periodic SpecDecoding log windows over the steady state; the same method is used on both sides of each pair.

| Configuration | Acceptance length, incl. bonus (parent → PR) | GSM8K (parent → PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DEP4 | 3.411 → **3.434** | 1234 → 1228 / 1319 (93.56% → 93.10%) |
| TP4 | 3.471 → **3.463** | 1227 → 1219 / 1319 (93.03% → 92.42%) |

- The acceptance deltas are within ±1% and have opposite signs across the two topologies, and the per-position acceptance curves coincide. The captured precompute therefore does not change what the drafter proposes.
- The GSM8K deltas are run-to-run noise: two repeats of the same DEP4 parent configuration scored 0.9219 and 0.9356 (an 18/1319 spread), which is wider than any delta in the table.
- These results establish parity with the parent; they do not claim an accuracy improvement.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K server configuration</summary>

Common flags:

```bash
--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128
```

DSpark is configured with 5 speculative tokens.

- **DEP4:** `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`, with adaptive verification enabled.
- **TP4:** `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, with the auto MoE backend and adaptive verification disabled.

</details>

### Serving benchmark

TP4, DSpark (5 speculative tokens, synthetic acceptance length 5.5), random dataset with 128 input / 1,024 output tokens. **Base** is main and **PR** is `d8de1d3a2f`. CPU/step is the host time per engine step, measured with an injected per-step probe.

| Concurrency | CPU/step | TPOT | ITL |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.77 → 5.03 ms | 1.27 → 1.08 ms (−15.2%) | 6.95 → 5.88 ms (−15.3%) |
| 8 | 6.64 → 5.24 ms | 1.87 → 1.84 ms (−1.6%) | 9.96 → 9.90 ms (−0.6%) |
| 64 | 6.82 → 5.43 ms | 3.90 → 3.87 ms (−0.7%) | 19.97 → 20.01 ms (+0.2%) |

The PR cuts host time per step by 1.4–1.7 ms. At concurrency 1 the step is host-bound, so this carries through to a ~15% lower TPOT and ITL; at higher concurrency the GPU dominates and latency is roughly unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Serving benchmark configuration</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":5.5}'

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <1|8|64>
```

</details>

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q
```
