title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix multimodal embedding merge in Llama 4 and Mistral Large 3 EAGLE drafters
author: nishantrevur
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57630.

Regression from #50417 (first released in v0.28.0): that change marked these drafters as `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` so the speculator started routing multimodal batches through their `embed_input_ids`, which had been an unreachable alias of `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids` until then. cc @TQCB

`EagleLlama4ForCausalLM` and `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM` implement `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` by borrowing the method object `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids`. That method calls `self._embed_text_input_ids(...)` and reads `self._has_oov_mm_tokens`, both of which live on `SupportsMultiModal`, which the drafters do not inherit. Any multimodal target paired with one of these drafters fails during the first draft prefill (already in the profile run at startup):

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 427, in _run_model
File "vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py", line 507, in embed_input_ids
AttributeError: 'EagleLlama4ForCausalLM' object has no attribute '_embed_text_input_ids'. Did you mean: 'embed_input_ids'?
```

Reproduced on main (bf13ecc) and present in v0.28.0 and v0.29.0 with `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, TP=4, `--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle","model":...,"num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, default cudagraph mode. The same aliasing exists in `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM`; Model Runner V1 takes the same `embed_input_ids` path.

## Change

Replace the borrowed method with an explicit `embed_input_ids` in both drafters that embeds the draft input ids via `self.model.embed_input_ids` and merges external multimodal embeddings with `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, the same shape `EagleMistralForCausalLM` already uses. No behavior change for text-only batches.

## Test plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py -v   # 21 passed (2 new)
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/llama4_eagle.py vllm/model_executor/models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py
```

New test `test_mm_capable_drafter_merges_multimodal_embeddings` (parametrized over both classes) checks text-only embedding and the merge of multimodal rows; it raises `AttributeError` on main.

E2E (4x NVIDIA L4, TP=4, TRITON_ATTN, `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, `max_patches=4`, 18 text + 12 image prompts, greedy, 48 new tokens):

| build | cudagraph_mode | text AL | image AL | image per-pos acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main @ bf13ecc | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | startup crash (`AttributeError: ... '_embed_text_input_ids'`) | | |
| main + this PR | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 2.637 (328 drafts) | 2.424 (238 drafts) | 0.710 / 0.445 / 0.269 |
| main + this PR | NONE | 2.674 (322 drafts) | 2.413 (240 drafts) | 0.708 / 0.446 / 0.258 |

Image prompts now draft with acceptance close to text prompts, i.e. the drafter is receiving the image embeddings.

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and draft this change; every line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Persist FlashInfer autotune cache per rank to fix the rank-0-only cache-hit deadlock
author: MadhavJivrajani
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57423.

`flashinfer_autotune` persists the FlashInfer autotune cache from rank 0 only and, on the next
engine start, broadcasts that file to every rank. FlashInfer keys persisted MoE entries by
`tp_rank` / `ep_rank` (`MoERunner.get_cache_key_extras`), so only rank 0's lookups can hit. A hit
skips the per-tactic reduce of the synchronized tuning pass (`autotuner.py`: "a cache hit skips
that profile's reduce"), so ranks 1..N-1 block in the reduce while rank 0 spins at the trailing
barrier until the 30-minute timeout. Any second engine start that sees the file trips it: a
container restart with the cache directory on a pod-lifetime volume, or a persistent
`VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`.

Fix: each rank saves and loads its own file (`autotune_configs_dp{dp}_rank{r}.json`), and ranks
load only when every rank has a file, decided by one `all_gather_object` over the CPU group. That
gather replaces the previous broadcast and barrier at the same spot, so no collective is added.
Old single-file caches are ignored by name and re-primed on the next start.

## Field report

Observed on one 8xH100 node (SM90), TP8 + EP8 FP8 MoE model, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8a728663`
(v0.28.1rc1.dev388), FlashInfer 0.6.18, `$HOME` on a pod-lifetime emptyDir.

- The engine died of an unrelated GPU fault. The kubelet restarted the container in place 18 times
  over 8.5 h. Every restart: weights and KV cache fine, then all 8 ranks log
  `Loaded 42 configs from .../flashinfer_autotune_cache/0.6.18/90a/<hash>/autotune_configs.json`,
  rank 0 logs `Config cache hit for trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1 (runner=MoERunner, source=config file)`
  (and `gemm2`), ranks 1-7 sit in `Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1: k/21 [30:00<...]`, EngineCore
  logs `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds` every minute, then
  `torch.distributed.barrier` in `flashinfer_autotune` times out and the API server exits with
  `Engine core initialization failed`. Same signature as the log in #57423.
- During the hang: GPU 0 at 100 % utilization, GPUs 1-7 at 0 %; rank 0's worker at 100 % CPU in
  state R, the other seven sleeping. No other process held GPU 0.
- Mitigation/confirmation: renamed only the `flashinfer_autotune_cache/` directory aside and
  restarted the same container on the same GPUs. Autotune ran for 1 s on all ranks
  (`Saved 42 configs`), engine init took 20 s, READY. 19 identical failures, then one success with
  one variable changed.
- The stale and the fresh cache files hold the same 42 keys and identical `_metadata`; the stale
  one is rank 0's, so its keys only match `ep_rank=0`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py
```

New test: `_all_ranks_have_file` with world size 1, world size 2 all present, and world size 2
with one rank missing (must not load). CPU-only, no GPU needed.

## Test Result

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.0) clean on both files.
- The three `_all_ranks_have_file` cases pass when run against the affected 8xH100 pod's Python
  (torch available there).
- The full pytest file was not run locally (no torch on the dev machine); relying on CI for it.
- Live validation of the patched build on the affected deployment: not yet. The failure mode
  itself was confirmed by the cache-removal experiment above.

## Note

This is an alternative to #57579 which ensures all ranks load identical files as the leader.
However, the deadlock leading to vLLM being stuck (and subsequently in a crash-loop) on K8s is
caused by non-leader ranks expecting to see their entries in the cache file, so even if all
ranks load files that are identical, you would still run into this issue.

## AI assistance

The the patch, and the test were drafted with Claude Code and reviewed line by line by the author.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3][Perf] Fuse MLA decode KV-cache write and Q-prep via AITER
author: rbrugaro-amd
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, Kimi-K3 MLA decode runs the per-layer query preparation and the KV-cache
write as separate launches:

1. `vllm::concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` — the fp8 KV-cache write
2. `triton_poi_fused__to_copy_cat_clamp_mul_reciprocal_view_0` — the
   `[ql_nope | q_pe]` concat and that query's static fp8 quant

This collapses both into a single AITER `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla`
launch: **288 → 144 kernel launches and 1351.8 → 682.8 µs (1.98×) per rank over
6 decode steps**, i.e. **9.39 → 4.74 µs per MLA layer per decode step** on
MI355X at TP=8.

Kimi-K3 MLA is NoPE (`mla_use_nope`), while that kernel always applies RoPE and
takes the cos/sin caches as required arguments. It is fed an **identity rotation**
(`cos = 1, sin = 0`) so the rotation degenerates to a no-op — the same approach
ROCm/ATOM uses to route K3 through this kernel.

The identity cache is a **single row**. AITER's per-head and `_opt` decode kernels
clamp `pos` into `[0, cos_cache.size(0))` before indexing, so real positions pass
straight through; a full-length constant cache would otherwise cost ~268 MB at
K3's `max_position_embeddings` of 1 048 576 to express a provable no-op. AITER's
*general* decode kernel does **not** clamp, so the layer refuses
the head counts that would select it (`kv_lora_rank * num_heads < 2048`, i.e.
≤3 heads/rank, reachable at TP=32).

## Scope, and why this is small

This is a **kernel-count / device-time optimization on the MLA decode path**. The
two replaced kernels are a sub-1% slice of a decode step, on 24 MLA layers in a
model that is roughly 1:3 MLA:KDA. End-to-end serving throughput improvement is below 1%

## Relationship to #47757 and #57452

**This supersedes #57452**, which I opened for the same optimization and will
close in favor of this one. That PR stacked on #47757: it carried #47757's six
commits so CI could run, and extended its hook in the shared
`MLAAttention.forward_impl`, also touching
`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py`. Two problems with that shape:

- it could not merge until #47757 did, and it is still under review
- it modified shared MLA code, so every MLA model and backend was in the blast
  radius of a Kimi-K3-only optimization

This PR drops both. It touches **no shared code at all** — only
`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/` — mirroring the vendor-local q/kv RMSNorm fusion that
the same wrapper already owns (#52494, merged). Consequences:

- no dependency on #47757, so CI runs standalone and this can merge in any order
- zero blast radius: no other model, backend or platform can be affected
- it is a **single file** — the AITER call lives directly in the K3 wrapper

#47757 remains complementary: it fuses the **sparse** MLA path (deepseek_v32)
through the shared hook, while this fuses the **dense** Kimi-K3 path inside the
vendor wrapper. Different call sites, no conflict in either merge order.

**Updated after review** (thanks @Rohan138) — the fused call is no longer a
registered custom op, the `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` guard is gone, and the
branch now lives directly in `forward()` instead of a helper returning `None`.
That folded the separate ops module away, so this is now one file. All numbers
below were re-measured on the refactored code.

On `is_compiling()`: the baseline's `triton_poi_fused…` kernel comes from
`mla_decode_concat_quant_fp8` compiling its own `forward_native` (class docstring
at `mla_attention.py:1541`), not from the model being compiled — Kimi-K3 is not
`@support_torch_compile`. The guard was dead code.

### Why not a duplicate

- **#47757** — same kernel, sparse MLA on deepseek_v32; this is the dense K3 path
  and the NoPE handling is new.
- **#55230** — same kernel family, DeepSeek-R1, edits shared `layers/mla.py`.
- **#45798 / #38313 / #41099 / #41101** — the same fusion as a torch.compile
  graph-rewrite pass. Kimi-K3 is not `@support_torch_compile`, so those never fire.
- **#53166** — K3 ROCm MLA, but chunked-context *gather*, a different op.
- **#52494** (merged) — the sibling q/kv RMSNorm fusion in this same wrapper.

## Implementation

One file, `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py`, on the existing K3 wrapper:

- **`_fused_qk_prep_supported()`** resolves everything fixed at load time —
  platform, KV-cache dtype, shapes, DCP/PCP/HiSparse, head padding, and which
  `W_UK` variant is live. Evaluated once in `__init__`.
- **`_fused_decode()`** mirrors `MLAAttention.forward_impl`'s `W_UK` dispatch
  *including its precedence* (fp4 before fp8; both flags can be set at once) so
  `ql_nope` is bit-identical to what the unfused path feeds its concat+quant,
  then issues the fused call and continues through `impl.forward_mqa` and
  `_v_up_proj`.

With the static gating hoisted into `__init__`, the only per-batch condition left
in `forward()` is that the batch is **decode-only**. Everything else takes the
stock `MLAAttention` path, unchanged:

- any batch that is not purely decode (the fused call covers only the MQA slice,
  so a mixed batch's prefill rows would never reach the KV cache)
- **DCP** (the kernel skips `slot < 0` rows, which would then be garbage after the
  query all-gather), **PCP** and **HiSparse** (both rewrite the KV inputs/slots
  before the standalone write, which this path bypasses)
- the fp8-bmm and AMX `W_UK` variants, and any `q_pad_num_heads` head padding
- profile/dummy runs, an unallocated KV cache, or a missing slot mapping
- non-ROCm, non-fp8 KV cache, or head counts that would select AITER's
  non-clamping general decode kernel

## Test Plan

All numbers below are from the **stock upstream nightly**
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0bfc7a15d095fe83ecc82b50561a93c177fece2d`
(2026-09-16), 8× MI355X, Kimi-K3 fp4, TP=8, with **no benchmark harness and no
vendor patches** — plain `vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`:

### Server (identical for both arms)

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1

vllm serve $MODEL \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8010
```

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is the only environment variable set.

### Perf

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tokenizer $MODEL --trust-remote-code \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8010 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 8192 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts $CONC --max-concurrency $CONC \
  --seed 42 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

### Kernel census

Add `--profiler-config` to the same serve command, then bracket a decode phase:

```bash
# appended to the serve command above
--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"/out/traces",
                    "torch_profiler_use_gzip":true,"ignore_frontend":true,
                    "delay_iterations":0,"max_iterations":6}'

# with a bench in flight and past prefill:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8010/start_profile
sleep 15
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8010/stop_profile
```

### Accuracy

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
  --tasks gsm8k --output_path out --log_samples \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1/chat/completions,\
api_key=EMPTY,eos_string='</s>',num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=32768 \
  --gen_kwargs max_tokens=4096,temperature=0,top_p=1
```

## Results

### 1. Decode kernel census — two kernels become one

Rank-0 torch profile, 6 engine steps, 24 MLA layers, `144 = 24 × 6`:

| kernel | baseline | fused |
|---|---:|---:|
| `vllm::concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` | 144 (668.0 µs) | **0** |
| `triton_poi_fused__to_copy_cat_clamp_mul_reciprocal_view_0` | 144 (683.8 µs) | **0** |
| `aiter::fuse_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` | 0 | **144** (682.8 µs) |

**288 → 144 launches, 1351.8 → 682.8 µs = 1.98×.**
Per MLA layer per decode step: **9.39 → 4.74 µs**.

Dispatch lands on AITER's `_opt` decode kernel rather than `per_head` —
`per_head` requires `kv_cache.size(1) == 1` and vLLM derives 1536 here. The `_opt`
gate is `kv_lora_rank × num_heads ≥ 2048`; at TP=8 that is 512 × 12 = 6144.
`_opt` is also the position-clamping kernel the single-row identity cache needs.

### 2. GSM8K — no accuracy regression

Full 1319 questions, 5-shot, `temperature=0, top_p=1`, `max_tokens=4096`,
chat template applied:

| arm | strict-match | flexible-extract | stderr |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fused | **0.9545** | 0.9553 | 0.0057 |

### 3. E2E serving — unchanged within noise

ISL 1024 / OSL 8192 C=1|8|32 one repeat showed TPOT p50 (ms), ITL p50 (ms), ITL p90 (ms), out tok/s for Conc 1 and 8 are flat to within 0.2%. Conc 32 moves ~0.7% in the baseline's favor, having moved ~1% the other way before the refactor — same essential code, opposite sign, so nothing is claimed in either direction.

This is the expected outcome. The fusion removes a sub-1% slice of a decode
step's device time; for scale, `cross_device_reduce_2stage` alone is ~46% of
rank-0 decode device time in the same trace.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Fix MoE reprocess test mock after #57405's kernel refactor
author: vllm-agent
body:
## Problem

Main red on `:nvidia: (H100) FP8 MoE Kernels` and `B200 Kernels Shard 3` (builds [#89911](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89911), [#89914](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89914); alerts #1680/#1681): all 4 parametrizations of `test_unquantized_flashinfer_trtllm_weights_can_be_reprocessed` fail with

```
AttributeError: 'object' object has no attribute 'fused_experts'
```

#57405 refactored `process_weights_after_loading` to delegate through `self.moe_kernel.fused_experts.process_weights_after_loading(layer)`, but the test's `_init_moe_kernel` monkeypatch installs a bare `object()` as the sentinel kernel. Both affected lanes were block-gated on the PR's CI (#89682) and never ran — selection leak, recorded in the ci-infra corpus.

## Fix

Swap the bare `object()` sentinel for a `MagicMock`, which absorbs the delegated call. The padding-clear logic under test stayed in the method itself (`unquantized_fused_moe_method.py:231-232`), so the test's assertions are unaffected.

Signed-off-by: kimi-no-na-wa <kimi-no-na-wa@users.noreply.github.com>

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Fuse TP all-reduce with mHC input preparation
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

Fuse TP all-reduce, mHC post mixing, delayed collapse, and RMSNorm at DSV4.1 decoder boundaries. This replaces three launches with one, preserves the BF16 boundaries, and retains coefficient overlap. The kernel reuses the existing MNNVL workspace without an additional persistent communication allocation.

Enabled by default for eligible SM100 TP4 forwards with 1–16 tokens, including speculative decoding. The selector requires hidden size 5120, hc_mult=4, EP disabled, and a multicast workspace; it does not restrict DP/PP size, LoRA, or attention backend. The existing overlap-support checks still apply, including disabling overlap for ubatching. Larger batches and graph boundaries use the existing operations. Sixteen is the largest size with a validated gain, not a measured crossover.

Builds on #57603, now merged into main, which overlaps coefficient computation but does not fuse collectives. This differs from #51244's terminal mHC/head fusion. Open-PR searches for `mhc allreduce` and `mhc fusion` found no duplicate of this decoder-boundary collective fusion.

The independent startup warmup fixes have been extracted: DeepGEMM mHC projection coverage is in #57843, and cached FlashInfer MXFP8 tactics are in #57842. Neither is included in this fusion PR.

## Communication choice and token cutoff

Keep multicast and the 16-token cutoff. A controlled GB200 TP4 experiment replaced multicast stores with explicit stores to each of the four peers, retaining the same math, Lamport synchronization, cleanup, and PDL. Push did not consistently improve performance:

| Tokens | Multicast kernel | Push kernel | Multicast model forward | Push model forward |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 14.348 µs | 14.634 µs | 4.054 ms | 4.060 ms |
| 8 | 14.395 µs | 14.972 µs | 5.724 ms | 5.728 ms |
| 16 | 13.910 µs | 15.795 µs | 7.133 ms | 7.130 ms |

Kernel timings use cold-L2 CUDA-graph replay, five samples of 50 replays, and the maximum rank time. Model timings use the same synthetic-weight model instance, KV8704, identical tactics, and three samples of 20 replays; they exclude the output head and serving. Multicast and push model outputs were byte-identical on every rank at all nine tested sizes (1–128).

Extending fusion to 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128 tokens regressed model-forward time in this screen, despite isolated kernel gains; coefficient overlap remained disabled above 16. Some nonstandard sizes used default tactics because exact cache buckets were absent. A follow-up using normal serving autotune buckets confirmed the gain at 1 and 16 tokens (4.667→4.060 ms and 7.783→7.127 ms). Near-boundary runs at 17 and 20 tokens failed the unfused baseline's native-top-k correctness check, so no timings from those shapes are accepted. This supports retaining 16 conservatively; it does not establish the exact crossover. No new model accuracy evaluation was run for the experimental variants.

Multicast requires a supported NVLink/NVSwitch configuration and successful group memory setup; GPU generation alone does not establish support. Explicit peer stores could broaden support to Hopper-or-newer systems with suitable peer-memory access without multicast. That would require separate allocation/dispatch support and hardware validation: this PR remains SM100 TP4, and the experimental push variant reused the existing workspace. Push is a possible portability fallback, not a demonstrated GB200 performance improvement.

## Latest model-forward comparison against main

Measured candidate `dd63c1fa00` (runtime source identical to the subsequently merged PR head `7be123b000`) versus main `d2983f2f16` fetched at benchmark start, including merged overlap and the latest DSpark block-table fix in both arms. GB200 ×4, TP4/DP1, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, auto MoE, KV8704, max model length 1M. Matched synthetic weights/KV and 210 cached tactics with normal hybrid token buckets. Five samples ×20 full-forward CUDA-graph replays after warmup, maximum rank time per sample; median reported below.

| Mode | Batch | Component / tokens | Main | Candidate | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No DSpark | 1 | main / 1 | 4.651 ms | 4.055 ms | 12.8% |
| No DSpark | 8 | main / 8 | 6.236 ms | 5.668 ms | 9.1% |
| No DSpark | 16 | main / 16 | 7.806 ms | 7.127 ms | 8.7% |
| DSpark | 1 | main / 6 | 5.867 ms | 5.280 ms | 10.0% |
| DSpark | 1 | draft / 5 | 0.353 ms | 0.344 ms | 2.4% |

DSpark uses fixed draft length5. These are model-forward measurements, excluding the output head, sampling, scheduling, HTTP and acceptance effects. The draft implementation is unchanged, so its small difference is not attributed directly to fusion. All accepted cases pass eager/graph and changed/restored-input replay checks with zero error. Initialization manifests and source/final tactic hashes match between arms.

An additional candidate DSpark B2 target case failed the harness native-top-k score check at layer2; no timing from that shape is accepted, and main B2 was not measured. This run does not establish B2 correctness or new model accuracy. Untimed setup permits compilation and strict JIT checking resumes before validation/timing; neither arm includes the extracted startup fixes #57842/#57843. The comparison measures warmed execution.

## Test Result

GB200 ×4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/DP1, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, auto MoE, no DSpark. Baseline disables only this fusion before model construction; it includes #57603. Both arms use the same checkpoint, configuration and FlashInfer autotuning cache (all 168 entries reused, checksum unchanged).

The latest polling/RMSNorm follow-up loads peer payloads together and distributes norm partials for local shared-memory reads. PDL completion stays early for multi-token forwards and moves to the end for one token. Compared with the previous fused kernel, a same-instance synthetic KV8704 forward comparison measured B1 4.558/4.588→4.044/4.044 ms, B8 6.014/6.012→5.969/5.979 ms, and B16 7.787/7.782→7.794/7.822 ms. B1 baseline varied between runs (4.184 ms in the prior controlled run), so the largest paired percentage is not a robust gain estimate. B16 is 0.1–0.5% slower in the final screen. Output bytes match on every rank for all three sizes; the final collective test also covers signed-zero sentinel collisions.

The serving and GSM8K measurements below are from the initial fused implementation (`fa59bb3883`). They have not been rerun after this output-equivalent follow-up.

8K input / 1K output serving, concurrency 1, three requests per run, forced output length:

| Baseline | 4.947 ms | 4.951 ms | 5.034 ms |
| Candidate, initial | 5.361 ms | 4.510 ms | 16.240 ms |
| Candidate, repeat after GSM8K | 4.578 ms | 4.506 ms | 7.676 ms |

The warmed repeat reduces mean TPOT by 7.5%, but the initial candidate had stalls and tail latency remains higher. These short serving runs do not establish a tail-latency improvement. All requests completed, with 8192 input and 1024 output tokens each.

A separate fixed-forward screen measured B8 6.565→6.028 ms (−8.2%) and B16 8.421→7.785 ms (−7.6%). B32 exercises fallback: 11.382→11.353 ms with identical output. These are three-sample synthetic-weight/cache measurements at KV8704, excluding the output head and serving.

| Flexible extraction | 1267/1319 (96.06%) | 1275/1319 (96.66%) |
| Strict match | 79.08% | 79.98% |

Prompt and target hashes match for every question. Floating-point ordering changes outputs; this is not bitwise model equivalence. The paired results have 11 candidate-only correct answers and 3 baseline-only correct answers.

- Four-GPU collective test passed: changing sizes, all-gather interleaving in the shared workspace, changed-input CUDA-graph replay.
- mHC regression selection: 137 passed.
- 77 saved real operator inputs: maximum relative RMS 2.3e-5 for residuals and 1.5e-4 for normalized inputs.
- CMake `_C_stable_libtorch` build and pre-commit checks passed.



Serving uses max model length 1048576, max sequences 8, max batched tokens 8192, 10 GiB KV cache, prefix caching disabled, Engram CPU offload, and `--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'`. The sequence cap is a validation setting, not a recipe recommendation.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. The human submitter confirmed review and relevant tests for the original submission; the warmup follow-up validation is reported separately below.

## Warmup validation

The sparse-candidate alignment fix and its tests were extracted into #57667. The validation below was run on combined commit `2219a281f8`, before the split, and includes that fix.

The missing mHC specialization was DeepGEMM split=4, not a TileLang epilogue. Warmup now covers splits 1/4/16 for both projection widths on GB200. A fresh-cache test compiled six variants, then successfully checked 26 runtime shapes with further compiler invocations forbidden.

A fresh real-weight TP4 server with `enable_jit_warmup=true` and `--jit-monitor-mode error --jit-monitor-verbose` completed 23 requests (736 generated tokens), spanning 3–8192 prompt tokens and mixed batches of up to eight requests. All four ranks enabled the monitor before requests: zero runtime Triton/TileLang/CuTeDSL JIT events, and no DeepGEMM compiler commands in this run. The 66 focused tests below and pre-commit checks passed.

The original serving measurements above explicitly disabled JIT warmup. These fixes close reproduced intermediate-prefill compilation gaps; they do not establish the cause of the original decode tails or a new steady-state speedup. GSM8K was not repeated for this startup/specialization follow-up, which leaves model arithmetic unchanged.

Rebased onto main `9b49f92344` (merged #57603). Retained the simplified overlap helper and existing fusion eligibility, multicast transport, and 16-token cutoff. The fused CUDA kernel and dispatcher are unchanged. Dropped the obsolete extraction commit so the sparse-indexer alignment fix already on main remains intact.

The kernel and 16-token cutoff are unchanged. The distributed replay test now includes 6/12-token fixed verification and shrinking/growing token counts.

title: [KV Offload] Expose the processed prefix at request finalization
author: mkhazraee
body:
## Purpose

[#51787](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51787) (f12fe10c5c) removed repeated scheduler touch() calls and introduced key positions for request-scoped recency handling. Those positions can include the full prompt before execution completes, so they cannot distinguish the processed prefix from an untouched suffix when a request terminates early.

Expose num_computed_tokens, num_in_flight_tokens, num_prompt_tokens, and num_tokens as read-only ReqContext properties that delegate to Request and stay up to date. These allow offload backends to derive the processed-prefix boundary, excluding in-flight work and the uncommitted final sampled token. Contexts without an associated Request return None. The complete key-position map remains available for outstanding transfers.

Since ReqContext now retains a reference to Request, release completed-batch context references in the async lookup worker before it waits for another batch.

This is separate from [#54979](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54979) and [#43569](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43569), which address GPU cache registration and rollback, and [#52103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52103), which carries provenance through stored events. This PR exposes metadata; it does not change existing eviction policies.

## Test Plan

- Added a scheduler context test checking that token counts reflect subsequent request updates and return None for contexts without a request.
- Added an async lookup regression test checking that completed request contexts are released while the worker remains idle.

## Test Result

All 20 isolated checks passed using the relevant production definitions and repository tests.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Correct the Laguna DFlash acceptance-length reference
author: okorzh-amd
body:
`test_dflash_correctness[laguna-nvfp4-mrv2]` enforces `expected_acceptance_len=3.55 * 0.9` = 3.195, which nothing reaches:

    AssertionError: acceptance_len 3.051 is below 3.195; accuracy=0.895

The reference is wrong rather than the platform slow. Measured with the same test, 200 GSM8K questions, transformers 5.17.0:

    MI355X (ROCm, emulated NVFP4)  acceptance_len 3.051   accuracy 0.895
    GB300  (CUDA, native NVFP4)    acceptance_len 3.0495  accuracy 0.890

Native and emulated NVFP4 on two vendors agree to three significant figures, and the in-run metrics oscillate 2.97/3.09/3.04, so ~3.05 is the steady state rather than a tail artifact. The sibling references in this file are annotated as coming from Table 1 of the DFlash paper; 3.55 looks like the same, and it was never exercised because this parametrization crashed in HF config parsing from the day it was added in #50330 until #57289 fixed that. Its first complete run is what surfaced the bad number.

Set the reference to the measured 3.05 and keep the file's 0.9 tolerance, giving a 2.745 floor and an 11% margin. Adjusting the reference rather than the tolerance leaves the other parametrizations untouched. Deliberately not a `current_platform` branch: the two vendors measure the same thing, so a per-platform floor would encode a difference that does not exist.

Verified on MI355X against main at a1bf8ac12d:

    tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py
        ::test_dflash_correctness[laguna-nvfp4-mrv2] PASSED
    1 passed, 5 deselected in 117.80s

title: [KV-Offloading][TP] : Expand replicated_layout detection to multi-group MLA
author: varun-sundar-rabindranath
body:
## Purpose
KV offloading for MLA models + TP need only offload KV values from one TP rank. 
This is controlled by replicated_layout determination in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`

Building on top of @almogtavor 's work https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50667 (which was eventually closed) , this PR expand the replicated_layout check to include, 
 - SlidingWindowMLASpec
 - Multi-group MLASpec / SlidingWindowMLASpec
 models. 
 
Notably, 
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 
- zai-org/GLM-5.3
fall in this category. 

### Changes:
 - `AttentionSpec.max_tp_shards: int | None = None`: how many distinct shards this cache splits into across TP. A value of means, all TP ranks are replicas. None means unknown and is treated as not replicated.
    * It's opt-in: no spec class has a default that claims replication, so a layer that forgets it only loses dedup, never correctness. This is the same pattern as MambaSpec.tp_replicated.
    * max_tp_shards=1 is set only where the cache has been checked to be identical on every TP rank:
        * generic MLAAttention (mla_attention.py), which covers the DSv3 / V3.2 / GLM-5.3 latent cache;
        * the DSv3.2 indexer cache (deepseek_v2.py; wk_weights_proj uses disable_tp=True);
        * DeepSeek-V4 attention and indexer caches (deepseek_v4/attention.py);
        * the DeepSeek-V4 compressor state (fused_wkv_wgate uses disable_tp=True);
        * the DeepSeek-V4 SWA cache (sparse_swa.py).
 - `KVCacheConfig.kv_tp_replicas: int = 1` : get_kv_cache_configs sets it through `kv_cache_groups_tp_replicas(groups, tp_size, dcp_size)` - The gcd of each layer's `tp_size // max_tp_shards`, taken per layer through `iter_layer_specs`. A layer counts as 1 if it isn't an attention spec, has no value set, or is DCP-sharded under DCP. 
 - Offloading: replicated_layout requires tp > 1 and kv_tp_replicas == tp. T

#### Justification for adding a KVCacheConfig member 
 MLAAttentionSpec shares `uniform_type_base_spec=FullAttentionSpec`, so one `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group can mix MLA and GQA layers. `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` keeps an arbitrary layer spec, so the value has to be computed before that. Otherwise the scheduler could see an MLA spec and wrongly de-duplicate head-sharded KV.

## Test Plan
Add unit tests.

[eval.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32408750/eval.sh)
Methodology : Run models with `vllm serve` and disk-offloading. Run lm-eval 3 times.

<clear gpu and cpu KV caches with reset-prefix-cache endpoint>

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Dedup transfer regions by (base_addr, block_len)
author: G-haoyu
body:
Fixes #57661

- **Root cause**: NIXL region registration deduped transfer regions by `base_addr` alone, and the collapsed branch only refreshed block geometry for MLA regions. In hybrid-attention models, a layer with a different block length aliasing another layer's base address (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash compressor `state_cache` / indexer `k_cache` overlaid on `swa_cache`) was silently folded and inherited the first region's block length. PD transfers of its state were truncated and misaligned, producing garbled output with no errors.
- **Fix**: dedup key is now `(base_addr, block_len)`. Identical-geometry aliases still fold (`test_overlaid_transfer_groups_share_region_geometry` continues to pass, confirming the lossless path is unchanged).
- **Behavior change (maintainer sanity-check welcome)**: `test_ring_scratch_without_mamba_registers_and_addresses_its_own_regions` now expects `_scratch_region_indices == [2]` instead of `[1]`. That fixture (introduced in #56214) overlays rings on a paged region whose block_len differs from the rings' page size — the old expectation had recorded the benign form of this very bug (the ring inheriting the paged region's geometry). If overlay folding was intentional design, this one assertion is trivially revertible.
- **Tests**: added `test_shared_base_regions_with_distinct_block_lens_stay_separate` (two geometries at one base address — 256B MLA swa page vs 128B compressor ring page — must register as two regions with their own block lens and descriptor geometry). Verified in a container: target test fails on HEAD / passes with the fix; `test_nixl_connector_hma/push_connector/tp_mapping` failure sets are identical before/after. `ruff check` + `ruff format` pass.

**Why this is not a duplicate**: searched open issues/PRs (nixl region dedup, deepseek pd disagg, base_addr, garbled output); #52627 is Mooncake-specific and #54926 is un-transferred draft KV — different root causes.

**Model evals**: 2×8 H200 cluster, NIXL P/D disagg — before: fully garbled output; after: clean English/Chinese generations, 0% garble rate, 6 concurrent streams clean (details in #57661).

**AI assistance disclosure**: root-cause analysis and this fix were produced with ZCode (local agent); cluster diagnosis, the initial mitigation patch, and remote test runs were done with Chaterm (remote agent). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and performed the end-to-end cluster verification above.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Refresh max tokens for streaming continuations
author: i-m-aditya
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose

Streaming-input sessions reuse the same scheduler `Request` across input
chunks. Although each continuation carries its own `max_tokens` value in
`StreamingUpdate`, `_update_request_as_session` only replaced the sampling
parameters and left `Request.max_tokens` unchanged. The scheduler could
therefore stop a continuation using the preceding chunk's output-token limit.

This change refreshes `Request.max_tokens` when applying a continuation. The
existing scheduler test now changes the limit from 2 to 10 and then from 10 to
4, so it verifies replacement in both directions instead of using the same
value for every chunk.

This is not a duplicate of an open PR. Searches for `streaming max_tokens` and
`StreamingUpdate max_tokens` found no scheduler continuation fix. Related open
work on cumulative session length and truncated frontend output addresses
different behavior.

No documentation update is required because this corrects the existing
per-chunk `SamplingParams` behavior without changing the public API.

Related issue #37842 and PR #37843 identified and proposed the same fix, but both were closed for inactivity without merging. This PR revives the fix against current main with regression coverage for increasing and decreasing per-chunk limits.

AI assistance was used to investigate the bug, update the implementation and
regression test, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line,
ran the tests listed below, and can explain and maintain the change.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_stop_via_update_from_output \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_check_stop_min_tokens \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_check_stop_length_cap_below_min_tokens \
  -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-format --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py

git diff --check
```

Model evaluation is not applicable. The change only corrects scheduler stop
accounting for streaming continuations and does not modify token generation,
sampling, or model execution.

## Test Result

Before the fix, the updated regression test failed after changing a session's
limit from 2 to 10:

```text
assert session.max_tokens == 10
E assert 2 == 10
```

After the fix:

```text
Streaming scheduler tests: 8 passed
Focused scheduler stop tests: 3 passed
Pre-commit hooks: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

title: [Model Loader] One post-load hook signature; the loader runs every module's hook
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

This PR now carries a follow-up to #64357. The earlier revision ran the model-level hook on every load and reload; that landed in reworked form as #64357. Part of RFC #54477.

#64357 made `finalize_model_weights(model)` run once after every full load and reload, but it calls only the **root model's** `process_weights_after_loading`. Module-level hooks still had two signatures:

| module | signature | who called it |
|---|---|---|
| attention layers (`Attention`, `MLAAttention`, `MMEncoderAttention`, Kimi-K3 MLA / KDA, DeepSeek-V4 CPU attention) | `(act_dtype)` | loader, attention pass |
| root model | `()` | `finalize_model_weights` |
| any other module (VL language models, HY-V4 inner model, Dots3 vision MoE FFN, Kimi-K3 AMD MLA wrapper) | `()` | **its parent, by hand** |

So parents forwarded the hook to their submodules by hand: VL wrappers to `language_model`, Kimi-K3 AMD through a `modules()` loop, Dots3 to `visual` and then to each `block.mlp`, and so on. When a parent forgot to forward, the submodule was never processed, with no error. The loader also carried `TODO(lucas): see if there is a way to unify the signatures`.

## Changes

1. **One signature.** Attention layers record `self.act_dtype` at init and take no argument. This is the default dtype the loader sets from `model_config.dtype` while building the model, which is the same value the loader used to pass. Backend impls (`AttentionImpl.process_weights_after_loading(act_dtype)`) are unchanged.
2. **One dispatcher.** After the quant-method pass and the attention pass, `finalize_model_weights` runs the hook of every module, each module after all of its submodules (depth-first; a submodule shared by several parents runs once, before all of them). It skips quant methods (some are `CustomOp` modules whose hook takes `layer`), does not enter quantized layers (their submodules, such as compressed-tensors Hadamard transforms, belong to the quant method and are processed in the per-layer pass), and skips attention layers, which have already run. The stages stay as they are: per-layer quant pass → attention pass → module hooks; later passes may read what earlier ones produced (e.g. MLA absorbs `kv_b_proj` through its transforms in the attention pass).
3. **No hand forwarding.** These are deleted:
   - the DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 (AMD, NVIDIA) VL wrapper and Kimi-K3 AMD wrapper forwards to `language_model`;
   - the HY-V4 AMD forward to `self.model`;
   - the Dots3 forwards to `visual` and to the `block.mlp` loop;
   - the Kimi-K3 AMD MLA-wrapper loop.

### Behavior

- **Ordering.** As before, all attention layers run before any module hook, and a module's hook runs after its submodules', which is what the deleted forwards guaranteed. Siblings run in registration order. No hook reads a sibling's derived state.
- **No hook runs for the first time, and none runs twice.** I enumerated every class with a no-argument `process_weights_after_loading` (AST scan of `vllm/`). Each one was already reached, either as a root model or through one of the forwards deleted above.
- **Layerwise reload and the sparse NCCL engine** both go through `finalize_model_weights`, so they get the same dispatch.

## Test Plan

- **New test.** `test_finalize_runs_every_module_hook_after_its_submodules` (`tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`) checks that each module runs exactly once (including one shared by two parents), after its submodules, with quant-method modules, quantized layers' submodules and attention layers skipped. `test_attention_post_load_reads_normalized_transform` runs the real loader `process_weights_after_loading` with a real `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod` + `HadamardTransform` and checks that the attention pass sees the transform already normalized, and normalized once.
- **Updated tests.**
  - The fake attention layers in `test_reload.py`, plus `test_mla_backends`, `test_vit_fp8_scaling` and `test_mla_attn_quant_fusion`, now call the hook without an argument.
  - `test_deepseek_v4_vl` now goes through `finalize_model_weights`.
  - `test_root_model_builds_the_fold` asserted the old forward-by-hand contract, so it is deleted.
- **End to end.** GSM8K before and after weight updates, on GB300.

## Test Result

All runs are on GB300, using the same image and seed, against plain main at `7fc467825d`, the PR's base.

**GSM8K.** Each run measures GSM8K at cold start, then again after 3 full-checkpoint direct reloads (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`).

| model | what it exercises | main: cold → after reload | PR: cold → after reload |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | `Attention` reads `act_dtype` from init | 0.895 → 0.895 | 0.895 → 0.895 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP2) | VL wrapper no longer forwards to `language_model` | 0.899 → 0.898 | 0.900 → 0.907 |
| gpt-oss-20b | attention sinks, MXFP4 MoE quant method is a `CustomOp` | 0.438 → 0.023 | 0.444 → 0.022 |

Cold start matches main within noise for all three models. gpt-oss-20b also collapses after a direct reload on plain main; that is a separate issue, fixed in #64692, and unchanged by this PR.

**Unit tests.** 332 passed, 21 failed, 41 skipped. The two new tests pass, and so do the updated tests. `test_attention_post_load_reads_normalized_transform` fails on the previous head of this PR (`fb3b81ad63`, attention saw `1.0` instead of `0.5`), which is the regression a review caught: that head ran Hadamard transforms in the module pass, after MLA had already absorbed `kv_b_proj`. None of the 21 failures comes from this PR:
- **7 DeepSeek-V3 reload tests** (`test_reload_weights` / `test_online_quantize_reload` with DeepSeek-V3-debug, and `test_kv_scale_reload`). They fail the same way on plain main.
- **14 GLM5-next KDA / sequence-parallel tests.** They failed only in the full batch run. Rerun on their own, they pass on both main and this PR.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Restore the fused query RMSNorm + MXFP8 quantization path
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

`can_fuse_query_quant` decides whether the DeepSeek-V4.1 attention block may hand `wq_b` a pre-quantized query, letting `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` do the q/kv RMSNorm and the MXFP8 quantization in one kernel. It probed `linear.input_quant_key`. #53793 renamed that attribute to the private `_input_quant_key` and introduced `get_input_quant_key` as its reader, but this call site was not updated, and it is the last one in the tree still reading the old name. The gate has been unconditionally `False` since that rename, so every layer runs a BF16 `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` followed by a standalone `MXFP8QuantizeSwizzled` over the query — exactly the pair the fused kernel exists to replace.

Read the capability through `get_input_quant_key`, and pass `launch_pdl` to the fused kernel's launch. The kernel already compiles in `gdc_wait()` / `gdc_launch_dependents()` from its `LAUNCH_PDL` constexpr, but without the launch attribute Triton issues an ordinary launch, so the kernel cannot start before its predecessor retires and the wait is inert. Its siblings `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm`, `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` and the Qwen4 PLE/HC kernels pass both. The fused path is CUDA-only by construction, since `can_fuse_query_quant` returns `False` off CUDA, so the new kwarg is never reached on ROCm.

This restores a lost fusion; it does not change model output. The fused kernel reproduces the separate-kernel FP8 bytes, swizzled scales and normalized KV bit for bit.

## Duplicate-work check

No issue tracks this, so issue-number checks are not applicable. Open-PR searches covered `can_fuse_query_quant`, `input_quant_key`, `get_input_quant_key`, `query_quant deepseek_v41`, `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm`, `launch_pdl triton` and `deepseek_v41 pdl`. Nothing else touches `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/query_quant.py`. #53793 performed the rename that stranded this gate. #55505 extends the same contract with input scales and does not change how the key is read. #48086 also adds a missing `launch_pdl`, but in `deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`, for a `TypeError` on non-PDL hardware rather than a lost overlap. #54063 and #53151 teach ROCm AITER kernels to consume `QuantizedActivation` instead of fixing a producer gate.

## Test Plan

```bash
PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13.1/bin:$PATH .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/query_quant.py
```

The existing suite already encodes this gate: `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` asserts `can_fuse_query_quant` is true for the two FlashInfer MXFP8 kernels and that the pre-quantized `wq_b` projection matches the BF16 path at `rtol=0, atol=0`. It needs Blackwell plus a FlashInfer that can JIT, so `nvcc` must be on `PATH` or the whole group skips, which is how the regression went unnoticed.

Two standalone harnesses, not included in the diff, produced the numbers below. One times the isolated production chain `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM → q/kv RMSNorm (+ query quantization) → `wq_b` GEMM and compares outputs bitwise before timing. The other serves the model and sweeps client concurrency, running both code versions inside one job so they share a node, with the order counterbalanced across two jobs.

## Test Result

Standalone commit `20538d465a`, based on `9d75dd4544`. **73 tests passed** in 107 s on GB200. On `main` the same file reports **24 failed**, all of them `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` cases failing at `assert can_fuse_query_quant([linear, linear])`, so no new test was needed. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, ruff format, typos and mypy 3.10.

Model output is unchanged. The microbenchmark checked FP8 data, swizzled scales, normalized KV and the downstream `wq_b` GEMM output for bitwise equality against the two-kernel path at all 14 shapes before timing, and the projection test asserts the same at `rtol=0, atol=0`. No accuracy evaluation is claimed, because the change cannot move a logit.

### Performance
Serving: `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` with `indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4` and `indexer_sparse_logits`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-num-seqs 128`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. Client is `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 1024 input and 256 output tokens, `--ignore-eos` and `--temperature 0` so every request runs exactly 255 decode steps. Concurrency 1 is repeated 10 times and the others 5 times; each cell is the median of per-run medians. The two columns of raw ITL are the two jobs.

| Concurrency | Base ITL (ms) | Patched ITL (ms) | ITL Gain |
|------------:|--------------:|-----------------:|---------:|
| 1   | 5.020 / 5.055   | 4.983 / 5.037   | 0.55% |
| 8   | 6.321 / 6.357   | 6.255 / 6.295   | 1.01% |
| 32  | 8.313 / 8.325   | 8.309 / 8.142   | 1.12% |
| 256 | 12.153 / 12.157 | 12.076 / 12.127 | 0.44% |

All eight paired measurements favour the patched build and swapping the order flips no sign. Concurrency 8 is the most trustworthy row: the two jobs agree at 1.05% and 0.97%, and 48 tokens per step is the shape where the microbenchmark predicts 69.7 us out of a 6.32 ms step, or 1.10%. 


## AI assistance

Claude Code assisted with the investigation, the benchmarks and this description. Juntian Liu requested this PR after reviewing the root cause, the measured gains and the benchmark caveats.

title: [Bugfix][V1] Reject encoder-cache hits with mismatched embedding counts
author: jackLei0901
body:
## Purpose

Addresses the engine-containment part of
[#55546](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55546) and is related to
[#55547](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55547). It does not close
#55546 because frontend multimodal processor-cache (P0) fingerprint/content
validation remains follow-up work.

Keep the encoder embedding count with each V1 multimodal encoder-cache entry and
reject a cache hit when the incoming request expects a different count. Complete
only the mismatched request through the scheduler's existing request-error path,
leaving EngineCore available to later requests.

Client-provided multimodal UUIDs must uniquely identify their data, but accidental
reuse can pair a cached encoder output with a request that expects a different
number of embeddings. The existing
[Multimodal Media UUID Security](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/usage/security.md#multimodal-media-uuid-security)
documentation already assigns UUID uniqueness to the client and documents the
integrity and confidentiality consequences of reuse. This PR leaves that
contract and those risks unchanged while closing the availability gap caused by
different embedding counts.

Related work: [#57833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57833) makes
`MultiModalReceiverCache` prefer a full payload resent by P0, preventing one
stale processor-payload substitution path. The harmful mismatch in both PRs
requires a client-provided multimodal UUID to be reused for different content;
without a UUID, the cache identity is derived from the media content. #57833
does not validate an encoder-cache entry already retained under that identifier:
if an earlier request completed and left such an entry, scheduling can still
skip encoding the preserved payload and reuse the old encoder output. This PR
checks the embedding count at that admission point; same-count,
different-content reuse remains outside its scope.

If the cached tensor is shorter, the mismatch currently reaches embedding merge,
EngineCore exits, and every subsequent request on that engine fails. If the cached
tensor is longer, slicing can succeed and silently serve embeddings from different
content. Checking counts at cache admission prevents both availability and silent
correctness failures; catching only the merge exception would not cover the latter.
This intentionally changes the longer-cache case from apparent success with
embeddings from different content to an explicit request error.

The old release path also re-derived cache size from the request being released.
With one identifier and different request sizes, that could corrupt freeable
capacity accounting and lead to later allocation assertions.

This PR keeps the existing UUID contract and cache keys. It rejects the request
rather than evicting or re-encoding under a contested identifier. Once admission
is validated, the stale entry cannot make EngineCore unavailable; evicting it on
a client-triggered mismatch would also let that client flush a shared entry that
other requests may still be using.

The request finishes through `FINISHED_ERROR`, which currently represents a
retryable request-level internal error and maps to HTTP 500, even though this
input will fail again until its UUID is corrected. The scheduler has no separate
client-error finish reason, and client-provided grammar compilation failures
already use the same `grammar_compile_error_reqs` drain. This PR reuses that
existing request-scoped containment path; it does not introduce the 500 mapping.

No flag is added because the change converts an engine-fatal condition into a
request-scoped error while preserving behavior for identifiers whose embedding
counts satisfy the existing contract.

For EC connectors, an external load calls `allocate()`, which records the
requesting request's expected count locally. That value is not derived from the
tensor returned by the remote cache, and the arriving tensor's row count is not
compared with it. A first remote hit is therefore outside this validation;
later reuse of the locally recorded entry is checked.

A mismatch schedules zero tokens, but it does not spin: both engine loops still
reach `update_from_output`, which drains and removes the request within one
scheduler step.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "encoder_cache and embed_count" -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "mamba_align_encoder_cache_cap_makes_progress or \
eagle3_mm_encoder_cache_with_shift or \
free_encoder_inputs_defers_for_eagle_lookahead or \
encoder_cache_retained_across_preemption_and_resume or \
encoder_cache_recomputed_when_evicted_during_preemption" -v
pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
pre-commit run ruff-format --files \
  vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
git diff --check
```

The GPU comparison runs three sequential SmolVLM requests with
`max_num_seqs=1`: seed a short entry, reuse its identifier for a longer input,
then submit a healthy request under another identifier.

## Test Result

- Five new tests: one encoder-cache-manager lifecycle test and four scheduler
  tests. Three existing manager tests also gain eviction/reset/subclass
  assertions.
- Full encoder-cache-manager file: 21 passed.
- Scheduler tests selected by `encoder_cache and embed_count`: 4 passed.
- Five named adjacent scheduler tests: 5 passed.
- Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check`: passed.

The baseline and fixed GPU arms used the same source baseline, SmolVLM model,
Python environment, and compiled artifacts. The HF processor produced 320 image
tokens for the cached input and 1088 for the later input under the same
identifier.

- Baseline: the mismatch reached V2 worker embedding merge; the mismatched request
  and a later healthy request both reported `EngineDeadError`.
- Final fixed revision: the mismatched request completed with
  `finish_reason="error"`, the healthy request completed, and the process status
  was 0.

The fixed `WARNING` identified `collision-id`, reported that its entry held 320
embeddings while the request expected 1088, and explained that a client-provided
multimodal UUID may have been reused for different content. It contained no
`Attempted to assign`, `EngineDeadError`, or `EngineCore failed` line.

The frontend multimodal processor cache (P0, configured by
`mm_processor_cache_gb`) was disabled to construct cache-lifetime drift
deterministically. A P0 hit reuses the old processed item, while production can
retain an encoder entry after the corresponding P0 entry has been evicted.

Model evals are not applicable. The check only runs while admitting an
identifier-based encoder-cache hit and cannot alter outputs for requests whose
identifier and embedding count satisfy the existing contract.

## Changes

- Store `identifier -> num_encoder_embeds` metadata in `EncoderCacheManager`.
- Preserve it while an unreferenced cache entry remains reusable; remove it on
  eviction and reset.
- Use the stored entry count when updating freeable capacity.
- Compare cached and requested counts before cache-hit admission mutates reference
  state.
- Compare counts when one request repeats an identifier in the same scheduling
  call without double-counting the encoder budget.
- Complete mismatched requests as `FINISHED_ERROR` through the scheduler's existing
  request-error drain.
- Warn with the identifier, cached and requested counts, and likely UUID-reuse
  cause.
- Add coverage for lifecycle accounting, compatible layouts, dangling-reference
  prevention, same-request duplicate identifiers, and scheduler liveness afterward.

The check is entirely in the scheduler and `EncoderCacheManager`, so it applies to
both model runners. The GPU reproduction used the V2 Model Runner.

## Duplicate-work check (2026-09-19)

- `gh issue view 55547 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`: #55547 is open.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "55547 in:body"`:
  no open PRs.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "encoder cache multimodal mismatch"`:
  no direct competing implementation was found.

#55549 and #55952 are closed, unmerged prior art. #55583 and #55616 remain open,
but modify processor/rendering and UUID-derivation paths rather than scheduler
encoder-cache admission. #55616 makes reuse more likely by allowing UUIDs to be
derived from URLs, which further motivates validating the cached embedding count.

<details>
<summary>GPU reproduction script</summary>

The short image must run first so its 320-row encoder output is reusable when the
long image requests 1088 rows. The frontend multimodal processor cache is disabled
so each request keeps its own placeholder layout.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate request-level handling of mismatched encoder-cache lengths."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import traceback
from typing import Any

from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoProcessor
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


PROMPT = "<image>\nDescribe the image briefly."


def make_image(width: int, height: int, color: tuple[int, int, int]) -> Image.Image:
    return Image.new("RGB", (width, height), color=color)


def make_request(image: Image.Image, identifier: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    prefix = f"Image dimensions {image.width} by {image.height}. " * 4
    return {
        "prompt": prefix + PROMPT,
        "multi_modal_data": {"image": image},
        "multi_modal_uuids": {"image": [identifier]},
    }


def count_image_tokens(processor: Any, image: Image.Image) -> int:
    processed = processor(text=make_request(image, "unused")["prompt"], images=[image])
    token_ids = processed["input_ids"]
    if hasattr(token_ids, "tolist"):
        token_ids = token_ids.tolist()
    if token_ids and isinstance(token_ids[0], list):
        token_ids = token_ids[0]
    return token_ids.count(processor.image_token_id)


def generate_once(llm: LLM, image: Image.Image, identifier: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        outputs = llm.generate(
            make_request(image, identifier),
            sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0),
        )
        output = outputs[0].outputs[0]
        return {
            "returned": True,
            "finished": outputs[0].finished,
            "finish_reason": output.finish_reason,
        }
    except BaseException as exc:
        traceback.print_exc()
        return {
            "returned": False,
            "exception_type": type(exc).__name__,
            "exception": str(exc)[:500],
        }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    short_image = make_image(1024, 128, (20, 20, 200))
    long_image = make_image(224, 224, (200, 20, 20))
    healthy_image = make_image(672, 224, (20, 200, 20))

    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True)
    short_tokens = count_image_tokens(processor, short_image)
    long_tokens = count_image_tokens(processor, long_image)

    result: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": args.model,
        "processor_cache_disabled": True,
        "prefix_cache_enabled": True,
        "token_counts": {"short": short_tokens, "long": long_tokens},
        "token_count_guard": short_tokens < long_tokens,
    }

    if short_tokens >= long_tokens:
        result["guard_error"] = "short image must produce fewer image tokens"
        with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            json.dump(result, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            handle.write("\n")
        print("SUMMARY_JSON=" + json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
        return 2

    llm = LLM(
        model=args.model,
        enforce_eager=True,
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        mm_processor_cache_gb=0,
        max_model_len=2048,
        max_num_seqs=1,
        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
    )

    result["short_seed"] = generate_once(llm, short_image, "collision-id")
    result["long_reuse"] = generate_once(llm, long_image, "collision-id")
    result["healthy_after"] = generate_once(llm, healthy_image, "healthy-id")

    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
        json.dump(result, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
        handle.write("\n")
    print("SUMMARY_JSON=" + json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))

    return 0 if all(
        step.get("returned", False)
        for step in (
            result["short_seed"],
            result["long_reuse"],
            result["healthy_after"],
        )
    ) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
