title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Refresh online NVFP4 scales before reload post-processing
author: S1ro1
body:
## Problem and change

Online NVFP4 reuses its MoE kernel and quantization config across weight reloads. Conversion installs new weight-scale tensors on the layer, but the reused config still references the previous alpha storage. Expert post-processing can therefore rebuild derived scales (for example TRTLLM's `g1_scale_c`) using the previous weights' scales. Restoring graph-visible parameter storage afterward is too late to correct those derived values.

Copy the converted `w13_scale_2` and `w2_scale_2` values into the persistent config alphas before expert post-processing. Preserve the kernel, config, and alpha storage identities. This follows up the kernel reuse introduced by #50074; it does not rebuild the kernel or change quantization policy.

Extend the existing lifecycle test with changed scales over three processing calls. Check the values visible during expert post-processing and stable config/alpha storage.

## Related work

Checked open reload/scale work, including #49789, #50521, #50538 and #53741. Those address broader reload arenas, CUTLASS/B12x runtime storage, or ModelOpt reload. None modifies `online/nvfp4.py` to refresh an already-reused config before expert post-processing. This is the narrow online-NVFP4 refresh; broader storage work may eventually subsume it.

## Validation

- On upstream base `606d124b377e6462fe0f9076df4d50c88e4dcf48`, the extended existing test fails before the fix: expert post-processing observes the preceding alpha values on the first changed-weight reload. It passes with this fix.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, and repository checks. The port adds explicit non-null alpha assertions for current-main typing.
- Focused test command on this CPU-only login node (using the existing dependency environment):

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" uv run --no-project --python /home/matej/prime-rl-pd-validation/.venv/bin/python python -c 'import vllm.platforms; from vllm.platforms.cpu import CpuPlatform; vllm.platforms._current_platform=CpuPlatform(); import pytest; raise SystemExit(pytest.main(["--confcutdir=tests/quantization", "tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_nvfp4_reuses_kernel_when_weights_are_reprocessed", "-q"]))'
```

- Earlier B300 component validation of the same seven-line fix used the GLM-5.3 RL deployment's older vLLM base (`2e6816c274496e0a6436773bfa3c1c640b64567b`) and the FlashInfer TRTLLM NVFP4 expert backend. Reloaded versus freshly loaded identical weights had approximately 9.58% and 22.49% relative output RMS error for deliberate 1.1x and 0.9x weight changes before the fix. Afterward both were bit-identical, including replay of a graph captured before reload. Same-weight reload was already exact. These deliberately large changes expose the bug; they are not estimates of normal optimizer-step error.
- No new full-model evaluation or GPU validation on current main was run for this draft. Earlier full-model GLM-5.3 RL measurements retained approximately 0.04–0.05 KL and included a separate trainer experiment, so they do not establish model-level improvement from this fix alone.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex investigated, ported the fix, extended the regression test, and prepared this draft. Submitted as a draft for collaborator assessment; human review and current-main GPU/model validation remain pending.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Parallelise AITER MLA page-index expansion over token chunks
author: fululi12
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a kernel-level microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured from torch-profiler traces on the same build, same shapes. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing a serial per-request loop on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency. Details under "End-to-end context".

## Purpose

`_expand_page_indices_kernel` in the AITER MLA backend is launched with a grid
of one program per request, and each program walks that request's tokens in a
serial loop:

```python
_expand_page_indices_kernel[(num_reqs,)](...)

    req_idx = tl.program_id(0)
    for i in tl.range(0, num_tokens, BLOCK_SIZE):
```

The parallelism is therefore entirely over the batch. That is fine at high
concurrency and degenerates at low concurrency: with `num_reqs == 1` a **single
workgroup** expands the whole sequence while the rest of the GPU idles. The
bug is invisible in the regime it was presumably tuned for.

On a long-context decode workload (MI355X, TP8, ~97k-token context, conc=1)
this measured **61.6 µs per call and 7 calls per model step — 0.431 ms, or
1.23% of a 34.9 ms step**. For scale, 97k int32 stores is ~388 KB, well under
a microsecond of HBM bandwidth. The kernel is not bandwidth-bound; it is
serialised.

This affects **any MLA model on ROCm at low concurrency**, not one model in
particular.

## The change

Add a second grid dimension over token chunks and drop the loop, so each
program handles exactly one `BLOCK_SIZE` chunk:

```python
num_chunks = max(1, cdiv(block_table.shape[1] * kernel_block_size, 1024))
_expand_page_indices_kernel[(num_reqs, num_chunks)](...)
```

The arithmetic, the masks and the stores are unchanged — only the iteration
space is mapped onto the GPU instead of onto one workgroup. The chunk count is
derived host-side from the block table width, an upper bound on tokens per
request, so **no device synchronisation is introduced**; over-launched
programs mask out entirely and cost nothing.

## Not a duplicate

Checked before opening:

```
repo:vllm-project/vllm is:pr is:open expand_page_indices      -> 0 results
```

No open PR touches this kernel or its launch. The nearby open ROCm MLA PRs
address unrelated concerns:

| PR | subject | overlap |
|---|---|---|
| #57085 | ROCM_AITER_MLA non-causal DSpark draft under DCP | none — DCP draft path |
| #53492 | sparse MLA Gluon kernel from Aiter | none — sparse kernel |
| #57923 | startup OOM in AITER MLA FP8 prefill workspace sizing | none — allocation sizing |
| #46172 | optimize rocm aiter sparse mla indexer | none — sparse indexer |
| #54899 | pad the AITER MLA decode head count to a native tile | none — head padding |

The kernel was introduced in #39616 (AITER MLA + Eagle3 on ROCm) and has not
been modified since.

## Test plan

**Bit-exactness against the existing serial kernel.** Both versions built from
source and compared on device — this is an index computation, so a wrong value
does not crash, it silently reads the wrong KV:

```
conc=1 long context, kbs=1    97000 indices identical
conc=1 long context, kbs=16   97000 indices identical
exact multiple of 1024         4096 indices identical
1024+1                         1025 indices identical
1024-1                         1023 indices identical
ragged 4 reqs                 38011 indices identical
kbs=16 ragged tail             4212 indices identical
single token                      1 indices identical
```

Cases cover chunk boundaries, ragged multi-request batches, and
`kernel_block_size > 1`.

### Kernel time — the direct measurement

This is what the change does, measured on the kernel itself rather than
inferred from an end-to-end delta. Torch-profiler traces, same build, same
workload, same serve config, six captured iterations each:

| | calls | total | **µs/call** | per step |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 18 | 0.402 ms | **22.4** | 0.067 ms |
| this PR | 18 | 0.059 ms | **3.3** | 0.010 ms |
| | | | **−85.4%** | |

**6.8× faster.** Identical call counts on both sides, so this is the same work
at the same frequency, no longer serialised onto a single workgroup. That is
the claim this PR rests on, and it is reproducible on any machine with a
profiler — it does not depend on our hardware, our workload mix, or run-to-run
variance.

Measured with `vllm serve --profiler-config.profiler=torch`, ISL 131072,
conc=1, TP8, MTP depth 6.

### Concurrency sweep — does the extra grid dimension cost anything?

Requested during review: the win above is at conc=1, where one workgroup walked
the whole context. At higher concurrency `num_reqs` already supplies
parallelism, so the question is whether the second grid dimension costs
anything there.

The kernel grid-strides rather than partitioning, so a grid width of 1
reproduces the pre-PR launch exactly. "Before" below is therefore the same
kernel launched the old way, not a reimplementation. Width is this PR's
launch-site formula, `num_chunks = max(1, cdiv(block_table.shape[1] * kernel_block_size, 1024))`
(an upper bound on tokens per request read from the block-table width, so
it needs no device sync; at `kernel_block_size=1` this gives 375 / 64 / 8 / 1
for the contexts below). MI355X, 256
CUs, `kernel_block_size=1`, `BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, median of 7 reps x 100
iterations on an idle node. Output compared byte-for-byte at every width and
shape; all agree.

| ctx | reqs | width | before µs | after µs | ratio |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 024 | 1 | 1 | 10.99 | 10.95 | 1.00x |
| 1 024 | 256 | 1 | 10.59 | 10.76 | 0.98x |
| 8 192 | 64 | 8 | 10.73 | 10.74 | 1.00x |
| 8 192 | 256 | 8 | 10.78 | 10.74 | 1.00x |
| 65 536 | 1 | 64 | 16.59 | 10.75 | 1.54x |
| 65 536 | 64 | 64 | 25.94 | 10.83 | 2.40x |
| 65 536 | 256 | 64 | 39.69 | 39.54 | 1.00x |
| 384 000 | 1 | 375 | 114.14 | 10.78 | 10.59x |
| 384 000 | 32 | 375 | 137.30 | 28.28 | 4.85x |
| 384 000 | 64 | 375 | 251.07 | 68.34 | 3.67x |
| 384 000 | 128 | 375 | 300.51 | 153.84 | 1.95x |

**No shape regresses.** The lowest ratio anywhere is 0.98x, on shapes sitting
at a ~10.7 µs floor where run-to-run spread is around ±2%. At 1k context the
width is 1, so the launch is bit-identical to before and those rows measure
noise rather than a change.

Ragged batches are the case worth checking explicitly, since
`num_token_blocks` comes from `max_seq_len` over the whole batch — one long
request widens the grid for every short request too, launching programs that
find nothing to do:

| batch | width | before µs | after µs | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1x384k + 7x1k | 375 | 115.60 | 10.86 | 10.64x |
| 1x384k + 63x1k | 375 | 115.67 | 13.80 | 8.38x |
| 1x65k + 127x512 | 64 | 16.62 | 10.74 | 1.55x |
| 8x65k + 56x1k | 64 | 17.01 | 10.80 | 1.58x |

The widened grid costs nothing measurable: 63 short requests at width 375 still
come out 8.4x ahead, because the programs with no work exit immediately.

Ratios converging to 1.00x at the high end (65k/256) are the expected
behaviour rather than a cost — the "before" side has enough requests to fill
the machine on its own. These remain kernel microbenchmarks; at high
concurrency this kernel is a small share of the step, so the table is here to
show the change does not cost anything there, not to claim a win.

### End-to-end context

The kernel runs 3 times per step on current main, so the 0.057 ms it saves is
about **0.24%** of a 23.40 ms step. That is below what a 1200 s conc=1 arm can
resolve, and it is the honest ceiling for this change on this configuration.

Earlier end-to-end arms are included for completeness, but should **not** be
read as the effect size:

| build | | interactivity p90 | tpot p90 | step time |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | baseline | 110.28 | 0.00907 | 34.01 ms |
| A | this PR | 112.06 (+1.61%) | 0.00892 | 33.45 ms |
| B | baseline | 140.97 | 0.00709 | 26.59 ms |
| B | this PR | 142.75 (+1.27%) | 0.00701 | 26.29 ms |

Both figures exceed what the kernel can physically save, so they are
noise-dominated at this effect size — a 1200 s conc=1 arm carries roughly 1%
run-to-run spread, against a ceiling here well under that. A third arm on
current main measured −0.35%, which is the same noise in the other direction.
The kernel measurement above is the reliable signal; these rows are not.

Worth noting why the end-to-end impact shrank across builds: the per-call cost
is essentially unchanged (23.3 µs then, 22.4 µs now), but upstream reduced the
call count from 6 per step to 3. The serialisation this PR removes is the same;
there is simply less of it to remove than there was.

**Accuracy** is unaffected by construction — the page indices are bit-
identical, so the model reads exactly the same KV. Confirmed anyway with
GSM8k over the full 1319 questions: 0.9659, unchanged.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this PR (Claude). The measurements above are from
runs on real hardware, not estimates. The submitter has reviewed every changed
line.
speedup_claims: 1% on a conc=1 arm), so > **no measurable serving throughput

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Stride-aware decode KDA
author: simondanielsson
body:
## Purpose

Remove 4 contiguous() calls inside the KDA decode hot path, and instead make the decode KDA kernel aware of the strides.

Perf: **0-4% better TPOT** and **0-7% better output tok/s** on decode-heavy workloads

NV added this in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55736.

Q/K are shaped [B,T,H,K] and V/beta is shaped [B,T,HV,V]. The token stride is hence

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Skip the fused silu-mul block-quant fast path when a swiglu clamp is set
author: garrett361
body:
## Purpose

The fused `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` fast path in `TritonExperts.apply` has no clamp
parameter, so a configured SwiGLU clamp limit (`gemm1_clamp_limit`, or `swiglu_limit` from
the model config) is silently dropped for fp8 w8a8 block-[128, 128] experts. Gate that fast
path on `clamp_limit is None` so clamped models fall back to the existing
`swiglu_limit_func` path, while unclamped models keep the fusion.

- Introduced by #42497. In-tree, EXAONE MoE reaches this path: it passes
  `activation="silu"` with a per-layer `swiglu_limit`.
- `TritonExperts` is selected whenever `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts` rejects DeepGEMM, so
  exposure depends on shape and environment: small `M`, small `N`, non-contiguous weights,
  or DeepGEMM not installed, in which case every shape is affected.
  `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1` also masks the bug via the existing
  `not is_deep_gemm_e8m0_used()` term in the same condition.
- `CutlassExperts` already gates its own fused SiLU+quant fast path on
  `activation_config.clamp_limit is None`, so this follows existing precedent.
- `DeepGemmExperts`, the sibling backend for larger shapes, threads `gemm1_clamp_limit`
  through its activation paths and was never affected.

**Relation to #53875.** That PR contains the same guard alongside a new fused CUDA kernel;
this PR is just the correctness guard, which was asked for separately in that thread so it
can land and be backported on its own. Close this one if #53875 lands first.

## Test Plan

`pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` on an H200, which now includes a dispatch
regression asserting the fused kernel is skipped when a clamp limit is set.

## Test Result

The new test fails before the fix and passes after. The rest of the suite is unchanged:
163 passed, and its 3 `test_w8a8_block_fp8_fused_moe` failures at N=4608/K=7168 reproduce
identically on unmodified `main`.

No model eval was run: the change routes clamped SiLU back onto the pre-#42497 unfused
path that the existing block-fp8 suites already cover. Separately, in our own deployment
(out-of-tree, `swiglu_limit = 10.0`, fp8 block quantization) this bug produced deterministic
junk-token argmaxes during decode, which the fix removes.

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] "Fit kpool top-k indices to AITER" with a single Triton kernel
author: simondanielsson
body:
## Purpose

The existing kernel is implemented in pytorch and leads to **18** elementwise kernel launched per forward. We replace it with a single triton kernel.

**Perf: -5% ITL, +3-5% out tok/s**

## What it does

GLM-5.3-Flash's indexer selects `topk + kpool_tail` tokens, where the tail size is <kpool=4 and depends on the number of tokens in the request. AITER expects a fixed topk value independent of request length. Hence we use `fit_kpool_indices_to_aiter` to select the a fixed topk tokens from history and tail respectively, and disregard any extras. 

The kernel prioritizes selecting the tokens from the tail, and then selects the highest prio tokens from the history, until topk tokens are chosen.

title: [Bugfix] Reject a prefix_match_unit that a single KV cache group cannot honor
author: QHarshil
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58020.

With a single KV cache group, `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` uses the block size as the hash unit and drops `--prefix-match-unit` without a warning. The Mamba prefill checkpoint builder (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/checkpoint.py`, used by the Kimi-K3 KDA path with FlashKDA) still reads the flag. It writes the checkpoint for a different position than the one the scheduler registers for that block, and a later prefix-cache hit resumes from the wrong recurrent state. Nothing errors.

This rejects a `prefix_match_unit` other than the block size when there is exactly one group and block hashing is active (prefix caching or a KV connector), the same condition the multi-group path checks before it reads the flag. The flag's docstring already requires every group's block size to be divisible by it, and one group can't honor anything else.

#58020 proposed propagating the resolved unit to the workers. The case above is the only divergence I could reach. With the flag unset, align mode sets the Mamba block size to the attention block size (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`), so the builder's fallback equals the resolver's GCD. #56960 moves the same builder into the shared GDN metadata path, and this check covers it there too.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/kv_connector/unit
```

The suites were also run on clean `main` in a separate worktree with the same packages. On an H100 NVL: the repro below on `main` and this branch, plus `lm_eval` gsm8k and `vllm bench serve` with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`.

## Test Result

- The resolver called directly: it raises for one group with prefix caching or a connector on and a different flag, and returns the block size with the flag unset or equal, with prefix caching and connectors off, and with no KV cache groups.
- `tests/v1/core` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` on CPU: every failure also fails on `main` (`e440b75`) from the environment (no CUDA, no ray, gated models), apart from Hugging Face 429s. Those were rerun three times on both trees and passed each time.
- `test_mooncake_store_worker.py` builds `cache_config` as a `SimpleNamespace`, so the stub gains `prefix_match_unit=None`.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files: passed.

The GPU runs below were on `3300c8c`, before the check was gated on block hashing. The repro enables prefix caching, so it takes the same path.

Repro, a tiny all-KDA `KimiLinearForCausalLM` with seeded random weights and a 2040-token prompt:

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 python repro_kda_checkpoint.py \
    --layout kda-only --prefix-match-unit 32 --block-size 16 --splice 2016:2032
```

On `main` the worker writes the checkpoint at 2016 into the slot the scheduler registers as 2032. The cached request matches a cold run of the prompt with tokens 2016-2031 removed exactly (max first-step top-20 logprob diff 0.0) and differs from the plain cold run by 0.0464. On this branch the command stops at startup:

```text
ValueError: Invalid prefix_match_unit=32; with a single KV cache group, prefix-cache hits land on the block size (16). Unset it or set it to 16.
```

Without the flag, and with one MLA layer added (two groups, flag honored), both arms produce byte-identical output.

`lm_eval` gsm8k 5-shot through `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --language-model-only`: flexible-extract 0.3601 on `main`, 0.3571 here (stderr 0.0132).

`vllm bench serve`, random dataset with a 512-token shared prefix plus 512 input tokens, 128 output, 400 prompts, concurrency 64, seeds 0-2, three rounds per arm with the last two interleaved: output throughput 6598 tok/s on `main` and 6422 here, sd about 400 on both, and the per-round gap changes sign. The shared prefix is shorter than the 544-token block, so there were no prefix-cache hits, and the model has four KV cache groups, so the new check is not on this path. Treat it as a regression check.

Full logs, sha256sums and scripts are attached in the review thread.

## Not a duplicate

```bash
gh issue view 58020 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "58020 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "prefix_match_unit"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes"
```

No open PR validates `prefix_match_unit` for single-group models. #56960 touches the checkpoint builder but not the resolver.

AI assistance was used for parts of this change. I have reviewed every changed line and can defend the design end to end.

title: [ROCm][CI] Add GELU activation for AiterExperts in the modular-kernel coverage
author: divakar-amd
body:
## Purpose

  Part 2 of #54966 plan. `AiterExperts` already declares support for `GELU`, `SITU`, `SWIGLUOAI`, and `SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE` (only `SILU` is exercised today), but the modular-kernel harness (`tests/kernels/moe/modular_kernel_tools/common.py` +  `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`) hardcodes `SILU` for every backend, so none of that support is verified through the actual `AiterExperts.apply()` path
  (shapes, `PrepareAndFinalize` combos, world sizes).

 This adds a real `activation` field to `Config`, threads it through `is_valid()` / `reference_moe_impl` / `make_modular_kernel` / `run_modular_kernel`, and extends the sweep with `GELU` alongside `SILU`. Scoped to:

  - **AITER-only**: pruned via `is_nyi_config` for now; other backends can opt in later.
  - **Unquantized-only**: FP8 + non-SILU-activation combos are a follow-up (needs scale-tensor interleave handling for some activations).

  Note `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` already has direct-kernel activation tests (e.g. `test_aiter_fused_moe_gelu_accuracy`, and `SWIGLUOAI` via the mxfp4  accuracy/determinism tests) — but those call `torch.ops.vllm.rocm_aiter_fused_moe`  directly, bypassing `AiterExperts` and the modular-kernel abstraction entirely. This PR covers the missing integration layer, not a duplicate of that coverage.

  `SITU` and `SWIGLUOAI`/`SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE` are left out of this PR:
  - `SITU`: AITER's SiTUv2 kernel is only implemented behind its MXFP4-quantized    (`per_1x32`) dispatch path. With unquantized bf16 weights      (this PR's scope), AITER falls through to its generic CK codegen instead,      which has no `situv2` instance by design (situv2 is FlyDSL-only per      AITER's own `moe_recipes.py`), causing the JIT failure 
      (`gemm_moe_ck2stages_lookup.h` not found). Verified directly against      `aiter.fused_moe()` outside vLLM. Exercising `SITU` for real needs the      same MXFP4 weight-quantization plumbing already noted as a follow-up      above, left for that work.
  - `SWIGLUOAI`/`SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE`: AITER currently doesn't support this for bf16 (as default ckpt for gpt-oss are in mxfp4). Unquantized bf16 with no tuned kernel config, `fused_moe()` falls back to the default CK  path (`ck_moe_stage1`/`ck_moe_stage2_fwd`), whose compiled kernel takes only an `activation` enum with no `gate_mode`/interleave parameter — it hardcodes  a separated gate/up layout for Swiglu. AITER's interleave-aware `gate_mode` dispatch only exists for the mxfp4 (`a4w4`) path and a CK-tile path gated on `quant_type == per_1x32`; neither is reached here. (Opened [aiter issue](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5760))

  Since `Config.activation` defaults to `SILU`, this has no effect on non-AITER backends: `AiterExperts` only registers when `has_aiter()` is true, and `is_nyi_config` prunes non-SILU activations paired with any other backend at collection time - no new test cases generated elsewhere.

  ## Test plan

  - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k "AiterExperts and singlegpu" -v -s` → 6 passed, GELU + SILU both exercised through `AiterExperts.apply()`.
  - Same file, full suite (all backends, singlegpu + multigpu) → 37 passed, no regressions.
  - `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -v` → 32 passed, 2 skipped.

  ##### Not duplicate work

  Searched open/merged PRs for `54966`, `AiterExperts activation`. Closest is #57074   (merged) — the FP8/unquantized-scoping step of this same issue, doesn't touch  the activation axis. No other open PR adds activation coverage here.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Clamp FP8 scales before UE8M0 rounding
author: rao-ashish
body:
## Purpose

Without this PR, [this reproducer][reproducer] crashes during DeepGEMM warmup for `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base` with the DeepGEMM FP8 linear backend.

`QuantFP8._quantize_group_native` previously rounded activation scales to UE8M0-compatible powers of two before applying `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR`. For zero or sufficiently small activation groups, the subsequent clamp replaced the rounded value with `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR`, which is not a power of two. DeepGEMM requires FP32 scale factors used for UE8M0 packing to have zero sign and mantissa bits, so these clamped scales triggered a device assertion while DeepGEMM packed them.

This PR applies the minimum-scale clamp before UE8M0 rounding. The resulting scale therefore remains at least `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR` while satisfying the exponent-only representation expected by DeepGEMM. The non-UE8M0 path retains its existing behavior.

The existing group-quantization edge-case test is extended to cover an all-zero input with UE8M0 enabled. It verifies both the minimum-scale bound and the zero-sign-and-mantissa invariant enforced by DeepGEMM.

[reproducer]: https://gist.github.com/rao-ashish/8a648b7aadbf4380bc3a6e643b1cb471

## Test Plan

Run the targeted `QuantFP8` group-quantization edge-case test:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant_group.py::test_quantfp8_group_edge_cases
```

Run the [reproducer][reproducer] on an NVIDIA GB300 with the DeepGEMM FP8 linear backend and verify that model initialization and DeepGEMM warmup complete without the scale-layout device assertion.

## Test Result

- The targeted pytest test passes.
- Before this change, the reproducer triggers the assertion in `smxx_layout.cuh` that FP32 scale factors must have zero sign and mantissa bits, followed by `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED`.
- After this change, the reproducer completes model initialization and DeepGEMM warmup without that assertion or CUDA launch failure.
- No documentation update is needed because this only corrects existing quantization behavior.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Optimize low-concurrency speculative KDA
author: jiacao-amd
body:
## Purpose

Optimize the active ROCm Kimi-K3 `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd_kernel` for
low-concurrency speculative decoding on MI355X.

The shipped gated configuration uses `BV=32`, `num_warps=4`, and
`num_stages=2`. With Kimi-K3 TP8 (`H=12`, `V=128`) at concurrency 1, this
launches only 48 workgroups for a four-token verification step on a 256-CU
MI355X. This change increases grid parallelism and removes recurrent-loop
runtime work when speculative requests have a uniform query length.

## Changes

- Select narrower V tiles from the number of head-sequences (`H * N`):
  - at most 24: `BV=4`, one warp;
  - 25-96: `BV=8`, one warp;
  - larger multi-sequence grids retain the dynamic path.
- Specialize equal-length speculative batches with a constexpr sequence length.
  C=1 additionally avoids sequence/head division and `cu_seqlens` loads.
- Detect uniform speculative query lengths from existing CPU metadata. Ragged
  batches retain the original dynamic loop. Token-padded graph inputs are
  checked against the packed tensor size before specialization.
- Tune pipeline stages by sequence length: 2 for T=1, 4/8 for T<=3, 6 for
  T<=6, 10 for T<=10, and 12 for longer specialized loops.
- Hoist `exp(A_log)` and `dt_bias` loads out of the token loop.
- Normalize Q/K with `tl.rsqrt` instead of division by `tl.sqrt`.
- Extend the existing KDA and metadata tests with C=1/2/4/8 uniform cases and a
  ragged fallback case.
- Keep static-loop eligibility separate from launch-configuration selection so
  the tuned thresholds and fallback behavior are explicit.

## Why this is not duplicate work

Open-PR searches were run for Kimi-K3, KDA, and `fused_recurrent_kda` work.
This does not duplicate:

- #57753, which tunes the shared `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel`;
- #54103, which proposes routing ROCm Kimi-K3 to ATOM kernels;
- #52988, which adds adaptive variable-length decode plumbing but does not
  specialize this AMD Triton kernel;
- #53525, which optimizes the NVIDIA non-speculative C=1 native/CuTe pipeline;
- #52375 and #56974, which fix launch-grid dimension limits.

If #54103 changes the active ROCm route before this lands, this PR should be
reassessed.

No issue is linked.

## Performance

Fresh validation was run on PR head `ec8d9db6db` with one MI355X (`gfx950`)
using image
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-d05da62e9ccdf8e342b15bf6785d83224cc165af`:

- Python 3.12.13;
- PyTorch `2.12.0+git6bbd260`, HIP `7.2.53211`;
- Triton `3.7.1`;
- Kimi-K3 TP8 dimensions `H=12`, `K=V=128`;
- BF16 inputs and FP32 recurrent state;
- 69 independent KDA layer launches captured in one HIP graph;
- 30 warmups, then 3 rounds x 100 replays; values below are the median
  microseconds per layer.

These are controlled, within-image comparisons of:

- shipped baseline `79468c20ef` (`4df8dc9a10^`);
- current PR `ec8d9db6db`.

The absolute timings are not directly comparable to the earlier ROCm
10.0/Triton 3.8 measurements in this PR because this validation uses the image
versions listed above.

Representative uniform speculative batches:

| C | Query length | Baseline (us) | Current (us) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4 | 16.198 | 5.606 | 2.889x |
| 1 | 7 | 27.003 | 9.108 | 2.965x |
| 2 | 4 | 17.545 | 7.451 | 2.355x |
| 2 | 7 | 28.186 | 10.480 | 2.689x |
| 4 | 4 | 18.934 | 10.180 | 1.860x |
| 4 | 7 | 29.448 | 14.551 | 2.024x |
| 8 | 4 | 22.502 | 13.244 | 1.699x |
| 8 | 7 | 34.468 | 19.086 | 1.806x |
| 8 | 16 | 69.085 | 36.727 | 1.881x |
| 8 | 32 | 130.414 | 73.073 | 1.785x |

Non-specialized and fallback paths were measured separately rather than
assuming the uniform-length result applies to them:

| Case | Baseline (us) | Current (us) | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ragged C=2, lengths `[4,3]` | 17.328 | 7.674 | 2.258x |
| Ragged C=8, alternating lengths 7/6 | 34.171 | 20.531 | 1.664x |
| Graph-padding fallback, C=2/T=4 + 4 padded tokens | 17.547 | 7.976 | 2.200x |
| Uniform C=9/T=7, H*N=108 dynamic policy fallback | 34.712 | 33.275 | 1.043x |
| Regular decode C=8 | 8.965 | 8.744 | 1.025x |

## Test results

All fresh GPU results below use the image and PR head listed in the Performance
section.

- `git diff 4df8dc9a10..HEAD --check`: passed.
- Python compilation of the five changed Python files: passed.
- Focused KDA metadata test: `5 passed, 27 deselected`.
  - Uniform C=2/4/8 is detected.
  - Ragged `[3,2]`, regular decode, and no-scheduled-draft-token cases return
    the dynamic-path sentinel.
- Focused AMD speculative-decode correctness:

  ```bash
  pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py \
      -k "test_kda_spec_decode_correctness and amd" -vv
  ```

  Result: `20 passed, 79 deselected`.
- Complete `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py`: `71 passed, 28 skipped`.
- Candidate-versus-baseline kernel validation: 12 case classes x 5 seeds using
  Kimi-K3 TP8 `H=12`, `K=V=128`.
  - Covers uniform C=1/2/3/4/8 through T=32, `fuse_gate=True/False/None`, lower
    bound enabled/disabled, no `dt_bias`, ragged inputs, graph-padding fallback,
    H*N=108 policy fallback, different accepted-token counts, and regular
    decode.
  - Maximum output absolute difference: `1.220703125e-4`.
  - Maximum recurrent-state absolute difference: `2.384185791015625e-7`.
  - No NaN or Inf was observed.
- HIP graph capture followed by 20 replays was stable for uniform, ragged,
  graph-padding fallback, and H*N=108 dynamic-policy paths.
- Pre-commit on all five functional/test files passed on `2a7b3938b7`, before
  the final launch-selection-only refactor. The validation image does not ship
  pre-commit; the final refactor was checked with `git diff --check`, Python
  compilation, metadata tests, the complete KDA pytest file, the correctness
  sweep, and the performance sweep above.
- All three PR commits contain `Signed-off-by` and AI-assistance trailers.

The image does not include `tblib`; pytest was run with the Kimi-K3 test
directory as `--confcutdir` and importlib import mode to avoid the unrelated
repository-root test dependency. No replacement Python packages were installed.

## Model evaluation

A concurrency-1 GSM8K A/B evaluation was run with the same protocol as
[SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX run 34332168553 attempt 3](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34332168553/attempts/3).
Both sides used image
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0961bbae2894d574be790d219651824eb199318e`
and the same model, server configuration, prompts, seeds, and evaluator:

- `lm-evaluation-harness` revision
  `b315ef3b05176acc9732bb7fdec116abe1ecc476`;
- GSM8K v3, 5-shot, `local-chat-completions`, and `--apply_chat_template`;
- `num_concurrent=1`, `max_tokens=12288`, temperature 0;
- TP8, `max_num_seqs=2`, DSpark K=6 with the TRITON_MLA draft backend and
  block rejection, FP8 KV cache, and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graph capture sizes
  2 through 14.

| Revision | Flexible extract | Strict match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 96.97% (1279/1319) | 96.97% (1279/1319) |
| Current PR `2a7b3938b7` | 97.04% (1280/1319) | 97.12% (1281/1319) |
| Difference | +0.08 percentage points | +0.15 percentage points |

All 1319 requests completed on both sides without request failures. For the
strict metric, 16 examples changed from incorrect to correct and 14 changed
from correct to incorrect, for a net gain of two. For flexible extraction, the
net gain was one. These differences are smaller than the approximately 0.47
percentage-point standard error, so this evaluation shows no model-level
accuracy regression.

The earlier custom raw-completions run used a different prompt and a 256-token
output limit, causing truncations and non-comparable aggregate scores; it is
superseded by the evaluation above.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex was used for code editing, benchmark analysis, testing, and drafting
this description. The human submitter must review every changed line and
validate and understand the change end-to-end before requesting review.

title: [Mypy] Fix mypy typing for Qwen and Qianfan models
author: ashraf-bhuiyan
body:
## Purpose

Address part of [#26533](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26533) by fixing typing in the Qwen/Qianfan model family and removing `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[qQ]"` from the mypy exclusions. All 24 selected model files are now checked.

The changes cover optional configuration and multimodal fields, tensor/container and cache types, generic processing-info types (including ASR inheritance), MoE mixin attributes, and the realtime async-generator protocol.

Five documented, line-specific typing exceptions preserve existing runtime contracts: four incompatible speculative-drafter/MTP overrides and one instance-local override of a class-level LoRA mapping. No file-wide ignores or replacement exclusions were added.

The branch incorporates upstream `main` at `276db94fb2`. The conflict resolution preserves upstream's multimodal processor interfaces, typed dummy options, ASR position fix, tensor video timestamps, and vision caches. The remaining diff against that revision touches 23 files.

## Reproducer

On upstream main, first remove the Q-model exclusion from `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, then run:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files \
  $(git ls-files 'vllm/model_executor/models/[qQ]*.py') --hook-stage manual
```

The initial baseline was 297 errors in the selected Q-model files on the original base, `7c877062ac`. This is a historical result, not an error count for current main.

## Validation

Rechecked after merging upstream `276db94fb2`:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD)

for version in 3.11 3.12 3.13; do
```

Runtime checks used the existing Python 3.12 environment with an editable, precompiled vLLM installation:

```bash
export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-qQ-uv-cache

  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_qwen3_asr_sanitize_prompt.py \
  -q --tb=short --maxfail=3
# 151 passed.

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python --no-managed-python python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py \
```

Total: **205 distinct tests passed**, with no failures. Processor tests used network access for Hugging Face metadata. Warnings included unavailable NVML and upstream TorchScript deprecations. Full model inference, GPU validation, and model-quality evaluations were not run because the NVIDIA driver is unavailable; these results establish CPU unit/processor and registry-import coverage only.

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip top-k slots routed to non-local experts in TritonExp…
author: ShuoleiWang
body:
## Purpose

Under EP with a full routing table on every rank (`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular`, DeepEP high-throughput), `TritonExperts.apply` aligns with `ignore_invalid_experts=False`: slots whose expert lives on another rank still get M-blocks in both `fused_moe_kernel` launches (the `off_experts == -1` branch writes zeros), and `moe_sum` adds the zeros back. At EP degree `ep`, `(ep-1)/ep` of the launched M-blocks do no useful work.

This PR aligns with `ignore_invalid_experts=True` when an `expert_map` is set and no LoRA context is active, and reduces with the existing pad-aware `moe_sum(input, output, topk_ids, expert_map)` (#48385) whenever `expert_map` is set. `fused_marlin_moe` already pairs the two.

Scope: dropped slots leave their workspace rows unwritten, so the skip requires a row-local activation quantization for the second GEMM (unquantized, static `a2_scale`, block-wise, or native dynamic per-token). Dynamic per-tensor activation scales (e.g. non-blocked online `--quantization fp8`) and LoRA keep the dense path. `TritonWNA16Experts` is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py -k expert_map` — new `test_w8a8_block_fp8_fused_moe_expert_map`: one EP rank of a block-FP8 layer (local weight shard, `expert_map` with `-1` entries) against the torch reference, which gains an `expert_map` argument.
- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py -k test_w8a8_block_fp8_fused_moe` (unchanged test, changed reference signature)
- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "test_fused_moe or moe_sum"` (`ep_size=4`: `TritonExperts` with an `expert_map`, BF16, CUDA-graph replay)
- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k Triton` (DeepEP HT/LL + Triton experts, 2 GPUs)
- Fixed-seed main-vs-PR comparison of `TritonExperts.apply` outputs with an `expert_map` (BF16 and block-FP8; E=64/EP4 and E=512/EP8/top-10; M = 1, 4, 33, 256)
- E2E: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, 8×H20, TP8 + EP, `--moe-backend triton`, `vllm bench serve` random 8192→1024, seed 1234, main → PR → main in one session, both arms launched through the same mechanism

## Test Result

Kernel tests (H20, 2 GPUs): new test 8/8 passed on the PR and on main; `test_fused_moe` ep_size=4: 252 passed / 60 skipped (Blackwell-only `use_td` cases) on both; `moe_sum`: 170/170; modular combinations `-k Triton`: 14/14 on both. `test_w8a8_block_fp8_fused_moe`: 158 passed / 20 skipped on both, plus 2 pre-existing failures at M=8192, N=4608, K=7168 (`fused_experts` vs the torch reference, max abs diff 0.0625 > 0.039) that reproduce identically on main with the untouched test file.

Fixed-seed comparison: max |main − PR| = 0.0 in all 20 cases; distance to the torch reference unchanged.

E2E, speculative decoding off (output tok/s = decode step rate), output tok/s / mean TPOT ms / mean TTFT ms:

| concurrency | main (1st) | PR | main (2nd) | PR vs main | main vs main |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 150.0 / 6.26 / 418 | 154.5 / 6.09 / 397 | 150.1 / 6.26 / 415 | +2.9% / −2.7% / −4.7% | +0.06% |
| 4 | 458.5 / 7.63 / 1128 | 479.3 / 7.31 / 1071 | 458.6 / 7.64 / 1120 | +4.5% / −4.3% / −4.7% | +0.02% |
| 128 | 1846 / 61.1 / 8417 | 1949 / 57.9 / 7895 | 1844 / 61.3 / 8248 | +5.7% / −5.4% / −5.2% | −0.10% |

With MTP (3 draft tokens) at concurrency 128: 1424 → 1489 output tok/s (+4.6%), TPOT 80.1 → 76.3 ms, mean acceptance length 2.53 vs 2.55. Greedy outputs on 4 prompts are byte-identical across all arms. All requests generated the full 1024 tokens; no failures.

## Related PRs

- #54083 (draft) wires the same pad-aware `moe_sum` into `TritonExperts` for stale rows when `topk_ids` contain `-1`; this PR contains that change and also drops the slots at alignment time. 


## AI assistance
Claude Code assisted with the trace analysis, implementation, benchmarking and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks myself.

title: [Bugfix][Transformers backend] Fix CUDA graph capture for dynamic-rope models
author: YongfengX
body:
## Overview

Transformers' `@dynamic_rope_update` syncs on `torch.max(position_ids)` in every rotary forward, so dynamic-rope models crash during CUDA graph capture on the Transformers backend. Since #53615, this stops Hunyuan V1 dense models (e.g. Hunyuan-7B-Instruct) from starting on `main` with default settings. Completes #23738.

Closes #57890

## Claims

- When `max_model_len <= max_position_embeddings` the update can never fire, so the decoder's dynamic rotary modules are relabelled as `"default"` after init. `inv_freq` is untouched, so outputs are bit-identical.
- These models are now compiled and run with CUDA graphs: 1.7x throughput on Hunyuan-7B-Instruct.
- Unchanged beyond `max_position_embeddings`, or with a `longrope` layer type, where the sync is real.

## Validation

`tencent/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct`, 1x B200, default `max_model_len` (32768):

| | Startup | GPQA-Diamond | gsm8k | Throughput (req/s) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model card | | 60.1 | | | |
| `main` | ❌ capture crash | | | | |
| `main`, `cudagraph_mode: NONE` | ✅ | | 0.321 | 34.78 | 4451 |
| PR | ✅ | 61.1 | 0.316 | **59.44** | **7608** |

GPQA-Diamond: 198 questions x 2, thinking mode, 1σ ≈ 2.5 pt. gsm8k: 1σ ≈ 1.3 pt, and it is low for this model regardless of implementation (native v0.28.0 also scores 0.314).

```bash
vllm serve tencent/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct --model-impl transformers --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
vllm bench throughput --model tencent/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct --model-impl transformers \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --dataset-name random --input-len 1024 --output-len 256 \
    --num-prompts 1000
# GPQA-Diamond: serve with --reasoning-parser hunyuan_a13b, gpt-oss simple-evals
# GPQAEval(n_repeats=2) with ChatCompletionsSampler(temperature=0.7, max_tokens=28000)

pytest tests/models/transformers/test_dynamic_rope.py  # 5 passed
```

## Details

- The rope type is relabelled on the modules rather than in the config, because model-specific dynamic inits (e.g. Hunyuan's `alpha`) only run when `rope_type == "dynamic"`.
- `can_enable_torch_compile` runs before the modules exist, so it shares the config-level check with the relabelling.

title: [Bugfix][Model][CPU] Fix Mamba2 quantized in_proj weight and scale loading for TP >1
author: Akashcodes732
body:
## Purpose
Fix `RuntimeError: start (...) + length (...) exceeds dimension size (...)` when serving quantized Mamba-2 models (e.g. `granite-4.0-h-tiny-quantized.w8a8`) with TP > 1.

- **Cause**: In `MambaMixer2`, `self.in_proj` groups B and C are replicated when `ngroups < tp_size`. While `weight` used `mamba_loader`, quantized parameters (`weight_scale`, `input_scale`) used default linear slicing, causing out-of-bounds indexing on Rank 1+.
- **Fix**: Apply `mamba_loader` to all parameters of `self.in_proj` and align sliced scale dimensions with `target_slice`.



## Test Plan
```bash
# Serve model with TP=2
vllm serve fedora-copr/granite-4.0-h-tiny-quantized.w8a8 --tensor-parallel-size 2

# Test completion
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "fedora-copr/granite-4.0-h-tiny-quantized.w8a8", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}]}'


## Test Result
- **Before**: Crashed on Rank 1 at startup: `RuntimeError: start (3352) + length (3352) exceeds dimension size (6448)`
- **After**: Server starts cleanly on TP=2 and successfully responds with `"2 + 2 = 4"`.
```

title: [CI] Emit a kernel symbol map from the csrc build (opt-in, for test selection)
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Part of the CI test-selection work in vllm-project/ci-infra (#555, #610, #611). The nightly CI runs now record which GPU kernels every step launches. To turn that into a decision ("this PR changed `csrc/foo.cu`, which steps launched a kernel from it?") CI also needs to know **which source file produced each kernel symbol**. That has to come from the real build, because the mangled names depend on template instantiations, the arch list and what CMake actually compiled.

This PR adds `tools/ci/kernel_symbol_map.py`, run inside the `csrc-build` Dockerfile stage right after the compile layers. Per compiled object it records the source file, the CMake target, the headers `ninja -t deps` says it read, and the kernel entry symbols `cuobjdump -symbols` finds in the fatbin. Output is one gzipped JSON, ~3.4 MB. A scratch stage `kernel-symbol-map` exposes the file and `image_build.sh` bakes that target with a local output and uploads it as a build artifact.

**Off by default.** Everything is gated on the build arg / env `VLLM_KERNEL_SYMBOL_MAP=1`, which only the nightly and daily full-run schedules will set. A normal build gains one `COPY` and one `RUN` that prints "Skipping", both after the compile layers so their cache is untouched. The script never fails the build; an empty map with a `reason` is the failure signal downstream.

Also regenerates `docs/assets/contributing/dockerfile-stages-dependency.png` for the new stage (pre-commit hook).

## Test Plan

Ran the image build on a fork branch with the arg set, image-build step only, three times while iterating (Buildkite `vllm/ci` builds 90006, 90008, 90011), then joined the resulting map with kernel recordings from real CI steps.

## Test Result

- Map produced in 62 s inside the (cached) `csrc-build` layer: 567 objects, 543 device objects, 10,447 kernel entry symbols, 0 `cuobjdump` errors, every object attributed to its CMake target (`_vllm_fa3_C` 194, `_C_stable_libtorch` 113, `_deepselect_C` 79, `_vllm_fa2_C` 79, `_flashmla_C` 56, ...). 89 of the 98 `.cu` files under `csrc/` appear (the rest are ROCm-only or not in the CUDA 13 arch list); 111 of 163 headers appear as dependencies.
- Probe in the build log: `fusedQKNormRopeKernel -> csrc/libtorch_stable/fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu`.
- Joined with the first nightly's recordings (187 CUDA steps): a change to `fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu` (the file behind #55755, which selects 225 of 226 steps today) selects 6 steps and drops 176; `topk.cu` selects the 12 DeepSeek/Qwen4/B200 attention steps; `cuda_compat.h` selects 169, as a header included everywhere should.
- With the arg unset (every other build): the `RUN` prints "Skipping kernel symbol map" and nothing else changes.

title: [ROCm][Compile] Support BF16 AsyncTP fusion
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Import `AsyncTPPass` on ROCm and match BF16 opaque GEMM with all-gather or reduce-scatter, preserving weight orientation and existing CUDA patterns.
- Add eight two-GPU numerical cases covering fixed/dynamic shapes, non-square GEMMs, rank-dependent inputs, rewrite counts, and output lifetime.
- Add four bounded Llama configuration cases and a pinned trained Qwen comparison requiring positive rewrites on both workers.
- Add one MI355 native mirror and matching legacy job; keep the eight new numerical cases outside the directory already scheduled by #50519/#56679.
- Force fresh Inductor compilation in the trained test so a warm cache cannot bypass its rewrite witness; support is limited to BF16 with explicit sequence-parallel thresholds.

MI355 validation reached working symmetric-memory primitives but found that ROCm never imported `AsyncTPPass`. The existing GEMM patterns also missed the opaque `rocm_unquantized_gemm` operations emitted by ROCm linear layers. This patch implements that BF16 path with explicit sequence-parallel thresholds and real numerical and serving checks.

title: [ROCm][Compile] Fuse AITER static FP8 attention output
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Match the actual static AITER per-tensor quantization operator after attention and preserve its scale output when replacing it with fused attention output quantization.
- Add BF16/FP16 regressions using non-unit scale `0.125`, checking numerical agreement, an unchanged scale, and removal of exactly the output quantizer while query quantization remains.
- Add a pinned trained FP8 Llama comparison requiring output-quantization fusion in all 32 layers, with fresh Inductor compilation for a reliable rewrite witness.
- Add one MI355 Fusion-and-Compile native mirror and matching legacy job for three existing fusion unit files plus the trained test, preserving existing MLA and distributed-suite ownership.
- Keep the independent core free of borrowed #50519 source; defer the seven extra TP2 FP8 sweep selections until that prerequisite merges.

The MI355 TP2 sweep exposed a missed attention-output fusion when static quantization used AITER's per-tensor operator. The existing matcher left that operator in the graph even though the backend supported a fused output scale. This patch extends the existing static-FP8 contract while retaining the scale and numerical assertions that guard the replacement.

title: [Perf][Qwen3.8] Reduce PLE metadata construction overhead
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

PLE metadata construction still synchronizes in mixed speculative batches and builds temporary tensors that its consumers do not need. This reduces per-step builder work while preserving request ordering, accepted-token routing, and persistent CUDA graph buffers.

- Supply `repeat_interleave` with the output size from CPU query offsets, excluding token padding, and use `index_fill_` for request-group labels to avoid scalar-assignment synchronization.
- In pure speculative batches, use request-prefix views instead of uploading indices and gathering state/acceptance tensors. Skip the unused device query-length calculation and identity token maps; request padding remains trailing.
- Let PLE skip generic causal-conv prefill metadata that neither PLE implementation consumes. Other Mamba builders retain the existing default.
- Reuse the builder's prefill query offsets in NVIDIA and AMD PLE consumers.

Related to #55922. This follows the already-merged #55054, which made request-index uploads asynchronous; the changes here remove additional work and mixed-batch synchronization. I checked the tracking issue and its comments, open PRs referencing it, and searches for `PLE metadata`, `short_conv_attn`, and `PleShortConvAttentionMetadataBuilder`. No open PR implements this change. The related CPU backend, quantization, QSA, and standalone PLE state-kernel PRs address different paths.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py \
  vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/ple_layer.py \
  vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ple_layer.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mamba_attn.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/short_conv_attn.py

git diff --check
```

New builder coverage exercises CPU/CUDA, eager/full-graph buffer preparation, request and token padding, interleaved speculative/non-speculative requests, accepted-token routing, and prefill offsets. CUDA synchronization debug mode is enabled during CUDA builder calls.

Before marking ready: complete human line-by-line review and required test review. The GB200 end-to-end smoke/performance results are below; AMD runtime validation and broader model evaluation remain outstanding.

## Test Result

- GPU validation through Vigil/Slurm on GB200: **69 passed** across the two test files.
- Pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Relevant output tensors matched the original builder in the synthetic A/B cases below.

### Metadata builder microbenchmark

Baseline: `986e217158a9ed54eca8307c6bb9abac7c5b2278`. Same GB200 node and Python/PyTorch environment; original builder loaded alongside the patched builder. Three speculative tokens, full-graph buffer preparation, one CPU thread, 30 warmup builds per variant, then seven alternating rounds of 200 builds each. CUDA synchronization brackets each timed round; the computed-token cache is reset before each build. Values are median amortized host+device wall time per build.

| Batch | Base (us) | Patched (us) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pure MTP, 1 request + padding | 395.10 | 244.25 | 38.18% |
| Pure MTP, 8 requests + padding | 390.80 | 244.33 | 37.48% |
| Pure MTP, 32 requests | 364.97 | 217.75 | 40.34% |
| Mixed spec/decode/1K prefill | 994.08 | 678.51 | 31.75% |
| Non-spec decode + 1K prefill | 414.81 | 215.74 | 47.99% |

These are metadata-builder measurements, not end-to-end throughput gains.

### End-to-end validation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 on one exclusive 4-GPU GB200 node via Vigil/Slurm: TP4, MTP3, prefix caching enabled, default serving capacities/backends/CUDA graph behavior. Baseline main `f92b78f6ef9c9b28f60668da77af5b65645b1a45`; patch `df5e6d382bb4cf80f4dc46073d546b44816c0956`. Both use the same checkout and binaries, with the four changed implementation modules imported from audited immutable source snapshots. FlashInfer Python/cubin both `0.6.18.post1`; no version-check bypass.

Four independent server starts in ABBA order (two per variant), three benchmark rounds per concurrency per start. Rust `vllm-bench`, exact 1024 input token IDs / 128 output tokens, temperature 0, ignore_eos, 8 warmup requests per invocation; 32 measured requests at C1 and 128 at C8. Matching seeds across starts (`4201/4301/4401` for C1, `4208/4308/4408` for C8). The installed client was separately checked to generate identical request bodies across repeated same-seed invocations.

**All 1,920 measured requests succeeded**, with exact input/output lengths. No prefix-cache hits during these performance runs. Throughput is total generated tokens divided by summed measured durations; TPOT excludes TTFT.

| Concurrency | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Output tokens/s | 244.326 | 240.623 | -1.52% |
| 1 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 3.635 | 3.710 | +2.07% |
| 1 | Mean TTFT (ms) | 62.158 | 60.625 | -2.47% |
| 8 | Output tokens/s | 489.977 | 514.283 | +4.96% |
| 8 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 14.040 | 13.380 | -4.70% |
| 8 | Mean TTFT (ms) | 287.536 | 274.665 | -4.48% |

Independent-start throughput (tokens/s):

| Start | C1 | C8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| A1 | 243.71 | 486.03 |
| B1 | 238.98 | 513.06 |
| B2 | 242.29 | 515.51 |
| A2 | 244.94 | 493.99 |

MTP acceptance lengths (baseline → patch): C1: 2.4496 → 2.3898, C8: 2.4693 → 2.4572.

Interpretation: the measured C8 workload improves across both paired starts; C1 does not demonstrate a reliable throughput gain. There are only two independent starts per variant, and output text/MTP acceptance varies even between same-version restarts. These are workload-specific observations, not a statistical confidence claim or a general serving-speedup guarantee.

GSM8K five-shot, 64 examples, thinking disabled, temperature 0, concurrency 4, max_tokens 4096: **baseline 63/64 and patch 63/64 (98.44%)**, zero request errors. All 64 per-question scores match, including the same incorrect example. Evaluations ran after performance measurements. This is an accuracy smoke test, not a full model evaluation.

Engine command used by Vigil:

```bash
vllm serve MODEL --served-model-name ple-metadata --port 8188 -tp 4 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

```bash

  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \

  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 4201 \
  --save-result --save-detailed --result-dir RESULTS --result-filename r1-c1.json \

```

Raw per-request data, server counters, configurations, source/binary hashes, and all 24 round results are retained in the local `ple_metadata_e2e_20260922` artifact directory.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Dispatch the QuantFP8 CUDA fallback on the class
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

Three tests in `tests/kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py` fail in the
`(MI355) Core Operation Kernels` job:

```
FAILED test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-False] - IndexError: tuple index out of range
FAILED test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-True] - IndexError: tuple index out of range
FAILED test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-64-False] - IndexError: tuple index out of range
```

Failing run:
https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90376/list?jid=01a0c7db-41fd-4aeb-9b8d-8509eee8af45&tab=output

`QuantFP8.forward_hip` falls back to the CUDA implementation through
`self.forward_cuda(...)`. `_DecodeConcatQuantFP8` overrides `forward_cuda` with
a different signature, taking the two halves of the decode query, so the
virtual call re-enters the subclass with every argument shifted by one and
`decode_q_pe` ends up holding the 0-d scale tensor.

The path is not new, only newly tested: AITER returns before the fallback is
reached, and #57458 added the first test that exercises it with AITER off.
Fixed by dispatching the fallback on the class instead of on `self`, which is
what the existing comment already intends.

## Test Plan

`pytest tests/kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py` on MI355X (gfx950), both with AITER
off, as the job runs it, and with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.

## Test Result

Before: 3 failed, 35 passed. After: 38 passed. With AITER enabled the file
passes either way, so the fast path is unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo: keep fused fp8 qkv_proj pairing state across weight-loading calls
author: vllmellm
body:
## Purpose
`XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` (and V2.5) produce degenerate output when using `--load-format fastsafetensors` or `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` when testing on Mi355x.  This issue should be platform-agnostic. 

## Root cause

MiMo's fused fp8 `qkv_proj` arrives as two checkpoint tensors (`weight` and `weight_scale_inv`) that must be sharded together, so `MiMoV2Model.load_weights` paired them in a dict and flushed only when both members arrived in the *same* call.

`AutoWeightsLoader._groupby_prefix` (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:260-274`) groups the stream with `itertools.groupby` on the first name component and calls a child's `load_weights` **once per contiguous run of `model.*`**. Any pair that straddles a group boundary therefore never flushes and both parameters are left uninitialised — zeros/NaN for the fp8 weight and `-inf` for its scale:

Instrumented load (`mimo_v2.py`), TP=2:

| loader | `layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight` | `…weight_scale_inv` |
|---|---|---|
| default | correct | correct |
| `--load-format fastsafetensors` | `sum=0` | `sum=-inf` |
| `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` | `sum=0`/`NaN` | `sum=-inf` |

`eager` fragments heavily because `safetensors.torch.load` returns a Rust `HashMap` (not file order). Nothing errored because weights tracking is disabled for quantized models (`default_loader.py:435-438`), hence gibberish tokens instead of a load failure.

## Fix

MiMo's fused fp8 `qkv_proj` arrives as two separate tensors — the weight and its scale — which have to be sharded together, so the loader holds the first one until the second shows up. That holding area was a local variable, and a local variable only lives for one call of `load_weights`; when the loader runs more than once (fastsafetensors, eager), a pair can be split across two calls, both tensors are dropped, and the attention projections are left empty.

Keep the holding area on the model instead (`mimo_v2.py`, and the same spot in `mimo_v2_mtp.py`), so a pair still completes no matter which call each half arrives in. Nothing in the loader itself is changed, so no other model is affected.

## Test Plan
Start serving with this, change model id to `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` and add `--load-format fastsafetensors` or `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` when testing the different case. 
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len auto \
```

title: [Bugfix] Narrow AuxOutput KV restrictions to known PD connectors
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Replace the blanket AuxOutput KV-connector rejection introduced by #45635 with a targeted exclusion of `NixlConnector`, `NixlPullConnector`, `NixlPushConnector`, `MoRIIOConnector`, and `MooncakeConnector`.

Reuse `KVTransferConfig.has_connector()` to check direct configurations and MultiConnector children. Do not infer PD versus offload from `kv_role`: `kv_both` can also be used for PD. MooncakeStoreConnector, OffloadingConnector, LMCacheConnectorV1, LMCacheMPConnector, and SimpleCPUOffloadConnector are not rejected by this AuxOutput check. Their own configuration validation remains unchanged.

The existing guard prevents even starting routed-expert return with `MooncakeStoreConnector` offload. This patch changes only that policy and its regression tests; it does not change scheduling, capture, storage, or the full-R3 output contract.

## Related work / scope

Checked #57025 and #57966. Those changes introduce prefix omission and external-lookup bypass with a caller-owned history contract. This is a separate, minimal configuration-policy proposal with no omission flag or session protocol. The distinction is recorded in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56402#issuecomment-5776573799. #57968 separately adds a Mooncake backend for auxiliary outputs.

**Joint KV/R3 recovery validation remains outstanding.** This is a targeted exclusion, not universal detection of every PD deployment or custom connector. External KV hits can skip forward computation, so historical R3 must still be available in the auxiliary store. This patch does not fix missing/evicted R3, coordinate the two stores' retention, or certify every connector not listed above. No new GPU/model evaluation or offload-recovery result is claimed. These remain merge gates, not silently handled fallbacks.

title: [Bugfix]Fix FlashInfer warmup crash: autotune(tuning_buckets=...) must round M up, not down (Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic with spec-decode)
author: ebfio
body:
## Fix FlashInfer warmup crash: `autotune(tuning_buckets=...)` must map runtime M **up**, not down

Fixes the engine crash-loop at startup for SM100/SM103 block-scaled cute-dsl linear kernels (`mm_mxfp8` / `mm_fp4`) when speculative decoding is enabled.

### The crash

`kernel_warmup` runs dummy forwards inside `fi_utils.autotune(tuning_buckets=tuning_buckets)`. With spec-decode, the DSpark draft model forward runs at M = `max_num_seqs × k` = e.g. 8 × 3 = **24** — not a bucket value. Boot dies:

```
ValueError: Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 16), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
```

at `flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py:5327` (`CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner.forward`), reached from the draft model's `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM.

Reproduced on DGX Station GB300 (SM103) with vLLM nightly + DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + dspark k=3; standalone FlashInfer-only repro at https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5450.

### Root cause

`mm_mxfp8`'s own tuning config maps runtime M to buckets with `map_to_hybrid_bucket_uncapped`, which rounds **up**, and the cute-dsl split-K MMA tile is likewise chosen by rounding M up (`mma_tiler_mn_for_m`: 8/16/32). A tactic tuned at bucket b is therefore valid for every M ≤ b — tune space and apply space agree.

But inside `autotune(tuning_buckets=...)` the autotuner **replaces the op's mapper** with `make_bucket_mapper(buckets, round_map=round_up)` and `round_up` **defaults to False** (floor). So the warmup dummy run at M=24 looks up the **bucket-16** tactic — tile (128,16), split_k=4 — and `forward()` rejects it because `mma_tiler_mn_for_m(24)` is (128,32).

Outside the context (serving, CUDA-graph capture) the op's own round-up mapper is restored, so **only the warmup pass ever crashes**: the engine can never boot, while the identical weights, tactics, and cache would serve fine.

Standalone repro (no vLLM, one process, same cache — all three regimes):

```
inside autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=False [default]):
  M=24 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 16), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
  M=12 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128,  8), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
  M=40 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 32), (1, 1), True, False,  2)
outside any autotune context (op mapper, rounds up):
  M=24 OK / M=12 OK / M=40 OK
inside autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=True):
  M=24 OK / M=12 OK / M=40 OK
```

### The fix

One line: `round_up=True` on the warmup `autotune()` call, making tune-context mapping equal serving-time mapping. Every cached tactic at bucket b is then applied only to M ≤ b — exactly the envelope both the split-K validator and the small swap-AB base tactics guarantee.

Profiling is per bucket, so tactic choices and the cache file are unchanged; only the dummy run's execution path changes. Verified live on GB300: the crash-looping boot (identical config) boots clean with this change and serves with full CUDA graphs; warmup passes on the pre-existing cache.

### Broader hazard (why this should land even before any FlashInfer-side change)

The base (non-split-K) candidate tactics include swap-AB tiles (128, 8/16/32) whose persistent-kernel `can_implement` requires `kernel_n ≤ tile_n` (kernel_n = token count in swap-AB) — and those tactics get **no apply-time check**. Under floor mapping, a bucket-16 winner applied at M=24 runs silently outside its envelope. The same tactic generator serves `mm_fp4`, so NVFP4 + spec-decode is exposed too. The split-K `ValueError` is just the one place that notices. Filed upstream with full analysis: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5450

### Notes for reviewers

- The change is one argument on one line (plus the explanatory comment); the diff is intentionally minimal.
- If maintainers prefer the fix inside FlashInfer (honor the op's mapping direction under bucket override, or size small tiles against `DynamicDim.max`), this line remains a correct, self-contained fix on the vLLM side and can be revisited later.
