title: [KV Offload] Expose OffloadingManager.lock()/unlock() and service the tiering control plane off the scheduler thread
author: liranschour
body:
## Purpose

Two things, in priority order.

**1. Expose exclusive access to an `OffloadingManager` as a public API.** `lock()` / `unlock()`, plus a `locked()` helper, guard a manager's whole state subtree: the manager, the tiers it composes, and any front-end state those tiers own. Manager methods never acquire it themselves, so a caller holds it across as many operations as its own invariants need. That property is the point — several manager operations only make sense in sequence. `prepare_load()` documents that its keys are offloaded, a fact `lookup()` established one hook earlier, so a caller has to be able to span both. Internal per-method locking cannot offer that.

**2. Use it for the first case that needs it** (#55179). The `p2p` secondary tier answers a remote peer, which the engine does not drive, so its control plane only advanced from `on_schedule_end`. A peer's lookup or fetch therefore waited for a model-step boundary — seconds on a saturated rank, gating a transfer of well under one. Tiers now opt in with `needs_control_plane_thread`, and `TieringOffloadingManager` runs one thread that polls them and lets them serve between steps.

## Not a duplicate of the open PRs on #55179

This overlaps open work and I want that on the record rather than buried.

| PR | Author | Driver | Locking |
|---|---|---|---|
| **this** | me | thread owned by `TieringOffloadingManager` | **public `lock()`/`unlock()` on `OffloadingManager`, held by callers** |
| #58113 | me | same thread, same sweep | private `_enter_step`/`_exit_step`/`_observation_lock` + `*_unlocked` variants |
| #57165 | @nilig | `EngineCore` poller thread | new `KVConnectorBase_V1.poll_pending_work` |
| #55962 | @Etelis | `EngineCore` + connector base API + executor changes | new base-API hook |
| #57139 | me | — | the separate async peer-registration half, not this |

**This supersedes my own #58113, which I will close.** The difference is not cosmetic:

- **#58113 does not expose an API.** It takes the lock inside the manager's public methods, which forces a `*_unlocked` variant of every method `_SecondaryTierFacingParent` can re-enter (`lookup`, `on_new_request`, `create_store_job`, `on_request_finished`, `reset_cache`) because the parent handle's caller already holds it. That duplication is most of its `+393` lines in `manager.py`, and it is precisely what prevents an outside caller from saying "hold this across several operations." Moving the lock to the caller removes every one of those variants.
- **#58113 releases at `on_schedule_end`, which is not the end of the step.** `build_connector_meta` called `on_schedule_end` ~40 lines early, before `_build_store_jobs` → `prepare_store` (which evicts) and before `on_request_finished`. So its `prepare_store` re-acquired via `_enter_step()` and nothing released it: on every step that builds store jobs — the common case under load — the lock was held across `future.result()`, starving the control thread in exactly the window the change exists to exploit. That plausibly explains #58113's own "parity-within-noise" result, which was measured through the bug, and that conclusion should be re-tested.

Relative to #57165 / #55962: same goal, but no new `KVConnectorBase_V1` hook and no `EngineCore` or executor changes. In #55179 @nilig asked for a read on "a thread touching the connector from inside `EngineCore`, even phase-exclusive, versus a control thread owned by the tier" — this is a working implementation of the second option, offered as input to that question. If maintainers prefer either existing PR, close this one.

## Changes

Commit 1, **`on_schedule_end` runs last** — independent of all locking, reviewable on its own. Its docstring already claimed "called once at the end of each scheduler step"; it was called ~40 lines early. Moving it makes the contract true and gives callers a sound release point. Two ordering consequences, both handled: `prepare_store`'s poll becomes unconditional (the per-step gate was previously reset mid-`build_connector_meta`, which is where its fresh completion data came from — without this, eviction decisions would run on data up to a step stale), and `_flush_pending_cascades` now re-parks keys this step parked, which is safe because `_maybe_finalize_request` holds off while `pending_cascade_keys` is non-empty.

Commit 2, **the API and its consumer**.

`OffloadingConnectorScheduler` holds one region per engine step, opened by the first manager-touching hook and closed at the end of `build_connector_meta`, so the manager is free while the engine runs the model. Hooks outside `schedule()` take a short region.

Two placements are load-bearing and easy to get wrong:

- **`has_pending_push_work` must use the short region.** `EngineCore.step()` returns early at `core.py:597` when `has_requests()` is false, so a step-scoped acquire there would never reach the release and would hold the manager for good — the state an idle engine settles into. It does still need the lock: `has_pending_work()` iterates `_req_state` while the control thread may insert or delete via `parent.on_new_request` / `on_request_finished`.
- **`take_events` drains inside the region.** `manager.take_events()` is a generator whose backing list is cleared once exhausted, so iterating it lazily both pinned the manager for the consumer's duration and discarded events a concurrent `complete_write` appended, unpublished. It stays a generator so the caller's truthiness check at `sched/scheduler.py` is unchanged.

The thread yields unconditionally *after* `unlock()`, which is what bounds the scheduler's wait to one round — Python locks are not fair, so a release-then-reacquire loop could starve it. A failed round is logged, not fatal, and `on_schedule_end` still serves every tier, so the fallback is per-step servicing. `_process_finished_jobs` takes a tier filter so a round does not drag tiers that expect the scheduler thread. `shutdown()` stops and joins the thread before any tier teardown, since closing a transport under a live round can end the process rather than raise.

Config: `control_plane_interval_s` in `kv_connector_extra_config`, default 1 ms, `0` disables the thread and restores per-step servicing.

Docstrings that claimed single-threaded tier access are corrected, including the eviction-race argument in `_pin_and_register_hits` — which still holds, now because `serve_external_requests` runs inside one hold of the lock. `async_lookup.py`'s "owned exclusively by the scheduler thread" claim was outright false once `parent.lookup` can fan out to `fs.lookup` from the control thread.

## Test results

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
  901 passed, 12 skipped in 295s      (baseline on this tree: 889 passed, 12 skipped)

pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ -q
  217 passed in 66s                   (subset of the above; re-run on its own)

pre-commit: all hooks pass, including ruff, ruff-format, mypy, and check-test-tethering.
```

Note for reviewers: a whole-directory run of `tests/v1/kv_offload/` produces a large number of CUDA IMA errors that are **pre-existing and unrelated** (`tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/` poisons the rest of the session). Run the subdirectories separately.

12 new tests. The two that matter most were both verified to fail without the change, not just to pass with it:

- `test_on_schedule_end_is_the_last_manager_call_of_a_step` — without the reorder it observes `['on_schedule_end', 'prepare_store']`. This is the check #58113's suite lacks, because its `_step()` helper drives `on_schedule_end` with no following `prepare_store`.
- `test_control_thread_and_scheduler_never_overlap` — with `lock()`/`unlock()` stubbed to no-ops it detects 86 overlaps. It also asserts both threads made progress, so neither a thread that never runs nor one that starves the scheduler passes it.

I wrote and then **deleted** a third test ("no eviction between a served lookup and its pin") after finding it still passed with the lock neutered: LRU keeps evicting the fresh keys rather than the constantly-looked-up hit keys, so it could never fail. The overlap test is the real guard for that property, and a test that cannot fail is worse than no test.

## Model evaluation — the 4-case matrix from #55179

Run on two H200 pods, Llama-3.2-1B, `--enforce-eager`, `--block-size 16`, 96 GiB CPU
primary tier, `secondary_tiers: [{"type": "p2p"}]`, `max-model-len 32768`.

**Topology.** Source = the pod holding the KV in its CPU offload tier. Consumer = the
other pod, which probes the source over P2P (`remote_kv_source`) and fetches. Every
measured fetch uses a freshly generated ~27k-token prompt that is populated on the source
first, so nothing hits a GPU prefix cache and the fetch is real work: each one moved
**~1720 chunks** (`kv_offload_tiering_chunk_hits` delta), i.e. the full prefix.

**Busy** = source saturated with 8 concurrent ~27k-token prefills. That took its
request latency from **0.018 s idle to 1.40 s**, so the control plane really is gated
behind ~1.4 s of model work — the same regime as the issue's report.

**Cold** = no P2P session yet. A session lives as long as the engine, so only the first
fetch after a restart is genuinely cold; both pods were restarted between every phase and
the cold fetch measured first.

**Signal** = the consumer's `vllm:kv_offload_lookup_async_delay_seconds` delta for the
measured request (one observation per fetch). Warm figures are the mean of 3 reps.

| case | A: baseline (`7b077f36a8`) | B: #58113 | C: this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| idle, cold | 0.177 s | — | **0.133 s** |
| idle, warm | 0.0455 s | — | **0.0457 s** |
| busy, cold | 0.440 s | 0.289 s | **0.155 s** |
| busy, warm | 0.220 s | 0.129 s | **0.0534 s** |

**The per-step gating penalty, which is what this PR removes:**

| arm | idle-warm | busy-warm | penalty |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: baseline | 0.0455 s | 0.2196 s | **4.83x** |
| C: this PR | 0.0457 s | 0.0534 s | **1.17x** |

Saturating the source costs baseline 4.8x on the consumer's lookup delay. With the control
thread it costs 1.17x — the stall is essentially gone, and a busy source now behaves like
an idle one.

Supporting numbers on busy-warm: per-chunk tiering delay
(`kv_offload_tiering_lookup_async_delay_seconds`) 0.100 s → 0.0174 s (5.8x), and end-to-end
TTFT for the fetch 0.310 s → 0.144 s (2.2x). Idle is parity within noise in every metric,
as expected — there is no model step to hide behind.

Per-rep spread, busy-warm: baseline `0.1929 / 0.2532 / 0.2127`, this PR
`0.0388 / 0.0427 / 0.0786`. The distributions do not overlap — the worst rep here is still
better than the best baseline rep.

**No source-side slowdown.** The concern that holding the manager lock slows the scheduler
does not show up: on the busy source, request latency was 1.4174 s (baseline) vs 1.4039 s
(this PR), and the populate-request mean 1.7056 s vs 1.7100 s. The background load
generator completed 158 vs 153 requests over comparable windows, a ~3% difference that is
within single-run noise and not corroborated by either latency measure. A dedicated
`vllm bench serve` throughput comparison is still worth running before merge; I did not
run one.

### On #58113

Arm B is #58113 at `b8ea135c71`, measured on the same pods in the same session. It lands
**between** baseline and this PR: busy-warm 0.129 s vs baseline 0.220 s vs 0.0534 s here.

That is what the release-point bug predicts. #58113's thread is not dead — on steps that
build no store jobs the lock is released normally, so it recovers some of the win (1.7x
over baseline). But on any step that does build store jobs, `prepare_store` re-acquires
after `on_schedule_end` released and nothing releases it again, so the lock is held across
`future.result()` and the thread is shut out for exactly that step. Under load most steps
build store jobs, which is why it recovers only about a third of what is available (4.1x
over baseline here, 2.4x over #58113).

I am reporting this as *consistent with* the bug rather than as direct proof of the
mechanism; the mechanism itself is demonstrated by the unit test, which observes the call
order `['on_schedule_end', 'prepare_store']` without the reorder in commit 1.

### Caveat on absolute magnitudes

These numbers are much smaller than the issue's 13.6 s, and deliberately so: this is
Llama-3.2-1B on a single H200 per side, not GLM-5.2-FP8 on DP8. What reproduces here is the
**mechanism and its scaling** — the consumer's lookup delay is proportional to the source's
step time under baseline, and roughly independent of it with the control thread. The issue's
13.6 s came from a far slower source; the ratio, not the absolute, is what transfers.

Raw per-rep JSON for all six runs is available on request.

## NIXL thread-safety: checked, and it holds

Checked against the **NIXL 1.4.1** sources (`ai-dynamo/nixl` at tag `v1.4.1`), which is the
deployed version. **This corrects an earlier version of this description**, which said
`NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_RW` does not exist and that the config offers no way to request a sync
mode. Both statements were true of 0.6.0, which is what I had installed; neither is true of
1.4.1.

**Serialized use from a second thread is supported.** `makeMtType`
(`src/plugins/ucx/ucx_utils.cpp:383-392`) returns only `WORKER` or `SINGLE`, never
`CONTEXT` -- and `mt_mode_t::CONTEXT` is the only value that maps to
`UCS_THREAD_MODE_SINGLE` (`ucx_utils.cpp:476-492`), the one UCX mode with creator-thread
affinity. Grepping confirms `CONTEXT` never appears as a produced value, only in switch
arms. So the weakest mode NIXL ever requests is `UCS_THREAD_MODE_SERIALIZED`, which UCX
documents as *"Multiple threads can access, but only one at a time"* -- precisely this
design. And because `enable_prog_thread` defaults on for this transport, it actually gets
`UCS_THREAD_MODE_MULTI`, with a hard library-support check that throws if unavailable.

**The manager lock is load-bearing, not redundant.** With `syncMode = NONE` -- which is what
this transport gets, since it sets neither `enable_listen` nor `sync_mode` -- NIXL's internal
agent lock compiles to no-ops (`src/core/sync.h:36-39`), leaving ~23 agent entry points
unguarded over shared, non-atomic containers. The external mutex is therefore the only
protection, and it must cover every entry point plus the lifetime of handles passed between
calls. It does.

Two caveats worth recording:

- NIXL binds a shared UCX worker per calling thread (`tlsSharedWorkerMap`,
  `ucx_backend.cpp:821-825`). That is harmless only while there is exactly one shared
  worker, which holds for this configuration (`num_workers` unset ⇒ `numSharedWorkers_ == 1`,
  so every thread maps to worker 0) but would not if a `num_workers` UCX backend param were
  ever set. The chosen worker also travels on the request handle rather than being
  re-derived per call, so a transfer prepped on one thread and polled on another still uses
  the same worker.
- 1.4.1 *does* accept an explicit `sync_mode` (including `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_RW`, value 2),
  which would make NIXL's own locking real as belt-and-braces, and is what every upstream
  multi-threaded test uses. I have not added it, because the parameter does not exist on
  0.6.0 and passing it unconditionally would break older environments; it needs the same
  kind of version gate `capture_telemetry` already needs. Worth a follow-up.

Honest limit: `~/nixl` is a 1.4.1 source checkout, not a build, and only 0.6.0 is installed
locally, so every 1.4.1 claim above is static source reading rather than runtime
introspection. A runtime confirmation (log the thread mode `ucp_worker_query` actually
grants, or run the two-thread pattern under TSan) would close the remaining gap. The
end-to-end matrix above ran on the deployed 1.4.1 across ~14k P2P chunk fetches with no
transfer failures, which is evidence but not a substitute.

pyzmq is fine under strict serialization: libzmq permits migrating a socket between threads
given a full memory barrier, which lock acquire/release provides, and nothing is bound
thread-locally at socket creation. The one hazard is `zmq_ctx_destroy` racing a socket call,
which the shutdown ordering handles.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude Code): the code-path analysis, the implementation, and the tests. I am reviewing every changed line. The two items that were blocking this leaving draft are now done: the 4-case matrix has been run on H200 hardware (results above) and the NIXL question has been checked against 1.4.1. What remains before undraft is a dedicated throughput comparison and a human pass over the diff.

title: [Perf][Attention] Avoid CPU-GPU sync in DCP sequence lengths
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

Passing an integer `dcp_rank` to `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` creates a CUDA scalar tensor, introducing a synchronous host-to-device copy during DCP attention metadata construction. Keep the rank as a Python scalar so PyTorch uses it directly in the existing tensor arithmetic.

Related work: #54790 includes the same scalar fix alongside fused draft metadata updates for sparse MLA. This PR intentionally extracts the shared helper fix into a separate, minimal change so it can be reviewed and landed independently of that larger feature. The implementation overlap is acknowledged.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used to implement and validate this change and prepare the PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_cp_utils.py \
  -k 'get_dcp_local_seq_lens or skip_gate' -q
```

<details>
<summary>Standalone CUDA synchronization check</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import torch
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import get_dcp_local_seq_lens

seq_lens = torch.arange(33, dtype=torch.int32, device='cuda')
expected = torch.tensor(
    [sum((pos // 2) % 4 == 2 for pos in range(length)) for length in range(33)],
    dtype=torch.int32,
)
previous_mode = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
try:
    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode('error')
    actual = get_dcp_local_seq_lens(seq_lens, 4, 2, 2)
finally:
    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(previous_mode)
torch.testing.assert_close(actual.cpu(), expected)
print('PASS: no synchronizing CUDA operation; values match the reference.')
print('GPU:', torch.cuda.get_device_name())
print('PyTorch:', torch.__version__)
PY
```

</details>



</details>

## Test Result

- Existing focused tests: **18 passed**.
- CUDA synchronization check on NVIDIA GB300 with PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`: before the fix, `RuntimeError: called a synchronizing CUDA operation`; after the fix, no synchronization error and exact agreement with the reference.
- All configured commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, and sign-off checks.
- Sequential and concurrent smoke requests: **12/12 passed**, including short arithmetic and retrieval from 2,528- and 5,024-token prompts, covering chunked prefill.
- GSM8K, first 64 samples, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, concurrency 8, max output 1,024 tokens: **59/64 (92.19%)** for both strict and flexible exact match; **0 request errors**. This is a serving/accuracy smoke evaluation; no pre-change model baseline was run.

title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo-V2: skip fused fp8 qkv_proj tensors for layers the model does not have
author: jmeadlock
body:
## Overview

Skip fused fp8 `qkv_proj` checkpoint tensors for decoder layers the `MiMoV2Model` instance does not have, as every other branch of `load_weights` already does. Related: #58142 (same loader, pending-pair state across calls).

## Claims

- A checkpoint with more decoder layers than the instance, e.g. `--hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": N}'`, no longer fails engine init with `AttributeError: ModuleList has no attribute 'N'` in `_try_load_fp8_qkv_proj`.
- One regression test through `MiMoV2Model.load_weights` guards this fix and #58142.

## Validation

`tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py::test_load_weights_pairs_split_fp8_qkv_proj_and_skips_absent_layers` builds a one-layer `MiMoV2Model` and calls `load_weights` twice. The present layer's `weight` / `weight_scale_inv` pair is split across the calls, and an absent layer's pair arrives within the first. The test asserts the returned loaded set, the dequantized values of the loaded layer against the unquantized source (existing helpers in the file), and an empty `_pending_fp8_qkv_proj`.

```
pytest tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py -q
```

CPU only (macOS arm64, Python 3.12, torch 2.13.0, `uv` venv with this tree on `PYTHONPATH`):

| `mimo_v2.py` | result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`cc9b0f097d`) | 1 failed, 19 passed: `AttributeError: ModuleList has no attribute '7'` |
| this PR with #58142's persistent pending dict reverted | 1 failed, 19 passed: the split pair is dropped |
| this PR | 20 passed |

`pre-commit run --files` (ruff, mypy, typos) clean on both changed files. CI runs this file in the Quantized Models step.

End to end, on an earlier head with the same fix (`a1538ff185`): `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL` with `--hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers":16}'` loads and serves on one GB300. Output is garbage, as expected for a truncated model, but it boots.

Model evaluation: not applicable. The new branch only runs for a checkpoint tensor with no matching parameter, which a full-depth model never has (pipeline-parallel missing layers are caught earlier by `is_pp_missing_parameter`), so the weights loaded for full models are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR changes this path. #46755 adds fused fp8 `qkv_proj` loading to the MTP loader (`mimo_v2_mtp.py`), not `MiMoV2Model.load_weights`.

## Details

`_try_load_fp8_qkv_proj` buffers a layer's fused `qkv_proj` weight and scale until both arrive, then calls `self.get_submodule(<layer>.self_attn)`. For a layer the instance does not have, that raises. Since #58142 made the pending dict persist across `load_weights` calls, a lone absent-layer tensor would otherwise also stay pending for the model's lifetime. The fix returns early when `<prefix>.weight` is not in `params_dict`, matching the expert and generic branches. Truncated boots take minutes instead of hours, which is what makes bisection on this model family practical (context: #58142, https://al-engr.com/gb300-mimo-v26-pro-testing.html).

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Restore successful push completion reporting
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Purpose

After #56104, successful NIXL push WRITEs are filtered through `_recving_metadata`, which tracks incoming requests. Ordinary producer requests have no entry there, so they never report `finished_sending` after their WRITEs complete and retain source KV blocks until lease expiry. The existing test injects a consumer acknowledgment that the push implementation does not send.

Report successful outgoing requests when every WRITE handle has been released. Track outbound submission and polling failures across polls so a later successful sibling cannot hide an earlier failure. Ignore late completions for requests already retired by lease expiry, avoiding duplicate scheduler completion reports.

Regression coverage includes staggered successful WRITEs (including PP/HMA), sibling failures, submission/release failures, and completion after expiry. The preexisting lease-expiry behavior while DMA remains active is outside this change.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs referencing #56104 and NIXL push completion/failure, and inspected the related changes. #50754 adds decode-side notification of failed WRITE submissions; #55470 prevents deferred WRITEs after producer retirement. Neither restores producer completion reporting for successful WRITEs or tracks outgoing failures across completion polls. This follows up the already-merged #56104.

## Test Plan

Run the existing push unit suite with mocked NIXL transfers. On the local macOS environment, apply the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker to avoid an unrelated PyTorch MPS allocator assertion during teardown. No test bodies are skipped. The existing virtualenv interpreter was used (shown below as `.venv/bin/python`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import pytest
class CpuOnlyTests:
    def pytest_collection_modifyitems(self, items):
        for item in items:
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup)
raise SystemExit(pytest.main(
    ['tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py', '-q'],
    plugins=[CpuOnlyTests()],
))
PY

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/push_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
git diff --cached --check
```

## Test Result

- Push unit suite on base `ca831d1c55` plus this change: **84 passed**.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent AI review checked the changed lifecycle paths; its expiry/late-completion finding was fixed and covered by tests.
- GPU/NIXL serving tests and model evaluations have not been run. These unit tests do not establish real RDMA behavior or performance.

## AI assistance / draft status

AI assistance (Codex) was used to implement, test, and review this change. The tests above were run by the assistant. This PR remains a draft pending the human submitter's line-by-line review, independent test execution, and serving/model validation required by the contribution policy.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Vectorized flat abs-max for dynamic per-tensor FP8 quantization
author: Monishver11
body:
## Purpose

This PR speeds up the abs-max pass of `dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant` (per-tensor dynamic FP8 quantization) in `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/fp8/common.cu`. It is the activation quant on every MoE layer of a model served with `--quantization fp8`, and it had never been performance-tuned.

I went in after reading #44173, which took the same kind of kernel (block-per-row, shared-memory tree reduction, scalar loads) and rewrote it as warp shuffles plus vector loads. This kernel had the same shape of problem, so I applied the same approach and measured what it actually buys.

**What was there before**

`segmented_max_reduction_strided` launched one block per token, did one scalar load per element, reduced through a 256-entry shared-memory tree with a `__syncthreads` per level, and issued one atomic per token. For a decode batch of 32 tokens, that is 32 blocks on a 132-SM GPU. For a 65536-token prefill it is 65536 atomics to one address.

**What this PR does**

- For contiguous input, the abs-max is a flat grid-stride kernel over 16-element vectors (32 B loads for bf16, 64 B for fp32). The reduction is a `__shfl_xor_sync` butterfly within each warp and one shared-memory exchange across warps, so a single barrier. The grid is sized from the vector count and capped at 8 blocks per SM, so a small batch gets exactly the blocks it needs and a large one loops. One atomic per block instead of one per token.
- Strided or unaligned input keeps the one-block-per-token kernel, now with vectorized loads (`vectorize_read_with_alignment`) and the same shuffle reduction in place of the tree.
- The quantize pass that follows is unchanged.

**Numerics**

Output is bit-for-bit identical to `main`. The per-element operations are unchanged (`fmaxf` for the abs-max, the same `scaled_fp8_conversion` for the quantize). `fmaxf` is order-invariant, and dividing by a positive constant is monotonic, so regrouping the max across threads, warps, or blocks cannot change any scale or any output byte. I verified this empirically rather than relying on the argument; see below. No API change. Strided rows and all dtypes behave as before.

**Not a duplicate.** #41115 (open since May, merge conflicts, no review) tunes block sizes on the per-token kernel and does not touch the per-tensor path. #55330 targets the per-token-group kernel and #45428 the fused RMSNorm quant kernel.

**Next work.** Once this is approved and merged, I plan a follow-up PR for the per-token kernel in the same file, which reuses the reduction helpers added here.

## Test Plan

- **Bitwise equivalence.** Built `main` and this branch on the same box. Dumped the quantized bytes and scales on CPU-seeded inputs for bf16 and fp32, M in {1, 7, 64, 512, 4096, 16384}, hidden in {17, 1024, 1025, 2048, 4096, 5137, 7168, 8192, 16384, 32768}, and three row layouts (contiguous, misaligned by 8 elements, aligned but padded by 16). Compared with `torch.equal`.
- **Unit tests.** `tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py`, plus a new strided-input test that forces the fallback kernel at both alignments.
- **Performance.** H100 80 GB HBM3, driver 580, CUDA 13.0.3, torch 2.13.0+cu130. `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph`, median of the full op including the memset and both kernels, so this is what a caller sees.
- **End to end.** Qwen3-30B-A3B with `--quantization fp8`, `vllm bench throughput` and `vllm bench latency`, main vs this branch on the same box.

Commands run:

```bash
pre-commit run --files csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/fp8/common.cu tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py -q
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 2048 --dataset-name random --input-len 1024 --output-len 128 --num-prompts 512
vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 2048 --input-len 1024 --output-len 128 --batch-size 32 --num-iters 10
```

## Test Result

- Bitwise: **1080 cases identical, 0 mismatched**, bytes and scales.
- Tests: **249 passed**.

**Per-tensor, bf16, `main` vs this PR**

| M | hidden | main (us) | PR (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 4096 | 8.21 | 5.61 | 1.46x |
| 16 | 8192 | 11.36 | 6.01 | 1.89x |
| 512 | 4096 | 9.58 | 7.39 | 1.30x |
| 512 | 7168 | 12.60 | 8.79 | 1.43x |
| 4096 | 4096 | 48.95 | 30.51 | 1.60x |
| 4096 | 7168 | 85.17 | 55.27 | 1.54x |
| 16384 | 4096 | 187.22 | 115.96 | 1.61x |
| 16384 | 7168 | 312.94 | 196.30 | 1.59x |
| 65536 | 4096 | 715.88 | 436.15 | 1.64x |
| 65536 | 8192 | 1378.42 | 866.10 | 1.59x |

Geomean **1.39x** across bf16 and fp32, M in {16, 512, 4096, 16384, 65536}, hidden in {2048, 4096, 7168, 8192}. Range 1.11x to 1.89x. At large M, the op now moves about 3.0 TB/s of real traffic (two reads and one write), which is where it should sit on this GPU.

**End to end: Qwen3-30B-A3B with online FP8**

`--quantization fp8` quantizes activations per-tensor dynamically, and on a MoE model, the expert input of every layer goes through this kernel. Same H100, `vllm bench throughput`, random dataset, 1024 in / 128 out, 512 prompts, three interleaved runs per build after a warm compile cache:

| build | tokens/s (3 runs) | mean | stdev |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| main | 43793, 43706, 43835 | 43778 | 66 |
| this PR | 45154, 44810, 44965 | 44977 | 172 |

**+2.7% throughput**, with run-to-run spread under 0.4%. Batch latency (`vllm bench latency`, batch 32, 1024 in / 128 out): 1.876 s vs 1.843 s avg, about 1.8% lower.

The gain lands where expected: with the compiler fusing this model's per-token quant sites into RMSNorm, the per-tensor abs-max pass on the MoE expert inputs is the only kernel this PR changes that runs in the trace. Model output is unaffected since the kernel is bitwise identical.

I used Claude Code for this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and benchmarks above myself.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Replace torch.topk in DSA candidate block selection
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body: ## Summary `select_candidate_blocks` picks the top-k blocks per row with `torch.topk`, which runs a multi-pass radix select (`computeBlockDigitCounts`, `computeBlockwiseWithinKCounts`, `gatherTopK`). That does two things this caller does not need: - **It orders the results.** The only consumer is `_candidate_flags_kernel`, which does `flags[block] = 1`. Nothing downstream reads the ranking or the scores — only the *set* of selected block ids matters. - **It scans the whole padded workspace.** The logits workspace is padded to `max_model_len`, so `nblocks` is `max_model_len / block_size` no matter how short the context is. Past a row's end every block scores `-inf` and can never win a slot, but `torch.topk` has no way to express a per-row extent, so it reads all of it. This PR replaces that select on ROCm with a Triton kernel: - Each score and its index are packed into one order-preserving `int64` key, so `tl.topk` returns both at once and the separate `_store_candidates_kernel` pass disappears. The float bits are sign-transformed so IEEE order becomes unsigned order, and the index rides inverted in the low bits so ties resolve to the smaller index, matching `torch.topk`. - Each row is bounded by its own `end`, which is the part `torch.topk` cannot do. At 4K context in a 256K workspace this skips ~98% of the columns. - Decode rows are `batch * next_n`, only 1–640, which is too few to fill the GPU one program per row. Rows are split across programs and merged, with the split size computed **on device** from each row's live extent — a host-side bound would need a sync, and sizing from the padded width instead measured 6.3x → 2.0x at low concurrency. **The CUDA path is unchanged**; the new kernel is behind `current_platform.is_rocm()`. ## Not a duplicate Checked open PRs touching this area: - **#57858** is the only other open PR touching `candidate_blocks.py`, but it optimizes **prefill consumer-layer scoring** (`candidate_mqa_logits`, scoring only candidate columns). The producer-side block select this PR rewrites is untouched there. The two are complementary. Note #57858 also flips `_store_candidates_kernel`'s NaN handling (`!=` → `>`); the ROCm path here bypasses that kernel entirely, so the behaviors do not collide. - **#48726** (LiteTopk) is the indexer's *token* top-k, a different kernel and stage. - **#50470**, **#46172**, **#56944** touch `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` only (AITER dispatch, indexer optimization, prefill row sharding), not block candidate selection. No open PR optimizes `select_candidate_blocks`. ## Correctness The new path must select the same block *set* as the existing path. Verified against the unchanged path across 27 configurations — contexts 512 to 262144, rows 1 to 640, ragged per-row ends, non-zero `row_ks` starts, `row_repeat` decode grouping, `topk_blocks > nblocks`, and NaN scores: ``` 27 cases, 0 mismatches ``` Two cases this caught during development, both now handled: - `torch.topk` ranks NaN *highest*, and `_block_scores_kernel` can emit NaN during warmup, so keys force NaN above `+inf`. - When `nblocks < topk_blocks` the internal `K_PAD` shrinks below the output width, leaving tail columns unwritten; they are now `-1` filled. ## Tests ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_candidate_mask.py -q 9 passed, 14 warnings in 4.23s $ pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py exit=0 (no failures) ``` ## Kernel performance (MI355X) Full `select_candidate_blocks`, CUDA-graph timed, swept over the decode shape space: concurrency 1–128 x spec-decode depth 1–5, `max_model_len=262144`, `block_size=8`, `k=64`. All 120 points are faster. | context | median | range | | --- | --- | --- | | 4096 | 4.16x | 3.97–5.08x | | 16384 | 3.99x | 3.27–4.70x | | 65536 | 2.94x | 1.64–3.15x | Representative points (microseconds): | context | conc | next_n | rows | before | after | speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4096 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 47.55 | 11.20 | 4.24x | | 4096 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 58.00 | 13.96 | 4.16x | | 4096 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 293.54 | 67.86 | 4.33x | | 16384 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 59.19 | 14.31 | 4.14x | | 16384 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 299.65 | 91.67 | 3.27x | | 65536 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 60.31 | 19.30 | 3.13x | | 65536 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 330.51 | 185.83 | 1.78x | These shapes are TP-independent: the DSA indexer is replicated across ranks (`index_n_heads` is not divided by `tp_size`, unlike the main attention heads), so TP2 and TP4 run identical selections and one sweep covers both. ## Notes The kernel is still well above the bandwidth roofline (~45x at the largest shapes, more at small ones where it is latency-bound on two launches), so there is headroom left. `TILE=512` is a compromise: 1024 would take 65536-context from 2.36x to 2.79x but drop 4096-context from 23.8x to 14.4x. A context-aware tile choice could get both. Benchmarks used uniform context per batch; heavily ragged batches are bounded by their longest row. ## End-to-end serving Measured on MI355X TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, dspark MTP (5 speculative tokens, acceptance pinned at 3.51 so acceptance variance cannot contribute). Both arms are the **same build** differing only by an env toggle on the selection path, run concurrently on separate 4-GPU sets, after a warmup pass over every shape so Triton JIT and graph capture are paid before measurement. snapshot of trace: Before: After: **There is no measurable end-to-end difference, and none should be expected.** Output throughput, ISL 4096 / OSL 128: | concurrency | baseline tok/s | this PR tok/s | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 259.4 | 257.1 | | 8 | 1287.7 | 1282.4 | | 32 | 1068.9 | 1070.3 | | 128 | 1253.8 | 1254.8 | Repeating a single configuration three times shows run-to-run spread of 1112–1191 tok/s on baseline and 1142–1166 on this branch, with the sign of the difference flipping between repeats. The noise floor is several percent, while the expected effect is about 0.2%: the selection saves roughly 45 us per step against a 14.6 ms inter-token latency. The kernel win is real but it is a sub-1% slice of step time, so it cannot show up above noise in serving throughput. Median ITL, the most stable metric here, is unchanged (14.59-14.64 ms baseline vs 14.61-14.73 ms this branch). This PR should therefore be read as removing a hotspot that is prominent in kernel traces and cutting its cost 2-5x, not as an end-to-end throughput win. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Perf] DiffusionGemma: constrained reads over the request's logprob_token_ids
author: mmastrac
body:
Adds a new `diffusion_constrained` property that allows us to reduce the amount of work needed when performing constrained diffusion (ie: structured answers). Experimental results: approx. 25% faster. Followup to #57250 ## Purpose By passing `logprob_token_ids` it means that you already know the possible answer set. `diffusion_constrained: true` allows us to save work - the unembedding is a GEMM over the K gathered rows of the tied embedding instead of all 262k, the sampler runs in K-space (Gumbel sample, argmax, entropy, convergence), and maps picks back through the set, and the self-conditioning soft embed multiplies K-space probs by the K embedding rows. Overall we save ~25% in my local experiments on a GB10.

The timings, warm engine, fresh prompts per arm, two runs of each arm shown as a range. Single-slot reads, one step, canvas 48:

read | arm | concurrency 1 latency, median | concurrency 1 answers/s | concurrency 32 latency, median / p90 | concurrency 32 answers/s -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- yes/no | plain | 105 to 106 ms | 9.5 | 551 to 561 / 575 to 621 ms | 56.7 to 56.9 yes/no | constrained | 95 to 96 ms | 10.5 | 420 / 430 to 440 ms | 76.0 to 76.2 choice (4-way) | plain | 98 to 100 ms | 10.0 to 10.2 | 502 to 530 / 590 ms | 60.0 to 60.1 choice (4-way) | constrained | 88 to 92 ms | 10.9 to 11.4 | 354 to 382 / 445 to 457 ms | 81.1 to 82.8 At concurrency 1 the constraint takes about 10 percent off. At concurrency 32 it is worth 34 to 38 percent more answers per second and about a quarter less latency, because the batched step spends a much larger share of its time in the vocabulary-sized work. ---

title: [Perf][ROCm][Attention] Narrow the Triton prefill-attention KV tile on RDNA3/RDNA4
author: lijipeng787
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58060. On RDNA3/RDNA4, `context_attention_fwd` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py` launches `_fwd_kernel` with a 128x128 tile for bf16/fp16, which is slow on these GPUs. This PR narrows only the KV tile (`BLOCK_N`) to 32 when `on_gfx1x()` is true. `BLOCK_M`, `num_warps` and `num_stages` are unchanged, float32 is untouched (its tile is already 32), and CDNA, gfx1250 and NVIDIA keep the existing configuration. No other open PR addresses #58060.

This kernel serves encoder / non-causal pooling, so embedding and reranking models benefit. Generation prefill and decode use different kernels and are unaffected.

## Test Plan

W7900 (gfx1100) and R9700 (gfx1201), ROCm 10.0, bf16, TP=1, stock clocks.

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_prefill_attention.py`, including 5 new cases that check the launch configuration with the platform predicates mocked, so CI covers the RDNA branch without an RDNA GPU.
- Kernel A/B over all 9 supported head sizes x 4 mask modes, checked against an fp32 reference.
- End-to-end A/B on gte-Qwen2-1.5B, bge-base-en and gemma-3-1b (non-causal): 24 interleaved ABBA pairs each.
- `vllm bench serve` on gte-Qwen2-1.5B embeddings at concurrency 1/4/16/64.
- SciFact retrieval accuracy, with a batching-only control run for comparison.

## Test Result

- Tests: 25/25 pass on both GPUs.
- Kernel: every cell is faster on both GPUs; median 2.56-2.67x (gfx1100) and 2.25-2.30x (gfx1201).

| | gfx1100 | gfx1201 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| End to end, embedding models | 1.10-1.23x | 1.08-1.12x |
| Serving throughput | 1.17-1.19x | 1.03-1.05x |

- Accuracy: nDCG@10 moves by -0.0001 (gfx1100) and -0.0005 (gfx1201). Changing only `max_num_seqs`, with no kernel change, moves it by +0.0011 and +0.0005. Recall@10 is identical.
- Limitations: measured on bf16, TP=1 and gfx1100/gfx1201 only. Other RDNA3/RDNA4 parts are covered by `on_gfx1x()` without being measured; the gate can be narrowed if preferred.

Developed with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot CLI) for the benchmarking, analysis and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran all measurements myself.

title: [Perf] DiffusionGemma: one-pass sampler statistics kernel
author: mmastrac
body:
## Purpose

Followup to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57250 - helps decoding for diffusiongemma in both text and structured answer mode (the latter only at high concurrency, the former in all cases I've found).

A custom diffusiongemma Triton kernel: 

 - one program per logits row
 - does an online max and sum in one pass
 - draws Gumbel noise inline from Philox instead of materializing a noise tensor
 - writes the softmax once in the embedding dtype (only when self-conditioning will read it)

Replaces _compiled_sample_step's older process which was several fused kernels that performed:

 - Cast the logits to fp32 and divide every element by the request's temperature.
 - Draw a uniform random tensor the same size as the logits, turn it into Gumbel noise with two logs, add it to the scaled logits, and take the argmax of that for the sample.
 - Take the argmax of the scaled logits themselves for the committed token.
 - Compute log_softmax over each row, exponentiate it to get the probabilities, multiply the two and sum for the entropy.
 - Cast the probabilities to bf16 for the self-conditioning matmul.

(each of those is at least one read and often one write of a [4096, 262144] fp32 tensor at concurrency 32)

## Test Plan

Default options, open-generation tok/s sweep at concurrency 1/4/8/16/32, engine restarted per arm, before and after.

## Test Result

DGX Spark, nvfp4

```
conc reqs    tok/s  req/s mean tok  mean s   (before)
```

title: [ROCm] Fix CI runtime and tests for MI355 DPX
author: mkunredd
body:
Fix CI runtime and test behavior supporting MI355 DPX coverage: wait for GPU memory release, match quantization references to production behavior, and prevent overlapping jobs from using the same render device.

- Share an opt-in gfx950 GPU-memory fixture between the deep-sleep and hybrid model tests.
- Match block INT8 MoE reference activation quantization to production truncation, preserve round-to-nearest for existing callers, and cover fractional values with exact regression cases.
- Round the MXFP4 skinny-GEMM reference to BF16 before comparison and fit the large-K skinny-GEMM regression within 128 DPX compute units.
- Wait for GPU memory release during metrics and NIXL test cleanup, with Ray cleanup waiting in the driver.
- Guard native DPX jobs with a nonblocking render-device lock and use AMD-SMI diagnostic options supported in Linux guests.
- Add the small gfx950 GSM8K model list used by the YAML companion PR.

The Quantization and Model Executor suites remain on non-DPX queues in [#57599](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57599), preserving the GPTQ and tensorizer tests with their normal assertions and failure reporting. Checkpoint metadata handling and the tensorizer test match `main`.

The original work used Claude Code assistance; the split, scope reduction, validation, and updated description were AI-assisted with Codex.

title: [Bugfix] Fix resumable request + async scheduling handoff race
author: yzong-rh
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a resumable-request handoff race when async scheduling is used. When a streaming turn stops, `_update_request_as_session()` uses `request.num_computed_tokens` as the prefix boundary for the next turn. That value is an optimistic frontier: it can already include input positions from older dispatches that are still in flight. When those dispatches later retire through `update_from_output()`, their output corrupts the new turn.

Consider a three-token prompt at turn 0 (`T0`). Let `A` be `all_token_ids`, `C` be `num_computed_tokens`, and `P` be `num_output_placeholders`.

```text
T0:              A=[0, 1, 2]                     P=0  C=0

  S0 scheduled:  A=[0, 1, 2]                     P=1  C=3
  S1 scheduled:  A=[0, 1, 2]                     P=2  C=4

    S0 runs worker on [0, 1, 2] and returns EOS

  S0 retired:    A=[0, 1, 2, EOS]                P=1  C=4
  _handle_stopped_request runs
  _update_request_as_session runs

T1:              A=[0, 1, 2, EOS, 3, 4]          P=1  C=4
```

`T1` is corrupted. It contains a spurious `EOS` token before the continuation. It will also receive a stale token after `S1` retires.

Other invariants are also broken.

### [#35755](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35755)

On the next scheduling step, the scheduler may do a chunked prefill on 2 prompt tokens:

```
T1:              A=[0, 1, 2, EOS, 3, 4]          P=1  C=4
  S2 scheduled:  A=[0, 1, 2, EOS, 3, 4]          P=1  C=6
```

Because `C < len(A) + P`, `S2` is considered to be a chunked prefill by the scheduler, so `P` isn't incremented. However, the worker will process `[3, 4]` of `[0, 1, 2, EOS, 3, 4]` as a final prefill, which yields a new token. When `S1` and `S2` eventually retire, `P` will be decremented twice, resulting in a `num_output_placeholders` underflow.


### [#52693](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52693)

Suppose `S1` retires before the `T1` continuation arrives and also outputs an
`EOS` token.

```
T0:
  ...
  S0 retired:    A=[0, 1, 2, EOS]                P=1  C=4
  _handle_stopped_request runs
  no continuation, request placed on skipped_waiting

    S1 runs worker on [0, 1, 2, EOS] and returns EOS again

  S1 retired:    A=[0, 1, 2, EOS, EOS]           P=0  C=4
  _handle_stopped_request
  no continuation, request placed on skipped_waiting again
```

The same request now appears on `skipped_waiting` twice. Before [PR #48245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48245), this would cause `Invalid request status: RUNNING` on the next scheduler call. That PR added a call to `skipped_waiting.remove_requests()` for stopped preempted requests in `update_from_output`, removing the duplicate entries in `skipped_waiting`.

The fix resets the next turn to the safe frontier `F = C - P` before the stale placeholders. Thus `F=3` in the trace above; `F=10` is the corresponding value in [`repro_35755.py`](repro_35755.py). It marks the remaining in-flight results as stale, drops them via `drop_stale_output`, and drains them with `num_stale_output_tokens`.

#52765 is a similar but incomplete fix because it marks in-flight results stale only after `_update_request_as_session` has already used the optimistic `num_computed_tokens` boundary, allowing stale old-turn positions to remain in the next turn.

## Test Plan

Unit tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_worker_slot_overflow.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_abort_final_step.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/test_realtime_validation.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py
```

Deterministic-ish E2E repro [`repro_35755.py`](https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/9f18b70d858b5350b2fcbf7ee908a129):

```bash
.venv/bin/python repro_35755.py
```

## Test Result

Unit tests:

`256 passed, 2 skipped, 29 warnings in 1353.75s (0:22:33)`

Deterministic-ish E2E repro:

The fix revision `PASS`; the main revision reproduced the `num_output_placeholders` underflow assertion.

cc @LucasWilkinson @yewentao256

- [x] The test result and end-to-end smoke-test result are recorded.
- [x] No documentation update is necessary for this scheduler fix.

title: [CPU][Whisper] Support W4A16 quantized Whisper on the CPU WNA16 kernel
author: harshaladhav-amd
body:
## Purpose
- Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58267
- `cpu_gemm_wna16`: Flatten >2-D activations to `[M, K]` and reshape the output back, matching `int4_scaled_mm_cpu`. The Whisper encoder passes 3-D `[B, T, D]` into quantized Linear layers, and the C++ kernel reads `K` from `input.size(1)`. 2-D inputs are unchanged.
- `_create_fake_bias_for_k_proj`: Also match `.k_proj.weight_packed` so compressed-tensors checkpoints get the synthetic k_proj bias required by `qkv_proj`/`kv_proj`. Forward real `.k_proj.bias` entries unchanged, and take `out_features` from `config.d_model` instead of `weight.size(0)` (wrong for packed AWQ/Marlin weights).
- Fake `k_proj.bias` entries are collected while walking the checkpoint and **yielded after the input iterator is exhausted**, rather than immediately after each matching weight. That applies to Whisper, GLM-ASR, and Moss-Transcribe (shared helper). `AutoWeightsLoader` resolves by name and fused qkv/kv shard loads are order-independent. Callers that omit `out_features` still size the fake bias from `weight.size(0)`.
- Tests: 3-D `int4_scaled_mm_cpu` / `cpu_gemm_wna16` shape+value checks, and unit tests for fake k_proj bias injection vs real bias.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep every multimodal feature in the partial-block KV event
author: haosenwang1018
body:
> **Rescoped after review.** This PR originally also changed `request_block_hasher` in `kv_cache_utils.py`. @sawsa307 pointed out that #51694 already covers that; I dropped that hunk and its tests, and this PR is now only the `block_pool.py` bug, using the same bisect helper #51694 uses.

## Purpose

`BlockPool.cache_partial_block` emits the `BlockStored` event that external KV cache consumers key on, and builds its `extra_keys` starting at the **last** multimodal feature:

```python
block_end = num_tokens
curr_mm_idx = -1 if block_start > 0 else 0
extra_keys, _ = generate_block_hash_extra_keys(
    request, block_start, block_end, curr_mm_idx
)
```

The event window is the last hash block of the partial block:

```python
# _get_partial_block_parent_hash_and_start
num_hash_blocks = num_tokens // self.hash_block_size
block_start = (num_hash_blocks - 1) * self.hash_block_size
```

and that window can reach into more than one feature — the tail of one plus the whole of a shorter next one. Starting at the last feature drops the others, so the event is published under a key that does not distinguish the dropped feature, and a consumer can hand one request the KV computed for another.

Reproduced through the real path, `hash_block_size=4`, `block_size=8`, `num_tokens=12`, features at `(offset=6, length=3)` and `(offset=10, length=2)`, so the event window is tokens `[8, 12)`:

```
emitted extra_keys : [(('B', 2),)]            # 'A' is missing
correct            : [(('A', -2), ('B', 2))]
```

## Changes

One site in `block_pool.py`: scan from the first feature that overlaps the window instead of from the last one, using `get_mm_features_in_window` — the same bisect over the sorted features that #51694 uses for the block hasher, so the two sites stay consistent.

## Test

`tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_partial_block_stored_event_keeps_every_mm_feature` builds a `BlockPool` with `enable_kv_cache_events=True`, calls `cache_partial_block` on a request whose partial block spans two features, and asserts the emitted event's extra keys.

On current `main`:

```
E   AssertionError: assert [(('B', 2),)] == [(('A', -2), ('B', 2))]
FAILED tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_partial_block_stored_event_keeps_every_mm_feature
```

With this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
121 passed
```

`main` gives 120 passed on the same host; the 5 failures present in both runs are platform-gated cases unrelated to this change (`test_mla_with_incompatible_swa_uses_one_full_allocation_group`, `test_unidentifiable_draft_with_mamba_warns`, `test_non_mtp_eagle_hybrid_still_warns[eagle|eagle3|dspark]`) — this is a CPU-only machine. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.

## How this was found

By asserting an invariant that was not covered — a block's cache key must not depend on when it was computed, and changing one multimodal input must change every key that covers it — and fuzzing it. The same fuzz is what surfaced the hasher-side problem that #51694 fixes.

---

*AI assistance disclosure, per [contributing/README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/contributing/README.md#ai-assisted-contributions): prepared with Claude Code. Every changed line was reviewed, the failure was reproduced through the real `cache_partial_block` path on current `main`, and the test was run with and without the fix. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Claude`.*

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Reap expired NIXL leases behind a heartbeated head
author: gokay-ai
body:
## Purpose

The NIXL send-side lease reaper treated `_reqs_to_send` as expiry-ordered and stopped at the first still-live entry. Heartbeats update that map **in place**, so a request that keeps getting renewed can sit at the head forever and block reclaim of every expired entry behind it. That is the case in #58222: A is heartbeated, B and C expire, and neither is ever released.

Delete+reinsert on heartbeat is not enough either — `max(old, now + extension)` can still leave a later-inserted longer TTL in front of an already-expired entry. The reaper now scans the whole map. Expired send-lease IDs are always in `_reqs_to_process` (stamped only after that set membership check), so the reaper keeps `_reqs_to_process.remove()`.

Fixes #58222.

**Not a duplicate of [#50789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50789):** that is a stale draft from August against an older `get_finished()` layout, and it does not target this issue. This change is against current `main`, extracts a testable helper, and pins the issue's stdlib repro as a unit test.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py -v
uvx ruff check vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py
```

No GPU. No model eval — reclaim path only, serving output unchanged.

## Test Result

```
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py
11 passed in 1.39s
```

Including:
- `test_reaper_reclaims_expired_leases_behind_heartbeated_head` (issue #58222 repro; also reaps A when `now == expires`)
- `test_reaper_reclaims_when_now_equals_expiry` (`now >= expires` boundary)
- `test_reaper_reclaims_shorter_lease_behind_later_deadline`
- existing heartbeat tests

Ruff check and format: passed on the two changed files.

AI assistance was used to locate the reaper/heartbeat code and write the regression tests. I reviewed the change.

title: [Perf][SM120][MLA] Use compact FP8 KV rows for NoPE models
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to merged #55277: use compact 528-byte `fp8_ds_mla` rows for native NoPE on the FlashInfer SM120 backend. Rebased onto upstream main `e6674262f1`. Only tests conflicted: #55528 made the MLA KV-spec test's fake layer carry `attn_backend`, and the HiSparse test helper gained `max_union_rows`; both were resolved by keeping both sides. The two commits are now `aab1e922fa` and `e879b2ef44` (head), and the branch merges cleanly into current main.

The row contains 512 FP8 latent bytes and four FP32 group scales. There is no RoPE payload. A single backend-owned row-size method supplies both the KV spec and early HiSparse registration. On SM120, compact selection depends solely on `kv_lora_rank=512` and `qk_rope_head_dim=0`, independent of model name, connector, or offloading configuration. Other backend layouts are unchanged; real RoPE64 `fp8_ds_mla` retains 656-byte rows. No new dtype or CLI option is added.

The writer accepts NoPE 528/656, preserves legacy zero-tail behavior for 656, and rejects RoPE64 with 528. It distinguishes logical row width from physical stride. The fixed 576-dimensional gather rejects compact input. HiSparse uses actual row widths for byte movement and rejects incompatible shared-staging layouts.

No connector changes, layout negotiation, or old-cache migration are added. Local prefix caching remains supported. External connectors were not tested end to end.

Duplicate-work check: #53969/#55778/#55543 use padded compatibility layouts; #55219/#57169 address broader paging/stride plumbing, not this compact writer/spec change. The community B12X GLM_NEXT path already uses the same 528-byte encoding; that is a useful precedent, not the FlashInfer backend wiring implemented here. Reference: local-inference-lab/vllm `cff8aebfeb73de96c97b4c5a0550c5a49f27451c`, `b12x_mla_sparse.py`. FlashInfer compact-row support was merged in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5075.

## Test Plan

Validation used 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell for official NVIDIA GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP4, BF16, no speculation, text-only, context 65536, max sequences 32, batched tokens 4096, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs. FlashInfer source: `dc04f50c9aa3eabcdaa5feb0934edb3d85e9529a`.

Commands below are shown without local environment wrappers, not as verbatim execution transcripts. Paths are relative to the vLLM checkout unless noted. The following checks were rerun after the rebase onto main:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py \
  -k concat_and_cache_ds_mla -q -rs
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_cp_gather_fp8.py -q
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_mla_kv_cache_spec_uses_layer_cache_dtype \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_index_group_preserves_row_width \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_shared_staging_requires_uniform_row_width \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_swap_in_preserves_rows_across_eviction \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_gather_prefill_cache_prefers_resident_rows
prek run --from-ref c843f0cab78b413f2b0a5c2282cb71e3a3937b11 --to-ref bea90f7efee
```

Earlier validation from the FlashInfer checkout, not rerun after the rebase:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/attention/test_sparse_mla_sm120.py \
  -k glm53_nope_compact_rows -q
```

Model validation preceded gate removal and was not rerun after the rebase. It used GSM8K and random-8k1k workloads with `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` explicitly selected. As in #55277, successful runs used the disclosed distributed-autotune workaround:

```text
VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS=fp4_gemm,trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1,trtllm::fused_moe::gemm2
```

This PR does not fix that separate autotune issue or the noncanonical-layout calibration restriction. FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, pinned in upstream vLLM, is not the dependency used for this validation.

## Test Result

### Revalidation after the rebase onto `e6674262f1` (head `e879b2ef44`)

Run on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with FlashInfer built from main (includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5075) and vLLM's CUDA extension rebuilt from a tree containing this branch:

- CUDA writer (`test_cache.py -k concat_and_cache_ds_mla`): **9 passed, 3 skipped**. Fixed-layout gather (`test_cp_gather_fp8.py`): **18 passed**. KV-spec tests (`test_mla_backends.py -k kv_cache_spec`): **10 passed**.

title: [Bugfix][CI] Fix the flaky sharded-sampling tests, and the engine teardown need
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

**The two sharded-sampling equivalence tests are flaky.** They were added in
#50465 (commit `d154d90d6c`) to show that batch-sharded sampling is a drop-in
for replicated sampling. On MI355 the non-spec one fails in about 40% of runs:

> AssertionError: 4/16 prompts diverged: beyond near-tie boot-state noise;
> sharded sampling is likely misrouting requests

Sharding is not the cause. Each test compares two engine boots, and with the
engine in its own process prefill starts before the last requests arrive over
IPC, so the boots pick different first batches. That changes the GEMM reduction
order, moves logprobs by up to 0.25 and flips near-ties. The same divergences
appear with sharding disabled on both sides, in prompt logprobs before any
sampling, and on a single GPU where sharding does not exist; they vanish when
the batch holds one request.

**The top-k comparison also misfires.** vLLM appends the sampled token when it
misses the requested top-k, so one side can hold k+1 entries where the other
holds k, and the allowance meant for one near-tie swap is spent on that extra
entry instead.

**Fixing the tests requires fixing engine teardown.** They need the engine in
the caller's process so every request is queued before the first step, but
`InprocClient` never tears its engine core down: unlike `MPClient` it has no
finalizer, and neither `LLM` nor `LLMEngine` calls its `shutdown()`. Its workers
keep their GPU memory for the life of the process, so the second boot fails with
81.5 of 288 GiB free against the 201.6 GiB requested. Seven tests already work
around this by calling `engine_core.shutdown()` by hand.

### What changed

- Both tests run the engine in the caller's process, so the two boots schedule
  the same batches. The divergence tolerances are removed and the comments state
  the measured cause.
- The top-k comparison separates the requested top-k from the sampled token
  before comparing sets.
- `InprocClient` gains the finalizer `MPClient` already uses, with an idempotent
  `shutdown()` so the seven manual calls keep working.

The spec-decode test was never observed failing, since it compares only token
ids over ten tokens. It is changed because the same mechanism applies, its
tolerance rests on an explanation that is not correct, and its own docstring
already asks for exact agreement.

## Test Plan

MI355 (gfx950), two GPUs. Both tests run repeatedly, before and after, to
measure flakiness rather than a single result:

- `pytest -v -s v1/e2e/general/test_sharded_sampling.py`
- `pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py`

Plus every test that calls `engine_core.shutdown()` by hand, run with and
without the finalizer.

## Test Result

**General test.** Before: ten instrumented runs gave 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
5 divergences out of 16 against a threshold of 3, so about 40% fail. A control
with sharding disabled on both sides gave 2, 2, 4, 5, which is what rules
sharding out. After: five consecutive passes, zero divergences.

**Spec-decode test.** No flakiness observed before, 0 of 120 comparisons; four
passes after. Runtime drops from about 117 s to about 87 s, since the engine now
releases its workers.

**Engine fix.** Without it the second in-process boot fails at 81.5 of 288 GiB
free; with it both boot and memory returns between them.

---

title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 enable prefill checkpoints on ROCm
author: kliuae
body:
## Purpose

In the `align` mamba cache mode, a Mamba state can only be reused at block boundaries. Without checkpoints, the scheduler splits the last prefill chunk into two steps where the first step cuts at the block boundary and materialize the checkpoint there, and the second step performs an additional forward pass on the remaining context. With checkpoints, the last chunk can be performed in a single step as KDA states are recorded by the KDA kernel when block boundaries are passed, eliminating the need for the additional forward pass when context lengths are not multiples of the block size.

This PR builds on top of the existing infrastructure for Mamba prefill checkpointing and enables that for Kimi-K3 on ROCm, leveraging the fused KDA prefill path that has intermediate mamba states exposed. The prefill checkpoint is only enabled for the fused path at the moment.

In enabling the ROCm checkpointing, there are two issues found where the scheduler and kv cache manager disagree on the block boundaries, causing wasted allocation and dropped cache. The issues are addressed in #59175, and the following evaluation and performance benchmark runs are performed in combination with the fixes from #59175.

Overall with the ROCm enablement and the fixes, checkpointing improves TTFT by ~20% in agentic workloads on MI355X.

AI agent was used in this PR.

- ROCm KDA checkpointing
- Core partial prefix cache hits

title: [ROCm][Perf] Drop two dead per-step ops from the AITER sparse MLA metadata build
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Purpose

`ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` runs once per KV-cache group per scheduler step and launches two GPU ops whose results are not needed:

1. **Unused `query_lens`.** `build()` computes `query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]`, but `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` only reads its size and device; the kernel derives per-request lengths from `cu_query_lens`. The parameter is dropped and `num_seqs` is taken as `cu_query_lens.size(0) - 1`.
2. **Self-aliasing `fill_`.** `paged_kv_indptr[n + 1:].fill_(paged_kv_indptr[n])` passes a view of the tensor being filled, so ATen clones the value first. A broadcast `copy_` from the same element writes the same values without the clone.

| op | aten ops | GPU kernels |
|---|---|---|
| `x[n+1:].fill_(x[n])` | `fill_` → `clone` (`empty_strided` + copy) → `copy_` | 2 |
| `t.copy_(x[n].expand_as(t))` | `copy_` | 1 |
| `qsl[1:] - qsl[:-1]` | `sub` (+ alloc) | 1 |

Each `build()` launches two fewer kernels and makes two fewer device allocations, with no change in output. #57885 removed a similar dead op from the DSA indexer builder.

On ROCm, sparse-MLA layers that do not bring their own backend select `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`. Of 18 current checkpoints probed on main (dummy weights, 8 layers, TP=1), three reach this `build()`:

| model | binding | `build()` per decode step |
|---|---|---:|
| GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`) | `DeepseekV32MLAAttention` → `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend` | 2 |
| GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 (`glm_moe_dsa`) | same | 2 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`, DSA every 4th layer) | `MLAAttention` → `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend` | 1 |

DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro and V4.1-Flash use their own builders, and the other 12 have no sparse MLA. CUDA never selects this backend.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py`. The new `test_build_fills_paged_kv_indptr_tail` poisons the `paged_kv_indptr` tail and checks that it reads as the running total; it fails if the tail copy is removed.
- Output equivalence: every benchmark run hashes the full `paged_kv_indptr` buffer (tail poisoned first), the returned metadata tensors and the AITER work/reduce metadata.
- Micro: the real `build()` on a builder constructed from a real `VllmConfig` (`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, top-k 2048, decode B ∈ {1, 7, 29, 61, 127}). Both implementations alternate on one builder, order flipped every pair, 300 warmup + 3000 pairs, in 3 processes. *Steady*: contexts > top-k, so the persistent-metadata key hits. *Growing*: the key misses, so `get_mla_metadata_v1` and a stream sync run on every build.
- e2e: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (fp8 KV faults on main with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, before and independent of this PR), a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm with the first discarded.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1031 --random-output-len 509 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 509 --max-concurrency 61 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```
- e2e: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (fp8 KV faults on main with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, before and independent of this PR), a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm with the first discarded.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1031 --random-output-len 509 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 509 --max-concurrency 61 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

## Test Result

**Unit:** 5 passed on MI355X (gfx950), main `863475eb9c`. Output hashes match between the arms for every config and batch size.

**Micro**, MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.12.0, main `c961121519`:

|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| GLM-5.3, steady (AITER persistent path) | 1 | 91.48 | 80.68 | 10.82 [9.71, 10.89] | +11.2 % |
| | 29 | 91.29 | 81.22 | 10.12 [9.71, 10.66] | +11.0 % |
| | 127 | 91.62 | 81.22 | 10.55 [10.00, 10.59] | +11.1 % |

title: [Bugfix] Detect the CUDA toolkit the way FlashInfer does in has_flashinfer()
author: abmfy
body:
## Purpose

When `flashinfer-cubin` is not installed, `has_flashinfer()` treats FlashInfer as unusable unless `nvcc` is on `PATH`. FlashInfer's own JIT (`jit/cpp_ext.py::get_cuda_path`) looks further: `$CUDA_HOME`, then `$CUDA_PATH`, then `nvcc` on `PATH`, then `/usr/local/cuda`.

On a bare-metal or SLURM host the toolkit usually sits at `/usr/local/cuda` without being on `PATH`. There, every `has_flashinfer()`-gated kernel is silently disabled (TRTLLM/CUTLASS MoE, FlashInfer FP8/NVFP4 linears, AllReduce+RMSNorm fusion), and only a `debug_once` line is logged. FlashInfer attention is not gated by `has_flashinfer()`, so on the same host it keeps JIT-compiling with that toolkit. Setting `CUDA_HOME` does not help on main either.

This PR:
- mirrors FlashInfer's toolkit lookup without importing FlashInfer, since importing it initializes CUDA;
- also requires `ninja` on `PATH`, because FlashInfer runs it from there and a non-activated venv lacks it;
- replaces the `debug_once` with a `warning_once` that points to `CUDA_HOME` or `flashinfer download-kernels`.

## Test Plan

- GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13.1 at `/usr/local/cuda`, no flashinfer-cubin.
- E2E: two venvs from the same precompiled wheel, main `a9f07d0bc5` (FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1) and this PR on top of it. `nvcc` is off `PATH` and `CUDA_HOME` is unset in all arms. Same node, interleaved rounds, fresh server per arm.
- Unit tests and probe: re-run after rebasing onto main `94d1462924` (FlashInfer 0.7.0).

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 32768 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-prefix-caching
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1000 \
  --random-output-len 1000 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --max-concurrency {1,32}
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** both new tests pass. On main both fail: the first because `has_flashinfer()` returns False, the second because it returns True. (Run unmodified, they error in the fixture, since `_DEFAULT_CUDA_HOME` does not exist on main.)

**Toolkit probe** (FlashInfer 0.7.0; "can JIT" is FlashInfer's own `get_cuda_path()` plus `ninja` on `PATH`):

| environment | FlashInfer can JIT | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| toolkit only at `/usr/local/cuda` | yes | **False** | True |
| `CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda` | yes | **False** | True |
| `CUDA_HOME=/nonexistent`, nvcc on `PATH` | no | **True** | False + warning |
| runtime image (no `bin/nvcc`) | no | False | False + warning |
| nvcc on `PATH`, venv not activated (no `ninja`) | no | **True** | False + warning |

**Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP1, 3 rounds.** MoE backend is Triton on main; FlashInfer TRTLLM with this PR and with `PATH` fixed by hand.

| | main | PR | main + `/usr/local/cuda/bin` on `PATH` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c=1 output tok/s | 274.4 ± 0.4 | **309.1** ± 1.1 (+12.6%, t = 51) | 308.4 ± 1.2 |
| c=32 output tok/s | 3312 ± 20 | **3808** ± 2 (+15.0%, t = 42) | 3813 ± 5 |
| GSM8K | 0.854 | 0.847 | 0.846 |

The PR matches the `PATH` workaround within noise, so the gain comes from the FlashInfer kernels being re-enabled. The GSM8K gap to main is the MoE kernel change and is within one standard error (≈1 pp).

**Supporting data: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8, TP2, 2 rounds.** Main falls back to DeepGEMM MoE with no AR fusion; the PR uses TRTLLM MoE with AR+RMSNorm fusion.

| | main | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| c=1 output tok/s | 160.3 | **209.9** (+30.9%) |
| c=32 output tok/s | 1746 | **2883** (+65%) |
| GSM8K | 0.880 | 0.876 |

Arms used separate FlashInfer autotune caches. That can shift results by about 2%, far below these deltas.

## Notes

- The warning now fires on every CUDA install that has neither flashinfer-cubin nor a usable toolkit. On main such installs log only at debug level.
- Once `has_flashinfer()` is True, TRTLLM MoE also needs the TRTLLM-gen cubins, from the artifactory or from `flashinfer download-kernels`. This PR does not change that.
- #58765 drops flashinfer-cubin from `requirements/cuda.txt`, so more installs will take this path.
- Related, no overlap: #54267 and #55651 gate SM12x on toolkits that are too old; #49314 and #51741 cover the sampler.
- FlashInfer's toolkit lookup is unchanged between 0.6.18 and 0.7.0, so the e2e numbers were not re-taken after the rebase.
