title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Restore prompt-tail prefix-cache hits with MTP
author: netanel-haber
body:
Regression introduced in #55390.
Affects hybrid Mamba/GDN models with MTP, prefix caching, `--mamba-cache-mode align`, and `hash_block_size` smaller than the Mamba `block_size`.

| Model                                          | Prefix-cache hit (%): before → main → fix | Output TPS/GPU: before → main → fix |
|------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| [Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4][l] (Mamba, TP1) | 95.72 → 92.02 → **95.71**                 | 2846 → 2228 → **2833**              |
| [Qwen3.5-122B NVFP4][q] (GDN, TP2)             | 95.47 → 89.80 → **95.57**                 | 687 → 480 → **688**                 |

[l]: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4
[q]: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4

- AIPerf: 50K-token shared prefix, 20 turns of 2K in / 1K out, concurrency 32.
- GSM8K is on par across the three builds (1319 questions, temperature 1.0): Lightning 91.7±0.6%, Qwen3.5 80.4±0.2%.

<details>
<summary>Full results, images, and commands</summary>

#### Full results

| Model        | vLLM          | Prefix-cache hit | Uncached prompt tokens | Output TPS/GPU | Gen TPS/user | GSM8K  |
|--------------|---------------|------------------|------------------------|----------------|--------------|--------|
| Lightning    | Before #55390 | 95.72%           | 2.25M                  | 2846           | 108.7        | 91.05% |
|              | Main          | 92.02%           | 4.19M                  | 2228           | 88.9         | 91.81% |
|              | Main + fix    | 95.71%           | 2.26M                  | 2833           | 109.4        | 92.27% |
| Qwen3.5-122B | Before #55390 | 95.47%           | 2.35M                  | 687            | 48.9         | 80.29% |
|              | Main          | 89.80%           | 5.27M                  | 480            | 34.1         | 80.67% |
|              | Main + fix    | 95.57%           | 2.29M                  | 688            | 49.4         | 80.21% |

Gen TPS/user is the mean of `1 / inter-token latency` per request.

#### Images

- Before #55390: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3df4ae153eb385e27b52f26c81f8edb9e20b9984`
- Main: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19`
- Main + fix: the main image with this PR's `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` mounted over the installed one.

#### AIPerf

Server environment: `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`.

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 114688 --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 64 --prefix-match-unit 64 --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
  --speculative_config.method mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --speculative_config.rejection_sample_method synthetic --speculative_config.synthetic_acceptance_length 3.0
```

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --language-model-only \
  --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 114688 --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 64 --prefix-match-unit 64 --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --speculative_config.method mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --speculative_config.rejection_sample_method synthetic --speculative_config.synthetic_acceptance_length 3.0
```

```bash
aiperf profile --model $MODEL --tokenizer $MODEL --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --url http://0.0.0.0:30000 \
  --endpoint-type chat --streaming --use-server-token-count --random-seed 42 \
  --concurrency 32 --num-conversations 32 --request-count 640 --warmup-request-count 16 \
  --shared-system-prompt-length 51200 --isl 2048 --isl-stddev 0 --osl 1024 --osl-stddev 0 \
  --conversation-turn-mean 20 --conversation-turn-stddev 0 --conversation-turn-delay-mean 0 \
  --extra-inputs temperature:0 --extra-inputs ignore_eos:true
```

#### GSM8K

Same `vllm serve` commands as above, without the two `synthetic` flags and without `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY`. [NeMo-Skills](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills) at `467b057372`:

```bash
python -m nemo_skills.inference.generate \
  ++server.server_type=vllm ++server.base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 ++server.model=$MODEL \
  ++input_file=$GSM8K_TEST_JSONL ++eval_type=math ++eval_config.split=test ++prompt_config=generic/math \
  ++inference.endpoint_type=chat ++inference.tokens_to_generate=4096 ++inference.temperature=1.0 \
  ++inference.top_p=0.95 ++inference.random_seed=0 ++chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=True \
  ++inference.extra_body.skip_special_tokens=False ++max_concurrent_requests=512 ++output_file=output.jsonl
```

</details>

## Explanation of regression

Example: `hash_block_size = 64`. Prompt A has 1600 tokens. Prompt B starts with A. With MTP, the prefix-cache lookup drops the last 64 matched tokens, so B can reuse at most 1536. [The scheduler](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L479-L486) ends a prefill chunk of A at 1536 to compute the Mamba state there. But [`_cache_partial_tail_block`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L2078-L2086) saves the state at 1536 only if the Mamba group has `use_eagle`. Otherwise, it saves at 1600.

The Mamba group got `use_eagle` only from **the all-groups fallback** in [the coordinator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L108-L110):

```python
if use_eagle and not self.eagle_group_ids:
    self.eagle_group_ids = set(range(len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups)))
```

#55390 marks the MTP group, so the all-groups fallback no longer runs. The Mamba state is saved at 1600, and B reuses 0 tokens instead of 1536.

## Fix
`_cache_partial_tail_block` checks `drop_eagle_checkpoint_block` instead of `use_eagle`. [The coordinator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L153-L156) sets it on every Mamba manager exactly when the scheduler shifts the chunk end:

```diff
-if self.use_eagle:
+if self.drop_eagle_checkpoint_block:
     latest_prompt_hash_boundary = max(
         latest_prompt_hash_boundary - hash_block_size, 0
     )
```

#### Tests

`pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_mamba_eagle_resume_checkpoint.py`: the new `annotated-draft` cases fail on main and pass with this change.

#### AI assistance

AI assistance was used.

title: [CI][ROCM] Add the Fusion E2E TP2 Quick group on MI355, and the AITER MLA fix it needs
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

**Add one AMD CI group.** It mirrors `(H100) Fusion E2E TP2 Quick`, keeping only the payloads the two AITER backends support, and is split out of #50519 so it can be reviewed and validated on its own.

**The test could not run on AMD.** `test_tp2_ar_rms_fp8_fusions` was CUDA only and offered three NVIDIA backends, so the models and backends are now parametrized per platform and `ROCM_AITER_MLA` is added as a backend case.

**The group's third command crashed the worker.** DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite at TP2 gives 8 heads per rank, which selects AITER's Gluon MLA decode on gfx950. Past 2 GiB of KV cache per layer that kernel swaps its masked `buffer_load` for an
unmasked `global_load` and reads outside the allocation:

> Memory access fault by GPU node-4 on address ... Reason: Unknown.

The fault surfaces in whichever kernel runs next, so the traceback points at the Triton MoE rather than at the attention kernel that caused it. Reported upstream as ROCm/aiter#4490, which is open with no reproducer.

### What changed

- Models and attention backends in `test_tp2_ar_rms_fp8_fusions` are chosen per platform. On ROCm the AITER all-reduce 
  pass owns the post-AR RMS sites, so the group checks `aiter_ar_rms_fusion` instead of the native fusions. DeepSeek-Coder
  on AITER MLA runs its MoE on Triton, since AITER's MoE GEMM rejects the reduced dummy shape; Llama-3 gets 
  explicit memory limits to fit alongside the second rank.
- The group is added as a `mirror: amd:` block and as the matching legacy `test-amd.yaml` entry. Three commands, 
   60 minute  budget.
- AITER MLA refuses the Gluon decode once the per-layer cache passes 2 GiB and takes the padded persistent-scheduling 
  ASM decode instead. The bound mirrors the kernel's own `within_2gb` computation, so the fallback engages exactly where the
  unmasked path takes over.
- The builder now derives the per-layer cache size, so the hand-built builder stand-ins in `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` 
   gain the two fields it reads, and a new routing test covers the bound.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), two GPUs. The whole group, all three commands in sequence as Buildkite runs it, plus the AITER MLA routing tests the new bound affects.

## Test Result

**Group.** Passes end to end

**Gluon guard.** Above the bound the kernel faults at every KV length tried (1, 64, 128, 129, 256); below it the same shapes are clean. End to end the ASM decode lands within about 2% of Gluon.

**Routing tests.** 552 passed; the new bound test fails when the guard is removed.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Enable fused multi-step draft decode for FlashInfer trtllm-gen
author: abmfy
body:
## Purpose

#46849 runs all MRV2 autoregressive draft decode steps from one metadata build in one CUDA graph when every draft attention backend opts in. FlashInfer, the default non-MLA backend on SM100, never did, so MTP and EAGLE drafters there log

```
Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s) FLASHINFER; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.
```

and rebuild metadata and replay a draft graph for each of the k−1 draft decode steps. Draft-model speculation (`method=draft_model`) does not use this loop and is unaffected.

The trtllm-gen decode metadata holds only views of buffers the fused loop keeps current (the draft `seq_lens`, advanced in place, and the block table, fixed during the loop) plus step-invariant values, and no host plan. This PR sets `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` for trtllm-gen decode without DCP and adds a no-op `update_draft_decode_metadata`, as the Triton backends do. Native-wrapper decode (host plan), DCP (local `seq_lens` are not advanced) and XQA (SM90/SM12x, where FLASH_ATTN is the default; not validated, see #49010) keep the fallback.

## Test Plan

GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13.1, torch 2.13.0+cu132, FlashInfer 0.7.0. Serving and GSM8K: main `94d1462924` vs this PR on top of it, same precompiled wheel. Tests and EAGLE3: re-run on main `d28795f1a7` (this head) vs this PR.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_trtllm_attention_integration.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/
# EAGLE3 (Qwen3-8B) as in tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_length.py, k=3 and k=5
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size <tp> --max-model-len 32768 --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":4}'
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1000 --random-output-len 1000 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101  # c=32: --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 320 --seed 102
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --model_args model=<model>,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False
```

Serving: same node per model, 3 interleaved rounds per arm, fresh server per round, compile cache per arm, one shared FlashInfer autotune cache.

## Test Result

| check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| unit tests | new test fails (flag not set) | 12 + 21 passed |
| `mtp/qwen3_5/` (`[piecewise]` runs the fused loop eagerly) | 3 passed | 3 passed |
| fallback line (serving, MTP, EAGLE3) | logged | not logged |
| EAGLE3 k=3, 2 runs per arm | acceptance 2.2355 | same acceptance, same tokens (80/80 prompts) |

EAGLE3 runs use `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`. With multiprocessing, whether the first engine step admits one request or two varies from run to run, which flips one near-tie token in 1 of 80 prompts on main alone.

MTP k=4, output tok/s, mean ± sd over 3 rounds, Δ with 95% Welch CI:

| model | concurrency | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP1 | 1 | 613.2 ± 0.3 | 618.7 ± 1.9 | +0.9% (+0.2, +1.6) |
| | 32 | 4205 ± 47 | 4283 ± 57 | +1.8% (−1.0, +4.7) |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8, TP2 | 1 | 419.3 ± 0.3 | 429.0 ± 6.2 | +2.3% (−1.4, +6.0) |
| | 32 | 3618 ± 6 | 3677 ± 19 | +1.6% (+0.5, +2.8) |

- c=1, claimed: acceptance is identical in every round, and every PR round beats every main round. The wide 122B interval is one slower PR round (421.8 vs 431.9, 433.1).
- c=32, not claimed: batch composition, and with it acceptance, varies between rounds (35B: 3.30–3.33 on main, 3.34–3.37 here).
- GSM8K strict-match, 35B with MTP: 0.829 on main, 0.826 here (stderr 0.010).
- The saving grows with k and is zero for k ≤ 2. Only k=4 was benchmarked.

Not a duplicate: searched for `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update`, `update_draft_decode_metadata` and the fallback string. #46849 leaves FlashInfer on the fallback; #54790, #57443 and #57659 opt in other backends.

title: [Perf][MRV2] Allow FULL decode graphs for one-token prompt tails
author: njhill
body:
A one-token prompt tail over existing context runs exactly like a decode. This covers a full prefix-cache hit, a P/D KV import on the decode node, and a final one-token chunk. The scheduler may also pad such a tail with placeholder drafts to the K+1 spec-decode shape. The Mamba, GDN and KDA metadata builders already classify these rows as decodes.

Since #51865, any prefilling row made MRV2 reject the FULL decode graph for the whole batch. In P/D serving, every newly arriving request therefore pushed its step's decode batch down to PIECEWISE.

Classify these rows once, from request state, in `gather_batch_req_state`: `prefill_runs_as_decode_np` marks prefilling rows that schedule exactly one new prompt token (not counting drafts) over existing context. A batch is eligible for the FULL decode graph if every prefilling row is in this mask. Fresh prompts and multi-token chunks are still excluded, so #49918 stays fixed. PCP batches keep the old behaviour.

- Add `prefill_runs_as_decode_np` to `BatchReqState`/`InputBatch`. It is sliced for ubatches and `None` for PCP-local batches.
- Add `decode_graph_eligible` to `BatchReqState`/`InputBatch`, derived from the mask. `get_uniform_decode_token_count` now takes `decode_graph_eligible` in place of `has_prefill`.
- The autoregressive and multi-module MTP drafters use the same flag, so they match the target model's graph mode.
- `MambaHybridModelState` now clears `is_prefilling` for masked rows, replacing its own prompt-tail check from #58434. The `is_prefilling` it passes to the builders is then the single source of truth for both prefill/decode splitting and spec-decode draft counts, as suggested in review of #58434. This also covers one-token mid-prompt chunks, which the Mamba builder already ran as decodes.
- Compute the per-request draft counts once in `gather_batch_req_state` and reuse them in `prepare_inputs`.

This is an alternative / more general fix to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58374, and a follow-up to #58434 (merged), which fixed the hybrid-model correctness issue for padded prompt tails.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py
```

173 passed. New tests cover the mask classification (padded tail, one-token mid-prompt chunk, fresh prompt, multi-token chunk) and the hybrid model state passing the adjusted `is_prefilling` to the GDN builder.

Used Opus 5.5 to help with this.

title: [ROCm][DSv4][Perf] Use the shared prefill chunk plan in the ROCm sparse prefill
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_prefill` splits prefill requests into fixed groups of `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE = 4` and sizes the bf16 gather workspace from the static worst case (`N = ceil(max_model_len / compress_ratio)`, `M = N + window_size + max_num_batched_tokens`). The NVIDIA FlashMLA path already uses `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata.get_prefill_chunk_plan()` (#45061), which packs requests by workspace area and returns each chunk's real widths.

This PR drives the ROCm prefill loop from the same plan. The loop allocates the workspace per chunk as `(chunk_size, chunk_M, head_dim)` and passes `chunk_N` / `chunk_M` to the SWA gather and `combine_topk_swa_indices`, matching the NVIDIA V4 path. Steps with more than 4 prefill requests now run as fewer, larger chunks. Peak memory is unchanged: the plan's area bound equals the worst case that `forward_mqa()` already reserves during warmup. Decode is unchanged, and steps with at most 4 prefills still run as a single chunk.

`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py` has the same loop and is not changed here.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), TP=1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, main `4fb767ff0a`.

- Micro: time `_forward_prefill` on live model inputs for main vs. this PR, in interleaved blocks within one process. Each scenario is one prefill step, summed over 43 layers.
- e2e: a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm per block with the first discarded, one server on the host at a time.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 307 --random-output-len 23 --random-range-ratio 0.25 \
    --num-prompts 1021 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- Accuracy: `lm_eval --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto`, greedy, `max_model_len=4096`, `seed=1234`. The base arm was run twice.

## Test Result

**Micro** (median of 3 runs; noise floor ≤ 1.1 %):

| prefill step | chunks main → PR | main (ms) | PR (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 × 11777 tokens | 1 → 1 | 84.6 | 84.8 | −0.2 % |
| 7 × 400–1800 | 2 → 1 | 43.6 | 40.5 | +7.8 % |
| 13 × 700–1100 | 4 → 1 | 70.5 | 58.5 | +20.9 % |
| 29 × 170–430 | 8 → 1 | 67.5 | 41.4 | +63 % |
| 53 × 90–250 | 14 → 1 | 105.0 | 37.7 | +182 % |

On gfx950, part of the gain comes from larger chunks crossing the 1024-query threshold that sends them to AITER OPUS (#54855). With routing pinned to Triton, the gains are +3.9 / +5.0 / +17 / +62 %, and outputs are bit-identical.

**e2e**, 1021 prompts in 307 / out 23 (9 base / 7 patched warm runs, ranges disjoint):

| metric | main | PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 27218 | 29075 | +6.8 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 5812 | 5401 | −7.1 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 5706 | 5328 | −6.6 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 272.6 | 254.9 | −6.5 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 275.8 | 256.5 | −7.0 % |

No regression under `--max-concurrency` 96, 48 and 3 (Δ of medians, PR vs main):

| workload | warm runs | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| in 211 / out 97, 509 prompts, concurrency 96 | 6 / 6 | +0.7 % | −1.9 % | −0.8 % | −1.2 % | −1.1 % |
| in 1033 / out 131, 307 prompts, concurrency 48 | 24 / 24 | −0.1 % | −0.2 % | +0.1 % | +0.1 % | +0.7 % |
| in 1033 / out 131, 61 prompts, concurrency 3 | 6 / 6 | +0.5 % | +0.0 % | −3.4 % | −0.7 % | −0.5 % |

**GSM8K** (strict-match):

| model | main | main (repeats) | PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 0.9492 | 0.9522 | 0.9560 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (does not reach this path) | 0.7028 | 0.7028 / 0.7081 | 0.7081 / 0.7081 |

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix TileLang mHC fused RMSNorm on 64-wide wavefronts
author: djramic
body:
## Purpose

27 tests in `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` fail in the `(MI355) Miscellaneous Kernels` job added by #50519, all with the fused RMSNorm enabled:

```text
FAILED test_mhc_pre_tilelang[True-*] (8 cases)
FAILED test_deepseek_v41_mhc_pre_delayed[True-False-*] (15 cases)
FAILED test_deepseek_v41_decoder_mixes_match_torch[disabled-*] (4 cases)
```

Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13378/list?sid=01a0c82f-6637-4452-80c8-a00e9f20a69b&tab=output>

The fused-norm mHC pre kernels split 96 threads: the mix phase runs on threads 0-31, and the collapse + RMSNorm on threads 32-95. TileLang's HIP AllReduce shuffle phase ignores the thread offset of the reduction group, so on a 64-wide wavefront the RMSNorm reduction sums only half of the values. As a result, layer_input is sqrt(2) times too large. CUDA is not affected because its 32-wide warps keep the group aligned.

On ROCm, the mix phase now runs on the last 32 threads, so the RMSNorm reduction uses threads 0-63, one full wavefront. On CUDA the generated kernel is unchanged.
## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950):

```bash
cd tests
pytest -v kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py kernels/test_mhc_jit_warmup.py kernels/test_mhc_tilelang_jit.py
```

## Test Result

Before:

```text
27 failed, 154 passed, 150 skipped
```

After:

```text
181 passed, 150 skipped
```

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Give LM heads standard linear metadata
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Checkpoints that explicitly quantize `lm_head` can fail during Humming weight preparation because `ParallelLMHead` lacks the linear dimensions and bias metadata expected by quantization backends.

Retain the linear weight dimensions, partition sizes, and prefix in `VocabParallelEmbedding` before quantization dispatch, and initialize `ParallelLMHead.has_bias` before weight creation. The weight factory consumes the same dimensions exposed on the layer. Vocabulary padding, tensor-parallel sharding, and checkpoint-controlled quantization selection are preserved.

Remove the now-redundant LM-head metadata fallbacks from ModelOpt and compressed-tensors, and compute the added-vocabulary count once in the embedding constructor.

This is an alternative implementation to #48856, addressing https://github.com/vllm-project/humming/issues/70. That PR adds LM-head fallbacks inside Humming's preparation helper; this change fixes the shared layer interface so the metadata is available to all quantization backends. No Humming code changes are needed. Open-PR searches for the issue, `humming lm_head`, and `ParallelLMHead linear` found no other implementation of this shared metadata fix.

Extend the existing LM-head suite with one parametrized test comparing real quantized heads against `ColumnParallelLinear`, including bias and vocabulary padding, for compressed-tensors FP8, NVFP4A16, INT4 W4A16, and ModelOpt NVFP4 W4A16. The ModelOpt cases replace a mocked test of the removed metadata fallback.

title: [GLM5.3 Perf] Optimize glm 5.3 metadata op, 1.6~4.8x kernel level performance improvement
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

- Reuse `arrange`
- persistent GPU buffer + Triton kernel for `_build_req_id_per_token`

## Test

Acc covered by current unit test

Perf can be seen in this ai generated script

```py

import statistics
import time

import numpy as np
import torch

from vllm.utils.torch_utils import np_to_pinned_tensor
from vllm.v1.attention.backend import CommonAttentionMetadata

TOKENS = [2**i for i in range(16)]  # 1 ... 32768
MAX_REQS = 128
WARMUP = 20
ITERS = 500
ROUNDS = 5


def bench(old, new):
    for _ in range(WARMUP):
        old()
        new()
    samples = [[], []]
    for r in range(ROUNDS):
        for i in (0, 1) if r % 2 == 0 else (1, 0):
            fn = (old, new)[i]
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
            start = time.perf_counter()
            for _ in range(ITERS):
                fn()
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
            samples[i].append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1e6 / ITERS)
    return [statistics.median(s) for s in samples]


def main():
    buffer = torch.empty(max(TOKENS), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    offsets = torch.arange(max(TOKENS) + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    print(torch.cuda.get_device_name())
    print(f"Buffer: {max(TOKENS)} tokens; requests: min(tokens, {MAX_REQS})")
    print("Eager amortized wall time in us/call; initialization excluded.")
    print(
        " tokens  reqs | mapping old      new  speedup | arange old    slice  speedup"
    )

    for n in TOKENS:
        num_reqs = min(n, MAX_REQS)
        lengths = np.full(num_reqs, n // num_reqs, dtype=np.int32)
        lengths[: n % num_reqs] += 1
        starts = torch.from_numpy(np.r_[np.int32(0), lengths.cumsum(dtype=np.int32)])
        common = CommonAttentionMetadata(
            query_start_loc=starts.cuda(),
            query_start_loc_cpu=starts,
            seq_lens=torch.tensor(lengths, device="cuda"),
            num_reqs=num_reqs,
            num_actual_tokens=n,
            max_query_len=int(lengths.max()),
            max_seq_len=int(lengths.max()),
            block_table_tensor=torch.empty(
                num_reqs, 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
            ),
            slot_mapping=torch.empty(n, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64),
        )

        def old_mapping(common=common, n=n):
            starts_cpu = np.asarray(common.query_start_loc_cpu, dtype=np.int32)
            lens = np.diff(starts_cpu)
            req_ids = np.repeat(np.arange(len(lens), dtype=np.int32), lens)
            buffer.fill_(0)
            buffer[: len(req_ids)].copy_(
                np_to_pinned_tensor(req_ids), non_blocking=True
            )
            return buffer[:n]

        def new_mapping(common=common):
            # A new scheduler step must rebuild the mapping, not hit the cache.
            common._token_to_req_indices_cache = None
            return common.token_to_req_indices(buffer)

        def old_offsets(n=n):
            return torch.arange(n + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

        def new_offsets(n=n):
            return offsets[: n + 1]

        expected = old_mapping().clone()
        torch.testing.assert_close(new_mapping(), expected)
        torch.testing.assert_close(new_offsets(), old_offsets())
        m_old, m_new = bench(old_mapping, new_mapping)
        a_old, a_new = bench(old_offsets, new_offsets)
        print(
            f"{n:7d} {num_reqs:5d} | {m_old:11.2f} {m_new:8.2f} {m_old / m_new:7.2f}x"
            f" | {a_old:10.2f} {a_new:8.2f} {a_old / a_new:7.2f}x",
            flush=True,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] kpool corruption with speculative decoding
author: mmastrac
body:
## Purpose

_Partial_ fix for #56868 and #56605. See also #58704 for one more fix. These both help, but there will likely be one or two more PRs with followups.

This patch is the result of hunting down random corruption in long GLM-5.3-Flash traces.

Rejected pool-completing drafts can end up subtly corrupting the pool selection logic: When a pool-completing draft is rejected, the drafts stashed behind it have already overwritten that pool's committed keys. A pool of 4 generated tokens gets an incorrect summary key, so the indexer may skip those tokens or pick a less useful pool.

This affects any speculative method with `num_speculative_tokens >= 2`. 

Only pools built during decode (the model's own output) are affected, and only once the context exceeds `index_topk` (2048), where pools compete for selection.

The most likely place it hurts is long reasoning traces, where later thinking refers back to earlier thinking, as slightly worse long-range self-reference. This _may_ be causing specific failures in re-transcription from memory.

The ring now holds `kpool * cdiv(kpool + num_spec, kpool)` slots, and the seed and decode kernels address it by `pos % RING`. The tail slot mapping already uses the spec's block_size, so it follows. 

Encountered this locally, fix based on work in #55219 by @ivanium. This is only a surgical fix + test for this particular issue.

## Test Plan

Tests included.

Also, a standalone repro that isolates the specific bug and corruption:

| kernel | ring | pool vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 4 (current sizing) | wrong: 106 of 128 fp8 key bytes differ |
| `main` | 8 | `AssertionError` (ring must equal `kpool`) |
| this PR | 8 (`4 * cdiv(4 + 3, 4)`) | identical 

<summary>
(repro file hidden here)
</summary>
<details>

```
"""Repro: rejected speculative drafts corrupt the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer.

kpool = 4 (GLM-5.3-Flash). A spec-verify step stashes 1 + num_spec rows into
the per-request tail ring before acceptance is known. Pool W covers positions
4..7; positions 4 and 5 were accepted earlier. Step t verifies 6, 7, 8, 9
(num_spec = 3): 6 is accepted, the pool-completing draft 7 and drafts 8, 9 are
rejected. With a ring of exactly kpool slots, drafts 8 and 9 overwrite ring
slots 0 and 1, which still hold the committed keys of positions 4 and 5. Step
t+1 re-verifies from 7 and recompresses pool W from those slots.

Reference: the accepted tokens fed one per step (no speculation).
Run with RING=4 (before the fix) and RING=8 (kpool * cdiv(kpool + num_spec, kpool)).
"""
import os
import torch
from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops.kpool_compress import (
    kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache_batched as update,
)

D, P, PAGE, BLOCK, POOL_LOC = 128, 4, 64, 3, 5
RING = int(os.environ.get("RING", P))
dev = "cuda"
torch.manual_seed(0)
rnd = lambda: torch.randn(D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)  # noqa: E731
keys, gates = {p: rnd() for p in range(4, 12)}, {p: rnd() for p in range(4, 12)}
dkeys, dgates = {p: rnd() for p in range(6, 12)}, {p: rnd() for p in range(6, 12)}
ape = torch.randn(P, D, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)


def fresh():
    return (torch.zeros(4, PAGE, D + 4, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev),
            torch.zeros(8, 2, RING, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev))


def step(kv, tail, positions, K, G):
    n = len(positions)
    t = lambda xs: torch.tensor([xs], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)  # noqa: E731
    update(kv, tail, t([BLOCK * RING + p % RING for p in positions]),
           torch.stack(K).view(1, n, D), torch.stack(G).view(1, n, D), ape,
           t([POOL_LOC if p == 7 else (99 if p % P == P - 1 else -1) for p in positions]),
           t(positions), pool_size=P, head_dim=D)


def pool(kv):
    return kv.view(-1, D + 4)[POOL_LOC].clone()


kv, tail = fresh()
for p in (4, 5, 6, 7):
    step(kv, tail, [p], [keys[p]], [gates[p]])
ref = pool(kv)

kv, tail = fresh()
for p in (4, 5):
    step(kv, tail, [p], [keys[p]], [gates[p]])
step(kv, tail, [6, 7, 8, 9], [keys[6], dkeys[7], dkeys[8], dkeys[9]],
     [gates[6], dgates[7], dgates[8], dgates[9]])
step(kv, tail, [7, 8, 9, 10], [keys[7], dkeys[8], dkeys[9], dkeys[10]],
     [gates[7], dgates[8], dgates[9], dgates[10]])
spec = pool(kv)
bad = (ref[:D] != spec[:D]).sum().item()
print(f"RING={RING}: pool W matches the no-speculation reference: {torch.equal(ref, spec)}"
      f" ({bad}/{D} fp8 key bytes differ)")
```

</details>


## Test Result

All tests pass.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Emit MXFP8 from the sparse decode reduce and run wo_a as a grouped FP8 GEMM
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body: ## Purpose Follow-up to #57435. That PR moved the inverse RoPE into the sparse-decode reduce epilogue, but the reduce still writes the attention output as bf16 `[T, H, 512]` and `wo_a` then reads it back through a bf16 hipBLASLt einsum (`Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS_BH_Bias...`) on a dequantized bf16 copy of the weight. `wo_a` is weight-bandwidth bound at decode, so it pays for twice the bytes the checkpoint actually stores. This PR takes the rest of the chain the way the SM100 path does: the reduce epilogue also emits `wo_a`'s MXFP8 input directly, and `wo_a` runs as a grouped FP8 GEMM on the checkpoint's MXFP8 weight. ``` before: sparse partial -> reduce + inv RoPE -> bf16 [T,H,512] -> bf16 einsum (dequantized W) -> wo_b after: sparse partial -> reduce + inv RoPE + MXFP8 quant/scales -> grouped MXFP8 GEMM -> wo_b ``` ## What changes - **Reduce epilogue (`_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel`, `QUANT_OUT`)**: after the inverse RoPE, the fp32 row is MXFP8-quantized in registers (one E8M0 scale per 32 lanes, the `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` rounding) and stored as e4m3 plus scales. There is no bf16 write, no read-back and no standalone quant launch. - **Grouped MXFP8 `wo_a` GEMM (`rocm_mxfp8_wo_a_bmm`)**: a Triton `tl.dot_scaled` kernel for `[T, G, 4096] x [G, 1024, 4096]` on the CDNA4 MX matrix cores. It reads the e4m3 weight and per-row E8M0 scales exactly as the ROCm MXFP8 linear leaves them after loading, with no scale re-layout and no dequantized copy (the cached bf16 `wo_a` is no longer built: ~33.5 MB/layer at TP2). Tile tiers are keyed on `T * G`, tuned under HIP graphs with a cold weight. It is registered as a custom op, because the tile choice branches on the token count and `_o_proj` runs compiled. - **Prefill rows (`rocm_inverse_rope_mxfp8_rows`)**: sparse prefill still writes bf16, into a workspace slice requested together with the prefill KV gather. One pass then rotates and quantizes it into the same MXFP8 buffer, so a mixed step feeds a single `wo_a` GEMM. - **Layer (`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention`)**: on gfx950 (`on_gfx950()`), `_alloc_attn_out` returns a `QuantizedActivation` (same contract as the SM100 mega-attention layer), and `_o_proj` runs the FP8 GEMM then `wo_b`. This replaces the bf16 path on gfx950. The bf16 path remains only for archs without MX matrix cores (gfx942), where `wo_a` is BF16-emulated anyway. ## Not a duplicate - **#57081** (open) also targets FP8 `wo_a` on MI355X, but it fuses less. It runs a standalone `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` pass over the bf16 attention output and feeds AITER's `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale` after re-laying the 32x32 scales into 128x128. That keeps the bf16 global-memory round trip and adds a launch per layer. It also predates #57435: it targets `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/`, which no longer exists on main, and is marked as conflicting. This PR fuses more ops into the current path instead. The quant and scale generation live inside the #57435 reduce epilogue, and the GEMM consumes the loaded weight layout directly. The only standalone pass left is for prefill rows, which never had a fused epilogue. - **#57977** chains MXFP8 activations between DeepGEMM kernels on NVIDIA; this PR is the ROCm counterpart for the attention -> `wo_a` hop. - **#57435** is the base this builds on (merged). ## Kernel performance (MI355X, gfx950) The measured unit is the reduce plus `wo_a`. **Before:** reduce + inverse RoPE writes bf16, then the bf16 einsum. **After:** reduce + inverse RoPE + MXFP8 quant, then the grouped FP8 GEMM. Times are in µs, shown as before → after (speedup). Everything is replayed from HIP graphs, and the weight rotates across >1 GB of copies so every call is cold, as in a real step. title: [Spec Decode] Remove eager metadata rebuild during MTP fused multi-step decode
author: TheEpicDolphin
body: ## Context https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46849 added the infrastructure to fuse last N-1 draft steps into a single cudagraph for models with attention backends that support it. Currently DeepSeek V4 satisfies the conditions to enable this, when using MTP > 1. ## This PR It turns out we can remove the first attention metadata build before drafting the last N-1 speculative tokens in a fused loop. In this PR, I make the necessary changes to `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.update_draft_decode_metadata` and refactor `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` so that the first draft metadata build can be safely skipped during FULL cudagraph replay. With these changes, DSV4 + MTP no longer rebuilds metadata during proposal, resulting in a correctness-preserving removal of about 1ms of host work per decode step. No significant throughput improvement was observed from these changes. ## Profile Captured while serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP=3 on 4xGB200: **Before** **After** In the decode step above, `propose`'s CPU time shrinks by an entire millisecond. ## Benchmarks / Evals **Setup.** DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MTP with `num_speculative_tokens=3`, 4x GB200 (TP4), `--block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend deep_gemm --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Baseline is `main` at `34b069080d`; PR is `cfb93dedca`. One server per arm; trace, benchmark and eval share it. ### Speed-Bench 2K/2K (`throughput_16k`, `low_entropy`, temperature 0) Prompts scaled 8x concurrency (min 16), seed 0. title: [Sampling] Add adaptive verification support to batch-sharded sampling
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
## Context
Batch-sharded sampling does not currently support adaptive verification: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7e3d55956577605838e9babcba84dce354b0b78c/vllm/config/vllm.py#L3144-L3157

Batch sharding sizes its `all_to_all_single` splits and buffers from host-side per-request logit counts (`cu_num_logits_np`). Under adaptive verification, the per-request split of the draft budget is decided on device, so `cu_num_logits_np` only holds the scheduled counts (an upper bound), while the device `cu_num_logits` holds the admitted counts. Once the budget binds, the shard plan built on the host no longer matches the rows placed on device.

## This PR
When the draft budget binds, `reallocate_drafts` copies the per-request admitted draft counts to the host (async D2H on adaptive verification's copy stream). `shard_sampler_inputs` waits on that copy and builds the shard plan from the exact admitted counts, so the lm_head GEMM (`compute_logits_local`), the all-to-all, and the sampler run only on the rows that are actually verified. When the budget does not bind, the host counts are already exact and nothing is copied. The copy is only enabled when batch-sharded sampling is on (`copy_admitted_drafts_to_host`).

Also: the local draft count now follows the admitted budget, so with a budget of 0 every rank runs the same sampler as the replicated path.

### Tradeoff
The alternative is to keep the host's scheduled counts and pad each rank's segment up to them, which avoids any host wait but runs the GEMM, all-to-all, and sampler on the padded rows too. This PR instead adds a host wait in `sample()` on the admitted counts. It blocks the CPU only (the base model forward is already queued behind it), but it limits CPU run-ahead: the CPU cannot launch step N's sampling until the GPU has started step N. That costs ~0.05 ms per step at concurrency 1 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The cost shrinks as the forward gets longer, so it matters least for large models at high concurrency, which are the cases batch-sharded sampling targets.

## Benchmarks

**Setup.** 4x GB200, TP4 + EP, vLLM `main` @ 7e3d559565 + this PR. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}'`, `--max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 32768 --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend deep_gemm --enable-expert-parallel --no-enable-prefix-caching --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=False --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 2048}'`. Both arms use adaptive verification; the sharded arm adds `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`.

**Client.** `vllm-bench`, SPEED-Bench `throughput_2k` with placeholder prompts removed (905 prompts), max 2048 output tokens with natural EOS, temperature 1.0, `--num-warmups <conc>`, prompts = 8x concurrency (min 32, max 1024).

**Method.** Adaptive verification profiles its cost curves at every boot, and boot-to-boot differences in the curves moved median ITL by up to ~10% at some concurrencies, which swamped the effect. So the curves were saved from the first boot and loaded on every later boot (a benchmark-only patch, not part of this PR), and both arms make identical admission decisions. 4 boots in ABBA order, 2 sweeps per boot. One base boot was excluded for anomalously slow tail steps (−9 to −17% tok/s, with median ITL and acceptance normal), so n=2 for base and n=4 for sharded. Negative ITL/TPOT/TTFT is better.

| conc | tok/s base / shard | Δ | median ITL base / shard (ms) | Δ | median TPOT base / shard (ms) | Δ | mean TTFT Δ | accept len base / shard |
|---:|:---:|---:|:---:|---:|:---:|---:|---:|:---:|
| 1 | 330 / 332 | +0.5% | 9.34 / 9.39 | +0.59% | 2.68 / 2.72 | +1.5% | +0.1% | 3.22 / 3.25 |
| 4 | 960 / 964 | +0.4% | 11.43 / 11.43 | +0.09% | 3.70 / 3.66 | −1.1% | +3.3% | 3.21 / 3.17 |
| 8 | 1557 / 1550 | −0.4% | 13.20 / 13.17 | −0.19% | 4.67 / 4.61 | −1.3% | −0.6% | 3.13 / 3.13 |
| 16 | 2391 / 2405 | +0.6% | 15.15 / 15.10 | −0.31% | 6.08 / 6.08 | −0.2% | +3.2% | 3.12 / 3.14 |
| 32 | 3565 / 3536 | −0.8% | 17.15 / 17.10 | −0.31% | 8.53 / 8.40 | −1.5% | +2.3% | 3.04 / 3.03 |
| 64 | 4872 / 4874 | +0.0% | 19.97 / 19.81 | −0.78% | 12.28 / 12.35 | +0.6% | +1.3% | 2.92 / 2.93 |
| 128 | 6602 / 6558 | −0.7% | 25.09 / 24.80 | −1.12% | 18.34 / 18.55 | +1.1% | +2.2% | 2.84 / 2.84 |
| 256 | 9709 / 9676 | −0.3% | 32.17 / 31.78 | −1.21% | 24.48 / 24.66 | +0.8% | +3.7% | 2.71 / 2.71 |

**Result.** With the cost curves pinned, median ITL is consistent across boots (0.1–0.4% sd), and sharded sampling lowers it by 0.3–1.2% from concurrency 16 upward, growing with concurrency. At concurrency 1 it is +0.05 ms (+0.6%) on every run, which is the cost of the host wait. End-to-end throughput and TPOT are flat within run-to-run noise (tok/s sd 0.8–2.7%), because the median step improves while end-to-end time is dominated by slow prefill-heavy steps that sampling barely affects. Acceptance length matches at every concurrency.

I wasn't expecting to see an improvement in tok/s or TPOT, but rather to not regress it for the batch-sharded sampling cases. The main benefit of batch-sharded sampling is reducing the maximum target logits allocations by a factor of TP size from `B x (K + 1) x V => B x (K + 1) x V / P`.

### Block verification, top-p 0.95

Same setup and method as above, with `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` added to the speculative config and `--top-p 0.95` on the client, at concurrency 64-256. Cost curves pinned across boots; 4 boots in ABBA order, 2 sweeps per boot, n=4 per arm. Negative ITL/TPOT/TTFT is better.

| conc | tok/s base / shard | Δ | median ITL base / shard (ms) | Δ | median TPOT base / shard (ms) | Δ | mean TTFT Δ | accept len base / shard |
|---:|:---:|---:|:---:|---:|:---:|---:|---:|:---:|
| 64 | 4841 / 4810 | −0.6% | 20.42 / 20.07 | −1.7% | 12.37 / 12.38 | +0.1% | +1.0% | 2.96 / 2.97 |
| 128 | 6507 / 6501 | −0.1% | 25.84 / 25.18 | −2.6% | 18.54 / 18.62 | +0.5% | +3.1% | 2.89 / 2.89 |
| 256 | 9441 / 9569 | +1.4% | 32.91 / 32.02 | −2.7% | 25.08 / 24.71 | −1.5% | +2.8% | 2.72 / 2.72 |

Median ITL improves by 1.7-2.7%, about twice the gain with standard rejection sampling. Throughput and TPOT are flat at concurrency 64-128 (tok/s sd 0.7-2.5%) and improve at 256. Acceptance length matches at every concurrency. This optimization is more worthwhile when the sampling operations are more expensive.

## Testing
`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py tests/v1/sample/test_dry.py`: 80 passed. Adds `test_admitted_counts_give_unpadded_plan`, which checks that an adaptive verification batch with copied admitted counts shards identically to a batch scheduled with only the admitted drafts.

title: [CI] Share BF16 baselines across quantization comparison tests
author: aarushjain29
body:
## What

`test_fp8_per_channel.py` and `test_mxfp8.py` each boot the model twice: once unquantized to build a BF16 reference, once quantized to compare against it. Both files compute that reference from identical inputs (same model, prompts, `max_model_len`, `max_tokens`, `num_logprobs`), so the second one redoes work the first already did.

This adds a session-scoped `quant_baseline_logprobs` fixture in a new `tests/models/quantization/conftest.py` that computes each reference once per config and caches the outputs.

Only the outputs are cached. Every engine still goes through `VllmRunner.__exit__`, so test isolation is unchanged.

## Timing

Measured on MI300X, `tests/models/quantization/test_fp8_per_channel.py` + `test_mxfp8.py`:

| | Engine boots | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 10 | 425.1 s |
| After | 8 | **247.9 s** |

**177 s saved (1.71x).** It removes 2 boots but saves more than that ratio suggests because the deduplicated boots are the `[moe]` baseline (`OLMoE-1B-7B`), where load and memory profiling dominate the group.


## Not a duplicate

The only open PR touching this test group is #56870, which edits `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml` to split the job into GPTQ Marlin / AWQ / other. That splits the group across runners; this reduces the work inside it. No file overlap, and the two compose.

---

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.

body:
## Update (2026-10-13)

Adopted @NickLucche's simplification from #60368 (thanks!): the source files now match that branch exactly, carried as a commit authored by him (his three commits squashed, his sign-off kept), followed by one commit of mine adapting the tests. Relative to the earlier revision:
- draft-region identity is computed once at `register_kv_caches` into `_head_sharded_draft_regions` (via `_layer_specs`), replacing the per-region head-count list and the three per-call helpers;
- the push-mode guard lives in `NixlPushConnectorWorker` and rejects only heterogeneous TP, so equal-TP push works; the base class keeps the `tp_ratio < 0` / DCP rejection;
- `tp_mapping.compute_head_offset` carries the rank-offset arithmetic for both the target and the draft mapping.
Tests were adapted to the new structure (see Test Plan); the end-to-end results below predate this revision and were obtained with the earlier implementation of the same behaviour.

## Purpose

Fixes #58470.

NIXL P/D mis-handles a draft model's KV when **all three** hold:

1. **The target is MLA** (e.g. GLM-5.3), so NIXL maps every KV region as replicated: `total_num_kv_heads=1`, `rank_offset_factor=0`.
2. **The draft is not MLA** (e.g. DFlash2, 8 KV heads), so its KV is actually split by head across TP.
3. **Prefill TP ≠ decode TP** (e.g. a DEP8 prefill with attention TP1 feeding a TP8 decoder), so each decode rank needs a different head slice.

Drop any one and it works: an MLA draft (MTP), or equal P/D TP. `_is_region_replicated` already marks the draft regions SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer:

| where | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| handshake size check (`model_replicated = self.use_mla or …`) | rejects the correct geometry, accepts an unscaled draft block | checks draft regions as SPLIT |
| read offset (`_build_fa_remote`) | every decode rank reads draft head 0 | rank *r* reads head *r* |
| hetero-TP layout guard | skipped when `use_mla` | requires the same block-contiguous layout on P and D |

**Fix.** When the target is MLA and the draft isn't, build a second `TPMapping` from the draft's KV head count (`compute_tp_mapping(..., head_sharded_kv_heads=...)`). The draft's SPLIT regions use it for reads, size checks and the layout guard; MLA regions are unchanged. Prefill TP > decode TP and DCP are rejected with `NotImplementedError` for such drafts. Mamba, CSA-linear and MLA drafts behave as before.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches this. Related:
- #49230 (merged): checks that P and D speculative configs match; they do here.
- #54926: Gemma 4 MTP draft groups are not transferred at all.
- #57309: moves helpers out of `tp_mapping.py`; a refactor only.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py
```

New tests:
- `test_resolve_head_sharded_draft_kv_heads`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_under_mla_target_gets_gqa_offset`
- `test_handshake_mla_target_reads_draft_head_slice` (also `_block_outermost`, for BLHNC)
- `test_handshake_mla_target_rejects_unsharded_draft_block`
- `test_handshake_mla_target_rejects_draft_with_prefill_tp_above_decode`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_regions_check_layer_identity`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_push_rejects_heterogeneous_tp` (push worker)

End-to-end A/B on 2 × 8×H200 over NIXL/IB:
- **Model:** GLM-5.3 FP8 + DFlash2 (k=4).
- **Topology:** P DP8/EP8 (attention TP1) → D TP8, `LBHNC`.
- **Builds:** the same wheel (`0.30.1rc1.dev29+g711fc55c1`) with and without this change.
- **Workload:** 80 MT-Bench prompts, 256 tokens, temperature 0, following `nixl_integration/test_spec_decode_acceptance.py`.
- **Comparison:** each prompt goes once through the P/D proxy and once straight to decode (local prefill), both on the same decode server.

## Test Result

**Unit:**
- This PR: 29 / 152 / 84 / 210 pass.
- The 2 failures are `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller`, which needs 24 GiB of RAM; it fails on `main` too.
- The new tests fail on `main`.

**End-to-end:**

| | P/D over NIXL | local prefill |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | **0 / 80**: handshake `AssertionError: KV cache sizes must match … (region 99: local=32768, remote=262144)`, HTTP 500 | 80 / 80, acceptance length 3.253 |
| this PR | **80 / 80**, acceptance length **3.221**, 0 failed transfers | 80 / 80, acceptance length 3.253 |

- **Acceptance:** P/D is within 1.0% of local prefill. The upstream test's tolerance is 5%.
- **Local path:** the local-prefill counters are identical on both builds.

**Follow-up B300 validation (GLM-5.3 NVFP4 + DFlash2):**
- Ran on `research-b300-pf` with one DEP8 prefill node and four TP4 decode engines across two B300 nodes (NIXL pull, `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV).
- GPU unit suite on the PR source: **357 passed** across the four NIXL test files in the test plan.
- 2026-10-13, after adopting #60368 and rebasing onto `main` `791f92135a`: 528 passed, 2 deselected (`test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller`, the known RAM-bound test), 0 failed across the four files on B300 (2026-10-14).
- Functional gate: **42/42** requests passed; long-context retrieval passed **3/3 at ~10.8K** and **3/3 at ~66.5K** tokens. Two 12-way concurrent repeat rounds passed **12/12** each and matched sequential outputs.
- Sustained AgentX load at concurrency 8 for 900 seconds: **310/310** successful requests, **0 errors** (including 0 HTTP 429), TTFT p50 **714 ms**, ITL p50 **4.06 ms**. The aggregate export completed with exit code 0. Worker logs showed **0 NIXL transfer failures** or handshake failures.

**Scope:** GQA draft KV under an MLA target is supported in NIXL pull mode, and in push mode at equal P/D TP; heterogeneous-TP push raises `NotImplementedError` at handshake (`NixlPushConnectorWorker`).

**Not covered end to end:**
- NIXL push mode for a GQA draft under an MLA target (equal TP allowed, heterogeneous TP rejected; covered by a unit test, not run end to end);
- fp8 draft KV;
- CUDA graphs;
- other TP pairs (unit-tested: 1→8, 2→8, 1→16);
- `MultiConnector`;
- NVLink transport.

title: [KV Connector] Fix DecodeBench fp8 fill values and add a startup fill mode
author: liuzijing2014
body:
## Purpose

Two changes to `DecodeBenchConnector`, one commit each:

- **Fix fp8 fill values.** fp8 KV caches are stored as `uint8`, and the fill used `torch.full(fill_mean, dtype=uint8)`, which truncates to 0. So the dummy prompt KV was all zeros, and random fill (`fill_std > 0`) raised.
  - Plain fp8 `uint8` caches now get the fill encoded in their fp8 dtype (platform e4m3, or e5m2 for `fp8_e5m2`).
  - Random values are sampled in float32 and clamped to the finite range.
  - Packed `uint8` layouts with scales or metadata (e.g. `fp8_ds_mla`, NVFP4) keep the zero fill, now with a one-time warning.
- **Add an opt-in `startup_fill` option** (`kv_connector_extra_config`).
  - Today's per-request fill runs inside the decode steps that admit new requests. For every layer it copies block IDs to the device, filters them with a boolean mask (a device sync) and builds a temporary tensor.
  - With `startup_fill`, the worker fills the KV cache once in `register_kv_caches` and skips the per-request fill.
  - Circular-buffer groups, and attention groups whose new blocks the engine zeroes (hybrid Mamba, mixed precision), keep the per-request fill, so the dummy KV is never left as zeros.
  - The fill isn't redone after sleep mode. The default behavior is unchanged.
- No open PR covers either change. #57751, which fixes Mamba state filling in the default mode, is complementary.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py`. New tests:
  - read-back as fp8 for `fp8` / `fp8_e5m2` `uint8` caches and a `float8_e4m3fn` cache, with constant and random fill;
  - a packed layout stays zero;
  - startup fill of strided, padded and fp8 caches;
  - no per-step fill;
  - circular-buffer and engine-zeroed groups keep the per-request fill.
- KV read-back on the workers, in the default mode and with `startup_fill`:
  - `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`;
  - `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` TP4 with fp8 main KV and fp8 indexer KV.
- Decode-only A/B with `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"[,"kv_connector_extra_config":{"startup_fill":true}]}'` and `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`: a warmup, then 3 runs per mode.
  - Qwen3-0.6B on 1× GB200, 3584 in / 256 out, concurrency 4.
  - M3 TP4 GB200 (`--language-model-only --block-size 128 --max-num-seqs 88 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`), 32000 in / 256 out, concurrency 32.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 29 passed (14 new). On `main`, the fp8 cases fail with zeros or `NotImplementedError`.
- KV read-back holds 0.015625 with no non-finite values:
  - default mode: 5.3% (Qwen) and 4.4% (M3) of cache elements, i.e. the blocks the requests used. On `main` these `uint8` caches hold 0.
  - `startup_fill`: 99.5% (Qwen) and 99.99% (M3 main and indexer caches), before and after requests.
- Decode-only A/B, mean of 3 runs (min–max):

| Model | Mode | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | P99 ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B | default | 1636 (1550–1682) | 70.8 (68.8–72.5) | 2.18 (2.11–2.31) | 2.15 (2.05–2.28) | 3.03 (2.86–3.19) |
| Qwen3-0.6B | `startup_fill` | 1839 (1782–1926) | 50.0 (47.0–51.6) | 1.99 (1.90–2.05) | 1.96 (1.87–2.02) | 2.59 (2.54–2.64) |
| M3 TP4 | default | 1273 (1265–1279) | 1477 (1382–1535) | 19.39 (19.13–19.65) | 11.55 (11.53–11.57) | 218.3 (216.3–219.5) |
| M3 TP4 | `startup_fill` | 1282 (1261–1303) | 1185 (1144–1242) | 20.34 (20.09–20.82) | 11.97 (11.77–12.25) | 193.3 (191.9–194.6) |

- M3: TTFT −20% and P99 ITL −11% at the same throughput. TPOT +4.9% because more requests are in the decode phase (24.6 → 26.0).
- Smoke runs with `startup_fill` passed:
  - `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` (circular buffer, TP4): 200/200 requests.
  - `Falcon-H1-0.5B` (Mamba): 100/100 requests.

title: [Compile][CI] Honor Triton cache overrides and add AMD timeout headroom
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Preserve an explicitly configured `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` in `InductorAdaptor` so processes and model configurations can reuse matching compiled kernels.
- Retain model-local Triton defaults when no caller override is supplied, while keeping Inductor graph caches separate for each model configuration.
- Document how an empty cache becomes populated, how to export an external Triton cache, and how cold-cache tests retain isolation.
- Increase the AMD Model Executor timeout from 60 to 75 minutes in both pipeline definitions, retaining the existing 900-second pytest watchdog.

[PR #58092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58092) enabled MRV2 sampler warmup, exposing substantial kernel compilation overhead in CI.
The AMD runner already supplies a cache directory for each job, but the Inductor adaptor overwrites it with a model-specific path, causing matching kernels to compile again across configurations. Preserving the supplied directory lets the first compilation populate it naturally and later processes reuse its artifacts without prepopulation or a new environment variable. In [build 90741](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90741/list?jid=01a0cfbf-3d05-4092-b1ed-9b0f3ddb0560&tab=output), a 13m47s checkout contributed to exceeding the 60-minute job budget, motivating separate timeout headroom. This addresses cache reuse and job time limits independently of [#58452](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58452), which disables warmup in the test fixture, and [#58462](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58462), which fixes the Gumbel warmup index dtype.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, validation, and drafting this description.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Keep pinned PLE prefetch ids out of the CUDA graph pool
author: Juntian777
body:
## Problem and fix

Fixes #58441. With `engram_config.cpu_offload=True`, `Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding.start_prefetch` launches the PLE lookup on a side stream and returns; `_finalize_prefetch` joins it one decoder layer later. Qwen4Exp defaults to breakable CUDA graphs, so for PIECEWISE batches (prefill/mixed batches up to the capture size, or every batch with `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`) `start_prefetch` is an eager break and its arguments are replaced by `weak_ref_tensor`s. Two things then combine:

- `gathered_ids.record_stream(prefetch_stream)` is a no-op: with `etp_data_parallel_size == 1`, `gathered_ids` is the weak ref itself, and the caching allocator skips `recordStream` for storage it does not own.
- The only strong reference to the ids is the local `ngram_ids` in `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding.start_prefetch`, which drops as soon as it returns, while the next segment is already being captured. The graph-pool block goes straight back to the free list and the rest of the preceding decoder layer can be captured on top of it.

At replay the side stream reads the ids while the main stream may be overwriting them, so greedy outputs silently stop being reproducible.

The fix computes the prefetch ids into a persistent per-layer buffer through the existing `output=` argument of `compute_ngram_ids`. This mirrors the persistent `_prefetch_buffer` already used for the lookup output, adds no kernel or copy, and costs `max_num_batched_tokens * ngram_heads * 8` bytes per PLE layer. FULL graphs and eager runs were already safe (the argument stays a real tensor there), and ETP spanning DP is unaffected (the ids are re-gathered into a fresh tensor inside the eager break).

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py
```

- **51 passed** on GB200. The new `test_ngram_prefetch_ids_outlive_start_prefetch` reproduces the lifetime bug without a full graph capture: the prefetch stub keeps a weak ref to the ids, as the eager break does, and a fresh `MemPool` makes the next same-size allocation reuse freed storage, as a later graph segment would. On main the weak ref reads the overwritten `-1`s (3/3 runs); with this change it reads the reference ids.
- Pre-commit passed.
- No model eval: the ids are produced by the same kernel into a different buffer, so outputs only change where the race corrupted them. The reporter's cold/warm greedy table in #58441 (8/8 identical once the ids are in a persistent buffer) covers the end-to-end effect.

## Related work and AI assistance

Open-PR search found no equivalent fix. #57785 joins side-stream work during breakable capture and does not affect replay (row 2 of the table in #58441); #57497 and #58439 move or add PLE backends without changing this lifetime.

Claude Code assisted with root-causing, implementation and validation; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][EPD] Skip sampling for encoder-only async steps
author: gty111
body:
## Summary

Use `is_mm_encoder_only`, rather than the EC consumer role, to decide whether an async step needs sampling. Without an EC connector, `--mm-encoder-only` was treated as a consumer: sampling discarded the encoder output and the engine crashed with `RuntimeError: unexpected error`.

No duplicate open fix found; #58086 mentions this failure but addresses checkpoint loading instead.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -k test_async_step_skips_sampling_for_mm_encoder_only -q`: 2 passed; the encoder-only case fails on the original implementation.
- GPU smoke with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, V2 runner, no EC connector: two image requests each with async and sync scheduling. Before: async HTTP 500, sync HTTP 200. After: all HTTP 200, with zero generated tokens as expected for encoder-only serving. No full accuracy benchmark run.

Server command (repeat with `--no-async-scheduling` for the sync control):
```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
  --mm-encoder-only --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
```

title: [Kernel][Perf] Add TP=2/4/8 per-rank shapes to the sm_120 batch-invariant matmul table
author: LioEinaudi
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #57456. The `sm120` family of `_BATCH_INVARIANT_MATMUL_TUNED_CONFIGS` only covered the TP=1 shapes of Qwen3-1.7B / 4B / 8B, so with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and `tensor_parallel_size > 1` every linear layer on RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50 still ran the batch-invariant persistent matmul with the default `128x128x64 / 8 warps / 3 stages` config (the TP=2 rows in #57456's comments show the resulting ~2.9x BI overhead unchanged by the table). Now that #57586 selects the tile config from the runtime M, the table is the remaining lever for TP.

This PR adds the 41 per-rank `(N, K)` shapes of the same three models at TP=2 / 4 / 8 (`qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` and the vocab-parallel `lm_head`; `(3072, 4096)` is shared by Qwen3-8B TP=2 qkv_proj and TP=8 gate_up_proj), 15 -> 56 entries. Same structure and invariance rule as the existing entries: one `BLOCK_K` per `(N, K)`, `BLOCK_M / BLOCK_N / num_warps / num_stages` per M bucket.

## Method

Identical to #57456 (same sweep tool, same gates), one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 188 SMs, driver 580.159.04), vLLM main @ 9ef37771b, torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1: per shape 3 `BLOCK_K` x 4 `BLOCK_M` x 4 `BLOCK_N` x 2 warps x 4 stages = 384 configs x 10 M values (1 ... 2048), CUDA-event timed against the current default config and cuBLAS; `BLOCK_K` chosen shape-wide by a decode-weighted score; gate: `allclose` to an fp32 reference and the M = 1 rows **bitwise identical** to the same rows computed at M = 8 / 32 / 256 / 2048 (sha256). All 41 shapes green.

title: [Bugfix] Don't sync-police or retry FlashInfer all-reduce workspace creation in eager mode
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fix a nightly regression from #58197 ("[Core] Disable JIT warmup in eager mode").

With `--enforce-eager` the V2 `warmup_kernels` dummy forward is now skipped. The standalone FlashInfer all-reduce (`FlashInferAllReduce`, enabled by default through `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1`) creates its workspace lazily. The profile run uses large tensors that are above the FlashInfer size cap (e.g. 0.5 MB at TP8 or 2 MB at TP4 on H200), so it never touches the workspace. As a result, the workspace is first created inside the first real `execute_model`, which runs after `enable_gpu_sync_check()`. In CI (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`), `flashinfer_comm.create_allreduce_fusion_workspace(...)` then raises `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` part-way through a collective. The failure is caught and returns `None`, and `get_fi_ar_workspace` does not remember it. The mnnvl attempt fails, the trtllm fallback fails, and the collective creation keeps getting retried. Each retry leaks partially created buffers, which leads to CUDA OOM, then a deadlock, then `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` and `EngineDeadError`.

Evidence (nightly build 90589):
- H200 LM Eval DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 (`--enforce-eager`): https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90589#01a0ccda-d861-443c-bcb5-9c8b22260601. At 11:45:56 it logs `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected`, followed by repeated `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. OOM follows by 11:46:18 and the RPC timeout at 11:50:53.
- B200 HiSparse (GLM-5.2-NVFP4 TP4), job `01a0cd35-9fed-4cff-a2be-b8c4ea5fb773` in the same build, fails the same way.
- Passing build 90513 (before #58197) logs `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during warmup.
- This is likely also behind the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E failure (`rank 0 did not report UNHEALTHY within 45s`) that #58318 is bisecting. That link is not verified.

## Fix

In `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py`:
1. Wrap the one-time `create_allreduce_fusion_workspace` call in `gpu_sync_allowed()`. This covers both the regular and the quant workspace paths, since both go through `_create_workspace`. Setup syncs are expected here and are not a per-step cost.
2. Remember a failed creation (`_fi_ar_workspace_failed` / `_fi_ar_quant_workspace_failed`) so a collective creation is never retried on every all-reduce call. `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()` resets both flags.

I also considered creating the workspace eagerly before `enable_gpu_sync_check()` when warmup is skipped. That approach would have to guess the hidden size and dtype in the worker. It would also leave the retry-storm failure mode in place for any other lazy-creation failure. The change above is smaller and local to the module that owns the workspace.

## Not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --state open --search "flashinfer all reduce workspace"`, `"58197"`, `"gpu_sync_allowed"`, `"flashinfer allreduce eager"` and `"enforce-eager warmup"` returned no PR that fixes this.
- #58318 is a DNM CI-bisect probe that reverts #58197. It is not a fix.

## Test Plan / Results

GPU checks ran on an idle 8×H200 host (GPUs 0-3), using the nightly image `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:de6674b0023b...` (the same image as build 90589). For "after", the patched file was mounted over the installed one. At that commit the file is identical to current `main`.

Repro: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", tensor_parallel_size=4, enforce_eager=True)`, 3× `generate` of 4 prompts. TP4 puts the FlashInfer cap at 2 MB, so the profile run skips it, which matches the CI case.
- **Before:** `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected` (mnnvl, then trtllm), then `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. Generation still finished because this small model falls back to other all-reduce backends, so the full OOM/deadlock cascade seen with DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 did not reproduce here.
- **After:** `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during the first step. No sync errors, and output is correct (`' Paris. ...'`).

Unit tests, run in the same image with the patched files mounted:
```
pytest distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer or checkpoints"
14 passed, 17 deselected
```
The new `test_flashinfer_workspace_failure_is_not_retried` checks that a failing creation runs once (mnnvl plus the trtllm fallback) across repeated calls and runs again after `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()`.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

Not verified: the full DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 and GLM-5.2 HiSparse CI jobs themselves, and the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E job.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). @khluu will review every changed line and is responsible for the change.

title: [Bugfix][DSV4.1] Avoid host sync in ViT CUDA graph replay metadata
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 35GB) Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)` has failed on every main build since 2026-09-20 (first failure: build 90097). The failing test is `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_vit_cudagraph_image[deepseek_v41]`. Example: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90589#01a0ccda-d883-4363-b95b-3c0434c9726e

```
encoder_cudagraph.py _run_budget_graph -> model.prepare_encoder_cudagraph_replay_buffers
deepseek_v41/common/vl_cudagraph.py -> build_packed_vit_metadata
deepseek_v4/common/vision.py:282   cos = torch.cat(cos_list).to(device)
gpu_sync_debug.py:81 RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
```

CI runs with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. The encoder CUDA graph path added in #56625 syncs the host in two places. The `deepseek_v41` test entry has no `core_model` mark, so it only runs in the Extended lane, not on the PR.

1. `build_packed_vit_metadata` / `build_packed_merge_metadata` copy host tensors to the GPU with pageable `.to(device)` / `torch.tensor(..., device=...)`. The eager `DeepseekV4ViT.forward` RoPE tables do the same.
2. After (1) is fixed, `postprocess_encoder_output` fails next. It copies `types` with a pageable `.to()`, then builds the span with boolean-mask assignment (`index_put_` calls `nonzero`, which syncs).

## Changes

- `vision.py`: use `async_tensor_h2d` (pinned staging, `non_blocking`) for cos/sin, `cu_seqlens`, `merge_idx`, `merge_mask`, and the eager RoPE tables. `max_seqlen` stays on CPU.
- `vl_cudagraph.py::postprocess_encoder_output`: build the gather index on the host from `types`, which is a CPU tensor, and copy it with `async_tensor_h2d`. The span is then assembled with a single index into `[aligner rows, image_start, image_newline, image_end]`. The result is still a freshly allocated tensor, so later replays cannot overwrite it. I checked on CPU that this matches the old masked-fill output bit for bit, across several grids.

I left the eager `_build_image_span` unchanged. I also did not add `core_model` to the test entry: several other entries (step3_vl, ernie45_vl) are also Extended-only, and adding it would put a DSV4.1 model build into the per-PR Standard 4 lane. Reviewers can decide whether to promote it.

## Not a duplicate

On 2026-09-23 I searched open PRs for `deepseek v4 vision`, `vit cudagraph deepseek`, `56625`, `vl_cudagraph` and `deepseek gpu sync`. None of the results touch these code paths. The closest one, #57898, changes DSV4.1 profiling in `mm_preprocess.py` only.

## Test Plan / Results

I ran this on an H200 using the CI image `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:e9f167129c09` (main), with the patched files bind-mounted over the installed package:

```
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -v -s models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k deepseek_v41
```

- Before (unpatched image): `1 failed, 1 skipped`. It fails with the same `GPU<->CPU sync detected` in `build_packed_vit_metadata`, matching CI.
- With only the `vision.py` change: still fails, now at `postprocess_encoder_output` (`types.to(...)`).
- With both changes: `1 passed, 1 skipped` (video is skipped for this model). The log shows the encoder CUDA graph was captured and used, with no sync errors.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, mypy).

I have not run model evals. The span-assembly change is an exact rewrite, confirmed by the bit-for-bit CPU check. The H2D changes affect only how the copies are made, not the values.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. @khluu will review every changed line before merge.

title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP8 GEMM on native 32x32 block scales for gfx950
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4/V4.1 checkpoints store MXFP8 weight scales in 32x32 blocks. The
ModelOpt loader expands them to one scale row per weight row, and on gfx950
`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` then runs one generic `tl.dot_scaled`
kernel on those per-row scales. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash these linears
(`fused_wqa_wkv`, `wq_b`, the indexer `wq_b`, `wo_b`, and the shared-expert
`gate_up` and `down`) make up 11.7% of GPU kernel time per decode step at
TP2 conc32.

This PR keeps the checkpoint's 32x32 scale blocks and adds a GEMM that reads
them directly, tuned per shape for the V4.1-Flash projections. It is 1.49x
faster than the current kernel at the median, and 1.07x faster than the
native group32 GEMM in ROCm/aiter#5750 (latest head). End to end, over a
1-hour InferenceX agentx run (TP2, conc 32, DSpark x5), TPOT is 4.8% lower.

## What changes

- **`rocm_block32_gemm.py` (new):** a `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM for an MXFP8
  activation times an e4m3 weight with `[N/32, K/32]` E8M0 block scales.
  - A tiled kernel for larger M.
  - A packed kernel for small M. It fills the MFMA's rows with K panels
    instead of tokens and keeps only the matching-panel (block-diagonal)
    products, so a handful of tokens still streams the weight at full width.
  - Either kernel can split K. Normally the last program of each output tile
    sums the partials in split order within the same launch, so the result
    is deterministic and needs no second launch. A tile's splits run on one
    XCD, so they meet in its L2. The arrival counters are kept per stream.
    If a stream's first split-K launch happens inside a graph capture, it
    has no counters yet and uses a second reduce launch instead.
  - N and K are `constexpr` and M is runtime (`do_not_specialize`), so
    serving does not recompile per batch size.
  - The tile, split-K, MFMA shape and occupancy come from a table tuned on
    MI355X for the ten V4.1-Flash projections at TP2/TP4. Untuned shapes
    use a generic default.
  - It is registered as a custom op, because the config choice branches on
    M and the linear runs under `torch.compile`.
- **`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`:**
  - `process_weights_after_loading` recovers the `[N/32, K/32]` blocks when
    every 32 rows share their scales, which is exactly what the loader
    produces from a 32x32 checkpoint.
  - `apply_weights` dispatches on the scale shape, so pre-processed
    (IPC-cached) weights work either way.
  - The block-scaled path also runs `K % 32 == 0` natively. DeepSeek-V4.1's
    shared-expert `down` at TP4 (K=576) was dequantized to BF16 at load
    before.
  - Checkpoints with per-row (1x32) scales keep the existing kernel
    unchanged.
- **Grouped MXFP8 `wo_a` GEMM (#58456):** `wo_a` goes through the same
  linear kernel, so its scales are now compact too. The kernel derives the
  scale row block from the scale shape and reads either layout.

## Kernel performance (MI355X, gfx950)

The numbers go through the vLLM entry point (custom op plus table lookup).
Weights are cold (rotated past the 256 MB MALL), timing uses HIP graphs,
and every arm gets identical MXFP8 inputs. All three kernels ran in one
session.

**Current kernel -> this PR**, in µs:

| shape (N x K) | M=2 | M=16 | M=48 | M=96 | M=160 | M=192 | M=384 | M=768 | M=2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fused wq_a\|wkv (1792x5120) | 7.2 -> 4.9 (1.47x) | 7.3 -> 5.6 (1.31x) | 9.0 -> 6.7 (1.35x) | 17.8 -> 7.8 (2.27x) | 17.8 -> 9.8 (1.82x) | 18.1 -> 10.0 (1.81x) | 27.2 -> 14.6 (1.87x) | 27.2 -> 22.7 (1.20x) | 33.1 -> 31.3 (1.06x) |
| wq_b TP2 (16384x1280) | 7.0 -> 5.4 (1.29x) | 7.2 -> 5.7 (1.27x) | 13.6 -> 7.1 (1.91x) | 12.1 -> 8.6 (1.41x) | 17.3 -> 10.9 (1.59x) | 17.5 -> 11.1 (1.58x) | 25.0 -> 16.2 (1.54x) | 47.7 -> 27.3 (1.75x) | 84.3 -> 60.0 (1.41x) |
| wq_b TP4 (8192x1280) | 5.9 -> 3.9 (1.49x) | 6.0 -> 4.2 (1.41x) | 7.9 -> 5.3 (1.50x) | 8.1 -> 6.5 (1.25x) | 10.4 -> 7.5 (1.40x) | 10.6 -> 7.6 (1.39x) | 16.2 -> 10.2 (1.58x) | 24.8 -> 15.6 (1.59x) | 43.4 -> 31.2 (1.39x) |

  every point, the same as the current kernel.

## End to end

This reproduces the InferenceX `dsv41flash_fp4_mi355x_vllm_mtp` agentic job
([run 35696055681](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35696055681),
TP2 conc32). It uses the same server flags (DSpark x5, synthetic acceptance
3.51, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, cudagraph capture size 1024) and the
same aiperf client: `inferencex-agentx-mvp`, `cc-traces-weka-062126`, 10
warmup requests per lane, then a 3600 s window. The two servers ran side by
side on one node. The baseline is `main` `26f49e336a`, which includes
#58456.

| server (GPUs) | output tok/s | ITL avg / p50 / p90 (ms) | TTFT p50 (ms) | tok/s/user p50 | server TPOT avg (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| this PR (6-7) | 995.2 | 13.57 / 10.77 / 22.34 | 911 | 92.9 | 12.93 |
| **change** | **+1.1%** | **-4.7% / -2.9% / -3.0%** | **-2.8%** | **+3.1%** | **-4.8%** |

The acceptance rate is identical on both servers, so the gain comes from
faster steps: the per-step verify time drops from 47.1 ms to 45.7 ms.

- **Consistency:** an earlier run, before the rebase onto #58456, used two
  swapped server pairs. Both PR servers beat both `main` servers (TPOT
  -4.2%), so placement does not explain the gain.
- **Measured commit:** this run is at `3b46e2d306`, before the in-launch
  split-K and retune. That change only makes the kernels faster. Most of its
  gain is at small M, but at this run's decode batch (M=192) it speeds up
  `fused_wqa_wkv` by 12% and shared `gate_up` by 2-3%. So this number is
  conservative.

TP4, DSpark x5, the InferenceX `gsm8k.yaml` (5-shot, chat completions,
concurrency 128, `max_tokens=12288`, greedy), with the server flags of the
