| this PR (`c3c00323dd`) | 0.9727 +/- 0.0045 | 0.9735 +/- 0.0044 |

The scores match the baseline exactly.

## Not a duplicate

- **#57857** (open) edits the same kernel for the same model. It masks the K
  tail of the existing per-row kernel so K=576 runs natively, and it adds
  `input_quant_key()` so `wq_b` and the indexer `wq_b` can share one
  pre-quantized activation. This PR instead keeps the checkpoint's 32x32
  scales and replaces the GEMM for them. It covers K=576 as well, at 4.3 µs
  vs the current 8.7 µs at M=192. The activation sharing is orthogonal and
  composes with this. Both touch `rocm_native.py`, so whichever lands second
  rebases.
- **ROCm/aiter#5750** (open) proposes the same idea as an AITER GEMM. This PR
  keeps the kernel in vLLM, so it does not depend on an AITER release, and
  it measures on par or faster at the V4.1 shapes (table above).
- **#48427 and #57760** re-quantize MXFP8 checkpoints to FP8 PTPC. That is a
  different trade-off: it changes the weights.

## Test Plan / Results

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py -q    # MI355X
83 passed
$ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q   # MI355X
95 passed
```

New tests:

- `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_block32_matches_dequant_reference`: 7 V4.1 shapes
  at TP2/TP4, including K=576, and token counts covering the packed, tiled
  and split-K configs. The block scales must stay compact and the output
  must match an fp32 reference.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_keeps_per_row_scales`: per-row scales are not
  compacted.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_block32_split_k_in_launch`: the in-launch split-K, tiled
  and packed, with K and M tails. It must match the reference and be
  bitwise repeatable.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_block32_split_k_first_use_in_capture`: a first split-K
  launch inside a graph capture must fall back and stay correct.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_wo_a_bmm` runs with both compact 32x32 and per-row
  `wo_a` scales.

The existing tests pass unchanged. `pre-commit run` (including mypy) is
clean.

title: [Kimi-K3][Perf] Dispatch GEMM for vision patch embedder
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Purpose

Kimi K2.5/K3 passes contiguous `[patches, 3, 14, 14]` inputs to its shared vision tower. Each Conv2d call produces one output per patch, so use the existing `Conv2dLayer.forward_native` GEMM path. Checkpoint keys and output shape stay the same; the explicit output width also handles zero patches.

**Alternative considered**:  We decide not to add GEMM dispatch to `Conv2dLayer.forward_cuda` because it serves many other models with different input layouts, which might not guarantee speedup by switching to GEMM. For example, GLM5Next forms a channels-last NCHW view with `view(..., 2, 2, C).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)` before its 2×2 feature merger. A
GB300 BF16 microbenchmark of a representative 1024→4096 merger shows GEMM regression.

| Input and layout | Conv2d | GEMM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `[256, 1024, 2, 2]`, channels-last view | 58.7 µs | 72.3 µs

Hence, the dispatch should be considered carefully for each model implementation.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Use the shared prefill chunk plan in the ROCm sparse prefill
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_prefill` splits prefill requests into fixed groups of `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE = 4` and sizes the bf16 gather workspace from the static worst case (`N = ceil(max_model_len / compress_ratio)`, `M = N + window_size + max_num_batched_tokens`). The NVIDIA V4.1 paths already use `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata.get_prefill_chunk_plan()`, which packs requests by workspace area and returns each chunk's real widths.

This PR drives the ROCm V4.1 prefill loop from the same plan. As on NVIDIA, it passes `has_compressed=not swa_only`, because ratio-1 layers carry a compressed region. Each chunk's KV is a `(chunk_size, chunk_M, head_dim)` view of the single prefill workspace, which also holds the MXFP8 staging rows, and `chunk_N` / `chunk_M` go to the SWA gather and `combine_topk_swa_indices`.

The ROCm V4.1 combine runs two `torch.repeat_interleave` calls per chunk, each forcing a host sync, so steps with more than 4 prefill requests gain the most. Peak memory is unchanged: the plan's area bound equals the worst case that `forward_mqa()` already reserves during warmup. Decode is unchanged, and steps with at most 4 prefills still run as a single chunk.

The same change for DeepSeek-V4 is #58405. #56720 touches this loop and composes with it.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, main `bbd7c24d6e`.

- **Micro:** time `_forward_prefill` on live model inputs for main vs. this PR, in interleaved blocks within one process. Each scenario is one prefill step. The model is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash truncated to 6 layers with dummy weights (compress ratios 0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1), TP=1, `max_model_len=65536`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`.
- **Reach:** under the default serving config, where main selects `CompilationMode.NONE` with FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs for V4.1, `_forward_prefill` runs on every prefill step on all layers.
- **e2e:** real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=2, a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm per block with the first discarded, one server on the host at a time.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 307 --random-output-len 23 --random-range-ratio 0.25 \
    --num-prompts 1021 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- **e2e at TP=4, 1k/1k:** one server per arm (warmed, prefix caching off), `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536 --max-num-seqs 512`, `--num-prompts` = 10 × concurrency, 3 runs per point.

```bash
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio <0|0.25> \
    --num-prompts <10 x conc> --max-concurrency <512|128|32> --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- **Accuracy:** `lm_eval --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto`, greedy, `max_model_len=4096`, `seed=1234`, on real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP=2. Main was run three times and this PR twice.

## Test Result

**Micro:** sum over 6 layers, median of 3 runs, noise floor ≤ 0.9 %.

| prefill step | chunks main → PR | main (ms) | PR (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 × 11777 tokens | 1 → 1 | 18.5 | 18.5 | −0.0 % |
| 7 × 400–1800 | 2 → 1 | 16.6 | 11.6 | +43 % |
| 13 × 700–1100 | 4 → 1 | 29.8 | 15.0 | +99 % |
| 29 × 170–430 | 8 → 1 | 45.3 | 11.2 | +305 % |
| 53 × 90–250 | 14 → 1 | 74.6 | 10.3 | +621 % |

On gfx950, part of the gain comes from larger chunks crossing the 1024-query threshold that sends them to AITER OPUS (#54855). With routing pinned to Triton, the gains are +24 / +51 / +189 / +411 %, and outputs are bit-identical.

**e2e**, 1021 prompts in 307 / out 23 (6 warm runs per arm, ranges disjoint):

| metric | main | PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 14563 | 22407 | +53.9 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 11678 | 7359 | −37.0 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 11677 | 7282 | −37.6 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 502.4 | 327.9 | −34.8 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 499.0 | 329.0 | −34.1 % |

With `--max-concurrency 3`, no step carries more than 3 prefills, so every step runs as one chunk on both sides (Δ of medians, PR vs main):

| workload | warm runs | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| in 1033 / out 131, 61 prompts, concurrency 3 | 6 / 6 | −0.9 % | +2.0 % | +2.4 % | +0.8 % | +0.7 % |

The two arms' ranges overlap (p = 0.07), and within-block drift is ±1 %.

**e2e at TP=4, 1k/1k** (median of 3 runs, Δ PR vs main):

| range ratio | concurrency | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 512 | +6.9 % | −19.4 % | −19.9 % | −4.7 % | −4.5 % |
| 0 | 128 | +3.4 % | −16.9 % | −43.0 % | −1.6 % | +2.5 % |
| 0 | 32 | +2.6 % | −22.4 % | −24.0 % | −0.6 % | −0.1 % |
| 0.25 | 512 | +0.0 % | −15.8 % | +0.7 % | +0.3 % | +0.3 % |
| 0.25 | 128 | +0.5 % | −12.0 % | −0.3 % | −0.3 % | −0.2 % |
| 0.25 | 32 | −0.1 % | −6.9 % | +0.7 % | +0.2 % | +0.3 % |

With fixed lengths (ratio 0), finished requests are replaced together, so every wave of admissions is a prefill step with dozens of requests. Throughput ranges are disjoint at each concurrency, and the gain is mostly in TTFT.

With ratio 0.25, completions spread out and later steps rarely carry more than 4 prefills. Throughput and median latency are unchanged; only the opening burst gets faster, which shows up in mean TTFT.

| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (does not reach this path) | 0.7013 | 0.7081 | 0.7028 / 0.7089 |

title: [Perf][PP] Skip sampled-token broadcasts whose requests leave the engine
author: LostFox11
body:
## Purpose

Under pipeline parallelism, `PPHandler.receive`/`broadcast`/`broadcast_drafts` only skip the sampled-token collective for **non-final** prefill chunks (`compute_need_sampled_mask`). Every other sample-producing batch runs the broadcast — including final prefill chunks whose request leaves the engine right after the sample:

- Disaggregated prefill submits `max_tokens=1`, so the final chunk's single token is handed off to the decode instance and the request finishes (`FINISHED_LENGTH`) on this engine.
- The deferred consumer (`get_prev_sampled_outputs`) discards that payload via its freed-request filter anyway — non-last ranks only use the broadcast tokens to build the inputs of a follow-up step for the same request, and there is none.
- The collective still couples all PP ranks at every request boundary and contends with the next chunk's activation p2p transfer. With short prompts (e.g. 8k / 4096-token chunks = 2 chunks per request) this drain dominates and shows up as per-chunk stalls between PP stages during chunked prefill.

This PR gathers `RequestState.max_seq_len` (`prompt_len + max_tokens`) into the per-step `InputBatch` (via `BatchReqState`, alongside `prefill_len_np`) and extends `compute_need_sampled_mask` to also exclude final prefill chunks whose single sampled token reaches the request's length cap (`prefill_len + 1 >= max_seq_len`). When every sample-producing row is such a request, the mask returns `None` and all three entry points take their existing no-op path — no collective is posted on either side. Both PP ranks derive the verdict from identical per-step batch/request state, so sender and receivers always agree.

The condition is per-request and role-agnostic: it fires for `max_tokens=1` requests on dedicated prefill instances and on hybrid producer-consumer deployments alike, while any batch where a request keeps decoding on this engine retains the broadcast.

Safety property preserved: **decoding rows are never excluded.** Speculative decoding advances `num_computed_tokens` several tokens per step and can transiently overrun `prompt_len + max_tokens` while the scheduler still runs the request; predicting "this one is finishing" would freeze the earlier stages' `last_sampled_tokens`/`draft_tokens` and desynchronize the PP stages (this hazard is exactly what `test_keeps_decoding_request_past_its_length_cap` documents — that test is unchanged and still passes).

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py` — extended with:
  - `test_excludes_final_prefill_chunk_reaching_its_length_cap` (max_tokens=1 final chunk → mask `None`)
  - `test_keeps_final_prefill_chunk_with_generation_budget_left`
  - `test_length_cap_overrun_decode_row_is_kept` (decode row past its cap still broadcast)
  - `test_finishing_prefill_row_does_not_drop_a_sibling_row` (mixed batch keeps the sibling row)
  - the four pre-existing mask tests are unchanged and pass (behavior identical when `max_seq_len_np` is `None`, e.g. dummy/capture batches).
- ruff check / ruff format / mypy clean on the changed files.

## Test Result

- All `compute_need_sampled_mask` cases (4 pre-existing + 4 new) validated locally; pre-commit ruff/format/mypy/SPDX hooks pass (two unrelated hooks fail only under the local Python 3.9 toolchain — `itertools.pairwise` / `X | None` at runtime — and pass under the repo's pinned Python).
- NPU/GPU end-to-end effect (PP2×TP8 disaggregated prefill, chunked prefill request-boundary stalls removed) verified on the vLLM-Ascend deployment where this was profiled; the equivalent plugin-side change is tracked in vllm-project/vllm-ascend#17500.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fix Gemma AR+RMS prefill fallback
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose

1. Teach the AITER compilation pass to preserve raw Gemma weights and pass `gemma_norm` through the fused all-reduce op.
2. When custom all-reduce rejects a large prefill tensor, run the regular all-reduce followed by AITER's fused-add RMSNorm (the registered `vllm_aiter.fused_add_rms_norm` op, which gains a `gemma_norm` flag) instead of decomposing the norm into fp32 pointwise and reduction kernels. Keep Gemma inputs out of the QuickReduce fused RMSNorm path, which has no weight-bias mode.

On main alone, large prefill does not reach this fallback, so the speedup only shows up together with #57547, which sends prefill above the custom all-reduce pool through it.

---

## Test Plan

- Hardware: 8× MI355X (gfx950)
- Model: `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`
- Base: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-21d93d0d8c0e9627900020382bfce4730e61cab7`, each arm adds only the PRs listed; empty compile caches per run
- Serving A/B: ISL=60000, OSL=600, concurrency `{4, 32, 128}`, range-ratio=1.0
- Accuracy: GPQA diamond, 198 problems, thinking on, temperature=1.0, top-p=0.95, top-k=20, max-tokens=100000, num-threads=32. Same servers as the serving A/B.
- Unit tests:
  - `tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py` — Gemma prefill that misses 1-stage fused AR+RMS goes through regular all-reduce then `fused_add_rms_norm(..., gemma_norm=True)`, and never enters fused QR+RMSNorm
  - `tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py` — Gemma variants of the AR+RMS fusion tests; fused graph matches the unfused Gemma residual path

---

## Test Result

### Unit tests

Hardware: 2× MI355X, this PR's diff applied to the nightly above.

```bash
python -m pytest -v --tb=short \
  tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py \
  tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py \
  -k "gemma_rmsnorm_falls_back or Gemma"
```

```text
7 passed, 4 skipped
```

### Performance

Median TTFT and output throughput.

#### This PR on main

| Cell | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | Δ | tok/s main | tok/s this PR | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c=4 | 5954 ms | 5733 ms | −3.7% | 109.5 | 109.4 | −0.1% |
| c=32 | 5513 ms | 5534 ms | +0.4% | 163.4 | 159.4 | −2.5% |
| c=128 | 158478 ms | 158404 ms | 0.0% | 176.1 | 176.0 | −0.1% |

Neutral, as expected: on main the 8k prefill chunks never reach the fallback.

#### With #57547: fallback norm as separate fp32 kernels vs this PR

| Cell | TTFT before | TTFT this PR | Δ | tok/s before | tok/s this PR | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c=4 | 7035 ms | 5423 ms | **−22.9%** | 95.7 | 113.0 | **+18.1%** |
| c=32 | 6795 ms | 5266 ms | **−22.5%** | 131.8 | 169.1 | **+28.3%** |
| c=128 | 195683 ms | 151098 ms | **−22.8%** | 143.0 | 184.3 | **+28.9%** |

The separate kernels take about 0.75 ms per call against about 0.09 ms for the fused kernel. With 185 calls per 8k prefill chunk, that is about 120 ms of a roughly 550 ms prefill step, which matches the TTFT change.

#### main vs main + #57547 + this PR

title: [Chore] Use Transformers v5 names and drop redundant processor `use_fast`
author: hmellor
body:
## Purpose

Transformers v5 keeps several v4 names as aliases only. vLLM requires `transformers >= 5.10.4`, so this PR moves to the real names and prevents the old ones from coming back.

### Legacy names

| Legacy | v5 |
| --- | --- |
| `PretrainedConfig` | `PreTrainedConfig` |
| `PreTrainedTokenizer` | `PythonBackend` |
| `PreTrainedTokenizerFast` | `TokenizersBackend` |
| `BaseImageProcessorFast` | `TorchvisionBackend` |
| `XImageProcessorFast` | `XImageProcessor` |
| `transformers.image_processing_utils_fast` | `transformers.image_processing_backends` |
| `transformers.models.<m>.<module>_fast` | `transformers.models.<m>.<module>` |

- Most of the diff is the mechanical `PretrainedConfig` -> `PreTrainedConfig` rename.
- A new `transformers legacy names` rule in `tools/pre_commit/check_forbidden_imports.py` rejects imports of all of the above, including parenthesised multi-line imports and the aliased `tokenization_utils` / `tokenization_utils_fast` modules. The rule has cases in the script's `--test-regex` suite.

### Processor `use_fast`

14 models passed `use_fast=True` to their HF processor, and this PR removes it. In v5 that flag only maps to `backend="torchvision"`, with a deprecation warning. It adds nothing because:

- Without the flag, `AutoImageProcessor` already chooses `torchvision` whenever it is installed. The only exceptions are the Lanczos processors (Chameleon, Flava, Idefics3, SmolVLM) on torchvision < 0.27, and none of these 14 models use them.
- If torchvision isn't installed, forcing the torchvision backend falls back to PIL anyway.
- The flag was passed at the call site, so it overrode `mm_processor_kwargs`. That meant users could not select a backend with `--mm-processor-kwargs '{"backend": "pil"}'`.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `PretrainedConfig`/`PreTrainedConfig` and processor `use_fast` and found no overlapping work.

## Test Plan

```
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
python tools/pre_commit/check_forbidden_imports.py --test-regex
# import every changed vllm module
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py::test_processing_correctness[...]  # 18 affected models
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_bailing_moe_v3_vl.py
```

## Test Result

- Pre-commit passes, including mypy and the new rule over the whole repo.
- All changed `vllm` modules import. The exception is `vllm.models.dots3_note.nvidia.vision`, which needs CUDA flash-attention and fails the same way on `main`.
- Processing tests: 31 passed, 3 skipped. The skips were already there: two models require `transformers<=4.57` and one model is not available online.

These tests used Transformers `5.18.0.dev0`. I also checked that every new name exists in v5.10.3.

No model evals were run. Processor outputs are unchanged, and the processing-correctness tests cover every affected model that runs on v5.

author: jayzuccarelli

title: [ROCm][CI] Mirror the DSv4-Flash disaggregated DP EP group on MI355
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

**Split out of #50519.** That PR mirrors the H200 DSv4-Flash P/D accuracy group
(#42310) on eight MI355X: a TP=4 prefiller against a DP=4 EP decoder over
NixlConnector. It comes along here because the fix below has nothing to
exercise it without a group.

**The mirror repeats the parent env**, which it does not inherit, and two of
the entries have to be written even though they are empty.
`run_accuracy_test.sh` defaults the two KV layouts to HND when they are unset,
and DeepSeek-V4 packs its indexer pages beside the MLA latent pages inside each
block, so `DeepseekV4IndexerBackend` accepts only the block-outermost BLHNC and
BLNHC. With HND both engines die before they load a single weight.

**What it exposed: NIXL cannot register a padded KV allocation.** #53698 rounds
the shared allocation up to a 4096-byte page so MoRIIO can register the whole
backing as one RDMA memory region, and #54247 narrowed that to ROCm.
`register_kv_caches` decides a cache is block-major by comparing
`num_blocks * block_stride` against the registered length exactly, so a padded
allocation fails the test and falls into the segmented branch, where
`cache.nbytes % segment_bytes` kills the engine during initialization. Here the
sliding-window layer misses by a 2816-byte tail. #54021 hardened the block-copy
path against the same padding and #53974 documented the regression; NIXL was
never fixed. The path is entirely on `main`.

**The fix widens the test by one block.** The tail is shorter than a page, so
shorter than a block: it cannot hold another block and cannot make block-major
storage segmented. `storage_block_len` then comes from `block_stride`, which is
what dividing the registered length evaluated to whenever the old equality held
and which stays exact once a tail is present. Registration still uses the whole
registered length, so a connector that needs the padded allocation in one
memory region still gets it.

## Test Plan

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, with a new case that
registers the same two overlaid MLA layers on an exact and on a padded
allocation and requires identical descriptor geometry, and the new group on
8x MI355X (gfx950).

## Test Result

Unit tests go from 210 to 212 passed. The group goes from an engine that dies
in `register_kv_caches` to 2 passed with accuracy 0.9568.

title: [Perf][Rust Frontend] Make histogram observations lock-free
author: BugenZhao
body:
## Purpose

`prometheus_client`'s `Histogram` takes an exclusive `RwLock` write on every `observe`. `vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds` is observed for every token-bearing output from every Tokio worker, so with one `(model, engine)` series all workers serialize on one lock and park on the futex. On the mock engine this caps a DP=1 frontend at ~725k output tok/s, with ~1 voluntary context switch per generated token and only ~12 busy cores.

This PR fixes it at the histogram type:

- Add `vllm_metrics::Histogram`, which keeps bucket counts and the sum in atomics and derives `_count` from the buckets, so `_count` always equals the `+Inf` bucket. Observers never block each other or a concurrent scrape. `+inf`/NaN go into the `+Inf` bucket, as in the Go client; `prometheus_client` counts them in `_count` only.
- Use it for every frontend histogram through the existing `HistogramMetric`/`HistogramFamily` aliases, so call sites in `vllm-llm` and `vllm-engine-core-client` are unchanged.
- Forbid `prometheus_client::metrics::histogram::Histogram` via clippy `disallowed-types`, so new metrics don't need to pick an implementation.

Exposition format, metric names, labels, and buckets are unchanged.

Supersedes #57582, which found the bottleneck and fixed it by batching ITL observations per request. This PR removes the lock instead, so there is no flush lifecycle, tuning knob, or delayed visibility, and throughput is on par (see below). Thanks @jthomson04, credited as co-author.

## Test Plan

```sh
cd rust
cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-metrics -p vllm-llm -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-server
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

New unit tests in `vllm-metrics`:
- rendering parity with `prometheus_client`'s histogram for boundary values;
- concurrent observations from 4 threads are not lost;
- non-finite values land in `+Inf`.

The parity test's `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_types)]` also checks that the clippy rule is active.

Red/green benchmark: base `e430f7421f` vs this change on top of it. The later rebase onto `26f49e336a` touches no files under `rust/`.
- Rust mock engine (`--output-token-chunk-size 1 --vocab-size 1`) with in-tree `vllm-bench` `openai-chat`: random ISL 32 / OSL 512, `--ignore-eos`, request rate inf, 32768 prompts, 256 warmups, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS=32`.
- Affinity: frontend `taskset -c 0-55`, mock `56-69`, client `70-139` on one GB200 host.
- Runs alternate order across reps.

## Test Result

All 575 tests pass; clippy and fmt are clean.

| Shape | Base out tok/s | This PR out tok/s | Change | Vol. ctx switches / 1k tok | TTFT p99 | E2E p99 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 engine, concurrency 2048, 4 reps | 725k (714–733k) | 1,565k (1.51–1.62M) | +116% | 1044 → 9.5 | 1248 → 635 ms | 2889 → 1069 ms |
| 4 engines, concurrency 4096, 2 reps | 1,438k | 1,434k | −0.2% (noise) | 70 → 12 | 1856 → 1839 ms | 2554 → 2425 ms |

In every run, `inter_token_latency_seconds_count == generation_tokens_total − request_success_total` after drain. In an earlier matrix with the same shape, #57582 reached ~1.60M tok/s at 1 engine, on par with this change.

Mean TTFT moves slightly up with the higher request turnover (+8% at 1 engine), while TTFT p99 halves. CPU per output token is roughly flat, because the base's cost is parked time, not spinning.

title: [Perf] Parallelize registered CUDA Triton kernel warmup at startup
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Compile registered CUDA Triton startup warmup variants with native `AsyncCompileMode`
and up to four compiler threads per worker. Applying this in
`VllmTritonJitKernel.compile_many` benefits existing registered kernels without
kernel-specific changes. Warmup waits for compilation to finish and propagates
errors; an isolated context prevents older Triton versions from leaving async
compilation enabled after a failure.

Dispatch, runtime JIT, and GPU autotuning remain synchronous. The existing
`enable_jit_warmup` gate and kernel registrations are unchanged. Set
`VLLM_TRITON_JIT_WARMUP_NUM_THREADS=1` for serial warmup; older Triton versions
without the async API also use the serial path. ROCm and other non-CUDA platforms
stay serial: [AMD CI build 90984](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90984/list?jid=01a0d458-5a46-4865-a025-16d5f392dd59&tab=output)
exposed LLVM `GCNRegPressure.cpp` assertions during concurrent AMD code generation
across MI300 and MI355 jobs, with compiler threads in `make_amdgcn` and the main
thread waiting in the new async warmup context.

Duplicate check: open-PR searches for `AsyncCompileMode` and parallel Triton
warmup found no equivalent implementation. This is separate from #58452's CI
fixture default and #56683/#56761's TileLang-specific warmup.


Three added tests cover real parallel compilation and synchronous runtime JIT,

## Test Result

- Focused GPU suite before the CUDA-only guard: **112 passed**.
- After the guard, the three existing fake-kernel host tests passed using:
  `.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup_triton_launcher.py::test_failed_parallel_warmup_does_not_leak_into_runtime tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup_triton_launcher.py::test_autotuning_warmup_stays_serial tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup_triton_launcher.py::test_triton_launcher_supports_compile_and_runtime_adapters -q`.

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] BF16 splitk kernel for sparse MLA decode
author: simondanielsson
body:
## Purpose Decode rows in the bf16 sparse MLA path go through the ragged **prefill** kernel, whose grid is `(q_len, heads_blocks)`. GLM-5.3-Flash at TP8 has one head block, so during decode with concurrency 4 launches only 4 workgroups on 256 CUs. Clearly underutilized. This new kernel instead uses splitK+reduce over the context dim, i.e. with a grid `(q_len, num_kv_splits, heads_blocks)`. DSv4 has a similar one. title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Disagg] Allow MoRIIO HMA per-layer block_len
author: avininjamay8
body:
## Purpose

MoRIIO KV cache registration under HMA requires a uniform `block_len` across attention layers. Hybrid models (GLM-5.2 DSA, MiniMax, Gemma4) register layers with different per-layer `block_len` / `block_size` (e.g. `9216` vs page default `2112`). Registration then raises:

```
ValueError: MoRIIO KV cache block length mismatch for layer ...: 9216 != 2112
```

and PD bring-up fails at health-gate. Layer transfers already size RDMA from per-layer geometry; the uniform check is stricter than the transfer path.

## Changes

`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py` (KV registration):

- Allow divergent per-layer `block_len` (bytes) always; log at debug per layer; advertise `max(block_lens)` to the peer with a single summary `logger.info`.
- Allow divergent `block_size` (tokens/page) **only when hybrid KV cache manager (HMA) is enabled** (Gemma4 SWA/full-attn from #53721). Without HMA, still raise on any `block_size` mismatch (including when `block_len` also differs — ChuanLi's case).
- Per-layer spam logs moved to `logger.debug` (okorzh).

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py`:

- divergent `block_len` allowed
- divergent `block_size` rejected without HMA
- size+len both differ still rejected without HMA
- divergent `block_size` allowed with HMA (Gemma4)

## Test Plan

### Unit

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py -k 'register_kv_caches_allows_hybrid or register_kv_caches_rejects_divergent or register_kv_caches_allows_hma' -q
```

title: [Kernel][DSV4.1] Fuse MoE finalize into the TP all-reduce + mHC boundary
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

DSV4.1 decode (TP4, `0 < M <= 16`, FULL CUDA graphs) closes every sublayer with a fused TP all-reduce + mHC kernel. After an MoE, that boundary is preceded by FlashInfer's MoE finalize (top-k weighted sum) and a separate shared-expert add. This PR folds the finalize and the shared add into the boundary:

- **Vendored FlashInfer LL kernels.** `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/` copies FlashInfer's CuTe DSL low-latency MNNVL all-reduce (`flashinfer/comm/mnnvl_cutedsl/kernel_ll`, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer@139af6f6, the H5120 presets):
  - `_SharedOnlyPublishDeviceKernel` and `_group_leader_block_sum` are byte-identical to upstream.
  - `_QuadFinalizePublishDeviceKernel` is upstream's plus an `fp32_weights` option. DSV4.1's router emits FP32 top-k weights with the routed scaling folded in; FlashInfer loads BF16.
  - `_LamportMHCDeviceKernel` is upstream's `_LamportResidualRMSNormDeviceKernel`. Its residual add and copy are replaced by the mHC post-mix of the hc streams (stored as the new residual) and their pre-mix collapse, which the unchanged RMSNorm then normalizes. This replaces `torch.ops._C_custom_ar.all_reduce_mhc` (#57643) on the overlap path. That CUDA kernel has no other user, so this PR deletes `csrc/libtorch_stable/all_reduce_mhc.cu` and its CMake entry. #57643's boundary wiring (`reduce_results`, `fuse_mhc_all_reduce`, `supports_mhc_all_reduce`) is kept and reused.
- **MoE left unfinalized, via #58635.** For layers whose experts are the modular TRTLLM MXFP4 ones, DSV4.1 requests deferral once at model build with `moe_config.defer_moe_finalize(MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS)`. Per call, `should_defer_moe_finalize(M)` picks the path, and the experts return a single `UnfinalizedMoEOutput`. This PR touches no fused-MoE code.
- **DSV4.1 wiring (model file only, no new runner).**
  - A layer defers when its successor opens with the fused boundary: 37/40 layers on DSV4.1-Flash. The last layer and the layers before an engram layer finalize as before.
  - `DeepseekV4MoE.forward_unfinalized` runs the runner's `_forward_impl` directly, since the custom op returns tensors only. It hands `MoEOutput(routed=UnfinalizedMoEOutput, shared_output=...)` to the next layer.
  - `mhc_shifted_post_pre` calls `AllReduceMHC.finalize`, so top-k reduce, shared add, all-reduce and mHC post/pre run as two PDL-chained kernels.
  - Outside FULL graphs (eager/PIECEWISE), the next mixes run inline instead of on the side stream.
  - `MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS` (16), the side-stream design and the M > 16 path are unchanged.

Duplicate check: #58635 (merged) supplies the modular-path deferral this builds on. #52601 (MoE tail all-reduce fusion for MiniMax-M3, last updated 2026-09-02) targets a different model and kernel. No open PR fuses the DSV4.1 MoE finalize into the mHC boundary.

## Test Plan

Unless noted, everything below is on main 378504a544 (includes #58635) plus this change, with main's pins: flashinfer 0.7.0, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130. Hardware is DSV4.1-Flash on TP4 GB300.

- Kernel regression test: `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py::test_all_reduce_mhc_matches_unfused_path`, which replaces #57643's CUDA-kernel test. It checks against the unfused math in torch (FP32 rank sum → BF16, mHC post FMA chain → BF16, collapse → BF16, RMSNorm). Run as `pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py` with ray workers; all 51 tests in the file passed on 4× GB300. It covers M in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 16}, visited in shrinking and growing order, ±0 sentinel inputs, CUDA graph replay with mutated inputs, and the finalize path with padded/permuted rows and an invalid (−1) route.
- `pre-commit run` (ruff, typos, SPDX, forbidden imports, test tethering, mypy 3.10) and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual` on the changed files.
- In-engine numerical check (ad-hoc patch, not in this PR) under FULL CUDA graphs.
- E2E perf, `vllm bench serve`: random 1024 in / 256 out, `--ignore-eos`, concurrency 1/4/8/16.
- Accuracy with mqa, using the eval config of this model's existing recipes. GPQA-Diamond runs at concurrency 16 so decode batches take the fused path.

Server: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`. GPQA used `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384` instead. The baseline arm is the same tree with deferral disabled, so both arms share the new all-reduce + mHC kernel and differ only in the MoE finalize.

## Test Result

**Correctness**
- Regression test: PASSED.
  - Post-mixed hc streams: bit-identical to the torch reference.
  - Fused-finalize path: bit-identical to an FP32 FMA-chain reference fed through the same collective.
  - Normalized layer input: within 1 BF16 ULP of the torch reference. The RMSNorm is FlashInfer's, which sums the squares in another order and uses an approximate rsqrt.
  - Before the CUDA kernel was deleted, an earlier revision of this test compared against it directly: the hc streams were bit-identical and the normalized input was within 1 ULP.
- In-engine, FULL graphs: on each rank, the fused boundary was compared against the plain collective run on a torch finalize of the same buffers, inside the same graphs. Over a GSM8K run, 51,393 fused boundaries ran per rank, of which 1,295 were host calls (eager or capture) and the rest graph replays. Both the post-mixed hc streams and the normalized input matched bit-for-bit: 0 of 1.6e10 elements differed, on every rank.
- Before the rebase, an eager check over 55,500 deferred MoE calls found the deferred GEMM2 rows plus an FP32 top-k sum bit-identical to FlashInfer's own finalized output.

**E2E decode.** Random 1024/256:

| concurrency | median ITL base → PR (ms) | median TPOT base → PR (ms) | output tok/s base → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.14 → 5.03 | 5.15 → 5.05 | 174.7 → 177.8 (+1.8%) |
| 4 | 5.71 → 5.56 | 5.71 → 5.58 | 581.7 → 591.7 (+1.7%) |
| 8 | 6.30 → 6.17 | 6.30 → 6.15 | 1069.7 → 1089.8 (+1.9%) |
| 16 | 7.19 → 7.13 | 7.36 → 7.64 | 1818.6 → 1817.6 (flat) |

At concurrency 16, TPOT moves with prefill interference, so median ITL is the steadier number. Over every c=16 sweep in this work, base median ITL ranged 7.19–7.39 ms (4 sweeps) and fused-finalize 7.13–7.24 ms (5 sweeps, including kernel iterations before the mirror). The pre-rebase sweep measured c=16 at +3.0% throughput.

**Kernel level** (before the rebase; the kernel file is unchanged). One decoder layer, two boundaries each followed by a sublayer, in µs. Each arm is timed as the slope between CUDA graphs of 8 and 40 calls, max over ranks, median of 50 replays:

| M | sublayers only | before (CUDA all_reduce_mhc, MoE finalizes itself) | CuTe LL, MoE finalizes itself | this PR (fused finalize) | Δ vs before |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 38.19 | 48.59 | 48.15 | 45.28 | −3.31 |
| 4 | 70.91 | 82.50 | 81.43 | 79.22 | −3.28 |
| 8 | 105.36 | 117.61 | 116.34 | 111.61 | −6.00 |
| 16 | 171.30 | 186.22 | 184.91 | 180.26 | −5.96 |

**Accuracy**

| eval | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (5-shot completions, greedy, n=1319, concurrency 16), 3 runs each | 0.9295 / 0.9287 / 0.9272, mean 0.9285 | 0.9249 / 0.9287 / 0.9265, mean 0.9267 |
| GPQA-Diamond (chat, thinking, temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, 57344 tokens, 4 epochs), exact match / pass@4 | 0.9040 / 0.9545 | 0.9066 / 0.9444 |

- Two GSM8K runs of the same code differ on about 46 of 1319 questions, so a single run has an SD of about 0.35 pt.
- Before the rebase, 13 base runs and 20 runs across fused-finalize variants averaged 0.9275 vs 0.9238. A control whose finalize rounds exactly like the unfused path (bit-identical per-rank contribution) trailed by the same amount. The per-question shift was diffuse (net about 5 of 1319, none consistently broken). So that gap was not the fused arithmetic; my best guess is timing-dependent batching, but it is unexplained. On this rebase it is 0.18 pt over 3 runs each.
- GPQA-Diamond: 0 request errors and no empty answers in either arm; 6 (base) and 1 (PR) of 792 generations hit the token cap. pass@4 differs by 2 of 198 questions. The pre-rebase pair was 0.904 vs 0.904. This model's dashboard history for the same config (4-epoch runs) has median 0.909 and IQR 0.906–0.913.

## Notes

- Like upstream, `_QuadFinalizePublishDeviceKernel` reads the routing metadata before `griddepcontrol.wait`. That is safe only if the preceding GEMM2 triggers its dependents after its own wait. The graph-mode check saw no mismatch; a wait-first variant measured about 0.08 ms/step slower at concurrency 1 (on a different node) with no accuracy difference.
- Moving the prenorm GEMM + Sinkhorn onto the critical path instead of the side stream was measured: +17–20 µs per decoder layer at M = 1–32, with the mixes inline or with TileLang's fused post + prenorm GEMM. So the side stream stays.

title: [Bugfix] Keep JIT warmup under enforce-eager when fault tolerance is on
author: njhill
body:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58197 disabled JIT warmup in eager mode. Fault-tolerant deployments run peer-fault detection against deadlines, and in-inference Triton compilation latency spikes can delay detection past the deadline: the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E job became flaky right after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58197 landed (rank 0 misses the test's 45s detection deadline when the injected
fault trips while kernels are still compiling mid-serving).

Keep `enable_jit_warmup` on when parallel_config.enable_fault_tolerance is set, so kernels compile during startup warmup instead of during serving.

title: [Perf] Reduce redundant Triton sampler warmup specializations
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Remove redundant integer-alignment specializations for `BATCH_SIZE` in the Triton top-k/top-p kernel and `ROUND` in the split top-p step kernel. Both retain Triton's value-1 specialization. Pointer/row-stride alignment, sampling modes, split counts, and warmup input enumeration remain unchanged.

This reduces the measured sampler warmup plan from **120 to 92 compile keys** without changing corresponding generated instructions. It is independent of #58582's parallel compilation. Unlike #45601's runtime warmup-coverage changes and fully dynamic `BATCH_SIZE`, this only removes duplicate alignment variants, preserves `BATCH_SIZE=1`, and also reduces `ROUND` variants. Open-PR searches found no equivalent alignment-only change.

## Test Plan

```bash
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py::TestTritonTopkTopp -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py
```

Additional standalone checks compared cold compilation, corresponding SASS, exact sampler outputs, CUPTI latency, runtime compile-key coverage, and Qwen3-0.6B generations. GPU work used `chg` reservations.

## Test Result

- **94 existing tests passed**; changed-file pre-commit checks passed.
- **556 sampler cases matched bit for bit**, including normal/sparse/tied/nearly-equal/peaked logits, four vocab sizes, batches 1–512, row padding, and offset views. The 540 aligned-base cases added no runtime compile keys after warmup. Offset views retain the baseline's existing pointer-alignment warmup gap.
- **112 runtime timing cases**: median change approximately zero; worst slowdown 1.03% (0.192µs). Three alternating repetitions of 80 CUPTI samples, CUDA graphs, cold L2, and identical input/output/scratch addresses. Timings include the common logits reset required for in-place masking.
- Every baseline warmup key maps to identical SASS in the reduced set for **SM103, SM100, SM90, and SM80** (480 matched key pairs). Only B300 was executed; other architectures were compiled only. ROCm/XPU were not tested.
- Qwen3-0.6B on one B300, V1 runner, Triton sampler, JIT warmup enabled, normal torch.compile and CUDA graphs: **384 tokens across 16 requests matched exactly** for greedy and seeded top-k/top-p/combined sampling; no inference-time JIT warnings. Serial JIT warmup for this 8-sequence configuration fell from 24.26s to 21.72s.

Cold compilation on B300 / Xeon 8559C, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1; vocab 128256, max sequences 256, no speculative tokens. Both configurations use four native compiler threads, independent empty caches, and two repetitions in reversed order. Times exclude imports and plan enumeration.

| Configuration | Compile keys | Run 1 | Run 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 120 | 21.18s | 21.07s |
| This patch | 92 | 15.65s | 15.60s |

**23.3% fewer compile cases and about 26% less compilation time**, additive to parallel warmup. Provider counts: monolithic 20→12, statistics 20→20, step 60→40, mask 20→20.

title: [CI] Split (B200) Miscellaneous Kernels into mHC, FLA Ops and Misc named jobs
author: Thangnguyenvn98
body:
## What

`(B200) Miscellaneous Kernels` runs 31–41m of wall time on recent `main`, and two workloads take up most of it: the mHC tests and the `flash_linear_attention` ops tests. This moves each group into its own folder and runs it as a named job, `(B200) mHC Kernels` and `(B200) FLA Ops Kernels`. The root catch-all stays as it is on `main` and adds `--ignore`s for the two new folders.

## Old

```
kernels-root-misc-test-b200   "(B200) Miscellaneous Kernels"   timeout 45
├── pytest kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py
└── pytest kernels/ --ignore=<7 dirs> --ignore=<9 root files, incl. test_mhc_kernels.py>
```

## New

```
tests/kernels/
├── mhc/                                  (new)
│   ├── test_mhc_jit_warmup.py            <- tests/kernels/
│   ├── test_mhc_kernels.py               <- tests/kernels/
│   └── test_mhc_tilelang_jit.py          <- tests/kernels/
├── fla/                                  (new; all import vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops)
│   ├── test_fla_layernorm_guard.py       <- tests/kernels/
│   ├── test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py       <- tests/kernels/
│   ├── test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py   <- tests/kernels/
│   └── test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py <- tests/kernels/
└── test_*.py                             (remaining root files, unchanged)

kernels-mhc-test-b200         "(B200) mHC Kernels"             pytest kernels/mhc   timeout 25
kernels-fla-ops-test-b200     "(B200) FLA Ops Kernels"         pytest kernels/fla   timeout 25
kernels-root-misc-test-b200   "(B200) Miscellaneous Kernels"   pytest kernels/ <main's --ignores> --ignore=kernels/fla --ignore=kernels/mhc
                                                               timeout 45 -> 30   (key retained)
```

The old key `kernels-root-misc-test-b200` becomes itself (narrowed), plus `kernels-mhc-test-b200` and `kernels-fla-ops-test-b200`. Nothing else references the key. Every file is claimed exactly once. All three jobs keep the old device, `source_file_dependencies` and triggers.

## Notes

- **The catch-all still collects the root, so new root files keep running by default.** An earlier version replaced the `--ignore`s with an explicit file list (#58608, now closed); review preferred keeping the catch-all.
- **mHC isolation holds.** `test_mhc_kernels.py` still never shares a process with the FlashInfer-importing root tests. The two other mHC files import only mHC and TileLang warmup modules, and none of them load FlashInfer at import time. `test_mhc_tilelang_jit.py` runs last in its folder and restores the `sys.modules` stubs it installs.
- **Moves are renames only.** The one content change: `mhc/test_mhc_tilelang_jit.py` now finds `kernels/scripts/check_no_tilelang_hijack.py` via `Path(__file__).parents[1]`. The docstring path in `vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/cpu.py` follows the move.
- Cross-PR: AMD mirror work in #50519 and #58654 builds on this layout. A `pytest kernels/ --ignore=...` copy on another lane needs `--ignore=kernels/fla --ignore=kernels/mhc` to avoid running these folders twice.

## Expected runtime and overhead

The file-list version of this split ran each group whole in one process in build [91058](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91058). This version runs the same files in the same groupings, so those measurements carry over. The one difference: the two small mHC files (well under a minute together) moved from Misc to mHC.

| job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| mHC Kernels | ~12.4m | ~13m | ~0.7m | container setup / checkout |
| FLA Ops Kernels | 6.0m | 6.7m | 0.8m | container setup / checkout |
| Miscellaneous Kernels | ~14m | ~15m | ~1.0m | container setup / checkout |

- **Slowest job:** Misc at ~14m pytest, under the 20m target.
- **Aggregate:** ~35 worker-minutes vs a ~34 median for the old job. **About +1 against the ≤20 budget**, from two added container setups.
- A validation build on this head will be posted in the comments.

AI assistance: this change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); I have reviewed every changed line. Local verification: `yaml.safe_load` on `kernels.yaml`, `py_compile` on all moved files, and `check_test_tethering.py --all` (exit 0).

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Anchor the partial-tail lookup on the full-attention prefix
author: nvyutwu
body:
## Purpose

Split out of #57216 per @orozery's review (part 1 of 2): the lookup half. The DCP store half is #58619.

`_lookup` anchors the partial-tail search on `_lookup_complete_chunks`, which requires *every* KV cache group to have a complete chunk at the anchor boundary, including the recurrent groups. A recurrent `align` group holds state only where a scheduler step ended on one of its block boundaries: in practice at the producer prompt's last full recurrent block and at its tail.

With **uniform block sizes** (dcp=1, the only shape `supports_partial_tail` admits today) the last-full-block boundary is also a full-attention chunk multiple, so that aligned row lands on the chunk grid, `complete_hit` reaches it, and the existing one-window probe finds the tail. The anchor only fails when that row is missing, e.g. evicted separately from the tail. So on `main` today this is a robustness fix.

With **mixed block sizes** -- under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp x` the attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8) -- the aligned row sits at a recurrent multiple that is essentially never a full-attention multiple. `complete_hit` is then 0 for any prompt past the first chunk, the search is capped at one window from zero, and a correctly stored tail further out is never probed although it is resident. That is the state #58619 (the DCP store side) would land in without this PR: tails get stored, but only those within one window of the complete-chunk hit are ever found -- the "#58619 only" column of the hardware table below. **This PR is the prerequisite for #58619's lookups to work.**

Instrumented `_lookup` on a replay (chunk 12288, hash 128), before the change:

```
n=12620  complete_hit=12288  complete_boundary=12288  max_boundary=12544
           boundary=12544 ALL GROUPS HIT                  <- restores
n=15136  complete_hit=0      complete_boundary=0      max_boundary=12160
           boundary=12160 group=0 MISS ... 11776 MISS     <- tail stored at 15104,
                                                            never probed
```

Fix: anchor the partial-tail search on the boundary the full-attention groups proved, which `_lookup_complete_chunks` already returns (since #63566), and check recurrent groups only at the candidate boundary. Per review, the search runs from one window past the anchor down to the complete-chunk hit and skips block-aligned boundaries (complete chunks, which the complete-chunk lookup already missed), so a longer full-attention prefix stored by another request cannot hide this request's own tail. If a full-attention chunk between the complete hit and the anchor is still being loaded, the search falls back to the complete hit. No second lookup and no new parameters.

The reported hit is never shorter than the complete-chunk hit, so the change can only widen what a lookup reports. Pending full-attention chunks are handled exactly as in the complete-chunk lookup on `main`.

## Test Plan

Unit tests on the existing dcp=1 hybrid fixture (`_make_partial_tail_scheduler`: 16-token full-attention and Mamba blocks, hash 4):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

- tail found with no recurrent state at the chunk boundary (30-token prompt, tail at 28)
- the same across **two** complete chunks (46-token prompt, tail at 44): the production shape, where the complete-chunk anchor is 0
- a longer full-attention prefix stored by another request does not hide this request's own tail, including when that prefix covers the whole prompt (per review)
- the load path requests only the verified chunk keys plus the tail keys
- `max_num_new_tokens` caps which tail the search may report
- a tail is found after a GPU prefix hit
- 0 when no tail was stored; 0 when the full-attention chunk is not resident
- the tail is preferred over an aligned recurrent state at the chunk boundary
- the search falls back while the anchor chunk is being loaded

## Test Result

**Unit tests** (`pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/`, GB300, same image), base `main` @ e318ac0979:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | 690 passed, 3 failed |
| this PR | 707 passed, 3 failed |
| this PR + #58619 | 721 passed, 3 failed |

The 3 failures are the same on `main` at this commit: `test_partial_tail_store_uses_attention_and_recurrent_cow_sources` and `test_eagle_partial_tail_round_trip_serves_mamba_checkpoint[True/False]` expect a recurrent group's CPU `BlockStored.block_size` of 0, which is 4 since #62613. `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes.

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-2b009fc6`; "fix" overlays the branch's `vllm/`, "main" is the stock nightly). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP2, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. "fix" is this PR + #58619.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| prompt tokens | DCP1: `main` | DCP1: fix | DCP2: `main` | DCP2: fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1541 | 1536 | 1536 | **0** | **1536** |
| 12549 | 12544 | 12544 | 12288 | **12544** |
| 24069 | 24064 | 24064 | **0** | **24064** |
| 39685 | 39680 | 39680 | 38912 | **39680** |

- **DCP1:** identical to `main` on every prompt (no regression).
- **DCP2:** every prompt restores to its last hash boundary.
- **All trials:** replayed greedy output (32 tokens) is identical to both the cold run and a GPU-prefix-cache replay, with 0 allocation failures. The same numbers reproduced on a second GB300 cluster on the previous rebase.

<details><summary>Earlier revision, per PR (TP4, DCP1/DCP4), measured before the review changes</summary>

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-29468dde8b` with only `offloading/scheduler.py` replaced). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP4, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. Recurrent block 512, full-attention offload block 2048 at DCP4 (512 at DCP1), hash 128: the K3 shape (1536 / 12288 / 128) scaled down.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| prompt tokens | best boundary | DCP1: `main` | DCP1: this PR | DCP4: #58619 only | DCP4: #58619 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 645 | 640 | 640 | 640 | 640 | 640 |
| 2309 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 |
| 2565 | 2560 | 2560 | 2560 | **0** | **2560** |
| 2949 | 2944 | 2944 | 2944 | **0** | **2944** |
| 3717 | 3712 | 3712 | 3712 | **0** | **3712** |
| 4101 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 |
| 4485 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 |
| 17029 | 17024 | 17024 | 17024 | **0** | **17024** |
| 2949, replay diverges at 2700 | 2560 | 2560 | 2560 | **0** | **2560** |

- **DCP1:** this PR is identical to `main` on every trial, including store and load bytes. That is the expected no-regression result: the aligned row is on the chunk grid there, so the anchor equals `complete_hit`.
- **DCP4:** without this PR, only tails within one window of the complete-chunk hit are found. With it, every prompt restores to its last hash boundary.
- **All trials:** replayed greedy output is byte-identical to the cold recompute (32 tokens), with 0 allocation failures and no errors in the server logs.

</details>

An earlier run of the combined change on a 2-node GB300 K3 deployment (TP8/DCP8) is in #57216.

## Notes

- Related: the DCP store-side half is in #58619. Both are standalone and merge cleanly together (verified; the merged tree passes the suite).
- Not duplicating an existing PR: #52832 fixed the analogous producer-side gap for the Mooncake connector; #52397 covers the `max_offload_tokens` cap in the store path, which this PR does not touch. #63566 also uses the full-attention boundary, to pin a shared-prefix junction for the next request; this PR uses it to find a tail that is already stored, so they are complementary.

title: [Perf][DSv4] Fuse inverse RoPE + FP8 quant into FlashInfer sparse MLA
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

FlashInfer 0.7.0 (already pinned) ships the TRTLLM-GEN DSv4 sparse-MLA **RopeQuant** epilogue (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4918): the kernel applies the inverse RoPE to the attention output and casts it to FP8 with packed UE8M0 scales, in the layout DeepGEMM's `fp8_einsum` consumes. This PR uses it on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` for DeepSeek V4, so `wo_a` reads the kernel's FP8 output directly instead of a bf16 `[T, 128, 512]` output plus a separate `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` pass.

It mirrors the pattern the DSv4.1 FlashMLA mega-attention layer already uses (`_alloc_attn_out` returning a `QuantizedActivation` that `_o_proj` consumes whole).

### Changes
- `DeepseekV4Attention` gets an `_alloc_attn_out` hook. The default stays the padded bf16 buffer (still head-sliced before `_o_proj`), so the FlashMLA, SM120, ROCm, XPU and CPU layers are unchanged.
- `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttention` allocates RopeQuant's buffers. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` now also takes a `QuantizedActivation`: it skips `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` and feeds the kernel's FP8 output and scales straight to `fp8_einsum`.
- The launcher requires the output's group stride to equal `sum_q` (it has no stride field for O), so a token slice of a shared buffer is rejected. Both the decode and prefill calls therefore span the full, CUDA-graph-padded buffer and select their tokens through `cum_seq_lens_q`; the prefill call's offsets are not rebased. Rows outside `cum_seq_lens_q` are never read or written (checked with garbage pad rows under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`).
- `build_flashinfer_mixed_sparse_indices` gains `num_rows` so it can size its outputs for those rows while computing only the real tokens.
- **DSpark non-causal decode (bugfix, affects the unfused path too).** The kernel treats every entry of its active index ranges as a key: the first `min(128, pos + 1)` columns (the query's causal SWA window) and `[128, sparse_topk_lens)`. `-1` is not skipped. DSpark's non-causal decode rows were copied in as one contiguous run with `sparse_topk_lens` set to the full row width. So the `-1` padding past the run was attended as keys, and with fewer than 128 context tokens the causal window also cut out the later block tokens. The builder now fills each row's causal window with the first visible entries, puts the rest from column 128 on, and sets `sparse_topk_lens` to exactly that. Every draft token then sees the whole block at any context length. Because the decode call passes real `seq_lens`, RopeQuant's derived positions match `positions` for the draft too. This is the DSv4 counterpart of #57432, which fixed the same two problems for DSv4.1 only; DSv4 reads neither of the metadata fields it added. #57432 presents each draft token as its own sequence with the full request length. RopeQuant cannot use that, because it derives RoPE positions from `seq_lens`. So this change keeps the real `seq_lens` and lays out each row around the query's causal window instead.

### When it is on
Automatically, with no flag, when all of these hold:
- exactly 128 local query heads (DSv4-Pro at TP1 or with DP attention). The kernel has one fixed 128-head schedule; padding fewer heads up to 128 measured slower;
- per-tensor FP8 KV cache;
- FP8 `wo_a`.

DSv4 has 8 heads per `wo_a` group at every TP size, so 128 local heads always means the kernel's 16 × 8 layout. That is DSv4-Pro at TP1 or with DP attention; Pro at TP2–16 and Flash have fewer heads and keep the existing path.

This includes the non-causal DSpark draft. The one inexact case is a draft block running past `max_model_len`: the draft clamps its positions there and RopeQuant does not reproduce the clamp, which only affects those drafts.

Everything else keeps the existing path.

## Not a duplicate
I searched open and closed PRs for RopeQuant, `dsv4_inv_rope_cos_sin_cache`, flashinfer#4918, and fused inverse-RoPE/FP8 on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`. No PR wires this epilogue into vLLM. The nearby DSv4 PRs (#57679 query RMSNorm+MXFP8, #57977 MXFP8 activations between DeepGEMM kernels, #55459 indexer Hadamard) touch different paths. #57432 (merged) fixed the DSpark non-causal FlashInfer layout for DSv4.1 only; the DSv4 fix here is the counterpart, done differently so RopeQuant can apply (see Changes).

## Test Plan
- **Unit (new):**
  - `test_flashinfer_rope_quant_matches_unfused_o_proj` runs one mixed step (two decodes, a three-token prefill, and three CUDA-graph pad rows) through the real `_forward` + `_o_proj`, fused and unfused, and compares the `wo_a` output.
  - `test_flashinfer_dspark_noncausal_block_sees_future_tokens[0|20|127|900]` runs a DSpark non-causal block (q_len 4) through the DSv4 layer. It checks each draft token against a reference over its full visible set (context window plus the whole block), then checks that the fused output projects like the unfused one. Without the fix it fails at both contexts it was run at (20, 900); the kernel probe below shows the old layout off at every context tried.
- **Existing suites:**
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py`
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py`
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py`
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`
- **Kernel microbenchmark** (standalone script, not included): decode under CUDA graphs, fused vs bf16 attention + `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant`, on 1×GB300.
- **E2E accuracy A/B**, as described in the results below.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files, including mypy.

## Test Result
**Tests:** all pass on GB300. `test_flashmla_sparse` 19/19, `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla` 33 passed and 8 skipped, `test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible` 28/28, `test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` 82/82 (on the first commit). pre-commit passes. The suites ran on a checkout of the parent commit (09fe178dba) plus this change; none of the 12 commits between it and the branch base touch these files.

**Kernel probe for the index layout:** FlashInfer called directly with a 4-token block per request, compared with a torch reference over the full visible set. With per-token split rows the max error is 0.008–0.029 at contexts 0, 1, 20, 100, 126, 127, 128 and 900, the same level as ordinary causal rows (0.008–0.02). The old contiguous rows are off by 0.09–0.6 at every context.

**E2E accuracy** (first commit; no DSpark), DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, DEP8 over 2×4 GB300 (tp 1 per rank, so 128 local heads), `--attention-config.backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, MegaMoE. The two arms are identical except that the baseline loads a clean worktree of the same HEAD. The fused arm logged `fuses the inverse RoPE and FP8 quant` on every node; the baseline did not.

| gsm8k 5-shot greedy, completions (n=1319), flexible / strict | 0.9530 / 0.9538 | 0.9545 / 0.9553 |
| aime25 ×4, temperature 1.0, max_tokens 98304 (n=120), exact_match | 0.9667 | 0.9833 |
| aime25 pass@4 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| request errors | 0 | 0 |

The gsm8k gap is 2 of 1319 questions, inside greedy batching noise. The aime25 gap is 2 of 120 samples at temperature 1.0, and both arms solve every problem at least once.

**E2E with DSpark** (the index-layout fix plus RopeQuant on the draft), same setup plus `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'`. The baseline is the same clean worktree (old layout, unfused). Acceptance comes from `vllm:spec_decode_*` snapshots on both nodes around each eval, and per-position acceptance from the whole run.

- Acceptance length rises 19.5% on gsm8k and 15.9% on aime25, in line with the +20% #57432 measured for the same fix on DSv4.1.
- Every draft position gains, and the gain grows with depth, from +3% at position 0 to 2.6× at position 6.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Fuse small-batch WO-A with inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant on SM100/SM103
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

On SM100/SM103, the DSv4.1 O-projection runs four kernels per layer. At decode batch sizes the first three are latency-bound and together take 11-12 µs on GB200 (DSv4.1-Flash, TP=4):

```
before: attn_out ─▶ [Triton] inverse RoPE + per-32 FP8 quant ─▶ [DeepGEMM] fp8_einsum wo_a ─BF16─▶ [FlashInfer] MXFP8 quantize ─▶ [FlashInfer CuTe-DSL] wo_b
after:  attn_out ─▶ [FusedWoAKernel] inverse RoPE + quant + wo_a + MXFP8 quant ──────────────────────────────────────────▶ [FlashInfer CuTe-DSL] wo_b
```

This PR adds `FusedWoAKernel`, a CuTe-DSL kernel that replaces the first three and hands `wo_b` a pre-quantized `QuantizedActivation`, so `wo_b` skips its own quantize. Each cluster owns 128 `wo_a` output rows and each of its CTAs one head of K (split-K by heads per group); at TP=4 that is 128 CTAs per token tile in clusters of 8:

1. **Weight prefetch under PDL:** before `griddepcontrol.wait`, each CTA TMA-loads its 64 KiB FP8 weight slice and TMA-loads its packed weight scales, overlapping the attention kernel. The MMA warp transposes the scales into the `tcgen05.cp` layout before use. TMEM is allocated after the wait, since a PDL predecessor may still hold it.
2. **Inverse RoPE + quant into SMEM:** the CTA reads its head of the BF16 attention output, applies inverse RoPE to the last 64 dims, quantizes per 32 elements with UE8M0 scales, and writes straight into the swizzled SMEM MMA operand, with no global round trip.
3. **Pipelined block-scaled MMA:** `tcgen05` MXFP8 MMA with the weight as the 128-row operand and tokens as N, accumulating in TMEM. Each 128-wide K stage has its own mbarrier, so the MMA starts on a stage once its weights land and its activations are quantized; the last stage triggers `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` for `wo_b`.
4. **Split-K reduce + output quant:** partials are reduced over DSMEM (each CTA reduces a subset of tokens), rounded to BF16 like the unfused `z`, and quantized to MXFP8 in FlashInfer's F8_128x4 scale layout, including the zero padding FlashInfer's quantizer writes.

The latest kernel update preloads the RoPE coefficients across tokens to overlap global loads, narrows two CTA barriers to the 128 TMEM readers, and uses `redux.sync.max.abs.f32` for output amax. Explicit `mul.rn.f32` / `fma.rn.f32` preserves the prior RoPE rounding order; split-K accumulation and BF16 rounding are unchanged.

`dsv41_o_proj(layer, attn_out, positions)`, which the FlashMLA and FlashInfer backends call directly, takes the fused path on SM100/SM103 when each group has at most 8 local heads (one portable cluster), `o_lora_rank` is a multiple of 128, `wo_a` is per-32 FP8 and `wo_b` is FlashInfer CuTe-DSL MXFP8. The pushed head supports 1–32 tokens. The local extension measured below supports 1–96 when `n_local_heads * (o_lora_rank // 128) <= 128` (DSv4.1-Flash TP4/TP8), retaining 1–32 for TP1/TP2. Other batches and unsupported layouts use `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`. Mega Attention retains its own output-projection path.

The extension keeps each compute tile at most 32 tokens and adds token tiles in the launch grid. For T65–96 it balances three tiles in multiples of four (24/28/32 tokens per tile). Scale stores use the global token row within the existing 128-row F8_128x4 layout; the extension preserves split-K accumulation and BF16 rounding.

The kernel follows the `VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel` warmup contract. The FlashMLA and FlashInfer SM100/SM103 backends register it at construction, and warmup compiles every token count accepted by dispatch: 32 on the pushed head, and 96 for eligible shapes in the local extension (all 96 TP4 keys compiled in 54.11 s in the earlier extension check): target graphs, DSpark draft graphs and eager batches land on different counts, so covering the whole range keeps runtime compile-free. `_wo_b_proj` keeps pre-quantized activations off GEMM-RS, which only runs from 128 tokens.

The kernel binds `amax`, `exponent` and `inv` before its output stage. vLLM imports `quack`, which rewrites `if const_expr(S) or D:` process-wide into a constexpr if; without the binding, token counts whose input stage takes the dynamic path (3, 5, 6, 7, 9, ...) fail warmup with `TYPE_UNSTABLE_JOIN` inside a server even though they compile in isolation.

Why not DeepGEMM: its 26/09 release lets `fp8_einsum` emit FP8 with packed UE8M0 scales from the GEMM epilogue, which covers only the third kernel and can only feed a DeepGEMM `wo_b`. It has no hook on the A-operand side, so the inverse RoPE + quant cannot be fused into it.

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for `wo_a`, `fused wo_a`, `DSv4.1 o_proj`, `inverse RoPE MXFP8`, `fused_inv_rope` and `o_proj cutedsl`. #57977 (draft) also targets the `wo_a` to `wo_b` handoff, but keeps `fp8_einsum`, has it emit MXFP8, and moves `wo_b` to DeepGEMM; this PR instead collapses the whole pre-`wo_b` chain into one kernel for small batches. Both touch the same call sites; if #57977 lands first, the fused kernel could emit DeepGEMM's packed scale layout for that `wo_b` instead. #58621 changes DSv4, not DSv4.1.

## Validation

The fused kernel should cut decode latency at small batch sizes without changing what the model produces. The kernel microbenchmark below was rerun on the local 96-token extension based on `4f59bdde4b`, against the unfused path unchanged from merge-base `e33de821c0`; rows 97–128 were added on the PR head `813bcd4042`. The serving benchmark, the DSpark GSM8K run 3 and the concurrency-16 GSM8K run 4 were run on the PR head `813bcd4042`; the other acceptance, GSM8K and GPQA results are retained from the earlier PR revision, before the latest kernel optimization and token-range extension.

### Serving / model evaluation setup

- **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.0, CuTe DSL 4.7.1; both sides share one venv built from the merge-base's precompiled wheel and the same kernel caches.
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).
- **Topology:** TP4 (no expert parallel), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` attention.

### Kernel microbenchmark

One NVIDIA GB200; DSv4.1-Flash TP=4 per-rank shape, BF16 `[T,16,512]` with token stride 32768 elements, FP8 weights `[2,1024,4096]`. FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, CuTe DSL 4.7.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132, CUPTI 13.3.1. The unfused and fused production kernel entry points run in the same process with default PDL settings. CUPTI measures the span from first kernel start to last kernel end, using CUDA graphs and cold L2. Every token count uses 7 alternating rounds × 500 iterations per path; each value is the median of the round medians. Compilation and warmup precede timing. The timed chain includes inverse RoPE, per-32 FP8 input quantization, WO-A GEMM, and MXFP8 output quantization; WO-B is excluded. This is a single-GPU measurement of the TP4 rank shape, not a distributed serving benchmark.

```bash

  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \

```

### Acceptance and GSM8K accuracy

Each run uses the full GSM8K test set (1,319 identical 5-shot completion prompts) with greedy decoding, concurrency 32, a 1,024-token output cap, and strict answer extraction, served with the benchmark configuration above. Runs 1 and 2 are two passes on one server; run 3 is one pass on a later head (DSpark: `813bcd4042`; no speculative decoding: `2ea0e22a47`). At concurrency 32, DSpark verifies 6 × 32 = 192 target tokens (and drafts 5 × 32 = 160) per step, past the 96-token fused limit, so DSpark runs 1–3 reach the fused kernel only in the last requests. Run 4 is one pass on `813bcd4042` at concurrency 16, where every decode-only step takes the fused path (6 × 16 = 96). DSpark uses 5 speculative tokens, and acceptance is read from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over each run.

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base, DSpark | 93.03% / 92.57% / - / - | 3.470 / 3.473 / - / - |
| PR, DSpark | 93.03% / 93.33% / 93.33% / 93.86% | 3.469 / 3.477 / 3.472 / 3.475 |
| PR, no speculative decoding | 93.03% / 92.42% / 92.95% / 93.10% | - |

- Every PR run at concurrency 32 is within 0.61 points of a base run, the largest spread between two repeats on the same server; run 4 at concurrency 16 scores 0.83 points above the best base run. These results establish parity with the base; they do not claim an accuracy improvement.

### GPQA Diamond

PR, TP4 without speculative decoding, `--max-model-len 1048576`; 198 problems, 0-shot chat completions, thinking on with the default (high) reasoning effort, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, 262,144-token output cap. Score **91.92%** from a single run (standard error about ±1.9 points); all 198 responses finished with `stop`, with a median of 2,134 and a maximum of 53,922 completion tokens.

### Tests


title: [MoE] Defer the TRTLLM-Gen top-k finalize on the modular path
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

#53152 lets the monolithic TRTLLM-Gen experts stop after GEMM2 (`do_finalize=False`) and hand an `UnfinalizedMoEOutput` to a consumer that fuses the top-k reduction into its own kernel. On `main`, a layer asks for this by setting `FusedMoEConfig.defer_moe_finalize`, optionally capped by `defer_moe_finalize_max_num_tokens`. This PR brings the same mechanism to the modular path, which models with their own router use (DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP4 MoE, for one).

- **Experts.** `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular`, `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsModular` and `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular` (block FP8 and MXFP8) return the unfinalized output when `moe_config.should_defer_moe_finalize(M)` holds. `TrtLlmBf16ExpertsModular` is left out: it only runs with all2all kernels, which never defer.
- **Requested through a method.** Layers call `moe_config.defer_moe_finalize(max_num_tokens=-1)` instead of assigning the flag and the cap; the flag becomes private. Kimi-K3's runner moves to it, with the same behavior. A layer requests deferral only after checking that its quant method's `experts_cls` is one of these TRTLLM-Gen experts, as Kimi-K3 already does; other experts ignore the request. Deferral also now requires `hidden_dim == hidden_dim_unpadded`, since a consumer can't strip hidden-dim padding from GEMM2 rows.
- **The request is a hint; `should_defer_moe_finalize(M)` is the answer.** Each launch permutes into its own buffer, so a call the MXFP4 or NVFP4 experts would split across launches can't be deferred. When built, those experts lower `defer_moe_finalize_max_num_tokens` to their single-launch size. A call above it finalizes as before, and `should_defer_moe_finalize(M)` returns `False` for it. The model asks before calling and takes the matching path, so it never gets an output form it didn't expect. For DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's MXFP4 experts (384 experts, top-k 6), that single-launch size is 86,868 tokens.
- **Modular kernel.** `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl` passes the unfinalized output through and skips `finalize`, but only when `prepare_finalize.supports_deferred_moe_finalize()` holds. That method moves up from the monolithic prepare/finalize base to `FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize`. `MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular` opts in, since its `finalize` is only the top-k weight-and-reduce.
- **Types.** `FusedMoEKernel.apply` now returns `torch.Tensor | UnfinalizedMoEOutput`, like `apply_monolithic`. So do `FusedMoEMethodBase.apply`, `RoutedExperts.forward_modular`, and the `apply` of each quant method whose oracle can pick one of these experts.

No layer requests deferral for modular experts yet, and Kimi-K3 behaves as before, so this changes no behavior on its own. The first consumer is #58586 (DSV4.1: MoE finalize fused into the TP all-reduce + mHC boundary), which will be restacked on this PR.

**Duplicate check.** #52601 (MiniMax-M3 MoE tail all-reduce fusion; last updated 2026-09-02) carries the same modular-kernel pass-through, NoDPEP opt-in and NVFP4 modular deferral, next to its model-specific tail. This PR splits out the shared part and adds the MXFP4 and FP8 experts and the `FusedMoEKernel.apply` return type, with no consumer, so #52601 and #58586 can both rebase onto it. No other open PR touches modular-path deferral.

## Test Plan

On GB300 (SM103), FlashInfer 0.7.0 (`main`'s pin), torch 2.13.0+cu130:

- New tests share `check_deferred_moe_finalize` in `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py`. Each builds the kernel for one rank of a TP group, as production does, and runs it. It then calls `defer_moe_finalize()` with no token cap and runs it again, checking three things:
  - the deferred output, reduced with `moe_unpermute` (TRT-LLM's finalize kernel), equals the first run's output bit for bit;
  - modular experts hand back the router's FP32 weights unchanged;
  - for MXFP4 and NVFP4, a forced chunked run finalizes, bit-identical to the non-deferred run, and `should_defer_moe_finalize` reports it.
  - `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_trtllm_mxfp4_deferred_finalize` (modular, plus one monolithic case)
  - `tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py::test_trtllm_fp4_moe_deferred_finalize`
  - `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py::test_trtllm_fp8_block_moe_deferred_finalize` (block FP8 and MXFP8)
- Regression: `tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py`, `test_flashinfer.py`, `test_trtllm_bf16_moe.py`, `test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py` and `test_ocp_mx_moe.py`, minus the two kernel sweeps that call FlashInfer directly. Also `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py` and `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py::test_deferred_finalize_enabled_before_moe_kernel_setup`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files (ruff, typos, SPDX, forbidden imports, test tethering, mypy 3.10), and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.

## Test Result

- New tests: 11/11 passed (MXFP4 modular ×3 and monolithic ×1, NVFP4 ×3, FP8 ×4 across block FP8 and MXFP8). The deferred output reduces to FlashInfer's own finalized output bit for bit in every case, and forced chunked runs finalize as `should_defer_moe_finalize` reports.
- Regression: all passed except failures that also occur on `main` (36f94d5fe8) on the same stack:
  - `test_trtllm_fp4_moe_no_graph` at the 704/4096 shapes, and with RELU² at 2048/1536, misses `atol=rtol=0.2` on 2–21 elements, out of up to 262144, against the torch reference.
  - `test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py` raises `NotImplementedError: Must use persistent kernel and be TMA-compliant for native MXFP` from triton_kernels on SM103.
- pre-commit (including mypy 3.10 and 3.12): passed.
- No model eval: nothing sets the knob for modular experts yet. #58586 will carry the DSV4.1 perf and accuracy results.

title: [CI] Shard (H100) Helion Kernels five ways
author: Thangnguyenvn98
body:
## What
Raise `(H100) Helion Kernels Shard %N` from 2 to 5 hash shards of the whole `kernels/helion/` directory, so each shard stays under the 20-minute target. The MI250 mirror is pinned at its current 2 replicas so the new base count does not multiply it.

## Old
```
kernels-helion-test       parallelism: 2   pytest kernels/helion/ --shard-id/--num-shards
  mirror amd (MI250)      inherits 2
```

## New
```
kernels-helion-test       parallelism: 5   pytest kernels/helion/ --shard-id/--num-shards   (command unchanged)
  mirror amd (MI250)      parallelism: 2   (explicit; unchanged behaviour)
```

## Notes
- No coverage change: same command on the same directory, and no filters before or after. Only the replica count changes.
- The directory has ~1,970 run cases per build. Each of 5 shards gets ~390, so no shard is empty.
- A named semantic split was considered and rejected. `test_rms_norm_per_block_quant.py` is about half of the job's pytest time on its own, so it would need a monolith split before it could fit in one job.
- Legacy `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` is untouched.

## Expected runtime and overhead
Predictions based on recent `main` builds (e.g. [91049](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91049), [91027](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91027)):

| Job / replica | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before: shard 1–2 (each) | ~34–40m | ~40–46m | ~1–10m | `pip install helion`, image pull when cold |
| after: shard 1–5 (each, predicted) | ~14–16m | ~15–17m | ~1m warm | same, now paid 5× |

- Baseline → new: ~81 → ~86 worker-minutes (predicted). That is about **+5 extra worker-minutes**, within the 20-minute budget, and comes from three extra setups.
- Slowest shard: ~16m pytest (predicted), inside the 20m target.
- Why 5: 4 shards would put each at ~19.6m of pytest with no headroom for hash skew or run-to-run variation.
