author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Add MI355 mirrors and matching native AMD jobs for mHC, FLA Ops, and Miscellaneous Kernels.
- Preserve the existing exclusions and supported AMD coverage across 32 test files; NVIDIA commands are unchanged.
- Fix two DeepSeek-V4.1 CSA2 assertions to compare the query in its required `[tokens, heads, head_dim]` shape.
- Read logical k-pool K and scale bytes through the platform cache layout in the writer-parity and rejected-draft tests.

[#50519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50519) established AMD coverage for the miscellaneous-kernel group, and [#58609](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58609) split the NVIDIA workload into three named jobs. Two CSA2 tests compared the returned `[19, 1, 512]` query with a flat `[19, 512]` fixture, although the three-dimensional shape is required by attention. The k-pool test read contiguous bytes even though ROCm preshuffles K; its pool-1 slice contained none of that pool's K bytes. Reading the correct offsets showed 122 of 128 pool-1 K bytes differed from the reference, confirming the one-pool ring check. The production kernels are unchanged.

title: [Perf][Frontend] Share orjson responses across render and pooling
author: Levius-Fubuki
body:
## Overview

Use shared `create_json_response()` in `api_utils.py` for render, embedding, token-embedding and generic pooling responses. Encode with orjson, including native NumPy input, and simplify hf3fs now that orjson is a required dependency.

Fix #44997. Latest head: `7f06159438` (token-embedding changes in `913437ee00`), including the [integration request](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58660#issuecomment-6333029142) for token embeddings introduced by #61772.

## Claims

- Accept Pydantic models, sequences of models and ready dictionaries. Preserve error statuses, explicit success statuses, integer keys and JSONResponse fallback for unsupported values such as opaque integers outside 64 bits.
- Reuse the helper across the affected render/pooling routes. Keep schemas, vector shapes, late-chunking field omission, usage accounting and binary streaming behavior unchanged. Plain Response objects retain load accounting until response completion.
- Avoid Python-list expansion for native NumPy embedding matrices. Earlier local measurements also show substantially faster serialization of large multimodal render responses; these are microbenchmarks, with no final-orjson end-to-end latency claim.

## Validation

All results below were agent-run. Latest local environment: Apple M3/macOS ARM64, Python 3.12.13, Pydantic 2.13.5, orjson 3.13.0 and PyTorch 2.14.0.

- **85 focused unit tests passed** after syncing main, across token-embedding late-chunking, API-utils, pooling-utils and scoring IO-processor suites. Coverage retains float32, bfloat16, non-contiguous matrices, optional late-chunking metadata and per-document ranges. Updated response tests use real serving/config/renderer constructors and replace only the external engine client. Obsolete response-class parameterization and render spies are removed.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Uncount stop-trimmed spec tokens from num_computed_tokens
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

When a speculative decode step stops on an accepted draft (EOS, a stop token, or `max_tokens` reached before the bonus token), `_update_request_with_output` trims the step's later tokens, but `num_computed_tokens` keeps counting them. Rejections are rolled back in `update_from_output`; trimmed tokens are not.

Ordinary requests are freed right after the stop, so the count is never read again. A resumable (streaming-input) request continues: `_update_request_as_session` uses `num_computed_tokens` as the fold boundary, so the next chunk starts "already computed" over positions whose KV belongs to the trimmed drafts.

Prompt `[1, 2, 3]`, `max_tokens=2`, k=2. The prefill samples `10`; a step with drafts `[11, 12]` returns `[11, 12, 13]` (both accepted) and stops at `11`. Folding in the next chunk `[7, 8]`:

| | `all_token_ids` | `num_computed_tokens` | next step computes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | `[1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 7, 8]` | 6 | `8` only; `7` reuses draft `12`'s KV |
| this PR | `[1, 2, 3, 10, 7, 8]` | 4 | `7, 8` |

The fix uncounts the trimmed tokens, so `num_computed_tokens` again covers all new tokens but the last kept one. The fold then drops that token exactly as it drops the final sampled token of a non-speculative turn, which is what makes a session's output identical with and without speculative decoding (see the GPU check below).

Under async scheduling the trimmed tokens' placeholders were never released either (`num_output_placeholders` was decremented by the post-trim count), so they are released too. `num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders` is unchanged, so neither the async `cache_blocks` frontier nor the `C - P` frontier from #58259 moves.

This count is also what stale block-hash truncation keys on (#52806, and the `del session.block_hashes[num_computed_tokens // hash_block_size:]` suggested on #58259): with the overshoot, the cut point lands too late and leaves stale hashes behind.

Diffusion schedulers inherit the change; resumable diffusion requests were not exercised.

## Not a duplicate

- #44526 clamps `num_computed_tokens` to `num_prompt_tokens` after the fold. That catches only an overshoot past the whole new chunk (`num_new_tokens <= 0`); in the example above it is a no-op and `7` is still skipped. This PR fixes the count where it goes wrong.
- #58259 (merged) fixed the async handoff race. Its `C - P` frontier also covers this case under async scheduling, but not under sync scheduling, where `num_output_placeholders` is always 0. This PR keeps `C - P` unchanged, so the two compose.
- #54979 caps its terminal `cache_blocks` call at `request.num_tokens` to work around the same overshoot; the cap stays correct.
- Searched open and closed PRs and issues for streaming input + speculative decoding, `num_computed_tokens` trimming, and `_update_request_as_session`; no other PR fixes this.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding -v
```

New test: `test_next_chunk_fully_computed_after_stop_on_accepted_draft` (scheduler, sync and async scheduling): after the trimmed stop, the fold drops the last kept token and the next chunk is scheduled in full.

GPU check, run manually and not kept in CI: a 6-chunk streaming session (opt-125m, fp32 + FLEX_ATTENTION, greedy, `max_tokens=2` per chunk) must produce the same tokens and logprobs with and without ngram speculative decoding (k=4), with drafts accepted. The greedy tokens of this repetitive prompt do not change with the context, so logprobs are what catch the difference.

## Test Result

- Scheduler test: the sync case fails on main and passes with the fix. The async case passes on main since #58259 and is kept to check that this PR's `C`/`P` accounting still composes with it.
- `test_scheduler_streaming.py` + `test_scheduler.py` + `test_async_scheduler.py`: 221 passed.
- `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input` (CPU): 797 passed. The 1 failure and 6 errors (`test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e`, `test_scheduler_e2e`) need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU on GB200:
  - Streaming session check, main: diverges from the second chunk on, e.g. logprobs `[-0.3593, -0.5455]` with ngram vs `[-0.3427, -0.7063]` without.
  - Streaming session check, this PR: tokens match and logprobs agree to ~1e-5; `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py` passes.
  - Async spec-decode regression check (the placeholder accounting change applies to every async spec request, not only streaming): `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding` passes, all 6 configs (sync/async, preemption, chunked prefill, mp/uni executor) match the non-speculative baseline in outputs and logprobs.
  - `ngram` is not yet supported by Model Runner V2, so the streaming session check uses the V1 model runner. The fix is in the scheduler and runner-independent. Async scheduling is covered by the scheduler test only.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Paged MXFP4 sparse indexer on aiter's MQA-logits kernel
author: cagrikymk
body:
## Summary

Adds a ROCm (gfx950) path for DeepSeek V4.1's indexer with an MXFP4 K cache, built on aiter's paged MXFP4 MQA-logits Gluon kernel. The CUDA path is unchanged. There are two modes:

- **Regular MXFP4** (`indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"`): dense logits over the whole context, read straight from the paged K cache.
- **Sparse MXFP4** (opt-in, also set `indexer_sparse_logits=True`): the candidate source takes block maxima from the same pass that writes its logits, and the consumer layers score only the candidate pool instead of the whole context. Steps whose contexts are too short for the pool to pay off keep the regular pass, so it helps mainly at long contexts.

Both modes:

- The logits kernel reads the preshuffled paged K cache in place, so no K gather is needed, prefill included.
- K is written to the cache by aiter's `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache`, and Q is quantized by `q_rope_mxfp4_quant`.
- Each prefill chunk is packed into one launch through `query_start_loc`. Uniform spec-decode steps run as `next_n`-row sequences, with the decode schedule built once per step.
- 128-token KV pages are preferred.

In sparse mode, the candidate pool is resolved once per step and shared by every consumer layer.

Requires aiter with the paged MXFP4 MQA-logits kernel and the cache ops (merged to aiter main) (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5834)

## Tests

- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`
- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py`

## Performance

## Benchmark: C=32, 128 prompts of 350K tokens, 350 out, spec. decoding = 5+1

| metric | tot_baseline | mxfp4_dense | Δ | mxfp4_sparse | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| total tok/s | 19,225 | 22,796 | +18.6% | 24,863 | +29.3% |
| output tok/s | 19.21 | 22.77 | +18.6% | 24.84 | +29.3% |
| requests/s | 0.0549 | 0.0651 | +18.6% | 0.0710 | +29.3% |
| duration s | 2,333 | 1,967 | -15.7% | 1,804 | -22.7% |
| TTFT mean s | 378.2 | 319.4 | -15.5% | 292.3 | -22.7% |
| TTFT median s | 400.8 | 339.3 | -15.4% | 309.0 | -22.9% |
| TTFT p99 s | 556.9 | 473.2 | -15.0% | 436.7 | -21.6% |
| TPOT mean ms | 490.8 | 412.1 | -16.0% | 380.5 | -22.5% |
| TPOT median ms | 513.8 | 429.9 | -16.3% | 399.1 | -22.3% |
| TPOT p99 ms | 638.6 | 525.8 | -17.7% | 467.4 | -26.8% |
| ITL median ms | 816.2 | 695.0 | -14.8% | 638.7 | -21.7% |
| E2E mean s | 549.5 | 463.3 | -15.7% | 425.1 | -22.6% |
| spec acceptance length | 1.64 | 1.65 | +0.9% | 1.64 | +0.3% |

Note, since this is done on artificial data, AL is lower (1.65) compared to more realistic 3.5.

8k/1k, NP=10*C, TP4, using mxfp4 dense path (too short kv for sparse), no spec decoding:

| C | FP8 output tok/s | MXFP4 output tok/s | Δ | FP8 mean TTFT | MXFP4 mean TTFT | Δ | FP8 mean TPOT | MXFP4 mean TPOT | Δ |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 102.0 | 109.3 | **+7.2%** | 291 ms | 290 ms | -0.3% | 9.53 ms | 8.88 ms | **-6.8%** |
| 16 | 1027.9 | 1061.0 | **+3.2%** | 1611 ms | 1580 ms | -1.9% | 14.00 ms | 13.55 ms | **-3.2%** |
| 64 | 2005.7 | 2065.9 | **+3.0%** | 2048 ms | 2025 ms | -1.1% | 29.92 ms | 29.01 ms | **-3.0%** |
| 128 | 2485.5 | 2564.0 | **+3.2%** | 2835 ms | 2798 ms | -1.3% | 48.73 ms | 47.18 ms | **-3.2%** |


## Accuracy

| check | tot_baseline | mxfp4_sparse | mxfp4_dense |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K flexible-extract | 0.9651 ± 0.0051 | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | 0.9598 ± 0.0054 |

### Long context accuracy check

- **The text:** the first 131,072 tokens of *War and Peace* (Project Gutenberg), tokenized with the model's own tokenizer. The token ids are saved, so every run scores exactly the same sequence.
- **One request** to the running server: `/v1/completions` with the ids as the prompt, `max_tokens=1`, `temperature=0`, `prompt_logprobs=0`. For every position the server returns the log-probability the model gave to the token that actually comes next, given everything before it. Nothing is sampled; it is one teacher-forced pass over the whole book.
- **The score:** NLL per token is minus that log-probability, averaged in four position buckets: 0-16K, 16K-32K, 32K-64K and 64K-128K.
- **Two runs per configuration** on the same server.


| run | 0K-16K | 16K-32K | 32K-64K | 64K-128K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| tot_baseline run1 | 0.0710 | 0.1302 | 0.1323 | 0.1460 |
| tot_baseline run2 | 0.0717 | 0.1293 | 0.1332 | 0.1484 |
| mxfp4_sparse run1 | 0.0709 | 0.1274 | 0.1334 | 0.1465 |
| mxfp4_sparse run2 | 0.0711 | 0.1269 | 0.1300 | 0.1449 |
| mxfp4_dense run1 | 0.0715 | 0.1313 | 0.1353 | 0.1489 |
| mxfp4_dense run2 | 0.0721 | 0.1302 | 0.1330 | 0.1494 |

## Not a duplicate

#57517 and #56834 also add a ROCm MXFP4 indexer K cache, with dense scoring. The main
addition here is sparse MXFP4 (`indexer_sparse_logits=True`): the candidate source takes
block maxima from the same pass that writes its logits, and the consumer layers score only
the candidate pool, read in place from the paged MXFP4 cache. Neither PR supports this
(#56834 rejects candidate blocks outright). For the dense path, this PR uses aiter's paged
MXFP4 MQA-logits kernel (ROCm/aiter#5834, in aiter v0.1.23) and leaves vLLM's shared Q/K
kernels untouched.

Follows the main idea from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56254 while going direct to the paged K for prefill.
## AI assistance
Claude is used during development, and the PR author reviewed the AI driven changes.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Shard the Engram wkv projection across TP ranks
author: ShuoleiWang
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's two Engram layers (1 and 14) project the looked-up n-gram rows with `wkv` (6144 → 25600, MXFP8 `[32, 32]` blocks). `wkv` is a `ReplicatedLinear`. Without sequence parallelism, every TP rank runs the full projection on every token. This covers plain TP and TP + EP with DP = 1, the single-node Hopper layouts in the recipe (H100 TP8, H200 TP4). Per Engram layer that is 315 MFLOP per token, plus a 157 MB weight read per step, repeated on each of the TP ranks.

This PR makes `wkv` a `ColumnParallelLinear` with `gather_output=True`. Each rank computes 25600 / TP output columns, and one all-gather rebuilds the full `kv` that `_fused_engram_post_wkv_kernel` already consumes, so nothing downstream changes.

The replicated layout is kept in two cases, so their behavior is unchanged:
- Under sequence parallelism each rank already projects only its own tokens, so `disable_tp=use_sequence_parallel` keeps the replicated layout there.
- TP = 1 behaves as before.

Model loading per GPU drops by 0.28 GiB at TP8 (61.63 → 61.35 GiB), which goes to the KV cache.

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "engram"` and `--search "wkv"` show no PR touching this projection.

## Test Plan

**Setup**
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink).
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (HF revision `dba1be0a`).
- vLLM: nightly `0.30.1rc1.dev85+g8b84e1506`, with this diff applied as a Python overlay. `engram.py` is identical between that nightly and current `main`.

**Server.** TP8 + EP8, DSpark with the synthetic acceptance length 3.51 (InferenceX's golden AL), so both arms decode the same number of tokens per step:

```bash

title: [Perf][Attention] Remove D2H sync from FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA plan under async scheduling
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

With async scheduling, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` did a blocking D2H copy on every metadata build. FlashInfer bakes each row's `kv_len` into its schedule on the host, and `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is optimistic under async spec decode, so the builder copied `positions` / `seq_lens` back to get exact lengths. With MTP that happens on every draft step too. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made async scheduling *slower* than `--no-async-scheduling` (11.1 vs 7.7 ms TPOT at c=1).

How it works:

1. **Plan on the CPU with the upper bound plus slack.** The host bound, padded by 32 tokens and capped at the max valid count, is available without touching the GPU, so there's no sync.
2. **Clamp on the GPU.** FlashInfer keeps the plan in its int workspace as a list of work items with `kv_start`/`kv_end`. A small Triton kernel (`_clamp_work_kv_end`) computes each row's exact valid count on device from `seq_lens` / `query_start_loc` / `req_id_per_token` (same formula as before) and clamps every work item's `kv_end` to it. The FA3 kernel never reads past `kv_end`, so the slack (and the `-1` tail of the index buffer) is never touched.
3. **Reuse the plan across steps.** Contexts grow by a few tokens per step and the slack absorbs that, so while the new bounds still fit, `wrapper.plan()` is skipped and only the clamp runs. This is also why no-async gets slightly faster.

```
before:  GPU seq_lens --(blocking D2H)--> CPU exact lens --> plan --> run
after:   CPU upper bound + 32 --> plan (usually reused)
         GPU: clamp kv_end to exact lens (Triton, no sync) --> run
```

Notes:
- This reads `wrapper._plan_info` and the planned int workspace (the `MLAPlanInfo` layout from `scheduler.cuh`). The plan-info length is asserted, and the per-work capacity is read from the layout rather than hardcoded.
- With adaptive verification the host query split may not match the device one, so the host bound falls back to the batch max for every row.
- The exact (syncing) path is only used when there's no host upper bound.
- Only affects `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (Hopper; the default sparse backend for NoPE models such as GLM-5.3-Flash).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs touching this backend. #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and indexer workspace sizing, and #58260 chunks plan/run for >16k-row steps. Neither addresses the sync. #58260 does touch `plan()` / `build()`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; I'm happy to do it.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py` on H100. I updated the existing tests to the new `plan()` signature and added two GPU tests against real FlashInfer. One checks that an upper-bound plan plus the device clamp matches an exact plan (including MTP-style multi-query rows around `index_topk` and a batch spanning several clamp blocks). The other checks that the plan is reused across growing contexts without replanning.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV cache, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, `max-model-len 32768`. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos` at concurrency 1/8/32, at least 32 prompts, each point run twice, no profiler.
- Accuracy: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot).
- Syncs: a torch profiler trace on the patched server shows no blocking sync left in the draft-step metadata build (before: 13 per ~5 steps, ~79 ms total, at `_kv_lens_host`).

All E2E runs, baseline included, have the fp8 plan-dtype fix from #55222 applied locally, since fp8 KV on this backend fails without it.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 18 passed.

Mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, async | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| **this PR, async** | 128.1 / 126.9 / **6.86** | 188.0 / 152.7 / **17.36** | 283.7 / 251.5 / **37.04** |
| main, no-async | 129.8 / 128.8 / 7.70 | 189.2 / 157.8 / 18.20 | 258.9 / 175.5 / 42.71 |
| this PR, no-async | 124.2 / 123.8 / 7.47 | 177.2 / 152.0 / 17.95 | 254.7 / 170.6 / 41.72 |

With async scheduling, TPOT drops 38% / 21% / 18%, and async is now faster than no-async at every concurrency.

GSM8K is unchanged: 0.913 → 0.921 (async), 0.911 → 0.917 (no-async). MTP mean acceptance length stays ~4.2. The random-token bench has ~no draft acceptance, so its TPOT is close to the worst case for spec decode.

---

title: [Perf] JIT monitor: hook TileLang JITImpl.compile instead of __call__
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

The JIT monitor is switched on after warmup, and it wraps TileLang's `JITImpl.__call__`. As a result, every TileLang kernel launch pays for the wrapper, including building the cache-miss key, even though nearly all of those calls hit the kernel cache. TileLang's `__call__` only calls `self.compile()` on a cache miss, so this PR hooks `compile` instead. The monitor still catches every post-warmup JIT compile, and cache hits no longer go through it.

This matters for models with many TileLang launches outside CUDA graphs. For example, GLM-5.3-Flash runs ~72 mhc TileLang calls per eager step (prefill / mixed batches).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for jit_monitor / TileLang and found nothing related.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/jit_monitor/` (the fake `JITImpl` now calls `compile()` on a cache miss, like the real one).
- Microbench: 2000 `mhc_post_tilelang` calls after warmup, with the monitor off and on, on H100.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, async scheduling. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve` with random 1024 in / 128 out, each point run twice.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 25 passed, 7 skipped.

Microbench (µs per call):

| | monitor off | monitor on |
|---|---|---|
| main (wrap `__call__`) | 15.7 | 25.9 |
| this PR (wrap `compile`) | 15.5 | 15.6 |

That's ~10 µs × ~72 calls ≈ 0.7 ms of CPU per eager step removed on GLM-5.3-Flash.

E2E, mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| this PR | 133.0 / 135.5 / 11.11 | 219.2 / 187.0 / 21.45 | 331.3 / 312.8 / 45.04 |

TTFT improves 2–3%. TPOT is within noise because decode runs under CUDA graphs. The change is small, but so is the diff, and the monitor stays functionally the same.

title: [Metrics] Count finished requests by watermark status
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add `vllm:watermark_requests{status}`, a Prometheus counter of finished requests by watermark status. It exists only when `watermark_config` is set.

## Claims

- Each finished request gets exactly one status: `watermarked`, `skipped` or `not_watermarked`.
- `skipped` means the request asked for the watermark (omitted or `true`) but could not use it, such as `temperature=0` and trace replay requests.
- `not_watermarked` covers explicit opt-outs, pooling requests and internal requests (beam search steps, generative scoring, language detection).
- On an instance with `watermark_config`, the sum over `status` equals `vllm:request_success`. Both come from the same call in `IterationStats.update_from_finished_request()`.
- Without `watermark_config` the counter is not registered.

## Validation

Unit tests:

- `tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py`: requests of every status, including pooling, engine `ABORT`, `ERROR` and an `n=2` parent, finish through `OutputProcessor.process_outputs()` and are recorded by `PrometheusStatLogger`. The labels sum to `vllm:request_success`.
- `tests/v1/metrics/test_histogram_buckets.py`: the counter is registered only with `watermark_config`.

```
pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_histogram_buckets.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py
64 passed
```

E2E on H200 (`tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py`, now also checks the three labels and the sum for a watermarked, an opted-out and a `temperature=0` request):

```
pytest tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py
1 passed
```

Manual scrape with `vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --watermark-config '{"key": 42}'` after one watermarked, one `temperature=0` and one opted-out completion:

```
vllm:watermark_requests_total{engine="0",model_name="facebook/opt-125m",status="watermarked"} 1.0
vllm:watermark_requests_total{engine="0",model_name="facebook/opt-125m",status="skipped"} 1.0
vllm:watermark_requests_total{engine="0",model_name="facebook/opt-125m",status="not_watermarked"} 1.0
vllm:request_success_total{engine="0",finished_reason="length",model_name="facebook/opt-125m"} 3.0
```

Without `--watermark-config`, `/metrics` has no `vllm:watermark_requests` series.

## Details

The status reads the same `SamplingParams` flags the GPU sampler reads: `watermarking`, and `_watermarking_skipped`, which the frontend sets when it resolves the request. `RequestState.from_new_request()` copies them into `RequestStateStats` once.

A request resolved again through the deprecated `EngineCoreRequest` path can carry both `_watermarking_skipped=True` and `watermarking=True`. It counts as `watermarked`, because `watermarked` is checked first.

The status is per request, not per token. A `watermarked` request can still contain tokens without the watermark (accepted draft tokens with `allow_target_only_watermarking`, repeated contexts with `deduplicate_contexts`, grammar-forced tokens). The docs list these cases.

Limitations, documented in `docs/features/watermarking.md`:

- In disaggregated prefill/decode, both instances count a request. Sum over decode instances only.
- For streaming input, the first input chunk sets the status.
- Client aborts are in neither counter, as with `vllm:request_success`.

Model Runner V1 cannot watermark, so there is no V1 path.

title: [Perf][MoE] Index expert mapping lookups in RoutedExperts.load_weights
author: Willian-Zhang
body:
## Purpose

`RoutedExperts.load_weights` scans the whole expert mapping for each checkpoint tensor. Both the mapping size and the tensor count grow with the number of experts, making matching quadratic in expert count. Original profiling of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on a DGX Spark attributed about 25 seconds of weight loading to this loop.

Build the index in a small `_index_expert_mapping` helper, grouping entries by the literal logical expert ID in the checkpoint name. `load_weights` selects candidates for each tensor, then runs the existing substring check and loading body. Preserve every physical destination and its order, including EPLB replicas. IDs remain strings, so `1`, `10`, and `01` stay distinct.

Fused 3-D tensors, repeated `experts.` prefixes, unrecognized IDs, and mappings that cannot be indexed safely retain the full scan. The inner loading body, including the fused contiguous-match break, is unchanged. No new configuration is needed.

## Validation

**124 focused tests passed** on the updated branch, covering expert loading, fused layouts, representative quantization metadata, biases, LoRA names, redundant experts, FP8 TP=2/4, and GPT-OSS loading. The mapping and expert-bias tests also pass against the pre-PR scan and the initial PR implementation: 37 tests per version. All pre-commit hooks and mypy for Python 3.10/3.12 passed.

The main mapping test uses 15 representative combinations of checkpoint naming and non-fused tensor ranks. A mixed stream of per-expert, fused, and per-expert tensors verifies that candidate selection resets between inputs while preserving payloads and layout. Deliberately moving that reset outside the input loop makes all four mixed-stream cases fail.

A standalone differential harness compared the actual selection code across 199,222 cases, including synthetic mappings and sampled names from nine cached checkpoint inventories: all agreed. Inventory checks are name-only checks, not full inference on those large models.

```bash
chg run -g=1 --timeout 15m -- env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONPATH="$PWD" \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py \
  tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py::test_routed_experts_loads_per_expert_biases \
  tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py::test_auto_gptq_moe_creates_zero_initialized_expert_biases \
  -q -rs

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py
```

### Real-model checks

Model and startup measurements below cover the equivalent loader in `f961624286`. For the subsequent helper extraction, the original loading-loop body is AST-identical; inlining the helper and normalizing its equivalent early-return fallback reproduces the validated function. The focused tests and differential comparisons were rerun after the extraction and the merge from `main`.

Fresh-process baseline/revised comparisons on B300 checked the ordered loader calls and SHA256 of every parameter before and after quantization/backend processing. **Every parameter and dispatch trace matched in all seven configurations.** Greedy, 5-shot GSM8K samples used a 256-output-token cap; these are bounded regression samples, not representative quality estimates.

| Checkpoint / configuration | GSM8K baseline / revised | Identical output sequences |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B BF16, fused checkpoint | 27/32 / 27/32 | 32/32 |
| RedHatAI Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 | 17/32 / 17/32 | 32/32 |
| NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B FP8, non-gated experts | 5/32 / 5/32 | 32/32 |
| Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat GPTQ Int4 | 12/32 / 12/32 | 23/32 |
| TheBloke Mixtral_7Bx2_MoE AWQ | 21/32 / 21/32 | 30/32 |
| Qwen3.6 NVFP4, TP=2 + EP=2 | 7/16 / 9/16 | 1/16 |
| Qwen3.6 NVFP4, TP=2 + EP=2 + four EPLB replicas | 6/16 / 6/16 | 16/16 |

The fully matching rows also have identical sampled-token log probabilities. Generation variability in GPTQ/AWQ/EP reproduced with the unchanged baseline and identical weights: GPTQ changed 15/32 responses within one loaded instance; AWQ changed 1/32 across baseline startups. A fresh EP baseline matched revised generation exactly, including log probabilities. Exact generation equality is therefore not claimed for every configuration.

Environment: Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, existing prebuilt CUDA extensions. Installed FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 predates the checkout's GDN API, so baseline and revised Qwen3.6 runs used `gdn_prefill_backend="triton"`. All comparisons used eager execution; single-GPU checks used TP=1, and distributed checks used two GPUs. EPLB coverage is initial replica loading, not dynamic rebalancing. Standalone tracing/benchmark harnesses are outside the code diff.

### Startup performance

RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 on one B300: three fresh processes per variant, interleaved with warm filesystem/kernel caches. TP=1, eager execution, text-only, context 2048, max sequences 8, 4 GiB KV cache, Triton GDN prefill, optional warmups/autotuning disabled. Parameter hashing and per-callback tracing were removed for timing. All runs produced identical smoke-test tokens.

| Median | Pre-PR scan | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Weight loading | 19.500 s | 12.819 s |
| Python entry to LLM ready | 38.977 s | 32.812 s |

The startup measurement excludes HTTP server setup, compilation/CUDA graphs, and cold-cache costs.

## Duplicate-work check

No issue tracks this. The original open-PR searches for `RoutedExperts load_weights expert mapping`, `expert_mapping`, and `load_weights FusedMoE slow` found no competing change to this loop. Nearby #49336/#49362 change `dbrx.py`; #49991/#50794 target host-to-device copies rather than name matching.

## AI assistance

Claude assisted with the initial profiling and implementation. Codex assisted with the simplification, expanded tests, local model validation, and this description.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Stop the host pool feeding device KV cache residency metrics
author: eopXD
body:
> **NOTE:** This PR was reduced to a one-line change: the HiSparse host pool no longer gets the device pool's metrics collector (`metrics_collector=None` in `HiSparseSourceManager.bind_host_pool`), so host blocks stop feeding the device `vllm:kv_block_*_seconds` histograms. That removes the block-ID collision described below at its source, instead of keying samples by pool. Host-tier residency metrics are proposed separately in #59485 (on top of #58949). The description below is the original.

## Purpose

With HiSparse and `--kv-cache-metrics`, the host and GPU pools share a metrics
collector, but each pool numbers its blocks independently. The collector keys
samples by `block_id` alone.

This results in incorrect metrics recording in KV cache block activities
when using HiSparse.

A false lifetime, idle-time, and reuse-gap histogram will affect users
relying on it to investigate cache turnover and reuse.

For example, allocate GPU block 1 at t=1 s and host block 1 at t=2 s. The host
allocation currently emits a false one-second GPU eviction sample, even though
the GPU block remains allocated. With this fix, **both histories remain active
and no eviction sample is emitted**.

This MR key samples by `(block.pool, block.block_id)` in allocation, access
and eviction callbacks. Allowing the KV cache block activities to be correctly
accounted.


The callbacks only update telemetry; allocation and eviction decisions are
unaffected. Ordinary hybrid/SWA groups sharing one pool retain their existing
behavior.


## Test Coverage

`test_hisparse_host_pool_preserves_device_lifecycle`
(`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py:59`) verifies the
production-wiring example. The test fails with metrics enabled without the fix.

title: [Perf] Fuse the mamba align block-table gather into one Triton kernel, 7 kernels -> 1, 6x speedup on all shapes for this kernel
author: fululi12
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a kernel-level microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured on the isolated kernel, both versions in the same process. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing six of seven kernel launches on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency.

## Purpose

`mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s `"align"` branch takes the last `1 + num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request:

```python
start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // kv_cache_spec.block_size
start_indices.clamp_(min=0)
offsets = torch.arange(1 + kv_cache_spec.num_speculative_blocks, ...)
indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
```

The arithmetic is trivial, but as PyTorch ops it is **seven kernel launches** over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor — which holds a **single element** in a one-request decode. Almost all of the cost is launch overhead rather than work.

This is a **shared utility**: `gdn_attn`, `mamba_attn`, `short_conv_attn` and `linear_attn` all call it, so the change is not specific to one model.

## Measured

On MI355X, both versions in the same process so it is like-for-like:

| num_reqs | spec blocks | kernels | us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **7** | **7 -> 1** | **10.81 -> 1.78** | **6.06x** |
| 1 | 3 | 7 -> 1 | 10.91 -> 1.79 | 6.11x |
| 8 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 10.73 -> 1.82 | 5.90x |
| 64 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 12.02 -> 1.95 | 6.16x |

The gain is **flat in batch size**, because the cost is per-launch rather than per-element.

For context on why this site was picked: in a Kimi-K3 concurrency-1 decode trace, attributing every GPU kernel back to its Python call site ranks this the **highest kernels-per-invocation** of any non-model-math site in that model — 7.0 kernels and 19.6 us per invocation. Every other call site in that model is already at or near one kernel per call.

To be explicit about scope: this is a **kernel-level claim**. Against a multi-millisecond decode step it is a fraction of a percent end-to-end, and I am not claiming a measurable throughput change.

## Correctness

**Update after review ([@ChuanLi1101](https://github.com/ChuanLi1101)):** the first version of this kernel indexed the block table as `base + req * stride(0) + start + offs`, which silently assumes a **column stride of 1**. The `torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)` it replaces honours any layout, and since this is a shared utility a caller holding a non-contiguous view would have read the wrong blocks. The kernel now takes `block_table.stride(0)`, `block_table.stride(1)` and `seq_lens.stride(0)` explicitly, matching the existing `kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py` helper.

Worth stating plainly: the original 48-shape sweep below **did not catch this**, because every block table it generated was contiguous. The test added in this PR closes that gap.

Verification now lives in-tree at `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`, so CI runs it rather than it being an out-of-tree script. It pins the kernel to the pre-fusion expression over:

- **48 shape combinations** — `num_reqs` 1/2/8/64 x `block_size` 16/64/256 x `num_speculative_blocks` 0/1/3/7, bit-identical (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- **a non-contiguous block table** (`stride(1) == 2`) — the regression test for the bug above
- **`seq_len == 0`**, the CUDA-graph padding row the previous `clamp_(min=0)` guarded, which must clamp to row 0
- **`num_reqs == 0`**, which must not launch a `(0,)` grid
- the **`"all"` / `"none"`** passthrough modes, which still return the input tensor itself rather than a copy

55 tests pass against the fixed kernel. The three non-contiguous cases **fail against the previous kernel**, so the suite catches the defect rather than merely covering the line.

The kernel keeps the same in-range assumption the existing `torch.gather` already relies on: `start + num_speculative_blocks` must lie inside the block-table row.

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py` — 55 tests, in-tree so CI runs them
- [x] 48 shape combinations bit-identical on device (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- [x] Non-contiguous block table (`stride(1) != 1`) — fails on the pre-fix kernel, passes now
- [x] Edge cases: `num_reqs == 0`, `seq_len == 0` clamp path, `"all"` / `"none"` passthrough
- [x] Timing on MI355X: 7 kernels -> 1, 10.81 us -> 1.78 us (6.06x) at the single-request shape. **Kernel-level only; no end-to-end throughput claim.**
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Gather nvfp4_ds_mla chunked-context KV with the NVFP4 kernel
author: stu-cao
body:
## Status (2026-10-15)

Reworked after @zyongye's review (thanks — every point was right) and @LucasWilkinson's stu-cao/vllm#2, which proposed the same `seq_starts` change; rebased onto `main` `19b0efce30`. Lucas's kernel-level test (random cache bytes, non-block-aligned starts, bit-exact against the same slots gathered without starts) is included as his commit in `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py`. Where this differs from #2: the BF16 workspace hunk is dropped (zyongye's point 1, it was unreachable) and DCP is rejected at startup instead of being left to fail in the generic gather (point 4).

- **`seq_starts` on the NVFP4 gather kernel** instead of a block-table shim. `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache` gains an optional `seq_starts` like its fp8 twin (`token_offset = out_token - workspace_starts[req] + seq_starts[req]`), and the dense dispatch passes `chunk.starts` exactly as the `fp8_ds_mla` branch does. `shift_block_table_to_starts`, its alignment precondition, the clamp, the per-chunk gather and its CPU test are gone. Other callers are unchanged (the argument defaults to `None`).
- **Dropped the `MLACommonMetadataBuilder` workspace hunk and the `fp8_query` test arm.** `nvfp4_ds_mla` is only accepted by `FlashMLASparseBackend`, whose builder (`SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder`) allocates its own BF16 workspace and hard-codes a BF16 prefill query, so neither was reachable.
- **DCP is rejected at startup** (`VllmConfig.validate_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_mla`) instead of in the per-layer forward on the first request with context; covered by `tests/test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism`.
- The raw `kv_c_and_k_pe_cache` pass is intentional: the `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache is allocated as `torch.uint8`. The three other gather dispatch sites that still send `nvfp4_ds_mla` to the generic gather (`mla_attention.py` DCP path, `kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py`, `sparse_mla_attention.py`) are unreachable today and left for a follow-up.

Verification on the rebased head (`dc6aa4ae53`, B300 SM103, from-source build): **17 passed, 0 failed** — `test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py` (1, the `seq_starts` path on real NVFP4 rows), `test_mla_context_chunks.py` (14), `test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism` (2); registered schema `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache(..., int batch_size, Tensor? seq_starts=None)`; torch 2.14.0+cu130, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3a`. `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k nvfp4`: 27 passed including `test_cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_seq_starts`.

## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` crashes in the MLA chunked-context prefill:

```
mla_attention.py  _compute_prefill_context
_custom_ops.py    gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache
RuntimeError: get_fp8_kv_cache_data_type, csrc/attention/dtype_fp8.cuh:34,
              Unsupported fp8 kv cache data type: nvfp4_ds_mla
```

`MLACommonBaseImpl._compute_prefill_context` gathers each chunk's cached context KV into a BF16 workspace. It has a branch for `fp8_ds_mla`; every other dtype goes to `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache`, which only knows the fp8 variants. The NVFP4 upconvert kernel added with the `nvfp4_ds_mla` format, `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache`, is never called here.

Sparse MLA reaches this path through its dense-MHA prefill: a prefill whose total length is `<= index_topk` and that has cached context. In practice:

- **speculative-decoding warm-up**: the dummy batch takes this path, so an engine with `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV and a DFlash draft never finishes starting;
- **chunked prefill splitting a short prompt**: the continuation step has context;
- **prefix-cache hits** on short prompts.

Longer prefills use the sparse FlashMLA kernels, which already handle `nvfp4_ds_mla`.

**Fix:**

- Route `nvfp4_ds_mla` to `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache`.
- Give that kernel an optional `seq_starts` (csrc + bindings + `_custom_ops`), mirroring `cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache`: a continuation chunk reads from its context start instead of the request's first token. Without it, every chunk after the first would silently re-read the request's first tokens.
- Reject `nvfp4_ds_mla` with decode context parallelism at config validation; that combination is not validated.

Other dtypes are unaffected. I found no existing issue or PR for this.

## Test Plan

New tests:

- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py` (SM100). Writes random KV into an `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache with `concat_and_cache_mla`, then runs `_compute_prefill_context` on it. The reference is the same method on a BF16 cache holding the dequantized values, through the generic gather. Every chunk must see bit-identical Q/K/V; the batch includes a chunk that continues one request and starts another.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py::test_cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_seq_starts` (SM100): the kernel's `seq_starts` with non-block-aligned starts, bit-exact against a full gather.
- `tests/test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism` (CPU).

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py tests/test_config.py -k "nvfp4 or context_chunks"
```

End-to-end on 1 × GB200 node (4 GPUs), run with the first revision of this change (block-table shift; same gather semantics):

- **Model:** GLM-5.3 (NVFP4 weights) + DFlash2 draft (fp8 KV, k=4).
- **Engine:** aggregated TP4, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla`, `--block-size 1024`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, prefix caching on.
- **Arms:** the same build with and without this change, plus an fp8-KV reference at `--max-model-len 262144`, since fp8 cannot fit one 1M-token request on TP4.
- **Checks:** startup; 6 distinct verifiable prompts, sequential then 12-way concurrent × 3 rounds; 12 concurrent ~1.7K-token prompts with `--max-num-seqs 8` and an 8192-token budget so some are necessarily split and their continuation runs this path, compared with the same prompts served unsplit; draft acceptance over 3 × 400 tokens on a short and a ~10K-token prompt.

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** see Status above for the current head. The first revision, on GB200 against `v0.30.1rc0`: the SM100 test failed before the change (`Unsupported fp8 kv cache data type: nvfp4_ds_mla`) and passed with it.

**End-to-end (first revision):**

| | without the change | **with the change** | fp8 KV reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| startup | crashes in warm-up (trace above) | serves | serves (at 256K) |
| KV capacity at 1M, TP4 | — | 1,646,592 tokens (1.57×) | does not fit one 1M request |
| correctness, 42 requests | — | 42 / 42 | 42 / 42 |
| forced split prefill, 36 requests | — | 36 / 36, identical to unsplit | 36 / 36, identical to unsplit |
| draft acceptance, short prompt | — | 39.0% | 37.7% |
| draft acceptance, ~10K-token prompt | — | 48.1% | 47.4% |

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write the change and tests, and run the tests above. I reviewed every changed line.

title: [ROCm][CI] Add quantized MoE serving test for gfx950
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose
Split out of #50519 to keep that PR reviewable. No functional changes outside tests and CI config.

`tests/quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py` guards the startup-and-generation contract for quantized MoE models, but there is no ROCm equivalent, so regressions in the ROCm quantized MoE paths are only caught by much heavier end-to-end jobs.

This adds `tests/quantization/test_rocm_moe.py` as the gfx950 counterpart. It follows the same recipe: reduced model configs, dummy weights, a real server, and assertions on the serving contract rather than on trained-model accuracy.

Each case starts a model through `RemoteOpenAIServer` and checks that it warms up and returns finite logprobs, in both eager and compiled mode:

| model | quantization | MoE backend | attention backend |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8 | per-tensor FP8 | triton | TRITON_MLA |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | block FP8 | triton | TRITON_ATTN |
| gpt-oss-20b | MXFP4 | aiter | TRITON_ATTN |

The backend selection is enforced, not advisory: `--moe-backend aiter` resolves through the MXFP4 oracle, which raises `ValueError` rather than silently falling back to Triton. So a case that starts at all has genuinely exercised the requested backend.

The whole file is skipped off gfx950.

## Changes

- `tests/quantization/test_rocm_moe.py` — new file, six cases (three models x eager/compiled).
- `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml` and `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` — add the `Quantized MoE` group that runs the new file, and exclude it from the existing quantization shards so it does not run twice.

## Test Plan

Run the new file on gfx950.

## Test Result

All six cases pass.

title: [ROCm][CI] Make ROCm 10.0 the default image; keep ROCm 7.2 as -rocm72
author: Rohan138
body:
## Purpose

Make ROCm 10.0 (TheRock) the default ROCm image and wheel, keeping ROCm 7.2 available for a transition period.

- Rename `Dockerfile.rocm{,_base}` → `Dockerfile.rocm_72{,_base}` and `Dockerfile.rock{,_base}` → `Dockerfile.rocm{,_base}`, so all CI now builds ROCm 10.0.
- Images: `:nightly` / `:latest` are ROCm 10.0 (also tagged `-rocm100`); ROCm 7.2 is published as `-rocm72`.
- Wheels: `wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/` now serves ROCm 10.0 (`rocm100`); ROCm 7.2 stays at `rocm/<ver>/rocm723`. Install:
  ```bash
  uv pip install "vllm[device-gfx942]" --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/
  ```
  The index hosts vLLM, triton, FA, aiter, amdsmi and a torch repacked to require our triton, and links the ROCm SDK and GPU kernels from AMD's whl-next index.

- Both stacks go through the same scripts and pipeline steps: each ROCm script takes the stack's base Dockerfile, and `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/stack.sh` derives the version, variant, cache keys and image tags from it.
- Internal ECR tags are renamed to the variant (e.g. `<commit>-rocm100`), so the first run rebuilds each base image once.

Known gaps: wheel installs miss the image's build-time ROCm patches, and the amdsmi wheel still needs a hardware check.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; reviewed and owned by me. No duplicate PR exists.

## Test Plan

YAML/shellcheck/ruff, `tests/tools/test_docker_build_metadata_args.py`, dry runs of the publish/upload scripts against a fake S3, and `uv pip compile "vllm[device-gfx942]"` against a locally generated index.

## Test Result

All pass; the one-liner resolves to our torch/triton plus AMD's SDK and gfx942 kernels. Full builds and the AMD test suite still need to run.

title: [Perf][MRV2] Reuse Mamba/GDN metadata across KV cache groups
author: lucamotz
body:
## Purpose

With #58207, `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3) trades KV capacity for fewer KV cache groups, because every group rebuilds its attention metadata each step. For Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash that's 17 groups instead of 46 and 30% less KV cache (RFC #58638, question 1). GDN groups with the same spec differ only in their state indices. This builds the first group's metadata and derives the others with `update_block_table()`, also at capture, so later groups' FULL graphs read the first group's batch-level buffers.

- `build_attn_metadata` does this for groups with the same `MambaSpec` and builder type, if the builder supports `update_block_table()`. No GDN-specific code in the runner.
- GDN implements `update_block_table()` and takes MRV2's precomputed `mamba_aligned_state_indices`.
- Mamba1/2 builders already support `update_block_table()` without spec decoding, so their metadata is now reused too.

Opened as part of [model runner discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52297#discussion_r4089381401) on #52297. Implements @MarkXCloud's second suggestion there. Same idea as #35166 by @jennyyyyzhen, which was closed as stale.
@xyang16 explicitly added as co author, since the original idea developed in their PR

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py
```

1× B200, main `24928a4d62` wheel plus the PR files. Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, serve and bench args as in RFC #58638 §8, 46 KV cache groups unless noted. 3–7 server restarts per variant in interleaved rounds, 95% CI. Step time is mean ITL at c=1.

## Test Result

72 passed, 14 skipped (CUDA-only) on CPU.

| | c=1 step time | c=1 output tok/s | c=32 output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| this PR vs main | −40% [−46, −34] | +57% [+43, +73] | +23% [+14, +32] |
| this PR vs #52297 | −17% [−24, −9] | +20% [+10, +32] | +10% [+2, +18] |

- CUDA API calls per step at c=1 (nsys, one capture each): 1032 on main, 548 with #52297, 424 with this PR. Syncs per step unchanged.
- GSM8K (250 questions, temperature 0) and acceptance length unchanged.
- 46 groups (main's grouping) vs 17 (+ #58207, default 3), c=1 step time:
  - +39% [+27, +51] with #52297;
  - +15% [+5, +26] with this PR;
  - +7% [−2, +16], not significant, with #52297 + this PR + the slice change from #58763 (ported onto #52297).

  c=32 is not significant in any of these. 46 groups keep 4.46M KV tokens vs 3.12M (+43%).
- Granite-4.0-H-tiny (Mamba2, 10 KV cache groups, prefix caching on, no spec decoding) vs main, n=3 each: c=1 step time −21% [−35, −5], c=32 output tok/s +12% [+1, +25]. GSM8K unchanged.

title: [Perf][GDN] Slice pure spec-decode rows instead of a host-mask gather
author: lucamotz
body:
## Purpose

Stacked on #58762; only the last commit is new. Opened as a draft in case the slice is wanted there.

Indexing a device tensor with a host boolean mask copies the index to the device and launches a gather, twice per GDN build and once per `update_block_table()`. In pure spec-decode batches the padded rows trail the spec rows, so this slices instead. This is MarkXCloud's first suggestion on #52297.

## Test Plan

pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py

title: [Frontend][Build] Add `vllm download-kernels` for FlashInfer precompiled kernels
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Add `vllm download-kernels` and recommend it after installing or upgrading vLLM, so that FlashInfer's precompiled kernels are installed instead of being downloaded and compiled at startup. This matters most on Hopper and newer GPUs, especially Blackwell.

- **`vllm download-kernels [--dry-run]`** runs FlashInfer's `download-kernels` for the installed FlashInfer and CUDA versions. Unlike FlashInfer's own CLI, it also works when the installed kernels belong to an older FlashInfer version, which is the state every vLLM upgrade that bumps FlashInfer leaves behind (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5886). It does nothing when FlashInfer is not installed.
- **Startup warning.** On Hopper and newer GPUs (`current_platform.is_cuda()` and `has_device_capability(90)`), the worker warns when `flashinfer-cubin` or `flashinfer-jit-cache` is missing or does not match `flashinfer-python`, and names the command. The check runs in `Worker.init_device()` after distributed init, so it is logged once by rank 0, before model load and the first FlashInfer JIT build, and not by the API server.
- **Docs.** The README, quickstart, CUDA installation guide (release and editable installs), and contributing guide include the command in the install block. The CLI guide documents it.
- **Docker.** The CUDA image installs the kernels through FlashInfer's CLI, which derives kernel versions and the CUDA index from the installed environment and defaults to all GPU architecture providers. It stays on FlashInfer's CLI, in the stage before vLLM is installed, so this large layer is not rebuilt for every wheel. The separate `FLASHINFER_VERSION` build argument is removed and `docker/versions.json` regenerated.
- **Requirements.** `flashinfer-cubin` and its index URL are removed from core CUDA requirements, along with the obsolete exclusion in `setup.py`. Published wheel dependencies are unchanged. The Rubin prerelease path keeps its explicit pins.

Duplicate-work searches found no open PR for this command, the Docker migration, or the runtime warning. Related #54724 is a docs note on stale packages after upgrades; this change makes that state recoverable with one command and detects it at startup.

## Test Plan

- `pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_download_kernels_cli.py`. The test runs the installed FlashInfer CLI through the wrapper with a stale `flashinfer-cubin` on the path, then checks that the startup warning fires while the kernels are missing or stale and stops once the packages the CLI resolved are installed. Nothing in it is pinned to a FlashInfer version, and `requirements/cuda.txt` is a run-all pattern, so a FlashInfer bump runs it.
- Mutation checks on that test: drop the version-check bypass, compare raw instead of public versions, and misname a kernel package in the warning.
- `pre-commit run` and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual` on the changed files; `git diff --check`.
- `vllm download-kernels --dry-run` with the kernel packages installed, missing, stale (`flashinfer-cubin==0.7.0` against `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1`), and without FlashInfer.
- `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` on a B300 (SM 10.3) with the kernel packages installed, missing, and stale, plus missing with `--tensor-parallel-size 2`.
- In a fresh venv: install `flashinfer-python==0.7.0`, run `flashinfer download-kernels`, upgrade to `0.7.0.post1`, then run the command the wrapper issues (`FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 flashinfer download-kernels`).
- `uv pip install --dry-run -r requirements/cuda.txt --torch-backend cu130`; compare old and new `get_requirements()` outputs for CUDA 12.9 and 13.0.
- `flashinfer download-kernels --dry-run` with FlashInfer 0.7.0 in a vLLM container without GPU access.

## Test Result

The unit tests passed (2 passed) and all hooks passed. Each of the three mutations made the test fail.

`vllm download-kernels --dry-run` resolved `flashinfer-cubin==0.7.0.post1` and `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.7.0.post1+cu130` and exited 0 in the installed, missing, and stale states, and logged a skip and exited 0 without FlashInfer. In the stale state, `flashinfer download-kernels` fails on import with the version mismatch. The non-dry-run path was exercised through the underlying command in the fresh venv: it replaced the 0.7.0 kernels with `flashinfer-cubin==0.7.0.post1` and `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.7.0.post1+cu130` (six providers), after which `import flashinfer` succeeded.

On the B300:

| Kernel packages | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Installed | No warning; server started. |
| Missing | One warning from `EngineCore` before model load; server started. FlashInfer JIT builds (`fmha_gen`, `sampling`) took about 140 s of a 252 s cold start. |
| Missing, TP=2 | One warning, from the rank 0 worker only. |
| Stale | Warning, then FlashInfer's version-mismatch `RuntimeError` on import. |

CUDA requirements resolved without the FlashInfer index, and all 76 published wheel requirements were identical before and after for both CUDA versions. The GPU-less container dry run selected FlashInfer 0.7.0 and CUDA 13.0 and reported `Install mode: all`; the published CUDA 13.0 x86-64 metadata includes sm80, sm89, sm90a, sm100a, sm103a, and sm120f providers.

A full multi-platform Docker build and model evaluations were not run. No model code or dependency versions changed.

AI assistance was used to implement and validate these changes.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep resumable sessions that stop while preempted
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58776.

With async scheduling, a resumable (streaming-input) request can be preempted while a step is still in flight. That step's output is delivered as stale output, and if it hits a stop condition the request stops in `PREEMPTED` state. Two things then go wrong:

1. **The session drops out of every queue.** `_handle_stopped_request` re-enqueues the resumable request, but the stopped-while-preempted cleanup in `update_from_output` removes it from `waiting`, `kv_holding_waiting` and `deferred_waiting`, including that new entry. The session is then in no queue and is never scheduled again. (Still the case after the queue rework in #58947 and the handoff fix in #58259.)
2. **The fold deletes the prompt.** `_update_request_as_session` keeps `all_token_ids[num_prompt_tokens:num_computed_tokens]` and deletes the rest. After preemption `num_computed_tokens == 0`, so it deletes the whole list, while `prompt_token_ids` (a separate list) is only extended; `num_prompt_tokens` then no longer matches `all_token_ids`, and the previous turn's output is lost.

Changes:

- After the stopped-while-preempted cleanup, re-enqueue requests that did not finish, so each ends up in exactly one queue.
- In the fold, keep up to `max(num_computed_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`. On a normal stop `num_computed_tokens == num_tokens - 1`, so nothing changes; after preemption the session keeps all but the final sampled token, and `num_computed_tokens` stays 0 so everything is recomputed.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for this path (`stopped_preempted_reqs`, streaming/resumable + preempt, `_update_request_as_session`, session hang symptoms); none found. #58668 fixes a different case where `num_computed_tokens` is wrong at the fold (a speculative step stopping on an accepted draft). Both PRs append a test to `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, so whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -k stop_while_preempted
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py -v
```

New tests in `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, using a real `AsyncScheduler`:

- `test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted` (next chunk queued before / after the stop) reproduces #58776. It asserts that the session is scheduled again, that `all_token_ids` and `prompt_token_ids` both hold the old prompt, the kept output and the new chunk, and that everything is recomputed.
- `test_non_resumable_request_stays_dequeued_after_stop_while_preempted` guards the re-enqueue: a request that finishes while preempted must stay out of the queues. It passes on main and fails if the `is_finished()` check is dropped.

## Test Result

`test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted`, with each half of the fix:

| scheduler | result |
| --- | --- |
| main | both cases fail: tokens are `[20, 21]` (prompt and output lost) |
| re-enqueue fix only | both fail: same token loss |
| fold fix only | both fail: `KeyError`, the session is never scheduled |
| this PR | both pass |

- CPU, `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input`: 806 passed with this PR vs 804 on main. The only difference is the two cases above; the remaining 1 failure and 6 errors need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py`: 14 passed.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/streaming_input` + the GPU-only core tests above: 19 passed, 2 errors. The errors are `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py`, which fails identically on main: engine profiling hits `assert prefill_query.shape[0] == num_prefill_tokens` in the FlashInfer backend with `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` on this machine.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line.

</details>

## Impact (update)

Besides the client-visible hang, the parked variant leaks scheduler capacity. When the session stops while preempted with no continuation queued, it is parked as `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` and `num_waiting_for_streaming_input` is incremented — and the queue cleanup then drops the session from every queue. If no continuation ever arrives, the counter is never decremented: each occurrence permanently consumes one `max_num_active_reqs` admission slot (the `num_running = len(self.running) + self.num_waiting_for_streaming_input` accounting in `schedule()`), so repeated occurrences silently shrink admission capacity. Verified locally on main: after the preempted stop, the parked case leaves `num_waiting_for_streaming_input == 1` with the session in no queue; if a continuation later arrives the counter rebalances in `_update_request_as_session`, but the session itself is already lost.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Reject draft slots that were never proposed
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Purpose

On a P/D decode instance, Model Runner V2 verifies draft slots its drafter never proposed. After the remote KV load the request resumes with one token left, and the scheduler pads that step with `k` placeholder drafts of `-1` (#45237, #55126). MRV2 fills those slots from `req_states.draft_tokens`, which are still zeros, so the rejection sampler verifies `k` real token-0 drafts against a stale draft distribution. With probabilistic drafting at T > 0 and block verification all `k` are accepted: on main, 71/80 MT-Bench responses through 1P1D start with at least 8 NUL tokens (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` + `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark`, `k=8`). MRV1 is not affected (#47029).

Fix: `RejectionSampler` gathers the verified tokens and positions with a Triton kernel that sets the draft rows of any step starting within the prefill (first position < `prefill_len`) back to `-1`, which the rejection kernels already reject. Drafts are only proposed after sampling past the prefill, so these rows are always placeholders. No new request state, and `input_ids` is unchanged.

#54102 (open) also restores these placeholders, via scheduler-side counts; this PR is a standalone runner-side fix with no scheduler changes. #58434 assumes these placeholders are rejected.

## Test Plan

- New `test_verify_rejects_unproposed_drafts`. Also ran the rejection-sampler, spec-decode and MRV2 worker suites, and `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k spec_decode_padding`.
- E2E on GB300, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=8`, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`, `rejection_sample_method=block`. Topologies: 1P1D (TP4 + TP4, `NixlConnector`) and co-located TP4. Workloads: 80 MT-Bench prompts at T=1 (count responses starting with NUL), the same prompts greedy (byte-compared with main), and GSM8K 5-shot.

## Test Result

title: [ROCm][Perf] Allocate the pinned PLE prefetch buffer lazily
author: mrodden
body:
## Why

The pinned PLE embedding (`Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding`) allocated its
prefetch stream and buffer in `__init__`, wasting VRAM on paths that never
prefetch. The AMD/ROCm serving path uses the synchronous pinned-lookup op and
never calls `start_prefetch`, so a `max_total_tokens * etp_data_parallel_size *
num_heads * dim` tensor sat in VRAM for every loaded model on ROCm.

This builds on #57497 (PLE n-gram table CPU offload).

## What

Allocate the prefetch stream + buffer on first `start_prefetch` instead:

- a per-instance `threading.Lock` keeps concurrent first callers from tearing
  the stream/buffer pair
- a capture-time tripwire raises if allocation happens inside cudagraph capture
- the gathered-ID count is checked against buffer capacity
- `forward` / `_finalize_prefetch` fail loudly if `start_prefetch` never ran

## Tests

- 4 new tests in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py` cover lazy allocation,
  missing-`start_prefetch` failures, and machinery under eager/compile/capture.
- Full `test_ple.py` suite: 61 passed on AMD MI300X (ROCm 7.2.4, torch 2.12).
- 256k-ctx serve smoke on MI300X: 51 CUDA graphs, KV cache 1,574,345 tokens
  (6.01x concurrency @ 256k), PLE banner `weight_device=cpu, pinned=True`,
  64k needle recall exact, `17*23` -> 391.

title: [CI] Stabilize batch submission in full CUDA graph tests
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Pause scheduling at level 0 while queueing the complete prompt batch for each engine.
- Resume scheduling in a `finally` block so an enqueue error cannot leave the engine paused.
- Collect typed `RequestOutput` results through `wait_for_completion`.
- Assert that both response counts match `batch_size` while retaining the exact output comparison.

This addresses the intermittent MI250 failure in [Buildkite build 91284](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91284#01a0da17-1395-4ad9-ad6f-b63ce962165a) while testing [#56679](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56679). Tracing showed that the nominal 64-request batch arrived as 1 + 63 requests in one engine and 1 + 34 + 29 in the other; replaying those splits reproduced the mismatch within either graph mode, motivating explicit batch submission.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and validation, and the repository pre-commit checks passed.

  existing `GateMode.INTERLEAVE` weight shuffle. AITER's INTERLEAVE stage-1
  GEMM has no tuned FlyDSL config for fp4x2 activations at this shape and
  silently falls back to a heuristic kernel that produces degenerate output
  end-to-end — AITER's own `op_tests/test_moe_2stage.py` cosine-similarity
  check (used to validate this commit) does not catch this, but real-model
  GSM8K does (near-chance accuracy, garbled reasoning traces).
- Commit 2 fixes that by switching a4w4 to ATOM's `GateMode.SEPARATED`
  gate/up weight layout instead, which AITER validates for fp4x2
  activations on this checkpoint. It's a single `is_guinterleave=False`
  flag flip in AITER's own `shuffle_weight`/`shuffle_scale` — no new
  shuffle function needed — gated on the same
  `FusedMoEConfig.use_mxfp4_w4a4_dsv4` flag that already gates the forced
  a4w4 activation dtype. a8w4 (default for every other MXFP4 model on this
  code path) is untouched.
- Commit 3 scoped the (then auto-detect-on) behavior to DeepSeek V4.1
  (`deepseek_v41`/`deepseek_v41_text`) model types, since DeepSeek V4
  shares the same MoE shape/dispatch path but had not been validated yet.
- Commit 4 dropped model-type auto-detection and made a4w4 a plain,
  explicit opt-in env knob instead of a default. The AgentX numbers below
  show a4w4 is -1.0% at c1, parity at c8, and only clearly wins at c64
  (+10.5% tok/s) — a perf knob with that profile should not silently
  change default behavior for every DeepSeek V4.1 deployment.
- **Commit 5 restores a model-type check, but as a hard guard instead of
  silent auto-detection or silent allow-anything.** `use_mxfp4_w4a4_dsv4`
  doesn't just pick an activation dtype — it also flips the MXFP4
  weight-shuffle layout at load time (`is_guinterleave` in
  `oracle/mxfp4.py`), and that shuffle call runs for *any* MXFP4 W4A16
  model (e.g. gpt-oss), not just DeepSeek V4.1. Setting
  `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1` while serving an unvalidated model
  would silently reproduce the exact garbled-output bug commit 2 already
  fixed once — just on a different model. `FusedMoEConfig.__post_init__`
  now raises a clear `ValueError` instead if the env var is set for any
  `hf_config.model_type` outside the validated DeepSeek V4.1 set. This also
  means #58869 (which extended the old auto-detection to DeepSeek V4) no
  longer applies; closing that PR in favor of this design.

## Test Plan & Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py vllm/_aiter_ops.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/mxfp4.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.13 --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py --hook-stage manual
```
45 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_aiter_fused_moe_fake_tensor_support`,
missing AITER JIT module, unrelated, reproduces on unmodified `main`).
New tests added for the opt-in behavior (unset/"0"/"1" x validated model
types).
pre-commit: clean.

Real-model validation on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP2, AITER `MXFP4_BF16` backend
(a4w4 = `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1` vs a8w4 = default):

- **GSM8K** (`lm_eval`, DSpark w/ real `block` rejection sampling): a4w4 and
  a8w4 both score `exact_match,strict=0.9712` / `flexible=0.9704` — identical.
- **AgentX** (`aiperf` `inferencex-agentx-mvp`, DSpark synthetic-AL=3.51
  rejection, settings matched to the public InferenceX dashboard run
  [`36101751233` attempt 2](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36101751233/attempts/2),
  3600s each, 0 errors):

  | Concurrency | Output tok/s (a4w4 vs a8w4) | Inter-token latency |
  |---|---|---|
  | c1  | 142.7 vs 144.1 (**-1.0%**) | 3.46 vs 3.37ms (+2.7%) |
  | c8  | 404.1 vs 404.5 (parity) | 4.39 vs 4.40ms (parity) |
  | c64 | 303.4 vs 274.5 (**+10.5%**) | 138.8 vs 149.0ms (**-6.9%**) |

  a4w4's fixed fp4-activation-quantization overhead isn't amortized at
  batch=1 (c1), reaches parity at c8, and wins clearly at c64 once the
  halved weight-read bandwidth dominates — consistent with a genuine
  compute/bandwidth crossover, not noise. This crossover behavior is
  exactly why the flag is opt-in rather than default: it is a net win at
  high concurrency but not universally so.

## Duplicate-work check

Same as prior commits on this PR; no other open PR touches this heuristic or
gate-mode path. #58869 previously extended the auto-detection this PR is
now removing; closed as no longer applicable.

## AI-assistance disclosure

Drafted with Cursor (Claude Sonnet 5): the AITER `GateMode`/shuffle
investigation, GSM8K root-cause debugging (INTERLEAVE+fp4x2 vs
SEPARATED+fp4x2), the AgentX perf sweep, the DeepSeek V4.1-only scoping,
the opt-in redesign (commit 4), the follow-up hard model-type guard
(commit 5, prompted by checking whether Kimi K3's MoE path was affected —
it isn't, since its SITU activation branch short-circuits before this
flag is read in the forward pass, but the weight-loading shuffle path
turned out to apply the flag unconditionally to any MXFP4 W4A16 model),
and this PR description. I (the submitting human) reviewed every changed
line and ran the test/eval commands above.
