title: [Kernel] Bump FlashKDA to keep the recurrent state in fp32
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Purpose

Bumps the FlashKDA pin from `b59532f` to `17a037d`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashKDA#13 on its `dev` branch.

Before this change, FlashKDA's K2 kernel stored the KDA recurrent state in bf16 and rounded it after every 16-token tile. On long GLM-5.3-Flash prefills the error builds up across tiles and across chunked-prefill boundaries, and it shows up as corrupted long-context tool-call output. FlashKDA#13 keeps the state in fp32 between tiles, adds missing TMA store waits, and fixes a register-pressure regression on sm_10x.

The only change is the one-line `GIT_TAG` in `cmake/external_projects/flashkda.cmake`. FlashKDA's op schema, `flash_kda.h`, source file list and cutlass submodule are the same at both commits.

Not a duplicate: no other change to the FlashKDA pin is on main since #12, and I found no open PR bumping it.

## Test Plan

All runs used RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, with FlashKDA built at the PR #13 content, on B200 (sm_100f, cu130) and H200.

- FlashKDA `tests/test_fwd_full.py`, which is a bitwise comparison against `torch_ref` covering fixed, varlen, batched and up to 1M-token cases.
- Relative error against an fp64 reference, using real GLM-5.3-Flash layer-0 activations.
- A long-context tool-call corruption probe (GLM-5.3-Flash, 34k and 42k-token prompts, salted cold prefills).
- `vllm bench serve` with the random dataset, 16 output tokens, 2k to 32k inputs and concurrency 1 to 64.

## Test Result

- `test_fwd_full`: 580/580 on B200.
- Final-state relative error, 4k to 128k tokens: 0.37-0.39%, previously 0.85-1.24%. Output relative error: 0.47%, previously 0.48%.
- Probe at 42k on B200, 256 samples per arm: 224/256 (87.5%) correct, previously 173/256 (67.6%). At 34k: 253/256 vs 256/256.
- H200 probe at 42k (emulated MoE, to isolate FlashKDA): 31/32, previously 21/32.
- Kernel time on B200: geomean 4.6% faster than the old pin.
- End-to-end serving on B200: throughput within ±1.3% of the old pin, which is within run-to-run noise.

**AI assistance:** Claude (Claude Code) helped with the FlashKDA kernel changes in FlashKDA#13, the benchmarks and quality runs above, and this pin bump and description. I reviewed the change and the results. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix receive post-process for different P/D block sizes
author: lucamotz
body:
## Purpose

NixlConnector pull with a smaller `--block-size` on P than on D writes wrong KV on D, or crashes D when a rank holds fewer KV heads than `block_size_ratio`. The receive post-process indexes attention views as `[B, N, H, D]`; since #44455 they are `[B, H, N, 2*D]` on every layout.

- `kv_postprocess_blksize_on_receive`: drop the two "physical order" permutes. On `LBHNC` they scramble every received block; with fewer heads than `block_size_ratio` the reshape fails.
- `post_process_device_kv_on_receive`: zero the untransferred tail along the token dim, not the head dim.
- `kv_postprocess_blksize_and_layout_on_receive` (`enable_permute_local_kv`): read the received bytes in memory order before viewing them as the remote's head-major blocks. It now also serves ratio 1 and replaces `kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive`, which had the same bug and a 5-D branch from #47791 that is dead since #51718.
- `enable_permute_local_kv` is enabled only for a local `LBNHC` cache; any other local layout (e.g. head-major `BLHNC`) now fails the handshake instead of receiving wrong KV.
- HMA groups alias the same KV tensors, but each group's block ids went through every attention view, regrouping a block once per aliasing group. Each group now uses its own views.
- `LBNHC`/`BLNHC` receive the remote sub-blocks in token order; only `is_block_contiguous` layouts are regrouped.

Block lists that start or end at different tokens on P and D are paired in #59746. No other open PR changes the receive post-process.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -k test_post_process_zeroes_untransferred_tail
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k test_handshake_fails_on_kv_cache_layout_mismatch
```

The test now holds distinct values in a `[B, H, N, C]` cache with fewer KV heads than the ratio, aliased by two attention groups, on `LBHNC`, `LBNHC` and `LBNHC` + `enable_permute_local_kv`.

GB10: P and D on one GPU, pull, greedy, `--enforce-eager`. Each run is compared with P and D both at D's block size, without `enable_permute_local_kv`; D loads the whole prompt over NIXL, except the last token on GDN or with #59330.

## Test Result

CPU, main `0cbac6cd13`: the 3 cases pass, and reverting any one fix fails at least one of them. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

GB10, main `0cbac6cd13`:
- Qwen3-0.6B, FLASH_ATTN, `LBHNC`, P 16 / D 64: 0/6 outputs match.
- `LBHNC` P to `LBNHC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`, 64/64: 0/6.
- Gemma-4-E2B-it, TRITON_ATTN, 1 KV head, 16/64: D's EngineCore fails with `shape '[-1, 4, 128, 0, 512]' is invalid`.

GB10, this PR at `ef0cc618a0` on main `0cbac6cd13`, logprobs bitwise equal:
- Qwen3-0.6B 16/64 on `LBHNC`, `BLHNC`, `LBNHC`, and `LBHNC` P to `LBNHC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`, the last also at 64/64: 6/6 each.
- Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN), FLASH_ATTN, 544/1088: 6/6, also with two attention groups forced by a local grouping hook.
- Gemma-4-E2B-it 16/64 no longer crashes; 4/7 outputs still differ in text. With #59746 and #59330: 7/7.

GB10, main `dd30786fef` + this PR's files at `0ccf122132`, MiniCPM5-2B (2 KV heads), `LBHNC` P to `BLHNC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`: main crashes D at 16/64; without the handshake check, 0/4 outputs match at 16/64 and 64/64 with no error. With it, the handshake fails and D keeps serving; an `LBNHC` D stays bitwise equal (4/4) at both.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, patch and tests. I reviewed every changed line.

title: [Perf][Model Loader] Fault in mmap'd weight pages before host-to-device copies on integrated GPUs
author: Willian-Zhang
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58726.

On integrated GPUs (DGX Spark / GB10), the shared weight loaders copy each checkpoint tensor to the GPU with `param.copy_(loaded_weight)` straight from the safetensors mmap view. For a contiguous, same-dtype source, PyTorch passes that pageable pointer directly to the driver copy, so the page faults happen inside the copy. On GB10 that is several times slower than faulting the same pages on the CPU first: 1.7–3.0 ms vs 0.08–0.64 ms per 800 KiB tensor in #58726. `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` has at least 140k such tensors, and its main weight load takes 452 s from NFS and 475 s from local NVMe.

This adds `copy_weight_(dst, src)` to `vllm/model_executor/utils.py`. On an integrated GPU it touches one byte per page of `src`, then runs `dst.copy_(src)`. It is used at the 26 copy sites of the shared loaders: `linear.py` (8), `parameter.py` (6), `routed_experts.py` (8), `vocab_parallel_embedding.py` (2) and `default_weight_loader` (2).

- **Gate:** `current_platform.is_integrated_gpu()` for a CUDA destination, cached per device. On a discrete Ada Lovelace GPU the same micro-benchmark shows the plain copy is fastest in every cache state, and the touch adds 0.022–0.028 ms per tensor, so it stays off there. When off, the extra checks cost ~0.46 µs per call (0.91 vs 0.45 µs for a 16-byte CPU copy), about 0.14 s per 300k tensors.
- **Only contiguous, same-dtype CPU sources are touched.** Non-contiguous or dtype-converting copies already go through a CPU temporary in PyTorch (`copy_requires_temporaries` in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu`), which faults the pages on the CPU.
- **Why at the copy site rather than in `safetensors_weights_iterator`** (discussed with @gitbisector in #58726):
  - Under TP each rank touches only the slice it copies. A prefault in the iterator read whole tensors: ~287 GiB per rank on DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4, and a slower load at the default `read_ahead_kb=128`.
  - The touch runs right before the copy, so a consumer that buffers the weight stream can't have the pages evicted in between.
  - Tensors a model serves from the mapping (#58439) are never copied, so they are never touched, and no size cap is needed.
- **Not covered:** model-specific loaders that call `.copy_()` or `.to(device)` themselves keep today's behaviour until they call the helper. Its docstring says to. @stecasta routed one such out-of-tree expert loader through it: ~55 GiB of copies moved onto the touch path, and its weight loading took about 70% less time. @JimmyToluene found an in-tree one, the Qwen4Exp PLE shard copy in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/ple.py`; routing it through the helper is a follow-up.
- **Measured only on GB10** (TP=1 below, TP=4 by @gitbisector). Other integrated devices, such as Jetson Orin / Thor, will take the touch path but are untested. I haven't checked what GH200 reports as `is_integrated`; if it reports 0, nothing changes there.

## Test Plan

- New tests in `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`:
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_copies_exact_bytes`: with the gate forced on, the helper accepts 0-d, empty, bf16, fp8 and dim-1-narrowed sources and copies them byte for byte. CI has no integrated GPU, so this is the only coverage of that path.
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_maps_the_mmap_view`: after the call, every page of a safetensors view is mapped (`/proc/self/smaps` Rss of the file mapping). With the touch disabled it fails: 64 KiB mapped vs 4 MiB.
- Existing CPU-runnable loader tests, before and after the change.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files, including `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.
- Boot A/B on a DGX Spark.

```bash
# CPU only, repo on PYTHONPATH inside vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 (torch 2.13.0+cu130), no GPU
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w:ro -e PYTHONPATH=/w -w /w --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 -c \
  "uv pip install --system -q tblib pytest && python3 -m pytest -q \
   tests/model_executor/test_utils.py \
   tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py"

pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`: 18 passed (12 existing, 6 new).
- Loader tests: 216 passed, 5 skipped. 38 tests fail with and without the change, the same set on both, all because the container has no GPU:
  - 18 error at setup with `Failed to infer device type`.
  - 18 `test_reload` cases fail because `current_platform.device_count` is `None`.
  - 2 `test_fp8_tp_default_keeps_refined_layout[*-triton]` cases can't confirm the Triton kernel, so the layer pads its TP shard instead of refining the block shape.
- `pre-commit` and `mypy-3.12` passed.

### Boot A/B, DGX Spark (GB10), TP=1

Nine full server boots of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, interleaved, with the client page cache for the checkpoint dropped before each one.

- **Build:** the image is vLLM v0.30.0 plus out-of-tree patches, not `main`. The helper is copied from this branch and applied to v0.30.0's copies of the same files (25 sites; v0.30.0's `_load_w2` has no chunk loop). It predates a cleanup that renamed the gate function and dropped a redundant `numel() > 0` check, which doesn't change behaviour here. A counting wrapper, not part of this PR, logged the gate and how many copies were touched.
- **Out-of-tree patches on in every arm:** the expert-name index (= #58720, merged), an MTP name prefilter, and the PLE table served from the mapping (never copied).
- **Storage:** NFS with the client's `read_ahead_kb` at 16384, or local NVMe at the default 128.

| loader | storage | main load (s) | MTP load (s) | start → `/health` (s) | swapped out, start → KV profile (GiB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | NFS | 451.8 | 36.1 | 584 | 4.4 |
| this PR (3 boots) | NFS | 25.9 / 27.0 / 28.0 | 0.8 | 124–129 | 3.6–4.3 |
| stock | NVMe | 475.2 | 31.7 | 609 | 4.2 |
| this PR (2 boots) | NVMe | 46.4 / 54.5 | 2.6–2.9 | 149–153 | 3.2–4.0 |
| *out-of-tree, for reference: `pread` tensors ≤ 64 MiB in the iterator, clone / chunked copy above that* | NFS / NVMe | 21.0 / 88.5 | 1.2 / 1.3 | 113 / 179 | 0 / 0 |

- The gate logged `cuda:0 = True` in every boot with this PR. By the counter's last line (140,000 calls), 139,965 copies (63.4 GiB) had been touched. The other 35 were copies PyTorch stages through a CPU temporary anyway.
- Greedy outputs (5 prompts × 400 tokens, temperature 0) and first-token logprobs are identical in all nine boots, and decode speed is unchanged. No accuracy eval was run here: the touch only reads the source, so the loaded weights are byte-identical (unit test above). @stecasta's GSM8K run is below.
- Swap: loading from mmap views pushes 3.2–4.4 GiB of other memory to swap on this 128 GB machine, and stock loading does it as much as this PR. The pread variant doesn't map the files and doesn't swap. vLLM counts the swapped-out memory as free when it sizes the KV cache. I haven't looked into why the kernel swaps here.

### TP=1, warm cache (from @hclsys, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5919067348))

`Qwen3-1.7B` on one GB10, `load_format=safetensors`, `enforce_eager`, page cache warm, fresh process per run, this branch vs its merge-base `77871126f9`.

| | `Loading weights took` | `LLM()` init |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge-base (3 runs) | 20.2–23.7 s | 44.4–54.8 s |
| this PR (2 runs) | 0.50 / 0.69 s | 26.3 / 29.4 s |

The third base run came after the PR runs, so the difference isn't cache order. With the cache warm the time isn't disk reads but the faults taken through a fresh mapping during the copy. On a discrete RTX PRO 6000 the touch makes no difference, ~0.1 ms per tensor either way (@gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58726#issuecomment-5918595410)).

### TP=1, cold cache (from @stecasta, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#pullrequestreview-5496877797))

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` with a DFlash2 drafter on one GB10, v0.31.0 plus internal patches with this PR applied as a Python overlay. Checkpoint on local disk (`read_ahead_kb=128`), page cache dropped before every boot, two boots per arm.

| | `Loading weights took`, main model | `Model loading took` | start → `/health` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | 96.5 / 96.7 s | 122 / 122 s | 595 / 591 s |
| this PR | 9.5 / 9.8 s | 16 / 16 s | 486 / 486 s |

GSM8K-256 with this PR: 244/256, in line with stock. Minimum `MemAvailable` (~38.5 GiB) and peak swap (0.5 GiB) during load were the same in both arms.

### TP=1 on a `main`-based nightly (from @jschmied, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5865989952))

RadixArk's ModelOpt NVFP4/FP8 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (120 GB, 206 files) on local NVMe at `read_ahead_kb` 128, nightly `1ea7c63f4` with this PR's diff (all 26 sites), 2 cold starts per arm, alternating. Main weight load 504.9 / 534.0 s stock, 65.9 / 64.9 s with this PR. With the expert-name index from #58720 (merged after `1ea7c63f4`) as well, 41.6 / 41.9 s ([data](https://github.com/jschmied/qwen38-flash-next-gb10/blob/1313d7b4b458f9e0462f0d79c02323663cbacdfd/notes/data/fastload/fastload.txt)). Greedy output identical in every start.

### TP=1, cold cache, current head (from @JimmyToluene, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-6349449742))

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (103 GiB, 299,817 tensors) on one GB10, nightly `21d93d0d8c0e` with this PR at `f66f2108c`. Local NVMe at `read_ahead_kb=128`, page cache dropped before each boot, one boot per arm. In stock, py-spy put 97.7% of load samples on the two expert `copy_` lines in `routed_experts.py`, with no I/O wait.

| | stock | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| main `Loading weights took` | 660.7 s | 71.3 s |
|  routed experts, 70.6 GB | 435 s | 52 s |
|  dense, 10.3 GB | 63 s | 5 s |
|  PLE n-gram table, 28.8 GB | 160 s | 14 s\* |
| MTP drafter load | 82.8 s | 55.5 s |
| start → `/health` | 969 s | 345 s |

\* With one more call site, the PLE shard copy in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/ple.py`, routed through `copy_weight_`. This PR doesn't change that file, so on its own the PLE table stays on the stock path.

Teacher-forced logprobs of 16 fixed generations (3,761 tokens) differ from stock by mean |Δlogprob| 0.034 (p99 0.37), the same as stock against itself.

### TP=4 (from @gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5852543296))

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on four GB10s, this PR ported to a v0.28.1-based build (25 of the 26 sites), load-only boots, page cache dropped before each, arms interleaved. Times are `Model loading took` on the slowest rank.

| `read_ahead_kb` | boots | stock | this PR | read per rank vs stock |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 3 + 3 | 192–195 s | 156–161 s (−18%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 128 | 3 + 3 | 205–207 s | 149–151 s (−27%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 1024, consumer that sorts the stream | 1 + 1 | 248 s | 225 s | +2–10 GiB |

At 128 the iterator-level prefault made this load slower (202 → 241 s) because every rank read whole tensors (~287 GiB); at the copy site each rank reads about what stock reads. Most of the gain is the slowest rank catching up: in stock, the ranks holding slices 0 and 2 lag by 25–60 s on small same-dtype slices (expert scales, FP8 attention rows). The routed experts there are `I8` loaded into `uint8` params, a converting copy that PyTorch already stages on the CPU, so the helper touches 5.6 of 72.3 GiB per rank.

## Duplicate-work check

- No open PR references #58726; searches for "prefault", "integrated gpu weight loading" and "mmap page fault copy" found none that change these copy sites.
- #49991 (ROCm, clones in the iterator behind an env flag, for a KFD copy-on-write issue) and #50794 (Ascend, clones before the H2D copy to avoid a DMA hang) handle the same copies on other platforms, for different causes.
- #57973 (safetensors prefetch loader) and #55985 (fastsafetensors fit planner) are alternative load paths.
- #58857 / #58782 remove the `sorted()` buffering in the DeepSeek-V4 VL wrappers; complementary to this.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Split fused_wqa_wkv by token across TP ranks on SM90
author: ShuoleiWang
body:
## Purpose

Without sequence parallelism, every TP rank computes DeepSeek-V4.1's `fused_wqa_wkv` (5120 → 1280 + 512) for all tokens, so all ranks do the same work. The checkpoint stores this weight as FP8 with UE8M0 block scales, which vLLM runs through its MXFP8 path. On SM90 that path is a W8A16 Marlin GEMM: on H20 it takes 1.79 ms per layer for an 8192-token prefill chunk, 72 ms per chunk over the 40 layers.

This PR splits the projection by token for batches of at least 2048 tokens. Each rank projects its token shard (`sp_shard`), and `sp_all_gather` rebuilds `qr_kv`. The change is confined to `DeepseekV4Attention._fused_wqa_wkv_gemm`:
- `_run_parallel_input_projections` is unchanged, so the multi-stream decision is the same as on main.
- The all-gather is issued on the current stream, right after the GEMM that produces its input.

`_shard_fused_wqa_wkv` in the NVIDIA decoder layer enables the split only when all of the following hold:
- **SM90.** On SM100, `fused_wqa_wkv` runs as a native MXFP8 GEMM, far cheaper than W8A16 Marlin, so the gather would be a much larger share of the cost. I have not measured SM100, and the H20 results below do not carry over to it.
- **No sequence parallelism.** There the hidden states are already sharded, and #57257 splits this projection for that case.
- **No LoRA.** The LoRA wrapper maps every token of the batch.
- **No micro-batching.** Two micro-batches would share the custom all-gather buffer.
- **No batch invariance.** Whether a token takes the split depends on the batch size.
- **The custom all-reduce is enabled and fully connected.** This serves only as a proxy for NVLink between all TP ranks. From 6144 tokens at TP8, the shard exceeds the custom all-gather's 2 MiB limit, so the gather itself runs on NCCL.

TP4 and TP2 take the same gate but were not measured. On Hopper they need pipeline parallelism to hold the checkpoint.

The compressor's `fused_wkv_wgate` and the indexer's `weights_proj` stay replicated, and `_run_parallel_input_projections`, which can run them on separate streams, is unchanged. They appear in only a few layers:
- the compressor in the 4 KV-source layers (2, 8, 14, 20);
- the indexer in the 8 index-source layers, which are those four plus 24, 28, 32 and 36.

At 8192 tokens, splitting them as well would save at most another 457 µs in a KV-source layer (last column of the second table; layer 20's compressor is half as wide). In the four indexer-only layers the projection is only 5120 → 32. This PR saves about 1.45 ms in each of the 40 layers, so it limits the split to this dominant projection.

**Why 2048 tokens.** On H20 the split is faster from 48 tokens (first table below). H100 and H200 have about 6.7 times H20's dense throughput with the same 900 GB/s NVLink, so the replicated GEMM costs much less there while the gather costs the same.

I have no H100 or H200 to measure on, so I scaled the H20 numbers pessimistically:
- a GEMM of 1024 rows or more runs 6.7 times faster than on H20;
- one of 512 rows runs 3.7 times faster, and one of 256 rows or fewer only twice as fast;
- the gather runs no faster.

Under these assumptions the break-even is about 1450 tokens, and 2048 is the next power of two. A measurement on H100 or H200 would confirm or retune it.

**Related work.** I found no upstream PR for the case without sequence parallelism. The fork commit bytedance-iaas/vllm@383776ac20 splits `fused_wqa_wkv` the same way, but behind an environment variable that is off by default, and not when speculative decoding is on.

## Test Plan

**Kernel benchmark.** Setup:
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink), TP8.
- Software: torch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7, vLLM nightly `0.30.1rc1.dev85+g8b84e1506` with this diff applied as a Python overlay.
- What it runs: `fused_wqa_wkv` is built as the model builds it, with random weights and the checkpoint's quantization, so SM90 runs Marlin. The second table times `_run_parallel_input_projections` from this branch, which calls `_fused_wqa_wkv_gemm`, with the model's projection shapes and three aux streams.

Timing follows `.agents/skills/kernel-microbenchmark`:
- One CUDA graph per candidate.
- Before every measured replay, an L2 flush (twice the L2 size) and a device-side barrier, both outside the timed interval.
- The time of a replay is the CUPTI span of its kernels. Each sample is the maximum over the 8 ranks, and the tables report the median of 50 samples.
- Candidates alternate within every round, and correctness is checked before timing.

The benchmark script is not part of this PR; I can add it under `benchmarks/kernels/` if that helps.

**Serving.** TP8 without expert parallelism. DSpark uses synthetic acceptance with a mean acceptance length of 3.51, the same distribution in both arms:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

One `vllm bench serve` call per point:

| Point | ISL | OSL | C | N |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K / 32K / 128K prompt TTFT | 8192 / 32768 / 131072 | 1 | 1 | 5 / 3 / 2 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | 1024 | 1024 | 1 | 6 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | 1024 | 1024 | 64 | 192 |
| 8K in / 1K out, C16 | 8192 | 1024 | 16 | 48 |
| 8K in / 1K out, C64 | 8192 | 1024 | 64 | 128 |

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --num-warmups <C> --seed 1
```

Each arm ran on a fresh server, in the order this PR (B1), main (A1), main (A2), this PR (B2).

**Accuracy.** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions) through `/v1/chat/completions`, with real DSpark verification (`rejection_sample_method: block`) instead of synthetic acceptance:
- 5-shot multi-turn chat with thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking": false}`);
- temperature 0, seed 123, `max_tokens` 1024, 32 concurrent requests;
- each reply is scored by the number after `####`, or else by its last number.

## Test Result

**`fused_wqa_wkv`, split vs replicated** (µs per call, TP8, every batch size split so the crossover is visible):

| Tokens | Rows per rank | Replicated | Split + all-gather | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 1 | 14.1 | 23.2 | 0.61x |
| 12 | 2 | 14.6 | 23.1 | 0.63x |
| 24 | 3 | 19.2 | 21.1 | 0.91x |
| 48 | 6 | 25.9 | 20.3 | 1.28x |
| 96 | 12 | 49.6 | 21.5 | 2.31x |
| 384 | 48 | 99.7 | 35.8 | 2.78x |
| 1024 | 128 | 239.4 | 66.8 | 3.58x |
| 2048 | 256 | 458.5 | 99.7 | 4.60x |
| 4096 | 512 | 903.6 | 173.3 | 5.22x |
| 8192 | 1024 | 1794.7 | 346.9 | 5.17x |
| 16384 | 2048 | 3570.8 | 635.4 | 5.62x |

Up to 4096 tokens the gather is the custom all-reduce's all-gather; from 6144 tokens it is NCCL. From 4096 tokens on, the replicated Marlin GEMM runs at 83–84 TFLOPS.

**Input projections of one attention layer, main vs this PR** (µs; only this stage is timed, not the whole layer):

| Tokens | Layer without compressor or indexer (32 layers): main | This PR | Speedup | Layer with compressor and indexer (layers 2, 8, 14): main | This PR | Speedup | If compressor and indexer were also split |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 236.7 | 236.5 | same code | 337.6 | 337.7 | same code | 337.5 |
| 1536 | 351.1 | 348.8 | same code | 478.5 | 480.6 | same code | 481.1 |
| 2048 | 458.1 | 99.9 | 4.59x | 660.4 | 301.8 | 2.19x | 198.3 |
| 4096 | 903.0 | 172.7 | 5.23x | 1276.2 | 545.9 | 2.34x | 343.5 |
| 8192 | 1794.2 | 346.0 | 5.19x | 2473.9 | 1028.4 | 2.41x | 571.6 |
| 16384 | 3569.4 | 635.6 | 5.62x | 4902.1 | 1976.6 | 2.48x | 1052.3 |

- **Estimate per 8K prefill chunk:** this stage gets about 1.45 ms faster in every layer, about 58 ms over the 40 layers. The serving results below are the measurement.
- **Correctness:** `qr_kv` differs from the replicated projection by at most 0.031 across two sweeps with different inputs. That is bf16 rounding from Marlin's M-dependent tiling. `kv_score` and `indexer_weights` are bitwise identical to main.

**Serving and accuracy.** The serving numbers are a sanity check with two servers per arm, not a precise measurement. Lower TTFT and higher output throughput are better, and Change compares the means of the two arms.

| Point | Metric | main A1 | main A2 | this PR B1 | this PR B2 | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT, 8K prompt, C1 | ms | 1117.8 | 1117.8 | 1066.5 | 1075.2 | −4.2% |
| TTFT, 32K prompt, C1 | ms | 4535.6 | 4559.3 | 4320.5 | 4322.3 | −5.0% |
| TTFT, 128K prompt, C1 | ms | 19648 | 19680 | 18859 | 18807 | −4.2% |
| 8K in / 1K out, C16 | output tok/s | 601.1 | 602.1 | 621.4 | 620.8 | +3.2% |
| 8K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 709.9 | 709.4 | 739.0 | 739.4 | +4.2% |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 1983.8 | 1987.6 | 2014.9 | 2010.1 | +1.4% |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | output tok/s | 335.2 | 335.2 | 338.0 | 334.1 | +0.2% |

At 1K in / 1K out, C1, no batch reaches 2048 tokens, so both arms run main's kernels. The two servers of this PR differ by 1.2% there, more than the gap between the arms.

| GSM8K, 5-shot chat, greedy (1,319 questions) | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Accuracy | 96.59% (1274) | 96.97% (1279) |
| DSpark acceptance length | 3.867 | 3.863 |

In three runs of main on the same nightly, one of them the run above, GSM8K accuracy ranged from 96.36% to 96.97%.

title: [Metrics][P/D] Add KV-fetch stage gauges for async KV loads
author: liuzijing2014
body:
## Purpose

Requests waiting on an async KV load (a P/D decode request pulling KV from the prefiller, or a `MultiConnector` child loading from a KV store) only show up as `num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="deferred"}`, together with LoRA, grammar and streaming waits. When decode TTFT goes up, there is no way to tell whether the transfer hasn't started yet, is in flight, or already finished and the request is just waiting for a run slot.

This adds `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage{stage}`, a per-engine gauge that is registered only when a KV connector is configured:

- `waiting_to_start`: the request needs an async load (remote prefill requested, or an async match confirmed) that hasn't started
- `in_progress`: the load started and hasn't been reported finished
- `completed_waiting`: the load finished (or failed under `recompute`), but the request isn't running yet

The stages are tracked in the scheduler, so this works for any async connector. The counts also show up in the periodic stats log. Related to #58004, which covers the producer side.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py
```

E2E: 1P1D with `NixlConnector` and `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`. The decoder runs with `--max-num-seqs 2`, gets two long requests first and then a burst, so the burst arrives while it is saturated. Same again with `--data-parallel-size 2` on the decoder.

## Test Result

All pass on one GPU, except the two pipeline-parallel tests in `test_scheduler.py` that need 2-3 GPUs (same on main).

E2E: all requests succeeded, and every stage went back to 0 after the run. Peak values on the decoder:

| Decoder | waiting_to_start | in_progress | completed_waiting |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP=1 | 48 | 2 | 46 |
| DP=2, engine 0 / 1 | 32 / 32 | 2 / 32 | 30 / 30 |

The prefiller stayed at 0, since its requests have no async load. The aggregated log line looks like `2 Engines Aggregated: ... KV fetch: 64 waiting to start, 0 in progress, 0 completed waiting`.

title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Count completion notifications that arrive after KV expiry
author: liuzijing2014
body:
## Purpose

When a transfer completion notification arrives for a request the worker no longer tracks, NIXL logs an error and moves on. With the pull connector, this is the prefiller hearing from a decoder that finished reading a request whose KV lease had already expired (`Potentially invalid KV blocks for unrecognized request ...`), so the decoder may have read blocks that were already reused. The push connector has the same path (`Unrecognized request ... notif (may have expired)`). Today both are only log lines.

This adds `vllm:nixl_num_notifications_after_expiry`, a per-engine counter incremented once per such notification, in both the pull and push workers. It is kept separate from `nixl_num_failed_transfers` (transfers that fail outright) and `nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs`, and it is documented in the NIXL usage guide next to them.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

E2E: 1P1D with `NixlConnector` and `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, with `kv_lease_duration=2` on the prefiller. Three normal requests, then three decoder reads that only start after the lease has expired.

## Test Result

All 248 pass.

E2E, counters on the prefiller:

| | `nixl_num_notifications_after_expiry` | `nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs` | "Potentially invalid" log lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| after 3 normal requests | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| after 3 late reads | 3 | 3 | 3 |

title: [Kernel] Enable OAI Triton MXFP4 MoE on SM12x
author: wtdcode
body:
## Purpose

Disclaimer: The code was largely assisted by Claude Code but the PR itself is handwritten and well tested.

In general, this PR is a follow-up to #41028.

#41028 tries to allow sm120 to use Triton kernels for GPT-OSS models instead of Marlin kernels. However, current implementation of triton kernels does not work on sm12x out-of-box and this PR fixes this. By testing on an RTX 5090:

- Decode speed is the same.
- Triton prefilling is 10% slower than Marlin kernels.The root cause is that the smem is too small for a larger tile for Triton. 
- Triton kernel earns +8% kvcache pool because Marlin kernel needs more space for alignment.

Therefore, this PR still keeps Marlin kernel as the default implementation, but allows sm12x to use Trition kernels if users would like the kvcache benefits by `--moe-backend triton`.

cc @Harry-Chen 

## Test Plan

CI, unit test.

See above.

title: [Perf][MoE] Use fused MiniMax2 routing with non-unit routed scaling
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

`get_routing_method_type` maps sigmoid + correction bias + renormalize routing (no expert groups) to `RoutingMethodType.MiniMax2` only when `routed_scaling_factor` is 1.0 (added in #44347). MiniMax-M3 uses `routed_scaling_factor=2.0`, so its MoE falls back to `Unspecified`. On SM100 with the MXFP8 checkpoint, that means the modular TRT-LLM path: a separate vLLM `topk_sigmoid` launch per MoE layer, then `trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`.

The restriction is no longer needed with the pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0:
- FlashInfer's MiniMax2 routing uses `routed_scaling_factor` as its route scale: final weight = `sigmoid(x) * routeScale / sum` (`trtllm_fused_moe_routing_runner.cu`: `routingData.mRouteScale = routedScalingFactor`).
- Every monolithic TRT-LLM caller that accepts MiniMax2 already passes `routed_scaling_factor` through: FP8 block scale / MXFP8, FP8 per-tensor, and NVFP4.
- The scale is not applied twice. When `apply_routed_scale_to_output` is false, which is the M3 case, the scale goes to the router and the runner gets 1.0.

This PR removes the restriction, and with it the now-unused `routed_scaling_factor` argument of `get_routing_method_type`.

The restriction also, by accident, kept zero-expert models (`ZeroExpertRouter`) off kernels with built-in routing whenever their scale was not 1.0. Those kernels cannot reproduce zero-expert handling, and with scale 1.0 such a model was already mapped to MiniMax2. `ZeroExpertRouter.routing_method_type` now returns `Unspecified` explicitly.

Effect: any model with sigmoid + bias + renormalize routing, no expert groups, and a non-unit scale becomes eligible for the monolithic TRT-LLM kernels on Blackwell. MiniMax-M3 is one such model. The routing semantics are the same as vLLM's `fused_topk_bias`: biased scores select the experts, unbiased sigmoid gives the weights, which are renormalized and scaled.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for `MiniMax2 routed_scaling_factor`, `MiniMax-M3 routing trtllm`, `minimax m3 moe routing fused` and `RoutingMethodType MiniMax2`. Nothing touches this mapping. The related merged PRs are #39141 and #44347, and #44347 introduced the restriction.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Routing-method unit tests (new: MiniMax2 with scale 2.0, zero-expert -> Unspecified)
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k "routing or degenerate or grouped or zero or minimax"
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py -k routing_method

# New GPU test (SM100): monolithic MXFP8 TRT-LLM with fused MiniMax2 routing and
# routed_scaling_factor=2.0 vs modular TRT-LLM with vLLM fused_topk_bias routing
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py -k "minimax2_routing or deferred_finalize"

# End to end, MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP4 on 4x GB300, this branch vs main
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 -tp 4 --max-model-len 8192
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
    --ignore-eos --max-concurrency {1,8} --num-prompts {16,128}
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests:**
- `test_routing.py`: 507 passed.
- The routing-method test in `test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py` passed.
- `test_flashinfer.py -k "minimax2_routing or deferred_finalize"`: 6 passed on GB300.
- Both new routing tests fail without the source change.
- The new FlashInfer test fails if the fused path ignores the scale: about 80% of elements mismatch, with a max abs diff of 0.39.
- pre-commit passes.

**Backend actually selected** (server log, MiniMax-M3-MXFP8):
- main: `Using MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular`

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Use prefiller cache hits for P/D usage
author: thuongvu
body:
## Purpose
Fix `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` in Rust P/D responses.

The decoder currently counts KV received from the prefiller as cached tokens. That can make a cold request look fully cached, even though the prefiller computed the entire prompt.

The Python frontend already handles this through `remote_prefill_cached_tokens` (#54222). This change reads the same metadata in Rust and uses it for response usage:

- Use the prefiller's count when `do_remote_prefill` is `true`, including an explicit zero. The parameters are read through a small typed view, so a non-boolean flag or a count that is not a non-negative integer leaves the decoder's count in place.
- Keep the existing decoder count when no usable override is available.
- Include `cached_tokens: 0` when prompt-token details are enabled. This also applies to ordinary local requests.
- Keep decoder metrics based on the raw engine statistics.

No new wire fields or prompt-length upper clamp are added.

Related-work searches found no matching open Rust fix. #58730 proposes bounds handling in Python; #56318 concerns cache-source metrics.

## Test Plan
From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p vllm-llm -p vllm-server --lib --tests
cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-llm -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
```
The added tests cover metadata parsing, positive and zero overrides, missing-count fallback, streamed and collected usage, unchanged decoder metrics, and explicit-zero JSON serialization.

## Test Result
Validated against `a9eafde59cbd`:

- The mock-engine regression fails without the fix and passes with it.
- 454 tests passed: 15 LLM unit, 11 LLM integration, and 428 server tests.
- Clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed.

Also tested with real NIXL transfers on two H100 GPUs using Qwen3-0.6B. Across chat and completions, streaming and non-streaming, eight baseline cases reproduced the bug and eight patched cases reported the correct prefiller count. Detailed setup and results are in the follow-up comment.

This PR was written in part with the assistance of generative AI.

title: [Perf][MoE] Cheaper triton_kernels 3.8 routing build in the OAI Triton MoE
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Purpose

On triton_kernels 3.8, which every ROCm build ships since #50605, the MoE routing metadata is rebuilt in torch with an int64 stable `argsort` and a `scatter_add_` histogram, costing 31–178 µs per MoE layer per step on MI355X / MI325X.

- `make_routing_data` sorts the ids in their own dtype and reads per-expert counts off the sorted keys with `searchsorted` instead of an atomic histogram. This path runs under expert parallelism and in `UnfusedOAITritonExperts`, which DeepSeek-V4 uses whenever AITER's MXFP4 MoE does not apply — on gfx942 that includes `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.
- `routing_data_from_sparse_topk` (gpt-oss without EP) reuses the `col_sum` / `col_sorted_indx` of the `SparseMatrix` that `triton_kernels.topk` already returned, as the 3.6 path does since #45457.

The routing metadata is identical to main's. CUDA is unaffected: it pins triton_kernels v3.5.1, and only the 3.8 branches change.

## Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_gpt_oss_triton_kernels.py tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py
```

44 passed on both main (`74f4404f58`) and the PR, on MI325X. The new `test_make_routing_data_tk38_matches_reference` checks the 3.8 build against a stable sort plus `bincount`, including `-1` slots, and fails if the `-1` clamp is removed while every other test still passes; `test_routing_data_from_sparse_topk_parity` no longer skips on 3.8.

## Measurements

Routing call under CUDA-graph replay, 1000 rows, µs (MI355X / MI325X):

| path | main | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash rebuild | 104 / 142 | 61 / 80 |
| gpt-oss-120b `topk` + routing | 132 / 176 | 32 / 44 |

e2e, TP=1, `vllm bench serve`, Δ of medians vs main:

| model | GPU | concurrency | total tok/s | mean TPOT | median TPOT | median TTFT |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | MI355X | 37 | +2.2 % | −2.6 % | −2.5 % | −0.3 % |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (AITER on) | MI325X | 37 | +1.4 % | −1.9 % | −1.7 % | −0.2 % |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (AITER on) | MI325X | 101 | +2.0 % | −1.7 % | −1.7 % | −0.1 % |
| gpt-oss-120b | MI355X | 61 | +9.7 % | −10.5 % | −11.1 % | −0.5 % |
| gpt-oss-120b | MI325X | 61 | +6.0 % | −5.8 % | −6.0 % | −1.2 % |

Throughput and TPOT ranges are disjoint in every row except MI325X DeepSeek-V4-Flash at concurrency 37, where they touch at the edges. TTFT is flat, so the gain is in decode.

GSM8K strict-match (5-shot, 1319 questions), PR vs main runs: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0.9522 vs 0.9538 / 0.9522 (MI355X) and 0.9538 vs 0.9560 / 0.9500 (MI325X); gpt-oss-120b 0.2782 vs 0.2881 / 0.2691 (MI355X) and 0.2654 / 0.2737 vs 0.2547–0.2805 (MI325X). The PR stays inside the main-vs-main spread. Llama-3.1-8B, which does not reach this path, moves by at most 0.0023.

vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev143+g29468dde8` image (triton 3.8.0, aiter 0.1.22.post1); main `027b6f3a22` on MI355X, `ccfd1cea75` on MI325X. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset except where noted. title: [ROCm][Model][Bugfix] Fix GLM-5.2 shared-expert fusion and MTP on the ROCm DSA path
author: jin-amd
body:
#51915 aliased `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` onto `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/`. That enabled GLM-5.2-MXFP4 there, but it also moved GLM-5.2-FP8 onto a path missing two things the model needs, so the AMD command from the [GLM-5.2 recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/zai-org/GLM-5.2) now fails twice on ROCm:

1. **`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` can't load the checkpoint** — `KeyError: 'layers.10.mlp.shared_experts.down_proj.weight'`. With fusion on, the checkpoint gives one widened `mlp.shared_experts` tensor per layer. `deepseek_v2.py` splits it into the expert slots appended after the routed experts, but `DeepseekV32Model` subclasses `torch.nn.Module` rather than `DeepseekV2Model`, reimplements `load_weights`, and has no equivalent handling.

2. **MTP kills the engine on the first request** — `AttributeError: 'DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor' object has no attribute 'compact_topk_indices'`. `llm_base_proposer` calls that method once `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is set, which GLM-5.2's config sets. `nvidia/mtp.py` implements it; `amd/mtp.py` never did.

Before #51915, GLM-5.2 fell through to the generic `deepseek_v2` implementation on ROCm, which handles both. This adds the missing pieces rather than changing the routing, so MXFP4 keeps the AMD path.

## Changes

- `amd/model.py`: set `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled`, size the expert params mapping to `n_routed_experts + n_shared_experts`, and split the widened shared-expert tensor into `mlp.experts.{n_routed_experts + j}` — dim 0 for the ColumnParallel gate/up, dim 1 for the RowParallel down. Ported from `deepseek_v2.py` to keep both paths consistent.
- `amd/mtp.py`: add `compact_topk_indices`, matching `nvidia/mtp.py`. The ROCm attention already maintains `skip_topk` and `topk_indices_buffer`, so it ports over unchanged.

## Test Plan

8x MI325X (gfx942), `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, recipe AMD command unmodified (fusion on, 5-token MTP on). Baseline `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` at `0.30.1rc1.dev143+g29468dde8`; patched run is the same image with these two files replaced.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter
```

## Test Result

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Weight loading | `KeyError` at `layers.10` | completes |
| KV cache @ 524288 | n/a | 1,668,416 tokens, 3.18x concurrency |
| First request | `AttributeError`, engine dies | returns normally |
| MTP | unusable | active, mean acceptance length 3.41 |

Correctness checked too, since a bad tensor split would give fluent-but-wrong output rather than an error: `17 * 23` → `391`, capital of Peru → `Lima`, `Is 91 prime?` → 822 chars of reasoning then the correct 7 x 13, and a correct three-sentence Rayleigh-scattering answer with `enable_thinking: false`. The `glm47` parsers behave as before.

I only have gfx942, so MI300X and MI355X are untested — the changed code is shared ROCm model code with no gfx-specific branching, but an MI355X run from someone would be welcome. MXFP4 on the AMD path is untouched here but likewise unverified.

title: [Bugfix][Compile] Replace Transformers AOT caching with graph caching
author: Taimys
body:
## Purpose

Fix compilation caching for the Transformers backend by running Dynamo tracing on each startup while reusing PyTorch graph caches.

Decorated HF `forward` methods can fail model-AOT serialization. Disabling model AOT alone is insufficient: direct artifact lookup can reuse stale compiled code when decorator state changes between processes.

Following the review suggestion, HF opts out through `support_torch_compile(..., use_aot_compile=False)`. The option is passed explicitly through `init_backend` to the backend, compiler manager, and adaptors:

- Skip model AOT, mega artifacts, and direct artifact loading/saving, including existing cache-index lookup.
- Retain PyTorch graph caching and initialize persistent Inductor/Triton cache directories.
- Preserve native AOT caching, including native EAGLE3 drafts under an HF target.

This replaces the earlier `CompileCachePolicy`, owner ContextVar, and loader changes. The opt-out applies in `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`; cache-disable settings remain respected. HF does not attempt forced model-AOT loading when opted out.

Related to #50128, specifically compilation caching. Follows the graph-caching recommendation in #53295 and preserves the cache-relocation behavior from #52142. This addresses HF cache routing rather than the cache-key API migration in #39517 or empty-artifact validation in #56879.

## Test Plan

- Fresh-process regression for changed decorator closure state, warm graph-cache hits, and repeated forward calls, covering both Inductor adaptors.
- Native AOT save/load after an opt-out module runs under the same configuration.
- Functorch configuration restoration on normal/exceptional exit and hash calculation; bypass of existing direct-cache metadata and handles.
- Three HF models and a native control under two cache-persistence protocols; real TP=2 and full HF-target/native-EAGLE3 generation.
- Full Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K evaluation under the batch-invariant compilation configuration described below.

## Test Results

### Warm startup: 8.9%–10.5% less time with persistent caches

Before is main at `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`; After is the smaller implementation described above.

Single L20, TP=1, BF16. Each model/backend/version/protocol has **1 cold + 5 fresh-process warm runs**, alternating A/B order. Values are `LLM(...)` initialization **median [min, max] in seconds**, excluding imports.

For the primary protocol, both versions receive persistent Inductor/Triton cache-directory settings. Caches are isolated by model/backend/version, and each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. Worker paths are verified because vLLM may redirect Inductor to its own persistent subdirectory.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 20.344 [20.105, 20.953] | **18.204 [17.595, 18.343]** | **10.52%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 15.570 [15.160, 16.111] | **14.121 [13.734, 14.297]** | **9.31%** |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 27.830 [27.769, 28.155] | **25.355 [25.183, 25.572]** | **8.89%** |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.857 [11.723, 11.978] | 11.719 [11.659, 12.030] | Ranges overlap |

The HF results are consistent in magnitude with the earlier 8–10% observation. No native speedup, throughput improvement, or TTFT improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Supplement: only VLLM_CACHE_ROOT persists</summary>

Inductor/Triton directory overrides are unset; each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. This measures the case where only the vLLM cache root persists, rather than ordinary same-user restarts.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 30.274 [30.041, 31.056] | **18.180 [17.794, 18.358]** | **39.95%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 25.188 [24.725, 25.983] | **14.109 [13.875, 14.304]** | **43.98%** |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 37.718 [37.262, 38.034] | **24.810 [24.631, 25.560]** | **34.22%** |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.909 [11.545, 12.693] | 11.958 [11.618, 12.532] | Ranges overlap |

The **34.2%–44.0%** reduction is specific to this protocol. Compared with explicit lower-level caches, HF Before is 9.62–9.93 s slower; After differs by 0.011–0.545 s. Worker paths and cache counters support a cache-persistence explanation, without establishing per-kernel attribution. Independently compiled caches and shared-host load also limit cross-protocol attribution.

Native median changes are −1.17% with explicit caches and +0.41% with root-only persistence. Ranges overlap in both protocols; no consistent native regression or speedup is established.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cold timings and reproducibility</summary>

| Model / backend | Explicit Before / After, s | Root-only Before / After, s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 46.855 / 44.519 | 47.267 / 45.283 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 37.518 / 35.636 | 37.459 / 36.782 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 56.375 / 54.423 | 56.104 / 52.939 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 51.503 / 51.999 | 52.575 / 51.835 |

- **96/96 starts completed; all 96 cache checks passed.** No samples were discarded. These are new measurements of the smaller implementation, not reused smoke timings.
- Baseline: `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`.
- Measured patch SHA256: `5edec6ae4c933e25df921c1c1d045b2ff277c0d8c56ed473ac12f99a2b2bf4eb`.
- Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Transformers 5.15.1, Triton 3.7.1. A/B use identical hashes for the five rebuilt dense-runtime extensions.
- BF16, FlashAttention, seed=0, max model length=512, max batched tokens=512, max sequences=8, memory utilization=0.8, CUDA graph sizes `[1,2,4,8]`, four CPU/compilation threads.
- Raw AOT/mega/standalone flags are enabled; cache-disable and force-load are disabled. No batch invariance or additional deterministic controls are enabled. All workers use `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`.
- Fixed physical L20 GPU 4, checked idle before every start. Runs were serial within the task; the host was not CPU-exclusive. A/B never share compiled artifacts; remote graph caches are disabled.
- Cold means an empty compilation cache. OS page caches were not cleared; model-file verification may warm them. Single cold observations and five warm samples do not establish statistical significance.
- Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. TinyLlama and Qwen3-14B snapshots are identified by per-file SHA256.

</details>

### Correctness and cache behavior

- **HF:** all After warm performance runs hit FX/AOTAutograd caches; model-AOT/direct-artifact save/load counts remain zero.
- **Native:** all cold runs save AOT; all five warm runs per version/protocol load it with zero model-AOT recompilations. Separate forced-load checks also pass.
- **TP=2:** Qwen3-0.6B HF completes cold/warm initialization and generation on both versions. Both After ranks record three FX and three AOTAutograd hits on warm start, with separate rank cache directories.
- **EAGLE3:** full generation with Qwen3-0.6B HF and `Nicolassuez/Qwen3-0.6B-eagle3` completes across cold/warm processes. The HF target uses graph caching; the native draft saves AOT on cold start and loads it on warm start.
- **Cache disable:** separate HF cold/warm checks retain compilation while recording zero FX/AOTAutograd cache hits and zero model-AOT/direct-artifact saves or loads.

Performance runs generate the same 32 prompts after initialization, using batch sizes 1/4/8, greedy decoding, and up to 64 tokens. **All 128 comparisons pass the existing repository helper without relaxed tolerances; 124/128 contain token-sequence differences.** Each comparison covers 32 prompts; this count is not a prompt failure rate or an accuracy measurement.

| Model / backend | Explicit: comparisons with token differences | Root-only: comparisons with token differences | Helper failures |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 16/16 | 16/16 | 0 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 14/16 | 16/16 | 0 |

Each group includes ten within-version cold/warm comparisons and six corresponding A/B comparisons. The helper checks first-divergence tokens against the other output's top-5; it does not establish full-sequence or accuracy equivalence.

### Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K

All **1,319 questions**, 5-shot, greedy decoding, 256-token generation limit. Before cold, After cold, and After warm each score **519/1319 (39.35%)**, with **identical per-question answers and complete token sequences**. Each run has 3 invalid answers and generates 132,670 tokens. After warm records **29 FX graph hits and 29 AOTAutograd hits**.

This uses batch invariance with compilation enabled, max model length=4096, max batched tokens=2048, and max sequences=8. Batch invariance disables model AOT upstream; mega/standalone remain enabled. This evaluation does not establish quality equivalence under the default AOT-enabled configuration or for Qwen3-14B. Evaluation timings are excluded from the performance results.

<details>
<summary>Numerical diagnostics and coverage limits</summary>

Default runs contain token differences across versions and between cold/warm starts within a version, despite passing the repository helper. Separate smaller-implementation smoke comparisons also pass the helper, with these token-sequence differences among 32 prompts:

| Path | Before cold → Before warm | Before cold → After cold | After cold → After warm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| HF | 4/32 | 6/32 | 3/32 |
| Native | 4/32 | 1/32 | 4/32 |
| HF TP=2 | 7/32 | 5/32 | 6/32 |
| EAGLE3 | 2/32 | 2/32 | 3/32 |

These smoke comparisons are separate from the 128 performance-run comparisons above. Cache-disabled HF runs also differ on 5/32 prompts, showing that cache hits are not necessary for output variation; this does not rule out all effects of the patch.

The largest common-prefix logprob difference in the performance matrix is **4.312496** for Qwen3-14B: an unselected token has logprobs −13.250004 and −17.5625, while both runs select the same token at that position. This is not evidence of an incorrect selected token, but the differences should not all be described as negligible rounding. Operator-level attribution has not been established.

The batch-invariant GSM8K result is separate evidence with its own configuration limits. Full Qwen3-14B quality evaluation has not been repeated for this implementation. Earlier implementation-specific numerical controls and quality results are not counted as current validation.

Testing covers the recorded dependency environment and L20 GPUs. Required dense-runtime components were rebuilt from pinned source, but this is not a full wheel/Rust build, every optional extension, or full upstream CI. ROCm execution and a separate real `model_impl=auto` → HF resolution check remain unverified. The independent TinyLlama breakable-CUDA-graph issue is outside this patch.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Regression commands and results</summary>

Relevant suites ran with fresh vLLM cache roots and the verified task environment:

```bash
.venv-verified/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/compile/test_config.py

.venv-verified/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/test_decorator.py \
  tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py \
  tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py
```

- **127 passed, 1 skipped:** configuration tests 89 passed; decorator/AOT/compiler-interface tests 38 passed, 1 skipped.
- Six targeted mutations were detected: index read, direct load, configuration restoration, second forward, disabled native AOT, and hash-configuration restoration.
- A subsequent test-only isolation fix mocks adaptor cache initialization in the old-index test. A focused rerun including an environment-state probe reports **5 passed**; both index-read/direct-load mutations remain detected. Product code was unchanged. These counts are not additive, and the full suite was not rerun after this test-only change.
- Twelve applicable Python hooks passed on the smaller implementation; ruff, formatting, mypy, and diff checks were rerun after the isolation fix. Full pre-commit was blocked by offline actionlint dependency installation; full CI is not claimed.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Retry Mooncake bootstrap registration on timeout (reopens #55763)
author: LCAIZJ
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55729.

This PR reopens #55763 and credit goes to @Sarimsaljook, the original PR author. Compared with #55763, the attempt limit is now an internal constant set to 3 instead of a user-facing environment variable. The original tests and documentation are adapted accordingly; the remaining fix is preserved.

During slow rank-0 initialization, bootstrap registration can time out. Previously, only connection errors were retried, and a failed sender listener could leave startup waiting indefinitely.

This change:

- Adds an explicit registration timeout through `VLLM_MOONCAKE_CONNECTOR_TIMEOUT` (default: 30 seconds).
- Retries connection errors and timeouts for up to 3 total attempts, with exponential backoff.
- Makes repeated registration of the same worker address idempotent, while still rejecting conflicting addresses.
- Bounds the sender-listener readiness wait and propagates startup failures.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Per-module LM heads for multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

Fix two issues with multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2 (MRV2):

1. **Multi-module MTP samples every draft step with module 0's LM head.**
   `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` runs step `i` through MTP module `i` (`spec_step_idx=step`), but `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` calls `self.model.compute_logits(hidden_states)` without `spec_step_idx`. MTP drafters whose `compute_logits` selects the module's own `shared_head` by `spec_step_idx` (Step3.5/3.7, DeepSeek MTP, GLM MTP, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, ...) therefore use module 0's head/norm for all steps. The same applies to the `use_local_argmax_reduction` path (`get_top_tokens`).
   Fix: `sample_draft` goes through two `DraftModelSpeculator` hooks, `compute_draft_logits` and `get_draft_top_tokens`, which ignore the step by default. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` overrides them to pass `spec_step_idx`, so other drafters (EAGLE, DFlash, ...) are untouched.

2. **Step-3.x MTP cannot run on MRV2** (needed to reproduce 1 end-to-end):
   - The drafter read `vllm_config.model_config.hf_config`, which for the Step-3.7 VLM target is the top-level `Step3p7Config` (`AttributeError: ... 'vocab_size'`), and used the target's quant config (`output_partition_size = 24 is not divisible by block_n = 128`). It is now built from its own text config and draft quant config, as the V1 `Step3p5MTPProposer` does.
   - `load_eagle_model` replaced every MTP layer's `shared_head.head` with the target `lm_head` because `Step3p5MTP` has no top-level `lm_head`. Step-3.7's three MTP heads differ from the target `lm_head` (checked in the checkpoint), so this collapsed position-0 acceptance from 0.93 to 0.06. `Step3p5MTP` now declares `has_own_lm_head = True`, and `_should_share` keeps a declared-own copy that has no top-level module.

## Relation to existing PRs

Item 2's config part overlaps #49490 by @chanh, credited as co-author on that commit. This PR additionally fixes the per-step LM head selection (item 1) and the per-layer LM head overwrite, without which the drafter loads but barely accepts anything.

## Test Plan

E2E on 4×GB200, `stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash-FP8`, TP4, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, GSM8K 500 questions 5-shot, temperature 0. Acceptance from the `/metrics` counters.

## Test Result

| MRV2 | GSM8K | pos 0 | pos 1 | pos 2 | mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Item 2 only (per-step head bug present) | 0.910 | 0.934 | 0.743 | 0.526 | 3.20 |
| This PR | 0.902 | 0.931 | **0.786** | **0.592** | **3.31** |

Position 0 (always module 0's head) is unchanged, while positions 1 and 2, the steps affected by the bug, improve by 4.3 and 6.6 points (~16k drafts per run). GSM8K differences are within noise. Before item 2, main fails to start with this model on MRV2.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; all changes were reviewed and tested by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Terminate streaming sessions on ABORT/ERROR and prevent zombie sessions
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

Split out from #53861 (bugs 2 and 3 of the 4 streaming-input session lifecycle fixes there), with the original author included as co-author — this is a carve-out for independent review/merge, not duplicate work. Bugs 1 (collector merging across chunk boundaries) and 4 (zero-chunk streams / DP sticky routing) are being split separately.

**Bug 2 — engine-side ABORT/ERROR treated as a normal chunk boundary.** `OutputProcessor.process_outputs` treated any `finish_reason` on a streaming-input request as "chunk done, wait for next chunk". ABORT and ERROR end the whole session, so treating them as a chunk boundary left `generate()` waiting forever and desynced the frontend/scheduler chunk queues. Fix: only non-terminal finish reasons are chunk boundaries (`streaming_chunk_boundary`); ABORT/ERROR finish the request state and also send an abort back to the engine (see below).

**Bug 3 — a chunk sent after the session finished resurrects it as a zombie.** If a chunk ADD reaches the engine after the session was aborted/finished, the scheduler sees an unknown resumable id and admits it as a new session. That session then sits in `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` forever, holding KV blocks, with no frontend state left to abort it. Fix (reworked per review, no new request fields):
- `handle_inputs` checks `output_processor.has_request()` before each non-first chunk and before the final empty request, and stops if the session is gone. There is no `await` between this check and the ADD send, and `AsyncLLM.abort()` removes frontend state before sending ABORT on the same socket, so any chunk that passes the check is ordered before the abort. This holds for every abort path, including direct `abort()` calls (e.g. realtime `cleanup()`).
- For the engine-finished race (engine finishes the session with ABORT/ERROR while a chunk sent before the frontend saw that finish is in flight), the output processor always re-sends an abort for a terminally-finished streaming session. That abort is ordered after any such chunk, so a re-created session is cleaned up.
- `DPLBAsyncMPClient.abort_requests_async` broadcasts aborts for ids with no routing entry to all engines, since the routing entry is dropped when the engine reports the request finished.

## Test Plan

```
ruff check / ruff format --check (ruff 0.14.0) on changed files
pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_async_llm_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -k "streaming or abort or chunk"
```

New coverage: `test_streaming_input_stop_is_chunk_boundary`, `test_streaming_input_abort_error_is_terminal[abort|error]` (bug 2); `test_handle_inputs_stops_after_session_finished[True|False]`, `test_dplb_abort_of_finished_request_goes_to_all_engines[1|2]` (bug 3).

## Test Result

- ruff check / format: pass.
- On macOS CPU: all streaming-input and output-processor tests above pass. `test_abort_requests[*]` errors only because the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` tokenizer cannot be downloaded here (same on main).
- `test_engine_core_client.py` is skipped on non-CUDA platforms, so `test_dplb_abort_of_finished_request_goes_to_all_engines` was run standalone: it passes with this change and fails against the previous `abort_requests_async`.
- Not yet validated end-to-end against a realtime model on GPU.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (split and adaptation onto latest main). The bug-3 approach was reworked following @njhill's review suggestion. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

Co-authored-by: Benedikt Falk <bfalk@nvidia.com>

title: [HiSparse] Log steady-state max concurrency and expose host-tier utilization gauges
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse's host KV pool is invisible at runtime, and the startup `Maximum concurrency` line understates a warm server's capacity: it charges every request its full admission footprint, while running requests that read from host pin only their active tail pages. This PR adds:

- **Startup log**: steady-state maximum concurrency, `1 + (num_blocks - admission) / steady` (all but one request at its active tail, plus one being admitted), capped by the host pool. Logged from the scheduler-side connector, so it uses the KV cache config after the cross-rank minimum.
- **Gauges**, sampled by the scheduler each engine step (constant-time read of the host block pool, no device sync):
  - `vllm:hisparse_host_cache_usage_perc`: host pool usage, mirroring `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc`. Evictable cached blocks count as free.
  - `vllm:hisparse_pending_page_transfers`: write-backs and restores not yet completed.
- **CLI**: `HiSparse host KV cache usage %` in the `KV Transfer metrics` line.
- **Docs**: a HiSparse section in `docs/usage/metrics.md` (metric names are now literals so the generator picks them up) and the two bounds in `docs/design/hisparse.md`.

Supersedes #58805.

## Test Plan

Unit tests (macOS, CPU):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  -k "hisparse or host_usage or stats"
```

E2E on H100: shrunk DeepSeek-V3.2 (4 layers, dummy weights), FP8 KV, block size 64, `/metrics` scraped every 0.2 s.

- **A**: TP2, `MultiConnector[HiSparseConnector (host_pool_gib 4), OffloadingConnector (cpu_bytes_to_use 4e9)]`, `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 1000000000`; `vllm bench serve` random 8000 in / 512 out, 64 prompts, concurrency 32.
- **B**: TP1, `HiSparseConnector` (host_pool_gib 4), `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 250000000 --max-model-len 16384`; random 15000 in / 1300 out, 40 prompts, concurrency 40 (saturates the GPU pool).

## Test Result

Unit: 45 passed at HEAD (with `test_multi_connector.py`) (`test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter` needs CUDA, not run on macOS).

E2E at `f792b5bd11` (later commits switch the ratio to the equivalent `BlockPool.get_usage()` and trim comments/docs). All requests succeeded, no errors.

A:

```
GPU KV cache size: 1,016,234 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 163,840 tokens per request: 6.20x
HiSparse steady-state maximum concurrency for 163,840 tokens per request: 8.07x (running requests reading from host).

vllm:hisparse_host_cache_usage_perc        0.0 -> 0.161 (32 running) -> 0.0
vllm:hisparse_pending_page_transfers       up to 256 during prefill, 1-2 during decode, 0 idle
```

title: [Bugfix] Fix moe_wna16 w13 zero-point shard split for 8-bit asym GPTQ MoE
author: spandantiwari
body:
## Summary

`MoeWNA16Method`'s weight loader splits the fused `w13_qzeros` (gate/up) zero-points at `shard_size // 2`, which is only correct for 4-bit. `w13_qzeros` is packed along the intermediate dim by `bit8_pack_factor` (`8 // weight_bits`), so the w1/w3 boundary is in **packed** units — `shard_size // bit8_pack_factor`. For **8-bit asymmetric GPTQ MoE** (`bit8_pack_factor == 1`, `has_zp=True`) the param's intermediate dim is `2 * intermediate` (unpacked), but each shard's loaded tensor is `intermediate` wide, so writing into a half-width `[: shard_size // 2]` slice raises a shape mismatch at load. The common 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ path is unaffected (`bit8_pack_factor == 2`, so `shard_size // 2 == shard_size // bit8_pack_factor`).

## Fix
My fix is as follows:
`moe_wna16.py` — split `w13_qzeros` at `shard_size // layer.quant_config.bit8_pack_factor` instead of the hardcoded `shard_size // 2`. Only `w13_qzeros` is affected: qweight/scales aren't packed on that axis, and `w2_qzeros` isn't shard-split.

## Impact for various backends

Platform-independent: the defect is in load-time weight-loader code with no CUDA/ROCm gate, and WNA16 INT4/INT8 GPTQ/AWQ MoE runs on ROCm (Triton fused-MoE). So this **affects AMD** as well as CUDA. Failure mode is a **loud load-time error** (shape mismatch), not silent wrong output, in the narrow 8-bit-asymmetric config. (Marlin doesn't support asymmetric GPTQ, so `sym=False` MoE routes to `moe_wna16` by construction — this path can't be diverted to Marlin.)

## Test plan

Added `test_moe_wna16_w13_qzeros_shard_split_int8_asym_gptq` in `tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py` — CPU-only. Builds a real 8-bit GPTQ `MoeWNA16Method`, runs `create_weights`, drives the actual weight loader for the w1/w3 shards, and asserts both load without error and land in the correct halves.

```
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py -q
# 16 passed, 9 skipped (CUDA/humming-gated)
# new test PASSES on the fix; FAILS when reverted to `shard_size // 2` (guards the exact regression)

ruff check <both files>          # All checks passed
ruff format --check <both files> # already formatted
```

## Model evaluation

No full-model eval — this fixes a checkpoint-**load** failure (weight placement / shape), not inference math, and the 4-bit path is provably unchanged (`shard_size // 2 == shard_size // bit8_pack_factor` when `bit8_pack_factor == 2`), so no accuracy regression is possible.

I did attempt to do an end-to-end run by quantizing a small MoE (OLMoE-1B-7B) to 8-bit asymmetric GPTQ, but it is blocked in this vLLM environment: **transformers 5.x fuses MoE experts into a single module**, while the GPTQ tooling (`gptqmodel`) quantizes per-expert submodules that no longer exist — so no MoE can be freshly GPTQ-quantized here without downgrading transformers. No public 8-bit *asymmetric* GPTQ MoE checkpoint exists to load directly either.

Evidence in lieu of an eval: the added unit test drives the **real** `create_weights` + `moe_wna16_weight_loader` on the actual code path (fails before the fix with the exact shape mismatch, passes after), and verifies the loaded zero-points land in the correct gate/up halves. A reviewer with an 8-bit-asym GPTQ MoE checkpoint (or a transformers-4.x quantization env) can confirm end-to-end load.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open/merged PRs touching this area:
- #51645 (open) — fixes `create_weights` **allocation** along the group dimension for non-divisible group sizes; different axis, doesn't touch the loader split.
- #51125 (merged) — sized `w13` allocation by `w13_num_shards`; established that pattern but left this loader split hardcoded.

Neither of these two PRs addresses the packed-unit shard boundary fixed here.

title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Fuse HC down projection and SiLU on NVIDIA

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep Mooncake bootstrap ports bound during startup
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Bind the bootstrap socket before starting Uvicorn and keep that listener open.

- Cover port ownership, cleanup, startup failures, and external registration.

[PR #58095](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58095) added the ROCm test and selected its bootstrap port before model startup without keeping the socket reserved. In [AMD CI 13668](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13668#01a0e3aa-1025-420f-9503-7c8a7ca86e87), that port was occupied when Mooncake tried to bind, and the test waited 20 minutes before failing. The startup loop that hid the bind failure dates to [#31034](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31034). This addresses the reservation gap in [#51275](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51275); duplicate checks found no open listener-ownership fix, while [#55137](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55137) handles registration timeouts.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Avoid target request padding in DP drafter
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Purpose

When a target FULL CUDA graph pads its request count, `DPSyncState.num_reqs` describes graph capacity rather than the number of scheduled requests. Reusing that capacity for uniform drafter steps makes active DP ranks select larger draft graphs than needed.

This PR keeps the DP-wide maximum real request count alongside graph capacity and uses it for uniform drafter dispatch. It also shrinks online dummy-rank DFlash batches coherently across input preparation, graph dispatch, attention metadata, EPLB preparation, and draft generation. Startup graph capture retains its required capacity.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Preserve host prefix publication after request completion
author: eopXD
body:
With HiSparse, a request can reach EOS or its output limit in the same step that reports completed host writes. The scheduler handles the final token and cleans up the request before processing the transfer acknowledgements from that same output. Any prefix publication still waiting for those acknowledgements is discarded, leaving valid host KV unavailable for reuse.

This PR preserves the publication information and host-page references until acknowledgement, then publishes the valid pages for reuse.

## Validation

- Four manager cases passed, covering terminal/nonterminal cleanup, partial acknowledgements, request-ID reuse, and allocation pressure.
- One H100 case passed with eager mirroring enabled and delayed acknowledgement: the repeated prompt reused 256 tokens and produced the same output token.
- Model testing used reduced DeepSeek-V3.2 with dummy FP8 weights.
- Formatting and type checks passed.

author: mganczarenko
body:
## Purpose

`inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL-fp4` fails at weight loading on every platform:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (3) must match the size of tensor b (12) at non-singleton dimension 1

```

The routed experts are MXFP4 (`routed_experts_quant_method: mxfp4`). `_configure_ling_fp8_quant_config` reads that from `config.quantization_config`, but the VL model builds its language model from `text_config`, which has no `quantization_config` (it lives on the top-level VL config). title: [Bugfix][Core] Schedule encoder-only prompts larger than one step
author: peperunas
body:
## Purpose

An encoder-only instance (`mm_encoder_only`, e.g. image-only serving) holds no KV cache, so `EngineCore.__init__` turns chunked prefill off *after* config validation has already passed (`"Disabling chunked prefill for model without KVCache"`, `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`). `SchedulerConfig.verify_max_model_len` only rejects `max_num_batched_tokens < max_model_len` while chunked prefill is off at validation time, so such an instance starts normally with a per-step budget smaller than its largest prompt.

At scheduling time `Scheduler.schedule` then reaches:

```python
if (
    not self.scheduler_config.enable_chunked_prefill
    and num_new_tokens > request_token_budget
):
    break
```

The request is only peeked from the waiting queue and never popped, and neither its prompt length nor the budget ever changes, so the same `break` fires on every step: the request waits forever and no error is raised anywhere.

This PR exempts encoder-only instances from that break with one clause, `and not self.is_mm_encoder_only`, so the existing `num_new_tokens = min(num_new_tokens, request_token_budget)` splits the prompt across steps. That is safe here specifically because an encoder-only instance keeps no KV cache for a resumed prefill to lose.

### Changes

- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — skip the "chunked prefill is disabled" break for encoder-only instances, letting the token budget split their prompt.
- `tests/v1/core/utils.py` — `create_scheduler(..., mm_encoder_only=True)` sets `model_config.multimodal_config.mm_encoder_only` after the model config is built.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` — `test_encoder_only_prompt_longer_than_budget_is_chunked`: a 2500-token prompt with `max_num_batched_tokens=1024` and `enable_chunked_prefill=False` schedules 1024 / 1024 / 452 over three steps.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and PRs for "encoder-only prompt", "max_num_batched_tokens validation", "mm_encoder_only stall" and related terms. No open PR makes the scheduler split an encoder-only prompt that exceeds one step; the nearest open work (#56826, #57368) concerns encoder input lifetimes across steps, which this does not touch.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py
ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=... .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q
```

## Test Result

- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` clean on the three changed files.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: 194 passed, the new test included.
- Negative control: reverting only the 4-line scheduler change makes `test_encoder_only_prompt_longer_than_budget_is_chunked` fail, so the test guards this change.
- No model eval: the change only schedules oversized encoder-only prompts that previously never ran; no logits-affecting code path changes.

## AI Assistance
