title: [Bugfix][Core] Requeue encoder-stalled waiting requests
author: peperunas
body:
## Purpose

A waiting request can end a scheduling pass with `num_new_tokens == 0`: its encoder inputs do not fit the cache or the compute budget, or the prefill-lookahead reserve consumes the tokens. The waiting loop `break`ed there, so the request kept its head-of-queue position and every request behind it went unscheduled for that step — repeating on every step while the resource condition holds.

It is now requeued with `skip_request()`, which preserves the drain-first priority of requests holding KV blocks (async KV-load resumes) and the `deferred_waiting` accounting.

The self-pinned encoder-cache release from the earlier revision is dropped here; #60553 proposes that.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and PRs for waiting-queue requeue / head-of-line blocking and encoder cache stalls. No open PR touches this path; the nearest matches are #56826 and #57368 (encoder input lifetimes across steps — different concern), #40707/#40709 (mamba split deadlock — different path), and umbrella EPD tracker #52409.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Never allocate GPU pages without host backing
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Description

When the HiSparse host pool fills, `HiSparseSourceManager.allocate_new_blocks` gives new pages a null host entry. Those pages are never written back, so they never become clean and their GPU blocks can never be reclaimed: they stay pinned for the life of the request. Freeing host capacity does not fix it, because later allocations extend the host table and the freed blocks go to new tail pages, never to the old null ones. Host prefix publication for the request also stalls at the first null page.

The result is GPU KV pressure and preemptions that HiSparse is meant to prevent, plus lost host prefix-cache coverage, persisting after host capacity has recovered.

Fix: never allocate a page without host backing (alternative to #58963, which backfills null pages after the fact):

- `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` requires host blocks for every page being allocated, not just external-load destinations, and reuses the existing admission sentinel when they don't fit. The scheduler then waits or preempts exactly as it does for GPU exhaustion.
- The best-effort `allocate_new_blocks` override (null padding) is deleted.
- `has_pending_reclamation` also reports host blocks that an in-flight write-back will return (freed request, spill not yet acked), so the scheduler waits a step instead of over-preempting.
- Startup rejects a host pool that cannot hold one `max_model_len` request (plus the null block and a copy-on-write tail), which would otherwise livelock.

## Effect on KV-cache memory over time

**Before.** While the host pool is full, every page a running request seals gets a null host entry and keeps its GPU block for the rest of the request. The pinned set only grows: host blocks freed later go to new tail pages, never to the old null ones. A request that decodes through a host-full window therefore holds GPU KV proportional to the tokens produced during that window, as if HiSparse were off for those pages, and releases it only when it finishes or is preempted. Across the batch, GPU free blocks drift down while the host stays full, and the scheduler preempts (and later recomputes) requests that HiSparse should have kept running. Prefix publication for those requests also stops at the first null page, so the host prefix cache never covers the rest of their context.

**After.** Every GPU-resident page has a host page, so its GPU footprint is transient: a sealed page is dirty until its write-back completes (about one step), stays pinned while within the two-page active tail, and is unpinned once the request can read from host (it has a hot region). Unpinned pages stay readable but count as free, so the GPU pool reclaims them under pressure. Per-request GPU usage is bounded by the hot region, the active tail and in-flight write-backs, independent of context length, for as long as the request runs.

The host pool becomes the hard capacity limit instead: running requests together hold one host block per computed page, and when it is full, new allocations wait or preempt even if GPU blocks are free. Since HiSparse only pays off when the host pool is much larger than the GPU pool, this replaces the gradual, hard-to-see GPU buildup above with a rare, explicit admission limit.

## Related

- #58963 fixes the same bug by backfilling host blocks for null pages after capacity frees up (one page per step). This PR prevents the null pages instead, which removes rather than adds state; only one of the two should land.
- #57457 also edits `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` (counts GPU copies pinned by a host-prefix hit). The changes compose: its copy-pin count replaces this PR's final `return 0`.
- #58949's steady-state concurrency estimate assumes resident pages spill to host; this PR makes that hold under host pressure, and its host-pool gauges become the direct signal for the new admission limit.

## Test Plan

Repro on main (unit-level): with a 3-block host pool, the request's pages 1-3 get null host entries; after the donor frees its block, the capacity goes to new tail page 4, and pages 1-3 stay pinned (`ref_cnt=1`) indefinitely while page 5 is null again.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -q
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -v
```

## Test Result

- CPU: 341 passed; other HiSparse-tagged suites (scheduler, NIXL HMA, stats, config): 22 passed.
- e2e (B300, reduced DeepSeek-V3.2, dummy weights): 3 passed. The new `test_hisparse_host_exhaustion_defers_requests` fails on main (a scheduled request has a null host page).

Accuracy with trained weights and serving throughput under host pressure were not measured.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Enable decoder SWA bounded replay
author: frida-andersson
body:
## Summary

#58132 added decoder-side SWA bounded replay for the CUDA model. This PR enables it on ROCm. During eager prefill, layer 20 writes its KV for every token, then layer 20 and layers 21–39 run on each request's last 128 tokens. The final `mhc_post` runs on that replay batch. Decode graphs stay on the full batch. #59532's replay graphs are already used: the AMD model uses `DeepseekV41ModelState`.

The AMD attention class does not override `forward_kv`. Replay calls `DeepseekV4Attention.forward_kv`, which writes the uint8 SWA cache through `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`.

## What changed

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`: `write_kv` on the last KV source, then `DecoderReplayLayers` from that layer. Pass `write_kv`, the attention metadata prefixes, and that layer's SWA prefix. `mhc_post` runs inside the replay batch. The return is `(hidden_states, pre_mix, *aux)`. The aux state at the cut is captured on the trimmed rows.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`: no `forward_kv` override. The shared method calls `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` and then the compressor insert and indexer K write.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py`: forward `decoder_replay_layers` from the language model.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py`: when decoder replay layers exist and the prefix-cache window is 0, build `replay_start` and warm the gather kernel. The pad kernel stays on the prefix-cache path.
- Tests cover a 300-token forward (trim, both `mhc_post` calls, the cut-aux capture, the prefix set from the cut, and the SWA insert) and window 0 warming gather without the pad kernel.

## Gating

On when `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` is set and the v2 model runner is in use. Off with `--no-swa-bounded-replay`. The last KV source must have `compress_ratio <= 1`, and no Engram layer may sit at or after it. ROCm does not read `swa_cache_layer.bounded_replay`; that flag is the prefix-cache path, and attention forces it off. CUDA still requires it. Replay graphs follow `compilation_config.cudagraph_decoder_replay` (default on) and `decoder_replay_trim_threshold` (default 768).

## Depends on

#59894 is in this base. It replaced the row buffers with `write_kv` and `first_swa_prefix`, and replay starts at the last KV source. #56638 is in this base. It replaced #59136 and bounds the ROCm prefill SWA indices at the replay start. #59532 is in this base and supplies the replay graphs. None of the three are in this diff.

## Performance

4× MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, spec decode off, prefix cache off, HIP INT4 QuickReduce, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. `max_num_seqs` left at the default. The extension is the installed ROCm nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d`.

4 prompts, 16384 in, 128 out, concurrency 1, seed 7. Both arms completed 4 requests.

| Median TPOT | 10.59 ms | 10.58 ms |
| Mean TPOT | 10.59 ms | 10.58 ms |

## Accuracy

RULER `niah_single_2` was not re-run after this drop. On the previous head, 500 samples at 16384 tokens scored 1.0 off and 1.0 on. 65536 was not run.

The 300-token forward wrote the same uint8 SWA cache as `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`. That write covers full blocks and a 12-token tail, and the spare block stayed at the poison value.

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip padded work in SM100 FP4 DeepGEMM experts
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
## Purpose

Avoid computing with padding in the Blackwell FP4 DeepGEMM MoEs layers. Currently we are doing so in both GEMMs and activations.  This mainly affects the decoder when running DeepEPv2+ DeepGEMM. This PR updates the grouped GEMMs to use DeepGEMM's prefix-sum scheduler, and changes the packed SiLU+mul+FP8-quantization kernel to use those endpoints to process only live rows.

Each endpoint is the aligned expert start plus its actual token count; the next expert starts at the preceding endpoint rounded up to the GEMM alignment. No count readback, additional launch, or DeepGEMM source change is required. Activation workspaces keep their allocated capacity. The per-row layout metadata shrinks from 112 KiB to 128 bytes for 32 local experts and 28,672 allocated rows.

The quantization metadata is optional. Calls without it retain the original dense launch configuration, and the metadata loads compile out. SM120 and FP8 expert callers retain their existing path. Padding outputs are left unwritten; the down GEMM uses the same bounds to identify live rows. `mk_alignment_scope` and `ensure_zero_padding=True` remain in place.

The new activation masking also differs from #51332/#51217 (shared masked activation/Humming paths) and #53911 (Humming indexed metadata preparation): `DeepGemmFP4Experts` directly calls the packed-UE8M0 fused activation kernel. Those changes do not pass this caller's expert endpoints into that kernel. Open-PR searches for DeepGEMM prefix sums and SiLU padding found no implementation of this change. No associated issue is being closed.

## Test Plan

Conflict-resolution update (2026-10-06): merged upstream main `5ab4e4445b` in `e704a97688`. Resolved the graph-replay test conflict by retaining upstream packed/float32/ceil-UE8M0 scale-format coverage and this PR's `is_cuda_alike()` CUDA/ROCm guard. Applicable pre-commit hooks (including mypy 3.10), mypy 3.12, syntax checks for the five affected Python files, and `git diff origin/main --check` passed. GPU tests and model evaluations were not rerun: the local machine has no CUDA GPU. The GPU results below describe the earlier validated revision.

Validation used 8×GB200, DeepSeek-V4-Flash revision `60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1`, EP8/DP8/TP1, DeepEP V2 + DeepGEMM. Both nodes shared one ready NVLink ComputeDomain; all eight ranks passed peer-memory and NCCL checks.

- 69 activation tests passed on GB200, including the corrected benchmark rerun. New cases check bitwise live FP8 values and packed scales, poisoned alignment gaps and unused capacity, empty experts, all-empty counts, clamping, and changing counts on CUDA-graph replay.
- Interleaved CUDA-graph kernel benchmarks used five warmups and 25 samples, with 16 calls per graph. The old packed quantization functions were loaded as the control; ten cases cover padded and fully populated buffers.
- Full FFN comparison uses the same saved real inputs on both variants: layer 10, 512 tokens/GPU, five warmups and 25 unprofiled graph replays per rank. A device all-reduce precedes the timed interval. Three separate outer profiles per rank provide kernel timings. Untimed audits verify both GEMMs' scheduler selection and the activation's actual expert bounds.
- Paired full-model GSM8K: all 1,319 questions, five-shot, greedy, seed 42, maximum output 256 tokens, concurrency 64, FP8 KV, no MTP, eager prefill and full decode graphs.

Commands executed in the validation environment:

```bash
/tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /bundle/test_padding.py -q --disable-warnings
/tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /bundle/benchmark.py --baseline /bundle/baseline.py --output "$out/benchmark.json"
/tmp/validation/.venv/bin/python /bundle/worker.pyz \
  --spec /bundle/$backend.json --job-id "$backend" \
  --output-dir "$out" --node-count 2 --local-world-size 4 \
  --node-rank-env JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX \
  --rendezvous-host "$head" --rendezvous-port 29500
/tmp/validation/.venv/bin/python -u /bundle/serve_and_evaluate.py
```

`test_padding.py` is an unchanged copy of `tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor.py`; `benchmark.py` is the standalone script included below (removed from the repository). The FFN and GSM8K orchestration uses an external experiment harness.

All relevant pre-commit hooks, including mypy, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Test Result

The latest paired run compares this PR's prefix-sum GEMMs with and without activation masking:

| Measurement | Prefix sums only | + activation masking |
|---|---:|---:|
| Full FFN, unprofiled | 425.5 µs | 385.7 µs |
| SiLU+mul+quant, separately profiled | 76.0 µs | 20.7 µs |
| Standalone quantization: 3,072 live / 28,672 allocated rows, hidden 2,048 | 63.984 µs | 10.510 µs |

Full FFN latency fell 9.36% (1.103× speedup); outputs match bit for bit on all eight ranks, including eager versus graph execution. Both projections used prefix sums in both variants; only the masked variant supplied expert bounds to activation. The median profiled activation saving is larger than the FFN saving because ranks carry different amounts of expert work and meet again at combine. Main activation workspaces are unchanged.

**Dense-path control:** calls without metadata preserve the original launch and differed by 0.20% faster to 0.39% slower across ten controls in the corrected rerun. At 28,672×2,048, the old and new dense paths measured 64.082 and 64.020 µs; at 28,672×7,168, 217.796 and 217.814 µs. No extra kernel or GPU-to-host count synchronization is introduced.

Supplying metadata for an already full buffer does have a small checking/scheduling cost in some shapes: 64.082→64.822 µs for the fully populated 28,672×2,048 case, and approximately 0.15–0.32 µs for the tested smaller group-128 cases. The ordinary dense path does not pay this cost. The 28,672×7,168 metadata-aware case improved from 217.796 to 212.236 µs. The benchmark includes these full-buffer cases rather than measuring padded buffers alone.

| Paired GSM8K | Prefix sums only | + activation masking |
|---|---:|---:|
| Correct / questions | 1,253 / 1,319 | 1,259 / 1,319 |
| Accuracy | 94.996% | 95.451% |
| Configured 95% threshold | Did not pass | Passed |
| HTTP errors | 0 | 0 |

All prompts and labels matched. There were three control-only correct answers and nine masked-only correct answers. This is an accuracy check, not evidence that masking improves model quality: repeating the unchanged control also produced 16 correctness flips while retaining the same total score. The previous and repeated controls used identical MoE sources.

The earlier scheduler-only validation, before this activation update, measured stock versus prefix sums at 717.4 versus 428.7 µs for the same FFN setup, also with bitwise-identical outputs. Those are from a separate paired run. Stock GSM8K was 1,255/1,319 (95.148%), versus prefix sums at 1,253/1,319 (94.996%).

The runtime image was pinned at `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f29125bcc6d276ed38a67c9dfd4e51ccbaba09ad92847a0913c0df38d9c05c71` (vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`). The experiment overlaid the two MoE Python files and only the two packed-quantization functions in `fp8_utils.py`; installed hashes were checked on both nodes. DeepGEMM headers were unmodified. These results are not from a rebuild of all of current main.

AI assistance: Codex helped implement the change, run validation, and prepare this description. This remains a draft pending human review and verification before marking ready.

## Standalone activation benchmark

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script, reproduction command, and recorded output</summary>

Save the following script as `benchmark.py`. It replays all three captured graphs and synchronizes before checking live FP8 values and packed scales. This fixes the pre-replay comparison of uninitialized captured scale tensors.

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project

"""Compare dense and expert-aware packed quantization with CUDA graph timing."""

import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils import (
    silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton,
)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--baseline", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", args.baseline)
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    baseline = module.silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton
    warmups, iterations, graph_calls = 5, 25, 16
    results = []
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    cases = [
        (128, 1, 128, 256, 128),
        (512, 4, 128, 2048, 128),
        (4096, 32, 128, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 896, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 96, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 1, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 0, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 896, 7168, 128),
        (28672, 32, 96, 7168, 128),
        (4096, 32, 128, 2048, 32),
    ]
    for capacity, experts, live_per_expert, hidden, group in cases:
        x = torch.randn((capacity, hidden * 2), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        starts = torch.arange(experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
        starts *= ((live_per_expert + 127) // 128) * 128
        ends = starts + live_per_expert
        graphs = {}
        for name, fn, kwargs in [
            ("baseline", baseline, {}),
            ("dense", silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton, {}),
            (
                "expert",
                silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton,
                {"expert_ends": ends, "expert_alignment": 128},
            ),
        ]:
            output = torch.empty(
                (capacity, hidden), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
            )

            def invoke(fn=fn, output=output, kwargs=kwargs, x=x, group=group):
                return fn(
                    x, group_size=group, output_q=output, clamp_limit=10.0, **kwargs
                )

            for _ in range(warmups):
                invoke()
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
            with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
                for _ in range(graph_calls):
                    q, s = invoke()
            graphs[name] = (graph, q, s)

        for graph, _, _ in graphs.values():
            graph.replay()
        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

        live = torch.zeros(capacity, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bool)
        for start in starts.tolist():
            live[start : start + live_per_expert] = True
        for name in ("dense", "expert"):
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                graphs[name][1].view(torch.uint8)[live],
                graphs["baseline"][1].view(torch.uint8)[live],
                rtol=0,
                atol=0,
            )
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                graphs[name][2][live], graphs["baseline"][2][live], rtol=0, atol=0
            )
        samples = {name: [] for name in graphs}
        for iteration in range(iterations):
            order = list(graphs)
            if iteration % 2:
                order.reverse()
            for name in order:
                begin, end = (torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2))
                begin.record()
                graphs[name][0].replay()
                end.record()
                end.synchronize()
                samples[name].append(begin.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / graph_calls)
        result = dict(
            capacity=capacity,
            experts=experts,
            live_rows=experts * live_per_expert,
            hidden=hidden,
            group_size=group,
            samples_us=samples,
            median_us={k: statistics.median(v) for k, v in samples.items()},
        )
        results.append(result)
        print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
    args.output.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
                "warmups": warmups,
                "iterations": iterations,
                "graph_calls": graph_calls,
                "results": results,
            },
            indent=2,
        )
        + "\n"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run from an environment with this PR installed. Extract the original dense implementation from the parent of the activation change:

```bash
git show 6117e97834:vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py > baseline.py
.venv/bin/python benchmark.py --baseline baseline.py --output benchmark.json
```

The following is fresh output from the corrected benchmark, run on GB200 on 2026-09-28 as `tms-silu-padding-replay-20260928`. title: [ROCm][CI] Pin OpenTelemetry to LMCache's cap in the ROCm images
author: Rohan138
body:
## Purpose

ROCm and ROCk release images have failed every nightly since 2026-09-26. OpenTelemetry 1.45 added `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-common`; LMCache caps `opentelemetry-api<=1.40.0`, so installing it downgrades the stack, strands that package, and fails `uv pip check`. This pins `opentelemetry-api<=1.40.0` when installing vLLM into both images.

Also reverts #59056: its SDK/exporter caps on LMCache's requirements don't remove the stranded package, and the build still fails with them.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; reviewed by me.

## Test Plan

Local `Dockerfile.rock` release image builds with `INSTALL_LMCACHE=true` on MI300X, with #59056 and with this change.

## Test Result

With #59056 the build fails with the same `uv pip check` error; with this change it passes, OpenTelemetry stays at 1.40.0, and `import lmcache` works.

title: [Feature][Quantization] Gather MiMo fused-QKV FP8 rows exactly by default
author: peperunas
body:
## Purpose

This PR upstreams work from the patch set of the MiMo recipe we deploy — Diffbot's MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL FP8KV/W4A8 recipe (Hugging Face: diffbot/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-FP8KV-W4A8-2x-RTX-PRO-6000, built by Mike Tung), itself porting parts from the local-inference-lab/vllm fork: the idea and the original implementation belong to the recipe's authors, not to us. Their version of this change is tracked in local-inference-lab/vllm#874; we re-derived the diff against upstream main, wrote or extended the tests, and ran the checks.

### Motivation

`_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` re-quantizes every gathered row through a dequantize-requantize round trip whenever `tp_size != ckpt_tp`: the fallback re-derives each block scale in fp32 and only reproduces the checkpoint's bytes when rounding cooperates.

When `ckpt_tp` is a multiple of `tp_size`, the rank's rows can be taken from the checkpoint byte-for-byte instead, in two shapes:

- **Block-aligned segments** (MiMo SWA chunks: 3712 = 29 x 128 rows, all three segments multiples of 128): a pure block permutation — gather the rows directly, no arithmetic, no scale re-derivation.
- **Straddling segments** (GA/Pro chunks: a 192-row K segment, one and a half scale blocks): each owned chunk keeps its K and V rows together, zero-padded to a whole block count, so every row still carries its checkpoint scale — the rank's parameter becomes the zero-padded `[Q_1 | ... | Q_g | K_1 V_1 pad | ... | K_g V_g pad]` layout, built as a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` instead of a de-interleaved `QKVParallelLinear`. The forward splits that padded output back per chunk. A checkpoint whose scales form one continuous grid (rather than one grid per chunk) fails loudly with a `ValueError` naming the precondition instead of dying in a shape assert at load.

Layouts failing the divisor or Q-segment alignment conjunct keep the existing path unchanged.

The exact gather is now the default: it is selected by geometry alone, so a rank whose layout qualifies takes checkpoint rows byte-for-byte. A padded layout whose scales are not per chunk now raises instead of silently requantizing. Four signed commits: the block-permutation gather with its tests, the padded gather for straddling segments, the module wiring with its round-trip test, and the removal of the environment gate.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `mimo qkv fp8`, `exact fp8 qkv gather`, and `mimo exact qkv` (zero hits). The open PRs in this loader area, verified against their pages, are orthogonal:

- #58142 keeps fused-QKV pairing state across weight-loading calls (edits `load_weights`);
- #58184 skips fused-QKV tensors for absent layers (edits `load_weights`);
- #46755 adds TP > num_kv_heads head replication (edits `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj`).

None changes the row-selection math for `tp_size < ckpt_tp`. Re-running `gh search` immediately before opening this PR returned no matching PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py vllm/envs.py tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py
ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py vllm/envs.py tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py -v
```

## Test Result

Results: **31 passed, 2 skipped** — the 19 pre-existing sharding tests, unchanged, plus:

- `test_exact_gather_permutes_checkpoint_rows` (SWA geometry, tp 1 and 2): weights and scales byte-identical to the checkpoint rows the rank owns;
- `test_exact_padded_layout_matches_checkpoint` (GA and Pro geometries, tp below `ckpt_tp`): every weight byte equal to the checkpoint's `[Q | K V pad]` order with zero pad rows, and every scale row in the padded order;
- `test_split_qkv_round_trips_the_padded_layout` (GA and Pro, tp below `ckpt_tp`): `_split_qkv` on the transposed rank slice returns exactly the checkpoint rows the rank owns, byte for byte — pinning the writer's padded order to the reader's so a one-sided layout change cannot slip through with shapes intact.

The 2 skips are `tp_size >= ckpt_tp` cases of the padded tests: the plain-chunk path covers that region, not the padded one. `test_flag_off_keeps_requantizing_loader` went away with the gate; the requantizing loader keeps its coverage in `test_fused_qkv_proj_sharding` at `tp_size=8`.

`pre-commit run` itself cannot execute in this NixOS environment (hook environments fail with the `stub-ld` dynamic-linker error), so the repo-pinned ruff 0.14.0 was run directly.

**No model eval was run.** The exact gather takes checkpoint rows without arithmetic and is now the default for the geometries that qualify, so a deployment should compare its outputs against a requantizing build on its own model before rollout — that comparison is not part of this PR.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used (pi coding agent): analysis, draft, and test runs were produced by the agent; the human author reviewed every changed line, ran the checks above, and defends the change end-to-end.

title: [ROCm]Keep LMCache OpenTelemetry on the image's 1.40 stack
author: micah-wil
body: LMCache 0.5.3 caps opentelemetry-api at 1.40.0 but leaves opentelemetry-sdk and opentelemetry-exporter-otlp unbounded. Installing the wheel into the final image downgrades the API and SDK to 1.40 while leaving 1.45 exporter packages that require sdk~=1.45.0, so uv pip check fails. title: [Bugfix][Core] Remove redundant AuxOutput reset guards after pause
author: aoshen02
body:
## Why

AuxOutput reset checks unnecessarily constrain the pause mode. For example, an abort-mode pause can finish draining outputs without setting `PAUSED_ALL`.

The supported workflow is to await pause completion before explicitly resetting the prefix cache. With `clear_cache=True`, pause performs the reset internally after draining. This PR does not add support for resetting AuxOutput during active inference without a completed pause.

## Change

- Remove the AuxOutput-specific pause-mode and in-flight checks from `Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache`.
- Keep the existing KV reset checks and Worker pending-output assertion.
- Update the scheduler test to reset after outputs have drained without requiring a particular pause mode.
- Remove the previously added EngineCore queue-draining implementation and its tests; `core.py` is restored to its pre-change implementation.

AuxOutput generation, temporary-state cleanup, and storage retention are unchanged. This does not implement retaining R3 across a GPU-only cache reset.

## Validation

- `/home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'reset_prefix_cache or aux_output_reset or pause_synchronizes_device_before_cache_reset' -q`: **5 passed**, 210 deselected.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks: **passed**, including mypy.
- No GPU model-output evaluation or serving throughput benchmark was run for this revision; validation is unit-level.

## Related work

This updates the existing fix rather than opening a duplicate. #56754 concerns in-process sleep waiting; #57810 concerns retaining external KV connector state. Broader investigation: https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/82.

AI assistance was used. Human review is required before merge.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Fuse AttnRes output with per-token FP8 input quantization
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Summary

Eligible Kimi-K3 AMD AttnRes outputs currently materialize BF16 activations that the next linear immediately quantizes. Fuse that per-token FP8 conversion into AttnRes and pass native `QuantizedActivation` to supported consumers.

```diff
 AttnRes + output RMSNorm
-  store BF16 → per-token FP8 quant → input GEMM
+  store FP8 + scale → input GEMM
```

Enable the path only for `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` and only when all consumers accept the same key. Mixed MoE/router consumers, unsupported linear kernels, and batch-invariant mode retain the original path. Preserve BF16 rounding before quantization and the prefix/block write contract.

This is independent of PD connector work and targets main. Duplicate checks covered #50682, #52968, and #53154: #52968's current diff covers convolution and sigmoid/multiply; #53154 covers MXFP4 output fusions. This PR supplies AttnRes per-token FP8 inputs. The current rowwise Torch FP8 KDA kernel does not expose the required input capability, so this PR does not claim all KDA inputs are fused.

## Evidence

### CI follow-up (2026-10-08)

[Buildkite #93497](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93497) exposed an implicit compiled reference in the FP8 output test when AITER is disabled. Commit `42f0ad593` sets `compile_native=False` for the `QuantFP8` reference, keeping its rounding independent of Inductor fusion. Production code and every numerical tolerance are unchanged. The AttnRes and MLA/KDA direct-return suites pass with AITER disabled (**23 passed**) and enabled (**23 passed**); changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy pass. [Buildkite #93546](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93546) retries the failed K3 step on that commit.


- **Before:** AttnRes and per-token quantization launch separately.
  **After:** A single producer emits activation and scale. Existing + new AttnRes cases passed on all eight MI355X GPUs (16 tests/rank in the final run, including the three capability cases), with exact prefix/block writes, scale rtol 1e-6, and rounding differences limited to an adjacent FP8 code in <1e-4 of values. Three direct-return tests also passed.
- In the paired rank-0 prefill trace, the corresponding standalone AITER per-token quant kernel count falls from 4009 to 3078 (931 calls removed), while AttnRes executes the same 3553 calls.
- `pre-commit run` and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`: passed.

title: [ROCm][MLA] Keep DCP prefill context in FP8 through AllGather
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Keep ROCm MLA's cached DCP context in FP8 through AllGather, then use AITER's fused gather/projection kernel to expand it into K/V. This removes the BF16 communication payload and separate reorganization, dequantization, projection and packing operations for supported configurations.

```diff
 local cached context
-  gather/dequant → BF16 AllGather → reorg → kv_b_proj → K/V pack
+  gather bytes → FP8 AllGather → fused reorg/dequant/kv_b_proj/K/V pack
```

## Claims

- Halves AllGather bytes for the same padded row count, preserving the existing FP8 cache bytes, workspace capacity, chunking and merge plan.
- Falls back to the original path for unsupported cache formats, dimensions, dtypes or projection layouts. The optional upstream K/V concatenation callback is forwarded on that fallback.
- Historical full-model K3 measurements below show unchanged aggregate GSM8K accuracy and lower cached-prefix TTFT with **both this PR and #59069**. Those measurements do not isolate this PR's end-to-end contribution or validate the current rebased head.

## Validation

### Full-set K3 GSM8K (2026-10-12)

| Full GSM8K | Original context path | Fused context path |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Strict match | **1264/1319 (95.8302%)** | **1263/1319 (95.7544%)** |
| Flexible extract | **1264/1319 (95.8302%)** | **1263/1319 (95.7544%)** |
| HTTP success | 1319/1319 | 1319/1319 |
| Output-cap hits | 0 | 0 |
| Natural DSpark token acceptance | 96567/121728 (79.3301%) | 96818/122628 (78.9526%) |

### End-to-end K3 serving performance

Historical paired run on **8 × MI355X, TP8/DCP8**, complete Kimi-K3, FP8 KV, DSpark3 with natural/standard rejection, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, 80 max sequences, 16,384 batched tokens and 1,048,576 context. Candidate includes **#59069 + #59070**. These are full-model, single-instance serving measurements, not PD throughput measurements.

Each row reports server TTFT in **milliseconds, median [min, max] over three unprofiled repetitions** of the same prefix chain. All 24 first-token outputs, cache-hit counts and computed-token counts match between baseline and candidate.

| Request | Baseline TTFT | Candidate TTFT | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold 32K prompt | 1701.03 [1700.41, 1701.44] | 1673.86 [1670.82, 1673.95] | −1.60% |
| Exact 32K repeat | 83.37 [82.56, 83.38] | 77.13 [77.05, 77.41] | −7.49% |
| Append 1,024 tokens | 290.44 [288.19, 297.70] | 291.09 [288.70, 294.20] | +0.22% |
| Fork at token 12,032 | 1114.15 [1114.11, 1114.24] | 1091.69 [1090.71, 1091.89] | −2.02% |
| Repeat fork | 69.97 [69.47, 72.26] | 64.42 [64.28, 64.70] | −7.94% |
| Append 1,024 to fork | 284.95 [284.06, 286.92] | 282.61 [278.15, 290.25] | −0.82% |
| Sibling at token 12,032 | 1115.93 [1114.84, 1116.79] | 1093.48 [1092.50, 1093.77] | −2.01% |
| Repeat sibling | 70.79 [70.36, 71.16] | 64.56 [64.54, 64.80] | −8.79% |

The 1,024-token append is effectively unchanged. In a separate single C16 natural-acceptance decode diagnostic, TPOT is **9.867 → 9.840 ms** and request-group elapsed time is **2.312 → 2.288 s**; no statistical speedup claim is made from that single pair. Eight 33K+ context arithmetic checks all answer correctly; 7/8 full continuations match.

<details>
<summary>Segment benchmark, provenance and reproduction</summary>

Eight-GPU gather-through-K/V-expansion benchmark with real NCCL AllGather, two requests with uneven rank tails/nonzero starts and BF16 weights. Nine rotated samples per rank, five-call CUDA-graph replay; median of eight rank medians:

| Context tokens | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,446 | 74.80 | 60.94 |
| 12,198 | 289.05 | 151.89 |
| 49,062 | 778.18 | 386.80 |
| 98,214 | 1267.18 | 709.19 |
| 196,518 | 2397.64 | 1356.37 |

K/V relative L2 is approximately 0.00135/0.00251 (<0.004), and RoPE channels are exact. This segment excludes attention and the rest of the model. The full-model trace records 384 fused gather/projection calls replacing 384 separate gather/dequant calls. The first graph benchmark required termination during NCCL cleanup after measurements were saved; a follow-up eight-rank 1,024-local-token run with explicit cleanup exited successfully. The benchmark was later removed from the PR to reduce review scope; its source remains in the [original PR revision](https://github.com/whx-sjtu/vllm/blob/b7cf4d59ad25437799c91ff1e2de570e72bad7aa/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py).

Historical K3 results were collected on 2026-09-28: saved diagnostic baseline `d7b093131` (snapshot based on `ccfd1cea75eff8956c5d08b15a7eaec8891642e9`) versus integration commit `3b1aa4f043ae37ba1b2099ae2ed5e04fdd31e5dd`. Archived `comparison.json`, `prefill-comparison.json`, raw per-request timings, model launch manifests and lm-eval result/sample files were checked when updating this description. Both arms use the same dependencies and serving configuration. The isolated DeepSeek smoke test loaded `f3bb722300272d27eee288657db9df8d75d79f6f`; subsequent `8c0884efd` has the identical production tree. Neither archived model experiment is a fresh run of the 2026-10-08 head.

K3 evaluation command (run against each serving configuration):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m lm_eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args 'model=Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:2584/v1/completions,tokenizer_backend=None,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=16,max_retries=1,timeout=1800,max_length=1048576,max_gen_toks=8192' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 --limit 128 \
  --gen_kwargs 'max_gen_toks=8192,temperature=0.0,do_sample=False' \
  --seed 0,1234,1234,1234 --log_samples --output_path results
```

Current regression commands (with AITER gather/projection dependencies available):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_op_registration.py -q
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py
```

The full-set K3 and independent prefix-path results above cover `e95f8244`. Whole-model validation of the later automatic main merge `c90a66e3` remains separate.

</details>

## Details

A compact row map is built once per metadata step; the shared eligibility check prevents unnecessary map construction for unsupported configurations. Expose the AITER operation through `_aiter_ops.py`, including mutation declarations, fake implementation and opcheck coverage. The required kernel was already present in main's pinned AITER `v0.1.23`; this PR requires no AITER bump or PD connector changes.

Duplicate checks covered #50682, #53166, #56881 and #52239. #53166 enables the AITER gather path only at DCP=1; #56881 packs already-projected K/V in the NVIDIA path; #52239 uses NVIDIA symmetric-memory multicast. This change supplies ROCm compressed AllGather plus fused expansion at DCP>1.

Rollback is a two-way change: no checkpoint or cache format changes; reverting restores the original computation path. Impact is limited to ROCm MLA DCP prefill. AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, analysis and validation.

title: [Bugfix] Respect Inductor deterministic mode in combo-kernel defaults
author: cheese-cakee
body:
## Purpose

vLLM enables combo-kernel benchmarking by default, which conflicts with Inductor deterministic compilation and can fail a fresh Qwen3 startup in `may_ban_benchmarking`.

Disable automatic combo-kernel benchmarking when effective Inductor determinism is enabled. Preserve horizontal fusion, explicit combo settings, and CPU/version guards. Per-compile `deterministic` overrides the global setting; older Inductor configurations without that field retain existing defaults.

Relates to #58899. This addresses the startup conflict only. It does not address PyTorch's separate flag-restoration issue (pytorch/pytorch#198563) or guarantee reproducible serving output.

## Test Plan

- Extend `tests/compile/test_config.py` for global/per-compile precedence, explicit combo settings, platform/version guards, and missing Inductor setting.
- Compare original and patched configurations with fresh compiler caches on CUDA.
- Compare Qwen3-0.6B cold generation against the explicit workaround and a warm-cache restart, plus a normal-mode cold start.

## Test Result

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/compile/test_config.py -k combo_kernel -v`: original source **3 failed, 14 passed**; patched source **17 passed**.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/compile/test_config.py -k 'not test_VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE and not test_use_cudagraphs and not test_stock_torch_compile and not test_no_compilation and not test_enforce_eager and not test_torch_compile_disable' -v`: **83 passed, 11 deselected**. Model-fixture cases excluded from this run; small-model checks below are separate.

- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual`: passed.
- Fresh CUDA q/k normalization compile: original defaults fail in combo benchmarking; patched defaults compile and match eager outputs at `rtol=atol=1e-5`.
- Qwen3-0.6B (`c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`), `custom_ops=['none']`, CUDA graphs disabled, greedy generation, three prompts × 16 tokens: original deterministic cold startup fails in `may_ban_benchmarking`; patched cold startup succeeds with 29 Inductor compilations. Tokens and all returned top-5 log probabilities exactly match the explicit `benchmark_combo_kernel=False` workaround and a warm-cache restart (0 recompilations). Normal-mode cold startup/generation also succeeds with 29 compilations.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04.4 WSL2, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, RTX 4050 Laptop GPU. Deterministic checks set `TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC=1`, `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, and `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` to keep the upstream flag-restoration issue separate. title: [CPU] Improve long-context MTP attention scheduling on AMX
author: tianmu-li

# [CPU] Improve long-context MTP attention scheduling on AMX

## Purpose

Extend CPU attention's grouped-query (GQA) scheduling to eligible
causal multi-token requests, including MTP verification and short prefill. The
existing batch-level GQA fast path requires an all-q1 decode batch, so these
requests do not receive the same grouped scheduling. The scheduler evaluates
grouped query heads and split-KV work using each request's query length,
causality, and AMX geometry, then selects a plan through its cost model. This
applies with auto, FP8 E4M3, and FP8 E5M2 KV cache.

## Duplicate-work Check

PR [#46154](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46154) is related but not
a duplicate. It fixes generic mixed-batch GQA decode classification when
split-KV can divide a prefill request into one-token work items. This change
adds request-level eligibility based on causality, prefill state, and
verification query length, and uses it to enable AMX speculative multi-token
GQA scheduling with BF16 attention and FP8 KV.

Issue [#46131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46131), its comments,
open PRs referencing the issue, and open PRs matching CPU attention/GQA/spec
decode terms were checked. #46154 was the relevant overlap found.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Make reset_cache re-entrant
author: sohom-cs
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A second `reset_cache()` on the offloading connector before the engine steps again fails on `assert not self._current_batch_jobs_to_flush`. The engine keeps running, but the call that made the second reset gets the error. It happens when two `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` calls arrive with no step in between while store jobs are in flight: the first reset moves those jobs into the flush set, which stays set until the next step sends it. In the multiprocess engine, pause and sleep clear caches only once the engine is idle, so they don't hit this; in the in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`), pause clears at once, so a pause or sleep can be one of the two resets. This lets the second reset add to the pending flush set instead of asserting.

The first version of this PR also kept an idle engine stepping until the flush set reached the workers. #62929 now does that (the engine keeps stepping until the flushed jobs are reported), so that part is gone after merging main.

## Claims

- Two `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` calls with no step in between no longer raise. The first reset's flush set still goes out on the next step, and the engine goes idle once the workers report those jobs.
- A single reset is unchanged, and the other three "not in the middle of a step" asserts stay.

## Validation

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q -k reset_twice_before_a_step
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

`test_cache_reset_twice_before_a_step_still_flushes` uses the real-scheduler helpers from #62929: it finishes a request with its store jobs in flight, resets twice, then checks that the next `schedule()` carries exactly those jobs in `jobs_to_flush` and that the engine goes idle once they are reported.

On main (8321d1119bc2, Linux CPU) the second reset fails:

```
>       assert not self._current_batch_jobs_to_flush
E       AssertionError
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py:2463: AssertionError
```

With the fix it passes, and so does the rest of the file (446 passed, Linux CPU); pre-commit is clean on both files. These tests build the CPU offload region in `/dev/shm`, so they don't run on macOS. No CI step runs this file today: the GPU "V1 KV Connectors" step is disabled, and the CPU step selects only `cpu_test`-marked tests. No GPU run: the reproducer is scheduler-level. Model outputs are unaffected, so no evals.

## Details

`_reset_cache()` moves every in-flight job id into `_current_batch_jobs_to_flush` and leaves it set on purpose: the workers must wait on those jobs before a later store reuses their CPU chunks, and the set goes out in the next step's metadata. A second reset before that step finds it non-empty. Merging into it is safe: the first reset already moved and cleared every in-flight job, so the second adds no ids, leaves #62929's fence as it is, and does not call `on_reset_flushed()` while the fence is held.

The reset is reached from `pause_generation(clear_cache=True)` and sleep (`EngineCore._reset_caches`, the RL weight-update path), from the dev-mode `POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` and from `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`.

Not a duplicate: #62929 leaves this assert in place, and none of the open offload PRs that touch this file removes it.

title: [CI][ROCm] Export kernel source maps for CI selection
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Add a ROCm kernel-to-source map producer that reads the actual CMake/Ninja objects, including host uses, header dependencies, and embedded GPU architectures.
- Record HIPify provenance for generated sources and copied or renamed headers while leaving the original sources intact.
- Preserve the original vendor header and repository patch as dependencies of generated Torch headers.
- Generate maps in an opt-in stage after native compilation and expose a separate Docker export target.
- Export and upload the map with its build commit after a successful build or image reuse, clearing stale exports; optional map failures leave the image job successful.
- Forward recorder output and job identity from single-node AMD Docker jobs to the agent's artifact directory.
- Run producer, provenance, export, and runner regressions through the existing CMake and Docker metadata test jobs.

NVIDIA image builds already export kernel source maps for the CI selector. ROCm needs the same ownership information, but its native build transforms CUDA sources and headers into HIP inputs. The map uses the retained compilation and dependency records to recover those original paths and refuses incomplete or unsupported builds. This supplies the source half of the companion native SDK recording path, allowing CI to join observed kernel names to repository changes without guessing ownership.

Companion: [ci-infra native recording and selection for both backends](https://github.com/vllm-project/ci-infra/pull/685). Its consumers should be deployed before enabling the new map and recorder producers.

AI assistance was used to implement these changes and run the validation.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Drop stale block hashes when a session truncates tokens
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #49377.

When a streaming-input session continues, `_update_request_as_session` truncates `_all_token_ids` at `num_computed_tokens`, discarding the last sampled (never-computed) output token. `update_block_hashes` only appends and the hasher resumes at `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size`, so if the discarded token completed a hash block, that hash kept identifying the replaced sequence and could later be committed under the stale identity — letting a request whose prefix matches the old tokens hit KV computed from the new ones. The fix drops the block hashes covering discarded tokens right where the token truncation happens; blocks fully inside the kept prefix stay valid.

## This PR carries #52806

This carries #52806 by @brianosaurus (original author unresponsive to review requests) with all review comments from @sawsa307 addressed:

- Removed the comment in `scheduler.py` that only described code behavior.
- Test no longer hardcodes the block size (`hash_block_size = scheduler.hash_block_size`).
- Test docstring shortened per AGENTS.md; details kept here instead.

The original author and contributors are credited via `Co-authored-by` trailers: Brian Woods (original #52806 author), Claude Opus 5 (original commit's co-author trailer), and Change72 (initial fix idea in #49377, requested by the reviewer). This is not a duplicate PR: #52806 has been stalled since the review round; this PR applies the identical fix with the requested changes so it can move forward, with full credit preserved.

Note on forward interaction with #58778: if #58778 (keep_end fold) lands first, this drop's lower bound should switch from `num_computed_tokens` to `keep_end`; conversely if this lands first, #58778 should keep the drop at `keep_end`.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=/tmp /Users/davidcheung/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -q -p skip_cleanup_plugin
uv tool run ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py
uv tool run ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py
```

Bug-guard: with the `scheduler.py` line removed, the new test must fail; restored, it passes.

## Test Result

- Full streaming-input scheduler suite: `10 passed, 2 subtests passed` (includes the new `test_update_request_as_session_drops_stale_block_hashes`).
- Bug-guard: with the fix line removed, the new test FAILS (`1 failed`); with the line restored, it passes (`1 passed`).
- Ruff: `All checks passed!`; `2 files already formatted`. Full pre-commit suite also passed on the commit.

No model evals: the change only affects streaming-input (resumable) session bookkeeping and does not alter model outputs for non-resumable requests.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Reserve the bonus KV slot for fill-in DSpark
author: notimesea
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59104. DSpark with `sample_from_anchor=false` writes a bonus query plus N draft queries, but reserves only N lookahead slots. At a KV-block boundary, the extra write can use a stale block-table entry and corrupt another request's target KV.

Reserve N+1 slots for this layout. Anchor-sampling DSpark and DFlash behavior remain unchanged.

Related PR #48909 addresses the same mismatch with a broader four-file change, including a shared query-width property and the older runner's max-length guard. This PR is a smaller two-file alternative limited to lookahead reservation and its regression test.

## Tests

The commits are ordered test-first, fix-second:

1. `58eff92e7`: adds a plain regression test with loops and asserts; no pytest import or decorators.
2. `a26af2d9d`: fixes lookahead reservation.

```sh
python -m pytest --noconftest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py -k dspark_lookahead_covers_query_window -q
```

**Before: 1 failed. After: 1 passed.** The test covers 12 combinations of true/false/missing anchor flag, N=1/7 and block sizes 16/32, with prompt lengths spanning two blocks. Validation used the exact test file in an isolated pinned-nightly environment with the source fix applied; the full repository suite was not run. Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.

Standalone [synthetic CUDA reproducer](https://gist.github.com/notimesea/7de52434b9ef659e1ae6a6aab4d201b7) exercises the actual draft slot-preparation kernel without model weights or user prompts. It fails before the fix and passes after it; instructions and expected output are included in the gist.

## GPU validation

Gemma4-31B-it + RedHatAI DSpark on one H200, BF16, FA4, V2 runner, eager, synchronous scheduling, prefix caching off, no LoRA; vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev284+gbeef814e1`.

- Before: deterministic malformed output on batch 9; instrumentation confirmed two draft writes into target-owned blocks.
- After: three cold starts × 20 batches × 16 requests (**960 responses**), no observed corruption; identical output tokens across the three runs. On the originally failing batch, no invalid draft writes or target-KV mutations were observed.

This is bounded regression validation, not a full quality benchmark or a claim of bitwise equivalence to non-speculative decoding.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with debugging, implementation and tests.

title: [Bugfix][CPU][DiffusionGemma] Support narrower canvas w/ sync scheduling
author: ojeda-e
body:
## Purpose

Fixes DiffusionGemma structured reads on the CPU backend.

Structured reads were added to DiffusionGemma in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57250 and tested on GPU. On CPU they fail with the faster narrower canvases. When async scheduling is disabled, reads that ask for a canvas narrower than the served one are rejected. CPU always runs synchronous scheduling (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31525), and the error asks for `--async-scheduling`, but CPU ignores that flag.

The same happens on any platform started with `--no-async-scheduling`.

This PR adds a synchronous diffusion scheduler that trims each request's canvas to its own width. The async diffusion scheduler already does this. Other models are not affected.

### Changes in this PR

- Add a `DiffusionScheduler` for sync scheduling. It cuts each request's canvas down to the width the request asked for, in `update_draft_token_ids()`. `DiffusionAsyncScheduler` now inherits from it.
- `VllmConfig` selects the matching diffusion scheduler for both sync and async scheduling.
- Remove the check that rejected narrow canvases unless `--async-scheduling` was set.
- Update the structured diffusion README and the tests in `tests/test_sampling_params.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` to match.

No open issue or PR covers this. I searched for `diffusion_canvas_length`, DiffusionGemma on CPU and CPU async scheduling for diffusion. The closest is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58964, which fixed a separate DiffusionGemma crash on CPU. Structured reads still fail on CPU after that fix. 

I used Codex to help with this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C, Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at 32cc3f1ea8, with the real `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` checkpoint in BF16.

**Unit tests:**

```bash
pytest -v tests/test_sampling_params.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
```

**End to end:**

1. Before and after. Send a read with a 32-token canvas to a server with a 64-token canvas, on `main` and with this PR.
2. Correctness. Compare that read with a full-width read on a server with a 32-token canvas. Both give the model the same 32 tokens. The logprobs of 8 label ids at the answer position should match.
3. Serving. Run `vllm serve` with `structured_server.py` in front of it, as in the example README. Send the README's `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/systemone` requests with an outage ticket and a typo ticket. Then send a plain chat completion straight to vLLM.

```bash
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=8 vllm serve google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it --served-model-name dgemma \
    --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 64}' --max-logprobs 32 --enable-prefix-caching \
    --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 8
python examples/features/structured_diffusion/structured_server.py --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --tokenizer google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it --canvas 64 --port 8011
```

## Test Result

Before (`main`), the read fails. The issue has the full traceback and the `collect_env.py` output.

```text
vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: A diffusion_canvas_length smaller than the served canvas requires --async-scheduling. (parameter=extra_args)
```

After:

- Unit tests: 276 passed.
- The narrow read now works. `DiffusionScheduler` serves it, and its logprobs at the answer position match the full-width read exactly (max difference 0 across 8 label ids). Both answer "yes" with p = 0.89.
- Through `structured_server.py`, `/v1/systemone` gives 0.91 urgency for the outage ticket (4 reads, 2.0 s) and 0.00006 for the typo ticket (1 read, 0.7 s). Every request returns HTTP 200, and the server logs show no errors.
- A plain chat completion straight to `vllm serve` returns `"thought\nThe capital of France is Paris."` and stops normally.

title: [DSv4.1] Avoid runtime recompiles of _ring_slot_mapping_kernel
author: Juntian777
body:
## Summary

`_ring_slot_mapping_kernel` builds the compressor ring slot mapping in `CompressorMetadataBuilder.build()` and runs on every step. Its int args `num_tokens` and `num_actual_tokens` change from step to step, and Triton specializes int args by value (`== 1`, `% 16 == 0`, or neither), so each new combination compiles a new variant while serving. These compiles are not covered by startup warmup because the triggering combinations depend on the live batch (for example, a real token count that is a multiple of 16 padded to one that is not). Under DP/EP, a rank that stops to compile stalls every other rank at the next collective.

This PR marks `block_table_stride`, `num_actual_tokens` and `num_tokens` as `do_not_specialize`, so one variant is compiled at startup and reused for every batch. These args only feed address and mask arithmetic; dropping their divisibility hints narrows some loads/stores, but the kernel is latency-bound on its dependent loads and performance is unchanged (see below).

Evidence from a DSv4.1-Flash DEP4 AgentX run on GB200: a new variant of this kernel was compiled 46 min after the server was healthy, in the middle of a benchmark, and the Triton cache holds 6 variants of it.

This does not overlap with #58560, which changes the kernel's store mask (null block), not its specialization.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py`
- Kernel microbenchmark: main (bare `@triton.jit`) vs this PR on GB200, FlashInfer `bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` (CUPTI), `block_table_stride=1` and `CAPACITY=8` (5 draft tokens) as in serving. 37 token counts from 1 to 8192, exact and padded; outputs match exactly.

## Test Result

- 136 passed, 13 skipped.
- Performance is unchanged. PR / main geomean over the 37 shapes is 1.005 with cold L2 (range 0.99–1.02) and 0.98 with warm L2 (noise at ~1.5 us). Compiled variants over the sweep: main 5, PR 1.

Cold L2, a subset of the shapes:

| real / padded tokens | main (us) | PR (us) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 / 1 | 2.11 | 2.14 |
| 42 / 48 | 1.98 | 2.02 |
| 256 / 256 | 2.02 | 2.02 |
| 366 / 368 | 1.70 | 1.73 |
| 1500 / 1504 | 1.86 | 1.89 |
| 4096 / 4096 | 2.27 | 2.24 |
| 8188 / 8192 | 2.24 | 2.24 |

title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA] Add opt-in FlyDSL FP8 prefill attention for AITER MLA
author: gbyu-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8`, an opt-in MLA prefill backend that runs AITER's FlyDSL FP8 flash attention on dynamically per-tensor quantized Q/K/V, for Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950). Port of the approach in [ROCm/ATOM#2191](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2191); supersedes #62447, which its author closed in favor of this PR.

## Claims

- New tokens, context chunks and context-free prefills all run FP8 FlyDSL attention. Selected with `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`; not auto-selected.
- Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 agentic replay (InferenceX agentx-mvp, c48): total throughput +4.5%, TTFT p90 -15.8%, ITL p90 -8.7%.
- 8K fresh prefill on current main and AITER v0.1.27, against the ASM FP8 prefill it replaces: TTFT mean -2.5%, p90 -9.1%.
- Accuracy unchanged. With DSpark MTP on current main: GPQA Diamond 91.4% in both arms, RULER NIAH 100% at 32K and 128K in both arms, DSpark acceptance length 3.819 vs 3.823, GSM8K 0.9651 vs 0.9591 (within one standard error of the difference). Earlier revision, without MTP: GSM8K 0.9621 in both arms; Kimi tool-call eval within run-to-run noise.
- No model or shape is hard-coded: availability and head dims come from AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported`; inputs the kernel cannot take (empty, or at least 2^31 elements) fall back to the parent BF16 `ROCM_AITER_FA` path.

## Validation

Unit tests, MI355X, main @ `410ab341a8` + this PR:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py        # 935 passed, 349 skipped (GLM dims, TRTLLM-only params)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_flydsl_fp8_prefill.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py   # 64 passed (kernel tests included)
```

`ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` is in `PREFILL_BACKENDS_TO_TEST`, so `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` check it against SDPA; a `context_free_prefill` spec checks context-free batches against SDPA with this backend selected. That spec checks output only: it also passes with `_asm_fp8_prefill_superseded` forced to `False`, so it does not show which kernel ran; the e2e runs below confirm the backend from the server log.

CI coverage: only the MI355 `test_mla_backends.py` step runs with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, so it is the one CI job that exercises this backend. The FlyDSL kernel test and the head-dim selector test skip in CI (the `kernels/attention` step runs on MI300/gfx942, and the selector step does not enable AITER); I ran them on MI355X above.

End-to-end, 8x MI355X. Server (InferenceX `kimik3_fp4_mi355x` config; the arms differ only in `mla_prefill_backend`):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}'
# baseline: --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' (ASM FP8 prefill for context-free batches)
```

| Benchmark | Command | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot (strict / flexible) | `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5` | 0.9621 / 0.9621 | 0.9621 / 0.9621 |
| Agentic replay, c48, 3600 s | `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp --concurrency 48 --benchmark-duration 3600 --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126` | 91,787 tok/s, TTFT p90 3690 ms | 95,931 tok/s, TTFT p90 3106 ms |
| 8K fresh prefill x128, c16, 2 runs | `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 16` | TTFT mean 6414 ms, p90 7303 ms | TTFT mean 6255 ms, p90 6638 ms |

Accuracy with DSpark MTP, current main + this PR at `4d1ee17353` (code identical to `aea6855e4d`), AITER v0.1.27. Same server plus `--speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'`; one run per arm.

|---|---|---:|---:|

<details><summary>Run details and more results</summary>

- The 8K row and the unit tests use current main with AITER v0.1.27. The GSM8K and agentic rows were measured on the first revision of this PR (same kernel calls behind an env flag, AITER 0.1.22 with the FlyDSL FP8 sources from AITER main); `cross_seqlen=True` since then is bit-identical.
- Full server command and environment:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --moe-backend auto --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --load-format fastsafetensors --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}' --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","max_cudagraph_capture_size":96,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,3,...,96]}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}' \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a
```
- Agentic replay, full table:

| Metric | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| TTFT p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 1176 / 3690 / 22443 | 1119 / 3106 / 16155 |
| ITL p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 51.1 / 74.6 / 188.0 | 49.2 / 68.2 / 130.5 |
| Total / output tok/s | 91,787 / 609.2 | 95,931 / 638.5 |

- Kimi Vendor Verifier `kimi_tool_call_schema_full` (408 records), two runs per arm: baseline 0.9779 / 0.9877, FlyDSL 0.9755 / 0.9951.
- Prefill TTFT, first revision: 32K chunked -1.6%, 128K -7.3%, 64K with a 56K cached prefix -6.2%.
- Backend micro-benchmark (12 heads, qk 192 / v 128, FP8 time includes quantization), BF16 vs FlyDSL: 1x8192 causal 313 vs 229 us; q 1024 + context 64K 1278 vs 549 us; q 128 + context 64K 1251 vs 351 us.

</details>

## Details

- **Backend.** Subclasses `ROCM_AITER_FA`. Q is quantized once per forward and reused by every context chunk; each chunk quantizes only its own K/V. The LSE layout is unchanged, so `merge_attn_states` is reused.
- **Context-free prefills.** With this backend selected, `ROCM_AITER_MLA` no longer runs its ASM FP8 prefill (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd`) or allocates its PS workspace; the gate is `_asm_fp8_prefill_superseded`, shared by the metadata builder and `forward_mha`.
- **Quantizer.** `triton_per_tensor_fp8_quant.py`, adapted from ATOM#2191's fused QKV quantizer (MIT), quantizes up to three strided tensors in two launches with no atomics and no recompiles across batch shapes. Existing ops do not fit: `ops.scaled_fp8_quant` matches numerically but takes the per-row path on strided V (65K tokens: 10.2 ms for Q/K/V vs 0.35 ms here), and `rocm_aiter_ops.per_tensor_quant` returns wrong results on strided V.
- **Docs.** `mla_prefill_backend`'s docstring, which renders the CLI reference, now lists the ROCm prefill backends.
- **AITER.** Needs `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported` (ROCm/aiter#5718); main's pinned AITER v0.1.27 has it, along with `softmax_scale`, short-query split-K and the AOT `varlen_cross` kernels for `kimi_k3_tp8` (ROCm/aiter#5796, #5901). The new-token call uses `cross_seqlen=True` so it hits those AOT kernels; output is bit-identical to `cross_seqlen=False`.
- **Not a duplicate.** #62447 (same idea inside `ROCM_AITER_FA`) is closed in favor of this PR. #51551 is a gfx942 Gluon path with static per-head scales.
