title: [Perf][MoE] Skip padded work in block-FP8 DeepGEMM experts
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
## Purpose

Skip padded work in block-FP8 `DeepGemmExperts` on SM90 and SM100-family GPUs. Both grouped GEMMs use DeepGEMM's prefix-sum scheduler, and fused SiLU/SwiGLU activation quantization consumes the same live expert endpoints. This avoids visiting unused padded GEMM tiles and quantizing the full allocated workspace when only a fraction contains live rows.

The shared permutation helper produces expert endpoints for both architectures. SM100 dispatch uses packed UE8M0 activation scales; SM90 dispatch uses the column-major FP32 activation-scale path, including plain and power-of-two-rounded scales. The dispatch remains limited to block-FP8 weights and supported fused gated activations. `mk_alignment_scope` and DeepGEMM's default `ensure_zero_padding=True` remain in place. Other paths keep their existing behavior.

## Relationship to existing work

This PR now includes the SM90 work from #59220 alongside the SM100 work. The latest commit restores the exact combined source tree tested before those paths were split; #59220 is being closed as superseded. #59044 enables prefix sums for FP4 weights on SM10.x but leaves FP8 callers unchanged. The shared permutation and packed-activation helpers from that PR are included here for review against main and should be reconciled when it lands. #54109 changes the padded activation-format contract and targets the FP4 DeepGEMM caller; it does not wire both FP8 GEMMs and fused activation to these endpoints. No issue is closed.

## Validation

The GPU runs used the combined implementation before the split. The final commit restores that same source tree; local pre-commit, mypy, and `git diff --check` passed after restoration. Validation overlaid three changed source files onto a pinned vLLM image rather than rebuilding current main. DeepGEMM binaries and headers were unchanged.

### SM100 on B200

Two independent single-B200 runs used Pirate (`b200-02`) and Pirate2 (`dell-b200-02`). The full-expert graph regression compared the existing FP8 scheduler with prefix sums during CUDA-graph replay, including changing routing, one live row, empty routing, GPU token-count metadata, and poisoned workspaces. Packed activation tests checked live values and scales, untouched gaps, clamping, empty experts, and changing endpoints. **75 tests passed on each cluster** (32.18 s and 39.48 s), before the SM90 extension. A later B200 run of the combined source passed 123 tests covering the packed and column-major paths, before two direct GEMM tests were added.

The full-expert benchmark covered permutation, both GEMMs, activation quantization, and unpermutation/reduction, using 32 experts, FP8 E4M3 weights with 128×128 scales, intermediate size 2,048, hidden size 7,168, top-k 8, and BF16 inputs/outputs. CUPTI kernel-span timings of captured CUDA graphs used cold L2 and 100 measured samples per arm across four alternating rounds; allocation, compilation, and capture were excluded. In the heavily padded 512-capacity / 16-live-token case, latency improved from 472.176 to 347.456 µs on Pirate and 469.101 to 344.942 µs on Pirate2 (26.4–26.5%). At 4,096 / 4,096 tokens, it improved from 1,570.834 to 1,509.025 µs and 1,590.503 to 1,513.257 µs (3.9–4.9%). All benchmark outputs matched bit for bit.

Paired full GSM8K evaluation used `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-block` at revision `6b2399be90eff484848cbbabd684930e01400d54`: all 1,319 questions, five-shot, greedy, seed 42, at most 256 output tokens and 64 sequences, model length 8,192, TP1/EP1, BF16 KV cache, `moe_backend=deep_gemm`, and full/piecewise CUDA graphs. Pirate baseline/optimized accuracy was 1,176/1,319 (89.158%) and 1,182/1,319 (89.613%); Pirate2 was 1,178/1,319 (89.310%) and 1,176/1,319 (89.158%). All runs passed the 85% threshold. Generated token sequences matched on 810 and 805 questions, respectively. These results do not establish bitwise model equivalence or an accuracy improvement.

### SM90 on H200

The SM90 regression covers both projections leaving unused output capacity untouched, changing routing and endpoints during CUDA-graph replay, empty routing, and both plain and rounded FP32 column-major activation scales. **125 tests passed for each scale mode** on one Waldorf H200. These runs used the combined implementation. The pinned DeepGEMM prefix-sum scheduler skips unused whole tiles; padding within a partially filled tile remains. All measured full-expert outputs matched bit for bit.

Using the same full-expert benchmark shape and timing method, the 512-capacity / 16-live-token case improved from 694.415 to 438.144 µs with plain FP32 scales and 694.735 to 438.735 µs with rounded FP32 scales (about 37%). At 4,096 / 4,096 tokens, it improved from 2,874.813 to 2,646.141 µs and 2,935.535 to 2,739.246 µs (6.7–8.0%). A ten-shape activation-only comparison found no material regression in the ordinary dense path. Expert metadata added roughly 0.3–1.8 µs for some fully occupied small shapes.

Paired full GSM8K used the same pinned model and revision, 1,319 questions, five-shot greedy decoding, seed 42, at most 256 output tokens and 256 sequences, model length 8,192, TP1/EP1, BF16 KV cache, `moe_backend=deep_gemm`, full/piecewise CUDA graphs, and rounded FP32 activation scales. Baseline accuracy was 1,180/1,319 (89.462%); optimized accuracy was 1,181/1,319 (89.538%). Both exceeded 85%, and 1,317 generated token sequences matched exactly. This was an accuracy check, not a model-throughput benchmark or evidence of improved accuracy.

### Commands and scope

GPU commands were run with the pinned container's `/tmp/check/.venv/bin/python`, with extracted tests in `/tmp/bundle` and source overlays under `/tmp/overlay`:

```bash
# B200: tests, benchmark, and paired model evaluation for each variant
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/bundle/test_fp8.py /tmp/bundle/test_activation.py -q --disable-warnings --junitxml=/tmp/bundle/pytest.xml
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/benchmark.py
FP8_VARIANT=dense PYTHONPATH=/tmp/eval_dense /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/model_eval.py
FP8_VARIANT=prefix PYTHONPATH=/tmp/eval_prefix /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/model_eval.py

# H200: repeat tests and benchmark once for each scale mode
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0 PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/bundle/test_fp8.py /tmp/bundle/test_activation.py -q
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1 PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/bundle/test_fp8.py /tmp/bundle/test_activation.py -q
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0 PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/benchmark.py
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1 PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/benchmark.py
```

`test_fp8.py` extracts the relevant tests and helpers from `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py` and `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py` to avoid unrelated test-package dependencies; `test_activation.py` copies the activation suite. Local checks on the restored combined tree:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py
git diff --check
```

The pinned runtime was `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f29125bcc6d276ed38a67c9dfd4e51ccbaba09ad92847a0913c0df38d9c05c71`, vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`; source changes were based on `953f90d25f`. B200 and H200 were tested. SM103, SM120 fallback execution, and distributed DeepEP V2 were not tested. Synthetic expert latency is not end-to-end serving throughput. Both clusters' model and benchmark artifacts are preserved under local `repros/block-fp8-padding-20260928/` and `repros/block-fp8-sm90-20260929/`; H200 artifacts are also on Waldorf PVC `synthid-bench-results` under `/block-fp8-sm90-padding-20260929/`.

AI assistance: Codex helped implement, validate, combine, and prepare this change. The human submitter must review every changed line and independently verify relevant tests before merge.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Gather the compressed KV once per KV-source group in prefill
author: gcanlin
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps compressed KV caches only on its kv-source layers (2, 8, 14 and 20 on V4.1-Flash); the other 34 compressed layers read their source's cache. The mega-attention prefill path still dequantized and gathered the whole compressed history in every compressed layer: 38 gathers per step for 4 distinct caches.

This PR gathers each source group's compressed history once per chunk:

- The gathered chunk sits in a retained span at the tail of the shared workspace (new `WorkspaceManager.get_retained`). Scratch requests come from the head, so they leave it alone.
- The span is keyed by source and chunk. A consumer reuses it when `get_retained` reports it intact under that key, and gathers again otherwise. Source layers always gather.
- The sparse indexer now requests its batch's K gather rows instead of the profiled bound. Before, it claimed the whole workspace and broke the span.
- No extra memory: the KV cache is unchanged (66.3 GiB on TP4).

## Test Plan

- TP4: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200, `vllm bench serve` with 128K prefixes plus 2K appends at concurrency 64. Base and PR ran side by side.
- PD: 2P1D on 16× B200 (Dynamo; 2× DEP4 prefill, DEP8 decode), aiperf AgentX trace at concurrency 2048, 30 min measured. Base and PR replay the same trace.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' --max-model-len 1048576
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name custom --dataset-path measure.jsonl --custom-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --temperature 0
aiperf profile --scenario agentx --concurrency 2048 --benchmark-duration 1800 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --url http://<dynamo-frontend>:8100
```
</details>

## Test Results

| setup | metric | base | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| TP4, 128K prefix, C64 | output tok/s | 7,675 | 7,766 (+1.2%) |
| | TTFT mean / p99 (ms) | 1,150 / 3,807 | 956 / 3,696 |
| 2P1D PD, AgentX C2048 | output tok/s per GPU | 3,693 | 3,782 (+2.4%) |
| | prefill computed tok/s | 378K | 397K (+5.0%) |
| | TTFT p50 / p90 (s) | 4.34 / 17.9 | 3.26 / 13.2 |

- In nsys, the gather took 5.8–7.3% of each prefill rank's GPU time. It was also the kernel with the largest spread across DEP ranks (18.6 ms of a 313 ms step), which every MoE barrier then waits on.
- GSM8K exact_match, strict / flexible: 0.7930 / 0.9621.

title: [ROCM][Perf] Add ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN attention-backend works across RDNA3/3.5/4
author: big-yellow-duck
body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` attention backend with segmented Triton attention for paged decode, prefill, and multi-token verification. Startup tuning persists launch choices and shares a Triton cache across target and draft compilation.

- Supports RDNA3, RDNA3.5, and RDNA4 (gfx11/gfx12) with native FP16/BF16 KV; FP8 KV is gated to gfx12.
- Covers head sizes 64, 128, and 256, GQA ratios 1–16, causal and non-causal attention, sliding windows, and attention sinks.
- Includes focused kernel, backend-selection, workspace, tuning-cache, and Triton-cache tests.
- Uses the existing Triton/ROCm stack and adds no package dependency or custom compiler build.
- Startup autotuning is disabled by default to avoid the tuning sweep during engine startup. Set `--kernel-config.enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune=True` to enable it; skipping tuning may reduce serving performance.

## Relationship to existing work

This overlaps with [#55996](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55996), which adds generalized Triton SplitKV paged decode plus an optional RDNA4 FlyDSL path.The overlap is in terms of paged attention optimization. That optional path requires a custom FlyDSL build. `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` uses Triton already in vLLM, with no additional dependency, and covers paged decode, prefill, and multi-token verification across gfx11/gfx12. It also covers D=64, sliding windows, and attention sinks. The serving results below compare against `ROCM_ATTN`; they are not a direct performance comparison with #55996.

## Validation

The three serving comparisons used ROCm 10, the same PyTorch version, and the same GuideLLM 0.7.3 `simple-agent-multiturn-prefix-cache` workload. Each run used eight turns, 2,048 configured prompt tokens per turn, 512 output tokens per request, seed `20260715`, and 1/2/4/8 configured streams with 8/16/32/64 completed requests, respectively. All runs finished with zero errors or incomplete requests.

Each table compares `ROCM_ATTN` (baseline) with `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` (candidate). Values are arithmetic means across successful requests; output tokens/s is **per-request**. These are end-to-end serving measurements, including model execution and scheduling, rather than isolated kernel timings. Hardware, model, and serving options are listed for each comparison.

### gfx1151 serving comparison

On gfx1151, the comparison used `dbirks/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound`.

| 1 | 5.49 → 10.79 | **+96.6%** | 8,424 → 6,878 | **−18.4%** | 102.33 → 47.49 | **−53.6%** |
| 2 | 4.22 → 8.54 | **+102.3%** | 18,215 → 10,549 | **−42.1%** | 135.15 → 60.12 | **−55.5%** |

| 8 | 2.77 → 5.22 | **+88.6%** | 63,995 → 34,987 | **−45.3%** | 218.37 → 105.57 | **−51.7%** |

The per-turn figures show that the segmented backend maintains a flatter per-request output rate as the conversation grows:

![gfx1151 per-turn output tokens per second](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm/d0fb7c78377536f892876303647cfe47de1cb35c/compare_tps_by_turn.png)

![gfx1151 per-turn end-to-end latency](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm/d0fb7c78377536f892876303647cfe47de1cb35c/compare_e2e_by_turn.png)

#### Serving commands

Baseline:

```bash
vllm serve dbirks/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \

### gfx1100 serving comparison

On two Radeon RX 7900 XTX GPUs (`gfx1100`, TP2), the comparison used `dbirks/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound`. Both backends ran the same earlier standalone checkout (`4f20819329`); only the attention backend changed.

## Speculative decoding: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + DFlash2 on gfx1201

Measured on two Radeon AI PRO R9700 GPUs (TP2), using `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` with `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, seven speculative tokens, FP8 KV, and concurrency 4. Both the target and draft use the backend selected for each case:

- **A:** `ROCM_ATTN`.
- **B:** `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN`, autotuning disabled.
- **C:** `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN`, autotuning enabled.

### Accuracy checks first

GSM8K uses the same first 100 test questions and five worked training examples in every case. Sampling follows the model's thinking-mode recommendation: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, min-p 0, presence penalty 0, repetition penalty 1, and default `xhigh` reasoning effort. Each question uses a fixed seed.

| Case | GSM8K correct / 100 |
| --- | ---: |
| A: baseline | 98 |
| B: segmented, static | 98 |
| C: segmented, tuned — pass 1 | 99 |
| C: segmented, tuned — pass 2 | 98 |

A/B miss IDs 12 and 45; C misses ID 12 in pass 1 and IDs 12 and 45 in pass 2. C repeats the same 100 questions, rather than adding 100 new evaluation questions. This is a quick quality check, not a full canonical GSM8K evaluation.

The long-context inputs are **coherent GSM8K worked problems**, followed by a new question; no random-token prompts are used. Actual input lengths are 16,606–16,636 and 32,817–32,847 tokens, with four requests at each length. These speed checks use a **512-token output cap**:

| Input | A correct / 4 | B correct / 4 | C correct / 4, passes 1 / 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16K | 3 | 3 | 3 / 3 |
| 32K | 3 | 3 | 3 / 3 |

The small sample and truncated outputs make the long-context results a serving check, not an accuracy claim.

### A → B: speculative-decoding speed with segmented attention

The backend covers multi-token verification and non-causal draft attention. The PR also reserves attention scratch space before graph capture, initializes draft attention in its own workspace lane, and preserves a shared Triton cache across target/draft compilation.

| Workload | A: baseline output tokens/s | B: segmented static output tokens/s | B / A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, 100 questions | 102.27 | **253.50** | **2.48×** |
| 16K coherent input, 4 requests | 8.20 | **185.47** | **22.62×** |
| 32K coherent input, 4 requests | 4.08 | **131.54** | **32.27×** |

These are **aggregate final output tokens/s**, calculated as returned completion tokens divided by batch wall time, including prefill and scheduling and excluding warmup and draft proposals. They differ from the **per-request** GuideLLM rates in the earlier tables.

Mean acceptance length (`1 + accepted draft tokens / draft rounds`) was approximately **4.05 → 4.05** for GSM8K, **1.04 → 3.92** at 16K, and **1.03 → 3.90** at 32K. The large long-context gains coincide with recovering draft acceptance from near one token per round in A. Both target and draft backends change, so this does not isolate a single kernel or establish the cause of the baseline acceptance collapse. The 22–32× figures describe this specific DFlash2 workload, not a general serving speedup.

### B → C: additional performance with autotuning

The tuner selects launch configurations for the target and draft attention workloads. Updated C uses the original C run's saved **125 target and 42 draft** tuning records, unchanged, with two warmed measured passes.

| Workload | B: static output tokens/s | C: tuned mean output tokens/s | C passes 1 / 2 | Observed C vs B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, 100 questions | 253.50 | **268.79** | 261.97 / 275.62 | **+6.0%** |
| 16K coherent input, 4 requests | 185.47 | **195.80** | 186.04 / 205.56 | **+5.6%** |
| 32K coherent input, 4 requests | 131.54 | **134.64** | 135.35 / 133.94 | **+2.4%** |

C is the arithmetic mean of both batch rates. These results suggest additional serving benefit from autotuning, but **A/B are historical single runs and C uses extended warmup plus prefix-cache resets**. The smaller B/C differences are observed comparisons, not an isolated or statistically established autotuning gain.

### First engine startup cost

Autotuning adds work on the **first startup with an empty matching tuning cache**:

| Configuration | Tuning time | Engine initialization time | Extra initialization vs B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B: autotuning disabled | — | 253.88 s | — |
| C: cold autotuning (separate startup measurement) | 410.02 s target + 88.44 s draft | 750.34 s | **496.46 s (~8.3 min)** |

These are logged engine initialization times (profiling, KV allocation, and model warmup), not full process launch-to-ready times. Matching cached startups loaded all 167 records and tuned zero workloads, avoiding the tuning sweep; model loading, compilation, and graph capture still have their own costs. Cache invalidation can require retuning. Set `--kernel-config.enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune=False` to skip tuning.

### Speculative-decoding serving commands

Run one server at a time on the two-GPU setup above. These commands select the attention backend for **both the target and the DFlash2 draft**, with seven speculative tokens.

**A — baseline (`ROCM_ATTN`):**

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
    --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-num-seqs 4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --load-format safetensors \
    --attention-backend ROCM_ATTN \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"ROCM_ATTN"}'
```

**C — segmented attention with autotuning enabled:**

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
    --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-num-seqs 4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --load-format safetensors \
    --attention-backend ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN \
    --kernel-config.enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune=True \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN"}'
```

For **B — segmented attention without autotuning**, omit the autotuning flag from the second command (the current default is disabled). Python callers enable tuning with `kernel_config={"enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune": True}`. The setting follows the existing FlashInfer autotuning pattern in `KernelConfig` and applies per engine to startup tuning, workspace sizing, and tuned-kernel selection.

The measured runs used cached model snapshots: target `017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a` and draft `50307d4c4cde6860d4eee73e2547cd786fe8e8a4`. title: [Docs] Fix stale W4A16 NVFP4 default kernel in ModelOpt docs
author: WarrierRajeev
body:
## Purpose

The ModelOpt docs say that for `W4A16_NVFP4` checkpoints, `auto` "currently selects Marlin". That isn't what the code does. #53014 added this sentence together with the logic that makes `auto` pick the FlashInfer CuTe-DSL kernel on SM100/SM103, which the `v0.30.0` release notes list under "New defaults".

ModelOpt W4A16 layers go through `select_linear_kernel` → `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel(use_a16=True)`:

```python
elif linear_backend == "auto" and use_a16:
    ...
    # Weight-only: prefer FlashInfer CuTe-DSL W4A16 on SM100/103,
    # otherwise Marlin.
    cutedsl_ok, _ = FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4W4A16LinearKernel.is_supported(
        compute_capability
    )
    if compute_capability in (100, 103) and cutedsl_ok:
        force_kernel = FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4W4A16LinearKernel
    else:
        force_kernel = MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel
```

What changed:

- `docs/features/quantization/modelopt.md`: the paragraph now says `auto` picks CuTe-DSL on SM100/SM103 when FlashInfer's BF16 x FP4 GEMM is available, and Marlin otherwise. It also notes that CuTe-DSL only handles BF16 activations, so FP16 models on SM100/SM103 need `--linear-backend marlin`. The existing sentence about explicitly selecting CuTe-DSL is unchanged.
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py`: fixed the comment in `select_linear_kernel`. It said `use_a16=True` defaults to Marlin and referred to `ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod`, which #49381 removed; it now points to #50273.

Docs and comments only, no functional changes.

I checked the open PRs touching `modelopt.md` or NVFP4 W4A16 selection (#48782, #44672, #55405, #48360); none change this text. 

I used Claude Code to find the mismatch and trace the selection path, and reviewed every changed line myself.

## Test Plan

Docs and a comment only. 
I have run pre-commit on the files and ran:
`grep -rn ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod vllm/`

## Test Result

All pre-commit hooks pass. The `grep` finds no remaining references to `ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod`.

<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Keep the prompt-end prefill checkpoint under sparse retention
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

Mamba prefix caching in align mode with internal prefill checkpoints and sparse retention (`retention_interval == 0`) drops the **prompt-end** checkpoint for most prompts. As a result, the next request that extends the prompt misses the entire prefix.

`MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` (added in #56794) treats a checkpoint as request-local and evicts it when `num_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens`. That is right for mid-prompt chunks. But the hybrid coordinator caches the final chunk only up to its last full block (`_align_cacheable`), so whenever the prompt length is not a multiple of the Mamba block size, the condition also holds on the final chunk. The prompt's own reusable checkpoint is then evicted.

Only a later request that happens to stop a chunk at the shared-prefix junction re-materializes the state. So the first follow-up after every new prompt misses, and in a multi-turn session, where each turn extends a prompt that was prefilled exactly once, **every turn misses**.

The existing test (`test_internal_checkpoint_publication_respects_retention`) does not catch this: it uses `hash_block_size < mamba_block_size`, where the final chunk is cached at full prompt length.

### Fix

Keep the checkpoint when its position is the prompt's own final checkpoint position (`get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(num_prompt_tokens, ...)`). Mid-prompt checkpoints are still evicted as before.

## Test Plan

- New test `test_prompt_end_checkpoint_survives_sparse_retention_with_coarse_hash`:
  - `hash_block_size == mamba_block_size`, a non-aligned 240-token prompt, two chunks;
  - checks that the prompt-end checkpoint is published and that a request extending the prompt hits 224 tokens;
  - fails on main, passes with this change.
- `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache`, `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`.
- End to end on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA with prefill checkpoints, B300), sending a prefix-only prompt, then 3 requests extending it:

| | TP2: hit on the 1st / 2nd follow-up | TP1 ranks (DEP4): hit on the 1st / 2nd follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0 / 193,280 | 0 / 192,000 |
| this PR | 193,280 / 193,280 | 192,000 / 192,000 |

## Test Result

- Unit tests on this branch: 317 passed across the files above, including the new test.
- `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` could not run in this environment: engine init fails in the Qwen3.5 GDN path with an unrelated `chunk_gated_delta_rule(... backend=...)` TypeError from the local library versions.
- Multi-session P/D serving (GLM-5.3-Flash, DEP4 prefill + DEP4 decode), prefill-side prefix hit rate:
  - main: 87.9%, i.e. one full miss per session;
  - this PR: 96.97%, the block-granularity ceiling.
  - TTFT p90 dropped from 16.7 s to 0.76 s.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; every line was reviewed and the tests above were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Make DeepSeek V4 FP8 sparse decode graph-capturable
author: yongqiw-i
body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4-Flash failing to start on XPU with graph capture enabled:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'level_zero backend failed with error: 44 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE)'
```

**Root cause:** `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8` used `.item()` host syncs, data-dependent tensor shapes, and a per-token Python loop. Level Zero graph capture doesn't support any of these.

**Changes:** Rewrite `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8` to use static shapes and vectorized index construction without host syncs, making it graph-capture safe to fix this bug.


## Test Plan

Start a DeepSeek-V4-Flash server on XPU with graph capture. The test cmds are as follows:

```

ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 --enable-expert-parallel  --data-parallel-size 2     -tp=4

title: [Feature] Release the CUDA graph pool on sleep
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

With sleep mode on, CUDA graphs keep their private tensor pools resident after `sleep()` has unmapped weights and KV cache. On large MoE deployments this is GiBs per GPU that sleep cannot release. This PR adds an opt-in, `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` (off by default), that captures CUDA graphs into a dedicated cuMem-backed pool, so sleep releases their physical memory and wake remaps the same virtual addresses. Graphs are not recaptured. With the option off, behaviour is identical to main: plain graph pools, custom allreduce registers graph buffers, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is untouched.

The design follows SGLang's `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH` (off by default; sgl-project/sglang#7873, #32718, #40648); the table below compares the two item by item.

It is based on the graph-pool design from aoshen02/vllm#50 (same author), ported to current main, plus two fixes needed on multi-GPU deployments.

**Based on main, which now includes #59156 and #59158 (both merged)**: per-tag pool lists in `CuMemAllocator.allocator_and_pools`, and the rule that any wake restores every tag other than `weights` and `kv_cache`. With #59158's `runtime` tag, `CuMemBackend.suspend()` offloads `("weights", "runtime", "cudagraph")` at level 1 and `("runtime", "cudagraph")` at level 2.

**Must merge after #59228** (free-while-asleep fix in `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp`). Without it, tearing down a cuMem graph pool while asleep (for example deleting the engine during sleep) double-unmaps it and leaves a sticky CUDA error. The weights and KV pools already have this failure on main; this PR extends it to the graph pool.

### Enabling it

```python
llm = LLM(model, enable_sleep_mode=True, sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph=True)
```

```bash
vllm serve <model> --enable-sleep-mode --sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph
```

`sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` is a `ModelConfig` field next to `enable_sleep_mode` and `sleep_mode_backend` (the name keeps their `sleep_mode_` prefix and says what it does to graphs). It reaches `ModelConfig` through `EngineArgs` like its neighbours, with the CLI flag `--sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph` next to `--enable-sleep-mode`.

The pool is active when the option is on, `enable_sleep_mode` is on, the sleep backend is `cumem`, CUDA graphs are on and the platform is CUDA (`VllmConfig.use_cumem_cudagraph_pool`, the single predicate that the capture routing, `CudaCommunicator` and the NCCL default all read). If the option is on but another requirement is not met, the pool is simply not used and startup logs one warning saying which requirement is missing.

**Benefit when on:** graph memory is released while asleep at both levels (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP: 2.3 GiB/GPU; DeepSeek-V4.1 TP8: 7.43 GiB/GPU; Qwen3-8B TP1: 332 MiB). **Cost when on:** pinned host memory for the pool's backup, also at level 2; about +3 % decode TPOT at concurrency 1 from the custom-allreduce copy (within noise at concurrency 16 and above); 0.05–0.1 s more per sleep.

### SGLang parity

| Item | SGLang | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Switch | env `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH`, default off | config field `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph`, default off |
| Preconditions unmet | pool not used, silently | pool not used; one startup warning naming the missing requirement |
| Graph pool across sleep | backed up and restored (#32718, #40804) | backed up at both levels, restored by any wake |
| `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` | defaulted to `0` when active (#40648) | `setdefault("0")` when active; an explicit value wins with a warning |
| Custom allreduce | unregistered capture (#7873), keyed on the env alone | unregistered only when the pool is active (same predicate) |
| Runners | single runner | Model Runner V2 capture sites; on V1 see the limitation below |
| Recapture | n/a | elastic EP releases the pool before recapture |

### Scope

- Runner-agnostic predicate; the capture sites and tests are those of Model Runner V2, and V1 code is unchanged. Covered capture paths all go through one helper, `use_cudagraph_pool()` in `vllm/compilation/cudagraph_pool.py` (next to the capture sites, which keeps the NCCL `set_graph_pool_id` coupling at the compilation layer). It gets the allocator through `get_mem_allocator_instance()`; the predicate already requires CUDA, so that is `CuMemAllocator` (a narrow cast at the call site rather than new `MemAllocator` protocol methods, which XPU's allocator would not implement):
  - V2 FULL graphs (`CudaGraphManager.capture`, including DBO microbatch capture on the ubatch capture stream);
  - compiled PIECEWISE graphs (`CUDAGraphWrapper`);
  - breakable CUDA graph segments (`BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper`);
  - speculator graphs (autoregressive/EAGLE/MTP, DFlash, DSpark), which subclass `CudaGraphManager` and reuse its `capture()`.
- Memory profiling is deliberately *not* routed through cuMem: V2's `profile_cudagraph_memory()` captures inside `plain_cudagraph_capture()` (a `ContextVar`), so destroying the profiling graphs frees their pool as before.
- **V1 limitation:** with the option on under Model Runner V1, V1's profiling graphs stay in the cuMem pool (awake +326 MiB on Qwen3-8B, +1.6 GiB on DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, not counted in the KV-cache estimate) and V1 DBO microbatch graphs stay in the plain pool; outputs are unaffected.
- Out of scope: encoder CUDA graphs (the encoder runner keeps its own `graph_pool_handle()`), and the Gemma4 centroids graphs in the V1 spec-decode path.

### Design

- **One graph pool, tagged `cudagraph`.** All routed captures share the process's single graph pool, as they share the global graph pool without sleep mode. `CuMemAllocator.use_cudagraph_pool()` creates one pluggable-allocator `MemPool` on the first capture, keeps it as a one-entry `cudagraph` list in `allocator_and_pools`, and yields its id for `torch.cuda.graph(pool=...)` while the allocator tags allocations `cudagraph`. There is no `use_mem_pool` (`capture_begin` routes allocations itself) and no trim loop, so reusing the pool is safe. The module-level `use_cudagraph_pool()` also points NCCL's graph allocator (`set_graph_pool_id`) at whichever pool is used, so the capture sites need no separate call.
- **CPU-backed at level 1 and level 2.** A captured pool is not only scratch activations. It can hold values written once at capture time (constants, persistent kernel or attention state) that replay reads but never rewrites. Discarding the pool corrupts those graphs. SGLang hit this and moved to backing up the graph pool across pause/resume (sgl-project/sglang#32718) and to keeping DSA graph state and the pool intact (sgl-project/sglang#40804). The pool is therefore always backed up to host memory, at level 2 as well. This costs pinned host RAM at level 2 as well: the pool is 2.3 GiB/GPU on DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 and 7.43 GiB/GPU on DeepSeek-V4.1 TP8 (about 60 GiB per 8-GPU node), in addition to the level-1 weight backup. Discarding the pool was also bit-exact on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2 and TP4, full and selective wakes), but it is not safe in general, so the default stays offload.
- **Sleep policy lives in `CuMemBackend`; the allocator is mechanism only.** `suspend()` offloads `cudagraph` at both levels; like every tag other than `weights` and `kv_cache`, it is restored automatically by any wake, selective or not. The RL flow `wake_up(["weights"])` → update → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` has graphs replayable once both are awake.
- **Pool lifetime.** The graph `MemPool` is kept together with its pluggable allocator wrapper and released by `release_pools()` like every other pool. Freeing an allocation while asleep (e.g. a graph pool at teardown) needs no spare VRAM and no Python remap: **this PR depends on #59228**, which makes the C++ `my_free` skip unmapping an allocation that `sleep()` already released and only free its address reservation (ROCm already skipped via an empty chunk list).
- **Recapture (elastic EP).** Elastic EP is the only runtime path that drops and recaptures graphs (on every scale). Each capture runs on a new stream (`graph_capture()`), and the caching allocator reuses a freed block of a live pool only on the stream that freed it, so recapturing into the kept pool grew it: DeepSeek-V2-Lite DP2↔4 with sleep mode went from 586 to 5098 MiB of graph pool on rank 0 over five scale cycles. Elastic EP now calls `release_cudagraph_pool()` (a no-op unless the pool is active) right after `release_graphs()` on the V2 path; the V1 path is as on main. Once no graph uses the pool, it is dropped, its segments are unmapped through the free callback, and the next capture starts a fresh pool. It refuses while the pool is asleep (freeing would unmap a second time) or while something still references it, and the message counts the other references and names the possible holders (live graphs, or a capture-time pool reference taken without a release, as NCCL symmetric memory did). That check found that graph release left the PIECEWISE graphs alive in the compiled model's wrappers until the recompile replaced them; `CudaGraphManager.release_graphs()` now clears them too, as profiling teardown already does. No other runtime path releases or recaptures graphs: LoRA and weight updates replay the existing graphs, and profiling captures into a throwaway plain pool.

### Custom allreduce fix

Custom allreduce IPC-registers the buffers that captured graphs read (`register_graph_buffers`). `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` rejects cuMem memory, so capture fails with `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:164 'invalid argument'` and the worker exits. This was reproduced on GB300 with Qwen3-8B TP4, `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0` and `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"fuse_allreduce_rms":false}}'`.

When the cuMem graph pool is active, custom allreduce captures with `registered=False`: it copies the input into the pre-registered IPC buffer, which is `cudaMalloc` memory. SGLang does the same (sgl-project/sglang#7873), keyed on its env alone; here it follows the same predicate as the pool. `CudaCommunicator` reads `use_cumem_cudagraph_pool` from the current config once at construction (workers build communicators under `set_current_vllm_config`; without a config there is no sleep-mode policy, so graph buffers stay registered) and passes `register_graph_buffers=False` to `CustomAllreduce`, which itself reads no config and does not look at allocator state during capture. Custom all-gather and reduce-scatter always copy into the pre-registered buffer already, so they need no change. The cost is one device-to-device copy per captured allreduce, the same path eager mode uses, and only when the pool is active. Measured on GB300 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP, MTP, sleep mode on and awake): over five server restarts per build (four of them with a warmup), median decode TPOT at concurrency 1 is about +3 % for the whole PR (5.35 vs 5.21 ms) and +3.6 % for a control that only forces the copy (no cuMem pool), so the cost is the copy; the cuMem pool itself adds nothing measurable. Main's own restart-to-restart spread is 2.4 %. `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` alone costs nothing measurable. At concurrency 16 and above the difference is within run-to-run noise. On MI355X (#59523) the same copy costs +3.4 % (vLLM custom allreduce) and +2.7 % (AITER).

### NCCL graph registration

With `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` enabled, NCCL registers graph-captured user buffers and retains their cuMem handles. That pins about 400–510 MiB/GPU through sleep. After wake remaps new physical memory at the same address, NCCL also keeps stale registrations; in SGLang this caused hangs and wrong results (fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver#88, sgl-project/sglang#40648). As in #40648, startup (`VllmConfig.__post_init__`, `_verify_cumem_cudagraph_pool`) sets `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` when the pool is active and it is unset, before any worker or communicator exists (workers inherit the environment; Ray copies `NCCL_*`). An explicit value is kept, with a warning giving the reason. An earlier revision also refused `TORCH_NCCL_USE_TENSOR_REGISTER_ALLOCATOR_HOOK`. On GB300 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP and DP4 + EP, hook=1 with that check removed, `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=REG`), NCCL logged no buffer registration, memory while asleep and after each wake matched hook=0, and outputs matched hook=0, so the check was removed.

### What is not released

Graph executables (`cudaGraphExec_t`) and the driver memory they own are not released. They live outside any PyTorch pool. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash DP4, about 1944 MiB of graph-exec memory plus 1142 MiB charged during capture stay resident per GPU after sleep. Releasing them would require destroying and recapturing graphs, or checkpointing the CUDA process.

### Related work

- #47700 captures CUDA graphs into the `weights` cuMem pool. Graph memory then follows the weights policy: it is discarded at level 2 and restored only with weights. This PR gives graphs their own tag with an always-backup policy, so level-2 sleep and selective wake cannot corrupt captured state. It also covers FULL, compiled PIECEWISE, breakable and speculator capture in both runners.
- #56373 (closed) used CUDA checkpoint of the whole process. That releases everything, including graph executables and the context, but it supports a single GPU only. This PR works with TP/DP and keeps communicators alive, at the cost of the resident graph executables described above.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py -k cudagraph_pool
pytest -v tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py -k cudagraph_pool  # TP=2 case needs 2 GPUs
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py -k cumem_cudagraph_pool
```

- `test_cudagraph_pool_sleep_and_release[sleep-1|sleep-2]` (allocator level): captures are not routed with the policy off or under `plain_cudagraph_capture()`, and are routed with NCCL's graph pool id following the pool. A captured graph that reads a pool-resident constant survives `suspend(level)` → `resume(["kv_cache"])` (which already restores the pool at the same addresses) → `resume(["weights"])` and replays correctly. Release is refused while asleep and while the graph is alive; afterwards the pool is empty and a recapture on a new stream refills it to the same size.
- `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool[...]` (engine level, tiny Llama): for each Model Runner V2 capture site (FULL, PIECEWISE, breakable) graph memory carries the `cudagraph` tag, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` defaults to `0`, and greedy output is exact after level-1 and level-2 selective wakes; on V2, elastic EP's sequence (`release_graphs()`, `release_cudagraph_pool()`, `capture_model()`) empties the pool and refills it to the same size, twice. The TP=2 case forces the legacy custom allreduce. The `off-by-default` case checks that without the option there is no cuMem graph memory and `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is untouched.
- `test_cumem_cudagraph_pool_startup_checks[...]`: active pool → `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0`; an explicit value wins with a warning; not opted in → untouched, no log; opted in but inactive → one warning, env untouched.

## Test Result

| V1 | off | 122379 | 731,296 | 0 | 1741 | 0.8832 / 0.8832 |
| V1 | on | 122705 | 731,296 | 658 MiB | 1411 | 0.8832 / 0.8817 |

- Probe outputs (16 prompts, greedy) after three rounds of full, selective and level-2 wakes are 14–16/16 in all four arms, the same as three awake repeats without sleep (13–15/16 against the first run), so the differences are run-to-run batching variation, not the option.

**Current head (GB300 rack 4, nightly `0cbac6cd1` + #59158 + this PR per file; DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP, MTP, V2):**

---

AI assistance (Codex, Claude Code) was used for the implementation, porting, review and drafting of this PR. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the changes and owns them end to end.

### AMD MI355X (ROCm)

This PR is gated on `current_platform.is_cuda()`, so it is inert on ROCm (verified: memory matches #59156 within 6 MiB). Enabling it on ROCm was tried as a local patch, not included here:
- `is_cuda()` → `is_cuda_alike()` alone fails at the first capture: a blocking `hipMemset` in `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp` makes the legacy stream depend on the capturing stream. Running it as `hipMemsetAsync` on a private non-blocking stream fixes it.

- With that patch, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 stays bit-exact over 10 cycles plus a level-2 reload, but the graph pool is only 72–244 MiB per GPU: most graph memory (0.95–1.7 GiB) is held by the HIP runtime outside torch pools. Unlike CUDA, ROCm returns it when graphs are destroyed, so destroy-and-recapture would be the better option there (9–50 s per wake).

ROCm support is left for a follow-up.

title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Exclude synchronous READ destinations from KV zeroing
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Synchronous MoRIIO RDMA READs can race GPU zeroing of recycled attention pages in hybrid models. Exclude this step's aligned READ destinations in `build_connector_meta()` and explicitly document the limited zeroing-list exception to that hook's read-only contract.

This fix was extracted from #58968. It complements #59504's asynchronous-load handling; neither contains this synchronous MoRIIO protection.

## Claims

- Only fully overwritten hybrid READ attention destinations skip zeroing. Local compute tails, recurrent-state/scratch pages, other requests' pages and later reuse retain zeroing.
- Check READ mode, hybrid state and a nonempty zeroing list once, outside the request loop. No new synchronization or metadata format.
- The base hook permits removal only from `new_block_ids_to_zero`, with completion-before-use and fail-on-load-error obligations. Every other output field remains read-only; scheduler/cache-manager/model-runner/MultiConnector runtime code is unchanged.
- Reuse `test_update_state_drops_decode_recompute_tail_block` and its helpers. Remove the duplicate test from `test_moriio_tp_ack.py` and the obsolete ROCm/MoRI skip around the CPU scheduler suite.

## Validation

**Review revision `a1aef7fe3`:** 16 parameterized boundary cases pass, including no external attention hit, attention-only loads, empty zeroing lists, local tails, other output fields and next-step reuse. The same cases pass against the previous PR method; substituting the unmodified main method produces the expected **2 failed / 14 passed**. Connector regressions: **216 passed / 4 deselected**. Core regression selection: **47 passed / 369 deselected**. Selections overlap. Changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy pass. Four local checks using the real MultiConnector allocation/metadata methods also pass, covering MoRIIO in either position and selected/unselected ownership.

**Completed model evaluation:** [run 37203257111](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/37203257111), integration `34735d677`, achieved **1268/1319 (96.1334%)** for both flexible extract and strict match. This evaluated the previous connector-local implementation (`08469e5c9`) before this minor refactor and documentation update, plus the K3 MLA grouping, atomic TCP-port allocation and discovery-heartbeat prerequisites. It is not a new model run of `a1aef7fe3`.

Configuration: Kimi-K3 + natural DSpark3, P8/D8, TP8/DCP8, eager, MoRI RDMA READ, no LMCache; full GSM8K, five-shot, C64, 4096 generated tokens, no limit. P/D each completed 1319 HTTP 200 requests without evaluator retries; external KV use was confirmed. Natural draft acceptance was **96858/126675 (76.4618%)**, with all three positions positive.

Both workload ranks returned 0, phase tokens matched, both cleanup queries returned 0 and container lists were empty. Slurm nevertheless records **FAILED/1:0**, while the workload records **COMPLETED/0**. Results were timestamped 13:46:18 UTC; prefill shutdown began at 13:46:22 and its output-handler `EngineDeadError` occurred at 13:46:34 during teardown. This discrepancy is retained, not counted as clean scheduler shutdown.

Historical evidence from before the allocation rebase and connector-local revision:

| Version | GSM8K Accuracy — Flexible Extract | GSM8K Accuracy — Strict Match |
|---|---:|---:|
| Main without #59164 | 265/1319 — **20.0910%** | 285/1319 — **21.6073%** |
| with #59164 | 1268/1319 — **96.1334%** | 1268/1319 — **96.1334%** |


<details>
<summary>CPU reproduction commands</summary>

From the candidate checkout with a prepared test virtualenv:

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  -k 'not multi_example_connector_consistency and not fewer_blocks_with_hma and not actual_lmcache and not multi_connector_handle_preemptions_integration and not multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'kv_connector or sync_kv_load or invalid_blocks or prefix_replay or zeroing or external'
```

Model validation ran outside upstream CI on the two-node ROCm runner. The run's matrix artifact records the pinned source and full serving configuration. The boundary test is now collected on CPU without pretending ROCm or MoRI is available.

</details>

## Details

```text
scheduler drains allocation zeroing IDs into a fresh output
  -> connector builds metadata and subtracts full READ destinations
  -> worker zeroes remaining pages and issues READs
  -> existing load barriers wait before the corresponding KV/state is used
```

Hybrid READ metadata already puts the aligned attention group first and excludes local compute tails. The output is built before the metadata hook and dispatched after it; no other connector currently consumes `new_block_ids_to_zero`. MultiConnector passes the same output to its children and gives external tokens only to the selected child. An unselected MoRIIO child has no attention READ destinations to exclude. The exclusion set is local to this call, so later allocations are unaffected.

The interface documentation change is deliberate: the prior unconditional read-only sentence conflicted with this implementation. The exception allows removal of fully overwritten attention blocks only, with load completion before use and step failure on error. Existing hybrid load barriers/failure handling satisfy those obligations. It does not permit changing scheduling counts, block assignments or other fields, or adding pages to the zeroing list.

This change is reversible and its runtime scope remains MoRIIO hybrid READ metadata. READ source ownership and FULL pre-forward context remain separate work.

``` python

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Concurrent traffic driver to force adaptive draft-budget trimming."""
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

PORT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "8002"
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 16
MAXTOK = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 8

URL = f"http://localhost:{PORT}/v1/completions"
PROMPTS = [
    "Explain the theory of relativity in simple terms.",
    "Write a poem about a rainy day in the city.",
    "Summarize the history of the Roman Empire.",
    "Describe how a neural network learns.",
    "List five facts about the human brain.",
    "Tell a short story about a lost dog.",
    "Explain photosynthesis to a child.",
    "What are the causes of climate change?",
    "Describe the water cycle step by step.",
    "Write about the importance of sleep.",
    "Explain how the internet works.",
    "Give a recipe for chocolate chip cookies.",
    "Describe the life cycle of a butterfly.",
    "Explain the stock market in simple words.",
    "Write about the benefits of exercise.",
    "Describe the process of making coffee.",
]


def one(i):
    body = json.dumps({
        "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
        "prompt": PROMPTS[i % len(PROMPTS)],
        "max_tokens": MAXTOK,
        "temperature": 0.7,
        "seed": i,
    }).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
            d = json.load(r)
        return i, d.get("usage", {}).get("completion_tokens"), time.time() - t0
    except Exception as e:
        return i, f"ERR {type(e).__name__}: {e}", time.time() - t0


with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N) as ex:
    for i, ntok, dt in ex.map(one, range(N)):
        print(f"req {i}: tokens={ntok} in {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
print("DONE")
```

  err=$(grep -cE "ERR" /tmp/pr59166/run_$r.log)
  printf "round %s: completed=%s err=%s\n" "$r" "$ok" "$err"
  if grep -qE "illegal memory access|EngineCore failed|CUDA error|Traceback" "$SERVE_LOG"; then
    echo "!!! CRASH at round $r"; crash=1; break
  fi
done
echo "crash=$crash"
curl -s http://localhost:8011/health -w "health %{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null

title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix mamba prefill checkpoint block reservation and prompt-end eviction in align mode
author: kliuae
body:
## Purpose
Enabling Mamba prefill checkpoint in the `align` mamba cache mode allows for the elimination of a second forward pass in prefill when the chunked context lengths are not multiples of the block size. In enabling prefill checkpointing for Kimi-K3 on ROCm (#58344), two issues were found where the scheduler and kv cache manager disagree on the block boundaries, causing wasted allocation and dropped cache that hurt prefix cache hits. This PR extracts the fixes to the core parts that are hardware independent out from the ROCm checkpoint enablement and addresses the following:

### 1. Surplus block reservation
The scheduler determines checkpoint positions from the prefill_end token
```
vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py's _mamba_block_aligned_split
prefill_end = max(request.num_prompt_tokens, request.num_tokens - 1)
...
checkpoint_position = get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(
    prefill_end, self.hash_block_size, drop_eagle_block=self.use_eagle_block_drop,
)
...
use_internal_checkpoint = (...
    and is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid(..., checkpoint_position=checkpoint_position, ...)
)
```
whereas the `MambaManager` uses a prefill chunk's end token `num_tokens`.
```
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's MambaManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate()
checkpoint_position = get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(
    num_tokens, self.block_pool.hash_block_size, self.drop_eagle_checkpoint_block,
)
...
# member methods that call
is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid(..., checkpoint_position=checkpoint_position, ...)
...
```
As the `num_tokens`-derived `checkpoint_position` is always below the end of the prefill chunk, the `query_start < checkpoint_position < query_end` condition in `is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid` is always True for MambaManager, and it allocates an additional block even for chunks that are in the middle of the requests. This makes MambaManager allocate blocks for mid-request chunks that the scheduler never plans as the scheduler only plans for blocks at the prompt-end chunks. These mid-request blocks are immediately discarded as transients, but they still consume and evict physical blocks that have held real prefix. Measured with AgentX workload at concurrency 64, these surplus block reservation can drop cache hit rate from 89% -> 49%.

This PR addresses this by using the same `prefill_end` as the scheduler to evaluate `checkpoint_position` in `MambaManager`, so that `query_start < checkpoint_position < query_end` is True only for the prompt-end chunk and checkpoint blocks are only allocated there where they're only required. This is only changed under `retention_interval == 0` where the surplus checkpoint blocks are truly redundant.

### 2. Dropped prompt-end checkpoint states (Superseded, fixed by #59146)
MambaManager's `_cache_partial_tail_block` decides whether a checkpoint block is mid-request by
```
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block
if (
    retention_interval == 0
    and **num_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens**
    and checkpoint_position != request.shared_prefix_boundary
):
    self.block_pool._maybe_evict_cached_block(checkpoint_block)
    return None
```
where `num_tokens` is rounded down to block size by the HybridKVCacheCoordinator
```
def _align_cacheable(self, num_tokens: int) -> int:
    if self.enable_partial_hash_hits:
        return num_tokens
    return round_down(num_tokens, self.scheduler_block_size)

def cache_blocks(self, request, num_computed_tokens):
    cached_num_computed_tokens = self._align_cacheable(num_computed_tokens)
    ...
```

This makes last chunk of a non-multiple-of-block-size prompt rounded down to below the prompt length, and, under retention_interval=0, its hash is then removed on the same step the kernel writes it. The next conversation turn then cannot find the checkpoint states at the prompt-end boundary, and the reusable prefix becomes the last boundary or to zero, causing prefix to be recomputed.

This PR addresses this issue by adding `_is_reachable_checkpoint` where it decides if a checkpoint belongs to a prompt-end chunk using checkpoint position instead of the rounded-down count.

## Test Plan

New unit tests are added for core partial prefix cache hits:

- `test_intermediate_chunk_checkpoint_reserved_only_under_dense_retention`: prefills a prompt in two chunks and checks that the mid-prompt chunk reserves a checkpoint block only under dense retention while the prompt-end chunk reserves one either way. Fails on main under retention_interval=0.
- `test_prompt_end_checkpoint_survives_block_aligned_cache_count`: prefills a prompt whose length is not a multiple of the block size at the default match unit and checks that the prompt-end checkpoint stays in the prefix cache and that a replay of the same prompt resumes from it. Fails on main for the unaligned lengths.

## Test Result

The added unit tests pass where they fail on main branch.

The performance impact of the two issues were measured together with the ROCm Kimi-K3 mamba checkpoint enablement #58344 on MI355X. In the following benchmarks and evaluations, #58344 only adds the enablement of prefix checkpoint for Kimi-K3 on ROCm, and the pre- and post-fixes for KV cache manager and scheduler are the distinction between the main branch and this PR.

AgentX benchmark runs were performed to reflect agentic workloads with prefix caching, and different conditions were set so that the two issues could surface individually.

The issue 1 "Surplus block reservation"'s cost surfaces under memory pressure when physical blocks holding real prefix caches get evicted to make space for mid-request transient blocks that get discarded immediately. For this, the concurrency=64 AgentX benchmark setting was used.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Skip SWA bounded replay for KV loads that carry the window
author: ivanium
body:
Also credit to @wangyicong52 who originally reported the issue and helped test the PR.

## Purpose

SWA bounded replay (#56227) replays the last window of every prefix hit, including KV loaded by P/D connectors, which transfer the request's own sliding-window KV. P/D decode on DeepSeek-V4.1 therefore recomputed the last 128 prompt tokens of every request. The whole-block rounding that replay applies to external hits also shrinks decode's allocation below what prefill exports, so NIXL's end-aligned pairing puts prefill block k + 1 into decode block k for the MLA groups whenever N % 128 != 0 (found with a CPU probe of the real scheduler and NIXL code).

## Changes

- The scheduler takes a load that restores every replayed group (`get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, added by #59504) as is: no replay, no whole-block rounding, and no dropping of hits no longer than the window. Async loads record the decision at admission and apply it when the KV arrives; failed loads and store / offloading loads still replay.
- Without the replay, decode relies on the transferred window as laid out, so NIXL and Mooncake now back off the last prompt token for models with bounded replay, as they already do for Mamba: prefill stops at N - 1, decode loads N - 1 tokens and computes the last one. Loading all N tokens and rewinding one after laying the window out for N dropped the block holding position N - W when N % block_size == block_size - 1, and the recomputed token attended to the null block, which DeepSeek-V4.1 does not keep zero.

- The prompt cut keeps two prompt-indexed features working (they were already broken for Mamba P/D): a request with prompt logprobs (e.g. completions with echo and logprobs) is not cut, since it skips reading the prefix cache and the decoder never loads its KV; before, the prefiller returned prompt logprobs for one token fewer than the prompt and the frontend failed. The routed-experts (R3) start is clamped to the prompt length; a start equal to the original length lay past the cut prompt and made the scheduler assert.

This PR stands alone. #59330 is the general fix: it applies the backoff to every model (a sliding window has the same rewind problem everywhere, it is only masked by a zero null block) and handles the prompt shapes that only Mamba used to reach (mixed token-id / embeddings prompts, a cut inside a multimodal item, push and Mooncake zero-token loads). DeepSeek-V4.1 is text-only and needs none of those.

## Not a duplicate

#59142 (draft, opt-in, Mooncake only) moves replay to prefill and certifies checkpoints; this PR drops the replay of KV that P/D already transfers, for any connector that declares it, with no new config. #58504 keeps partial external hits exact by retaining the boundary block; loads carrying the window skip the rounding here.

## Test Plan

title: [Model][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support DCP for the kpool sparse indexer
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot run with decode context parallelism. Its kpool sparse indexer compresses the indexer KV (`index_kpool=4`), and the indexer metadata builder rejects DCP whenever `compress_ratio > 1`. This check does not depend on the platform or the attention backend:

```
NotImplementedError: DCP is not supported with sparse indexer KV compression (compress_ratio=4)
```

This PR shards the kpool indexer across DCP ranks by pool:

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` must be a multiple of `index_kpool` (e.g. 4), so each compressed pool lives entirely on one rank. The builder now raises a clear error when this does not hold.
- `CompressedSlotMappingKernel` is DCP-aware. Each rank writes only the compressed states it owns, at rank-local positions. Prefill chunk metadata uses the interleave measured in compressed units.
- Each rank scores its local pools, takes a local top-k, and merges it across ranks with the existing DSA DCP global top-k merge (`_merge_dcp_topk_global`), using the interleave in pool units. The result is global token ids, which the sparse MLA backend already filters and localizes under DCP.
- The CuteDSL DCP merge warmup keys use pool-level top-k and interleave for kpool models.
- The raw kpool tail ring (`KpoolTailSpec`) stays replicated on every DCP rank, like Mamba state. Its pages are self-addressed (`uses_slot_mapping=False`), so `resolve_kv_cache_layout` no longer treats it as a replicated draft group that requires a block-outer layout.
- Unchanged: DeepSeek-V4 compressed KV stays unsupported under DCP, and ROCm kpool raises explicitly.

## Repro

On `main`, this fails at engine startup with the error above. On Blackwell, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` supports DCP; the indexer builder check applies on any platform.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8
```

With this PR, set the interleave to a multiple of `index_kpool`:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4
```

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
    tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

New tests:
- `test_compressed_slot_mapping_dcp_uses_rank_local_state_positions`: each DCP rank writes only its own compressed states, at rank-local slots.
- `test_dcp_replicated_kpool_tail_keeps_block_interior_layout`: a replicated kpool tail does not force a block-outer layout.

E2E: GSM8K (1319 questions) at 5, 25, 50 and 100 shots with `vllm serve` at TP8 + DCP8 + `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`, compared with TP8 alone (bf16 KV, no MTP).

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 309 passed on 1×H100. The 2 failures are `test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_*`, which need more than 1 GPU for their PP config and are unrelated to this change.
- E2E was run on 8×H100 together with a separate local SM90 attention-backend change that Hopper needs for DCP at head_dim 512 (out of scope here). I did not have Blackwell hardware to run this PR on its own.

| Config | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.911 – 0.922 |
| TP8 + DCP8 (interleave 4) | 0.916 |

5-shot GSM8K prompts are shorter than `index_topk` (2048 tokens), so that eval only lightly exercises the cross-rank top-k selection. To cover longer contexts, I raised the shot count. Both configs ran on the same build:

| Shots | Prompt tokens | TP8 | TP8 + DCP8 (interleave 4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | ~650 | 0.916 | 0.913 |
| 25 | ~4.3k | 0.909 | 0.917 |
| 50 | ~8.5k | 0.920 | 0.920 |
| 100 | ~16.9k | 0.926 | 0.922 |

Accuracy matches TP8 at every length, including 100 shots (about 8× `index_topk`). Prefix caching was on, so the shared few-shot prefix is mostly a cache hit, while decode and the question chunks run the top-k selection over the full context.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs and issues for GLM-5.3-Flash / kpool / sparse-indexer DCP and found none that enables DCP for compressed indexer KV. #57161 reworks kpool compression and scheduling but does not touch DCP.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed the changes and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Enable AITER fused shared experts on gfx950
author: jin-amd
body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is silently ignored for GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`): `Glm5NextMoE` builds `FusedMoE` with `n_shared_experts=None`, so each of the 42 MoE layers still runs the shared expert as a separate MLP (two FP8 block-scale GEMMs, a clamped SiLU and a quant) and adds it to the routed output.

This PR wires the flag up the way `DeepseekV2MoE` does:

- **MoE:** when `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert()` allows it, `Glm5NextMoE` drops the separate MLP and passes `n_shared_experts` / `fuse_shared_experts` to `FusedMoE`, so the shared expert runs as one more expert inside the AITER fused MoE (`E=289, topk=9`). The routed weights keep `routed_scaling_factor` and the shared slot gets 1.0, so the output is the same `shared + routed` sum as before.
- **Loading:** in both the target and the MTP draft model, the checkpoint's `mlp.shared_experts.*` tensors (FP8 scales included) load into expert slot `n_routed_experts`. `is_model_fused_shared_expert_compatible()` keeps fusion all-or-nothing, and more than one shared expert raises.
- **Gate:** AITER has tuned configs for the fused shape only on gfx950 at TP4 and TP8 (ROCm/aiter#5735, shipped in AITER v0.1.23, already in vLLM's ROCm image since #58867). Like DeepSeek-V4's shared-expert gate, `_fused_shared_experts_tuned()` allows fusion only there, and only without data, prefill context or expert parallelism, which change the per-rank shape. Anywhere else the flag logs a one-time warning with the reason, and the shared experts stay a separate MLP.

Nothing changes unless the flag is set on gfx950 at TP4 or TP8: it defaults to off, and `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert()` returns False on non-ROCm platforms. gfx942 will follow in a separate PR once its rows (ROCm/aiter#5953) ship; without them the fused MoE would run untuned kernels (4289 µs vs 3033 µs for one 16K-token MoE call on MI325X).

## Test Plan

gfx950 (MI350X), `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` FP8, on the stock ROCm nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0cbac6cd1305f710e12193596b27488397bcb205` (AITER v0.1.23) with no patches besides this PR. Flag-on and flag-off runs use the same image and differ only in the flag. Perf ran as three back-to-back sweeps on the same GPUs (flag on, off, on), with gsm8k after each.

```bash
# Flag off: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0
# MTP runs add: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["all"]}'

for c in 2 4 6 8 10 12 16; do
  vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 \
    --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 20 --num-warmups 2 --max-concurrency $c
done

# lm_eval 0.4.13, all 1319 questions
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,timeout=3600,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=16384

pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py
```

Perf, gsm8k and MTP ran at [10a457c](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/10a457c764afe1274f4b93495d9833a3c73329d1), when the gate checked only the GPU (TP4 passes the full gate too). The gate runs and unit tests ran at [3c2d001](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/3c2d001f37069274f941d8fe4a95e2ff6c5c79e8), which has the same three files as the current head (18fa78d).

## Test Result

With the flag on, TPOT drops 6-9% at concurrency 2-4 and by up to 3% at 6-16, while gsm8k and MTP acceptance are unchanged.

**Perf (TP4).** "on" is the mean of the two flag-on sweeps, which agree within 1.4 points of throughput at every concurrency. TTFT is unchanged within noise: every run is within 3.5% of flag off. No request failed, and every request generated all 1024 output tokens.

| concurrency | output tok/s, off → on | TPOT (ms), off → on |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 101.8 → 106.5 (+4.6%) | 13.06 → 12.28 (-6.0%) |
| 4 | 133.2 → 142.3 (+6.8%) | 19.15 → 17.43 (-9.0%) |

| concurrency | tok/s off | tok/s on (run 1 / run 2) | TPOT off (ms) | TPOT on (run 1 / run 2) | mean TTFT off (s) | mean TTFT on (run 1 / run 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 16 | 180.8 | 185.8 / 185.6 | 49.30 | 47.80 / 47.80 | 31.80 | 31.65 / 31.76 |

</details>

**Accuracy.** gsm8k strict-match / flexible-extract is 0.9757 / 0.9750 with the flag off, and 0.9712 / 0.9704 and 0.9735 / 0.9719 with it on. Each run's standard error is about ±0.0045, so accuracy is unchanged.

**Fused path.** `AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1` shows every fused-MoE lookup is `(E=289, topk=9)` with the flag on and `(E=288, topk=8)` with it off. Flag-on lookups with 4, 8 and 1024-16384 tokens hit the gfx950 rows from ROCm/aiter#5735; the other decode sizes (1-2 and 16-512 tokens) have no tuned row in either arm and use AITER's defaults.

**MTP (k=5).** The draft model's MoE layer is fused too (every lookup in the flag-on run is `E=289, topk=9`), and acceptance from the engine's spec-decode counters over the gsm8k run is unchanged, within 0.006 at every position.

| | flag off | flag on |

title: [CI][Kimi-K3] Test prefix cache reuse with KV offload, P/D and DCP
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 has no end-to-end prefix-cache coverage. FlashKDA exports Mamba prefill checkpoints, a path the Qwen3.5-based `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` never takes, so regressions such as the dropped prompt-end checkpoint fixed by #59146 / #59175 reach users unnoticed. KV offload, P/D and DCP are not tested with K3 at all.

This adds `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py`. It serves [`riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy`](https://huggingface.co/riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy) (the official Kimi-K3 config with 8 layers and no weights) with `--load-format dummy`, and runs 3 turns where each turn extends the previous prompt. Each turn must:

- hit at least the previous prompt's end checkpoint (`cached_tokens`), and
- produce the same greedy tokens as a recompute of the same prompt under a fresh `cache_salt` (`check_logprobs_close`). This catches restored state that is wrong even though the hit count looks right.

With offloading, GPU prefix caches are reset before each turn, so the hit has to come back from CPU.

Every deployment runs in 4 modes:

- `block`: Mamba-block granularity.
- `partial`: `--prefix-match-unit 128`, i.e. partial hits.
- `block-dspark` and `partial-dspark`: the same, plus DSpark speculative decoding as in the recipe. The draft is [`riverclouds/Kimi-K3-DSpark-for-8L-dummy`](https://huggingface.co/riverclouds/Kimi-K3-DSpark-for-8L-dummy), which is `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` with `target_layer_ids` remapped to the 8-layer target and no weights. With EAGLE-style block drop, the expected hit is one unit lower.

| deployment | GPUs |
|---|---|
| plain | 1 |
| SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (config from the [Kimi-K3 recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3?kv_offload=simple)) | 1 |
| DCP2 | 2 |
| DCP2 + SimpleCPUOffloadConnector | 2 |
| P/D (NIXL) TP1 → TP1 | 2 |
| P/D TP2 → DEP2 (decode: DP2 + EP, TP1 per rank; prefix caching on P only, since NIXL rejects it on a hybrid decoder with a different TP) | 4 |
| P/D + SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (MultiConnector) | 2 |

CI: a new `(4xB200) Kimi K3 Prefix Cache Shard %N` step runs the file in 2 shards. It installs NIXL with `.buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh` first, because the CI image does not include it. It is triggered by `vllm/v1/core/`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/`, the NIXL and SimpleCPUOffload connectors, `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/` and `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`. The existing 1xB200 Kimi K3 step ignores this file.

### Known failures (strict xfail)

- `dcp2-*-dspark`, `dcp2-offload-*-dspark`: FlashInfer MLA DCP decode crashes on ragged spec-decode batches (`causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)`). This is fixed by #59392.

### Not covered

P/D + DCP: NIXL with DCP sets `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to the block size (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), but FlashInfer MLA native DCP requires 1, so the server fails to start. A P TP → D DCP case can be added once that is fixed.

### Depends on #59146 or #59175

On current `main`, every block-granularity case fails at turn 1 with `cached=0 expected=17280`, which is the bug those PRs fix. Partial cases pass on `main`. This PR stays a draft until one of them lands.

### Not a duplicate

There are no open PRs adding Kimi-K3 prefix-cache, offload, P/D or DCP tests. #59146 and #59175 fix the scheduler bug and add unit tests only.

## Test Plan

On GB200 (SM100), with #59146 cherry-picked onto main (`379e9a1`):

```
pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py
pre-commit run --files tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py .buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml
```

## Test Result

On main + #59146, one 4xGB200 node. The full run predates two changes: `pd-tp1-tp2` was replaced by `pd-tp2-dep2`, and `pd-dcp2` was dropped. It ran 32 cases: `24 passed, 4 failed, 4 xfailed in 5136.53s (1:25:36)`. The 4 failures are the `dcp2*-dspark` cases, marked xfail after the run started. The 4 xfails were `pd-dcp2`. The `pd-tp2-dep2` cases were run separately on this branch at `c2a0aaa` (merged with main): `4 passed in 1138.28s (0:18:58)`.

| deployment | block | partial | block-dspark | partial-dspark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plain, offload | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| dcp2, dcp2-offload | pass | pass | xfail (#59392) | xfail (#59392) |
| pd, pd-offload | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| pd-tp2-dep2 | pass | pass | pass | pass |

Each case prints its turns. For example, `dcp2-offload-partial`, with GPU prefix caches reset before every turn:

```
turn  prompt  cached  expected  matches_recompute
   0    8869       0         0  True
   1    9646    8832      8832  True
   2   10423    9600      9600  True
```

With DSpark (`pd-offload-partial-dspark`), the expected hit drops by one 128-token unit:

```
turn  prompt  cached  expected  matches_recompute
   0   18469       0         0  True
   1   19246   18304     18304  True
   2   20023   19072     19072  True
```

On main without the fix, `plain-block` fails at turn 1 (`cached=0 expected=17280`) and `plain-partial` passes. Each server start takes about 70–90 s.

With `OffloadingConnector` instead, DCP2 hits CPU only when the prompt-end checkpoint lands on a multiple of the DCP-scaled MLA chunk. That connector is not in the recipe, so it is not covered here.

No model outputs change (test and CI only), so no eval was run.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this test.
