title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Resolve MTP verification rows with a union residency kernel
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Resolve all of a request's MTP verification rows with one union residency kernel, on every sparse MLA backend, and drop the fragile routing that worked around the old kernel.

The old `hisparse_resolve_residency_kernel` ran one block per row, but `device_global_indices` and the LRU are per request, so two rows of one request in one launch could claim the same free slot and read each other's KV. Callers avoided that by resolving verification one step per launch (FlashMLA, FlashInfer TRTLLM) or by treating it as prefill (backends without `hisparse_supports_multi_token_decode`). On FlashAttn sparse MLA a FULL CUDA graph froze that prefill path's residency check at capture, so replays with spilled pages still hit the race. Found via #59036's CI failure (`test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore`).

## Changes

- **Union kernel.** Each request's first-row block resolves all its rows: one hash-table union of host misses, one LRU walk, eviction slots in deterministic (row, top-k) order, one LRU rewrite. Each host row is copied once per request; a reused slot counts as a hit. The table is sized from `max_decode_query_len * index_topk` (~90 KB for GLM-5.3 + MTP3, MTP ≤ 9 at `index_topk=2048`), checked at startup; a union past that bound traps.
- **One routing path.** Verification resolves in one `swap_in` per layer, and `hisparse_supports_multi_token_decode` is removed, so every backend keeps verification as decode. Request ids (with CUDA-graph padding rows masked) live in a group-owned buffer, since the resolver reads them on the copy stream.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_speculative_rows_resolve_host_misses_consistently` (disjoint, overlapping, and multi-pass rows) plus unit tests for hit counting, union-bound sizing, the startup check, spec-as-decode, and padding/request-id handling.
- HiSparse kernel, sparse MLA backend, and e2e tests; #59036 applied on top.
- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 + MTP3 on B200 (FlashInfer TRTLLM, HiSparse under spill pressure), and a layer-level benchmark on H100.

## Test Result

- Race test fails 30/30 on main's kernel and passes with this PR; HiSparse tests pass (H100, H200, B200); `test_hisparse.py` passes, also with #59036.
- GLM-5.3 B200: MTP acceptance in line with main (1.06–1.32 vs 1.19 per window on random prompts); a shrunk GLM-5.3 config matches main's tokens and drafts exactly under FULL graphs.

Decode residency per layer, µs (H100, MTP3, `index_topk=2048`, main → this PR). **Bold** = faster by >5%.

| Mode | Regime | 1 req | 8 reqs | 32 reqs | 64 reqs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph | steady | 155 → **64** | 185 → **87** | 264 → **167** | 373 → **268** |
| | cold | 189 → **129** | 582 → **539** | 2119 → 2174 | 4213 → 4139 |

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the root cause was reproduced and validated on H200, H100, and B200.

title: [CI][ROCm] Drop the duplicate OAI Triton MoE run from FP8 MoE Kernels
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

`kernels/moe/test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py` runs twice in the AMD pipeline, both times on the `mi355_dpx` agent pool:

| Step | Form |
| --- | --- |
| `(MI355 DPX) MoE Kernels Shard %N` | own command, sharded over 5 jobs |
| `(MI355 DPX) FP8 MoE Kernels` | whole file, unsharded |

The sharded run in `MoE Kernels Shard` matches the form the upstream and MI300 steps use, so the copy in `FP8 MoE Kernels` adds no coverage. It just repeats the same 21 tests on the same hardware. The file is also not an FP8 test, so it does not belong in that step.

This removes the duplicate and keeps the sharded run.

The `source_file_dependencies` entry is dropped together with the command, since nothing left in that step reads the file.

## Test

Ran the file in the sharded form the remaining step uses, 5 shards on separate GPUs:  21 passed, 0 failed. 
That is the whole file, so the kept run covers everything the removed one did.

The compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE loader transposed every expert weight on the CPU straight from the safetensors mmap view. title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Warm up top-k/top-p and greedy rejection kernels for speculative decoding
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Purpose

With speculative decoding, Model Runner V2 compiles sampling kernels in the first verification steps instead of at startup, so the first requests stall.

- **Commit 1:** register the native top-k/top-p warmups on CUDA when speculative decoding is configured. #58465 limited them to ROCm, but verification always masks top-k/top-p with these kernels, never with FlashInfer's fused sampler. Target-only CUDA engines are unchanged.
- **Commit 2:** when a rejection sampler exists, run the scheduler warmup a second time with greedy requests. All-greedy batches skip logits processing, so the rejection kernels see BF16 logits, a variant the warmup never compiled. Fixes #54455.

Not a duplicate: #56654 and #58465 removed CUDA sampler registration for its startup cost; this re-enables only what speculative decoding needs. #54630 (open) targets #54455 with mixed warmup configs, but on current main it calls `Sampler.add_request` with the signature from before #56497.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup*.py`, and pre-commit including mypy.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (5 speculative tokens), TP4 on one GB300, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Main, commit 1 and this PR were started interleaved on one node with a fresh Triton cache per start (4 starts each; other caches warm). After `/health`, each server got one streaming request (top-p 0.9 or greedy), then 64 concurrent mixed requests. Compiles were counted with `--jit-monitor-verbose`.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 219 passed, 1 skipped on main and on this PR. pre-commit and mypy pass.

| | main | + commit 1 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| First top-p request, 2nd token | 2.07 / 2.09 s | 0.45 / 0.44 s | 0.43 / 0.45 s |
| First greedy request, 2nd token | 1.58 / 1.50 s | 1.47 / 1.62 s | 0.42 / 0.42 s |
| Compiles in the 64-request burst | 27 | 0–5 | 0 |
| Warmup time¹, cold Triton cache | 37.2 s | 52.9 s | 55.0 s (greedy pass 2.0 s) |
| Warmup time¹, warm Triton cache | 26.6 s | 26.1 s | 27.0 s (greedy pass 1.0 s) |

¹ JIT kernel warmup plus `warmup_kernels`. Commit 1 adds 22.1 s of registry warmup (120 more keys) and saves 6.5 s in `warmup_kernels`, which on main compiled these kernels itself.

TTFT doesn't change (0.40–0.57 s on all builds); the first token comes from prefill. The stall was in the first verification step, before the 2nd token. Greedy outputs are byte-identical across the three builds, and acceptance length is unchanged (2.84).

Limits: target-only batches that can't use the fused sampler still compile on first use, as on main. Seeded requests (#54425) aren't covered. Only tested on GB300 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark; ROCm and pipeline parallelism are untested.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Adopt GPU prefix copies after the hit's allocation
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fix an engine crash (`Cannot get N free blocks from the pool`) on a HiSparse host-prefix hit under GPU memory pressure. This is an alternative to #57457.

Closes #59440.

"Adopting" a GPU copy means a host-prefix hit points its page at a still-valid GPU copy of that host page (a GPU-side prefix-cache hit) instead of reading the page back from host.

A host-prefix hit re-pins free GPU copies of its pages so the prefix comes back GPU-resident. Admission counts those copies as free blocks, but adoption pinned them before the hit's own allocation (hot region and new pages), which could then run the pool dry.

#57457 fixes this by charging the pins at admission. That mixes host and GPU accounting in `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, and under pressure it defers a request that could run by reading its prefix from host, just to keep an optimization.

## Changes

HiSparse-only (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`):

- **Adopt after allocation.** `commit_computed_blocks` records the pages to adopt, and `update_residency` (in `cache_blocks`, after `allocate_new_blocks`) adopts the copies that survived. The allocation always gets what admission counted, so no admission accounting is needed. A copy the allocation reuses is dropped by its reuse watcher and never adopted.
- **Tail first.** HiSparse releases a prefix's pages tail first, matching `free_blocks`' convention, so pressure trims a prefix from its end.

Replaying #57457's scenario (a resumed 3-page host prefix hit, `free_blocks` left in the pool):

| `free_blocks` | main | #57457 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5–6 | rejected | rejected | rejected |
| 7–8 | crash | rejected | admitted, 0/3 copies |
| 9 | crash | rejected | admitted, 1/3 |
| 10 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| 11+ | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |

Near the boundary this keeps fewer copies than #57457, because blocks freed after the copies are queued behind them. #59283, stacked on this PR, is an optional core change that restores 3/3 at 10.

## Test Plan

- `test_hisparse_prefix_hit_under_pressure_adopts_surviving_copies[7, 10]`: exact adopted pages, and no block shared between adopted copies and fresh allocations. `7` fails without the adoption timing, and `10` without tail-first release.
- `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, with `CpuPlatform` selected:

```bash
python cpu_pytest.py --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

## Test Result

- Both new cases fail on main and pass with this PR.
- CPU (`CpuPlatform`): 295 passed. 8 errors are `fixture 'caplog_vllm' not found`, from running outside the top-level conftest, and are identical on main.
- H100, HiSparse unit tests across `tests/v1` (`-k hisparse`): 156 passed.
- H100, `test_prefix_caching.py` + `test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 301 passed. The 2 failures (`test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_*`) need 4 visible GPUs and fail identically on main with 1.
- H100, `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: fails with this PR alone (see the dependency note); with #59235 merged in, 2 passed in each of 2 runs.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, implementation, tests, and this description.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Qualify Transformers backend attention layer names with the model prefix
author: Legend-2727
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59292.

`method="draft_model"` speculative decoding fails at engine start-up when both the target and the drafter run on the Transformers modeling backend. One example is OLMo-2, which has been served through `TransformersForCausalLM` since v0.26.0:

```text
ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn
```

`Base._create_attention_instances` named every attention layer `f"{i}.attn"` and ignored the `prefix` passed to `Base.__init__`. The drafter is built in the same engine with `prefix="draft_model"`, in both the V1 proposer and the model runner V2 speculator. Target and drafter therefore registered the same layer names.

This PR passes the model prefix through and names each layer `maybe_prefix(prefix, f"{attn_prefix}.{VLLM_ATTN_ATTR}")`, where `attn_prefix` is the attention module's qualified name inside the model:

- The drafter's layers now sit under `draft_model.`, so they no longer collide with the target's.
- Layer names follow the module path, which is how native models already name their attention layers. This also changes the names of a model built with an empty prefix, from `0.attn` to the module path.
- The new argument is optional, so direct callers of `Base._create_attention_instances` are unaffected.

**Update after review.** My original commit named the layers `maybe_prefix(model_prefix, f"{i}.attn")`. The review commit 9bef685 by **hmellor** switched to the qualified module name, renamed the loop variable to `attn_prefix` so the parameter can be called `prefix`, and removed a unit test that only restated the naming formula with mocks. The description above reflects the final code.

## Test Plan

- End-to-end (1 GPU): `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_draft_model.py::test_draft_model_transformers_backend`. OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct drafts for itself with greedy sampling, so acceptance should be close to 1.
- The issue's minimal reproduction, on model runner V2 (default) and V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`), before and after the change.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`
- Full CI on the final commit.

## Test Result

**Final commit (`de4e6c4`).** [Buildkite CI #92113](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92113) passed, including the `spec-decode-draft-model` jobs on NVIDIA and AMD.

**Local runs.** These were done on my original commit (`d544cff`), before the review changes. I have not repeated them on the final commit.

Before (`main` at `cb4f016c5`), the minimal reproduction from the issue fails on both model runners:

```text
ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn
```

The new end-to-end test fails the same way (`1 failed … RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`, root cause `Duplicate layer name: 0.attn`).

After:

- Reproduction: the engine starts and generates on model runner V2 (default) and on V1. Greedy output is identical on both: `' Paris, and the largest city in France is Lyon. Lyon is known for its'`.
- A realistic pairing, `OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct` as target with `OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct` as drafter: fails with `Duplicate layer name: 0.attn` before the change; after it, the engine starts and generates.
- End-to-end: `test_draft_model_transformers_backend` gives `1 passed in 200.68s`, with `acceptance_rate=0.99, acceptance_len=3.98` (K=3, so at most 4.0), as expected when a model drafts for itself.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed, including ruff, typos, mypy and the Buildkite test-wiring check.

Environment: NVIDIA RTX 5090, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python-only build (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`). This machine has no CUDA toolkit, so FlashInfer's JIT sampler cannot build here. I ran the V1 reproduction and the end-to-end test with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`; that setting is unrelated to this change.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix MTP acceptance collapse under FULL graphs with a saturated GPU pool
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Purpose

Fixes MTP acceptance collapsing with HiSparse + speculative decoding under FULL CUDA graphs once the HiSparse GPU pool saturates. Two independent causes; both are needed on current main.

**1. Draft rows mirrored before the drafter writes them.** The MTP layers are HiSparse layers too, and HiSparse marks a page clean and releases it for all of its layers, target and draft, at once. Each step does:

```
start_step → target forward → finish_forward → propose (drafter writes its rows)
```

`finish_forward` mirrored *all* layers to host, including draft layers whose rows `propose` had not written yet, and then reported the step's pages clean. The drafter's own per-layer mirror is skipped under FULL graphs, so the fresh draft rows never reached host. When the page's GPU block was reused, the drafter read stale host rows.

**2. The residency resolver can read stale request ids** (regression from #59235). The resolver runs on the HiSparse copy stream, which outside PIECEWISE graphs waits only on `logical_topk_ready`, recorded right after the indexer. #59235 writes the masked request ids later, on the compute stream, so the resolver can read the previous call's ids. The MTP layer alternates four rows per request (draft prefill) with one (draft decode), so stale ids resolve draft rows against other requests' KV.

## Changes

- The speculator tags its draft attention layers (`AttentionLayerBase.is_draft_layer`); HiSparse binding marks their cache handles as draft layers.
- `finish_forward` mirrors only target layers.
- The next step's `start_step` first mirrors the previous step's draft-layer rows (the drafter has run by then), then submits that step's page transfers behind them on the same DMA stream, so a page is only reported clean after its draft rows are queued. They are queued before the step swaps host write events, so the new step's forward and host copies wait for them: by then the scheduler may have handed a finished request's GPU and host blocks to another request. No connector API changes (`wait_for_save` stays a no-op).
- Build the resolver's masked request ids on the copy stream after its wait, into buffers owned by the HiSparse index group (moved from the generic `SparseMLAIndexGroup`); `swap_in` now requires the valid-row count.

**Why not just move `finish_forward` after `propose`?** Outside FULL graphs the drafter re-prepares the draft handles with its own (decode-shaped) metadata, so a combined end-of-step mirror hits HiSparse's metadata consistency checks (`RuntimeError`) for every target/drafter graph-mode mix except FULL/FULL. Target and draft layers need to be mirrored at different points, which requires knowing which layers are draft layers.

**Known limitation (follow-up).** A host block freed after step N (finished or preempted request) can be reallocated to a P/D import before step N's deferred copies land; NIXL writes are not ordered against the copy stream, so an imported request could, rarely, receive stale draft-layer rows (or, with the non-default lazy mirror mode, stale rows for all layers of a preempted request's spilled page). GPU writes and host copy-on-write are ordered: the next step waits for the deferred copies before its forward and host copies. The follow-up holds freed host blocks until the step's deferred writes are reported done.

## Test Plan / Results

**Unit:**
- `test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter[FULL|NONE]` drives the real worker and checks that host draft rows equal the drafter's writes, with exactly one draft-layer copy and the page reported only after it. On main the FULL case fails.
- `test_hisparse_resolver_reads_current_request_ids` (GPU) stalls the compute stream between `logical_topk_ready` and attention, then resolves four rows per request followed by one row per request plus a padding row. It fails on main and passes here.
- H100: `test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or index_group"` 40 passed; HiSparse connector/worker tests pass.
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: the FULL-graph host-mirror check now verifies MTP rows when the next step's start mirrors them (it compared them right after `finish_forward`, before the drafter writes them) and requires the MTP layer to be detected as a draft layer. 4 passed (H100); fails if the speculator stops tagging its layers.

**E2E, cause 1 (on the pre-#59235 base):** H200 2×8, GLM-5.3 TP8/EP8 HiSparse decoder, MTP3, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, NIXL P/D from a PCP8/DCP8 prefiller; Agent X workload at concurrency 48 (HiSparse GPU pool ≥95%).

| | MTP acceptance | per position | output tok/s | ITL p50 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 0.248 | 0.46/0.19/0.09 | 438* | 66.0 ms |
| cause 1 fixed | **0.503** | 0.68/0.48/0.35 | **727.7** | 50.1 ms |
| before, PIECEWISE only (per-layer mirror active) | 0.471 | 0.66/0.45/0.30 | 664.6 | 51.8 ms |

\* includes debug-counter overhead; the pre-fix sweep peaked at ~500 tok/s.

- Host-vs-GPU audit of sealed MTP-layer pages: 98.7% mismatch before, 60.3% after, in line with the target layers' 58.6% (the audit also samples pages that are still being written).
- gsm8k (5-shot, 500) through P/D: 0.928 (0.920–0.936 before).

**E2E, current main:** B300 ×4, GLM-5.3 FP8 TP4, MTP3, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, GPU KV capped at 8 GiB (pool saturated), 40 code prompts × ~16k in / 512 out.

| | acceptance length | output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 1.37 | 113–138 |
| cause 1 fix only | 1.31–1.48 | 123–138 |
| cause 2 fix only | 1.37 | 133 |
| **both (this PR)** | **2.68** | **295** |

title: [Perf][KV Offload] Avoid repeated hash-prefix scans
author: milesial
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Avoid repeated scans of previously processed request hashes when `OffloadingConnector` updates offload keys. Preserve key order, chunk boundaries, and recorded token positions.

## Claims

- Each update reads only the newly selected hashes, instead of traversing the existing prefix again for each cache group.
- Updates with no complete new chunk avoid scanning old hashes.
- The regression test checks incremental updates, incomplete chunks, repeated calls, multiple chunk sizes, key order, and token positions.

## Validation

On macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.13, the five focused tests below passed on this rebased change. All applicable hooks passed.

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python3 -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  --noconftest -q \
  -k 'update_offload_keys_without_scanning_hash_prefix or normal_store_excludes_align_mode_mamba_sources or partial_lookup_returns_exact_boundary_and_group_load_keys or recurrent_group_unhashed_block_does_not_truncate_load_boundary or partial_lookup_requires_every_cache_group'

uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python3 -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

These are CPU tests with mocked scheduler inputs. `--noconftest` excludes unrelated GPU fixtures. Buildkite already includes this test file in the V1 KV Connectors suite.

The regression uses a hash list that rejects iteration but permits indexed access. Restoring the method from main (`8fb16ea5a66f0ef362e728f0ff025f2845927fd5`) in memory makes the test fail. The rebased method passes. This establishes the traversal change without a timing threshold.

End-to-end serving and model evaluation remain pending for this rebased commit. No model, GPU, workload, or serving speedup is claimed. Human review of every changed line and the required serving validation remain pending.

## Details

Without this change, `RequestOffloadState.update_offload_keys()` uses `islice` to skip hashes that already have offload keys. Skipping still consumes the iterator from the beginning. Every call therefore traverses the hash list again, even when the request has no new complete chunk.

This method runs during offload lookup, scheduler updates, and request completion. The repeated CPU work grows with the request hash count and affected requests. It adds work to the scheduler path. The effect on serving latency and throughput is not measured here.

`Request.block_hashes` is a list. Indexed slicing starts at the next unprocessed chunk boundary and selects each chunk's final hash. Key construction and position updates remain unchanged. The temporary list contains only newly selected hashes, at the cost of one short-lived list per group per update.

Open-PR searches for `update_offload_keys` and `offload hash` found no duplicate of this traversal fix. Related #54743 changes which cache groups support offloading. It does not remove this repeated hash-prefix traversal.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Faster Engram host lookups: sorted rows, inline big lookups
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

Speed up DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram lookups from CPU-offloaded tables. On GB200 they are bound by GPU address translation, not bandwidth: each row misses the TLB on the small pages that back the table.

- **Sorted host lookups.** Large lookups from small-page host tables (pinned or `/dev/shm`) sort their rows by table offset, so neighboring rows share page walks. THP tables skip it, and so do lookups below the sort threshold.
- **Inline big lookups.** From the inline threshold (tokens, max over DP ranks), the lookup runs on the main stream at full width instead of the prefetch stream. Persistent main-stream kernels (MegaMoE, mHC, block-scaled GEMMs) cannot co-reside with lookup CTAs, so a background lookup stalls them anyway, and EP collectives then wait on the slowest rank.

`_engram_lookup_thresholds` picks both thresholds per GPU family: 36864 rows and 4096 tokens on Blackwell (measured on GB200). Other GPUs, including ROCm, keep both paths off and behave as before.

All Engram logic now lives in `common/engram.py`, so NVIDIA and AMD share one implementation and `nvidia/engram.py` is removed.

Also fixed along the way:

- DP replicas share the tables only if `/dev/shm` has enough free space (it used to check the total size). The Engram DP leader decides and broadcasts, so replicas always agree, and peers do not hang if the space query raises.
- The lookup kernel no longer ties the output row index to the id dtype, so int64 ids compile.

## Kernel microbenchmark

Kernel only, single GB200 bound to its NUMA node, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash table sizes (24 heads x 16M rows, 94.4 GiB), uniform random ids, CUPTI median of 3 runs rotating 16 id sets. Grid as in production: 76 CTAs below 4096 tokens, 152 from there. HEAD, new unsorted and new sorted outputs are bitwise identical, and from 64 tokens up the new kernel is never more than 1.5% slower than HEAD below the sort threshold.

DEP2/DEP4 (24 heads per rank, `/dev/shm` table shared across DP replicas):

| tokens/rank | before (us) | after (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 90.1 | 88.1 | 1.02x |
| 512 | 620.5 | 620.6 | 1.00x |
| 1024 | 1236.0 | 1237.0 | 1.00x |
| 2048 | 2463.7 | 2163.7 | 1.14x |
| 4096 | 4621.3 | 3773.7 | 1.22x |
| 8192 | 9243.6 | 5925.9 | 1.56x |
| 16384 | 18476.0 | 8174.7 | 2.26x |
| 32768 | 36963.3 | 9905.1 | 3.73x |

TP2/TP4 (per-rank pinned tables):

| tokens | TP2 before (us) | TP2 after (us) | TP4 before (us) | TP4 after (us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1791 | 834 | 440 | 447 |
| 8192 | 3578 | 1846 | 877 | 160 |
| 16384 | 7162 | 3457 | 1745 | 232 |
| 32768 | 14319 | 4291 | 3481 | 396 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual
```

New coverage: the sorted lookup reconstructs the checkpoint under TP padding; a `/dev/shm` that is too small or cannot be queried falls back to sharding, and the leader still broadcasts that decision.

## Test Result

117 passed on 4x GB200. Ruff, format and mypy pass.

## E2E prefill (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB200 node: DeepGEMM mega MoE, FlashMLA mega attention, fp8 KV cache, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, prefix caching off. `vllm bench serve` on random prompts with one output token, so every request is a single prefill. Base (5e887a078b) and this PR ran in the same job on the same node; each point is the median of 3 repeats with unique seeds after a warmup pass. No timed run saw a runtime compile.

| prompt | concurrency | base TTFT p50 (ms) | PR TTFT p50 (ms) | speedup | base tok/s | PR tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4k | 1 | 126 | 128 | 0.99x | 31,961 | 32,060 |
| 8k | 1 | 166 | 160 | 1.04x | 49,498 | 51,176 |
| 16k | 1 | 321 | 295 | 1.09x | 51,265 | 55,732 |
| 32k | 1 | 597 | 548 | 1.09x | 54,845 | 59,752 |
| 4k | 64 | 1059 | 863 | 1.23x | 222,676 | 270,319 |
| 8k | 64 | 2107 | 1721 | 1.22x | 236,670 | 282,490 |
| 16k | 64 | 4239 | 3472 | 1.22x | 236,677 | 283,612 |
| 32k | 64 | 8620 | 7056 | 1.22x | 233,837 | 284,409 |

At concurrency 64 every step prefills the 16384-token budget on all four ranks, so those rows share one step shape and differ in context length; their repeat spread is under 4%. At concurrency 1 the spread is up to 11%. Concurrency 4 and 16 are left out: their TTFT depends on arrival order and repeats spread up to 40%.

Where the time goes at concurrency 64 (estimated from the throughput and the microbenchmark, not profiled): a step takes about 280 ms on base and 230 ms with this PR. Sorting saves about 20 ms of it: each step looks up 16384 tokens x 24 heads in each of the two Engram layers, which drops from 18.5 ms to 8.2 ms per layer. The other ~30 ms comes from running those lookups inline, so they no longer stall the persistent MoE, mHC and GEMM kernels on every rank. At concurrency 1 only one rank is busy and the gain (about 24 ms per 16384-token step) is close to the sorting saving alone.

## Accuracy (DEP4, this PR)

GSM8K: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 4096-token cap, concurrency 32. Strict match 92.49% (flexible 92.49%), no request errors.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for Engram storage and lookup work. #58766 (FP8 rows into `wkv`) edits the same lookup kernel, #58310 (reject tables larger than host memory) adds a host memory check, and #57195 shares host tables across SP ranks. None sorts lookups or runs big lookups inline, but they touch the same files.

title: [Core] Include the LoRA path in prefix-cache block hashes
author: njhill
body:
## Purpose

Prefix-cache block hashes identify a LoRA adapter only by its name. If a name is
re-pointed at a different adapter (unload then load under the same name, or
`load_inplace` with a new path), requests for that name can reuse KV computed with the
previous adapter until those blocks are evicted. See #42125 and #30931.

This adds the adapter path to the LoRA extra key: `("lora", name, path)`.

- Re-pointing a name at an adapter stored elsewhere no longer reuses the old blocks.
- Hashes stay deterministic across instances: no file I/O, no per-process counter.
- Connectors and offload tiers keyed by block hash pick the change up automatically.
- KV events are unchanged: they publish only the LoRA name for this key.

An in-place reload from the same path with changed files still cannot be detected
without hashing the adapter's contents, so that case now logs a warning suggesting a new
path. Content-based versioning (as proposed in #48352) could be added on top of this key
later.

## Why this is not a duplicate

#48352 versions the LoRA key with a digest of the adapter's files. That handles
same-path content changes for local absolute paths, but it adds about 190 lines of file
hashing that runs on the API server's request path. This PR is the minimal,
deterministic fix for re-pointed names and is compatible with #48352 as a follow-up.

## Compatibility

Prefix-cache and external-store hashes change for LoRA blocks, so KV stored by an
earlier version for LoRA requests misses once after upgrade. Instances that serve the
same adapter from different absolute paths no longer share LoRA blocks with each other.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache tests/v1/simple_kv_offload \
  tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/entrypoints/serve/lora \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker/test_sagemaker_lora_adapters.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_lora_resolvers.py
```

## Test Result

- New `test_lora_path_change_changes_block_hashes` fails without the change (2 failed)
  and passes with it.
- On 4x GB200, the command above gives 1013 passed, 8 skipped.
- The KV event tests are unchanged and pass, so the event format is unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Suppress completion for empty pulls
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Purpose

Mooncake can issue a pull with no local destination blocks only to notify the Prefill side that its producer blocks may be released. The Decode request does not wait for remote KV in this case.

`MooncakeConnectorWorker.process_pulling_result` currently reports every successful pull as `finished_recving` after its worker tasks drain. For an empty pull, this sends a completion for a request that is not in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and can trip the scheduler's request ownership/status assertion.

Empty pulls are reachable both during early-abort cleanup and when a remote prefix hit is reduced to no transferable local blocks.

## Change

Report a successful receive completion only when the pull contains at least one local destination block:

```python
if pull_meta.pull_tasks_count == 0 and any(pull_meta.local_block_ids):
    self.finished_recving_reqs.add(pull_meta.d_req_id)
```

The producer notification and pull-task accounting are unchanged. This also matches the existing failed-receive path, which already skips scheduler notification when the pull has no local blocks.

## Relationship to other work

#50565 addresses the early-abort cleanup variant by adding an explicit `notify_scheduler` flag. Its current version intentionally still reports completion for an ordinary empty-block full-prefix pull. That does not cover the case where Decode does not enter `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` after the connector returns no transferable blocks.

This PR applies the check at the worker completion sink, covering both cleanup-only and full-prefix empty pulls while preserving completion for every pull with real local destinations.

## Test Plan

```bash

  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py::test_pull_completion_requires_local_blocks \

  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \

```

- a non-empty pull: normal scheduler completion.

## Test Result

## GPU Validation

title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Support sampling mask replay for MRV2 MTP
author: vx120
body:
## Purpose

Add sampling-mask replay for fixed-boundary speculative decoding in Model Runner V2, on top of the compact sampling-mask representation.

The implementation preserves the ordinary single-token fast path and exact packed-mask fallback, and returns one processed-target support set for each emitted accepted, recovered, or bonus token. Output D2H is scheduled before postprocessing and the next proposal.

## Supported configuration and boundaries

The merged implementation does **not** restrict replay to `method="mtp"` or standard rejection sampling. Configuration tests accept MTP, EAGLE/EAGLE3, dFlash, dSpark and draft_model, and accept standard, block and synthetic rejection configurations. Configuration acceptance is not a claim that every combination has GPU E2E coverage.

title: [Core] Release the FlashInfer allreduce workspace (MNNVL or TRT-LLM) with --enable-nccl-comm-suspend
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Part of #59055 (sleep-mode residual memory).

With `--enable-sleep-mode --enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, `CudaCommunicator.suspend()` only suspends pynccl. The FlashInfer MNNVL allreduce workspace (used by the allreduce+RMSNorm fusion and by standalone FlashInfer allreduce) stays resident while asleep. That is 512 MiB/GPU on DeepSeek-V4 TP4 on GB300.

This PR makes `suspend()`/`resume()` also detach and reattach the group's FlashInfer allreduce workspaces. It reuses the existing `checkpoint_prepare_fi_ar_workspaces` / `checkpoint_restore_fi_ar_workspaces` helpers, which wrap FlashInfer's stable-VA checkpoint API:
- `checkpoint_prepare()` unmaps and releases the physical handles.
- `checkpoint_restore()` recreates them at the same virtual addresses, re-exchanges them over the gloo `cpu_group`, and resets the Lamport flags.
- Because the addresses don't change, captured CUDA graphs stay valid.

Details:
- **Idempotence** comes from FlashInfer 0.7.0: `checkpoint_prepare()` returns early when already detached and `checkpoint_restore()` when already mapped, before any barrier. The executor already blocks a double sleep. There is no extra flag, so if a restore fails (e.g. `cuMemCreate` OOM) a retried `wake_up` retries the restore.
- **Order vs. NCCL** doesn't matter, since FlashInfer synchronizes over gloo. Resume runs in reverse order: pynccl first, then FlashInfer.
- **No workspace** (FlashInfer AR unused): the helper finds nothing and the call is a no-op.
- **Workspaces backed by torch symmetric memory** raise `NotImplementedError` in FlashInfer. The helpers skip them per workspace (`skip_unsupported=True`, set only by `suspend()`/`resume()`), so the other workspace is still released, and log once at info level that the workspace stays resident. The CUDA-checkpoint path (`checkpoint_prepare()`/`checkpoint_restore()`) still raises.
- **FlashInfer all2all** managers also expose `checkpoint_prepare/restore`. They are left out of scope because the default all2all backend doesn't use them.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests in `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py`, with a distinct mock per workspace:
  - `test_cuda_communicator_suspend_detaches_flashinfer_workspaces[mnnvl|symm-mem+mnnvl]`: suspend/resume routing, and a symm-mem workspace next to a normal one (the normal one is still released and restored);
  - `test_cuda_communicator_checkpoint_rejects_symm_mem_workspace`: the CUDA-checkpoint path still raises;
  - `test_cuda_communicator_resume_retries_failed_restore`: a retried resume after a failed restore calls restore again.
- GB300 tests on the `nightly-af7f9488` image with this file overlaid (identical to `d86cf91240` for the touched file).
- Single-node config: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP, MTP n=1, `--enable-sleep-mode --enable-nccl-comm-suspend`. The log shows `FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl`.
- Harness: gated, deterministic batches. It runs 11 rounds of 553 requests (groups 1 to 256, temperature 0) compared bit-exactly: token ids, logprobs and prompt logprobs. Rounds come after a full wake and after a selective wake (`weights`, then `kv_cache`).
- Then 10 level-1 sleep/wake cycles alternating full and selective wake. Each cycle records per-GPU memory while asleep, and bit-exactly checks the first request after wake against the pre-cycle reference.
- 2-node config: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 over 2 nodes, no MTP, same flags.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 18/18 pass (`pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer or symm_mem or restore"`, torch 2.13.0+cu130).
- The GB300 numbers below were measured on the first commit (08b09bf453). The follow-up commit changes only the failure and symm-mem paths; on the MNNVL happy path the same prepare/restore calls run.

Level-1 asleep memory, per GPU (nvidia-smi):

| Config | Without this PR | With this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| V4-Flash TP4, main | 14029 MiB | **13517 MiB** | −512 |
| V4-Flash TP4, stacked with the other sleep PRs of #59055 | 5161 MiB | **4649 MiB** | −512 |
| V4.1-Flash TP8, 2 nodes (all 8 GPUs) | 19885 MiB | **19373 MiB** | −512 |

- **Stability.** Asleep memory is identical across all 10 cycles with no drift, and awake memory is unchanged. There are no errors or tracebacks, and host MemAvailable is flat.
- **Bit-exactness, single node.** All 553/553 requests are bit-identical in every round, after both full and selective wake, both with and without this PR. The first request after every wake matches exactly in 10/10 cycles; that request is the one that exercises the Lamport flag reset.
- **Bit-exactness, 2 nodes.** Upstream V4.1 TP8 is already not bit-reproducible between two *awake* rounds: 84.1% of requests are identical, and some prompt-logprob NaN 400s occur. Both runs show exactly the same 84.1% in every round, before and after sleep, so this PR causes no regression there.
- **Wake latency.** The mean full `wake_up` goes from 1.58 s to 1.64 s on TP4, and from 1.06 s to 1.09 s on TP8 2-node. The cost is re-creating the fabric handles plus a gloo exchange and barrier. Sleep latency is unchanged.

---
AI assistance: this change and its GB300 validation were produced with Claude Code under the author's direction.

### AMD MI355X (ROCm)

ROCm also uses `CudaCommunicator`, so the new calls run there, but they are a no-op: FlashInfer allreduce is unavailable and a probe on every worker found 0 workspaces. Verified on DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 / TP2 eager / DP2 with `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`: memory while asleep matches unpatched within ±20 MiB, outputs are bit-identical after full and selective wake, wake latency is unchanged (0.37–0.42 s), with no errors. Separately, RCCL's comm suspend frees ~0 MiB by default because RCCL does not allocate with cuMem (with `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` it frees 505 MiB, but cuMem adds 389 MiB).

### Re-check on current main, GB300 (single-node groups now use the TRT-LLM workspace)

- Rechecked on main bdd31c31de (clean rebase), GB300, arm64 nightly 18f8f9602 + this PR's 2 files (sha256-gated bind mounts), `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, 3 level-1 cycles:
  - Since #56891, single-node groups use the TRT-LLM workspace and multi-node groups use MNNVL. This PR frees whichever workspace the group has (both implement `checkpoint_prepare/restore` on FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1).

  | Model | Allreduce workspace | Asleep MiB/GPU without → with this PR | Probes after each wake |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, MTP 1 | TRT-LLM (default) | −1030 (the TRT-LLM workspace; measured with the graph pool released, see note) | 28/28 ×3 |
  | DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, MTP 1 | MNNVL (forced) | 9199 → 9139 (−60) | 28/28 ×3 |
  | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 over 2 nodes | MNNVL (default) | 4811 → 4299 (−512) | 28/28 ×3 |

  - Wake time is unchanged within launch noise (V4-Flash ~2.0 s, V4.1 ~1.5 s).
- Unit tests on GB300 (aarch64, CUDA 13.0), rebased on main `bdd31c31d`, run the CI way: `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py` 39/39 in 3/3 runs, including the 4 new workspace tests (main: 35/35). With #59939 also applied, the two suspend/resume calls compose (46/46 in 3/3 runs).
- Note on the TP4 TRT-LLM row: an earlier reading of 10169 → 8687 (−1482) kept the CUDA graph pool resident, whose size varies by ±452 MiB between launches with the FlashInfer MoE tactic. With the pool released, this PR frees 1030 MiB/GPU at TP4 (the TRT-LLM workspace).

title: [Kernel][LoRA] Add deterministic split-K=8 LoRA shrink for batch invariance
author: ShengleiFu
body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the LoRA shrink kernel runs with `SPLIT_K=1`, because split-K normally reduces with float atomics. This PR makes the batch-invariant shrink keep K parallelism without atomics: `_lora_shrink_kernel` stores unscaled FP32 partials for 8 fixed K splits (BLOCK_K=256 for every M) and a small reducer adds them in a fixed order and applies scaling once.

This PR:
- adds a `STORE_PARTIALS` branch to `do_shrink_kernel` / `_lora_shrink_kernel` and a fixed-order reducer, used whenever `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (no new env var);
- allocates the FP32 partials per call with `torch.empty`, so each CUDA graph keeps its scratch in its own pool;
- leaves the non-batch-invariant path unchanged; the split-K path does not use PDL.

Batch-invariant LoRA outputs are still invariant across batch composition, but they change relative to the previous `SPLIT_K=1` path because the reduction order differs.

Not a duplicate: #50278 forces `split_k=1` on the default (non-BI) path; #58533 changes PDL overlap on the dual-stream path.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k batch_invariant` (FP64 reference over K tail / empty split / 3 slices / no-LoRA rows; bitwise-equal target row across M = 31…129)
- `pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k "test_kernels and shrink"` (non-BI path)
- `lm_eval` gsm8k and `vllm bench serve`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, Qwen3-4B + LoRA adapter, requests targeting the adapter, this PR vs main

## Test Result

- `pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k batch_invariant`: 6 passed; `-k "test_kernels and shrink"`: 2136 passed (H100 and B200)
- Raw `lm_eval` and `vllm bench serve` logs (B200 vs main, H100 vs the previous base) are in the comment below.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Return lazily offloaded GPU blocks to the eviction end
author: obendidi
body:
## Purpose

In lazy mode, SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler offloads the cached blocks at the eviction end of the GPU free queue, then releases them with free_blocks, which appends cached blocks as most recently used. The blocks the CPU now holds outlive fresher blocks it doesn't hold, so the allocator evicts those instead. The scan keeps offloading new blocks, and the CPU cache turns over faster than it can serve hits.

* Adds evict_first to BlockPool.free_blocks (off by default) to free cached blocks to the front of the queue.
* Lazy store completion uses it, eager mode and abandoned stores are unchanged.
* Adds test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end, which fails without the fix.

## Test Plan

Regression test fails on `main`

```bash
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -k test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end
```

The bug only affects throughput when the lazy CPU tier is smaller than the GPU KV cache, and the GPU free queue is
much longer than one lazy scan (for example `2 × max_num_batched_tokens` tokens). 

With a small GPU cache, each scan covers the whole free queue, so block order doesn't matter: in a run with a 1,024-block GPU cache on one L4, `main` and this branch served the same CPU hits.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix FlashInfer MLA DCP decode on ragged spec-decode batches
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59065

With DCP > 1 and speculative decoding, FlashInfer MLA decode crashes when the decode batch is ragged, i.e. requests carry different numbers of query tokens. That happens whenever a request has fewer drafts than the others, and also during warmup. For example, Kimi-K3 with `-tp 2 -dcp 2` and DSpark fails at engine startup:

```
ValueError: causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)
```

Here a 1+7 request and a 1-token request make 9 decode tokens.

DCP cannot take the compact ragged path (`cum_seq_lens_q`), because it needs LSE. So ragged batches fall to the "uneven length" branch. That branch has two problems:

- **Shape mismatch.** It splits `q` into one row per token, but it keeps `block_table`, `seq_lens` and `causal_seqlens_kv_global` per request. FlashInfer then rejects the call.
- **Silent wrong reshape.** The branch is only taken when `num_decode_tokens % num_decodes != 0`. A ragged batch whose token count happens to divide evenly (e.g. 8 + 2 tokens) is instead `view`ed as a uniform 5 + 5 batch, and each request's rows attend to the wrong KV.

## Fix

A batch is now treated as ragged when `num_decode_tokens != num_decodes * max_query_len`. Ragged causal batches are split into single-token rows:

- `block_table` and `seq_lens` are expanded per row with the existing `_flattened_decode_metadata`.
- Each row's DCP bound is `T - (tokens of its request after it)`. FlashInfer defines `causal_seqlens_kv_global` as the global exclusive causal bound of each row's newest query token, and `dcp_tot_seq_lens` (`T`) already includes all of the request's query tokens.

The non-DCP causal path is unchanged; it already goes through `cum_seq_lens_q`.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR touches this branch. #56784 edits the same file, but only for backend selection.

## Test Plan

- Kernel check on GB200, run directly against `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` with the cute-dsl backend, `cp_world=2`, both ranks, and `(T, q_len)` in `{(301, 8), (97, 8), (130, 4), (64, 1)}`:
  - One request with `q_len` rows and bound `T` gives bit-identical output and LSE (max error `0.0`) to `q_len` single-token rows bounded at `T - (q_len - 1 - j)`.
  - Negative control: bounding every split row at `T` gives a max output error of `0.26`.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py`: `test_flashinfer_mla_forward_uses_native_dcp_api` is extended with a ragged `(3, 1)` batch. The new `ragged-causal` case fails without this change and passes with it.

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py
```

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py` + `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py`: 23 passed, 1 skipped (GB200).
- Without the source change, only `ragged-causal` fails.
- An end-to-end run with Kimi-K3 was not done here. The `dcp2-*-dspark` cases in #59229 are strict xfails for this bug and will flip once this lands.

No output changes for batches that worked before, so no model eval was run.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Bugfix] Probe the preshuffled FP4 GEMM config by logical K
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`, `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` sends decode-sized MXFP4 linears (M ≤ 64) to AITER's Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle` when `rocm_aiter_ops.is_triton_gemm_afp4wfp4_presh_ws_tuned(N, k_bytes)` reports a tuned config, and to the ASM `gemm_a4w4` otherwise.

The gate checks the wrong file. `k_bytes` is `weight.shape[1]`, i.e. K/2, and the gate probes `GEMM-AFP4WFP4_PRESHUFFLED-N={N}-K={4 * k_bytes}.json`, which is 2K. `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle` itself resolves `N={N}-K={2 * k_bytes}`, the logical K. So the gate asks about a different shape than the one the kernel then runs:

- If the layer's own shape is tuned but 2K is not, the gate says no and the layer falls back to ASM.
- If 2K is tuned but the layer's own shape is not, the gate says yes and the layer runs the Triton kernel on AITER's generic default config.

Of the 25 `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffled` configs AITER ships for gfx950 (ROCm/aiter@89a47b8), 19 are never selected on main. Another 19 shapes are accepted only because a file exists at twice their K:

| | (N, K) |
| --- | --- |
| Tuned, rejected on main | (1280, 8192), (2112, 7168), (2560, 8192), (3072, 1536), (4096, 512), (4096, 14336), (5120, 8192), (7168, 8192), (8192, 8192), (8192, 28672), (10240, 8192), (14336, 8192), (16384, 16384), (16384, 53248), (18432, 16384), (28672, 8192), (36864, 7168), (57344, 8192), (106496, 16384) |
| Untuned, accepted on main | (1280, 4096), (2112, 3584), (2560, 4096), (3072, 768), (4096, 256), (4096, 7168), (5120, 4096), (7168, 4096), (8192, 512), (8192, 1792), (10240, 4096), (14336, 4096), (16384, 8192), (16384, 26624), (18432, 8192), (28672, 4096), (36864, 3584), (57344, 4096), (106496, 8192) |

This PR probes `2 * k_bytes`, the same file the kernel loads.

The existing tuned-shape case in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py`, `(M, N, K) = (32, 8192, 16384)`, only passed because `N=16384-K=16384` exists. It is replaced by `(64, 4096, 8192)` and `(32, 16384, 16384)`, and the test now also asserts that the kernel resolves a tuned config for the shape. `test_aiter_fp4_preshuffled_tuned_gate_uses_logical_k` pins the gate itself: `(N=16384, K=16384)` is tuned and `(N=16384, K=8192)` is not.

---

## Test Plan

- Hardware: 8× MI355X (gfx950)
- Unit tests: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py -k preshuffled`
- Model: `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`. The GDN `in_proj_qkvz` (N=4608, K=8192) and `out_proj` (N=8192, K=2048) linears are quantized online to MXFP4 and served with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`.
- Serving A/B (same image except this change and one AITER config file, see below): random dataset, ISL=8192, OSL=1024, range-ratio=0.8, concurrency `{4, 8, 16, 32, 64}` with 32/64/96/128/256 prompts and one warmup request per concurrency slot
- Accuracy: GSM8K, 1319 problems, 5-shot, thinking off, temperature=0.0, max-tokens=2048. Same servers as the A/B.

The PR arm also carries a gfx950 `GEMM-AFP4WFP4_PRESHUFFLED-N=4608-K=8192.json` from https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5998 tuned for `in_proj_qkvz`. Without this change the file is never read, because the gate probes `N=4608-K=16384`, so `in_proj_qkvz` runs the ASM `gemm_a4w4` in the control either way (confirmed in the control trace below). `out_proj` uses AITER's existing `N=8192-K=2048` file and runs the preshuffled kernel in both arms, only because `N=8192-K=4096` also exists.

---

## Test Result

On one MI355X (gfx950), with AITER 0.1.22.post1. None of the selected tests use the config from ROCm/aiter#5998.

```bash
python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py -k preshuffled
```

This PR:

```text

================ 3 passed, 55 deselected, 14 warnings in 4.73s =================
```

The same tests against main's gate (`4 * k_bytes`) fail wherever a shape's own config exists but its doubled K does not: both failures are `N=16384-K=16384`, where main probes the missing `N=16384-K=32768`. `shape0` (`N=8192-K=4096`) passes on main too, because `N=8192-K=8192` also exists:

### Performance

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Select page-aligned kernel blocks for pooled indexers so the block table addresses storage pages (GLM-5.3-Flash)
author: vllmellm
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58858

GLM-5.3-Flash serving on ROCm silently corrupts its DSA index cache. Root cause: `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` returned `[1, MultipleOf(16)]` on ROCm for every deployment, so `select_common_block_size` keeps the hybrid KV manager block (640/1152/2176/4352 for TP8..TP1) as the kernel block size, while `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` drops the spec's `storage_block_size` which every other consumer (cache views, metadata builders, hisparse) already uses as the kernel block. `Glm5NextIndexerCache` with `index_kpool = 4`, however, stores index-cache entries in pool pages of `page * index_kpool` = 128/256 tokens, and both the writer (`get_compressed_slot_mapping`) and the gather address the block table as `column = pos // storage_block_size`. A manager-granular table therefore skips the builder's conversion branch (`storage % kernel != 0`), indexes far outside the request's row (TP2 @32K: raw table 16 columns wide, 256 needed -> page 0 aliased everywhere), and at TP4 writes past the row buffer entirely.

This is also the root cause behind these issues, #55280, #54359 and #56380.

## Changes

* `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py` - `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` is the point where the cache group's spec (`kv_cache_group.kv_cache_spec`) and the group's backends are both in hand, but `storage_block_size` was dropped before dispatch. It now takes `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size` as the kernel block size if the group's backends support it, otherwise falls back to `select_common_block_size` unchanged. On CUDA the indexer declares an exact `[64]`, so the storage block fails validation there and the conversion path keeps working the same way as today. The support check is the existing `block_size_is_supported` logic moved out of `select_common_block_size` to module level, so both call sites use the same check (exact `==` for `int`, multiple-of for `MultipleOf`).

## Test Plan

Sample command gsm8k + bench:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size {2,4} --max-model-len 262144 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser glm47

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template

vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --host localhost --port 8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 100 --max-concurrency 32
```

> If NIAH config is required, I can add in. 

New tests:

* `tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_indexer_block_sizes.py`: `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` returns the storage block (128/256), not the manager block (640/1152/2176/4352), for the kpool group at every TP floor with the real group backends (indexer + tail + aiter sparse MLA) - fails on main as `[640] == [128]`; plus the fallback, backend rejects the storage block (CUDA-style exact `[64]`) or spec without `storage_block_size` -> `select_common_block_size` as before.


## Test Result

| suite |  main (`713ec07`) | this fix |
|---|---|---|
| NIAH 4096-32000, TP2 | 12/28 | **28/28** |
| NIAH 4096-32000, TP4 | 12/28 | **28/28** |
| NIAH 131072/261632, 3 seeds, TP2 | 3/42 | **32/42** | 
| lm-eval gsm8k 20-shot (1319) | 0.8552 ± 0.0097 | **0.9742 ± 0.0044** |

Benchmark (`random` 1024/1024/100, c32, 4 runs incl. `--no-enable-prefix-caching`):

| branch | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `713ec07` | 1017.8 / 1066.7 | 2035.5 / 2133.4 | 24.58 / 24.71 ms | 
| this PR | 1051.4 / 1033.3 | 2102.8 / 2066.5 | 24.90 / 24.97 ms |

In general no difference between main and this PR.

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py \

test_gpu_model_runner block-size cohort            -> 12 passed
```

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
author: amd-sriram
body:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

On ROCm native decode is used for `next_n` 1 and 2 today, so MTP with one speculative token goes through this path. #59421 raises that cap, which needs this fix.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mqa_context_lens.py` (new): the helper returns the per-sequence lengths for a `(B, next_n)` table and passes `[B]` / `(B, 1)` through unchanged.
- Direct call of `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` on one MI355X against a torch reference: `B=4`, `next_n=3`, contexts 8192/1500/3000/700, block size 64.

## Test Result

| Gluon | Rows correct | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| This PR | 12/12 | max rel diff 2.4e-7 |
| Before | 9/12 | the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row |

With this fix, GLM-5.3 MTP at `next_n=3` and `next_n=5` completes the full throughput sweep, GPQA (0.889 / 0.904) and RULER niah_single_2 (1.0 / 1.0).


| next_n (spec tokens) | GPQA | NIAH | Geomean tok/s/GPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| no MTP | 0.879 | 1.00 | 2435.5 |
| 3 (2) | 0.889 | 1.00 | 3309.1 |
| 5 (4) | 0.904 | 1.00 | 3607.8 |

Throughput per GPU:

| Conc | 8k/1k no MTP | 8k/1k n=3 | 8k/1k n=5 | 60k/600 no MTP | 60k/600 n=3 | 60k/600 n=5 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 544.4 | 1105.3 | 1337.0 | 2925.1 | 4067.3 | 4422.3 |
| 8 | 897.5 | 1650.6 | 2015.3 | 3889.2 | 4658.8 | 4408.6 |
| 16 | 1415.4 | 2177.6 | 2648.5 | 4550.6 | 4948.6 | 5050.4 |
| 32 | 2058.7 | 3061.8 | 3638.4 | 4938.2 | 5175.0 | 5303.4 |
| 64 | 2853.3 | 4013.9 | 4447.8 | | | |
| 128 | 3741.3 | 4715.5 | 4291.3 | | | |
| 256 | 4603.2 | 4663.6 | 5208.6 | | | |

The no-MTP run is the same setup without speculative decoding (decode paged MQA logits on the FlyDSL kernel instead of Gluon).

title: Disable mypy `arg-type` and `assignment` checks in tests
author: hmellor
body:
## Purpose

Tests routinely pass mocks, stubs and `SimpleNamespace` objects where real types are expected. This produced ~400 `# type: ignore[arg-type]` / `# type: ignore[assignment]` comments that add noise without catching real bugs.

This PR:

- Adds a `[[tool.mypy.overrides]]` for `tests.*` that disables `arg-type` and `assignment`.
- Re-enables `method-assign` in that override, since it is a subcode of `assignment` and would otherwise be silently disabled too.
- Removes the now-unused ignores from 130 test files (and any trailing comment that only justified the ignore). Mixed ignores keep their other codes.
- Retargets two `ignore[assignment]` comments in `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py` to `ignore[method-assign]`, as that is the error they were actually suppressing.

The override is in `pyproject.toml`, so it only affects modules under `tests`, regardless of which mypy invocation checks them. Test directories without `__init__.py` still resolve as `tests.*` and are covered.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for mypy/`type: ignore`/`disable_error_code` changes in tests and found none.

## Test Plan

- Probe files in `tests/config`, `tests/lora` and `vllm/` with mypy 1.20.2 (pre-commit's version): both error codes suppressed in `tests/`, still reported in `vllm/`; `method-assign` still reported in `tests/`.
- `python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.10 <changed files>` with the pre-commit dependencies, before and after the change.
- `ruff format` / `ruff check` (0.14.0) on the changed files.

## Test Result

- mypy output before vs after is identical except for the removed `arg-type`/`assignment` errors.
- ruff: all checks pass.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change; I have reviewed it.

title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Keep discovery heartbeats running while workers hold the GIL
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Keep MoRIIO discovery registration alive during worker GIL holds and temporary
router outages. Report unexpected heartbeat subprocess exit through worker
completion polling. This independent fix was extracted from #58968, which no
longer contains the implementation; it has no dependency on the K3 data path.

## Claims

```text
rank-0 worker -> heartbeat subprocess -> unchanged MessagePack registration
  temporary send timeout -> retry until the worker exits
  unexpected child exit -> worker get_finished() raises with its exit code
  worker shutdown / parent pipe EOF -> stop and reap the child
```

## Validation

- **Before:** main's actual threaded sender fails the 300 ms GIL-hold test.
  At pre-review HEAD `512a877511`, the new router-outage test fails to resume
  registration; killing the child or ending its input pipe leaves worker
  completion polling silent (**3 failed**).
- **After:** **46 passed, 0 skipped** across the existing proxy-routing and
  MoRIIO TP-ACK suites. Tests use real subprocesses and loopback ZeroMQ for
  GIL independence, initial registration, router disappearance until the send
  queue times out, registration after the router returns, parent death,
  repeated shutdown, and propagation of both signal and zero-code child exits.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy 3.10, and manual mypy 3.12 passed.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_heartbeat.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_heartbeat.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py
```

Validation covers process and worker lifecycle on CPU. No model-output,
accuracy, throughput, or end-to-end model-serving result is claimed for this
isolated control-plane change.

## Details

The finite retry limit previously treated ZeroMQ send timeouts during temporary
disconnection as terminal. Those timeouts now retry for the worker lifetime;
other repeated ZMQ errors still terminate the child. The parent previously
never inspected child status. It now checks on each worker completion poll,
including unexpected exit code zero. An idle worker observes a fatal child
exit when it next polls; this does not introduce a background restart manager.

**Door:** Two-way. Reverting restores the threaded sender without changing the
discovery wire format. **Blast radius:** MoRIIO workers with a discovery proxy.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, extraction and PR preparation.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Size the KV cache from the groups HiSparse allocates
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

With HiSparse, a GPU pool too small for one `max_model_len` request passes the startup check, and requests then wait forever with no error ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55398#issuecomment-5903470382): `--num-gpu-blocks-override 160`, two 6k prompts never run).

The startup check sized HiSparse from the model's grouped specs rather than the groups HiSparse actually allocates. So it counted only indexer pages, missing the resident and hot groups, and used the wrong block size for the override.

## Changes

- HiSparse's grouping hook now returns the groups it allocates, and workers report its derived resident/hot caches. The standard startup check, override conversion and cross-rank sync then work for HiSparse unchanged.
- KV cache layout resolution skips specs without per-layer views, such as these caches, which lay out their own raw backing.
- Resident groups are sized by their admission window (`max_admission_blocks_per_request`), which #59494 now enforces at runtime.
- Auto-fit uses the startup check's criterion, so it can't pick a length that check rejects.
- Removed the HiSparse-specific memory estimate and the cross-worker `min(available_memory)` workaround.
- Projection returns a group unchanged when all its layers are on the worker, so HiSparse's group flags survive.

A pool that can't hold one request now fails the standard "max seq len" check at startup, before KV cache allocation.

## Test Plan

- Unit test: a 160-block pool is rejected at `max_model_len=8192`, and the boundary is exact at 32768 with 2048 tokens in flight (656 blocks rejected, 657 accepted). Auto-fit with 657 blocks starts. Layout resolution is unaffected by the derived caches.
- B200 (shrunk GLM-5.3, dummy weights), on this branch merged with #59494: TP=1 and TP=2 including ranks with unequal memory, 131k context, auto-fit, the reported setup, and `test_hisparse.py`.

## Test Result

- Unit tests pass.
- B200, this branch (includes #59494):
  - Too-small pools fail at startup: 160 blocks at 8192, 2400 blocks at 131072.
  - Pools that fit serve: 1000 blocks at 8192, auto-fit, and 3200 or 4000 blocks at 131072 with a 120k-token prompt. Without #59494, the 4000-block case livelocks.
  - TP=2 serves, including with unequal ranks.
  - The reported setup at 700 blocks: both 6k prompts complete.
  - `test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed.

title: [Bugfix] Bind routed-experts capture to the MoE layer, not the kernel
author: erictang000
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59449. With `enable_return_routed_experts`, the FLASHINFER_TRTLLM (monolithic) MoE path returns stale `routed_experts` after a layerwise weight reload, which every full-weight RL sync performs.

**Root cause.**
- The capture callback carries a `layer_id`, so it has the lifetime of the layer.
- It was bound to the kernel's `fused_experts` instance, whose lifetime is a single weight version: FP8 `process_weights_after_loading` builds a new kernel on every reload.
- The new kernel has no callback, so the capturer keeps the rows from before the reload.
- The router-side path does not have this bug, because it binds to the router, which lives as long as the layer.

**Fix: give the state to its owner, then pass it explicitly.**
- `RoutedExpertsSink` holds the preallocated int16 replay buffer and the callback. `bind_routed_experts_capturer` creates it once and stores it on the layer as `RoutedExperts.routing_sink`.
- Every quant method's `apply_monolithic` passes `routing_sink=layer.routing_sink`, the same route `e_score_correction_bias` and `expert_map` already take.
- `FusedMoEKernel.apply_monolithic` takes `routing_sink` as a required keyword. A method that forgets it fails mypy (or raises `TypeError` out of tree) instead of silently dropping capture.
- `FusedMoEKernelMonolithicImpl.apply` hands the batch's rows of the sink buffer to the experts as a plain `routing_replay_out` output tensor, then passes the same rows to the sink's callback. FlashInfer already rejects a replay buffer shorter than the batch.
- The experts hold no capture state: `set_capture_fn` and the replay-buffer helpers are removed, so a rebuilt kernel has nothing to lose.
- The buffer address is fixed for the layer's lifetime, so CUDA graphs captured before a reload keep writing to a valid buffer.
- Capability is checked on every call. A reload that switches to a kernel without replay support raises instead of returning stale routing.

**API note.** Out-of-tree code that calls `FusedMoEKernel.apply_monolithic` directly must now pass `routing_sink` (use `None` when not capturing).

## Test Plan

- Unit tests:
  - For the trtllm bf16, fp8 block and nvfp4 kernels, under both Renormalize and DeepSeekV3 routing: the router logits plant an unambiguous top-k, and `routing_replay_out` must report exactly those experts and nothing past the batch.
  - Capture follows each rebuilt kernel through the real `FusedMoEKernelMonolithicImpl`, and a rebuild to an unsupported kernel raises.
  - Binding gives the layer the sink; the sink holds a full DP/EP-gathered batch.
  - Mutation checks: dropping the capture in the impl fails the rebuild test, and dropping `routing_sink=` from any quant method fails mypy (`Missing named argument "routing_sink"`).
- End-to-end state-transition oracle (aoshen02/vllm-state-transition-verifier):
  - Setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 on FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, weights updated over the NCCL weight-transfer engine.
  - Each request is a 1024-token single-forward probe. The run alternates a scored prompt Q with a prime P, so stale capture would return P's routing.
  - Transitions: no update, lifecycle only, identity reload, reload to an expert-relabelled copy σA, and back to A.
  - Every step on A must match the first probe bit for bit.
  - Afterwards, 16 concurrent decodes replay FULL CUDA graphs captured before the reloads.

## Test Result

GB300, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (gac68c3087, digest `b5406fca`), with this PR's files synced in and sha-checked:
- **Unit tests:** 259 passed, 36 skipped across `tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py`, `test_fp8_tp_loading.py`, `test_flashinfer.py` and `test_ocp_mx_moe.py`.
- **mypy:** clean over the whole repository.
- **State-transition oracle** (49,152 routing rows per probe), run on 6995f55, which has the same runtime path (the only later change to it is the required-keyword signature):

| step | nightly | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| no update | identical | identical |
| pause/resume only | identical | identical |
| identity reload | 48,946 rows differ, **all equal to the previous request's routing (stale buffer)** | identical |
| A → σA → A reload | same stale rows | identical |
| decode under FULL CUDA graphs after the reloads | valid | valid |
