title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse main QK-norm/RoPE/gate and KV-cache write into the AMD QSA prepare launch
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the Qwen4Exp QSA layer's main-attention QK-norm, RoPE, gate split and K/V cache write now run inside the fused QSA prepare launch, as #57097 did for NVIDIA.

## Claims

- MI355X TP2 `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`: +0.9% to +2.9% output throughput, faster in all 8 measured cells (4 points × 2 repeats).
- Accuracy neutral: GSM8K 0.9638 → 0.9605 over 6 pairs, a −0.33 point paired difference within run-to-run noise (paired t = −1.8, 5 df).
- Kernel numerics no worse than the unfused AMD chain against an fp64 reference; the gate is bit-identical.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (gfx950): 24 passed, 8 skipped.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py
```

- `test_qsa_prepare_amd.py` (renamed from `test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py`): in all 8 bf16 configurations, the indexer outputs match as before, and the main attention matches the AMD layer's unfused chain (split, Gemma RMSNorm, the layer's `rotary_emb`, `reshape_and_cache_flash`): Q and the paged K/V cache within bf16 tolerance, including MRoPE; the gate bit for bit, in the caller's buffer. The 8 FP8 cases skip: the AMD QSA caches are bf16-only.
- `test_qsa_amd.py`: the fused path passes the real tokens' `qkv`, `slot_mapping`, gate buffer, per-token cache view and norm weights; the unfused path never calls the kernel.
- Runs in the existing AMD `models_basic` step.

**Serving**, MI355X TP2, one-factor A/B against the same image without this change (#57947 in both arms), two repeats with the arms on rotated GPU pairs. `control → candidate`, mean of the repeats:

| ISL | OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Per repeat, tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 4 | 462.0 → 475.5 (+2.9%) | 7.39 → 7.12 (−3.7%) | +1.1% / +4.8% |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 16 | 964.1 → 975.3 (+1.2%) | 13.70 → 13.51 (−1.4%) | +1.4% / +1.0% |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 64 | 1457.2 → 1471.0 (+0.9%) | 35.44 → 35.17 (−0.8%) | +1.4% / +0.5% |
| 60,000 | 600 | 4 | 144.8 → 147.4 (+1.8%) | 14.23 → 13.96 (−1.9%) | +0.8% / +2.7% |

```bash
# plus the checkpoint card's ROCm environment and flags, identical in both arms
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 128
```

**Accuracy**, GSM8K 5-shot on the checkpoint card's recipe (flexible-extract), 6 control/candidate pairs run side by side:

| pair | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| control | 0.9659 | 0.9674 | 0.9629 | 0.9621 | 0.9598 | 0.9644 | 0.9638 |
| candidate | 0.9560 | 0.9606 | 0.9636 | 0.9629 | 0.9553 | 0.9644 | 0.9605 |

One GSM8K run's standard error is about 0.005, so the per-pair differences (−1.0 to +0.1 points) sit within run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Kernel numerics against fp64, 256 tokens at positions up to 200k, Flash-Next per-rank head counts</summary>

| | fused, max / mean abs error | unfused, max / mean abs error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main Q, text RoPE | 0.0296 / 0.00130 | 0.0411 / 0.00139 |
| main K, text RoPE | 0.0259 / 0.00127 | 0.0432 / 0.00134 |
| main Q, MRoPE | 0.0302 / 0.00124 | 0.0302 / 0.00132 |
| main K, MRoPE | 0.0200 / 0.00123 | 0.0287 / 0.00132 |

</details>

## Details

- **Kernel.** `amd/ops/qsa_pre_indexer.py` becomes `amd/ops/qsa_prepare.py`, matching NVIDIA's naming, and takes #57097's main-attention programs unchanged. Its only other difference from NVIDIA's kernel is still #57947's two-masked-load state select.
- **Gate out of the op.** The AMD layer applies the output gate after its opaque QSA op, so the gate has to come out of it. A new `qwen4_exp_qsa_prepare_with_output` custom op takes the packed `qkv` and mutates `output` and `gate`; the wrapper's optional `main_gate_out` writes the gate straight into that buffer.
- **Padding rows.** `* sigmoid(gate)` stays in the compiled graph, where Inductor fuses it as before. NVIDIA's attention kernel gates real tokens only; AMD's graph gates every row, so the op zeroes the gate's cudagraph-padding rows, keeping them at the zero output `forward_qsa` writes. With no padding the fill launches nothing.
- **Eligibility.** On when the layer has an output gate, the indexer passes `supports_fused_pre_indexer`, and the main head dim is a power of two. The main RoPE reads the indexer's cos/sin table, which is the layer's own `rotary_emb`. Otherwise both prepares take the unfused chain, as on NVIDIA.
- **No CPU/GPU sync** on the hot path: eligibility is decided at init; the gate padding size is the static difference between the padded and real token counts.

title: [Perf] Keep non-speculative GDN decode on the standard path
author: DimensionSTP
body:
## Overview

Keep ordinary GDN execution on the existing standard path when speculative decoding is not configured. Addresses #59520 without changing the speculative CUDA kernel or the backend default.

## Claims

- Avoid the packed fused-normalization wrapper when the model cannot produce an MTP batch.
- Preserve the existing fused CUDA path for models configured for speculative decoding.
- Improve measured non-speculative Qwen3.5-9B throughput by 1.31% and 1.47% on two H100s under the two tested prefix-cache policies.

## Validation

Validation uses Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B revision `c202236235762e1c871ad0ccb60c8ee5ba337b9a`, BF16, two H100 GPUs, TP=2, and Model Runner V2. Matched performance runs used main `e5d33a36e`; the final branch was fast-forwarded to `f7999d2e4` and its CUDA suite, CPU controls, and real-model output smoke were revalidated. The affected GDN implementation, kernel, and existing test file are unchanged between these main revisions. After review, the dispatch flag was renamed and the redundant constructor test was removed. The existing CUDA suite and CPU controls were rerun; AST comparison confirms no additional runtime-logic change. The throughput and real-model smoke results below were collected before that rename and were not repeated for this follow-up.

- `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py`: 16 passed, no skips, including the existing MTP, ordinary decode, prefill, and mixed-batch numerical tests.
- CPU metadata and worker controls: 62 passed, 3 CUDA-only tests skipped.
- Real-model greedy comparison: identical token IDs for all eight prompts, including on the final main revision. This is an output smoke comparison, not a benchmark-quality equivalence claim.
- All ten applicable official hooks passed: Ruff check/format, typos, SPDX headers, forbidden imports, Torch CUDA calls, boolean context managers, Buildkite test tethering, and mypy for Python 3.10/3.12. `git diff --check` also passed.

GPU tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py
```

The test file is already covered by the Mamba Kernels CI job. Local execution reused existing native extensions and compiled the unchanged upstream fused GDN source separately with CUDA 12.9 for SM90. This is not a fresh full-project native build. The supplementary registration and experiment tooling are not in this PR.

Each measured arm generated exactly 204,800 output tokens from the same 200 requests. Baseline backend selection used CUDA/Triton/Triton/CUDA ordering for each retention policy; the candidate used the unchanged default CUDA setting with two independent launches per policy. Values below are mean output tokens/s, not total prompt-plus-output tokens/s.

| Prefix-cache retention | Original default | Patched default | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `0` | 1708.92 | 1731.32 | +1.31% |
| `None` | 1889.00 | 1916.75 | +1.47% |

<details>
<summary>Repeated measurements and reproduction</summary>

- Retention `0`: original CUDA 1707.08 / 1710.75; original Triton 1727.51 / 1728.13; patched default 1732.41 / 1730.24.
- Retention `None`: original CUDA 1890.19 / 1887.81; original Triton 1911.11 / 1913.52; patched default 1914.69 / 1918.81.

Run on the original and patched source, substituting `RETENTION` with `0` and `None`:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=cuda \
vllm bench throughput --backend vllm --async-engine \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \
  --revision c202236235762e1c871ad0ccb60c8ee5ba337b9a \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition --num-prompts 200 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 20 \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 32768 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 1024 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 1024 --num-warmups 20 \
  --seed 42 --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --additional-config '{"gdn_prefill_backend":"triton"}' \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --max-num-seqs 20 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-cache-retention-interval RETENTION \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --scheduling-policy fcfs \
  --disable-detokenize --output-json result.json
```

Torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Transformers 5.16.1. Identical supported Triton prefill was selected for every arm because the preserved FlashInfer installation does not accept the newer prefill `backend` argument. The issue's reported 30-35% H200 speedup was not reproduced here; these H100 gains are smaller. Neither cross-hardware equivalence nor broad model-quality equivalence is claimed.

</details>

## Details

The fused CUDA recurrent operator is eligible for speculative/MTP batches. The outer forward path currently selects its packed wrapper solely from the configured CUDA backend, so an ordinary model still takes that wrapper and its fallback normalization even though it cannot use the fused recurrent operator.

Gate that outer selection on the model's existing speculative configuration. The flag is named `enable_fused_gdn_spec_decode` to make its scope explicit. This is a static construction-time decision, not a new per-batch host read or synchronization. Ordinary models retain the existing standard recurrent and normalization path. Models configured for speculation retain their current dispatch, including their prefill and mixed-batch fallbacks.

This differs from #53463, which enables the fused CUDA recurrent operator for ordinary decode with draft width one. It also does not duplicate the FlashInfer decode backend being developed in #41966 or the SM120-specific work in #53645. #51954 removes gate copies within standard decode; this patch changes which outer route an ordinary model selects. No new kernel, hardware-selection heuristic, dependency, or public option is added.

title: [Perf] Enable PDL for fused MoE top-k gating
author: wolfcomos
body:
## Overview The FP32 router GEMM supports programmatic dependent launch (PDL), but fused MoE `topkGating` uses an ordinary launch. Enable PDL for the consumer on SM90+ with CUDA 12+, allowing it to start early and wait before reading producer-dependent data. ## Claims - On GB200, the M=4 MiniMax-M3 router-to-gating CUDA Graph chain saves **0.486 us (-9.12%)** with hot weights and **0.466 us (-7.77%)** with rotating weights. - In ordinary MiniMax-M3 aggregated serving, mean TPOT improves **0.61–1.16%** at request concurrency 1/16/32. All three paired runs improve for both tested input lengths at these concurrencies. C4 is effectively unchanged. - Pure-prefill C16/C32 mean TTFT regresses **0.54%/0.49%**. The results support a modest decode benefit on this setup; broader workload and platform coverage remains open. ## Validation **End-to-end accuracy (`713192bab`):** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, concurrency 8), MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, TP8 on the same 8x GB200 GPUs, with real EAGLE3 verification and three draft tokens. Each variant ran twice without restarting its server. | Strict-match accuracy | Baseline | PDL | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Run 1 | 1247/1319 (94.54%) | 1248/1319 (94.62%) | | Run 2 | 1254/1319 (95.07%) | 1249/1319 (94.69%) | | Mean | 94.81% | 94.66% | Mean change is -0.152 percentage points; baseline repeats differ by 0.531 points. These two repeats per variant do not establish accuracy equivalence. All evaluation requests succeeded. Baseline uses official vLLM v0.29.0; the candidate overlays the pinned PR kernel in the same image, rather than a full PR checkout build. **Serving:** MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, 8x GB200 on two four-GPU nodes, TP8 with expert parallelism disabled, one aggregated worker, FP8 KV/indexer cache, FlashInfer/TRTLLM attention, no prefix caching or speculative decoding. Direct `vllm serve` / `vllm bench serve` uses the same physical GPUs for A/B, three valid pairs per workload, and 64 measured requests per variant per pair. | Request concurrency | TPOT change, ISL/OSL 128/1024 | TPOT change, 8192/1024 | TTFT change, 8192/1 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | -0.61% | -0.63% | +0.89% | | 4 | +0.05% | -0.01% | -0.12% | | 16 | -1.16% | -1.00% | +0.54% | | 32 | -0.93% | -1.09% | +0.49% | Negative latency changes are better. Changes are computed within each pair and then averaged. For 128/1024 C1, mean TPOT is 3.874 → 3.851 ms; individual paired changes range from -0.82% to -0.48%. These finite bursts and three repeats do not establish statistical significance or sustained-load capacity. **Kernel chain:** M=4, H=6144, E=128, top-4 sigmoid; three same-GPU A/B pairs. Hot-weight latency is 5.330 → 4.844 us. Rotating weights use 64 distinct 3 MiB matrices; paired changes range from -8.28% to -6.51%. Each repetition ends with a non-PDL serial boundary to prevent overlap into the next repetition and premature logits-buffer reuse. Its approximately 0.682 us cost is included equally. Latencies are medians across rounds; savings are medians of paired differences. Isolated gating with that boundary saves 0.076 us (-2.16%). **Correctness and integration:** - 866 unchanged upstream fused-top-k and FP32-router tests passed against the pinned runtime with the PDL overlay. - 360 representative original-versus-patched operator cases per process match with zero tolerance: FP32/FP16/BF16, expert counts 6–512, selected index types/top-k values, bias, normalization, padding, ties and nonfinite values. Equal NaNs are accepted; NaN payload-bit identity is not asserted. - 1,200 preallocated-chain and 960 runtime-dispatch changing-input graph checks passed, including poisoned intermediates and the M=32/33 dispatch boundary. - The changed SM100a CUDA translation unit compiled; the original standalone harness passed Compute Sanitizer memcheck with zero errors. - All 74 raw serving measurements completed: 4,736 requests, zero failures. One JIT-contaminated pair is excluded and replaced as described below. - Separate untimed GPU traces confirm PDL gating on all eight TP ranks. Directly adjacent router/gating calls overlap in residence in 6,720/6,720 patched pairs versus 0/6,720 baseline pairs. Residence includes dependency waits; it does not directly measure time saved.
Runtime pins, commands and measurement controls The serving, kernel-chain and correctness/integration results above use vLLM `9ea8f3ffc354901b740f0b31988900897b7221d7`, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and CUDA 13.0. Those measurements used the PR CUDA file on base `d2125ea681784c17251c47939f5ed6d1c67384f8`, before the later guard simplifications. Both controls load identically recompiled original/patched translation units, with library hashes verified on every TP rank. This is not a full current-main rebuild. The upstream tests were copied unchanged from the PR base into that pinned runtime. Equivalent in-checkout commands: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fp32_router_gemm.py -v ``` Example client command; sweep the listed length pairs and C=1/4/16/32: ```bash vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \ --model nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \ --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 64 --num-warmups 8 \ --ignore-eos --seed 1729 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \ --metric-percentiles 50,90,95,99 --save-result --save-detailed ``` Server limits: model length 16384, batched tokens 16384, sequences 32, CUDA Graph capture limit 64, block size 128 and GPU memory utilization 0.9. FlashInfer autotuning and `float32_matmul_precision=high` are enabled. Each variant starts fresh workers and autotuning. Paired variants use the same seed and workload order; the main sequence is A/B, B/A, A/B. Round 0 used eight warmups and exposed attention JIT during measured 8192/1024 C32 requests. That whole pair is excluded. Later pairs use `max(8, 2*C)` warmups; a dedicated same-GPU A/B with verbose JIT monitoring replaces the excluded pair. Neither replacement measurement has observed measured-window JIT. Raw excluded results are retained; each workload has three valid pairs. Capture, JIT/warmup, correctness checks and diagnostic traces are outside timing. Request-level P99 has only 64 samples per run and is descriptive. Eager host-wall results are retained separately from graph GPU timings. The microbench and overlay harnesses are external to this 30-line CUDA diff. ## Details The dependency wait and completion signal precede dependent reads and row-dependent exits. CUDA launches set the PDL attribute without a host architecture query, matching `topk_softplus_sqrt` and `per_token_group_quant`, and check `cudaLaunchKernelEx` errors. Device-side PDL instructions remain guarded by `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900`. Routing math, launch geometry, output layout and the operator API are unchanged. ROCm and the unfused fallback retain their existing paths. Hopper, ROCm and a full current-main build remain unvalidated. For the host-launch cleanup in `09647c0364`, `git diff --check` and `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu` passed. GPU tests were not rerun for this cleanup; the accuracy results above remain pinned to `713192bab`. OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, validation and this description. The submitting author has reviewed the change and approved this draft submission with the validation scope and limitations documented above. ---

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Pair P/D blocks by the last token with different block sizes
author: lucamotz
body:
## Overview

With different P/D block sizes, NIXL pull pairs D's and P's block lists by position, so KV lands in the wrong blocks, or D crashes, when the two lists start or end at different tokens. This pairs them by the request's last token and rejects DCP across different P/D logical block sizes.

## Claims

- With different P/D block sizes, D receives every page into the right block, also after a partial prefix hit on D or sliding-window clipping.
- Equal kernel blocks under different logical block sizes (e.g. FLASHINFER) land in the right blocks too, and D's EngineCore no longer dies on `assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)`.
- DCP across different P/D logical block sizes is rejected at the handshake.
- Pulls between equal P/D block sizes are unchanged.
- Without `remote_num_tokens`, pulls between different P/D block sizes fail instead of pairing by position, with an error logged once per remote engine.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k "hetero_ppl or dcp"
```

`_run_hetero_case` now passes `remote_num_tokens`, the hetero-ppl sweep and `test_hetero_ppl_with_block_size_ratio` gain a pure-MLA row (the latter with a 2-block hit on D), and `test_dcp_rejects_different_logical_block_sizes` covers the DCP guard. `test_hetero_ppl_pull_without_remote_num_tokens_fails` covers the failed pull, and `test_dcp_pull_with_block_size_ratio_writes_stay_within_request_blocks` DCP reads between different kernel block sizes.

CPU, this PR at `4524ec3cdc` on main `8530a778f7`: 44 cases fail without this PR and pass with it. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>CPU output</summary>

```
# main 8530a778f7 + this PR's tests
44 failed, 182 passed, 106 deselected
  34 TOKEN MISALIGNMENT, 8 assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group), 1 DID NOT RAISE NotImplementedError, 1 READ posted without remote_num_tokens
# this PR 4524ec3cdc
226 passed, 106 deselected
```

</details>

GB10 (setup as in #58860): with this PR, every case below gives logprobs bitwise equal to matched-block P/D, and gpt-oss-20b with FLASHINFER, P 64 / D 128, no longer kills D's EngineCore.

<details>
<summary>GB10 runs</summary>

main `8530a778f7`, without and with this PR at `0afbebd9e0`. Identical texts vs the matched-block P/D run on the same image (D's block size on both sides; for TRITON_ATTN, whose prefill tile follows the block size, P's):

| case | without | with, logprobs bitwise equal |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B, FLASH_ATTN, 16/64, 512-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |
| Gemma-4-E2B-it, TRITON_ATTN, 16/64 | 4/7 | 7/7 |
| Gemma-4-E2B-it, 16/64, 512-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN), 544/1088, 1088-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |

gpt-oss-20b, FLASHINFER, P 64 / D 128 kills D's EngineCore on main (`assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)`) and runs with this PR.

</details>

## Details

With different P/D block sizes:

1. P's scheduler returns its block ids and `remote_num_tokens` in `kv_transfer_params`, with the sliding-window blocks that left the window dropped.
2. D's scheduler hands NIXL its block ids past a local prefix hit, window-clipped the same way. The hit and the clipping start the two lists at different tokens, and each side pads to its own logical block past the last token.
3. D's pull pairs each group's block lists by position: `_map_block_ids_for_block_size_ratio` front-clips D's sub-blocks to P's count, then `_apply_prefix_caching` end-trims P to D's count. That holds only if both lists start and end at the same token, which step 2 breaks. Pages then land one or more blocks off.
4. D's receive post-process zeroes the sub-blocks the read did not cover.

Equal kernel blocks under different logical block sizes (e.g. FLASHINFER) shift pages the same way; when D's padded list is longer than P's, D's read fails `assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)` and its EngineCore dies.

This drops each side's padding past the last of the `remote_num_tokens` that P already sends and pairs the lists backwards from there, once per request in `_read_blocks_for_req`. `ReqMeta.covered_sub_blocks` lets the receive post-process zero exactly what P doesn't send: D's padding, and D's leading sub-blocks when D's sliding window starts before P's.

Without `remote_num_tokens`, which a router may not forward, D can't find the last token, so the pull fails. P's block size is only known after the handshake, so the scheduler can't decline the request earlier.

DCP reads keep positional pairing, which needs equal logical block sizes because each side shards tokens at its own. They are mapped to remote-sized sub-blocks in `_read_blocks_for_req` too, so `_read_blocks` no longer maps block ids.

#51527 (draft) lets Mamba hybrids with different logical but equal kernel block sizes use prefix caching, pairing their full-attention groups from new scheduler metadata; it leaves the attention-only end-trim and the `block_size_ratio > 1` pairing fixed here unchanged. #60483 (draft) rejects different P/D DCP sizes when `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` differs from the block size; this PR rejects DCP across different P/D logical block sizes. #60484 rejects DCP peers with different interleave sizes; since NIXL sets the interleave to the block size by default, that overlaps this PR's DCP guard when both sides use DCP.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Reject push handshakes between different P/D block sizes
author: lucamotz
body:
## Overview

NixlPushConnector now rejects P/D peers with different block sizes at the handshake, so their requests fail at once instead of stalling or crashing D.

## Claims

- A P/D pair that differs in kernel block size or kernel blocks per logical block is rejected at the handshake, and D keeps serving.
- Pull and equal-block-size push are unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py
```

`test_push_handshake_rejects_different_block_sizes` covers the new check. Of the two tests of the removed PP-only check, `test_layer_handshake_rejects_unsupported_geometry` keeps only its TP case, and `test_packed_mla_rejects_unequal_block_sizes_before_peer_registration` is removed: the new check does not depend on packed MLA or PP and runs before any registration.

CPU, this PR at `32bad14c7d` on main `8530a778f7`: the new test's 3 cases fail without this PR and pass with it. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

GB10, main `8530a778f7` without and with this PR at `1675f70e48`: both P/D pairs that stall or crash D on main are rejected at D's handshake and D keeps serving; 64/64 push is bitwise equal to main's push.

<details>
<summary>GB10 runs</summary>

Qwen3-0.6B, NixlPushConnector, P and D on one GPU, greedy, `--enforce-eager`, code prompts (2 per rejected pair, 6 for 64/64).

| P / D | backend | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 / 64 | FLASH_ATTN | P's handshake fails with `Local block size 16 is not divisible by remote block size 64 or vice versa.`; both requests still pending at the 150 s client timeout | D's handshake raises `NixlPushConnector requires identical P/D block sizes. Kernel block size and kernel blocks per logical block: local (64, 1), remote engine … (16, 1).`; both requests fail at once |
| 128 / 64, both with 64-token kernel blocks | FLASHINFER | D's EngineCore dies with `IndexError: tuple index out of range` in `get_transfer_results` | rejected the same way (local (64, 1), remote (64, 2)) |
| 64 / 64 | FLASH_ATTN | 6/6 served | 6/6 outputs, logprobs bitwise equal to main's push |

In both rejected cases D's `/health` stays 200 and a direct completion sent to D succeeds.

</details>

## Details

NixlPushConnector cannot convert or re-pair blocks when P and D differ in kernel block size or kernel blocks per logical block, and D registers P for notifications without checking either. On main, for such a pair:

1. D handshakes with P and sends `PUSH_REG` with its block ids.
2. P handshakes with D and WRITEs into those blocks. Depending on the sizes, P's handshake fails or P writes misaligned blocks.
3. D waits for a WRITE that never comes, or its receive fails on the block-size-ratio assert or on empty push block ids.

This PR rejects such peers in `NixlPushConnectorWorker._validate_remote_parallel_config`, which `_nixl_handshake` runs for P's and both of D's handshakes (registration and heartbeat) before registering the peer, so the request fails like any failed handshake. It replaces the PP-only block-size check in `add_remote_agent` and removes push's `block_size_ratio > 1` branch in `_xfer_blocks`, which can no longer run.

No open PR rejects push peers with different block sizes.

title: [Bugfix][Quark] Pass grouped-routing arguments to OCP MX monolithic kernels
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

`QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.apply_monolithic` does not forward `num_expert_group`, `topk_group`, `e_score_correction_bias` or `routed_scaling_factor` to the monolithic kernel, so the kernel falls back to their defaults.

Quark OCP MX picks its experts through `select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, the same path `Mxfp4MoEMethod` uses. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` has forwarded these four arguments since #50000; the Quark copy, added earlier in #38774, was never updated.

**Who is affected.** The bug needs three things at once:

1. A Quark **weight-only MXFP4 (`w_mxfp4`, W4A16)** checkpoint.
2. DeepSeek-V3/V4-style routing (grouped top-k and/or a correction bias with a scaling factor).
3. A **monolithic** MXFP4 kernel. On SM100, the BF16-activation priority list selects `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16` (`TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic`, which supports `DeepSeekV3` routing) by default. On ROCm, `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` (`DeepSeekV3`/`DeepseekV4`) is used when requested explicitly.

In that setup the kernel routes with `n_group=0`, `topk_group=0` and no bias, and the scaling factor is `None` (TRT-LLM) or 1.0 (aiter).

The published Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints are W4A4: `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4`, `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4`, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4` and others. W4A4 resolves to the modular `AiterExperts` on ROCm and to emulation on CUDA, so routing happens in vLLM's router with every argument. As far as I can tell, no public checkpoint hits this today. This PR fixes a latent inconsistency before a W4A16 export does.

This PR forwards the four arguments exactly as `Mxfp4MoEMethod` does. Models without grouped routing pass `None` or the default values and are unaffected.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy).
- Code-path analysis above (`oracle/mxfp4.py` activation filtering and priority lists). There is no public W4A16 Quark checkpoint to run end to end.

## Test Result

`pre-commit` passes. Related: #59757 moves the monolithic kernel call into `FusedMoEMethodBase`, which also removes this inconsistency.

title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add SM121 TP=1 skinny-GEMM plans
author: stecasta
body:
## Overview

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next decode ITL **-9.5% at concurrency 1 on a single DGX Spark (SM121, TP=1)** by adding SM121 skinny-GEMM plans for the TP=1 BF16 shapes, which today fall back to cuBLAS. The LM head `(248320, 2560)` gives most of it (-8.3% alone); the remaining rows add -1.3% on `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, where the router, HC projections and shared-expert gate are BF16 and the other dense projections are MXFP8. On `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` attention, GDN and shared experts are BF16 as well and use the same rows; that checkpoint does not fit a single Spark, so it is not measured end to end.

Complements #59632 (SM121 plans for TP=2 shapes, from #59605): this PR only adds TP=1 keys to the same mechanism. Happy to fold this into #59632 or rebase on it, whichever lands first.

## Claims

- In a c1 decode step (MTP k=3) the LM head runs 4 times: 3 draft steps at M=1 (cuBLAS gemv, 6.8 ms each) and the target verify at M=4 (5.3 ms), 25.7 ms or about 33% of the 77.6 ms step (torch profiler, `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`). Almost all of the end-to-end gain comes from the three M=1 calls (about 2.2 ms saved each).
- cuBLAS reaches about 175 GB/s at M=1 on this shape; the skinny GEMM reaches 253 GB/s: **1.45x at M=1**, 1.04x to 1.08x at M=2 to 16.
- End to end: ITL 25.30 to 22.91 ms (-9.5%), output tokens/s +9.9% at concurrency 1 (mean of two interleaved runs per arm; LM-head rows alone: 23.20 ms, -8.3%); parity at concurrency 8 (its M=32 verify step is outside the skinny GEMM range and stays on cuBLAS).
- GSM8K within run-to-run noise: base 249 / 247, LM-head rows only 245 / 247, full table 246 / 246 of 256 (two runs each; two identical base runs differ by 2).

## Validation

**Kernel**, GB10 (p4242-0063, about 2.5 GHz), FlashInfer CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 30; cosine 1.000000 vs `F.linear` for every config:

| M | cuBLAS (us) | skinny (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 7262 | 5016 | 1.45x |
| 2 | 5217 | 5038 | 1.04x |
| 4 | 5257 | 4917 | 1.07x |
| 8 | 5291 | 4890 | 1.08x |
| 16 | 5336 | 4933 | 1.08x |
| 32 | 5608 | n/a (M <= 16) | |

Other TP=1 shapes, same sweep (selected config vs cuBLAS; cells under 1.03x stay on cuBLAS):

| Shape (N, K) | Layer | M=1 | M=4 | M=8 | M=16 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (1, 2560) | shared-expert gate | 5.58x | 1.91x | 1.47x | 1.07x |
| (96, 2560) | GDN B/A | 1.82x | 5.53x | 4.07x | 1.14x |
| (336, 10240) | HC down/injection | 1.41x | 1.36x | 1.31x | 1.13x |
| (512, 2560) | router | 1.71x | 2.09x | 1.88x | 1.38x |
| (640, 2560) | QSA indexer Q/K | 1.73x | 1.95x | 1.92x | 1.48x |
| (1280, 2560) | shared-expert gate/up | 1.86x | 1.52x | 1.55x | 1.46x |
| (2560, 640) | shared-expert down | 2.01x | 1.74x | 1.72x | 1.34x |
| (2560, 6144) | GDN/QSA output | 1.12x | 1.17x | 1.18x | 1.13x |
| (10240, 320) | HC up | 1.23x | 1.22x | 1.20x | cuBLAS |
| (13312, 2560) | QSA QKV/gate | 1.48x | 1.12x | 1.16x | 1.13x |
| (16384, 2560) | GDN QKVZ | 1.47x | 1.11x | 1.12x | 1.11x |

These are cold-L2 numbers. Weights of 7 MB or less stay in L2 in the server, where an in-server torch profile showed little gain for the HC, router and shared-gate rows; the end-to-end numbers below are the claim.

A bake-off on the LM-head shape (FlashInfer `mm_bf16` cudnn / cublaslt / tinygemm, b12x `bf16_vocab_projection` default config) found nothing faster than the skinny GEMM at M=2 to 16; at M=1 b12x was 4% faster than the skinny config but would need a new dependency.

**End to end**, same node (p4242-0074), `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, TP=1, MTP k=3 with forced acceptance length 3, FP8 KV, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, SPEED-Bench 2K in / 1K out, two interleaved runs per arm, mean:

| Concurrency | Requests | ITL p50 (ms) base / LM head / full | Output tok/s base / LM head / full | TTFT p50 (ms) base / LM head / full |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 8 | 25.30 / 23.20 / 22.91 (-9.5%) | 38.3 / 41.55 / 42.1 (+9.9%) | 891 / 878 / 881 |
| 8 | 16 | 57.92 / 58.05 / 58.17 | 127.7 / 128.0 / 128.3 | 4429 / 4416 / 4430 |

**Accuracy**: GSM8K, first 256 test questions, greedy, thinking off, speculative decoding off, 8 concurrent requests, two runs each: base 249 and 247, LM-head rows only 245 and 247, full table 246 and 246 (of 256). Batch composition varies between runs, so identical configs differ by a few questions.

Disclaimers:
- End to end ran on vLLM `af7f9488c` (the image used for Flash-Next serving) with this PR's table overlaid on `low_latency_gemm.py`.
- Small request counts per cell (8 and 16); baseline repeats on one node agreed within 1.5%.
- `(13312, 2560)` is the unfused QSA QKV/gate shape; after #59533 lands, the fused `(13952, 2560)` key needs a row (sweep data available).
- SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) is not covered: on the 600 W Server Edition the LM head gains only 1.07x to 1.09x, since cuBLAS is already close to that card's bandwidth.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k "qwen4_exp" -v
```

On GB10 (p4242-0070): the Qwen4Exp capability-routing test and the SM121 selected-shape test (cosine > 0.999 vs `F.linear` for every shape and M in the table), run against this branch's `low_latency_gemm.py`: 64 passed. The rest of the file needs GLM-5.2 modules that are not in the Spark serving image.

</details>

## Details

- Same table pattern as SM100/SM90 (#59214): exact capability `(12, 1)`, keyed by the local weight shape, configs selected by a CUDA graph sweep against cuBLAS.
- This PR does not change any other GPU or the selection logic.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the sweep scripts, measurements and this description; the change and the numbers were reviewed by the submitter. Duplicate check: #59632 is the only open SM121 plan PR for Qwen4Exp and covers TP=2 shapes only.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire stale Mamba spec blocks in prefill checkpoint steps
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step. The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path. ## Claims - Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`. - No behavior change without speculative decoding, for `mamba_cache_mode` other than `align`, or for steps without an internal checkpoint. ## Validation Setup: RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on 2 H200 GPUs, served with default settings plus MTP: ``` vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' ``` Reproducer (script below): send a long prompt while another long prompt is still being processed, then send the exact same prompt again. The second request reuses the cached start of the prompt. - Before the fix, the second answer was garbage in 3 of 3 trials, for example `File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4 # File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4 ...`, while the first answer was a normal list of function names. - With the fix, both answers were normal in 3 of 3 trials. Other checks: - A single long prompt sent twice, with nothing else running, also came back broken in 4 of 7 runs at about 25k tokens before the fix, and in 0 of 12 runs after. - In an 8-agent coding-agent run (10 turns, full history resent each turn), 2 agents switched to word salad right after reusing their cached history and stayed broken. With the fix, and with MTP off, no agent broke. - New test `test_mamba_checkpoint_hash_maps_only_to_checkpoint_block` fails on main and passes with the fix. - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache` passes; the GPU part, `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` (`base` and `mtp`), was run on one H200.
repro.py ```python """Reproducer: with MTP on, sending the same long prompt twice can return garbage the second time. Server (any recent main): vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' Run: python repro.py http://localhost:8000/v1 Each trial sends a long prompt while another long prompt is running, then sends the same prompt again. The second answer reuses the cached start of the prompt. Before the fix it is often garbage; after the fix both answers are normal. """ import random import sys import threading from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="none") MODEL = client.models.list().data[0].id WORDS = "alpha beta gamma delta kernel buffer index cache shard block token commit".split() def long_prompt(seed, size): """Made-up Python code of about size characters, different for every seed.""" rng = random.Random(seed) lines = [] while sum(map(len, lines)) < size: lines.append(f"def {rng.choice(WORDS)}_{rng.choice(WORDS)}(x): return {rng.randrange(10**6)} " f"# {' '.join(rng.choices(WORDS, k=8))}\n") return "Here is a file:\n" + "".join(lines) + "\nList the first five function names, then summarize the file." def ask(prompt, max_tokens): out = client.chat.completions.create( model=MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], max_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0, extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "low"}}) # GLM-5.3: short thinking msg = out.choices[0].message thinking = getattr(msg, "reasoning", None) or getattr(msg, "reasoning_content", None) or "" return (thinking + (msg.content or "")).replace("\n", " ") def run_together(prompts, max_tokens): threads = [threading.Thread(target=ask, args=(p, max_tokens)) for p in prompts] for t in threads: t.start() for t in threads: t.join() # Whether a prompt is affected depends on its exact length; these lengths trigger it. for trial, size in enumerate([60000, 60000, 60000]): # Keep the server busy for a moment, as it would be in production. run_together([long_prompt(1000 + 10 * trial + k, 90000) for k in range(6)], 64) # A long request is running while the target prompt is processed for the first time. background = threading.Thread(target=ask, args=(long_prompt(10 * trial + 1, size), 300)) background.start() threading.Event().wait(0.3) target = long_prompt(10 * trial + 2, size) first = ask(target, 60) background.join() # The exact same request again. second = ask(target, 60) print(f"trial {trial}") print(f" first: {first[:100]}") print(f" second: {second[:100]}") ``` Example output on main (before the fix): ``` trial 0 first: **First five function names:** 1. `alpha_beta` 2. `index_token` 3. `buffer_cache` 4. `gamma_shard` 5 second: List the first five function names, then summarize the file. ## Details In align mode a request keeps its running state in the block after the last computed one, followed by `num_speculative_blocks` scratch blocks. A normal `allocate_new_blocks` call moves the old scratch blocks that fall below the new running state to the end of the table and nulls their slots. In a checkpoint step this was skipped (`if blocks_allocated and not checkpoint_block`). With MTP, the checkpoint position P is shifted one block down. When one of the previous step's scratch blocks sits at index `P // block_size - 1` (with k=1: the chunk starts one block below P), it occupies the natural slot of P. The checkpoint itself is written into a new block at `cdiv(end, block_size) - 2`, one index above it. In the same step, `cache_full_blocks` registers the unwritten scratch block under hash(P), and `_cache_partial_tail_block` then adds the real checkpoint block under the same hash. `get_one_block` returns the first block registered, so later hits at P resume from the scratch page. The entry stays until eviction, so every request that shares this prefix is affected. It happens when a prompt's final prefill chunk starts one block below the shifted checkpoint, so it depends on prompt length and on how much of each step's token budget other requests use. Overlapping long prompts make it much more likely. For example, with a second request of 22350 tokens, a first request of up to 23424 tokens triggers it (3/3) and one of 23440 tokens does not (0/3). The fix relocates scratch blocks below the checkpoint index (`block_idx < num_skipped_blocks - checkpoint_block`). A scratch block exactly at the checkpoint index stays and becomes the checkpoint block, since the worker exports the checkpoint into that column. Because relocated blocks are reused, checkpoint steps for already-allocated requests no longer need `num_speculative_blocks` extra new blocks. The allocation cap in `allocate_new_blocks` and the admission estimate in `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` both drop that term, so they stay equal. The existing `test_mamba_checkpoint_admission_matches_allocation` and the new test both check this. On unfixed builds, disabling MTP or prefix caching avoids the bug. Possible CI follow-up: no current job would catch this. The only nightly on this path, the B200 Kimi-K3 spec-decode GSM8K job, uses ~640-token prompts, and GSM8K accuracy does not move noticeably. A small extra phase in that job could catch this class of bug. After the GSM8K pass, it would send about 15 long prompts with lengths spread over one chunk-budget period, then send each again and check that the cached answer starts the same as a fresh computation. On GLM-5.3-Flash such a phase failed on unfixed main in 3 of 3 runs and passed with this fix in 3 of 3. I can send it as a separate PR if that is useful. AI assistance (Claude) was used; the change was reviewed and validated by the submitter. ---

title: [Misc] Remove code paths for Transformers < 5.16.1
author: hmellor
body:
## Overview

#57387 raised the minimum Transformers version to 5.16.1, so code that only runs on older versions is now unreachable. This PR removes it (~600 net lines), including the Transformers backend's legacy multi-modal processor.

## Claims

- Removes the Transformers v4 import guard (`transformers_utils/config.py`) and the `< 5.15` Mistral `tokenizer_mode="hf"` error (`tokenizers/registry.py`).
- Mistral3: drops the `< 5.15` dummy-text fallback for `PixtralProcessor`. The base `_get_hf_mm_text` already returns `None`.
- Transformers backend: deletes `LegacyMultiModalProcessor` (the pre-5.15 placeholder search), merges `_MultiModalProcessorBase` and `OffsetsMultiModalProcessor` into a single `MultiModalProcessor`, and removes `check_version` and its six calls (all ≤ 5.15).
- HYV4 tool/reasoning parsers: unwraps an always-true `major >= 5` check.
- Voxtral `fetch_audio`: drops the `list[float]` special case, which `is_valid_audio` handles since 5.10.
- Tests:
  - Transformers backend processor tests no longer parametrise over both processors and use `MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY` directly, so the `transformers_backend.py` helper is deleted.
  - `test_spliced_prompt_matches_hf_expansion` now compares against the HF processor's own output instead of the legacy processor's.
  - Removes dead version skips (MTP Gemma4, Transformers backend MLA, Granite), the unused `check_transformers_version` helper, and all 52 `min_transformers_version` values in `tests/models/registry.py` (all ≤ 5.16.0).

Not changed: the 25 registry entries with `max_transformers_version` < 5.16.1, and the `>= 5.0.0` skips on the bitsandbytes MoE and PaddleOCR-VL tests. Those tests can no longer run, but fixing or removing them is a separate decision.

## Validation

No behaviour change is expected on supported Transformers versions, so no model evals were run. Tests were run locally on macOS CPU with `transformers` 5.18.0.dev0:

```bash
pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py tests/transformers_utils/processors/test_voxtral.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_image.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_audio.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py
# 63 passed, 8 skipped (mistral3, needs CUDA), 2 xfailed (existing Emu3/Voxtral xfails)

pytest --collect-only tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/language/generation/test_granite.py \
  tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp
# 458 tests collected
```

GPU tests whose skips were removed (`test_backend.py::test_mla`, Gemma4 MTP) were not run locally and rely on CI.

title: [ROCm] Octave KV (`ROCM_OCTAVE`): native 3-bit KV cache backend for AMD GPUs
author: JartX
body:
## Overview Adds `ROCM_OCTAVE`, an attention backend that keeps the KV cache of full-attention layers at 3-4 bits per value, with native HIP kernels for RDNA3 (gfx1100) and MI300X (gfx942). Select it with `--kv-cache-dtype octave_k3v3`, `octave_k3v4` or `octave_k3v3_compact` (216, 248 and 196 bytes per slot at head size 256, against 1024 for fp16). RFC: #59773. `docs/design/rocm_octave.md` describes the format and the per-architecture contract. ## Claims - **Capacity:** - On 4× RX 7900 XTX with Qwen3.8-27B, 4.6× the KV tokens of fp16. - On one MI300X, 1.95× the tokens of AITER's fp8 cache (7.0M vs 3.6M, i.e. 53 vs 27 concurrent 128k requests). - **Quality:** GSM8K and a 126k needle-in-a-haystack test match fp16 and fp8 on both architectures. Next-token NLL at 380k is +0.0009 to +0.0015 nats over fp16. - **Speed:** - On MI300X, decode for one request matches AITER fp8. Per layer it is faster from 32k on (65 vs 103 µs at 128k). - On RDNA3 at 380k, per layer, decode is 4.6× faster than TurboQuant and MTP verification 11× faster. - **Works with MTP and CUDA graphs.** No host syncs in the metadata builder. We have served it in production on RDNA3 since October 2, 2026. - **Guarded to the validated architectures**, gfx1100 and gfx942: - CMake builds the sources and registers the ops only for them. - `supports_compute_capability` rejects other devices. - The tests skip elsewhere. ## Validation **Models.** Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (compressed-tensors, int4, group 32). To reproduce, [`cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4`](https://huggingface.co/cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4) is a public checkpoint with the same scheme and architecture; KV token counts will differ slightly. **Tests** (`pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_octave.py`), on this branch at 28aa54ed9a (merged with `main` 3897f95cf1): | | gfx1100 | gfx942 | |---|---|---| | `test_rocm_octave.py` | 105 passed | 87 passed, 18 skipped (sparse decode is gfx1100-only) | | Octave kernels with scratch in the built `.so` | 0 of 108 | 0 of 108 | - The tests compare store, decode and prefill with the PyTorch reference for all three cache dtypes. That covers: - the native and the portable decode; - 1 and 4 query tokens (MTP); - padded queries and 1-256 KV splits; - fp16 and bf16; - prefill over a cached prefix with several requests; - the sparse (QSA) decode. - To check that the tests can fail, I broke the kernels on purpose several times: a wrong codebook, a least-squares scale, a wrong `log2(e)`, a missing query debias. Each time the relevant tests failed. - `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on gfx942: served `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4` with `octave_k3v3` and MTP k=3 through 40 GSM8K questions with no sync error (97.5%). - pre-commit passes on the changed files, except `update-dockerfile-graph`, which needs `/bin/bash` and cannot run on my machine. mypy (CI stage) passes. - CI: the AMD `kernels/attention` step runs `test_rocm_octave.py` on its MI300 runners (gfx942). gfx1100 is not in CI; it was validated locally as above. **MI300X end to end.** Setup: - 1× MI300X, TP1, fp16, MTP k=3, `--max-model-len 131072`; only the cache dtype changes between rows. - GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, chat, thinking off, 200 questions, temperature 0.6. - NIAH: details below. - Speed: `vllm bench serve`. - The fp8 row is forced with `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA`. With only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, vLLM picks `ROCM_ATTN`. | KV cache | KV tokens | GSM8K | NIAH | decode at 126k | TPOT 1 user, 8k / 32k / 100k | TTFT 100k | 16 users, 8k | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 7,014,973 | 98.0 | 28/28 | 52 tok/s | 15 / 18 / 16 ms | 20.2 s | 221 tok/s | | `octave_k3v4` | 6,391,547 | 97.5 | 28/28 | 52 tok/s | 15 / 15 / 19 ms | 20.2 s | 226 tok/s | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 7,446,005 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 50 tok/s | 16 / 18 / 16 ms | 20.1 s | 211 tok/s | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 3,597,048 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 50 tok/s | 15 / 17 / 16 ms | 18.6 s | 235 tok/s | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 1,952,899 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 6 tok/s | 22 / 45 / 108 ms | 23.1 s | 120 tok/s | AITER is ahead with 16 users and in time to first token at 100k, which points at our prefill over a cached prefix; that is the next thing to work on.
MI300X: NIAH in detail The haystack is vLLM's own Python source, cut to 126k tokens. 16 keys are inserted every ~7.7k tokens, each a line such as `# PROJECT KEY Aldebaran: WK3DEGZD`, with star names as look-alike labels and random 8-character values. The same document is cut at 32k, 64k and 126k, which hold 4, 8 and 16 keys. For each key present the model is asked, thinking off, for only that key's value; an answer counts if it contains the exact value. Keys sit between 3% and 95% of the context. | KV cache | 32k (4 keys) | 64k (8 keys) | 126k (16 keys) | another key's value returned | |---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | `octave_k3v4` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | The model saturates this task at 128k. So it shows that the 3-bit cache loses no retrieval there; it does not rank the formats. The harder test is the 800k key curve in the RFC, where the keys start to blur only past 640k, because of the model and not the cache.
MI300X: vllm bench serve in detail Setup: - Random prompts (`--dataset-name random`), 512 output tokens with `--ignore-eos`, `--seed 0`, no prefix reuse. - One user at a time: 6 prompts at 8k, 4 at 32k and 3 at 100k. - 16 concurrent users: 64 prompts at 8k. No request failed. Each cell is median TTFT / median TPOT / output tok/s. Random tokens give MTP a low acceptance, the same for every row. | KV cache | 8k, 1 user | 32k, 1 user | 100k, 1 user | 8k, 16 users | |---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 1.55 s / 15.3 ms / 51.3 | 5.99 s / 18.1 ms / 33.4 | 20.2 s / 15.6 ms / 17.9 | 3.34 s / 62.1 ms / 221 | | `octave_k3v4` | 1.55 s / 15.4 ms / 52.4 | 6.06 s / 15.3 ms / 35.8 | 20.2 s / 19.2 ms / 17.1 | 3.95 s / 57.0 ms / 226 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 1.57 s / 16.2 ms / 50.2 | 6.73 s / 17.6 ms / 32.4 | 20.1 s / 15.6 ms / 17.9 | 3.27 s / 57.2 ms / 211 | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 1.57 s / 15.2 ms / 49.3 | 5.53 s / 17.1 ms / 34.1 | 18.6 s / 16.2 ms / 19.0 | 3.29 s / 49.9 ms / 235 | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 1.64 s / 22.5 ms / 36.8 | 5.78 s / 44.6 ms / 16.9 | 23.1 s / 108.4 ms / 6.2 | 7.26 s / 112.4 ms / 120 | Without MTP, to compare with UltraQuant (#57057), which needs bf16 here: | KV cache | KV tokens | 8k, 1 user | 32k, 1 user | 100k, 1 user | 8k, 16 users | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` (fp16) | 9,437,184 | 1.57 s / 51.9 ms / 18.2 | 5.28 s / 52.2 ms / 16.0 | 19.1 s / 52.6 ms / 11.1 | 10.9 s / 82.0 ms / 157 | | `ultraquant_4bit` (bf16) | 7,730,626 | 1.84 s / 58.5 ms / 16.1 | 6.24 s / 66.0 ms / 12.8 | 20.3 s / 87.5 ms / 7.9 | 14.0 s / 94.5 ms / 135 | On gfx942 UltraQuant's FlyDSL decode is not used, because it targets gfx950 and does not cover 6 query heads per KV head, so this is its Triton fallback. With MTP k=3 its output was not usable on this setup (GSM8K 1%, NIAH 0/28); without MTP it is correct (GSM8K 98.0, NIAH 28/28). This says nothing about UltraQuant on gfx950.
MI300X: attention per layer `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`, 6 query heads, 1 KV head. | | `octave_k3v3` | fp8, AITER | |---|---|---| | decode, 1 token at 8k | 25 µs | 16 µs | | decode, 1 token at 32k | 32 µs | 33 µs | | decode, 1 token at 128k | 65 µs | 103 µs | | decode, 16 requests at 32k | 227 µs | 323 µs | | decode, 64 requests at 8k | 220 µs | 352 µs | | MTP verify, 4 tokens at 32k | 61 µs | — | Prefill, against `ROCM_AITER_FA` with an fp16 cache: - 8k with no prefix: 2.76 vs 2.50 ms. - Two 2k chunks over an 8k prefix: 3.28 vs 6.76 ms. - A 2k chunk over a 32k prefix: 5.44 vs 7.15 ms.
RDNA3 (4× RX 7900 XTX, TP4) evaluation Setup: - 8 GB of KV cache per GPU, same image and flags for every row. - GSM8K: chat, thinking off, 500 questions, temperature 0.6, no MTP so that TurboQuant is correct. - NLL: one 380k-token document. | KV cache | Bytes | GSM8K | NLL over fp16 | |---|---|---|---| | fp16 | 1024 | 91.8 | — | | `turboquant_k3v4_nc` | 230 | 89.8 | +0.00155 | | `octave_k3v4` | 248 | 91.4 | +0.00086 | | `octave_k3v3` | 216 | 92.4 | +0.00125 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 196 | 91.8 | +0.00150 | Attention per layer at 380k (one TP4 shard): | | fp16 | `turboquant_k3v4_nc` | `octave_k3v3_compact` | `octave_k3v3` | |---|---|---|---|---| | decode, 1 token | 2370 µs | 2565 µs | 563 µs | 614 µs | | MTP verify, 4 tokens | 48.8 ms | 6.65 ms | 0.58 ms | 0.62 ms | | prefill, 2048-token chunk | 125.6 ms | 86.6 ms | 60.8 ms | 63.9 ms | Time to first token at 380k, end to end with MTP and a cold prefix: - `octave_k3v3_compact`: 297 s; - fp16: 371 s; - TurboQuant: 621 s. At 100k all three are within 8%, because the GEMMs and the all-reduce dominate. When I replaced the metadata builder the backend first inherited with its own, I checked that nothing moved (TP4, MTP, GSM8K 500 at concurrency 6): - GSM8K: 92.2 → 91.8; - MTP acceptance: 83.33% → 83.39%; - output: 216.1 → 216.8 tok/s.
Sparse attention (qwen4_exp QSA) evaluation Setup: - 4x RX 7900 XTX, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 (asymmetric, g32), TP4, fp16, `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`, no prefix caching. - NLL from `prompt_logprobs` over 12 documents of ~8k tokens, split at position 2048, and over 24 short documents. - Values in nats over fp16; mean NLL repeats to about ±0.003 nats. | KV cache | KV tokens | NLL pos >= 2048 | NLL pos < 2048 | NLL short | |---|---|---|---|---| | fp16 | 47,409 | 1.0856 | 1.6707 | 1.1788 | | `octave_k3v3`, no window | 155,930 | +0.0395 | +0.0851 | +0.0708 | | `octave_k3v3` | 155,930 | +0.0163 | -0.0221 | +0.0085 | That run used our fork for the fp16 port of QSA and two RDNA3 MoE fixes, which go in separate PRs. On this branch alone the QSA path is bf16, like upstream.
## Details What changes. Most of the PR is new files: - `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_octave.py`: the format and its PyTorch reference, which defines the byte layout. - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_octave_attn.py`: the backend and its metadata builder. - `csrc/attention/octave_*`, the kernels: - store, reduce, rotation and a portable decode, shared by both architectures; - WMMA decode and prefill for gfx1100; - MFMA decode and prefill for gfx942; - the op registration in `octave_torch_bindings.cpp`. - Tests, docs, and `--model` plus the new cache dtypes in `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`. Changes to existing files are small: - the three cache dtypes in `vllm/config/cache.py`, `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` and `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`; - the backend in the registry and in the ROCm platform's selection; - the sources in `CMakeLists.txt`; - `customize_spec` now runs under the current vLLM config, because the backend needs the model's rotary dims to size the slot; - in `qwen4_exp` (QSA), Octave as the main cache through a sparse decode, with the new fused QSA prepare turned off for an Octave cache, since it writes raw BF16 K/V. Nothing changes for other backends or cache dtypes. Design choices a reviewer may want to know about: - **Native kernels only.** There is no Triton fallback; an architecture is added once it has its own kernels and passes the tests and an end-to-end run. The RFC lists what each one needs. - **The metadata builder is the backend's own.** It builds the per-query maps on the device without host syncs, supports `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graphs, and refreshes the maps between fused MTP draft steps. - **On gfx942**: - QK runs on `v_mfma_i32_16x16x32_i8`, with the query split into high and low int8 halves. - V is widened to fp16 by one `v_perm`: each codebook byte becomes an exact fp16 denormal, which the MI300 MFMA keeps. - The decode file is built with `-amdgpu-mfma-vgpr-form`, so the accumulators do not halve the occupancy. - **Supported models.** Head size 256 with 64 RoPE dims, i.e. Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 / 3.6 / 3.8. - The decode handles up to 8 query heads per KV head on each GPU. - The sparse decode and the exact sink/recent window are QSA-only and gfx1100-only for now. - Head size 128 is the next step. - **Size.** This is a large PR: about 1.4k lines of gfx942 kernels on top of the RDNA3 ones. Each architecture lives in its own file behind the same `octave_prefill` / `octave_decode` entry points, so it can be reviewed and later removed on its own. **Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs and issues for `octave`, `turboquant rocm`, `kv cache 3-bit`, `kv cache quantization hip` and `lloyd-max kv`. The closest are: - UltraQuant (#57057): FP4 with FlyDSL for gfx950, built on TurboQuant. - KVarN (#46613 / #46812): Triton, CUDA-first. - #43835: HIP int8/int4 for CDNA. - #40396: a Triton TurboQuant decode for MI300X. - #53231: TurboQuant for Gemma 4 on ROCm. - #59132: Triton attention for RDNA without KV quantization. None targets RDNA with native kernels, and none runs below 8 bits with MTP on ROCm. **AI assistance.** I used AI assistance to write this PR: Claude, and Qwen3.8-27B running locally on the boxes it was measured on. I have reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and evaluations above, and can answer for the change. ---

title: [Bugfix][Watermarking] Keep draft prompt lengths valid under CUDA graphs
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

Fix stale prompt lengths in the draft watermark deduplication mask under CUDA graphs. The bug came in with #56807. I found it while reviewing #59554, which would expose DFlash to it too.

## Claims

- With `dual_key_gumbel` and the default `deduplicate_contexts="single_turn"`, draft sampling under FULL CUDA graphs (default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) read prompt lengths from a stale UVA buffer after new requests arrived. This affects EAGLE3, MTP and DSpark (reproduced; EAGLE shares the autoregressive path). Some drafts were sampled without key A where they should carry it, and some repeated contexts were not deduplicated. Graph and eager mode now agree.
- No host sync, and no end-to-end change I can separate from run-to-run noise (see Performance). The fix adds one async copy of `max_num_reqs` int32 values per propose. The captured dedup kernel then reads device memory instead of pinned host memory, which is faster in a microbenchmark.

## Validation

Engine harness: Qwen3-4B targets (Qwen3.5-0.8B for MTP) with dedup `single_turn`. It compares the dedup mask each draft row actually used against a CPU reference built from the true prompt lengths. Compared with the engine-level script under Reproduction, it also covers Poisson arrivals, MTP and DSpark. λ is arrivals per engine step.

| Workload | Before (FULL graph) | After (FULL graph) | Eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 K=3, crafted (one request at a time, prompt-copying) | 576/1905 mask rows wrong; 536 accepted drafts lacked key A | 0/1896 | 0/1896 |
| EAGLE3 K=3, online Poisson (λ=0.2, mean concurrency 12) | 43/23178 mask rows wrong (41 falsely skipped, 2 missed dedup) | 0/23178 | 0/23325 |
| MTP K=3, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 32.6% / 2.06% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |
| DSpark K=7, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 39.5% / 2.05% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |

The MTP and DSpark "after" numbers come from the harness's patched `prepare()`, not from a commit tree. The EAGLE3 online "after" rows used the first revision of this fix, which differed only in copying into a `[:num_reqs]` slice. The EAGLE3 crafted "after" and eager runs use this commit.

Host sync: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, EAGLE3 under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, 12 staggered admissions and 98 `prepare()` calls: clean. A deliberate `.item()` in `prepare()` trips the check, so the check does cover this path.

Unit test:

```bash
pytest tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py -k reads_current_prompt_lens   # fails on main, passes with the fix
pytest tests/watermarking/                                                    # 148 passed (B300)
```

The test is CUDA-only. CI runs `tests/watermarking` only in the CPU "V1 Others" step, where it is skipped. I ran it locally on a B300: it fails on main and passes with the fix, and the suite passes (148).

About 1-2% of accepted drafts are affected at low traffic (EAGLE3 0.98%, MTP 2.06%, DSpark 2.05%) and 0.54% when busy (EAGLE3). Per-category detection rates in paired runs are identical for EAGLE3 and within noise for MTP and DSpark: at most 2 of 19-20 requests differ. The bug still breaks the watermark's own contract, and graph and eager runs diverge.

### Performance

Setup: B300, Qwen3-4B with EAGLE3 (`AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3`, K=3, probabilistic), `dual_key_gumbel`, temperature 1.0, random 1024 in / 256 out with `--ignore-eos` (64 prompts at c=1 and c=8, 256 at c=64), default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Main and fix servers ran in parallel on two GPUs, swapped each round, for 10 rounds of 2 passes. Δ is the mean of the per-round paired change, ± the 95% CI. A/A is the same comparison of main against main (4 rounds).

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (main → fix) | Δ tok/s | Δ mean TPOT | Δ mean TTFT | Acceptance length | A/A Δ tok/s | A/A Δ TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 464.7 → 462.3 | −0.5% ± 0.6 | +0.5% ± 0.6 | +1.8% ± 2.0 | 1.632 → 1.632 | −0.4% ± 0.6 | +0.6% ± 3.4 |
| 8 | 3032 → 3012 | −0.6% ± 0.8 | +0.4% ± 0.9 | +2.3% ± 1.7 | 1.658 → 1.662 | −0.3% ± 3.3 | −1.2% ± 5.6 |
| 64 | 10543 → 10495 | −0.4% ± 0.8 | +0.3% ± 0.9 | +0.8% ± 1.5 | 1.533 → 1.533 | +0.3% ± 1.2 | −0.7% ± 4.1 |

Throughput and TPOT change by less than 1%, with CIs that include zero. The A/A differences are of similar size.

Mean TTFT is 0.35-0.65 ms (0.8-2.3%) higher. Only the c=8 CI excludes zero (+0.7% to +4.0%). Between two identical main servers, per-round TTFT differences range from −6% to +3%, and one A/A CI (c=64 acceptance length) also excludes zero. I read the TTFT difference as noise, but these runs cannot rule out a TTFT cost of a few percent at c=8.

`prepare()` alone, with a UVA-backed prompt-length source and the speculator's two gathers: host time goes from 48.4-48.9 µs to 51.4-52.1 µs (+3 µs for one more copy launch). The copy itself takes 4.2 µs on the GPU at `max_num_reqs=1024` and 0.9 µs at 256. The dedup kernel runs once per draft step, so three times per propose at K=3. Replayed in a CUDA graph, those three steps get faster because the kernel reads device memory instead of pinned host memory: 12.3 → 8.7 µs with 1 request and 30.2 → 17.0 µs with 1024 requests (`max_num_reqs=1024`).

### Reproduction

A standalone script shows the bug without a model. It captures the draft dedup mask in a CUDA graph, admits a request (which moves `prompt_len.gpu` to the next pool buffer), and compares the replayed graph with eager mode. Run it on a CUDA GPU with `python repro_stale_prompt_len.py`.

<details>
<summary>repro_stale_prompt_len.py</summary>

```python
# Draft watermark dedup mask under a CUDA graph reads a stale prompt length.
import torch

import vllm
from vllm.v1.watermarking.gumbel import GumbelWatermarker
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils import UvaBackedTensor

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
dev = torch.device("cuda")
wm = DraftWatermarker(GumbelWatermarker(key=42, context_width=2), max_num_reqs=1,
                      device=dev, num_speculative_steps=1,
                      deduplicate_contexts="single_turn",
                      deduplicate_contexts_max_history=None)
prompt_len = UvaBackedTensor(1, dtype=torch.int32)  # like req_states.prompt_len
# Request in slot 0: prompt [5, 6, 9], generated [5, 6], next draft context
# [5, 6]. The context repeats only inside the prompt, so with single_turn the
# draft must use key A. Read with prompt length 0, it looks like repeated
# generated text and the draft skips key A.
tokens = torch.tensor([[5, 6, 9, 5, 6]], device=dev)
total_len = torch.tensor([5], device=dev)
ctx = torch.tensor([[5, 6]], device=dev)
enabled = torch.tensor([True], device=dev)
logits = torch.zeros(1, 8, device=dev)
idx = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
temp, draft_step = torch.ones(1, device=dev), torch.tensor(0, device=dev)

def prepare():  # the speculator calls this on every propose()
    wm.prepare(ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_len.gpu, total_len)

def uses_key_a():  # per-row mask that draft sampling uses for key A
    return wm._sampling_state(logits, idx, temp, draft_step, ctx)[1]

prepare()  # capture time: slot 0 has prompt length 0
uses_key_a()  # warm up outside capture
graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
    graph_out = uses_key_a()
# A step that admits a request runs copy_to_uva(), which moves
# prompt_len.gpu to the next buffer of its round-robin pool.
prompt_len.np[0] = 3
prompt_len.copy_to_uva()
prepare()
eager = uses_key_a().item()
graph.replay()
replayed = graph_out.item()
print(f"eager: key A={eager}  graph: key A={replayed}  ->",
      "OK" if eager == replayed else "STALE prompt length in graph")
```

</details>

Main:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=False  -> STALE prompt length in graph
```

With the fix:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=True  -> OK
```

An engine-level script runs EAGLE3 with `dual_key_gumbel` through `LLM`, admits 24 requests one at a time, and counts draft rows whose dedup mask differs from the mask built from the current prompt lengths. Run `python engine_repro.py` for the default CUDA graph mode and `python engine_repro.py eager` for eager mode (30-45 s each on a B300).

<details>
<summary>engine_repro.py</summary>

```python
# EAGLE3 + dual_key_gumbel: compare the dedup mask each draft row used with the
# mask recomputed, in the same CUDA graph, from the current prompt lengths.
import os
import sys

import torch

os.environ.update(VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER="1", VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING="0")
import vllm  # noqa: E402
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker as DW  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.watermark import draft_watermarking_mask  # noqa: E402

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
orig_init, orig_prepare, orig_state = DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state
instances = []

def __init__(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args):
    orig_init(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args)
    self.true_pl = torch.zeros(max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    self.stats = torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)  # rows, wrong, skip
    instances.append(self)

def prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens):
    orig_prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens)
    self.true_pl.copy_(prompt_lens)  # current prompt lengths

def _sampling_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx):
    steps, mask = orig_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx)
    ref = draft_watermarking_mask(
        self.all_token_ids, idx, self.true_pl, self.total_lens, self.prior_contexts,
        ctx, steps, self.enabled[: len(ctx)] & (temps != 0),
        self.deduplicate_contexts_max_history, False)
    self.stats += torch.stack(
        [torch.ones_like(ref).sum(), (mask != ref).sum(), (ref & ~mask).sum()])
    return steps, mask

DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state = __init__, prepare, _sampling_state
wm = {"algorithm": "dual_key_gumbel", "key": 42, "context_width": 4}
spec = {"method": "eagle3", "model": "AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}
llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-4B", speculative_config=spec, watermark_config=wm, seed=0,
          max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
          enforce_eager=sys.argv[1:] == ["eager"])
(dw,) = instances
dw.stats.zero_()  # drop warmup and capture rows
text = ("The committee met on Tuesday to review the annual budget. The members agreed "
        "to fund the public libraries, repair the old bridge near the river, and hire "
        "two more nurses for the clinic. The mayor promised a full report next month.")
for i in range(24):  # one request at a time; each admission rotates the UVA pool
    ask = f"Repeat exactly, word for word:\n{text}" if i % 3 == 1 else "Say hi."
    llm.chat([{"role": "user", "content": f"[{i}] {ask}"}],
             SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, seed=i, max_tokens=96), use_tqdm=False,
             chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False})
rows, wrong, skipped = dw.stats.tolist()
print(f"draft rows={rows}  mask rows wrong={wrong}  wrongly skipped key A={skipped}")
```

</details>

| Run | Output |
|---|---|
| Main, CUDA graphs (2 runs, identical) | `draft rows=714  mask rows wrong=129  wrongly skipped key A=129` |
| Fix, CUDA graphs | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Main, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Fix, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |


## Details

**Root cause:** `req_states.prompt_len` is a `UvaBackedTensor`. `copy_to_uva()` runs from `apply_staged_writes` on steps that add requests, and it moves `.gpu` round-robin across the buffer pool. `DraftWatermarker.prepare()` stored that reference, so a captured `draft_watermarking_mask` kept reading the capture-time buffer. Newly admitted requests then see the previous occupant's prompt length until the pool comes back around:
- If the stale length is shorter than the real one, prompt n-grams count as generated history and the draft skips key A.
- If it is longer, real repeats are missed.

**Fix:** `DraftWatermarker` owns an int32 `[max_num_reqs]` buffer, and `prepare()` copies into it. This follows the existing `contexts` and `enabled` copies in the same method. It is also the principle MRV2 states for fused draft decoding: replayed tensor state must live in persistent storage.

I found no other inputs to captured draft sampling that go stale:
- `all_token_ids` and `total_len` are `StagedWriteTensor`s whose `.gpu` never moves.
- `contexts` and `enabled` are already copied into owned buffers.
- Other UVA-backed inputs to the draft path (temperature, seeds) are already copied into speculator-owned buffers. The remaining readers run eagerly.

**Unchanged behavior:** eager mode and the watermark-off path are unaffected. By code inspection, dedup modes `none` and `all` do not depend on prompt lengths: `none` returns before the mask is built, and `all` searches from position 0. The copy still runs in those modes; its cost is negligible.

**Alternatives:**
- Making `RequestState.prompt_len` a stable `StagedWriteTensor` would fix this for every future graph reader. It touches the penalties, bad_words, trace_replay and model_runner readers, and the `LogitsProcessor` interface types `prompt_len` as `UvaBackedTensor`, so it is better done as a separate refactor.
- A persistent device mirror inside `UvaBackedTensor` would cost a copy for every user.
