title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Keep store pins and AbortAck until NIXL transfers stop
author: apex-mochen
body:
## Overview

The P2P producer released store pins, and sent `AbortAck` to the consumer, while its NIXL WRITEs could still be running. Neither cancelling the handle nor removing the remote peer stops a running WRITE with the UCX backend. This PR keeps the pins, and holds back `AbortAck`, until NIXL reports each transfer terminal. Addresses #59569 and the review on this PR. The consumer-side counterpart is tracked in #61532.

## Claims

- `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` releases only transfers that are no longer `PROC`/`PEND`. Previously it reported running WRITEs as cancelled, because `release_xfer_handle` never fails for an in-progress UCX request.
- A round whose store timed out, or which the consumer aborted, fails its jobs but keeps the pins of jobs that inflight transfers still read, until those transfers are terminal. Late completions settle each job exactly once, and new supply cannot restart such a round.
- The abort drain no longer falls back to `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `AbortAck` after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. Past the timeout it logs once and keeps retrying. `AbortAck` is sent only when no transfer of the round can still write to the consumer.
- Wait-mode cancel retries are paced to one attempt per round per 100 ms, shared by the store-timeout sweep and the abort drain.
- When one transfer of a round fails, the round's other transfers are no longer cancelled with `mode="immediate"`. The round is marked cancelled instead: their pins and the round's `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)` wait until they are terminal.
- `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` from `check_xfer_state`, which NIXL raises when the peer process is gone, is treated as a terminal failure, so a dead peer no longer pins its transfers until the session closes.

## Validation

Real NIXL 1.4.1, UCX over TCP, CPU DRAM. This is not RDMA hardware.

| scenario | result |
|---|---|
| 512 MiB WRITE, old `cancel(mode="wait")` | returned `[]` while `PROC` in 5/5 runs; all bytes landed afterwards |
| 512 MiB WRITE, new `cancel(mode="wait")` | returned the tid as still inflight in 5/5 runs; `poll()` reported DONE only after all 512 MiB landed |
| 512 MiB WRITE, `remove_remote_peer` | returned with 14–392 MB landed in 5/5 runs; the rest still landed, and the handle then raises `nixlNotFoundError` |
| 1 GiB WRITE stalled by SIGSTOPping the target, then `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `remove_remote_peer`, then resume | 64/64 blocks still landed |
| stalled WRITE, target left stopped | stays `PROC` for 60 s, no timeout of its own |
| stalled WRITE, target SIGKILLed | `check_xfer_state` raises `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` |

Unit tests use the fake transport in `test_sessions.py` and a mocked NIXL agent in `test_data_transport.py`. The new behavior tests fail on the respective previous logic and pass now.

```sh
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
# head 387b0ba092 (agent-run):  486 passed, 1 skipped
# head 84ec0d792f (I ran it myself, and the agent independently): 484 passed, 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 78.57s
```

ruff 0.14.0 and mypy 1.20.2 (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12`) are clean.

Not done: RDMA/InfiniBand hardware, GPU memory, serving load or model evaluation.

## Details

**Root cause.** `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` relied on `release_xfer_handle` raising for a transfer that is still running. With UCX it never raises: `nixlUcxBackendReqH::release` calls `ucp_request_cancel`, which does nothing for an RMA PUT, then frees the request and returns success. The producer therefore treated running WRITEs as cancelled, released their store pins, and acked aborts while bytes were still landing. `remove_remote_peer` → `invalidateRemoteMD` only drops the connection entry, and the endpoint is later closed in flush mode, so outstanding writes complete rather than stop. That rules out the suggested "tear down the peer, then ack" fallback.

**Abort flow after this change.**
1. The consumer sends `AbortFetchMsg`.
2. The producer marks the round cancelled, fails the jobs no transfer reads, and keeps the rest pinned. A failed transfer takes its round down the same path.
3. It retries `cancel(mode="wait")` at the paced rate. A transfer leaves only when NIXL reports it terminal, or the peer is gone.
4. When no transfer of the round remains, the producer releases the remaining pins and sends `AbortAckMsg`. An aborted round sends no `TransferDoneMsg`.

**Tradeoff.** There is no hard deadline on the producer side. If a peer stays alive but the WRITE never progresses, the pins stay held, with one warning after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. A bound would need a transport primitive that guarantees a running WRITE has stopped. An awaited forced endpoint close (`UCP_EP_CLOSE_FLAG_FORCE`) might be one, but NIXL does not expose it. The consumer still gives up after `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S` and frees its slots; that is the open issue #61532.

The `store_timed_out` flag on a round is renamed `cancelled`, because it now covers aborts and failed transfers as well. All three paths share it: jobs no transfer reads fail at once, and the others keep their pins until their transfers are terminal.

The remote-disconnect check matches the binding's class name or the `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` status code, so the NIXL bindings are not imported in this module. An error it does not recognize keeps the transfer inflight, which is the conservative side.

The shutdown drain in `manager.py` still falls back to `mode="immediate"` after `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`, because the engine is exiting. Only its docstring is updated.

This is distinct from #59329, which withdraws timed-out parked supply before Fetch. Its withdrawal set must be derived from the results actually emitted (`{r.job_id for r in results}`), so that unconfirmed inflight jobs are not removed from the round's pending jobs. Whichever PR merges second needs that adjustment.

AI assistance was used for the investigation, implementation, tests and this description.

title: [Perf] Use value-only reduction for native per-token FP8 quantization
author: jackLei0901
body:
﻿<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Use `amax` instead of `max(dim=-1)` with discarded indices in the native per-token FP8 path. Inductor lowers the discarded-index form to `max_with_index`; `amax` requests a value-only reduction.

Related to #59564: that PR changes group quantization; this changes the per-token branch. Either can merge first. The value-only reduction approach follows #59564. I am happy to fold this change into that PR if reviewers prefer.

#41427 (open) also edits this line for NaN handling. The changes compose (`amax` applies equally to its `x_f`); whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase at the reduction site.

## Claims

- Removes `max_with_index` from the generated per-token kernel (24 → 0 call-text occurrences in the served FP8-dynamic model; not a dynamic call count).
- Standalone compiled operator, H800 PCIe, measured at `378504a5`: 7.7–39.8% lower latency across 21 shapes (hidden 4096/7168/14336, tokens 1/8/32/128/512/2048/8192). Not a latest-main, model-level or TPOT claim.
- Outputs and scales were bitwise identical for tested finite operator inputs, including zero, −0.0 and ties; NaN and ±Inf behavior was preserved in the tested checks. This does not assert whole-model output equivalence.

## Validation

Evidence and reproduction scripts: https://github.com/jackLei0901/vllm-runtime-reliability-lab/tree/e67366ce043f3422d806c2f78ce0b5031d05a8e9/experiments/fp8-per-token-amax-20261002. Final validation summary: https://github.com/jackLei0901/vllm-runtime-reliability-lab/blob/e67366ce043f3422d806c2f78ce0b5031d05a8e9/experiments/fp8-per-token-amax-20261002/VALIDATION_20261002.md.

- Eight selected native per-token fusion cases passed. Independent A/B/A lowering checks passed in four contexts, with bitwise-equal tested outputs and scales; BF16/FP32 bounded/unbounded special-value checks passed.
- Seventy-two CUDA per-token quant tests passed as regression context; they do not exercise the changed native Python line.
- Full pre-commit exited 0: 13 hooks passed, including mypy, and 20 were skipped for no applicable files.

- GSM8K, `RedHatAI/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic` @ `33cf8c95`, default compilation: base **0.6179**, patch **0.6050** (815 versus 798 / 1,319); both pass the existing **0.60** threshold. Requests are concurrent and the run reports `batch_invariant=False`, so run-to-run variation is plausible but was not measured; the difference is not attributed. This does not establish accuracy equivalence or exclude regression.

## Details

<details>
<summary>Method and limits</summary>

Validation Python pin: `b558f160a2c0abcb5902acc3c91a14c38a4af173`. The target file remains unchanged at preparation main `2a537887de7a103baa49bbfdce93e99d48d19441` (blob `161baf44`).

Historical timing used CUDA-graph replay, five samples per process, fresh processes and independent caches in max/amax/max/amax/max order. Across all 21 shapes, maximum baseline spread was 1.5% (hidden 4096 alone: 0.8%). At hidden 4096, one token changed from 2.356 to 2.014 µs and 2,048 tokens from 24.535 to 15.665 µs.

Model eval ran on H800 PCIe with PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, TP=1, max length 4096 and identical resolved configurations. Its text hidden size is 2048, separate from the operator timings. Existing parent-commit binaries were reused, not a full latest-main build; the validation summary records source-identity limits.

Offline comparison paired all 13 generated Triton kernels and nine execution wrappers. No added fusion, changed memory operation or removed cast was found. Selected autotune configurations were not saved; removing index maintenance could change tuning choices and fused norm summation order, but that remains an untested hypothesis. The score difference stays unattributed.

Scale calculation, upper-bound handling, clamping and FP8 conversion are unchanged; the patch changes no CUDA kernel or fusion policy. Serving quality was checked, but model-level performance was not benchmarked.

</details>

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Overlap the mHC gate projection with attention and FFN
author: cpersson-amd
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, each DeepSeek V4.1 mHC seam ran the whole fused AITER kernel pair on the default stream before the next sublayer could start. That pair is the post block, the gate projection, Sinkhorn, and the collapse with RMSNorm. This PR moves the gate projection onto a side stream inside FULL HIP graphs, so it overlaps with the following attention or FFN. The default stream now only runs the post block plus the RMSNorm'd collapse, in one new Triton kernel. This is the ROCm counterpart of the CUDA overlap in [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603).

## Claims

- Output throughput is up 0.3% to 5.4% end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, EP, FP8 KV, MI355X, at every concurrency from 1 to 128 at TP2, TP4 and TP8.
- The new residual and the gates (post, comb, next pre) are bit-identical to the fused AITER seam. The layer input is bit-identical up to 16 tokens and within one bf16 ulp above that.
- No change outside FULL-graph decode with at most 128 tokens. Prefill, piecewise graphs, eager mode, CUDA and DSpark draft layers keep the current path.



## Validation



### Kernel

MI355X, HIP-graph replay time per seam. "Fused" is `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter` (main + reduce kernels). "Input kernel" is the new `mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton`, the only part left on the default stream. "Gates" is the side-stream work.


| tokens | fused (µs) | input kernel (µs) | gates on side stream (µs) |
| ------ | ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| 1      | 9.91       | 4.15              | 8.48                      |
| 4      | 10.24      | 4.26              | 9.01                      |
| 16     | 10.41      | 4.37              | 9.17                      |


The default-stream seam goes from about 10 µs to about 4.3 µs. That is roughly 0.5 ms per decode step across the 86 seams that take the overlap (43 layers × 2).

### End-to-end

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, TP4, EP, FP8 KV, 12 sweep points. Mean TPOT in ms and output throughput in tok/s:


| input / output | concurrency | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | Δ     | tok/s main | tok/s this PR | Δ     |
| -------------- | ----------- | --------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------- | ------------- | ----- |
| 8192 / 1024    | 4           | 8.08      | 7.70         | -4.8% | 466.71     | 488.68        | +4.7% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 8           | 9.80      | 9.46         | -3.5% | 773.17     | 799.60        | +3.4% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 16          | 11.84     | 11.50        | -2.9% | 1262.50    | 1300.66       | +3.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 32          | 16.12     | 15.69        | -2.7% | 1786.03    | 1833.31       | +2.6% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 64          | 23.14     | 22.90        | -1.1% | 2516.82    | 2539.97       | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 128         | 35.31     | 34.51        | -2.3% | 3161.18    | 3225.27       | +2.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 256         | 58.27     | 57.96        | -0.5% | 3795.31    | 3815.37       | +0.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 4           | 13.80     | 13.47        | -2.4% | 227.83     | 233.61        | +2.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 16          | 39.88     | 39.98        | +0.2% | 337.21     | 338.35        | +0.3% |
| 60000 / 600    | 64          | 138.79    | 136.17       | -1.9% | 388.60     | 394.46        | +1.5% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 4           | 16.85     | 16.53        | -1.9% | 185.12     | 187.66        | +1.4% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 16          | 54.22     | 53.73        | -0.9% | 247.55     | 250.08        | +1.0% |


The mean is -2.05% TPOT and +2.00% throughput. Throughput is higher at all 12 points and TPOT lower at 11; the exception is 60000 / 600 at concurrency 16, at +0.2%. Median TPOT gives -2.14%, also 11 of 12, so the whole distribution moves rather than a tail.

**TP2, TP4 and TP8 at concurrency 1 to 128.** Random 2048 in / 256 out, same build for both arms on one node, overlap on against `MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS=0`. The overlap arm ran with a limit of 512, which at these concurrencies covers the same decode steps as 128. TP2 and TP8 had a warm-up pass and TP4 did not. These sweeps predate the switch to the global aux stream and events. Change in output throughput:

| concurrency | TP2   | TP4   | TP8   |
| ----------- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1           | +5.4% | +5.2% | +5.4% |
| 2           | +5.0% | +5.4% | +4.9% |
| 4           | +4.5% | +4.7% | +4.0% |
| 8           | +3.4% | +3.7% | +3.6% |
| 16          | +3.0% | +3.2% | +4.2% |
| 24          | +2.3% | +3.9% | +3.7% |
| 32          | +1.9% | +2.9% | +2.6% |
| 48          | +2.2% | +2.8% | +3.7% |
| 64          | +1.3% | +2.9% | +2.4% |
| 96          | +0.8% | +2.0% | +0.3% |
| 128         | +1.4% | +1.7% | +1.4% |

Every point improves. The gain shrinks from about +5% at concurrency 1 to +0.3–2% at 96–128, where it is within about 1% run-to-run noise.

### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, `lm_eval` `local-completions`, full test split, `num_concurrent=32`:


| run     | flexible-extract | strict-match    |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------- |
| default | 0.9227 ± 0.0074  | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 |
| this PR | 0.9234 ± 0.0073  | 0.9234 ± 0.0073 |


### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k rocm
```

All pass on MI355X. `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_mhc_overlap_matches_fused_seam` is new and runs at 1, 2, 7, 16, 64 and 128 tokens. After joining the side stream, it compares every output with `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` (the fused AITER seam):

- the residual and gates must match exactly;
- the layer input must match within one bf16 ulp, and it must already be usable before the join;
- the same checks are repeated across three HIP-graph replays with changing inputs.

CI runs it in `:amd: (MI355) mHC Kernels`.

## Details

**Why the split is exact.** In AITER's fused seam (`_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rmsnorm_main_kernel`), the post-mix is rounded to bf16 once, and that rounded `R'` feeds the projection, the square sums and the collapse. This PR splits the seam in two:

- The new kernel recomputes `R'` with the same expression order, so it is bit-identical, then collapses it with the carried pre-mix and applies the RMSNorm.
- The side stream runs AITER's own fused kernel on `R'` without the post (`HAS_POST=False`). Its gates are therefore the same numbers.

Only the RMSNorm's row sum differs. The new kernel holds a token's row in registers and sums it in one pass, while AITER reduces it across split-K programs, so the order changes. That is exact at decode sizes, and within one ulp otherwise.

**Gating.** The overlap runs only inside FULL HIP-graph capture, not in piecewise graphs, with `0 < tokens <= MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS` (128). Fork and join then become graph edges; `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention` keeps its aux streams to captured graphs for the same reason. It also requires AITER's fused delayed seam (`HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM`), `hc_mult == 4`, and no ubatching. The 128-token limit is the largest tested point. The gain was still positive there but shrinking (above), and the overlap was not measured beyond it, although FULL graphs go up to 512 tokens.

**Seams.** The overlap applies to every FFN seam and to the attention seam of every layer after the first. Layer 0's broadcast seam and Engram seams already take a different path and keep it. The gate stream is joined after attention and at the end of each layer, which is where the gates are next read. The stream is separate from the attention aux streams, as on CUDA. `record_stream` keeps the side stream's inputs and the main stream's gate outputs alive across the fork. No host synchronization is added.

**Limitations.**

- **Tuning:** the token limit was tuned on MI355X TP2, TP4 and TP8.



### Existing PRs

I searched vllm-project/vllm PRs (open and closed) for mHC overlap, coefficient and side-stream work on ROCm. None moves the mHC seam off the default stream on ROCm.

- [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603) (merged) is the CUDA version. It needs SM100 and DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`, and stops at 16 tokens. This PR follows its structure, gating and join points.
- [#56853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56853) (merged) adds an attention-side aux stream for DeepSeek-V4 HCA layers. It keeps the mHC seam serial on the default stream, which is what this PR changes.
- [#58655](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58655) (merged) introduced the fused AITER delayed seam that this PR splits.

title: [Quantization] Support compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE with FP8 activations via Mxfp4MoEMethod
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load compressed-tensors checkpoints with MXFP4 weights and dynamic FP8 activations (e.g. `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash converted to CT) and run them with the FP8 activations the checkpoint declares. Alternative to #59376 (cc @kylesayrs).

**Depends on #61556.** Humming 0.1.16, which `main` pins today, rejects FP8 (GS128) activations with MXFP4 weights, so these checkpoints fail to load with `--moe-backend humming` until #61556 lands.

## Claims

- MoE experts: `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4MoEMethod(Mxfp4MoEMethod)` only handles the `*_weight_packed` checkpoint naming and the declared activation scheme. Backend selection, weight conversion, size round-up, monolithic kernels and EPLB are inherited from the native MXFP4 method.
- The checkpoint's FP8 activation key reaches the Humming MoE backend. Before, it was dropped and Humming ran BF16 activations (W4A16) unless `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` was set.
- Dense linears with MXFP4 weights and FP8 inputs (GLM-5.3's dense MLPs target `Linear`) use a new `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4` scheme that requests FP8 activations, instead of the W4A4 scheme requesting MXFP4 activations.
- `get_moe_method` looks up the expert scheme with the layer's `ckpt_*_proj_name`, and DeepSeek-V4 (NVIDIA) passes `ckpt_names=("w1", "w2", "w3")`, so name-based targets such as `re:.*experts\.\d+\.w\d+$` match.

## Validation

H200 (SM90), `--moe-backend humming`, checked by inspecting the loaded layers.

| Model | Config | Dense MXFP4 linear | MoE experts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8 (real weights) | TP1 | n/a (FP8 block) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (W4A16 before this PR's 2nd commit) |
| GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK (dummy weights, 5 layers) | TP1, TP2, TP2+EP | Humming, FP8 GS128 (FP8 per-token before) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (BF16 before) |

These runs used the v0.32.0 release branch with #61556, and `main` with #61556 applied. With `main` alone, the Humming 0.1.16 schema check rejects the combination. EP selects `HummingGroupedExperts` and TP selects `HummingIndexedExperts`. Greedy outputs match between TP2 and TP2+EP.

GSM8K, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --temperature 0 --max-tokens 1024`, 1319 questions, 5-shot):

| Checkpoint / activations | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` BF16 | 0.956 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A16 (previous behavior) | 0.958 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A8 (this PR) | 0.961 |

Tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k mxfp4 -v  # 4 passed (H200, main)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>  # incl. mypy
```

The original commit was also validated on B300 (SM103): a layer harness loading a real `RoutedExperts` with random MXFP4 weights was bitwise equal to native `Mxfp4Config` across the default, monolithic TRTLLM, unaligned-shape, `triton_unfused`, `marlin`, `deep_gemm`, `flashinfer_cutlass` and `flashinfer_trtllm` backends. Converted DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 generated the same token ids and logprobs as the original checkpoint on 8 prompts.

## Details

**Root cause of the BF16 fallback.** For `Mxfp4MoeBackend.HUMMING`, the MoE conversion built Humming's input schema only from `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` (`TODO: read input_quant_config from quant_config`), so an unset env meant BF16. With schema fallback enabled, Humming also demotes group-scaled FP8 to A16 (`prefer wna16 for groupwise weight or groupwise input`). Output still looked correct, so the slower path went unnoticed. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` now takes an optional `activation_key`. The HUMMING conversion uses it with fallback disabled, unless the env override is set. Other backends ignore the key.

**Performance.** At the GLM-5.x expert GEMM shapes (N/K 4096/6144 and 6144/2048, 32 experts, top-8; `benchmarks/bench_humming.py` at the #61556 Humming pin), W4A8 is 1.4-1.8x faster than W4A16 for M >= 256. End to end, the small Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 is 3-8% slower with W4A8 than with W4A16 across prefill- and decode-heavy runs (hidden 2048, expert intermediate 512, so the per-layer activation quantization is not amortized). This PR follows the checkpoint's declared scheme. `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` still overrides it.

**Limitations**
- ROCm, XPU and CPU have no MXFP4 linear kernel for FP8 activations, so MXFP4 x FP8 dense layers keep the previous MXFP4-activation path there, with a warning. MI300 CI hit this; the linear test is CUDA-only.
- Blackwell: dense linears now use Humming FP8, which is slower than FlashInfer W4A4 on SM100 but matches the checkpoint. The MoE still picks its Blackwell backend without the activation key, so it uses MXFP8 or BF16 activations instead of `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` (FP8 GS128 x MXFP4). Hooking that up is left for a follow-up issue.
- The AMD, XPU, CPU and V4.1 DeepSeek model variants still need the same `ckpt_names` one-liner; untested here.
- The rename breaks the pre-processed weight cache, so `supports_pre_processed_weights` is off for this method.
- Converting DeepSeek-V4-Flash with vllm-project/compressed-tensors#902 also emits `shared_experts.w\d+` targets, while vLLM names that layer `shared_experts.down_proj`; that needs a fix in the converter or model.

**Not a duplicate:** #59376 targets the same scheme with a different design; only one should merge. #58714 adds a separate CT -> `HummingMoEMethod` route for the same checkpoints; this PR covers that path through the native MXFP4 method. #56523 and #56306 migrate the W4A4 method to the oracle and do not touch this scheme.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Support DSpark adaptive verification on MI355X
author: okorzh-amd
body:
**Requires #55504 and #56831.** Both are open, and this branch carries them as separate commits until they merge.
> - **#55504** "Preserve GDN recurrent state on zero-draft speculative decode steps". Without it, the 1-token-per-request varlen capture dummies record the non-spec KDA path, which trimmed verify batches then replay. This PR also contains the fix I'm proposing for #55504: a row is a spec-decode row only if it is no wider than k+1.
> - **#56831** "Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks". Without it, rank-local confidences can choose different draft budgets or request boundaries on different TP ranks, which leaves the collectives mismatched and can hang. Kimi-K3 runs at TP8, and trimming happens on ~97% of steps at conc ≥ 8.

### Purpose

`speculative_config.enable_adaptive_verification` (#47808) trims each verify request to 1..k+1 tokens on the device, using the DSpark confidence head. #52988 enabled it for Kimi-K3 on NVIDIA only. On ROCm, Kimi-K3 is refused at engine start:

1. `KimiK3ROCmKDABackend` inherits GDN's `is_ssm()`, so `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch()` returns `False`.
2. The ROCm KDA builder is `UNIFORM_BATCH` and declares no varlen bound.
3. `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` is `UNIFORM_BATCH` and declares no varlen bound.

This PR removes those three gates. It also fixes two bugs that showed up once adaptive verification actually ran on a hybrid model.

### Changes

**ROCm KDA** (`models/kimi_k3/amd/kda_metadata.py`)
- The backend accepts a CPU/device query-length mismatch. The spec path plans from `spec_query_start_loc` and `num_accepted_tokens` on the device.
- `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` returns k+1 under adaptive verification. The builder keeps `UNIFORM_BATCH`, because FULL capture is decode-only.
- Under adaptive verification, the builder drops the host-derived `uniform_spec_sequence_length`. The fixed-length recurrent kernel places sequence *i* at `i * L` and bakes `L` in at graph capture. Varlen graphs are captured with an even split (e.g. 2×4) and replayed with ragged batches (e.g. 1×8), so keeping it corrupts KDA state: acceptance length fell from about 3.8 to 2.0 when we kept it.

**AITER MLA** (`v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py`)

These changes apply under adaptive verification only, with DCP=1 and causal batches:
- Every decode batch runs as uniform k+1 blocks. That is the width the FULL graph's ASM kernel variant was captured at.
- Real tokens are left-aligned in their block, and the kernel's KV length is extended by the pad. Each real token keeps its exact causal window, and no row gets an empty window. Right-alignment faulted the ASM kernel (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION`) on contexts shorter than k+1.
- The appended page-list entries repeat the request's first page (`CLAMP_TAIL` in `_expand_page_indices_kernel`), so they stay in bounds.
- q is gathered into the blocks and the output is gathered back using index maps built on the device from `query_start_loc`. This adds no host sync.
- `query_len_support` becomes `VARLEN`, and `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` returns k+1.
- Causality is decided per batch, not from the group spec. Kimi-K3 DSpark draft layers share the target's MLA group, and `MLAAttentionSpec.merge` sets `non_causal_multi_token_decode` on the whole group. Non-causal draft batches keep the existing path.
- No aiter change is needed: the kernels only ever see uniform blocks.

**Adaptive-verification cost profiling** (`v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py`, `v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, `v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`)

With the default `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=8192`, profiling faulted on the second prefill-shaped dummy batch ("Write access to a read-only page"). Two causes:
- `compute_num_decode_draft_tokens` (from #55504) made every non-prefilling row without drafts a spec row, including the dummy run's 12-token rows. Those rows carry no prefill flag. The recurrent kernel then walked 12 tokens through an 8-wide state-index row. Now only rows no wider than k+1 are decode rows. Before this fix, running without the fabricated context avoided the crash but silently corrupted memory: acceptance dropped about 10% at conc 1, and recovered fully once the bug was fixed.
- `set_dummy_context` gave every KV cache group the same `arange` block ids, including the recurrent-state groups. Hybrid models back all groups with the same tensors, so KDA wrote fp32 state over blocks the MLA layers read as fp8 KV. Context blocks now count up from the first block past the null block, and state slots count down from the top of the pool.

### Dependencies

Both are required for adaptive verification to run correctly on Kimi-K3. Until they merge, this branch carries them as separate commits, and they will be dropped on rebase.

| PR | Status | Commit here | Why it is required |
|---|---|---|---|
| #55504 | open | `83f1d05dd4` (unchanged backport, original author) | Zero-draft decode rows, including the 1-token varlen capture dummies, must take the GDN/KDA spec path that applies `num_accepted_tokens`. Without it, the FULL varlen graphs record the plain decode kernel. |
| #56831 | open | `2a4a548fd6` (cherry-pick) + `7777ad03c3` (test adapted to this base's `async_tensor_h2d`) | Rank 0's draft budget and per-request capacities are broadcast, so all TP ranks build the same verify layout. |

The width check in `compute_num_decode_draft_tokens` (commit `843d1663e8`) fixes #55504 itself. I've also proposed it on #55504; if it lands there, it will drop from this PR.

### Test Plan

One new test per fix, plus the updates existing tests need:
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_adaptive_varlen_decode_correctness` (GPU, 2 cases at 16 heads). Ragged device query lengths (1..k+1) are run against an even host split and checked against an SDPA reference. The two cases are fp8 KV, and bf16 with contexts shorter than k+1 (the left-alignment case).
- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`: `test_varlen_cudagraph_bound_follows_adaptive_verification` (on/off, DCP, and a draft group that shares the target's spec) and `test_varlen_rows_left_align_each_request_in_its_block`.
- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_adaptive_verification.py`: the backend/builder opt-in, and dropping the uniform length under adaptive verification (with a control case without it).
- `tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py::test_rows_wider_than_a_verify_block_keep_the_sentinel`.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py::test_dummy_context_keeps_state_slots_apart_from_context_blocks`.
- End to end: Kimi-K3 FP4, TP8, MI355X (vLLM nightly 36768d1b plus this branch). DSpark K=7 with block (real) acceptance, adaptive verification on vs off, measured on fresh servers.

### Test Result

**Unit tests**
- All of the new tests above pass on MI355X.
- The touched files pass in full: AITER MLA mtp_split 67/67, the new KDA file, pcp manager, and mamba_hybrid model state.

The difference is the new tests from this PR, #55504 and #56831.

**Kimi-K3 end to end**

| | adaptive off (static K=7) | adaptive on |
|---|---|---|
| Startup with default 8192 profiling context | – | passes (faulted before the fix) |
| conc 1, AL @32k / @128k | 3.68–3.88 / 2.91–3.15 (2 runs) | 3.82 / 3.00 (no trimming at conc 1) |

**Not covered yet**

Today ROCm uses the NVIDIA module, which keeps it.

title: [Perf][KV Connector][Mooncake] Send the KV layout once per peer
author: staryxchen
body:
## Overview

`MooncakeConnector` now sends the decode KV layout to each prefill worker once, instead of on every pull. Later pulls carry only block ids and a `layout_id`, and decode stops attaching the layout only after prefill echoes that id back. This is the exchange-once, cache-per-peer model `NixlConnector` already uses for its handshake. Follows the packed-region work in #57952.

## Claims

- On DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4P4D (146 registered regions), each later pull is **9184 B smaller per rank**: 9500 B → 316 B at ~8k tokens. The saving is the same at 508 and 8008 tokens.
- Prefill-side control-plane time per pull drops from **0.078 ms to 0.014 ms** (steady-state P50). The absolute saving is ~0.06 ms, so **TTFT does not change** (1.10 s at ~8k tokens on both sides).
- Mixed versions stay correct in both directions. A prefill without this change never receives a layout-less pull; a decode without this change keeps today's behavior.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k (Qwen3-0.6B 1P1D; DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4P4D vs. single node).

## Validation

**Unit tests**: 123 passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
```

The environment was `uv venv --system-site-packages`, with the default test model `facebook/opt-125m`. The cu129 precompiled wheel for the base commit returned 404, so this is not a `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` install.

New tests cover:
- layout-less pulls after the echo;
- a `LAYOUT_MISS` resend;
- a prefill that never echoes (old peer);
- a reused layout arriving under a new id;
- LRU eviction.

`pre-commit` passes: `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, and `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.

**Version matrix** (Qwen2.5-0.5B, greedy, TP=1, RDMA). "Old" is `origin/main` (`4e4d75c459`). The `MooncakeXferMetadata to <addr> is N bytes (layout|blocks)` line is a DEBUG log (`VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`). These runs used an earlier revision that logged the same line once per address at INFO.

| Prefill | Decode | PP (P/D) | Decode log | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| new | new | 1/1 | `1615 B (layout)`, then `256 B (blocks)` | same output, 100% external prefix hits |
| old | new | 1/1 | `(layout)` only, never `(blocks)` | same output |
| old | new | 2/1 | `(layout)` only for both prefill addresses; no `no matching consumer` on prefill | same output |
| new | old | 1/1 | (old decode has no size log) | same output |

The old/new-PP 1/1 and new/old rows were run on the pre-rebase commit; the Mooncake code is identical. The LRU commit does not touch the code those two rows run: an old prefill never executes it, and an old decode sends `layout_id=0`, which the new prefill never stores.

**Bytes and TTFT** (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=4, EP, fp8, block 256, 4P4D on one node). Each TTFT row is 8 streamed requests with `max_tokens=1`, after warmup.

| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Metadata per pull, per rank, ~8k tokens | 9483 B every pull | 9500 B first pull, then 316 B |
| Prefill control plane, steady-state P50 / P99 | 0.078 / 0.099 ms (n=44) | 0.014 / 0.029 ms (n=24) |
| TTFT, ~8k tokens | 1.092–1.097 s | 1.096–1.099 s |

The control-plane time was measured from `send_kv_to_decode` entry to the end of region-length validation, on all 4 ranks, dropping the first pull. The timing code was temporary and is not part of this PR.

**Accuracy** (gsm8k, `exact_match,strict-match`, 1319 questions).

| Setup | Score |
|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B 1P1D, `tests/v1/kv_connector/mooncake_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh` | 0.422 (expected 0.41 ± 0.05) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4P4D | 0.951 (1255/1319) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash single node, TP=4, same eager / fp8 / `max_num_seqs=8` | 0.951 (1254/1319) |

Both P/D runs had 100% external prefix hits and 0 failed transfers.

**Not covered end to end.** Prefill side-channel ports come from `bind_to_random_port`, and decode RPC ports from the transfer engine, so a restarted peer always comes back at a new address. Three paths therefore have unit coverage only:
- the `LAYOUT_MISS` resend;
- the same address reusing a layout under a new id;
- LRU eviction followed by a resend.

Prefill and decode restarts were run end to end; they re-sent the layout to the new address, with unchanged output.

## Details

**Why.** Every pull sends the whole registered layout in `MooncakeXferMetadata`: base addresses, block lengths, layer names, group ids and row offsets. On a 146-region model that is ~9 KB per rank per pull, mostly layer names. Prefill then builds and hashes a tuple of all of it on every batch, just to hit `_prepared_transfer_regions`. Both costs grow with the number of registered regions, not with the request.

**Prior art: `NixlConnector`.** NIXL already exchanges the KV layout once per remote engine and keeps the per-request message small:

| | `NixlConnector` (pull mode) | `MooncakeConnector`, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Data direction | Decode reads from prefill, so **decode** caches the prefill layout | Prefill writes into decode, so **prefill** caches the decode layout |
| When the layout is exchanged | Once per remote engine, in `_ensure_handshake`; concurrent requests to the same engine share one handshake future | Once per decode worker address, piggybacked on the first pull |
| Where it is cached | `add_remote_agent` stores `kv_caches_base_addr[engine_id][tp_rank]`, block lengths, and region metadata | `_layout_by_peer`, keyed by decode host, port, ranks, and `layout_id` |
| Per-request message | `RemoteMeta`: block ids, host, port, `engine_id`, request id | `req_blocks` and `layout_id` |
| How a new layout is detected | The cache is keyed by `engine_id`; a restarted engine has a new id and is handshaken anew, and the replaced engine is cleaned up (`_track_remote_engine_replacement`) | Each `register_kv_caches` mints a new `layout_id`; an unknown id gets `LAYOUT_MISS` and a resend |

Mooncake has no separate handshake round trip; decode simply sends its pull to the prefill side channel. So instead of adding a handshake, this PR makes the first pull carry the layout. Prefill's echo of `layout_id` then plays the part of NIXL's handshake response: decode treats the layout as delivered only after it sees the echo, so a peer that never echoes keeps getting the full layout. NIXL's compatibility hash (`NixlHandshakePayload.compatibility_hash`) is out of scope here.

**Protocol.**
- `register_kv_caches` draws a random nonzero 63-bit `layout_id`. A counter would restart at 1 in every process, so a restarted decode at the same address could match a stale prefill entry and be written with the old layout.
- Prefill stores aligned regions by `(decode host, port, tp_rank, pp_size, tp_size, layout_id)`. It stores them on both a fresh alignment and a `_prepared_transfer_regions` hit. A hit can carry a new id for a layout prefill has already seen.
- Prefill echoes `layout_id` in `MooncakeXferResponse` once it holds that layout. Decode omits the layout for a worker address only after seeing the echo.
  - A plain `FINISH` is not enough. A prefill without this change ignores the new field and answers `FINISH`. With equal PP it would then reject every layout-less pull. With different PP, `allow_partial_layers` would align zero regions, transfer nothing, and report success.
- A layout-less pull whose id prefill does not hold gets the new `LAYOUT_MISS` status. Decode resends with the layout once; a second miss fails the request normally. Only layout-less pulls can receive `LAYOUT_MISS`, and only a new decode sends those, so an old decode never sees the new enum value.
- `_layout_by_peer` is an LRU capped at 1024 entries, because every decode re-registration mints a new id. Eviction is always safe: the evicted decode gets `LAYOUT_MISS` and resends.

**Tradeoff.** About 130 net lines in the connector, for ~9 KB and ~0.06 ms per pull, with no TTFT change on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The case for the change is that this overhead is fixed per pull and grows with the region count and layer-name length, so it grows with deeper and multi-cache models. It is not a latency win at today's scale.

**Limitations (pre-existing, unchanged here).**
- `_prepared_transfer_regions` is still unbounded. Its key includes decode base addresses, so it grows on every decode restart. Its entries could take the same LRU in a follow-up.
- After a prefill restart, the proxy must be restarted too. Otherwise decode keeps the old `engine_id` and requests stall instead of failing.
- A pull with empty `req_blocks` gets no response.

**Related PRs.**
- #59592 adds `remote_block_size` to `MooncakeXferMetadata`, in code this PR moves into `_build_pull_metadata`. Whichever lands second should set it on both full and layout-less pulls.
- #59625 (draft, sleep mode over RDMA) re-registers KV caches on wake-up. Here that mints a new `layout_id` and clears the caches, so a woken peer re-sends or re-receives the layout. That PR also restructures `send_kv_to_decode`, so expect a textual conflict.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR sends the Mooncake layout once or caches it per peer. Searched `mooncake layout`, `mooncake handshake` and `mooncake metadata` with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search ...`.

**AI assistance.** This PR was written with AI assistance (Cursor). I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

---

title: [Bugfix][DeepEP] Upgrade to 2.1 and retain per-context GIN completion ordering
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Upgrade vendored DeepEP to 2.1 (`a56d6156febcd9976e55adc85b5155bfac9f28f8`), which includes the upstream NVLink visibility fix, and retain a smaller patch for per-context GIN completion signaling.

## Claims

- Use upstream flush, NVLink fence, and grid synchronization placement; remove the custom deferred-flush implementation. Completion signals cover every allocated context, while arrival-only barriers use context 0.
- Retain the nine-context allocation for vLLM's direct-mode MoE buffers, matching automatic active-QP selection. Hybrid allocation stays automatic.
- Preserve skipped/already-applied/failed patch diagnostics requested in review, including aborting on failed application. Add the NCCL library search path required by DeepEP 2.1's SONAME linking and document runtime-version requirements.

## Validation

**Current revision: build and offline checks pass. Distributed correctness, model execution, and overhead remain unvalidated on this revision.** GPU attempts were blocked by unavailable capacity and RDMA device admission failures (`no healthy devices present ... rdma/ib`); these are infrastructure failures, not correctness results. Earlier performance numbers do not apply to this upgrade, so this description makes no overhead claim.

| Current-revision check | Result |
|---|---|
| Fresh native wheels, CUDA 13 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130 / SM90 | Built against NCCL 2.30.7 and 2.31.2 |
| Patched world/rail barrier templates, completion and arrival variants | Compiled with nvcc against both NCCL versions |
| Linux patch application, byte-exact header, complete reverse dry-run | Passed; patched header SHA256 `1bc42abd841cc6e9ba6c59b68962d7e260e163a750873bd50633f91e89d0979f` |
| Native import and loaded-NCCL provenance | Passed on two H200 workers with NCCL 2.30.7; distributed operation did not start |
| Installer behavior | Seven paths passed: fresh, already applied, partial, wrong ref, broken patch, missing patch, other project |
| NCCL linker-path selection | Passed for explicit EP root, legacy root, pip metadata, missing installation |
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks | Passed |

Build checks used `uv build --wheel --no-build-isolation` with `EP_NUM_TOPK_IDX_BITS=64`, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0`, and explicit matching NCCL roots. Patch checks used `patch --batch -p1` and `patch --batch --force --reverse --dry-run -p1`. Local validation artifacts retain the source, wheel, NCCL, and resulting-header hashes.

```bash
pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile docker/versions.json \
  docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md \
  tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh \
  tools/ep_kernels/patches/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch
```

Before merge, rerun matched EP8 direct-mode stock/patched correctness at 9/17 contexts, representative direct/hybrid operator timings, and the original vLLM model reproducer on this revision. Ordinary CI does not cover the three-node H200/GDAKI reproducer.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence on the previous DeepEP pin — not validation of this upgrade</summary>

The previous `d4f41e4e` implementation at PR commit `c781de2f82` passed the original DeepSeek-V4-Flash reproducer: DP8/TP1/EP, three H200 nodes (4+2+2), NCCL 2.30.7, direct `deepep_v2`, eager execution. Six rounds of 64 requests completed (384/384); all eight audit ranks saved checkpoints and all three servers exited 0, with no count/slot mismatches, barrier timeouts, or illegal memory accesses. The audit run was not a serving-performance comparison.

The old pristine pin and per-context-only variant had previously faulted. Subsequent isolated controls also reproduced old-pin correctness failures before graph capture/profiling. These results concern the old pin with direct mode explicitly forced; they do not establish that default hybrid deployments are affected or that stock DeepEP 2.1 fails.

</details>

## Details

GIN ordering is per context ([NVIDIA/nccl#2302](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/2302)); a completion signal on context 0 alone does not supply ordering for puts on other contexts. The selected upstream revision already contains the NVLink visibility fence from [DeepEP#715](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/715). The remaining vendor patch signals and waits on each context at data completion, retaining upstream flush/fence placement and adding context information to timeout diagnostics.

The pin also includes runtime-sized NCCL DevComm compatibility and strict-ordering window registration. Builds against NCCL <2.31 require the same runtime NCCL version. Both tested NCCL configurations used rebuilt native extensions. The constructor/combine signatures are unchanged, and dispatch's new optional argument is compatible with vLLM's keyword calls. DeepEP 2.5 removes the ElasticBuffer and legacy APIs used by vLLM, so that broader migration is outside this fix.

This updates the existing PR rather than creating a duplicate. AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation, validation, and this description. The human submitter must review all changed lines and the validation evidence.

title: [Feature][PCP] Add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash support
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Overview

Add text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) support on NVIDIA CUDA to Model Runner V2 with FlashMLA sparse attention.

This PR intentionally targets a colocated single-model instance only. P/D disaggregation and KV transfer are not supported in this initial scope. The implementation keeps compressed KV, indexer, SWA, Engram lookback, MoE routing inputs, and padding consistent across PCP ranks while closing ratio-2 pairs split across PCP chunks with gathered predecessor rows.

Related to #25749 and #49109. This PR targets the DeepSeek-V4.1 ratio-1/2 cache path and does not add the V4 C4/C128 or MegaMoE work from #43809.

## Supported Scope

- NVIDIA CUDA only: text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Model Runner V2 with `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`.
- One colocated model instance with PP=DP=DCP=1.
- Prefill PCP with arbitrary PCP chunk boundaries, including ranks with no local decode requests.
- Tensor parallelism and PCP can be composed; the validation below covers TP8/PCP1, TP4/PCP2, and TP2/PCP4 on an 8-GPU node.
- Expert parallel execution with the `allgather_reducescatter` all-to-all backend.
- Eager execution with synchronous scheduling.

## Not Supported Yet

- P/D disaggregation or any KV connector.
- ROCm.
- Pipeline parallelism, data parallelism, decode context parallelism, or microbatching with PCP.
- Prefix caching or SWA bounded replay with PCP.
- Speculative decoding, CUDA graphs, or MegaMoE with PCP.
- Multimodal inputs, encoder-decoder models, or LoRA with PCP.
- Attention backends other than the DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashMLA sparse path.

These constraints are deliberate so the first upstream step establishes standalone PCP correctness without mixing in KV handoff or replay semantics. Follow-up work will expand one boundary at a time: first standalone cache/replay behavior, then additional single-instance parallel topologies and runtime features, and finally P/D disaggregation with a minimal direct connector before layering prefix caching, bounded replay, and speculative Decode support.

## Implementation

- Compress ratio-2 groups on each rank's local token rows. Gather only the last FP32 row of each local chunk to close cross-rank pairs and keep the open ring rows consistent.
- Keep PCP linkage in model-specific compressor metadata; `InputBatch` and `PCPManager` remain unchanged relative to `main`.
- Gather BF16 compressor latents in one cache-insert path shared with ratio 1, then use the aligned gathered positions and slots for main KV and Indexer K writes.
- Keep Engram lookback, MoE routing token IDs, padding, compressed KV, indexer keys, and SWA metadata aligned across PCP ranks.
- Keep PCP collectives ordered consistently across ranks, including empty local shards and requests with no local decode rows.

Engram embeddings remain TP-sharded, so increasing PCP can increase host memory requirements.

## Rank-local Compressor Revision

Following LucasWilkinson's review, this revision adopts [wangyicong52/vllm#1](https://github.com/wangyicong52/vllm/pull/1), authored by Lucas Wilkinson, at `b06bea7abc4eb5cf6965fe704d16257ac7c70697`. It removes the `InputBatch.pcp_metadata` / `PCPBatchMetadata` plumbing and the global FP32 `kv_score` gather.

Local validation of this revision: 101 passed, 6 CUDA-only skipped; applicable pre-commit hooks, mypy 3.10/3.12, syntax and diff checks passed. Additional CPU regressions cover PCP2/4 predecessor linkage, replicated short prefills, empty ranks, request isolation and newest open ring rows.

The GPU/model measurements below belong to the preceding global-order compressor implementation. They have not been rerun for this revision. The rank-local kernel, GSM8K and Prefill benchmark require renewed validation on the target H20 configuration before these historical results can support claims about this version.

## Validation Environment

- Hardware: one node with 8x NVIDIA H20 (96G, SM90) GPUs.
- SM100 was not validated in this PR.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691`.

## vLLM Launch Arguments

Only the TP/PCP pair changed across the accuracy arms: `TP_SIZE=8, PCP_SIZE=1` for TP8/PCP1, `TP_SIZE=4, PCP_SIZE=2` for TP4/PCP2, and `TP_SIZE=2, PCP_SIZE=4` for TP2/PCP4. PP, DP, and DCP remained 1.

```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}" \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size "${PCP_SIZE}" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

## Validation

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://<HOST>:18001/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-hub modelscope \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":4}}' \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-batch-size 64 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"max_tokens":65536,"reasoning_effort":"high","seed":42,"timeout":10000}' \
  --timeout 10000
```

EvalScope's GSM8K report exposes extracted-answer `accuracy` and per-request `avg_output_tps`; it does not report separate exact-match or flexible-match metrics.

| Topology | Correct | Accuracy | Avg output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8/PCP1 baseline | 1281/1319 | 97.1190% | 7.36 |
| TP4/PCP2 | 1282/1319 | 97.1948% | 7.04 |
| TP2/PCP4 | 1284/1319 | 97.3465% | 7.10 |

The Prefill benchmark used `vllm bench serve` with exact-length random prompts, one output token, seed 42, prefix caching disabled, one warmup wave, and four measured waves. Results below include input tok/s and mean TTFT in milliseconds; values in parentheses are changes relative to the TP8/PCP1 baseline.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Count heartbeats as remote engine activity
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

`_send_heartbeats` does not stamp `_engine_last_active`, so a decode instance that holds requests waiting on a prefill engine evicts that engine once `engine_ttl` passes, and the same heartbeat starts a new handshake that reloads every remote agent. This stamps the engine when a heartbeat is sent to it.

Fixes #59871

## Claims

- An engine that this instance is heartbeating is no longer evicted by `_evict_stale_engines`, so heartbeats stop causing an evict-and-handshake cycle every `engine_ttl`.
- Engines with no reads and no heartbeats are still evicted after `engine_ttl`, unchanged.

## Validation

New test `test_heartbeated_engine_is_not_evicted` sends a heartbeat every 5 s for twice the TTL with no reads, and checks that the engine stays registered, no remote agent is removed and no handshake is submitted.

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_heartbeated_engine_is_not_evicted
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `1 failed`: `AssertionError: assert 'remote-engine-1' in defaultdict(<class 'dict'>, {})` |
| this PR | `1 passed` |

NIXL unit files (`test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_nixl_heartbeat.py`, `test_nixl_push_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_handshake_pp_aggregation.py`, `test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `3 failed, 609 passed` |
| this PR | `3 failed, 610 passed` |

The 3 failures are the same on both and come from the CPU-only test machine: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]` and `[None]` (no `torch.ops._C.init_cpu_memory_env`, no Ray on CPU) and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` (gated model, run with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`). Runs were on macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and the manual-stage `mypy-3.12` hook pass.

End-to-end on GPUs. Rig: upstream `main` CI image for `5f30fc7031` (`0.30.1rc1.dev619+g5f30fc703`), NIXL 1.4.1 installed as CI does, bundled UCX 1.22.0, `UCX_TLS=rc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc` over 8 ConnectX RoCE HCAs per node, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B TP1, prefill engines on one H100 node and the decode on another. The change is applied as an overlay of the installed package. Decode with `engine_ttl: 60` and `--max-num-seqs 1`; a 14,000-token request from prefill 2 holds the decode while a request from prefill 1 waits behind it for about 150 s:

| | Handshakes on the decode while the request waits | Decode EngineCore `VmPin` | Requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 2 -> 3 -> 4 (prefill 1 evicted and re-handshaked every ~62 s) | +2,560 KiB per re-handshake | both complete |
| this PR | 2 -> 2 | flat | both complete |

Accuracy, `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_accuracy.py` (gsm8k, P/D through `toy_proxy_server.py`, expected 0.41): `main` 0.4147, this change together with the other two NIXL fixes from the same investigation 0.4139. Both pass.

## Details

Root cause: `_engine_last_active` is stamped at handshake completion (`base_worker.py:1336` on `main`) and when a read is issued (`pull_worker.py:156`). A request queued on the decode side is heartbeated from `on_new_request` until `finished_recving` or abort, and it issues no read until it is scheduled. When `engine_ttl` passes, the heartbeat's `_ensure_handshake` call runs `_evict_stale_engines` first, evicts the engine it is about to heartbeat, finds it missing and submits a handshake.

Why it matters: each reload runs `remove_remote_agent` and `loadRemoteMD` for every remote rank. On a deployment with TP2 decode and PCP8 prefill (8 remote agents per engine per worker), each full re-handshake left 476-481 64 KiB UCX buffers (about 960 VMAs) per worker, which is a separate NIXL/UCX issue. A decode rank that could not admit work kept requests waiting for tens of minutes at a time. It ran about 6 handshakes per hour against about 1 per hour on healthy ranks, and it hit `vm.max_map_count` after about 31 hours. This change removes the heartbeat-driven part of that churn. An engine that is idle with nothing waiting on it is still evicted, and it is handshaked again when new work arrives, which is the intended TTL behavior.

The stamp sits after the pending-handshake `continue`, so it runs only when `_ensure_handshake` returned `None`, which means the engine is in `_remote_agents`. That keeps the invariant #52245 relies on: no `_engine_last_active` entry without a `_remote_agents` entry, since `_cleanup_remote_engine` asserts it.

Tradeoff: a dead prefill engine stays registered while requests still wait on it. Those requests fail their reads, which stops the heartbeat, and #50047 releases a replaced peer without waiting for the TTL.

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR or issue matched `nixl heartbeat`, `engine_ttl`, `engine ttl evict`, `nixl heartbeat engine_ttl`, `engine_ttl heartbeat`, `stale remote engine` or `nixl re-handshake` for this mechanism. Closest precedents are #52245 (same stamp for the push-mode D side) and #54689 (eviction skips engines with in-flight reads).

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Release shared memory on NIXL setup failure
author: DGlan
body:
## Overview

Prevent leaked shared memory when ECCPU scheduler initialization fails with NIXL enabled. The constructor currently raises without releasing the region it has already allocated.

## Claims

- Failed NIXL setup releases the scheduler-owned mmap file, file descriptors, and mapping while preserving the original exception.

## Validation

Review validation with NIXL 1.4.1: the previous constructor test file reproduced the test-order failure (6 passed, 1 failed); importing `data.nixl` before monkeypatching fixes its cached bindings, and all 7 constructor tests pass together. The suites below were rerun after merging upstream main.

The missing-NIXL regression fails against the unchanged scheduler because the mmap file remains, and passes with this fix. A second CPU regression raises during control-transport creation after data transport setup, and checks deregistration, shared-region release, and preservation of the original exception.

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/scheduler \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/test_ec_shared_region.py -q
# 76 passed (NIXL 1.4.1 installed)

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -m cpu_test tests/v1/ec_connector/unit -q
# 62 passed, 350 deselected

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/scheduler/__init__.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.
```


Nearby transport/session/scheduler tests also passed (95 tests):

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_data.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_session.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_control.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_consumer.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_producer.py -q
```

A separate CPU check exercised `ECConnectorFactory` through `ECCPUConnector` using real `VllmConfig`/`ModelConfig` objects and a local tiny Llava configuration, without replacing the shared-memory factory. The unchanged scheduler left the file, two file descriptors, and a mapping after the missing-NIXL error; the fixed scheduler left none, with the same error. Descriptors and mappings were checked through `/proc/self/fd` and `/proc/self/maps`.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cpu, editable source with official v0.30.0 CPU precompiled binaries. Exact-commit CPU binaries were unavailable. NIXL 1.4.1 was installed for this review revision, and the constructor wiring test exercised real NIXL registration and ZMQ session startup. Full GPU serving and cross-process NIXL data transfer were not run; local validation covers scheduler construction and startup-failure cleanup. The new test is selected by the existing CPU EC connector job in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

The region is allocated before `_setup_nixl`; if setup raises, the caller never receives a scheduler to shut down. The constructor owns failure unwinding through `shutdown()`, releasing NIXL resources before the shared region. `_setup_nixl()` propagates errors without a second cleanup handler.

Related: #56507, #56508. The related test/doc PR covers import isolation and documentation, rather than constructor cleanup. Searches for EC scheduler cleanup, NIXL initialization, and shared-memory leaks found no equivalent open PR.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the patch and this review revision, and ran the validation above. The submitting human reviewed the original patch, personally reran its 74-pass/1-skip suite, and authorized this revision to address the review. No inference-output or performance change is claimed.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix speculative block reservations across KV cache groups
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix speculative decode block reservations for asynchronous KV loads with
multiple KV cache groups. Under KV memory pressure, under-reserving these
blocks can leave a request admitted for an asynchronous KV load but unable
to start decoding once the load completes.

## Claims

- Account for every KV cache group using its actual allocation block size.
- Extend the existing promotion-margin regression test to cover single-group,
  multi-group, and mixed-block-size configurations.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

**32 passed.** Pre-commit checks and manual Python 3.12 mypy passed.

Regression controls replace only the reservation method in the test process:

| Implementation | Single group | Multiple groups | Different block sizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original | Pass | Fail | Fail |
| Original × group count | Pass | Pass | Fail |
| This fix | Pass | Pass | Pass |

The broader scheduler/decode/recovery run showed no additional failures:
both the patched implementation and the original reservation method produced
171 passes and the same 46 failing test IDs. Observed environment limitations
included unavailable offline model configurations and insufficient visible
GPUs for parallel tests.

Validation exercises the scheduler and KV allocation paths with simulated
remote completion. Live NIXL P/D and model-level evaluations were not run.

## Details

The existing calculation converts the speculative token margin to blocks
using the scheduler block size once. However, each KV cache group allocates
independently from the shared block pool, and groups may use different
allocation block sizes.

Sum the reservation across cache managers using each manager's block size.
Simply multiplying the old result by the group count is insufficient for
mixed-block-size configurations. The existing conservative reservation
approach is preserved.

The regression test checks admission and subsequent scheduling rather than
asserting the helper's arithmetic directly.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmarks] Name the real cause when the /tokenize alignment probe fails
author: TyroneNel
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`vllm bench serve` aligns `random` / `prefix_repetition` prompts to the server tokenizer through a `/tokenize` probe. Every failure of that probe prints `WARNING: /tokenize unavailable, skipping alignment.`, even when the route exists. This PR names the actual cause instead.

Replaces #58024 (closed when my fork was re-created). Related: #59889 is the server side of the same 404.

## Claims

- A failed probe names its cause: 404 (no route, or `--model` is not a served name), another HTTP status, an unreachable host, or the exception.
- Alignment behavior is unchanged: a failure still skips alignment and never stops the run, and a tokenizer mismatch still re-aligns the prompts.

## Validation

The patched `_align_prompts_to_server_tokenizer` against a local `aiohttp` server for each case (no GPU or model needed):

| Server | Output |
|---|---|
| 404 | ``/tokenize unavailable (404 Not Found: either this server has no /tokenize route, or it does not serve a model named `my-model` (its served names are listed by GET /v1/models))`` |
| 500 | `/tokenize unavailable (HTTP 500)` |
| nothing listening | `http://127.0.0.1:18902 unreachable (ClientConnectorError(... ConnectionRefusedError ...))` |
| tokenizer mismatch (server 6 tokens, local 3) | `tokenizer mismatch (server=6, expected=3), re-aligning prompts.`, then prompt `'a b c'`, `prompt_len=3` |

The 404 on a live server (`--model /models/x --served-model-name my-model`):

```
POST /tokenize {"model":"my-model"}   -> 200
POST /tokenize {"model":"/models/x"}  -> 404 The model `/models/x` does not exist.
```

**Live run on upstream main** (RTX 3090, at the main merge-base `84bcbc626`). The server is `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --api-key test-key`. The client is the same checkout, with the `serve.py` from main or from this PR. All runs use `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 16 --num-prompts 20 --ignore-eos --seed 0` against the same server:

| client | `--model` / `--tokenizer` | probe output | ok / failed | Total input tokens | server `prompt_tokens_total` Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `gpt2` | `tokenizer mismatch (server=696, expected=512), re-aligning prompts.` | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| this PR | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `gpt2` | `tokenizer mismatch (server=696, expected=512), re-aligning prompts.` | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| this PR | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | (no probe line) | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| main | `not-a-served-model` / `gpt2` | `/tokenize unavailable, skipping alignment.` | 0 / 20 | 0 | 0 |
| this PR | `not-a-served-model` / `gpt2` | ``/tokenize unavailable (404 Not Found: either this server has no /tokenize route, or it does not serve a model named `not-a-served-model` (its served names are listed by GET /v1/models)), skipping alignment.`` | 0 / 20 | 0 | 0 |

- Tokenizer mismatch: the server reads the 512 gpt2-token prompt as 696 tokens. After re-alignment, the server counts 10,240 prompt tokens for the 20 requests (512 on average), with and without this PR. I checked the totals, not each request.
- Auth: on this server, `POST /tokenize` without a key returned 200, and `GET /v1/models` without a key returned 401.

`pre-commit` passes. No unit test is added; the harness above can go into `tests/benchmarks/` if you want it in CI.

## Details

**Root cause.** The probe sends `args.model` as the request `model` and catches every exception into one message. With `--served-model-name`, the model check answers 404, which reads as "no `/tokenize` route".

**Review changes.** An earlier revision also sent `OPENAI_API_KEY` with the probe. It is removed: `--api-key` does not guard `/tokenize` on vLLM, and it overrode a lowercase `authorization` passed with `--header`.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Trim the last KV-source layer in decoder replay
author: gcanlin
body:
## Purpose

In decoder replay steps, the last KV-source layer (layer 20 on DSV4.1-Flash) still ran on every row, though for the trimmed rows only its KV (SWA, compressed, index K) is read. Its indexer scoring and top-k, sparse MLA, wo and MoE feed only the replay layers.

- The cut layer now writes its KV for every row (`DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.write_kv` → `DeepseekV4Attention.forward_kv`), then runs as the first replay layer (`decoder_replay_start = cut`) on the replay rows, in the replay batch and its CUDA graphs. Its sliding-window metadata keeps the batch's window starts, so it stays exact. The indexer row-buffer compaction goes.
- PIECEWISE graphs now decide the replay break (and `write_kv`) by graph size (`DecoderReplayLayers.replays()`) instead of `replay_batch is not None`, which is unset at capture: before, the break was never captured and PIECEWISE steps did not trim.

## Results

DSV4.1-Flash DEP4 on B200, CUDA graphs up to 8192 tokens, `vllm bench serve` random. Baseline: #59532 with PIECEWISE trimming working, layer 20 not cut.

| | baseline | this PR | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8k in / 1 out, C16, total tok/s | 236,952 | 245,556 | +3.6% |
| 32k in / 1 out, C16 | 235,791 | 245,996 | +4.3% |
| 128k in / 1 out, C4 | 194,012 | 204,764 | +5.5% |
| 32k in / 256 out, C32, output tok/s | 1,281 | 1,303 | +1.7% |

GSM8K 5-shot: 0.9606 both.

AgentX C128 (InferenceX DEP4 recipe, synthetic AL 3.51, 3,600 s), nightly 43b4aaea + this PR vs. the InferenceX CI run ([37070984585](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/37070984585), dev image ac9126):

| TTFT mean / p50 / p99 (ms) | 293 / 163 / 2,558 | 255 / 155 / 2,004 | |
| ITL mean / p50 / p99 (ms) | 8.66 / 7.60 / 29.3 | 8.21 / 7.36 / 24.0 | |
| per-user output tok/s | 132.0 | 136.6 | +3.5% |
| requests completed | 18,804 | 19,572 | +4.1% |
