title: [Bugfix] Drop enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce from FlashInfer CuteDSL MegaMoE config
author: wangshangsam
body:
## Overview Fixes #59887. `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` (added in #54049) passes `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` to FlashInfer's CuTeDSL MegaMoE config. The pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 calls that field `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, so the backend raises `TypeError` while the layer is built. This PR drops the kwarg and adds a regression test that doesn't need SM100. `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` is unaffected. ## Claims - With the pinned `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` no longer raises `TypeError` when the layer is built. Behavior is as intended: `False` is the field's default in every FlashInfer release from v0.7.0 through v0.7.1. - The fix doesn't depend on the FlashInfer version: 0.7.1 (released 2026-10-09; #60948 bumps the pin) renames the field but keeps its `False` default, and the new test passes against 0.7.1's config types (constructor check only; the backend itself was not run on 0.7.1). With 0.7.1, `main`'s current kwarg becomes valid too; this PR keeps 0.7.0.x working and adds the drift test. - On 4× GB200 at current `main`, with `nvshmem4py` installed and #61041's decoder-replay fix copied in, the backend serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with default CUDA graphs (FULL and PIECEWISE captured). GSM8K is 0.891 (one run), vs 0.901 for `deep_gemm_mega_moe` and 0.910 for the default MoE backend on the same image. - New test `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer`: it builds the adapter against the installed FlashInfer's real config types, without SM100 or multiple GPUs (it also passes with no GPU visible). It lives in `tests/kernels/moe`, which the L4 `kernels-moe-test` job runs; no Buildkite job has run on this PR yet. - **What it catches:** a renamed or removed kwarg in FlashInfer's MoE-EP config types, or removal of the deprecated `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`/`DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig` aliases. Before, these only failed at model load on SM100. - **What it doesn't cover:** `MoEEpTensors` and the megakernel layer's own methods. Only the SM100 e2e test covers those. ## Validation ### Retest at current `main` (3c062d391d) `main` was merged into this branch (no conflicts); the PR still changes only `flashinfer_moe_ep.py` (the kwarg) and its test. All runs were on 4× GB200 (docker, with the Slurm job's IMEX channel) in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:f853a683…`, built from 7d0b4e57aa. That image's `flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and `vllm/config/kernel.py` are identical to `main`'s. - **base:** the image as is. - **fix:** the image with this PR's `flashinfer_moe_ep.py` copied over the installed one. - Tests ran from this branch's `tests/` tree. The CuTeDSL path also needs `nvshmem4py` (#59903, installed by #59912), so `nvshmem4py-cu13` (0.4.0) was installed in the container. | Check | base | fix | |---|---|---| | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer` | `[cutedsl]` ❌ `TypeError: Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce'`; `[deep_gemm]` ✅ | ✅ 2/2; also 2/2 with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=` | | Same, with `flashinfer-python==0.7.1` installed (constructor check only; run with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`, and with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1` because the image's `flashinfer-cubin` is 0.7.0.post1) | ✅ 2/2 | ✅ 2/2 | | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k "test_init_warmup and cutedsl"` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | ❌ same `TypeError` (ran the 2-GPU dsv4-flash case) | ✅ 8/8, run twice | | DEP=4 serve, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, default CUDA graphs | all 4 DP ranks raise the same `TypeError` right after the checkpoint loads; the server exits about 2 minutes in | serves (FULL and PIECEWISE graphs captured); answers correct; GSM8K **0.891** | - **Serve command:** `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` (revision `2cba9e42`, pre-downloaded; containers run with `--ipc=host` so the DP replicas share the Engram tables through `/dev/shm`). Startup takes about 10 minutes, which can exceed the default 600 s engine-ready timeout. - **GSM8K:** `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 128`, one run. For reference, on the same image the default MoE backend scored 0.910 and `deep_gemm_mega_moe` 0.901 (#61041's validation). One run's standard error is about 0.008 (about 0.012 for a two-run difference), so the gap to the default is about 1.6 SE; other runs of this backend scored 0.888–0.899 (#59912's retest, #61041). The fix run also had #61041's one-file decoder-replay fix copied in: without it, every FlashInfer MegaMoE backend crashes under GSM8K load on current `main` (#61040), independent of this PR. - **Also covered:** #59912's retest, on images built from `main` c41b2639e2 + #59912 + this PR, passed the kwargs test (2/2) and the CuTeDSL e2e tests (8/8) on GB200, GB300 and B200, and, with the same decoder-replay fix, served DEP=4/8/16 with GSM8K 0.888–0.897. - **pre-commit:** `pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/flashinfer_moe_ep.py` passes. - **pytest:** run from `tests/` with `-v -rs --timeout=900`.
Earlier validation (at 7712663, on main 84bcbc6264; locally built images) All runs were on 4× GB200. Images were built from `docker/Dockerfile` with the arm64 CI build args, with these deviations: `torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0`, no sccache, `RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false`, local `max_jobs`/`nvcc_threads`, and an added `vllm-openai` target. **fix** from this branch at 7712663 (35b3ca5 only edits a comment and docstrings), **base** from `main` @ 84bcbc6264. | Test | base (main) | fix | |---|---|---| | `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[cutedsl]` | ❌ `TypeError: Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce'` | ✅ | | `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[deep_gemm]` | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs[*-cutedsl-*]` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | ❌ same `TypeError` in every worker | ✅ 8/8 (one case hung once and passed on retry) | Serving DEP=4: base, with the default cudagraph mode, crashed on every DP rank with the `TypeError` before graph capture. Fix, with `--compilation-config.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (full-graph capture failed in that environment), served, answered correctly, and scored GSM8K 0.898 (`flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`) vs 0.901 for the default backend with the same flag. `nvshmem4py-cu13==0.4.0` was installed in a test-only layer, and containers got the Slurm job's IMEX channel (without it NVSHMEM's fabric `cuMemCreate` fails with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`).
## Details **Root cause.** FlashInfer renamed `in_kernel_fc2_reduce` to `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4604, first shipped in v0.7.1rc1 and now in v0.7.1. The adapter was written against the new name while vLLM still pins 0.7.0.post1 (`requirements/cuda.txt`). Every other kwarg and method the adapter uses on FlashInfer's MoE-EP types is present in both 0.7.0.post1 and 0.7.1, so this was the only mismatch. **Why CI missed it.** The only test that constructs the adapter, `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs`, needs SM100 and 2+ GPUs. `kernels-moe-test` runs on L4, so it always skips there, and no B200 job runs this file. The new test fakes four things: - `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpMegaLayer`, which allocates symmetric memory; - the EP group; - the device index; - `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer`, which imports DeepGEMM. Everything FlashInfer receives is its own config dataclasses plus a real `MoEWeightPack`. **Relation to #60948 (FlashInfer 0.7.1).** #60948 bumps the pin to 0.7.1 and doesn't touch `flashinfer_moe_ep.py`; the two PRs don't conflict and pass in either order. After #60948, `main`'s explicit `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce=False` would be valid; dropping it still gives the same `False` default (0.7.1 documents the flag as an opt-in to nondeterministic accumulation), keeps the backend working on 0.7.0.x, and the new test guards both versions. **Alternatives considered.** *Version-gate the kwarg name:* unnecessary, since the value equals the default. **Related, found while validating.** - **`nvshmem4py` packaging:** vLLM's images don't ship `nvshmem4py`, so without it `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` fails at FlashInfer's runtime bootstrap. Tracked in #59903, fixed by #59912. - **Decoder replay under load:** on current `main`, DeepSeek-V4.1 with either FlashInfer MegaMoE backend crashes under GSM8K load in the decoder-replay CUDA graph. Tracked in #61040, fixed by #61041. - **Earlier limitations that no longer reproduce at current `main`:** full CUDA-graph capture with this backend (FULL graphs captured above), and the DeepGEMM "type Runtime is already registered" import error (#59904; the vendored DeepGEMM moved to `TORCH_LIBRARY` in #48962). The one-off 2-GPU e2e hang did not recur in 16 cases. - The adapter still imports FlashInfer's deprecated `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`/`DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig` aliases, which FlashInfer has scheduled for removal. Switching to the `Sm100_*` names is a follow-up; the new test would flag the removal. **Duplicate check.** Apart from #59887, which I filed for this bug, no open or closed issue or PR mentions `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` or `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig` as a fix for it. #60948 (FlashInfer 0.7.1 bump) makes `main`'s kwarg valid but leaves 0.7.0.x broken and adds no test. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Exchange packed FP8 Engram rows across DP and feed wkv MXFP8
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables are already MXFP8 (FP8 rows with one ue8m0 scale per 32 values) and `wkv` is an MXFP8 GEMM, but the lookup dequantizes each row to BF16, DP replicas all-gather those 512-byte rows layer by layer, and `wkv` quantizes them right back. This PR keeps rows packed from the host table to `wkv`.

- **Packed rows, direct MXFP8.** The lookup copies each row's 256 FP8 bytes and 8 scale bytes as they are, and one unpack kernel writes them in FlashInfer's MXFP8 activation layout (F8_128x4 scales). `wkv` takes them as a `QuantizedActivation`, so both the dequant and the requant are gone, and the output is bit-identical.
- **One all-to-all per prefill step.** `EngramBatch` looks up every local Engram layer into one packed buffer and exchanges it with a single all-to-all, which sends each rank only its own tokens (264 instead of 512 bytes per head row, 1/DP of an all-gather), then unpacks all layers in one launch.
- **Peer exchange for decode.** Below 128 tokens per rank, `EngramPeerExchange` replaces the hash all-gather and the per-layer row all-gathers: ranks publish ids in symmetric memory, look up their head shard for every peer's tokens, and read their own tokens back from the peers after a barrier. All layers share one lookup and one unpack launch.

The batched path serves DP-sharded tables (`embedding_across_dp` without DP-shared memory) with TP = 1, `head_dim % 128 == 0`, no LoRA (it wraps `wkv` after construction), and a `wkv` kernel that takes F8_128x4 scales (reusing `can_fuse_query_quant`). The peer exchange also needs SM100, CPU offload, and 2/4/8 fully connected GPUs; without it every slot uses the all-to-all, which on DEP4 HBM tables at 1–127 tokens per rank is 19–58 us faster than the BF16 path. Everything else, including TP, DP-shared tables, single replicas and ROCm, keeps the existing BF16 path unchanged. Communication stays on the current stream and `wkv` still runs in `Engram.forward`.

Also changed along the way:

- `EngramBatch` is an `nn.Module`, so the peer exchange's pointer tables are model buffers that level-2 sleep restores.
- `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` and the Engram unpack kernel share the F8_128x4 scale offset and size helpers.

## Kernel microbenchmark

The benchmarks, E2E runs and the first accuracy table were measured on d593d7f5df. 3724967bb9 only drops paths that DEP + THP never takes and keeps its `wkv` outputs bitwise identical (see Test Result).

Engram only, two layers (lookup, exchange, and anything needed to reach the MXFP8 `wkv` input), 4 x GB300 in one node. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash table sizes (24 heads x 16M rows, 94.4 GiB per layer) as DP-shared `/dev/shm` tables or private THP shards, uniform random ids rotating 3 sets, 256 MiB L2 flush per sample, full CUDA graph replay, median of 40 samples of the slowest rank, best of 2 rounds. Since this PR's output is already the `wkv` input, the BF16 columns include their activation quantization (17 us for decode, 203 us at 32K tokens).

DEP4:

| tokens/rank | DP-shared (us) | THP + all-gather (us) | this PR (us) | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 34 | 80 | 36 | 2.22x |
| 8 | 34 | 81 | 38 | 2.13x |
| 32 | 38 | 93 | 40 | 2.33x |
| 64 | 44 | 106 | 43 | 2.47x |
| 127 | 136 | 136 | 50 | 2.72x |
| 128 | 140 | 136 | 72 | 1.89x |
| 1024 | 2442 | 315 | 179 | 1.76x |
| 4096 | 5326 | 1097 | 534 | 2.05x |
| 8192 | 8224 | 2087 | 1010 | 2.07x |
| 16384 | 11854 | 4047 | 1954 | 2.07x |
| 32768 | 16008 | 7860 | 3800 | 2.07x |

DEP2:

| tokens/rank | DP-shared (us) | THP + all-gather (us) | this PR (us) | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 34 | 73 | 38 | 1.92x |
| 8 | 34 | 74 | 40 | 1.85x |
| 32 | 35 | 81 | 43 | 1.88x |
| 64 | 41 | 90 | 44 | 2.05x |
| 127 | 66 | 107 | 49 | 2.18x |
| 128 | 62 | 107 | 71 | 1.51x |
| 1024 | 2015 | 228 | 168 | 1.36x |
| 4096 | 4629 | 754 | 507 | 1.49x |
| 8192 | 6873 | 1407 | 970 | 1.45x |
| 16384 | 9511 | 2709 | 1879 | 1.44x |
| 32768 | 12389 | 5268 | 3672 | 1.43x |

DP-shared tables need no exchange, so at 1–64 tokens they are at most 8 us faster than this PR; from 1024 tokens this PR is 3.4–13.6x faster than them. The 127 → 128 step is the switch from the peer exchange to the all-to-all.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual
```

New coverage: the packed lookup output, and a 4-GPU check of the batched staging across peer and all-to-all slots, uneven and idle replicas, and full and breakable CUDA graph replays. The peer path needs SM100, so other GPUs only cover the all-to-all path.

## Test Result

On 3724967bb9, 202 passed on 4x GB200 (102 Engram kernel, 27 distributed, 73 `test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py`). Ruff, format and mypy pass.

Also checked locally, without adding tests:

- The staged MXFP8 bytes equal the table rows byte for byte on DEP2 and DEP4 with 22 and 24 heads, 1–3 layers starting at a non-zero hash index, pinned, THP and HBM tables, 1–4096 tokens around the 127/128 boundary (sorted lookups included), and 24 unsynchronized steps that switch between peer exchange and all-to-all.
- Real layer 1 and 14 checkpoint rows and `wkv` weights: the `wkv` output is bitwise identical to the BF16 path at 129, 1024 and 4096 tokens, with CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS.
- DEP4 `Engram.forward` through the peer exchange and the all-to-all in eager mode and full and breakable graph replays: bitwise identical to the BF16 path.
- 3724967bb9 vs d593d7f5df on DEP4 (24 heads x 256, 2 layers, 10% dead ids, idle ranks; pinned tables at 1–512 and HBM tables at 128–512 tokens per rank): staged MXFP8 values and `wkv` outputs (CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS) are bitwise identical; only the scales of padding and unowned rows change from 127 to 0.
- After a simulated level-2 sleep the peer exchange's pointer tables are restored and its lookups stay exact.

## E2E prefill (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB300 node: DeepGEMM mega MoE, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV cache, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, prefix caching off. Offline `LLM` per DP rank, one prompt per rank (nominal length minus 7 tokens per rank), `max_tokens=1`; TTFT is `scheduled_ts` to `first_token_ts` on the slowest rank, median of 3 repeats after a warmup repeat. Measured on top of #59532 with `max_cudagraph_capture_size=8192` (default size list, so 1K–8K prefills run in PIECEWISE graphs) and `max_num_seqs=64`. Prompts are uniformly random token ids; a repeated sentence keeps the few distinct n-gram rows in cache and hides Engram entirely.

| tokens/rank | DP-shared TTFT (ms) | THP + all-gather TTFT (ms) | this PR TTFT (ms) | vs DP-shared | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 60.2 | 61.7 | 60.5 | 0.99x | 1.02x |
| 4096 | 129.7 | 128.0 | 127.2 | 1.02x | 1.01x |
| 8192 | 220.2 | 214.2 | 213.9 | 1.03x | 1.00x |
| 16384 | 248.1 | 242.6 | 240.5 | 1.03x | 1.01x |
| 32768 | 466.0 | 447.4 | 446.5 | 1.04x | 1.00x |

Repeat spread is under 2.5 ms (5 ms for DP-shared at 32K). The gain over DP-shared tables matches the microbenchmark: at 8K the two Engram layers take 7.2 ms less, close to the 6.3 ms measured end to end. Against THP tables with all-gather it is about 1 ms per step, within noise end to end.

## E2E decode (DEP4)

Same setup on `main` (default capture sizes up to 512, `max_num_seqs=128`), short prompts, 64 output tokens with the decode token fixed to hold MoE routing constant. Mean request TPOT of the slowest rank, median of 3 repeats after a warmup repeat.

| batch/rank | DP-shared TPOT (ms) | THP + all-gather TPOT (ms) | this PR TPOT (ms) | vs DP-shared | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.072 | 6.128 | 6.082 | 1.00x | 1.01x |
| 8 | 6.457 | 6.501 | 6.453 | 1.00x | 1.01x |
| 32 | 8.199 | 8.292 | 7.928 | 1.03x | 1.05x |
| 64 | 10.833 | 11.157 | 10.832 | 1.00x | 1.03x |
| 127 | 14.043 | 14.403 | 14.046 | 1.00x | 1.03x |

Engram is under 1% of TPOT, and the fixed decode token keeps its rows cache-resident, so decode shows that private THP tables no longer cost anything over DP-shared ones rather than the full lookup saving.

## Accuracy (DEP4, this PR)

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 4096-token cap, concurrency 32, two passes on one `vllm serve` DEP4 server per side (same engine setup as the E2E runs, `main` with DP-shared tables vs this PR with THP tables). No request errors.

| | strict match (pass 1 / 2) | flexible extract (pass 1 / 2) |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, DP-shared tables | 92.87% / 92.95% | 92.80% / 92.87% |
| this PR, THP tables | 93.33% / 93.10% | 93.25% / 93.03% |

Both are within one standard error (±0.7 points); no accuracy gain is claimed.

GSM8K with DSpark on 3724967bb9 (DEP4, MegaMoE, `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`, 5 speculative tokens with adaptive verification, THP tables; same lm-eval setup with a 1024-token cap), against the DEP4 base run in #59511 with DP-shared tables:

| | strict match | acceptance length, incl. bonus | per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| #59511 base, DP-shared tables | 92.57% | 3.365 | 0.792 / 0.641 / 0.441 / 0.310 / 0.181 |
| this PR, THP tables | 92.57% | 3.398 | 0.795 / 0.644 / 0.446 / 0.319 / 0.194 |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <model> --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --language-model-only --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"dp_shared_memory":false,"use_thp":true}'

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=4096,temperature=0"
```

The baseline uses `"dp_shared_memory":true,"use_thp":false`. The DSpark run uses the DEP4 GSM8K serve flags from #59511 plus the `--engram-config` above, and `max_gen_toks=1024`.

</details>

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `engram`, `engram fp8`, `engram all-to-all`, `engram peer` and `DeepSeek-V4.1 engram`. #56989 packs FP8 rows for the TP head exchange (opt-in, TP > 1 without SP) and dequantizes them before `wkv`; this PR leaves TP alone and covers Engram DP, feeding `wkv` directly. #57893 tunes small-lookup tiles. #58766 fed MXFP8 rows to `wkv` through the existing gathers and was closed by its author after merge conflicts, without review; this PR keeps that idea and also replaces the gathers.

title: [Model][DeepSeek-V4] Make MegaMoE shared-expert finalize independent of linear post-load order
author: aoshen02
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

MegaMoE fuses the DeepSeek-V4 shared expert using the shared linears' block-FP8 UE8M0 scales. Those linears' own DeepGEMM post-load hook repacks the same scales into int32, in place.

`_finalize_shared_expert_weights` only converted scales that were still in checkpoint layout, and passed packed scales straight to MegaMoE. So it was only correct when it ran **before** that hook:
- Real loads finalize inside `load_weights`, before the hook, so they are fine.
- A dummy load never calls `load_weights` and finalizes **after** the hook. With DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MegaMoE + EP, DeepGEMM then asserts at startup (`layout.hpp:114`).

The packed layout already stores one UE8M0 byte per (row, k-block), four k-blocks per int32. `_prepare_shared_expert_scale` now reads per-row exponents from either layout and builds the same 1x32 MegaMoE scale. The rest of the path is unchanged, including the existing shape check and the fallback to the serial shared MLP.

This removes the ordering constraint that keeps DeepSeek-V4 finalizing inside `load_weights`. #57733 builds on it.

## Test Plan / Results

`tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py::test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe_finalizes_native_shared_expert_weights` gains two `-packed` cases. Their scales are packed by the real linear-hook packer (`deepgemm_post_process_weight_scale_block`) before finalize runs. Results on GB200:
- With this PR: 7 passed.
- On `main`: both `-packed` cases fail at the check that the scale reaching MegaMoE equals the checkpoint scale.
- The rest of the file has 14 failures, identical on `main`. They are V4.1 / hash-routing tests that need a DeepGEMM build with `bf16_mega_gate`.

GPU checks with real DeepGEMM. Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this commit, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

| check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Fused shared scale from checkpoint scales vs from hook-packed scales. Shapes (4096, 4096), (4096, 2048), (6144, 7168), (7168, 3072). | packed scales not converted | **bitwise identical** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4-layer config (FP4 experts), MegaMoE + EP, TP1, `load_format="dummy"` | startup crash, DeepGEMM `layout.hpp:114` | starts; shared expert **fused** on all 4 layers; finite logprobs |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, real weights, `vllm serve` DP4 / EP4, MegaMoE (shared expert fused); greedy decoding, top-5 logprobs | baseline | **bit-identical** tokens and logprobs, 4/4 prompts |

`pre-commit` passes.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `MegaMoE shared expert`, `_finalize_shared_expert_weights`, `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` and `deepseek v4 dummy load mega moe`. None of them changes how the shared-expert scales are read.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve fp16 in legacy fused MoE LoRA
author: sudhanshu112233shukla
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59920. Preserve the input dtype in the legacy fused MoE LoRA GEMM instead of unconditionally converting operands to bfloat16.

## Claims
 Prevents silent fp16-to-bfloat16 conversion in the legacy shrink/expand kernel.
Keeps both Triton descriptor and pointer-load paths aligned with the hidden-state input dtype.
Extends large-rank fallback correctness coverage to fp16 and bf16.

## Validation

 `uv run --no-sync ruff check vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`
 `uv run --no-sync ruff format --check ...`
 `uv run --no-sync python -m compileall -q vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`
 The focused Triton test collection/execution could not run in this Windows CPU-only environment: vLLM native extension and `uvloop` are unavailable. CI or an Intel/NVIDIA/AMD GPU runner must execute `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`.
 No kernel benchmark was claimed; this is a correctness fix.

## Details

The legacy two-kernel path previously cast both dot operands to `tl.bfloat16` to work around ROCm type inference across TMA and pointer-load branches. That changes fp16 LoRA arithmetic and can produce incorrect outputs. The kernel now derives the dot dtype from the input pointer element type and casts both operands to that type. The large-rank fallback test is parameterized over the existing fp16 and bf16 dtype matrix.

title: [KV Connector] Support sleep mode with MooncakeStoreConnector
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59625 (merged). Rebased onto main.

MooncakeStoreConnector registers the GPU KV cache with the Mooncake store (`register_buffer`). Over RDMA, that registration pins the physical pages. Sleep mode unmaps the KV cache, and wake maps new pages at the same virtual addresses. The store keeps using the old pages, so puts and gets read and write memory the model no longer uses.

Evidence on main (GB300, Qwen3-8B, two instances sharing one store; instance A sleeps at level 1, instance B never sleeps):

- After the wake, every store hit on A gives wrong output: 0/8 for KV that B put, and 0/8 for A's own post-wake puts.
- A's puts after the wake store stale bytes. B reads them and also returns wrong output (0/8), even though B never slept.
- While asleep, A still holds 67.8 GB of GPU memory, because the KV cache stays pinned. After the wake it holds 150.8 GB (85.4 GB before the sleep).
- There are no errors and no log lines.

On main, this combination is refused at startup ("MooncakeStoreConnector does not support sleep mode").

This PR implements the sleep-mode hooks from #59625 for MooncakeStoreConnector:

- `unregister_kv_caches()` runs before the KV cache is unmapped. It waits until the put queue and the shared get queue have no queued or running tasks, then calls `unregister_buffer` on each device KV region. All store puts and gets run on those queues; lookups only query keys.
  - The wait is bounded by `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (480 s by default), the same bound `MooncakeConnector.unregister_kv_caches` uses. That is well above Mooncake's 60 s per-transfer timeout, so a slow queue does not fail the sleep. On timeout it raises `TimeoutError` and keeps the registration. The wait shares one helper with `close()`.
- `restore_kv_caches()` runs after the KV cache is mapped again. It registers the same addresses and lengths.
- Both calls are all or nothing and idempotent. If an (un)register call fails partway, the calls already made are undone and the error is raised. A failed sleep leaves the engine awake and fully registered; a failed wake leaves the regions released, so a retry starts clean.
- Host-resident (HiSparse) regions are host memory, which sleep does not touch, so they stay registered.
- `supports_sleep_mode()` reads the protocol from the Mooncake config file (`MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`). The workers use the same file to set up the store. It accepts `rdma` and `tcp` and refuses other configured protocols. The check runs only when sleep mode is enabled, and it does not import mooncake. If the config is missing, startup fails with the existing "MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH is not set" error.
  - Why RDMA and TCP: no peer holds a key to our KV cache. Puts and gets use our local lkey against peers' host-DRAM segments, so registering again locally is enough.
  - TCP registration only records the address range. Data moves with `cudaMemcpy` on the virtual address, and nothing is pinned.
  - Other configured protocols (e.g. nvlink) can export handles to peers, so they stay refused.
  - It also refuses when `MC_FORCE_MNNVL` or `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK` is set. Mooncake then installs an nvlink transport even with `protocol: rdma`. Like Mooncake, it checks only that the variable is set, not its value.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests (CPU, fake store), one per invariant:
  - Release and restore round-trip exactly the device regions, with the same addresses and lengths (dense layout, and HiSparse with one host group plus one device group). Both calls are idempotent across two cycles.
  - Release waits for a queued or running put or get. A real thread finishes the task when a `threading.Event` is set. A timeout keeps the registration.
  - A failed unregister or register is rolled back, and a retry then succeeds.
  - The config gate: rdma/tcp accepted; nvlink, `MC_FORCE_MNNVL` (also `=0`) and `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK` refused; missing config. Mooncake is blocked from import.
- Mutation check: each piece of the change was altered on its own (gate and each env var, region recording, host skip, idempotence, state, lengths, rollback, each drained queue, the bound, the deadline). 23 mutants, all killed, and every test kills at least one.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_config,test_mooncake_store_*,test_mooncake_connector,test_multi_connector}.py tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py`. The store tests were also run 5 times. pre-commit was run on the changed files.
- Hardware (GB300, Mooncake 0.3.13.post1, RDMA, standalone `mooncake_master`, Qwen3-8B):
  - Two servers share one store: A sleeps and B never sleeps. GPU prefix caching is off, so every cached token comes from the store.
  - 8 random 2048-token prompts per phase, greedy decoding, 32 output tokens.
  - After every cycle: A gets KV that B put, B gets KV that A put after the wake, and A gets its own post-wake put back.
  - Cycles: 3× `/sleep?level=1` + `/wake_up`; 1× level-1 sleep then `/wake_up?tags=weights` and `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`; 1× `/pause` + `/release_kv_cache_memory` + `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`.
  - Control run: `/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` at the same points. This performs the same store wipe as sleep, without unmapping anything.

## Test Result

- Unit tests (`test_config`, `test_mooncake_store_worker`, `test_mooncake_connector`, `test_multi_connector`, `test_sleep_mode_backend`): 407 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are in `test_multi_connector.py` and are unrelated to this change: one needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, the other needs `ray`, which is not installed. They fail the same way on #59625 alone. All `test_mooncake_store_*` files: 332 passed in each of the 5 runs.
- Hardware, sleep run vs awake control: 224/224 outputs are token-for-token identical across all 28 phases. Every hit read 2032 tokens from the store.
  - Before this change, each post-wake hit phase was 0/8.
  - Each run also compares hits with the cold output of the same prompt. A few phases there show 7/8, and the control run shows exactly the same mismatches. These come from near-tie prompts where a store hit and a cold prefill differ, not from sleep.

| GPU memory on A | this PR | main (earlier run) |
|---|---|---|
| awake | 85.1 GB | 85.4 GB |
| asleep, level 1 (3 cycles) | 2.1 GB each time | 67.8 GB |
| after wake | 85.1 GB each time | 150.8 GB |
| selective wake: weights only | 19.4 GB | — |
| after `release_kv_cache_memory` | 19.7 GB | — |

- After the review changes (rollback, env check, shared drain), a shorter rerun on the final commit with 2 level-1 cycles gave 104/104 outputs identical to its control. Every hit read 2032 tokens from the store. A held 2.1 GB asleep and 85.1 GB awake in both cycles.
- Transfer errors: none in either run (non-zero error counters, glog `E` lines, `ERROR` lines, and tracebacks were all 0 on A and B).

Not covered:

- TCP on hardware. On this cluster, TCP puts and gets fail with `TRANSFER_FAIL` even without sleep, with both P2PHANDSHAKE and the HTTP metadata server. An earlier H200 run of main with TCP and sleep returned 8/8 with memory fully freed, but it was not repeated with this commit.
- The HiSparse path on hardware (unit-tested only).
- TP > 1 and multi-GPU runs.
- The in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`). The drain inside `unregister_kv_caches` is what covers it there.

Known limitations:

- Mooncake builds with NVLink support (such as the cuda13 wheel) also install an nvlink transport when they find no RDMA NIC. That can't be detected at config time, so it is not refused.
- Pre-existing: sleep at level ≥ 1 and `release_kv_cache_memory` reset the connector before the release. On rank 0 that reset waits for the put queue with no bound, so a stuck put hangs there, not in the bounded release.
- Pre-existing: a load task that raises before the `try` in `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread._handle_request` never calls `task_done`. The drain then never sees an empty queue, and every later sleep fails with `TimeoutError`. We found no scheduler input that reaches it. A fix needs a load-error report too, so it is left for a follow-up.
- Pre-existing, not specific to this connector: `/sleep?mode=wait` (and `/pause?mode=wait`) while connector loads are in flight returns 500 "Failed to reset KV cache ...", and the scheduler stays paused until `/resume`. Under `PAUSED_NEW` the scheduler counts only running requests, so requests holding blocks for an async load look idle. Use `mode=abort`, or call `/resume` and retry.

Known separate issue, not fixed here: sleep at level ≥ 1 resets the connector, which runs `remove_all(force=True)` on the Mooncake master. One instance's sleep therefore deletes the KV of every instance that shares the master. It should be scoped by tenant.

### Additional Test Result: stress run

- Stress run (GB300, 1 node, Qwen3-8B, Mooncake RDMA, one shared store; the image plus per-file mounts of this stack, sha-checked):
  - Three servers: TP2 and TP1 sleep with staggered, overlapping windows, and a TP1 server never sleeps; `store_tp_size=2`, so TP2 and TP1 share keys. 20 cycles. After each wake: get of keys another server put while it was asleep, own put read back, and cross-server read-back of its post-wake puts.
    - 2080/2080 outputs are token-identical to an awake control run (`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` at the same points). Every hit read 2032/2048 tokens from the store.
  - TP2 plus a never-sleep server, 10 cycles: full sleep, selective wake (`weights`, then `kv_cache`), and `release_kv_cache_memory`. 400/400 identical to control.
  - Memory had no drift: TP2 at 3583 MiB/GPU asleep and 86467 woken, TP1 at 2077 / 85101, the same in every cycle. Host RSS of each server was unchanged from cycle 1 to cycle 20. 0 transfer errors.
  - 64 concurrent requests up to `/sleep?mode=wait`, with puts in flight: 64/64 complete, 0 timeouts, and requests not yet scheduled run after the wake. `mode=abort`: all aborted, and sleep takes 0.5 s.
  - HiSparse (GLM-5.2-FP8 TP4, HiSparse + MooncakeStore through MultiConnector): 78 host regions stay registered and the device region is released and registered again. 12 `release_kv_cache_memory` cycles: device memory returns to the same value every cycle, and store hits read 4160+ tokens. Exact-retrieval accuracy on store hits after a release equals an interleaved control on the same prompts (72/96 vs 72/96, with 140/144 per-request outcomes equal). Level-1 sleep was not run on this model: it would back up about 704 GB of weights to host RAM.

---

title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Quantize audio towers independently
author: sudhanshu112233shukla
body:
## Overview

Fixes [#59905](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59905) by selecting quantization for Gemma 4 vision and audio towers independently.

## Claims

Quantizable Gemma 4 audio towers now receive the checkpoint quantization config even when the vision tower dimensions are not supported by that kernel.
Non-quantizable towers retain the existing unquantized path.
Methods that support arbitrary tower dimensions keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

Ruff check passed for the changed Python files.
 Ruff format check passed.
Python compileall passed.
 git diff --check passed.
 Added a focused regression test for independent tower dimension checks.
 The focused pytest could not complete in the available Windows environment: the local uv environment lacks pytest, and the prepared pytest environment hung while importing the full Gemma 4 multimodal module. No GPU checkpoint load was available locally.

## Details
The constructor previously computed one tower_quant decision from vision_config and reused it for audio_tower. AutoRound-GPTQ Gemma 4 checkpoints can have a non-quantizable vision tower and quantized audio tower. In that combination, vLLM created an unquantized audio weight, while the checkpoint provided GPTQ tensors such as qweight, scales, qzeros, and g_idx.

The new helper applies the existing dimension and method checks to each tower configuration separately. The change is limited to Gemma 4 multimodal model construction and does not alter quantization behavior for the language model.

title: [Bugfix] Resolve eager_break_during_capture at call time, not import time
author: C-C-Hao
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59940. `@eager_break_during_capture` decided whether to wrap a function when the decorated module was
imported. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the breakable-graph flag is turned on later, inside `VllmConfig` (#57586).
Any import of `attention.py` before that point leaves `unified_attention_with_output` unwrapped, and FA2 then produces
wrong tokens for short prefills. This PR makes the decorator always return its wrapper, so the setting is read at call
time. It's a 2-line removal plus CPU tests.

## Claims

- Breakable-graph eager breaks no longer depend on import order. In-process and default-fork engines with a cold
  model-info cache now get the wrapped attention op.
- With the flag off, behavior is unchanged: the wrapper calls the function directly when no breakable capture is
  active.
- Every current and future user of the decorator is covered (33 sites, plus those added by #46372 and #57881), with no
  new imports.

## Validation

Environment: `uv venv --python 3.12`, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .`, plus `requirements/lint.txt`, `pytest`
and `tblib`; Python 3.12.14, main 5f30fc703 plus this commit. Tests ran on CPU only.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py -v
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q
```

| `test_decorator_passthrough_returns_fn_result[False/True]` | pass | pass |
| `test_decorated_op_traces_without_graph_break[False/True]` (`fullgraph=True`) | pass | pass |
| whole `test_breakable_cudagraph.py` | 2 failed, 11 passed, 13 skipped | 13 passed, 13 skipped (the skips need CUDA) |

run, main 5f30fc703), using the repro from the issue:

recompiles. Two unpatched runs agree on 10/14 hashes (all 14 token sequences equal, max |Δlogprob| 0.097). One patched
run is bitwise identical to one unpatched run (14/14); the other patched run differs from every other run (3 token

0.49-0.75 s. Both trees have identical worker state (flag set before attention is imported, `CompilationMode.NONE`).

Pass-through overhead, from a microbenchmark of 1e6 calls × 5 with no capture active: about 0.5 µs per call on a shared,
loaded x86_64 host with Python 3.12. That's an upper bound of about 14 µs per step for 28 attention layers. Before this
change, the cost only arose when the flag was on.

## Details

- **Root cause:** `vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py` had `if not is_breakable_cudagraph_enabled(): return fn`.
  On a cold model-info cache, `ModelConfig` construction imports `attention.py` via `registry._save_modelinfo_to_cache`
  → `weight_utils.atomic_writer` before `VllmConfig._maybe_enable_breakable_cudagraph` sets the env. Forked engine
  cores inherit the bare op. First reported by @Taimys in #58918 and in the #57311 thread.
- **Scope beyond batch invariance:** as @LioEinaudi pointed out in #59940, the other branch of
  `_maybe_enable_breakable_cudagraph` (`_uses_breakable_cudagraph_by_default`, #52861) sets the same env var after the
  same early import, for the `DEFAULT_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH_ARCHITECTURES` models on CUDA, with no
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` involved. The ordering hazard is the same and this change covers it. I only validated the
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` path above, and I did not run those models, so I can't say whether their outputs are
  affected.
- **Why this isn't a duplicate of #57311:** #57311 (open) removes that particular import chain, and @Taimys confirmed it
  fixes that trigger on L20. The decorator stays import-order dependent, though: with #57311 applied on main and a warm
  cache, a user script that imports `vllm.model_executor.model_loader` before building `LLM` still ends up with the
  unwrapped op (verified by inspecting the op, not by comparing outputs). #53293 fixed the same root cause for Ray only. This PR removes the
  dependence at its source and works alongside #57311.
- **Dynamo:** the wrapper's thread-local lookup traces without a graph break (`fullgraph=True` test), so no
  `is_compiling()` fast path is needed.
- **Not included:** a GPU end-to-end regression test. Maintainers: would you like one (for example a cold-cache
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` FA2 run in the BI test suite)?

title: [Bugfix][Core] Retain encoder cache references for repeated multimodal inputs
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Prevent premature encoder-cache eviction when repeated multimodal inputs are deduplicated within the same scheduling step. 

## Claims

- Preserve cache references for partially consumed duplicate inputs, including locally encoded and externally loaded inputs.
- Avoid unnecessary re-encoding and scheduling stalls caused by premature eviction.
- Register duplicate occurrences within the final scheduled window, including the existing prefill lookahead, without registering later occurrences outside that window.

## Validation

On upstream base `d61081dc3d`, using the existing development environment:

```bash
uv run --no-project --python /workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -q
```

Result: **241 passed, 2 failed**.

Both failures require multiple GPUs and also fail on the unchanged upstream base in the same single-GPU environment:

- `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`
- `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait`

The new parameterized regression test covers newly admitted and running requests, with local encoding and external cache loads. All four cases pass. It verifies that:

- a competing request cannot evict an input that still has a partially consumed duplicate;
- no additional local encoding is scheduled; and
- later unscheduled occurrences are not registered as references.

Pre-commit checks pass.

Model end-to-end validation and latency measurements have not been performed, so no measured performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

Same-step deduplication allocates cache space only for the first occurrence of an input. Later occurrences within the same scheduling window reuse that entry but are not registered as references.

Once the first occurrence is consumed, the cache manager can therefore consider the entry reclaimable even though another occurrence is still partially consumed. A competing request can then evict the entry prematurely.

After scheduling is finalized, register cached occurrences overlapping the final scheduled window before advancing request progress. This reuses the existing reference-tracking mechanism without allocating additional cache space or scheduling duplicate encoder work.

The additional work is a window lookup and reference updates for overlapping inputs on scheduled requests that already hold encoder-cache references. Encoder-decoder models retain their existing behavior.

---

title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Quantized draft lm_head for drafters that share the target head
author: stecasta
body:
## Overview **Decode at c=1 on SPEED-Bench goes from 39.4 to 46.5 tok/s (+18%) with average AL unchanged (-0.4%)** with an NVFP4 draft head, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP (k=3), one DGX Spark, measured on three nodes with the SM121 skinny-GEMM plans from #59753. An MTP or EAGLE drafter that shares the target's lm_head reads the whole head once per draft token; on a 248k x 2560 BF16 head that is the largest kernel in a draft step. A new opt-in key gives the drafter a private quantized copy of the head. The target still verifies with its own BF16 head, so outputs are unchanged; only the acceptance length can move. ```bash vllm serve --speculative-config \ '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_lm_head_quantization": "nvfp4"}' ``` ## Claims - `"nvfp4"`: E2M1 weights with an E4M3 scale per 16 values, weight-only on the platform's W4A16 kernel, chosen by `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel` (Marlin on SM12x; activations stay BF16/FP16). `"fp8"`: per-row FP8 weights and per-token FP8 activations, reusing the existing online `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` on the platform FP8 kernel (`CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` on GB10). CUDA graphs and TP work (each rank quantizes its own shard). - Decode on GB10: +17.5% to +18.4% at c=1 and +9% to +11% at c=4 (NVFP4, three nodes), +10.8% / +6.5% (FP8, one node). AL within run-to-run noise, including multilingual (every row of the head stays available). GSM8K unchanged (earlier run, below). - Probabilistic drafting stays exact: the quantized logits are both sampled and used as q. - Extra memory: about 0.35 GiB (NVFP4) or 0.6 GiB (FP8) for a 248k x 2560 head, created inside model loading, so profiled KV sizing accounts for it. With `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`, leave room for it. ## Validation SPEED-Bench qualitative (11 categories at c=1 and c=4, greedy, 256 output tokens), Flash-Next, MTP k=3, real AL from the spec-decode counters, full vocabulary. Each node ran stock and the quantized head back to back; vLLM nightly `0cbac6cd1` with the skinny-GEMM plans of #59753 applied, plus this PR. ``` decode tok/s per user stock c=1 NVFP4 c=1 stock c=4 NVFP4 c=4 p4242-0121 39.42 46.63 (+18.3%) 26.61 29.46 (+10.7%) p4242-0547 39.45 46.69 (+18.4%) 26.54 29.44 (+10.9%) p4242-0122 39.36 46.24 (+17.5%) 26.55 28.95 (+9.0%) p4242-0122, FP8 head 43.61 (+10.8%) 28.28 (+6.5%) AL, mean of 3 nodes stock 2.670 NVFP4 2.658 (-0.4%) multilingual 2.799 / 2.845 ```
Earlier measurement, before #59753 (ABBA, larger gain) Without the skinny-GEMM plans the BF16 head GEMV is slower, so the same change measured +27%. Stock and NVFP4 ran in ABBA order (stock, nvfp4, nvfp4, stock) on one GB10 node (p4242-0073, median SM clock 2242 MHz); numbers are the mean of the two runs per arm. | vs. BF16 head | AL (avg) | AL (multilingual) | decode c=1 | decode c=1 (multilingual) | decode c=4 | step, forced AL 3, c=1 | GSM8K (256) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | BF16 head (stock) | 2.673 | 2.859 | 35.6 tok/s | 36.9 tok/s | 27.2 tok/s | 73.7 ms | 243 | | NVFP4 draft head | 2.664 (-0.3%) | 2.851 (-0.3%) | **45.2 tok/s (+27.1%)** | 46.7 tok/s (+26.7%) | 30.4 tok/s (+11.7%) | 58.2 ms | 243 | | FP8 draft head (separate node, own stock) | +0.2% | -0.6% | **+21.0%** | +19.1% | +9.7% | 61.6 ms | 247 vs 244 | The FP8 serving row comes from a second GB10 node (p4242-0067, 2496 MHz, 7G KV) against its own stock arm (36.1 tok/s c=1, AL 2.664); the forced-AL step times and GSM8K for stock and NVFP4 are from an earlier same-node run (p4242-0074, 2489 MHz). Forced AL 3, c=4 per-user step: 114.2 / 102.4 / 104.1 ms (stock / NVFP4 / FP8).
Kernel choice, draft head GEMV only (248320 x 2560, CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 3 x 100 replays): ``` GB200 (SM100) GB10 (SM121, M>=4) BF16 (cuBLAS) 191 to 196 us 5.50 to 5.58 ms FP8 W8A8 (selector) 111 to 113 us 2.80 to 2.84 ms <- used for "fp8" FP8 W8A16 Marlin 145 to 153 us 2.80 to 2.82 ms NVFP4 W4A16 Marlin 133 to 149 us 1.60 to 1.64 ms <- used for "nvfp4" ``` FP8 reuses the online PTPC method (platform W8A8 kernel, needs SM89+): 1.3x faster than Marlin on GB200, parity on GB10. NVFP4 picks its kernel with `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel(use_a16=True)`, so `--linear-backend`, `linear_backend_per_quant` and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` apply as for any NVFP4 linear layer. On SM100/103 the default is the CuTe DSL W4A16 kernel, which measured 1.42x slower than Marlin at M=16 on GB200; `linear_backend_per_quant={"nvfp4_w4a16": "marlin"}` selects Marlin there. Independent reproduction at TP2 on 2x DGX Spark (earlier revision, MTP k=4, [#56577 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56577#issuecomment-5994233686)): +18.5% (fp8) and +19.5% (nvfp4) decode at c=1, greedy outputs byte-identical across arms. Disclaimers: - Greedy decoding on this model is not bit-reproducible run to run; per-category AL moves up to about 3% in either direction for stock as well. Across the three nodes above stock varies by 0.2% and NVFP4 by 1.0%. Absolute tok/s also varies across Spark nodes and recipes, so compare arms only within one node. - The gain shrinks with concurrency, where more tokens share each head read. ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py # all passed (GB10) pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py -k draft_lm_head # 2 passed (GB10) ```
Setup Setup: vLLM nightly `0cbac6cd1` with #59753 applied (not in the earlier ABBA run), this PR and two Flash-Next serving prerequisites (#59309, #56273); `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` @ada4da32, FP8 KV cache, `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 7G` (8G in the earlier ABBA run), `--max-model-len 49152`, `--max-num-seqs 8`, MTP drafter MoE on Marlin. Every arm used the same settings.
## Details - Design: the quantization lives with the other online quantization methods, in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/lm_head.py`. `quantized_lm_head_copy()` builds a plain `ParallelLMHead` with that quant method and quantizes it straight from this rank's shard of the target head, so no bf16 copy is made and the target head is unchanged. FP8 reuses the existing `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod`; NVFP4 adds a small weight-only method (`_LMHeadNvfp4Method`) that quantizes the head and hands it to the selected W4A16 kernel. `ParallelLMHead` gains an optional `quant_method` argument, which `VocabParallelEmbedding` already has. vllm-ascend overrides `ParallelLMHead.__init__` without this argument, so the soft-fail Ascend NPU interface check flags it; on Ascend, `draft_lm_head_quantization` needs the override updated. `"nvfp4"` needs a CUDA W4A16 kernel, so on ROCm only `"fp8"` is available and the tests skip the nvfp4 cases there. - Hook: `load_eagle_model` gives the drafter that head instead of the shared target head, including the MTP per-layer `shared_head.head`. - Derived state: the copy is kept out of layerwise reload and re-derived in place from the target head whenever the target's weights are replaced (`reload_weights`, weight transfer), so sleep mode, weight reload and weight transfer keep working. During a draft-only weight update the drafter shares the target head again, as on main, and the copy is re-derived when the update finishes. - Scope: MRV2 drafters loaded through `load_eagle_model` (EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP) that share an unquantized fp16/bf16 lm_head running in the model dtype; other cases are rejected at config validation or load. Gemma-4 MTP is excluded because it scores a subset of its tied embedding rows directly and has no shared lm_head. DFlash and DSpark can call the same helper in a follow-up. - Not a duplicate: #56577 (Qwen4Exp only, env var, eager only) and #47584 (DSpark only, env var) add an FP8 draft head for one model or method; this is the generic version behind one config key, with CUDA graphs and NVFP4. #59740 (reduced draft vocabulary) composes with it; both add a draft-head key to `speculative_config` and hook the same place in `load_eagle_model`, so whichever lands second will reuse this quantizer for the list rows (as `draft_token_map_quantization` there) rather than add a second one. #41000, #42124 and #58343 concern heads quantized in the checkpoint, and the online quantization framework (#51285) covers linear and MoE layers but not `ParallelLMHead`. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and benchmark harness; I reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements above.

**Reproduction on upstream main (DGX Spark, GB10)** Upstream main 02b83919aa with the heads of #59958, #59973, #59740, #60068 and #54614 merged, no other runtime patches. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP 6 with confidence stop 0.6, sparse draft head via `draft_token_map` (32k ids, 16384 dynamic rows at rank 256, `draft_token_map_quantization: nvfp4`), FP8 KV, `host_file_gather` PLE tables. SPEED-Bench throughput 2K in / 1K out, fixed OSL, c=1, n=20: | Build | tok/s/user | AL | GSM8K-256 | |---|---|---|---| | upstream main + these PRs | 49.94 | 2.68 | 249/256 | | our internal stack, same node | 49.73 | 2.65 | 245/256 | The PR route reproduces the internal stack result within noise.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Transfer the whole PLE short-conv page in disaggregated P/D
author: aijanai
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59642 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 0% MTP acceptance in disaggregated P/D serving with `NixlConnector`).

The NIXL worker folds every KV cache layer that reports the same base address into one region (`register_kv_caches`, `if base_addr in seen_base_addresses`). In the block-outer HMA layout every cache group places its first page at byte 0 of the shared allocation, so on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next the PLE short-conv state (`Qwen4ExpPLELayer`, a tp-replicated `MambaSpec`, page = `channels × (conv_state_len + num_spec_tokens)` = 245760 B) lands in the same region as layer-0 GDN, the layer-3 QSA ring and the layer-3 MLA indexer cache, and that region keeps the MLA page length (204800 B). The PLE descriptors built from `block_len_per_layer[_ple_region_index]` therefore transfer only 204800/245760 bytes of each PLE slot: 8534 of 10240 channels arrive on the decode worker, the rest is whatever the block held before (never zeroed: the block is exempt from zeroing because an async load is expected to overwrite it). With `num_speculative_tokens >= 2` the spec-decode short conv reads those stale columns, the layer-1 hidden state becomes NaN, the target logits are NaN and the rejection sampler rejects every draft (the generated tokens are garbage too, not just slow).

This PR records the PLE page length at registration (`_ple_block_len`) and uses it for the PLE descriptors on both sides of the transfer (`_build_mamba_local` / `_build_mamba_remote`), exchanging it through `NixlAgentMetadata.ple_block_len` (optional, backward compatible) so the existing P/D geometry check still compares PLE pages. Region discovery is unchanged: the PLE keeps sharing its region with the pages it aliases, as `test_csa_linear_registration_discovers_shared_regions` expects; only the transfer length of its pages changes.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_ple_region.py`: a CSA-linear-like config (MLA + GDN + ring + PLE sharing byte 0 of one block-outer tensor, PLE page larger than the MLA page); asserts the PLE descriptors cover the whole PLE page and that the page length is advertised in the handshake metadata. Before the fix the PLE descriptors carry the MLA page length.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` + `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` run inside the serving image (vLLM `109b5363fc`) with the patch hot-patched: 307 passed before and after (one HF-download test deselected).
- End-to-end on GB200 (vLLM `109b5363fc` + this patch hot-patched into the image, Dynamo + `NixlConnector`, 1P/1D, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, MTP k=3, 200 requests of 64/64 tokens): mean acceptance length goes from 1.00 on 20/21 windows (zero accepted drafts) to 2.7–3.5 on every window, no NaN; the same configuration in aggregate mode gives ~2.1–2.4.

## Test Result

See above; details and the full investigation (per-request probes of the PLE conv state on prefill and decode, per-column comparison of the transferred slot) are in #59642.

title: [Bugfix] FlashInfer: declare only KV layouts it can address
author: hyunnnchoi
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59998. On non-SM100 GPUs, declare the five KV cache layouts FlashInfer can address, so layout resolution can no longer pick LHBNC.

### User case

1. FlashInfer on SM80/SM90/SM120 with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`.
2. `FlashInferBackend.supported_kv_cache_layouts()` returns `None` there, so `resolve_kv_cache_layout` accepts LHBNC.
3. FlashInfer only takes NHD/HND pages; `get_flashinfer_layout_string` has no LHBNC entry.
4. The engine dies at startup on `AssertionError: KV cache layout LHBNC has no FlashInfer equivalent` (A100, Llama-3-8B) instead of rejecting the layout at resolution.

The fix returns the default preference order without LHBNC (LBNHC, LBHNC, BLNHC, BLHNC, BHLNC) instead of `None`.

Unchanged: the default layout (still LBNHC), the SM100 set, connector preferences (LBHNC and BLHNC stay valid), and every layout FlashInfer could already run.

Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR covers this. #46329 and #56550 add an SM120 branch to the same function but keep the `None` fallback. Related: #55431, #55312.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \
  -k test_flashinfer_declares_only_layouts_it_can_address
ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
ruff format --check vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
git diff --check
```

The new test patches the device capability to SM80/90/100/120 and checks that every declared layout maps through `get_flashinfer_layout_string` and that LHBNC is not declared.

## Test Result

```text
4 passed; on main 3 fail (SM80/90/120: supported_kv_cache_layouts() is None)
ruff check, ruff format --check (v0.14.0), git diff --check: passed
```

| A100, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, FlashInfer | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` | `AssertionError` during startup | `ValueError` at resolution listing the 5 valid layouts |
| default | LBNHC, serves | LBNHC, serves |

<details>
<summary>Test environment</summary>

- A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03, torch 2.13.0+cu129, flashinfer-python 0.6.18.post1.
- Unit test: main (1388100) with this patch, compiled extensions from the v0.30.0 wheel, run with `--noconftest` because the env lacks `tblib`; the test only uses `monkeypatch`.
- Engine check: v0.30.0 (ced6857) with the same patch. `supported_kv_cache_layouts` and `get_flashinfer_layout_string` are identical on v0.30.0 and main.
- The other five layouts also run in FlashInfer's attention benchmark on A100; LHBNC is the only one that asserts.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, code and tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests on my own hardware.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Clean up sweep workers after the server exits
author: zupengwang
body:
## Overview

Fix benchmark sweep cleanup when a server exits before its workers: terminate the surviving process group and reap the directly owned server process. This update also avoids signalling an already-reaped process group during test cleanup and documents the cleanup scope.

## Claims

- `ServerProcess.stop()` terminates workers remaining in the server's process group after its leader exits.
- Cleanup reaps the direct child and is safe to repeat after successful cleanup.
- The regression's fallback cleanup only signals the group while its direct child has not been reaped.

## Validation

Current candidate is based on main `fce61a05a76ccf34e1af6511ff7071affc306424`. Linux RTX 3090 host, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; CUDA devices were hidden throughout these CPU/process tests.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unmodified main plus the same regression tests | 2 failed: direct child unreaped / surviving worker |
| Candidate, standard `tests/benchmarks/sweep` suite with normal conftest fixtures | 28 passed |
| All 17 applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, mypy, markdownlint and test tethering | Passed |
| Diff whitespace check | Passed |

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py --timeout=60
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/benchmarks/sweep --timeout=60
pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/sweep/server.py tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py docs/benchmarking/sweeps.md
```

The tests use real subprocesses, a forked worker, and a socket handshake. The standard suite uses normal global fixtures, with no `--noconftest`. Hooks with no matching files were excluded using their actual file/type filters after an unrelated actionlint environment download failed.

The environment reuses an older official native wheel. No fresh native build, real model-serving or GPU-resource-recovery test, upstream CI, or performance benchmark is claimed. The earlier macOS global-teardown failure remains uninvestigated; this Linux result does not establish that it was fixed.

## Details

`start_new_session=True` makes the server PID the process-group ID. Previously, the `poll() is None` guard prevented cleanup after the leader was reaped, and looking up its PGID required it to remain alive. Signal the known group ID and wait for the direct child; a per-start completion flag prevents repeated successful cleanup from signalling the old group again.

The test's finalizer now checks `returncode` before its emergency signal, addressing the review suggestion about PID/PGID reuse. Closing the worker's socket releases the deliberately orphaned child on failure paths. Production cleanup still covers only workers in the original group, not detached sessions, and does not promise complete GPU-memory recovery. Numeric PGID reuse before the first cleanup remains a limitation.

The rendered benchmark guide at `docs/benchmarking/sweeps.md` describes these semantics. Existing Buildkite benchmark CLI coverage selects the tests. Duplicate-work checks were recorded when the original PR was opened; this updates that same PR.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex investigated, implemented, and ran the recorded checks.

title: [ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Use fused PLE Triton kernels on the AMD backend
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Overview

Ports the fused Qwen4Exp PLE Triton kernels from [#54517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54517) (with the [#55375](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55375) stride fix) to the AMD backend, which still runs the older PyTorch PLE path. Follows up on [#54764](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54764); supersedes [#58325](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58325).

## Claims

- Output throughput on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MXFP4, TP2 on MI355X, rises by +1.2% to +2.6% at each serving point (geomean +1.7%, +2.2% and +1.6% over three repeats). GSM8K is unchanged within noise.
- Per decode step, the PLE layer drops from 19 kernel launches to 3.
- The AMD backend no longer builds padded `[num_reqs, max_len]` n-gram buffers.
- NVIDIA and AMD now share one PLE kernel module. Net −360 non-test lines (+226 / −586).

## Validation

**Unit tests.** MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-18f8f96025` with this branch's `vllm/models/qwen4_exp` and `tests/models/qwen4_exp` mounted (the nightly and this branch's base have no other differences in that package):

```text
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py
90 passed, 15 warnings in 27.71s
```

- `test_fused_conv_correctness` now also runs on `amd.ple_layer.Qwen4ExpPLELayer`, covering every decode, prefill, spec and mixed case and both conv-state layouts.
- New `test_amd_ngram_embedding_matches_reference_under_compile` checks the AMD n-gram embedding under `torch.compile(fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` against the Python reference, including an empty request and EOS in the context.

**End to end.** `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`, TP2 on MI355X. Control and candidate are the same ROCm image, with and without this change. Mean of 3 repeats, control → this change:

| ISL / OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Per repeat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k | 4 | 537.5 → 551.4 (+2.6%) | 6.82 → 6.64 | +2.1%, +3.0%, +2.7% |
| 8k / 1k | 16 | 1,277.3 → 1,301.1 (+1.9%) | 11.35 → 11.16 | +1.6%, +2.5%, +1.4% |
| 8k / 1k | 64 | 2,296.3 → 2,336.0 (+1.7%) | 24.48 → 24.04 | +1.6%, +2.1%, +1.6% |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 231.1 → 233.7 (+1.2%) | 10.49 → 10.39 | +1.7%, +1.0%, +0.8% |

GSM8K (5-shot, chat template, 1,319 questions, flexible-extract): 0.9639 → 0.9624 (mean of 3). **No regressions.**

| Repeat | Control → this change | Fixed / broken | Exact McNemar p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0.9659 → 0.9598 | 11 / 19 | 0.20 |
| 2 | 0.9629 → 0.9629 | 18 / 18 | 1.00 |
| 3 | 0.9629 → 0.9644 | 18 / 16 | 0.86 |

**Decode trace.** Torch profiler on rank 0, 8k/128 at c16, 128 decode steps per arm:

| | Control | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PLE kernel launches per step | 19 | 3 (`_ple_ngram_ids`, `_ple_gate`, `_ple_conv`) |
| PLE GPU time per step | 134 µs | 18 µs |
| Decode step | 10.45 ms | 10.22 ms (−2.2%) |

**Reproduce:**

```bash
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --port 8000

# per point: (ISL, OSL, conc, prompts) = (8192,1024,4,32) (8192,1024,16,64) (8192,1024,64,128) (60000,600,4,16)
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --port 8000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 64 --warmup-requests 16 --request-rate inf

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_gen_toks=2048 \
  --seed 4321 --log_samples --output_path gsm8k-out
```

## Details

**Why the kernels port unchanged.** They are plain Triton. Their PDL path is gated on `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`, which is false on ROCm, so `nvidia/ops/ple.py` moves to `common/ops/ple.py` as is, with the NVIDIA imports updated.

**AMD model changes:**

- **`Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding`:** calls `ple_ngram_ids` instead of building padded buffers with gathers, a shift and a scatter, and drops the `max_num_reqs` argument. The pinned-host and device embedding lookups that follow are unchanged.
- **`Qwen4ExpPLELayer`:**
  - `key_proj` and `value_proj` become one replicated `MergedColumnParallelLinear` named `kv_proj` (`disable_tp=True`, as on NVIDIA).
  - The gate is `ple_gate`.
  - The short conv is `ple_conv`, which replaces the separate decode, prefill and spec `F.conv1d` branches with NVIDIA's single dispatch.
  - `qwen4_exp_ple_short_conv` stays a splitting op.
- **Residual:** the fused conv also adds the decoder layer's residual, so `Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer` now assigns `hidden_states = self.ple(...)` instead of adding the PLE output itself.
- **Weight loading:**
  - `ple.key_proj` and `ple.value_proj` map onto the two `kv_proj` shards.
  - `_HC_WEIGHTS_MAPPER` becomes `_EXTRA_WEIGHTS_MAPPER`, since it now also maps PLE weights.
  - `kv_proj` is added to `packed_modules_mapping`, so a quantization exclude list that names the original projections still applies. The Quark MXFP4 checkpoint keeps both in BF16.
  - The AMD MTP draft runs without PLE, so it only picks up the mapper rename.

**Design choice: a custom op around `ple_ngram_ids` on AMD.** Unlike the NVIDIA path, the AMD model runs the n-gram embedding inside `torch.compile`, where `query_start_loc` has a dynamic leading dimension. The kernel's launch grid comes from the request count, which Dynamo would otherwise trace symbolically. So the call goes through a small opaque op, `qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_ids`. The new compile test covers that path.

> Validated on MI355X (gfx950) only, not MI300X/MI325X (gfx942). The kernels contain no architecture-specific code.

title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Keep the HC up projection on the skinny GEMM path
author: stecasta
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The SM121 `(10240, 320)` skinny-GEMM plan for the Qwen4Exp HC up projection never runs. The fused HC down projection returns its LoRA activations as a column slice, and the Qwen4Exp dispatch only accepts packed row-major inputs, so every HC up call falls back to cuBLAS. This PR lets the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM take row-major column slices, which its kernel already supports.

## Claims

- On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 on DGX Spark, the HC up projection is the only BF16 GEMM still on cuBLAS during decode: about 101 calls per decode step at 31.6 us each, **3.2 ms per step** (torch profiler on a main-based build, 446 MTP decode steps, c=1). With this PR those calls use the planned skinny kernel. The GEMM is bandwidth bound (6.5 MB of weight per call), so the expected saving is the per-call delta, about 0.8 ms per step (~1%), not the full 3.2 ms.
- Kernel on the real producer layout (column slice of the 336-wide down+inject output): **1.17x to 1.23x** faster than cuBLAS at M=1 to 8, bit-exact against the same kernel on a packed copy.
- No behavior change for packed inputs or other callers (Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.2 keep their own guards).

## Validation

HC up projection, N=10240, K=320, `x = out[:, :320]` with `out` of shape `[M, 336]` (stride `(336, 1)`), DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), CUDA graph, cold L2, CUDA event timing, median of 50 replays:

```
 M   cuBLAS on slice (main)   skinny on slice (PR)   speedup   matches skinny on packed copy
 1   28.8 us                  23.6 us                1.22x     bit-exact
 2   29.1 us                  23.8 us                1.23x     bit-exact
 4   29.1 us                  24.8 us                1.17x     bit-exact
 8   28.7 us                  24.5 us                1.17x     bit-exact
```

Tests on DGX Spark (SM121): `pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k qwen4_exp` passes (61 passed, the rest skip on other architectures). A direct check confirms the 336-wide column slice now dispatches to the skinny kernel at M=1, 4, 8 (cosine 1.0 vs `F.linear`) and that a non-row-major `a` is still rejected.

End-to-end, same Spark node, Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP-4, SPEED-Bench 2K in / 1K out, c=1, 20 requests, one run per arm:

```
           decode tok/s/user   AL      tok/s per unit AL
main       46.55               2.959   15.73
PR         46.42               2.983   15.56
```

The expected ~1% is within run-to-run noise at c=1, so this PR does not claim an end-to-end speedup; it fixes a dispatch path that silently skips the planned kernel.

## Details

Root cause: `hc_down_silu` returns `output[:, :rank], output[:, rank : rank + hc]`, so the LoRA tensor fed to `input_mix_weight_up` has row stride `rank + hc + pad` (336 for Flash-Next). `_runtime_ok` required `stride == (K, 1)` and rejected it at every M, including M=1. The non-fused path (`split` of the merged projection) produces the same layout.

The skinny kernel is compiled with `make_fake_tensor`, which marks only K as unit stride and leaves the row stride dynamic, and it indexes A through its CuTe layout. Only the Python guards required contiguity. The change:

- `ShapeDynamicSkinnyGemm.__call__` no longer requires `a.is_contiguous()`; `row_stride_ok` requires `a.stride(1) == 1` and checks that the row stride and base pointer keep the `vector_width` loads aligned. Both the kernel entry point and the Qwen4Exp dispatch use it, so an unaligned slice falls back to `F.linear` instead of raising.
- The weight must still be packed.

Same class of silent fallback as #53109 (packed outputs so the Kimi-K3 `q_b_proj` keeps its fast path) and #54565 (row-strided inputs for the DSV3 GEMM).

Not in this PR: Qwen4Exp plans only cover M in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}. Speculative decoding verify widths that are not padded to a planned size (for example M=5 with MTP-4 and default capture sizes) also fall back to cuBLAS. That needs plan or warmup changes and is left for a follow-up.

Duplicate check: the open Qwen4Exp skinny PRs (#59632, #59869, #57848) only edit plan tables, not the input guards.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and the patch. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements above on DGX Spark.

title: [Model][GLM-5.3-Flash] Warm up the DCP top-k merge kernels for the kpool indexer
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59211 (now merged; this branch is rebased on main).

Under DCP, the GLM-5.x kpool indexer merges the per-rank top-k with `_merge_dcp_topk_global`, which runs `PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel` and `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`. Only `SparseAttnIndexer.__init__` registers these kernels for JIT warmup, so with the kpool indexer they were compiled on the first long-context request:

```
WARNING [jit_monitor.py:140] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel.kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config.
```

This PR registers them from `SparseAttnIndexerKpool.__init__` under the same conditions: DCP > 1, JIT warmup enabled, CUDA, and CuteDSL available. #59211 already makes the warmup keys use pool-level top-k and interleave for kpool models.

## Test Plan

`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on 8×H100 with `vllm serve`, bf16 KV cache, no MTP. TP8 + DCP8 with `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`, compared with TP8. GSM8K (1319 questions) at 5, 25, 50 and 100 shots, i.e. prompts from about 650 to about 17k tokens. Checked the server log for JIT monitor warnings.

## Test Result

`PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel` no longer compiles during inference under DCP8. Without this change, it compiled during inference in the same setup. The other JIT warnings in the log (`fused_moe_kernel`, kpool compress kernels) also appear without DCP and are unrelated.

| Shots | TP8 | TP8 + DCP8 |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.918 | 0.920 |
| 25 | 0.914 | 0.917 |
| 50 | 0.911 | 0.911 |
| 100 | 0.917 | 0.921 |

The E2E runs used the same local SM90 FlashMLA bf16 DCP change as #59211, which Hopper needs for DCP at head_dim 512.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs for kpool / `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` / `PackDCPTopkCandidates` warmup and found none. #54345 deals with prefill metadata JIT, not the DCP top-k merge kernels.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.
