title: [Core][Mamba] Remove leftovers of mamba_cache_mode="all"
author: ZJY0516
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #58997. Removes what was left of `mamba_cache_mode="all"` and deprecates `--mamba-cache-mode`, which no longer has any effect.

## Changes

- **KV cache manager:** `MambaManager` asserts that prefix caching runs only with `mamba_cache_mode="align"`. A `"none"` group under a caching manager used to silently run all-mode dense caching. Production never pairs them: `MambaModelConfig` ties `"align"` to prefix caching on and `"none"` to off.
- **CLI:** deprecated `--mamba-cache-mode`. `MambaModelConfig` already overwrote any user value (`"align"` iff prefix caching is on), so the flag is now ignored with a warning and will be removed in v0.33.0. ReplaySSM/RecoverSSM errors, config docstrings, docs, CI configs and e2e tests now refer to prefix caching instead of the flag.
- **Kernels:** dropped the APC per-block state inputs from Triton `causal_conv1d_fn` / `causal_conv1d_update`. No caller used them, and the non-APC path is unchanged. XPU is untouched.
  - Two all-mode leftovers are kept on purpose:
    - SSD's `return_intermediate_states`: #57329 uses it for Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoints.
    - CUDA `selective_scan_fwd`'s per-block state outputs: Mamba1 internal checkpoints will need mid-prefill state output from that kernel.
  - Conv-window checkpoints do not need the `causal_conv1d` inputs, because they are written from the pre-conv input.
- **Models:** removed the `supports_mamba_prefix_caching` flag. Its only reader was the all → align fallback deleted in #58997. Dropped the `SupportsMambaPrefixCaching` base from hybrid models, since `IsHybrid` already declares `get_mamba_state_copy_func(s)`. Only attention-free `Mamba`/`Mamba2` keep it.
- **Docs/comments:** fixed stale all-mode descriptions.
- **Tests:**
  - Mamba prefix-caching tests use `"align"`. `req0` is split so align keeps a state at the shared prefix.
  - Dropped `test_mamba_shared_prefix_survives_zero_retention`. Its flow is covered by `test_mamba_shared_prefix_reuse_under_zero_retention`.
  - The simple-offload DCP geometry test uses a replicated attention group.
  - `test_p_side_chunked_prefill_mamba` runs without prefix caching.
  - Fixed `test_mixer2_gated_norm_multi_gpu`, which also failed on `main`: its spawned workers had no vLLM config.

## Compatibility

- `ModelConfig.supports_mamba_prefix_caching` is removed. A leftover `supports_mamba_prefix_caching` class attribute is ignored.
- `--mamba-cache-mode` / `EngineArgs.mamba_cache_mode` is deprecated: ignored with a warning, removed in v0.33.0. Behavior is unchanged for Mamba models, since the value was already overwritten. `CacheConfig.mamba_cache_mode` stays and is still derived from `enable_prefix_caching`.

## Validation

GB200:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py   # 560 passed, 2 skipped
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k mamba     # 18 passed
pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py tests/test_config.py   # 546 passed, 5 skipped
```

`EngineArgs(model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B", ...).create_engine_config()`: no flag → `align`; `mamba_cache_mode="none"` with prefix caching → deprecation warning, `align`; `mamba_cache_mode="align"` without prefix caching → `none`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR covers these #58997 leftovers.

title: [Perf][GDN] Internal prefill checkpoints for the FlashInfer GDN prefill backend
author: ZJY0516
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Internal prefill checkpoints (RFC #52959) for Qwen GDN models (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5) on the FlashInfer GDN prefill backend. With prefix caching on (Mamba align mode), a prompt that crosses its cacheable block boundary no longer needs two forward passes: FlashInfer's prefill emits the boundary state in the same call. Kimi-K3 does the same with FlashKDA (#52789, #53614). Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) keeps main's split prefill and block: its PLE short-conv Mamba layer cannot export checkpoints, and the scheduler takes them only when every Mamba layer can.

## Claims

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 1x GB200, 8000-token prompts, on main `716961c`: TTFT −20% at concurrency 1, −12% at 4, −10% at 16. TPOT and accuracy are unchanged.
- Only enabled when the GDN prefill backend resolves to FlashInfer, prefix caching is on, and every Mamba layer of the model can export checkpoints; nothing is reserved otherwise. Triton/FLA, CuteDSL and ROCm are unchanged.
- No flags needed: align-mode blocks are put on FlashInfer's 64-token grid automatically (Qwen3.5-35B: 1056 → 1088 tokens), and only when the checkpoints are taken. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next keeps its 800-token block and main's TTFT.

## Validation

Setup: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B BF16, GB200, CUDA graphs, MRV2, `--enable-prefix-caching` (align mode; `--mamba-cache-mode` is deprecated since #60043). The baseline is main (`716961c`) with `--block-size 64`, so both arms use the same 1088-token block this PR picks automatically.

**TTFT** (`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 8000 in / 1000 out, `--ignore-eos`, 16 prompts per unit of concurrency, seed `100 + concurrency` so no prompt repeats across levels; prefix cache hit rate 0% in both arms):

| Concurrency | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 188.0 ms | 150.8 ms | −20% |
| 4 | 398.4 ms | 349.4 ms | −12% |
| 16 | 770.6 ms | 694.0 ms | −10% |

TPOT is within ±2%. The prompt's last block boundary sits at 7616 tokens: with a scheduler log, main ran all 336 prompts as 7616 + 384 tokens, and this PR ran every one in a single step with an internal checkpoint (FlashInfer emitted one state per prefill, `every_n=7616`).

Reusing one seed across concurrency levels makes the first prompts of each level repeat the previous level's, and those requests hit the prefix cache and skip the split in both arms; a run measured that way showed no gain at 4 and 16, so it is not used here.

**GSM8K** (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions; independent runs separated by `/`):

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 5-shot | 0.7915 / 0.8150 | 0.7779 / 0.7998 / 0.7908 |
| 20-shot | 0.3192 / 0.3177 | 0.3374 / 0.3245 / 0.3275 |
| 40-shot, MTP (3 tokens) | 0.7900 / 0.8082 | 0.7763 / 0.8036 |
| 20-shot, bf16 SSM cache | 0.3510 | 0.3412 |
| 20-shot, TP=2, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | – | 0.3677 |
| After merging main `716961c`: 5 / 20 / 40-shot MTP | – | 0.7915 / 0.3753 / 0.8135 |

- 5-shot prompts fit in one block, so no checkpoint is taken. The ~2-point spread between runs of the same arm is the noise floor.
- Qwen3.5 scores ~0.3 at 20-shot with a 256-token budget on both arms. Only the A/B comparison is meaningful there.
- The 20- and 40-shot runs take and resume from checkpoints (prefix hit rate 70–82% on both arms). With MTP, EAGLE block drop needs prompts longer than 2 blocks, hence 40-shot.
- The TP=2 run under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed without a sync violation.
- MRV1 not validated: main itself OOMs at KV-cache allocation in this configuration under MRV1. The checkpoint path is shared code in the GDN layer and metadata builder.

**After the review fixes** (`f3df8ff`, main `7fad7db`, default flags, so the block is the one this PR picks):

| Metric | this PR |
|---|---|
| Attention block / KV cache memory | 1088 tokens / 99.01 GiB |
| GSM8K 20-shot | 0.3601 |
| GSM8K 40-shot, MTP (3 tokens) | 0.7854 (mean acceptance length 3.55) |
| TTFT c1 / c4 / c16 (same benchmark as above) | 157.3 / 361.0 / 722.1 ms |
| TPOT c1 / c4 / c16 | 3.32 / 4.33 / 7.15 ms |

- The server ran with `--enable-prefix-caching` only and picked the 1088-token block itself.
- The 40-shot MTP run hits the prefix cache at 82%, so its requests resume from checkpoints exported with the MTP-sized conv cache.
- TTFT is 3–5% above the `716961c` run in the table above. Main was not re-measured on `7fad7db`, so that table remains the A/B comparison.
- With `7500dd1` (blocks aligned only when every Mamba layer can checkpoint), Qwen3.5-35B keeps the 1088-token block: TTFT 147.7 / 337.7 / 671.9 ms at c1 / c4 / c16, GSM8K 20-shot 0.3093.
- With `5089abd` (the plan reuses the checkpoint rows' query lengths): GSM8K 20-shot 0.3207, 40-shot MTP 0.7885, prefix hit rate 79% / 82%, so batches mix decodes and checkpointed prefills.

**Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP (3 tokens), `--enable-prefix-caching`, same TTFT benchmark; every arm on one GB200 node, main `7fad7db`):

| | main | `0b19574` | this PR (`7500dd1`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attention block | 800 | 832 | 800 |
| TTFT mean c1 / c4 / c16 | 282.1 / 354.8 / 437.4 ms | 408.3 / 506.4 / 600.3 ms | 279.6 / 358.5 / 450.2 ms |
| TTFT median c1 / c4 / c16 | 281.6 / 323.7 / 332.5 ms | 406.0 / 459.8 / 468.3 ms | 278.7 / 334.4 / 337.8 ms |
| TPOT c1 / c4 / c16 | 2.86 / 3.85 / 8.02 ms | 2.75 / 4.41 / 9.96 ms | 2.75 / 3.95 / 7.92 ms |
| GSM8K 20-shot, chat, thinking off | 0.9629 | 0.9689 | 0.9583 |

- Qwen4Exp's PLE layer is a second Mamba layer (short conv) without checkpoints, so the scheduler still splits its prefills. `0b19574` aligned the block anyway (800 → 832), which moved an 8000-token prompt's split from 7200 + 800 to 6656 + 1344. The 1344-token tail is above the 1024-token CUDA graph capture size and ran eagerly: 120 ms per step against 45 ms for the 800-token tail in a torch profile. Blocks are now aligned only when every Mamba layer declares an alignment, and the GDN layer then reserves no checkpoint block, workspace or checkpoint kernels.
- Raw-completion GSM8K scores 0 on every arm (the model ends few-shot completions immediately), hence the chat run.

**Tests** (GB200, `f3df8ff`):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py        # 5 passed (new export test x4)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py           # 62 passed
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py        # 8 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_checkpoint_state.py        # 14 passed
pytest tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py             # 46 passed
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py \
       tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py
                                                                 # 160 passed, 35 skipped (AMD-only)
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "checkpoint_grid or block_size"   # 14 passed (7500dd1)
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py           # 4 passed
# 0b19574, new:
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py::test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async_flashinfer   # 1 passed
```

- The new test in `test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py` runs FlashInfer with checkpoints and the exporter on a decode row plus three prefills, two of which checkpoint at offsets whose gcd is below both, and compares each exported recurrent state with a prefill stopped at its offset and each conv window with the raw input (both FlashInfer routes, fp32 and bf16 SSM cache). The conv cache has MTP's spec slots after the window; the test checks they stay untouched.
- `test_blocks_land_on_the_mamba_checkpoint_grid` checks that a Mamba layer declaring a 64-token checkpoint alignment moves Qwen3.5-0.8B's block from 544 to 576, and that nothing changes without one or when another Mamba layer declares none.
- `test_mamba_prefix_cache.py` scripts the align-mode split at the prompt's last block boundary step by step. On FlashInfer machines (its CI runs on H200) this PR skips that split, so all four cases failed at `prompt_2_block_size`; the align-mode LLMs now pin `gdn_prefill_backend="triton"`, which keeps the script's premise. ROCm and XPU already resolve to Triton.
- `test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async_flashinfer` (new, MRV2 + async scheduling, H200 CI job) scripts the FlashInfer schedule instead: 2B and 2B + 10 prompts run in one step, 10B and 10B + 10 in two (5B, then the rest with the 9B checkpoint), with the checkpoint block and state copies asserted at each step. It then checks the state a 2B + 10 prefill exports at B against the final state of a prefill that stops at B, over distinct tokens: the conv window matches exactly and the SSM state within 2.7e-3 relative error.

## Details

- **Kernel.** `flashinfer.gdn_prefill.chunk_gated_delta_rule` can emit a state every N tokens of each sequence (`state_checkpoints`, `checkpoint_cu_starts`, `checkpoint_every_n_tokens`), where N is a multiple of 64. On GB200, each emitted state matches a separate run truncated at that position (max abs err 5e-3), and the final state is bit-identical with checkpoints on.
- **Plan.** Computed once per step on the host from `MambaPrefillCheckpointBuilder`'s offsets, so the scheduler and `MambaManager` agree on which rows checkpoint.
  - N is the gcd of the batch's offsets.
  - The plan also has the per-sequence checkpoint counts and each row's index into the emitted states.
  - It uses the host copies of the offsets (from #57329) and of the rows' query lengths on `MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata`, so there is no device→host sync, and the counts and rows go to the device in one copy. It runs only in steps that take a checkpoint; at 16 rows the host work is a few µs.
- **Forward.** A step with checkpoints calls `fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule` directly with the plan; every other step calls `ChunkGatedDeltaRule` as before, whose signatures are unchanged.
- **Export.** Exporting a checkpoint is the same copy for every backend: the conv window ending at the offset, and one recurrent state picked out of a buffer the prefill kernel emitted.
  - `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter` was an ABC with one implementation (Kimi-K3's, in `kda_checkpoint.py`). That implementation now is the class, in `layers/mamba/checkpoint.py`, with an optional `recurrent_rows` that picks each row's state out of the buffer; by default row `i` holds checkpoint `i`'s.
  - GDN passes FlashInfer's buffer and the plan's rows, so the only copy is one state per checkpointed row; decode rows and rows without a checkpoint are masked.
  - `FlashKDAPrefillCheckpointExporter` stays as a subclass, so the Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash code is untouched. Mamba2's `ssd_checkpoint` kernel is the same copy with `chunk_idx` as the rows; folding it in is left to #61466.
  - GDN exports `conv_kernel_size - 1` columns of the conv window. Under MTP the conv cache has `num_spec` more, which the conv kernels never read (thanks @fuscof-ibm).
  - FlashInfer computes in an FP32 state (the wrapper upcasts), so the checkpoint buffer is FP32. The store casts it to the cache dtype.
- **Block alignment.** Offsets must be multiples of 64. Qwen3.5-35B's align block is 1056 (16 × 66), so every other checkpoint would be declined and fall back to a split prefill.
  - Mamba layers declare the alignment their checkpoints need through `MambaBase.get_prefill_checkpoint_alignment()`; GDN returns 64 when it takes FlashInfer checkpoints. When every Mamba layer declares one (`get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_alignment`), `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` makes align-mode blocks a multiple of their LCM (1056 → 1088). Otherwise the scheduler never takes internal checkpoints, so the block and the GDN spec stay as on main. sglang avoids this the same way, by keeping its Mamba cache grid at max(64, page_size).
  - The spec's `prefill_checkpoint_alignment` is the prefix-cache grid: the block, or `lcm(prefix_match_unit, 64)` when a finer match unit is set. A checkpoint off it falls back to the split prefill.
- **Workspace.** With every offset on the grid, FlashInfer's stride (their gcd) is a multiple of it, so a batch emits at most one state per grid step. The buffer holds `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, grid)` FP32 states, sized at profile time once the block is final: 16 states (32 MiB) on Qwen3.5-35B TP1 with 16384 batched tokens.
- **Warmup.** FlashInfer compiles separate CuTeDSL kernels for its context-parallel and regular routes, each with and without checkpoints. The GDN warmup now calls all four (`use_cp="auto"` and `False`). Before this, it only reached the route a single 64-token sequence takes, so the others compiled during serving (seconds on a cold cache).

**Tradeoffs.**

- The 64-aligned block is ~3% larger.
- Qwen4Exp gains nothing yet: its PLE short conv would need its own checkpoint export.
- With a `prefix_match_unit` finer than the block, the grid shrinks to `lcm(prefix_match_unit, 64)`, and the workspace and the states FlashInfer writes grow with it. In the worst case (a 64-token grid) this is 0.5 GiB and about 1 ms per 8k-token step.
- Validated on SM100 (GB200) only. FlashInfer also supports these checkpoints on SM90 and SM120.
- The shared Triton store kernel still compiles on first use, because its strides depend on the allocated KV cache.

**Related / not a duplicate.** No open PR adds internal checkpoints for GDN (searched 2026-10-05).

- #57329 (merged) does this for Mamba2; this PR reuses its host `offsets` on `MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata`.
- #61466 (draft) follows up: every Mamba layer declares its alignment through the same method, and the base spec derives the checkpoint fields from it.
- #50372 (open) edits FlashInfer GDN prefill state I/O in the same file; the overlap is mechanical only.
- #55873/#55875/#55876 add application-directed checkpoints via scheduler splits.

title: fix: exclude flashinfer-jit-cache from wheel install_requires
author: tarukumar
body:
## Problem

`setup.py` excludes `flashinfer-cubin` from `install_requires` because it is only published on the FlashInfer custom wheel index (`https://flashinfer.ai/whl`), not on PyPI. However, `flashinfer-jit-cache` — which is hosted on the same custom index — is not excluded.

The Dockerfile already installs `flashinfer-jit-cache` separately from the custom index:

```dockerfile
uv pip install --system flashinfer-jit-cache==${FLASHINFER_VERSION} \
    --index-url https://flashinfer.ai/whl/cu...
```

If `flashinfer-jit-cache` is added to `requirements/cuda.txt` (e.g. for pre-compiled JIT cache support), it would leak into the wheel metadata and make the published wheel uninstallable without the custom index configured:

```
error: No solution found when resolving dependencies
  cause: Because there is no version of flashinfer-jit-cache==X.Y.Z
         and vllm depends on flashinfer-jit-cache==X.Y.Z, ...
```

## Fix

Extend the existing `flashinfer-cubin` exclusion in `setup.py` to also cover `flashinfer-jit-cache`, keeping wheel metadata free of custom-index-only dependencies.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Honor speculative cacheability in SimpleCPU
author: SherifWaly
body:
## Overview

Fix lost CPU prefix-cache reuse during speculative decoding with eager `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. Share the GPU coordinator's per-group cacheability rule with CPU store selection, and pass the configured prefill lookahead to the CPU coordinator.

Related: #54736, which is already merged and provides the underlying per-group offload geometry.

## Claims

- Prevent the CPU store cursor from permanently skipping blocks whose trailing KV is still re-prefillable during multi-module MTP.
- Preserve the extra cached draft block required by hybrid speculative prefix lookup.
- Preserve existing GPU cache-publication behavior by extracting its eligibility calculation into a shared helper.

## Validation

[Complete public reproducer, exact model config, patches, commands, and structured before/after records](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217).

Both GPU A/B cases use native `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` with a reduced config and **dummy weights**, three MTP modules, BF16, TP2/DCP2, model runner V2, a 64-token prefill budget, and real GPU/CPU transfers. The before/after columns compare separate unpatched and patched engines. Full reuse means matching that prompt's GPU-reusable prefix; block alignment and speculative cache-safety rules leave a suffix to recompute.

### Serial: the missing block persists across two CPU replays

Run one prompt at a time (`max_num_seqs=1`). For each prompt, clear both caches initially, then run **cold → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay 1 → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay 2 → GPU-hot control**. CPU caching survives both intermediate resets.

| Prompt tokens | CPU replay | GPU-hot reuse, both arms | CPU before | CPU after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,257 | 1 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,257 | 2 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,321 | 1 | 8,192 | **8,064** | **8,192** |
| 8,321 | 2 | 8,192 | **8,064** | **8,192** |

Both CPU replays have **zero local GPU-cache hits** in both arms. The unpatched 8,321-token case stays one effective 128-token block short on the second CPU replay; the later 8,192-token GPU-hot hit is a separate local-cache control. Output token IDs match across all four phases and both arms (16 request outputs).

Raw records and checked summary: [`serial-before.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-before-jsonl), [`serial-after.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-after-jsonl), and [`serial-comparison.json`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-comparison-json).

### Concurrent: uneven prefill chunks can eliminate CPU reuse

Submit both prompts together (`max_num_seqs=2`). They share the 64-token prefill budget with `long_prefill_token_threshold=63`, allowing uneven 63/1-token chunks. Each arm runs **cold → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay → GPU-hot control**. Each row below identifies a different prompt in the same concurrent batch.

| Prompt tokens | GPU-hot reuse, both arms | CPU replay before | CPU replay after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,257 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,321 | 8,192 | **0** | **8,192** |

The 8,257-token prompt is an unaffected control: its 8,064-token CPU hit already matches its full GPU-reusable prefix. The 8,321-token prompt reproduces the bug: CPU reuse is zero before the fix and reaches its full 8,192-token reusable prefix afterward.

CPU replay has **zero local GPU-cache hits** in both arms. Output token IDs match across all three phases and both arms (12 request outputs). The later GPU-hot control cannot warm the earlier CPU replay.

Raw records and checked summary: [`concurrent-before.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-before-jsonl), [`concurrent-after.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-after-jsonl), and [`concurrent-comparison.json`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-comparison-json).

### Environment and additional checks

- **GPU environment:** 2× B200, driver 580.126.20; public image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:584c6bc58f76411936e0f22a37039e436019e155ae144c017b7eebbe2edc1d4e`; vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`. Only the two production files in this PR are patched in the fixed arm. They are identical at the image's source revision and the PR base `30d4032363d4a1f6412d9a235049673b41309f98`.
- **New CPU regression on the PR base:** baseline **12 failed / 6 passed**; patched **18 passed**, included in the **78/78** passing offload scheduler tests. The matrix covers replicated SWA, replicated full-attention, and sharded full-attention drafts; dense/latest-only retention; small/large chunks and multi-token prefill lookahead. It checks GPU/CPU hit equivalence and the loaded block hashes using real cache managers with simulated transfer completion.
- **Existing prefix-cache coverage:** **31 passed**, selecting EAGLE, cache publication, retention, and per-group DCP tests.
- **Code checks:** all applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy 3.10, and CI test tethering; the additional mypy 3.12 check and `git diff --check` passed.
- The added cases extend the existing offload scheduler suite already run by `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

The tables report one serial A/B and one concurrent A/B. They establish cache/transfer consistency, not trained-model accuracy or production throughput. Elapsed times include warmup effects and are not used to claim a speedup. Both cases exercise sharded MTP; replicated SWA is covered by the CPU matrix. A trained-model accuracy evaluation is not included.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Download the linked gist into a fresh directory for each case. This command selects the concurrent case:

```bash
mkdir -p models/tiny_mtp
cp config.json models/tiny_mtp/config.json
docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --ipc=host \
  -e REPRO_CASE=concurrent \
  -v "$PWD:/repro" --entrypoint bash \
  vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:584c6bc58f76411936e0f22a37039e436019e155ae144c017b7eebbe2edc1d4e \
  -lc 'REPRO_ROOT=/repro bash /repro/run_in_container.sh'
```

For the serial case, run the same command in another fresh gist directory with `-e REPRO_CASE=serial`. It runs both CPU replays with a GPU-only reset before each. Each invocation uses a fresh container so the baseline starts from the stock package.

The measured run used this image through Enroot; the equivalent Docker launcher above has not itself been run. The scripts and comparison logic are the measured versions. No checkpoint download is required. The wrapper enables serialization for its own offline layout-inspection RPC and starts no HTTP server.

CPU commands run on the PR checkout (`GIST_DIR` points to the downloaded gist containing the upstream logging fixtures; dependencies and the public OPT-125M config used by the existing test fixture are already installed):

```bash
# Run with only regression.patch applied to reproduce the baseline failures.
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q \
  -k test_dcp_draft_offload_preserves_prefix --tb=short
# Baseline: 12 failed, 6 passed.

# Run with the full fix applied.
PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$GIST_DIR" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  -p upstream_log_fixtures tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q --tb=short
# 78 passed, including all 18 new cases.

PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q \
  -k 'eagle or cache_blocks or retention or per_group_dcp' --tb=short
# 31 passed, 140 deselected.
```

Code checks (with the three changed files staged):

```bash
uv --no-config tool run --from 'pre-commit>=4.5.1' pre-commit run
uv --no-config tool run --from 'pre-commit>=4.5.1' pre-commit run \
  mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py
git diff --check
```

</details>

## Details

Eager CPU selection currently rounds confirmed tokens to a common alignment. This can disagree with GPU cacheability in two ways:

1. Multi-module MTP keeps `num_prefill_lookahead - 1` trailing tokens re-prefillable. A block can fall inside the CPU scan before the GPU has hashed it. Selection skips it as not hashed but advances the persistent store cursor, so it is never revisited after finalization. A missing early block can collapse the reusable CPU prefix to zero.
2. Hybrid speculative lookup matches an extra draft block and then drops it. GPU publication already allows this block past the aligned boundary, but CPU selection truncates it away, losing otherwise reusable prefix length.

`get_num_cacheable_tokens()` extracts the existing GPU eligibility calculation. GPU publication and eager CPU selection now use it, including the per-group draft-block rule. The CPU coordinator also receives `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens`, so both sides agree on finalization. This adds no GPU synchronization and does not change model computation.

**Duplicate-work check:** #54736 fixes geometry/fine-grained offload support, not this speculative eligibility mismatch. #58413 changes align-mode Mamba chunks in the separate `OffloadingConnector`; #54979 concerns terminal GPU cache registration; #50897 proposes a broader successor-aware hash/publication protocol. None implements this `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` store-boundary fix. Searches for open SimpleCPU/speculative offload fixes found no equivalent PR.

**AI assistance was used** for implementation, tests, reproduction, and this description.

title: [MoE] MXFP4 oracle: add CUTLASS W4A4 backend and BF16 activation fallback
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

First step of #54959 for the packed MXFP4 MoE methods. This PR only touches the MXFP4 oracle; no quant method changes behaviour yet.

**Contract.** The `activation_key` passed to `select_mxfp4_moe_backend` is the activation precision the checkpoint declares (`None` = BF16). Backends that match it are preferred. If none supports the deployment, the oracle falls back to BF16-activation backends and logs a warning, so a W4A4 checkpoint runs as W4A16 on hardware without a W4A4 kernel. Activations are never quantized below what the checkpoint declares.

Previously a non-`None` key was an exact filter, so a W4A4 checkpoint raised on any deployment without a W4A4 kernel (including `--moe-backend marlin`). This matches the MXFP4 linear kernels, where weight-only kernels already accept MXFP4 activation keys as a fallback.

**CUTLASS W4A4 backend.** `CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP4` (vLLM's `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`) is added to the oracle: enum, kernel class, scale swizzle in `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`, quant config and 128 round-up. Today that kernel is only reachable through device probes hand-rolled in `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` and `INCMxfp4MoEMethod`.

**Behaviour change for existing callers.** Callers that pass no activation key (gpt-oss) and callers of `select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend` (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3) select the same backend as main for every `--moe-backend` value I compared. Callers that already pass a key (online MXFP4, Quark W4A4 and static-FP8 W4A8) change only where main raises:

| Caller | `--moe-backend` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Online MXFP4 / Quark W4A4 | auto | raises | CUTLASS W4A4 |
| Online MXFP4 / Quark W4A4 | marlin, flashinfer_trtllm, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |
| Quark W4A8 static FP8 | auto | raises | TRTLLM BF16 |
| Quark W4A8 static FP8 | marlin, flashinfer_trtllm, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |
| gpt-oss with `quantization_config.moe.activation=mxfp8` | marlin, triton, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |

Measured on NVIDIA SM103 without `amd-quark`. I have not loaded a model through these newly reachable combinations, and could not measure ROCm. With `amd-quark` installed on CUDA SM100, W4A4 would select CUTLASS ahead of EMULATION.

**Relation to #59460.** The fallback is the default here; #59460 (`VLLM_STRICT_QUANT_SCHEME`) is the opt-in to refuse it. This PR passes BF16 fallback backends their own key, so whichever lands second should pass the checkpoint key through and let `executed_activation_key` report the downgrade, replacing the warning added here.

**Why this is split out.** #55232, #56306 and #56523 each move the CUTLASS swizzle into the oracle and each add a different selection path next to it (an `input_quant` flag, `select_w4a4_mxfp4_moe_backend`, a `candidates=` list). The mechanical part is the same in all three; the selection contract is what differs and what review has stalled on. This PR settles the contract in the existing `activation_key` argument, with no new entrypoint. A follow-up reduces the compressed-tensors and INC methods to weight creation plus oracle delegation.

Not a duplicate: those PRs change the quant methods; this one does not, and is intended as the base they (or the follow-up) build on.

**Follow-up motivation (measured on main, NVIDIA B300).** `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` selects `CutlassExpertsMxfp4` with MXFP4 activations for every checkpoint and every `--moe-backend` except `b12x`, including weight-only (A16) checkpoints, and fails on shapes that are not 128-aligned (`shape '[960, 34]' is invalid for input of size 36864`).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k select_mxfp4
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py -k oracle_matches
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py \
  tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_quark.py tests/quantization/test_auto_round.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py
pre-commit run; pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual
```

- `test_select_mxfp4_moe_backend_respects_checkpoint_activation` (CPU): exact match wins, BF16 fallback (auto and explicit backend), BF16 checkpoint never quantized.
- `test_cutlass_mxfp4_oracle_matches_direct_kernel` (SM100): the oracle-built kernel equals calling `run_cutlass_moe_mxfp4` with manually swizzled scales.

To check the API is sufficient, I also prototyped the follow-up (compressed-tensors method as a thin `Mxfp4MoEMethod` subclass that passes the checkpoint activation to this oracle) and compared it with main through a real `RoutedExperts` layer on a B300.

## Test Result

NVIDIA B300 (SM103): 2552 passed, 77 skipped, 5 failed across the suites above. The same 5 fail on unmodified main on this machine and are unrelated (Int8 unsupported on SM103, a DeepGEMM JIT panic, MXFP8 AutoRound). pre-commit and mypy pass.

Three of the four new selection cases fail on main and pass here.

Follow-up prototype vs main (layer harness, random MXFP4 weights, B300):

| Checkpoint / backend | main | prototype on this oracle |
|---|---|---|
| W4A4, auto | CUTLASS W4A4 | CUTLASS W4A4, bitwise equal to main |
| W4A4, auto, Renormalize routing | CUTLASS W4A4 | CUTLASS W4A4, bitwise equal to main |
| W4A4, `--moe-backend marlin` | CUTLASS W4A4 (flag ignored) | Marlin W4A16 |
| W4A4, hidden 1088 / intermediate 480 | reshape error | CUTLASS W4A4, padded to 1152 / 512 |
| W4A16, auto | CUTLASS W4A4 | TRTLLM BF16 |
| W4 + dynamic FP8 (group 128), auto | CUTLASS W4A4 | TRTLLM BF16 (fallback, warned) |

ROCm, XPU and CPU paths were not run; the ROCm selection tests are skipped on this machine. No model evals were run, since no quant method changes in this PR.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Cache per-request residency instead of rescanning every page each step
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse decode is CPU-bound on main because of one scheduler-side scan. Every step, `HiSparseCoordinator.all_context_pages_resident` walks every page of every scheduled request in every resident group (one group per layer), only to decide whether prefill can skip host staging. That is O(requests × context pages × layers) Python per step, even for pure-decode batches.

The scan arrived in c4b9b7deac ("bypass host resolution for resident decode"), after the GLM-5.3 results in #53781 were measured, and shipped with 3/N. This PR caches the requests whose resident pages are all non-null. A request is scanned once. Pages become null only at admission or host import, before the first scan, or when the pool reuses an unpinned page (`_lose_page`), so those paths plus `free` drop the cache entry. The per-step check is O(requests).

HiSparse-only change (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this scan.

## Results

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200, fp8 KV, block 64, random prompts, 1k output tokens. Each point is one run, main vs. this PR back to back on the same node and config. The gain tracks how much resident context the scan walks per step relative to GPU step time: it's largest when every page is GPU-resident and contexts are long. It disappears at low concurrency, and in the host-offload regime, where the old scan already exited at the first host page.

| TP | input | concurrency | peak KV | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ | mean TPOT main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 16k | 64 | 61% | 764 | 1209 | **+58%** | 73.3 → 42.0 ms |
| 4 | 16k | 40 | 76% | 809 | 906 | **+12.0%** | 40.9 → 35.7 ms |
| 4 | 4k | 160 | 89% | 2470 | 2583 | +4.6% | 57.7 → 54.8 ms |
| 4 | 4k | 128 | 70% | 2777 | 2882 | +3.8% | 40.1 → 38.3 ms |
| 4 | 8k | 64 | 64% | 1510 | 1551 | +2.7% | 35.8 → 34.7 ms |
| 4 | 16k | 24 | 46% | 744 | 760 | +2.2% | 26.5 → 25.8 ms |

For reference, the TP8 16k c=64 config without HiSparse gives 1302 tok/s and 39.2 ms TPOT. Single-run differences under ~3% are within noise.

```bash
# TP8: host_pool_gib 128; TP4: -tp 4 and host_pool_gib 64 (the host pool lives in /dev/shm)
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len <input+2048> --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":128}}'
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <input> --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts <2×concurrency> \
  --max-concurrency <concurrency> --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

Notes:
- The TP4 runs restarted the server per point and included the #60109 crash fix (#60117, cherry-picked) on both sides. Without it, reusing a server across points crashes.
- The TP8 row is a single fresh-server run of 128 prompts on main and on this PR; it has no prefix hits, so it doesn't trigger #60109.

## Test plan

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k hisparse`: 58 passed (CPU).
- `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py`: 17 passed (H100).
- Coverage: `test_hisparse_reports_when_context_is_fully_resident` and `test_hisparse_keeps_resident_pages_until_hot_buffer_is_allocated` already assert resident (which now populates the cache), make the pool reuse a page, then assert non-resident. Removing the `_lose_page` invalidation fails 3 of their cases, so no new test is needed.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Restore 32-bit buffer addressing for TRITON_ATTN KV cache views
author: umarkovi-amd
body:
## Overview



On ROCm, give the K/V cache views used by `TRITON_ATTN` a Triton `ptr_range()` bounded by their layer's region. This lets Triton's AMD backend keep 32-bit buffer addressing for them, fixing a ~16% throughput regression on RDNA3 introduced by #51718, which moved the KV cache into one backing allocation.

## Claims



- `TRITON_ATTN` throughput on Radeon Pro W7900 (gfx1100):
  - **+18%** for Whisper-large-v3: 5.34 → 6.31 req/s, back to the pre-#51718 level of 6.40.
  - **+18%** for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: 2.70 → 3.19 req/s.
- No accuracy change:
  - Whisper transcripts are token-identical on all 2,703 LibriSpeech validation-clean clips.
  - lm-eval GSM8K is within run-to-run noise.
- No change to KV-cache allocation, layouts, KV connectors/offloading or non-ROCm platforms, and no new configuration.

## Validation



W7900 (gfx1100) Base = this PR's parent, using the same build (the change is Python-only). Base and PR ran back to back on the same GPU.

| `vllm bench throughput` | base (3 runs) | this PR (3 runs) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whisper-large-v3, fp16, eager, LibriSpeech, 100 prompts × 200 tokens | 5.33 / 5.35 / 5.34 | 6.32 / 6.31 / 6.31 | **+18.2%** |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, bf16, `TRITON_ATTN`, CUDA graphs + compile, random 1024 / 256, 500 prompts | 2.698 / 2.698 / 2.700 | 3.191 / 3.197 / 3.196 | **+18.4%** |

| Accuracy | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Whisper, LibriSpeech validation-clean (2,703 clips), greedy, identical outputs | — | 2,703 / 2,703 |
| Whisper WER (simple normalization) | 4.410% | 4.410% |
| GSM8K, Qwen2.5-7B, `TRITON_ATTN`, 5-shot (strict / flexible) | 79.98 / 83.32 (repeat: 80.14 / 83.47) | 79.76 / 83.85 |

The GSM8K stderr is ±1.1. Base-vs-base differences are the same size as base-vs-PR.

<details>
<summary>Profile, code generation and lint</summary>

- **rocprofv3 kernel trace:** Whisper cross-attention, about 63% of GPU time, goes from 1,843 µs to 1,379 µs median per `kernel_unified_attention` call.
- **Code generation** (compiled into an empty `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`): with this PR, `key_cache_ptr`/`value_cache_ptr` carry `tt.pointer_range = 32` in `kernel_unified_attention` (VGPRs 256 → 205) and in `reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash`.
- **Lint:** `pre-commit run --from-ref main --to-ref HEAD` and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual` pass.
- **No new tests:** the change only affects code generation, and CI has no RDNA runners.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 FLASH_ATTENTION_TRITON_AMD_ENABLE=TRUE
vllm bench throughput --model openai/whisper-large-v3 --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --dtype float16 --max-model-len 448 \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openslr/librispeech_asr --hf-subset clean --hf-split validation \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":1}' --num-prompts 100 --backend vllm --output-len 200
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --attention-config.backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 500 --seed 0
# GSM8K: lm_eval.simple_evaluate(model=VLLM(pretrained="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", dtype="bfloat16",
#   max_model_len=4096, attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}), tasks=["gsm8k"], num_fewshot=5)
```
</details>

## Details



**Root cause.**
- Triton's AMD backend marks a pointer argument `tt.pointer_range = 32`, which enables buffer loads with 32-bit offsets, only if `arg.ptr_range()` or else `arg.untyped_storage().size()` is ≤ 2 GiB (`is_within_2gb`).
- Since #51718, each layer's KV cache is a view into one allocation (~36.6 GiB here), so the storage check fails.
- `kernel_unified_attention` therefore uses 64-bit addressing: 205 → 256 VGPRs, and occupancy on gfx1100 drops from 7 to 5 waves/SIMD.
- Bisected with only vLLM changing: #51718 measures 5.40 req/s, its parent 6.40.

**Change.**
- `set_triton_ptr_range(region, *views)` sets each view's `ptr_range()` to the bytes from its `data_ptr()` to the end of `region`, computed from shape and strides.
- `TritonAttentionImpl` calls it on ROCm for the K/V views in `forward` and in `do_kv_cache_update`.

**Safety.**
- The bound is the view's real extent, and Triton still checks it against 2 GiB at every launch. Layers above 2 GiB, or block-outermost layouts, keep 64-bit addressing.
- Both kernels only address within the view: through block-table indices or slot mappings, with padding slots skipped. This is the assumption Triton already made before #51718.
- Views are rebuilt every forward, and only host-side metadata is read, so there is no GPU synchronization.

**Duplicates.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `ptr_range`, `pointer_range`, buffer ops/addressing, 2 GiB, and #51718 regressions; none overlap.

title: [Fast Start] Preload the FlashInfer autotune table on the weight cache daemon
author: liusy58
body:
Extend the preload framework from weights-only to host-side artifacts and make the FlashInfer autotune table the first one.

The daemon gains a bounded, exactly-keyed artifact store served over its existing Unix socket, so any local process can fetch the table, not only the engine that owns the GPU. An engine that finds a table loads it and skips the autotune pass outright; an engine that has to tune hands its table back, so the pass runs once per GPU rather than once per restart. A hit still raises the Kimi K3 KDA projection-overlap limit that the pass sets on the model, since the table does not carry it.

`vllm preload --preload-autotune` runs one throwaway engine against the ready daemons so the pass and the JIT compilation happen at preload time, leaving the table on the daemons for every engine that follows. That engine resolves its defaults under the same usage context as `vllm serve`, since they feed the config hash the table is keyed by, and drops preload's disk-loader config, which its IPC loader would reject.

title: [Model][MoE] Load MegaMoE experts directly into the DeepGEMM layout
author: aoshen02
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE (also used by Kimi-K3) loads the routed experts into loader-side parameters, then `finalize_weights` asks the `DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend` (#58053) to transform them into DeepGEMM's layout and drops the loaded parameters, so any later `load_weights` has nowhere to write. The fused shared expert is built the same way, from a shared MLP whose weights the fusion then takes over.

This PR moves the layout into load time. The backend is selected when the experts are constructed, registers the kernel-layout tensors as the parameters (`create_weights`), and writes each checkpoint shard straight into them (`load_weight`). Whether the shared expert is fused is also decided at construction. Loading, reloading and updating weights then write into the tensors the kernel reads, and there is no MegaMoE post-load step left: `finalize_weights`, `finalize_mega_moe_weights` and the post-load hooks that only called them are removed (DeepSeek-V4 keeps its mHC hook).

## Claims

- `reload_weights` works with MegaMoE. DeepSeek-V4-Flash GSM8K after a reload: `main` 0.948 → 0.008, this PR 0.951 → 0.948.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 (MXFP8 shared expert) keeps its fused shared expert across a reload: `main` 0.898 → 0.010, this PR 0.904 → 0.901.
- An identity reload changes no parameter and moves no storage (0 of 1588 per-rank checksums, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP2).
- The shared expert has no second copy: its four kernel tensors are the parameters (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP2: 76.6 GiB, same as `main`).
- Kimi-K3 drops its `finalize_weights` override and the `_mega_l*` buffers.

## Validation

GB200, real weights, `vllm serve`, `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, EP. GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy.

| model, parallelism | `main`: GSM8K → `reload_weights` → GSM8K | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP2, MTP k=2 | 0.948 → **0.008** | 0.951 → 0.948 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 | 0.898 → **0.010** | 0.904 → 0.901 |
| Kimi-K3 (1.5T MXFP4), 4 nodes, TP4 × DP4, EP16 | 0.944 → 0.950, 137.52 GiB | 0.949 → 0.937 and 0.945 → 0.954 (two runs), 137.52 GiB |

The `main` column was measured before #58053; #58053 moved the transform into the backend but kept the post-load transform that drops the loaded parameters. On `main`, Kimi-K3 survives this reload only because the checkpoint is the same: its `finalize_weights` returns early once transformed experts exist, so reloaded expert weights never reach the kernels.

Neither DeepSeek run logs the shared-expert fusion fallback warning, so both keep the fused shared expert.

`tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py` (68 passed on GB200):
- Shuffled, per-shard routed loads (with EPLB replicas) are compared against DeepGEMM's batched transform, including the real DeepGEMM CUDA transform.
- A second routed load updates the kernel tensors in place.
- Shared-expert shards (gate, up, down; weights and 1x32 scales, both `.w2.` and `.down_proj.` names) land where DeepGEMM's transform puts them; reloading one shard overwrites in place and leaves the other half alone; the returned names are the registered parameters (for `enable_weights_track`).
- The fusion decision at construction: fused for DeepSeek-V4-Flash (e8m0 128x128) and V4.1 (uint8 1x32) scales; not fused for an older DeepGEMM, BF16 shared experts, non-UE8M0 scales or scales that do not tile to 1x32.

`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_weight_loading.py` is removed: it only checked that the removed Kimi-K3 finalize ran once.

`pre-commit` passes.

Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this change, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

Reviews: Codex (gpt-6-astra), Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5.1 audited this change. The two Codex should-fix findings (backend chosen for GPU 0 when the model is built on `meta` under `ipc_cache`; fused shared parameters reported under checkpoint names to weight tracking) are fixed and re-verified by Codex.

## Details

**Backend interface.** #58053's `transform_weights` / `transform_shared_expert_weights` / `supports_shared_experts(deep_gemm)` become:
- `create_weights(layer, ...)`: register the routed (and fused shared) parameters in the kernel layout, indexed by local expert on dim 0 (EPLB moves experts along it);
- `load_weight(dst, src, shard_id, is_scale)`: write one checkpoint shard into one expert slice or a shared parameter;
- `supports_shared_experts(shared_experts)`: decide fusion at construction.

A post-load transform cannot coexist with in-place weight updates, because it replaces the storage the loaders write into. A backend with a different layout (e.g. an SM90 plugin) expresses it in `create_weights` and `load_weight`. Out-of-tree backends written against #58053 need this migration.

**SM100 layout.** DeepGEMM's `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` interleaves gate/up rows in groups of 8 and permutes scale rows for UTCCP; the L2 weight is unchanged. Each row of each shard lands at a fixed position, so `load_weight` copies a shard into a strided view of its final location:
- L1 gate row `r` → `(r // 8) * 16 + r % 8`, up row `r` → `(r // 8) * 16 + 8 + r % 8`.
- Scales are the UE8M0 bytes expanded to one per 1x32 block, packed four along K per int32, stored MN-major, with the UTCCP row map `128b + 32j + i → 128b + 4i + j`.

Routed FP4 parameters are int8 (the kernel's dtype) instead of uint8; loads reinterpret the bytes.

**Shared expert.** Fusion requires FP8 shared weights with UE8M0 scales that tile to 1x32 (checked on the shared MLP's parameters, which its quant method creates at init) and a DeepGEMM with the shared-expert API. Otherwise it warns once and keeps the separate shared MLP, as on `main`, but at construction instead of after loading, so the layout never changes after load. When fused, `DeepseekV4MoE.shared_experts` is `None` and `load_weights` routes `shared_experts.*` tensors to the experts' four kernel-layout parameters.

**Backend selection.** The backend is selected for the device the model is built on, or for the worker's current GPU when that is `meta` (`--load-format ipc_cache`).

**Scope.** EPLB with a reload after a rebalance is broken on `main` and is not addressed. XPU keeps its own implementation.

**Not a duplicate.** #59003 (draft, stacked on #53509) also targets MegaMoE reload, but by staging new checkpoint sources and re-packing into buffers through a reload lifecycle. This PR removes the packed copy: the parameters are the kernel tensors, so there is nothing to stage or rebuild.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Route gfx942 sparse MLA prefill to AITER pa_prefill_sparse
author: frida-andersson
body:
## Summary

On gfx942, fp16/bf16 sparse MLA prefill with at least 512 query rows goes to AITER `pa_prefill_sparse`. Shorter calls stay on the in-tree kernel. The import and the `Using AITER pa_prefill_sparse for sparse MLA prefill on gfx942` log happen only when that kernel launches.

## What changed

- `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`: after the gfx950 OPUS attempt, call `pa_prefill_sparse` when the gfx942 gate passes. One KV pool. The caller output is passed as `out` when it matches `q`; a narrower output is copied from the kernel result.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py`: the dense Triton fallback test stubs the getter, so that case stays in-tree.

## Gating

gfx942, AITER enabled, `q` fp16 or bf16, `kv.dtype == q.dtype`, and `q.shape[0] >= 512` (`_GFX942_AITER_PA_PREFILL_SPARSE_MIN_QUERIES`).

The long-BF16 test still patches `on_gfx942()` so other ROCm devices take that routing decision. It pins `get_cdna_version()` to the physical chip first, so `pa_prefill_sparse` runs only on real CDNA3.

`pa_prefill_sparse` does not split the KV. Under 512 rows the call stays on the in-tree ragged prefill, which also does not. DeepSeek-V4.1 decode uses `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` and does not enter this function. The 2-row and 16-row shapes stay off `pa_prefill_sparse`. On this branch that is the in-tree kernel, not Gluon split-K.

## Depends on

[ROCm/aiter#6002](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6002). The symbol is imported only after the gate. A missing symbol raises on an eligible call. A short call does not import it.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Fuse per-layer slot invalidation and shorten the all-resident resolver path
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Cut HiSparse's per-layer decode overhead in GPU time and launches: fuse per-layer slot invalidation into one launch per step, mask CUDA-graph padding rows inside the resolver, and cheapen resolver arithmetic.

## Claims

- Slot invalidation: one launch per step instead of one per leader layer. On B200 with 78 index groups, each step drops from 374–759 µs to 3.5–162 µs.
- Resolver: 1.16×–3.69× faster per layer than main at every swept shape on B200, with bit-identical outputs.
- GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP8 B200, 16k/1k: mean TPOT −1.8% at c=16 and −0.5% at c=64.

## Validation

#### Microbenchmarks (B200, main vs PR kernels in one process, CUPTI device time)

Outputs are bit-identical between main and PR at every point.

**Slot invalidation per step** (78 = GLM-5.3 index groups):

| groups × tokens | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 61 × 64 | 367 µs (61 launches) | 9.9 µs (1) |
| 78 × 8 | 374 µs (78 launches) | 3.5 µs (1) |
| 78 × 64 | 634 µs | 13.0 µs |
| 78 × 256 | 759 µs | 59.1 µs |

**Resolver per layer** (top-k 2048, CUDA graph; main includes the padding `copy_` + `masked_fill_`):

| requests (rows/graph rows) | pages on host | main | PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 (64/64) | 0% | 9.2 µs | 4.6 µs | 2.00× |
| 64 (64/64) | 10% | 18.8 µs | 14.0 µs | 1.34× |
| 100 (100/128) | 0% | 15.3 µs | 4.8 µs | 3.19× |
| 64, MTP3 (256/256) | 0% | 20.0 µs | 11.4 µs | 1.76× |
| 100, MTP3 (400/512) | 0% | 48.8 µs | 13.2 µs | 3.69× |
| 128, MTP3 (512/512) | 100% | 54.7 µs | 47.2 µs | 1.16× |

PR is faster at all 36 swept points (1–128 requests, q=1/4, 0/10/100% host pages): 1.16×–3.69×.

#### End to end (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 8×B200, TP8, 16k in / 1k out)

Main and PR were run back to back on one node, interleaved, with 2 reps each and a server restart per point. Both have the same KV capacity (1.49M GPU + host tokens).

| concurrency | variant | output tok/s | mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | main | 802 / 809 | 15.84 / 15.67 |
| 16 | PR | 816 / 817 | 15.47 / 15.46 |
| 64 | main | 1265 / 1262 | 40.23 / 40.35 |
| 64 | PR | 1267 / 1270 | 40.12 / 40.02 |
| 64 | no HiSparse | 1327 | 38.27 |

Summary: −1.8% TPOT at c=16, −0.5% at c=64. That closes about 11% of HiSparse's remaining 2.0 ms TPOT gap to no-HiSparse at c=64; the rest is outside these kernels.

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len 18432 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":128}}'
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts $((2*C)) --max-concurrency $C --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

Benchmarks compare main at `d0c20bb840` with this PR at `ab5afbdab6`. The later merge of main only routes the op calls through the HiSparse platform backend (#62592), and the unit tests were rerun on it.

**Tests**

- [x] `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py` → 103 passed on B200. New test: `test_hisparse_invalidation_covers_every_index_group`.
- [x] `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` → 5 passed on B200.
- [x] GLM-5.3-NVFP4 serve A/B on B200 (above).

## Details

Cut HiSparse's per-layer decode overhead on the GPU and in launches:

- **One slot-invalidation launch per step.** Today it's one eager launch per leader layer after the forward graph. The kernel now runs over (written tokens × index groups) using a cached device table of each group's `device_global_indices`. `HiSparseRuntime.invalidate_written_slots` is replaced by `HiSparseSlotInvalidator`.
- **Resolver masks CUDA-graph padding rows itself** from `num_valid_rows`, one block per padding row. This removes the per-layer `copy_` + `masked_fill_` and the `request_ids`/`row_indices` buffers. On main, one block masks the whole padding run serially, which dominates the launch on padded batches.
- **Cheaper resolver arithmetic.** Power-of-two block math uses shift/mask (compile-time for 64-row blocks), and the first row's top-k is loaded before the request lookups resolve.

- `HiSparseSlotInvalidator` caches one device table of `device_global_indices` addresses per leader set. It is built on first use, so steady-state steps do no H2D copy. All index groups must share one hot layout (checked).
- Remaining HiSparse TPOT overhead at c=64 (~1.8 ms vs no HiSparse) is outside these kernels.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these kernels.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Size per-region replicate flags by each region's block count
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Background

With P_TP > D_TP (e.g. PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 decode), each decoder rank reads a block from several prefill ranks. Each local descriptor gets a replicate flag: full-attention regions are **SPLIT** (each rank fills its head slice), MLA regions are **REPLICATE** (whole block read once).

`_fa_desc_replicated` assumed every region holds the same number of blocks. HiSparse breaks this: host-resident MLA regions hold `hisparse_host_num_blocks`, GPU regions hold `num_blocks`. Every P_TP > D_TP handshake into a HiSparse decoder failed with `AssertionError: FA desc flags N != num_fa_descs M`.

## Fix

Build the flags the same way `_build_fa_local` builds the descriptors: same region order, `region_num_blocks[i] * block_size_ratio` per region. Companion fix for the same topology: #60108. No other open PR touches this function.

## Validation

**main vs. this PR**, checked against the descriptors `_build_fa_local` emits:

| Region layout | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Equal block counts | OK | OK |
| HiSparse, unequal block counts | assert | OK |
| Unequal counts that divide evenly | flags silently wrong | OK |
| Layer-name routing, region listed twice | flags silently wrong | OK |

**Unit:** `test_tp_mapping.py` + `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`: 121 passed.

**E2E** (GLM-5.3, 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 HiSparse decode, with #60108): main asserts on the first request. title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Return NumPy descriptors from mixed-memory local registration
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Overview

With mixed DRAM/VRAM registration (HiSparse host-resident regions), `register_local_xfer_handler` returned the local descriptors as a list of tuples instead of its annotated `np.ndarray`. The P_TP > D_TP split path (`_build_local_splits_from_plan`) calls `.tolist()` on them, so a PCP8/DCP8 prefiller feeding a HiSparse decoder failed the NIXL handshake with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist'`. Companion fix for the same topology: #60107.

**Fix:** keep the Nx3 `uint64` array in the mixed-memory path. DRAM rows get device 0 via `blocks_data[desc_is_dram, 2] = 0`, and the DRAM/VRAM subsets are array slices.

## Validation

**Unit:** `test_mixed_memory_local_descriptors_split_by_memory_type` now asserts the returned descriptors are an `np.ndarray` (fails before the fix). `test_tp_mapping.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`: 498 passed (3 GPU e2e tests left to CI).

| vLLM | Result |

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Fold q_b_proj and W_UK into one GEMM for the MLA decode query
author: nsusanto
body:
## Purpose

On the ROCm/AITER decode path every Kimi-K3 MLA layer spends two launches on the query
projection (M = 56 rows at the InferenceX c14 point, 12 heads per rank at TP8):

| Kernel | What it does | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hgemm_bf16_t16x32x128x5` | `q_b_proj`: x[56,1536] → q[56,12,192] | 6.76 | – |
| `_batched_gemm_a16wfp4_kernel` | absorb-in BMM: q_nope × W_UK (fp4) → ql_nope[56,12,512] | 5.49 | – |
| `_gemm_a16_w16_kernel` (aiter Triton `gemm_a16w16`) | x[56,1536] × W_fold[1536,6912] → [ql_nope \| q_pe] | – | 9.20 |
| **per layer** |  | **12.25** | **9.20** |

`q_b_proj` and the `W_UK` are consecutive linear maps, so
`ql_nope[h] = x · (W_UK[h] · W_qb_nope[h])ᵀ`. This PR builds once at load, from the bf16
checkpoint weights,

    W_fold[h] = [ W_UK[h] · W_qb_nope[h] ; W_qb_pe[h] ]        # [512 + 64, 1536] per head


**Decode only:** the W_UK absorb exists only on the MQA decode path. Prefill uses the
un-absorbed form and keeps `q_b_proj`, so any step with prefill tokens takes the original path.

**Small M win:** the fold reads 21 MB instead of 7.5 MB and does 2.5x the FLOPs. The save shrinks as M grows and would turn negative at prefill sizes, which this path never sees. 

We do additional 1.9Gb for the extra weight fold for all 93 layers of Kimi k3.

We're actively testing the prefill shape such that it cannot be much worse than non w-fold so that we don't have to pay for extra 1.9Gb.

## Server command:
```

  --trust-remote-code --moe-backend auto --tensor-parallel-size 8 --load-format fastsafetensors \

  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","max_cudagraph_capture_size":112,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,3,...,112]}' \
```

## Overview

Follow-up to #57084 (merged). Extends the `/pr-checklist` skill so that fixes involving disaggregated prefill/decode (PD) logic, such as the NIXL connector, include a minimal example of the flow being changed and/or the initial flow that caused the failure.

## Claims

- Adds one paragraph to section 4.3 (Root-Cause Analysis) of `.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md`: for disagg PD fixes (NIXL connector named as the example), make a best effort to include a minimal example of the changed flow and/or the initial failing flow.
- Links the existing disaggregated-prefill feature doc and the NIXL design docs for reference.
- Documentation/agent-instructions only: no code, PR template, or `AGENTS.md` changes.

## Validation

Docs-only change; no runtime behavior is modified, so runtime tests, model evaluations, and benchmarks are not applicable.

```bash

```

- `git diff --check`: clean (no whitespace errors).
- `pre-commit run --files .agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md`: all hooks passed, including `markdownlint-cli2` and the agent-instruction/skill checks (also enforced again by the commit-time hooks).
- All three linked docs and the referenced NIXL connector path exist at the linked locations.
- Reviewed the full diff: one added paragraph, no other changes.

### Duplicate-work checks (run 2026-10-05)

```bash
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --limit 30 "pr-checklist"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --limit 30 "skill in:title"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --limit 30 "checklist in:title"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --limit 30 "disagg PD flow"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --limit 30 "nixl flow example"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --limit 20 "57084 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --author NickLucche --limit 20
gh api "repos/vllm-project/vllm/commits?path=.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md&per_page=10"
```

- No open PR modifies the `pr-checklist` skill or adds a similar flow-example requirement; the only commit touching `SKILL.md` is the original merge `8fb16ea5` (#57084).
- No associated issue exists (this is a follow-up to a merged PR), so issue-specific duplicate checks were not applicable.

## Details

### Motivation

The review discussion on #57084 (njhill) suggested adding "pointers to examples of some of the points, in the form of prior PR or existing code sections / features that exemplify our expectations" as a later improvement. Recent NIXL / disagg PD fixes (e.g. #59953, #59586, #56341) show the gap this closes: the root cause often only manifests across the P/D boundary (scheduler admission, prefill execution, KV transfer registration/write, decode-side read), and a reviewer cannot trace it from the diff alone.

### Change

One paragraph added to section 4.3 (Root-Cause Analysis); see the diff for the full text. In short: for fixes that involve disaggregated prefill/decode (PD) logic, such as the NIXL connector (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/`), make a best effort to include a minimal example of the flow being changed and/or the initial flow that caused the failure, as a short numbered sequence (or diagram) of a request's path across the P and D instances, kept to the steps and components involved in the change.

Placement rationale: section 4.3 owns bug-fix PR contents (root cause), and section 4 applies to both authors and reviewers, so reviewers can also use it to request a missing flow example. The requirement is a "best effort" rather than a hard gate. The PR template and `AGENTS.md` are unchanged: the template's "Pull Request Contents" checklist item already covers root causes, and `AGENTS.md` already mandates the skill for agents.

### A/B test on #59586 (reviewer request)

> Ran the updated skill against #59586 (NIXL/disagg-PD bugfix). The only difference between skill versions is the new §4.3 paragraph:
>
> - Old skill: §4.3 passes on the prose root cause; no flow example requested.
> - New skill: §4.3 flags that the description lacks a minimal PD flow example. Draft produced by that check:
>   1. Startup (P and D): the runner picks a kernel block size per KV cache group from that group's backends (`prepare_kernel_block_sizes`) — the MLA group gets 128/256.
>   2. Startup (P and D): `_sync_block_size_with_kernel` picks one block size across all attention backends in the process; the drafter's backend supports only 64 → NIXL block = 64, `num_blocks` doubled.
>   3. Startup, failing flow: `register_kv_caches` builds the MLA view `[num_blocks, 1, 128, C]`; a kernel row spans two 64-token NIXL pages → `AssertionError: KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions` (silent variant: whole storage registered as one region with the 128-token row stride).
>   4. Serving, failing flow: P writes KV through those descriptors, D reads them → wrong bytes, no error.
>   5. Fixed flow: the contiguous MLA row is split into dense 64-token NIXL pages (`_uses_dense_virtual_transfer_pages`, now also for `tokens_per_state == 1` and `SlidingWindowMLASpec`); one region per layer, page-sized `block_len`/`block_stride`, identical on both peers via the handshake.
> - All other sections: identical verdicts under both versions. §1/§2/§3 pass; re-review items on #59586 (4 inline comments + 1 open question) remain outstanding there.
> - Fix verification: new unit test fails without the fix (`[256]`: the partition `AssertionError` above; `[128]`: silent wrong registration, `num_regions == 1 != 2`) and passes with it; full `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`: 224 passed.
>
> A/B run with Mistral Vibe.

### AI assistance

AI assistance (Mistral Vibe) was used to draft this one-paragraph change, run the duplicate-work checks, and prepare this description. Opened as a draft: per the `AGENTS.md` accountability policy, the human submitter must review every changed line before this PR is marked ready for review.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] MegaAttn: wo_a writes wo_b's MXFP8 input
author: Juntian777
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MegaAttn's (`FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`) `wo_a` einsum now writes `z` directly as MXFP8, together with the F8_128x4 UE8M0 scales that `wo_b`'s FlashInfer MXFP8 GEMM reads. `wo_b` therefore no longer quantizes a BF16 `z`, at any token count. It uses vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40 (merged), which adds the 128x4 scale layout to DeepGEMM's FP8 einsum epilogue. This PR bumps the DeepGEMM pin to it.

## Claims

- `_o_proj` drops the standalone `mxfp8_quantize` kernel. On GB200 it is 0.4-2.0 us per layer faster in decode (1-256 tokens) and 2.8-141 us faster in prefill (512-32768 tokens). The one regression is +0.6 us at 384 tokens (see Details).
- `wo_b` receives byte-identical FP8 data and scales, so model outputs do not change.
- Only `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` changes (+33/-5 lines vs main). Shared o_proj code and other backends are untouched.

## Validation

`_o_proj` alone (`wo_a` einsum, then `wo_b` CuTe-DSL MXFP8 GEMM) at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP1 shapes: 8 groups x 4096 -> 1024, `wo_b` 8192 -> 5120. Setup: 1 x GB200, CUPTI, full CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 3 rounds, both arms in one process. Software: torch 2.13.0+cu132, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, DeepGEMM a7a9277 + DeepGEMM#40. Outputs are bitwise identical at all 20 sizes measured.

| tokens | main (us) | this PR (us) | delta (us) | main: einsum BF16 + quant (us) | PR: einsum FP8 (us) |

| 1 | 26.2 | 24.9 | -1.3 | 10.9 + 2.4 | 11.2 |
| 4 | 25.5 | 23.8 | -1.7 | 10.9 + 2.4 | 11.2 |

The previous revision of this PR wrote MN-major scales, swizzled them with a separate Triton kernel (1.6-5.2 us per call), and was gated to 1024+ tokens. The E2E prefill (DEP4) and accuracy results below were measured on that previous revision and were not re-run. This revision only removes the swizzle kernel from the same prefill path, and it hands `wo_b` the same bytes. Decode E2E has not been measured.

Tests:
- vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40: all 7 tests in `tests/test_einsum.py` pass, including the new bitwise check of the 128x4 scales against the MN-major path.
- `tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py::test_quantized_o_proj_matches_quantized_bf16` now covers 1, 129 and 8193 tokens (decode, partial and multiple 128-row tiles), including CUDA graph capture and replay. It checks that `_o_proj`'s FP8 data and valid-row scales are byte-identical to `wo_b` quantizing the BF16 `z`. All 5 tests in the file pass on 1 x GB200 (torch 2.14.0+cu132, DeepGEMM with #40): `pytest tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py -v`.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, format, typos, shellcheck, mypy) passes.

## Details

- **Why the gate is gone.** DeepGEMM's einsum could only write MN-major packed scales, so `wo_b` needed a separate swizzle kernel. Below about 1024 tokens, that launch cost about as much as the quantization it saved. vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40 changes only the scale address in the einsum epilogue, so no extra kernel is left.
- **Gate conditions (unchanged).** The path runs when the einsum uses the per-32 recipe, `o_lora_rank % 128 == 0`, and `wo_b` is an MXFP8 kernel that accepts F8_128x4 scales (`can_fuse_query_quant`). It also requires no GEMM-RS, because the fused GEMM + reduce-scatter takes a BF16 `z` only.
- **Padded scale rows.** Rows past the last token in the final 128-row tile are not written. They only feed `wo_b` output rows that are never stored, so the test compares valid rows only.
- **384 tokens.** At 128-384 tokens (and at 2048 tokens), DeepGEMM's FP8-output einsum is slower than its BF16-output einsum, for example 17.9 -> 22.3 us at 384. The old MN-major scales show the same slowdown, so it is independent of this change. It is a DeepGEMM kernel-selection issue that can be fixed there.
- **DeepGEMM pin.** The pin points at `727f847`, the merge commit of DeepGEMM#40 on the fork's `dev` branch. The einsum selects the 128x4 scales with `use_128x4_sfd_layout=True`, which an older externally installed `deep_gemm` (vLLM prefers site-packages) does not accept.
- Merged `main` to resolve conflicts.
