title: [Bugfix][ROCm] RDNA3 W4A16 MoE: handle the N-first CT weight layout
author: JartX
body:
## Purpose

#52798 ("Use canonical N-first weight format for CT WNA16 MoE", merged
September 28) changed the layout compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE weights reach
the backends in, but the RDNA3 (gfx1100) path was not updated. Since then any
compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE checkpoint fails on RDNA3 at the first forward,
with an assertion on `w1_zp` in the experts.

Two things broke:

- `_process_weights_rdna3` still read the weights as K-first
  (`[E, K // 8, N]`, scales `[E, groups, N]`), which is what
  `moe_gptq_gemm_rdna3` needs, but they now arrive N-first
  (`[E, N, K // 8]`, scales `[E, N, groups]`).
- `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod` registered the synthesized zero points
  only for the CPU backend. The RDNA3 kernel needs them too, even for
  symmetric checkpoints (the oracle synthesizes them), so `w13/w2_qzeros`
  never reached the layer.

## What changes

- `oracle/int_wna16.py`: `_process_weights_rdna3` transposes weights and
  scales to the kernel's K-first layout before the exllama shuffle.
- `compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py`: register the synthesized zero points
  for `WNA16MoEBackend.RDNA3` as well as CPU.

Nothing changes for other backends.

## Not a duplicate

`upstream/main` (df417f780a) still has the K-first read. I searched open PRs
for `rdna3 moe`, `rdna3 w4a16`, `gfx1100 moe`, `moe_gptq_gemm_rdna3`,
`rdna3 compressed-tensors` and `52798`. The only open PR touching
`int_wna16.py` for RDNA3 is #59783, which adds a group-size check in backend
selection and does not touch weight processing.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py -v
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

- [x] A regression test, `test_process_weights_from_compressed_tensors_layout`:
  it builds weights the way compressed-tensors hands them to the oracle
  (N-first, packed `[E, N, K // 8]`, scales `[E, N, groups]`), runs them
  through `_process_weights_rdna3` and a full MoE forward (w1, SiLU, w2,
  top-k reduce), and compares with a dequantized PyTorch reference. The
  existing tests build the kernel's K-first layout directly and call the op,
  so they never exercised weight processing, which is why this regression
  went unnoticed.
- [x] End to end on 4x RX 7900 XTX with a symmetric compressed-tensors
  checkpoint (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B GPTQ W4A16, g32, `pack-quantized`): fails on
  `main` without this change, starts and passes GSM8K with it (below).

## Test results

On gfx1100, in an image built from `main` (df417f780a):

- Without this change, the new test fails for fp16 and bf16: the kernel
  rejects the weights (`group size (K/groups = 1) must be a multiple of 32`),
  because it reads N-first data as K-first.
- With this change (its `int_wna16.py` applied on the same `main` and mounted
  into that image; the C++ kernel is unchanged): the new test passes, and `test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py` passes
  in full (99 passed).
- pre-commit passes, except `update-dockerfile-graph`, which needs
  `/bin/bash` and could not run on my machine.

End to end, on an image built from `main` (df417f780a) for gfx1100, 4x RX
7900 XTX, TP4, `--dtype float16`, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B GPTQ W4A16 g32 (symmetric,
compressed-tensors):

- Without this change the engine fails at the first forward:
  `assert self.w1_zp is not None and self.w2_zp is not None`.
- With this change it selects `Rdna3WNA16Experts`, starts, and scores 97.5% on
  GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --num-questions 200
  --temperature 0.6 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 2048`, 5-shot, 0% invalid).

The two files of this change were mounted over that image; the C++ kernel is
unchanged. The stock RCCL in the image could not set up P2P between these
GPUs, so it was rebuilt; this is unrelated to this PR.

## AI assistance

I used AI assistance to find the cause and write this change. I have
reviewed every changed line and will run the tests above before marking it
ready.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode layer for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## Purpose

Opt-in (`VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`, meant as the one switch for every model's mono decode kernels) fast path for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode on MI355X (gfx950). Every backbone layer of a decode step runs on persistent FlyDSL launches:

| Launch | Layers | Stages |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | 30 standard layers | the mHC attention seam, then the attention front: wqkv, q/kv norms, the KV insert, wq_b |
| K2 | 30 standard layers | the attention back (split attention, combine, wo_a, wo_b), the attention TP all-reduce, the FFN seam, the MoE (router, top-6, shared expert, MXFP4 experts) and its TP all-reduce |
| FFN | the other 10 | after vLLM's attention seam and attention: the attention TP all-reduce (wo_b's unreduced output pushed to every rank), then K2's FFN seam and MoE |

All TP all-reduces run in-kernel over symmetric peer memory. K1 + K2 replace the ~40 kernels this path launches per standard layer today; the FFN launch replaces the attention all-reduce, the FFN seam and the MoE's kernels on the others.

**Scope**
- **Layers:** K1 + K2 on the 30 backbone layers with the standard mHC seam and no compressor or indexer of their own: 3–7, 9–13, 15–19, 21–23, 25–27, 29–31, 33–35, 37–39. The FFN launch on the other 10: layer 0 (embedding-broadcast seam), the Engram layer 1, and the compressor/indexer layers 2, 8, 14 (also Engram), 20, 24, 28, 32, 36.
- **Steps:** decode only, ≤ 48 rows (8 requests × 1 + 5 DSpark drafts), TP2 or TP4, eager or a FULL CUDA graph. K1 + K2 also need causal SWA windows and `fp8_ds_mla` KV records.
- **Everything else** runs as before: the DSpark draft layers, and prefill, mixed or larger steps. The paths take and return the same tensors at the layer boundary, so they interleave freely.

### Layout

```
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py   eligibility per layer / per step, vLLM tensors -> kernel inputs
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono/
    runner.py     DSV41MonoLayer: scratch, epoch, peer memory, the launches
    layer.py      K1 / K2 and the FFN launch, composed from the stages below
    attention/    attention stages
    stages/       seam.py (mHC seams, attention reduce), moe.py, moe_shape.py, moe_plan.py, router.py, gemv.py, dims.py
    common/       tagged mailbox, device ops, MX helpers, build keys, peer memory
```

`stages/` and `common/` are adapted from ROCm/ATOM's DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode (MIT License, commit 97359d6). Each adapted file names its origin and keeps AMD's copyright notice. The changes from ATOM:
- the seams are specialized to these layers;
- vLLM's numerics: f32 router logits, the shared expert reading vLLM's row-major FP8 weights, vLLM's `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` and `silu_and_mul_with_clamp`;
- hand-offs carry epoch tags instead of per-step mailbox clears, so no host step hook and the launches are graph-safe. ATOM's clears also wiped what another step width had laid out differently; without them each width gets a scratch of its own;
- ATOM's engine-side modules are dropped.

### Design

- **Weights** are read in place, with no second copy. The attention linears stay vLLM's row-major MXFP8 (32×32 E8M0 scales). The routed experts stay in AITER's shuffled MXFP4 layout.
- **Path selection.** The model is not torch.compiled, so the per-step decision is plain Python. It runs when a FULL graph is captured (uniform decode) and on every eager step. PIECEWISE (breakable) captures are always declined, because they are replayed for mixed batches.
- **wo_b's reduce on the FFN-launch layers.** Their `wo_b` is built with `reduce_results=False`, as the sequence-parallel path already does. A decode step hands the partial to the FFN launch; any other step reduces it in the decoder layer with the same `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`. ROCm's preshuffled-FP8 `wo_b` path now honors `reduce_results` as the linear does. This also fixes a bug on main: with sequence parallelism and an FP8-block checkpoint, `wo_b` was all-reduced and then reduce-scattered.
- **TP ranks stay in lockstep.** Every rank must take the same path at every layer, since the kernels wait on each other's pushes. The conditions read only metadata that all ranks hold alike.
- **Failure modes.** An explicit opt-in that cannot run raises: a CDNA version outside the kernels' (`get_cdna_version()` in `CDNA_VERSIONS`, CDNA4 / gfx950 today, so a later generation is one entry once ported), TP other than 2 or 4, FlyDSL missing, expert / data parallelism or EPLB, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4`, a routed-expert backend other than `AITER_MXFP4_BF16`, or fewer than 256 compute units (a partitioned GPU: every CTA of a launch must stay resident). The MoE and shared-expert tensors are checked for the kernels' shapes and dtypes at the first step, as the attention ones are. A layer outside the kernels' scope is logged once.
- **All-reduces are exact:** fp32 sum in rank order, then bf16. At ≤ 48 rows vLLM's own decode all-reduces are below the INT4 quick-reduce threshold, so the current path runs them exact too.
- **A scratch per step width.** Hand-offs between CTAs are tagged mailbox pairs in a scratch laid out per step width. Each width has its own scratch, allocated at its first (eager) step: 3–16 MB, and at most 8 widths under DSpark. So a word one width polls as a tag only ever holds tags. The MoE's task counters outlive a width and live in the epoch buffer.
- **Dependencies:** the `flydsl` wheel, plus two small AITER helpers that path already depends on: `aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.buffer_ops` (FlyDSL's wheel no longer ships it) and `UncachedIpcHeap` for peer memory.

## Duplicate check

- No open PR targets DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode. Searched "dsv41 mono", "DeepSeek V4.1 mono", "mono decode layer" and "dsv41_mono".
- The sibling mono-decode PRs are for other models: #59705 (MiniMax-M3) and #60216 (GLM-5).
- This PR hooks per decoder layer rather than replacing the model forward, because only 30 of DSv4.1's 40 layers are eligible.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` (CPU, wired into the MI355 Basic Models job): a decode step takes the mono path and hands the kernels `[blocks, block, 584]` cache views. A padded FULL-graph step takes it too (the kernels skip pad rows, whose slot is -1). PIECEWISE steps, prefill or mixed steps, more decode tokens than rows, non-causal windows, missing metadata, more than 48 rows and the first layer all take the original path. Deployments the kernels cannot run raise.
- `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` (4 × MI355, its own CI step). One layer with random weights in the checkpoint's formats, at TP2 and TP4: the kernels against the ops vLLM runs for the same decode step (the mHC seams, the ROCm attention chain, the all-reduce, `DeepseekV4MoE`). Each stage is checked on its own input, by cosine and relative error, for the whole layer and the FFN launch, at 1×6 and 8×6 rows. Then both widths' launches are captured in one graph and replayed 300 times, bit for bit against the first run.
- `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (same CI step). A five-layer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP2 and TP4 holding both layer kinds the mono path takes: the whole layer at a ratio-2 and a ratio-1 consumer, and the FFN launch at the sliding-window and KV / index-source layers. It is served with mono on and off on the same random weights, and every decoder layer's outputs at every decode token must match. It runs `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward` as the engine does, so a change to the layer that the kernels do not follow fails it.
- Race stress: the whole layer and the FFN launch in one HIP graph, 48-row and 6-row steps alternating, every intermediate compared bit for bit with the first run. 100K replays each on layers 3 and 9 (ratio 2) and 21 (ratio 1).
- Compile-only build (`COMPILE_ONLY=1`) of the in-tree kernels: K1 and K2 at TP2 and TP4, M = 6 and 48, both layer types.
- No regression of K1 + K2: K2's FFN half is factored out and shared with the FFN launch. K2 disassembles instruction-identical to the first commit's (TP2 M=6 ratio 1, TP4 M=48 ratio 2), and the whole-layer accuracy check reproduces its earlier numbers exactly.
- FFN launch, kernel level: against vLLM's FFN half (the attention all-reduce, `MHCPreDelayedOp`, `DeepseekV4MoE` with its all-reduce) on the real weights of the 10 layers, with the attention partial from a real ROCm attention chain. 48 points: TP2/TP4 × concurrency 1/2/4/8 × 1–6 tokens per request; the 10 layers chained in one HIP graph, cold weights.
- Kernel level (MI355X): the layer against vLLM's own modules (`DeepseekV4MoE`, the mHC seams, the ROCm attention chain, the all-reduce) in a TP process group, with real checkpoint weights. 96 points: TP2/TP4 × concurrency 1–8 × 1–6 tokens per request × the two layer types. Timing: 8 layers chained in one HIP graph, cold weights, vLLM's path captured under `graph_capture`.
- GSM8K: InferenceX's task, 5-shot, full 1,319, temperature 0, concurrency 8, DSpark block rejection; TP2 for K1 + K2 alone, TP2 and TP4 with the FFN launch.
- AgentX e2e with the InferenceX#3690 recipe (this tree's image, a8w4 MoE, INT4 quick reduce), golden DSpark acceptance 3.51, 3600 s per point, c1/c2/c4/c8 at TP2 and TP4.
- Accuracy, per RFC #59665: GPQA-Diamond and AIME25 at TP2, thinking on with `reasoning_effort` high, 8 requests in flight a server (every decode step within 48 rows), against the same build with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0`. Long context: RULER NIAH (single, multikey 2 and 3) at 32K, 128K and 256K.

## Test Result

**Unit:** 33 passed. **Compile-only:** all K1 / K2 / FFN builds compile.

**Numerics test (GPU):** passed at TP2 and TP4: every token's output cosine ≥ 0.9993 against vLLM's chain, relative errors 0.3–0.5% (bounds 1–1.5%; a routed scale off by 3% fails), 300 replays bit-exact. **Race stress:** no mismatch in 100K replays on each layer. Before the per-width scratch, layer 3 diverged at replay 13 on every run. **Model-level test:** passed at TP2 and TP4 (9 of 9 local runs of the final version; 40 of 41 of the TP2-only one before it, the failure not recurring and its log not kept). A routed scale off by 3% fails it at both sizes.

**Accuracy**, TP2, per RFC #59665 ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60397#issuecomment-6051909168)):
- pass@1, against this build with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0`;
- thinking on, `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, 8 requests in flight a server;
- ± is the standard error across questions; Δ is paired by question.

| | Reference | Mono |
|---|---|---|
| GPQA-Diamond (8 samples a question) | 85.3 ± 2.2 | 85.1 ± 2.2 (Δ −0.2 ± 0.6) |
| AIME25 (16 samples a problem) | 99.4 ± 0.3 | 98.3 ± 0.8 (Δ −1.0 ± 0.7) |

RULER NIAH, long context ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60397#issuecomment-6052301592)): single, multikey 2 and multikey 3 at 32K, 128K and 256K, 40 samples a cell. Every cell is 40/40 for both mono and the reference.


**FFN launch, kernel level, µs per layer** (vLLM's FFN half → the FFN launch, at 6 tokens per request). Every point is faster or at parity: TP2 1.01–2.14×, TP4 1.12–2.32×. The residual and the MoE input match vLLM's bit for bit at every point; the layer output's cosine is ≥ 0.99999, and every token's ≥ 0.9999.

| TP | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 136→81 (1.69×) | 181→128 (1.41×) | 241→215 (1.12×) | 345→342 (1.01×) |
| 4 | 111→57 (1.96×) | 147→85 (1.74×) | 176→140 (1.26×) | 234→209 (1.12×) |

**Kernel level, µs per layer.** Every one of 96 points is faster, 1.10–2.18×. Accuracy: residual cosine ≥ 0.99999. MoE output: 1,234 of 1,260 tokens at cosine ≥ 0.999. Each of the other 26 is a top-6 routing near-tie: the reference's own 6th/7th expert score gap is ≤ 3.2e-3, against medians near 1e-2. On the same FFN input the MoE matches vLLM's at cosine 0.99999.

title: Remove Python 3.10 support now that it is EOL
author: hmellor
body:
## Overview

Python 3.10 reached end of life this month, so the minimum supported version becomes 3.11. Follows the same shape as #26416, which dropped 3.9.

## Claims

- `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.15"`. The 3.10 classifier, the CMake supported version and the cp310 `triton-cpu` wheel are removed.
- `spinloop` and `fs_io_C` no longer need a Python 3.11 guard in `CMakeLists.txt` or `setup.py`.
- Version-gated code is simplified: `USE_SCHED_YIELD` in `vllm/distributed/utils.py`, the `sre_parse`/`sre_constants` fallback in `backend_outlines.py`, and the `co_qualname` TODO in `vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py`.
- `backend_outlines.py` imports `re._parser` and `re._constants` directly instead of going through `importlib`. `check_forbidden_imports.py` allows exactly that import, because `regex` has no equivalent.
- mypy runs once, on the minimum supported version, in a single `mypy` hook. The 3.12 and 3.13 CI-only hooks are removed, ahead of a move to `ty`, which will only check the lowest version.
- Ruff's pyupgrade fixes for a 3.11 target are applied: `typing_extensions` imports of `Self`, `assert_never`, `Never`, `Required`, `NotRequired` and others move to `typing`, and `asyncio.TimeoutError` becomes `TimeoutError`. `TypedDict` stays on `typing_extensions` because pydantic needs it before 3.12.
- `UP042` (`(str, Enum)` to `StrEnum`) is ignored for now, because it changes `str()`/`format()` output for 18 enum classes. That will be audited in a follow-up.
- Docs list Python 3.11 to 3.14, and the SkyPilot examples use `python=3.12`.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files, using the pinned ruff 0.14.0.
- `pre-commit run mypy --all-files`: the same 3 errors as `mypy-3.10` on `main`. They come from Linux-only `os`/`mmap` APIs and only appear when checking on macOS.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py`: 11 passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/structured_output -k outlines`: 22 passed.
- I checked the forbidden-import pattern by hand. `from re import _constants, _parser` passes. `import re`, `from re import compile`, `from re import _parser, compile` and `from re import _parser as p` are still rejected.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).

title: [Bugfix][Quant] Read safetensors headers of checkpoints with other file names
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Summary

A GPTQ checkpoint whose weights are not named `model.safetensors` fails to load whenever they are not already in the local cache, because the lookup that decides which layers are quantized cannot see the file and every linear layer is then built unquantized.

Failure in CI: [build 93298](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93298/list?jid=01a11652-3695-4590-86b6-eda1b6ced9ea&tab=output)

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.qweight'
in LlamaModel. The available parameters belonging to layers.0.mlp.down_proj
(RowParallelLinear) are: {'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight'}
```

## Cause

`modules_in_block_to_quantize` is optional, and older GPTQ checkpoints do not carry it, so `AutoGPTQConfig.maybe_update_config` derives the list from the safetensors headers. That goes through `HfApi.get_safetensors_metadata`, which asks for two fixed names only, `model.safetensors` and its index.

`LnL-AI/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-GPTQ-4bit` stores its weights in `gptq_model-4bit-128g.safetensors`, so the call always raises `NotASafetensorsRepoError`. That error is fatal, so it is raised without a log line and swallowed, which is why nothing shows up in the logs. The only remaining fallback reads the local cache, where files are matched by `*.safetensors` and the odd name is found, so a warm cache is the only reason this ever worked.

AWQ handles the same checkpoint shape correctly because it derives the complement, so an empty answer excludes nothing instead of excluding everything.

Nothing changed in `safetensors` or `huggingface_hub`. The local cache fallback added in #43197 has been masking it since, and this checkpoint only entered the test in #54809, so CI has only ever met it through a warm shared cache.

## Fix

When the fixed-name lookup fails, list the files the repo actually has and read the headers of every `*.safetensors` among them, the way the weight loader already locates weights. Only headers are fetched.

An empty module list now also means "unknown" rather than "nothing is quantized", so a machine with no network at all still loads the checkpoint. This is reachable only for GPTQ checkpoints without the field, and only when no metadata can be read by any route.

## Validation

Cold cache, the test that fails in CI: `1 failed in 21.16s` before, `1 passed in 52.56s` after. With the metadata forced empty, standing in for a machine with no network: `1 failed in 16.30s` before, `1 passed in 48.32s` after. Cold cache, both `test_quantization` parameters plus `quantization/test_auto_gptq.py`: `10 passed in 105.78s`.

title: [Perf][ROCm][Kernel] Add W4A8 int8-dot MXFP4 GEMV for RDNA3/RDNA3.5 d…
author: xiao-llm
body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in MXFP4 linear kernel for RDNA3/RDNA3.5 (gfx11) decode. For 1-8 tokens, activations are quantized to int8 per 32-element group, and each group is reduced with `v_dot4_i32_iu8` (`__builtin_amdgcn_sudot4`). E2M1 values times 2 are integers in [-12, 12], so weights map to int8 exactly through a 16-entry table; one fp32 multiply per group applies the E8M0 weight scale, the activation scale, and the 1/2. The approach follows ggml's MMVQ / q8_1 path (llama.cpp, MIT).

- Weights are read in the Quark OCP MX checkpoint layout (`[N, K/2]` uint8 E2M1, `[N, K/32]` uint8 E8M0). No repack, no extra weight memory.
- M > 8 (prefill) runs the same math as `EmulationMxfp4LinearKernel` (activation QDQ, dequant, `F.linear`).
- The M <= 8 / M > 8 split is inside a custom op, so torch.compile and CUDA graphs see one op.

Enable with:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8=1
```

Opt-in because int8 activation rounding differs from the MXFP4 activation QDQ the checkpoint declares. With the flag off, or on non-gfx11 GPUs, kernel selection is unchanged.

Related: #46676 adds a W4A16 (fp32 FMA) scalar + WMMA MXFP4 kernel for gfx1100. This PR is independent: a different algorithm for the small-M regime (2-5x fewer instructions per weight at M = 1-8). The two PRs only touch the same registration lists.

## Benchmarks

AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151, RDNA 3.5), `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`, single stream (`--max-num-seqs 1`), CUDA graphs and torch.compile on, `vllm bench serve` random 128 in / 256 out.

### Comparison with #46676 and emulation (MTP=3, MXFP4 lm_head)

Same model, same machine, all three with the lm_head quantized to MXFP4 (see note). GSM8K 5-shot, lm-eval `local-completions`, greedy.

| Config | Decode kernel (M <= 8) | Decode tok/s | GSM8K (questions) |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| **This PR + MXFP4 lm_head** | W4A8 int8-dot GEMV | **28.89** | **96.51% (1319)** |
| #46676 + MXFP4 lm_head | W4A16 scalar FMA (WMMA for M > 8) | 26.19 | 96.51% (1319) |
| Emulation + MXFP4 lm_head | dequant + `F.linear` | 4.94 | 96.75% (1319) |

- 10% faster than #46676 at equal accuracy, 5.8x faster than the default emulation path.
- For reference, llama.cpp (ROCmFP4 4-bit GGUF, own quantization incl. lm_head) runs 29.1 tok/s at MTP=3 on the same machine.

**Note on activations:** this PR skips the checkpoint's MXFP4 activation QDQ when the flag is on. Decode quantizes activations to int8 per 32-element group (finer than MXFP4); prompts (M > 8) use bf16 activations. Applying the MXFP4 activation QDQ on prompts while decoding with int8 activations dropped GSM8K to ~80% in our runs, so the prompt path is weight-only, matching #46676.

**Note on the MXFP4 lm_head:** the checkpoint ships the lm_head ([248320, 5120]) in bf16, and this PR keeps it that way. For the comparison above, it was quantized to MXFP4 at load time (round-to-nearest, one E8M0 scale per 32 weights), the same for all three configs. It cuts the lm_head from 2.54 GB to 0.68 GB; with MTP=3 the lm_head is read 4 times per step (3 draft + 1 verify), so this is worth ~6 tok/s (22.45 â†’ 28.89). It is not part of this PR and will be proposed separately.

The model card reports 95.0% (bf16 base: 93.3%) with sampling and thinking-mode settings

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_w4a8_rdna.py
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py
```

All pass on gfx1151. The new tests cover:

- output vs a reference implementation for M = 1..8, four shapes, fp16 and bf16;
- closeness to the bf16 dequantized result;
- M = 0 and M = 9 rejected by the op;
- `torch.library.opcheck`;
- CUDA graph capture and replay;
- dispatch for M = 1, 8, 9, 64 (kernel vs fallback);
- selection: chosen only with the flag on gfx11; MXFP6 and non-ROCm rejected.

Serve command used:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8=1 vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'   # MTP rows only
```

## Details

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `csrc/rocm/mxfp4_w4a8_gemv.cu` | int8 activation quant + W4A8 GEMV, templated on M = 1..8 and fp16/bf16 |
| `csrc/rocm/ops.h`, `csrc/rocm/torch_bindings.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt` | build and register `_rocm_C::mxfp4_w4a8_gemv` |
| `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp4/rdna_w4a8.py` | `RdnaW4A8MxFp4LinearKernel`, M-based dispatch in a custom op |
| `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py` | first in the ROCm MXFP4 kernel list (selected only when supported) |
| `vllm/envs.py` | `VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8` (default `False`) |
| `vllm/_custom_ops.py` | Python wrapper and fake impl |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_w4a8_rdna.py` | new tests |

- Device code is compiled only for `__GFX11__` (empty stubs elsewhere); the host entry point also checks for gfx11 at runtime.
- One wave per output column; lanes stride over the 32-weight groups along K, then a shuffle reduction. Accumulation is fp32 over the full K, one rounding to the output dtype.

Trade-offs and follow-ups:

- One extra activation-quant launch per linear (fusing it into the GEMV is a follow-up).
- M > 8 dequantizes per call, as the emulation kernel does; a faster prefill path is a separate PR.

title: [HiSparse] Read GPU-resident KV directly for mixed and BF16 prefills
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
Fixes #60420.

**Problem on main:** with HiSparse, a prefill batched with any decode copies its entire KV history into a temporary GPU buffer on every layer of every chunk, then joins the decode and prefill outputs with `torch.cat`. This happens even when all of its KV is already on GPU, which is the common case in aggregated serving. FlashMLA BF16 does the copy on every prefill. Startup profiling sees neither allocation. Two results:
- **Crash:** a long prompt arriving while other requests decode kills EngineCore with CUDA OOM, and the running requests die with it.
- **Slowdown:** the per-layer copy grows with context. A 1M-token prefill on FlashMLA BF16 takes 3.3x longer than without HiSparse.

**Now:** when all KV is on GPU, decode and prefill rows run in one kernel against the GPU pages, with no copy and no `torch.cat`. Covers FlashInfer, FlashAttn, FlashInfer SM120 and FlashMLA BF16 sparse MLA.

**Evidence:** 1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers with dummy weights, 2 requests decoding, then one 1.04M-token prompt. Peak is the largest per-step peak above the step's starting allocation.

```bash
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-NVFP4> --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 4}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
  --scheduler-reserve-full-isl \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":24}}'
```

| Path | main | this PR | no HiSparse |
|---|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer fp8, util 0.97 | **OOM at 934K** in `torch.cat`; peak 6.30 GiB | 58.6 s; peak 4.91 GiB | 53.7 s; peak 4.91 GiB |
| FlashMLA BF16, util 0.95 | 184 s; peak 6.58 GiB | 56.0 s; peak 4.48 GiB | 55.2 s; peak 4.48 GiB |

With debug logging, no host-staging calls happen with this PR.

**Tests**
- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` (B200): 509 passed. The resident-mixed routing cases in `test_sparse_mqa_hisparse_lanes` fail on main.
- GSM8K, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4 with HiSparse, 4×B200 (1319 questions, 5-shot, FlashInfer sparse MLA), two runs each: 0.896 / 0.914 vs main 0.914 / 0.909.
- After merging #55866 (shared HiSparse forward), the 4-layer repro at util 0.97 still OOMs on main (12b005eefa, in `torch.cat`) and completes with this PR.

title: [ROCm] [RDNA] [Perf] Add tuned configs for TRITON_ATTN kernel and swap places of TRITON_ATTN and ROCM_ATTN in priority list
author: nemanjaudovic
body:
## Purpose

On gfx1201 (RDNA4) and gfx1100 (RDNA3), swap `ROCM_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN` in vLLM's attention-backend priority list, so `TRITON_ATTN` becomes the default. This PR also adds launch configs for `TRITON_ATTN` on both GPUs, tuned with synthetic sweeps. With them, `TRITON_ATTN` is faster than `ROCM_ATTN` overall, including where `ROCM_ATTN` uses its HIP paged-attention decode kernel. The same configs are used with an fp8 KV cache.

This PR includes #60658 (closed), which had the launch configs only.

## Changes

**`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`:**
- `get_valid_backends()`, on gfx1201 and gfx1100: `ROCM_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN` swap places in the priority list. Nothing else moves.
  - **Exception:** an `fp8_e5m2` KV cache keeps `ROCM_ATTN`. `Attention` quantizes the query to fp8 only for `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` caches, and rejects `fp8_e5m2` for backends that take an fp8 query, as `TRITON_ATTN` does on gfx1201.
  - **Unchanged:** an explicit `--attention-backend`, and every other GPU (including gfx1200, gfx1101 and gfx1151).
- New `on_gfx1201()` helper.

**`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`:** only launch parameters change (`BLOCK_M`/`BLOCK_Q`, `TILE_SIZE`, `num_warps`, `num_stages`, split-KV segments) and, on gfx1201, the 2D/3D decode threshold. The kernels themselves are untouched.

How the configs are applied:
- They're looked up by the padded head size (`next_power_of_2`): head 96 uses the 128 configs, 192 the 256 configs.
- They apply to every attention variant (sliding window, sinks, softcap, ALiBi), because those are applied per element inside each tile.
- Batch-invariant mode keeps the default launch.

*gfx1201:*
- **Prefill / chunked / mixed** (`max_seqlen_q > 64`, GQA ≤ 16), as (`BLOCK_M`, `TILE`, warps, stages):

  | head_size | 64 < max_seqlen_q < 4096 | max_seqlen_q ≥ 4096 |
  |---|---|---|
  | 64 | 64, 64, 4, 1 | 128, 64, 8, 1 |
  | 128 | 64, 32, 4, 1 | 128, 32, 8, 2 |
  | 256 | 32, 32, 4, 1 | 128, 32, 8, 1 |
  | 512 | 64, 16, 8, 1 | 64, 16, 8, 1 |

  Decode-heavy mixed batches with `BLOCK_M // GQA > 16` and fewer than 16 new tokens per request keep the default. With an fp8 query (see below), only configs with `TILE ≥ 32` are used, so head 512 keeps the default.
- **2D decode** (decode batches above the split-KV threshold), as (`TILE`, warps, stages): head 64 (16, 1, 1), 128 (16, 2, 1), 256 (16, 2, 1), 512 (16, 8, 1). With an fp8 query, `TILE` is at least 32.
- **2D/3D switch:** pure decode batches with a 16-bit KV cache use split-KV (3D) up to `64 // num_kv_heads` requests instead of `128 // num_kv_heads`.
- **Split-KV (3D) segments**, head 64/128/256. vLLM always uses 16 segments per request, so the kernel launches requests × KV heads × 16 programs: too few for one request (1 × 2 KV heads × 16 = 32 programs on 32 CUs), and too many tiny ones for larger batches. This PR picks the segment count so that requests × KV heads × segments ≈ 128.
  - 16-bit query: 4 to 128 segments; `TILE` 16, 2 warps, 1 stage.
  - fp8 query: only more segments for small batches (head 256: about 64 programs); head 64 `TILE` 32 / 1 warp, others `TILE` 32 / 4 warps / 2 stages above 16 segments.
  - Sliding windows < 2048 keep 16 segments (head 64: `TILE` 32 / 1 warp, head 128: `TILE` 16 / 1 warp).
  - The scratch the metadata builder allocates is reused as rows × segments. The count depends only on the batch size and the model shape, so it is fixed per CUDA graph.
- **fp8 KV cache:** on gfx1201, `Attention` passes `TRITON_ATTN` an fp8 query; the rules above note where that changes the launch. The 2D/3D switch keeps vLLM's threshold with an fp8 KV cache.

*gfx1100:* applied after the 2D/3D choice, so the 2D/3D threshold is vLLM's.
- **Batches with prefill tokens:** three `max_seqlen_q` bands, as (`BLOCK_M`, `TILE`, warps, stages); "–" keeps the default.

  | head_size | ≤ 64 | 65–4095 | ≥ 4096 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 64 | 16, 32, 2, 1 | 32, 32, 2, 1 | 128, 64, 8, 1 |
  | 128 | – | 64, 32, 4, 1 | 128, 32, 8, 1 |
  | 256 | 32, 32, 8, 1 | 64, 32, 8, 1 | 128, 64, 8, 1 |
  | 512 | 64, 32, 8, 1 | 64, 32, 8, 1 | 64, 32, 8, 1 |

- **2D decode**, as (`TILE`, warps, stages): head 64 (16, 2, 1), 128 (16, 2, 1), 256 (16, 4, 1), 512 (32, 8, 1). `TILE` is raised to 32 with a per-tensor fp8 KV cache.
- **Split-KV (3D) segments:** `next_pow2(T / (requests × KV heads))`, at most 128, with `T` = 512 / 128 / 128 / 64 for head 64 / 128 / 256 / 512. Sliding windows ≥ 512 use 8× as many segments. Sliding-window decode switches to 2D at requests × KV heads ≥ 32 (head 64) / 8 (head 512).
- **fp8 KV cache:** gfx11 has no fp8 matrix instructions, so the query stays bf16 and the configs apply as they are.

**`tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py`:**
- New `test_rdna_prefers_triton_attn`. It calls `RocmPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls()` with a mocked arch. Expected selections:
  - gfx1201 and gfx1100 select `TRITON_ATTN`, for the HIP-kernel config (head 128, block 16, bf16, `auto` KV) and for an `fp8` cache;
  - `fp8_e5m2` keeps `ROCM_ATTN`;
  - an explicitly selected `ROCM_ATTN` stays `ROCM_ATTN`;
  - gfx1200 and gfx1101 keep `ROCM_ATTN`.
- Two existing tests that check vLLM's default order now pin `on_gfx1201()` / `on_gfx1100()` to False.

## How it was measured

All measurements call `TRITON_ATTN` (and, for the A/B, `ROCM_ATTN`) as vLLM runs them:
- vLLM's KV-cache allocator, and the backend's own cache writer, metadata builder and `forward()`;
- with an fp8 KV cache, the query is quantized exactly when `Attention` would;
- short-query batches configure speculative decoding, as a server would.

Every output is compared to an fp32 PyTorch reference (causal mask, sliding window, sinks, softcap, ALiBi), within 0.02 + 0.02·|ref|; with an fp8 KV cache, 0.25 + 0.1·|ref|.

Timing:
- each timed call reads its own copy of the KV cache, query and output, with ≥ 512 MB of KV across copies, so data comes from GPU memory and not from L2 / Infinity Cache;
- all copies run in one CUDA graph;
- time per call = graph time / copies.

**Tuning, in order** (each on gfx1201; gfx1100 used the same method):

1. **2D launch configs**, against `TRITON_ATTN`'s default launch.
   - Shapes: head 64/128/256 × GQA 1–16 × KV heads per GPU 1–8 × block 16/528 (138 shapes), plus head 512 (Gemma 4's global layers, 5 shapes).
   - Batches: 214 per shape (decode, prefill, chunked prefill, mixed).
   - Configs: `BLOCK_M` × `TILE` × warps × stages. A pilot timed every config on 2 shapes; a greedy cover kept the fewest configs within 2% of the best on every pilot batch.
   - Rule: per head size and region, the simplest rule (one config per band) close to the per-shape best, and ≥ 0.97× the default on almost every batch.
   - 29,532 measurements, 0 wrong outputs. Over the default launch on prefill-containing batches: 2.32× (head 64), 2.12× (128), 1.82× (256), 3.41× (512).
2. **2D/3D switch:** 3,888 decode and short-query batches, each run forced-2D and forced-3D. Under full CUDA graphs the choice is frozen per captured batch size, so the rule can only depend on batch size. Decode: half of vLLM's threshold; short queries: vLLM's.
3. **Split-KV segments:** 1,534 + 880 batches; segments 4–128 × 6 launch configs; head 64–512, GQA 3–16, KV heads 1–8, sliding windows, fp8. The best count follows requests × KV heads (about 128 programs), in both directions.
4. **Against `ROCM_ATTN`, through the backend:**
   - every HIP-kernel layout (4,245 batches);
   - a head-64 decode sweep: 16 launch variants × 256 batches (found the head-64 2D decode config: 1 warp);
   - a 1-warp sweep over every remaining regression cluster: 12 variants × 538 batches (chose 2 warps for split-KV; 1 warp lost everywhere except head-64 2D decode and short sliding windows).

**Final A/B: upstream vs this PR** (the results below).
- Two checkouts of the same vLLM build: upstream (`dde9aca41c`, this PR's base) and this PR.
- For every config and batch, each tree runs the backend it selects by default. Speedup = upstream time / PR time (> 1: this PR is faster).
- 14,608 batches; KV caches above 4 GB are skipped.

| region | what |
|---|---|
| `hip` | every layout where `ROCM_ATTN` uses its HIP decode kernel: head 128, block 16, bf16/fp16, GQA 3/4/5/6/8/10/12/16 × KV heads 1/2/4/8, plus softcap. Decode 1–64 requests × 1k–128k |
| `nonhip` | plain attention elsewhere: head 64/96/128/192/256/512 × GQA 1–16 × block 16/528, bf16/fp16 |
| `variants`, `fp16_variants` | sliding window 2048, sinks, sliding window 128 + sinks (gpt-oss), softcap, ALiBi; bf16 and fp16 |
| `fp8` | fp8 KV cache, plain and sliding window, head 64–512, block 16/528 |
| `prefill_mixed`, `qlen`, `spec` | prefill (128–8192 tokens, chunks on 16k–128k), mixed batches, query lengths 9–128, spec-decode verification (2–8 tokens) |
| `lowfill_3d`, `highconc` | 1–16 requests at every head size and block size (incl. 64k); 7–256 requests around the 2D/3D switch |
| `swa_decode`, `gptoss`, `blocksizes` | sliding windows 256–4096 (incl. Muse Glimmer); gpt-oss shapes; block 32/64 |

Batch families:

| family | batches |
|---|---|
| decode | 1–256 requests × 1k–128k context |
| spec decode | 2–8 new tokens per request |
| prefill | fresh prompts and chunks on cached context |
| mixed | 1–4 prefill chunks + 4–63 decodes |

## Results

### gfx1201 (Radeon AI PRO R9700)

Every cell: geomean speedup (worst) and batches below 0.97× / batches. 14608 batches; 313 (2.1%) below 0.97×.

**By head size, 16-bit KV cache, all attention variants**

| head size | decode | spec decode | prefill | mixed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 4.91× (0.76) 20/1615 | 5.14× (0.97) 1/382 | 1.62× (0.53) 17/275 | 1.83× (0.62) 6/146 |
| 96 | 4.68× (0.77) 37/412 | 25.25× (3.56) 0/124 | 2.96× (2.25) 0/80 | 3.25× (1.59) 0/31 |
| 128 | 1.68× (0.78) 154/4634 | 14.49× (0.98) 0/844 | 2.54× (1.39) 0/665 | 2.69× (1.18) 0/337 |
| 192 | 4.54× (0.87) 12/424 | 43.13× (9.56) 0/124 | 5.18× (3.69) 0/80 | 4.86× (2.68) 0/36 |

Causes, by cluster:
- **softcap:** the cost of the tanh softcap in the Triton kernel. Only Gemma 2 uses an attention softcap in vLLM (head 256, and head 128 at GQA 2), where this PR is faster; the head-128 GQA 3–16 and head-64 softcap shapes don't occur in supported models;
- **split-KV decode at 1k–4k context:** split / merge overhead when each segment covers few tokens;
- **head-128 2D decode at GQA 1–2, 8–64 requests,** and **head-256 2D decode at 32–64 requests:** `ROCM_ATTN`'s Triton decode kernel is a few percent faster there;
- **fp8 KV, head 64, one fresh 1k–4k prompt:** upstream's prefill reads the new tokens unquantized, while `TRITON_ATTN` reads them back from the fp8 cache.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Drop the unaccounted, write-only prefill mirror staging buffer
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

`initialize_hisparse_runtime_buffers` allocates a per-layer prefill mirror staging buffer (`num_layers × max_num_batched_tokens × row_bytes`) after the KV cache is sized, so memory profiling never counts it. That's about 0.69 GiB per GPU for GLM-5.3 (78 layers).

Nothing reads it: `HiSparseConnectorWorker.start_step` sets `mirror_from_resident = True` every step, so the host mirror always copies from the resident cache, and only dummy batches ever wrote the buffer. This PR removes it, along with `mirror_write_target` and `mirror_from_resident`.

Related: #60420.

## Test Plan / Result

1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 8 layers with dummy weights, MNBT 16384, HiSparse with `host_pool_gib=24`. Measured persistent torch memory after init, excluding weights and KV:

| | allocated beyond weights + KV | KV budget |
|---|---|---|
| no HiSparse | 0.7031 GiB | 112.99 GiB |
| HiSparse, main | 0.7756 GiB | 112.96 GiB |
| HiSparse, this PR | 0.7052 GiB | 112.96 GiB |

- Greedy outputs are identical on main and this PR (4 prompts, 300–7000 tokens).
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k "hisparse or profiling"`: 10 passed. The CUDA-only kv-update test now asserts only the resident write.

title: [Kernel] Remove WAR for LL CuTeDSL BF16 GEMM
author: jiahanc
body:
## Overview

The pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4772. With it, `mm_bf16(backend="cute-dsl")` falls back to cuBLASLt (with fused bias) when M > 32, and one autotune call profiles both M ranges. This PR removes vLLM's workarounds for the M <= 32 limit of the low-latency CuTeDSL BF16 GEMM, which were added in #50572 and #57285.

## Claims

- `--linear-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` BF16 linears no longer fall back to `F.linear` for M > 32. FlashInfer dispatches them to cuBLASLt with an autotuned algo and fused bias.
- Removes the supplemental 32-token BF16 autotune pass and the `autotune_bf16_only` / `ContextVar` isolation from #57285. The single `max_num_batched_tokens` pass now tunes every BF16 bucket: CuTeDSL for M <= 32, cuBLASLt above.
- Net -77 lines (+16 / -93).

Setup: 1x B300 (SM103), torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_flashinfer_bf16_gemm.py \
```

The existing correctness test gains two cases, M=64 (bias + PDL) and M=512, which cover the FlashInfer cuBLASLt fallback.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Remove invalid NC from Kimi-K3 KDA autotune keys
author: warrendeng
body:
## Overview

Both AMD and NVIDIA Kimi-K3 KDA kernels list `NC` in their autotune keys even though they have no `NC` argument. Older Triton ignored this unused entry but Triton 3.9 rejects it at import so this PR removes `NC` from both copies (fixes [test-infra #9028](https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/9028)).

## Claims

- AMD and NVIDIA KDA modules import with Triton 3.9, without changing kernel computation or the effective autotune key used by older Triton.

## Validation

  - With `torch==2.15.0+cu130` and `triton==3.9.0`, unchanged `main` (`a8260cbc5c`) fails during KDA test collection with `ValueError: key contains names that are not kernel arguments: NC`. Importing the NVIDIA copy separately fails the same way.
  - With the fix, both modules import, and `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only -q tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py` collects 102 tests. Local `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
  - On an AMD MI350 (`gfx950`), compared Triton-ROCm `3.8.0+git10f6be36` and `3.9.0+gitaad2a60d` with the same Torch build, GPU, inputs, and vLLM sources. The unpatched AMD and NVIDIA modules both fail to import on 3.9; both import with this fix. Both versions import on 3.8.
  - Ran the actual vendored AMD `chunk_kda_fwd_intra(safe_gate=True)` kernels on MI350. For a synthetic BF16 input (`B=1, T=1024, H=HV=12, K=128`, chunk size 64), the defined outputs on patched 3.9 were bit-identical to unpatched 3.8. A ragged input with sequence lengths `[63, 73]` also matched within `rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-6`

## Details

[Triton #11602](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11602) added validation of autotune key names. `NC = ceil(BT / BC)` is computed for the launch grid, not passed to the decorated kernel. The KDA test imports the AMD vendored copy first, masking the same bug in the NVIDIA copy.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Size the permute scratch from its inputs
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Stop predicting the MoE permute scratch capacity from `FusedMoEConfig`; size it from the inputs it actually receives, growing until the workspace manager is locked. This is intended as the root fix behind #55105 (DeepEP v2 + sequence parallelism) and #60423 (PCP), which each patch a different term of the same capacity formula for the `assert n_token <= self.max_num_tokens` failure in the Humming grouped path.

## Claims

- The Humming grouped experts no longer derive a row bound from `max_num_tokens * dp_size * experts_per_token`, so DP, sequence parallelism, PCP, and DeepEP v2's power-of-two receive buckets cannot make the scratch too small.
- The scratch no longer has a hidden-state buffer or dtype, which removes the `hidden_states.dtype == self.hidden_dtype` mismatch on the prequantized (block-FP8 activation) path.
- `CutlassExpertsFp8` and the CUTLASS W4A8 experts get the same behavior. They sized the scratch with `max_num_tokens` and no `dp_size` factor.
- One scratch is shared per `(num_experts, num_local_experts, device)` instead of one per `(capacity, topk, hidden size, dtype)`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "permute or humming or cutlass or block_fp8"` (1x B300) | 906 passed (with `tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py` and `-k "permute or humming or cutlass"`) |
| GSM8K, `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, `--moe-backend humming`, `VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped_contiguous`, 1x B300, eager (existing `configs/humming/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-humming.yaml`) | 0.8817 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| GSM8K, same model, DP=2 + EP, `allgather_reducescatter`, CUDA graphs, `--max-num-batched-tokens 3000` | 0.8969 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "test_reload_weights and FP8_DYNAMIC"` (1x B300, `VLLM_CUTLASS` FP8 backend, in-place weight reload) | 1 passed, 1 skipped; failed in CI before the shared-scratch fix |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PCP on 8x H20 (SM90), run by @wangyicong52 (results in #59857) | reported working; #60423 closed in favor of this PR |
| pre-commit on changed files, `mypy-3.12` | passed |

Not validated:

- The DeepEP v2 topology from #55105 is not reproduced here: DeepEP v2 is unavailable on the test machine (NCCL 2.29.7 < 2.30.4). @elvircrn, could you try this branch on your setup?
- The prequantized Humming grouped path (block-FP8 activations before dispatch) was not run with real kernels; in-tree coverage of `HummingGroupedExperts.apply` is mock-based. It is guarded by dtype and shape assertions.

## Details

**Root cause.** `workspace13`/`workspace2` are sized from the actual `M` and grow until `lock_workspace()`. `MoEPermuteScratch` was instead sized up front from config, which requires knowing how many rows every prepare/finalize backend can return in every topology. That bound is a property of the dispatcher, not of the experts, and it has been wrong for PCP, for DeepEP v2 with non-power-of-two capacities, and for CUTLASS with DP.

**Change.**

- `MoEPermuteScratch` holds only index metadata and gains `reserve(expanded_rows)`. It reallocates while the workspace manager is unlocked and raises `Scratch growth is not allowed after locking` afterwards, matching the shared workspace's contract.
- Permuted hidden states come from the caller's workspace. CUTLASS already passed a `workspace2` slice. Humming's prequantized path now writes into `quanted_gate_up_input`, which is allocated with the right shape and dtype and is otherwise unused when w13 quantization is skipped, so this costs no extra memory.
- The index buffers stay a persistent resource rather than moving into `get_simultaneous`: a second `get_simultaneous` call inside `apply()` would alias the live `workspace13`/`workspace2`, and `token_expert_indices` is an `arange` that would otherwise be refilled every call. They are small (seven int32 arrays over the expanded rows plus the sort workspace).

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- A runtime shape larger than anything seen during warmup still fails, with the same contract and at the same point as `workspace13`.
- `moe_permute(scratch=...)` without `permuted_hidden_states` now allocates that tensor per call. Both in-tree callers pass a buffer; `benchmark_moe_permute_unpermute.py`'s scratch numbers are not comparable to earlier ones.
- `get_persistent_resource`'s docstring is loosened from "must not resize" to "must not resize once the manager is locked".
- The CUTLASS experts use the same shared scratch as Humming. A scratch owned by the experts instance broke weight reload: the experts are rebuilt after the workspace is locked, so the new scratch was empty and could not grow (caught by `test_reload_weights` in CI build 93385).
- Anything that first reaches a scratch-using path after the lock, without that path having run during warmup, now fails where the old fixed-size scratch would have allocated lazily.

**Relation to open PRs.** Not a duplicate: #55105 and #60423 extend the capacity formula for one topology each and conflict with each other; this removes the formula. The DeepEP v2 handle-capacity change in #55105 (`next_power_of_2(ceil(max_num_tokens / sp_size))`) is independent and still useful. Searches for `MoEPermuteScratch` and `permute scratch workspace` found no other open PR.

AI assistance was used to analyze the capacity mismatch, implement the change, and run the validation above.

title: [WideEP] Explain how to fix a too-old NCCL for DeepEP v2
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Make a too-old NCCL for DeepEP v2 self-explanatory on pip/uv installs. PyTorch pins an NCCL older than the 2.30.4 that `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` needs (PyTorch 2.13 pins `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`). The Docker images override it since #45321, but installs outside the images fail with a message that states the requirement and not the fix. This does not change any dependency.

## Claims

- The startup log line and the `DeepEPV2All2AllManager` assertion now name the cause and the upgrade command for the installed CUDA major.
- `tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh` warns, before and after the build output, when the installed NCCL is too old for DeepEP v2. It does not fail, so DeepEP v1 builds are unaffected.
- `tools/ep_kernels/README.md` reflects the current PyTorch pin, explains that later `uv pip install` runs restore it without `UV_OVERRIDE`, and that DeepEP must be rebuilt after upgrading NCCL.

## Validation

On an environment with torch 2.13.0, `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`, and DeepEP 2.0.0:

```console
$ python -c "from vllm.utils.import_utils import deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason as r; print(r())"
DeepEP v2 requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 but found 2.29.7. PyTorch pins an older NCCL; upgrade it with `pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps` and rebuild DeepEP against it. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md.
```

The NCCL check from the install script, run in isolation against the same environment:

```console
WARNING: nvidia-nccl-cu13 2.29.7 is installed, but the deepep_v2 backend
requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 when DeepEP is built and when it runs. To use deepep_v2, run
    uv pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps
and then run this script again. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md.
```

pre-commit (including shellcheck and markdownlint) and `mypy-3.12` pass on the changed files.

Not validated: the full install script was not re-run end to end, the Docker build was not run (it sets `UV_OVERRIDE`, so the warning should not trigger there), and the available path (NCCL >= 2.30.4) was not exercised on a real environment. No tests were added; the change is message text plus a shell warning.

## Details

`has_deep_ep_v2()` now delegates to a new `deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason()`, so the log line and the assertion share one message. One behavior difference: an environment with a pre-v2 DeepEP installed now also gets the one-time INFO line saying `deepep_v2` is unavailable.

The alternative of forcing a newer NCCL through `[tool.uv] override-dependencies` in `pyproject.toml` was left out on purpose to avoid changing dependencies.

Not a duplicate: searches for `deepep_v2 NCCL` and `nccl install_python_libraries` found no open PR addressing this.

AI assistance was used to investigate and implement this change.

title: [Perf] Warm up DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernels before serving
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution -->
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepGEMM warmup covers `fp8_gemm_nt` and the grouped MoE GEMM. It does not cover `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` or the `bf16_mega_gate` that routes into it. With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 therefore JIT-compile these kernels on the first request at each new prefill size. This PR adds them to `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, following the structure of the two existing DeepGEMM warmups there.

## Claims

- No serving-time compiles of the MegaMoE kernels: `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, `bf16_mega_gate` and the Triton input-staging kernel. Before: 60 DeepGEMM compiles in one DeepSeek-V4 benchmark run. For Kimi K3, the 2 SiTU `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` compiles during serving that cost 2.6-2.9 s of TTFT each go to 0, at about +10 s of startup.
- MTP speculative decoding needs nothing extra. The DeepSeek-V4 MTP drafter's MegaMoE layer uses the same kernels as the target's, and there were 0 DeepGEMM compiles during serving with MTP on.
- DeepSeek-V4: the first request at a new prefill size no longer stalls for 3.5 to 6 s. It now takes about the same time as a repeat. The exception is a one-time 60-85 ms communication-buffer setup on the server's first large prefill, which is not a compile (see Details).
- Cost: for DeepSeek-V4, the first startup on a cold DeepGEMM cache takes about 4 to 5 min longer (+247 to +299 s on fully empty caches). A warm restart takes the same time as before. For Kimi K3, it is about +10 s.

## Validation

**Setup (DeepSeek-V4).** DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 2x B300, TP2 + EP2, `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384, `--max-model-len 16384`, prefix caching off, Model Runner V2. vLLM precompiled wheel `3ca00a82` (cu130) with its bundled DeepGEMM.

Each run used a fresh `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` seeded with every non-mega DeepGEMM kernel, so only the mega kernels start cold.

**Workload.** One request at a time: token-ID prompts to `/v1/completions`, `max_tokens` 4, streamed time to first token (TTFT).
1. Six fixed lengths (100 to 8000 tokens). Each gets a first request, then 3 repeats with new random tokens.
2. 40 seeded random lengths from 51 to 15504 tokens. The warmup did not pick these.
3. 32 concurrent requests.

**JIT compiles during serving.** Counted as new entries in the DeepGEMM cache dir between "Application startup complete" and the end of the workload, across all kernel families. Triton, CuTeDSL and TileLang compiles were counted with `--jit-monitor-verbose`.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sm100_bf16_mega_gate` | 58 | 0 |
| `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe` | 2 | 0 |
| other DeepGEMM families | 0 | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` | ≥1 (see note) | 0 |

On main, the Triton row comes from the default (non-verbose) JIT monitor, which logs only the first compile per kernel, so the true count is unknown. The previous revision of this PR, which warmed without a padding mask, compiled 3 variants for just three prompt lengths in a verbose run.

A separate single-GPU check called both kernels for every per-rank token count from 1 to 8192 after the warmup's representative sizes. It produced 0 new cache entries. An independent rerun of the patched server, with 20 prompt lengths, 16 of them chosen to give unaligned per-rank chunks, saw 0 JIT events.

**TTFT, first request vs median of 3 repeats (ms):**

| prompt tokens | main, first | main, repeat | this PR, first | this PR, repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| 2000 | 3503 | 106 | 112 | 103 |
| 4000 | 5913 | 119 | 178 | 117 |
| 8000 | 3489 | 136 | 141 | 136 |

- 40 random lengths: 24 of the 40 requests on main took 3.5 to 6.0 s. The slowest on this PR took 0.27 s. Total TTFT went from 90.1 s to 6.1 s.
- 32 concurrent requests: worst TTFT went from 8.33 s to 1.47 s.

**Startup, `init engine` (profile, KV cache, warmup, graph capture):**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cold mega-kernel cache (all other kernels cached) | 141 s | 428 s |
| fully empty caches, no MTP (separate tester run) | 444 s | 691 s (+247 s) |
| fully empty caches, with MTP (separate tester run) | 406 s | 705 s (+299 s) |
| warm restart, same cache dir | 63 s | 63 s |

KV cache sizing is unchanged: 163.13 GiB and 465,145 tokens in both.

**MTP (DeepSeek-V4, `--speculative_config.method=mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens=2`, same setup and workload):**

| MegaMoE compiles during serving | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| seeded cache (mega kernels cold), 1 run | not run | 0 |
| fully empty caches, 1 run (separate tester) | 2 `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, 10 `bf16_mega_gate`, 6 Triton staging | 0 |

On this PR's commit with MTP: the server was healthy, GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot) scored 0.970, and mean MTP acceptance length was 2.62 on GSM8K. On the random-token benchmark, acceptance was 1.61, against 1.55 on the previous revision. DeepGEMM compiles during serving: 0.

The drafter needs no extra warmup. Its MegaMoE layer reuses the target's kernels, and the tester's tracer saw no DeepGEMM compile in the drafter during serving on either build.

**Kimi K3 (`mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75`, a pruned checkpoint):** 4x B300, TP4 + EP4 with sequence parallelism, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192 (2048 per rank), fp8 KV, no prefix caching, no spec decode.
- Each run started with empty DeepGEMM, Triton, Inductor and vLLM caches. One run per build.
- Workload: one 3000-token request, a second 3000-token request with new tokens, then 137, 1500, 5000 and 8000 tokens.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepGEMM compiles during serving | 2 (`fp8_fp4_mega_moe` SiTU, `block_m` 128 and 192) | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` compiled during serving | yes (ranks 1-3, first request) | no |
| TTFT at 1500 / 5000 tokens | 2734 / 3139 ms | 153 / 244 ms |
| `init engine` | 46 s* | 56-57 s |

\*The main run had a warm FlashInfer JIT cache from an earlier run. The PR runs had one too, so the +10 s compares like with like.

On both builds, two non-MegaMoE kernels still compile during serving: the Inductor kernel `triton_poi_fused_mul_sigmoid_0`, on the first prefill above the capture sizes, and the KDA gated RMSNorm Triton kernel `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel`. They are outside this PR.

**Fully cold cache.** With every DeepGEMM and Triton cache empty (not just the mega kernels), three other DeepGEMM kernel families still compile on first use with this PR. They are outside MegaMoE and left for follow-ups:
- `fp8_einsum` in `o_proj` (`sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d`): 2 kernels.
- `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`: 8 kernels without MTP, 6 with MTP.
- The sparse indexer's `sm100_mqa_logits`: 1 kernel.

With MTP, the spec-decode rejection-sampler Triton kernels also compile on first use on both builds. That is unrelated to this PR.

**Tests.** `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py` adds two CPU tests:
- The layer predicate is False for other models, and neither model module is imported. It is True only for DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 MegaMoE layers.
- The warmup sizes for each `bf16_mega_gate` config are above the gate's token threshold, so the forward reaches the kernel.

All 8 tests pass.

**CI gap.** This path needs SM100 GPUs, DeepSeek-V4 or Kimi K3 with the native MegaMoE backend, and expert parallelism. CI has no such setup, so the validation above was run by hand.

<details>
<summary>Repro commands</summary>

```bash
# server (baseline: same command on main)
export VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=<fresh dir>
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --jit-monitor-verbose --port 8234

# client: fixed lengths x (1 first + 3 repeats), 40 random lengths, 32-request burst;
# records TTFT and the new DeepGEMM cache entries per request
SWEEP=40 python bench.py 8234 $DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR results.json
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>bench.py</summary>

```python
"""First-hit benchmark. Phase 1 (fixed): for each prompt length, one request
at a time: a first hit, then REPEATS more with fresh random tokens. Phase 2
(sweep, optional): random lengths the warmup did not pick, then a concurrent
burst (mixed prefill + decode). Records TTFT and every DeepGEMM JIT cache
entry created during serving, per kernel family."""
import collections, concurrent.futures as cf, json, os, random, re, sys, time
import requests

port, dgdir, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
LENGTHS = [int(x) for x in os.environ.get("LENGTHS", "100,400,1000,2000,4000,8000").split(",")]
REPEATS = int(os.environ.get("REPEATS", "3"))
SWEEP = int(os.environ.get("SWEEP", "0"))
URL = f"http://localhost:{port}/v1/completions"
MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash"
cache = os.path.join(dgdir, "cache")

def entries():
    return set(os.listdir(cache))

def family(e):
    m = re.match(r"(?:kernel\.)?(.+?)\.[0-9a-f]{32}$", e)
    return m.group(1) if m else e

def fam_count(es):
    return dict(collections.Counter(family(e) for e in es))

def ttft(prompt_ids, max_tokens=4):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    r = requests.post(URL, json=dict(model=MODEL, prompt=prompt_ids, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                                     temperature=0, stream=True, ignore_eos=True),
                      stream=True, timeout=3600)
    first = None
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line and line.startswith(b"data: ") and line != b"data: [DONE]" and first is None:
            first = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return first, time.perf_counter() - t0

rng = random.Random(0)
def prompt(L):
    return [rng.randrange(1000, 100000) for _ in range(L)]

start = entries()
print(f"entries at ready: {len(start)} {fam_count(start)}", flush=True)
rows = []
ttft(prompt(8))  # HTTP/tokenizer warm; 4 per-rank tokens -> no mega gate
for L in LENGTHS:
    for i in range(1 + REPEATS):
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        new = entries() - before
        rows.append(dict(phase="fixed", prompt_len=L, rep="first" if i == 0 else f"repeat{i}",
                         ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e, new=fam_count(new)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
after_fixed = entries()
sweep_lengths = []
if SWEEP:
    srng = random.Random(1)
    sweep_lengths = sorted(srng.randrange(17, 16380) for _ in range(SWEEP))
    for L in sweep_lengths:
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        rows.append(dict(phase="sweep", prompt_len=L, rep="first", ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e,
                         new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
    # concurrent burst: 32 requests, mixed lengths, 64 output tokens -> prefill + decode mix
    burst = [prompt(srng.randrange(17, 6000)) for _ in range(32)]
    before = entries(); t0 = time.perf_counter()
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(32) as ex:
        res = list(ex.map(lambda p: ttft(p, 64), burst))
    rows.append(dict(phase="burst", prompt_len=-1, rep="32 concurrent", ttft_s=max(r[0] for r in res),
                     e2e_s=time.perf_counter() - t0, new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
    print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
end = entries()
summary = dict(rows=rows, entries_at_ready=fam_count(start), new_during_fixed=fam_count(after_fixed - start),
               new_during_serving=fam_count(end - start), new_entries=sorted(end - start),
               sweep_lengths=sweep_lengths)
json.dump(summary, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
print("new during serving:", summary["new_during_serving"])
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Both kernels choose a JIT config from the per-rank token count:
- `bf16_mega_gate`: block tokens, MMA CTAs, split-K, expert groups and stages (`heuristics/mega_gate.hpp`). That is 87 configs for per-rank sizes 17 to 8192.
- `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`: `block_m` in {16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 240}.

Startup only compiles the sizes that the profile run and CUDA graph capture hit, here 512 or fewer tokens per rank. Every other prefill size compiles on first use, about 1.7 s per kernel. DeepSeek-V4 needs two gate kernels per size, because hash-routed and bias-routed layers pass different optional inputs.

**Design.** The warmup lives in `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, with the same parts as the existing DeepGEMM warmups:
- A layer predicate that matches DeepSeek-V4's `DeepseekV4MoE` and Kimi K3's `KimiMoE` when they use the native MegaMoE backend.
- A cache constant.
- `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values`: for every per-rank size, it asks DeepGEMM for the `block_m` and, for DeepSeek-V4, the gate config. It keeps the largest size of each distinct config (95 sizes for DeepSeek-V4 here), because DeepSeek-V4 only calls `bf16_mega_gate` above a small token threshold and a config's largest size is always above it. The configs come from DeepGEMM's own getters, so the dedup is exact and `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=full` would add nothing.
  - Kimi K3 routes with its `GateLinear`, which the bf16x3 router warmup already covers, so for Kimi only `block_m` matters.
  - Kimi's experts call the SiTU variant of `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, which picks `block_m` with the same heuristic.
- A private worker and a public loop, an `elif` branch in `_count_warmup_iterations`, and calls in `deep_gemm_warmup`.

The worker runs the whole MoE layer at each size, not the raw kernels:
- The gate gets the same optional inputs it gets in serving.
- Every EP rank runs the same sizes in the same order, which the collective MegaMoE kernel needs.
- It runs under a minimal forward context with a padding mask, because the layer reads `is_padding` from the forward context. This makes the Triton input-staging kernel compile the variants serving uses.
- Under sequence parallelism with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` on (the default), ranks above 0 get mask slices at any alignment, so each size runs once with an aligned slice and once with an unaligned one.

The predicate looks the model modules up in `sys.modules`, as other model-specific warmups in this package do (`kimi_k3_triton_warmup.py`, `qwen4_exp_qsa_warmup.py`), so other models import neither model. The cache key reads two DeepSeek-V4-only attributes (`tid2eid`, `image_sentinel_lo`) with `getattr`, because they do not exist on Kimi K3. The two config getters are reached through `_import_deep_gemm`, as in the model code.

`models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py` gains one line, which stores `use_sequence_parallel` on `KimiMoE` as `DeepseekV4MoE` already does. The warmup needs it to compute the per-rank token count.

<details>
<summary>Startup trade-off: where the cold warmup time goes</summary>

- About 84% of the cold warmup is serial `nvcc` time for 136 gate kernels (1.7 s each).
- About 14% is about 24 Triton staging variants.
- About 3% is 3 MegaMoE kernels.
- The layer forwards and the size search take under 1 s.

Compiling in parallel threads crashed inside DeepGEMM's JIT, which has no locking and no compile-only API. Parallel compilation would need DeepGEMM changes. vLLM keeps the DeepGEMM cache in `~/.cache/vllm/deep_gemm`, so the cold cost is paid once per machine and DeepGEMM version.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Remaining one-time first-request cost</summary>

The first eager prefill whose reduce-scatter falls in the MNNVL multimem size range sets up a symmetric-memory buffer (`_init_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_buffer`). This adds 60-85 ms to that one request (+61, +66 and +83 ms in three runs). CUDA graph capture skips this setup. It is paid once per server and is not a compile. A torch profile and a request-order test confirm both points.
</details>

**Limitations.** DeepSeek-V4 was validated only on 2x B300 with TP2 + EP2 and Model Runner V2, with and without MTP. Kimi K3 was validated only with a pruned checkpoint on 4x B300, TP4 + EP4, Model Runner V2.
- Not run: Model Runner V1, DP > 1, other EP sizes, EPLB, and routed-experts capture. With EPLB or routed-experts capture on, the warmup forwards would pass dummy tokens to the load recording and the capture hook.

title: [KV Offload] Align KVCR cache recency with request prefixes
author: mkhazraee
body:
## Overview

Use KVCR’s `align_sequence()` API to align cached blocks in request-prefix order after load/store completion and refresh the processed prefix when a request finishes. Finalization excludes in-flight work and the uncommitted final sampled token.

Depends on #57646, which exposes the request token counts needed to identify the processed prefix. No matching implementation was found among open PRs.

## Validation

Regression tests added in `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py` cover processed-prefix filtering, resident-prefix inclusion, and batching consecutive completions while preserving cross-request ordering. All pass.

AI-assisted implementation.

title: [Bugfix] Keep GPTQ linear layers batch invariant
author: yifanFengg
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` still runs the Marlin GEMM. Marlin picks its tiling and K-split from the number of tokens, so the reduction order changes with the batch size and the logprobs depend on the batch.

This PR makes the GPTQ path use `matmul_batch_invariant` directly: in batch-invariant mode it skips the Marlin kernel selection and repacking, keeps the checkpoint layout in memory, and unpacks the weight in `apply()`.

(The matching AWQ change was part of this PR until 2026-10-19 and was dropped: on current `main` the AWQ fallback is already batch invariant through #52231, which overrides `aten::mm.out`/`aten::addmm.out`; #60013, which this PR deferred to, was closed for the same reason.)

## Claims

- On `main`, `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` fails for `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4` (14 of 22 ids). With this PR all 22 ids pass.
- Accuracy is unchanged: `lm_eval` gsm8k on the batch-invariant path matches the Marlin path within noise, and the top-1 tokens of the two GPTQ paths agree on a fixed prompt set.
- Without `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` nothing changes: the same Marlin kernel is selected.
- Throughput in batch-invariant mode is lower than on `main` (numbers below): the GPTQ weight is dequantized on every forward and the model uses the batch-invariant Triton matmul instead of Marlin.
- New unit test checks the GPTQ unpack against vLLM's reference packer bit for bit.

## Validation

```text
======================= 14 passed, 14 warnings in 5.62s ========================
```

## Details

**Root cause.** `vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py` overrides `aten::mm`/`aten::matmul` through `torch.library` and exposes `matmul_batch_invariant` for callers; linear methods that run their own kernels have to opt in. `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` never did: it always builds a Marlin `MPLinearKernel`. The same pattern is why `UnquantizedLinearMethod` calls `linear_batch_invariant` explicitly.

**Change.**
- `auto_gptq.py`: with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` skips `verify_marlin_supported` / `choose_mp_linear_kernel`, leaves `qweight`/`scales`/`qzeros` in the checkpoint layout, and `apply()` unpacks the weight (`(q - bias) * scale` in the scales dtype, the same arithmetic as the Marlin dequantization) and calls `matmul_batch_invariant`. Without the flag the code path is unchanged.
- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_gptq.py`: `_dequantize_gptq_weight` is compared bit for bit against `gptq_quantize_weights` + `gptq_pack` for 4/8 bit, group sizes -1/32/128, fp16/bf16.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- The GPTQ weight is unpacked on every forward in batch-invariant mode, and the model runs the batch-invariant Triton matmul instead of Marlin. On the A10 this costs throughput in batch-invariant mode (blocks in section 6): the decode-heavy benchmark takes about 2.5x longer than `main`'s non-invariant Marlin path, the prefill-heavy one about 1.4x. Keeping a dequantized copy would be faster but would need the memory of the unquantized model, which is usually why a GPTQ checkpoint is used. A fused batch-invariant W4A16 Triton kernel would remove the cost; I kept that out of this PR.
- Only symmetric GPTQ without act-order is covered, which is what `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` supports today (`desc_act=True` is rejected at config time).
- `AutoGPTQMoEMethod` (GPTQ MoE experts) still uses Marlin MoE and is not batch invariant; #46639 covers that kernel. (The compressed-tensors wNa16 dense scheme was fixed separately in #60524.) This PR covers the dense GPTQ path that was tested.

title: [Perf] Reduce fallback decode CPU by 69% at 32K
author: spa5k
body:
## Overview

Fallback detokenization copies the full token-string history on every decode step, even though it reads only the trailing window. This change copies the required window and keeps the caller's absolute offsets.

## Claims

- **69% lower fallback decode CPU time** at 32,768 tokens per request in the final-output replay: **7.46 s → 2.30 s**.
- Decoded text and token IDs match the baseline. Prompt initialization and offset behavior are preserved.

## Validation

The replay runs the real `SlowIncrementalDetokenizer` caller on one CPU core, with four English, Chinese, Burmese, and emoji inputs and the Pixtral Mistral tokenizer. Each version has one warmup and three timed runs per size and output mode. Times cover all four requests. No model inference runs in this benchmark.

| Tokens per request | Output | Baseline CPU median (range) | Patch CPU median (range) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,192 | Final | 0.85 s (0.83–0.88) | 0.51 s (0.50–0.52) |
| 32,768 | Final | 7.46 s (7.34–7.62) | 2.30 s (2.26–2.33) |
| 32,768 | Streamed | 8.85 s (8.80–9.04) | 2.28 s (2.26–2.36) |

Live checks used Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512 on one L4. All 24 baseline/patch response pairs matched text, token IDs, finish and stop reasons, and usage. Four requests of 6,144 tokens showed no confirmed serving gain: request-time medians were 145.03 s and 145.23 s. API CPU medians were 4.64 s and 4.765 s, with overlapping ranges. The 69% claim applies to the replay above.

Tests run on both helper versions:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py -q -k '(gpt2 or Pixtral or long_history or prompt_window) and not logprobs_count'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -q
```

Each version passed **81 tokenizer tests and 94 renderer tests**. There were 91 existing skips, 660 deselected cases, and one expected failure. The added cases cover long Unicode output, the first-call prompt window, and offsets past the window. The 81 tokenizer tests passed again on both helper versions after the base update. Local pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy checks passed. Upstream CI is enabled. Its failed steps are being checked and retried.

## Details

`prev_tokens + new_tokens` creates the full-history copy before the helper takes its decode slices. The patch starts at the earliest required offset and adjusts the slice indexes within that window. It returns the full token count as the absolute read offset and keeps the initial prompt tokens. The window can still grow when text is incomplete. Other copies in the caller remain.

This removes a full-history copy in the Python fallback helper. The open prompt-priming PRs #51281 and #57330 change the fast `DecodeStream` path. PR #46723 changes the Rust frontend. These are separate code paths.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark reproduction and test environment</summary>

Use this [benchmark script](https://github.com/spa5k/vllm/blob/4d8b5db4daef6d5ef38332d0d2df57bdff47aa53/benchmarks/benchmark_fallback_detokenizer.py), saved as `/tmp/vllm_fallback_benchmark.py`. Run each command on the base and patch with the same tokenizer cache:

```bash
.venv/bin/python /tmp/vllm_fallback_benchmark.py --sizes 1024 8192 32768 --iterations 3 --output-json final.json
.venv/bin/python /tmp/vllm_fallback_benchmark.py --sizes 1024 8192 32768 --iterations 3 --stream --output-json stream.json
```

The tokenizer is `mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409` in Mistral mode. Compare text hashes and token IDs across versions.

Tests used Linux, Python 3.12, and the prebuilt [vLLM 0.30.1rc1.dev751+gad0f67a7e wheel](https://wheels.vllm.ai/ad0f67a7ec8f0393c8b4ae50a2a0e66672db372f/vllm-0.30.1rc1.dev751%2Bgad0f67a7e-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl), with the candidate Python files installed. The affected baseline sources matched the checked PR base. This was a wheel-based environment; the full current source tree was not compiled. No compiled code changed. Dependencies included PyTorch 2.13.0, Transformers 5.18.0, and mistral_common 1.12.0.

</details>
