Because `Gemma4Unified` is encoder-free (no ViT tower), we list both the total `llm.generate()` latency (which includes CPU PIL image preprocessing + the 40-layer 12B LLM) and the deterministic GPU savings from `_process_image_input` (Suite 1) for the corresponding total image count (`Batch Size * Num Images`).* | Model | Case | Batch Size | Imgs/Req (Total Imgs) | Max Tokens | Base E2E (ms) | Feat E2E (ms) | Isolated Vision Embedder Δ (ms) | E2E Speedup | Token Match | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_1img_bs1 | 1 | 1 (1) | 1 | 72.69 | 70.43 | -0.11 ms (1.22 -> 1.11) | **1.03x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_1img_bs2 | 2 | 1 (2) | 1 | 122.67 | 118.89 | -1.02 ms (2.27 -> 1.25) | **1.03x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_1img_bs4 | 4 | 1 (4) | 1 | 216.97 | 210.18 | -2.91 ms (4.44 -> 1.53) | **1.03x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_1img_bs8 | 8 | 1 (8) | 1 | 408.97 | 393.92 | -6.34 ms (8.72 -> 2.38) | **1.04x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_4img_bs1 | 1 | 4 (4) | 1 | 233.87 | 228.26 | -2.96 ms (4.45 -> 1.49) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_4img_bs2 | 2 | 4 (8) | 1 | 440.64 | 434.88 | -6.59 ms (8.83 -> 2.24) | **1.01x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_4img_bs4 | 4 | 4 (16) | 1 | 859.29 | 838.22 | -13.87 ms (17.70 -> 3.83) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_serving_e2e_bs1 | 1 | 2 (2) | 16 | 387.77 | 382.00 | -1.02 ms (2.27 -> 1.25) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_serving_e2e_bs2 | 2 | 2 (4) | 16 | 475.80 | 468.50 | -2.91 ms (4.44 -> 1.53) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_serving_e2e_bs4 | 4 | 2 (8) | 16 | 675.28 | 660.30 | -6.34 ms (8.72 -> 2.38) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_serving_e2e_bs8 | 8 | 2 (16) | 16 | 1076.41 | 1031.63 | -13.55 ms (17.59 -> 4.04) | **1.04x** | 100.0% | ## Technical Details ### Root Cause Analysis In `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` (`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py`): 1. **Un-vectorized 2D Position Embedding Kernel**: `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb` previously computed factorized 2D sinusoidal position embeddings using separate PyTorch operations: slicing coordinate channels, executing multiple 3D tensor indexing lookups (`self.pos_embedding[clamped_pos[..., 0], 0, :]`), masking invalid patch positions where `positions_xy != -1`, and concatenating/normalizing. On modern GPUs, dispatching multiple small kernels over 280-2240 visual tokens caused excessive kernel launch latency (~0.31 ms), bounding vision preprocessing throughput. 2. **Sequential Un-batched Multimodal Inputs**: In `_process_image_input`, when multiple images were passed (either as a 3D tensor or a list of tensors across requests in continuous batching), each image was processed individually through `self.vision_embedder` and `self.embed_vision` via an inline `for pv, pp in zip(pixel_values, pixel_position_ids)` loop. Similarly, `_process_video_input` iterated over each video and each frame sequentially in Python. For an 8-frame video, this dispatched 8 independent vision embedder projections and 8 `ColumnParallelLinear` multimodal projections, incurring significant CPU launch overhead and leaving GPU SMs underutilized. ### Implementation Details 1. **Vectorized PyTorch 2D Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: - Replaces multi-step 3D tensor slicing with a single contiguous 1D embedding lookup using `F.embedding`. - Flattens `self.pos_embedding` from `[max_size, 2, embed_dim]` to `[max_size * 2, embed_dim]` via `.view(-1, embed_dim)`. - Computes flat indices `x_flat = pos_x * 2` and `y_flat = pos_y * 2 + 1`, clamping `-1` padding values before lookup. - Computes `out = F.embedding(x_flat, flat_weights)` and performs an in-place accumulation `out.add_(F.embedding(y_flat, flat_weights))`. - Applies `.masked_fill_(~valid_mask.unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)` in-place where `positions_xy == -1`, producing exact zero padding and preserving 100% bit-exact parity without Triton or custom kernel dependencies. 2. **Memory-Bounded Dynamic Chunking (`_vision_chunk` and `_embed_vision_patches`)**: - Mirrors the proven `_encoder_chunk` mechanism to dynamically split large image/video batches based on available accelerator memory budget, avoiding OOMs on large multimodal prompts. - Short-circuits when `total_items <= 1` (a single image or video), directly passing inputs through without executing the `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()` syscall. - Wraps accelerator memory queries with `with gpu_sync_allowed():` context guards to respect vLLM async execution and CUDA graph capture invariants. 3. **Unified Batched Multimodal Projections**: - `_process_image_input`: - When receiving a 3D `torch.Tensor` of shape `[N, S, D]` (batched images), it passes the tensor directly through `self._embed_vision_patches` in one pass, flattens all patches across images to `[N * S, D_in]`, executes a single batched GEMM projection through `self.embed_vision`, and unbinds into per-image feature chunks. - When receiving a `list[torch.Tensor]` of variable-length images, it flattens each image's patch tokens, tracks slice lengths, concatenates into a unified 2D batch `[total_patches, D]`, runs a single `self.embed_vision` projection, and splits back into per-image tensors using `torch.split`. - `_process_video_input`: - Embeds all frames of all videos in a single unified tensor pass through `self._embed_vision_patches` and `self.embed_vision`, splitting features by `video_frame_counts`. ### Tradeoffs & Encapsulation - **Zero Non-Gemma Regressions**: All modifications are strictly encapsulated within `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`. Standard Gemma 4 models (`E2B`, `E4B`, `26B-A4B`, `31B`) and text-only generation paths are completely untouched. - **Pure PyTorch Simplicity & Portability**: Completely eliminates the need for Triton or hardware-specific kernels, ensuring immediate zero-overhead support across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD ROCm, TPUs, and CPUs. - **Bit-Exact Numerical Fidelity**: Position embedding outputs are 100.0% bit-exact to PyTorch reference implementations. Full image and video embeddings retain 100.0% bit-exact parity at low batch sizes and > 0.99999 cosine similarity across large batches. ### Model & Workload Applicability Matrix | Model / Workload | Direct / Transitive / N/A | Supported Architecture | Technical Justification | | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | | `google/gemma-4-12B-it` | Direct Optimization | Gemma4Unified (Encoder-free Vision) | Uses `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`. | | `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. Verified 100% token match. | | `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. Verified 100% token match. | | `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 MoE (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. Verified 100% token match. | | `google/gemma-4-31B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 Dense (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. Verified 100% token match. | | `DiffusionGemma` | N/A | Diffusion Transformer (DiT) | Diffusion model architecture; does not use Gemma4Unified vision embedder. | ## Reproducibility & Benchmark Scripts
Microbenchmark Reproduction Script (bench_pr4_unified_vision.py) ```python # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 """Benchmark PR4: Unified Vision Embedder Vectorization and Batching. Compares `main` (0838cd6593) vs `lucianommartins/gemma4-pr4-unified-vision`. Supports branch comparison, worker mode, standalone benchmark, and file comparison. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import os import sys from pathlib import Path from types import SimpleNamespace from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union import torch import torch.nn as nn sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent)) from common_harness import compute_parity_metrics, measure_cuda_latency, run_branch_comparison CASES = [ ("Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=280)", "posemb", 280), ("Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=560)", "posemb", 560), ("Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=1120)", "posemb", 1120), ("Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=2240)", "posemb", 2240), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (1 images, 280 patches)", "image", 1), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (2 images, 280 patches)", "image", 2), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (4 images, 280 patches)", "image", 4), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (8 images, 280 patches)", "image", 8), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (16 images, 280 patches)", "image", 16), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (varlen 2 images, 140..280 patches)", "image_varlen", 2), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (varlen 4 images, 140..280 patches)", "image_varlen", 4), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (varlen 8 images, 140..280 patches)", "image_varlen", 8), ("Gemma4Unified._process_video_input (1 videos, 4 frames, 280 patches)", "video", (1, 4)), ("Gemma4Unified._process_video_input (1 videos, 8 frames, 280 patches)", "video", (1, 8)), ("Gemma4Unified._process_video_input (2 videos, 16 frames, 280 patches)", "video", (2, 16)), ("Gemma4Unified._process_video_input (4 videos, 32 frames, 280 patches)", "video", (4, 32)), ] _VLLM_CTX = None def init_dist(): global _VLLM_CTX import tempfile from vllm.config.vllm import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config from vllm.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel if _VLLM_CTX is None: _VLLM_CTX = set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()) _VLLM_CTX.__enter__() if not torch.distributed.is_initialized(): fd, temp_file = tempfile.mkstemp() os.close(fd) init_distributed_environment( world_size=1, rank=0, distributed_init_method=f"file://{temp_file}", local_rank=0, backend="nccl", ) initialize_model_parallel(1, 1) def setup_embedder_and_model(): init_dist() from vllm.model_executor.models.gemma4_mm import Gemma4MultimodalEmbedder from vllm.model_executor.models.gemma4_unified import ( Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration, Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder, ) device = torch.device("cuda:0") dtype = torch.bfloat16 # Real dimensions from google/gemma-4-12B-it Unified vision config model_patch_size = 48 patch_dim = model_patch_size * model_patch_size * 3 # 6912 mm_embed_dim = 3840 mm_posemb_size = 1120 v_config = SimpleNamespace( model_patch_size=model_patch_size, mm_embed_dim=mm_embed_dim, mm_posemb_size=mm_posemb_size, rms_norm_eps=1e-6, ) multimodal_config = SimpleNamespace( hidden_size=mm_embed_dim, output_proj_dims=mm_embed_dim, rms_norm_eps=1e-6, ) text_config = SimpleNamespace( hidden_size=mm_embed_dim, ) torch.manual_seed(42) torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(42) embedder = Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder(v_config).to(device=device, dtype=dtype) for p in embedder.parameters(): p.data.normal_(0.0, 0.02) embedder.patch_ln1.weight.data.fill_(1.0) embedder.patch_ln1.bias.data.zero_() embedder.patch_ln2.weight.data.fill_(1.0) embedder.patch_ln2.bias.data.zero_() embedder.pos_norm.weight.data.fill_(1.0) embedder.pos_norm.bias.data.zero_() embed_vision = Gemma4MultimodalEmbedder(multimodal_config, text_config).to(device=device, dtype=dtype) for p in embed_vision.parameters(): p.data.normal_(0.0, 0.02) class UnifiedRunner(nn.Module): def __init__(self, ve, ev): super().__init__() self.vision_embedder = ve self.embed_vision = ev if hasattr(Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration, "_vision_chunk"): _vision_chunk = staticmethod( Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration._vision_chunk ) if hasattr(Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration, "_embed_vision_patches"): _embed_vision_patches = ( Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration._embed_vision_patches ) _process_image_input = Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration._process_image_input _process_video_input = Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration._process_video_input model = UnifiedRunner(embedder, embed_vision) return embedder, model, patch_dim, mm_posemb_size def run_worker(out_path: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]: device = torch.device("cuda:0") dtype = torch.bfloat16 embedder, model, patch_dim, max_posemb_size = setup_embedder_and_model() results = {} for name, kind, param in CASES: print(f" Executing case: {name}") torch.manual_seed(42) torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(42) if kind == "posemb": num_tokens = param xy = torch.randint(0, max_posemb_size, (num_tokens, 2), device=device, dtype=torch.long) # Inject ~10% padded -1 positions to verify bit-exactness on padded tokens pad_mask = torch.rand(num_tokens, device=device) < 0.10 xy[pad_mask] = -1 def run_fn(): return embedder._factorized_posemb(xy) latency_ms = measure_cuda_latency(run_fn, warmup=10, reps=50) out_tensor = run_fn() results[name] = { "latency_ms": latency_ms, "tensor": out_tensor.detach().clone().cpu(), } elif kind == "image": num_images = param num_patches = 280 pv_img = torch.randn(num_images, num_patches, patch_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype) pp_img = torch.randint(0, max_posemb_size, (num_images, num_patches, 2), device=device, dtype=torch.long) # Add ~10% padded patches pad_mask = torch.rand(num_images, num_patches, device=device) < 0.10 pp_img[pad_mask] = -1 image_input = {"pixel_values": pv_img, "pixel_position_ids": pp_img} def run_fn(): res = model._process_image_input(image_input) return torch.cat(res, dim=0) latency_ms = measure_cuda_latency(run_fn, warmup=5, reps=25) out_tensor = run_fn() results[name] = { "latency_ms": latency_ms, "tensor": out_tensor.detach().clone().cpu(), } elif kind == "image_varlen": num_images = param # Generate variable length list of images with 140..280 patches pv_list = [] pp_list = [] for i in range(num_images): p_count = 140 + (i % 2) * 140 # 140 or 280 pv = torch.randn(p_count, patch_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype) pp = torch.randint(0, max_posemb_size, (p_count, 2), device=device, dtype=torch.long) pad_mask = torch.rand(p_count, device=device) < 0.10 pp[pad_mask] = -1 pv_list.append(pv) pp_list.append(pp) image_input = {"pixel_values": pv_list, "pixel_position_ids": pp_list} def run_fn(): res = model._process_image_input(image_input) return torch.cat(res, dim=0) latency_ms = measure_cuda_latency(run_fn, warmup=5, reps=25) out_tensor = run_fn() results[name] = { "latency_ms": latency_ms, "tensor": out_tensor.detach().clone().cpu(), } elif kind == "video": num_videos, total_frames = param num_patches = 280 pv_vid = torch.randn(total_frames, num_patches, patch_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype) pp_vid = torch.randint(0, max_posemb_size, (total_frames, num_patches, 2), device=device, dtype=torch.long) pad_mask = torch.rand(total_frames, num_patches, device=device) < 0.10 pp_vid[pad_mask] = -1 frames_per_vid = total_frames // num_videos frame_counts = [frames_per_vid] * num_videos # adjust if remainder frame_counts[-1] += total_frames - sum(frame_counts) video_input = { "pixel_values_videos": pv_vid, "pixel_position_ids_videos": pp_vid, "video_frame_counts": frame_counts, } def run_fn(): res = model._process_video_input(video_input) return torch.cat(res, dim=0) latency_ms = measure_cuda_latency(run_fn, warmup=5, reps=25) out_tensor = run_fn() results[name] = { "latency_ms": latency_ms, "tensor": out_tensor.detach().clone().cpu(), } if out_path: torch.save(results, out_path) print(f"Worker finished. Saved to {out_path}") return results def print_comparison_table(data_base: Dict[str, Any], data_feat: Dict[str, Any]): header = ( f"| Case | Base (ms) | Feat (ms) | Speedup | Gain (%) | " f"Bit-Exact (%) | Within 1-ULP (%) | Max Diff | Cos Sim | Extra |" ) separator = "| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |" print(header) print(separator) for case, cb in data_base.items(): if case not in data_feat: continue cf = data_feat[case] base_ms = cb["latency_ms"] feat_ms = cf["latency_ms"] speedup = base_ms / max(feat_ms, 1e-6) pct_gain = (speedup - 1.0) * 100.0 tb = cb.get("tensor") tf = cf.get("tensor") if tb is not None and tf is not None: parity = compute_parity_metrics(tb, tf) else: parity = {"bit_exact_pct": 100.0, "within_1ulp_pct": 100.0, "max_abs_diff": 0.0, "cosine_sim": 1.0} extra_b = cb.get("extra", "") extra_f = cf.get("extra", "") extra_str = f"{extra_b} -> {extra_f}" if (extra_b or extra_f) else "" diff_str = f"{parity['max_abs_diff']:.2e}" if parity['max_abs_diff'] > 0 else "0.0" print( f"| {case} | {base_ms:.3f} | {feat_ms:.3f} | {speedup:.2f}x | " f"{pct_gain:+.1f}% | {parity['bit_exact_pct']:.1f}% | " f"{parity['within_1ulp_pct']:.1f}% | {diff_str} | " f"{parity['cosine_sim']:.5f} | {extra_str} |" ) def run_standalone(save_path: Optional[str] = None): print("Running PR4 benchmark in standalone mode on active branch...") results = run_worker(out_path=save_path) print("\n| Test Case | Latency (ms) |") print("| :--- | :---: |") for name, r in res

title: [ROCm][RDNA][Perf] W4A16: packed fp16 prefill dequant and tiles for gfx1151
author: stoivonen-amd
body:
## Overview

Speeds up fp16 prefill in `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` on gfx1151 (Strix Halo). The Triton prefill GEMM dequantizes two 4-bit weights per instruction, and gets tiles tuned for that dequant. Supersedes draft #55711.

## Claims

- fp16 prefill latency on gfx1151: 5–18% faster on Qwen3-4B (symmetric) at every prompt length from 64 to 2048 tokens, and 17–19% faster on Qwen3-8B (asymmetric) from 512 tokens, unchanged below.
- No change for bf16, or on any GPU other than gfx1151.
- No accuracy change: the dequant arithmetic is exact, and kernel output is bit-identical to main in all 1248 configs swept.

## Validation

All measurements: gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), torch 2.13.0+rocm10.2, Triton 3.8.0. main is c83935b300. Benchmarks ran on 23a1a2b640, which differs from this PR's head only in comments and in where `packed_dequant` is decided (same result for every dtype, zero-point and M). GSM8K and tests ran on the head.

**End-to-end prefill latency**: `vllm bench latency --batch-size 1 --output-len 1 --num-iters-warmup 5 --num-iters 30 --max-model-len 4096 --seed 0`. One process per run, main and this PR alternating, 3 reps. Each cell is main → this PR, median over reps in ms, with the delta; "~" marks overlapping rep ranges.

| prompt tokens | Qwen3-4B, fp16, sym | Qwen3-8B, fp16, asym | Qwen3-8B, bf16, asym (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 34.9 → 33.0 (−5.4%) | 71.1 → 71.6 (+0.7% ~) | 74.1 → 74.2 (+0.2% ~) |
| 128 | 51.5 → 46.7 (−9.4%) | 92.2 → 92.5 (+0.3% ~) | 96.3 → 96.2 (−0.2% ~) |
| 192 | 76.5 → 72.6 (−5.1%) | 140.9 → 140.3 (−0.4% ~) | 147.9 → 148.0 (+0.0% ~) |
| 256 | 91.1 → 76.5 (−16.0%) | 165.0 → 163.1 (−1.1%) | 174.8 → 172.8 (−1.1% ~) |
| 512 | 175.7 → 144.3 (−17.9%) | 325.7 → 264.5 (−18.8%) | 340.6 → 342.1 (+0.4% ~) |
| 2048 | 782.7 → 673.5 (−14.0%) | 1346.3 → 1118.8 (−16.9%) | 1366.0 → 1364.8 (−0.1% ~) |

**Large batches**: `vllm bench latency --batch-size {128,256} --output-len {1,128} --num-iters-warmup 1 --num-iters 1 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --seed 0`. One process per run, main (11a8d571d2, this PR's parent) and this PR alternating, 3 reps. Each cell is the change in end-to-end latency from main, median over reps; "~" marks overlapping rep ranges.

| batch | prompt tokens | Qwen3-4B fp16 sym, output 1 | Qwen3-4B fp16 sym, output 128 | Qwen3-8B fp16 asym, output 1 | Qwen3-8B fp16 asym, output 128 |

| 128 | 128 | −47.8% | −26.3% | −51.8% | −28.6% |

| 256 | 128 | −48.0% | −29.2% | −51.8% | −29.7% |
| 256 | 256 | −48.0% | −32.7% | −51.7% | −36.1% |
| 256 | 512 | −47.8% | −35.6% | −51.6% | −41.0% |

Qwen3-8B bf16 (control, prompt 512): batch 128 +2.9% ~ at output 1 and −0.1% ~ at output 128; batch 256 −0.5% ~ and +0.4% ~.

Models are `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` and `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16`.

**Accuracy**: GSM8K, 5-shot, 500 questions, greedy, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against a server started with `--dtype float16 --max-model-len 4096`. Differences are ±1 question.

| model | dtype | quant | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` | fp16 | asym | 0.884 | 0.882 |
| `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` | fp16 | sym | 0.848 | 0.850 |

**Tests**: 135 passed on gfx1151. CI has no gfx11 runners: the AMD kernel quantization shards run on MI300/MI355, where these tests skip.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py \
       tests/kernels/quantization/test_w4a16_kernel_selection.py
```

<details>
<summary>Kernel sweep</summary>

Calls `_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply_impl` directly with the main and PR copies of `rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`, timed with `triton.testing.do_bench` and a cache flush between reps, as in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_gemm.py`. Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-1.7B qkv/o/gate_up/down shapes, group size 32/64/128, M 6–2048, 1248 configs, 3 reps with rotating order. Geomean kernel time vs main; lower is better.

| dtype | quant | M | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-1.7B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp16 | sym | ≤ 128 | 0.972 | 0.979 |
| fp16 | sym | 129–256 | 0.845 | 0.968 |
| fp16 | sym | > 256 | 0.762 | 0.787 |
| fp16 | asym | ≤ 128 | 0.999 | 0.999 |
| fp16 | asym | 129–256 | 0.996 | 0.999 |
| fp16 | asym | > 256 | 0.766 | 0.795 |
| bf16 | sym | all | 0.997–1.000 | 0.999–1.000 |
| bf16 | asym | all | 0.997–1.000 | 1.000 |

Output bit-identical to main: 1248 of 1248 configs.

Geomeans hide some per-shape losses for symmetric fp16: 46 of its 312 configs are more than 2% slower than main (195 are more than 2% faster). The worst is Qwen3-1.7B `down_proj` (K = 6144, N = 2048) at M = 129–192, 13–22% slower. Every loss was already present in #55711.

</details>

## Details

**Packed dequant.** For a 4-bit value `n`, the bits `0x6400 | n` read as fp16 are exactly `1024 + n`. One `v_and_or_b32` (`(x & 0x000F000F) | 0x64006400`) does this for two values at once, instead of the `v_and_b16` + `v_or_b16` per value that Triton emits. The ExLlama shuffle layout already puts paired values 16 bits apart, so no extra shuffling is needed. The kernel subtracts `1024 + zp` instead of `zp`, which is exact because fp16 represents every integer below 2048.

**When it is used.** Only fp16 on gfx1151, the only GPU it was measured on, decided on the host and passed to the kernel as the `PACKED_DEQUANT` constexpr. Asymmetric layers use it only above M = 256: the extra zero-point load made it 1.2–2.4x slower per GEMM below that.

**Tiles.** The packed fp16 path and the scalar bf16 path want different tiles, most visibly `BLOCK_N` 256 vs 64 at deep M. `_select_skinny_gfx1151_config` picks new tiles and `num_stages=1` for fp16 above M = 128 (M = 256 for asymmetric). Everything else keeps the existing ladder and overrides unchanged. `num_stages=1` stays off bf16, where it cost 15.8% end-to-end on an asymmetric model.

**Numerics.** The dequant result is unchanged. The new tiles change `BLOCK_K`, and with it the fp32 accumulation order, so fp16 output is not guaranteed bit-identical. In the kernel sweep it was bit-identical in all 1248 configs.

**Not duplicating.** #57199 changes the HIP decode kernel, not the Triton prefill path. #52637 changes symmetric weight loading in `process_weights_after_loading`. #60710 adds an opt-in (default off) dense weight cache that skips the int4 dequant at M ≥ 256; it edits the same file but leaves the Triton dequant and tile selection alone. No other open PR touches the prefill dequant or the gfx1151 tile selection.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Make AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill default on gfx942/gfx950
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Overview

Under `--gdn-prefill-backend auto`, use the AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill backend from #57560 on gfx942 and gfx950, as agreed in that PR's review. It applies only to BF16 models with 128-dim linear-attention heads, and only when AITER is enabled and the build ships the FlyDSL kernels. Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "gdn prefill flydsl"` finds no other PR that changes the default; #57560 added the opt-in backend, and #60659 changes the prefill kernels' internals, not which backend `auto` picks.

## Claims

* Lower time to first token by default for GDN models on MI300X and MI355X: −2.7% geomean on Qwen3-Next-80B (MI300X), −3.6% on Qwen3.8-2.4T (MI355X). Decode is unchanged.
* GSM8K is unchanged on Qwen3-Next (0.9606 → 0.9606).
* Anything FlyDSL cannot serve (other architecture, missing kernels, other head dims or dtype) stays on Triton/FLA under `auto`. `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` opts out.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py
```

The new `test_auto_defaults_to_aiter_flydsl` fails against the old resolver and passes with this change. In a ROCm container without a GPU, `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py` gives 12 passed, 2 skipped. The two skips are the on-device FlyDSL-vs-Triton numerics test from #57560, which this PR does not change. `ruff check` and `ruff format` (0.14.0) pass.

TTFT with FlyDSL (default) vs Triton, from this PR's earlier run and the opt-in runs in #57560:

| Hardware | Model | Mean TTFT | Accuracy, Triton → FlyDSL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MI300X, TP2 | `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct` | −2.7% geomean over 4 points, ISL/OSL 8k/1k at c=4/16/64 and 60k/600 at c=4 | GSM8K flexible-extract 0.9606 → 0.9606 (8 fixed, 8 broken, McNemar p = 1.00) |
| MI355X, TP8 | `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` | −3.6% median geomean over 16 cells | GPQA-Diamond 0.9192 → 0.9343; GSM8K 0.9787 → 0.9825 |
| MI300X, TP2 | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | −1.9% geomean over 4 cells | GSM8K 0.9697 → 0.9712 |

## Details

One new `auto` branch in `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend` returns `aiter_flydsl` when `on_mi3xx()` and the same conditions an explicit request must meet hold. Those conditions now live in one helper, `_aiter_flydsl_unsupported_reasons`. An explicit request still raises when the kernels are missing, and warns before falling back to Triton/FLA when the model is outside the gate. `test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py` pins `triton`, since it checks the Triton path and `auto` would now route it to FlyDSL.

The gain depends on the model: about −1% TTFT on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, against −3.6% on Qwen3.8-2.4T.

title: [HiSparse] Own GPU residency instead of editing core block-table rows
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109. This is an alternative to #60117 and #60123.

HiSparse stored GPU residency by editing core block-table rows after sending them: it adopted GPU copies of host prefix pages, and nulled pages the pool reused. The edits reached the worker through `SchedulerOutput.block_table_updates`, and #60109 was a new request's row arriving twice in one step. With this PR, HiSparse owns residency, and the worker only ever sees core rows grow (the scheduler fills an imported prefix's null tail entry before the row is first sent):

- **Scheduler:** `HiSparseResidentManager` records adopted and lost pages as per-request `residency_changes`. For each scheduled request, the coordinator sends the block ids of only the pages the worker lacks (new pages, plus pages adopted or lost since the last send; a new or re-admitted request gets its full row once), in HiSparse's connector metadata. At batch scale some request gains a page nearly every decode step.
- **Worker:** HiSparse keeps one persistent device table `[request state rows, resident groups, pages]`, written with one scatter per step that carries updates. It adds to core's per-group resident block tables, which still drive KV writes; HiSparse reads residency from its own table. The decode resolver kernel indexes it by state row, so nothing is copied per step; prefill staging gathers its rows once per batch.
- **Core:** `block_table_updates` is removed and `update_requests` is back to its pre-HiSparse form. `add_requests` is unchanged.

**Why this over #60117/#60123:** those keep HiSparse's row edits in core (in `update_requests`, and in `add_requests` for #60123). This removes them entirely. Cost: about 230 added lines versus about 10, plus one int32 table: about 18 MB at 256 seqs × 18k context × 61 groups, and about 0.25 GB at 512 seqs × 128k. It is allocated after memory profiling, like MRv2's block tables.

## Test plan

All on 4×B200 (TP4, pirate `b200-02`), GLM-5.3-NVFP4, PR at `81bf678ee5` (later head commits only rename) unless noted, vs main at its merge base `51ef239768`. Each tree's `_C_stable_libtorch` was built for SM100 from its own sources, and `/proc/<pid>/maps` confirmed every TP worker loaded its own tree's build. Each row below is a fresh server unless it says "wave 2". Common server command (`--max-model-len 17408` for the perf runs):
```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 22528 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}'
```

**#60109 repro.** One server, runs back to back. The fixed seed repeats prompts, so later waves hit the prefix and adopt GPU copies:
```bash
# c=1 once, then c=4 three times.
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 20480 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 4
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 20480 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 8
```

| | c=1 | c=4 waves |
|---|---|---|
| main | 4/4 | 0/8 ×3, a TP worker dies in the first c=4 wave |
| this PR | 4/4 | 8/8 ×3, 0 CUDA errors (at `8ce8c1d297` and `81bf678ee5`) |

With temporary counters (not committed), the c=4 waves adopted GPU copies for 127,600 page × resident-group entries.

**Accuracy.** Main serves only one wave per server (the second wave hits #60109), so main's rows are first waves; the PR also runs a second wave on the same server.

- GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8123 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 128`
- Multi-needle retrieval, 16.6k–20.9k tokens: 192 prompts, each hiding 32 seven-digit codes at random depths in filler text and asking for all 32 (6,144 scored codes per wave, greedy, script below): `python niah.py --n 192 --waves <1|2> --concurrency 32`. A concurrent long-decode load (`vllm bench serve --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 192 --max-concurrency 48 --ignore-eos --seed 7`, started 90 s earlier) keeps the GPU pool full, so pages are lost.

| | GSM8K | GSM8K wave 2 | retrieval | retrieval wave 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.911, 0.906, 0.903 | crashes (#60109) | 6142, 6143 / 6144 | crashes (#60109) |
| this PR at `8ce8c1d297` | 0.911, 0.905 | 0.911, 0.903 | | |
| this PR at `81bf678ee5` | 0.917 | 0.903 | | |
| this PR at `8801b4011b` | | | 6140, 6142 / 6144 | 6142, 6143 / 6144 |

The counters show the paths ran. In one PR server running the #60109 repro, GSM8K and retrieval (with 4 codes asked per prompt), they recorded 608,240 adopted and 1,388,980 lost page × resident-group entries, 1,495 updates that resent a request's row from a lost page, and every TP worker applying residency updates (393,125 pages over 5,500 steps). Those counters were taken at `8ce8c1d297`, which resent a request's row from its first lost page on.

**Residency update size.** Per-step updates now carry only new pages and pages adopted or lost since the last send, so they no longer grow with context. Measured with temporary instrumentation (not committed) at `5bad90f9f2` (before) vs `81bf678ee5`, rank-0 worker, steps that carry updates:

| | pages per step, p50 / mean | `update_hisparse_residency` µs, p50 / mean | `take_residency_updates` total |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16k/1k, c=64, before | 145 / 160 | 224 / 234 | 344 ms |
| 16k/1k, c=64, after | 2 / 29 | 135 / 150 | 179 ms |
| 124k/1k, c=11, before | 828 / 908 | 758 / 852 | 401 ms |
| 124k/1k, c=11, after | 2 / 188 | 131 / 326 | 137 ms |

The remaining mean is new requests' rows and prefill chunks, which are sent once. The 124k run (`--max-model-len 131072`, `--random-input-len 126976 --max-concurrency 11 --num-prompts 22`) filled 92% of the host pool and lost pages throughout.

<details><summary>niah.py</summary>

```python
"""Multi-needle retrieval at 16k-20k tokens against a vLLM completions server."""
import argparse, asyncio, json, random, re, time
import aiohttp
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

ADJ = "quiet amber distant hollow brisk silver crooked gentle rusty vivid narrow ancient humid pale restless sturdy".split()
NOUN = "river lantern orchard engine meadow harbor violin ledger tower canyon market glacier compass furnace garden archive".split()
VERB = "follows shelters outlines remembers crosses lifts measures echoes guards circles borrows mirrors".split()
PLACE = "the old mill|the northern ridge|the city wall|the train yard|the salt flats|the copper mine|the library steps|the dry lake".split("|")
KEYS = [a + b for a in "Bri Cal Dun Elm Fen Gal Har Ing".split()
        for b in "ton dor wick mere ford holm by stead".split()]
NEEDLES, ASKED = 32, 32

def sentence(rng):
    return (f"The {rng.choice(ADJ)} {rng.choice(NOUN)} {rng.choice(VERB)} the "
            f"{rng.choice(ADJ)} {rng.choice(NOUN)} near {rng.choice(PLACE)}.")

def build(tok, n, seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    prompts = []
    for i in range(n):
        target = 16384 if i % 2 == 0 else 20480
        keys = rng.sample(KEYS, NEEDLES)
        values = [str(rng.randrange(1_000_000, 9_999_999)) for _ in keys]
        depths = [rng.random() for _ in keys]
        asked = rng.sample(range(NEEDLES), ASKED)
        filler = [sentence(rng) for _ in range(target // 11)]
        body_tokens = len(tok.encode(" ".join(filler), add_special_tokens=False))
        filler = filler[: int(len(filler) * (target - 200) / body_tokens)]
        for d, k, v in sorted(zip(depths, keys, values), reverse=True):
            filler.insert(int(d * len(filler)), f"The secret code for {k} is {v}.")
        names = [keys[q] for q in asked]
        prompt = ("Read the document and answer the question.\n\nDocument:\n"
                  + " ".join(filler)
                  + "\n\nQuestion: What are the secret codes for "
                  + ", ".join(names[:-1]) + f" and {names[-1]}? Reply with one "
                  + "line per name in the form 'name: code'.\nAnswer:\n"
                  + f"{names[0]}:")
        prompts.append(dict(id=i, prompt=prompt, names=names,
                            answers=[values[q] for q in asked],
                            ntok=len(tok.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False))))
    return prompts

async def run_wave(url, model, prompts, conc):
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(conc)
    timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=3600)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout) as s:
        async def one(p):
            async with sem:
                body = dict(model=model, prompt=p["prompt"], max_tokens=512, temperature=0)
                async with s.post(f"{url}/v1/completions", json=body) as r:
                    js = await r.json()
                    if "choices" not in js:
                        return p["id"], None, str(js)[:300]
                    return p["id"], js["choices"][0]["text"], None
        return await asyncio.gather(*(one(p) for p in prompts))

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4")
    ap.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8123")
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=192)
    ap.add_argument("--waves", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(a.model)
    prompts = build(tok, a.n, a.seed)
    print(f"prompts={len(prompts)} tokens min={min(p['ntok'] for p in prompts)} "
          f"max={max(p['ntok'] for p in prompts)}", flush=True)
    results = []
    for w in range(a.waves):
        t = time.time()
        res = asyncio.run(run_wave(a.url, a.model, prompts, a.concurrency))
        errors = sum(e is not None for _, _, e in res)
        def score(i, text):
            if text is None:
                return 0
            full = f"{prompts[i]['names'][0]}:" + text
            got = 0
            for name, answer in zip(prompts[i]["names"], prompts[i]["answers"]):
                m = re.search(rf"{name}:\s*(\d+)", full)
                got += m is not None and m.group(1) == answer
            return got
        correct = sum(score(i, text) for i, text, _ in res)
        print(f"wave {w}: correct={correct}/{ASKED * len(prompts)} errors={errors} "
              f"time={time.time()-t:.0f}s", flush=True)
        results.append([dict(id=i, text=text, error=e, answers=prompts[i]["answers"],
                             names=prompts[i]["names"]) for i, text, e in res])
    json.dump(results, open(a.out, "w"))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
</details>

**Performance.** c=64, a fresh server per run, order main, PR, main, PR. Both variants spill to host (GPU KV capacity 741k tokens < 64 × 17.4k):
```bash
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 128
```

| | output tok/s | mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|
| main | 952.1, 953.4 | 54.90, 54.81 ms |
| this PR | 950.9, 951.8 | 54.97, 54.91 ms |

**Tests.**
- `test_hisparse_residency_update_sends_only_changed_pages`: losing page 0 of a synced 6-page request sends only page 0 (fails at `5bad90f9f2`, which resends all 6).
- The existing adoption and page-loss tests now also assert that core rows stay append-only.
- `test_hisparse_readmitted_request_resends_its_full_residency`: a preempted request resends its whole row when re-admitted (fails if its sync state survives `free`).
- `test_hisparse_prefill_resident_sources_follow_each_resident_group`: each resident group stages prefill sources from its own table (fails if the staging cache is keyed on a per-call gather).
- On B200 at `81bf678ee5`: `pytest tests/v1/core -k hisparse` and `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py`: 84 passed. `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or index_group"`: 41 passed.

Not addressed: the other HiSparse hooks in the MRv2 runner (`start_load_kv` kwargs, `has_sync_kv_loads`, `reset_capture_state`). AI-assisted (Claude).

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Specialized decode for Kimi-K3 on MI355X
author: hyukjlee
body:
## Purpose

An opt-in specialized decode for Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950), TP8, following RFC #60904. It uses the same `specialized_decode` shape as #61867 (Kimi-K3, NVIDIA) and #60889 (GLM-5.2, ROCm), in layer mode. It is enabled with `additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}` and has no other options.

A pure spec-verify decode step of at most 8 rows runs each MoE decoder layer as persistent FlyDSL MonoKernels. The TP all-reduces run in-kernel over peer memory:

- **Whole layers** (68 KDA layers): K1 (AttnRes, in_proj, f_b, spec conv, KDA recurrence, gated RMSNorm), then K2.
- **FFN layers** (24 MLA layers): vLLM's AttnRes and MLA up to o_proj's input, then K2.
- **K2**: o_proj + all-reduce + MLP AttnRes, then the latent MoE (router, top-16 MXFP4 experts, shared experts, latent all-reduce + RMSNorm, up_proj, final all-reduce).

The kernels read vLLM's loaded weights and KDA states in place. Every other step (prefill, mixed, wider and PIECEWISE steps) runs vLLM's layers. With `decode_backend=auto` (the default) nothing changes.

### Layout: no common code

```text
vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/
    README.md        supported deployments, refusals, steps, fail-stop
    hooks.py         SpecializedDecodeMixin: the model-side hooks
    model_state.py   KimiK3ModelState: builds the executor after load, binds KV caches
    runtime/
        __init__.py  DecodeConfig, specialized_decode_config(), unsupported()
        decode.py    SpecializedDecode: plan() -> Step, Step.layer(i), prepare_kv(), after_step()
        guards.py    weight / KV cache refusals, fail-stop
        layers.py    layer kernels: vLLM tensors -> launches
        runner.py    per-rank launch state;  peer.py  peer memory, TP agreement
    mono/            kernel source (K1, K2, MoE stages, device primitives)
tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/
```

The existing Kimi-K3 files only call into the folder (26 added lines):
- `linear.py`: `specialized_decode_config()` in `__init__` before any module allocates weights, `plan_specialized_decode()` in `forward`, `(step.layer(i) or layer)(...)` in the layer loop, and `after_specialized_decode_step()` in `compute_logits`.
- `model.py`: `get_model_state_cls`.
- `mla.py`: `skip_o_proj`, which returns o_proj's input for the MLA layers' K2.

Outside `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` the only change is one Buildkite step.

### Refusal and steps

- **Refusal.** An unsupported deployment fails at startup with one `ValueError` that lists every reason. Refusals run in three stages: the config in `__init__`, the loaded weights when the model state builds the executor, and the KV caches at every bind. Every TP rank agrees on each verdict. It is default-deny for PP/DP/EP/EPLB/PCP, DBO, LoRA, KV connectors, routed-expert capture, sleep mode, CPU offload, weight updates, adaptive or dynamic speculative decoding, ReplaySSM/RecoverSSM, the V1 runner, `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`, other model shapes, and other GPUs or partitioned GPUs.
- **Steps.** `plan()` runs once per step. It picks the kernels for pure spec-verify steps of whole uniform requests at a built width, i.e. multiples of `k+1` up to 8 rows.
- **CUDA graphs.** vLLM's capture sizes are not changed. Under FULL graphs the plan is baked in at capture. A replay with fewer requests than its graph pads whole requests (null state slot, one accepted token), and the kernels serve those like real ones.

### Fail-stop

Every in-kernel wait gives up after 10 s. The rank records it in its sticky health words, so a stalled peer fails every rank instead of hanging them. In `compute_logits` each rank queues a non-blocking copy of its `FAILED` word. Every 16 steps the TP ranks agree on what has landed over the TP CPU group, and then every rank raises at the same step. This keeps all ranks out of the next collective.

Detection takes up to about 16 steps. A zero-delay check through a core hook can follow in a separate PR.

## Not a duplicate

- #61867 is Kimi-K3 on NVIDIA (CuTeDSL, SM100); this is the ROCm/FlyDSL counterpart under `kimi_k3/amd/`.
- #60397, #60889, #61482 and #60731 target other models (DeepSeek-V4.x, GLM-5.2), with different attention, residual and MoE.
- #61311 proposes shared abstractions. This PR keeps its runtime per model, as #61867 and #60889 do, and can move onto shared helpers once those land.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3          # 8x MI355X; includes amd_specialized_decode/
pre-commit run --files <changed files>     # incl. mypy
```

- **CPU:** the switch (auto / unknown value), widths, layer pattern, every refusal (one at a time, then all at once), PIECEWISE warning, cache refusal, step eligibility, `plan()` routing (PIECEWISE, too wide, prefill, PP input, unbound or re-bound KV cache), weight-view refusals.
- **GPU:** K1 against vLLM's KDA op chain; K2 at TP8 against o_proj + all-reduce + AttnRes + KimiMoE, with 300 bit-identical graph replays; a stalled rank finishes every launch and fails the step; warm-up compiles without launching.
- **Engine:** an 8-layer dummy K3 at TP8 stalls rank 3 inside a served decode step. A request fails, every rank raises at the same step, and the server exits.

Kimi-K3, TP8, DCP8, DSpark MTP, fp8 KV, `--stream-interval 10`, MI355X, FULL CUDA graphs, Model Runner V2. "Off" means the same image, tree and flags with `decode_backend=auto`.

## Test Result

This revision ran on 8x MI355X with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-1b2a6663`, which is 20 commits behind this branch's base with no `kimi_k3`, mamba, `gdn_attn` or model-state changes in between. This branch's `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` was mounted over the image.

- **Startup refusal:** TP4 + V1 runner + no speculative decoding gives one `ValueError` with all three reasons. `decode_backend="fast"` is rejected.
- **8k/1k, c1, k=7, 3 seeds:** TPOT p50 5.44 → **4.31 ms (−20.8%)**, p90 5.48 → 4.35 ms, output 170.2 → 210.3 tok/s (+23.6%); the server logs `Kimi-K3 specialized decode: 92 layers, widths [8], 30 builds`.
- **GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 q:**

  - Padded replays (k=1, c3, vLLM's default capture sizes, so 3-request steps replay the 4-request graph): off 0.9621 vs on 0.9613 (±0.0053).

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] MSA prefill attends with the E4M3 query; bump fmha_sm100 to 968061a
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview With CUTLASS MSA sparse decode on (an NVFP4 KV cache, or an FP8 E4M3 cache with the `CUTLASS_MSA` decode backend), the fused QK-norm/RoPE/insert kernel writes MiniMax-M3's query only in E4M3. `MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl` then dequantized it back into the BF16 query buffer before every prefill. Both `fmha_sm100` prefill kernels take an E4M3 query natively, so prefill now passes it through as is. The PR also bumps `fmha_sm100` (vllm-project/MSA) from `be4a52a` to `968061a`. The new pin includes MSA's Blackwell prefill port, which now serves an E4M3 query over vLLM's packed K|V pages (vllm-project/MSA#32). ## Claims - MSA prefill attention is **26–37% faster with an FP8 KV cache** and **8–13% faster with an NVFP4 KV cache** than on main (per layer on GB300; table below). - Prefill no longer makes a BF16 copy of the query. Only the Triton decode fallback still reads the dequantized query. - BF16 caches and the default Triton decode backend for FP8 caches still pass a BF16 query, so their path is unchanged. ## Validation **Tests:** on GB300 (SM103, CUDA 13.4, `fmha_sm100` built from the new pin), `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_sparse_attn_fp8_scale.py tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py` gives **240 passed, 45 skipped**. All skips are ROCm-only tests. The MSA test file runs in CI on B200. - New `test_msa_prefill_reads_query_fp8_over_fp8_cache[tp1|tp4]` covers FP8-cache prefill, including chunks over cached context, with CUTLASS decode on. It checks that `sparse_atten_func` receives the E4M3 query and that the output matches Triton on the dequantized query. - `test_msa_prefill_nvfp4_matches_triton_on_dequantized_cache` now checks that `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` receives the E4M3 query. Its reference is now the cache as an E4M3-query kernel reads it (see Details). - Both prefill tests require all but 1e-4 of the elements within atol/rtol 0.05 and bound the rest at 0.25. The E4M3 probabilities are rounded per split, and splits follow the SM count, so a rare element lands just past 0.05: 1 of 4.1M on B200 CI. On GB300 over 16 seeds the worst case is 2.4e-7 of the elements and 0.07 max abs error. - On the old code, all four prefill cases fail with `[torch.bfloat16] == [torch.float8_e4m3fn]`. **Performance:** `MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl.forward` on prefill-only batches (`build_k2q_csr` + attention + combine, plus the dequant where the query is BF16). GB300, one request, top-k 16, page 128. Each value is the median of 3×50 iterations after warmup; spread ≤1%, except ±5% on the first FP8 row of the main run. | KV cache | Q heads / KV heads | Query tokens @ cached context | main (MSA `be4a52a`, BF16 q) | pin bump only (BF16 q) | this PR (E4M3 q) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 | 16 / 1 (TP4) | 8k @ 0 | 411 µs | 368 µs | 303 µs (-26%) | | FP8 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 32k | 462 µs | 439 µs | 314 µs (-32%) | | FP8 | 16 / 1 | 16k @ 112k | 801 µs | 754 µs | 530 µs (-34%) | | FP8 | 64 / 4 (TP1) | 8k @ 0 | 1423 µs | 1320 µs | 891 µs (-37%) | | FP8 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 32k | 1498 µs | 1423 µs | 985 µs (-34%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 0 | 379 µs | 375 µs | 342 µs (-10%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 32k | 457 µs | 458 µs | 420 µs (-8%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 16k @ 112k | 798 µs | 795 µs | 695 µs (-13%) | | NVFP4 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 0 | 1411 µs | 1395 µs | 1255 µs (-11%) | | NVFP4 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 32k | 1491 µs | 1491 µs | 1317 µs (-12%) | Percentages are relative to main. With the new pin, a BF16 query over the FP8 cache also reaches the Blackwell port, but with BF16 MMAs. The E4M3 query gives the bulk of the FP8 gain at either pin: on main's pin alone it is 13–24% (411 → 356, 462 → 367, 801 → 623, 1423 → 1083, 1498 → 1162 µs).
Benchmark script (run from the repo root with PYTHONPATH=.) ```python """Per-layer MSA prefill attention (impl.forward) with an E4M3 query.""" import math from types import SimpleNamespace import torch import tests.kernels.attention.test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode as t from vllm.forward_context import ForwardContext, override_forward_context from vllm.models.minimax_m3.common.sparse_attention import ( MiniMaxM3SparseMetadata, MiniMaxM3SparsePrefillMetadata) BLK, TOPK = 128, 16 def case(q_len, seq_len, hkv, g): pos = torch.arange(seq_len - q_len, seq_len, device="cuda") visible = pos // BLK + 1 vmax = int(visible.max()) r = torch.rand(q_len, hkv, vmax, device="cuda", generator=g) ar = torch.arange(vmax, device="cuda") r = torch.where(ar < visible[:, None, None] - 1, r, -1.0) r = torch.where(ar == visible[:, None, None] - 1, 2.0, r) k = min(TOPK, vmax) val, idx = r.topk(k, dim=-1) topk = torch.where(val >= 0, idx, -1).int() if k < TOPK: topk = torch.cat([topk, topk.new_full((q_len, hkv, TOPK - k), -1)], -1) pages = math.ceil(seq_len / BLK) block_table = torch.randperm(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")[None] seq = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") cu_q = torch.tensor([0, q_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") cu_k = torch.tensor([0, seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") p = MiniMaxM3SparsePrefillMetadata( cu_seqlens_q=cu_q, cu_seqlens_k=cu_k, seq_lens=seq, context_lens=seq - q_len, block_table=block_table, max_query_len=q_len, max_seq_len=seq_len, total_kv_blocks=pages) md = MiniMaxM3SparseMetadata( seq_lens=seq, max_seq_len=seq_len, slot_mapping=torch.empty(q_len, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"), num_actual_tokens=q_len, num_decodes=0, num_decode_tokens=0, num_prefills=1, num_prefill_tokens=q_len, prefill=p) return md, topk, pages def bench(fn, iters=50): for _ in range(10): fn() torch.cuda.synchronize() s, e = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True) s.record() for _ in range(iters): fn() e.record() torch.cuda.synchronize() return s.elapsed_time(e) / iters * 1e3 g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0) for kv_dtype in ("fp8", "nvfp4"): for hq, hkv, q_len, ctx in ((16, 1, 8192, 0), (16, 1, 8192, 32768), (16, 1, 16384, 114688), (64, 4, 8192, 0), (64, 4, 8192, 32768)): md, topk, pages = case(q_len, ctx + q_len, hkv, g) k_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") v_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") if kv_dtype == "nvfp4": kv_cache, _ = t._make_nvfp4_kv_cache(pages, hkv, "nvfp4", k_scale, v_scale) else: kv_cache = (torch.randn(pages, hkv, BLK, 256, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) layer = SimpleNamespace(layer_name="l", topk_indices_buffer=topk, _q_scale_float=0.5, _k_scale=k_scale, _v_scale=v_scale) qf = torch.randn(q_len, hq * 128, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) query = torch.empty(q_len, hq * 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") out = torch.empty_like(query) impl = t.MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl( num_heads=hq, head_size=128, scale=t.SM_SCALE, num_kv_heads=hkv, kv_cache_dtype=kv_dtype, topk_blocks=TOPK, sparse_block_size=BLK, msa_decode_backend="cutlass") assert impl.use_cutlass_decode with override_forward_context(ForwardContext(no_compile_layers={}, attn_metadata={"l": md}, slot_mapping={})): bench(lambda: impl.forward(layer, query, kv_cache, out, query_fp8=qf), iters=200) ts = [bench(lambda: impl.forward(layer, query, kv_cache, out, query_fp8=qf)) for _ in range(3)] print(f"{kv_dtype} H{hq}/{hkv} q{q_len} ctx{ctx}: " + " ".join(f"{x:.1f}" for x in ts) + " us") ```
**No end-to-end accuracy eval or serving benchmark** is included; validation is the kernel-level numerics and per-layer timings above. ## Details **Kernel capability (MSA `968061a`; same at `be4a52a` except the Blackwell port):** - `sparse_atten_func` accepts an FP8 E4M3 query over FP8 E4M3 K/V and runs FP8 QK/PV MMAs, on the Blackwell port when eligible. The BF16-Q × FP8-K/V mode stages K/V up to BF16 instead. - `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` accepts a BF16 or E4M3 query. With E4M3 it dequantizes each NVFP4 `code × block_scale` to E4M3 instead of BF16, and applies the K global scale to the scores and the V global scale in the combine. **Scales:** `q_scale` folds into `softmax_scale`. The FP8 cache is written with unit scales and the NVFP4 global scales are passed as before, so K/V scale handling is unchanged. **Numerics:** the E4M3-query kernels round the softmax probabilities to E4M3. The NVFP4 kernel also rounds K/V to E4M3. On the NVFP4 test (TP1): - Against the E4M3-staged cache: max abs error 0.06, and 0 of 4.1M elements outside atol/rtol 0.05. - Against the exact BF16 dequantization: max 0.14, with 122 of 4.1M elements outside that tolerance. This is why the test's reference changed. On the FP8 test the max abs error is ≈0.03. **Limitations:** validated on SM103. SM100 is covered by the CI kernel job. The E4M3-query NVFP4 kernel is untested on SM107 here. **MSA pin bump (`be4a52a` → `968061a`):** - The functions vLLM calls keep their signatures: `fmha_sm100`, `fmha_sm100_plan`, `_fmha_sm100(_plan)`, `sparse_topk_select`, `sparse_atten_func`, `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` and `nvfp4_head_slot_views`. - vLLM's decode plans still pin `decode_backend="kv_mode3"`. The new `prefill_backend` plan option only routes sparse-prefill plans built through `fmha_sm100_plan`, which vLLM does not use. - The cmake install list adds the files the package now imports: `_jit_cache.py`, `msa_warmup.py`, `q8kv4_prefill_adapter.py` and `prefill_q8kv4/`. **Duplicate check:** no open PR touches the MSA prefill query or `fmha_sm100.cmake`. Open MiniMax-M3 MSA PRs (#55838, #56932, #59979) change decode or indexer metadata only. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement, test and benchmark this change. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Spec Decode] Skip metadata build for dflash/dspark when all model backends support it
author: TheEpicDolphin
body: # Context Continuing the effort from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58463 to remove unnecessary attention metadata rebuilds before FULL cudagraph replays for draft model-based speculators. I found an opportunity to use the same `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` flag to gate updating the metadata within the captured decode step for DFlash/DSpark, reducing GPU kernel launch overhead. # This PR Adds support for skipping the full attention metadata rebuild before replaying the uniform decode cudagraph. Previously, only the `TargetDependentARSpeculator` was leveraging the `update_draft_decode_metadata` operations for its attention backends to update the attention metadata in a cudagraph-safe way. In this PR, I move that logic for deciding draft model eligibility (`supports_update_decode_metadata`) for this optimization to the base class `DraftModelSpeculator`, and then i have both `TargetDependentARSpeculator` and `DFlashSpeculator` check this eligibility. If True, capture the `_update_draft_decode_metadata` op in the graph before the draft model forward. Otherwise, rebuild the attention metadata eagerly via `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` before replaying the graph. This optimization has been enabled for DeepSeek V4.1 + DSpark, as verified below. ## Profile Captured while serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on 4xGB200: **Before** **After** ## Benchmarks / Evals **Setup (both subsections).** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=5`, 4x GB200 (TP4), `--max-model-len 102400 --max-num-seqs 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'`, adaptive verification off, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Speed-Bench is 2K/2K (`throughput_16k`, `low_entropy`), with prompts scaled 8x concurrency (min 16), seed 0, and a fresh server per arm. In both subsections the PR server logged no "cannot update draft decode metadata" warning, so the in-graph metadata update was active. ### Greedy draft sampling Baseline is `main` at `b6d8e8afd9`; PR is `1abc890148`. **Speed-Bench, temperature 0.** Each value is the mean of repeated runs: 3 runs at concurrency 1, 2 runs at 16 and 64. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.96 | 6.94 | -0.3% | 1.91 | 1.90 | 521.2 | 520.7 | -0.1% | 3.760 | 3.747 | | 16 | 16.11 | 16.04 | -0.4% | 4.92 | 4.91 | 3144.3 | 3113.5 | -1.0% | 3.775 | 3.755 | | 64 | 30.37 | 30.36 | 0.0% | 9.88 | 9.94 | 6249.0 | 6250.2 | 0.0% | 3.795 | 3.795 | Step time is unchanged at every concurrency. As with MTP in #58463, the host work this removes is not on the critical path for this model at TP4. Acceptance length differs between arms by at most 0.02, while runs of the same arm vary by up to 0.16 at concurrency 1. **AIME25** (MQA, 2 epochs x 30 problems, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max 98304 tokens, 64 concurrent): | Arm | Exact match | pass@2 | Samples | Request errors | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | base | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 60 | 0 | | PR | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 60 | 0 | Accuracy is identical. Every sample includes reasoning, with median completion lengths of 5.3k tokens (base) and 4.9k (PR). ### Probabilistic draft sampling `--speculative-config` adds `"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"`. Baseline is `main` at `240785b82c`; PR is `6065f7c37c` (this branch rebased onto that baseline). **Speed-Bench, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0.** Each value is the mean of 2 runs. Individual acceptance lengths are in brackets. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.89 | 6.86 | -0.4% | 1.95 | 1.86 | 505.1 | 514.8 | +1.9% | 3.60 [3.68, 3.52] | 3.66 [3.71, 3.61] | | 16 | 16.05 | 16.02 | -0.2% | 5.01 | 5.06 | 3051.8 | 3046.9 | -0.2% | 3.64 [3.65, 3.62] | 3.65 [3.65, 3.65] | | 64 | 30.51 | 30.50 | 0.0% | 10.28 | 10.43 | 6061.4 | 5972.4 | -1.5% | 3.66 [3.65, 3.67] | 3.67 [3.66, 3.68] | Median ITL matches within 0.03 ms. The -1.5% throughput at concurrency 64 comes from a single PR run (5930 vs 6015 tok/s for the other); output lengths vary between runs at temperature 1.0. Acceptance length is equal or higher for the PR at every concurrency, and the largest gap (+0.06 at concurrency 1) is smaller than the baseline's own run-to-run spread (0.16). **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot `/v1/completions`, temperature 1.0, max 512 tokens, 64 concurrent). Acceptance is computed from the server's spec-decode counters over the eval: | Arm | Accuracy | Invalid | Accept. len | Per-position acceptance (0-4) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | base | 0.838 | 1.1% | 3.296 | 0.779 / 0.605 / 0.423 / 0.298 / 0.190 | | PR | 0.835 | 1.1% | 3.299 | 0.782 / 0.603 / 0.421 / 0.298 / 0.195 | Accuracy is within 4 questions, and per-position acceptance shows no drop at later draft positions, which is where a stale non-causal window would show up first.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Save the EAGLE attention proof with hybrid Mamba partial tails
author: Dao007forever
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This is the Mooncake connector part of #59826 by @wzhao18. It was split off at review so the core fixes could land first as #60533, which is now merged. The Mooncake store tail save now includes the full-attention KV that proves the Mamba checkpoint under EAGLE. It also pins those blocks until the asynchronous save completes.

## Claims

- After a GPU prefix-cache reset, a hybrid attention + Mamba prompt that uses EAGLE can hit its Mamba checkpoint again from the Mooncake store. Before this change the external hit was 0 tokens.
- The tail's attention blocks stay referenced until every rank finishes the save. They can no longer be reused while the save reads them.
- The scheduler computes each tail once and sends it to the worker, so the blocks it pins are exactly the blocks the worker puts. Later saves no longer re-send the tail.
- The Kimi K3 prefix-cache test starts a Mooncake master from a pytest fixture and runs a Mooncake resend case (`test_mooncake_resend_reuses_prompt_checkpoint`).

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU):

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py
```

| Code under test | Result |
|---|---|
| This branch | 480 passed |
| `main`, with this PR's test files copied in (measured at 22948c5, before the scheduler-side tail commit) | 29 failed, 233 passed (scheduler, worker and HMA end-to-end suites) |

On `main`, failing tests include `test_eagle_attention_proof_published_after_checkpoint_handoff`, `test_mooncake_lookup_reuses_resolved_hash_checkpoint`, `test_finished_partial_tail_is_pre_pinned_as_store_job` and `test_sub_block_partial_tail_offload_reads_cow_block`.

`ruff` is clean. `mypy` reports no new errors: the 10 in `worker.py` also appear on `main` in the same environment and come from pyzmq typing.

**Not run here:** the Kimi K3 end-to-end case (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py::test_mooncake_resend_reuses_prompt_checkpoint`). It needs GPUs, RDMA and `mooncake_master`; its fixture starts the master, and it skips where the binary is missing. #59826 reports an end-to-end gain with this change and the core fixes combined: Kimi K3, 1P1D DCP8 + DCP8, DSpark k4, prefix-match unit 128. At concurrency 128, the prefix hit rate went from 90.47% to 94.04% and throughput from 11,371 to 15,754 TPS/GPU. Those numbers include #60533 and have not been re-measured for this PR alone.

## Details

**Root cause.** Take P = 7,449 tokens, prefix-match unit U = 128 and EAGLE block drop on, so the Mamba checkpoint is H = 7,296.

1. The first request computes the prompt. On the GPU, the Mamba state is registered at 7,296 and the attention tail at 7,424, which is H + U.
2. Normal Mooncake saves store attention only up to the last scheduler-block boundary, 7,168. Mamba state is never stored by normal saves.
3. The partial-tail save stores the Mamba state at 7,296. But it clipped attention to the same position (key `hash@7296`), so the proof at `hash@7424` was never stored.
4. After a GPU reset, the Mooncake lookup works like this:
   - Attention matches 7,296, and the EAGLE drop brings it to 7,168.
   - Mamba has no state at or below 7,168.
   - The hit is 0.

**Fix.**
- **Boundary puts.** `ReqMeta.boundary_puts` lists every block the job stores under an explicit prefix hash, as `BoundaryPut(group_id, block_id, num_tokens)`. The scheduler resolves and pins all of them; the worker writes each block under `block_hashes[num_tokens // U - 1]` (`_boundary_puts`). Two kinds of entries:
  - **Mamba state.** Each core hand-off, whether a block-aligned snapshot or the sub-block tail at H, becomes one put of the handed-off block. Under DCP, Mamba blocks are smaller than the LCM, and only the boundary block is stored.
  - **Non-Mamba tail.** `_partial_tail_non_mamba_puts` (scheduler, once per store job) covers each non-Mamba group from the last scheduler-block boundary to H plus that group's `eagle_proof_margin`, once that much has been computed. Each block is keyed at its end, clipped to that point; null and missing blocks are skipped.
- **Publishing.** The tail is published on the save that first covers the whole prompt (`ReqMeta.publish_partial_tail`, which mirrors the tracker's `partial_tail_sent`), or when a Mamba hand-off arrives. The boundary is derived from the prompt length, so a job without a Mamba hand-off can still publish the attention proof. Later saves carry no tail.
- **Pinning.** A store job pins exactly its boundary puts' blocks (plus every non-Mamba block for a normal save). Before, a finish-time tail pinned only the Mamba block while the worker read attention blocks from the freed table.
- **Prompt length vs. prefill end.** `ReqMeta` separates `num_prompt_tokens` (used for the checkpoint) from `prefill_end_tokens` (includes output tokens replayed after preemption, used for store masks), and adds `completed_token_len`.
- **External lookup.** It scans past the hit limit for EAGLE groups, as the core lookup does since #60533. The shared helpers `eagle_proof_margin` and `partial_hash_hits_enabled` replace the local copies.
- **Partial hits follow core.** Mooncake used to decide `enable_partial_hash_hits` itself, from the Mamba specs of the groups it transfers. Core also requires every group's manager to support fine-grained lookups (a sliding-window group needs block-aligned ones) and counts groups the store does not transfer, so the two could disagree. Mooncake's scheduler and worker now read core's resolved `kv_cache_config.cache_hit_alignment_tokens`. One core line makes that possible: `engine/core.py` sets the field (and `hash_block_size`) on the scheduler's `KVCacheConfig` as well as the workers'; the scheduler's copy is deep-copied before they are resolved, and core itself does not read them there.

**Known limitations and follow-ups:**
- The prompt-completion tail is sent once. If that save is skipped under store pressure or its put fails, it is not retried; before, every later save rebuilt it (and `batch_is_exist` dropped it once stored). The Mamba state already worked this way, because its CoW block is pinned only for its own job.

**Duplicate check.** #59826 contains these changes. Splitting it into core (#60533) and Mooncake parts was requested at review, so this PR is that Mooncake part, not a duplicate.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used to port #59826's Mooncake changes onto current `main`, run the tests above and draft this description. The submitter has reviewed the changes.

title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: opt-in dense weight cache for RDNA hybrid prefill
author: zohaibm-amd
body:
## Overview

Adds opt-in `KernelConfig.rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant` (`"enable"`/`"disable"`, case-insensitive, default `"disable"`). When it is `"enable"`, `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` caches a dense fp16/bf16 copy of each weight at load time and runs GEMMs with `M >= 256` on it, so prefill no longer dequantizes int4.

## Claims

- TTFT −22% to −26% on Qwen3-4B/8B w4a16 and −21% on Gemma-4-31B AWQ with MTP-3, on Strix
  Halo (gfx1151). TPOT is unchanged at concurrency 1.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K is within ±0.6 pp.
- Decode, small batches and spec-decode verify stay on the int4 path.
- Disabled by default, which leaves current behaviour unchanged.

## Validation

Usage: `--kernel-config '{"rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant": "enable"}'`. `vllm bench serve` with random 2048 in, concurrency 1, `disable` vs `enable` on the same build, interleaved (3 pairs per Qwen model, 2 for Gemma); values are the mean of per-run medians. Measured only on gfx1151; the kernel also runs on other gfx11/gfx12 parts, where the `M >= 256` threshold may need tuning.

| Model | TTFT disable → enable | TPOT disable → enable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-8B w4a16, fp16 (asym) | 1328 → 1033 ms (**−22.2%**) | 27.7 → 27.7 ms |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-8B w4a16, bf16 (asym) | 1341 → 1023 ms (**−23.7%**) | 28.2 → 28.2 ms |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-4B w4a16, fp16 (sym) | 782 → 578 ms (**−26.1%**) | 16.4 → 16.5 ms |
| cyankiwi Gemma-4-31B AWQ, MTP-3, 128 out | 8.75 → 6.88 s (**−21.4%**) | 68.0 → 67.2 ms |

Disabled matches current main (554340f3d3) within 1% TTFT on all four models.

At concurrency 16 (Qwen3-8B fp16, 512 in / 256 out, 64 prompts, 2 pairs): TTFT 3069 → 2252 ms (−26.6%), TPOT 85.2 → 83.1 ms.

GSM8K (in-tree `tests/evals/gsm8k`, 5-shot, 500 questions, concurrency 16), Qwen3-8B: fp16 0.886 → 0.880, bf16 0.872 → 0.878.

`pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`: All 293 passed on gfx1151.

## Details

- **Why opt-in:** the copy is 4x the int4 layer weight and is taken from the `gpu_memory_utilization` budget, so it comes out of KV cache. Qwen3-8B: +13.5 GiB weights, −13.5 GiB KV. Gemma-4-31B: weights 20.2 → 75.1 GiB, KV 71.6 → 16.6 GiB. The trade targets unified-memory parts like Strix Halo, where TTFT matters more than KV capacity. Enabling it caches every layer or none: if the copies do not fit while leaving 4 GiB of activation headroom plus KV cache for one `max_model_len` request, startup fails with an error naming the option. It is a mode string rather than a bool so further modes can be added without renaming it.
- **Why `M >= 256`:** below it the dense GEMM is still memory bound and reads 4x the bytes. Per-GEMM on gfx1151 it is up to 2.3x slower than int4 on Gemma-4-31B MLP shapes. At 256 and above it is no slower on any Qwen3-8B or Gemma-4-31B shape measured.
- **Limitation:** the dense copy is built once at load time, so in-place weight reloads (`reload_weights`, RL weight sync through the weight-transfer engines) are not supported with `"enable"`. The option is intended for pure inference; keep it `"disable"` when weights are updated at runtime.

### Related Work
- no open PR caches a dense copy of W4A16 weights for this kernel.
- #55711 makes the int4 prefill dequant cheaper, and this PR skips it, so the two stack. On top of #55711 this PR still cut TTFT by 6.7% (Qwen3-8B fp16), 12.8% (Qwen3-4B fp16) and 23.0% (Qwen3-8B bf16, since #55711 is fp16 only)
- #52637 (int4 repack in `process_weights_after_loading`) and #55742 (profiler labels) touch the same file, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
- #53709 applies the same idea (opt-in load-time dequant for prefill) to DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 experts on another GPU family. It's a different kernel with no shared code path.

title: [Mooncake] Allow Mamba cache mode `none` for capacity-only workers
author: wzhao18
body:
Allow Mooncake capacity-only consumers to use Mamba cache mode `none`, which is selected when prefix caching is disabled.

Disabling prefix caching is required for Kimi K3 TP8 + DEP16 disaggregated serving because heterogeneous physical blocks per logical KV block are not supported with prefix caching for Mamba hybrid models. Otherwise, this configuration triggers the [runtime error](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d766ac98285bf1a84acfeb37c99c73d5396d4df6/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py#L2542):
```
        if (
            self._has_mamba
            and remote_physical_per_logical
            != self._physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block
            and self.vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching
        ):
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Prefix caching with heterogeneous physical_blocks_per_logical "
                "is not supported for Mamba hybrid models. "
                f"Local: {self._physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block}, "
                f"Remote: {remote_physical_per_logical}. "
                "Disable prefix caching with --no-enable-prefix-caching."
            )
```

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Restore FP fusion for indexer Q quantization
author: warrendeng
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make DeepSeek V4 sparse-indexer Q RoPE + FP8/FP4 quantization match the CUDA reference when Triton disables implicit floating-point fusion.

Fixes https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/9069 which was uncovered through the Triton 3.9 pin update. Root cause is https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11270 from Triton which disables `enable_fp_fusion` by default. Here we enable it for 2 callsites to preserve bitwise equivalence. 

## Claims

- Restore exact output-byte agreement for the three B200 failures reported in the issue.
- Restore Triton 3.8 fusion behavior for the FP8 and FP4 indexer Q kernels by setting `enable_fp_fusion=True` on both launches.

## Validation

Tested on NVIDIA B200 using the unchanged reference comparison:

| Triton pin | Result |
|---|---|
| `3.8.0+gitc01b6774` | 80 passed |
| `3.9.0+gitaad2a60d` | 80 passed |

Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and compiler controls</summary>

Environment: CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch `2.16.0.dev20261008+cu130` (`b3066be1bcce444d3785d76e971516314db375d6`). PyTorch was held fixed across pins. GPU validation covers B200 CUDA; AMD hardware was not tested.

The original reproduction uses vLLM `458ba2edf85bc9b7ebc0d5141f34ea658520faf5` from [Buildkite #93593](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93593#01a11b83-9c23-4de5-807f-441a9b71de3c). Its three reported cases pass on 3.8, fail on 3.9 with 3/1/2 differing bytes, and pass when fusion is restored on 3.9.

Native compiler controls confirm the boundary: parent `d816107c1` passes all three cases; `140c33fc3` reproduces the failures; this patch passes all three on the same bad build.

The 80-case matrix covers 5 token counts, 2 cache dtypes, FP8/FP4, 32/64 heads, and Triton/CuteDSL. Quantized Q bytes, FP4 scales, and output weights are compared exactly.

Repeat with each isolated pin selected by `TRITON_PIN_DIR` and a separate `TRITON_RUN_CACHE`:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \
PYTHONPATH="$TRITON_PIN_DIR" \
TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$TRITON_RUN_CACHE" \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short --confcutdir=tests/kernels \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py -k matches_unfused

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_indexer_q.py
```

</details>

## Details

Triton [PR #11270](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11270) disabled floating-point fusion by default. The CUDA `rotary_embedding` reference still uses fused arithmetic. Separate FP32 operations can cross a BF16 rounding midpoint and change the encoded FP8/FP4 bytes.

Both launches explicitly request `enable_fp_fusion=True`, restoring the compiler policy used in Triton 3.8. Kernel arithmetic and signatures are preserved.

Authored with Codex

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Use vLLM's FP8 max in the fused AttnRes quantization
author: Rohan138
body:
## Overview

Fixes `test_amd_attn_res_fp8_preserves_prefix_and_quantized_output` on MI300 (fnuz FP8), which has failed since #59069 landed.

## Claims

- The fused AttnRes per-token FP8 quantization now uses `get_fp8_min_max()` (224 on fnuz) instead of `torch.finfo(dtype).max` (240), matching vLLM's `QuantFP8` and the unfused path before #59069. MI355 (OCP `e4m3fn`, 448 either way) is unchanged.
- The test's FP8 code-distance check orders codes by value, so a midpoint step across zero (`0x00` vs `0x81`) counts as one step rather than 129.

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), AMD CI test image for #58761 (`rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a11cfd-…`, ROCm 10). Both changed files are identical on main.

| `pytest models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py` | Result |
|---|---|
| main | 3 failed, 13 passed (same 3 cases as CI) |
| kernel fix only | 1 failed (`[320-8-False-False]`, the zero-crossing case) |
| kernel + test fix | 16 passed |

The MI300 Kimi K3 CI job's full test set (`test_amd_attn_res.py test_amd_kda_decode.py test_kda.py test_kda_metadata.py`) passes: 139 passed, 30 skipped. I did not run an end-to-end Kimi-K3 eval (no checkpoint or hardware here). On MI300 this restores the 224 scale convention that `QuantFP8` used before the fusion.

## Details

On fnuz, every scale the fused kernel produced was 240/224 of `QuantFP8`'s (relative diff exactly 1/15). The remaining failure was a value at the rounding midpoint near zero (−0.000484 vs midpoint −0.000488): the kernel quantizes its fp32 result, the reference quantizes the bf16-rounded one, so they land on adjacent codes on opposite sides of zero.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this. #58861 touches the same `QUANT_MAX` line as context and will need a trivial rebase.
