title: [Misc] Consolidate csrc shared headers and prune dead code
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Tidy `csrc/`: merge one-macro/one-function headers, rename the misnamed `attention/` dtype directory, move stragglers next to the extension that builds them, delete unreferenced code, and flatten `csrc/libtorch_stable/` back into `csrc/` now that nearly every GPU kernel is stable-ABI. No functional change intended.

Not a duplicate: the only open PR touching this area is #38134 (WIP, removes the KV cache dtype enum), which has a different goal and predates the `libtorch_stable/` layout.

## Claims

- `csrc/` is now `core/` (shared by every extension), `cpu/` and `rocm/` (legacy-ABI code), and everything else is the stable-ABI CUDA/HIP tree. `libtorch_stable/` is gone; extension names (`_C_stable_libtorch`, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch`) are unchanged.
- Every quoted `#include` resolves to the same file before and after the flatten (scripted over all 250 sources).
- The built CUDA extensions register the same 160 op schemas as `main`.
- Every `csrc/` path in the CI `source_file_dependencies` filters exists again. 68 entries had been left naming paths that moved under `libtorch_stable/`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CUDA build of `_C_stable_libtorch`, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch`, `cumem_allocator`, `spinloop`, `fs_io_C` with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5 8.0 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0"` (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13) | builds and links |
| Registered op schemas vs. a build of `main` (`torch._C._jit_get_all_schemas()` after loading each `.so`) | identical, 160 schemas |
| Unified Marlin generator vs. the two old scripts, all archs | byte-identical output, 27 files each |
| x86 CPU extension (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, GCC 13) | every TU compiles except `cpu/utils.cpp` (missing system `numa.h` on the build box, file untouched here); not linked |
| ROCm | **not compiled** (no HIP toolchain). Ran torch's `hipify` on the old and new trees and checked that every quoted include of every HIP translation unit resolves after renaming |
| `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` | passes |

GPU kernel tests on an H200, run against the build of the first two commits (before the flatten):

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/core/test_{layernorm,activation,pos_encoding,fused_quant_layernorm,fused_silu_mul_block_quant,fused_qk_norm_rope,opcheck}.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_{merge_attn_states,cache}.py`, `tests/kernels/test_{cache_kernels,concat_mla_q}.py` | 6215 passed, 590 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{fp8_quant,fp8_quant_group,int8_quant,per_token_group_quant,cutlass_scaled_mm,machete_mm}.py` | all passed except `test_cutlass_subset` (see below) |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py` | 394 passed |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{cutlass_w4a8,quant_op_schema,awq,gptq}.py` | 136 passed, 8 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_{moe_align_block_size,moe_permute_unpermute,grouped_topk,fused_topk}.py` | 2266 passed |

After the last commit (generator dedupe, folded files, `div_ceil`), rebuilt and re-ran the tests covering what it touched:

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_marlin_gemm.py` plus the Marlin cases of `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py` | 638 passed, 6 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{per_token_group_quant,int8_quant,fp8_quant_group}.py`, `tests/kernels/mamba`, `tests/kernels/test_{cache_kernels,concat_mla_q}.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py` | 2781 passed, 629 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{cutlass_scaled_mm,machete_mm,cutlass_w4a8,block_fp8}.py` | 1375 passed, 108 skipped, 1 failed (`test_cutlass_subset`, see below) |

After the flatten commit, a fresh build directory builds and links for the same arch list with the same 160 op schemas, and:

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_marlin_gemm.py`, `tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py` | 624 passed, 264 skipped |
| `test_merge_attn_states.py`, `test_layernorm.py`, `test_fused_quant_layernorm.py`, `test_machete_mm.py`, `test_cutlass_w4a8.py`, `tests/kernels/mamba` | 5450 passed, 39 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_{moe_align_block_size,grouped_topk,moe}.py` | 2079 passed, 127 skipped |

`test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py::test_cutlass_subset` fails identically on a build of `main` on the same machine, so it is not caused by this PR.

Caveats on the local build: the machine has GCC 11.5, so the GCC ≥ 13 gate was bypassed in a scratch build dir and the DeepGEMM / DeepSelect / FlashMLA external projects were not built. ROCm and non-x86 CPU rely on CI.

## Details

**Layout**

```
csrc/
  core/             registration.h  scalar_type.hpp  cuda_compat.h
                    utils.hpp       (math.hpp + batch_invariant.hpp)
                    vec_dtypes/     (was attention/)
  cpu/              + ops.h, dynamic_4bit_int_moe_cpu.cpp
  rocm/             + dispatch_utils.h, quickreduce/
  attention/ moe/ quantization/ cutlass_extensions/ mamba/ gdn/ kimi_k3/
  *.cu, *.cuh, ops.h, torch_bindings.cpp   (was libtorch_stable/)
  cumem_allocator.*, fs_io.cpp, spinloop.cpp, *_registration.cpp
```

- `csrc/attention/` only held `Vec`/`FloatVec` dtype helpers. ROCm paged attention is the one place they are used for attention; elsewhere they are half/bf16/FP8 conversions. Hence `core/vec_dtypes/`.
- The legacy `_C` extension is ROCm-only and contains just quickreduce, so its bindings, kernel and headers live in `rocm/quickreduce/`. The op namespace (`_C_custom_ar`) is unchanged.
- The top-level `ops.h` only declared CPU ops (plus quickreduce), so it moved to `cpu/`.

**Removed as unreferenced**

- Files: `core/exception.hpp`, `cache.h`, `torch_utils.h`, `attention_utils.cuh`, `mamba/static_switch.h`, `cutlass_extensions/common.cpp`, the int8 `per_token_group_quant.cu` wrapper and its header, the second Marlin `generate_kernels.py`.
- Symbols: `VLLM_IMPLIES`, `Qk_dot`, `VLLM_SHFL_SYNC`, `TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL_EXPAND`, `DEVICE_INLINE`/`HOST_INLINE`, the legacy `AT_*` dispatch macros other than `VLLM_DISPATCH_FP8_TYPES`, `cuda_utils::ceil_div` (now `div_ceil`), `TrivialEpilogue`, `identity`, `equivalent_cutlass_type`, `enable_sm120_only`, `barrier_at_start_release`, and the non-stable-ABI branches in two CUTLASS headers.

**Things reviewers may want to look at**

- `TORCH_UTILS_CHECK` is replaced by `STD_TORCH_CHECK`. The stable build already resolved to it; in the legacy-ABI `_rocm_C` extension an unsupported KV cache dtype string now raises `std::runtime_error` instead of `c10::Error`.
- `div_ceil` is `constexpr` without `__device__` and is now called from device code in `cache_kernels.cu`, which is also built for HIP.
- The CUTLASS include dirs and `CUTLASS_ENABLE_DIRECT_CUDA_DRIVER_CALL` were dropped from the ROCm-only `_C` target, which no longer includes CUTLASS headers.
- The flatten renames about 190 files, so open PRs touching `csrc/libtorch_stable/` will need a rebase (git follows the renames for edits; newly added files need moving by hand).
- CI: the filter commits change which jobs trigger. Also, quickreduce and the CPU `ops.h` now sit under `csrc/rocm/` and `csrc/cpu/`, which `ci_config.yaml` excludes from its run-all pattern, so changes to them only trigger jobs listing those paths.

**Out of scope**

- Grouping the loose kernel files at the `csrc/` top level into subdirectories.
- `get_device_attribute` in `cuda_utils_kernels.cu` caches its first result in a function-local `static` regardless of arguments, so the SM-count and max-shared-memory queries can return each other's value. Found while reviewing; it needs its own fix.

title: [Test] Allow one bf16 ulp in the fused mHC post/pre residual check
author: Rohan138
body:
## Overview

Makes `test_deepseek_v41_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed` tolerate a one-ulp rounding difference between the fused and unfused TileLang kernels. It fails on MI355 with the ROCm 10.0 (TheRock) stack (#58761) and in main's scheduled ROCm 10 AMD CI lane.

## Claims

- The residual check allows one bf16 ulp (`rtol=2**-7`) instead of requiring bit equality.
- `layer_input` is still checked exactly, against the collapse of the fused kernel's own residual.

## Validation

`pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k fused_post_pre_delayed` (test body run directly on MI300X; the test is gated to TileLang mHC hardware), all 12 parametrizations:

| | ROCm 10 image | ROCm 7.2 image |
|---|---|---|
| before | 2 failed (`[*-7168-8]`, as in CI) | pass |
| after | pass | pass |

## Details

One of 229,376 residual values differs by 1 bf16 ulp. Its exact value sits 1.6e-7 below a rounding midpoint. ROCm 10's clang 23 packs two multiplies in `mhc_post_tilelang` into `v_pk_mul_f32`, which stops them being contracted with the following adds. That is legal under hipcc's default `-ffp-contract=fast-honor-pragmas`, and the fused kernel's result is the correctly rounded one. Comparing the reference collapse against the fused residual keeps that check exact without carrying over this rounding difference.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this test.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode on MI300X and MI325X (gfx942)
author: maeehart
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR ports the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels of #60397 to gfx942 (MI300X and MI325X). A standard decoder layer then runs as 2 kernels instead of 32. The path is opt-in with `--monokernel`, as on gfx950.

The PR was rebased onto `main` after #61082 as one commit. The commits after it merge `main` and answer the second review (see Details). gfx942 now runs the same layers whole as gfx950, with the switch of #61082 (see Details). The latest commits take the PR out of shared code, as RFC #60904 asks, and merge `main` with #62131 (see Details). The AgentX and GSM8K comparisons below are from 67206b7 and the commits before it, when the switch was `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`. The checks of the latest commits are at the end of Validation.

## Claims

MI325X, TP4, DSpark with 5 drafts. Each AgentX run is 3,600 s and is scored with InferenceX's own result code.

- AgentX at concurrency 1, against `main`: interactivity P50 goes from **216.85 to 503.53 tokens/s/user** (2.32×), P90 from **182.25 to 411.26** (2.26×), and total throughput per GPU from 4,024 to 6,546 tokens/s (1.63×).
- AgentX at concurrency 2, 4 and 8, against InferenceX's published MI325X points: P90 goes from **153.22 to 368.64** (2.41×), from **142.75 to 316.28** (2.22×) and from **81.52 to 162.61** (1.99×).
- A standard decoder layer takes 115 µs instead of 320 µs. A decode period of one request takes 7.2 ms instead of 17.9 ms.
- GSM8K strict match at concurrency 7, 3 runs each: `main` 0.9247 and this PR 0.9270 on average (pooled p 0.49). The difference is not significant.
- On a2ce22d7e317 at concurrency 7, GPQA-Diamond is 85.0%, AIME25 99.0% and RULER NIAH 40 of 40 in every cell, against 85.3%, 99.4% and 40 of 40 for the reference arm of #60397 on MI355X.
- The gfx942 code runs only with `--monokernel`, on gfx942. Outside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and the tests, the PR adds an 8-line hook to the DSpark speculator and two CI jobs.
- On gfx950 all 76 builds of the mono kernels, the 12 of the DSpark draft's runner included, have the same register and LDS use as on `main` and the same count of each instruction, apart from 1 or 2 more `s_waitcnt` in K2 and the FFN launch. The draft runner's scratch is now laid out for its MoE, see Details.
- On MI355X with `--monokernel` at TP2, two runs of each arm on 6caadd0, before #62131: GSM8K strict match 0.9257 and 0.9242 against 0.9249 and 0.9272 for `main` (see Validation).

## Limits on gfx942

- TP4 only. At TP2 the path logs one line and every layer runs vLLM's path.
- Decode steps of up to 42 rows, which is 7 requests with 5 DSpark drafts. A gfx942 workgroup has 64 KB of LDS, against 160 KB on gfx950, so a GEMV pass takes 6 tokens instead of 16. A larger step, prefill, a mixed step and a PIECEWISE graph run vLLM's path on every layer and every rank.
- gfx942 has no scaled FP4 or FP8 MFMA and uses FNUZ FP8, so the kernels read their own copies of the weights. At TP4 the weights take 170.11 GiB a rank instead of 98.88 GiB. On MI325X with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` the KV cache still holds 11.18 million tokens. MI300X (192 GiB) does not fit this well, so the numbers here are for MI325X.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on MI325X, TP4. The `main` arm is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`. The PR arm is the same image with the `vllm/` changes of #60397 and this PR copied over its `vllm` package. Both arms use the same command and environment, apart from the switch, which was `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1` on those commits.

**AgentX, concurrency 1, against `main`.** One 3,600 s run per arm, each on a fresh server.

| | `main` | PR | PR / `main` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Measured requests, no errors | 239 | 306 | |
| Interactivity P50 (tokens/s/user) | 216.85 | 503.53 | 2.32× |
| Interactivity P90 (tokens/s/user) | 182.25 | 411.26 | 2.26× |
| TTFT P50 (s) | 0.510 | 0.544 | |
| Total throughput per GPU (tokens/s) | 4,024 | 6,546 | 1.63× |

**AgentX, concurrency 2, 4 and 8.** There is no `main` run at these concurrencies, so the reference is InferenceX's published MI325X TP4 points ([Actions run 35637516947](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35637516947)). They come from an older nightly. At concurrency 1 the published P90 is 189.90, close to our `main` run.

| Concurrency | P90, published | P90, PR | Throughput per GPU, published | Throughput per GPU, PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 153.22 | 368.64 (2.41×) | 4,255 | 6,729 (1.58×) |
| 4 | 142.75 | 316.28 (2.22×) | 6,315 | 8,882 (1.41×) |
| 8 | 81.52 | 162.61 (1.99×) | 10,998 | 14,839 (1.35×) |

At concurrency 8, steps of more than 42 rows ran vLLM's path during 0.14% of the decode time.

**Accuracy.** `lm_eval` `gsm8k`, 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, greedy, DSpark with block rejection. At concurrency 7 every decode step of this PR takes the mono path. Strict match of each run:

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrency 1 | 0.9340, 0.9318 | 0.9272 |
| Concurrency 7 | 0.9242, 0.9257, 0.9242 | 0.9295, 0.9242, 0.9265, 0.9303 |

Two runs of the same code differ by up to 0.6 points, so the runs are pooled with a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with one stratum a question. At concurrency 7 this PR scores 0.23 points more than `main` (p 0.49). Over all runs the mono path scores 0.14 points less (p 0.54). The mono kernels quantize the activations to MXFP8, where vLLM's gfx942 path keeps bf16.

**GPQA-Diamond, AIME25 and RULER NIAH.** A build of a2ce22d7e317 with `--monokernel` at TP4 and concurrency 7, with the sample counts of #60397: GPQA-Diamond with 2 option orders and 4 seeds at up to 32K tokens, AIME25 with 16 seeds at up to 64K tokens, and NIAH with `niah_single_1`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K, 40 samples a cell. The reference is the MI355X result of #60397. The runs are in the comments [for NIAH](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6178954285), [for AIME25](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6182853591) and [for GPQA-Diamond](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6191592654).

| | This PR, MI325X TP4 | #60397 mono, MI355X TP2 | #60397 reference, MI355X TP2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPQA-Diamond | 85.0% (1347 of 1584) | 85.1 ± 2.2% | 85.3 ± 2.2% |
| AIME25 | 99.0% (475 of 480) | 98.3 ± 0.8% | 99.4 ± 0.3% |
| RULER NIAH, 9 cells | 40 of 40 in each | 40 of 40 in each | 40 of 40 in each |

A debugging patch, not part of this PR, ran vLLM's own layer after each mono layer on the same inputs, in steps of 6 to 42 rows. No output had a non-finite value, and the index layers' top-512 lists matched vLLM's in all 481,944 entries.

**gfx950.** `main` and this PR on the same MI355X node, two runs each, in the order PR, `main`, `main`, PR. All four runs use `--monokernel` at TP2, DSpark with 5 drafts, probabilistic drafts and block rejection, and the same server arguments (see Reproduce). `main` is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-39983a5e7a5a575a7829f5d5ada50a33d9337ec1`, and the PR runs use the same image with this PR's files at 6caadd0 copied in. At 6caadd0 the PR still held a change of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` that it no longer has (see Changes outside the model directory), and `main` did not have #62131 yet. The speed rows use random prompts of 1024 tokens and 1024 output tokens, 16 requests at concurrency 1 and 64 at concurrency 8.

| | `main`, run 1 | `main`, run 2 | This PR, run 1 | This PR, run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 8, strict match | 0.9249 | 0.9272 | 0.9257 | 0.9242 |
| Concurrency 1, output throughput (tokens/s) | 520.34 | 579.54 | 584.43 | 577.95 |
| Concurrency 1, median TPOT (ms) | 1.59 | 1.56 | 1.54 | 1.48 |
| Concurrency 1, median ITL (ms) | 7.60 | 7.59 | 7.36 | 7.38 |
| Concurrency 1, median TTFT (ms) | 66.30 | 66.55 | 67.09 | 67.02 |
| Concurrency 8, output throughput (tokens/s) | 2038.63 | 1986.51 | 2049.16 | 2099.40 |
| Concurrency 8, median TPOT (ms) | 3.37 | 3.35 | 3.47 | 3.17 |
| Concurrency 8, median ITL (ms) | 17.06 | 16.99 | 16.84 | 16.77 |
| Concurrency 8, median TTFT (ms) | 84.37 | 83.77 | 84.51 | 83.91 |

GSM8K is the same within the spread of the runs, and the median TTFT differs by less than 1 ms. With DSpark a decode step streams several tokens, so the median ITL is the time of one decode step. It was about 0.2 ms shorter with the PR, from that `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` change. The TPOT also depends on how many drafts are accepted. In the first `main` run a few first tokens took more than a second, which lowered its throughput at concurrency 1.

**Tests.** The kernel tests are in `tests/kernels/models/amd/` and run in a new one-GPU MI300 job in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`. A new four-GPU MI300 job in `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` runs the real-model and graph replay tests on gfx942 at TP4. On MI325X all of them pass on 6cb1400, and the two TP4 files take about 10 minutes. On MI355X the two TP4 files pass their CDNA4 cases on 0597d94 too, and their gfx942 cases skip there.

| File | Compared against |
|---|---|
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_topk.py` | vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode` and its candidate mask, for contexts from 100 to 300,000 tokens |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_cand_logits.py` | AITER's dense logits at the candidate positions, bit for bit |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_sparse_indexer.py` | vLLM's ROCm indexer op on a decode step, for a layer without candidate blocks, for layer 20, which writes them, and for a layer that reads them. The gfx942 indexer layer runs its own copy of that op's decode path, and this test fails when the two stop agreeing |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py` | the old SWA metadata ops and top-k packing, on 800 random batches |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_fused_markov.py` | vLLM's Markov sampling loop, and each draft token against vLLM's `_sample_logits` on the same step's logits, exactly |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_draft_lm_head.py` | an fp32 GEMM. It also checks that `wvSplitK` gets no 5-row GEMM with `--monokernel` and keeps it without |
| `test_dsv41_mono_gfx942.py` | torch references for K2's key lists, the first layer's seam, the GEMV cores and the gfx942 FP4 and FP8 conversions |
| `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` | vLLM's own decoder layers in a five-layer model with random weights, at TP4 with the FP8 indexer, at steps of 8 rows (two GEMV passes, the second one padded) and 42 rows (the limit), every layer at every decode step |
| `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` | the composed runner at TP4 on the copies made at load: the padded step against its rows run alone, and 300 replays of steps of 6, 8 and 42 rows in one CUDA graph against the first run, bit for bit |

On f0a549d a TP4 server with the mono path also answered the sanity prompts correctly, one at a time and 7 at once, and three GSM8K runs at concurrency 7 gave strict match 0.9303, 0.9272 and 0.9257. On the rebased commit pre-commit passes, and the 60 tests of `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` pass on CPU. On a2ce22d7e317, which merges `main` into the rebased commit, the new MI300 job passes in CI, and a TP4 server with the mono path ran GPQA-Diamond, AIME25 and NIAH (see Accuracy). The commits after it merge `main` again and follow four changes on `main`: #58689, which renamed the V4.1 ROCm attention classes, #55090, which split the skinny GEMM check, #58800, which moved the gfx1250 check out of `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`, and #61161, which mixes the draft step into the seed of the draft sampler. The fused Markov launch now mixes in its draft step too, so its draft tokens stay the same as those of vLLM's loop.

The latest commits move the gfx942 top-k launches into an indexer layer in the model folder, add a test that compares that layer with vLLM's indexer op, drop the `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` change, and merge `main` with #62131. On 6cb1400 pre-commit passes, the 76 tests of `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` pass on CPU, and the kernel tests and the two TP4 files pass on MI325X with the ROCm 7.2 nightly and with the ROCm 10 nightly. The new indexer test fails on a copy of the layer whose logits take the head weights of the wrong rows. With the ROCm 7.2 nightly a TP4 server with the mono path answered the sanity prompts correctly, one at a time and 7 at once, and three GSM8K runs at concurrency 7 gave strict match 0.9310, 0.9303 and 0.9295. With the ROCm 10 nightly such a server also answered the sanity prompts correctly, and GSM8K gave 0.9295, 0.9272 and 0.9242. In one of three starts with the mono path on ROCm 10 the server hung before it was ready: three ranks stopped in AITER's custom all-reduce while it registered the buffers of the decoder replay CUDA graphs, which `main` also captures. On gfx950 the 76 builds compile, see Claims, and on MI355X a TP2 server with the mono path ran the DSpark draft layers whole with the fix of #62131's scratch and answered the sanity prompts correctly.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server, the same for both arms apart from `--monokernel`, which the `main` arm leaves out:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_ROCM_FLYDSL_QR_INT4=1
export VLLM_DSV41_FUSED_COMBINE_TOPK_SWA=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
```

GSM8K uses `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` instead of the two synthetic keys, with `lm_eval` 0.4.9.2 and `num_concurrent=1` for the concurrency 1 runs:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=7,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=512,temperature=0.0,top_p=1.0
```

AgentX is the InferenceX AgentX client ([agentx-standalone.md](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/docs/agentx-standalone.md)) with the arguments of the InferenceX AgentX sweep and `--concurrency 1`, 2, 4 or 8. InferenceX's `python -m infx.results.agentic.process_agentic_result` scored each run with `TP=4 GPU_COUNT=4`.

The gfx950 runs, with the same server for both arms:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 --monokernel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
```

The speed rows are `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, with `--max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 16` and with `--max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 64`. GSM8K is the `lm_eval` command above with `num_concurrent=8` and `--gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048`.

Kernel tests on one GPU, and the TP4 tests on four:

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/models/amd/
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py
```

</details>

## Details

- **Layers.** gfx942 runs every backbone layer whole, as gfx950 does since #61082. The index layers use vLLM's FP8 indexer, because the MXFP4 indexer cache needs CDNA4. vLLM's compressor and indexer run between K1 and K2, as on gfx950. On gfx942 `mono/keylist.py` then writes the layer's key lists, so K2 is the build without the key table. On gfx942 the 3 DSpark draft layers take the FFN launch after vLLM's attention, built for the draft's 128 experts and top 3, on the target's runner. On gfx950 they run whole on a runner of their own, as #62131 added.
- **gfx942 helper ops** in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/`: the sparse indexer's decode top-512 (`topk512_gfx942.cu`) and its candidate logits, the SWA decode metadata and the top-k packing as one launch each, and DSpark's Markov sampling as one launch a draft step. With `--monokernel` on gfx942 the V4.1 ROCm attention takes the indexer layer of `sparse_indexer.py`. It runs vLLM's ROCm indexer op on every step except a step of only decode rows, which runs the decode path of that op with the top-k launches in front of vLLM's ops. The DSpark speculator asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, and the DSv4.1 draft model runs the fused Markov launches there. `draft_lm_head.py` pads the DSpark draft's 5-row logits GEMM to 6 rows, so that vLLM's dispatch takes the torch GEMM instead of `wvSplitK`. For the 32320 × 5120 lm_head shard that takes 96 µs instead of 295 µs on MI325X. Each helper leaves a call it cannot take to vLLM's own op. `topk512_gfx942.cu` is built with hipcc when the model is created. If the build fails, a warning is logged and the indexer runs vLLM's top-k ops.
- **Weight copies.** The routed experts are copied in the byte order of the gfx942 GEMVs, without vLLM's padding columns, and the dense linears as e4m3 bytes, because vLLM dequantizes those to bf16 on gfx942. The copies are made when vLLM processes the weights at load, so vLLM counts them as model memory when it sizes the KV cache. A reload writes the new copies into the first ones in place, because the kernels and the captured CUDA graphs hold their addresses.
- **Changes outside the model directory.** One hook in the DSpark speculator: `_sample_sequential` asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, if the model has one, and runs its own loop when the call returns False. Only the DSv4.1 draft model has one, and it takes a step only with `--monokernel` on gfx942. The rest are the two CI jobs. The earlier hooks in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` are now the indexer layer of `sparse_indexer.py`. The change of the padding loops of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` is dropped, because #58633 parallelises the same padding.
- **Merge of #62131.** #62131 runs the DSpark draft layers whole on gfx950, on a runner of their own whose MoE takes one FP4 group an ug task (`DRAFT_UG_GROUPS`). Its scratch was laid out for the default two groups, and with one group the ug flags take twice the room. So the flags of the upper half of the tasks were written over the start of the `normed` rows that the MoE reads as its input, at TP 2 and 4 and for every step width. Only the draft layers could be affected, not the target's output, and in a GSM8K check on MI355X `main` accepted as many drafts as this PR, so the overlap did not show there. `scratch_layout` and `scratch_bytes` now take the runner's groups. `run_ffn` checks that each MoE region of a build fits the layout, and that check found the overlap when the draft runner's K2 was built. The FFN launch reads the target's layout, because it runs on the target's runner, also for a gfx942 draft layer.
- **Since the first review.** The branch is rebased onto `main` as one commit. The gfx942 ops moved from `vllm/model_executor/layers/dsv41_gfx942/` into `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/`, as RFC #60904 asks for model kernels. `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW` and its layer-by-layer check are removed. The rebase onto #61082 takes its switch and its layer plan on gfx942 too. That removes the gfx942 paths of their own for the first layer, the window layers and the index layers, apart from `mono/keylist.py`.
- **Since the second review.** The kernel tests moved to `tests/kernels/models/amd/`. The fused Markov test checks each draft token against vLLM's `_sample_logits` on the same step's cached logits. The change to vLLM's skinny GEMM dispatch is reverted, and only the DSpark draft's lm_head avoids `wvSplitK`, with `--monokernel` on gfx942. `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` and a gfx942 graph replay test in `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` run at TP4 in a new four-GPU MI300 job. On gfx942 the first layer's output bound in `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` is 6% instead of 3%, because vLLM's gfx942 MoE keeps bf16 activations and the kernels quantize them to MXFP8, which alone moves the FFN output of the test's random weights by 4.65%. The residual stream then differs by up to 2.5% instead of 0.4 to 0.7%, so past the first layer a routing near-tie there is a gap of up to 0.02 instead of 0.01, and up to a third of the tokens may flip an expert instead of a quarter (22% seen).
- **Relation to other PRs.** Draft #61482 moves the FlyDSL stages to `vllm/models/common/amd/mono/`, and this PR edits the files it moves. Whichever of the two merges second needs a rebase. If this PR merges first, its gfx942 tests can check #61482's move on MI325X. #62131 is merged into this branch, see Merge of #62131. #58633 parallelises the padding of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`, which this PR changed until the latest commits, and neither PR needs the other. #61311 moves `amd/mono/` to `amd/specialized_decode/mono/` and replaces `mono_decode.py`, as RFC #60904 describes. A trial merge of the two conflicts in 15 files, among them `mono_decode.py` and `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`, which #61311 deletes and this PR changes. So whichever of the two merges second needs a port. #61869 adds a fused Markov sampler at the start of `_sample_sequential`, next to this PR's hook, and the two merge there without a conflict.
- **Follow-ups.** Steps of more than 42 rows on gfx942, so that 8 or more concurrent requests with 5 drafts also take the mono path. One copy of the routed experts instead of two. Other TP sizes on gfx942. The whole DSpark draft layers on gfx942, as on gfx950. `topk512_gfx942.cu` as a compiled op in `csrc/`.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Clamp BLOCK_SIZE_K to the FP8 quantization block in the batched Triton MoE
author: aniravich
body:
## Overview

`invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel` (the `BATCHED_TRITON` FP8 MoE used with DeepEP low-latency and other batched-activation all2all backends when DeepGEMM is unavailable or disabled) takes `BLOCK_SIZE_K` straight from the tuned config. With block-quantized FP8 weights the kernel loads one weight and activation scale per `BLOCK_K` tile (`offs_ks = k * BLOCK_K // group_k`), so a `BLOCK_SIZE_K` wider than the 128-wide quantization block applies one block's scale to the next block's values. 53 of the 64 shipped `fp8_w8a8, block_shape=[128,128]` configs pick `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256 for some batch sizes. The standard path already clamps (`fused_moe.py:843-844`); this PR applies the same clamp in the batched launcher.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `fused_batched_moe BLOCK_SIZE_K`, `BLOCK_SIZE_K batched fp8`, `batched triton block_shape BLOCK_K`). Rechecked 2026-10-08: open PR #51605 resizes batched Triton MoE tiles on XPU and edits the same launcher, but it does not clamp `BLOCK_SIZE_K` for block-quantized FP8 on CUDA; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong outputs from the batched Triton FP8 block-quant MoE whenever the selected config has `BLOCK_SIZE_K` > the quantization block. GLM-5.3 FP8 with DeepEP low-latency and DeepGEMM off: GSM8K 0.02 → 0.93.
- No change when the config already has `BLOCK_SIZE_K` <= 128, for per-token / per-tensor FP8, or for unquantized dtypes (`block_shape is None`).
- A smaller `BLOCK_K` can cost some kernel speed for the affected configs; correctness requires it, and the standard Triton MoE path made the same choice.

## Validation

**Unit test**: `test_batched_mm` (`tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py`) only ever ran FP8 with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 32, below the quantization block, so it could not catch this. It now also runs FP8 with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256.

| Build | `test_batched_mm` |
|---|---|
| this branch | 168 passed (216 skipped: non-FP8 dtypes and invalid quantization combinations) |
| without the fix | 12 failed: every FP8 block-quant case with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256 and K = 1024 (K = 128 is a single block, so it cannot show the bug) |

Whole `test_batched_moe.py` with the fix (H200): 470 passed, 0 failed. These counts were re-run on the branch after rebasing onto main @ 240785b8 (the rebase did not change the patch); the GSM8K runs below predate the rebase. pre-commit passes.

**End to end, GLM-5.3 FP8** (1 x 8 H200, DP4 x TP2, EP8, `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, which selects the `BATCHED_TRITON` FP8 MoE backend; fp8 KV; `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot):

| Build | CUDA graphs | Questions | GSM8K flexible / strict |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `NONE` | 200 | 0.020 / 0.005 |
| main + this fix | `NONE` | 200 | 0.930 / 0.930 |
| main | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | 1,319 | 0.012 / 0.005 |
| main + this fix | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | 1,319 | 0.923 / 0.923 |
| reference: main, DeepEP high-throughput (`FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` MoE) | `NONE` | 1,319 | 0.927 / 0.928 |

The two `main + this fix` rows ran with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` (V1 model runner); the other rows used the default V2 model runner. The unit tests and GSM8K runs above were built on main at 4a705c7b5; `fused_batched_moe.py`, `test_batched_moe.py` and the test helpers it imports are unchanged from there to this PR's base.

**In production (vLLM 0.29.0)**: GLM-5.3 RL decode on DeepEP low-latency with DP32/EP32 used `E=8,N=2048,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json`, which picks `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256 at M = 3072. Trainer-vs-inference mismatch KL was 0.139 / 0.149 instead of the usual 0.017 until we capped `BLOCK_SIZE_K` at 128 in a copy of that config (`VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER`).

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# unit test
pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py::test_batched_mm

# GSM8K
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause:** `moe_mmk` iterates K in `BLOCK_K` steps and, for block quantization (`group_k > 0 and group_n > 0`), loads the scales for `k_start // group_k` once per step (`fused_batched_moe.py:162-170`). The launcher passes `config["BLOCK_SIZE_K"]` through unchanged (`:452`). With `BLOCK_K` = 256 and `group_k` = 128, the second half of every K tile is scaled with the first half's scales. `fused_experts_impl` avoids this: its launcher `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` clamps `BLOCK_SIZE_K` to `min(block_shape)` before launch (`fused_moe.py:843-844`), but `BatchedTritonExperts`, which reads the same tuned config files through `try_get_optimal_moe_config` (`fused_batched_moe.py:934`), does not.

**How it was found:** GLM-5.3 RL with prefill/decode disaggregation; the decode instance (DeepEP low-latency, DeepGEMM off) produced much higher trainer-vs-inference KL than the prefill instance. The layer-level GEMM output matched the reference only after capping `BLOCK_SIZE_K`.

**Fix:** clamp `BLOCK_K` exactly as the standard path does.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch and test, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep DeepEP high-throughput buffers alive across DBO streams
author: aniravich
body:
## Overview

Under DBO, `DeepEPHTPrepareAndFinalize` has DeepEP allocate its dispatch outputs on the DBO comm stream, then reads them on the compute stream; the combine input crosses the other way. The caching allocator is never told about these cross-stream reads, so the other microbatch's next DeepEP call can reuse a block and overwrite it before it is read. With the DeepGEMM FP8 MoE this crashes the engine at startup with an illegal memory access in `ep_scatter`. This PR calls `record_stream` on every tensor that crosses between the two streams.

A GitHub search found no existing issue or PR for this. Related: #46990 added a ROCm-only host sync after HT dispatch/combine under DBO, possibly for the same hazard (see Details). #27666 and #38451 fixed other DBO + DeepEP HT problems.

## Claims

- Fixes the startup crash with DBO + DeepEP high-throughput + the DeepGEMM FP8 MoE (`VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1`, the defaults). For GLM-5.3 FP8 on main, 2 of 2 runs crashed in the first microbatched step without the fix. On 0.29.0, so did all 7 runs that had neither the fix nor a serializing workaround (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`, no caching allocator, host sync). With the fix, full GSM8K scores 0.927 with CUTLASS linears and 0.912 with DeepGEMM linears (DBO off: 0.923).
- Covers both directions for every experts backend behind DeepEP HT: DeepEP's outputs (comm stream to compute stream) and the reduced expert output passed to combine (compute stream to comm stream; defensive on main, see Details). With `--enable-dbo`, main runs Model Runner V1 unless `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` is set. MRV2's opt-in DBO uses the same microbatch contexts and streams, so it gets the same fix. Only Model Runner V1 was run.
- No change when DBO is off. With DBO on, there are no host syncs and no extra kernels. The cost is at most 9 `record_stream` calls per MoE layer per microbatch, plus one CUDA event per recorded block when it is freed; the allocator reuses that block only after the event completes. The throughput cost was not measured.
- DeepEP low-latency, NIXL-EP and DeepEP v2 are not affected, because on main they do not switch streams under DBO. `deepep_ll.py` is unchanged. The open #52177 adds the same comm-stream switching to DeepEP v2, so it may need the same treatment.

## Validation

**On main, without and with this PR.** Setup: GLM-5.3 FP8 on 1 x 8 H200, DP4 x TP2, EP8, `--all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --enable-dbo`, `cudagraph_mode NONE`, fp8 KV, prefix caching, Model Runner V1. Env: `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0 VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip`; the logs show `Using DEEPGEMM Fp8 MoE backend`. Build: main @ 4a705c7b + #60732 + #60734. Running GLM-5.x with DBO needs both of those; this PR is independent of them. Eval: `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 questions, `num_concurrent=256`, standard error ±0.007–0.008. Microbatched steps were counted with a diagnostic log that is not part of this PR.

| Linears | DBO | This PR | GSM8K flexible / strict | Microbatched steps per worker |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUTLASS (`--linear-backend cutlass`) | on | no | crash in the profile run, 2 / 2 runs | dies in the first one (2 x 4,096 tokens) |
| CUTLASS | on | yes | 0.927 / 0.927 | 100–149 |
| DeepGEMM | on | yes | 0.912 / 0.913 | 100–149 |
| DeepGEMM | off | yes (no-op) | 0.923 / 0.923 | 0 |

DeepGEMM-linears DBO on and DBO off differ by 0.010, about one standard error of the difference. We did not run CUTLASS linears with DBO off, or DeepGEMM linears with DBO on without the fix, on main. On 0.29.0 the latter crashes the same way (see below).

The crash without the fix:

| Run | What fails |
|---|---|
| no fix | The server never becomes ready. In the first microbatched step of the profile run, one worker raises `RuntimeError: DeepEP error: CPU recv timeout` in `buffer.dispatch`. The other microbatch thread gets `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` at `comm_stream.wait_event`, and the run ends with `torch.cat(): expected a non-empty list of Tensors`. |
| no fix, CUDA core dump | `CUDA Exception: Warp Out-of-range Address` in `_fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_2<<<(8192,1,1),(256,1,1)>>>` at `deep_gemm_utils.py:109`, which is `tl.load(expert_map + expert_id)` in `apply_expert_map`, inlined from `:241` (`expert_id = tl.load(recv_topk + ...)`). The faulting SASS loads `expert_map + expert_id * 4` after the `expert_id != -1` check, so the expert id read from the `torch.where` over DeepEP's topk ids was out of range. |

**Isolating the cause on vLLM 0.29.0.** Same 1-node GLM-5.3 setup, with backports of #60732 and #60734, DeepGEMM MoE and CUTLASS linears unless noted. The record_stream rows use an env-gated version of this patch: same three call sites, using `torch.cuda.current_stream()`.

| Variant | Questions | GSM8K flexible / strict | Microbatched steps per worker |
|---|---|---|---|
| no fix: stock 0.29.0; with backports; with backports + the `ep_gather` int64 fix from fe284ea17 (#53914); DeepGEMM or CUTLASS linears; with a core dump | | crash in the profile run, 5 / 5 runs. Core dump: same kernel and source line as on main (`deep_gemm_utils.py:110` on 0.29) | |
| no fix, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | | crash | |
| no fix, `VLLM_RANDOMIZE_DP_DUMMY_INPUTS=1` | | crash | |
| no fix, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | 200 | 0.920 / 0.920 | 69 |
| no fix, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` | 200 | 0.945 / 0.945 | 71 |
| no fix, host sync after HT dispatch/combine (the ROCm path forced on) | 300 | 0.943 / 0.943 | 90 |
| record_stream | 1,319 | 0.926 / 0.926 | 118 |
| record_stream, DeepGEMM linears | 1,319 | 0.923 / 0.923 | 132 |
| reference: no fix, FLASHINFER_CUTLASS MoE, DeepGEMM linears | 1,319 | 0.926 / 0.927 | 124 |
| reference: DBO off, DeepGEMM MoE and linears | 1,319 | 0.919 / 0.919 | 0 |

Taken together, these runs narrow the cause:
- Disabling the SM partition and randomizing the dummy inputs do not help.
- Serializing launches, disabling the caching allocator, a host sync, or `record_stream` alone each remove the crash.
- The FLASHINFER_CUTLASS MoE is fine with the same DeepGEMM linears.

That points at allocator reuse of DeepEP's buffers across DBO streams, which only the DeepGEMM MoE turns into a crash.

**Production shape (vLLM 0.29.0).** Setup: 4 x 8 H200, one engine per GPU (TP1, DP32/EP32, external load balancing), GLM-5.3-BF16 quantized online with `fp8_per_block`, DeepEP HT, eager, prefix caching, fp8 KV, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.70`. Each row is one run with the same backports as above. Prefill load: three waves of 1,536 unique prompts of about 9.7k tokens each, `max_tokens=1`, 6 in flight per rank. GSM8K (1,319 questions) was then run against rank 0.

| MoE / linears | DBO | Fix | GSM8K flexible / strict | Microbatched steps per worker | KV cache per GPU (tokens) | Prefill tok/s, wave 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FLASHINFER_CUTLASS / CUTLASS (FlashInfer autotune off*) | on | no | 0.924 / 0.923 | 278 | 645k | 79.4k |
| DeepGEMM / DeepGEMM | on | record_stream | 0.917 / 0.917 | 280 | 736k min, 796k median | 75.0k |
| DeepGEMM / DeepGEMM | off | n/a | 0.925 / 0.925 | 0 | 733k min, 803k median | 67.5k |

\* Two earlier attempts with FlashInfer autotune on stalled during startup autotuning. Throughput is the third wave over all 32 GPUs. DeepGEMM kernels JIT-compile during the first waves (`VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip`), and all three runs were still speeding up in wave 3, so these are not steady-state numbers. This table shows that DBO + DeepGEMM MoE works at production scale with the fix. It is not a performance claim for this PR. Without the fix this configuration does not start, so measuring the fix's own cost needs a MoE backend that runs either way, such as FLASHINFER_CUTLASS. We did not do that.

**CI coverage.** This PR adds no test. The existing DBO test, `tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, DP2), already runs the changed lines in its `deepep_high_throughput` case, with a BF16 MoE (`TritonExperts`) rather than the DeepGEMM path. It runs in the 2 x H100 "Distributed Features" job (optional), the B200 "Distributed" job (also optional; xfailed on Blackwell for unstable DBO accuracy; we have not checked whether that is related) and the AMD mirrors. With this patch, on 2 x H200 it passes both cases (`deepep_low_latency`, `deepep_high_throughput`) in 9 minutes, with 200+ microbatched steps per worker in the HT case. To build a 2-GPU reproducer, we quantized that model's MoE online to block FP8 with `--quantization online --quantization-config '{"moe": "fp8_per_block"}' --moe-backend deep_gemm`. The logs confirm the DEEPGEMM MoE behind `DeepEPHTPrepareAndFinalize`. That variant passed without the fix every time, so it cannot catch a regression:

| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (H200, threshold 0.62) | This PR | GSM8K strict | Microbatched steps per worker |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP2, 256 questions | no | 0.648 | 200+ |
| DP2, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256`, 512 questions | no | 0.666 | 200+ |
| DP8 / EP8, 256 questions | no | 0.652 | 100+ |
| DP2, 256 questions | yes | 0.645 | 200+ |

It would add DeepGEMM-MoE coverage of the patched path for 5–7 minutes on 2 GPUs. We can add it if reviewers want it, but it would not have caught this bug. The regression evidence is the manual GLM-5.3 runs above. Separately, quantizing V2-Lite's linears as well (`--quantization fp8_per_block`) scored about 0 on GSM8K in this DBO setup, both with and without this PR. That is unrelated and was not investigated.

**Lint:** pre-commit passes on the rebased commit: ruff check and format (0.14.0), typos (1.43.5), mypy (1.20.2), and the local SPDX, forbidden-import, `torch.cuda` and boolean-context-manager hooks. Before the rebase, with torch types resolved, mypy reported 2 errors, which also appear on the unpatched file.

**Not run:**
- Model Runner V2 with DBO (opt-in via `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). It uses the same code path.
- ROCm. The AMD CI mirrors run `test_dbo.py` with DeepEP HT, so CI will exercise the change there.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep*.py` with this patch. They do not enable DBO, so the change is a no-op in them.
- Multi-node on main.
- Whether this fixes the DeepSeek-V3.2 DBO illegal memory access noted in #60734 (see Details).
- The GPU runs on main used 4a705c7b. This branch is rebased on main @ 240785b8 (the rebase did not change the patch: same `git patch-id`), where `deepep_ht.py`, `ubatching.py`, `gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py` and `gpu/ubatch_utils.py` are unchanged. `deep_gemm_utils.py`, `deep_gemm_moe.py` and `modular_kernel.py` changed in between (#58373, #59128, #49194). On the rebased commit we re-ran `pytest -v -s tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py` on 2 x H200: 2 passed (`deepep_low_latency`, `deepep_high_throughput`) in 9 minutes. The GLM-5.3 runs were not repeated on the newer base.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# GLM-5.3 with DBO also needs #60732 and #60734.
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0 VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --enable-dbo --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --linear-backend cutlass   # omit for DeepGEMM linears
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5

# Without this PR the server fails during startup (profile run). To get the core dump, add:
CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_EXCEPTION=1 \
CUDA_COREDUMP_GENERATION_FLAGS=skip_nonrelocated_elf_images,skip_global_memory,skip_shared_memory,skip_local_memory \
CUDA_COREDUMP_FILE=core_%h_%p.nvcudmp
cuda-gdb -ex 'target cudacore core_<host>_<pid>.nvcudmp'
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main @ 240785b8, before this PR):
- **Shared streams.** `UBatchWrapper` creates one comm stream (`gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py:76`) and gives both microbatches that comm stream and the same compute stream (`:288-291`). MRV2's `UBatchRunner` does the same (`gpu/ubatch_utils.py:327,458-462`).
- **Where DeepEP allocates.** `_do_dispatch` switches to the comm stream (`deepep_ht.py:126`). It then calls `get_dispatch_layout` and `dispatch` with `allocate_on_comm_stream=False` (`:139,168`) and, under DBO, `async_finish=False` (`:138,167`). DeepEP therefore allocates recv x, scales, topk ids and topk weights on the current stream, which is the DBO comm stream's allocator pool. It runs its kernels on its own internal stream, which waits only on `previous_event`. With `async_finish=False` it then makes the calling stream wait for that internal stream, and it records no other stream on its tensors: its HT dispatch and combine call `record_stream` only when `async_finish=True` (`csrc/deep_ep.cpp`).
- **Where they are read and freed.** `dbo_switch_to_compute_sync()` (`:177`) orders the compute stream after the dispatch, and `_receiver` reads the outputs there: first the `torch.where` over the topk ids (`:225`), then the experts. Once those kernels are enqueued the Python references are dropped; for example, `expert_topk_ids` is rebound by the `torch.where`. The blocks go back to the comm pool, free for any later comm-stream work.
- **How they get overwritten.** The other microbatch's next DeepEP call allocates from the same comm-stream pool. Its kernels wait only on its own `previous_event`, captured on the compute stream before it yielded (#38451). The DBO comm stream itself waits only on that microbatch's compute-done event (`ubatching.py:86-87`, recorded in `yield_and_switch_from_compute_to_comm` before the yield). Both events were recorded before this microbatch enqueued its reads. So that call's outputs can land in the freed blocks and be written before the reads run. The DeepGEMM contiguous path then loads `expert_map[expert_id]` for whatever id it finds (`deep_gemm_utils.py:107-110`, called from `_fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_2` at `:244-247`), which is the faulting load in the core dump.
- **Reverse direction.** For experts that leave the weight-and-reduce to the prepare/finalize (`TopKWeightAndReduceDelegate`), `_finalize` reduces into a new compute-stream tensor (`apply(output=None)`, `:365`), and combine reads it on the comm stream (`:376`). `dbo_switch_to_compute()` (`:389`) does not order the compute stream after the combine. The tensor is freed when `_finalize` returns, so later compute-stream work, such as shared experts or the other microbatch, can reuse the block while combine is still reading it. On main, though, no experts class that can run behind DeepEP HT delegates: the delegating classes all use the batched activation format, DeepEP HT uses the standard one, and the standard CUTLASS FP8 and Marlin experts return `TopKWeightAndReduceNoOP`. Every experts class that can run behind DeepEP HT reduces itself (DeepGEMM, Triton, FlashInfer CUTLASS, ...), so the combine input is the per-microbatch workspace (or the caller's output tensor when the shapes match), which is not freed there. The `_finalize` call (1 of the 9) is therefore defensive on main, for a future delegating experts class. We did not observe this direction.
- **Dispatch inputs.** Tokens, scales, topk ids and topk weights are already safe today, because they are freed only after `dbo_switch_to_compute_sync()` makes the compute stream wait on the comm stream. They are recorded anyway (4 of the 9 calls), so their safety does not depend on that ordering; this is also the version validated on 0.29.

**Fix:** `_dbo_record_stream()` calls `t.record_stream(current_stream())` on each non-`None` tensor when `dbo_enabled()`. It is called in three places:
- in `_do_dispatch`, after switching to comm, on the dispatch inputs (compute to comm);
- in `_receiver`, before the `torch.where`, on DeepEP's outputs (comm to compute);
- in `_finalize`, after switching to comm, on the reduced expert output (compute to comm).

When a recorded tensor is freed, the allocator records an event on the consuming stream and does not reuse the block until that event has completed. For the two compute-to-comm sites the actual reader is DeepEP's internal stream. Recording the DBO comm stream still covers it, because with `async_finish=False` the DBO comm stream waits for DeepEP's kernels before dispatch or combine returns, and the tensors are freed after that. DeepEP's handle and layout tensors and `combined_x` are used only on the DBO comm stream and DeepEP's internal stream, so they are not recorded (but see "Not covered").

CUDA graphs: DeepEP HT is never captured. vLLM forces `cudagraph_mode` NONE for HT with DP > 1, and DBO needs DP > 1. PyTorch also supports `record_stream` during capture.

**Why FLASHINFER_CUTLASS does not crash, but may still race.** The hazard is in the prepare/finalize, so it does not depend on the experts backend; what differs is what a corrupted id does. FlashInfer's CUTLASS MoE receives `ep_rank`/`ep_size` and keeps only ids in this rank's range (`expert >= start_expert && expert < end_expert`, `cutlass_fused_moe_kernels.cuh:223,449` in FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1). A garbage id is therefore dropped instead of dereferenced, and garbage activations or weights would only produce wrong numbers. With FLASHINFER_CUTLASS, DBO matches DBO off on GSM8K: 0.922–0.927 on main in #60734, and 0.924 at EP32 above. So we have no evidence that the race fires there in practice. We also do not know why the window opens reliably for GLM-5.3 with DeepGEMM but not for DeepSeek-V2-Lite with DeepGEMM. #60734 notes an illegal memory access with DeepSeek-V3.2 and DBO that also uses FLASHINFER_CUTLASS and also disappears with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`. We have not tested whether this PR fixes it.

**Why ROCm already host-syncs.** #46990 added `_sync_dbo_comm_if_needed` (`deepep_ht.py:61,71-76`), a host `synchronize()` of the current stream after HT dispatch and combine under DBO, on ROCm only. Its comment cites reuse of "Buffer-owned communication workspace". Forcing the same sync on CUDA also removed the crash (0.29 table). We suspect ROCm hit the same allocator hazard, but we have no ROCm hardware to check, so this PR leaves the ROCm sync in place; on ROCm, `record_stream` only adds bookkeeping.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

1. Use the host sync on CUDA as well. It works (0.29 table), but it blocks the CPU after every HT dispatch and combine of every microbatch: 300 times per step for GLM-5.3's 75 MoE layers. That gives up the CPU run-ahead DBO needs for overlap. Not benchmarked.
2. `allocate_on_comm_stream=True`. This moves the outputs to DeepEP's internal stream, but the compute stream still reads them, so on its own it does not order reuse. DeepEP also accepts it only together with `previous_event` and `async_finish=True`, and vLLM disables `async_finish` under DBO. Not tried.
3. `record_stream` (this PR). It marks exactly the tensors that cross streams, adds no syncs or kernels, and keeps the fix inside the one prepare/finalize that switches streams under DBO.
</details>

**Not covered:** blocks freed on the comm stream itself, for example `combined_x` after `output.copy_` in the finalize receiver, are reused by later comm-stream allocations. DeepEP's kernels for that later call wait on `previous_event`, a compute-stream event, rather than on the comm stream, so in principle they could run before the earlier comm-stream copy finishes. We inferred this from DeepEP's source (its internal stream waits on `previous_event` when one is given, otherwise on the calling stream) and have not observed it. `record_stream` cannot express this ordering. Passing `previous_event=None` under DBO would make DeepEP wait on the comm stream instead. That is left for a follow-up because it changes the ordering #38451 tuned.

**Related:**
- #60732 fixes the DSA indexer crash under DBO.
- #60734 fixes DSA shared top-k under DBO.
- #60733 clamps `BLOCK_SIZE_K` in the batched Triton FP8 MoE.
- #52177 (open) adds DBO to DeepEP v2 with the same comm-stream switching as HT.

The first three came out of the same GLM-5.3 bring-up and are independent of this PR. The `ep_gather` int64 fix in fe284ea17 (#53914) is already on main; the 0.29 no-fix runs crash with and without a backport of it.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Use int64 index mappings to fix row-offset overflow
author: njhill
body:
Kernels compute row offsets as `req_state_idx * stride`. With int32 idx_mapping / expanded_idx_mapping this wraps once the product crosses 2**31 (e.g. slot 2148 at 1M context, slot 716 for mrope positions), causing illegal memory accesses or silent writes to the wrong row.

Restore int64 for the request-slot index mappings at their creation sites (main and dummy input batches, speculator and dflash buffers, batch-shard local copies, penalties bincount mapping) so the offset math is promoted to int64 in every kernel, rather than casting at each load site. Derived tensors in batch_shard / pcp_manager now use new_empty/new_zeros to inherit dtypes from their source. expanded_local_pos stays int32. The staged-write kernel casts its own int32 row index to int64.

Fixes #57030. Supersedes #60535; the test is adapted from that PR.

Co-authored by @vllmellm.

title: [CPU] Optimize routed INT8 W8A8 MoE GEMM dispatch
author: tianmu-li
body:
## Overview

Extend the routed CPU MoE dispatch approach from [#50949](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50949) to INT8 W8A8: select brgemm from each expert tile's actual row count instead of the call-wide average. Use brgemm for four-row tiles and share the existing tinygemm arithmetic between BF16 and FP16.

On a 32-core Qwen3 W8A8 serving comparison, the change improves the geometric mean of output throughput across nine concurrency levels by 1.41%, with 5.76% at concurrency 32 and 4.42% at concurrency 64. Peak-concurrency throughput remains at parity. The concurrency-32 baseline varies between repeats; both runs are shown below.

As #50949 describes the approach:
> Select BRGEMM from each expert block's actual `M` and `N`.

Open-PR searches for CPU INT8 MoE and routed GEMM dispatch found no duplicate. #50949 covers FP8/MXFP4; this change covers the separate INT8 W8A8 implementation.

## Claims

- Concentrated routing can use brgemm even when the average tokens per expert would select tinygemm.
- Both routed INT8 GEMM stages select their kernel per tile and release brgemm state when used by the parallel callback.
- BF16 and FP16 support small expert tiles through the same VNNI arithmetic, with conversion directly to the requested intermediate dtype.

## Validation

Reviewed head: `cedc8f26c0`; branch base: `9f3d70e081`.

```bash
# Focused checks: 68 passed during PR readiness review
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py \
  -k 'int8_w8a8 or small_expert_blocks' \
  tests/kernels/test_awq_int4_to_int8.py::TestInt4ScaledMmCpu -q

pre-commit run --files csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/gemm.h \
  csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/moe_int8.cpp \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py
git diff --check 9f3d70e081 HEAD
```

All applicable hooks passed. The BF16/FP16 test covers expert occupancies `(3, 4, 5, 33)`, including mixed dispatch and a block tail, and runs in CPU kernel CI. Commands omit host-specific affinity settings.

### Serving comparison

Following #50949's Sonnet 256/256 concurrency sweep, compare the same base and candidate with `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w8a8` (revision `b2b37fb1c4cd5a5769b841ef1f672627b8304d8e`), BF16, TP=1, DP=1, and 32 physical compute cores.

| Concurrency | Base output tok/s (runs 1 / 2) | Candidate output tok/s (runs 1 / 2) | Mean throughput change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 35.19 / 35.21 | 35.14 / 35.07 | -0.26% |
| 2 | 53.20 / 53.16 | 53.07 / 53.18 | -0.09% |
| 4 | 82.35 / 82.31 | 82.57 / 82.45 | +0.22% |
| 8 | 130.33 / 130.31 | 131.64 / 131.43 | +0.93% |
| 16 | 192.93 / 191.13 | 195.61 / 195.89 | +1.94% |
| 32 | 294.42 / 279.66 | 303.41 / 303.74 | +5.76% |
| 64 | 437.61 / 435.76 | 456.60 / 455.33 | +4.42% |
| 128 | 654.13 / 654.97 | 652.40 / 655.86 | -0.06% |
| 256 | 872.06 / 871.38 | 872.51 / 871.71 | +0.04% |

## Details

The previous selector uses `max(1, M * topk / E)` for the whole call. That average hides concentrated routing and expert-block tails. Both stages now use actual tile dimensions, skip empty tiles, and track brgemm use within each parallel callback.

The routed INT8 two-argument selector uses `M > 3` for full-width tiles. The existing one-argument selector continues to serve INT8 linear, INT4, and shared-expert callers. FP8/MXFP4 thresholds are unchanged.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, and this description.

title: [Feature][Model Loader] Apply model-owned MTP shard selection to RunAI ModelStreamer
author: zhy76
body:
## Overview

Apply the existing model-owned checkpoint selection hook to RunAI ModelStreamer before reading safetensors shards. Closes #60691; extends the DefaultModelLoader optimization in #60152 without duplicating MTP naming rules.

## Performance: Qwen3.5 MTP with remote RunAI

Five alternating baseline/patch pairs ran on the same H20×8 node (TP=8), with the same checkpoint, serving arguments, resources and experiment-only quantization compatibility setting. Both images shared the same runtime base; only the RunAI loader override differed. All ten replicas reached Kubernetes Ready with zero restarts. Each passed four fixed HTTP requests (256 output tokens total) with nonzero draft acceptance.

| Metric | Baseline median (range), 5 runs | Patch median (range), 5 runs | Median improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scheduled → Kubernetes Ready | 473 s (450–511) | 360 s (326–394) | 1.31×; 113 s less |
| Draft load and weight-finalization window | 143.646 s (135.974–147.128) | 14.908 s (14.444–15.724) | 9.64×; 128.738 s less |

The five paired observations, in execution order (baseline → patch, seconds), were:

- Scheduled → Ready: 473 → 360, 477 → 394, 462 → 379, 450 → 353, 511 → 326.
- Draft window: 143.646 → 14.572, 146.395 → 14.444, 141.378 → 15.724, 135.974 → 14.908, 147.128 → 15.054.

The median improvements are separately calculated statistics, not additive stage savings. The main-load window varied considerably and showed no stable improvement. Compilation, CUDA Graph capture, and warmup remained enabled and still contribute to Ready time.

RunAI checkpoint iterator entries for the draft fell from **75,881 to 1,121**; main remained at 75,881. The code path therefore ran, but entries are not measured object-store bytes, and the draft window includes more than pure I/O. Pending time is excluded. Pod events showed cached application images in every run. One patch run had a 58 s post-scheduling, pre-main interval, retained in the total. OSS/network load was not controlled, and no independent I/O/CPU bottleneck profile was taken; this is a result for this checkpoint and environment, not a general speedup guarantee.

Initial TP=8 runs had near-zero draft acceptance in **both** arms: this checkpoint's compressed-tensors ignore entry for mtp did not match its BF16 draft subtree under this runtime's exact-name matching. The reported pairs apply the same experiment-only subtree regex to **both** arms. That configuration change is not in this PR. Across restarts, some generated continuations differed even baseline versus baseline, so the fixed requests demonstrate working serving and nonzero draft use, not numerical equivalence or a full accuracy evaluation.

The final PR commit was separately rebuilt and checked on GPU: Ready, zero restarts, four HTTP 200 responses, 256 output tokens, and 122/133 draft tokens accepted/proposed. This one final-image check is not mixed into the five-pair performance medians. A local RunAI Qwen3.5 smoke test also reached Ready with nonzero draft acceptance. Exact OSS bytes were not measured.

## Additional GLM-5.3 MTP check (one pair, remote RunAI)

GLM-5.3 uses the existing DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM MTP model hook; this PR adds no GLM-specific naming rule. A separate H20×8, TP=8 baseline/patch pair used the same checkpoint, node, GPUs and serving configuration, changing only the loader image. Both replicas reached Ready with zero restarts and served four HTTP 200 requests (256 output tokens total per arm) with nonzero draft acceptance.

| Metric | Baseline | Patch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main RunAI iterator entries | 118,629 | 118,629 |
| Draft RunAI iterator entries | 118,629 | 2,698 |
| Scheduled → Kubernetes Ready | 1,735 s | 1,079 s |
| Draft load/weight-finalization window | 705.267 s | 21.896 s |

This is one paired observation, not a repeated performance estimate. Iterator entries are not measured OSS bytes; mixed shards can still be read in full. The GLM runtime disabled global torch.compile in both arms, although graph/kernel warmup still ran, so these figures do not establish compile-on performance. Exact object-store bytes were not measured.

## Design and implementation

- **Why before the iterator:** RunAI previously prepared the complete checkpoint file list before the model's load_weights method could discard unwanted MTP tensors. A later filter cannot undo whole-file RunAI reads. The loader now obtains the existing model-owned is_unused_checkpoint_weight predicate and selects complete shards before constructing the RunAI iterator. This PR does not define new MTP naming rules or add hooks to model classes; #60152 introduced the hook for opted-in models.
- **How selection works:** Local checkpoints reuse the safetensors-header selector. For S3-compatible and other remote storage, the loader reads model.safetensors.index.json at the resolved weights URI (including model_weights overrides) and maps wanted tensor names to files before RunAI reads payloads. Mixed and unindexed shards remain included. Before excluding an indexed shard, RunAI's metadata reader verifies its actual safetensors header using range reads. If the index omits a required tensor or the header cannot be verified, selection retains the original full list. Only selection metadata is fetched locally; weight payloads are not staged to disk.
- **Safety and distributed behavior:** Selection retains original file order. WORLD CPU ranks agree on a conservative union of required files; differing original file lists disable selection. With distributed RunAI and pipeline parallelism, selection retains the original full file list and skips the new WORLD agreement collective, preserving the existing streaming path. Without a model hook, or with missing/unusable optional index metadata, the original full file list is used. If the predicate rejects every shard, the full list is retained so the model's own missing-weight error can still surface. Model-rule and tensor-read errors propagate.
- **Scope and tradeoff:** This is file-level selection, not tensor-range filtering: a mixed shard is still read in full. The extra index fetch, header-range reads for excluded shards and CPU collective are the cost. Earlier Hugging Face checkpoint download and runai_streamer_sharded are unchanged. Examples of existing hook-bearing MTP implementations include Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next, Nemotron-H and DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM; unadapted models keep the full-list fallback.

This complements #60152 (Default loader) and #58016 (lazy per-tensor reads): the former owns the model rule, while this PR applies it to RunAI whole-file loading. It also complements #48023/#42060 (draft weights URI inheritance).

## Tests and CI status

The review fixes add a runtime default checkpoint-selection method that keeps all weights, preserve detection of structural models without the optional hook, and add regressions for stale indexes and unavailable shard headers. The real Qwen3.5 MTP checkpoint E2E test is included. This follow-up passed local Ruff, formatting and Python syntax checks; the new native RunAI and GPU cases have not been executed in this follow-up and await the authorized upstream test run. The performance measurements above were not repeated for these review fixes.

Commit focused model-loader tests: **44 passed, 4 deselected**, including five real two-process Gloo selection/fallback cases. Separate RunAI/S3-emulator fixtures exercise actual file GETs and tensor values with Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next and Nemotron-H predicates. Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passed locally. Full-repository pytest did **not** pass: CPU collection lacked soundfile. Upstream CI is **not green**: the pre-run authorization gate and Read the Docs build failed, while full Buildkite CI has not run. These are not represented as passing checks.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, test and prepare this change; the submitter reviewed the contents.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Declare 64-token kernel blocks for SM120 sparse backends
author: xzwgit
body:
### Summary
On SM120, the DSV41 sparse-MLA backends declare only `[128]`-token kernel blocks (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` returns `[64 if family(90) else 128]` / `[128]`), so serving with `--block-size 64` dies in block-size negotiation:

```
ValueError: No common block size for 64 (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41: [128]; DEEPSEEK_V41_INDEXER: [128])
```

This declares `[64]` on SM12x for the two sites (indexer backend, sparse MLA backend, FlashInfer sparse backend), mirroring the existing SM90 branch. The SWA/backend selection is untouched.

The approach is @aagallo's (described in #59203); this PR adds the validated matrix below.

### Matrix validation (8x RTX PRO 6000, SM120, TP8)
Stack: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev158+gab905a885` + FlashInfer `0.7.1rc5`, `--block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`, DeepGEMM switched between PR14 head (`40592bd`) and the current pin (`1e1842a`):

| vLLM tree | DeepGEMM | result |
|---|---|---|
| stock | `1e1842a` | fails negotiation (error above) |
| this PR (uniform `[64]`) | `40592bd` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| this PR (uniform `[64]`) | `1e1842a` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| per-layer variant (`[64,128]` + `64*max(1,cr)` specs) | `40592bd` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| per-layer variant | `1e1842a` | serves, 17x19=323 |

All four patched cells boot in ~90-160 s and answer correctly; zero failures. An earlier `attention.hpp:484` observed with uniform-64 on an older stack (0.30.1rc1.dev738 + FlashInfer main @c11f8ba + DeepGEMM 6901431) does not reproduce on current main with either DeepGEMM build — details in #59203.

Pairs naturally with #57292 (fail-fast when FlashInfer lacks runtime page sizes).

Addresses the SM120 serving failure in #59203.

### Test Plan
- [x] 5-cell matrix above (serve + correctness per cell)
- [x] pre-commit / CI

---

## Requirements & validation (added after review)

**FlashInfer requirement: `flashinfer-python >= 0.7.1rc5` (runtime page sizes).** Measured end to end on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120):
- pinned `0.7.0.post1` + this PR: does **not** serve — fails in ~110 s with `page_block_size=32 is unsupported; decode kernels are instantiated only for page_block_size=64` (64-token kernel blocks give ratio-2 layers 32-token compressed pages; the pin has no runtime page sizes). Stock fails on the pin as well.
- `0.7.1rc5` + this PR: serves at default and `--block-size 64`; `--block-size 128` does not serve on this stack in either declaration form (see matrix below), so the PR buys default-64 — the only geometry that serves on the default BLHNC layout.

Landing order per review discussion: after the FlashInfer bump (#60948), or together with the #57292 guard.

**Matrix (stock / A=[64] / C=[64,128] x default / 64 / 128, GSM8K n=100):** stock fails both ways (assertions upthread); A and C serve at default and 64 (GSM8K 89-91%, no variant-dependent degradation); 128 fails under both declarations (A: BLHNC layout guard; C: FlashInfer `block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64`). Decode throughput of the four servable configs is within <1% at c1/c4.

**No unit test, by review:** an earlier revision added `tests/v1/attention/test_dsv41_indexer_block_sizes.py`, but it pinned kernel-support values that will drift (and the block size is asserted in C++ at kernel launch, so a black-box version would need a real kernel anyway). Per review it was removed and each SM12x `[64]` now carries a short inline comment naming the failure it avoids (#59203).

**Revalidation on the final form** — 8x RTX PRO 6000 96 GB (SM120), vLLM 0.33.0 with these two declarations, fp8 KV, no explicit `--block-size`: negotiation reports `Setting kv cache block size to 64 for FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41/DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA/DEEPSEEK_V41_INDEXER/CompressorBackend`; READY in ~7.5 min (cold JIT); KV cache 2,397,337 tokens at 32,768 max-model-len; 4/4 short-answer probes correct and greedy output byte-identical across 3 runs.

Coordinated with #56509 (same failure, overlapping declarations).
