title: [Kernel][Build] Bump DeepGEMM to the 26/09/30 release and adapt the sparse indexer
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

Bump the vendored DeepGEMM pin to the tip of `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` (`6ce1c5e`): upstream's 26/09/30 public release (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#30, deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#462) plus vendoring import fixes (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) and a relaxed paged sparse MQA page-stride guard (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33). Adapt vLLM to the breaking MQA-logits API.

## Claims

- vLLM builds, vendors and imports DeepGEMM 2.8.1.
- The DSA sparse indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, HY-V4) keeps working on SM90/SM100/SM120 with the new MQA-logits API.
- On SM100 the FP8 indexer cache stays numerically identical: same FP8 values and the same per-token power-of-two scale, now stored as four packed UE8M0 bytes (a valid MXFP8 encoding) because SM100 MQA kernels only take MX scales.

## Breaking changes in DeepGEMM `1e1842a` → `6ce1c5e`

| Change | vLLM impact | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| `deep_gemm/__init__.py` imports a new `deep_gemm/locality_domain.py` | not vendored → `import vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` fails | install it in `deepgemm.cmake` |
| `_C.py` registered the locality-domain shim as `deep_gemm._C.locality_domain` | relative import fails when vendored as `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`, and vLLM then silently treats DeepGEMM as unavailable | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31 (in the pin); `tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py` now imports the package so CI catches this |
| The C++ MLOPart bridge imported `deep_gemm.utils.mlopart` and the epilogue module was named `deep_gemm.epilogue` | `localize()` (not called by vLLM) would fail when vendored | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 (in the pin): `_C.py` passes its `__package__` to the new `init(library_root_path, python_package_name)` |
| `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` page-stride guard lowered from 512 to 256 B (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33) | DeepSeek-V4.1's sparse-logits block stride stays 512-aligned, which still satisfies it | none |
| `fp8_mqa_logits`, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `fp8_gemm_nt_skip_head_mid`, `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` removed | unused by vLLM | none |
| `clean_logits` / `logits_dtype` removed from `fp8_fp4_(paged_)mqa_logits`; `max_seqlen_k` now required (> 0) | wrapper signatures | `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`; prefill chunk metadata carries a host `max_seqlen_k` bound (no device sync) |
| `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` returns **compressed** logits `[M, max_seqlen_k]` (row `i` starts at K position `ks[i]`) on every arch | prefill top-k / candidate-block / DCP consumers indexed absolute columns | consumers run on row starts `0`, ends `ke - ks`; output indices are unchanged (already relative to `ks`) |
| SM100 MQA kernels take only MXFP8/MXFP4 with packed UE8M0 scales, **BF16 weights**, return **BF16 logits**; paged is varlen-only | FP8 indexer (fp32 per-token scale, scale folded into fp32 weights) rejected | see below |
| `bf16_mega_gate` default `scoring_func` → `'sqrtsoftplus'` | vLLM always passes it | none |
| FP8×FP4 / BF16 Mega MoE assert DeepGEMM's SM count equals the device's | only DBO + DeepEP-HT lowers it (`ubatch_utils.py`), not combined with Mega MoE today | none (noted) |
| Epilogue classes (`epilogue=` kwarg), locality domains, `shutdown` | additive | none |

### SM100 FP8 indexer

Every CUDA FP8 indexer writer already stores an exact power-of-two scale `2^ceil(log2(amax/448))` per 128-wide token. On SM100 (`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()`) the writers store that scale's exponent as four equal UE8M0 bytes instead of the fp32, which is an exact MXFP8 encoding of the same values (same cache size, same FP8 bytes):

| Writer | Models |
|---|---|
| C++ `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` (`scale_fmt="mxfp8"`) | DeepSeek-V2-class `Indexer` (V3.2 via that class, DeepSeek MTP), HY-V4, DeepSeek-V3.2 under PCP |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 fused norm/RoPE (`_fused_norm_rope_kernel`) | DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5/5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`), Dots3Note, V3.2 MTP |
| DeepSeek-V4 compressor (Triton; the CuTeDSL compressor is head-512 MLA only) | DeepSeek-V4 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `indexer_k_norm_rope_store` | DeepSeek-V4.1 |
| GLM-5.3 kpool prefill compress + decode update | GLM-5.3 |

Readers need no change: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (prefill, all of the above) and the DCP/PCP gathers copy the 4 scale bytes verbatim, and DeepGEMM reads the paged cache directly. The 512-wide MLA caches, MXFP4 caches, and the MiniMax-M3 / Qwen4 indexers are untouched.

FP8 Q keeps folding its per-(token, head) power-of-two scale into `weights`; `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` passes unit MX Q scales (exact, since `relu(s·x) = s·relu(x)` for `s > 0`) and casts weights to BF16. The BF16 logits are upcast to FP32 for the existing FP32-only top-k kernels (`as_fp32_logits`); routing BF16 logits straight to a BF16-capable top-k (DeepSelect / LiteTopK, #59921/#59922) is a follow-up.

SM90 and SM120 keep the FP8 format, FP32 weights and FP32 logits. Consequently the FP8 indexer cache's scale bytes now differ between SM100 and other architectures: moving that KV cache between SM100 and non-SM100 nodes (cross-generation PD disaggregation, shared KV offload) is not supported for these models. Same-architecture setups are unaffected.

## Validation

All on 4x GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13, torch 2.13; baseline = `main` with the old pin `1e1842a`, same build otherwise.

**GLM-5.3-Flash** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP=3, `--max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --reasoning-parser glm47`, `reasoning_effort=low`), on the rebased branch vs `main` bfa7e5b7af. MRCR prompts are far longer than the indexer's coverage (2048 pools × 4 = 8K tokens), so they exercise top-k selection; long prefills also engage the TP prefill row sharding from #54951 (confirmed with a temporary log, e.g. 129K-row steps split `[47458, 18791, 42577, 19957]` across ranks):

| | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRCR, 60 samples of 16K–32K tokens (`tests/evals/mrcr`), match ratio (2 / 4 / 8 needles) | 0.794 (0.823 / 0.798 / 0.760) | 0.810 (0.904 / 0.791 / 0.735) |
| MRCR, 24 samples of 57K–66K tokens, match ratio | 0.578 (4 runs hit max_tokens) | 0.665 |
| GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | 90.8% | 91.6% |
| Serving, 4 runs of 128 × (4096 in / 512 out) at concurrency 32, output tok/s | 1492 / 1544 / 1491 / 1471 | 1484 / 1476 / 1337 / 1501 |
| Median ITL | 19.85 ms | 19.9 ms |

GLM-5.3 serving throughput tracks the MTP acceptance length, which varies per run (the 1337 tok/s run had 1.31 vs ~1.7–1.8 elsewhere); runs with matching acceptance agree (1476 @ 1.70 vs 1471 @ 1.71).

**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (before the rebase onto current `main`; baseline 26a488ad93), TP2 + EP, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`; GSM8K via `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot, 2 rounds). GSM8K prompts fit inside the indexer's coverage (512 × 4 = 2K tokens), so this checks the SM100 path end to end rather than top-k selection:

| indexer cache | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | 95.5% / 94.6% | 94.8% / 94.6% |
| mxfp4 | 94.9% | 94.7% |

**Serving** — same server, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos`, one warm-up + 3 runs each, sequential on the same GPUs:

| this PR | 2946 (2928–2958) | 18.89 ms | 12.94 ms |

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid reusing random draws across block verification rounds
author: DimensionSTP
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61114. Give block verification fresh acceptance and draft random draws when an uncommitted position is revisited in a later round.

## Claims

- Removes the cross-round sampling bias for deterministic and probabilistic drafts in Model Runner V2.
- Preserves seeded repeat, request-order and batch-splitting behavior in both verification modes. Standard probabilistic token sequences change, but their target distribution is retained.
- Uses a shared step-seed helper without new forwarding parameters, round-position tensors, scheduler state, host synchronization or sampling kernel launches.
- Covers ordinary draft sampling, the shared DFlash2/LiLiCorr candidate walk, DSpark and ordinary watermark fallback.

## Validation

Real V2 generation with one-layer, context-independent Llama target/draft models, TP=1, float32, two speculative tokens and 10,000 requests per configuration:

| Draft | Verification | Expected P(third token = 0) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deterministic | standard | 0.5000 | 0.5039 | 0.5039 |
| Deterministic | block | 0.5000 | 0.4171 | 0.4989 |
| Probabilistic | standard | 0.3000 | 0.3083 | 0.3055 |
| Probabilistic | block | 0.3000 | 0.3558 | 0.2898 |

All six output marginals pass in each updated configuration; both original block cases fail. Worker types and nonzero acceptance metrics confirm the real V2 draft-model path. All four updated configurations pass seeded repeat, reordered requests and split batches. Standard deterministic output retains its original hash; standard probabilistic output does not. The probabilistic block run also passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Before-fix values are the retained original model measurements; the updated four-case matrix was rerun after this review.

The official multi-round regression fails before the fix. Disabling only the acceptance step helper fails the deterministic block distribution assertion. Disabling only the cached draft step helper while retaining the acceptance repair also fails the probabilistic distribution assertion. Disabling only the candidate-walk helper fails both FP32/FP64 parity cases. These negative controls contain actual assertion failures, not setup errors or skips. The mixed watermark test covers the fused ordinary fallback and unchanged raw-logit caching.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/watermarking --ignore=tests/watermarking/test_engine_compatibility.py --ignore=tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/watermark.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash2/speculator.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/watermarking/test_gumbel.py
git diff --check
```

Results: 350 official tests pass in the CUDA run, with three existing skips; all applicable native hooks pass. Separately, 175 CPU controls pass, with 76 accelerator-dependent skips. Five supplemental CUDA controls cover signed seeds, scalar/per-token cache columns, padding, graph replay and ordinary watermark fallback. Model tests use Triton attention and a bounded KV cache because this host's driver cannot run the reused CUDA 13 FlashAttention wheel. The candidate-walk tests cover FP32/FP64 step-seed parity and retain the existing conditional proposal-cache, padding and graph-replay checks. No AMD, full-runner CUDA graph, adaptive-policy model evaluation or throughput claim is made.

## Details

Block verification reads uniforms for draft positions past the finally accepted prefix. Reusing `(request seed, position)` in the next round reuses randomness conditioned on the preceding decision. Probabilistic drafting has the same problem with its position-keyed Gumbel noise.

Following review, `spec_step_seed(seed, step)` mixes the draft step into the seed's upper 32 bits. Cached Gumbel sampling uses its existing cache column; the DFlash2/LiLiCorr walk uses its loop step. A request's `(position, step)` pair does not repeat across rounds. Block acceptance calls the same helper with `i` inside its verification loop, always starting from the original request seed. No new flag is needed, including in DSpark and the watermark adapters. The fused ordinary watermark fallback uses the same cached step seed; context-keyed watermark draws are unchanged.

Cached draft seeding now applies under standard verification too. This changes standard probabilistic seeded sequences, not their target distribution; the updated implementation remains reproducible. This is distinct from #59355/#60945's residual lookahead bounds and #60652's grammar-invalid drafts, and complements #54282's within-round draft/target stream separation.

Related PR #61153 addresses the same bug with an explicit round-position tensor and a different seed mixer. This implementation instead uses the existing draft step inside the kernels. Both implementations passed the earlier shared four-case CUDA distribution comparison on #61153 at `170dcc217`; that comparison predates this reviewer-requested simplification. This is an alternative implementation of the same repair, not a claim that #61153 is incorrect.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Clear stale shared block-table rows
author: positive666
body:
## Overview

A larger MTP decode graph can read stale shared block-table rows after the target batch shrinks, allowing padded work to address another request's cache or state.

Move shared-row cleanup into `BlockTables`, as suggested in review.

## Claims

- Clear previously active rows during gather and dummy preparation, using the existing buffers and gather kernel.
- Preserve active rows, returned views, and independent PCP output buffers.
- Remove the MTP caller workaround without changing model math.

## Validation

Base: `92dc3dd39332`, H20.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regressions without the fix | 7 failed |
| BlockTables, speculator, PCP suites with the fix | 140 passed |
| Model/cache/offload compatibility suites | 656 passed |
| Pre-commit, including mypy and CI test tethering | Passed |
| BlockTables with strict GPU sync checking | 17 passed |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP8/MTP3, stream=true | 47/47 correct, no truncation |

Serving used CUDA Graphs and native CPU offload on H20×8: cold requests, GPU cache hits, forced CPU restores, branched prefixes, and mixed concurrency (8/5/2/8/3), with 1,281–32,769 input tokens and a 1,024-token output cap. CPU restore phases recorded 56,960 external cache-hit tokens; MTP accepted 1,549 of 1,573 draft tokens. This is correctness validation, not a throughput comparison.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py -q
```

## Details

`BlockTables` tracks potentially dirty shared rows. Gather clears through `max(num_reqs_padded, previous_dirty_rows)`; dummy preparation follows the same rule and tracks rows that profiling may populate. External `out` buffers leave shared tracking unchanged.

Regressions cover real/dummy transitions, shrink/grow/empty batches, independent outputs, and physical KPool slots under eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. PCP has unit coverage; distributed PCP serving was not tested.

The full serving run used sync-check `warn`: strict mode reports a separately reproduced, unchanged SM90 MLA metadata copy. The affected BlockTables methods passed all 17 tests under strict checking.

title: [Core][Refactor] Move KV cache planning logic to kv_cache_planning.py
author: andakai
body:
## Overview

Move the KV cache grouping, sizing, and capacity-planning logic from `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` into a new module, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py`. This is a pure code move with no behavior change.

Split out from #53558 so the large move can be reviewed separately from the pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder` change.

## Claims

- `kv_cache_utils.py` goes from about 2.8k to about 1.2k lines. It keeps the block, hash, and free-queue utilities, plus the helpers that consume a finished `KVCacheConfig`: `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config`, `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config`, `get_kv_cache_capacity`, and `update_kv_cache_capacity`.
- `kv_cache_planning.py` holds the planning path: `get_kv_cache_configs`, `get_kv_cache_groups`, `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`, page-size unification, packed/hybrid grouping, memory and max-model-len estimation, auto-fit, and TP-replica helpers (38 functions).
- Function names and bodies are unchanged. No compatibility re-exports are left in `kv_cache_utils.py`; all in-tree callers are updated.

## Validation

- Every moved function is byte-identical to `origin/main`. This was checked by comparing each top-level definition with the AST. Reviewers can confirm with:
  ```bash
  git diff --color-moved=dimmed-zebra origin/main...HEAD -- vllm/v1/core/
  ```
- `pre-commit` passes (ruff, mypy, typos, and the test-tethering checks).
- Ran the affected unit tests on CPU, on both this branch and `origin/main`. Both give the same result: **294 passed, 19 skipped**.
  ```bash
  pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
    tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \

    tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py \
  ```

- `tests/models/test_initialization.py`, `tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py`, and `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py` import and collect cleanly. They need a GPU, so they are left to CI.

## Details

Besides the move itself, these updates keep behavior and CI coverage the same:

- **Imports:** updated in `v1/engine/core.py`, `v1/hisparse/layout.py`, `v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`, `v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`, and the affected tests.

Out-of-tree code that imports planning functions from `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils` needs to switch to `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning`.

title: [CI][ROCm] Compare greedy output only in the AITER attn+quant test
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Overview

Fixes the intermittent failure in `:amd: (MI355) Fusion and Compile FP8`: [Buildkite #94104](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94104/list?jid=01a12e24-6a90-4b79-b882-a91da3ba7420&tab=output).

```
FAILED tests/compile/correctness_e2e/test_attn_quant.py::test_rocm_aiter_static_attention_output_correctness
AssertionError: Results for model='...Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8' are not the same.

ref_result=    {'test': 'seeded_sampling', 'text': ' Yvonne Cohen and', ...}
compare_result={'test': 'seeded_sampling', 'text': ' Tony and I'm an',  ...}
```

The test was added in [#58099](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58099) and pinned to the v1 model runner from the start. [#61014](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61014) removed that pin as part of the MRV1 cleanup, so it now runs on v2 for the first time.

## Claims

- Only the `seeded_sampling` comparison fails. Every `temperature=0.0` comparison matches, and the unit tests for the same fusion pass with `atol=rtol=1e-2`.
- Fusing output quantization drops a bf16 round-trip, so the two settings agree on the argmax but not on the exact distribution. Sampling at `temperature=1.0` over a 128k vocabulary turns that into a different token.
- The forward pass is bit-identical on v1 and v2, and the fused/unfused gap is the same size on both. What changed is that the v2 sampler draws a different token for seed 33, and that one sits close enough to a boundary to flip. The pin was hiding the problem rather than preventing it.
- This PR compares greedy output only, as [#41102](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41102) already does for the cpu offload test. The five greedy comparisons and the assertion that the fusion fires in all 32 layers are unchanged.

## Measurements

Measured on MI355 by running both settings as servers and asking each the same 100 seeded prompts, plus the top-20 logprobs of the first token:

| compared | seeds that disagree | max abs delta logprob |
|---|---|---|
| unfused vs unfused | 0 / 100 | 0.000000 |
| fused vs fused | 17 / 100 | 0.045204 |
| unfused vs fused | 21 / 100 | 0.158091 |

The unfused path is reproducible across server starts; the fused one is not, so no choice of seed or tolerance makes an exact-equality check on sampled tokens stable here. Greedy output was identical in all of the above.

## Validation

`pytest -v -s tests/compile/correctness_e2e/test_attn_quant.py` on MI355:

- before, on v2: fails with the strings above
- with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`: passes
- after this change, on v2: passes in 115.69 s, with `rewrite counts: [32]`

title: [Bugfix][Watermarking] Skip incomplete opening contexts
author: TQCB
body:
## Overview

Skip watermarking until the response contains a complete generated-token context, across Gumbel and dual-key Gumbel standard and speculative sampling. Follow-up to the shared padded-opening issue discussed in #58426; that PR adds SynthID and leaves this behavior question separate.

## Claims

- The first `context_width` output tokens use ordinary sampling independently of context deduplication, including draft, recovery, and bonus tokens.
- Detection behavior and PRF mappings are preserved.

## Validation

- `../vllm_fork/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/watermarking -q`: 134 passed, 61 accelerator-only tests skipped on macOS.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.
- Rescored all 23 pre-change golden generations with the default detector: scores, p-values, scored-token counts, and decisions match within the existing 1e-9 tolerance.
- GPU engine validation remains pending. Retained model outputs establish detection compatibility only; they do not evaluate generation with this patch.

## Details

Response-local contexts are padded with -1 before enough output tokens exist. With a fixed key, this reuses the same opening watermark randomness across prompts and can reduce opening diversity. The patch combines an incomplete-context mask with the existing sampling masks; it adds no host read or device synchronization. Prompt tokens remain excluded from the seed under every deduplication setting; `all` still searches the prompt for repeated contexts.

Submitted detection text may be a fragment and need not start at the generation boundary, so this PR does not change detector preprocessing or add detector options. On new full responses, the unwatermarked opening positions can dilute the detector signal. Generation can diverge beyond the opening because later tokens depend on earlier choices.

Goldens reflect the new generation behavior. Engine reproducibility tests now pin request seeds because openings use ordinary randomness. The repetitive-fixture confidence guard allows a p-value ratio up to 0.6 rather than 0.5: one updated fixture has ratio 0.514 while remaining below the unchanged detection threshold.

AI assistance: implementation, tests, and this description were prepared with Codex (OpenAI).

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Stage fused KDA decode weights after loading
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

The ROCm Kimi-K3 fused KDA decode read uninitialized memory as its conv1d and gated-norm weights whenever weight loaders were skipped, as with `--load-format dummy`. This intermittently produced NaN logprobs. Those copies are now built from the final parameters after loading.

## Claims

- `process_weights_after_loading` stages `decode_conv1d_weight` and `decode_norm_weight` from `conv1d.weight` and `o_norm.weight`, and the two side-effect weight loaders are removed.
- This fixes the intermittent HTTP 400 (`Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan`) in `test_prefix_cache.py` on MI355.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. In `test_prefix_cache.py[offload-partial]`, NaN runs went from 5 of 21 to 0 of 20. The new `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` fails before (18432/18432 elements are NaN) and passes after. `models/kimi_k3` passes: 311 passed.

The perf runs used `riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy` at TP1, 5 interleaved runs per column, each with a fresh server. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 256 out, conc 16) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 7.687 ± 0.025 | 7.672 ± 0.009 |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 634.4 ± 6.5 | 633.5 ± 2.5 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 5.434 ± 0.004 | 5.454 ± 0.017 |

No real-weight Kimi-K3 checkpoint was available for an accuracy run. With real weights, the buffers receive the same values the loaders wrote before.

## Details

The fp32 copies from #50654 are non-persistent `torch.empty` buffers that were written only inside the conv1d and o_norm weight loaders. `DummyModelLoader` skips both, so the fused decode used whatever the allocator returned: usually zeros, sometimes NaN. That poisoned the recurrent state from the first decode step. The post-load hook runs for every loader, including layerwise reload (the buffer storage is reused, so CUDA graphs stay valid). It skips weights that arrive already processed. The NVIDIA `KimiK3DeltaAttention` has the same latent issue and is left for a follow-up. #59245 reads these buffers and will need a rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Perf] Improve `_topk_topp_kernel()` for masked logits
author: tomasruizt
body:
* **Problem:** the `_topk_topp_kernel()` kernel wastes work searching for a top-k cutoff even when the input logits have less than `k` finite logits (the rest are `-inf`).
* **Solution:** Skip the search when `num_finite_total <= k`, preserving the existing top-p path.
* Does this make sense to the kernel authors & reviewers? @cakeng @njhill 

## Benchmarks

Using the `benchmark_topk_topp.py` script on an H100 80GB. CUPTI, 5 warmups and 20 measured iterations, cold L2, no CUDA graphs, Triton only.

### Table 1: Masked Logits

We observe multi-ms savings for `num_finite_logits <= k`. The runtimes below are a single call to `apply_top_k_top_p_triton()` plus `logits.clone()`, averaged over 20 measurements. All logits are `-inf` except for `num_finite_logits`. The scenario uses bsz=1024 and vocab=131072. This bsz happens e.g. with concurrency=64, DFlash K=15 (64 * 15+1 = 1024). The speedups are probably larger because the timings include cloning a 512 MiB logits tensor (1024 × 131072 × 4 bytes). At peak H100 SXM memory bandwidth, that copy alone takes about 320 µs (read and write).

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Fix MultiConnector stats and proxy SSE responses
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Using direct Mooncake with Mooncake Store can fail in MultiConnector's metrics handler, and the Mooncake example proxy labels SSE responses as JSON, causing clients such as AIPerf to reject them. Fix both integration issues by respecting optional metrics exporters and returning the correct streaming Content-Type.

## Claims

- Skip children without Prometheus exporters while continuing to forward supported metrics and `engine_idx`.
- Return `text/event-stream` for streaming requests on `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`; preserve JSON responses for non-streaming requests and forward response bytes unchanged.

```diff
 P transfer stats -> MultiConnector metrics
-  require an exporter for every child with stats
+  forward stats only to registered exporters

 D SSE frames -> Mooncake proxy -> client
-  Content-Type: application/json
+  Content-Type: text/event-stream
```

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_proxy.py \
  -k 'TestMultiConnectorStats or test_mooncake_proxy' -q
```

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stats-only child, with empty or mixed exporter registry | Both regression cases fail on main `c75cb63cd2bb` | All 17 stats cases pass |
| Real ASGI routes, completion/chat × streaming/non-streaming | 2 streaming cases fail on main `258b97ff6bc1`; 2 non-streaming cases pass | All 4 cases pass |
| Combined PR branch, based on `258b97ff6bc1` | — | **21 passed, 15 deselected** |

The metrics regression also checks that the supported child's payload reaches its exporter with `engine_idx=2`. The proxy regression mocks only the remote P/D calls and checks the actual response headers and bytes. In Buildkite, the V1 KV Connectors step runs the metrics regression. The proxy regression is CPU-only, so it is marked `cpu_test` and runs in the CPU V1 Others step, which also lists the proxy as a source dependency so proxy-only changes still trigger it.

Changed-file pre-commit checks pass:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  .buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml \
  examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_proxy.py
```

Earlier ROCm end-to-end validation used integration commit `b41cf676db9cc124fffbcf305f7fa8c8d2f895b8`, containing the identical proxy file and metrics `observe()` implementation:

- [Before the proxy fix](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38169410559): AIPerf attempted JSON parsing of SSE frames; all 13 sampled warmup responses were rejected.
- [C16 serving](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38174661539): Kimi-K3 + DSpark3, 1P1D/16 MI355X, Mooncake RDMA + TCP Store completed a 3600-second performance window with 2006 successes and 4 errors. The workflow later failed while importing the separate GSM8K evaluator.
- [Natural GSM8K](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38203116096): flexible extraction 1269/1319 (96.21%).

GPU evidence belongs to that integration revision; the current main-based PR branch has local regression coverage. Store lease timeouts and empty-response failures remain separate limitations. No additional GPU experiment was dispatched for this PR.

## Details

**Metrics:** `KVConnectorBase_V1.build_prom_metrics()` may return `None`. MultiConnector's metrics factory already excludes null exporters, while stats collection independently includes stats-only children. Direct Mooncake provides stats without an exporter, so its worker stats trigger the assertion in the API output handler. A conditional exporter lookup follows the existing optional-interface contract. Stats collection is unchanged; missing exporter IDs are skipped, so this assertion no longer detects inconsistent IDs in the metrics path.

**HTTP:** `_handle_completions` already forwards the request's streaming mode to D. Use the same flag to select the response media type. KV transfer and generation logic are unchanged.

The metrics portion follows up the **same fix proposed in #43836 for #43828**, adapted to the current flat stats payload with regression coverage. That PR remains open; this is not a distinct solution. The submitting operator explicitly requested including it here to cover both direct-Mooncake integration failures. Searches found no overlapping proxy SSE-header fix.

Both changes are reversible and scoped to metrics forwarding and the example proxy. AI assistance (Codex) was used; this remains a draft submitted at the human operator's request.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] V2 rejection sampler: return logprob_token_ids scores
author: SCcagg5
body:
## Overview

With the V2 model runner and speculative decoding, a request that sets `logprob_token_ids` (and no `logprobs`) gets no logprobs back whenever another request in the same batch has draft tokens. `RejectionSampler` only looked at `max_num_logprobs`, so `logprob_token_ids` was dropped on that path. The regular V2 `Sampler` already handles it through `get_logprobs_dims`.

`/v1/systemone` reads are such requests (`max_tokens=1`, `logprob_token_ids`): next to a streaming chat on an MTP model, every read failed with `HTTP 400: No logprobs available for item 0`. This passes the per-request token ids to `compute_topk_scores` in the rejection sampler. Related: #42592 / #44727 (the same kind of mixed batch, on the V1 sampler, a different file).

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-27B with MTP 3, 6 `/v1/systemone` calls (4 questions, 2k-token state) while 4 chat streams run: 6/6 fail before, 6/6 succeed after.
- Chat is not affected: time to first token 0.52 → 0.60 s and inter-chunk latency p50 191 → 192 ms with and without systemone on the engine.
- The returned probabilities are not changed by the chat load: mean absolute difference 0.007 (max 0.041) between a cold call and the same call next to chat, the same as between a cold call and the same call repeated alone on a cached state (0.007, max 0.039).
- Batches without `logprob_token_ids` are unchanged (`compute_topk_scores` takes its fast path when `max_token_ids == 0`); without speculative decoding this code path is not used.

## Validation

Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit with MTP 3 on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev273` (`2eb491e18b`), V2 model runner, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --logprobs-mode raw_logprobs`, `--max-num-seqs 8`. The same change was applied to the nightly's copy of the file for the runs. Chat: 4 closed-loop streaming requests (256 tokens).

| | systemone alone | systemone + 4 chats, main | systemone + 4 chats, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| errors | 0 / 6 | 6 / 6 (HTTP 400, no logprobs) | 0 / 6 |
| chat errors | | 0 | 0 |

After the review changes the run was repeated (mixed: 0 errors, cold vs next-to-chat mean absolute difference 0.004, max 0.033). The same server also runs `/v1/systemone` accuracy (120 synthetic tickets: 0.90 / 0.67 / 1.00, unchanged) and the question-count cases (6.4 / 8.2 / 11.9 / 28.7 s for 1 / 4 / 16 / 64 questions, unchanged) with the change applied. MTP off, on main: no errors (no drafts, so the batch does not go through the rejection sampler); not re-run with the change.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py
```

31 passed with the change. New tests in `test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py` build a real `LogprobTokenIdsState` and check the returned ids and scores against `log_softmax` / the raw logits for every row:
- `test_logprob_token_ids_without_topk_logprobs`: token ids only, raw and logits modes, and nothing is computed when none are requested;
- `test_logprob_token_ids_with_topk_logprobs`: top-k `logprobs=1` narrower than the widest `logprob_token_ids`, requests with and without ids;
- `test_logprob_token_ids_with_adaptive_verification`: one chunk over compacted logits, device `cu_num_logits` and a host-side upper bound, same result as the fixed-boundary layout;
- `test_get_logprobs_dims_with_only_token_ids`.

`test_gather_sampler_output_logprobs_and_nans` is parametrized over top-k only, token ids only and token ids wider than top-k. The CUDA tests of these files are skipped on ROCm by `current_platform.is_cuda()`; I ran them locally with that check replaced by `torch.cuda.is_available()`. The new tests fail on main. The `model_runner.py` call site of the sharded gather (TP > 1) has no test and was not run.

## Details

- `RejectionSampler.__call__` calls `Sampler.get_logprobs_dims` once and passes `logprobs_dims` to `_verify_in_chunks` and `_get_logprobs_tensors`, which also takes the chunk's `expanded_idx_mapping` (`compute_topk_scores` needs it to map each logits row to its request).
- `Sampler.get_logprobs_dims` no longer has `include_token_ids`: the sharded gather in `model_runner.py` sizes its buffers with the token-id columns for batches with draft tokens too.
- Not covered: DSpark and the other speculators were not run; they go through the same `RejectionSampler.__call__`.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Reduce residency hash probes
author: Etelis
body:
Related to #60072.

At top-k 2,048, the resolver can fill 2,048 of its 2,049 hash slots. Looking up cached rows that aren't selected for the current step then requires long probe chains.

This lets the table grow toward the existing four-slots-per-position target, within the device's shared-memory budget.

Default shared memory rises from 26,148 to 75,300 bytes per block. Resident-only calls cost an extra 0.16–0.90 µs in the kernel checks. This is separate from #60103's slot-invalidation and all-resident work.

On **4 H200s, TP4, GLM-5.2-NVFP4**, with 32 concurrent requests, 16,384-token random prompts and 1,024-token outputs, median throughput improved **130.26 → 133.45 tok/s (+2.45%)**. Three runs each ranged from 130.21–130.32 and 133.36–133.69 tok/s. Reverting gave 130.01 tok/s.

This used FP8 KV, 10 GiB GPU KV per rank, a 64 GiB host pool, CUDA graphs, and no prefix caching. The serving comparison predates the rebase (`d61081dc` → `94b81a59`) and used targeted native builds with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Post-rebase serving, speculative serving, and other GPU architectures haven't been benchmarked.

On the final commit, `b605dfa0`:

- **1 H100 80GB:** 106 focused tests and 4 end-to-end tests passed with MRV2 and GPU sync checking enabled.
- **1 H200:** 18 resolver cases matched baseline indices, ownership, and LRU state. The 4× target beat 2× in every host-backed case tested.
- Pre-commit passed.

The earlier serving run also passed 12 cache-state comparisons and four short output checks. No full model-quality evaluation was run.

## Overview

Serve the MTP layers of any model that opts into the Transformers MTP standard (huggingface/transformers#46229) as a speculative decoding draft in the Transformers modeling backend.

Draft: depends on huggingface/transformers#49544, which adds the `MtpModel` helpers this uses (`forward_layer`, `get_mtp_weights_regex`, `get_weight_conversions`) so vLLM shares the per-layer logic and weight loading with Transformers instead of duplicating them. The minimum version is set to 5.20.0, assuming that PR lands in it.

## Claims

- `--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", ...}'` works for targets on the Transformers backend whose config sets `num_mtp_layers` (`TransformersForMTP` / `TransformersMoEForMTP`)
- MTP weights are found and renamed by the same `MtpModel` helpers as `MtpModel.from_pretrained`, so new checkpoint layouts only need the Transformers-side mapping
- Multi-module MTP: `spec_step_idx` selects the MTP layer, so `num_speculative_tokens > 1` uses every checkpoint layer
- Covers DeepSeek-V3/R1 and GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7 today, and Mellum with huggingface/transformers#49531

title: [Quantization] Auto-disable DeepGEMM for Kolibri 1 on SM12x
author: lucamotz
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Auto-disable DeepGEMM for Kolibri 1 on SM12x, next to the existing Qwen3.5 exclusions, and apply the exclusions to automatic FP8 MoE backend selection. Follow-up to #60827; 

## Claims

- On B200, Kolibri 1 FP8 is faster at the defaults than with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`., no claimed accuracy issues could be found
- On SM12x, FP8 MoE layers of excluded models select Triton instead of DeepGEMM. SM90 and SM100 selection is unchanged.
- On DGX Spark, Kolibri 1 and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8 now run as fast at the defaults as with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, with GSM8K unchanged.

## Validation

Kolibri 1 FP8 on B200, TP=1, nightly `253e02b95e` + #60827 (identical to main `0838cd6593` in all files this PR or kernel selection touches). Two runs per arm, interleaved; latency uses 512 input / 256 output tokens, throughput 256 requests of 1024 / 256 after a full-batch warmup.

| Kolibri on SM100 | Dense / MoE | Batch 1, s | Batch 32, s | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Not excluded (main, this PR) | DeepGEMM / TRTLLM | 1.295 | 2.208 | 5562 |
| Excluded | CUTLASS / TRTLLM | 1.487 | 2.409 | 5014 |

The excluded arm selects the same kernels as `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, so Kolibri is listed for SM12x only.

DGX Spark (GB10), TP=1, main `61d9c777bf` (Kolibri + #60827), same timing protocol, one run per arm:

| GB10 | Dense / MoE | Batch 1, s | Batch 32, s | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kolibri 1, main | DeepGEMM / DeepGEMM | 6.258 | 37.782 | 213 |
| Kolibri 1, this PR | CUTLASS / Triton | 5.567 | 27.063 | 248 |
| Kolibri 1, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | CUTLASS / Triton | 5.518 | 27.243 | 247 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, main | CUTLASS / DeepGEMM | 5.631 | 32.574 | 411 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, this PR | CUTLASS / Triton | 5.067 | 23.049 | 494 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | CUTLASS / Triton | 5.012 | 22.601 | 499 |

GSM8K (all 1319 questions; `tests/evals/gsm8k` 5-shot, plus sampled zero-shot chat), paired by question: this PR vs main and vs `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` is unchanged for both models (every 95% CI includes 0). The Qwen3.5 exclusion is still needed: with the list emptied, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8 drops from 79.4% to 71.0% on the 5-shot eval (95% CI −10.5 to −6.2 pt), below its CI threshold of 0.76.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and results</summary>

Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy, passed.

Per-run B200 results (batch 1 / batch 32 s, output tok/s): main 1.257 / 2.184 / 5707 and 1.333 / 2.232 / 5417; excluded 1.491 / 2.417 / 5062 and 1.483 / 2.400 / 4967.

GB10 build: main's Python tree on the aarch64 nightly wheel `0fae39a014` (`0fae39a0..61d9c777` is Python-only), torch 2.13.0, flashinfer-python 0.7.0.post1. Repeat runs of the `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` arms: timing within 2.1% (Kolibri) and 0.6% (Qwen3.5); Kolibri 5-shot outputs identical.

| GSM8K, % | main | this PR | `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | list emptied |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Kolibri 1, 5-shot | 85.97 | 86.28 | 86.13 | |
| Kolibri 1, chat | 92.68 | 92.97 | 92.70 | |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 5-shot | 78.92 | 79.91 | 79.42 | 71.04 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, chat | 95.53 | 95.28 | 95.17 | 95.09 |

</details>

## Details

The exclusions only reached the dense DeepGEMM kernel; `select_fp8_moe_backend` checked only the environment variables. On SM12x, block-FP8 MoE has no TRTLLM or FlashInfer CUTLASS backend, so DeepGEMM was selected. With E8M0, `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts` then runs DeepGEMM for every shape, including the N ≤ 512 experts it otherwise leaves to Triton; Kolibri 1 and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B both use 512. On SM100 these models select TRTLLM ahead of DeepGEMM, so only the dense kernel is affected there.

Kolibri's entry is for latency, so the warning no longer cites accuracy. An explicit `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1` still selects DeepGEMM for MoE.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER tuned configs to select a4w4 gemm kernel instead of env var
author: afriedri
body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` is currently used to select the weight layout (preshuffled vs plain) for every layer. With preshuffled layout, ASM gemm is used for prefill and preshuffled Triton gemm for decode. 

In previous PRs, attempted to remove the environment variable altogether and default to on, but caused regressions because various models (Kimi, DS) do not have tuned preshuffled Triton decode kernels. Ideally we would like to have this active for the models that it helps (Llama, mostly) without the environment variable. 

This PR removes the environment variable and decides per layer at weight-load time. A layer takes the preshuffled (ASM) layout only when aiter has tuned configs for both the ASM and Triton preshuffled kernels. 

## Testing

### Unit tests

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py
59 passed
```

### Serving setup

MI350X ×8, fresh server per arm, two restarts per arm. "Before" is `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=0` on main.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve $MODEL -tp $TP --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 16384 --load-format dummy

vllm bench serve --model $MODEL --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
```

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Start async lookup when a request arrives via on_new_request
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Overview

Start MooncakeStore's async prefix lookup from `on_new_request()`, when the scheduler adds a request, so the lookup can finish while the request waits in the scheduler's waiting queue. GPU KV allocation and transfer stay in the scheduler's existing path.

This uses the existing connector hook `KVConnectorBase_V1.on_new_request(request)`. An earlier revision added a new hook that ran on the input thread. That needed a handle handoff to stay lock-free, and it bought little: the engine core thread and the input thread share the GIL, so the only thing the lookup needs to overlap is GPU execution. `on_new_request` runs on the engine core thread, so all lookup state stays on one thread and needs no locking.

`on_new_request` runs when the core thread handles the ADD:

- Today, that is in `_process_input_queue` between engine steps. With async scheduling (the default with the mp executor), the next batch is already running on the GPU at that point.
- With #65466, ADDs are handled while the core thread waits for a step's output, so the lookup starts up to one step earlier.

## Design

- `MooncakeStoreConnector.on_new_request` calls `MooncakeStoreConnectorScheduler.start_lookup_prefetch`. That calls `LookupKeyClient.prefetch()`, which submits the lookup to the existing single lookup executor and registers it in `_lookups`. The ZMQ socket is still used only by the executor thread.
- The scheduler's first `get_num_new_matched_tokens` probe goes through the existing `lookup()`, which reuses the registered lookup instead of submitting a second RPC.
- A completed async result is cached per request and reused by later probes until it is discarded or expires. Before this PR, the first read popped it.
- The lookup is discarded in `update_state_after_alloc` (consumed; a reschedule after a failed load looks up again), in `request_finished` / `request_finished_all_groups`, on preemption in `build_connector_meta`, and on `reset()` and `close()`.
- Requests with `skip_reading_external_kv`, prompts shorter than the lookup alignment, or no block hashes are not prefetched.

## Claims

- With `lookup_async=True`, `enable_lookup=True`, and a positive `lookup_prefetch_limit`, eligible requests submit their lookup when they are added. Off by default.
- `lookup_prefetch_limit` caps arrival-time lookups in flight. A slot is released when the RPC completes or is cancelled. Over the cap, the request is looked up when the scheduler first reaches it. Scheduler lookups are not capped.
- Arrival-time lookups create no `LoadSpec` or GPU allocation. The scheduler still computes the external tokens to load from its current local-prefix hit count.
- A completed async result older than `lookup_prefetch_ttl_s` (default 2 s, measured from when its RPC returned) is looked up again. So is a lookup whose token count or block-hash chain changed. A lookup still in flight never expires, so it is not resubmitted behind the backlog it is waiting on.
- `MultiConnector` already forwards `on_new_request`, so this also works when MooncakeStore is wrapped in one.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py -q
```

**141 passed** (Linux aarch64, Python 3.12, at 86cc07f53). New and updated cases cover:

- a lookup started by `on_new_request` and reused by the scheduler's probes with a single RPC, then dropped once allocated
- the in-flight cap, including slot release on completion and scheduler lookups bypassing the cap
- refreshing on a changed token count or hash chain, or an expired result, and not restarting a lookup that is still in flight
- skipping ineligible requests
- a finished request's queued lookup being cancelled before it runs, and discarding on preemption, reset and close

Not run: GPU serving, real Mooncake transfers, model evaluation, TTFT/throughput benchmarks.

## Trade-offs

- An earlier lookup adds backend work for requests that later abort or hit entirely in the local cache, and the single lookup worker can queue that work ahead of later requests. The cap bounds this.
- The TTL can cause a second lookup after a long queue wait.
- Both defaults need measurement on real workloads.
- Cancelling a queued future works; an RPC that is already running cannot be interrupted.

Duplicate-work checks: searched open vllm-project/vllm PRs for Mooncake lookup, async/prefetch lookup, and `on_new_request` lookup. #48230 skips lookups for locally reused prefixes, which is a different change. #42321 (enqueue-time prefetch for `LMCacheMPConnector` via `on_new_request`) is the same idea for another connector; it was closed for inactivity, not rejected.

title: [MoE] Shape-based padding for FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP8 experts (gated and non-gated)
author: jhaotingc
body:
## Overview

The FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP8 MoE kernel needs `intermediate % 128 == 0` and `hidden % 256 == 0`; otherwise it fails with `No valid config found`. This PR pads MXFP8 experts by shape on that backend, for gated and non-gated experts alike, so MXFP8-MoE checkpoints with misaligned expert sizes can run.

## Claims

- MXFP8 MoE layers with misaligned intermediate or hidden sizes now run on `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM`, gated or not.
- Aligned models are unchanged: no copy and no runtime padding.
- A W4A4 checkpoint with an MXFP8 MoE that this enables reaches **1.71×** the output tok/s/GPU of the BF16 model on GB300 at concurrency 64.

## Validation

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py -k mxfp8` gives 14 passed on B200. That is the new test (gated SiLU and non-gated ReLU², aligned and misaligned shapes such as 1856×2688, against `fused_experts` on the dequantized weights) plus the 4 existing MXFP8 TRT-LLM tests.

```bash
vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"moe_backend":"flashinfer_trtllm"}' \
  --mamba-cache-mode none --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
  --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 --use-replayssm \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":32768}'
```

- Accuracy (GB300): GPQA-diamond through NeMo Gym on 1x GB300, TP1, MTP=2 (198 questions x 8 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95), served as above plus
  `--max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3`. pass@1 (mean over the 8 repeats ±
  standard error) is 76.45 ± 0.70% without prefix reuse and 76.58 ± 0.45% with prefix reuse
  (`--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, no ReplaySSM).
- Perf (GB300, TP1, speed-bench 1k prompts / OSL 200, no spec decode, same serve flags otherwise, concurrency 64): the W4A4 + MXFP8-MoE checkpoint reaches **9,640 output tok/s/GPU** (189.6 tok/s/user) vs BF16 5,648 (101.2), i.e. 1.71× throughput and 1.87× per user.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including mypy.

## Details

- New `align_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_fi_trtllm`, next to `align_moe_weights_for_fi`:
  - It reuses `align_moe_weights_for_fi` for the intermediate size, padding gate and up halves separately.
  - It pads the hidden size with zero weights, and pads the UE8M0 scales the same way with 127 (scale 1.0).
- `prepare_fp8_moe_layer_for_fi` calls it on the MXFP8 TRT-LLM path and sets `intermediate_size_per_partition` and `hidden_dim` at the call site. The MoE runner then pads the activations to the padded hidden size and crops the output.
- The test uses `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsMonolithic`. `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular` (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`) never passes `activation_type`, so it always runs the kernel gated.

title: [Bugfix] Merge supported KV cache layouts across pipeline stages instead of asserting they match
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview With pipeline parallelism, a model whose stages use different attention backends fails at startup. `resolve_kv_cache_layout` asserts that every worker reports the same list of supported KV cache layouts, but PP stages hold different layers, so their lists can differ. This PR makes the engine core merge the worker lists with the same rule `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` already uses for the backends of one worker. This addresses failure 1 ("PP2 on SM100") of #60791. Failures 2-5 in that issue are not touched here. ## Claims - `vllm serve` of a 10-layer MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 with `--pipeline-parallel-size 2` on B200 now starts, picks `LBHNC`, and answers requests. Before, it died in `_initialize_kv_caches` with `AssertionError: Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts`. - When all workers report the same list (one GPU, TP only, PP with equal stages), the result is the same as before. - If no layout is supported by every worker, the existing `ValueError` is still raised. - New unit test `test_pipeline_stages_resolve_a_layout_every_stage_supports`. It fails on the old code with the bug's assertion. ## Validation Hardware: 2 x NVIDIA B200 (SM100, x86_64). The issue was reported on GB200 (aarch64), which has the same SM. Software: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev173+g8cbd5d030` (commit `8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986`), with and without this patch. Attention backend chosen: FLASHINFER. Model: the issue's 10-layer cut of `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` is not published, so I rebuilt it from the Hub checkpoint (revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`) with the script below. Layers 0-2 are dense and layers 3-9 are sparse. I cannot show it is tensor-identical to the reporter's cut.
cut script (replace $HF_HOME with your Hugging Face cache path) ```python # Cut MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 to its first 10 decoder layers (+ vision tower), as the report describes. import json, re, glob, os, shutil, sys from safetensors import safe_open from safetensors.torch import save_file src = glob.glob("$HF_HOME/hub/models--MiniMaxAI--MiniMax-M3-MXFP8/snapshots/*")[0] dst = "/tmp/m3-10layer" os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True) N = 10 for f in os.listdir(src): if f.endswith(".safetensors") or f == "model.safetensors.index.json": continue shutil.copy(os.path.realpath(os.path.join(src, f)), os.path.join(dst, f)) def trunc(o): if isinstance(o, dict): return {k: trunc(v) for k, v in o.items()} if isinstance(o, list) and len(o) == 60 and all(isinstance(x, int) for x in o): return o[:N] return o cfg = json.load(open(os.path.join(dst, "config.json"))) cfg["text_config"] = trunc(cfg["text_config"]); cfg["text_config"]["num_hidden_layers"] = N q = cfg["quantization_config"] q["ignored_layers"] = [x for x in q["ignored_layers"] if not (m := re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.", x)) or int(m.group(1)) < N] json.dump(cfg, open(os.path.join(dst, "config.json"), "w"), indent=2) wm = {} for shard in sorted(glob.glob(src + "/*.safetensors")): out = {} with safe_open(shard, "pt") as f: for k in f.keys(): m = re.search(r"language_model\.model\.layers\.(\d+)\.", k) if m and int(m.group(1)) >= N: continue out[k] = f.get_tensor(k) name = os.path.basename(shard) save_file(out, os.path.join(dst, name), metadata={"format": "pt"}) for k in out: wm[k] = name print(name, len(out), flush=True) json.dump({"metadata": {}, "weight_map": wm}, open(os.path.join(dst, "model.safetensors.index.json"), "w")) ```
Reproducer. It fails at startup, so no request is needed to see the bug: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \ vllm serve /tmp/m3-10layer --trust-remote-code --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \ --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --enable-prefix-caching --pipeline-parallel-size 2 ``` Before: 4 of 4 runs failed like this, about 160 s after start. 3 runs used the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986` image and 1 used a source install. One more source run never got this far, because of a file permission problem in my setup, so it is not counted. ``` AssertionError: Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts: [['LBHNC', 'BLHNC'], ['LBNHC', 'LBHNC', 'BLNHC', 'BLHNC', 'BHLNC', 'LHBNC']]. ``` After: 5 of 5 runs started and answered one request with HTTP 200. 3 of the runs used the final code (the last one was run by a separate reviewer) and 2 used an earlier version of the patch. ``` Using LBHNC KV cache layout. INFO: Application startup complete. "POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` The request was `curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -d '{"model":"/tmp/m3-10layer","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":8,"temperature":0}'`. The returned text is junk, which is expected from a 10-layer cut of a much deeper model. I did not run an accuracy eval. Startup takes more than 10 minutes, mostly for FlashInfer autotuning of the MXFP8 MoE kernels. Unit tests (run with `--noconftest`, because my environment had no `tblib`, which `tests/conftest.py` imports): - `pytest --noconftest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k pipeline_stages`: passes with this patch. With the old `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` it fails with the same `Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts` assertion. - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py`: 197 passed, 76 skipped. The 8 errors are tests that need the `caplog_vllm` fixture from `tests/conftest.py`. The 2 failures are PP tests that need 4 GPUs (`World size (4) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`). They fail the same way on the old code with 1 GPU, and they pass with 4 GPUs visible. - `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks pass. ## Details Root cause: each worker reports the layouts that all of its own attention backends support (`WorkerBase.get_supported_kv_cache_layouts`). `resolve_kv_cache_layout` then asserted that all reports are equal, because "all ranks run the same backends". With PP, each stage builds only its own layers. For this model with PP2: - PP0 holds layers 0-4. Layers 0-2 use FlashInfer, which supports only `(LBHNC, BLHNC)` on SM100, so PP0 reports `['LBHNC', 'BLHNC']`. - PP1 holds layers 5-9, which are all sparse. `MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE` and `MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE_INDEXER` declare no layout set, so PP1 reports the default list of six layouts. The two lists differ, but they share `LBHNC` and `BLHNC`. With PP=1 the model works, because one worker sees all backends and intersects their sets. A debug run that printed each stage's backends confirmed this. Fix: the merge code in `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` moves into a helper, `_merge_supported_layouts`, and `resolve_kv_cache_layout` now uses the helper on the worker reports. - Identical lists keep their order, so setups where all workers agree are unchanged. - Otherwise, the candidates are the layouts that appear in every list, and the layout that the most lists put first wins. - A worker that reports the default list (no backend declares a set) does not vote, in the same way that a backend that declares nothing does not vote inside one worker. Without this rule, an all-sparse stage would vote for `LBNHC`, and PP could pick a different layout from PP=1. The second case of the new test covers this. - If no layout is in every list, the code still raises `ValueError: No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set`. Tradeoff: the removed assertion also caught TP ranks of one stage that report different lists, for example after one rank picked a different backend by mistake. Those lists are now merged like PP stages. The chosen layout is still one that every worker supports. A per-stage check could be added back, but the engine core would then need to know which worker is in which stage, and this fix does not need that. Limitations: only failure 1 of the issue is fixed. Validation used B200 with FLASHINFER and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, not GB200. ---

title: [Benchmark] Add vllm bench forward: exact-shape forward timing
author: WoosukKwon
body:
> Commits: *[Benchmark] Add vllm bench forward*, the *model-microbenchmark* agent skill, and *Support DCP*. No changes to the model runner or model code.

## Overview

Add `vllm bench forward`: time the model forward of an **exact** batch (prefill, chunked prefill, prefix hit, decode, spec-decode verify, or any mix), built without the scheduler and run through the real `execute_model`, captured as a one-shot CUDA graph. Works single-GPU and with DP/TP/EP/DCP across nodes via `torchrun`.

```bash
vllm bench forward --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --case decode=64*1@8192 --case prefill=8192 --case mix=4096,32*1@8192
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model ... -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --shapes shapes.json
```

## Claims

- Exact shapes: requests are `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]` (query length, KV length including the query, draft tokens). A prefill's prefix is a prefix-cache hit (SWA bounded replay on DeepSeek-V4.1) unless `c` marks a chunked prefill. Every run checks that the runner built exactly that batch.
- Accurate GPU time: one-shot FULL graph even for prefill (host-side plans are correct by construction, since the graph only replays the batch it captured). Rendezvous and timing events live inside the graph, so rank skew and launch gaps are excluded; each replay is reduced with MAX over ranks; per-replay jitter is reported (sample spread) and flagged above 0.5%.
- Realistic defaults for dummy weights: KV lengths vary +-50% (same on every DP rank, `--kv-len-jitter`); MoE routing is balanced per EP rank (`--routing auto`), replacing the degenerate routing of dummy gates.
- Matches independent references (below).

## Validation

GB200. CLI and unit tests (Benchmarks CLI job runs `tests/benchmarks/`):

```
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py   # 3 passed
```

Against serving (decode, same model/config, `vllm bench latency` per-step time from 65- vs 1-token runs, FULL decode graph):

| Model | bench forward | serving step | gap (sampler, LM head, step overhead) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 32 x 4K context | 3.48 ms | 3.69 ms | 0.21 ms |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (43 layers, 1 GPU), 32 x 4K | 7.94 ms | 8.93 ms | 0.99 ms |

Against a standalone DeepSeek-V4.1 forward harness (recorded Sept 16; same shapes and config: DEP4, MegaMoE, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV; ~100K KV, decode):

| batch | harness | bench forward |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 6.39 ms | 6.31 ms |
| 8 | 9.97 ms | 9.85 ms |
| 32 | 15.77 ms | 15.58 ms |
| 128 | 20.07 ms | 19.97 ms |

DCP: Kimi-K3 (9 layers, MLA) TP4 with DCP1 vs DCP4 on decode, chunked prefill and prefix hit: the runner builds the expected batches, DCP4 allocates the scheduler's block count (`block_size * dcp` tokens per block for DCP-sharded specs), and replays are deterministic.

Also run: DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 DEP4 (1 node) and DEP8 (2 nodes, MNNVL), TEP4, prefix hits, verify. Median run-to-run reproducibility within ~0.3%; sample spread mostly 0.01-0.4% (higher on V4.1 DEP prefill, from MegaMoE cross-rank sync and host engram reads).

## Details

- **Flow per case:** build `SchedulerOutput` (disjoint block IDs across KV groups) -> zero the case's KV blocks -> `execute_model` twice: eager warmup (JIT, autotune), then capture/validate/time. For those two steps the bench shadows `runner.prepare_inputs` (to check the batch the runner built) and `model.forward` (to take over the eager model call) with instance attributes, then deletes them; the runner itself is unchanged. Requests are re-added on the second call; `sample_tokens` is never called, so the pending step state is dropped.
- **State restore:** the KV blocks a step writes are snapshotted and restored inside the graph before each replay, so in-place state (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1's compressor) is identical across replays.
- **KV init:** zeros only for now (`--kv-init zeros`). Random KV was measured within 3% on DeepSeek-V4.1 at ~100K context, so its per-layout model code isn't worth it yet.
- **Routing:** forward hooks on `GateLinear` replace gate logits with a balanced fixture; this covers backends that route from logits, including monolithic FlashInfer TRTLLM (verified on Kimi-K3) and modular (verified on DeepSeek-V4: router top-k equals the fixture). Models that compute top-k themselves (e.g. MegaMoE's fused gate on DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 and Kimi-K3) instead get the fixture's `topk_ids` through a forward pre-hook on any experts module whose `forward` takes `topk_ids`; on DeepSeek-V4.1 DEP4 this matches the earlier model-local override within run-to-run noise (+0.05% to +0.8%). Grouped top-k is rejected; layers the fixture can't reach fail loudly.
- **Model code:** none.
- **Dependencies / limitations:**
  - Dummy-loaded DeepSeek-V4.1 loses MegaMoE shared-expert fusion (fixed by #60096); the bench's dummy loader finalizes early as a temporary workaround (TODO to remove).
  - Data-dependent kernels need realistic activations: #61323 keeps dummy norms neutral (e.g. V4.1 sparse top-k 27.8 ms -> 10.7 ms, real weights 10.6 ms).
  - The batch builder mirrors scheduler semantics (block counts, prefix-hit replay); the unit test and the per-run layout check guard against drift.
  - Model branches on `is_current_stream_capturing()` (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 short-context top-k, V4.1 mHC overlap) make small batches' graph output differ slightly from eager; reported, not asserted.
- **Agent skill:** `.agents/skills/model-microbenchmark` documents usage and pitfalls (dummy-weight artifacts, torch.compile models, timing spread) for agents.
- **Size:** ~1,050 non-test lines, isolated under `vllm/benchmarks/forward/` plus the CLI entry, docs and agent skill.

title: [Tests][Mamba] Wait for accepted counts in fake MTP proposer
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Overview

Fix `test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1` / `_mrv1_async`, failing on `main` since #61134 on H200 MIG and MI250 (e.g. [main build #94362](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94362#01a1333b-d247-49be-b767-84df48ec72c7)): `ValueError: Mamba state is not equal for key: 576 at index 0`. Test-only change.

## Claims

- The test's fake MTP proposer read `num_accepted_tokens_cpu` before the same-step non-blocking D2H copy finished, so a GPU lagging behind the host fed off-by-one draft tokens. It now waits on `num_accepted_tokens_event` first.
- No runner change: the real proposer uses GPU tensors, and the runner already synchronizes that event in `_prepare_inputs` before reading the CPU counts.

## Validation

The failure does not reproduce on GB200 as-is (fast GPU hides the race), so I injected GPU lag with a `sitecustomize.py` that runs `torch.cuda._sleep(20_000_000)` (~10 ms) at the start of every `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`:

| GB200, `-k test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1*` | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no injected lag | pass | pass |
| injected GPU lag, sync | **fail** (`key: 576 at index 0`, same as CI) | pass |
| injected GPU lag, async | — | pass |

```bash
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py -k "test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1" -s
```

`pre-commit` passes.

## Details

- In `accept_2_1`, the mismatching conv state at token 576 differed only in row 0 (the token carried over from the previous step); rows 1-2, computed in the current step, matched the reference bit-exactly. That row was produced from a wrong draft token: the fake proposer computed its offset from a stale `num_accepted_tokens_cpu` (still the value written before `postprocess_mamba_align_gpu`'s non-blocking D2H landed).
- Why now: before #61134, FP8 dummy weights were ±1e-3 (mostly rounded to 0 in E4M3), so conv states were ~0 regardless of the input token and the comparison passed vacuously. With ±1 FP8 dummy weights the states are meaningful, and slow CI GPUs (16-SM H200 MIG slice, MI250) expose the race. `main` passed this test at c6566bb9f6 and fails from the next build onward; the other commits in that window only touch DSv4.1/ROCm or Intel CI yaml.
- Related but distinct: #51571 (row-ownership race of the same CPU tensor under async scheduling, fixed in the runner by #51599/#53919). This PR touches neither; the test runs a single request and fails without async scheduling too.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`.

title: [Perf] per_token_group_quant_8bit: multiply by reciprocal instead of dividing per element
author: gau-nernst
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Speed up FP8 per-token-group quantization by computing the per-group scale reciprocal once and multiplying, instead of dividing per element. This covers both CUDA group-quant kernels: `per_token_group_quant_8bit` (smem and register-resident schedules) and the fused RMSNorm+group-quant kernel (`layernorm_utils.cuh`), so that all CUDA fp8 group-quant paths share the same reciprocal-multiply numerics. ~1.2-1.3x kernel speedup on GB300 across M=1..32768; ~1-2% e2e TPOT improvement on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (TP4).

## Claims

- 1.15-1.29x faster `per_token_group_fp8_quant` CUDA kernel on GB300 across M=1..32768 (details below).
- All CUDA fp8 group-quant paths (unfused kernel, fused RMSNorm+quant kernel, Triton fallback, UE8M0 path) now use the same reciprocal-multiply numerics; previously the fused and unfused kernels could disagree by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements.
- ~0.6-2.0% e2e TPOT improvement on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, 8k input / 1k output, at concurrency 1-64.
- Accuracy-neutral: GSM8K / GPQA-Diamond deltas within noise (details below).

## Validation

### Correctness

- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py`: 848 passed, including `test_per_token_group_quant_fp8_register_matches_smem` (bitwise register-vs-smem equality; both schedules are changed identically, so the invariant is preserved).
- Scale outputs are bit-identical to main; quantized values can differ by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements (randn data) when a quotient lands within 1 fp32 ulp of an fp8 rounding boundary.

### Microbenchmarks

GB300, K=4096, group=128, bf16 -> fp8e4m3 + fp32 scales. FlashInfer CUPTI with CUDA graph and cold L2; median of interleaved rounds. Both columns are standalone same-toolchain builds (nvcc 13.1) of the register-resident kernel; repro harness: `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_per_token_group_quant.py`.

| M | main (us) | this PR (us) | speedup | achieved BW (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 2.30 | 1.92 | 1.20x | 6 GB/s |
| 4 | 2.34 | 1.92 | 1.22x | 26 GB/s |
| 16 | 2.56 | 2.14 | 1.20x | 93 GB/s |
| 64 | 2.69 | 2.27 | 1.19x | 350 GB/s |
| 256 | 3.20 | 2.78 | 1.15x | 1.14 TB/s |
| 1024 | 6.14 | 5.02 | 1.22x | 2.53 TB/s |
| 4096 | 15.23 | 12.19 | 1.25x | 4.17 TB/s |
| 16384 | 52.35 | 41.09 | 1.27x | 4.95 TB/s |
| 32768 | 101.25 | 78.34 | 1.29x | 5.19 TB/s |

The kernel is memory-bound (~2 FLOPs/element; TFLOPS is not the meaningful metric here). This PR lifts achieved bandwidth from 4.0 to 5.2 TB/s at M=32768. A flat-index Triton variant we prototyped reaches 6.7 TB/s at M=32768 but loses at small M; modifying the existing CUDA kernel is the lower-risk change.

### E2E perf

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, 8k input / 1k output, vllm bench serve; median TPOT. main (`c077dc663d`) and the branch (`1aca0a263f`) ran sequentially on the same GB300 node:

| Concurrency | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.27 | 6.23 | -0.6% |
| 4 | 8.30 | 8.14 | -1.9% |
| 16 | 12.06 | 11.82 | -2.0% |
| 64 | 24.98 | 24.67 | -1.2% |

Request throughput +1.2% at concurrency 64. Note: the e2e delta includes a toolchain effect (branch built from source with local nvcc 13.1; baseline is the nvcc 13.0 wheel, whose stock quant kernel is mis-scheduled -- see Details), so it mildly overstates the pure source-change effect. The same-toolchain kernel numbers above are the honest claim.

### Accuracy

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, identical server flags on the same GB300 node:

| Task | main | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K flexible-extract (n=1319) | 0.8211 | 0.8112 | -0.99pp |
| GSM8K strict-match (n=1319) | 0.8158 | 0.7991 | -1.67pp |
| GPQA-Diamond (n=198) | 0.8586 | 0.8687 | +1.01pp |

Mixed and within noise (binomial std error ~1.06pp per arm at n=1319), but GSM8K drifts down directionally; consistent with the ~0.05% of elements whose fp8 rounding flips under reciprocal-multiply.

## Details

- Root cause: `div.rn.f32` is a multi-instruction slow sequence, and the kernel issued it once per *element* when one division per *group* suffices. The kernel's own UE8M0 path already uses reciprocal-multiply (a power-of-two scale makes the reciprocal exact); this PR applies the same transform to the fp32-scale path.
- The per-element division was inherited from the SGLang kernel this file was ported from (#21083); the register-resident path (#55330) kept it so the new schedule stayed bit-exact with the smem one. That invariant is a test convenience, not an accuracy requirement, and is preserved by changing both schedules identically.
- Numerics: this is the same rcp-mul numerics class already shipped by this kernel's UE8M0 path, vLLM's Triton fallback (`_per_token_group_quant_fp8`), and SGLang's production quant kernel.
- Scope: no Python/dispatch changes. The file is also hipified into ROCm builds; the change uses only portable float ops, so ROCm gets the same numerics (not separately benchmarked there).
- Related work: #60903 adds a separate Triton row kernel for prefill-sized inputs (large M only); this PR instead speeds up the existing CUDA kernel at all M and is complementary. No open PR duplicates this change.
- Consistency: the fused RMSNorm+group-quant kernel (`layernorm_utils.cuh`, the target of `RMSNormQuantFusionPass` for block-FP8 models, on both CUDA and ROCm via hipify) is switched to the same reciprocal-multiply. Without this, fused and unfused paths diverge by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements (caught by `test_fused_quant_layernorm` and `test_mamba_prefix_cache`). The fused kernel also drops 4 div.rn per vec4. Per-token fp8 keeps exact per-element division for FBGemm parity; int8 paths are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Toolchain note: nvcc 13.0 x sm_100 mis-schedules the stock kernel</summary>

All official artifacts (release pipeline nvcc 13.0.2, Dockerfile CUDA_VERSION=13.0.3) target `... 10.0 ...` (no sm_103). nvcc 13.0 targeting sm_100 mis-schedules this kernel's div.rn slow paths: 864 instructions / 3095 static stall cycles vs 568 / 1655 under nvcc 13.1; the shipped wheel runs the stock kernel at 167.6us vs 101.2us for a 13.1 rebuild at M=32768 (sm_100 SASS loads natively on sm_103; verified with CUDA_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1). This PR's variant is insensitive to the compiler (78.3us on nvcc 13.0 vs 78.1us on 13.1) because it removes the per-element div.rn entirely. Worth a separate build-toolchain discussion; out of scope here.
</details>

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Require explicit MXFP4 opt-in for MegaMoE shared-expert fusion
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #61004. Fusing DeepSeek-V4's shared expert into AITER MegaMoE requantizes it from FP8 to MXFP4. With this PR, that requires an explicit opt-in through the online quantization API instead of a dedicated env var, and it goes through the shared fused-shared-expert (FSE) helpers.

## Claims

- Removes `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`. Under `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`, the existing `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` requests the fusion.
- The shared expert is fused only when it is explicitly requantized to MXFP4:
  ```bash
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe ... \
      --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_experts*": "mxfp4"}'
  ```
  Without that target, a warning is logged and the shared expert stays unfused in checkpoint precision (FP8).
- No model-specific logic:
  - The decision goes through `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert` / `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible`, which now take a `moe_backend` argument.
  - The requantization reuses `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` and the `ONLINE_SHARED_EXPERT_QUANTIZERS` from #55686.
- Kernel, routing and performance are unchanged from #61004.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X, DEP4, `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`. GSM8K: lm-eval, 5-shot.

| `--quantization-config.targets` | Shared expert | GSM8K (strict) |
|---|---|--:|
| `{"*shared_experts*": "mxfp4"}` | fused, MXFP4 | 0.9469 ± 0.006 |
| none | unfused, FP8 + warning | 0.9545 ± 0.006 |

```
INFO  Quantizing 122 layers of types: ffn.shared_experts.down_proj: 61 (from targets: *shared_experts*, mxfp4); ffn.shared_experts.gate_up_proj: 61 (...)
WARNING  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS is enabled but cannot be enabled - skipping for this layer: AITER MegaMoE fuses the shared experts only when --quantization-config.targets requantizes them to MXFP4.
```

Unit tests:
- `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` covers `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` with the MegaMoE backend.
- `tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py::test_online_mxfp4_shared_expert_rejects_quark_weight_only_mxfp4_fse` keeps Quark weight-only routed experts incompatible with an `mxfp4` shared-expert target.

## Details

- **Activation key.** MegaMoE (a8w4) quantizes every slot's activations to MXFP8 itself. A `"mxfp4"` target cannot express "MXFP4 weights, MXFP8 activations", so for MegaMoE only the weight key is compared. Other backends still compare both keys: Quark weight-only routed experts have no activation key (BF16 activations), which an `mxfp4` target does not match.
- **Why the shared expert is not built with `Mxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`:**
  - `Fp8LinearMethod` has no `dequantize_weight`, so it can't serve as the source for requantization.
  - `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` pre-shuffles the weights into a layout MegaMoEV2 can't use.

  Instead, the fused shared expert keeps the checkpoint quant config, minus online quantization. MegaMoE then dequantizes it with `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` and quantizes it with the registered quantizer.
- **Config class.** On CUDA and ROCm, `deepseek_v4_fp8` resolves to the v4.1 `DeepseekV4FP8Config`, so the check accepts both the v4 and v4.1 classes.
- **Breaking:** `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`, added in #61004 and present in v0.32.0rc0–rc2, is removed without a deprecation period. Setting it afterwards triggers vLLM's "Unknown vLLM environment variable" warning (an error with `--fail-on-environ-validation`), and the shared expert stays unfused in FP8. If preferred, I can keep it as a deprecated no-op with a warning for one release instead.
- **Out of scope:** making MegaMoE a generic MoE backend in the oracle.
