title: [Model] Enable torch.compile and CUDA graphs for EmbeddingGemma2
author: Vivaansharma2003
body:
## Overview

Enable `torch.compile` and CUDA graphs for EmbeddingGemma2 by adding `@support_torch_compile` to `EmbeddingGemma2TextModel`, the same way `Gemma3Model`, `Gemma4Model` and `BertModel` are compiled. This compiles the text backbone only; the multimodal encoders are untouched, and the encoder `TODO(lucianomartins)` from #60254 stays.

## Claims

- EmbeddingGemma2 now runs with piecewise compilation and CUDA graphs instead of eagerly.
- Single-query latency drops from 49.8 ms to 10.6 ms on A100-80GB (4.7x) and from 48.8 ms to 15.5 ms on L40S (3.1x); batch throughput rises 61% and 21%.
- Embeddings are unchanged: cosine similarity to sentence-transformers is 0.9998 at minimum before and after.

## Validation

Same vLLM build on both sides: nightly image `cu134-nightly-5555a2d` (its `embedding_gemma2.py` is identical to main), with and without this file. Model `google/embeddinggemma-2`, bf16, `--runner pooling`, `max_model_len=8192`, multimodal limits set to 0. Offline `LLM.embed`, 86 real queries (~20 tokens) and 1,495 document chunks from a RAG corpus, after 20 warm-up calls.

| GPU | | one query p50 / p95 (ms) | throughput (chunks/s) | cos vs sentence-transformers (min / mean) | engine startup (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A100-80GB | before | 49.75 / 52.50 | 333.8 | 0.99959 / 0.99993 | 57.9 |
| A100-80GB | **after** | **10.57 / 12.85** | **537.6** | 0.99982 / 0.99993 | 138.4 |
| L40S* | before | 48.77 / 56.24 | 382.5 | 0.99970 / 0.99993 | 48.7 |
| L40S* | **after** | **15.54 / 17.75** | **464.7** | 0.99978 / 0.99993 | 159.9 |

\* L40S has 99 KiB of opt-in shared memory per block, so EmbeddingGemma2 cannot start on it today (#60847). Both L40S rows include the tile fix from #60848, which is independent of this change.

Existing tests, A100-80GB, before and after:

```
EG2_MODEL_PATH=google/embeddinggemma-2 pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py
```

On the unmodified build (A100-80GB): 18 passed, 3 skipped (media assets not in the repo), 2 failed: `test_instance_attribute_access` and `test_video_loader_real_video`. Both fail without this change, so they are pre-existing in that environment. A run on the patched build was started and stopped early to save GPU time; text parity on the patched build is covered by the table above (cosine >= 0.9998 against sentence-transformers, above the test's 0.999 threshold). These tests need `EG2_MODEL_PATH` and are skipped in CI.

## Details

Root cause: `EmbeddingGemma2TextModel` was never decorated, so the model provides no compiled submodule and vLLM logs `Cudagraph mode PIECEWISE requires piecewise capture, but the loaded model provides neither a compiled submodule nor breakable CUDA graphs. Overriding to NONE.` A torch.profiler trace of one ~20-token query (transformers, L40S) shows why that matters for this model: 2,453 CUDA kernels per forward (24 layers with per-layer embeddings, q/k/v norms and two attention head sizes), with the GPU busy for 4.8 ms of a 49 ms forward. The same forward captured as a CUDA graph takes 5.6 ms. The model is launch-bound, not compute-bound.

The text backbone's `forward(input_ids, positions, inputs_embeds)` takes only model-runner tensors and has no data-dependent control flow, so the default decorator applies as is. The vision, audio and video towers stay eager and outside the compiled region. Compiling them or capturing them as encoder CUDA graphs (`compile_mm_encoder` / `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph`, as `gemma4_mm.py` does) is the separate encoder TODO, not part of this change.

Tradeoffs: engine startup grows by about 80-110 s for compilation and graph capture (first start; the compile cache shortens later starts), plus the memory for captured graphs. `--enforce-eager` restores the previous behaviour.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds compilation for this model (searched `EmbeddingGemma2` and `embedding_gemma2` in PRs). #60848 and #60942 fix the separate shared-memory crash on 99 KiB GPUs.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Mask grammar-invalid implicit reasoning ends
author: vMaroon
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With an engine-based reasoning parser, a structured-output request fails with "grammar rejected tokens" and HTTP 500 when the model samples an implicit reasoning end, such as GLM's `<tool_call>`, that the request's grammar cannot start with. Reasoning rows of the bitmask are unconstrained, so the token can be sampled, and since #59627 it is fed to the grammar. This masks those tokens while the request reasons. Implicit ends the grammar accepts stay allowed.

Related: #60722 (RFC; this is the "remaining issue" it describes, using its first option restricted to grammar-rejected tokens), #59627 (feeds the implicit end to the grammar), #59608 (`required`/named tool calls, which must keep `<tool_call>` allowed), #61456 (open; also edits `_fill_bitmasks`).

## Claims

- A request whose grammar rejects an implicit reasoning end as its first token (a JSON schema, `tool_choice="none"` with `response_format`) can no longer sample that token while reasoning, so it no longer ends in "grammar rejected tokens".
- Requests whose grammar accepts the implicit end are unchanged: `tool_choice` `required`, named, and `auto` with tools (with or without `response_format`).
- The explicit end (`</think>`) and every other token stay allowed while reasoning. Draft and bonus rows under speculative decoding are masked the same way.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, xgrammar and guidance:

```text
python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py
# main source + these tests: 181 passed, 8 failed, 1 xfailed
# this branch:               189 passed, 1 xfailed
```

The 8 that fail on main: `test_real_flow[implicit_end_rejected-*]` (pattern `RRUUU`; main gives `UUUUU`), `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[json-*]`, `test_parallel_fill_masks_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[*]`, and the two `TestReasoningEndTokenIds` cases for the new property. `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[regex_starts_with_marker-*]` passes on both: a grammar that starts with the marker keeps it allowed and consumes it.

Wider run on this branch: `tests/v1/structured_output`, `tests/parser` (without `tests/parser/cohere`, which needs `cohere_melody`), `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py`: 6636 passed, 1 xfailed. `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`: 19 passed on both. `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: the same 48 multimodal tests fail on main and on this branch, because this kernel-less install cannot inspect the Llava architecture.

**Real components, no model.** GLM-5.3 tokenizer, `--reasoning-parser glm45` (`Glm47MoeParserReasoningAdapter`), xgrammar, prompt ending in `<think>`. Bitmask rows while reasoning, then `accept_tokens([<tool_call>])` as the scheduler would call it:

| constraint | main: `<tool_call>` allowed / masked bits | this branch | `accept_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON schema, no spec | yes / 0 | no / 1 (`<tool_call>` only; `</think>` allowed) | False |
| JSON schema, 3 draft rows + bonus | yes / 0 in all 4 rows | no / 1 in all 4 rows | False |
| `required` structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |
| named structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |

**End to end, CPU server.** arm64 CPU image of main `206e45d47`, whose four changed files are identical to `a2fb48273`, with the structured-output backends from `a2fb48273` mounted in both arms and this branch's four files in the second. A 2-layer Llama with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer and vocabulary, `--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, xgrammar, greedy, 3 runs per case. `logit_bias` makes `<tool_call>` (154843) the top token.

| request | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` | 500 x3, "grammar rejected tokens [154843]" | 200 x3, no `<tool_call>` in reasoning |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"`, same bias | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` 100, `</think>` 50, answer tokens 30 | 500 x3 | 200 x3, `{"answer": "yes"}`, finish `stop` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="auto"`, same bias | 200 x3, tool call | 200 x3, same tool call |
| `tool_choice="required"` / named / `auto` without `response_format` | 200 x3 each, tool call | 200 x3 each, same tool call |
| `json_schema`, no bias | 200 x3 | 200 x3 |

Every request that returns 200 on main returns the same response on this branch. The engine log on main has one `Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843]` per 500 (12 of 12); the branch logs have none.

<details>
<summary>Raw request and responses (third row)</summary>

```json
{"model": "glm-tiny", "max_tokens": 96, "temperature": 0,
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Is the sky blue? Reply as JSON."}],
 "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "a", "schema": {
   "type": "object", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}},
   "required": ["answer"], "additionalProperties": false}}},
 "logit_bias": {"154843": 100, "154842": 50, "4913": 30, "9214": 30, "788": 30, "330": 30,
                "9689": 30, "9204": 30, "154820": 30}}
```

main, 3 of 3:

```text
HTTP 500 {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}
(EngineCore pid=131) ERROR 10-14 06:31:44 [scheduler.py:2189] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843] for request chatcmpl-8bf78d42551e682d-8a4ad66a. Terminating request.
```

this branch, 3 of 3 (fields from the response):

```text
HTTP 200  finish_reason=stop  reasoning="" (no <tool_call>)  content={"answer": "yes"}  tool_calls=[]
```
</details>

**Speculative decoding, end to end.** `logit_bias` is rejected with speculative decoding, so these runs use fixed weights instead: layer outputs are zero and the LM head prefers `<tool_call>`, then ` the`, at every position. ngram, 3 speculative tokens, `json_schema`, 96 tokens:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema` | 500 x3 | 200 x3, 96 reasoning tokens, all ` the` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"` | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| drafts accepted (`json_schema` only) | | 207 of 225 |
| `required`, `auto` + tools | tool calls | same tool calls |

Each accepted draft position used a masked row; an unmasked draft row would have sampled `<tool_call>` and failed the request.

<details>
<summary>CPU harness note</summary>

On main the CPU stand-in `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl` (`vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py`) takes its arguments in an order that no longer matches `ComputeSlotMappingKernel.kernel`, so the dispatcher passes `slot_mapping` as `block_size` and the first forward fails. These runs mount a copy of that one function, with the kernel's parameter names, in both arms. Separate from this change.
</details>

**GPU, end to end.** @simon-veitner-redhat ran main `a2fb482732` against this branch `6d144d6478` on H200 ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61574#issuecomment-6163972357)): GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, `glm47` tool and reasoning parsers, xgrammar, 8 seeds per row. "Tagged" means a tool result in the conversation quotes GLM's own tags (`<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<arg_value>`), followed by a `json_schema` request.

| request, no spec decode | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 7/8 500s, 0/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 4/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 5/8 500s, 3/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 7/8 valid JSON |
| `logit_bias` forcing `<tool_call>`, blocking `</think>` | 8/8 500s | 0 500s, empty content |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

| request, MTP 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, async scheduling | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 6/8 500s, 2/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 6/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 2/8 500s, 6/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 8/8 valid JSON |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

Main logs one `Failed to advance FSM` per 500; this branch logs none. The remaining invalid JSON on this branch is a separate frontend issue: the token stream is valid JSON, but the model quotes `<tool_call>` inside a JSON string and `content` is cut there. The CPU runs above use the V1 model runner, so both runners are covered.

**Motivation.** A GLM-5.3 deployment (MTP with 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, xgrammar, `glm45`) logged 649 "grammar rejected tokens" terminations in 8 hours; 625 of them ended on `<tool_call>` (154843). A non-streaming request terminated this way returns HTTP 500.

## Details

Path of the failure, `enable_in_reasoning=False`:

1. A request with a JSON schema is reasoning. `_get_constraint_bounds` puts `constraint_start` past every scheduled row, so `grammar_bitmask` fills each row with the full mask.
2. The model samples `<tool_call>`, which `Glm47MoeParser` treats as an implicit reasoning end: it ends reasoning and starts a tool call.
3. `accept_tokens` finds that end and, since #59627, sets `grammar_start` to its offset, so `<tool_call>` is fed to the grammar. A JSON grammar rejects it and `accept_tokens` returns False.
4. The scheduler logs "Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens" and finishes the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`.

The change, in `StructuredOutputManager`:

- `ParserEngine.implicit_reasoning_end_token_ids`: reasoning-end tokens other than the explicit end, the same split `find_reasoning_end` uses to report an implicit end. Exposed through `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter`. This only adds a read-only property, so no parser changes behavior.
- `_masked_reasoning_ends`: the implicit ends the grammar rejects as its first token (`validate_tokens([t])`, non-mutating in every backend). The grammar does not advance before reasoning ends, so the set is computed once per request and cached on `StructuredOutputRequest`.
- `_fill_bitmasks`: a row the grammar does not constrain allows every token except those ids. Only rows before `constraint_start` (including the bonus row while reasoning) get them, in both the serial and the parallel fill. Constrained rows and rows after padding are unchanged.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- This changes the reasoning distribution only by removing tokens whose sampling makes the output invalid under the request's own constraint. The model keeps reasoning or ends with the explicit end. The alternative outcome is an error, so there is no flag.
- Same scope as #59627: engine-based parsers and single-token implicit ends. Multi-token or text-only ends (`deepseek_v4`, `inkling`) are not covered.
- Cost: one `validate_tokens` call per implicit end per request, and a bit clear per masked id on reasoning rows. No device work and no host sync.
- #61456 replaces the guidance path of `_fill_bitmasks` with a batch fill. Whichever lands second has to keep the reasoning-row mask.

title: [Core][Spec Decode] Lookahead block hashes for EAGLE prefix caching
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Overview

Part 1 of 2 split from vllm-project/vllm#50897 (implements vllm-project/vllm#50438): **lookahead block hashes** for the local prefix cache. EAGLE, EAGLE3 and MTP drafters write the draft KV at a block's last position from the token after the block, so `main` drops the last matched block on every hit. This PR puts that token into the block hash and removes the drop when no KV connector is configured. KV connector support is in the stacked PR (part 2).

## Claims

- Local prefix-cache hits with EAGLE, EAGLE3 and MTP reach `floor((N - 1) / B) * B`, the same as without speculative decoding, instead of one cache unit less (544–1600 tokens on hybrid attention + Mamba/GDN models). Multi-module MTP with k modules reaches `floor((N - k) / B) * B`.
- A block is reused only when its lookahead token matches, so a hit reads the same draft KV as a cold run.
- New `SpeculativeConfig.disable_lookahead_block_hashes` restores `main`'s behavior. With any KV connector configured, this PR keeps the legacy hashes.
- KV events publish the lookahead token in a new `BlockStored.lookahead_token_ids` field, so consumers can reproduce the hashes.
- Model runners are unchanged; no new CPU/GPU synchronization.

## Validation

Unit tests on this branch (one GB200 node):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \
  tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  --ignore tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py -k "not ray"
```

Result: 1,256 passed. `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` is excluded because it launches the `vllm` CLI (see the TODO below).

Hash format CPU cost: one `request_block_hasher` call over a whole prompt, SHA-256, one pinned GB200 Grace core, median of 15 alternating-order rounds of 5 calls. Token IDs are random, and the prompt length is aligned + 1 so every format emits the same hashes; MM rows add a 512-token image every 1,024 tokens. Each variant is the real hasher with only its lookahead branch replaced; an unmodified copy run the same way stays within 0.2% of the real one. Percentages are versus `main`.

- nested: `H((parent, tokens[s:e], (E(s, e), tokens[e], E(e, e + 1))))`, the previous revision of this PR
- expanded window: `H((parent, tokens[s:e + 1], E(s, e + 1)))`
- this PR: `H((parent, tokens[s:e], (E(s, e + 1), tokens[e])))`

| Input | Prompt tokens | B | main | nested | expanded window | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| text | 32K+1 | 16 | 3.166 ms | 4.107 ms (+29.7%) | 3.394 ms (+7.2%) | 3.566 ms (+12.6%) |
| text | 32K+1 | 128 | 0.917 ms | 1.033 ms (+12.6%) | 0.940 ms (+2.5%) | 0.963 ms (+5.0%) |
| text | 32K+1 | 1024 | 0.636 ms | 0.647 ms (+1.7%) | 0.635 ms (-0.2%) | 0.639 ms (+0.5%) |
| text | 128K+1 | 16 | 13.007 ms | 16.770 ms (+28.9%) | 13.945 ms (+7.2%) | 14.406 ms (+10.8%) |
| text | 128K+1 | 128 | 3.805 ms | 4.248 ms (+11.6%) | 3.907 ms (+2.7%) | 3.967 ms (+4.3%) |
| text | 128K+1 | 1024 | 2.705 ms | 2.786 ms (+3.0%) | 2.717 ms (+0.4%) | 2.746 ms (+1.5%) |
| MM | 32K+1 | 16 | 3.777 ms | 5.126 ms (+35.7%) | 4.104 ms (+8.7%) | 4.271 ms (+13.1%) |
| MM | 32K+1 | 128 | 1.013 ms | 1.194 ms (+17.9%) | 1.065 ms (+5.1%) | 1.087 ms (+7.3%) |
| MM | 32K+1 | 1024 | 0.654 ms | 0.675 ms (+3.2%) | 0.658 ms (+0.6%) | 0.660 ms (+0.9%) |

One `E` call instead of two saves 7–17% at B ≤ 128 versus the nested form. The expanded window is cheapest, but its hash input equals a legacy hash with block size `B + 1`; keeping `tokens[e]` in the extra keys costs 3–5% more than it at B = 16 and at most 2.5% at B ≥ 128. With one lookahead token the hasher indexes `tokens[e]` instead of slicing, which builds the same tuple; the slice cost about 7 more points at B = 16.

End-to-end and draft-KV results from the combined PR (vllm-project/vllm#50897, earlier revision; not yet re-run on this split):

| Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, MTP k=4, 1x GB200, `prefix_repetition` | `main` | lookahead hashes |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix-cache hit rate | 72.7% | **85.0%** |
| Request throughput | 9.09 req/s | **12.43 req/s** |
| Mean / median TTFT | 404 / 304 ms | **318 / 226 ms** |
| GSM8K 5-shot | 0.4359 | 0.4359 |

Hit length, Qwen3.5-2B + MTP k=1, unit 544, 1,367-token prompt sent twice: `main` without spec decode 1088, `main` with MTP 544, lookahead hashes 1088.

Draft-KV check (KV of the hit blocks vs a cold run, bf16 max abs diff): Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 0.09–0.14 (negative control with a stale lookahead token: 7.55); Qwen3.5-2B MTP 0.19 (control: 14.53).

TODO before review: re-run `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`, `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` and the benchmark on GPU.

## Details

**Enablement.** `get_num_hash_lookahead_tokens` (`v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`) returns `L = num_prefill_lookahead_tokens` (1, or k for multi-module MTP with k modules) when `use_eagle_block_drop()`, `not disable_lookahead_block_hashes`, prefix caching is on and there is no KV transfer config; otherwise 0, which keeps the legacy hashes and the block drop. DFlash and DSpark build draft KV from target hidden states alone; vllm-project/vllm#54163 removes them from `use_eagle_block_drop()`, after which they keep the legacy hashes with no drop. Until then they get lookahead hashes too, which is correct but unnecessary. `num_hash_lookahead_tokens` replaces the former boolean flag through the KV cache manager, coordinator, block pool and scheduler. Part 2 replaces the last condition with a per-connector capability.

**Hashing.** `get_request_block_hasher(..., num_hash_lookahead_tokens=L)` hashes a block `[s, e)` only once tokens up to `e + L - 1` are in `all_token_ids`, as `H((parent, tokens[s:e], (E(s, e + L), *tokens[e:e + L])))`; for `L = 1` that is `(E(s, e + 1), tokens[e])`. `E` is `generate_block_hash_extra_keys` over the block and its lookahead tokens, called once per block, so MM inputs or prompt embeddings there are covered too; the MM cursor then steps back to the first input the next block overlaps. The hashed tokens stay the block's tokens, and the `(E, token)` shape keeps these hashes apart from legacy ones; hashing `tokens[s:e + L]` instead would equal a legacy hash with block size `B + L`. Different `L` give different tuple lengths. All KV cache groups share these hashes.

**KV events.** `BlockStored.lookahead_token_ids` holds `tokens[e:e + L]` per block, and `extra_keys` keeps its untagged per-block shape but covers `[s, e + L)`. A block hash is reproducible from `token_ids`, `extra_keys` and `lookahead_token_ids` (`test_kv_events_reconstruct_lookahead_block_hashes`). Consumers that ignore the new field still decode events, but blocks with the same tokens at the same position can now carry different hashes, so routers that index one hash per position need to key on the lookahead tokens. The extra field widens the msgpack map header of every `BlockStored` (fixmap to map16); decoded contents are unchanged. `examples/features/kv_events/kv_events_subscriber.py` includes the field.

**Caching.** Blocks are cached at allocation, as without lookahead hashes; `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.cache_blocks` stops at the last hashed block. At request finish, `update_from_output` caches the block whose lookahead the last sampled token completes.

**Drop removal.** The scheduler clears `use_eagle_block_drop`. `KVCacheCoordinator.drop_eagle_group_ids` is empty in this mode and drives the per-group drop and `replay_boundaries`, so the last-block drop, the Mamba checkpoint back-off and the replay-boundary shift are all skipped from one place. `eagle_group_ids` stays, since `mamba_shared_prefix_checkpoint` still applies.

**Docs.** A new "Prefix caching" section in `docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md` covers the default, `disable_lookahead_block_hashes` and `BlockStored.lookahead_token_ids`.

**Why it is correct.** The drafter writes the draft KV at `e - 1` (input `(h_{e-1}, token e)`) in the step that prefills or samples token `e`. The hash exists only once token `e` is in `all_token_ids`, which never holds draft or in-flight tokens, so a cached block's draft KV is written by the end of that step. With k-module MTP, module j writes its KV at `p` from token `p + j`, so the hash waits for tokens up to `e + k - 1`. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` re-prefills a slot written from a rejected draft in the step that samples its replacement, and the coordinator already keeps the last `k - 1` computed tokens out of the cache.

**Limitations**

- Multi-module MTP lookahead hashes are covered by unit tests only; the draft-KV check against a cold run has not been run for them yet.
- HiSparse requires `HiSparseConnector`, so like other connectors it keeps the legacy hashes and the block drop. Its host tier publishes pages once their host copies finish; whether those copies include the last position's draft KV needs GPU validation before part 2 lets `HiSparseConnector` opt in.
- Streaming-input sessions are not supported. When a turn ends on a lookahead boundary, the block cached with the discarded sampled token keeps that hash (its draft KV was written from that token), so later blocks of the session are unreachable by prefix lookups from other requests.
- Hybrid models lose the hit when a prompt diverges exactly at the producer's last retained Mamba boundary (0 vs one unit on `main`); see vllm-project/vllm#50897 for the reproducer.

<details><summary>Duplicate-work check</summary>

Split from vllm-project/vllm#50897 by the same author. No other open PR adds the successor token to the prefix-cache key (vllm-project/vllm#44986, vllm-project/vllm#45614, vllm-project/vllm#48375 and vllm-project/vllm#39171 change when the drop applies, not the key).

</details>

title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Internal prefill checkpoints for the PLE short conv
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #60050. Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) has a second Mamba layer, the PLE short conv, that could not export internal prefill checkpoints. Since the scheduler takes them only when every Mamba layer can, Qwen4Exp prefills kept splitting at the prompt's last cacheable block boundary. The PLE layer now exports its conv window at the checkpoint, so a Qwen4Exp prefill that crosses that boundary runs in one step, like Qwen3.5 does since #60050.

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP (3 tokens), 1x GB200 node, 8000-token prompts, against main `ec317a4`: mean TTFT −17% / −17% / −23% at concurrency 1 / 4 / 16, median −18% / −20% / −21%. TPOT drops 2–9%; GSM8K is unchanged.
- Only active where #60050's checkpoints are (FlashInfer GDN prefill, prefix caching on). Elsewhere every spec, block size and kernel is unchanged; ROCm's PLE layer is a separate class and is untouched.

## Validation

Setup: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, `-tp 4 -ep --enable-prefix-caching --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'`, MRV2, every arm on the same GB200 node.

**TTFT** (`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 8000 in / 1000 out, `--ignore-eos`, 16 prompts per unit of concurrency, seed `100 + concurrency`; one run per arm):

| Concurrency | main `ec317a4` mean / median | this PR mean / median | Δ mean | TPOT main → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 274.8 / 275.0 ms | 227.0 / 224.5 ms | −17% | 2.72 → 2.67 ms |
| 4 | 341.0 / 319.0 ms | 281.8 / 254.8 ms | −17% | 3.97 → 3.62 ms |
| 16 | 438.1 / 324.2 ms | 337.3 / 255.1 ms | −23% | 7.87 → 7.16 ms |

- Main splits an 8000-token prompt at 7200 + 800 tokens (block 800). This PR runs it in one step: a torch profile shows a single `execute_context_1(8000)` step (126 ms), and `store_cache_checkpoints_kernel` runs 37 times per prefill (36 GDN layers + the PLE layer).
- TPOT drops at concurrency 4 and 16, not 1: decoding requests share a step with each new prompt's prefill and wait for it. Main makes them wait for two steps per prompt (the 800-token one is ~45 ms), this PR for one. At 16, each request sees about 16 prefills while decoding 1000 tokens, so ~45 ms × 16 / 1000 ≈ 0.7 ms per token, close to the measured 0.71 ms.
- The 64-token checkpoint grid moves the block from 800 to 832 tokens (KV cache memory 124.01 vs 124.03 GiB), as it does for Qwen3.5 since #60050.

**GSM8K** (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --max-tokens 1024`, 20-shot, 1319 questions):

| main `ec317a4` | this PR |
|---|---|
| 0.9651 | 0.9606 |

Other main runs of this eval on the same node scored 0.9629 and 0.9583, so the difference is within run-to-run noise.

- The shared 20-shot prefix makes 60% of prompt tokens prefix hits (main: 77%), so requests resume from the exported checkpoints. MTP mean acceptance length is 3.49 on both arms.
- The hit rates differ because of the block size, not the export: these prompts are 4122–4287 tokens with a 4087-token shared prefix, just under 5 × 832, so with MTP's dropped block they hit at 3 × 832 − 832 = 2496 here and at 5 × 800 − 800 = 3200 on main.
- Raw-completion GSM8K is not used: this model ends few-shot completions immediately on every arm.
- Under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, 300 GSM8K questions (0.9833) and 64 8000-token prompts at concurrency 4 completed without a sync violation.

**Tests** (GB200):

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py                        # 117 passed, 2 skipped (new export test x4)
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_checkpoint_exporter.py           # 12 passed (new)
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py        # 5 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py           # 62 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_checkpoint_state.py        # 14 passed
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py \
       tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py
                                                                 # 160 passed, 35 skipped (AMD-only)
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "block_size or checkpoint_grid"   # 14 passed
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py::test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async_flashinfer \
       tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py::test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async   # 2 passed
```

- `test_prefill_exports_conv_window_at_checkpoint` runs the PLE layer's dispatch on a batch of decodes and two prefills that checkpoint mid-query, alone and mixed with spec-decode rows (whose prefill tokens the kernels reach through the non-spec token map), in both conv-state layouts. Each checkpoint must equal the state `ple_conv` leaves after a prefill stopped at its offset, and nothing else in the cache may change, including the checkpoint block's speculative columns.
- `test_checkpoint_exporter.py` calls the shared exporter the way each of its callers does (GDN with FlashInfer's row map into an FP32 SSM cache as on Qwen3.5 and Qwen4Exp, or a BF16 one as on Qwen3-Next; Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash FlashKDA; Kimi-K3 ROCm conv-only; Qwen4Exp PLE with a token map), in both conv-state layouts, against a PyTorch reference, and checks that nothing else in either cache changes. It needs only Triton, so it runs on every GPU in the Mamba Kernels job whenever the exporter changes. Breaking the token map fails only the PLE cases; ignoring the row map fails only the GDN ones.
- The Qwen4Exp and GLM5Next CI jobs now also run when the shared exporter (`layers/mamba/checkpoint.py`) changes. Before, an exporter change ran only the GDN tests in CI.

## Details

- **PLE layer.** `get_prefill_checkpoint_alignment()` returns 1 in align mode: the conv window ending at any offset of at least `(kernel - 1) * dilation` (9 tokens here) is a copy of the inputs before it. When every Mamba layer can checkpoint, the PLE spec reserves a checkpoint block on the same grid as GDN, and the prefill path exports each window with `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter(state_len=(kernel - 1) * dilation)`. Under sequence parallelism the conv input is all-gathered before the conv, so the export sees every token.
- **PLE metadata builder.** Builds `MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata` over the non-spec rows in both of its paths (decodes then prefills, or the non-spec rows of a mixed spec batch).
- **One grid for every Mamba spec.** The scheduler checks offsets against one alignment (the first Mamba group's), so GDN's checkpoint grid moves to `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_grid` in `layers/mamba/abstract.py` and both specs use it: the prefix-cache grid made a multiple of the model's checkpoint alignment.
- **Exporter.** The recurrent half of `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter.export` is now optional, and an optional `token_indices` maps the rows' tokens to their rows of the input. Existing callers pass the same keyword arguments as before.

**Tradeoffs.**

- The block is 4% coarser (800 → 832), so prefix hits land on a coarser grid. How much that costs depends on where prompts end relative to block boundaries; the GSM8K run above is an unlucky case (60% vs 77% hit rate) that still keeps its accuracy.
- Validated on SM100 (GB200) only, like #60050.
- The exporter's new conv-only and token-map variants compile on the first checkpointed step, like the GDN one does since #60050: its strides depend on the allocated KV cache.

**Related / not a duplicate.** No open PR adds internal checkpoints for the PLE short conv (searched 2026-10-14).

- #60050 (merged) added internal checkpoints for the FlashInfer GDN prefill and aligns blocks only when every Mamba layer can checkpoint.
- #60861 (draft) fixes where the PLE short conv reads and writes its state in align mode when a KV connector loads a prefix hit. It touches the same two files (`ple_layer.py`, `short_conv_attn.py`) but not the scheduler's internal checkpoints; whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- #61454 (open) cleans up the HC and PLE implementations; the overlap is mechanical.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Update FlashKDA pin, consume row-strided QKV directly
author: qianlihuang
body:
## Overview GLM-5.3-Flash prefill hands FlashKDA packed Q/K/V views (`3 * H * D` token stride, contiguous H/D rows), and `_flashkda_prefill` copied them into three contiguous buffers because the kernel required dense inputs. FlashKDA #15 (vllm-project/FlashKDA#15) accepts row-strided Q/K/V, so this PR pins that revision and passes the views directly. This is the consumer-side alternative to producing dense QKV in the convolution itself. ## Claims - Removes the three per-layer Q/K/V copies from GLM-5.3-Flash prefill; profiles show 4 -> 1 copy kernels (the remaining one is the beta transpose). - Serial A/B/A on H200, ISL2048/OSL1: saturated prefill throughput **21.37 -> 21.78 req/s (+1.9%)**, median TTFT **-2.1%**. - GSM8K is unchanged within sampling noise: 0.9163 (A1) / 0.9125 (candidate) / 0.9170 (A2), i.e. 1204 / 1199 / 1205 of 1314 questions. ## Validation Environment: 4 x H200, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 checkpoint, BF16 KDA projections, serial A/B/A on the same host. Server: ```sh vllm serve --served-model-name glm53flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Client (three runs per arm at each rate, 256 prompts per run): ```sh vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8234 \ --model --served-model-name glm53flash --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos \ --request-rate <20|inf> --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 256 --seed <101+> ``` | Arm | rate=inf (req/s) | rate=20 (req/s) | median TTFT (ms) | GSM8K | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A1 base | 21.37 / 21.46 / 21.38 (mean 21.40) | 16.69 / 18.51 / 18.63 | 1456.9 | 0.9163 | | B candidate | 21.72 / 21.77 / 21.86 (mean 21.78) | 18.81 / 18.41 / 18.91 | 1425.5 | 0.9125 | | A2 base | 21.35 / 21.27 / 21.40 (mean 21.34) | 18.72 / 18.12 / 19.17 | 1456.6 | 0.9170 | At 20 req/s the arms overlap; the first A1 repetition is a cold run and the bracketing A2 matches the candidate. GSM8K is 5-shot, greedy, 1314 questions: the two baselines answer 1204 and 1205 correctly (0.07 pp apart) and the candidate answers 1199, 5-6 questions fewer (about 0.4 pp). One binomial standard error on 1314 questions at this accuracy is about 0.8 pp, so the difference is not distinguishable from sampling noise, but it is larger than the spread between the two baseline runs. Profile (captured on the earlier producer-side revision that removed the same three copies; the copy removal is identical here since the convolution output is unchanged): - Before: [trace](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33468759/baseline-dp0_pp0_tp0_dcp0_ep0_rank0.perfetto.pt.trace.json.gz) — - After: [trace](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33468763/producer-dp0_pp0_tp0_dcp0_ep0_rank0.perfetto.pt.trace.json.gz) — ## Details - The change is two lines: pin FlashKDA `17a037d` -> `47fc9fec` in `cmake/external_projects/flashkda.cmake`, and drop `q/k/v.contiguous()` in `vllm/models/glm5next/common/kda.py`. `g`, `beta`, states, workspace and output handling are unchanged, as is the tensor operator schema. - FlashKDA #15 accepts any aligned token stride as long as the H/D rows are contiguous, the base pointer and row starts are 16-byte aligned, rows do not overlap and the B*T flattening is uniform. The merged convolution output satisfies all of these, including the 16-byte alignment (`3 * H * 128 * 2` bytes is always a multiple of 16). - Beta still needs the transpose inside FlashKDA; that is unchanged and is the single remaining copy kernel in the profile. - The pin also brings FlashKDA #15's standalone `launch_prepare` / `launch_recurrence` signature change. Nothing in vLLM `main` calls those launchers today (main pinned `17a037d`, which predates them), but the in-flight KCP work (vllm#59304) should pass `0` / its strides when it rebases. ---

title: [Perf][MRV2] Skip empty draft-token resets on request admission
author: jzakrzew
body:
## Overview
On GH200, short-input embedding inference at high concurrency is **CPU-bottlenecked by the EngineCore main thread**, with GPU SM utilization only **~9–18%**. Skip unnecessary per-request draft-buffer indexing and zeroing when Model Runner V2 has zero speculative steps, improving throughput by **~11–28%** in the measured workload while preserving the stale-slot reset from [#39833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39833) for nonempty buffers. The improvement is largely due to reduced GIL contention.



## Claims
- Remove unnecessary PyTorch operations from request admission for pooling and ordinary non-speculative generation.
- Preserve draft-token clearing on slot reuse whenever the buffer has columns, including speculative decoding and diffusion models.
- The PyTorch operation releases the GIL, leading to the main thread being unnecessarily preempted by other threads that could do their work while the main thread waits for the GPU instead.
- Existing pinned GH200 embedding benchmarks report +10.6% request throughput for short inputs at concurrency 512 and +25.0–28.2% at concurrency 2048 for this guard alone.


## Validation
Checks run for this change:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py -v -rs
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
git diff --check
```

With short inputs on GH200, throughput plateaus at roughly **5–6k requests/s (~85–100k tokens/s)** while the EngineCore main thread is CPU-saturated and GPU SM utilization remains **~9–18%**. For comparison, 1024-token inputs reach roughly **400k tokens/s** on the same server. These observations identify per-request work on the engine's main thread as the short-input throughput bottleneck.

| Concurrency | Stock throughput | With guard, pass 1 / pass 2 (estimated) | Gain, pass 1 / pass 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | ~4.66k req/s | ~5.15k / ~5.15k req/s | +10.6% / +10.6% |
| 2048 | ~5.57k req/s | ~6.96k / ~7.14k req/s | +25.0% / +28.2% |

Configuration: `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16`, FP8 quantization, v0.31.0 aarch64 container, one GH200, MRV2 with synchronous scheduling, 16 API servers, and unique random short text inputs. Two reverse-order benchmark passes used six runs per configuration. Engine cores 4–5, API-server cores 8–39, and client cores 40–71 were pinned on GPU 0's NUMA node. Stock pinning-validation repeats spanned 4741–4965 req/s; per-patch raw variability is unavailable here.

Server flags:

```text
--max-num-batched-tokens 65536 --max-model-len 32768
--max-cudagraph-capture-size 32768
--api-server-count 16 --chat-template-content-format openai
```



## Details
`RequestState` allocates `draft_tokens` with shape `[max_num_reqs, num_speculative_steps]`. Admission previously evaluated `self.draft_tokens[req_idx].zero_()` even when the row had zero elements. The guard tests the configured width before indexing.

**Why such a large improvement:** The reason seems to be GIL contention. The pytorch op releases the GIL and then the main thread spends time waiting in pthread_cond_timedwait to reacquire it. If GIL is not released at that point, other threads will acquire it when the main thread waits for the GPU instead, leading to better overlapping GPU and CPU work.

**Why short inputs matter for embedding models:** semantic search commonly embeds a short question or a few keywords to retrieve much longer passages. Short-query embedding is therefore a core online serving workload, even when the indexed documents are long.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Convert two FP8 values per cvt in the FP8 quant kernels
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #60927: the FP8 `cvt` instruction converts two values at once, but our scalar helper issues it with a zero partner. On sm_100+ this change quantizes pairs with `__nv_cvt_float2_to_fp8x2` and lets the saturating `cvt` replace the explicit clamp. Output is bit-identical to `main`.

## Claims

- **Speedup, bit-identical output:** RMSNorm + FP8 per-token/per-block quant is 1.05–1.24x faster; static, dynamic per-tensor and per-token `scaled_fp8_quant` are 1.00–1.08x faster; `merge_attn_states` with FP8 output is up to 1.03x faster. All measured on B300 with bf16/fp16/fp32 inputs.
- **No meaningful small-batch regression:** among bf16 cases, the worst at ≤128 rows is 0.98x.
- **One arch gate:** the switch is `VLLM_FP8_CVT_X2` in `csrc/core/cuda_compat.h` (`VLLM_FP8_CVT_X2_MIN_ARCH 1000`, matching #60927). The per-token-group packed path from #60927 now uses it too, with identical SASS. Hopper and older keep today's code; ROCm is unchanged.
- **All-zero input:** dynamic per-tensor quant of an all-zero tensor now writes zero bytes. On `main` it writes 448 with a 0 scale: `0 * (1/0)` is NaN, and only the clamp turned that into 448.

## Validation

**Bit-exactness.** I dumped the raw outputs (FP8 bytes and scales) of every touched op from a build of `main` and from this branch, then compared them exactly. Coverage: bf16/fp16/fp32 inputs, hidden sizes 17/1030/2048/4096/5120, aligned and unaligned views, static, per-tensor, per-token (with and without `scale_ub`), 1x128 groups, fused RMSNorm (FP8 and int8, with and without residual) and `merge_attn_states`. Result: 0 of 515 output tensors differ.

I also checked all 2^32 fp32 bit patterns: clamp-then-`cvt` and `cvt` alone agree on every non-NaN input, and the software `c10::Float8_e4m3fn` cast matches the hardware `cvt` on every non-NaN input. NaN is the only difference: it now stays FP8 NaN instead of becoming +448.

**Tests** (B300):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py \
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_silu_mul_block_quant.py tests/kernels/core/test_layernorm.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_merge_attn_states.py tests/kernels/test_fused_quant_activation.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py
# 5118 passed, 164 skipped
```

The new `test_dynamic_per_tensor_fp8_quant_all_zero` fails on `main` and passes here.

After rebasing onto `main` with #60927 and switching its gate, the per-token-group SASS is byte-identical to the old gate. Re-ran tests on that build:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant_group.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py tests/kernels/attention/test_merge_attn_states.py
# 3704 passed
```

Re-validated after merging `main` at e92bac311c, on a B300: 5803 passed across the FP8 quant, group quant, fused quant, layernorm and `merge_attn_states` kernel suites. Raw outputs again match a build of that `main`, 0 of 515 tensors differ. The performance numbers below are from the original branch; the kernel sources are unchanged since then.

**Performance.** FlashInfer `bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` with CUDA graphs and cold L2, median, on one B300. 526 cases: batch 1–8192, hidden sizes 4096/5120/7168/2880/1030/1025/17, bf16/fp16/fp32, plus unaligned views. Each build ran twice in alternating order (base, new, new, base); I report the min of the two runs. Run-to-run variation was ≤1% in nearly every case. Overall geomean is 1.023x.

Speedup vs `main`, bf16, geomean over hidden sizes:

| op | 1 row | 32 | 128 | 512 | 2048 | 8192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scaled_fp8_quant` static | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.02 | 1.05 |
| static, 1x128 group scales | 1.04 | 1.04 | 1.04 | 1.03 | 1.03 | 1.02 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.00 | 1.02 | 1.03 | 1.04 |
| dynamic per-token | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.01 | 1.02 | 1.02 |
| `rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_quant` | 1.05 | 1.04 | 1.04 | 1.08 | 1.10 | 1.10 |
| `rms_norm_per_block_quant` (1x128) | 1.11 | 1.10 | 1.10 | 1.18 | 1.20 | 1.24 |

Example absolute times (bf16, hidden 4096):

| op | rows | `main` (us) | this PR (us) |
|---|---|---|---|
| static quant | 8192 | 20.96 | 19.39 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 8192 | 37.12 | 34.75 |
| `rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_quant` | 2048 | 32.67 | 27.62 |
| `rms_norm_per_block_quant` | 8192 | 102.91 | 83.75 |
| `merge_attn_states` FP8 (2048 tok, 128 heads x 128) | — | 42.88 | 41.60 |

Hidden sizes 1030, 1025 and 17 are flat (1.00x geomean): they mostly take the unchanged scalar prefix/tail path.

<details>
<summary>CUPTI benchmark script</summary>

```python
"""CUPTI + CUDA-graph, cold-L2 timing of the FP8 quant ops. usage: cupti_bench.py out.json"""
import json, os, statistics, sys
OPS = os.environ.get("OPS")
OPS = OPS.split(",") if OPS else None
import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops

FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
torch.manual_seed(0)
dev = "cuda"

def bench_us(fn):
    for _ in range(25):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True,
                                  repeat_time_ms=150)
    return statistics.median(t) * 1e3

ROWS = [1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 512, 2048, 8192]
HIDDEN = [4096, 5120, 7168, 2880, 1030, 1025, 17] if not OPS else [4096, 2880, 5120]
res = {}
for dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32):
    dn = str(dtype).split(".")[-1]
    hiddens = HIDDEN if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else [4096, 1030]
    rows_l = ROWS if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else [1, 32, 2048]
    for hidden in hiddens:
        for rows in rows_l:
            x = (torch.randn(rows, hidden, device=dev) * 3).to(dtype)
            w = (torch.rand(hidden, device=dev) + 0.5).to(dtype)
            out = torch.empty(rows, hidden, device=dev, dtype=FP8)
            sc = torch.tensor([0.0371], device=dev)
            dsc = torch.empty(1, device=dev)
            tsc = torch.empty(rows, 1, device=dev)
            resid = (torch.randn(rows, hidden, device=dev)).to(dtype)
            tag = f"{dn}/{hidden}/{rows}"
            cases = {
                "static": lambda: torch.ops._C.static_scaled_fp8_quant(out, x, sc, None),
                "dyn_tensor": lambda: torch.ops._C.dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant(out, x, dsc),
                "dyn_token": lambda: torch.ops._C.dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant(out, x, tsc, None),
                "rms_static": lambda: torch.ops._C.rms_norm_static_fp8_quant(out, x, w, sc, 1e-6),
                "add_rms_static": lambda: torch.ops._C.fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant(out, x, resid, w, sc, 1e-6),
                "rms_dyn_token": lambda: torch.ops._C.rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_quant(out, x, w, tsc, 1e-6, None, None),
            }
            if hidden > 64:
                xv = x[:, 1:-15] if hidden % 16 == 0 else x[:, 1:]
                outv = torch.empty(xv.shape, device=dev, dtype=FP8)
                cases["static_unaligned_view"] = lambda: torch.ops._C.static_scaled_fp8_quant(outv, xv, sc, None)
            if hidden % 128 == 0:
                gsc = torch.rand(rows, hidden // 128, device=dev) * 0.05 + 0.01
                bsc = torch.empty(rows, hidden // 128, device=dev)
                cases["static_group128"] = lambda: torch.ops._C.static_scaled_fp8_quant(out, x, gsc, (1, 128))
                cases["rms_block128"] = lambda: torch.ops._C.rms_norm_per_block_quant(out, x, w, bsc, 1e-6, None, None, 128, False)
            if dtype == torch.float32:
                cases.pop("add_rms_static", None)
            for name, fn in cases.items():
                if OPS and name not in OPS:
                    continue
                try:
                    res[f"{name}/{tag}"] = bench_us(fn)
                except Exception as e:
                    print("skip", name, tag, type(e).__name__, str(e)[:80])

# merge_attn_states with fp8 output
for T, H, D in [] if OPS else [(1, 16, 512), (64, 16, 512), (4096, 16, 512), (2048, 128, 128)]:
    p = (torch.randn(T, H, D, device=dev) * 0.1).bfloat16(); s = (torch.randn(T, H, D, device=dev) * 0.1).bfloat16()
    pl = torch.randn(H, T, device=dev); sl = torch.randn(H, T, device=dev)
    o = torch.empty(T, H, D, device=dev, dtype=FP8); ol = torch.empty(H, T, device=dev)
    sc = torch.tensor([0.02], device=dev)
    res[f"merge_fp8/bfloat16/{H}x{D}/{T}"] = bench_us(lambda: ops.merge_attn_states(o, p, pl, s, sl, ol, None, sc))

json.dump(res, open(sys.argv[1], "w"))
print("cases", len(res))
```

</details>

## Details

- **Design:** `scaled_fp8_conversion_vec<is_scale_inverted, fp8_type, N>` in `w8a8/fp8/common.cuh` is the one helper. It pairs elements under `VLLM_FP8_CVT_X2` and otherwise, or for an odd tail, falls back to the existing scalar `scaled_fp8_conversion`. That scalar function is unchanged.
- **Call sites:** `common.cu` reaches the helper through a small functor that passes both a scalar op and a 16-wide op to `vectorize_with_alignment`. The fused RMSNorm kernels reach it through a new `ScaledQuant::quant_vec_fn` (a plain loop for int8).
- **Zero scale:** skipping the clamp means `0 * inf` would yield FP8 NaN, so every site that feeds an inverted scale into the paired path uses `fp8_reciprocal_scale`, which returns 0 for a zero scale. It measured as free.
- **Left out after measuring:**
  - Pairing in `rms_norm_static_fp8_quant` gained 3–6% at ≥512 rows but cost 1–3% at small batches.
  - Pairing in `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant` gained nothing.
  - Removing the clamp from the scalar path was about 2% slower in those kernels.
  - Pairing while keeping the clamp was up to 15% slower on small static quant.
  - `silu_and_mul_quant` and SiTU quant were flat.
- **Known regression:** static quant on fp32 input with hidden 1030 at 2048 rows is 4.5% slower (9.54 → 9.98 us). That branch's source is unchanged, so this is a codegen side effect of the neighbouring changes in the same kernel. bf16/fp16 on the same shape are 1.01x.
- **Hopper:** the instruction exists from sm_89, but I could only validate on Blackwell. Lowering `VLLM_FP8_CVT_X2_MIN_ARCH` is the one change needed once validated on other GPUs.
- **CI coverage:** the quantization kernel tests run on L4 (sm_89) and MI300, which take the unchanged path. The sm_100+ path was validated locally on B300 as above.
- **End to end:** no serving benchmark. Output is bit-identical, so accuracy evals are unchanged by construction. The gains are prefill-weighted; decode-size launches move by ≤11% on the fused RMSNorm quant ops and ≤4% elsewhere.
- **Not a duplicate:** #60927 (merged) covers only `per_token_group_quant`. The open #41115 changes the per-token kernel's launch configuration on a since-moved file, not the conversion.

title: [Refactor] [AMD] flydsl: Move UltraQuant/TurboQuant decode to public APIs
author: aditi-amd
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #47896 (TurboQuant FlyDSL decode) and #57057 (UltraQuant FlyDSL
decode), addressing review feedback that both kernels lean on low-level FlyDSL
APIs that are unstable or slated for deprecation. The kernels are rewritten
against FlyDSL's public `fx.*` API, following aiter's
`flydsl-kernel-code-cleanup` guide.

It also fixes a load failure on the pinned stack (`AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.24.post1`,
flydsl 0.3.4.1): neither FlyDSL decode kernel currently loads on main, and both
silently fall back to Triton. `tq_decode.py` / `tq_decode_gqa6.py` import
`buffer_ops` and `vector` from `flydsl.expr`, and `ultraquant_decode_hd256.py`
imports them from aiter internals (`aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels`); none of these

title: [Model] Add Nemotron Parse 3.5 serving and MTP support
author: DenisOvchinnikov93
body:
## Overview

Adds native serving for Nemotron Parse 3.5's causal visual-prefix architecture and a one-token auxiliary MTP proposer. This extends the Parse model implementation; related earlier-model speculative work is [#51168](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51168).

## Claims

- Register RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM and process variable-resolution packed RADIO images with content-normalized positional embeddings and visual-prefix placeholder expansion.
- Add ParseAuxMTPModel, loading the checkpoint's integrated auxiliary projections and routing causal-prefix configurations to one speculative token on Model Runner V2.
- Extend HF/vLLM generation coverage to Parse 3.5 and add five MTP configuration/loading/sharing contract tests to Basic Models CI. End-to-end MTP correctness and speedup remain unvalidated.
- Older generations of Nemotron-Parse are still supported.

## Validation

Tests ran locally. The nemotron-3.5-parse (with and without mtp) and nemotron-parse-2.0 accuracy verified on internal benchmarks. Parse 3.5 mtp acceptance rate is verified at various concurrencies. Tested on A100, H100. 

## Details

New nemotron-3.5-parse model uses an updated architecture which the current vllm implementation does not support. To simplify the change, created a new nemotron_parse3_5.py implementation while leaving code for previous versions unchanged. Major differences compared to previous implementation and approaches taken for implementations: 
1. New model uses visual prefix and removes cross-attention. 
add_cross_attention field controls whether to add cross-attention in decoder layer. Parse 3.5 implementation in vllm only supports checkpoints that has it set to False (as official checkpoint). Added a hard fail check that nemotron-3.5-parse models have it set to False. 
2. New model uses GQA vs old model using MHA.
Since WhisperAttention does not support GQA, created a local attention implementation that copies Whisper but adds GQA support. Can instead add GQA support to Whisper, but this increases common-code change. 
3. New model uses dynamic-size vision encoder with packed batching (NaVit-style) vs old model using static resolution. 
New RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM and pre-processing. Parse 3.5 is not using device-side preprocessing for parse 3.5 for simplicity (d1d8e6c). 
4. New model uses a different version of RADIO encoder.
Added RADIOv4-SO400M parameters to RADIO file. Model: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/C-RADIOv4-SO400M

## Known limitations and future work

1. Only V2 runner is supported for mtp-enabled parse 3.5. V1 runner fails because it expects kv-cache in the speculator and parse mtp does not have attention. 
2. RADIO dynamic packing causes a sync on . This code is reused between models, so leaving it as-is for this PR. The torch.tensor constructor should be replaced with async copy in the future. Will submit separate PR. 
3. Nemotron-3.5-Parse is currently not public, so the 3.5-specific tests are disabled. Those tests and additional validation for parse 3.5 was ran locally.

title: [Refactor] Migrate FlashInfer NVLink one-sided to MoEEpCommunication
author: suiyoubi
body:
## Overview

Migrate `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` from the deprecated `MoeAlltoAll` entry point to FlashInfer's `MoEEpCommunication` API introduced in [FlashInfer #5532](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5532).

This is an API prerequisite for the CFT integration discussed in [#57069](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57069). It does not enable CFT or migrate the two-sided backend.

FlashInfer 0.7.2 is released and upstream's stable dependency update is merged. Head `a0d97611` also addresses the public-API compatibility feedback: prefer checkpoint methods on `communication`, retain the 0.7.2 `.alltoall` fallback, and avoid importing removed legacy cache classes during test teardown. **The updated source passed all 11 one/two-sided tests on 0.7.2 and all 9 one-sided tests on the pinned upcoming FlashInfer API, with zero skips.**

## Claims

- Adopt `create_communication`, typed dispatch results, and the communication wrapper's combine interface.
- Preserve dispatch workspace sizing for BF16/FP16, NVFP4, MXFP8, and DeepSeek blockwise FP8, including padded MXFP8 scales.
- Share one communication wrapper across layers, growing token, dispatch, and combine capacities independently.
- Preserve the existing low-precision combine option and keep bootstrap metadata on CPU when CUDA is the default device.
- Extend regression coverage for workspace growth, quantized payloads, empty ranks, CUDA Graph replay, and low-precision combine.

## Validation

### Latest head — stable and upcoming API compatibility (October 19, 2026)

Head `a0d97611`, job **804205**, one exclusive Rubin node (`hecate0004`), pinned CUDA 13.4 image; **COMPLETED 0:0**.

| Dependency / check | Result |
|---|---|
| Official FlashInfer 0.7.2: one-sided + two-sided | 11/11 passed (9 one-sided, 2 two-sided), zero skips |
| FlashInfer [#6621](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6621) at `aa7ad45a32a6a5bf25b77803ff5afa3c66204cc1`: one-sided | 9/9 passed, zero skips |
| Actual-module import and manager checkpoint API-selection checks, both variants | Passed |
| Pre-commit, mypy and commit hooks | Passed |
| GPU cleanup / memory-clock reset | Passed; no GPU processes remained |

The existing GPU tests exercise checkpoint/restore and subsequent eager/CUDA Graph execution, empty ranks, workspace growth, quantized payloads and worker shutdown. The newer dependency has both legacy modules removed; its import checks confirm the public checkpoint API is selected. The shared `CustomCommunicator` no longer requires the legacy two-sided backend to exist. Legacy cache cleanup accesses only classes already loaded in the process.

The newer dependency is **unreleased source**, not a stable release. Its pinned source includes the upstream SM107 JIT build fix. This validates the one-sided path with the upcoming API; the production two-sided migration remains a separate change. The stable run retains a shared-memory resource-tracker warning, with no test failures or native shutdown crashes.

Commands: `python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py -k 'one_sided or two_sided' -v -s --timeout=1200` on 0.7.2; the same command with `-k one_sided` on the newer source. Both use fresh processes and separate JIT caches. No dispatch/combine implementation or numerical tolerances changed. Full model evaluations below were not repeated on the new FlashInfer revision.

### Previous head — two-sided shutdown fix (October 18, 2026)

Head `5d917258` was checked with FlashInfer **0.7.2 stable** and the pinned CUDA 13.4 image on Rubin GPUs in job `798176`. The committed source was verified to match the tested candidate.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Two-sided communication, repetition 1 | 2/2 passed, zero skips, exit 0 |
| Two-sided communication, repetition 2 | 2/2 passed, zero skips, exit 0 |
| Two-sided communication, repetition 3 | 2/2 passed, zero skips, exit 0 |
| One-sided communication | 9/9 passed, zero skips, exit 0 |
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including mypy | Passed |
| Post-test GPU cleanup and memory-clock reset | Passed |

The fix adds explicit cleanup of FlashInfer's cached two-sided workspace tensor views and their owners at the end of the test worker, before interpreter finalization. Child exit-code assertions remain enabled. This is a test-only shutdown fix; it does not change production communication or kernels.

The same allocation also ran an unmodified `36b34b68` control, which reproduced both shutdown SIGSEGVs. The diagnostic job deliberately preserves those control failures and therefore has aggregate Slurm status **FAILED 1:0**; **all candidate tests passed**. This resolves the observed test shutdown failure in this environment, without claiming a general production lifecycle fix.

### Stable model and component validation — October 18, 2026

Baseline `e80b6c64` and migrated `f592f3b5` used FlashInfer **0.7.2 stable**, the same pinned CUDA 13.4 image, and Rubin GPUs (job `796374`).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Dispatch layout | 13 passed, zero skips |
| One-sided communication | 9 passed, zero skips |
| MoE layer, DP=EP=2 and 4 / TP=1 | Three subcases per topology passed: two BF16 configurations and blocked FP8 |
| Fixed model prompts, eager and Graph | 24/24 exact token and logprob matches between baseline and migration in each mode |
| Full GSM8K, eager | 89.69% baseline → 89.08% migrated |
| Full GSM8K, Graph | 89.54% baseline → 89.69% migrated |
| Historical two-sided controls, before the test cleanup fix | Both baseline and migration reproduced shutdown SIGSEGVs; superseded for current-head test status by the passing results above |

Model evaluation used Qwen3-30B-A3B, 1,319 GSM8K questions, five-shot prompting and max 256 output tokens. Mixed prefill/decode and actual CUDA Graph replay were checked. All model-comparison gates passed; no accuracy or performance improvement is claimed.

The layer-log parser initially misclassified inline `PASSED` as missing because it required a preceding newline. Each named subcase and the “3 passed of 3 total subcases” summaries were reconciled against the raw logs. The original logs and failed job status remain preserved: the two-sided native crashes are real failures, and the overall job is **FAILED 1:0**, not a clean pass.

The intermediate `36b34b68` rerun (job `798024`) passed 9/9 one-sided tests but still reproduced the two-sided shutdown failure. These historical failures are retained in the evidence; the current-head results above supersede them. At `36b34b68` and `5d917258`, production code was identical to `f592f3b5`. The October 19 follow-up changes checkpoint API selection and the shared communicator's import dependency; its targeted cross-version validation is listed above.

All eight changed files at `f592f3b5` passed pre-commit, including mypy; the changed test file at `36b34b68` also passed all applicable hooks. The official stable wheel’s corresponding 499 MoE EP / one-sided Python files match the stable tag; these API paths are unchanged from the official rc3 tag.

Preparation job `796345` ran no tests because source verification followed a Git symlink to a directory. Symlink-target hashing was corrected in the separate `796374` attempt; original evidence was retained.

### Previous validation — October 14, 2026

Migration commit `c1ad8076` was validated against vLLM baseline `5555a2d8` using FlashInfer **0.7.2rc3**, CUDA **13.4**, and two Rubin GPUs. Baseline and migrated code used the same dependency versions.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including mypy | Passed |
| Host manager lifecycle/capacity checks | 28 passed; GPU allocation and collectives stubbed |
| Dispatch layout tests | 13 passed, zero skips |
| One-sided GPU communication tests | 9 passed, zero skips |
| MoE layer regression, DP=EP=2 / TP=1 | BF16 and blocked-FP8 cases passed, zero skips |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, eager and CUDA Graph | Model comparison checks passed |

For each execution mode, baseline and migrated code produced **identical token sequences and logprobs for all 24 fixed prompts**. Validation also exercised mixed prefill/decode traffic, verified actual CUDA Graph replay, and enabled `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

Full GSM8K evaluation used 1,319 questions, five-shot prompting, and a maximum of 256 output tokens:

| Execution mode | Baseline accuracy | Migrated accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|
| Eager | 89.16% | 90.07% |
| CUDA Graph | 89.76% | 90.22% |

These results support correctness; no accuracy improvement or performance improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Historical two-sided shutdown failures — resolved in the current test run</summary>

Both two-sided regression tests encountered child-process `SIGSEGV` during interpreter teardown, with a tensor/storage-deleter stack under `Py_FinalizeEx`.

The **unchanged baseline reproduced both failures under the same dependency versions**. This supports treating the issue as existing in the tested environment rather than specific to this migration. The failures remain recorded as failures; the overall validation job retained a nonzero exit status.

The distributed test launcher checks child exit codes so native crashes cannot silently appear as passing tests. The explicit end-of-worker cleanup in `5d917258` resolves this failure in the tested environment, as shown by the same-allocation control/candidate experiment above.

</details>

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Reuse pinned host pool after graph profiling
author: Etelis
body:
HiSparse allocates and pins its host KV pool during profiling, then repeats that work for serving. Keep one engine-scoped pool, keyed by `instance_id`, and reuse its backing for the real KV cache.

Profiling teardown detaches temporary layer caches; connector shutdown or failed initialization releases the pool. This removes the per-layer ownership and preservation flags, leaving CUDA-graph teardown unchanged from main.

Adopts Matthew’s approach in [Etelis/vllm#9](https://github.com/Etelis/vllm/pull/9). Refs #60072; complements #60869.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Allow explicit SimpleCPUOffload block counts
author: SherifWaly
body:
## Overview

Allow `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` users to set a shared `num_cpu_blocks` so uneven pipeline stages use the same offload pool size. This implements the explicit-count alternative [suggested in the review of #52921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52921#pullrequestreview-5449639086).

## Claims

- The scheduler and workers honor the configured count for CPU or disk offload.
- Startup rejects nonpositive/noninteger counts and counts exceeding the local byte-derived capacity, before allocating offload buffers.
- Omitting the option retains automatic sizing. No engine-core changes, collectives, or runtime synchronization are added.

## Validation

- **116 scheduler/worker tests passed**, including 15 added regression cases. Tested current-main Python sources on a B200 using the deployed v0.30.0 compiled extensions; this was not a full current-main native build.
- **All pre-commit hooks passed**, including mypy, formatting, and CI test tethering.
- **End-to-end A/B serving:** Kimi K3, two nodes with 8 B200 GPUs each, TP8/DCP8/PP2, fp8 KV, TOKENSPEED MLA, MRV2, RDMA, no speculative decoding, 128 MiB CPU budget per rank. The same connector change was backported to the deployed v0.30.0 image for serving validation.

| Observation | Automatic sizing | Explicit `num_cpu_blocks: 23` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Scheduler / PP0 / PP1 block counts | 25 / 25 / 23 | 23 / 23 / 23 |
| Highest CPU destination ID | 24 | 22 |
| Out-of-bounds native copy calls | 40, across all 8 PP1 ranks | 0 across 1,088 copy calls |
| Nonempty streaming responses with `[DONE]` | 34/34 | 35/35 |
| Forced CPU reload after GPU prefix-cache reset | Not requested | All 16 ranks; identical 16 output tokens |

The baseline reproduced invalid copy IDs and completed its responses without a model segfault. These results establish the sizing/copy defect; they do not attribute every historical crash to it. No throughput or broad model-accuracy improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and serving exercise</summary>

The GPU test environment put the current-main source tree at `/tmp/upstream-vllm` and used a `uv` virtualenv with the deployed wheel's compiled extensions:

```bash
/tmp/offload-test-venv/bin/python -I -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/upstream-vllm"); import pytest; sys.exit(pytest.main(["tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py", "tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py", "-v"]))'
```

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
```

Baseline transfer configuration:

```json
{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":134217728,"lazy_offload":false}}
```

Add `"num_cpu_blocks":23` for the patched run. Both runs use `--enable-prefix-caching --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA`. The tested model's stage allocations contain 12 and 13 block-strided tensors, respectively, with 442,368 bytes per tensor block. Other models/layouts need a different count.

Exercise `/v1/completions` with `stream:true`, `stream_options:{"include_usage":true}`, `return_token_ids:true`, `temperature:0`, `seed:42`, `ignore_eos:true`, and `max_tokens:16`. Send one approximately 11k-token prefix twice, then 32 different approximately 3.7k-token prefixes to cycle the CPU pool. Check positive usage and `[DONE]` for every response.

In the patched run, enable `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` and POST `/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false` after the cold prefix stores drain. Require `success:true`, repeat the prefix, and compare output text and token IDs with the cold result. Reset the GPU cache every four unique prefixes. Instrument `cuda_mem_ops.build_params`/`copy_blocks` to record tensor allocation limits, copied block-ID ranges, and actual CPU-to-GPU copies; successful API responses alone do not establish that offload was exercised.

Baseline trace excerpt:

```json
{"event":"copy_params","layers":13,"source_blocks":10844,"destination_blocks":23,"source_order":1}
{"event":"out_of_bounds_copy","source_max":27,"destination_max":24,"source_limit":10844,"destination_limit":23}
```

Patched trace excerpts (same allocation limits on both stages):

```json
{"event":"copy_enter","blocks":3,"destination_min":20,"destination_max":22,"destination_limit":23,"source_order":1}
{"event":"copy_enter","blocks":5,"source_min":1,"source_max":5,"source_limit":23,"source_order":3}
```

</details>

## Details

Automatic sizing divides the byte budget by each stage's cache geometry independently. With uneven PP stages, the scheduler can assign IDs beyond a heavier worker's allocation; the DMA implementation forms pointers from those IDs without a bounds check. An explicit shared count limits both the scheduler's pool and each worker's allocation, with worker validation based on live tensor strides. For the disk backend, the bound is `disk_capacity_bytes`.

This is materially different from the open #52921: that PR automatically aligns counts using worker collectives and engine RPC. This PR provides the reviewer's smaller configuration-based alternative and leaves engine core untouched. It requires operators to choose a count that fits every worker and configure it identically on every rank. Recalculate it when model layout, parallelism, or speculative decoding changes; unspecified automatic sizing is not repaired by this option.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Segment host KV pool backing files
author: Etelis
body:
HiSparse stores its host KV pool as one logical chunk. The segmented backing support in merged #59546 splits whole rows, so this pool still uses one `/dev/shm` file, where page-cache insertion limits parallel pre-faulting.

Split the single chunk at 2 MiB boundaries and use the shared 32-file limit (`REGION_SEGMENTS`). The mapping stays contiguous; capacity and CUDA registration ranges stay unchanged. Reserve virtual space with a sparse memfd mapping, which needs no writable temp directory and does not charge the full pool against the commit limit.

Previously measured on two nodes with 8 H100 workers and a 1 TiB pool each: RAM preparation fell from **264.5 / 232.3 s to 44.5 / 44.4 s**. Preparation plus pinning fell from **378.1 / 340.6 s to 152.3 / 146.8 s**. These benchmarks were not rerun for this update.

## Tests

title: [MoE] Add locality-domain allocation for FlashInfer CuTeDSL NVFP4
author: soodoshll
body:
## Overview

Add opt-in locality-domain weight allocation and MoE execution on Rubin, using upstream PyTorch locality APIs and FlashInfer CuTeDSL. Requires the stream-execution compatibility fix in [FlashInfer #6488](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6488).

## Claims

- Support locality-domain allocation and localized MoE execution.
- Support optional backfill, overlapping output memset, and releasing full-width weights.
- Use CUDA graph autotuning consistently for localized and baseline execution.

## Validation

### MoE op performance

Measured on Rubin with NVFP4 inputs/weights, BF16 output, SiTU activation, and balanced routing. Both paths independently autotune with CUDA graph profiling—no manually fixed tactics. Timing covers **FC1 + memset + FC2**, excluding routing and input preparation.

Per-rank shapes (hidden / intermediate / experts / top-k):

- **TP8-shaped:** 3584 / 384 / 896 / 16; no backfill.
- **TEP16-shaped:** 3584 / 3072 / 56 / 16; backfill enabled.

Median latency over 10 alternating paired rounds, each with 8 calls per graph and 125 replays. Speedup is the median paired ratio; ranges show min–max.

| Shape | Tokens | Baseline (µs) | Localized (µs) | Speedup | Range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8-shaped | 64 | 199.163 | 185.427 | 1.074× | 1.074–1.075× |
| TP8-shaped | 128 | 203.928 | 188.833 | 1.080× | 1.080–1.080× |
| TP8-shaped | 256 | 207.981 | 192.078 | 1.083× | 1.083–1.083× |
| TEP16-shaped | 32 | 92.315 | 80.600 | 1.145× | 1.145–1.146× |
| TEP16-shaped | 64 | 92.368 | 79.582 | 1.161× | 1.160–1.161× |
| TEP16-shaped | 128 | 93.310 | 82.644 | 1.129× | 1.128–1.130× |
| TEP16-shaped | 256 | 94.930 | 81.353 | 1.167× | 1.152–1.179× |
| TEP16-shaped | 512 | 128.676 | 126.227 | 1.019× | 0.992–1.047× |
| TEP16-shaped | 1024 | 191.054 | 189.298 | 1.008× | 0.995–1.021× |

## Details

Enable with `VLLM_USE_LOCALITY_DOMAINS=1` and `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutedsl`. Requires compatible PyTorch, CUDA, and FlashInfer builds. Optional controls:

- `VLLM_MOE_LOCALIZE_BACKFILL=1`: enable backfill.
- `VLLM_MOE_LOCALIZE_FREE_FULL_WEIGHTS=1`: release original weights and restrict tuning to localized execution.
- `VLLM_MOE_LOCALIZE_MEMSET_OVERLAP`: enabled by default.

Localization is disabled by default; localized per-token activation quantization is unsupported.

Also includes K3 KDA compatibility adjustments for Triton nightly: remove `B` from `do_not_specialize` because it is not a kernel argument in the NVIDIA/AMD implementations, and align gated normalization with [upstream FLA #1062](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/pull/1062), preserving K3's head-aware, row-strided gate addressing. The block-pointer migration is already in vLLM main; the remaining gated-norm diff only aligns the gate-load expression/mask and records upstream provenance. AMD runtime validation remains pending.
