title: [Benchmark] Add per-case kernel profiles to vllm bench forward
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Add `--profile-dir` to `vllm bench forward` (#61339): a per-kernel GPU time breakdown of each benchmarked batch, in a form an agent or a script can read and compare directly.

## Claims

- `--profile-dir DIR`: after timing, each case's graph is replayed 3 more times under `torch.profiler`. Every rank writes `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.trace.json.gz` (Perfetto) and `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.kernels.json` (GPU time per kernel per forward, sorted, with call counts and one full name per group). Rank 0's top kernels are printed and included in `--output-json`.
- Only the timed forward is counted: the in-graph KV restore and rank rendezvous that precede it in each replay are left out (reported as `pre_forward_us`), so the profile accounts for the same interval as `median_us`.
- `python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile A.kernels.json [B.kernels.json]` prints one summary, or a per-kernel diff of two (e.g. before/after a change) sorted by the largest change.
- Nsight Systems: each case's 3 profiled replays always run between `cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop` in an NVTX range `forward/<case>`, so `nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat --cuda-graph-trace=node` records just them, one small report per case (and per rank with `torchrun --no-python nsys ...`). `--profile-dir` and nsys can't share CUPTI; combining them fails with a clear message.
- Timing runs before profiling, so reported latencies are unchanged; without a profiler the extra 3 replays per case are the only cost.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py   # 4 passed (GB200): new summary unit test; the end-to-end test now also runs --profile-dir
```

Llama-3.2-1B, 1 GPU: profiled forward span vs timed median: decode 1291 vs 1265 us, prefill 4755 vs 4498 us, prefix hit 1782 vs 1770 us (profiler overhead; prefill's own sample spread was 1.75%). Decode excluded 512 restore copies per replay (~830 us), as intended.

Nsight Systems (2025.5), Llama-3.2-1B: one ~680 KB report per case; `nsys stats --report nvtx_sum` shows the `forward/<case>` range and `cuda_gpu_kern_sum` matches the JSON summary (48 calls = 16 layers x 3 replays). DP2 via `torchrun --no-python nsys`: one report per rank per case. `--profile-dir` under nsys: fails with the CUPTI message.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (1 GB200 node), ~100K KV: all 4 ranks wrote traces and summaries; span vs median: decode b32 15731 vs 15734 us, b128 20087 vs 19975 us, prefill 16K 204.2 vs ~202 ms. Example (prefill 16K, rank 0):

```
        us      %  calls  kernel
   62146.8  30.35     40  deep_gemm::sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_impl
   22000.9  10.74    131  kernel_cutlass_kernel_flashinfergemmkernelsdense_blockscaled_gemm_sm100Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmKernel
   20274.8   9.90     40  fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16H512PagedKvDenseDynamicTokenSparseP1VarSeqQ64Kv128PersistentKeepsAbForGen
   19139.9   9.35      2  _engram_lookup_kernel
   10378.6   5.07     23  vllm::topKPerRowPrefill
```

## Details

- Each replay's GPU activities are split into the `len(state_views)` restore copies (one copy each), the rendezvous all-reduce (multi-rank), and the forward. The summary checks that the activities divide evenly into replays and raises otherwise.
- Kernel names are grouped without return type, template and function arguments (`void ns::foo<T>(...)` -> `ns::foo`); generic launchers keep their first template argument (`cutlass::device_kernel<Op>`), CuTe DSL names drop their per-shape suffix. Non-kernel activities (memcpy/memset) keep their names.
- `span_us` is first-to-last forward activity and should track `median_us`; `busy_us` sums kernel durations and can exceed it with multi-stream overlap.
- Why both: `torch.profiler` needs no extra tooling, is scoped per case in-process, and is tested in CI, so it backs the agent-facing JSON summary and diff. Nsight Systems adds NVTX, NCCL, CPU-side and GPU-metric views that many users reach for; the capture range makes it record only the benchmarked replays instead of the whole process (load, JIT, warmup, timing).
- The model-microbenchmark skill gets a short "Kernel breakdown" section on both workflows (including keeping `--capture-range-end=repeat`, since nsys's default stops after the first case and leaves the bench hanging).
- Size: `profile.py` ~200 lines plus ~40 lines of wiring; tests and docs ~60.

title: [CI] Fix B200 FusedMoE Layer Kernels hang on NVSHMEM IB setup
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

`(B200) FusedMoE Layer Kernels` is failing ~24% of main runs (59/247 over the last two weeks), almost all of them by hanging until the 90 minute job timeout. The hang is in `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_low_latency-2-1-True]`, where NVSHMEM's InfiniBand transport setup fails and the spawned workers never exit. This PR keeps these single-node DeepEP tests on NVLink and off the NICs, and makes any future hang fail fast.

Alternative to the stalled draft #53332, which retries the launch instead of avoiding IB; details below.

## Claims

- The CUDA DeepEP cases of `test_moe_layer` no longer use NVSHMEM's IB transports. That is where every B200 hang starts. Both GPUs in each test are on the same node, connected by NVLink, so the IB path carries no test traffic anyway.
- `parallel_launch_with_config` kills its workers and raises `TimeoutError` after 15 minutes. `test_moe_layer` already turns that into a normal test failure, so a future hang costs one test instead of the whole job.
- The B200 job timeout drops from 90 to 45 minutes. Passing runs take 15–18 minutes, and the slowest passing run in the last two weeks took 36 minutes.

## Validation

**CI history (job logs from builds 94300–94498, 56 runs: 47 passed, 8 timed out, 1 failed fast).** All 8 timeouts show the same signature and then no further output until the job is cancelled:

```
ibrc.cpp:427:  non-zero status: 22 ibv_modify_qp failed
ibrc.cpp:1526: non-zero status: 7 ep_connect failed
init.cu:1047:  non-zero status: 7 nvshmem setup connections failed
```

**Local repro (2x B300 on one node).** IB is unusable on this box for an unprivileged user (8 MB memlock), which makes it a stand-in for a broken IB setup. Command:

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k deepep
```

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_low_latency-2-1-True]` | fails in NVSHMEM init (`ibrc.cpp:314: cq creation failed`) | passes (48/48 subcases) |
| `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_high_throughput-2-1-True]` | n/a | 191/192 subcases pass |

The one high-throughput miss is a local DeepGEMM JIT failure (`nvcc fatal: Failed to preprocess host compiler properties`), unrelated to this change. DeepEP high-throughput mode with 2 ranks allocates no RDMA buffer and does not initialise NVSHMEM.

**Launcher timeout.** Tested with a worker that sleeps forever and the timeout set to 30 s: it raised `TimeoutError` after 31 s, and no child processes were left behind. A normal launch still returns.

## Details

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

- **It is the first NVSHMEM init that fails, not re-initialisation.** The test creates a new DeepEP low-latency buffer for each subtest, so a passing run initialises NVSHMEM 48 times. Each init logs 32 `cudaHostRegister` fallback warnings (1536 per passing run). All 8 hung runs stop after exactly 32, before the first subtest finishes. So the hang always happens on the first init of the job, never on a later one.
- **IBGDA is unavailable in these pods, so NVSHMEM falls back to IBRC.** The `cudaHostRegister ... error=800` / `ibgda_*` fallback warnings appear in passing runs too. The fallback IBRC queue-pair connect is what intermittently fails, and the worker group then hangs instead of exiting.
- **It looks host- or contention-related.** Timeouts hit dgxB200-09/12/14 (8 of 32 runs) and none of 01/11/16 (0 of 23). 5 of the 8 timeouts started within 2–5 minutes of another run of this job on the same host. Every B200 pod sees all of the node's NICs (the job's `nvidia-smi topo -m` lists 12), so concurrent pods share them. This is suggestive, not proven.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why these settings</summary>

- `NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` disables IBRC.
- `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST=none` hides the NICs from IBGDA. DeepEP's low-latency buffer sets `NVSHMEM_IB_ENABLE_IBGDA=1` unconditionally, and `REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` alone still tried IBGDA locally and failed.
- With no remote transport, NVSHMEM uses its P2P transport. DeepEP's low-latency kernels take the NVLink store path whenever `nvshmemi_get_p2p_ptr` returns a peer pointer, which is the case for every peer in a single-node test.
- The settings are applied through the existing `env_dict` hook, only for CUDA DeepEP backends. ROCm/MoRI paths are untouched.
- The CI pods for both jobs that run this file have their GPU pair on NVLink (`NV18` in the `nvidia-smi topo -m` of the B200 job and the H100 job). If a future runner had a GPU pair without peer access, the low-latency case would fail clearly rather than hang.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Relation to #53332</summary>

#53332 (draft, idle since Sep 14) adds an opt-in join timeout plus a single retry with NVSHMEM debug logging. It is framed around NVSHMEM re-initialisation. The B200 data above shows the failure is on the first init and in the IB transport, so this PR removes the IB dependency rather than retrying it. The timeout here applies to every `parallel_launch_with_config` caller: the longest single launch seen in a passing B200 run is ~195 s, against the 900 s limit.

The H100 SIGSEGV that #53332 also describes happened after `init failed for transport: IBGDA`. This change should avoid that too, but I have not reproduced it.

</details>

**Limitations.** This drops IB transport coverage from `test_moe_layer`. That coverage was never meaningful here: the tests are single-node, and IB setup on the CI pods only works via fallback. Multi-node DeepEP coverage belongs in a multi-node test.

title: [Perf] Read VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS once per IterationStats
author: peilii
body:
## Overview

`IterationStats.update_from_output` read `envs.VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` once per request output per step. This reads it once per `IterationStats` instead.

## Claims

- Removes one `envs` module `__getattr__` and two `os.getenv` calls per request output per step from the API-server output-processing loop. Measured on the installed vLLM (CPU, aarch64): `IterationStats.update_from_output` goes from 4.1 µs to 1.6 µs per output with the envs cache off, which is the API server's state today.
- No behaviour change: the flag is read at the start of each iteration instead of for each output within it.

## Validation

- py-spy GIL profile of a `vllm serve`-based worker streaming a few thousand concurrent requests: `update_from_output` → `envs.__getattr__` → the `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` lambda accounted for a little over 1% of all GIL-held samples in the API-server process. With the read hoisted that frame disappears.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py` passes.

## Details

`enable_envs_cache()` is only called in the multiprocess executor, so processes that run `OutputProcessor` (the API server, or any `AsyncLLM` host) always take the uncached path. The flag cannot change between outputs of one step in any meaningful way, so reading it per `IterationStats` keeps the semantics while taking it off the per-output path.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] silu_and_mul_quant: run the vectorized loop
author: Monishver11
body:
## Purpose

`silu_and_mul_quant` (`act_and_mul_quant_kernel` in `csrc/quantization/activation_kernels.cu`) is the fused SiLU-and-mul + static per-tensor FP8 quant that the manual activation+quant fusion (#51415, `maybe_fused_act_quant`) routes static-FP8 models through by default.

Its 128-bit vectorized loop has never executed. The loop bound is computed as `round_to_previous_multiple_of(elems_per_128bit_load, block_end)`, with the two arguments swapped: the helper rounds its first argument down to a multiple of its second, so this rounds 8 down to a multiple of `block_end`, which is 0 for any `d > 8`. With `vec_loop_end = 0` the vectorized loop has an empty range and every element goes through the scalar cleanup loop with 2-byte loads and 1-byte stores. Present since the kernel landed in #10867. Runtime proof on `main`: with the input and output pointers misaligned by 8 bytes the op completes and matches the aligned result for d = 14336 and 10752 (no 16-byte load executed), and faults with `misaligned address` at d = 8, the one shape where the bound is non-zero.

The cost: on H100 the kernel runs at 1.9 TB/s effective against 3.1 TB/s for the Inductor-fused kernel it replaced, and Llama-3.1-8B-FP8 serves about 3.5% slower with the fusion wired than on the Inductor path (numbers below).

This PR:

- Fixes the argument order, so the bound is `block_end` rounded down to the vector width and the 128-bit loop covers the block.
- Takes the vectorized path only when `d` is a multiple of the vector width (8 for bf16/fp16) and both data pointers are 16-byte aligned, via the existing `vllm::is_16byte_aligned`. Rows of other widths are not 16-byte aligned (d = 781, hidden size 1562 in the unit test, starts odd rows 4 bytes off) and would fault on the fixed loop; they keep the scalar loop, which is what every shape runs today.
- In the scalar case the cleanup loop starts at the block's own `block_start` instead of 0. With 2 to 4 blocks per row at 32 tokens or fewer, starting at 0 made each block redo the preceding blocks' elements (same values written, wasted bandwidth).

Output is bit-identical to `main`: both loops evaluate the same per-element expression. Verified below. No change to grid, block size or arithmetic; the remaining gap to the Inductor kernel (0.9x at prefill, about 0.5x at decode) is the subject of a separate follow-up.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches this kernel. #49828 adds a separate per-token dynamic kernel in the same file with its own launch. #59514 is my earlier PR that bundled this fix with a kernel rewrite; it is being split into this fix and a follow-up so each can be reviewed on its own.

## Test Plan

- Runtime proof of the dead loop on `main` and of the alignment guard on this branch (misaligned-pointer test, script in the attached logs).
- Bitwise vs `main` (4b61f300c0): sha256 of the output bytes over bf16 and fp16, tokens 1 to 16384, d in {8192, 10752, 14336, 28672} plus {8, 24, 781, 2048, 4104, 10760, 14341}, and misaligned-pointer cases; 302 cases.
- `pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_quant_activation.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_functionalization.py`
- Microbenchmark: H100 80GB, driver 615, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, `do_bench_cudagraph`; the op on both builds and a `torch.compile` of `SiluAndMul.forward_native` + `QuantFP8(static).forward_native` as the Inductor column.
- E2e on RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 with main's own wiring, three interleaved arms: `main` kernel, this fix, and the same tree with the `llama.py` wiring line reverted (Inductor path):

title: [Bugfix] Fix NaN output of the Mamba2 chunk scan kernel on sm90
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview Fixes #61603. On Hopper (sm90), the Mamba2 SSD kernel `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` writes NaN/Inf into whole output rows from finite inputs with some of its autotune configs (8 of 23 in the reproducer). The autotuner picks configs by speed only, so it can pick one of them. This PR drops these configs on CUDA sm90 only. It uses one rule taken from the compiled code: drop a config when `num_warps % 4 == 0`, `BLOCK_SIZE_M % 64 == 0` and `num_stages > 1`. Compared with #61664, this fix: - also drops three configs (M/N/K, warps, stages) that compile to the same racy code on Triton 3.7.1: 64/32/32 8w 2s, 128/256/64 8w 3s and 128/32/32 4w 4s. On the [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) tree the reproducer still prints `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 1 of 15` (128/32/32 4w 4s gave NaN in 81 of 100 calls), and 128/256/64 8w 3s gave NaN in 50 of 50 calls at dstate 256. - adds a test that runs the real kernel with every config in the list. It fails on the old code and on the [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) tree. The tests in [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) are mock-only and never run the kernel; on the old code they fail only with an `ImportError` that comes from that PR's own refactor. ## Claims - On sm90, no config left in the autotune list gives NaN on the reproducer: `0 of 12`, against `8 of 23` before. - Other platforms keep all 23 configs. The filter returns the list unchanged unless the device is CUDA with capability 9.0. - No speed cost at the shapes measured on an H20-3e: the fastest config of the old list is kept. - The new test `test_chunk_scan_fwd_every_config_matches` fails on the old code and passes with the fix. ## Validation Setup: 1 x NVIDIA H20-3e (sm90), torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, vLLM at commit `77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989`, then the same commit plus this PR. Reproducer: the issue's script, changed to force each config of `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` in turn and run it 100 times on finite inputs (seed 0, 181 tokens, 2 chunks). Run it with `python sweep.py`. I swept the whole list because the issue's `GOOD` config is not in the list at this commit.
sweep.py (the issue's unused BAD/GOOD/force_old lines left out) ```python import torch, triton from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.ssd_chunk_scan import ( _chunk_scan_fwd, _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel) print("triton", triton.__version__, "torch", torch.__version__, torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0)) seqlen, nchunks = 181, 2 dev, g = "cuda", torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0) rn = lambda *s, dt=torch.bfloat16, sc=0.5: (torch.randn(*s, generator=g, device=dev)*sc).to(dt) x, C = rn(seqlen,64,64), rn(seqlen,8,128) cb = rn(nchunks,8,128,128, dt=torch.float32, sc=1.0) dt_ = (torch.rand(64,nchunks,128, generator=g, device=dev)*0.1).float() dA = (-torch.rand(64,nchunks,128, generator=g, device=dev).cumsum(-1)*0.05).float() states = rn(nchunks,64,64,128, dt=torch.float32, sc=0.1) cu = torch.tensor([0,128,181], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) sidx = torch.zeros(nchunks, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) ALL = list(_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel.configs) print("inputs finite:", all(bool(torch.isfinite(t.float()).all()) for t in (x,C,cb,dt_,dA,states))) nbad = 0 for i, c in enumerate(ALL): _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel.configs = [c] hits = 0 try: for _ in range(100): out = torch.empty(seqlen,64,64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev) _chunk_scan_fwd(cb, x, dt_, dA, C, states, cu, out, sidx, D=rn(64,64, dt=torch.float32, sc=0.1)) hits += int((~torch.isfinite(out.float())).any().item()) except Exception as e: print(i, c.kwargs, c.num_warps, c.num_stages, "ERR", type(e).__name__); continue nbad += hits > 0 print(i, c.kwargs, "warps", c.num_warps, "stages", c.num_stages, "-> NaN in", hits, "/100 calls") print("configs producing NaN from finite inputs:", nbad, "of", len(ALL)) ```
| Tree | Runs | Last line, every run | |---|---|---| | `77154ca6116a` | 3 (1 in a source checkout, 2 in the nightly image for that commit) | `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 8 of 23` | | this PR | 3 | `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 0 of 12` | Before the fix, the NaN configs were 64/64/64 with 4 warps and 2 stages (NaN in 22 to 31 of 100 calls) and the seven configs with 4 warps and 4 stages (53 to 100 of 100). 128/256/64 with 8 warps and 3 stages raises `OutOfResources` at this shape. After the fix, each of the 12 configs left gave NaN in 0 of 100 calls. Tests: ``` python -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py -k test_chunk_scan_fwd_every_config_matches -v ``` - With this PR: passed, 2 of 2 runs. - With the old config list: failed at 64/64/64, 4 warps, 2 stages, 2 of 2 runs. One run failed the finite check. The other failed the closeness check with `Greatest absolute difference: 1.7147041145625415e+38`, so the test compares outputs and does not only check `isfinite`. - Whole file `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` with this PR: `95 passed`. - `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed files passes. I used `--noconftest` because the test environment did not have `tblib`, which `tests/conftest.py` imports. The new test uses only `monkeypatch`. In CI, the Buildkite step `kernels-mamba-test` runs `pytest -v -s kernels/mamba` on an H200 (sm90), so the new test runs on the affected architecture. Speed: `triton.testing.do_bench` on every config of the old list, NemotronH-like prefill shape (128 heads, headdim 64, 8 groups, dstate 128, chunk 128, bf16), on the H20-3e: | seqlen | Best of old list | Best of new list | Best config | |---|---|---|---| | 1024 | 62.2 us | 62.2 us | 64/64/32, 4 warps, 1 stage | | 8192 | 425.4 us | 425.4 us | 64/64/32, 4 warps, 1 stage | At seqlen 8192 the dropped configs took 481.7 to 1818.1 us. Not run: an end-to-end NemotronH server run (the issue's empty responses and `not JSON compliant: nan`). Only the kernel reproducer and the tests above were run. ## Details Root cause. In the K loop, `acc += tl.dot(cb, x)` uses `cb` built in registers (decay `exp`, `dt`, causal mask, cast to bf16). With whole warpgroups (`num_warps % 4 == 0`) and `BLOCK_SIZE_M % 64 == 0`, Triton lowers this dot to wgmma with the A operand in registers. With `num_stages > 1`, Triton's `TritonGPUPipeline` pass splits the dot into async wgmmas and waits with `pendings = 1`. So the last wgmma of an iteration is still running when the loop jumps back. The next iteration loads the next `cb` tile into the same registers before it waits for that wgmma. The PTX ISA does not allow changes to the A registers of `wgmma.mma_async` before `wgmma.wait_group`. The running wgmma reads raw fp32 bits as bf16, which gives NaN, Inf and values near 3.4e38 in whole output rows. The race depends on timing, so the NaN rate changes by config and by run. The bug is in Triton's pipeliner, which vLLM cannot change. The vLLM part is that the autotune list offers configs that Triton compiles this way.
SASS of the K loop, 128/128/32 with 4 warps and 4 stages ``` /*58f0*/ LDS.128 R160, [R234] ; <- overwrites R160..R163 /*5b90*/ LDS.128 R156, [R234+0x1000] ; <- overwrites R156..R159 ... /*70a0*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R88, R160, gdesc[UR12].tnspB, R88 ; <- A = R160..R163 /*70b0*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R24, R156, gdesc[UR12].tnspB, R24, gsb0 ; <- A = R156..R159 /*71d0*/ WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0, 0x1 ; <- leaves the 0x70a0/0x70b0 group running ... /*7720*/ @!P5 BRA 0x5750 ; ```
The fix. `_drop_racy_wgmma_configs` wraps the existing list. On CUDA sm90 it drops 11 of the 23 configs (old indices 2, 9, 10, 12, 13 to 19). - It keeps the 1-stage wgmma configs: Triton waits on them with `pendings = 0` right after the dot. It keeps the 2-warp and `BLOCK_SIZE_M = 32` configs: they use `mma.sync`, which is synchronous. - Only sm90 has wgmma, so other GPUs keep the full list. `is_cuda()` is needed because ROCm gfx90a also reports capability (9, 0). - The filter is a rule, not a list of configs that failed once. Configs 2, 10 and 12 have the same racy code but gave little or no NaN at the reproducer's shape (12 does not fit there). At dstate 256, config 10 gave NaN in 1 of 20 calls and config 12 in 20 of 20. A TTGIR check of all 23 old configs at dstate 128 and 256 found 0 mismatches between the rule and the racy pattern. - The filter runs when the list is built, not as `early_config_prune`. Triton skips pruning when the list has one config, and `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG` walks `self.configs` without pruning, so pruned configs could still run. - A TTGIR scan of the other Mamba2 SSD kernels (`_bmm_chunk_fwd`, `_chunk_state_fwd`, `_state_passing_fwd`, `_chunk_cumsum_fwd`) found no register-A async wgmma, so only this kernel changes. Reading the diff: `ruff format` re-indents the config list because it is now a function argument. With whitespace hidden (`git diff -w`), the change in `ssd_chunk_scan.py` is about 25 lines. No config is added, removed or edited by hand. Limitations: this works around a Triton bug seen with Triton 3.6.0 (in the issue) and 3.7.1 (here). The new test does not check that non-sm90 platforms keep the full list. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Perf][Core] Skip the null head of sliding-window block tables
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

A sliding-window KV group keeps one null block per out-of-window block, so a long request's block table is almost all null (8,183 of 8,192 entries for a 128K-token prompt with a 128-token window and 16-token blocks). `KVCacheBlocks.get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups` and `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.free` walked every entry in Python. This PR skips that null head.

* `null_head_len()` finds the leading null run by binary search and checks it with one `list.count` of the shared null block. If the null blocks are not one contiguous head, it falls back to a scan.
* `get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups` and `pop_blocks_for_free` (so both `free` and the deferred-free path) start after the head. `free_blocks` skips any other null blocks; the null block's `ref_cnt` is not maintained (see `BlockPool.__init__`).
* No behavior change: the same block ids are collected, and the same blocks reach the free queue in the same order.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `null block sliding window free`, `null_block free_blocks`, `sliding window null blocks` and `get_unhashed_block_ids`. vllm-project/vllm#42276 and #55818 change SWA eviction and allocation, not these walks.

## Where it matters

The cost is paid per sliding-window group, on the scheduler's critical path, each time a request is admitted with async KV loads or freed. It shows up when GPU steps are short and requests turn over quickly, as in **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, WideEP DEP16 decode** (GB300, 64 requests/rank, 169.5K-token prompts):

* A decode step takes ~22 ms on the GPU, and all 16 DP ranks wait for the slowest rank's scheduler.
* Each rank admits and frees ~9 long requests per second.
* Each request has 8 sliding-window groups x 5,298 blocks, 5,292 of them null.

| Scheduler CPU per request | main | PR |
| -- | --: | --: |
| free | 2.0 ms | 0.5 ms |
| async-KV admission (135K prompt) | 0.73 ms | 0.47 ms |

End to end, output throughput went from 8,892 to 9,025 tok/s/GPU **(+1.5%).** 

## Microbenchmark

One request on one sliding-window group (window 128, block size 16): `KVCacheBlocks.get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups` (collect) and `SlidingWindowManager.free` (free). Median of 300 calls on a Grace CPU, main (`8530aed2b7`) vs this PR, consistent across two runs.

| Prompt tokens | Blocks (null) | Collect, main / PR (us) | Free, main / PR (us) |
| -- | -- | --: | --: |
| 32K | 2,048 (2,039) | 54.1 / 9.7 | 92.9 / 10.8 |
| 128K | 8,192 (8,183) | 214.9 / 34.8 | 370.6 / 35.8 |
| 512K | 32,768 (32,759) | 867.5 / 135.9 | 1471.7 / 137.5 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

New test `test_null_head_len`: empty, no-null, all-null, contiguous-head and non-contiguous tables, plus `get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups` on two groups.

## Test Result

312 passed. Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

---

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Support heterogeneous TP in WRITE mode for all attention and mamba layers
author: junkang1991
body:
Fixes #60101. This PR fixes a hang in MoRIIO WRITE-mode disaggregated serving when using MLA models with a smaller tensor-parallel size on prefill than on decode.

For example, with prefill TP2 and decode TP4, the expected mapping is:

- Prefill rank 0 → decode ranks 0 and 1
- Prefill rank 1 → decode ranks 2 and 3

Previously, each prefill rank wrote the KV cache to only the first mapped decode rank. The other decode ranks did not receive their KV cache or completion notification and continued waiting indefinitely.

## Root cause

MoRIIO already calculated the first corresponding remote TP rank, but the WRITE data path treated this as a one-to-one mapping.

That behavior is sufficient for equal TP sizes and mappings that do not require replication. However, the MLA KV cache must be fanned out when the decode TP size is a multiple of and larger than the prefill TP size.

The existing heterogeneous-TP acknowledgement logic expects completion from all corresponding decode ranks, while the WRITE path previously reached only one of them.

## Changes

This PR introduces a small helper, `get_moriio_write_target_tp_ranks`, which extends the existing remote-rank mapping for MLA WRITE fan-out.

When MLA is used and decode TP is larger than prefill TP:

1. Determine the first decode rank using the existing MoRIIO TP-rank mapping.
2. Calculate the required fan-out from the prefill and decode TP sizes.
3. Establish sessions with every corresponding decode rank.
4. Write the KV cache through every target session.
5. Wait for all resulting transfer statuses before completing the request.
6. Send `write_done` to every target decode rank.
7. Send `write_failed` to every affected target if a deferred write times out.

## Scope and compatibility

The fan-out behavior is restricted to:

- MoRIIO WRITE mode
- MLA models
- Prefill TP smaller than decode TP

This change is contained within the vLLM MoRIIO connector and does not require changes to the MoRI library.

Routing is based on TP/DP ranks and the existing endpoint-resolution logic rather than physical node placement. Runtime validation was performed on a single node.

## Unit tests

Added coverage for:

- MLA TP2 → TP4 target mapping
- MLA TP4 → TP8 target mapping
- Equal and decreasing TP mappings
- Non-MLA behavior remaining unchanged
- Creating a write session for every fan-out target
- Accumulating all transfer statuses
- Sending completion notifications to every target
- Sending timeout/failure notifications to every target
- Passing fan-out routing information from the connector to the writer
- Existing DP and multi-pod notification behavior

Command:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_write_done_routing.py
```

Result:

```text
26 passed
```

## Runtime validation

### Environment

- Single AMD MI355X node
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite
- MoRIIO RDMA WRITE mode
- Prefill TP2
- Decode TP4

The router, prefill instance, and decode instance were started in separate terminals.

### Router

```bash
vllm-router \
  --vllm-pd-disaggregation \
  --kv-connector moriio \
  --vllm-discovery-address 0.0.0.0:36367 \
  --port 8402
```

### Prefill instance

```bash
MORI_IO_CP_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 \
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --tensor_parallel_size 2 \
  --port 18400 \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_producer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "rdma",
      "read_mode": false,
      "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
      "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
      "http_port": "18400",
      "handshake_port": "18600",
      "notify_port": "18500"
    }
  }'
```

### Decode instance

```bash
MORI_IO_CP_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 \
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
```

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fill K-padded output in silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant
author: gkswns0531
body:
## Overview

Fixes #48898. Under torch.compile, NVFP4 models whose per-rank MLP width K is 16 mod 32 (e.g. Qwen2.5-72B / Qwen2.5-VL-72B at TP=8, K = 3696) produce garbage once a batch has more than one token. The SiluMul+NVFP4 fusion replaces the K-padded `scaled_fp4_quant` of the CUTLASS NVFP4 linear (#42774) with `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant`, which writes that buffer with the unpadded row pitch. #63382 fixed the padded scale factors of this kernel; the row pitch is what remains.

## Claims

- `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` writes a K-padded output the way `scaled_fp4_quant(..., padded_n=...)` does: row pitch and scale tile from the output width, zero data in the padding.
- Compiled output matches eager again on a padded-K model (perplexity 1290959 → 29.45, eager 29.43).
- Unpadded outputs keep the same addressing, and the kernel is not slower on any of the 24 shapes timed (−13% to +0.3%).

## Validation

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.14.0+cu130. Base is main at 08e3f26, built in the same cmake tree.

| Check | Base | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel test (`test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`) | 10 failed, 20 passed | 30 passed |
| Fusion pass tests (`test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py`, `test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py`) | | 154 passed, 48 skipped |
| GEMM reproducer (K = 3696 → 3712, M = 4): relative error per row vs BF16 | 0.127, **1.533, 1.556, 1.532** | 0.127, 0.134, 0.138, 0.128 (same as unfused) |
| WikiText-2 perplexity, padded K = 4848, eager / compiled | 29.430 / **1290959** | 29.430 / 29.451 |
| Same, unpadded K = 4864, eager / compiled | 24.855 / 24.833 | 24.855 / 24.833 |

The perplexity model is `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with its MLP narrowed to 4848 channels so that `down_proj` needs K padding on one GPU (ModelOpt `NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG`, `--linear-backend cutlass`, 64 test texts).

<details>
<summary>Kernel time</summary>

`silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` in µs per launch: BF16 input, one CUDA graph of 200 launches whose inputs rotate through more than three times the 128 MB L2 (where memory allows), timed with CUDA events, mean of three alternating base/fix rounds; output buffers padded as the fusion allocates them. The base time for K = 3696 is for reference only, since that kernel writes the wrong layout.

| M | K = 3696 → 3712 | K = 4864 | K = 7392 | K = 14336 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.27 → 1.24 | 1.39 → 1.34 | 2.01 → 1.97 | 1.82 → 1.79 |
| 16 | 1.38 → 1.31 | 1.54 → 1.45 | 2.07 → 1.98 | 2.93 → 2.60 |
| 128 | 2.70 → 2.60 | 2.89 → 2.64 | 4.50 → 3.91 | 6.43 → 6.09 |
| 1000 | 11.58 → 11.00 | 14.70 → 14.04 | 23.10 → 20.66 | 39.57 → 39.19 |
| 1024 | 11.90 → 11.35 | 15.02 → 14.27 | 23.36 → 21.11 | 40.67 → 40.19 |
| 8192 | 91.09 → 91.15 | 123.8 → 123.6 | 187.6 → 187.3 | 361.1 → 362.1 |

Both builds use 40 registers per thread.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Commands and GEMM reproducer</summary>

```bash
# Both arms from one build tree (only the kernel file differs)
cmake --build cmake-build-release --target _C_stable_libtorch -j 44

pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py

# Kernel timing: for each (M, K) above, a CUDA graph of 200
#   torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant(out, out_sf, x_i, global_scale) launches over rotating inputs x_i,
#   with out, out_sf from ops.create_fp4_output_tensors(M, K, device, True, padded_n=round_up(K, 32));
#   CUDA-event time of a replay / 200, median of 7 replays

# Model check: LLM(model, quantization="modelopt_fp4", linear_backend="cutlass", enforce_eager=True/False);
#   perplexity from prompt_logprobs over 64 WikiText-2 test texts
```

```python
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_utils import (
    pad_nvfp4_weight_for_cutlass, swizzle_blockscale)

rows, k, n = 4, 3696, 512
x = torch.randn(rows, 2 * k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
weight = torch.randn(n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.02
y = torch.empty(rows, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul(y, x)
w_gs = (448.0 * 6.0 / weight.abs().amax().float()).reshape(1)
w_fp4, w_sf = ops.scaled_fp4_quant(weight, w_gs, is_sf_swizzled_layout=False)
w_sf = swizzle_blockscale(w_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn))
w_fp4, pad = pad_nvfp4_weight_for_cutlass(w_fp4)
x_gs = (448.0 * 6.0 / y.abs().amax().float()).reshape(1)
alpha = 1.0 / (x_gs * w_gs)
eager = ops.scaled_fp4_quant(y, x_gs, padded_n=k + 2 * pad)
fused = ops.create_fp4_output_tensors(rows, k, y.device, True, padded_n=k + 2 * pad)
torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant(*fused, x, x_gs)
ref = y.float() @ weight.float().T
for name, (a, a_sf) in {"eager": eager, "fused": fused}.items():
    out = ops.cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm(a, w_fp4, a_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn), w_sf, alpha, torch.bfloat16)
    print(name, [round(float((out[r].float() - ref[r]).norm() / ref[r].norm()), 3) for r in range(rows)])
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The fused kernel writes into the buffers allocated for the padded quant: `[M, (K + 16) / 2]` data and a 128x4 scale tile. It used K instead of K + 16 as the row pitch, so every row after the first is shifted against its scales. Single-token checks still pass. It also left the padded scale columns and rows unwritten (the stale-column failure analysed in #48898), which #63382 has since fixed.

**Fix.** The launcher passes the output width. The kernel takes the row pitch and the scale tile from it and writes the zeros it already computes for padded positions into the K padding. For an unpadded output the width equals K, so the addressing is the same as before. A `TORCH_CHECK` requires the output width to be a multiple of 16 that holds the input.

**Scope.** In practice only the down_proj input (K = intermediate size / TP) gets padded; the other quant fusions feed K = hidden size or heads × head_dim and are unchanged. Skipping the fusion for padded outputs would be simpler but would drop it on exactly these layers.

**Duplicate check.** #63382 fixed the padded scale factors but not the row pitch, so #48898 still reproduces on main (table above). #49092 and #49093 came out of the same investigation and fix other problems. #59467 (open) rewrites this kernel to add GELU-tanh; whichever lands second carries the padded-output handling, and I can rebase this one onto it.

**CI coverage and limitations.** The kernel test needs SM100+ and is skipped on CI's L4 runners; the `(B200) Fusion and Compile` job runs the two fusion tests. I validated on SM120 only, with a CUDA 13.4 build (16-element path; the 8-element path of CUDA < 12.9 builds has the same change but was not run). The model-level check used the narrowed 0.5B model on one GPU, not a TP=8 72B deployment.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), which traced the root cause, wrote the fix and tests, ran the validation above and drafted this description.

---

title: [Bugfix] Include KV cache quantization settings in IPC weight cache key
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix incorrect KV scales when an engine reuses IPC-cached weights prepared with a different KV cache quantization configuration.

Related to #56049

## Claims

- Detect incompatible KV cache dtype or skipped-layer settings through the existing cache mismatch and fallback handling.
- Retain the KV cache configuration used during initial loading for subsequent standalone weight reloads.

## Validation

Added one parameterized regression test covering dtype mismatches, skipped-layer mismatches, and equivalent skipped-layer lists. It checks initial loading and standalone reloading, including after the caller's configuration is mutated.

- Before: **2 failed, 1 passed**.
- After: **9 passed, 3 deselected**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/model_executor/model_loader \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py \
  -k 'not cold_start_and_warm_restart' -q
```

GPU validation used an H800 NVL, PyTorch `2.14.0+cu130`, and a synthetic FP8 checkpoint derived from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, with BF16 activations, TP=1, eager execution, and the Torch FP8 linear backend. Three prompts were tested with greedy decoding, 32 output tokens, and prompt logprobs.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Before: `auto` daemon → `fp8` engine | Incorrectly accepted cached weights; K/V scales became `1.0` instead of `0.0250244140625`, changing generated tokens for all three prompts |
| After: mismatch, fallback disabled | Raised `CacheConfigMismatchError` naming `kv_cache_dtype` |
| After: mismatch, fallback enabled | Both `zero_copy` and `copy` matched disk loading |
| After: matching `fp8` configurations | Both modes loaded 424 cached tensors and matched disk loading |

For matching configurations and fallback loading, KV scales, generated token IDs, and prompt logprobs matched disk loading exactly. Disk-loading results were unchanged by the fix. These checks validate loading consistency for the tested FP8 path, not model accuracy or all quantization backends.

## Details

The daemon caches tensors after weight processing, which depends on the KV cache configuration. The existing fingerprint includes model quantization settings but omits the KV cache dtype and skipped layers, allowing incompatible processed scales to be reused.

Include `kv_cache_dtype` and `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` in `WeightCacheKey`. Sort and deduplicate skipped layers so equivalent lists still match.

Pass `CacheConfig` when constructing daemon and engine keys. Save a copy on models returned by the IPC loader, including disk fallback, so standalone `load_weights()` calls retain the configuration used during initial loading without requiring an active configuration context. Models without a saved configuration use the current vLLM configuration.

---

title: [Perf] Low-latency CPU all-reduce for DP metadata syncs
author: njhill
body:
This is a refactored version of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60267 from @hjjq.

Main changes from that PR:
- Move out of MRV2 since it's a generic collective, make compatible with elastic ep
- Don't use `batch_isend_irecv` which is actually slower with gloo
- Generalize to any DP size (not just power of 2)
- Also use for the post-step DP state sync
- Remove the env var, just use it unconditionally

---

Gloo's all_reduce on the small CPU tensors used for DP synchronization is latency-bound and grows roughly linearly with the DP size. Add `cpu_all_reduce_()` to `vllm.distributed.utils`: recursive doubling within power-of-two blocks of ranks, then one concurrent exchange between blocks, so any group size completes in log2(largest power-of-two factor) + 1 rounds. Block sums are added in a fixed order, so results are bitwise identical across ranks.

It calls `ProcessGroup.send/recv` with group-local ranks, so it also works with stateless (unregistered) groups such as the engine-core DP group and elastic EP's DP group.

It is used automatically (no env var) for:
- the V2 worker's DP padding/cudagraph sync, via `GroupCoordinator.cpu_all_reduce_()`
- the engine-core DP state sync, `ParallelConfig.sync_dp_state()`

### Performance

Standalone microbenchmark: p50 latency (µs) of an in-place SUM all-reduce of a 6×N int32 CPU tensor (the V2 DP metadata shape) over gloo, one process per rank, on GB200 nodes with gloo over the nodes' Ethernet NIC. Each method was run for 5,000 calls, interleaved in random order; the value is the median across ranks of per-rank p50.

- **gloo**: `dist.all_reduce` (current main)
- **#60267**: the original PR (`VLLM_DP_METADATA_TRANSPORT=gloo-tree`); power-of-two sizes only
- **this PR**: `cpu_all_reduce_`

| nodes | ranks | gloo | #60267 | this PR | speedup vs gloo |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2 | 161 | 121 | **99** | 1.6× |
| 1 | 3 | 326 | n/a | **175** | 1.9× |
| 1 | 4 | 780 | 265 | **224** | 3.5× |
| 1 | 5 | 566 | n/a | **266** | 2.1× |
| 1 | 6 | 695 | n/a | **252** | 2.8× |
| 1 | 7 | 850 | n/a | **365** | 2.3× |
| 1 | 8 | 1690 | 377 | **326** | 5.2× |
| 1 | 9 | 1094 | n/a | **459** | 2.4× |
| 1 | 11 | 2379 | n/a | **695** | 3.4× |
| 1 | 12 | 2749 | n/a | **400** | 6.9× |
| 1 | 15 | 3920 | n/a | **1042** | 3.8× |
| 2 | 2 | 308 | 146 | **129** | 2.4× |
| 2 | 4 | 845 | 271 | **234** | 3.6× |
| 2 | 6 | 1366 | n/a | **344** | 4.0× |
| 2 | 8 | 1977 | 413 | **362** | 5.5× |
| 2 | 10 | 2563 | n/a | **444** | 5.8× |
| 2 | 12 | 3005 | n/a | **536** | 5.6× |
| 4 | 4 | 1114 | 281 | **267** | 4.2× |
| 4 | 8 | 2560 | 459 | **409** | 6.3× |
| 4 | 12 | 3806 | n/a | **482** | 7.9× |
| 4 | 16 | 5354 | 604 | **546** | 9.8× |

Where #60267 applies (power-of-two sizes), this PR has 5–18% lower latency. Gloo's latency grows roughly linearly with the number of ranks, while this PR adds about one round per doubling plus one round for the odd factor.

Correctness: `tests/distributed/test_cpu_all_reduce.py` (sizes 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12; exact match vs `dist.all_reduce`, bitwise-identical float results across ranks, and a stateless process group). `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py` with DP=4 passes with the multiprocessing backend (ray backend not tested).

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Remap Quark layer names for the MTP draft model
author: tpopp
body:
## Overview

Previously, `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` with MTP would fail with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1280) must match the size of tensor b (2560)`.

Remap Quark's layer names (`exclude`, `layer_quant_config`) for the Qwen4Exp MTP draft (both AMD and NVIDIA copies) so that checkpoint names (`mtp.layers.0.*`) match the draft's layer names (`mtp.layers.48.*`), the same way `ignored_layers`, `exclude_modules` and ModelOpt `quantized_layers` are already remapped (#55513) in both copies.

Related checkpoint fix:https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4/commit/89d245391842bf53fb9b0700646843c1f40de341.

**Checkpoint status:** AMD has updated `config.json` on both `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` and the `-PLEFP8` sibling with literal `mtp.layers.0.*` names only -- no catch-all regex -- matching the convention other AMD checkpoints use (e.g. `amd/Qwen3.5-397B`). Per AMD's confirmation on the checkpoint discussion linked above and the model card's own Reproduction section: without MTP, the formal `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0` release runs the checkpoint as documented; with MTP enabled, that release does not remap Quark's exclude list for the draft, so this PR is required for MTP to load at all -- this is the checkpoint as shipped, not a hypothetical variant.

## Claims

- Bug fix: with a Quark checkpoint whose `exclude` list names MTP modules by checkpoint index (the form Quark exports), BF16 MTP layers are no longer built as quantized layers.
- Per-layer Quark schemes (`layer_quant_config`) for MTP modules are applied to the draft as well.
- No functional change for the target model, for no-MTP serving, or for ModelOpt checkpoints.
- Also fixes the identical bug on the NVIDIA backend: MXFP4 has real NVIDIA-native MoE backends (FlashInfer, vLLM CUTLASS, DeepGEMM, Marlin -- not just AMD's AITER path), so a Quark-quantized checkpoint with MTP hit the same dead-exclude-list bug there. Flagged by @okorzh-amd's review; same fix, ported to `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/mtp.py`.
- Scope: entries in Quark `exclude` and keys of `layer_quant_config` that **start with** `mtp.layers.<i>.` (for `i < mtp_num_hidden_layers`) are rewritten to `mtp.layers.<mtp_start_layer_idx + i>.`; this includes globs such as `mtp.layers.0.*`. Entries that start with `re:` or `*`, and non-MTP names, are left exactly as written, matching the existing `ignored_layers`/`exclude_modules`/`quantized_layers` remaps.

## Validation

**Unit test (CPU)**

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py   # 15 passed
```

`test_qwen4_exp_mtp_remaps_quark_layer_names`, parametrized over `backend` (`amd`/`nvidia`, matching the existing `test_qwen4_exp_mtp_remaps_mixed_precision_layer_indices` convention), builds the draft config from a `QuarkConfig` and checks that MTP names in `exclude` and `layer_quant_config` shift to layer 48, non-MTP and `re:` entries are unchanged, and the checkpoint's list is not mutated. It also asserts the actual `get_quant_method_target` decision for the draft's routed experts (`UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, not the quantized MoE method), using an `exclude` fixture whose only regex entry (`re:mtp\.fc_hidden`) does not match the experts path on its own -- a broader catch-all regex would mask the bug this assertion exists to catch (see Scope above). Verified locally (and re-verified by removing the `apply_vllm_mapper` call on both backends) that the exclude-list assertion is what catches the bug: it fails cleanly without the fix and passes with it, on both backends.

**End to end (MI355X, TP2)**

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8f7` with this PR. Checkpoint `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`. GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions; acceptance length (AL) over the GSM8K run, MTP k=3. Also confirmed on NVIDIA B300: this fix resolves the identical error with similar results to the MI355X run below. B300 additionally needed an out-of-scope workaround for a separate Quark/Qwen4Exp weight-conversion gap with the CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP4 MoE backend, tracked separately and not part of this PR; the NVIDIA fix itself is also covered by the parametrized unit test above, same code path as the AMD side.

| Checkpoint `exclude` | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| exact MTP module names only (as Quark exports) | fails to load: `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1280) must match the size of tensor b (2560)` | loads; GSM8K 0.923 / 0.916; AL 3.52 (0.928 / 0.845 / 0.748) |

GSM8K is flexible-extract / strict-match (±0.007); AL per draft position in parentheses. With exact names only, the server log reports `Quark excludes shared experts at mtp.layers.48.mlp.shared_expert`, i.e. the checkpoint's `mtp.layers.0.*` entries now reach the draft.

No-MTP reference on the same setup: GSM8K 0.927 / 0.921 (flexible / strict).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --served-model-name qfn \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=qfn,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The AMD Qwen4Exp draft builds its layers as `mtp.layers.<num_hidden_layers + i>`, while checkpoints name them `mtp.layers.<i>`. `_make_draft_vllm_config` shifts the checkpoint names in `ignored_layers`, `exclude_modules` and `quantized_layers`, but `QuarkConfig` keeps its layer names inside `quant_config` (`exclude`, `layer_quant_config`), which was not touched. Every literal MTP entry there was dead for the draft, so `QuarkConfig.get_quant_method` fell through to the global scheme (MXFP4) for BF16 MTP modules.

**Fix.** Rename them through Quark's existing hook for this, `QuarkConfig.apply_vllm_mapper`, with a `WeightsMapper` prefix map `mtp.layers.<i>.` -> `mtp.layers.<num_hidden_layers + i>.`. The mapper is built in the draft rather than declared as a class-level `hf_to_vllm_mapper` because the target index depends on `num_hidden_layers`.

**Why keep the layer offset.** Qwen3-Next removed the same offset in #25079 and Qwen3.5 builds its MTP layer as `mtp.layers.{idx}` (#34110), so their checkpoint names match without a remap. Qwen4Exp's offset (introduced with the model in #53896) is now relied on: #60023 documents `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48` to keep only the MTP layer's KV cache unquantized, and that option selects layers by index; the offset also keeps index-keyed PLE layer assignment (`ple_layer_ids`) off the draft. Renumbering would change both silently, so this PR keeps the offset and completes the existing remap.

**Scope.** AMD and NVIDIA Qwen4Exp MTP drafts; Quark only.

**Related.** Not duplicated by: #49900 (strips the synthetic `draft_model.` root for draft-model drafters), #59040 (`mtp.fc` in `qwen3_5_mtp.py`).

**CI.** The unit test runs on CPU in the existing Qwen4Exp test file. The end-to-end validation above was run outside CI.

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip the TRTLLM fp8-block activation-scale transpose copy
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Overview

Skip the per-layer `a1q_scale.t().contiguous()` copy between per-token-group FP8 quantization and the FlashInfer TRTLLM fp8-block MoE experts by emitting the scales in the layout the experts consume. This is pure plumbing on top of the quant kernel's existing `column_major_scales` mode — no kernel changes. ~2% TPOT improvement at concurrency 4 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (TP4+EP).

## Claims

- Removes one `direct_copy_kernel` per MoE layer per decode step (24/step -> 0 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) from the critical path.
- ~2% TPOT p50 improvement at concurrency 4 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP on 4xGB300; parity at concurrency 1 (details below).
- Bitwise-identical expert inputs: the scale bytes are the same values, just allocated in the final physical layout, so there is no accuracy impact.
- Python-only change (+77/-14 across 5 files, mostly the test).

## Validation

### Correctness

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py`: 49 passed (+2 mxfp8 skips), including the new `transposed` arm of `test_trtllm_fp8_block_moe_deferred_finalize`, which builds the quant config through the production oracle + `no_dp_ep` path, asserts the prepared activation scale is column-major (`a1q_scale.t().is_contiguous()`), and asserts bitwise-equal expert output against the non-transposed baseline.
- No new test for the `column_major_scales` wrapper mode itself: it is a pre-existing feature already exercised by the CUTLASS/DeepGEMM/FlashInfer/PyTorch scaled-mm kernels on every CUDA run and by existing fusion/eplb tests.

### Profiler evidence

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP, decode step trace:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `per_token_group_quant` launches / step | 24 | 24 |
| `direct_copy_kernel` launches / step | 24 | 0 |

### E2E perf

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP on 4xGB300, `vllm bench serve`, 2048 input / 256 output, `--ignore-eos`. main (`f46021a7fa`) and the branch (`9f75804588`) ran sequentially on the same node, two server instances each:

| Concurrency | main TPOT p50 (ms) | this PR TPOT p50 (ms) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.92-3.93 | parity (see below) | ~0% |
| 4 | 5.11-5.12 | 4.98-5.00 | -2.3% |

TPOT p99 at concurrency 4 improves from 5.67-6.04 ms to 5.57-5.58 ms. Concurrency-1 serve numbers were noisy across instances, so c=1 was A/B'd with interleaved `vllm bench latency` (bs=1, 2048/128): 0.756/0.704 s (this PR) vs 0.756/0.800 s (main) — no regression, as expected since the eliminated copies are nearly free inside a bs=1 CUDA graph.

## Details

- Root cause: the TRTLLM fp8-block kernels consume activation scales in the physical `[K/128, M]` (scale-major) layout, while the MoE per-token-group quant emits `[M, K/128]` row-major, so every layer paid a transpose copy between the quant kernel and the experts.
- The quant kernel's existing `column_major_scales=True` mode already allocates the scale buffer as a contiguous `[G, M]` tensor viewed as `[M, G]`, so on that buffer the experts' `.t().contiguous()` is a no-op returning the same tensor. The change just threads a new `FusedMoEQuantConfig.is_scale_transposed` flag — set by the fp8 oracle only for `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` + `[128, 128]` blocks — through `no_dp_ep` into `moe_kernel_quantize_input`. TRTLLM expert code is unchanged.
- Scope: only `no_dp_ep` forwards the flag; dispatch-based paths (deepep, naive-dp, fi-nvl) keep row-major scales since their scales cross an all2all dispatch. Other MoE backends are unaffected.
- No accuracy eval: the scale bytes handed to the experts are bitwise-identical (same values, different physical layout), so outputs cannot change; the e2e runs above exercised the modified path at c=1-4.
- Duplicate-work check: nearest open PRs inspected — #59564 (value-only amax reduction inside the quant kernel, orthogonal), #53345 (deepep ep_scatter scale-stride bugfix), #44034 (XPU quant fallback); none touch the MoE activation-scale layout.

AI assistance: Kimi Code helped develop, benchmark, and validate this change.

title: [Bugfix] Validate draft-token capacity in forward benchmark
author: znzryb
body:
## Overview

Validate draft-token capacity in `vllm bench forward` before preparing a case's inputs. Fixes #61766: a verify case requiring three draft tokens currently reaches CUDA execution even when the runner has zero draft capacity.

## Claims

- Reject cases whose draft count exceeds the runner's resolved `num_speculative_steps`, with a case-specific `ValueError` and a `--speculative-config` hint.
- Preserve execution for ordinary decode and verify cases with sufficient capacity.
- Cover missing and insufficient capacity in the existing benchmark test suite, and document the requirement in the microbenchmark skill.

## Validation

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selected benchmark regression tests | 2 failed, 2 passed | 4 passed, 1 deselected |
| L4: `verify=2*4@64:3`, no speculative config | CUDA illegal memory access | Expected `ValueError`, no illegal memory access |
| L4: `decode=2*1@64` | Passed | Passed |
| L4: same verify, configured draft capacity 3 | Passed | Passed |

The patched GPU controls use the same publicly exported random Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint. Both successful cases have finite, deterministic outputs and graph-versus-eager relative RMS difference 0. These are correctness smoke checks, not model-quality or performance measurements.

The existing model-dependent pytest end-to-end case was deselected; three separate benchmark CLI runs provided GPU coverage. New tests live in `tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py`, already included in the Buildkite benchmarks CLI job.

Commands executed (validation scripts are in the separate archive branch):

```bash
UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-audit-uv-cache uv run --no-project --python 3.12 \
  --with 'modal[api-proxy-support]' --with huggingface_hub \
  modal run reproductions/forward-verify-2026-10-15/validate_modal.py::check \
  --model-revision 4bae0ac45199180f8d59d05bb3b6cc1b19c58357

UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-audit-uv-cache PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/vllm-audit-precommit \
  uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with pre-commit \
  pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py .agents/skills/model-microbenchmark/SKILL.md
```

Pre-commit passed, including Ruff, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, and skill validation.

Environment: one NVIDIA L4 on Modal, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Python source at `c5f8adc0b1944b9142a31d85cfbc6a61973d0b3a` was overlaid on compiled extensions and generated wrappers from an official vLLM image reporting `0.32.0rc1.dev100+g77154ca61`. This is composite source/runtime validation, not a full build from that source commit. Source/runtime provenance is recorded separately in the archive.

- [Scripts, original logs, synthetic inputs, and validation receipts](https://github.com/znzryb/vllm/tree/contribution-rules-and-bug-audit/reproductions/forward-verify-2026-10-15)
- [Public random checkpoint, pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/znzryb/qwen3-0.6b-dummy-forward-repro/tree/4bae0ac45199180f8d59d05bb3b6cc1b19c58357)
- [Public raw data and validation logs, pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/datasets/znzryb/vllm-forward-verify-repro/tree/239159c4fdaaf568fe9c00153cbfbf57ab1bf8bc)

## Details

The benchmark builds scheduler inputs directly. Without speculative configuration, the observed runner has `num_speculative_steps=0` and a draft-token buffer of shape `[4, 0]`, yet the verify case schedules three draft tokens per request. The missing consistency check lets this invalid combination enter GPU input preparation. CUDA errors are asynchronous; no exact faulting kernel is claimed.

The guard runs at the start of `run_case`, before batch construction and input preparation, using resolved runner capacity rather than requiring a particular CLI configuration. Engine initialization still precedes the check. This is benchmark configuration validation; it does not change a CUDA kernel or repair computation under a valid configuration.

Duplicate checks: read #61766 and searched open PRs for the issue number and `bench forward`. No overlapping fix was found. #61692 adds profiling, not draft-capacity validation. The three affected files are unchanged on the latest upstream main checked before submission.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Stop declaring the MXFP4 MoE intermediate padding to AITER
author: PerryZhang01
body:
## Purpose

The AMD CI job `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` goes red intermittently with

```
AssertionError: (0, 1, (973, 973), 'residual', nan)
```

(e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94971). The NaN comes from AITER, on
vLLM's ordinary MoE path, not from the mono kernels the test compares against.

AITER's a8w4 MoE (FP8 activations x MXFP4 weights) allocates several scratch
buffers with `torch.empty`, sized for the padded sorted length, and reads them
where the producing kernel never wrote. In FP8/E8M0 a garbage `0xFF` byte is
NaN, so a whole token row of the output comes back NaN. It only happens with a
non-zero `intermediate_pad`, at decode-sized batches, after larger calls have
run in the same process — which is why it shows up as a flaky decode failure.
Root cause, a standalone repro and a fix are filed upstream:

- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/6565
- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6568

## This change

Stop declaring `intermediate_pad` to AITER on the MXFP4 path. It is redundant
there, and dropping it keeps the call off the buggy AITER path.

Why it is redundant — the padded region is zero at the point AITER sees it, and
stays zero through every step between allocation and the kernel call:

| step | padded region | where |
|---|---|---|
| allocation | `torch.zeros` for `w13`/`w2`, their scales and `w13_bias`/`w2_bias`, at the **padded** intermediate size | `Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` |
| checkpoint load | the destination is narrowed to the loaded shard before the copy, so the padded rows are never written — this is deliberate, the helper is named for it and its docstring calls out "padding ... on the shard (intermediate) dimension (e.g. for MXFP4 GEMM)" | `RoutedExperts._narrow_expert_data_for_padding`, used by `_load_w13` / `_load_w2` right before `expert_data.copy_()` |
| weight shuffle | pure `view` + `permute` (asserts `N % 16 == 0`, `K % 32 == 0`, no re-padding), so zeros stay zeros | `aiter.ops.shuffle.shuffle_weight` |
| scale shuffle | re-pads the scale to 256 rows / 8 cols, but fills the pad with `0x7F` (E8M0 = 1.0) before copying, so it is never garbage | `aiter.utility.fp4_utils.e8m0_shuffle` |

So for the padded columns the kernel computes

- stage 1: `x @ 0 = 0` (gate and up are both zero there, and the bias is zero,
  so the activation output is exactly `silu(0) * 0 = 0`)
- stage 2: `0 @ 0 = 0`

Exact zeros also mean the padded columns cannot disturb the stage-2 activation
quantization: `amax` over an MX group is unaffected by zeros, whether or not a
group straddles real and padded columns.

Two things are deliberately left alone:

- **`hidden_pad`** — the activation columns it covers are not guaranteed to be
  zero, so dropping it would not be equivalent.
- **SITU** (`activation == MoEActivation.SITU`, the a16w4 FlyDSL port used by
  Kimi K3) — that kernel consumes the pad. The surrounding code already skips
  the rounding for it ("SITU's A16W4 FlyDSL kernel pads per gate/up half; pass
  through unrounded"), and on that path AITER keys its own scratch
  initialization on the value: `_alloc = torch.zeros if inter_dim_pad > 0 else
  torch.empty` in `aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`. Zeroing the declaration
  there would *remove* an initialization that is currently happening, which is
  the opposite of what this PR is for.

This is a workaround and should be reverted once the AITER fix is merged and
pinned. The surrounding code already carries a similar TODO about AITER padding
behaviour.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, stock AITER 0.1.25 — i.e. **without** the
AITER-side fix — running `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` unmodified,
each run covering TP2 and TP4:

| build | runs | cells | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| exactly this patch | 4 | 8 | **all passed** |
| same logic, earlier iterations of the comment/wording | 10 | 20 | **all passed** |

14 runs, 28 cells, no NaN. Before the change the same test failed intermittently
— locally about 2 runs in 6 — so 14 clean runs is about 0.3% likely if the
change did nothing.

Overhead: none measurable. Timing the same shape with and without the
declaration (median over 6 rounds, per `fused_moe_2stages` call):

| M | declared | not declared |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.139 ms | 0.141 ms |
| 4 | 0.156 ms | 0.158 ms |
| 1439 | 0.534 ms | 0.536 ms |
| 16384 | 2.010 ms | 2.010 ms |

All within run-to-run noise (~4%).

## Scope and limits

- Validated on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 (`model_dim=5120`, per-rank
  intermediate 576 padded to 640, E=384, topk=6). Other MXFP4 models on this
  path (e.g. gpt-oss with INTERLEAVE) are covered by the same zero-fill
  argument but were not run here, so reviewers may prefer a narrower gate.
- The zero-fill chain above is established from the code, with the citations in
  the table. It is not confirmed by a run against a real MXFP4 checkpoint that
  actually has padding: the test that exercises this path uses a random-weight
  loader which also zero-fills the padding, and every MXFP4 checkpoint we have
  locally has `moe_intermediate_size = 2048`, which is already aligned per rank
  (pad = 0). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (2304) is the one that pads, and the local copy
  of it is FP8 rather than MXFP4.
- Models whose per-rank intermediate size is already 128-aligned get
  `intermediate_pad == 0` and are unaffected either way.
- The `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4` opt-in is a sub-case of
  `use_mxfp4_w4a16`, so it is covered by this change as well. The same
  zero-fill argument applies to it, but it runs different kernels and was not
  exercised here.

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Overlap the unfused shared expert with AITER MegaMoE
author: benenzhu
body:
## Overview

With `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` and an unfused shared expert, DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm ran the shared expert after the router and MegaMoE, on the main stream. This PR runs it on the aux stream next to the router + MegaMoE through `maybe_execute_in_parallel`. It follows the existing `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM` / `VLLM_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` convention: the overlap applies to steps of at most 256 tokens by default, and `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=1` keeps the serial order. ATOM overlaps its shared expert with the routed experts the same way.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro, AgentX agentic workload: P90 interactivity +2.7% at concurrency 128 and +6.4% at concurrency 64.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k.
- Prefill-sized steps and the fused shared-expert path are unchanged.

## Validation

Setup:
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, DP8 attention + EP8 AITER MegaMoE, shared expert unfused.
- AgentX agentic workload, 1200 s runs, requests counted in the 300-1200 s window.
- Single runs per configuration.

| | Without | With this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| c128 (same node, same job): P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 27.13 | 27.87 (+2.7%) |
| c128: output tok/s/GPU | 335 | 346 (+3.3%) |
| c128: total tok/s/GPU | | +1.4% |
| c64 (same node, separate jobs): P90 interactivity | 48.26 | 51.33 (+6.4%) |
| c64: P50 interactivity | 61.65 | 64.31 (+4.3%) |
| c64: total tok/s/GPU | | -1.5% |
| gsm8k 5-shot, real speculative decoding (flexible / strict) | 0.9697 / 0.9704 | 0.9727 / 0.9735 |

Unit tests and lint:
- `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` on MI355X: 10 passed, against 6 on main. The 4 new cases run the shared expert on the aux stream.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed, mypy included. This was rerun on the current main, which includes #61262.

## Details

- When MegaMoE fuses the shared expert, `shared_experts` is `None` and the routed path runs alone, as before.
- `maybe_execute_in_parallel` falls back to sequential execution when the stream is `None` and during breakable CUDA graph capture.
- #61262's runtime selection runs inside the MegaMoE call on the main stream, so it is not affected.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Add the bias in the SM120 NVFP4 CUTLASS GEMM epilogue
author: gkswns0531
body:
## Overview

NVFP4 linears add the bias in a separate kernel after the GEMM. When the output goes straight to the attention custom op (the QKV projection of BERT/XLM-R and Qwen2-style models), Inductor cannot fuse that add, and on large prefills it costs more than the GEMM. This PR adds an optional `bias` to `cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm`, applied in the SM120 epilogue (CUTLASS `LinCombPerColBias`) as the FP8 CUTLASS path already does, and passes it from `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`.

## Claims

- The SM120 epilogue add costs 0.007 ms on an 81920 x 3072 x 1024 GEMM, vs 0.749 ms for a separate `out + bias`.
- `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` passes the bias to the GEMM on SM12x unless N is padded.
- `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` NVFP4 with `linear_backend="cutlass"`: 12-13% less GPU time per batch on an RTX PRO 6000.

## Validation

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.13.0+cu130.

- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_scaled_mm.py`: 28 passed, 14 of them with a bias.

bge-reranker-v2-m3 (ModelOpt `NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG`, classifier excluded), `linear_backend="cutlass"`, GPU kernel time of one `classify` call on 128 sequences; two alternating rounds per arm agree within 0.1 ms:

| | 128 x 640 tokens | 128 x 320 tokens |
|---|---|---|
| main (separate bias add) | 135.1 ms | 60.4 ms |
| this PR | **119.1 ms** | **52.5 ms** |

The QKV bias kernels (16.1 ms at 640 tokens) disappear and the GEMMs take 0.4 ms longer; Inductor already fuses the other bias adds into the next LayerNorm or GELU kernel. Recall@10 on 60 questions each of Ko-StrategyQA / MIRACL-ko: 0.898 / 0.941 vs 0.881 / 0.950 (one question or less either way); mean |logit − FP32| 0.675 / 0.702 vs 0.676 / 0.695.

<details>
<summary>GEMM microbenchmark and commands</summary>

bge-reranker-v2-m3 GEMMs at 128 x 640 tokens, FP16 output:

| M x N x K | GEMM | GEMM + bias epilogue | `out + bias` alone | max diff vs separate add |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 81920 x 3072 x 1024 (QKV) | 0.447 ms | 0.454 ms | 0.749 ms | 0.0039 |
| 81920 x 1024 x 1024 (attn out) | 0.163 ms | 0.164 ms | 0.265 ms | 0.0039 |
| 81920 x 4096 x 1024 (FFN up) | 0.593 ms | 0.599 ms | 0.991 ms | 0.0039 |
| 81920 x 1024 x 4096 (FFN down) | 0.476 ms | 0.478 ms | 0.265 ms | 0.0078 |

The difference is one FP16 rounding of the GEMM output before the add.

```python
# GEMM: median of flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, cold_l2_cache=True, use_cuda_graph=True) for
#   fn = lambda: ops.cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm(x_fp4, w_fp4, x_sf, w_sf, alpha, torch.float16, bias=bias)  # or bias=None
#   fn = lambda: out + bias

# Model: VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1, prefix caching off. The main arm runs this branch with
# bias_epilogue forced to False in CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel, which is main's code path.
llm = LLM(nvfp4_checkpoint, runner="pooling", dtype="float16", linear_backend="cutlass")
# torch.profiler around one llm.classify call on 128 prompts; sum of CUDA kernel time
```

</details>

## Details

**Kernel.** `Fp4GemmSm120` gets a `HasBias` template flag that switches the epilogue from `LinearCombination` to `LinCombPerColBias` (D = alpha * acc + bias[n]); the dispatch instantiates both and picks one by whether a bias is passed.

**Default backend.** SM120 selects `FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` first, and FlashInfer's `mm_fp4` takes no bias (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2290, closed as not planned), so this helps where `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` is selected. On bge both backends' GEMMs take about the same time, so `cutlass` becomes the faster choice there; the default stays because FlashInfer's autotuned GEMM is faster on Qwen3-4B decode shapes.

**Limitations.** SM100 is unchanged because I could not test it: its kernel rejects a bias, and the linear keeps the separate add there. CI has no SM12x runner, so the bias test cases are skipped in CI.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR adds a bias to `cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm` or to the NVFP4 linear kernels.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), which wrote the change and tests, ran the validation above and drafted this description.

title: [CI/Build] Build DeepEP for SM103 (B300/GB300) in the Docker image
author: ibrahimnd2000
body:
## Overview

The Docker image builds DeepEP for `9.0a 10.0a` only, so DeepEP cannot run on SM103 (B300/GB300). This adds `10.3a` to DeepEP's arch list when building with CUDA >= 12.9.

## Claims

- `--all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput` (and the other DeepEP backends) work on SM103 GPUs with the image's DeepEP.
- No change for CUDA < 12.9 builds (12.8 has no SM103 target) or for other GPUs: `9.0a` and `10.0a` cubins are unchanged.

## Validation

On 8x B300 (SM103, driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, NVSHMEM 3.4.5), DeepEP at the image's commit (`d4f41e4e`) built with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST='10.0a 10.3a'`, replacing the DeepEP wheel in `vllm/vllm-openai` v0.31.0:

| Check | Stock image DeepEP (`9.0a 10.0a`) | With `10.3a` |
|---|---|---|
| `cuobjdump --list-elf deep_ep/_C*.so` | `sm_90a`, `sm_100a` | `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` |
| `tests/legacy/test_intranode.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 4096 --hidden 6144 --num-topk 8 --num-experts 256` | n/a (kernels cannot launch) | 24/24 dispatch/combine checks pass (BF16/FP8, sync/async); best dispatch FP8 0.41 ms, combine 0.67 ms |
| `vllm serve` GLM-5.3 FP8, prefill context parallel 8 + EP 8, `--all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput` | startup fails: `CUDA runtime exception (DeepEP/csrc/kernels/legacy/intranode.cu:21): 999 (cudaErrorUnknown)` | starts with `DeepEPHTAll2AllManager`; greedy answers match the default all2all backend on a fixed prompt set |

Version gating of the shell snippet (`CUDA_VERSION` from the stage):

```
CUDA 12.8.1 -> 9.0a 10.0a
CUDA 12.9.1 -> 9.0a 10.0a 10.3a
CUDA 13.0.3 -> 9.0a 10.0a 10.3a
```

Not done: a full rebuild of this Dockerfile (the change only alters the DeepEP arch list passed to `install_python_libraries.sh`). CI has no SM103 runners, so this path is not exercised in CI. `pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile` passes (with `update-dockerfile-graph` skipped locally: the stage graph is unchanged).

## Details

- Root cause: arch-specific (`a`) cubins only run on their exact compute capability, and DeepEP's build embeds no PTX, so `sm_100a` code does not load on SM103 (10.3). The failure surfaces as `cudaErrorUnknown` (999) from DeepEP's legacy intranode/layout kernels at the first dispatch.
- `10.3a` requires CUDA 12.9+, hence the gate on `CUDA_VERSION`; the default image is CUDA 13.0.
- Build time grows by one more arch for DeepEP only (its wheel is built in parallel with the csrc build).
- Performance is not a claim of this PR. On the configuration above, a closed-loop real-prompt prefill load (12 and 24 requests in flight, unique prompt prefixes, `cached_tokens` = 0) measured, in prompt tokens/s: `allgather_reducescatter` with FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE 60.4k / 60.7k, `deepep_high_throughput` (which selects DeepGEMM MoE) 56.5k / 56.9k, `deepep_v2` with FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE 54.0k / 62.2k (the first run includes DeepEP v2 JIT warm-up). Single runs on one node. An earlier version of this description cited a DeepEP gain; that comparison was inflated by prefix-cache hits from repeated prompts and is withdrawn.

author: Thangnguyenvn98

Takes over #61473 (Kevin's batch 1), rebased onto main. This PR only enables `automatic_shard`; it changes no tests.

- The AMD mirror: rendered with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and in main's OTel mode; every test ran in exactly one shard. It is optional like its step, so it needs the same scoped build.
