title: [ROCm][Perf] Any-shape low-latency MoE router GEMM on MI355
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

On MI355 (gfx950), the MoE router GEMM now has a low-latency kernel for **any** router shape (fp32 or bf16 weights, fp32 output, M ≤ 32), matching the CuTeDSL `ll_fp32w` / `ll_bf16` router kernels from #44343 and #50174. Previously only five hard-coded `(hidden_size, num_experts)` shapes had a fast path; every other model paid 9–13 µs per MoE layer per decode step in `F.linear` / hipBLASLt.

## Claims

- **Decode 1–14% faster** on all 8 tested MoE models whose router path changes, largest at low concurrency.
- **No accuracy change**: GSM8K matches `main` on every model (paired McNemar p = 1.0 and 0.34 where runs varied most).
- **No regressions**: prefill, an unchanged-path control (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and the 5 previously tuned shapes stay flat; shapes where the kernel would lose keep today's path.
- **New MI355 CI job** mirroring `(B200) Gate Linear CuTeDSL Kernels`.

Changes:

- Generalize `rocm_fp32_router_gemm` to any shape: masked K tail, MI355-swept launch rule, bf16 weights, size guards
- `GateLinear`: enable the fp32 router tier on gfx950 for any shape and route bf16-weight fp32-logit gates (tier 6) through the same dispatch op
- Extend `test_rocm_fp32_router_gemm.py` and fix the now-outdated rejection test in `test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py`
- Add `:amd: (MI355) Gate Linear Router Kernels` (B200 mirror + optional `test-amd.yaml` entry) and move the 3 ROCm router test files there from MI355 Misc

## Validation

`main` vs this PR, end to end on MI355 (decode TPOT Δ, + is faster; median of 5 reps):

| Model | Router | Decode Δ C1 / C8 / C32 | GSM8K main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B | fp32 2560×64 | **+14.1 / +3.4 / +2.1%** | 86.58 → 86.28 |
| Trinity-Nano | fp32 1024×128 | **+9.6 / +4.9 / +4.0%** | 79.08 → 79.00 |
| Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 | fp32 2688×128 | **+9.4 / +5.4 / +2.2%** | 90.96 / 90.69 (A/A) → 90.83 |
| Ling-mini-2.0 | fp32 2048×256 | **+7.7 / +4.6 / +2.5%** | 88.02 → 88.10 |
| GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 (TP2) | fp32 4096×128 | **+5.0 / +5.0 / +2.9%** | 72.33 → 72.02 |
| Step-3.5-Flash-FP8 (TP2) | fp32 4096×288 | **+4.7 / +3.1 / +2.7%** | 89.61 → 89.31 |
| Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | bf16 2816×128 | **+8.9 / +5.5 / +3.5%** | 94.31 → 94.39 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2) | bf16 4096×256 | **+2.0 / +1.2 / +1.0%** | 95.80 → 95.86 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (control) | unchanged | −0.2 / 0.0 / +0.2% | 91.66 → 91.58 |

8K prefill TTFT is flat on every model (within ±0.7%).

<details>
<summary>Methodology and accuracy details</summary>

- `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, prefix caching off, 1–8 input / 256–512 output tokens. `main` and the PR were served at the same time on separate GPUs, alternating every run, with GPU load logged each rep.
- GSM8K: lm_eval 5-shot chat, median of 3+ runs.
- Nemotron and DeepSeek-V4 were re-run with `--log_samples` for a paired per-question test. Nemotron PR vs `main`: 9 / 9 discordant, McNemar p = 1.0; `main` vs `main` A/A: 9 / 6, p = 0.61. DeepSeek-V4: 3 / 7 in the PR's favor, p = 0.34. An earlier DeepSeek-V4 round read 96.06 → 95.53; the repeat did not reproduce it.
- ERNIE's −0.7% prefill is within the 0.3–0.5% spread between GPUs, which a GPU-swap A/B confirmed. Trinity's prefill TTFT ranges overlap.
- **Why decode improves:** one router GEMM per MoE layer per step drops from 9–13 µs (`F.linear`) or 5–11 µs (hipBLASLt) to 1.9–4.9 µs at ≤ 8 tokens, saving 0.2–0.6 ms per step. Prefill and large batches never reach the kernel.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Kernel benchmark</summary>

MI355, one idle GPU, median of 30 graph replays, 2 runs with ≤5% drift. M = 1–32.

| | Shapes | vs today's path |
|---|---|---|
| fp32, the 5 old shapes | 5 | 0.97–1.30× vs old tuned configs (median 1.07×) |
| fp32, new shapes (DeepSeek-V3, Kimi-K2, Qwen3, Qwen3.8, gpt-oss, Llama4) | 7 | **1.2–6.8×** vs `F.linear` (median 4.1×) |
| fp32, held out from the sweep (GLM-4.5, Ernie, 1000×100, 1024 experts, …) | 10 | **1.1–7.0×**; two 1024-expert M=32 cases keep `F.linear` |
| bf16 | 9 | **1.7–5.4×** vs hipBLASLt at M ≤ 8, 1.04–2.9× at 16–32; never slower |

Max relative error vs float64: 1.3e-7 (fp32 weights), 8.9e-8 (bf16 weights).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- New CI command `pytest -v -s tests/kernels/test_rocm_fp32_router_gemm.py tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py tests/kernels/test_bf16x3_router_gemm_rocm.py`: 847 passed, 10/10 loops, ~5 min each.
- Each new test fails against a mutated kernel or dispatcher: no K-tail mask, the old shape list, a bypassed dispatcher, no bf16 cutoff, or no gfx950 tier-6 routing.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Design details, scope and related PRs</summary>

- **Launch rule:** one program computes `BLOCK_M` tokens for one expert. Narrow routers (< 64 experts) keep `BLOCK_M = 1`; wide routers grow it with the token count. Fitted on 12 shapes, checked on 10 held-out shapes: within 1.11× of the per-shape best and faster than the fallback everywhere.
- **Size guards:** at M·N·K ≥ 2^27 (fp32) or tokens × experts > 8192 (bf16) the fallback is faster, so the kernel declines and today's path runs.
- **Compile safety:** runtime branching stays inside the existing `fp32_router_gemm_dispatch` custom op.
- **Scope:** gfx950 only; gfx942, CUDA, biased/quantized gates and batch-invariant mode are unchanged.
- **Not covered end to end:** MiniMax-M2.5-MXFP4 decodes at ~196 ms/token on both `main` and the PR, so the difference is unmeasurable. Kimi-Linear-48B and LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 crash on unmodified `main`, unrelated to this change. Their router shapes are covered by the kernel tests.
- **Related PRs:** #59023 does the bf16 extension for Kimi-K3's 7168×896 gate only (this PR gives the same M ≤ 9 limit there, for any shape). #57626 forces fp32 weights for the 5 listed shapes instead; this PR runs bf16 weights directly with no fp32 copy. #61687 targets a separate AITER tier and is orthogonal.

</details>

title: [Perf][Kernel] Add a CuteDSL BF16x3 router GEMM for fp32 router weights on Hopper
author: ischencheng
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On H100/H200, `GateLinear` runs fp32 router weights above 32 tokens as `F.linear(x.float(), w)`, an fp32 SGEMM on CUDA cores. SM100 has the CuteDSL BF16x3 kernel for this (#47973, #55899) and gfx950 has a hipBLASLt one (#52668). SM90 had nothing. This PR adds a CuteDSL BF16x3 kernel for SM90 behind the existing BF16x3 tier.

Models on main that hit this path on SM90 (fp32 router weight, bf16 activations): MiniMax-M2/M2.5/M3, GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7 and GLM-4.5-Air, Hunyuan-V3/V4, Step-3.5-Flash, ERNIE-4.5, Ling 2.0 (`router_dtype: fp32`), and others. The new models are on it too. Beam-1.0 (#62074) keeps fp32 router weights `(5120, 256)`, and Muse Spark Open (#61879) keeps `(8192, 256)`. Both shapes are in the fp32 GEMV table since #62042 and #62126, so on H200 every batch above its limit runs the fp32 SGEMM.

The first revision of this PR used Triton. It is now CuteDSL, like the other router GEMMs in the tree, and uses the `VllmJitKernel` warmup contract.

## Claims

- Router GEMM on 1xH200, inside CUDA graphs with cold L2, over 10 router shapes: 1.6-3.8x faster at 33-512 tokens and 3.3-7.7x faster at 1024-16384 tokens.
- MAE against an fp64 reference is 0.16-0.73x that of the fp32 SGEMM it replaces, at every shape and token count measured.
- MiniMax-M2.5 FP8, TP2 on 2xH200, with main and PR alternating in one container: TTFT 3-5% lower for 8K and 32K prompts, prefill throughput 4-6% higher, and on a mixed 1K-in/128-out workload 4.6% more output tokens/s and 4% lower TPOT. GSM8K accuracy is unchanged and its wall time is 2.5% lower.
- In eager mode one router call costs 17-18 µs of host time, against 21-36 µs on main.
- Beam-1.0 FP8 on one H200, as one TP8 rank (all 52 layers, dummy weights, main and PR alternating): an 8K prefill chunk takes 14.0% less time (155.3 to 133.5 ms), and a decode step at 64 and 128 requests takes 7.4% and 10.9% less.
- On SM90 the fp32 GEMV now runs up to 24 tokens instead of 32, where the new kernel is faster. The GB200 rule for `(5120, 256)` from #62042 and the B300 rule for `(4096, 352)` from #61727 stay Blackwell-only.
- No change for 24 or fewer tokens on the fp32 GEMV shapes, under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, or on other architectures.

## Validation

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/test_bf16x3_router_gemm_cutedsl.py tests/kernels/test_fp32_router_gemm.py tests/kernels/test_ll_fp32w_gemm.py
```

1xH200: 662 passed, 83 skipped with this head. 76 of them are the SM90 tests in `test_bf16x3_router_gemm_cutedsl.py`. The skips are the SM100-only tests: the 5 SM100 cases in that file and `test_router_retains_fp32_weights_and_logits`.

1xB200, after the rename (`test_bf16x3_router_gemm_cutedsl.py` and `test_fp32_router_gemm.py`): 485 passed, 76 skipped (the SM90 cases).

The SM90 tests check:
- MAE against fp64 is not above the fp32 SGEMM's, for 9 router shapes (with Beam-1.0 and Muse Spark Open) and 7 token counts (8 to 8192);
- partial K and expert tiles, and a K with fewer tiles than the largest split;
- the weight split is bit-exact (one-hot activations);
- `GateLinear` dispatch: the fp32 GEMV runs up to 24 tokens for `(5120, 256)` and `(4096, 352)`, so the GB200 and B300 rules stay off Hopper, and this kernel runs above that and for a generic shape.

The file runs in the new `(H100) BF16x3 Router GEMM Kernels` Buildkite step, and in `Kernels (B200)` as before.

```python
"""PR component benchmark: SM90 router GEMM for fp32 gate weights, main vs this PR (1xH200).

main: F.linear(x.float(), W) for M > 32 (fp32 SGEMM). PR: torch.ops.vllm.sm90_bf16x3_router_gemm.
Each number is the per-call time inside one CUDA graph that replays the op on N rotating copies of
(x, W) whose footprint is >= 4x L2, so every call starts with cold weights. MAE is against fp64.
"""

import json
import os
import statistics

import torch

import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.bf16x3_router_gemm_sm90  # noqa: F401

torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("highest")
dev = torch.device("cuda")
L2_BYTES = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(dev).L2_cache_size
print("device", torch.cuda.get_device_name(), "torch", torch.__version__, flush=True)

SHAPES = {
    "MiniMax-M2/M2.5": (3072, 256),
    "MiniMax-M3": (6144, 128),
    "GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7": (5120, 160),
    "GLM-4.5-Air": (4096, 128),
    "Hunyuan-V3": (4096, 192),
    "Hunyuan-V4": (2816, 256),
    "Step-3.5-Flash": (4096, 288),
    "Ling-flash-2.0": (4096, 256),
    "ERNIE-4.5-300B": (8192, 64),
    "Step-5": (4096, 352),
}
MS = [int(m) for m in os.environ.get("MS", "33,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384").split(",")]
SCALE = 0.053


def graph_time_us(fns, reps=7):
    for f in fns:
        f()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(g):
        for f in fns:
            f()
    g.replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    times = []
    for _ in range(reps):
        s = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        t = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        s.record()
        g.replay()
        t.record()
        t.synchronize()
        times.append(s.elapsed_time(t) * 1000 / len(fns))
    return statistics.median(times)


def mae(out, ref):
    return (out.double() - ref).abs().mean().item()


def main_path(x, w):
    return torch.nn.functional.linear(x.float(), w)


def pr_path(x, w):
    return torch.ops.vllm.sm90_bf16x3_router_gemm(x, w)


rows = []
for name, (k, e) in SHAPES.items():
    gen = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(0)
    for m in MS:
        nc = int(min(64, max(4, -(-4 * L2_BYTES // (m * k * 2 + e * k * 4)))))
        xs = [torch.randn(m, k, generator=gen, device=dev).to(torch.bfloat16) for _ in range(nc)]
        ws = [torch.randn(e, k, generator=gen, device=dev) * SCALE for _ in range(nc)]
        ref = xs[0].double() @ ws[0].double().T
        row = {"model": name, "K": k, "E": e, "M": m}
        for label, fn in (("main", main_path), ("pr", pr_path)):
            row[f"{label}_us"] = round(graph_time_us([lambda i=i: fn(xs[i], ws[i]) for i in range(nc)]), 2)
            row[f"{label}_mae"] = mae(fn(xs[0], ws[0]), ref)
        row["speedup"] = round(row["main_us"] / row["pr_us"], 2)
        rows.append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
        del xs, ws
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()

os.makedirs("control/artifacts", exist_ok=True)
with open("control/artifacts/pr_component.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(), "torch": torch.__version__, "rows": rows}, f, indent=1)
```

## Details

**Kernel.** The MMA runs swapped: 64 experts form the wgmma M dimension and tokens the N dimension (32 to 128 per CTA), so small batches still fill the instruction. One TMA warp brings fp32 weight tiles and bf16 token tiles into shared memory. The MMA warpgroup reads each k16 slice of its weight fragment as fp32 and splits it in registers into three bf16 terms. Each term keeps the top 16 bits of what is left, so the three terms sum back to the weight bit for bit. It then issues register-A wgmma against the token tile, and splits the next slice while the current one runs. Products with bf16 activations are exact in fp32, so all error comes from accumulation:
- The first-term products go to a tensor-core partial that starts from zero every K-tile (64 or 128 wide). It is then added into an fp32 register accumulator.
- The second and third terms are about 2^-8 of the output. They keep their own partial across K, as the SM100 kernel does. This is the one numerical change from the Triton revision, which promoted all three terms every K-tile. It makes the largest tiles up to 9% faster. The worst MAE in my checks is 0.87x of the fp32 SGEMM's (GLM-4.7 shape, 7 tokens).

Split-K uses a thread-block cluster of up to 8 CTAs. Each CTA writes its partial tile to its own shared memory, reusing the weight stages, and after a cluster barrier sums one slice of the tile over all peers through DSMEM, in rank order. Results are deterministic, and there is no workspace and no second kernel. There is no host sync and no data-dependent shape, so the op is safe to capture in CUDA graphs.

**Configs.** There is no autotuning. `_pick_config` scores 4 tiles x 4 splits with a fixed cost model: waves times per-CTA time. A wave is one CTA per SM, and clusters of 4 or 8 only fill 15/16 of the SMs (120 of 132; at one CTA per SM, `cuOccupancyMaxActiveClusters` gives 30 clusters of 4 and 15 of 8 on H200). The per-tile costs were fitted to H200 timings. Over 10 shapes and 14 token counts, the rule is within 0.1% (geomean) of the fastest of the 16 configs per cell, and at most 4% slower. Each of the 10 shapes reaches 9-13 configs between 1 and 16384 tokens, at about 1 s of compile each.

**Warmup.** The kernel is a `VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel`. `GateLinear` registers it with its `(K, E)` and `max_num_batched_tokens`, as it does for `ll_fp32w` and as #50177 does for SM100. Warmup traces `dispatch` over 1..max tokens and compiles each key from fake tensors, with no launch. In the end-to-end runs above, the PR arm warmed 13 keys in about 10.5 s at startup. The JIT monitor logged no compile of this kernel while serving; it logged two `fused_moe_kernel` Triton compiles on both arms.

**Host overhead.** Outside CUDA graphs (mixed prefill/decode batches above the capture sizes), the host cost per call matters as much as the kernel. `_pick_config` is cached, and the launch is one TVM-FFI call. Eager host time per call on an idle H200 host:

| | M=64 | M=930 | M=4096 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, fp32-GEMV dispatch op (MiniMax-M2.5 shape) | 26.3 µs | 29.2 µs | 28.9 µs |
| PR, same op | 18.1 µs | 18.4 µs | 18.3 µs |
| main, `F.linear(x.float(), w)` (GLM-4.7 shape) | 21.7 µs | 24.1 µs | 36.3 µs |
| PR, `torch.ops.vllm.sm90_bf16x3_router_gemm` | 17.1 µs | 17.5 µs | 17.1 µs |

The Triton revision took about 31 µs here. Its GSM8K runs (mostly eager mixed steps) were slower than main by a few percent in some containers.

**Integration.**
- `allow_bf16x3_router_gemm` is now also true on SM90, with the same `K % 8 == 0` condition as SM100. `bf16x3_router_gemm_module()` returns the SM90 module on SM90 and the SM100 module otherwise. The fp32-GEMV dispatch op and tier 4 use it.
- In the fp32-GEMV dispatch op, SM90 bf16 inputs use the fp32 GEMV up to 24 tokens. The `(5120, 256)` GB200 rule from #62042 and the `(4096, 352)` B300 rule from #61727 are in the non-SM90 branch unchanged.
- `bf16x3_router_gemm_cutedsl.py` is renamed to `bf16x3_router_gemm_sm100.py`, next to `bf16x3_router_gemm_sm90.py`.
- The kernel is the custom op `torch.ops.vllm.sm90_bf16x3_router_gemm`, as #55899 does for SM100. The fp32-GEMV shapes keep dispatching on the runtime token count inside `fp32_router_gemm_dispatch`.
- PDL is always on. SM90 supports it.

**Alternatives measured on H200.**
- The Triton revision of this PR. This kernel is 1.25x faster (geomean over 10 shapes and 15 token counts). It is slower only for ERNIE-4.5 (E=64) at 128 or fewer tokens, where 9.6 µs vs 7.2 µs: one 64-expert tile and at most 8 splits leave most SMs idle. It is still 1.55x faster than main there.
- One cuBLAS GEMM over the stacked `(3E, K)` bf16 weight, which is what gfx950 does: MAE 1.4e-6 to 4.3e-6 for the Step-5 shape, worse than the fp32 SGEMM's 3-5e-7.
- A round-to-nearest split, like the SM100 kernel's but without `sub.rn.f32x2` (sm_100 only): 0.5-4% slower than the truncating split at 64-8192 tokens on the Step-5, Beam-1.0, MiniMax-M2.5 and Muse shapes. Both MAEs are well below the fp32 SGEMM's. The other way round, the truncating split in the SM100 kernel on B200 is 0.1-2.3% slower than its own split on the same shapes, so each kernel keeps its own.
- Two bf16 terms (BF16x2): 16 of fp32's 24 significand bits. Even with exact accumulation, that alone gives an MAE of 5.7e-6 to 7.4e-6 at 1024 tokens on the Step-5, Beam-1.0 and MiniMax-M2.5 shapes, against 0.8e-6 to 1.4e-6 for the fp32 SGEMM.
- A pre-split weight kept in memory: needs 1.5x the fp32 router weight per layer (about 760 MB per rank for 88 layers of Step-5). The in-register split needs no extra memory.
- One promoted partial for all three terms per k16 slice, instead of keeping the small terms apart: MAE rose above the fp32 SGEMM's at 33 tokens.
- Two MMA warpgroups per CTA, along the experts or along the tokens (up to 4): not faster than the selected configs in my sweeps.

**Limitations.**
- With one token, cuBLAS's fp32 GEMV is more accurate than this kernel for 3 of the 10 shapes (for example MiniMax-M3: MAE 3.1e-7 vs 4.7e-7). From 2 tokens up, all 10 shapes beat it. In eager mode those batches stay on the fp32 GEMV or `ll_fp32w`. The test starts at 8 tokens.
- As on SM100, generic shapes reach tier 4 through tier 3's Python check on `x.shape[0]`. Under vLLM's guard-free `torch.compile`, that branch can be fixed at the first traced size, the issue #60681 fixes for tier 1. Small batches of those shapes may then run this kernel, which is still faster than the `F.linear` path main would freeze.
- The cost model was fitted on H200 (132 SMs). Other SM90 parts get correct results and an SM-count-aware choice, but the choice may not be the fastest.
- #61727 lowers the fp32 GEMV cutoff for Step-5 to 11 tokens when `allow_bf16x3_router_gemm` is set, based on B300. On H200 the fp32 GEMV is still faster at 16 tokens for that shape, so that rule belongs in the non-SM90 branch next to the GB200 one.
- The Beam-1.0 numbers come from a one-rank proxy with dummy weights. A full TP8 run needs #62074 merged and 8xH200.

**Not a duplicate.** I listed every open PR that touches `gate_linear.py`, `fused_moe/router/`, `fp32_router_gemm*` or `ll_fp32w*`, or that has router/gate/bf16x3 in its title. Most are for other hardware or other tiers: #60376 (SM100 large batch), #60681 (tier 1 custom op), #61727 (Step-5), #50177 and #49627 (warmup), #50535, #61687, #61895, #59023 and #57626 (ROCm), #59486 (quantization), #59925 (deterministic MoE), #37306 (Llama4), #57848 (SM103) and #61463 (ll_bf16 split-K fix).

Merged since this PR opened: #62042 (`(5120, 256)` fp32 GEMV up to 48 tokens and its GB200 rule) and #62126 (Step-5 and Muse Spark Open shapes in the fp32 GEMV). Neither adds an SM90 path above the GEMV's limit. I merged main into this branch and moved the GB200 rule behind the SM90 check.

#49312 (for #49277) also targets SM90 fp32 router weights. It adds an opt-in path (`VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_ROUTER_GEMM=1`) through the external hpc-ops library, with a cached bf16 high/low copy of the weight. This PR is on by default, adds no dependency, keeps no extra weight copy, and its error stays below the fp32 SGEMM's.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the kernel and tests, run the benchmarks above and draft this description.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER top-k for the DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-5 sparse indexer
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

On gfx950 with AITER enabled, the uncompressed sparse indexer of DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x (`index_topk` 2048) now takes AITER's top-k for decode and for prefill chunks whose longest row reaches 32K tokens, through the adapters #52882 added for DeepSeek-V4. Related: #55327, #50470, #46172, #60012.

## Claims

- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, `--max-model-len 133120`: 128K/1K TPOT -7.0% / -4.6% / -3.0% at c1 / c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 -3.0%; 8K/1K within noise; gsm8k and passkey unchanged.
- DeepSeek-V3.2, TP4, default max_model_len (163840): 128K/1K c1 TPOT -15.6%, 4K/1K c16 -1.1%, 4K/1K c1 +0.7% (+0.085 ms); gsm8k unchanged.
- Compressed indexers, other `index_topk`, GLM-5.3-Flash kpool, gfx942, AITER off and non-ROCm are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_top_k_per_row.py`, MI355X: 43 passed (8 new), 246 skipped, 1 failed as on main (pre-existing, see below). glm5next dispatch tests pass. pre-commit clean.
- AITER vs in-tree on FP8 scorer output: same selections on 29,934 rows (by value where scores tie).
- Serving, mean TPOT (ms), GLM-5.2-MXFP4 unless noted; main 2 runs / PR 3 runs (4 each with MTP3, 2 each for DeepSeek-V3.2), no failed requests:

| workload | main | PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128K/1K c1 / c8 / c16 | 14.73 / 45.05 / 78.94 | 13.70 / 42.97 / 76.60 | -7.0% / -4.6% / -3.0% |
| MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.84 | 33.79 | -3.0% |
| 8K/1K c1 / c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 | 13.48 / 17.37 / 22.66 / 9.06 | 13.45 / 17.39 / 22.54 / 9.16 | within noise |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c1 | 16.23 | 13.70 | -15.6% |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c1 / c16 | 12.81 / 22.86 | 12.90 / 22.61 | +0.7% / -1.1% |

- gsm8k 5-shot strict: GLM-5.2 0.9287 main, 0.9348 PR (stderr 0.007); DeepSeek-V3.2 0.9522 main, 0.9507 PR (stderr 0.006). MTP3 acceptance length 3.29 / 3.30.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel data and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source, MI355X.

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, mean TPOT per run (ms). Order: main, PR, PR, main, PR. A further main run between the two PR sessions was dropped: another process held about 88 GiB per GPU while it started, so its KV cache was 1.23M tokens instead of 3.2M. MTP3 order: main, PR, PR, main, PR, PR, main, main.

| workload | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8K/1K c1 | 13.43, 13.53 | 13.44, 13.45, 13.46 |
| 8K/1K c8 | 17.27, 17.47 | 17.27, 17.51, 17.38 |
| 8K/1K c16 | 22.46, 22.86 | 22.44, 22.66, 22.52 |
| 128K/1K c1 | 14.72, 14.75 | 13.66, 13.67, 13.78 |
| 128K/1K c8 | 44.55, 45.56 | 42.95, 42.98, 42.98 |
| 128K/1K c16 | 78.89, 79.00 | 76.58, 76.62, 76.60 |
| MTP3 8K/1K c8 | 8.91, 9.16, 9.08, 9.10 | 9.14, 9.34, 9.08, 9.10 |
| MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.27, 35.52, 34.45, 35.12 | 33.96, 33.67, 34.17, 33.35 |

- Median ITL (ms): 128K c1 14.83 to 13.76, c8 18.22 to 17.01, c16 21.52 to 20.49, MTP3 128K c8 27.04 to 25.39. Output throughput at 128K: +5.8% / +3.7% / +2.8%. KV cache size and startup time match across arms.
- The 128K c1 ITL drop (1.07 ms) matches the kernel estimate of 21 indexer layers x 53 us (1.11 ms).
- gsm8k flexible: 0.9295 main, 0.9363 PR. MTP3 gsm8k, first 400 questions: 0.935 main, 0.9325 PR (stderr 0.012). Passkey at 32K / 64K / 120K: 12/12, 8/8, 6/6 in both arms.
- Operator check: decode logits from AITER's `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (buffer poisoned past each row), prefill logits from `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`, calls mirroring `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`; widths 133120 and 1M, `next_n` 1 (1-D), 2 (native 2-D) and 4 (one row per token), packed multi-sequence prefill, and graph replay with new lengths. Every row has `min(L, k)` distinct indices in `[0, L)` followed by `-1`.

DeepSeek-V3.2 (FP8 checkpoint), TP4, same env and flags but no `--max-model-len` (163840), mean TPOT per run (ms), order main, PR, PR, main; median ITL and output throughput follow TPOT:

| workload | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4K/1K c1 | 12.83, 12.80 | 12.91, 12.89 |
| 4K/1K c16 | 22.84, 22.88 | 22.62, 22.60 |
| 128K/1K c1 | 16.24, 16.22 | 13.72, 13.69 |

- 4K/1K c16 mean TTFT: 2333, 2326 ms main, 2465, 2327 ms PR. 128K/1K c1 output throughput +10.0%. KV cache 2.07M tokens in every session. gsm8k flexible: 0.9530 main, 0.9507 PR.
- A static cut-off for 131072-200000 columns would put this deployment back on the in-tree kernel: it would recover the 0.085 ms at 4K c1 and lose the 128K gain (2.53 ms) and the 4K c16 gain. GLM-5.2 at 133120 would lose its 128K gains as well.

Decode top-k per indexer layer (us, in-tree to AITER), GLM-5.2 indexer (32 heads, k=2048); scoring and top-k for 21 layers captured in one graph, LLC flushed before each replay, median of 20:

| width | context | 1 row | 8 rows | 16 rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 133120 | 4K | 17.5 to 20.4 | 17.3 to 22.3 | 17.2 to 22.7 |
| 133120 | 32K | 34.0 to 22.2 | 34.9 to 22.8 | 34.7 to 23.5 |
| 133120 | 128K | 80.8 to 27.9 | 81.8 to 28.8 | 81.3 to 28.5 |
| 1M | 4K | 37.0 to 25.9 | 35.3 to 29.3 | 35.3 to 35.3 |
| 1M | 32K | 42.8 to 26.8 | 42.3 to 29.6 | 43.7 to 32.3 |
| 1M | 128K | 46.3 to 27.1 | 50.0 to 31.2 | 50.2 to 34.4 |

MTP1 (2-D bounds) and MTP3 (one row per token) follow the same pattern. At 262144 columns AITER wins at every measured context.

Prefill top-k GPU time per 16K-row chunk (us, in-tree to AITER): context 16K 304 to 370, 20K 426 to 469, 24K 568 to 558, 32K 757 to 680, 64K 1681 to 1320, 128K 4026 to 2635. 512-row chunks cross over near 20K. Host enqueue per call: in-tree 5-12 us, AITER 27-36 us.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 133120 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# MTP3: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# DeepSeek-V3.2: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2, same env and flags without --max-model-len.

# 128K/1K: num-prompts max(C, 3). 8K/1K: --random-input-len 8192,
# num-prompts max(3C, 6), --seed 42. MTP3 c8: 8 prompts at 128K, 24 at 8K.
# DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K: --random-input-len 4096, 6 prompts at c1, 48 at c16, --seed 42.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 43

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Gate: compress ratio 1 and k=2048 only. Decode always takes AITER (FULL graphs are not keyed by context length); prefill when `chunk.max_seqlen_k`, a host int, reaches 32K.
- Cost: with max_model_len between 131072 and 200000 and up to 48 rows, AITER loses 3-6 us per layer below 8-16K context. DeepSeek-V3.2 (default 163840, 61 indexer layers) measures +0.085 ms TPOT at 4K/1K c1. Keeping the in-tree kernel for that width band would also give up the 2.53 ms gain at 128K on the same deployment, so the gate does not exclude it.
- Not measured end to end: GLM-5/5.1, TP8. CI (MI300, NVIDIA) runs only the new selection test; the GPU tests need gfx950.

<details>
<summary>Design notes, pre-existing failure and related PRs</summary>

- Cause: the in-tree decode kernel has gfx950 policies only for k=512 and k=1024 (#55327). At k=2048 its cost grows with context; AITER's stays near flat.
- Semantics come from #52882's wrappers. ROCm DSA decode carries `(B, next_n)` bounds for native MTP1 and one row per token otherwise, so `seq_lens.reshape(-1)` with `next_n=1` gives AITER each row's exact end. Prefill turns AITER's chunk-global indices into sequence-local ones and keeps `-1`.
- Decode is not split by context length because a FULL graph replays one kernel for every length. Eager decode could use the length, but would then pick a different kernel for the same shape depending on graph mode. AITER's extra host time per call only shows in eager steps.
- `test_aiter_decode_topk_matches_per_row_under_mtp` (from #58167, `requires_gfx950`, so not in CI) fails identically on main: it passes `(B, 1)` seq_lens with `next_n=4` to the in-tree k=512 gfx950 kernel, which reads any 2-D `seq_lens` per row, so its reference rows are wrong. It does not reach the code changed here.
- #60012 (open) tunes the in-tree k=2048 kernel above 200000 columns for #55327. With this PR it still serves AITER-off deployments and short prefill chunks; the gate should be re-measured if it lands. #57844 (open) edits the same selector. #59421 (draft, native MTP above `next_n=2`) is compatible because decode flattens the bounds.
- #50470 (draft) and #46172 also move the k=2048 decode top-k to AITER. Both have merge conflicts and no activity since 2026-08-22, and both swap the call unconditionally, passing vLLM's `next_n` with its 2-D MTP bounds. On both, the author of #52882 noted that AITER v0.1.19 needs those bounds adapted and asked to treat #52882 as the consolidated direction; #52882 then merged with AITER enabled for compressed indexers only. This PR applies its adapters to the k=2048 path, adds prefill and serving results, and leaves every other indexer unchanged. The `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` entry point that #50470 waited for ships in AITER 0.1.25 and is the function called here.
- Duplicate search, `gh pr list --state all --search`: "aiter topk", "top-k ROCm", "topk ROCm", "indexer ROCm", "indexer aiter", "DeepSeek-V3.2 ROCm", "GLM-5 ROCm", "sparse indexer AMD", "top_k_per_row_decode", "top_k_per_row_prefill", "compress_ratio aiter topk".

</details>

Not a duplicate: #50470 and #46172 target the same decode call, have been inactive since 2026-08-22, and were marked superseded by #52882's author; #52882 left k=2048 on the in-tree kernel (details above). Thanks @JH-Leon-KIM-AMD for #50470.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] hadacore: don't load past the input on a partial last warp
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fixes an intermittent `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `hadacore::hadamard_transform_kernel`. Since Oct 15 it has crashed the `(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantization` step on main (nightly 95042, builds 95065 and 95066) and on PR runs (95016, 3 of 3 attempts). The crash happens in `test_per_token_kv_cache.py::test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head[int4-0-16-128-1-42]` and aborts the whole pytest process.

**Cause:**
- The masked kernel variant (`enable_mask=true`) issues `cp.async` loads for all `num_chunks` chunks of a warp, even when the warp owns fewer (`real_num_chunks`).
- For the int4 per-token-head KV path, 42 tokens × 128 bf16 = 21 chunks of 256 elements, at 2 chunks per warp. So the last warp reads 512 bytes past the end of the input.
- That over-read only faults when the input ends at the end of a CUDA memory segment. Whether it does depends on what earlier tests left in the caching allocator. That's why it showed up when automatic sharding put `test_online.py` in the same process.
- The `cp.async.wait_group` counts further down already assume only `real_num_chunks` groups were committed (`switch(k + diff_num_chunks)`).

**Fix:** skip the loads past `real_num_chunks` in the masked variant.

## Test Plan

Repro on Buildkite, Quantization step only, on a throwaway branch:

| Build | What it ran | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [95264](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95264) | `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` alone, and after each single suspect file | passes |
| [95264](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95264) | after the full 8-file shard-4 order | **crash** |
| [95275](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95275) | full order, leaving one file out each time | crash unless `test_online.py` is left out |
| [95292](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95292) | **this fix**: full crashing order ×3, plus the file alone | **all pass** (244 passed / 25 skipped each run, 82 passed alone) |

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix Kimi K3 online quantization with padded projections
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Fix ROCm Kimi K3 online weight loading so its padded merged KDA projection finishes as soon as all checkpoint shards arrive. Following review, the fix lives in an AMD-local `_PaddedKimiGDNMergedColumnParallelLinear`, mirroring the NVIDIA implementation; no shared loader code is changed.

### Summary

```text
six KDA checkpoint shards arrive
  → complete using real elements, excluding alignment rows (weight_loader_numel)
  → layerwise processing materializes the weight and replays the loads
  → loader re-zeroes the padding rows
  → process the layer and release its input tensors
```

## Claims

- Avoid accumulating full GPU checkpoint tensors across incomplete KDA layers during online quantization.
- Keep the alignment padding zero after online materialization, which allocates with `empty_strided` and drops the constructor's zero-init.
- Only `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py` changes; the shared Kimi-Linear projection and `reload/meta.py` are untouched.

## Validation

### Evidence

Local regression on ROCm (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` container), using the KDA online-loading test from this PR's first revision as an out-of-tree harness: real `KimiK3DeltaAttention` construction at TP8, two TP ranks × two shard orders × padded/unpadded head counts, `empty_strided` poisoned with NaN.

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | 4 padded cases fail: projection stays on meta and holds all six sources |
| This PR | 8 pass |
| This PR with loader re-zeroing disabled | 4 padded cases fail: padding rows are NaN |

```bash
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_fused_conv1d.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_direct_return.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \
  tests/models/test_alice_ai.py -q
# 181 passed, 31 skipped (MI355X)
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -k test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading -q
# 4 passed
```

ruff passes; the mypy hook reports no new errors in `amd/kda.py` (28 vs. 29 pre-existing on `main`).

No unit test is added. The first revision's test imported the Kimi K3 KDA layer into the shared `model_executor` pytest process; that pulls in numba, which exposes a latent `triton_utils/dispatcher` issue and fails the Triton dispatcher tests that run afterwards. That dispatcher issue is independent of this fix and is left to a separate PR.

Full-model GPU validation used vLLM `81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93` plus the first revision of this fix (same `weight_loader_numel` accounting; padding zeroed during materialization instead of in the loader), on 2 × 8 MI355X GPUs, TP8/DCP8, fastsafetensors, target-model FP8 PTPC, DSpark4 with synthetic AL=3.36, C48/3600s. Both runs had the same P/D hosts and started with ~287.707 GiB free per GPU. The current revision has not been rerun at full-model scale.

| Measurement | [Original run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38805434237) | [Fixed run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38805460289) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loading | HSA out-of-resources at 10/12 checkpoint groups | All 16 workers loaded; 513 target online layers per worker |
| Maximum buffered GPU source references per worker | ~42.19 GiB | 0.451 GiB |
| Lowest sampled free VRAM, P / D | 22 / 88 MiB | 25.818 / 24.869 GiB |
| Benchmark | Did not start | Full 3600s coverage; 4224 successful requests |

Source-reference bytes overlap allocated/reserved memory and must not be added to those counters. This verifies loading and serving completion, not decoding accuracy or a throughput gain. The fixed run had 7 empty-content request errors and a 300s cancel-drain timeout, retained in the run logs.

## Details

At TP8, KDA's local merged projection has 6284 real rows and 4 alignment rows. Without `weight_loader_numel`, online processing waits for 6288 rows although the checkpoint only provides the six real projections, so it defers processing and retains every source until model finalization. With GPU-backed fastsafetensors inputs this exhausts VRAM before loading completes.

During online loading the constructor's padding `zero_()` runs on meta, and materialization allocates with `empty_strided`. Layerwise processing then replays the buffered calls through the layer's weight loader, so re-zeroing the padding rows there restores them. `CopyCounter` only counts `copy_`, so the zeroing does not affect completion accounting. It adds no steady-state inference work.

The subclass extends the shared Kimi-Linear projection instead of importing the NVIDIA class, which would pull NVIDIA backend modules into the ROCm path and change AMD loading through its block-scale replication.

**Related work / duplicate check:** #50523 fixes general zero initialization for rematerialized weights; it does not declare KDA's loadable size and does not resolve this source-retention failure. If it lands, the loader re-zeroing becomes redundant but harmless. Open KDA quantization PRs and #61287 were also checked; no matching KDA completion fix was found.

### Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast Radius:** Kimi K3 ROCm KDA weight loading.

AI assistance was used: Codex prepared the first revision; Claude Code prepared the review revision and the CI analysis. Results above describe agent-run validation.

title: [KV Offload] Load small CPU-tier hits synchronously within the step
author: kfirtoledo
body:
## Overview

On wide-EP MoE prefill (such as GLM-5.3), a step takes 0.3 to 0.5 s. Almost every request has a small CPU-tier hit, and an async load parks it for about 2 steps although the copy takes ~1 ms.

This adds an opt-in `sync_load_budget_bytes` option (`kv_connector_extra_config`, default 0, off): small hits load in the same step, up to that many KV bytes per GPU per step. The change stays in the offloading connector, the `OffloadingWorker` interface, and the CPU offloading worker.

## Changes

- `scheduler.py`: a hit that fits the step's remaining budget returns `load_async=False`, so the request is scheduled in this step; the load targets its blocks by position and is marked sync. `_current_batch_sync_loads` and the byte total reset every step.
- `worker.py`: submits sync loads with `submit_load(..., expedited=True)`, waits for them before the forward pass, and does not report them in `finished_recving`.
- `kv_offload/base.py`, `cpu/gpu_worker.py`: an `expedited` flag on `OffloadingWorker.submit_load`; the CPU worker runs expedited loads on their own stream.
- `common.py`: a `TransferJob.sync` flag carries that decision from scheduler to worker.

## Claims

- Small hits load in the same step, up to `sync_load_budget_bytes` of KV per GPU per step; the rest stay async. The budget exists because the whole batch waits for the copy. A hit that would leave nothing to compute stays async.
- Sync-load blocks are hashed at allocation, so the load range is found by position. Other requests can match them in the same step, which is safe since the forward pass waits for the copy.
- Sync loads use their own stream, so they never wait behind async loads.
- With the option at 0, behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

Qwen3-30B-A3B on H100, OffloadingConnector + TieringOffloadingSpec. 12k-token prefix in GPU cache, 2k-token tail only in the CPU tier. Median extra TTFT vs a GPU-hit control:

| Setup | Without fix | With fix (limit 4096) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 node: DP=2 + EP (this version, 10 reps) | +219 ms | +1 ms |
| 2 nodes: TP=8, DP=2, EP over 16 GPUs (12 reps) | +344 ms | +8 ms |

These numbers were measured with the earlier per-request token limit (`sync_load_max_tokens=4096`) and a shared load stream; the per-step byte budget and separate stream are not yet run end to end.

GLM-5.3, one prefill group (4x8 H100, wide EP), request latency with a CPU-tier hit: ~1.9 s without the fix or above the limit, ~0.85 s under it (hits of 2k to 15k tokens).

Correctness: greedy continuation with the tail served from the CPU tier is correct 7/7 (Qwen3 and GLM-5.3).

    pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/   # 644 passed
    pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py         # 41 passed, 1 skipped

## Details

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds sync offload loads (closest: #60574, #58198).

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Bump FlashMLA to pass int64 positions to MegaAttn
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview

MegaAttn casts the RoPE positions from int64 to int32 in every layer because the FlashMLA fused norm + RoPE + attn + RoPE + cast kernels took int32. In a full CUDA graph each cast is a separate kernel: 40 per target forward on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. FlashMLA [d1a1c92](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/commit/d1a1c92eff2cf558ddf49293828cd2bd21ca48c4) (vllm-project/FlashMLA#38) now takes int64 positions directly and rejects int32, so this PR bumps FlashMLA and drops the cast.

## Changes

- Bump FlashMLA `e2afa5f` -> `d1a1c92`. The only change in between is #38.
- Pass `positions` straight to `fused_norm_rope_attn_rope_cast_{decode,fwd}` in `flash_mla_mega_attn.py`.
- Same change in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`, which would otherwise fail the new dtype check.

## Validation

Earlier revisions of this PR shared one int32 cast across layers within a forward context. These numbers come from that version, with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8 x GB300 across two nodes, DP8 x TP1 + EP, 64 requests/rank, 131,072 input tokens, 2,048 output tokens, DSpark with 5 draft tokens and full decode CUDA graphs:

| Target forward | Before | Shared cast |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPU time, median (ms) | 17.903 | 17.834 |
| GPU time, p10 / p90 (ms) | 17.847 / 17.996 | 17.793 / 17.941 |
| Kernels in the captured forward | 766 | 727 |

This revision removes all 40 casts, one more than the shared-cast version, and moves the conversion into the kernel. It has not been re-timed or rebuilt against the new FlashMLA yet.

```bash
pre-commit run --files cmake/external_projects/flashmla.cmake benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py
```

Pre-commit passed. No accuracy evaluation was run. RoPE math is unchanged, and the FlashMLA tests in #38 cover int64 positions.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR bumps FlashMLA to `d1a1c92` or removes this cast.

AI assistance (Codex, Claude Code) was used to implement and validate this change.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep scheduling running requests after a priority self-preemption
author: apex-mochen
body:
## Purpose

Under `--scheduling-policy priority`, when a running request cannot get KV blocks the scheduler preempts the lowest-priority running request. `self.running` is in admission order, not priority order, so that request can sit in the middle of the list, for example when higher-priority requests arrived after it. If it is the request currently being scheduled, it preempts itself, and the running loop then `break`s:

```python
if new_blocks is None:
    # Cannot schedule this request.
    break
```

Every running request after it gets no tokens in that step, even though they all have higher priority, the self-preemption just freed blocks, and budget remains. This is a priority inversion: the requests the policy is meant to protect lose a step whenever a lower-priority request ahead of them runs out of KV.

After a self-preemption the request has already been removed from `self.running` (`del self.running[victim_index]` with `victim_index == req_index`), so `req_index` already points at the next request. The fix continues the loop in that case. Nothing changes for FCFS: it preempts `running[-1]`, so a self-preemption there only happens on the last request. Other reasons for a failed allocation (a deferred free that will not help, pending connector frees) still end the loop.

Related but different: #49097 (fixed by #49206) adjusted `req_index` when the victim sits before the cursor. #39375, a larger rework of this preemption path that has been open since March, would also remove this `break`.

## Test Plan

- New `test_priority_self_preemption_keeps_scheduling_later_running_requests`. Setup: one free block, `running = [A(p0), B(p5), C(p0)]`; A and B both need a new block on the same decode step, C does not. A takes the block, B preempts itself, and C must still be scheduled.
- `tests/v1/core` in full, main vs this PR.
- A random-workload stall check on the real `Scheduler` (small per-step budgets, priority/FCFS mixed, hybrid attention+Mamba and full-attention layouts, 40 seeds each). It flags a running request that gets 0 tokens while the step has budget left for its whole remainder; this is how I found it.

## Test Result

(CPU only.)

- New test: fails on main (`{'A': 1}` scheduled, C skipped), passes with this PR.
- `tests/v1/core` in full: same failed/errored set on main `fa75d3456d` and on this PR (68 environment failures on both trees, e.g. missing `torchvision` and offline model configs); 0 failures only on this PR; 953 → 954 passed (the new test).
- Stall check, hybrid layout: main stalls on 1/40 seeds (this bug), this PR on 0/40. Full-attention layout: 0/40 on both, with identical per-run action counts. A KV-content check over 60 more seeds on this PR found nothing.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

AI-assisted (Claude Code). I reviewed the change and ran the tests listed above myself.

title: [Feature][LoRA][MoE] Expert LoRA for FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4 experts
author: aoshen02
body:
## Overview

Add expert LoRA to the fused FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE kernel for MXFP4 expert weights with BF16 activations (`TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts`, next to `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`). TP > 1 relies on #61235 (merged).

## Claims

- MXFP4 MoE models can serve expert LoRA adapters on `moe_backend="flashinfer_trtllm"` instead of falling back to Marlin / unfused Triton.
- Opt-in: `moe_backend="auto"` selects the same backend as before. `flashinfer_trtllm_afp8` (MXFP8 activations) with expert LoRA is rejected with an explicit reason.
- Requires FlashInfer >= 0.6.18 (`gemm1_lora_delta` on `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3987); vLLM pins 0.7.2.

## Validation

Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly arm64 image built from `af7f9488c` (flashinfer-python 0.7.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130), NVIDIA GB300, with the changed files of this PR and #61235 backported onto that commit and mounted over the image. Not run on the PR base itself; the changed files apply to it without conflicts.

**Kernel-level** — `pytest tests/lora/test_trtllm_mxfp4_lora_moe.py -v`: 9 passed. Random MXFP4 weights through vLLM's TRTLLM weight conversion, float64 reference from the dequantized weights, with and without an FC1/FC2 bias:

- delta in `[up | gate]` order: output and FC1 activation within 2% relative error of the reference; the swapped order is off by more than 30%;
- zero delta vs. the non-LoRA path: within 2%;
- the four incoming delta layouts are converted exactly;
- oracle: unchanged without LoRA, `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts` first with LoRA + BF16 activations, explicit error with MXFP8 activations.

**End-to-end** — `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, offline `LLM`, `enable_lora=True`, fixed-token logprobs (`prompt_logprobs`) of 16 prompts x 200 tokens. Adapters are seeded random expert-only LoRAs (rank 8, alpha 32, only `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` nonzero; B std 0.01 = small, 0.05 = large). Reference: `moe_backend="triton_unfused"`, TP 1. On the reference the adapters move the logprobs by 0.53 (small) and 1.89 (large) mean abs. "Effect" is adapter minus base logprob per token; projection is `<new, ref> / <ref, ref>`.

| backend | TP | set | MAE vs ref | median abs | effect projection | effect correlation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 1 | base | 0.136 | 0.038 | - | - |
| | 1 | small | 0.132 | 0.046 | 0.81 | 0.86 |
| | 1 | large | 0.963 | 0.629 | 0.84 | 0.79 |
| `marlin` | 1 | base | 0.126 | 0.040 | - | - |
| | 1 | small | 0.137 | 0.046 | 0.81 | 0.86 |
| | 1 | large | 0.973 | 0.621 | 0.82 | 0.79 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 2 | base | 0.149 | 0.044 | - | - |
| | 2 | small | 0.146 | 0.051 | 0.74 | 0.81 |
| | 2 | large | 1.023 | 0.665 | 0.81 | 0.76 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm`, without #61235 | 2 | small | 0.472 | 0.232 | 0.33 | 0.42 |
| | 2 | large | 1.703 | 1.193 | 0.54 | 0.49 |
| `triton_unfused` | 2 | base | 0.137 | 0.044 | - | - |
| | 2 | small | 0.144 | 0.051 | 0.80 | 0.84 |
| | 2 | large | 0.993 | 0.619 | 0.83 | 0.79 |

The base rows are the floor between two backends or TP sizes on this text (same size for Marlin and for Triton at TP 2 against Triton at TP 1; the mean is tail-heavy, see the median). With the small adapter the new backend stays on that floor; with either adapter it tracks the reference as closely as Marlin does. At TP 2 it needs #61235 (now on main). The large adapter breaks the model (mean logprob -4.6) and is only there to make the direction of the effect visible. Repeating a request gives identical logprobs on `flashinfer_trtllm` at TP 1 (Marlin: 0.07 MAE between two passes). One run per configuration.

**Throughput** — same model, TP 1, 64 concurrent requests, 256 output tokens each, output tokens/s (second of two passes):

| backend | base requests | with expert LoRA |
|---|---|---|
| `triton_unfused` | 5828 | 4593 |
| `marlin` | 10510 | 7047 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 13388 | 7699 |

Supplementary, on a 384-expert, top-6 MXFP4 MoE at TP 4 (prototype of this change on an older base, 128 requests of ~3.3k output tokens): with an expert adapter 1.5-1.65x the throughput of `triton_unfused` and 1.02-1.16x Marlin; base requests 2.5-2.7x `triton_unfused`.

Not validated: EP, `fully_sharded_loras`, per-expert (2D) adapters end-to-end, more than one loaded adapter, CUDA graph specialization per LoRA, GPT-OSS at TP 4 / 8. `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` are clean on the changed files.

## Details

Design. `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts` subclasses `_TrtLlmLoRAExpertsBase` and reuses its flow unchanged: the gate/up delta is computed by punica and passed as `gemm1_lora_delta`, so the kernel adds it before the activation; the down delta is computed from the post-activation FC1 output the kernel returns, and the base finalize and the delta reduction happen in one FP32 pass. Kernel arguments (`gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`, unpadded hidden size) come from the existing `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsBase`.

Three things differ from the BF16 class, each behind the new `prepare_gemm1_lora_delta` hook or a small base change:

- FC1 bias. The kernel has one FC1 bias slot, used either by the static `gemm1_bias` or by the per-token delta. On the LoRA path the static bias (GPT-OSS has one) is un-shuffled to logical order and added to the delta; `gemm1_bias` is then not passed. The sum is rounded to BF16, the dtype the kernel takes for the delta.
- Delta layout. The kernel takes `[up | gate]` halves. Per-expert adapters already arrive that way (or as interleaved pairs for `SWIGLUOAI`); fused 3D adapters arrive in checkpoint row order. All four cases are converted.
- Hidden padding. MXFP4 TRTLLM pads the hidden size (2880 -> 3072 for GPT-OSS) and returns an unpadded output, so the shared finalize now writes `output.size(1)` columns instead of the padded width. No change for the BF16 class, where the two are equal. The modular kernel also sized its output from the padded input and asserted on the narrower result in the no-op finalize; it now asks the experts for the output hidden size (`FusedMoEExpertsModular.output_hidden_dim`, default: the input size; the TRTLLM MXFP4 experts return the unpadded size) and allocates `output` at that width up front, so the result is used without a copy on a single rank. This also applies to the non-LoRA `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular`. This was found by the end-to-end run, not by the kernel tests.

MXFP8 activations are not supported because the kernel then returns the FC1 activation as uint8 without block scales (observed with FlashInfer 0.6.18), so the down delta cannot be computed.

Limitations.

- DP is rejected (explicit `flashinfer_trtllm` + LoRA + DP raises, as before this PR): the inherited no-LoRA fast path reads the local batch's adapter flag, while under DP the experts see the gathered batch. `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts` has the same gap; left for a separate fix.
- Top-1 routing with the weight applied on the input double-weights through the shared LoRA base (also `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`); fixed separately in #62019.
- The kernel tests need SM100, so the H200/L4 LoRA CI shards skip them; they were run on GB300 only.
- Not chunked, like `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`: the LoRA token mapping covers the whole batch. The TRTLLM-Gen grid limits one call to about `(65535 - num_experts) * 8 / top_k` tokens (~130k for GPT-OSS).
- `SITU` activation is not enabled for the LoRA class (untested).
- With a static FC1 bias, a delta far below the BF16 step of the bias is rounded away.

Related work, not duplicated: #47226 adds FlashInfer MoE LoRA for FP8 / MXFP8 / MxInt4 (not MXFP4, not updated since July) and uses the same opt-in rule; #34421 routes NVFP4 LoRA to Marlin; #61164 and #61165 fix other parts of the MoE LoRA path and do not overlap.

title: [Perf][Bugfix] Prefer MNNVL for single-node FlashInfer allreduce again
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a 3-5% decode regression in v0.32.0, caused by #56891.

#56891 changed automatic FlashInfer allreduce selection to use `trtllm` for every node-local process group. Before it, single-node runs used `mnnvl`, falling back to `trtllm` on nodes without NVSwitch multicast. The PR included no perf data, and on single-node NVSwitch systems `trtllm` is slower.

## Evidence

The perf-eval nightlies show a step in the 14 commits between the 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04 nightlies, and #56891 is the only distributed change among them. Only TP>1 workloads moved:

| workload | before (10-03) | after (10-04 on) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200 | ~5650 tok/s, TPOT 20.8 ms | ~5460 tok/s, TPOT 21.6 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP4, H200 (same host) | 10883 tok/s, TPOT 11.20 ms | 10571 tok/s, TPOT 11.54 ms |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200 | ~2770 tok/s | ~2650-2720 tok/s |
| MiniMax-M3 TP8, H200 | TPOT 35.9 ms | TPOT 36.8 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP1, B200 | unchanged | unchanged |

A/B on the v0.32.0rc2 image with `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` forced:

| workload | default (`trtllm`) | `mnnvl` |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200, 8k/1k conc 128 | 5462 tok/s, TPOT 21.78 ms | **5728 tok/s, TPOT 20.22 ms** |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200, 3 repeats | 2533 / 2753 / 2771 tok/s | **2581 / 2811 / 2845 tok/s** |

## Change

For node-local groups, auto-selection goes back to `mnnvl` with `allow_trtllm_fallback=True`. The existing fallback still builds a `trtllm` workspace when `mnnvl` can't create one (no NVSwitch multicast). Multi-node selection from #56891 is unchanged: `mnnvl` on Blackwell, disabled on Hopper. The unit test's expectations are updated to match.

cc @elvircrn: is there a case where single-node `mnnvl` misbehaved that #56891 was fixing? The PR description only covers the multi-node cases.

## Test Plan

- `test_flashinfer_auto_backend_uses_group_topology` updated for the single-node cases.
- ruff check/format pass.
- Perf A/B above (perf-eval build 680).

title: [Spec Decode] Support PCP with DSpark for DeepSeek-V4.1
author: chaunceyjiang
body:
## Overview
Enable fixed-length DSpark speculative decoding with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) on NVIDIA CUDA, extending the standalone PCP path from #59857. Preserve compressor rollback states and keep replicated draft proposals consistent across PCP ranks.


## Claims
- Retain and publish compressor ring tails across PCP ranks so rejected speculative suffixes can resume at an earlier position without losing the predecessor needed by ratio-2 compression.
- Broadcast draft tokens and, for probabilistic drafting, their corresponding logits from PCP rank 0 before target verification. The shared DFlash path also synchronizes confidence values when adaptive verification is enabled; V4.1 PCP still rejects adaptive verification.
- Cover PCP2/4, 0/5/9 speculative tokens, ring capacities 8/16, partial rejection, odd/even accepted prefixes, empty local ranks, and decode-owner changes through the existing compressor regression.


## Validation

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --seed 0 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --no-async-scheduling -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE

```

title: [Perf][Sampler] Speed up the small-batch split top-p pipeline
author: abmfy
body:
## Overview

The small-batch split top-p pipeline (#54651) caps its grid at one program per SM (`S * B <= num_SMs`), and at that occupancy its step kernels are latency-bound. On a 148-SM GPU S drops to 2 at 38 rows, so a top-p call at 38-64 rows (e.g. 8 requests x 8 spec-decode verify tokens) takes about twice as long as at 37 rows. This PR makes two changes:

1. It keeps splitting rows past one wave while each slice still spans at least 7168 vocab entries.
2. It lets MRV2 skip the split pipeline when no row is top-p-only. Today the pipeline is still launched in that case, as 7 kernels whose programs all exit immediately.

cc @njhill

## Claims

- With the `has_topp_only_rows` hint that MRV2 passes, `apply_top_k_top_p` on <= 64 rows is as fast or faster for every row mix measured: all top-p-only, half and half, and all top-k on both GPUs, plus 1, 10% and 25% top-p-only rows on B300. This holds on B300 (148 SMs) and H200 (132 SMs), across the vocab sizes of current models (120K-262K, plus 32K). Main -> this PR:
  - Top-p-only rows, where main is at S=2: 1.22-2.16x on B300 and 1.05-1.90x on H200.
  - Batches that mix top-k rows with top-p-only rows, B >= 32, V >= 120K: 1.43-2.70x. At 32K, where S changes only from B=38 on B300 and B=34 on H200, it is 1.00-1.62x. The fewer top-p-only rows, the bigger the win: with a single top-p-only row, up to 3.7x at V=151936 and 4.4x at V=262144 (B300).
  - Batches where every row has top-k (e.g. the Qwen3.8 and Gemma 4 defaults): 1.00-1.21x. MRV2 no longer launches the split pipeline for them.
  - The worst ratio, 0.97x, is in configs where nothing changes, within the A/A noise. Callers that do not pass the hint get the same gains, except that all-top-k batches run at 0.90-0.98x (see Change 2).
- Real MiMo-V2.6 spec-decode verify rows (top_p 0.95) on B300: 561 -> 219 us at B=38 (2.56x) and 565 -> 318 us at B=64 (1.78x).
- End to end on the Triton sampler path (B300):
  - Llama-3-8B-Instruct, seeded top-p, c=48: median ITL -5.1%.
  - MiMo-V2.6-Pro TP4 with DFlash K=7, c=8: top-p goes from 558 to 301 us per step, and GPU busy time excluding MoE GEMMs drops by 0.27 ms of a 22.7 ms decode step.

## Validation

**Tests**, on fa75d3456d + this PR:
- B300: `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_sampling_params_e2e.py tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sample_warmup.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py`: 287 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm only).
- B300: `cd tests && pytest watermarking`, in its own session as CI runs it: 191 passed, 3 skipped. In a shared session, the default device that `test_topk_topp_sampler.py` sets leaks into these CPU tests; that is unrelated to this PR.
- H200: `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`: 140 passed, 1 skipped. This ran on the revision before the new test gained its monkeypatch; the kernel code is the same.
- New tests:
  - B=48 in `test_topp_only` and `test_topk_and_topp`. On 128-152-SM GPUs this is the only tested size where main uses S=2.
  - `test_skip_split_without_topp_only_rows`: with `has_topp_only_rows=False` the split pipeline is not launched, and the result is bitwise identical, including for a grammar-masked row.
  - `test_has_topp_only_rows`: covers MRV2 `SamplingStates`, including top_k values that disable top-k.
- CI runs `tests/v1/sample` on H200 MIG and MI355.

**Microbenchmark setup.** Calls are to `apply_top_k_top_p_triton`, one CUDA graph per variant, with variants interleaved and capture order alternated between configs. Each number is the median of 100 replays with L2 hot. On an earlier revision without the hint, cold L2 agreed within 0.07x.
- "main" is this tree with `_topp_split_count` patched back and no hint.
- "PR" passes `has_topp_only_rows` computed from k and p, as MRV2 does.
- A second capture of "PR" (A/A) gives the noise floor: 95% of configs fall within +-1.5%, the worst at 0.96x/1.05x.
- Logits are randn x 3; p=0.95 and k=50 unless stated. The script is below.

V=151936, main -> PR:

| rows | GPU | B=16 | B=32 | B=38 | B=48 | B=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| top-p only | B300 | 1.09x | 1.01x | 1.93x | 1.52x | 1.29x |
| | H200 | 1.16x | 1.06x | 1.69x | 1.38x | 1.05x |
| half top-k, half top-p only | B300 | 1.09x | 1.50x | 2.44x | 2.16x | 1.86x |
| | H200 | 1.08x | 1.51x | 2.06x | 1.92x | 1.66x |
| all top-k + top-p | B300 | 1.08x | 1.09x | 1.07x | 1.07x | 1.05x |
| | H200 | 1.06x | 1.07x | 1.04x | 1.07x | 1.07x |

S goes 8->16 at B=16 and 4->16 at B=32. It goes 2->16 from B=38 on B300 and from B=34 on H200; at B=34 the H200 speedups are 1.74x for top-p only and 2.13x for half top-k.

Popular models, with each model's vocab size and default sampling: generation_config, or the model card's recommendation when the repo sets none (*). B=38 (B300) and B=34 (H200) are the first sizes where main uses S=2. (†) gpt-oss sets no sampling defaults and OpenAI recommends top_p 1.0, which skips top-p entirely; the row shows a client that sends top_p 0.95.

| model | vocab | default sampling | B300 B=16 | B300 B=38 | B300 B=64 | H200 B=16 | H200 B=34 | H200 B=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| MiMo-V2.6-Pro | 152576 | top_p 0.95 | 1.11x | 1.88x | 1.30x | 1.15x | 1.78x | 1.06x |
| GLM-5.3 | 154880 | top_p 0.95 | 1.09x | 1.87x | 1.30x | 1.16x | 1.71x | 1.05x |
| Kimi-K3 | 163840 | top_p 0.95* | 1.09x | 1.98x | 1.38x | 1.15x | 1.79x | 1.16x |
| MiniMax-M3 | 200064 | top_p 0.95 | 1.06x | 1.85x | 1.27x | 1.13x | 1.76x | 1.13x |

Real MiMo-V2.6 verify-step logits on B300, top-p only, p=0.95. Rows are drawn from 1424 dumped verify rows (V=152576); the dump is not attached.

| main (us) | 151.3 | 259.8 | 561.2 | 561.5 | 565.0 |
| PR (us) | 125.2 | 188.4 | 219.0 | 280.7 | 317.8 |
| speedup | 1.21x | 1.38x | 2.56x | 2.00x | 1.78x |

GB300 (152 SMs) shows the same picture at V=128K-262K: top-p only 1.18-1.94x where main is at S=2 (B >= 39), and mixed 1.43-2.55x at B >= 32. At 32K, where S changes, the numbers are 1.17-1.19x and 1.11-1.45x. These numbers come from an older vLLM tree with an earlier revision of this PR's `topk_topp_triton.py` swapped in. That revision used a 6144-entry floor, which picks the same S as 7168 at these vocab sizes, and predates the hint, so it covers only top-p-only and mixed rows.

**Serving on B300.** These runs used upstream 30e79c3a76, whose `topk_topp_triton.py` matches this PR's base, with the split-count change loaded in. Servers ran back to back on one node. Per-step times come from a 29-step torch-profiler window; ITL comes from the benchmark client.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 5-shot, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, T=0.6, top_p=0.9, c=64, 6 runs per variant (2 servers x 3 seeds): main 73.25 +- 1.11, PR 73.82 +- 0.96.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script (bench_topp_split.py)</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Microbenchmark for the small-batch split top-p changes in topk_topp_triton.py.

Run from a checkout with the PR applied. "main" monkeypatches
_topp_split_count back to the rule on main (S * batch_size <= num_SMs) and
always launches the split pipeline, as main does; "pr" uses the module as is
and passes has_topp_only_rows computed from k and p, as MRV2 does.
Every config is captured once per variant as a CUDA graph on a scratch
copy of the logits; each rep restores the scratch copy outside the timed
region (and optionally flushes L2), then times one graph replay with CUDA
events. Variants are interleaved rep by rep, the
capture order alternates between configs, and the median is reported.
--aa adds a second capture of "pr" to show the noise floor.

    python bench_topp_split.py --vocabs 32000 128256 151936 262144 \
        --out results.json
"""

import argparse
import gc
import json

import torch

import vllm.v1.sample.ops.topk_topp_triton as tt

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--vocabs", type=int, nargs="+", default=[151936])
ap.add_argument("--bs", type=int, nargs="+",
                default=[1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 38, 48, 56, 64])
ap.add_argument("--modes", nargs="+", default=["p", "kp", "mixed", "k"])
ap.add_argument("--p", type=float, default=0.95)
ap.add_argument("--topk", type=int, default=50)
ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=100)
ap.add_argument("--cold", action="store_true", help="flush L2 before each rep")
ap.add_argument("--real", help="optional .pt file with a [N, V] 'logits' tensor")
ap.add_argument("--aa", action="store_true", help="also time an A/A copy of pr")
ap.add_argument("--no-hint", action="store_true",
                help="pr does not pass has_topp_only_rows (non-MRV2 callers)")
ap.add_argument("--out")
args = ap.parse_args()

dev = torch.device("cuda")
props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(dev)
NUM_SM = props.multi_processor_count
FLUSH = torch.empty(256 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.int8, device=dev)
PR_RULE = tt._topp_split_count


def main_rule(batch_size: int, vocab_size: int, num_sm: int) -> int:
    splits = 1
    while splits < tt._SPLIT_MAX_SPLITS and splits * 2 * batch_size <= num_sm:
        splits *= 2
    return splits


VARIANTS = {"main": (main_rule, False), "pr": (PR_RULE, not args.no_hint)}
if args.aa:
    VARIANTS["pr_aa"] = (PR_RULE, not args.no_hint)


def make_inputs(mode, B, V, real):
    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(B * 7919 + V)
    if real is not None:
        cpu_g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(B * 7919 + V)
        idx = torch.randint(0, real.shape[0], (B,), generator=cpu_g)
        x = real[idx].to(dev).float().contiguous()
    else:
        x = torch.randn(B, V, device=dev, generator=g) * 3.0
    p = torch.full((B,), args.p if mode != "k" else 1.0, device=dev)
    k = None
    if mode != "p":
        k = torch.full((B,), args.topk, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32)
        if mode == "mixed":
            k[1::2] = V  # odd rows have no top-k
        elif mode == "onep":
            k[0] = V  # one row has no top-k
        elif mode.startswith("pfrac"):
            k[: max(1, round(B * int(mode[5:]) / 100))] = V
    if mode == "k":
        p = None
    return x, k, p


class Runner:
    def __init__(self, rule, hint, x, k, p):
        self.x, self.buf = x, x.clone()
        buf = self.buf

        def fn():
            tt._topp_split_count = rule
            tt.apply_top_k_top_p_triton(buf, k, p, has_topp_only_rows=hint)

        fn()  # compile and warm up outside capture
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        gc.collect()
        gc.disable()
        try:
            self.g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
            with torch.cuda.graph(self.g):
                fn()
        finally:
            gc.enable()
            tt._topp_split_count = PR_RULE
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

    def rep(self):
        self.buf.copy_(self.x)
        if args.cold:
            FLUSH.zero_()
        st = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        en = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        st.record()
        self.g.replay()
        en.record()
        return st, en


def bench(x, k, p, flip):
    items = list(VARIANTS.items())
    if flip:
        items.reverse()
    ponly = True
    if k is not None and p is not None:
        ponly = bool(((k >= x.shape[1]) & (p < 1)).any())
    runners = {
        n: Runner(rule, ponly if use_hint else True, x, k, p)
        for n, (rule, use_hint) in items
    }
    evs = {n: [] for n in runners}
    for i in range(args.reps + 5):
        for n, r in runners.items():
            e = r.rep()
            if i >= 5:
                evs[n].append(e)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    out = {}
    for n, lst in evs.items():
        ts = sorted(s.elapsed_time(e) * 1e3 for s, e in lst)
        out[n] = ts[len(ts) // 2]
    # Same kept sets? (they may differ only at exact ties at the threshold)
    masks = {}
    for n, r in runners.items():
        r.rep()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        masks[n] = r.buf != float("-inf")
    out["rows_diff"] = int((masks["main"] != masks["pr"]).any(-1).sum())
    return out


real = None
if args.real:
    real = torch.load(args.real, map_location="cpu")["logits"]
    args.vocabs = [real.shape[1]]

print(f"# {props.name}, {NUM_SM} SMs, torch {torch.__version__}, "
      f"{'cold' if args.cold else 'hot'} L2, p={args.p}, k={args.topk}, "
      f"median of {args.reps} graph replays (us)")
aa_hdr = (" A/A |", "---|") if args.aa else ("", "")
print("| vocab | mode | B | S main | S pr | main | pr | speedup | rows diff |" + aa_hdr[0])
print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|" + aa_hdr[1])
results = []
for V in args.vocabs:
    for mode in args.modes:
        for B in args.bs:
            x, k, p = make_inputs(mode, B, V, real)
            r = bench(x, k, p, flip=len(results) % 2 == 1)
            s_main, s_pr = main_rule(B, V, NUM_SM), PR_RULE(B, V, NUM_SM)
            row = dict(gpu=props.name, sms=NUM_SM, vocab=V, mode=mode, B=B,
                       S_main=s_main, S_pr=s_pr, **r)
            results.append(row)
            print(f"| {V} | {mode} | {B} | {s_main} | {s_pr} | {r['main']:.1f} | "
                  f"{r['pr']:.1f} | {r['main'] / r['pr']:.2f}x | {r['rows_diff']} |"
                  + (f" {r['pr_aa'] / r['pr']:.3f} |" if args.aa else ""),
                  flush=True)
if args.out:
    with open(args.out, "w") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=1)
```

```bash
BS="1 8 16 32 34 38 39 48 64"
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --bs $BS --modes p kp mixed --p 0.95 --topk 50 \
    --vocabs 32000 120832 128896 129280 131072 151936 152576 154880 163840 200064 201088
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --bs $BS --modes p kp mixed --p 0.9 --topk 50 --vocabs 128256
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --bs $BS --modes p kp mixed --p 0.95 --topk 20 --vocabs 248320
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --bs $BS --modes p kp mixed --p 0.95 --topk 64 --vocabs 202048 262144
# share of top-p-only rows; add --no-hint for callers that do not pass the hint
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --vocabs 128256 151936 262144 --bs 16 32 38 48 64 \
    --modes kp onep pfrac10 pfrac25 mixed p
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --real <logits.pt>   # [N, V] "logits" tensor
```
</details>

## Details

**Why more than one program per SM.** Each split program sweeps a `V/S` slice serially, so at small B the call time follows S, not B. I forced S to 1..128 on B300 over 425 top-p-only configs: 6 synthetic logit kinds x 4 vocab sizes plus real MiMo rows, B=1-64. Regret is time over the time at the best S <= 32:

| rule | configs > 5% slower than main | worst vs main | regret, geomean / max |
|---|---|---|---|
| main: `S * B <= num_SMs` | - | - | 1.24 / 2.95 |
| `S * B <= 2 * num_SMs` | 20 | 0.72x | 1.10 / 2.00 |
| `S * B <= 4 * num_SMs` | 69 | 0.59x | 1.07 / 1.87 |
| this PR | 0 | 0.96x | 1.02 / 1.26 |

Pure occupancy targets shrink slices down to 1000 entries at V=32K. Raising `_SPLIT_MAX_SPLITS` would not help at B=38-64, where the one-wave cap is what binds.

**Change 1: split count.** `_topp_split_count` keeps doubling S, still a power of two capped at 32, while either main's condition holds or the doubled S leaves slices of at least `_SPLIT_MIN_SLICE = 7168` entries. The value sits between two measured regimes:
- Around 200K vocab (gpt-oss, MiniMax, Muse), a forced S sweep shows S=32 (about 6.3K-entry slices) 3-24% slower than S=16 for top-p-only rows at B=16-64. S=32 wins only at B=8-24, by up to 20% for half-top-k batches at B=16. So the floor must be above 6314 to exclude it.
- At 256K-262K, S=32 (8.0-8.2K entries) is faster than S=16 in most configs, and at most 4% slower at V=256000 (9% at 262144). So the floor must be at most 8000 to allow it.

Qwen3.8 (248K) lands on S=32 with 7.8K-entry slices. I measured it against main, not against a forced S=16.

S never drops below main's value, and the workspace size is unchanged. The set of S values per vocab can only shrink: at V >= 120K it becomes {32, 16} or just {32}, instead of {32, 16, 8, 4, 2}. The warmup providers already push every B through the same dispatch functions, so no runtime JIT is added.

**Change 2: skip the idle split launch.** `apply_top_k_top_p` gains `has_topp_only_rows: bool = True`. False means no row has p < 1 together with k >= vocab_size. In that case the monolithic kernel already masks every row, including grammar rows whose top-k is a no-op, and the split pipeline is not launched. MRV2's `SamplingStates.has_topp_only_rows()` computes the flag from host-side numpy state, with no sync, and the MRV2 call sites pass it: verification and logits processing via `apply_sampling_params`, non-fused random sampling, and the watermark sampler. So does diffusion_gemma, which uses the MRV2 sampling state. The flag is computed only when both top-k and top-p are active, since it matters only then. MRV1 keeps the default: it gets the new split count but still launches the split pipeline. All-top-k batches there run at 0.90-0.98x (+2 to +23 us) at B=32-64 in the graph-captured microbenchmark (B300 and GB300, V=128K-262K; the "none, without the hint" row below), and at 0.96-0.99x (+2 to +11 us) in the upstream benchmark above.

A cutoff on the share of top-k rows would not work. The gain is largest when only a few rows are top-p-only, and only zero top-p-only rows lose (B300, V=151936):

| top-p-only rows | B=32 | B=38 | B=64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| none, without the hint | 0.97x | 0.95x | 0.91x |
| none, with the hint | 1.09x | 1.07x | 1.05x |
| 1 row | 1.96x | 3.68x | 3.66x |
| 25% | 1.60x | 3.00x | 2.83x |
| 50% | 1.50x | 2.44x | 1.86x |
| all | 1.01x | 1.93x | 1.29x |

**Unchanged: the split/monolithic handover at B=64.** On peaked logits (real MiMo rows, Zipf) the monolithic kernel at B=65 is still faster than the split pipeline at B=64, even with this PR: 318 vs 193 us on MiMo rows. On flat logits the order flips. Where to hand over depends on the distribution, so `_SPLIT_MAX_BATCH` is left alone here.

**Output changes.** S only changes how rows are partitioned, and it already varies with B on main. Kept sets differ only at the p boundary:
- On real (bf16-valued) MiMo logits, every differing token is an exact tie with the boundary logit; this affects 19% of row evaluations.
- On continuous fp32 logits (synthetic flat, peaked and Zipf), 3671 of 41424 row evaluations differ. 2536 of them are not boundary ties and come from fp32 summation order, with kept mass differing by at most 1.1e-4.
- Against a float64 reference, rows below p are unchanged (6 vs 6 over 33776 real-row evaluations). Rows that over-keep boundary copies drop from 6698 to 2445 and rows that under-keep rise from 6 to 30, mostly because the mask kernel's tie count restarts at every 8192-entry block, which shorter slices hit less often. That restart is a pre-existing bug, separate from this PR.

**Scope and limits.** Only the Triton sampler path is affected:
- Spec-decode verification, for any model.
- Non-spec batches that cannot use the fused FlashInfer sampler: per-request seeds, greedy rows in the batch, processed logprobs, or FlashInfer disabled.
- ROCm takes the split path too, and S changes there as well; for example, at V ~152K S becomes 16 from B=20 on MI300X (304 CUs). I have no AMD hardware to measure it.
- GPUs with fewer than 132 SMs were not measured either.

**Related PRs.** No open PR changes the split count for performance.
- #55414 (@njhill) buckets B before the same one-wave rule, to bound the precompiled variants. Since #56323 the warmup dispatcher enumerates every B, so I think its goal is covered. If you still plan to land it, the two compose.
- #56154 (draft) carries a copy of the same dispatchers with the 2-argument `_topp_split_count`.
- #58231, #59540, #59804 and #60104 touch other code in these files. #60104 adds tests right above the `test_topk_and_topp` parametrize line edited here.
