title: [ROCm][DI][CI]  Add DeepSeek-V3 NIXL accuracy steps
author: avininjamay8
body:
## Purpose

Add DeepSeek-V3 disaggregated prefill/decode accuracy steps that use NIXL over UCX RDMA on MI350, next to the existing MoRIIO steps. Read uses `NixlConnector`. Write uses `NixlPushConnector` for 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8, and 2P2D EP16.

The 2P2D EP16 write step needs https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62055. That change keeps push heartbeats and outgoing WRITE polling on the writer thread, so a blocked NIXL call cannot miss an expert-parallel collective.

## Changes

- `pipeline-disagg.yaml`: six DeepSeek-V3 steps. Read (`NixlConnector`): 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, 2P2D EP16/DP16. Write (`NixlPushConnector`): 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, and 2P2D EP16/DP16.
- `run-slurm-disagg-test.sh`, `run_xPyD_disagg.slurm`: add `KV_CONNECTOR` (default `MoRIIOConnector`) and pass it to the containers. For NIXL, start vllm-router with `--kv-connector nixl` and fixed `--prefill`/`--decode` URLs, because NIXL has no discovery service.
- `vllm_disagg.sh`: when `KV_CONNECTOR` is `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector`, use that name in the NIXL KV transfer config (UCX backend). On 2P2D EP16 prefill, set `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`. At 0.85 the AITER MoE sort buffer runs out of memory. EP8 stays at 0.85.
- `cluster.sh`: for either NIXL connector, set UCX defaults for the ionic RoCE NICs (RC verbs on `ionic_0`, GPU-direct RDMA) and run accuracy with one concurrent request. The router flag stays `--kv-connector nixl` for both.

MoRIIO steps do not change. All new settings apply only when `KV_CONNECTOR` is `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector`.

Requirement: the image's UCX must support `rc_verbs` on ionic NICs that report `max_srq=0`. The results below used UCX 1.22 with that support. The 2P2D EP16 write result also used the writer-thread ownership from #62055.

## Test plan

UCX environment (the same on every node):

```bash
export UCX_TLS=rc_verbs,ud_verbs,tcp,self,rocm
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=ionic_0:1,lo
export UCX_IB_GID_INDEX=1
export UCX_UD_VERBS_ETH_DGID_CHECK=n
export UCX_IB_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA=yes
export UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y
export UCX_PROTO_EMULATION_ENABLE=n
export UCX_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL=inf
export UCX_UD_VERBS_RX_QUEUE_LEN=1024
export UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED=1024
```

KV config (`kv_role` is `kv_producer` on prefill and `kv_consumer` on decode):

```bash
KV='{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["UCX"],"kv_lease_duration":180}}'
```

Write uses the same commands with `"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector"`.

TP8, prefill (port 8100) and decode (port 8200, `kv_consumer`):

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --host $PREFILL_IP --port 8100 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

EP8/DP8, prefill:

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --port 20005 -tp 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address $PREFILL_IP --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --api-server-count 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

EP8/DP8, decode: the same command with `--data-parallel-address $DECODE_IP`, `--all2all-backend mori_low_latency`, no `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`, and `kv_consumer`.

2P2D EP16/DP16 uses the same EP command with `--data-parallel-size 16` on four nodes. Prefill uses `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`. The second prefill node and the second decode node join headless with `--data-parallel-start-rank 8`. The router points only at the two masters. Write uses `NixlPushConnector` and the #62055 writer.

Router (`--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` for TP8, `8` for EP8 and EP16):

```bash
vllm-router --vllm-pd-disaggregation --kv-connector nixl \
  --prefill http://$PREFILL_IP:8100 --decode http://$DECODE_IP:8200 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 1800 --port 30000 --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --intra-node-data-parallel-size 1 --policy round_robin \
  --prefill-policy round_robin --decode-policy round_robin
```

For 2P2D EP16 the router uses `--worker-startup-timeout-secs 7200` and `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 8`.

Accuracy:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args model=DeepSeek-V3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True
```

Script checks: `bash -n` on all changed scripts, YAML parse, NIXL KV config parses as JSON, router arguments checked for 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8 and 2P2D EP16, `git diff --check`.

## Results

GSM8K (5-shot) exact_match. KV moved GPU memory to GPU memory over `rc_verbs/ionic_0`.

| Config | Connector | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1P1D TP8 | NixlConnector | 0.92 | 0.92 |
| 1P1D EP8/DP8 | NixlConnector | 0.94 | 0.94 |
| 2P2D EP16/DP16 | NixlConnector | 0.964 | 0.964 |
| 1P1D TP8 | NixlPushConnector | 0.98 | 0.98 |
| 1P1D EP8/DP8 | NixlPushConnector | 0.94 | 0.94 |
| 2P2D EP16/DP16 | NixlPushConnector | 0.96 | 0.96 |

The 2P2D EP16 write row used the writer-thread ownership from #62055.

title: [Perf][EPLB][DSv4] Add a symm_mem weight-migration backend and fuse MegaMoE replica mapping
author: abmfy
body:
## Overview

This PR makes EPLB cheaper for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, running DP attention with EP MegaMoE on multi-node NVLink. It does three things:

- adds an opt-in `symm_mem` weight-migration backend;
- fuses EPLB's logical→physical replica mapping and expert-load recording into the DeepGEMM MegaMoE staging kernels;
- takes async EPLB's host work off the decode critical path.

Not a duplicate. No open or merged PR adds a symmetric-memory EPLB backend or fuses the MegaMoE mapping. #61176 and #61839 enable EPLB for the ROCm AITER MegaMoE backend. Related: #61767 (`cpu_all_reduce_`, reused here), #57549, #56716, #61643. #61395 (EPLB for the V4.1 DSpark draft) runs together with this PR in the GB300 validation.

## Claims

- With this PR and #61395, EPLB raises DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode throughput on GB300 NVL72 by +12.0% at DEP16 and +25.0% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank, and by +26.2% at DEP32 with 128 req/rank. At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, main-model MegaMoE drops from 14.7 to 7.6 ms per step. Earlier GB200 runs on an older build showed smaller gains; see Validation.
- `symm_mem`: senders push expert rows into the receiver's `expert_buffer`, which is allocated in CUDA symmetric memory. There is no staging buffer, and it needs no memory beyond `expert_buffer`. Cross-node peer copies run at about 800 GB/s, against about 88 GB/s for NIXL, and a 40-layer rearrangement transfers in 0.3–0.6 s at DEP32.
- MegaMoE layers no longer launch a separate EPLB mapping kernel, which saves 5–6 µs per layer. The replica choice is shared with the router through one Triton helper, so physical ids and load counts match `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` exactly.
- Async EPLB no longer adds a GPU→host sync to the decode loop. It also raises on every rank when the worker fails on any rank, instead of stalling.

## Validation

### GB300 NVL72

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-aarch64-dev-20261019`, which is main 49cb2bbf71 (2026-10-16) with this PR and #61395 copied over the installed `vllm` package. The PR code in the image predates the rebase and the last cleanup commit, which changes no runtime behavior.

Setup: decode only, DSpark with 5 draft tokens, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached). EPLB with one redundant expert per rank, `window_size` 1000, `step_interval` 3000, async. Throughput is the output rate from 120 to 240 s into the steady part of the decode pass, after EPLB's first rearrangement on steady traffic. The arms alternate on the same nodes, n=3 per arm.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | Target EPLB (tok/s) | Target + draft EPLB (tok/s) | Δ target (Welch t) | Δ both (Welch t) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 314.7k ± 1.1k | 349.8k ± 1.5k | 352.5k ± 1.0k | +11.1% (33) | +12.0% (43) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 586.0k ± 0.7k | 721.9k ± 3.2k | 732.7k ± 4.5k | +23.2% (72) | +25.0% (56) |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 710.6k ± 2.0k | 895.7k ± 0.9k | 897.1k ± 5.3k | +26.0% (147) | +26.2% (57) |

- Balancing the draft on top of the target adds +1.5% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank (t=3.4) and +0.8% at DEP16 (t=2.6). At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, +0.2% is not resolved (t=0.5).
- Balancedness (mean ÷ max rank load per step, 72 req/rank), off → on: target 0.50 → 0.95 at DEP16 and 0.35 → 0.94 at DEP32; draft 0.36 → 0.94 at DEP16 and 0.21 → 0.89 at DEP32.

Per-step GPU time, DEP32 with 128 req/rank (mean of four 3 s CUDA profiles per arm over one rearrangement cycle, all 32 ranks):

| | EPLB off | Target EPLB | Target + draft EPLB |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main-model MegaMoE | 14.65 ms | 7.62 ms | 7.63 ms |
| DSpark draft MegaMoE | 0.93 ms | 0.92 ms | 0.55 ms |
| All other kernels | 16.03 ms | 16.14 ms | 16.18 ms |
| Decode step | 31.70 ms | 24.80 ms | 24.47 ms |

GSM8K, same image and server flags, with EPLB rearranging during the eval: `num_redundant_experts` = DP, `window_size` 50, `step_interval` 150, so every pass runs five 40-layer rearrangements with requests in flight. A rearrangement takes 1.6–1.9 s at DEP32. 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, concurrency 64. Off and on alternate, with two server starts per arm and two passes per start.

| Config | EPLB off (4 passes) | `symm_mem`, target + draft (4 passes) | Δ, paired bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16 | 0.902 | 0.898 | −0.40 pp [−1.08, +0.27] |
| DEP32 | 0.903 | 0.905 | +0.21 pp [−0.45, +0.85] |

The number of questions whose answer differs between an EPLB pass and an off pass (66–95) is in the same range as between two off passes (71–92).

Tests after rebasing onto 5d35ce3934, one GB300 node with 4 GPUs, run from this branch's source inside the image above (the PR changes only Python files):

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py -k "eplb or capture"` (incl. `test_prepare_megamoe_eplb_maps_and_records_under_graph_replay`) | 5 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 34 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k "symm_mem or gloo or registers"` | 19 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py` | 14 passed |

### Earlier GB200 NVL72 runs

These runs show smaller EPLB gains than the GB300 runs above. Besides the hardware, they differ in build (nightly fe4df3df, 2026-10-12, before #56716 kept warmup out of the EPLB load stats) and in measurement window (the whole 16k-token pass, not a steady window after a rearrangement on steady traffic).

Hardware: GB200 NVL72, 4 GPUs per node.

Serving setup: DSpark with 5 draft tokens, MRV2, FULL CUDA graphs, async scheduling.

EPLB setup: `{"num_redundant_experts": <DP>, "window_size": 1000, "step_interval": 3000, "use_async": true, "communicator": "symm_mem"}`, i.e. one redundant expert per rank.

Workload: decode only, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached), 16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, and requests pinned evenly to DP ranks. Throughput is the output rate over the window in which every request is decoding.

Off and on arms ran interleaved (ABAB) on the same nodes. These runs used a branch of nightly fe4df3df (2026-10-12) with this change set and #61767, before the rebase and without the second commit.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | EPLB on (tok/s) | Δ | Welch t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 223.6k ± 2.0k (n=4) | 228.1k ± 4.2k (n=4) | +2.0% | 2.0 (not resolved) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 419.5k ± 1.3k (n=4) | 435.1k ± 5.8k (n=4) | +3.7% | 5.3 |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 500.7k ± 5.1k (n=3) | 539.4k ± 9.7k (n=3) | +7.7% | 6.1 |

- DEP16 step time, p50 of 2000-step windows at full batch, same build: 24.34 / 24.28 ms off vs 23.61 / 23.25 ms on.
- At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, one pass per arm is excluded. A host stall unrelated to EPLB cut that pass by 13–34%.

Per-step breakdown, DEP32 with 128 req/rank:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
|---|---|---|
| Step time (CUDA events, unprofiled) | 38.8 ms | 36.5 ms |
| GPU idle at the step boundary | 0.27 ms | 0.27 ms |
| Main-model MegaMoE (5 s CUDA profile) | 18.1 ms | 13.4 ms |
| All other kernels (same profile) | 21.5 ms | 21.2 ms |

The GPU never waits on the host, so the MegaMoE saving turns into step time. MegaMoE is about 40% of the step, which caps the end-to-end gain.

Microbenchmarks (GB200):

- **Fused EPLB staging**, one MoE layer, hidden 5120, top-k 6, 384 logical experts. Each arm is timed as a CUDA graph replay, median of 200. Outputs, ids and load counts match main bit for bit in every case.

  | Format | Tokens | Physical experts | main: `torch.where` + map kernel + staging | Fused | Saved |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MXFP8 | 432 | 400 | 9.4 µs | 4.2 µs | 5.1 µs |
  | MXFP8 | 768 | 416 | 11.0 µs | 4.7 µs | 6.3 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 432 | 400 | 49.5 µs | 44.0 µs | 5.5 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 768 | 416 | 49.1 µs | 43.8 µs | 5.3 µs |

  That is about 0.2 ms per decode step across 40 MoE layers.
- **Weight-migration bandwidth**, 2 nodes, one MegaMoE layer of 25 experts (470 MB):

  | Path | Bandwidth |
  |---|---|
  | `symm_mem` peer copies, intra- or cross-node over multi-node NVLink | ~808 GB/s (bulk), ~294 GB/s (100 per-tensor copies) |
  | NIXL, cross-node | ~88 GB/s (UCX picks RoCE, not multi-node NVLink) |
  | NIXL, cross-node, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp` | ~0.12 GB/s (TCP) |

- **MegaMoE kernel time under serving load**, DEP16 with 72 req/rank, layers 2–40: p50 per call drops 12.6–14.0% across three profiled runs (222→194 µs). Layer 1 is excluded because it absorbs cross-rank arrival skew.

Tests on one GB200 node with 4 GPUs, before the rebase onto 5d35ce3934. The GB300 section has the rerun after it.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` | 110 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k eplb` | 18 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` | 35 passed, 14 skipped (NIXL not installed, XPU) |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k nixl`, NIXL installed | 7 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 6 passed, 28 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` | 13 passed, 7 passed |

GSM8K on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (one node):
- Setup: 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, `num_redundant_experts=16`, `window_size=100`, `step_interval=300`. Every arm rearranged all 40 layers four times during the eval.
- Command: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`

| Arm | Accuracy (2 passes) | 40-layer rearrangement |
|---|---|---|
| EPLB off | 0.898, 0.901 | — |
| `symm_mem` | 0.897, 0.895 | 2.9–3.3 s |
| `symm_mem`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 0.889, 0.883 | 2.9–3.3 s, no sync error |
| `nixl` | 0.892, 0.886 | 2.7–3.2 s |

The EPLB-off and `nixl` arms ran on the commit before the final cleanup, which does not touch either path. Within one node, `symm_mem` and NIXL (CUDA IPC) move weights at a similar rate; `symm_mem`'s advantage is across nodes over multi-node NVLink.

## Details

**`symm_mem` backend**
- The receive buffer is one symmetric `uint8` buffer per EP group, set up with a single rendezvous and carved into per-tensor views. The backend checks the NVLink/MNNVL domain before allocating.
- Senders and receivers derive each receive row from the global placement with the same helper, so `add_recv` is a no-op. Push backends get every rank's rows through a new `recv_rows` argument to `set_transfer_context`. This argument is optional and other backends ignore it.
- Each `execute()` runs two CPU barriers. GPU spin barriers can deadlock against MegaMoE's cooperative launches.
- Rejected with elastic EP. The buffer lives outside the caching allocator, so sleep mode does not free it.

**Fused mapping**: `fused_moe/eplb_triton.py` holds the replica hash, map lookup and gated load count. The MXFP8/BF16 and NVFP4 staging kernels call it, and so does the router kernel. Routed-experts capture still sees logical ids.

**Async EPLB**
- Per-layer maps are committed with pinned non-blocking copies, and the worker thread fences `expert_buffer` reuse.
- Balancedness stats are read back non-blocking and logged in order once they land.
- `should_record_tensor` is rewritten only when its value flips.
- The per-step "all ranks ready" check runs over `cpu_all_reduce_`. A gloo ring all-reduce costs several ms per step at DP16/DP32.

**Also**
- `logical_to_physical_map` is sized to R+1 slots unless elastic EP is on.
- `compute_logical_maps` is vectorized.
- DeepSeek V4.1 decoder-replay padding and dummy rows are marked as padding, which complements #61643.

**CI**: the `symm_mem` execution tests need NVLink peers. They are added to the optional 8×H100 "Distributed DP + EP" job; the 4×L4 EPLB job skips them. The MegaMoE staging test needs SM100.

**Limitations**
- In mixed prefill/decode serving, per-rank prefill imbalance bounds the step. There, EPLB mostly lowers tail TTFT rather than raising throughput.
- Likely rebase overlap with #61786, #59168 and #41141. Offline placements without elastic EP (#41141) could exceed R+1 replicas.

title: [Perf] Enable DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits on the FP8 indexer cache, DSv4.1
author: LopezCastroRoberto
body:
## Purpose

`attention_config.indexer_sparse_logits` (#56254) lets DeepSeek-V4.1's candidate-consuming indexer layers score only the candidate blocks with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels instead of dense logits over the whole context. Today it requires the MXFP4 indexer cache (`indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"`), so with the default FP8 cache the flag fails at startup:

```
ValueError: attention_config.indexer_sparse_logits requires the MXFP4 indexer cache
```

The restriction dates from before #61149: the FP8 cache then stored one fp32 scale per token, while the sparse kernels take UE8M0-packed (granularity-32) scales. Since #61149, the SM100 FP8 indexer cache stores each token's power-of-two scale as four equal UE8M0 bytes, which is exactly the MXFP8 layout DeepGEMM expects, and DeepGEMM's sparse kernels already have an FP8 (`float_e4m3_t`, `SM100_MMA_MXF8F6F4_SS`) variant for both the contiguous (prefill) and paged (decode) paths. Its paged accessor reads the same page layout as vLLM's FP8 cache (`PAGE_KV x 128` value bytes, then `PAGE_KV` uint32 scales).

This PR wires the FP8 cache into the existing sparse path, so the decode speedup no longer requires trading the K cache down to 4 bits.

## Results

title: [Kernel] Allow registering OOT block-scaled FP8 linear kernels
author: R3hankhan123
body:
## Overview

Lets out-of-tree platforms register block-scaled FP8 linear kernels by adding `kernel_type="fp8_block"` to `register_linear_kernel`.

## Claims

- `register_linear_kernel(..., kernel_type="fp8_block")` adds the kernel to `_POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_KERNELS`.
- OOT platforms can now serve `--quantization fp8_per_block`, which previously failed during kernel selection because the OOT platform had no entry in the block-kernel list.
- The docstring now lists every `kernel_type` the function accepts. It previously listed only `mp`, `int8` and `fp8`.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX).
- The change adds one `elif` branch that matches the existing `fp8`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`, `mxfp4` and `mxfp6` branches. Existing kernel types behave as before.

## Details

`Fp8PerBlockOnlineLinearMethod` (and `Fp8LinearMethod` with `block_quant`) use a `GroupShape(1, 128)` activation key. Because `is_per_group()` is true for that shape, `init_fp8_linear_kernel` picks the kernel from `_POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_KERNELS`. That dict only has entries for CUDA, ROCm, CPU and XPU, and `register_linear_kernel` had no way to add to it. An OOT platform that registered its FP8 kernel with `kernel_type="fp8"` therefore got per-tensor and per-channel FP8 but never block-wise.

To support both, an OOT plugin registers the same class twice, once as `"fp8"` and once as `"fp8_block"`. If that class subclasses `FP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, the block path already builds it with `layer_param_names` (see the `issubclass` branch in `init_fp8_linear_kernel`), so no new base class or interface change is needed.

title: [Perf][Parser] Stream Qwen3 tool argument values incrementally (12 KB call: 2.1 s to 11 ms)
author: deadstrobe5
body:
## Overview

Streaming a Qwen3 XML tool call re-parses the whole argument on every delta: `_qwen3_arg_converter`, then `_safe_arg_prefix`, a per-character Python loop over the full JSON. A long parameter value, such as a file written by a coding agent, costs quadratic CPU on the API server. This adopts the `arg_value_extender` hook from #61253 (GLM) and #61494 (Gemma4) for the Qwen3 grammar.

## Claims

- Parser cost per delta no longer grows with argument length: 1.1 ms at 12 KB and 2.2 ms at 25 KB become about 4 us at every size.
- A 12 KB `write_file` call (2,788 Qwen3 tokens) goes from 2.1 s to 11 ms of parser time. A 25 KB call goes from 8.4 s to 22 ms.
- Streamed deltas are unchanged, including newline trimming, schema coercion and truncated calls.
- Covers every parser on `qwen3_config` (qwen3_coder, qwen3_xml, Seed-OSS, Step3p5, Nemotron-v3, Granite thinking, MiniCPM-V). MiMo gets a variant without newline trimming, since its converter keeps values verbatim.

## Validation

`pytest tests/parser/engine`: 6026 passed. Also passed: the qwen3coder, step3p5 and minicpm5xml tool parser tests, the qwen3, nemotron_v3, granite_thinking and step3p5 reasoning tests, and `tests/parser/test_streaming.py`, `test_parse.py` and `test_abstract_parser.py`. ruff and mypy pass on the changed files.

New tests in `TestArgValueExtender`: long Qwen3 and MiMo calls with escapes, blank lines and prefixes of the closing tags stream the same arguments as `extract_tool_calls`; converter calls stay constant from 20 to 200 lines (they grow on `main`); a closer split across deltas and a split next `<parameter=`; and the cases where no extender is created.

A local differential fuzz streamed 27,500 random Qwen3 and MiMo calls with and without the extender: random chunk sizes, schemas with string, integer, boolean, object and nullable keys, repeated keys, whitespace-variant closers, tag fragments inside values, and truncated calls. Every per-delta `DeltaMessage` was identical, and about 194K deltas went through the extender. Breaking the newline hold-back, the split-closer window or the leading-newline strip made the fuzz fail.

Benchmark: `Qwen3Parser.parse_delta`, one real Qwen3 token per delta, Apple M5, Python 3.12, 7 alternating runs.

| Argument size | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 KB | 187-192 us | 3.9-4.1 us |
| 12 KB | 1.09-1.44 ms | 3.8-4.6 us |
| 25 KB | 2.21 ms | 3.8 us |

A short three-parameter call also gets about 10% faster (338 us to 304 us), because each delta skips a conversion. I couldn't run a GPU server end to end; model output is unchanged by construction.

## Details

The extender reads the open value with the same regexes as the converter. It refuses when the open key repeats an earlier one, since that key keeps its first position in the JSON. A delta that completes `</parameter>` or the next `<parameter=` (whitespace variants included, even split across deltas) returns None, and the converter takes over again. A future change to `_PARAM_RE` needs a matching change to `_PARAM_VALUE_END_RE`.

title: [Attention] Use trtllm-gen for the FlashInfer DCP prefill context pass
author: GagandeepKang-cohere
body:
## Overview Run the FlashInfer DCP prefill context pass on the trtllm-gen context kernel (non-causal, with LSE) instead of the native FlashInfer kernel, under the same conditions in which non-DCP prefill auto-selects trtllm-gen. No existing PR switches this kernel; #58519 is complementary (it reduces overhead around the same pass). ## Claims - On 8×B200 (TP8, DCP2), 100k input / 512 output: mean TTFT −39–48% and output throughput 1.23–1.79× across concurrency 1–32. - On 4×B200 (TP4, DCP2) with GLM-4-9B, same workload: mean TTFT −37–44% and output throughput 1.26–1.68× across concurrency 1–32. - Accuracy matches the native path (MRCR, GSM8K), and a new kernel test checks the pass against the native one. - Applies on SM100/SM103 when trtllm-gen prefill is available (`--attention-config.use_trtllm_attention` not 0) with an unquantized KV cache, to layers without a sliding window or soft-capping. Other layers keep the native kernel. ## Validation Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP8 / DCP2 / EP8, a2a DCP combine, prefix caching off, one run per arm. | Concurrency | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT ms | Mean TPOT ms | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 106.9 → 131.5 (1.23×) | 2190 → 1332 | 5.1 → 5.0 | | 2 | 151.3 → 204.6 (1.35×) | 3203 → 1881 | 7.0 → 6.1 | | 4 | 190.8 → 287.2 (1.51×) | 5061 → 2832 | 11.1 → 8.4 | | 8 | 221.7 → 364.9 (1.65×) | 8722 → 4675 | 19.0 → 12.8 | | 16 | 239.3 → 414.0 (1.73×) | 12875 → 6792 | 41.6 → 25.3 | | 32 | 250.7 → 448.8 (1.79×) | 16277 → 8460 | 95.6 → 54.5 | TPOT improves at higher concurrency only because decode steps share batches with shorter prefill chunks. GLM-4-9B-chat (32 Q / 2 KV heads), 4×B200, TP4 / DCP2, a2a DCP combine, prefix caching off, one run per arm. | Concurrency | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT ms | Mean TPOT ms | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 90.3 → 113.9 (1.26×) | 3220 → 2019 | 4.8 → 4.8 | | 2 | 117.9 → 162.2 (1.38×) | 4851 → 3073 | 7.5 → 6.3 | | 4 | 140.2 → 209.8 (1.50×) | 7836 → 4837 | 13.2 → 9.6 | | 8 | 154.4 → 245.4 (1.59×) | 13599 → 8145 | 25.3 → 16.7 | | 16 | 163.2 → 270.1 (1.66×) | 24774 → 14267 | 49.7 → 31.4 | | 32 | 168.1 → 282.6 (1.68×) | 33043 → 18366 | 125.9 → 77.4 | | Eval (real weights) | Native | trtllm-gen | |---|---|---| | MRCR match ratio (40 samples) | 0.480 | 0.496 | | GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot) | 0.888 | 0.899 | Both accuracy differences are within noise. A kernel-level comparison against the native kernel (all layers and ranks, real metadata) gave max relative output error 2.3e-4 and matching LSE. These runs used an earlier revision of this PR that was opt-in through an env var and included `q_scale` (1.0 for this checkpoint) in `bmm1_scale`; the kernel path is otherwise unchanged. `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_attention.py -k dcp_prefill` on B200: TODO.
Commands ```bash # Baseline: the parent commit. --load-format dummy for perf vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 2 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \ --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --max-model-len 128000 --max-num-seqs 256 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --generation-config vllm vllm bench serve --backend openai --dataset-name random --random-input-len 100000 --random-output-len 512 \ --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts $((C*4 < 8 ? 8 : C*4)) --max-concurrency $C --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 0 python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py --port 8000 --num-samples 40 --concurrency 8 python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64 # GLM-4-9B on 4 GPUs: same bench command vllm serve THUDM/glm-4-9b-chat-hf --tensor-parallel-size 4 --decode-context-parallel-size 2 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \ --attention-backend FLASHINFER --max-model-len 128000 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching --generation-config vllm --load-format dummy \ --compilation-config '{"custom_ops":["all"]}' ```
## Details - **Kernel.** `trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache(causal=False, return_lse=True)` over the DCP-local paged KV. Its LSE is base 2 like the native kernel's, so the combine and merge are unchanged. Non-causal mode and LSE output (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3020, #3116) postdate the original FlashInfer DCP support (#25438). The native context wrapper is not planned when this kernel runs. - **Requests with no local context.** The kernel's LSE for these rows is unspecified: FlashInfer computes it from softmax stats in the reused workspace, which the kernel never writes for `kv_len == 0`. Stale values corrupted the merge intermittently. These rows are masked as empty shards in the combine (`seq_lens` / `query_start_loc`), as on the trtllm DCP decode path, and the output is zero-initialized because the all-gather combine multiplies it by a zero weight. - **Test.** `test_flashinfer_dcp_prefill_trtllm_context` compares the pass with the native one, including requests with no local context, and runs in the "(B200) Kernels" CI job. The GQA DCP end-to-end test in `tests/distributed/test_context_parallel.py` needs 4 GPUs and only runs on SM90, so it does not cover Blackwell. - **Limitations.** FP8 KV keeps the native kernel; FlashInfer DCP with FP8 KV currently fails at startup on SM100 independently of this PR, to be fixed separately. `use_trtllm_attention=0` disables this together with trtllm-gen decode, as it does for non-DCP prefill. ---

title: [Perf][Parser] Stream MiniMax M2 tool argument values incrementally (16 KB call: 5.9 s to 26 ms)
author: deadstrobe5
body:
## Overview

The MiniMax M2 parser re-runs its argument converter and the engine's safe-prefix scan over the whole argument on every streamed delta, so a long parameter value (write_file, code edits) costs quadratic CPU. This adds an `arg_value_extender` for the MiniMax M2 config, the same mechanism glm47 (#61253) and gemma4 (#61494) use.

## Claims

- Parser CPU for a streamed write_file call, one Qwen3 token per delta: 1 KB 31.8 ms to 2.1 ms, 4 KB 387 ms to 6.7 ms, 16 KB 5.9 s to 26 ms. At 32 KB the old path took 22.6 s.
- Streamed output is unchanged.

## Validation

- A/B in fresh processes, 7 runs per side, median [min-max]: 16 KB 5921 [5859-6003] ms vs 25.6 [25.2-26.2] ms.
- Differential fuzz over 44k random streams (random chunking, split and spaced tags, quotes in names, unclosed values, truncated input, several invokes, with and without a schema): every per-delta `DeltaMessage` matches the parser without the extender. Disabling each guard in the extender makes the fuzz fail.
- New tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_minimax_m2.py`: streamed arguments match non-streaming extraction with and without a schema, converter calls do not grow with argument length, split closing and next-parameter tags end the value, and the cases where no extender should be built.
- `pytest tests/parser/engine tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m2_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning` passes; ruff and mypy are clean.

## Details

The converter is split into `_minimax_m2_parse_args`, which also returns the match of the open trailing value. The extender is built only when that value is the last JSON value and its opener can't re-parse once more text arrives, which rules out an earlier unmatched `<parameter name=` and a bare name that starts with a quote. It keeps a small window from the last `<` so a value end split across deltas (`</param` + `eter>`, `< parameter` + ` name =`) is still detected, and then hands back to the converter.

title: [Bugfix][Sampler] Carry the boundary tie count across blocks in the split top-p mask kernel
author: cipheraxat
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61997. The split top-p mask kernel (`_topp_sb_mask_kernel`) restarts its count of tied boundary tokens at every 8192-entry block. Slices longer than one block therefore keep too many copies of the boundary value. This PR carries the count across blocks, as the monolithic kernel already does.

## Claims

- In the split top-p pipeline (top-p-only rows, batch ≤ 64, CUDA/ROCm), the number of copies of a tied boundary value that are kept now matches the sort-based reference. The kept copies are the first ones in index order, as the cross-slice logic intends.
- Rows without an exact tie at the boundary, and rows whose ties fit in one block, are unchanged.

## Validation

All runs on an NVIDIA L4 (58 SMs, so S=1 at B=64; torch 2.14.0+cu132), branch at `bc6de71192`, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

**New test, unfixed kernel (`main` version of `topk_topp_triton.py`):** fails as expected.

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -k test_topp_ties_across_blocks
E   AssertionError: kept [4160], expected [2300]
1 failed, 133 deselected
```

**Fixed kernel, the whole Triton class:**

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -k TestTritonTopkTopp -v
95 passed, 39 deselected in 210.12s
```

**Issue's repro script** (4096 tied tokens at the boundary, B=64, p=0.7, run against the `main` kernel file; the script patches its own copy with the same line as this PR):

| kernel | ties over 8 blocks | ties in 1 block |
|---|---|---|
| float64 reference | 1913 (mass 0.700) | 1913 (mass 0.700) |
| `main` | 4160 (mass 0.994) | 1913 (mass 0.700) |
| this PR | 1913 (mass 0.700) | 1913 (mass 0.700) |

**End to end:** `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` routes top-p through these Triton kernels. With it set, `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")` generated 16 prompts with `SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=48)`, which uses the split path at batch ≤ 16. All 16 completions came back with no errors, and the text reads normally.

## Details

**Root cause.** A copy of the boundary value `dup` gets rank `num_preceding + cumsum(dmask)`, and only copies with rank ≤ `numkeep` are kept. Here `num_preceding` is the number of copies in lower-indexed slices. The block loop never advanced `num_preceding`, so every block of a slice ranked its copies starting from the same base. Each block could keep up to `numkeep - num_preceding` copies of its own. Only slices longer than `BLOCK=8192` are affected, i.e. `S < V / 8192`. On current GPUs, S is 1 or 2 at batch 64, so every current vocab hits this.

**Fix.** Add `num_preceding += tl.sum(dmask.to(tl.float32))` after each block. It counts every copy, kept or not, which matches how the cross-slice `num_preceding` is built from `nmin`. The monolithic kernel counts kept copies (`num_kept += tl.sum(duplicate_keep_mask)`), which is equivalent here. The added work is one block reduction per block, and it runs only when the row has a tie at the boundary.

**Test.** `test_topp_ties_across_blocks` spreads 4096 tied tokens over every block of the row, at stride 37 in a 151936-entry vocab. It adds 64 higher tokens and a `-8.0` tail, and sets `p=0.75`, so the boundary falls mid-copy inside the tie group. That keeps the fp32 reference from landing one copy off. The tail matters: if the tied value were the row's minimum, the ladder search could not place a pivot below it, and the row would take the keep-everything fallback before reaching the mask loop. The test asserts that the kept count equals `apply_top_k_top_p_pytorch`, and that the kept copies are an index-ordered prefix. The existing `test_topp_tie_break_deterministic` puts all its ties in one block, so it can't catch this. B=64 gives multi-block slices on any GPU with fewer than 256 SMs. That includes the H200 MIG slice used by the "V1 Sample" CI step. The test also still covers this after #61996, which shrinks slices to about 9.5K entries (two blocks) at this vocab.

**Not duplicating:** the issue has no comments or assignee, and searches for the issue number, `num_preceding`, `topp_sb_mask` and "split top-p tie" turned up no PR. #61996, also by the reporter, changes `_topp_split_count` but not the mask loop.

**Model evals:** the `tests/evals/gsm8k` configs either decode greedily or sample without `top_p`, so none of them reaches the split top-p path. They can't measure this change. The kernel-level comparison against a float64 reference is above.

cc @njhill @abmfy

title: [MoE] Use the sorted fused-MoE path for host-resident expert weights
author: mushroomcarbon
body:
## Overview

At small batch (`num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= num_experts`, e.g. up to 4 tokens for Qwen3 MoE) the Triton fused-MoE path skips `moe_align_block_size` and gives every (token, expert) pair its own block (#29354, #39016). That saves the alignment kernel when weights are in device memory. With UVA weight offloading (`--offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-params experts`) the expert weights are read from host memory in place, and an expert routed to several tokens is then read over PCIe once per token. This PR takes the sorted path when the expert weights carry the UVA offload marker, so each routed expert is read once per step. Device-resident weights keep the naive path.

## Claims

On RTX 4090 (PCIe 4.0 x16), natural-text chat requests, 128 output tokens:

- Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8, one GPU, 16 GiB of experts offloaded: **+7% / +10% / +15–19% output throughput at 2 / 3 / 4 requests in flight**; unchanged at 1, 8 and 16.
- Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8, TP8, 16 GiB per GPU offloaded: **+7% / +10% / +18% at 2 / 3 / 4**; unchanged at 1.
- Base is the vLLM 0.31.0 wheel, whose two touched files are byte-identical to the base commit. Measured on CUDA only; ROCm's Triton path takes the same branch.
- No change without offloading: the code path is the same; measured on the 30B at TP2 with weights in VRAM (one start per build).
- Quality: GSM8K (lm-eval 0.4.13, 5-shot, greedy, first 250 questions, 4 requests in flight so decode steps take the changed path), 30B with 16 GiB offloaded: 0.888 flexible / 0.880 strict exact match for both builds, and all 250 responses byte-identical.
- Output: greedy completions identical to unpatched on the 30B (all starts). On the 235B at TP8 greedy output varies from start to start *without* the patch (three unpatched starts gave three different completions and three patched starts two, with one completion common to both builds), so it cannot distinguish the builds there.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "host_resident_weights or naive_block_assignment"`: 44 passed on an RTX 4090, on the original base and again after rebasing onto current main (nightly wheel of the base commit, patched files applied). The new `test_host_resident_weights_take_sorted_path` runs UVA-mapped weights (and device weights as the control) at 1/2/4 tokens through both the modular `TritonExperts` path and the legacy `fused_moe`, asserts that `moe_align_block_size` is called exactly when the weights are host-resident, and compares the output with `torch_moe` (inputs scaled to O(1) outputs, `atol=rtol=2e-2`). Without the change its 6 host-resident cases fail.
- Every applicable pre-commit hook passes: ruff check/format, mypy 3.10–3.13, `check_torch_cuda`, test tethering, typos, SPDX, lazy imports, forbidden imports, boolean context manager.
- End to end, base vLLM against this PR, one `vllm serve`, requests from a client sending natural-language chat prompts (32 topics × 8 tasks, temperature 0.7, a fixed seed per request, `ignore_eos`):

  | setup | in flight | starts (base / PR) | output tok/s, base | output tok/s, this PR | change |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 30B, 1 GPU, 16 GiB on host | 1 | 2 / 2 | 20.7 | 20.5–20.7 | −0.5% (within spread) |
  | | 2 | 2 / 2 | 22.2 | 23.8 | +7% |
  | | 3 | 2 / 2 | 22.6 | 24.9–25.0 | +10% |
  | | 4 | 2 / 2 | 23.1 | 26.5–27.4 | +15–19% |
  | | 8 | 2 / 2 | 34.5–34.9 | 33.5–35.0 | within spread |
  | | 16 | 2 / 2 | 49.0–49.1 | 48.5–49.1 | within spread |
  | 235B, TP8, 16 GiB/GPU on host | 1 | 1 / 1 | 16.6 | 16.6 | 0% |
  | | 2 | 3 / 3 | 17.9–18.3 | 19.1–19.5 | +7% |
  | | 3 | 3 / 3 | 19.0 | 20.9 | +10% |
  | | 4 | 3 / 3 | 19.7 | 23.2–23.3 | +18% |
  | 30B, TP2, all in VRAM | 1–4 | 1 / 1 | 196.8 / 300.3 / 364.1 / 474.8 | 197.0 / 300.6 / 363.0 / 473.5 | within 0.3% |
  | | 8 | 1 / 1 | 741.5 | 727.1 | −1.9% (one start; both builds run the same code here) |

- Reproducible with vLLM's own benchmark (`vllm bench serve --dataset-name sharegpt --sharegpt-output-len 128 --ignore-eos --num-prompts N --max-concurrency c --seed 1`, ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split; N = 8 for c < 4, else 2c), 30B on one GPU with 16 GiB offloaded, two starts each:

  | `--max-concurrency` | output tok/s, base | output tok/s, this PR | change (midpoints) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 20.3 | 20.3 | 0% |
  | 2 | 21.3–22.2 | 23.4–23.6 | +8% |
  | 3 | 21.6–22.6 | 25.3–25.4 | +15% |
  | 4 | 22.2–23.0 | 25.6–26.7 | +16% |

<details>
<summary>Server commands</summary>

```
# 30B, one GPU (GPU 0 on NUMA node 3 here), 16 GiB of experts on the host
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 numactl --cpunodebind=3 --membind=3 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 16 --cpu-offload-params experts
# 235B, TP8
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 16 --cpu-offload-params experts --kv-cache-dtype fp8
```
The table above the benchmark used our own client sending natural-language chat prompts (32 topics × 8 tasks, temperature 0.7, fixed seed per request, 128 tokens with `ignore_eos`; N requests at concurrency c, N = 8 for c < 4, else 2c; one unrecorded warm-up per level).

</details>

## Details

**Why.** With experts in host memory, a decode step's cost is dominated by the bytes it reads over PCIe, and on the naive path an expert routed to several of the step's tokens is read once per token. The sorted path reads each routed expert once per step. How much that saves depends on how often a step's tokens share experts: on natural-text prompts the gain is in the Validation table; on random-token prompts with greedy decoding, whose routing is far more repetitive, the same change doubles throughput at 4 requests in flight. We report natural text.

**Implementation.**

- `_prepare_expert_assignment` takes `weights_host_resident` (default `False`), which disables the naive block assignment.
- `TritonExperts.apply` and the legacy `fused_experts_impl` pass `_weights_host_resident(w1, w2)`: true when either weight has `_vllm_is_uva_offloaded`, which the UVA offloader sets (and `device_loading_context` re-sets after `process_weights_after_loading`). `w1`/`w2` are the layer's own parameters on this path, so it is a getattr per forward inside the `moe_forward` custom op; the result depends only on the parameters, so CUDA-graph capture per size is unaffected. "Either", because UVA offloads per parameter and a budget cut-off can leave w13 on the host and w2 on the device.
- Other MoE paths are unaffected: Marlin and `TritonWNA16Experts` always align; the prefetch offloader copies weights to the device before compute and never sets the marker. Two model-specific callers of `_prepare_expert_assignment` (`models/k2_horizon.py`, `models/dots3_note/nvidia/vision_moe.py`) do not pass the flag and keep today's behaviour; they can opt in separately.
- Why a per-forward check rather than a decision when the kernel is built: `replace_parameter` in `process_weights_after_loading` installs a new Parameter without the marker, and `device_loading_context` re-marks it only afterwards, so a setup-time check would read False.

**Related.** No open or merged PR makes this change (searched 2026-10-07, rechecked 2026-10-16). The naive path came from #29354 and #39016; #34920 (closed, stale) proposed making it tunable from configs; #55268 (open) warms up Triton MoE variants per batch size, and this PR changes which variant host-resident weights use at ≤ 4 tokens. #57215 (open) keeps MoE experts offloaded during weight post-processing on XPU, the marker lifecycle this PR relies on; #56177 (open) is a shared GPU expert pool. RFC #38256 discusses expert caches for offloaded MoE, where a comment reports the same effect with a GPU-side slot buffer (the naive path stops sharing an expert's weight tile between tokens at batch ≥ 2). #37190, #57794 and #57943 decide which experts stay in VRAM; this PR is independent of that and helps whichever experts remain on the host.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

title: [ROCm][Model] Add Beam 1.0 support on ROCm
author: jamesETsmith
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview


ROCm follow-up to [#61978](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61978), which adds day-0 support for Reflection's [Beam 1.0](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B) and its [DFlash2 drafter](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2).


EDIT: Since #61978 has been split into smaller PRs (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62042, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62052, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62074), I've updated against main and now the PR diff isn't swamped by the changes from #61978.

This PR adds AMD-owned implementations under `vllm/models/beam/amd/` for both `BeamForCausalLM` and `DFlash2BeamDraftModel`. The NVIDIA implementation from #61978 is unchanged in the relative diff. Shared package dispatch selects the AMD classes on ROCm and the NVIDIA classes elsewhere.

## Claims

- Beam 1.0 BF16 loads and serves on 8x MI350X with TP8 and expert parallelism through the AMD model path.
- Beam's required FP32 activation, normalization, Q/K preprocessing, attention-output gate, and logit-softcap arithmetic is retained in AMD-local Triton kernels.
- The AMD target uses standard vLLM ROCm attention and KV-cache updates, linear layers, finalized MoE output, and RCCL collectives rather than NVIDIA direct-cache, CuTe/FlashInfer, or MNNVL fast paths.
- The AMD DFlash2 implementation loads the released 1.93B drafter, generates successfully, and delegates cache writes and cache-format handling to the selected ROCm attention backend.
- The change adds no HIP/C++ kernels and does not modify the scheduler, KV-cache manager, model runner, attention backends, or NVIDIA Beam implementation.
- Added recipe in line with https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/issues/1107

### Serving commands

Target only:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --reasoning-parser beam \
  --tool-call-parser beam \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

With DFlash2:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --speculative-config '{
    "method": "dflash",
    "model": "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 8
  }'
```

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 10.1, PyTorch 2.13, TP8 with expert parallelism, Beam 1.0 BF16 and the BF16 DFlash2 drafter.

| Check | Target only | DFlash2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ruff checks and formatting | Passed | Passed |
| Current-source ROCm build | Passed | Passed |
| Full 501B checkpoint and drafter load | Passed | Passed |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, strict extraction | 1,202/1,319 (91.13% ± 0.78%) | 1,200/1,319 (90.98% ± 0.79%) |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, flexible extraction | 1,212/1,319 (91.89% ± 0.75%) | 1,212/1,319 (91.89% ± 0.75%) |

The GSM8K used 5-shot chat, greedy decoding, `max_gen_toks=1024`, TP8, and expert parallelism.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B,tensor_parallel_size=8,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=16384,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enable_expert_parallel=True \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size auto \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024
```

The lm-eval vLLM wrapper also accepts the top-level speculative aliases:

```text
spec_method=dflash,spec_model=/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2,spec_tokens=8
```

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model beam \
  --tokenizer /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dataset-name random \
  --num-prompts 10 \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 10 \
  --max-concurrency 10 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 42
```

</details>

### Short concurrency sweep
On NVIDIA SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` / `low_entropy`, with a fixed 1,024-token output, greedy decoding, 16 warmup requests per point, and `10 * concurrency` measured requests:

| Concurrency | Prompts | Target tok/s | DFlash2 tok/s | Speedup | Target TTFT | DFlash2 TTFT | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10 | 117.40 | 168.47 | 1.44x | 234.66 ms | 241.48 ms | 3.41 |
| 4 | 40 | 331.88 | 443.00 | 1.33x | 657.87 ms | 297.50 ms | 3.51 |
| 8 | 80 | 492.26 | 769.78 | 1.56x | 634.83 ms | 240.43 ms | 3.63 |
| 16 | 160 | 803.81 | 1,263.22 | 1.57x | 788.46 ms | 265.18 ms | 3.57 |

All 580 measured requests across both modes succeeded. DFlash2 token acceptance ranged from 30.13% to 32.83%. These are single runs without variability estimates.

<details>
<summary>SPEED-Bench run configuration</summary>

Both servers used the same target configuration:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --served-model-name beam \
  --disable-log-requests
```

The DFlash2 server added:

```bash
--speculative-config '{
  "method": "dflash",
  "model": "/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 8
}'
```

Each server was reused across all four concurrency points. `vllm bench serve` issued its initial probe and 16 warmup requests before the measured requests at each point:

```bash
for concurrency in 1 4 8 16; do
  num_prompts=$((10 * concurrency))
  vllm bench serve \
    --backend vllm \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --model beam \
    --tokenizer /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
    --dataset-name speed_bench \
    --dataset-path /path/to/prepared/speed-bench \
    --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_8k \
    --speed-bench-category low_entropy \
    --speed-bench-output-len 1024 \
    --num-prompts "${num_prompts}" \
    --num-warmups 16 \
    --max-concurrency "${concurrency}" \
    --request-rate inf \
    --ignore-eos \
    --temperature 0 \
    --seed 42
done
```

</details>

### Remaining validation

- [x] Accuracy benchmarks (with and without dflash2)
  - [X] GSM8k 
  - [x] GPQA-diamond
  - [x] AIME2025
- [X] Performance baseline using NVIDIA [speedbench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) 8k with low entropy and 1k fixed OSL
- [x] Same checks for gfx942

## Details

- **Vendor ownership:** All ROCm target and DFlash2 implementation code lives under `vllm/models/beam/amd/`. The relative diff does not modify `vllm/models/beam/nvidia/`.
- **Platform dispatch:** `vllm.models.beam` exports AMD target and draft classes on ROCm and NVIDIA classes on other platforms.
- **Target execution:** AMD attention uses ordinary backend-owned K/V cache updates. AMD projections use standard vLLM linear layers, MoE returns finalized output normally, and distributed reductions use standard RCCL paths.
- **DFlash2 cache handling:** AMD-local Triton computes context K normalization and RoPE. Cache layout, slot scattering, optional shuffling, and quantization are delegated to each ROCm attention backend's native cache-update API rather than hard-coded pointer arithmetic.
- **Numerics:** AMD-local Triton kernels retain Beam's required FP32 operations and intermediate BF16 rounding boundaries.
- **HIP launch compatibility:** AMD kernels omit CUDA-only Triton launch options such as `enable_reflect_ftz` and `launch_pdl`.
- **Footprint:** 1,968 additions and 2 deletions across 12 Beam model files; no core execution or NVIDIA implementation changes.

AI assistance was used. The submitter should review every changed line and this description before converting the PR from draft.

title: [Model] Add Reflection Beam
author: WoosukKwon
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add day-0 support for Reflection's Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`), a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters, and its DFlash2 drafter (`DFlash2BeamDraftModel`). This is the model slice of #61978.

Builds on #62042 (merged). This PR doesn't need FlashInfer nightly. The `beam` reasoning and tool parsers are in #62052. The fused MNNVL all-reduce (with Beam's norm and MoE-finalize epilogue) is split out into a stacked follow-up PR. MegaMoE support (attention DP + expert parallelism on FlashInfer CuTeDSL), which does need FlashInfer nightly, follows in #62073.

## Claims

- **Architecture:**
  - hybrid sliding-window (RoPE) and full-attention NoPE layers with SSMax;
  - per-head Q/K norm and a sigmoid output gate;
  - DeepSeek-V3-style MoE with an FP32 router;
  - sandwich norms and depth-scaled residuals.

  It runs with tensor, data or expert parallelism. `BeamConfig` and the model follow the released `config.json` schema (`layer_types`, `mlp_layer_types`, per-type `rope_parameters`); behavior the release does not configure is fixed rather than switchable.
- **Fused kernels for Blackwell**, under `vllm/models/beam/nvidia`: attention, norm/residual boundaries, and DFlash2 context ops. TP all-reduce uses vLLM's standard path in this PR.
- **DFlash2 speculative decoding:** works with FP8 KV cache and adaptive verification. The Beam drafter is self-contained and does not subclass the Qwen3 DFlash classes.

## Validation

**Serving:** Beam-1.0 NVFP4 + DFlash2 (7 draft tokens), TP8 on GB200, SPEED-Bench `throughput_1k` low-entropy subset, greedy decoding. *Measured on the previous revision, which included the fused all-reduce; re-run on this revision pending.*

| Concurrency | Fixed draft (tok/s) | Adaptive (tok/s) | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 708 | 707 | 3.71 → 3.61 |
| 128 | 15,012 | 16,632 | 3.68 → 3.23 |

```bash
vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --reasoning-parser beam --tool-call-parser beam --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER"}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

**Unit tests** on this branch, GB200. These need no checkpoint: the construction test builds a small random-weight Beam and generates with it (TP/EP up to 4). The released `config.json` files for `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B` and `-NVFP4` also load through `get_config` (9 NoPE layers, 3 dense layers).

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_beam_construction.py tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py \
  tests/models/test_beam_weight_mapping.py tests/transformers_utils/test_beam_config.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py \
  "tests/test_config.py::test_dflash_candidate_draft_forces_v2_model_runner"
# 301 passed, 2 skipped
```

## Details

- **Shared code touched outside the model directory:**
  - `BeamForCausalLM` is added to `DEFAULT_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH_ARCHITECTURES`.
  - The DFlash2 speculator also selects `DFlash2BeamDraftModel`.
- **Packaging:** no `.cu` sources ship with the model; all kernels here are Triton or CuTeDSL.
- **Not a duplicate:** no other open PR adds Beam.

title: [CI] Move Attention, Quantization and MoE kernel tests and their AMD mirrors from fixed to automatic shards
author: Thangnguyenvn98
body:
## Overview

Moves two kernel test steps and their two AMD mirrors from fixed pytest shards to `automatic_shard`, the way #61200 and #61477 moved other steps. For each: `parallelism` is dropped, `--shard-id`/`--num-shards` come off the commands, `Shard %N` comes out of the label (the generator adds `shard N/M`), and `automatic_shard: true` is set. No tests change.

## Claims

- Each step runs as parallel jobs planned from main's per-file timings, with each job running only its share of the tests:

| Step | Was | Shards in `/ci run` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `kernels-attention-test` | 7 fixed | 4 |
| `amd-kernels-attention-test` | 6 fixed | 6 |
| `kernels-moe-test` | 5 fixed | 4 |
| `amd-kernels-moe-test` | 5 fixed (inherited) | 3 |

- Fixed pytest shards split by test count, so some shards finish in a few minutes while others take much longer, and every shard pays the job startup again. The plan balances by measured time, so these steps use fewer jobs and finish sooner than main's fixed split.
- Every test runs exactly once across the shards, with the same environment as before.

## Validation

- Planned each step and mirror with ci-infra main's `runtime_shard.plan_step` against main's timings on the step's own queue.
- Rendered each step and mirror with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and with main's `pytest -p ci_otel` wrapper: every test of every command ran in exactly one shard, with the same env.
- Build on the current head (scoped to the four steps): every shard passed with no retries; the slowest took under 18 minutes. Machine time is 21-38% below main's fixed split. Passed counts match main exactly. Skipped counts are lower only because main's fixed shards each collect every file, so files skipped at module level count once per shard there and once here.
- MI300 Attention: in two earlier builds its slowest shard ran 21-23 minutes. Nearly all of that is `test_swap_blocks` in `test_cache.py`, whose CPU-GPU copy cases vary several-fold between hosts; main's fixed split has the same problem, with its slowest shards running longer.

## Details

- **Left out.** `kernels-quantization-test` (NVIDIA) stays on its fixed split: one automatic shard ran past the 22-minute bar in three builds, because some tests cost more when they share a process than their per-file timings show. Its AMD mirror stays fixed with it, since a mirror shards only when its base step is enrolled. `kernels-b200` stays fixed too: its command is a hand-written `case "$$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB"` per shard, which needs rewriting as plain pytest commands first. Helion is out because main has disabled it.
- **Untimed files.** Each plan lists some files with no timing on main, mostly tests for other hardware that skip on these queues. The plan places them in the first shard.
- **`caplog`.** `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py` asserts on log text through `caplog_vllm`, but in a unit test that starts no engine, so test order within a shard doesn't affect it.
- **Timeouts unchanged (human).** `timeout_in_minutes` is per job and stays sized for one shard, as in #61200 and #61477. If planning fails, or the `VLLM_CI_RUNTIME_SHARD` rollback switch turns sharding off, these steps run as one job and the L4 steps and the Attention and MoE mirrors would hit their timeouts. Making the timeout follow the shard count belongs in a central timeout setting rather than in per-step values.
- **Where to look.** `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`: the two steps and their `mirror.amd` blocks.

title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Wait for pending expert buffer copies before NIXL READs
author: djramic
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the intermittent `test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy[nixl-*]` failure in `mi300_4: (MI300) EPLB Execution`:

```text
verify_redundant_experts_have_same_weights failed: rank=0, layer=0, weight_idx=0, logical_expert=1, physical_pos=4, actual_head=[2100.0, 2101.0, ...], reference_head=[1000.0, 1001.0, ...]
FAILED distributed/test_eplb_execute.py::test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy[nixl-4-2-2-5] - AssertionError
```

Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14810/list?jid=01a143f1-ca27-459c-90a8-b3ef97f5fcaf&tab=output>

The test encodes weights as `logical_expert * 1000 + layer * 100 + ...`, so layer 0 ends up with experts from layer 1. `move_from_buffer` only queues the copies out of `expert_buffer` on the stream, and `add_recv` for the next layer immediately issues NIXL READs into the same buffer from the CPU. The READs are not ordered with the stream, so when the GPU lags (e.g. waking up from idle), they overwrite the buffer before the copies of the previous layer run. Only multi-layer cases fail.

The original NIXL communicator (#36276) synchronized the stream before issuing READs. #41633 removed that sync together with the send buffer packing and made `set_stream` a no-op, while READs now land directly in `expert_buffer`. 

This PR synchronizes the current stream and the EPLB stream in `set_transfer_context`, before the first READ of each layer, and removes the no-op `set_stream` override so the stream is stored. The current stream covers the sync path. In async EPLB, the main thread copies out of the buffer on the main stream, which the worker sees only through `self._stream` waiting on `consumed_event`.

## Test Plan

MI300X (gfx942):

```bash
cd tests
pytest -v -s distributed/test_eplb_execute.py
```

To trigger the race, I ran the `nixl-4-2-2-5` and `nixl-2-2-3-4` cases of `test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy` in a loop with the same seed and expert mapping as CI, either with the GPU idle for 2 s before each rearrangement or with a `torch.cuda._sleep` delay before `move_from_buffer`.

## Test Result

| Setup | `main` | `main` + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GPU idle 2 s before each rearrangement | 5/100 failed | 0/100 failed |
| 10-20 ms GPU delay before `move_from_buffer` | 20/20 failed | 0/10 failed |
| Async EPLB flow, 10 ms GPU delay | 40/40 failed | 0/40 failed |

The async flow was emulated with a worker thread calling `transfer_layer` and the main thread calling `move_from_buffer`, as in `async_worker.py` and `eplb_state.py`. All failures had the same signature as CI, while `torch_gloo`, `pynccl` and `torch_nccl` passed under the same delay.

With this PR, `distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` passes: `35 passed, 7 skipped`.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation and validation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Read GPU Engram tables from peers' HBM instead of DP collectives
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

With `cpu_offload: false`, DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables live in HBM, but every lookup still goes through DP collectives: a pynccl `all_gather` of the hash ids and an `all_to_all_single` of the rows on the node-local `edp` group. Decode runs in FULL CUDA graphs, which do not honor `eager_break_during_capture`, so these collectives are captured next to MegaMoE's cross-rank kernels. In DEP decode on GB200, every rank then blocks in `graph.replay()` of the same decode graph at the first real step (seen with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`); host-offloaded tables, with no NCCL in the graph, never hang. I did not pin down the exact NCCL/MegaMoE interaction. This PR removes the collectives instead: GPU tables are row-sharded over the Engram DP group in symmetric memory, and each rank looks up only its own tokens, reading every row from the owning peer's HBM. Lookups need no collective, barrier or graph break.

* **Kernel.** `_engram_lookup_kernel` gains `PEER_ROWS`. With it, `weight` is a per-rank pointer table: a row's owner is `id // PEER_ROWS`, and its scales follow the rows in the same symmetric buffer. Tables are read-only after loading, so reads need no synchronization.
* **When.** `cpu_offload: false`, TP=1 and an Engram DP group (co-located DP replicas). The table sets `dp_size = 1`, as `dp_shared_memory` does, and `DeepseekV4Model` reads that to skip the hash gather and dummy hashes. Host tables keep `dp_shared_memory` / `EngramPeerExchange`, since symmetric memory cannot map another process's host memory.
* **Across nodes.** By default the group stays node-local. With `embedding_across_dp: true` (off by default), GPU tables are split over every DP rank, e.g. 1/32 of the table per GPU at DEP32; all DP ranks must then share one NVLink domain, as on GB200 NVL72. A group with the DP group's ranks reuses `_DP` instead of building a second communicator: a separate 32-rank group cost ~1.1 GiB/GPU and failed `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`.
* **Not covered.** GPU tables with TP > 1 keep head sharding and its collectives. Peer mode stages BF16 rows per layer rather than `EngramBatch`'s packed MXFP8 rows, so `wkv` quantizes its own input; feeding packed peer rows to `EngramBatch` is a possible follow-up.

## Where it matters

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode-only on GB200, DEP16 / DEP32 (DP x TP1 + EP), 16 requests/rank, MegaMoE, MegaAttention, DSpark (5 tokens, synthetic acceptance 3.51), EPLB, full decode CUDA graphs, `DecodeBenchConnector` replaying an agentic coding trace. Unprofiled steady state (+60 to +240 s), one run each, on a development tree based on `fe4df3df` with #61767; its Engram code is identical to main. Without this PR, `cpu_offload: false` hangs in this setup, so the baseline is the default host offload. GPU tables use `embedding_across_dp: true`.

| | host offload | GPU tables, peer read |
| -- | --: | --: |
| DEP16 step (ms) | 14.13 | 13.71 |
| DEP16 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,777 | 3,827 |
| DEP32 step (ms) | 13.15 | 12.90 |
| DEP32 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,877 | 3,939 |
| Model memory, DEP16 / DEP32 (GiB/GPU) | | 28.9 / 20.3 |

## Microbenchmark

Both Engram layers' lookups for one decode step, 96 tokens/rank, 16 ranks on 4 GB200 nodes, CUDA graph replay with fresh ids, median over ranks.

| Table layout | us/step |
| -- | --: |
| Host UVA (offload) | 233-324 |
| HBM, heads over 4 GPUs + `all_gather` + `all_to_all` (main; hangs in FULL graphs) | 46.7 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs + `all_gather` + `reduce_scatter` | 180.6 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs, peer read (this PR) | 19.8 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
```

* `test_engram_table_shared_across_dp_replicas` (4 GPUs): the TP1 x DP4 GPU-table case now takes the peer path, asserts that no DP `all_gather` runs, and replays a FULL CUDA graph with fresh ids.
* `test_engram_group_creation_honors_model_and_options`: TP1 x DP4 cases for the node-local group vs `embedding_across_dp`, and `_DP` reuse.

## Test Result

On 4 x GB200: 29 passed. Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

## Accuracy

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MegaAttention, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, DSpark (5 tokens), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`.

| | Engram tables | strict match | flexible extract |
| -- | -- | --: | --: |
| this PR, DEP8 over two GB200 nodes | GPU, rows over all 8 DP ranks (peer read) | 92.57% (±0.72) | 92.72% |
| #61371, DEP4 | host offload | 92.87% (±0.71) | |

The first revision of this PR gave 92.87% / 92.95% on the same setup.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
# head node
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --port 8123 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --data-parallel-address <head> --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false,"embedding_across_dp":true}' \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --numa-bind
# second node: the same command plus --headless --data-parallel-start-rank 4

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8123/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=1024
```

</details>

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `engram symmetric memory`, `engram peer`, `engram cpu_offload`, `engram hang` and `engram DP`. #59923 and #56512 cover the exchange for host-offloaded tables; #60625 changes head sharding for TP16/TP32 and keeps the collectives.

title: [Perf][Model] Cohere2MoE: attention/MoE dual stream, single TP all-reduce per layer, fused add + RMSNorm
author: XiaochunTong-Cohere
body:
## Overview

This PR makes Cohere2MoE decode **1.14–1.36× faster** (TPOT) on CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0, with no accuracy change. Measured on the bf16, FP8, and W4A16 checkpoints at TP2 on H100.

Cohere2MoE layers are parallel blocks: attention and the MLP/MoE read the same normed input, and their outputs are summed. The PR makes three changes to that block:
- **Attention/MoE dual stream**, on by default on CUDA (`VLLM_COHERE2_ATTN_MOE_DUAL_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=0` disables it). During decode, the MLP/MoE runs on a side CUDA stream, overlapping with attention. This accounts for nearly all of the speedup.
- **Single TP all-reduce per layer.** Attention and the MLP are reduced together instead of separately. At TP > 1, the dual stream relies on this: the layer's only collective then runs after the join, so no all-reduce runs on the side stream alongside the main-stream one.
- **vLLM fused add + RMSNorm.** It lets the existing `allreduce_rms` pass fuse that all-reduce with the next layer's norm.

The changes are confined to `cohere2_moe.py`, plus one env var. Related: #61508 (`swiglu_limit`) edits the MLP/MoE constructors and does not overlap with this PR.

## Claims

- **Dual stream:** decode TPOT improves by 1.14–1.36× across the bf16, FP8, and W4A16 checkpoints at concurrency 1–64.
- **Dual stream disabled (`VLLM_COHERE2_ATTN_MOE_DUAL_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=0`):** up to 1.05× from the single all-reduce and the `allreduce_rms` fusion. The pass goes from `Replaced 0 patterns` to `Replaced 1 patterns` in every compiled subgraph.
- **No quality change:** gsm8k stays within noise. Speculative decoding acceptance is unchanged with both the EAGLE and Eagle3 drafts.
- **No new GPU→CPU syncs:** every dual-stream run passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

## Validation

**Setup:** TP2 on 2×H100 80GB, `--max-model-len 8192`, base 4f49b55c1f unless noted.
- TPOT (ms) comes from `vllm bench serve` on the random dataset, 1024 input / 512 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`.
- Speedup is main TPOT ÷ this PR's TPOT.
- gsm8k is 5-shot over all 1319 questions at concurrency 64; its standard error is about ±0.8 points.
- Each configuration was run once.

**main vs. this PR (default settings):**

| Checkpoint | Configuration | gsm8k | TPOT (c=1) | TPOT (c=8) | TPOT (c=32) | TPOT (c=64) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0) (bf16) | main | 0.899 | 4.07 | 7.00 | 10.59 | 14.04 |
| | this PR | 0.898 | 3.04 (**1.34×**) | 5.61 (**1.25×**) | 9.29 (**1.14×**) | 11.97 (**1.17×**) |
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0-fp8](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0-fp8) | main | 0.895 | 5.34 | 6.93 | 10.00 | 12.32 |
| | this PR | 0.908 | 4.31 (**1.24×**) | 5.89 (**1.18×**) | 8.80 (**1.14×**) | 10.68 (**1.15×**) |
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0-w4a16](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0-w4a16) | main | 0.905 | 4.19 | 5.57 | 8.00 | 10.17 |
| | this PR | 0.908 | 3.07 (**1.36×**) | 4.62 (**1.21×**) | 6.59 (**1.21×**) | 8.93 (**1.14×**) |

After rebasing onto 153a17166e, the bf16 re-run gives main 4.08 / 6.82 / 10.68 / 14.28 ms and this PR 2.82 / 5.67 / 9.15 / 12.71 ms, i.e. 1.45× / 1.20× / 1.17× / 1.12×. gsm8k is 0.899 vs. 0.898.

On the current head (34de23219b, merged with main 005cef040a), default settings give 3.04 / 5.89 / 9.30 / 11.97 ms and `VLLM_COHERE2_ATTN_MOE_DUAL_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=0` gives 3.99 / 6.75 / 10.66 / 13.16 ms. gsm8k is 0.898 for both.

The FP8 run uses the `VLLM_CUTLASS` MoE backend. W4A16 uses NVFP4 weights; for it, vLLM enables `act_quant` by default rather than `allreduce_rms`, so its gain comes from the single all-reduce and the dual stream only.

**Speculative decoding** (bf16, 3 speculative tokens). Acceptance is aggregated over gsm8k at concurrency 64 (1319 questions) and concurrency 1 (100 questions).

| Draft | Configuration | Acceptance rate | Mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0-eagle](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0-eagle) (EAGLE) | main | 0.503 | 2.510 |
| | this PR | 0.503 | 2.508 |
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0-EAGLE3](https://huggingface.co/AlexWortega/North-Mini-Code-1.0-EAGLE3) (Eagle3, community) | main | 0.289 | 1.868 |
| | this PR | 0.290 | 1.869 |
| | this PR, aux states with the residual dropped (negative control) | 0.005 | 1.016 |

The Eagle3 draft reads aux hidden states from layers 2/24/46, which is the path the residual-flow change touches. The negative control confirms that this comparison catches a broken aux capture.

**Unit tests:** `tests/models/test_cohere2_moe_parallel_block.py` runs in the CPU "Basic Models Other" job. It covers:
- the deferred-reduction decision and the single all-reduce;
- the residual flow across layers;
- Eagle3 aux capture under in-place residual updates;
- dual-stream gating and its inline fallbacks;
- a CUDA side-stream race test.

The race test is skipped on CPU and passes on H100. It fails if the join stops waiting on the side stream.

**Per-commit ablation (bf16):**

| Configuration | gsm8k | TPOT (c=1) | TPOT (c=8) | TPOT (c=32) | TPOT (c=64) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.899 | 4.07 | 7.00 | 10.59 | 14.04 |
| + single all-reduce | 0.900 | 4.05 (1.00×) | 6.67 (1.05×) | 10.43 (1.02×) | 13.73 (1.02×) |
| + fused add + RMSNorm | 0.899 | 4.02 (1.01×) | 6.81 (1.03×) | 10.54 (1.00×) | 13.42 (1.05×) |
| + dual stream (default) | 0.898 | 3.04 (1.34×) | 5.61 (1.25×) | 9.29 (1.14×) | 11.97 (1.17×) |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# Dual stream is on by default; add VLLM_COHERE2_ATTN_MOE_DUAL_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=0 to disable it.
# Swap in the -fp8 / -w4a16 checkpoint for the quantized rows.
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
  vllm serve CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0 --served-model-name north-mini-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192

# TPOT, for C in 1 8 32 64
vllm bench serve --model north-mini-code --tokenizer CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts $((C * 8 > 16 ? C * 8 : 16)) --max-concurrency $C --seed 0

# gsm8k
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64

# Speculative decoding: add to the serve command, then read
# vllm:spec_decode_num_{drafts,draft_tokens,accepted_tokens}_total from /metrics.
#   --max-num-seqs 128 --speculative-config \
#   '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "AlexWortega/North-Mini-Code-1.0-EAGLE3", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'

# allreduce_rms matches: compile with debug logging for
# vllm.compilation.passes.fusion.allreduce_rms_fusion and grep "Replaced".

pytest -v tests/models/test_cohere2_moe_parallel_block.py
```
</details>

## Details

**Dual stream.** The MLP/MoE is wrapped in two custom ops, `vllm::cohere2_mlp_fork` and `vllm::cohere2_mlp_join`. They find the layer through the forward context, so Dynamo keeps the stream switch while attention stays the piecewise splitting op.
- Fork runs the MLP on a dedicated side stream. It is separate from `aux_stream()`, which FusedMoE already uses for the shared-expert overlap.
- Join makes the main stream wait for the side stream before the layer's single all-reduce.
- The MLP runs inline instead in these cases:
  - batches above `VLLM_COHERE2_ATTN_MOE_DUAL_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` (default 256; 0 disables the dual stream);
  - piecewise CUDA graphs, i.e. prefill and mixed batches, since a fork cannot span a graph boundary;
  - breakable CUDA graph capture.

  In practice, the overlap covers full CUDA graph decode and small eager batches.
- These setups run single-stream, logged at info level:
  - MoE layers that reduce internally under TP;
  - EP all2all MoE;
  - microbatching (DBO), because each layer keeps a single fork/join state;
  - non-CUDA platforms.

**Single all-reduce.** Both branches of the parallel block end in row-parallel partial sums, so a single `all_reduce(attn + mlp)` is equivalent to reducing them separately.
- `o_proj` and the dense MLP now return unreduced outputs.
- A routed-only MoE passes `reduce_results=False` to `FusedMoEFactory` at TP > 1. When FusedMoE has to reduce internally anyway (EP all2all, sequence parallel), `Cohere2Moe.output_is_reduced` records that, and the decoder then reduces only attention.
- MoE layers with shared experts keep their existing internal reduction.

**Fused add + RMSNorm.** The model-local torch `RMSNorm` is replaced with vLLM's `RMSNorm`, using the same residual flow as Llama.
- Each layer returns its reduced block output and the residual separately; the next layer's norm (or the final norm) adds them.
- Eagle3 aux states add the residual back via `EagleModelMixin._maybe_add_hidden_state`.
- The first layer's residual is the embedding tensor itself, and the fused norm updates the residual in place. So the start-layer aux capture is cloned, only when that layer is captured.
- Checkpoints that use Cohere's LayerNorm keep the old flow.

**Limitations**
- The token threshold was tuned without speculative decoding. With speculation, each request adds `1 + k` tokens per step, so the threshold is reached at lower concurrency.

These changes are ported from Cohere's vLLM fork and adapted to current upstream. AI assistance was used in preparing this PR.
