title: [Bugfix] Fix multi-layer MTP module selection for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next
author: spandantiwari
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen3.5-family MTP drafters (`Qwen3_5MTP`, `Qwen3_5MoeMTP`; also used by Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8 and Intern-S2 checkpoints) and Qwen3-Next (`Qwen3NextMTP`) ran **MTP module 0 for every draft step** when a checkpoint has more than one MTP module, instead of the module trained for that step. This PR makes each draft step use its own module on Model Runner V2, including in the default compiled configuration.

Not a duplicate: #35607 proposed only the `forward` part of this (closed unmerged in Mar 2026, as published Qwen3.5 checkpoints ship one MTP layer); no open PR addresses it.

## Claims

- **Bug fix (MRV2):** multi-module Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next drafting now uses module `i` for draft step `i`, in eager, default compiled (`VLLM_COMPILE` + CUDA graphs), and breakable-CUDA-graph modes. Previously every step reused module 0.
- **No behavior change for shipped checkpoints:** all published Qwen3.5 / 3.6 / 3.8 / Intern-S2 checkpoints have one MTP layer; their drafter keeps its current execution mode (compiled or CUDA graphs), and outputs and acceptance are identical to `main` (below). No published checkpoint of any MTP family changes routing.
- **Lossless:** the target verifies every draft token; this affects draft acceptance (speedup), not output.

## Validation

**Regression test through `LLM` (new):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_steps_use_their_own_module`. It adds a second MTP module with random weights to the real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base` checkpoint (the original shard is symlinked; only module 1 is written), runs MRV2 with the default compiled drafter, `num_speculative_tokens=2` and `use_local_argmax_reduction=True`, and checks that step 1 is accepted (module 0 intact) while step 2 is rejected (module 1 really used).

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_steps_use_their_own_module
# main (7128f568ac):
E       AssertionError: module 1 acceptance 0.419: module 0 was reused
# previous revision of this PR (eager-only fix, no compile gating):
E       AssertionError: module 1 acceptance 0.350: module 0 was reused
# this PR:
1 passed in 102.01s
```

Per-position acceptance on that two-module checkpoint (MI350x, greedy, 100 prompts):

| runner / mode | step 1 | step 2 |
|---|---|---|
| MRV2, default compiled | 0.807 | **0.000** |
| MRV2, `enforce_eager` | 0.805 | **0.000** |
| MRV2, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` | 0.805 | **0.000** (previous revision: `AttributeError: 'Qwen3_5Config' object has no attribute 'num_nextn_predict_layers'`) |
| MRV1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | 0.776 | 0.422 (module 0 reused; see limitations) |

**Routing unit test (real configs):** `tests/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_num_hidden_layers_selects_multi_module_mtp` builds real `Qwen3_5Config` / `Qwen3_5TextConfig` configs (multimodal and text-only) through `ModelConfig` + `SpeculativeConfig`. On `main` the two-module cases fail with `assert False is True`; with this PR all 16 tests in the file pass.

**No regression on shipped checkpoints:** `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base` (one MTP layer), MRV2 compiled, `num_speculative_tokens=3`: output tokens identical to `main`, and acceptance identical on a paired run (415 drafts, per-position `[0.7663, 0.4458, 0.2458]` on both; run-to-run noise on `main` alone is ±3 drafts). The drafter is still compiled (`[eagle_head] torch.compile took 7.7 s`).

Also passed: `pytest v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/` (5 passed, 1 CUDA-only skip), `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`, `tests/test_config.py` (2 failures need gated `meta-llama` access, unrelated).

**Qwen3-Next (local only, no small checkpoint for CI):** `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`, MRV2 compiled, `num_speculative_tokens=2`. Shipped one-module checkpoint: drafts, acceptance (`[0.9487, 0.8063]`) and outputs identical to `main`; drafter still compiled. With a second, random-weight MTP module (`num_nextn_predict_layers=2`, module-1 FP8 scales x100 so it dominates the residual): step-2 acceptance 0.000 with this PR vs 0.688 on `main`.

The Qwen3.5 MTP CI step did not run for changes to these model / config files; its `source_file_dependencies` now include them.

## Details

**Root causes (all needed for multi-module drafting to work):**
1. `Qwen3_5MTP.forward` / `Qwen3NextMTP.forward` did not pass `spec_step_idx` to the inner predictor, which selects `self.layers[spec_step_idx % num_mtp_layers]`. Their `**kwargs` silently accepted and dropped it; it is now a named parameter and `**kwargs` is removed (no caller passes anything else).
2. `use_multi_module_mtp()` only read `num_nextn_predict_layers`, but Qwen3.5 declares `mtp_num_hidden_layers` (nested in `text_config` for multimodal checkpoints), so it never routed to `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`, the only speculator that varies `spec_step_idx`. `SpeculativeConfig.num_mtp_modules()` now reads the `n_predict` that `hf_config_override` already normalizes for every MTP family, so new multi-layer models use the multi-module speculator by default. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator.capture()` uses the same count (it read `num_nextn_predict_layers` unconditionally, which Qwen3.5 configs lack).
3. **Compiled drafters reused module 0.** vLLM compiles the drafter once with all Dynamo guards dropped, so the Python-indexed module chosen on the first trace was replayed for every step. The other multi-module drafters (Inkling, Step-3.5, MiMo-V2, Qwen4Exp, MiniMax-M3) are not compiled, which is why this did not surface. The Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next drafter is now compiled only when it runs single-module (`support_torch_compile(enable_if=...)`); multi-module drafters run eager with full CUDA graphs over the draft loop, like the other multi-module drafters. Since #51012 the CUDA Qwen3.5 drafter is no longer compiled, so this gate now applies to Qwen3-Next and the ROCm Qwen3.5 drafter.
4. With multi-module routing, the local-argmax path calls `get_top_tokens(hidden_states, spec_step_idx=...)`; `Qwen3_5MTP` now accepts and ignores it, since the MTP modules share one `lm_head` (as in `compute_logits`).

**Scope:** Qwen3-Next already routed correctly via `num_nextn_predict_layers`; it needed only (1) and (3). Drafts with MTP index sharing (`index_share_for_mtp_iteration`, from the checkpoint or the override) and MiniMax-M3 stay on the single-module speculator, with TODOs: index sharing is only implemented there, and MiniMax-M3 is not yet verified with the multi-module speculator.

**Files:** since #51012, CUDA loads `Qwen3_5MTP` from `vllm/models/qwen3_5/nvidia/mtp.py`, while ROCm and Intern-S2 (`InternS2MobiusMTP`) still use `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`. Fixes (1) and (4) are applied to both files.



**Limitations:** Model Runner V1 never passes `spec_step_idx` for any MTP family (only Step-3.5's proposer does), so multi-module drafting there still uses module 0; MRV1 is deprecated and this PR targets MRV2. Multi-module Qwen drafters trade the compiled drafter for eager + full CUDA graphs; no shipped checkpoint takes that path.

title: [CI] Move B200 Kernels and MoE Refactor evals from manual to automatic shards
author: Thangnguyenvn98
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Moves three steps that split their tests by hand onto `automatic_shard`, following #62077 and #62084. `kernels-b200` ran a hand-written `case "$$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB"` block per shard. The two MoE Refactor integration steps read a different config list in each shard (`config-*-shard-$$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB.txt`). Each now runs plain pytest, the planner splits it using main's timings, and new tests or configs no longer need placing in a shard by hand.

## Claims

| Step | Was | Planned shards |
|---|---:|---:|
| `kernels-b200` | 3 hand-written `case` shards | 3 |
| `moe-refactor-integration-test-b200-temporary` | 4 config-list shards | 6 |
| `moe-refactor-integration-test-h100-temporary` | 4 config-list shards | 4 |

- Every test and every config runs exactly once across the shards, with the same environment as before.
- A test file or config added later is placed by the planner, not by editing a `case` arm or a shard list.
- Labels drop `Shard %N`; the generator names jobs `<label> shard N/M`.
- The AMD mirrors (NVFP4 Dense Emulation, both MoE Refactor mirrors) are short. They stop inheriting the fixed shards and run as one job each.

## Validation

- Planned each step with ci-infra main's `runtime_shard.plan_step` against this branch and main's timings.
- Rendered each step with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and with main's `pytest -p ci_otel` wrapper. Every test of every command ran in exactly one shard, with the same env (6/6 cases).
- For the config-list steps, also ran the generated shard jobs against vLLM's real `tests/evals/gsm8k/conftest.py` and config files, with the test body stubbed. All 19 B200 configs and all 12 H100 configs ran once each across the shards. No shard printed `not in the plan`, so the plan matched every config ID that main has timings for.
- `/ci run` [97474](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97474), rebased on main after ci-infra#836:
  - `kernels-b200` passed in 3 shards. Its 28 pytest runs total 2640 passed, 504 skipped and 1424 deselected, the same as main [97527](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97527); machine time in line with main.
  - The MoE Refactor B200 step passed in 6 shards and the H100 step in 4, with all 19 B200 and all 12 H100 configs passing once each, as on main. Machine time is in line with main for both.
  - All three AMD mirrors passed as one job each.

## Details

- **`kernels-b200` setup.** `python3 examples/basic/offline_inference/chat.py` was in shard 1 only. The planner needs plain pytest after the first pytest command, so it now runs as a setup command, once in each shard.
- **Config lists.** `moe-refactor/config-b200.txt` already listed exactly the union of the four B200 shard lists. `config-h100.txt` is the union of the four H100 shard lists. The per-shard lists are removed.
- **ROCm list kept twice.** The H100 step's AMD mirror now reads a new combined `config-rocm.txt`. `config-rocm-shard-*.txt` stay because the separate `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` still reads them.
- **`moe-refactor-integration-test-h100-temporary`.** Before ci-infra#836 the planner gave it 3 shards that ran longer than the old fixed shards. With each job's setup now in the budget it plans 4, each under the 20-minute target.
- **Timeouts unchanged (human).** As in #62077 and #62084, `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job. A single-job fallback (no plan, or the `VLLM_CI_RUNTIME_SHARD` rollback switch) would outrun it. Fallback-aware timeouts belong in a central timeout setting.
- **Left out.** `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus` and `lora-tp-distributed` move in #62537, and `basic-models-tests-extra-initialization` in #63907. `spec-decode-mtp-other-acceptance-nightly` and the Humming A100/H100 steps stay on fixed shards: their fixed shards are already as short as a plan can make them, or they have no timings.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Fix speculative warmup deadlock with pipeline parallelism
author: chenjr97
body:
## Overview

Fix a pipeline-parallel startup deadlock in MRV2 speculative decoding introduced by [#59260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59260).

## Claims

- Ensure all PP stages participate in the additional greedy warmup pass.
- Add regression coverage for matching warmup rounds across PP stages, with speculative decoding enabled and disabled.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py -q
```

- **34 passed** in 9.64 seconds. These suites are covered by the existing `V1 Executor + Worker` CI job.
- **GLM-4.7-Flash smoke test passed**: MRV2, TP=2, PP=2, BF16, MTP with one speculative token, JIT warmup and CUDA graphs enabled.
- Warmup completed and generation produced exactly **1,024 tokens** using `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, and `ignore_eos=True`. Recorded 532 draft tokens and 492 accepted tokens; process exited successfully.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed.

The model run validates startup and generation; no accuracy benchmark was performed.

## Details

Only the last PP stage owns a rejection sampler. Previously, the additional greedy warmup pass was gated on its presence, so earlier stages skipped the pass while the last stage waited for their activations.

Gate this pass on `speculative_config` instead, ensuring every PP stage executes matching forwards. The change is limited to the warmup condition and regression tests.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode for the DSpark draft layers
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DSv4.1-Flash mono decode (MI355X, `--monokernel`): the DSpark draft's three layers now run on the mono K1 / K2 kernels too, as ATOM's `DraftMonoRunner` does, instead of vLLM's per-op path. Follow-up to #60397 and #61082; they follow `--monokernel` like the target's layers, with no new switch. Overlaps files with #60731 (gfx942 port), so whichever merges second needs a rebase.

## Claims

- The draft's three layers cost about 227 us of kernel time per step on mono, in place of about 640 us on the original path (graph profile, TP4 c1): about 414 us less GPU time a step.
- AgentX at c1, per-request ITL p50 is 0.030 ms (1.8%) lower than InferenceX's run with `--monokernel`, at TP4 (1.646 against 1.678 ms) and at TP2 (1.970 against 2.000 ms).
- Draft quality is unchanged: DSpark mean acceptance length 3.889 / 3.935 (TP4) and 3.917 (TP2) against 3.899 / 3.896 without, and GSM8K 0.975 / 0.972.
- Target layers' kernels are untouched: their ISA is identical to `main`'s.

## Validation

All on MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, the InferenceX #3690 recipe, `main` at `ce49c47cbb` plus this PR unless a row says otherwise. "Off" is the same build with the draft layers on vLLM's path (a throwaway env switch for the A/B, not in this PR).

**Layer level.** The draft layers against the original layers on real eager decode steps (TP4 c1 and TP2 c1, 5- and 10-row steps), same inputs: x output cosine >= 0.99975 (relative L2 up to 2.3%, the MoE's top-3 routing near-ties), residual, post / comb / pre mixes >= 0.9999 cosine.

**Acceptance and accuracy** (real block rejection, GSM8K as in InferenceX's DSv4.1-Flash eval: custom `gsm8k` task, chat, 5-shot multiturn, `max_tokens` 12288, 64 requests in flight, full 1,319):

| | draft on mono: GSM8K strict / flexible; mean acceptance length | draft off |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 0.9750 / 0.9742; 3.889 (3.935 on the final rebase) | 0.9750 / 0.9742; 3.899 |
| TP2 | 0.9719 / 0.9712; 3.917 | 0.9727 / 0.9719; 3.896 |

**AgentX, c1, 3,600 s** (InferenceX's `infx.bench agentic` client, the #3690 recipe with `--monokernel`, DSpark with synthetic acceptance 3.51, the Rust frontend). Reference: InferenceX's run [38377181342](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38377181342) (same recipe, nightly 5555a2d8, its own node). TP4 and TP2 ran at the same time on one node. The confidence intervals are bootstrap over the per-request ITL of the profiling phase (about 330 requests an arm).

| | TP4 PR | TP4 ref | TP2 PR | TP2 ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ITL p50 (ms), from the summary | 1.650 | 1.680 | 1.970 | 2.000 |
| per-request ITL p50 (ms), diff [95% CI] | 1.646 | 1.678: -0.032 [-0.034, -0.027] | 1.970 | 2.000: -0.030 [-0.034, -0.026] |
| per-request ITL p90 (ms), diff [95% CI] | 1.690 | 1.757: -0.068 [-0.189, +0.012] | 2.053 | 2.178: -0.125 [-0.292, +0.196] |
| interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 607.6 / 591.8 | 596.1 / 569.1 | 507.6 / 487.1 | 499.9 / 459.1 |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (s) | 0.170 / 0.247 | 0.245 / 0.336 | 0.183 / 0.293 | 0.210 / 0.383 |
| E2E p50 (s) | 1.85 | 1.93 | 2.14 | 2.18 |
| requests completed | 335 | 331 | 318 | 316 |

The p50 gain is outside the noise at both TP sizes; the p90 interactivity gain (+4.0% and +6.1%) is not (its interval spans zero), and the TTFT difference is the node, not this PR (prefill is untouched). The reference is not a same-node baseline, so the p50 difference also includes any difference of node, image and commit; an earlier run on the same node of `main` plus only #61934's change (a different kernel change) gave ITL p50 1.670 / 2.000 ms (per-request 1.675 / 1.998).

**Kernel time** (graph-mode torch profile, TP4 c1, draft on mono): K1 about 20 us and K2 about 56 us a layer for the three draft layers (227 us a step); the non-target kernels of a step total 1.76 ms against 2.17 ms with the draft off (excluding all-reduce spin-waits).

**Tests.** `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`: 41 pass, 3 new (the draft layer takes the mono path on its own runner, its first layer takes the broadcast embedding, a layer takes only its own SWA row width). The K1 / K2 ISA of the target builds at TP4, M=6 is identical to `main`'s (`FLYDSL_DUMP_IR` diff: 0 lines).

**Accuracy** (RFC #59665 protocol, as in #60397: thinking on, `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, 8 requests in flight a server, DSpark with block rejection, `--monokernel` so the draft layers run on mono; pass@1, ± is the standard error across questions). The baselines are #60397's numbers; no reference arm of this build was rerun.

| | this PR | #60397 |
|---|---|---|
| TP2 GPQA-Diamond (8 samples a question) | 84.8 ± 2.2 | 85.3 ± 2.2 reference, 85.1 ± 2.2 mono |
| TP2 AIME25 (16 samples a problem) | 98.3 ± 0.9 | 99.4 ± 0.3 reference, 98.3 ± 0.8 mono |
| TP4 GPQA-Diamond (4 samples a question) | 84.5 ± 2.3 | 85.2 ± 2.2 mono |
| TP4 AIME25 (8 samples a problem) | 98.8 ± 0.7 | 100.0 mono (240/240) |

AIME25's wrong samples: 8 of 480 at TP2 (3 empty, out of the 64K budget; 4 on one hard problem) and 3 of 240 at TP4 (1 empty).

**RULER NIAH** (lm-eval, prefix-free chat copies, thinking on, greedy, 40 samples a cell): `niah_single_1`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K score 40/40 in every cell at both TP2 and TP4, as in #60397.

## Details

The draft layers are `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`s with window-only attention (compress ratio 0, no indexer), so the kernels need no new stage. What differs is carried by the build and the step's integers:

- **Routing:** 128 routed experts, top-3 (`dspark_n_routed_experts` / `dspark_num_experts_per_tok`) and one FP4 group per ug task. `MoeBuild` already took these; `MonoBuild` now carries `experts`, `topk`, `ug_groups` and `swa_width` into the MoE stage and the scratch layout.
- **SWA rows:** the draft's metadata is non-causal, with rows `get_dspark_swa_index_width(window, num_speculative_tokens)` wide (192 for window 128 and 5 drafts). K1's key-table stage read the row width as the constant 128; it reads it from the build now.
- **First layer:** the draft hands it the embedding already repeated to the hc copies, `[rows, hc, dim]`; K1 takes it as the settled residual (`fold=False`), as for the target's layer 0.
- **Its own runner:** the scratch layout depends on the number of experts, and a mailbox word must never be a tag to one launch and data to another, so the draft's layers share a second `DSV41MonoLayer` (epoch, scratch, peer buffers) as in ATOM. Every rank creates it at the same layer of the same eager step, like the target's.

Target builds are unchanged: every new field defaults to the target's value, the kernel symbols gain no suffix for them, and the ISA diff above is empty.

Limitations: MI355X (CDNA4), TP2 / TP4, steps of at most 48 rows (the draft's are 5 per request, so up to 8 requests); the layer comparison is on eager steps only. The draft's remaining per-step cost is outside its layers: `_prepare_dflash_inputs` (3 launches of 113 us), the six skinny head GEMMs (279 us), and about 75 small elementwise and copy kernels. I found no open PR doing this. Developed and measured with Claude Code; the submitter's line-by-line review is still pending.

title: [CI][AMD] Mirror ReplaySSM, MiniMax-M3 attention kernels and Kimi K3 prefix cache on MI355
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
Adds AMD mirrors for the three test groups in `test_areas` that still had none: ReplaySSM E2E, MiniMax-M3 Attention Kernels and Kimi K3 Prefix Cache. The Kimi K3 Prefix Cache mirror needs two fixes that have not landed yet (see Details).

- `engine.yaml`: ReplaySSM E2E on `mi355_2`. The FlashInfer-only cases in `test_replayssm_decode.py` skip off CUDA.
- `kernels.yaml`: MiniMax-M3 Attention Kernels on `mi355_dpx`, plus a test that checks the AITER indexer against a reference implementation.
- `models_basic.yaml`: Kimi K3 Prefix Cache on `mi355_4` with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. The existing MI355 Kimi K3 jobs now skip `test_prefix_cache.py` so it does not run twice.
- `test_prefix_cache.py`: on ROCm it gates on native MX support instead of SM100. The FlashInfer DCP xfail applies on CUDA only. The Mooncake transport can be set with `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL` (default `rdma`), and the AMD mirror uses `tcp`.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950), on current main with its ROCm pins (AITER `v0.1.25`, NIXL `1683cf3b`):

| Group | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ReplaySSM E2E | 10 | 10/10 pass (4 passed, 6 skipped each) |
| MiniMax-M3 Attention Kernels | 10 | 10/10 pass (161 passed, 14 skipped each) |
| Kimi K3 (existing job, with the new `--ignore`) | 1 | 336 passed, 67 skipped |
| Kimi K3 Prefix Cache, current main | 1 | 29 passed, 2 failed (`pd-tp2-dep2-block`/`-partial`, fixed by #61002) |
| Kimi K3 Prefix Cache, with #61002 and the AITER fix | 6 | 31/31 in 4 runs; the other 2 failed when another process on the shared node took the GPU memory |

## Details

The Kimi K3 Prefix Cache mirror depends on two fixes:

- #61002 (NixlConnector): pairs non-divisible hybrid MLA block sizes. Without it the two `pd-tp2-dep2` cases fail at the NIXL handshake.
- ROCm/aiter#6446: fixes an LL128 all-reduce deadlock that can hang the DCP cases under host contention. vLLM picks it up through an AITER release that includes it and a pin bump in `Dockerfile.rocm_base`. `v0.1.25` does not include it yet.

The new Mooncake test needs RDMA NICs (`mlx5_*`) by default, which MI355 runners may not have. The mirror runs it over TCP, which passes locally. The mirror inherits `optional` from the NVIDIA step, so like the 4xB200 job it runs nightly.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [MyPy][5/N] Fix mypy errors in hard tests/ dirs and enforce follow-imports=silent
author: adarshxs
body:
## Overview

Part 5 of enabling mypy on `tests/` (#49569). Fixes the mypy errors in the PR 5 directories and moves them from `SEPARATE_GROUPS` to `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so they are now checked with `--follow-imports silent` and cannot regress: `tests/entrypoints/llm`, `tests/entrypoints/openai`, `tests/kernels` (absorbing the previously listed `tests/kernels/{attention,core,helion,mamba,quantization}` and the separate `tests/kernels/moe`), `tests/lora`, `tests/tool_parsers`, `tests/v1/attention`, `tests/v1/e2e`, `tests/v1/ec_connector`.

Builds on #49570 (PR 0/1) and #51043 (PR 2). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these directories for mypy (checked `gh pr list --search "49569 in:body"` and `"mypy tests"`; the open `[MyPy]` PRs are #55485 (PR 4), #55542 (kv-A) and #55901 (kv-B)).

Partial #26533.

## Claims

- 533 mypy errors across the eight directories → 0, with `--warn-unused-ignores` also clean. (The issue's ~650 estimate predates #59428, which disabled `arg-type` and `assignment` under `tests/`.)
- Type-only: no `vllm/` changes, no `cast()`, no bare `# type: ignore`; the 29 ignores added are scoped to an error code and carry a reason (inline when the line fits in 88 columns, on the preceding line otherwise); 12 ignores that no longer suppressed anything are removed.
- 49 mock method assignments replaced with `monkeypatch.setattr`.
- Pre-existing test defects surfaced by the stricter check are fixed where safe, and flagged in a comment where fixing would change what the test exercises (list in Details).

## Validation

Environment: the pre-commit hook env (mypy 1.20.2, no torch/transformers so they resolve to `Any`), Python 3.11 like the hook.

```bash
# 1. the directories are clean at the strictness being enforced
.venv/bin/mypy --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports silent --warn-unused-ignores \
    tests/entrypoints/llm tests/entrypoints/openai tests/kernels tests/lora \
    tests/tool_parsers tests/v1/attention tests/v1/e2e tests/v1/ec_connector
# Success: no issues found in 632 source files   (before: 533 errors in 111 files)

# 2. the hook as CI runs it, with the new grouping in effect
pre-commit run mypy --all-files --hook-stage manual
# passes; the only output is 3 darwin-only errors in vllm/ (posix_fadvise, MADV_HUGEPAGE)
# that exist on macOS before this change and do not appear on Linux CI

# 3. routing proof: each PR 5 directory now lands in the "" (silent) group
.venv/bin/python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/pre_commit'); import mypy; \
  print([k for k,v in mypy.group_files(['tests/lora/utils.py']).items() if v])"
# ['']   (same for a file in each of the other seven directories; tests/v1/core still prints ['tests/v1/core'])

# 4. all other hooks on the changed files
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only main)
# ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, ... all pass
```

Test runs (macOS CPU build of vLLM, so only CPU-runnable suites; everything else collected only):

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest --collect-only` on all 116 changed test files | 8316 tests collected; 6 collection errors, all missing optional deps on macOS (triton-cpu, tilelang, datasets), none from this change |
| `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/{chat_completion/test_chat_error,completion/test_completion_error,completion/test_completion_text_offset,responses/test_function_call_parsing,responses/test_response_input_to_harmony,responses/test_responses_utils,responses/test_serving_responses,test_render_parity,test_tool_choice_content_none}.py` | 243 passed, 1 xfailed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_*.py` (14 changed files) | 528 passed, 1 skipped, 19 xfailed |
| `pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit tests/v1/attention` (3 pre-existing non-collecting files ignored) | 984 passed, 1150 skipped, 214 failed + 16 errors; the identical set of 230 ids fails on unchanged `main` in the same environment (CUDA/ROCm-only tests, `/dev/shm`, NIXL), so none is from this change |

No model evaluation: the change does not touch `vllm/` and cannot affect output, accuracy or serving.

## Details

Most fixes follow the issue's recipe: `assert x is not None` before an `X | None` access, `assert isinstance(...)` to narrow a union or an abstract base to the concrete class the test builds, annotations on fixtures and helpers, and `monkeypatch.setattr` instead of assigning to a method. Scoped ignores remain only where a test stub intentionally does not satisfy the real interface (`misc` for `None` fallbacks of optional kernel classes and a `Final` attribute, `attr-defined` for `SimpleNamespace` stubs, `type-abstract` where a test instantiates an abstract class through a factory).

Pre-existing defects the stricter check surfaced (all in tests; none changes what a test exercises):

- `tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py`: `StructuredOutputsParams(backend=...)` has no such init field (`_backend` is `init=False`), so the call raised `TypeError`; the kwarg is removed and the helper no longer takes a backend.
- `tests/lora/utils.py`: `DummyLoRAManager.init_lora` passed `embeddings_tensor=` to `LoRALayerWeights(...)`, which no longer accepts it.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_{internlm2,longcat,phi4mini}_tool_parser.py`: `tokenizer.get_vocab = MagicMock()` permanently mutated the module-scoped tokenizer fixture and leaked into later tests; now `monkeypatch.setattr`, undone per test.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py`: assignments to a non-existent `FusedMoEParallelConfig.use_dp` removed; the no-DP state already comes from `make_no_parallel()`.
- `tests/kernels/moe/modular_kernel_tools/{mk_objects,common,cli_args}.py`: registries and `Config` fields were annotated as holding instances although they hold classes; now `type[...]` of the Modular subclasses that are actually registered.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py`: the mock prefill backends' `run_prefill_new_tokens` / `run_prefill_context_chunk` did not match the ABC (`chunk_idx` vs `chunk`, missing `out` / `output_scale`).
- `tests/v1/attention/utils.py`: `try_get_attention_backend` was annotated `type[AttentionImpl]` but `get_impl_cls()` returns `type[AttentionImplBase]`; and the `add_mock_model_methods` block is removed: its `get_num_layers` mock shadowed the real method with the wrong arity, the three `*_for_layer` hooks no longer exist on `ModelConfig`, nothing reads any of them, and no caller passed the flag.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py`: `query_len_support` is a `ClassVar` and was assigned through an instance; the assignment is removed (the inherited default is the value it set).
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`: `get_fake_sample_fn` was annotated `-> SamplerOutput` although it returns a callable.
- `tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_metadata.py`: asserted load entries as `(transfer_id, block_ids)` pairs; the metadata carries `(transfer_id, block_ids, shape)` and the worker unpacks three values, so the test is updated to the real contract.

Deliberately not changed, flagged with a comment and a scoped ignore:

- `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py`: the int8 non-block branch of `moe_quantize_weights_2d` calls `ops.scaled_int8_quant(w, w_s, use_per_token_if_dynamic=...)`, but the signature is now `(input, scale, azp, symmetric) -> (q, scale, azp)`, so it would raise if reached. No test reaches it (every int8 caller uses block quant and the modular-kernel CLI only accepts fp8); a replacement needs a GPU to validate, so it is left for a follow-up.

Typing gaps in `vllm/` that the per-test fixes keep running into, left for follow-ups:

- four identical `type-abstract` ignores: `select_common_block_size` / `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` take `type[AttentionBackend]`, but the indexer backends leave `get_impl_cls` abstract;
- repeated narrowings of `Metric.value` (only `Counter` / `Gauge` have it), `LLMEngine.engine_core` (to `InprocClient`), `EmbeddingCache.get/alloc` (`CacheEntry | None`) and `FusedMoEQuantConfig.*_scale` (`Tensor | None`).

`MockMLAAttentionLayer.forward_impl` in `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` keeps a scoped `override` ignore because the replica deliberately takes only the arguments the test passes; the prefill-registry mocks above were aligned to their ABC instead because they are registered as real backends.

The hook change is routing only: the absorbed `tests/kernels/*` entries become redundant under the `tests/kernels` parent entry and are removed, mirroring what #51043 did for `tests/plugins_tests`.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Size cooperative_topk's single pass by row length, not stride
author: haosdent
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`cooperative_topk` now chooses between its single-pass and two-pass paths from each row's length instead of the
logits row stride. Rows that fit the single-pass staging no longer stream through TMA twice just because the
buffer is wide (`max_model_len`).

## Claims

- InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200: together with #62170 and #62172, decode time per turn
  drops 2.8%, 2.5%, 1.5% and 1.5% at concurrency 1, 4, 8 and 16 (main vs main: within 0.7%). This PR is
  about half of that.
- The decode top-k is up to 8% faster on B300 for rows that fit the single-pass staging when the stride is larger
  than the per-block staging, for example `max_model_len` 1M at 1-8 rows, or about 200K at 9-64 rows.
- Selection is unchanged: both paths compute the same exact radix top-k.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`: 265 passed, 37 skipped on GB200 (SM100); after rebasing onto #59645's
  overflow recovery, 402 passed, 44 skipped on B300 (SM103). The new `test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride`
  covers every cluster size (1, 4, 8, 33 and 64 rows) with strides of 64K and 1M and rows of 300 to 300K tokens, so
  one launch mixes trivial, register, single-pass and streaming rows. It compares the selected values with
  `torch.topk`.
- InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200, main + #62170, #62171 and #62172 vs main (median per-turn change
  on the same turns, 95% CI; setup below):

  | concurrency | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | decode time | -2.8% [-3.1, -2.6] | -2.5% [-3.1, -1.7] | -1.5% [-2.2, -1.1] | -1.5% [-2.4, +0.3] |
  | e2e latency | -3.3% [-3.9, -3.0] | -1.8% [-2.7, -0.9] | -1.2% [-2.0, -0.5] | -0.6% [-1.9, +2.4] |
  | KV cache tokens | +0.2% | +0.7% | +1.4% | 0 |
  | main vs main, decode | -0.1% | -0.7% | +0.3% | -0.3% |

- `cooperative_topk` microbenchmark, k=2048, rows = requests x 4 (MTP), CUDA graph replay, B300:

  | rows | context | stride | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 4 | 40K | 1M | 10.99 | 10.27 |
  | 4 | 150K | 1M | 12.98 | 12.11 |
  | 16 | 40K | 1M | 12.18 | 11.24 |
  | 16 | 40K | 64K | 11.27 | 11.09 |

- Target verify forward (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, B300, MTP verify shapes, spread < 0.1%), on top
  of #62170: -0.58% to -1.36% at 1, 3 and 7 requests, 25K and 94K context.
- Exactness: with real MTP verification on 32 GSM8K questions (greedy), the three changes together give the same
  outputs and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- MRCR (8 needles, 4K to 256K, 594 samples), GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200, greedy: main 0.903, with #62170,
  #62171 and #62172 0.890; paired difference -0.013 [-0.038, +0.012], and every bin's CI includes zero. The
  256K bin, run three times each: -0.019 [-0.069, +0.031].

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and results for all GLM-5.3 PRs (4x GB200)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
with synthetic acceptance 2.99, native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, `max-num-seqs` = 2 x
concurrency. vLLM main dcd07967ca with its default backends and CUDA graph config, plus the PRs cumulatively in
the order below (FlashInfer with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631 and
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632 from #62174 on). One FlashInfer MoE autotune per concurrency, shared by all
variants. A fresh server per point, with the page cache dropped before each, and main run again at the end of
each concurrency as an A/A check. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM
all-reduce fusion and `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`.

Each cell is the median, over the turns both runs finished (150 to 520), of the per-turn ratio to the previous
variant, with a 95% paired bootstrap CI. Decode is request latency minus TTFT. The bootstrap does not include
run-to-run variance; the main-vs-main row does.

p = 2/70); e2e latency -0.29% [-1.41, +0.82].

## Details

The DSA indexer allocates its decode logits with `max_model_len` columns, and `cooperative_topk` gets that as
`stride`. The kernel sized `per_block` (elements per CTA of the cluster) from the stride. But `large_topk` splits
the row by its actual length (`seq_len`, in 16-byte units across the cluster ranks). With a long `max_model_len`,
every row took the two-pass streaming path even when its context fit the all-stages-resident single pass. For
example, 16 rows use 4-CTA clusters, and a 256K stride gives 64K elements per block, above the 48K single-pass
staging, while a 40K-token row needs only 10K per block.

`per_block` is now `ceil(seq_len / CS)`, so each row picks its path from its own length. `large_topk` rounds each
block to 16-byte units, but the single-pass limit and the stage size are multiples of that unit, so this gives the
same path and stage count as the exact split. Rows in one launch can take different paths. Each row is its own
cluster, and the barrier setup already follows the chosen path.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Let cooperative_topk read the BF16 indexer logits
author: haosdent
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`cooperative_topk` now also reads BF16 logits. On SM100 the DSA indexer then keeps the paged MQA logits in BF16
instead of upcasting them to FP32 before the decode top-k. Main already does this for `deep_select` and (since
#64138) `persistent`, but `auto` picks `cooperative` for up to 64 rows, which is every decode step in the runs
below (at most 16 requests x 4 tokens). From review, the top-k kernels themselves are also faster now, mostly
for BF16 (Details).

## Claims

- Decode top-k on B300, main (FP32 upcast + FP32 top-k) vs this PR (BF16 top-k): 22% to 57% faster at every
  point of rows {1, 4, 8, 16, 33, 64} x row length {16K, 64K, 128K, 256K, 1M} x k {512, 2048}. The BF16
  top-k alone is 8% to 38% faster than main's FP32 top-k. With FP32 logits (#64580's default) the top-k is up
  to 16% faster and at most 0.2% slower.
- `persistent_topk` with BF16 logits (#64138) is 24% to 31% faster on rows up to 32K, the single-CTA path it
  shares with `cooperative_topk`.
- InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200: together with #62170 and #62171, decode time per turn
  drops 2.8%, 2.5%, 1.5% and 1.5% at concurrency 1, 4, 8 and 16 (main vs main: within 0.7%). This PR is
  about 1/3 of that. (Measured before the kernel changes from review.)
- No precision changes: DeepGEMM's SM100 logits kernels already return BF16 on main
  ([`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd/vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py#L597-L606)), and main only widens them
  ([`as_fp32_logits`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L304-L305)). BF16 widens to FP32
  exactly, so the top-k selects the same values.
- DCP, top-k backends that take only FP32, and BF16 rows that are not 16-byte aligned still upcast as before.

  `test_cooperative_topk_overflow_mixed_lengths` also run BF16 logits.

  `test_sparse_indexer_resolved_persistent_bf16` (#64138) now expects `auto`'s `cooperative` choice to take them
  too and checks that its selection is exact.

  rounded to BF16, every row is full length, row stride = length. Main and this PR each ran twice in fresh

```python
"""cooperative_topk sweep for vllm#62172: rows x row length x k, timed with triton's do_bench_cudagraph.

usage: python coop_sweep.py TAG OUT_JSON  (from the vLLM tree to test, with its _C_stable_libtorch built)
       SWEEP_ONLY=fp32 times only the FP32 kernel, so both builds make the same allocations.
Logits are torch.randn rounded to BF16 (what DeepGEMM returns on SM100); every row has the full length and the
row stride equals the length. Timed per case (median us of CUDA-graph replays; L2 is not flushed):
  fp32          cooperative_topk on the FP32 widening (main's top-k kernel)
  upcast_fp32   as_fp32_logits(BF16) + cooperative_topk on FP32 (main's SM100 decode stage)
  bf16          cooperative_topk reading BF16 directly (this PR; None where the build rejects BF16)
Each result must select exactly torch.topk's values, with no repeated index. Run main, PR, PR, main in fresh
processes and compare the means of each build's two runs.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import torch
from triton.testing import do_bench_cudagraph

import vllm._custom_ops  # noqa: F401  (registers torch.ops._C)
from vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer import as_fp32_logits

tag, out_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
ROWS = (1, 4, 8, 16, 33, 64)
LENGTHS = (16384, 65536, 131072, 262144, 1048576)
KS = (512, 2048)
ws = torch.empty(1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")


def bench(fn):
    return do_bench_cudagraph(fn, rep=100, return_mode="median") * 1000


def exact(logits32, out, k):
    sel = logits32.gather(1, out.long()).sort(1).values
    ref = logits32.topk(k, dim=1).values.sort(1).values
    uniq = all(out[r].unique().numel() == k for r in range(out.shape[0]))
    return bool(torch.equal(sel, ref)) and uniq


# Warm up (clocks, graph capture) on the first shape; the first timed case of a process reads high otherwise.
_x = torch.randn(ROWS[0], LENGTHS[0], device="cuda")
_l = torch.full((ROWS[0],), LENGTHS[0], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
_o = torch.empty(ROWS[0], KS[0], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
torch.cuda.synchronize()
bench(lambda: torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(_x, _l, _o, ws, KS[0], LENGTHS[0]))

results = []
for rows in ROWS:
    for length in LENGTHS:
        torch.manual_seed(rows * 7 + length)
        logits16 = torch.randn(rows, length, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
        logits32 = logits16.float()
        lengths = torch.full((rows,), length, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
        # do_bench_cudagraph runs on a side stream that does not wait for these writes.
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        for k in KS:
            r = dict(tag=tag, rows=rows, length=length, k=k)
            out = torch.empty(rows, k, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

            def fp32():
                torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(logits32, lengths, out, ws, k, length)

            r["fp32"] = bench(fp32)
            r["fp32_exact"] = exact(logits32, out, k)
            if os.environ.get("SWEEP_ONLY") == "fp32":
                # Same allocations in every build: skip the BF16 variants.
                r["upcast_fp32"] = r["bf16"] = None
                r["upcast_fp32_exact"] = r["bf16_exact"] = True
                results.append(r)
                print(json.dumps(r), flush=True)
                continue

            def upcast_fp32():
                x = as_fp32_logits(logits16, lengths)
                torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(x, lengths, out, ws, k, length)

            r["upcast_fp32"] = bench(upcast_fp32)
            r["upcast_fp32_exact"] = exact(logits32, out, k)

            def bf16():
                torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(logits16, lengths, out, ws, k, length)

            try:
                bf16()
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
                r["bf16"] = bench(bf16)
                r["bf16_exact"] = exact(logits32, out, k)
            except RuntimeError:
                r["bf16"] = r["bf16_exact"] = None
            results.append(r)
            print(json.dumps(r), flush=True)
        del logits16, logits32
json.dump(results, open(out_path, "w"))
```

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured as one group. `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3. #62173 changes only decode steps of 3, 5 or 7 requests; steps with 3 or
more requests are 0%, 4%, 13% and 37% of all steps at c=1/4/8/16. At c=1 both runs capture the same graphs, so
its +0.5% there is noise. At c=16, three more runs each of + #62174 and + #62173 (4 runs each, compared as
runs): decode time -0.54% [-0.93, -0.16], with every + #62173 run faster than every + #62174 run (permutation
p = 2/70); e2e latency -0.29% [-1.41, +0.82].

</details>

## Details

- `CooperativeTopKParams`, the TMA staging buffers and the histogram loads are templated on the input type.
- TMA units are 16 bytes (8 BF16 or 4 FP32 elements), so the stride and per-block alignment follow the element
  size.
- Scores are widened to FP32 when binned, so both input types use the same radix keys.
- #59645's exact overflow recovery in `cooperative_topk_overflow.cuh` reads scores through the widening helpers
  #64138 added (`to_float`, `load_score4`), so a BF16 row recovers exactly as its FP32 widening does.
- The extension dispatches on `logits.scalar_type()`.
- `SparseIndexerTopk.takes_bf16_logits` (from #64138) now also returns true for `cooperative`, explicit or as
  `auto`'s choice, when its constraints hold (at most 64 rows; contiguous, 16-byte-aligned rows).
- Candidate-block selection (DeepSeek-V4.1) keeps FP32 block scores for explicit `cooperative`, as main does for
  `auto` and `persistent`. On B300, BF16 and FP32 block scores select the same blocks, including rows where every
  block ties. I could not run that model here.

Kernel changes from review, each A/B'd on B300 against the step before it (same method as above):

| commit | change | effect |
|---|---|---|
| [d8a0039](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172/commits/d8a0039505edf7c8e1bdbc84b3010ec68c30f45d) | The tie refinement ORs the ties' keys against the first one and runs only the radix-256 rounds over bits they differ in: one for BF16 (keys end in 16 zero bits), usually three for FP32. FP32 keeps the four rounds in the single-CTA path, where the extra pass measured up to 0.9% slower even on rows that refine no ties | with the next row, rows 1 to 64 at 64K and 256K: BF16 -11% to -21%, FP32 -2% to -16% |
| [f45b4b4](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172/commits/f45b4b4e3cdb53314635213e4172cc340fd52068) | The BF16 hot loops read two staged scores per 32-bit load and bin both with one packed FP16 conversion and key flip. An exhaustive GPU check gives the same bins as the scalar path for all 2^32 inputs | (above) |
| [ff286db](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172/commits/ff286dbe970d1929f9ec4a97d2450c8f2def8d88) | BF16 keeps twice as many elements resident in the same shared memory | -18% to -20% where rows now fit a single pass (4x1M, 8x512K, 16x256K, 33x256K, 64x128K to 192K), unchanged elsewhere |
| [9970c5a](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172/commits/9970c5ac5b4e6664400890d11159b19b41f0735f) | The single-CTA register path keeps BF16 packed (four scores per `uint2`) and bins it with two packed conversions; FP32 bins as before | BF16 rows up to 16K: -8% to -19%; `persistent_topk` BF16 rows up to 32K: -24% to -31%; FP32 unchanged |

Measured and not adopted:

- Storing bins instead of recomputing them in the scatter pass: the spare shared memory now holds the extra BF16
  stages, overwriting the staged scores would break the overflow recovery that rereads them, and after the packed
  conversion a bin costs one conversion per two scores.
- A 32K single-CTA limit for BF16 (the registers FP32 uses for 16K): -21% to -25% just past 16K, but up to +40%
  at 32K with k=2048 and +3% at 16K, so it stays at 16K.
- Re-tuning the cluster sizes: forcing each of 2, 4, 8 and 16 on every shape above, the row-count rule is within
  2% of the best in 112 of 120 shapes. The others (16 rows at 512K and 1M, 1 row at 64K) depend on the row
  length, which the launcher does not know: lengths are on the device, and a CUDA graph captures
  `max_model_len`.
- In ncu, FP16 conversions were 2% to 4% of the original BF16 kernel's instructions, while the per-element loop
  (`LOP3`, `ISETP`, `BRA`) was about 45%; the pair loads cut the latter.

title: [Kernel] Batch invariance: pin FlashInfer FP8 bmm and W4A16 NVFP4 kernels
author: 0z5a
body:
## Overview

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, pins two GEMM paths so that a row's result does not depend on the batch:

- FlashInfer's FP8 `bmm` (`flashinfer_scaled_fp8_mm`) is pinned to the `cutlass` backend.
- W4A16 NVFP4 linears use the Humming kernel.

This was split from #62017 by @aoshen02. Without BI, behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`: `flashinfer_scaled_fp8_mm` passes `backend="cutlass"` to `bmm_fp8` under BI and `"auto"` otherwise. With FlashInfer autotune (on by default at `-O1` and above), `"auto"` tunes over cutlass, cuBLAS and cuDNN per M bucket, so different batch sizes can run different backends.
- `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`: under BI, a W4A16 NVFP4 linear selects `HummingNvFp4LinearKernel`, which already reads `use_batch_invariant` from `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. Before this change, the BI branch forced the W4A4-only `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`, and kernel init raised `ValueError: CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel does not support W4A16`. With `--linear-backend` set to something other than Humming, a warning is logged and the setting is overridden.
- Tests:
  - `test_flashinfer_fp8_mm_batch_invariant_after_autotune` in `tests/v1/determinism/test_cutlass_batch_invariance.py` (SM100+);
  - `test_batch_invariant_w4a16_selects_humming` in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_kernel_selection.py` (CPU).

The router FP32-logits branch (with the `out_dtype` argument of `mm_batch_invariant`) and the two sm100 tuned M buckets for Nemotron-H shapes were moved out of this PR. They stay in #62017 for the Nemotron-H wiring.

## Validation

Hardware: GB200 (SM100), vLLM nightly image `0.32.0rc1.dev281+g49cb2bbf7`, FlashInfer 0.7.2. The touched files are identical between that image and this PR's base `fa75d3456d`, so "base" is the image as shipped and "PR" is the image with this PR's two files overlaid.

**FP8 `bmm`.** Static per-tensor FP8 inputs. Each M slice `x[:M]` was compared bitwise against the first M rows of the M=2048 output, for M in {1, 2, 7, 16, 64, 128, 512, 2048}, on four (N, K) shapes. The table counts rows that differ.

| Backend | Autotune | 4096x4096 | 2688x4096 | 4608x2688 | 14336x4096 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` (base) | off | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `auto` (base) | on | M=128: 14, M=512: 50 | M=512: 21 | 0 | M=7: 2, M=64: 15, M=128: 30 |
| `cutlass` (PR) | off | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `cutlass` (PR) | on | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Max abs diff of the differing rows is 3e-5 to 6e-5. Without autotune, `"auto"` falls back to its first runner (cutlass), so it is invariant; the variance only appears after tuning. As a diagnostic, cuBLAS alone and cuDNN alone were each invariant after autotune on these shapes: the variance comes from switching backends between buckets. The new test failed in 1 of 2 runs at base (the tuner's pick is timing dependent) and passed in 2 of 2 runs with the PR.

**W4A16 NVFP4.** A synthetic `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4(use_a16=True)` layer, with the same M sweep, on shapes 4096x4096, 2688x4096 and 4608x2688.

| Code | BI | Kernel | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 1 | — | `ValueError: CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel does not support W4A16` at init |
| PR | 1 | `HummingNvFp4LinearKernel` | 0 rows differ at every M, outputs finite |
| base/PR | 0 | `FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4W4A16LinearKernel` (unchanged) | 0 rows differ in this sweep (without autotune) |

So the W4A16 change fixes a crash at init under BI rather than a numerical difference.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_kernel_selection.py
# 4 passed; the new test fails at base with the ValueError above
pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_cutlass_batch_invariance.py -k test_flashinfer_fp8_mm_batch_invariant_after_autotune
# GB200: PR 2/2 passed; base 1/2 failed
```

`pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes on the changed files.

Not tested: end-to-end serving of an FP8 or W4A16 NVFP4 model under BI, and throughput. Humming and pinned `cutlass` are chosen for invariance, not speed.

title: [Model] NemotronHMTP: share the target's embedding and LM head
author: 0z5a
body:
## Purpose

`NemotronHMTP` now loads only `mtp.*` weights and always uses the target's embedding and LM head, on every pipeline stage. Both modules start as `None`, and `has_own_embed_tokens = False` / `has_own_lm_head = False` let the existing sharing helpers attach the target's modules before execution. Because the drafter holds the target's modules, a target weight refit also updates the drafter.

Before this change, with PP=2 the drafter got its own copy of the embedding instead of the target's. MTP acceptance dropped to about 9%.

This is a self-contained split of #62017 by @aoshen02, with authorship retained.

## Behavior change

On main, a checkpoint containing `lm_head.*` sets `has_own_lm_head = True`, and the drafter shares the head only if it equals the target's. With this PR the drafter always uses the target's head. For Nemotron-H checkpoints the MTP `lm_head.*` is the target's, so the result is the same. A checkpoint with a genuinely different MTP head would have that head ignored.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py
```

The new tests check two things:
- Only `mtp.*` weights are loaded, with and without the `language_model.` prefix.
- With PP=1 and PP=2 the drafter shares the target embedding, and a target refit is visible to the drafter.

Model probe: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`, GH200, TP=1, MTP with 3 draft tokens, temperature 0, 12 prompts × 64 tokens, eager.

## Test Result

- Both test files: 45 passed.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passes on the changed files.

| Run | Embedding / head shared | Draft acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PP=2, main | head only | 161/1797 (9.0%) |
| PP=2, this PR | both | 526/747 (70.4%) |
| PP=1, this PR | both | 526/747 (70.4%) |

With this PR, the PP=1 and PP=2 outputs are token-identical on 12/12 prompts.

title: [Perf][ToolParser] Scan Kimi K3 streaming tool calls incrementally
author: waizuichougou
body:
## Overview

Kimi K3 streaming tool extraction rescanned the accumulated tools section and
redecoded completed calls on every delta. This change resumes parsing from the
last unfinished call boundary and decodes each completed call once.

## Claims

- Reduce CPU parsing time for native Kimi K3 tool streams, including `auto` and
  `required` tool choices.
- Preserve response content, tool-call timing, names, argument bytes, indices,
  types, and ID presence.
- Keep the optimization inside `KimiK3ToolParser` and reuse its existing call
  matching and decoding logic.
- This is separate from [#60882](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60882),
  which optimizes the generic JSON scanner for `tool_choice="required"`.
- [#50627](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50627) streams Kimi K3
  arguments before a call closes; this change preserves the existing
  announcement timing and removes repeated parsing after calls close.

## Validation

Five-run CPU parser medians after warmup, using four-character deltas and
alternating before/after order. Timings include text-history accumulation and
parsing, excluding parser construction.

| Workload | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256-character string argument | 0.523 ms | 0.332 ms | 1.57x |
| 4,096-character string argument | 5.463 ms | 2.602 ms | 2.10x |
| 16,384-character string argument | 36.611 ms | 10.000 ms | 3.66x |
| 65,536-character string argument | 401.085 ms | 43.256 ms | 9.27x |
| Truncated 65,536-character argument | 398.718 ms | 42.784 ms | 9.32x |

Response-only parsing remains at baseline speed. These are CPU parser results and
do not establish GPU inference or end-to-end serving throughput.

- Differential replay: 16,540 streams and 189,754 deltas, with no differences.
- Composed `KimiK3Parser` replay matched across `auto`, `required`, and `none`,
  with and without reasoning.
- Relevant tests: 178 passed.
- Ruff, formatting, mypy, and `git diff --check` passed.

```bash
python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/tool_use/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_kimi_k3_named_tool_choice.py \
  tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -k kimi_k3
```

## Details

The existing call regex and decoder remain responsible for recognizing and
decoding calls. A call-close regex finds newly completed call blocks; the parser
then scans only the unparsed interval. Partial matching preserves close markers
split across deltas, including whitespace variants. Matched invalid call blocks
still advance the parsed span, so they do not affect later call indices.

The change adds two parser offsets and does not introduce a scanner class or a
second accumulated text buffer. Response extraction and tools-channel discovery
remain unchanged. The optimization reduces repeated tool-call work while the
existing caller-side history concatenation and full response/channel searches
remain. The existing K3 decoder remains responsible for decoding calls after a complete call boundary is found.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep the EAGLE-reachable SWA tail at a shared-prefix junction
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Overview

This PR fixes cross-request prefix reuse for sliding-window groups under EAGLE/MTP with sparse prefix-cache retention. The shared-prefix junction pin from #47782 kept a sliding-window tail one block too high, so requests that share only a prefix got no prefix-cache hit at all. The fix also pins the tail one block lower, which is where an EAGLE sibling's hit actually lands.

## Claims

- Under sparse retention, a sibling request that shares only a prefix now gets a prefix-cache hit when the drafter's groups are sliding-window and the full-attention groups are not EAGLE groups. On Step-5-Preview with MTP, the GSM8K 5-shot prefix goes from 0 hit tokens to a hit on every request after the first two.
- Nothing changes without EAGLE, or when every group is flagged as an EAGLE group. In those cases the junction already sits one block lower, because the full-attention group drops its block too.
- The cost is one extra cached block per sliding-window group for each request that registers a junction.

## Validation

**Unit test.** `test_swa_shared_prefix_reuse_under_zero_retention` gets a `use_eagle` case that flags only the SWA group, as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61455 does for drafters. It fails on main (0 instead of 48 hit tokens) and passes with the fix.

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py
620 passed, 2 errors
```

The 2 errors are `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate`, which needs a GPU and a model checkpoint (the run was CPU-only). On a wider set (`tests/v1/core`, Mooncake Store and offloading connector unit tests), the failure set with and without this PR is identical (GPU- or model-dependent tests), apart from the new case.

**End to end.** Step-5-Preview (MTP layers are sliding-window, the target also has full-attention DSA layers), 4x GB300, TP4 + EP, MTP k=3. Prefix caching runs with `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 1024`. The test runs on the Step5 preview branch of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61727, with this change applied.

12 GSM8K 5-shot prompts are sent one at a time. They share a 565-token prefix, and every prompt is shorter than 1024 tokens.

| | request 1 | request 2 | requests 3–12 |
|---|---|---|---|
| no MTP | 0 | 0 | 560 each |
| MTP k=3, without this PR | 0 | 0 | **0** |
| MTP k=3, this PR | 0 | 0 | 544 each |

Request 2 detects the junction, so later requests can hit. 544 is one block below the 560-token junction, which is the deepest hit an EAGLE lookup can verify.

Full GSM8K (1319 questions, concurrency 64, MTP k=3, Mooncake Store connector on):

| | without this PR | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| local prefix-cache hit tokens / queried | 0 / 839,793 | 737,520 / 839,793 (87.8%) |
| accuracy | 0.933 | 0.935 |
| Mooncake Store replay vs GPU-cache replay | 64/64 bit-identical | 64/64 bit-identical |

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. Request A runs alone.
2. Request B shares a prefix with A, but under sparse retention only A's full-attention blocks are still cached. `get_computed_blocks` reports the junction J as the full-attention hit length (B's shared prefix floored to a block), and B pins J.
3. The sliding-window mask keeps the `need`-block tail at J. Under EAGLE, that tail is shifted one block right, to include the block past J as the lookahead (#44082). This is right for a replay of the same prompt.
4. The block past J holds B's own tokens, so for request C it is not shared. C's SWA lookup must verify one block past its hit, so its best hit is J − block_size. That hit needs the window one block lower than the pinned tail, and the lowest block was never kept.
5. C gets no hit and pins the same J again, so no later request ever hits.

When every group takes the EAGLE drop (no group flagged), the full-attention hit is already one block lower, so J lands where the SWA hit can verify. The bug therefore shows only when a sliding-window group is an EAGLE group and the full-attention group that reports the junction is not. Step5 MTP already met this under the older "group holding the last registered layer" rule. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61455 makes per-group flags the general rule: drafters whose layers are sliding-window now flag only those groups.

**Fix.** Under EAGLE, `cache_blocks` registers both J and J − block_size as reachable boundaries. The masks overlap, so this keeps one extra block. Replay boundaries are unchanged, because they already account for the EAGLE drop (#54713, #61012). Mamba checkpointing reads `shared_prefix_boundary` directly and is unaffected.

**Not covered.** `OffloadingConnector` builds its own reachable boundaries from `shared_prefix_boundary` and is not changed here.

title: [NIXL] Drop unreachable producer-side notif counting in push mode
author: sawsa307
body:
## Overview

Remove the producer-side branch of `NixlPushConnectorWorker._get_new_notifs`, which no push-mode code path can reach. Split out of #61488 / #61580 as an independent simplification, as suggested in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61580#issuecomment-6237375565.

## Claims

- No behavior change for P or D in push mode: the removed branch only ran on a plain `"<req_id>:<n>"` notif arriving at P, which push mode never sends.
- `_get_new_notifs` now only counts consumer-side completion notifs and always returns an empty set; P keeps reporting finished sends from its WRITE handles in `get_transfer_results`.
- 26 insertions, 59 deletions.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py`: 103 passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py`: 182 passed. The two `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller` cases fail locally on main as well.
- With a tripwire in the removed branch, the push, heartbeat and NIXL connector unit tests pass without reaching it.
- On GB200, the tripwire was not reached in end-to-end push runs with TP1 → TP1, producer TP2 → consumer TP1 and producer TP1 → consumer TP2, and those runs met their expected outputs. These runs used the same `push_worker.py` change on the #61488 branch.

## Details

In push mode, D sends P only two kinds of notifs:
- `PUSH_REG`, consumed by the writer thread before notifs are forwarded to `_get_new_notifs`;
- `HB:`, handled at the top of `_get_new_notifs` before the counting.

Plain `"<req_id>:<n>"` notifs to P come from `_pending_recv_notifs`, which only `pull_worker.py` fills. P → D completion notifs are attached to the push WRITEs and are counted on D, which is the branch this PR keeps.

The removed code is the producer-side counting copied from pull mode, the `transfer_topo` assert it needed, and the counter cleanup for finished pushes in `get_transfer_results`. One edge case changes: on a `kv_both` instance where one request is both loading and saving, a completion notif for it is now counted as a load instead of a send. Push mode never sends such a notif to the producer side.

Not a duplicate: #55470 also edits `_get_new_notifs` (it adds a failed-WRITE notif path) but keeps the producer-side branch. Whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

title: [Kernel][Perf] Add H100 tuned configs for Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B to the batch-invariant matmul table
author: Monishver11
body:
## Overview

In short: in batch-invariant (BI) mode (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`), every bf16 linear layer and the lm_head run the Triton kernel `matmul_kernel_persistent` instead of cuBLAS. Its tile comes from a per-GPU table, and the Hopper table only has the five Qwen3-1.7B shapes (measured on an H20), so Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B run the default 128x128x64 tile on H100. This PR adds H100-measured entries for their 8 TP=1 shapes to the `"hopper"` family.

With BI on, on an H100 SXM:
- `vllm bench latency` is 1.85-2.79x faster than main.
- The BI tax (latency with BI on / latency with BI off) drops from 2.13-2.99x on main to 1.03-1.20x with this PR.
- GSM8K stays within 0.5 standard error (SE) of main.

Related: tracker [#27433](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433), same kind of table as [#53247](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53247), [#57456](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57456), [#58495](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58495).

## Key results

- 8 new `(N, K)` entries in `_BATCH_INVARIANT_MATMUL_TUNED_CONFIGS["hopper"]`: gate_up/down/lm_head of Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B plus their shared qkv/o. Existing entries and other families are not touched.
- One `BLOCK_K` per shape, so a row's K-reduction order does not depend on M. Checked bit for bit through the real `matmul_persistent` dispatch: 2028/2028 cases identical.
- Kernel (H100 SXM, cold L2): geomean 2.03x vs main over 80 (shape, M) cases, 2.89x at M <= 64; the slowest case is 1.00x (Qwen3 gate_up at M=2048, 827 vs 828 us). At M <= 64 the kernel is now 0.90-1.12x of cuBLAS time (main: 1.48-4.09x).
- E2E latency with the flag on (fresh process per run, 2 interleaved rounds):

- `vllm bench serve` (1024 in / 128 out, 1000 prompts, rate inf, 3 interleaved rounds, req/s; rounds 1 / 2 / 3, then the mean). Llama-3.1-8B gains 13.6%. Qwen3-8B does not change; Details explains why (the execution mode these shapes switch on, not the tiles).

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GPU: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 SXM, 132 SMs, power limit 700 W of 700 W.
- Software: driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, triton 3.8.0.
- main = 307c5844ad. PR = main + this commit, applied on the box with `git am` (same diff).
- main and PR are the same checkout, switched with `git checkout`. Every run is a fresh process.
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct checkpoint: `unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, an ungated copy. It has the same architecture and layer shapes as `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`; its config.json adds `pad_token_id`. I did not compare the weights against the gated repo.
- [#61118](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61118) merged after this base. It enables Inductor's `batch_invariant` flag. It can only change the torch.compile arms (main, and PR + torch.compile under Details). It does not change this PR's default breakable-graph mode, because that mode does not run Inductor.

**Bitwise.**
- Path: `matmul_persistent` on the PR tree, all 13 hopper shapes.
- Check: a probe row at rows 0, M/2 and M-1 must equal the same row computed at M=1.
- M values (39): 1-17, every bucket edge ±1, 100, 1000, 3000 and 4096.
- 2 seeds. Weight as `w.t()` (the linear layout) and as a contiguous `(K, N)` tensor.
- Result: 2028/2028 identical, 0 mismatched.

**Tests** (PR tree):

```
pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py                                  # 35 passed, 2 skipped
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-8B pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py            # 22 passed
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py  # 22 passed
```

**Kernel**, `matmul_persistent` main -> PR, us per call.
- Each point is a CUDA graph of 4-24 launches. The script aims for about 2 ms of work per replay (4 to 20 launches), rounded up to whole cycles of the weight copies.
- The launches cycle over enough weight copies to read >= 4x L2 per pass.
- main is the mean of two runs, one before and one after the PR run. The two runs agree within 0.98-1.08x.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Align speculator hidden norm in GLM-4.5/4.6 MoE and GLM-OCR MTP with GLM5Next to recycle post-final-hidden.
author: spandantiwari
body:
### Overview

Three GLM-family MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) models — `glm4_moe_mtp.py` (GLM-4.5 / GLM-4.5-Air / GLM-4.6), `glm4_moe_lite_mtp.py` (GLM-4.7-Flash), and `glm_ocr_mtp.py` (GLM-OCR) — return the **pre-final-norm** hidden from the MTP layer, so the speculator recycles a hidden that is one RMSNorm short into the next draft step's `hnorm`. The established GLM/DeepSeek-NextN contract (already merged in vLLM by #47448 and also SGLang's `glm4_moe_nextn`/`deepseek_nextn` `vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py`) recycles the **post-final-norm** hidden. This PR extends that contract to the three models it missed, and registers them in `SpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple()` so Model Runner V1 unpacks the new tuple return. Draft-only change; verified output is unaffected.

**Relation to #62986:** #62986 (opened after this PR) fixes the same recycle for `Glm4MoeMTP` only, DeepSeek-style; its description offers to close in favour of this PR once the V1 registration is included, which it now is (`6ecfab6`). #62987 (enabling `torch.compile` for `Glm4MoeMTP`) is independent.

### Claims

- **Correctness/contract alignment:** each MTP layer now applies the final norm once (fused `shared_head.norm(hidden, residual)`) and returns the post-final-norm hidden for both tuple positions, with `compute_logits` consuming it directly — identical to #47448 and `glm5next`.
- **Both model runners:** Model Runner V2 unpacks tuple returns generically; Model Runner V1 (`SpecDecodeBaseProposer`) only unpacks registered architectures, so `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` and `GlmOcrMTPModel` are added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Without that, V1 crashes on the first draft step (below).
- **Lossless:** speculative decoding verifies every drafted token, so the target-visible output is unchanged; only the drafter's recycled state changes (affects draft steps ≥1, i.e. `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 2`).
- **No performance regression, and no performance claim.** On a real checkpoint (GLM-4.5-Air) a controlled, paired acceptance measurement shows **no statistically significant change** in draft acceptance (details below).

### Validation

**Drafter contract (unit, real objects):** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden`, parametrized over GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-OCR configs (shrunk). Each drafter is built by `get_model` with `load_format="dummy"` and runs its real forward. The feedback hidden must equal `shared_head.norm` of the MTP block output (captured with a forward hook), which is also what `compute_logits` used to feed the `lm_head`, so logits are unchanged.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k feeds_back_final_normed
# model files from the PR base (49f944be3e): 3 failed
E       AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E       Mismatched elements: 1536 / 1536 (100.0%)
# this PR: 3 passed
```

**Both model runners (e2e through `LLM`, real weights):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1|mrv2]` runs `zai-org/GLM-OCR` with `num_speculative_tokens=2` and asserts both draft positions are accepted. Per-position acceptance on MI355X: MRV2 `[0.610, 0.285]`, MRV1 `[0.592, 0.271]`.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py
# first commit of this PR (c10a4c9: tuple return, no V1 registration), [mrv1]:
TypeError: only integer tensors of a single element can be converted to an index
FAILED ...::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1] - EngineDeadError
# this PR: 2 passed
```

The registration itself is also covered by `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (CPU CI), extended with the three architectures. The new e2e directory runs in the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo (+ GLM)" step. `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` and `test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`: 13 passed; `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

**Test durations** (`pytest --durations=0`, single MI355X; checkpoints already cached):

| test | cases | time per case |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden` (new) | 3 | 1.1–4.9 s (GLM-4.5-Air 4.9 s, GLM-OCR 1.4 s, GLM-4.7-Flash 1.1 s) |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners` (new) | 2 | 52 s (MRV1), 94 s (MRV2, incl. `torch.compile` + CUDA-graph capture) |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (3 cases added, CPU) | 3 | < 0.5 s |

The e2e test adds about 2.5 min to the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo + GLM" step (first run also downloads `zai-org/GLM-OCR`, 2.7 GB).

**Acceptance measurement (end-to-end, fixed-prefix)** — GLM-4.5-Air (bf16), MI355X, `method=mtp`, k=3, 600 gsm8k prompts, each generating one spec-decode round from a **fixed starting prefix**, paired per prompt. Position 0 does not consume the recycled hidden, so it is a near-control (not bit-exact — see below):

| position | before (pre-norm) | after (post-norm) | diff | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p0 (near-control) | 0.7330 | 0.7298 | −0.0032 | 0.88 |
| p1 | 0.5438 | 0.5479 | +0.0042 | 0.86 |
| p2 | 0.2232 | 0.2277 | +0.0045 | 0.82 |

Paired per-prompt accepted tokens: +0.018 ± 0.016 (Wilcoxon p=0.25). The position-0 result is **statistically consistent with no change** (p=0.88); its tiny drift is floating-point from the eager→fused add+norm (mathematically identical). No affected position shows a significant change either. This is an end-to-end comparison from fixed prefixes; it does not isolate each later position's conditional acceptance, since draft histories can still diverge within a round. Net: acceptance (and thus speed) is effectively unaffected.

**Reference** — SGLang `glm4_moe_nextn.py` / `deepseek_nextn.py` apply the final norm and recycle the post-norm hidden; GLM-4-MoE NextN is a faithful DeepSeek-V3 NextN clone.

### Details

Root cause: the MTP layer forward ended with `hidden_states = residual + hidden_states; return hidden_states` (pre-final-norm), and `compute_logits` applied `shared_head` to it. The speculators store the model's returned hidden as the next step's `previous_hidden_states` (fed into `hnorm`), so the recycled state was missing the final `shared_head` RMSNorm that DeepSeek/`glm5next` apply; the logits path was always correctly single-normed. Fix (per file):

```python
hidden_states, _ = self.shared_head.norm(hidden_states, residual=residual)
return hidden_states, hidden_states
```

plus `compute_logits`: `shared_head.head, hidden_states` (drop the second norm), and the three architectures added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Affects the single-module AR path (`num_nextn_predict_layers=1`, k≥2 — the common GLM-4.5/4.6 case) and the multi-module path; k=1 is unaffected.

The two tuple elements are intentionally the same post-norm tensor, as in #47448 and `glm5next`, which go through the same recycle sites: the MRV2 AR step-0 setup stores `last_hidden_states[idx]`, MRV2 steps ≥1 and the multi-module path recycle the second element, and V1 unpacks the tuple once the architecture is registered.

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimal change; mirrors the existing #47448 / `glm5next` pattern exactly.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Real-object drafter test and an e2e test on both model runners (GLM-OCR) in CI; acceptance validated out-of-CI on GLM-4.5-Air (checkpoint too large for CI).
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.
