title: [Perf][DSA] Rank the prefill indexer logits with DeepSelect in BF16
author: Juntian777
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `sparse_indexer_topk_backend="deep_select"`, the sparse-indexer prefill path still upcasts DeepGEMM's BF16 MQA logits to FP32 and ranks them with `top_k_per_row_prefill`. This PR ranks the BF16 logits with DeepSelect directly, as decode already does since #56464.

## Claims

- On SM100 with `deep_select`, each indexer prefill chunk drops the FP32 upcast (`as_fp32_logits`) and its top-k gets 3.7x faster.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill, DEP2 on GB200, 8 requests per rank of 4,096 new tokens on a 128K prefix hit: 429.8 -> 401.5 ms per step (-6.6%), indexer 64.5 -> 30.9 ms.
- The selected top-k values are unchanged: BF16 widens to FP32 exactly. Which index wins among exactly equal logits was already unspecified (see #56749).
- Accuracy is unchanged: GSM8K strict-match 0.924 / 0.923 over two runs and passkey retrieval 20/20 at ~8K / 31K / 62K-token prompts (DEP4 on GB200).
- Default behavior is unchanged: only `--kernel-config '{"sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}'` takes the new path. DCP, XPU, other top-k backends and logits whose row stride DeepSelect cannot read keep the FP32 path.

## Validation

Top-k alone, one GB200, CUPTI, cold L2, median of 3 rounds. Rows of one query chunk over 65,536 compressed keys (a 128K V4.1 request) with causal row ends, top-k 512, random BF16 logits. Base is `as_fp32_logits` + `top_k_per_row_prefill`, new is `deep_select_topk(..., end=row_ends)`:

| rows | base (us) | new (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 66.5 | 13.6 | 4.9x |
| 2048 | 414.4 | 110.1 | 3.8x |
| 4096 | 777.2 | 210.0 | 3.7x |
| 8192 | 1503.9 | 410.7 | 3.7x |

On every row both select exactly the values `torch.topk` selects; index sets differ only among ties at the 512th value, and all indices lie inside the row.

Prefill step, `vllm bench forward`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with dummy weights, DEP2 on one GB200 node, `--case 'ds8x4k=8*4096@131072' --kv-len-jitter 0 --max-num-batched-tokens 34816`, no speculative decoding, FlashMLA MegaAttn with the MXFP4 indexer, `deep_select` top-k, rank 0 under nsys, ms per step:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| step (bench median) | 429.8 | 401.5 |
| indexer logits + top-k | 64.5 | 30.9 |
| of which upcast + top-k | 39.4 | 5.7 |

The step numbers come from our DSv4.1 branch (nightly 49cb2bbf plus DSv4.1 changes outside the indexer); `sparse_attn_indexer` there is identical to main before this change.

Tests on GB200, same branch with this change:

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "deep_select or sparse_indexer" \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
43 passed, 4 skipped
```

No new test: `test_deep_select_topk` and `test_deep_select_topk_preallocated_output` already cover what this path relies on (BF16 input, per-row `end`, -1 fill for rows shorter than top-k, output into a slice of a wider buffer).

Accuracy with this change (`vllm serve`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 on one GB200 node, `sparse_indexer_topk_backend="deep_select"`, DSpark K=5 with standard rejection sampling, greedy):

| eval | result |
|---|---|
| passkey retrieval, ~8K / 31K / 62K-token prompts (20 each; 4K-31K compressed keys per row, well above top-k) | 20/20, 20/20, 20/20 |
| GSM8K, lm_eval 5-shot, max 1024 tokens, concurrency 32, strict-match (two runs) | 0.9242 / 0.9227 (±0.0073) |
| DSpark acceptance length over the second GSM8K run | 3.44 (48.9% per draft token) |

The GSM8K and acceptance numbers match what we saw before this change on the same model (0.9318 strict-match and 3.36 in a P/D setup).

## Details

- Multi-request chunks: since #61149, DeepGEMM returns compressed logits in which every row starts at column zero (`row_starts is None` on CUDA), so `end = cu_seqlen_ke - cu_seqlen_ks` is each row's full causal interval for any number of requests in a chunk. #57206 tried this before that change, limited itself to single-request chunks, and was closed.
- Duplicate check: #57206 (closed, see above); #62172 lets `cooperative_topk` read BF16 logits on the decode path; #60618 (WIP) fuses scoring and top-k for prefill in a new kernel; #56749 changes tie-breaking of the existing prefill kernel. None changes the `deep_select` prefill path.
- The logits chunk budget (`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`) still assumes FP32 logits; counting BF16 would allow chunks twice as tall and is left for a follow-up.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, write and validate this change and to draft this description.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Report every transfer group as loaded in DecodeBenchConnector
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

`DecodeBenchConnector` fills a new request's own blocks in every KV cache group, like a P/D transfer, but it inherits the base `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, which reports only the prefix-cacheable groups (what a hash-addressed store holds). A bounded-replay sliding-window group (DeepSeek V4.1) is not prefix-cacheable, so `_load_restores_replay_window` is false and the scheduler replays the last window on the first step of every filled request. That step becomes a prefill of about one window (128 tokens on DeepSeek V4.1) instead of a one-token decode, and with DP every rank leaves the FULL decode graph whenever any rank admits a request, so decode-only benchmarks with this connector do not reflect P/D decode.

This returns `transfer_group_ids`, the same as `NixlConnector` and `MooncakeConnector` since #59197. The connector is synchronous, so `skip_zeroing_group_ids` (async loads only) is unaffected; the only change is that the filled window is taken as is.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR changes the loaded groups of `DecodeBenchConnector`. #61543 skips non-transfer groups on the fill side (a HiSparse crash) and is complementary: with both, the connector fills and reports the same `transfer_group_ids`. #59197 added the replay skip and the NIXL / Mooncake overrides but left this connector on the default.

## Test Plan

- New `test_decode_bench_fill_does_not_replay` in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py`: the real scheduler with `DecodeBenchConnector` on a full-attention + bounded-replay `SlidingWindowMLASpec` layout; a filled request must start with a one-token step and no replay. It fails without the fix (`replay_start` is 64, not 0).
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py`
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files

## Test Result

44 passed. `pre-commit` passed.

No model eval: this only changes which tokens a decode benchmark recomputes after a dummy fill; real serving and P/D connectors are untouched.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [XPU] Enable spec-decode adaptive verification without a confidence head
author: yma11
body:
## Overview

PR #52228 provides support adaptive verification without a confidence head and this PR enable it for XPU path. We identified perf gap caused by FA kernel and can be addressed by PR [647](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/647)(Not block current enablement). With these 2 PRs, we got below bench results:

## Performance Summary

Benchmarked Muse-Glimmer-30B + DFlash2 on **8 Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs (TP8)**,
comparing adaptive verification enabled/disabled at K=3/5/7.

Server launch:
```
ADAPTIVE=true

"${VLLM[@]}" serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name "$MODEL" --port 8000 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config "{
    \"method\":\"dflash\",
    \"model\":\"z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2\",
    \"attention_backend\":\"FLASH_ATTN\",
    \"num_speculative_tokens\":${K},
    \"draft_sample_method\":\"probabilistic\",
    \"enable_adaptive_verification\":${ADAPTIVE}
  }"
```

Output throughput change with adaptive verification enabled, relative to
disabled at the same K:

| Workload | K3 | K5 | K7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SPEED, high entropy, BS24 | -2.59% | +5.40% | +6.25% |
| SPEED, low entropy, BS24 | -4.99% | +3.81% | +2.21% |
| Sonnet, BS32 | -3.18% | +11.10% | +11.70% |

- **SPEED:** 12 configurations, 512 requests/configuration, 512 output
  tokens/request. Adaptive verification improves K5/K7 throughput, while K3
  without adaptive remains the fastest measured configuration.
- **Sonnet:** 6 configurations, 96 requests/configuration, 2048 output
  tokens/request. K5 + adaptive achieves the highest throughput
  (**468.55 tok/s**), 2.80% above K3 without adaptive. Mean E2E latency decreases
  by **8.17% at K5** and **10.98% at K7** versus their respective disabled controls.
- All **6,720 requests succeeded**, with zero failures.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3] Enable the fp8 indexer cache on gfx942
author: akii96
body:
## Overview

Unlocks `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'` for MiniMax-M3 on ROCm gfx942 (MI300-series, CDNA3). gfx950 (MI350-series) keeps its fp8 routing through the AITER indexer, and CUDA behavior is unchanged.

## Claims

- fp8 indexer cache now selects on gfx942: Triton scorers get an e4m3**fnuz** cache instead of bf16, with correct saturation in both index-cache writers.
- +32% KV cache capacity for the same GPU memory.
- Serving throughput is neutral at short context and better at long context; GSM8K is unchanged.
- gfx950 keeps the pre-patch routing (fp8 via the AITER indexer, e4m3fn/OCP convert); NVIDIA keeps e4m3fn, `constexpr` 448.

## Validation

8x MI325X (gfx942), nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-39983a5e`, `EmbeddedLLM/MiniMax-M3-FP8-dynamic`, TP4, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 262144`.

| run | log line |

| before | `MiniMax M3 indexer: selected Triton (no fmha_sm100) [topk_blocks=16, indexer_kv_dtype=bf16, sm100=False]` |
| after | `MiniMax M3 indexer: selected Triton (no fmha_sm100) [topk_blocks=16, indexer_kv_dtype=fp8, sm100=False]` |

| | KV tokens | max concurrency @ 262k |
|---|---|---|
| before | 4,554,368 | 17.37x |
| after | 6,020,992 | 22.97x |

`vllm bench serve` (openai-chat, random dataset, exact ISL/OSL, `--ignore-eos --temperature 0`, N=32/48/16/8, median):

| ISL/OSL/conc | Out tok/s | Δ | TTFT p50 (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 (ms) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k/1k/8 | 468.6 → 470.4 | +0.4% | 3540 → 3519 | −0.6% | 13.95 → 13.93 | −0.1% |
| 8k/1k/16 | 697.4 → 700.4 | +0.4% | 4359 → 4365 | +0.1% | 18.85 → 18.66 | −1.0% |
| 32k/1k/8 | 284.2 → 290.0 | +2.0% | 9945 → 9830 | −1.2% | 18.43 → 17.98 | −2.4% |
| 128k/1k/4 | 92.6 → 96.3 | +4.0% | 21587 → 21104 | −2.2% | 22.12 → 20.94 | −5.3% |

GSM8K (lm-eval 0.4.13, `local-chat-completions`, 8-shot, chat template, temp 0, 1319 samples):

| | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| before | 94.69% ± 0.62 | 94.62% |
| after | 95.00% ± 0.60 | 94.92% |

Kernel tests on gfx942 (`tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py`): **61 passed, 32 skipped (nvfp4-only), 0 failed**, including the new insert-saturation, foreign-flavour-rejection, and fp8-vs-bf16 top-k equivalence tests. 

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
# after (before: omit the last flag)
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0
vllm serve EmbeddedLLM/MiniMax-M3-FP8-dynamic \
  --served-model-name minimax-m3 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --block-size 128 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --async-scheduling --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --language-model-only \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model minimax-m3 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \
  --save-result --result-dir . --result-filename result.json

pip install "lm-eval[api]"
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,model=minimax-m3,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8 --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=1024 --output_path gsm8k_out

python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py -v
```
</details>

## Details

Root cause, three pieces:

- `select_indexer_impl_cls` refused `indexer_kv_dtype="fp8"` on every ROCm platform, although the Triton scorers are flavour-agnostic (fp8 x fp8 accumulated in fp32).
- The index cache was pinned to e4m3**fn** (`torch.float8_e4m3fn`), which gfx942 cannot convert.
- The fused qknorm/rope/kv-insert writer picked its convert with `#if defined(HIP_FP8_TYPE_OCP)` — the macro is always defined (to 0 or 1), so gfx942 took the OCP branch and emitted OCP-labelled bytes that read back as wrong fnuz values (e.g. 1.1 -> 1.0, 0.77 -> 0).

The fix: the cache takes `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` (fnuz on gfx942, fn on gfx950/CUDA as before), the selector admits fp8 on ROCm gfx942 via the platform's `on_gfx942()` predicate, and the writer picks the flavour per target (`__gfx942__` -> fnuz) with saturation at `quant_type_max_v` (224 for fnuz, 448 for e4m3fn). Host checks expect the device's own flavour via the existing `is_fp8_ocp()`, and the Triton index-cache insert (AITER sparse-PA path) saturates at the same bound instead of producing NaN for out-of-range keys. gfx950's fp8 path keeps going through the AITER indexer (`SUPPORTED_ARCHS=("gfx950",)`), selected before this fallback is consulted.

Not a duplicate: the closest open PRs touching this area (#60930 CuTe prefill scorer, #59979/#59980 FMHA/MSA) are NVIDIA-side work; none enable the fp8 index cache on gfx942

title: [ROCm][CI] Pin Inductor pointwise configs in the MoRIIO dummy-weight P/D test
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Turn off Inductor pointwise autotuning (`triton.autotune_pointwise`) next to deterministic mode in `test_write_dummy_e2e_rocm.py`, and update the comment and docstring that explain why

Since the ROCm 10 image became the default (#58761), the attention-only cases fail with first-token log-prob distances of one or two bf16 steps (0.03-0.14), e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95663. P/D is not involved: two plain direct serves of the same model on the same GPU disagree by the same amount, while each server is bitwise stable across repeats. Inductor's deterministic mode only pins reduction configs and still picks the XBLOCK of pointwise kernels by timing. On ROCm the XBLOCK changes which multiply-adds of the fused QK-norm + RoPE kernel get contracted into FMAs (e.g. 4 unfused packed adds at XBLOCK 1024, none at 4096), and the candidates are within timing noise of each other, so each server ends up with a random config. Pinning every pointwise kernel's config in two fresh processes makes them agree bitwise; flipping only the QK-norm + RoPE kernel's XBLOCK reproduces the CI distances.

With this change the CI-failing `qwen3_dense-TRITON_ATTN-P_FULL_AND_PIECEWISE-D_FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` case passes 10/10 on MI355 with ROCm 10 (distances exactly 0.0, full external prefix-cache hits).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Wait for all peers before completing failed receives to avoid potential KV block write-after-free
author: zhou-yuhan
body:
## Overview

Address premature D-side KV block reclamation when one Mooncake P peer fails while another peer can still write to the request's destination blocks (write-after-free).

## Related

- [Improving MooncakeConnector #60523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523).
- [Mooncake bootstrap and KV transfer failures can leave PD requests waiting without terminal error propagation #55870](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55870)
- [Report failed remote KV loads to the scheduler #50984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50984): adds error handling at D-side but leaves this bug.
- [#61006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61006): guards stale scheduler notifications.
- [#50565](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50565): suppresses cleanup-only completions.
- [#57529](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57529): adds an unwired failure ledger.

These related PRs do not track outstanding peer results for a failed receive.


## Motivation

### Failure mechanism

A D request can receive KV slices from multiple P peers (P0, P1), if a peer (say P0) fails to transfer a request's KV:

1. P0 reports a transfer error while P1 still holds the destination addresses.
2. `_handle_failed_recv()` marks the request failed, reports its invalid blocks, and **adds it to `finished_recving_reqs` without waiting for the other peers**.
3. With `kv_load_failure_policy=fail`, the scheduler marks the request `FINISHED_ERROR` and consumes that completion to release its blocks.
4. P1 can subsequently write to those addresses, after the blocks have returned to the pool or been allocated to another request.

Failure notification therefore permits reclamation before all writers have finished. This is a KV-block write-after-free; the underlying registered GPU allocation remains valid, so the stale WRITE can succeed. [#50984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50984) fixed failure propagation and stranded requests; this reproducer exposes the remaining multi-peer destination-lifetime gap.

### Reproduction

Configs:

- Qwen3-32B BF16, P TP2 on node 0, D TP1 on node 1, Nvidia H20. Nodes are interconnected with 200 Gbps RoCE RDMA (per rail)
- Workload: replay Alibaba bailian [open-source in-production trace](https://github.com/alibaba-edu/qwen-bailian-usagetraces-anon) `qwen_coder_blksz_16.jsonl` with [trace-replayer](https://giohub.com/blitz-serving/trace-replayer). Replayed for 1800s

<details>
<summary>Launch commands</summary>

```bash
# P instance
vllm serve /home/models/Qwen3-32B \
    --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 40960 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 16 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --port 8100 --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'

# D instance
vllm serve /home/models/Qwen3-32B \
    --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 40960 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 16 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --port 8200 --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'

# vllm-router
vllm-router --vllm-pd-disaggregation --kv-connector mooncake \
    --prefill "http://$P_IP:8100" 8998 --decode "http://$D_HOST:8200" \
    --intra-node-data-parallel-size 1 --policy round_robin --disable-retries \
    --request-timeout-secs "$REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS" --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
    --prometheus-host 127.0.0.1 --prometheus-port 29000

# trace-replayer
trace-replayer --tokenizer /home/models/Qwen3-32B/tokenizer.json \
    --tokenizer-config /home/models/Qwen3-32B/tokenizer_config.json \
    --api openai --dataset bailian --hash-block-size 16 --dataset-path qwen_coder_blksz_16.jsonl \
    --stream --scale-factor 0.1 --ttft-slo "$REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS" --tpot-slo 0 \
    --threads 16 --num-producer 16 --channel-capacity 1024 \
    --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    --time-in-secs 1800
```

</details>

To trigger and observe the subtle write-after-free bug, we manually simulate P0 failed write and P1 delayed write: P0 reports `err_reqs` through its existing `MooncakeXferResponse` after a successful WRITE with 5% failure rate per request; P1 waits for a randomly sampled 0–500 ms before submitting WRITE (batch delay = maximum selected-request delay). D's failure/reclamation logic and RDMA network configuration are unchanged.

We add tracing hooks for each kv block and analyze the dumped traces offline after experimental runs, matching successful WRITE starts and target addresses to block generations, pool returns, and subsequent owners:

| Requests | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Total; all with actual writes from both P peers | 791 |
| P0 experimental failures | 33 |
| **P1 WRITE started after destination block free** | 21 |
| **Of those, P1 WRITE started after block reallocation** | 20 |

## Solution

Each peer keeps a pending request map sharing the existing `PullReqMeta` (`pull_metas.copy()` shallow copy). Success and failure both consume that peer's entry and decrement `pull_tasks_count`, including success after another peer failed. Report the first failure once; publish receives completion only when the count reaches zero. Partial replies, peer-wide errors, and receive exceptions settle only pending entries.

On `FINISH`, requests still pending for that peer are considered to be failed and are settled, covering expired requests omitted by P (otherwise, P0 expires + P1 successes -> `pull_tasks_count` remains positive and D's KV blocks would never be released -- also a mem-leak bug left in the current implementation).

Bootstrap failures with no peer tasks still complete; empty pulls produce no D completion. The fix is confined to connector bookkeeping. It covers error replies followed by the other peers' results; remote quiescence after a local
socket timeout remains outside its scope.

## Validation

### Unit Tests

All relevant unit tests pass (with two added unit tests related to this bug)

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_error_propagation.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
    vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py
```

</details>

### E2E Result

The E2E run config is the same as in the Reproduction section. With fixed:

| Requests | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total; all with actual writes from both P peers | 791 | 791 |
| P0 experimental failures| 33 | 39 |
| **P1 WRITE started after destination block free** | **21** | **0** |
| **Of those, after block reallocation** | **20** | **0** |

All 39 P0 errors reached D before P1's WRITE ended; 31 arrived before it started. Every failed receive followed **all WRITE ends -> receive completion -> scheduler consumption -> block pool return**. Thus the reproduced write-after-free did not recur.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. All code changes are reviewed by the human (me), and all tests are run by the human

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pre-commit run:** passed all hooks
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Preserve DP replica index for standalone draft models
author: MuonChaser
body:
## Overview

Preserve the target DP replica index when constructing a standalone
`method="draft_model"` model. This prevents separate replicas from sharing
device-bound compiled draft artifacts and fixes a reproduced DP=2 warm-cache
startup failure. Follow-up to #62285 and the standalone analysis on #62062;
the root-cause analysis and suggested restoration were reported by @Siquan-Li.

#62062 currently changes DFlash/DSpark paths; this PR fixes the standalone
`draft_model` loader and does not duplicate those changes.

## Claims

- Restore the replica index after draft config construction and before loading
  the model. General `ParallelConfig` semantics and sibling speculators are
  unchanged.
- Isolate draft compilation/AOT artifacts by replica. Existing loader
  regressions cover zero and nonzero target indices.
- Fix the observed warm-cache `CUDA driver error: invalid argument`; do not
  claim an accuracy improvement or serving speedup.

## Validation

61 targeted CPU cases passed:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py -q
```

The scoped regression without the fix fails for the three nonzero-index cases;
rank-zero controls pass. It is part of the existing Buildkite
`v1-executor-worker` suite. Scoped pre-commit checks passed during
implementation; upstream pre-commit execution is currently gated by
contributor eligibility.

[Raw commands, server logs, evaluation outputs/samples and benchmark outputs/per-request JSON](https://github.com/MuonChaser/vllm/releases/tag/pr-62301-validation-20261019).

The end-to-end validation used the public Apache-2.0 model
[`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B) as both target and
draft, pinned to public revision
`c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`.
The equivalent public-model reproducer is:

```bash
export MODEL_ID=Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
export MODEL_REVISION=c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/vllm-62301/cache/vllm
export TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-62301/cache/inductor
export TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-62301/cache/triton

.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model "$MODEL_ID" \
  --revision "$MODEL_REVISION" \
  --served-model-name probe \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 18986 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-backend mp \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.15 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --seed 256 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$MODEL_ID\",\"revision\":\"$MODEL_REVISION\",\"method\":\"draft_model\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

Start once with fresh cache directories, stop after startup/serving, then run
the identical command again without deleting the caches. On the pinned main
baseline `494663940b9b44f667c4f61c8c2407ba8e725ceb`, the warm restart fails with
`CUDA driver error: invalid argument`; at PR commit
`b2303c5e49471603cd31c1904352ad7d99164dbd`, cold and warm starts both serve.
The full raw logs retain the original local snapshot path so the executed argv
is not rewritten after the fact; the updated command uses the corresponding
public model revision.

GPU experiment: 2 H100 PCIe 80GB per arm, DP=2/MP, MRV2, BF16, compilation
enabled, CUDA graphs disabled. Both arms start with a fresh shared compilation
cache, then restart without removing it. The failure/fix was reproduced over
two separate cold/warm cycles per arm, with nonzero speculative acceptance on
both replicas. The 16-request smoke outputs, finish reasons and token counts
match across successful arms.

Full GSM8K (`lm_eval` 0.4.13, 5-shot, 1,319 questions, greedy, seed 256):
default-mode accuracy was **41.39% baseline vs 40.71% PR**. Unchanged-baseline
repeats also varied (48/128 vs 46/128; prefix cache not reset). A separate
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` comparison produced identical responses for all 1,319
questions (40.33% each), with compilation still enabled. These controls do not
rule out a default-mode regression; all raw results are retained.

Three sequential `vllm bench serve` runs per arm used 128 prompts, input
256/output 128, concurrency 8, 16 warmups and fixed seed 256: **768 measured
requests and zero failures**. Shared GPU load and repeated prefix-cache effects
prevent an isolated-GPU speedup/non-regression claim.

Source is the full Python tree at main baseline
`494663940b9b44f667c4f61c8c2407ba8e725ceb` and PR
`b2303c5e49471603cd31c1904352ad7d99164dbd`, using official nightly
native/build-supplied files from parent
`3c13653738dad0acd877c23373816fefffbdd373` (PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Python
3.12.13). Native-source files do not change between the wheel parent and
baseline; CUDA kernels were not rebuilt. This is not a claim about the latest
moving main. Both arms disable the unavailable optional FlashInfer
sampler/toolchain. Same-model serving/cache validation does not establish
different-draft quality or broader model coverage.

## Details

Independent dense DP stores replica identity in `data_parallel_index` while its
distributed DP rank is reset to zero. Constructing the draft config with
`replace` reconstructs the parallel config and resets the index. Restoring the
target index before `get_model` gives distinct `rank_0_0`/`rank_0_1` draft
caches. No steady-state inference operation or synchronization is added.

AI assistance was used for implementation and to execute/document these
validations. The detailed results were collected by the agent and do not
represent independent human-run H100 validation.

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Read only a group's own regions in hybrid SSM transfers
author: NickLucche
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

In the NIXL hybrid (attention + SSM) descriptor path, every attention group read **all** registered regions. When some regions hold only another group's layers, every attention block re-reads those bytes, which that group's own descriptors already transfer. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made ~38% of the wire bytes duplicates.

`register_kv_caches` now records which transfer groups have layers in each region. `_compute_desc_ids` addresses only a group's own regions, for both attention and SSM groups. This generalizes the existing `CircularBufferSpec` special case (`_scratch_region_indices`, removed). The wire format is unchanged. See the example at the bottom.

## Results

P TP2 → D TP2 on separate GB300 nodes, pull mode, fp8 KV, scrambled KV pool, 2 runs per point.

| Model | ISL | Bytes / req (before → after) | Descs | Xfer avg | GSM8K via P/D (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 32k | 859,615,744 → 565,391,872 (−34%) | 950 → 646 | ~8.4 → ~5.2 ms | |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 100k | 2,177,711,104 → 1,348,099,072 (−38%) | 2150 → 1306 | ~20.5 → ~12.4 ms | 81.8% → 80.6% (run-to-run 80.8–82.8%) |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B | 32k / 100k | identical | identical | | 40.8% → 41.2% (non-P/D 41.2%) |

- **Byte model:** a byte-level model of the descriptor layout reproduces every pre-fix measurement exactly (9 points). The 283,136 B left above the useful bytes is the tail page aliasing an indexer region and being read at the indexer's block length. That is region identity (base-address keying), which #57662 fixes, so it is out of scope here.
- **Unaffected layouts:** layouts where every group has a layer in every region (pure attention, non-SSM models through the fast path, Qwen3.5/Nemotron-style hybrids) produce the same descriptor ids as before.

## Tests

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py
# PR (f1a5bab606):   557 passed, 4 failed, 113 errors
# main (be03d19750): 555 passed, 4 failed, 113 errors   <- identical failing set
```

- **Same failures on main:** the failing tests are exactly the same on unpatched main. They are test-environment issues: the `test_nixl_connector.py` fixtures error at setup with a venv prebuilt from an older commit, HF is offline, and the FlashMLA module is missing. None of them touch region selection.
- **New:** `test_mla_hybrid_groups_read_only_their_own_regions[False/True]`. `[True]` adds a KDA-only tensor and fails without the `base_worker.py` change. `[False]` (every group in every region) passes before and after.
- **Existing tests:** `_scratch_region_indices` assertions now check `_group_region_indices[<scratch group>]`, with the same values.
- `pre-commit` passes.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Remote descriptor ids use the local group→region map.** This adds no new assumption. The hybrid path already builds remote ids from local `_ssm_region_indices`, `_ple_group_index` and `_scratch_region_indices`, and the handshake asserts identical per-region block lengths for hybrid MLA+SSM. If P and D group layers differently, per-group `block_ids` would already disagree.
- **SSM descriptor layout:** each SSM layer owns `ssm_regions_per_layer` consecutive descriptors, in `_ssm_region_indices` order. The layout is unchanged; only the subset of slots read changes.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR fixes this. #57662 is complementary: it keys regions by `(base_addr, block_len)`, i.e. what a region *is*, while this PR fixes which groups *own* it. Both touch the same lines in `register_kv_caches`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to develop this change and write this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and e2e validation above.

## Example: what main does at runtime

This is the layout of the new unit test (`kda_only_tensor=True`): one MLA group M and two KDA groups Ka and Kb, where Ka has one extra layer. There are 4 blocks per region, all drawn from one shared pool, so each block id belongs to exactly one group.

**1. `register_kv_caches`** keys regions by base address:

| Region | Tensor | Layers in it | `region_group_ids` |
|---|---|---|---|
| r0 | tensor0 | mla.0, kda_a.0, kda_b.0 | -1 (shared) |
| r1 | tensor1 | mla.1, kda_a.1, kda_b.1 | -1 (shared) |
| r2 | tensor2 | kda_a.2 | 1 (Ka) |

`_ssm_region_indices = [0, 1, 2]`. The hybrid path never consults `region_group_ids`.

**2. Local descriptor list:** one handle holding two views of the same tensors.
- FA descriptors are `d = r*4 + block`, giving d0–d11.
- SSM descriptors are `d = 12 + (slot*4 + k)*4 + block`, giving d12–d59 (4 sub-descriptors per layer).

**3. A request with `block_ids = ([1], [2], [3])`** takes the hybrid path in `_compute_desc_ids`:

| Group | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| M | `arange(num_regions)` → d1, d5, **d9** | d1, d5 |
| Ka | `arange(num_ssm_regions)` → slots r0, r1, r2 | slots r0, r1, r2 |
| Kb | `arange(num_ssm_regions)` → slots r0, r1, **r2** | slots r0, r1 |

- **d9** is tensor2 at block 1. Block 1 belongs to M, but M has no layer in tensor2.
- **Kb's r2 slot** is tensor2 at block 3. Block 3 belongs to Kb, but Kb has no layer in tensor2.

No layer ever writes those pages. Reading them doesn't corrupt anything, but every byte is wasted.

**On GLM-5.3-Flash** (11 DSA, 34 KDA in 4 groups, 11 `KPOOL_TAIL` layers; 40 regions per rank):
- The d9 case is every DSA block re-reading the 8 KDA-only regions (2.2 MB each) and the 10 tail-only regions (2 KB each).
- The Kb case is the two 8-layer KDA groups each reading one empty slot.

At 100k that is 829,612,032 of the 829,895,168 duplicate bytes measured. The remaining 283,136 B are the #57662 aliasing case.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: load checkpoints with quantized q/k/v and a BF16 QSA indexer
author: srkim-business
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62308. Since #59533, `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` lists `indexer.index_qk_proj`. Quant configs read that class-level mapping before the model is built, so they check q/k/v and the QSA indexer as one fused layer. Checkpoints that quantize q/k/v but keep the indexer in BF16 fail to load with `Found different quantization schemes for the shards of ...qkv_proj`.

This PR keeps the indexer out of the mapping that quant configs see, and fuses it into `qkv_proj` only when both resolve to the same quant method.

## Claims

- Checkpoints with quantized q/k/v and a BF16 indexer load again, for example `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ`. Their indexer runs as its own GEMM, as before #59533.
- No change for BF16, ModelOpt FP4, and checkpoints that treat q/k/v and the indexer the same way: the indexer stays fused.
- The `--enable-lora` mapping override is removed. It is no longer needed, and it never reached the quant config.

## Validation

End to end on 4x A100-PCIE-40GB (TP4 + EP) with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image built from `1b2a666` (2026-10-18). Its `model.py` and `qsa.py` match this PR's base `371745e`; for "after", the two files from this PR were mounted over them. A test-only hook (not part of this PR) logged the fusion decision of every QSA layer.

| Checkpoint | Code | Server start | QSA layers (12 per worker, 4 workers) | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ` (q/k/v W4A16, indexer BF16) | before | fails: `ValueError: Found different quantization schemes ... layers.3.self_attn.qkv_proj` | - | - |
| same | after | ok | 48/48 unfused: `QKVParallelLinear` (`CompressedTensorsWNA16`) + BF16 `index_qk_proj` | GSM8K 86.2% (n=500), 0 invalid |
| `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AWQ-INT4` (attention BF16) | before | ok | 48/48 fused (`Qwen4ExpQSAQKVIndexerLinear`) | - |
| same | after | ok | 48/48 fused, same layer and quant method | sample request ok |

Both GPU runs used an earlier revision of the fusion check. The final check makes the same decision for both checkpoints: different quant methods for Swift, the same for cyankiwi.

GSM8K (an API key header was added by a small wrapper):

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8002 --use-chat-completions \
  --model swift-1.5-flash-next-awq --reasoning-effort none --num-shots 0 \
  --num-questions 500 --max-tokens 512 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 32
```

The default 5-shot completions mode does not suit this model family: it emits EOS right after `Answer:` once the prompt is longer than about 400 tokens, on vLLM and on llama.cpp alike.

- Unit test (CPU): `test_qkv_proj_mapping_allows_bf16_indexer` in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py`. With the old mapping, both cases fail with the error from #62308.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passed.
- CI: the test runs in the existing CPU Qwen4 Exp step (`qwen4-exp-unit-tests-cpu`). CI has no Flash-Next checkpoint with this layout (about 165 GB), so the end-to-end load is validated only as above.

## Details

- Root cause: `configure_quant_config` passes the class-level `packed_modules_mapping` to the quant config before `__init__` runs. Even the plain `QKVParallelLinear` built before fusion is resolved as a four-shard layer. The LoRA branch rebinds the mapping on the instance, so the quant config never saw it.
- Change:
  - `packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` is `["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"]` for both model classes.
  - `Qwen4ExpQSAAttention` builds q/k/v and the indexer as before, then fuses only if both resolve to the same quant method type. Without a quant config for the fused layer (BF16, or ModelOpt FP4 via `without_modelopt_fp4`) it fuses as before.
- Limitation: if q/k/v and the indexer are both quantized with the same quant method but a different scheme or parameters (bits or group size), they are still fused, and loading fails at weight loading. I have not seen a checkpoint with this layout.
- I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, the code and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

title: [Quantization] replace_parameter keeps the parameter object by default
author: aoshen02
body:
## Overview

`process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL) often replaces a loaded parameter with a fresh `torch.nn.Parameter`. That drops the parameter's class (`ModelWeightParameter`, ...) and its loader attributes (`weight_loader`, `output_dim`, ...), so weight reload and RL refit have to rebuild them.

This PR makes `replace_parameter` keep the registered object, like SGLang's `copy_or_rebind_param`. It is part 1 of 3:
- #62405 converts the remaining `layer.x = Parameter(...)` sites.
- #62407 keeps deleted and renamed params registered.

## Claims

- **`replace_parameter(layer, name, tensor)` keeps the existing parameter object:**
  - It copies `tensor` in when shape, stride, dtype and device match (`data_ptr` is kept); otherwise it rebinds `.data`.
  - It carries the new tensor's attributes over.
  - It registers a new param only when the name is not registered yet.
- **The `prefer_copy` flag is removed.** The one internal exception is online requantization sources (marked `requantization_source`), which `release_requantization_source_weights` releases by identity, so they still get new params.
- **Kept params keep their checkpoint-layout dim tags** (`input_dim`, `output_dim`, `packed_dim`), because the loader uses them to TP-shard on the next load. `parameter.py` is unchanged.
  - `MPLinearKernel._transform_param` hands each transform a shallow copy of the param: a new object of the same class that shares the data and has its own copy of the attributes. `permute_param_layout_` and Conch's zero-point unpacking retag and rebind that copy, and only its data goes to `replace_parameter`, so the kept param's tags are never touched.
  - The RDNA hybrid W4A16 kernel used to permute registered params directly. It now permutes through `_transform_param` too.
  - Compressed-tensors W8A16 FP8 transposes its weight to (K, N). It no longer retags the param; it sets `layer.processed_weight_dims = (0, 1)`, which Humming's `convert_linear_layer_to_humming_standard` reads.
- **`layer_utils.replace_parameter`** now delegates its re-register fallback to the core helper.
- **Existing callers that the new default affects:**
  - The per-site `prefer_copy=True` is dropped (MLA, Kimi-K3 MLA). Unquantized MoE now keeps the objects on the first load as well, not only on weight updates.
  - FlashInfer MoE-EP: the params must alias the megakernel buffers, which EPLB permutes in place, so it rebinds `.data` explicitly instead of copying.
  - The quantized lm_head copy (`online/lm_head.py`) is never loaded and shares the source storage, so it assigns a new Parameter directly instead of copying into the head.
  - ModelOpt NVFP4 `_nvfp4_*_for_gather` buffers are cloned. A kernel may now write its layout into the params in place, which would change these buffers.
  - The obsolete "plain Parameter for TorchDynamo" comment in `MPLinearKernel` is removed.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes.
- `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py` tests:
  - the single keep behavior;
  - the requantization source;
  - attribute carry-over;
  - a kept param transposed by a kernel transform keeps its checkpoint dims.
- `tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` (new; SM100 only) checks that each loaded param is the same object after PWAL, with its attributes, its loader and its checkpoint dim tags.
  - It has 8 cases that this PR makes pass and that fail on `main`: FP8 block linear/MoE, online MXFP4 linear/MoE, unquantized MoE, ModelOpt MXFP8/NVFP4 MoE, and MXFP4 MoE.
  - #62405 and #62407 add 7 more cases.
  - Both files pass on GB200: 21 passed.
- **End-to-end on GB200.** Arms: `main` (`8e5cae09f1`), this PR (`659cae0a2a`), and the top of the stack (#62407, `d350ae822e`). Each arm is a cold start with `torch.compile` and CUDA graphs, with FlashInfer autotune off. Each run records:
  - the kernels selected;
  - a byte checksum of every tensor after PWAL;
  - 8 greedy prompts;
  - full GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot);
  - a repeat run of the same code, to measure run-to-run noise.

  | Config (Qwen3-30B-A3B unless noted) | GSM8K main / this PR / stack | Post-PWAL tensors |
  |---|---|---|
  | BF16 | 0.886 / 0.890 / 0.890 (repeat 0.886) | identical |
  | FP8 block (DeepGEMM); forced Marlin / Humming | 0.895 / 0.893 / 0.896 | identical |
  | MiniMax-M3 MXFP8, TP4 | 0.859 / 0.859 / 0.859 | identical |
  | ModelOpt NVFP4; forced Marlin / Humming | 0.886 / 0.890 / 0.890 (repeat 0.891) | identical |
  | compressed-tensors NVFP4; forced Marlin / Humming | 0.889 / 0.889 / 0.888 | identical |
  | compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE (CUTLASS) | 0.858 / 0.858 / 0.858 | identical |
  | online MXFP4 / online FP8 | 0.858 ×3 / 0.906, 0.899, 0.896 (repeat 0.902) | identical |
  | requantization: compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE → MXFP4, ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE → FP8, M3 MXFP8 linear → FP8 | within the repeat-run spread | identical |
  | compressed-tensors W4A16 (Marlin; forced Humming) | 0.894 / 0.898 / 0.895 (repeat 0.897) | identical |
  | compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 + FP8 KV cache, Llama-3.1-8B (forced Humming / Marlin) | 0.738 ×3 | identical |

  - The forced Marlin and Humming backends ran on Blackwell through `kernel_config`.
  - In every config, the post-PWAL tensors are byte-identical to `main` and the same kernels are selected.
  - The GSM8K differences are within the spread of repeat runs of the same code. The largest is the M3 requantization run of this PR, −1.8 pt; a repeat of it scores 0.880, the same as a repeat of `main`.
  - Configs that are deterministic run to run (compressed-tensors MXFP4, online MXFP4, W8A8 FP8) give identical GSM8K text in all three arms.
  - A BF16 compiled run that diverged in text was re-checked: a repeat on another node, and an eager run, match `main` (1302 and 1307 of 1319 answers identical, greedy 8/8).
- **Object census:** the share of loader-visible params that are the same object after PWAL.

  | | `main` | this PR | stack |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | BF16 | 80% | 100% | 100% |
  | FP8 block | 34% | 78% | 100% |
  | ModelOpt NVFP4 | 23% | 54% | 100% |
  | W4A16 | 42% | 75% | 100% |

- **Reload.** A bucketed layerwise reload W0 → W1 (BF16, FP8 block, ModelOpt NVFP4, compressed-tensors MXFP4) gives byte-identical results to a cold start on W1 in all three arms.
  - No `data_ptr` moved, and the extra peak memory is the same as on `main`.
  - `test_reload.py` gives 74 passed, 1 failed in all three arms. The same test, `test_kv_scale_reload`, fails on `main`.

## Details

- **Coverage.** A whole-tree enumeration found 1786 statements reachable from PWAL that replace, delete or rename a module param (on `main`). This PR covers:

  | Rows | What |
  |---|---|
  | 282 | Converted: 270 existing `replace_parameter` call sites that now keep the object, plus 12 sites changed here |
  | 7 | Exceptions (below) |
  | 1238 | n/a: creation time, not a loader-visible param, or already keeps the object |

  #62405 covers 141 rows and #62407 covers 109 rows, plus 9 n/a rows that sit inside their hunks.

- **Exceptions** (no object is kept):

  | Site | Why |
  |---|---|
  | `online/requantization.py` release and `online/fp8.py` `del weight_scale` | requantization sources |
  | `online/lm_head.py` | the derived head is never loaded and shares the source storage |
  | `auto_gptq.py` MoE bias placeholders (2) | absent from the checkpoint; dropped so kernels see no bias |
  | `torchao.py` (2) | tensor subclasses cannot be written through `.data` / `copy_` |

- **torch.compile.** Kept `BasevLLMParameter` subclasses are traced through `__torch_function__`, so the Inductor graph split can differ from `main`. The semantics are the same: there were 0 graph breaks, and the logprob differences seen were within Inductor autotune run-to-run noise. `main` already keeps these subclasses for unquantized linear weights.
- **CI.** The new test is skipped on the H200/MI300 CI runners (it needs SM100).

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Finalize the NIXL DCP interleave size before profiling
author: NickLucche
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

NIXL P/D + DCP resolved the KV-cache interleave after profiling, allowing sparse indexers and compiled graphs to consume a stale value. Resolve global cache groups first, finalize interleave once in the engine core, and assign the resolved value on workers before profiling.

Builds on the root-cause analysis and global-group approach in #60671 by @andylolu2, and incorporates @LucasWilkinson's [suggestion](https://github.com/NickLucche/vllm/pull/13). This updates the existing alternative PR; it retains the legacy interleave field and CLI behavior that #60671 removes.

## Claims

- The engine builds global KV-cache groups before profiling and reuses them for final allocation.
- `VllmConfig.finalize_kv_cache_layout` resolves NIXL DCP interleave once in the engine core. `set_kv_cache_layout(layout_name, cp_kv_cache_interleave_size)` sends the resolved values to workers, which only assign them.
- Connector initialization no longer adjusts interleave. Sparse indexers read the shared configuration directly instead of maintaining a separate lazy cache.

## Validation

**Current revision, CPU:** 85 tests passed, including the new core-to-worker startup test with different worker block sizes and an explicit interleave override, plus empty-group handling. All pre-commit hooks passed on the combined changed files, including mypy and test-CI tethering.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/engine/test_kv_cache_group_metadata.py \
  tests/test_config.py::test_pd_dcp_interleave_size_is_adjusted_to_block_size \
  tests/test_config.py::test_kv_offloading_does_not_adjust_dcp_interleave_size \
  tests/test_config.py::test_finalizing_empty_kv_cache_layout_preserves_interleave \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py
```

**GPU serving/model evaluation has not been rerun for the global-group revision.** The results below validate the earlier worker-local revision and are retained as historical evidence. A NIXL + DCP serving rerun is still required for the updated startup flow. The new CPU tests run through the existing V1 Engine CI step; they do not replace GPU validation.

<details>
<summary>Earlier revision: GPU reproducer and model evaluation</summary>

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5next`, MRV2), real weights, 1x GB300 node, TP4 + DCP4, NIXL `kv_both`, GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions:

| Build | Configuration | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main (`e80b6c642f`) | Automatic interleave | Startup fails: compressed indexer requires interleave to be a multiple of 4; profiling still sees 1 |
| main (`e80b6c642f`) | Explicit `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4` | 0.921 |
| Earlier worker-local revision of this PR | Automatic interleave resolved to 4 before profiling | 0.920 |

```bash
VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --decode-context-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --language-model-only \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}'
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

The earlier dummy-weight `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` reproducer (`index_topk`, TP2 + DCP2, NIXL `kv_both`, compilation mode 0 and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs) observed indexer/metadata values of 1/64 during serving on main, versus 64/64 with early finalization. Its tokens/logprobs matched an explicit-interleave workaround. Dummy weights did not measure accuracy impact.

</details>

## Details

Startup order:

1. Load models and update backend block sizes.
2. Resolve the layout and global cache groups in the engine.
3. Finalize interleave once in the engine using the global groups, then send the resolved layout and interleave to workers for assignment before profiling.
4. Profile memory; allocate from the previously computed global groups.
5. Initialize the connector and capture serving graphs.

The existing layout RPC carries the resolved interleave alongside the layout name. The core owns resolution; workers assign the value to their existing `ParallelConfig`, preserving model-held references. Global groups stay in the core for final allocation. No additional RPC or configuration field is introduced.

The temporary KV cache used for CUDA-graph memory profiling still uses the model runners' existing local grouping. The core reuses its global groups for interleave resolution and final allocation; it does not redesign temporary profiling allocation or synchronize separate draft-model config copies.

Out-of-tree `set_kv_cache_layout` overrides must accept the resolved interleave argument. The legacy `dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` field and its current precedence rules are retained.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Don't count content-free chunks as streamed outputs in chat
author: dilberx
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The chat benchmark clients count the opening role-only chunk as a streamed output, so TTFT is measured to a chunk with no output in it and the first real token appends a spurious ITL sample. A check prevented this between #3768 and #12288; this restores it in a form that also handles `reasoning` and `tool_calls`. Original report: #3759.

Benchmark client only. No engine, scheduler or serving code is touched, and no measured figure here reflects a change in how fast vLLM runs.

## Claims

- TTFT for `--backend openai-chat` is measured to the opening `delta: {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}` chunk, which carries no output.
- As a result 208 of 600 requests recorded `len(itl) == output_tokens`, which cannot happen when every interval sits between two tokens; there are at most `output_tokens - 1`. `/v1/completions` on the same server recorded exactly 200 x 255 samples and zero impossible counts.
- Every request on `main` carried a first ITL sample timing the role chunk, median 4 microseconds, so the minimum and low percentiles time metadata arrival. The error runs in the flattering direction: `main` reports chat as slightly faster than it is. With the fix, the minimum and each request's first sample rise to real decode intervals, and vLLM's actual speed is unchanged.
- This does **not** materially change any printed summary metric. Mean and median TTFT, ITL and TPOT all move by less than the run-to-run spread. The fix is to the sample array, which `--save-detailed` writes to JSON.
- 43 lines across the two clients, no new abstraction, no change to `async_request_openai_completions` or `async_request_openai_audio`.

## Validation

Four behaviours added to `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, parametrized over the packaged and legacy clients. 18 tests to 26, all passing. All eight fail against current `main`:

| behaviour | fails on `main` as |
|---|---|
| opening role chunk is not a streamed output | `assert 5 == (5 - 1)` on the interval count |
| mid-stream content-free chunk adds no interval | `assert 4 == (3 - 1)` |
| stream with no streamed output is rejected | `assert not output.success`; `main` marks it successful |
| token rendering as an empty string is counted | `assert len(output.itl) == 2`, got 3, TTFT on the role chunk |

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v
```

`pre-commit run --files` clean on all three files. The test file gains 188 lines and loses 2: two small chunk builders, `_role_chunk` and `_empty_chunk`, the four tests, and the module docstring reworded to describe them. The two removed lines are the old docstring wording. No existing test function is modified and no other test file is touched.

End-to-end on one RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B`, three interleaved blocks per side against a single server, 200 requests each, 600 per side, 256 output tokens, concurrency 64:

```
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B --port 8031 --backend openai-chat \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random --num-prompts 200 \
  --output-len 256 --max-concurrency 64 --save-result --save-detailed
```

Across those 600 requests on `main`:

- all 600 had a first sample under 0.1 ms, timing the arrival of the role chunk, median 0.0040 ms. That is exactly one spurious sample per request and never more than one, and it is what drags the reported minimum ITL down to 0.0025 ms.
- 208 recorded `len(itl) == output_tokens`, more intervals than exist between that many tokens. These are the requests where no two tokens happened to share a read, so nothing offset the extra sample. The other 392 carried it too and landed under the limit.

On this branch, no request records `len(itl) == output_tokens` and none exceeds `output_tokens - 1`. Two of 600 had a first sample under 0.1 ms, both from two tokens arriving in a single read.

Total sample counts are not compared here. They differ between separate runs against a live server because the server coalesces tokens differently each time, so a gap between two runs' totals is not evidence of anything.

`/v1/completions` on the same server, same workload, recorded exactly 51,000 samples for 200 requests of 256 tokens, which is 200 x 255, and no impossible counts.

<details>
<summary>Printed summary metrics, which do not meaningfully change</summary>

Pooled over the three blocks per side, with the spread across `main`'s own three blocks for comparison:

| metric | main | this branch | delta | main's block spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mean TTFT | 463.74 ms | 251.13 ms | -212.61 | 724.23 |
| Median TTFT | 332.08 ms | 232.07 ms | -100.01 | 442.91 |
| P99 TTFT | 2465.88 ms | 423.67 ms | -2042.21 | 2293.71 |
| Mean ITL | 8.99 ms | 6.11 ms | -2.88 | 8.71 |
| Median ITL | 4.81 ms | 4.73 ms | -0.07 | 0.08 |
| P99 ITL | 114.96 ms | 53.65 ms | -61.32 | 71.91 |
| Mean TPOT | 8.94 ms | 5.98 ms | -2.96 | 8.79 |

Every delta is smaller than the spread between `main`'s own blocks, so none of it is a real difference; the pooled TTFT gap is mostly `main`'s first block being a cold start. The role chunk and the first token arrive about 4 microseconds apart, against swings of 85 ms in Mean TTFT between `main`'s two warm blocks alone.

The GPU also drives a display and was not idle during these runs. That is why the comparison is interleaved and why the spread column is included.

</details>

## Details

### Root cause

#3759 reported a chat TTFT of 0.005 s and printed the chunk it had been measured to, a role-only delta with `content: null`. @ywang96 identified the role chunk as the cause and #3768 added:

```python
delta = data["choices"][0]["delta"]
if delta.get("content", None):
```

#12288 restructured the same block to read token counts from the usage chunk. That required tolerating a trailing chunk with `choices: []`, since `data["choices"][0]` raises on it, and the gate became:

```python
if choices := data.get("choices"):
    content = choices[0]["delta"].get("content")
```

`content` is still read but no longer decides anything. The packaged client in `vllm/benchmarks/lib/` has the same shape. #3768's own note explains why nothing caught it: "This does not affect existing CI results since by default vLLM uses completions instead of chat completions for benchmarking."

### Tokens that render as empty strings

#12288 left this note on the completions side:

```python
if choices := data.get("choices"):
    # Note that text could be empty here
    # e.g. for special tokens
    text = choices[0].get("text")
```

That is correct: a token can decode to an empty string under `skip_special_tokens=True`, and dropping it would lose a real interval. #3768's truthiness gate would drop it. So the check here tests whether the chunk carries a token:

```python
if delta.get("content") or delta.get("reasoning") or delta.get("tool_calls") or delta.get("function_call"):
    return True
return delta.get("content") == "" and "role" not in delta
```

The two cases are distinguishable on the wire. An empty-rendering token serialises as `{"content": ""}`. The opening chunk serialises as `{"role": "assistant", "content": ""}`, and `role` is set only there, on the first iteration of `chat_completion_stream_generator`, and on no other `DeltaMessage` in the streaming path. A suppressed or finish chunk serialises as `{}`. A third-party server that repeats `role` on every chunk is unaffected, because a chunk with real content satisfies the first condition.

Three of the four fields, `content`, `reasoning` and `tool_calls`, are what vLLM's own streaming logger checks to decide whether a delta carried anything, in the same file. `function_call` is the fourth and vLLM never emits it; it is there because OpenAI's legacy spec puts it on streaming deltas and these clients are pointed at third-party OpenAI-compatible servers too.

### Tradeoffs and notes

The gate is a named helper with one call site per file, which §3.3 of the PR checklist would normally have inlined. It is kept because the two clients must stay in sync, per #55508, and a shared name makes a divergence between them visible; and because the second condition needs the comment explaining why an empty string counts, which reads badly inline.

Content-free chunks now reach the `elif usage:` branch, which the `if choices:` arm used to swallow. Under `continuous_usage_stats` the opening chunk carries both `choices` and `usage`, so its `completion_tokens: 0` is read and then overwritten by every later chunk. For servers that attach usage to an empty finish chunk with no trailing `choices: []` chunk, the count is now captured where it was dropped before.

`most_recent_timestamp` advances only inside the gated branch, so #55508's `latency - ttft == sum(itl)` guarantee is unchanged. #54708's rejection of tokenless streams is unchanged and now also fires on a stream whose chunks all carry content-free `choices`.

### Relation to #46652

#46652 proposed inserting zero-duration ITL samples so `len(itl)` matched the token count. `docs/benchmarking/cli.md` says ITL records only the gaps between streamed outputs and adds no zero-duration gaps for tokens in the same output, so #46652 is closed. This PR removes a sample with no output on either side of it. Both came out of #27485, which the stale bot closed; the reasoning and tool-parser case reported there is a different cause.

### Duplicate check

Nobody is fixing this. Every reference to #3759, #3768 and #12288 across issues and PRs is a coincidental numeric match; the 190 hits for 12288 are hidden and intermediate sizes. The regression was never re-reported after #12288 merged, so #3759 is still the only issue describing it.

A search by fix shape found nothing either. No PR restores a content gate, and `_choice_has_streamed_output` has no hits. #55508 touched this exact function on 2026-09-13 to make TTFT and latency accounting consistent across endpoints and left the gate ungated. #28183 attempted per-token ITL from continuous usage stats and was closed unmerged without adding a gate.

Open PRs touching either client file are #49720, #51155, #51172, #55719, #57519 and #58734. None modify the chunk gating. My own #46652 is in this area and is being closed.

#59722 is related. It reports the Rust `vllm-bench` chat backend counting token-less streams as successful and notes that Python fails them, which is true for the case tested there: a stream with no `choices` chunks at all, which `first_chunk_received` already rejects. It is not true for a stream whose chunks all carry content-free `choices`, which is the third behaviour above.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share Engram host tables as host-NUMA cuMem across DP ranks
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview

With `dp_shared_memory`, node-local DP ranks share one registered `/dev/shm` mapping for the Engram host tables (2 layers x 94.4 GiB on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Lookups are random row reads and on GB200 they are bound by GPU TLB misses: the registered mapping uses 64K pages.

This PR allocates the shared table as host-NUMA cuMem instead, which the GPU maps with 2M pages. Rank 0 creates it on its GPU's NUMA node and broadcasts FABRIC handles; the other node-local DP ranks import and map them. Where FABRIC handles are unavailable (probed once: create + export), the existing `/dev/shm` path is used and logged.

Allocation never OOMs; it falls back instead:

- Rank 0 allocates in 2 GiB chunks and stops once its NUMA node would drop below a 5% reserve. Freed cuMem pages stay in the driver's page pool (`NVreg_EnableSystemMemoryPools`), which this estimate does not count, so reusing them after a restart is not penalized.
- The driver allocates with `__GFP_RETRY_MAYFAIL | __GFP_THISNODE`: the kernel compacts for 2M pages and fails the allocation rather than invoking the OOM killer. It never falls back to small pages.
- Any create, export, import or map failure on any rank releases everything on every rank, logs a warning, and falls back to `/dev/shm`.

Two `/dev/shm` fixes, since that path is now the fallback:

- **Orphaned tables:** rank 0 used to unlink the backing file only after every peer had registered it, and registration faults in the whole table. A rank killed in that window left a fully populated 94 GiB file in `/dev/shm` that nothing owned. Every rank now opens the file first, rank 0 unlinks it while it is still sparse, and only then do ranks mmap and register.
- **OOM kills:** `check_shm_free_space` only checks tmpfs capacity. A table larger than available host memory was faulted in anyway and the OOM killer made room. `/dev/shm` sharing now also requires the tables to fit in available host memory (cgroup-aware; `get_available_memory`, moved from `weight_utils` to `cpu_resource_utils`), both when sharing is decided and before allocating. The pre-check requires this even where cuMem will be used, so a per-layer fallback always has room.
- **NUMA binding:** under `--numa-bind` (`numactl --membind`), the fallback is most likely exactly when the GPU's node is full, and the membind confined the `/dev/shm` pages to that node, so the OOM killer fired despite free memory on the other node. The mapping now gets `mbind(MPOL_LOCAL)`: local node first, then any node.

Lookups only sort rows when the table has small (64K) pages. Sorting was keyed on "no THP", so cuMem tables were sorted too, which only adds the sort.

Files:

- New NVIDIA-only `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/engram_host_table.py` holds all cuMem code, including the create/broadcast/import protocol (`share_host_table`).
- `common/engram.py` (shared with ROCm): `DPSharedEngramStorage` keeps its interface. On CUDA it tries `share_host_table` first, behind an `is_cuda()` check and a lazy import; ROCm goes straight to `/dev/shm` as before. The `/dev/shm` fixes are platform-neutral and apply to ROCm too. The startup log says `via cuMem` or `via /dev/shm`.
- No new config option.

Not a duplicate: open Engram PRs cover pinned sizing (#59849), SP/PCP sharing (#57195, #61553), Mooncake and disk offload (#57023, #62238); none changes the shared host table backing.

## Performance

### Forward (GB200)

GB200, DEP4, `--numa-bind`-equivalent binding (`numactl` per rank), dummy weights, uniformly random tokens. Same node, back-to-back A/B. Measured before the sort change, i.e. with cuMem lookups still sorted from 1536 tokens.

Engram lookup, one layer, fresh ids every iteration:

| tokens | /dev/shm | cuMem |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 69 us | 49 us |
| 128 | 184 us | 90 us |
| 1024 | 1.21 ms | 0.47 ms |
| 4096 | 3.78 ms | 1.21 ms |
| 32768 | 9.92 ms | 4.36 ms |

`vllm bench forward` (median per-rank forward):

| case | /dev/shm | cuMem | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prefill 32768 | 346.76 ms | 333.93 ms | -3.7% |
| prefill 4 x 8192 | 347.18 ms | 333.65 ms | -3.9% |
| prefill 4 x 8192 @ 16384 ctx | 353.86 ms | 338.71 ms | -4.3% |
| prefill 16384 | 181.99 ms | 170.87 ms | -6.1% |
| prefill 4096 | 56.72 ms | 50.87 ms | -10.3% |
| decode 64 @ 16384 | 16.61 ms | 16.61 ms | 0% |
| decode 128 @ 16384 | 17.10 ms | 17.10 ms | 0% |

Decode lookups already overlap on the side stream. Real text repeats 15-22% of rows, so real prefill gains should be somewhat smaller than the random-token numbers.

```bash
vllm bench forward --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"use_thp":false}' --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe","sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}' --case p32k=32768 --case chunk4=4*8192 --case chunk4mid=4*8192@16384c --case p16k=16384 --case p4k=4096 --case d64=64*1@16384 --case d128=128*1@16384
```

### Row sorting (GB300)

`ParallelEngramEmbedding.lookup` microbenchmark on GB300 with one real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash layer (24 heads x 16M rows x 256, 94.4 GiB), shared by two ranks. Each cell is the median of 20 iterations with fresh uniformly random ids, packed FP8 output, and the sort included in the time. The ratio is sorted time over unsorted time.

| tokens | cuMem unsorted | cuMem sorted | ratio | /dev/shm unsorted | /dev/shm sorted | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 128 | 62 us | 202 us | 3.24 | 141 us | 235 us | 1.67 |
| 512 | 72 us | 217 us | 3.03 | 369 us | 384 us | 1.04 |
| 1024 | 84 us | 250 us | 2.99 | 690 us | 624 us | 0.90 |
| 1536 | 105 us | 265 us | 2.52 | 1021 us | 856 us | 0.84 |
| 2048 | 124 us | 288 us | 2.33 | 1341 us | 1108 us | 0.83 |
| 4096 | 192 us | 352 us | 1.84 | 2636 us | 2161 us | 0.82 |
| 8192 | 330 us | 497 us | 1.51 | 5174 us | 3270 us | 0.63 |
| 16384 | 609 us | 776 us | 1.27 | 10308 us | 4386 us | 0.43 |
| 32768 | 1167 us | 1343 us | 1.15 | 61864 us | 37227 us | 0.60 |

- **cuMem:** sorting only adds its own ~150-175 us at every size.
- **/dev/shm:** sorting pays off from about 1024 tokens, which matches the existing 36864-row (1536-token) threshold, so the threshold is unchanged.
- **This PR:** cuMem lookups now take the unsorted path, and the default thresholds measure the same as forced unsorted.
- **Chunk size:** 1 handle, 48 x 2 GiB and 189 x 512 MiB chunks give the same lookup latency.

## Accuracy

GSM8K on the first revision of this branch (`via cuMem` in the startup log), DEP4 on one GB200 node, same server and lm-eval setup as #61039: `--max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 32768`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs up to 384, `cpu_offload` + `dp_shared_memory` Engram tables, DSpark with 5 speculative tokens, standard rejection sampling, adaptive verification off. lm-eval 0.4.13, 1319 problems, 5-shot, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32.

| | strict match | flexible extract | acceptance length, incl. bonus | per-position acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this PR | 92.65% (±0.72) | 92.57% | 3.451 | 0.795 / 0.651 / 0.458 / 0.333 / 0.214 |
| #61039 (`/dev/shm` tables) | 92.57% | 92.49% | 3.423 | 0.790 / 0.646 / 0.452 / 0.329 / 0.205 |

Sorted and unsorted lookups write the same rows, so the sort change does not affect outputs.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py`: 27 passed (GB300).
  - New `_check_cumem_host_table`: chunked cuMem tables read back across ranks; a reserve failure on rank 0 or an import failure on rank 1 falls back to `/dev/shm` on all ranks.
  - The existing shared-storage lifetime/failure test forces the `/dev/shm` path, so both paths stay covered.
- Full-size stress on GB300 (2 ranks, one 94.4 GiB table):

| scenario | result |
| --- | --- |
| cuMem, 48 chunks | maps in 2.4 s (0.9 s when served from the driver pool), cross-rank readback correct |
| node reserve trips mid-allocation | stops at 66 GiB, releases, falls back to `/dev/shm`, readback correct |
| real `cuMemCreate` OOM (470 GiB table, reserve disabled) | clean fallback to `/dev/shm`, no process OOM-killed |
| another process holds 400 GiB on node 0 | cuMem fails (reserve or OOM), falls back; the holder survives, and a later 10 GiB node-0 allocation succeeds |
| both nodes held, table exceeds `MemAvailable` | before: the OOM killer killed the 430 GiB holder; now: a clean `RuntimeError`, both holders survive |
| SIGKILL during `/dev/shm` registration | before: an orphaned 95 GiB file; now: no file left, Shmem back to baseline |
| SIGKILL both ranks holding a cuMem table | the driver frees it: a 420 GiB node-0 allocation then succeeds and node 0 is back to 464 GiB free |
| two layers under `numactl --membind=0`; node 0 left with 60 GiB after layer 1; layer 2 cuMem fails | before: layer 2's `/dev/shm` pages were confined to node 0 and the OOM killer killed the other process; now: 49 GiB on node 0, 44 GiB on node 1, both layers read back, the other process survives |
| same, with both nodes held (34 GiB available) | layer 2 cuMem hits the reserve at 16 GiB, then a clean `RuntimeError` (94.4 GiB exceeds 34.1 GiB available); no process killed |
| table on node 0, lookups from a GPU on the other Grace | same latency as the local GPU (e.g. 32768 tokens: 1150 us vs 1160 us) |

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.
