title: [Model][Perf] Fuse Beam's TP all-reduce with its sandwich norms and MoE finalize
author: WoosukKwon
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fuse Beam's TP all-reduce with its sandwich norms and, for TRTLLM-Gen NvFP4 MoE layers, the top-k finalize. TP only; replicated-token EP deferral is in #62073, which builds on this PR. Follow-up to #62074 (merged). The kernel is built ahead of time in `csrc/beam/`, with no runtime JIT and no CUDA source in the model folder.

## Claims

- `csrc/beam/allreduce_norm.cu`: MNNVL one-shot/two-shot all-reduce with Beam's FP32 norm-residual-norm epilogue and an optional MoE finalize before the reduction (keeping the local BF16 rounding). Exposed as `torch.ops._C.beam_allreduce_norm`, plus `beam_allreduce` (two-shot all-reduce only) for the large-batch path, which then runs the Triton boundary kernel.
- `csrc/mnnvl_lamport.cuh`: the subset of FlashInfer's MNNVL Lamport device helpers (`trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh`, v0.7.2, the version vLLM pins) that the kernel uses, vendored with its license header.
- Beam defers the TRTLLM-Gen NvFP4 top-k finalize into the fused all-reduce under TP, using the existing `FusedMoEConfig.defer_moe_finalize()`. No shared MoE code changes.
- Same speed as the previous JIT build of this kernel, and 6–16% faster at hidden 8192 from 64 tokens up (microbenchmarks below).

## Validation

**Unit tests** on GB200 (4 GPUs):

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_beam_construction.py tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py
```

178 passed, 3 skipped (8-GPU case; two upstream FlashInfer tile-config skips). This covers the 2- and 4-rank all-reduce and MoE finalize numerics.

**TP8 across two GB200 nodes** (one MNNVL clique): the all-reduce numerics worker from `test_beam_numerics.py` (batch changes, one-shot/two-shot, large-batch path, CUDA-graph replay) passes at hidden 5120 and 8192 when launched with `torchrun --nnodes=2`. The 8-rank MoE-finalize case was not run (its test is single-node).

**FlashInfer version:** these runs used an environment with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 installed. `trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh` is byte-identical in v0.7.2, and the `flashinfer.comm.mnnvl` allocator APIs used here are unchanged (v0.7.2 only adds NVML init/shutdown around a capability probe).

**Build:** `_C_stable_libtorch` built for SM100 with CUDA 13.2; `csrc/beam/allreduce_norm.cu` also compiles for `sm_90a`. Not run on Hopper.

**Kernel microbenchmark**, GB200, BF16, each op captured 20× in a CUDA graph; µs per call, slowest rank. "JIT" is the previous FlashInfer-JIT build of the same kernel, "AOT" is this one. Fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm:

| config | 1 tok | 8 tok | 64 tok | 256 tok | 1024 tok | 4096 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4, hidden 5120 (JIT → AOT) | 5.39 → 5.75* | 5.48 → 5.43 | 8.70 → 8.78 | 11.71 → 11.67 | 34.06 → 33.71 | 138.0 → 139.2 |
| TP4, hidden 8192 | 6.34 → 6.31 | 6.34 → 6.21 | 9.97 → 9.34 | 19.00 → 16.05 | 64.52 → 54.28 | 251.2 → 226.8 |
| TP8, hidden 5120 | 6.53 → 6.48 | 6.42 → 6.39 | 9.00 → 8.97 | 12.89 → 12.88 | 35.52 → 35.53 | 140.3 → 140.4 |
| TP8, hidden 8192 | 7.86 → 7.78 | 7.98 → 7.91 | 10.59 → 9.88 | 19.82 → 16.67 | 68.27 → 57.19 | 265.1 → 225.8 |

TP4 is the median of 3 runs; TP8 is the mean of two runs with the measurement order swapped. \*Whichever kernel is measured first in a process reads about 0.4 µs slow at 1 token; with the order reversed, TP4/5120 at 1 token is 5.79 (JIT) → 5.36 (AOT). The kernel code is unchanged: register usage matches, and at hidden 5120 the AOT kernel on the JIT path's workspace matches the JIT kernel within 0.07 µs. The hidden-8192 gap appears only with the JIT path's own workspace sized for 8192 tokens (it vanishes at 4096); its cause was not isolated.

**Performance:** TODO — end-to-end before/after against #62074 (standard TP all-reduce), TP8 batch-1 decode and 8 × 2K prefill on GB200.

## Details

- **Why vendor FlashInfer's helpers instead of reusing vLLM's MNNVL Lamport kernels:** on GB200, vLLM's Lamport all-gather (`csrc/custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.cuh`) is about 10% slower at TP4 and 25–40% slower at TP8 than FlashInfer's one-shot all-reduce, which does the same communication plus a reduction (TP8, 64 tokens × 5120: 16.7 vs 11.9 µs). Its reduce-scatter + all-gather pair is 1.3–1.8× slower than FlashInfer's single-launch two-shot. A likely cause is that vLLM waits on peer ranks one at a time, while FlashInfer polls them all at once; not verified with a patched kernel. Building on vLLM's primitives would have regressed Beam, so the device code is kept as-is.
- **Workspace:** FlashInfer's `McastGPUBuffer` still maps the multicast memory. The Lamport protocol, its initialization and its generation flags are vLLM's, so the build no longer depends on FlashInfer's headers or installed version. Torch symmetric memory works too, but measured 0.2–0.3 µs slower per call at 1–4 tokens (even from 8 tokens up). Rounding it to the 512 MB multicast granularity didn't help. Beam's GB200 path already requires FlashInfer for its MoE.
- **Build:** compiled only for SM90/SM100 (`VLLM_ENABLE_BEAM_ALLREDUCE`), with `--fmad=false` on that file only, so the FP32 boundary math is not contracted into FMAs. `BeamAllReduceWorkspace.create` returns `None` (standard TP all-reduce) when the op is not built, multicast is unavailable on any rank, or the shape/TP size is unsupported.
- **CI coverage:** `tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py` runs on a CPU agent in Buildkite, so the GPU and multi-GPU cases skip in CI. They were run on GB200 as above.
- **Scope:** an earlier revision also added `defer_moe_finalize(allow_ep=True)` to `FusedMoEConfig` for TP=1, EP>1. It moved to #62073, which extends it to MegaMoE under DP/EP, so this PR leaves the shared MoE config untouched.
- **Not a duplicate:** no other open PR touches Beam's all-reduce.

title: [ROCm][Compile] Fuse AITER static FP8 quant into MLA attention output
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
Fuse MLA attention with AITER's static per-tensor FP8 output quant on ROCm. Closes #62339.

- With AITER on and `fuse_attn_quant` enabled, MLA output quant now fuses into the attention op. On DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8, 27 of 27 layers match (0 before).
- The fused path runs AITER's quant straight into the FP8 output, so it uses the same kernel as the unfused graph. Numerics are unchanged, and performance is neutral.
- No change on CUDA, or on ROCm with AITER off.

Specifically:
- `RocmMLAAttnFp8StaticQuantPattern` mirrors `RocmAttnFp8StaticQuantPattern` from #58099. AITER's per-tensor quant declares `scale` mutable, so the pattern returns it and the replacement passes it through. It is registered only on ROCm with AITER enabled.
- Matching alone made decode 2.4% slower at batch 4 (2.476 vs 2.417 s, ranges not overlapping). The fused MLA path computed bf16 output, then ran `QuantFP8` and a `copy_`, which replaced the graph's single AITER quant kernel. Running AITER's quant directly into the output removes that cost. It is gated on whether `QuantFP8` itself dispatches to AITER, so fused and unfused always use the same quant and clamp.
- This is parity rather than a speedup. On ROCm the MLA decode output is still produced in bf16 by the v_up_proj BMM and quantized afterwards. A real gain needs that BMM to write FP8 directly.
- No open PR covers this: searched for #62339, `MLAAttnQuantFusionPass` and MLA + AITER quant fusion.

Validated on: MI300X, AITER v0.1.25, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, RedHatAI/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8 (static FP8, `ROCM_AITER_MLA`), `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"fuse_attn_quant":true}}'`. "Before" is this branch with the new pattern unregistered.

| | before | after | after / before |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mla_attn_quant_fusion` matches | 0 | 27 | |
| `vllm bench latency` 32 in / 512 out, batch 4 (4 interleaved runs) | 2.454 s [2.426-2.482] | 2.443 s [2.409-2.483] | 0.996 |
| batch 32 | 3.950 s [3.906-3.996] | 3.958 s [3.892-3.966] | 1.002 |
| `vllm bench serve` random 1024/256, conc 4, TPOT p50 (3 runs) | 4.70 ms [4.68-4.75] | 4.59 ms [4.57-4.70] | 0.977 |
| conc 32, TPOT p50 | 7.79 ms [7.75-7.85] | 7.78 ms [7.68-7.82] | 0.999 |
| rate inf, output tok/s | 11724 [11722-11834] | 11791 [11740-11878] | 1.006 |
| gsm8k 5-shot flexible / strict | 0.767 / 0.755 | 0.765 / 0.752 | McNemar p = 0.86 / 0.80 |

Tests:
- `pytest tests/compile/passes/test_mla_attn_quant_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_fusion_attn.py` passes 10/10 (31 passed, 24 skipped).
- `test_mla_attn_quant_fusion.py` passes with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset, `=1` and `=0`.
- The new `test_rocm_aiter_static_quant_mla_attention` fails without the new pattern (`All nodes remain for op vllm::rocm_aiter_per_tensor_quant`).
- `test_fusion_attn.py` fails 12 cases with an explicit `=1`, on `main` as well. This PR does not touch it.

The new test runs on AMD CI in the MI300 compile-passes job, which runs all of `tests/compile/passes`. It skips on NVIDIA.

title: [PCP] Allow decode-only full CUDA graphs for DSv3.2/GLM-5.2/5.3 sparse MLA with DCP=1
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Overview

Allows decode-only full CUDA graphs (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` / `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) under MRV2 PCP with DCP=1 for sparse-MLA models on the DeepSeek-V3.2 attention path (DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2/5.3: `deepseek_v32`, `glm_moe_dsa`). In that mode, decode requests are round-robin sharded across PCP ranks. These models previously had to run with `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, but the pure-decode full-graph path from #53867 already handles them. Other `index_topk` models (DSv4/V4.1, MiniMax-M3, ...) still require `NONE`, because they need model-specific work (see #61555 for DSv4.1).

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 with TP1 × PCP4 + EP captures and replays decode-only full CUDA graphs.
- On GSM8K, that is 2.6× faster than eager, with matching accuracy (0.9083 vs 0.9075).

## Validation

Tested with GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4×B300: `-tp 1 -pcp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`:

| cudagraph_mode | GSM8K accuracy | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| NONE | 0.9075 | 379.5 s | 330 |
| FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 0.9083 | 145.9 s | 859 |

Every rank captured 11 FULL and 19 PIECEWISE graphs.

`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`: passes.

## Details

- Pure FULL mode is still rejected, so prefills under PCP keep running piecewise.
- DeepSeek-V3.2 shares GLM-5.3's attention/indexer code but was not run end-to-end.
- Not validated yet with MTP.

title: [Perf][AuxOutput] Do not rescan referenced keys in the routed-experts store
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Split from #62044 (by @faresobeid): only the store eviction fix.

`BlockObjectStore` kept referenced and unreferenced objects in one LRU, and eviction scanned it from the oldest key, skipping referenced ones. Keys referenced by running requests pile up at the front, so every `put()` that had to evict rescanned all of them on the writer thread. #62044 measured about 9 ms per `put` with 300k keys, and reports that removing this rescan cut the writer thread from 281 s to 2.3 s over 20 RL steps on GLM-4.5-Air, for +15.6% throughput.

The store now follows `BlockPool`'s free block queue: the LRU holds only unreferenced objects.

- `_slots` maps every stored key to its slot.
- A key leaves the LRU when its reference count goes from 0 to 1, and goes back to its tail when the count drops to 0. Within one `put()`, released keys end up after the batch's objects, in release order, as before.
- Eviction takes keys from the front of the LRU. As before, it skips keys stored by the same `put()` unless that call also releases them; they are at the tail by then.

With balanced retains and releases, eviction order, victims and errors are the same as before. Releasing a key that is not referenced raises `KeyError`, as before; keys released earlier in that call go to the tail of the LRU instead of keeping their old position, so later victims can differ. The writer thread stops after that error.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py
```

`test_store_eviction_does_not_rescan_referenced_keys` fills a store with 900 referenced and 100 unreferenced objects, then makes 100 `put()` calls. The referenced keys are a `str` subclass that counts its own hashes, so any dict or set lookup of a referenced key is counted, whatever container the store uses. The test also checks that the 100 unreferenced objects are the ones evicted and that every referenced object stays readable. It does not touch store internals.

## Test Result

- `test_store.py`: 65 passed.
- The new test counts 0 hashes of referenced keys with this change and 180,000 on `main` (limit 900). It also fails on `main` with `_references` or `_lru` renamed.
- Differential fuzz against `main` (not part of the PR), 5,000 random sequences of `put` (duplicate keys, varying payloads, retains, releases) and `get` on stores of 1 to 10 slots:
  - balanced references: stored keys, allocated keys, reference counts and eviction order are identical after every operation;
  - with unreferenced releases: the store invariant holds after every operation; 404 sequences pick different victims after the `KeyError`.
  - Evicting from the wrong end of the LRU differs on the first sequence.

## Benchmark

GLM-4.5-Air, one GB200 node (TP4), `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9` (2,434,064 KV tokens, 167,341 store objects), `max_model_len=20480`, routed experts enabled. Each step is an RL-style rollout: 64 prompts x 8 samples (512 sequences), 1k-16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, seeded per step so every run generates exactly the same 13,448,609 tokens over 3 steps. Both arms use the same 2026-10-16 nightly image and differ only in `store.py`; runs are ordered main, PR, PR, main. The store is set to 1.1x the KV-sized default so that `main` does not hit the full-KV crash fixed by #62044. Writer-thread time is the sum of `BlockObjectStore.put` wall time.

| Run | Step 0 | Step 1 | Step 2 | Throughput | Writer `put` time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 510.5 s | 487.8 s | 425.5 s | 9,446 tok/s | 526.0 s |
| PR | 417.2 s | 415.0 s | 414.4 s | 10,788 tok/s | 4.4 s |
| PR | 417.5 s | 415.1 s | 413.9 s | 10,789 tok/s | 7.3 s |
| main | 420.0 s | 545.5 s | 549.4 s | 8,878 tok/s | 617.7 s |

Throughput is +17.7% (9,162 to 10,788 tok/s on average). On `main`, the step time follows the writer-thread time: about 420 s at 140 s of `put`, about 545 s at 240 s. With `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5` (753,552 KV tokens, about 52k objects) the writer was busy for 17% of each step on `main` and throughput was unchanged (5,868 vs 5,897 tok/s), so the gain needs a store large enough for the rescan to delay the engine.

### Reproduce

Run the script below once with `main` and once with this PR, on one node with 4 GPUs (`max_bytes` is 1.1x the default store size for this model and KV size):

```python
import random
import sys
import time

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

WORDS = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "prime", "integer", "triangle", "sum",
         "product", "remainder", "circle", "radius", "matrix", "vector", "angle"]


def main():
    model, steps = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
    llm = LLM(
        model=model,
        tensor_parallel_size=4,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
        max_model_len=20480,
        enable_return_routed_experts=True,
        aux_output_config={"max_bytes": 985_303_808},
        seed=0,
    )
    for step in range(steps):
        rng = random.Random(1000 + step)
        prompts, params = [], []
        for g in range(64):
            body = " ".join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(rng.randint(150, 900)))
            text = f"Problem {step}-{g}: {body}. Solve it step by step."
            for _ in range(8):
                prompts.append(text)
                params.append(SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, ignore_eos=True,
                                             max_tokens=rng.randint(1024, 16384)))
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        outs = llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
        dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
        gen = sum(len(c.token_ids) for o in outs for c in o.outputs)
        print(f"step {step}: {dt:.1f} s, {gen} tokens, {gen / dt:.0f} tok/s", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```bash
python repro.py zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air 3
```

A single step with this script gave 459.3 s on `main` and 417.7 s with this PR for the same 4,543,356 tokens.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix wrong output of the QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion on ROCM_ATTN
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Purpose

On `ROCM_ATTN`, the QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion (`fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache`) stores V in an interleaved layout, and the layer's attention kernels must read it that way. Two places break that contract, so the fusion produces wrong output on `main`:

1. **Qwen3 models decode garbage** (Qwen3-8B GSM8K 0.87 → 0.005). `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` calls `set_interleaved_v_cache()` on each eligible layer, but with `layer_name` hoisted (`_USE_LAYERNAME`, torch >= 2.11) one layer's patterns cover the model, so the loop `break`s after the first eligible layer and skips the call for every other one. Those layers keep `_use_interleaved_v_cache=False`: the fused kernel then writes the NHD layout into a cache their kernels read as the paged layout. Prefill looks right because it attends over the fused kernel's `k_out`; every decode step after it reads the cache. The existing fusion tests use a single attention layer, so they never reached the second layer.
2. **With `fuse_rope_kvcache` also on, models without QK-norm get a corrupted V cache** (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K 0.766 → 0.71). The pass switches layers to the interleaved V cache before any pattern matches. On a layer the QK-norm pattern does not match, the RoPE + KV-cache fusion writes the KV cache instead, through `RocmAttentionImpl.do_rope_and_kv_cache_update`, whose Triton writer (`rocm_aiter_ops.triton_rope_and_cache`) only stores the regular V layout. A per-layer check at pattern registration cannot keep such layers out, because with `layer_name` hoisted one pattern serves every layer and graphs loaded from the compile cache skip the passes.

Fixing the first alone makes the second hit every layer instead of one (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K 0.012), so both are fixed here, one commit each:

1. `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` switches every eligible layer and only skips the duplicate pattern registration.
2. `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update` applies RoPE in place (`ops.rotary_embedding`) and takes the unfused `do_kv_cache_update`, which already writes the interleaved layout, on layers that use the interleaved V cache. Layers with the regular V cache keep the fused Triton writer.

Only `ROCM_ATTN` is affected; `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` is off by default.

## Test Plan

Single MI300-series GPU (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.11, AITER v0.1.25, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `ROCM_ATTN`, TP1. The change is on `main` @ `6af1e0ae27`; it was exercised on a source build of `main` @ `5be4266f5c` with the touched files replaced (they and the pass manager are unchanged between the two).

- `pytest tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`
- `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0` against `vllm serve <model> -cc.pass_config.fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache=true [-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=true] -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=true`
- Speed: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0.0 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency C --num-prompts max(16, 4*C)`, median TPOT, two rounds per arm in the order PR, base, PR, base.

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** 1497 and 50 passed (24 skipped). Two new cases fail on `main` and pass here:

- `test_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion_interleaves_every_layer` builds three `ROCM_ATTN` layers and checks that all of them switch.
- `test_rope_kvcache_fusion` gains an `interleaved_v` case that compares the fused and unfused caches of an interleaved-V `ROCM_ATTN` layer; its bf16 variants fail on `main`. (With an fp8 cache and `block_size=16` the two V layouts coincide, so those pass either way.)

**Root cause of the first bug, confirmed at runtime** on Qwen3-0.6B (28 layers): on `main`, `set_interleaved_v_cache()` ran for one layer; that layer's fused writes used `use_shuffle_layout=True` and the other 27 layers' used `False`. The fused writer and the unfused interleaved writer produce byte-identical caches, and the decode and prefill kernels read the interleaved layout correctly, so only the flag was missing.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions unless noted):

| Model | Fusions on | `main` | This PR | Fusions off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | QK-norm | 0.005 (200 questions) | 0.871 | 0.879 / 0.873 |
| Qwen3-8B | QK-norm + RoPE | — | 0.876 | 0.879 / 0.873 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | QK-norm + RoPE | 0.718 / 0.706 | 0.757 | 0.766 / 0.763 |

The QK-norm pass replaces all 36 patterns of Qwen3-8B in both arms. With only the first commit, the Llama row drops to 0.012.

**Speed, Qwen3-8B.** QK-norm fusion on with this PR, versus stock `main` without the fusion. On the fusion arm `splitting_ops` is limited to the attention ops and the `rotary_embedding` CustomOp is dispatched, which keeps the request from being dropped without turning on Inductor graph partition; the RoPE + KV-cache fusion is also on there but does not match Qwen3. Mean of two rounds:

| Concurrency | `main` (ms) | With fusion (ms) | TPOT | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.886 | 4.650 | **−4.8%** | +5.2% |
| 8 | 6.552 | 6.275 | **−4.2%** | +4.4% |
| 32 | 8.983 | 8.715 | −3.0% | +2.6% |
| 64 | 11.576 | 11.368 | −1.8% | +2.5% |
| 128 | 17.554 | 17.206 | −2.0% | +4.2% |

GSM8K in that setup: 0.876 / 0.876.

On interleaved-V layers the RoPE + KV-cache fusion now runs as two kernels instead of one. A fused write of the interleaved layout needs the Triton RoPE + cache kernel to support it, which is an AITER change.

---

title: [Quantization] Use replace_parameter for params re-created in process_weights_after_loading
author: aoshen02
body:
**Depends on #62326; review only the last commit.**

## Overview

Part 2 of 3 of keeping the loaded parameter objects through `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL). With #62326, `replace_parameter` keeps the registered object. This PR converts the PWAL sites that still register a fresh `torch.nn.Parameter` over a loaded one to `replace_parameter`.

## Claims

- `layer.x = Parameter(...)`, `setattr(layer, x, Parameter(...))` and no-op rewraps (`Parameter(layer.x.data)`) in PWAL now go through `replace_parameter`, so the loaded object (class, `weight_loader`, dim attributes) survives. This covers:
  - linear kernels: MXFP4, MXFP6, MXFP8, NVFP4 (CUTLASS, FlashInfer, FBGEMM, PyTorch, Humming scales), mixed precision (ExLlama, RDNA3, XPU);
  - compressed-tensors, Quark, INC, FBGEMM FP8, ModelOpt, AutoAWQ and online lm_head methods, and Marlin FP4 helpers;
  - `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm`, CPU AMX MLA, and DeepSeek-V4 CPU attention.
- Coverage (whole-tree enumeration of PWAL-reachable sites on `main`, 1786 rows split across the three PRs): 141 sites converted here, plus 2 n/a rows inside the changed hunks. Deletes and renames in the same functions are left as on `main`; they are in the follow-up PR.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes.
- On GB200, `tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` and `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py` pass: 23 passed. This PR adds the `modelopt-fp8-pb-wo-linear` and `modelopt-mxfp8-linear` cases, which fail on #62326 alone.
- The end-to-end GB200 run is described in #62326. It compares `main`, #62326, and the top of the stack, which includes this PR. The rows that touch this PR's sites are below.

  | Config | GSM8K main / stack | Post-PWAL tensors |
  |---|---|---|
  | MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 (ModelOpt MXFP8 linear), TP4 | 0.859 / 0.859 | identical |
  | compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 per-tensor + FP8 KV cache | 0.738 / 0.738 | identical |
  | same, Humming forced (reads `processed_weight_dims`) | 0.751 / 0.758 | identical |
  | same, Marlin forced | 0.738 / 0.734 | identical |

  - The same kernels are selected in both arms.
  - Every loader-visible param is the same object after PWAL; on `main`, 10% are for W8A8 FP8 and 49% for M3.

## Details

- Compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 and ModelOpt FP8 per-tensor transpose the weight to (K, N). The kept param keeps its checkpoint dim tags, and the layout reaches Humming via `layer.processed_weight_dims` (added in #62326) instead of a retag.
- Where a site re-creates a param whose shape or dtype changes, `replace_parameter` rebinds `.data`; where the layout matches, it copies into the existing storage.
- `modelopt.py`, `quark_nvfp4.py`, `fbgemm_fp8.py`, `inc_wna16_linear.py` and `kernels/linear/nvfp4/humming.py` also delete or rename params. Only their `Parameter(...)` assignments are converted here.

title: [Quantization] Keep deleted and renamed params registered after process_weights_after_loading
author: aoshen02
body:
## Overview

Part 3 of 3 of keeping the loaded parameter objects through `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL). After #62326 and #62405 (both merged), a loaded param can still disappear when PWAL deletes or renames it. This PR keeps those params registered, so after PWAL every loader-visible param is still registered under the same name, as the same object, and keeps its loaded data unless that would cost real memory.

## Claims

- **Renames alias one param under both names.** The new `move_parameter(layer, src, dst)` registers the `src` param object under `dst` as well and records `dst` as its runtime name. The loader writes through the checkpoint name and kernels read the runtime name, both pointing at one storage, so a later `replace_parameter` on either name updates both and no extra memory is used. This covers:
  - compressed-tensors `*_weight_packed` (linear, NVFP4/MXFP4/W4A8 MoE);
  - INC MXFP4;
  - the NVFP4 MoE oracle;
  - Humming NVFP4 and Humming's checkpoint-to-standard renames;
  - compressed-tensors W8A16 block FP8, which now aliases `weight_scale_inv` to `weight_scale`.
- **Loaded params no kernel reads keep their data and are marked retired** (`retire_parameter`). This covers:
  - consumed NVFP4 per-tensor scales (ModelOpt, Quark);
  - small Humming leftovers (at most 1/256 of the largest converted tensor);
  - the input scales of ModelOpt and Quark NVFP4 MoE when a weight-only backend (Marlin, Humming) is selected. These used to be set to `None`, which unregistered them. The method now leaves them registered and passes `None` to the MoE quant config.
- **Large released sources stay registered with empty storage** (`replace_parameter(layer, name, t.new_empty(0))`). Their data was converted into a different-layout kernel tensor, so keeping it would double that memory. This covers:
  - unused zero points, e.g. symmetric GPTQ `qzeros` (Conch, CPU, Marlin, Zentorch via `MPLinearKernel._release_unused_zp`; int8 scaled-mm; Quark int8 linear and MoE);
  - KV-cache scale placeholders (`kv_cache.py`, compressed-tensors KV);
  - released weights (XPU W4A8, wNa8o8, dynamic 4-bit, CPU int8, Triton MXFP4 MoE, INC ARK);
  - Humming leftovers larger than 1/256 of the largest converted tensor.
- **Not changed:** `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm` keeps `main`'s fresh `Parameter(empty(0))` on release, since the released weight can be a tied lm_head shared with `embed_tokens`.
- **Readers see the kernel view.**
  - `kernel_parameters(layer)` returns the live params, each object once under its runtime name. `get_live_param` treats retired or empty params as absent. Humming uses both helpers.
  - The Triton MXFP4 MoE wrapper is stored as a plain `<name>_triton` attribute read via `triton_weight()`, so it no longer takes over the param name.
- **Coverage** (whole-tree enumeration of PWAL-reachable sites on `main`, 1786 rows split across the three PRs): 73 delete/rename sites fixed here, plus 36 sites converted together with them (Humming's delete-then-recreate pattern), plus 7 n/a rows inside the changed hunks.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes.
- On GB200 (rebased on `main`), the tests of every changed file: `tests/quantization/` (all), `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`, `model_loader/test_reload.py`, and the kernel/MoE/LoRA/model tests that import changed modules: 1609 passed.
  - Every remaining failure fails identically on `main` in the same image: Int8 cutlass on SM100, Hopper-only Machete/W4A8, gated repos, DeepGEMM UE8M0 `int32` scales on SM100 (`fp8_block_enabled[auto]`, `fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`), qutlass forward, int4 per-token KV kernel, AutoRound MXFP8 MoE `NotImplementedError`, and `test_kv_scale_reload`.
  - Existing tests that asserted a deleted or renamed param now assert it is still registered (renames alias the runtime name; Humming leaves the large unused checkpoint weights empty).
  - `test_keep_param_objects.py` runs ModelOpt and compressed-tensors NVFP4 linear and MoE with Marlin and Humming forced; `test_utils.py` covers aliasing, retiring, and the runtime name.
- End-to-end on GB200 (before the rebase), `main` vs the stack with this PR. Each run is a cold start with GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot), greedy decoding, a byte digest of every post-PWAL tensor, and an object census of loader-visible params:

  | Config | GSM8K main / stack | Post-PWAL tensors | Loader params registered (main → stack) | Kept with empty storage |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ModelOpt NVFP4 (Qwen3-30B-A3B) | 0.8878 / 0.8886 | identical | 69% → 100% | 0 |
  | ... forced Marlin (3 runs each) | 0.8749, 0.8901, 0.8863 / 0.8779, 0.8893, 0.8855 | identical | 62% → 100% | 0 |
  | ... forced Humming (3 runs each) | 0.8802, 0.8901, 0.8870 / 0.8734, 0.8863, 0.8961 | identical | 69% → 100% | 0 |
  | compressed-tensors NVFP4, forced Humming | 0.8931 / 0.8946 | identical | 36% → 100% | 0 |
  | compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE (CUTLASS, `*_weight_packed` → `*_weight`) | 0.8582 / 0.8582 (1314/1319 identical text) | identical | 46% → 100% | 0 |

  - Marlin and Humming are not run-to-run deterministic. Two `main` runs agree on about 390 of 1319 GSM8K outputs, so their rows show three runs per arm.
  - The extra tensors in the stack are aliases, with no extra memory, or kept scalars and per-tensor scales. Kept data adds at most 0.15 MiB per model (under 0.001%).
- Direct load of W1 into the live params (`model.load_weights`, no PWAL): every checkpoint name now resolves.
  - On `main`, ModelOpt NVFP4 with Marlin or Humming fails with `has no parameter 'w2_input_scale'`, and compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE fails with `has no parameter 'w2_weight_packed'`.
  - With this stack, compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE loads all 675 tensors with no param moved. ModelOpt NVFP4 then stops at a shape mismatch, because Marlin/Humming repack to a different layout.
  - Direct load is only exact for layout-preserving PWAL, as on `main`; layerwise reload is the supported path.
- Layerwise reload W0 → W1:
  - ModelOpt NVFP4: all tensors are byte-identical to a cold start on W1, and greedy matches `main` 8/8.
  - compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE: all tensors are byte-identical to a cold start on W1, and greedy matches 8/8.
- Earlier runs of the stack (#62326) gave `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`: 74 passed, 1 failed (`test_kv_scale_reload`), the same as on `main`.

## Details

- **Reload:** layerwise reload restores checkpoint-format params before loading. It goes through `layer._parameters`, so both alias names are restored, and a param kept empty is never handed to a `weight_loader`.
- **Humming:** used to delete every param and re-create the set it needs. It now writes through `replace_parameter`. Leftovers are skipped if they alias a replaced param, retired if small, and emptied if large.
- **Weight-only NVFP4 MoE input scales:** Humming's MoE quant config reads the input scales from the layer, so they are retired rather than left live. A live loaded scale would switch Humming to the static checkpoint scale, while `main` uses none.
- **Known limitation:** an aliased param appears under both names in `state_dict()`, so the UVA offloader and elastic-EP scale-up copy it twice (no data change).
- **Not kept (exceptions, listed in #62326):** the online FP8 requantization-source `weight_scale`, AutoGPTQ placeholder MoE biases, and torchao tensor subclasses.

## Update: loaded storage is never shrunk, emptied or split (0dcd74c070..682db58ae5)

A loader-visible param now keeps the checkpoint bytes it had at `create_weights` after PWAL. Its storage is never emptied. When two names refer to the same bytes, they are registered as one Parameter object. This supersedes the "kept with empty storage" item above for every site that has a plain tensor to back.

- **Shrink.** `replace_parameter` copies a smaller result into a prefix view of the param's own storage instead of rebinding it to a new, smaller allocation. Results of equal or larger size are still rebound. Online quantization (`uses_meta_device`) still frees its bf16 source. This covers:
  - ModelOpt/Quark NVFP4 MoE `w13_weight_scale_2` / `w13_input_scale` (`[E,2]` → `[E]`);
  - merged per-tensor scales (`[3]` → `[1]` or scalar: Humming NVFP4 `weight_scale_2`, CT NVFP4 `weight_global_scale` / `input_global_scale`, FP8 `input_scale.max()`);
  - the CUTLASS W4A8 FP8 scales and the CPU AWQ repack, which now go through `replace_parameter`.
- **Triton MXFP4 MoE.** The weights and scales are no longer emptied. Each param holds the swizzled storage, and its `triton_kernels` tensor points at it, so no second copy is kept.
- **Humming.** A converted tensor under a new name is registered as the leftover loaded param it came from (`move_parameter`). This applies when the tensor lives in that param's storage or replaces a large leftover; other leftovers are retired with their data.
  - This removes the second Parameter object that block-FP8 MoE `w13/w2_weight_scale` and NVFP4 `input_scale_2` had over `*_weight_scale_inv` / `input_global_scale`.
  - It also removes the emptied CT WNA16 `*_weight_packed`.
- **No more emptied loaded params.**
  - Unused zero points (Marlin, Conch, CPU, Zentorch), dynamic 4-bit scales and INC ARK qzeros/scales are retired with their data.
  - Zentorch, the DeepSeek-V4 CPU `wo_a` pack, CT W4A8 int8 MoE and CT WNA8O8 put the repacked tensor into the loaded param's storage. The K3 gfx942 MXFP4 repack no longer empties its source.
- **Not changed (reported):** sites whose kernel copy is opaque or split across several tensors still release the loaded weight. Keeping it would double weight memory:
  - CPU oneDNN int8 (`scaled_mm/cpu.py`) and `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm`;
  - AMX MLA `kv_b_proj`;
  - the SM12x b12x linear/MoE/Q8_0 packs.
- **Coverage:** whole-tree AST call-graph enumeration from every PWAL root (1715 site rows), cross-checked with a `git grep` for release and alias patterns.
  - 1030 rows are not applicable: creation time, or not a loader param.
  - 409 `replace_parameter` rows are covered by the shrink rule.
  - The remaining rows were reviewed by hand. The `.data` rebinds there keep the same or a larger size, except the two converted above.

**Census on GB200** (verify-generic-restore census: C1 = storage ≥ checkpoint bytes, C2 = another param or buffer overlapping the bytes). Before = a693c5e9a2; after = 682db58ae5. 4-layer slices; gpt-oss-20b full.

| config | C1 before → after | C2 before → after |
|---|---|---|
| ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE default / FI-CUTLASS / CuteDSL / vLLM CUTLASS | 8 → 0 each | 0 → 0 |
| ModelOpt NVFP4 Marlin / Humming | 4 / 8 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| CT NVFP4 default / Marlin | 8 → 0 | 12 → 12 (KV-scale buffer views, harmless) |
| CT NVFP4 Humming (new) | – → 0 | – → 12 (same KV-scale views) |
| gpt-oss Triton MXFP4 | 96 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Qwen3-30B block-FP8 Humming | 0 → 0 | 8 → 0 |
| controls: q30-fp8 default/Marlin, gpt-oss default | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

In every config, all loader params are still registered as the same object (`missing=0`), and generation works.

- **Tests (GB200):** `model_executor/test_utils.py`, `quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` (now also asserts storage ≥ loaded bytes and no two param objects on one storage), `test_moe_wna16`, `test_zen_da8w4`, `test_gpt_oss_triton_kernels`, `test_gfx942_int4`, `test_auto_round`, `test_cpu_wna16`, `test_triton_w4a16`, `test_cutlass_w4a16`, `test_reload`, and the MXFP4 / scaled-mm kernel selection tests.
  - 299 passed.
  - 10 failed, and each fails identically on `main`: Hopper-only Machete, AutoRound MXFP8 MoE, and `test_kv_scale_reload`.
  - `pre-commit` passes.
- **Greedy GSM8K, 5-shot completion:**
  - ModelOpt NVFP4 Qwen3-30B-A3B, default backend, 300 questions: this change vs a32836e18b agrees on 245–256/300 outputs, the same as run-to-run (262/300). Accuracy is 0.927 / 0.930 vs 0.923.
  - gpt-oss-20b on Triton MXFP4 (chat, 200 questions): byte-identical to `main` (200/200 vs a `main` repeat), accuracy 0.675.

title: [XPU] Enable kernel/sampler unit tests on Intel XPU
author: pmanczak
body:
## Purpose

Many kernel / sampler / speculator unit tests exercise Triton kernels that are reachable on Intel XPU, but are gated to CUDA only: `torch.cuda.is_available()` module skips, `is_cuda()` / `is_cuda_alike()` skipifs, or hardcoded `"cuda"` devices. On XPU they are skipped or fail with `Torch not compiled with CUDA`, so those kernels have no XPU unit-test coverage even though they run.

This PR enables 27 such test files on XPU. Changes are mechanical and CUDA behaviour is unchanged.

## Changes

27 files under `tests/` (no source changes):

- Gates accept `current_platform.is_cuda_alike() or current_platform.is_xpu()` (inline, the same form already used elsewhere in `tests/`).
- Devices come from `current_platform.device_type` instead of a hardcoded `"cuda"`; `.cuda()` becomes `.to(DEVICE)`.
- Cases that need CUDA-only machinery (CUDAGraph, SM100, CUDA-only extension ops) stay CUDA-only.

Test files that still fail on XPU for unrelated reasons (`test_mrope`, `test_gemma4router`, `test_qkvr_prep`, `test_dflash2`, `test_precopy_mamba_align`, `test_compressor_kv_cache`, ...) are deliberately not part of this PR.

## Method

Each file was run as its own job, one card per job, and the PR versions were compared against the same files at the base commit (`8fa5ae844a`).

- **XPU:** one Arc Pro B60 per file, `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:nightly` with the python tree from `origin/main` (`8fa5ae844a`).
- **CUDA (regression check):** one NVIDIA L40S per file (8 cards in parallel), vLLM CI CUDA image (`0.31.1rc1.dev253`) with the python tree from the base commit overlaid; PR test files vs. base test files.

After these runs the branch was rebased onto `852989f580`; the only conflict was an import in `test_rejection_sampler_utils.py`, and the new `fly` / multiround / adaptive tests that landed on main there now use `DEVICE` too. The rebased branch was not re-run on hardware.

## Results

### XPU (Arc Pro B60): all 27 files green

| test file | result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py` | 507 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_dcp_a2a_pack_mask.py` | 354 passed |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_memcpy_u64_tiled.py` | 120 passed |
| `tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py` | 90 passed, 19 skipped |
| `tests/watermarking/test_gumbel.py` | 27 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py` | 22 passed |

### CUDA (L40S): no regression

Per-file pass / skip counts are identical to base in all 27 files (1007 passed / 95 skipped / 0 failed on both sides).

## Test plan

- All 27 files pass on XPU (Arc Pro B60), see Results.
- Same 27 files give identical results to base on CUDA (L40S): 1007 passed / 95 skipped / 0 failed on both sides.

title: [Perf] Avoid redundant tensor operations during serialization
author: jzakrzew
body:
## Overview
Reduce GIL contention in EngineCore's output thread by avoiding redundant PyTorch operations when exporting contiguous CPU tensors for serialization. This is a follow-up of sorts to #61640, has a similar motivation, and addresses a similar problem, this time in the EngineCore output thread.


## Claims
- Improve embedding throughput on short inputs by **7.5% at concurrency 128** and **2.6% at concurrency 64** on the GH200 workload below, with no request errors.
- Reduce contiguous CPU FP32 export latency from **4.61 µs to 1.10 µs** and GIL releases from **7 to 1** per call.
- Reuse `TORCH_DTYPE_TO_NUMPY_DTYPE` to export NumPy-native dtypes directly and view other dtypes as uint8, avoiding exception overhead for BF16, FP8 and packed FP4.



## Validation

Existing serialization, buffer-lifetime, and prompt-embedding hashing tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/utils_/test_serial_utils.py \
  tests/v1/test_serial_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  -k 'serial or prompt_embeds' -q
```


**Review-fix validation:** 84 passed, 88 deselected with the command above. Coverage includes exact dtype, shape and byte round trips for 19 tensor dtypes as scalars and matrices. All pre-commit hooks passed.

A local CPU comparison against commit `22b25cb319` (2048 elements, minimum of 5 repeats of 5000 calls) reduced export time for `float8_e4m3fnuz`, `float8_e5m2fnuz`, `float8_e8m0fnu` and `float4_e2m1fn_x2` from 14.6–14.9 µs to 2.24–2.26 µs. FP32/BF16 timings were effectively unchanged. Exception tracing confirmed these FP8/FP4 formats export without entering the exception path. The GH200 serving measurements below predate this review fix and have not been rerun.

**End-to-end performance**: `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16` (`--quantization fp8_per_tensor`,
  `--api-server-count 16`), `/v1/embeddings`, ViDoRe v3 finance-en queries (~30 tokens each),
  closed-loop client on the other NUMA node, 1× GH200, `orjson` in use. Mean of 3 × 30 s runs.

  | Concurrency | Metric | main | this PR | Change |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 64 | Throughput (req/s) | 4,482 | 4,600 | **+2.6%** |
  | 64 | p50 latency (ms) | 14.26 | 13.87 | −2.7% |
  | 64 | p99 latency (ms) | 14.97 | 15.04 | +0.5% |
  | 128 | Throughput (req/s) | 6,601 | 7,093 | **+7.5%** |
  | 128 | p50 latency (ms) | 19.37 | 18.04 | −6.9% |
  | 128 | p99 latency (ms) | 20.72 | 18.85 | −9.0% |

  **Per call** (`tensor_data()` on a contiguous 2048-element CPU tensor):

  | dtype | main | this PR | Speedup | GIL releases (main → PR) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | float32 | 4.61 µs | 1.10 µs | 4.2× | 7 → 1 |
  | float16 | 4.44 µs | 1.10 µs | 4.1× | — |
  | bfloat16 | 4.78 µs | 3.83 µs | 1.25× | 7 → 3 |
  | float8_e4m3fn | 4.53 µs | 3.84 µs | 1.18× | — |
## Details
The original chain releases and reacquires the GIL repeatedly even when the tensor is already contiguous and on CPU. This overhead adds contention when the output thread serializes many small tensors during concurrent serving.

The fast path exports a NumPy-backed byte memoryview directly. Membership in the existing `TORCH_DTYPE_TO_NUMPY_DTYPE` mapping identifies NumPy-native dtypes; other dtypes are viewed as uint8 before export. The mapping includes native real floating-point, integer and boolean dtypes. This preserves raw bytes without another dtype registry or unnecessary `.view()` calls for the listed native types. Noncontiguous or non-CPU tensors, and failed exports (including BF16 scalars), use the original conversion chain.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: don't select float4 tail lanes past the row length
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

FIX #62466

`histogram_2048_topk` in `csrc/persistent_topk.cuh` can return indices `>= seq_len`. This happens when the row length is not a multiple of 4 and the top-k threshold lands in the fp16 `-inf` bin. This PR skips lanes past `seq_len` in the collection loop and adds a regression test.

## Claims

- `persistent_topk` no longer returns indices past the row length on the `histogram_2048_topk` path (k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows).
- The out-of-bounds reads of `logits` in the refinement pass are gone.
- Rows with length % 4 == 0 and rows whose threshold is above the `-inf` bin are unchanged. The guard only drops lanes that were never real elements.

## Validation

GPU: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130. `_C_stable_libtorch` rebuilt from this branch; main measured with the precompiled wheel for 3e96f9cf6.

New test, `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_masked_row_tail`. It covers k in {512, 1024, 2048}, length = k + {1, 2, 3, 4}, 0 or 100 finite scores, and in-row fill of `-inf` or `-1e30`:

```text
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k masked_row_tail
main:     36 failed, 12 passed   (every length % 4 != 0 case fails; % 4 == 0 passes)
this PR:  48 passed
```

Sample failure on main: `AssertionError: row 0: indices outside [0, 513): [513, 514, 515]`.

Op-level repro (1 row, k = 512, stride 516, every in-row score `-inf`, padding 0.0):

```text
            main                      this PR
len=513:    [513, 514, 515]           []
len=514:    [514, 515]                []
len=515:    [515]                     []
len=516:    []                        []
```

compute-sanitizer memcheck, one row of length 513 that is also the tensor width, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`:

```text
main:     3 x "Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes" in histogram_2048_topk<512>, kernel aborts
this PR:  ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
```

Full file with this PR: `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` gives 294 passed, 44 skipped (platform-gated cases).

No end-to-end serving repro: no shipped model reaches this path (see Details). CI runs this test file on Blackwell (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause. The last float4 load of a row (`load_float4_predicated`) fills the lanes past `seq_len` with `-inf`. They are binned like real elements. The collection loop gates candidates only on `vec_valid = i < n_vec`. When fewer than k in-row scores are above the `-inf` bin, the threshold is that bin, so the tail lanes become "equal" candidates. Refinement then reads `logits[idx]` for them and can output them.

Fix. Add `in_range = vec_valid && elem_idx < seq_len` and use it for `is_above` and `is_equal`. Tail lanes still count in the histogram, but that does not move the threshold. They only add to the `-inf` bin, the lowest non-NaN bin, so the counts above it are unchanged. And since `seq_len > k`, the in-row elements alone already reach k at the `-inf` bin.

Reachability, and why there is no end-to-end repro. The kernel path needs a decode row with k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows, and the persistent backend. The persistent backend is picked by `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend persistent`, by `auto` on SM12x and pre-SM90 GPUs, or by `auto` when the logits row stride is not divisible by 4. The bug also needs fewer than k in-row scores above the fp16 `-inf` bin. I checked every in-tree caller:

- DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5 style DSA decode (`sparse_attn_indexer`): in-row scores come from `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` and are finite. Prefill uses `top_k_per_row_prefill`, not this kernel.
- Qwen4-exp QSA: scores are sums of ReLU terms, so they are finite and >= 0.
- Step5 rejects the persistent backend.
- DeepSeek V4.1 `apply_candidate_mask` does write `-inf` inside decode rows. But the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config keeps 2048 candidate blocks of 8 tokens (16384 positions) on full-length (`compress_ratio` 1) layers. Every row on this path (<= 8192) is therefore fully covered.

So no shipped model reaches the bug with default or near-default flags. Reaching it needs a config with `candidate_topk_blocks * candidate_block_size < index_topk`, or more than `length - k` scores at or below about -65504. The layer-level script in the issue shows the V4.1 composition (`apply_candidate_mask` then `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")`) with such a candidate set. If the bug were hit, `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index` only drops `tok < 0`, so the result would be wrong KV slots with no error.

`cooperative_topk`, `histogram_256_topk` and the radix path are not affected. I checked lengths 8193 to 70001 with all-`-inf` rows on main and saw no bad indices.

Performance: one extra compare per element in the collection loop. No measurable change expected; not benchmarked.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Release every prefill rank a READ holds
author: tjtanaa
body:
## Overview

Fix three MoRIIO READ-mode bugs: prefill blocks left allocated after a fan-in read, a scrambled equal-TP read between different cache layouts, and a single-node xGMI crash in the flexible MLA mirror. Also add READ cases to the dummy-weight P/D E2E, and fix a port collision in that test. Follow-up to #61726. Split-head and Mamba READ across TP sizes is a separate PR stacked on this one.

## Claims

- **READ fan-in releases every prefill rank that holds the request.** Decode used to release only the rank it read from. With a larger prefill TP size, including the flexible MLA mirror (TP prefill + DP decode), the other prefill ranks kept the request's blocks until the `defer_timeout` reaper freed them: 60 s by default, logged as "Reaped N deferred sends".
- **Equal-TP READ between different cache layouts reads the right bytes.** Whole-block copies scrambled heads and tokens when prefill and decode lay them out differently. Such reads now move heads one by one. Matching layouts keep the same whole-block path.
- **Flexible MLA mirror on xGMI reads the fixed source.** The round-robin over prefill TP ranks spreads RDMA NIC load. On one node over xGMI it picked prefill ranks whose GPU MoRI cannot open a session to from a decode rank that sees one GPU ("MoRI could not open a session ... _tp1"). RDMA keeps the round-robin.

## Validation

- **Unit tests:** new `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_read_tp.py`, 93 tests. Each decode rank runs the real READ path on real cache tensors, and a fake transport executes the posted reads. The tests check that decode ends up byte-exact and that each prefill rank is released exactly as many times as it waits for. They cover:
  - equal TP for every fixture model × 3 cache-layout pairs
  - MLA in every TP pair, and replicated GQA at TP2 ↔ TP4
  - abort and failure releases
  - the RDMA round-robin vs the xGMI fixed source
- **The tests catch the bugs:** releasing only one holder fails 16 tests, and always copying whole blocks fails 12.
- **Full MoRIIO unit suite:** 818 passed. Ruff is clean, and mypy reports no new errors.
- **GPU, MI355X, xGMI:**

| Case (dummy-weight P/D) | Result |
|---|---|
| Equal-TP READ vs direct serve: kimi_linear, qwen3_5_moe, qwen3_dense, qwen3_dense HMA_off, deepseek_v3 HMA_off, gemma3 HMA_off | distance 0.0 on every prompt (ROCm 10; kimi_linear and qwen3_dense also on ROCm 7.2) |
| READ negative control (corrupted prefill KV): kimi_linear, qwen3_dense | detected |
| READ deepseek_v3 MLA, prefill TP1 → decode TP2 and TP2 → TP1 | pass, exact external hits. TP2 → TP1 crashed on main. |

## Details

- **Release accounting:** `get_moriio_read_holder_tp_ranks` lists the prefill ranks holding a decode rank's share. Decode releases all of them on completion, failure and abort, so prefill's existing `get_moriio_expected_ack_count` is met in both directions.
- **READ hit count in the E2E:** a READ decode always computes the last prompt token itself, so it reports `len − 1` external hits per prompt.
- **Port collisions in the E2E:** every TP rank binds the configured MoRIIO handshake and notify port plus its rank offset, and vLLM scans upward from each server's `VLLM_PORT`. The test handed out single ports, so a TP > 1 server's later ranks could land on another server's ports (`ZMQError: Address already in use`). This also affected #61726's heterogeneous WRITE cases. The test now reserves blocks of free ports.

title: [ROCm][Build] Compile paged attention kernels in parallel (7.6x faster attention build)
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

`csrc/rocm/attention.cu` is a single 3.9k-line translation unit whose kernel instantiation is the tail of the ROCm build: ~9 min of a ~10.5 min build, on one core. This inflation was probably especially caused by recent: #42755  (adds `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` as a template parameter to all 12 kernels = interleaved + non-interleaved instantiation (+50%))

This PR splits the instantiations into one translation unit per (dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size) combination so ninja builds them in parallel.

*Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this (searched issues and PRs for `attention.cu` split / translation unit / ROCm compile time / `MAX_JOBS`). The closest open items are #17419 (general "builds are too slow" RFC) and #60906 (reuse the CMake build dir for editable installs); both are orthogonal to removing the single-TU bottleneck.*

## Claims

- Attention kernel compile drops from **547 s on 1 core to 72 s on 12 cores** (7.6×); the full editable install from ~10 min 40 s to ~1 min 35 s.
- `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link drops from ~2 s to 0.26 s (it no longer waits behind one 9-minute object).
- No behavior change: identical template instantiations, identical dispatch order, unchanged `paged_attention` signature and op registration.
- Cost: `_rocm_C.abi3.so` grows 196.3 MB → 219.2 MB (+11.6%) and aggregate CPU work grows ~30%, both traded for the 7.6× wall-clock win.

**How the file got this big.** The instantiation matrix was grown one axis at a time:

| PR | landed | what it added | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| #8310 | 2024-09-13 | initial ROCm custom paged attention | 1,038 lines, 4 kernels; already `{fp16,bf16}` × head `{64,128}` × block `{16,32}` × alibi `{on,off}` |
| #8577 | 2024-09-19 | fp8 KV cache | adds the `KV_DTYPE`/`cache_t` axis (fp8, `kFp8E4M3`) |
| #12348 | 2025-03-04 | "Faster Custom Paged Attention" rewrite | 4 → 6 kernels (`mfma16`, `mfma4`, partition `reduce`), +1,084/−422 |
| #17139 | 2025-05-07 | FP8 output fusion | `if (fp8_out_scale) → OUTT=uint8_t` = ×2 |
| #17004 | 2025-05-21 | RDNA/NAVI support on v1 | duplicates the kernel set for gfx11/gfx12, 6 → 12 `__global__`, ≈×2, +1,880/−171 |
| #22222 | 2025-09-15 | fp8 paged attention update | adds `MFMAType` (`Fp8` vs `F16`) = ×2 on the fp8 path |
| #42755 | 2026-10-15 | Qwen3-30B QK-norm/RoPE/KV-cache fusion | adds `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` to all 12 kernels = +50% |

Cumulative, per architecture: 6 dtype/kv-cache combinations × head (2) × block (2) × fp8-out (2) × alibi (2) × {NAVI, non-NAVI, interleaved} ≈ 288 launcher instantiations → ~860 device kernels in one file. `--offload-arch` values are additionally compiled serially inside that file, so release builds covering `gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950` pay ~3× the per-architecture cost.


## Validation

Compile times on MI350 in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-39983a5e7a5a575a7829f5d5ada50a33d9337ec1` with `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950`; no compiler flags were set by hand, `-O2 -g` comes from the default `RelWithDebInfo` build type:

| Step | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| attention kernel compile (wall) | 547 s on 1 core | 72 s on 12 cores (58–72 s per TU) |
| `attention_dispatch.cu` (now the dispatch TU only) | — | 15 s |
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link | ~2 s | 0.26 s |
| full `MAX_JOBS=64 pip install -vvv -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation` | 10 min 40 s | 1 min 35 s |
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` size | 196.3 MB | 219.2 MB |

Per-edge timings come from `.ninja_log` of a cold build (`CCACHE_DISABLE=1 ninja -j64 _rocm_C`); all 12 attention TUs start within 2 ms of each other and finish 58–72 s later, so the split parallelizes as intended.

Kernel correctness — the positive matrix covers head 64/128 × block 16/32 × fp16/bf16 × kv auto/fp8 × alibi on/off × interleaved-V on/off × GQA 1/4/8, i.e. every one of the 12 instantiation TUs:

```bash
# f16 MFMA path (default)
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention -k num_heads0 -q
# 128 passed, 256 deselected, 414 s

# fp8 MFMA path (*_fp8_fp8 TUs)
VLLM_ROCM_FP8_MFMA_PAGE_ATTN=1 python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention -k "num_heads0 and fp8" -q
# 64 passed, 320 deselected, 206 s

# head-size `default:` branch of the dispatch
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention_unsupported_head_sizes -q
# 7 passed, 1 s
```

No model eval is included: the split does not change kernels, dispatch, or numerics, only how many objects they are compiled into.

**Left for other PRs** (no automated coverage today, unchanged by this PR):
- [ ] Block-size `default:` of `ATTN_LAUNCH` (`Unsupported block size: `): `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` returns `MultipleOf(16)`, so `block_size=64` does reach the op — needs a `test_paged_attention_unsupported_block_sizes` analogue of the head-size test.
- [ ] `*_fp8_fp8` TUs in CI: only run here via `VLLM_ROCM_FP8_MFMA_PAGE_ATTN=1`, and no `.buildkite/` or `.github/` job sets it; parametrizing a subset over `mfma_type in {"f16", "fp8"}` would cover them.
- [ ] `fp8_out_scale` (`OUTT=uint8_t`, doubles the instantiations in every TU): no test references it.
- [ ] `kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3"` alias handled in `attention_dispatch.cu`: untested.
- [ ] Compile-test the NAVI regions with `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx1100;gfx1201"`: the `__HIP__GFX9__`/NAVI `#if` blocks are now evaluated once per file and were only exercised on MI350.

## Details

**Root cause.** A HIP translation unit is compiled by one clang process on one core; there is no clang equivalent of `nvcc --threads`, and additional `--offload-arch` values are also processed serially inside that process. `attention.cu` instantiates 12 kernels across 6 dtype/kv-cache combinations × 2 head sizes × 2 block sizes × alibi on/off × fp16/fp8 output × 2 v-cache layouts × CDNA/NAVI, so the whole tail is one serial 9-minute compile that `MAX_JOBS=64` cannot help with. (The popular "`Linking _moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` is slow" symptom is a ninja progress artifact: the link is 159 ms and the following line is simply not printed until `attention.hip.o` finishes.)

**Why splitting helps, measured.** Compile time is linear in the number of instantiations: restricting head size to 64 (half the instantiations) gives 270 s vs 547 s for the full set. So distributing the instantiations over N TUs gives ~N× wall-clock, minus a fixed cost.

**Why not just drop debug info.** Building the same TU with `-g0` gives 451 s vs 547 s, i.e. `-g` is only ~18% of the cost, and it would change the shipped build type. Splitting removes 475 s while keeping `RelWithDebInfo`.

**Design.** `csrc/rocm/attention_kernels.cuh` (renamed from `attention.cu`) holds the device helpers, all kernel and launcher templates, and the parameter-list macro. Each `csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_<head>_<dtype>_<kv>.cu` is ~4 lines: it includes the header and instantiates one combination via `ATTN_LAUNCH(...)`, exposing a fixed-head-size entry point. `csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu` keeps `is_navi_gpu()` and the dtype/kv-cache dispatch (unchanged order) and forwards to those entry points. The instantiation sets are disjoint, so nothing is compiled twice on purpose. hipify follows quoted includes, so the new header is hipified like any other (`attention_kernels_hip.cuh`) and no build-system special-casing is needed beyond listing the new `.cu` files in `VLLM_ROCM_EXT_SRC`. Renaming `attention.cu` to `attention_kernels.cuh` keeps the 3.9k moved lines recorded as a rename, so `git blame`/`--follow` survive.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- `.so` grows 196.3 → 219.2 MB (+11.6%), and the extra is debug info, not code: `.hip_fatbin` carries the device DWARF, and each TU emits its own copy of it for the headers/types it includes (the split's objects total 207.6 MB vs 169.4 MB, of which `.hip_fatbin` is 188.8 MB with `-g` but 42.2 MB with `-g0`, i.e. the ISA does not duplicate). Building these TUs with `-g1` gives a 96.1 MB `.so` and `-g0` a 74.9 MB one, both well below `main`'s 196.3 MB; that is left out here because it changes shipped debug info for the ROCm kernels, so it belongs in its own PR (there is exactly one out-of-line device helper, `warpReduceMax`, so marking helpers `__forceinline__` recovers nothing).
- Adding a head size, dtype, or kv-cache combination now means adding a TU and a `CMakeLists.txt` entry; the comments in `attention_kernels.cuh` and `CMakeLists.txt` point at this.
- The split is unbalanced: head size 128 TUs take ~70 s vs ~59 s for head size 64. Splitting within head size 128 (e.g. by block size) would lower the 72 s further, but the floor is ~20 s of frontend parsing per TU (measured with `-fsyntax-only`), so gains beyond 12–24 TUs are small unless a precompiled header is added.
- `attention_kernels.cuh` is hipified (`attention_kernels_hip.cuh`) like the ~15 other headers already in the tree (`quant_utils.cuh` → `quant_utils_hip.cuh`, `layernorm_utils.cuh`, …). `hipify_all` is an `add_custom_target` with no output file, so ninja treats it as always dirty and re-runs hipify on every build (~1 s), which regenerates those headers; editing the source header is therefore re-hipified normally and picked up by the next compile.

title: [Perf][KV Connector][Mooncake] Vectorize transfer descriptor build
author: CJJ1008
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`_build_transfer_params` groups the same block ids again for every registered region and builds each descriptor in a Python loop. This PR groups once per KV group and request and computes each region's descriptors with NumPy. The output is unchanged: same values, same order, Python ints.

The branch is rebased on #63142 and keeps its normalization. That PR reduces how many descriptors there are; this one makes building the remaining ones cheap. Related: RFC #63006.

## Claims

Measured against main `41f5146b5`, which includes #63142.

- In a 1P1D serving run, `_build_transfer_params` takes 0.77 ms instead of 12.8 ms on fragmented calls (median). Those calls are about half of all calls under load.
- Mean TTFT drops by 6.5 / 10.8 / 7.9 ms at 3 / 5 / 6 req/s. The paired 95% CIs exclude zero.
- Greedy outputs are identical to main.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (nightly `41f5146b5`, `huggingface-hub==1.31.0` as in CI): `test_mooncake_connector.py` and `test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py` give 140 passed on main and 146 passed with this PR. The 6 new tests cover run boundaries, and fragmented ids that #63142 does not merge. The hybrid test now patches `_contiguous_runs`.

**Equivalence.** I extracted `_build_transfer_params` from main and from this PR and ran both on 2,000 randomized inputs. Inputs covered multiple layers, KV groups, Mamba null blocks, shared packed regions, heterogeneous TP, non-coalescible rows and prefix trimming. Outputs were identical.

**Microbenchmark.** One request through the real method, 64 KiB regions, Xeon 8358P:

| Layers × blocks | Block ids | Descriptors | main | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 28 × 224 | ascending or jointly descending | 28 | 1.93 ms | 0.38 ms |
| 28 × 224 | random | 6,272 | 13.07 ms | 0.80 ms |
| 64 × 500 | random | 32,000 | 74.50 ms | 2.54 ms |

**End to end.**
- Setup: 1P1D on two hosts, A800 + ConnectX-6 200 Gb/s, DeepSeek-MoE-16B BF16, TP=1, block size 16, no prefix caching, `mooncake_connector_proxy.py`.
- Load: open-loop Poisson arrivals of 3,584-token prompts, 80 per rate, with the same seed for every run.
- Runs alternated main / PR / PR / main, and requests were compared pairwise.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `_build_transfer_params`, fragmented calls, median / p90 | 12.83 / 20.08 ms | 0.77 / 1.32 ms |
| `_build_transfer_params`, other calls, median | 2.73 ms | 0.45 ms |
| TTFT Δ, 3 / 5 / 6 req/s (paired mean, 95% CI) | — | −6.5 [−9.9, −3.1] / −10.8 [−15.4, −6.4] / −7.9 [−13.2, −2.5] ms |
| TTFT p50 Δ, single 3,584-token request | — | −11.5 ms |

Block ids under this load stay fragmented after #63142. Only about 1% of requests merge into one run. The median request (224 blocks) has 101 runs per layer, down from 213 without #63142.

## Details

- After #63142's normalization, block ids are the same for every region of a KV group. So `_contiguous_runs` computes the runs once per `(group_index, shared_group_ids)`, and each region's addresses come from one NumPy expression. Regions are visited in the original order. Heterogeneous TP, replicated KV, shared packed regions and Mamba handling are unchanged. `_contiguous_runs` replaces `group_concurrent_contiguous`.
- #60605 rewrites that same helper. Before #63142, on the same setup, a fragmented call took 2.7 ms with #60605 and 0.7 ms with this PR. If this one is preferred, I'm happy to carry over its tests and credit @feidudeqiu.

title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Send routed-experts block hashes only for computed or scheduled blocks
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Split from #62044 (by @faresobeid): only the scheduler-side hash fix. The store eviction fix is #62392.

The scheduler sent a request's block hashes to the worker as soon as they existed. A prompt's hashes all exist before its first chunk runs, so with chunked prefill the worker pinned one store object for every prompt block, including blocks whose KV had not been computed yet. When those objects were still stored from an earlier turn, the extra pins could push the KV-sized store over capacity and make `put()` raise `BlockObjectStoreError` in the writer thread.

`AuxOutputSchedulerConnector` now sends only the hashes of blocks covered by `num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens` (or `num_computed_tokens` for hash-only updates and finished requests). It takes the hash block size from the scheduler to do that.

As a side effect, when a request finishes and its last sampled token completes a block, that block's hash is no longer sent unless a step that computes that token is already in flight: otherwise the token's KV is never computed, so the worker held a reference to a key with no stored object.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector
```

- `test_routed_experts_hashes_follow_scheduled_tokens` runs a 160-token prompt with a 64-token budget and 20 decode steps through the real scheduler, and checks the number of hashes sent after each step against fixed values: 4, 8 and 10 during prefill, then 11 once the decode tokens complete the next block.
- `test_scheduler_connector_sends_only_computed_hashes_off_schedule` (hash-only update, finish) schedules a request's first 4-token block, then lets a settled token complete a second hash block while only 7 tokens are computed. Neither a hash-only update nor the terminal event may send the second hash; the hash-only update sends it once the eighth token is computed.
- `test_worker_does_not_pin_unscheduled_prompt_blocks` drives the scheduler connector and the worker with a 4-object store. A first request stores 4 prompt blocks and finishes. A second request with the same prompt runs its first 4-token chunk next to a request that stores a new block.

## Test Result

- With this change: the new tests pass; `test_scheduler.py` and `tests/distributed/aux_output_connector` pass (288 tests).
- On `main`, with the new constructor argument removed from the tests, all new tests fail:
  - the scheduler sends all 10 prompt hashes at the first step (`[10, 10, ...] != [4, 8, ...]`);
  - after the first block is sent, the hash-only update and the terminal event both send the second hash although only 7 of its 8 tokens are computed;
  - the worker pins all 4 stored prompt blocks, so storing the new block raises `BlockObjectStoreError: auxiliary output store cannot retain the requested batch: limit=4 objects`, the writer-thread failure seen in production.
- Reverting only one of the three bounds to "send every hash" fails only the tests for that path: the scheduled-step bound fails the scheduler and worker tests, and the hash-only and terminal-event bounds each fail their case of `test_scheduler_connector_sends_only_computed_hashes_off_schedule`. The scheduler test cannot see the terminal-event bound, because its request finishes with 179 computed tokens and 11 complete hash blocks either way.

title: [MoE][Model] Gemma 4: skip CUDA-graph padding rows in the routing kernel
author: Blaze-DSP
body:
## Overview

Gemma 4's MoE routing kernel ignores `forward_context.is_padding`, so the rows that pad a decode batch up to a captured CUDA graph size are routed to 8 real experts each and the expert GEMMs do their work for nothing. This passes the padding mask into the Gemma 4 kernel, as #48979 did for the fused top-k kernels, and shares the mask lookup that two routers each defined.

## Claims

- `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, default `vllm serve`, 1x H200 (80 GB cap): **+19% output tok/s at 9 concurrent users, +12% at 17, +6% at 33**; unchanged at 1 user and at CUDA graph sizes (no padding there).
- Real tokens are unchanged: greedy outputs and logprobs are bit-identical to `main` for 9- and 17-request batches.
- No behaviour change for other models: `fused_topk_router` and `fused_topk_bias_router` call the same helper they inlined before.

## Validation

**End to end.** `main@852989f`, 1x H200 NVL with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.5219` (80 GB, as an H100), BF16, default backend (`TRITON_FLASH_ATTN`), V2 model runner. `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-prefix-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 8*users`, 2 runs per arm, alternating `main` / PR in the same session:

| Users | `main` tok/s (run 1 / 2) | PR tok/s (run 1 / 2) | Change | TPOT p50, `main` → PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 189.5 / 190.3 | 189.9 / 190.0 | 0% | 4.98 → 4.95 ms |
| 9 | 840.3 / 841.6 | 1001.7 / 1004.3 | +19.3% | 9.83 → 8.05 ms |
| 17 | 1346.2 / 1338.1 | 1505.0 / 1513.9 | +12.5% | 11.50 → 9.87 ms |
| 33 | 2118.5 / 2128.3 | 2258.7 / 2259.5 | +6.4% | 13.72 → 12.67 ms |

9, 17 and 33 users run as 16-, 24- and 40-row graphs (7, 7 and 7 padding rows).

**Accuracy.** GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot chat, greedy) at 9 concurrent users: `main` 95.9%, PR 96.1%.

**Bit-identity.** Offline `LLM.chat`, greedy, 256 tokens with `ignore_eos`, all requests starting in the same step: 9 requests (16-row graphs) and 17 requests (24-row graphs) give the same token ids and the same logprobs as `main`; `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` on this branch also matches `main`.

**Tests.** `tests/kernels/moe/test_gemma4router.py` adds a padding case: real rows bit-identical to the unmasked call, padding rows id -1 and weight 0. `tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py` patches the renamed helper. `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` serving GSM8K: no syncs flagged (same as `main`). V1 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, 1 run): 823.5 → 989.5 tok/s at 9 users (+20%), 1312.0 → 1477.6 at 17 (+12.6%), GSM8K (300 q) 98.0% on both.

## Details

#46428 introduced `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` as a `torch.where` in the modular kernel, which every router went through. #48979 moved the mask into the fused top-k kernels and removed that step, so routers that do not use those kernels lost it. Gemma 4 routes with its own Triton kernel through `CustomRoutingRouter`; with a 9-request decode batch replayed as a 16-row graph, each of the 7 padding rows selected 8 experts, so the expert GEMMs loaded weights for up to 56 extra (token, expert) pairs per layer.

The kernel now takes an optional `is_padding` tensor (a `HAS_PADDING` constexpr, so the unmasked path compiles as before) and writes id -1 / weight 0 for padding rows, which `moe_align_block_size` already drops. The mask costs nothing extra: it is applied in the kernel's existing stores.

Other users of `CustomRoutingRouter` (Llama 4, Cohere2-MoE, Phi-MoE, InternS1-Pro, the Transformers MoE backend) route with Python functions and have the same gap; a generic mask there would add two small kernels per MoE layer, so it is left for a separate change with its own measurements.

title: [Benchmark] benchmark_moe: read Gemma 4's MoE shape from its text config
author: Blaze-DSP
body:
## Overview

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` crashes before tuning starts, so fused-MoE tile tables cannot be generated for Gemma 4. Same fix as #45789, which the stale bot closed for inactivity without review.

## Claims

- `benchmark_moe.py` tunes and benchmarks Gemma 4 MoE models (`Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`, `Gemma4ForCausalLM`) instead of raising `AttributeError: 'Gemma4TextConfig' object has no attribute 'num_local_experts'`.
- The tables it writes have the shape vLLM loads at runtime (`E=128,N=704` for 26B-A4B).
- A config with no MoE experts (dense Gemma 4 31B/E2B, or any dense model) now stops with `ValueError: <architecture> has no MoE experts in its config; benchmark_moe.py only tunes MoE layers.` instead of a `TypeError` in `ensure_divisibility` or an `AttributeError` on `num_local_experts` (raised in review by @chrikrah).

## Validation

On 1x H200 NVL; the first two rows on `main@852989f`, the tuning run on `main@2534a96`:

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it --tp-size 1 --dtype auto --batch-size 1 16 256` | `AttributeError ... num_local_experts` | runs; kernel time 43.9 / 265.5 / 437.0 us at batch 1 / 16 / 256 |
| same with `--dtype fp8_w8a8` | same error | runs; kernel time 31.5 / 152.2 / 258.0 us |
| `--tune` (fp8_w8a8, 11 batch sizes) | same error | writes `E=128,N=704,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json`; the server logs `Using configuration from ...` for it |

`get_model_params` on real configs (CPU, `transformers` `AutoConfig`), after the dense-config check:

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B | `(128, 8, 704, 2816)` |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, OLMoE-1B-7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Granite 3.1 3B-A800M | unchanged |
| Gemma 4 31B, Gemma 4 E2B, Qwen3-0.6B, SmolLM2-135M (dense) | `ValueError: ... has no MoE experts in its config` |

## Details

Gemma 4 architectures fell through to the Mixtral branch of `get_model_params()`. Gemma 4 keeps its MoE fields on the text config under the same names as DiffusionGemma (`num_experts`, `top_k_experts`, `moe_intermediate_size`), so it joins that branch. `moe_intermediate_size` (704) is the expert width; `intermediate_size` (2112) is the dense MLP's and would produce a table vLLM never loads.

title: [Core][MRV2] Warm up the sampler after CUDA graph capture to stop memory growth under load
author: GodRishUniverse
body:
## Overview

On Model Runner V2, GPU memory keeps growing after startup while load ramps up. The sampler makes an fp32 copy of the `[num_reqs, vocab]` logits on every step. `capture_model()` ends with `empty_cache()`, so serving starts with no cached block of that size, and each new largest batch reserves a slightly bigger block while the smaller ones stay cached.

V1 already avoids this: `compile_or_warm_up_model` runs the sampler once at the largest batch *after* `capture_model()` ("on purpose to prevent memory buffers from being cleared by `torch.accelerator.empty_cache`"). This PR adds the same step for MRV2.

**Depends on #57926.** That PR makes `_dummy_sampler_run` take the fp32 path and counts it in `profile_run`. Without it, the dummy run skips the copy and this warm-up keeps nothing.

## Claims

- Memory no longer grows step by step under load (Qwen3-4B: +1.77 GB in 18 steps to +0.11 GB in 1 step; Gemma-4-31B TP4: +0.24 to +0.003 GB per GPU).
- No KV cache cost on top of #57926.
- No throughput change.

## Validation

**Qwen3-4B, TP1, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`**

| | main | #57926 | #57926 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV cache (tokens) | 106,912 | 105,680 | 105,680 |
| Memory growth under load | +1.78 GB (18 steps) | +1.77 GB (18 steps) | +0.11 GB (1 step) |
| Peak GPU memory under load | 25.72 GB | 25.54 GB | 24.11 GB |
| Output tok/s, c=16 / 64 / 160 / 256 | 608 / 1279 / 1562 / 1519 | 607 / 1277 / 1563 / 1503 | 608 / 1276 / 1561 / 1499 |

**Gemma-4-31B-it, TP4, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --kv-cache-memory 3GB`**

| | #57926 | #57926 + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| KV cache (tokens) | 18,806 | 18,806 |
| Memory growth under load (each GPU) | +0.24 GB (3 steps) | +0.003 GB |
| Output tok/s, c=8 / 32 / 64 / 128 | 133 / 496 / 520 / 536 | 133 / 496 / 521 / 537 |

Setup:
- Hardware and software: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB), ROCm 10.1, torch 2.13, vLLM `8a6c0449b3` with #57926 and this PR.


Run on `main`, #57926 and #57926 + this PR. Requests carry no sampling params, so each model's default top-k/top-p applies.

**Qwen3-4B, 1 GPU**

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --port 8000

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 1280 --max-concurrency 256 --request-rate inf --seed 1256
```

**Gemma-4-31B, 4 GPUs** (fixed KV size so all builds get the same KV cache)

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --kv-cache-memory 3221225472 --port 8000

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model google/gemma-4-31B-it --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 640 --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --seed 1128
```

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fix Kimi-K2.6 int4 MoE prefill regression on Triton 3.8 (gfx950 tuned config)
author: afriedri
body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K2.6 (int4 W4A16, TP8) prefill regressed between v0.29 and v0.31 on MI350/MI355: c32 TTFT went up ~150%. The cause is a Triton 3.7.1 → 3.8.0 codegen regression in `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` for one tile, which the tuned config uses for its `"8192"` entry (every batch from ~6k tokens up): BLOCK 256×256×32, 8 warps, 2 stages, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=32`. On Triton 3.8 that tile is 3–8x slower; the same tile with 1 stage, or with BLOCK_N 128, is fine.

This PR changes that entry to BLOCK_N 128 and `num_stages=1` in the four identical `E=384,N=256,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI35*,dtype=int4_w4a16.json` files. Nothing else changes: only Kimi-K2-family int4 checkpoints at TP8 on MI350/MI355 load these files, and only batches of ~6k+ tokens use this entry.

## Test Result

Kernel (Kimi-K2.6 TP8 shapes, w13 + w2 summed over M=8192 and 16384, Triton 3.8.0):

| `"8192"` entry | µs |
| --- | ---: |
| current (256×256×32, 8 warps, 2 stages) | 44180 |
| 256×256×32, 8 warps, **1 stage** | 7677 |
| 256×**128**×32, 8 warps, 2 stages | 7631 |
| **this PR** (256×128×32, 8 warps, 1 stage) | 6129 |

Serving (change vs. current table):

| conc | TTFT (before → after) | TPOT | E2EL | tok/s |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 118 → 117 ms (−0.9%) | +1.8% | +1.8% | −1.7% |
| 32 | 1981 → 829 ms (−58%) | −1.5% | −5.8% | +6.2% |

c1 doesn't reach the `"8192"` entry; its TPOT difference comes from one restart (20.93 vs 21.92 ms) and is run-to-run noise.
