title: [EPD] Support metadata-only audio-in-video requests
author: gty111
body:
## Overview

Support metadata-only `use_audio_in_video` requests for Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni in the Python EPD frontend/proxy.

## Claims

- Forward video timing and audio lengths without repeating media preprocessing on the consumer.
- Preserve both features' EC hashes and transfer handles; fall back to raw media for the whole request when metadata is incomplete.

## Validation

Original validation before the review fixes, GB200, 1E + 1PD, Model Runner V2: **48/48 functional smoke requests succeeded** across ECExample, Mooncake TCP, and CPU/NIXL with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B` and `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct`.

Covered one/two videos with audio, image + video, and audio disabled, each repeated twice. Audio-enabled requests use `mm_processor_kwargs={"use_audio_in_video": true}`; both instances use `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`.

Review-fix validation:

- GB200, cached Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct weights, MRV2, eager mode, `enable_mm_embeds=True`, no EC connector: **4/4 synthetic embedding requests completed** (one/two images and one/two videos), followed by a successful text request on the same engine. Inputs used BF16 embeddings shaped `(4 * n, 8192)` with `grid_thw=[[1,4,4]] * n`; this checks request completion and item handling, not semantic accuracy. Runtime: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.15.0, existing precompiled extensions.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passes the changed embedding-split path, then stops at the pre-existing `input_ids.cpu()` in Qwen3-Omni's `embed_input_ids`; the successful smoke above ran without that strict check. The full EPD connector matrix was not rerun for this follow-up.

## Details

A video with audio produces two encoder features. Carry both in one `video_embeds` content part with a companion `audio_embeds` payload and shared source UUID, preserving the chat template's single video item and interleaved placeholders.

Review fixes keep precomputed vision embeddings split by `grid_thw` in the shared Omni mixin. For push transfers, proxy-assigned IDs remain per occurrence even when encoder responses aggregate repeated hashes. Encoder response modalities select the audiovisual path; a single video feature uses the existing matching and raw-fallback behavior. Non-push connector-provided transfer handles remain supported.

Related: #52409. Duplicate checks found no equivalent PR; #57275 fixes raw-fallback identity and transfer lifecycle, not audiovisual metadata-only inputs.

title: [Bugfix] Defer MRV2 Triton validation to worker startup
author: jeffreywang88
body:
## Overview

Defer MRV2's Triton availability check from `VllmConfig` construction to worker startup, allowing CPU frontends to build configs for GPU deployments.

## Claims

- CPU prompt-rendering processes can retain the deployment's speculative config without requiring a local Triton driver.
- Actual MRV2 workers still raise `Model Runner V2 requires Triton.` when Triton is unavailable. Feature compatibility checks remain in `VllmConfig`.

## Validation

- Config construction succeeds with Triton imports blocked, including Beam NVFP4 and Qwen3-4B with DFlash2. Prompt rendering and tokenization also succeed.
- MRV2 worker startup still rejects unavailable Triton.
- Both new regression tests and 73 related config/scheduler tests pass.

## Details

This fails when a CPU-only frontend constructs a full engine config for prompt rendering while inference runs on separate GPU nodes. For example, Ray Serve's `KVAwareRouter` starts an `LLMRouter` on each proxy node, including the CPU-only head. A deployment with speculative decoding needs MRV2, but the head has no active Triton driver. With MRV2 selected, config validation raises `Model Runner V2 requires Triton.`, preventing that router from starting and leaving the head's HAProxy on load-only routing.

`HAS_TRITON` reflects local runtime availability. Using it during config construction incorrectly requires the frontend to have the worker's runtime. This change removes the availability-based runner fallback and config-time rejection, and checks Triton in the shared worker constructor instead.

Related PR: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/67174.

Open-PR searches found no equivalent CPU-frontend fix. Related [#50612](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50612) addresses TPU-specific config exemptions; this change moves the runtime requirement to the worker boundary.

title: [CI] Keep a per-PR 2-GPU core of the NIXL PD accuracy sweeps
author: NickLucche
body:
## Overview

#62564 moved the 4-GPU L4 PD-disagg accuracy steps to nightly-only, leaving PRs without NVIDIA-side PD accuracy coverage (the AMD mirrors still run on PRs per #62567). This adds one automatic 2-GPU L4 step that keeps a core set of NIXL PD paths and architectures running on every PR, with prefill and decode sharing GPUs where needed to stay within the 2-GPU budget.

Not a duplicate of #62568, which shards the nightly-only 4-GPU sweeps themselves; this PR restores per-PR coverage at a smaller scale.

## Claims

- A single new automatic step, `(L4) NixlConnector PD accuracy core` (`nixlconnector-pd-accuracy-core-2-gpus`), runs 10 configurations on a 2-GPU L4 pod (~2.5-2.7 GPU-h per PR) covering every model family in the NIXL PD suite that fits a 24 GB L4:

| # | Config | Model | Path / architecture covered | P / D GPUs | Util |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | TP1/TP1 | Qwen3-0.6B | Dense GQA baseline, pull connector | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.6 |
| 2 | P-TP1 / D-TP2 | Qwen3-0.6B | Hetero-TP, decoder TP>1 | 0 / 1,0 shared | 0.35 |
| 3 | P-TP2 / D-TP1 | Qwen3-0.6B | Hetero-TP, prefiller TP>1 | 0,1 / 0 shared | 0.35 |
| 4 | DP-EP (P-TP1, D-DP2) | deepseek-vl2-tiny | MoE expert parallel + DP-attention decode | 0 / 1,0 shared | 0.4 |
| 5 | Push PP2xTP1 | Qwen3-0.6B | NixlPushConnector, PP prefill layer slicing | 0,1 / 0,1 shared | 0.35 |
| 6 | SLEEP_WAKE TP1/TP1 | Qwen3-0.6B | Sleep/wake round-trip before serving | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.6 |
| 7 | TP1/TP1 | deepseek-vl2-tiny | MLA KV transfer | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.8 |
| 8 | TP1/TP1 | granite-4.0-h-tiny | Hybrid SSM Mamba2 conv state (+ small MoE) | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.8 |
| 9 | TP1/TP1 | Qwen3.5-0.8B | Hybrid SSM GDN conv state | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.8 |
| 10 | TP1/TP1 | gemma-4-E2B-it | Sliding-window attention + model-native cross-layer KV sharing (`num_kv_shared_layers: 20`) | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.8 |

- The gemma config was previously unreachable: no CI step ever set `SW_ATTN`, so gemma PD accuracy had no coverage anywhere, including nightly. Sleep/wake previously ran nightly only (inside the 4-GPU step).
- `run_accuracy_test.sh` is unchanged; all engine launch logic is reused. The new sweep script follows the existing `config_sweep_*` pattern.

## Validation

No GPUs were available locally, so validation was static plus the `/ci run` below:

- `pre-commit` hooks pass on the commit (shellcheck with the repo rcfile, Buildkite key check, test tethering).
- Stubbed dry-run of the sweep script executes all 10 configs with the intended env and args (verified by capturing the `run_accuracy_test.sh` invocations).
- GPU-assignment math from `run_accuracy_test.sh` simulated for a 2-GPU pod: shared configs peak at 0.7-0.8 memory fraction per GPU (two engines), dedicated configs at 0.6-0.8. DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny is ~6.5 GB bf16 (3B total / 1B activated), fitting two engines on one 24 GB L4 at 0.4.
- `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` HF config verified to declare `num_kv_shared_layers: 20`, and vLLM consumes that key natively (`add_kv_sharing_layers_to_kv_cache_groups`), so config 10 exercises cross-layer KV sharing without any extra flag.
- First `/ci run nixlconnector-pd-accuracy-core-2-gpus` is the real gate: configs 2-5 (P/D GPU co-location) and 10 (first-ever execution of the gemma PD config) have never run on hardware.

## Details

- Sharing mechanics: `run_accuracy_test.sh` spreads engines modulo the visible GPUs, so on a 2-GPU pod every TP>1 config co-locates prefill and decode ranks. Shared configs cap `--gpu-memory-utilization` at 0.35 (0.4 for vl2-tiny) so two engines fit side by side on 24 GB L4s; Qwen3-0.6B is ~1.2 GB bf16 per TP1 engine.
- Left in the nightly-only 4-GPU sweeps: TP2/TP2, FlashInfer, Mamba1, the wider cross-layer and SW sweeps, MoE DP-EP variants at higher util. Cross-layer layout keeps per-PR coverage via the existing 2-GPU MultiConnector step (normal + BLHNC).
- No AMD mirror on the new step: the MI300/MI355 mirrors of the nightly-only steps are `optional: false` (#62567) and already cover these paths on PRs.
- Known gap left out of scope: the NHD decoder layout (`enable_permute_local_kv`) is not wired to any CI step, nightly included. Worth a separate PR if that path matters.
- Follow-up option: once #62568 lands, this step could enroll in `automatic_shard` to cut wall time across jobs at the same GPU-hour cost.

title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Retain routed experts while a KV cache tier holds their blocks
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Split from #58328, after #62392 and #62489.

The routed-experts store evicts by its own LRU, so a prefix hit can reuse KV whose routed experts are gone, and the worker fails with `BlockObjectStoreError`.

- **Retention:** the scheduler tracks, from KV cache events, which blocks still have routed experts and tells the worker which to retain and release.
- **Hit capping:** a local hit past the retained blocks is dropped. An external hit is trimmed to what the connector can load (new `KVConnectorBase_V1.external_load_alignment`, full attention only), or dropped if it loads only whole hits.
- **Store sizing:** the store starts at the KV cache size and grows with a warning instead of failing.

Not handled: hits before `routed_experts_prompt_start` still need retained outputs, and hybrid Mamba hits ending mid-block are dropped.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_lmcache_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result

All pass. On `main`, the new tests fail: hits past the retained outputs are served, and the store raises `cannot retain the requested batch`.

title: [Feature][HiSparse] Add a platform backend for device operations
author: zhenwenqi2024
body:
## Overview

Add a platform-selected backend so hardware plugins can reuse HiSparse's runtime and connector. CUDA uses the same cache operations and kernels.

Related: #60072. Ascend integration: vllm-project/vllm-ascend#19109.

## Claims

- Add `HiSparseBackend` for cache operations, host registration, IPC handles, resident-row payload handling, capture queries, DMA and statistics dtype.
- Let each platform select its HiSparse backend through a `@classmethod` hook. The base platform returns `None`; CUDA overrides the method in `platforms/cuda.py`.
- Validate cache formats before allocation and prepare device views inside the existing initialization rollback scope.
- Use `torch.Stream`, `torch.Event` and `torch.accelerator` directly for common device operations. Only IPC events need backend-specific creation/import/export. FP8 prefill keeps its existing custom-op call.

Speculative group prefetch is excluded. Follower staging keeps the original `decode_batch` condition. No CUDA performance improvement is claimed.

## Validation

- CPU fixture follow-up for [Buildkite #97663](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97663#01a17e0c-4bb9-473c-a68f-35f5ad9fe991): planning and configuration tests now select the real CUDA HiSparse backend through the platform hook instead of overriding the old CUDA predicates. Unsupported-platform checks use the hook's `None` result. On Linux/aarch64 with PyTorch 2.10 and an explicit CPU target, the command below gave `22 failed, 5 passed` at `5b8e00878206`, then `27 passed` with `bb13de1884ba`. Existing capacity, layout and configuration assertions were retained. This is CPU validation, not CUDA/NPU execution.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py -k hisparse
```

The default Qwen3-0.6B configuration was cached for both runs; no model weights were loaded.

- The platform selector and CUDA override use `@classmethod`, matching other platform backend hooks. Class/instance calls and descriptor inheritance were checked on the actual base class and exact CUDA method source. An independent audit of the exact Ascend override confirmed existing instance calls remain compatible; its matching classmethod override is still needed for class calls. This CPU descriptor check does not qualify device execution or the full Ascend pair.

- Whole-PR follow-up checked the eight changed vLLM modules and all 28 test files mentioning HiSparse, including 43 literal module patch targets. Existing connector tests now patch the accelerator/backend entry points, the row-DMA fixture initializes its backend, and resident-prefill gathering uses a bound runtime. Existing payload and ordering assertions are retained.
- The existing zero-token TP ordering regression reproduced four `AttributeError` failures on the removed patch target before the fix and passed all four parameters afterward. It used exact production/test definitions in an out-of-tree CPU runner. The draft-mirror runner reaches pinned allocation but cannot execute on CPU-only torch; device regressions remain unrun locally.

- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff check/format, mypy, typos, markdownlint-cli2, SPDX, import checks and test tethering. Python syntax and `git diff --check` passed.
- The two checked-in resident-gather cases passed with real CPU tensors and the actual `HiSparseBackend`, checking page stride, reordered/repeated rows and packed-byte payloads. An out-of-tree runner selected the unchanged test function to avoid full worker-module imports; no backend or torch methods were substituted. This is not a full vLLM pytest or device result.
- A real CUDA stream/IPC-event ordering regression was added to the existing attention suite; it is not run locally.
- Standard worker pytest collection was attempted on Windows with faulthandler and terminated with an access violation (exit `-1073741819`). CUDA/NPU model, graph replay, accuracy and performance validation remain pending.
- Hooks for untouched CUDA, workflow, shell, dependency and Rust files were skipped to avoid unrelated tool installation. No unfiltered full-hook run is claimed.

Focused commands for a prepared vLLM environment:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k hisparse
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k hisparse
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  -k 'hisparse_generic_stream or index_group_converts_decode_indices_once or hisparse_fp8_prefill_gather'
```

The existing Buildkite worker and attention suites select these files. Retained additions check real payload values and initialization rollback; mock-only backend routing tests have been removed.

## Details

A plugin overrides `Platform.get_hisparse_backend_cls()` with its backend's qualified class name. Lookup is lazy and cached by class name. HiSparse uses generic torch streams, events, current-stream queries and synchronization. The constructor validates backend availability once. Generic resident gathering has a base implementation; plugins may override packed-payload handling.

The linked Ascend draft must align its resolver workspace ownership and tests with this interface before the pair can merge. Its currently published head still accesses the removed `backend_state` field. Speculative group prefetch is separate work in #63801. Installed PTA 2.10.0.post7 headers provide generic stream/event/device-guard operations, but this source inspection does not establish NPU graph replay or final-pair correctness. Final-head Ascend integration and device validation remain required.

The scheduler, HMA allocation, residency policy, KV formats and attention math keep their existing ownership. The device-view hook runs once after allocation and before binding; per-step metadata and transfers stay outside it. Existing PP/CP/graph restrictions remain. DMA submission retains upstream error handling; this PR adds no exception-drain/quarantine branch or unused backend state.

The open HiSparse PRs checked for overlap, including #57602 and #60358, address ROCm execution/registration and other fixes. This PR provides the platform interface without their kernels or unrelated lifecycle changes.

AI assistance was used for implementation and preparation. Final human review and hardware/model validation remain required before merge.

title: [KV Offload] Emit self-describing events for recurrent state groups
author: luckyq
body:
## Purpose

`OffloadingEventsTracker` emits a `block_size=0` placeholder `BlockStored` for every group that has a load window. `MambaSpec` groups get a one-chunk window because they depend on a single state, not because their hashes are meaningless: the offloaded chunk is the recurrent state checkpoint at the chunk's last hash. External consumers that index offload residency (a KV-aware router with a CPU/KVCR tier) therefore cannot see where a hybrid prefix is reusable and overestimate it from the attention group (vllm-project/vllm#62510).

## Changes

- `events.py`: `describes_group()` returns true for full-attention and `MambaSpec` groups; windowed attention groups keep the placeholder.
- A recurrent chunk (or partial tail) is announced as **one state checkpoint**: `block_hashes` is the chunk's last hash only, `parent_block_hash` is the hash before it, `token_ids` is empty, `kv_cache_spec_kind="mamba"`, `group_idx` and `block_size` as for attention. `BlockRemoved` fans out to that same single hash. Consumers align it by hash with the attention group's blocks; announcing the whole hash range would let them treat every hash in a multi-hash chunk as a resumable position. The payload is also small: no per-chunk `token_ids` copy is retained for recurrent groups.
- Tests: Mamba chunk store/remove, a multi-hash (chunk-mode) chunk announcing only its last hash, and partial tail (store and lookup); windowed groups still skip.
- `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`: one sentence.

## Test plan

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py`: 51 passed in a CPU-only `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` container with this `events.py` dropped in; the 4 tiering-config tests in that file fail there identically without the patch (`VllmConfig` hybrid-KV-manager validation in that environment), so they need the CI environment.
- Qwen3.5-4B, `mamba_cache_mode=align`, `CPUOffloadingSpec` + `self_describing_kv_events`, ZMQ subscriber: before, the three SSM groups publish only `block_size=0` events; after, they publish one `kv_cache_spec_kind=mamba` event per chunk carrying the chunk's last hash, at the same hash as the attention group's chunk (table in the first comment; re-run on the checkpoint-only payload pending).

title: [Perf][Kernel][DSv4.1] Copy-based Q zero-pad for large eager mega-attention steps
author: roborluo
body:
## Overview

  Makes the per-layer Q pad + KV insert of DeepSeek-V4.1 mega-attention layers **1.9-2.15x faster** on eager steps of 2048 tokens or more at TP2, with bit-identical outputs. On layers with 32 live heads padded to 64 (TP2 of a 64-head model), those steps
  now run the fused insert op in its existing KV-only mode and build the zero-padded, chunk-interleaved Q with a contiguous Triton copy, instead of padding Q inside the fused op.
  Part of #57448, on top of FlashMLA mega attention (#56935) and the interleaved V4.1 KV records (#61371); related: #58872, #55654, #60076 (see *Not a duplicate*).

  ## Claims

  - **1.9-2.15x faster Q pad + KV insert per layer** on eager steps of 2048-16384 tokens (2.10x at 8192 tokens; table below). With 32 live heads padded to 64, the Q half of the fused op reads 32 KiB and writes 64 KiB per token, against about 1.8 KiB for
  its KV half, and it writes Q one (token, head) slot per warp, in 16-element pieces `64 * 16` elements apart. The copy writes each token's 32 rows of 1024 elements contiguously.
  - **Bit-identical results:** the padded Q and the sliding-window KV cache bytes equal those of the fused launch (for NaN-free Q), so model outputs do not change.
  - **Narrow, automatic dispatch:** only eager steps with at least 2048 query tokens on mega-attention layers with 32 of 64 padded heads take the new path. Captured CUDA graphs, smaller steps, other shards (TP1/TP4/TP8 of a 64-head model), other attention
  backends and other platforms run exactly as before. There is no new flag, env var or config option.
  - **No new sync or memory:** the per-step decision reads only host metadata, and the padded Q tensor has the shape the op would have allocated itself. A full GSM8K run against a server started with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` detects no host sync.

  ## Validation

  **Kernel time** of the Q pad + KV insert per layer, fused op vs KV-only launch + copy (bf16, 32 live / 64 padded heads, `python bench_q_pad_copy.py` below: each arm replayed as a CUDA graph and timed with CUDA events, median; correctness asserted before
  timing; two runs agree to within 0.1%):

  | Tokens | **Speedup** |
  | ---: | ---: |
  | 512 | 1.61x (below the 2048-token threshold: keeps the fused op) |
  | 1024 | 1.87x (also below the threshold: the copy's extra eager launch eats this; see the 64-16384 sweep in the comments) |
  | 2048 | **1.93x** |
  | 4096 | **2.06x** |
  | 8192 | **2.10x** |
  | 16384 | **2.15x** |

  The shipped copy launch config (`BLOCK_ROWS=4`, 4 warps) is the fastest of the 12 configurations swept at 2048 tokens and tied fastest at 8192.

  <details>
  <summary>bench_q_pad_copy.py</summary>

  ```python
  """Fused Q pad + KV insert vs KV-only insert + _pad_interleaved_q (32 of 64 heads)."""

  import statistics

  import torch
  from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti

  from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention import (
      _pad_interleaved_q,
      _pad_interleaved_q_kernel,
  )
  from vllm.triton_utils import triton

  LIVE, PADDED, D, ROPE, BLOCK, REC = 32, 64, 512, 64, 64, 528
  op = torch.ops._C.fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert
  # After q_head_padded: eps, block_size, then the mega-attention layer's flags
  # apply_q_norm, kv_mxfp8, apply_q_rope and is_q_interleaved.
  TAIL = (1e-6, BLOCK, False, True, False, True)


  def bench_us(fn):
      times = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True)
      return statistics.median(times) * 1e3


  def compare(n):
      q = torch.randn(n, LIVE, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      kv = torch.randn(n, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      pos, slots = torch.arange(n), torch.arange(n)
      cos_sin = torch.randn(n, ROPE)  # values do not affect timing
      cache_a = torch.zeros(n // BLOCK + 1, BLOCK * REC, dtype=torch.uint8)
      cache_b = torch.zeros_like(cache_a)
      out = torch.empty(n, PADDED, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)

      def fused():
          return op(q, kv, cache_a, slots, pos, cos_sin, PADDED, *TAIL)

      def kv_only():
          op(q, kv, cache_b, slots, pos, cos_sin, 0, *TAIL)

      def copy():
          _pad_interleaved_q(q, out)

      # Correctness before timing: same cache bytes and Q bits as the fused launch.
      want = fused()
      kv_only()
      copy()
      assert torch.equal(cache_a, cache_b)
      assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int16), want.view(torch.int16))

      t_fused, t_kv, t_copy = bench_us(fused), bench_us(kv_only), bench_us(copy)
      t_new = bench_us(lambda: (kv_only(), copy()))
      # Every byte read or written once: Q in, padded Q out, KV row, position,
      # slot and cos/sin row in, KV record out.
      nbytes = n * ((LIVE + PADDED) * D * 2 + D * 2 + 16 + ROPE * 4 + REC)
      print(
          f"{n:6d} {t_fused:9.1f} {t_kv:11.1f} {t_copy:8.1f} {t_new:11.1f} "
          f"{t_fused / t_new:7.2f}x {nbytes / t_fused / 1e3:11.0f} "
          f"{nbytes / t_new / 1e3:9.0f}"
      )


  def sweep(n):
      """Time the copy alone per launch config; the PR ships BLOCK_ROWS=4, 4 warps."""
      q = torch.randn(n, LIVE, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      want = torch.empty(n, PADDED, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      _pad_interleaved_q(q, want)
      rows = n * (D // 16)
      for block_rows in (1, 2, 4, 8):
          for num_warps in (2, 4, 8):
              out = torch.empty_like(want)
              run = _pad_interleaved_q_kernel[(triton.cdiv(rows, block_rows),)]
              args = (q, out, rows)
              kwargs = dict(
                  LIVE=LIVE * 16,
                  PAD=(PADDED - LIVE) * 16,
                  BLOCK_ROWS=block_rows,
                  num_warps=num_warps,
              )
              run(*args, **kwargs)
              assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int16), want.view(torch.int16))
              t = bench_us(lambda run=run, args=args, kwargs=kwargs: run(*args, **kwargs))
              print(f"{n:6d} {block_rows:10d} {num_warps:9d} {t:8.1f}")


  torch.set_default_device("cuda")
  torch.manual_seed(0)
  print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), "torch", torch.__version__)
  print("tokens  fused_us  kv_only_us  copy_us  kv+copy_us  speedup  GB/s(fused, new)")
  for n in (512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384):
      compare(n)
  print("tokens  BLOCK_ROWS  num_warps  copy_us")
  for n in (2048, 8192):
      sweep(n)
  ```

  </details>

  **In serving** (TP2, mega attention selected explicitly, Engram offload and indexer settings as in the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe). 8192-token steps are above the default CUDA-graph capture sizes, so they run eagerly and take the new path: the torch
  profiler of an 8192-token prefill shows `_pad_interleaved_q_kernel` (server flag `--profiler-config '{"profiler": "torch", "torch_profiler_dir": "./prof"}'`, then the bench command below with `--profile --num-prompts 2`).

  ```bash
  vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
    --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
    --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching

  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 \
    --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 16
  ```

  **Correctness: unit tests** (CUDA GPU with the `_C` extension built):

  ```bash
  pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py::test_q_interleaved_pad_copy_matches_fused_insert"
  pytest -v tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py
  pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer"
  ```

  | Test | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | `test_q_interleaved_pad_copy_matches_fused_insert` (new) | 6 passed |
  | `test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, whole file | 221 passed |
  | `test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer` | 2 passed |

  The new test runs the KV-only launch plus `_pad_interleaved_q` and the fused launch on the same input at 17, 1024 and 2049 tokens (both sides of the op's `NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF`), with and without 5 trailing DP-padding rows that have no slot. It requires
  identical cache bytes and identical padded-Q bits, with the copy writing into a NaN-filled buffer.
  **Lint:** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.0), `typos`, `py_compile` and the local pre-commit hooks (`check_spdx_header`, `check_forbidden_imports`, `check_torch_cuda`, `check_boolean_context_manager`, `check_init_lazy_imports`,
  `validate_config`, `check_test_tethering`) pass on the four changed files, and so does the pre-commit mypy hook (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, Python 3.11).

  **CI coverage:** the new test is in `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, which `:nvidia: (H100) DeepSeek V4 Kernels`, `:nvidia: (B200) DeepSeek V4 Kernels` and the `:amd: (MI355 DPX) DeepSeek V4 Fused Kernels` mirror run. This
  PR's test change triggers them, but their `source_file_dependencies` do not list `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`, so a later change to the copy alone would not re-run the test; I can add it if wanted. `test_compressor_kv_cache.py` runs in
  `:nvidia: (B200) Miscellaneous Kernels`. No CI job serves mega attention at TP2 (the DeepSeek-V4.1 GSM8K config in CI is TP4, where the copy is off), so the serving check above is a manual run.

  ## Details

  **Motivation.** Mega attention applies Q RoPE itself and reads Q chunk-interleaved: per token, 32 chunks of `[heads, 16]` with the padding heads at the tail of every chunk. The V4.1 layer norms `qr` before `wq_b`, so the Q half of
  `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert` is a pure zero-pad in that layout. With 32 live heads padded to 64 it reads 32 KiB and writes 64 KiB per token, against about 1.8 KiB for the KV half sharing the launch, so on large steps the op's time
  is mostly the Q pad. The op processes Q one (token, head) slot per warp, and in this layout a head's 16-element lane chunks sit `padded_heads * 16` elements apart; the copy instead writes each (token, chunk) row of 1024 elements contiguously.

  **Design.**
  - `_pads_q_by_copy` is set once per layer: the layer reads Q interleaved (`accepts_unnormed_unroped_query`), has 32 live heads padded to 64, and `max_num_batched_tokens >= 2048`. Such layers register `_pad_interleaved_q` for JIT warmup, so the first
  long prefill does not compile it.
  - Per step, `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` takes the copy when the layer qualifies, the step has at least 2048 tokens and the current stream is not capturing. The op then runs with `q_head_padded=0`, the KV-only mode TP1 mega attention already uses on
  main: it schedules no Q slots and runs the same per-token RoPE, MXFP8 quantization and paged insert, skipping DP-padding rows as before (`fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` launches the same KV kernel; passing 0 keeps the existing call).
  `_pad_interleaved_q` then writes the padded Q into a fresh `[num_tokens, 64, 512]` tensor.
  - `_pad_interleaved_q` is a Triton kernel over `num_tokens * 32` rows, one per (token, 16-dim chunk): 512 live elements copied, then 512 zeros. It goes through `triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup` like other warmed Triton launchers.
  - 1024 equals the op's `NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF`, where it switches to its reduced-grid kernel; smaller steps keep one launch. The copy would also win at 512 tokens (1.61x above), but steps that small normally run inside captured CUDA graphs, which keep the
  fused pad.
  - The branch lives in the shared `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert`, next to the existing interleaved-Q handling; a mega-attention override would have to duplicate that method's KV-insert setup.

  **Exactness.** With norm and RoPE off, the op's live-Q path converts bf16 to fp32 and back with no arithmetic in between, which reproduces every non-NaN value bit for bit, and it stores +0.0 in the padding slots. The copy moves the bits unchanged and
  stores the same +0.0. The KV half runs the same code in both modes, and the test compares the cache bytes with `rtol=0, atol=0`.

  **Tradeoffs and limitations.**
  - Eligible steps issue two launches instead of one; the extra Triton launch is host-side overhead that large prefill steps hide.
  - Only the 32-of-64 shard qualifies: with 16 or 8 live heads a chunk's padding is 768 or 896 columns, not the power of two `tl.arange` needs, so TP4/TP8 keep the fused pad.
  - Work captured into a CUDA graph keeps the fused pad, so the copy applies only where this method runs outside stream capture: by default, steps above the largest captured size; under Model Runner V1, whose wide eager region spans this method, also
  captured sizes of 1024 tokens or more.
  - Deployments that select another attention backend (for example FlashInfer sparse MLA) are unaffected.
  - The CUDA op is unchanged; reworking its interleaved Q stores would keep a single launch, but in a kernel shared by every DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 backend.

  **Compatibility.**
  - Backends and platforms: the FlashMLA sparse, FlashInfer and ROCm layers do not read Q interleaved, so `_pads_q_by_copy` is false for them; mega attention itself is SM10x-only. DeepSeek-V4 (non-4.1) code is untouched.
  - TP sizes (64-head model): TP1 (64 live heads) already skips the pad; TP2 takes the copy; TP4 and TP8 are unchanged.
  - Prefill context parallelism (#59857) selects the FlashMLA layer, so it never reaches the copy; the stand-in layer of `test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer` now declares `_pads_q_by_copy=False`, since that test calls
  `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` on it. The SM90-only token-sharded `fused_wqa_wkv` (#58872) never meets mega attention, and `forward_kv` (decoder replay) builds no Q.
  - CUDA graphs: capture keeps the fused pad, so captured graphs are unchanged. Batch invariance: both paths produce the same bits, so taking the copy (which depends on the step's token count) changes no result.
  - CPU/GPU sync: none added; the decision reads `q.shape[0]`, a flag set at init and the stream's capture state.

  **Not a duplicate.** On 2026-10-18 I searched open PRs and PRs since 2026-08-15 for "pad interleaved q", "qnorm rope kv insert", "Q pad mega" and "heads padded 64 decode"; none moves the mega-attention Q pad out of the fused insert. Related work: #56935
  added mega attention and the fused interleaved pad this PR bypasses on large eager steps; #61371 changed the V4.1 KV record, which both launch modes share; #58872 added the token-sharded `fused_wqa_wkv` whose `_SHARD_FUSED_WQA_WKV_MIN_TOKENS` sits next
  to the new constant; #60076 (open) switches the ROCm DSpark context-KV insert to the existing KV-only `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` and touches neither mega attention nor its Q pad (it and this PR edit different tests in
  `tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py`). #55654 (open) adds KV-only insert ops (`fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_quant_insert`, and `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_norm_rope_quant_insert` with kv_norm folded in) so DeepSeek-V4's DSpark `_insert_context_kv` no
  longer builds a dummy query. This PR adds no KV op and touches neither DSpark nor DeepSeek-V4: it calls the existing `q_head_padded=0` mode of the fused op from the V4.1 attention layer. That path also sees DP-padding rows (more KV rows than slots),
  which the fused op's KV-only mode skips and #55654's ops reject. The only file both PRs touch is `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, where each adds tests.

  **AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to develop this change, port it onto current main, run vLLM's `pr-checklist` skill and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation reported above.

title: [Perf][Kernel][DSv4.1] Swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention for small TP2/TP4 steps
author: roborluo
body:
## Overview

  Makes DeepSeek-V4.1's per-layer decode attention step **1.4-2.15x faster** for decode steps of up to 16 tokens at TP2 / TP4, by adding a swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention kernel to the FlashMLA mega-attention layer (#56935) on SM10x. Steps of up to 16
  tokens with 16 or 32 live heads per rank (TP4 / TP2 of the 64-head model) now take it instead of the mega kernel, which pads the heads to 64.
  Part of #57448; it reads the interleaved V4.1 KV records from #61371. Related work that this PR does not duplicate (see Details): #59418, #61615, #57711, #61868.

  ## Claims

  - **1.4-2.15x faster decode attention for 1-16 tokens:** 1.8-2.15x with 16 live heads (TP4) and 1.4-1.8x with 32 (TP2), for both NVFP4 and fp8 compressed records (per-layer Q pad + KV insert + attention, table below; the lower ends are B300). End to end at TP2 this is 4.5-7.6% lower median TPOT at concurrency 1-16 (see the A/B comment). The mega kernel's FP8 decode maps
  query heads to the MMA's M dimension, which is at least 64, so at TP2 and TP4 half or three quarters of its MMA work goes to padding heads; swap-AB puts the KV slots on M and only the live heads on N.
  - **Accuracy:** the output's error against an fp64 reference is at most 1.1x the mega kernel's, and the output is within 2% of the mega kernel's, over 64 test cases.
  - **Automatic and contained.** There is no new flag, environment variable or config option. Every other decode step, layer and TP size keeps the mega kernel; prefill and other platforms are unchanged. The new kernel is CUDA-graph safe and deterministic,
  and adds no host sync.

  ## Validation

  **Performance.** This PR adds a swap-AB arm to the existing `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`. Each arm's per-step ops (Q pad + KV insert + attention) are timed as a CUDA graph replay, the same harness that produced the mega vs split-KV
  table in `flash_mla_mega_attn.py`.

  ```bash
  for heads in 16 32; do
    for rec in 288 528; do
      .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py \
          --local-heads $heads --extra-bytes $rec --decode-s-q 1 2 4 8 16 32 64
    done
  done
  ```

  Speedup = mega step time / swap-AB step time (median of two runs, which differ by at most 9% per cell):

  | Live heads | Compressed record | 1 token | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
  |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 16 (TP4) | NVFP4 (288 B) | **2.15x** | **2.00x** | **2.06x** | **1.94x** | **2.04x** | 1.25x | 0.94x |
  | 16 (TP4) | fp8 (528 B) | **2.13x** | **1.96x** | **2.02x** | **1.90x** | **1.99x** | 1.22x | 0.91x |
  | 32 (TP2) | fp8 (528 B) | **1.76x** | **1.66x** | **1.71x** | **1.62x** | **1.71x** | 0.98x | 0.73x |

  At 32 tokens swap-AB still wins with 16 heads (1.22-1.25x) but only breaks even with 32 (0.98-1.02x), and at 64 it loses with both, so `_SWAPAB_MAX_TOKENS = 16` is the largest step size where it wins for both head counts. On B300 (nightly 76c6f3f2) the same harness gives 1.83-2.0x with 16 heads and 1.41-1.64x with 32 heads at 1-16 tokens, for both record formats. As in the existing harness,
  every replay reuses the same buffers, so the KV reads hit a warm L2 for both kernels; timed alone with the L2 flushed before every call, the attention kernel is 1.6-2.3x faster than the mega kernel over 48 shapes with 1-16 tokens (geomean 1.94x).

  **Correctness: unit tests.** The kernel tests skip unless the GPU is SM10x and the CuTe DSL is built with CUDA 13.2+.

  ```bash
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_swapab_decode.py
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode"
  ```

  | Test (cases) | Checks | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `test_matches_reference` (64) | 16/32 heads x 1/2/5/16 tokens x NVFP4/fp8 compressed records x 64/128-slot pages x partial/full lengths. Output is finite; Frobenius and max-abs error vs an fp64 reference are <= 1.1x the mega kernel's; within 2% of the
  mega output | 64 passed |
  | `test_untouched_padding` (2) | Padding heads' output groups keep their bytes | 2 passed |
  | `test_cuda_graph_and_determinism` (12) | Repeated eager calls and a CUDA graph replay agree bit for bit, also after the inputs change in place | 12 passed |
  | `test_dispatch_rule` (9, CPU) | Which kernel each dispatch condition selects | 9 passed |
  | `test_warmup_key_matches_launch` (4, CPU) | The key the layer registers at construction is the key a decode step launches, on a compressed cache shaped as the model runner binds it | 4 passed |
  | `test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode` (3, existing) | The V4.1 cache writers and FlashMLA agree on the interleaved records the kernel reads | 3 passed |

  ## Details

  **Motivation.** Mega attention is the default DeepSeek V4.1 decode path on SM10x. Its FP8 decode kernel takes 64 or 128 query heads, so at TP2 and TP4 half or three quarters of its MMA work goes to padding heads. The mega vs split-KV note in
  `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` already records that this padded-head cost dominates small decode steps. Small steps are what low-concurrency decode and spec-decode verify and draft steps run.

  **Why a separate kernel, not a FlashMLA change.** FlashMLA's decode maps query heads to the MMA's M dimension, which is at least 64. Serving 16 or 32 heads without padding needs the opposite mapping, with KV slots on M and heads on N. That is a
  different kernel, not a smaller tile. In FlashMLA it would be CUDA C++ shipped through a vllm-project/FlashMLA release and a vLLM bump, as #61371 was. The CuTe DSL kernel instead compiles from Python at JIT warmup, needs no build change, and lives next
  to its only caller in the DSv4.1 model package. It is adapted from SGLang's swap-AB DSv4 decode attention (Apache-2.0, attribution in the file header).

  <details>
  <summary>Kernel design</summary>

  - **MMA shape.** `SwapABDecodeKernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/swapab_decode_attn.py`) puts the KV slots on the tcgen05 MMA's M side (128 rows) and the live heads on N (16 or 32).
  - **One CTA per (token, KV tile).** Tiles are 64 slots of the SWA list or 128 slots of the compressed list. Each CTA:
    - gathers its slots' V4.1 records in place (fp8 528 B, NVFP4 288 B, each token's scales after its data);
    - dequantizes them exactly to bf16 in SMEM;
    - RoPEs Q in fp32 from the mega kernel's chunk-interleaved, head-padded layout;
    - computes S = KV Q^T and O = KV^T P, with P split into bf16 hi and lo parts.
  - **One cluster per token.** A token's tiles form one thread-block cluster: 6 CTAs for V4.1-Flash's 128-slot window plus 512 compressed slots. The cluster merges the partials and the attention sink over DSMEM in a fixed peer order. It then applies the
  inverse RoPE and writes MXFP8 with the mega kernel's rounding rule into the o-fused buffers `wo_a` reads, for the live heads' groups only.
  - **One launch.** The kernel uses PDL and has no workspace, second kernel, allocation or host sync.
  - **JIT warmup.** The compile key is (live heads, slot-list widths, compressed record size, SWA and compressed page sizes); the token count is the grid's y dimension. Every field is fixed when the layer is built: the backend has one kernel block size (128), so a compressed page always holds
  `128 // compress_ratio` slots, whatever the KV cache manager's block size. The layer registers the key in `__init__`, next to its other JIT warmups, and `kernel_warmup` compiles it before CUDA graph capture. V4.1-Flash needs two keys, one per compressed page size.

  </details>

  **Dispatch.** `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention._forward_decode_mega` takes the swap-AB kernel only when all of these hold:
  - the GPU is SM10x;
  - the layer has a compressed cache;
  - the layer has 16 or 32 live heads;
  - a token's tiles fit one portable cluster: `ceil(window / 64) + ceil(index_topk / 128) <= 8`;
  - the CuTe DSL imports and was built with CUDA 13.2+, which the direct fp8 / fp4 to bf16x2 conversions need (PTX ISA 9.2);
  - `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is off;
  - the step has at most 16 decode tokens (`_SWAPAB_MAX_TOKENS`). Under CUDA graphs this is the padded count, so each captured graph holds exactly one of the two kernels;
  - the step's SWA list is exactly the window. DSpark's non-causal draft steps widen it, so they keep the mega kernel.

  The first six conditions are fixed when the layer is built. The last two are host-side shape checks on each step. If any condition fails, the step runs the mega kernel exactly as before.
  **Complexity.** The change adds about 1,260 lines of kernel code (about 400 of them are 23 small inline-PTX wrappers) and about 100 lines in the layer. Nothing changes in the model runner, the scheduler, FlashMLA or shared attention code. At runtime the
  kernel module is imported only by SM10x layers with a compressed cache, 16 or 32 heads and an importable CuTe DSL. Most of the maintenance cost is the inline PTX and the SMEM / TMEM layout math. Both are documented next to the code, and the tests pin
  them to an fp64 reference and to the mega kernel.

  **Tradeoffs and limitations.**
  - **Cost grows with tokens.** The kernel runs one cluster of up to 8 CTAs per token, and its 150+ KiB of SMEM means one CTA per SM. Hence the 16-token cutoff, which is the same for TP2 / TP4 and both record formats: in the table above swap-AB is at
  least 1.6x faster at every step size up to 16 tokens (at least 1.4x on B300).
  - **Not bit-identical.** The fp32 sums are ordered differently from the mega kernel's, so the output depends on which kernel the step size selects. Batch-invariant runs therefore keep the mega kernel at every size.
  - **Unused Q padding.** The fused KV insert still zero-pads Q to 64 heads, which swap-AB does not read. This keeps one Q contract for both kernels.
  - **Toolchain.** The kernel needs a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+. With an older build the layer keeps the mega kernel and the kernel tests skip.
  - **Startup.** V4.1-Flash adds two JIT compiles per worker, at warmup.

  **Compatibility.**
  - **Scope.** Only `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention` changes. The FlashMLA sparse layer, FlashInfer sparse MLA, and the SM90, SM120 and ROCm paths are untouched. TP1 (64 heads) and TP8 (8 heads) keep the mega kernel.
  - **Model runners.** Both V1 and V2 build the model under the JIT warmup registry, so both register the key.
  - **CUDA graphs, batch invariance, spec decode.** See Dispatch above.
  - **Unchanged.** Prefill, the KV cache layout and checkpoints.

  **CI.** The new tests run in the optional (nightly) 4xB200 step, renamed "(4xB200) DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA Kernels" (`models_basic.yaml`, key `dsv41-nvidia-kernels-4xb200`), next to the specialized-decode tests. The kernel tests need SM10x, the FlashMLA mega ops and a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+, and skip otherwise; with vLLM's pinned `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.8.0` they run. The optional "(B200)
  LM Eval Spec Decode" step runs the V4.1-Flash NVFP4 DSpark TP4 GSM8K config. It runs at full concurrency, where few steps are small enough for swap-AB.

  **Not a duplicate.** On 2026-10-18 I searched GitHub (open PRs plus PRs since 2026-08-15) for "swap-AB", "swapab", "small-head decode", "heads padded 64 decode", "mega attention DSv4.1" and "V4.1 decode attention". No PR adds an SM10x small-head decode
  kernel for the mega-attention path. Related work:
  - **#59418** (open, small-head sparse decode on SM90) is a Triton kernel for Hopper. It targets 8 or 16 heads in the plain FlashMLA sparse layer, which reads the 584 B `fp8_ds_mla` records used off SM10x. This PR targets SM10x tcgen05 and 16 or 32 heads
  in the mega-attention layer, which reads the V4.1 records and fuses the inverse RoPE and MXFP8 output.
  - **#61615** (open) is small-head FlashMLA sparse prefill on SM90. This PR changes decode only, on SM10x.
  - **#57711** (closed by its author on 2026-09-25) was an opt-in split-KV mode inside the mega decode kernel, behind the `VLLM_DSV41_MEGA_SPLITKV` env flags and blocked on vllm-project/FlashMLA#25. That kernel still pads the heads to 64. This PR leaves
  FlashMLA alone, removes the padded-head work and adds no flags.
  - **#61868** (open) is an opt-in GB300 TP4 DSpark executor whose sparse-MLA decode uses FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4`. That is a separate opt-in path; this PR changes the default mega-attention path.

  **AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). It drafted the port of the kernel onto main, the tests, the benchmark arm, the `/pr-checklist` pass and this description. The submitter reviewed every changed
  line and ran the validation above.

title: [Perf] Watermarking: skip greedy-fallback argmax when no request is greedy
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

`GPUWatermarkSampler._sample_random` ran a full-vocabulary argmax on every watermarked step to give greedy (temperature 0) rows their token, even when the batch had no greedy row. This PR checks the host-side temperatures first and skips the argmax and the `torch.where` when no row is greedy.

## Claims

- The watermarked sampler step is 13 to 41 µs faster under CUDA graphs on H200 (B = 1 to 128, vocab 151,936), for both `gumbel` and `dual_key_gumbel`. That is 15 to 22% of the step, and 17 to 41% of the watermark's overhead over the plain sampler.
- Serving Qwen3-0.6B with Gumbel watermarking at concurrency 32: mean TPOT drops by 21.5 ± 11.5 µs (6 paired replicates), which matches the 20 µs saved per step at B = 32. The no-watermark arm does not change.
- Speculative decoding (`dual_key_gumbel` + DFlash): the verify step uses the rejection sampler, which handles greedy rows inside its kernel and never reaches the changed code. Verify-step time and serving throughput are unchanged. Only steps where no request in the batch has drafts go through `_sample_random`; those get the same saving.
- Sampled tokens are unchanged. When any row is greedy, the old code runs as before.

## Validation

![Sampler step time before and after, CUDA graph replay, H200](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/5571ba41e2321317fe8f5c7357b7031ffd9b43b4/sampler_step_before_after.png)

**Tests.** `pytest tests/watermarking tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sample_warmup.py tests/entrypoints/openai/test_watermarking.py` on 1x H200: 229 passed, 3 skipped, both before and after this change (the skips are the 2-GPU tests). `tests/watermarking/test_parallel_compatibility.py` on 2x H200: 3 passed. The new `test_gpu_sampler_uses_argmax_only_for_greedy_rows` checks one greedy plus one watermarked row (greedy row gets the argmax) and two watermarked rows (both keep the watermarked token). It also passes against the old `gpu_sampler.py`, so the tokens match the previous behaviour. `tests/watermarking` runs in the CPU `watermarking` CI step.

**Microbenchmark, sampler step.** CUDA graph replay, µs, 1x H200. fp32 logits, vocab 151,936, temperature 1, no top-k/top-p, context width 4, `deduplicate_contexts=single_turn`. Before and after interleaved, 3 rounds, mean of the per-round medians (round-to-round sd ≤ 0.4 µs).

| Step | B | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `gumbel` | 1 | 72.7 | 59.3 | −13.4 (−18%) |
| `gumbel` | 32 | 98.7 | 78.5 | −20.2 (−20%) |
| `gumbel` | 128 | 185.9 | 144.6 | −41.3 (−22%) |
| `dual_key_gumbel` | 1 | 90.8 | 77.5 | −13.3 (−15%) |
| `dual_key_gumbel` | 32 | 135.4 | 114.5 | −20.9 (−15%) |
| `dual_key_gumbel` | 128 | 280.2 | 239.1 | −41.0 (−15%) |
| Spec decode, step without drafts (`dual_key_gumbel` target) | 1 | 73.4 | 60.4 | −13.1 (−18%) |
| Spec decode, step without drafts | 32 | 96.9 | 76.9 | −20.0 (−21%) |
| Spec decode, step without drafts | 128 | 184.7 | 143.2 | −41.5 (−22%) |
| Spec decode, verify step (3 drafts, B × 4 rows) | 1 | 73.4 | 73.4 | −0.1 |
| Spec decode, verify step | 32 | 149.5 | 149.2 | −0.3 |
| Spec decode, verify step | 128 | 326.8 | 326.6 | −0.2 |
| No watermark (`Sampler._sample_random`) | 1 / 32 / 128 | 13.3 / 31.2 / 85.2 | 13.1 / 31.3 / 85.3 | ±0.2 |

The verify row times `RejectionSampler._verify` with watermarking. In that benchmark `_sample_random` is replaced by a stub that raises, which confirms the verify step never calls it. In eager mode the step is launch-bound (about 350 to 540 µs) and the two skipped launches save 10 to 40 µs.

**Serving, Gumbel.** Qwen3-0.6B, 1x H200 per replicate, random 1024 in / 128 out, 1000 prompts, concurrency 32, T = 1.0, `--ignore-eos`, `--watermark-config '{"algorithm":"gumbel","key":42,"context_width":4}'`. A fresh server per arm, one discarded warm-up bench, then the median of 3 benches. Arm order rotated, server and client pinned to the GPUs' NUMA node. 6 paired replicates, mean ± SE of the paired difference:

| Comparison | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|
| Gumbel, after − before | +38 ± 33 | −21.5 ± 11.5 µs |
| No watermark, after − before | −16 ± 11 | −5.8 ± 5.2 µs |
| Gumbel overhead over no watermark, before | −292 ± 21 (−3.3%) | +114.6 ± 7.8 µs |
| Gumbel overhead over no watermark, after | −238 ± 14 (−2.7%) | +98.9 ± 5.9 µs |

The TPOT gain is about 0.7% for this small model, close to run-to-run noise. The microbenchmark is the main evidence.

**Serving, speculative decoding.** Qwen3-8B with `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` (`dflash`, 3 speculative tokens, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`), `--watermark-config '{"algorithm":"dual_key_gumbel","key":42,"alpha":0.1}'`, same client and protocol as above. Arms: no watermark, before, after. 3 paired replicates, each on its own H200, mean ± SE of the paired difference:

| Comparison | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Watermarked, after − before | +0.8 ± 0.2 (+0.03%) | +14.0 ± 14.5 µs (+0.13%) | 1.74 → 1.74 |
| Watermark vs no watermark, before | +28.5 ± 0.7 (+1.0%) | −145 ± 8 µs | 1.67 → 1.74 |
| Watermark vs no watermark, after | +29.3 ± 0.9 (+1.1%) | −131 ± 7 µs | 1.67 → 1.74 |

Arm means: no watermark 2760 tok/s / 10.83 ms TPOT, before 2788 / 10.69, after 2789 / 10.70. Spec-decode serving does not change, as the code path predicts. (On this random-token workload the watermarked arms run slightly faster than no watermark because their acceptance length is higher.) A seeded completion produced the same text before and after.

**No GPU syncs.** Serving Qwen3-0.6B with Gumbel watermarking under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed 200 of 200 requests with no sync error.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

Before = upstream main `b7701fc3e4`; after = this branch. The "before" runs used the branch checkout with upstream main's `vllm/v1/watermarking/gpu_sampler.py` overlaid through `PYTHONPATH`; each run logged which file it imported.

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1

# Tests
pytest tests/watermarking tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sample_warmup.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_watermarking.py
pytest tests/watermarking/test_parallel_compatibility.py   # 2 GPUs

# Serving, Gumbel (arms: with and without --watermark-config)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --watermark-config '{"algorithm":"gumbel","key":42,"context_width":4}'

# Serving, speculative decoding (arms: with and without --watermark-config)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --watermark-config '{"algorithm":"dual_key_gumbel","key":42,"alpha":0.1}'

# Client (one warm-up run, then 3 measured runs per server)
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model <model> --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 1000 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --num-warmups 32 --temperature 1.0 --seed 1
```

The microbenchmarks call `GPUWatermarkSampler._sample_random`, `Sampler._sample_random` and `RejectionSampler._verify` directly with real vLLM code and synthetic state (prompt 1024, 64 generated tokens, random token history), and time them with `triton.testing.do_bench` on a captured CUDA graph.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The greedy fallback was unconditional:

```python
sampled = torch.where(temperatures == 0, processed_logits.argmax(dim=-1), sampled)
```

The argmax reads the whole `[B, V]` fp32 logits tensor again after the watermark kernel has already read it. At B = 32 and V = 151,936 that is 19.4 MB per step, plus a second kernel launch for `torch.where`. Most watermarked traffic has no greedy rows, because a greedy request cannot be watermarked, so the result was usually discarded.

**Change.** Run the fallback only if `self.sampling_states.any_greedy(idx_mapping_np)` is true. This existing helper reads the host-side temperature array, the same one `_sample_random` already reads to decide whether watermarking is on for the batch. The branch is decided on the host, like the existing watermarking-enabled check above it, so there is no GPU sync. Expanded (speculative) rows repeat `idx_mapping` rows, so the host check covers them too.

**Speculative decoding.** When the batch has drafts, the V2 model runner calls `RejectionSampler`. It applies sampling params and runs the watermarked `rejection_sample` kernels, which handle temperature-0 rows in-kernel (accept if the draft matches the target argmax). It does not call `_sample_random`. The draft side (`DraftWatermarker.sample`) has no greedy-fallback argmax either. So this PR only affects spec-decode steps where no request in the batch has drafts. In the DFlash serving run above, 13 of the first 5,000 sampling steps (0.3%, startup warm-up included) went through `_sample_random`, counted with a diagnostic hook; the rest used the rejection sampler.

**Behaviour.** Tokens are unchanged for every batch. One internal difference: padding rows (`expanded_idx_mapping == -1`) used to read slot −1's temperature on the GPU and could receive an argmax token. They now keep the sampled token when no real row is greedy. Padding rows are discarded, so this is not observable.

**Tests.** Three existing tests stub `sampler.sampling_states` with a `SimpleNamespace`; they get an `any_greedy` stub that returns `False`, since all their rows use temperature 1.

---

title: [Perf][MRV2] Parallelize staged writes across 1024-element chunks
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview

`_apply_write_kernel` (MRV2 `StagedWriteTensor` / `FusedStagedWriter`) runs one program per staged write and loops over 1024-element chunks, so writing an admitted long prompt into its `all_token_ids` row runs on a single SM. This PR launches one program per chunk instead. It also removes per-block checks from `BlockPool.get_new_blocks` when neither prefix caching nor a metrics collector is enabled.

## Claims

- Long staged writes are 31x faster at 128K tokens (76 -> 2.5 us) and 120x faster at 855K tokens (443 -> 3.7 us) on GB200. Small writes (decode steps, block tables) do not regress.
- In DEP decode, every admission ran this copy on the admitting rank right before its forward, which made that rank the straggler for the step. With this PR, admitting a request adds ~10 us of rank skew instead of ~200 us.
- `get_new_blocks` + `free_blocks` for 4000 blocks without prefix caching: 616 -> 528 us.

## Validation

**Kernel microbenchmark**, GB200, FlashInfer CUPTI, int32, old kernel copied into the script, outputs checked equal before timing:

| writes | old (us) | new (us) | speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256 x 1 token (decode step) | 2.82 | 2.30 | 1.2x |
| 256 x 8 (block table) | 2.78 | 2.32 | 1.2x |
| 1 x 8K | 7.04 | 2.24 | 3.1x |
| 1 x 32K | 20.94 | 2.18 | 9.6x |
| 1 x 128K | 76.32 | 2.46 | 31.0x |
| 1 x 855K | 443.42 | 3.71 | 119.5x |
| 1 x 128K + 63 x 1 token | 75.20 | 5.94 | 12.7x |

**Serving context** (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, P/D decode instance, DEP, 128K-token prompts, GB200; measured on our internal branch, which runs the same kernel): at DEP32 BS64, the admitting rank was the last to reach the first MoE in 90 of 98 steps, 252 us behind the median rank (46 us in steps with no admission). With this change at DEP8 BS64, the last rank trails the median by 73 us when a rank admits vs 63 us when none does.

**BlockPool**: in-process CPU microbenchmark, 4000 blocks, `enable_caching=False`, no metrics collector, NUMA-pinned on GB200 Grace, best of 5 x 200: 616 us (current code path) -> 528 us.

**Tests** (GB200):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py
# 266 passed, 4 skipped
```

The existing `test_staged_write_inflight` already covers multi-chunk and mixed-length writes on the `StagedWriteTensor` path. The new `test_block_tables_fused_write_spans_multiple_chunks` covers a fused write longer than one chunk.

## Details

- Grid dim 1 is `cdiv(max_write_len, 1024)`. Programs past the end of a shorter write are fully masked. Each `StagedWriteTensor` records its longest staged write as it stages, so launching adds O(1) host work. Computing the max from `cu_lens` at apply time would cost ~40 us per 1024 writes on Grace. The bytes written are unchanged, and no new sync is added.
- Tradeoff: in a batch with one long write and many short ones, the short writes launch programs that exit immediately (1 x 128K + 63 x 1: 5.9 us vs 2.5 us for 1 x 128K alone). This is still far below the old 75 us.
- `get_new_blocks`: blocks popped from the free queue always have `ref_cnt == 0`, so the no-caching, no-metrics path sets `ref_cnt = 1` directly. The caching and metrics paths are unchanged.
- Duplicate check: #62018 fuses separate staged-write calls into fewer launches, and #51334 / #59908 reduce the host-side staging cost. None of them changes how the kernel parallelizes a single long write, so they are complementary to this PR.

---

<details>

title: [Perf][Core] Keep prompt token ids as int32 buffers
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview Keep prompt token ids as one int32 buffer from the frontend to the GPU workers. The frontends send `prompt_token_ids` as a rank-1 ndarray (out of band when long), `Request` stores them in `TokenBuffer` (an int32 `array` that reads like a list), and the MRV2 worker stages them as one chunk. Merged with main and tested at `fc510b3710` (main at `dd4e40142a`, 2026-11-04). #65300 is on main and already sends a new request's prompt to workers once, so that is not counted below. What is left is the per-token work: main still creates or walks one Python int per token on every hop, and keeps one per token in memory. ## Claims CPU time per admitted request and EngineCore memory, main -> this PR, on one 128K-token prompt: - **Step's critical path:** pickle + unpickle + staging, 6.86 -> 0.17 ms (40x). Pickle and unpickle run before the worker reaches the step's DP all-reduce, so a rank admitting a long prompt makes every rank wait. - **Input thread, with frontend hashes:** decode + `Request()`, 3.99 -> 0.24 ms (16x). This thread holds the GIL the engine loop needs. - **EngineCore memory:** 6.45 -> 1.68 MB per request (3.8x). - **Costs:** the Python frontend's encode goes from 3.53 to 4.33 ms (+23%). Requests hashed in the engine (e.g. multimodal) do not gain on the input thread. - **Not shown:** end-to-end throughput on this head. These are per-stage CPU measurements. ## Validation ### CPU repro GB200 Grace, `numactl` node 0, sha256 hashes, block size 16. Each value is the middle of 3 interleaved rounds, each round the best of 10 calls (engine hashing: best of 3). Rounds agree within ~4%, except values under 0.1 ms, which vary by up to 0.01 ms. The host was shared but lightly loaded. Stages run in-process; the ring or zmq transfer is not measured. | Stage (thread) | 128K tokens: main (ms) | this PR (ms) | 855K tokens: main (ms) | this PR (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Pickle `NewRequestData` (scheduler) | 1.69 | 0.04 | 11.36 | 0.20 | | Unpickle (worker) | 3.60 | 0.04 | 25.54 | 0.33 | | `StagedWriteTensor.stage_write` + `apply_write` (worker) | 1.57 | 0.09 | 9.80 | 0.32 | | **Critical path total** | **6.86** | **0.17** | **46.70** | **0.85** | | Decode + `Request()`, frontend hashes as in #63842 (input) | 3.99 | 0.24 | 27.13 | 1.72 | | Decode + `Request()`, no hashing (input) | 3.81 | 0.04 | 25.88 | 0.33 | | Decode + `Request()`, engine hashes (input) | 16.44 | 15.70 | 111.02 | 106.75 | | Python frontend encode (frontend) | 3.53 | 4.33 | 23.46 | 28.88 | | Memory | 128K tokens: main | this PR | 855K tokens: main | this PR | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Python heap held per request in EngineCore (`tracemalloc`) | 6.45 MB | 1.68 MB | 42.98 MB | 11.23 MB | | Pickled `NewRequestData` | 0.52 MB | 0.53 MB | 3.49 MB | 3.50 MB | **What this means for a decode instance (arithmetic, not a measurement).** The reference is a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D run with `max-num-seqs` 128 and ~0.36 admissions per step per DP rank: - Critical path: ~6.86 ms x 0.36 = ~2.5 ms per step on average on each rank, or ~14 ms on a step where one rank admits 2 requests. All-reduce makes the other ranks wait for the part before it. This PR makes both negligible. - Input thread: 3.99 ms x 15.5 req/s = ~6% of a core holding the GIL, against ~0.4%. - Memory: 128 running requests x 4.77 MB = ~0.6 GB less per EngineCore at 128K, not counting requests waiting for a slot. ```bash # On main and on this branch. No GPU needed: the staging row is skipped without one. PYTHONPATH=. numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 python repro_prompt_ids_int32.py 2>/dev/null ```
repro_prompt_ids_int32.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python """CPU and memory one long prompt costs with list[int] (main) and int32 (#62702). Run from a vLLM checkout, on main and on #62702 (no GPU needed; staging is skipped without one). Times one request through each CPU stage, in-process, with random ids: PYTHONPATH=. numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 \ python repro_prompt_ids_after_65300.py 2>/dev/null The frames come from the Python encoder, which produces the same (dtype, shape, data) ndarray wire format as vllm-rs. The transfer through the ring or zmq is not measured. """ import json import pickle import time import tracemalloc import numpy as np import torch from vllm import SamplingParams from vllm.utils.hashing import get_hash_fn_by_name from vllm.v1.core import kv_cache_utils as kcu from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import NewRequestData from vllm.v1.engine import EngineCoreRequest, PrefixHashConfig, core_client from vllm.v1.request import Request from vllm.v1.serial_utils import MsgpackDecoder, MsgpackEncoder from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils import StagedWriteTensor BLOCK = 16 OOB_BYTES = 1 << 20 # MessageQueue sends buffers of at least this size out of band pack = getattr(core_client, "_with_packed_prompt", lambda request: request) enc, dec = MsgpackEncoder(), MsgpackDecoder(EngineCoreRequest) sha256 = get_hash_fn_by_name("sha256") kcu.init_none_hash(sha256) hasher = kcu.get_request_block_hasher(BLOCK, sha256) hash_config = PrefixHashConfig( hash_algo="sha256", hash_block_size=BLOCK, none_hash=kcu.NONE_HASH ) staged = None if torch.cuda.is_available(): staged = StagedWriteTensor( (2, 1 << 20), torch.int32, torch.device("cuda"), uva_instead_of_gpu=True ) rng = np.random.default_rng(0) def best_ms(fn, n=10): times = [] for _ in range(n): start = time.perf_counter() fn() times.append(time.perf_counter() - start) return min(times) * 1e3 def dumps(obj): oob = [] def callback(buf): raw = buf.raw() if len(raw) < OOB_BYTES: return True oob.append(raw) return False return pickle.dumps(obj, protocol=5, buffer_callback=callback), oob def admit(frames, block_hasher): """EngineCore's input thread: decode a request and build the Request.""" request = dec.decode(frames) return Request.from_engine_core_request( request, block_hasher, kcu.frontend_block_hashes(request, hash_config) ) def engine_request(ids, block_hashes=None): return EngineCoreRequest( request_id="r", prompt_token_ids=ids.tolist(), mm_features=None, sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=16), pooling_params=None, arrival_time=0.0, lora_request=None, cache_salt=None, data_parallel_rank=None, block_hashes=block_hashes, ) def encode(ids, block_hashes=None): return [bytes(f) for f in enc.encode(pack(engine_request(ids, block_hashes)))] def held_mb_per_request(make, count=8): tracemalloc.start() live = [make() for _ in range(count)] held = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()[0] tracemalloc.stop() del live return held / count / 1e6 for n in (131072, 875520): ids = rng.integers(0, 129280, n, dtype=np.int32) plain = encode(ids) req = admit(plain, hasher) hashed = encode(ids, list(req.block_hashes)) assert admit(hashed, hasher).block_hashes == req.block_hashes prefill = getattr(req, "prefill_token_ids", req._all_token_ids) new_req = NewRequestData.from_request(req, ([],), prefill) blob, oob = dumps(new_req) data = pickle.loads(blob, buffers=[bytearray(b) for b in oob]) assert list(data.prefill_token_ids) == list(data.prompt_token_ids) == ids.tolist() row = { "python_frontend_encode": best_ms(lambda: encode(ids)), "input_frontend_hashes": best_ms(lambda: admit(hashed, hasher)), "input_no_hashing": best_ms(lambda: admit(plain, None)), "input_engine_hashes": best_ms(lambda: admit(plain, hasher), n=3), "pickle": best_ms(lambda: dumps(new_req)), "unpickle": best_ms( lambda: pickle.loads(blob, buffers=[bytearray(b) for b in oob]) ), } if staged is not None: def stage(): staged.stage_write(0, 0, data.prefill_token_ids) staged.apply_write() torch.cuda.synchronize() row["stage_apply"] = best_ms(stage) assert torch.equal(staged.gpu[0, :n].cpu(), torch.from_numpy(ids)) row["engine_mb_per_request"] = held_mb_per_request(lambda: admit(hashed, None)) row["pickle_mb"] = (len(blob) + sum(len(b) for b in oob)) / 1e6 print(json.dumps({"n": n, **{k: round(v, 3) for k, v in row.items()}}), flush=True) ```
### E2E correctness Run on the previous head (`2a40199395`), before main was merged, and not repeated on `fc510b3710`. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, MRV2, GB200, Rust frontend with prefix caching: - Prompts of 25, 18,684 and 31,204 tokens: cached tokens on repeat 16 / 18,672 / 31,200, and 0 with a new `cache_salt`. No fallback to engine hashing in the logs. - Against main on 3 prompts of 23K-31K tokens: prompt ids are identical (`return_token_ids`) and greedy outputs are identical on the first and the repeated run. On the 31K prompt, the block hashes and sampling params reaching the engine are also identical. - Greedy output is sensitive to how the server is launched: the same `vllm-rs` binary at a different path changed some outputs on this branch, while main's binary gave the same outputs at the two paths tested. First-token logprobs moved by 1e-3 to 3e-2 (bfloat16 weights), as much as main's Rust and Python frontends differ from each other. Converting the ids to int32 or a list in the engine, or ignoring frontend hashes, did not change outputs. I did not root-cause this sensitivity. - GSM8K (lm-eval 0.4.13, 5-shot, greedy, 1024 max tokens, concurrency 32), flexible / strict: Rust frontend 0.5398 / 0.3086, Python frontend 0.5375 / 0.3169, stderr 0.013-0.014. **Regression**: before the fix in `frontend_block_hashes`, every Rust frontend request with block hashes returned HTTP 500 (`ValueError: The truth value of an array...`). `test_frontend_block_hashes_count_check` now uses an ndarray and fails without the fix. ### Tests After merging main (`6f34a97a51`); the only later commit changes one test, and `tests/v1/test_request.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_output.py` and the preprocess test were rerun on `fc510b3710`: - `tests/v1/test_request.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_output.py`, `tests/utils_/test_gc_utils.py`, `tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, `test_prompt_block_hash_vectors.py`, `test_prefix_caching.py`, `test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`, `tests/reasoning/test_minimax_m3_reasoning_parser.py`: 534 passed, 2 skipped. 34 `test_output_processor` cases could not start because they load a gated Llama config; main gives the same 27 passed, 34 errors in that file here. - `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/streaming_input`, `tests/reasoning`, `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py`: 837 passed. - `tests/v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py`, in its own process: passed. - `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-llm -p vllm-mock-engine`: all passed. Pre-commit passes on the Python files changed since the merge. ## Details **Why main still pays per token.** An N-token prompt is N Python ints when msgspec decodes it, again when the scheduler output is pickled and unpickled, and again in worker staging. Each int also takes ~32 bytes plus an 8-byte list slot, and `Request` keeps two lists. With an int32 buffer, each hop copies one block of memory, and stored ids take 4 bytes per copy. - `TokenBuffer` subclasses `array('i')`. Indexing returns `int`; slices and `copy()` return lists; it compares equal to lists; `+` returns a list. Type checkers see it as a `list[int]` subclass. A third-party consumer that JSON- or msgpack-encodes `request.prompt_token_ids` directly would need `list(...)`. - Both frontends send a 32-bit int ndarray: vllm-rs as `WireNdArray`, the Python frontend through `_with_packed_prompt`. Above `VLLM_MSGPACK_ZERO_COPY_THRESHOLD` it goes in its own frame. `EngineCoreRequest.prompt_token_ids` is an ndarray only in its runtime annotation; in-process clients still pass a list. Token ids must fit in 32 bits. - `TokenBuffer` pickles as a `PickleBuffer`, which `MessageQueue` sends out of band at 1 MiB and above. - The Rust block hasher decodes the ids into a `Vec` once per request with `WireNdArray::to_u32_vec`; hashes are byte-identical to main's. - Reasoning parsers and other engine scans use `rfind_tokens`, so a `TokenBuffer` is searched with numpy rather than one Python int at a time. **Tradeoffs and limitations:** - The Python frontend pays one list -> int32 conversion per request (+23% encode). - Engine hashing pickles Python ints, so requests hashed in the engine only move the int creation from decode to hashing. #63454 (draft) adds an opt-in hash over int32 buffers, which would help them. - Output tokens are unchanged: `_output_token_ids` stays a list. - This touches 50 files (+794/-283), much of it call sites that assumed a list. Reviewers should weigh that against the numbers above, which do not yet include end-to-end throughput. **Not a duplicate:** #65300 (merged) shares the send-once change, already on main, and none of the costs measured here. #59908 covers the scheduler -> worker hop only; #51334 is inactive. ---
