title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3] MonoKernel decode for M3 MXFP4 on MI355X
author: micah-wil
body:
### Summary
Adds an opt-in specialized decode path (`--monokernel`) for MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on gfx950. During decode, layers 3–59 run their FFN half as one persistent FlyDSL launch:
- TP all-reduce, residual add and post-attention RMSNorm;
- the FP32 router with top-4 selection;
- the shared and routed BF16×MXFP4 experts;
- the final TP all-reduce.
Attention, the dense layers 0–2, prefill and mixed batches stay on the stock path.
- Follows the RFC #60904 / Kimi-K3 layout: `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/specialized_decode/`. There is one `plan()` per step, and layers are selected with `step.layer(i)`.
- Supports eager and FULL CUDA graphs, at 1–16 decode rows. Larger batches, PIECEWISE steps and prefill use the stock path.
- Startup refuses unsupported configs (default-deny), with every reason reported. Kernel faults fail-stop on every rank, and no token is returned from a failed step.
- Requirements: TP4 on gfx950, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`, `--moe-backend aiter`, `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`.
- Temporary dependency: imports the DeepSeek-V4.1 `mono.common` FlyDSL helpers (peer memory, sync), to move once a common AMD runtime lands.
### Results (MI355X, TP4, FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs)
Baseline is the recommended serve command. `--monokernel` adds the flags it requires.
**Random 1024 in / 1024 out**
| Concurrency | Baseline TPOT (ms) | `--monokernel` TPOT (ms) | TPOT | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.12 | 4.27 | **−16.6%** | 192 → 230 (**+19.6%**) |
| 2 | 5.54 | 4.85 | **−12.5%** | 355 → 403 (+13.4%) |
| 4 | 6.23 | 5.69 | **−8.7%** | 628 → 687 (+9.3%) |
| 8 | 7.46 | 6.88 | **−7.8%** | 1054 → 1136 (+7.8%) |
| 16 | 8.89 | 8.87 | parity | 1755 → 1751 |
| 32 (stock fallback) | 11.51 | 11.54 | parity | 2684 → 2708 |

**Long context, 8192 in / 1024 out:** TPOT −14.9% at concurrency 1 (5.25 → 4.47 ms), −9.0% at 4 (6.42 → 5.84 ms), and −3.4% at 16 (10.12 → 9.78 ms).
**MT-Bench (chat, greedy, ≤1024 output tokens):** TPOT −17.0% at concurrency 1 (5.00 → 4.15 ms; 196 → 235 tok/s), −8.6% at 4 (6.30 → 5.76 ms), and parity at 16.
Kernel-only effect, against the same server with identical flags and no `--monokernel`: TPOT −19.1% at concurrency 1, −14.3% at 2, −11.1% at 4, −8.8% at 8, and parity at 16.

### Accuracy (GSM8K 5-shot, full 1319, flexible-extract)
| Config | Score |
|---|---|
| Same flags, no `--monokernel` | 0.8969 |
| `--monokernel` | 0.9052 (paired +0.83 pp, 95% CI [−0.83, +2.50], McNemar p=0.37) |

### Commands
Baseline:
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --block-size 128 --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --max-model-len 10240
```
`--monokernel`, which is the baseline plus:
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1 ... \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --moe-backend aiter --monokernel
```
Benchmarks. Each point is preceded by a discarded warmup with a different seed. `--num-prompts` is max(32, 4×concurrency) for random and max(16, 4×concurrency) for MT-Bench.
```bash
# random
vllm bench serve --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code --backend vllm \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 1234 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
# MT-Bench
vllm bench serve --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path philschmid/mt-bench --skip-chat-template \
  --hf-output-len 1024 --temperature 0 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 1234
# accuracy
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,model=amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4,num_concurrent=4,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 1234
```
### Limitations / follow-ups
- Spec decoding is refused in this PR. The stock path is about 1.6× faster than `--monokernel` 
- TP4 only. TP2 and TP8 are follow-ups.
- At 16 rows the kernel is at parity

title: [ROCm][Build][3/5] Speed up ROCm build: split the skinny GEMMs per kernel family and trim torch headers
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

**Splits `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu` on one item - the kernel family (#15830 landed the file, #33762, #34304 and #40687 added kernels).**

`csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu` holds four unrelated kernel families (LLMM1, wvSplitK, wvSplitKrc, wvSplitKQ) whose device code generation was serialized on one core (~58 s). Move the kernels to a header, give each family its own translation unit, and stop pulling `<torch/all.h>` into kernel headers.

`main` already contains #62475, so this PR is a single commit on top of it. Part of a 5-PR series with #62716 (paged attention), #62717 (topk softplus-sqrt), #63364 (int4 skinny GEMM) and #63365 (fused MUSE-Spark op); the gain is joint, see *Validation*. #62716 and #63364 have since landed in `main` and are merged into this branch, so the int4 unit is already split here.

The single-arch rows are `pip install -e .` on MI350 (gfx950); the 9-arch row is the `setup.py bdist_wheel` described under *Validation*. All cold builds:

| build | `main` | this PR | All 5 PRs (#62921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_JOBS=16`, gfx950 only | 107 s | 110 s | 87 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, gfx950 only | 85 s | 85 s | 50 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, 9 archs | 1263 s | 1248 s | 472 s |

## Claims

- Splits the skinny GEMM launchers per kernel family, so the four families compile in parallel instead of on one core; the largest unit drops from 58.3 s to 43.4 s.
- Trims `<torch/all.h>` from the launcher units: `rocm/quickreduce/custom_quickreduce.cu` goes from 30.4 s to 20.1 s.
- The skinny GEMMs stop being a straggler, which is what lets the attention and topk gains of the series show up in the wall clock.
- Nothing about what runs changes: 528 of the 534 launcher-body lines are byte-identical to the old file, no numerics change.

- The kernels and launchers are unchanged: 528 of the 534 launcher-body lines are byte-identical to the old file, and the 6 remaining lines are the two includes moved into `wvSplitKQ` plus the four workspace-pool constants moved into `wvSplitKrc`. No numerics change.
- The skinny GEMMs stop being a straggler, which is what lets the series' attention and topk gains show up in the wall clock.

### Why five PRs

The two builds are bound by different things, so no single change moves both.

**Why the three single-arch PRs are all needed.** At 1 arch (`gfx950`, `MAX_JOBS=64`, `main` = 85 s) three groups take turns setting the wall, in this order:

1. topk softplus-sqrt (#62717) - 74.5 s, a single unit
2. paged attention (#62716) - 71.6 s, the slowest of 12 units
3. other skinny GEMMs (#62718) - 40.9 s, a single unit

#62717 takes (1) to 7.4 s, #62716 takes (2) to 31.1 s and #62718 stops (3) from becoming the next tail; with all three the tail moves to `selective_scan_fwd` (37.7 s) and the build goes from 85 s to 49 s. Drop any one of them and a ~70 s unit is back at the top, so the single-arch win needs all three.

**Why that is not enough at 9 archs.** A 9-arch build multiplies every unit's time by ~9, and the tail becomes two files that none of the first three touch: `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` at 1232 s and `csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` at 478 s. All three merged take the 9-arch build from 1263 s to only 1253 s. #63364 split the first (its tail drops to 448 s; that PR has landed) and #63365 the second (to 171 s), which is what reaches 472 s.

The `skinny_gemms_int4.cu` tail (now a `.cuh` plus one unit per `N_in`, after #63364) is invisible in a `gfx950` build because that file **only emits its kernels for RDNA (that is part of the 9-arch build)**:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L17-L19
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L568-L579

`csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` fails differently: it has no arch guard, so a `gfx950` build compiles it for real - it is just 25 s there against 478 s across nine archs, which is why a single-arch profile ranks it as irrelevant (#63365).

| slowest unit per group, 1 arch (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| topk softplus-sqrt | 74.5 s | 7.4 s |
| paged attention | 71.6 s | 31.1 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | 40.9 s | 31.6 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 36.5 s | 37.7 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 25.0 s | 10.9 s |
| int4 skinny GEMM | 19.4 s | 17.5 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **76 s / 15.8x** | **39 s / 30.2x** |

| slowest unit per group, 9 archs (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| int4 skinny GEMM | 1232 s | 448 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 478 s | 171 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 288 s | 296 s |
| paged attention | 284 s | 286 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | not recorded | 247 s |
| topk softplus-sqrt | not recorded | 99 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **1234 s / 8.7x** | **472 s / 25x** |

## Validation

### Single arch build

```bash
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx950" VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=N \
  pip install --no-cache-dir -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation
```

 MI350 (gfx950), four builds run one after the other in the same container, each from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so` and `build/` removed first), so every number is a cold build with no ccache and no shared CMake cache. Run-to-run variance is a few seconds, so the single-PR rows are indicative:

| | MAX_JOBS=16 | MAX_JOBS=64 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`main`, `f4edf9f0f0`) | 107 s | 85 s |
| #62716 paged attention 089bbaf68a | 92 s (−14 %) | 86 s (≈0 %) |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 107 s (≈0 %) | 85 s (≈0 %) |
| **this PR** (`78a62ceb1c`) | **110 s (+3 %)** | **85 s (≈0 %)** |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | 109 s (+2 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| #63365 fused MUSE-Spark 31de254fe4 | 108 s (+1 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | 87 s (−19 %) | 50 s (−41 %) |

Environment, one host: AMD EPYC 9575F (64 cores / 256 threads), 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (251 GiB each), ROCm 10.0, `torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950`, `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED=0`.

| check | configuration | result |
|---|---|---|
| moved code identity | scripted diff of the 4 launcher bodies and the header against `main` | 528 of 534 launcher-body lines byte-identical; header 1989 of 2035 lines byte-identical |
| `LLMM1` | fp16/bf16, M=16, K=4096 | rel. err 3e-3 (bf16) |
| `wvSplitK` / `wvSplitKrc` / `wvSplitKQ` vs torch matmul | fp16/bf16, k up to 4096, the N range each kernel supports (<=5, >=16, <=4) | rel. err 3e-4 (fp16), 3e-3 (bf16) |
| fresh configure + full build | from a clean tree | configure + build + link OK |

Repo tests for the kernels this PR touches:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_skinny_gemms.py tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py
```

`2519 passed, 636 skipped, 14 warnings in 223.85s (0:03:43)` — identical to `main` on the same host (`2519 passed, 636 skipped`).

The +1.1 MB is the per-family duplication of the now-inline helpers; sizes are RelWithDebInfo (debug info dominates).

### 9 archs build

The multi-arch wheel build with the 9 release archs of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, mold as the linker and sccache disabled, from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so`, `build/` and `dist/` removed first):

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" \
  PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151" \
  VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=64 \
  python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist
```

The 9 release archs, one build at a time, same container and same command:

| build | wall time | wheel |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`f4edf9f0f0`) | 1263 s | 266 MB |
| #62716 paged attention 089bbaf68a | 1261 s | 275 MB |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 1243 s | 269 MB |
| **this PR** (`78a62ceb1c`) | **1248 s** | **266 MB** |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | **600 s (−52 %)** | **257 MB** |
| #63365 fused MUSE-Spark 31de254fe4 | **1241 s (−2 %)** | **266 MB** |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | **472 s (−63 %)** | **270 MB** |

At 9 archs the build is translation-unit-latency bound, not link bound: every host link is sub-second, while a handful of single units run for most of the wall (`skinny_gemms_int4.hip.o` alone is 1232 s of a 1234 s span). So a single PR does not move the 9-arch wall; that is expected, this PR's win is at 1 arch. It also does not make the 9-arch wheel any bigger. Pre-reland `main` (`db3b0f0fae`, i.e. #62475 without `--offload-compress`) fails this exact build with `mold: error: ... relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against .eh_frame out of range`, the failure #62983 reverted for.

## Details

Four kernel families with no code in common shared one translation unit, so `LLMM1` waited for `wvSplitKQ`'s device code generation and vice versa; the file was the second slowest unit of a ROCm build and became the slowest one as soon as the paged attention units were split.

The kernels and their shared helpers move to `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cuh`, and `skinny_gemms_{llmm1,wvsplitk,wvsplitkrc,wvsplitkq}.cu` each keep one host launcher. The five file-scope helpers (`get_lds_size`, `on_gfx1x`, `on_gfx12`, `on_gfx1151`, `mindiv`) become `inline` so the header can be included by several units, and CMake gains a single `VLLM_SKINNY_SRC` list used by the extension sources, by the `_rocm_C_skinny` object library and by the existing gfx1250 exclusion (which used to name the two files three times).

`<torch/all.h>` drags autograd, nn and jit into every kernel unit, and the header also included `rocm/dispatch_utils.h` - which includes `<torch/all.h>` itself - without using any of its FP8 dispatch macros. `skinny_gemms.cuh` now uses `<torch/types.h>` and no longer includes `dispatch_utils.h`; `skinny_gemms_wvsplitkq.cu` includes `dispatch_utils.h` (for `VLLM_DISPATCH_FP8_TYPES`) and `quantization/w8a8/fp8/common.cuh` (for `is_fp8_ocp()`) itself, and `custom_quickreduce.cu` switches to `<torch/types.h>`.

**Diagnostics change (the only one).** The arch-`#else` stubs in the header now `__builtin_trap()` instead of hitting a device `assert` with file/line (the old code `#undef`/`#define`d `NDEBUG` around `<assert.h>` to keep the assert live, which is order-dependent now that the file is a header). Those stubs are never launched - they exist so that the arch-specific `#if` in the launchers has something to call - so the difference only shows up if that invariant is ever violated.

**Naming and references.** The rename is followed through everywhere it leaks out of the build: the `.buildkite` `source_file_dependencies` entries that used to name `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu` (which would have silently stopped triggering `test_rocm_gemm_rs_ar.py`) now list the new family units, and the `TORCH_CHECK` hint, the `vllm/` comments that point at the source (`layers/utils.py`, `v1/worker/utils.py`), the test comment and `torch_bindings.cpp` now name `skinny_gemms_wvsplitkrc.cu` / `skinny_gemms.cuh`. Those two lists are the only `.buildkite` change: the `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` entry stays as it was, so this PR does not change which int4 files trigger the step.

**Header hygiene.** `skinny_gemms.cuh` is now included by four units, so the pieces that used to be file-local were made safe for that: SPDX header, `#ifndef` guards around the `__HIP__GFX9__`/`__HIP__GFX1X__`/`__HIP__MI3XX__`/`LDS_SIZE` macros, `#undef LDS_SIZE` at the end of the header (the int4 unit defines its own, different value), `UNREACHABLE_CODE` is `__builtin_trap()` instead of an `#undef`/`#define NDEBUG` dance around `<assert.h>` (which used to depend on include order), and the inline helpers carry a note that their function-local statics are now one object per program rather than one per translation unit. `kWvSlots`/`kWvCaptureSlots` moved next to their only user, and the four launcher units keep a one-line header.

**How the file got this big.** Four PRs added kernels to `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu` (created by #15830), all in one TU:

| PR | landed | what it added |
|---|---|---|
| #15830 | 2025-04-21 | the file: 11 `__global__` kernels across the llmm1 / wvsplitk / wvsplitkrc / wvsplitkq families, 27 templates |
| #33762 | 2026-02-28 | 3 padded-stride kernel variants |
| #34304 | 2026-03-10 | 1 more kernel variant |
| #40687 | 2026-05-28 | the N=5 arm |

Arch support (#34709 for gfx1x, #40037 for gfx1102/gfx1103) multiplied those kernels by more targets without adding any, and the rest of the history (#33493, #34410, #34100, #40784, #56098, #60721) is tuning, workspace and header work. So 15 kernels ended up in one TU, which is why splitting by family is enough: they barely share code any more.

### Left to do

Follow-ups identified while doing this, deliberately out of scope:

- [ ] Guard the host-only ATen includes and launcher bodies with `__HIP_DEVICE_COMPILE__`: the device pass still parses them (10.5 s of the 43.4 s unit) although the kernels only need `c10::Half`/`BFloat16`/`Float8_e4m3fn`.
- [ ] Split `wvSplitk` by dtype: it is still the largest unit (43.4 s, of which ~32 s is codegen) and the frontend floor per unit is ~20 s, so the trade-off improved but did not disappear.
- [ ] `<torch/all.h>` still comes in via `rocm/dispatch_utils.h` for ~50 other TUs; trimming it there needs a CUDA build check.
- [ ] The `_rocm_C` extension holds `_rocm_C_skinny` as an object library; with the families split, giving each its own target would let `MAX_JOBS` scheduling prioritise the big ones.
- [ ] Not done here on purpose: splitting `skinny_gemms.cuh` into a common header plus per-family kernel headers (the per-unit parse cost is real, ~20 s for the ~2000-line header, but it is unchanged by this PR and the split adds churn).
- [ ] Not done here on purpose: new tests (the existing `test_rocm_skinny_gemms.py` already covers all four families: 2519 passed, 636 skipped) and an execution run on gfx1100/gfx942 - a gfx1250-only configure and a gfx1030 compile were done instead.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Serve gfx942 MLA verify past 4 tokens with a Triton kernel
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Route causal verify longer than 4 tokens on CDNA3 (no DCP) to a new Triton verify kernel in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`; shorter verify, decode, prefill, DCP and gfx950 keep their current paths.
- Add `decode_attention_fwd_verify` to `triton_decode_attention.py`: one program reads each KV tile once for a block of a request's (token, head) rows, with a per-row causal limit, int64 page offsets and FP8 dequant. Its variants are compiled before serving, so ngram drafts of any length never JIT mid-request.
- Undo the FP8 V-scale drop of AITER's qlen 2-4 FP8 decode kernel (ROCm/aiter#6732), found by a one-time probe, so a fixed AITER turns the correction off by itself.
- Apply the per-TP head override of `test_mla_backends.py` on ROCm as well (it was XPU only), so ROCm CI tests real per-rank head counts instead of 128 heads at every TP.
- Below page size 8 with bf16, read the block table one tile ahead instead of two: above 2 GiB of KV, Triton's global-load variant of the kernel otherwise spills VGPRs (2.1-3.1x slower at `--block-size 1`).
- Add an op test for the new kernel (bf16 and FP8, pages 1 and 16, ragged, padded and varlen rows).

On MI300X, MTP or ngram with 4 or more draft tokens fails at startup: AITER's persistent bf16 MLA decode only has kernels up to 4 query tokens, and its non-persistent kernels are not a safe fallback. They return wrong results at 32 heads, ignore the causal mask at 64/128 heads, and at 16 heads (what padded ranks such as TP2 of a 16-head model use today) read the wrong KV pages once the cache passes 4 GiB (ROCm/aiter#6733). That last case is silent: DeepSeek-V2-Lite at TP2 with k=7 drops to GSM8K 0.004 once serving fills the cache past 4 GiB, and goes back to 0.605 with this PR. Raising an error instead (as #57642 does) would leave MTP 4+ unusable on MI300 and break the gfx942 DCP verify routes that work today. This fixes item 1 of #55609 and needs no AITER change to be correct.

**Still open on the AITER side (not blocking this PR, but blocking a fully green `test_mla_backends.py` on MI300):**
- ROCm/aiter#6731: the persistent `_ps` decode kernel returns wrong output in about 1 of 1000 calls (a race). ROCm/aiter#6277 (open) brings it to 6 bad calls in 250k but not to zero. In 30 runs of the whole file on this branch it shows up as an occasional `ROCM_AITER_MLA` mismatch on unchanged decode paths.
- ROCm/aiter#6735, fixed by ROCm/aiter#6748 (rounds CK forward attention to nearest): `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[...glm...]` fails on main and on this branch because CK's FMHA forward truncates bf16; it passes 100/100 seeds with that change.
- ROCm/aiter#6732, ROCm/aiter#6733: the FP8 V-scale and the non-persistent kernel bugs worked around here.

**Results** (MI300X, AITER v0.1.25, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, ngram drafts; `vllm bench serve`, mean of 2 runs, output tok/s):

| config | workload | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP1, no spec | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 281 / 2046 | 280 / 2001 |
| TP1, no spec | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | 259 / 3202 | 258 / 3100 |
| TP1, k=3 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 306 / 2507 | 315 / 2669 |
| TP1, k=7 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | startup fails | 339 / 2700 |
| TP1, k=7 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | startup fails | 325 / 3201 |
| TP2, k=7 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 356 / 3042 | 370 / 3264 |
| TP2, k=7 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | 324 / 3557 | 369 / 3766 |

The c32 differences without spec decode are within this host's run-to-run noise (the same path runs on both). GSM8K 5-shot (lm_eval, 1319) is 0.647-0.663 for every config on both branches, and the TP2 k=7 0.004 above is the >4 GiB case.

**Against the per-token row-view** (what gfx942 DCP verify uses: one row per draft token through the generic split-KV kernel). MI300X, AITER v0.1.27, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, ngram k=7, TP1, one server at a time on the same GPU, output tok/s:

| | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 426 / 3864 | 490 / 4606 |
| row-view, launch config and splits tuned for gfx942 | 400 / 3520 | 454 / 4086 |
| row-view, as it ships | 290 / 3385 | 313 / 3511 |

Per layer, with both kernels in HIP graphs on identical inputs and a production-size KV pool, row-view is 1.8-4.6x slower as it ships and 1.44x slower on geomean when tuned (0.96-2.4x across 16-128 heads and batch 1-64). The c1 gap over tuned row-view (6-8%) is outside this host's noise; at c32 this PR is ahead in every round run, but by less than the c32 run-to-run spread. TP2 and k=5 show the same ordering, and GSM8K is 0.648-0.668 on every arm.

Tests: `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py -k verify` (48 passed; 10/10 runs with the page-size fix), `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` 30 times: every run passes all spec-decode and verify cases (634 passed). The two remaining failures are both AITER-side and listed above: `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[...auto-glm...]` fails in all 30 runs (max diff 0.031, identical on `TRITON_MLA`, the CK prefill), and 8 of 30 runs have one FP8 `large_decode` (qlen 1, unchanged decode path) `ROCM_AITER_MLA` mismatch of 0.16-0.39 from the persistent-kernel race. On main the 16 `spec_decode_medium` cases fail every run with `cannot get heuristic kernel ... qseqlen:8`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [ROCm][CI][Bug] Remove padding from AITER output for quantization/tes…
author: qli88
body:
## Overview

When using VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 as default, 2 test cases will fail:

quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py::test_online_shared_expert_loads_bf16_weights_into_mxfp4_slot;
quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py::test_online_shared_expert_reload_compatibility.
The cause is: previously VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0, so this test used Triton MoE backend, which doesn't have padding in results; now it uses AITER MoE backend, which returns results with padding. We need to remove the padding before we can compare the results.

## Claims

Now this test is able to handle possible padding in the returned results, so no matter VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 or 0, the test always finishes successfully.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Read resident prefill rows by request state slot
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse's resident prefill conversion lazily gathers a batch-ordered copy of the residency table inside the layer-0 conversion. The gather is queued after `logical_topk_ready`, but the side-stream converter waits only on that event, so it can read the table before it's written.

This PR removes the gathered table. The sparse-MLA index remap kernel gets an optional `idx_mapping` indirection, off for other callers, and HiSparse passes its persistent residency table plus `request_state_indices` directly. Both are written before the forward, so the existing event orders them. Residency is stored group-major, so each group's view is a contiguous table.

Alternative to #62401, which keeps the gather and adds a layer-0 `wait_stream`.

## Test Result

- `test_hisparse_resident_prefill_reads_residency_by_state_row` reproduces the race: it fails on main (3/3 runs) and passes here.
- HiSparse unit and e2e tests pass.
- With JIT monitoring on, the new variant is never compiled after warmup.

**End to end:** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 8×B200 TP8, HiSparse, mean of 2 reps, change vs main. Greedy outputs are byte-identical.

| workload | c | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16k in / 1k out | 16 | −0.2% | −0.3% | +0.5% |
| 16k in / 1k out | 64 | +0.0% | +1.1% | −0.4% |
| 4k in / 64 out | 16 | +1.3% | −0.3% | −2.4% |
| 4k in / 64 out | 64 | +0.1% | −0.1% | −0.1% |

**Kernel:** speedup vs main for the HiSparse conversion. H200, top-k 2048, 256 max requests, 61 resident groups, CUDA graph timing. Other sparse-MLA callers are unchanged (0.94–1.09× across the sweep).

| query tokens | 512 pages | 2048 pages | 8192 pages |
|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 1 | 2.08× | 2.25× | 2.86× |
| 128 | 2.02× | 2.15× | 2.52× |
| 1024 | 1.33× | 1.35× | 1.53× |
| 8192 | 1.02× | 1.02× | 1.06× |
| 16384 | 0.98× | 0.98× | 1.01× |
| 32768 | 0.98× | 0.97× | 0.99× |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```sh
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -k "hisparse or index_group or sparse_mqa or convert or remap or residency"

vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-model-len <ISL+OSL+1024> \
```

title: [Perf][Kernel] mHC TileLang: skip Sinkhorn on non-finite padding rows; single-pass fused post+pre for <=4 tokens
author: suiyoubi
body:
## Overview

Two small mHC TileLang changes in `vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang_kernels.py` that speed up low-batch decode for GLM-5.3-Flash (hidden 4096, hc_mult 4):

1. `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` skips the remaining Sinkhorn iterations when a row's RMS is non-finite. Output is bit-exact. CUDA-graph padding rows reach this kernel as NaN; the root cause is below.
2. `mhc_fused_post_pre_split_config` uses a single-pass config (tile_n 2, 16 splits, 256 threads) for <= 4 tokens when `hidden_size == 4096`. on CUDA devices with compute capability >= 10.0 (where it was tuned). SM90, older GPUs and the ROCm TileLang fallback keep the existing configs.

Related: #61461 tunes the same function for SM90 (H20). This PR targets hidden 4096 on Blackwell and SM107; both changes speed up both. The numbers below are for Blackwell (GB300, RTX PRO 6000). 

## Claims

- **Fused mHC post + pre op** (one per sublayer boundary, ~89 calls per GLM-5.3-Flash decode step), clean rows: **1.08-1.19x** at 1-3 tokens on GB300 and RTX PRO 6000, 0.99-1.05x at 4 tokens, unchanged from 5 tokens on.
- **Decode batches smaller than their CUDA-graph size:** the mHC ops on the padded batch are **1.2-1.55x** faster, saving ~3 us on each of ~89 calls per padded step. Clean rows are unchanged.
- **SM107:** both changes are also faster there, at 1-4 tokens and on padded batches, with the same numerics. 
- **Numerics:**
  - Change 1 is bit-exact for all inputs.
  - Change 2 only reorders an fp32 split-sum: post/comb differ by at most 2.4e-7, and `layer_input` is bit-identical in the kernel A/B.
  - GSM8K (5-shot, greedy, 1319 questions) on a GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 server with both changes stayed within the baseline's run-to-run spread (91.2% vs 91.8%; baseline spread 1.0 pt).

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/kernels/mhc` on GB300 and on RTX PRO 6000. The branch's mHC files were overlaid onto a nightly image, and the same harness was run on `main`.
- All of `test_mhc_jit_warmup.py` and `test_mhc_tilelang_jit.py` pass on both GPUs. This includes the new band cases (1 and 4 tokens -> (2, 16, 256); 5 tokens -> (2, 8, 128)) and the warmup-input check for the new compile key.
- GB300: 278 passed with this PR vs 275 on `main`.
- The remaining errors are identical on `main`: DSv4.1 tests that need `tests/conftest.py` fixtures the out-of-tree harness lacked.

**Kernel A/B:** CUDA-graph median per op. Input sets are rotated so the projection weights are not all L2-resident. A/A control within 0.05 us. "1/8 rows NaN" emulates CUDA-graph padding.

| tokens | GB300 main -> PR (us) | RTX PRO 6000 main -> PR (us) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.91 -> 6.22 (1.11x) | 5.69 -> 4.77 (1.19x) |
| 2 | 6.98 -> 6.42 (1.09x) | 5.66 -> 5.12 (1.11x) |
| 3 | 7.24 -> 6.73 (1.08x) | 5.79 -> 5.46 (1.06x) |
| 4 | 7.43 -> 7.49 (0.99x) | 6.03 -> 5.73 (1.05x) |
| 8 | 7.89 -> 7.90 | 6.69 -> 6.69 |
| 8, 1/8 rows NaN | 11.20 -> 8.32 (1.35x) | 9.12 -> 6.70 (1.36x) |
| 128, 1/8 rows NaN | 15.68 -> 12.95 (1.21x) | 13.85 -> 11.10 (1.25x) |

**Config choice:** other configs were swept at 1-4 tokens. (4, 16, 256) is ~1.1x flatter across 2-4 tokens but slower at 1 token. (2, 16, 256) is kept because it is the fastest at one token (C1 decode) and is never meaningfully slower.

**End to end on GB300**:
- Setup: GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4, agg TP4, `vllm serve` behind the Dynamo frontend, sa-bench ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, `random_range_ratio 1.0`, 10 × C prompts. FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE with autotune, FP8 KV cache, max-num-batched-tokens 32768.
- Baseline: the nightly image at 1b2a666, whose `tilelang_kernels.py` is identical to `main`. "This PR" = the same image with only this PR's `tilelang_kernels.py`.
- 3 runs per arm, each on its own node; all requests completed.

| concurrency | main: tok/s/user (range), TPOT | this PR: tok/s/user (range), TPOT | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 216.5 (215.5-217.1), 4.48 ms | 228.9 (228.4-229.7), 4.23 ms | **+5.8%** |
| 6 | 151.3 (150.8-151.7), 6.12 ms | 156.4 (156.0-156.5), 5.90 ms | **+3.4%** |

- C1 has no CUDA-graph padding, so its gain comes from change 2 alone.
- C6 runs every decode step in the 8-token graph, which is above the 4-token band, with 2 padding rows. So its gain comes from change 1 alone. It matches the kernel saving (~3 us x ~89 calls).
- The C1 gain (0.25 ms per step) is larger than the isolated-kernel saving (~0.06 ms per step). We see the same ratio on SM107. We have not profiled why.
- TTFT is unchanged.
- At concurrencies that exactly fill a graph (e.g. 8, 32, 128) neither change applies, so no gain is expected there. On SM107 we measured none.

## Details

**Why padding rows are non-finite (root cause).**
- In GLM-5.3-Flash, layer 0 is a KDA layer.
- `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` returns early for `NULL_BLOCK_ID` slots (CUDA-graph padding) without storing its output.
- Those rows of `core_attn_out` (`torch.empty`) therefore keep stale graph-pool memory, and the padding rows are non-finite from layer 1 on.
- An nsys trace of a padded decode step matches this: the layer-0 mHC pre runs at clean speed, and every later one is slower by the same amount.
- In `pre_big_fuse`, the Sinkhorn then runs ~40 IEEE divisions on NaN in its serial warp-0 chain, each taking the slow path.

**Why the guard is bit-exact.** A non-finite RMS already makes the whole comb result NaN, so skipping the remaining iterations changes nothing. Real rows are unaffected: every op on this path is row-local, and padding outputs are discarded.

**Scope.**
- The guard also covers other sources of non-finite padding, such as other attention backends and the DSv4 delayed mHC path.
- Writing zeros for null slots in the FLA recurrent kernels, as the packed-decode kernel already does, is the complementary source-side fix. It affects all GDN/KDA hybrids and will be proposed separately.

**Why one pass helps at <= 4 tokens.**
- With 8 splits x 128 threads over hidden 4096, each thread makes four serial load passes. At 1-4 tokens the grid (96 CTAs per token) is too small to hide their latency.
- Twice the splits with 256 threads gives each thread a single pass. From 5 tokens on, the existing (2, 8, 128) config is as fast or faster.
- The band is limited to hidden 4096; DeepSeek-V4's 5120/7168 configs are untouched.
- It is gated to SM100+ because that is where it was measured. The mechanism (latency hiding at tiny grids) is generic, but #61461 found a different optimum on SM90, so other architectures keep their current configs.
- It adds one compile key. Warmup now compiles it together with the (2, 8, 128) key, which the old `warmup_inputs` never selected (it JIT-compiled at runtime for 5-15 tokens).

title: [Perf][MRV2] Skip idle sampler staged writes
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Remove two host costs that Model Runner V2 pays on every decode step: re-flushing all sampler staged writes when no request was admitted, and allocating a pinned staging tensor for each per-step H2D copy in `prepare_inputs`.

## Claims

- B=1 decode step on `facebook/opt-125m` (B300, TP1): **1217 → 1078 µs (−11%)**; B=8: 1342 → 1215 µs (−10%).
- B=1 decode step on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` (`language_model_only`): **1790 → 1605 µs (−10%)**.
- No change in outputs: greedy tokens are identical to main, with and without ngram speculative decoding.

## Validation

Decode step = (T(1024 output tokens) − T(1 token)) / 1023 through the offline `LLM` API, greedy, `ignore_eos`, 128-token random prompts, median of 5 reps per run. Configurations were interleaved over 3 rounds on one B300. At these sizes the step is host-bound, so the step time is effectively the engine's host floor.

| config | main | this PR (gate only) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| opt-125m B=1 (3 runs) | 1210 / 1236 / 1205 | 1128 / 1156 / 1145 | 1068 / 1076 / 1092 |
| opt-125m B=8 (3 runs) | 1339 / 1355 / 1332 | 1272 / 1286 / 1276 | 1215 / 1202 / 1227 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B B=1 (2 runs) | 1772 / 1808 | — | 1615 / 1594 |

The "gate only" column is the first change alone; the pinned-buffer change accounts for the remaining ~65 µs.

- `ngram` speculative decoding (k=3), opt-125m B=1: 402 → 363 µs per output token, same greedy tokens.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` runs (plain decode and ngram) complete with no sync errors.
- Tests (B300):
  - `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logit_bias.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py` → 33 passed.
  - `pytest tests/v1/logits_processors/test_custom_offline.py` → 12 passed.

## Details

**Idle sampler staged writes.** #36824 moved `sampler.apply_staged_writes()` out of the `if scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs:` branch when it added the non-last-PP-rank `None` check.
- Every step since then re-copies each `UvaBackedTensor` of the sampling states (temperature, top-k/p, min-p, seeds, logit bias, min tokens, stop tokens, logprob ids, …) into a fresh UVA buffer: ~16 full `max_num_reqs` copies per step, ~125 µs.
- All sampler writes are staged by `Sampler.add_request()`, and its only caller is the `scheduled_new_reqs` loop in `add_requests`. Flushing them only on steps that admit requests is therefore exactly equivalent.
- `LogitsProcessor.apply_staged_writes()` (#56497) documented "called once per step". That docstring now states the actual contract: called before the forward of every step that admits requests.

**Per-step pinned allocations.** `prepare_inputs` copied `idx_mapping`, `cu_num_logits` and `query_start_loc` with `async_tensor_h2d`, which allocates a pinned staging tensor per call (~40 µs each).
- They now go through three persistent `UvaBufferPool`s in `InputBuffers`.
- These use the same round-robin contract (depth ≥ in-flight steps) as `UvaBackedTensor` and `StagedWriteTensor`, so the async-safety argument is unchanged.

**Not duplicate work.**
- #62018 fuses admission-time staged writes into fewer kernels, and #62698 parallelizes `_apply_write_kernel`. Both reduce the cost of writes that are needed. This PR skips flushes that write nothing new.
- #59981 changes UVA/staging behavior for Confidential Computing and does not touch these call sites.

Context: part of an effort to lower the B=1 host floor of hybrid Qwen3.5/3.8 decode, measured at ~1.8 ms/step on B300.

title: [Quantization] Block Hadamard input rotation for linear layers: online `mxfp4_hadamard32` and Quark online-rotation checkpoints
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Overview

Adds `InputHadamardLinearMethod`, which wraps any linear method and rotates the layer input by an orthonormal block Hadamard matrix in PyTorch before the wrapped `apply`, in the manner of `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod`. Rotating each block of the input dimension of both operands leaves the GEMM unchanged, \((xH)(WH)^T = xW^T\), while spreading outliers across the block, which shrinks block-scaled quantization error. Two producers use it:

- Online quantization: `QuantSpec.hadamard_size` and the shorthand `mxfp4_hadamard32` (also per layer through `--quantization-config.targets`). The wrapper rotates the weight once before the online method quantizes it.
- Quark MXFP4 checkpoints exported with an online rotation: the weights are stored rotated and each layer carries an int8 `input_rotation` (the +-1 Sylvester matrix), which is checked and dropped.

The wrapper doesn't depend on the weight format, the backend or the platform. Paths that haven't been validated raise `NotImplementedError` with a TODO: online methods other than MXFP4 linear, MoE, online rotation on top of a checkpoint that is already quantized, Quark formats other than MXFP4, and non-Sylvester rotations.

Follow-up: #63272 lets kernels rotate inside their activation quant instead of in PyTorch (AITER's HIP MXFP4 quant, ROCm/aiter#6734). It removes the serving cost of the PyTorch rotation measured under Limitations below.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "hadamard", "online rotation", "input_rotation" and "rotation mxfp4".
- #32272 also loads Quark online-rotation checkpoints, covering OCP MX, FP8, INT8 and trained rotations. It has needed a rebase since February, and its last code change was in April. It has no online path. If it lands first, the Quark part here can move onto its loader.
- #54006 adds MXFP4 Hadamard rotation for AutoRound checkpoints on XPU.

## Why not compressed-tensors' `HadamardTransform`

`CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod` is the closest existing logic, and the wrapper follows its pattern: wrap the scheme's method, transform the input before `apply`, and hand the v1 weight loader to wrapped methods that aren't in `WEIGHT_LOADER_V2_SUPPORTED`. Its `HadamardTransform` can't be reused as it is:
- It raises `NotImplementedError` for tensor parallelism above 1, and the target model runs at TP8.
- It loads the transform matrices from the checkpoint as `SharedWeightParameter`s. Online quantization has no matrices to load, and Quark stores a +-1 matrix with a different name and scale.
- It applies the transform with `ops.hadacore_transform`, a CUDA sm80+ kernel with no ROCm or CPU build.
- It is configured with compressed-tensors types (`TransformScheme`, `TransformArgs`).

Generalizing `HadamardTransform` to cover these would be a larger change to compressed-tensors. This PR keeps a small, format-agnostic wrapper that compressed-tensors could later route through.

## Claims

- On Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Quark MXFP4 (TP8, MI355X), `mxfp4_hadamard32` on the GDN projections, compared with round-to-nearest (RTN) online MXFP4 on the same layers:
  - GSM8K: reasoning chains 4.7% shorter, and 140 answers fixed against 98 broken (p = 0.0077).
  - Against BF16 projections: 2.6% longer, which is within the ±5% equivalence margin, and -0.2 accuracy points (p = 0.057).
  - GPQA Diamond: reasoning chains 9.6% shorter (mean ratio 0.904 [0.867, 0.942]), with accuracy unchanged within noise (93.1% vs 92.4% mean over 5 reps; +19 / -12 answers, p = 0.28).
- Quark MXFP4 checkpoints with an online rotation load and run.
  - Qwen3-0.6B exported with a size-32 rotation matches Quark's simulated quantization to a mean absolute per-token logprob difference of 0.69 to 0.81 in eager and compiled mode, against 12.4 with the rotation skipped.
  - Quark's public size-64 test checkpoint gives a wikitext word perplexity of 45.82, within the test's 45.9 ± 0.1. Without this PR it fails to load.

## Accuracy

Model: `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8 on MI355X. Its routed experts are MXFP4 in the checkpoint; the shared experts are online MXFP4 in every arm. Arms differ only in `--quantization-config.targets` for the three GDN projections (`in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z`, `out_proj`):
- **BF16**: unquantized, as shipped.
- **RTN MXFP4**: `mxfp4`.
- **This PR**: `mxfp4_hadamard32`.

Sampling is thinking-on at temperature 1.0. Within a rep, every arm gets the same per-question seed; the seed changes between reps. Length is completion tokens. Ratios are against BF16 unless stated: the mean ratio is total tokens over total tokens, the geomean is over per-question ratios, and the brackets are 95% bootstrap CIs over questions. For GSM8K, the mean ratio was the primary measure, with ±5% as the equivalence margin, both fixed before the runs. p-values are exact McNemar tests on per-question correctness, over all question-rep pairs.

**GPQA Diamond** (198 questions, 5 reps, max 100k tokens, simple-evals prompt and answer regex, choices shuffled with `random.Random(0)`), on this PR's code:

| GDN projections | Mean accuracy over reps (sd) | Per rep | Mean / median completion tokens | Mean length ratio vs BF16 | Per-question geomean | Fixed / broken vs BF16 | p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | 92.3% (1.3) | 92.4, 93.4, 93.4, 91.9, 90.4 | 12729 / 6608 | 1 | 1 | | |
| RTN MXFP4 | 92.4% (1.1) | 92.4, 90.9, 92.4, 93.9, 92.4 | 13232 / 7038 | 1.040 [1.002, 1.079] | 1.036 [1.005, 1.070] | +21 / -20 | 1.0 |
| This PR | 93.1% (0.6) | 92.9, 92.9, 93.9, 93.4, 92.4 | 11965 / 5958 | 0.940 [0.904, 0.977] | 0.926 [0.895, 0.955] | +20 / -12 | 0.22 |

- RTN MXFP4 against this PR: the rotation shortens completions by 9.6% (mean ratio 0.904 [0.867, 0.942], geomean 0.893 [0.863, 0.923]). It fixes 19 answers while breaking 12 (p = 0.28).
- The rotation removes the length MXFP4 adds, and doesn't shorten chains below BF16 in any meaningful sense
- 1 to 3 completions per arm hit the 100k-token limit or gave no answer.
- At 92 to 93%, the model is near the ceiling on GPQA Diamond too, so the accuracy columns can only show large regressions; the length ratios are the sensitive measure.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions, max 32k tokens).

| GDN projections | Reps | Mean length ratio vs BF16 | Per-question geomean | Accuracy (BF16 → arm) | Fixed / broken vs BF16 | p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTN MXFP4 | 8 | 1.122 [1.082, 1.167] | 1.073 [1.064, 1.082] | 0.9630 → 0.9586 | +95 / -142 | 0.0027 |
| This PR | 8 | 1.059 [1.018, 1.104] | 1.022 [1.013, 1.030] | 0.9630 → 0.9626 | +106 / -111 | 0.79 |
| This PR | 12, interleaved with BF16 | 1.026 [1.000, 1.052], equivalent within ±5% | 1.025 [1.019, 1.031] | 0.9634 → 0.9613 | +125 / -158 | 0.057 |

- RTN MXFP4 against this PR, from the same 8 reps: the rotation shortens completions by 4.7% (geomean CI [3.9%, 5.6%]), and fixes 140 answers while breaking 98 (p = 0.0077).
- The remaining length against BF16 is a uniform shift rather than a tail of runaway completions. The mean ratio is 1.020 to 1.024 with completions capped at 2k, 4k, 8k or 16k tokens. Completions longer than 4k tokens are as frequent as with BF16 (308 vs 302, p = 0.76).
- A single rep's mean ratio ranges from 0.97 to 1.12, so the per-question geomean is the steadier measure.

**Numerical check against Quark.** Qwen3-0.6B exported by Quark 0.12 as MXFP4, with an online size-32 rotation on q/k/v/gate/up. The table gives the absolute per-token prompt-logprob difference against Quark's simulated quantization on 8 prompts (241 tokens), on one MI355X:

| vLLM path | Mean | Max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eager, AITER Triton GEMM | 0.811 | 5.78 |
| eager, emulation kernel (`VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=AiterMxfp4LinearKernel`) | 0.811 | 5.78 |
| compiled, AITER Triton GEMM | 0.689 | 8.42 |
| eager, rotation skipped (control) | 12.42 | 28.59 |

## Validation

On one MI355X (gfx950), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-df3bd094aeea829f27baa0a5282830464f601d9f` (an ancestor of this PR's base) plus this PR. None of the files this PR touches differ between the two.

- `tests/quantization/test_input_hadamard.py`: 11 passed. The CPU tests run anywhere. The GPU test runs on MX hardware only, with the emulation and AITER MXFP4 kernels.
  - `test_block_hadamard_rotate_preserves_products`: fails if the rotation is not orthonormal.
  - `test_rotates_weight_once_and_input_on_apply`: fails if the weight is rotated twice when online methods process weights again, or if a v1 method loses its v1 weight loader.
  - `test_checkpoint_rotation_is_checked_and_dropped` and `test_rejects_non_sylvester_and_missing_rotation`: fail if a checkpoint rotation is accepted without being the Sylvester matrix `apply` uses, or if a missing one goes unnoticed.
  - `test_online_mxfp4_hadamard[Emulation/Aiter, 16/256 tokens]`: fails if the rotated layer stops matching the unrotated kernel on explicitly rotated operands, or stops lowering the error.
- `tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py`: 36 passed (CPU). `test_hadamard_size_not_implemented_for_unvalidated_methods` fails if a rotation is accepted on a path that isn't validated (FP8 linear, MXFP4 MoE).
- `tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py`: 15 passed, 4 skipped. It doesn't exercise the rotation, but checks that the online MXFP4 path still works.
- `test_quark_online_rotation_wikitext`: its `lm_eval` settings, run as a script, give 45.82 against an expected 45.9 ± 0.1. The previous revision gave 45.91 on an older nightly (5555a2d8). The rotation math is the same, and BF16 Qwen3-0.6B wikitext is unchanged between the two images (26.205 vs 26.204), so the 0.09 shift is unexplained.

**Reproduce:**

```bash
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_expert*": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_qkv": "mxfp4_hadamard32", "*linear_attn.in_proj_z": "mxfp4_hadamard32", "*linear_attn.out_proj": "mxfp4_hadamard32"}'
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=amd-quark/internal-testing-qwen3_0.6b-mxfp4-hadamard,add_bos_token=True --tasks wikitext
```

## Details

**Online path.**
- `QuantSpec.hadamard_size` (a power of two) makes `OnlineQuantizationConfig` return `InputHadamardLinearMethod(<online method>(), size, rotate_weight=True)`.
- Online methods may process weights twice (once after layerwise loading, once from the model loader), so the wrapper rotates the weight only while `_already_called_process_weights_after_loading` is unset.
- `_ONLINE_HADAMARD_LINEAR_METHODS` lists the validated online methods; only `Mxfp4OnlineLinearMethod` so far.

**Quark path.**
- `QuarkConfig.maybe_update_config` finds `*.input_rotation` tensors in the safetensors metadata when the config has a `rotation` algorithm. It rejects anything that isn't a square int8 matrix (trained rotations).
- `get_quant_method` wraps `QuarkLinearMethod` with `rotate_weight=False` for layers whose shards all share one rotation size.
- The wrapper registers `input_rotation`, checks on load that it is the Sylvester matrix of that size, and drops it after loading.

**Interaction with fusions.** The rotation is a separate op in front of the wrapped method's `apply`, so compile passes see it and can't drop it. A pass that fuses RMSNorm with the following linear's activation quant would have to keep the rotation in between.

**Limitations and CI gaps.**
- Validated with MXFP4 linear layers only, at sizes 32 (online) and 64 (Quark's test checkpoint). Other paths raise `NotImplementedError`.
- The rotation is an fp32 matmul on `(tokens, K / size, size)` per rotated layer, so it costs throughput here. TP8 serving, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Quark MXFP4, dummy weights, ISL/OSL 1024/1024, mean of 2 reps, rotation on the GDN projections (measured in #63272, which also has the fused arm):

  | GDN projections | Output tok/s c=4 | c=64 | c=256 | Mean TPOT ms c=4 | c=64 | c=256 |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | RTN `mxfp4` | 373.0 | 1807.1 | 4028.3 | 10.45 | 34.09 | 60.91 |
  | `mxfp4_hadamard32`, PyTorch rotation (this PR) | 326.9 (-12.4%) | 1694.4 (-6.2%) | 3787.7 (-6.0%) | 11.94 | 36.23 | 64.86 |

  #63272 moves the rotation into the activation quant on ROCm and brings it to within 1% of RTN (371.3, 1796.6 and 4024.2 tok/s).
- CI: AMD's quantization job runs on MI300 (gfx942, no MX), where the MX tests skip. The CPU tests run there and on NVIDIA. The MX paths, wikitext and the TP8 runs above were validated on MI355X outside CI.
- CUDA: nothing changes unless a rotation is requested. The rotation path is untested on NVIDIA hardware beyond the CPU tests.

title: [Quantization] Honor MoE activation override for Humming MXFP4
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

`--moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation <name>` was silently ignored for gpt-oss: the Humming conversion for `GptOssMxfp4MoEMethod` never received an input schema, so experts always ran with BF16 activations, and vLLM logged a misleading "Falling back to 'HUMMING' with BF16 activations". This PR passes the user's MoE activation override to Humming (gpt-oss, plus the shared MXFP4 converter).

Depends on vllm-project/humming#157 being released and the `humming-kernels` pin being bumped separately. Without that fix, Humming's MX group-scaled activations produce NaN rows whenever K is padded, which includes gpt-oss (hidden 2880, padded to 2944).

## Claims

- On gpt-oss, `--moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation {mxfp8,mxfp4,fp8_per_token}` now runs Humming with that activation format instead of BF16. Unsupported requests fail at load ("No compatible Humming input schema") instead of silently running BF16.
- The BF16-fallback warning no longer fires when Humming applies the user's override itself. It still fires when Humming really does run BF16, e.g. online MXFP4, whose W4A4 preference Humming does not apply.
- Adds GPQA coverage for Humming + MXFP8 on gpt-oss-20b to the optional B200 GPT-OSS eval job.

## Validation

GPT-OSS-20B on B300 (SM103). `humming` here is humming `main` plus vllm-project/humming#157.

GPQA (`tests/evals/gpt_oss/test_gpqa_correctness.py`, reasoning effort low, TP=2, threshold 0.568), using a local copy of the configs pointing at the `RedHatAI/gpt-oss-20b` mirror:

| Config | GPQA | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| `--moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8` (new config) | 0.5764, 0.5720 | 2 |
| `--quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8` (auto, FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP8, existing config) | 0.5663 | 1 |

Both pass (the harness uses threshold 0.568 with tolerance 0.05). In one of the two Humming runs, the harness's post-test GPU-memory wait (120 s) timed out after the score passed. The server and workers had exited cleanly, and a dedicated teardown check on the same config (serve, load, SIGTERM) released all GPU memory within 10 s, so I attribute it to the shared machine rather than this change.

GSM8K sanity check (first 200 test questions, reasoning low, TP=1), with the MoE path the engine actually selected, read back from the layer:

| Config | Before (main, humming 0.1.17) | After (this PR + humming#157) |
|---|---|---|
| `--moe-backend humming` | Humming, BF16 act: 0.475 | Humming, BF16 act: 0.535 |
| `... --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8` | Humming, **BF16 act** (override ignored): 0.480 | Humming, MXFP8 act: 0.535 |
| `... --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp4` | Humming, **BF16 act** (not scored) | Humming, MXFP4 act: 0.415 |
| `... --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token` | Humming, **BF16 act** (not scored) | Humming, FP8 per-token act: 0.530 (per-token scales are unaffected by humming#157; measured on 0.1.17) |
| `--quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8` (auto) | FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP8: 0.535 | unchanged |

With this PR but humming 0.1.17 (without #157), the MXFP8 and MXFP4 rows score 0/200 because of the humming padded-K bug described above.

Reproduce:

```bash
pytest -s -v tests/evals/gpt_oss/test_gpqa_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/models-b200.txt
vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b --moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8
```

## Details

- **Root cause:** `select_mxfp4_moe_backend` resolves the override, but `convert_gpt_oss_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format` called `convert_to_humming_moe_kernel_format` without an input schema, so Humming used its default (BF16, or `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG`). The Humming branch now builds the input schema from `_resolve_activation_key(None)`, mirroring the existing checkpoint-key handling in `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`. The env var still takes precedence, and input-schema fallback is off, so an explicit request is either honored or fails loudly.
- **Both converters share one helper:** `_humming_input_schema()` resolves the checkpoint key together with the override, replacing the checkpoint-only logic in `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`. Humming therefore applies exactly the user's override on every MXFP4 path, which is what makes the narrowed warning exemption correct. On online MXFP4, selection asks for W4A4 but Humming runs BF16 unless the user overrides, so the warning still fires there.
- **Relation to #59488:** that PR also changes the generic converter's Humming branch and additionally changes backend *selection* for `Mxfp4MoEMethod` models (DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3), which this PR does not touch. The two will conflict in that one hunk; whichever lands second can drop its version. This PR is needed independently because #59488 does not cover the gpt-oss path.
- **Override resolution timing:** the override is resolved from the current vLLM config during `process_weights_after_loading`. Both initial load and `reload_weights` run inside `set_current_vllm_config`.
- **CI:** the new config runs in the optional `(B200) GPQA Eval (GPT-OSS)` job and will fail there until the humming pin includes #157.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Count tool call deltas as generated tokens in openai-responses
author: dilberx
body:
## Overview

`vllm bench serve --backend openai-responses` marks every tool-call-only response as failed. It counts only `output_text` and `reasoning_text` deltas as tokens, and a forced tool call streams only `function_call_arguments` deltas. This counts the four tool delta events the vLLM Responses server emits, as `openai-chat` counts `tool_calls` deltas.

## Claims

- 100 tool calls the server completed with HTTP 200 went from 0 to 100 successful, with totals now identical to `openai-chat` on the same workload.
- Added events: `function_call_arguments`, `custom_tool_call_input`, `mcp_call_arguments`, `code_interpreter_call_code` (from `responses/streaming_events.py`). Tool arguments are timed but not added to `generated_text`, as on chat.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py`: a tool-call-only response (TTFT, ITL, usage, `latency - ttft == sum(itl)`), each tool delta type, and text followed by a tool call. 30 passed; the 6 new ones fail on `main` with "Never received a token delta". Timing tests (29) and pre-commit pass.

RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, 100 prompts, concurrency 16, `tool_choice: "required"` via `--extra-body`:

| | `main` | this branch | `openai-chat` |
|---|---|---|---|
| completed / failed | 0 / 100 | 100 / 0 | 100 / 0 |
| input / output tokens | 0 / 0 | 20,610 / 2,090 | 20,610 / 2,090 |

Per request, output tokens match the server's `usage` and ITL counts match the token events recorded on the wire.

## Details

#54628 added this backend with tool calls out of scope. Leaving them out fails the request, so tool-calling workloads such as the BFCL dataset (#42457) can't be measured on it. The Rust `vllm-bench` Responses backend has the same gap; I'll send that separately.

No issue or PR covers this. Open PRs touching `endpoint_request_func.py` (#51155, #55719, #57519, #58734) don't change these events.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this and write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.

title: [Quant] LUT-B MoE with MXFP8 activations: native Rubin kernel + emulation
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"mgoin"} -->


## Overview

Adds `--quantization lut_b_moe`: online LUT-B quantization of routed MoE experts with MXFP8 activations. On Rubin (SM 10.7) it runs a new native grouped GEMM built on `tcgen05.mma.kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale.decompress::lut::b`; every other GPU emulates the same numerics so accuracy can be checked without Rubin hardware.

This reworks #51880 on current main. That PR emulated LUT-B weights with BF16 activations, which Rubin cannot run natively (the LUT-B tensor core forms only take FP8/FP6/FP4 A), and it needed a fused Triton decode GEMM plus a dequantize fallback. This PR replaces it; #51880 can be closed. No other open PR touches LUT-B.

## Claims

- New `lut_b_moe` online scheme (MoE only, dense layers unquantized): 3-bit indices into an E4M3 codebook plus a UE8M0 exponent per 8x64 weight tile (3.14 bits/weight logical), MXFP8 activations (E4M3, UE8M0 per 1x32).
- Native Rubin path (`LutBSm107Experts` + `ops.lut_b_moe_gemm`): weights stay packed in memory and are decoded by the tensor core (`UTCQMMA.LUTB` in SASS). A deliberately simple kernel, not tuned for peak throughput.
- Emulation path (`LutBEmulationTritonExperts`): dequantize weights once at load, MXFP8 quantize-dequantize activations before each GEMM, run the existing BF16 `TritonExperts`. Selected automatically off Rubin, or with `--moe-backend emulation`.
- GLM-4.7-Flash on Rubin: GSM8K for native (0.839) and emulated (0.843) LUT-B agree within one standard error and sit about 1.5 points below BF16 (0.857). Loaded memory drops from 56.3 to 15.9 GiB (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: 65.5 to 18.6 GiB).

## Validation

All runs on one Rubin GPU (CC 10.7, CUDA 13.4, driver 615.22).

**Kernel/unit tests** (`tests/kernels/moe/test_lut_b_moe.py`, 14 tests, plus `test_quantization_config_args.py` and `test_online.py::test_online_lut_b_moe`): 46 passed on Rubin. They cover packing, the SM107 tile layout against an independent per-element decoder, emulation against a loop reference, one native grouped GEMM against an FP64 reference of the decoded operands, and native vs emulated full MoE for 1/33/300 tokens.

**GSM8K, reference model** zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash (lm_eval 0.4.13, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, non-thinking chat mode, `max_gen_toks=2048`, TP=1, one Rubin GPU):

| MoE weights / activations | MoE path | strict | flexible |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| BF16 / BF16 | `TritonExperts` (`moe_backend=triton`) | 0.857 ± 0.010 | 0.857 ± 0.010 |
| LUT-B / MXFP8 | emulated (`moe_backend=emulation`) | 0.844 ± 0.010 | 0.843 ± 0.010 |
| LUT-B / MXFP8 | native Rubin kernel | 0.839 ± 0.010 | 0.839 ± 0.010 |

<details>
<summary>Other models</summary>

Same settings except where noted.

| Model | BF16 Triton | LUT-B emulated | LUT-B native |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (flexible) | 0.954 | 0.958 | 0.957 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, `max_gen_toks=256` (flexible) | 0.890 | 0.883 | 0.871 |

Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 is saturated on GSM8K, so it cannot show a 1-2 point quantization loss. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is a thinking model: in plain-completion mode BF16 often opens a long `<think>` block that a 256-token limit truncates (flexible 0.33), so it needs non-thinking chat mode.
</details>

```bash
# native (Rubin)
lm_eval --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash,quantization=lut_b_moe,max_model_len=4096,enable_thinking=False,max_gen_toks=2048 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --batch_size auto
# emulated: same, plus moe_backend=emulation (automatic on non-Rubin GPUs)
```

Native and emulated agree within one standard error; both sit about 1.5 points below BF16.

**Layer timing** (one Qwen3.6 MoE layer: E=256, top-8, H=2048, I=512; CUDA graph replay, median of 50). The native path uses the mixed FP8/FP6/FP4 K64 LUT-B instruction family; the baseline is the unquantized BF16 `TritonExperts`. Times include MXFP8 activation quantization.

| tokens | LUT-B native (us) | BF16 Triton (us) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 25.2 | 19.3 |
| 4 | 39.7 | 37.7 |
| 16 | 80.3 | 105.4 |
| 64 | 153.9 | 151.7 |
| 256 | 172.9 | 239.7 |
| 1024 | 202.1 | 222.3 |
| 4096 | 358.8 | 327.6 |

## Details

**Format.** Same tile as #51880 (8 output channels x 64 K, eight E4M3 entries), plus one UE8M0 exponent per tile. The exponent maps onto the instruction's per-32-K B scale, which has to be supplied anyway, so it is free at runtime. Without it, small-magnitude tiles fall into the E4M3 subnormal grid: on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B experts (layers 0/10/20/39, gate_up and down) relative weight MSE is 0.038-0.040 with the exponent versus 0.044-0.045 without.

**Rubin kernel** (`csrc/moe/lut_b_moe_sm107.cu`, compiled only for `10.7f` with CUDA >= 13.4). One CTA computes a 128x128 output tile of one expert over rows from `moe_align_block_size(block_size=128)`. Four warps fill a 3-stage `cp.async` pipeline (gathered E4M3 rows, A scales, and a pre-laid-out 7 KB weight tile per 128N x 128K), one thread copies scales/codebooks to TMEM with `tcgen05.cp` and issues the two K64 LUT MMAs per K128 (collector fill, then lastuse), and all warps run a TMEM-to-BF16 epilogue that scatters rows back to `sorted_token_ids` order. Weights are rearranged once at load (`lut_b_to_sm107_tiles`, 3.5 bits/weight resident including padding). Layouts and instruction descriptors follow the dense LUT-B probes that were validated on Rubin.

**Limitations.**
- Native path needs hidden and per-partition intermediate sizes divisible by 128, no bias, and no LoRA; otherwise it falls back to emulation with a log line.
- M is padded to 128 rows per expert, so decode wastes tensor-core work. No swap-AB / small-N tile, no TMA, no persistent scheduling.
- Expert parallelism goes through the standard `expert_map` handling but was not exercised on hardware.
- Emulation stores dequantized weights: it validates accuracy, not memory or speed.

**CI coverage.** CI has no Rubin GPUs, so the native tests skip there; the emulation, layout, and config tests run on any CUDA GPU.

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The human submitter will review every changed line before marking it ready for review.

title: [Perf][MoE] Add H200 FP8 fused MoE config for Beam-1.0 TP8
author: ischencheng
body:
## Overview

Reflection Beam-1.0 FP8 on H200 runs TP8 with `--moe-backend triton`, as in its recipe. There is no tuned config for its fused MoE shape (`E=256, N=320`, fp8_w8a8), so every layer uses the default config. This PR adds a tuned H200 config for that shape. It also lets `benchmark_moe.py` time the per-token activation / per-channel weight FP8 path that Beam's compressed-tensors checkpoint runs, and parse `BeamForCausalLM`. Follow-up to #62074.

## Claims

- Fused MoE on 1xH200, Beam-1.0 TP8 shape, per-token FP8 path: 3-19% faster at 96-512 tokens when replaying top-k ids recorded from Beam's real weights, and 9-45% faster at 96-1536 tokens with uniform random routing. At 1024 tokens the kernel goes from 31% to 57% of the HBM bound.
- One TP8 rank of Beam-1.0 FP8 on 1xH200 (all 52 layers, dummy weights, uniform simulated routing): a decode step at 128 and 256 requests takes 9.4% and 16.7% less time.
- Up to 64 tokens and from 2048 tokens the file holds the default config, so small-batch decode and prefill do not change. With DFlash2 (recipe: 7 draft tokens), a verify step has 8 rows per request, so 12-192 requests land in the range that gets faster.
- `benchmark_moe.py` now times the kernel variant the model runs: for compressed-tensors checkpoints with `strategy: token` input activations it uses per-token activation and per-channel weight scales. Before, it always timed per-tensor FP8.

## Validation

### Kernel with recorded routing (1xH200)

Top-k ids recorded from Beam-1.0 FP8 with real weights (first 6 layers, so MoE layers 3-5, TP1), decode batches of M requests over two corpora: Python and Markdown files from site-packages, and wikitext-103. They are replayed on the TP8 shape (`E=256, N=320, K=5120`, top-8, per-token FP8) with this file and with the default config. 24 recorded steps per M in one CUDA graph, median of 7 replays, µs per step.

| M | code corpus: default → this PR | wikitext: default → this PR | uniform random: default → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 213.9 → 214.0 (+0.0%) | 180.4 → 180.0 (-0.2%) | 313.5 → 313.7 (+0.1%) |
| 96 | 244.5 → 229.8 (-6.0%) | 211.2 → 204.7 (-3.1%) | 357.9 → 326.1 (-8.9%) |
| 128 | 280.5 → 253.2 (-9.7%) | 239.1 → 223.3 (-6.6%) | 387.7 → 337.9 (-12.8%) |
| 256 | 384.7 → 311.4 (-19.1%) | 339.2 → 277.4 (-18.2%) | 468.4 → 357.8 (-23.6%) |
| 512 | 445.4 → 390.2 (-12.4%) | 414.0 → 357.3 (-13.7%) | 488.3 → 397.3 (-18.6%) |

Real routing is not uniform: a decode batch of 128 touches 156 (code) or 133 (wikitext) of 256 experts per layer, against 252 for uniform routing, and the busiest expert gets 76-85 rows. So these steps load fewer experts and are shorter than the uniform ones.

### Kernel with uniform routing (1xH200)

`benchmark_moe.benchmark_config` on the per-token path (`per_act_token_quant=True`), random gating, CUDA graph of 10 calls, 100 iterations, median of 3 runs. "Bound" is the expert weights that uniform routing touches, `256 * (1 - (1 - 8/256)^M) * 4.92 MB`, over 4.8 TB/s; FP8 compute is below that at every M here.

| M | bound µs | default µs (of bound) | this PR µs (of bound) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 96 | 250.1 | 366.2 (68%) | 334.4 (75%) | -8.7% |
| 128 | 258.2 | 398.5 (65%) | 346.6 (74%) | -13.0% |
| 256 | 263.2 | 475.2 (55%) | 365.1 (72%) | -23.2% |
| 512 | 264.3 | 497.8 (53%) | 407.0 (65%) | -18.2% |
| 1024 | 266.5 | 856.7 (31%) | 470.1 (57%) | -45.1% |
| 1536 | 268.7 | 902.0 (30%) | 519.7 (52%) | -42.4% |

At 1-64 tokens the tuned configs were within -4% to +0.3% of the default here, and +1.9% at 64 on the recorded code corpus, so the file keeps the default config there.

### One TP8 rank of Beam-1.0 FP8 (1xH200)

All 52 layers and 256 experts; attention heads and widths are one TP8 rank's share (6 Q heads, 1 KV head, expert width 320). Dummy weights with `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`, `--moe-backend triton`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Arms ran in one container in the order default, tuned, tuned, default. ms per decode step, median of 4 runs; spread within an arm is under 0.3%.

| | default | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode, 16 requests | 12.13 | 12.12 | -0.1% |
| decode, 128 requests | 25.95 | 23.51 | -9.4% |
| decode, 256 requests | 31.67 | 26.38 | -16.7% |
| 8K prefill chunk | 180.6 | 180.6 | 0.0% |

This run used the tuned configs at 1-64 tokens as well; the file now holds the default there, which only matters for the 16-request row.

### Correctness

Only Triton tile parameters change. At the Beam shape and M = 96, 128, 256, 1024 and 1536, the output with this file and with the default config both have a mean relative error of 1.41-1.44% against the per-column reference in `tests/kernels/moe/test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py` (its threshold is 5%). Both configs use `BLOCK_SIZE_K=128`, and the outputs were the same.

`benchmark_moe.py --model reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8 --tp-size 8 --dtype fp8_w8a8 --batch-size 1 128 1024` runs on this branch and prints `Benchmarking per-token activation and per-channel weight FP8.` before the timings (checked on an L4, which has no config file and uses the default config). The tuning run above used the same `benchmark_config` path.

## Details

- Dummy weights route almost every token of a step to the same 8 experts, so each expert sees many rows and larger M tiles win. Without uniform simulated routing, the proxy above shows this file 9.8% and 13.0% slower at 128 and 256 requests. The recorded real routing sits much closer to uniform than to that.
- Per-tensor and per-token FP8 read the same config file name. For this shape, configs tuned on the per-tensor path time within 1% of these on the per-token path.
- The search space was pruned to keep tuning near half an hour: `BLOCK_SIZE_M` 16 up to 128 tokens, 16-32 up to 512, 16-64 above; `GROUP_SIZE_M` in {1, 16, 64}. The pruning was in my tuning script, not in `benchmark_moe.py`.
- Not covered: H100, TP4 (`N=640`), DFlash2 verify, and the full model. 503 GB FP8 needs 8xH200, which I did not run. The recorded routing comes from 3 early MoE layers; later layers may route differently.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds a fused MoE config for `E=256,N=320`, and none adds per-token FP8 to `benchmark_moe.py`. The open `benchmark_moe.py` PRs change model parsing or error handling (#62526, #49088, #50711, #51353), or add zipf-skewed expert loads (#57100), which is a separate axis from the quantization path here. #61688 (runtime Triton autotune, draft) would make static configs less important if it lands.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the change, run the tuning and the measurements above, and draft this description.
