title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Skip drafting in steps where no request can use the drafts
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Overview

Continues #48244 by @njhill (co-author). In steps where no scheduled request can use the
drafts proposed after the step, the speculator now proposes with K=0 instead of
drafting. Such requests are non-final prefill chunks and requests sure to reach
`max_tokens`. This covers every request on a P/D prefill instance, which runs with
`max_tokens=1`.

Related: #39266 (draft) skips EAGLE drafting on MRV2 for P/D prefill instances and
non-final chunks; this PR decides in the scheduler and also covers requests about to
finish, DFlash and DP. #53426 makes the K=0 draft sync forward optional; this PR keeps
that forward.

## Claims

- On Model Runner V2, when no scheduled request on any DP rank can use the drafts, the
  speculator runs with `num_speculative_tokens=0`:
  - EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP still run the draft prefill pass, which keeps the drafter's KV cache
    in sync, but skip draft sampling and the draft decode steps.
  - DFlash stores the context K/V and skips the query pass. DSpark, DFlash2 and
    LiLiCorr share this code.
- The drafter's prefill pass still runs, so the gain is modest. Prefill-only throughput
  (Qwen3-8B, 64 x 16,384-token prompts, 1 output token, one GB300 GPU) improves by
  **+1.9% with EAGLE3** and **+7.3% with DFlash** at `max_num_batched_tokens=512`, and by
  +1.4% and +2.7% at 2048. On a 1P1D prefill instance every step proposes with K=0,
  and prefill throughput improves by +2.1% (EAGLE3) and +3.4% (DFlash) at 512, and by
  +0.6% and +1.9% at 2048.
- Outputs and acceptance do not change. With batch-invariant kernels, outputs and every
  spec-decode counter are identical to `main`.

## Validation

Qwen3-8B with `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3` (K=3) and `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` (K=16),
`--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN`, GB300. Baseline is `main` at `532a7d19d2`, the base of
this PR; every run below used the rebased commit.

An earlier version of this description reported +9.0% (EAGLE3) and +3.4% (DFlash) at 512.
Those runs were CPU-starved (the benchmark processes were confined to one CPU core),
which inflated host-side costs. The numbers below replace them.

**Prefill-only throughput** (total tokens/s; mean of 3 reps on one engine after a warm-up
pass). The workload matches `vllm bench throughput --dataset-name random
--random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 64 --max-model-len 20480`.
main and this PR ran at the same time on two GPUs of one node, then swapped GPUs. The
table shows the GPU whose reps stayed within 1%; on the other GPU, reps of both builds
varied by up to 30%. With the PR, every proposal in these runs used K=0.

| Method | `max_num_batched_tokens` | main | this PR | Delta | Step time saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | 2048 | 72,100 | 73,144 | +1.4% | 0.4 ms |
| EAGLE3 | 512 | 33,834 | 34,473 | **+1.9%** | 0.3 ms |
| DFlash | 2048 | 72,569 | 74,508 | +2.7% | 0.7 ms |
| DFlash | 512 | 32,367 | 34,730 | **+7.3%** | 1.1 ms |

The skipped work is draft sampling and the draft decode steps (EAGLE3), or the query pass
(DFlash). Host time spent in `propose()` at 512 drops from 1.41 to 0.98 ms per step for
EAGLE3 and from 1.05 to 0.92 ms for DFlash; the rest of the saving is GPU time. The
drafter's prefill pass still runs: it writes the draft KV cache that later steps, and on
a P/D decode instance the transferred KV, depend on.

**1P1D prefill throughput.** P and D each on one GPU with `NixlConnector`, the same
drafter on both, P at the given `max_num_batched_tokens`. Through the toy proxy, 3
phases of 128 random 8,192-token prompts at concurrency 32 (`max_tokens=8`). P's waiting
queue was non-empty in at least 89% of samples. main and this PR ran side by side on the
node's two GPU pairs, then swapped; tokens/s and deltas are means over both placements.

| Method | P `max_num_batched_tokens` | main | this PR | Delta | P proposals with K=0 (PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | 2048 | 56,809 | 57,213 | +0.6% | 3,072 / 3,072 |
| EAGLE3 | 512 | 28,447 | 29,043 | **+2.1%** | 12,288 / 12,288 |
| DFlash | 2048 | 56,950 | 57,883 | +1.9% | 3,072 / 3,072 |
| DFlash | 512 | 28,527 | 29,524 | **+3.4%** | 12,288 / 12,288 |

**Equivalence** (offline, greedy). There are 80 requests: 24 long prompts chunked at 512
tokens with `max_tokens` 1, 2 or 64, run alone and then mixed with 32 short decode
requests.

| Method | Mode | Outputs equal | Spec-decode counters | Proposals with K=0 (PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | 80/80 | identical (3,349 drafts, 1,775 accepted) | 19 |
| DFlash | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | 80/80 | identical (2,244 drafts, 2,953 accepted) | 18 |

Without batch invariance, two runs of `main` already differ on 23/80 EAGLE3 outputs, and
main vs this PR differ on 31/80. DFlash is deterministic across runs of `main`, but main
vs this PR differ on 31/80: in a K=0 step DFlash stores all context K/V in one eager
pass instead of partly inside the FULL graph, so rounding can differ, and acceptance then
changes batch shapes.

**Existing e2e tests** give the same results on both:

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/eagle/test_eagle_correctness.py -k "medium and qwen3_eagle3 and not transformers"` | GSM8K 0.886, pass | GSM8K 0.886, pass |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py` (MRV2 reference acceptance) | MT-Bench 4.07, HumanEval 6.42, GSM8K 6.42 | same |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py::test_dflash_correctness[qwen3-mrv2]` | GSM8K 0.884, AL 4.12 | same |

**Serving equivalence.** 1P1D with `NixlConnector` used EAGLE3 K=3 on both sides and CUDA
graphs on. DP=2 used EAGLE3 K=3. Requests were sent one at a time.

| Setup | Outputs equal | Decode-side acceptance length |
|---|---|---|
| 1P1D | 40/40 | identical (1.521, 1.598) |
| DP=2 | 40/40 | identical (1.539, 1.597) |

There were no hangs with DP ranks voting to skip.

**Unit tests.** `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`,
`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dp_utils.py` and
`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py` pass (281 tests), except two
pre-existing PP scheduler tests that fail the same way on `main`.

## Details

- **Scheduler.** It sets `SchedulerOutput.skip_drafts` when no scheduled request can use
  the step's drafts, on the V2 runner and for drafters that reserve lookahead slots.
  `_drafts_unused` counts only the output tokens a request is sure to have, assuming
  every draft is rejected, so it never skips drafts a later step could verify.
- **DP.** The flag is ANDed across ranks in the batch-descriptor all-reduce that already
  runs, giving `DPSyncState.skip_drafts`. The runner then proposes with K=0. A rank
  running a dummy batch votes no, so an idle DP rank disables the skip for that step.
- **Changes from #48244:**
  - The per-request lookahead-slot skip is dropped. For a non-final chunk, the lookahead
    slots are the next chunk's first positions, which are allocated one step later
    anyway. For a finishing request it saves at most about one block for one step.
    Keeping it safely means masking every draft KV write, including inside captured
    FULL draft-decode graphs; the fused decode path is the default on FlashAttention,
    FlashInfer and Triton, and its captured graphs compute their own slot mappings.
  - Skipping reuses the existing `num_speculative_tokens == 0` path, which already skips
    the AR draft decode steps, instead of a separate flag in each speculator.
    `skip_sample` and the DFlash early return also apply to K=0 from dynamic speculative
    decoding.
  - The scheduler reports one flag instead of a set of request ids.
- **Not covered.** Multi-module MTP and the draft-model speculator ignore K, so they
  still draft in these steps and the drafts go unused, as before. N-gram reserves no
  lookahead slots, so the flag is never set for it. MTP, DSpark, DFlash2 and LiLiCorr
  share the changed code but were not run; all validation used Qwen3-8B. MRV1 is
  unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Throughput script (one engine, warm-up then timed reps)</summary>

```python
llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B", speculative_config=spec, max_model_len=20480,
          max_num_batched_tokens=mbt, enable_prefix_caching=False, seed=42,
          attention_backend="FLASH_ATTN")
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
prompts = lambda n: [TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=r.tolist())
                     for r in rng.integers(1000, 100000, size=(n, 16384))]
params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1, ignore_eos=True)
llm.generate(prompts(8), params)
for _ in range(3):
    batch = prompts(64)
    t = time.perf_counter(); llm.generate(batch, params)
    print(64 * 16385 / (time.perf_counter() - t))
```
</details>

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Align adaptive draft prefill graph padding
author: amenomori
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62793. Align adaptive-verification draft-prefill CUDA graphs with the target's shared attention metadata, including when another data-parallel rank is prefilling.

## Claims

- Capture varlen draft-prefill graphs under AV and exclude prefill-bearing batches from decode-only graphs.
- Preserve the agreed `max_query_len` in `DPSyncState` and reuse it, including `None`, without another collective.
- Extend the existing regression with DP > 1 peer-prefill and longer-peer-decode cases.

## Validation

Rebased onto upstream main `5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9`. Local checks on macOS:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/cudagraph \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  -k 'not test_full_capture_sets_graph_pool_id_before_cuda_graph' -q
```

**29 passed, 1 deselected.** The excluded pre-existing capture test requires a current stream unavailable on this host; CI runs the complete file.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py \
  -k 'test_every_dp_rank_must_agree_to_microbatch or test_decode_threshold_only_applies_when_every_rank_is_a_uniform_decode or test_microbatching_pads_all_ranks_to_the_largest or test_microbatching_survives_a_rank_that_cannot_fill_it or test_microbatching_off_when_a_rank_does_not_allow_it' -q
```

**5 passed, 25 deselected.** Applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, mypy and CI test tethering, and `git diff --check` passed.

The existing **CPU V1 Others** (`v1-others-cpu`) Buildkite job already runs `test_cudagraph_manager.py` and depends on `vllm/v1/` and `tests/v1`. No CI configuration changes are needed. [Buildkite CI #97530](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97530) is running for `94fcf82c7f83`. Pre-commit and docs passed; `v1-others-cpu`, which includes the added DP regressions, has not completed yet.

`CPU-Spec Decode Tests` soft-failed on the existing `test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype`: `ReplicatedLinear` has no `cpu_linear`. The exact upstream base `5d35ce39` has the [same failure in main CI #97527](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97527#01a17bf7-46e5-4f1f-bc9e-95f8e3cd8d54), also with 1 failed, 111 passed and 121 skipped. The affected test/model/linear files are unchanged by this PR. The same failure was independently reproduced on both the PR head and a clean base worktree with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` and the isolated pytest node. The test omits CPU linear post-load initialization; this unrelated baseline failure is left outside this PR.

<details>
<summary>DP regression before and after the fix</summary>

Before rebasing, the extended regression was run with production files from the previous PR head `b3ae85bbec7eb348130f4a2e18a71b1bfcbca06c`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/cudagraph \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  -k draft_prefill_matches_shared_target_metadata_shape -q
```

Before: **2 failed, 5 passed, 23 deselected**. The peer-prefill case selects draft FULL versus target PIECEWISE; the longer-peer-decode case exposes the missing synchronized-bound field. With the fix: **7 passed, 23 deselected**.

These are CPU dispatch regressions with a simulated external collective, not real multi-GPU inference results. The rebased suite also passes, as reported above.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier single-GPU model validation</summary>

The equivalent candidate-source fix was validated on v0.31.0, H100 NVL, Qwen3-32B W4A16 + Eagle3, K=3, FA3, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, concurrency 4. Across two independent starts with 10s warmup and 30s measurement, mean output throughput was 352.4 tok/s unpatched versus 684.0 tok/s with the candidate; mean acceptance lengths were 1.425 and 2.906. Both candidate runs had zero request errors and matched a fixed-K greedy smoke on four prompts. The isolated FA3 reproducer in #62793 failed with mismatched padding and passed with aligned padding.

Those results are from v0.31.0, not this rebased checkout or the DP follow-up. The instance was destroyed. No current multi-GPU validation or AV trimming speedup is claimed.

</details>

## Details

Draft prefill shares the target's attention metadata and must use the same padded request layout. With DP, another rank's prefill makes the agreed query bound `None`; reusing a local decode bound can incorrectly select FULL after the target selected PIECEWISE. All state-construction paths now preserve the agreed bound, while uniform draft batches reset it to their own query length. The upstream benchmark's eager state is updated for the new field.

Duplicate checks were refreshed: #62953 handles final redispatch disagreement between rank-local graph inventories; #63523 optimizes CPU metadata math. Neither implements this target-to-draft bound reuse fix. No other open PR was found linked to #62793.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation, tests, review and validation.

A human submitter must also review every changed line and run the relevant tests as required by `AGENTS.md`.

<details>
<summary>Model evaluation reproduction</summary>

Save the following as `/tmp/eval_humming.py`:

```python
from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import _build_gsm8k_prompts, get_answer_value
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

        max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=32, gpu_memory_utilization=0.25,
    )

        temperature=0, max_tokens=256, seed=42,
        stop=["Question", "Assistant:", "<|separator|>"],

    correct = sum(
        get_answer_value(o.outputs[0].text) == label
```

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \
VLLM_HUMMING_ONLINE_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int6","hadamard_block_size":-1}' \
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}' \
```

title: [ROCm] Bump UCX to v1.23.0-rc1 so NIXL uses rocm_ipc
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Bump `UCX_BRANCH` to `v1.23.0-rc1` in `Dockerfile.rocm` and `Dockerfile.rocm_72`
- Drop `UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y`
- Set `UCX_ROCM_IPC_SIGPOOL_MAX_ELEMS=inf`, matching the existing `rocm_copy` setting

NIXL opens its UCX endpoints with peer error handling, and at the current UCX pin `rocm_ipc` does not advertise that capability, so NIXL never uses it for GPU-to-GPU reads on ROCm. Reads fall back to TCP emulation, or, with the `UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y` override from #49251, to a host-staged pipeline whose fragment pool grows until `/dev/shm` allocations fail; under long-context P/D load that stalled transfers and killed the decode engine. openucx/ucx#11977, included in `v1.23.0-rc1`, adds the capability. With it, `rocm_ipc` is selected again and the override is no longer needed. Each in-flight `rocm_ipc` copy holds one HSA signal, and the 1024 default made multi-request NIXL reads fail, hence the signal pool setting.

On MI355, a 256 MiB NIXL READ between two GPUs goes from 0.48 GB/s (8.8 GB/s with the override) to 60.9 GB/s. With NIXL at its current pin built against the new UCX the same way as the Dockerfile, the MI355 NixlConnector groups pass: spec decode acceptance, PD accuracy sweep, AITER PD accuracy and DP EP PD accuracy. The PD accuracy sweep's lm_eval time drops from 370s to 183s. Step-5 1P1D (TP4 + TP4) passed 10/10 rounds of GSM8K and long-context NIAH; on the current image it hung in round 5.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][EPD] Check encoder readiness for prefix replay
author: gty111
body:
## Overview

Wait for encoder embeddings needed by prefix replay before admitting an EPD request.

## Claims

- Include the replayed prefix tail in EC readiness checks without changing KV-hit accounting or replay behavior when a KV load restores the window.
- Prevent missing encoder embeddings from crashing the consumer during DeepSeek-V4.1 prefix replay.

## Validation

Slurm E2E: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1E (TP1) + 1PD (TP2), Mooncake TCP, MRV2, raw-image forwarding, prefix/processor caches and CUDA Graphs enabled. After 128 disjoint random-image warmups, MUIRBench (512 questions, concurrency 64) completed with **512/512 HTTP 200**, **303/512 correct (59.18%)**, and no `Encoder cache miss`, using an 8 GiB consumer pool.

## Details

EC readiness was checked before SWA replay rewound the computed-token boundary. For example, a KV hit at 640 covers an image ending at 567, but replay starts at 512 and still needs that image. Skipping its load causes `Encoder cache miss`. Check EC readiness against the replay start while retaining the original KV-hit boundary for allocation and statistics.

Checked related open EPD/prefix-replay PRs; none addresses this missing-load path. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Avoid re-marking committed prompt-tail boundaries as cached this step
author: khyun1109
body:
## Overview

On hybrid models with `mamba_cache_mode="align"` (e.g. Qwen3.5), requests whose prompts share their last hash-aligned boundary are admitted one per engine step once that boundary is committed. This hits reads fanned out over one prompt and the children of a parallel-sampling request (`n > 1`). This PR skips re-caching that boundary in `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` when the block already carries its hash, so these requests are admitted together. Related: #29387 (the same-step guard this interacts with), #61192 (`/v1/systemone` reads over one state, which take this path).

## Claims

- Bug fix: requests that hit an already committed prompt-tail boundary are no longer deferred, so a fan-out over a shared prefix is admitted together instead of one request per step. Which blocks are cached and hit does not change.
- `vllm bench serve` on Qwen3.5-4B: 5.0x request throughput for a fan-out over shared prefixes with 1-token outputs, 3.0x with 64-token outputs, and 4.7x for parallel sampling with `n=16`. Median TTFT drops 5–15x.
- No accuracy change: on `/v1/systemone` decisions, flips against a serial reference stay at noise level (1/458 vs. 2/458, same max |Δp|), and accuracy is 0.891 with and without the fix.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** Qwen3.5-4B on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, `main` at 81c2bd702 with and without this PR, one fresh server per variant:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 --max-num-seqs 256

# Fan-out: 24 prefixes x 16 prompts, each prefix's prompts sent together.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
    --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 592 \
    --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 48 --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 24 \
    --prefix-repetition-output-len 1 --num-prompts 384 --disable-shuffle \
    --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1

# Parallel sampling: 64 prompts of 640 tokens, n=16.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 640 --random-output-len 32 \
    --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8 --extra-body '{"n": 16}' \
    --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1
```

The default `max_num_seqs` exceeds the Mamba cache blocks available at this memory share, hence `--max-num-seqs 256`. The 592-token prefix is one 576-token hybrid block plus 16 tokens, so each prompt's last hash boundary (576) lies inside the shared prefix and away from the prefix/suffix junction, where re-tokenization could shift it. Engine steps are the `/metrics` delta of the `iteration_tokens_total` count. Mean ± std over seeds 1–3:

| workload | output len | variant | req/s | median TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | engine steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fan-out, 384 prompts | 1 | main | 36.31 ± 0.72 | 3341 ± 127 | 3646 ± 21 | 342 ± 6 |
| | 1 | main + fix | **181.31 ± 7.42** | 649 ± 28 | 832 ± 22 | 42 ± 4 |
| | 64 | main | 23.71 ± 0.66 | 3729 ± 157 | 4852 ± 449 | 763 ± 15 |
| | 64 | main + fix | **70.78 ± 0.06** | 353 ± 12 | 783 ± 3 | 222 ± 1 |
| parallel sampling, n=16, 64 prompts | 32 | main | 1.52 ± 0.02 | 3871 ± 26 | 4232 ± 81 | 1952 ± 0 |
| | 32 | main + fix | **7.10 ± 0.04** | 264 ± 1 | 551 ± 8 | 293 ± 1 |

Prefix-cache hit rates are the same with and without the fix (0.844, 0.900 and 0.844 for the three rows).

**Tests** (on 81c2bd702):

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_mamba_align_siblings_hit_committed_boundary_in_one_step` fails on `main` (`sibling 0 was deferred`) and passes with the fix. A producer commits a 2-block prefix in step 1; in step 2 it finishes its prompt and three siblings hit the committed boundary.
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/`: 475 passed, including the GPU end-to-end `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` (`[base]` and `[mtp]`).
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`: all hooks pass.

The new test is marked `cpu_test`, so it runs in the existing `v1/core` CPU step in CI.

**Model evaluation.** `/v1/systemone` on `main` (0d00d8b9c): 458 questions over 30 long states (four RACE-middle passages per state, 1,200–1,600 tokens, about 15 questions per request), 8 requests in flight. The serial reference uses `--max-num-seqs 1` without prefix caching.

| | main | main + fix |
|---|---|---|
| questions/s | 36.35 | 57.10 (+57%) |
| p50 request latency | 3.22 s | 2.06 s |
| accuracy | 0.891 | 0.891 |
| decision flips vs. serial reference, max \|Δp\| | 1/458, 0.087 | 2/458, 0.087 |

<details>
<summary>Earlier end-to-end runs: main 0d00d8b9c, v0.32.0 sweep, 27B decision model</summary>

Our own harness: N prompts share a prefix that ends on a hybrid block boundary, plus a 64-token suffix each, sent as token IDs to `/v1/completions` with `max_tokens=1`, 8 groups of 16 in flight.

**main (0d00d8b9c), Qwen3.5-4B, 576-token prefix, N=16:**

| | main | main + fix |
|---|---|---|
| reads/s (prefix-cache hit rate) | 41.96 (0.84) | 235.03 (0.84), 5.6x |
| engine steps for 384 requests | 361 | 25 |
| mean running requests | 1.07 | 15.98 |
| mean queue time per request | 1.98 s | 0.18 s |

**v0.32.0, Qwen3.5-4B (528-token hybrid block), reads/s.** A dense Qwen3-4B on the same harness reaches 239.9, 195.3 and 126.8 reads/s at N=16 for the three prefix lengths.

| prefix (tokens) | fan-out | v0.32.0 | v0.32.0 + fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 528 | 16 | 37.4 | 239.3 |
| 1056 | 16 | 37.6 | 184.3 |
| 2112 | 16 | 35.0 | 128.7 |
| 528 | 4 | 35.6 | 112.8 |

**v0.32.0, 27B Qwen3.5-hybrid decision model (`openjev/openjev`, 784-token hybrid block):**

| | v0.32.0 | v0.32.0 + fix |
|---|---|---|
| fan-out reads/s | 17.4 | 36.6 |
| engine steps for 384 requests | 384 | 24 |
| `/v1/systemone` long-state questions/s | 9.44 | 13.06 |
| decision flips vs. serial reference (458 questions) | 0 | 0 |

Throughput without prefix reuse (distinct cache salts) is unchanged: 47.0 reads/s on `main` (4B) and 5.5 reads/s on v0.32.0 (27B).

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` re-caches the prompt's last hash-aligned boundary whenever a request whose prompt passes that boundary is scheduled. The request's block at that boundary may already carry exactly that hash, either because it is a prefix-cache hit or because the request committed it in an earlier step. Nothing new is written in that step, but the function still returns the hash. `cache_blocks` then adds it to `cached_blocks_this_step`, and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` defers every other request whose hit ends on that block (the guard from #29387). This repeats whenever the producer's next chunk or a sibling is scheduled, so siblings are admitted one per step. Because the deferral is reported as insufficient blocks, the scheduler also stops scanning the waiting queue for that step. We found it by logging each deferral with the step that had added the hash: every one pointed at a re-cache of a block already keyed at that boundary.

**Fix.** In the non-checkpoint branch, return early when `source_block.block_hash_num_tokens == num_tokens`. The checkpoint branch above already uses the same condition.

**Why this is safe.** The skip applies only when the block already carries the hash for exactly this boundary, so its state was written in an earlier step or arrived as a hit. A sibling scheduled in this step reads it after that write, since forwards run in order. A step that does write the state still marks the hash, either through the first `cache_partial_block` call for a mid-block boundary or through the full-block loop in `cache_blocks`, so the #29387 guard still applies where it is needed.

**Not a duplicate.** The open PRs that touch `_cache_partial_tail_block` or `cached_blocks_this_step` fix other problems:

- #52972 and #53158 add a similar check to the full-attention manager's `_cache_partial_tail_block`, for stale partial hashes after full-block promotion.
- #56525 replaces the same-step set with a commit fence. The re-mark would still re-publish the hash there and fence siblings until the step commits, so the two changes compose.
- #61282 keeps the boundary state alive until the request ends.
- #55142, #52244 and #53802 change when or where the boundary is registered (connector loads, MTP, EAGLE).

None of them skips the re-cache in `MambaManager`'s non-checkpoint path. RFC #55697 and #55873/#55875/#55876 add application-declared checkpoints with producer/consumer scheduling; this fix is for the default path, with no markers.

**Scope.** The gain depends on siblings arriving together. With many unrelated prefixes interleaved, the bug still admits about one sibling per prefix in each step before the first deferral, so the gap shrinks. In a shuffled `prefix_repetition` run (24 prefixes of 1200 tokens with 64-token suffixes, otherwise as above), main and the fix were within noise: 105.6 ± 6.5 vs. 108.4 ± 5.2 req/s with 1-token outputs, and 35.4 ± 0.2 vs. 36.4 ± 0.9 req/s with 128-token outputs. That run is also close to compute-bound, since each sibling recomputes 112 tokens.

A sibling that arrives in the same step as the producer's first write is still deferred by the #29387 guard, as intended. We also tried letting the scheduler skip a deferred request instead of stopping the scan; with this fix in place it gave no further gain, so it is not included.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the issue, write the change and the test, and run the benchmarks. The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the regression test, and reviewed the results reported here.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3] Enable GLM low-latency BF16 GEMM on SM107
author: csahithi
body:
## Overview


The GLM-5.2/5.3 low-latency BF16 GEMM selection (CuTe DSL skinny GEMM + `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` at decode batch sizes) is gated to SM103, so on VRNVL72 (SM107) every unquantized decode projection runs cuBLAS. This PR enables the selection on SM107 with a table swept on VRNVL72, the same way #54606 enabled the Kimi-K3 low-latency GEMM plan on SM107.

## Claims


- **VRNVL72 coverage:** on SM107, GLM-5.2/5.3 BF16 decode projections use tuned CuTe DSL skinny GEMM / `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` configs where they beat cuBLAS. That covers fused qkv_a, q_b / indexer wq_b, o_proj (M ≤ 3), indexer wk + weights_proj, shared-expert gate_up / down and MTP eh_proj, at TP4. TP8 q_b keeps the existing SM103 row, re-measured on sm107.
- **Kernel times:** each shape is 1.2× to 1.9× faster than cuBLAS at its target M on VRNVL72 (table below).
- **End-to-end (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, VRNVL72, 8k in / 1k out, vs `main` behavior):** output throughput rises by +8.1% at c1 (ITL 6.35 → 5.86 ms), +5.9% at c2 and +2.2% at c4–c8 without speculative decoding. With MTP K=3 it rises +8.5% at c1, in a single run.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K is unchanged within run-to-run noise: 0.9735 stock vs 0.9773 with this PR.
- **No change on other devices:** SM103 keeps its existing table and routing (same shapes, M ranges, backends and CuTe warmup set). Every other device stays on the default GEMM. Checked on B300: tests, routing, GSM8K and throughput are unchanged (see Validation).

## Validation


**Kernel microbenchmark** (one VRNVL72 GPU, BF16, CuTe DSL skinny GEMM vs cuBLAS; a (shape, M) entry is in the table only where CuTe wins by more than the 0.15 µs noise band):

| Projection (local N×K, TP4) | M | CuTe (µs) | cuBLAS (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fused qkv_a, replicated (2624×6144) | 4 | 5.84 | 6.91 | 1.18× |
| q_b / indexer wq_b (4096×2048) | 4 | 4.31 | 5.71 | 1.32× |
| o_proj (6144×4096) | 1 | 5.90 | 7.77 | 1.32× |
| indexer wk + weights_proj (160×6144) | 4 | 2.83 | 5.43 | 1.92× |
| shared expert gate_up (1024×6144) | 4 | 3.96 | 5.40 | 1.36× |
| shared expert down (6144×512) | 4 | 3.19 | 4.28 | 1.34× |
| MTP eh_proj (6144×12288) | 1 | 12.90 | 16.96 | 1.31× |

M=4 is the target-model batch for one request with MTP K=3. The TP8 q_b entry (2048×2048) is the existing SM103 row; re-measured on VRNVL72, it beats cuBLAS at every measured M:
- CuTe at M=1–2: 3.2–3.3 vs 5.0 µs.
- `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` at M=3–16: 4.0–4.2 vs 4.9–5.1 µs.

**Decode step profile** (nsys, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4 on one VRNVL72 tray, MTP K=3, c=1; the SM107 table vs the SM103 table reused on SM107):
- Step time: 6.97 → 6.87 ms.
- Kernels per step: 2,004 → 1,801.
- Dense-GEMM kernel time: 4,355 → 3,859 µs per step.

Less of the GEMM saving reaches step time because at c=1 the routed-MoE chain on the auxiliary stream is the critical path.

**Accuracy:** GSM8K 5-shot 0.9765 with this change combined with other decode-path changes, vs 0.976 stock (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, VRNVL72, real MTP verification).

**Tests:**
- `pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm`.
- GPU (SM103 / SM107): the shape tests now cover the union of both tables' CuTe configs and the SM107 `dsv3_fused_a` range.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `typos` pass at the versions pinned in pre-commit.

**End-to-end A/B** 
- **Model and hardware:** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4 on one VRNVL72 node.
- **Server:** the 8k1k recipe (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 9216 --quantization modelopt_fp4`, Rust front end).
- **Client:** aiperf, synthetic 8000 in / 1000 out, ignore_eos, at least 20 requests per point (5×C at c8).
- **Run order:** stock and this PR alternated (stock, PR, stock, PR), then the MTP arms.
- **Engagement:** every PR arm logged the SM107 table as installed, with both backends available.

| Spec decoding | c | Stock out tok/s (run 1 / run 2) | This PR out tok/s (run 1 / run 2) | Δ | Stock ITL (ms) | This PR ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 1 | 153.0 (152.6 / 153.4) | 165.3 (165.2 / 165.4) | **+8.1%** | 6.35 | 5.86 |
| none | 2 | 286.6 (287.5 / 285.6) | 303.5 (303.0 / 304.0) | **+5.9%** | 6.69 | 6.30 |
| none | 4 | 506.2 (505.7 / 506.6) | 517.5 (517.6 / 517.4) | **+2.2%** | 7.42 | 7.26 |
| none | 8 | 860.2 (858.0 / 862.3) | 879.4 (877.3 / 881.6) | **+2.2%** | 8.58 | 8.39 |
| MTP K=3 | 1 | 201.1 | 218.2 | +8.5% | 4.78 | 4.39 |
| MTP K=3 | 2 | 350.4 | 357.6 | +2.0% | 5.27 | 5.27 |
| MTP K=3 | 4 | 555.1 | 562.2 | +1.3% | 6.74 | 6.53 |

- **Variability:** the two runs per arm without MTP differ by at most 0.7%, well below the deltas.
- **MTP rows:** one run per arm. Sampling is at temperature 1, so acceptance varies: the mean acceptance length over the sweep was 1.58 (stock) vs 1.61 (PR), so part of the MTP difference may come from acceptance.

title: [Perf][Multimodal] Make encoder cache free linear in items per request
author: GOavi101
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #54284. `EncoderCacheManager.free_encoder_input` scans all of a request's other cached inputs on every call, so freeing a request with N multimodal items is O(N²) on the scheduler thread. This makes it O(N) with the same release semantics.

## Claims

- Freeing a request with N multimodal items is now linear in N: 1,024 items drops from 15.9 ms to 0.29 ms, and 4,096 from 235 ms to 1.2 ms.
- No behaviour change: an entry is still held until the request's last occurrence of that `mm_hash` is freed, as #54284 requires.
- Only matters for prompts with hundreds of items (the default limit is 999 per modality). Typical prompts see under 0.1 ms difference.

## Validation

`EncoderCacheManager.free(request)` timed on `main` vs this PR: 5 runs, median in ms, CPU only (CPython 3.12).

| Items per request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| 256 | 1.36 | 0.09 |
| 1,024 | 15.87 | 0.29 |
| 4,096 | 234.64 | 1.21 |

`pytest tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py`: 22 passed (21 existing, including the duplicate-hash tests from #54284, plus 1 new). CI runs the file through `pytest -m cpu_test v1/core`.

I did not do a GPU end-to-end run. This only changes scheduler bookkeeping, so model outputs are unaffected.

## Details

The `any(...)` check added in #54284 runs on every free, so freeing N inputs costs N(N−1)/2 comparisons on the engine-core thread, and the whole batch waits. This PR keeps `request_hash_refs[req_id][mm_hash]`, a count of the request's cached input ids per hash, updated where `request_cached_ids` changes. The check becomes a dict lookup.

Tradeoff: one small dict per request. An out-of-tree manager that subclasses `EncoderCacheManager` and writes `request_cached_ids` directly would also need to update `request_hash_refs`.

title: [CI][ROCm] Give the M3 embed-sharing fixture a kernel_config
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Problem

`(MI355 DPX) V1 Executor + Worker` fails on every parametrisation of `test_m3_target_allocates_embedding_on_required_stage` with `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'kernel_config'`.

Failing job: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15124/list?sid=01a15db1-bce5-4cd0-a3c0-f39c922bfb4b

## Cause

#62712 wired `specialized_decode_config()` into `MiniMaxM3Model.__init__` on the AMD path, and that helper reads `config.kernel_config.monokernel` unconditionally. The `m3_config` fixture in this test builds a fake `VllmConfig` as a `SimpleNamespace` and never carried a `kernel_config`, so the constructor now raises before the test reaches its assertion. Both halves are correct on their own; the fixture simply was not updated alongside the new call.

Only the AMD variant is affected, because the fixture imports `vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model` on ROCm and the nvidia model has no `specialized_decode_config` call.

The last upstream nightly passed because it started before #62712 landed, not because upstream is unaffected. The same group will fail there on its next run.

## Fix

Give the fixture a `kernel_config` with `monokernel` disabled, which is the real `KernelConfig` default, so the model falls back to the non-specialized path and the test keeps asserting exactly what it asserted before. This matches the fixture style already used by the DSv4.1 mono decode tests added in #60731.

## Test plan

`pytest -v -s v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py` on MI355X, which is the command behind the failing CI step.

title: [Core][Rust Frontend] Report structured-output compile failures as validation errors
author: BugenZhao
body:
## Overview

A structured-output constraint that EngineCore fails to compile finishes the request as `FINISHED_ERROR` with no error attached. The Python frontend rarely sees this, because it validates constraints with the backend library before submitting. The Rust frontend cannot, so its clients get HTTP 500 for an invalid regex or grammar, and an empty 200 when llguidance builds a matcher in an error state (for example a schema with `uniqueItems`). This PR reports compile failures with the `validation_error` code that #49625 introduced for backend mismatches, so both frontends return 400, and makes the guidance backend fail compilation instead of continuing with a broken matcher.

## Claims

- When a request's grammar fails to compile, its error output carries `RequestError(code="validation_error", message="Invalid structured outputs: <compile error>")`. Python already maps that code to `VLLMValidationError` (400) since #49625.
- The guidance backend raises on a matcher that reports an error (`Grammar error: ...`) instead of logging a warning and generating nothing.
- The Rust frontend maps `validation_error` to HTTP 400 (an SSE `BadRequestError` event when streaming) and gRPC `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. This also covers #49625's backend-mismatch rejection, which the Rust frontend reported as 500.
- Rust non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate` fails the request on every engine-typed error, as Python raises every `RequestError`; before, only retryable ones did.

## Validation

GPU smoke on GB200, Qwen3-8B with `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser hermes` via `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve`, `main` (`e9cc6244a0`) against this PR. On `main` the Rust frontend sends native HTTP constraints as guidance and parser-built output grammars as xgrammar, and EngineCore keeps the first request's backend, so two request orders cover both backends and #49625's mismatch rejection. Each order ends with a valid request; the engine stays healthy on both builds.

| Order | Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| guidance first | completions `regex: "("` | 200, empty text | 400 `Grammar error: ... unclosed group` |
| | completions `grammar: "root ::= ("` | 500 | 400 `Failed to convert the grammar from GBNF to Lark ...` |
| | completions json `{"type": "array", "uniqueItems": true}` | 200, empty text | 400 `Grammar error: Unimplemented keys: ["uniqueItems"]` |
| | chat `regex` (composed into an xgrammar tag, mismatch) | 500 | 400 `... only supports one backend per engine ...` |
| xgrammar first | chat `regex: "("` (composed) | 500 | 400 `Regex parsing error at position 2 ...` |
| | chat streaming `grammar: "root ::= ("` | SSE `InternalServerError` | SSE `BadRequestError` |
| | completions `regex` (guidance, mismatch) | 500 | 400 `... only supports one backend per engine ...` |

Tests:

- Python (`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py`, `test_validation.py`, `tests/test_outputs.py`): 104 passed. `test_grammar_compile_error_finishes_only_request` now asserts the error output's `RequestError`; the new `test_backend_guidance_rejects_grammar_matcher_cannot_build` compiles a `uniqueItems` schema. Both fail with the engine changes reverted (`error` is `None`; compilation does not raise).
- Rust: `cargo nextest run --workspace` (2229 passed), clippy, fmt. `engine_request_errors_map_to_http_status` (was `retryable_engine_error_returns_service_unavailable`) runs a retryable and a validation error through completions, chat, and raw generate against the mock engine; `engine_errors_map_to_status_codes` covers gRPC.

## Details

**Root cause.** Grammar compilation runs asynchronously after `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_init`. Since #47312, a failed compilation finishes only that request, through `grammar_compile_error_reqs`, but without a `RequestError`, so every frontend reports an internal error. #49625 added `validation_error` for the separate case where a request names a backend other than the one the engine already uses; that check runs in `grammar_init`, before compilation, and does not cover a constraint that the right backend fails to compile. The guidance backend creates its `LLMatcher` without failing on a build error: `check_error()` only logs it, and the matcher allows nothing, so the request ends with empty output.

**Why `validation_error`.** It is the existing "the request itself is invalid" signal on `RequestError`, and Python's `to_exception` already maps it to 400; a compile failure of the request's own constraint is the same kind of error. Python's frontend validation already returns 400 for these constraints when it can check them, so this only changes requests that reach the engine unvalidated. The Rust side adds `RequestError::VALIDATION_ERROR` and `is_validation_error()` next to the existing `retryable` handling rather than an enum: `code` is an open string on the Python side, and no other code needs distinct Rust behavior.

**Not changed.**
- A streaming request still gets HTTP 200 with an SSE error event, as with Python, since compilation finishes after the response starts.
- xgrammar error messages include its log prefix (`[time] /project/cpp/...:line:`). Python's HTTP layer rewrites such paths with `sanitize_message`; the Rust frontend passes the message through.

**Not a duplicate.**
- #49625 (merged) rejects backend mismatches before compilation; this PR reports compilation failures with the same code.
- #45012 (open, inactive since 2026-08-19) handles failed grammar futures leaving requests blocked and reports them through the internal-error path (500); #47312 has since fixed the hang. This PR changes the status of those failures to 400.
- vllm-project/vllm#62456 (open) gives every Rust route one backend, which removes the mismatch case for the Rust frontend; the two PRs are independent.

title: [CI][KV Connector] Start NIXL accuracy decoders after prefillers on shared GPUs
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fix `:nvidia: (L4) NixlConnector PD accuracy core`. It has failed on every main build since 96279 and also hits PR builds, e.g. [96345](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96345#01a15d7b-d2e0-44fb-af42-73adadf13e22). It failed intermittently in an earlier stretch too (96041 to 96139).

The failing config is `DP_EP=1 GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.4 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=1 DECODER_TP_SIZE=2 MODEL_NAMES=deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny`:

```
(EngineCore) Model loading took 6.29 GiB memory
(EngineCore) Available KV cache memory: -2.34 GiB
ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks.
(Worker_DP1_EP1) AssertionError: Error in memory profiling. Initial free memory 14.91 GiB, current free memory 17.29 GiB.
```

**Root cause:** a startup race on a shared GPU. The L4 step has 2 GPUs. The prefiller gets GPU 0, and the decoder (DP=2) gets `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0`, so decoder rank 1 wraps onto GPU 0. All servers launch at once. If the decoder loads its weights while the prefiller is profiling, the prefiller counts the decoder's 4 GiB as its own usage, and its 0.4 × 22 GiB budget goes negative. The decoder's "Error in memory profiling" is a follow-on: the prefiller dies and frees GPU 0 in the middle of the decoder's own profiling.

Nothing changed in the memory footprint between pass and fail. Prefiller weights are 6.29 GiB and the decoder takes 4.04 GiB per rank in both. Only the timing changed: the prefiller load took 10.7 s in passing 96249 and 17.5 s in failing 96279.

| | 96249 (pass) | 96279 (fail) |
|---|---|---|
| Prefiller model load | 6.29 GiB, 10.7 s | 6.29 GiB, 17.5 s |
| Prefiller available KV cache | 1.92 GiB | −2.34 GiB |
| Decoder model load per rank | 4.04 GiB | 4.04 GiB |

**Fix:** when the instances need more GPUs than the host has (so some GPUs are shared), wait for the prefillers to be ready before launching the decoders. Configs with dedicated GPUs keep launching everything in parallel. The prefiller is then steady when the decoder profiles, so the decoder correctly sees the prefiller's reservation as already used, and 0.4 × 22 GiB still fits in the remaining free memory.

**Not a duplicate:** #62806 changes how a worker reacts when another process frees memory during profiling, which is the decoder-side symptom. It doesn't stop the prefiller's budget going negative. #62568 restructures the sweep into pytest but keeps concurrent startup.

## Test Plan

- `bash -n` and shellcheck (pre-commit) pass.
- Not run on a GPU locally. The `(L4) NixlConnector PD accuracy core` step will confirm.

## Notes

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; reviewed by the submitter.

title: [CPU] Warm up MRV2 Triton kernels at startup
author: ganeshr10
body:
## Purpose

On x86 CPU the V2 model runner compiles its scheduler-driven Triton kernels (`input_batch`, `block_table`, the sampler, KV-block zeroing, ...) on first use, so the first requests after server start pay the compile in TTFT. With `triton-cpu` (installed by `requirements/cpu.txt` on `x86_64` since #58140) the first plain request waits ~11-20 s, and the first request using penalties or structured output waits 70-80 s.

Two changes:

- **Run `warmup_kernels` on CPU.** The GPU worker calls it from `compile_or_warm_up_model`, but `CPUWorker` overrides that method and never did. `profile_run` alone builds its tensors directly, so it never reaches these kernels.
- **Use `BLOCK_SIZE = 1024` on CPU for `_penalties_kernel` and `_apply_grammar_bitmask_kernel`.** 

## Test Plan

- End to end: Qwen3.5-9B, BF16, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`,  `--max-model-len 2048`, v0.32.0 CPU wheel with and without each change, cold Triton cache, AMD EPYC Turin (32 cores). Rounds of 2 concurrent streaming requests (512 input / 32 output tokens); rounds 2-4 each enable one sampler feature for the first time.
- Cold compile and steady-state runtime of the two bitmask kernels per block size (Qwen3.5 vocab, 248320), with OpenMP threads bound as in the CPU worker.

## Test Result

TTFT of the first request in each round (s), and engine init:

| build | engine init | plain | penalties | structured output | temperature / top-p / top-k | plain, steady | compiles in requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.32.0 | 84 s | 20.2 | 81.0 | 73.7 | 11.0 | 1.7 | 32 |
| + `warmup_kernels` only | 317 s | 4.3 | 1.7 | 2.5 | 1.7 | 1.7 | 2 |
| + this PR | 100 s | 3.9 | 1.7 | 2.5 | 1.7 | 1.7 | 2 |

Bitmask kernels, cold compile per kernel and runtime at 64 tokens:

| BLOCK_SIZE | `_penalties_kernel` compile | `_apply_grammar_bitmask_kernel` compile | LLVM IR | penalties runtime | bitmask runtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Add a ucx_backend_params key for UCX backend init params
author: jbelofamd
body:
## Overview

`NixlConnector` creates NIXL's UCX backend with `num_threads` only, so UCX runs with NIXL's default `ucx_error_handling_mode=peer`. In peer mode UCX wires up only transports that can detect peer failure. On one MI355X node that left tcp: GPU-to-GPU KV reads ran as software emulation over tcp at about 3.4 Gbps, while with `ucx_error_handling_mode=none` UCX picks rocm_ipc zero-copy and a 74 MiB read ran at 483.7 Gbps. `UCX_*` environment variables cannot set this (it is a NIXL backend init parameter), and vLLM has no way to pass one.

## Claims

- New `kv_connector_extra_config.ucx_backend_params` (a dict of strings) passes extra init parameters to the UCX backend. Without the key nothing changes.
- When it is set and UCX is a selected backend, the agent is created with no backends and the worker creates each configured backend itself, in order, with the parameters NIXL would have used; UCX also gets the extra ones. In sleep mode, where the worker already creates UCX itself, the params are added to that call.
- Documented in `docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md` ("UCX backend parameters").

## Validation

Single MI355X node, an equivalent out-of-tree change, one 74 MiB KV read between two GPUs:

| `ucx_error_handling_mode` | UCX transport | throughput |
|---|---|---|
| peer (NIXL default) | tcp | 3.4 Gbps |
| none (`ucx_backend_params`) | rocm_ipc | 483.7 Gbps |

New `test_ucx_backend_params` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py`, 4 cases: no key (the agent config creates the backends, as before); UCX only (created explicitly with `num_threads` and the extra params); UCX + LIBFABRIC (both created in order, params on UCX only); LIBFABRIC only (nothing to apply, nothing changes).

<details>
<summary>commands and output</summary>

Rebased on main `db3b0f0fa`, CPU only:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k test_ucx_backend_params    # with this change
4 passed, 197 deselected, 1 warning in 36.94s

# connector reverted to main
FAILED tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_ucx_backend_params[extra_config1-agent_backends1-created_backends1]
FAILED tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_ucx_backend_params[extra_config2-agent_backends2-created_backends2]
2 failed, 2 passed, 197 deselected, 1 warning in 42.92s
```

Full `test_nixl_connector.py` on main `8e2beaa3b`: 199 passed, 2 failed with the change; 195 passed and the same 2 failed without (`test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[None|ray]`). ruff, typos, SPDX and mypy (3.11 hook) are clean.
</details>

## Details

**Flow.** Only worker start-up changes, on both P and D:

1. `NixlBaseConnectorWorker.__init__` reads `ucx_backend_params` from `kv_connector_extra_config`.
2. Without it: `nixl_agent(..., nixl_agent_config(backends=[...]))` creates the backends, as today.
3. With it and UCX selected: `nixl_agent_config(backends=[])`, then `create_backend(name, params)` for each configured backend in order. UCX gets the params NIXL's agent config would have given it (`num_threads` when UCX is the only backend) plus the extra ones.
4. Memory registration, handshake, and the decode-side read are unchanged; UCX simply selects its transports with the requested error-handling mode, e.g. rocm_ipc instead of tcp within a node.

**Trade-off.** With `ucx_error_handling_mode=none` UCX does not detect a failed peer; the docs section says so. The parameter is opt-in and passed through as given.

**Not tested.** Cross-node transfers with mode none, sleep mode with the params (no unit test), and NVIDIA (cuda_ipc), where we expect the same transport-selection effect but did not measure it.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Hold promotions after a cache reset until jobs report
author: javieratomic
body:
## Overview

`reset_cache()` in the `OffloadingConnector` scheduler releases the CPU-tier chunks of in-flight transfer jobs at once, but the workers may still write those chunks until they report the jobs. With secondary tiers, a lookup in that window can promote a secondary-tier hit into one of the released chunks, and the late worker write then overwrites it, so a later load hands the GPU wrong KV. This PR adds an `OffloadingManager.on_reset_flushed()` hook, called once the workers have reported every job flushed by the reset, and `TieringOffloadingManager` holds promotions from `reset_cache()` until then.

It is a standalone bugfix on `main` and also applies to a single node.

## Claims

- With `TieringOffloadingSpec` and at least one secondary tier, no promotion into the CPU tier starts after a cache reset until the workers have reported every job the reset flushed. This covers lookups from the scheduler and from tiers that serve peers through their `ParentManager` (`p2p`, `kvcr`). A late DMA of a flushed store, or any other worker write still pending, can no longer land on a chunk a promotion has just filled.
- Lookups keep running in that window: CPU-tier hits are served as before, and a chunk found only in a secondary tier is a miss, so the request recomputes it (or the peer is told it is absent).
- Without secondary tiers (`CPUOffloadingSpec`, or `TieringOffloadingSpec` without tiers), nothing is held (see Details for why it is not needed there). The scheduler still waits for the flushed jobs' reports before calling the hook, so after a reset with jobs in flight the engine keeps stepping until they arrive, normally on the next step.
- While the scheduler waits, the engine keeps stepping even with no request left (`has_pending_push_work()`), so the flush reaches the workers and their reports come back on an idle engine too.
- The scheduler logs when it starts and stops waiting for the reports, and warns once if that lasts more than 60 s; the check runs on every step, including the empty steps of an idle engine.

## Validation

**Regression through `LLM`** (GPU): `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py::test_tiering_cache_reset_resumes_promotions_on_idle_engine`. `facebook/opt-125m`, `TieringOffloadingSpec` with an `fs` tier, `async_scheduling=False`. The engine core and its worker run in the test process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`). A prefix is stored down to the `fs` tier; then the worker's job reports are withheld behind a `threading.Event` while another prompt's stores are issued, so `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` always finds them in flight (the test asserts that the hold started). The gate is opened, the idle engine is stepped until the hold is released, and the prefix must be promoted back from the `fs` tier (`num_cached_tokens == len(prefix)`). No retries and no log parsing.

On a DGX Spark (GB10), with `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-00b6c4c565` and this branch's changed Python files on top, this test and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_worker.py` pass (18 passed). An earlier revision without the `has_pending_push_work()` change failed with `TimeoutError: timed out after 30 s waiting for promotions to resume`.

**Scheduler-level tests** (CPU), in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`, on a real `Scheduler` whose `OffloadingConnector` runs the real `TieringOffloadingSpec` manager with an `example` secondary tier. A finished request leaves real store jobs in flight, the reset goes through `Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`, `schedule()` delivers `jobs_to_flush`, and the worker reports come back through `update_from_output()`. Only the workers are played, since the CPU job has no GPU transfers.

- `test_cache_reset_holds_promotions_until_flushed_jobs_report[True|False]`: `Scheduler.has_requests()` stays true until the flushed jobs report, the next step flushes exactly the in-flight jobs, and a secondary-tier-only key is a miss until their reports arrive and promotes after; without secondary tiers nothing is held. Without the `has_pending_push_work()` change it fails on `assert scheduler.has_requests()`.
- `test_cache_reset_fence_ignores_reports_of_other_jobs`: a late report of a job completed before the reset does not count as a flushed job's report.
- `test_cache_reset_without_in_flight_jobs_holds_nothing`: a reset with nothing in flight calls `on_reset_flushed()` at once and holds nothing.
- `test_cache_reset_fence_held_too_long_warns_on_idle_steps`: with a monkeypatched `time.monotonic` in the scheduler module, the 60 s warning fires on an empty step with no request left. It fails if the check runs only on lookups, as it did before.

- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::test_held_promotions_answer_peer_lookups_with_miss`: a real `P2PSecondaryTierManager` serves a peer under a real `TieringOffloadingManager`, next to an `example` tier that holds the key; a second P2P manager is the peer, and only the control and NIXL transports are faked (the existing loopback fakes). The peer's `LookupMsg` goes through the real `serve_external_requests()` path: after `reset_cache()` it is answered MISS and nothing is submitted to the `example` tier; after `on_reset_flushed()`, the same lookup starts the promotion. It fails if the hold is ignored. (`p2p` is the lightest in-tree serving tier; `kvcr` needs the external `kvcr` package.)
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py::test_held_promotions_keep_primary_hits`: while held, a CPU-tier chunk is still a hit; `test_reset_holds_promotions_until_flushed`: `reset_cache()` holds promotions and `on_reset_flushed()` releases them.

**Suites** (CPU-only container):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
# 1289 passed, 1 failed (on 71294c2e9a)
```

The one failure, `test_worker.py::test_register_packed_kv_caches_skips_scratch_group`, needs a GPU and fails the same way on `main`. The new `LLM` test runs in the "V1 KV Connectors" GPU step (`pytest -m 'not cpu_test' v1/kv_connector/unit`).

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files, and mypy reports no new errors in them.

There is still no reproducer of the data race itself: it needs a late worker DMA to land after a promotion's copy into the same chunk, which a test cannot force on real hardware.

## Details

**Root cause.** `reset_cache()`, reached through `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` (`POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true`, or `pause_generation(clear_cache=True)`), adds every in-flight job to `jobs_to_flush`, resets the manager, which frees their CPU-tier chunks, and drops later worker reports of those jobs through `_stale_job_threshold`. The workers submit and wait for the flushed jobs in `handle_preemptions()` of the next step they run. The scheduler builds that same step first, and its lookups run before any worker has seen the flush. On a secondary-tier hit, `TieringOffloadingManager.lookup()` reserves a free CPU-tier chunk (`_initiate_promotion()` → `primary_tier.prepare_write()`), which may be one the reset has just released, and the tier copies into it from the engine core after `on_schedule_end()`. Nothing orders that copy against the worker's DMA into the same chunk. If the DMA lands last, the chunk holds stale KV (or KV from blocks the GPU already reused) under the promoted key, and the next load hands it to the GPU. `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()` already drains the secondary tiers' own transfers for exactly this reason ("preferable to silent corruption from reusing primary slots while a transfer is mid-copy"); the workers' transfers were not covered.

The scheduler is not the only caller of `lookup()`. Tiers that serve external requests (`p2p`, `kvcr`) call it through their `ParentManager` from `serve_external_requests()`, in `on_schedule_end()` and on the tier-poll thread, and such a lookup promotes from any other secondary tier the same way.

**Why only promotions.** A promotion is the only write to a CPU-tier chunk that does not come from a worker. A worker submits the flushed stores and waits for them before it submits any job of a later step, and a load, or a secondary tier's read for a cascade or a peer, only uses a chunk whose post-reset store has completed. So a late worker write either finishes before anything that depends on the chunk or is overwritten by it. That is why lookups keep serving CPU-tier hits during the hold, and why engines without secondary tiers hold nothing.

**Fix.**

- `OffloadingManager.on_reset_flushed()` is new, a no-op by default: it is called once the workers have reported every job in flight at the last `reset_cache()`, so blocks that reset freed are no longer written by them.
- `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()` holds promotions when it has secondary tiers, and `on_reset_flushed()` releases them. While held, its `lookup()` returns `MISS` for a chunk that is not in the CPU tier, without querying the secondary tiers, whoever calls it. `MISS` rather than `RETRY`: `RETRY` would stall the request (and keep a peer's lookup pending) until the hold is released, while the chunk can simply be recomputed. The hold sits in the manager rather than the scheduler because peers' lookups reach `lookup()` without going through the scheduler.
- At reset, if any job is in flight, the scheduler records, for every flushed job, the worker reports still due (`pending_count`, so reports received before the reset count). Stale reports decrement it as they arrive, and the last one calls `on_reset_flushed()`; with nothing in flight it is called right away. The reports normally arrive within a step or two of the reset, so the cost is a short window without promotions.
- `has_pending_push_work()` also returns true while the scheduler waits for those reports. The reset clears `_jobs`, so without this an engine left with no request went idle before the flush reached the workers, and promotions (including peers' lookups) stayed held until unrelated work arrived.

**Limitations.** A worker that never reports its flushed jobs keeps promotions held; the warning makes that visible.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs (`reset_cache offloading`, `offload promotion reset`, `TieringOffloadingManager reset_cache`, `hold promotions offload`). None holds promotions across a reset. The closest are complementary:

- #59099 keeps the engine stepping until a reset's flush reaches the workers and makes `reset_cache()` re-entrant. This PR keeps the engine stepping only until the flushed jobs report; #59099 also covers engines without secondary tiers. A second reset before they report adds its own flushed jobs to the wait.
- #61667 quarantines `p2p` consumer slots whose remote write is unconfirmed. It covers a secondary tier's own late write, not a worker's.

**Related.** The multi-node CPU-region mirror proposed in #54415 (#62933) adds a second late writer, a remote node's pending slot push, and relies on this hook to cover it.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [KV Offload] Reject secondary tiers on engines that span nodes
author: javieratomic
body:
## Overview

This PR makes `TieringOffloadingSpec` fail at startup, instead of serving wrong KV, when secondary tiers run on an engine whose workers span several nodes (#54415).

It applies to `main` on its own and depends on no other PR. #62933 builds on it to support the multiprocessing executor with `--nnodes` > 1.

## Claims

- With secondary tiers and more than one worker, every worker checks at creation whether the engine's workers share a node, and raises `NotImplementedError` if they do not. This covers every way to place workers on several nodes (mp with `--nnodes`, Ray, `external_launcher`) without looking at the executor.
- Single-node engines, single-worker engines and engines without secondary tiers are unchanged.

## Validation

**Multi-node startup** on 2× DGX Spark (GB10), `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-00b6c4c565` with this branch's changed Python files on top, TP=2, mp executor with `--nnodes 2`, `facebook/opt-125m`:

- `TieringOffloadingSpec` with an `fs` tier: both workers fail at startup with `NotImplementedError: TieringOffloadingSpec secondary tiers are not supported on engines whose workers span several nodes.`
- `TieringOffloadingSpec` without secondary tiers: starts and serves; the same prompt sent twice gives the same output.

**Unit test:** `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py::test_tiering_spec_rejects_secondary_tiers_across_nodes` fakes the TP, PP and PCP groups and `in_the_same_node_as()`: it rejects a TP, PP or PCP group that spans nodes, accepts groups that each share a node, queries all three groups even after one spans nodes, and queries none without secondary tiers. Without the fix, four of its five cases fail. CI provides one host only, so it cannot run a real multi-node rejection.

**Suites** (CPU-only container):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
# 1286 passed, 1 failed (on 71294c2e9a)
```

The one failure, `test_worker.py::test_register_packed_kv_caches_skips_scratch_group`, needs a GPU and fails the same way on `main`; it passes on GPU.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** The tiering scheduler and its secondary tiers run in the engine core and address only its node's `/dev/shm` region. Since #58497 every worker writes the slot of its rank, but workers on other nodes write it into their own node's region. Secondary tiers therefore persist rows without those slots, and promotions never fill them.

**Detection.** An engine's workers form a grid of its TP, PP and PCP groups (DCP lives inside TP), so they all share one node exactly when each of those groups does. `create_worker()` therefore calls `in_the_same_node_as()` on each group with more than one rank. It is a collective over that group, which every worker of the group reaches during KV cache registration. Every rank runs all three before any of them raises, so a rank whose own TP group spans nodes cannot leave the ranks of a node-local TP group waiting in the PP or PCP collective. It runs only with secondary tiers, since without them each node's region serves its own workers.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for "54415 in:body", "multi-node offload", "secondary tiers nodes", "local_world_size offload" and "shared region node". #53474 also sizes node-local regions and rejects multi-node secondary tiers from the config; #46556 moves rank-local shards to a shared filesystem through worker transfers instead; #62058 and #53073 deal with `/dev/shm` capacity and region lifecycle, not with nodes.

**Docs:** `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md` states the restriction.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Perf] Bypass DispatchPooler grouping for homogeneous tasks
author: jzakrzew
body:
## Overview
When all requests use the same pooling task, `DispatchPooler` still slices metadata and hidden states, calls the sub-pooler, and converts its dense output into individual row tensors. Bypass grouping for homogeneous tasks and return the sub-pooler's output directly, allowing MRv2's existing dense output path to issue one D2H copy for a fully finished batch.


## Claims
- Improve short-query embedding throughput by **3.8% at concurrency 64** and **10.3% at concurrency 128** on the GH200 workload below. The gain comes from doing less CPU work per request on the EngineCore busy loop, which is the bottleneck in this scenario: one batched device-to-host copy per step instead of one copy, one pinned-memory allocation and one pinned free (with their CUDA event bookkeeping) per request.
- Avoid redundant pooling metadata operations and per-row D2H copies when the sub-pooler returns a dense batch. Ragged outputs and the mixed-task fallback remain supported.


## Validation


### Benchmark

Embedding throughput for short text queries on one NVIDIA GH200 (144 GB). Each row is the mean of 2 server starts with 2 runs of 30 s each.

- **Model:** `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16` with online FP8 (`--quantization fp8_per_tensor`).
- **Data:** ViDoRe v3 finance (English) queries (mean length 31 tokens).
- **Server:** `--api-server-count 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, V2 model runner, `orjson` present.
- **Client:** concurrent `/v1/embeddings` requests from 8 client processes on a separate NUMA node.

| Concurrency | Metric | main | This PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | Throughput (req/s) | 4082 | 4236 | **+3.8%** |
| 64 | Latency p50 (ms) | 15.7 | 15.1 | −3.8% |
| 64 | Latency p99 (ms) | 16.5 | 16.1 | −2.0% |
| 128 | Throughput (req/s) | 6044 | 6665 | **+10.3%** |
| 128 | Latency p50 (ms) | 21.2 | 19.2 | −9.5% |
| 128 | Latency p99 (ms) | 22.6 | 21.6 | −4.3% |

Embeddings match main within its run-to-run variation: the minimum cosine similarity over 512 queries is **0.9996**, the same as the comparison between two main runs.

### Local checks

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_methods.py -q
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/special.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_methods.py
```

**58 tests passed**, covering dense and ragged sequence outputs, unfinished token-pooling state, and mixed-task token offsets. All pre-commit hooks passed.

## Details
The implementation adds a homogeneous-task check before the existing grouping loop. Returning the sub-pooler's output unchanged preserves dense tensors instead of splitting them into Python row objects. Sub-poolers can still return ragged lists, including for requests with different embedding dimensions or token counts. Mixed tasks, empty batches, and unsupported tasks retain the existing fallback behavior.

Frontend pooling multi-task support was deprecated in #37956 and removed in #37861. Instances select one pooling task through `PoolerConfig(task=...)`, making homogeneous batches the normal frontend path even when a model supports multiple selectable tasks.

title: [Perf][glm5next] Add SM121 TP=2 skinny-GEMM plans for GLM-5.3-Flash
author: TimRen01
body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash decode TPOT **-15% at concurrency 1 on 2x DGX Spark (SM121, TP=2)** by running the BF16 decode GEMMs on the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM instead of cuBLAS. On `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` the attention projections (KDA and MLA), shared experts and LM head stay BF16 and take roughly 46 of a 68 ms decode step on cuBLAS gemv. `glm5next` has no low-latency GEMM module yet, so this adds one modelled on `qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py` (#59753, #59632, #61437) with measured SM121 skinny-GEMM plans for the TP=2 local shapes, installed from `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextMTP`. Supersedes #62949.

## Claims

- 7 local `(N, K)` shapes at M = 1/2/4 (20 entries), routed only on capability `(12, 1)`; other GPUs, dtypes, token counts and shapes keep the standard linear path (cuBLAS).
- Kernel: skinny GEMM is 1.35x to 1.73x faster than cuBLAS gemv at M=1 (238-283 GB/s vs 162-176 GB/s), 1.04x to 1.36x at M=2/4.
- End to end, no speculation, concurrency 1: TPOT 64.0 -> 54.1 ms (-15%), 15.3 -> 18.0 tok/s. With MTP k=3 the decode step is one verify pass at M=4 plus three draft passes at M=1: ITL -3.6%, TPOT -2.7%, 26.7 -> 27.8 tok/s.
- GSM8K (n=100): 93 with cuBLAS, 94 with skinny GEMM.

## Validation

Kernel, cuBLAS (`F.linear`) vs skinny GEMM through the module path on GB10 (CUDA graph replay, weight rotated out of L2, nightly 8e2beaa3bf), cosine 1.000000 between the two outputs for every entry:

| shape (N, K) | layer | M | cuBLAS (us) | skinny GEMM (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (12576, 4096) | KDA in_proj | 1 | 608 | 429 | 1.42x |
|  |  | 2 | 453 | 425 | 1.07x |
|  |  | 4 | 450 | 429 | 1.05x |
| (4096, 4096) | KDA o_proj | 1 | 203 | 137 | 1.48x |
|  |  | 2 | 147 | 136 | 1.08x |
|  |  | 4 | 148 | 140 | 1.06x |
| (2048, 4096) | shared gate_up, MLA qkv_a | 1 | 103 | 64 | 1.61x |
|  |  | 2 | 78 | 64 | 1.22x |
|  |  | 4 | 79 | 63 | 1.24x |
| (4096, 1024) | shared down | 1 | 51 | 30 | 1.73x |
|  |  | 2 | 39 | 29 | 1.34x |
|  |  | 4 | 39 | 29 | 1.36x |
| (8192, 1536) | MLA q_b | 1 | 147 | 102 | 1.44x |
|  |  | 2 | 115 | 102 | 1.13x |
|  |  | 4 | 122 | 101 | 1.20x |
| (4096, 8192) | MLA o_proj | 1 | 291 | - | not included |
|  |  | 2 | 289 | 278 | 1.04x |
|  |  | 4 | 300 | 280 | 1.07x |
| (77440, 4096) | lm_head | 1 | 3606 | 2663 | 1.35x |
|  |  | 2 | 2789 | 2655 | 1.05x |
|  |  | 4 | 2741 | 2581 | 1.06x |

These are cold-L2 numbers, which is the serving case: decode reads each weight once per step and 45 layers do not fit the 24 MB L2. Weighted by how often each shape runs in a decode step, the entries save about 13 ms per step at M=1 and 3 ms at M=2 or M=4 in the probe; the server gains 10 ms at M=1 because the GEMMs interleave with MoE and attention. MLA o_proj at M=1 is not included: cuBLAS already streams this shape at 231 GB/s (162-176 GB/s on the other shapes), so the best skinny config from the sweep gained only 3% in the module path, under the 5% bar. M=8/16 are within 2% of cuBLAS and are not listed.

End to end, cuBLAS (current main) vs skinny GEMM (this PR): `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` TP=2 on two Sparks, FP8 KV, SPEED-Bench 2K in / 1K out, 8 requests at concurrency 1, greedy (`--temperature 0`), two interleaved runs per arm (each cell lists run 1 / run 2), nightly 8e2beaa3bf:

| | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | GSM8K (n=100) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cuBLAS (main) | 64.17 / 63.83 | 63.94 / 63.68 | 15.27 / 15.33 | 93 |
| skinny GEMM (this PR) | 54.14 / 54.10 | 54.03 / 53.96 | 18.02 / 18.03 | 94 |
| change (mean of the two runs) | **-15.4%** | -15.4% | +17.8% | +1 |

With MTP k=3 (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.875 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8`, same nightly and sampling):

| | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cuBLAS (main) | 36.05 / 36.11 | 102.72 / 103.27 | 26.79 / 26.66 | 2.87 / 2.87 |
| skinny GEMM (this PR) | 35.08 / 35.16 | 99.18 / 99.41 | 27.51 / 28.02 | 2.85 / 2.90 |
| change (mean of the two runs) | -2.7% | **-3.6%** | +3.9% | +0.2% |

With MTP the ITL is the decode step (one verify pass at M=4 plus three draft passes at M=1); TPOT and tok/s divide it by the tokens accepted per step. Under greedy decoding the acceptance length stays within 2.85-2.90 across the four runs, so the step gain carries over: TPOT -2.7%, tok/s +3.9%. An earlier 4-request run at model-default sampling gave -12% without speculation (the number in the commit message); with MTP its acceptance length swung 3% between repeats, which hid the step gain.

An nsys census of the skinny GEMM arm shows every listed shape on `CuteSkinnyGemm` in the server (45% of GPU time without speculation, 39.5% with MTP); what is left on cuBLAS is KDA `f_b`/`g_b` (4096, 128) (#57617), the fp32-output router gate (288, 4096) and MLA o_proj at M=1.

Tests: `pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm5next`, 26 passed on GB10 (table validity, capability routing, hook installation, 20 selected shapes with cosine > 0.999 against `F.linear`). The selected-shape test skips off capability (12, 1), which CI does not have.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# on each DGX Spark, --node-rank 0 / 1
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \
  --master-addr 192.168.100.1 --master-port 29500 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.84 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prefix-caching --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --reasoning-parser glm45 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
# MTP k=3 arm: add --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
#   and use --gpu-memory-utilization 0.875 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8
# SPEED_BENCH_DIR holds throughput_2k.jsonl, built from nvidia/SPEED-Bench with NeMo-Skills prepare.py
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path $SPEED_BENCH_DIR --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_2k \
  --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --num-warmups 2 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1 \
  --temperature 0 --seed 0
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm5next
```

</details>

## Details

- Plans come from a CUDA-graph sweep over block_size, outputs_per_block, k_unroll, vector_width and static_k with the weight rotated out of L2, keeping entries that beat cuBLAS by more than 5%. `(2048, 4096)` serves both the shared-expert gate/up and the MLA fused q_a/kv_a projection.
- The replacement method follows the quant method the layer carries: a quant config that excludes `lm_head` gives `ParallelLMHead` an `UnquantizedLinearMethod` rather than an `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, and the head stayed on cuBLAS until this was handled.
- Not covered: TP=1 (the model does not fit one Spark), KDA `f_b`/`g_b` `(4096, 128)` (#57617), MTP `eh_proj` (a plain `nn.Linear`), and M=3, which uses cuBLAS.

Add optional `WatermarkConfig.enforce` (default `False`) so deployments can override request-level watermarking opt-outs. Without enforcement, existing behavior is unchanged.
