title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Reserve in-flight imports' host pages at admission
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #62217. Alternative to #62230.

HiSparse admits an async KV load only if its prompt fits in free host pages, but it ignores pages that earlier admitted loads still need. Two waiting loads can each hold pages the other needs. Waiting requests are never preempted, so the scheduler stalls forever with `running == []`.

Fix: reserve host pages for admitted loads, as `reserved_blocks` does for the GPU pool. The change is confined to `HiSparseSourceManager` and `HiSparseCoordinator`; the scheduler loop is unchanged.

- At admission of a load, `HiSparseSourceManager` sizes its host pages (prompt + spec decode step) and admits it only if they fit beside the pages other loads still need.
- The coordinator keeps a running total of outstanding pages (O(1) check), reduced as each load allocates its pages and dropped when the request is freed.
- Local admissions are not gated (they can be preempted), matching the GPU pool.

Alternatives: #62230 skips past held waiting requests in the scheduler loop. It changes the core loop, can starve the head of the queue, and still deadlocks when no admitted load fits.

Trade-off: a load whose host pages don't fit beside those reserved for in-flight loads waits for them, instead of being admitted and risking the deadlock.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Repro: both cases fail on main ({'first', 'second'} == {'first'}), pass here
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running

pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py   # 1x H100
```

New/extended tests in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`:
- `test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running`: the issue's scenario, plus an MTP case where the first load to resume has no host page for its draft tokens.
- `test_hisparse_async_admission_fits_beside_inflight_import`: boundary case, a load that exactly fits is admitted.
- `test_hisparse_import_reservation_released`: released on free and on resume.
- `test_hisparse_import_reservation_does_not_gate_local_admissions`.

## Test Result

- Unit (CPU): all pass. 3 unrelated failures (`test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, `test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter[FULL|NONE]`) fail identically on `main` locally.
- E2E (1x H100, `f96ae2830d`): `test_hisparse.py` 5 passed (`standalone-fa4` skips on SM90). New path exercised: in the `offload` case (HiSparse + OffloadingConnector), a coordinator probe logged the load sized at 5 pages, a 2-page reservation, and its release to 0 on resume.

## Performance

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 P/D on 8x B200: TP4 NIXL prefiller + TP4 HiSparse decoder (`MultiConnector[HiSparse, Nixl]`, `host_pool_gib=8`), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` on both servers.

```bash
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 512 \
  --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

Fresh decoder per run, interleaved. NIXL over TCP (no IB on that node), so the run is transfer-bound with the host pool ~96% full.

| Decoder | Output tok/s (2 runs) | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR (`c02494d57c`) | 191.52, 184.44 | 68.9 s, 72.3 s | 17.00, 16.82 ms |
| `main` (`cc1a6d3135`) | 182.61, 185.10 | 73.2 s, 73.0 s | 17.26, 16.33 ms |

No regression; at most 11 of 2,949 host pages were reserved. Without MTP, a P/D load allocates all its host pages at admission and nothing is reserved, so admission matches `main` exactly (verified on an earlier revision over IB: 580–581 tok/s in both arms).

title: [Bugfix] Support online quantization of Kimi K3 NVIDIA projections
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose

Fix online quantization of the Kimi K3 NVIDIA projections, e.g.

```
--quantization-config '{"targets":{"*.in_proj_qkvgfab":"mxfp8","*.fused_qkv_a_g_proj":"mxfp8","*.routed_expert_down_proj":"mxfp8","*.routed_expert_up_proj":"mxfp8"}}'
```

Three places in the model broke:

- **KDA input projection padding.** `in_proj_qkvgfab` pads each TP-local row block for alignment. No checkpoint shard covers that padding, but online processing counted it toward the layer's expected load size, so the layer never reached completion and every KDA layer was deferred to `finalize_layerwise_processing`, keeping all its buffered checkpoint tensors alive until the end of loading. The projection now declares `weight_loader_numel` without the padding. Online processing also rebuilds the weight from uninitialized storage, so the padding is re-zeroed after each shard load (both `weight_loader` and `weight_loader_v2`).
- **Routed output transform.** `KimiRoutedOutputTransform` fused the residual add as `residual.addmm_(x, up_proj.weight.t())`, bypassing the quantized linear method and its scales. The fused add is now used only for an unquantized up-projection; otherwise the layer is called and the residual added in place.
- **Latent MoE tail kernels.** They multiply by the raw `up_proj.weight`, so `LatentMoERunner` now enables the fused tail path (and deferred MoE finalize) only for an unquantized up-projection.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k nvidia_kda_online_loading
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py -k deferred_finalize
```

The new KDA test (adapted from the reproducer in #61950) loads the merged projection through online processing for 96 heads (padded) and 128 heads (no padding), TP ranks 0 and 3, and both weight loaders (in forward and reverse shard order). It checks that the layer finishes loading, every source tensor is released, the loaded rows match the checkpoint, and the padding is zero (uninitialized storage is filled with NaN to catch it).

End to end: Kimi K3 MXFP4 on GB300, 2P1D (TP8 prefill x 2, DEP16 decode, 32 GPUs), DSpark K4, AgentX agentic traces at concurrency 240 for 3600 s, with and without online MXFP8 quantization of the KDA/MLA input projections, routed expert projections, and (decode only) `o_proj` and the shared experts.

## Test Result

Performance (p90; the perf runs use synthetic acceptance with AL 3.36):

| | Base | Online quant | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | 19,991 | 24,769 | +23.9 % |
| Interactivity (tok/s/user) | 40.0 | 40.5 | +1.2 % |
| E2E latency (s) | 78.2 | 59.8 | -23.4 % |
| TTFT (s) | 21.8 | 12.2 | -43.9 % |
| E2E-normalized interactivity | 6.9 | 12.5 | +79.8 % |

Accuracy (gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, real rejection sampling, 1P1D TP8 + DEP16):

| | Base | Online quant |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match | 0.9606 | 0.9674 |

title: [ROCm] Revert "[ROCm][Build] Compile paged attention kernels in parallel (7.6x faster attention build) (#62475)"
author: micah-wil
body:
## Overview

Reverts #62475 to unblock the ROCm 10.0 nightly while we pick a proper fix.

## Claims

- Fixes the `Build release image - x86_64 - ROCm 10.0` nightly failure: the `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link fails with `mold: relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against .eh_frame out of range`.

## Validation

Built and linked the full `_rocm_C` with this revert in the ROCm 10.0 CI build image (same compiler, mold, 9 release archs, `RelWithDebInfo`): link succeeds.

## Details

**Root cause:** `_rocm_C`'s embedded GPU code (`.hip_fatbin`) was already ~1.94 GiB, ~80% of it uncompressed GPU debug info. Splitting attention into 12 files duplicates that debug info per file and pushed the library past the 2 GiB relocation limit. This revert only gets us back under it, with ~64 MB of headroom.

**Alternatives** (each lets us reland #62475). Measured on one attention file, 9 archs:

| Option | GPU code size | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Today | 137 MiB | | |
| `-Xarch_device -g0` | 36 MiB (−74%) | Simple; ~20% faster compile | No GPU debug info (no kernel source debugging, no source lines for GPU faults) |
| `--offload-compress` | 4.9 MiB (−96%) | Keeps full debug info; output unchanged after decompression; smaller wheel | Decompression at module load (not yet measured on GPU); needs ROCm ≥ 6.2 |

Either option is a one-line CMake change. Both make every HIP object miss sccache once, so the next nightly after either lands is a cold build.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3] MonoKernel: serve EAGLE3 verify steps
author: micah-wil
body:
## Summary
`--monokernel` (MiniMax-M3 FFN MonoKernel, #62712) previously refused speculative decoding. The fused FFN launch is per-row and reads no KV cache, so EAGLE3 verify rows need only host-side changes:
- The config refusal accepts `eagle3` (all other spec methods are still refused).
- Routing drops the one-token-per-request checks: a decode step with <= 16 rows and no prefill runs fused (eager or FULL graph); larger or mixed steps run stock.
- The mono layer loop captures EAGLE3 aux hidden states.

No kernel changes and no core vLLM changes.

## Results (MI355X, TP4, MT-Bench, FULL graphs, EAGLE3 k=3)
Identical flags on both arms except `--monokernel`. Two interleaved rounds, which agreed within 0.04 ms.

| Concurrency | ITL p50 stock -> mono | Output tok/s stock -> mono | Acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.98 -> **6.11 ms (-12.5%)** | 383 -> **435 (+13.6%)** | 2.78 / 2.78 |
| 2 | 8.03 -> **7.25 ms (-9.7%)** | 617 -> **683 (+10.7%)** | 2.74 / 2.76 |
| 4 | 9.11 -> 9.01 ms (-1%) | 1019 -> 1028 (+0.9%) | 2.83 / 2.79 |

Above 4 requests (more than 16 verify rows), steps run stock, so behavior is unchanged.

GSM8K 5-shot (500 samples, paired): mono+EAGLE3 0.892 vs stock+EAGLE3 0.900 (-0.8 pp, 95% CI [-3.7, +2.1], McNemar p=0.69).

## Serve command
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --block-size 128 --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64]}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --moe-backend aiter \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --monokernel   # omitted for the stock arm
```
Capture sizes in multiples of 4 are recommended: MRV2 rounds spec graph sizes to multiples of 4, so without 12, three requests pad to a 16-row graph.

## Benchmark command
```bash
vllm bench serve --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path philschmid/mt-bench --skip-chat-template \
  --hf-output-len 1024 --temperature 0 --seed 1234 \
  --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1   # c in {1, 2, 4}; num-prompts = max(16, 4*c)
```

## Tests
`tests/models/minimax_m3/amd_specialized_decode/`:
- New mini-model test (4 GPUs): EAGLE3 FULL-graph verify steps at 4/8/12/16 rows run fused and match native teacher-forced logprobs (cos 0.9991); a late rank fault during a verify step returns no token.
- Routing unit tests for q=4 at 4/8/12/16 rows (including padded rows); 20 rows, prefill and PIECEWISE steps route to stock.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization][Spec Decode] Load ModelOpt mixed-precision DFlash and DSpark drafts
author: sragrawal
body:
## Overview

Fix loading of nested ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` checkpoints, quantization
settings for DFlash/DSpark drafts, and per-tensor FP8 normalization on FNUZ GPUs.
This incorporates the parser fix from the
earlier closed, unmerged [PR #36312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36312)
and adds draft-layer name mapping, regression tests, CI coverage and documentation.

## Claims

- Nested `MIXED_PRECISION` metadata selects the existing `modelopt_mixed` backend.
- ModelOpt draft settings match the weight aliases, runtime module prefix and
  decoder layer offset before quantized layers are constructed.
- Per-tensor FP8 weights and static input scales are normalized for FNUZ GPUs
  such as AMD MI300, using the existing conversion helper.
- Other quantization backends retain their existing quantization-config handling.
  No FP8 kernel changes are needed.

## Validation

The current source passes 24 focused CPU checks and changed-file pre-commit,
including mypy and CI selection. CPU checks used Torch 2.13.0+cpu and
Transformers 5.17.0; current main pins Torch 2.14.0.

AMD CI exposed an existing per-tensor FP8 loader omission: both checkpoint
regressions failed during engine initialization at `input.dtype == weight.dtype`
in [MI300 quantization CI](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96958#01a16a9a-8a0e-4f38-8027-3356b1307ef8).
The loader retained FN weights while the activation quantizer selected FNUZ.
The fix applies the existing FN-to-FNUZ normalization before requantization,
including both weight and static input scales. The existing regressions now
require the exact platform dtype and input scale. Fresh AMD validation is
pending CI. A CPU check confirmed the conversion preserves dequantized weights, including
negative zero, while doubling both scales.

GPU validation below used vLLM 0.32.0 with the source fixes backported. The
checkpoint-loading regressions are retained, with shared fixture setup and
the existing speculative-metric reader. GPU tests were not rerun for this
cleanup; the full current-main environment and full suites remain untested.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native/legacy mixed config, uppercase/lowercase | Four mixed-config failures; NVFP4 control passes | All five cases pass |
| Draft mapping, aliases, offsets and Quark preservation | Missing runtime-name mapping | 17 CPU cases pass against real quantization configurations |
| Small mixed Llama checkpoint through `LLM` | Config conversion fails | Loads actual FP8/BF16 layers; nested/flat metadata produce identical completions |
| Small mixed DSpark checkpoint through `LLM` | Missing `fc.weight_scale` parameter | Mixed FP8 `fc`, Markov and offset decoder projections; positive proposals and exact OFF/ON token equality |

Observed errors before the respective fixes:

```text
Value error, Unknown ModelOpt quant algo: MIXED_PRECISION

ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'fc.weight_scale' in Qwen3DSparkModel. The available parameters belonging to fc (ReplicatedLinear) are: {'fc.weight'}
```

The small GPU regressions create random checkpoints and integer token prompts
locally. Exact comparisons use batch invariance. CI dependencies and the
rendered ModelOpt documentation are updated. Changed-file pre-commit checks
pass, including mypy and CI test selection.

Additional GPT-OSS-20B mixed-FP8 DSpark smoke on B200, TP=1, fixed K=2:

- All 1,120 output tokens across 35 prompts match SpecDec OFF.
- 2,140 tokens were proposed and 16 accepted with normal verification.
- Runtime inspection confirms per-channel weight and per-token activation FP8
  for `fc`, and per-tensor FP8 for the Markov output projection.
- Export files are unchanged.

The GPT-OSS draft was trained for eight optimizer updates and quantized with
synthetic calibration inputs. These are functional smoke results, not a held-out
quality evaluation or a speedup measurement. Other hardware, tensor-parallel
sizes and quantization formats were not tested.

<details>
<summary>Regression commands</summary>

Repository test entrypoints:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k modelopt -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_modelopt_mixed_nvfp4.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'draft_quant_config or draft_weight_aliases' -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'nested_mixed_checkpoint or mixed_dspark_checkpoint' -v
```

Earlier GPU execution used the vLLM 0.32 compatibility setup described above.
The regression bodies at that point ran with the real stock test fixture:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider \
  -v -s test_gpu_regression.py
```

Each GPU regression passes after its fix and fails before it with the error
shown above. Current-main GPU execution remains pending.

</details>

## Details

There are two failures. Config conversion rejects nested `MIXED_PRECISION`
metadata before the existing backend can load it. After that is fixed, the
draft loader looks up per-layer settings using runtime names such as `model.fc`,
while the checkpoint names the layer `fc`. It builds an unquantized projection
and then fails to load `fc.weight_scale`.

The shared `map_draft_quant_config` helper in `models/utils.py` maps ModelOpt's
draft settings through the existing weight aliases, module prefix and decoder
layer offset before constructing the layers. Apply this
only to ModelOpt: other backends can use semantic configuration keys or suffix
rules that must not receive a module prefix.

Related work has different scope: [#49900](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49900)
handles `draft_model.` prefixes in another proposer path;
[#53122](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53122) configures draft
quantization aliases and context-KV projection, without this runtime-root and
teacher-layer remapping. No equivalent open PR was found.

AI-assisted implementation and testing using Codex.

title: [Perf][Frontend] Build run-batch TypeAdapters once instead of per request
author: inc-jeong
body:
## Overview `vllm run-batch` builds a new pydantic `TypeAdapter` for each `/v1/embeddings`, `/score` and fallback input line, and for each `JSONResponse` it converts back. Each build regenerates the core schema, which costs about 0.5 ms. This PR builds the four adapters once at module level. ## Claims - In the current run-batch flow, the per-line frontend cost for an embeddings batch drops from 1,952 µs to 178 µs (~11×, median of 3 runs). For a 1.45M-line batch, single-threaded frontend CPU time drops from about 47 min to about 4.3 min. - The event-loop ceiling of `run_one_request` rises from about 800 to about 6,600 req/s. - Behavior does not change. Parsed bodies, validation errors (type, loc and msg), and converted responses are identical before and after. ## Validation **Regression test.** `test_requests_and_responses_reuse_type_adapters` wraps `TypeAdapter` in a spy, parses embeddings, score and fallback lines, and runs one `JSONResponse` through `run_request`. It also asserts the parsed body types and the converted error response. ``` # base (30aded62d4), fix reverted $ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k reuse_type_adapters E AssertionError: Expected 'mock' to not have been called. Called 8 times. 1 failed, 55 deselected # this PR $ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k reuse_type_adapters 1 passed, 55 deselected ``` **Existing unit tests.** All tests in `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py` that do not launch a model pass locally (43 passed). The 13 model-backed tests (`test_embeddings`, `test_score`, ...) need a vLLM build I don't have on macOS, so they are left to the Entrypoints Unit CI step. **Equivalence.** I compared the original and patched modules side by side on 13 input lines and 4 responses. Inputs: embeddings str/list/tokens/chat, extra field, missing input, bad type, score text/queries-documents/invalid, chat, fallback valid/invalid. Responses: embedding, error, unparseable body, handler exception. All 17 results are identical. **Microbenchmark.** Apple M1 Pro, CPU only. 20k `/v1/embeddings` lines (`dimensions=128`) and a stub handler that returns an `EmbeddingResponse` as a `JSONResponse`. No model or engine is involved. The table shows the median of 3 alternating runs, with the range in brackets. | step | before | after | |---|---|---| | pass 1: `validate_batch` | 689 µs [678–718] | 26 µs [25–27] | | pass 2: `run_one_request` (parse + handler + response conversion) | 1,254 µs [1,233–1,441] | 151 µs [144–154] | | **total per line** | **1,952 µs [1,932–2,130]** | **178 µs [169–179]** | | 1.45M lines (scaled) | 47.2 min | 4.3 min | **End to end.** I have not run an end-to-end comparison on main. In our deployment on v0.31.0, which has the same per-request `TypeAdapter` code, a 1.45M-line embeddings batch spent 25.5 min just reading input (~950 lines/s). Processing was capped at 1,150–1,600 req/s, which matches the ~0.63 ms per response conversion on the event loop. With this change applied as a patch, the end-to-end batch time went from about 60 min to about 20 min.
Benchmark script (python bench_run_batch.py path/to/run_batch.py) ```python """Per-line cost of the run-batch flow: validate_batch pass + run_one_request. Usage: python bench_run_batch.py """ import asyncio import hashlib import importlib.util import io import json import random import sys import time from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.embed.protocol import ( EmbeddingResponse, EmbeddingResponseData, ) import vllm.entrypoints.launchers # noqa: F401 (parent package for relative imports) spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( "vllm.entrypoints.launchers.rb_bench", sys.argv[1] ) rb = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) spec.loader.exec_module(rb) N_IN, N_REQ, PROD = 20000, 5000, 1_451_852 print("module:", sys.argv[1]) base = "Recent interests: camping gear, hiking boots, outdoor clothing, travel, coffee. " lines = [ json.dumps( { "custom_id": "_" + hashlib.md5(str(i).encode()).hexdigest(), "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": { "model": "vllm", "input": (base * (1 + i % 4)) + f"#{i}", "dimensions": 128, }, }, ensure_ascii=False, ) for i in range(N_IN) ] for ln in lines[:200]: rb.BatchRequestInput.model_validate_json(ln) def report(label, per_us): print(f"{label:<34} per={per_us:8.1f}us -> {per_us * PROD / 1e6 / 60:5.1f} min") t0 = time.perf_counter() for ln in lines: rb.BatchRequestInput.model_validate_json(ln) report("parse model_validate_json", (time.perf_counter() - t0) / N_IN * 1e6) t0 = time.perf_counter() n = rb.validate_batch(io.StringIO("\n".join(lines) + "\n")) assert n == N_IN validate_per = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / N_IN * 1e6 report("pass1 validate_batch", validate_per) usage = EmbeddingResponse.model_fields["usage"].annotation(prompt_tokens=30, total_tokens=30) rnd = random.Random(0) payloads = [ EmbeddingResponse( id="embd-x", created=0, model="vllm", data=[ EmbeddingResponseData( index=0, embedding=[rnd.uniform(-0.2, 0.2) for _ in range(128)] ) ], usage=usage, ).model_dump() for _ in range(N_REQ) ] async def run_all(): it = iter(payloads) async def handler(_body): return JSONResponse(content=next(it)) registry = { "embeddings": { "url": "/v1/embeddings", "handler_getter": lambda: handler, "wrapper_fn": None, } } t0 = time.perf_counter() outs = [await rb.run_one_request(lines[i], registry) for i in range(N_REQ)] return outs, time.perf_counter() - t0 outs, el = asyncio.run(run_all()) bad = sum( 1 for o in outs if o.error is not None or not isinstance(o.response.body, EmbeddingResponse) ) run_per = el / N_REQ * 1e6 report("pass2 run_one_request (loop)", run_per) print(f" bad={bad}, event-loop cap ~{1e6 / run_per:,.0f} req/s") report("total pass1 + pass2", validate_per + run_per) ```
## Details **Root cause.** - Input side: `TypeAdapter(...)` inside `BatchRequestInput.check_type_for_url`, added in #12420. - Response side: `TypeAdapter(AllResponse | ErrorResponse)` in `run_request`, added in #28631. It also builds a new `Union` object on every call, so caching by type identity would not help. A module constant is the simplest fix. - Since #52505, each line is parsed twice: once in `validate_batch` before the engine starts, and again in `run_one_request` on the event loop. That doubles the input-side cost. **Import cost.** Building the four adapters adds about 2–3 ms at import. `vllm.entrypoints.cli.run_batch.subparser_init` imports this module for every `vllm` CLI invocation, including `vllm serve`, so the cost applies there too. It is negligible against the module's ~9 s import. **Safety.** `TypeAdapter.validate_python` does not keep per-call state, so sharing one adapter across concurrent requests is safe. vLLM never calls `model_rebuild` on these models at runtime, so a cached adapter cannot hold a stale schema. **Scope.** I checked the other per-call `TypeAdapter(...)` sites under `vllm/entrypoints`. They run only on rare paths: a dict `structural_tag` `response_format`, and the Responses API streaming error path. `sagemaker` already caches its adapters. This PR leaves them alone. **Duplicate check.** As of 2026-10-22, searching vllm-project/vllm issues and PRs for `TypeAdapter run_batch` / `run_batch TypeAdapter` returns nothing. None of the open PRs that touch `run_batch` (#51859, #57825, #59716) change this code. ---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Reset the store cursor when a request restarts from token 0
author: AdvayMonga
body:
## Overview

A request resumed from preemption kept `next_stored_chunk_idx` from before the preemption. If the CPU tier had evicted its chunks meanwhile, the chunks below the cursor were never offered again and everything stored afterwards sat behind a chunk-0 miss. Reset the cursor in `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, which only runs when a request starts from `num_computed_tokens == 0`.

## Claims

- A resumed request offers its chunks from chunk 0 again; `prepare_store` drops the ones still resident, so nothing is stored twice.
- A CPU prefix hit on resume is unchanged: `update_state_after_alloc` still raises the cursor afterwards.

## Validation

- `test_request_preemption` gains a `cpu_hit=False` case that fails on `main` and passes here, both scheduling modes.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector`: 609 passed, 2 skipped. `pre-commit` clean.
- No open PR or issue covers this (searched `next_stored_chunk_idx`, `preempt offload`); #57813, #61375, #60574, #60810 and #62929 touch nearby code and compose with it.

## Details

`_reset_cache` already resets the cursor for the same reason. The reset cannot live in `_update_req_states` under `if preempted:`, which runs after `update_state_after_alloc` in the same step and would clobber the hit-derived cursor.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; I reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Tile the NVFP4 compressed-KV dequant-gather
author: nbommi19
body:
## Overview

Speed up `_dequantize_and_gather_k_nvfp4_kernel`, the Triton kernel that dequantizes and gathers the DeepSeek-V4.1 NVFP4 compressed K cache (`nvfp4_ds_mla`) for sparse prefill. Output is bit-identical.

## Why

- The old kernel handled one token per loop iteration: a chain of dependent block-table, record and scale loads, so long gathers were bound by load latency, not memory bandwidth.
- The new kernel handles 8 tokens per iteration with one vector load each for block ids, packed values and scales, and decodes e2m1 with exact bit placement instead of `exp2`/`select`.
- Replaced in place: same signature and callers, no new flags, other cache formats unchanged.

## Results (B300, kernel time)

| gather | before (us) | after (us) | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 x 16K rows | 17.4 | 11.3 | 1.5x |
| 8 x 64K rows | 341.0 | 128.0 | 2.7x |
| 32 x 100K rows | 1,707 | 722 | 2.4x |
| skewed: 1 x 100K + 3 x 64 rows | 181.2 | 33.8 | 5.4x |

- Single-request gathers of up to ~1K rows are within one ~2 us timer tick of the old kernel.
- End to end at 16-32K contexts there is no measurable change: the gather is well under 1% of a prefill step. Output is bit-identical, so accuracy is unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py
```

- B300: 180 passed, 19 skipped (the skips are ROCm-only).
- The new tests compare raw bits against the previous kernel, kept in the test as the reference. They cover ragged batches (empty requests, partial last blocks, a context past the grid cap, `-1` in unread block-table slots, random cache bytes including NaN and subnormal scales), plus every (packed byte, scale byte) pair.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: tuned K1/K2 for the TP2 compress-ratio-2 layers on MI355X
author: chao-xu-spec
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Faster K1/K2 for the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode layer on gfx950 (MI355X), applied only to the compress-ratio-2 target layers at TP2. A static build flag, `MonoBuild.tuned`, selects the new paths; their outputs are bit-identical to main's, and every other build (ratio 0/1, TP4, DSpark draft, gfx942, FFN launch) compiles to the same MLIR as on main.

1. **Tuned builds of the ratio-2 layers**: the `MonoBuild.tuned` gate with its own scratch; unsigned index math in the MoE stages; polled ready flags replicated on separate lines; independent loads issued ahead of waits.
2. **Down stage**: two-task down CTAs pipeline their rounds through LDS; their shared-expert down rows are offloaded to the next one-task CTAs.
3. **FFN seam and attention hand-offs**: a shorter seam -> norm -> router chain, whole-sector attention partials, per-tile `wo_a` ready flags.

Each commit builds and is bit-exact on its own. Related: #61482 (moves these kernels to `vllm/models/common/amd/mono/`).

**Rebased** onto main 8977b13a1c, which includes #63576 (K2's combine awaits `krdy` before reading `klen` in index-source launches) and #63689 (vLLM's scale code for zero and subnormal MXFP8 groups). Both fixes apply to the tuned builds as well: the tuned paths share `stage_combine` and its `krdy` wait, and quantize with the same `vllm_mx_code` / `mx_code`. No conflicts; the diff is unchanged.

**Result vs main:** ratio-2 layer K1+K2 8.6-18.1% faster (M = 1..48), index-source launches included; E2E TPOT p50 −3.3% (c32) and −3.7% (c4).

## Validation

8x MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce39` (AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0; no kernel or build changes between it and the base commit); only the Python tree differs between arms.

**Repo tests**

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py \
  tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py
```

| GPUs | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 80 passed, 2 skipped (gfx942 only) | 80 passed, 2 skipped (gfx942 only) |
| 2 | 78 passed, 4 skipped (2 need 4 GPUs) | 78 passed, 4 skipped (2 need 4 GPUs) |

The numerics test also checks the tuned layer bit for bit against a `generic=True` runner at 12/36/48 rows.

**Correctness vs main**: 115/115 cases bit-identical at TP2 (92 on tuned builds; all K1+K2 outputs and the SWA cache, hashed per rank, index-source and no-fold launches included). The MLIR of every non-tuned build is byte-identical to main's (168/168 gfx950, 76/76 gfx942).

**Layer microbench** (TP2, ratio 2, K1+K2 µs per layer, cold L2, max over ranks, median of 11 fresh runs on 3 GPU pairs):

| M | 1 | 6 | 12 | 18 | 24 | 36 | 48 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 89.1 | 134.4 | 194.1 | 238.2 | 292.8 | 402.1 | 472.2 |
| this PR | 73.0 | 118.6 | 173.0 | 208.3 | 259.1 | 360.2 | 431.8 |
| change | −18.1% | −11.7% | −10.9% | −12.6% | −11.5% | −10.4% | −8.6% |

Weighted by the widths served at c32 / c4: −10.7% / −11.6%. Index-source launches (the ratio-2 layers that feed the indexer, which now wait on `krdy`): −8.9% to −17.3%, weighted −10.9% / −11.4% (7 runs); the `krdy` wait itself costs < 0.6% on main and on this PR.

**E2E** (TP2 + MTP, agentic-coding trace, 1 h per run, CI server arguments; main and this PR on two lanes at once, swapped in a second wave; mean of the two waves vs main; measured before the rebase, same kernel code):

| vs main | c32 | c4 |
|---|---|---|
| TPOT p50 | **−3.31%** | **−3.74%** |
| TPOT p90 | −1.22% | −6.84% |
| interactivity p50 | +3.49% | +3.78% |
| interactivity p90 | +1.16% | +7.59% |
| output tok/s/GPU | +0.53% | −0.66% |
| per-request ITL ratio | 0.973 / 0.976 | 0.970 / 0.960 |

MTP acceptance length 3.51 in every run; TTFT within run-to-run noise.

## Details

**Where it applies**: gfx950, TP 2, compress ratio 2, the target's routing (384 experts, top-6) and SWA window. The gate is static per build; no new flag or env var.

**Tradeoff**: tuned builds lay out their scratch differently, so the runner keys scratch by (width, tuned): up to ~20 MB per tuned width per rank. Peer memory is unchanged.

**Not covered**: gfx942 and DSpark draft builds were not run on GPU (MLIR identical to main's); TP4 is not tuned.

title: [Perf][DSpark] Stack DeepSeek V41 context WKV projections
author: chaunceyjiang
body:
## Overview

Replace DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark’s per-layer context Q+KV projections with one stacked KV-only projection. The existing context path computes Q values that are immediately discarde

refer to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54674

## Claims

- Compute context KV for all draft layers with one MergedColumnParallelLinear.
- Reuse the existing V4 weight-duplication helper to load each layer’s WKV weights and scales into the stacked projection.


## Validation

### microbenchmark

<details>
<summary> script </summary>

```
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
"""Compare V4.1 DSpark context projection, normalization and cache insertion.

Uses checkpoint WQA/WKV/RMSNorm weights and synthetic BF16 hidden states.
The baseline source must expose the original DSparkDeepseekV4Model method.
Humming uses its production heuristics in both arms; no tuning overrides.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import statistics
from functools import partial
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
from safetensors import safe_open

from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.config.kernel import IrOpPriorityConfig
from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8.humming import HummingMxfp8LinearKernel
from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8.Mxfp8LinearKernel import (
    Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig,
)
from vllm.model_executor.layers.layernorm import RMSNorm
from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia import dspark

K, Q, V, LAYERS = 5120, 1280, 512, 3


class Projection(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, weight, scale, parts):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_size = K
        self.output_partition_sizes = parts
        self.params_dtype = torch.bfloat16
        self.has_bias = False
        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(weight.cuda(), requires_grad=False)
        self.weight_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(
            scale.view(torch.uint8)
            .repeat_interleave(32, dim=0)
            .cuda()
            .view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu),
            requires_grad=False,
        )
        self.kernel = HummingMxfp8LinearKernel(
            Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig(weight_shape=tuple(weight.shape))
        )
        self.kernel.process_weights_after_loading(self)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.kernel.apply_weights(self, x)


def benchmark(args):
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    index = json.loads((args.checkpoint / "model.safetensors.index.json").read_text())[
        "weight_map"
    ]

    def read(name):
        with safe_open(args.checkpoint / index[name], framework="pt") as f:
            return f.get_tensor(name)

    old = []
    kv_weights, kv_scales, norms = [], [], []
    for i in range(LAYERS):
        prefix = f"mtp.{i}.attn."
        qw, qs = read(prefix + "wq_a.weight"), read(prefix + "wq_a.scale")
        vw, vs = read(prefix + "wkv.weight"), read(prefix + "wkv.scale")
        old.append(Projection(torch.cat([qw, vw]), torch.cat([qs, vs]), [Q, V]))
        kv_weights.append(vw)
        kv_scales.append(vs)
        norm = RMSNorm(V, eps=1e-20, dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda()
        norm.weight.data.copy_(read(prefix + "kv_norm.weight"))
        norms.append(norm)
    merged = Projection(torch.cat(kv_weights), torch.cat(kv_scales), [V] * LAYERS)
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.dspark_baseline", args.baseline_source
    )
    baseline = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(baseline)
    report = {
        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
        "torch": torch.__version__,
        "checkpoint": str(args.checkpoint),
        "source_sha256": {
            "A": hashlib.sha256(args.baseline_source.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
            "B": hashlib.sha256(Path(dspark.__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        },
        "boundary": "3-layer context projection + RMSNorm + RoPE/quant/cache insert",
        "timing": "CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2, ABBA, median of round medians",
        "input": "Synthetic BF16 hidden states; actual checkpoint weights/scales",
        "compute_config": merged.kernel.compute_config,
        "tuning": "Both arms warmed; unchanged production Humming heuristics",
        "correctness": "Normalized KV atol=0.02, rtol=0.02; cache bytes may differ",
        "rows": [],
    }
    for m in args.tokens:
        x = torch.randn(m, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        positions = torch.arange(m, device="cuda")
        rope = torch.zeros(m, 64, device="cuda")
        rope[:, :32] = 1
        models = []
        for _ in range(2):
            layers = []
            for i in range(LAYERS):
                attn = SimpleNamespace(
                    fused_wqa_wkv=lambda x, i=i: (old[i](x), None),
                    q_lora_rank=Q,
                    kv_norm=norms[i],
                    kv_mxfp8=True,
                    rotary_emb=SimpleNamespace(cos_sin_cache=rope),
                    swa_cache_layer=SimpleNamespace(
                        block_size=64,
                        kv_cache=torch.zeros(
                            (m + 63) // 64, 64, 528, device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8
                        ),
                    ),
                )
                layers.append(SimpleNamespace(attn=attn))
            models.append(
                SimpleNamespace(
                    layers=layers,
                    context_wkv_proj=merged,
                    num_dspark_layers=LAYERS,
                    config=SimpleNamespace(head_dim=V),
                )
            )
        modules = [baseline, dspark]
        functions = [
            partial(
                module.DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv,
                model,
                x,
                positions,
                [positions] * LAYERS,
            )
            for module, model in zip(modules, models)
        ]
        for _ in range(20):
            for function in functions:
                function()
        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

        normalized = []
        for module, function in zip(modules, functions):
            outputs = []
            with patch.object(
                module,
                "_insert_context_kv",
                lambda attn, kv, p, s, out=outputs: out.append(kv.clone()),
            ):
                function()
            normalized.append(torch.stack(outputs, dim=1))
        torch.testing.assert_close(normalized[1], normalized[0], rtol=0.02, atol=0.02)
        max_abs = (normalized[1].float() - normalized[0].float()).abs().max().item()
        samples = {"A": [], "B": []}
        for arm in "ABBA":
            times = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
                functions[arm == "B"], use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True
            )
            samples[arm].append(statistics.median(times) * 1000)
        a, b = [statistics.median(samples[arm]) for arm in "AB"]
        row = {
            "tokens": m,
            "A_us": a,
            "B_us": b,
            "latency_reduction_pct": (1 - b / a) * 100,
            "speedup": a / b,
            "normalized_kv_max_abs": max_abs,
            "round_median_us": samples,
            "useful_kv_projection_tflops_A": 2 * m * K * LAYERS * V / (a * 1e6),
            "useful_kv_projection_tflops_B": 2 * m * K * LAYERS * V / (b * 1e6),
        }
        report["rows"].append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    report["status"] = "completed"
    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--baseline-source", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[8, 48, 1024, 16384])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    priority = IrOpPriorityConfig.with_default(
        ["native"], rms_norm=["vllm_c", "native"]
    )
    with (
        torch.inference_mode(),
        set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()),
        priority.set_priority(),
    ):
        benchmark(args)


```

## Details

The stacked projection uses disable_tp=True and contains one WKV shard per draft layer. Checkpoint WKV weights and scales also continue loading into each layer’s original fused Q+KV projection for draft-query computation.

Context outputs are split by layer before the existing normalization and cache insertion. This adds a separate copy of the WKV weights and scales per TP rank.

title: [Docs][KV Connector] Document standalone Mooncake EGM deployment
author: neverhook
body:
## Overview

Document how to deploy an external Mooncake EGM Store with `MooncakeStoreConnector`, using the existing NVLink allocator and GPU KV transfer path. Related to #45036.

## Claims

- Add a standalone EGM Provider example and a deployment guide covering requester configuration, cross-instance prefix reuse, and shutdown.
- Keep the requester's existing positive `local_buffer_size`. The Provider owns the EGM capacity; its storage-only example uses zero local buffer.
- Limit the final diff to documentation and the Provider example. There are no changes to vLLM runtime code or tests.

## Validation

- Provider CLI help, invalid capacity, setup arguments, signal handling, and setup/close error handling checked locally. Lifecycle checks used a fake Store; they do not exercise EGM transfers.
- Requester JSON checked through the existing `MooncakeStoreConfig.from_file()`; KV configuration JSON and example syntax checked.
- Ruff check/format, Markdownlint, and `git diff --check` passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store/egm_provider.py --help
pre-commit run ruff-check --files examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store/egm_provider.py
pre-commit run ruff-format --files examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store/egm_provider.py
npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.21.0 --config tools/pre_commit/.markdownlint.yaml docs/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage.md
git diff --check
```

Full pre-commit environment setup could not complete locally. The targeted checks above passed; commit hooks were bypassed.

The [Mooncake GB200/NVL72 report published on August 18](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/3335#issuecomment-5323495953) records 208 successful HBM ↔ remote EGM Put/Get pairs across four GPUs on two GB200 nodes, including correctness, cleanup, and Fabric-health checks.

That report used Mooncake's `batch_put_from` / `batch_get_into` APIs with zero local buffer. **The vLLM deployment described here, including multi-buffer transfers and cross-instance prefix reuse, has not been tested end to end on hardware.**

## Details

The connector already uses registered GPU buffers for its memory-replica multi-buffer transfers. Keeping the SDK's local staging allocation does not insert a CPU staging step into that path. The guide therefore uses the existing requester configuration without adding a zero-buffer exception or new allocator restrictions.

The example starts a separate Provider with Mooncake's EGM configuration API and closes it after the requesters exit.

The duplicate-work check covered #45036 and open EGM-related PRs; no equivalent deployment guide was found. AI assistance was used for the example, documentation, and local checks.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Triton sigmoid+bias top-k when MoE grouping eliminates nothing
author: chennyiiis
body:
## Overview

AITER `biased_grouped_topk` runs an LDS group scan even when the grouping cannot eliminate any expert — that is, when `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, so every group is selected. This adds a register-resident Triton sigmoid+bias top-k and substitutes it at `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk`, the single call site both ROCm routers reach.

Previously this PR specialised `rocm_aiter_grouped_topk` only. Moving it to the wrapper came out of review (thanks @simondanielsson) and covers both paths without touching routing metadata:

| caller | group arguments it passes |
|---|---|
| `GroupedTopKRouter` | the model's own `1/1` for a degenerate router |
| `FusedTopKBiasRouter` | a count synthesised to fit an AITER kernel — measured `2/2` for a 64-expert router — with `topk_group == num_expert_group` |

`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py` is no longer modified; the diff is three files, additions only.

## Claims

- 1.67×–2.15× on the routing op on gfx942, and 1.16×–1.57× per shape on gfx950, under CUDA graph replay, across the configurations listed below.
- The gate stops at 512 experts and top-8. On gfx950 the kernel loses at top-16 (896-expert top-16 down to 0.62×), so those routers keep AITER — see *Scope and bounds*.
- Equivalent to the call it replaces whenever no group is eliminated, including `num_expert_group == topk_group > 1`, which is the shape `FusedTopKBiasRouter` produces.
- Eager execution is **not** faster, so it is excluded by the substitution rather than claimed as a win.
- Selected expert ids match AITER on 3323 of 3328 routing calls in a live Moonlight-16B-A3B forward and on 1248 of 1248 in Kimi-VL-A3B.
- **Scope: single-token batches only (`_MAX_TOKENS = 1`), as suggested in review**, i.e. one request decoding without speculation, which is where the end-to-end gain is. Larger batches keep AITER.
- End to end on MI355X with current `main`, five models with 64 to 384 experts, 1k to 32k context: **single-request decode is 0.4% to 4.2% faster on every model**, and higher concurrency is within noise; nothing regresses beyond the same-arm drift. GSM8K is unchanged on GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K2.6. Earlier gfx942 runs were within noise.
- No new env var, and no change to router selection or to the advertised routing method.

## Dispatch scope: why this is restricted to CUDA graph steps

The kernel's advantage is device time. Timed from a plain Python loop it is *slower* — it is a Triton launch from Python against a single C++ dispatch, and that overhead is not amortised.

Because the gate is a token-count bound rather than an execution-phase check, eager steps can reach it, so this was measured end to end with `--enforce-eager`, interleaved B-A-B-A on Moonlight:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | ungated PR tok/s | Δ | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 / 256 | 8 | 488.7 | 471.8 | **−3.5%** | 0.6% / 1.2% |
| 64 / 256 | 32 | 1910.4 | 1876.9 | **−1.8%** | 0.8% / 0.1% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 8 | 780.8 | 758.1 | **−2.9%** | 0.8% / 0.2% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 32 | 3008.8 | 2915.3 | **−3.1%** | 0.0% / 0.9% |

Consistent sign and a magnitude several times the drift, so this is a real regression, not noise. The dispatch therefore substitutes only while a CUDA graph is being captured, tested with `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` as `custom_all_reduce.py` and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` already do, and eager steps keep AITER. An earlier revision tested `get_forward_context().cudagraph_runtime_mode` instead; that misses every FULL graph under the V2 model runner, which captures them with the forward context set to `NONE` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`), so on current main it substituted only inside PIECEWISE graphs. Re-running the same eager A/B with the check in place:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 / 256 | 8 | 490.2 | 492.5 | +0.5% | 0.7% / 0.1% |
| 64 / 256 | 32 | 1934.9 | 1933.3 | −0.1% | 1.2% / 0.0% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 8 | 787.1 | 786.8 | −0.0% | 0.1% / 1.0% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 32 | 3018.7 | 3009.5 | −0.3% | 1.9% / 0.8% |

Instrumentation observed no Triton dispatches with `enforce_eager=True`. With graphs enabled, on current main and MI355X, a server records these substitution decisions while it captures its graphs:

| model | cudagraph mode | substituted with the forward-context check | substituted with the stream-capture check |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (forced by the model) | 0 of 2912 | 494 of 2912 |
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 988 of 8190 | 1482 of 8190 |

494 is 19 captured decode sizes up to 128 tokens times 26 MoE layers; the remaining decisions are larger captured sizes, the profiling run and warm-up runs, all of which keep AITER. Those counts are with the earlier `_MAX_TOKENS = 128`; with the current `_MAX_TOKENS = 1` a Moonlight server substitutes 78 of 8190 decisions, all of them in the 1-token graphs, and keeps AITER everywhere else.

## Validation

All runs on one MI300X (gfx942, 304 CUs), torch 2.10.0, triton 3.6.0.

Three checkpoints are used, all with `num_expert_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, a sigmoid router and a `noaux_tc` correction bias. Which one carries which measurement, since they differ:

| model | experts / top-k | context | used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 64 / 6 | 8192 | routing comparison, e2e ≤6k, NIAH 4096, GPQA |
| Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct | 64 / 6 | 131072 | routing comparison, e2e 1k |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | **256 / 8** | 1M | e2e 1k, GPQA, and the 8k/64k attempt |

NIAH ran at 4096 and GPQA at roughly 1k prompts, both well under the 8192 input length at which the engine fault described below appears, so those results and that fault are not in conflict.

Which model carries which measurement, since they differ:

| measurement | model | context used |
|---|---|---|
| unit, micro | — (kernel in isolation) | n/a |
| routing comparison | Moonlight-16B-A3B **and** Kimi-VL-A3B | short decode rows |
| e2e 1k/1k, 6k/1k | Moonlight-16B-A3B | ≤ 7k |
| e2e 1k/1k | Kimi-VL-A3B | ≤ 2k |
| e2e 8k/1k, 64k/1k | **not obtained** — see below | — |
| NIAH | Moonlight-16B-A3B | 4096 |
| GPQA | Moonlight-16B-A3B | ~1k prompts |

NIAH and GPQA ran on Moonlight at 4096 and ~1k respectively, both well under the 8192 input length at which the engine crash below appears, so there is no contradiction between those results and that crash.

### Unit

Against upstream `db3b0f0fa`:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py -k "flat_topk or substitutes"
# 61 passed on MI355X (gfx950), this PR at 7c6559d9 cherry-picked onto main 3966924d
```

Each correctness test compares against `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk(..., 1, 1, ...)` — the exact call being replaced — through the same wrapper production uses.

| test | coverage |
|---|---|
| `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter` | 40 cases: {bf16, fp32} × {renorm on, off} × 10 shapes, including primes/odd sizes that exercise the masked tail of `BLOCK_E = next_power_of_2(num_experts)`: `(3,257,8)`, `(7,131,5)`, `(13,509,7)`, `(1,2,1)`, `(5,65,3)` |
| `test_flat_topk_casts_bias_like_aiter` | bf16 gating with an fp32 bias — see *Bias dtype* |
| `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter_with_uneliminating_groups` | `num_expert_group == topk_group` ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} × renorm on/off — the `FusedTopKBiasRouter` shape |
| `test_flat_topk_honours_routed_scaling` | `routed_scaling_factor` 1.0 / 2.446 / 2.827 |
| `test_biased_grouped_topk_substitutes_only_when_expected` | captures a real CUDA graph around the wrapper: it substitutes for `1/1` and `2/2` during capture, and not for `8/4` or in eager |

The rest of that file reports 34 failures in my container which reproduce identically on unmodified `db3b0f0fa` (34 failed / 5 passed before this change, 34 failed / 77 passed after it, measured before the review trim); this PR does not touch them.

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/rocm_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py
```

### Micro

Per-call **device** time under CUDA graph replay, 50 calls captured per graph so the replay overhead is amortised ~50× instead of landing on both arms.

| gating | experts | tokens | AITER (µs) | PR (µs) | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | 256 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 5.47 / 5.67 / 5.72 / 5.76 | 3.00 / 3.18 / 3.20 / 3.27 | 1.82× / 1.78× / 1.79× / 1.76× |
| bf16 | 384 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 6.80 / 7.03 / 7.07 / 7.14 | 4.01 / 4.14 / 4.16 / 4.26 | 1.69× / 1.70× / 1.70× / 1.67× |
| fp32 | 256 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 6.05 / 6.12 / 6.24 / 6.26 | 2.82 / 2.99 / 3.00 / 3.16 | 2.15× / 2.05× / 2.08× / 1.98× |
| fp32 | 384 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 7.33 / 7.54 / 7.61 / 7.62 | 3.56 / 3.70 / 3.73 / 3.79 | 2.06× / 2.04× / 2.04× / 2.01× |

That is gfx942 (MI300X) at 256 and 384 experts.

On gfx950 (MI355X), the same method over a wider range of shapes: bf16 gating, fp32 bias, `routed_scaling_factor` 2.446, renormalised, six random seeds per point, plus one input where a single row has an exactly tied top score. Expert ids matched a stable-sort reference on every input, and AITER's id set on all 192 random inputs.

| experts | top-k | AITER µs, 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 tokens | PR µs, 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 tokens | mean speedup | worst random launch | one tied row |
|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 6 | 5.40 / 5.79 / 5.85 / 5.77 | 3.45 / 3.65 / 3.72 / 3.74 | 1.57× | 1.51× | 1.33× |

| 512 | 16 | 6.59 / 7.11 / 7.17 / 7.24 | 5.36 / 5.85 / 5.92 / 6.97 | 1.18× | 0.80× | 0.78× |

The advantage shrinks as the router widens on gfx950; it does not grow. The slow launches are the tie fallback: when a row has two experts with exactly equal biased scores among its top-k, the fast path picks more than k and that row redoes the selection, and the launch waits for its slowest row. bf16 logits make exact ties common enough at top-16 to matter (0.8% of rows at 896 experts, so about one 32-row launch in five), which is where the 0.6× launches come from. Rows above 512 experts or top-8 therefore stay on AITER.

### Routing comparison on live models

Comparing generated text between arms is not a usable instrument on this setup: it is not deterministic run to run — two baseline-only runs of the same four greedy prompts already diverge. Instead both kernels were run on identical inputs inside a live forward, AITER into the real buffers and the new kernel into scratch, with generation continuing on the AITER result so the measurement cannot perturb the run.

| model | calls compared | calls where **all** selected ids match | max abs weight delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 3328 | 3323 | 4.77e-07 |
| Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct | 1248 | 1248 | 4.77e-07 |

Both have `n_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, `scoring_func="sigmoid"`, `noaux_tc`, `norm_topk_prob=true`, 64 experts, top-6. The five differing Moonlight calls each carry a weight delta of 1.19e-07 or 4.77e-07; that is consistent with a near-tie in the biased score resolving to a different expert, but the weight delta alone does not prove the scores were exactly equal.

### End to end on MI300X (gfx942)

`vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`, interleaved, one fresh server per block.

An initial sequential A/B (all of arm 0, then all of arm 1) showed +16–24% throughput. That did not reproduce under interleaved testing and has been withdrawn — the same AITER baseline measured 1789 tok/s sequentially and 2250 tok/s interleaved on a shared host.

| model | in / out | concurrency | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Moonlight | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +0.7% | −0.8% | 0.4% / 1.4% |
| Moonlight | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.8% | −0.9% | 1.1% / 0.6% |
| Kimi-VL | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +0.4% | −0.6% | 1.0% / 0.9% |
| Kimi-VL | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.7% | −0.9% | 3.6% / 0.7% |
| Kimi-Linear | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +1.1% | −1.1% | 0.4% / 0.4% |
| Kimi-Linear | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.1% | −0.1% | 1.1% / 0.7% |

Comparable to the same-arm variation, so no gfx942 end-to-end speedup is claimed. The Kimi-Linear rows discard the first repetition of each block: the very first benchmark run of the campaign returned 1066 tok/s against 1510-1543 for the other seven runs of that point, a warm-up artefact rather than a property of either arm.

**The 8k/1k and 64k/1k points are now measured.** The earlier report that they could not be served was wrong, and the reason is worth stating because it is a bug in the benchmark harness rather than in serving.

`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random` samples token ids from `tokenizer.vocab_size`. For this checkpoint that is **163842**, while the model's embedding has `config.vocab_size` = **163840** rows, so ids 163840 and 163841 index past the table and the embedding gather faults. The dataset emits a *contiguous run* of ids, so a 65536-token prompt covers 40% of the vocabulary and nearly always includes one of the two; an 8192-token prompt covers 5%, which is why 8k completed under some seeds and not others. On stock vLLM, with no part of this PR installed, the identical 8192 configuration completes 3/3 with `--seed 7` and faults 3/3 with `--seed 1234`:

| seed | completed | `Memory access fault` |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 8, 8, 8 | 0 |
| 1234 | 0, 0, 0 | 1 |

That also explains the fault seen earlier on a different machine with Kimi-VL, where the kernel named in the HSA exception was `at::native::vectorized_gather_kernel` — the embedding gather.

Replacing the synthesised prompts with real text (a custom dataset whose maximum token id is 138177, verified below the embedding size) removes the fault entirely: 8 of 8 runs complete at 64k with zero faults.

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 4305.4 | 4466.3 | +3.7% | −4.0% | 4.1% / 1.7% |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 6154.7 | 6162.5 | +0.1% | −1.2% | 1.4% / 1.8% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 1 | 13528.3 | 14305.7 | +5.7% | −7.0% | 8.6% / 8.4% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 2 | 18045.6 | 17927.5 | −0.7% | −1.6% | 1.7% / 0.9% |

Every point has a same-arm drift of the same size as the difference between arms, so these do not change the gfx942 conclusion. The 64k rows carry only 2 and 4 requests per run, which is why their drift is the largest in the table.

### End to end on MI355X (gfx950), current main: five models

These runs used `_MAX_TOKENS = 128`, so concurrency 8 and up also substituted. The PR now substitutes only for 1-token batches, which the concurrency-1 rows measure; the other rows show what the wider bound did and why it was dropped.

Asked for in review: short and long context across several models. Every model below has a sigmoid router with a `noaux_tc` correction bias whose grouping eliminates nothing, so it reaches the substitution; the probe column is how many of the routing decisions a server makes while capturing its graphs took the Triton path (the rest are larger captured sizes, the profiling run and warm-up, which keep AITER).

As concurrency grows the router becomes a smaller share of the step and the difference shrinks into the noise. The four negative points (-0.21% at most) all overlap with the base runs. Nothing regresses outside the same-arm drift.

Accuracy on the same build, lm-eval 0.4.9 `gsm8k` (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy) through `/v1/completions`:

| model | base | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 92.12% ± 0.74 | 92.04% ± 0.75 |
| Kimi-K2.6 | 93.48% ± 0.68 | 93.71% ± 0.67 |

One question apart on GLM, three on Kimi-K2.6, both inside the standard error. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash routes through a group count `FusedTopKBiasRouter` synthesises (128 experts, top-4, 4/4); at that shape the kernel selects the same experts as AITER on all 17040 rows of a randomised check (fp32 and bf16 gating and bias, 1-128 rows), max weight difference 7.45e-08.

An earlier A/B on Kimi-Linear, taken before the graph-capture fix, measured +0.07% to +0.16%; the probe shows that run never substituted, so it is not used.

### Accuracy on MI300X (gfx942)

A/B on Moonlight through the served endpoint, lm-eval 0.4.13.

**NIAH** (RULER, 4096): the three reported task scores match between arms — `niah_multikey_1` 1.00/1.00, `niah_single_2` 0.94/0.94, `niah_single_1` 0.00/0.00. The subtask scoring zero on both arms is inconclusive; this is task-level agreement, not per-sample output agreement.

**GPQA** (`gpqa_diamond_zeroshot`, 198 questions, loglikelihood). A first single-run A/B looked like +2.0 points for this PR. Three interleaved runs per arm show the difference changes sign:

| run | AITER | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.3131 | 0.3333 |
| 2 | 0.3384 | 0.3182 |
| 3 | 0.3485 | 0.3283 |

AITER alone spans 0.3131–0.3485 across its own three runs.

Repeated on Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, three interleaved runs per arm:

| run | AITER | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.3889 | 0.4040 |
| 2 | 0.3990 | 0.4192 |
| 3 | 0.3990 | 0.4091 |
| median | 0.3990 | 0.4091 |

Here this PR is nominally higher in all three runs, by 1.0 point. **That is not claimed as an accuracy improvement**: 1.0 point is 2 questions out of 198, well inside the ±3.4 point standard error, and a routing difference confined to 0.15% of calls has no mechanism by which it could make a model more accurate. Taken with the Moonlight runs, these results show no regression, but are not sufficient to establish accuracy equivalence.

### Bias dtype

`rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk` casts `correction_bias` to the gating dtype before dispatching, because AITER raises on a mismatch. A bf16 gating output next to an fp32 correction bias is a common router layout, so without the same cast the new path would score experts at a precision the replaced path never uses, and could select different experts. `sigmoid_bias_flat_topk` therefore makes the same cast at its own entry; Removing the cast fails 4 of the 6 cases in `test_flat_topk_casts_bias_like_aiter`; the other two shapes happen not to be sensitive to the bias precision.

### Known behavioural differences

| input | result |
|---|---|
| well-formed gating | weights agree to 2e-3 in unit tests; selected ids match on 4571 of 4576 live routing calls across two models |
| near-ties in the biased score | weights agree to 1.19e-07; the index chosen among near-equal experts may differ |
| NaN in gating output | **materially different from AITER** (6/10 synthetic configs, max weight delta 0.93) |

If maintainers would rather the gate reject non-finite input, that is a small addition to `can_use_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk`.

## Details

### Why the substitution sits at the wrapper

Review asked whether a model with no grouping should simply not be routed to `GroupedTopKRouter`. Two things make the wrapper the better place.

First, the advertised routing method is not a label. `layer.py:378` takes it from `router.kernel_routing_method_type` and stores it on the MoE config, where the AITER mxfp4 expert kernels consume it: `_supports_routing_method` lists `[Renormalize, RenormalizeNaive, DeepseekV4, DeepSeekV3]`, `self.renormalize` is derived from the same tuple, and the apply path branches on `DeepSeekV3` to pick `score_mode="sigmoid"`. `MiniMax2` is in none of them, so degenerating `num_expert_group` 1 → None would make those backends refuse these models and would flip `renormalize` to False for a checkpoint whose config says `norm_topk_prob: true`.

Second, and more decisively, changing the router would not remove the op. Calling `fused_topk_bias` directly — the routine `FusedTopKBiasRouter` uses — with a 64-expert, top-6 sigmoid+bias router on ROCm with AITER enabled:

```
synthesised group count for 64 experts: 2
biased_grouped_topk CALLED 1x with (num_expert_group, topk_group) = (2, 2)
```

`_aiter_get_num_expert_group` picks a divisor AITER has a kernel for, with `topk_group == num_expert_group` so the grouping is a no-op. A model moved off `GroupedTopKRouter` would still reach the grouped kernel, with a fabricated two-group configuration in place of its real single group.

Specialising at `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk` covers both callers, needs no routing-metadata change, and generalises the condition from "one group" to "no group is eliminated".

### Relation to #49870

[#49870](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49870) short-circuits the same degenerate shape for the case where AITER fused MoE is **not** enabled, which this PR does not touch.

### Scope and bounds

`can_use_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk` requires `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, a contiguous bias of exactly `num_experts`, and bounded token/expert/topk counts. The scoring function is not checked: at this call site the op is AITER's biased (sigmoid) top-k by construction, so matching that op is the contract. `_MAX_EXPERTS = 512` and `_MAX_TOPK = 8` are where the gfx950 measurements above stop showing a win: up to there the mean per shape is 1.16×–1.57× and no launch falls below 0.92×, even with a forced tie; at top-16 single tied rows pull launches to 0.62×–0.78×. An earlier revision of this PR accepted up to 1024 experts and top-32, set to cover the widest router in this family without having measured it there; the gfx950 sweep showed that was wrong, and those routers, Kimi-K3 (896 / top-16) among them, now keep AITER. `_MAX_TOKENS = 1` restricts it to single-token batches, one request decoding without speculation, where the end-to-end sweep shows a gain on every model; at larger batches the gain was within noise, so those keep AITER.

### Limitations

- Micro and unit tests on gfx942 and gfx950. The MI355X e2e and GSM8K runs are on current `main`; the gfx942 e2e, NIAH and GPQA runs are on an older build, see the next point.
- The e2e and accuracy comparisons used the container's own older vLLM build for both arms, because today's `main` cannot start against this image's AITER (`aiter.ops.flydsl.moe_common` missing, `fused_moe()` without `swiglu_limit`). Both arms are that same build differing only in this kernel. Unit and micro results are against `db3b0f0fa`.

title: [Feature][DSv4.1] Enable PCP with PP or DP
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Overview

Relax the model-level PCP compatibility checks for text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA CUDA to enable the existing PCP + PP and PCP + DP execution paths. The underlying MRV2 implementations are already provided by #59139 (PP) and #57075 (DP). No other open PR was found enabling these model-specific combinations; #49246's generic DP approach was superseded by #57075, while #63106 addresses cross-stage cache relay with PCP=1.

## Claims

- Remove the blanket PP=DP=1 restriction when PCP is enabled, allowing the existing PP or DP execution paths. Combining PP + DP is allowed when TP=1 or expert parallelism is disabled; DCP must remain 1.
- Add PP2 + PCP2 and DP2 + PCP2 cases to the existing `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py`, using real-weight serving and generation.

## Validation

**Hardware**: 1 node with 8 H20(96G) GPUs.

**Image**: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-df3bd094aeea829f27baa0a5282830464f601d9f`

**Startup Command**:

PP+PCP（`VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26`）：
```bash
VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26 vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18001 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --moe-backend humming --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager --no-async-scheduling --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

DP+PCP：
```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18001 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --moe-backend humming --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager --no-async-scheduling --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

4. **GSM8K**
   - EvalScope 1.11.1，GSM8K full 1319，4-shot，batch 64，temperature 0，top_p 1，seed 42，max_tokens 8192。
   - PP+PCP：`1286/1319 = 97.50%`，0 API error。
   - DP+PCP：`1282/1319 = 97.19%`，0 API error。

## Details

The runtime change is confined to the NVIDIA model's compatibility checks. PP/PCP execution, stage-entry Engram handling, and DP/EP communication reuse their existing implementations. The existing PCP test file adds generation cases for the newly enabled combinations: the PP case uses Flash's `14,26` partition, and the DP case sends a request to each replica.

With PCP enabled, PP>1 and DP>1 are rejected only when TP>1 and expert parallelism is enabled: PP currently disables the model's sequence-parallel path required by DP+PCP AgRs MoE communication in that topology. TP=1 or disabled expert parallelism passes this combined-topology gate; these additional combinations still require GPU validation. DCP must remain 1; KV transfer, microbatching, and MegaMoE remain disabled. Preserve main's fixed-length DSpark support with PP=1 and the existing PR's exclusion of speculative decoding with PCP + PP. Prefix caching still requires SWA bounded replay.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change. The human submitter remains responsible for line-by-line review; validation beyond the two configurations reported above remains pending.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Match the DeepSeek-V4.1 FP8 config in the shared-expert FSE compatibility check
author: BaoYunkai
body:
## Overview

On CUDA and ROCm, `deepseek_v4_fp8` always resolves to the DeepSeek-V4.1 `DeepseekV4FP8Config`, which subclasses `Fp8Config`, not the V4 class. `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` runs its DeepSeek-V4 checks only for the V4 class, so on these platforms it falls through to the generic `Fp8Config` branch and reports every DeepSeek-V4 shared expert as FSE-compatible. This PR matches both classes for MXFP4 routed experts, as the online-quantization branch of the same function already does.

Founded by Hyperloom.

## Claims

- Fixes the weight-loading failure of DeepSeek-V4-Flash on ROCm with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. Quark MXFP4 checkpoints hit the same failure on the FP8 MTP shared expert.
- No change when the variable is unset: the check is not called.
- No change for FP8-expert checkpoints such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base: they keep the generic FP8 check, as on main.
- Adds `test_deepseek_v41_quant_config_rejects_fp8_mtp_shared_expert_fse` and `test_deepseek_v41_fp8_experts_keep_fp8_fse_check`.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, TP1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256`, vLLM built from main at 15a78aa88e (the touched files are unchanged on current main).

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, main fails during weight loading in 2 of 2 runs:

```
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_weight_scale_inv'
```

With this PR, all 43 layers reject FSE ("only implemented/tested with Quark MXFP4"), run the shared expert unfused, and serve.

`vllm bench serve`, random 1000 in / 200 out, 400 prompts, concurrency 50, a fresh server per run. 4 runs per arm, median of the last 3, within-arm spread in parentheses:

| Arm | Total tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, variable unset | 10061 (±3.5%) | 1026 | 24.68 |
| this PR, variable unset | 10033 (±0.8%) | 1024 | 24.76 |
| this PR, variable = 1 | 10045 (±0.2%) | 1027 | 24.77 |

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, `lm_eval --model local-completions`:

| Arm | strict-match | Same verdict as main |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9515 ± 0.0059 | - |
| main, repeated (noise floor) | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 | 98.10% |
| this PR, variable = 1 | 0.9538 ± 0.0058 | 97.95% |

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base (FP8 experts), TP2, vLLM built from main at b3b0bc3059: with the variable set, main runs the shared expert fused (257 experts, top-7 in the MoE), and GSM8K (same settings as above) stays within the noise of unfused runs: 0.9174 vs 0.9090 and 0.9234 from two runs without the variable. This PR gives the same FSE answer as main for this checkpoint.

Unit tests on MI355X against the built tree, `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py`: this PR 107 passed. Main fails `test_deepseek_v41_quant_config_rejects_fp8_mtp_shared_expert_fse`; `test_deepseek_v41_fp8_experts_keep_fp8_fse_check` passes on both.

## Details

The existing unit test missed the bug because it constructs the V4 class directly. CI does not run DeepSeek-V4 with this variable set; the new tests are CPU-only.

AI assistance (Hyperloom with Claude) was used to find and prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and reproduced the results above.

title: [Perf][MXFP4] Optimize activation quant for mxfp4. 3x kernel speedup, 5% throughput improvement
author: ilmarkov
body:
## Overview

Pass optional `sorted_expert_ids` through Cutlass MXFP4 MoE activation quantization so each sorted token row uses a direct expert index instead of searching expert offset tables.

## Claims


- Kernel: sorted_expert_id path is bitwise identical to offset_search on microbenchmark cases; up to ~3.3× lower median latency at 256 experts for representative input / intermediate_fused shapes.
- E2E: On RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4 (TP=4, no spec), ~+5.7% output tok/s vs main.
- API change: Optional sorted_expert_ids on mxfp4_experts_quant, silu_and_mul_mxfp4_experts_quant, and get_cutlass_moe_mm_data; wired from Cutlass MXFP4 MoE when routing metadata exists.
## Validation

### Microbenchmark 
`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mxfp4_experts_activation_quant.py`
Hardware: NVIDIA B300

mm_data + shuffle + quant


Kernel | E=16 | E=32 | E=64 | E=128 | E=256
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
mxfp4 main → PR (µs) | 10.55 → 10.77 | 11.85 → 11.61 (1.02×) | 14.06 → 12.96 (1.08×) | 17.56 → 14.94 (1.18×) | 22.48 → 16.78 (1.34×)
silu+mul main → PR | 10.18 → 10.41 | 11.45 → 11.27 (1.02×) | 13.70 → 11.42 (1.20×) | 17.32 → 14.65 (1.18×) | 22.30 → 16.46 (1.35×)



Benchmarks time `get_cutlass_moe_mm_data` + activation quant together; main and PR's paths share ~14–15 µs metadata at 256 experts (mo overhead on `sorted_expert_ids`), so the reported speedup is ~1.4× on the full replay while quant still saves ~5–6 µs by skipping offset lookup.

### E2E benchmark
