title: [ROCm][Build] Reland #62475: paged attention kernel split with `--offload-compress` => x4-x7 wheel build speedup on ROCm
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

**Only difference compared to #62475:** one line in `CMakeLists.txt`, adding `--offload-compress` to `VLLM_ROCM_EXT_FLAGS`.

**Toolchain scope:** `--offload-compress` exists since clang 18 (LLVM PR #67162, 2023-10: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/67162). I only tested it with **ROCm 7.2.0 and 7.2.3 (clang 22)** and **ROCm 10.0.0 (clang 23)**; ROCm 6.x was not tested.

Followup PRs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62716 / https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62717 / https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62718 (to be re-tested and PR description updated with 9 archs targets build)

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

`csrc/rocm/attention.cu` is a single 3.9k-line translation unit whose kernel instantiation is the tail of the ROCm build: ~9 min of a ~10.5 min build, on one core. This inflation was probably especially caused by recent: #42755  (adds `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` as a template parameter to all 12 kernels = interleaved + non-interleaved instantiation (+50%))

This PR splits the instantiations into one translation unit per (dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size) combination so ninja builds them in parallel.

*Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this. The closest open items are #17419 and #60906.*

## Why #62475 broke the nightly build?

**TL;DR.** #62475 splits one huge kernel file into 12 smaller ones so they compile in parallel. Side effect: each of the 12 files now carries its own copy of the GPU debug info, so the linked library grows. #62475 measured that growth on **1 architecture** (+23 MB), but the nightly library is built for **9** architectures:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4/docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base#L26

At 9 architectures the library measures ~2200 MiB (its objects alone are 2149 MiB), and past ~2100 MiB a 32-bit relative address inside the library can no longer reach its target — the failing link overflowed at 2104 MiB — so both mold and lld refuse to link it:

```text
FAILED: [code=1] _rocm_C.abi3.so 
mold: error: /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/lib/llvm/lib/clang/23/lib/linux/clang_rt.crtbegin-x86_64.o:(.text): relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against .eh_frame out of range: -2206798738 is not in [-2147483648, 2147483648)
clang++: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)
```

Plain `main` links fine but is already 2011.5 MiB, i.e. only ~93 MiB below where the split overflowed, while the split adds ~119 MiB of duplicated debug info. So the reland has to make the 9-architecture library *smaller* than today (e.g. `-Xarch_device -g0`, `--offload-compress`), not merely "not bigger".

Mold is selected for the `csrc-build` wheel at the main HEAD used for the measurements (49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4):
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4/docker/Dockerfile.rocm#L335

Sizes measured at 9 archs, `RelWithDebInfo`, on e8ae84bf and on main, `MAX_JOBS=64`:

| | `main` (1 attention TU) | #62475 (12 attention TUs) |
|---|---|---|
| attention objects | 1088 MiB (`attention.hip.o`) | 1214 MiB (**+119 MiB** of duplicated device DWARF) |
| attention `.hip_fatbin` | 1070 MiB | 1189 MiB |
| `.hip_fatbin` in the link | 1983 MiB | 2103 MiB |
| build | 85 min 28 s | 21 min 34 s |
| build errors | none | none |
| link errors | none | `relocation R_X86_64_PC32 ... out of range` |

**Not a linker bug.** Switching mold for `lld` reproduces the same overflow, so this is the 32-bit PC32 reach and not a mold defect:

```text
ld.lld: error: CMakeFiles/_rocm_C_skinny.dir/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.hip.o:(.rodata+0x0): relocation R_X86_64_PC32 out of range: 2206616580 is not in [-2147483648, 2147483647]; references section '.text'
>>> referenced by skinny_gemms.hip
```

**Exact command that fails**, run at e8ae84bf7e992c63570905fce3073fd7a7de2412 (the merge of #62475) inside `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-39983a5e7a5a575a7829f5d5ada50a33d9337ec1` (same compiler, mold, 9 archs and `RelWithDebInfo` build type as the `csrc-build` stage of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`):

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" \
  PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151" \
  VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=64 \
  python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist
```

## Claims

- Cold 9-arch build drops from **85 min 28 s to 21 min 25 s** (4×, `MAX_JOBS=64`, mold): the attention kernels stop being one serial ~9-minute compile and become 12 parallel TUs of 58–72 s each (at 1 arch), and the `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link no longer waits behind them.
- The module now fits: instead of the ~2200 MiB that #62475 alone could not link, `_rocm_C.abi3.so` is **125.9 MiB** and `.hip_fatbin` **95.8 MiB** (from 2103 MiB), with no change to the shipped `RelWithDebInfo` build type or to the device debug info.
- No behavior change: identical template instantiations, identical dispatch order, unchanged `paged_attention` signature and op registration; the compressed kernels were executed on gfx950 (see Validation).
- Costs: aggregate CPU work grows (~30% more work, measured in #62475), and the module is decompressed at load — ~0.6 s moves from the first attention call into `import vllm`, while per-process RAM ends ~135 MiB lower.

**How the file got this big.** The instantiation matrix was grown one axis at a time:

| PR | landed | what it added | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| #8310 | 2024-09-13 | initial ROCm custom paged attention | 1,038 lines, 4 kernels; already `{fp16,bf16}` × head `{64,128}` × block `{16,32}` × alibi `{on,off}` |
| #8577 | 2024-09-19 | fp8 KV cache | adds the `KV_DTYPE`/`cache_t` axis (fp8, `kFp8E4M3`) |
| #12348 | 2025-03-04 | "Faster Custom Paged Attention" rewrite | 4 → 6 kernels (`mfma16`, `mfma4`, partition `reduce`), +1,084/−422 |
| #17139 | 2025-05-07 | FP8 output fusion | `if (fp8_out_scale) → OUTT=uint8_t` = ×2 |
| #17004 | 2025-05-21 | RDNA/NAVI support on v1 | duplicates the kernel set for gfx11/gfx12, 6 → 12 `__global__`, ≈×2, +1,880/−171 |
| #22222 | 2025-09-15 | fp8 paged attention update | adds `MFMAType` (`Fp8` vs `F16`) = ×2 on the fp8 path |
| #42755 | 2026-10-15 | Qwen3-30B QK-norm/RoPE/KV-cache fusion | adds `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` to all 12 kernels = +50% |

Cumulative, per architecture: 6 dtype/kv-cache combinations × head (2) × block (2) × fp8-out (2) × alibi (2) × {NAVI, non-NAVI, interleaved} ≈ 288 launcher instantiations → ~860 device kernels in one file. `--offload-arch` values are additionally compiled serially inside that file, so the 9-arch release build pays ~9× the per-architecture cost.


## Validation

Environment for every number below:
- `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-39983a5e7a5a575a7829f5d5ada50a33d9337ec1`,
- the 9-arch list (`gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151`)
- `LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold"` of the `csrc-build` stage in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`, `RelWithDebInfo` (`-O2 -g`, the default build type),
- `MAX_JOBS=64`, `VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1`, cold build directories.

| | `main` (pre-split `attention.cu`) | #62475 as merged | this PR (#62475 + `--offload-compress`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold build, 9 archs | 85 min 28 s | 21 min 34 s (**fails at link**) | **21 min 25 s** |
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` | 2011.5 MiB | not produced (link fails) | **125.9 MiB** |
| `.hip_fatbin` | 1983 MiB (in the module) | 2103 MiB (sum of objects) | **95.8 MiB** (in the module) |
| `_rocm_C` objects, total | 2022 MiB | 2149 MiB | **142 MiB** |
| 12 attention TUs | `attention.hip.o` 1088 MiB | 1214 MiB | **84.5 MiB** (6.0–8.3 MiB each) |
| `skinny_gemms_int4.hip.o` | 846 MiB | 846 MiB | **32.1 MiB** |
| wheel | 379 MiB | not produced (no wheel) | 266 MiB |

The split is the 4× build win (21 min 34 s vs 85 min 28 s) and `--offload-compress` costs nothing measurable in compile time (21 min 25 s vs 21 min 34 s, within noise); the revert buys ~100 MB of link margin at the price of ~64 min per build.

Load cost on MI350 (gfx950): 10 runs per module, interleaved, one process per run, page cache dropped before every run (`sync; echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches`), vLLM installed from each wheel — the only difference is `vllm/_rocm_C.abi3.so`. Medians with min–max in parentheses:

| metric | `main` (2011.5 MiB module) | this PR (125.9 MiB module) |
|---|---|---|
| `import vllm` (dlopen + decompression) | 3.64 s (3.39–3.81) | 4.25 s (3.51–5.41) |
| first `paged_attention` call (HIP module load, gfx950) | 0.657 s (0.629–0.838) | **0.034 s** (0.029–0.059) |
| total to first kernel | 4.31 s (4.02–4.54) | 4.28 s (3.55–5.47) |
| RAM used by the vLLM process after `import vllm` | 836 MiB | 1168 MiB |
| RAM used by the vLLM process after first kernel | 1746 MiB | **1612 MiB** |

Compression moves ~0.6 s of work from the first attention call into `import vllm`, so time-to-first-kernel is unchanged (4.31 s vs 4.28 s) while the first request is 19x cheaper to serve (0.657 s → 0.034 s) and steady-state RAM use ends ~135 MiB lower.

### Why vLLM import uses more RAM now?

Same runs, showing the RAM used by the vLLM process (RSS from `/proc/self/statm`) split into anonymous (per-process, private) and file-backed (page cache, shared and reclaimable) at the three stages:

| point | `main` (2011.5 MiB module) | this PR (125.9 MiB module) |
|---|---|---|
| after torch init | 652 MiB = 303 anon + 346 file | 651 MiB = 303 anon + 344 file |
| after `import vllm` | 837 MiB = 430 anon + 403 file | 1168 MiB = 660 anon + 504 file |
| after first kernel | 1747 MiB = 1101 anon + 601 file | 1613 MiB = 1053 anon + 546 file |

Growth relative to torch init:

| stage | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| import (dlopen, decompression) | +127 anon, +57 file | **+357 anon**, +160 file |
| first kernel (module load) | **+671 anon**, +198 file | +393 anon, +42 file |
| total | +1094 | +962 |

Both builds converge on **~1.05 GiB anonymous** once the gfx950 code object is loaded: that is the loaded kernels, identical in both, which is why the final RAM use is comparable. Compression only changes *when* the device code is materialised — decompressed at import instead of paged in from a 2 GiB file at first kernel use — and ends ~134 MiB lower because the uncompressed module keeps more of its 2 GiB resident (`+601` vs `+546` file over baseline) plus ~48 MiB of extra anonymous data from parsing the larger fatbin. The file-backed share is page cache (shared, evictable); only the anonymous share is per-process, so a worker's private cost is the ~1.05 GiB, not the total.

**Reproduce:** build the wheel on the branch under test with the 9-arch command above, then, inside the ROCm 10.0 container with the GPU:

```bash
pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall dist/*.whl
```

and `load_time_bench.py`:

```python
"""Time `import vllm` (dlopen of _rocm_C + device-code decompression) and the
first paged_attention call (HIP module load for the current arch)."""
import ctypes, os, time
import torch


def rss_mb():
    return int(open("/proc/self/statm").read().split()[1]) * 4096 / 2**20


t0 = time.perf_counter()
torch.cuda.init()
torch.cuda.synchronize()
rss_torch = rss_mb()

import vllm, vllm._custom_ops as ops  # noqa: E402
t_import = time.perf_counter() - t0
rss_vllm = rss_mb()

so = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__), "_rocm_C.abi3.so")
ctypes.CDLL(so, mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)

# same tensors as tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py
num_seqs, num_query_heads, num_kv_heads = 1, 8, 1
head_size, block_size, max_seq_len = 64, 16, 256
PARTITION_SIZE_ROCM, NUM_BLOCKS = 256, 4321
x = 16 // 2
torch.set_default_device("cuda")
scale = 1.0 / head_size**0.5
query = torch.empty(num_seqs, num_query_heads, head_size,
                    dtype=torch.float16).uniform_(-scale, scale)
seq_lens = torch.tensor([max_seq_len], dtype=torch.int)
block_tables = torch.tensor(
    [[1] * ((max_seq_len + block_size - 1) // block_size)], dtype=torch.int)
key_cache = torch.randn(NUM_BLOCKS, num_kv_heads, head_size // x, block_size, x,
                        dtype=torch.float16)
value_cache = torch.randn(NUM_BLOCKS, num_kv_heads, head_size, block_size,
                          dtype=torch.float16)
k_scale, v_scale = torch.tensor(1.0), torch.tensor(1.0)
out = torch.empty_like(query)
npart = (max_seq_len + PARTITION_SIZE_ROCM - 1) // PARTITION_SIZE_ROCM
tmp_out = torch.empty(num_seqs, num_query_heads, npart, head_size,
                      dtype=torch.float16)
exp_sums = torch.empty(num_seqs, num_query_heads, npart, dtype=torch.float32)
max_logits = torch.empty_like(exp_sums)
torch.cuda.synchronize()

t = time.perf_counter()
ops.paged_attention_rocm(out, exp_sums, max_logits, tmp_out, query, key_cache,
                         value_cache, num_kv_heads, scale, block_tables, seq_lens,
                         None, block_size, max_seq_len, None, "auto", k_scale,
                         v_scale)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
t_first = time.perf_counter() - t

print(f"so={os.path.getsize(so) / 2**20:.1f} MiB  import_vllm={t_import:.2f}s  "
      f"first_paged_attn={t_first:.3f}s  total={t_import + t_first:.2f}s  "
      f"rss: torch={rss_torch:.0f} vllm={rss_vllm:.0f} kernel={rss_mb():.0f} MiB")
```

And repro:

```bash
# cold: drop the page cache before every run
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  sync && echo 1 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches >/dev/null
  HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 load_time_bench.py
done
```

Kernel correctness — run against the wheel built with `--offload-compress` at 9 archs, on gfx950, i.e. on the compressed code objects themselves. The full matrix is head 64/128 × block 16/32 × fp16/bf16 × kv auto/fp8 × alibi on/off × interleaved-V on/off × GQA 1/4/8 across the 12 instantiation TUs; the runs below cover the slices actually executed:

```bash
# this PR, compressed module: head 64, GQA (32,8), block 16+32, no alibi,
# bf16+fp16 x kv auto+fp8 x interleaved-V on/off
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py -k "paged_attention and num_heads0 and 64-num_heads0 and False-cuda" -q
# 16 passed, 185 deselected

# f16 MFMA path (default), from #62475 - kernels unchanged by this PR
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention -k num_heads0 -q
# 128 passed, 256 deselected, 414 s

# fp8 MFMA path (*_fp8_fp8 TUs), from #62475
VLLM_ROCM_FP8_MFMA_PAGE_ATTN=1 python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention -k "num_heads0 and fp8" -q
# 64 passed, 320 deselected, 206 s

# head-size `default:` branch of the dispatch, from #62475
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_paged_attention_unsupported_head_sizes -q
# 7 passed, 1 s
```

No model eval is included: the split does not change kernels, dispatch, or numerics, only how many objects they are compiled into, and `--offload-compress` only changes how the device code is stored in the module (the runtime decompresses it before loading). The runtime numbers above were taken on gfx950; the other 8 release archs are compiled and linked by this build config but were not executed.

**Left for other PRs** (no automated coverage today, unchanged by this PR):

**Test coverage is partial.** The 9-arch compressed build executed 16 cases on gfx950 — head 64, block 16/32, no alibi, both dtypes, both kv-cache dtypes, both V layouts; everything else in the matrix is covered only by the earlier 1-arch (#62475) runs above, and the other 8 release archs were compiled and linked but never executed.

- [ ] Block-size `default:` of `ATTN_LAUNCH` (`Unsupported block size: `): `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` returns `MultipleOf(16)`, so `block_size=64` does reach the op — needs a `test_paged_attention_unsupported_block_sizes` analogue of the head-size test.
- [ ] `*_fp8_fp8` TUs in CI: only run here via `VLLM_ROCM_FP8_MFMA_PAGE_ATTN=1`, and no `.buildkite/` or `.github/` job sets it; parametrizing a subset over `mfma_type in {"f16", "fp8"}` would cover them.
- [ ] `fp8_out_scale` (`OUTT=uint8_t`, doubles the instantiations in every TU): no test references it.
- [ ] `kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3"` alias handled in `attention_dispatch.cu`: untested.
- [ ] Compile-test the NAVI regions with `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx1100;gfx1201"`: the `__HIP__GFX9__`/NAVI `#if` blocks are now evaluated once per file and were only exercised on MI350.
- [ ] Run the compressed module on gfx942 (MI300): only gfx950 was executed here, and gfx942 is the most-deployed arch.
- [ ] Guard `--offload-compress` on compiler support (`check_compiler_flag`, or a clang-version check) and add an opt-out, so a pre-clang-18 toolchain fails with a clear message instead of `unknown argument`.
- [ ] Measure a real `vllm serve` with a non-`ROCM_ATTN` backend (AITER/Triton): every process that imports `vllm._rocm_C` after a HIP agent is initialised pays the decompression, including processes that never launch paged attention. If that cost matters, compress only the largest TUs (attention, `skinny_gemms_int4`) instead of the whole target.
- [ ] Post-build size assertion for the ROCm extensions (fail above ~1.5–2 GiB), and run the 9-arch `csrc-build` stage in CI: this revert happened because only the nightly links 9 archs.
- [ ] Replace the configure-time `ATTN_ENTRY` regex guard with generated TUs/prototypes/dispatch arms from a single list, so the 12 near-identical files cannot drift out of sync.
- [ ] gfx90a fp8 output: the `TORCH_CHECK(false, "fp8 out scale unsupported for gfx90a")` arm is selected by `#if defined(__gfx90a__)` in host code, where that macro is never defined, so the check is dead and gfx90a silently gets the `uint8_t` instantiations — issue draft in `issue-gfx90a-fp8-out-scale.md`.

## Details

**Root cause.** A HIP TU is one clang process on one core, and extra `--offload-arch` values are processed serially inside it too, so `attention.cu`'s ~860 device kernels (6 dtype/kv-cache combinations × head 2 × block 2 × alibi 2 × fp8-out 2 × {CDNA, NAVI, interleaved} ≈ 288 launcher instantiations) were one ~9-minute serial compile that `MAX_JOBS` cannot help with. (The "`Linking _moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` is slow" symptom is a ninja progress artifact: the link is 159 ms, the line is only printed once `attention.hip.o` finishes.)

**Design.** `csrc/rocm/attention_kernels.cuh` (renamed from `attention.cu`, so the 3.9k moved lines stay a rename and `git blame`/`--follow` survive) keeps the device helpers, the kernel and launcher templates, and the parameter-list macro. Each `csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_<head>_<dtype>_<kv>.cu` is ~4 lines: include the header, instantiate one combination with `ATTN_LAUNCH(...)`, expose a fixed-head-size entry point. `csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu` keeps `is_navi_gpu()` and the dtype/kv-cache dispatch (unchanged order) and forwards to those entry points. The instantiation sets are disjoint, so nothing is compiled twice, and hipify follows the quoted include, so the new header is hipified like the ~15 other headers already in the tree.

**Tradeoffs.**
- The split duplicates device DWARF: at 9 archs the attention TUs go from 1070 to 1189 MiB of `.hip_fatbin` (+119 MiB), which is what pushes the link over 2 GiB — hence `--offload-compress` here, which keeps the device debug info that `RelWithDebInfo` ships.
- Adding a head size, dtype, or kv-cache combination means adding a TU and a `CMakeLists.txt` entry; the comments in `attention_kernels.cuh` and `CMakeLists.txt` point at this.
- The split is unbalanced (head 128 TUs take ~70 s vs ~59 s for head 64), and the floor is ~20 s of frontend parsing per TU (`-fsyntax-only`), so a finer split would not buy much.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix cooperative_topk illegal memory access on NaN scores
author: LopezCastroRoberto
body:
## Purpose

Since #59645, `cooperative_topk` crashes with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` when a row of 64K columns or more contains more NaNs than `top_k` (e.g. 1% of a 256K row, or a fully-NaN row). NaN scores can reach decode top-k during warmup and CUDA-graph capture, where the indexer reads uninitialized KV blocks (see the note in `candidate_blocks.py`). Before #59645 such rows produced garbage indices; now they take down the process.

**Root cause.** nvcc compiles the integer expression `bits | 0x80000000u` in `convert_to_uint32_v2` as the FP operation `-|x|`:

```
ISETP.GE.AND P0, PT, R2, RZ        // bits >= 0 ?
FADD R10, -|R2|, -RZ               // "bits | 0x80000000u" emitted as -|x|
@P0 IMAD.MOV.U32 R9, RZ, RZ, R10
```

That is bit-exact for finite values and ±inf, but FADD canonicalizes NaN to `0x7FFFFFFF`, which is the ordered key of -0.0. The FP16 coarse bins put NaN above +inf (bin 1023), so the two orderings disagree. When NaNs overflow the threshold bin, the exact recovery takes the single-key path with a -0.0 pivot. Every positive score then counts as "above" it, and the unchecked append in `collect_exact_candidates` writes past `s_topk` (compute-sanitizer: invalid `__shared__` write in `unbounded_round0_single_key`).

**Fix.** Read the bits through an opaque `mov.b32`, so the key stays bit-exact and NaN orders above +inf in both the coarse and exact keys, matching `torch.topk`.

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Gate FlashInfer all-reduce on 16-byte row widths
author: fuscof-ibm
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

FlashInfer's fused all-reduce cannot run every tensor shape and [`should_use_fi_ar`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ef5bcaa387632c9943f1e1cd0716354d75b99285/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py#L469) checks all the kernel requirements. However, this is not complete as it never validated row width, so a tensor whose row is not a whole number of 16-byte vectors passed the gate and reached a kernel that cannot run it. On the MNNVL backend this kills the worker; on the trtllm backend, which has no equivalent assert, it truncates its indexing and silently returns wrong results. This PR adds the missing check so these reductions fall back to NCCL.

Mamba2 with `mamba_n_groups=1` hits this at TP>1 (see [`mamba_mixer2.py:144`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/87b804f09d698bdcc5dc53062d2058d7faad08ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L144)). Since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52998 made `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` default to on, hybrid models using Mamba2 layers such as `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` cannot start out of the box.

To reproduce on `main`:

```
vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

fails to start on main (49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4) with the following message:

```
(EngineCore pid=2676902) ERROR 10-20 09:35:05 [core.py:1545] RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Check failed: token_dim % (sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type)) == 0 (1 vs. 0) : token_dim must be divisible by 4', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
(EngineCore pid=2676902) ERROR 10-20 09:35:09 [multiproc_executor.py:315] Worker proc VllmWorker-0 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor.
```

However, it starts correctly with the VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER disabled:

```
VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 \
  vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

CC: @njhill @tdoublep @jeejeelee 

## Claims

- Granite-4 (and any Mamba2 model with `n_groups == 1`) starts at TP>1 with the default FlashInfer all-reduce, instead of dying in `determine_available_memory`.
- Closes a silent-correctness hole on the trtllm backend, which vectorizes the same way but validates nothing.
- Pure gating change: shapes the kernel already accepted take exactly the same path as before. Only shapes that previously crashed now fall back.

## Validation

- **End-to-end.** On main, the serve command above does not start unless FlashInfer all-reduce is disabled:

```
VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 \
  vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

starts as expected. With this PR, the same command *without* the env var starts and serves.

Both the failure and the fix were exercised on the default `auto` backend, which resolves to mnnvl on this 8x H100 box. Similar results for a 2x GB200.

- **Unit test.** `tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_all_reduce.py` covers the shape/dtype combinations the gate has to separate:

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_all_reduce.py -v
```

| shape | dtype | row bytes | accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(16, 1)` | fp32 | 4 | no |
| `(16, 2)` | fp32 | 8 | no |
| `(16, 1)` | bf16 | 2 | no |
| `(16, 4)` | bf16 | 8 | no |
| `(16, 4)` | fp32 | 16 | yes |
| `(16, 8)` | bf16 | 16 | yes |
| `(16, 4096)` | bf16 | 8192 | yes |

The change only diverts shapes that previously aborted the worker onto the NCCL path, which is the default reduction when the FlashInfer all-reduce is off. Shapes the kernel already accepted are unaffected, so there is no numerical delta to measure.

## Details

### Root cause

FlashInfer's fused all-reduce kernels load each token row as a `float4`, so a row must be a whole number of 16-byte vectors. The MNNVL kernel enforces this with a throwing TVM FFI `ICHECK` ([`trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cu:59-60`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/csrc/trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cu#L59-L60)):

```cpp
TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(token_dim % (sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type)), 0)
    << "token_dim must be divisible by " << sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type);
```

The divisor is dtype-dependent — 4 for fp32, 8 for fp16/bf16 — so the observed "token_dim must be divisible by 4" is the fp32 instantiation of the general rule, not a fixed bound. The trtllm path vectorizes the same way (`reinterpret_cast<float4*>` indexed as `hidden_dim / VEC_SIZE`) but carries no equivalent assert, so an undersized dim there truncates its indexing instead of aborting.

`should_use_fi_ar` validated device, rank, contiguity, dtype and workspace capacity, but never row width. A narrow tensor therefore passed the gate and the throwing assert killed the worker instead of the communicator falling back to NCCL.

Mamba2 with `mamba_n_groups=1` hits this at TP>1. The gated RMSNorm parallelizes over the reduction dim and all-reduces an fp32 `(num_tokens, 1)` partial sum ([`mamba_mixer2.py:143-144`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L143-L144)):

```python
local_sums = x.pow(2).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
global_sums = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(local_sums)
```

A row of one fp32 is 4 bytes, so the kernel rejects it and the engine dies inside `determine_available_memory`.

### Why nobody hit this earlier

Both halves predate the user-visible breakage:

| when | what | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-02-22 | `n_groups == 1` TP all-reduce added to `Mixer2RMSNormGated` | #13660 |
| 2026-02-26 | `should_use_fi_ar` reaches current form, no row-width check | #34109 |
| 2026-08-20 | `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` flipped `0` → `1` | #52998 |

The narrow shape and the unvalidated gate coexisted for ~6 months, reachable only by users who explicitly opted in. #52998 exposed the bug rather than creating it.

### Why gate, rather than fix the caller

A caller-side flatten in `mamba_mixer2.py` would be smaller, and there is precedent for it — see #44983 below. Two reasons to prefer the gate:

- **It is not Mamba2's bug.** Any caller reducing a narrow fp32 tensor hits the same kernel constraint. The gate's job is to decide which shapes the kernel can run, and it was answering that question incompletely.
- **The trtllm path needs it regardless.** A caller-side fix for Granite leaves these shapes silently corrupting results on the backend with no assert.

A `try`/`except` fallback would be worse than either: a rank that catches the assert and falls back while its peers proceed deadlocks the collective. The fix has to be a deterministic predicate that all ranks evaluate identically.

### Relation to MiniMax, #44983

MiniMax has a structurally identical reduction — a per-token fp32 variance all-reduced across TP inside an RMSNorm — and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44983 fixed it caller-side by flattening before the reduction ([`rms_norm_tp.py:41`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4/vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/rms_norm_tp.py#L41)), relying on the `len(shape) != 2` check in `should_use_fi_ar` to keep 1-D inputs off the FlashInfer path.


## Not a duplicate

Checked per `AGENTS.md`:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "flashinfer all reduce"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "should_use_fi_ar"
```

No open PR adds a row-alignment check, so this is not a duplicate. Three open PRs are nearby, and two touch the same file:

- **#55973** — fixes FlashInfer fused all-reduce when NVLink multicast is unavailable. Same file, but entirely inside `get_fi_ar_workspace` (it caches unsupported workspace configurations and bails out during CUDA graph capture).
  It does not touch `should_use_fi_ar`. Complementary rather than overlapping: it makes workspace *creation* failures survivable, this makes a *shape* the kernel rejects survivable.
- **#53852** — honours an explicit FlashInfer size override on H200. Same file, and it rewrites the `max_workspace_size` assignment in `__init__` immediately above this change. Textually adjacent, semantically independent (it decides *how big* the workspace is, this decides *which shapes* are eligible), but expect a trivial rebase if it merges first.
- **#60011** — makes `--disable-custom-all-reduce` fall back to NCCL. A different switch, does not touch this file, and does not address shapes the kernel rejects.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

title: [Quantization][Quark] Support MXFP8 (W8A8) routed experts
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

Support AMD Quark checkpoints whose routed experts are OCP MX MXFP8 (W8A8) instead of MXFP4/MXFP6, by adding a `QuarkW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod`.

This also makes per-layer mixed checkpoints (some MoE layers MXFP8, others MXFP4) loadable, since Quark already resolves the scheme per layer.

## Claims

- A Quark checkpoint with MXFP8 (W8A8) routed experts now loads and serves instead of failing at model construction with `ValueError: Unsupported OCP MX dtype combination for MoE: input_dtype=mxfp8_e4m3, weight_dtype=mxfp8_e4m3`.
- MXFP8 experts use the existing MXFP8 MoE stack (`select_mxfp8_moe_backend`, `convert_to_fp8_moe_kernel_format`, `make_fp8_moe_kernel`), i.e. `AITER_MXFP8` on gfx950, with dynamic MXFP8 activations — no new kernel, no new weight layout.
- Per-layer mixed MXFP4/MXFP8 routed experts work with no change to Quark's config resolution: `layer_quant_config` entries matching `<layer>.experts*` select MXFP8 for that layer, everything else falls back to `global_quant_config`.
- Unsupported spellings fail early with an actionable error: only the 1-D `per_group`/`group_size=32`/`e8m0` weight spelling is accepted for MXFP8 experts (the 2-D `per_block` spelling is Linear-only), and biases are rejected.
- No change for existing MXFP4/MXFP6/INT8/FP8/NVFP4 Quark checkpoints.

## Validation

New and affected tests in `tests/quantization/test_quark.py`, on MI350:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  "tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quant_method_dispatch_target[ocp_mx_mxfp8_activation]" \
  "tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quant_method_dispatch_target[ocp_mx_mxfp8_per_block_experts]" \
  "tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quant_method_dispatch_instantiation[ocp_mx_mxfp8_activation]" \
  tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quant_method_dispatch_mixed_mxfp4_mxfp8_experts \
  tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quark_w8a8_mxfp8_moe_weight_shapes
```

```
5 passed, 14 warnings in 8.78s
```

The dispatch matrix these extend, which re-checks every pre-existing Quark scheme:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -k "dispatch_target or dispatch_instantiation" tests/quantization/test_quark.py
```

```
60 passed, 75 deselected, 14 warnings in 36.07s
```

- The `[ocp_mx_mxfp8_activation]` cases resolve W8A8 MXFP8 experts to `(kMxfp8Static, kMxfp8Dynamic, QuarkW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod)` and instantiate that method; `[ocp_mx_mxfp8_per_block_experts]` rejects the 2-D `per_block` spelling on experts.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mixed_mxfp4_mxfp8_experts` checks that a `<layer>.experts*` entry selects MXFP8 for that layer only, with other layers on the global MXFP4 and `shared_experts` unaffected.
- `test_quark_w8a8_mxfp8_moe_weight_shapes` checks the `[E, rows, cols]` E4M3 / `[E, rows, cols / 32]` uint8 parameter layout and the rejection of shapes not divisible by 32.

End-to-end accuracy of a Quark MXFP8 MoE checkpoint was not measured here; the numerics are those of the shared MXFP8 MoE path.

## Details

Quark resolves MoE schemes per layer (`global_quant_config` plus `layer_quant_config` globs), but `quark_moe.py` had no MXFP8 MoE method: `fp8_e4m3`/`per_group`/`group_size=32`/`e8m0` routed experts were dispatched to `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod`, which only implements MXFP4/MXFP6, and failed at model construction.

`QuarkW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod` mirrors `CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w8a8_mxfp8.py#L35).

Behavior changes:
- `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod` no longer declares MXFP8 in its `supported_*_quant_keys`, so MXFP8 experts are rejected by the shared `QuarkMoEMethod` validation instead of the later `OCP_MX_Scheme` check (its `ValueError` keeps upstream's wording),
- Quark checkpoints that previously failed to load now serve

Limitations:
- `hidden_size`/`intermediate_size_per_partition` must be divisible by 32,
- no bias,
- dynamic MXFP8 activations only, and the kernel comes from `select_mxfp8_moe_backend` (`AITER_MXFP8` on gfx950)

No new flag, config field or env var, so no docs change.

No duplicate work: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "quark mxfp8"` and `--search "mxfp8 MoE quark in:body"` return no PR adding a Quark MXFP8 MoE method; #61457 (per-layer fused shared expert) and #56523 (MXFP4 oracle) are distinct.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Validate gfx942's int4 expert requant as int4
author: xaguilar-amd
body:
## Overview

Since #59042, Kimi-K3 with `--quantization-config '{"moe": {"weight": "int4_per_group_32"}}'` fails at startup on gfx942. This PR changes the fail-closed MoE experts check so it validates gfx942's load-time int4 requant as int4.

## Claims

- Kimi-K3 with the int4 expert requant starts and serves on gfx942 again.
- MXFP4 backend selection is unchanged for every other model and GPU.

## Validation

All runs on 8x MI325X (gfx942).

- **Before:** `upstream/main` (`87b804f09d`) fails in `Mxfp4MoEMethod._setup_kernel_k3_situ_gfx942`. I reproduced it by calling `_validate_mxfp4_experts_config(AiterMxfp4Experts, <K3 SiTU MoE config>, AITER_MXFP4_BF16)` on the device:
  ```
  ValueError: AiterMxfp4Experts does not support this MoE deployment since kernel does not support quantization scheme QuantKey(u8,scale(u8,static,GroupShape(row=1, col=32)),symmetric)xNone.
  ```
  With this change the same call passes.
- **Serving:** `vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 -tp 8 --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}'`, with DSpark (k=7) and stock decode.
  - The server starts, requantizes the experts, logs `Using AiterMxfp4Experts`, and runs AITER's `flydsl_moe*_abf16_wint4` kernels.
  - GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 1) scores 0.9575 ± 0.0056 on both strict and flexible extract.
- **Tests:** two new tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`. Both fake the arch, so any ROCm CI machine covers every arch.
  - `test_aiter_mxfp4_experts_quant_scheme_support_by_arch`: `AiterMxfp4Experts` accepts MXFP4 on gfx950 only and int4 on gfx942 only.
  - `test_mxfp4_experts_check_accepts_aiter_deployments`: the fail-closed check accepts every AITER MXFP4 backend on each arch it is deployed on, plus the gfx942 Kimi-K3 int4 requant.
  - `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k "quant_scheme_support or check_accepts_aiter"` gives 13 passed. On `upstream/main`, exactly the two gfx942 int4 cases fail (2 failed, 11 passed), one with the `ValueError` above.
  - `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_gfx942_int4.py` gives 7 passed.

## Details

- **Root cause:** #51274 requantizes K3's MXFP4 experts to packed int4 (`kInt4Static32`, bf16 activations) on gfx942. It builds the kernel with `make_mxfp4_moe_kernel(experts_cls=AiterMxfp4Experts)`.
  - #59042, a CUTLASS FP4 expert-parallel fix, added `_validate_mxfp4_experts_config` at the top of that shared function. The check validates an experts class with the first of `_MXFP4_SCHEME_CANDIDATES` the class supports. If none match, it falls back to the MXFP4 keys.
  - The AITER experts accept MXFP4 keys on gfx950 only. #60322 kept that rule when it split `AiterExperts` into per-quant classes.
  - So on gfx942 no candidate matched, and the check rejected the int4 experts.
- **Fix:** `AiterMxfp4Experts` accepts `(kInt4Static32, None)` on gfx942 only, and that pair is appended as the last candidate.
  - The oracle's backend selection passes `kMxfp4Static` explicitly, so it is unaffected.
  - Classes that support an MXFP4 key still pick that key first, so gfx950 is unchanged.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to develop this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [KVConnector][Mooncake] Coalesce descending block ids to reduce descriptor number for Mooncake TE
author: zhou-yuhan
body:
## Overview

Implements phase 1 of [RFC #63006: Reduce descriptor and WR overhead to improve Mooncake KV transfer bandwidth](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006). Reallocated blocks can arrive in descending order, which Mooncake's ascending-only grouping leaves as individual descriptors. Coalescing these blocks reduces descriptor construction and downstream Transfer Engine (TE) request/WR overhead.

## Claims

- For Qwen3-235B-A22B + 16k prompt, the descending layout drops from **96,256 × 8 KiB descriptors to 94 × 8 MiB descriptors**, with the same 752 MiB payload per rank/request. With 64 KiB Mooncake TE slices, data WRs drop from 96,256 to 12,032.  Reduces **KV xfer time by 56.38%** (79.832 -> 34.820 ms) and increases **KV bandwidth by 125.32%** (9,590.51 -> 21,609.67 MiB/s).

- Reaches comparable performance with NIXL connector for 1-16k prompt length, as benchmarked in [RFC #63006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006), instead of a significant gap.

- This PR can **only cover jointly descending runs** (e.g. P `[3, 2, 1]` blocks and D `[10, 9, 8]` blocks). Anti-diagonal src-dst pairs (e.g. P `[3, 2, 1]` blocks and D `[8, 9, 10]` blocks) cannot be coalesced and remain per-block descriptors.

## Details

Add a `_normalize_paired_block_order()` helper in `_build_transfer_params()`, before logical-to-kernel expansion and `group_concurrent_contiguous()` (which produces `group_remote_block_ids`). For each request/KV group, reverse segments where both source and destination IDs decrease consecutively by one, applying the same permutation to both lists. This preserves every `(src, dst)` pair and lets `group_concurrent_contiguous()` produce fewer descriptors.

- Why normalize before kernel expansion, instead of inside the grouping helper: With two kernel blocks per logical block, source `[3, 2]` and destination `[13, 12]` expand into `[6, 7, 4, 5]` and `[26, 27, 24, 25]`. These kernel lists have no consecutive descending edges, so reversing descending runs inside grouping would miss the merge. Normalize logical IDs first to `[2, 3]` / `[12, 13]`, then expand to `[4, 5, 6, 7]` / `[24, 25, 26, 27]`

- Why not full sort: sort takes O(NlogN), we reverse segments in O(N) to minimize the overhead of the helper. We identify jointly descending consecutive segments, and each segment is reversed independently. With vectorized numpy implementation, the helper overhead is **0.2 ms avg**, **0.64 ms max** with 16k prompt runs.

## Validation

### Unit Tests

**138 passed, 2 deselected** across the Mooncake connector and hybrid-Mamba unit suites. The two bootstrap HTTP-client mock tests are excluded pending [#63122](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63122). Pre-commit passed all applicable hooks.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --noconftest -p pytest_asyncio \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
  -k 'not test_register_worker_retries_on_read_timeout and not test_register_worker_raises_after_max_attempts'

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
```

</details>

### Qwen3-235B-A22B E2E Results

Hardware, model, serving parameters, and workload follow [RFC #63006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006): Qwen3-235B-A22B BF16, 1P1D on two nodes, each with 8 × H20 GPUs and four RDMA HCAs (~48 GiBps RoCE each); TP8/PP1/DP1, block size 16, max model length 40,960. Each prompt length uses the same synthetic trace across variants: 150 requests at 0.5 requests/s over 300 seconds. Mooncake binary is main@74944a77 with `MC_RDMA_SIGNAL_INTERVAL=32 MC_MAX_WR=4096`

Values are means:

| Prompt | Connector | TTFT (ms) | TTFT delta vs. NIXL | KV BW (MiB/s) | KV BW delta vs. NIXL | Xfer time (ms) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1K | MC Before | 172.01 | +13.84% | 11225.49 | -24.82% | 4.272 |
| 1K | MC After | 168.36 | +11.42% | 21642.55 | +44.95% | 2.178 |
| 1K | NIXL | 151.11 | — | 14930.98 | — | 3.062 |
| 2K | MC Before | 225.72 | +13.78% | 10359.36 | -45.91% | 9.172 |
| 2K | MC After | 212.24 | +6.99% | 21678.17 | +13.19% | 4.346 |
| 2K | NIXL | 198.38 | — | 19151.58 | — | 4.704 |
| 4K | MC Before | 394.90 | +12.55% | 10198.04 | -50.29% | 18.674 |
| 4K | MC After | 365.38 | +4.13% | 21610.32 | +5.33% | 8.705 |
| 4K | NIXL | 350.88 | — | 20517.07 | — | 8.782 |
| 8K | MC Before | 770.57 | +13.28% | 9326.52 | -56.07% | 40.603 |
| 8K | MC After | 698.95 | +2.75% | 21986.85 | +3.57% | 17.117 |
| 8K | NIXL | 680.23 | — | 21229.52 | — | 16.965 |
| 16K | MC Before | 1695.34 | +11.85% | 9590.51 | -55.45% | 79.832 |
| 16K | MC After | 1543.78 | +1.85% | 21609.67 | +0.38% | 34.820 |
| 16K | NIXL | 1515.75 | — | 21527.40 | — | 33.518 |
| 32K | MC Before | 115834.41 | +8.69% | 6875.05 | -67.87% | 221.395 |
| 32K | MC After | 113426.24 | +6.43% | 10220.36 | -52.23% | 159.904 |
| 32K | NIXL | 106573.46 | — | 21394.52 | — | 67.050 |

After optimization, Mooncake's GQA performance shows:

- For 1-16k prompt: comparable or higher KV BW compared with NIXL. Each rank achieves ~21 GiBps KV BW, compared to ~24 GiBps (4 x ~48 GiBps HCAs) theoretical maximum.

- For 32k prompt: better than baseline before optimization, but still -52.23% slower than NIXL because of anti-diagonal src-dst block pairs. With APC on, MC After gives KV BW 21612.980 MiB/s and Xfer time 69.672 ms. See detailed explanation in the discussion below https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63142#issuecomment-6358485864.


### Execution Time Breakdown

We show the 16k prompt run execution time breakdown with the same approach in [RFC #63006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006). Each call transfers 752 MiB, mean values:

| Configuration / input layout | Calls | Descriptors/call | Submit (ms) | Wait (ms) | First post offset (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before normalization, ascending| 600 | 94 | 2.275 | 40.825 | 2.881 |
| Before normalization, descending| 600 | 96,256 | 30.483 | 52.060 | 33.254 |
| After normalization| 1,200 | 94 | 2.464 | 31.382 | 3.247 |

- **submit** constructs and enqueues WRs
- **wait** polls completion while background workers continue posting and progressing RDMA.
- **first post offset** is the wall time from the C++ API entry to the return of the first worker WR post. Normalization reduces descriptors so that TE workers don't need to wait for a long WRs contruction period.

## Related

- [#63006 — Reduce descriptor and WR overhead to improve Mooncake KV transfer bandwidth](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006): this PR implements Phase 1.
- [#60523 — Improving MooncakeConnector](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523): broader connector optimization roadmap.
- [#57952](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57952): packed-region coalescing; does not normalize descending block IDs.
- [#62478 — Vectorize transfer descriptor build](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62478): accelerates construction while preserving descriptor values/order, including descending boundaries.
- [#60605 — Optimize Mooncake contiguous block grouping](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60605): reduces grouping overhead while preserving the ascending-only grouping behavior.
- [#63122 — Mooncake tests: patch the httpx module the connector uses](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63122): independent fix for the two existing bootstrap test failures.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Capture the decoder replay graphs on the model graphs' stream
author: xqoasis
body:
## Overview

Capture the DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder replay graphs on the model graphs' capture stream, so that they reuse the model graphs' free blocks in the shared graph pool instead of reserving a second pool. Fixes #62965.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on GB200 (DP4, breakable PIECEWISE graphs up to 16384 tokens): graph capture memory drops from 15.52 GiB to 9.88 GiB per rank, and the replay capture no longer adds a graph pool segment.
- No accuracy or capture-time change beyond run-to-run noise (table below).
- Only the replay graphs move to the shared stream. The speculator and encoder captures, and Model Runner V1, keep a new stream per capture.

## Validation

GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1P1D, prefill DP4, `max_model_len` 16k, breakable PIECEWISE graphs with capture sizes up to 16384 tokens, DSpark on. Two fresh service starts per arm. Measured on a v0.32.0-based build with this change; see Details for what differs on `main`.

| | separate streams (`main`) | shared stream (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| prefill graph capture memory per rank | 15.52 / 15.52 GiB | 9.88 / 9.88 GiB |
| capture time | 36 / 36 s | 36 / 37 s |
| GSM8K (1319, greedy) | 97.50 / 97.42 | 97.57 / 97.12 |

- Before the change, `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` segments at the end of `capture_model()`, grouped by `(segment_pool_id, stream)`, show the replay graphs' own pool: 5.18 GiB reserved, none of it in use. After the change, the replay capture adds no graph pool segment.
- First-token top-20 logprobs on 64 prompts of 1k-7k tokens (prefix cache off, concurrency 1 and 16) differ across arms by as much as across two starts of the same arm. At concurrency 1: first token equal in 59-62/64 across arms vs. 60-61/64 within an arm; median |Δlogprob| of the first token 0.05-0.06 in both cases.

No test is added: CI has no runner for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with replay graphs, and the existing replay capture test (`tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py`) calls `capture_replay_graphs()` without a stream, so it keeps today's behavior.

## Details

**Root cause.** Since #59532, `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager` captures the replay graphs after the model graphs, in a `CudaGraphManager.capture()` call of its own. Every `capture()` enters `graph_capture()`, which creates a new stream. Both managers capture into the global graph pool, but the caching allocator reuses a free block only on the stream that freed it, so the replay graphs cannot use the model graphs' free pool blocks and reserve their own.

**Change.**

- `graph_capture(device, stream=None)` reuses `stream` when one is given.
- `CudaGraphManager.capture(..., stream=None)` captures on it and records the stream it used in `capture_stream`.
- `GPUModelRunner.capture_model()` passes the model graphs' `capture_stream` to `ModelState.capture_inner_cudagraphs()`, and DeepSeek-V4.1 forwards it to `capture_replay_graphs()`.

**Why sharing is safe.** A replay graph runs inside an eager break of a model graph. `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager.run()` first gathers the layer inputs into its static `input_buffers`, then replays. After the break, the model graph reads only the break's own output buffers (`DecoderReplayLayers._break_outputs`), which live outside the graph pool. KV caches and the replay batch metadata are persistent. So no model graph tensor in the pool is still needed while a replay graph runs.

The one exception is aux hidden states captured before the replay layers: the forward holds them across the break. `DecoderReplayLayers.has_early_aux()` reports whether any aux layer id is below the replay start, and in that case the replay graphs keep their own stream. For DSpark on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, the aux layers (37-39) are produced inside the replay layers (from layer 20 on), so the fallback does not apply there.

**Differences from the measured build.** The port to `main` also forwards the stream through the specialized decode model state's `capture_inner_cudagraphs()` override (#61868), and the `graph_capture()` change sits next to #57481's edits. The early-aux fallback is new in this PR. It returns `False` in the measured configuration, so the measured path is unchanged.

**Alternatives.**

- #59537 caches one capture stream per device for every `graph_capture()` call. It would also let the replay graphs reuse the model graphs' pool, but it puts the speculator capture on that stream as well. The speculator runs after the target forward and reads its outputs, so it needs its own lifetime argument. Passing the stream only to the graphs replayed inside the model graphs limits the change to the case argued above.
- Capturing the replay graphs nested inside the model graph capture, as #56752 did, also shares the pool, but then a replay graph is captured inside one model graph size and replayed inside others.
- Smaller `decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes` shrink the replay pool proportionally, but larger replay batches then run eagerly.

title: [CI][Benchmarks] Fix attention smoke test backend names and failure exit status
author: johncalesp
body:
## Overview



The attention benchmark smoke test uses flash flashinfer, but the benchmark now requires the exact backend names FLASH_ATTN FLASHINFER. Both configurations therefore report Unknown backend.

These errors were caught and recorded without changing the process exit status. The command returned 0, allowing CI to report success even though neither benchmark ran successfully.

This change:

* Updates benchmarks.yaml to use FLASH_ATTN FLASHINFER.
* Makes the benchmark exit with status 1 when any configuration fails, after reporting results and writing requested JSON/CSV output.
* Applies the same failure check before the profiling path’s early return.
* Documents the corrected command and exit behavior.

PR #45728 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45728) addressed obsolete arguments in the same smoke test but retained the lowercase backend names.

title: [ROCm] Fuse tiny-M MXFP8 quant into the block32 GEMM; guard lm_head skinny-GEMM by weight size
author: alexm-redhat
body:
## Overview

Two decode-time fastpaths for DeepSeek-V4.x block32 MXFP8 linears on MI355X (gfx950): fuse the tiny-M activation quant into the block32 GEMM (one launch instead of two), and guard the lm_head skinny-GEMM dispatch by weight size (weights far larger than L2 stay on the generic GEMM fall-through).

Part of the DSV4.1-Flash MI355X serving fastpath series — four **independent** PRs on `main`@90c4a1a73e, each reviewable and mergeable separately, in any order. Siblings: #63180 (fused shared experts), #63181 (fused draft sampling), #63182 (draft-prepare fastpaths). The four series PRs all register kill switches in `vllm/envs.py` at the same anchor and therefore conflict textually with each other there; the resolution is to keep both sides. This branch trial-merges cleanly into current `main`.

## Claims

- **Fused quant+GEMM** (`rocm_block32_gemm.py`): at M ≤ 8 (decode shapes) the block32 linear path launched `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel` solely to produce the e4m3 tiles + E8M0 scales the packed GEMM immediately re-reads. The fused kernel computes that quant inside the GEMM's K loop, in registers, with the same arithmetic — one launch instead of two, no activation round trip. Bit-exact against the stock two-launch path at all eligible shapes (tuned tiers, masked K tail, in-launch split-K); ineligible inputs (non-contiguous x, fp32 x, M > 8) fall back bit-identically. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_FUSED_MXFP8_QUANT_GEMM`.
- **lm_head skinny-GEMM guard** (`layers/utils.py`): `wvSplitK_hf_sml` re-reads the weight matrix once per K-shard, so its effective bandwidth collapses on weights far larger than L2 — at TP=4 the DSpark draft vocab-parallel lm_head shard ([32320, 5120] bf16, ~315 MiB, one call per decode step) hit this collapse. Weights above `VLLM_SKINNY_GEMM_MAX_WEIGHT_BYTES` (default 256 MiB) stay on the generic hipBLASLt fall-through at 1 < n ≤ 5; n = 1 (no pathology) is unchanged. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_LMHEAD_SKINNY_GEMM_GUARD`.
- **−117 µs median decode ITL (−2.1%) on the current base** (`main`@`717cf84342`) — official DSV4.1-Flash serving command at TP=4 on MI355X, every paired run faster (rebase re-check under Validation). The submission-base study measured **−2.45% (−177/−188 µs)** over 12 position-balanced A/B cycles, and the win holds at the same magnitude across bases and images (−127 µs on the nightly ROCm-10 re-verification, −117 µs on the rebased tip). TTFT unchanged within noise.

## Validation

**Benchmark** — official serving command (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, DSpark k=5, `--monokernel`, MI355X), measured at TP=4; both fastpaths key on batch/weight shapes, not TP size. Both arms run this branch's tip; the OFF arm disables only this PR's two levers. 12 position-balanced A/B cycles (blocked AAA BBB, then BAB, then ABA), fresh server per arm per cycle, 2 sampled + 1 greedy client run per cycle (16 prompts, ISL 16 / OSL 2048, concurrency 1); arm statistic = median of per-run mean ITL; every lever's engagement asserted from the server log before the client runs.

| metric | ON median | OFF median | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| ITL t>0 | 7.065 ms | 7.243 ms | −177 µs (−2.45%) |
| ITL t0 | 6.977 ms | 7.165 ms | −188 µs |
| TTFT t>0 | 24.70 ms | 25.01 ms | −0.31 ms |
| TTFT t0 | 24.74 ms | 25.68 ms | −0.94 ms |

11 of 12 sampled cycles faster (one boundary overlap: ON max 7.148 ms vs OFF min 7.120 ms).

**Nightly ROCm-10 re-verification** — re-measured on the current nightly ROCm-10 image (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly, TP=4, same command and protocol; one fresh boot per arm, 2 sampled + 1 greedy run each): ON 5.498 ms vs OFF 5.625 ms median mean-ITL → **−127 µs (−2.27%)**, fully disjoint per-run ranges (ON 5.438–5.510, OFF 5.550–5.636), spec-decode acceptance parity (sampled-run means 3.29 vs 3.34).

**Rebase re-check** — rebased onto the latest `main`; the runtime diff is unchanged, with one added test-only commit hardening the skinny-GEMM guard tests against dropped ROCTracer captures (the profiler flake behind the `amd-mi300-model-executor` CI failure). Full local CI-equivalent suites on this tip: model_executor 1313 passed, benchmarks 219 passed. Same A/B protocol: ON 5.510 ms vs OFF 5.627 ms median mean-ITL → **−117 µs (−2.09%)**; every paired run is faster (sampled −133/−92 µs, greedy −169 µs), and both arms' censuses assert the fused path engaged / disabled respectively.

**Accuracy** — gsm8k, 5-shot, strict match, 1319 samples, one run per arm: ON 0.9325, OFF 0.9242. Both inside the 0.9196–0.9340 band observed across repeated draws of this build; across the series the paired on/off deltas scatter on both sides of zero (engine run-to-run scatter) and no arm falls outside the band.

**Tests** — the fused-quant tests live in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py` next to the other `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` tests (the standalone file from the first revision is gone). Beyond the bit-exactness-vs-stock comparison, the serving-shape test now also checks the fused output against a high-precision QDQ reference — dequantize both MXFP8 operands and contract in fp32, independent of the block32 GEMM kernel under test (rel err < 5e-3) — so a regression in the GEMM itself cannot hide behind the bit-exact comparison. All tests pass locally on MI355X (gfx950):

```
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py \
       tests/model_executor/layers/test_lmhead_skinny_gemm_guard.py -q
111 passed, 15 warnings in 47.26s
```

Of the 111, the tests added by this PR are 28 items — 21 fused-quant tests (~1.8 s) and 7 skinny-GEMM-guard tests (~1.4 s); the rest of the wall time is interpreter/import startup and the pre-existing MXFP8 suite. Single MI355X GPU, nightly ROCm-10 image.

CI notes: the fused-quant tests are CDNA4-gated (`current_platform.is_rocm() and supports_mx()`) and skip on MI300 CI pools — they are validated locally above; the skinny-GEMM guard test runs on any ROCm GPU (needs the `wvSplitK` custom op). The full pre-commit suite passes on the changed files (ruff, typos, mypy, check-torch-cuda-call, check-test-tethering, check-forbidden-imports, ...), and every commit is DCO-signed.

The tip adds review-driven changes over the benchmarked tree — tests centralized into the existing file, the QDQ reference, the kill switches renamed to `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_*`, and the long docstrings trimmed to the dispatch rules (benchmark details now in this description) — plus two earlier lint-level fixes (`torch.accelerator.synchronize()` for pre-commit `check-torch-cuda-call`, a local `args: tuple` annotation in `rocm_block32_gemm.py` for mypy). No serving-path semantics change: the renamed kill switches are the only env-facing difference.

<details><summary>Reproduction</summary>

Server (ON arm) — official serving command, as measured at TP=4 (the fastpaths are not TP=4-specific):

```
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 --port 8123 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --moe-backend aiter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --block-size 128 --monokernel \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

OFF arm: identical, plus `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_FUSED_MXFP8_QUANT_GEMM=1 VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_LMHEAD_SKINNY_GEMM_GUARD=1`.

Load (after a 4-prompt warmup; add `--temperature 0` for the greedy run):

```
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --port 8123 --backend openai --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16 --random-output-len 2048 \
  --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 90,95,99 \
  --save-result
```

Accuracy (same engine config; `max_model_len 16384` and no `cpu_offload` are the only harness deviations):

```
python -c '
import lm_eval
lm_eval.simple_evaluate(
    model="vllm",
    model_args=dict(
        pretrained="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017",
        max_model_len=16384, tensor_parallel_size=4,
        tokenizer_mode="deepseek_v41", gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
        block_size=128, moe_backend="aiter", monokernel=True,
        attention_config={"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4",
                          "indexer_sparse_logits": True},
        compilation_config={"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 6, 8]},
        speculative_config={"method": "dspark",
                            "num_speculative_tokens": 5,
                            "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
                            "rejection_sample_method": "block",
                            "enable_adaptive_verification": False}),
    tasks=["gsm8k"], num_fewshot=5, batch_size=8)'
```

</details>

## Details

**Fused quant+GEMM.** At M ≤ 8 the block32 linear path pays a full `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel` launch just to produce the e4m3 tiles + E8M0 scales the packed GEMM immediately re-reads; the fused kernel computes that quant inside the GEMM's K loop, in registers, with the exact same arithmetic. Eligibility is a shape-table hit (serving shapes at TP=4 covering the K-structure variety: multi-band K=5120 with the in-launch split-K tier, the masked-K-tail K=1280, a small-K tile, and the default-config tier); degenerate activation blocks (all-zero, denormal, huge, negative-mirror) quantize identically, and CUDA-graph capture/replay is bit-exact in both counter states. The per-row-scale dispatch branch of the linear kernel is unaffected.

**lm_head skinny-GEMM guard.** The guard is a byte-size predicate on the weight at the skinny dispatch site: above the cap, at 1 < n ≤ 5, the call goes to the generic hipBLASLt GEMM (the same kernel class the n=6 path uses); below the cap, or at n=1, or with the kill switch, dispatch is stock. The swap is not bit-exact (different GEMM kernel, different accumulation order) — numerics are checked within bf16 GEMM tolerance, and the decision table, dispatch selection, env behavior and one-shot-per-site census warning are pinned by tests.

Both paths log their engagement as WARNINGs (one line per site/state), so ON/OFF arms can be asserted from the server log before benchmarking.

<details><summary>MI355X measurements behind the skinny-GEMM guard</summary>

Measured on MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP=4, vocab-parallel `[32320, K]` bf16 lm_head shards, from serving traces and isolated microbenches:

- The DSpark draft lm_head `[32320, 5120]` (315.5 MiB, n=5, once per decode step) ran `wvSplitK_hf_sml<..., 2, 5>` at **1.55 TB/s** (213.8 µs/call in-graph), while the generic fall-through class runs the same GEMM at **~6.5 TB/s** (~51–73 µs).
- The n=6 target-verify lm_head `[32320, 7168]` (442 MiB) already dispatches to hipBLASLt `Cijk MT64x16x512` (56.2 µs/call in-graph, 7.9 TB/s), i.e. the fall-through kernel is fast and CUDA-graph-capture-safe in this exact serving configuration.
- Isolated microbench on the target-shape shard at n=5: wvSplitK 313.3 µs vs `torch.linear` 71.2 µs (4.4×).
- The n=1 variant (`wvSplitK_hf_sml<..., 2, 1>`) shows no pathology on large weights (6.9 TB/s on the 442 MiB shard); its fall-through (LLMM1) would be a numerics change with no speed win, so n=1 keeps stock dispatch.

The mechanism is weight re-reads: `wvSplitK_hf_sml` streams the weight once per K-shard, so above L2-sized weights the effective bandwidth collapses. This is orthogonal to VGPR-spill fixes in the skinny kernel itself (#63015, #62846) — see the related-PRs note below.

</details>

**Related PRs.**

- #63015 / #62846 (skinny-GEMM tile/spill fixes): the guard here addresses a different mechanism — weight re-reads vs L2 bandwidth on very large weights — not VGPR spills, so the two are orthogonal and compose. The spill fixes should recover `wvSplitK` throughput on shapes that spill; the re-read cost on weights far above L2 remains. Once either lands we can re-measure the `[32320, 5120]` n=5 shard on top of it and revisit the guard's byte cap / n-window if the fixed `wvSplitK` wins there.
- #59782 (fused MXFP8 quant, draft): same fused-quant idea, per-shape cutoffs and keeps the fusion past M=8 on some shapes, where this PR caps every shape at M=8 with a bit-exactness contract against the stock path. In our measurements the fusion works well at M ≤ 8; we have not measured beyond that and are happy to coordinate on which approach to keep.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Don't reject LoRA for speculative decoding drafters
author: YaashuDave
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #61884. `LoRAConfig.verify_with_model_config` now skips the `SupportsLoRA` check for speculative decoding drafters (`runner_type == "draft"`), so LoRA + spec decode works again with drafters that don't implement `SupportsLoRA`. Reported by @cjackal in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61884#issuecomment-6346398560 and the following comments.

## Claims

- With `enable_lora` and a drafter without `SupportsLoRA` (e.g. `DeepSeekMTPModel`), the draft `VllmConfig` validates again instead of raising `LoRA is not supported for ...`.
- Target models without `SupportsLoRA` (e.g. Zamba2) are still rejected at config time, as in #61884.
- No change for drafters that implement `SupportsLoRA` (e.g. EAGLE-Llama, Llama draft models).

## Validation

CPU reproduction: `EngineArgs(model="luccafong/deepseek_mtp_main_random", enable_lora=True, speculative_config={"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}).create_engine_config()`, then `replace(cfg, model_config=cfg.speculative_config.draft_model_config)`, as `DraftModelProposer` and other proposers do:

| | main @ `71e9320633` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| target `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` (`SupportsLoRA`) | OK | OK |
| draft `DeepSeekMTPModel` (`runner_type="draft"`, no `SupportsLoRA`) | `ValidationError` from the LoRA check | OK |

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/test_config.py -k lora
```

- New `test_lora_allowed_for_drafter_without_lora_support`; the existing #61884 test now sets `runner_type="generate"` and still checks the rejection.
- Full `tests/test_config.py`: 438 passed. The same 14 tests fail on main and on this branch, all on Hugging Face downloads (gated or unavailable models in my environment).
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

Validated on CPU only; I did not run LoRA + spec decode end to end on a GPU.

## Details

**Root cause:** `VllmConfig.__post_init__` calls `lora_config.verify_with_model_config(self.model_config)`. Several proposers rebuild the `VllmConfig` with the draft model config via `dataclasses.replace` (e.g. `DraftModelProposer`, Step-3.5, the MRV2 standalone/Gemma4 speculators, Qwen4Exp/Step5 MTP), so the check from #61884 also ran on the drafter.

**Fix:** skip the check when `model_config.runner_type == "draft"`. LoRA is only applied to the target model (`load_lora_model` wraps `self.model` in the model runners), so drafters don't need `SupportsLoRA`.

cc @cjackal @jeejeelee @linitra24

title: [Refactor][ROCm][MoE] Let each AiterExperts subclass own its AITER call args
author: divakar-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Final part of #54966 item 5 ("Split AITER experts by weight quantization key"). #60322 split `AiterExperts` into 5 leaf classes; this PR moves each scheme's AITER call arguments into its leaf, so the shared `rocm_aiter_fused_experts()` no longer branches on quant scheme.

## Claims

- Each leaf declares its AITER `QuantMethod` (`_AITER_QUANT_METHOD`); `rocm_aiter_fused_experts()` takes `quant_method` instead of re-deriving it from `quant_config` flags.
- `AiterMxfp4Experts` owns its gate_mode / bias / `q_dtype_a` overrides (incl. DSV4 a4w4) via `_extra_fused_moe_kwargs()`.
- `AiterFp8ChannelExperts.apply()` owns the topk=1 / `apply_router_weight_on_input` dispatch to `asm_moe_tkw1` and its `num_local_tokens` restriction; the generic function has no tkw1 branch.
- `AiterFp8BlockExperts` declares it doesn't support `apply_router_weight_on_input`.
- No numerical change intended.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` | 88 passed |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k aiter` | 67 passed, 14 skipped, 2 failed* |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py` | 53 passed |

\*Both failures are `MoriEPv2PrepareAndFinalize` + `AiterUnquantizedExperts` (multi-GPU) hitting a GPU memory fault; they fail identically on `main` without this PR.

New `test_aiter_fp8_channel_experts_owns_tkw1_dispatch` drives `AiterFp8ChannelExperts` through the modular kernel and checks both routes against the reference MoE: topk=1 → `asm_moe_tkw1`, topk=2 → `fused_moe`.

No model eval: refactor with no intended numerical change; kernel tests compare against the reference MoE.

## Details

- Direct callers that bypass the leaves (quark W4A8, DSV4, two test references) pass `quant_method` explicitly. `derive_aiter_quant_method()` and `mxfp4_w4a16_extra_kwargs()` give them the values a leaf would; the test references use these rather than the leaf under test so a wrong leaf value can't hide on both sides.
- For direct callers only, `rocm_aiter_fused_experts()` no longer auto-dispatches tkw1. No in-tree caller relied on it (quark W4A8 has no per-token activation quant, so it already took `fused_moe`). Out-of-tree callers must also pass the new required `quant_method`.
- Dropped the block-FP8 `w1_scale`/`w2_scale is not None` asserts: the FP8 oracle always builds the quant config with scales.
- Not a duplicate: this is the last open item-5 PR in the #54966 progress tracker.

title: [Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Speculator config classes and custom speculators
author: njhill
body:
## Overview

Lets users plug their own speculator into Model Runner V2. Each speculator now has a declarative config class that describes its behavior, replacing the speculative-method name checks spread across config, scheduler, KV cache and model code.

## Claims

- **Custom V2 speculators.** A plugin registers a method name with `register_speculative_method(name, config_cls)`, typically from a vLLM general plugin, and users select it with `method="<name>"`. The implementation is a `BaseSpeculator` subclass, usually via `DraftModelSpeculator` or `TargetDependentARSpeculator`. A config that subclasses a built-in one (e.g. `Eagle3SpeculatorConfig`) inherits that speculator's draft-model setup and behavior. Custom methods require MRV2. A custom speculator can take its own options via `speculator_options`.
- **Declarative speculator configs.** Each V2 speculator has a `SpeculatorConfig` subclass in an import-light `config.py` next to it. The class declares traits such as `uses_target_hidden_states`, `uses_aux_hidden_states`, `num_lookahead_tokens`, `max_model_len`, `supports_watermarking` and `supports_pcp`, and names its implementation class. Callers query `speculative_config.speculator_config` (or shortcut properties for the most widely used traits) instead of comparing method names. The scheduler process never imports a speculator implementation.
- **Per-method setup moves out of `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__`.** It goes into the config classes: `default_model`, `configure`, draft-checkpoint hooks (`adapt_draft_model_config`, `resolve_num_speculative_tokens`), and `apply_options` for method-specific options. Each config lists the method-specific options it accepts in `supported_options`, and passing another one fails at startup.
- **Draft models declare their speculator.** A draft model sets `speculator_config_class` to its speculator's config class (new `SpeculativeDraftModel` interface, exposed through the model registry by qualified name). This replaces the hardcoded draft-architecture lists used to select DFlash2, LiLiCorr, XPress, DSpark and Gemma4 MTP.
- **Checkpoint detection never overrides an explicitly configured method.** For example, an explicit `mtp` could previously be rewritten to `eagle` by the draft checkpoint's name. An explicit method is now checked against the speculator the draft model declares, if any, and a mismatch fails with an explanatory error. This incorporates the intent of #41834 / #47490.
- `BaseSpeculator` now provides defaults for the members the runner reads (`supports_mm_inputs`, `draft_logits`, `prepare_watermarking()`), so speculators, custom ones included, only define what they use.

## Validation

Unit tests run on the NVIDIA GCP cluster (GB200), on this branch with current main merged in:

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode` (excluding the slow e2e/acceptance tests), `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/config`, `tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py`, `tests/models/test_registry.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, workspace / EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state / PP embedding-sharing worker tests | 2125 passed, 1 failed (gated `meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout` download, unrelated) |
| Tests that fake the speculative config: KV offload scheduler, Kimi K3 KDA metadata, fused shared expert, DSpark MLA, DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP, MRV2 model runner | 659 passed |
| e2e `draft_model/test_async.py::test_no_sync_with_spec_decode[eagle-mla-deepseek]` | passed |

Each draft model module that declares a speculator, and each speculator config module, was also imported in a fresh process to check for import cycles.

New tests are in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py`. They cover:
- registration, validation and V2-only enforcement;
- `init_speculator` construction;
- the import-light check for all speculator config modules;
- checkpoint resolution, explicit-method mismatch errors, and selection via draft model declarations.

Not yet done: an end-to-end run of a custom speculator plugin, and e2e spec-decode acceptance runs (EAGLE3/MTP/DFlash/DSpark) to confirm there are no behavior changes.

## Details

- **Line count.** About +1430/−750 non-test lines. Much of this moves existing per-method logic out of `speculative.py` (which shrinks substantially) into per-speculator config modules.
- **V1 runner.** `SpeculativeConfig` is shared with the V1 runner, so V1-only pieces are grouped in `v1_speculator_configs.py` (suffix, V1 `custom_class` proposers) or marked "V1 model runner only", to be deleted along with V1. The V1 `custom_class` proposer interface is unchanged on V1 and still rejected by V2. V1-only checks (e.g. P-EAGLE `parallel_drafting`, heterogeneous vocab) stay as method checks rather than declared traits, and `parallel_drafting` is now documented as deprecated.
- **`base_method`.** `method` keeps the registered custom name, for logging, usage stats and the config hash. `SpeculativeConfig.base_method` gives the built-in method a custom config is based on, and is what the `use_*` predicates and model-specific checks consult.
- **Behavior-preserving trait moves.** Upstream logic is kept but expressed as traits:
  - the draft max-model-len cap from #63251 (`SpeculatorConfig.max_model_len`);
  - DSpark's separate workspace lane (`uses_separate_workspace_lane`);
  - target input-embedding sharing under PP, now inferred from the draft model class;
  - the draft-pass `max_num_active_seqs` limit (`max_num_draft_seqs`).
- **Speculators-format checkpoints.** The speculators override no longer replaces a custom method that is based on the checkpoint's method. It rejects one that's based on a different method.
- **Docs.** See "Custom Speculators (Experimental)" in `docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md`.
- **Reviewing.** The branch has accumulated review and merge commits, so it's best reviewed as a whole diff.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Per-request draft retention for structured output under PP
author: yzong-rh
body:
Co-authors: @michael-gpu, @tomasruizt 
cc @ArcheyChen 

## Overview

Revert https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442, which introduces a performance regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs, and re-fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54437 by addressing the root cause in `DraftTokensHandler`.

Rework of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61348, rebased, with remaining comments addressed, pre-commit fixed, and simplified implementation + tests.

## Claims

#54442 patched the issue in #54437 by masking out the draft tokens after a handoff race in `DraftTokensHandler`. This fixes #61348 but effectively shortens the draft sequence, causing an acceptance-length (and performance) regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs.

This PR addresses the `DraftTokensHandler` handoff race directly, fixing the original issue #54437 while maintaining acceptance length.

This PR also adds an E2E repro for #54437 and acceptance length regression.

## Validation

This branch

More tests

Performance:

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e15dc602fbfd11e2b64c2d41527a1a72
