tight / c96 | 3,865.53 [3,771.94, 3,959.13] | 21,029.32 [20,574.89, 21,483.75] | +444.02%

</body></html>

## Details

### Background

`DraftTokensHandler` allows workers to asynchronously send draft tokens back to the scheduler / structured output manager for processing.

With async scheduling, it works roughly like:
```
Scheduler-side                          Worker-side
--------------------------------------------------
schedule step N
sample step N
                                        execute step N
schedule step N+1
wait for step N
                                        sample step N
                                        DraftTokensHandler.set_draft_tokens
                                        execute step N+1
DraftTokensHandler.get_draft_tokens
generate sampling bitmasks
sample step N+1
                                        sample step N+1
...
```

On main, `DraftTokensHandler` holds the latest batch set by the worker. This works fine for PP=1, but when PP>=2, this can occur:
```
Scheduler-side          Worker-side
----------------------------------
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch A)
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch B)
get_draft_tokens
```

Micro-batch B replaces micro-batch A in the handler. Scheduler-side cannot recover A's drafts and generates incorrect grammar bitmasks, leading to #54437.

#54442 fixes this by effectively truncating the worker-side draft sequence, reducing acceptance length.

This PR fixes this by making `DraftTokensHandler` track draft tokens by request ID. So micro-batch B cannot override micro-batch A.

Final notes:
- Suggest reviewing commits independently
  - `e3595db629d88881e74eafc357e471924b4d9c1f`: revert #54442, could be a separate PR
  - `c67afdec130ca06c6beb5e286a5b83b91fdae3a2`: track draft tokens by request ID.
  - `bb3694db86066ea2d272051b0495bad3ae09d026`: E2E repro
- Alternative #61348 includes adding a debug flag to catch the handoff race, this is not included in this PR in favor of the E2E repro.

title: [Core] Change default --block-size from 16 to 64
author: NickLucche
body:
## Overview

Changes the default `--block-size` for `vllm serve` / `EngineArgs` from 16 to 64, via `CacheConfig.DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE`. Also teaches `RocmAttentionBackend` to prefer 16-token blocks for default-sized runs, keeping ROCm on its native paged-attention kernel.

## Claims

- `CacheConfig()` (and therefore `vllm serve` without `--block-size`) now resolves to `block_size=64`; an explicit `--block-size` still sets `user_specified_block_size=True` and takes precedence.
- Platforms/attention backends that declare a preferred or restricted block size continue to override the default exactly as before: `update_block_size_for_backend` only consults `DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE` when the user did not specify `--block-size`.
- ROCm runs without an explicit `--block-size` keep the native C++ paged-attention kernel (block sizes 16/32) instead of silently falling back to the slower Triton path that any other multiple of 16 routes to.

## Validation

- Full Buildkite CI build [#97300](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97300) passed (171 jobs), including the suites that caught regressions in the first run (#96922): H200/MI355 KV connector offload, MI250 PyTorch fullgraph cudagraph compatibility, and model executor.
- First CI run (#96922, default alone) failed exactly where 16-token assumptions were baked in: offloading-connector chunk sizes (48/16 vs the 64 GPU block), shared-storage connector hash-count expectations, an autotune cache-key test using 64 as a "non-default" control, and a 25-minute MI250 hang in RocmAttn with 64-token blocks (engine never returned from a step). All are fixed by this PR; the MI250 job went from timeout to passing in 8m51s, confirming the hang was block-size-related, not a flake.
- `tests/config/test_config_utils.py` (includes new `test_cache_config_default_block_size`): 28 passed.
- `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 159 passed.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py`: 16 passed, 93 skipped.
- `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py::test_autotune_cache_key_normalizes_kv_init_fields`: passed locally.
- `pre-commit run` on changed files: passed (ruff check/format, mypy, new-test CI-tethering check).
- Sanity check on CPU: `CacheConfig().block_size == 64`, `CacheConfig(block_size=16).user_specified_block_size is True`.

Still missing: a 16-vs-64 throughput/memory benchmark on a real serving workload. This change is motivated by per-block bookkeeping overhead; reviewers with GPU access should run `vllm bench serve` (or equivalent) on a representative model before merging if quantitative gains are required.

## Details

Motivation: a 64-token block reduces per-block bookkeeping overhead (block tables, allocator metadata, prefix-cache hash operations per token) and matches the granularity many attention backends already prefer. `user_specified_block_size` keeps explicit user settings authoritative, and the per-platform `get_preferred_block_size` / `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` negotiation in `Platform.update_block_size_for_backend` is unchanged, so backends that cannot run with 64 still select a supported size automatically.

ROCm specifics: the native ROCm paged-attention C++ kernel only supports block sizes 16 and 32 (shared-memory/LDS constraints); every other multiple of 16 is routed to a Triton fallback (see `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_attn.py`). With the new default, `get_preferred_block_size(64)` returned 64 because 64 is nominally "supported", pushing every default-sized ROCm run onto that fallback — which is where build #96922's MI250 job hung. The new `RocmAttentionBackend.get_preferred_block_size` returns 16 unless the user passes an explicit `--block-size`, restoring pre-PR behavior on ROCm.

Tradeoffs:
- Prefix-cache hits land on 64-token boundaries instead of 16, so short shared prefixes (< 64 tokens) may no longer hit. Workloads with many short shared prefixes can pass `--block-size 16` to restore old behavior.
- Coarser blocks waste more KV memory per request on ragged tails (up to 63 tokens per request, vs 15).
- Third-party configs that hardcode chunk/block sizes as multiples of 16 (e.g. KV connector `kv_connector_extra_config["block_size"]`) now fail validation at startup against the 64-token default; the error message suggests the nearest valid value.
- This is a user-visible behavioral default change; docs use 16 only as an illustrative example and were not updated.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs/issues (`block size default`, `block_size in:title`) — no open PR changes the global default. Related but distinct open PRs (e.g. #62265, #60880) fix backend-specific preferred-size selection, which this change composes with.

title: [Perf][FlashAttention] FA4: pass no FP8 descale for a unit per-tensor scale
author: zyongye
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

For an FP8 KV cache whose per-tensor scales are 1.0, FlashAttention now passes FA4 no descale at all. Before, it passed broadcast descale views that FA4 copied into contiguous tensors, three copy kernels per attention layer and step.

This PR began as the squash of the whole MiniMax-M3.1-Flash tree. That squash has since been split into the PRs below; this PR now holds only the FA4 change.

## How #63232 was split

| Part of the original squash | Where it went | State |
|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-M3.1 model and DSpark draft model, with their kernels (MSA NVFP4 KV cache and indexer, MegaMoE staging, ROCm MXFP8 linears, ...) | #64111 | merged |
| ROCm: NVFP4 MoE re-quantization to MXFP4/MXFP8, and fused shared experts through online quantization | #64378 | merged |
| FA4: no FP8 descale for a unit per-tensor scale | this PR | open |
| NIXL P/D: re-sharding NVFP4 KV pages across heterogeneous TP (`AttentionSpec.kv_head_major_slots`) | #64475 | open |
| Scheduler: keep KV cache zeroing for mixed-precision `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups | #64472 | open |
| DSpark/DFlash draft step: Markov bias in the Gumbel kernel, wider DFlash padding, `is_padding` from the positions kernel, top-p fix | #64476 | open |
| Batch-sharded DSpark draft sampling | dropped from #64476; #63886 covers it | open (#63886) |
| SimpleCPUOffload: one host buffer per rank with HugeTLB pages | already open as #60130; the squash's extra ROCm change (SDMA copy-engine flag for batched copies) was pushed onto #60130 | open (#60130) |
| Scheduler draft-slot change | dropped: `main`'s `max_num_new_slots_for_drafting` already returns 0 for DFlash/DSpark | – |
| Sparse paged-attention KV block count fix (ROCm) | dropped: already on `main` via #63270 | – |

The full squash as it was before the split is a0ea941097 (on 5d35ce3934), in this PR's force-push history.

PRs that were opened against this branch (`minimax-m31-flash`) while it held the squash: #64359, #64273, #64264, #64206, #63528, #63491 and #62509. Their diffs against this branch now include the whole old squash (e.g. #64359 shows 193 files). The model (#64111) and the ROCm re-quantization (#64378) are on `main`, so they can retarget `main`.

## Claims

- **Unit scales:** when FA4 runs with a per-tensor Q/K/V scale of exactly 1.0, `FlashAttentionImpl` passes `None` for that descale.
  - FA4 reads a missing descale as 1.0, so the output is bit-identical.
  - FA4's `maybe_contiguous` no longer copies the three broadcast descale views per layer and step.
- **Other scales:** calibrated per-tensor scales and per-head scales keep their descale tensors. Other FlashAttention versions get the same broadcast descale as before; only the strides of its size-1 dims are made canonical, which changes metadata, not values.
- **(1, 1) descale views:** a view with one sequence and one KV head per rank now gets canonical strides. FA4 treats such a view as contiguous and skips its copy, and its layout check then rejects the zero stride.

## Validation

On GB300:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
```

148 passed, 9 skipped, 4 failed. The 4 failures are `test_sliding_window_encoder_backend_correctness` (embeddinggemma-300m). They fail the same way on `main` (2abde627d9) in this environment.

The new `test_flash_attn_fa4_unit_fp8_descale_is_exact` (Blackwell only) checks that:

- a unit scale gives no descale;
- FA4's output with no descale equals its output with the broadcast unit descale, bit for bit;
- a descale of 2 changes the output, so the comparison is not vacuous;
- calibrated and per-head scales keep their descale tensors.

Not covered:

- No end-to-end benchmark on this branch; the three copy kernels saved per layer and step were not timed.
- No accuracy eval: the output is bit-identical by the test above.
- The (1, 1) stride case is not in the new test, which uses 3 sequences and 4 KV heads.

## Details

- **Why the check is on the host:** the scales are fixed once the weights are loaded, so the `_scale_float` mirrors decide the case on the host with no GPU sync. A per-head scale's float mirror holds only its maximum, so the check also requires a single-element scale.
- **Compiled kernels:** FA4 compiles a separate kernel without descales, since descale presence is part of its compile key. A model with unit scales always takes that kernel.
- **Not a duplicate:** the open FA4 PRs change other things. #48156 warms up the paged FA4 kernels, #60372 adds SM90 FP8 MMA for Gemma-4, #63328 is sparse-MLA FP8 prefill, and #54705 covers Inkling per-tensor scales outside `flash_attn.py`. None of them changes how `FlashAttentionImpl` passes descales.

Credits: qizixi wrote the FA4 change and is a co-author in the commit. AI assistance (Claude) was used to split the original squash into the PRs above, to write the FA4 test and to draft this description. The submitter reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

title: [Compile] Make the compile cache device-neutral with compile_on_one_rank
author: kouroshHakha
body:
## Overview

Make the torch.compile cache device-neutral, so a cache built on one GPU can be reused on another. Since #45026 a worker's local rank no longer implies its device, so a cache built with `--device-ids 0` and reused with `--device-ids 1` crashes on startup. This enables torch 2.14's `compile_on_one_rank` mode via a new `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` (default on for torch >= 2.14 on CUDA/ROCm and XPU).

## Claims

- Fixes `CUDA driver error: invalid argument` during the first warm-up forward when a compile cache built on one device is reused on another (`--device-ids`).
- The cache is reused across device indices with no recompile.
- `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` is part of the compile cache key: caches built with the mode off are never loaded with it on, and vice versa.
- No throughput or output change (TP=1 and TP=2, greedy outputs identical).

## Validation

All runs: Qwen3-0.6B, 2x H100, torch 2.14.0, `vllm serve --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5`, one fresh `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` shared by the runs of each table.

**Reproducer.** Run A builds the cache, then B and C reuse it:

| Run | Device in-process | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| A `--device-ids 0` | cuda:0 | Up, compiles, writes the cache | Up, compiles, writes the cache |
| B `--device-ids 1` | cuda:1 | **Crash**: loads A's AOT cache, `CUDA driver error: invalid argument` | **Up**: loads A's AOT cache, no recompile |
| C `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` (control) | cuda:0 | Up | Up |

C runs on the same physical GPU as B and reuses the same cache, but in-process it is `cuda:0`, so the device index alone decides the failure.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --device-ids 0 --port 8000   # A: wait until healthy, then stop
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --device-ids 1 --port 8000   # B: crashes before this PR
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8000  # C: control
```
</details>

**What changes in the cached code.** Counts over the generated Inductor modules in the cache:

| | Literal device index (`_DeviceGuard(0)`, `get_raw_stream(0)`, `DeviceProperties(..., index=0`) | Runtime expression (`torch.cuda.current_device()`, `index=None`) |
|---|---|---|
| Mode off | 76 | 0 |
| Mode on | 0 | 62 |

**Cache-key isolation.** Starting with `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK=0` on a cache root built with the mode on recompiles instead of loading it.

**TP=2.** Cold and warm start with the mode on and off: warm starts load both ranks' caches with no recompile, and there are no CUDA errors.

**Outputs.** Greedy completions (32 tokens, 3 prompts) are identical with the mode on and off, at TP=1 and TP=2.

**Throughput.** `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 300 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 0`, one run per cell:

| | Output tok/s (off → on) | Mean TPOT ms (off → on) | Mean TTFT ms (off → on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP=1 | 12,283 → 12,459 | 3.88 → 3.80 | 134.6 → 137.4 |
| TP=2 | 13,372 → 13,653 | 3.36 → 3.34 | 149.3 → 140.5 |

The differences are within run-to-run variation.

**Tests.** `tests/compile/test_compile_on_one_rank.py`: the default and its gates, the flag being a compile cache factor that changes the hash, `env_override` applying it to torch, and (on CUDA) that Inductor's generated code bakes in the device index with the mode off and resolves it at run time with it on. It runs in the existing `find compile/ -maxdepth 1 -name 'test_*.py'` Buildkite step.

## Details

**Root cause.** The AOT compile cache lives under `torch_aot_compile/<hash>/rank_{rank}_{dp_rank}`, where the hash covers the vLLM config and env factors. Neither includes the device. That was safe while rank r always ran on `cuda:r`. Since #45026, `--device-ids` maps logical ranks to physical devices without narrowing `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, so a rank can run on any device index. Inductor bakes the compile-time device in two places:

1. **The generated wrapper code:** `torch.cuda._DeviceGuard(0)`, `torch.cuda.set_device(0)`, `get_raw_stream(0)`.
2. **Each Triton kernel's load device:** statically launched kernels are loaded into the device recorded at compile time.

Reusing the cache on `cuda:1` launches kernels against `cuda:0`'s stream (`invalid argument`). In an experiment on torch 2.13, rewriting only the wrapper code still failed (`invalid resource handle`), because the kernels are loaded into `cuda:0`'s context. Both have to be device-relative.

**Fix.** torch 2.14's `torch.compiler.config.compile_on_one_rank` makes Inductor emit `torch.cuda.current_device()` in the wrapper and compile kernels with `DeviceProperties(index=None)`. That covers both places, so no Inductor patching is needed in vLLM. Torch also includes the mode in Inductor's own cache key. vLLM's AOT cache key needs it as well, which a registered vLLM env var provides through `envs.compile_factors()`. `env_override` sets torch's config from `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` in every vLLM process, so an outside `TORCH_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` cannot make the compiled code disagree with the cache key.

**Relation to #38962 / #53312.** #38962 fixed the same crash by adding the device index to the cache path; it was reverted in #53304 for a CPU regression, and #53312 re-lands it. That approach stops the crash but gives each device index its own cache, so replicas on different GPUs recompile instead of sharing one. This PR keeps a single cache that works on any device index, and its default is off on CPU. The two can coexist; with this PR, device-keyed paths are no longer needed for correctness.

**Limitations.**
- On torch < 2.14 the mode does not exist, so the default stays off and the bug remains. Fixing it there would need patches to Inductor's codegen and its static Triton launcher.
- The default is off on platforms other than CUDA/ROCm and XPU, because Inductor raises for backends without `current_device_idx_expr()`.
- Existing caches recompile once after upgrading, because the cache key changes.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve stored event prefix order
author: Alex-ai-future
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve offload store key order so self-describing `BlockStored` events remain
parent-before-child within a transfer job. This prevents KV-aware routers from
dropping child blocks when a parent mapping has not been indexed yet.

## Claims

- Keep `TransferJobStatus.keys` in prefix order and deduplicate keys while
  retaining their first occurrence.
- Do not change the KV-event wire format or guarantee ordering across separate
  secondary-tier jobs, tiers, or promotion events; router-side pending/replay
  still covers those cases.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py -q`:
  51 passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q`
  with the affected cases selected: 100 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed-files>`: passed.
- Model evaluation is not applicable because this changes event ordering only.

## Details

The missing prefix order resulted from three assumptions rather than a decision
that order was unnecessary:

- [`#39186`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39186) introduced
  `TransferJobStatus.keys` as set-backed job bookkeeping before offload events
  existed.
- [`#43468`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43468) made stored events
  self-describing and explicitly treated key order as irrelevant because each
  payload contains its parent hash. The order-independent test and
  “key order is free” comment codified that assumption.
- A consumer test in
  [`#52103`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52103#issuecomment-6251409146)
  later showed that llm-d still needs the parent event indexed first. The author
  confirmed the gap in
  [this reply](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52103#issuecomment-6255856451).

`prepare_store()` returns keys in prefix order, but the scheduler stored them in
a set. This can emit a child first even when transfer completion is FIFO. The
scheduler now preserves job order without removing set-style deduplication.

Secondary tiers are intentionally outside the ordering guarantee. FS/OBJ jobs
complete asynchronously and may become distinct raw events; tier aggregation
emits primary and secondary events by tier, not by parent topology. Therefore
this change fixes intra-job ordering but does not reorder across secondary jobs,
tiers, or promotions. Those cases remain a consumer concern.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR directly fixes this ordering path. #63129
addresses reused-key metadata lifecycle, and #52103 refactors event provenance
and removals while still retaining set-backed job keys.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and tests. The human
submitter must review every changed line and rerun the validation above.

title: [ROCm][Recipe] MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: MI355X PD, DBO / SP prefill, Quark MXFP4, mono decode
author: benenzhu
body:
## Overview

AMD MI355X additions to the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash recipe (`recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml` only). No other open PR changes this recipe.

## Claims

1. **PD on MI355X**: `pd_cluster` renders the guide's 1P1D. One TP4 engine per role; BLHNC KV layout and NIXL with 4 threads; the prefill node drops `indexer_decode_cp` and offloads KV to host memory in 1 GiB HugeTLB pages (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`).
2. **TP4 on MI355X** for `single_node_tp` (Hopper keeps the FP8 variant's TP8).
3. **DBO / SP prefill** (opt-in feature, MI355X single node): SP + DBO, DBO, or SP. Guide section with the flags; one 32K-token prefill takes 1035 ms plain, 655 ms with DBO, 484 ms with SP + DBO (MXFP8 MoE).
4. **MXFP4 (Quark) variant**: `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, MXFP4 W4A4 experts on the AITER MoE (`--moe-backend aiter`, no shared-expert fusion). `--quantization-config.moe mxfp8` moves into the default variant, since only that checkpoint stores NVFP4 experts.
5. **Mono decode** (opt-in feature, MI355X + Quark only): a decode step of up to 16 tokens runs each layer as one kernel. Needs FP8 KV and indexer caches and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs. On the released image (aiter 0.1.26) it also needs #63270, the backport of #61889, to start.
6. **Fixes**: one `fp8` variant, limited to Hopper (the merge of `main` had duplicated the key; on MI355X and Blackwell it rendered NVFP4 caches). VRAM minimums per GPU: the NVFP4 variant shows 285 GB, and MI355X gets 533 GB after the MXFP8 re-quantization.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes` passes on vllm-project/recipes `main`. Rendered commands were checked for the default, Quark, and FP8 variants on MI355X, B300, and H200, with and without the new features.
- Rendered commands served on MI355X TP4 with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash`, DSpark 3, AIME26 (16 epochs, max_tokens 98304, thinking on) and MMMU-Pro (all, 3460):

  | command | AIME26 | MMMU-Pro |
  |---|---|---|
  | default (MXFP8 MoE) | 0.9351 x6 ¹ | 0.7676 x1 |
  | MXFP4 (Quark) | 0.9368 x6 | 0.7763 x1 |
  | MXFP4 (Quark) + mono decode, concurrency 4 | 0.9417 x8 | – |

  ¹ Same image, KV/indexer/MoE settings and DSpark 3, but served by our eval script (block verification), not the rendered command.

## Details

- The DBO / SP modes are offered on the default variant only (SP and SP + DBO were measured on the MXFP8 MoE); the Quark variant gets DBO.
- The recipe schema needs a mode per variant, so `mono_decode` carries an empty mode for the other variants: enabling it there changes nothing.
- The Quark MMMU run used `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": 0}'`. With video inputs on, one Quark server ran out of memory in the vision encoder at MMMU concurrency 256 (`--gpu-memory-utilization` 0.92).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the recipe changes and run the validation above; I reviewed the changes.

title: [Spec Decode] Support trace replay with speculative decoding
author: aoshen02
body:
## Overview

Allow `trace_decode_token_ids` (MRv2 trace replay) together with speculative decoding. A draft is accepted only if it equals the trace token at its position, and the verified tokens are replaced by the trace, so the replay emits the trace and scores it on the decode path while skipping target forward passes for drafts that match.

## Claims

- Trace replay works with ngram, EAGLE3 and MTP speculators; emitted token ids equal the trace for every request.
- With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the returned raw logprobs (trace token and top-5) are bitwise equal to trace replay without spec decode.
- Replay speedup with a good drafter: 1.47x–2.03x (EAGLE3, Qwen3-8B), 1.64x–1.88x (MTP, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8).

## Validation

### Experiments

GB300, one GPU per run, nightly `8e2beaa3bf` with this patch overlaid (the three source files), MRv2. 64 traces per model, up to 512 tokens, 3/4 sampled at temperature 1.0 with a seed and 1/4 greedy, generated by the target model without spec decode. Each replay uses `trace_decode_token_ids=trace, max_tokens=len(trace), logprobs=5`. Arms: A = replay without spec, A2 = A with reversed request order (numerical floor), B = replay with spec (k=3), `*1` = batch size 1 on 16 traces, `*bi` = `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. All arms returned every request with ids equal to the trace and a logprob entry per token.

| model / speculator | comparison | speedup | acceptance | trace-token logprob bitwise equal | top-5 logprobs bitwise equal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B / EAGLE3 (RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3) | A vs A2 (floor) | - | - | 86.0% | 82.4% |
| | A vs B | 1.47x | 46% | 39.4% | 24.8% |
| | A1 vs B1 | 2.03x | 47% | 100% | 100% |
| | Abi vs Bbi | 1.82x | 46% | 100% | 100% |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 / MTP | A vs A2 (floor) | - | - | 10.7% | 5.6% |
| | A vs B | 1.64x | 66% | 9.3% | 4.4% |
| | A1 vs B1 | 1.88x | 66% | 9.4% | 4.6% |
| Qwen3-0.6B / ngram | A vs A2 (floor) | - | - | 99.7% | 99.7% |
| | A vs B | 0.82x | 3.5% | 97.7% | 97.7% |
| | A1 vs B1 | 0.91x | 3.7% | 100% | 100% |
| | Abi vs Bbi | 1.05x | 3.5% | 100% | 100% |

Without batch invariance, the spec arm changes batch shapes, so logprobs differ at the same order as reordering requests. With batch invariance they are bitwise equal. The FP8 MoE model is not batch invariant even run-to-run, so for MTP the evidence is exact token match plus differences at the reorder floor. ngram accepts few drafts on these chat traces and is slower; that is a drafter-quality effect.

Sampling parameters and off-distribution traces (Qwen3-8B / EAGLE3, replay with `temperature=0.5, top_p=0.95`, `logprobs_mode=processed_logprobs`; "random" traces replace every trace token with a uniformly random id, so drafts almost never match):

| traces | comparison | speedup | acceptance | trace-token logprob bitwise equal | top-5 ids equal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| model-generated | Abi vs Bbi | 2.14x | 46% | 99.99% | 98.97% |
| model-generated | A vs B | 2.32x | 46% | 92.1% | 97.1% |
| random | Abi vs Bbi | 0.89x | 0% | 99.36% | 99.99% |
| random | A vs B | 0.68x | 0% | 99.19% | 82.9% |

Emitted ids equal the trace in every arm. Raw logits are bitwise equal under batch invariance (table above), so the remaining processed-logprob differences come from top-p masking: `apply_top_k_top_p_triton` uses the split top-p pipeline for at most 64 rows (`_SPLIT_MAX_BATCH`) and the monolithic kernel above that, and the two can place the nucleus boundary differently. Verification expands each request to k+1 rows, so the two arms land on different paths. This is an existing batch-invariance gap of top-p masking (non-spec decoding hits it too when the batch crosses 64 rows), not specific to trace replay.

### Tests

Old = image vLLM, new = image vLLM with the patched files, same test tree.

| test | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_trace_replay.py` (new `TestApplyTraceToVerified`) | collection error (missing function) | pass |
| `tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay_params.py` | 1 failed (spec decode rejected) | pass |
| `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_trace_replay_with_spec_decode` | fail (spec decode rejected) | pass |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_*.py`, `tests/v1/engine/test_input_processor_trace_replay.py` | 1122 passed, 18 failed (the 16 below plus the 2 changed trace replay params tests) | 1140 passed, 16 failed, all also failing on old |

The 16 failures shared by old and new are environment or baseline failures unrelated to this change: `test_acceptance_length.py::test_eagle3_acceptance_length` (11 cases), `test_gpu_model_runner.py` mamba cases (2), `test_gpu_pcp_manager.py::test_parallel_config_manages_decode_sharding` (3). No test fails only on new.

## Details

`RejectionSampler._verify` runs the usual rejection sampling, then for requests with a trace `TraceReplayState.apply_trace_to_verified` rewrites the verified tokens: starting from the current trace step, it writes trace tokens while each draft equals the trace token at its position, stopping at the first mismatch, at the bonus position, or at the end of the trace, and sets `num_sampled` accordingly. Logprobs, rejection counts, the committed tokens and the drafter's next-step inputs all read the rewritten `sampled`/`num_sampled`, so no other path changes. The hook is a single kernel launch per verify step with no host synchronization, and requests without a trace return immediately in the kernel.

Penalties stay consistent with non-spec replay: row i of the verify step folds in drafts 0..i-1, and a row is emitted only if all of those drafts matched the trace, so the history of every emitted row is the trace prefix.

Limitations:
- Bitwise equality with non-spec replay requires batch invariance, and for processed logprobs under top-k/top-p it is limited by the top-p masking path switch described above.
- Not covered by tests or experiments: preemption/resume mid-trace, prefix caching, TP/DP, non-neutral penalties. Code reading shows the trace step comes from `total_len - prompt_len`, which these paths keep consistent.

title: [ROCm][Build][5/5] Speed up ROCm build: instantiate the fused MUSE-Spark op per head size
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

**Splits the fused MUSE-Spark op on one item - `head_dim` (64/128/256), the whole op having landed in #62132 five days ago.**

`csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` holds the whole fused MUSE-Spark qknorm/rope/kv-insert op: its host entry dispatches `head_dim` x `heads_per_group` x rope type, so 18 kernel instantiations land in a single translation unit. On a 9-arch build that unit is one of the longest compiles of the build - 478 s, behind only the int4 skinny GEMM (1232 s).

This PR instantiates one unit per `head_dim` (64/128/256): the kernels move into an include-only `fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cuh` whose entry is a template over `HEAD_DIM`, each unit is two lines (`#include` + `VLLM_MUSE_SPARK_ENTRY(, hd)`), and `fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_api.cu` keeps the public symbol and dispatches on `head_dim`, `extern template` keeping the device code in the three units.

Same kernels, same dispatch rules, same numerics: the only change is which translation unit generates which `head_dim`, plus the runtime forward in the API unit. At 1 arch the file is not the build's tail, so the single-arch wall is unchanged.

**This one only pays off once the int4 unit is split** (#63364): while that 1232 s unit exists it is the tail regardless of what this op costs, so on `main` alone this PR is expected to be neutral. The 9-arch numbers below are therefore measured on top of the int4 split.

The single-arch rows are `pip install -e .` on MI350 (gfx950); the 9-arch row is the `setup.py bdist_wheel` described under *Validation*. All cold builds:

| build | `main` | this PR | All 5 PRs (#62921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_JOBS=16`, gfx950 only | 107 s | 108 s | 87 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, gfx950 only | 85 s | 87 s | 50 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, 9 archs | 1263 s | 1241 s | 472 s |

## Claims

- Removes the second-longest compile of the 9-arch build (478 s, one unit) by instantiating one unit per `head_dim`: 3 units of the same total device code.
- Only pays off once the int4 unit is split; on `main` alone the 1232 s int4 unit stays the tail, so this PR is measured on top of #63364.
- Single-arch is unchanged within noise (107 -> 108 s at 16 jobs, 85 -> 87 s at 64).
- The op is not re-instantiated or reduced: each lane emits its `head_dim` arm's 18 configurations (2 dtypes x 3 heads_per_group x 2 rope types) exactly as before.
- One entry template with one explicit instantiation per `head_dim`, i.e. three distinct symbols; specialising a shared body by macro instead made the linker keep one copy and fail `head_dim` 128/256 at runtime.

### Why five PRs

The two builds are bound by different things, so no single change moves both.

**Why the three single-arch PRs are all needed.** At 1 arch (`gfx950`, `MAX_JOBS=64`, `main` = 85 s) three groups take turns setting the wall, in this order:

1. topk softplus-sqrt (#62717) - 74.5 s, a single unit
2. paged attention (#62716) - 71.6 s, the slowest of 12 units
3. other skinny GEMMs (#62718) - 40.9 s, a single unit

#62717 takes (1) to 7.4 s, #62716 takes (2) to 31.1 s and #62718 stops (3) from becoming the next tail; with all three the tail moves to `selective_scan_fwd` (37.7 s) and the build goes from 85 s to 49 s. Drop any one of them and a ~70 s unit is back at the top, so the single-arch win needs all three.

**Why that is not enough at 9 archs.** A 9-arch build multiplies every unit's time by ~9, and the tail becomes two files that none of the first three touch: `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` at 1232 s and `csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` at 478 s. All three merged take the 9-arch build from 1263 s to only 1253 s. #63364 splits the first (its tail drops to 448 s) and #63365 the second (to 171 s), which is what reaches 472 s.

The `skinny_gemms_int4.cu` tail is invisible in a `gfx950` build because that file **only emits its kernels for RDNA (that is part of the 9-arch build)**:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L17-L19
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L568-L579

`csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` fails differently: it has no arch guard, so a `gfx950` build compiles it for real - it is just 25 s there against 478 s across nine archs, which is why a single-arch profile ranks it as irrelevant (#63365).

| slowest unit per group, 1 arch (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| topk softplus-sqrt | 74.5 s | 7.4 s |
| paged attention | 71.6 s | 31.1 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | 40.9 s | 31.6 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 36.5 s | 37.7 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 25.0 s | 10.9 s |
| int4 skinny GEMM | 19.4 s | 17.5 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **76 s / 15.8x** | **39 s / 30.2x** |

| slowest unit per group, 9 archs (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| int4 skinny GEMM | 1232 s | 448 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 478 s | 171 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 288 s | 296 s |
| paged attention | 284 s | 286 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | not recorded | 247 s |
| topk softplus-sqrt | not recorded | 99 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **1234 s / 8.7x** | **472 s / 25x** |

## Validation

### Single arch build

```bash
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx950" VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=N \
  pip install --no-cache-dir -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation
```

| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | 87 s (−19 %) | 50 s (−41 %) |

### 9 archs build

The multi-arch wheel build with the 9 release archs of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, mold as the linker and sccache disabled, from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so`, `build/` and `dist/` removed first):

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" \
  PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151" \
  VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=64 \
  python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist

| build | wall time | wheel |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`f4edf9f0f0`) | **1263 s** | **266 MB** |
| #62716 paged attention 089bbaf68a | 1261 s | 275 MB |

Per-unit detail at this configuration:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| MUSE-Spark unit | 478 s, one unit | 3 units of the same total device code |
| `fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_api.cu` | - | 27 lines, no device code |

Environment, one host: AMD EPYC 9575F (64 cores / 256 threads), 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (251 GiB each), ROCm 10.0, `torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, clang 23, mold.

Structure check on the 9-arch objects: the API unit emits 0 device kernel symbols and each of the three lane units 240 - i.e. each unit instantiates only its own `head_dim`.

#### Linked artifact sizes at 9 archs

Context for these: [#62983](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62983) had to revert #62475 because the 9-arch `_rocm_C.abi3.so` outgrew the 2 GiB reach of the 32-bit PC-relative relocations in `crtbegin`'s `.text` (plain `main` was already at 2011.5 MiB, and the 12-way split added ~119 MiB of duplicated GPU debug info, overflowing at 2104 MiB). `--offload-compress`, which landed with the reland (#63105), shrinks the fatbin ~20x and is what keeps us away from that wall.

| linked artifact (9 archs) | `main` | this PR | All 5 PRs (#62921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` | TBD | **125.9 MB** | **129.3 MB** |
| `_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` | TBD | **499.8 MB** | **499.8 MB** |
| `_moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` | TBD | **235.2 MB** | **239.8 MB** |
| `_C.abi3.so` | TBD | **30.7 MB** | **30.0 MB** |
| `.o` files under `CMakeFiles/` | TBD | **935 MB** | **932 MB** |

The split does not add device code - it moves the same `head_dim` arm's kernels into different units - so the 9-arch `_rocm_C` stays where `main` puts it, and across the five PRs the wheel is about the same size (266 -> 270 MB).

### Runtime check

The existing kernel test file covers `head_dim` 64/128/256 through the public entry, i.e. through the new forward, and was run on both builds of `bdc0f947` (each a fresh `MAX_JOBS=64 pip install -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation`; the later `main` merge does not touch these files):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py
```

```
29 passed, 2 skipped in 15.74s      # CUDA, 8x H100, cu134 nightly
26 passed, 5 deselected in 10.01s   # ROCm, MI350X/gfx950, -k "not attention_metadata"
```

The 2 CUDA skips are ROCm-only cases (backend gate, compile boundary). The 5 ROCm deselects are `test_query_fusion_respects_attention_metadata`, which import `flashinfer` and were absent from that container only; they are among the 29 that pass on CUDA. The split builds and runs on both paths, and each `head_dim` gets its own `..._typed<hd>` instantiation.

## Details

The kernel is untouched: the `__global__` template and the `DISPATCH_ARGS`/`DISPATCH_HPG`/`DISPATCH_ROPE_T` tower are unchanged. What changed is how the `head_dim` arm is selected - `HEAD_DIM` is a template parameter of `launchFusedMuseSpark`, so the runtime `switch (head_dim)` is a single `DISPATCH_ROPE_T(HEAD_DIM)` and each unit's symbols carry their own head_dim - plus the API unit dispatching to `..._typed<64/128/256>`. A `head_dim` outside 64/128/256 still reports "unsupported head_dim".

**How the file got this big.** It has no growth history: #62132 landed the whole op five days ago, in one TU, as 1 `__global__` with 8 templates and `head_dim` {64,128,256} x `heads_per_group` {1,2,4} x rope type {fp32, scalar_t} - 18 configurations per dtype pair, plus the fp8-output arms. Nothing has been added to it since.

So its 478 s at 9 archs is the cost of that configuration set on day one, not of accretion; this PR splits it into 3 units.

### Left to do

- [ ] Cross-check with #63364: this branch is based on `main`, so its 9-arch numbers are taken with the int4 split merged in; on `main` alone the change is neutral (1241 s vs 1263 s).
- [x] Run `tests/kernels/test_fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py` on this revision (it covers head_dim 64/128/256 through the public entry, i.e. through the new forward). Done, see *Runtime check*.

title: [Bugfix][NVFP4] Fix NaN logits and garbage output from uninitialized fused act+quant scales
author: nv-nikitaj
body:
## Overview

Make the fused `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` kernel initialize the padded entries of the swizzled NVFP4 block-scale buffer, as the unfused `scaled_fp4_quant` kernel already does. Fixes a regression from #53568, which switched the scale allocator to `torch.empty` (previously `torch.zeros`, restored in #45739).

## Claims

- Fixes NaN logits and garbage output (`other other other ...`) on NVFP4 checkpoints, e.g. `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4`.
- Fixes HTTP 400 `Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan` on `/v1/chat/completions` with `logprobs`.
- Covers both users of the kernel (the `ActivationQuantFusionPass` and the manual fusion in `fused_act_quant.py`) with no allocator memset.

## Validation

Setup: 8x RTX PRO 4500 (sm120), TP=8, `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4`, FlashInfer-Cutlass NVFP4 linear backend, `fuse_act_quant: True`, built from source with CUDA 13.2.

Repro:

```bash
# 1. Serve (TP=8)
vllm serve nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --served-model-name nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5 --port 8000

# 2. Once the server is up, send 100 chat+logprobs and 100 completions requests
NAME=nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5
echo -n "chat:  "; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /tmp/r_chat_$i.json -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"model\":\"$NAME\",\"logprobs\":true,\"top_logprobs\":1,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are a helpful assistant.\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hello!\"}],\"max_tokens\":100}"; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '; echo
echo -n "compl: "; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /tmp/r_compl_$i.json -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"model\":\"$NAME\",\"prompt\":\"What is the test plan?\",\"logprobs\":2,\"max_tokens\":50,\"temperature\":0}"; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '; echo
echo "nan-errors: $(grep -l 'Out of range float' /tmp/r_*.json | wc -l)"
```

Unit tests: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`, 20 passed (12 existing, 8 new).

## Details

The fused `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` kernel only wrote valid rows of the swizzled block-scale buffer, but the NVFP4 GEMM reads the padded entries, so since #53568 switched the allocator to `torch.empty` it consumed stale memory as scales and produced NaN logits. This PR makes the kernel zero the padded scale rows and columns itself (as `scaled_fp4_quant` does) and keeps the allocators as `torch.empty`, so there is no extra memset.

---

title: [Core][CUDA Graph] Separate prefill (token) and decode (request) CUDA graph capture sizes
author: Pb314314
body:
## 1. Why this change A CUDA graph's batch size means different things for two kinds of step: - A prefill or mixed batch is sized by its **tokens**. - A uniform decode batch, where every request has the same query length `q = 1 + K`, is sized by its **requests** and `q`. On main, model runner V2 captures both from one token list (`cudagraph_capture_sizes`, capped at 1024 tokens on GB200). A decode graph must be a list entry divisible by `q`, so the larger K is, the fewer decode requests the graphs cover, and every mixed batch above 1024 tokens runs eagerly. Example: with the 1024-token cap and K = 7 (`q = 8`), decode graphs cover at most 128 requests. Uniform decode batches above 128 requests exceed main's FULL coverage. This is the "separate prefill/decode graph sizes" item of the Q4 roadmap (#61024). ## 2. What this PR changes This PR adds five configuration fields: a cap and a capture-size list for each kind of graph, plus a token budget for uniform decode graphs. Prefill coverage is configured in tokens; uniform decode coverage is configured in requests. | field | unit | controls | default on SM100 (GB200, B200) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens` | tokens | Maximum token count for prefill, mixed, and fallback decode PIECEWISE graphs | `min(8192, max_num_batched_tokens)` | | `prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes` | tokens | Token counts at which those graphs are captured | Default prefill grid up to the cap: 54 sizes at 8192 tokens | | `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests` | requests | Request-count cap for uniform decode FULL graphs, before applying the token budget | `max_num_seqs` | | `decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes` | requests | Request-count capture sizes, converted by each runner into `n × q` tokens | Default decode grid up to the cap: 64 sizes at 1024 requests, before applying the token budget | | `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens` | tokens | Maximum token count of each uniform decode graph | 8192 | For either kind, setting only a cap generates the default grid up to that cap. An explicit list selects the capture sizes; if a cap is also supplied, the list must fit within it. An empty list disables that kind. The decode request grid is the starting point for capture planning. Each runner uses its own query length `q` and captures only shapes that fit its execution limits and token budget. At the default 1024-request cap, the target captures 64 decode sizes through 1024 requests for K ≤ 7, or 48 sizes through 512 requests for K = 15. Wider target decode batches try the prefill token graphs before falling back to eager execution. The token budget also bounds adaptive-verification graphs. It does not bound one-token draft decodes, which reach `max_num_seqs` whatever the decode caps are (only `[]` turns them off). On other GPUs, the prefill and target decode defaults stay as on main. **How the defaults were chosen.** Defaults trade padding and coverage against memory/startup cost; current padding measurements are in appendix A. The decode budget limits wide graphs (why 8192: section 5.1); explicit lists/caps support workload- and parallelism-specific tuning. The default configuration and tuned performance ceiling are separate evaluation targets.
Grids, other GPUs and edge rules Defaults on other GPUs: the prefill cap is the platform's `max_cudagraph_capture_size` (512 on H100 / H200) and the prefill sizes are main's list; the decode cap is main's reach, 512 / (1 + K) requests, with main's request counts; there is no decode token budget. | what you set for a kind | graphs captured for that kind | | --- | --- | | nothing | the default grid up to the default cap | | a cap only | the default grid up to that cap | | a list only | exactly those sizes | | both | the list; a size above the cap is an error | | `[]` | none | - **Grids.** - **Prefill** / mixed (tokens): 1, 2, 4, every 8 up to 64, four sizes per doubling up to 1024 (…, 512, 640, 768, 896, 1024), then multiples of 256 through 7680, followed by 8192 — **54 capture sizes** at the default cap. Between 64 and 1024 tokens, a mixed batch pads by at most 25%, reducing padding-induced crossings of a model's own shape threshold (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's decoder-replay trim at 768 tokens; DEP section). - **Decode (requests):** every count from 1–6; then 8–16 in steps of 2, 20–48 in steps of 4, 56–128 in steps of 8, 144–352 in steps of 16, and 384–1024 in steps of 32. **64 capture sizes before applying the decode-token budget**; the default 8192-token budget keeps all of them for K ≤ 7 and limits target K=15 to **512 requests / 48 sizes**. - **Adaptive verification (tokens):** 1, 2, 4, 8; then four additional sizes per doubling through 1024—for example, 10, 12, 14, 16, followed by 20, 24, 28, 32. Above 1024, use steps of 128 through 4096, then steps of 256. The cap is `min(decode request cap × (K + 1), max_num_batched_tokens, max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens)`; **K=5 with a 1024-request cap gives 64 sizes through 6144 tokens**. Adaptive verification picks its verify width from the captured sizes, so this grid is finer than the prefill grid. - Sizes above `max_num_batched_tokens` (prefill) or `max_num_seqs` (decode) are dropped with a warning. `[]` for both kinds turns decoder CUDA graphs off. Under `cudagraph_mode` FULL or PIECEWISE (no separate decode routine) every batch uses the prefill sizes; under FULL_DECODE_ONLY the prefill sizes are not captured and do not count toward the recorded maximum. - Setting one kind leaves the other kind's graphs unchanged. Exception: DSpark, DFlash, DFlash2 and LiLiCorr are also capped by the resolved `max_cudagraph_capture_size` divided by their `q`. That value is the largest token count over the language-model/drafter graphs: prefill sizes, target decode `n · q`, one-token draft decodes and adaptive-verification sizes. At the SM100 defaults with K ≤ 7 it is the 8192-token prefill cap. Off SM100 with an EAGLE-family drafter it is the one-token draft decode reach (`max_num_seqs`, 1024), above the 512-token prefill cap. - `cudagraph_capture_sizes` and `max_cudagraph_capture_size` are deprecated on model runner V2. Set alone, they seed both kinds as on main, with a warning; combined with the new fields, they raise. Adaptive verification, DSpark and one-token draft decodes do not reproduce main's graphs under them. Model runner V1 is unchanged and rejects the new fields. ```bash # Before: one cap for both kinds, in tokens. --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 1024}' # After: delete it to take the defaults, or set each kind in its own unit. --compilation-config '{"max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens": 8192, "max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests": 256}' # Prefill instance of a disaggregated deployment: no decode graphs. Adaptive verification # needs decode graphs and is rejected with this; a prefill instance never verifies, so disable it there. --compilation-config '{"decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes": []}' # Decode instance of a disaggregated deployment: FULL decode (and adaptive verification) only, no PIECEWISE graphs. --compilation-config '{"prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes": []}' ```
## 3. Which graphs run ```mermaid flowchart TD C["Resolved config
prefill grid (tokens) · decode grid (requests) · decode budget (tokens)"] C --> T["Target
PIECEWISE: prefill / mixed, by tokens
FULL uniform decode: q = 1 + K, by requests, up to the decode budget
wider decodes: PIECEWISE, or eager without a prefill grid"] T -->|"adaptive verification on"| V["FULL varlen decode, by tokens
replaces the target's uniform decode graphs"] C --> E["EAGLE / EAGLE3 / single-module MTP"] E --> E0["Draft step 0: copies of the target's shapes
PIECEWISE + FULL at q = 1 + K"] E --> E1["Draft steps 1 … K − 1: FULL, q = 1
default request grid through max_num_seqs"] C --> B["DSpark (q = K) · DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr (q = K + 1)
FULL, one graph per draft round"] C --> M["Multi-module MTP (q = 1 + K, the target's layout)
after a decode step: 1 FULL graph with all K modules, by requests
after a prefill / mixed step: K PIECEWISE runs, by tokens"] ``` Each runner owns its graphs and picks among them by its own inputs. A decode step wider than the decode budget falls back to the PIECEWISE prefill graphs; on an instance with an empty prefill grid, such as a disaggregated decode instance, it runs eagerly. The list/cap labels above refer to the exact fields in section 2; a graph mode or attention backend can restrict which paths are available. **YOCO decoder replay: rule unchanged.** Its breakable PIECEWISE grid is still derived from `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, which now follows the prefill cap: 32 sizes up to 8192 tokens (main: 8 up to 1024; memory in section 5). Replays above the grid run eagerly. Forcing every replay eager (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DSpark K5 + AV, GSM8K twice per launch) kept GSM8K answer agreement with the graph runs at the graph-vs-graph level (TP4 / 256K 98.6–99.1% vs 99.0%, DEP4 / 64K 99.0–99.4% vs 99.2%); the debug switch had no counter, so it does not prove that every replay ran eagerly. [Implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cff6224872ad24b10c224bc4186778dcd90a1b21/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py#L26). **DEP applies these grids to per-rank execution batches.** Ranks synchronize execution mode and padding before the final dispatch; API concurrency is not a per-rank capture size. Dynamic SD is currently disabled for DP > 1; AV is a separate setting. [DP dispatch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cff6224872ad24b10c224bc4186778dcd90a1b21/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/dp_utils.py#L43). Every step picks the smallest captured graph that holds it; a step no graph holds runs eagerly. | step | graph | sizes from | decode budget | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | target prefill / mixed batch | PIECEWISE, by tokens | prefill grid | – | | target uniform decode | FULL at `q = 1 + K`, by requests | decode grid; wider decodes run PIECEWISE (eagerly with an empty prefill grid) | yes, up to budget / `q` requests | | target verification with adaptive verification (DSpark, DFlash) | FULL varlen: query lengths 1 … 1 + K in one batch, by tokens | adaptive-verification token grid | yes, up to the budget in tokens | | EAGLE, EAGLE3, single-module MTP: draft step 0 | the target's shape: a PIECEWISE copy for a mixed batch, a FULL copy at the target's `q = 1 + K` for a uniform decode (under dynamic SD, one `q = 1 + k` per tier) | the target's prefill and decode grids | yes, for the FULL copies | | same drafters, draft steps 1 … K − 1 | FULL at `q = 1`, by requests | default request grid through `max_num_seqs`; an empty decode list disables this path | no | | DSpark (`q = K`); DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr (`q = K + 1`) | FULL, one graph per draft round | decode grid, also capped at `max_cudagraph_capture_size` / `q` | yes, up to budget / `q` (all 1024 requests for DSpark K = 7) | | multi-module MTP: draft round after a uniform-decode target step | **one** FULL graph at the target's `q = 1 + K` holding all K module forwards and samplings | the target's decode grid (Inkling K=8: 61 graphs up to 910 requests; main 76 up to 112); wider decodes run as in the next row | yes | | multi-module MTP: draft round after a prefill / mixed target step | **K** breakable PIECEWISE runs, one per module (breakable models, e.g. Inkling, Step5, Kimi-K3); other models run the K modules eagerly | prefill grid (Inkling: 54 sizes up to 8192; main 91 up to 1024) | – | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash YOCO decoder replay | breakable PIECEWISE, by replay tokens (unchanged) | rule unchanged; bound now 8192 (32 sizes; main 8 up to 1024) | no | | n-gram, draft model | none (eager) | – | – | **The rule for `q`:** a FULL decode graph is captured at the query length its runner sees per request. The target and EAGLE-family draft step 0 see the 1 + K verified positions (`q = 1 + K`); later EAGLE-family steps add one token (`q = 1`); DSpark drafts K positions per round (`q = K`); DFlash, DFlash2, LiLiCorr and multi-module MTP draft K + 1 (`q = K + 1`). Dynamic SD changes the target's verification length. EAGLE-family drafters also shorten their drafting sequence, while DSpark and DFlash currently retain their maximum draft-block width (K = 7: all 1024 requests under the 8192-token budget). A graph for `n` requests holds `n · q` tokens, which is what the decode budget bounds. **The decode budget** applies to every FULL uniform-decode graph with `q > 1`: the target's, the drafter copies of it, DSpark, DFlash and multi-module MTP. Each runner divides it by its own `q`: at K ≤ 7 the target and every drafter reach the 1024-request cap, while at K = 11 the target (`q = 12`) reaches 682 requests and DSpark (`q = 11`) 744. Why 8192: section 5.1. Adaptive verification's token-keyed graphs stop at the budget too. One-token draft decodes (`q = 1`, at most `max_num_seqs` tokens) are not bounded by it. **Graph count, one example:** MiniMax-M3 with EAGLE3 K = 3 at the GB200 defaults. | runner | this PR | main | | --- | --- | --- | | target PIECEWISE | 54, up to 8192 tokens | 83, up to 1024 tokens | | target FULL (`q = 4`) | 64, up to 1024 requests | 81, up to 256 requests | | drafter step 0 (copies of the target's) | 54 + 64 | 83 + 81 | | drafter steps 1–2 (`q = 1`) | 64, up to 1024 requests | 83, up to 1024 requests | | **total** | **300** | **411** | Current total memory is in section 5. Counts for every runner, K, dynamic SD tier and for GPUs other than SM100: appendix G (recomputed on the measured base; every launch's logged capture counts match).
Scope: vision encoder and TPU graph planning The new prefill/decode fields configure **GPU language-model and drafter graphs**. Vision-encoder graphs have an independent shape contract; TPU uses XLA compilation rather than CUDA graph replay. | Component | Size / execution contract | Controls | | --- | --- | --- | | GPU vision encoder | Visual **output tokens**, item/frame capacity, model paths and optional shape axes; captures a whole encoder path, including attention, with eager fallback | `cudagraph_mm_encoder`, `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch` | | GPU language-model prefill / decode | Scheduled tokens / requests × query length; PIECEWISE / FULL as described above | This PR's prefill/decode fields | | TPU language-model backbone | Token and request buckets select JAX/XLA executable shapes; these are not CUDA FULL/PW graphs | `MIN_TOKEN_BUCKET`, `VLLM_TPU_BUCKET_PADDING_GAP`, `additional_config.compilation_sizes`, `ATTN_BUCKETIZED_NUM_REQS` / `ATTN_CUSTOM_NUM_REQS_BUCKETS` | | TPU vision encoder, supported budget-manager path | Reuses GPU encoder budget generation and packing, with JIT compilation replacing CUDA capture/replay | Existing `cudagraph_mm_encoder` / `encoder_cudagraph_*` fields | **Vision defaults and counts.** Encoder capture is off by default. Its empty budget list means **automatic sizing**, unlike the new decoder lists where `[]` disables that kind. Budgets double from a model-provided minimum and include the maximum. For Qwen3-VL, with `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` and sufficient context, this gives `[64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192]`: **8 graphs**. Model paths and extra axes multiply the count: at the same cap, Gemma4 with five enabled row widths has **40**, and DeepSeek-OCR's global/local paths have **14**. These are source-derived examples, not measured captures in this PR. Multi-path models may regenerate their own per-path grids from the maximum; an explicit encoder list is not universally an exact per-path list. [Planner and count formula](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/vllm/v1/worker/encoder_cudagraph.py#L82-L280). Changing the decoder prefill cap alone does not resize encoder graphs. Encoder auto-sizing can depend on the scheduler token cap and model context. Encoder preparation and cached-output cloning remain outside graph replay. `compile_mm_encoder` is a separate compilation switch; `enforce_eager` disables encoder capture, whereas decoder mode `NONE` alone does not. **Memory / performance.** Encoder capture owns a separate shared graph pool plus persistent per-budget input/output buffers; runtime embedding caches and gather buffers add further costs. Graph count alone does not determine GiB. Upstream's GB200 Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B benchmark reports mean encoder latency **5.42 → 4.36 ms** with FLASHINFER and an explicit nine-size grid; that is an encoder benchmark, not an E2E result from this PR. See the [design and reproduction commands](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md). No encoder-specific memory measurement is claimed here. The pinned base already checks `runner.needs_cudagraph_capture()` before returning early for decoder mode `NONE`; the earlier encoder-only profiling caveat is resolved in the base ([current guard](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/08e3f264583e57199c167c577f3b445a58c155ab/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L944-L948)). Encoder-specific memory and runtime evaluation remain outside this refresh. **TPU scope.** At plugin `7840339bd3`, a DP1 configuration with an 8192-token cap and default minimum 16 has **10 token buckets**, doubling from 16 to 8192. This is not the total executable count: request buckets, embedding/PCP variants, SD and helper functions add variants. A positive padding-gap setting trades more compiled shapes for less padding. This PR's split CUDA-grid fields do not configure those TPU backbone buckets. The TPU vision manager already shares the encoder planner, but currently declines extra capture axes and assumes a single default path. [Token buckets](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/utils.py#L163-L263), [runner](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/tpu_runner.py#L1099-L1207), [vision JIT manager](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/7840339bd3a9a848a2f64cc72653efb11ca40ac9/tpu_inference/runner/mm_encoder_jit_manager.py). No TPU runtime or HBM validation is claimed. **Integration direction:** share shape planning, dispatch diagnostics and memory accounting while retaining explicit units and backend execution. A concrete planning follow-up is to prune infeasible budget/axis pairs: in the Gemma4 example above, 10 of 40 pairs have a budget below one image/frame row width and cannot be selected for nonempty replay. This is a source-derived pruning opportunity, not a measured memory saving ([shape contract](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c1a342b10d51443aefe7689a56420986184b0c69/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py#L1710-L1900)). Keep encoder budget overrides; do not silently copy the decoder grid into vision or TPU. Per-path/axis budgets remain follow-ups; encoder-only profiling is already handled by the pinned base. This refresh does not add encoder changes.

Throughput and correctness below were measured on main `51c6dfd8c8`, which includes the extensible KV cache (#56492), with the earlier 4096-token decode budget; the 8192 default changes only uniform decode steps wider than 4096 tokens, measured in section 5.1. The measured CG stack is this PR plus **2 GiB indexer chunking (#64806)**; rows marked † also carry the masked-candidate-consumer chunking, now in #64806, and the empty-prefill-chunk fix, now on main (#65046). title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Pass zero positions to the fused MLA decode q-prep kernel
author: seungrokj
body:
## Purpose
Fixes a large accuracy regression for Kimi-K3 on ROCm when DCP is off (dcp1). It comes from the fused decode q-prep path added in #59634.

`KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._fused_decode` gives AITER's `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` a **one-row** identity cos/sin cache (K3 is NoPE). It also passes the **real** token positions, assuming the kernel clamps them into the cache.

That assumption is false on AITER v0.1.26. DeepSeek-shaped inputs now go to the head-grouped `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla_seg_kernel<PAGE_SIZE=0>`, which only clamps on the DCP (`compute_all_q_rope`) path:
- **One head per block**, i.e. every small decode batch (`T*H/num_CU <= 32`): cos/sin reads past the cache return 0. For every token at position ≥ 1, q_pe is written as **all zeros** and a wrong k_pe goes into the KV cache. This is silent.
- **More heads per block**: the kernel reads past the allocation and can fault (see ROCm/aiter#6879).

Since the RoPE here is the identity, position 0 gives exactly the right result for every token. This PR passes a preallocated all-zeros positions buffer, sliced to the kernel's token count (taken from `slot_mapping`). That removes the dependency on any AITER clamp behaviour.
- The buffer is allocated once in `__init__` as a non-persistent buffer, so captured CUDA graphs need no extra per-layer memset.
- The now-unused `positions` argument of `_fused_decode` is dropped.
- The comment that wrongly said the kernel clamps is corrected.

ROCm/aiter#6879 fixes the kernel side. This change keeps vLLM correct on AITER versions with or without that fix.

## Test Plan / Results
1. Kernel microtest (MI355X, AITER v0.1.26, T=8 and 64, H=12):

| cos/sin cache | positions | q_pe max err | q_pe fraction == 0 | cached k_pe max err |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 row | real (1 … 900000) | 2.9–3.8 | 1.00 | 2.0–3.1 |
| 1 row | **zeros (this PR)** | ≤ 0.125 (fp8 rounding) | 0 | ≤ 0.125 |
| full 1M rows | real | ≤ 0.125 | 0 | ≤ 0.11 |

2. End to end with the InferenceX agentic eval:
   - Setup: Kimi-K3 MXFP4, TP8, dcp1, DSpark k=7, max-num-seqs 8 (the CI conc=4 recipe).
   - Eval: Kimi-Vendor-Verifier `kimi_tool_call_schema_full`, 408 cases.
   - Image: `nightly-rocm100-df6603f0`.

| | score | DSpark mean AL |
|---|---|---|
| before | 0.740 | 2.95 |
| fused path disabled | 0.988 | 3.47 |
| **zero positions** (per-call `positions.new_zeros` patch, same kernel input as this PR) | **0.988** | **3.52** |
| old image, before #59634 | 0.983 | 3.25 |

   The same regression shows up in InferenceX run 39733293799: conc 1/2/4 (dcp1) score 0.75–0.78, while conc ≥ 10 (dcp8, fused path disabled) scores 0.97–0.995.

3. End to end with the c1 recipe from SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4393, using **this PR's `mla.py`** unchanged:
   - Setup: dcp1, max-num-seqs 1, DSpark k=7, `decode_backend=latency_specialized`, `kda_prefill_backend=fused`, Model Runner V2.
   - The specialized decode was active. Its MLA layers still go through `mla_attn.forward`, so they use the fused q-prep path.
   - Eval: same suite, run at concurrency 1 as in CI.

| | score |
|---|---|
| before ([InferenceX CI job](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39923143820/job/120542350622)) | 0.7819 |
| **this PR** | **0.9926 (405/408)** |

   The 3 remaining failures hit the 2048-token limit without emitting a tool call. That is the same small residual seen on the old image and in the runs above.

4. `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_mla_direct_return.py`: 5 passed.

## Notes
- Separate from this PR: K3 has 96 heads, so TP8 gives 12 heads per rank, padded to 16. `_fused_decode` allocates `q_out_padded` with `torch.empty`, so the padding heads 12–15 go to the asm MLA kernel uninitialized. Their outputs are discarded and heads are independent, so this looks benign, but it may be worth zero-filling.
