title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Pair KV regions by layer for every transfer
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Purpose

NIXL pairs a peer's KV regions with the local ones in several ways, depending on the transfer:

- **By index**, for PP=1 peers: region *i* there is region *i* here, and the region group lists must match. Otherwise only pure MLA models transfer, through region-mapped reads.
- **By a PP window**, for pull from a PP stage: a slice `[offset : offset + num_local_regions]` of the peer's regions (`_remote_region_offset`).
- **By layer name**, for push from a PP stage under HMA or packed caches: `_align_remote_regions_by_layer` rewrites the peer's metadata into one region per local layer. `_compute_desc_ids` then routes blocks through `_transfer_layer_group_ids`.
- **By packed-row splitting**, when only the peer packs its rows: `_split_remote_packed_rows`, which refuses multi-group rows.

`_compute_desc_ids` has a separate mode for each: flattening, group mapping (with its handling of shared `-1` regions) and layer routing.

This PR replaces all of them with one rule: **every transfer pairs regions through the layers both sides hold.**

- Every worker advertises the layers of each of its regions (`region_members`) and the cache group of each layer (`layer_group_ids`), not only push PP stages under HMA.
- On the handshake, `_pair_regions` looks each layer up on both sides and records one pair (peer region, local region, cache group) per layer, deduplicated. A layer registered as two regions (K and V apart) pairs them in order. A region shared by several groups pairs once per group it holds a layer of. So which layers share a region no longer has to match between P and D, nor between a PP stage and the decoder.
- Group numbers are compared per layer, so a mismatch is caught even inside a region shared by several groups (group `-1`), where a per-region check cannot see it. Group ids are deterministic for a given model and config (PP stages group the whole model), so this guards against P and D having different plans, e.g. when KV page sizes unify at one TP size but not the other and the sliding-window layers fall back to full attention.
- Mamba/SSM hybrids pair the same way: attention pages and SSM sub-regions (conv sub-projections, SSM state, CSA-linear PLE page) are read from the peer region their layer pairs with. A hybrid peer with a different cache-group plan is refused at the handshake. PP stages stay refused for hybrids (not validated).
- Descriptor lists stay one per region on both sides. A peer's list keeps only its regions that pair (`_select_remote_regions`). A transfer reads or writes each pair at its group's blocks, which is the only mode of `_compute_desc_ids` for attention: `pairs=(regions, keys)`.
- When only the peer packs its rows, `_expand_remote_packed_rows` first views each row as one region per layer. That also covers rows holding layers of several groups, which `_split_remote_packed_rows` refused.
- Each pairing is kept per engine (`_dst_pairs`), and every TP rank of one engine must pair the same way.
- Refused at the handshake:
  - a peer that advertises no layers;
  - a peer missing a local layer;
  - a PP=1 peer holding layers this worker does not;
  - a layer split into a different number of regions on the two sides;
  - region metadata of different lengths;
  - a Mamba/SSM hybrid peer with any layer in another cache group.
- A non-hybrid layer in different cache groups on P and D still falls back to region-mapped reads for pull (MLA only), and is refused otherwise.
- `NIXL_CONNECTOR_VERSION` 15 → 16. A peer without `region_members` fails the compatibility hash instead of pairing by index.

Removed: `_remote_region_offset`, `_align_remote_regions_by_layer`, `_split_remote_packed_rows`, `_requires_layer_name_routing`, `_tracks_region_layers`, the `_transfer_layer_*` tuples, `_uses_region_group_mapping`, `dst_uses_region_group_mapping` and `_check_mamba_pairs`.

The pull guard for PP + HMA stays. This PR changes how regions pair, not which topologies are allowed.

### Related PRs

None of these replaces how regions pair; this PR does not duplicate them.

- #53360 adds `region_members` to the pull path for PP producers, including hybrid Mamba. It pairs each stage region with one local region, by the region's first layer, and copies every member group's blocks between those two regions. With layers of several groups sharing a region, that copies one group's KV into another group's pages. Pairing by layer, as here, avoids that.
- #56187 extends push's layer-name routing to Mamba/SSM. This PR replaces that routing, so the two conflict; Mamba pairs through the same layer pairs here instead.
- #57662 changes how regions are deduplicated at registration (by base address and block length). That is orthogonal to pairing, but both PRs touch `register_kv_caches`.
- #60113 adds support for different cache-group plans on P and D; this PR only detects them.

## Test Plan

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" pytest -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

Changed tests:

- **`test_nixl_push_connector.py`**:
  - The layer-alignment tests are now `_pair_regions` tests: pooled regions kept once, a PP stage keeping the decoder's regions of its layers, split layers, packed rows next to unpacked regions, and each refusal above.
  - The PP-window test now selects regions by layer.
  - The region-groups test now checks `groups_match`; a new test has the peer treat a sliding-window layer of a shared region as full attention.
- **`test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`**: packed rows advertise `region_members` and expand through `_expand_remote_packed_rows`. The asymmetric packed PP test computes descriptor ids from the stored pairs. New MLA + KDA hybrid test: a peer putting a KDA layer in another cache group is refused.
- **`test_nixl_connector_hma.py`**: the descriptor-id tests pass `pairs`.
- **`test_nixl_connector.py`**: the fake handshake advertises `region_members`.

## Test Result

- **Unit suites:** the failing set is identical to `main` on the same machine (CPU only), test for test:
  - 145 need a GPU;
  - 113 need NCCL;
  - one needs a gated HF repo, one Ray, one a newer `humming`.
- **`pre-commit`:** all hooks passed, including mypy.

### Real model KV layouts (simulation)

Each model's real per-layer KV plan, built with vLLM's own planner and allocator (model on the `meta` device, `load_format=dummy`, no weights). Real NIXL workers (P and D) register those caches; D handshakes with P and reads one request (pull), or P writes it (push); every recorded descriptor pair is executed as a memory copy, then every D page is compared byte for byte with tagged data written into P, and all of D's other bytes must stay zero.

TP and PP ranks are simulated in one process. Each P and D rank builds its own KV plan and caches at its TP/PP rank (a PP engine groups the layers of all its stages, as the engine core does), and D (pull) or each P rank/stage (push) handshakes with every peer rank. Attention split across TP ranks is compared per KV head, by global head index (heads replicated when TP > KV heads); MLA pages are compared whole; TP-split SSM state is compared row by row with the P rank and position holding it, each concatenated projection split on its own (Kimi-Linear conv `[q | k | v]`, Qwen3-Next conv `[q | k | v]` with key and value sizes, Nemotron conv `[x | B | C]`; recurrent and SSM state split by head). Pages are paired by token position when P and D have different logical block sizes (Kimi-Linear: 1920 vs 1024 tokens at TP1 vs TP2). Swapping two descriptors, or swapping D's q and k conv rows after the transfer, fails the check.

- **GPU**: one GB300, real GPU attention backends.
- **CPU**: CPU attention backend, block sizes 128, or 1152/1408 after Mamba alignment. FP8 checkpoints (MiMo-V2-Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Kimi-K2, MiniMax-M2, GLM-4.5-Air) are built without their quantization config, which has no CPU kernel and does not change the KV plan. Descriptor counts are from the first CPU run (TP1, same).

TP mismatch: P TP1 → D TP2 and P TP2 → D TP1. PP: P PP2 → D TP1 and D TP2. Numbers are descriptor counts.

| Model | KV plan (groups → regions) | Sim | pull: same | pull: TP mismatch | push: same | push: TP mismatch | push: PP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3.2 | 61 sparse MLA + 61 indexer, 1 group → 122 | GPU | ✅ 366 | ✅ 732 / ✅ 366 | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / ✅ |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | 20 KDA + 7 MLA, 4 groups → 7 shared | GPU | ✅ 710 | ✅ 832 / ✅ 496 | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | refused (Mamba PP) |
| gpt-oss-20b | 12 sliding window + 12 full, 2 groups → 12 shared | GPU, CPU | ✅ 72 (CPU: 48) | ✅ 144 / ✅ 144 | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / refused (HMA push, D TP > P TP) |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | 27 MLA, 1 group | GPU | ✅ 81 | ✅ 162 / ✅ 81 | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / ✅ |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | 36 GDN + 12 full, 4 groups → 12 shared | CPU | ✅ 168 | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | refused (Mamba PP) |
| NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 | 27 Mamba2 + 4 full, 8 groups → 4 shared | CPU | ✅ 116 | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | refused (Mamba PP) |
| Gemma 3 1B (1 KV head) | 22 sliding window + 4 full, 7 groups → 4 shared | CPU | ✅ 52 | ✅ / refused (replicated KV) | ✅ | ✅ / refused (replicated KV) | ✅ / refused (HMA push, D TP > P TP) |
| MiMo-V2-Flash | 39 sliding window + 9 full, 6 groups → 9 shared | CPU | ✅ 96 | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / refused (HMA push, D TP > P TP) |
| DeepSeek-V3 / Kimi-K2 | 61 MLA, 1 group | CPU | ✅ 122 | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / ✅ |
| Qwen3-8B / MiniMax-M2 / GLM-4.5-Air | 36 / 62 / 46 full, 1 group | CPU | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / ✅ |

Every refusal is a documented guard. "Replicated KV": with fewer KV heads than TP ranks, a non-MLA, non-Mamba transfer is refused when the side issuing it (D for pull, P for push) has the lower TP (`_validate_remote_agent_handshake`, unchanged by this PR). Kimi-Linear (as any Mamba hybrid over NIXL) needs `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`. MiniMax-M1 is not covered: `MiniMaxM1ForCausalLM` (and `MiniMaxText01ForCausalLM`) were removed from vLLM in v0.23.

DeepSeek-V3 also passes with block-major MLA on both sides (`BLNHC`, the whole block row is one region), and with P on `BLNHC` and D on `LBNHC`, where D expands P's packed row into one region per layer (`_expand_remote_packed_rows`).

Compared with older code on the same layouts:
- `main` (merge base 4541fcdd8), GPU rows plus Gemma 3 1B and MiMo-V2-Flash PP push (CPU): same results and identical descriptor counts. Main pairs PP stages by layer name in push (`_align_remote_regions_by_layer`), which this PR replaces with the one pairing rule.
- This branch before the Mamba pairing commits (`90ec0cb5c`), CPU rows: identical descriptor ids (same digests on Qwen3-Next, Nemotron, gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V3).
- `main` before this PR, DeepSeek-V3 with P on `BLNHC` and D on `LBNHC`: identical descriptor ids. The old `_split_remote_packed_rows` and the new expansion make the same reads.

Different cache-group plans on P and D are covered by the unit tests only.

### End-to-end P/D

gpt-oss-20b, pull, P TP1 → D TP2 on one GB300 node: GSM8K 5-shot (completions) flexible-extract 0.364 through the P/D proxy vs 0.362 on a single instance without P/D; 1320 requests, 2640 NIXL reads, no failed transfers or notifications.

Found along the way, independent of this PR (also before it): Qwen3-Next and Nemotron with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` read wrong bytes and write outside the request's blocks even with identical P and D. The likely cause is that Mamba registration in `register_kv_caches` uses `block_stride = physical_page_size`, which only holds for layer-major layouts. Auto layout picks `LBHNC` for these models, so it needs the layout forced. To be fixed or refused separately.

- **Not run yet:**
  - model evals for the other topologies above (the simulation checks the bytes of each block directly);
  - pull from PP stages, which is still refused under HMA.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change. The submitter reviews every changed line before marking it ready.

title: [Mooncake] Support selective leases for prefix lookups
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeStoreConnector` prefix lookups call `batch_is_exist`, which grants a read lease on every key it finds and moves it to the hot end of the eviction order. A lookup therefore renews every stored key of the prompt, including keys that loading the hit never reads: blocks outside a sliding window, or the per-block-boundary states of linear-attention / Mamba layers before the hit's tail. Once the store is full, those never-loaded keys look hot and survive eviction, while keys that later requests would actually load are evicted.

This PR adds an opt-in mode, `VLLM_MOONCAKE_STORE_SELECTIVE_LEASE=1`, in which a lookup:

1. probes the candidate keys with `batch_probe_key`, which checks existence without leasing ([kvcache-ai/Mooncake#3801](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/3801));
2. computes the hit as before;
3. leases only the keys that loading that hit reads (`batch_is_exist` on the hit's load set, per group load mask and tail key).

If a key was evicted between the probe and the lease, the hit gets shorter, and the shorter hit can end at a key the first lease did not cover (for example, an earlier boundary state). So the shorter hit is leased in a second round. A hit is returned only when the lease on all of its keys succeeded; otherwise the lookup reports a miss. A failing lease RPC also reports a miss and never breaks the lookup server.

The default path is unchanged.

## Changes

- New `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/selective_lease.py`: `SelectiveLookupLease` (probe, compute the load set, lease, record the `lookup_lease` operation in the connector metrics).
- `store/worker.py`: when the env var is set, the lookup probes through `SelectiveLookupLease` and passes its hit to `lease_hit`. The longest-hit computation moves into `_longest_hit` so it can be reused after an eviction.
- `envs.py`: `VLLM_MOONCAKE_STORE_SELECTIVE_LEASE` (default off).
- Startup fails with a clear error if the installed Mooncake lacks `MooncakeDistributedStore.batch_probe_key`.

## Requirements

Requires Mooncake >= 0.3.14 on the master and every client. `batch_probe_key` is not in a tagged release yet; this was tested with the nightly `0.3.14.dev20261022`.

## Test Plan

Unit tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py`, on a full-attention + Mamba (align mode) worker over an in-memory store:

- default mode still leases every probed key;
- selective mode leases only the loaded keys, and they cover every key the load reads (including partial hash hits);
- a key evicted between probe and lease yields a shorter, fully leased hit; continued evictions yield no hit;
- error results and a raising lease RPC report a miss;
- startup fails without `batch_probe_key`.

End-to-end A/B on Kimi-K3 (hybrid KDA + MLA), disaggregated 4 prefill workers (TP8) + 1 decode worker (DEP16) on GB300, agentic coding traces at concurrency 480, 60 min. Mooncake store with 160 GB per rank (7.5 TB total), eviction at 95% high-watermark. Both arms run the same build and the same Mooncake nightly; only the env var differs.

## Test Result

### Disaggregated, 4P1D (DEP16 decode), concurrency 480

| metric | lease all (default) | selective lease | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| total throughput / GPU (tok/s) | 27,491 | 28,305 | +3.0% |
| P90 ITL | 35.8 ms | 36.4 ms | +1.7% |
| TTFT P50 | 2.35 s | 1.73 s | −26% |
| TTFT P90 | 12.8 s | 3.83 s | −70% |
| TTFT P95 | 20.9 s | 6.39 s | −69% |
| E2E latency P90 | 79.0 s | 75.8 s | −4% |
| prefix cache hit rate (benchmark) | 93.4% | 95.0% | +1.6 pt |

The store's raw capacity is the same in both arms: about 523k keys at the watermark, 10% evicted per pass, no failed evictions. What changes is which keys survive. A per-request audit against the trace (which prefixes had a saved state available when the request arrived) shows misses on states saved 2–10 min earlier falling from 1.13 to 0.21 points of prompt tokens, and on states older than 10 min from 1.55 to 0.91. Misses on states younger than 2 min are unchanged (0.46 vs 0.45), since nothing that young is evicted.

Cost: the extra lease RPC averages 1.07 ms (P90 1.9 ms) per lookup, with no errors and no keys evicted between probe and lease during the run. The lease-free probe was itself slightly faster than the leasing one (36.8 ms vs 43.1 ms average).

### Aggregated, concurrency sweep

One aggregated worker (TP8, DCP8, FP8 KV cache) on 8 GB300 GPUs, the same agentic coding traces, 60 min per run, Mooncake store with 160 GB per rank (1.25 TB total). Both arms run the same build; only the env var differs. Prefix cache hit rate is the benchmark's: cached prompt tokens / prompt tokens over the measured requests.

| concurrency | lease | prefix cache hit rate | throughput / GPU (tok/s) | TTFT P50 / P90 | P90 ITL | E2E latency P90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 48 | all (default) | 96.50% | 19,921 | 1.13 / 2.58 s | 36.1 ms | 61.3 s |
| 48 | selective | 96.22% | 19,531 (−2.0%) | 1.10 / 2.81 s | 36.4 ms | 63.3 s |
| 64 | all (default) | 95.05% | 19,574 | 1.42 / 4.87 s | 55.9 ms | 94.6 s |
| 64 | selective | 95.18% | 20,341 (+3.9%) | 1.36 / 3.96 s | 52.6 ms | 84.8 s |
| 80 | all (default) | 93.33% | 18,104 | 6.09 / 21.2 s | 80.6 ms | 127.0 s |
| 80 | selective | 93.93% | 19,254 (+6.4%) | 5.30 / 19.4 s | 72.2 ms | 117.9 s |
| 96 | all (default) | 92.48% | 16,599 | 27.1 / 53.1 s | 84.8 ms | 156.9 s |
| 96 | selective | 93.97% | 18,080 (+8.9%) | 24.6 / 43.2 s | 73.5 ms | 145.9 s |

The gain grows with concurrency, i.e. with pressure on the store: at concurrency 96, misses on states that were saved and later evicted fall from 2.7 to 1.0 points of prompt tokens. Since the GPU KV cache is full from concurrency 64 on, the extra hits also save prefill work in the shared worker, which shows up as lower ITL.

At concurrency 48 the store is under little pressure, and selective lease is slightly worse. The difference comes from a few long requests (150k–690k tokens) that resumed from a state saved at an earlier boundary and not loaded since: the default mode kept it alive because later lookups over the same prefix renewed it, while selective lease let it age out. This is the trade-off of the mode: states that are only passed over by lookups are no longer protected.

title: [Spec Decode] Replace torch.compile'd AV draft-budget selection with a Triton kernel
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Replace adaptive verification's `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` draft-budget selection with a single-launch Triton kernel, JIT'd once in `warmup_kernels`. This removes the mid-serving compile stalls and cuts the host cost of every budget-binding step about 6x.

Related: #62539 fixes the same stall by pre-compiling the Dynamo specializations at startup. This PR instead removes the compile, which also removes the launch overhead it never paid for (details below). Credit to #62539 for the root cause and for spotting the `max_num_reqs` duck-sizing specialization.

## Claims

- No budget-kernel compiles during serving: one Triton JIT at warmup (0.45 s warm cache, 1.0 s cold) instead of 4–5 Dynamo graphs compiled on the first trimmed steps (1.8–4.7 s per process).
- Host time per budget-binding step drops from 76–90 µs (compiled) to ~15 µs. GPU time drops from 85–100 µs to 22–30 µs at typical batch sizes.
- Qwen3-4B + DSpark, GSM8K, concurrency 16 (H200): adaptive verification goes from 4,783 to 6,803 output tok/s (median), on par with #62539 (6,756; within run-to-run noise). Accuracy unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py` gives 24 passed on H200. The new GPU tests check the kernel against a torch global top-k reference: K ∈ {3, 8}, {1, 2, 300} requests (300 crosses a block boundary), budgets from 1 to total − 1. A ties test checks that exactly `draft_budget` drafts are admitted. They run in the existing `V1 Spec Decode` (H200 MIG) job. `pre-commit run` passes, including mypy.

**End to end, Qwen3-4B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7`.** Setup: 7 speculative tokens, probabilistic drafts, GSM8K 1-shot, 128 prompts, concurrency 16, 1×H200. All arms use the same build at `d561af5df`, run in alternation. Compiles are counted the same way as #62539: `TORCH_LOGS=dynamo` `start tracing _assign_draft_token_budget` lines during generation.

| Arm | Runs | Output tok/s, median (range) | Compiles during generation | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed verification | 3 | 6,507 (6,117–6,837) | – | 0.81–0.82 |
| Adaptive, main | 3 | 4,783 (3,072–5,541) | 2–3 | 0.83–0.84 |
| Adaptive, #62539 | 3 | 6,756 (6,735–6,785) | 0 | 0.83–0.84 |
| Adaptive, this PR | 3 | 6,803 (6,594–6,864) | 0 | 0.83–0.84 |

The script is the one from #62539, without `attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN"`. A separate run of this PR with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed with no errors (6,910 tok/s, accuracy 0.836).

**End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark.** Setup: TP4 + EP, H200, random 8K-token prompts. The metric is the warmup bench's worst TTFT (16 requests, concurrency 4, issued right after startup):

| | main | this PR | no adaptive verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| K=3 | 2,424 ms | 866 ms | 824 ms |
| K=8 | 1,815 ms | 789 ms | – |

Steady-state TTFT, TPOT, KV capacity and CUDA-graph memory are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Kernel microbenchmark (H200, median µs per call, host / GPU)</summary>

Host time is wall time across the Python call with no sync. GPU time is CUDA events around the call. `idx_mapping` is int64, as in `prepare_inputs`.

| num_reqs | budget | eager | torch.compile | Triton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 93 / 102 | 79 / 88 | 15 / 22 |
| 16 | 20 | 98 / 106 | 88 / 97 | 15 / 23 |
| 64 | 64 | 91 / 99 | 84 / 93 | 15 / 23 |
| 256 | 300 | 91 / 100 | 84 / 93 | 15 / 24 |
| 1024 | 2000 | 90 / 104 | 85 / 99 | 15 / 37 |

(K=3. K=5 and K=8 are similar, except Triton GPU time at 1,024 requests rises to 49 µs and 67 µs.)

First-call cost of the compiled version: 3.0 s cold (1.4 s with a warm Inductor cache), plus 0.45–0.64 s (0.11–0.16 s warm) for each of the `num_reqs == 1` / `draft_budget == 1` specializations. The Triton kernel compiles once, and later shapes, including 1 request with budget 1, run in under 0.1 ms.

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause.** `warmup_kernels` runs with adaptive verification off, and cost profiling never trims, so the compiled budget function first ran on a live trimmed step. It then recompiled for each 0/1 specialization (and for `num_reqs == max_num_reqs`, per #62539).
- **Why not keep the compile.** The op is about six tiny kernels and is bound by host launch overhead. Compiled it saves only ~0–20 µs over eager, and it still costs ~80 µs of host time on every binding step. It runs eagerly in `prepare_inputs`, outside any CUDA graph, so that cost lands on the step's host critical path whenever the host is the bottleneck.
- **Kernel.** A single program does three passes:
  1. Survival prefix products, stored as float bits. Values are non-negative, so int order matches float order; ineligible slots store −1.
  2. A binary search on the bits for the `draft_budget`-th largest value.
  3. Per-request counts above the threshold, with ties handed out in request order.

  Survival is non-increasing along a request, so per-request counts fully describe the winners, as before. With distinct values the result is identical to the old top-k. On exact ties, top-k's choice was already unspecified.
- **Specialization.** `num_reqs` and `draft_budget` are `do_not_specialize`, so the one JIT in `warmup_budget_kernel()` covers every shape. The kernel needs a `max_num_reqs × K` int32 scratch buffer.
- **Tradeoffs.** The binary search takes 31 sequential passes over `num_reqs × K` slots, so GPU time grows with very large batches (67 µs at 1,024 requests and K=8). That's still below the old path, and negligible next to a step at that batch size. I couldn't test ROCm or XPU here, where adaptive verification is also used. The kernel uses only standard Triton ops (`bitcast`, `cumsum`, `debug_barrier`, a scalar `while`).

title: [Bugfix][CUDA Graph] Weak-ref nested outputs of captured graphs
author: ZJY0516
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`weak_ref_tensors` only weak-refs one level. For a model output like `(hidden_states, [aux_hidden_states, ...])`, the inner list is returned as is, so every captured CUDA graph entry keeps its aux hidden states alive and the graph pool cannot reuse that memory for the next capture size. This PR makes `weak_ref_tensors` recurse into nested lists/tuples.

Related: #63406 lists this as "aux hidden states kept by every PIECEWISE size" in its memory breakdown. This PR is the standalone fix and also applies to main's capture sizes.

## Claims

- Captured graphs no longer pin the aux hidden states used by EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash and `extract_hidden_states`. Before, each captured size leaked `num_aux × num_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size` bytes (3 × 8192 × 4096 × 2 B = 192 MiB for one 8192-token size of DeepSeek-V4-Flash).
- No output change: the outputs alias the same memory as before; only the references held by the graph entries become weak.
- `weak_ref_tensors` now raises on unknown types at any nesting level, not only at the top level, and passes ints and `LayerName`s through (piecewise subgraph outputs can contain ints, and Inductor graph partition outputs can contain `LayerName`s, see below).

## Validation

**Unit test** (`tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py`, run by the "Async Engine, Inputs, Utils, Worker" CI step), on GB200:

```
# with this PR
pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py -v
39 passed

# torch_utils.py reverted to main, new tests only
pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py -v -k weak_ref
FAILED test_weak_ref_tensors_does_not_keep_nested_tensors_alive
E       AssertionError: assert 4194304 == (8388608 - 8388608)
FAILED test_weak_ref_tensors_rejects_unknown_nested_types
E       Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError
```

**What actually reaches `weak_ref_tensors`.** I wrapped the function in `vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py` and `vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`, then started each engine and recorded the structure of every input during capture (`T` = tensor; `[n:...]` = list of length n; `(n:...)` = tuple of length n):

| Model | CUDA graph path | Inputs seen |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B + EAGLE3 | torch.compile piecewise | `[1:T]` `[2:T]` `[4:T]` `[5:T]` `[6:T]` |
| Qwen3-1.7B + EAGLE3 | breakable | target `(2:T,[3:T])`, drafter `(2:T)` |
| gpt-oss-20b + EAGLE3 | torch.compile piecewise | `[1:T]` `[2:T]` `[5:T]` `[6:T]` |
| gpt-oss-20b + EAGLE3 | breakable | target `(2:T,[3:T])`, drafter `(2:T)` |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | torch.compile piecewise | `[1:T]` `[5:T]` `[6:T,int]` |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | breakable | `T` |

The nested case is the breakable target output with aux hidden states. The int case is a piecewise subgraph output of the FP8 MoE model, which is why ints are passed through. No `None`, float or 0-size tensor showed up.

The table does not cover `use_inductor_graph_partition=True`. There, on torch >= 2.11, `CUDAGraphWrapper` wraps each Inductor partition, and a partition's outputs can include `LayerName` objects that torch.compile hoists as graph inputs. This PR's first CI run caught it (`ValueError: Invalid type for tensors: <class 'vllm.utils.torch_utils.LayerName'>` in `test_full_cudagraph.py[*-partition=True]` and `test_full_graph.py::test_custom_compile_config`), so `LayerName`s pass through as well. After the fix, on GB200:

```
pytest compile/fullgraph/test_full_cudagraph.py -k "True and not MLA"
30 passed, 20 skipped (FA3, RocmAttn)

pytest compile/fullgraph/test_full_graph.py -k "compilation_config4 or compilation_config5"
2 passed
```

**End-to-end A/B**: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, TP4+EP, DSpark K=7, 4×GB200. Breakable CUDA graph is on by default for this model, and capture sizes are main's defaults. Main is this PR's parent (2c58be22b6). Memory numbers are from TP rank 0.

| | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph pool, actual | 5.86 GiB | 5.39 GiB | −0.47 GiB |
| CUDA graph pool, profiler estimate | 8.55 GiB | 7.90 GiB | −0.65 GiB |
| Available KV cache memory | 112.94 GiB | 113.59 GiB | +0.65 GiB |
| GPU KV cache size | 7,277,119 tokens | 7,319,402 tokens | +0.58% |
| GSM8K 5-shot, flexible-extract | 0.9560 | 0.9522 | −5 / 1319 questions |
| DSpark acceptance (accepted / drafted) | 57.74% | 57.84% | |
| Mean acceptance length | 5.04 | 5.05 | |

The leak on main is about 0.65 GiB here, and it grows with the number and size of PIECEWISE capture sizes (#63406 raises both).

The 5-question GSM8K gap is from a single run per arm; serving is not batch invariant, so some run-to-run variance is expected. It does not indicate corrupted aux hidden states: they only feed the drafter, so corruption would lower acceptance, and acceptance is unchanged. The target model alone decides the output tokens under greedy rejection sampling.

<details>
<summary>Serve command</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'
```

GSM8K: 5-shot, temperature 0, chat completions, thinking off. Acceptance is read from `vllm:spec_decode_*` metrics after the GSM8K run. Memory numbers come from the `CUDA graph pool memory`, `Available KV cache memory` and `GPU KV cache size` log lines.
</details>

## Details

**Affected paths.** `weak_ref_tensors` is called on capture outputs by:
- `BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper._capture`: captures the whole model forward, so EAGLE3/DSpark targets return `(hidden_states, [aux, ...])`. Breakable CUDA graph is on by default for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, MiniMax-M3, GLM-5-Next, Kimi-K3 and others, under both model runners.
- `CUDAGraphWrapper` in FULL mode on MRV1, which also wraps the whole model.

Not affected: torch.compile piecewise subgraph outputs are flat, and MRV2 FULL graphs copy outputs into persistent buffers instead of weak-refing them.

**Safety of the weak refs.** Once the aux tensors are weak, later captures may reuse their memory, the same as for `hidden_states` today. So the aux tensors must be consumed before the next graph replay. Every consumer copies them first: MRV1 `torch.cat`/`torch.stack` in `gpu_model_runner.py`, MRV2 DFlash `_store_hidden_states` (concatenates into its staging buffer), MRV2 `extract_hidden_states` (`torch.stack` + `copy_`).

**Type contract.** Previously, non-tensor values inside a list/tuple passed through `weak_ref_tensor` silently, which is how the nested list slipped through. Now containers recurse, ints and `LayerName`s pass, and any other type raises with its type name. The tradeoff: a model whose capture output contains a leaf type not in the table above (e.g. `None`) fails at capture time instead of passing silently. The raise already caught one such case before (`IntermediateTensors`, #24275), and caught `LayerName` in this PR's first CI run.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches `weak_ref_tensors` or this leak. #63406 changes capture sizes and only references the leak in its memory accounting.

The fix and analysis originate from Bo Pang (co-author). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the change, the tests and the validation scripts.

title: [Doc][Recipe] MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: DEP2 + DEP4 PD on GB200/GB300, 7-token FLASHINFER_TS DSpark on NVIDIA
author: zyongye
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Update the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash recipe's NVIDIA prefill/decode setup to one DEP2 prefill + one DEP4 decode on GB200 and GB300, and switch the NVIDIA DSpark default to seven speculative tokens on the FlashInfer PrimiTS (`FLASHINFER_TS`) draft backend.

**Draft:** served and evaluated on GB300 with the public image (see Validation); GB200 and the B200/B300 single-node smoke test are still pending.

## Claims

- **Guide:** "Prefill/decode disaggregation (1P1D, DEP2 + DEP4, NVIDIA GB200 / GB300)" replaces the GB200 TP4 + TP4 section. A DEP2 prefill on one tray feeds a DEP4 decode on a second tray. Both roles run DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE over expert parallelism, the V2 model runner and `--numa-bind`, with NIXL `engine_ttl: 0` and `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600`. The decode adds `--watermark 0.05`, 28 seqs per rank and FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs up to 224 tokens. Host KV offload on the prefill is documented as an option.
- **Command builder:** `strategy_overrides.pd_cluster` renders the same pools and role flags for `gb200` / `gb300`. `vllm-router` is pinned to `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1`, because it takes one DP size for both pools.
- **DSpark on NVIDIA (B200, B300, GB200, GB300):** `num_speculative_tokens` 3 → 7 and draft attention `FLASH_ATTN` → `FLASHINFER_TS`, in the feature and in the single-node GB200 guide command. AMD (3 tokens, `TRITON_ATTN`) and Hopper (no DSpark) are unchanged.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes` passes on vllm-project/recipes `main` (6027ec8).
- Rendered commands checked:
  - `pd_cluster` on `gb200` / `gb300` renders DEP2 + DEP4 with the flags above.
  - Every NVIDIA rendering carries the 7-token `FLASHINFER_TS` draft.
  - MI355X renders unchanged, as do the B200 and B300 `pd_cluster` layouts and the non-`pd_cluster` GB200/GB300 layouts, apart from the draft.
- `pre-commit run --files recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml` passes.
- **Served on GB300 (4-GPU trays) with `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash`** (arm64 `sha256:5d76347628973fb80519a919a2f2740b6645b62cba3fe2bd87b25f111bd0e948`), checkpoint `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash@a60dfa7` with its built-in `dspark/` draft. The guide's commands were run as written; only `--port` and cluster NIC/cache env were added. Each run checked the engine's logged args (DP sizes, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, the 7-token `FLASHINFER_TS` draft, `--watermark`) before evaluating.
- **gsm8k:** 5-shot, chat completions, `chat_template_kwargs: {thinking_mode: disabled}`, temperature 0, `max_tokens` 2048, all 1319 questions at once. Acceptance length comes from the engine's `/metrics` spec-decode counters around the eval (decode node for P/D).

  | Command | gsm8k flexible / strict | Null answers / truncated | DSpark acceptance length (k=7) | Other |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1P1D DEP2 + DEP4 (guide P/D section) | 0.9189 / 0.9067 | 0 / 0 | 4.55 | passkey 9/9 at 7.9K / 30.9K / 96.2K prompt tokens × 3 depths; 0 NIXL errors, 0 decode preemptions |
  | Single node TP4 (guide single-node command) | 0.9242 / 0.9151 | 0 / 0 | 4.77 | — |
  | Reference: TP4, same weights and eval, pre-release builds (2 runs) | 0.9204-0.9227 / 0.9128-0.9166 | | | |

  The P/D run is within run-to-run noise of the references (gsm8k at T=0 has varied by about 1pt between repeated runs of one config).
- **Startup:** the first P/D attempt failed on a cold node. The prefill's API servers hit vLLM's 600 s default `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` during JIT builds, CUDA graph capture and FlashInfer autotune, so both P/D roles now set it to 3600. With partly warm JIT caches the prefill still took about 9 minutes and the decode about 5 minutes to start. The limit only applies with data parallel (one API server per DP rank). The single-node TP4 command is unaffected.
- **Pending (blocks ready-for-review):**
  - [ ] The P/D commands on GB200.
  - [ ] Single-node TP4 smoke test with the 7-token `FLASHINFER_TS` draft on B200 or B300, and on GB200: the server starts, answers a chat request, and draft acceptance is nonzero.

## Details

- **Where the layout comes from:** it and the per-role settings were tuned in GB300 AgentX runs on a pre-release build. In those runs, DEP4 decode beat DEP8 per GPU at the same batch per rank. A second DEP2 prefill did not raise throughput, because decode was the bottleneck. That build used features not upstream (a NIXL push transfer mode and a Mooncake-backed prefix pool), plus synthetic acceptance for throughput. The recipe uses NIXL pull, real acceptance (`rejection_sample_method: block`) and the public image instead.
- **Decode sizing:**
  - `--watermark 0.05` makes extra requests wait in the queue instead of preempting running ones.
  - The decode's `--max-num-batched-tokens` stays at 8192, because a preempted request recomputes its context in chunks of that size while every DP rank runs eager steps.
  - NIXL `engine_ttl: 0` turns off idle remote-engine cleanup; with the default one-hour TTL, a decode crashed an hour after its prefill went away.
- **Removed:** the GB200 TP4 + TP4 section (eager prefill, decode `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`, `enforce_handshake_compat: false`). Both roles now share the attention and DSpark configs, which the NIXL compatibility hash covers, so the handshake check can stay on.
- **Tradeoff:** the renderer applies a feature's args per hardware, not per strategy. So the 7-token draft is now the default for every NVIDIA layout, including high-concurrency DEP serving, where a shorter draft can give more throughput. InferenceX's GB200/GB300 DEP4 aggregated lanes use 3 tokens.
- **Known renderer behavior:** for models that fit on one node, the static JSON API co-locates the two PD roles on one node, so `hw/gb{200,300}/strategies/pd_cluster.json` shows the DEP4 decode on `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3`. The interactive builder uses the recipe's per-role `nodes` (one tray each). The current recipe has the same co-location.
- **Not a duplicate:** #63232 (the `minimax-m31-flash` support branch) adds an earlier version of this file. No other open PR changes it.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash: run the aux hidden state FC in the draft dtype
author: azaidy
body:
## Overview

A DFlash / DFlash2 drafter fails to start when the target model gives it FP32 aux hidden states (Muse Spark keeps its residual stream in FP32). The drafter's bf16 `fc` gets an FP32 input. This PR casts the input of `fc` to the FC's `params_dtype` in `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM.combine_hidden_states`.

## Claims

- Bug fix: Muse Spark Open with a DFlash2 draft (`"method": "dflash"`) now loads and serves. Before this change, the profile run failed with `expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype`.
- No change for targets whose hidden states are already in the draft dtype: `Tensor.to()` returns the same tensor and adds no kernel.
- This PR makes no performance claims.

## Validation

**Unit test** (runs on CPU tensors): `test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype` in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py` builds a bf16 `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM` on CPU through its constructor (with the file's `_mock_draft_configs` helper), gives `combine_hidden_states` FP32 aux hidden states, and checks that the result is bf16 and equal to `fc` applied to the bf16 input.

Before the fix (this PR's base 5f63ea4 + the new test):

```
$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -k fp32_target -q
vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py:89: in default_unquantized_gemm
    return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, bias)
E       RuntimeError: expected m1 and m2 to have the same dtype, but got: float != c10::BFloat16
FAILED tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py::test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype
1 failed, 103 deselected
```

With the fix:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -k fp32_target -q
1 passed, 103 deselected

$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \
    tests/transformers_utils/test_muse_spark_config.py -q
34 passed, 92 skipped        # the skipped tests require CUDA
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, check-test-tethering).

**End to end** (8x MI355X, `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, `--dtype bfloat16`, TP8, speculative config `{"method": "dflash", "model": "<Muse-Spark-Open DFlash2 draft, bf16>", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, ...}`):

| Server | Result |
|---|---|
| Without the fix | Fails at startup in the profile run: `expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype` in `combine_hidden_states` |
| With the fix | Loads (`DFlash2Speculator`) and serves requests |

The GPU runs used the same change on an earlier main (6ee316e). Between 6ee316e and this base, main changed `qwen3_dflash.py` only in the draft quantization-config mapping (#63001), not in `combine_hidden_states` or `fc`, and did not change `qwen3_dflash2.py`.

## Details

**Root cause.** Muse Spark keeps its residual stream in FP32, so the aux hidden states that it captures for the drafter are FP32. `DFlashQwen3Model.fc` is a `ReplicatedLinear` with `params_dtype = model_config.dtype` (bf16). `combine_hidden_states` called `fc` on the FP32 tensor directly, and the GEMM rejects the mixed dtypes. `DFlash2Qwen3ForCausalLM` inherits this method, so DFlash2 drafters fail the same way.

**Fix.** Cast the input to `self.model.fc.params_dtype` before `fc`. We use `params_dtype` and not `fc.weight.dtype`: `params_dtype` is the activation dtype that the FC's linear method expects, also when the FC is quantized (an FP8 or packed int weight has a different dtype or no `weight`). For an unquantized FC the two are equal.

**Muse Spark DSpark.** `MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM` (subclass of `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` -> `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM`) has its own `combine_hidden_states` override that casts to `fc.weight.dtype` and then calls this method. Its draft checkpoint is bf16 and unquantized, so the second cast is a no-op. This PR does not change that file.

**Not a duplicate.** #40334 proposed the same one-line cast for an AWQ + `cpu_offload_gb` case. Its author closed it without a merge after pre-commit failures, and it did not cover the FP32-residual target case. Issue #42588 (ROCm, `float != c10::Half` at the same line) was closed after #42646, which changed the RMSNorm path and not `combine_hidden_states`. No open PR changes `combine_hidden_states` (searches: `dflash dtype`, `dflash fp32`, `dflash mat1 mat2`, `combine_hidden_states dtype`, `aux hidden states dtype draft`).

**Cost.** The cast is not a host-device sync and is safe in CUDA graphs. For a bf16 target it is a no-op. For an FP32 target it is one cast kernel on the `fc` input, which the FC needs anyway.

**CI.** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py` runs in the "V1 Spec Decode" step (`pytest -m 'not slow_test' v1/spec_decode`; `source_file_dependencies` include `vllm/model_executor/` and `tests/v1/spec_decode`). The new test runs the model on CPU tensors. We cannot add a CI regression test through `LLM` with real weights: the only FP32-residual target that we know is the 816B Muse Spark model, which needs 8 GPUs. We did the end-to-end validation above outside CI.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] FlyDSL decode monokernel for DSpark verify steps on MI355X (--monokernel)
author: azaidy
body:
## Overview

With `--monokernel`, Muse Spark Open MXFP4 on 8x MI355X (TP8 + expert parallelism, 7-token DSpark draft) runs
decoder layers 1-60 of every verify step of 1-16 requests as persistent FlyDSL launches. One launch, or three, cover
the work from a layer's attention output to the next layer's q, o-gate and KV insert. All other steps and layers 0 and
61 run the stock path. The flag is off by default.

## Claims

- AgentX (agentic-coding traces, DSpark at synthetic acceptance length 4.05, all requests, full mode), this PR's head
  with `--monokernel` vs the faster stock recipe on its base (main 3d81a51): interactivity (1000 / p90 ITL) / total
  tok/s/GPU of 413.8 / 2974 vs 263.1 / 2325 at c = 1 (+57 % / +28 %), 314.1 / 3056 vs 232.7 / 2368 at c = 2
  (+35 % / +29 %), 295.2 / 4430 vs 217.3 / 3585 at c = 4 (+36 % / +24 %) and 208.4 / 7384 vs 143.3 / 6126 at c = 8
  (+45 % / +21 %).
- Accuracy contract (GPQA-Diamond, AIME25, RULER NIAH; method of #60397), `--monokernel` vs stock: GPQA-Diamond
  88.7 vs 88.5 (delta +0.1 ± 0.5; boxed-letter prompt -0.7 ± 0.6), AIME25 98.6 vs 98.3 (+0.3 ± 0.4), RULER NIAH 348 vs 346 of 360.
- Accuracy and DSpark acceptance, real acceptance, stock (main 3d81a51) and `--monokernel` (c0f424a) with the same
  server flags: GSM8K (full set, 5-shot) 0.9651-0.9735 with `--monokernel` and 0.9666-0.9742 stock at c = 1-16, mean
  acceptance length 4.512 vs 4.431. Long-context needle retrieval at 33k-529k tokens: 192/192 in both arms, mean
  acceptance length 3.638 vs 3.600.
- Opt-in only. If the deployment is not supported, vLLM refuses it at startup with every reason. Steps that the
  kernels do not cover run stock. Nothing changes without `--monokernel`.

## Validation

All runs: c0f424a (`--monokernel`) and its base, main 3d81a51 (stock), on the vLLM ROCm nightly image 00b6c4c (AITER
0.1.26) with the Python files of each commit, 8x MI355X. After these runs, the head e2ed1f0 removes redundant code and
adds two startup refusals (sleep mode, weight transfer): all 30 builds compile to identical `.text`, and the 26
monokernel code objects that its server loads have the same sha1 as on c0f424a. On 49485cc (the head without the two
refusals): GSM8K c = 8 0.9674 with acceptance length 4.495; AgentX fast mode vs c0f424a 328.8 / 2867 vs 330.5 / 2865
at c = 1 and 209.2 / 6135 vs 215.4 / 6151 at c = 8 (fast-mode noise).

### Performance: AgentX

Server: the recipe's Muse Spark Open MXFP4 command on 8x MI355X with the DSpark draft. Changes for the benchmark:
`--max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, and synthetic acceptance
(`"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":4.05`). The `--monokernel` server is TEP8.
Stock runs the recipe's two strategies: plain TP8 (with `--max-num-seqs 8`, the recipe's 1M-context TP setting; the
recipe's lowest-latency choice for one request) and TEP8 (the same command as the `--monokernel` arm without
`--monokernel`). Benchmark: `agentx profile --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --concurrency C`. This
dataset is agentic-coding traces with an ISL p50 of 159k tokens and a maximum of 397k. Metrics are over all
requests: interactivity = 1000 / p90 ITL (tok/s/user) and total tok/s/GPU.

Full mode (`--benchmark-duration 3600 --warmup-requests-per-lane 10`), one run a point. Each cell: interactivity /
total tok/s/GPU (p90 ITL in ms, requests):

| c | `--monokernel` (TEP8) | stock TP8 | stock TEP8 | `--monokernel` vs the faster stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 413.8 / 2974 (2.42, 291) | 263.1 / 2325 (3.80, 256) | | +57 % / +28 % |
| 2 | 314.1 / 3056 (3.18, 474) | 232.7 / 2368 (4.30, 398) | 223.5 / 2367 (4.47, 398) | +35 % / +29 % |
| 4 | 295.2 / 4430 (3.39, 668) | 217.3 / 3585 (4.60, 580) | 212.5 / 3392 (4.71, 557) | +36 % / +24 % |
| 8 | 208.4 / 7384 (4.80, 1362) | | 143.3 / 6126 (6.98, 1176) | +45 % / +21 % |

Stock TP8 at c = 8 and stock TEP8 at c = 1 were not run (the recipe names TEP8 the faster choice from a few
concurrent requests, and TP8 for one request). This PR does not measure c >= 16.

### Accuracy

Real acceptance (the recipe's block verification), stock and `--monokernel` with the same server flags: TEP8
(`--tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel`) in both arms; the only difference is `--monokernel`. The
acceptance length is the DSpark mean acceptance length from the server's `/metrics` over each run.

GSM8K = InferenceX gsm8k.yaml, full set (1319), 5-shot, prefix caching off (flexible-extract; strict-match differs by
0.0008 at most). Output tok/s = the generated tokens (from `/metrics`) / the wall time of the run:

| c | GSM8K stock | GSM8K mono | acceptance length stock | acceptance length mono | output tok/s stock | output tok/s mono |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.9666 | 0.9666 | 4.533 | 4.570 | 300 | 480 |
| 2 | 0.9719 | 0.9735 | 4.488 | 4.465 | 520 | 662 |
| 4 | 0.9719 | 0.9697 | 4.461 | 4.524 | 862 | 1124 |
| 8 | 0.9712 | 0.9704 | 4.400 | 4.422 | 1329 | 1465 |
| 16 | 0.9742 | 0.9651 | 4.273 | 4.577 | 1973 | 2125 |
| mean | 0.9712 | 0.9691 | 4.431 | 4.512 | | |

The stderr of one GSM8K score is about 0.005; the per-c differences go both ways. Three more runs at c = 16 (on the
head e2ed1f0): stock 0.9682 / 0.9689 / 0.9704, `--monokernel` 0.9727 / 0.9727 / 0.9742.

With the AgentX server flags (prefix caching on), GSM8K at c = 8: stock 0.9682 with acceptance length 4.526,
`--monokernel` 0.9704 with 4.426.

Long context: multi-key needle retrieval. Each prompt hides 8 seven-digit numbers in filler text and asks for one;
the answer is scored by exact match. 12 prompts at each length, each run at c = 1, 2, 4 and 8, prefix caching on:

| context | correct stock | correct mono | acceptance length stock | acceptance length mono |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 33k | 48/48 | 48/48 | 3.525 | 3.648 |
| 132k | 48/48 | 48/48 | 3.649 | 3.607 |
| 264k | 48/48 | 48/48 | 3.620 | 3.672 |
| 529k | 48/48 | 48/48 | 3.623 | 3.627 |

The answers are short (about 360 tokens), so the acceptance length is lower than on GSM8K in both arms.

#### Accuracy contract: GPQA-Diamond, AIME25, RULER NIAH

Method of #60397 / RFC #59665: pass@1, the same build and server flags in both arms (TEP8, DSpark with real
acceptance, prefix caching on, 8 requests in flight); stock = main 3d81a51, `--monokernel` = the head
e2ed1f0. ± is the standard error across questions; delta is mono - stock, paired by question.

| | stock | `--monokernel` | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPQA-Diamond, the GPQA authors' prompt (16 samples a question) | 88.5 ± 1.8 | 88.7 ± 1.8 | +0.1 ± 0.5 |
| GPQA-Diamond, boxed-letter prompt (16 samples a question) | 86.4 ± 1.8 | 85.7 ± 1.8 | -0.7 ± 0.6 |
| AIME25 (32 samples a problem) | 98.3 ± 0.7 | 98.6 ± 0.7 | +0.3 ± 0.4 |
| RULER NIAH (single, multikey 2 and 3 at 32K / 128K / 256K, 40 a cell) | 346/360 | 348/360 | |

- GPQA-Diamond: InferenceX's questions (each in 2 option orders), 8 seeds, `reasoning_effort` xhigh, temperature
  1.0, top-k 64 (the model's generation config), 64K tokens. First row: the zero-shot prompt and answer parser of the
  GPQA authors' repository. Second row: a "put the letter in `\boxed{}`" instruction, graded with InferenceX's
  last-letter rule. With 4 seeds per arm the delta moved from -1.3 (seeds 0-3) to +1.5 (seeds 4-7) on the same prompt,
  so the seed-to-seed spread is larger than the per-question standard error.
- AIME25: lm-eval's `aime25` with the boxed-answer instruction, `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95,
  64K tokens, 32 seeds.
- RULER NIAH: lm-eval's RULER tasks, greedy, `reasoning_effort` high, 32K tokens, every needle must be in the answer.
  The misses are the same kinds in both arms (stock 11 / mono 8 with an empty answer, 3 / 4 with a distractor key).

The server logs have 0 errors and 0 peer-wait timeouts in every run.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
       AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN_SHORT_QUERY_3D=1 VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --reasoning-parser muse --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser muse \
  --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend mp --language-model-only \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --disable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --monokernel        # stock TEP8: the same command without --monokernel; stock TP8: also without
                      # --enable-expert-parallel, and --max-num-seqs 8

# GSM8K: InferenceX gsm8k.yaml (5-shot, full set), lm-eval chat completions, temperature 0, concurrency C (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template --tasks gsm8k.yaml \
  --model_args model=amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=C,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=1048576 \
  --gen_kwargs max_tokens=16384,temperature=0,top_p=1
```

For AgentX: add `--enable-prefix-caching` and set `"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":4.05`.
</details>

## Details

### Hook point

- `MuseSpark1xForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading` calls `maybe_attach_mono`. This runs after the per-layer quant
  finalize, so the experts are already in their shuffled kernel layout. The call is collective over the TP group.
  `MuseSpark1xModel.mono` is `None` without `--monokernel`.
- `MuseSpark1xModel.forward`: if `mono.try_forward(...)` returns the residual stream, the stock layer loop does not
  run. Otherwise the stock loop runs as before.
- `MuseSpark1xAttention.forward` ends in a new `back` (o-norm, o-gate, o_proj), and `MuseSpark1xDecoderLayer.forward`
  in a new `after_attention`. The monokernel runs layer 1 up to the attention with the stock functions and calls these
  two at the seams. The stock path calls the same code in the same order.
- `compute_logits` and `compute_logits_local` start an asynchronous read of the kernels' health words (every 64
  steps, outside graph capture). A peer-rank wait that timed out raises there, instead of a hang.
- The model runner, the scheduler and the attention backends are not changed.

### Eligibility

- At startup (default deny; one `ValueError` with every reason, agreed over the TP CPU group): gfx950 with 256 CUs,
  the checkpoint's text config, TP8 + `--enable-expert-parallel` (linear placement, no EPLB), no PP / DP / DCP / PCP,
  DSpark with 7 draft tokens, no LoRA, sleep mode or weight transfer, no KV connector or offloading, bf16 model and KV
  cache, Quark OCP-MXFP4 W4A4 experts on AITER (shuffled weights and scales), the fused QK-norm / RoPE / KV insert,
  `ROCM_AITER_FA`.
- Every step, from rank-invariant data only (the batch shape and the attention metadata counts, because all ranks
  must take the same path). The step must be a uniform verify step of 1-16 requests x 8 tokens, in FULL CUDA graph
  or eager mode, with dense bf16 LBHNC KV caches (block size 16). All other steps run stock.

### Buckets

| rows (requests) | build | launches a layer |
|---|---|---|
| 8 (1), 16 (2) | K3, S = 8 / 16 | 1 |
| 24-32 (3-4) | HA + HM + HB, S = 32 | 3 |
| 40-128 (5-16) | HA + HM + HB, S = 64 / 96 / 128 (rows padded up; `nrows` = real rows) | 3 |

`--max-num-seqs` selects the builds that the server compiles. Weights are views of vLLM's parameters. The kernels
write KV into vLLM's pages through `slot_mapping` (padding slots are skipped). The peer buffers are plain `cudaMalloc`
memory, opened over IPC on the TP CPU group. All launch arguments are fixed pointers, so vLLM's FULL CUDA graphs
capture the launches.

### Fused verify attention (8, 16 and 32 rows)

From layer 2 on, layer i's verify attention runs at the head of K3_i / HA_i, for both the sliding-window and the full
layers. It is split over all 256 CTAs by (request, KV head, key range) and merged before o_proj. It reads the layer's
bf16 KV cache through its KV cache group's `block_table` / `seq_lens`, the impl's softmax scale, and the window
(2047, 0). Only blocks inside the window are read. The descriptor tables hold pointers and counts only. They are
keyed by their contents and written once, so captured graphs read fixed tables. If `max_model_len` is above the 1M
keys that the builds stage block ids for, vLLM's op runs. Builds of 40 rows and more keep vLLM's op.

### Numerics: a16w4, opt-in behind `--monokernel`

The kernels keep the MoE activations in bf16 (MXFP4 weights x bf16 activations). The stock path is W4A4: it
quantizes the expert inputs and the SwiGLU output to MXFP4. Thus `--monokernel` output is close to the stock output,
but not bit-identical. Prefill runs stock (W4A4). Other differences are the reduction order (fixed rank order in fp32)
and the bf16 norm multipliers. The flag help, the module README and the recipe describe this.

### Known issues

- With the DFlash2 draft (not the recipe's draft), `--monokernel` lowers the real acceptance length: AgentX c = 4
  4.83 -> 3.52. The aux-hidden-state bookkeeping is the same as in the stock loop: the new tests compare the aux
  states for the DSpark, DFlash2 and seam target layers. The cause is open (per-rank draft divergence, or a draft
  that is more sensitive to the a16w4 numerics). The recipe's DSpark draft is not affected on AgentX (2.83 vs 2.87).
- The FlyDSL cleanup keeps some unused launch arguments (the timeline and EPLB-replica pointers) and LDS slots. With
  them, every build compiles to the same code objects as the validated kernels: identical `.text` for all 30 server
  builds.
- CI cannot run the kernels: they need 8x MI355X and the checkpoint's shapes. The CI test runs the host side on one
  MI355X (below). The kernel paths were validated with the serving runs above.

### Vendored kernels

`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/mono/kernels/` (about 6.7k lines) holds AMD's Muse Spark FlyDSL monokernel sources,
reduced to the builds that vLLM launches. They carry their MIT license header after vLLM's SPDX lines (as in
`rocm_block32_gemm.py`). They import FlyDSL and AITER's FlyDSL helpers only when the monokernel attaches. The host code
(mono/ without kernels/, model.py and two small core edits) is about 1.3k lines.

### Test plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main)
```

- On the head e2ed1f0 (main 3d81a51): 1x MI355X: 47 passed (39 s), on the vLLM ROCm nightly image 00b6c4c with the
  Python files of this branch. Pre-commit: all hooks pass.
- `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` builds a tiny real MuseSpark1x model (Quark MXFP4 experts, `ROCM_AITER_FA`, LBHNC bf16
  KV cache). It loads the model through the dummy loader + `load_weights` + `process_weights_after_loading`, and runs
  it with real attention metadata builders and bound KV caches.
  - Guards: refused before the weight finalize, accepted after it. Config and deployment guards use real vLLM
    configs.
  - Weight views alias vLLM's parameters.
  - Step tests (7 shapes x 3 aux-layer sets: the DSpark and DFlash2 drafts' layers and the stock / mono seams): the
    FlyDSL launches build only for the checkpoint's TEP8 shapes. The test runs each launch as the stock layer pieces
    that it replaces, on the device memory at the pointers that the host passes. Hidden states and the KV caches of
    all layers are bit-exact vs the stock loop. Aux hidden states match at fp32 rounding. Prefill, mixed, short-query,
    too-wide and PIECEWISE steps run stock.
  - Mutants fail these tests: aux shifted by one layer, dropped aux gather, wrong q buffer for the fused attention,
    KV written to the wrong layer, dropped stock layer-1 aux.
- The test is in the `Basic Models (Other)` step and its MI355 mirror (`models_basic.yaml`).

### Follow-ups

- Move to the RFC #60904 layout (`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/specialized_decode/`, tests under
  `tests/models/muse_spark/`) in a separate PR.
- A TP8 numerics test on 8x MI355X: each launch vs vLLM's layer on random full-size weights, as
  `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` does.
- Fused attention for the 40-128-row builds (c >= 5).
- Remove the unused launch arguments and LDS slots (this changes the code objects, so it needs a new validation).
- The DFlash2 acceptance drop (known issues).

and ran the tests and benchmarks listed above.

title: [CI][ROCm] Take MoRIIO P/D test port blocks from below the ephemeral range
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- `test_write_dummy_e2e_rocm.py`: `_open_port_block` picks its block below the kernel's ephemeral range instead of starting from `get_open_port()`

The MoRIIO dummy-weight P/D test hands each server handshake and notify ports that MoRIIO only binds, plus one port per TP rank, after the model loads. #62473 already stopped the test from handing the same port to two of its own servers. But the blocks still started at `get_open_port()`, i.e. inside the ephemeral range, and a released port there can go to any other `bind(0)` listener the servers start in the meantime (RCCL, gloo, ZMQ). The listener thread then dies with `Address already in use`, e.g. a TP1 decode server's notify port in [amd-ci build 15267](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15267/table?jid=01a167fe-b072-4523-b8b6-522a7cfa0163&tab=output) and a handshake port in [build 96960](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96960/list?jid=01a16a64-0c77-44f1-bcd6-4c5ade40c544&tab=output). The race has been there since the test was added in #60544. `bind(0)` and `connect()` never hand out ports below `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`, so taking the blocks from there removes it. #60743 is complementary: it makes MoRIIO fail startup loudly when the bind fails.

Locally, a released `bind(0)` port came back to a later `bind(0)` listener in 26 of 5000 trials with 32 listeners, while 200,000 `bind(0)` calls never returned a port below 32768. The new `_open_port_block`, called from 8 threads, gave 400 disjoint blocks of 8, all below 32768 and none containing any of 614 ports held by another process.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [CI][Bench] Keep captured request headers case-insensitive in Responses test
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fix the `Benchmarks CLI` failure on main, on both H200 and MI355. It has failed deterministically since #62835 bumped aiohttp to 3.14.5, multidict to 7.1.0 and yarl to 1.25.1:

```
FAILED benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py::test_request_payload_is_accepted_by_the_server_schema
    assert seen["headers"]["x-request-id"] == "bench-7"
KeyError: 'x-request-id'
```

**Root cause:** the test's aiohttp handler copies `request.headers`, a case-insensitive `CIMultiDictProxy`, into a plain `dict`, then looks keys up case-sensitively. With the new versions, the client sends the well-known header as `X-Request-ID`. A minimal aiohttp server and client, with no vLLM involved, shows the change:

| aiohttp / multidict | Header keys the server sees |
|---|---|
| 3.14.3 / 6.7.1 | `Content-Type`, `x-request-id`, `x-team` |
| 3.14.5 / 7.1.0 | `Content-Type`, `X-Request-ID`, `x-team` |

HTTP header names are case-insensitive, so the benchmark code itself is correct.

**Fix:** keep the headers case-insensitive with `request.headers.copy()`, which returns a `CIMultiDict`. The existing assertions are unchanged.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches this test.

## Test Plan

- Ran the same capture-and-lookup with `.copy()` under both version sets: all three lookups (`x-request-id`, `Content-Type`, `x-team`) succeed on 3.14.3/6.7.1 and on 3.14.5/7.1.0.
- `Benchmarks CLI` CI will confirm the full test.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: sync the CTA around radix barrier arrivals
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Sync the CTA before thread 0 arrives at the per-round inter-CTA barrier in `radix_topk`.
- Sync the CTA at the end of each radix row, before it moves on to its next row.

`radix_topk` uses thread 0 alone to signal the inter-CTA barrier. In each radix round it arrives while the other threads of its CTA may still be adding their local histogram into the group's global histogram, or (on CTA 0) zeroing the next round's buffer, so peers can read an incomplete histogram, pick a different pivot and emit duplicate or missing indices. Separately, a CTA that owns several rows moves on to the next one while slower threads are still scanning `shared_ordered` for pivot ties, and the next radix row's vectorized load, or CTA 0's short-row path, overwrites that dynamic shared memory. The cost is one CTA barrier per radix round, next to the grid-wide spin barrier that round already waits on, plus one per radix row. I found both races while porting the kernel to ROCm (stacked on #62298), and I am sending the fix on its own because the code is shared with CUDA. No CUDA GPU was available to me, so the reproduction below is on MI355X and CUDA CI has to confirm the CUDA build and the existing `persistent_topk` tests.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, tests and duplicate check</summary>

**Reproduction (MI355X, gfx950).** A standalone HIP build of `persistent_topk_kernel` from my ROCm port, launched with the same grid sizing as `topk.cu`. Its `radix_topk` matches main except for the warp-shuffle macro, and the barrier's acquire load is a device-scope HIP atomic instead of PTX. Each run executes 150 random cases (k ∈ {512, 1024, 2048}; widths 32K-256K; randn, near-constant, 4-value ties, mostly `-inf`, all-equal; ragged and negative lengths; 1-32 rows, so CTAs own several rows) and checks every row against a CPU top-k by value set.

| variant | runs | rows checked | wrong rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| neither barrier (main) | 169 | 882,700 | 146 (57 runs) |
| end-of-row barrier only | 169 | 882,700 | 152 (59 runs) |
| pre-arrival barrier only | 169 | 882,700 | 0 |
| both (this PR) | 169 | 882,700 | 0 |

The end-of-row race did not show up on its own in these runs, so I checked it by making odd waves sleep (`s_sleep`) before the tie scan:

| variant (odd waves delayed) | runs | rows checked | wrong rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-arrival barrier only | 32 | 29,820 | 712 (32 runs) |
| both (this PR) | 32 | 29,820 | 0 |

**Tests.** The kernel builds only for CUDA on main, so `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k persistent` could not run here; CUDA CI covers it.

No new test: the races depend on scheduling and do not reproduce deterministically, so a unit test would be flaky.

**Duplicate check.** Searched open PRs for `persistent_topk`, `persistent topk`, `radix_topk`, `topk race` and `persistent_topk.cuh`, and read the `persistent_topk.cuh` diffs of #62936, #55122, #41748, #41105, #58785, #55314 and #52149. None adds a sync before the per-round arrival. #55122 rewrites the tie-collection stage and ends it with a grid barrier plus `__syncthreads()`, which would also close the end-of-row race, so whichever lands second drops that hunk. #41105 adds a trailing grid barrier only for its fused page-table variant.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Exclude rc_gda lanes from the P2P NIXL agent
author: nilig
body:
## Overview

The P2P KV offload tier creates its NIXL UCX backend with UCX's default transports, which include the `rc_gda` GPU device lanes. After a P2P peer stalls or is replaced, connecting those lanes fails, so the peer was not usable again during the observation window (90 s): registering it fails, or its WRITEs stall, and every pull from it falls back to local prefill. This creates the tier's UCX backend with `engine_config="TLS=^rc_gda"`; the tier only moves host memory.

Fixes #63499.

Related: #63207 (the control-plane freeze in the same fault cases; without it the replacement cases freeze before reaching this bug), ai-dynamo/nixl#2437 / ai-dynamo/nixl#2337 (the `NIXL_ERR_INVALID_PARAM` loop that follows the first failed registration).

## Claims

- After a pause, the peer is pulled from again: the first pull succeeded 9-12 s after SIGCONT, and every probe from 40 s after SIGCONT on was pulled. After a replacement, the first pull came 0.3-0.7 s after the switch, and every probe from 10 s after the switch was pulled. Without the change, no pull from that peer completed during the observation window (90 s).
- No change for a healthy fleet, and none when `UCX_TLS` is set: UCX env vars take precedence over `engine_config`.

## Validation

Three single-GPU engines (Qwen3-0.6B, `--enforce-eager -O0`) on 8xH200 nodes with mlx5 InfiniBand: consumer A, source B that the fault hits, healthy source C. `OffloadingConnector` + `TieringOffloadingSpec`, 8 GiB CPU tier, P2P tier over RDMA, NIXL 1.5.0. Both arms run nightly `8e2beaa3b` + #63207 (`478d86b21`); the change is the only difference. A probe seeds a fresh ~2K-token prefix on B or C every 200 ms and asks A to pull it (`kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source`); "recovered" means A's requests to B (or B2) after recovery were pulled (A logged `request_blocks ... blocks>0` for them).

| fault on B | without this change | with this change |
|---|---|---|
| none | pass 1/1 | pass 1/1 |
| SIGSTOP 60 s, then SIGCONT | no pull in 90 s, 0/3 | recovers, 2/2: first pull 9-12 s after SIGCONT; every probe pulled from SIGCONT + 40 s (p50 0.051-0.057 s) |
| pod deleted gracefully, replacement B2 | no completed pull from B2 in 90 s, 0/3 (35-36 requested per run, none completed) | recovers, 2/2: first pull 0.7 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s (p50 0.056-0.057 s) |
| pod force-deleted, replacement B2 | recovers 1/3 (no pull from B2 in 90 s in the other two) | recovers, 2/2: first pull 0.6-0.7 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s (p50 0.053-0.058 s) |
| SIGSTOP, B on another node | no pull in 90 s, 0/1 | recovers, 1/1: first pull 10.6 s after SIGCONT; 242/242 from SIGCONT + 40 s |
| graceful replacement, B2 on another node | no pull from B2 in 90 s, 0/2 | recovers, 1/1: first pull 0.3 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s |

Across nodes, the graceful replacement fails through registration (`REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, then `INVALID_PARAM`) rather than the WRITE stall seen on one node. With NIXL main + ai-dynamo/nixl#2337 (and UCX v1.23.x) the `INVALID_PARAM` loop is gone, but recovery still fails: registration retries fail with `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` in the pause and force-delete cases, and 35-39 WRITEs stall in the graceful-replacement case. With `UCX_TLS=tcp,self,cuda_copy` all three recover (5/5); with `UCX_TLS=^rc_gda` set in the environment all three recover (3/3), matching this change.

Unit tests (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p`, CPU):

```
# this change
311 passed
# updated agent-config tests against main's nixl.py
FAILED test_data_transport.py::TestNixlAgentConfigSelection::test_ucx_only_creates_backend_without_rc_gda
FAILED test_data_transport.py::TestNixlAgentConfigSelection::test_default_backends_is_ucx_only
2 failed, 1 passed
```

CI cannot reproduce the failure: it needs RDMA NICs, GPUs and a peer fault between two engines. The updated tests only pin the backend configuration.

## Details

With UCX's GPU device API (NIXL sets `UCP_FEATURE_DEVICE`), every UCX endpoint gets `rc_gda` lanes next to its `rc_mlx5` lanes, whether or not GPU memory is ever transferred. UCX debug logs on the consumer for the SIGSTOP case:

1. At t+31 s (B stopped at t+21 s) the P2P session drops B and NIXL closes the endpoint; UCX destroys it after the UD keepalive times out at t+62 s.
2. B resumes at t+81 s and the session re-registers it at t+91 s: the new endpoint connects all eight `rc_mlx5` lanes, then the next lane connect fails:
   ```
   ib_mlx5_dv.c:446  UCX  ERROR   mlx5dv_devx_obj_modify(opcode=0x503) failed, syndrome 0x5d668c: Remote I/O error
   ucp_ep.c:1621 UCX  DEBUG ep 0x...: set_ep_failed status Input/output error
   nixl_agent.cpp:1679] loadRemoteMD: error loading remote metadata for agent '<B>' with status NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
   P2PSession <B>: peer registration failed, rejecting peer: NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
   ```
3. On NIXL 1.5.0 every later registration of B then fails with `NIXL_ERR_INVALID_PARAM` (ai-dynamo/nixl#2437). With NIXL main + #2337 the retries fail with `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` instead.

In the graceful-replacement case on one node, registration succeeds, but B2's WRITEs to A do not complete during the run and report no error; the stalled transfers pin CPU-tier chunks on both sides until both report `cannot store chunks`, which also drops some pulls from the healthy C (679/847 pulled). Excluding `rc_gda` removes that form as well.

The tier registers and transfers DRAM only, so it never uses the device lanes; dropping them also removes four lanes per endpoint. The change follows the `engine_config` mechanism the NIXL connector uses for its sleep-mode agent. On UCX versions without `rc_gda`, an unknown name in a negated `TLS` list is ignored without a warning. The underlying UCX failure (an `rc_gda` connect rejected after a peer fault) is not addressed here.

title: [Fast Start] Key the weight cache on MoE and linear kernel backends
author: liusy58
body:
## Purpose

Part of the cache-key audit in the Fast Start roadmap (#56049).

`process_weights_after_loading` converts weights into the selected kernel backend's layout, for example shuffled or repacked. Weights processed for one backend are therefore wrong for another. `WeightCacheKey` did not include the kernel backends, so an `ipc_cache` engine whose `--moe-backend` or `--linear-backend` differed from the daemon's still mapped the daemon's weights.

The NVFP4 MoE pre-processed path has a guard, but it only checks the **engine's** backend. That leaves one case silently wrong:

- the daemon runs with `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, so the weights are in CUTLASS layout;
- the engine runs with `auto`, which resolves to `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` on B300;
- the engine maps the CUTLASS-layout weights, `/health` returns 200, and every completion is garbage.

This PR adds `moe_backend`, `linear_backend` and `linear_backend_per_quant` to `WeightCacheKey`. The daemon and the IPC loader both build the key from `vllm_config.kernel_config`. A backend mismatch is now reported as a key mismatch on the backend field before any tensor is mapped. With `fallback=true` (the default) the engine then loads from disk.

The key uses the **configured** backends rather than the resolved ones. This is conservative:
- A daemon on `auto` and an engine on the backend `auto` resolves to counts as a miss and falls back to disk.
- Two `auto` configs that resolve differently, e.g. because of different environment variables, are not caught.

Keying on the resolved backend would close both gaps. It needs the resolution to run before the key is built, so I left it for a follow-up.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k "not cold_start"`
  - New `test_ipc_cache_key_tracks_kernel_backends` covers matching and mismatched `moe_backend`, `linear_backend` and `linear_backend_per_quant`, on both the initial load and a standalone `load_weights` reload.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files.
- End to end on B300 with Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, TP1, `--load-format ipc_cache`, zero_copy mode, `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.6`, `--max-model-len 8192`. Each case runs one greedy completion of "The capital of France is", comparing `main` with this PR.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 52 passed.

| Daemon `--moe-backend` | Engine `--moe-backend` | `fallback` | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | `flashinfer_trtllm` | false | — | Maps 1444 tensors, KV 142.04 GiB, output " Paris. Which of the following is the capital of Germany? …" |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | `flashinfer_cutlass` | false | `RuntimeError: pre-processed weights require FLASHINFER_TRTLLM backend …` while building the model | `CacheConfigMismatchError: WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['moe_backend']`, raised before mapping |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | `flashinfer_cutlass` | true | — | "Weight cache unusable (… ['moe_backend']); falling back to disk loading", then serves " Paris. …" |
| `flashinfer_cutlass` | `auto` (resolves to TRTLLM) | false | **Maps 1396 tensors, `/health` 200, output " Ivanka保卫 offence neighbours organisation centre centre defence …"** | `CacheConfigMismatchError: … ['moe_backend']` |
