title: [KV Connector] Mooncake store: skip padding in stored KV blocks
author: wzhao18
body: ## Purpose In a hybrid model, the KV cache groups share one allocation. Layer `j` of every group is a view of the same layer slot, there are as many slots as layers in the largest group, and each slot's page is sized for the largest per-layer state. Groups are kept apart by block ids: a block belongs to one group at a time. The Mooncake store connector registered every layer for every group, and copied whole pages. So each value of a Mamba / linear-attention group also held: - the layer slots of the group's padding layers, which only other groups use, and - the padding of each state up to the page size. Kimi K3 (DCP8) has 3 KDA groups of 23 layers and 1 attention group of 29 layers (24 MLA + 5 drafter), sharing 29 slots of 516,096 B per block. Every key therefore stored 29 × 516,096 B = **14.97 MB**. A KDA group uses only 23 slots, and each KDA state is 457,728 B. The real data is 23 × 457,728 B = **10.53 MB**, so **30% of every KDA value was bytes the group does not use**: 20.7% is the 6 slots of other groups and 9.0% is state padding. A saved KDA state (3 KDA groups × 8 DCP ranks = 24 keys) drops from about 359 MB to 253 MB. This PR: - **Registers each group's own layers only.** Each group's values are built from the regions of that group's own layers, with each Mamba state view as its own region. - **Copies only the used bytes of each block.** `RankLocalStoreLayout` now keeps `block_len` next to `block_stride`. `block_stride` is still the stride used to find a block in the GPU cache, and `block_len` is the number of bytes copied from it: up to the last byte the group uses. Mooncake stores the concatenation of the copied pieces, so the padding never reaches the store. Keys are unchanged. A model with a single KV cache group, or an attention group without padding, stores the same bytes as before. If a group has no layers on a PP rank, its keys are still written from all layers' regions, as before. HiSparse and TP-shared layouts are unchanged. A Mamba value now has one region per state view instead of one per layer slot. The measured put and get times still go down (below). ## Test Plan - Unit tests (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/`, all 376 Mooncake store tests pass). The new or changed tests below fail on main: - `test_rank_local_layout_skips_block_padding`: on a layer-outermost buffer, checks the regions, `block_stride` and `block_len`, `prepare_values` sizes (single and multi-block chunks), and `prepare_value_for_block`. - `test_hybrid_mamba_values_hold_only_group_states`: an attention group and a padded Mamba group are overlaid by `allocate_kv_cache`, and each Mamba layer has two state views of different dtypes with a gap between them. The test checks that the saved value is exactly the states of the block. It then clobbers the block and restores it: only the state bytes come back; the gap, the padding and the attention-only layer slot are untouched. - The SWA HMA test now also checks that each group registers only its own region. - Accuracy, Kimi K3 agg (TP8 + DCP8, dspark4 MTP with real rejection): GSM8K 50-shot, two passes. Prompts are ~8.1k tokens, which is more than one 7,168-token store block. Between the passes the GPU prefix cache is reset with `/reset_prefix_cache`, so pass 2 loads from Mooncake. - Perf A/B, Kimi K3 agg (2 GB300 nodes, 1.28 TB Mooncake store, agentic coding traces, 60 min, concurrency 64/80/96). The base build is the same build without this commit. ## Test Result ### Accuracy | pass | prompt tokens | loaded from Mooncake | GSM8K strict-match | |---|---|---|---| | 1 (cold) | 10,747,031 | 0 | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 | | 2 (GPU cache reset) | 10,747,031 | 10,492,800 (97.6%) | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 | Both passes get 1281/1319 correct. ### Stored value sizes Every Mooncake put interval of every run decomposes exactly into whole keys of the two expected sizes. That is 1,548 intervals with this PR and 1,551 on base. | | MLA key | KDA key | KDA share of saved keys | avg MB per saved key | |---|---|---|---|---| | base | 14,966,784 B | 14,966,784 B | n/a | 14.97 | | this PR | 14,966,784 B | 10,527,744 B (= 23 × 457,728) | 57–60% | 12.30–12.43 | ### Effective capacity and hit rate (same 1.28 TB store) "Unexpected miss" comes from a per-request trace audit. It counts prompt tokens whose saved state was stored earlier in the run but did not hit, i.e. tokens that were evicted. | concurrency | keys held at watermark, base → PR | benchmark prefix cache hit | unexpected miss (pts) | of which states > 10 min old | |---|---|---|---|---| | 64 | 83,009 → 96,375 (+16.1%) | 95.02% → 95.35% | 0.92 → 0.62 | 0.47 → 0.21 | | 80 | 82,730 → 95,952 (+16.0%) | 93.34% → 93.98% | 1.86 → 1.17 | 1.30 → 0.70 | | 96 | 82,761 → 95,094 (+14.9%) | 92.56% → 93.41% | 2.55 → 1.66 | 1.59 → 0.87 | ### Performance | concurrency | build | throughput / GPU (tok/s) | TTFT P50 / P90 | P90 ITL | E2E latency P90 | completed requests | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 64 | base | 19,559 | 1.42 / 4.63 s | 57.6 ms | 93.1 s | 4,811 | | 64 | this PR | 20,137 (+3.0%) | 1.38 / 3.77 s | 53.8 ms | 89.5 s | 4,951 | | 80 | base | 18,075 | 6.38 / 21.9 s | 81.5 ms | 125.8 s | 4,991 | | 80 | this PR | 19,140 (+5.9%) | 5.41 / 15.7 s | 73.4 ms | 115.3 s | 5,325 | | 96 | base | 16,039 | 26.6 / 57.6 s | 83.8 ms | 164.6 s | 4,398 | | 96 | this PR | 17,673 (+10.2%) | 25.8 / 53.3 s | 82.0 ms | 157.6 s | 4,880 | Mooncake transfers also shrink: - avg put time: 2.2–2.4 ms → 2.0 ms; - avg get time: 13.4–17.1 ms → 12.5–16.8 ms. There is one run per arm. Earlier runs of the same base store code at the same concurrencies give a sense of run-to-run noise: - hit rate: 95.05 / 93.33 / 92.48%, within 0.08 pts; - unexpected miss: 0.90 / 1.80 / 2.71 pts; - throughput / GPU: within 0.1 / 0.2 / 3.4%. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? title: [Perf][MoE] Size the DeepGEMM MegaMoE symmetric buffer for one sequence-parallel shard
author: mispa-ms
body:
## Overview With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `--enable-expert-parallel`, TP > 1 and PP = 1, Kimi K3 runs its MoE layers sequence parallel: each rank feeds MegaMoE at most `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, tp_size)` tokens. The MegaMoE symmetric buffer is still sized for `max_num_batched_tokens` tokens per rank. This PR sizes it for the shard. ## Claims - Kimi K3, `-tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`: MegaMoE buffer per GPU **10.73 GiB → 2.50 GiB**. - MegaMoE outputs do not depend on the buffer size (bitwise equal in a one-off check). ## Validation **Buffer per GPU** (one buffer shared by all MoE layers), allocated on GB300 by the vendored DeepGEMM with the arguments `KimiMoE` passes: 896 experts, top-k 16, `routed_expert_hidden_size` 3584, intermediate 3072, `fp8xfp4`, `situ`, no fused shared experts. EP = TP, DP = 1; TP8 ran on two 4-GPU nodes. | TP = EP | `--max-num-batched-tokens` | main | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | 8 | 16384 | 10.73 GiB | 2.50 GiB | | 8 | 32768 | 21.29 GiB | 3.68 GiB | | 4 | 8192 | 3.74 GiB | 1.66 GiB | | 4 | 16384 | 6.52 GiB | 2.34 GiB | | 4 | 32768 | 12.80 GiB | 3.74 GiB | DeepGEMM rounds the per-rank token bound up to a multiple of 1920 before sizing (the TP8 shard of 2048 tokens is sized for 3840).
Repro ```python # torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 buf.py (TP8: 2 nodes x 4) import os, sys, torch, torch.distributed as dist from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import _import_deep_gemm dist.init_process_group("nccl") torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])) buf = _import_deep_gemm().get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe( dist.group.WORLD, 896, int(sys.argv[1]), 16, 3584, 3072, mma_type="fp8xfp4", activation="situ") if dist.get_rank() == 0: print(f"{buf.buffer.nbytes / 2**30:.2f} GiB") ```
**Checks** on GB300, nightly image for main `c50aca144` + this diff: - Bitwise check (one-off, not added to CI per review): on one GPU with a small MXFP4 layer, buffers with 1920- and 15360-token capacity give `torch.equal` outputs at 1, 7, 48, 500 and 1920 tokens; 1921 tokens is rejected. - `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_sequence_parallel.py`: 132 passed. - `pre-commit`: pass. ## Details - **Why it is safe:** DeepGEMM sizes every region from `num_max_tokens_per_rank`. Its expert ring assumes every EP rank sends its full `num_max_tokens_per_rank`, so routing imbalance fits. With sequence parallelism each rank's MoE input is its shard, at most `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, tp_size)` rows at any DP size. The DeepGEMM warmup already uses this bound, and `forward()` raises above it. - **Why outputs match:** DeepGEMM picks `BLOCK_M` from the token count, not from the buffer capacity. - **Scope:** `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts` gets an optional `max_num_tokens` (default unchanged); only `KimiMoE` passes the shard bound. DeepSeek-V4 has the same sequence-parallel MegaMoE path and is left for a follow-up. - **Not validated end-to-end yet:** no `vllm serve` run of Kimi K3 with this change, and no KV-cache measurement. - **Not a duplicate:** no open PR changes the token bound of this buffer. Draft #53556 adds fused shared-expert space to the same buffer. #54347 enables Kimi K3 sequence parallelism with PP, where this bound also holds. - **AI assistance:** Claude Code drafted the code and description, and ran the measurements and checks above at my direction. ---

title: [Bugfix] Keep MRV2 model state in the runtime pool under sleep mode
author: xinyuangui2
body:
## Overview Build the Model Runner V2 model state in the `runtime` cuMem pool when sleep mode is on, so its device tensors survive level-2 sleep. Same approach as the LoRA state in #62358. #60009 lists Qwen4Exp `ngram_context_offsets` as out of its scope ("held by non-module objects"); this covers it. ## Claims - **Bug fix:** after `sleep(level=2)` + `wake_up()`, Qwen4Exp's `ngram_context_offsets` (a constant `arange(-ngram_context_len, 0)` on `Qwen4ExpModelState`) comes back as garbage (zeros in practice). Every later PLE n-gram context is wrong, so outputs are corrupted even when the weights are reloaded bit-exact. With this change it survives. - **Scope:** every MRV2 model state, not only Qwen4Exp: all of `init_model_state`'s device tensors move from the `weights` pool to the `runtime` pool. Only under `enable_sleep_mode` on CUDA/ROCm (XPU excluded: no nested pools, as in #62358). - **Cost:** level-2 sleep now copies the model state to host memory, as level 1 already did, instead of discarding it. These are per-request bookkeeping buffers (`max_num_reqs`-sized), plus `inputs_embeds` (`max_num_tokens x hidden`) for models that use it. - **Test:** `test_deep_sleep_model_state` checks that every model-state device tensor is allocated in the `runtime` pool and is unchanged after level-2 sleep + weights wake-up. ## Validation 4x H100 80GB, vLLM wheel for the base commit c9dbc926 (`0.32.1rc1.dev463+gc9dbc9263`, torch 2.14.0+cu130). Each arm swaps in that commit's `model_runner.py` (Python-only change); tests run from this branch's `tests/`. | Check | main (c9dbc926) | this PR | |---|---|---| | `test_deep_sleep_model_state` | **fails**: `AssertionError: {'num_accepted_tokens_gpu': 'weights'}` | passes | | `num_accepted_tokens_gpu` (Mamba2 tiny, MRV2) after `sleep(level=2)` + `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` | all 1s → **all 0s** | all 1s → all 1s | | `tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py` | — | 15 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only) | | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 4-layer slice, TP=4: `ngram_context_offsets` on all ranks, before → after sleep | `[-2, -1]` → **`[0, 0]`** | `[-2, -1]` → `[-2, -1]` (3/3 runs) | | Same: greedy output after sleep vs before (4 prompts, 64 tokens) | diverges at token 0–1, max \|Δlogprob\| 2.29 | same divergence patterns as a no-sleep control (below) | | `pre-commit` on the changed files (incl. mypy) | — | passed | ```bash VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py -k test_deep_sleep_model_state VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py ``` The Qwen3.8 repro uses `LLM(model, tensor_parallel_size=4, enable_sleep_mode=True, max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, disable_custom_all_reduce=True)`, then generate → `sleep(level=2)` → `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` → `collective_rpc("reload_weights")` → `wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])` → generate. The slice has random weights, so greedy TP=4 decoding is not run-to-run deterministic even without sleep. A no-sleep control (generate twice on one engine, 3 runs per arm) produces the same few late divergence patterns (none, or tokens 5–63) that this PR shows after sleep. On main, every prompt diverges at token 0–1. ## Details **Root cause:** `Worker.load_model` runs `GPUModelRunner.load_model` inside the `weights` pool. `init_model_state` runs there too, so the model state's tensors land in that pool. Level-2 sleep discards the `weights` pool, and wake-up restores only `model.named_buffers()` (and parameters, through the weight update). The model state belongs to the model runner, not the model, so registering its tensors as module buffers (the #60009 approach) does not apply. **Fix:** wrap `init_model_state` in `use_memory_pool(tag="runtime")` under sleep mode. Nested `use_memory_pool` calls restore the outer tag, so the weights pool around the rest of `load_model` is unaffected. Restoring from the pool keeps tensor addresses, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid. **Unrelated, seen while testing:** exiting while the KV cache is still asleep (level-2 sleep, weights-only wake) intermittently logs `CUDA Error: invalid argument at csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp:249` on main too (also with LoRA), from freeing the asleep KV-cache allocation; on CUDA, `_python_free_callback` unmaps asleep allocations. The new test wakes the KV cache before exiting. ---

title: [Spec Decode][Sampling] Batch-sharded draft logits
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
## Context
During batch-sharded sampling, the target logits are sharded along the token dimension. The requests are deterministically assigned to ranks using the formula: `req_state_idx % tp_size`. So during TP=4, rank 0 only samples (and in the case of spec decoding verifies) requests with state indices: 0, 4, 8, 12, ....

Currently, draft model-derived speculators allocate persistent draft logits tensors to hold all requests up to `max-num-seqs`, which is wasteful during batch-sharded sampling because only `max-num-seqs // TP` of those request logits are actually used by each rank. Sharding the draft logits can enable us to save GPU memory.

## This PR

Under batch-sharded sampling, each rank now allocates draft logits only for the requests it verifies. The draft logits cache shrinks from `max_num_seqs` rows to `cdiv(max_num_seqs, tp_size)` rows per rank, and the freed memory goes to the KV cache.

**Layout.** A request's draft logits live only on its owner rank, at row `req_state_idx // tp_size`. Two Triton helpers in `batch_shard.py` define the pair: `shard_owner` (`req_state_idx % num_shards`, the existing owner rule) and `shard_row` (`req_state_idx // num_shards`). Every write and read of the cache goes through them. With one shard both reduce to the current behavior and compile away.

**Writes.** Drafting stays replicated, so every rank still samples every draft token and no new collectives are added. Each rank writes only the rows it owns:
- `gumbel_sample` takes `logits_cache_num_shards` / `logits_cache_shard_idx` and masks its cache store to the owner rank. `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` and DSpark's `_sample_logits` pass them through.
- DFlash2's `_cache_draft_logits_kernel`, which writes only the top-k candidate columns, applies the same mask.

**Reads.** `RejectionSampler` takes `draft_logits_num_shards`, and the rejection kernels index draft logits with `shard_row(req_state_idx, DRAFT_LOGITS_NUM_SHARDS)`.

**Allocation.** The cache moves from `DraftModelSpeculator.__init__` to `load_model`, so it is allocated once at its final size after the target and draft models are loaded. It is sharded when all of these hold:
- batch-sharded sampling is active for the target (`batch_sharded_sampling_enabled`, a new helper that the model runner also uses to create the `BatchSharder`),
- the speculator opts in via `supports_batch_sharded_draft_logits()`,
- no draft watermarker is configured.

The model runner passes `speculator.draft_logits_num_shards` to the `RejectionSampler`. It also asserts that a custom rejection sampler never receives a sharded cache.

**Speculators that opt in:** every one whose cache writes honor the owner mask.
- `TargetDependentARSpeculator`: Eagle, MTP, Gemma4.
- `StandaloneARSpeculator` and `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`.
- `DFlashSpeculator`, and through it DSpark, XPress, DFlash2 and LiLiCorr.
- **Exception:** DSpark keeps the full cache when the draft model provides its own fused `sample_sequential` (the AMD DeepSeek-V4.1 path), because those kernels write the full-size cache.

**Memory freed per rank** (TP4, `max_num_seqs=256`, probabilistic drafts), from server startup logs:

| Target + draft | Draft logits cache, base → shard | KV cache memory, base → shard | KV cache tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=5) | 0.31 → 0.08 GiB | 74.44 → 74.67 GiB | +0.31% |
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP (K=3) | 0.36 → 0.09 GiB | 150.69 → 150.96 GiB | +0.18% |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash (K=7) | 0.83 → 0.21 GiB | 145.77 → 146.39 GiB | +0.43% |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 (K=7, fp32 cache) | 1.66 → 0.41 GiB | 147.07 → 148.31 GiB | +0.85% |

## Benchmarks

No regression in accuracy or acceptance rate for any speculator that now writes batch-sharded draft logits.

**Setup:** 4x GB200, TP4, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`, prefix caching off, natural EOS. Each pair ran 4 server boots in the order base, shard, shard, base. "base" is `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` off and "shard" is on. Startup logs confirmed every shard boot sharded the draft logits cache on all 4 ranks.

- **GSM8K:** `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions. t0 is temperature 0, one run per boot. t1 is temperature 1 with 3 seeds per boot, 6 runs per arm. The Qwen models use chat completions with thinking disabled.
- **SPEED-Bench:** `low_entropy` subset, `throughput_2k` config, concurrency 64, 256 prompts, temperature 1, top_p 1.
- **Acceptance length** = 1 + accepted / drafts, from the server's Prometheus metrics.
- Each cell shows the mean over the arm's runs.

### GSM8K accuracy

| Target + draft | K | t0 base | t0 shard | t1 base | t1 shard |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark | 5 | 0.907 | 0.906 | 0.816 | 0.807 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP | 3 | 0.969 | 0.970 | 0.968 | 0.967 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash | 7 | 0.970 | 0.970 | 0.966 | 0.966 |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 | 7 | 0.964 | 0.961 | 0.960 | 0.960 |

### Acceptance length

| Target + draft | GSM8K t0 base | GSM8K t0 shard | GSM8K t1 base | GSM8K t1 shard | SPEED-Bench base | SPEED-Bench shard |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark | 3.554 | 3.540 | 3.275 | 3.283 | 3.546 | 3.556 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP | 3.617 | 3.619 | 3.519 | 3.515 | 3.258 | 3.271 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash | 5.499 | 5.490 | 4.980 | 4.984 | 3.905 | 3.927 |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 | 6.164 | 6.152 | 5.876 | 5.890 | 3.636 | 3.647 |

### SPEED-Bench noise check (Qwen3.6-27B + MTP)

Every pair read 0.3–0.6% higher acceptance on SPEED-Bench with sharding. To check whether that was real, I ran a third arm that shards verification but keeps the draft logits cache replicated. I ran each arm with top-k on and off, with 2 boots per arm.

| Arm | top_k=20 (model default) | top_k disabled |
|---|---|---|
| base | 3.266 | 3.268 |
| sharded verification, replicated draft logits | 3.263 | 3.262 |
| sharded verification, sharded draft logits | 3.263 | 3.261 |

The three arms match. Base alone ranged from 3.254 to 3.279 across boots, so the shift is boot-to-boot noise.

### Notes

- **DFlash2 GSM8K t0, 0.964 → 0.961:** a 4-question difference. At temperature 0, verification compares against the target argmax and never reads cached draft logits, so this can't come from this change.
- **DSV4.1 GSM8K t1, 0.816 → 0.807:** not significant (Welch p≈0.3). This model's t1 accuracy varies a lot from seed to seed (0.78–0.83).

title: [CI][ROCm] Take NIXL PD accuracy side-channel ports from below the ephemeral range
author: AndreasKaratzas
body: - `rocm_pd_accuracy_utils.py`: take each server's `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT` from below the kernel's ephemeral range instead of from `get_open_port()` `test_rocm_pd_accuracy[nixl-aiter-deepseek-p1-d1]` failed in [amd-ci 15356](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15356/list?sid=01a1707d-94ec-44ea-af1c-5245434b7339&tab=output): the decode server's `nixl_handshake_listener` hit `ZMQError: Address already in use (tcp://localhost:55235)`, and the server then waited out its startup timeout. The test has picked the side-channel port with `get_open_port()` since #58095, and NIXL only binds `side_channel_port + data_parallel_index` after the model loads, so for ~30 s the released port sits in the ephemeral range where any other `bind(0)` can be given it. This group otherwise passed 6/6 params in every nightly and weekly build from 14934 to 15350, so it is a rare race (about 1 in ~300 param runs) rather than a regression. Ports below `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` are never handed out by `bind(0)` or `connect()`, the same approach as #63453 for MoRIIO. Separately, a dead handshake listener leaves the server neither failing nor healthy; that is a product issue for a follow-up. The full CI file passes with this change on MI350X (6 passed; GSM8K 0.412-0.424 for Qwen, 0.195-0.202 for DeepSeek, in line with 15356's passing params). title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Pin a shared-prefix junction when a sparse group cuts the offload hit
author: KaloyanNaumov
body:
## Overview Fixes #63565. On hybrid models with sparse retention (the default), a prefix that lives only in the CPU offload tier is never reused by a request that diverges before the single stored Mamba/sliding-window state. The offload lookup now pins a shared-prefix junction there, as the local prefix cache already does, so the prefix heals after one miss. ## Claims - A revisit that shares a prefix but diverges inside the prompt's last block hits the offload tier from the second revisit on (today: never). - No change when every group hits, when no full-attention group proves a hit, under dense retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=None`), or for models without a sliding-window/Mamba group. - A junction set by the local prefix cache is never lowered. ## Validation CPU (x86, torch 2.14.0+cpu, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`): ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k junction # main: test_sparse_group_miss_registers_shared_prefix_junction FAILED assert 0 == 16; 2 passed # this PR: 3 passed pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_offload \ tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py # this PR: 86 failed / 1,740 passed / 24 skipped (the same 86 fail on main) ``` The 86 failures are the same on main and are environmental on a CPU-only host: 32 in `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py` (copies through a GPU) and 54 EC-connector cases in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` (a multimodal model config is not available there). `pre-commit run --files `: all hooks pass. GPU (4 × Intel Arc Pro B70, torch 2.14.0+xpu, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.15.4): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B BF16, TP 4, `--enforce-eager --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 16 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, 576-token blocks, GPU KV cache capped at 66K tokens (`--kv-cache-memory`) so that filler requests evict the documents from the GPU prefix cache. Serial requests. Six ~16.1K-token documents, three whose question starts inside the block that holds the stored GDN state (in-band) and three whose question starts after it (out-of-band); each is read with question A, then revisited with question B and question C, with six 16K-token fillers before each revisit. GPU prefix-cache hits were 0 on every revisit. | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | in-band, revisit B | 0/3 offload hits, TTFT 1.49 s | 0/3, TTFT 1.49 s (one more GDN state stored: 0.15 vs 0.09 GB) | | in-band, revisit C | 0/3, TTFT 1.50 s | 3/3, 15,552 of ~16,140 tokens from the offload tier, TTFT 0.30 s | | out-of-band, B and C | 3/3, 3/3 | 3/3, 3/3 | Same documents and questions in both runs (fixed seed). The greedy answers of the three healed in-band hits equal main's answers to the same prompts, which main computed without a hit. ## Details Under sparse retention each request keeps one sparse-group checkpoint, in the last block of its prompt. A later request that shares the prefix but diverges before that block finds its full-attention chunks in the offload tier but no Mamba state at or below them, so `_lookup_complete_chunks` returns 0 for the whole request. The local prefix cache handles the same geometry by returning a shared-prefix junction from `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks` (`kv_cache_manager.py:318-326`); the recompute then retains the sparse state there. The offload lookup never set one, so once the prefix had left the GPU cache every recompute stored its state inside the differing suffix again. Change (`offloading/scheduler.py`): - `_lookup_complete_chunks` records, in `RequestOffloadState.full_attention_hit_boundary`, the boundary the full-attention groups proved before the first sliding-window/Mamba group narrowed it (not on a deferred lookup). - `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, when the final hit is shorter than that boundary and retention is sparse, raises `request.shared_prefix_boundary` to it. No core change is needed: the scheduler sets the local junction before it calls the connector (`sched/scheduler.py:1077-1089`), and everything downstream reads the request field: the align split stops a chunk there (`sched/scheduler.py:610`), `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` retains it (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:511-518`), and the aligned-boundary hand-off stores it to the offload tier. Limits: the first revisit still misses (a first-visit hit needs a state retained below the replay boundary, which is the subject of #57613). Connectors that set `hit_diverged` and load nothing re-read the local junction (`sched/scheduler.py:1162-1172`) and can overwrite this one; the plain `OffloadingConnector` does not take that path. If #62278 (junction as a tuple of positions) merges first, this needs a small rebase to add the junction to `shared_prefix_boundaries`. Why this is not a duplicate: searched on 2026-10-24 for "shared_prefix_boundary", "junction", "offload shared_prefix_boundary", "offloading mamba junction" and "OffloadingConnector hybrid". #45238 is the GPU-cache form of this geometry (main has the GPU junction, #47782 / #37898); #57613 retains a block below sliding-window replay boundaries (first visit, different mechanism); #59146 keeps the prompt-end checkpoint; #56795 is a different offload-store bug; #52774 backfills GPU-local divergent hits only; #62400 adds junctions to the MooncakeStore connector; #63221 changes the connector load boundary under EAGLE. None sets a junction from the `OffloadingConnector` lookup. AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write the change and the tests, and draft this text. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above. ---

title: [Benchmark] Add PCP support to vllm bench forward
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview Add prefill context parallelism (PCP) support to `vllm bench forward`, including PCP with expert parallelism and decode context parallelism. ## Claims - Validate requested batch shapes against the global batch and inject the correct token slices into each rank's split or replicated request rows. - Account for PCP workers in balanced MoE routing fixtures and report local batch sizes/order in per-rank results. - Document PCP usage and the distinction between full-forward graph timing and serving latency. ## Validation - Seven CPU tests passed in `tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py` (all tests except the existing single-GPU model test). The new two-rank parameterized regression checks split prefill slices with a continued prefix, replicated decode inputs, and untouched padding. This file runs in the existing Benchmarks CLI Buildkite job. - All pre-commit hooks passed on the four changed files. - Before the change, the four-GPU CLI reproducer fails in `_check_batch` with `AssertionError: ['bench-0', 'bench-0']`. With the change, uneven prefill, mixed prefill/decode, and decode cases complete. - On four GB200 GPUs, GLM-5.2 NVFP4 with dummy weights was exercised with PCP4/EP4, PCP2/TP2/EP4, and PCP2/TP2/DCP2/EP4. DCP used `ag_rs`, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, and `fp8_ds_mla`. Real and balanced synthetic routing were exercised; full-model timing was compared with `vllm serve`. - Real `nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4` weights were also tested with PCP4/EP4, normal routing, and both TRTLLM and NVFP4 MegaMoE backends: | MoE backend | Prompt tokens | Forward graph (ms) | Serving TTFT (ms) | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `flashinfer_trtllm` | 1,024 | 50.708 | 94.067 | | `flashinfer_trtllm` | 8,192 | 163.816 | 174.005 | | `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | 1,024 | 58.483 | 95.870 | | `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | 8,192 | 153.638 | 160.496 | These are functionality/timing checks, not speedup claims for the patch. Forward timing used 10 replays × 3 samples; MegaMoE sample spread was 0.14% / 0.49% for 1K / 8K. TTFT is the median of 10 serial requests after four warmups. Both paths used identical README-derived prompt IDs, disabled FlashInfer autotuning, and real routing; serving used `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, while the benchmark captures the full forward. Kernel traces confirmed the selected MoE implementations. Outputs were finite. The real-weight 1K graph/eager comparison was exact; the 8K case showed variability even between eager repeats, so these results do **not** establish 8K numerical parity or task-level accuracy. No inference/model implementation is changed.
Reproduction commands ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \ -k 'not test_bench_forward' -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py::test_bench_forward_rejects_oversized_verify -q # Four-layer functional smoke; MODEL is a local GLM-5.2 NVFP4 config/tokenizer. .venv/bin/torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \ --model "$MODEL" --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers":4}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune false \ --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 --kv-len-jitter 0 \ --case uneven=1025 --case mix=513@2048c,3*1@2048 --case decode=4*1@2048 \ --iters 3 --samples 2 --output-json /tmp/forward-pcp-smoke.json ``` The performance table comes from the earlier full-model experiments in this work, rather than the reduced-layer smoke command above.
## Details PCP can represent one global request with two disjoint local rows. Previously the benchmark required unique local request IDs and copied the entire query for every row. It now checks the global batch contract and derives each local token slice from its computed-token offset and scheduled-token count. Balanced routing includes PCP in the EP world size and reserves capacity for gathered PCP rows without EP. Duplicate-work checks found no open PCP/forward benchmark PR or matching issue. #62300 addresses CUPTI profiling and is separate from this change. No issue number was supplied. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and PR preparation. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] hadacore: fix skipped wait_group on partial-chunk warp for odd row counts (#63514)
author: bandham-manikanta
body:
Fixes #63514

### Problem
When using INT4 per-token-head KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head`), `reshape_and_cache_int4` rotates Key and Value tensors via `hadacore_transform`. 

For `head_dim = 256`, `num_chunks` is 2. When the row count (`num_tokens * num_kv_heads_per_rank`) is odd, the last warp receives only 1 chunk (`real_num_chunks = 1`).

`diff_num_chunks` was calculated as:
```cpp
int64_t diff_num_chunks = real_num_chunks - num_chunks; // 1 - 2 = -1
```
Because `diff_num_chunks` was negative, `switch(k + diff_num_chunks)` evaluated to `-1`. Since the switch statement only contains `case 0..31` and had no `default:` fallback, it silently skipped `cp.async.wait_group` completely. 

The warp proceeded to read shared memory before the asynchronous DMA copy completed, causing:
1. Silent data corruption (relative errors up to 10^36).
2. Intermittent `CUDA illegal memory access` crashes during prefill.

### Fix
1. Correct the difference to `num_chunks - real_num_chunks` so `k + diff_num_chunks` maps to the intended wait barrier count (`wait_group 0` for the single tail chunk).
2. Add `default: asm volatile("cp.async.wait_group 0;\n"); break;` so an unhandled case can never silently skip synchronization.
3. Add parameterized unit test in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_hadacore.py` covering odd and large row counts (`num_rows in [1, 17, 53, 65, 165, 173, 257, 513, 1025, 4097, 8193]`).

### Validation
Verified on NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB:
- **Full range test (`N = 1` to `512`):**
  - Unpatched `main` (`2c880f1e`): 39 failing row counts (all odd), errors up to 10^36.
  - With this fix: **0 failures out of 512** (100% bit-exact match against float64 reference).
- Tested small (`N <= 128`), medium (`128 < N <= 513`), and large (`1024 <= N <= 8193`) shapes across both odd and even counts.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction Script</summary>

```python
import math
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops

D = 256
H = torch.ones(1, 1, dtype=torch.float64, device="cuda")
while H.shape[0] < D:
    H = torch.cat([torch.cat([H, H], 1), torch.cat([H, -H], 1)], 0)
H = H / math.sqrt(D)

bad = []
for n in range(1, 513):
    torch.manual_seed(n)
    x = torch.randn(n, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    y = ops.hadacore_transform(x.clone(), inplace=True)
    ref = (x.double() @ H).to(torch.bfloat16)

    rel_err = ((y.double() - ref.double()).abs().max() / ref.double().abs().max()).item()
    if rel_err > 2e-2:
        bad.append((n, f"{rel_err:.2e}"))

print(f"Tested 1..512 row counts: {len(bad)} failures")
if bad:
    print("Sample failing counts:", bad[:10])
```
</details>

title: [Benchmark] Add steady-state PP support to bench forward
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview Add pipeline parallelism to `vllm bench forward`, measuring a microbatch's full-pipeline forward latency under steady-state load from identical microbatches. Builds on the merged PCP support in #63613. ## Claims - Includes PP transfers and waits between the first stage's forward start and the last stage's forward completion; excludes pipeline fill/drain, input preparation before the forward, and sampling. - Captures each stage's forward in a CUDA graph and streams matching microbatches without a per-step host barrier. Reports stage timelines and estimated cross-rank clock uncertainty. - Adds rendered CLI documentation and a two-GPU CLI/profiler regression test wired into the existing distributed CI job. ## Validation Full 93-layer Kimi K3 with dummy MXFP4 weights on **4 nodes × 4 GB200 GPUs**. Balanced routing, 8,192 query tokens per microbatch, EP enabled. PP2 uses TP8/EP8; PP4 uses TP4/EP4. Kimi currently disables SP with PP. Median full-pipeline GPU latency (ms): | PP | Prefill | TRT-LLM bench | TRT-LLM serving | MegaMoE bench | MegaMoE serving | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 8 × 1K | 338.3 | 339.3 | 525.4 | 525.8 | | 2 | 1 × 8K | 357.1 | 357.9 | 517.6 | 518.1 | | 4 | 8 × 1K | 490.7 | 491.6 | 645.7 | 646.9 | | 4 | 1 × 8K | 507.3 | 505.5 | 637.8 | 637.2 | Serving measurements match request IDs across stages and use the same first/last GPU-event boundaries; these are not TTFT or Prometheus prefill histogram values. Serving uses piecewise graphs. All differences are within 0.35%. Benchmark-only KV restoration is outside stage compute timing but can affect pipeline cadence. Each benchmark case has 100 measured microbatches (5 × 20), trimming 4 × PP microbatches at each end. Final-run sample-median spread was below 1%; estimated cross-rank clock uncertainty was about 0.18–0.21 ms. All intermediate and final benchmark outputs were finite and matched the eager pipeline reference exactly. These dummy-weight checks validate execution and timing, not model quality. Both MoE backends use MXFP8 × MXFP4. MegaMoE's additional cost here includes replicated token dispatch with SP disabled; this PR does not change the model or MoE implementation.
Commands and regression evidence Full CLI suite before the final aggregation/profiling cleanup: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -v # 9 passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ .buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml docs/cli/README.md docs/benchmarking/cli.md \ tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py \ vllm/benchmarks/forward/pipeline.py # All applicable hooks passed ``` After the cleanup, reran the real two-GPU CLI/profiler test: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py::test_bench_forward_pipeline -v # 1 passed ``` The CPU aggregation reproduces all 100 saved latency samples exactly for each of the eight Kimi/backend/layout/shape cases. Final pre-commit checks also pass. The cleanup removes a redundant GPU reduction after gathering timelines, skips clock calibration and timing events in the profiling pass, and removes duplicate checks; the timed transfers and graph replay order are unchanged. Before the implementation, the new test was copied into an isolated worktree at `dbbb4f73de` (PCP branch tip) and run there with the same environment: ```bash PYTHONPATH=/tmp/vllm-forward-pp-base \ /home/woosuk/workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py::test_bench_forward_pipeline -v # FAILED: Value error, Model Runner V2 does not yet support: # pipeline parallelism with external_launcher ``` Benchmark command, run on each node (set `PP=2` or `4`, and the torchrun rendezvous variables): ```bash VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip .venv/bin/torchrun \ --nnodes=4 --nproc-per-node=4 --node-rank="$NODE_RANK" \ --master-addr="$MASTER_ADDR" --master-port=29641 \ -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \ --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy \ --pipeline-parallel-size "$PP" --tensor-parallel-size "$((16 / PP))" \ --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 9216 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune false \ --routing balanced --kv-len-jitter 0 \ --case 'prefill8x1k=8*1024' --case prefill1x8k=8192 \ --iters 20 --samples 5 --output-json results.json ``` For MegaMoE, add `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`. Model config/tokenizer revision: `f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06`. Serving used the same layouts, model, routing fixture and input tokens, with prefix caching and FlashInfer autotuning disabled, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=16*PP`, and `{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[8192]}`. A diagnostic worker recorded CUDA events around real stage forwards, without per-step synchronization. The client sent 100 groups of eight 1K requests, then 100 8K requests, all with one output token; analysis selected exact-shape microbatches and discarded fill/drain. Backend class and precision were checked on all 16 ranks for MegaMoE.
## Details The implementation is isolated to the benchmark. A benchmark-specific external-launcher executor enables stage loading; the benchmark drives the runners directly, without serving schedulers or sampling broadcasts. It reuses runner input preparation, forward context, KV-state handling, and PP/TP transfer conventions. Cross-device CUDA events cannot be subtracted directly. Pre/post calibration correlates each GPU's timeline to rank zero's monotonic clock using CPU ping-pong and host/GPU event bracketing. The benchmark reports the earliest first-stage TP start to latest last-stage TP completion for each microbatch, with the calibration uncertainty retained in JSON. This adds code compared with timing isolated stages, but is needed to measure pipeline traversal while other stages remain occupied. The full-model validation covers prefill with PP+TP+EP. Decode and combinations with PCP/DCP are not covered by these full-model runs. No serving/model code or non-PP benchmark behavior is changed. Duplicate check: searched open PRs for `"bench forward"`, pipeline benchmarking, PCP/PP benchmarking, and references to #63613. No open PR implements this feature. #62300 fixes profiling in the existing forward path and is separate from PP support. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and this description. Human review of the final diff remains required before marking the draft ready. ---

title: [Benchmark] Include speculative drafting in bench forward
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview Include the configured MTP, EAGLE, DSpark, or DFlash drafter in `vllm bench forward` timing by default. Add `--exclude-drafter` for target-only timing. This follows the PP support merged in #63616 and is rebased onto `main`. Open-PR searches for `bench forward` and speculative drafting found no duplicate; the existing speculator CUDA-graph work concerns serving, not this benchmark entry point. ## Claims - Capture the target forward and real draft proposal, including draft sampling, in the timed CUDA graph. Assume all draft tokens are accepted, with a fixed bonus token; exclude target sampling, rejection sampling, and CPU overhead. - Reserve draft KV lookahead and restore KV, slot mappings, and block tables for repeatable replays. PP runs the drafter on the last stage. - Report the timing scope and graph/eager draft-token agreement in JSON; document the default and exclusion option. ## Validation GB200, dummy weights, greedy drafting: - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k 'drafter and METHOD' -q`, separately for `mtp`, `eagle3`, `dspark`, and `dflash`: **4 passed**. Each checks verification, prefill, and mixed batches with drafting included and excluded (24 cases). - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k 'pcp_query or build_batch or jitter or oversized_verify or profile_summary' -q`: **7 passed**. - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py::test_bench_forward -q`: **1 passed**, including kernel profiling. - All pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and CI test-wiring checks. The benchmark CI job selects the new parametrized test. - Before-change check: copied the new EAGLE3 test to base `97135395dd` and ran `-k 'drafter and eagle3'`; it failed with `KeyError: 'timing_scope'`. The same test passes on this branch. Additional full-model CLI checks used `verify=4*4@128:3` and `prefill=128`, three draft tokens, `--iters 3 --samples 2`. All target outputs and draft token IDs matched eager execution exactly: | Target / drafter | Configuration | | --- | --- | | MiMo-7B-Base / MTP | Single GPU | | Qwen3-1.7B / AngelSlim EAGLE3 | Single GPU, PP=2, DP=2 (DP also checked a mixed batch) | | Qwen3-8B / z-lab DFlash | Single GPU | | Qwen3-8B / Qwen3 DSpark | Single GPU; synthetic DSpark config using the DFlash backbone and a Markov head | | Reduced DeepSeek-V3.2 / MTP | PCP=2, FLASHMLA_SPARSE, fp8_ds_mla; verification, prefill, and mixed batches | For example, EAGLE3 verification measured 2.393 ms including drafting versus 1.534 ms with `--exclude-drafter`; prefill measured 2.553 ms versus 1.875 ms. These validate the timing scope, not a serving speedup. ```bash vllm bench forward --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B \ --speculative-config '{"model":"AngelSlim/Qwen3-1.7B_eagle3","method":"eagle3","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \ --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 \ --case verify=4*4@128:3 --case prefill=128 --iters 3 --samples 2 # Repeat with --exclude-drafter for target-only timing. # For PP/DP, launch two workers with torchrun and add -pp 2 / -dp 2. ``` Additional DSV4.1-Flash validation used the full cached `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` checkpoint (revision `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`), including its three-layer DSpark and Engram tables, on 4 GB200 GPUs with TP=4, EP=4, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, FP8 KV, and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41`. Both dummy and real weights completed verification, prefill, and mixed workloads. Five draft tokens were accepted; target sampling remains excluded. The trace has 43 MegaMoE calls with drafting and 40 without. Real-weight CUDA graph timing (3 samples × 10 replays, maximum rank time): | Case | Target + DSpark | Target only | Draft tokens match eager | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | verify1 | 7.086 ms | 6.230 ms | No | | verify16 | 12.240 ms | 11.107 ms | Yes | | prefill1k | 22.983 ms | 22.016 ms | Yes | | prefill8k | 94.595 ms | 92.537 ms | No | | mixed | 25.932 ms | 23.915 ms | No | **This is not a clean numerical validation of DSV4.1.** All ranks produced finite outputs and valid draft IDs; the 16-request verification case matched target and draft eager outputs exactly. However, single-request verification had a 0.985 target graph/eager relative RMS difference, and prefill varied even between eager repeats (about 0.09 at 1K and 0.15 at 8K). The target-only control reproduced these discrepancies. The drafter integration does not introduce the observed target discrepancy, but its underlying cause is not fully resolved. Real-weight sample-median spread with drafting was 0.21–1.36%; these timings establish execution scope, not serving performance or model accuracy. ```bash torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \ --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --load-format auto --routing real \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \ --language-model-only \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --kernel-config.enable_jit_warmup false --kernel-config.enable_cutedsl_warmup false \ --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --kv-len-jitter 0 \ --case verify1=6@8192:5 --case 'verify16=16*6@8192:5' \ --case prefill1k=1024 --case prefill8k=8192 --case 'mixed=1024,8*6@8192:5' \ --iters 10 --samples 3 --output-json results.json --profile-dir profiles # Repeat with --exclude-drafter. ``` A separate dummy-weight diagnostic disabled `supports_mhc_overlap` outside the repository: single-request target verification became bit-exact between graph and eager, while 1K prefill still varied. This isolates the small-batch discrepancy to the model’s capture-specific mHC path; the prefill discrepancy remains unresolved. No model code or correctness tolerances were changed. Additional parallel-layout checks used the same real DSV4.1-Flash checkpoint, DSpark configuration, MegaMoE backend, and four GB200 GPUs: - **DEP=4 (DP=4, TP=1, EP=4):** all five cases completed with finite target outputs and valid draft IDs on every rank. The 16-request verification case matched target and draft eager outputs exactly on every rank. Single-request verification and prefill retain the target numerical discrepancies described above; the target-only DEP control reproduces them. Prefill draft agreement varies by rank. - **PP=2, TP=2, EP=2:** model initialization fails with `ValueError: DeepseekV41ForCausalLM does not support dspark with pipeline parallelism`. The shared runner requires `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp`, which this model does not implement. This is an underlying model/speculator restriction; no guard was bypassed and no PP timing is claimed for DSV4.1 + DSpark. The Qwen3/EAGLE3 PP checks above remain the PP coverage for this PR. DEP timing with drafting included (3 samples × 10 replays; each workload is **per DP rank**, with four replicas active): | Per-rank case | Target + DSpark | | --- | ---: | | verify1 | 9.655 ms | | verify16 | 16.351 ms | | prefill1k | 29.473 ms | | prefill8k | 121.820 ms | | mixed | 32.108 ms | Repeat the DSV4.1 command above with `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4` for DEP, or `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2` to reproduce the PP restriction. Included-drafter DEP sample-median spread was 0.18–1.42%. The first target-only control had a mixed-case timing outlier (114.238 ms, 18.71% sample-median spread); its trace showed large Engram lookup and elementwise times. Do not infer drafter overhead from that run. Repeated target-only control (5 samples × 20 replays): | Per-rank case | Target only | Sample-median spread | | --- | ---: | ---: | | verify1 | 8.623 ms | 2.19% | | verify16 | 15.083 ms | 1.68% | | prefill1k | 28.555 ms | 0.40% | | prefill8k | 122.050 ms | 1.35% | | mixed | 30.928 ms | 0.73% | The mixed-case outlier did not recur (30.928 ms on repeat). At 8K, included/excluded timing differences are within variability, so these runs do not resolve drafter overhead. Numerical discrepancies persisted in both target-only controls. No serving/model implementation changes were made. GLM5.3-NVFP4 supplies additional real-weight MTP + PP coverage. On four GB200 GPUs, PP=2 / TP=2 / EP=2 with `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=42,36`, three accepted draft tokens, FlashMLA sparse attention and FP8 MLA KV passed exact target graph/eager, full-pipeline/eager, and draft-token agreement for single-request verification, 16-request verification, 1K prefill, and the mixed batch. All outputs were finite. The checkpoint is `nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, revision `e3b8f9f2fad29727dfa95e766c5cac18ea1414bf`; it contains a BF16 MTP layer. Automatic backend selection uses TRTLLM NVFP4 target MoE and BF16 MTP MoE, not NVFP4 MegaMoE. Traces confirm three MTP forwards on the last stage. | GLM case | Including MTP | Target only | Included / excluded sample spread | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1K prefill | 66.845 ms | 63.538 ms | 0.049% / 0.087% | | Mixed: 1K prefill + 8 verification requests | 72.095 ms | 68.505 ms | 0.047% / 0.083% | Each timing uses 3 samples of 10 steady-window microbatches; eight fill and eight drain microbatches are excluded. Both cases show stage 1 overlapping stage 0's next microbatch for all 30 measured microbatches. Clock-correlation uncertainty was at most 0.179 ms. Included/excluded cases were run through the existing `run_case` in the same loaded-model session, with garbage collection disabled during execution and performed between cases. An initial paired attempt failed when old CUDA graphs were collected during a new capture; per-case results from the successful rerun were saved separately. Limits exposed by this check: - The default 39/39 split starts the second stage inside a shared sparse-index group and fails verification graph/eager agreement even without MTP. Starting that stage at index-producing layer 42 fixes the verification and mixed-case disagreements without changing model code. - 8K prefill still has a target graph/eager discrepancy (maximum relative RMS about 0.323 across ranks), also present in the target-only control. Similar 8K disagreement was present in the earlier real-weight GLM PCP run. It is not counted as clean correctness coverage. - Verification outputs are exact with 42/36, but its included-MTP pipeline latency grows as the faster first stage queues work ahead of the last stage (49–55% sample spread). Those medians are **not** valid steady-state latency estimates. Bounded in-flight work/backpressure remains a PP benchmark issue; this PR does not fix it. Reproduction uses the benchmark CLI with `--model nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --load-format safetensors --routing real --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=42,36`, and cases `verify1=4@8192:3`, `verify16=16*4@8192:3`, `prefill1k=1024`, `prefill8k=8192`, `mixed=1024,8*4@8192:3`. Use max model length 16384, max batched tokens 8192, GPU memory utilization 0.8, KV jitter 0, 10 iterations and 3 samples; disable FlashInfer autotune and kernel JIT/CuTeDSL warmup. Repeat with `--exclude-drafter` for target-only execution. ## Details The benchmark calls the existing speculator `propose` interface rather than duplicating drafting implementations. Serving and model implementations are unchanged; accuracy evaluation is not applicable to this synthetic timing fixture. Balanced MoE routing still applies only to the target, so representative MoE drafter timing requires real weights. AI assistance was used to implement and validate this change. Documentation discovery was checked locally, on the GitHub branch, and through web access; search indexes still show the pre-merge documentation. ---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Roll back failed P2P NIXL registration
author: Levius-Fubuki
body:
## Overview Roll back a newly registered NIXL agent when descriptor preparation fails in the P2P KV-offload transport. Related to #63602, gap 4 only. AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for investigation, implementation, tests, and this description. The human submitter confirmed completion of manual review and authorized submission. The reviewed contribution carries their DCO sign-off. Original-submission results below are the recorded server runs; review follow-up results are the recorded local runs. No additional human test execution is asserted. ## Claims - A failure in `get_xfer_descs` or `prep_xfer_dlist` rolls back the unpublished remote registration. - A failed repeat using already-published native metadata leaves that registration owned by its existing peer. - Cleanup failure is logged without replacing the original registration exception. Native cleanup success cannot be guaranteed when NIXL itself rejects removal. ## Validation The table and native validation below describe the original submission, `18349008c`; follow-up results are recorded separately below. Base: `a7407ab44557802ca32a0ba2c2707362d7d21563`. | Check | Base | Changed | | --- | --- | --- | | Eight new constructor-based cases | 6 failed, 2 passed | 8 passed | | Complete data-transport file | Not measured | 64 passed | | Data transport, sessions, ZMQ transport | Not measured | 223 passed | | Full P2P suite, including manager | Not measured | 319 passed | | Native NIXL 1.5.0 DRAM/UCX reproducer | Metadata survives descriptor failure | Rollback succeeds; 6 real WRITE byte comparisons pass | | Applicable pre-commit hooks | Not measured | Passed, including pinned Ruff, mypy, and test tethering | ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_zmq_transport.py -q .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/data/nixl.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py ``` Tests construct the real `NixlTransport`; only the external NIXL boundary is mocked. Native validation uses the production transport with two real NIXL agents, host buffers, UCX TCP/shared memory/CUDA-copy, injected descriptor failures, native metadata queries, retries, and exact byte comparisons. Both descriptor stages and an idempotent repeat are checked. This source-level Python validation used Python 3.12.3 and the server's existing torch 2.12.1+cu130. It did not build main's torch 2.14 native extensions. The command excludes the heavyweight root `tests/conftest.py`, and uses the P2P suite's real conftest. No LLM/OpenAI serving run, output-quality evaluation, or RDMA/multi-node fault injection was performed; those are not implied by the transport results. ## Review follow-up — sync registration Commit `6ed41ccf1b` routes `add_remote_peer()` through `add_remote_peer_async(...).result()`, so synchronous and asynchronous builds share the single registration worker. Superseded synchronous registrations now raise, and the rollback check documents its serialization requirement. Validation of this follow-up used macOS/Python 3.12 with the real `NixlTransport` constructor and a mocked external NIXL boundary: | Check | Original PR `18349008c` | With follow-up | | --- | --- | --- | | Race regression plus sync/async superseded-registration cases | 2 failed, 1 passed | 3 passed within the full suite | | Complete data-transport file | 64 passed before adding the regressions | 66 passed | | Full P2P suite | Previously recorded server result: 319 passed | 321 passed | | Applicable pre-commit hooks | Previously passed | Passed, including pinned Ruff, mypy, and test tethering | The before-fix failures were `assert set() == {'peer'}` (the newer registration's agent was removed) and `Failed: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError` (superseded sync registration returned silently). ```bash # With the final tests and original nixl.py from 18349008c: .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py \ -k 'failed_registration_keeps_newer_sync_agent or registration_landing_after_remove_is_discarded' -q # 2 failed, 1 passed, 63 deselected # With the follow-up: .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p -q # 321 passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/data/nixl.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py # All applicable hooks passed ``` Both baseline and changed runs emit the same missing generated `vllm._version` warning. No new native-NIXL/RDMA or serving validation is claimed for this follow-up. The already-existing dlist replacement leak remains outside this PR. ## Details The registration worker can register native metadata and then fail before `_publish_peer` records cleanup ownership. `_build_peer_handles` now uses the existing independent teardown helper on that exception path, while preserving the exception and avoiding removal of an already-published native name. All registration builds now use the existing single-worker executor, including the synchronous entry point; the generation/publish flow is unchanged. No steady-state inference work, synchronization, public option, or model arithmetic is added. Duplicate checks covered the issue discussion, open PRs referencing #63602, and P2P/NIXL rollback keywords. #59524 fixes incomplete registration in the separate KV connector `nixl/base_worker.py`; this change fixes the P2P secondary-tier transport. #61667 covers consumer-slot quarantine for unconfirmed writes. Contributor `tejachavali` expressed interest in the broader issue; this PR does not claim assignment or close the full issue. The existing Buildkite `v1-kv-offload` step selects the data-transport tests via `pytest -v -s v1/kv_offload`, and its source dependencies include `vllm/v1/` and `tests/v1/kv_offload`. ---

title: [Perf][MRV2] Stage buffer contents by reference and copy straight into UVA
author: njhill
body:
## Overview Builds on #63210 (typed-array staging in `StagedWriteTensor`), which is the first commit here. Only the last commit belongs to this PR. That commit stages numpy and `array.array` contents by reference, concatenates all staged contents straight into a UVA buffer slot, and has the write kernel read them through UVA for GPU-resident targets too. Ideas are taken from #59908 (@benenzhu) and #62702 (@Juntian777), who are credited as co-authors. ## Claims - On both GB200 and MI350X, `apply_write` is faster than main and than #63210 alone, in GPU time and in host time, across every shape measured. This includes the small block-table writes, where #63210 alone was slightly slower than main. - A numpy array or `array.array` is staged without a copy. For example, mrope positions or a 131k-token `array('i')` take about 65µs to stage and apply on GB200, against 4–13ms on main. - The write kernel reads staged contents through UVA for GPU-resident targets too, not only UVA targets. This removes the per-apply pinned allocation and `cudaMemcpyAsync`. Without pinned memory, the existing `NonUvaBuffer` fallback copies into a preallocated device buffer. - There is no new option. All existing callers get the same values in the same rows. ## Validation **Tests** (`tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py` and `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`): | Platform | GPUs visible | Runs | Result | |---|---|---|---| | GB200 | 2 | 3 | 50 passed, 4 skipped each | | MI350X, ROCm 7.2.2 | 1 | 4 | 25 passed, 22 skipped each | On ROCm, `test_gpu_block_table.py` is skipped as CUDA-only. **GPU time per `apply_write`**, in µs at p50 (p10–p90 in the notes below), int32 target resident on the GPU: | case | GB200 main | GB200 #63210 | GB200 this | MI350X main | MI350X #63210 | MI350X this | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | block table 256 × 1 | 19.1 | 10.9 | 6.8 | 12.5 | 12.4 | 6.5 | | block table 32 × 64 | 10.9 | 12.2 | 6.8 | 12.4 | 12.4 | 6.3 | | dense 1 × 8192 | 19.0 | 19.1 | 8.8 | 26.0 | 26.0 | 6.3 | | dense 8 × 8192 | 19.1 | 19.1 | 8.9 | 31.1 | 31.3 | 10.2 | | dense 1 × 131056 | 19.1 | 19.1 | 9.9 | 35.8 | 35.8 | 14.7 | **Host time per stage + apply**, in µs (median): | case | GB200 main | GB200 #63210 | GB200 this | MI350X main | MI350X #63210 | MI350X this | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | block table 256 × 1-int lists | 168 | 179 | 131 | 76 | 75 | 67 | | block table 32 × 64-int lists | 177 | 122 | 79 | 81 | 48 | 40 | | block table 32 × 64, 4 groups (fused) | 527 | 247 | 201 | 272 | 127 | 118 | | `all_token_ids` (GPU target), 1 × 131k list | 5413 | 1384 | 1327 | 3009 | 918 | 910 | | `all_token_ids`, 1 × 131k `array('i')` | 4076 | 65 | 64 | 3502 | 27 | 26 | | mrope positions, 1 × 131k | 13097 | 176 | 178 | 11790 | 65 | 64 |
Method - **Builds compared:** all three `buffer_utils.py` versions (main, #63210, and this PR) are loaded side by side in one process, on one GPU. - **GPU time:** 1. Stage the writes; this part is not timed. 2. Enqueue `torch.cuda._sleep` so the GPU is busy. 3. Record a CUDA event, call `apply_write`, and record a second event. 4. Keep the sample only if the GPU was still sleeping when the host finished enqueueing. This measures what `apply_write` enqueues back to back (the H2D copy plus the kernel, or just the kernel), without host launch gaps. Each case uses 600 samples. - **Host time:** median wall time of stage + apply, with `synchronize()` excluded from the "host" number. - **Distributions:** on GB200 the H2D variants are bimodal, at about 11µs and about 19µs. With UVA contents, p10–p90 stays within about 2µs.
There is no end-to-end serving benchmark yet. The gains are on the step-critical path of MRV2 input preparation (block-table updates every step, prompt staging on admission). They are microbenchmarks only, so the effect on whole steps is unmeasured. ## Details - **Buffer inputs by reference.** - `stage_write` keeps an `np.ndarray` or `array.array` as its own chunk, closing off any pending list contents into a chunk first. - Lists still go through `array.fromlist`, and other iterables through `extend`. - `apply_write` does one `np.concatenate(chunks, out=uva_slot, casting="unsafe")`. - Callers must not modify a staged buffer before `apply_write`. Values are cast to the target dtype, and out-of-range values wrap. Both behaviours are documented in the docstring. - `rope.py` now passes `prefill_positions[i].numpy()` instead of `.tolist()`. - **Direct copy into UVA** (after #59908). `UvaBufferPool._next_buf` and `copy_chunks_to_uva` write the concatenation straight into the pool slot, with no intermediate contents buffer. - **UVA contents for GPU targets.** - Before: #63210, like main, copied contents with `async_tensor_h2d` for GPU-resident targets. That costs about 25µs of host time per apply (a pinned allocation plus `cudaMemcpyAsync`) and about 10–25µs of GPU time for the copy engine. - Now: the kernel reads the pinned contents directly. Both approaches cross the link once and run serialized on the same stream. The UVA read was cheaper on NVLink-C2C (GB200) and on PCIe (MI350X) alike, including for 512KB dense writes. - `FusedStagedWriter` gets a UVA contents pool for the same reason. - **No rollback in `stage_write`.** The try/except from #63210 is removed: `fromlist` is already atomic, and a failed staging call is a caller bug. - **Typecode map.** `TORCH_DTYPE_TO_ARRAY_TYPECODE` moves to `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py`, next to `TORCH_DTYPE_TO_NUMPY_DTYPE`. - **Interaction with #62702.** #62702 keeps prompt token ids as int32 `array`s end to end. With this PR, those arrays are staged into `all_token_ids` without any copy. - **Tests.** - `test_staged_write_input_types`: interleaves lists, ranges, int64 and strided int32 arrays, `array('i')`, empty arrays and `stage_write_elem`. - `test_staged_write_uses_uva_contents`: now covers both target kinds, pinned to the target's device. Without that, a leftover current device from an earlier test makes the GPU-target case fail when two GPUs are visible. - `test_staged_write_without_uva`: forces the `NonUvaBuffer` fallback through `apply_write` and through `FusedStagedWriter`. ---

title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3.1] Fuse MXFP8 activation quant into the Gemma input_layernorm for qkv_proj
author: RuibinCheung
body:
## Overview On ROCm, a MiniMax-M3 decoder layer whose `qkv_proj` is MXFP8 (e.g. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, whose attention projections are 1x32 MXFP8) runs the fused add + Gemma RMSNorm, writes the normed bf16 rows, and then `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` reads them back and quantizes them with a separate `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` launch. This PR quantizes the normed row per 32-element block in the epilogue of the norm kernel and hands `qkv_proj` a `QuantizedActivation`, so each layer drops one launch and the bf16 round trip. The fp8 values and E8M0 scales are bitwise equal to norm -> `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`, so the model output does not change. ## Claims - Norm + activation quant: 1.41x-2.06x per call (hidden 6144, M = 1-4096, bf16, MI355X); norm + quant + `qkv_proj` GEMM: 1.07x-1.19x. - Bitwise equal fp8 values, scales and residual vs. norm -> `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`, for bf16 and fp16. - MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP4, decode: the separate activation quant for `qkv_proj` disappears in 59 of 60 layers (kernel trace), the norm kernel time is unchanged, and the removed launches are 1.9% of decode GPU kernel time. AgentX P90 interactivity is 1.018x at concurrency 1 and 1.017x-1.045x at concurrency 16 (two runs, order swapped); c4, c8 and c32 are within run-to-run noise; GSM8K unchanged within stderr. - No change for layers whose `qkv_proj` is not served by `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` with fp8 weights, under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, with LoRA on `qkv_proj`, or with mono decode. ## Validation **Unit tests** (`tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_amd_ops.py`, already run by the AMD kernels CI step): 81 passed on this branch (MI355X, main nightly image with this branch's Python tree), 81 passed + 1 skipped with this PR applied on #63232. `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py` and `tests/v1/determinism/test_mx_linear_batch_invariant.py` (the existing consumer tests of the changed kernel): 97 passed. New tests: - `test_gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8_bitwise_eq_unfused`: `torch.equal` against `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` -> `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` for values, scales and residual, n in {2048, 3072, 6144}, bf16 and fp16. Every row has a block with a scale above 1, an all-zero block and a tiny block (`1 + w = 2**-8`), plus all-zero, tiny, single-block-dominated and partly-zero rows. - `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_qkv_proj`: a real `QuarkOCP_MX` MXFP8 layer (per-row scales, 32x32 block scales, and K % 128 != 0, where the weight is dequantized to bf16 at load), M in {1, 37}. Checks the producer gate (fuses iff the kernel reads the fp8 activation as is) and that `qkv_proj(QuantizedActivation)` is bitwise equal to `qkv_proj(norm output)`. - `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_off_under_batch_invariance` **Microbenchmark** (method as in #59782: one HIP graph of 128 back-to-back calls cycling through 16 input sets, best of 5; MI355X; hidden 6144, bf16; `qkv_proj` is 2560 x 6144 at TP4). "separate" is `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` + `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` (current behaviour), "fused" is `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8`. Speedup of fused over separate: | M | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 1024 | 4096 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | norm + quant | 1.66x | 1.58x | 1.58x | 1.57x | 1.58x | 1.59x | 1.64x | 1.70x | 2.06x | 1.41x | 1.49x | | norm + quant + qkv GEMM | 1.18x | 1.16x | 1.15x | 1.16x | 1.19x | 1.15x | 1.09x | 1.10x | 1.10x | 1.07x | 1.11x | The plain `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` (the kernel gains a `QUANT_MXFP8` constexpr) is unchanged: the separate path times within 1% of the pre-PR kernel at every M. **End to end**: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP4, MI355X, mono decode off, FULL_DECODE_ONLY CUDA graphs, on #63232 (`8d0f05a0c`, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash`) with this PR applied on top; baseline is the same image unchanged. AgentX trace replay (InferenceX), 600 s per point, `max-num-seqs` = 2 x concurrency, the arm that runs first alternates per concurrency. opt / baseline (> 1 is better): | Concurrency | P90 interactivity | |---:|---:| | 1 | 1.018x | | 4 | 0.990x | | 8 | 1.106x | | 16 | 1.017x | | 32 | 1.064x | GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, full test set of 1319, greedy, concurrency 16): baseline 96.51 / opt 96.44 strict-match (stderr 0.51 / 0.51), flexible-extract 96.44 / 96.36. The difference is one question; vLLM is not batch invariant at concurrency 16, so greedy outputs vary between runs even with bit-identical kernels. ## Details - **Producer and consumer.** `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` declares `kMxfp8Dynamic` as its input quant key and accepts a `QuantizedActivation` on the `dot_scaled` and block32 GEMMs; `QuarkOCP_MX` exposes the key for MXFP8 layers (ModelOpt MXFP8 already does). The `QuantizedActivation` contract itself is unchanged. - **Scale layout.** `kMxfp8Dynamic` does not encode the scale layout: the FlashInfer MXFP8 kernels read swizzled scales under the same key, this kernel reads row-major `[M, K // 32]`. So the producer (`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8`) also requires the consumer to be `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` with fp8 weights, the same way DeepSeek V4.1's `can_fuse_query_quant` checks for the FlashInfer kernels. If a `QuantizedActivation` reaches the kernel for a weight it dequantized to bf16 at load (K % 128 != 0), `apply_weights` dequantizes the activation instead of failing; the producer does not fuse in that case. - **Other producers of `kMxfp8Dynamic`.** On main, no other producer fuses into a Quark MXFP8 linear: DeepSeek V4.1's query-quant fusion is CUDA-only and requires the FlashInfer kernels, and `maybe_fused_act_quant` has no MXFP8 entry. ModelOpt MXFP8 MiniMax-M3 checkpoints on ROCm also take this path (same kernel, same bitwise result). - **First layer.** Layer 0 has no residual and uses the non-add `gemma_rmsnorm`; it keeps the separate quant (1/60 of the calls on M3.1-Flash). A non-add variant is a small follow-up if wanted. - **Batch invariance, LoRA.** Off under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, like the other producer-side quant fusions (#59069), so that mode keeps exactly the path `tests/v1/determinism` covers. With LoRA on `qkv_proj`, `get_input_quant_key` returns `None` and nothing changes. - **Mono decode.** The `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO` executor calls `input_layernorm` and `self_attn` directly, so it is unaffected; the end-to-end numbers are with mono off. - **No new env var.** The output is bitwise equal, so there is no accuracy reason to turn it off. ---
