title: [Perf][Kimi K3] Opt-in KV-balanced FP8 MLA decode for agentic workloads
author: wzhao18
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds an opt-in MLA attention backend for Kimi-K3 on Blackwell, `--attention-backend KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`. Its decode splits each request's KV by its own length, so the decode stays balanced across the GPU when the context lengths in one batch differ a lot, as they do in agentic workloads. It is a standalone backend built on the common MLA backend classes (`MLACommonBackend`, `MLACommonImpl`, `MLACommonMetadataBuilder`); it does not depend on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`. The code lives in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kv_balanced_mla/`. Outside it, the PR only adds the backend's entry to `AttentionBackendEnum` (as the DeepSeek V4, MiniMax M3 and Step5 backends in `vllm/models/` have).

## Claims

- **Decode attention, AgentX context lengths on GB300:** 1.34–1.59x faster than `TOKENSPEED_MLA` with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=8`, and 1.91–2.67x faster than its default (geometric mean over batch sizes, DEP16 and DCP8, target verify and draft).
- **End-to-end, AgentX on GB300:**
  - DEP16 decode (3P1D c336): +7.8% TPS/GPU and +20% p90 interactivity.
  - DCP8 decode: +4.6% TPS/GPU and +10% p90 interactivity at 3P4D c240, and +2.7% / +13% at the prefill-bound 2P3D c240.
  - The baseline is `TOKENSPEED_MLA` with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=8`, the setting these recipes already use.
- **Accuracy:** gsm8k with real speculative rejection on the latest revision is 0.961 (DEP16) and 0.967 (DCP8).
- **Opt-in.** The backend is never selected automatically; without `--attention-backend KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` nothing changes.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kv_balanced_mla.py`, 12 tests, passing on GB300). They check the kernel against an FP32 reference for:
- unequal lengths and an empty request;
- the DSpark draft block (non-causal);
- a DCP8 shard on rank 0, and on rank 5 with interleave 64. The rank-5 lengths end inside that rank's chunks, so the causal mask cuts its last keys. Passing the wrong rank or interleave gives about 80% error, versus 2% when correct.
- a peaked softmax that fails without the P prescale;
- plan plus decode captured in a CUDA graph and replayed with KV lengths changed in place;
- a shared workspace larger than 2 GiB.

The backend tests check that `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` resolves to this backend, its builder and its base-2 LSE convention, and is in no platform's priority list; that selection rejects an FP16 model, a non-FP8 KV cache, a non-SM10x GPU and a `kv_lora_rank` other than 512; and that `forward_mqa` only runs the kernel. The decode tests check one plan per forward, the DCP path with the LSE, and that a step the kernel can't run raises a `ValueError`.

**Microbenchmark.** Time per decode step on one rank, from CUDA-graph replays, mean of 5 random batches per N. Context lengths are sampled from the AgentX trace (median about 98K tokens, p90 about 284K). Every variant decodes the same requests and was checked against an FP32 reference.
- `ts1` is `TOKENSPEED_MLA` with the default `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=1`.
- `ts8` is the same with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=8`.
- `kvb` is this PR's decode, excluding its plan. The plan takes 4–13 µs, runs once per forward and is shared by all MLA layers.

| Decode | Step | kvb vs ts1 | kvb vs ts8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16: 96 heads, full KV | verify (q=5, causal) | 2.63x (1.93–3.30) | 1.37x (1.25–1.54) |
| DEP16 | draft (64 heads, q=4) | 2.67x (1.17–4.39) | 1.34x (1.17–1.47) |
| DCP8: 96 gathered heads, 1/8 KV shard, LSE | verify | 1.91x (1.34–3.33) | 1.52x (1.41–1.70) |
| DCP8 | draft | 2.46x (1.78–3.32) | 1.59x (1.48–1.82) |

<details>
<summary>Per batch size (µs)</summary>

| Decode | Step | N | ts1 | ts8 | kvb | kvb vs ts1 | kvb vs ts8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16 | verify | 4 | 402.1 | 308.7 | 208.5 | 1.93x | 1.48x |
| DEP16 | verify | 8 | 928.3 | 433.6 | 281.1 | 3.30x | 1.54x |
| DEP16 | verify | 16 | 2335.6 | 1017.3 | 759.1 | 3.08x | 1.34x |
| DEP16 | verify | 24 | 2744.4 | 1341.3 | 1045.3 | 2.63x | 1.28x |
| DEP16 | verify | 32 | 4374.5 | 2223.9 | 1783.0 | 2.45x | 1.25x |
| DEP16 | draft | 4 | 189.5 | 189.5 | 161.4 | 1.17x | 1.17x |
| DEP16 | draft | 8 | 470.6 | 295.2 | 203.7 | 2.31x | 1.45x |
| DEP16 | draft | 16 | 1175.5 | 593.9 | 403.6 | 2.91x | 1.47x |
| DEP16 | draft | 24 | 2473.4 | 764.9 | 563.3 | 4.39x | 1.36x |
| DEP16 | draft | 32 | 3778.6 | 1245.7 | 964.9 | 3.92x | 1.29x |
| DCP8 | verify | 16 | 295.5 | 151.3 | 88.7 | 3.33x | 1.70x |
| DCP8 | verify | 32 | 413.3 | 293.1 | 189.1 | 2.19x | 1.55x |
| DCP8 | verify | 64 | 763.2 | 640.3 | 430.8 | 1.77x | 1.49x |
| DCP8 | verify | 96 | 984.9 | 971.1 | 662.0 | 1.49x | 1.47x |
| DCP8 | verify | 128 | 1189.6 | 1251.3 | 888.6 | 1.34x | 1.41x |
| DCP8 | draft | 16 | 159.5 | 91.9 | 50.5 | 3.16x | 1.82x |
| DCP8 | draft | 32 | 340.5 | 168.1 | 102.7 | 3.32x | 1.64x |
| DCP8 | draft | 64 | 561.5 | 350.5 | 228.6 | 2.46x | 1.53x |
| DCP8 | draft | 96 | 668.0 | 508.4 | 339.1 | 1.97x | 1.50x |
| DCP8 | draft | 128 | 780.4 | 649.2 | 438.4 | 1.78x | 1.48x |

</details>

**End-to-end.**
- **Setup:** Kimi-K3 MXFP4 on GB300 NVL72, using the InferenceX AgentX agentic-coding replay with Dynamo disaggregated serving, Mooncake KV offload, and DSpark speculative decoding with 4 tokens (synthetic acceptance, as the recipes use).
- **Builds:** both sides run the same vLLM main build. The only difference is the decode workers' decode kernel. These runs used this PR's earlier revision, which selected the same kernel and dispatch through `additional_config` instead of the attention backend name. A rerun of the DEP16 point on the latest revision gave the same result.
- **Baseline:** the decode workers use `TOKENSPEED_MLA` with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=8`.
- **Runs:** one run per side for each point. A repeat of the DEP16 pair gave +8.6% TPS/GPU.

| Config | TPS/GPU | Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s) | E2E latency p90 | TTFT mean / p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3P1D, TP8 prefill + DEP16 decode, c336: baseline | 27,267 | 38.1 / 35.2 | 60.6 s | 3.14 / 5.82 s |
| same, KV-balanced | **29,402 (+7.8%)** | 45.8 / 42.4 (+20% / +20%) | 53.9 s (−11%) | 4.22 / 9.69 s |
| 3P4D, DCP8 prefill + DCP8 decode, c240: baseline | 20,421 | 75.7 / 68.9 | 33.3 s | 1.89 / 3.03 s |
| same, KV-balanced | **21,370 (+4.6%)** | 83.1 / 75.9 (+10% / +10%) | 30.8 s (−7%) | 1.84 / 2.94 s |
| 2P3D, DCP8 prefill + DCP8 decode, c240: baseline | 24,503 | 63.7 / 58.0 | 43.9 s | 5.21 / 10.74 s |
| same, KV-balanced | **25,162 (+2.7%)** | 72.6 / 65.3 (+14% / +13%) | 40.7 s (−7%) | 5.83 / 12.41 s |

- **Why TTFT rises at 3P1D and 2P3D:** a faster decode lets more requests through, which puts more load on the prefill workers that limit those points. At 3P4D, with more prefill capacity, TTFT improves slightly.
- **Why DCP8 gains less:** with DCP8, MLA attention is a smaller share of each decode step than with DEP16.

**Accuracy.** gsm8k (5-shot, lm-eval) with real speculative rejection, `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` on the decode workers (latest revision). Every decode step ran on the kernel.

| Config | strict-match | flexible-extract | Acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1P1D, TP8 prefill + DEP16 decode | 0.961 | 0.961 | 3.61 |
| 1P1D, DCP8 prefill + DCP8 decode | 0.967 | 0.967 | 3.27 |

**CI.** The B200 Kimi K3 step (`models/kimi_k3`) runs the new tests. They were validated on GB300 (SM103) and not run on B200 (SM100). On the MI355 step the tests are skipped, and the test module imports without the CuTe kernel.

## Details

**KV imbalance in agentic decode.** An agentic decode batch mixes very different context lengths, for example 5K, 20K, 98K and 300K tokens. To spread one request's attention over the GPU, the decode cuts its KV into splits; clusters process the splits in parallel and a reduction merges them. `TOKENSPEED_MLA`, the existing FP8 MLA decode for this model, uses one split count for the whole batch: it's chosen from the batch size and SM count, with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv` as a floor. With a skewed batch, any single count is wrong for most requests:
- **Too many splits for short requests.** Short requests are cut into tiny splits that each pay the per-split setup and the reduction.
- **Too few splits for long requests.** The longest requests leave a tail in which a few clusters stream hundreds of thousands of keys while the rest of the GPU is idle.

`min_split_kv=8` helps the long requests and hurts the short ones; at DCP8 N=128 it is slower than the default (see `ts8` vs `ts1`).

**What the KV-balanced decode does:**
1. **Plan.** A Triton planner gives each request its own split count from its KV length: 1 to 8 splits of at least 1024 tokens, sized to fill at most 8 waves of the GPU's clusters. It writes the planned (query tile, request, split) entries as a device work list. It reads nothing on the host, so it is captured in the decode CUDA graph. It runs once per forward, and every MLA layer reuses it.
2. **Execute.** One wave of persistent 2-CTA clusters walks the work list, so every cluster gets about the same amount of KV.
3. **Skip the merge where possible.** A request planned as a single split stores its final output directly, and the reduction skips it.
4. **Keep small probabilities.** Long splits can make probabilities small enough to flush to zero in E4M3, so P is stored scaled by 2^6 and the LSE removes the factor.

**Code layout** (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kv_balanced_mla/`):
- `kernel.py` and `helpers.py`: TokenSpeed MLA 2.0.3's FP8 decode kernel (MIT), vendored with the changes above. Compared with the release, the kernel adds 347 lines (including renames and casts so it passes `typos` and mypy) and drops its 1,252-line benchmark harness; the helpers add 59 lines, the work-list tile scheduler. They do not import the `tokenspeed_mla` package at runtime.
- `core.py`: the planner and the compiled kernel.
- `decode.py`: the per-layer dispatch: the once-per-forward plan, the DCP arguments and the shape checks.
- `backend.py`: `KimiK3KvBalancedMLABackend`, `KimiK3KvBalancedMLAMetadataBuilder` and `KimiK3KvBalancedMLAImpl`. The impl's `forward_mqa` runs the kernel.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py`: the `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` entry.

Kimi-K3's MLA layer (`mla.py`) is unchanged: it calls the selected backend's `forward_mqa`.

**Why a standalone backend.** The backend is about 190 lines on the common MLA classes, and it states everything the kernel relies on itself, so a later change to `TOKENSPEED_MLA` can't silently change what this backend runs:
- the FP8 KV cache layout (576 values per token, pages of 32 or 64);
- the decode metadata (`seq_lens`, `block_table`, `dcp_tot_seq_lens`) with uniform query lengths and `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graphs;
- the packed FP8 query from the common MLA impl;
- the base-2 LSE convention of the DCP combine (`lse_base_on_e=False`);
- non-causal multi-token decode for the DSpark draft, with and without DCP.

Prefill uses the configured MLA prefill backend, as in the other MLA backends.

**Supported configurations.** An FP8 E4M3 KV cache, an SM10x GPU, a BF16 model and MLA dimensions (`qk_nope_head_dim`, `qk_rope_head_dim`, `v_head_dim`, `kv_lora_rank`) = (128, 64, 128, 512); backend selection rejects anything else with the reason. Alibi, sliding window, soft cap and non-decoder attention raise a `ValueError` when the layer is built. The kernel also needs more than 64 query rows per request (heads × query tokens) and at most as many requests as it plans for; the head count isn't known at selection, so these fail at model build with a `ValueError`. There is no fallback decode: a decode step the kernel can't run raises a `ValueError` with the reason. In the end-to-end runs every decode shape (target verify q=1–5, draft q=4) ran on the kernel. `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` is read from the parallel config on every call, since NIXL P/D sets it after the model is built. The DSpark draft takes its backend from the speculative config's `attention_backend`.

**Tradeoffs and limitations:**
- **Size:** the vendored kernel adds about 4.9K lines. Integrating through the `tokenspeed_mla` package instead (reusing its compiled kernel with planned per-request splits) gave about 20% less speedup in our microbenchmarks. The work-list scheduler, direct output and P prescale need kernel changes.
- **Memory:** the split-KV scratch is sized as requests × query tiles × 8 splits of FP16 partial outputs. That's about 0.5 GB for 128 requests at heads=96, q=5, versus about 0.23 GB for TokenSpeed's SM-based bound; it's logged at startup.
- **Host syncs:** by inspection, the decode path adds none. Planning is a device kernel, and the once-per-forward check compares the forward context and a data pointer. This was not checked with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not store sliding-window chunks with null blocks
author: pepmach
body:
## Overview Fixes #63653. With offloaded chunks of several GPU blocks, `OffloadingConnector` could store a sliding-window chunk that contained a null block. A later CPU hit then loaded the never-written slot as KV, and the request's output changed with no error. ## Claims - A sliding-window chunk is stored only when every block that the store mask marks reachable is present, so a CPU hit no longer loads a slot that no store wrote. - One-block chunks and full-attention groups behave as before. A one-block chunk with a null block was already skipped, and full-attention block tables hold no null blocks. ## Validation Two new tests: - `test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`: scheduler level, sync and async scheduling. - `test_cpu_offloading_sliding_window_partial_chunk` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py`: LLM level, CUDA, `google/gemma-3-1b-it` with `blocks_per_chunk=8` and `store_threshold=2`. Request B's GPU hit ends mid-chunk, which leaves null sliding-window blocks inside chunk 0, and B stores that chunk. The test asserts that this hit length is reached, so the case is exercised, and that a request hitting the chunk on the CPU tier produces the same output as a cold run. Scheduler-level test without the fix (main `24324ef0`), failing at the store check for request B: ``` $ pytest --tb=short -q "tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored" tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py:2299: in test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/utils.py:680: in run E AssertionError FAILED ...::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored[True] FAILED ...::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored[False] 2 failed in 1.11s ``` Line 2299 is `runner.run(decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID], expected_stored=((0, 0), (0, 1)))`: on main, B also stores sliding-window block 1 without block 0. With the fix, `2 passed in 1.29s`. LLM-level test: not run on a GPU, because I don't have one. CI runs it on CUDA. I ran its helper `_sliding_window_partial_chunk_test` on CPU against a tiny random Gemma-3 (512-token window, GPU block 32, 8 blocks per chunk). The offload copy was done by an out-of-tree spec that runs `gpu_worker.py`'s transfer code with `memmove` in place of the CUDA kernel (described in the linked issue). - On main it fails at `assert out_c.outputs[0].token_ids == cold_c.outputs[0].token_ids`: C's greedy tokens change, and C loaded 114,688 bytes that no store wrote. - With the fix it passes, and C loads nothing. End to end on CPU with the same spec, comparing C's output against a run without offloading: | Run | C's CPU hit | Loaded bytes no store wrote | C's logprobs vs no offloading | |---|---|---|---| | main, 64-token window, 2 blocks per chunk | 64 tokens | 16,384 | off by 0.11 to 0.15 at every step | | main, chunk-aligned control | 64 tokens | 0 | identical | | main, 512-token window, 8 blocks per chunk | 512 tokens | 114,688 (7 blocks) | off by 0.18 to 0.39; 3 of the top-5 first tokens change | | this PR, both shapes | none (recomputed) | 0 | identical | Model evaluation: the fix changes only which chunks get stored, so an affected request recomputes a chunk instead of loading it. An accuracy benchmark wouldn't isolate the bug, because the bug needs a specific hit-then-evict pattern. The runs above construct that pattern and compare against a run without offloading. The LLM-level test does the same in CI against a cold run on `google/gemma-3-1b-it`. Suites, run with `pytest -q ` on CPU (macOS arm64, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`) at `24324ef0`: | Suite | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` | 628 passed, 2 skipped | 630 passed, 2 skipped | | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py` | 2 failed, 3 skipped | 2 failed, 4 skipped (the same 2 failures) | | `tests/v1/core` | 1059 passed, 1 failed, 4 errors | the same counts and the same failing tests | | `tests/v1/kv_offload` (without `cpu/test_gpu_worker.py`) | 718 passed, 54 failed, 10 skipped | the same counts and the same failing tests | The failures on both sides are environment limits on this Mac: - the two tiering tests download a gated model; - in `tests/v1/core`, the hybrid test model needs `causal_conv1d_weight_pack`, which the CPU build lacks, and one test's block size is unsupported; - the `kv_offload` failures are `cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py`, which needs `/dev/shm`. `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including ruff 0.14.0, typos, mypy and the Buildkite test-wiring check. The branch merges cleanly into main `237d2ffd`. On that merge, the scheduler-level test, the LLM-level helper on CPU and the `offloading_connector` suite (632 passed, 2 skipped) all pass. ## Details Root cause, with lines at `24324ef0`: - A GPU prefix-cache hit leaves sliding-window blocks before the window null (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1004-1037`). A sliding-window free also zeroes pending store positions (`offloading/scheduler.py:1503-1522`). - With the default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, a GPU hit lands on an earlier prompt's replay boundary. That boundary is block-aligned but not necessarily chunk-aligned, so the null run can end mid-chunk. - `_build_store_jobs` selected chunks by their last block only (`offloading/scheduler.py:1880-1891`, `1917`), then dropped null blocks from the store spec (`1995`). - The worker wrote part of the chunk (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py:635-654`), while `complete_store` marked all of it ready (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py:370-387`). The fix adds one check to key selection. After the existing reachability test, a chunk is skipped if any block the store mask marks reachable is null. With no mask, any null block skips it. No GPU block exists to copy for that position, so the chunk can't be completed. A later request that would have hit this chunk computes it instead: it loses a partial CPU hit and avoids loading stale KV. Null blocks that the mask marks unreachable are still allowed. A request whose window excludes them holds null blocks there too, and its load skips those slots. Test changes: - `RequestRunner` rejected `blocks_per_chunk > 1` whenever custom KV cache groups were passed. It now accepts them when every group uses the runner's block size. - `_wait_for_prefix_cache_reset` takes `reset_connector`, so the LLM-level test can clear the CPU tier before its cold run. Not a duplicate: as of 2026-10-26, no open or closed issue or PR reports this bug. I ran 20 keyword searches over issues and PRs and checked the 171 open PRs that touch the offloading connector or `kv_offload/`. The closest are these two: - #57216 guards the end-of-request partial-chunk store against null blocks. This PR covers full chunks. - Draft #61426 moves this loop into `store_triggers/on_compute.py` and keeps the last-block check. If it lands first, this check goes there. AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) found this bug with a randomized checker over the offloading connector. It also wrote the reproductions, the CPU end-to-end harness, both tests and the fix, and ran the suites above. I reviewed every changed line and reran the tests and the CPU end-to-end check. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer. ---

title: [ROCm][Perf] Make MXFP4 the default indexer K cache dtype for DeepSeek-V4
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Overview #60834 brought the paged MXFP4 sparse indexer (dense path) to DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm gfx950. It was opt-in: ```bash --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}' ``` Its measurements show the MXFP4 indexer is better than the FP8 one on almost every axis: - lower TTFT (up to -30.7%) and TPOT; - +9.2% KV cache capacity (68 B vs 132 B per compressed token); - near-lossless accuracy: GSM8K -0.16pt, and GPQA Diamond is unchanged at 0.7121. The results are copied below. This PR therefore makes MXFP4 the **default** indexer K cache dtype for DeepSeek-V4 (`model_type == "deepseek_v4"`, i.e. V4-Pro / V4-Flash) on ROCm CDNA4, and logs that it is enabled. ## Claims Nothing else changes: - CUDA, XPU and CPU behave as before; - DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps its current opt-in; - every other model is untouched. ## Validation ### Benchmark (from #60834, DeepSeek-V4-Pro) Fixed sequence length (`8k1k`, TP8, MTP=2): | Conc | Indexer | Output token throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change | | ---: | :------ | ------------------------------: | ------: | -------------: | -------: | -------------: | ------: | | 1 | FP8 (old default) | 145.99 | — | 597.24 | — | 6.24 | — | | 1 | MXFP4 (new default) | 156.34 | 7.09% ↑ | 413.91 | 30.70% ↓ | 5.96 | 4.49% ↓ | | 4 | FP8 (old default) | 454.91 | — | 504.07 | — | 8.02 | — | | 4 | MXFP4 (new default) | 466.92 | 2.64% ↑ | 437.29 | 13.25% ↓ | 7.95 | 0.87% ↓ | | 16 | FP8 (old default) | 1020.90 | — | 744.88 | — | 14.51 | — | | 16 | MXFP4 (new default) | 1030.30 | 0.92% ↑ | 681.89 | 8.46% ↓ | 14.46 | 0.34% ↓ | | 64 | FP8 (old default) | 1629.53 | — | 1637.36 | — | 36.85 | — | | 64 | MXFP4 (new default) | 1656.28 | 1.64% ↑ | 1622.58 | 0.90% ↓ | 36.29 | 1.52% ↓ | Agentic replay (DP8, MTP=3, prefix caching): | Indexer | Output Token Throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | KV Cache Capacity (tokens) | |---|---|---|---|---| | FP8 (old default) | 697.25 | 2,442.24 | 46.01 | 4,589,684 | | MXFP4 (new default) | 675.83 (3.07% ↓) | 2,321.05 (4.96% ↓) | 43.42 (5.62% ↓) | 5,010,749 (9.17% ↑) | - **Latency improves:** mean TPOT -5.62% and mean TTFT -4.96%. - TPOT is the most consistent signal: both MXFP4 runs (44.60 / 42.24 ms) had lower TPOT than both FP8 runs (46.98 / 45.03 ms). - TTFT varied by up to 13% between runs of the same configuration, so treat its gain as indicative. - **Output throughput is within noise (-3.07%).** On this workload it is driven mainly by the trace replay and by output lengths. - **KV cache capacity: +9.17%.** Peak KV usage stayed below 40% here, so this workload does not yet turn the extra capacity into throughput. Higher-concurrency or longer-context workloads should benefit more. ### Accuracy (from #60834, DeepSeek-V4-Pro) GSM8K: | Task | Filter | n-shot | Metric | FP8 (old default) | MXFP4 (new default) | Change | | ----- | ---------------- | -----: | ------------- | ----------------: | ------------------: | -------: | | gsm8k | flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match ↑ | 0.9492 | 0.9477 | -0.16% ↓ | | gsm8k | strict-match | 5 | exact_match ↑ | 0.9500 | 0.9484 | -0.17% ↓ | GPQA Diamond: | Indexer | GPQA Diamond | Empty Responses (reasoning over budget) | |---|---|---| | FP8 (old default) | 0.7121 ± 0.0323 | 13 / 198 | | MXFP4 (new default) | 0.7121 ± 0.0323 | 11 / 198 | - **Accuracy is unchanged on GPQA:** both indexers score 0.7121. Per question, 124 are correct in both runs, and the disagreements are symmetric (17 vs 17, McNemar p = 1.0). - **This exercises the indexer's long-context path:** reasoning traces run to tens of thousands of tokens, far past the 4096 tokens where sparse top-k selection starts. - **The GSM8K change is negligible** (< 0.2% relative). ## Details ---

title: [Fast Start] Support online FP8 and CUTLASS NVFP4 weight-cache restarts
author: liusy58
body:
## Overview Allow the weight-cache daemon to reuse online FP8/MXFP8 linear weights and ModelOpt NVFP4 CUTLASS MoE weights across engine restarts. Related to #56049; this covers a subset of its quantization roadmap. ## Claims - Restore online quantization runtime state without quantizing or transforming shared weights again. FP8 is limited to CUTLASS; MXFP8 requires the selected kernel's pre-processed-weight capability. Requantization from serialized checkpoints and online MoE remain excluded. - Preserve the unpadded CUTLASS FP8 output width when IPC loading skips weight post-processing. - Restore ModelOpt NVFP4 CUTLASS MoE kernels without multiplying activation scales into shared weight scales a second time. ## Validation Current head `35711168b0135573234bbaa4bd8f9e8fe32647e8` includes main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`. October 29 agent-run validation after resolving the inherited online-FP8 import conflict with upstream #60163. The merge retains both CUTLASS and Humming imports, the upstream processed-dimension metadata, and upstream rejection of the unsupported Humming per-token/channel path. It adds no Humming IPC capability. | Check | Exact-head result | |---|---| | `online-units` | 108 passed, 685 deselected, 14 warnings in 98.42s (0:01:38) | | `online-models` | 4 passed, 30 warnings in 305.90s (0:05:05) | | `nvfp4-model` | 1 passed, 18 warnings in 99.83s (0:01:39) | | Full feature-file and commit hooks | Passed, including mypy and ruff | Runtime: NVIDIA B300, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, process-local CUDA 13.4 compatibility libraries. The two stable-libtorch extensions are from the official CUDA 13.0 wheel for main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`, checked against wheel RECORD hashes and linked only into task worktrees. The shared venv and host driver were unchanged. This does not validate the full upstream PyTorch 2.14 dependency matrix. Full-model checks use TP1, BF16, eager mode, CUTLASS and TRITON_ATTN, with the existing batch-invariant exact greedy-output comparisons. Each completed case checks ordinary load, missing-daemon fallback, IPC and a second IPC load; both IPC loads forbid fallback. These are output-equivalence smoke checks, not accuracy or performance benchmarks. No multi-GPU, ROCm or other-backend result is claimed. The temporary local helper calls the existing `run_cold_start_and_warm_restart` with `dataclasses.replace(case, model=local_checkpoint, llm_kwargs={**case.llm_kwargs, "gpu_memory_utilization": 0.12})` and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. It changes only checkpoint location and the GPU memory budget; loading paths, prompts and assertions are unchanged. Online cases keep their checked-in 0.2 budget. NVFP4 checkpoint: `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, pinned `2538ded2a4edb247b4d2b4a8ba24e44bd4c017c3`.
Commands for this revision All commands set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, `PYTHONPATH` to the corresponding worktree and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/liusy/codex-runtime/cuda-compat-13-4/usr/local/cuda-13.4/compat`. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py -k 'test_cutlass_fp8_gemm_padded or (not cutlass and not cold_start and not d2d_warmup and not online)' -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_online_fp8 tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_online_blackwell -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 CODEX_CACHE_VALIDATION_CASE=nvfp4 CODEX_CACHE_MODEL_PATH=/home/liusy/codex-runtime/checkpoints/nvfp4-2538ded2a4 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/_codex_oct29_validation.py -q ```
GitHub checks for the new head are pending at publication. No Buildkite GPU-suite pass or completed human review is claimed. AI assistance and original feature baselines are recorded below.
Earlier validation and original feature baselines (previous heads) Earlier head `aa141888102c8431c5f25c53477cf18cb837fd5d` includes main `36d4ef654a83e227216b0c0b55cf4041d96b1675`. Agent-run B300 validation on October 29, after synchronizing the native extensions with that main commit: | Check | Result | |---|---| | Online FP8/Blackwell full-model cases | 4 passed, 268.86s | | Qwen3-30B-A3B NVFP4 full-model case | 1 passed, 102.00s | | Weight-cache and padded CUTLASS regressions | 108 passed, 83.35s | | Full feature-file and commit hooks | Passed, including mypy and ruff | The four online cases use their checked-in settings (`gpu_memory_utilization=0.2`). The NVFP4 case uses a local copy of `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` pinned at `2538ded2a4edb247b4d2b4a8ba24e44bd4c017c3`, with only the checkpoint path and GPU memory fraction (`0.12`) substituted for shared-machine coexistence. B300, TP1, BF16, eager mode, CUTLASS linear kernels and TRITON_ATTN. Full-model cases exercise ordinary loading → missing-daemon fallback → IPC → second IPC, with fallback forbidden on both IPC loads and the existing exact batch-invariant greedy-output comparisons unchanged. These are output-equivalence smoke tests, not accuracy or performance benchmarks; multi-GPU and other hardware are not claimed. Runtime: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 with process-local CUDA 13.4 compatibility libraries. The two stable-libtorch native extensions were taken from the official CUDA 13.0 wheel for exact main `36d4ef654a83e227216b0c0b55cf4041d96b1675`, verified against wheel RECORD hashes, and linked only into the task worktrees. Their declared stable ABI supports PyTorch >=2.11. This is not validation of the complete upstream PyTorch 2.14 dependency matrix; the shared venv and host driver were unchanged. An initial Llama run stalled reading the shared NFS checkpoint; it was stopped and rerun using a pinned local-disk checkpoint. An initial NVFP4 ordinary load failed before IPC because the old native extension exposed an 11-argument operator while current source required 12; the matching extensions above resolved that environment mismatch. Neither initial run is counted as a passing test or as a cache regression. All results in the table use the matching extensions. Existing torch/fork deprecation warnings are retained in the logs. The exact heads above are MERGEABLE; GitHub pre-commit, DCO and Read the Docs passed on October 29. No Buildkite GPU-suite success or completed human review is claimed. Original feature baselines and earlier results remain below and are not reruns of the October 29 conflict resolution.
Original feature baselines, reproduction commands and earlier validation B300, single GPU per scenario. Each end-to-end case compares normal loading, disk fallback without a daemon, first IPC attachment, and a second IPC attachment. Both IPC runs disable fallback. Quantization tests use greedy output comparison with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 and TRITON_ATTN. On main 0f6b261910, branch 084cab1bc7: online FP8 per-tensor/per-channel/per-block and MXFP8: 4 passed (272.15s); Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 with CUTLASS linear/MoE: 1 passed (102.83s); weight-cache unit and CUTLASS padding/scales/bias cases: 102 passed (79.85s). After merging main 2fb320d830 (including #62734 and #63506), on then-then-current head d771fd8528: - All four online FP8/MXFP8 full-model cases passed again: 4 passed (299.37s), using the checked-in configuration. - Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 passed again: 1 passed (122.73s). This local run substituted the same-model checkpoint directory and set `gpu_memory_utilization=0.12` instead of the CI case's `0.3` to coexist with other B300 workloads. The four loading paths and output assertions were unchanged; the earlier `0.3` result above is from 084cab1bc7. - Weight-cache unit and padded CUTLASS cases: 108 passed (102.27s). - Changed-file/commit hooks, GitHub pre-commit, DCO and Read the Docs passed. No Buildkite GPU-suite result is asserted. The unit runs emitted a background-thread warning in unchanged upstream seed.py: self._server became None before accept during listener shutdown; the warning is retained. Model runs emitted torch/multiprocessing deprecation warnings. Before the fix, the real online-FP8 daemon reported `UnsupportedQuantForIPCError: ... Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod does not support loading from pre-processed weights`. The padded CUTLASS regression failed at `assert output_size is not None` when IPC skipped post-processing; the same regression passes with the constructor restoring the logical width. Reproduction from the branch using an idle GPU: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k 'online_fp8 or online_blackwell' -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k nvfp4_cutlass -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py -k test_cutlass_fp8_gemm_padded -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k 'not cold_start and not d2d_warmup and not online and not nvfp4_cutlass' -q ``` Post-merge command (small GPU allocations only): ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py -k 'test_cutlass_fp8_gemm_padded or (not cutlass and not cold_start and not d2d_warmup and not online)' -q ``` NVFP4 local validation substitutes the existing same-model checkpoint directory for its Hugging Face ID. This validates IPC equivalence to ordinary quantized inference, not quantization accuracy against BF16. No TP/PP/DP/EP, multi-node, or full hardware matrix claim. Earlier shared-GPU profiling failures are retained in the logs; the same online suite passed on an isolated GPU without changing assertions. Precompiled FlashAttention was incompatible with this host, hence the explicit Triton attention choice.
## Details Online methods previously rejected daemon caching despite successful ordinary loading. The restore paths opt in only when their kernel state can be reconstructed. NVFP4 CUTLASS otherwise performs an in-place scale fusion during kernel initialization, which must not run again on shared daemon tensors. Adds focused loading regressions, extends the existing padding test to construct a real kernel, adds L4/B200 Buildkite selection, and documents supported paths in the preload guide. No model-runner/scheduler changes or new steady-state host synchronization. Duplicate checks on October 26 examined issue #56049 and its comments and searched open PRs for the issue, preload quantization, and weight-cache FP8. #62734 covers daemon-loss detection and #63506 covers kernel cache keys; neither adds these restore paths. #60015 concerns compressed-tensors scale registration and is outside this change. No duplicate implementing this scope was found in those searches. AI assistance: implementation, debugging, validation, and this description were prepared with Codex at the submitter's request. This is a draft for human review; no completed human approval or human-run validation is asserted. ---

title: [KV Offload] Carry request context on raw stored events
author: Change72
body:
## Overview

Carry the originating `ReqContext` on internal store events across the CPU, filesystem, and object tiers. This is the transport-only first step split from #52103. Published `BlockStored` and `BlockRemoved` payloads are unchanged.

## Changes

- CPU store completion attaches the `ReqContext` it already receives. FS/OBJ retain the in-flight `TransferJob` and use its context when the asynchronous store completes, including cascaded stores. No new side map is added.
- When a successful raw store event is emitted, it carries context regardless of `self_describing_kv_events`. The option is not plumbed through managers, specs, or secondary tiers; the event tracker remains the place to decide whether to use that context for published self-describing events.
- Inventory and removal events do not gain request context. This PR does not change event payload generation or removal semantics.

## Validation

- On GPU Server: `PYTHONPATH="$PWD" ../vllm-52103/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py -q` — 154 passed.
- On GPU Server: `PYTHONPATH="$PWD" ../vllm-52103/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py -q` — 51 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files` on all seven changed files and `git diff --check` passed.
- Model evaluation is not applicable: model execution and published KV event payloads are unchanged.

## Follow-ups (not part of this PR)

- #59599 aligns per-block `extra_keys` independently; this transport-only PR does not depend on it.
- **B — complete chunks and removals:** Use the carried context to build complete-chunk `BlockStored` payloads, reusing the extra-key alignment from #59599. Emit chunk-key `BlockRemoved` events so consumers can undo their recorded chunk-to-block mapping. B should land after #59599.
- **C — partial tails and cleanup:** Build partial-tail metadata from request context, then remove the remaining `_pending_event_metadata` map and old recording hooks. C follows B.

#52103 remains the umbrella discussion for the complete change. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. This PR remains draft for human review and testing of this revision.

title: [KV Offload] Describe complete stores from request context
author: Change72
body:
## Summary

Step B of the split from #52103, built on merged #63695.

- Build complete-chunk `BlockStored` payloads from the request carried by the raw store event and the existing key position in `ReqContext`. Partial tails still use the current metadata snapshot.
- Keep the existing block-granular `BlockRemoved` expansion from saved metadata. Chunk-key removals are deferred so this PR does not change the removal contract for downstream consumers.

This remains draft. #59599 aligns block extra keys and should land before this is finalized. Follow-ups will handle partial tails and, with downstream coordination, chunk-key removals.

title: [Bugfix] Initialize valid ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE dummy scales
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview Initialize ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE dummy quantization scales to valid positive values. Random initialization could produce nonpositive block/input scales and inconsistent gate/up global scales when benchmarking with `--load-format dummy`. ## Claims - Dummy NVFP4 MoE weights use positive scales and matching gate/up global scales through the existing `dummy_weight_value` loader contract. - A regression test constructs a small Qwen3 MoE through `LLM`, confirms the FlashInfer TRTLLM backend and valid scales, and generates two tokens with finite returned log probabilities. - The ModelOpt documentation explains dummy benchmarking and the FlashInfer MegaMoE backend flag. ## Validation One GB200 GPU, BF16 activations, NVFP4 dummy experts, FlashInfer TRTLLM, eager execution: | Check | Without fix | With fix | | --- | --- | --- | | `test_modelopt_nvfp4_dummy_scales` | Failed: `AssertionError: w13_weight_scale` at `assert (values > 0).all()` | 1 passed, 22 deselected; two generated tokens and finite returned log probabilities | The same test command was run with the production change removed and restored: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HF_HOME=/mnt/lustre/hf-models \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py \ -k test_modelopt_nvfp4_dummy_scales -x -v -s ``` Relevant before/after output: ```text Before: AssertionError: w13_weight_scale assert tensor(False, device='cuda:0') 1 failed, 22 deselected, 1 warning in 15.15s After: 1 passed, 22 deselected, 1 warning in 16.22s ``` The test runs in the existing B200 Quantized MoE Buildkite step, whose dependencies already cover both changed Python files. ```bash .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py \ tests/quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py \ docs/features/quantization/modelopt.md git diff --check ``` Both passed, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown lint, and test tethering. A fresh-agent local-checkout documentation search found and quoted the dummy benchmarking section. A separate real-LLM smoke run on this PR checkout also passed with two GB200 GPUs, TP2/EP2, the same tiny Qwen3 MoE configuration, and `moe_backend="flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl"`: two generated tokens with finite log probabilities. This uses the native dummy loader, without a benchmark wrapper. No real-checkpoint quality evaluation was run: this change only supplies values consumed by dummy weight initialization, and dummy outputs are unsuitable for quality evaluation. ## Details The generic dummy initializer samples floating-point values around zero. NVFP4 MoE quantization scales require positive values, and the fused gate/up projections share a global scale. The change assigns block scales `1.0`, global weight scales `1e-3`, and input scales `1e-2` using parameter metadata already supported by the loader. It adds no inference-time work; normal checkpoint loading continues to use checkpoint values. Duplicate-work searches on 2026-10-26 for `ModelOpt dummy`, `NVFP4 scales`, `MegaMoE dummy`, and `"dummy_weight_value"` found no open PR implementing this dummy initialization fix. Related #55073 reconciles differing scales in real checkpoints, #45320 rejects missing checkpoint scales, and #55997 refactors ModelOpt MoE methods; they address different behavior. There is no associated issue. AI assistance was used to implement, validate, review, and document this change. ---

title: [Recipe][AMD] Refresh Kimi-K3 PD configurations

title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 prefill GEMMs on AITER tuned kernels
author: whx-sjtu
body:
Ready for review. No blocking issues. ## Overview Online FP8 prefill for Kimi-K3 on MI355X is slower than BF16 today. This PR quantizes `routed_expert_down_proj` online and builds AITER's tuned GEMMs at startup. ## Claims - `routed_expert_down_proj` follows the online quantization config. Its checkpoint weights are BF16, so the checkpoint config is still bypassed. - `kernel_config.enable_rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup` (off by default) runs one dummy forward per AITER GEMM M bucket during kernel warmup. - Kimi-K3 agentic PD benchmark, with in_proj padded to 128 on AITER v0.1.24.post1: +2.1% total tok/s/GPU and mean TTFT 5.35 s to 4.05 s over online FP8 prefill without this PR, +0.7% over BF16 prefill. ## Validation - New `test_rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup.py` covers bucket coverage and the opt-in. A new KDA online-loading test checks the alignment padding: loading completes after six shards and the padding stays zero. pre-commit clean; GPU reload tests in `test_reload.py` not run. - End to end: one run per configuration, below. No accuracy evaluation. Variance not measured; the closest pair, BF16 with and without warmup, differs by 0.4% in throughput and 0.01 s / 1.2 s in mean / p90 TTFT. - KDA in_proj keeps main's 16-row alignment: AITER v0.1.27, main's pin, tunes 6288x7168 at the latency of 6400x7168. Not re-run end to end on v0.1.27.
End-to-end benchmark Kimi-K3, agentic multi-turn trace at concurrency 48, 1 prefill + 1 decode instance on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X, TP8 + DCP8, FP8 KV cache, MoRIIO. vLLM ROCm nightly `81198e97` with these changes mounted as file overlays. Online FP8 prefill means `--quantization-config` with `fp8_per_channel` targets on the attention projections, shared experts and dense MLPs, plus `re:.*\.routed_expert_down_proj$: mxfp4` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1` from the down_proj step on. | Prefill | Run | Total tok/s/GPU | TTFT mean / p90 | |---|---|---|---| | BF16 GEMMs | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39140308384) | 10775 | 4.50 s / 9.22 s | | Online FP8 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39226586488) | 10626 | 5.35 s / 13.31 s | | + down_proj MXFP4 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39253422535) | 10663 | 5.14 s / 12.73 s | | + in_proj pad 128 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39260261980) | 10552 | 5.78 s / 14.18 s | | + GEMM warmup (this PR) | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39352208397) | 10851 | 4.05 s / 8.50 s | | BF16 GEMMs + warmup only | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39487012805) | 10729 | 4.51 s / 10.45 s | The `+ in_proj pad 128` step was needed on that nightly's AITER v0.1.24.post1, whose table tunes 6400x7168 but not 6288x7168; this PR no longer pads. In v0.1.27's `a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv` (gfx950, 256 CUs) the 6288/6400 latency ratio has median 1.00 and range 0.92 to 1.09 over the 52 M values from 256 to 8192, and both shapes use the same FlyDSL kernel at M=8192. Padding alone is slower because the newly tuned kernels are built on first use while serving; the warmup moves that to startup. Warmup without online quantization gives no gain. Load-time checks: 92 `routed_expert_down_proj` on `Mxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`, 69 `in_proj_qkvgfab` on `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel`.
## Details - Warmup sizes: AITER buckets up to `max_num_batched_tokens`, multiples of 8 up to 512, and `max_num_batched_tokens - 1` for Triton's divisibility specialization; 164 forwards at 8192 tokens, 541 to 585 s on the Kimi-K3 prefill instance (104 s without online quantization). The measured runs added a second timing sweep, dropped here. - An online config whose `linear` default does not ignore `routed_expert_down_proj` now quantizes it; add it to `ignore` to keep BF16. ---

title: [Bugfix][Perf][ROCm] RDNA launch config for kernel_paged_attention_2d
author: lijipeng787
body:
## Overview On RDNA (`on_gfx1x()`), launch `kernel_paged_attention_2d` with `num_stages=1` and 4 / 8 / 16 warps by tile size, for tiles of 32+ tokens or ≥ 4096 elements. This fixes the gfx1201 Pattern A decode failures of #62697 that remain after #63268, and speeds up decode on gfx1100 and gfx1201. No open PR changes this launch config; #45916 and #58156 (open) add split-KV decode for RDNA and leave it as is. #58156 edits the same launch call, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. ## Claims - gfx1201, KV cache < 2 GiB: the new test shape and the #62697 reproducer case `p1-d128-bs528-fp16` fail on main (NaN rows, GPU memory fault) and pass with this PR. Pattern B (the cache writer) is not addressed. - Decode throughput, PR / main at batch 1 / 32, with GSM8K unchanged: | model | gfx1100 | gfx1201 | |---|---|---| | gemma-3-1b-it | 1.51× / 1.57× | 1.94× / 1.81× | | Qwen3.5-9B | 1.15× / 1.10× | 1.07–1.09× / 1.14–1.16×* | | Qwen3-4B `--block-size 32` | 1.30× / 1.50× | 1.12× / 1.05× | `LLM(..., attention_backend="ROCM_ATTN")` (the RDNA default), CUDA graphs, 1024-token random prompts, 256 output tokens; GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy. Ratio: median of 4 adjacent main/PR run pairs (2 GPUs × 2); on gfx1100 every pair is within 2% of it. \* gfx1201 runs fall into one of two throughput levels for both variants; these ratios compare runs at the same level, one per level. ## Validation W7900 (gfx1100) and R9700 (gfx1201), ROCm 10.0, Triton 3.8.0: - `test_prefix_prefill.py --optional`: no failures with this PR. On gfx1201 main, 4 nodes fail: the new shape, plus three `test_contexted_kv_attention_f32` nodes that hang. - Of 41 kernel cases from an earlier failure sweep, 35 fail on main; none fail with this PR. - `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` and pre-commit pass.
New test on gfx1201: fails on main, passes with this PR (10/10 runs each) ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py -k "test_qwen3_nonstandard_block_size and False-chunked_prefill_paged_decode and 32-4-128-528" ``` main: ``` E AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close! E Mismatched elements: 4096 / 21860352 (0.0%) E Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (5336, 0, 0) (up to 0.0001 allowed) Warning: Queue error - HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT FAILED tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py::test_qwen3_nonstandard_block_size[False-chunked_prefill_paged_decode-cuda:0-dtype0-32-4-128-528] ``` This PR: ``` PASSED tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py::test_qwen3_nonstandard_block_size[False-chunked_prefill_paged_decode-cuda:0-dtype0-32-4-128-528] ```
Test environment - GPUs: Radeon PRO W7900 (gfx1100) and Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), several of each; one GPU per test process, no other workload on it - Host: Ubuntu 24.04.3, kernel 6.8.0-138, amdgpu 6.16.13 - Container: `vllm/rocm10.0.0_rdna_ubuntu24.04_py3.14_pytorch_2.12.0_vllm_0.28.0.dgpu:v2.1.0`; Python 3.14.7, torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0 - vLLM: main @ a7407ab44 vs this branch, Python sources mounted over the image; `_C` / `_rocm_C` built from a7407ab44 (`PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx1100;gfx1201"`) and shared by both
## Details - Trigger: Triton uses AMD buffer ops for tensors ≤ 2 GiB. Turning them off, a KV cache > 2 GiB, or `num_stages=1` each remove the failures. The Triton/LLVM root cause is unknown, so this is an empirical workaround. gfx1100 never failed. - A few shapes get slower, down to 0.83×. Other RDNA parts were not measured. - Only `ROCM_ATTN` calls this kernel; the opt-in `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` (#59132) uses its own kernel and is unchanged. - No `LLM`-level test: the models we ran on main (Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3-1.7B / Qwen3-4B `--block-size 32`, with KV caches down to 0.52 GiB) did not hit the failing shapes, so the regression test is at kernel level. - CI has no RDNA runner, so the new test only catches regressions on gfx12. ---

title: [Perf][Mamba] Use the shared checkpoint exporter for Mamba2 and drop ssd_checkpoint
author: roikoren755
body:
## Overview Mamba2 prefill checkpoints now use the shared `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter` (introduced for GDN/KDA in #60050) instead of their own `ssd_checkpoint.py` kernel, which is deleted. Part of the internal prefill checkpoint work tracked in #52959. ## Claims - One checkpoint-store kernel for GDN, KDA and Mamba2 instead of two. Diff: +53 / -157 in `vllm/` (including the deleted 118-line file) and +35 / -17 in tests (the Mamba2 test retarget, plus new Mamba2 and wide-state cases in the exporter test). - Mamba2 checkpoint store time is faster than the removed kernel in 39 of 48 cases, and no TP1/2/4 case is slower. The 3 slower cases are all TP8 (Nano 30B at 1-2 rows, Super at 2 rows), by at most +2.9 µs per step. GDN/KDA are 13-37% faster at 4+ rows on TP1/2. Across 96 cases, 25 are slower than main by at most +15 µs per step, mostly at TP4/8 with 1-2 rows (details and numbers below). - Stops Mamba2 from writing skipped prefill checkpoints into the null block. Under the default sparse retention a non-final prefill chunk that spans two or more Mamba blocks gets a checkpoint offset but a null destination (by design since #59175, so that the export is masked); the removed kernel had no null check and wrote it into block 0, while the shared kernel skips it (reproduced with `check_mamba2_null_block_write.py`, which runs both kernels on a Super TP1 row whose column is null). Latent: no reader of block 0 was found (details under "Behavior of the swap"). ## Validation Hardware: one B200, torch 2.14.0+cu130. All outputs are bitwise equal to the baseline kernel before timing. Tests (all pass): ``` pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_checkpoint_state.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_checkpoint_exporter.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_mixer2.py tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints.py tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py -v pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py -k mrv2_async_flashinfer -v ``` `tests/kernels/mamba` runs in CI (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`). No CI test exercises the Mamba2 mixer's internal checkpoints end to end (the kernel is covered by the unit test above), so that path was checked only by the Nemotron serving run below. The test changes are pointing `test_store_selects_the_checkpoint_from_all_chunk_states` at the shared exporter, and adding a `mamba2` caller and a wide recurrent state shape to `test_checkpoint_exporter.py`. The wide shape launches programs past the conv window, so the guard is covered for correctness (not speed). With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, serving Nemotron 3.5 Super at TP1 (4224-token Mamba block) under the traffic below triggered no host-device sync from the exporter; afterwards the server was healthy and prefix-cache hits were recorded: ``` VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code 2>&1 | tee serve.log & M=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4; PORT=8000 B="vllm bench serve --model $M --port $PORT --seed 0 --num-warmups 4" # 1) one long prompt at a time (1 checkpoint row per step) $B --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 32 \ --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 # 2) bursts of 2.7k-token prompts (below the Mamba block, so no checkpoints) $B --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2700 --random-output-len 32 \ --num-prompts 120 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 6 # 3) repeated long prefixes (checkpoint exports, then prefix-cache hits) $B --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 6144 \ --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 1024 --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 4 \ --prefix-repetition-output-len 32 --num-prompts 64 --request-rate inf # 4) mixed lengths, 600-11400 tokens (up to 3 checkpoint rows per step) $B --dataset-name random --random-input-len 6000 --random-range-ratio 0.9 \ --random-output-len 32 --num-prompts 64 --request-rate inf curl -s localhost:$PORT/health -o /dev/null -w "health: %{http_code}\n" grep -i -E "traceback|synchron|error" serve.log | head curl -s localhost:$PORT/metrics | grep -E "^vllm:prefix_cache_(queries|hits)" ``` GSM8K (`python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 50`, 1319 questions, greedy) on the same server without `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`. Every prompt starts with the same 50-shot prefix, longer than the 4224-token Mamba block, so the first prompts export checkpoints inside it and the rest resume from them (prefix-cache hit rate about 86% on both servers). Two runs per server: | | run 1 | run 2 | |---|---|---| | main (`24324ef0f6`) | 0.928 | 0.926 | | this PR | 0.926 | 0.926 | The two servers differ by at most 3 questions, within run-to-run variation. The two assertions added to `export()` (see "Behavior of the swap") were profiled in a real Nemotron 3 Nano 30B-A3B step that exports a checkpoint in all 23 Mamba layers: one 4177-token prompt, one more than the 4176-token Mamba block, with fresh tokens every step (`profile_mamba2_checkpoint_step.py`, attached, 30 profiled steps per run). They add about 1.4 µs of host time per `export()` call (75.1 vs 73.7 µs median, inflated by the profiler). The GPU idle time right before each store kernel is unchanged: 34.8 vs 36.0 µs median, within the 33-55 µs spread between steps. Benchmarks (microbenchmark scripts that are not part of this PR, attached). Shapes are per-rank states derived from the models' Hugging Face configs. Each arm is timed over 3 rounds in rotating order with fresh buffers; a second copy of the baseline is the noise control, and the `noise` column (mostly ≤0.03) is the floor a ratio has to clear. `step` = per-layer delta × layer count. Each attached output comes from one command, run from the repo root with the attached scripts saved under `benchmarks/kernels/`: ``` python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mamba_prefill_checkpoint.py # out_benchmark.log python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mamba_prefill_checkpoint.py --block-sweep # out_sweep_benchmark.log python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mamba_checkpoint_exporter_callers.py --block-sweep # out_sweep_callers.log python benchmarks/kernels/scratch_mamba_checkpoint_ablation.py # out_ablation_sass.log python benchmarks/kernels/check_mamba2_null_block_write.py # check_mamba2_null_block_write.log ``` **What "rows" means.** A row is a request in the step that exports a checkpoint: its final prefill chunk spans more than one Mamba block, so the checkpoint falls inside this chunk (`is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid`). Decodes and other prefills add no rows. 1 row is one long prompt finishing in the step; several rows are a burst of mid-length prompts finishing together. A step holds at most about `max_num_batched_tokens / mamba_block_size` rows. Super at TP1 has a 4224-token block, so at most 3 rows at the default 16k budget. The block size is set so an attention page is at least as large as a Mamba page, so it shrinks with TP once the attention KV heads are replicated and the per-rank Mamba state keeps shrinking; higher TP therefore allows more rows per step (not measured here). The kernel only reads 3 conv tokens and one state row per request, so lengths do not affect its time, only the row count does. Mamba2, new exporter vs the removed SSD store (`out_benchmark.log`): | shape | rows | SSD µs | new µs | ratio | step µs | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Super (128 heads) TP1 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 4.70 / 6.43 / 9.22 / 12.26 | 4.13 / 5.60 / 8.26 / 11.04 | 0.88 / 0.87 / 0.90 / 0.90 | -23 / -33 / -38 / -49 | | Super TP4 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 3.49 / 4.00 / 4.83 / 5.73 | 3.14 / 3.49 / 4.19 / 4.77 | 0.90 / 0.87 / 0.87 / 0.83 | -14 / -20 / -26 / -38 | | Super TP8 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 3.17 / 3.36 / 3.94 / 4.22 | 3.17 / 3.39 / 3.74 / 4.26 | 1.00 / 1.01 / 0.95 / 1.01 | 0 / +1 / -8 / +1 | | Nano 30B TP1 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 3.97 / 4.77 / 6.30 / 7.74 | 3.52 / 4.26 / 5.44 / 6.91 | 0.89 / 0.89 / 0.86 / 0.89 | -10 / -12 / -20 / -19 | | Nano 30B TP8 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 3.10 / 3.36 / 3.46 / 3.68 | 3.23 / 3.46 / 3.42 / 3.58 | 1.04 / 1.03 / 0.99 / 0.97 | +3 / +2 / -1 / -2 | Across all 48 Mamba2 cases 39 are faster, 6 are within noise and 3 are slower: Nano 30B TP8 at 1 and 2 rows (+3 and +2 µs per step) and Super TP8 at 2 rows (+1). GDN/KDA, the exporter at 512 vs main's kernel (`out_sweep_callers.log`): | shape | rows | main µs | new µs | ratio | step µs | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Kimi K3 (KDA) TP1 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 6.18 / 9.92 / 17.41 / 24.86 | 4.83 / 6.91 / 11.30 / 15.81 | 0.78 / 0.70 / 0.65 / 0.64 | -93 / -208 / -422 / -625 | | Kimi K3 TP8 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 3.04 / 3.36 / 4.35 / 5.28 | 3.14 / 3.42 / 4.10 / 4.51 | 1.03 / 1.02 / 0.94 / 0.85 | +7 / +4 / -18 / -53 | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (GDN) TP1 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 3.71 / 5.09 / 7.65 / 10.24 | 3.62 / 4.16 / 5.47 / 6.98 | 0.97 / 0.82 / 0.71 / 0.68 | -3 / -28 / -65 / -98 | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B TP8 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 | 2.91 / 3.04 / 3.17 / 3.42 | 3.26 / 3.13 / 3.30 / 3.39 | 1.12 / 1.03 / 1.04 / 0.99 | +11 / +3 / +4 / -1 | Across the 96 GDN/KDA cases (all six models, TP1/2/4/8, 1/2/4/6 rows) 63 are faster, 8 are within noise and 25 are slower: ratio up to 1.144 and up to +15.0 µs per step (both Qwen3-Next-80B TP8, 1 row), per-layer cost +0.06 to +0.42 µs. 21 of the 25 are TP4/8 and 21 are at 1-2 rows; the four at 4+ rows are all TP8 (ratio at most 1.05). At 4+ rows on TP1/2 all 24 cases are 13-37% faster. The slower cases are ~3 µs launches, where the same case moved by up to 0.4 µs between two runs of this benchmark (more than the in-run noise floor), so individual verdicts there are not stable; the counts and the TP1/2 results are. Not validated: end-to-end serving throughput (microbenchmarks only), how often real traffic reaches 4+ checkpoint rows in a step (3 at most for Super at TP1; higher TP allows more, but was not measured), and any hardware other than B200. ## Details **Why this swap makes sense now.** Before #60050 the two checkpoint-store kernels were not interchangeable: the shared one read each checkpoint's recurrent state from row `i` of the prefill output, while Mamba2's SSD store picked it out of all chunk states through `checkpoint_chunk_idx`. #60050 added `HAS_RECURRENT_ROWS` (`recurrent_rows`) to the shared kernel, which is exactly that selection. Since then the two kernels are basically identical: they differ in launch configuration (block size 1024 vs 256 on main), in the null-block and short-offset masks described under "Behavior of the swap" (the shared kernel already has them), and in how the conv window is addressed (the removed kernel took `x` as `(dim, tokens)`; the shared one takes `raw_qkv` as `(tokens, width)`, and the mixer now passes `x.transpose(0, 1)`). This PR sets the shared kernel's block size to 512 and makes its strides runtime arguments, so Mamba2 can use it without losing time and the duplicate can go. **Why the kernel changed.** Three changes to `store_cache_checkpoints_kernel`, each measured separately (the callers benchmark's `cx`, `guard` and `wide` arms each take one change out of the shipped kernel; `scratch_mamba_checkpoint_ablation.py` is a replica kernel that toggles one change at a time, with SASS diffs in `out_ablation_sass.log`): - **Block size 256 -> 512 (one value for all callers).** The removed Mamba2 kernel used 1024-wide blocks, and at 256 the shared kernel was 1.19-1.27x slower than it at 4-6 rows on large states (Super and Nano 4B at TP1), so Mamba2 would have regressed. 512 has a better worst case than 1024: 1024 is slower than the old kernel in 11 of the 24 TP4/TP8 cases, by up to about +12 µs per step, and it is ahead of 512 in only 7 of 48 cases (by 1-6%, mostly TP1/2 at 4+ rows). GDN/KDA share the kernel and get 512 as well. Keeping them at 256 was measured and is worse: with the conv guard below, 44 of 96 GDN/KDA cases were slower than main (up to ratio 1.19, +20 µs per step, both at Qwen3-Next-80B TP8 1 row), against 25 at 512 (up to ratio 1.14). A larger block means fewer programs, so the guard's fixed cost matters less. (The 256 and 1024 figures come from the block-size sweeps `out_sweep_benchmark.log` and `out_sweep_callers.log`, which time 256, 512 and 1024 side by side. `out_sweep_callers.log` is also the source of the GDN/KDA table; `out_sweep_benchmark.log` is a separate run from the Mamba2 table, so its 512 counts differ by a case or two.) - **Strides as runtime arguments, not `tl.constexpr`.** Specializing the 8 strides costs about 6% on average (`cx/cur` column of the callers benchmark: 0.97-1.20, mean 1.06 over the 144 Mamba2/GDN/KDA shapes), most at 1-2 rows (mean 1.08 and 1.07) and least on large states (TP1 at 4-6 rows: mean 1.015). The SASS has 192 vs 184 static instructions (216 vs 192 at TP8 shapes), with more IADD3/IMAD where runtime strides use LEA, and an identical sequence of global memory ops. On the conv-only Qwen4Exp PLE shape the two are within 2% (`cx/cur` 0.98-1.01). - **Skip the conv window in programs that don't cover it.** The conv section used to run, fully masked off, in every program. Guarding it on `program_id(1) * BLOCK_SIZE < WIDTH * STATE_LEN` cuts the time by 15-22% on large states in the ablation (for example 14.2 -> 11.1 µs at Super TP1, 6 rows) and is about neutral on small ones (-5% to +3% at Super TP4/TP8 and Nano 30B TP8). In the callers benchmark, removing it (`wide` arm) makes TP1 shapes at 4-6 rows 13-29% slower (mean 22%). **Tradeoff of the conv guard.** The guard is what makes the Mamba2 swap faster than the removed kernel. Removing it (`wide` arm: the shipped kernel without the guard) measured, by rows (mean over the 12 shapes per model kind; positive means removing it is slower): | rows | GDN | KDA | Mamba2 | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 0% | +1% | -1% | | 2 | +6% | +2% | +4% | | 4 | +10% | +8% | +10% | | 6 | +14% | +12% | +15% | So the guard is about neutral on average at 1 row and wins from 2 rows up, by up to about 255 µs per step on TP1/2 (Kimi K3 TP1, 6 rows; Super TP1 at 6 rows about 125 µs). It loses on a few launch-bound shapes: 15 of the 72 1-2 row cases are 3% or more faster without it (13 of them TP4/8), by at most +0.5 µs per layer (+19 µs per step, Super TP8 2 rows). Without it Mamba2 would be slower than the removed kernel at TP1 with 2+ rows (Super TP1 about 1.03x at 2 rows and 1.15x at 6, from the ablation). On GDN/KDA's 1-2 row TP4/8 cases (2.6% slower than main on average) the guard accounts for about 1 point: removing it makes them 1.2% faster, while going back to 256 or to constexpr strides alone makes them 6% and 9% slower. The benchmarks' main kernel predates #63761's int64 cast; the `guard` arm (the shipped kernel with an int32 index) shows the cast is free (-2.4% to +2.0% per case), so the comparisons with main still hold. **Behavior of the swap.** The shared kernel also skips null destination blocks, which the removed kernel did not check, and for an offset shorter than the conv window it skips the conv window but still stores the recurrent state. The manager would cache such a block as a valid checkpoint, so `export()` now asserts that every nonzero offset covers the conv window, and that `recurrent_rows` has one entry per checkpoint row. Both are host-side checks with no device sync. Neither can fire today: a valid checkpoint's offset is at least `hash_block_size` (`query_start + hash_block_size <= checkpoint_position`), above the 3-token Mamba2 conv window, and every caller sizes recurrent_rows per checkpoint row. The null-block skip is reachable. Under the default sparse retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`) the manager reserves a checkpoint block only for the chunk that ends the prefill, and leaves the column null for earlier chunks so that the export is masked (#59175, `test_checkpoint_reservation_matches_worker`). An earlier chunk that spans two or more Mamba blocks still gets an offset, and the removed kernel wrote that checkpoint into the null block (block 0); the shared kernel skips it. `check_mamba2_null_block_write.py` reproduces this with Super TP1's geometry (a 12672-token first chunk, checkpoint offset 8448 in column 1): the removed store writes the row's checkpoint into block 0 and the shared exporter leaves it untouched, while a row with a real block is written identically by both. No reader of that write was found: Mamba's decode conv and SSU kernels skip `NULL_BLOCK_ID` rows, and cache groups overlay the same memory, so it also lands in attention's block 0, which only the FA4 restricted-sliding-window gap path assumes is zero (not used by full-attention hybrids such as Nemotron). That needs a prompt longer than the token budget and a budget of at least two Mamba blocks (Super TP1: prompts over 16k tokens at the default budget). The `mamba2` case in `test_checkpoint_exporter.py` covers the skip. Mamba2 passes the pre-conv activations through `x.transpose(0, 1)`, the same view the removed kernel read. **Considered: keeping main's launch shape for GDN/KDA.** A per-caller option that keeps GDN/KDA on 256-wide blocks without the guard, with only the runtime strides, is the callers benchmark's `wide256` arm. It is slower than main in 69 of 96 GDN/KDA cases (up to 1.04x, +58 µs per step at Kimi K3 TP1 with 6 rows) and gives up the 13-37% gains at 4+ rows on TP1/2. On the 1-2 row TP4/8 cases it would be 0.9% slower than main on average instead of 2.6%. So all callers share 512 and the guard. **Limitations.** Measured on B200 only; microbenchmarks, not serving. The shared kernel is also used by the ROCm Kimi-K3 KDA exporter (conv half only, `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_checkpoint.py`), so the 512 block size and conv guard apply there too; `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py` covers it but needs gfx950 and was not run. The Qwen4Exp PLE short conv (#61601: conv-only with a token map, one layer) shares the kernel too. It is 2-6% slower than main at 1, 2 and 6 rows and within noise at 4, at most +0.19 µs per step, which comes from the 512 block size (at 256 the shipped kernel is up to 6% faster on that shape); its conv window spans every program, so the guard skips nothing there. **Related PRs.** No open PR does this swap (searched 2026-10-26: issue #52959 and open PRs that cite it, `ssd_checkpoint`, `store_cache_checkpoints_kernel`, `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter`, "Mamba2 prefill checkpoint"). #61601 (Qwen4Exp PLE checkpoints) and #61497 (Mamba2 SSD host overhead) are merged, and this PR is rebased on them. #59175 is where the manager leaves a non-final chunk's checkpoint column null for the exporter to skip (see "Behavior of the swap"). Open PRs near this code: #60659 (GDN Triton/FLA and AITER checkpoints) and #61951 (ROCm GLM-5.3-Flash KDA on Triton) add new `export()` callers without changing the exporter, so they pick up these kernel changes; #61501 (opt-in FlashInfer SSD prefill scan, draft) edits `conv_ssm_forward` next to the Mamba2 export but keeps checkpointed prefills on the Triton scan; #61466 (per-layer checkpoint alignment) edits `mamba_mixer2.py`'s imports and spec override; #60888 (checkpoints at or before the initial-state column, draft) changes the scheduler and manager rules, not the exporter, and like #59175 expects checkpoints into null columns to be skipped; #62232 (Mamba2 prefill checkpoints on CPU) adds a CPU path to `store_prefill_checkpoint`, which this PR deletes, and a test to `test_mamba2_checkpoint_state.py`; whichever lands second moves that path into `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter.export()`, which, like the removed kernel, always launches Triton (Mamba2 checkpoints on CPU are broken on main too, #62153).
Scripts and outputs

[benchmark_mamba_checkpoint_exporter_callers.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964545/benchmark_mamba_checkpoint_exporter_callers.py) [benchmark_mamba_prefill_checkpoint.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964546/benchmark_mamba_prefill_checkpoint.py) [check_mamba2_null_block_write.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964550/check_mamba2_null_block_write.log) [check_mamba2_null_block_write.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964552/check_mamba2_null_block_write.py) [mamba_checkpoint_bench_utils.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964553/mamba_checkpoint_bench_utils.py) [out_ablation_sass.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964556/out_ablation_sass.log) [out_benchmark.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964557/out_benchmark.log) [out_sweep_benchmark.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964558/out_sweep_benchmark.log) [out_sweep_callers.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964559/out_sweep_callers.log) [scratch_mamba_checkpoint_ablation.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33964560/scratch_mamba_checkpoint_ablation.py) [profile_mamba2_checkpoint_step.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34316357/profile_mamba2_checkpoint_step.py) [profile_mamba2_checkpoint_step.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34316397/profile_mamba2_checkpoint_step.log)

title: [Fast Start] Support ModelOpt CUTLASS FP8 weight-cache restarts
author: liusy58
body:
## Overview Enable serialized ModelOpt per-tensor and per-channel FP8 linear weights to be reused by the weight-cache daemon with CUTLASS. Related to #56049; depends on #63672 for restoring CUTLASS's logical output width. Incremental review: https://github.com/liusy58/vllm/compare/35711168b0135573234bbaa4bd8f9e8fe32647e8...7f75449765425d759565d3a770d829070d909f99 (the GitHub diff against main includes the prerequisite). ## Claims - Enable CUDA IPC for ModelOpt `FP8` and `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` linear layers using CUTLASS and the default format scheme. - Restore the transposed-weight layout metadata without transposing, requantizing, padding, or mutating the daemon's already processed weights/scales a second time. - Keep other ModelOpt FP8 backends and block FP8 unsupported; existing FP4/MXFP8 capability rules are unchanged. ## Validation Current head `7f75449765425d759565d3a770d829070d909f99` includes main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`. October 29 agent-run validation after resolving the inherited online-FP8 import conflict with upstream #60163. The merge retains both CUTLASS and Humming imports, the upstream processed-dimension metadata, and upstream rejection of the unsupported Humming per-token/channel path. It adds no Humming IPC capability. | Check | Exact-head result | |---|---| | `modelopt-layers` | 117 passed, 5 deselected, 14 warnings in 85.71s (0:01:25) | | `modelopt-model` | 1 passed, 70 deselected, 18 warnings in 78.89s (0:01:18) | | Full feature-file and commit hooks | Passed, including mypy and ruff | Runtime: NVIDIA B300, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, process-local CUDA 13.4 compatibility libraries. The two stable-libtorch extensions are from the official CUDA 13.0 wheel for main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`, checked against wheel RECORD hashes and linked only into task worktrees. The shared venv and host driver were unchanged. This does not validate the full upstream PyTorch 2.14 dependency matrix. Full-model checks use TP1, BF16, eager mode, CUTLASS and TRITON_ATTN, with the existing batch-invariant exact greedy-output comparisons. Each completed case checks ordinary load, missing-daemon fallback, IPC and a second IPC load; both IPC loads forbid fallback. These are output-equivalence smoke checks, not accuracy or performance benchmarks. No multi-GPU, ROCm or other-backend result is claimed. ModelOpt full-model tests use their checked-in configurations without checkpoint/budget overrides. Per-channel/per-token checkpoint: `CedricHwang/qwen2.5-0.5b-modelopt-fp8-pc-pt`, pinned `d9c87375a9b950b1c7965a1110ac6ca455929726`.
Commands for this revision All commands set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, `PYTHONPATH` to the corresponding worktree and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/liusy/codex-runtime/cuda-compat-13-4/usr/local/cuda-13.4/compat`. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k 'not checkpoint_setup and not nested_mixed_checkpoint and not mixed_dspark_checkpoint' -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k modelopt_fp8 -q ```
GitHub checks for the new head are pending at publication. No Buildkite GPU-suite pass or completed human review is claimed. AI assistance and original feature baselines are recorded below.
Earlier validation and original feature baselines (previous heads) NVIDIA B300, BF16, CUTLASS linear backend. The real-model test uses `CedricHwang/qwen2.5-0.5b-modelopt-fp8-pc-pt`, pinned to `d9c87375a9b950b1c7965a1110ac6ca455929726`, TP1, eager mode, TRITON_ATTN and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. | Check | Before implementation, base `93a266aaa2` plus new tests | With implementation | |---|---|---| | Real checkpoint, ordinary loading → missing-daemon fallback → IPC → second IPC | 1 failed, 48.62s: daemon rejects ModelOptLinearMethod | 1 passed, 74.98s; exact output equality for both prompts × 16 generated tokens across all four loads | | Fused linear layers, tensor/channel scales × aligned/padded output widths, two attachments each | 4 failed, 10.28s: pre-processed weights rejected | All 4 pass; exact outputs, shared pointers and tensor contents preserved | | Unsupported Torch/Triton backend rejection | — | Both pass | | Existing ModelOpt suite excluding five checkpoint-setup/integration cases; includes all six new layer cases | — | 113 passed, 5 deselected, 72.13s | | Changed-file and commit hooks | — | Passed, including mypy and ruff | Both real IPC loads set `fallback=False`. The deterministic generation comparison is a smoke evaluation, not a broad accuracy benchmark. Full-model coverage is per-channel/per-token; static per-tensor FP8 is covered by real CUDA layers with unequal fused-projection scales. No performance, multi-GPU, other-platform, or FP8-MoE claim is made. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k modelopt_fp8 -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k 'preprocessed_shared_weights or preprocessed_unsupported_backend' -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k 'not checkpoint_setup and not nested_mixed_checkpoint and not mixed_dspark_checkpoint' -q ``` `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` assumes the pinned checkpoint and OPT-125m configuration are cached; omit it for the initial download. Before implementation the first command reported: ```text UnsupportedQuantForIPCError: layer model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj: ModelOptLinearMethod does not support loading from pre-processed weights. 1 failed, 70 deselected, 16 warnings in 48.62s ``` The four new shared-weight layer cases reported `RuntimeError: layer : ModelOptLinearMethod does not support pre-processed weights`. With the implementation, all six new cases passed in 12.00s; the full selected regression run above was repeated after test formatting/type-check fixes. Runs emitted existing torch deprecation warnings. Initial setup attempts encountered a missing offline revision reference and a changing-free-memory profiling assertion; the pinned, isolated baseline above then reproduced the intended rejection.
## Details The daemon currently rejects every ModelOpt FP8 linear method even when CUTLASS can consume the processed tensor layout. Opt in only the two plain FP8 weight schemes with the actual selected CUTLASS kernel and no format wrapper. The engine restores `processed_weight_dims=(0, 1)` and returns before post-load weight transformations. CUTLASS logical width is initialized from configuration by #63672, so padded shared weights still produce the original output width. The existing L4 preload CI step now selects the real ModelOpt IPC test and the six layer cases, with dependencies on the changed ModelOpt source and tests. The preload feature guide documents the formats, matching daemon/engine kernel configuration, and exclusions. Local validation used B300; L4 CI has not been run locally. No new scheduler/model-runner path or steady-state GPU synchronization. Duplicate checks on October 26 covered #56049 and its comments, issue-linked PRs, and open searches for ModelOpt FP8 preload/pre-processed weights. #63672 covers online quantization and NVFP4, #63673 covers compressed-tensors FP8, and #62036 covers W4A16 NVFP4 layerwise reload; none implements this serialized ModelOpt FP8 IPC path. This branch includes main `373614f66d`. AI assistance: Codex implemented and ran the recorded validation at the submitter's request. This is a draft for human review; no completed human approval or human-run tests are asserted. ---

title: [ROCm][CI] Raise MI300 Core Operation Kernels timeout to 90 min
author: djramic
body: ## Purpose `:amd: (MI300) Core Operation Kernels` timed out at the 45 min limit on every attempt in [ci#97263](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97263) and [ci#97107](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97107). #61862 moved this mirror to `automatic_shard: true` but kept the 45 min timeout of one fixed shard. When the pipeline generator can't fetch main's timings, which happened in both builds, the step runs as one unsharded job, and a full run on MI300 takes about 70 min. This PR raises `timeout_in_minutes` for the AMD mirror from 45 to 90, so that fallback completes. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- Need help on this PR?
