title: [Bugfix][Bench] Handle packed hybrid KV and speculative recurrent state
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Fix `vllm bench forward` on hybrid attention/recurrent models: initialize packed KV caches using manager-block views and reserve/restore all speculative recurrent state slots.

## Claims

- Packed hybrid KV layouts no longer fail with `No block dim of size ...` during benchmark initialization.
- Verify requests get disjoint recurrent scratch blocks for every configured speculative token, and replay restores all those blocks.
- Changes are confined to benchmark setup and replay state; serving execution and the timed model-forward interval are unchanged.

## Validation

GB200 validation of the retained tests: 3 cases passed (native CLI, cache isolation, recurrent state). All targeted pre-commit checks pass.

Base: `b82393b77315692f390880d2e931fdc1fbd13928`. Validation used four GB200 GPUs, native MRV2, and dummy weights (this checks benchmark execution/state, not model accuracy).

| Reproducer | Base | Fixed |
|---|---|---|
| Native GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, FP8 KV, FlashInfer sparse MLA, ngram 5 target-only | All ranks fail: `ValueError: No block dim of size 3979 in (6619401, 64, 132)` | Decode, Verify, Mixed finish; all ranks finite, deterministic, graph/eager relative RMS 0 |
| Tiny Qwen3Next public CLI | `assert 5 == (1 + (7 * 2))` fails: only one state per request | Passes: all speculative slots counted, Verify/Mixed finite and deterministic |
| CPU speculative-state regression | Too few recurrent scratch slots per request | Passes capacity, non-overlap, and complete state-restoration checks |
| CPU packed-view regression | Native GLM reproducer above covers the original layout failure | Passes; adjacent interleaved layers remain unchanged |

Native cases: `decode=1*1@512`, `verify=2*6@512:5`, `mixed=128@512,2*6@512:5`; two samples of two replays. Measured medians were 4.723 / 8.443 / 20.134 ms respectively, with sample spreads 0.04% / 0.03% / 0.05%. These are execution checks, not a speedup claim.

Commands (run from this checkout with the installed vLLM environment):

```bash
/home/woosuk/workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k 'test_bench_packed_kv_blocks or test_bench_speculative_mamba_blocks or test_bench_forward_hybrid_verify' -v
```

Final CPU selection: 7 passed; public CLI: 1 passed (53.47 s), base: 1 failed (52.53 s).

The public CLI regression creates a local tiny Qwen3Next model and checks finite, deterministic Verify/Mixed replay. The benchmark instantiates the real LLM engine. No checkpoint loading behavior changes; dummy weights are appropriate to this forward-state regression.

## Details

Hybrid cache groups can pack multiple attention kernel blocks inside one manager block and interleave layers. The existing `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache_to_manager_blocks` reconstructs the correct manager view without copying. Recurrent state requires one base slot plus `MambaSpec.num_speculative_blocks`; unlike attention tails, every recurrent slot may be read or overwritten during verification.

These three fixes form one benchmark-state correctness change: without the packed-view fix the affected hybrid model cannot initialize; without either recurrent-state fix verification allocates or restores the wrong state. The CPU tests check allocation capacity and memory isolation without pinning block IDs or a complete storage layout. The snapshots use additional GPU memory proportional to the actual speculative state slots. Their copies remain outside the measured interval.

Duplicate-work checks searched open PRs for `"bench forward" "KV"`, `"bench forward" "Mamba"`, `"bench forward" "KDA"`, and `"packed" "benchmark"`. No open PR addressed these benchmark-state failures. The issue inventory came from local model experiments and has no linked GitHub issue number. Existing packed-cache connector and kernel PRs affect different paths.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement, test, and prepare this change. The human submitter confirmed review of every changed line and execution of the relevant tests before submission.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Build the SWA decode metadata in one launch
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview With `--monokernel` on gfx950 (MI355X), DeepSeek-V4.1 decode batches of up to 32 rows now build their SWA metadata with `swa_decode_meta`'s single Triton launch (#60731). Before, they took vLLM's 8 launches per SWA group. #60731 enabled the kernel only on gfx942, but the kernel has no arch-specific code. This PR converges with #63994: it takes #63994's gate, `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` (`on_gfx942() or on_gfx950()`), and adds the gate test, the MI355 CI step and the GPU validation below. ## Claims - **49 fewer launches per decode step at c1: 114 to 65.** That is 7 SWA groups (4 target, 3 DSpark draft), each going from 8 launches to 1. Counted in a torch-profiler trace of each arm. - **Decode step (ITL p50): c1 -100 us (-1.75%), c2 -80 us (-1.16%).** - Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X TP4, `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6 (synthetic AL 3.87, AV off), 32k in / 1k out, on `main` nightly 5d35ce3934. - Runs: 2 rounds with the arms' GPU halves swapped. The per-round deltas are -1.85% and -1.66% at c1, and -1.70% and -0.61% at c2. - **Same metadata, same accuracy.** - On MI355X, the kernel test matches vLLM's ops. - With AV off, GSM8K matches base at 4 parallel requests, where every decode-only step takes the new path (6 runs per arm), and at 8 parallel (10 runs per arm). - Acceptance length (AL) on first passes and on passes with a per-request `cache_salt` is 3.577 in both arms. - With AV on (1 server per arm), GSM8K and AL match as well. - **Unchanged:** gfx942, runs without `--monokernel`, other arches, and prefill, mixed or >32-row batches. The gate test covers arch x flag; the row and prefill guards are #60731's and untouched. The servers run `--monokernel` with DSpark k=6, synthetic AL 3.87 and AV off. The workload is random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, 32 prompts per run, 3 runs per point on the same server. Per-server means: -0.006, below the 0.0077 binomial SE of a single run. | | Mono forced off, so the aiter attention reads the kernel's ragged views. 4 parallel, 2 runs per arm, 1 server each. | 0.9132 | 0.9143 | +0.0011 | | Mono forced off, 8 parallel (mostly vLLM's views). 4 runs per arm, 1 server each. | 0.9166 | 0.9177 | +0.0011 | | AV on, 8 parallel: 2 runs per arm, 1 server each | 0.9143 | 0.9166 | +0.0023 | | AV on, 4 parallel: 1 run per arm | 0.9227 | 0.9158 | -0.0068 (per-run sd is about 0.005) | | AL with AV off, on a first pass (only the shared 8-shot prefix cached) or with a per-request `cache_salt` (nothing cached). 8 runs per arm: 6 at 8 parallel, 2 at 4 parallel. | 3.577 | 3.577 | 0 | | AL with AV on, first pass | 3.373 | 3.383 | +0.010 | - **Run-to-run variation:** - Any two AV-off runs with mono on, at the same parallelism, on the same server or not, differ on 53-88 of the 1319 questions (53-92 including the mono-off runs). - Greedy decode on this stack is not run-to-run deterministic on either arm. The first token can differ even with a fresh `cache_salt`, so a text-identity check was not possible. - **The mono-off rows:** - With `--monokernel`, mono consumes only the dense indices and lengths. - The 4-parallel mono-off row is therefore the end-to-end check of the ragged indices, `indptr` and `is_valid_token`. **Sync check.** One TP4 server per arm ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, which polices the worker's `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` after warmup. Each served c1 and c2 (8 requests each, 512 out), 300 GSM8K questions at 4 parallel requests, and 4 greedy probes. Neither arm reported a sync, logged an error or failed a request.

Accuracy servers: "rejection_sample_method":"block", without synthetic_acceptance_length. # AV-on round: "enable_adaptive_verification":true. # Perf: warm up (c2, 4 prompts, 256 out, seed 7), then run each point 3 times: vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 # c2: --max-concurrency 2 --seed 102 # GSM8K: sglang few_shot_gsm8k prompt and scoring, 8 shots, 1319 questions, temperature 0, max 512 tokens, # 8 or 4 parallel requests. # AL = 1 + delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total) / delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total) # Uncached passes: a unique "cache_salt" per request. # Tests on MI355X pytest tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py -k swa_decode_meta pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py # Fail-before: keep the new test, restore the pre-PR vllm files, re-run. git checkout $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/__init__.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/swa_decode_meta.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py # 81 passed, 1 failed ([gfx950-True]) ```
## Details **Change.** `ops.swa_decode_meta_enabled()`, the gate from #63994, returns true with `--monokernel` on ROCm when `on_gfx942()` or `on_gfx950()` holds. Only `swa_decode_meta.build` uses it. The other gfx942 helpers keep `ops.enabled()`. On gfx942 the two gates agree. **Limits.** - The kernel takes at most 32 rows; gfx950 mono takes up to 48. - With AV off at k=6, steps with 5 or more requests keep vLLM's build: the target at 35 or more rows, and the draft, which is padded to the 36-row graph. gfx942 behaves the same. - With AV on, the cutoff is 32 rows, not a request count. - AV-on `--monokernel` deployments now take this path. The AV-on round served without errors and matched base on accuracy and AL. **Related PRs.** - **#63994** (cpersson-amd) made the same change, and the two are converged here. This PR takes #63994's `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` gate, with Carl Persson as co-author of that commit. It adds the gate test, the MI355 CI step (#63994 used the optional `test-amd.yaml` step) and the GPU validation. #63994 can be closed. - **#58352:** it does not conflict textually, but the gains overlap. If it lands first, about 20 of the 49 launches remain (inferred, not measured). - **#61311** touches 4 of this PR's 5 files: `models_basic.yaml`, `ops/__init__.py`, `rocm.py` and `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`. - It renames `KernelConfig.monokernel` and `record_monokernel` to `specialized_decode`, and replaces `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` with `test_dsv41_specialized_decode.py`. - Whichever lands second rebases: rename `_monokernel` in `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` and move the gate test. - **#63486 (draft)** moves the DSv4.1 mono CI and `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`. If it lands first, I drop the `models_basic.yaml` hunk and move the gate test. - **#63891 (draft)** runs fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with `--monokernel`. It adds its own `mi3xx_enabled()` on `on_mi3xx()`, and the same review applies to it. Both PRs touch the same `models_basic.yaml` step and the `ops/__init__.py` docstring; the second to land merges those hunks.
Why the metadata is the same, and who reads it - **What the kernel writes.** `_decode_swa_meta_kernel` is integer Triton with no arch intrinsics. - For rows `[0, n)` it writes `is_valid_token` and the dense window indices and lengths. It sets the lengths from row `n` to the end of the buffer to 0. It writes `indptr[:n+1]` and the ragged indices up to `indptr[n]`. - These are the same values that `torch.ge`, the length fill, `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` (or `ComputeDSparkNoncausalSWAIndicesKernel` for the draft block), `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` and `_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers` produce. - `build()` returns views of the same persistent buffers, with the same lengths: ragged `[:max(n*width, 1)]` and `indptr[:n+1]`. - **Who reads it.** - **Mono:** with `--monokernel`, every target and DSpark-draft layer runs mono on decode-only steps of 48 rows or fewer that replay a FULL graph or run eagerly. Mono reads only the dense indices and lengths, `slot_mapping` and `token_to_req`. - **aiter sparse MLA:** on steps that mono declines, such as PIECEWISE steps, it (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA`) reads the ragged indices between `indptr[t]` and `indptr[t+1]`. It sizes its splits from the ragged view's `numel()`, which is `n*width` on both paths. - **Top-k build:** it reads `is_valid_token` on compressed layers. - Draft and target builders do not share buffers. - **The only bytes that differ** are the ragged entries past `indptr[n]`. vLLM's build copies them from a `torch.empty` tensor; the kernel leaves the previous contents. No reader reads past `indptr`. - **#60154** is on `main` but not in the measured image. It fuses inverse RoPE and the MXFP8 quant into the aiter sparse-MLA output, and does not change the index views that call reads. So this argument holds on current `main`.
An AL caveat for anyone reproducing (affects main, not this PR) On 4 of the 10 AV-off servers, AL fell from about 3.58 to 3.42-3.45 on GSM8K passes that repeated the same prompts. Those passes had about 96% prefix-cache hits, against about 89% on a first pass. The 4 servers were 2 base and 2 PR; one of the PR servers had mono forced off. - The two dropped servers that ran later passes stayed low. - On the one dropped server that also ran passes with a per-request `cache_salt`, those passes stayed at 3.58. - Accuracy did not move. - With AV on, the PR server's repeat pass also fell (3.383 to 3.279); base's did not (3.373 to 3.364). Compare AL on first or salted passes only. I will look into the drop separately.

title: [Spec Decode][DSpark] Batch-sharded sequential block
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
## Context

Under batch-sharded sampling, #64356 shards verification and the draft logits cache by batch position: request `i` is owned by rank `i % tp_size`. The DSpark sequential (Markov) block still runs replicated, though. Every rank computes full-vocab draft logits and samples every request at every draft step, even though each rank only keeps the draft logits of the requests it owns.

## This PR

This PR shards the DSpark sequential block along the same ownership rule, so each rank runs the Markov loop only for its own requests.

**`DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential_sharded`.** Each rank owns at most `capacity = cdiv(num_reqs, tp_size)` requests, so every shape depends only on `num_reqs` and the step is captured in the existing draft CUDA graphs. No second graph set is needed. Each step:
1. Each rank computes its vocab shard of the base draft logits (`compute_draft_logits_local`) for every request, in owner-major order. Padding slots read request 0's rows and are discarded.
2. An all-to-all re-shards the logits from the vocab dimension to the batch dimension, so each rank holds full-vocab logits for its own requests.
3. The Markov loop (`_sample_markov_chain`, now shared with the replicated path) samples those rows and writes the owner's draft logits rows. Padding lanes pass `-1` and write nothing.
4. An all-gather of the drafts (plus the confidences, under adaptive verification) restores batch order on every rank.

**Single NCCL communicator.**
- `PyNcclCommunicator.all_to_all_single` (new) does a variable-split all-to-all, and is graph-capturable when the split sizes are fixed.
- Verification's logits exchange now goes through the same TP PyNCCL communicator, via `all_to_all_vocab_shards` (which replaces `all_to_all_logits`) and `get_tp_pynccl_comm()`.
- A separate c10d all-to-all would make NCCL allocate a second set of point-to-point buffers, about 1.1 GiB per GPU on GB200.
- The c10d path remains as a fallback when PyNCCL is unavailable.

**When the loop stays replicated.** It logs the reason and runs replicated when:
- the draft logits cache is replicated (PCP, a draft watermarker, or a draft model whose fused `sample_sequential` writes the full cache);
- the online acceptance estimator is used;
- top-k Markov sampling is configured;
- the draft model lacks a vocab-sharded `compute_draft_logits_local`;
- PyNCCL is unavailable.

**Models.** `compute_draft_logits_local` is added for DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1 DSpark (NVIDIA) and Qwen3 DSpark.

## Benchmarks

**Setup:**
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark, K=5, probabilistic drafting.
- 4× GB200, TP4, `max_num_seqs=256`, FP8 KV cache, prefix caching off, natural EOS.
- Arms: **main** (55b677b2d1, loop replicated) vs **this PR** (loop sharded). Both use `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, so the comparison isolates the sharded loop.
- 4 boots, ordered PR, main, main, PR.
- SPEED-Bench `low_entropy`, `throughput_2k`, temperature 1. GSM8K: 1319 questions, temperatures 0 and 1.
- Latencies are medians.

### Speed (this PR vs main)

| | c1 | c8 | c16 | c32 | c64 | c128 | c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ITL, AV off | +1.0% | −0.1% | −0.4% | −0.6% | −0.7% | −1.5% | **−2.6%** |
| tok/s, AV off | +1.6% | −0.4% | +1.5% | +2.4% | −0.4% | +4.3% | **+5.4%** |
| ITL, AV on | +1.9% | +0.7% | −0.6% | −0.4% | −0.9% | −2.2% | −1.4% |
| tok/s, AV on | +0.4% | +1.3% | +2.7% | +2.4% | +3.2% | +2.3% | +1.7% |

With AV off, ITL at c256 goes from 48.43 to 47.16 ms; the two boots of each arm agree within about 0.05 ms. Throughput and the AV-on runs are noisier. At c1 the extra collectives cost about 1%. A minimum batch size for the sharded loop (no extra CUDA graphs needed) could remove that cost as a follow-up.

### Accuracy and acceptance (main → this PR)

| | GSM8K t0 | GSM8K t1 | Acceptance length c64 | Acceptance length c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AV off | 0.898 → 0.901 | 0.800 → 0.797 | 3.54 → 3.54 | 3.54 → 3.54 |
| AV on | 0.898 → 0.910 | 0.809 → 0.810 | 3.28 → 3.27 | 3.35 → 3.36 |

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py  # 59 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_pynccl.py  # 17 passed, incl. the new test_pynccl_all_to_all_single
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py  # 92 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py  # 2 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_sharded_sampling.py  # 12 passed
```

`test_pynccl_all_to_all_single` covers uneven and zero-row splits, plus CUDA graph replay. `test_dspark_sharded_sampling_equivalence` (new) runs Qwen3-4B-FP8 + DSpark at TP2. It checks that the draft logits cache and the loop are sharded only when the flag is on, and that greedy and seeded outputs match replicated sampling up to near-tie noise. The general e2e test covers verification's all-to-all, which now runs on PyNCCL.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Skip the top-k -1 fill on the rows vLLM's decode top-k writes
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

The paged MXFP4 sparse indexer (gfx950, #58671) fills the step's top-k rows with -1 before its top-k kernels run. On decode rows that go to vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode` (gfx950 k = 512 path: #56743), the fill is dead: that kernel writes all k entries of every row. This PR skips the fill on those rows, as the gfx942 indexer already does (#60731), and adds a GPU test for the mixed and padded steps the skip also covers.

## Claims

- **Same output as main.** Below 128 rows and below k = 2048, every path of `top_k_per_row_decode` stores all k slots of each row, with -1 past a short row's end, so the skipped -1 would always be overwritten. On the gather path, `_remap_compact_topk` then rewrites every slot. This write-all property was checked on MI355X at k = 32, 512 and 1024, rather than by diffing outputs against main:
  - A sentinel sweep of the kernel, called as `_topk` calls it, found no unwritten slot in 480 of 480 cases (240 shapes, each with two data distributions).
  - With the fill removed from every row, the indexer's GPU tests still pass, except the 6 cases with trailing padding rows. Those fail only on the padding rows, after their decode and prefill rows have passed.
- **8 fewer kernels per decode step (measured), all inside the decode graph.** That is one per index layer of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. `FillFunctor<int>` drops from 17 to 9 per decode step at both c1 and c2. Total kernels per step drop by exactly 8, and the `topKPerRowDecode`, mono K1 and eager-fill counts do not change.
- **Gain: small.** A 2-round ABBA on a main nightly measured -13 us (-0.25%) per decode step at c1 and -7 us (-0.11%) at c2.
  - The gain has the same sign and size on both GPU halves: -13 / -14 us at c1, -8 / -7 us at c2.
  - The 8 removed fills took about 37 us of in-graph kernel time per step in the profile, so the end-to-end saving is about a third of that.
  - There is no regression.
- **Accuracy unchanged.** GSM8K-1319: 0.9191 vs 0.9183. Real AL: 3.579 vs 3.576. Both are means over 4 runs per arm. Per-question flips between main and this PR (mean 66.9 questions) are within the flips between two runs of the same code (main 72.8, PR 63.2).
- **Unchanged elsewhere.** These rows keep the fill:
  - rows that aiter's top-k takes (128+ decode rows, which is about 19+ requests at DSpark k = 6, or k >= 2048);
  - steps without decode rows;
  - rows after the decode rows (padding, prefill).

## Validation

**CPU, on 9fc85b7dda** (this PR's first commit, rebased on main 434eadcbf8; same diff as the earlier 517b6d3f44). It ran in a CPU-only container on the nightly below.
- [x] `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py`: 8 passed. That is the new `test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes` (4 cases) plus 4 existing tests.
- [x] The test fails without the change, and against each of these mutants (output below):
  - main's behaviour (fill from row 0): fails `[7-512-7]`
  - no kernel gate: fails `[128-512-0]` and `[7-2048-0]`
  - a `<= 128` / `<= 2048` gate: fails `[128-512-0]` and `[7-2048-0]`
  - a decode step that skips the whole fill: fails `[7-512-7]`
- [x] `pre-commit run --files` passed on both commits (ruff, mypy, typos, test tethering). No kernel source changed.

**GPU: MI355X, main = `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c5285a1c12e7e4f83c1af709b319a01b`.** The GPU runs were done against main a6c3635e36, which that nightly is 63 commits behind. Main is now 434eadcbf8.
- **Same as main in the image (sha-checked against a6c3635e36):** the ops file; the MXFP4 and base indexer metadata builders; `deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py`; `deepseek_v41/attention.py`; `backends/utils.py`; `breakable_cudagraph.py`.
- **Changed on main since then,** none of it on this skip's path:
  - #63047 sizes the base builder's (`mla/indexer.py`) expanded decode block table by decode tokens. The decode-row order and `decode_row_lens` are unchanged.
  - #60229 captures adaptive-verification FULL graphs with padding rows. Those rows have length 0, so vLLM's top-k writes them as all -1.
  - #64101 lets mono decode run at TP8. It calls the same op the same way.
- **Same as main in git:** the top-k kernel (`csrc/sampler.cu`) and the three test files are unchanged between edad8b03c5 and main. The image ships neither, and the tests ran from this PR's head.
- **Two nearby files differ,** neither on this op's path: a fused-shared-expert guard in `deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`, and one DBO-only capture line in `v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`.
- **PR arm:** the same image plus this PR's ops file.
- **Commits tested:** the unit tests were re-run on the current head, f3dc96acdb: plan test 8 passed, indexer GPU test 42 passed on both arms. The sweep, profile, ABBA and GSM8K ran on 4eddaa283f, which differs from the head only in comments.

- [x] **Plan test:** 8 passed.
- [x] **`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`:** 42 passed. That includes the new `test_decode_rows_skip_the_fill_in_mixed_and_padded_steps`: 9 cases (decode rows + 3 padding rows, mixed decode + prefill, and both) at k = 32 / 512 / 1024.
  - It also passes 42/42 with main's ops file.
  - With the fill removed from every row, exactly its 6 padded cases fail. They fail on the padding-row check, after the dense layer's decode and prefill rows have passed.
- [x] **`tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k gfx950`:** 22 passed. No CI step runs these on gfx950.
- [x] **Sentinel sweep of `top_k_per_row_decode`:** 480/480 cases clean. Two corrupted-output controls each fail 480/480. Details are below.
- [x] **Profile, main vs this PR, c1 and c2:** 8 fewer `FillFunctor<int>` per decode-graph replay, all in-graph. Table below.
- [x] **ABBA at c1/c2:** 2 rounds with the GPU halves swapped. Table below.
- [x] **GSM8K-1319 and real AL:** 2 swapped rounds, cold and cache-salted passes, with per-question flips. Table below.
- [ ] **DeepSeek-V4 end to end:** not run, because there is no V4 checkpoint on the test node.
  - **CI that reaches this op:** with AITER on and the indexer dtype left at `auto`, #63669 picks MXFP4, so these DeepSeek-V4-Flash jobs run through this op:
    - `:amd: (MI355) LM Eval Large Models FP8` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4, TP4);
    - the nightly `:amd: (MI355) [Nightly] LM Eval Large Models` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4, TP8);
    - AMD CI's optional `:amd: (MI355) DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP`.

    This PR's files trigger only the last one, and it needs `/amd-ci run` and an Unblock.
  - **CI that does not:** the DSpark DeepSeek-V4 GSM8K configs pin `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, so they never reach this op.
  - **Coverage of V4's k:** any `index_topk` below 2048 takes the same skip. DeepSeek-V4-Flash's is 512, the same as V4.1, and V4-Pro's is 1024 (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/mono/dims.py`). The new test and the sweep cover both.

**Profile.** The table is per decode step, over 440-462 one-request (7-row) steps and 258-336 two-request (14-row) steps of the profiled window, on ranks 0 and 3.
- Counts are the per-step mode, identical on both ranks.
- Fill time is the per-step median: 36.1-36.2 us on rank 0, 37.5-37.6 us on rank 3.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `FillFunctor<int>` per step | 17 (8 in-graph, 9 eager) | 9 (0 in-graph, 9 eager) |
| In-graph fill time per step | 36.1-37.6 us | 0 |
| Kernels per step, 7-row / 14-row | 410 / 416 | 402 / 408 |
| `topKPerRowDecode` / mono K1 per step | 12 / 40 | 12 / 40 |

All 8 removed fills run inside the FULL decode graph (via `hipGraphLaunch`), each right after the layer's `_q_rope_mxfp4_quant` kernel.

**Perf.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one MI355X node: TP4 `--monokernel`, DSpark k = 6, AV off, random 32k in / 1k out with `--ignore-eos`, synthetic AL 3.87.
- Decode step = ITL p50, mean of 3 runs of 32 prompts per point.
- The profile and GSM8K servers used block rejection instead. The fill count and fill time per step do not depend on acceptance, because every decode step verifies 7 rows per request.

| conc | main | this PR | ABBA change | per round (P1 / P2) | same half (GPUs 0-3 / 4-7) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.446 ms | 5.432 ms | -13 us (-0.25%) | -0.54% / +0.05% | -13 / -14 us |
| 2 | 6.649 ms | 6.642 ms | -7 us (-0.11%) | -0.44% / +0.23% | -8 / -7 us |

- GPUs 4-7 run about 0.3% faster than GPUs 0-3, which is why the two rounds differ. The swap cancels that.
- This PR is faster on both halves, by less than the ~37 us of fill time the profile removes. With 3 runs per point (spread up to 24 us), read the result as a small gain with no sign of a regression.
- An earlier unswapped A/B on a stack image showed -63 us at c1. That is more than the fills can account for, so it was drift.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy, 8 in parallel. AL is taken from cold and cache-salted passes only.

| arm | runs | GSM8K | AL |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4 | 0.9183 (0.9143-0.9212) | 3.576 (3.569-3.583) |
| this PR | 4 | 0.9191 (0.9143-0.9212) | 3.579 (3.568-3.594) |

Per-question correctness flips have these means:
- main vs PR: 66.9 (56-77, 16 pairs);
- main vs main: 72.8 (65-81, 6 pairs);
- PR vs PR: 63.2 (56-67, 6 pairs).

Greedy text identity is not reproducible on this stack even between two runs of one arm, so it is not used.

<details>
<summary>Setup, commands and test output</summary>

**CPU.** The CPU run overlays the given ops file onto the vLLM in the image. A stub `amdsmi` reports gfx950, and the container runs with `--network none` and no `/dev/kfd`.

```text
$ pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py     # this PR
8 passed, 14 warnings in 17.39s
# fill from row 0 (main's behaviour)
FAILED tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[7-512-7]
1 failed, 7 passed, 14 warnings in 17.01s
# no kernel gate
FAILED ...::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[128-512-0]
FAILED ...::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[7-2048-0]
2 failed, 6 passed, 14 warnings in 17.08s
# a decode step skips the whole fill
FAILED ...::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[7-512-7]
1 failed, 7 passed, 14 warnings in 17.05s
# <= 128 / <= 2048 gate
FAILED ...::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[128-512-0]
FAILED ...::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[7-2048-0]
2 failed, 6 passed, 14 warnings in 17.33s
# main's ops file
E   ImportError: cannot import name '_fill_topk_rows' from 'vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer'
```

**GPU unit tests, one MI355X each.**

```text
plan test, PR                       8 passed
indexer GPU test, PR                42 passed
indexer GPU test, main's ops file   42 passed
indexer GPU test, no fill at all    6 failed, 36 passed   (exactly [decode-3-*] and [mixed-3-*], on the padding-row check)
test_top_k_per_row.py -k gfx950     22 passed, 640 deselected
sentinel sweep                      SWEEP OK: 480/480 cases clean
sweep, corrupted outputs            SWEEP FAILED: 0/480 cases clean (each of 2 controls)
```

**Sentinel sweep.** The output is pre-filled with -777. The kernel is then called as `_topk` calls it: `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode(logits, 1, lengths, out, rows, logits.stride(0), logits.stride(1), k)`, with fp32 logits and 1-D int32 lengths.
- Parameters:
  - k: 512 and 1024.
  - Rows: 1, 7, 14, 32, 33, 60, 64, 65, 100 and 127.
  - Widths: 4096, 12287, 12288, 16385, 65537, 199999, 200000, 262145, 524288 and 1048576.
  - Row lengths: 0, 1, k-1, k, k+1, the full width, and random.
  - Data: randn, and a tie-heavy integer distribution.
  - Logits: contiguous, plus a strided view at two widths.
- This reaches every gfx950 k = 512 config below 128 rows (one block; split + merge for <= 32 rows above 16K, and for <= 128 rows above 64K). For k = 1024 it reaches the insertion, radix, split and device-length-aware paths.
- For each row of length L and n = min(k, L), it checks:
  - no -777 is left;
  - there are exactly n distinct indices in [0, L);
  - each index's logit is >= the n-th largest;
  - exactly k - n slots hold -1.
- The two controls each fail 480/480:
  - one leaves one -777 slot;
  - the other turns a -1 slot into a stale index. That index is in range wherever the row is not empty, and the checker catches it as a duplicate.

**Servers.** Each arm is one TP4 server per GPU half (GPUs 0-3 and 4-7). The perf rounds used synthetic AL 3.87. The accuracy and profile rounds used `"rejection_sample_method":"block"`, without the synthetic AL.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --moe-backend aiter --block-size 128 --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

**Perf client.** It runs for c = 1 and 2, 3 times each, after a 4-prompt warm-up (32k/256 at conc 2). P1 put main on GPUs 0-3 and this PR on 4-7. P2 swapped them.

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency $c --num-prompts 32 --seed $((100 + c)) \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

**Accuracy.** The test is GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy, at 8 in parallel, on two rounds with the GPU halves swapped. Each server ran one cold pass, then one pass with a per-request `cache_salt`, so no prefix-cache reuse. Warm repeat passes lower DSpark AL on main and are not used. AL = 1 + Δ`vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total` / Δ`vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total`, read from `/metrics`.

**Profile.** `--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch",...}'` was set on the first accuracy round's servers. After their GSM8K passes, the window was c1 with 2 prompts and c2 with 4 prompts, 32k in / 256 out.
- Steps are delimited by the mono K1 kernel for 7 rows or 14 rows. The 7-row steps include the c2 window's single-request steps.
- A fill counts as in-graph when its runtime call is `hipGraphLaunch`. Kineto records no grid or block for graph-replayed kernels, so the indexer fill is identified by the kernel just before it.
- Step times in a profiled run are inflated and are not used.

**Why every vLLM-kernel row is fully written** (`csrc/sampler.cu` on main):
- `topKPerRowJob` either takes the `rowLen <= topK` shortcut (indices, then -1 up to k) or ends in the final store loop over all k slots.
- gfx950 k = 512 (`topKPerRowDecode512DeviceLengthAware`): a row runs either in one block that stores directly, or in split blocks plus a merge launch. Both launches compute the same `activeBlocks`, so each row is written exactly once.
- The k = 1024 path and the generic insertion, radix and split+merge paths end in the same store loop.
- `rowEnd` is clamped to >= 0, so a padding row (length 0) is written as all -1.
- Rows are addressed at stride k. Both callers, DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1, allocate the buffer as `[max_num_batched_tokens, index_topk]`, so its width is k.

</details>

## Details

**Design.** `_vllm_topk(rows, k)` holds `_topk`'s dispatch condition (`rows < 128 and k < 2048`). Both entry points call `_fill_topk_rows`.
- When `_vllm_topk` holds for the decode rows, the fill starts after them. Otherwise it fills from row 0, as before.
- Decode rows lead the step (flattened). Padding requests have seq_len 0, so the kernel writes all -1 for their rows.
- Both decode paths write exactly `topk_buffer[:rows, :k]`.

**Gate and tradeoffs.**
- **Env-free and shape-only.** FULL graphs capture the same choice, and breakable graphs decide per step. No device tensor is read on the host.
- **In-graph.** At c1/c2 every decode step replays a FULL uniform-decode graph of 7/14 rows (`v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`). Mono takes a layer only in NONE or FULL mode, and `eager_break_during_capture` passes the op through under FULL. So the op and main's 8 fills are captured in the graph, and the saving is in-graph GPU time only. Only mixed and prefill steps (breakable PIECEWISE) run the op as an eager break.
- **Scope.** #60731 requires a pure-decode, unpadded step. This gate also skips the decode rows of padded and mixed steps.
  - The new GPU test covers both: decode rows followed by prefill rows, and by padding rows, at k = 32, 512 and 1024.
  - The GSM8K runs at 8 in parallel also run mixed steps end to end.
  - The decode-only form (`metadata.prefill is None`) is a one-line change if reviewers prefer it.
- **Models.** The op serves DeepSeek-V4.1 and, on CDNA4 with AITER on, DeepSeek-V4 by default (#63669). DeepSeek-V4 decode takes the same skip whenever its `index_topk` is below 2048 (512 on V4-Flash, 1024 on V4-Pro). V4-Flash has 21 indexer layers, so its decode step should drop 21 fills rather than V4.1's 8. It has not been run end to end; see Validation.
- **Contract.** The skip relies on vLLM's kernel writing every slot. These tests check that:
  - `test_topk_matches_torch_on_both_kernels[8-4096-512]`: vLLM's kernel at k = 512, pre-filled with 7, with a row shorter than k.
  - The new mixed/padded test: the full op at k = 32 / 512 / 1024.
  - `test_top_k_per_row_decode_gfx950_k512_1d_seq_lens` and `_masked_graph_replay`, which pre-fill -777.

  The decode-layer tests run k = 32, the generic path. The shared predicate guards edits to `_vllm_topk` only; other edits to `_topk`'s aiter branch are caught only by these GPU tests. Rows taken by aiter's top-k keep the fill.

**Limitations.**
- **Small gain.** The profile removes ~37 us of in-graph kernel time per step. The end-to-end ABBA measured -13 us at c1 and -7 us at c2, on 2 rounds, one MI355X node and a main nightly.
- **No DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end run.**
- **CI coverage.** Default CI runs only the CPU plan test here: `:amd: (MI300) V1 Attention` and `:amd: (MI355 DPX) V1 Attention` are not optional and start once the PR is `ready`. The GPU indexer test runs only in AMD CI's optional `:amd: (MI355 DPX) Attention Kernels`, which needs `/amd-ci run` and an Unblock. No CI job runs `test_top_k_per_row.py` on gfx950.

<details>
<summary>Related PRs and sibling PRs</summary>

Related:
- #44527 dropped the ROCm FP8 indexer's fill for all rows, and #53906 restored it (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:1393` on main). This PR keeps the fill on every row that the decode top-k does not write.
- #61985 (GLM-5/DSv3.2 on this indexer at k = 2048) keeps the fill under this gate. It has a trivial textual conflict in the plan test file.
- #50201 (top-k NaN hardening) is complementary.

This is one of six independent PRs against main from the same DeepSeek-V4.1 low-concurrency MI355X work. It shares no files with the others:
- #63885: build the SWA decode metadata in one launch on gfx950
- #63890: use AITER's all-gather for small TP all-gathers
- #63891: run DSpark's fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with --monokernel
- #63892: mono, batch TP4 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late
- #63893: mono, tuned K1 at TP4

</details>

title: [Perf][KV Offload] Reduce KVCR adapter overhead
author: mkhazraee
body:
## Overview

Reduce Python overhead in KVCR pin acquisition, transfer descriptor construction, and completion handling. Builds on #60469.

## Claims

- Avoid redundant key-set checks and key conversions during pin acquisition.
- Convert NumPy chunk IDs to Python integers in bulk and cache the NIXL agent name used by descriptors.
- Skip unused successful-key accumulation on fully successful completion while preserving partial-failure reporting.

## Validation

Extended tests added in `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py` cover reordered and invalid pin jobs, Python-integer descriptors, and successful and partially failed transfers.

AI-assisted implementation.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER's all-gather for small TP all-gathers
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

On ROCm gfx950 and gfx942, TP all-gathers now use AITER's IPC all-gather instead of RCCL when the TP group already runs AITER custom all-reduce. "Small" means fp32/fp16/bf16 at TP 2, 4 or 8, up to AITER's own per-rank limit (`should_custom_ag`: vLLM's 128 MiB AITER buffer / (2 x TP) = 32 / 16 / 8 MiB). vLLM adds no cap of its own: in two AITER vs RCCL sweeps, no timed size (TP2: up to 20 of its 32 MiB) was faster on RCCL in both runs. gfx1250 stays on RCCL until it is measured; gfx942 was verified by @frida-andersson on MI325X ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63890#issuecomment-6590588082), Claims). This extends #48247 (DP only) to TP. #48446's RCCL path stays as the fallback. Below, `base` is a main-equivalent image, `pr` adds the previous head's files (b8fd6897a0, with a 2 MiB cap) and `r1` adds 1eb0aa0805's: the round-1 code with a gfx950-only gate, called "this head" below. The current head, 8ca2504b97, is that code rebased onto main with the gate widened to gfx942; it routes gfx950 the same way. See the image table under GPU. cN means N requests in flight.

## Claims

- **Decode step 1.2-1.9% faster at TP4 c1-c4 (4 swapped rounds), 1.4% at TP4 c8 (one swapped pair) and 0.8-1.2% at TP8 c1-c4** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X; `base` matches main on the touched files).
  - TP4 `--monokernel`, previous head, 4 position-swapped rounds (P1-P4): -106 / -120 / -102 us at c1 / c2 / c4 (-1.94 / -1.79 / -1.19%). pr was faster in all 12 round and concurrency pairs, and each drop exceeds the largest same-arm, same-half spread (15 / 27 / 77 us). This head routes c1-c4 decode the same way (every decode gather there is at most 1.81 MB per rank, under the old cap). A c1 re-run on the rebased head gives -113 us against base (previous head: -106 us) and -12 us against pr.
  - TP4 c8 / c16 / c32, this head, where the logits gathers (3.1-14.5 MB per rank) now move to AITER. Against base (one swapped pair, R1/R2): -185 / -350 / -133 us (-1.41 / -2.11 / -0.65%). Against pr (R3/R4, the cap removal alone): -83 / -52 / -307 us. Together they imply pr - base of -102 us at c8, in line with P1-P4 (-106 us at c1), but -298 / +174 us at c16 / c32, where pr differs from base only by Engram gathers. So about 200 us of between-round drift sits in c16 and c32, and neither is established. c8 holds in all four orientations but is marginal: against base, R1's -121 us is just above r1's 116 us same-half spread and inside the cell's largest rep range (145 us); against pr, both orientations (-77 / -89 us) are inside the spread.
  - TP8 without `--monokernel`, previous head (T1-T4: base, pr, pr, base): -0.81 / -1.11 / -1.24% at c1 / c2 / c4, each above the same-arm spread across server starts (21 / 6 / 54 us). The routing there is unchanged; not re-run.
  - Always copying in, instead of AITER's registered capture path (scratch mutant `mut_reg`, M1/M2), costs about 25 us per step at c1, about a quarter of the c1 gain.
  - Under the torch profiler, pr's TP4 step was slower at c1 and c2; without it, pr and r1 were faster than base in every run (see Tradeoffs).
- **gfx942 (MI325X), verified by @frida-andersson** ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63890#issuecomment-6590588082)), with the gate widened to gfx942. The cell is TP4 `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, synthetic AL 3.87, random 32768 -> 1024, 32 prompts, c1. ITL p50 went 7.15 -> 7.01 ms (-140 us) on the same 4 GPUs and 7.04 -> 6.99 ms (-50 us) on different GPU halves: two passes, not position-swapped. TTFT and TPOT were flat, and `niah_single_2` at 16384 scored 1.0. Not measured on gfx942: c2 and up (including the c8+ gathers above the old 2 MiB cap) and the AITER vs RCCL sweep.
- **AITER never lost to RCCL in both of two sweeps** (TP 2/4/8, 768 timed points each; table below). The sweeps cover 1 KiB up to AITER's limit (TP2: up to 20 MiB of its 32), dims 0 / middle / last, bf16 and fp32, eager and graph replay, all bit-exact against RCCL. The better run is at least 1.07x at every point. Run 1 alone lost at 13 points (down to 0.32x, TP2 graph, 2.004 MiB), each at least 1.21x in run 2. Dim 0 (a copy-in plus AITER's kernel against one RCCL kernel) has graph-replay medians of 1.18 / 1.41 / 1.43x at TP 2/4/8 and lost only in run 1 (5 graph points of 128 KiB or less), so it stays on AITER.
- **Bit-exact gathers; GSM8K accuracy unchanged; acceptance length (AL) has no consistent direction.** The PR's GPU test checks TP2 with `torch.equal`, eager and under graph replay; scratch matrices extend this to TP4 and TP8 and up to AITER's limit. On GSM8K-1319 (6 base-vs-PR pairs of the same pass), mean accuracy is 0.916 on both arms, and the per-question flips between arms (68-82) are about the same as within one arm (63-81). AL changed by +0.005, -0.010, -0.021 and -0.055 with pr on half B, and by -0.005, +0.013, +0.027 and -0.014 with r1 on half A. Only the -0.055 (GSM8K-300 with expandable segments, E1, one unswapped run) exceeds every same-arm AL span (at most 0.030). The +0.027 (r1, 16 in flight, no same-condition repeat) exceeds every same-condition span (at most 0.024), but not base's 0.030 across 4/16/32 in flight. The perf tables use synthetic AL 3.87.
- **No change elsewhere.** CUDA, ROCm archs other than gfx950 and gfx942, ROCm without `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, non-TP groups, TP6 and gate rejects keep their current path. No new flag. GPU-checked on gfx950: gate rejects, the DP group and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0`. The arch gate rests on a CPU probe.
- **Not claimed:** gfx1250 (gated off, not tested); gfx942 beyond the reviewer's two c1 passes (no sweep, no c2+, no swapped rounds); other models; timing at TP2 between 20 and 32 MiB per rank (bit-exact in the matrix, not timed). The earlier stack-image result (-2.2% to -2.6% at c1, with 5 other PRs) is context only (see Runs and noise).

## Validation

**CPU** (this head unless noted)
- [x] `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py::test_rocm_tp_all_gather_uses_aiter` (default L4 and MI300 "Distributed Comm Ops" steps): 7/7 pass (whole file: 39 passed, 10 skipped for GPUs). Dropping the `should_custom_ag` check fails exactly the rejection case. A gate widened to gfx1250 (`get_cdna_version() >= 3`) still passes, because the mock sets `use_aiter_tp_all_gather` directly. On the previous head, main's communicator failed the dim-0, middle-dim and last-dim cases, and dropping any one of the TP-size, 16-byte-row, non-empty or 2-D-view checks failed exactly one case (output below).
- [x] Arch-gate probe (scratch; vLLM's own gate inputs, arch faked). AITER all-reduce is enabled only on gfx942, gfx950 and gfx1250, at CDNA versions 3 / 4 / 5. So `in (3, 4)` is true on gfx942 and gfx950 only, and false on gfx90a, gfx908, gfx1250, gfx1100, gfx1201 and non-ROCm. The probe ran for the previous gate (`== 4`); the new result follows from the same logged inputs.

- **Same-arm AL differences.** Base: its four 4-in-flight GSM8K-1319 passes span 3.573-3.588 (0.015), all six including 16 and 32 in flight 3.568-3.598 (0.030), and GSM8K-300 differs by 0.009 between the sync-check and E1 servers. pr: 0.000 (GSM8K-1319, cold vs salted) and 0.024 (GSM8K-300). r1's four passes span 3.578-3.595 (0.017; 0.014 at 4 in flight).
- **Why AL can move at all.** The gathers are byte copies, so the PR can change AL only indirectly, for example through timing-dependent batch composition under real rejection.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Run DSpark's fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with --monokernel
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

This PR runs #60731's `fused_markov` DSpark sampler (one launch per draft position) on gfx950 (MI355X) with `--monokernel`, for steps of up to 5 requests. Today it runs only on gfx942, so gfx950 runs vLLM's loop of about 51 kernels per decode step at k=6. On MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 c1 decode steps get 2.4% faster at equal GSM8K and AL. It interacts with #63181, #63486 and #61311 (see Details).

## Claims

- With `--monokernel` on gfx950, a DSpark decode step's Markov sampling takes k+1 = 7 launches instead of about 51. Measured with the torch profiler, TP4, 2 rounds:
  - GPU kernels per decode step go from 365-366 to 321 (net -44 to -46);
  - the PR runs 7.00-7.01 `_markov_*` kernels per step.
- On gfx950 the fused launches take steps of at most 5 requests (`MAX_ROWS_GFX950`). From 6 on, vLLM's loop is faster there. Both archs launch the step kernel at 4 warps.
- On MI355X, `main` 335dd77b09 vs this PR (c128b8ba44):
  - Workload: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, AV off, synthetic AL 3.87, random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`. Step = ITL p50.
  - Runs: 4 fresh servers per arm in ABBA order, each with 3 runs of 32 prompts. TP2 runs Engram on the host.

  | Config | `main` | PR | Delta | Spread across servers (`main` / PR) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | TP4 c1 | 5.372 ms | 5.245 ms | **-127 us (-2.36%)** | 0.39% / 0.44% |
  | TP4 c2 | 6.637 ms | 6.498 ms | **-139 us (-2.10%)** | 1.02% / 0.41% |
  | TP4 c4 | 8.614 ms | 8.530 ms | **-84 us (-0.98%)** | 0.91% / 0.49% |
  | TP4 c8 | 13.053 ms | 13.056 ms | +3 us (+0.02%): 8-row steps take vLLM's loop | 0.64% / 1.06% |
  | TP2 c1 | 6.434 ms | 6.288 ms | **-146 us (-2.27%)** | 0.52% / 1.01% |
- GSM8K-1319 and AL are unchanged (6 passes per arm):

  | Parallel requests | `main` GSM8K / AL | PR GSM8K / AL |
  |---|---|---|
  | 8 | 0.9189 / 3.576 | 0.9156 / 3.576 |
  | 4 | 0.9151 / 3.584 | 0.9151 / 3.581 |

  - At 8 parallel requests most steps have 8 rows, so both arms run the loop. At 4, every step takes the fused launches.
  - Numerics change only in the draft, as on gfx942: a 1-bf16-ULP bias difference can change a draft token, and rejection sampling keeps the target distribution.
- Unchanged: runs without `--monokernel`, other archs and every existing fallback (greedy drafts, AV, more than 8 requests, ...). No new flag or env var. No CI config change.
- gfx942 is unchanged by construction: there `monokernel_cdna3_or_4()` is true exactly when `enabled()` is, and the step kernel keeps 4 warps and `MAX_ROWS` = 8. Nothing was rerun on gfx942.

## Validation

All runs are at c128b8ba44 on MI355X. The current head, 9751254a4e, is rebased onto newer `main`. Its only code change since then is the gate refactor below: one check replaces the two wrappers, and it tests the same condition. The `main` arm is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-335dd77b09161c5d63139b4e7ae51bb9928305b1`, built from this PR's base. The PR arm is that image plus this PR's `ops/__init__.py` and `ops/fused_markov.py`. The tests run in the image with `--noconftest`, because the image lacks `tblib`.

- [x] `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_fused_markov.py` on gfx950 at 4 warps: 6 passed. With `main`'s code: 6 failed (`assert fused_markov.sample_sequential(...)` is False, because the gate is gfx942-only).
- [x] `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py` on gfx950 (#63885's kernel test, whose gate now shares the check): 3 passed.
- [x] `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`: 82 passed.
  - With `main`'s code, 80 passed and 2 failed:
    ```
    E       assert False is True
    FAILED tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py::test_dspark_draft_model_samples_with_fused_markov[gfx950-True-5-True]
    FAILED tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py::test_dspark_draft_model_samples_with_fused_markov[gfx942-True-8-True]
    ```
    The gfx942 case fails only because `main`'s gate reads `on_gfx942()`, while the test sets the arch through `get_cdna_version()`.
  - Each of these mutants fails the test (CPU runner, gfx950 shim):

    | Mutant | Failed cases |
    |---|---|
    | Gate left gfx942-only | `[gfx950-True-5-True]`, `[gfx942-True-8-True]` |
    | No gfx950 cap | `[gfx950-True-6-False]` |
    | gfx950's cap on gfx942 too | `[gfx942-True-8-True]` |
    | Cap keyed on CDNA3 instead of CDNA4 | `[gfx950-True-6-False]`, `[gfx942-True-8-True]` |
    | `record_monokernel` leaves the shared check cached | `[gfx950-False-1-False]` and 2 SWA gate cases |
    | Shared check ignores `--monokernel` | `[gfx950-False-1-False]` and 2 SWA gate cases |
- [x] `pre-commit run --files` on the 5 changed files passes.
- [x] TP4 c1/c2/c4/c8: 4 rounds, with `main` and PR running at once on the two GPU halves. One half ran (main, PR, PR, main) and the other (PR, main, main, PR).
  - Per round, c1 is 2.04-2.75% faster with the PR, c2 1.34-2.70% faster, and c4 0.60-1.43% faster.
  - c8 ranges from -0.86% to +0.84%.
- [x] TP2 c1: 2 rounds of 4 servers each, 4 servers per arm. The two rounds are 2.51% and 2.02% faster with the PR.
- [x] Launch count from the torch-profiler window on both GSM8K rounds (above).
- [x] GSM8K-1319 and AL at 8 parallel requests: 2 rounds with the GPU halves swapped, 3 passes per server.
- [x] GSM8K-1319 and AL at 4 parallel requests: same design. Every step has at most 4 rows, so the PR arm takes the fused launches throughout.

**Microbench (the basis for the 5-row cap and for 4 warps).**
- It times one decode step's Markov sampling at k=6: all 6 draft positions, which is 7 launches fused and the whole loop on `main`.
- Shapes: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's head (vocab 129280, rank 256), random bf16 weights.
- Hardware: one MI355X GPU, graph-replayed with the MALL flushed.
- Values: median of 9 rounds of 200 replays, in us per decode step.

| Rows | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM's loop (`main`) | 225 | 286 | 339 | 355 | 1127 | 275 | 283 | 289 |
| fused, 4 warps (this PR; gfx950 takes 1-5) | 120 | 178 | 228 | 281 | 337 | 394 | 447 | 500 |
| fused, 8 warps (an earlier revision) | 120 | 177 | 240 | 290 | 347 | 403 | 457 | 514 |

- `rocm_unquantized_gemm` runs the loop's Markov GEMV on wvSplitK only for `0 < n <= 5`. From 6 rows it takes the generic GEMM, and the loop is cheaper there than the fused launches, whose cost grows by about 54 us per row.
- The loop's 5-row point (1127 us, seen in one run, not profiled) is `main`'s loop, not the fused path. Even without it, the fused 5-row cost (337 us) is below the loop's 4-row cost (355 us).
- 4 warps is 2-5% faster than 8 at 3-8 rows and within 2% at 1-2 rows.
- The microbench only times the two paths. It does not compare their outputs.

- [ ] Optional: `main`+#63181 with and without this PR. Not run: #63181's head d5ed219630 predates #64356 (`DraftLogitsCache`) and passes the cache object where its kernel expects a tensor.

<details>
<summary>Design, commands and per-round results</summary>

**Server** (TP4). For accuracy, use `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` and drop the synthetic AL. TP2 runs the same command with `--tensor-parallel-size 2` and `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`, because GPU Engram does not fit at TP2.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter --block-size 128 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --language-model-only \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

**Bench.**
- Each server starts fresh and warms up with 4 prompts at 32k/256 and c2.
- Then 3 runs of each c in {1, 2, 4, 8} (TP2: c1 only), each with 32 prompts and seed 100+c.
- Step = ITL p50, averaged over the 3 runs.

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

**Design.**
- TP4: one server per GPU half (GPUs 0-3 and 4-7). Over 4 rounds, the halves ran (main, PR, PR, main) and (PR, main, main, PR).
- TP2: 4 servers at a time: (main, PR, PR, main), then (PR, main, main, PR).
- Every server's log was checked. Each PR server logs `DSpark fused Markov sampling: 6 steps, vocabulary 129280, rank 256, 505 blocks`, and no `main` server does.
- No server failed a request or hit an engine error.

| TP4 round | c1 `main` / PR | c2 `main` / PR | c4 `main` / PR | c8 `main` / PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.381 / 5.234 (-2.75%) | 6.667 / 6.487 (-2.70%) | 8.616 / 8.557 (-0.68%) | 13.002 / 13.110 (+0.84%) |
| 2 | 5.360 / 5.251 (-2.04%) | 6.635 / 6.509 (-1.89%) | 8.573 / 8.521 (-0.60%) | 13.085 / 12.973 (-0.86%) |
| 3 | 5.377 / 5.257 (-2.24%) | 6.600 / 6.511 (-1.34%) | 8.651 / 8.527 (-1.43%) | 13.053 / 13.058 (+0.03%) |
| 4 | 5.368 / 5.239 (-2.40%) | 6.649 / 6.485 (-2.46%) | 8.618 / 8.515 (-1.20%) | 13.070 / 13.082 (+0.09%) |

**GSM8K** runs on separate block-rejection servers, because the perf servers force a synthetic AL.
- The client is an out-of-tree script over `/v1/completions`, using sglang `few_shot_gsm8k`'s prompt and scoring: 8-shot, temperature 0, at most 512 tokens.
- Each server runs one cold pass and two passes with a per-request `cache_salt`.
- Per pass at 8 parallel:
  - `main`: 0.9151 0.9158 0.9212 0.9196 0.9249 0.9166
  - PR: 0.9189 0.9090 0.9166 0.9151 0.9121 0.9219
- Per pass at 4 parallel:
  - `main`: 0.9105 0.9143 0.9166 0.9128 0.9196 0.9166
  - PR: 0.9090 0.9265 0.9067 0.9105 0.9143 0.9234
- AL = 1 + Δ`vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total` / Δ`vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total` over each pass.

**Launch count.**
- It comes from the torch-profiler window on the GSM8K servers: c1 x 2 and c2 x 4 prompts at 32k/256, with the prefills prefix-cached.
- For each TP rank, it divides the rank's GPU kernels in the window by its decode steps. All 4 ranks give the same rate.

Per decode step, the PR removes:
- 6 each of argmax, gather, `_gumbel_sample_kernel` and the Markov GEMV (`wvSplitK`, two variants);
- 7 embedding and index lookups;
- about 8.5 copies and about 12 adds.

It adds 6 `_markov_step_kernel` and 1 `_markov_last_kernel`.

**Compile-only, gfx950** (step kernel at 4 warps, BLOCK 256, STEP 0 and 1, 1, 2, 4 and 8 rows; the kernel is unchanged since): 266-342 VGPRs+AGPRs, with no VGPR spills or scratch.
</details>

## Details

**Why:** #60731 was the gfx942 port, so it gated all of its helpers on `ops.enabled()`, which is gfx942-only. `fused_markov` is plain Triton on vLLM's own Gumbel helpers, with nothing gfx942-specific.

**Change:**
- `fused_markov` runs under `ops.monokernel_cdna3_or_4()`: `--monokernel` + ROCm + `get_cdna_version() in (3, 4)`, the same CDNA versions as the mono layer.
  - `swa_decode_meta` (#63885) uses the same check, in place of its `swa_decode_meta_enabled()`.
  - The other helpers keep `ops.enabled()`.
- `_why_not` caps CDNA4 (gfx950) at `MAX_ROWS_GFX950` = 5 rows. A larger step takes vLLM's loop, as a step of more than `MAX_ROWS` = 8 already does on gfx942. Under FULL CUDA graphs, the choice is made at capture for each padded batch size.
- Both archs launch the step kernel at 4 warps. `BLOCK` is unchanged.
- No speculator, model-runner or CPU-GPU sync changes.
- Tests:
  - `test_dspark_draft_model_samples_with_fused_markov` now drives the real gate with stub kernels in 4 cases. With `--monokernel`, the fused launches take a 5-row step on gfx950 and an 8-row step on gfx942. vLLM's loop takes a 6-row step on gfx950, and any step without the flag.
  - The gfx942 kernel test clears the new check's cache.
  - No new test or test file.

**CI coverage:** there is no `.buildkite` change.
- The gate test runs in the existing MI355 "Basic Models (Other)" job.
- The kernel test runs only in the MI300 gfx942 kernels job.
- No CI job runs the fused launch on gfx950. It was run by hand at this head: 6 passed.

**Limitations:**
- The kernel test compares the fused launches with vLLM's loop at 1 and 2 requests and k=5 only.
- 3-5-row steps on gfx950 were timed by the microbench and ran end to end at c4 and in GSM8K. Outputs at those row counts are compared only through GSM8K and AL.
- AV on: no effect, because a step with the acceptance estimator or the confidence head falls back to the loop.
- `use_fp64_gumbel` is untested on either arch, as before this PR.

**Related PRs:**
- **#63181:** a separate fusion of the same loop: a Markov GEMV and a sample epilogue, 2 launches per draft position.
  - With both merged, this hook runs first. So #63181's path runs without `--monokernel`, on steps that `fused_markov` declines, and on gfx950 steps of 6-8 requests.
  - Its head predates `main`'s `DraftLogitsCache` and conflicts with `main`. The head-to-head waits for its rebase.
- **#63885** (merged: SWA decode metadata in one launch on gfx950) added `swa_decode_meta_enabled()`. This PR replaces it with `monokernel_cdna3_or_4()`, which both helpers use.
- **#63486** and **#61311** move or delete the test files and the MI300 CI job that runs them, and make the kernel test gfx942-only.
  - #61311 also renames `ops._monokernel` and `record_monokernel` to `_specialized_decode` and `record_specialized_decode`. The shared check and both tests use those names.
  - Whichever lands first, this PR follows: it widens that skip to gfx950 and, after #61311, renames the flag.
- **#61869:** a CUDA-only fused Markov sampler. It does not reach ROCm.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: batch TP4 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

This PR makes two register-pressure fixes in the DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode K2 (`--monokernel`) at TP4 on MI355X (gfx950), for both the target and the DSpark draft. It is bit-exact and adds no env var. The code change is +16/-1 lines in 2 files, plus one compile-only test, on main e5196e2959. It builds on #60397 and overlaps #63027 (TP2).

## Claims

- **Step time (measured on main):** c1 -51 us (-0.9%), c2 -235 us (-3.5%), TP4 with DSpark k=6, over 4 ABBA rounds. At both, every PR server ran faster than every main server. The profiler puts the saving in K2 (target and draft); K1 is unchanged.
- **Bit-exact (measured):** per-rank output hashes of K1, K2 and the FFN launch equal main's at 257 TP4 configs (every width from 1 to 48, ratios 0/1/2, index sources, the DSpark draft). GSM8K-1319 is within one pass's standard error of main's, and acceptance length does not move (main 3.576, this PR 3.579, at 2 requests in flight).
- **Compile-level (measured):** at 1-16 rows the target TP4 K2 uses 230-248 VGPRs (main: 246-256) and the draft's 161-181 (main: 166-207); neither spills. On main, 14-16 rows spill, and 13 rows at an index source. Serial X8 copy chains drop from 23-25 to 3-4. Past 16 rows only the base loads move in the source, and no width spills on either tree. TP2, TP8, every K1, the FFN launch and gfx942 are binary-identical to main's.

## Validation

GPU runs used one 8x MI355X node and two images (plus `pr` with the one-line mutant below, for the negative controls): `main` = `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d56` with the mono-path files of main f97a8d6647 overlaid (#64008, #63816 and #64101 are newer than the nightly), and `pr` = `main` + this PR's 2 files (0a44cb7166; the head 02c9253428 only adds the `push_bases` default in `moe_context()`, and its builds are byte-identical at the 10 configs compared; main has no mono changes between f97a8d6647 and e5196e2959). Both have vLLM 0.33.0rc1.dev229, AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0 and torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0.

- [x] `pytest -v tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_{numerics,layers,decode}.py` on MI355X with this PR: `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[2|4|8]` (6- and 48-row steps, then 300 graph replays), layers `[2-8]`, `[4-8]`, `[8-8]`, `[8-28]` and the 76 decode tests pass. `[4-42]` and the gfx942 test skip, as on main. Main's image passes the same tests, except the new one.
- [x] The new compile-only `test_mono_decode_k2_tp4_no_scratch` (TP4 K2 at 14 rows) fails on main (6 `scratch_` ops) and passes with this PR, under pytest on MI355X. It catches a revert of the late base load (255 VGPR, 4 spilled again), not a revert of the batched copies alone (250 VGPR, no spill). `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[4]` covers the copies at runtime: a one-line mutant of the batched copy, which fills the last row's last 16-byte quad with the quad before it, fails its 6-row case.
- [x] Per-rank output hashes vs main at TP4: 257 configs (target ratios 0/1/2 and the draft at every width from 1 to 48; index sources at 1-16, 21, 28 and 48 rows; padded and fold-off steps; the FFN launch), 3 reps each on each of the 4 ranks. Main and this PR are equal on 1028 of 1028 (config, rank) pairs (41,868 tensor-hash comparisons), and both are deterministic. The mutant above changes only the last row of K2's MoE output, on every rank, at all 5 of its configs of up to 16 rows, and nothing at 21 or 28 rows or in the FFN launch, so the check sees a one-quad error.
- [x] c1/c2 ABBA on main, plus c4 (Performance).
- [x] GSM8K-1319 and AL with this PR alone (Accuracy).
- [x] 553 configs per tree (505 gfx950, 48 gfx942) compiled and compared with main's builds (table under Details). The three 48-row gfx942 K2 configs fail on both trees, since gfx942 caps decode at 42 rows. `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes.

**Performance.** Setup: two TP4 servers at a time, one per GPU half, one per arm. 4 rounds with the halves swapped (main|pr, pr|main, pr|main, main|pr). Each server ran a warm-up, then 3 runs x 32 prompts per concurrency. TP4 mono, DSpark k=6, adaptive verification off, random 32k/1k, synthetic acceptance length 3.87, step = ITL p50. Delta = the mean of the two same-half deltas.

| | c1 (7 rows) | c2 (14 rows) | c4 (28 rows) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, mean of 4 servers | 5.443 ms | 6.707 ms | 8.685 ms |
| this PR, mean of 4 servers | 5.392 ms | 6.472 ms | 8.618 ms |
| delta | **-51 us (-0.9%)** | **-235 us (-3.5%)** | -67 us (-0.8%) |
| delta per round | -62, -34, -73, -35 us | -257, -198, -251, -233 us | -37, -79, -55, -98 us |
| servers, main / this PR | 5.429-5.459 / 5.377-5.402 | 6.669-6.722 / 6.464-6.484 | 8.656-8.727 / 8.610-8.628 |

Rows are target rows per step; the draft runs 6, 12 and 24. At c4 the copies are not batched and nothing spills on main, so only the base loads move. This PR is faster in every round (-37 to -98 us), but I did not profile it. An earlier single unswapped run on a stack image (nightly 83c078d955 + 5 PRs) gave c1 -59 us and c2 -256 us.

Profiler (attribution, not the measurement): GPU time of the mono launches per decode step, mean over the 4 ranks, then over the two accuracy rounds (halves swapped). The traced windows are short: 2 prompts at c1 and 4 at c2, 32k/256.

| per decode step | 7 rows | 14 rows |
|---|---|---|
| target K2 (40 launches) | -78 us (-2.7%) | -224 us (-6.0%) |
| draft K2 (3 launches) | -6 us (-3.4%) | -12 us (-5.8%) |
| target and draft K1 | within 0.2%, inside A/A noise | within 0.2%, inside A/A noise |
| all 86 mono launches | -86 us (-2.2%) | -238 us (-4.8%) |

**Accuracy.** Same images, block rejection (real acceptance), 2 rounds with the halves swapped. GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy. With 2 requests in flight, every decode step takes this PR's one-tile path (7-14 target / 6-12 draft rows). With 8 in flight, 97% of the samples had 7 or more requests running, which is past the 48-row mono limit for the target, so those passes mostly check the rest of the stack.

| requests in flight | passes per arm | GSM8K, main / this PR | AL, main / this PR | questions that flip: main vs PR (main vs main, PR vs PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 4 | 0.9181 / 0.9143 (-0.0038) | 3.576 / 3.579 | 68.5 (66.0, 71.3) |
| 8 | 6 | 0.9169 / 0.9138 (-0.0030) | 3.572 / 3.573 | 71.4 (72.3, 72.0) |

One pass's binomial standard error at n=1319 and 91.5% is 0.0077. Flips are the mean over pairs of passes; between arms they match the flips between two passes of the same arm.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# server (one TP4 replica per GPU half)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'

# warm-up
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency 2 --num-prompts 4 --seed 7

# step time = ITL p50; 3 runs per concurrency
for c in 1 2 4; do
  vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
    --max-concurrency $c --num-prompts 32 --seed $((100 + c)) --percentile-metrics itl --metric-percentiles 50
done
```

Accuracy: the same server with `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` and no synthetic acceptance. GSM8K test set, 1319 questions, 8-shot, temperature 0, max 512 tokens, over `/v1/completions`, with sglang `few_shot_gsm8k`'s prompt and scoring, at 2 or 8 requests in flight. Each round's first pass is cold; every later pass uses a per-request cache salt. Acceptance length = 1 + accepted / drafts, from `/metrics` around each pass. The profiler ran on these servers (`--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch",...}'`).

Hashes: a test that is not part of this PR runs each config eagerly 3 times on every rank, with main's `test_dsv41_mono_numerics` builders (seeded random weights in the checkpoint's formats), and hashes every K1, K2 and FFN-launch output tensor. Both images run the same test file.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. *X8 copies.* At one token tile (up to 16 rows, covering c1 and c2 at k=6), `load_x8_rows` issues one 16-byte load per branch. Each load waits (`s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`) before its LDS store. With this PR it issues every load first, then the masked stores. The row count is a Python int on these paths.
2. *Peer bases.* K2 loads the four peer bases at its start (`peer_bases`, #60397) and holds them to the MoE all-reduce push. At 14-16 rows (13 at an index source) K2 spills 2-4 VGPRs. At 14 and 16 rows the push reloads the bases: each reload is followed by `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` (4 between peer stores), which on gfx950 also waits for earlier system-scope stores, so each peer's push waits for the previous ones. At 15 rows and the 13-row index source, 2 VGPRs spill with no wait between peer stores. `stage_down` now loads the bases right before its barrier, and they still land before the first push.

**Gate.** `build_mono_k2` passes a `push_bases` callable to `run_ffn`, which puts it in the MoE context only at `tp == 4`. That one entry enables both halves. `load_x8_rows` takes the batched path only when it is set, not on gfx942, and only when the row count is a Python int (one token tile). `stage_down` rebinds `peer_addr` to the bases it loads late; gfx942 returns through `stage_down_942` before that line. The FFN launch and K1 never get the entry. TP2 is excluded: its K2 does not spill on main (70 builds, including ratio 2 at every width from 1 to 48), neither half was measured at TP2, and #63027 tunes TP2 ratio 2 with its own batched copy. TP8 is #64153.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- SGPR lane spills: at 7 rows (the c1 width), target builds go 103 → 174 `v_writelane` (32 in loops, main 0) and index sources 93-105 → 68. At 14 rows (c2), target builds go 75-79 → 82 and index sources 85 → 78, none in loops. Across target and index-source builds, loop-resident `v_writelane` rises on 21 of 88 at 1-16 rows (falls on none) and on 15 of 162 past 16 rows (falls on 100). The c1, c2 and c4 measurements include these builds.
- The DSpark draft K2 at 5 rows (not a k=6 width) goes 166 → 180 VGPR, the only build at 1-16 rows that uses more VGPRs; its `v_writelane` falls 219 → 63. Past 16 rows the draft gains 1 VGPR at 16 widths, without VGPR spills, and its loop-resident `v_writelane` rises at 17 of 32 widths (0 → 8-72, including the k=6 widths 36 and 42) and falls at 1. Target builds past 16 rows never use more VGPRs.
- The FFN launch keeps main's 16-row spill (256 VGPR, 2 spilled; 4 with the draft's dims). It serves only fallback layers.
- No pytest launches K2 at 9-16 rows. The hash check covers those widths, and c2 runs 14 rows.
- The ISA test uses FlyDSL privates and MiniMax-M3's `code_object` (as M3's ISA test does), and skips without `llvm-objdump` on PATH (the nightly ROCm image has it). It guards only the late base load.
- The DSv4-Pro copy (`deepseek_v4/amd/mono`, #61482) has its own `load_x8_rows` and `peer_bases`. It is not changed or checked here.

**Related.**
- **#63027** (TP2 tuned K1/K2) batches the same copies in its tuned builds (`load_x8_rows_all`, gated on `tuned`) and moves `stage_down`'s barrier into a new `down_sums`. Whichever lands second keeps one batched path, enabled by `tuned` or `push_bases`, and puts the base rebind before `down_sums`' barrier.
- **#64153** (draft) applies the same two fixes at TP8. It is stacked on this PR's previous head (92852abd06) and needs a rebase onto this version.
- **#63486** (draft) moves the test file. If it lands first, this PR's test follows it.
- **#61934** (closed, "No e2e gain observed") issued the FFN seam's static loads before their polls. Those are different loads from this PR's.

<details>
<summary>Sibling PRs (MI355X low-concurrency work)</summary>

None of these touches this PR's files: #63888, #63890, #63891 (#63885 is merged).

#63893 (tuned K1 at TP4, draft) is stacked on #63027. Its own commit also edits `run_ffn` and `build_mono_k2` (their scratch-layout lines, not this PR's) and moves the TP4 K2's scratch offsets.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Compile-level evidence (gfx950, FlyDSL 0.4.0, COMPILE_ONLY=1, main f97a8d6647)</summary>

553 builds per tree: 505 gfx950 and 48 gfx942 (the three 48-row gfx942 K2 builds fail on both trees). The TP4 K2 is built at every width from 1 to 48 (314 builds). With this PR none of the 314 uses scratch; on main 21 do.

| TP4 K2 build | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 14 rows, ratio 0 / 1 / 2 | 255 VGPR, 4 spilled, 20 B scratch, 4 reload waits between peer stores, 23 copy chains | 248 VGPR, no spill, no scratch, 3 chains |
| 14 rows, index source | 255 VGPR, 4 spilled, 20 B, 4 reload waits | 248 VGPR, no spill |
| 15 / 16 rows | 256 / 255-256 VGPR, 2 / 4 spilled | 242 VGPR, no spill |
| 13 rows, index source | 256 VGPR, 2 spilled, 12 B | 248 VGPR, no spill |
| 1-13 rows (1-12 at index sources) | 246-252 VGPR, 25 or 23 chains | 230-248 VGPR, 3 or 4 chains |
| DSpark draft K2, 1-16 rows (ratio 0, as the runner builds it) | 166-207 VGPR, 23-25 chains | 161-181 VGPR, 3-4 chains |
| 17-48 rows, every width, ratios 0/1/2 and index sources | 231-234 VGPR, 22-23 chains | 231-233 VGPR, 22-23 chains (only the base loads move) |
| DSpark draft K2, 17-48 rows | 171-234 VGPR | 171-233 VGPR |
| TP2 K1/K2, TP8 K1/K2, every TP4 K1, the FFN launch at TP2/TP4/TP8, gfx942 TP2/TP4 | | binary-identical (236 configs hashed: 191 gfx950, 45 gfx942) |

Copy chain = `buffer_load_dwordx4` → `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` → `ds_write_b128`. Reload wait = a `vmcnt(0)` between two system-scope peer stores.
</details>

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Avoid double rounding in fused MoE expand
author: chaojun-zhang
body:
## Overview

Fix FP16 residual accumulation in the fused MoE LoRA fallback on XPU, without changing tests or tolerances. CUDA and ROCm keep their previous accumulation behavior.

## Claims

- Keep the XPU expand accumulator and residual sum in FP32, converting only when storing the result.
- Preserve the existing dtype conversion and addition order for non-XPU backends.
- Addresses the precision path introduced by #59931 without changing shared behavior on CUDA/ROCm.

## Validation

- Atomic-add cast cleanup: `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -k large_rank_fallback` — 16 passed; file-level pre-commit passed. A direct `SPLIT_K=2` shrink check also matched the FP32 reference exactly for binary-scaled FP16/BF16 inputs on XPU.
- After removing the redundant cast before `tl.store`: `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` — 433 passed in 309.11s on two Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs; original tests/tolerances unchanged. CUDA was unavailable.
- `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -k test_fused_moe_lora_kernel_large_rank_fallback` — 16 passed on Intel Arc Pro B60.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py` — passed.
- The CI BMG-specific numerical discrepancy was not reproduced on local B60; Intel CI is still needed to validate that hardware-specific case.

## Details

The XPU specialization keeps the FP32 dot accumulator through residual addition so the LoRA result is not rounded to FP16 before adding the residual. It is selected only for XPU expand calls; shrink and all non-XPU calls retain the existing conversion order. No test code or tolerance was modified.
