title: [KV Offload] Remove unused touch from CachePolicy and OffloadingManager
author: mindungil
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove the now-unused `touch` hooks, as suggested in the [#61050 approval](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61050#pullrequestreview-5653251367). This also finishes the `touch` to `on_store_miss` cleanup from the [#51787 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51787#discussion_r4014470687), where `touch` was kept only as a compatibility fallback.

## Claims

- Nothing in the scheduler or managers calls `touch` anymore. #51787 moved recency to `on_request_finished`, and #61050 moved in-flight ordering into `insert(req_context)`. The remaining definitions only forwarded to each other.
- `CachePolicy.touch`, `OffloadingManager.touch` and `SecondaryTierManager.touch` are removed, along with their overrides. The KVCR tier now calls `_align_sequence` directly from `on_request_finished`, which is all its `touch` override did.
- `CachePolicy.on_request_finished` becomes abstract and replaces `touch` as the required recency hook. `on_store_miss` now defaults to a no-op.
- Built-in LRU and ARC behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD)
```

- All `tests/v1/kv_offload` tests pass, including `test_kvcr_tier.py` with the `kvcr` commit that CI installs.
- Compared with `main`, no test changes outcome apart from the two removed tests that exercised `touch` directly.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass.

## Details

- LRU did not override `on_store_miss`, so its store misses reached `touch` through the base default. Those keys are never resident (`prepare_store` only reports keys the policy does not hold), so `_update_recency` skipped them. The no-op default keeps LRU identical.
- ARC already overrides `on_store_miss` and `on_request_finished`; its `touch` was only reachable from tests.
- Interface change for out-of-tree `CachePolicy` implementations: they must implement `on_request_finished`. An outdated policy now fails at construction rather than silently losing recency. The custom-policy guide documents this, as #61050 did for `insert`. A no-op default would also work; I chose the explicit contract, but am happy to switch if you prefer. `touch` overrides on custom `OffloadingManager` or `SecondaryTierManager` subclasses are simply no longer called.
- `TieringOffloadingManager.touch` was the only caller of `SecondaryTierManager.touch`. The KVCR tier (#60469) overrode it only to call it from its own `on_request_finished`, so inlining `_align_sequence` there keeps KVCR's behavior unchanged.
- Tests that used `touch` to set LRU order or promote ARC chunks from T1 to T2 now go through a finished request (`prepare_load`, `complete_load`, `on_request_finished`). The ARC ghost-hit setups use `on_store_miss`, through `prepare_store` where the test allows the insert. `test_touch_forwards_req_context_to_policy`, `test_touch_propagates_to_all_tiers` and the `manager.touch.assert_not_called()` checks are removed.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR removes these hooks. Open #63578 subclasses `LRUCachePolicy` and overrides `on_request_finished`, so it is unaffected. Open #50422 still implements `touch`, but it already conflicts with `main` (it predates #51787 and the `insert(req_context)` change), so a rebase would move its recency to `on_request_finished` anyway.

AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the specialized decode's FlashInfer paths on newer FlashInfer
author: yaoyaoding
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepSeek-V4.1 `latency_specialized` decode (#61868) turned on four of its FlashInfer paths only when `flashinfer-python` was exactly 0.7.2. #63466 moved `requirements/cuda.txt` to 0.7.2.post1, so on `main` all four have been off since then: the server logs a warning per path and runs the stock path, and the numerics test that covers two of them skips. This PR gates each path on what it actually needs, so they run on 0.7.2.post1 and later releases. Thanks to @mgoin for catching it ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61868#discussion_r4380766753)).

## Validation

On one GB300 tray with `main`'s FlashInfer (0.7.2.post1):

- `test_numerics.py` (4 GPUs) passes instead of skipping; it compares the publishing `wo_b` GEMM and the MXFP8 layer input with FlashInfer's own GEMM and quantize bitwise.
- `test_kernels.py::test_sparse_mla_persistent_kv_counters` and `::test_low_latency_mxfp8_mm`: 18 passed, none skipped.
- `vllm serve` with `decode_backend=latency_specialized` logs "specialized decode on" and no fallback warning, and answers a completion and a chat smoke request correctly.

## Details

- Publishing `wo_b` GEMM and MXFP8 layer input (they use FlashInfer internals): FlashInfer ≥ 0.7.2 instead of == 0.7.2. Those internals are unchanged in 0.7.2.post1, and `test_numerics.py` now runs on the pinned release, so a later change to them fails the test instead of turning the paths off.
- Pinned MXFP8 tactics: no version gate; they already fall back to tuning every tactic when FlashInfer does not list the pinned one.
- Sparse-MLA KV counters: on the decode taking `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse MXFP8 activation quant into the 1x32 dot_scaled linear for M <= 16
author: RuibinCheung
body:
## Overview

On gfx950, `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` (1x32-scale MXFP8 dense layers: MiniMax-M3/M3.1, ModelOpt/INC MXFP8) runs a separate `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` launch before every `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM. For bf16 activations with 1-16 rows, this PR quantizes the activation inside the GEMM instead, so each such linear is one launch and the output is bit-identical. Fused: K <= 1024 for M <= 16, and K = 2048 for M <= 4.

The fused GEMM quantizes only `min(16, next_pow2(M))` activation rows per K step and repeats them to fill the 16-row MFMA tile; that keeps the per-N-tile quant cost proportional to the real rows and is what makes K = 2048 profitable.

## Claims

- Per-call speedup on MI355X: 1.14x-1.64x for K <= 1024 at M = 1-16, and 1.03x-1.27x for K = 2048 at M = 1-4 (1.15x-1.27x for MiniMax-M3.1 o_proj at TP4, 6144 x 2048). Every other shape and M keeps the existing path (1.00x).
- Output is bitwise equal to the existing path (separate quant + `_select_cfg` tile), including where the fused tile has a different `BLOCK_K`/`BLOCK_N`.
- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP4 (on #63232), AgentX concurrency 1: o_proj and shared-expert down_proj run fused with no separate quant launch. Over baseline, in two runs with the arm order swapped: P90 TPOT 1.011x in both, P90 interactivity 1.011-1.012x.
- No change under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, for fp16 activations, for M > 16, for K = 2048 at M > 4, or for K > 2048.

## Validation

**Microbenchmark**: "separate" is `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` + GEMM (current behaviour); "fused" is this PR. Speedup over separate, MI355X:

| shape (N x K) | M=1 | M=2 | M=3 | M=4 | M=5 | M=8 | M=16 | M=32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6144 x 384 (M3.1 shared down, TP8) | 1.64x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 1.47x | 1.45x | 1.01x* |
| 8192 x 512 | 1.48x | 1.49x | 1.49x | 1.51x | 1.44x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 0.99x* |
| 6144 x 768 (M3.1 shared down, TP4) | 1.37x | 1.29x | 1.29x | 1.29x | 1.26x | 1.26x | 1.26x | 1.00x* |
| 6144 x 1024 (M3.1 o_proj, TP8) | 1.52x | 1.48x | 1.39x | 1.41x | 1.34x | 1.36x | 1.30x | 1.00x* |
| 4096 x 1024 | 1.47x | 1.37x | 1.29x | 1.30x | 1.22x | 1.25x | 1.14x | 1.01x* |
| 6144 x 2048 (M3.1 o_proj, TP4) | 1.27x | 1.20x | 1.16x | 1.15x | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 4096 x 2048 | 1.17x | 1.11x | 1.05x | 1.03x | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 2560 x 6144 (M3.1 qkv, TP4) | 0.99x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 1536 x 6144 (M3.1 shared gate_up, TP4) | 0.99x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |

\* not fused at this shape; the column times the fallback, i.e. the noise floor.

**End to end**: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP4, MI355X, mono decode off, FULL_DECODE_ONLY CUDA graphs, on #63232 (`8d0f05a0c`, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash`) with this PR applied on top; baseline is the same image unchanged. AgentX trace replay (InferenceX), concurrency 1, 600 s per run, `max-num-seqs` 2; run 1 in the order baseline, this PR, run 2 reversed. This PR / baseline (> 1 is better; TPOT as baseline / this PR; P90 interactivity is InferenceX's `intvty.p90` = 1 / P90 TPOT):

| Run | P90 TPOT | P90 interactivity | Total throughput / GPU |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.011x | 1.012x | 1.004x |
| 2 | 1.011x | 1.011x | 1.020x |

GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, full test set, greedy), measured with K <= 1024 fused: baseline 96.51 / this PR 96.21 strict-match (stderr 0.51 / 0.53), within one stderr; vLLM is not batch invariant when requests are batched together, so greedy outputs vary between runs even with bit-identical kernels. The fused output is bitwise equal to the existing path for every tested shape, including K = 2048.

## Details

- **Row trimming.** `BLOCK_M` = 16 is the smallest MFMA tile, but at M < 16 only the first M rows are stored. The kernel takes a constexpr `QUANT_ROWS = min(16, next_pow2(M))`, loads and quantizes that many rows, and repeats them with `broadcast_to` + `reshape`. At `BLOCK_K` = 128 the repeat costs more than the saved quant, so those tiles (K = 384, 640, ...) keep quantizing 16 rows. The unfused path passes `QUANT_ROWS = BLOCK_M` and generates the same code as before.
- **Why only M <= 16, and K = 2048 only up to M = 4.** The fused GEMM requantizes the activation once per N-tile. At small M the separate launch (plus the round trip of the fp8 activation and its scales) dominates; with more rows or larger K the redundant quant work wins (table above). The gate does not look at N; cutting K = 2048 at M = 4 keeps every measured N at or above 1.03x.
- **`K` becomes a `tl.constexpr`.** Without it the fused loop is not unrolled/pipelined and the fused GEMM is ~0.8x even at K = 512. #63232 makes the same change.
- **Compiles.** Triton already specializes M on `== 1` and `% 16 == 0`; `QUANT_ROWS` adds up to three more variants per fused shape (6 instead of 3 for M = 1-16 at `BLOCK_K` >= 256; 5 at K = 2048, where M = 5-16 stays unfused). For MiniMax-M3.1 at TP4 that is 17 instead of 12 `_mxfp8_linear_kernel` compiles over M = 1-16 (15 instead of 12 at TP8). They are compiled in the eager warm-up before CUDA graph capture; vLLM's capture sizes include every M from 1 to 16, so decode never compiles at runtime, and graph capture time was unchanged in the end-to-end runs.
- **bf16 only.** The in-kernel fp8 cast makes the compiler enable the FP16 overflow clamp in the MODE register for the whole kernel, so an fp16 output that overflows saturates at +-65504 where the unfused GEMM produces inf. bf16 output is unaffected and bit-identical; fp16 activations keep the separate quant.
- **Batch invariance.** Fused and unfused use different tiles (and therefore K-reduction orders), so under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (#52231) every M stays on the unfused path.
- **Limitations.** Only gfx950 (`dot_scaled` path). Shapes are tuned on MI355X.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Extend the latency_specialized decode on NVIDIA
author: yaoyaoding
body:
## Overview This PR makes the `latency_specialized` decode from #61868 faster for DeepSeek-V4.1 on NVIDIA GPUs. Most of the work is in the decode step's kernels: larger batches now stay on the low-latency paths, more of each step overlaps, and the indexers split their work across the TP ranks. "What changed" below goes through each part. On one GB300 tray with DSpark, the decode step takes 5.9–17.0% less time than on `main` at batch 1 to 32, and AgentX P90 interactivity is 4–26% higher at concurrency 1 to 32, with slightly higher throughput. ![Decode step and AgentX, main against this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaoyaoding/vllm/93d0aafb7e0d32b440d597fa680476b5de27d5f9/pr3_perf.png) Left: three ABBA sets at `0cdfc566`, 12 measurements per arm and batch. Right: AgentX at `0cdfc566`, both arms of each concurrency on one tray. ## Validation This branch includes #63914 (merged into this branch), which keeps the specialized decode's FlashInfer paths on `main`'s FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1; this PR's two further paths on FlashInfer internals follow the same rule. The runs below are from before this branch merged `main`: `main` at `76518259` on that commit's wheel with FlashInfer 0.7.2, against this PR at `0cdfc566`, except compute-sanitizer, which ran at `5ab5ef9e`, the commit before it (`0cdfc566` adds only a start-up requirement, no runtime weight updates, a test option, a comment and documentation). After the merge, on `main`'s wheel at `ed1a7307` with FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, four GB300: these GPU tests pass at `b7bb822b` (`test_kernels.py`, `test_all_gather.py`, `test_decode_topk.py`, `test_sparse_mla_cute.py`, `test_numerics.py`, `test_layers.py`, `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`, `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`; all but `test_kernels.py` ran at `d7fcb755`, which differs only in that file), and a TP4 server with `decode_backend: latency_specialized` starts with the specialized decode on and no fallback warning, and answers a completion and a chat request correctly. FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1's MoE finalize adds the top-k products in a different order at small batches, so `b7bb822b` lets one test's finalize comparison allow FP32's reordering error. ### Correctness | Task | `main` | This PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | GSM8K, strict match (1,319, c8, real verification) | 0.9742 | 0.9735 | | GPQA-Diamond (198 × 16, c32) | 0.789 | 0.791 | | AIME25 (30 × 16, c32) | 0.983 | 0.985 | | RULER NIAH (`single_2`, `multikey_2`, `multikey_3`; 32K, 128K, 256K; 40 samples each), concurrency 8 | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | | RULER NIAH, same, concurrency 32 | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | | GSM8K with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | | 0.9719, no GPU↔CPU sync reported | | GSM8K with `decode_backend` unset (stock decode) | | 0.9704 | | All-gather stress: CUDA graphs of three back-to-back gathers of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, replayed 2,000,000 times in a seeded random order on four GPUs; every word encodes its rank, gather and replay, checked on the GPU (`test_all_gather.py` as a module; `--custom-all-gather` replays the same graphs on vLLM's custom all-gather) | custom all-gather: 392 stale words | 0 bad words (6,000,000 gathers) |
Tests ```bash # One SM100-family GPU: the new kernels against FlashInfer, cuBLAS or torch references .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_decode_topk.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_sparse_mla_cute.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py -v # Four GPUs: the all-gather, AllReduceMHC's LL and two-shot protocols, TP4 numerics .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_all_gather.py tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -v # The all-gather stress run (four GPUs), then the same replays on vLLM's custom all-gather .venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather --replays 2000000 .venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather --replays 2000000 --custom-all-gather # Four GB300: five-layer model at TP4 with DSpark, switch on vs off .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_layers.py -v ``` | Check | What it covers | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Kernel tests | Routed experts against FlashInfer up to 192 rows, eagerly, in graphs and over 500 replays with alternating inputs (bitwise); the front against the stock chain; pinned and wide low-latency MXFP8 GEMMs; the replicated embedding lookup; the metadata graph against eager builds, with slow clamping builders | 299 passed (with `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`), 1 skipped | | Decode top-k (CuTe DSL) | An exact top-k of the BF16 logits against `torch.topk`, k 512 and 2048, 1–64 rows: sampled and direct paths, crowded, constant and rising values, NaN and infinities, a sample that misses the top values, the wide 16-CTA rows, CUDA graphs; block mode against the stock `select_candidate_blocks` | 77 passed | | Sparse MLA (CuTe DSL) | Against an FP32 reference: widths of 1–5 chunks (128 to 640 columns), masked columns, a token with no active column, as many tokens as the GPU holds clusters for, with and without sinks, CUDA graph replay | 33 passed | | All-gather | Against NCCL, bitwise: int32, BF16 and FP32 inputs of 1 pack to the full 4 MiB, growing and shrinking from call to call, one rank late each call; the sentinel word; CUDA graphs of three gathers of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, replayed in a random order with new contents each replay, 4 GPUs | Passed; the stress run: 0 bad words in 6,000,000 gathers | | `AllReduceMHC` | Shrinking and growing batches in one mailbox with LL only, two-shot only (to 200 rows) and both in turn; the two protocols give the same bits, 4 GPUs | 61 passed (the whole file) | | Numerics, layers (4 GB300) | TP4 collectives through the new paths, including the logits and the row-sharded indexer at 1, 2, 5, 8 and 32 requests through the new all-gather; with the switch on the executor runs, embeds from the replicated table and replays its graphs | Both passed | | compute-sanitizer | memcheck and synccheck over the new kernels' single-GPU tests | memcheck and synccheck: 0 errors each (199 tests: 110 in the two new test files, 89 selected from `test_kernels.py`; at `5ab5ef9e`) | | pre-commit | All hooks | Passes | **CI.** The new test files (the all-gather's among them), the `AllReduceMHC` tests (`test_custom_all_reduce.py -k all_reduce_mhc`) and `test_engram.py` join the nightly 4×B200 DeepSeek-V4.1 step. Three tests need hardware that step does not have, and skip there: `test_pinned_mxfp8_mm` and `test_wide_low_latency_mxfp8_mm` (the tactics are pinned for GB300, SM103) and the layers test (four GB300).
### Performance All runs: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4), DSpark (5 draft tokens), Model Runner V2, FULL CUDA graphs for decode. The decode step and AgentX use DSpark's synthetic acceptance (length 3.51, as InferenceX runs AgentX); the accuracy runs above verify for real.
Server command and clients Both arms ran the same command, on `main`'s wheel with either `main`'s or this PR's source: ```bash VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"use_thp":true}' \ --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}' \ --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}' \ --compilation-config '{"mode":"VLLM_COMPILE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092]}' \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 4092 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 \ --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice ``` - Decode step and AgentX: the speculative config adds `"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51`. - GSM8K: InferenceX's lm-eval GSM8K (5-shot, temperature 0, all 1,319 questions), 8 requests in flight, one run per cell. - GPQA-Diamond and AIME25: zero-shot through lm-eval, reasoning effort high, temperature 0.6, 16 samples of every question, 32 requests in flight, as for #61868. GPQA-Diamond is InferenceX's task (the last standalone A–D letter, 16,384 output tokens); AIME25 is lm-eval's with DeepSeek-R1's math prompt (65,536 output tokens). - RULER NIAH: lm-eval's RULER generator and scorer for `niah_single_2`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K tokens, 40 seeded samples per task and length (upstream lm-eval draws 500), 128 output tokens, thinking off, one run per cell. - AgentX: InferenceX's AgentX scenario (AIPerf, the 393-trace corpus), closed loop at a fixed concurrency for 3,600 s. - Decode step: one server per block. A block runs batch 1 (a 524K-token context), batch 8 and batch 32 (84K–648K tokens a request) twice each. The requests are prefilled one at a time, then sent together for 3,000 tokens each, so they decode from the prefix cache. The step is the client-side window in which every request decodes, divided by its chunk count.
**AgentX.** The InferenceX AgentX trace corpus (393 traces), 3,600 s per concurrency, closed loop, DSpark at the synthetic acceptance length 3.51 as InferenceX runs it, at `0cdfc566`. Both arms of a concurrency ran on the same tray, one after the other (the first arm alternates with the concurrency). Each cell reads `main` → this PR. | Concurrency | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Change | Total tok/s/GPU | Change | TPOT p50 (ms) | TTFT p50 (s) | E2E p50 (s) | Requests | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 817.7 → 852.0 | +4.2% | 7,856 → 8,016 | +2.0% | 1.110 → 1.050 | 0.984 → 0.783 | 2.10 → 1.52 | 341 → 395 | | 4 | 666.3 → 808.7 | +21.4% | 10,336 → 10,477 | +1.4% | 1.110 → 1.040 | 0.434 → 0.431 | 1.13 → 1.09 | 764 → 769 | | 8 | 539.6 → 678.7 | +25.8% | 16,813 → 17,198 | +2.3% | 1.280 → 1.110 | 0.414 → 0.434 | 1.26 → 1.16 | 1,443 → 1,456 | | 16 | 431.1 → 536.2 | +24.4% | 29,316 → 29,922 | +2.1% | 1.520 → 1.230 | 0.496 → 0.448 | 1.30 → 1.11 | 2,715 → 2,748 | | 32 | 225.0 → 258.2 | +14.8% | 61,858 → 63,312 | +2.3% | 2.210 → 1.640 | 0.829 → 0.671 | 2.30 → 1.80 | 4,869 → 4,966 | Some trace turns ask for one output token. When that token ends the reasoning, the response has no content, and the client records the request as an error: 0–1 such requests a run for `main` and 0–1 for this PR.
TTFT: API server and engine AgentX TTFT is mostly the API server's single-threaded work before the engine sees the request: chat-template rendering and tokenization of the whole conversation. aiperf's per-request `request_ack_ns` separates that work from the engine's (acknowledgement to first token). This PR changes only worker-side code, and the engine part stays within 18 ms of `main` at every concurrency; the TTFT differences in the table are in the API server: | Concurrency | API server p50 (s) | Engine p50 (s) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 0.693 → 0.479 | 0.267 → 0.249 | | 4 | 0.215 → 0.219 | 0.177 → 0.167 | | 8 | 0.237 → 0.244 | 0.150 → 0.153 | | 16 | 0.284 → 0.239 | 0.158 → 0.162 | | 32 | 0.503 → 0.354 | 0.214 → 0.213 |
**Decode top-k.** `decode_topk` against vLLM's opt-in DeepSelect and the stock path (FP32 upcast + `cooperative_topk`), k = 512, µs per call: Random BF16 logits; "valid" is the share of each row's columns before its end. One GB300, a CUDA graph of 20 back-to-back calls, median of 20 replays. Each cell: `decode_topk` / DeepSelect / stock. With row sharding, a rank selects 12 rows at batch 8 and 48 rows at batch 32 (6 rows a request, over 4 ranks). - Up to 12 rows, `decode_topk` is faster than DeepSelect at every shape but two: 65,536 columns with 1/8 valid (7.3–7.7 against 4.2–4.3 µs), and 1,048,576 columns with 1/8 valid at 12 rows (17.1 against 16.5). - From 24 rows, DeepSelect is faster when 1/8 of the columns are valid (65,536 columns at 48 rows: 17.1 against 4.3 µs) and at 65,536 columns from 48 rows and 524,288 all-valid columns from 48 rows (44.2–44.1 against 46.1–44.7 µs). `decode_topk` stays faster with all 262,144 columns valid (11.8–22.5 against 26.1–26.2 µs). - Above 12 rows, `decode_topk` does not take 1,048,576-column rows, so they use the stock path (81.7–289.3 µs against DeepSelect's 16.6–76.6). - In block mode `decode_topk` is faster at every size (5.9–12.7 against 9.3–80.0 µs). - Against the stock path `decode_topk` is faster at every shape it takes, except 65,536 columns with 1/8 valid (7.3–17.4 against 6.7–12.9 µs; equal at 24 rows).
All shapes | Columns, valid | 1 row | 6 rows | 12 rows | 24 rows | 48 rows | 64 rows | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 65,536, 1/8 | 7.3 / 4.2 / 6.7 | 7.4 / 4.2 / 7.0 | 7.7 / 4.3 / 7.4 | 8.9 / 4.3 / 8.9 | 17.1 / 4.3 / 11.3 | 17.4 / 4.3 / 12.9 | | 65,536, all | 9.0 / 10.8 / 11.5 | 9.3 / 10.7 / 12.2 | 9.4 / 11.0 / 14.1 | 10.3 / 11.0 / 15.7 | 17.9 / 11.0 / 21.4 | 20.2 / 11.0 / 23.3 | | 262,144, 1/8 | 7.4 / 8.2 / 11.1 | 7.9 / 8.2 / 13.2 | 8.0 / 8.2 / 17.0 | 9.9 / 8.3 / 22.3 | 19.3 / 8.3 / 35.9 | 19.6 / 8.4 / 54.6 | | 262,144, all | 9.5 / 25.8 / 14.6 | 11.3 / 25.9 / 18.6 | 10.1 / 26.0 / 29.7 | 11.8 / 26.1 / 34.9 | 20.8 / 26.2 / 62.0 | 22.5 / 26.2 / 80.7 | | 524,288, 1/8 | 8.7 / 11.0 / 11.8 | 9.0 / 11.1 / 17.2 | 9.3 / 10.9 / 23.8 | 15.5 / 11.0 / 36.3 | 28.5 / 11.0 / 81.4 | 35.0 / 11.1 / 102.6 | | 524,288, all | 12.4 / 16.8 / 18.0 | 11.5 / 17.0 / 29.7 | 28.9 / 43.9 / 49.3 | 37.0 / 44.0 / 63.2 | 46.1 / 44.2 / 130.0 | 44.7 / 44.1 / 151.9 | | 1,048,576, 1/8 | 9.4 / 11.8 / 14.3 | 10.1 / 12.0 / 23.9 | 17.1 / 16.5 / 39.4 | – / 16.6 / 81.7 | – / 16.7 / 149.9 | – / 16.8 / 190.7 | | 1,048,576, all | 12.1 / 20.9 / 27.0 | 12.4 / 21.1 / 49.1 | 27.3 / 76.1 / 90.1 | – / 76.2 / 129.9 | – / 76.4 / 246.8 | – / 76.6 / 289.3 | Block mode (the candidate source: top 2,048 blocks of 8 columns; DeepSelect over the block maxima), 1/8 valid, `decode_topk` / DeepSelect: | Columns | 1 row | 6 rows | 12 rows | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 524,288 | 5.9 / 9.3 | 6.2 / 24.5 | 6.3 / 42.7 | | 1,048,576 | 6.3 / 13.3 | 6.5 / 43.6 | 12.7 / 80.0 |
**Memory and start-up.** The replicated embedding table takes 1.32 GB per GPU and the all-gather's mailbox 48 MiB, which the KV cache gives up (106,281,697 → 105,286,588 KV-cache tokens on the tray, −0.9%). Engine start: the engine's init (profile, KV cache, warm-up) took 98.8–103.0 s (`main`) and 98.8–108.9 s (this PR) with warm compile caches, three starts each; a tray's first start, with cold caches, took 680–748 s in either arm. ## Details **Duplicate-work check.** No open PR extends the DeepSeek-V4.1 specialized decode. Related open PRs: - #62633 adds a swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention to the FlashMLA mega-attention layer. This PR's sparse-MLA kernel replaces the TRTLLM-gen decode of the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` backend, which the specialized decode requires. - #62172 lets `cooperative_topk` read BF16 logits, and #57109 adds FlashInfer's sampled `gvr_2` as an opt-in indexer top-k. `decode_topk` serves only this model's decode indexers. It also selects the candidate source's blocks, and it covers the 1M-wide rows on 16 CTAs. The comparison with DeepSelect is above. - #62635 fuses the finalize with the shared-expert add where the fused all-reduce + mHC does not take it. This PR's MoE finalize stays deferred into that fused kernel.
What changed, and what each part saved when it was added Each row was measured against the tree before it, mostly as decode-step ABBA blocks on one tray (batch B = B requests × 6 rows). They were measured one at a time, on a moving base that also held DSpark-draft changes not in this PR, so they do not add up exactly. | Change | Why | Measured when added | | --- | --- | --- | | Pinned CuTe DSL MXFP8 tactics for the attention projections above 8 rows | The autotuner sometimes picked an unclustered `wo_b` tactic (15.3 against 5.9 µs at 48 rows), about 310 µs a step at batch 8, depending on the server start | Batch 8 −7.3% | | The next layer's mHC coefficients on the side stream at every executor step (was up to 48 rows) | They ran inline above 48 rows | Batch 32 −3.9% | | Low-batch routed experts up to 64, then 192 rows: a fused front, a routing-record prefix, the router's padding mask | Above 8 rows the stock FlashInfer chain ran (routing, sort, GEMMs, finalize) | Batch 2 −8.6%, batch 4 −7.0%; 12 cold layers at 80–128 rows 10–13% under FlashInfer | | Low-latency MXFP8 projections up to 48 rows | FlashInfer's block-scaled GEMMs, 13.5 µs for the three projections at 12 rows against 4.3 µs of HBM time | Attention sublayer at batch 2 50.4 → 48.5 µs | | Dense indexers row-sharded from two requests; Engram WKV run ahead; candidate expansion overlapped | Every rank scored every row of the indexers | Batch 2–21 −0.6% to −4.7% (all separated) | | Two-shot all-reduce + mHC from 64 rows, adapted from FlashInfer's MNNVL two-shot all-reduce | Each rank read four contributions per value; the owner now sums them once | Batch 21 −1.0%, batch 28 −0.9%; 192 rows 15.7 → 12.1 µs per call | | The dense indexer planned before the index-key wait | 6.6–7.2 µs of reset, schedule and cast waited for the keys without reading them | About −25 µs a step at batch 2, −50 at batch 8 (profile) | | Embedding from a replicated table into the hyper-connection streams | Sharded lookup + all-reduce + copy | Not measured on its own: it was added in a set of four changes, which together gave batch 4 −1.6% and batch 21 −1.4%. From the work it removes, about −13 µs a step is expected at batch 2 and −23 at batch 32 | | Indexer metadata builds on branches of their own | 13 nodes ran in series on one block-table branch | Draft end → next target −7 to −10 µs | | Decode top-k from BF16 logits (CuTe DSL) | `cooperative_topk` plus the FP32 upcast took 182 µs a step on the slowest rank at batch 8 | Batch 2 −1.5%, batch 8 −1.5% (two trays) | | Sparse MLA up to 8 requests (CuTe DSL): a cluster per token, one CTA per 128 columns, merged over distributed shared memory | TRTLLM-gen's kernel at these shapes | Batch 2 −5.3%, batch 4 −2.7%, batch 8 −4.9% | | GEMM2 starts per token tile | GEMM2 waited for GEMM1's whole grid | MoE pair at batch 2 39.2 → 35.4 µs a layer; batch 2 −1.6%, batch 8 −1.3% | | The front's top-k over eight CTAs; its stores after the cluster release | The top-k was issue-bound on one SM (0.18 µs a row) | Batch 2 −1.1%, batch 4 −1.6% (five sets, three trays) | | Layer 20's top-k on 16 CTAs a row | Its 1M-wide rows fell back to the upcast and the stock top-k | Layer 20 at batch 2 38.5 → 24.7 µs a step; batch 2 −1.1% | | The executor's own all-gather for the indexer rows and the logits (CuTe DSL) | `main` gathers them with the custom all-gather, whose Lamport kernel never waits for the rank's own multicast copy, so a late copy can corrupt a later gather of another size (`test_all_gather.py --custom-all-gather` reproduces it) | Not measured on its own | | The decode Q/KV norm and the fused `wo_a` trigger their dependents early (≤ 48 rows) | `wq_b` and `wo_b` load their weights before their own wait, but were launched late | Attention per layer at batch 2 34.9 → 33.4 µs, about −60 µs a step |

title: [Perf][KV Offload] Keep offload event metadata out of the cyclic GC
author: jthomson04
body:
## Overview

`OffloadingEventsTracker` keeps one `_OffloadEventMetadata` entry for every chunk resident in any offload tier, and each entry held three objects tracked by Python's cyclic GC. With a large secondary tier, these entries make up most of the EngineCore's long-lived heap, so every full collection pauses the scheduler for over 100 ms. This PR keeps the entries out of the cyclic GC.

Not a duplicate. The only open PR touching this class is #63129 (draft). It fixes a separate correctness problem: metadata loss when an `OffloadKey` is reused. It doesn't change how entries are tracked.

## Claims

- Each event-metadata entry goes from 3 GC-tracked objects to 0.
- In a cold-cache KV-offload serving run, the full-collection pause drops from 106 to 31 ms and ITL p99 from 119 to 55 ms, and req/s rises 7%. That is within 1.5% of the same run with GC disabled.
- No behaviour change: residency bookkeeping keeps `set` semantics, and the emitted events are unchanged.

## Validation

| Cold-cache run | main | this PR | GC disabled (reference) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| req/s | 13.5 | **14.5** | 14.7 |
| ITL p50 / p99 | 14.5 / 119 ms | 14.3 / **55 ms** | 13.9 / 49 ms |
| TTFT p50 | 2398 ms | 1803 ms | 1800 ms |
| Full-collection pause, mean / max | 106 / 121 ms | **31 / 38 ms** | – |
| Objects scanned by a full collection | 252,147 | **49,209** | – |
| ...of which event-metadata entries | 199,969 | 0 | – |

**Setup:**
- **Engine:** `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --load-format dummy`, with `OffloadingConnector` + `TieringOffloadingSpec`: an 8 GiB CPU primary tier plus a KVCR secondary tier with 65,536 slots. KV events and `self_describing_kv_events` are on.
- **Mocks:** only the model forward and the GPU↔CPU copies are mocked, by a `UniProcExecutor` subclass passed via `--distributed-executor-backend`. A step is modeled as 10 ms plus 3 µs per prefill token. No GPU is used.
- **Load:** 64 concurrent unique 8K-token prompts, 128 output tokens.
- **Runs:** one 90 s window per arm, back to back, on `41f5146b5b`. There are no offload-path changes between that commit and this branch's base. The GC-disabled reference is a 30 s window.
- **Measurement:** pauses come from `gc.callbacks`, and object counts from `gc.get_objects()` at the end of the window. I can share the mock executor.

This change does not affect model outputs, so no model evaluation was run.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering   # 1123 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # passed (ruff, mypy, ...)
```

`test_reoffload_preserves_secondary_residency` now also asserts that the entry is untracked, and checks through removals that both residencies survive a re-offload.

## Details

**Why each entry had three tracked objects:**
- the slotted dataclass, since dataclass instances are always tracked;
- the `active_residencies` `set`;
- one `(Medium, ownership)` tuple per secondary residency. `Medium` members are tracked objects, so the collector never untracks that tuple.

**The change:**
- `_OffloadEventMetadata` is now a `msgspec.Struct` with `gc=False`, the same pattern `KVCacheEvent` uses. Its fields are hashes, token ids, ints, strings and a shared `NamedTuple`, so an entry can't be part of a reference cycle.
- `active_residencies` is now an `int` bitmask. A `(medium, ownership)` pair gets the next bit the first time a store expects its removal. The table belongs to the tracker, survives `reset()`, and is bounded by the number of distinct tier/ownership pairs. A removal for a pair that was never registered clears nothing, as `set.discard` did.

`freeze_gc_heap()` doesn't help here, because it only freezes objects that exist at startup. The largest remaining source of scanned objects is the CPU tier's per-chunk `ChunkStatus`, which this PR leaves alone.

---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not offload the partially computed block of a request that finished with an error
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Overview

When a request finishes with an error before its prefill is complete, the block it was computing is stored under the hash of the full block. A later request with that prefix hits the offloaded block and loads KV for tokens that were never computed. One-expression fix in `_build_store_jobs`; sibling of #59096 and #59329.

## Claims

- A request that ends in `FINISHED_ERROR` mid-prefill stores only the blocks it fully computed, as `FINISHED_ABORTED` already does.
- Requests that finished normally are unchanged: they computed their whole prompt, so the clamp is a no-op.

## Validation

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q -k finish_mid_prefill
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

`test_finish_mid_prefill_stores_only_computed_blocks[FINISHED_ERROR|FINISHED_ABORTED]` runs a 16-token prompt through chunked prefill at 6 tokens a step (block size 4), finishes the request after the first chunk, and checks that the finish step stores nothing beyond the one full block step 1 already stored.

On main (6fe3d447ac64) the `FINISHED_ERROR` case fails:

```
AssertionError: FINISHED_ERROR: stored 1 blocks [2] but only 1 full block(s) were computed (num_computed_tokens=6, prompt=16)
```

With the fix both cases pass; the file's other tests still pass (CPU only, macOS, no GPU run). Model outputs are unaffected, so no evals.

## Details

`_build_store_jobs` (`offloading/scheduler.py:1874-1883`) clamps the storable token count to `num_computed_tokens` only for `FINISHED_ABORTED`; every other finish uses `max(num_prompt_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`, which is the whole prompt for a request that produced no output. `storable_chunks` then only bounds by allocated blocks, so the half-written block goes out under its full hash. A request can finish this way mid-prefill through `finish_requests(..., FINISHED_ERROR)` (`sched/scheduler.py:2525-2540`): an encoder-cache mismatch, or a failed KV load under the `fail` policy.

Fix: `min(req.num_computed_tokens, max(req.num_prompt_tokens, req.num_tokens - 1))`. The spec-decode clamp is kept.

Not a duplicate: #63010 (store cursor reset on a restart from token 0) and #60810 (the block table of a resumed streaming session), both merged on 10-25, and the open #62795 (flush promotions before a request's tiers are finalized) are adjacent; none touches this clamp.

AI assistance: I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to trace this path and write the test; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests myself.

title: [Perf][DSA] Token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill under TP; remove indexer row sharding
author: ZJY0516
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Shard DSA sparse-MLA prefill across TP ranks by token instead of by head ("ShardQ", Ulysses style) and remove the indexer TP row sharding from #54951, which it supersedes, including in GLM-5.3-Flash's k-pool indexer. Enabled by default for steps with >= 1024 tokens after the decodes (`sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens`), including mixed prefill + decode steps (whose decode tokens stay head-sharded); at 4K the gain is small and within end-to-end noise. Validated on GLM-5.3; GLM-5.3-Flash is covered by a forward-time microbenchmark and a greedy retrieval A/B.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 (NVFP4, TP4, GB200, default FlashInfer sparse MLA backend) TTFT at concurrency 1: **1.24x at 32K, 1.29x at 64K, 1.40x at 128K** prompts.
- Per-step prefill forward is **1.11x-1.70x faster** than main, growing with context length (16K-token chunk at 128K context: 926 ms -> 544 ms), and **1.18x-1.25x faster than the removed row sharding** even with row sharding forced on. With default settings row sharding never engages: it needs >= 65536 prefill rows in one step, above the default `max_num_batched_tokens`.
- At 64K-token chunks, where main's row sharding engages by default, per-step forward is **1.14x-1.26x faster than row sharding** (B300; 64K chunk at 1M context: 11.17 s -> 9.83 s).
- GLM-5.3-Flash (k-pool indexer, now ShardQ-enabled): per-step forward at 64K-token chunks is **1.08x-1.13x faster than row sharding**, which this PR replaces there too.
- Mixed prefill + decode steps (one prefill chunk plus 32 decodes, GLM-5.3, B300): per-step forward is **1.16x-2.90x faster than main** on FlashInfer and **2.04x-2.97x** on FlashMLA sparse with `fp8_ds_mla`. Before mixed-step support, this PR was up to 2.4x slower than main's row sharding on such steps at a 64K budget.
- B300 serving A/B with the #54951 protocol (GLM-5.3 NVFP4, TP4, concurrency 1, 256 output tokens, four fresh-process pairs): server TTFT **1.19x at 8K, 1.29x at 32K, 1.46x at 128K, 1.99x at 512K and 2.62x at 1M** (162.5 s -> 62.0 s); 1K-4K prompts (below the threshold) unchanged; generated tokens identical to main in 132/132 matched retrieval probes.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k (5-shot and ~10K-token 45-shot prompts) or long-context passkey retrieval.

## Validation

The performance and accuracy numbers below were measured before the restructure from ZJY0516/vllm#24 (exchanges around the regular `forward_mqa`, indexer chunked over each rank's tokens) and with the earlier 8192-token default threshold; they have not been re-run on the current head.

All numbers: GLM-5.3 NVFP4, TP4 on one GB200 tray (4 GPUs).

**TTFT** (real weights, `vllm serve` defaults plus `--max-model-len 524288`; `vllm bench serve` random prompts, 1 output token, concurrency 1, 3-8 prompts per length after a warmup; both servers on the same node, one after the other):

| prompt | ShardQ off | ShardQ on | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4K (below the threshold, ShardQ inactive) | 191 ms | 233 ms | run-to-run noise |
| 8K | 203 ms | 232 ms | within noise |
| 16K | 327 ms | 294 ms | 1.11x |
| 32K | 634 ms | 511 ms | 1.24x |
| 64K | 1228 ms | 950 ms | 1.29x |
| 128K | 2546 ms | 1819 ms | 1.40x |

`--max-model-len 524288` is needed because the 1M default needs 46.6 GiB of KV cache per GPU at TP4, independent of this PR.

**Accuracy** (real weights, same server settings, greedy):

| eval | ShardQ off | ShardQ on |
|---|---|---|
| gsm8k 5-shot, concurrency 128 (short prompts take dense MHA; ShardQ inactive) | 0.9196 | 0.9196 |
| gsm8k 45-shot (~10K-token prompts), concurrency 1, 200 samples: every prefill goes through ShardQ | 0.930 | 0.925 |
| passkey retrieval, 8K-128K prompts, 15 prompts | 15/15 | 14/15 |

The one passkey miss is a near tie on the first answer token (the off run picks the key with p = 0.64); the off run has a similar near-tie detour at 32K that still contains the key. Confident tokens have matching logprobs.

**Forward time** (dummy weights, prefix caching off) (`vllm bench forward`, median per step, CUDA-graph timed; `NK@MK c` = an N-token chunk whose prefix up to M tokens came from earlier chunks):

| step | main | main, row sharding forced (`indexer_tp_shard_min_rows=4096`) | this PR | vs main | vs row sharding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh prefill 4K | 142.0 ms | 143.0 ms | 127.7 ms | 1.11x | 1.12x |
| fresh prefill 8K | 278.5 ms | 277.1 ms | 233.9 ms | 1.19x | 1.18x |
| fresh prefill 16K | 550.1 ms | 539.5 ms | 444.3 ms | 1.24x | 1.21x |
| 16K @ 32K c | 612.6 ms | 574.3 ms | 460.9 ms | 1.33x | 1.25x |
| 16K @ 64K c | 701.8 ms | 602.8 ms | 483.1 ms | 1.45x | 1.25x |
| 16K @ 128K c | 926.3 ms | 676.3 ms | 544.4 ms | 1.70x | 1.24x |

This PR with `sparse_mla_shard_q=false` measures 141.9 / 278.4 / 546.6 / 608.7 / 697.7 / 922.6 ms, matching main: removing row sharding costs nothing at these shapes.

```bash
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --kv-len-jitter 0 --case p4k=4096 --case p8k=8192 --case f16k=16384 \
  --case c32k=16384@32768c --case c64k=16384@65536c --case c128k=16384@131072c
# baseline arm: --attention-config.sparse_mla_shard_q false
# row sharding arm (on main): --attention-config.indexer_tp_shard_min_rows 4096
```

**Forward time at 64K-token chunks, where row sharding engages by default** (B300, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, otherwise as above; median per step):

| step | main, row sharding (default) | main, row sharding off | this PR | vs row sharding | vs row sharding off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh prefill 64K | 2237 ms | 2442 ms | 1769 ms | 1.26x | 1.38x |
| 64K @ 128K c | 2470 ms | 3144 ms | 1959 ms | 1.26x | 1.60x |
| 64K @ 256K c | 2958 ms | 4648 ms | 2388 ms | 1.24x | 1.95x |
| 64K @ 512K c | 4793 ms | 11542 ms | 4115 ms | 1.16x | 2.80x |
| 64K @ 1M c (1,000,000) | 11166 ms | not measured | 9834 ms | 1.14x | |

- **Row sharding is effective at this size:** 2.41x over no sharding at 512K, unlike at the 16K chunks above.
- **The margin narrows with context:** both methods split the indexer, whose cost grows with context. ShardQ also splits the sparse attention, whose per-token cost is fixed by the top-k.
- **Checks:**
  - This PR with `sparse_mla_shard_q=false` measures 2429 / 3135 / 4645 / 11463 ms on a different node, within 0.7% of main with row sharding off.
  - Sample spread is at most 0.7%.
  - A 16K @ 128K reference case in the same runs gives 920 ms for main and 534 ms for this PR, consistent with the table above.
- **Setup:**
  - One process per arm.
  - The KV cache is capped with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 64424509440` so the 64K-token graph fits.
  - Both trees include the FlashInfer sparse MLA fix from #64122. Without it, main's 65,536-token steps silently skip the attention kernel (see "Batch budget" below).
- **Mixed prefill + decode steps:** ShardQ now also covers them (see "Where it applies" and the mixed-step table below).

```bash
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 64424509440 --kv-len-jitter 0 --iters 5 --samples 3 \
  --case f64k=65536 --case c128k=65536@131072c --case c256k=65536@262144c \
  --case c512k=65536@524288c --case c1m=65536@1000000c --case ref16k_128k=16384@131072c
# row sharding off (on main): --attention-config.indexer_tp_shard_min_rows 1000000000
# this PR without ShardQ: --attention-config.sparse_mla_shard_q false
```

**Mixed prefill + decode steps** (GLM-5.3, B300, TP4, `vllm bench forward` with dummy weights, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65600 --max-num-seqs 64`; each step is one prefill chunk plus 32 decodes at 16K context; median per step):

| step | main (row sharding default) | main, row sharding forced (4096) | this PR | vs main | vs row sharding forced |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16K @ 128K c + 32 decodes | 927 ms | 688 ms | 545 ms | 1.70x | 1.26x |
| 16K @ 512K c + 32 decodes | 3334 ms | 1360 ms | 1150 ms | 2.90x | 1.18x |
| 64K @ 128K c + 32 decodes | 2468 ms | 2487 ms | 1972 ms | 1.25x | 1.26x |
| 64K @ 512K c + 32 decodes | 4807 ms | 4821 ms | 4136 ms | 1.16x | 1.17x |

- **FlashInfer (default backend):** main's row sharding engages by default only for the 64K chunks.
  - Without mixed-step ShardQ, this PR measured 3154 ms and 11513 ms on the two 64K rows, up to 2.4x slower than main's row sharding.
  - The 32 decodes add about 9 ms per step; the same 16K @ 128K chunk alone takes 536 ms.

FlashMLA sparse with `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, same cases:

| step | main | this PR | vs main |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16K @ 128K c + 32 decodes | 1339 ms | 656 ms | 2.04x |
| 16K @ 512K c + 32 decodes | 3753 ms | 1263 ms | 2.97x |
| 64K @ 128K c + 32 decodes | fails | 2442 ms | |
| 64K @ 512K c + 32 decodes | fails | 4618 ms | |

- **Why main fails at 64K:** main's fp8 mixed-batch kernel takes all 65,568 tokens in one call, padded to 64 heads, and fails with `[FlashMLA] Stride exceeds int32 limit: 2417098752`. Under ShardQ each rank attends about a quarter of the prefill tokens, so this PR stays under the limit, but non-ShardQ configurations (TP1, DCP) still hit it.

**Mixed-step accuracy:** #54951's retrieval probe with mixed steps, real weights, TP4, ShardQ on vs `sparse_mla_shard_q=false`.
- **Setup:** 24 2K-token prompts and six 64K/128K-token prompts (needles at 10/50/90% depth) submitted together, so the long prompts' prefill chunks share steps with the short prompts' decodes. Greedy, 32 tokens, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 32`.
- **Results:** strict answer 30/30 in both arms, and generated tokens identical in 30/30, for each of:
  - GLM-5.3 on FlashInfer
  - GLM-5.3 on FlashMLA sparse with `fp8_ds_mla`
  - GLM-5.3-Flash on FlashInfer

**GLM-5.3-Flash forward time at 64K-token chunks** (B300, TP4, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, same `vllm bench forward` setup as above; median per step):

| step | main, row sharding off | main, row sharding (default) | this PR | vs row sharding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh prefill 64K | 1173 ms | 1159 ms | 1030 ms | 1.13x |
| 64K @ 128K c | 1254 ms | 1181 ms | 1057 ms | 1.12x |
| 64K @ 256K c | 1407 ms | 1218 ms | 1099 ms | 1.11x |
| 64K @ 512K c | 1729 ms | 1304 ms | 1181 ms | 1.10x |
| 64K @ 1M c (1,000,000) | 2462 ms | 1493 ms | 1378 ms | 1.08x |

- **The gain over row sharding is about 120 ms per step at every context length.** Only 11 of GLM-5.3-Flash's 45 layers are sparse MLA, and both methods split the k-pool indexer. ShardQ also splits the sparse attention, which costs about 150 ms per step regardless of context.
- **Setup:**
  - Row sharding off and on were measured in the same runs as each other. Row sharding on and this PR ran concurrently on the same node, and row sharding on repeated within 0.2% on a second node.
  - Sample spread is at most 0.15%.
  - The linear-attention state tensors are not paged, so the bench's per-case KV zeroing skipped them (local bench change, not in this PR).
- **Accuracy:** GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash@46a050b`, TP4, real weights) on #54951's retrieval probe:
  - Setup: 16K, 64K, 128K and 256K prompts with needles at 10/50/90% depth; greedy, 32 tokens, one request at a time; `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, so every prefill chunk takes ShardQ.
  - Strict answer: 12/12 with ShardQ and 12/12 with `sparse_mla_shard_q=false`.
  - Generated tokens are identical between the two in 12/12 prompts.
- **Not measured:** GLM-5.3-Flash end-to-end serving performance.

**Serving A/B on B300, following the #54951 protocol** (TTFT, TPOT, C1 throughput, retrieval, 1K-1M prompts):

| Context | main TTFT ms | this PR TTFT ms | TTFT improvement | main TPOT ms | this PR TPOT ms | TPOT improvement | main total tok/s | this PR total tok/s | Throughput improvement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1K | 120.73 | 120.00 | +0.61% | 7.365 | 7.274 | +1.22% | 639.22 | 646.35 | +1.11% |
| 2K | 122.52 | 120.85 | +1.37% | 7.194 | 7.140 | +0.75% | 1173.00 | 1184.08 | +0.94% |
| 4K | 150.73 | 150.25 | +0.32% | 7.252 | 7.199 | +0.73% | 2167.69 | 2185.42 | +0.82% |
| 8K | 288.14 | 241.50 | +16.19% | 7.282 | 7.234 | +0.66% | 3928.96 | 4035.16 | +2.70% |
| 16K | 566.47 | 453.12 | +20.01% | 7.413 | 7.340 | +0.98% | 6745.88 | 7134.71 | +5.76% |
| 32K | 1188.06 | 918.47 | +22.69% | 7.434 | 7.360 | +1.00% | 10675.05 | 11763.77 | +10.20% |
| 64K | 2550.34 | 1882.37 | +26.19% | 7.475 | 7.400 | +1.00% | 14704.50 | 17377.01 | +18.17% |
| 128K | 5748.79 | 3940.08 | +31.46% | 7.537 | 7.462 | +1.00% | 17058.09 | 22362.08 | +31.09% |
| 256K | 14418.55 | 8672.19 | +39.85% | 7.650 | 7.575 | +0.98% | 15977.93 | 24622.16 | +54.10% |
| 512K | 41621.55 | 20898.05 | +49.79% | 8.011 | 7.978 | +0.41% | 11986.22 | 22772.37 | +89.99% |
| 1M (1,000,000) | 162546.75 | 62043.79 | +61.83% | 8.364 | 8.334 | +0.36% | 6067.32 | 15543.38 | +156.18% |

Improvement is `1 - PR/main` for latency and `PR/main - 1` for throughput. Throughput is input + output tokens over the wall time of the measured requests at concurrency 1, not saturated serving throughput. From 8K up, the four restart pairs agree to within ~0.5%, and every 95% interval excludes zero (details below). Below the 8192-token threshold ShardQ is inactive and TTFT stays within noise.

TPOT is 0.2-1.6% lower with this PR in every pair. ShardQ does not run on decode steps, and the cause of this small difference has not been investigated.

- Hardware and model: GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (`nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4@e3b8f9f`), TP4 on 4x B300 in one node; torch 2.14.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 (matching cubin and jit-cache), Transformers 5.19.0.
- Arms: main at the merge base `ed1a730` and this PR at `c937e6f`. Both use identical compiled extensions from the official `ed1a730` wheel. A check of `/proc/<pid>/maps` confirmed that all six processes of every server loaded their own arm's source tree.
- Server: `vllm serve` defaults (FlashInfer sparse MLA backend, FP8 KV cache, default CUDA graphs) plus `--max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-per-request-metrics`.
- Protocol, the same as #54951:
  - Runs: eight fresh server processes in ABBA/BAAB order (main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR), forming four adjacent restart pairs. Each process runs 3 excluded warmups and 8 measured requests per length.
  - Prompts: exact-token prompts from #54951's generator, the same in both arms. 1M means 1,000,000 input tokens.
  - Sampling: temperature 0, 256 output tokens with `ignore_eos`.
  - Server timings: TTFT runs from scheduling to the first token, and TPOT is the server's mean inter-token latency.
  - Aggregation: the per-process median, then the geometric mean over the four processes of each arm. 95% intervals resample the four restart pairs (20,000 bootstrap draws).
  - Measured requests: 352 main and 352 PR, every one with exactly 256 output tokens.
  - Only difference from #54951's client: the GLM-5.3 non-thinking boundary `<|assistant|><think></think>` in place of GLM-5.3-Flash's.
- **Batch budget:** #54951 used `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`. On B300 with the default FlashInfer sparse MLA backend, main fails on 65,536-token prefill steps:
  - Every request of 64K or more logs `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` at `flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh:478`, about 312 times per request.
  - Those requests return garbage, with 0/15 retrieval correct from 64K to 1M.

  This run therefore uses GLM-5.3's default budget of 16,384. At that budget, main's indexer row sharding, which this PR removes, never engages, so the baseline is main's default path. Both arms logged zero CUDA errors while serving.

**Retrieval correctness** (#54951's targeted probe: three needles at 10/50/90% depth per length, greedy, up to 64 tokens, repeated in every process; not a general quality eval):

| Context | Baseline strict answer | Optimized strict answer | B answer present | O answer present | A/B exact tokens | Baseline A/A exact tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 2K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 4K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 8K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 16K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 32K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 64K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 128K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 256K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 512K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 1M (1,000,000) | 10/12 | 10/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 6/9 |

Totals: main strict 130/132, this PR strict 130/132; answer present 132/132 vs 132/132. Main and this PR generate identical tokens for 132/132 matched prompts. Because the outputs are token-identical, the two strict misses at 1M are the same in both arms: the model appends a period after the correct code. Main against itself across restarts (A/A) matches 96/99.

- Before ZJY0516/vllm#24:
  - PCP/DCP regression, this PR (`93ecf97`) vs the merge base, one pytest process per file, identical results on both:
    - `test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k 'dcp or pcp'`: 7 passed
    - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`: 92 passed, 3 failed (the same 3 fail on the merge base)
    - `tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py` (4 GPUs): 24 passed, 3 failed (the same 3 fail on the merge base)
    - `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py`: 114 passed
    - `test_mla_context_chunks.py`: 14 passed
    - `test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py`: 42 passed
    - `test_mla_backends.py -k 'dcp or pcp'`: 15 passed
  - `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`: 29 passed, 11 skipped
  - `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py`: 121 passed
  - `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py`: 21 passed
  - `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: 511 passed, 1384 skipped

## Details

**How it works.** Under TP every rank holds `H / tp` heads, so each rank runs the indexer over all prefill tokens, and the sparse attention kernel processes all tokens for its few heads. ShardQ instead gives each rank a slice of the step's tokens:

1. Tokens split zigzag: each request cuts into `2 * tp` chunks, and rank `r` owns chunks `r` and `2 * tp - 1 - r`, which balances the causal indexer cost.
2. The indexer scores only this rank's tokens and writes their top-k compactly, after the decode tokens' top-k, to the shared top-k buffer.
3. An all-to-all moves the MQA query from `[T, H / tp, D]` to `[T / tp, H, D]`; the sparse attention kernel attends all heads over the replicated KV cache.
4. A second all-to-all restores `[T, H / tp, 512]` for the `W_UV` projection.

The exchanges sit around the regular `forward_mqa` call, next to DCP's `query_gather` and combine; there is no ShardQ-specific attention entry point. They push tokens directly into peers' symmetric-memory buffers with one Triton kernel, falling back to NCCL `all_to_all_single` when the TP group has no symmetric memory. The fp8 query of the FlashInfer backend is exchanged as is.

**Where it applies.**
- Steps with at least `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens` tokens after the decodes, one of whose requests is longer than the top-k; shorter prefills already take dense MHA.
- Mixed prefill + decode steps:
  - Only the tokens after the decodes are split. Decodes here are requests of at most `1 + num_speculative_tokens` tokens, and stay head-sharded.
  - The indexer scores every decode token in place, then this rank's tokens compactly after them, so tokens that the indexer treats as prefill but MLA treats as decode stay consistent.
  - The attention layer calls `forward_mqa` twice: once for the decode tokens with the step's metadata, once for this rank's tokens with ShardQ's narrowed metadata (`ShardQMetadata.attn_metadata`, which reads the top-k from `topk_start`). FlashMLA's token-sharded call uses its own lazily initialized scheduler metadata.
  - The decode output is written in place before the restored tokens rather than concatenated.
- The indexer metadata builder chunks only the decode tokens and this rank's tokens (`shardq_gather_indices`), each at its own position, so it makes fewer, fuller launches.
- TP > 1, no DCP/PCP/HiSparse, and no FULL CUDA graphs for mixed batches.
- Backends opt in with `SparseMLACommonImpl.supports_shardq`: FlashInfer sparse MLA and FlashMLA sparse (fp8 mixed-batch path).
- Models mark eligible layers with `MLAAttention(shardq_eligible=...)`: DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash (NVIDIA k-pool indexer) do. Other sparse MLA models keep the head-sharded path.
- The sparse MLA and indexer metadata builders both call `build_shardq_split` and, like every TP rank, derive the same split from the same batch.
- MTP layers are not eligible, including GLM-5.3-Flash's: draft steps reuse each token slot's top-k.

**Config.** New `AttentionConfig` fields `sparse_mla_shard_q` (default `True`) and `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens` (default 1024). `indexer_tp_shard_min_rows` is deprecated, has no effect, and is removed in v0.34.0.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- Memory: the exchange buffers (above) come out of the KV cache budget.
- GLM-5.3-Flash's k-pool indexer, which #54951 row-sharded, now follows the ShardQ split instead. Its MTP layers no longer shard the indexer.

**Not duplicating existing work.** No open PR implements token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill. #54394 and #56944 shard only the indexer rows (like the removed `PrefillRowShard`) and keep attention head-sharded.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Let decodes reuse divergent local hybrid prefix hits
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

`MooncakeConnector` does not opt into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` (#50344), so a hybrid-model decode (attention plus Mamba, GDN or KDA) drops its local attention hit and pulls the whole prompt from P every turn. This opts the `kv_consumer` role in, as MoRIIO READ and NIXL already do.

## Claims

- On a hybrid model, a Mooncake decode keeps its local attention prefix and pulls only the uncached suffix plus the recurrent state.
- `kv_producer` and `kv_both` keep the current lookup.

## Validation

- Kimi-K3 1P1D on MI355X, Mooncake RDMA, multi-turn agentic replay at concurrency 48: decode local prefix hit rate 0.0% to 93.9%; draft acceptance 58.78% to 58.79% (MoRIIO READ 58.79%).
- The new scheduler test fails on main and passes here. Mooncake unit tests: 164 passed. pre-commit clean.

<details><summary>Request flow, test output and serving numbers</summary>

Turn k of a session whose prompt extends turn k-1:

1. The router sends the request to P with `do_remote_decode`; P prefills and pushes KV.
2. On D, the attention blocks pulled in turn k-1 are still cached. Mamba has no state at any block boundary, since D never computes those positions.
3. Before: `get_computed_blocks` returns the hit every group shares, 0 tokens. Mooncake asks for N-1 tokens and pulls every attention block plus the state slot.
4. After: `get_computed_blocks_for_connector` returns the attention hit H. Mooncake asks for N-1-H tokens and pulls the suffix blocks plus the state slot; P pairs the last blocks of each group.
5. D decodes from the recurrent state P computed at N-1.

Unit test, on main and on this branch:

```
$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py -k keeps_local_attention_prefix
# main
E       assert 6 == 2
E        +  where 6 = len([9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14])
FAILED ...::test_hybrid_gdn_remote_prefill_keeps_local_attention_prefix[kv_consumer-2]
1 failed, 1 passed, 11 deselected
# this branch
2 passed, 11 deselected

$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
164 passed
```

Serving, Kimi-K3 1P1D, decode flags `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'`, aiperf multi-turn agentic trace replay at concurrency 48. One run per column.

| Decode metric | Mooncake before | Mooncake after | MoRIIO READ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local prefix cache hit rate (log) | 0.0% | 93.9% | 91.2% |
| Prompt tokens, `local_cache_hit` / `external_kv_transfer` | 0 / 801.7M | not recorded | 731.3M / 70.9M |
| Draft acceptance | 58.78% | 58.79% | 58.79% |
| TTFT mean / p50, same request window | 2984 / 1727 ms | 3137 / 1730 ms | 2611 / 1365 ms |

The "after" run was cancelled by the cluster after 4598 requests, so it has no end-of-run Prometheus snapshot; its hit rate is the decode's periodic log line. MoRIIO's hit rate is `local_cache_hit` over all prompt tokens.

</details>

## Details

A decode never computes the block boundaries of a pulled prompt, so it caches attention blocks but no recurrent state. With the opt-in, the scheduler keeps the attention hit, and `update_state_after_alloc` already pulls every transfer group's unhashed blocks, the state slot included. With nothing to pull, the scheduler falls back to the reconciled lookup (#50344).

Only `kv_consumer` opts in: the per-group lookup reports a shared-prefix boundary of 0, which would disable junction checkpoints on roles that prefill locally.

Limitations:
- Serving runs used vLLM 81198e97 with this property forced to True on the decode, matching this PR; not re-run on main.
- Under `MultiConnector` every child must opt in until #63041.
- TTFT did not change on this workload.

Not a duplicate: the open Mooncake PRs (#53730, #63420, #63425) do not touch this property. AI assistance (Claude in Cursor) was used to write the change, the test and this description.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Drain unfetched P2P stores before cache reset
author: maithilijoshi20
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix cache reset on P2P prefill nodes when store jobs are waiting for a decoder to fetch their KV blocks.

Fixes #63948.

## Claims

- Queued stores report failure and release their primary-tier pins during reset.
- Late fetches fail promptly without reading released slots or leaving stale session bindings.
- Active transfers keep their pins until completion, and fresh symmetric lookup rounds remain usable after reset.

## Validation

Tested on WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, NIXL 1.5.1/UCX, and an RTX 3050 8 GB.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py -q --tb=short
# 808 passed, 1 skipped

export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 VLLM_PLUGINS=
export CUDA_HOME=/home/maithijoshi/.venvs/vllm-py312/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nvidia/cu13
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py::test_p2p_cache_reset_with_absent_decoder \
  -q --tb=short
# 1 passed
```

The OPT-125m test waits for an active cascade with an absent decoder, calls `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`, and checks that the next request has zero cached tokens and identical greedy output. Unit tests cover queued stores, mid-drain fetches, symmetric lookup rounds, active transfer pins, and abort acknowledgements. Pre-commit checks pass for the changed files.

Without the fix, the issue's producer-reset reproducer fails at `assert not self._jobs` in `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()`; with the fix, both unbound and session-bound stores drain successfully, as confirmed in the issue author's PR feedback.

## Details

A prefill node can finish storing KV before its decoder sends a fetch. These jobs hold primary-tier slots but are not counted as active transfers, so waiting only for transfers leaves jobs behind when the parent resets its cache.

Drain fails unbound stores through the existing expiry path and withdraws queued session supply once. Fetches received during polling are rejected without binding their request IDs. In-flight writes retain their pins until the transport reports completion.

Withdrawn symmetric lookup rounds retain enough state to reject a late fetch without invalidating a fresh round under the same request ID. Aborted rounds use the existing acknowledgement path to avoid duplicate terminal messages.

This addresses producer stores waiting for decoder demand. Related #61667 covers consumer write quarantine. No duplicate fix was found when opening this PR. AI assistance was used for review, and validation.

title: [Bugfix] Forward launch grid to Triton kernel overrides
author: wangxiyuan
body:
## Overview

The kernel dispatcher's KernelOverride dropped the caller's launch grid, so platforms could not remap grids (e.g. to physical core counts). Triton kernel implementations are now swapped in directly, launching natively and staying inlinable as Triton device functions; non-Triton implementations are wrapped, receive the grid via __getitem__, and delegate compile-only warmup.

This PR fixes three gaps in the Triton kernel dispatcher: (1) the launch grid is now forwarded to overrides instead of being dropped, (2) Triton device functions called from inside other kernels can be overridden without breaking the outer kernel's compilation, and (3) JIT warmup is delegated to the override instead of failing.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3][Perf] Cut gfx942 MXFP4-to-int4 requant time under pure TP
author: xaguilar-amd
body:
## Overview

Cut the gfx942 Kimi-K3 MXFP4-to-int4 MoE requant (`--quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}'`, added in #51274) from ~19 min to 25 s under pure TP8. TP8 server startup drops from 22.5 min to 3.5 min. The converted weights are byte-identical.


## Validation

**End to end:** 8x MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 10.0, Kimi-K3 with the DSpark draft. The checkpoint was in the page cache for all startup numbers. Before and after use the same base; only `mxfp4.py` differs.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only -tp 8 [--enable-expert-parallel] \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 4 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'
```

| Config | Requant before | Requant after | Startup to `/health` before | Startup to `/health` after | KV cache before | KV cache after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | 19 min 15 s | 25 s | 1348 s | 210 s | 27.37 GiB | 28.21 GiB |
| EP8 | 4 min 38 s | 24 s | 431 s | 181 s | 22.57 GiB | 23.41 GiB |

The requant is the time between `Loading weights took` and `Online quantization as part of model loading` on rank 0.

**Accuracy** (GSM8K, 5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions`, with the fix):
- TP8: 0.988 ± 0.007 on 250 questions.
- EP8: 1.000 on 100 questions.

The weights are byte-identical to the current code (see below), so I didn't rerun accuracy on the baseline.

**Per-layer microbenchmark:** one full Kimi-K3 MoE layer (w13 + w2), per-rank shapes with `routed_expert_hidden_size` 3584, run under `max_split_size_mb:20` like `gpu_worker.load_model`. Times are the median of 7 runs, alternating before and after. The old code's first run in a fresh process is faster (1.94 s TP8, 0.85 s EP8); its `hipFree` cost grows as the process maps more memory.

| Shape | Time before | Time after | Peak allocated before | after | Peak reserved before | after | `empty_cache()` calls before | after | Byte-identical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 (896 experts, w13 768 x 3584) | 3.79 s | 0.13 s | 1.56 GiB | 2.89 GiB | 1.85 GiB | 4.56 GiB | 228 | 4 | yes |
| EP8 (112 experts, w13 6144 x 3584) | 3.07 s | 0.30 s | 3.43 GiB | 2.89 GiB | 5.66 GiB | 4.56 GiB | 32 | 4 | yes |

**New test:** `tests/kernels/quantization/test_k3_gfx942_int4_requant.py`. It runs on gfx942 only and is picked up by the existing "(MI300) Quantization Kernels" step. It checks that the output does not depend on chunking, and that no device memory is allocated after the first chunk on the Kimi-K3 TP8 w2 shape under `load_model`'s allocator settings. It passes 4/4 with the fix and fails before it. Against the refactor-only parent (9acd4b58ba), every chunk allocates:

```
E       assert [1724, 1737, ...76, 1789, ...] == [1724, 1724, ...24, 1724, ...]
1 failed, 3 passed
```

Against the first revision of this PR (3bdfe8097f), the shorter last chunk allocates:

```
E       assert [90, 90, 90, 90, 111] == [90, 90, 90, 90, 90]
1 failed, 3 passed
```

For those runs the test loaded `mxfp4.py` from each commit. On the parent I appended `_K3_INT4_CONVERT_CHUNK_VALUES` only so the test's `monkeypatch.setattr` resolves; the old code ignores it.

`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_gfx942_int4.py` and `tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py` still pass.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_setup_kernel_k3_situ_gfx942` converted 8 experts per chunk and called `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` after every chunk. Pure TP keeps all 896 experts per rank at 1/tp width, so TP8 ran 112 chunks per weight where EP8 runs 14, for the same bytes. That is 20,608 chunks over 92 MoE layers.

Every `empty_cache()` hands the chunk's temporaries back to the driver, and the next chunk allocates them again. In a live TP8 server, a native py-spy profile of the requant showed 92% of the time in `emptyCache -> release_block -> hipFree` (HSA `munmap`/`ioctl`) and about 5% in `hipMalloc`. The conversion kernels themselves barely appeared. That worked out to about 56 ms per chunk.

**Fix.**
- Size each chunk by unpacked values instead of experts, using `_K3_INT4_CONVERT_CHUNK_VALUES = 1 << 27`. TP8 and EP8 both run 19 chunks per w13 and 10 per w2.
- Drop the per-chunk `empty_cache()`, so later chunks reuse the cached temporaries. The cache is still emptied once per converted weight.
- Keep every chunk the same shape by shifting the last chunk back to overlap the previous one. Under `max_split_size_mb:20`, a cached block of 20 MiB or more is only reused for a request less than 20 MiB smaller, so a shorter last chunk would allocate a second set of temporaries. The overlapping experts are recomputed to identical values, which costs less than one chunk per weight.
- The output can't depend on chunk size: `per_1x32_i4_quant`, `shuffle_weight` and `shuffle_scale_for_int4` all work per expert along the leading dimension. The new test checks this explicitly.

**Tradeoffs.** The TP8 per-layer peak grows (allocated 1.56 to 2.89 GiB, reserved 1.85 to 4.56 GiB), because the old TP chunks were tiny. The EP8 peak shrinks (allocated 3.43 to 2.89 GiB, reserved 5.66 to 4.56 GiB). Both stay below the old EP8 peak, which already fit.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Reuse compiled FlyDSL host launchers
author: coderfeli
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reduce CPU overhead for warm FlyDSL launches by reusing compiled host launchers instead of repeating JIT argument binding and cache-key construction. Covers DeepSeek V4/V4.1 mono decode, Kimi K3 specialized decode, TurboQuant and UltraQuant.

## Claims

- Fix all nine remaining in-tree FlyDSL host launchers using the warm JIT path.
- Reduce measured host enqueue overhead by approximately 88% for TurboQuant and 89% for UltraQuant.

## Validation

Measured on gfx950 with PyTorch 2.10.0 and FlyDSL 0.4.0: 30 alternating batches of 100 launches, with GPU synchronization outside timed sections. Times are median (min–max), µs.

| Launcher configuration | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TurboQuant: B1, Hk8, GQA8, D128, BS16, context256 | 72.33 (70.71–74.15) | 8.57 (8.15–9.74) |
| UltraQuant: B1, Hk1, GQA8, D256, BS32, context2048 | 73.57 (72.98–79.64) | 8.30 (8.08–10.94) |

Existing GPU correctness suites: **68 passed before and after**. Dynamic batches **1→2→4→8→3→1** reuse the same compiled callable and match reference outputs. Dynamic arguments, row strides, compile-only and graph replay checks passed; pre-commit including mypy passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/kernels/turboquant/test_flydsl_turboquant_decode.py \
  tests/kernels/ultraquant/test_flydsl_decode_d256.py
```

Validation used a source-only editable installation. Full-model accuracy, TP serving and end-to-end performance were not measured because the target checkpoints and a complete ROCm extension build are unavailable.

## Details

Targets host dispatch during warm eager execution and graph capture. The results measure host enqueue time; steady graph-replay speedup was not measured. Open-PR searches found no duplicate fix for these call sites.
