title: [Model] Add Unlimited-OCR-2 DASH attention support
author: gty111
body:
Add native [Unlimited-OCR-2](https://huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2) support with DASH sparse attention and page-aware RoPE.

- FlashAttention and FlashInfer for chunked prefill and decode, using Model Runner V2.
- R-SWA retains input KV and bounds output KV to 128 tokens; full decode graphs and opt-in segmented prefill graphs.
- Model-specific preprocessing, decoder construction and optional GPU page-count guard. Shared DeepSeek decoder and scheduler files match main.

<details>
<summary>Usage and limitations</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 python examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_multi_image_offline.py \
    --model-type unlimited_ocr2 --num-images 2 --method generate
```

Use `"<PAGE><image>" * len(pages) + "Multi page parsing."` with images in page order, `temperature=0` and `skip_special_tokens=False`. `mm_processor_kwargs={"crop_mode": False}` selects a 1024-square global view. Invalid page/image sequences are rejected before worker execution.

FA is the default; select FI with `attention_config={"backend": "FLASHINFER"}`. The vision encoder falls back from FI to FA. `hf_overrides={"rswa_window": 0}` retains full output KV. Segmented prefill graphs require `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` and `cudagraph_mode="FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"`; dynamic DASH routing, attention and KV writes remain eager breaks. Whole-prefill FULL graphs are unsupported.

The page-count guard is opt-in through `vllm.model_executor.models.unlimited_ocr2:PageCountGuardLogitsProcessor`; it respects existing sampling masks, preserving EOS when it is the only finite choice. Its `SamplingParams.extra_args` include `page_token_id`, `eos_token_id` and `max_page_tokens` (default 20000; 0 disables the cap).

V1, prefix caching, quantization, PP/CP, LoRA, speculative decoding and KV transfer are unsupported. Validated on GB200/BF16 with prebuilt extensions; clean-build validation remains pending.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Evaluation and validation</summary>

MPDocBench historical full run (before chunked-prefill changes): 420 documents / 3,135 pages, V2. Overall is **84.7407** with the published-client fallback budget and **84.8430** with available-context budgets (paper reference **84.5900**). The latter has no length stops or page-count mismatches. This uses a local evaluation adapter and does not establish identical paper deployment or unpublished per-PDF budgets. MarathonDocBench was cancelled.

The preceding `f5033fd` 4-document / 29-page FA check (B=4, 513-token chunks) retains byte-identical raw and Markdown predictions. Real-weight `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_unlimited_ocr.py -k 'batched_pages and False' -x -q` passes all 6 FA/FI eager/decode/prefill-graph cases. No new throughput claim.

The [EOS-only guard review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64016#issuecomment-6523759526) is fixed: `allowed_token_ids=[EOS]` previously emitted `[0,0,0,0]`; it now emits exactly `[EOS]` and stops. CPU/GPU retain EOS when masking it would remove the last finite choice. GPU checks run within the existing kernel, stop at the first finite alternative, and perform no host readback. The same FA/FI eager/decode/prefill generation command above covers this case alongside normal OCR content.

Merged main `f1fd044b`. Prefill request metadata is prepared once from existing CPU buffers and shared across decoder layers. The mixed decode/prefill forward fails the CUDA-sync check before this change and passes afterwards with identical output.

**Open review issue:** the excess-marker raw-logit regression remains unresolved; its `atol=0.5, rtol=0` and source are unchanged. A zero-preemption control reproduces a 0.9375 difference at output 123 when comparing B=1 with B=2. A B=2/no-preemption vs B=2/preemption experiment passed FA/FI once, then failed FA with 0.875 on final confirmation, so that test rewrite was discarded. This establishes numerical sensitivity but does not rule out a simultaneous recomputation defect. Reconstructed pre-fix routing still fails (2.75). No passing preemption claim is made for this head. Reproducer: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_unlimited_ocr.py -k excess_markers -x -q`.

CI compatibility: FA2/3 use paged segment addressing, reduced-layer test configs resize DASH metadata, and vision/cold-shape initialization avoid blocking transfers. On GB200, FA2 real OCR and all 12 FA4/FI eager/decode/prefill-graph generation cases (with/without crops), plus both encoder-pressure cases, pass with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Hopper FA3 execution, ROCm and clean-build CI remain pending.

</details>

AI-assisted implementation. No duplicate model-support PR found; #57540 concerns generic n-gram sampling.

- [x] Local validation and model evaluation recorded above.
- [ ] Human design/code review and upstream CI complete.

</details>

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Specialized decode K2: sentinel all-reduces, pre-AR loads, tagged x rows
author: hyukjlee
body:
Stacked on #61435 (the last commit is this PR).

K2 options as `K2Build.opt` bits, default on (`K2_OPT = 891`). All are bit-exact vs `opt=0` (= #61435):

- 1 / 16 / 32: o_proj / latent / final all-reduce through sentinel regions (plain bf16 words, deferred re-arm)
- 2: AttnRes slice loads issued before the all-reduce poll
- 8: x rows as tagged pairs to the router / latent GEMVs
- 64: shared-down tasks needed by up run first
- 256: router partials pushed straight to every rank
- 512: batched polls

The runner adds ~10 MB of peer memory and ~4 MB of scratch.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DFlash draft acceptance of 0 with FULL CUDA graphs
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #63587. With the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, the DFlash draft reads a stale kernel block table, so none of its tokens are accepted. This PR maps the draft kernel block tables before the FULL graph replay, the same way `TargetDependentARSpeculator` already does (#57169).

## Claims

- DFlash-family drafts work again under FULL draft CUDA graphs when the KV cache block is split into smaller kernel blocks. Tested with hybrid `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` and a DFlash2 draft on B200: acceptance goes from 0.0000 to about 0.185, the same as the PIECEWISE control (0.1863).
- The FULL draft path from #60692 stays on. Throughput is 20.56–21.21 requests/s, against 6.59–6.67 before the fix and 11.57 with PIECEWISE.
- Adds one row to `test_dflash_correctness`. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- The code change is 8 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py`.

## Validation

Setup: 1 x NVIDIA B200. vLLM at `00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b` (`0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56`), with and without this patch. Target `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` (rev 851bf6e8), draft `nchapman/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash2` (rev 8d8bb628), both BF16. Every server log shows `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `Using FlashAttention version 4`, `Setting attention block size to 640 tokens` and `Capturing dflash2 CUDA graphs (FULL)`.

Server:

```
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"nchapman/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":15}' \
  --max-num-seqs 24 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8000
```

Wait for `Application startup complete`, then run `python client.py`. The client uses only the standard library. It sends 200 chat requests (concurrency 16, `max_tokens` 256, temperature 0) and prints how much the `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters changed.

<details>
<summary>client.py</summary>

```python
import json, sys, time, urllib.request, concurrent.futures as cf, re
base = "http://localhost:8000"
model = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B"
N, C = 200, 16
topics = ["the water cycle","binary search","the French revolution","how a transformer works","photosynthesis","TCP congestion control","the Roman empire","quicksort","black holes","the stock market"]
def metrics():
    t = urllib.request.urlopen(base + "/metrics").read().decode()
    d = {}
    for k in ["num_drafts_total","num_draft_tokens_total","num_accepted_tokens_total"]:
        m = re.search(r"^vllm:spec_decode_%s(?:\{[^}]*\})? ([0-9.e+]+)" % k, t, re.M)
        d[k] = float(m.group(1)) if m else None
    return d
def one(i):
    body = {"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"Write a detailed explanation of {topics[i%10]} (variant {i}). Include examples."}],
            "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0}
    if i == 0: print("REQUEST BODY (example, i=0):", json.dumps(body), flush=True)
    t = time.time()
    r = urllib.request.Request(base + "/v1/chat/completions", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    resp = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(r, timeout=900))
    print(f"req {i} status 200 {time.time()-t:.2f}s tokens={resp['usage']['completion_tokens']}", flush=True)
    return resp
m0 = metrics(); t0 = time.time()
with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(C) as ex: list(ex.map(one, range(N)))
dt = time.time() - t0; m1 = metrics()
d = {k: m1[k]-m0[k] for k in m0}
print(f"requests/s {N/dt:.2f}")
print("drafts", d["num_drafts_total"], "draft_tokens", d["num_draft_tokens_total"], "accepted", d["num_accepted_tokens_total"])
print(f"acceptance {d['num_accepted_tokens_total']/max(d['num_draft_tokens_total'],1):.4f}")
```

</details>

 | Tree | `cudagraph_mode` | Runs | `acceptance` | requests/s |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | base | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (default) | 4 | 0.0000 in every run (0 of 765000 draft tokens) | 6.59–6.67 |
 | base | `PIECEWISE` (control: adds `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`) | 1 | 0.1863 (37889 of 203325) | 11.57 |
 | this PR | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (default) | 6 | 0.1850, 0.1853, 0.1845, 0.1849, 0.1856, 0.1845 | 20.56–21.21 |

```
# base
drafts 51000.0 draft_tokens 765000.0 accepted 0.0
acceptance 0.0000
# this PR (run 1 of 6)
drafts 13678.0 draft_tokens 205170.0 accepted 37948.0
acceptance 0.1850
```

Every request returned status 200 in every run. Base: 3 runs were on one server, and 1 was on a fresh server on the same GPU as the patched runs. This PR: each run started a fresh server, 3 by me and 3 in a separate check. The base result also showed in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit (0 of 765000 accepted).

Regression test (new row `qwen3.5-4b-dflash2-mrv2`, same models, 15 speculative tokens, 32 sequences, default compilation config, GSM8K):

```
cd tests && python -m pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py -k 'qwen3.5-4b-dflash2'
```

 | Tree | Runs | Result | GSM8K accuracy | acceptance_len |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | base | 2 | FAILED: `acceptance_len 1.000 is below 4.095` | 0.845 | 1.00 |
 | this PR | 2 | PASSED | 0.845 | 4.55 |

The thresholds follow the other rows: accuracy 0.8, and acceptance length `4.55 * 0.9`, from the values measured with the fix. `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passes.

## Details

**Root cause.** Qwen3.5 is a hybrid model (attention plus GDN layers). To make the attention page match the mamba page, the KV cache manager uses 640-token blocks. The draft's FlashAttention 4 backend uses 128-token kernel blocks. So the draft attention group reads its block table from the persistent `AttentionGroup.kernel_block_table` buffer (`vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`), and the captured FULL graph reads that buffer. Only `map_to_kernel_block_table` fills it, and only the eager metadata build calls that (`_with_kernel_block_table`).

Since #60692, `DFlashSpeculator.propose` skips `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` when it replays a FULL graph and every draft backend supports `update_draft_decode_metadata`. The in-graph `_update_draft_decode_metadata` only asks each builder to refresh its own data. It does not map the block table. So after capture, the buffer keeps the rows from the dummy all-zero block table: kernel pages 0..4, which belong to the null block. On every replay the draft reads the null block's K/V instead of the request's. The drafts are unrelated to the context, and the target rejects all of them. The output stays correct because the target checks every token.

A debug print before `run_fullgraph` (not part of this PR) confirmed this. Request 0 owned manager block 83, so its kernel row should be `[415, 416, 417, 418, 419]`, but the buffer held `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`. With the fix, it held `[415, 416, 417, 418, 419]`.

**Fix.** In the branch where the build is skipped, call `group.map_to_kernel_block_table(self.block_tables.input_block_tables[group.kv_cache_group_id])` for every draft attention group before the replay. This is the same step `TargetDependentARSpeculator._fused_multi_step_decode` takes before its FULL replay. `map_to_kernel_block_table` already handles the kernel block size, the packed stride and the backend, and it returns at once for groups with no split. When the build does run, it maps the table itself, so that path is unchanged. DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark, LiLiCorr and XPress all use this `propose`.

**Other FULL draft replays checked.** `TargetDependentARSpeculator` (MTP, EAGLE, Gemma4) already maps the table before its fused FULL replay. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` builds the metadata before `run_fullgraph`. `StandaloneARSpeculator` does not use FULL replay.

**Not chosen.** Mapping inside `_update_draft_decode_metadata` would also map again on every `TargetDependentAR` step, which already maps. Reporting `supports_decode_metadata_update = False` for split groups would turn #60692 off for these models.

**Limitations and notes for reviewers.**

- The issue does not name its checkpoints (a 9B FP8 target and an NVFP4 target, served through Dynamo). I validated with the 4B BF16 pair above and plain `vllm serve`. The issue saw acceptance of 0.004 and 0.0005; here it was exactly 0. The issue's `no KV cache group could be identified as the draft model's` warning did not appear here, and I did not look into it.
- The test row uses a community draft checkpoint, `nchapman/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash2`, the one used in the issue thread. If CI should use only official checkpoints, the row can point at another hybrid target/draft pair with the same block split.
- CI: the row id contains `dflash2`, so the nightly `spec-decode-dflash2-nightly-b200` step (`-k "dflash2"`) selects it. `-k dflash2` also selects it in non-B200 steps (H100, MI355), and the thresholds were measured only on B200.

title: Ship mamba SSU and Helion tuned kernel configs in wheel package_data
author: tarukumar
body:
## What this PR does

The tuned Triton kernel config JSONs under `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/configs/selective_state_update/` and `vllm/kernels/helion/configs/` are not listed in `package_data` in `setup.py`. They only end up in the wheel through the **setuptools-scm git file-finder**: because `include_package_data` is enabled, every git-tracked file under the package is swept into the wheel.

That mechanism only works when the wheel is built from a **git checkout**. When someone builds vLLM from a source without `.git` — e.g.:

- `pip install vllm.tar.gz` (building from the **sdist** — the sdist itself does not carry the configs either, since `MANIFEST.in` doesn't include them),
- building from a `git archive` export / source tarball with `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` set (common in distro and internal-mirror packaging),
- any build environment where setuptools-scm's file finder cannot run,

the file finder is inactive and only the explicitly-listed `package_data` globs are packaged. The result is a wheel that **installs and runs fine but silently drops all tuned kernel configs**:

- Mamba/hybrid models log `Using default Mamba SSU config. Performance might be sub-optimal!` and fall back to the hard-coded launch heuristic (`_get_default_ssm_launch_config`), which is badly mismatched at small batch sizes — for hybrid models on Blackwell this showed up as ~8x slower CUDA-graph capture in the small/mid batch range, with no error anywhere,
- Helion kernels similarly lose their per-device tuned configs (`nvidia_b200.json`, `nvidia_h100.json`, ...).

Notably `model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/*.json` *is* listed explicitly, which is why those configs survive every build path — the two new entries bring the mamba and Helion config trees to the same guarantee.

## Reproduction

```bash
# from a git checkout: wheel contains the configs
python setup.py bdist_wheel  # SOURCES.txt: 7198 files, incl. 24 selective_state_update entries

# from a .git-less export: configs silently vanish
git archive HEAD | tar x -C /tmp/export && cd /tmp/export
SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.26.0 python setup.py bdist_wheel
# SOURCES.txt: 3513 files, selective_state_update/helion entries gone
```

## Fix

List both config trees explicitly in `package_data` so wheel contents no longer depend on the build context:

```python
"model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/configs/selective_state_update/*.json",
"kernels/helion/configs/*/*.json",
```

title: [ROCm][Model] Enable ROCm AITER unified attention for MiMo-V2.6
author: vllmellm
body:
## Overview

MiMo-V2.6 has asymmetric K/V head dims (192 / 128), which today pins it to the DiffKV attention backends: any other `--attention-backend` is silently replaced by the DiffKV auto-pick, and the native KV-cache write would copy V with K's head width. This PR makes `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` usable for the model (opt-in, defaults unchanged) and fixes the write kernel.

## Claims

- `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` now selects unified attention for every MiMo-V2.6 layer instead of being dropped; verified on Flash (TP2, TP4, TP8) and on Pro (TP8, gsm8k n=100 parity).
- `reshape_and_cache_flash` writes V with its own head size and head stride. Symmetric callers run the same code as before: the new checks live in the asymmetric branch, and the existing kernel is byte-identical to `main`.
- Accuracy and speculative-decoding parity with the default backend (gsm8k at n=1319, MTP x3 acceptance).
- At long context prefill is 1.43x faster at 128k and 1.21x at 32k, with decode 1.17x faster per token (TPOT p50 2.94 vs 3.45 ms) and output throughput up 21-45%. At 8k with concurrency 8 the two are at parity. Measured with `--block-size 16` on both arms, which tested better than the backend's default for this shape. On Pro at TP8 the same benchmark gives 1.13x prefill and 1.66x lower inter-token latency.

## Validation

### Commands

```bash
# serve (TP4 shown; TP2/TP8 differ only in --tensor-parallel-size; the control arm drops
# --attention-backend and gets the DiffKV auto-pick)
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 270336 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.82 \
  --block-size 16 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \
  --disable-prefix-caching \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo

# serve bench, one cell (input/output lengths and prompt counts per the tables)
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 32 \
  --num-prompts 2 --max-concurrency 1 --num-warmups 1 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 0

# gsm8k 25-shot against the running server
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template

# tests
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k asymmetric
pytest tests/models/test_mimo_v2_attention_backend.py
```

### Bench serve

Mimo-V2.6 Flash at TP4:

| workload | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k in / 32 out, 2 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 7633.8 ms | 5317.7 ms | -30% (1.44x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: output throughput | 4.10 tok/s | 5.96 tok/s | +45% |
| 32k in / 128 out, 4 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 890.9 ms | 738.2 ms | -17% (1.21x) |
| 32k in / 128 out: TPOT p50 | 3.45 ms | 2.94 ms | -15% |
| 32k in / 128 out: output throughput | 96.1 tok/s | 116.0 tok/s | +21% |
| 8k in / 256 out, 8 prompts, c8: ITL p50 | 8.42 ms | 8.48 ms | parity |
| 8k in / 256 out: output throughput | 929 tok/s | 947 tok/s | +2% |

On MiMo-V2.6-Pro at TP8:

| workload | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k in / 32 out, 2 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 9665.0 ms | 8576.9 ms | -11% (1.13x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: ITL p50 | 19.52 ms | 11.77 ms | -40% (1.66x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: output throughput | 3.23 tok/s | 3.68 tok/s | +14% |

Acceptance rate:
| | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified |
|---|---|---|
| MTP acceptance, 128k (acc % / length) | 53.33 / 2.07 | 56.67 / 2.13 |
| MTP acceptance, 32k | 61.40 / 2.23 | 55.60 / 2.11 |
| MTP acceptance, 8k c8 | 57.4-60.5 | 58.2-60.3 |


### lm_eval

| checkpoint | unified | DiffKV | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flash, gsm8k n=1319 | 0.9750 / 0.9742 | 0.9719 / 0.9712 | strict / flexible |

### Needle-In-A-Haystack

Unified attention only; `--max-model-len 270336`, thinking off, greedy.

| probe | config | result |
|---|---|---|
| niah | 265,673 tokens, depths 0 / 50 / 100 % | 3/3 |

### Tests

```
# kernel fix: main's cache_kernels.cu vs this one
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k asymmetric        # 33 failed -> 33 passed
# model change: main's backend selection vs this one (either kernel)
pytest tests/models/test_mimo_v2_attention_backend.py             # 2 failed, 5 passed -> 7 passed
```

The asymmetric kernel test runs MiMo's geometry (K 192 / V 128, 4 KV heads) at both block sizes the model uses (16 and 64) over a parametrized token count, in both layouts unified attention hands the kernel, for bf16 and fp8 caches and per-tensor and per-head scales. The whole file stays green (694 passed, 602 skipped).

The model test gained two checks: the selected backend's *impl* has to be unified attention's, not just its enum; and the cache the layer writes has to match a cache built in torch, per slot, with K in the first `head_dim` columns of a row and V in the remaining `v_head_dim`. Both fail on `main`. The kernel test's buffers carry slack past the cache, so a regressed kernel fails that comparison instead of writing out of bounds.

## Details

`reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel` derived one head size, one page stride, one head stride and one element count from key/key_cache and reused all of them for the value side:

```cpp
cache_t* v_dst_h = value_dst + head * head_stride;             // K's stride
vectorize_with_alignment(value_src, value_dst, n_elems, ...);  // K's width
```

Every caller until now was symmetric, so this was invisible. Unified attention is the first caller that passes `v_head_size != head_size` (MiMo is 192 / 128, packed as one `(head_size + head_size_v)` content dim per KV head), and for it V was read at K's per-head offset, copied at K's width - 64 elements past the end of each head - and written past the end of the cache on the last slot. The asymmetric case now gets its own kernel that addresses V with the value side's own head stride and length; the existing kernel and its NHD fast path are untouched, so symmetric callers run the same code as before.

Model side: the attention backend is chosen per layer, and the gate now consults a backend capability (`supports_head_size_v`) rather than listing backend names. DiffKV declares that it can serve any K/V width relation; unified attention declares `v <= k`, because it splits the page with `split(head_size)`. A backend that cannot serve the shape still gets the previous behaviour: a warning and the DiffKV auto-pick.

Known limitations:

- Requires aiter >= 0.1.25 for the V-dim-masked unified-attention kernels; `main` pins 0.1.26.
- Unified attention serves V narrower than K, not wider (`v_head_dim > head_dim` cannot be expressed by its page split); such a request falls back to the DiffKV auto-pick with a warning.


---

title: [Perf] Muse Spark Open Specialized Decode: Optimized GB300 Decode (1.5x)
author: djmmoss
body:
## Overview This is an NVIDIA-developed specialized decode of Muse Spark Open (NVFP4, DSpark speculative decoding) for GB300 that gives 1.5x single-stream decode throughput, in the form of the Kimi K3 specialized decode (#61867). - Tensor parallel 4, 8 or 16 with expert parallelism (EP = TP); at TP8 the routed experts run tensor-parallel inside the executor. - DSpark verification with 7 draft tokens, including the draft model's forward and its Markov sampling loop. - Any context length up to `--max-model-len`, including sliding-window layers. It is opt-in with `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`; the default, `auto`, keeps the stock decode. Changes are localized to `vllm/models/muse_spark/` (the executor in `nvidia/specialized_decode/`, the model hooks, and the DSpark draft model, which implements the speculator's `sample_sequential` hook) plus three CUDA C ops in `csrc/muse_spark/` and their registration (`CMakeLists.txt`, `csrc/ops.h`, `csrc/torch_bindings.cpp`, `vllm/_custom_ops.py`, additions only). No other shared vLLM code changes. ## Claims Single-stream decode (ISL 1, OSL 1000, concurrency 1, DSpark K 7 with forced acceptance length 6) on GB300 NVL72 trays, ours and stock vLLM on one allocation per row: - **TP8+EP8: 1.53x** (698.60 -> 1072.14 tok/s/user) - **gsm8k matches stock** within one standard error at TP8+EP8 (1253 vs 1255 of 1319). ## Validation ### Correctness Testing | Task | Stock TP8+EP8 | Ours TP8+EP8 | |---|---|---| | gsm8k 5-shot, flexible-extract (n 1319) | 0.9515 +- 0.0059 | 0.9500 +- 0.0060 | | gsm8k 5-shot, strict-match (n 1319) | 0.9522 +- 0.0059 | 0.9492 +- 0.0060 | `--max-model-len 32768`, adaptive verification off, block rejection, concurrency 1, both arms on one allocation. Paired, U - S is -2 questions (flexible-extract; exact McNemar p 0.83). Greedy outputs at TP4, TP8 and TP16 are identical across server starts. **Accuracy** (TP=4, single concurrency, real rejection sampling, max-model-len 32768) | Dataset | Original decode | Dedicated decode | |---|---|---| | OCRBench (1000 questions) | 81.8 | 81.6 | | AIME26 (30 questions, temperature 1.0) | 93.3% (28/30) | 93.3% (28/30) | ### Performance Validation DSpark speculative decoding only (the executor serves the verify step); median interactivity (1000 / median TPOT) over 200 requests, each row's two arms on one allocation.
Commands and setup ```bash # Server: each tray runs one vllm serve with --node-rank k (rank 0 serves the API, the others add --headless) vllm serve meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size <8|16> --enable-expert-parallel --nnodes <2|4> --node-rank --master-addr \ --max-model-len <2048|1048576> --reasoning-parser muse --tool-call-parser muse --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --numa-bind --numa-bind-nodes 0 0 1 1 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"","num_speculative_tokens":7, "draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length":6,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \ --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}' # ours only # Client vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 1000 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --seed 0 \ --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 200 --num-warmups 2 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el ``` Both arms: vLLM main at 1fd6337e22 (stock) and the same with this change, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 (vLLM's pin), the model with its two BF16 expert layers quantized to NVFP4 locally, no `--linear-backend`, the default FlashInfer all-reduce backend.
## Details ### vLLM Integration The Muse Spark model builds a `SpecializedDecode` after its weights load (`nvidia/model_state.py`, using the ModelState protocol and `initialize_kv_cache()` as #61867 does) and calls it from `forward()`. It serves the verify step of one request (1 + 7 draft tokens) captured into FULL CUDA graphs; when `plan()` returns None (prefill, mixed batches, several requests, partial drafts, eager or PIECEWISE steps) the stock forward runs. `unsupported()` checks the deployment at startup and names the first requirement it fails. The lm_head, `compute_logits` and the attention backend's metadata and KV cache stay shared. The executor runs, per layer, the input boundary, the attention (fused QKV + QK-norm + RoPE + KV insert, decode attention fused with the output norm and gate, o_proj), the attention boundary and the MoE (FP32 router, routing that also writes the routed experts' metadata, pooler GEMM with a fused all-gather + norm + NVFP4 quantization, the TRT-LLM-gen routed experts, finalize, unpooler GEMM), each block a provider in `specialized_decode/runtime/`. The fused all-reduce boundaries sum in the order of the stock FlashInfer all-reduce backend the deployment resolves (MNNVL or TRT-LLM), so TP4 needs vLLM's FlashInfer all-reduce. The draft model runs its forward and, through the DSpark speculator's `sample_sequential` hook, the Markov loop over a vocab-parallel Markov head (`runtime/draft.py`, `runtime/markov.py`). Kernels are in `specialized_decode/cutedsl/` (CuTe DSL) and `csrc/muse_spark/` (CUDA C: the QKV front, the decode attention and the routing). FlashInfer is used only from `runtime/flashinfer_ops.py`: the public routed experts ops, and on NVFP4 layers the runner below the public op, fed by the package's routing metadata, with the expert-TP tactic pinned per trtllm-gen cubin package (the op's default under any other). Kernels that reuse FlashInfer code are adapted from its source at a public sha, each header carrying the Apache-2.0 notice. Unit and kernel tests are kept out of this PR, as in #61867 (available on request; 2735 passed on one GB300 tray).

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf]  Enable prefix-cache SWA replay on gfx950
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Overview

Re-enable DeepSeek-V4.1 prefix-cache sliding-window bounded replay on gfx950. Decoder replay is a separate path and is already enabled by #59039 when `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` is on. This PR only restores the prefix-cache path from #57906.

The AITER sparse MLA path consumes slot IDs that `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` has already clamped to `replay_start`. The ROCm force-off in `attention.py` stays in place for every ROCm GPU other than gfx950, including gfx942. On gfx950 the sliding-window cache follows `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay`.

## Claims

- On gfx950, prefix-cache SWA replay is no longer forced off. The flag still defaults on, and `--no-swa-bounded-replay` still disables it. Other ROCm GPUs stay on the existing force-off path.
- On our best MI355X config, end-to-end throughput is 13.5% higher at concurrency 128 and 12% higher at concurrency 256.
- GSM8K and RULER NIAH are unchanged between stock and replay.

## Validation

GSM8K, 1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, all questions in flight:

| Arm | Accuracy |
|---|---:|
| Stock, replay off | 0.904
| Replay on | 0.902

RULER `niah_single_1` (single needle, word key, number value, repeated haystack), 131,072 tokens, 5 samples, temperature 0:

| Arm | Score |
|---|---:|
| Stock, replay off | 1.0 |
| Replay on | 1.0 |

Prefix-cache sweep across the prefill-chunk boundary. Each point primes eight DP replicas with a shared prefix plus 128 new tokens, then repeats the query. `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` is the hit signal. Every second-wave request completed on both arms, with no GPU fault.

| Prefix tokens | Stock hit tokens | Replay hit tokens |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,920 | 15,360 | 15,360 |
| 2,048 | 16,256 | 16,384 |
| 2,176 | 17,280 | 17,408 |
| 4,096 | 32,640 | 32,768 |

A separate single-request check on an otherwise stock nightly (`00b6c4c`, chunk 2048, DEP8, one request, token-id prompts) shows the config-flag A/B. Warmed requests:

| Shape | Stock | Replay |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8k TTFT | 492 ms | 316 ms |
| 32k TTFT | 1.84 s | 1.23 s |
| 128k TTFT, 1k output | 7.42 s | 4.83 s |
| 128k prefill | 17,667 tok/s | 27,136 tok/s |
| 128k decode | 52 tok/s | 49–62 tok/s |

Decode does not change. A decode step is already one new token inside the window.

CI does not have this MI355X checkpoint, so Buildkite does not cover this path.

## Details

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 40 layers. KV is written at layers 2, 8, 14, and 20. The sliding window is 128 tokens. After layer 20 has written KV for a token, layers 21–39 only need the last 128 tokens. That trim is decoder replay (#59039). It is built from `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` and is already active on ROCm when the flag is left on.

This change is the prefix-cache half. On a prefix-cache hit, the SWA cache replays from `replay_start` instead of storing the full sliding window. gfx950 can take that path because AITER sparse MLA uses the already-clamped slot list. The old force-off assumed an extra clamp inside the FlashInfer and FlashMLA prefill kernels, which this path does not use. gfx942 cannot take AITER sparse MLA, so it stays forced off.

To enable it on a gfx950 recipe that sets `VLLM_NO_SWA_BOUNDED_REPLAY=1`, remove that setting. Keep model runner V2 and breakable CUDA graphs. A 4096-token prefill chunk is above the 768-token replay trim threshold, so it uses the trimmed graph.


## ROCm consumers

CDNA4 keeps prefix-cache SWA replay. Both ROCm consumers clamp to replay_start:

- Opt-in AITER sparse MLA reads slot ids from _compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel, which clamps start_pos.
- The default Triton gather path clamps the prefill gather length in ComputePrefillMetadataKernel and clamps swa_start again in combine_topk_swa_indices.

Every other ROCm GPU, including CDNA3, stays forced off. get_cdna_version() != 4 is the gate.
Limitations:

- Measured on gfx950 with the AITER Triton sparse MLA path.
- The flag defaults on, so gfx950 behavior changes for every DeepSeek-V4.1 server that does not pass `--no-swa-bounded-replay`.

title: [KV Connector][Spec Decode] Support lookahead block hashes in KV connectors
author: andakai
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #61589, extending lookahead block hashes to NIXL P/D, Mooncake P/D, Mooncake Store, and OffloadingConnector. MultiConnector supports them when all configured children opt in.

This allows compatible connectors to reuse KV whose hashes include the required lookahead tokens, without the additional EAGLE/MTP trailing-block drop. Unsupported connectors retain legacy hashing.

## Implementation

- **Enablement:** Enable lookahead hashing for supported connectors through `supports_lookahead_block_hashes`, and propagate `num_hash_lookahead_tokens`. MultiConnector enables it only when all children support it.

- **P/D connectors:** Enable lookahead hashing for NIXL and Mooncake. Clear and rebuild request hashes after P-side prompt truncation.

  For example, with block size 4 and lookahead 1, hashes are computed when the request is created. In the Mamba P/D path, P then removes the final token for D to process:

  ```text
  Request creation:  ABCDE → hashes = [H(ABCD, E)]
  P-side truncation: ABCD  → hashes = [H(ABCD, E)]  # stale entry
  After rebuilding:  ABCD  → hashes = []           # no lookahead token yet
  ```

  Truncating the token sequence does not automatically remove existing hashes. This PR adds the following after truncation in both connectors:

  ```python
  request.block_hashes.clear()
  request._prompt_embeds_per_block_hashes.clear()
  request.update_block_hashes()
  ```

  Clearing is necessary because `update_block_hashes()` only appends new hashes; it does not remove stale entries.

- **Mooncake Store and OffloadingConnector:** Limit saves to KV covered by available hashes (`len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size`), since computed KV may extend beyond the hashed prefix. Skip the extra EAGLE trailing-block drop in lookahead mode and align hybrid/Mamba cache boundaries with core prefix caching.

  For example, with block size 4 and eight computed tokens:

  ```text
  Computed KV:      [A B C D] [E F G H]

  Legacy hashes:    H(ABCD), H(EFGH)
  Lookahead = 1:    H(ABCD, E), no hash for EFGH yet
                               └─ requires the next token I
  ```

  With lookahead hashing, eight computed tokens do not necessarily mean two available cache keys.

- **Mooncake Store request completion:** Save blocks that become eligible after the final sampled token completes their lookahead hash.

  For example, with block size 4, lookahead 1, prompt `ABCD`, and `max_tokens=1`:

  ```text
  Build metadata:  ABCD  → no lookahead hash; no save scheduled
  Sample E:       ABCDE → H(ABCD, E) becomes available
  Request ends:         → queue a finish-time save for ABCD's KV
  ```

  The hash appears after this step's metadata was built, and the finished request will not return to normal scheduling. `register_finished_lookahead_save()` queues the save, while `_reference_save_blocks()` prevents the source blocks from being reused before the asynchronous save completes.

## Validation

Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B on GB300, BF16, TP=1, MTP k=4, prefix caching enabled, and an 80 GiB KV cache.

GSM8K uses all 1,319 questions with 5-shot strict-match scoring. GPQA Diamond uses all 198 questions with thinking enabled. Both use temperature 0 and seed 42.

The GPU results below compare candidate `d8f84103ee66` against main `0076619a94f5`. Baselines run without a connector, using the same SSM layout as the corresponding candidate: DS for NIXL/MultiConnector and SD for the remaining configurations.

| OffloadingConnector | 96.51% | 96.51% | 81.31% | 81.31% |

**Performance**

Tested with GB300, Qwen3.6-27B, MTP with k=4, ISL=8K, OSL=1K, gpu-memory-utilization=0.8

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode at TP8 on MI355X
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Purpose

Mono decode (`--monokernel`) for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs only at TP2 and TP4. `MonoDecodeLayer._create` refuses any other tensor-parallel size. At conc 1 a TP8 server can still use mono decode: each rank streams half the weights, while the persistent K1/K2 chain stays the same length. This PR makes the existing FlyDSL kernels correct at TP8 on gfx950. That means 8 attention heads per rank, and a 288-wide routed/shared expert intermediate (routed is padded to 384 by the loader).

At TP8 the only kernel changes are the head-tile rounding and one GEMV tail. The cross-rank reduction, MoE, router, K1 front, combine and draft runner already loop over `tp` and need no changes.

## Changes

- `mono/attention/plan.py`, `Dims`: `head_tiles` now rounds up (`cdiv(heads, 16)`), and a new `heads_pad` gives whole tiles. Before this, `head_tiles` was `8 // 16 = 0` at TP8, so the split-attention loops (`back.py`) emitted no MFMAs and would silently produce wrong output once the gate opens.
  - At M=7, ratio 2, the CPU compile for gfx950 shows 0 bf16 MFMAs before the fix and 32 after, the same count as TP4.
  - A rank must have at least one tile; this is asserted.
- `mono/attention/back.py`: the split stage's q/p/st LDS and the stat offset are sized by `heads_pad`. The padded head columns are computed but never stored. That is correct by column independence:
  - each head has its own score max and its own PV column;
  - the stat stores and the combine read only `h < heads`.
- `mono/stages/gemv.py`: the row-major FP8 step load accepts `K % 64 == 32`, which is the shared expert's down projection at K = 288. The last step's upper lanes are clamped into the row, and `_fp8_step_mfma` already zeroes them on both sides.
- `mono_decode.py`: the gate admits TP8. gfx942 stays TP4 only (`:410`).
- Tests: TP8 cases are added to `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` (`tp in [2, 4, 8]`) and `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (`(8, 8)` and `(8, 28)` on cdna4).

## Test Plan

1. CPU-only FlyDSL compile for gfx950 (AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0), on this branch and on unmodified main:
   - TP8 builds: K1, K2 and FFN at M = 7 and 28; ratios 0, 1 and 2; the index-source and fold variants; and the DSpark draft K1/K2.
   - TP2 and TP4 builds: compared byte for byte against main.
2. GPU, 8x MI355X: a TP8 server with `--monokernel` running the MLPerf conc-1 recipe:
   - DSpark k=6;
   - adaptive verification off;
   - decoder SWA bounded replay;
   - MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer.

   Measurements:
   - `vllm bench serve`, random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic acceptance length 3.87, so the step time is isolated from acceptance;
   - GSM8K-1319, 8-shot greedy, block rejection with real acceptance, on the same server.
3. To run on this branch with 8 GPUs:
   ```
   pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py -k "8"
   pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py -k "8-8 or 8-28"
   ```

## Test Result

**CPU compile:** every TP8 build compiles with 0 VGPR spills, scratch 0, and LDS ≤ 137,248 B. TP2 and TP4 kernel binaries are byte-identical to main.

| Build | VGPR | LDS (B) |
|---|---|---|
| TP8 K1, M=7 | 142 | 38,944 |
| TP8 K2, M=7 (ratio 1/2, index) | 250 | 96,640 |
| TP8 K2, M=28 | 232 | 137,248 |
| TP8 FFN, M=7 | 243 | 79,408 |
| TP8 draft K2, M=6 | 199 | 96,640 |

**GPU, this PR alone:**
- Image: nightly `5d35ce3934` + this PR, with none of the other open DSv4.1 PRs. `mono/` and `mono_decode.py` are identical to this PR's base.
- Setup: one TP8 server with the MLPerf conc-1 recipe, `--monokernel` on or off and nothing else changed.

Decode step: random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic AL 3.87; ITL p50 is one DSpark step.

| TP8 | c1 step | c1 tok/s | c4 step | c4 TPOT | c4 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--monokernel` (this PR) | **5.36 ms** | 580 | **8.10 ms** | 2.57 ms | 1163 |
| without | 8.59 ms | 392 | 10.10 ms | 3.38 ms | 1014 |
| change | **-37.5%** | +48% | **-19.8%** | -24% | +15% |

Quality, same servers, real (block) acceptance:

| TP8 | GSM8K-1319 (2 runs) | AL | RULER NIAH 32k (8 tasks x 50) | RULER NIAH 128k (8 tasks x 25) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--monokernel` | 0.910 / 0.910 | 3.562 / 3.587 | 0.997 | 0.993 |
| without | 0.923 / 0.923 | 3.563 / 3.593 | 0.998 | 0.990 |

- NIAH: lm-eval 0.4.13, all 8 `niah_*` tasks, greedy, mean over tasks.
- GSM8K: mono on vs off is a paired McNemar of 26/44 flips (p 0.041) and 28/45 (p 0.060). The same arm run twice gives 35/35 and 33/32.
- Status of the GSM8K gap: investigated, but not explained yet. The layer tests below pass, and an earlier TP4 on/off pair went the other way (mono 0.929 vs 0.919).

Layer tests, all passing on 8x MI355X:
- `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[8]` and `[4]`;
- `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-8]` and `[8-28]`.

CI: an optional `mi355_8` step runs the TP8 cases (the 4-GPU step skips them).

An earlier measurement on nightly `83c078d955` + #63182, #63027, #63367, #63181 and #63355 gave 4.97 ms at c1 for TP8 + mono, vs 5.27 ms for TP4 + mono. There, GSM8K was 0.917 and AL 3.568.

**Follow-ups (not in this PR):**
- With the launch-count reductions in #63885, #63888, #63890 and #63891 and the tuned K1 of #63893 (on #63027) and X8R of #63892 widened from TP4 to TP8, conc 1 reaches **4.53 ms** (GSM8K 0.919, AL 3.570). That is -14% vs TP4 + mono on the same image. The TP8 widening of #63892/#63893 is a follow-up. It also needs #63027's tuned seam (`attn_words`) to poll its 16 per-rank ATTN units in one batch: `POLL_MAX` is 12, so a split batch costs two serial round trips.
- **Not for conc ≥ 4.** At conc 4, one TP8 server is 26% lower in throughput than 2 x TP4 replicas: 1262 vs ~1706 tok/s, TPOT 2.35 vs ~1.71 ms. TP8 mono is a conc-1 configuration.
- The mono kernels' cross-rank spin-waits are unbounded, at TP4 as well. A hang on one rank stalls every rank of the server, which matters more at 8 ranks. A bounded wait with a host fail-stop, as the Kimi-K3 mono has, is planned as a separate PR.

title: [New Model] Add MiniMax-M3.1-Flash Model and Kernels
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

The first PR of the split of #63232. It adds the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash model code (everything under `vllm/models/minimax_m3`, NVIDIA and ROCm, including the DSpark draft) and all kernel changes. The model-runner, sampling and KV cache manager changes from #63232 are left out and will follow as separate PRs (plan under Details).

## Claims

- **Serve MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on Blackwell (SM100/SM103/SM107):** the NVFP4 routed experts of the MXFP8 checkpoint load through the compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE with per-token FC1 input scales. The KV cache and the index-K cache run in NVFP4 on the MSA CUTLASS Q8KV4 kernels.
- **DSpark speculative decoding:** a draft model that defaults to the checkpoint's `dspark/` subfolder, with fused draft kernels and a `FLASHINFER_TS` backend for non-causal draft blocks.
- **Decode kernels:**
  - fused QKV+indexer MXFP8 GEMM epilogue;
  - SM100 fused dense GEMM1;
  - persistent QK-norm/RoPE/KV-insert kernel;
  - small-batch MoE finalize fused into all-reduce + Gemma norm + MXFP8 quant;
  - DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE (opt-in, with expert parallelism);
  - opt-in NVFP4 indexer decode context parallelism at TP4.
- **ROCm:**
  - NVFP4 KV + NVFP4 indexer on gfx950;
  - one-launch-per-layer FlyDSL mono decode;
  - small-M MXFP8 linear tuning;
  - gfx942 fallbacks.

## Validation

Unit tests ran on GB300 (SM103) against this branch, with MSA `25c1447` (the pinned version) vendored and CUDA 13.4 for the Q8KV4 JIT:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/attention -k minimax_m3` | 219 passed, 64 skipped (ROCm/other-SM) |
| fused QK-norm/RoPE/KV insert, DSpark draft kernels, MegaMoE, `tests/models/minimax_m3`, Qwen3-DFlash MXFP8 context KV, reasoning parser, speculative config, `FLASHINFER_TS`, DFlash/DSpark spec-decode unit tests, aux hidden states over PP, M3 multimodal processing, `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py` | 689 passed, 5 skipped, 3 failed (below) |
| `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py` (2 GPUs) | 57 passed, 5 skipped |

The 3 failures (`test_modelopt_fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`, `test_modelopt_mixed_dspark_checkpoint`, `test_modelopt_nested_mixed_checkpoint`) fail identically on `main` in the same environment. They are not caused by this PR.

**End-to-end on this branch.** `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` served with the command below (TP4 on GB300, NVFP4 KV + NVFP4 indexer, DSpark k=7). Higher is better. MAL is the mean number of tokens accepted per verify step, out of 8.

| Eval | Config | Score | DSpark MAL |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k (1319) | chat path, 5-shot, `thinking_mode: disabled`, T=0, max_tokens 2048 | 0.9287 flexible / 0.9196 strict | 4.77 |
| aime26 mean@16 (30 × 16) | chat path, `thinking_mode: enabled`, T=1.0, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 98304 | 0.9271 (pass@16 0.9667) | 3.48 |

Neither run had request errors. gsm8k had no truncated or unanswered rows. On aime26, 11 of 480 samples (2.3%) hit the max_tokens limit, and they are the only unanswered rows.

**On #63232 (the full branch)**, same setup with thinking on (aime26 mean@16, MMMU-Pro strict-match over 3460 questions):

| Arm | aime26 | MMMU-Pro strict | DSpark MAL (aime26 / MMMU-Pro) |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain | 0.9458 | 0.7936 | – |
| DSpark k=7 | 0.9208 | 0.7861 | 3.33 / 3.21 |

The two arms ran on different revisions of #63232. The paired comparison on one revision was within noise: aime26 +0.00 pp (95% CI ±3.0 pp), MMMU-Pro McNemar p=0.876.

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash -tp 4 --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "attention_backend": "FLASHINFER_TS", "kv_cache_dtype": "fp8", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}' \
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
```

Not covered:
- ROCm was not run (no AMD hardware here); the ROCm code is from the AMD contributors' branch and tests.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` was not run.

## Details

**Shared code this PR touches.** All of it is opt-in or a no-op for other models:
- `FusedMoEConfig.qat_activation_key` (default `None`): a model declares the activation scheme its experts were QAT'd against. `make_nvfp4_moe_kernel` now raises instead of silently dropping `per_token_activation` for a backend that cannot honor it.
- `ModelOptMxFp8Config.moe_quant_algo` (default `None`): routes `moe_quant_algo: NVFP4` experts to the compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE.
- `Attention(query_pre_quantized=False)`: lets the DSpark draft skip a second query quantization.
- `DraftModelSpeculator.attn_vllm_config`: the draft's metadata builders now see the draft overrides (attention backend, KV cache dtype). The copies are shallow, so engine-resolved state such as `cache_config.kv_cache_layout` survives. Covered by `test_draft_attention_backend_override.py`.
- New `FLASHINFER_TS` attention backend, `attention_config.indexer_decode_cp`, a MiniMax-M3 TP check for NVFP4 KV, and the MSA pin bump (`968061a` → `25c1447`).
- The CuTe DSL primitives of the DeepSeek-V4.1 all-reduce and the Kimi-K3 latent MoE tail move to `vllm/models/common/ops/moe_tail_fusion`, shared with the M3 finalize fusion. Their callers only change import paths.

**For reviewers:**
- The ROCm mono decode here (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO`) predates and overlaps the upstream M3 MonoKernel (#62712, `kernel_config.monokernel`). The two need reconciling; it can also move to its own PR.
- `attention_config.indexer_decode_cp` (NVFP4 indexer, TP4) sits next to the existing `minimax_m3_indexer_cp` (ROCm bf16 Triton CP).
- The Q8KV4 prefill keeps a per-device split workspace that is only allocated on SM107. It was a stopgap on the source branch.

**Split of #63232.** Later PRs:

| PR | Contents | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| this | MiniMax-M3.1 model + DSpark draft + kernels | – |
| 2 | ROCm NVFP4 → MXFP8/MXFP4 online re-quantization and fused shared experts through the online quantization API (needed to serve the NVFP4-expert checkpoint on ROCm) | – |
| 3 | NIXL P/D for per-head-contiguous NVFP4 pages (`AttentionSpec.kv_head_major_slots`) | this |
| 4 | FA4: no descale tensors for a unit per-tensor scale | – |
| 5 (deferred) | DSpark/DFlash sampling performance: Markov bias in the Gumbel kernel, batch-sharded draft sampling, wide DFlash padding, top-k/top-p | this |
| 6 (deferred) | KV cache manager: keep KV zeroing for mixed-precision groups | – |
| 7 (deferred) | SimpleCPUOffload HugeTLB host buffer (not MiniMax-specific) | – |

<details>
<summary>Where the excluded files of #63232 go</summary>

- **PR 2:** `quantization/online/*` (incl. `shared_expert.py`, `requantization.py`), `quantization/utils/config_utils.py`, `fused_moe/{utils,routed_experts}.py`, `quark/*`, `nvfp4_emulation_utils.py`, `base_config.py`, `model_loader/utils.py`, the NVFP4 oracle's re-quantization hook, the dequantize-iterator change in the ModelOpt/CT NVFP4 MoE, and the ROCm NVFP4-expert guard and FSE resolver in `minimax_m3/amd/model.py`.
- **PR 3:** `kv_cache_interface.py` (`kv_head_major_slots`), `nixl/base_worker.py`, the model's `kv_head_major_slots=True`, and its insert test.
- **PR 4:** `v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`.
- **PR 5:** `v1/worker/gpu/{sample/gumbel,sample/batch_shard,input_batch,model_runner}.py`, the rest of the DFlash/DSpark speculators, `v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_*`, the scheduler's DFlash/DSpark draft slots, and `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM.compute_draft_logits_local`.
- **PR 6:** `v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` and `KVCacheConfig.mixed_precision_kv_cache`.
- **PR 7:** `v1/simple_kv_offload/*` and its connector.
</details>

AI assistance (Claude, Codex, Kimi) was used to write parts of these changes and this PR; the author reviewed the split and ran the tests above.

title: [CI/Build] Add nixl auto-label rule and assign topic owners
author: NickLucche
body:
## Overview

Adds a `nixl` auto-label rule to `.github/mergify.yml`, mirroring the existing `mooncake` rule ([#59192](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59192)). PRs touching NIXL-related files or KV-offloading paths — the multi-tiered offloading path (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/`, KVCR tiering) and the NIXL KV connector (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/`, `vllm/distributed/nixl_utils.py`) — are labeled `nixl` and assigned to @ovidiusm and @iyastreb, so the NIXL team gets notified of KVCR / connector changes.

The `nixl` GitHub label itself is created out-of-band (labels are not versioned in this repo, and mergify cannot add a label that does not exist).

## Claims

- PRs touching any path containing `nixl` (case-insensitive) get the `nixl` label. This covers the NIXL KV connector and `vllm/distributed/nixl_utils.py`, NIXL EP dispatch (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/nixl_ep.py`), EC-transfer NIXL data (`vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/data/nixl.py`), the NIXL p2p data layer of the multi-tiered offload path (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/data/nixl.py`), and all NIXL tests, design docs, examples and tools.
- PRs touching any path containing `kv_offload` get the `nixl` label. This covers the multi-tiered offloading path (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/`, KVCR tiering), the simple offload path (`vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/`), their tests, and `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`.
- PRs with "NIXL" in the title get the `nixl` label.
- Matching PRs are assigned to @ovidiusm and @iyastreb (the assignment is what notifies them).

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files .github/mergify.yml` — all hooks pass, including `check-label-rules` (every `files=`/`files~=` condition matches at least one tracked file).
- Verified the two regexes against `git ls-files`: 155 tracked files match, all of them NIXL or KV-offloading related; negatives (e.g. `gpu_model_runner.py`, mooncake connector/tests, `offloading_connector.py`) correctly do not match; all paths covered by the original hardcoded list are still covered (strict superset).
- `gh label list --repo vllm-project/vllm` — confirms the `nixl` label exists.
- Duplicate checks: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "nixl label"` and `--search "auto-label"` — no open PR adds a nixl auto-label rule.
- No model evaluations: mergify/CI configuration only, no serving, output, or accuracy impact.

## Details

- The file conditions use `files~=(?i)nixl` and `files~=kv_offload` (per @hmellor's review suggestion) instead of a hardcoded directory list, matching the style of the existing `kimi`/`rust` rules. A path regex survives files moving between directories; the `check-label-rules` pre-commit hook exists precisely because hardcoded paths silently rot.
- Scope note: the `kv_offload` substring intentionally also covers `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/`, and `(?i)nixl` covers NIXL EP dispatch and EC-transfer NIXL files — all NIXL / KV-offloading work the team wants to be notified of.
- The rule follows the `label-mooncake` pattern exactly: label add + `assign` to the topic owners.

title: [Perf][DCP] Sparse indexer: key only significant bits in the DCP top-k merge
author: NickLucche
body:
## Overview

Since #61149 (DeepGEMM 2026-09-30), the SM100 MQA logits of the sparse indexer are BF16. Under DCP they are upcast to FP32 before the top-k, so the low 16 bits of every candidate score that reaches the DCP top-k merge are zero. The merge selector, `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`, radix-sorts the 64-bit key `score << 32 | ~token_id` in 11-bit passes. BF16 scores almost always tie at the top-k boundary. The radix then also walks the 16 zero score bits and the constant high bits of the token id, and each of those passes funnels every remaining candidate into a single histogram bin.

This PR packs only the bits that carry information into the key: the 16 high score bits when the logits were BF16, and the token-id bits that positions below `max_model_len` need. The selected set is unchanged.

## Claims

- Removes the DCP top-k merge cost that #61149 added. It applies to every DSA model with a sparse indexer under DCP on SM100 (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x).
  - With BF16 scores, the selector costs 1.6-1.7x what it costs with FP32 scores.
  - With this PR it is back to the FP32 cost. Per call at top-2048 on GB300:
    - DCP4: 16.7 → 10.6 us (FP32: 10.4), and 21.0 → 11.5 us on concentrated scores;
    - DCP8: 24.8 → 14.5 us (FP32: 14.3), and 32.2 → 19.0 us.
- GLM-5.3, TP4 DCP4 on one GB300 node, 60k-token prompts, 4 runs per variant on 2 nodes:
  - the selector goes from 21.0 to 14.2 us per call in decode (21 calls per step);
  - c1 TPOT p50 drops from 13.55 to 13.44 ms (-0.8%);
  - c2 TPOT p50 drops from 17.77 to 17.65 ms;
  - c8 ITL p50 drops from 19.30 to 19.13 ms.
- No behavior change:
  - The selection uses the same total order: score at the precision it was computed in, then the smaller token id.
  - Main and this PR select the same set:
    - in unit tests with forced boundary ties;
    - on 28.4M rows merged in GLM-5.3 runs and checked against main's selector. 97% of the rows with more than 2048 candidates had a tie at the boundary.
  - FP32 logits keep 32 score bits.
  - GSM8K is within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

### Serving: GLM-5.3 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`, FP8)

Setup:
- TP4 + DCP4 on one GB300 node (4 GPUs), model runner V2, default DCP backend (`a2a`);
- `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`;
- `--max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching`;
- `-cc.cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: decode steps replay full CUDA graphs. With the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `main` itself did not start on this setup: the ranks diverged during PIECEWISE capture. That is unrelated to this PR.
- `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 60000 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos`, with 6 prompts at c1, 12 at c2 and 24 at c8.

Method:
- Two Slurm jobs on two nodes. Each job runs four servers on the same node: `main, PR, main, PR` and `PR, main, PR, main`.
- Values are the means over the 4 runs of each variant. The per-run spread of c1 TPOT p50 is 0.01-0.03 ms.
- `main` is 803bc13cf9.

| | c1 main | c1 this PR | c2 main | c2 this PR | c8 main | c8 this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 13.55 | **13.44** | 17.77 | **17.65** | 52.52 | **51.91** |
| TPOT p99 (ms) | 13.65 | **13.47** | 20.65 | **20.46** | 61.50 | **61.07** |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 13.64 | **13.51** | 15.09 | **14.95** | 19.30 | **19.13** |
| TTFT p50 (ms) | 6673 | **6609** | 10059 | **9997** | 16284 | 16405 |
| output tok/s | 49.84 | **50.29** | 72.41 | **72.96** | 116.53 | **117.29** |

- Per run, c1 TPOT p50 is 13.55-13.56 ms on `main` and 13.43-13.46 ms with this PR.
- At c8, TPOT includes the steps that carry 8192-token prefill chunks of the other 60k-token prompts, so it varies by ±1 ms between runs. ITL p50 is the plain decode step: 19.23-19.42 ms on `main` and 19.04-19.21 ms with this PR.
- c8 TTFT depends on how the prefills interleave and is within its run-to-run spread (14.6-17.3 s).

GLM-5.3 has 21 sparse-indexer layers per step (`index_topk_freq=4`). Models with an indexer in every layer, like DeepSeek-V3.2, or DCP8 with 2x the candidates, save proportionally more per step.

### Kernel time in the model (torch profiler)

Same setup, 60k-token prompts, 8192 candidates per row (4 ranks × top-2048). The table gives the median per call on ranks 0 and 2 (they agree within 0.1 us). Each decode trace covers 29-40 steps (609-840 selector calls).

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge selector (`StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`), decode c1 (1 row) | 19.4 us | **13.8 us** |
| merge selector, decode c8 (8 rows) | 21.0 us | **14.2 us** |
| merge selector per decode step (21 calls), c1 / c8 | 409 / 441 us | **290 / 298 us** |
| merge selector, first 8192-token prefill chunk (8192 rows) | 649 us | **449 us** |
| local top-k `cooperative_topk` (control), c1 / c8 | 9.6 / 9.9 us | 9.7 / 9.9 us |

The per-step saving (119 us at c1, 143 us at c8) matches the measured TPOT/ITL gain. The prefill-chunk saving is where the ~1% lower c1 TTFT comes from: every prefill chunk runs the merge in each of the 21 indexer layers.

### Microbenchmark

All-gather selector alone on one GB300, top-2048, ids drawn from a 64k context (16 id bits). us per call, CUDA graph of 100 launches. "Wide" scores are N(0, 3²). "Narrow" scores are 60 + N(0, 4²): they are more concentrated, so more of them tie at BF16 precision. "set == ref" checks the selection against an FP64 reference.

| DCP | rows | scores | main | this PR | set == ref |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 4 | 1 | FP32 wide | 10.4 | **9.3** | yes |
| 4 | 1 | BF16 wide | 16.7 | **10.6** | yes |
| 4 | 1 | BF16 narrow | 21.0 | **11.5** | yes |
| 4 | 8 | BF16 narrow | 20.6 | **11.9** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | FP32 wide | 14.3 | **12.7** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | BF16 wide | 24.8 | **14.5** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | BF16 narrow | 32.2 | **19.0** | yes |
| 8 | 8 | BF16 narrow | 32.7 | **19.1** | yes |

FP32 logits keep 32 score bits and gain a little from the shorter id field.

### Correctness

- Selection on real model data:
  - A check-only build of this PR (not part of the diff) re-ran `main`'s selector (64-bit key) on the same gathered candidates after every DCP merge and compared the selected sets. It ran in eager mode, so it could sync.
  - Workload: GLM-5.3 TP4 DCP4, serving the greedy prompts below (up to 51k tokens), 200 GSM8K questions and 8 random 60k-token requests at c8. Prefill chunks and decode steps are both covered.
  - Two runs, counted on DCP rank 0: 28.4M merged rows.
    - 24.3M of them had more than 2048 valid candidates.
    - 23.7M (97%) had a tie at the top-k boundary.
    - **0 rows differed from `main`'s selection.**
  - The same check on GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, kpool indexer, top-512 pools out of 2048 candidates), TP4 DCP4 with `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 64`, covered the long greedy prompts and 4 random 60k-token requests at c8.
    - It checked 4.65M rows: 4.45M had more than 512 candidates, and 4.23M had a tie at the boundary.
    - **0 mismatches.**
- GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, completions, max concurrency 64), same setup as above:

| | runs | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| main | 3 | 90.8, 91.4, 91.4 |
| this PR | 2 | 91.8, 91.6 |

- Greedy (`temperature=0`), sequential at c1, 38 prompts: 34 short ones (128 tokens each) and 4 real-text prompts of 8k, 20k, 38k and 51k tokens (256 tokens each). This setup is not deterministic run to run, even on `main`:
  - `main`, the same server queried twice: 11/38 and 16/38 outputs differ;
  - `main` across server restarts: 14/38 and 15/38;
  - this PR, the same server twice: 12/38;
  - this PR vs `main`: 11/38, 13/38 and 16/38.

  Most of the differing prompts are short ones. There every valid candidate is selected, so this PR cannot change their result. The outputs diverge after a common prefix, as numerical noise does. So greedy identity cannot separate the two here. The check on real model data above can.

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

| | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py` (GB300) | 117 passed (incl. 3 new) | 114 passed |
| `pre-commit` (ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy, ...) | all hooks pass | |

New test `test_cutedsl_gathered_select_compact_keys_match_reference[16384|131072|1048576]`:
- BF16-valued scores: random, 64 distinct values (so the boundary tie spans hundreds of ids), all negative, padding mixed in, and all tied;
- token ids up to `num_positions - 1`;
- it checks that the default 64-bit key and the compact key (`score_bits=16`, `id_bits=dcp_topk_id_bits(num_positions)`) both select the FP64 reference set.

The server logs show no CuTeDSL JIT compilation during inference with this PR (`jit_monitor_mode=warn`), on GLM-5.3 and on GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool, `max_model_len // 4` id bits). So the new warm-up keys match the runtime keys.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- #61149 made the SM100 MQA logits (`fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`, `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`) BF16. `sparse_attn_indexer` upcasts them (`as_fp32_logits`) whenever DCP is on.
- `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel` builds `score_key << 32 | ~token_id` and runs up to 6 radix passes (11 bits each, the last one 9). It stops at the first pass whose threshold bin fits.
- With FP32 scores, the first 1-2 passes usually resolve the boundary. A BF16 score is complete after the first 16 key bits (passes 1-2), and it often ties at the boundary. The radix then continues:
  - pass 3 sees the 10 low score bits, which are all zero, plus the top id bit;
  - pass 4 sees id bits 30-20, which are constant because ids are below `max_model_len` (16 bits for a 64k context);
  - only passes 5-6 separate the tied candidates.
  - In the passes that separate nothing, every remaining candidate falls into one histogram bin, and the shared-memory atomics serialize on it.

**Fix.**
- `CompileKey` gains `score_bits` and `id_bits`.
- The key is `score_key >> (32 - score_bits)` followed by the low `id_bits` of `~token_id`, packed at the top of the 64-bit word. With BF16 logits and a 64k context, that is 32 bits and 3 passes.
- Padding keys stay 0 and still decode to -1.
- The order is unchanged:
  - the dropped score bits are zero for upcast BF16 values;
  - `~id & mask` preserves the order of ids below `2**id_bits`.
- `sparse_attn_indexer` (DSA) and the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer pass the following:
  - `score_bits=16` when the raw logits are BF16;
  - `id_bits` from `max_model_len`, or `max_pool_len` for kpool pool ids.
  - On a DCP rank whose prefill chunk is empty (no logits to inspect), `score_bits` follows the platform. That keeps it on the warmed-up key. 32 bits would also select correctly.
- Warm-up compiles the SM100 key: 16 score bits, and id bits for `max_model_len // index_kpool`.
- The last radix pass can now be narrower than the 512-thread block. For example, a 30-bit key gives passes of 11, 11 and 8 bits. The bin scan now covers whole block slices; bins at or above `num_bins` stay zero.

**Scope.**
- Only DCP > 1 with BF16 indexer logits (SM100) changes speed. FP32 logits keep 32 score bits.
- DCP = 1 does not run the merge.
- No new host syncs: `score_bits` comes from the logits dtype and the platform, and `id_bits` from `max_model_len`. All three are host-side metadata.
- No new CI step: the new test runs in the existing B200 "V1 Attention" step (`pytest v1/attention`), which has CuTeDSL.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` with "dcp topk", "top-k merge", "indexer dcp", "radix select bf16", "61149", "StableTopKFromGatheredCandidates", "dcp_indexer_cutedsl", "dcp top-k" and "sparse indexer bf16 logits" found no PR that changes the merge selector's key:
  - #47348 (CuTeDSL DCP top-k merge optimizations, before BF16 logits) and #50010 / #50366 (consumer-direct and owner-sharded top-k) restructure the exchange. They do not touch the key layout.
  - #63200, #62172 and #62240 make the local (non-DCP) top-k read BF16 logits. Under DCP, the upcast and this merge stay as they are.
  - #59367 bounds the merge's scratch memory and also edits `_merge_dcp_topk_global`. The changes are independent, and a rebase conflict would be trivial.
- No upstream issue covers it.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the regression, write the change and its test, and run the benchmarks and evals above. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the measurements.

title: [Perf][DSA] Read BF16 logits directly in persistent top-k
author: Pb314314
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Merged by WoosukKwon on 2026-10-30 as [`e31cf3dec7cf`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0), following approval of final PR head `5ff957619959`. The validation revisions and their scope are recorded below.

Let the existing persistent top-k backend read BF16 indexer logits and widen loaded scores to FP32 inside its kernels. On SM100 decode without DCP, this removes the full FP32 logits allocation whenever `auto` resolves to persistent, as well as for explicit persistent.

Query chunking is separate work. This PR complements [#62172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172), which implements BF16 input for cooperative top-k. This change implements persistent, filtered and sampled paths instead. Open-PR searches found no separate persistent-BF16 implementation. The caller uses the same `takes_bf16_logits()` capability-interface design as #62172; cooperative support remains with that PR.

## Claims

- Keep the existing backend selection and top-k algorithms. Scores loaded from BF16 widen to FP32 before binning/refinement; register score arrays remain FP32.
- Remove the dense FP32 logits copy for supported persistent decode calls, including default auto. Cooperative, DCP and prefill retain their existing behavior. No DeepSelect switch or query-row chunking is introduced.
- Preserve exact selected scores and valid top-k indices in the tested cases. Equal-score index identity/order and generated-token equivalence are not claimed.

## Validation

### Performance breakdown and memory traffic

**DeepGEMM's logits computation is unchanged.** This PR saves work **after** BF16 logits have been produced: it removes the separate BF16-to-FP32 materialization and lets persistent top-k read BF16 directly. It does not reduce Q/K projection work, the score computation, or the number of logits. The measurements below exclude DeepGEMM and are not end-to-end model speedups.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["DeepGEMM: unchanged score computation"] --> B["BF16 logits in GPU memory: unchanged"]
    B -->|Before PR| C["Separate conversion kernel: read BF16, write FP32"]
    C --> F["Full FP32 logits buffer"]
    F --> O["Load FP32 scores; existing FP32 top-k algorithm"]
    B -->|With PR: supported persistent calls| N["Load BF16 scores; widen in registers; same FP32 top-k algorithm"]
    O --> I["Top-k indices"]
    N --> I
```

| Where the saving occurs | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| External conversion | Allocate a full FP32 logits buffer; read 2 bytes and write 4 bytes per valid score | Remove this allocation and GPU conversion kernel |
| Top-k input loads | 4 bytes per FP32 score; an aligned four-score load reads 16 bytes | 2 bytes per BF16 score; an aligned four-score load reads 8 bytes and expands to four FP32 registers |
| Score arithmetic inside top-k | FP32 comparison/binning/refinement | The same FP32 algorithm, with on-load widening; register score arrays are still FP32 |

Code: [producer and conversion bypass](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L939-L954), [old allocation and conversion kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L297-L329), and [FP32/BF16 load helpers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L70-L100).

**Measured breakdown: pre-PR `98fc6da9d735` versus PR `293880733f87`, GB200.** The PR source is unchanged by the subsequent main merges. The BF16 top-k timing includes its loads, register widening, and selection; it is not the cast alone.

| Q / valid K / top-k | External conversion: before → after (µs) | Native top-k: FP32 → BF16 (µs) | Native top-k latency change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | 2.848 → removed | 4.832 → 5.632 | +16.56% |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | 19.296 → removed | 31.232 → 30.240 | -3.18% |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | 35.264 → removed | 44.800 → 42.352 | -5.46% |

The **33–44% full selection-stage improvement** in the long-row cases mainly comes from eliminating the external conversion; native top-k alone improves by only about 3–5%. The short-row native kernel is slower with BF16, while the measured complete caller still improves after removing the conversion. Smaller input loads can help, but widening adds register instructions. Halving score-input bytes does not establish that total HBM traffic or latency halves; cache behavior and multiple passes matter. No hardware-counter measurement proves a bandwidth-only explanation.

**Allocation size and accessed bytes are different quantities.** At Q=128 and valid K=100000, the removed conversion logically reads 25.6 MB of BF16 data and writes 51.2 MB of FP32 data (decimal MB). A single full scan by top-k reads 51.2 MB of FP32 score payload versus 25.6 MB of BF16 payload; this is byte accounting, not measured DRAM traffic. The full FP32 allocation is larger because it retains capacity W=262144 and padded stride=262656: about **128.248 MiB**. That temporary disappears; the original BF16 logits and existing workspace remain. CUDA graph replay does not remove conversion kernels automatically; this PR removes that node and its FP32 storage from supported captured paths.

These component timings are separate cold-cache ablations, **not additive**. The complete caller measurements below remain the primary before/after result.

<details>
<summary>Breakdown measurement method and why the columns are not additive</summary>

Baseline `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus measured PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`, using the same frozen runtimes and matching fixed BF16 inputs as the full-stage table below. GB200 job 41138: A/B/B/A fresh processes, 30 cold-L2 CUPTI graph samples per stage/run (60 per arm). Conversion uses the actual `as_fp32_logits`; top-k uses the native persistent entrypoint. Input capacity W=262144, padded stride=262656, host scheduling bound=1048576.

These are separately captured cold-cache ablations, not timestamps of nodes in one production graph. Conversion warms its FP32 output for the following kernel, while standalone top-k starts cold. The full caller also clears the output-index buffer; this native-only ablation omits that common operation. Summing the component columns therefore does not reconstruct the full-stage table. Jointly captured conversion+FP32 top-k medians are retained separately in the raw results (6.816, 46.5755 and 78.0805 µs); the full caller table remains the primary before/after comparison.

For intuition only, one full score scan would give 2-byte BF16 read + 4-byte FP32 write + 4-byte FP32 read before this PR, versus a 2-byte BF16 read after it. This 10→2 byte accounting excludes unchanged producer writes, metadata/workspace accesses, multiple selection passes and cache effects; it is not a measured traffic reduction or a 5x speedup prediction.

Every ablation passes exact selected-score, valid/unique-index and input-preservation checks. Raw samples, identities and commands are retained in `main_vs_packed_breakdown_v1` (`bench.py`, `run.sbatch`, `SUMMARY.json`, `results/41138_*`). These component measurements do not establish full-model accuracy or end-to-end performance.
