Pre-commit checks passed for the final helper delta. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation and this description.

## Details

The aligned BF16 vector-load helpers use the same packed integer load and bit-expansion implementation as #62172; scalar and guarded tail loads remain available. FP32 overloads are unchanged.

### BF16 and FP32 load behavior

The helpers separate the input storage type from the existing FP32 selection arithmetic:

| Helper | BF16 input | FP32 input |
|---|---|---|
| `to_float(x)` | Widen one BF16 value with `__bfloat162float(x)` | Identity: `return x;` |
| `load_score2(ptr)` | Read 4 bytes containing two BF16 values and expand them to two FP32 values (8 bytes of value storage) | The existing `float2` load (8 input bytes) |
| `load_score4(ptr)` | Read 8 bytes containing four BF16 values and expand them to four FP32 values (16 bytes of value storage) | The existing `float4` load (16 input bytes) |
| Guarded tail load | Read only valid BF16 elements, widen individually, and fill invalid elements with negative infinity | Retain the existing FP32 predicated-load implementation |

For the aligned four-score BF16 helper, [`topk_histogram_4096.cuh:78–82`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L78-L82) contains:

```cpp
const uint2 raw = *reinterpret_cast<const uint2*>(ptr);
return make_float4(
    __uint_as_float(raw.x << 16), __uint_as_float(raw.x & 0xFFFF0000u),
    __uint_as_float(raw.y << 16), __uint_as_float(raw.y & 0xFFFF0000u));
```

`uint2` contains two 32-bit words, so the input payload is 8 bytes. Each word holds two BF16 values. The shifts and masks place each BF16 bit pattern in the upper 16 bits of its own FP32 word; `__uint_as_float` reinterprets that word as a float. `make_float4` returns four 32-bit values: **8 input bytes become 16 bytes of FP32 values, not 32 bytes**. These values feed the kernel's existing FP32 register computation; the helper does not allocate or write a full FP32 logits tensor in global memory.

The [FP32 scalar overload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L70-L73) returns its input unchanged, and the [FP32 four-score overload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L75-L77) retains `*reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(ptr)`. FP32 inputs are never downcast to BF16.


Code references: [BF16-to-FP32 register conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L71-L92), [backend capability query](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py#L236-L255), and [conditional full-tensor conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L951-L954).

BF16 input is widened losslessly on load; this avoids materializing FP32 logits in global memory. All existing raw-score rereads, including exact overflow recovery, accept the input type and immediately widen it. The FP32 comparison keys, candidate/refinement logic and backend thresholds are preserved. Candidate-block selection retains FP32 compact scores for auto/persistent so this change does not alter that selection stage's arithmetic.

The capability query reports input support; it does not change `resolve_backend()` or choose a backend by measured speed. It inspects host shape/type metadata without reading GPU tensor values. Cooperative continues to receive FP32. BF16 native persistent requires at least 128 KiB opt-in shared memory and contiguous columns. Existing addressing limits remain unchanged; large-row measurements do not cross the pre-existing filtered uint32 row-offset limit.

### Integration with #62172

The two features can coexist and share `takes_bf16_logits()` plus the same BF16 load helpers. The local reconciled version was validated as described above. **Current online heads still require rebase/conflict resolution**; helper alignment alone does not make them a clean merge.

Whichever PR merges second should:

- Combine cooperative and persistent capability predicates and their test expectations, retaining the existing explicit DeepSelect support.
- Preserve main's exact-overflow correction from #62936 when rebasing the older cooperative branch.
- Retain guarded BF16 predicated loads needed by persistent, instead of importing the cooperative-only assertion that rejects that instantiation.
- Preserve small-Q auto's FP32/cooperative fallback where only the widened stride satisfies TMA alignment, and preserve FP32 compact candidate-block scores for explicit cooperative as well. These integration-policy guards were included in the local validated reconciliation.

No cooperative implementation is copied into this standalone persistent PR. Cooperative-first followed by this PR rebasing onto the shared interface is one straightforward merge order; either order requires the same reconciliation.

title: [Spec Decode] Disable batch-sharded draft logits for PCP

title: [Bench] Default to Zipf routing for forward benchmarks with dummy weights
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Add `vllm bench forward --routing zipf` for skewed synthetic target-model MoE routing, with fixed alpha=1.25. The default `auto` selects Zipf with dummy weights and real routing otherwise; sequence-parallel TP ranks select their corresponding fixture token rows.

## Claims

- Each token selects distinct experts with weighted sampling without replacement; a seeded permutation assigns popularity ranks to expert IDs per layer.
- Reuse the existing gate-logit and explicit expert-ID hooks. Generate fixtures outside timing and keep them fixed across graph replays.
- Sequence-parallel ranks use their corresponding fixture slice instead of repeating rank zero's token rows.

## Validation

On GB200, with dummy weights:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Zipf frequency, distinct IDs, deterministic row prefixes | Passed |
| Existing Qwen3-Next hybrid CLI verification/mixed cases, default `auto` and explicit `balanced` | 2 passed; `auto` reports Zipf, override reports balanced; finite, deterministic graph outputs |
| Native DeepSeek V4.1 TP4/EP4 MegaMoE Q6/prefill | Correct fixture slices on all four ranks for both modes; finite outputs; Q6 graph/eager exact |

The native check uses a four-layer dummy DeepSeek V4.1 config (hidden size 512,
384 experts/top-6), `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, and cases `verify=6@1024:5` and
`prefill=1024`. Against the unmodified main routing module, ranks 1–3 reuse
rank zero's rows for both cases; the branch reconstructs the global fixture
exactly. For the first balanced Q6 layer this changes 12 distinct experts to
the intended 34. A separate real-TP-group check confirms replicated Q2 keeps
offset zero.

Native prefill output is not bitwise deterministic on either main or this
branch (eager-repeat relative RMS: 1.38% main, 1.42% balanced, 1.41% Zipf).
Those values are recorded as an existing limitation, not hidden by a relaxed
test tolerance. The fixture-row checks are exact.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \
  -k 'zipf_expert_selection or bench_forward_hybrid_verify' -v
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/benchmarks/forward/routing.py vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py docs/benchmarking/cli.md \
  docs/cli/README.md .agents/skills/model-microbenchmark/SKILL.md
```

The existing Benchmarks CLI CI step selects both the sampler check and parameterized CLI test. Multi-GPU native MegaMoE validation is external to that single-GPU CI step. No serving code changes or model-quality claims: this option intentionally substitutes synthetic routing for benchmark inputs.

## Details

Exponential races implement weighted sampling without replacement with weights proportional to `rank**-1.25`. Chunked CPU generation bounds temporary memory. The expert-ID permutation avoids systematically assigning hot experts to the lowest EP ranks; load imbalance remains intentional. Seeding from global gate names keeps layer popularity stable across PP partitions.

The TP fix uses the native forward context's padded token count to recognize a local sequence shard. Replicated rows retain offset zero. Both synthetic modes share this correction. Grouped top-k remains unsupported; explicit Zipf also rejects prefill context parallelism, whose token mapping needs separate handling. When a synthetic fixture is unsupported, `auto` warns and falls back to real routing. Synthetic routing applies to the target, not the drafter.

Duplicate-work checks searched open PRs for `forward routing` and `zipf`. [#57100](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57100) is complementary: it changes only `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` and uses a Gaussian-logit bias; it does not add full-model forward routing. [#63872](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63872) addresses Muse gate discovery/bias handling, not this new distribution. This branch is based directly on OSS main and does not bundle local timing experiments.

AI assistance was used to implement, validate, and review this change.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma 4 vision crash with online FP8 quantization
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #63732. With `--quantization fp8`, an image request to Gemma 4 returns HTTP 500 and kills the engine core. The transformers patch embedder casts the pixel values to `input_proj.weight.dtype`. Once vLLM quantizes that layer, this dtype is `float8_e4m3fn`, so the FP8 linear gets an FP8 input. This PR runs the patch embedder steps in `gemma4_mm.py` with the pixel values cast to `self.model_dtype`. It makes the same change for the pooled states before `embedding_projection` in the encoder CUDA graph path.

Compared with #63911, this fix:

- Also fixes `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and `EmbeddingGemma2Model`. They borrow Gemma 4's `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` and build their own FP8-quantized tower. [#63911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63911) swaps the embedder only in `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.__init__`, so their image and video paths still crash with the reported error (checked with a probe that loads E4B with FP8 and builds each model's own tower, since no checkpoint of either model was at hand).
- Adds tests that fail on the old code for video and for the encoder CUDA graph path, including the `embedding_projection` cast. The compiled and encoder-graph cases in [#63911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63911) pass on the old code, so they guard neither path.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 image requests with online FP8 no longer crash the engine. `input_proj` stays FP8 and still uses the same FP8 kernel.
- The same fix covers video inputs. On the old code, `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` with video enabled crashed at engine start, because the encoder profile run sends dummy video through the same patch embedder.
- The same fix covers the encoder CUDA graph path (the patch embedder call and the `embedding_projection` cast).
- Online `fp8_per_block`, `fp8_per_channel` and `mxfp8` (eager, custom ops off) crashed at engine start on the old code. With this fix, all three answer `The sign in the image is a **STOP** sign.`
- `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and `EmbeddingGemma2Model` get the same fix through the borrowed methods.

## Validation

Hardware and software: 1 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 16 GB (SM 12.0), vLLM `00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b` (`0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56`) with and without this patch, transformers 5.20.2.

Reproducer. Server:

```bash
vllm serve --port 18000 --model google/gemma-4-E4B-it --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enforce-eager --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0}'
```

Once it logs `Application startup complete`, send a 64x64 white PNG:

```bash
BODY='{"model":"google/gemma-4-E4B-it","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAEAAAABACAIAAAAlC+aJAAAAS0lEQVR42u3PMQ0AAAwDoPo33UrYvQQckD4XAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAYHLAMpT0sIcNbcEAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"}},{"type":"text","text":"What color is this image?"}]}],"max_tokens":16}'
OUT=$(curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}' localhost:18000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$BODY")
echo "$OUT"
echo "IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=$(echo "$OUT" | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}')"
```

Before (3 of 3 runs, each on a fresh server): `IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=500`. The server log shows:

```
RuntimeError: ... "dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant_kernel_scalar_type" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
```

After (6 of 6 runs, each on a fresh server: 3 by me and 3 in a separate re-check): `IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=200`, answer `"The image is **white**."`. No `not implemented`, `Traceback` or `EngineDeadError` line in any log. The server still selects `CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod`. The old code gives the same answer only when `input_proj` is left out of FP8 with `--quantization-config '{"ignore":["vision_tower.patch_embedder.input_proj"]}'`.

New tests, on the old `gemma4_mm.py` and on this patch:

 | Test | Old code | This PR |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | `pytest -v -s tests/models/quantization/test_fp8.py -k gemma4` (image, video) | 2 failed, reported `RuntimeError` | 2 passed |
 | `pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k gemma4_fp8` (image, video) | 2 failed, reported `RuntimeError` | 2 passed |

On the old code, the CUDA graph row fails earlier, in the eager video profile run. So I also checked each CUDA graph change on its own: with only the `encoder_cudagraph_forward` patch-embedder call reverted, or only the old `embedding_projection.weight.dtype` cast restored, the row fails with the same error.

Borrowing models: a script builds a vision tower with random weights from the E4B config (unquantized) and calls `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` on all three classes. Image and video outputs for all three match the old code exactly (same shapes and sums).

`pre-commit run` on the four changed files passes.

## Details

Root cause: vLLM builds the Gemma 4 vision tower with `AutoModel.from_config`. It then replaces each `nn.Linear` with a `ReplicatedLinear` that carries the tower quant config. With online FP8, `input_proj.weight` becomes `float8_e4m3fn` after loading. The transformers `Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder.forward` does:

```python
pixel_values = 2 * (pixel_values - 0.5)
if (target_dtype := self.input_proj.weight.dtype).is_floating_point:
    pixel_values = pixel_values.to(target_dtype)
hidden_states = self.input_proj(pixel_values)
```

This is right for a plain `nn.Linear`. For a quantized layer, though, the weight dtype is the storage dtype. FP8 is a floating type, so the guard lets the cast through. The bf16 pixel values are rounded to FP8 without a scale, and the FP8 linear's activation quant gets an FP8 input. `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` only accepts fp16, bf16 or fp32. A debug run confirmed the chain: the pixel values enter the patch embedder as bf16, and only `vision_tower.patch_embedder.input_proj` receives an FP8 input. `encoder_cudagraph_forward` had the same mistake in vLLM code: it cast the pooled states to `embedding_projection.weight.dtype`, which is also FP8 under the tower quant config.

The CUDA kernel runs when the `quant_fp8` custom op is on: with `--enforce-eager`, with `+quant_fp8`, and by vLLM's default for block-scaled FP8 checkpoints and ROCm AITER FP8 linear. With the op off, eager `forward_native` also fails (`"abs_cuda" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'`). Only the default compile mode passes without an error, and there the pixel values are still rounded to FP8 without a scale.

Fix: a module-level `_embed_patches(patch_embedder, pixel_values, pixel_position_ids, padding_positions, dtype)` repeats the steps of the transformers forward (`2 * (x - 0.5)`, `input_proj`, `_position_embeddings`, sum), but casts to the given dtype. The image, video and encoder CUDA graph paths call it with `self.model_dtype`. The CUDA graph path also casts the pooled states to `self.model_dtype`, as the eager paths already do before `embed_vision`. The quant config is not touched, so the layers stay FP8. For an unquantized layer nothing changes, because then the weight dtype is the model dtype. The helper is a module-level function, not a method, because the two borrowing models copy `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` without inheriting from Gemma 4. A method would be missing on those classes.

Alternatives not taken:

- Building `input_proj` without quantization: this changes which layers the user's quantization covers. It can also break loading of pre-quantized checkpoints that quantize this layer, and it leaves the `embedding_projection` cast as it is.
- Making the FP8 linear accept an FP8 input: this treats the crash site, and by then the input has already been rounded to FP8.

Tradeoffs and limitations:

- `_embed_patches` uses the private `_position_embeddings` of the transformers embedder. This file already splits `Gemma4VisionModel.forward` into its parts, so this goes one level deeper in the same style.
- With online FP8 in the default compile mode, which did not crash before, image outputs may change a little because the pixel values are no longer rounded to FP8 first. On `input_proj` against the bf16 weight, the relative error went from 4.50% to 3.68%. I did not run a vision eval.
- The tests use `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, which CI already uses. E2B has the same vision tower and would be cheaper, but I could not confirm the answer checks (`stop`, `book`) on E2B.
- CI: `gemma4_mm.py` is added to `source_file_dependencies` of `quantized-models-test` and its AMD mirror, so the eager test runs when this file changes. This adds an estimated 14% more runs of that step. The `gemma4_fp8` row (`core_model`) runs in the existing multimodal step.
- Not run on AMD.
- Out of scope: online `mxfp4` on SM 12.x fails at engine start in `input_proj` with `ValueError: SM12x cute-dsl requires NVFP4 with 128x4 scales`, the same before and after this patch, with a bf16 input.

title: [Feature][Quantization] Support AWQ/GPTQ Marlin cache restarts
author: liusy58
body:
## Overview

Allow the weight-cache daemon to reuse AWQ/GPTQ linear weights already packed for Marlin across engine restarts. Related to #56049; updated against main `8cf1277362aef963a71cf6860c28387acf6ecb90`.

## Claims

- Support AWQ INT4 and symmetric GPTQ INT4/INT8 linear weights with the actual Marlin kernel and FP16/BF16 activations.
- Preserve shared repacked weights, scales, zero points and padded bias without repeating checkpoint conversion or Marlin transformations.
- Continue rejecting other kernels, INT8/FP8 activation overrides and AWQ/GPTQ MoE.

## Validation

November 3 integration update: preserve the GPTQ batch-invariant ordinary-loading path from #60479 and restore the symmetric Marlin runtime zero-point name after #62407. The latter now keeps checkpoint `qzeros` registered and reads a separate empty `w_zp`; an IPC attachment must restore that kernel metadata and mark checkpoint `qzeros` retired. No tensor data is transformed on attachment. The existing tests reproduced 5 failures (GPTQ real-model IPC and four layer cases) before this correction, with 6 passing. Final results: **11 passed, 68 deselected in 244.14s** on B300 (same two pinned real models, ordinary/fallback/IPC/restart with `fallback=False`, plus nine layer/boundary cases). A real CPU/Gloo GPTQ construction check also preserves checkpoint tensors in batch-invariant mode and rejects Marlin IPC without initializing CUDA. Changed-file hooks pass, including mypy and CI tethering. Existing torch/fork deprecation warnings remain; no L4 Buildkite run is claimed.


B300, TP1. The two real-model cases use FP16, eager execution, TRITON_ATTN, explicitly selected Marlin, two prompts × 16 generated tokens, and prompt/sample top-5 logprobs. Each compares ordinary loading → missing-daemon disk fallback → IPC → second IPC; both IPC starts set `fallback=False`. Comparison uses the existing `check_logprobs_close` helper. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` is intentional: AWQ and GPTQ use unpacked implementations when enabled, and Marlin does not guarantee batch invariance.

| Check | Before implementation | After implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Pinned Qwen2.5-0.5B AWQ and GPTQ-INT4 checkpoints | 2 failed, 118.22s; ordinary/fallback generation works, both daemons reject their quant method | 2 passed, 144.56s, all four loading paths |
| Real fused INT4 layers, aligned/padded outputs and bias | 4 failed, 32.41s: pre-processed weights rejected | All pass, with exact output/shape/shared-pointer/tensor-content checks across two attachments |
| Final layer/boundary suite, including GPTQ INT8/channelwise BF16 and actual Triton/A8 rejection | — | 9 passed, 12.92s |
| Existing AWQ/GPTQ config and weight-cache regressions | — | 76 passed, 18 deselected, 63.38s |
| Changed-file hooks | — | Passed, including mypy, ruff and CI test tethering |

Checkpoints: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-AWQ` at `db09cd27ead7fee40cdee309693cf83601b9c899`; `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4` at `c34a4a91629f09f73a285f32dbd26106b033c654`. INT8/BF16 and padded outputs are covered by real CUDA layers, not a complete INT8 checkpoint. This is cache-versus-ordinary output equivalence, not quantization accuracy against BF16 or a performance benchmark. Multi-GPU, other hardware and other kernels are not claimed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and baseline evidence</summary>

```bash
# Run each on an idle GPU; HF_HUB_OFFLINE assumes the pinned models are cached.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k marlin_preprocessed -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k ipc_cache_marlin -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_auto_awq.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k 'not quantization_method and not cold_start and not d2d_warmup and not marlin' -q
```

Apply the new tests to main `6376fda7a9` without the two production changes to reproduce the failures. Before implementation, the real daemons report:

```text
UnsupportedQuantForIPCError: layer model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj:
AutoAWQMarlinLinearMethod does not support loading from pre-processed weights.
UnsupportedQuantForIPCError: layer model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj:
AutoGPTQLinearMethod does not support loading from pre-processed weights.
2 failed, 74 deselected, 16 warnings in 118.22s
```

Host-specific environment: its precompiled Marlin path first failed with unsupported PTX during ordinary loading. Baseline and passing results above both use process-local `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/liusy/codex-runtime/cuda-compat-13-4/usr/local/cuda-13.4/compat`, containing NVIDIA's checksum-verified `cuda-compat-13-4` package `615.71.10-1ubuntu1`, as supported by [NVIDIA's compatibility matrix](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/cuda-compatibility/latest/forward-compatibility.html). It was extracted under the user's task directory; the host driver and shared Python environment were not modified. Initial environment failures and corrected negative-test setup errors are retained separately and are not represented as cache bug reproductions. Runs emit existing torch/fork deprecation warnings.

</details>

## Details

Both methods previously rejected daemon caching even though ordinary Marlin loading worked. Their kernel configuration is constructed before post-load processing. Normal post-load work converts AWQ packing and/or repacks weights, permutes scales/zero points, pads/permutates bias and selects the symmetric GPTQ runtime zero-point name. IPC already supplies transformed tensors; the GPTQ attachment restores the runtime name and retirement metadata. Opt in only the actual `MarlinLinearKernel` with FP16/BF16 activations, and return before those transformations on the pre-processed path. No common loading interface, kernel implementation, scheduler/model-runner change or steady-state synchronization is added.

Reuse the existing daemon, generation and comparison helpers. The L4 Marlin Preload CI step selects the real-model and layer/boundary cases and tracks their source dependencies. Local validation is B300; L4 Buildkite execution is not claimed. The preload guide documents commands, defaults and exclusions, with links from the AWQ/GPTQ guides.

Duplicate checks covered current #56049/comments, issue-linked drafts and open Marlin-preload/AWQ/GPTQ-cache searches. #61908 introduces a different on-disk AWQ-v2 format, while #60479 changes GPTQ batch-invariant execution; neither restores daemon IPC weights. Existing FP8/FP4 cache drafts do not cover this path.

AI assistance: Codex implemented and ran the recorded validation at the submitter's request. This draft is for human review; no completed human approval or human-run tests are asserted.

title: [Perf][Model Loader] Make the EP weight filter EPLB-aware
author: mrn3088
body:
## Overview

Let `--enable-ep-weight-filter` work with `--enable-eplb`. Since #37322 the loader turns the filter off whenever EPLB is enabled, so every rank of an EPLB deployment reads every expert weight. This derives the experts each rank needs from EPLB's initial placement instead. Follow-up to #37136, #37351 and #37322.

## Claims

- With EPLB, each rank reads only the experts its physical slots hold in the initial placement, including redundant replicas. DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 with DEP8 and 32 redundant experts: **105.2 GiB per rank instead of 384.9 GiB** (the plain EP filter without EPLB reads 100.1 GiB).
- Outputs match EPLB without the filter within run-to-run noise, across 32-33 rebalancing steps: GSM8K 0.9636 vs 0.9621 (A/A 0.9629), and the same final answer on 97.4% of questions, equal to the A/A agreement. Weight loading on a warm page cache: 43.6 s to 39.8 s (A/A 43.9 s).
- The comparison is sensitive: a negative control that applies the plain EP filter under EPLB (main without #37322's guard) falls far outside the run-to-run noise.
- Falls back to loading every expert, as on main, for elastic EP and whenever the model's MoE layout (`num_logical_experts`, `num_physical_experts`) differs from the config, e.g. for MoE models that don't implement `MixtureOfExperts`.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (macOS CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py
# 44 passed (7 new)
```

The new unit tests check the expert set against `determine_expert_map` plus the initial map on every rank, coverage of all logical experts, an iterator-level regression for redundant slots, and the model-side round-robin to linear fallback under EPLB that the filter relies on.

**End-to-end test** (new, `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter_eplb.py`, 2 GPUs): `luccafong/deepseek_mtp_main_random`, already used in CI, with TP2 + EP + synchronous EPLB and 2 redundant experts, so rank 1's redundant slots replicate experts from rank 0's EP shard. Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (set by the test), the filter-off and filter-on runs must produce identical tokens while EPLB rebalances mid-generation, and the filter must log that it engaged. It runs in a new nightly 2xB200 step and is skipped on ROCm, where MLA lacks batch invariance.

Run on 2xB300 in the same nightly image as the A/B below, first as is (main) and then with this PR's two loader files mounted:

```bash
python -m pytest -v -s tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter_eplb.py
```

main, where the filter never engages under EPLB:

```
E           AssertionError: expected the filter on
FAILED tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter_eplb.py::test_ep_weight_filter_matches_unfiltered_with_eplb
```

this PR (EPLB rearranged experts 12 times across the two runs):

```
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=3272835) INFO 10-28 02:16:45 [default_loader.py:511] EP weight filter: ep_size=2, ep_rank=0, loading 37/72 experts
PASSED
========================= 1 passed in 89.80s (0:01:29) =========================
```

**End-to-end A/B** (one 8xB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9` with this PR's two loader files mounted over the image's copies, as of 2cbb82aee4; later commits change only comments, docs and tests; the A/A arm reruns the unmodified image to measure noise):

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"window_size":100,"step_interval":200,"num_redundant_experts":32,"use_async":false,"communicator":"torch_nccl"}' \
  --enable-ep-weight-filter --max-num-seqs 64
```

The small EPLB window and interval make rebalancing happen during the evaluation.

| | main (filter skipped) | this PR | main again (A/A) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EP weight filter` log | none | `loading 36/256 experts` | none |
| `Rearranged experts` events | 33 | 32 | 33 |
| GPU KV cache tokens | 4,779,264 | 4,779,264 | 4,779,264 |
| GSM8K accuracy (1319 questions, max_tokens 2048) | 0.9621 | 0.9636 | 0.9629 |
| GSM8K same final answer as main | — | 97.4% | 97.4% |
| greedy smoke identical to main (4 prompts) | — | 1/4 | 2/4 |
| prompt-logprob top-1 agreement with main (640 / 20k / 118k tokens) | — | 95.8% / 94.6% / 77.9% | 95.9% / 94.7% / 77.8% |
| `Loading weights took` (rank 0) | 43.62 s | 39.81 s | 43.88 s |
| `Model loading took` (8 ranks) | 57.4-58.1 s | 54.2-54.8 s | 56.5-56.8 s |

This configuration is not bitwise deterministic even between two runs of the same image, so the PR column is compared with the A/A column rather than expecting identical outputs.

**Negative control** (separate job on the same kind of node, smoke only): mounting the nightly loader with only #37322's EPLB guard removed, i.e. the plain EP partition under EPLB (`loading 32/256 experts`), leaves 144 of the 288 physical slots without their weights. Compared with main in the same job, greedy outputs are identical for 0/4 prompts and prompt-logprob top-1 agreement drops to 75.3% / 80.4% / 31.5%, far outside the A/A noise above (95.9% / 94.7% / 77.8%). Its short greedy answers can still be correct, so the logprob comparison, not answer accuracy alone, is what separates a wrong expert set from run-to-run noise.

Load times were measured with the checkpoint already in the page cache (NFS, where vLLM also auto-prefetches), the same condition as #37136's numbers; the saving comes from not materializing non-local expert tensors. The 8 ranks of one node share the page cache and together need every expert, so reads from storage don't shrink on a single node; the per-rank saving matters more where ranks read independently, e.g. EP across nodes or a page cache that cannot hold the checkpoint.

pre-commit passes.

## Details

- **Root cause.** EPLB allocates N + R physical slots per MoE layer and splits them linearly across EP ranks. Slot p initially holds logical expert `initial_map[p]` from `EplbState.build_initial_global_physical_to_logical_map` (identity, then `i % N` for the redundant slots), so a rank's redundant slots replicate experts from other ranks' default partitions. The plain filter skips those, which left the replicas uninitialized; #37322 therefore disabled the filter under EPLB.
- **Fix.** The filter keeps `{initial_map[p] for p in this rank's physical slots}`, built from the same map `RoutedExperts.build_expert_params_mapping` uses to route checkpoint tensors to slots, so the two cannot disagree. Rebalancing moves weights GPU-to-GPU and never re-reads the checkpoint, so loading only has to satisfy the initial placement. Custom initial maps (#49572, open) are applied after loading through `rearrange_expert_weights_inplace`, so they stay compatible.
- **Linear placement.** `determine_expert_placement_strategy` refuses round-robin when EPLB is enabled, so the filter always splits physical slots linearly; a test pins this.
- **Layout check.** The expert set comes from the config, so it is used only when the model reports the matching `MixtureOfExperts` layout (resolved with `get_mixture_of_experts_model`, which unwraps VLMs). This matters because `--enable-eplb` is accepted for MoE models that don't implement `MixtureOfExperts`: EPLB is simply not registered for them, and they allocate only N slots, so the EPLB set would skip experts they need.
- **Loaders.** Every loader that consumes `local_expert_ids` uses the new set under EPLB: the safetensors iterator (all load strategies; auto-prefetch on NFS still reads whole files, but tensors are skipped per name) and InstantTensor (#61167), which was not validated end to end. The multi-threaded and fastsafetensors loaders don't filter at all (#48891 addresses the former).
- **Test coverage.** The fallback for a mismatched layout has no automated test: exercising it needs a MoE model whose layout disagrees with its config, and the guard is a single comparison.
- **Unchanged.** Elastic EP keeps loading every expert (padded capacity, placement evolves at runtime). Scale and metadata tensors are still never filtered, so #37322's NVFP4 fix is untouched.
- **Not a duplicate.** Open PRs and issues searched for "EP weight filter EPLB", "ep_weight_filter", "enable-ep-weight-filter", "37322 in:body" and "weight filter redundant experts" found nothing equivalent. Related but orthogonal: #48891 (apply the filter in the multithreaded safetensors loader) and #63075 (EPLB expert-weight regions in `RoutedExperts`).
- **Limitations.** Not validated with speculative decoding; DeepSeek MTP's MoE follows the same EPLB layout and passes the check, but the run above has no drafter.

AI assistance (Kimi Code and Claude Code) was used to write this change and run the validation above. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Renew prefill KV leases from the decoder
author: CJJ1008
body:
## Overview Today the Mooncake prefiller holds a finished request's KV until the decoder pulls it, or until `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (480 s) runs out. This PR adds an opt-in `kv_lease_duration` that replaces that fixed timeout with a lease the decoder renews, following NixlConnector's lease (#41383, [design](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md)). It addresses the "480s expire fallback" in item 6 of RFC #60523. ## Claims - **D crash:** P frees the dead decoder's KV within one lease of D's last renewal, instead of after 480 s. - **D overload:** requests queued on a busy decoder keep their KV for as long as they wait. A short fixed timeout fails them. - **Late pulls:** a pull for KV that P has already freed fails at once, instead of waiting out the timeout. This also applies when the lease is off. - Without `kv_lease_duration`, behavior is unchanged. ## Validation **Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py` → 144 passed (A800, `huggingface_hub==1.31.0` as in CI). The new tests use the real scheduler, real ZMQ sockets and a stubbed bootstrap service. They cover: - renewal is off without the option, and throttled to every `lease / 6` with it; - D renews until the pull settles or the request aborts; - renewals reach every paired P worker, querying the bootstrap first if needed; - on P, renewals extend only known transfers and never shorten a deadline, and a P without the lease rejects them; - pulls on the same channel still work; - a pull for freed KV gets an immediate error. `pre-commit` passes. **End to end:** 2× A800 with 200G HDR IB, Mooncake TE 0.3.13.post1, DeepSeek-MoE-16B, TP=1 per side. Both sides run main `10e8e921b`, with only `mooncake_connector.py` swapped (baseline vs this PR). - Load: 128 requests, 3,000-token prompts, 1,000 output tokens. That is 2.4× D's KV capacity, so D always has a queue. - Probe: a 512-token request sent straight to P every 10 s. | Case | Unmodified main | This PR | |---|---|---| | **A.** D killed at t≈23 s; 480 s timeout vs 30 s lease | P's KV stays at 99% until t≈484 s; the probe sent at t≈10 s takes 475.5 s | P's KV is below 5% at t≈103 s; that probe takes 61.3 s, later probes 36–46 ms | | **B.** No crash, requests wait on D up to ~80 s; 20 s timeout vs 20 s lease | 79 / 128 requests fail | 128 / 128 succeed, no lease expires | In case A, requests still queued on P when D died are prefilled afterwards. The baseline holds them for another 480 s, and P is still at 37% KV when the run ends at t=660 s. The lease holds each for one 30 s lease.
Reproduction ```bash # Same on D with "kv_role":"kv_consumer" and --port 8020. Drop kv_lease_duration for the baseline; # case B's baseline sets VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=20 on both sides. vllm serve deepseek-ai/deepseek-moe-16b-chat --port 8010 --dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code \ --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"device_name":"mlx5_102","kv_lease_duration":30}}' python examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \ --port 8000 --prefill http://

:8010 8998 --decode http://:8020 ``` - Load: 128 streaming completions sent at once through the proxy, each with random prompt token ids, `max_tokens=1000` and `ignore_eos`. - Probe: a plain completion with `max_tokens=1`, sent to P without `kv_transfer_params`. - Case A sends `SIGKILL` to D's process group 20 s after the load starts.

**Overhead:** - P checks each side-channel message for a renewal: 0.7 µs for a steady pull, 1.3 µs for a pull carrying the layout, 21 µs for an 18 KB pull of 32 requests. - D sends one message of about 1 KB per 128 transfer ids, to each paired P worker every `lease / 6`. ## Details **Flow** 1. D starts tracking a request in `on_new_request`, while it may still be queued. 2. Every `lease / 6`, `build_connector_meta` groups the tracked transfer ids by P engine. 3. `start_load_kv` sends them to each P worker that D would pull from. 4. P sets `expire_time = now + lease` when prefill ends. On each renewal it sets `expire_time = max(expire_time, now + 2/3 · lease)`. 5. D stops renewing on `finished_recving` or `request_finished`. 6. When renewals stop, P frees the blocks on its next scan and remembers the transfer id, so a later pull fails at once. **Design notes** - **Opt-in, unlike NIXL.** Mooncake has no handshake compatibility check, so an old decoder paired with a lease-enabled prefiller would silently lose the KV of requests queued longer than the lease. The docs say to set the same value on both sides and to upgrade prefillers first. An old prefiller rejects renewals, and D warns once. - **Transport.** Renewals use P's existing ZMQ ROUTER, so there is no new port and the pull format is unchanged. - A pull decodes as an empty renewal, because msgspec skips unknown fields. - P's listener answers renewals itself, since all sender workers may be blocked waiting for prefills. - D waits for the reply, because a `linger=0` socket drops unsent messages. - Renewals go to the same P workers as the pull, using the address selection now shared with `receive_kv`. A P engine that D has not contacted yet gets a bootstrap query first. - **Expiry scan.** P keeps scanning every entry, because renewals reorder deadlines; NIXL's ordered reaper hit this in #58222. Deadlines never cross processes, so there is no clock skew (cf. #50326). - **Limitation.** Backpressure is unchanged: P holds KV for as long as a slow decoder needs it. In case B with the lease, P sits at 99% for about 40 s and a probe waits 35 s. The 20 s timeout frees KV sooner (probe 17 s) only by failing requests. Fixing that needs D-side staging (rd2h / host receive). - **#57530 failure spine.** With the lease on, P's deadline is the lease. `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` still bounds the wait for an unfinished prefill and how long freed transfer ids are remembered. **Not a duplicate.** I searched for Mooncake lease, heartbeat, `ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` and `expire_time`. #63420 and #59522 are leases in the Mooncake Store connector. #63804 is an external connector, and #57529 is a standalone failure ledger. Open PRs on this file (#62657, #62658, #62255, #61974) do not change P's expiry. **AI assistance:** written with Claude Code. I reviewed every changed line, ran all tests and experiments above, and can answer for the design. ---

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Restore --input-len/--output-len/--prefix-len in vllm bench throughput
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

`vllm bench throughput` silently ignores `--input-len`, `--output-len` and `--prefix-len` on the random dataset and benchmarks 1024 / 128 / 0 instead, while warning that the matching `--random-*` flag was also given. Regression from #29105.

## Claims

- `--input-len/--output-len/--prefix-len` take effect again; an explicit `--random-*` flag still wins, and with neither the defaults stay 1024 / 128 / 0.
- The "Both --X and --random-X are specified" warnings only fire when both are actually passed, and "--prefix-len will be ignored" only when `--prefix-len` is passed.
- The help of all six flags, and so the CLI reference, states the precedence and the effective defaults.

## Validation

```bash
vllm bench throughput --model RedHatAI/gemma-3-1b-it-FP8-dynamic --input-len 2048 --output-len 512 --prefix-len 64 --num-prompts 8
```

| | sampled lengths (log) | prompt / output tokens | warnings |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | input 1023, output 128 (the 1024 / 128 / 0 defaults) | 8192 / 1024 | 3 ("Both --input-len and --random-input-len are specified", same for output and prefix) |
| this PR | input 2047, output 512 | 16896 (8 × (2048 + 64)) / 4096 | none |

(The log reports the input length after the special token; the 64-token prefix shows in the prompt-token total.)

Every flag combination, from the real parser through `validate_args` and `get_requests` (gpt2 tokenizer, random dataset; prompt length includes the prefix):

| flags | main: prompt / output, warnings | this PR: prompt / output, warnings |
|---|---|---|
| none | 1024 / 128, "Both --prefix-len and --random-prefix-len" | 1024 / 128, none |
| `--input-len 256 --output-len 64 --prefix-len 32` | **1024 / 128**, 3 × "Both ..." | **288 / 64**, none |
| `--random-input-len 200 --random-output-len 16 --random-prefix-len 8` | 208 / 16, "Both --prefix-len ..." | 208 / 16, none |
| `--random-prefix-len 0` | 1024 / 128, "Both --prefix-len ..." | 1024 / 128, none |
| `--input-len 256 --random-input-len 100` | 100 / 128, "Both --input-len ...", "Both --prefix-len ..." | 100 / 128, "Both --input-len ..." |
| `--dataset-name hf` (no length flags) | "--prefix-len will be ignored" | no `--prefix-len` warning |

New tests build args with the real parser (the existing `test_to_serve_args_keeps_legacy_flag_fallback` uses a bare `Namespace` without the `--random-*` attributes, which is why it passes on main):

```bash
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py -k "precedence or not_warn"
# main (these tests, main's throughput.py): 5 failed, 2 passed
#   assert (1024, 128, 0) == (2048, 512, 64)
#   assert not ['Both --input-len and --random-input-len are specified. ...', ...]
#   assert not ['Both --prefix-len and --random-prefix-len are specified. ...']   (x3)
# this PR: 7 passed

pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py -k "not test_bench_throughput"
# this PR: 16 passed
```

## Details

- **Root cause.** #29105 moved the random dataset onto the shared `add_random_dataset_base_args`, whose `--random-*` lengths default to 1024 / 128 / 0. `_to_serve_args` (`getattr(args, "random_input_len", input_len)`) and `validate_args` treat `None` as "not passed", but the parser never leaves them `None`, so the legacy value is never used and the conflict warnings always fire.
- **Fix.** The throughput parser leaves the three `--random-*` lengths unset (default `None`), and `_to_serve_args` resolves explicit `--random-*` > legacy flag > `RandomDataset.DEFAULT_*`, from one `_RANDOM_LEN_FALLBACKS` table that also writes the help text. `bench mm-processor` passes its own parsed `--random-*` values (never `None`) and is unaffected.
- **No duplicate.** No open issue or PR reports or fixes this; searched open PRs and issues for `bench throughput` with `--input-len` / `--random-input-len`.
- **`--prefix-len` default.** It defaulted to 0, so it always looked passed: `--random-prefix-len` alone warned, and every non-random dataset warned that `--prefix-len` would be ignored. It now defaults to `None` like `--input-len` / `--output-len`.
- **Docs.** With the `--random-*` lengths unset in the parser, the CLI reference would no longer show their defaults, so all six flags' help now states: explicit `--random-*` > legacy flag > `RandomDataset` default (1024 / 128 / 0).
- **Impact in tree.** The documented example in `docs/cli/README.md` (`--input-len 32 --output-len 1`) has been running 1024 / 128 since #29105, and `benchmarks/benchmark_pin_memory.py` works around the bug by setting the `--random-*` lengths to `None` by hand.
- **Removed check.** `validate_args` required `--input-len` or `--random-input-len` for a random dataset; since #29105 it could not fire, and keeping it would now break runs that pass neither. Those keep today's 1024 / 128 / 0.

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Select push mode for NixlConnector via transfer_mode
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview

Let `NixlConnector` run the push connector through `kv_connector_extra_config={"transfer_mode": "push"}`, for serving frameworks that only accept the `NixlConnector` name (e.g. Dynamo's P/D connector registry).

## Claims

- `{"kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"transfer_mode": "push"}}` resolves to `NixlPushConnector`.
- Default (`transfer_mode` unset or `"pull"`) is unchanged: `NixlPullConnector`.
- Other values raise `ValueError` at config resolution instead of silently falling back to pull.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hma_auto_config.py -q
# 25 passed
```

The new test covers unset → pull, `"push"` → push, and an invalid value → `ValueError`. No E2E run on this branch: the resolved class is the existing `NixlPushConnector`, unchanged. Our DeepSeek-V4.1 P/D deployment on Dynamo already runs exactly this (push connector under the `NixlConnector` name), currently through a `kv_connector_module_path` alias module that this PR replaces.

## Details

- Resolution happens in `KVConnectorFactory.get_connector_class`, which every class-level hook goes through (HMA support, sleep mode, piecewise CUDA graph, KV cache layout, metrics, MultiConnector children). So these hooks see the push class, and `kv_connector` stays `"NixlConnector"` for the existing `has_connector("NixlConnector")` checks.
- `transfer_mode` matches the existing `_TRANSFER_MODE` values (`"pull"` / `"push"`) of the NIXL workers, which already feed the handshake compatibility hash.
- No duplicate: no open PR adds a mode switch to `NixlConnector` (searched `NixlPushConnector`, `transfer_mode`).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

title: [Bugfix][Compile] Fix KV-cache corruption under whole-graph compile (revert #42129)
author: ericschreiber
body:
## Overview

Implements solution 2 as outlined in issue #62865.
In more detail: fixes #62865 by reverting #42129 and, under torch < 2.13, keeps its intended hang protection by not formatting the slow log message for vLLM ops.
Currently using compile mode 1/2, or mode 3 with `splitting_ops: []` on Transformers-backend models corrupts the KV cache because Inductor passes tensors in a different layout than the kernels assume. As discussed with maintainers and @okorzh-amd (author of #42129) in Slack, this is the revert-based alternative to #62924.

## Claims

- Fixes degenerate output for Transformers-backend models (e.g. Qwen3, Kolibri-1, likely others) under compile mode 1/2, or mode 3 with `splitting_ops: []`.
- It does so by restoring PyTorch's default handling for all `vllm::` and `vllm_aiter::` custom ops.
- Keeps the compile-hang protection from #42129 through: (1) from torch 2.13 the slow log message is only built with INFO logging; (2) below 2.13 (currently only the gfx1250 preview image) the message is never built for `vllm::` and `vllm_aiter::` ops, the same ops #42129 covered.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, torch 2.13.0+cu130, precompiled kernels. All runs with vLLM and Inductor compile caches disabled.

### Correctness
**1. Regression test** 
Added a new test `test_whole_graph_compile` which uses Qwen3-0.6B on the Transformers backend on compile mode 2 vs eager with `check_logprobs_close`:

```bash
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_whole_graph_compile -v
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | failed: `Matched tokens: []`, ref `'LLM is a large language model, ...'`, test `'>>1\n\n\n\n...'` |
| this PR | passed 2 runs|

**2. GSM8K** 
With this PR, mode 2 matches eager and the native implementation on GSM8K (Qwen3-0.6B, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`); while on main there is a clear regression.

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|
| Transformers backend, eager | 0.391 | 0.3% |
| Transformers backend, mode 2, `main` | 0.011 | 10.8% |
| Transformers backend, mode 2, this PR | 0.401 | 0.2% |
| native vLLM implementation, default mode 3 | 0.400 | 0.2% |

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl transformers --max-model-len 4096 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 2, "backend": "inductor", "cudagraph_mode": 2}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

**3. Bounded log message for vLLM ops under torch < 2.13**
Introduced a test `tests/compile/test_inductor_operator_str_patch.py` which checks that a `vllm::` op's message is only its name. Running on torch 2.12 (CPU, a small compiled graph with a `vllm::` op and a custom op from another namespace), unpatched torch builds the full message for both ops; with the patch it is never built for the `vllm::` op. 
I could not test on gfx1250 itself.

### Compile time
On CUDA, cold-cache compile time is unchanged within noise (`main` vs this PR): Kolibri-1 mode 3 28.3 vs 28.1 s, Kolibri-1 TP=2 61.1 vs 62.1 s, Qwen3-4B mode 3 19.4 vs 19.5 s.

On ROCm, @djramic reported on Slack that without the #42129 allow-list the Kimi-K2 arch (dummy weights, torch 2.13) compiles about as fast as before. I had no ROCm access to verify this myself.

## Details

**Root cause:** #42129 added every `vllm::*` and `vllm_aiter::*` op to Inductor's `FALLBACK_ALLOW_LIST`. Inductor creates fallbacks for allow-listed ops without PyTorch's default layout constraint for custom ops. Without it, Inductor passes `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` a head-major key, strides `(128, 128*S, 1)` instead of eager's `(1024, 128, 1)`. `reshape_and_cache_flash` only reads `key.stride(0)` and assumes packed heads, so every cached key is scrambled and the output is garbage. Default mode 3 is unaffected because it splits the graph at the attention and KV-cache ops.

**Why revert:** The allow-list only existed to skip an implicit-fallback INFO message that torch <= 2.12 builds eagerly, which hung compilation on deep MoE/TP graphs. pytorch/pytorch#185951 makes it lazy from torch 2.13, and CUDA, CPU, XPU and the default ROCm images are on >= 2.13. Reverting restores PyTorch's behavior for all vLLM ops. #62924's own control row (allow-list disabled) already gives token-identical output to its patched run. The allow-list cannot stay for torch < 2.13 either, because the layout bug is in that code path on every torch version; those versions only need the hang protection, which skipping the message for vLLM ops provides.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- The torch < 2.13 patch can be removed once every platform pins torch >= 2.13. Until then, Inductor messages for vLLM ops (including lowering errors) show only the op name on those versions, as with #42129.
- On torch >= 2.13 with Inductor's graph logger at INFO, the full message is still built and can be slow on very deep graphs (`IRNode.__str__` has no depth limit, as #43111 found). This is opt-in debug logging.
- Overlaps with #57310, whose allow-list change should become unnecessary.
- A follow-up PR could make the KV-cache writers (reshape_and_cache, reshape_and_cache_flash and their Triton versions) reject keys whose heads are not packed, so a future layout change raises an error instead of silently corrupting the cache.

title: [Model] Add Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe
author: DongjiGao
body:
## Overview

Adds NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe (`Nemotron3_5TranscribeForConditionalGeneration`), a speech-language model: a
native audio tower whose embeddings replace `<|audio|>` placeholders in the prompt of the existing NemotronH decoder.
It loads the released checkpoint `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B` and its FP8 and NVFP4 variants, serves
chat completions with audio and `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, and supports MTP and DFlash2 speculative decoding. The PR adds model files plus
the usual registry, config, docs and test entries, and, in its own commit, a small DFlash2 fix in shared
speculative-decoding code; it does not change the engine, scheduler or API server.

## Claims

- New architectures `Nemotron3_5TranscribeForConditionalGeneration` and `Nemotron3_5TranscribeMTPModel` (MTP draft).
- Native audio tower: log-mel features, the Parallel Expert Encoder (a transformer ASR encoder and an online
  Sortformer speaker branch, fused), and a projection. No Transformers implementation is needed.
- Loads the released checkpoint's NeMo SpeechLM layout (`model_type: nemo_speechlm`, architecture
  `Nemotron3_5TranscribeForConditionalGeneration`). The checkpoint's CTC timestamp head is skipped; word timestamps
  are a planned follow-up.
- Loads the FP8 and NVFP4 repos (`-FP8`, `-NVFP4`; ModelOpt FP8 and mixed FP8/NVFP4 recipes). Their decoder uses
  Hugging Face NemotronH names, one tensor per expert. The audio tower's linear layers are vLLM `ReplicatedLinear`
  layers built with the quantization config, so the recipe quantizes the ASR encoder to FP8 as it does the decoder.
  The MTP draft keeps the recipe, so the FP8 MTP head loads with its scales.
- Audio batching: a clip is batched only with clips that span as many 40 s encoder windows, and padding frames are
  zeroed before the speaker head's convolution, so a clip's result does not depend on its batch.
- `/v1/audio/transcriptions` splits long audio into pieces of up to one hour; a chat request takes one clip of up to
  one hour by default.
- DFlash2 works with this target. On main, a request in chunked prefill anchored on `<|audio|>`, past the draft
  vocabulary, and the selector's codebook lookup failed a device-side assert. The DFlash2 commit clamps the anchor
  and keeps top-k candidates inside the draft vocabulary.
- Accuracy matches the NeMo reference implementation within its run-to-run spread on the Open ASR Leaderboard
  English and multilingual quick sets; with the FP8 and NVFP4 repos, WER stays within 0.1 of the NeMo reference
  running the same checkpoints, and MTP accepts as many drafts.

## Validation

Quick set v2 (18,341 English and 15,486 multilingual clips; greedy; Skills scorer):

| Run | WER (%), English | WER (%), multilingual |
|---|---:|---:|
| This PR's model code on vLLM main (`6ae62b5368`) | 3.89 | 4.91 |
| Same model code on vLLM v0.32.0 | 3.88 | 4.88 |
| NeMo reference (vLLM plugin), two runs | 3.87 | 4.98 |
| FP8 repo, this PR | 3.92 | 5.10 |
| FP8 repo, NeMo reference | 3.86 | 5.02 |
| NVFP4 repo (FP8 KV cache), this PR | 3.94 | 5.22 |
| NVFP4 repo (FP8 KV cache), NeMo reference | 3.88 | 5.16 |

The released checkpoints' loaded weights are byte-identical to the checkpoints behind this table; only their CTC
timestamp heads, which are not loaded, differ. With NVFP4, this PR's transcripts agree with the NeMo reference's as
often as two NeMo reference runs agree with each other (80% of English clips).

Served smoke on vLLM main with the released checkpoint (one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, MTP2, the checkpoint's chat
template):
- 24/24 quick-set clips give the same transcript through `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/chat/completions`.
- An unknown language code and the translation task return HTTP 400.
- MTP2 mean acceptance length 2.90 of 3 in the server's last logged interval (per position 95.8% and 94.2%).

The same smoke with DFlash2 K=7 (`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2`): 24/24 clips give the same
transcript on both endpoints; draft acceptance 75% and 82% in two runs' last logged intervals (mean acceptance
length 6.3 and 6.7 of 8). Without the DFlash2 commit, the engine stops with a device-side assert.

The same smoke with the FP8 and NVFP4 repos (`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`; NVFP4 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`):
MTP2 mean acceptance length 2.97 (FP8) and 2.94 (NVFP4, as the NeMo reference); DFlash2 K=7 on NVFP4 5.7 of 8. FP8
gives the same transcript on both endpoints for 24/24 clips, NVFP4 for 18 to 21 of 24, the others differing on near
ties (a comma, "we'll" for "will"). Without the MTP recipe fix, MTP2 accepted 1 to 2% of drafts.

Tests and checks on vLLM main (`a75277a0a1`, with CUDA hidden):
- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron3_5_transcribe.py`: 23 passed. Three of them load a
  `config.json` through vLLM: the released layout builds a `ModelConfig`, and NeMo's generic architecture is refused,
  with the `architectures` value to set when the checkpoint has this model's structure (fails without the hint) and
  with a pointer to the NeMo Speech vLLM plugin otherwise. A tiny audio tower checks the embedding count per audio
  length and that each clip encodes as if alone (fails without the padding fix); an FP8 recipe quantizes exactly the
  ASR encoder's linear layers and their scalar scales load; the decoder renamer reads both checkpoint layouts; the MTP
  draft config keeps the quantization recipe (fails without the fix); a non-audio modality is refused.
- `pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "Nemotron3_5 or coverage"`: 3 passed.
- `pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Nemotron3_5Transcribe`, which the online registry entries enable: 2
  passed on one GPU, for `Nemotron3_5TranscribeForConditionalGeneration` and `Nemotron3_5TranscribeMTPModel` (dummy
  weights, one decoder layer), with the entries online and the Hub repo read with an access token before launch.
- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py`: 106 passed on one GPU; on the CPU platform (CUDA hidden), 14 passed
  and 92 skipped (they need CUDA). The two new CPU tests, for the anchor clamp and for top-k past the processor's
  vocabulary, fail without the DFlash2 commit.
- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py`: 33 passed. The DFlash2 commit moves the padding mask of
  `get_top_tokens` and `get_top_k_tokens` into `_mask_outside_vocab`, which also reads `org_vocab_size`. This test
  calls `get_top_k_tokens` with a `SimpleNamespace` as `self`, so its stand-in now has both; without that test-only
  change, two cases fail with `AttributeError`.
- `pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual`, as CI runs it: all hooks pass.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: no GPU-to-host sync on the inference path (clip lengths stay on the host).

CI coverage: the Hub repos became public at the launch, after this PR opened, so here both registry entries still set
`is_available_online=False`.
CI runs the import and interface checks in `tests/models/test_registry.py` and the CPU tests above (the CPU multimodal
processor step collects `tests/models/multimodal/processing`); `tests/models/test_initialization.py` and the shared
processor tests skip the model. A follow-up PR sets the entries online once the repos are public. The local runs above
cover those tests, loading, generation and MTP; a short generation test can follow.

On this branch (two RTX PRO 6000, MTP2, 24 clips through both endpoints), TP=2 and DP=2 serve every clip; 21 of 24
transcripts are identical to one GPU, and the others differ only in spelling or punctuation. Earlier, with the same
model code on vLLM v0.32.0: TP=2 and DP=2 match one GPU; DFlash2 and MTP2 keep accuracy on
the quick set.

Reproduce:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}'
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions -F model=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \
  -F file=@clip.wav
# DFlash2 instead of MTP:
#   --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2",
#                          "num_speculative_tokens": 7}'
# FP8 or NVFP4: serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-FP8 or ...-NVFP4 the same way (MTP from the
# same repo); NVFP4 was validated with --kv-cache-dtype fp8.
```

## Details

- Native tower: the audio encoder has no public Transformers implementation, so it is implemented in vLLM, with the
  NeMo checkpoint names (`perception.*`).
- Names: the checkpoint declares `nemo_speechlm`, the model type of every NeMo SpeechLM checkpoint; the architecture
  name selects this model. The config class refuses other NeMo SpeechLM architectures. A checkpoint with this model's
  structure (the Parallel Expert Encoder on a NemotronH decoder) under NeMo's generic name, as older exports have,
  gets the `architectures` value to set in its `config.json`; others are pointed to the NeMo Speech vLLM plugin.
- MTP: the drafter shares the target's embedding and LM head. Its weight filter accepts the checkpoint's `llm.mtp.*`
  names, so a sharded checkpoint loads only the shards that hold the MTP head.
- DFlash2 fix (separate commit): the anchor clamp in `qwen3_dflash2.py`; `get_top_k_tokens` and `get_top_tokens` in
  `logits_processor.py` mask columns past the processor's vocabulary, as `_get_logits` drops them; the DFlash2
  candidate processor is sized by `min(get_vocab_size(), config.vocab_size)`, so targets whose vocabulary is not
  larger than the draft's behave as before. The 10 head rows past the draft vocabulary are zero, so the candidate
  path rarely fires; the anchor path crashed every smoke run.
- Pre-review: @Isotr0py reviewed this change privately before the launch and approved it.
- Model Runner V2 only: all validation ran on V2, the default on main.
- The decoder's Mamba SSM state dtype comes from the decoder config (`MODELS_CONFIG_MAP` entry), as for NemotronH.
- Long audio: the encoder cache is sized from the `--limit-mm-per-prompt` audio length, so a longer configured clip
  is admitted. Server-wide decode limits (`VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S`, 600 s by default, and the 25 MB upload
  limit) still apply and are documented in the supported-models note.
- Thinking: the chat template turns thinking on by default; transcription servers should pass
  `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'` (documented).
- Limitation: the audio tower runs replicated on every tensor-parallel rank.
- Quantized repos: `hf_to_vllm_mapper` maps the recipe's layer names (`backbone.*`, `lm_head`, `perception.*`) onto
  `language_model.*` and `audio_tower.*`. The tower's linear layers flatten their input to 2-D, because vLLM's
  quantized kernels take `(tokens, features)`. The NVFP4 recipe declares no KV-cache quantization; the NeMo reference
  ran it with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, as did the validation above. vLLM's FP8 linear layer adds the bias after
  rounding, where the NeMo reference adds it inside the CUTLASS kernel (one bf16 step on some elements).
- Memory note: the quick-set runs on main used `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
  --max-num-seqs 512` on one 96 GB GPU (0.75 for the FP8 and NVFP4 repos). FlashInfer's autotune runs after vLLM's
  memory plan: with 32,768 batched tokens, start-up ran out of memory at both 0.85 and 0.80, and the NVFP4 repo did at
  0.85 even with 8,192. This is not specific to this model.
- Not in this PR: CTC word timestamps (follow-up through the transcription API, with forced alignment) and the
  Transformers-layout conversion of the checkpoint (Hugging Face's Transformers port uses its own layout and
  `model_type`).
- Duplicate check: no open PR adds this architecture.

---
