title: [Quantization] Support CSF-compressed NVFP4 block scales in ModelOpt
author: lesj0610
body:
## Overview

Lets vLLM load ModelOpt checkpoints whose routed-expert NVFP4 block scales are CSF-compressed. Each layer names its format in `quantized_layers[...]["weight_scale_encoding"]`, and two formats ship today: `csf` in `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local` and `csf_32x2_v1` in `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local`. This started from #60646 (draft since Oct 8); its two commits are still in the history, and the `csf` decoder comes from it.

## Claims

- `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` takes the CSF streams as its own params, decodes each scale matrix once all of its streams have arrived, and loads it through the scale param's own weight loader. TP and EP sharding, the MoE backends and the kernels see the same E4M3 scales as with an uncompressed checkpoint.
- Each encoding is one entry in `layers/quantization/utils/csf_scales.py`: its stream names and its decoder. The ModelOpt config renames `<proj>.weight_scale.<stream>` to the method's params, so model loaders don't change.
- A stream param sets `weight_loader_target` to the scale it fills. `track_weights_loading` counts the scale as loaded through it, and layerwise reload leaves its loader unwrapped so the scale's own wrapper buffers and counts the load.
- Both decoders are lossless against NVIDIA's reference decoders.
- An unknown encoding, or an encoding on a non-NVFP4 layer, fails when the config is built. An encoding on any layer other than routed experts, including one shard of a fused linear, fails in `get_quant_method`. Malformed streams and matrices with missing streams raise instead of loading wrong bytes.

## Validation

On CPU, main (`dc45a5f552`) plus this PR:

```text
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_csf_scales.py  # 13 passed
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py    # 9 passed
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py      # 64 passed, 33 skipped, 1 failed, 2 errors
pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py                   # 109 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed, 3 errors
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                       # passed
```

The failures and errors in `test_reload.py` and `test_modelopt.py` start an engine and need a GPU, which was hidden for this run; they fail the same way without this PR. The new `test_registry.py` and `test_reload.py` cases and the stream test in `test_csf_scales.py` fail without the `weight_loader_target` handling.

`csf`: all 73,728 scale matrices in a local copy of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local decode byte-identical to `decode_csf_slab_scales` in NVIDIA's reference implementation, with up to 13,793 exceptions in one matrix and no stream pair split across shards. The whole decode takes 25.3 s in one process.

`csf_32x2_v1`: 378 GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local matrices fetched from the Hub (every CSF layer, three experts each, gate/up/down) decode byte-identical to `decode_csf_scales` in the same reference.

End to end on two SM80 GPUs with TP=2, running this PR's Python against the compiled ops of nightly `0.32.1rc1.dev467+g444d69110`: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local (`--language-model-only`) loads with `enable_weights_track` and no missing weights, holds 96 decoded scale params per rank, and answers five greedy prompts correctly. `reload_weights` then processes all 48 CSF MoE layers on each rank with no delayed or failed loads, and leaves the scale checksums and the greedy outputs unchanged.

## Details

The decode happens at load time rather than in `process_weights_after_loading` because the compressed streams can't be TP-sliced: holding them until then would keep every layer's compressed scales on each rank. The streams add up to 4.0 GB in Qwen3.8 and 10.3 GB in GLM-5.3, summed from the safetensors headers. The stream params are empty, so they never reach kernels or EPLB.

The decoders run in numpy rather than torch: every small torch op goes through the intra-op thread pool, which the loader sizes to CPUs per local worker, and that made the `csf` decode about 1.7x slower in #60646's form.

Both checkpoints keep weights in a `tensors/` subdirectory, which the default loader doesn't search yet: all 21 Qwen3.8 shards, and the 214 attention and indexer tensors of GLM-5.3. Neither loads in full from the Hub until that lookup lands in #64739.

Not a duplicate: #63908 decodes CSF inside the Qwen4Exp NVIDIA model file. Searching open PRs for "CSF", "weight_scale_encoding" and "nvfp4_csf" turns up nothing else.

Like #60646, this doesn't keep the scales compressed in GPU memory; that needs kernels that read compressed scales.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Keep 32-bit buffer addressing for per-token-head KV and AITER cross-attention fallback
author: umarkovi-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

<!-- Summarize the change in 1-2 lines. Link relevant issues and PRs. -->

Follow-up to #60084. On ROCm, two more paths now give their KV-cache views a Triton `ptr_range()`, so Triton's AMD backend keeps 32-bit buffer addressing for them:
- the per-token-head quantized KV cache (`int8_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`) in `TRITON_ATTN`;
- the non-causal fallback of `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, which runs vLLM's `kernel_unified_attention` for encoder-decoder cross-attention.

Updated to current `main`, which now includes the extensible KV cache (#56492). How the two interact is described under Details.

## Claims

<!-- State the accomplishments in a few concrete bullets: speedups, feature support, bug fixes, etc. -->

- Throughput on Radeon Pro W7900 (gfx1100), current `main`, default settings:
  - **+56%** for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, `TRITON_ATTN` with an `int8_per_token_head` KV cache: 1.93 → 3.02 req/s.
  - **+60%** for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with an `fp8_per_token_head` KV cache: 2.01 → 3.22 req/s.
- When the extensible KV cache is off (V1 model runner, explicit `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, or no VMM support):
  - **+49%** for gpt-oss-20b with an `int8_per_token_head` KV cache: 2.46 → 3.66 req/s.
  - **+1%** for Whisper-large-v3 on `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`: 6.88 → 6.95 req/s.
- No regressions: AITER's own causal kernel is not touched, and the other workloads measured are unchanged.
- No accuracy change: Whisper transcripts are token-identical, and GSM8K with per-token-head KV caches (Qwen2.5-7B, gpt-oss-20b) is within run-to-run noise.
- 6 lines in two files; no new configuration.

## Validation

<!-- Show evidence that the claims are met by this change, and steps to reproduce validations. -->

W7900 (gfx1100), ROCm 10.2, PyTorch 2.14, Triton 3.8.0. Base = this PR's parent, using the same build (the change is Python-only). Base and PR runs alternated on the same GPU. Each variant started from an empty `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, warmed by an untimed first run.

**Current `main` (c7a7607519), extensible KV cache on by default**

| `vllm bench throughput`, random 1024 / 256, 500 prompts unless noted | base (3 runs) | this PR (3 runs) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, bf16, `TRITON_ATTN`, `--kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head` | 1.93 / 1.93 / 1.93 | 3.02 / 3.02 / 3.02 | **+56%** |
| Same, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_per_token_head` | 2.01 / 2.01 / 2.01 | 3.21 / 3.22 / 3.22 | **+60%** |
| gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4 MoE, sinks, sliding window), `TRITON_ATTN`, `int8_per_token_head` | 2.48 / 2.49 / 2.48 | 2.48 / 2.48 / 2.48 | ±0 (see Details) |
| Whisper-large-v3, fp16, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, LibriSpeech, 100 prompts × 200 tokens | 7.03 / 7.02 / 7.02 | 7.02 / 7.02 / 7.02 | ±0 (see Details) |

**Current `main`, `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`**

| `vllm bench throughput` | base (2 runs) | this PR (2 runs) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, `TRITON_ATTN`, `int8_per_token_head` | 2.46 / 2.46 | 3.66 / 3.66 | **+49%** |
| Whisper-large-v3, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` | 6.88 / 6.87 | 6.95 / 6.94 | **+1%** |

<details>
<summary>Earlier measurements on the parent before #56492 (5ea8301982), 3 runs per side</summary>

| `vllm bench throughput` | base | this PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, `int8_per_token_head` | 1.99 / 1.99 / 1.99 | 3.04 / 3.04 / 3.04 | +53% |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, `fp8_per_token_head` | 2.10 / 2.10 / 2.10 | 3.19 / 3.20 / 3.19 | +52% |
| gpt-oss-20b, `int8_per_token_head` | 2.45 / 2.45 / 2.45 | 3.67 / 3.67 / 3.67 | +50% |
| gpt-oss-20b, `fp8_per_token_head` | 2.55 / 2.55 / 2.55 | 3.71 / 3.71 / 3.71 | +45% |
| Whisper-large-v3, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` | 6.83 / 6.83 / 6.84 | 6.91 / 6.91 / 6.93 | +1.2% |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` (decoder-only, AITER's causal kernel) | 3.87 / 3.87 / 3.87 | 3.87 / 3.87 / 3.87 | ±0 |
</details>

| Accuracy | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Whisper, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, 32 LibriSpeech clips, greedy (current `main`) | — | 32 / 32 token-identical |
| GSM8K, Qwen2.5-7B, `int8_per_token_head`, 5-shot, strict / flexible (current `main`) | 78.01 / 81.50 | 79.00 / 82.34 |
| GSM8K, Qwen2.5-7B, `int8_per_token_head`, 5-shot, strict-match, 3 runs (parent before #56492) | 79.23 / 79.23 / 77.86 (mean 78.77) | 78.17 / 78.62 / 79.00 (mean 78.60) |
| GSM8K, gpt-oss-20b, `int8_per_token_head`, chat template, 0-shot, 2048 tokens, flexible-extract, 3 runs (parent before #56492) | 85.75 / 85.37 / 86.20 (mean 85.77) | 86.28 / 86.20 / 86.05 (mean 86.18) |
| Same, `fp8_per_token_head` | 85.52 / 85.29 / 86.28 (mean 85.70) | 85.67 / 85.60 / 86.28 (mean 85.85) |

GSM8K stderr is ±1.1 for Qwen and ±1.0 for gpt-oss. Greedy Qwen outputs can't be compared token for token: with `TRITON_ATTN` (compile + CUDA graphs), `main` itself is not run-to-run deterministic on this GPU (base-vs-base agreed on 37–43 of 128 prompts; 58 of 128 for BF16).

<details>
<summary>Code generation, profile and lint</summary>

- **Code generation** (Triton cache of each run, current `main`):
  - Per-token-head (Qwen2.5-7B): `key_cache_ptr`, `value_cache_ptr`, `k_scale_cache_ptr` and `v_scale_cache_ptr` carry `tt.pointer_range = 32` in `kernel_unified_attention` and `_reshape_cache_per_token_head`. FP8 split-KV decode: 252 → 191 VGPRs. INT8: 242 → 239 VGPRs; the gain there comes from 32-bit address arithmetic on the four pointers.
  - gpt-oss-20b with the extensible KV cache off: split-KV decode variants 255/256 → 156/167 VGPRs (INT8).
  - AITER fallback: `kernel_unified_attention` K/V gain `tt.pointer_range = 32`, 255 → 205 VGPRs.
- **Why AITER's causal kernel is excluded** (measured before #56492):
  - Hinting it as well gives its K/V `tt.pointer_range = 32` without lowering its VGPRs (232–240; 256 for `_3d`).
  - A rocprofv3 trace shows its `_2d` decode variant 5.9% slower per call (715.8 → 758.2 µs); Qwen on `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` lost 0.8%.
- **Host overhead:** `set_triton_ptr_range` costs ~1 µs per call. A `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` run on both changed paths passes.
- **Lint:** `pre-commit run` (ruff, mypy, typos, …) passes on the changed files.
- **No new tests:** the change only affects code generation, and CI has no RDNA runners.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 FLASH_ATTENTION_TRITON_AMD_ENABLE=TRUE
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --attention-config.backend TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 500 --seed 0
# gpt-oss-20b: same with --model openai/gpt-oss-20b, plus --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache for the second table
vllm bench throughput --model openai/whisper-large-v3 --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --dtype float16 --max-model-len 448 \
  --attention-config.backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openslr/librispeech_asr --hf-subset clean --hf-split validation \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":1}' --num-prompts 100 --backend vllm --output-len 200
# GSM8K: lm_eval.simple_evaluate(model=VLLM(pretrained="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", dtype="bfloat16",
#   max_model_len=4096, attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}, kv_cache_dtype="int8_per_token_head"),
#   tasks=["gsm8k"], num_fewshot=5)
# gpt-oss-20b: pretrained="openai/gpt-oss-20b", num_fewshot=0, apply_chat_template=True,
#   gen_kwargs="max_gen_toks=2048,temperature=0"; score = flexible-extract
```
</details>

## Details

<!-- Explain motivation, design decisions, root cause, tradeoffs, and limitations concisely. Link or collapse lengthy supporting material. -->

**Root cause.**
- #60084 fixed the 32-bit addressing loss caused by #51718's single KV-cache allocation, but only for the K/V views built in `TritonAttentionImpl.forward` and `do_kv_cache_update`.
- The per-token-head path builds its views in `_pth_key_value_caches()`. Its per-(token, head) scale caches are strided float32 views of the same storage.
- The AITER backend calls `kernel_unified_attention` directly for non-causal attention.
- In all these cases Triton's `is_within_2gb` saw the whole allocation and chose 64-bit addressing.

**Change.**
- `TritonAttentionImpl`, on ROCm (existing `_set_kv_ptr_range` flag):
  - `_ensure_scale_caches()` sets the bound once on the two scale caches when it creates them;
  - `_pth_key_value_caches()` sets it on the K/V views on every call.
- `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionImpl.forward` sets it on the K/V views right before the non-causal fallback call.
- All reuse `set_triton_ptr_range` from #60084; the bound is the distance from each view's `data_ptr()` to the end of the layer's region.

**Interaction with the extensible KV cache (#56492).**
- Until warmup ends, each layer's view spans the layer's whole *reservation*; CUDA graphs are captured in this phase. After `extend_kv_cache`, `committed_views()` rebinds each layer to storage of exactly its committed blocks.
- Eager launches after the extend therefore get 32-bit addressing without any hint (Whisper above: base = PR). The fallback hint still matters when the extensible cache is off.
- Kernels captured in CUDA graphs keep the binary compiled during warmup. When a layer's reservation is ≤ 2 GiB (Qwen2.5-7B), this PR gives them 32-bit addressing. When it exceeds 2 GiB, nothing can: gpt-oss-20b INT8 here reserves 126,664 blocks × 17,408 B = 2.05 GiB per layer, while the committed size is 1.64 GiB. Traced inside the engine, the hint reports 2.054 GiB during capture and 1.641 GiB afterwards, and Triton correctly refuses the first.
- This also affects #60084, is independent of this PR, and is better handled separately.

**Safety.**
- The scale and K/V offsets the kernels compute are non-negative and stay within the layer: block-table index × block stride + slot/head/channel offsets.
- Triton still checks the bound against 2 GiB at every launch. `set_triton_ptr_range` reads only shapes, strides and `data_ptr()`; it never touches uncommitted memory.
- The INT4 per-token-head kernel and AITER's causal kernel are unchanged.

**Limitations.**
- Measured on RDNA3 only.
- Not covered:
  - `TRITON_MLA` / AITER MLA `decode_attention_fwd`, which reviewers of #60084 measured a CDNA gain on; left for a separate PR;
  - `TritonAttentionDiffKVImpl` and the gfx1250 shuffled-KV Triton cache write.

**Duplicates.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `ptr_range`, `set_triton_ptr_range`, per-token-head + `ptr_range`, and AITER cross-attention; only #60084 overlaps.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Wait for MoRIIO WRITE mode completions in short chunks
author: kliuae
body:
## Overview

In MoRIIO WRITE mode, the prefill (P) instance waits for a request's KV copies before it sends `write_done` to the decode (D) instance, and the READ barrier waits for its reads the same way. Both go through `MoRIIOWrapper.waiting_for_transfer_complete` which makes one MoRI `wait_all` call with the whole `transfer_timeout`. On MoRI's xGMI backend, that call polls each status once and then sleeps until its deadline, so a copy that is still running at that poll holds the wait for the full timeout (30s by default). This also happens on MoRI's scatter/gather copy path under load, where a wait that still sees `IN_PROGRESS` at its deadline fails the transfer and leaves the decode request waiting. This PR calls `wait_all` in 10ms intervals, and checks the statuses between the intervals, up to the same `transfer_timeout`.



## Claims

- On MI355X with MoRI v1.2.3.post1, a prefill process writing 118 layers (128 blocks of 32 KiB each) into a decode process on another GPU over xGMI with MoRI's default copy path, `transfer_timeout` 30s: on main all 6 of 6 waits took 29.999 s, even though every one of the 118 statuses had succeeded. With this PR, 100 of 100 waits ended after 0.210 s (median; min 0.183 s, max 0.210 s), all succeeded.
- When a status fails, the wait raises at once with `fail_fast=True` (WRITE), or once no status is in flight with `fail_fast=False` (READ barrier), as the polling fallback already does. Timeouts and error messages are unchanged.
- With P/D serving, for DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat served with prefill TP1 and decode TP1 on MI355X over xGMI, with `MORI_IO_XGMI_SCATTER_GATHER_THRESHOLD=0` (MoRI's scatter/gather copy path) on prefill, 16K-token prompts: on main, two of three runs at concurrency 8 left requests that never completed (92 and 95 out of 96), each after a completion wait that failed with `IN_PROGRESS` when its 30s `transfer_timeout` expired. In the run that finished, concurrency 16 reached only 2.28 req/s with a client TTFT p90 of 30.2 s. With this PR, all 96 requests completed in each of three runs, with no failed wait, at 6.96–7.20 req/s.



## Validation

### Unit tests
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_transfer_completion.py`: the native wait returns once the statuses succeed, follows `fail_fast` after a failure, and calls `wait_all` in 10ms slices.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py`: the READ barrier's native-timeout test runs on a fake clock and checks that the wait lasts `transfer_timeout` in slices of at most 10ms.


### Completion wait over xGMI

On MI355X with MoRI 1.2.3.post1 (no `MORI_IO_XGMI_SCATTER_GATHER_THRESHOLD`, so MoRI uses its default copy path). A prefill process on GPU 0 writes 118 layers of 128 blocks (32 KiB each) into a decode process's buffer on GPU 1, one `batch_write` per layer, and waits for them through `MoRIIOWrapper.waiting_for_transfer_complete` with `transfer_timeout=30`, as the WRITE producer does before `write_done`.

| | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| number of waits timed | 6 | 100 |
| wait, median (s) | 29.999 | 0.210 |
| wait, min / max (s) | 29.999 / 29.999 | 0.183 / 0.210 |
| statuses succeeded at the end | 118 of 118 in every wait | 118 of 118 in every wait |

<details>
<summary>reproducer (moriio_wait_repro.py)</summary>

```python
"""Time vLLM's MoRIIO WRITE completion wait over xGMI.

A prefill process on --p-gpu writes 118 layers of 128 blocks (32 KiB each) into a
decode process's buffer on --d-gpu, one MoRI batch_write per layer, then waits
for them with MoRIIOWrapper.waiting_for_transfer_complete (transfer_timeout 30 s),
as the WRITE producer does before it sends write_done.

    python moriio_wait_repro.py --p-gpu 0 --d-gpu 1 --requests 3
"""

import argparse
import multiprocessing as mp
import os
import pickle
import tempfile
import time

LAYERS, BLOCKS, BLOCK_BYTES = 118, 128, 32768
LAYER_BYTES = 2 * BLOCKS * BLOCK_BYTES


def setup(role, port, run_dir):
    import torch
    from mori.io import (
        BackendType,
        EngineDesc,
        IOEngine,
        IOEngineConfig,
        MemoryDesc,
        XgmiBackendConfig,
    )

    buf = torch.zeros(LAYERS * LAYER_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    engine = IOEngine(f"{role}-repro", IOEngineConfig("127.0.0.1", port))
    engine.create_backend(BackendType.XGMI, XgmiBackendConfig())
    mem = engine.register_torch_tensor(buf)
    mine = os.path.join(run_dir, role)
    peer = os.path.join(run_dir, {"p": "d", "d": "p"}[role])
    with open(mine + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
        pickle.dump((engine.get_engine_desc().pack(), mem.pack()), f)
    os.rename(mine + ".tmp", mine)
    while not os.path.exists(peer):
        time.sleep(0.1)
    with open(peer, "rb") as f:
        peer_engine, peer_mem = pickle.load(f)
    engine.register_remote_engine(EngineDesc.unpack(peer_engine))
    return engine, buf, mem, MemoryDesc.unpack(peer_mem)


def decode(port, run_dir):
    _ = setup("d", port + 1, run_dir)
    while not os.path.exists(os.path.join(run_dir, "done")):
        time.sleep(0.5)


def prefill(port, run_dir, requests):
    from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.moriio.moriio_engine import (
        MoRIIOWrapper,
    )

    engine, _buf, mem, peer_mem = setup("p", port, run_dir)
    session = engine.create_session(mem, peer_mem)
    wrapper = MoRIIOWrapper(moriio_engine=engine, transfer_timeout=30.0)
    sizes = [BLOCK_BYTES] * BLOCKS
    for request in range(requests):
        statuses = []
        for layer in range(LAYERS):
            offsets = [layer * LAYER_BYTES + 2 * b * BLOCK_BYTES for b in range(BLOCKS)]
            uid = engine.allocate_transfer_uid()
            statuses.append(session.batch_write(offsets, offsets, sizes, uid))
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            wrapper.waiting_for_transfer_complete(statuses)
            outcome = "ok"
        except Exception as e:
            outcome = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        succeeded = sum(s.Succeeded() for s in statuses)
        print(
            f"request {request}: wait {time.monotonic() - start:.3f} s, "
            f"{succeeded}/{len(statuses)} statuses succeeded, {outcome}",
            flush=True,
        )
    open(os.path.join(run_dir, "done"), "w").close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--p-gpu", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--d-gpu", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=29600)
    parser.add_argument("--requests", type=int, default=3)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
    run_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    os.environ["HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = str(args.d_gpu)
    d = ctx.Process(target=decode, args=(args.port, run_dir))
    d.start()
    os.environ["HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = str(args.p_gpu)
    p = ctx.Process(target=prefill, args=(args.port, run_dir, args.requests))
    p.start()
    p.join()
    d.join()
```

```
python3 moriio_wait_repro.py --p-gpu 0 --d-gpu 1 --requests 6     # main
python3 moriio_wait_repro.py --p-gpu 0 --d-gpu 1 --requests 100   # this PR
```

</details>


### P/D serving over xGMI

DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, prefill and decode both served with TP1, MoRIIO WRITE over xGMI, using MoRIIO toy proxy, `MORI_IO_XGMI_SCATTER_GATHER_THRESHOLD=0` on the prefill instance, benchmarked with ISL/OSL=16k/16.

| | main (runs 1 / 2 / 3) | PR (runs 1 / 2 / 3) |
|---|---|---|
| concurrency 8: requests completed (out of 96) | 92 / 96 / 95 | 96 / 96 / 96 |
| completion waits that failed with `IN_PROGRESS` | 1 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| concurrency 8: client TTFT mean (ms) | – / 1,089.8 / – | 1,074.3 / 1,085.7 / 1,075.3 |
| concurrency 8: client TTFT p99 (ms) | – / 1,490.3 / – | 1,584.5 / 1,607.7 / 1,588.6 |
| concurrency 16: requests completed (of 192) | – / 192 / – | 192 / 192 / 192 |
| concurrency 16: request throughput (req/s) | – / 2.28 / – | 7.12 / 7.17 / 7.20 |
| concurrency 16: client TTFT median (ms) | – / 2,191.7 / – | 2,174.4 / 2,164.0 / 2,159.1 |
| concurrency 16: client TTFT p90 (ms) | – / 30,151.4 / – | 2,317.5 / 2,212.6 / 2,187.5 |
| concurrency 16: client TTFT p99 (ms) | – / 31,936.9 / – | 3,571.5 / 3,560.5 / 3,569.3 |

On main the unfinished requests are the ones whose transfer failed with the prefill write worker raising `TransferError` ("MoRIIO batch wait failed (StatusCode.IN_PROGRESS): RDMA transfer timed out after 30s") while the decode instance being told nothing, so the decode request kept waiting for its KV. In main's second run at concurrency 16, the waits returned at their 30s deadline instead of failing. As the write worker handles one transfer at a time, every transfer queued behind such wait was delayed too.

<details>
<summary>serving and benchmark commands</summary>

```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
ARGS="--tensor-parallel-size 1 --block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype auto --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --compilation-config {\"cudagraph_mode\":\"FULL_DECODE_ONLY\"} --max-model-len 40960"

python3 examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 11350 --service-discovery-port 11353

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_PORT=11358 MORI_IO_XGMI_SCATTER_GATHER_THRESHOLD=0 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --port 11351 $ARGS \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backend":"xgmi","proxy_ip":"127.0.0.1","proxy_ping_port":"11353","http_port":"11351","handshake_port":"11354","notify_port":"11355"}}'

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 VLLM_PORT=11362 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --port 11352 $ARGS \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backend":"xgmi","proxy_ip":"127.0.0.1","proxy_ping_port":"11353","http_port":"11352","handshake_port":"11356","notify_port":"11357"}}'

for cn in 8:8 8:96 16:192; do   # warm-up, the concurrency-8 run, the concurrency-16 run
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:11350 \
    --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 16 \
    --max-concurrency ${cn%:*} --num-prompts ${cn#*:} --ignore-eos --seed 0 \
    --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
done
grep -c 'MoRIIO batch wait failed (StatusCode.IN_PROGRESS)' prefill.log   # failed completion waits
```

</details>



## Details

On MoRIIO's WRITE path of the prefill instance under PD disaggregated serving, for one request:

1. D allocates blocks for the request and sends their ids to every P rank.
2. In P's forward, each layer's write is scheduled with the layer's CUDA event.
3. P's write worker waits for each event and posts the layer's copies (`batch_write` on a MoRI session).
4. After the last layer, `_finalize_if_complete` waits for every copy of the request (`waiting_for_transfer_complete`) and sends `write_done`.
5. D marks the request's KV as received and starts decoding it.

Step 4 makes one MoRI call with the whole timeout:

```
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_engine.py's MoRIIOWrapper.waiting_for_transfer_complete
timeout_ms = ceil(self._transfer_timeout * 1000)
result = wait_all(transfers_to_wait, timeout_ms=timeout_ms)
```

On MoRI's xGMI backend, a status completes only when it is polled, and a bounded `wait_all` polls each status once and then sleeps until its deadline. If the copies are still running at that one poll, the wait costs the whole `transfer_timeout`; when the statuses are still `IN_PROGRESS` at the deadline, the transfer fails with `TransferError`, and on main no failure notice reaches decode. With the default copy path the last layers are nearly always still running when step 4 starts, so the wait lasts the whole `transfer_timeout` and the request's `write_done` reaches D 30s late. As shown in the the reproducer above, however, every status had succeeded long before the call returned. On the scatter/gather path the copies are fast, but when prefill has already queued its next step, they complete only after that step, so under load the one poll misses them there as well.

This PR addresses this by calling `wait_all` with at most 10ms and checking the statuses with `poll_transfer_batch` between calls, until `transfer_timeout`:

- every status succeeded: return;
- a status failed: raise at once with `fail_fast=True`, or once nothing is in flight with `fail_fast=False` (on main the native path ignored `fail_fast` and always waited for the deadline);
- an error result without a failed status, or the deadline: raise, with the same messages as before.

AI agent was used in this PR.

title: [Bugfix] Flashinfer attention warmup deadlock under PP>1
author: yzong-rh
body:
## Overview

Fix a deadlock during Flashinfer attention warmup under PP>1.

## Claims

Fix a deadlock that occurs when one PP rank contains only Flashinfer attention groups while another PP rank contains a mix of Flashinfer and non-Flashinfer attention groups.

Most commonly affects models with dflash / dspark drafters on Blackwell, where Flashsinfer is often the default attention backend for the target model.

## Validation

Ran on B200:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":2,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

On this PR, we get
```
INFO:     Started server process [771742]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

On main, we get stuck after
```
EngineCore pid=813035) INFO 10-28 17:46:40 [shm_broadcast.py:878] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work (e.g. compilation, weight/kv cache quantization).
(EngineCore pid=813035) INFO 10-28 17:47:40 [shm_broadcast.py:878] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work (e.g. compilation, weight/kv cache quantization).
```

`--enforce-eager` doesn't resolve this because Flashinfer attention warmup is run regardless of enforce eager and compilation mode.

`--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` doesn't resolve this because it controls Flashinfer autotuning, not Flashinfer attention warmup.

```
pytest -v -s \
  tests/model_executor/test_attention_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py

99 passed, 2 warnings
```

## Details

During `kernel_warmup`, we may call `mixed_batch_attention_warmup` to run "a mixed prefill+decode batch to warm up both attention paths".

This is currently gated under "all attention groups use the Flashinfer backend" because hybrid attention backends may not support the dummy run.

With spec decode, the drafter may choose a different attention backend than the target model. Since the drafter is present on the last PP rank only, different ranks will disagree on whether they should participate in the Flashinfer warmup, causing deadlock.

The current fix synchronizes across PP ranks and only runs the Flashinfer attention warmup if all ranks agree. In effect, warmup behavior is consistent between PP=1 and PP>1.

Related:
- #60791 tracks issues with MiniMax-M3. Item 8 lists "PP where stages differ in running the M3 attention warmup". M3 warmup also uses `mixed_batch_attention_warmup` but it's separate from Flashinfer warmup.

title: [CI] Bump pre-commit hooks (except ruff)

body:

## Overview

Bumps the pre-commit hooks to their latest releases, except ruff, and pins every hook by commit SHA with a version comment. Supersedes #42618.

## Claims

- Hook bumps: typos v1.43.5 → v1.51.1, clang-format v21.1.2 → v23.1.3, markdownlint-cli2 v0.21.0 → v0.24.0, actionlint v1.7.7 → v1.7.12, shellcheck-py v0.11.0.1 → v0.11.0.1-1, uv-pre-commit 0.11.1 → 0.13.6.

- `pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` passes locally on every changed hook. The mypy and `test-nonroot-entrypoint` hooks fail locally for macOS-only reasons, but both are unchanged by this PR.

title: [Model Loader] Direct reload: reset MoE expert padding at begin
author: hao-aaron
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

At the start of a direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336), zero MoE expert padding, so that post-load processing reruns over the same bytes as a cold start. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477).

MoE expert parameters are often larger than the checkpoint tensors loaded into them: DeepEP rounds the hidden size up, MXFP4 / TRT-LLM / AITER backends round the intermediate size, and block-aligned FP8 TP pads shards. Loaders copy only the checkpoint part. On a direct reload the padding then holds the previous post-processed bytes, which post-load processing processes again. After a `load_format=dummy` cold start (the usual RL setup) it holds random values.

## Claims

- **gpt-oss-20b (TP2, MXFP4), direct reload through IPC weight transfer:** every tensor is bit-identical to a fresh start, both after 3 same-weight syncs and after a dummy start plus one sync. On main, 168 expert tensors differ after every sync and drift from one sync to the next. After a dummy start, 288 differ and GSM8K drops about 2 points.
- Cold start and layerwise reload are unchanged.
- No loader changes: whether to fill is decided from `moe_config` when the checkpoint layout is recorded at cold start, so it also covers dummy and other cold starts that skip loaders, and the load plan (#64418) that bypasses them.

## Validation

**This PR's head (`1e25cc87e2`) with #66010 (`84ab98b6d8`) applied, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 1319 questions, 3 updates; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with Python files overlaid). Differing expert parameters are 0 on every rank after every update. Jobs 45934, 45935.

| Sleep | Start | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 | Differing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 2 | Real | 0.9090 → 0.8984 → 0.9007 | 0 / 160 |
| | Dummy | — → 0.8999 → 0.9007 | 0 / 160 |
| None | Real | 0.9007 → 0.8969 → 0.9022 | 0 / 160 |
| | Dummy | — → 0.9060 → 0.9037 | 0 / 160 |

**Layerwise reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise`, the default).** `materialize_meta_tensor` now zeroes the tensor it allocates, because loaders write only checkpoint regions and padding otherwise keeps uninitialized memory. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, no sleep, 1319 questions, on main `5c97556318` with and without that one line. Jobs 46042, 46043.

| Arm | Differing after updates 1 / 2 / 3 | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 160 / 160 / 160 | 0.9037 → 0.0 → 0.0 |
| With the zero fill | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8954 → 0.9007 → 0.9030 |

`test_padded_moe_reload_releases_each_layer` fails 8 of 16 cases without the line.

**main vs this PR, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, reload from disk, no sleep mode; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with each arm's Python files overlaid, PR at e6403484fc; later commits change a comment and a CI trigger and merge main). "Differing" counts expert parameters per rank, out of 160, against a real cold start on the same arm. GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions. Jobs 45840, 45841.

| Start | Arm | Differing after updates 1 / 2 / 3 | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real | main | 120 / 120 / 120 | 0.9052 → 0.9105 → 0.8984 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9014 → 0.9067 → 0.9075 |
| Dummy | main | 160 / 160 / 160 | — → 0.8787 → 0.8400 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | — → 0.8976 → 0.8999 |

On main after a dummy start the padding is random and GSM8K keeps falling across updates. Run-to-run noise on the real cold start is up to 1.5 points, so the real-start GSM8K rows don't separate the arms; the tensor counts do.

**Earlier revision.** The tables below ran before the fill became zero-only (it then kept block scales at 1).

**End to end** (GB200, nightly wheel 81a2879403 with each arm's Python files overlaid, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, real IPC weight transfer). "Differing" means device tensors (registered and reachable from module attributes) whose digest differs from a fresh real start; GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions. The PR ran at 5b3856b564; later commits change only tests.

| Model (TP, MoE backend) | Arm | Real start + 3 syncs: differing | GSM8K | Dummy start + 1 sync: differing | GSM8K |

| gpt-oss-20b (TP2, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16`) | main | 168 / 168 / 168 | 0.9030 | 288 | 0.8825 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9022 | 0 | 0.8969 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`, intermediate 576 → 640; NCCL, trainer on a second node) | main | 120 / 120 / 120 per rank | 0.9022 | 160 per rank (MoE)† | — |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9045 | 0 (MoE)† | — |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 (TP4, FlashInfer TRT-LLM, intermediate 192 → 256) | main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8961 | 0 | 0.8878 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8939 | 0 | 0.8961 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (TP4, Triton, block-aligned TP) | main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9075 | 1152* | 0.8992 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9037 | 1152* | 0.9007 |

- On main, the gpt-oss tensors that differ are expert biases and scales after real-start syncs, and all six expert parameters after a dummy start.
- The two Qwen3 configs are already correct on main: `_zero_intermediate_padding` and the block-aligned TP loader fill rewrite their padding on every load. They show the change does no harm.
- \* Attention KV-cache scales the checkpoint doesn't contain keep their random dummy values. This happens on both arms and isn't MoE padding; it's fixed separately (KV-scale `dummy_weight_value`).
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: on main the 120 tensors per rank are `w13_weight`, `w13_weight_scale` and `w2_weight_scale` of all 40 MoE layers, and their bytes change on every sync; after a dummy start `w2_weight` differs too. PR 3 ran at b5130fff61, main at e5d9bad98e. † The Engram embedding tables (about 203 GB, tensors of ~98 GB) can't be sent through the transfer path, so after a dummy start they keep dummy values in both arms and GSM8K isn't meaningful there; they are the only tensors that differ on this PR.
- Jobs: 44520, 44529 (gpt-oss); 44521 (BF16); 44522, 44530 (FP8); 45005, 45002 (DeepSeek-V4.1).

**Cold-start A/B** (A = main 81a2879403, B = this PR a096f3f138, same nightly wheel, same node, arms back to back). GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1319 questions; throughput from `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64.

| Model (GB200, TP) | GSM8K A → B | Output tok/s A → B | KV cache A → B |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4, chat GSM8K (TP2) | 0.8886 → 0.8976 | 14390 → 14727 | 7.259M → 7.259M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 (TP4; intermediate 192 → 256) | 0.8946 → 0.8893 | 9230 → 9444 | 6.791M → 6.791M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 block (TP4) | 0.9045 → 0.9083 | 7269 → 7098 | 7.274M → 7.274M |

All within noise: GSM8K within 1 point, throughput within 2.4% in both directions, KV cache identical. At cold start this PR only records the fill list (jobs 44551–44553).

**Unit tests** (GB200, job 44519):
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py::test_direct_reload_after_dummy_start_resets_padding[block|static]` builds a real fp8 `RoutedExperts` with intermediate 256 → 384, fills every parameter with 7 instead of loading, records, then begins and loads. It checks that the result equals a zero-initialized load, that per-expert scalars and `e_score_correction_bias` are left alone, and that the record made at cold start decides the fill.
- `test_fp8_tp_loading.py` and `test_direct_reload.py` and `test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py` on the final code: 153 passed (GB200 job 23710). Earlier, `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py` and `test_reload.py -k padded` (layerwise) also passed.

## Details

**Design.**
- `RoutedExperts.padding_fill_params()` applies when `moe_config` shows the hidden size or the per-partition intermediate size rounded up past its unpadded value, or block-aligned TP sharding.
- It returns the layer's parameters minus per-expert scalars: a parameter is filled if it has more than two values per expert. So per-tensor and static input scales, which may be absent from the checkpoint, are kept.
- `record_checkpoint_layout` stores `(module, name)` at cold start, before post-load processing. Some post-load processing pads only the runtime copy and writes the padded size back into `moe_config`, so the decision must not be made later.
- `begin_direct_reload` looks up each name after the view-back, skips parameters post-load processing has dropped, and zero-fills the rest whole. Loaders then overwrite every checkpoint region.

**Requirement.** The fill erases the checkpoint region too, so every checkpoint tensor loaded into these parameters must be resent on every update. The direct delivery contract in `direct.py` says so; the completeness check (F2 in #54477) will enforce it.

**Padding value.** Everything is filled with 0. A padding-only scale block only multiplies weights the same fill zeroes, so its value doesn't change the output. MXFP4 (DeepSeek-V4.1, gpt-oss) and NVFP4 scales are created as zeros or empty, so 0 also matches a cold start. Block-aligned TP padding is rewritten by its loader after the fill, with scales at 1. Weights created with `torch.empty` had uninitialised padding at cold start; they get 0 here.

**`moe_config` is the source today, not the only possible one.** A layer padded some other way implements `padding_fill_params()` and reuses the same fill.

**Not changed.** Layerwise reload, the block-aligned TP loader fill, and `_zero_intermediate_padding` (cold start still needs it, since those weights are `torch.empty`).

**History.** This replaces this PR's earlier design, where loaders recorded the padding regions on every load and `fill_padding` wrote them before post-load processing. That design worked with layerwise reload and partial updates. Under the decision to require full updates and to drop layerwise reload (#54477), the fill at begin is much smaller and needs no loader changes. The streamed gpt-oss MXFP4 TP split moved to #65353, and Inkling AMD's padding (#64690) is covered by this fill.

title: [Spec Decode] Batch-sharded draft logits refactor
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
## Context

#63554 sharded the draft logits cache under batch-sharded sampling, assigning each request to a rank by its persistent slot: owner `req_state_idx % tp_size`, row `req_state_idx // tp_size`. That ties per-rank load to how the slot allocator happens to spread requests, and it gives each rank a varying number of requests per step. The DSpark follow-up (sharding the sequential Markov block) needs per-rank shapes that are fixed for a given batch size, so it can be CUDA-graph captured.

## This PR

This PR refactors how requests are assigned to ranks, and moves the sharding logic into one object.

**Ownership by batch position.** Every draft step gives the request at batch position `i` to rank `i % tp_size`, at row `i // tp_size` of that rank's cache (`DraftLogitsCache.assign`, called from `DraftModelSpeculator.prepare_propose`). Each rank holds at most `cdiv(num_reqs, tp_size)` requests, however the slots are spread. Verification runs each request on the rank that cached its drafts, via `DraftLogitsCache.owners_of`, which `BatchSharder` uses.

**Reused rows.** Rows are reassigned every step, so a request that the scheduler skips can find its row overwritten. `inverse_row_mapping` records which request last wrote each row. `DraftLogitsCache.stale_drafts` (a Triton kernel) marks drafts whose row has since changed hands, and `RejectionSampler` routes them through the existing invalid-drafts path, so verification resamples from the target. This is lossless: only that step's acceptance drops. **Note that this staleness only affects batch-sharded draft logits.**

**`DraftLogitsCache`** (new, `spec_decode/draft_logits.py`) owns the cache and its mappings:
- `values`: `[num_rows, num_steps, vocab]`;
- `row_mapping`: request slot → row on this rank, or −1;
- `shard_mapping`: request slot → owning rank;
- `inverse_row_mapping`: row → request slot.

The speculator owns it, and `rejection_sample`, `gumbel_sample` and the DFlash2 candidate cache take it, or its `row_mapping`, instead of `num_shards`/`shard_idx` arguments. `draft_logits_row()` is the single lookup: −1 means "no row on this rank", and every writer masks on `row >= 0`. With a replicated cache, `row_mapping` is `None` and every path reduces to indexing by slot. The opt-in rules from #63554 and #64151 are unchanged: the speculator must support it, no draft watermarker, and PCP = 1.

**Balance:** I simulated TP4 with MRv2's LIFO slot allocator and measured the busiest rank's verification load relative to a perfect split.
- Steady load: both rules are within about 1% on average.
- While a burst of 256 requests drains (≤ 64 live), slot ownership averages 1.32× and hits 3.0× worst case. Batch-position ownership averages 1.00×, because it rebalances every step.

## Benchmarks

**Setup:**
- 4× GB200, TP4, `max_num_seqs=256`, probabilistic drafting, prefix caching off, natural EOS.
- 4 boots per pair, ordered base, shard, shard, base. "base" has `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` off; "shard" has it on (sharded verification plus the sharded draft logits cache).
- GSM8K: 1319 questions. t0 is temperature 0, one run per boot. t1 is temperature 1, 3 seeds per boot.
- SPEED-Bench: `low_entropy` subset, `throughput_2k` config, temperature 1. Acceptance is measured at c64.
- Latencies are medians.
- Measured on a pre-cleanup revision of this branch. Later changes are renames, docstrings and the rebase; the logic is unchanged.

### Accuracy and acceptance (base → shard)

| Target + draft | GSM8K t0 | GSM8K t1 | AL GSM8K t0 | AL GSM8K t1 | AL SPEED-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP (K=3) | 0.970 → 0.970 | 0.968 → 0.968 | 3.618 → 3.621 | 3.515 → 3.517 | 3.267 → 3.267 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash (K=7) | 0.970 → 0.969 | 0.965 → 0.965 | 5.492 → 5.500 | 4.985 → 4.973 | 3.894 → 3.920 |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 (K=7) | 0.964 → 0.963 | 0.960 → 0.960 | 6.164 → 6.157 | 5.890 → 5.893 | 3.646 → 3.649 |

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=5) with sharding on had GSM8K accuracy 0.900 at t0 and 0.809 at t1, with acceptance 3.539 and 3.308. That matches the shard numbers in #63554 (0.906 / 0.807 and 3.540 / 3.283).

### Speed, sharding on vs off (median ITL, output tok/s)

| Target + draft | ITL c8 | ITL c64 | ITL c256 | tok/s c64 | tok/s c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP | +2.1% | −5.1% | −8.6% | +3.3% | +6.0% |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash | +15.4% | −7.6% | −9.5% | +4.0% | +5.5% |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 | +0.8% | −8.4% | −9.8% | +4.7% | +7.4% |

### Memory, sharding on vs off (from startup logs)

The KV cache gains match #63554: the cache still holds `cdiv(max_num_seqs, tp_size)` rows per rank.

| Target + draft | KV cache memory | KV cache tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP | 150.69 → 150.95 GiB | +0.17% |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash | 145.77 → 146.39 GiB | +0.43% |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 | 147.07 → 148.31 GiB | +0.85% |

### Notes

- **c8 cost with sharding on.** At c8, step time is bound by rank 0's host work. Per-rank host timers on DFlash at c8 show +1.7 ms of host time per step with sharding on: shard plan 0.35 ms, output gather 0.29 ms, stale-drafts/assign launches about 0.2 ms, and about 0.85 ms not yet attributed. GPU work per step is unchanged. Most of this comes from batch-sharded sampling itself, which already exists on main. The main vs this PR table separates out this PR's share.
- **Not a duplicate.** This refactors the ownership scheme from #63554 and builds on #64151. No other open PR touches this code.

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py \
  tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py
# 499 passed
```

title: [Model Loader] Run the model-level post-load hook once at the end of every load and reload
author: hao-aaron
body:
Thanks to Tony Wang (@new-TonyWang) for design and review contributions.

PR 1 of the direct weight reload stack (RFC #54477). It replaces #57733. The code is the same, plus the Llama4 DP-vision fix that #57733 dropped when it was narrowed.

## Problem

RL weight updates do not load a model in one `load_weights` call. The weight-transfer engines (NCCL, IPC, M2N, sharded RDT) and `reload_weights` call it once per bucket, or once per tensor, between `initialize_layerwise_reload` and `finalize_layerwise_reload`. On main, three things go wrong with that:

1. **The model-level hook never runs after a reload.** `finalize_layerwise_reload` only finishes the layers. The model's `process_weights_after_loading()` runs only from the cold-load path. So any state a model derives from its weights in that hook, such as fused buffers or broadcast copies, keeps the old weights' values after an update.
2. **Some models do that work inside `load_weights` instead.** It then runs once per bucket, on partial weights. Under layerwise reload it runs while the layers are still on meta, which fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor`. This affects DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, the DFlash/DSpark drafters and Muse Spark.
3. **Checks on "what this call loaded" fire on every bucket.** A bucket that happens not to contain a layer or head raises "MTP layer N weights missing", or silently sets the DSpark `confidence_head` to `None`.

## Fix

- **One finish step.** New `finalize_model_weights(model)` calls the model's `process_weights_after_loading()`. It is called once at the end of a cold load (as before, after per-layer quant processing) and once at the end of every `finalize_layerwise_reload`. That covers `reload_weights` and the NCCL, IPC, M2N and sharded-RDT engines.
  - The sparse NCCL engine patches weights in place without layerwise reload; its `finish_weight_update` now calls `finalize_model_weights` once.
  - An M2N update whose plan is all direct does not call `finalize_layerwise_reload`, so it still skips the hook, as on main.
  - The torchao reload decorator and the expert-substitution error path finish the layers in the middle of a load. They now call `finalize_layerwise_processing`, so they do not run the model hook early.
- **Post-load work moves from `load_weights` into the hook.** Each `load_weights` below now only loads, and the hook runs at the end:
  - DeepSeek-V4 NVIDIA, V4.1 NVIDIA/AMD: the mHC broadcast (V4.1 AMD's `finalize_mega_moe_weights` is a no-op).
  - DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA: the Engram checkpoint page-cache drop and THP collapse. They now also run after every reload and after dummy loads; both are harmless to repeat.
  - DeepSeek-V4 XPU target, MTP and DSpark: `finalize_mega_moe_weights`. The lazy call in MegaMoE `forward()` is removed, since dummy loads run the hook too.
  - Qwen3 DFlash / Qwen3 DSpark / Gemma4 DSpark / Muse Spark DSpark: `_build_fused_kv_buffers`.
    - The hook now runs after quant processing.
    - In Qwen3 DFlash/DSpark and Gemma4 DSpark, the fused path that reads `.weight` directly is used only when the projections are unquantized and not CPU-repacked (`_reads_raw_weights`). Otherwise each projection runs through its quant method.
    - Muse Spark DSpark still slices `qkv_proj.weight` directly, now after quant processing, so a quantized or CPU-repacked Muse Spark drafter would read kernel-layout weights.
    - Qwen3 DFlash's MXFP8 context K/V projection copied the K/V rows of each layer's QKV weight and scales, which is only valid before quant processing. It is now created at construction and loaded from the checkpoint's K/V tensors as they stream through `load_weights`, so its own post-load step runs and a reload refills it in place.
  - Muse Spark AMD and Muse Spark DSpark: `materialize_residual_path_constants`.
- **The DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL wrappers drop their workaround.** They had reordered the weight stream so that the language model's in-`load_weights` finalization saw all its weights (`stream_language_model_first`, `finalizes_weights_during_load`, `_weights_finalized`). That is no longer needed and is removed.
- **"Complete load" checks are gated on `is_mtp_completeness_check_enabled()`**, which the weight-transfer engines turn off during an update:
  - The MTP layer checks in DeepSeek-V3.2 AMD, GLM5-next and Kimi-K3 (AMD/NVIDIA).
  - The DSpark `confidence_head` drop in Qwen3, Gemma4 and DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 (NVIDIA/AMD).
  - The Qwen3 DSpark vocab checks.
  - `AutoWeightsLoader._check_skipped_aliases`.
- **dots3 vision: the block compile runs once.** The vision hook now reruns after every reload, and main's `compile_block_modules` would wrap the blocks in another `torch.compile` each time. It now compiles in place with `Module.compile` (parameter names keep no `_orig_mod`) and only once. The vision MoE is unchanged from main: its hook fuses the experts into FP8 once, deletes the checkpoint experts and returns early afterwards, so a reload leaves the vision experts as they are.
- **Llama4 DP vision (`mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`).**
  - Before: the vision attention used `ReplicatedLinear`, and `load_weights` gathered `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` and called `torch.cat` once all three had arrived. An update that sends them in separate calls failed on `torch.cat` of `None`.
  - Now: it uses `QKVParallelLinear` / `RowParallelLinear` with `disable_tp=True` in DP mode, so q/k/v go through the normal stacked mapping and each part is written into its rows as it arrives. `_consolidate_qkv_weights` is removed.
- **Raw Tensorizer loads use the shared loader path.** Loading a non-vLLM-tensorized checkpoint used its own `_load_model_serialized_cpu`, which ran the model hook but skipped per-layer `process_weights_after_loading`. It now goes through `BaseModelLoader.load_model`.

## Not in this PR

- **Weights combined from several checkpoint tensors inside `load_weights`.** A weight plus its scale, or a fused FP8 qkv, still need every part in the same call, as on main:
  - the FP8 indexer `wk` dequant;
  - GLM5-next MLA projections;
  - MiMo-V2 fused qkv;
  - Molmo/Molmo2 split embedding.

  These are later PRs in the stack (PR 6).
- **Drafters that still finish inside `load_weights`, unchanged from main:**
  - LiLiCorr: the coverage check and `materialize_inference_buffers`.
  - Laguna DFlash: the fused KV build.
  - Qwen3 XPress: the `mix.L` check, `fold_from_raw_` and the fused buffers. It also inherits the new DFlash hook, so at cold start its fused KV buffers are built twice, the second time after quant processing.

  A bucketed update of these drafters behaves as on main. LiLiCorr and Laguna are in the F9 follow-up.
- **Hooks that are not safe to rerun.** Every model-level hook reachable from a top-level model was checked for a second run on reloaded weights. These are not fixed here:
  - **DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm (model, MTP, DSpark): a reload now fails instead of leaving wrong weights.**
    - On main this hook ran only at cold start, so a reload left the mega-MoE experts and the preshuffled attention and gate/up weights unshuffled or stale.
    - With this PR it reruns at the end of a reload. With `fuse_shared_expert`, the first run sets `shared_experts = None` (`finalize_mega_moe_weights`), so the second run raises `AttributeError` in `load_shared_expert`.
    - Without it, the mega-MoE `finalize_weights` returns early (stale experts), and `prepare_attn_preshuffle` / `prepare_gateup_preshuffle` shuffle in place again, so layers that the update did not resend are shuffled twice.
  - **dots3 vision MoE: stale, as on main.** Making it reloadable without keeping the BF16 experts resident (about 11 GiB per GPU on dots3-note-prev-fp8 TP4) needs a loader that quantizes each expert into the fused FP8 buffers as it arrives; that is a follow-up.
  - **Muse Spark NVIDIA: stale, as on main.** The router multiplier is folded once and then dropped, and the mega-MoE `finalize_weights` returns early after dropping `w13_weight`.
  - **DeepSeek-V4 XPU mega-MoE: guarded, as on main.** `finalize_weights` returns early once the weights are transformed. The XPU runtime currently rejects mega-MoE, so the hook is a no-op.
  - **Rebuilt as new tensors.** Kimi-K3 AMD's MLA `_w_fold` and Muse Spark's residual `alpha`/`beta` are re-created by the hook, so a captured CUDA graph keeps reading the old ones.
    - On main Kimi-K3's hook did not run on reload, and Muse Spark rebuilt them the same way from `load_weights`, so neither is worse than main.
    - The DFlash/DSpark (Qwen3, Gemma4, Muse Spark) and Beam DFlash2 context K/V buffers, and Kimi-K3 NVIDIA DSpark's `_context_kv_norm_weights`, are also re-created. The V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads the context K/V buffers, so after a reload it reads freed memory and draft acceptance drops (Beam DFlash2 TP4, split reload: 7.03 → 4.89; MiniMax-M3.1 MXFP8 DSpark TP4: 5.70 → 4.07). Outputs stay correct because the target verifies the drafts. Writing these buffers back in place is PR 5 (`refill_derived`); with it, acceptance after the reload matches the cold start.

## Tests

- Unit tests:
  - `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::TestModelHookOnSplitLoad`: the model hook runs once, after all weights, for a layerwise reload split into two buckets, a partial layerwise update, and a sparse NCCL update in two chunks.
  - `tests/models/test_qwen3_dflash_mxfp8_context_kv.py`: the MXFP8 context projection matches the QKV projection, following the real load order (post-load steps, then the context buffers).
  - `test_expert_substitution.py`: updated for the Tensorizer path.
  - `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl.py`: replaces `test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py` and `test_deepseek_v4_vl_rocm.py`. It checks that the VL wrappers leave finalization to the hook.
  - `test_tensorizer.py::test_deserialized_hf_weights_are_ready_for_forward`.
- Run on GB200 (slurm 41251), nightly `dc45a5f552` (this PR's merge base) with this branch at `4df1d673d` overlaid:
  - Passed: `test_reload.py::TestModelHookOnSplitLoad` 2, `test_qwen3_dflash_mxfp8_context_kv.py` 6, `test_deepseek_v4_vl.py` 3, `test_expert_substitution.py` 13.
  - `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py`: 33 passed after `7e0898bdc` (its coverage test builds the model without `__init__` and needed `_context_kv_proj`).
  - `test_tensorizer.py::test_deserialized_hf_weights_are_ready_for_forward` was not run here: the venv has no `tensorizer` package.
- End to end, Llama-4-Scout BF16 (RedHatAI mirror) on GB200, slurm 41251 (same build):
  - Setup: TP=4, `mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`, prefix caching off.
  - The vision q/k/v are reloaded in separate `load_weights` calls in v, k, q order, through `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`.
  - main fails with `expected Tensor as element 0 ... got NoneType` (the `torch.cat` in `_consolidate_qkv_weights`).
  - This PR: 1047/1047 tensors byte-identical to cold start, and the greedy image+text sample is identical before and after the reload.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark on GB200, head `0403d305a`, nightly `dbcf568821` with this branch overlaid:
  - **Cold start with the DSpark drafter** (slurm 40659): TP=4, 7 speculative tokens, GSM8K 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy.

    | | GSM8K | draft acceptance |
    |---|---|---|
    | main | 0.9477 | 0.4938 |
    | this PR | 0.9484 | 0.4938 |

  - **Weight update through NCCL** (slurm 40658), with the [sharded-trainer benchmark](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm-state-transition-verifier/tree/sharded-trainer-bench/scripts/vllm_weight_update_client/bench):
    - Setup: server TP=2, trainer `fsdp=2`, layerwise reload, 2 syncs of a checkpoint in which every tensor changes.
    - The audit compares every device tensor with a fresh server on that checkpoint.
    - main: the update fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor` (the post-load step inside `load_weights`).
    - This PR: 3440 tensors compared, 0 mismatched, no memory growth.
    - 86 derived tensors are reallocated: MoE kernel scale configs and permute caches, `gemm1_clamp_limit`, `tid2eid`, the RoPE cache and `topk_indices_buffer`. These are rebuilt by layerwise reload's per-layer processing, not by this PR's hook; keeping their addresses is the job of direct reload (#58382).
- Cold-start A/B against the same nightly, on GB300, H200 and MI355X ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64357#issuecomment-6512153023)): DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3-8B + DFlash, Llama-4-Scout FP8 with DP vision, dots3-note-prev-fp8 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash on MI355X. GSM8K, image accuracy, DFlash acceptance length, throughput and KV cache size match within run-to-run noise. The dots3 KV cache loss it found came from the earlier dots3 vision MoE change, which is reverted here.
- Not covered: DeepSeek-V4.1 reload (needs two nodes), the drafter weights during an update (the benchmark updates only the target), Muse Spark, dots3 reload, XPU and ROCm reload.

title: [Spec Decode][ROCm] draft_lm_head_quantization for DSpark drafters
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This lets the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 DSpark drafters use `draft_lm_head_quantization` (#59973), which so far was limited to EAGLE and MTP. A drafter that shares the target `lm_head` then computes its base logits through a private FP8 or NVFP4 copy of that head, while the target keeps verifying with its own BF16 head. It is the vLLM counterpart of sgl-project/sglang#39622.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --speculative-config \
  '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"}'
```

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, AgentX, `"fp8"`: ITL P50 is 4.0% lower at TP2 c1 and 2.4% lower at TP4 c1. A trace shows the draft-head GEMM going from 348 µs to 60 µs per step. From c8 up the result is neutral within noise.
- Acceptance length and GSM8K are unchanged within run-to-run noise, because the target still verifies with its own head.
- No new mechanism: the sharing logic EAGLE and DSpark had in common is now one helper, `share_target_lm_head`, and DSpark opts in through `DSparkSpeculatorConfig.supported_options`. Off by default.

## Validation

All runs: MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03` (the same vLLM commit as this PR's base) with the changed files mounted, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, InferenceX recipe `dsv41flash/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml` (DSpark k=5, probabilistic drafting, `--monokernel`). The only difference between arms is `"draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"`.

**AgentX** (InferenceX `infx.bench agentic`, golden synthetic AL 3.51, 900 s, fresh server per point, one run per point). ITL P50 in ms, BF16 head -> FP8 head:

| | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 | c16 | c32 | c64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP2 | 1.89 -> 1.81 (**-4.0%**) | 1.90 -> 1.81 (-4.9%) | 1.95 -> 1.86 (-4.5%) | 2.26 -> 2.24 (-0.7%) | 3.13 -> 3.11 (-0.5%) | 4.67 -> 4.69 (+0.4%) | 9.42 -> 9.35 (-0.8%) |
| TP4 | 1.56 -> 1.52 (**-2.4%**) | 1.57 -> 1.52 (-2.9%) | | | | | |

The c1 numbers match the trace below. At c2 and c4 the trace accounts for only about 0.5% (44 µs per step at c4), so most of the improvement measured at those points is run-to-run variance.

**Draft-head kernel per decode step** (torch profiler, TP2, rank 0, 60 steps). The draft-head GEMM is swapped one for one, and the target verify head (`Cijk_..._BBS`, about 104 µs) is untouched:

| | BF16 head | FP8 head |
|---|---|---|
| c1 (M=5) | `wvSplitK_hf_sml` 347.8 µs | `Cijk_..._F8BS` 54.6 µs + per-token quant 5.0 µs |
| c4 (M=20) | `Cijk_..._BBS` 104.5 µs | `Cijk_..._F8BS` 55.8 µs + per-token quant 5.0 µs |

**Acceptance and accuracy** (TP2, `rejection_sample_method: block`):

| | BF16 head | FP8 head |
|---|---|---|
| AL, AgentX traces at c8 (from `vllm:spec_decode_*` counter deltas, about 112k drafts each) | 3.416 | 3.400 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319, greedy, 2 runs | 0.909 / 0.913 | 0.904 / 0.914 |

**Tests** (MI355X, rebased branch): `pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py`: 54 passed, 4 skipped (the NVFP4 cases, which are CUDA-only). `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_lm_head_quantization`, which exercises the refactored EAGLE/MTP path with `"fp8"`: passed. `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main`, including mypy: passed.

<details>
<summary>Full AgentX table, draft-head microbenchmark, run notes</summary>

| TP | conc | ITL mean/P50/P90 (ms) | output tok/s/GPU | TTFT mean (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | 1.99/1.89/2.27 -> 1.92/1.81/2.26 | 78.6 -> 80.4 | 247 -> 242 |
| 2 | 2 | 2.02/1.90/2.30 -> 1.93/1.81/2.27 | 109.7 -> 109.2 | 249 -> 252 |
| 2 | 4 | 2.28/1.95/2.97 -> 2.11/1.86/2.41 | 137.6 -> 143.8 | 152 -> 140 |
| 2 | 8 | 2.50/2.26/3.64 -> 2.49/2.24/3.47 | 215.6 -> 212.9 | 140 -> 148 |
| 2 | 16 | 3.12/3.13/3.78 -> 3.17/3.11/3.78 | 336.3 -> 336.6 | 2030 -> 1999 |
| 2 | 32 | 5.03/4.67/6.02 -> 5.25/4.69/5.89 | 659.8 -> 661.8 | 6485 -> 6527 |
| 2 | 64 | 10.25/9.42/14.29 -> 10.05/9.35/14.19 | 1120.4 -> 1134.2 | 315 -> 321 |
| 4 | 1 | 1.61/1.56/1.80 -> 1.58/1.52/1.80 | 44.7 -> 44.9 | 189 -> 193 |
| 4 | 2 | 1.62/1.57/1.80 -> 1.60/1.52/1.81 | 56.6 -> 59.3 | 191 -> 207 |

At each TP2 point both arms ran at the same time on GPU pairs {2,3} and {4,5}, swapping pairs every point. The TP4 points ran one arm at a time on the same four GPUs. AgentX replays paced traces, so at low concurrency the arms serve different request mixes and token throughput follows that mix. ITL is the speed metric.

Draft-head GEMM alone (`ParallelLMHead` against `quantized_lm_head_copy`, CUDA-graph replay), in µs:

```
TP2 64640 x 5120   M=5    M=10   M=20   M=40   M=80   M=160  M=320
BF16               352.4  96.7   99.4   101.4  107.0  124.2  185.0
FP8                57.0   56.7   57.2   59.0   63.3   71.4   171.6
TP4 32320 x 5120
BF16               183.9  60.5   55.5   59.9   71.7   73.8   136.9
FP8                33.7   33.7   32.3   38.3   38.2   49.2   63.2
```

</details>

## Details

- **Changes**:
  - `share_target_lm_head` in `eagle/utils.py`, next to `_should_share`, installs the target head or its quantized copy, raises if quantization was requested but the drafter keeps its own head, and returns the installed head. `load_eagle_model` uses the returned head for the MTP `shared_head` fixup. `load_dspark_model` passes its vocab-size check as `can_share`. `load_dflash_model` can adopt it with `quantization=None` in a follow-up.
  - `DSparkSpeculatorConfig` accepts `draft_lm_head_quantization` only for `DSparkDraftModel` and `DSparkV41DraftModel`. Other DSpark drafters may read `lm_head.weight` directly: Muse Spark casts its activations to the head's dtype, which would be FP8 for a quantized copy. They are rejected during config validation, before the target loads. EAGLE's `head_dtype` check is shared through `check_draft_lm_head_quantization`.
  - Weight reload and weight transfer already refresh the copy, because `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` and `share_source_lm_heads` run on any `DraftModelSpeculator`.
- **Not a duplicate of #47584**: that PR adds a separate env var (`VLLM_DSPARK_FP8_DRAFT_HEAD`) and a new rowwise FP8 module, for the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4 DSpark path only. This PR reuses the existing `draft_lm_head_quantization` config and kernel selection, so it works on any platform with an FP8 linear kernel.
- **Kernel on ROCm**: `"fp8"` resolves to `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` (hipBLASLt FP8 `_scaled_mm`).
- **Why c1 benefits most**: at M=5 (one request, five drafts) the BF16 dispatch picks `wvSplitK`, which is about 3.5x slower than at M=10. `deepseek_v41/amd/ops/draft_lm_head.py` already pads around that, but only on gfx942. A lossless fix to that dispatch is a separate follow-up.
- **Memory**: one extra FP8 copy of the per-rank head shard, about 0.33 GB at TP2 and 0.17 GB at TP4 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. It is created during model loading, so KV sizing accounts for it.
- **CI coverage**: the quantized copy and its refresh are covered by the existing `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py`. The shared EAGLE/MTP path is covered by the MTP e2e test above. The DSpark path is validated end to end above. CI has no DSpark checkpoint test for it. `"nvfp4"` takes the same path but was not measured here.

title: [ROCm][Quantization] NVFP4 MoE re-quantization and fused shared experts through online quantization
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

Second PR of the split of #63232, stacked on #64111. Its base is `minimax-m31-flash-model`, so only this PR's commit shows up; it will be retargeted to `main` after #64111 merges. The change lets ROCm serve NVFP4-expert checkpoints such as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: the routed experts are re-quantized to MXFP4/MXFP8 at load. It also makes fused shared experts (FSE) work with online quantization.

## Claims

- **NVFP4 MoE re-quantization without an NVFP4 backend:** main can already re-quantize serialized NVFP4 MoE (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark) to an online MoE method. This PR makes that work where no NVFP4 MoE backend exists (ROCm):
  - The NVFP4 oracle skips backend selection for layers whose checkpoint method only serves as the dequantization source (`requantization_source_scope`).
  - `dequantize_weight` for MoE now yields `(experts, w13, w2)` per group of experts, which bounds the staging memory.
- **FSE with online quantization:** `OnlineSharedExpertLoader` stages the shared expert at load and quantizes it into its routed slot after loading. It replaces `RoutedExperts._fused_shared_expert_quantizer`, which only handled full-precision shared experts. Supported combinations:
  - NVFP4 routed experts re-quantized to MXFP4, with the shared expert re-quantized to the same scheme;
  - Quark MXFP4 routed experts (kept as stored) with an MXFP8 shared expert quantized to MXFP4 online.

  FSE is refused with a warning when the shared and routed experts would not run with the same `(weight, activation)` keys. Two cases raise `NotImplementedError`: BF16 routed experts quantized online combined with a quantized shared expert, and reloading weights with FSE.
- **MiniMax-M3 on ROCm:** a clear error for the NVFP4-expert checkpoint unless the routed experts are re-quantized (`--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` or `mxfp8`).
- **Two small ROCm fixes from the same branch:**
  - gfx942: the online FP8 PTPC MoE quantizes W13 in torch, because `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` can crash there during load.
  - The MXFP8 Triton activation quant uses a tuned block size for M == 1.

## Validation

Pre-commit passes, including mypy (Python 3.11) on all changed files.

Unit tests were run on GB300 (CUDA) for this branch and for #64111 (its base) in the same environment. The changed and new tests pass; the failures were identical on both branches (table below).

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py tests/quantization/test_fp8_per_channel.py \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_emulation.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py
```

| | this PR | #64111 |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 656 | 646 |
| skipped | 86 | 54 |
| failed | 27 | 27 (the same tests) |

- The 10 extra passes are this PR's new tests.
- The 32 extra skips are the ROCm-only tests in `test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py`.
- The 27 shared failures are environmental: engine start-up on GPUs shared with other jobs (about 10 GB free), a Triton "PTX compiled with an unsupported toolchain" error in this environment, and one out-of-memory error. Three `test_modelopt` failures also fail on `main` here.

Not covered:
- `tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` holds most of the coverage of this PR (NVFP4 routed × online targets × FSE for compressed-tensors and Quark, Quark MXFP4 routed + MXFP8 shared, NVFP4 oracle skip). It is ROCm-only, and its CI jobs are disabled (`tools/pre_commit/test_tethering_allowlist.txt`: pending locked torchao dependencies). I did not run it: there is no AMD hardware here.
- No ROCm end-to-end run on this branch. The code comes from the AMD contributors' branch (#63232).

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** #63547 (draft) also serves the NVFP4 M3.1 checkpoint on AMD, but converts NVFP4 → MXFP4 inside the model (`minimax_m3/common/nvfp4_mxfp4.py`). This PR goes through the generic online quantization API instead, so it applies to any ModelOpt, compressed-tensors or Quark NVFP4 MoE and supports FSE.
- **Shared code touched (all at load time, no forward-path change):**
  - `resolve_quant_method` builds the checkpoint method of re-quantized experts under `requantization_source_scope`.
  - `select_nvfp4_moe_backend` returns the emulation backend inside that scope.
  - `QuantizeMethodBase.dequantize_weight` returns an iterator for MoE. All three MoE implementations (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark NVFP4) and the one caller are migrated.
  - `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` and `load_weights` route shared-expert slots through the loader.
  - `process_weights_after_loading` finalizes the staged shared experts. It is a no-op unless FSE and online quantization are both used.
  - `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` now compares the effective `(weight, activation)` keys of the routed and shared experts.
  - `QuarkLinearMethod.dequantize_weight` supports MXFP8.
- **Conflicts with main:** main's #61457 (per-layer FSE selection) landed after the source branch. I kept main's `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert`. The source branch's extra warning, for `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` set without AITER MoE, was dropped: it also fires on CUDA, where AITER is unavailable.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/quantization/online.md` already documents NVFP4 MoE re-quantization; FSE with online quantization is not documented yet.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to port these changes from #63232 and resolve the conflicts with main. The original code is by fxmarty-amd (re-quantization + FSE), andyluo7 (gfx942 FP8) and hongxiayang (MXFP8 M=1), credited in the commit. The submitter reviewed the port and ran the tests above.
