title: [Kernel][DSA] Restore FP32 indexer MQA logits for non-DeepSeek models and add `indexer_logits_dtype`
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

Bump DeepGEMM to `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` tip `ae4fd25`. It restores FP32 output for `fp8_fp4_(paged_)mqa_logits` behind a `logits_dtype` argument (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#46) and fixes the mega_mhc CUDA-graph replay barrier (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#48). The tip also includes MegaMoE NVFP4 epilogue and BF16 weight-layout changes (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#51), which touch no MQA-logits kernel.

This PR also adds `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype` (`auto` default, `float32` or `bfloat16`) for the DSA sparse indexer. #61149 had forced BF16 indexer logits on SM100, because that DeepGEMM release dropped `logits_dtype`. `auto` restores FP32 for GLM-5, GLM-5.3 and HY-V4, and keeps DeepSeek-V3.2/V4/V4.1 on main's behaviour (BF16 on SM100).

## Claims

- New option `-ac.indexer_logits_dtype={auto,float32,bfloat16}`. It applies to every CUDA user of DeepGEMM's dense MQA-logits kernels:
  - the DSA sparse indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, HY-V4);
  - the GLM-5.3 kpool indexer;
  - the DeepSeek-V4.1 specialized decode indexer.
- **Per-model default (`auto`).** On SM100, GLM-5, GLM-5.3 and HY-V4 go back to FP32 logits, and DeepSeek-V3.2/V4/V4.1 keep main's BF16. Against an FP64 reference on GB300, FP32 logits select the exact top-2048. BF16 logits change 0.4–0.75% of the selected tokens.
  - The DeepSeek default is set in the `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` and `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMConfig` config hooks. GLM-5 runs the DeepSeek-V3.2 model class, so the default is keyed on the architecture name rather than on the layer.
  - Indexer models without a hook resolve `auto` to FP32. An explicit `float32` or `bfloat16` overrides the model default.
- **SM90/SM120 behaviour is unchanged by default**, for every model including DeepSeek. These architectures always produced FP32; `bfloat16` is now also available there.
- With the default top-k backend (`auto`), FP32 decode logits skip the `as_fp32_logits` upcast that main launches on SM100.
- `bfloat16` keeps main's current SM100 behaviour: BF16 head weights, BF16 reduction, and DeepSelect ranking BF16 logits directly.
- The sparse MQA-logits path (`indexer_sparse_logits`) is unchanged and always BF16.

## Validation

The unit tests and the logits table are from 1x GB300 (SM100 family) at the earlier pin `9918052`; `ae4fd25` changes only MegaMoE on top of it. The tests marked "at ae4fd25" and the GLM-5.3 eval ran on GB200 at the current pin.

**Unit tests.** `test_deepgemm_fp8_mqa_logits` and `test_deepgemm_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` are now parametrized over both logits dtypes and assert the output dtype.

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py                                  # 13 passed
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -k sparse_mqa_logits  # 22 passed
# at ae4fd25, GB200:
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py                                  # 13 passed
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k decode_chunk                                 # 13 passed
```

**Logits accuracy.** The script below runs both dtypes through vLLM's wrappers on random inputs (64 heads, head dim 128). It compares each against an FP64 reference computed on the same FP8-quantized inputs. Overlap is the fraction of each row's top-2048 tokens that match the FP64 top-2048. Time is the median `do_bench` µs in eager mode. The BF16 column includes the FP32 upcast that every non-DeepSelect top-k needs.

| Case | Rel. error FP32 / BF16 | Top-2048 overlap FP32 / BF16 | µs FP32 / BF16 + upcast |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 2048 q × 16K kv | 6.4e-8 / 4.8e-3 | 1.0000 / 0.9959 | 217 / 210 |
| prefill 4096 q × 64K kv | 6.3e-8 / 4.8e-3 | 1.0000 / 0.9929 | 1770 / 1645 |
| decode b=64, ctx 16K | 6.5e-8 / 4.9e-3 | 1.0000 / 0.9958 | 54 / 93 |
| decode b=8, ctx 64K | 6.7e-8 / 5.0e-3 | 1.0000 / 0.9925 | 49 / 92 |

- In prefill, BF16 is 3–7% faster even after the upcast.
- In decode, the gap is mostly the extra upcast launch; these timings are not CUDA-graphed. DeepSelect with BF16, which skips the upcast, was not timed.

**Per-model default.** `tests/models/test_indexer_logits_dtype_config.py` (CPU) resolves `auto` through each indexer architecture's config hook, on and off SM100, and checks that explicit values win: 30 passed.

**CLI.** `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype` defaults to `auto` and accepts `float32` or `bfloat16`; other values (e.g. `float16`) are rejected.

**E2E: GLM-5.3 GSM8K.** `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8), TP4 on 4x GB200, no MTP, at `afb1192fd7` with DeepGEMM `ae4fd25`. Run with `lm_eval` local-completions, 5-shot, on all 1319 questions.

```
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype {auto,bfloat16}
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
    --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=128,tokenized_requests=False
```

| `indexer_logits_dtype` | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` (FP32 for GLM) | 93.10 ± 0.70 | 93.03 ± 0.70 |
| `bfloat16` (main's SM100 behaviour) | 93.18 ± 0.69 | 93.03 ± 0.70 |

- The two settings are equal within noise.
- This was expected: GLM-5.3's indexer selects 2048 pools of 4 tokens (8K tokens), more than any GSM8K prompt, so top-k never drops a token. The eval confirms that both logits paths serve correctly, not that FP32 selects better tokens.
- Long-context MRCR, which exercises top-k selection, is still pending.

<details>
<summary>compare.py (logits accuracy / timing script)</summary>

```python
"""FP32 vs BF16 indexer logits through vLLM's DeepGEMM wrappers: error against
an fp64 reference on the same quantized inputs, top-k agreement, and rough
kernel timings (incl. the FP32 upcast the default top-k needs for BF16)."""

import torch
from triton.testing import do_bench

from vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer import as_fp32_logits
from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import (
    _ceil_to_ue8m0,
    fp8_fp4_mqa_logits,
    fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits,
    get_num_sms,
    get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata,
    mqa_logits_mx_inputs,
    mqa_logits_use_mx_scales,
)

torch.manual_seed(0)
H, D, TOPK = 64, 128, 2048
DTYPES = (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16)


def quant_k(k):
    sf = _ceil_to_ue8m0(k.abs().float().amax(-1, keepdim=True).clamp(1e-4) / 448.0)
    kq = (k / sf).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    return kq, sf.squeeze(-1)


def encode(sf):
    if not mqa_logits_use_mx_scales():
        return sf
    b = (sf.view(torch.int32) >> 23).to(torch.uint8)
    return b[..., None].repeat_interleave(4, -1).view(torch.int32)[..., 0]


def topk_overlap(a, b, valid):
    a = a.masked_fill(~valid, float("-inf")).topk(TOPK, -1).indices.sort(-1).values
    b = b.masked_fill(~valid, float("-inf")).topk(TOPK, -1).indices.sort(-1).values
    hits = [
        torch.isin(x, y).float().mean().item() for x, y in zip(a, b, strict=True)
    ]
    return sum(hits) / len(hits)


def prefill(seq_len, seq_len_kv):
    q = torch.randn(seq_len, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    k = torch.randn(seq_len_kv, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    w = torch.randn(seq_len, H, device="cuda") / H
    q8 = q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    k8, ksf = quant_k(k)
    rows = torch.arange(seq_len, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
    ks = torch.zeros_like(rows)
    ke = rows + (seq_len_kv - seq_len) + 1
    width = int((ke - ks).max())
    # fp64 reference on the dequantized inputs, compressed like the kernel
    # (ks == 0); row chunks bound the [rows, H, N] fp64 intermediate.
    kd = (k8.double() * ksf.double()[:, None])[:width]
    ref = torch.cat(
        [
            (
                torch.einsum("mhd,nd->mhn", q8[i : i + 256].double(), kd).relu()
                * w[i : i + 256].double()[..., None]
            ).sum(1)
            for i in range(0, seq_len, 256)
        ]
    )
    valid = torch.arange(width, device="cuda")[None] < (ke - ks)[:, None]
    out = {}
    for dt in DTYPES:
        qs, wk = mqa_logits_mx_inputs(q8, None, w, dt)

        def run(dt=dt, qs=qs, wk=wk):
            lg = fp8_fp4_mqa_logits(
                (q8, qs), (k8, encode(ksf)), wk, ks, ke, width, logits_dtype=dt
            )
            return as_fp32_logits(lg, ke - ks)

        lg = run()
        err = (lg.double() - ref).abs().masked_fill(~valid, 0)
        rel = (err.sum() / ref.abs().masked_fill(~valid, 0).sum()).item()
        out[dt] = (lg, rel, do_bench(run, warmup=25, rep=200))
    return out, ref, valid


def decode(batch, ctx, block=64):
    q = torch.randn(batch, 1, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    nblk = batch * ctx // block
    k = torch.randn(nblk, block, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    w = torch.randn(batch, H, device="cuda") / H
    q8 = q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    k8, ksf = quant_k(k)
    cache = torch.empty(nblk, block * (D + 4), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
    cache[:, : block * D] = k8.view(nblk, -1).view(torch.uint8)
    cache[:, block * D :] = encode(ksf).view(torch.uint8).view(nblk, -1)
    cache = cache.view(nblk, block, 1, D + 4)
    tables = torch.randperm(nblk, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).view(batch, -1)
    lens = torch.full((batch, 1), ctx, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
    idx = torch.arange(batch, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
    sched = get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(lens, block, get_num_sms(), indices=idx)
    kd = (k8.double() * ksf.double()[..., None])[tables.long()].view(batch, -1, D)
    ref = torch.einsum("bhd,bnd->bhn", q8[:, 0].double(), kd).relu()
    ref = (ref * w.double()[..., None]).sum(1)
    valid = torch.ones_like(ref, dtype=torch.bool)
    out = {}
    for dt in DTYPES:
        qs, wk = mqa_logits_mx_inputs(q8, None, w, dt)

        def run(dt=dt, qs=qs, wk=wk):
            lg = fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits(
                (q8, qs), cache, wk, lens, tables, sched, ctx,
                logits_dtype=dt, indices=idx,
            )
            return as_fp32_logits(lg, lens.view(-1))

        lg = run()[:, :ctx]
        rel = ((lg.double() - ref).abs().sum() / ref.abs().sum()).item()
        out[dt] = (lg, rel, do_bench(run, warmup=25, rep=200))
    return out, ref, valid


def report(name, res):
    out, ref, valid = res
    f32, b16 = out[torch.float32], out[torch.bfloat16]
    print(
        f"{name}: rel_err fp32={f32[1]:.2e} bf16={b16[1]:.2e} | "
        f"top{TOPK} overlap vs fp64 ref: fp32={topk_overlap(f32[0], ref, valid):.4f} "
        f"bf16={topk_overlap(b16[0], ref, valid):.4f} | "
        f"us fp32={f32[2] * 1e3:.1f} bf16(+upcast)={b16[2] * 1e3:.1f}"
    )


print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), "mx_scales:", mqa_logits_use_mx_scales())
report("prefill 2048x16384", prefill(2048, 16384))
report("prefill 4096x65536", prefill(4096, 65536))
report("decode  b=64 ctx=16384", decode(64, 16384))
report("decode  b=8 ctx=65536", decode(8, 65536))
```
</details>

## Details

**Semantics per architecture**, following vllm-project/DeepGEMM#46:
- On SM100, the head-weights dtype selects the reduction. `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` now takes `logits_dtype` and casts the weights to it:
  - FP32 weights reduce in FP32;
  - BF16 weights reduce in BF16 and emit BF16 logits.
- SM90/SM120 keep FP32 weights for either output dtype.

**Memory profiling.** The indexer's dummy logits allocation is now sized from `logits_dtype` instead of from the architecture. The GLM-5.3 kpool profile also counts the BF16 output alongside its FP32 copy.

**Interaction with open PRs.** #62170 (emit BF16 indexer weights on SM100) and #62172 / #64138 (BF16 input for cooperative / persistent top-k) optimize the BF16 path. They still apply wherever the logits are BF16, including DeepSeek's SM100 default. With FP32 logits:
- #62170's BF16 weights would be upcast back to FP32;
- the top-k changes don't engage, since the logits are already FP32.

**Upstream DeepGEMM note.** vllm-project/DeepGEMM#46 relaxed the shared weights-dtype check. As a result, the sparse MQA-logits kernels, which read BF16 weights, now also accept FP32 weights on SM100. vLLM always passes BF16 there (`sparse_mqa_indexer.py`), so it is unaffected; this should be fixed in DeepGEMM.

**Not a duplicate.** Open-PR searches for `logits_dtype`, `indexer fp32 logits`, `mqa logits bf16`, `DeepGEMM bump` and `deepgemm.cmake` found no PR that restores FP32 indexer logits or bumps to this pin. The related PRs listed above build on the BF16 path rather than adding a dtype switch.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Fix Mamba region stride on block-outermost layouts
author: Dao007forever
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix NIXL transfers of Mamba/SSM hybrid state on block-outermost KV cache layouts (`BLHNC`, `BLNHC`), and add a CPU test that pulls one request between two NIXL workers on real model KV layouts and checks every byte.

Related: vllm-project/vllm#63416 changes how NIXL pairs regions. This PR does not depend on it, and #63416 rebases onto it without conflicts.

## Claims

- **Fix.** With `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`, Qwen3-Next (GDN) and Nemotron-H (Mamba2) disaggregated P/D read the wrong Mamba state and wrote outside the request's blocks, with no error. They now transfer correctly. Layer-outermost layouts (the default) are unchanged. Hybrids whose attention is MLA, such as Kimi-Linear, were not affected (see Root cause).
- **Test.** The NIXL unit tests build KV cache configs and tensors by hand. The new test plans and allocates both sides with vLLM's own planner (`get_kv_cache_configs`) and allocator (`allocate_kv_cache`), from the per-layer KV specs of 12 models. D pulls one request from P through the real worker code; the recorded descriptors run as memory copies. Every page of every layer must land in D's block for the same layer and request position, and no other D byte may change.

## Validation

CPU only: `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`. No weights or model code: the KV specs are built in the test.

```
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k real_model
# 14 passed in ~10 s
```

| Case | KV plan in the test (groups → regions) | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B (same shape as GLM-4.5-Air, MiniMax-M2) | 4 full, 1 → 4 | auto (LBHNC) |
| gpt-oss-20b | SW + full, 2 → 2 shared | auto |
| Gemma 3 1B | 10 SW + 2 full, 6 → 2 shared | auto |
| MiMo-V2-Flash | 9 SW + 3 full, 4 → 3 shared | auto |
| DeepSeek-V3 (same as Kimi-K2) | 4 MLA, 1 → 4 | auto; BLNHC → BLNHC; BLNHC P → LBNHC D |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 | MLA + indexer cache, 1 → 8 | auto |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | 6 GDN + 2 full, 4 → 2 shared | auto; BLHNC |
| NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 | 11 Mamba2 + 2 full, 7 → 2 shared | auto; BLHNC |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | 6 KDA + 2 MLA, 4 → 2 shared | auto; BLNHC |

Fails before the fix: the new test with `main`'s `base_worker.py`:

```
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k "real_model and BLHNC"
FAILED ...[Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-BLHNC-BLHNC]
  AssertionError: ['model.layers.0.linear_attn[0].0', 'model.layers.4.linear_attn[0].0', ...]
FAILED ...[NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-BLHNC-BLHNC]
  AssertionError: ['model.layers.0.mixer[0].0', 'model.layers.11.mixer[0].0', ...]
2 failed
```

Every GDN/Mamba2 page arrives wrong. With the fix, all 14 cases pass.

The test also catches descriptor bugs it was not written for: dropping the conv-state offset from the peer's SSM descriptor (`_build_mamba_remote`) fails the three layer-outermost hybrid cases.

NIXL unit suites (`test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_push_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py`), on `main` and on this branch:

| Tree | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `main` @ `4e0ad5720` | 646 | 4 |
| this branch | 660 | 4, the same ones |

- **The 4 failures on both:** `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma` needs a gated HF repo, `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray, None]` needs Ray/GPU, and `test_register_packed_dsv4_mla_cache_as_single_region[v41-aliased-groups]` fails on `main` as well.
- **Transient failures:** the branch's first suite run also had 11 consecutive failures in `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, during a period of HF Hub rate limiting (see below). All 11 passed on rerun, and a full run of that file passed (271 tests).

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

Note on flakiness: the new test builds two `create_vllm_config` configs per case, as other NIXL unit tests do. When the HF Hub rate-limits the `facebook/opt-125m` file listing (HTTP 429), any of these tests fails in setup. That was the only failure cause seen in about 600 local runs of the new test.

## Details

**Root cause.** Under the hybrid KV cache manager, cache groups share KV cache tensors. With a block-outermost layout, block *b* of every tensor sits side by side in one row, so a layer's view advances by the row: 4,718,592 B for Qwen3-Next's two tensors in the test, not by one 2,359,296 B page. `register_kv_caches` registered Mamba regions with `block_stride = physical_page_size` and took the view's stride only for CSA-linear. So every Mamba descriptor past block 0 pointed into the other tensor's pages. Attention regions on the same rows already used the view stride.

Only some hybrids hit it. A shared region keeps the stride of the first layer registered into it (layer-name order), and a later layer replaces it only if it is MLA. Mamba sub-region descriptors use the region's stride:
- In Qwen3-Next and Nemotron-H a Mamba layer comes first, and their full-attention layers never replace its page stride.
- In Kimi-Linear the MLA layer replaces it with the row stride, so its KDA descriptors were right by accident; the Kimi-Linear BLNHC case passes with or without the fix.

The fix takes the view's stride for Mamba views on block-outermost layouts too. Elsewhere the page stride stays. A view indexed by kernel block (several per logical block) has a stride of a fraction of the page, and taking the view's stride there breaks the existing hetero-block-size tests.

Flow (pull, the failing case):
1. Startup, P and D: `register_kv_caches` registers each region as `(base, len, stride, count)`; Mamba regions get stride = one page.
2. Handshake: D builds descriptors for P's Mamba sub-regions (conv q/k/v parts, SSM state) from P's metadata, and its own from its local regions.
3. Read: a descriptor id for block *b* resolves to `base + b × stride`. With stride = page instead of row, block *b*'s address lands in another tensor's page of a lower block, on both sides.

**The test.**
- Models are those tested end to end for vllm-project/vllm#63416. MiniMax-M1 is left out; vLLM removed it in 0.23.0.
- Specs mirror what each model's layers return. Nine were dumped from a meta-device model build on CPU. DeepSeek-V3.2 (sparse MLA + indexer) and Kimi-Linear (MLA + KDA) cannot be built on CPU, so their specs come from their configs and vLLM's state-shape helpers.
- Each case uses the first layers of its model, enough for its group and region pattern (2 regions for the hybrids). The largest case allocates about 120 MB per side.
- Hybrid block sizes are the ones vLLM aligns to on CPU (1152, 1408). For Kimi-Linear it is 1920, the first 64-token multiple whose MLA page holds the KDA state.

**Not covered.**
- Push, TP mismatch, PP stages, and P and D with different settings. With the same model and settings the region pairing is the identity; those cases stay with the hand-built tests.
- GPU, and an end-to-end P/D run with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` on a hybrid model.

**Mocks.** `tests/AGENTS.md` asks for real objects. The workers are patched the same way as the existing `_make_mla_hybrid_worker` helper in this file:
- the platform reports a CUDA device, so the GPU registration path runs on a CPU host;
- attention backends and kernel block-size selection are faked, since no model layers are built;
- TP rank and size are fixed at 0 and 1;
- NIXL itself is the file's `_RecordingNixl`.

Planner, allocator, layout resolution, registration, handshake and descriptor code are all real.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#62453 fixes Mamba page padding on the CPU host-buffer path, and vllm-project/vllm#64140 fixes packed Mamba addressing in the KV offloading worker. Neither touches NIXL's Mamba region stride.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change. The submitter reviews every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Fall back from the latent-MoE tail fusion under sleep mode
author: aleksandr-inherent
body:
## Overview

On SM100 at TP 8 or 16, `LatentMoERunner` raises `ValueError: K3 latent-MoE tail fusion does not support sleep mode.` when `--enable-sleep-mode` is set, so Kimi-K3 cannot start with sleep mode, which the process checkpoint lifecycle (#62570) requires. The runner now falls back to the default latent-MoE path with a warning, as it already does for unsupported TP sizes. No open PR or issue addresses the sleep-mode raise. #64276 and #65582 change the same block; whichever merges later needs a rebase.

## Claims

- Kimi-K3 starts with `--enable-sleep-mode` on SM100 at TP 8 and 16, on the default latent-MoE path.
- Without sleep mode nothing changes, and DBO or ubatching with the tail fusion still raises.

## Validation

- The new `test_sleep_mode_falls_back_to_default_path` fails on main and passes with this change. Both tests build the runner with the file's existing stand-ins and need no GPU. A regression test through `LLM` needs Kimi-K3 on 8 B300s, which CI does not have, so the end-to-end run below is the validation outside CI.

  <details>
  <summary>Before and after</summary>

  ```text
  $ pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py -k "deferred_finalize_enabled or sleep_mode"

  # main (aa738c38c3) with the new test
  E   ValueError: K3 latent-MoE tail fusion does not support sleep mode.
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py:102: ValueError
  1 failed, 1 passed, 3 deselected

  # this branch
  2 passed, 3 deselected
  ```

  </details>

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.
- End to end on vLLM 0.31.0 with an equivalent local change (the tail fusion turned off whenever sleep mode is on), on 8x B300: `nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4` at TP 8 and DCP 8 with sleep mode, captured and restored with ai-dynamo/snapshot. Without the change the engine raised the error above at startup. With it, a restored replica returned the same text as a cold replica running the tail fusion, with per-token logprobs 0.01-0.09 apart, and served 861 requests at 48 concurrent with no errors. This exact diff has not been run end to end.

## Details

**Why fall back.** The raise came in with the runner without a stated reason. On the same GPUs the K3 specialized decode already treats sleep mode as a reason to run the stock forward (`specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py`), and the TP-size check just above falls back with a warning. Sleep mode now does the same, before the tail op is initialized.

**Tradeoff.** Under sleep mode Kimi-K3 loses the tail fusion's speedup, which we have not measured. Making the tail fusion work across sleep and wake is out of scope.

title: [NIXL][CI/Build] Bump NIXL to 1.5.2 and drop source build for Rubin
author: erezzarum
body:
## Overview

Use the released NIXL 1.5.2 wheels in the Rubin CUDA 13.4 image and stop building NIXL from source there. NIXL 1.5.2 ships a NIXL EP extension built for torch 2.16, which the Rubin prerelease uses, so the `BUILD_NIXL=true` workaround from #60090 is no longer needed. Fixes the gap tracked in ai-dynamo/nixl#2297 (now closed).

Related: #64579 bumps `requirements/kv_connectors.txt` to the same version for the default images. <!-- merge order / rebase note, see Details -->

## Claims

- `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt`: `nixl` 1.4.1 -> 1.5.2.
- `requirements/kv_connectors.txt`: `nixl` 1.5.0 -> 1.5.2 (same line as #64579).
- `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml`: the nightly "aarch64 - Rubin CUDA 13.4" build drops `--build-arg BUILD_NIXL=true` and its TODO, so it installs the PyPI wheels.

## Validation

- `nixl-cu13==1.5.2` wheels from PyPI (cp312) contain `nixl_ep_cpp_torch216`:
  - `manylinux_2_28_aarch64`: torch 2.12, 2.13, 2.14, 2.15, 2.16
  - `manylinux_2_28_x86_64`: includes torch 2.16
  - Reproduce: `pip download --no-deps --only-binary=:all: --platform manylinux_2_28_aarch64 --python-version 3.12 nixl-cu13==1.5.2 && python -m zipfile -l nixl_cu13-*.whl | grep nixl_ep_cpp_torch`
- `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt` pins `torch==2.16.0.dev20261009+cu134`, so the 216 variant is the one that gets loaded.
- TODO before submitting: build the aarch64 Rubin image without `BUILD_NIXL` and check that the NIXL EP extension loads (`import nixl_ep_cu13` on a GPU host, or the same `nixl_ep_cpp_torch216` glob the Dockerfile check uses).
- Not run: NixlConnector P/D serving on Rubin hardware.

## Details

- The source build added in #60090 is kept (`BUILD_NIXL` ARG, `tools/build_nixl_with_torch215_for_rubin.py`, `docker/versions.json`) as an opt-in escape hatch for future torch nightlies that get ahead of NIXL releases. No CI job sets it after this change. <!-- or remove it; see author notes -->
- Updated the installation doc, which said NIXL's release wheels lack NIXL EP for the Rubin PyTorch nightly. <!-- only if the doc edit is added -->

title: [Startup] Skip the CUDA graph memory profile when its estimate is disabled
author: emmericp
body:
## Overview

Cleanup: with `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`, `determine_available_memory()` still runs `profile_cudagraph_memory()` and then ignores the result. Skip the call when the flag is 0. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR; I reviewed every changed line.

Since #56492 (extensible KV cache), MRV2's `profile_cudagraph_memory()` returns 0 when the extensible cache is on. The startup saving therefore applies only to fallback configurations (MRV1, elastic EP, `LMCacheMPConnector`, etc.) with the flag at 0.

## Claims

Fallback configurations with the flag at 0 no longer run the throwaway capture pass. On current main the pass costs:

| Fallback configuration | Estimate pass on main | Startup, main → this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRV2, `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` | 89 s, 90 s | 260.8 s → 171.0 s |
| MRV1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | 3 s, 3 s | within run-to-run noise |

Setup: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP1, one GB300, `--compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 4096}'`, `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`, warm caches, main at c96e5f60bb. The estimate pass is the span from vLLM's `Profiling CUDA graph memory` log line to `Estimated CUDA graph memory` (MRV1), and the first `Graph capturing finished` line (MRV2). The real capture takes the same time with and without this PR (MRV2: 95 s and 96 s). The earlier 95.1 s → 72.5 s figure was measured before #56492 and is superseded.

There is no behaviour change with the flag at 1 (the default).
- The "profiling is disabled" warning now fires only when the flag is 0, graphs may be captured, and the extensible cache is off. It no longer suggests a `--gpu-memory-utilization` value, since that needed the skipped estimate.

## Validation

`test_cudagraph_memory_profile_runs_only_when_applied` covers MRV1, MRV2 with and without the extensible cache, and MRV2 without graphs. For each case it checks the estimate call, the KV cache budget and the warning.

```
$ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -k cudagraph_memory_profile_runs_only_when_applied
7 passed                    # this PR (CPU)
3 failed, 4 passed          # main: all three flag-0 cases still run the estimate
3 failed, 4 passed          # previous revision of this PR: warns with the extensible cache on, and for MRV2 without graphs
```

CI runs this file in the H200 "V1 Executor + Worker" step (`pytest -v -s v1/worker`, `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`).

title: [Perf][LoRA][MoE] Use the shrink/expand kernels for MoE-LoRA batches of up to 64 tokens
author: aoshen02
body:
Diff: 3 files, +262 / -17.

This PR was split into a stack. Its earlier revisions (problem-sized configs, threshold 256, fp32 intermediate, removal of the small-batch kernel) moved to:

1. this PR: shrink/expand for batches of up to 64 tokens
2. #64746: problem-sized shrink/expand configs, threshold 256
3. #64747: fp32 intermediate, single output rounding
4. #64748: remove the small-batch kernel

## Purpose

For `max_lora_rank <= 128` and `fully_sharded=False`, `_fused_moe_lora` on main always uses the single-launch one-shot or small-batch kernel. Each program in them runs the whole K loop serially, so at decode the grid is a few dozen programs and the kernels run far below memory bandwidth. The existing `_fused_moe_lora_shrink` + `_fused_moe_lora_expand` path spreads the work over more programs.

## Changes

- Batches of up to `FUSED_MOE_LORA_TWO_KERNEL_MAX_TOKENS = 64` tokens use shrink/expand. Larger batches keep the one-shot / small-batch kernels. With the current default configs (from the base-MoE `get_default_config`), shrink/expand wins at every size up to 64 tokens and is mixed above, so the threshold is 64. #64746 raises it to 256 together with configs sized for the LoRA problem.
- TMA descriptors need 16-byte aligned strides. Shrink/expand now also runs small ranks, so TMA is used only when `max_lora_rank * element_size % 16 == 0` (rank 4 in bf16 would otherwise fail with `strides must be 16-byte aligned`).
- The TMA descriptor calls import `TensorDescriptor` where they use it. `import triton` does not load `triton.tools.tensor_descriptor`; on main it is only loaded as a side effect of other imports (in a server, `fused_moe/config.py` through `triton_kernels`). Once small batches reach these calls, `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` fails 18 cases with `AttributeError: module 'triton.tools' has no attribute 'tensor_descriptor'` after #64748.

## Kernel time

bf16, CUDA graph over N layers with distinct LoRA weights (at least 512 MB in total, so the weights do not stay in L2), the second-best of 7 timed trials, µs per call. "main" is e49ea84e9. E=128, top_k=4, hidden=6144, moe_intermediate=768, rank 32, max_loras 1:

| M | GB200 w13 main | GB200 w13 this PR | GB200 w2 main | GB200 w2 this PR | H200 w13 main | H200 w13 this PR | H200 w2 main | H200 w2 this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 72.2 | **18.9** | 14.2 | **6.0** | 60.1 | **25.8** | 13.5 | **7.0** |
| 2 | 72.1 | **19.7** | 14.5 | **6.8** | 78.0 | **30.4** | 16.7 | **8.7** |
| 4 | 104.0 | **23.3** | 19.6 | **9.1** | 95.3 | **49.7** | 20.3 | **14.1** |
| 8 | 56.5 | **26.4** | 40.9 | **13.3** | 54.1 | **30.7** | 43.5 | **14.8** |
| 16 | 84.1 | **28.8** | 59.5 | **19.8** | 70.0 | **38.0** | 63.3 | **21.9** |
| 32 | 89.2 | **35.5** | 113.4 | **31.0** | 79.4 | **59.8** | 114.5 | **35.4** |
| 64 | 99.5 | **49.2** | 133.6 | **38.4** | 90.5 | **77.2** | 159.1 | **32.4** |
| 96 | 107.6 | 107.6 | 135.0 | 135.0 | 91.1 | 91.5 | 160.7 | 160.1 |
| 256 | 87.3 | 87.5 | 124.9 | 124.9 | 109.1 | 109.3 | 164.1 | 164.9 |

Over 5 MoE shapes (the one above, Qwen3-30B-A3B, OLMoE, Mixtral TP8, DeepSeek-V3 TP8) x rank 8/16/32/64 x max_loras 1/4 x w13/w2 (80 problems per M), geomean speedup over main of this PR's kernel path (measured on the previous head 389e07498, which has the same dispatch and kernels):

| M | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GB200 | 2.10x | 2.23x | 2.41x | 2.53x | 2.51x | 2.20x | 2.00x |
| H200 | 2.04x | 2.02x | 1.96x | 2.27x | 2.08x | 1.84x | 1.86x |

## Accuracy

Kernel level, max |out - ref| / max |ref| against an fp64 reference, divided by the error from rounding the fp64 result to bf16 (1.0 = exact up to output rounding), 80 problems x M 1-64 on GB200: main 1.171 geomean / 2.163 max, this PR 1.289 / 2.163. Shrink/expand rounds the rank-sized intermediate to bf16, which the small-batch kernel did not; #64747 removes that rounding.

Model level, OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct with `jeeejeee/olmoe-instruct-text2sql-spider`, 6147 teacher-forced tokens scored with `max_num_batched_tokens=64` (every forward goes through shrink/expand), mean |Δ logprob| against an fp32 HF reference: GB200 main 0.0624 / this PR 0.0635, H200 0.0574 / 0.0576. This PR differs from main by 0.0165 / 0.0125 nats mean, the same as two runs of main differ from each other (0.0164 / 0.0151). With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the logprobs are bit-identical to main. Full setup and tables are in #64747.

## Test Plan

- `test_fused_moe_lora_token_threshold_dispatch`: 23 shapes (naive and sorted assignment, top_k 1-8, rank 4-128, bf16/fp16, w13- and w2-like shapes, split-K 4) check the path chosen on each side of the threshold and the result against a torch reference. `m16-topk1-r4-naive` covers the TMA alignment check.
- `test_fused_moe_lora_expert_parallel`: shrink/expand and one-shot with an `expert_map`; non-local experts must leave the output unchanged.
- The early-exit and zero-grid tests now run on both paths. The NPID and bad-`BLOCK_SIZE_M` tests use more than 64 tokens so they still reach the one-shot kernel.

## Test Result

- `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` on 1 GPU: 451 passed, 12 skipped (GB200 and H200). With the whole stack (#64748): 468 passed, 12 skipped; without the import change, 18 of them fail.
- The new and changed tests on the parent with only the 64-token constant added: 22 failed, 21 passed (every dispatch assertion below the threshold fails). Without the TMA alignment check, `m16-topk1-r4-naive` fails with `AssertionError: strides must be 16-byte aligned`.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` (0.14.0) clean; mypy reports no new errors on the changed files.

title: [Test][UMBP] Restore a Mamba2 hybrid end to end through UMBP
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Add a Granite 4.0-H hybrid restore test to `test_mori_token_e2e.py`, run through embedded UMBP.
- Require bitwise-equal tokens and logprobs against a local GPU prefix hit, plus an exact external-hit count.
- Cover a prompt ending mid-block and one ending exactly on a block boundary.

No hybrid model restores through UMBP end to end today. The Nemotron-H GSM8K row never gets a prefix hit because its 1088-token hybrid block is longer than the prompts, so the Mamba boundary-state handoff is only covered with fake runtimes. Mamba hybrids have no batch-invariant kernels, so a cold run can't be the reference, and prompts go one at a time because async load timing changes the batch layout and batched hybrid outputs aren't bitwise stable. On MI350X with MORI v1.2.3.post1 built with UMBP, `pytest -v -s -rs v1/kv_connector/umbp_integration/test_mori_token_e2e.py -k hybrid` passed 10/10 in a loop and the whole file gave 3 passed, but every case fails once the restored Mamba pages are zeroed after the load. The MI355 UMBP integration group already runs this directory, so CI is unchanged. No open UMBP PR (#61795-#61798, #63002, #59276) restores a hybrid end to end, though #63830 and #63670 rework Mamba align mode and may need this test adjusted if they land first.

title: [Test][UMBP] Cover TP=2 restore through per-rank MORI pools
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Parametrize `test_restore_matches_recompute` through its `umbp_llm` fixture over TP=1 and TP=2.
- Add a 2-GPU UMBP Connector TP2 Integration group in `test-amd.yaml` and `misc.yaml` that runs only `[tp2]`.

Rank routing and the rule that every rank must hit are only unit-tested with fake clients today, so nothing runs the real path where each TP worker binds its own lookup socket and restores its own head shard from its own MORI pool. If rank 1 loaded rank 0's shard the logprobs would diverge, and if one rank's pool missed, the external-hit count would come up short. Exactness depends on batch invariance keeping the all-reduce deterministic, and a 2-rank sum is order-independent, so the multi-GPU case stops at TP=2. On MI350X (2 GPUs) with MORI v1.2.3.post1 built with UMBP, `pytest -v -s -rs "v1/kv_connector/umbp_integration/test_mori_token_e2e.py::test_restore_matches_recompute"` passed `[tp2]` 11/11 and `[tp1]` 3/3. The existing integration group stays on one GPU, and no open UMBP PR covers this; the TP2/PP2 test that #61794 removed never ran real TP.

title: [Test][UMBP] Cover end-to-end restore while the embedded DRAM pool is evicting
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Let the `umbp_llm` fixture take pool options through indirect parametrization.
- Add `test_restore_under_pool_eviction` on a 64 MiB pool: the newest prompt restores exactly, the oldest is evicted.

The existing end-to-end UMBP tests never fill the pool, so the connector and scheduler path under eviction never runs, and `test_mori_embedded_gpu.py` only overfills it at the runtime level. Prompts run one at a time so MORI's LRU commit order is deterministic, and the pool size assumes Qwen3-0.6B KV on MORI's 64 KiB pages. On MI350X with MORI v1.2.3.post1 built with UMBP, `pytest -v -s -rs v1/kv_connector/umbp_integration/test_mori_token_e2e.py` gave 3 passed and the new test passed 10/10 in a loop. With a 1 GiB pool the same flow restores the oldest prompt in full, so the miss comes from eviction. While probing this we found that equal watermarks, or a high watermark at or below MORI's default low of 0.7, silently disable eviction; that fix is a separate PR. No open UMBP PR covers end-to-end restore under eviction.

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Sequence parallelism and GEMM-RS for TP + MegaMoE
author: gau-nernst
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds sequence parallelism (SP) to MiniMax-M3 on NVIDIA when running TP + EP with the MegaMoE backend, plus the GEMM-RS kernel for `o_proj` and the dense MLP `down_proj`. The design follows the existing Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1 SP.

Without SP, MegaMoE already shards tokens across TP ranks internally, but then writes its shard into a zero-filled full-size buffer, and the next RMSNorm all-reduces it. So every layer pays 2 full all-reduces: one after attention, and one on a mostly-zero MoE output. With SP, the residual stream stays sharded by token, and each MoE layer does 1 all-gather before attention and 1 reduce-scatter after `o_proj`. MegaMoE consumes the shard directly. The 3 dense layers do one more all-gather/reduce-scatter pair around their MLP.

## Claims

- SP is enabled automatically for TP > 1 + EP + MegaMoE + PP1, same rule as DeepSeek-V4.1 and Kimi-K3. GEMM-RS is opt-in with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1`.
- On 4×GB300 with `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (8k in / 1k out, DSpark spec decode), compared to TP4 + EP without SP:
  - P50 TTFT is 14-20% lower at all concurrencies.
  - Output throughput is +6.5% at concurrency 16 and +13.6% at concurrency 64, a tie at concurrency 4, and -4% at concurrency 1 (see below).
- gsm8k is unchanged.

## Validation

All benchmarks were done on a single 4×GB300 node, with `f81a414fae` as the base and `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (`9e7ebac`). The serve command is the "Single node (TP4, NVIDIA GB200)" command from the [vLLM recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash), plus `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. 3 setups are compared:

- **TP4**: the recipe command as-is, on main
- **TP4 + EP**: `-ep --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, on main
- **TP4 + EP + SP**: same flags with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1`, on this PR

<details>
<summary>Serve command (TP4 + EP + SP)</summary>

```bash
VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 \
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
  -tp 4 -ep --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "use_prefill_query_quantization": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER_TS","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

</details>

### E2E: SpeedBench throughput_8k

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1 vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat \
  --dataset-name speed-bench --speed-bench-config throughput_8k \
  --speed-bench-max-input-len 8192 --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-warmups 5 --sweep-max-concurrency 1,4,16,64 --sweep-num-prompts-factor 10
```

The full sweep was run twice for each setup, restarting the server in between. Each cell is the range over the 2 runs; best (by mean) in **bold**.

**Output throughput**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | **410–411 tok/s** | 370 tok/s | 355 tok/s |
| 4 | **1,022–1,058 tok/s** | 928–950 tok/s | 945–972 tok/s |
| 16 | 2,212–2,245 tok/s | 2,254–2,260 tok/s | **2,397–2,410 tok/s** |
| 64 | 3,937–3,938 tok/s | 4,299–4,338 tok/s | **4,896–4,914 tok/s** |

**P50 TTFT**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 164–166 ms | 140 ms | **111–114 ms** |
| 4 | 190–193 ms | 163–167 ms | **134–137 ms** |
| 16 | 200–202 ms | 179–184 ms | **151–152 ms** |
| 64 | 289–329 ms | 266–280 ms | **233–236 ms** |

**P50 TPOT**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | **2.53 ms** | 2.68 ms | 2.76 ms |
| 4 | **3.65–3.79 ms** | 4.30–4.53 ms | 3.98–4.28 ms |
| 16 | 6.55–6.64 ms | 6.52–6.81 ms | **6.12–6.68 ms** |
| 64 | 15.38–15.71 ms | 14.05–14.08 ms | **12.16–12.39 ms** |

As expected, pure TP4 is the fastest at low concurrency, and EP pulls ahead at high concurrency. SP lowers TTFT at every concurrency, with no overlap between the ranges, and widens EP's lead in throughput at concurrency 16 and 64. At concurrency 4 and for TPOT at concurrency 16, the SP and EP ranges overlap, so those are a tie.

At concurrency 1, TPOT is 3% higher with SP. This comes from spec decode acceptance (3.10 vs 3.20), not from slower steps: TPOT × acceptance length is the same (8.56 ms vs 8.58 ms). Concurrency 1 only has 10 prompts, so a small numerical difference in the outputs is enough to change the acceptance length. It was identical in both runs.

<details>
<summary>Acceptance length (mean of 2 runs)</summary>

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.02 | 3.20 | 3.10 |
| 4 | 3.08 | 3.11 | 3.09 |
| 16 | 3.14 | 3.15 | 3.17 |
| 64 | 3.15 | 3.14 | 3.16 |

</details>

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, chat completions, temperature 0. One eval per server start (run 1 / run 2).

| Metric | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| flexible-extract | 95.53 / 95.75 | 95.45 / 95.98 | 96.13 / 95.45 |
| strict-match | 95.00 / 95.45 | 95.22 / 95.68 | 95.91 / 95.22 |

### GEMM-RS microbenchmark

```bash
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -- benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py \
  --model minimax_m3 --backend flashinfer_cutedsl \
  --m 128 512 768 1024 1152 1280 1536 2048 4096 8192 16384 32768
```

TP4, N=6144. Baseline is the existing unfused path in vLLM (MXFP8 GEMM + `sp_reduce_scatter`).

| M | o_proj (K=2048) baseline | o_proj GEMM-RS | down_proj (K=3072) baseline | down_proj GEMM-RS |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 36.6 us | 39.8 us (0.92x) | 55.9 us | 60.5 us (0.92x) |
| 512 | 61.8 us | 63.3 us (0.98x) | 64.6 us | 64.9 us (1.00x) |
| 768 | 68.2 us | 67.4 us (1.01x) | 68.7 us | 66.7 us (1.03x) |
| 1024 | 79.0 us | 76.9 us (1.03x) | 79.0 us | 72.9 us (1.08x) |
| 1536 | 101.5 us | 84.0 us (1.21x) | 105.3 us | 82.2 us (1.28x) |
| 2048 | 114.1 us | 90.9 us (1.26x) | 119.4 us | 89.2 us (1.34x) |
| 4096 | 179.3 us | 133.7 us (1.34x) | 191.6 us | 129.9 us (1.47x) |
| 8192 | 271.3 us | 211.6 us (1.28x) | 299.7 us | 210.0 us (1.43x) |
| 16384 | 475.0 us | 363.6 us (1.31x) | 558.9 us | 374.4 us (1.49x) |
| 32768 | 952.6 us | 680.1 us (1.40x) | 1146.9 us | 704.8 us (1.63x) |

M=512-1536 was repeated two more times. GEMM-RS was faster at M ≥ 1024 every time, while M=768 was mixed, so GEMM-RS is only used for M ≥ 1024.

Above 1024 tokens, the fused dense GEMM1 hands `down_proj` an MXFP8 `QuantizedActivation`, so the BF16-input numbers above include an activation quantization that production skips. Re-measured with the same pre-quantized input for both paths (range over 2 runs):

| M | down_proj (K=3072) baseline | down_proj GEMM-RS |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1152 | 66.4–74.4 us | 61.4–66.2 us (1.08–1.12x) |
| 1280 | 72.8–74.9 us | 63.6–65.7 us (1.14x) |
| 1536 | 88.9–91.4 us | 65.1–66.7 us (1.37x) |
| 2048 | 109.7–110.3 us | 76.9–78.2 us (1.41–1.43x) |
| 4096 | 173.8–175.8 us | 111.3–114.0 us (1.54–1.56x) |
| 8192 | 279.4–279.7 us | 190.6–192.1 us (1.45–1.47x) |
| 16384 | 534.0–534.7 us | 343.3–345.2 us (1.55–1.56x) |
| 32768 | 1083.8–1087.4 us | 650.4–652.4 us (1.66–1.67x) |

GEMM-RS stays faster at every M above the threshold.

### Tests

- `tests/kernels/test_gemm_rs_ar.py`: extended with a pre-quantized MXFP8 input for both MXFP8 backends. Passes on 2×GB300. CI runs it in the 2×B200 distributed step.
- E2E SP needs 4 SM100 GPUs in one NVLink domain plus the M3.1 checkpoint, which CI does not have. It is covered by the benchmark and gsm8k runs above.

## Details

Changes in `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py`:
- **Model forward**: shard the hidden states after the embedding, and shard the MegaMoE padding mask once. At the end, all-gather the output together with the EAGLE3/DSpark aux hidden states in 1 collective.
- **Attention**: all-gather the input, reduce-scatter the output (`o_proj` + `sp_reduce_scatter`, or GEMM-RS).
- **MegaMoE**: takes the shard as-is (`input_is_sequence_sharded`), so no shard/gather/zero-fill. The existing `use_sequence_parallel` flag in `MiniMaxM3MoE` is renamed to `shard_replicated_input`, since it means the opposite of model-level SP.
- **Dense MLP** (3 of 60 layers): all-gather, `gate_up` (keeps the fused dense GEMM1) and `down_proj`, then reduce-scatter.
- **Fusions**: the AR + Gemma RMSNorm fusions are skipped under SP, since there is nothing left to all-reduce.

**GEMM-RS with a quantized input** Above its token threshold, the fused dense GEMM1 outputs an MXFP8 `QuantizedActivation` instead of BF16. So `GemmRsAr.apply()` now accepts it and skips its own quantization. The scales are already in the F8_128x4 swizzled layout that the kernel expects.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- MTP blocks and PP > 1 don't use SP.
- The dense MLP stays TP-sharded instead of adding Kimi-K3's replicated option, since it is only 3 layers.
- The all-gathers move BF16. Gathering the MXFP8 `qkv_proj` input instead would halve the bytes; this is left for a follow-up.

title: [Perf][Parser] Skip tool-argument conversions after a replaced value
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

When a tool call repeats a key whose value was already streamed, `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta` fails the prefix check before it installs the argument value extender. Every later delta then re-converts the whole argument text, only to fail the same check, so the API server's cost per token grows with the call. This installs the extender with streaming off on that failure. Follow-up to #61253 and #64535.

## Claims

- On GLM-4.7/GLM-5.x, a long value written under a repeated key costs 15.1 us per engine step at 66K output chars, against 2514 us on main. From 64K to 256K chars the mean is 17.3 us against 6.16 ms.
- On a real server (GLM-4.7-Flash, one H200), streaming that call to 256K chars costs the API server 14 s of CPU against 215 s on main, and `/health` p99 stays at 0.8 ms against 17.9 ms.
- Streamed arguments are unchanged in every case checked, and so are non-streaming results. One case groups deltas differently: a repeated key whose new value starts with the text already streamed for the old value. It streams the rest of the value when the value closes, while main streams it at the next delta containing `>`.
- The change is in `engine/` because the wasted conversion follows any failed prefix check, whatever the parser. Only GLM's extender accepts a value under a repeated key today, so Qwen3 and DSML streams are unchanged (see Details).
- No new config, flag or API.

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `8084f0624d` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cost test | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py::TestStreamedToolArguments::test_replaced_value_conversions_do_not_grow` | `AssertionError: assert 135 == 1215` | passed |
| Parser suite | `pytest tests/parser --ignore=tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py --ignore=tests/parser/test_harmony.py` | 6570 passed, 93 errors | 6571 passed, 93 errors (same set) |
| Errored files, with Hugging Face access | `pytest tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py tests/parser/test_include_reasoning.py` | 71 passed | 71 passed |
| Streaming equivalence (below) | real tokenizers, `parse_delta` at chunk sizes 1, 3, 4, 7, 64, plus `parse` | | 343 of 348 records identical; 5 differ in grouping only, arguments identical in all 348 |
| Cost per step (below) | GLM-5.3 tokenizer, `glm47` + `glm45`, through `OutputProcessor` and `chat_completion_stream_generator` | 2514 us at 66K chars | 15.1 us |
| Server run (below) | GLM-4.7-Flash on one H200, forced repeated-key stream to 256K chars | API server 214.7 s CPU (33% busy), `/health` p99 17.9 ms | 14.1 s (2%), p99 0.83 ms |

Tests ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. Of the 93 errors, 70 are the three files in the third row, which need Hugging Face access the first run did not have. The other 23 are in `tests/parser/mistral/test_reasoning.py`, which fails the same on main with the image's mistral-common. `ruff`, the repo's `mypy` hook and the CI-wiring hook pass.

CI coverage: `tests/parser` jobs are disabled since #63609, and `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py` is on the tethering allowlist with them, so CI will run the new test once that job is back.

<details>
<summary>Streaming equivalence</summary>

Each output is tokenized with the model's real tokenizer and streamed as token-id chunks through `ParserManager.get_parser(...)`. Every delta's content, reasoning, tool-call name and arguments are recorded, plus one non-streaming `parse`. The outputs cover every case shape below for each family, plus 9 repeated-key cases: a different new value, an identical value, a new value that extends the old one, a new value that is a prefix of the old one, a repeated key that is not the last key, a third occurrence that restores the first value, another key after the repeat, an unclosed repeat, and a second call.

| Parsers (tokenizer) | Records | Identical | Grouping differs, arguments identical |
|---|---|---|---|
| `glm47` + `glm45` (GLM-5.3) | 120 | 115 | 5 (`dup-last-extends-old` at all 5 chunk sizes: 112 deltas to 13 at size 1) |
| `deepseek_v41` + `deepseek_v41` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) | 114 | 114 | 0 |
| `qwen3_coder` + `nemotron_v3` (Qwen3) | 114 | 114 | 0 |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cost per step</summary>

`Write` with `file_path`, `content` set to `x`, then `content` again holding a long HTML file, streamed in 4-token engine steps. The cost is the endpoint's per-step time (`chat_completion_stream_generator` with the `glm47` tool parser), mean of the 195 steps at each mark.

| Output chars | 3K | 6K | 18K | 66K | 66K-256K mean | Whole stream (94K tokens) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 94.5 us | 210 us | 662 us | 2514 us | 6165 us | 116 s |
| This PR | 13.9 us | 13.5 us | 13.7 us | 15.1 us | 17.3 us | 0.8 s |

Both stream the same 7 frames (1,867 bytes).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server run</summary>

`vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice` from the CUDA CI image of main `8084f0624d`, one H200 per server, Model Runner V2, no speculative decoding. The PR server runs the same image with the changed file first on `PYTHONPATH`. A test logits processor forces the token ids of the cost-per-step stream at temperature 0, so both servers generate the same output; weights, engine, detokenizer, parsers and HTTP server are real. The client streams `/v1/chat/completions`, probes `/health` every 0.5 s and samples the API server process's CPU time.

| Run | Output | main: API-server CPU, busy, `/health` p99 / max | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forced, 64K chars | 23,464 tokens in 130 s | 16.1 s, 12%, 4.1 / 4.2 ms | 3.3 s, 2%, 0.78 / 0.91 ms |
| Forced, 256K chars | 93,963 tokens in 648 s | 214.7 s, 33%, 17.9 / 38.0 ms | 14.1 s, 2%, 0.83 / 2.1 ms |
| Forced, 64K chars, 8 streams at once | 8 x 23,464 tokens in 175 s | 109.7 s, 63%, 38.1 / 39.9 ms | 8.2 s, 5%, 0.82 / 1.0 ms |
| Unforced `Write` of an HTML page, thinking off | 41,649 argument chars in 45 s | 1.9 s, 4% | 2.0 s, 4% |

- Streamed arguments are identical between the two servers in every run, and across the 8 streams. The forced runs end at `{"file_path": "/repo/a.html", "content": "x` on both, the flush truncation under Details. The unforced run streams in 8,473 events on both, and its streamed arguments parse as JSON.
- No `/health` probe failed on either server.
- GLM-5.3 itself needs 8 GPUs per server and was not run. GLM-4.7-Flash uses the same `glm47` and `glm45` parsers.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.**
- A model that repeats a key replaces that key's value in the converted JSON. The JSON then stops extending `slot.streamed_json`, so `_compute_arg_delta` returns at `if prev and not safe_json.startswith(prev)`. That return comes before `slot.extend_open_value` is set.
- GLM sets `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, so every later delta containing `>` runs `arg_converter`, `_fix_arg_types` and `_safe_arg_prefix` over the whole argument text, then fails the same check.
- HTML, JSX and most code put a `>` in nearly every engine step. So the cost per step is linear in the argument and the total is quadratic. Merging deltas under load caps it near one conversion per pass, so on its own this saturates the event loop without failing liveness (replayed on `f4efba72e6`, which has the same path).

**Change.**
- On that failure, set `slot.extend_open_value` from `self._arg_value_extender(slot.args)` and set `slot.open_value_streams = False`. The existing branch at the top of `_compute_arg_delta` then returns `None` for a delta that only extends the open value, without converting.
- The extender returns `None` at the value's closing tag. The next delta then converts, and streaming resumes if the JSON extends `streamed_json` again. The final flush converts the full text as before.
- A delta that only extends the new value can make the JSON extend `streamed_json` again only when the new value starts with the text already streamed for the old one. That is the grouping difference in the equivalence table.

**Which parsers.** The change applies to every parser with an `arg_value_extender`. GLM's extender accepts an open value under a repeated key when that key is the last one. `_param_value_extender` (Qwen3) and `_dsml_arg_value_extender` (DeepSeek V3.2/V4) return `None` for any repeated key, so for them this installs nothing. On main they still pay a conversion per delta for a long value under a repeated key: 5.5 ms per step at 64K chars for `deepseek_v41` and 29.6 ms for `qwen3_coder`. Replayed at a production pod's measured API-server load, the `deepseek_v41` stream fails liveness and is killed at 335 s. Letting those extenders accept a repeated last key, as GLM's does, would be one follow-up per parser.

**Unchanged here and the same on main.** When the repeated key closes with a value that does not extend what was streamed, the flush withholds the final JSON, so the client gets truncated arguments. #53739 (open) addresses that flush.

**Not a duplicate.** #63385 (open) rewrites this block of `_compute_arg_delta` for incremental type repair and keeps the same early return on a failed prefix check. The overlap is textual, and whichever lands second rebases. #53739 (open) changes the flush fallback. #64196 (open) and #58780 (merged) cover DSML open values, and #61253 and #64535 (merged) cover GLM open values and closed pairs. No open PR covers conversions after a failed prefix check.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the analysis, the change, the tests and this description.

title: [Perf][Frontend] Decode streamed custom-tool input incrementally
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

For a Responses `custom` tool, every streamed argument delta re-runs `partial_json_parser` over the whole accumulated arguments, so the API server's cost per delta grows with the tool input. This decodes only the new tail of the input string. Follow-up to #57322.

## Claims

- Cost per streamed delta at 64K chars of tool input drops from 1.59 ms to 4.3 us, and at 256K chars from 14.9 ms to 11.4 us.
- On a real server (GLM-4.7-Flash, one H200), streaming a 256K-char `apply_patch` input over `/v1/responses` costs the API server 22 s of CPU against 563 s on main, and `/health` p99 stays at 0.9 ms against 42.8 ms.
- Streamed `response.custom_tool_call_input.delta` events are unchanged. After every delta the streamed payload equals `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix` of the arguments so far.
- Arguments that do not start the way `encode_custom_tool_input` writes them (`{"input": "`) keep the full decode, as does every delta after the payload string closes.
- No API, event or config change. Scope is non-Harmony Responses streaming (`responses/streaming_events.py`, `responses/utils.py`).

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `8084f0624d` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cost test | `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_streaming_events.py::TestCustomToolStreaming::test_payload_deltas_do_not_reparse_the_input` | `AssertionError: assert 44 == 404` | passed |
| New equivalence test | `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_streaming_events.py::TestCustomToolStreaming::test_streamed_payload_matches_prefix_decode` | passed | passed |
| Responses tests | `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses` | 313 passed, 85 errors | 316 passed, 85 errors (same set) |
| Fuzz (below) | 12,000 random inputs, 7 argument forms, random delta sizes | | 0 mismatches in 251,923 deltas |
| Server run (below) | GLM-4.7-Flash on one H200, forced `apply_patch` call to 256K chars, `/v1/responses` | API server 563.2 s CPU (88% busy), `/health` p99 42.8 ms | 22.2 s (3%), p99 0.86 ms |

Cost per `emit_simple_tool_call_delta` call, a patch streamed in 12-char deltas (one 4-token engine step):

| Tool input | 1K chars | 4K | 16K | 64K | 256K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 23.7 us | 80.8 us | 328 us | 1588 us | 14899 us |
| This PR | 3.9 us | 2.4 us | 2.5 us | 4.3 us | 11.4 us |

Tests and measurements ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The 85 errors are server tests that download models; the container has no Hugging Face access, and they fail the same on main. `ruff` and the repo's `mypy` hook pass on the changed files.

<details>
<summary>Fuzz</summary>

Each input is a random payload (quotes, backslashes, control characters, `\x85`, `\u3000`, CJK, emoji, ZWJ sequences), encoded with `ensure_ascii` on or off in one of 7 forms: the canonical shim, compact separators, `input` after another key, `input` before another key, raw unescaped text after the head, an invalid `\U` escape, and a dangling high surrogate before the close. The arguments go through `emit_simple_tool_call_open` and `emit_simple_tool_call_delta` in deltas of 1 to 64 chars. After every delta, `state.tool_call_payload` is compared with `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix(state.accumulated_text)`. Seeds 1-3, 4,000 inputs each: 251,923 deltas, 122,443 of them on the incremental path, 0 mismatches.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server run</summary>

`vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice` from the CUDA CI image of main `8084f0624d`, one H200 per server, Model Runner V2, no speculative decoding. The PR server runs the same image with the two changed files first on `PYTHONPATH`. The request is a streaming `/v1/responses` call with a `custom` tool `apply_patch`. A test logits processor forces the token ids of an `apply_patch` call carrying a patch at temperature 0, so both servers generate the same output; weights, engine, detokenizer, parsers and HTTP server are real. The client probes `/health` every 0.5 s and samples the API server process's CPU time.

| Run | Output | main: API-server CPU, busy, `/health` p99 / max | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forced, 64K chars | 23,290 tokens in 130 s | 53.7 s, 41%, 4.6 / 4.9 ms | 5.3 s, 4%, 0.86 / 1.5 ms |
| Forced, 256K chars | 93,110 tokens in 640 s | 563.2 s, 88%, 42.8 / 73.7 ms | 22.2 s, 3%, 0.86 / 1.3 ms |
| Forced, 64K chars, 8 streams at once | 8 x 23,290 tokens in 174 s | 157.4 s, 90%, 44.5 / 70.6 ms | 15.9 s, 9%, 1.3 / 1.6 ms |
| Unforced `apply_patch` of a new module, cut at 16,000 output tokens | 86 s | 40.1 s, 47%, 5.2 / 5.7 ms | 3.4 s, 4%, 0.85 / 0.86 ms |

- In every forced run, on both servers, the concatenated `response.custom_tool_call_input.delta` text equals the `done` input and the final item's input, and equals the forced patch exactly (64,014 and 256,014 chars), across the 8 streams too.
- The event count differs under load: main merges more tokens per event (51,406 events against 82,769 at 256K chars) because its event loop is busy. The streamed text is identical.
- The unforced run streams the same text on both servers. It ends at the token limit, inside the call; see Details.
- No `/health` probe failed on either server.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `emit_simple_tool_call_delta` appends each delta to `state.accumulated_text` and calls `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix` on all of it. That runs `partial_json_parser.loads`, which strips and completes the whole text in Python on every call. Cost per delta is linear in the input and the total is quadratic. Custom tools carry freeform input such as patches, so long inputs are the normal case for Codex-style clients.

**Change.**
- `extend_custom_tool_input_prefix` returns the same payload as `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix`, decoding only the arguments after the end of the previous call. It matches `partial_json_parser` on a partial string:
  - it decodes up to the last complete escape;
  - it holds back a trailing high-surrogate escape, so a pair is never split between calls;
  - it holds back trailing whitespace, which `partial_json_parser` strips before completing the string.
- When the tail does not decode as a JSON string body (the closing quote, a raw control character, an invalid escape), it returns `None`. The state then uses `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix` for the rest of the call.
- `SimpleStreamingState.tool_call_payload_end` records where decoding stopped, or -1 after the fallback. `tool_call_payload` already holds the decoded payload, since `_emit_custom_tool_input_delta` stores every payload it gets.

**Cost.** The work that stays linear in the input on each delta is C-level: `accumulated_text +=`, `payload + chunk` and the `startswith` in `_emit_custom_tool_input_delta`. That is the 11.4 us at 256K chars.

**Limitations.** Arguments in another form keep the full decode on every delta. The shim arguments come from the tool parsers' `json.dumps`, which writes the canonical head.

**Unchanged here and the same on main.** A call cut off by `max_output_tokens` leaves the shim JSON unclosed. `decode_custom_tool_input` then returns the raw arguments, so `emit_simple_tool_call_done` resends them in full as a last delta, and the `done` event and the output item carry the raw JSON. In the unforced server run, both servers stream 106,815 decoded chars followed by the 109,606-char raw `{"input": "...` text. That is a separate fix.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix`, `emit_simple_tool_call_delta` and Responses custom-tool streaming. #56418 (open) changes custom-tool naming for namespaces and leaves the streaming decode as is. #56285 (open, inactive since 2026-09-18) is the original that #57322 split out.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the analysis, the change, the tests and this description.

title: [Bugfix][UMBP] Copy every KV cache layout's per-head runs
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Split each layer's page into per-head runs in `data.py`, using the allocator's `compute_layout_strides`.
- Register the same runs in the `embedded.py` bulk path, falling back to per-range copies for a group whose stride doesn't match.
- Fail at startup instead of corrupting KV when a page is split and `kv_cache_layout` is unset.
- Round-trip all 6 layouts through the bulk and range paths in `test_umbp_embedded.py`.

UMBP took `cache.stride(0)` as the block stride and copied one contiguous page per layer, both on the range path in `data.py` and on the bulk path in `_register_load_layouts`, as noted in the review of #61794. Under LHBNC, the default with `ROCM_AITER_FA` and `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`, K and V are head planes spanning every block, so the engine fails at init with `KV region bytes (65536) exceed its stride (32768)`, and under BHLNC heads of different layers interleave inside a block row, so UMBP silently restores the wrong KV. `pytest -q v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_embedded.py -k every_kv_cache_layout` gives 4 failures without the fix and 12 passed with it. On MI350X with Qwen3-0.6B, 16 greedy tokens after a 192-token UMBP hit now match recompute under BHLNC (`TRITON_ATTN` with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BHLNC`) and under AITER shuffle-KV, and stay identical under the default layouts; the batch-invariant tests in `test_mori_token_e2e.py` likewise fail without the fix and pass with it under `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BHLNC` and `LHBNC`. Batch invariance rules out `ROCM_AITER_FA`, so those tests run on `TRITON_ATTN`, and AITER shuffle-KV is covered only by the greedy check above. Other layouts and MLA keep the single-span copy, and refusing LHBNC and BHLNC instead would make UMBP unusable with AITER shuffle-KV, since forcing LBHNC trips the shuffle decode path. LHBNC and BHLNC now issue one bulk range per head instead of one per layer, which I haven't benchmarked yet, and no open PR touches UMBP layout handling.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Model Loader] Refill weight-derived tensors in place on every post-load rerun
author: hao-aaron
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Keep tensors derived from weights (kernel constants, inverse scales, decode copies) at their startup addresses when post-load processing reruns on a weight reload, so captured CUDA graphs read the new values instead of freed memory. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477, rule 3). Builds on #64357 (merged); replaces aoshen02/vllm#180.

> **Direct reload.** #64336 (direct reload core) is now in main, and this branch has main merged. The direct reload tests that waited on it are back in this PR (see Validation). Results marked "direct" were measured with #64336 on both arms, before it merged.

## Claims

- After a weight reload with CUDA graphs on, MoE models whose post-load step derives kernel tensors serve the same output as before the reload. Without this PR they collapse:
  - gpt-oss-20b (TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct reload): GSM8K 0.39 → 0.01;
  - Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (CuteDSL): 0.90 → 0.01 with direct reload, 0.93 → 0.00 with layerwise reload.
- With direct reload (#64336), every tensor the MoE kernel reads keeps its cold-start address across a reload on these backends: TRT-LLM MXFP4/NVFP4, CuteDSL NVFP4 (including per-locality-domain shards), FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4/FP8, and per-tensor FP8 (including TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor's shuffled weights).
- After a draft-model weight update, the tensors the V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads (DFlash/DSpark context K/V weights and norms, including Beam's DFlash2 and Kimi-K3's DSpark drafters) keep their addresses. Without this PR, Beam DFlash2 acceptance fell from 7.03 to 4.89 after an update.
- The same holds for linear kernels that derive tensors in their post-load step (CUTLASS/Triton INT8 asymmetric `azp_adj`, CUTLASS W4A8, Marlin W4A8-INT8/FP8, b12x NVFP4 W4A16, ModelOpt block-quant), for the ROCm gpt-oss MXFP4 AITER shuffles, Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` and the bf16x3 router split, and for MXFP4 MoE on Marlin (gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.43 → 0.00 after a reload without this PR, 0.45 → 0.43 with it).
- Humming MoE: its post-load step runs once per quant method; direct reload refuses it (in main with #64336).
- Across 17 served models with direct reload (3 full-checkpoint updates each, measured by aoshen02), GSM8K holds after every update with this PR; on main it collapses on 8 of them (e.g. gpt-oss-120b 0.80 → 0.006, Kimi-K3 0.95 → 0.25).
- No cold-start change: GSM8K, throughput and KV cache match the base on 12 model/backend configurations, all within noise.

## Validation

All runs are on GB200 with nightly `4b47db922` plus this branch's Python files. "Base" = main `255431b5e` + #64357 + #64336.

**Reload with CUDA graphs on.** Start a server on a checkpoint, then record greedy tokens and top-1 logprobs on 8 fixed prompts (one request at a time) and a 300-question GSM8K slice. Push 2 weight updates through the NCCL weight-transfer engine and record the same again. "Greedy = fresh" compares with a fresh server on the last checkpoint sent; for a same-weight update the fresh server is the one before the update.

| Model, MoE backend, reload mode | Update | Base: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh | This PR: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.390 → **0.013**, 0/8 | 0.393 → 0.413, **8/8** |
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | 2 perturbed variants | → 0.007 (fresh 0.007), **0/8** | → 0.003 (fresh 0.003), **8/8** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.903 → **0.007** | 0.927 → 0.900 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, layerwise | same weights ×2 | 0.927 → **0.000** | 0.923 → 0.910 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (block), TRT-LLM FP8, direct and layerwise | same weights / perturbed | 8/8 | 8/8 |

- The "this PR" MXFP4/NVFP4 rows ran on `a4a859064`; the FP8 rows ran on this PR's first commit (`deaba72c6`). Since then the FP8 and MXFP4/NVFP4 paths changed only in comments and type annotations, and the direct-reload-only branch of `replace_parameter` moved to #64336.
- The perturbed variants flip the low bits of every FP4/FP8 payload and scale the scales by 2^k. These models score ≈0 themselves, so those rows are judged by token equality with the fresh server.
- One perturbed gpt-oss run (job 41424) gave 0/8 against the fresh server. This was not reproducible: three reruns gave 8/8.
- **NVFP4 CuteDSL** is not bit-reproducible across servers: two cold starts agree on 0–2 of 8 greedy sequences. GSM8K is its signal.
- **FP8 block quant** has no per-tensor derived constants, so it is a no-regression row.

**Served reload across models (aoshen02, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6543567448)).** Direct reload, GSM8K before → after 3 full-checkpoint updates, main vs this PR plus the review commits (aoshen02/vllm#227, now on this branch). Model runs used the tree before the final simplification commit, and before the ModelOpt gather-copy fix.

| Model | Cluster | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-120b | GB300 TP2 | 0.803 → **0.006** | 0.807 → 0.813 |
| gpt-oss-120b (chat) | GB200 | 0.940 → **0.005** | 0.939 → 0.941 |
| gpt-oss-20b | GB300 | 0.422 → **0.017** | 0.425 → 0.423 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (CuteDSL) | GB300 | 0.908 → **0.000** | 0.903 → 0.903 |
| Muse Spark NVFP4 | GB200 TP4 | 0.949 → **0.002** | 0.945 → 0.951 |

## Details

**Root cause.** `process_weights_after_loading` reruns on every reload (#64357), in both layerwise and direct mode. Many quant methods and models build tensors from the weights there as new allocations: kernel constants (SwiGLU alpha/beta/clamp folded by `g1_alphas`, `g1_scale_c`, inverse activation scales), experts objects rebuilt with fresh constants, decode-path copies. Captured CUDA graphs keep the startup pointers, so after a reload they read freed memory. Every weight is reloaded correctly, so comparing weight values cannot see it.

**Fix.**
- `replace_parameter` already refills parameters in place (unchanged here).
- `refill_derived(obj, name, tensor)` (new) refills a plain attribute in place when shape, dtype and device match, else replaces it. It never creates a parameter, and the held tensor must own its storage.
- MoE experts objects list the tensors their kernels read in `kept_constants`. `keep_constants(layer)` keeps them on the layer and points the new object at them. `FallbackExperts` forwards it to both wrapped experts.

<details>
<summary>Sites</summary>

- **MoE:**
  - TRT-LLM MXFP4/FP8/NVFP4 constants, including the MXFP4 LoRA experts (which declare the MXFP4 names themselves, since the MRO resolves the base experts' empty tuple first) and their FC1 bias index, now built at construction instead of lazily (Quark NVFP4 skips the experts' post-load step and keeps the constructor's).
  - FlashInfer CUTLASS SwiGLU constants, and `fake_input_scale` on its MXFP4-weight / MXFP8-activation path.
  - CuteDSL `per_token_global_scale` and per-locality-domain shards.
  - CUTLASS FP8/W4A8 strides.
  - TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor: the weight shuffle writes into the weights instead of rebinding `.data` (without alignment padding `w2` is the layer parameter itself).
  - FP8 per-tensor `g1/g2_alphas` and `a1/a2_gscale` (now also Quark W8A8 FP8).
  - NVFP4 `a1/a2_gscale`; compressed-tensors NVFP4 input scales.
- **Linear kernels:** CUTLASS/Triton INT8 asymmetric `azp_adj`, CUTLASS W4A8 `weight_chan_scale` and Marlin W4A8-INT8 `input_global_scale` (linear and compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE) go through `replace_parameter`; Marlin W4A8-FP8 scales its weight scales in place; b12x NVFP4 W4A16 and ModelOpt block-quant reuse the packed weight's storage, as b12x MXFP8 and tensor FP8 already do.
- **MXFP4 MoE on Marlin:** `begin_direct_reload` zeroes the storage it views back to checkpoint layout, since the loaders write only the unpadded region and the repack moved bytes into the padding. A stopgap: #64352 records and fills the padding right before the post-load step, which also covers layerwise reload and is what the load plan (#64418) needs.
- **ROCm:** the gpt-oss MXFP4 AITER CK shuffles (`AITER_MXFP4_BF16`, `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4`) return the shuffled tensors for `replace_parameter` instead of rebinding `.data`; Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` and `GateLinear._bf16x3_weight` use `refill_derived`.
- **Fused MoE gate:** with fused shared experts (e.g. ROCm AITER), Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 and AliceAI pass `shared_expert_gate` to `MoERunner`, which concatenated it with the router weight on the first forward and never rebuilt it, so routing kept the cold-start gates. `finalize_model_weights` now refills `_combined_gate_weight` in place after every load (`test_fused_gate_weight_refilled_after_reload`: fails on the previous head, passes with the fix; slurm 43121 / 43118).
- **Kimi-K3:** the specialized decode's packed MoE front, padded TP16 down projection, and KDA conv weight and norm, refreshed from a model-level post-load hook. The MLA inverse q/k scales. `PreparedMla` keeps the softmax and KV-cache scales as host floats; that is safe because no quant config gives K3's attention a KV-cache method, so its post-load step resets the q/k scales to 1.0 every run (a code comment says so).
- **GLM-5-next:** the indexer's fp32 head gate.
- **ModelOpt W4A16 NVFP4:** the gather copies (Qwen3-DSpark `markov_w2`), now refilled attributes instead of non-persistent buffers re-registered on every rerun.
- **Muse Spark:**
  - The residual alpha/beta coefficients and the NVIDIA NVFP4 MoE constants.
  - The router output multiplier, two patterns:
    - NVIDIA folds it in the router weight's loader (once per load).
    - AMD already keeps its post-load fold on main, guarded by a flag the loader clears, with its bf16x3 router planes refilled in place; unchanged here.
- **Drafters:** DFlash/DSpark context K/V weights and norm stacks (Qwen3, Laguna, Gemma4, Muse, Beam DFlash2, Kimi-K3 DSpark), Gemma4 MTP's gathered lm_head (built in the post-load step, outside inference mode), LiLiCorr buffers. Drafter weights are updated through the weight-transfer engines' draft target (`start_draft_weight_update`), whose finish reruns the drafter's post-load step.

</details>

**Limitations / known gaps.** Direct reload (#64336) is the target path; layerwise reload is planned for removal (F10 in the #54477 tracker), so its gaps are listed but not planned for fixing.

*Affect direct reload:*
- **Muse Spark MegaMoE:** `finalize_weights` returns early once transformed and drops checkpoint parameters, so a reload leaves the experts stale (or fails to load them), along with the hybrid TRT-LLM scales built there. Same on main. Tracked as F15.
- **DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE (MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, Step-5 NVIDIA): the L2 activation scale is a host float.** The max of `w2_input_scale` is passed by value to the Triton prepare kernel and to DeepGEMM `nvfp4_mega_moe`, so CUDA graphs keep the cold-start value when an update changes `w2_input_scale` (QAT-style updates such as verl's NVFP4 W4A4 send it on every sync). Fix: vllm-project/DeepGEMM#49 takes the scale as a device tensor, then vLLM bumps the pin and passes a buffer refilled in place. Tracked as F16; moving the max into PWAL is #64418 L2.
- **Qwen3 XPress:** `XPressHead.build_fused_buffers` builds its fused copies anew.
- **FlashInfer b12x NVFP4 MoE** (SM12x only, opt-in): it rebinds the weight scales to new storage and rebuilds their MMA views and `_fc2_input_scale`.
- **FlashInfer MoE-EP megakernel** rebinds the layer parameters to new adapter buffers on every rerun.
- **DeepSeek-V4 AMD:** e8m0 upcasts, compressor `cat` and the MegaMoE early return; handled separately in aoshen02/vllm#226. None of them runs for V4.1.
