title: [Perf][Qwen3.5] (NVIDIA path) Fused AR+norm+quant
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Overview

Fuses the consumer's activation quant into the TP all-reduce + Gemma RMSNorm on the Qwen3.5 NVIDIA path, via FlashInfer's `kARResidualRMSNormOutFP8Quant` / `kARResidualRMSNormOutFP4Quant`. Targets `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4`.

## Claims

- On `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` (MoE, no EP) at TP8, all **92 input norms per decode step** produce the static FP8 input of their projection (69 GDN `in_proj_qkvz` + 23 attn `qkv_proj`); 91 of them in the same kernel as the all-reduce (layer 0 has no all-reduce and uses #64509's norm-quant).
- The fused kernel's outputs (new residual, bf16 norm output, FP8 / NVFP4 codes, swizzled 128×4 NVFP4 scales) are bitwise identical to FlashInfer AR + norm followed by `scaled_fp8_quant` / `scaled_fp4_quant`.
- Above the FlashInfer workspace budget, static FP8 / NVFP4 use an explicit all-reduce + #64509's Triton norm-quant, keeping quant fusion at every batch size.
- Model-private: no torch.compile pass or custom op, and no changes to shared code.

## E2E perf

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` (MoE, no EP), TP8 across two 4× GB300 nodes (FlashInfer MNNVL all-reduce). `vllm bench serve`, random 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, 10 warmups, 8 × concurrency prompts, median TPOT. Base = merge-base `main`. Same two nodes for both arms, alternating; ranges over 3 base runs and 2 PR runs.

| Concurrency | Base TPOT | PR TPOT | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 8.28–8.30 ms | 7.95 ms | −4.0 to −4.2% |
| 16 | 17.24–17.38 ms | 17.18–17.34 ms | −1.2 to +0.6% |
| 64 | 39.89–40.33 ms | 39.47–39.84 ms | −2.1 to −0.1% |

At c1 the step saves ~0.34 ms, ~3.7 µs per fused input norm, consistent with removing the consumer's standalone FP8 quant kernel per norm. At c16/c64 the change is within run-to-run spread.

## E2E accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, full 1319-question set, 0 request errors, 8× B300, same node.

| Checkpoint | Config | Base | PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` | TP8 | 0.9773 | 0.9735 |

## Validation

- `tests/models/qwen3_5/test_fused_allreduce_norm_quant.py` (TP2, one spawn): `Qwen3_5RMSNorm.forward_fused` against the chain it replaces, with real ModelOpt static FP8 and NVFP4 linears as consumers.
  - AR + norm + quant, M = 1/17/333: residual, bf16 norm output, codes and NVFP4 scale bytes bitwise identical to FlashInfer AR + norm + `scaled_fp8_quant` / `scaled_fp4_quant`.
  - M = 8192 (above the TP2 workspace budget, Triton fallback): residual bitwise; norm output and codes within the Triton norm-quant's reduction-order tolerance (≤ 1 code step, ≤ 1e-4 of entries).
  - No all-reduce, and unquantized consumers: same paths as before this PR.
- `tests/models/qwen3_5/`: 50 passed on 2× GB300.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/ -q
```

CI: the existing `:nvidia: (B200) Qwen3.5` step (`qwen3-5-unit-tests-b200`), which runs `tests/models/qwen3_5/`, now requests 2 GPUs.

## Details

- `ops/fused_allreduce_norm_quant.py` calls `flashinfer_comm.allreduce_fusion` directly on the quant workspace (`get_fi_ar_quant_workspace`). It returns the `QuantizedActivation`, the bf16 norm output (GDN's `in_proj_ba` reads it) and the new residual, or None when the fused kernel does not apply.
- `Qwen3_5RMSNorm.forward_fused(x, residual, linear, *, write_y)` is the single entry point for the decoder-layer norms: it absorbs the deferred all-reduce when the norm was built with `reduce_inputs` (input norm: MLP output is a TP partial; post-attention norm: attention all-reduce deferred) and a residual is given, and quantizes for `linear`'s input when the norm can produce its key. `forward()` keeps the plain `(y, residual)` contract (final and MTP norms).

Dispatch (decoder-layer norms):

| Case | Path |
|---|---|
| TP>1, FlashInfer AR, static per-tensor FP8 consumer | AR + norm + FP8 (FlashInfer) |
| Same, NVFP4 with no K padding and `K % 64 == 0` | AR + norm + NVFP4 (FlashInfer) |
| Static FP8 / NVFP4, above the FlashInfer workspace budget | Explicit AR + Triton norm-quant |
| Everything else (block FP8, dynamic per-token FP8, padded NVFP4, BF16, W4A16, LoRA; MoE router input) | AR + norm; consumer quantizes as before |
| TP1 or non-FlashInfer-AR model path | Norm(-quant) from #64509, unchanged |

Complementary to @benchislett's draft #56530: that PR targets torch.compile/Inductor AR+norm+FP8 patterns with Gemma support and shared qkvz/ba quantization for 2.4T. This PR targets the eager NVIDIA path and retains the bf16 `ba` input; the open-PR search found no other change covering this scope.

title: [MiniMax-M3.1][PP] m31-pp-opt: NIXL pull from PP prefill stages and the Q8KV4 prefill workspace on SM10x
author: liusy58
body:
## Purpose

Brings into `m31-pp-opt` the remaining changes the MiniMax-M3.1 PP prefill benchmark ran with, so the branch reproduces it. Three commits on top of the branch head (`c905d49982`):

1. **Pair KV regions by layer for every transfer**: #63416 as one commit (@Dao007forever, with @NickLucche).
2. **Pull KV from pipeline-parallel prefill stages**: #64397, stacked on #63416. Both stay open against `main` for review; this branch only carries them.
3. **Reserve the Q8KV4 prefill workspace on every SM10x GPU** (new). The Q8KV4 prefill split workspace was reserved only on Rubin (SM107). On B200/B300 the prefill allocated its split partials on every step, about 8 GiB at 32K tokens, outside memory profiling. So PP2 with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` ran out of memory on its first long prefill:
   ```
   torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 8.00 GiB. GPU 1 has a total capacity of 267.68 GiB of which 458.25 MiB is free.
   ```
   This commit reserves the workspace once, for the largest batch, on the whole SM10x family.

## Test Plan

- NIXL unit tests:
  ```bash
  pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
         tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
         tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
  ```
- The full PP prefill benchmark, run with this branch on `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-335dd77b0`. The setup was one 8-GPU HGX B300 node and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash with the NVFP4 KV cache. TP2, DEP2 and PP2 were each screened, swept and repeated over three seeds, all at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`.

## Test Result

- NIXL: the 12 files of commits 1-2 are byte-identical to #64397's head. On a CPU-only machine, the failure set of the tests above is identical to #64397's head; the failures come from the missing CUDA/NIXL environment.
- Workspace: without commit 3, PP2 with the CuTe DSL MoE ran out of memory on the first long prefill at 0.9. With it, every PP2 config ran screening, sweeps and finals at 0.9 with no out-of-memory error.
- Accuracy: GSM8K (all 1,319 questions) is 0.9613 for PP2's final config, against 0.9568 for the TP2 reference. Every config also matched the reference's first token on 64 long prompts (top-1 agreement 1.0).

AI assistance: commits 1-2 were assembled with Claude Code from the existing PRs; commit 3 and the benchmark runs were done with Claude Code and reviewed by the submitter.

title: [ROCm][CI] Run MI355 MoE Kernels on a full MI355 instead of DPX
author: djramic
body:
## Purpose
`:amd: (MI355 DPX) MoE Kernels` failed in shards 2-5 of the nightly [amd-ci#15747](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15747). Each of these shards ran one case of `test_aiter_moe_sort_backend_dispatch_env_matrix_mxfp4` (added in #62976), and all four failed with `Expected this MXFP4 DSV4 shape to set aiter's internal output_aux flag`. Shard 1 passed only because pytest-shard placed none of the four cases there.

The test relies on aiter selecting a tuned DSV4 MXMOE kernel, which sets `output_aux`. aiter keys its tuned MoE configs by `(gfx, cu_num, ...)`, and `dsv41_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` only has `gfx950,256` rows. The DPX agents expose 128-CU partitions, so aiter falls back to a heuristic FlyDSL config without `output_aux`. No gfx950 MoE config in aiter has 128-CU rows.

This PR moves the step from `mi355_dpx` to `mi355_1` (full MI355X, 256 CUs). 

## Test Plan
Full MI355X (gfx950, SPX, 256 CUs), in the `rocm/vllm-dev:ci_base` image with aiter 0.1.26, vLLM at 617135eed3.
The whole step ran as in CI: its three commands from `test-amd.yaml`, 5 shards in parallel with one GPU each, and the `run-amd-test.sh` environment.
The DSV4 cases were also run on their own:
```bash
cd tests
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -v -s kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py \
  -k test_aiter_moe_sort_backend_dispatch_env_matrix_mxfp4
```

## Test Result

|---|---|---|
| 1 | passed | passed (7.4 min) |

title: [Bugfix][Mistral] Carry token ids in stream state for byte-fallback tokens
author: cjackal
body:
## Overview

Fix streaming derender for Tekken-based Mistral tokenizers, where a byte-fallback token in the decode window breaks the client-carried `stream_state`.

The `/v1/responses` corruption originally reported here was fixed by #65118; this PR only covers the derender endpoints.

## Claims

- Streaming `/v1/completions/derender` and `/v1/chat/completions/derender` keep working when the decode window contains a byte-fallback token instead of rejecting the request.
- With a parser configured, chat derender for `MistralTokenizer` now uses the request's `skip_special_tokens`, matching serving after #65118.


## Validation

### Unit test

```shell
python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -v

# 124 passed, 1 xfailed in 76.12s
```

### E2E test

#### Server:

```shell
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B \
  --config-format mistral \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --reasoning-parser mistral \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser mistral \
  --load-format mistral
```

#### Client:

**req.json**

```json
{
  "model": "mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B",
  "stream": false,
  "max_output_tokens": 100,
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "name": "get_weather",
      "description": "Get current weather for a location",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}, "unit": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["location"]
      }
    }
  ],
  "input": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "서울의 날씨가 어때?"},
    {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "udM7soqYx", "name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"location\":\"서울\",\"unit\":\"celsius\"}"},
    {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "udM7soqYx", "output": "서울의 현재 날씨: 22°C, 맑음, 습도 60%"}
  ]
}
```

**Request**

```shell
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d@/tmp/req.json | jq .output[0].content
```

#### Result:

- main: `[{"text": "사용자가 \"서울의 날씨가 어���?\"라고 물어��고, get_weather 함수를 호출해서 ...`
- PR: `[{"text": "사용자가 \"서울의 날씨가 어때?\"라고 물어봤고, get_weather 함수를 호출해서 ...`

## Details

- Root cause: `MistralTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens` returns raw `bytes` for byte-fallback tokens. This happens with `skip_special_tokens=True` too, so it already affects `main`. Streaming derender stored those pieces in `DerenderStreamState.prev_tokens: list[str]`, which goes through JSON between chunks. An incomplete UTF-8 piece can't be carried there.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Honor draft moe/attention backend overrides for MRV2 standalone draft model
author: aoshen02
body:
Proposed title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Honor draft moe/attention backend overrides for MRV2 standalone draft model

## Purpose

With model runner V2, `method: draft_model` (`StandaloneARSpeculator`) silently ignores `moe_backend` and `attention_backend` from `--speculative-config`. The draft inherits the target's `--moe-backend` / `--attention-backend` instead.

- V1 honors all three draft overrides (`moe_backend`, `attention_backend`, `kv_cache_dtype`) through `_create_draft_vllm_config` in `llm_base_proposer.py`, which `draft_model.py` inherits (#37880, #39930).
- The V2 standalone drafter (#43091) never got them. #61240 added `kv_cache_dtype` by hand. #57312 moved the V2 EAGLE/MTP overrides into `SpeculativeConfig.apply_draft_overrides` but did not touch the standalone path.

The fix builds the draft `VllmConfig` from `spec.apply_draft_overrides(self.vllm_config)`, the same way `load_eagle_model` does, and removes the hand-written `kv_cache_dtype` branch. Any new entry in `_DRAFT_VLLM_CONFIG_OVERRIDES` now reaches this drafter too.

`attn_vllm_config` is unchanged. `init_attn_backend` takes each group's backend from the constructed layer (`attn_layers[name].get_attn_backend()`), and the draft layers are built under the overridden config, so their builders already match the draft backend. No metadata builder reads `attention_config.backend` or `kernel_config.moe_backend`. The `kv_cache_dtype` condition is still needed because builders read `cache_config.cache_dtype`.

## Test Plan

- Extended `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_standalone_draft_kv_dtype_override`. It now also parametrizes the draft `moe_backend` / `attention_backend`, and asserts that the draft config gets them when set, keeps the target's when unset, and leaves the target config untouched.
- Ran this test plus `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_moe_backend_override.py` and `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_attention_backend_override.py`.
- E2E on one GB200 GPU with a recent nightly image and the patched `speculator.py` overlaid. Model runner V2 was on, with `ibm-granite/granite-3.0-1b-a400m-base` as both target and draft. Target flags: `--moe-backend triton --attention-backend FLASHINFER`. Speculative config: `{"method": "draft_model", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "moe_backend": "flashinfer_cutlass", "attention_backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}`. Three greedy prompts, 48 tokens each. I read the backends from the loaded target and draft modules.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 35 passed. Without the fix, the 6 new override cases fail with `assert 'flashinfer_cutlass' == 'triton'`.
- E2E:

| | target attn / MoE | draft attn / MoE | accepted / drafted |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | FLASHINFER / TRITON | FLASHINFER / TRITON (overrides ignored) | 108 / 108 |
| after | FLASHINFER / TRITON | TRITON_ATTN / FLASHINFER_CUTLASS | 108 / 111 |

  Greedy outputs are identical in both runs. The small acceptance drop is expected now that the draft runs different kernels than the target.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the standalone draft config path. #62193 adds a `batch_invariant` entry to `_DRAFT_VLLM_CONFIG_OVERRIDES`. This PR does not include it, but once that lands, the entry will also apply to the standalone drafter.
- Possible overlap: #60989 (AR speculator refactor / draft CUDA graph) edits `standalone_ar/speculator.py` but not `load_draft_model`, so any conflict should be trivial. #63205 (speculator config classes) adds `standalone_ar/config.py` and edits `vllm/config/speculative.py` next to `apply_draft_overrides`, but not the method itself. I don't expect a semantic conflict with either.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm][HY4] Use breakable graphs without torch.compile
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Overview

Remove `torch.compile` support from the HY4 AMD backbone and use breakable HIP graphs by default, matching the NVIDIA execution approach. This follows #57526 while retaining graph capture for prefill and decode.

## Claims

- Retain HIP graph replay without compiling the AMD backbone.
- Improve output throughput by 18.7% and median TPOT by 15.6% in the measured C8 decode workload.

## Validation

Benchmarked public `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8` on upstream `b91df5a9`, 8× MI355X, TP8/MRV2, BF16 activations/KV, identical prompts and serving settings, and no speculation or prefix caching. Ran compiled → no compile → compiled, three repeats per arm; the table compares medians of six compiled controls and three no-compile runs.
The client streams `/v1/completions` with seeded synthetic token prompts, temperature 0 and `ignore_eos=true`.

| Workload (concurrency; input/output tokens) | Compiled tok/s | No compile tok/s | Change | Compiled TPOT | No compile TPOT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C1; 1024/256 | 36.77 | 42.62 | +15.9% | 26.26 ms | 21.88 ms |
| C8; 4096/600 | 245.71 | 291.59 | **+18.7%** | 30.65 ms | **25.86 ms (−15.6%)** |
| C8; 4096/16 | 42.91 | 44.89 | +4.6% | 132.25 ms | 127.13 ms |
| C8; mixed 128–6144/32–256 | 181.30 | 206.61 | +14.0% | 36.76 ms | 31.68 ms |

The main C8 throughput ranges were 241.71–249.22 versus 286.54–293.28 tok/s. Mixed-workload TTFT increased 5.5% (555→586 ms).

Compilation freezes prefill-sized MXFP8 GEMM tiles into small-batch decode. Without it, graph capture selects decode-specific tiles: `_mxfp8_linear_kernel.kd` summed duration falls **7.534→2.437 ms per rank/step**, with the same 411 calls. Forcing prefill tiles back reproduces 69% of this kernel-time penalty. Both paths retain HIP graph replay; attention and communication barely change. These kernel sums are not wall-clock latency.

### GPQA-Diamond

Parent `f2ba523d67` versus patch `c4f150d739`, same checkpoint: all 198 questions, zero-shot chat, temperature 0.9/top-p 1.0, matched prompts and seeds, 65,536 output-token limit and concurrency 15. Scores use explicit final-answer exact match; blank/unextractable answers count as wrong.

| Dataset | Compiled | No compile | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPQA-Diamond | 91.92% (182/198) | 92.42% (183/198) | +0.51 pp |

Truncations decreased from 5 to 3. Other accuracy discrepancies remain under investigation; this GPQA result alone does not establish overall accuracy parity.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -v -s`: **6 passed** on AMD. The new default-graph regression fails on the unmodified parent and passes with this patch.

No duplicate removal PR was found during the HY4 compile/breakable-graph search. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Bound SM100 decode indexer logits with query-row chunks
author: Pb314314
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On SM100, compute the sparse indexer's decode logits in chunks of query rows, each at most `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (default 2 GiB), instead of one tensor for all decode rows of a step. This applies to every model that uses this indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, V4, V4.1, GLM-5.x (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), HY-V4), with either the FP8 (default) or the MXFP4 indexer cache.

It removes most of the memory these logits take at long context, and it unblocks the CUDA graph refactor (#63406), whose wide decode graphs would otherwise hold the full logits.

### Motivation

The sparse indexer scores every cached KV position of a request for each query row and keeps the top-k (512 for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, 2048 for V3.2 and GLM-5.x). On SM100, the decode scores come from one DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` call, which writes a dense BF16 tensor of shape `[decode rows, W]`:

- `decode rows` = requests × (1 + speculative tokens);
- `W` = `max_model_len / compress_ratio`, fixed by the model length, not by the requests' actual context.

At 1M context with 8192 decode rows this tensor is 16 GiB, and main's memory profile reserves it plus an FP32 copy (48 GiB). The copy is no longer made at runtime, since persistent top-k reads BF16 (#64138). The tensor costs memory in two places:

- **Eager and PIECEWISE steps** (mixed prefill + decode steps, and decode steps wider than the largest FULL graph) allocate it at runtime. So the memory profile reserves the worst case, and that memory is taken from the KV cache.
- **FULL CUDA graphs** allocate it inside the graph memory pool, which grows with the widest captured decode graph. #63406 captures decode graphs up to the full `max_num_seqs`.

### Change

When a step's decode logits would exceed the budget, the decode rows are split into balanced, 16-row-aligned chunks. Each chunk runs the same operations as the unchunked path on its own rows, and writes its rows of the shared top-k output:

1. DeepGEMM schedule metadata for the chunk;
2. logits;
3. V4.1 candidate-block selection or masking;
4. top-k.

Rows are independent, so nothing is merged across chunks. A step that fits the budget runs the existing single call unchanged, and so do prefill rows (already chunked by `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`). The memory profile reserves one BF16 chunk instead of every decode row plus an FP32 copy.

## Results

In every table, **Baseline** means decode logits are not chunked (main, or budget `0` on the same build), and **After PR** means this PR with the default 2 GiB budget. Unless noted: one GB200 node (4 GPUs), FP8 KV cache, DSpark with 7 speculative tokens for DeepSeek-V4.1, MTP with 5 for GLM-5.3, and ShareGPT prompts with their recorded output lengths. Memory numbers come from the startup log and are deterministic.

### Memory

On main (default memory settings, extensible KV cache):

| Model and config | | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FP8 indexer cache (default), 1M, TP4+EP, `max_num_seqs` 512 | memory-profile activation peak | 26.31 GiB | 5.23 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 49.67 GiB | **86.02 GiB (+73%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, dense candidate consumers (`indexer_sparse_logits=false`), 1M, `max_num_seqs` 1024 | memory-profile activation peak | 49.49 GiB | 4.41 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 7.62 GiB | **86.51 GiB** |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (FP8 indexer cache), 256K, TP4+EP | memory-profile activation peak | 11.39 GiB | 4.37 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 38.93 GiB | **51.25 GiB (+32%)** |

With #63406 (decode graphs up to `max_num_seqs`), CUDA graph memory per GPU, KV cache fixed:

| Model and config | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FP8 indexer cache, 1M, TP4+EP, 512 seqs | 22.36 GiB | **12.36 GiB** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, 1M, TP4+EP, 512 seqs | 22.35 GiB | **12.35 GiB** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, 1M, DP4+EP, 1024 seqs per rank | 39.70 GiB | **15.71 GiB** |

For GLM-5.3 at 256K with #63406, the widest decode graph (4092 rows) already fits the budget, so graph memory is unchanged (12.35 GiB). The smaller profile reservation still raises its KV cache from 590,464 to 745,984 tokens.

### Performance

Output tok/s; each cell lists every server launch, and the change is between the means. Launches of the two versions run on the same node unless noted.

| Setting | Workload | Decode rows per step | Baseline | After PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #63406, V4.1 FP8, TP4+EP | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 13114 / 12939 | 13008 / 12834 | −0.8% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 4045 / 4055 | 4050 / 3994 | −0.7% |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4, TP4+EP ¹ | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 12828 / 12938 / 12808 | 12858 / 12759 / 12840 | −0.3% |
| | 256 concurrent | up to 2048, chunked | 11803 / 11772 | 11833 / 11848 | +0.4% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 4091 / 4106 / 4076 | 4135 / 4097 / 3958 | −0.7% |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4, DP4+EP, AV ² | random 128 in / 512 out, 2048 concurrent | up to ~4096 per rank, chunked | 57855 / 55920 | 56854 / 56687 | −0.2% |
| | same, 4096 concurrent | up to 8192 per rank, chunked | 62059 / 61396 | 61297 / 61948 | −0.2% |
| #63406, GLM-5.3, TP4+EP | 256 concurrent | up to 1536 | 7155 | 7034 | −1.7% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 192 | 2569 | 2597 | +1.1% |
| main, V4.1 FP8, TP4+EP | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 5799 / 5920 | 5890 / 6067 | +2.0% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 3509 / 3643 | 3548 / 3648 | +0.6% |
| main, V4.1 MXFP4, dense consumers, 1024 seqs | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 5666 | 5550 | −2.0% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 3324 | 3398 | +2.2% |
| main, GLM-5.3, TP4+EP | 256 concurrent | up to 1536 | 3966 | 4043 | +1.9% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 192 | 2368 | 2409 | +1.7% |

¹ Budget sweep below; KV fixed at 16 GiB. ² Adaptive verification on, KV fixed at 16 GiB.

Steps that do not chunk run the same code as Baseline, so single-launch differences of about ±2% in those rows are run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Other runs: long outputs, and a worst-case graph setup</summary>

Long outputs on main (V4.1 MXFP4, default candidate logits, 1M, TP4+EP, random 1K in / 4K out, one launch each):

| Concurrency | Chunked | Baseline | After PR | Change | TPOT p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | no | 5280 | 4873 | −7.7% | 5.39 → 5.14 ms |
| 128 | no | 9972 | 9713 | −2.6% | 10.45 → 10.60 ms |
| 256 | yes | 4596 | 4488 | −2.3% | 46.2 → 49.0 ms |

The 32 and 128 rows run identical code in both versions, so they bound the noise of these short runs.

Worst case: `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with sparse capture sizes `[8, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]` on main, V4.1 MXFP4, adaptive verification, KV fixed at 16 GiB, random 128 in. Every mixed step runs the whole model eagerly, so each extra chunk adds host launches.

| Topology | Workload | Baseline | After PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP4+EP, 1024 seqs per rank | 2048 concurrent, 512 out | 39226 / 40143 | 37518 / 36456 | −6.8% |
| | 4096 concurrent, 512 out | 34566 / 35732 | 24452 / 34633 | −16% (−1.5% without the 24452 launch) |
| TP4+EP, 1024 seqs | 1024 concurrent, 1024 out | 17054 / 15729 | 15973 / 16658 | −0.5% |

Deployments with this setup and workload should use the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, or raise `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (e.g. to 4096). Graph memory in this setup: DP4 36.46 → 12.44 GiB, TP4 32.08 → 10.12 GiB per GPU. With 2048 seqs, TP4 Baseline cannot start on main (its profile reserves 96 GiB for decode logits).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Choosing the 2 GiB default</summary>

#63406, V4.1 MXFP4, TP4+EP, 512 seqs, KV fixed at 16 GiB; one column per budget.

| | Baseline (0) | 1 GiB | **2 GiB** | 4 GiB | 6 GiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph memory | 22.35 GiB | 10.36 GiB | **12.35 GiB** | 14.35 GiB | 20.35 GiB |
| CUDA graph memory, adaptive verification | 22.51 GiB | 10.52 GiB | **12.52 GiB** | 14.51 GiB | 20.51 GiB |
| 512 concurrent | 12828 / 12938 / 12808 | – | 12858 / 12759 / 12840 (−0.3%) | 12906 / 12926 (+0.3%) | 12931 / 12757 (−0.3%) |
| 32 concurrent | 4091 / 4106 / 4076 | – | 4135 / 4097 / 3958 (−0.7%) | 4050 / 4095 (−0.6%) | 4114 / 4084 (0.0%) |
| adaptive verification, 512 concurrent | 16573 / 16815 / 16690 | – | 16149 / 17112 / 16944 (+0.3%) | 16819 / 17007 (+1.3%) | 16495 / 17060 (+0.5%) |
| adaptive verification, 512 concurrent, 9216 prompts | 18121 / 17942 / 17971 | 18059 / 18209 / 17912 (+0.3%) | 18082 / 17990 / 18041 (+0.1%) | – | – |
| adaptive verification, 128 concurrent | 10037 / 10134 / 10045 | 10245 / 10250 / 10098 (+1.2%) | 10224 / 10179 / 10150 (+1.1%) | – | – |

2 GiB is the smallest budget that leaves every step with up to 1024 decode rows at 1M (128 requests × 8 tokens) unchunked. 1 GiB saves 2 GiB more but chunks from 512 rows. 4 and 6 GiB keep 2 and 8 GiB more graph memory without a measurable gain.
</details>

### Correctness

**Chunked vs single call, on the real kernels.** A standalone check on GB200 runs DeepGEMM logits, candidate selection or masking, and the `auto` or `persistent` top-k. It compares chunking against a single call for FP8 and MXFP4 caches, 1000–8192 rows, W from 256K to 1M, and chunks down to ≤ 64 rows (which take the cooperative top-k and an FP32 upcast):

- chunked logits are bit-identical to the single call;
- candidate blocks are identical;
- the selected top-k values match an exact `torch.topk` on the same logits in every row (indices may differ only among tied scores).

The same check shows that main's single call returns a wrong top-k once one call exceeds 2^32 logits elements. At 1M context this happens above about 4094 rows: 4097 of 8192 rows were wrong, for both cache types and both top-k backends, while the logits themselves were correct. At the default budget a chunk holds at most 2^30 elements, so this PR avoids it. A separate fix for the top-k kernel's addressing will follow.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions, greedy). Same build launched repeatedly varies by up to ~1.8 points.

| Setting | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|
| #63406, V4.1 FP8 | 0.904 / 0.901 | 0.898 / 0.899 |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4 | 0.900 / 0.904 / 0.897 | 0.913 / 0.897 / 0.895 |
| #63406, GLM-5.3 | 0.907 | 0.904 |
| main, V4.1 FP8 | 0.895 / 0.903 | 0.911 / 0.894 |
| main, V4.1 MXFP4, dense consumers | 0.897 | 0.893 |
| main, GLM-5.3 | 0.916 | 0.918 |

GSM8K runs 256 concurrent requests (up to 2048 decode rows for V4.1), so these runs exercise chunked steps.

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "decode_chunk or sparse_indexer or persistent"` on GB200: 348 passed, 4 skipped. The new tests check that chunks cover every row once, respect alignment, balance and the budget, and handle zero, fitting and invalid budgets.

## Details

- **Where it applies:** SM100, top-k backend `auto` or `persistent`, top-k ∈ {512, 1024, 2048}, no decode or prefill context parallelism. Both indexer cache types, and V4.1's candidate source and masked candidate consumer layers. V4.1's compact sparse consumers (`indexer_sparse_logits`) already score only candidate blocks and are unchanged.
- **Mixed steps:** chunking depends only on the number of decode rows, so it also applies to the decode rows of a mixed prefill + decode step; prefill rows are unchanged. These steps run PIECEWISE or eager, where each extra chunk adds a few kernel launches.
- **When to raise the budget:** a step chunks once its decode rows exceed `budget / (2 bytes × W)` on the widest indexer layer (1024 rows at 1M with the default). If running requests × (1 + speculative tokens) is usually above that and the KV cache is not the bottleneck, raise `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (for example to 4096). At 1M, keep it below 8192, where one call would exceed 2^32 elements; `0` turns chunking off.
- **Disaggregated prefill/decode:** prefill rows are unchanged, and prefill instances also get the smaller reservation. The decode instance produces the first token, so time to first token includes one decode step, which pays the chunking cost above if that step is wider than the limit.
- **Interaction with #64580:** #64580 would make SM100 logits FP32 again by default. Whichever PR lands second must pass the logits dtype to the chunk's `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` call and size the budget by the logits element size.
- **Models measured:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (FP8 and MXFP4 indexer caches) and GLM-5.3-NVFP4. DeepSeek-V3.2, V4 and HY-V4 run the same indexer code but were not measured end to end; at their usual context lengths (≤ 256K) decode steps chunk only above 4096+ rows, so the main change for them is the smaller memory-profile reservation.
- **Not covered:** decode context parallelism, non-default top-k backends (e.g. `deep_select`), the V4.1 GB300 specialized decode path, and indexers with their own implementation (GLM-5-Next, MiniMax-M3) keep their current path.

## Not a duplicate

#62169 chunks the SM90 / SM120 uniform decode path by request, and excludes SM100 varlen decode. No other open PR bounds the SM100 decode logits.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Vectorize first-layer HC expansion copy
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's first decoder layer builds its `hc_mult` residual streams with `x.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, hc_mult, -1).contiguous()`. This replaces it with `hc_expand`, a small Triton copy that reads each input element once and stores it to every stream. The output is the same contiguous `[M, hc_mult, H]` tensor, bit for bit.

The kernel lives in the DeepSeek-V4.1 mHC ops (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mhc.py`) and is called directly; DSv4.1 does not run under `torch.compile`, so no custom op is registered. Shared mHC kernels are unchanged.

## Results

GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP1 / DP2 / EP2, DSpark K=5, FlashInfer autotune on. Full model-forward latency (target + DSpark), FI → HC → FI per shape, 3 samples × 5 iterations, 5 s warmup.

| Tokens / rank | Main | This PR | Reduction | Main drift |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8192 | 84.755 ms | 84.214 ms | 0.638% | +0.188% |
| 32768 | 292.447 ms | 291.563 ms | 0.302% | +0.276% |

- Hidden states and draft tokens are bitwise identical to main on both ranks.
- A single sequence; earlier prototype rounds gave 0.38% / 0.32% at 32K and no gain at 8K, so only the 32K gain is claimed.
- This revision moves the kernel into DeepSeek-V4.1 with the same indexing and launch. Re-checked against the measured commit (`be1a44dee6`) on 6 decode/prefill shapes, old → new → old in fresh processes: outputs bitwise identical, latency equal or up to 0.3% faster (within run-to-run drift).
- Copy alone at `[32768, 5120]`, `hc_mult=4`, BF16: 1321 → 241 µs (CUPTI, cold L2). PTX uses `ld.global.v4.b32` / `st.global.v4.b32`.

GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, max 1024 tokens, same FI tactics):

| Concurrency | Main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1192 (90.372%) | 1192 (90.372%), all responses and token counts identical |
| 32 | 1205 (91.357%) | 1198 (90.826%) |

C32 batches are dynamic and main itself is not output-stable there (two main runs flip 31 questions each way), so equal C32 accuracy is not claimed. 60 passkey cases at 8K/16K/32K match main's full responses and token counts.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k hc_expand -v
```

GB300: 20 passed. `pre-commit` passes.

The test checks bitwise equality with `expand().contiguous()` in eager mode and under CUDA graph replay, for empty, strided and odd-sized inputs, NaN and −0.0. It runs in the existing B200 mHC CI job.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

Both arms carry the benchmark-only warmup fix from #63876 (not part of this PR) and use the same checkpoint, prompt tokens and tuned FI cache.

```bash
python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward --model "$MODEL" \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 196608 \
```

title: [Kernel] Qwen4Exp: compute HyperConnection and PLE gate row offsets in int64
author: seanbell
body:
## Overview

The Qwen4Exp HyperConnection kernels (`nvidia/ops/hc.py`, `amd/ops/hc.py`) and the PLE gate kernel (`common/ops/ple.py`) compute each token row's address as `ptr + row * stride` with `row = tl.program_id(0)`, so the product is evaluated in int32 and wraps once it exceeds 2**31 - 1. This widens the row index to int64 once per kernel.

## Claims

- For a 2560-wide hidden state with 4 HC streams, the HC row stride is 10240 elements and the PLE key/value row stride is 12800. The products wrap from row 209,716 and row 167,773 respectively, so any forward pass over 167,774 or more tokens loads and stores at the wrong rows. The startup profile run alone reaches this when `max_num_batched_tokens >= 167,774`.
- After the change every row offset in the 11 kernels is int64. Column, group, stream and tile indices stay int32.

## Validation

- `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_row_offsets.py` (new) runs every HC op and `ple_gate` on inputs whose third row starts 2**31 + 8192 elements into its storage. It compares the result with the same rows stored contiguously, with `atol=0, rtol=0`. On CPU under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`:
  - on `main` (`212f3666`) both tests crash (SIGSEGV);
  - on this branch both pass.
- Compiled for sm90 with Triton 3.6.0, no GPU needed: `_grouped_gemma_rmsnorm_kernel` on `main` emits `arith.muli %row, %stride_x : i32` (PTX `mul.lo.s32`), and on this branch `arith.muli %row_1, %x : i64`. `_ple_gate_kernel` behaves the same way for `t * key_rs`, `t * value_rs` and `t * HC * H`.
- A CPU-interpreter run of each kernel at rows 209,715 / 209,716 / 262,143 (and 167,772 / 167,773 for the PLE gate), with Flash-Next-sized row strides, reads the row at the int32-wrapped offset on `main`. On this branch it reads the right row. The NVIDIA and AMD variants behave the same.
- Not run on a GPU, and performance was not measured. The change adds one int64 conversion per program. The AMD kernels get the identical one-line change but no ROCm test.

## Details

- `hc_silu`'s own row strides (336/320) stay below the limit at these sizes. It is widened anyway so that every kernel in the file follows one rule.
- The test is in a new file because `test_hc_ops.py` is CUDA-only at module level, and some of its bit-exact comparisons do not hold under the interpreter. The new file holds only stride-invariance checks. It is added to the `models_basic` test area.

title: [CPU][Perf] Speed up GDN speculative-decode recurrent update
author: ekintel
body:
**Purpose:** Speed up `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_spec_cpu`, which runs in every GDN layer during speculative-decode verify on CPU (e.g. Qwen3.5/3.6 with DFlash/MTP).
- Work is split over (sequence, value head, 64-column block) instead of (sequence, value head). At batch 1, Qwen3.6 now has 64 work items instead of 32.
- Each item loads its fp32 state block once and keeps it in cache across all draft tokens. The old kernel re-read the previous slot twice per token.
- The per-token intermediate states, which are only read again on a later step, are written with streaming stores (AVX-512, aligned addresses). This avoids the read-for-ownership on every store.

**Test plan:**
- New `test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_spec_cpu`: fp32/bf16/fp16 state; uneven, empty and 0-accepted rows; value dim not a multiple of the vector width. All existing GDN CPU tests pass.
- New `benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_gdn_spec.py`: cold-state, 30 layers.

**Results (GCP c4-standard-48, 23 threads):**
- Kernel, 30 layers, 8 tokens: fp32 state 9.01 → 4.91 ms (−45%); bf16 state 4.90 → 2.61 ms (−47%).
- End-to-end, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash2 (7 speculative tokens), HumanEval, concurrency 1: median ITL 127.85 → 120.08 ms (−6.1%), mean TPOT 23.23 → 22.07 ms (−5.0%), output throughput 38.17 → 39.92 tok/s (+4.6%). Acceptance length 5.58 vs 5.53.

**Kernel, batch scaling (fp32 state, 8 tokens per request, 30 layers):**

 | batch | before | after |
 |---|---|---|
 | 1 | 8.97 ms | 5.45 ms (−39%) |
 | 4 | 28.60 ms | 20.77 ms (−27%) |
 | 16 | 110.86 ms | 82.89 ms (−25%) |

 **Accuracy:** gsm8k (5-shot, limit 200) through the full DFlash2 + Qwen3.6-35B-A3B server: 0.290 after vs 0.295 before (±0.032 standard error). Outputs are not bit-identical: the summation order changed, and with bf16/fp16 state the running state stays fp32 between draft tokens within a step.

 **Tests:**
 - `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py`: 224 passed, including the new spec-kernel test with an unaligned state cache.
 - `pytest tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py -k mtp`: Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN) with MTP, 1 passed.

Assisted by GHCP.

title: [Config] Move V2-only checks into V1 model runner unsupported features
author: njhill
body:
use_v2_model_runner special-cased HiSparse, custom speculative methods and watermarking to force Model Runner V2. These are just features the V1 model runner doesn't support, so list them in
_get_v1_model_runner_unsupported_features() alongside the other V2-only features and let _validate_v1_model_runner() reject them.

Since V2 is already the default, use_v2_model_runner no longer needs to inspect them. The behavior change is that watermarking with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 now raises instead of silently overriding the env var, consistent with the other V2-only features.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Fix bench mm-processor crash with HF datasets
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

`vllm bench mm-processor --dataset-name hf`, the HuggingFace example in `docs/benchmarking/cli.md`, crashes with `AttributeError`. This one-line fix closes the same kind of gap as #56300, which fixed random-mm sampling.

## Claims

`bench mm-processor` runs on HF datasets. `bench throughput` and `bench serve` behave as before.

## Validation

```bash
vllm bench mm-processor --model Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --dataset-name hf \
  --dataset-path lmarena-ai/VisionArena-Chat --hf-split train --num-prompts 5 --seed 0 \
  --load-format dummy --enforce-eager --disable-tqdm --output-json out.json

pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py -k hf_dataset_with_mm_processor
```

```text
# before
AttributeError: 'Namespace' object has no attribute 'hf_name'    # both commands

# after
bench: exit 0, completed 5, failed 0, 5 encoder calls
pytest: 1 passed
```

The bench ran on an L4 with real VisionArena data and dummy weights, on a pinned wheel with the same bug and the same one-line change. The new test uses the real `VisionArenaDataset` with only the HF download stubbed, and checks for text and image chat prompts.

## Details

`get_samples` reads `args.hf_name` for every HF dataset. `bench mm-processor` has no `--hf-name` flag, and `_to_serve_args` backfills its other missing flags but not this one. With `None`, datasets fall back to `--dataset-path`.

`bench mm-processor` still accepts only its listed dataset paths, so local copies stay unsupported. I found no open PR or issue for this.

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] (NVIDIA-only) Fused norm+quant MXFP8
author: gau-nernst
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Overview

Add a new Triton kernel for fused norm+quant MXFP8. To simplify integration, this kernel also covers additional no-quantize callsites:
- norm+quant before QKV proj
- No quantize: Input norm, final norm, MTP enorm/hnorm

dspark drafter's per-head norms remain on FlashInfer kernels.

## Claims

- MXFP8 norm + quantization: 1.39–1.60× faster than the norm → quantize chain across M=1–16K tokens (launch-bound at small M); 6.46 TB/s at M=16K tokens (~96% of the 6.76 TB/s streaming ceiling).
- BF16 norm: faster than FlashInfer at all but one measured M (plain M=1024 tokens: 0.99×, noise level).
- Bitwise residuals/UE8M0 scales; E4M3 code distance ≤1; BF16-out within 1 BF16 ulp.
- GSM8K accuracy: 0.9360 vs 0.9380 base (1-question delta, within noise). E2E prefill TTFT p50 is 0.4–0.9% lower at c=1/16 and neutral at c=4; decode TPOT p50 is neutral at c=32 and 5.4–9.6% lower at c=128/512 (2 rounds per arm).

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/minimax_m3/test_norm_mxfp8.py -v` → **13 passed** on GB300.
- `pre-commit`: all hooks passed.

### Microbenchmark

- CUPTI cold-L2 CUDA-graph medians, 3 rotated rounds, GB300 SM103, H=6144 BF16 elements. BW counts 7.03 bytes/element: BF16 x in, residual in + out, FP8 out, UE8M0 scales; measured streaming ceiling: 6.76 TB/s.

**Fused MXFP8 norm vs FlashInfer norm + separate MXFP8 quantize chain**

| Tokens (M) | Norm → quantize | Fused | Speedup | Fused BW |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.64 µs | 3.33 µs | 1.39× | 13.0 GB/s |
| 4 | 5.15 µs | 3.26 µs | 1.58× | 53.0 GB/s |

**BF16-out norm parity vs FlashInfer norm**

- This PR also backs the plain BF16 norm paths. Speedup = FlashInfer ÷ Triton latency, range across 2 bench runs; latencies are from the latest run.

| Form | Tokens (M) | FlashInfer | Triton | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fused-add | 1 | 2.91 µs | 2.72 µs | 1.058–1.071× |
| Fused-add | 4 | 3.33 µs | 2.75 µs | 1.209× |

Faster everywhere except plain M=1024 tokens (0.99×, noise level; a standalone re-measure had the ordering flipped). In the MXFP8 checkpoint, the BF16 path serves the post-attention norm (TP1 branch of the fused all-reduce helper), the final norm, and the MTP norms.

### E2E serving

- `vllm bench serve`; MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on GB300; base = `upstream/main`, PR = this branch.
- 2 full runs per arm; ranges shown.
- Decode used the mega MoE backend (`--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`); both configs use dspark speculative decoding.

**Prefill:** PP2 TP1, 100k-token random prefix + 8k-token input, 1 output token.

| Concurrency | Base TTFT p50 | PR TTFT p50 | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 288.0 ms | 286.5–286.9 ms | 0.4–0.5% |
| 4 | 638.2–642.4 ms | 638.2–640.7 ms | -0.4–+0.7% |
| 16 | 1835.9–1836.0 ms | 1820.4–1820.6 ms | 0.8–0.9% |

**Decode:** DEP4, 60k-token cached prefix, 1024 output tokens.

| Concurrency | Base TPOT p50 | PR TPOT p50 | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 7.18–7.61 ms | 7.61–7.70 ms | -7.2–0.0% |
| 128 | 11.75–12.03 ms | 10.72–10.88 ms | 8.8–9.6% |
| 512 | 22.06–22.95 ms | 20.87–21.23 ms | 5.4–7.5% |
| 1024 | 34.82–35.54 ms | 33.68–34.71 ms | 0.3–5.2% |

Speedup is per-round paired (base vs PR within the same run), range across 2 rounds; decode is neutral at c=32 and faster at c≥128, so the fusion does not regress decode.

### GSM8K

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, PP2 TP1 on 2× GB300; first 500 examples, 5-shot, temperature 0, `max_tokens=8192`:

| Config | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: |
| upstream/main | 0.9380 |
| This PR | 0.9360 |

0.002 delta = 1 question, within run-to-run noise; the BF16 norm path differs from FlashInfer by at most 1 ulp, MXFP8 path is bitwise-identical.

## Details

- `MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm.forward` calls the Triton kernel (`ops/norm_mxfp8.py`) via `gemma_rmsnorm_mxfp8(x, weight, eps, residual=None, mxfp8=True)`.
- Non-2-D inputs (the dspark drafter per-head norms, e.g. (16384, 4, 128)) keep the FlashInfer kernels.
- `forward_input_norm` passes `mxfp8=True` when `get_input_quant_key(qkv_proj) == kMxfp8Dynamic` with a supported FlashInfer MXFP8 linear kernel.
- TP>1 keeps the fused all-reduce + norm path; that helper's TP1 branch calls the norm module, so it uses Triton too.
- Kernel: hidden size is `tl.constexpr`; token count is `do_not_specialize` (2 compiled variants total: MXFP8 on/off). Specializes on `None` residual/`sf` pointers instead of constexpr flags; asserts 2-D row-contiguous inputs, with arbitrary row stride supported.
- PDL: every CTA calls `gdc_wait` before any global access, then `gdc_launch_dependents`.
- Model-local to MiniMax-M3 NVIDIA; no new flags or dependencies.

**Duplicate-work check (2026-10-31):** no open NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 TP1 norm+MXFP8 PR found.

| [#62509](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62509) | ROCm M3.1; this targets NVIDIA |
| [#61073](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61073) | General QuantizedActivation fusion contract, still iterating; this PR uses model-local dispatch and can migrate later |
| [#64723](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64723) | TP>1 Qwen3.5 fusion; complementary scope |
| [#61783](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61783) | Compile-pass NVFP4 fusion; different format/mechanism |

title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Fuse HyperConnection up projection and gate mix for long prefills
author: Gin-Sin
body:
## Overview Fuse the HyperConnection up projection (rank 320 → 4 × 2560) and the gate mix (sigmoid gate, mean over the 4 HC streams) into one tcgen05 kernel for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next prefill on SM100. `GatedResidual.mix` / `combine_and_mix` in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/hyperconnection.py` take the fused kernel once a forward has **≥ 512 tokens**. Below that, the existing GEMM + `hc_gate_mix` path stays. At prefill sizes the serving chain writes a `[M, 10240]` bf16 gate (20 KB per token) only to read it back in `hc_gate_mix`. The fused kernel keeps the gate in TMEM. It is `csrc/qwen4_exp/hc_up_gate_mix.cu`, exposed as `torch.ops._C.qwen4_exp_hc_up_gate_mix`, and built for the SM100 family with CUDA ≥ 13, like the Kimi-K3 AttnRes kernel. This is the NVIDIA/SM100, large-M counterpart of #64263, which fuses the same two ops in Triton for ROCm at decode sizes. It complements #58957, which fuses the HC *down* projection for decode batches of ≤ 48 tokens. Related work is under Details. ## Claims 1. **Kernel speed.** On B300, against the serving chain (cuBLAS GEMM + Triton `hc_gate_mix`), the fused kernel is **1.37× at M = 1280, 2.01× at 4096 and 2.26× at 16384**, reaching 53% of the HBM speed of light at M = 16384. It is faster than the chain from M = 32 up (0.84× at M = 1). Measured with CUPTI, cold L2 and CUDA graphs; the spread across processes is ≤ 2.6% from M = 64 up. 2. **Accuracy.** - **ULP bound:** max 0.51 bf16 ULP against an fp32 reference (gate, sigmoid and mix all in fp32). The unfused chain is at 1.87, because it rounds the gate to bf16. The ULP is taken relative to the magnitude of the summands. - **GSM8K:** full GSM8K is 0.964 / 0.968 / 0.970 on three PR servers vs 0.970 / 0.966 on `main`. - **Not bitwise:** the output is not bitwise equal to the chain, because the gate stays in fp32 and the sigmoid uses `tanh.approx`; it differs from the chain by at most 0.0078. See E2E accuracy for greedy outputs. 3. **E2E prefill, TP1.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 on one B300 per engine, 8k-token prompts, 1 output token. Input throughput rises **+3.1% at c1 and +3.8% at c4 / c16 / c64 on average** (+2.8% to +4.2% across 3 placements). Main-vs-main noise is −0.8% to 0.0%. The gain is close to what the kernel time predicts (+3.2% at c1, +3.9% to +4.0% at c ≥ 4), and TTFT drops by about the same amount. 4. **Where it does not apply.** All of these keep the existing code (the dispatch table is under Details): - batches below 512 tokens (decode and MTP verify); - non-SM100 GPUs and CUDA < 13 builds; - `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`; - LoRA-wrapped HC projections. ## Validation ### Microbenchmark The benchmark script is under Reproduce (collapsed). On one B300: - **Timing:** FlashInfer `bench_gpu_time_with_cupti`, CUDA graph, cold L2. The op is called directly at every M, including below the dispatch threshold. Each value is the median over 8 processes on different GPUs, each with its own seed and shuffled arm order (median of 3 × 100 replays per process). - **Baseline:** the serving chain, `qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm` followed by `hc_gate_mix`. On SM103 the GEMM is cuBLAS, because there is no skinny-GEMM plan for (10240, 320). - **Inputs:** `lowrank` is a column slice of the 336-wide down+inject output, as in the model. - **Accuracy check:** the fused output is checked against an fp32 reference before timing. | M | GEMM + gate mix (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup | Fused TFLOPS | Fused GB/s | Fused % of SOL | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 5.82 | 6.91 | 0.84× | 1 | 952 | 12% | | 4 | 6.02 | 6.64 | 0.91× | 4 | 1003 | 13% | | 16 | 6.51 | 6.71 | 0.97× | 16 | 1039 | 13% | | 64 | 9.06 | 7.04 | 1.29× | 60 | 1169 | 15% | | 256 | 10.11 | 9.12 | 1.11× | 184 | 1456 | 18% | | 512 | 12.24 | 11.10 | 1.10× | 302 | 1800 | 23% | | 1024 | 18.16 | 14.83 | 1.22× | 452 | 2253 | 28% | | **1280** | 21.71 | 15.81 | **1.37×** | 531 | 2539 | 32% | | 2048 | 30.95 | 20.96 | 1.48× | 640 | 2877 | 36% | | **4096** | 63.78 | 31.74 | **2.01×** | 846 | 3593 | 45% | | 8192 | 121.10 | 54.96 | 2.20× | 977 | 4031 | 50% | | **16384** | 230.24 | 102.00 | **2.26×** | 1053 | 4279 | 53% | **Crossover.** A finer sweep (fused / chain, µs) puts it at about 32 tokens: | M | 16 | 24 | 32 | 40 | 48 | 64 | 96 | 128 | 192 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Chain | 6.43 | 6.56 | 6.81 | 7.26 | 7.38 | 9.18 | 9.42 | 9.19 | 9.94 | | Fused | 6.69 | 6.69 | 6.69 | 6.75 | 6.88 | 7.04 | 7.23 | 7.31 | 8.80 | | Speedup | 0.96× | 0.98× | 1.02× | 1.08× | 1.07× | 1.30× | 1.30× | 1.26× | 1.13× | The fused kernel's time is flat at about 6.7 µs up to M = 32 (one 128-row tile per column block), while the chain jumps between 48 and 64 tokens. The dispatch threshold in this PR is still 512 tokens. Lowering it towards 32 would also move decode and MTP-verify batches onto the fused path, so I'd rather do that separately, with decode E2E numbers. SOL = max(ideal bytes / 8 TB/s, FLOPs / 2.25 PFLOP/s): - **Ideal bytes:** `lowrank`, `xn` and `w_up` read once, and the output written once. - **FLOPs:** 2·M·10240·320. - **Regime:** the op is memory-bound but close to balanced: ~246 FLOP/B against a ridge of ~281. At M = 16384, SOL = 54.6 µs. **How close to the practical ceiling.** At M = 16384: - a streaming kernel that touches only the ideal bytes reaches 6.2 TB/s (70.3 µs), the same as `cudaMemcpy` of the same size; - a data-path-only build of this kernel (same TMA loads, pipeline, barriers and stores; no MMA, no math) takes 97.8 µs; - the full kernel takes 102.0 µs. So the math and MMA add about 4% on top of the data path (the data-path-only build predates the last two changes, so this is approximate). The remaining gap to the copy ceiling is the data path itself: only one `xn` stage fits next to four operand stages, and `lowrank` / `w_up` are re-read from L2 for every tile.

This is expected: the output differs from the chain by up to 0.0078, which flips near-tied tokens. 81 of the 93 differing generations still reach the same final `####` answer, and both arms produce one in 190/200. ### Reproduce ```bash pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops.py python bench_hc_up_gate_mix.py --seed --output # script below; 8 processes, one per GPU vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \ --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 32768 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos \ --temperature 0 --seed 0 --max-concurrency {1,4,16,64} --num-prompts {32,64,256,512} python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --temperature 0 --max-tokens 1024 \ --num-questions 1319 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' ```

Shapes are Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's: hc_count 4, hidden 2560, rank 320, with ``lowrank`` a column slice of the merged down+inject output. python bench_hc_up_gate_mix.py --seed --output Timing is FlashInfer CUPTI with CUDA graphs and a cold L2. Before timing, the fused output is checked against an fp32 reference in bf16 ULPs of the summands' magnitude (sum over streams of |sigmoid(gate) * xn| / 4). """ import argparse import json import random import statistics from pathlib import Path import torch import torch.nn.functional as F from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti import vllm._custom_ops # noqa: F401 from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.low_latency_gemm import ( QWEN4_EXP_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY, ) from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.ops.hc import ( hc_gate_mix, hc_up_gate_mix, hc_up_gate_mix_supported, ) from vllm.platforms import current_platform HC, HIDDEN, RANK = 4, 2560, 320 D = HC * HIDDEN DOWN_N = RANK + HC + 12 # merged down+inject output width, 16-row padded def make_inputs(m: int, seed: int): gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed) kwargs = dict(device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=gen) down = torch.randn(m, DOWN_N, **kwargs) xn = torch.randn(m, D, **kwargs) w_up = torch.randn(D, RANK, **kwargs) * RANK**-0.5 return down[:, :RANK], xn, w_up def bench_us(fn, args) -> list[float]: return [ statistics.median( bench_gpu_time_with_cupti( fn, use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True, dry_run_iters=5, repeat_iters=args.repeat, ) ) * 1000 for _ in range(args.trials) ] def benchmark(m: int, args) -> list[dict]: lowrank, xn, w_up = make_inputs(m, args.seed) gemm = torch.ops.vllm.qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm gate = gemm(lowrank, w_up) arms = { "unfused": lambda: hc_gate_mix(xn, gemm(lowrank, w_up), HC), "fused": lambda: hc_up_gate_mix(lowrank, xn, w_up), "gemm": lambda: gemm(lowrank, w_up), "gate_mix": lambda: hc_gate_mix(xn, gate, HC), } expected = arms["unfused"]() assert torch.equal(expected, hc_gate_mix(xn, F.linear(lowrank, w_up), HC)) actual = arms["fused"]() # fp32 reference (gate, sigmoid and mix in fp32); errors in bf16 ULPs. g = F.linear(lowrank.float(), w_up.float()).unflatten(-1, (HC, HIDDEN)) prod = torch.sigmoid(g) * xn.float().unflatten(-1, (HC, HIDDEN)) ref = prod.mean(-2) # bf16 ULP of the summands' magnitude (sum |sigmoid * xn| / HC), so that # cancellation between streams does not inflate the error. scale = prod.abs().mean(-2).clamp_min(2.0**-126) ulp = 2.0 ** (torch.frexp(scale).exponent.float() - 8) err = {} for name, t in (("fused", actual), ("chain", expected)): d = (t.float() - ref).abs() err[name] = dict(max_abs=d.max().item(), max_ulp=(d / ulp).max().item(), mean_ulp=(d / ulp).mean().item()) err["bitwise_vs_chain"] = torch.equal(actual, expected) err["max_abs_vs_chain"] = (actual.float() - expected.float()).abs().max().item() print(json.dumps(dict(m=m, err=err)), flush=True) if args.check == "bitwise": assert err["bitwise_vs_chain"], f"fused != unfused at M={m}" elif args.check == "tol": assert err["fused"]["max_ulp"] <= args.max_ulp, err # Ideal traffic reads every input and writes every output once. weight_bytes = D * RANK * 2 io_bytes = { "fused": weight_bytes + m * (RANK + D + HIDDEN) * 2, "gemm": weight_bytes + m * (RANK + D) * 2, "gate_mix": m * (2 * D + HIDDEN) * 2, } io_bytes["unfused"] = io_bytes["gemm"] + io_bytes["gate_mix"] flops = 2 * m * D * RANK rows = [] names = args.arms or list(arms) random.Random(args.seed + m).shuffle(names) for name in names: trials = bench_us(arms[name], args) us = statistics.median(trials) rows.append( dict( m=m, arm=name, us=us, trials_us=trials, tflops=flops / (us * 1e6) if name != "gate_mix" else None, gbps=io_bytes[name] / (us * 1e3), # Lower bound on the time of the fused op at the given rates. sol_us=max( io_bytes["fused"] / (args.peak_tbps * 1e6), flops / (args.peak_tflops * 1e6), ), ) ) return rows def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) parser.add_argument( "--num-tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 4, 16, 64, 256, 512, 1024, 1280, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768], ) parser.add_argument("--repeat", type=int, default=100) parser.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=3) parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0) parser.add_argument("--peak-tbps", type=float, default=8.0) parser.add_argument("--peak-tflops", type=float, default=2250.0) parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path) parser.add_argument("--check", choices=["bitwise", "tol", "none"], default="tol") parser.add_argument("--max-ulp", type=float, default=4.0) parser.add_argument("--arms", nargs="+") args = parser.parse_args() w_up = torch.empty(D, RANK, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) if not hc_up_gate_mix_supported(w_up, HC): raise SystemExit("hc_up_gate_mix needs an SM100-family GPU and build") plans = QWEN4_EXP_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY.get( current_platform.get_device_capability(), {} ) metadata = dict( gpu=torch.cuda.get_device_name(), torch=torch.__version__, cuda=torch.version.cuda, skinny_gemm_m=sorted(plans.get((D, RANK), {})), args=vars(args), ) print(json.dumps(metadata, default=str)) results = [] for m in args.num_tokens: for row in benchmark(m, args): results.append(row) print(json.dumps(row), flush=True) if args.output: args.output.write_text( json.dumps(dict(metadata=metadata, results=results), indent=2, default=str) + "\n" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
## Details **Dispatch and eligibility** | Case | Path | |---|---| | SM100 family (B200 / B300 / GB200 / GB300), CUDA ≥ 13 build, HC count 4, hidden 2560, rank 320, bf16 HC weights, ≥ 512 tokens in the forward | **fused** (single-CTA 32-column tiles below 1024 tokens, CTA-pair 64-column tiles from 1024) | | < 512 tokens: decode, MTP verify and draft steps, short prefills or prefill chunks | unchanged (skinny GEMM / cuBLAS + `hc_gate_mix`) | | SM90, SM120, ROCm, CPU, XPU | unchanged (op not built or not dispatched) | | CUDA < 13 build | unchanged (op not built) | | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | unchanged | | LoRA wrapping `input_mix_weight_up` | unchanged (the LoRA delta is never skipped) | | Checkpoint quantization (BF16 / FP8 / NVFP4 / MXFP4) | HC projections are always unquantized bf16 (`quant_config=None`), so eligibility does not depend on it. Measured with the FP8 checkpoint. | | MTP | the MTP block's `GatedResidual` follows the same rule (fused only for ≥ 512-token draft prefills) | | TP / HC sequence parallelism | weights are replicated; M is the per-rank token count | **Design** - **Structure.** Persistent and warp-specialized: - warp 0 TMA-loads `lowrank` and `w_up`; - warp 1 issues `tcgen05.mma`, with fp32 accumulators in TMEM; - warp 2 allocates TMEM; - warp 3 TMA-loads the `xn` tile with `EVICT_FIRST` into swizzled shared memory; - 2 or 4 epilogue warpgroups each own 16 output columns. - The warp index comes from `cutlass::canonical_warp_idx_sync()`, so the compiler treats the role branches as warp-uniform. - **Tiling.** An output tile is 128 rows × BC hidden columns. Its GEMM tile has N = 4·BC: the same BC columns of all 4 HC streams, loaded by one TMA box per stream. Each epilogue thread therefore holds all four gates of its output elements in one TMEM row. No permuted copy of `w_up` is needed, and nothing is built at load time or on first call. - **Two configurations, picked by M:** - **Below 1024 tokens:** single CTAs with BC = 32, 4 operand / 4 accumulator / 2 `xn` stages. - **From 1024 tokens:** CTA pairs (`tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2`, 256-row tiles) with BC = 64. Each CTA of the pair loads its own 128 rows of `lowrank` and two of the four `w_up` streams. The halved `w_up` tile leaves room for 4 operand stages next to the 64 KB `xn` stage. The leader's MMA commits are multicast to both CTAs, and both CTAs' epilogue warps release the accumulator to the leader. - **Epilogue.** - The gate stays in fp32; the chain rounds it to bf16 as the GEMM output. - sigmoid(x) = 0.5·tanh.approx(0.5·x) + 0.5. - The streams are accumulated 0..3 with fp32 FMAs and scaled by 1/4. - Each warpgroup stages its 128 × 16 output block in double-buffered shared memory. After a warpgroup barrier, one thread issues a single TMA store, which also clips rows past M. - A `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` before an `xn` stage is released keeps the next TMA load from overtaking the epilogue's `ld.shared` reads. - **PDL.** The kernel launches with programmatic stream serialization. It waits on the grid dependency before allocating TMEM (and releases the allocation permit right after), so a preceding kernel that allocates TMEM after triggering its dependents cannot deadlock with it. - **Input layout.** `lowrank` is the row-major column slice `out[:, :320]` of the 336-wide down+inject output (#60027). TMA reads it in place with its row stride of 336 elements, so there is no copy. The other inputs only need 16-byte-aligned rows. - **Dispatch.** The size check is a Python branch in `GatedResidual._up_gate_mix`, as in #58957. #64263 has to choose inside the op because its path is compiled once for all batch sizes. The NVIDIA Qwen4Exp model runs without `torch.compile` (#55272), and breakable CUDA graphs evaluate the branch per captured size. - **Why CUDA rather than CuTe DSL as in #58957.** The kernel is AOT-compiled in the existing CMake build, so there is no JIT at startup. It uses only CUTLASS/cute headers already in the build. **Limitations** - Measured on B300 (SM103) only. The kernel is built for and dispatched on the whole SM100 family; B200/GB200 should behave the same, but the crossovers were not measured there. - At M = 16384 the kernel is at 53% of the HBM speed of light and 69% of the practical copy ceiling (70.3 µs). The remaining gap is the data path, as shown above. More `xn` stages would need smaller operand stages or a different split of the shared memory. **Related PRs** - **#64263** (open, ROCm): the same up projection + gate mix fusion in Triton (`amd_hc_up_gate_mix` in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/`), used at 1–256 tokens. This PR is its NVIDIA/SM100, large-M counterpart. The ops share the name pattern (`hc_up_gate_mix` next to `hc_gate_mix` in `nvidia/ops/hc.py`), and the `mix()` / `combine_and_mix()` call sites have the same shape. - **#58957** (merged): HC down projection + SiLU fusion for NVIDIA decode (M ≤ 48), with dispatch by measured crossover. This PR follows it for the up projection at the other end of the batch range; the two never overlap. - **#60027** (merged): keeps the HC up projection on the skinny GEMM at M ≤ 16 and lets it take the strided `lowrank` slice. Those sizes are below this PR's threshold. On SM103 there is no skinny plan for (10240, 320), so the baseline at the sizes this PR targets is cuBLAS on the same slice. - **#64820** (merged): int64 HC/PLE row offsets. This kernel addresses rows through TMA coordinates. - **#61454** (merged): HC/PLE cleanup. This PR is based on `main` after it and keeps its structure. - **#54687** (merged): HC combine-norm reuse for MTP. Unaffected: the norm in `combine_and_mix` is unchanged, and the MTP mixer gets the same dispatch. No open PR fuses the HC up projection on NVIDIA. **Follow-ups** - Lower the dispatch threshold towards the measured crossover (~32 tokens), with decode E2E numbers. - Measure the crossovers on B200/GB200 and adjust the thresholds if they differ. - Close the data-path gap at large M, e.g. by keeping a `lowrank` block resident per CTA, or by finding room for a second `xn` stage. AI assistance was used to implement, benchmark and test this change. ---

title: [Spec Decode][Perf] Fuse DFlash2 candidate edge scoring into a Triton kernel
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
## Purpose

The DFlash2 path selector scores every candidate pair for each draft step:
```
    S_t(a, b) = U_t(b) + <A(a) ⊙ H(h_t), B(b)>
```

The Qwen3 DFlash2 model did this with a compiled torch graph that runs several kernels (anchor clamp, gathers, a
concat, an elementwise product and an einsum). Beam carried its own Triton kernel, `candidate_edges`, that did the same thing.

This PR replaces both with a single Triton kernel, `dflash2_score_edges`, that both implementations call through `_score_edges`:
- One program per (request, step) gathers the anchor and candidate predecessor/successor rows, forms `A ⊙ H` in FP32, and computes the K×K edge block with `tl.dot`, then adds the unary term.
- The torch implementation remains as `_score_edges_reference`, which is used on CPU and in tests.
- Beam's `dflash2_ops.py` is deleted, and `DFlash2BeamCandidateSelector` calls `_score_edges`.

**Numerics.** The kernel and the reference now always return FP32 scores, and the edge term is no longer rounded to bf16. Before this PR, Beam's kernel stored scores in the unary dtype and the Qwen3 reference rounded the edge term to bf16. Inputs to the dot product stay bf16, because bf16 × bf16 products are exact in FP32. Mean absolute error against an FP64 reference drops from 7.2e-5 to 5.2e-5. The output is K-wide (`[num_reqs, steps, K, K]`), so storing it in FP32 costs negligible memory.

## Test Plan

### Unit Tests
```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -q
```
The DFlash2 test suite passes on GB200: `102 passed`.

### Microbenchmark
The microbenchmark times edge scoring alone: CUDA-graph replay of the compiled op, median of 5, comparing the base implementations with this PR's kernel.

| Concurrency | Qwen base | Qwen PR | Speedup | Beam base | Beam PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.85 µs | 2.16 µs | 2.70× | 2.16 µs | 2.26 µs | 0.96× |
| 4 | 6.98 µs | 2.26 µs | 3.09× | 2.77 µs | 2.26 µs | 1.23× |

| 256 | 43.35 µs | 8.51 µs | 5.10× | 64.86 µs | 16.72 µs | 3.88× |

Qwen base is the compiled torch graph, and Beam base is the old `candidate_edges` kernel. Mean absolute error against FP64 is 7.2e-5 for base and 5.2e-5 for the PR, at every point.

### End-to-end Benchmark

For end to end, I compared `vllm serve` at base commit 67d677bdef with this PR, on GB200:

- **Sweep:** concurrency 1→256 in powers of two, with 4 × concurrency prompts (minimum 16) and one discarded warmup per server.
- **Sampling:** greedy, `--ignore-eos`.
- **Prefix caching:** off.
- **Workload:** SPEED-Bench `throughput_2k` / `low_entropy`, which has about 2.2K-token prompts, run through the chat endpoint with 2048 output tokens.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Count reasoning_content deltas as streamed outputs in chat
author: Than0316
body:
## Overview

Some servers, like SGLang, send reasoning tokens in a field called `reasoning_content`. vLLM uses `reasoning`. Since #62341, the chat benchmark client only looks for `reasoning`, so it skips SGLang's reasoning tokens.

Two things go wrong:
- TTFT is measured to the first answer token instead of the first reasoning token, so it looks much slower than it really is.
- A response that ends before the model starts answering is counted as failed.

This PR makes the client accept `reasoning_content` too.

## Claims

- TTFT is measured to the first reasoning token again, as it was before #62341. A stub streaming SGLang's chunks went from 842 ms to 205 ms, against a true 201 ms.
- Reasoning-only responses go from 0/20 to 20/20 successful.
- No change for vLLM's own server, which streams `reasoning`.

## Validation

Two tests added to `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`: reasoning followed by an answer (TTFT and ITL), and a reasoning-only stream (success). Both are parametrized over `reasoning` / `reasoning_content` and both clients. 46 passed. The 4 `reasoning_content` cases fail on `main` (`assert 1 == (4 - 1)` and "Never received a valid chunk to calculate TTFT"). pre-commit passes.

End to end: `vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat`, 20 prompts, concurrency 4, against a local stub that streams SGLang's chunk sequence. The stub sends its first output at 200 ms, then 30 reasoning and 10 answer tokens 20 ms apart, and logs its own send times. Two runs each:

| | `main` | this branch | stub's send log |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean TTFT | 843 / 841 ms | 206 / 205 ms | first reasoning token ≈ 201 ms |
| reasoning-only, successful | 0 / 20 | 20 / 20 | 30 tokens sent per request |

<details><summary>Stub server and command</summary>

`stub_sglang_server.py` sends the same chunk sequence as SGLang's streaming chat endpoint, with fixed timings, and logs when it sent the first reasoning and answer tokens:

```python
"""Minimal stub of SGLang's streaming chat endpoint, for integration-testing a client.

It reproduces the chunk sequence SGLang streams as of sgl-project/sglang 504f9cf
(sse_utils.py StreamDelta/StreamChoice, omit_defaults=True; serving_chat.py):
  opening chunk  delta {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": null},
                 sent when the first engine output arrives
  reasoning      delta {"reasoning_content": "..."}          (no `content` key)
  answer         delta {"content": "...", "reasoning_content": null}
  finish         delta {"reasoning_content": null}, finish_reason set
  usage          "choices": [] plus "usage"
Every choice carries logprobs, finish_reason and matched_stop, as StreamChoice serializes them.
It uses fixed, known timings and logs server-side send times per request as ground truth.

Usage: python stub_sglang_server.py --port 18731 --log ground_truth.jsonl
Binds to 127.0.0.1 only.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import time

from aiohttp import web


def _chunk(delta: dict, finish_reason=None) -> bytes:
    # StreamChoice always serializes logprobs, finish_reason and matched_stop.
    choice = {
        "index": 0,
        "delta": delta,
        "logprobs": None,
        "finish_reason": finish_reason,
        "matched_stop": None,
    }
    body = {
        "id": "chatcmpl-stub",
        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
        "created": int(time.time()),
        "model": "stub",
        "choices": [choice],
    }
    return f"data: {json.dumps(body)}\n\n".encode()


def _usage_chunk(usage: dict) -> bytes:
    # SGLang's final usage chunk carries no choices (serving_chat.py ~2792-2796).
    body = {
        "id": "chatcmpl-stub",
        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
        "created": int(time.time()),
        "model": "stub",
        "choices": [],
        "usage": usage,
    }
    return f"data: {json.dumps(body)}\n\n".encode()


def make_app(args) -> web.Application:
    log = open(args.log, "a", buffering=1)

    async def chat(request: web.Request) -> web.StreamResponse:
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        await request.json()
        resp = web.StreamResponse(headers={"Content-Type": "text/event-stream"})
        await resp.prepare(request)

        sent = {}
        # SGLang sends the opening role chunk when the first engine output arrives.
        await asyncio.sleep(args.first_token_ms / 1000)
        await resp.write(_chunk({"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": None}))
        for i in range(args.reasoning_tokens):
            if i:
                await asyncio.sleep(args.itl_ms / 1000)
            await resp.write(_chunk({"reasoning_content": f"r{i} "}))
            sent.setdefault("first_reasoning_s", time.perf_counter() - t0)
        for i in range(args.answer_tokens):
            await asyncio.sleep(args.itl_ms / 1000)
            await resp.write(_chunk({"content": f"a{i} ", "reasoning_content": None}))
            sent.setdefault("first_answer_s", time.perf_counter() - t0)
        n = args.reasoning_tokens + args.answer_tokens
        # Finish chunk: build_sse_content(finish_reason=...) gives delta {"reasoning_content": null}.
        await resp.write(
            _chunk({"reasoning_content": None}, finish_reason="stop" if args.answer_tokens else "length")
        )
        await resp.write(_usage_chunk({"prompt_tokens": 8, "completion_tokens": n, "total_tokens": 8 + n}))
        await resp.write(b"data: [DONE]\n\n")
        log.write(json.dumps({**sent, "tokens": n}) + "\n")
        return resp

    async def models(_request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        return web.json_response({"object": "list", "data": [{"id": "stub", "object": "model"}]})

    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_post("/v1/chat/completions", chat)
    app.router.add_get("/v1/models", models)
    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18731)
    p.add_argument("--log", default="ground_truth.jsonl")
    p.add_argument("--first-token-ms", type=float, default=200.0)
    p.add_argument("--reasoning-tokens", type=int, default=30)
    p.add_argument("--answer-tokens", type=int, default=10)
    p.add_argument("--itl-ms", type=float, default=20.0)
    a = p.parse_args()
    web.run_app(make_app(a), host="127.0.0.1", port=a.port, print=None)
```

Run it, then benchmark it:

```bash
python stub_sglang_server.py --port 18731 &
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18731 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model stub --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16 --random-output-len 40 \
  --num-prompts 20 --max-concurrency 4
```

For the reasoning-only case, start the stub with `--answer-tokens 0`.

</details>

## Details

SGLang streams reasoning only as `reasoning_content`; its reasoning deltas carry no `content` key (`StreamDelta` in `sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/sse_utils.py`). It fixed the same issue in its own benchmark client (sgl-project/sglang#23954). The Rust `vllm-bench` ports in #64626/#64627 have the same gap; I'll note it there.

No issue or PR covers this. #64703 edits the same file on different lines and applies independently.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this and write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and the end-to-end comparison.

cc @DarkLight1337, who reviewed #62341.
