title: [Perf][MoE] Fuse padding skipping in grouped and Muse prepared routing
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Skip CUDA-graph padding in Muse Spark's prepared NVFP4 routing path, and fuse existing grouped-routing padding masks into the CUDA top-k kernels. Padding produces `-1` expert IDs and zero weights without separate CUDA masking launches.

## Claims

- Muse's prepared TRT-LLM path now supplies its native padding mask to the existing fused router. The backend-specific fast path and matching-layout check gate this behavior.
- Grouped routing retains its existing backend opt-in and handles padding in all four CUDA kernel families. Existing XPU/AITER interfaces remain compatible.
- Eight isolated grouped-routing cases reduce five kernel launches to one, with 43.34–70.06% lower median operation span. This is not a whole-model speedup claim.

## Validation

- Isolated SM100 `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` build and all pre-commit hooks: passed.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_grouped_topk.py tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_router.py -q`: **632 passed** on GB200.
- Five selected downstream sentinel test functions, including invalid expert IDs and poisoned finalizer slots: **27 passed**. Exact commands are in the [validation receipt](https://github.com/Inferact/vllm-perf-data/blob/main/research/moe-padding/2026-11-01/grouped-routing/validation.json).
- Five existing CPU Muse router tests: passed.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Grouped routing, 8/128 tokens, four kernel families | Exact output parity; 43.34–70.06% lower isolated span; five kernels → one |
| Real-weight Muse, 100K KV, TP4/EP4, same instrumented graph | N7 mask off/on: 10.857728 → 9.822160 ms; N8 control: 10.006304 → 10.005904 ms |
| Actual parent vs patch, same rebuilt binary and identical real inputs/KV history | 16 active outputs and 2,880 active routing tensors byte-identical; patched padding IDs/weights exactly `-1`/zero |

[Grouped benchmark, all raw samples and traces](https://github.com/Inferact/vllm-perf-data/tree/main/research/moe-padding/2026-11-01/grouped-routing) uses 100 CUPTI spans per arm, reversed orders and cold L2. The comparator uses the same rebuilt CUDA operation with explicit postmasks. GPU clocks were not locked.

[Muse measurements and actual-source parity evidence](https://github.com/Inferact/vllm-perf-data/tree/main/models/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4/gb200/decode-buckets/2026-11-01/padding-mask) have an explicit qualification: all measurement/correctness phases completed, but the diagnostic harness retained captured NCCL graphs and hung during shutdown. Those jobs remain **FAILED**; separate reviewed completed-phase validators and independent audits checked the saved results after owned cleanup. A tiny two-rank experiment reproduced retained-graph teardown waiting and normal shutdown after release. No successful full-model harness shutdown is claimed. The actual-source comparison has no accepted timing samples; the timing comparison uses an instrumented graph, not stock production before/after.

The old Muse helper also passed the NaN-padding test; no before-failing numerical bug is claimed for that helper. The actual-source baseline instead demonstrates the missing call-site mask: its padded rows retain expert assignments, while the patch invalidates them with exact active-output parity.

## Details

Muse's prepared path calls `_compute_routing` directly, bypassing the common router wrapper. Its routed TRT-LLM experts support negative expert IDs. The mask is passed only on that prepared path; layout mismatches retain the existing behavior. The Triton fallback writes literal zero for padded weights, including when padded logits are nonfinite.

Grouped routing previously applied two `masked_fill` operations after routing; traces also show their two copy kernels. The optional mask is now consumed by the CUDA kernels. Rendered ModelOpt documentation, the generated environment reference, and CI source dependencies are updated.

Duplicate checks found no open Muse-specific or fused-grouped-padding PR. Related #50759 adds a generic fallback after `BaseRouter._compute_routing`; it misses Muse's direct prepared call and does not fuse the grouped kernels. This change addresses those distinct paths and preserves backend gates rather than adding blanket fallback masking. If #50759 merges first, its native-padding hook should recognize the grouped path to avoid applying a second mask.

AI assistance was used to implement, review and validate this change.

title: [Bugfix][MM] Keep FlashInfer cu_seqlens halves aligned in Qwen3-VL encoder CUDA graph replay
author: wguo7
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `mm_encoder_attn_backend=FLASHINFER` and encoder CUDA graphs enabled, Qwen3-VL image replays copy the packed FlashInfer `cu_seqlens` into the capture buffer with `EncoderCudaGraphManager._copy_padded_buffer`. That copy misaligns the q/k/o and v halves of the packed tensor. The vision encoder output then differs between replays of the same image and from eager mode. This registers the existing Qwen2.5-VL helper `_pad_flashinfer_cu_seqlens_buffer` (from #42796) for Qwen3-VL through `EncoderCudaGraphConfig.padding_logics`. SyaOtiLan found the instability and ran the GPU validation below while testing #63809, which adds the same hook for Qwen3-Omni.

## Claims

- Qwen3-VL encoder CUDA graph replays on FLASHINFER keep each half of the packed `cu_seqlens` in its own half of the capture buffer. In the tested cases, replays are identical and match eager mode on the same padded buffers.
- Other attention backends use `_pad_cumulative_seqlens_buffer`, as Qwen2.5-VL does (changed in 3b80be3 after review). It repeats the last offset, so padded entries are zero-length sequences, while the default copy filled them with zeros. The default copy gave no wrong output in the FLASH_ATTN replays of the earlier GPU runs below, and the GPU run of 3b80be3 below shows exact replays on both backends.

## Validation

CPU unit tests (no GPU) in `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`, class `TestFlashInferCuSeqlensPadding`:

```
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -k FlashInferCuSeqlens
```

On this branch, 8 pass. The test pads replay `cu_seqlens` with the padding function Qwen3-VL registers (falling back to `_copy_padded_buffer`, as replay does) and checks that the result equals the `cu_seqlens` computed for the same inputs at the capture batch size. It runs four replay and capture batch sizes on FLASHINFER and FLASH_ATTN. With `qwen3_vl.py` from main, 7 of the 8 cases fail. The one that passes is the FlashInfer case where replay and capture fall in the same batch bucket, so no padding happens. The whole file passes (52 passed, 25 skipped on CPU).

GPU validation by SyaOtiLan ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557439065), with raw outputs and scripts): RTX 4090 (SM 8.9), FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct in BF16 through `LLM(mm_encoder_only=True)`, `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`, budgets [64, 256, 1024], at most 2 vision items and 16 frames per batch, one 224 x 224 image. The values are max abs differences of the vision encoder output embeddings. "Replay vs replay" compares later replays of the same input with the first one, and "Replay vs eager" compares the first replay with eager mode on the same padded buffers. The run used the same `qwen3_vl.py` change on top of 3687acad21, the head of #63809 at the time. `encoder_cudagraph.py`, `mm_encoder_attention.py`, `vit_attn_wrappers.py` and `qwen2_5_vl.py` are identical there and on this branch.

| Input | Replay vs replay, before | Replay vs replay, after | Replay vs eager, before | Replay vs eager, after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 x 16 grid (processor default), 64 tokens | 9.65625 | 0 | 26.984375 | 0 |
| 14 x 14 grid, 49 tokens | 10.875 | 0 | 23.234375 | 0 |

In a [second run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557974253) on the same branch, mixed-size and two-image batches, video, alternating input shapes and oversized inputs that fall back to eager were also checked: all 110 graph-covered conditions matched eager on the same padded buffers exactly, and the 1,368 calls of a shape-transition stress test were exact.

Padded and unpadded eager runs of the 49-token input still differ (max 0.28125, RMSE 0.0088). That difference does not involve graph replay, and this PR does not change it. A per-layer trace in the second run found that the first difference appears in `blocks.0.mlp.linear_fc1`, while the patch embedding, norms, QKV and attention before it match exactly, which points to shape-dependent numerics in the linear layer. End-to-end generation quality was not measured.

GPU validation of the current head 3b80be3 by SyaOtiLan ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64984#issuecomment-6570819059), with scripts, raw logs and checksums): same RTX 4090, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct in BF16, TP=1, `LLM(mm_encoder_only=True)`, budgets [64, 256, 1024], at most 2 vision items and 16 frames per batch, two fresh worker lifetimes per backend. The run reused precompiled extensions from 4135590ffe01 rather than a new wheel, and this PR changes only Python files. Each cell gives two max abs differences of the vision encoder output: a later replay against the first replay, then the first replay against eager mode on the same padded buffers.

| Input | Output tokens | FLASH_ATTN | FLASHINFER |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image 224, matched grid | 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Image 448 | 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Image 224, default processor grid | 64 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Mixed images 224 + 448 | 49 + 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Mixed images 448 + 224 | 196 + 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 2 frames | 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 8 frames | 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 16 frames | 392 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

The image replays exercise the new tail fill: on FLASH_ATTN, 3 replay offsets go into a 17-entry capture buffer and the last offset fills the 14 tail entries. FLASHINFER keeps its split-half padding (18 replay entries, 34 capture entries). Video replays have the same length as capture on both backends. All 32 case checks and 192 later shape-switch executions passed. These results cover encoder replay correctness, not generation quality or latency.

## Details

For FlashInfer, `MMEncoderAttention.maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens` returns the q/k/o offsets followed by the v offsets, each half padded to a FlashInfer batch bucket (8, 16, 32 or 64), and `flashinfer_wrapper` splits the tensor at its midpoint. The BF16 and FP8 paths both use this two-half layout, and only BF16 was run on a GPU. Qwen3-VL captures with `cu_seqlens` padded to `max_frames_per_batch` (bucket 16 for 16 frames, 34 entries) and pads image replays to `max_batch_size` (bucket 8 for 2 items, 18 entries). `_copy_padded_buffer` zeroes the capture buffer and copies the 18 entries to its start. The q/k/o half then holds the 9 q/k/o offsets followed by the first 8 v offsets, and the v half holds the last v offset followed by zeros. Offsets count elements of the packed QKV buffer, so a v offset is 3 x tokens x hidden size. For one 196-patch image with an illustrative hidden size of 1152, the first two v offsets are [0, 677376] in eager mode and [677376, 0] after the default copy, so the kernel sees a sequence of negative length. That would explain why replays of the same input differ from each other, since the kernel then reads outside the valid range, but I have not confirmed this inside the kernel.

The fix mirrors the registration Qwen2.5-VL already has for the same key (`cu_seqlens`) and layout. Changing how image replays are padded would touch the shared graph manager and every model that uses it, while the hook keeps the change inside Qwen3-VL. Video replays pad to `max_frames_per_batch`, the same bucket as capture, so they are not affected, and video replays on the base commit were stable in the second run.

This PR and #63809 touch different model files. Both add tests to `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`, and this commit cherry-picks cleanly onto #63809, so they can merge in either order.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Release temporary device KV bindings after graph profiling
author: zhenwenqi2024
body:
## Overview

Release HiSparse's temporary device KV bindings after CUDA-graph memory profiling, while preserving the engine-scoped registered host pool for the real KV cache.

## Claims

- Live attention handles and runtimes no longer retain the throwaway KV slab and its per-binding tables after profiling cleanup.
- Cleanup is idempotent. Rebinding preserves host registration and clears stale hot-cache tags before the new backing is consumed.
- No throughput, accuracy, or reproduced model OOM improvement is claimed.

## Validation

### Review follow-up (2026-11-04)

- Both the runtime and attention handle now use `_reset_binding_state()` from construction and unbinding. Persistent index-group/draft membership is retained.
- Removed the `runtimes` argument from `release_pinned_state()`. Connector shutdown/error paths detach their attention handles; the Host release helper retains its existing drain, unregistration and shared-region cleanup responsibilities.
- Also fixed an adjacent partial-initialization failure path: if KV binding fails before initialization returns, already-bound context handles are detached before the Host-pool reference is dropped.
- Removed redundant handle deduplication and the extra bind-time Hot-state reset. Real model capture retains ownership of the existing connector reset; the throwaway profiling capture uses a no-op connector.

Four source-isolated CPU lifecycle checks passed (2.52 s), covering storage detachment, repeated cleanup, shutdown and partial-binding rollback. title: [Perf][Model] DeepSeek V4/V4.1 Vision: encode a call's images in packed passes
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 Vision run the ViT and aligner once per image, even when a call carries several images. This PR encodes a call's images in one packed pass through `forward_packed`, the path V4.1's encoder CUDA graphs already use. No new flag.

## Claims

- Across 54 multi-image encoder calls, encoding is 2.0–2.6× faster on V4 and 1.6–2.1× faster on V4.1, on two H100 machines. No call got more than 2% slower.
- With the real V4 checkpoint on 2× B200, median TTFT drops from 367–378 ms to 271 ms for 4-image requests at concurrency 1, and from 914–959 ms to 548 ms on VisionArena at concurrency 16.
- MMMU-Pro scores match main within run-to-run noise (862 correct vs 861 / 860 on main; multi-image 75 vs 74 / 75) on a direct-answer setup described below. Startup KV-cache capacity is effectively unchanged in the tested configuration.
- Cost: peak encoder memory per call grows with the number of images, up to about 1.7 GB more on V4 and 2.0 GB on V4.1 for a 32-image call. Output is not bit-identical to the per-image path, and the PR disagrees with main on more answers than main does with itself (200 vs 96 of 1730), in both directions.

## Validation

**Encoder.** H100, FlashAttention, real tower weights, random patches at VisionArena sizes. 54 multi-image calls, 3 rounds, shuffled call order, alternating arm order. [Benchmark script](https://gist.github.com/subhashpolisetti/0f74ea61d8c3dbd32d7e5ef49a235f85). ms is the median across calls, and peak is the largest across calls, measured above the allocation just before the call. Per-image → this PR:

| images per call | V4 ms | V4 peak MiB | V4.1 ms | V4.1 peak MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 59.6 → 29.9 | 141 → 142 | 59.6 → 30.1 | 120 → 189 |
| 4 | 119.2 → 47.0 | 79 → 281 | 118.8 → 57.9 | 132 → 371 |
| 8 | 237.6 → 88.8 | 87 → 450 | 236.3 → 101.8 | 110 → 530 |
| 16 | 483.0 → 172.2 | 105 → 883 | 481.6 → 219.2 | 148 → 1133 |
| 32 | 962.9 → 328.4 | 144 → 1832 | 961.2 → 418.6 | 190 → 2191 |
| **all 54 calls, total** | **2.61×** | | **2.10×** | |

The first version of this PR capped a pass at 8 images. In the same container, the capped version gave similar speedups of 2.55× and 2.08×, with lower peak memory on 16+ image calls.

**Accuracy.** MMMU-Pro standard (10 options), 1730 questions, 138 with more than one image. Real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp`, 2× B200, TP2 + EP, FP8 KV cache, block size 256, greedy, thinking off, no speculative decoding, `max_tokens=32`, concurrency 32. Runs in the order main → this PR → main, with a fresh server each time and 0 failed requests.

| | main | this PR | main again |
|---|---|---|---|
| correct, all 1730 | 861 | 862 | 860 |
| correct, 138 multi-image | 74 | 75 | 75 |

| answers that changed | total | multi-image | right → wrong | wrong → right |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main vs main again | 96 | 7 | 21 | 20 |
| this PR vs main | 200 | 13 | 47 | 48 |
| this PR vs main again | 196 | 11 | 50 | 52 |

Scoring takes the option letter only from the start of the reply or after "answer is"; anything else counts as no answer. That leaves 131 / 136 / 135 replies with no answer (main / PR / main again), mostly step-by-step explanations at the 32-token limit, and the same 2 multi-image replies in every run. Finish reasons were not saved, so I can't confirm each one hit the limit. This is a direct-answer setup, not a full MMMU-Pro evaluation, so the scores aren't comparable with published results.

Most changed answers are single-image questions. Under concurrency, images from different requests share an encoder call, so they also take the packed path.

Encoder-level error against an FP32 per-image reference, on 3 multi-image calls built from 2 real photos, is unchanged from the capped version:

| model | per-image | packed | packed vs per-image |
|---|---|---|---|
| V4 | 3.29 / 3.84 / 5.47% | 3.28 / 3.85 / 5.47% | 0.39 / 1.33 / 0.16% |
| V4.1 | 2.19 / 2.03 / 2.02% | 2.19 / 2.03 / 2.01% | 0.04 / 0.16 / 0.24% |

**KV cache.** Startup KV-cache size on the same servers: 202,321 and 202,340 tokens on main, 202,335 with this PR.

**Serving.** Same servers, run after MMMU-Pro, 0 failed requests. Values are main / main again → this PR, one run each.

| workload | requests | median TTFT ms | p99 TTFT ms | req/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 images, concurrency 1 | 100 | 378 / 367 → 271 | 413 / 431 → 311 | 2.51 / 2.56 → 3.44 |
| VisionArena, concurrency 16 | 500 | 959 / 914 → 548 | 9608 / 1012 → 652 | 10.0 / 16.0 → 24.6 |

The first main VisionArena run had a slow tail and lower throughput than the second, so I'd compare throughput and p99 against the second. The median is similar in both.

**Tests.** The unit test is removed, as requested. It compared packed and per-image output on H100 and passed there. Accuracy is covered by the MMMU-Pro run above.

**Revision.** All runs used the `190df0b900` main wheel with this PR's files on top. The PR is rebased on `bca1bc6516`, and the commits in between don't touch these files. The speedup depends on the machine: my first H100 run gave 2.01× and 1.63× (per-image 44.9 ms for 2 images, capped version, which runs within 2% of the uncapped one in the same container), this one 2.61× and 2.10× (59.6 ms). The per-image path is bound by kernel launches, so it is sensitive to the host. On one H100, the per-image path of the two main wheels (`2abde627d9`, `190df0b900`) differs by about 4%, close to the 2.6% between two runs of the same wheel, so the gap is mostly the machine.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 8}'

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path lmarena-ai/VisionArena-Chat --hf-split train \
  --hf-output-len 8 --num-prompts 500 --max-concurrency 16

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name random-mm --random-input-len 32 --random-output-len 8 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 4 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "video": 0}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config "{(768, 1024, 1): 0.4, (434, 600, 1): 0.3, (512, 512, 1): 0.3}" \
  --num-prompts 100 --max-concurrency 1
```

MMMU-Pro prompt: the question, then the options as `A. ...`, then "Answer with the option's letter from the given choices directly.", with the question's images before the text. The answer is the option letter at the start of the reply or after "answer is"; any other reply counts as no answer.

</details>

## Details

`_process_image_input` loops over images, so each one pays for its own kernel launches through 32 blocks. `forward_packed` runs them together, with per-image attention through `cu_seqlens`.

- **Scope.** Packing applies only to FlashAttention with two or more images. One image gains nothing from it, and I didn't measure other backends, so both keep the per-image path. `run_dp_sharded_vision_tower` and the graph manager's eager fallback are unchanged.
- **Memory.** Peak encoder memory grows with the images in a call. The startup profile run encodes the maximum items per batch, and the KV-cache size above did not change.
- **Rounding.** Each matmul sees more rows, so packed output rounds differently. Together with batching, that can change generated answers; the evaluation above shows more disagreements with no net change in scores, but does not separate the two causes.
- **Not tested.** V4.1 serving and MMMU-Pro (encoder results only), AMD (it shares the helper), thinking mode, DSpark speculative decoding, and MMMU-Pro with a larger output budget.
- **Overlaps.** #62802 has since merged and this branch still merges cleanly with main. #57985 touches some of these files and merges cleanly too. It removes the patch dtype cast, which is why `merge_mask` takes its dtype from the aligner weights. #58782 conflicts in `amd/vl_model.py`. #64435 and #57872 also target V4.1 but don't touch these files.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Keep P/D prompt tails on FULL graphs with adaptive verification
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview On a P/D decode instance with adaptive verification (AV), a step that admits a KV-transferred request runs eager instead of replaying the FULL decode graph, and under DP every rank runs eager with it. This PR fixes the condition that rejects the graph, in the runner and in the EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP drafter: two lines. ## Claims - **Before.** On D, a transferred request recomputes its last prompt token, so it is scheduled as 1 real token + K placeholder drafts, the shape of a decode row. It still counts as prefilling (`has_prefill=True`). The AV path (#57263) drops the query-length bound for any batch with `has_prefill`, so the AV decode graph rejects the step. The step runs eager under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (PIECEWISE under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), and the requests already decoding in the batch run eager with it. DP ranks agree on the bound, so one rank's arrival makes every rank run eager. - **After.** The bound is dropped only when the batch is not `decode_graph_eligible` (#58400). That existing classifier admits a one-token extension over existing KV and rejects real prefills, and the non-AV decode path already uses it. The drafter uses the same condition, so it keeps the target's padded layout (#62796). - **Effect.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark, vLLM P/D recipe settings at 1P1D DEP4. On main, eager steps (about 6x slower than FULL) take 60–77% of D's time, and most of them are ranks pulled eager by another rank's arrival. With this PR all of them replay FULL: output throughput is **2.0x** (OSL 256) and **1.76x** (OSL 1024), and D TPOT goes from 19.2 to 6.95 ms and from 10.6 to 5.69 ms. - **No degradation expected.** The changed value only feeds CUDA graph dispatch, and matching is monotonic: a bound where there was `None` can only add a match, since graphs without a bound match either way. Only AV captures bounded graphs, so dispatch without AV is unchanged. Real prefills (multi-token prompts, one-token prompts without prior KV, PCP batches) still run eager or PIECEWISE. GSM8K and draft acceptance stay within the baseline's run-to-run spread (DSpark and MTP, TP4 and DEP4). - **No extra resources.** No new graphs are captured, so graph count, CUDA graph memory and KV cache size are unchanged. The condition is a host-side bool already computed each step, so there is no new GPU sync or DP collective. - **Trade-offs.** An arrival step now pads its requests to the graph's capture size, the same padding every decode step pays; it is still about 6x faster than eager in the runs below. With D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, arrival steps move from PIECEWISE to FULL; D TPOT is unchanged within noise (TP4 cross-check below).
Code path on main: why an arrival step runs eager 1. **The arriving request counts as prefilling.** `prefill_len` is the number of tokens handed to the runner ([`states.py#L106`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py#L106)), usually the prompt length. `num_computed_prefill_tokens = min(num_computed_tokens, prefill_len)` ([`model_runner.py#L1332-L1336`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1332-L1336)). On D, the transferred KV covers all but the last prompt token, so the request arrives with `num_computed = prefill_len - 1` and is prefilling ([`#L1385-L1386`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1385-L1386)). After that step `num_computed >= prefill_len`, and the request decodes. 2. **`has_prefill` clears the bound.** The runner passes `max_query_len = None` for any batch with `has_prefill` ([`model_runner.py#L1848-L1851`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1848-L1851)), and so does the drafter ([`speculator.py#L273`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/target_dependent_ar/speculator.py#L273)). 3. **DP spreads `None`.** Ranks exchange the bound and keep it only if no rank sent `None` ([`dp_utils.py#L117-L119`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/dp_utils.py#L117-L119)). 4. **AV decode graphs need a bound.** With AV, decode graphs are captured as varlen graphs with `max_query_len=decode_query_len` ([`cudagraph_utils.py#L305-L319`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L305-L319)). A bounded graph matches only a batch that carries a bound within it ([`cudagraph_utils.py#L130-L133`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L130-L133)), so a `None` batch matches no decode graph. Under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` there is no PIECEWISE graph to fall back to, so the step runs eager. 5. **Without AV this does not happen.** Uniform decode graphs carry no bound and are matched by `uniform_token_count`, which already uses `decode_graph_eligible` ([`model_runner.py#L1404`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1404), [`utils.py#L1011`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L1011)). An arrival row (1 real token + K placeholder drafts) is uniform with the decode rows, so the step replays FULL. This PR uses `decode_graph_eligible` in step 2, the same classifier step 5 already uses.
## Validation All runs use upstream main `b8c04dd3b4` with that commit's precompiled wheel, 1P1D on two GB200 nodes over NIXL, with a fresh P/D pair per run. "Baseline" is that main commit without this PR. ### Performance The deployment follows the vLLM recipe preset for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (`gb300_agentx_pd`, from InferenceX #3941), scaled to one GB200 node per role: - P: DEP4, 64 seqs/rank, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, no AV. - D: DEP4, 40 seqs/rank, `max_num_batched_tokens=400`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with capture sizes 6..240, AV on, no prefix caching. - Both: DSpark K=5, MegaAttention, MegaMoE, DeepSelect top-k, Engram CPU offload. The client keeps 320 requests in flight (2x D capacity). Each request goes to P with `max_tokens=1`, then streams from D. Prompts are unique, outputs use `ignore_eos`, and 640 warmup requests run first. Baseline and this PR run in ABAB order; the table shows both rounds. TPOT and TTFT are measured on the D stream; TTFT includes queueing, since the client oversubscribes D. | Workload | Version | Output tok/s | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ISL ~290, OSL 256, 4096 req | baseline | 4,100 / 4,385 | 19.0 / 19.4 ms | 33.4 / 32.8 ms | 7.4 / 6.8 s | | | this PR | **8,559 / 8,519** | **6.93 / 6.97 ms** | 10.5 / 10.5 ms | 3.6 / 3.7 s | | ISL ~2.2K, OSL 1024, 2048 req | baseline | 8,533 / 8,666 | 10.7 / 10.6 ms | 19.3 / 19.4 ms | 13.0 / 12.8 s | | | this PR | **15,099 / 15,231** | **5.71 / 5.66 ms** | 9.9 / 10.1 ms | 7.3 / 7.2 s | **Why it is large under data parallelism.** DP ranks agree on one graph shape per step, and the agreed query-length bound is `None` if any rank sends `None`. So a single rank admitting a transferred request forces every rank's step to run eager, including ranks that only have decodes. A second traced run of the same setup splits D's steps per rank (4 ranks, warmup excluded). Step time is the gap to the next step on the same rank: | Workload | Version | Own arrival steps | Decode steps forced eager by another rank | FULL decode steps | Time in eager steps | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | OSL 256 | baseline | 11.7%, eager, 102 ms | **20.5%, 102 ms** | 67.8%, 15.0 ms | 77% | | | this PR | 10.0%, FULL, 15.2 ms | 0 | 90.0%, 15.4 ms | 0 | | OSL 1024 | baseline | 5.4%, eager, 101 ms | **13.0%, 101 ms** | 81.6%, 17.1 ms | 60% | | | this PR | 5.5%, FULL, 16.1 ms | 0 | 94.5%, 17.7 ms | 0 | Steps forced eager by another rank outnumber a rank's own arrival steps 1.75–2.4x. The chance that some rank admits a request in a given step rises with the DP size, so we expect the effect to be larger on the recipe's DEP16 decode (not measured here). The gain depends on how often a decode step admits a transferred request, so it is smaller for longer outputs. In the TP4 cross-check below, D under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with this PR reaches the same TPOT (6.7 ms) as the same D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, where arrival steps ran PIECEWISE instead of eager.
TP4 cross-check: P PIECEWISE, D TP4 FULL_DECODE_ONLY + AV, 128 seqs, 128 in flight, ISL ~290, OSL 256, 3 ABAB rounds | Model | Version | TPOT mean (3 rounds) | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark K=3 | baseline | 17.8 / 20.0 / 20.0 ms | 29.9-31.0 ms | 1.08-1.12 s | | | this PR | 6.72 / 6.70 / 6.75 ms | 9.4 ms | 0.40-0.42 s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP K=3 | baseline | 17.8 / 24.7 / 25.8 ms | 35.0-37.6 ms | 1.41-1.54 s | | | this PR | 5.42 / 5.41 / 5.38 ms | 7.1-7.2 ms | 0.37-0.39 s | Same workload with D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, where main runs arrival steps PIECEWISE and this PR runs them FULL: | Model | Version | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark K=3 | baseline | 6.72 ms | 9.38 ms | 0.44 s | | | this PR | 6.75 ms | 9.27 ms | 0.41 s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP K=3 | baseline | 5.44 / 5.68 ms | 7.41 / 7.48 ms | 0.47 / 0.39 s | | | this PR | 5.33 ms | 7.19 ms | 0.39 s |
### Correctness Setup: - P and D TP4 + EP. - D: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` + AV, 128 seqs. - The decode-side graph mode is traced per step on all ranks; the ranks agree. - "Arrival step" means a decode-eligible batch with `has_prefill`, i.e. it contains a transferred request computing its last prompt token. Workload per run: - 8 serial prompts (19..8195 tokens), 16 staggered and 32 burst requests. - Two direct-to-D negative controls: a multi-token prompt without transferred KV, and a fresh one-token prompt. - Full GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 8, temperature 0. **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=3)** | Version | Arrival steps | Real prefills | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 1128 eager | 6 eager | 1190 / 1319 | 1.962 | | this PR | **1316 FULL** | 6 eager | 1194 / 1319 | 1.961 | | baseline, repeat | | | 1187 / 1319 | 1.976 | **DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP (K=3)**, which uses `TargetDependentARSpeculator` | Version | Arrival steps: target / drafter | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | eager / eager (1010) | 1248 / 1319 | 1.879 | | runner condition only | FULL / **eager** (1168) | 1249 / 1319 | 1.877 | | this PR | **FULL / FULL** (1163) | 1253 / 1319 | 1.873 | **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=5), DEP4 recipe config from the performance section** | Version | Own arrival steps | Decode steps forced eager by another rank | Real prefills | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 5.0%, eager | 11.7%, eager | 2 eager | 1193 / 1319 | 2.067 | | this PR | 5.1%, **FULL** | **0** | 2 eager | 1184 / 1319 | 2.049 | | baseline, repeat | | | | 1196 / 1319 | 2.048 | | this PR, repeat | | | | 1200 / 1319 | 2.090 | Serving with expert parallelism is not bitwise deterministic run to run. Baseline spans 1193–1196 and 2.048–2.067; this PR spans 1184–1200 and 2.049–2.090. Between the first baseline and first PR runs, 45 questions flip correct → wrong and 36 wrong → correct. With only the runner condition, an arrival step replays the target graph padded to, for example, 32 requests, while the drafter runs eager over the 7 real ones on the same attention metadata. That is the mismatch #62796 removed. On this sparse-MLA model it costs no measurable acceptance; #62793 shows that it does on FA3. In every run, all measured requests succeeded, with no preemptions and no KV transfer failures. Pure decode steps are FULL in every run, except the startup warmup steps, which run eager. The GSM8K and acceptance differences fall within the baseline repeat spread.
Unit tests ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dp_utils.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py # 116 passed, on the branch rebased onto current main ``` - Reverting only the runner condition fails `test_prompt_tail_keeps_decode_graph_bound[True-8]`. - Reverting only the drafter condition fails `test_draft_prefill_matches_shared_target_metadata_shape[decode-eligible-prefill-tail]`. - Both files already run in CI under `tests/v1/worker` and `tests/v1/cudagraph`.
## Details **Request path.** 1. The proxy sends the prompt to P with `max_tokens=1` and `do_remote_decode`; P prefills and returns KV transfer metadata. 2. The proxy sends the same prompt with that metadata to D. D's scheduler pulls the KV over NIXL and marks the whole prompt as computed. 3. On load completion, the scheduler sets `num_computed_tokens = N - 1`, so D recomputes the last prompt position to get logits for its first sampled token. With K speculative tokens, the request is scheduled as 1 real token + K placeholder drafts (`q = K + 1`): the shape of a decode row. 4. The runner classifies the batch and dispatches a CUDA graph. This step is the one that changes. **Root cause.** In step 4, the request is still prefilling (`num_computed_prefill < prefill_len`), so `has_prefill` is True. - #57263 cleared the runner's `max_query_len` for any batch with `has_prefill`, because a varlen decode graph matched on that bound alone would admit a short real prefill. - Two days later, #58400 added `decode_graph_eligible`, which treats a one-token extension over existing context as a decode. Input preparation already handles this case through `prefill_runs_as_decode`. #58400 wired the classification into the uniform decode path only. - The varlen path that AV uses kept the `has_prefill` check. So with AV off, D replays FULL on arrival steps; with AV on, it does not. - `TargetDependentARSpeculator.propose` has the same check for its draft-prefill dispatch. **Dispatch before and after.** The red edge is main's path for a P/D arrival step; the green edge is the path this PR takes. Real prefills take the grey path in both. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["D step: transferred request = 1 real token + K placeholder drafts
(+ requests already decoding)"] --> B["gather_batch_req_state
has_prefill = True
decode_graph_eligible = True"] P["Real prefill: multi-token prompt, or one-token prompt without context"] --> Q["decode_graph_eligible = False"] Q --> N B -->|"main: if has_prefill"| N["max_query_len = None"] B -->|"this PR: if not decode_graph_eligible"| K["max_query_len = K + 1"] N --> S["DP sync: the agreed bound is None if any rank sent None"] S --> X["AV varlen FULL decode graph rejected on every DP rank
FULL_DECODE_ONLY → eager · FULL_AND_PIECEWISE → PIECEWISE"] K --> Y["AV varlen FULL decode graph replayed
(drafter draft-prefill uses the same bound and padded layout)"] linkStyle 3 stroke:#d62728,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 4 stroke:#2ca02c,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 2 stroke:#999999 ``` Without AV, the decode graph is matched by `uniform_token_count`, which already uses `decode_graph_eligible`, so arrival steps were not affected. **Change.** - Two conditions change from `has_prefill` to `not decode_graph_eligible`: one in `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`, one in `TargetDependentARSpeculator.propose`. The other edits update comments that described the old rule. - The classifier, scheduler, input preparation, capture sizes and kernels are unchanged. - Keeping the bound only removes one rejection reason. The existing graph checks (query-length bound, request/token coverage, explicit eager, DP agreement on the bound) still apply. - DFlash/DSpark drafters dispatch with a fixed uniform shape and are not affected. - Model Runner V1 does not support AV, so it needs no change. **Relation to #64915.** #64915 contains the same runner condition as part of a larger feature: varlen decode graphs for fixed-width speculation, with new backend and capacity checks. This PR is only the AV bug fix. It adds the drafter condition, which #64915 lacks, plus a regression test and P/D validation with real KV transfer, which #64915 lists as outstanding. If this PR merges first, #64915 drops the overlapping line. No other open PR changes these conditions. **Limitations.** - GPU validation covers DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DSpark) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MTP) on GB200 with the MLA backends those models use. FA3/FlashInfer targets are covered only by the unit test of the drafter/target layout contract. - The performance runs are 1P1D with D scaled down from the recipe's DEP16 to DEP4. Prompts are synthetic, with no prefix reuse. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, implementation, validation and this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the results. ---

title: [Kernel] Enable CuteDSL GDN prefill on SM110
author: yeh-sudo
body:
## Overview

Lets the opt-in CuteDSL GDN prefill backend (`--gdn-prefill-backend cutedsl`) run on SM110 (Jetson Thor), and fixes its kernel launch on GPUs with fewer SMs than value heads. Related: #63284 rewrites the same selector function, so whichever PR merges second will need a small rebase. #62149 is a separate Thor GDN warmup crash that this PR does not fix.

## Claims

- `--gdn-prefill-backend cutedsl` now runs on SM110. Before, the selector fell back to Triton/FLA.
- On GPUs with fewer SMs than value heads, the CuteDSL kernels failed to launch with `CUDA_LAUNCH_INVALID_CONFIG`. Thor has 20 SMs and Qwen3.8-27B has 48 value heads. The kernels now launch at least one CTA per head.
- On Thor with `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, cutedsl lowers TTFT on 16k-token prompts by about 6% compared with triton. GSM8K is within error.
- `auto` makes the same choice as before on every platform. On SM10x, the larger grid size only takes effect for models with more than 148 value heads.

## Validation

Jetson AGX Thor (SM110, 20 SMs), CUDA 13.2, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (BF16, `head_k_dim=128`, 48 value heads).

**Kernel test** (`tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py`):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Without the `num_sms` fix | 6 failed, 7 passed: every `num_v_heads=160` case raises `CUDA_LAUNCH_INVALID_CONFIG` in `kkt_inv_uw_cutedsl` |
| With the fix | 13 passed |

**End to end**, `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` vs `cutedsl` (startup logs confirm the selected kernel):

| Backend | GSM8K strict | GSM8K flexible | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P90 TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.7058 | 0.7339 | 16573.6 ± 8.9 | 16563.6 ± 11.8 | 16634.4 ± 14.0 |
| cutedsl | 0.6990 | 0.7240 | 15555.3 ± 1.0 | 15551.1 ± 1.6 | 15565.8 ± 6.6 |

- GSM8K: full 1319-question set, 5-shot. lm-eval reports a standard error of ±0.012–0.013 per score, so the −0.7 / −1.0 point differences are within noise.
- TTFT: 16k-token random prompts, 1 output token, concurrency 1, 16 prompts per run, 3 runs with seeds 1–3 (mean ± stdev). `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, so each prompt is prefilled in two chunks.
- All 48 benchmark requests succeeded on both backends, and neither server log has errors.

CI has no SM110 runner. The B200 `Kernels` job runs the updated test, and its `num_v_heads=160` case exceeds the B200's 148 SMs, so it covers the grid fix.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --language-model-only --gdn-prefill-backend {triton,cutedsl}

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=8,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False

vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 16 \
  --max-concurrency 1 --seed {1,2,3} --percentile-metrics ttft,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90
```

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause:** `kkt_inv_uw_cutedsl` and `o_cutedsl` launch `grid = (num_sms // Hv, Hv, 1)`. When `num_sms < Hv`, the first grid dimension is 0 and CUDA rejects the launch. Both kernels now clamp the first grid dimension to at least 1 (`cutlass.max(num_sms // Hv, 1)`), which gives one CTA per head and also covers direct callers of the kernels. Both kernels loop over chunks with a stride equal to the grid size (`range(bid, num_global_chunks, grid_x)`), so the grid size doesn't affect results. `kernel_h` uses a `(Hv, N)` grid and isn't affected.
- **Selector:** SM11x with `head_k_dim == 128` and CUDA 13+ now allows CuteDSL. It doesn't allow FlashInfer, so `auto` still resolves to Triton on SM110.
- **Not a duplicate of #63284:** that PR splits "can run" from "preferred" for FlashInfer and CuteDSL, but doesn't add SM110 or touch the kernel grid size. If it merges first, this PR only needs SM110 added to its `can_run_cutedsl` check and its "targets SM100" error text updated.
- **Test gap:** no unit test checks that the selector picks CuteDSL on SM110. CI has no SM110 GPU, and faking the GPU type would need mocks. The startup log line from the Thor run is the evidence instead.
- **Docs:** the `--gdn-prefill-backend` help text now says where `cutedsl` works.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used to write and validate this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

---

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Only set PDL launch attr for MoE top-k gating on SM90+
author: srkim-business
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65055. Since #59737, `topkGating` is launched with the PDL attribute on every CUDA arch. Pre-SM90 GPUs cannot use PDL, but stream capture still records the attribute as a programmatic edge in the CUDA graph, and replaying those graphs is slower. This PR sets the attribute only when the device is SM90+. SM90+ keeps the #59737 behaviour; older GPUs launch without the attribute, which measured the same as the v0.32 `<<<>>>` launch. The standalone effect was measured on sm80, sm86 and sm89; end-to-end numbers are A100 only.

## Claims

- 4× A100, TP4 + EP + MTP (our deployment config, private NVFP4 checkpoint of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; setup below): per-request decode is 6.5–13.6% faster in 17 of 18 prompt × concurrency (1–16) cells, and 2.1% in the 18th. At concurrency 16: prose 74.3 → 80.1 and code 88.7 → 94.8 tok/s, close to the last commit before #59737 (3b05805d4: 81.5 and 95.3, one run).
- Standalone CUDA (no vLLM): the attribute adds one programmatic edge per launch and 0.6–1.1 µs of graph replay per edge on A100 (sm80), RTX A4000 (sm86) and RTX 4090 (sm89), in every round; without the attribute `cudaLaunchKernelEx` matches `<<<>>>`.
- 1× A100, CUDA graph replay of a router GEMM → `topk_softmax` chain: 6.9–9.0% faster for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Qwen3-30B-A3B and OLMoE shapes at 1/16/48 tokens, in every round against a no-change rebuild.
- 1× A100 end to end, `vllm bench latency`: batch 1 is 0.7% faster for OLMoE-1B-7B (every round vs a no-change rebuild, 2 of 3 rounds vs the shipped build) and 1.2% faster for Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 (every round). Batch 16 is within noise for both.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K 5-shot on Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 is 85.90% (base) vs 86.13% (fix). The kernel body is identical.
- SM90+ is unchanged by construction (the same attribute is set as before); not measured.

## Validation

Hardware: A100-PCIE-40GB, driver 590.48.01, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, vLLM v0.33.0 (4ba787ec9). `base` = the v0.33.0 `_moe_C` as shipped. `rebuilt` = the same source built with the same toolchain, no change. `fix` = `rebuilt` + this diff. Builds are `_moe_C` only, for sm80, overlaid on the v0.33.0 install. The diff applies unchanged to main (the file is identical).

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py` on A100: base 864 passed, fix 864 passed.
- GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`): Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 85.90% → 86.13%; OLMoE-1B-7B (base model, near the floor with this script) 9.93% → 10.01%. Invalid rate 0–0.8%.
- CI: the L4 (sm89) "MoE Kernels" step runs `tests/kernels/moe` on `csrc/moe/` changes and covers the launch without the attribute; the SM90+ launch is unchanged. No new test: there is no functional change, and a regression check would need graph-edge inspection or timing, which does not belong in `tests/`.

**Op chain, CUDA graph, µs per replay** (median of 6 rounds, A/B/B/A order; Δ = median paired `fix − rebuilt`)

| shape (experts, top-k, hidden, layers) | tokens | base | rebuilt | fix | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (512, 10, 2560, 48) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 843 / 893 / 917 | 846 / 894 / 916 | 782 / 831 / 850 | −7.6% / −6.9% / −7.2% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (128, 8, 2048, 48) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 592 / 672 / 688 | 596 / 674 / 691 | 542 / 620 / 636 | −9.0% / −7.9% / −8.0% |
| OLMoE-1B-7B (64, 8, 2048, 16) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 194 / 209 / 221 | 194 / 209 / 221 | 177 / 192 / 204 | −8.7% / −8.4% / −7.8% |

**End to end, `vllm bench latency`** (input 128, output 256, 3 rounds, ms per step)

| model | batch | base | rebuilt | fix | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 | 1 | 2.952 | 2.950 | 2.932 | −0.7% (3/3 rounds vs rebuilt, 2/3 vs base) |
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 | 16 | 7.789 | 7.731 | 7.802 | within noise |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 1 | 5.805 | – | 5.722 | −1.2% (3/3 rounds) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 16 | 12.188 | – | 12.136 | within noise (2/3 rounds faster) |

<details>
<summary>TP4 setup</summary>

v0.33.0, 4× A100-PCIE-40GB, `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel`, NVFP4 weights, MTP with 2 draft tokens, `--compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, bf16 KV, a custom logits processor. Client: c concurrent streaming chat requests, 384 output tokens, model-default sampling; per-request decode = (tokens − 1) / (last − first token time), averaged. Prose / code / numbers prompts × c = 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16; two server starts per arm, A/B/B/A. With MTP, c = 1 varies by about ±10% from run to run through the draft acceptance rate.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Standalone CUDA reproduction (no vLLM) and commands</summary>

48 × (plain kernel → consumer kernel); only the consumer launch changes. A100, 21 rounds:

| consumer launch | graph replay, GPU µs | eager, GPU µs |
|---|---:|---:|
| `<<<>>>` | 128.7 | 239.8 |
| `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, no attribute | 128.7 | 239.3 |
| `cudaLaunchKernelEx` + PDL attribute | 181.8 | 239.8 |
| PDL attribute on the first consumer only | 130.3 | 239.4 |

Same harness, graph replay, other pre-Hopper GPUs (21 rounds, PDL attribute slower in every round):

| GPU (arch) | `<<<>>>` µs | + PDL attribute | per edge | `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, no attribute |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A100-PCIE-40GB (sm80) | 128.7 | +53.1 (+41%) | 1.1 µs | +0.03 |
| RTX A4000 (sm86) | 83.6 | +29.9 (+36%) | 0.62 µs | +0.11 |
| RTX 4090 (sm89) | 79.0 | +30.0 (+38%) | 0.63 µs | −0.10 |

`cudaGraphGetEdges` reports one programmatic edge per PDL launch on all three. The standalone harness and the op-chain script are in https://gist.github.com/srkim-business/ec5db57f7b78a9c9f06af65c891216c2.

```bash
# end to end (OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, batch 1 and 16)
vllm bench latency --model <model> --batch-size <1|16> --input-len 128 --output-len 256 \
  --num-iters-warmup 5 --num-iters 15 --seed 0 --max-model-len 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
# GSM8K
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --seed 0
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --seed 42 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64
# kernel tests
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Root cause: on pre-SM90 the attribute does nothing for eager launches, but stream capture records it as a programmatic edge (`cudaGraphGetEdges` counts one per launch on sm80). Each edge adds about 1.1 µs of GPU time per graph replay on A100.
- #59737 first had this host check (uncached); review asked to drop it for consistency with `topk_softplus_sqrt` / `per_token_group_quant` and to avoid `cudaGetDevice` + `call_once` per eager launch. The measurements above are the reason to bring it back. It is cached in a function-local static as in `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` (`numAttrs = (sm_version >= 90) ? 1 : 0`), so eager launches pay nothing per call. This also matches the scope in #59737's own description ("Enable PDL for the consumer on SM90+"). Python launch sites already gate PDL on `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`.
- The static is initialized once per template instantiation, on the device the caller's `DeviceGuard` selects. It assumes all GPUs in a process share the major arch, which holds for vLLM workers (one GPU each); a mismatch would only affect speed, not results.
- The 1-GPU gain (about 1%) matches the GPU-side edge cost. The TP4 + EP + MTP gain does not: at concurrency 16 a decode step goes from about 29.5 to 27.3 ms, while 48 edges × 1.1 µs is about 0.05 ms per forward; we have not located the rest. The TP4 A/B swaps only `_moe_C` (shipped → this diff built from the same source); on one GPU a no-change rebuild is within 0.8% (median) of the shipped build, so we attribute the gain to this diff.
- Other C++ launchers still set the attribute on all archs, for example `topk_softplus_sqrt_kernels.cu` and `per_token_group_quant.cu` (the latter can run on sm89 for FP8). They are left out to keep this fix small enough to cherry-pick; a shared helper can follow if maintainers prefer.
- Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR changes this launch attribute (searched `topkGating PDL`, `topk_softmax PDL`, `59737`). #62912 (open) changes top-k selection in the same file and keeps `config.numAttrs = 1` as context next to this change, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; it does not touch the attribute.
- Not covered: Hopper/Blackwell (unchanged code path, not measured), sm75 and older, end to end on GPUs other than A100, and a full main build (only `_moe_C` was rebuilt and overlaid on v0.33.0).
- This is a performance regression against v0.32.0; we'd like it cherry-picked into a v0.33.x patch release if one is planned.
- I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, the code and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix KV role detection for MultiConnector with nested connectors
author: xsxszab
body:
## Overview

`KVTransferConfig.is_kv_producer` and `is_kv_consumer` only look at the top-level `kv_role`, but a `MultiConnector` never passes that role to its child connectors; each child uses its own. The documented MooncakeStore prefiller (top-level `kv_producer`, with a `kv_both` MooncakeStore child) therefore does not look like a consumer, so the scheduler does not defer freeing blocks, and a step still running for an aborted request can overwrite KV that was just loaded into the reused blocks. This PR makes both properties follow the child connectors' roles.

Credit to @nandanadileep, who found this issue and proposed the first fix in [#62438](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62438), and is a co-author of this PR. #62438 defers block freeing for every connector; this PR instead fixes how a `MultiConnector`'s role is determined, so blocks are deferred only when one of its child connectors loads KV.

## Claims

- For a `MultiConnector`, `is_kv_producer` and `is_kv_consumer` follow the roles of its child connectors. The top-level `kv_role` no longer matters.
- The documented prefiller is now a consumer, so it defers block freeing and its loaded KV is no longer overwritten after an abort. If every child is `kv_producer`, blocks are still freed immediately.

## Validation

**Regression test.** `test_multi_connector_role_follows_children` checks both properties for four combinations of top-level and child roles. On main, the three where the top-level role disagrees with the children fail; with this PR, all four pass. It is marked `cpu_test`, so the CPU CI step runs it.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children
```

<details>
<summary>Output on main and with this PR (B300, trimmed)</summary>

```text
# vllm/ at main (db7f2d7c44), with this PR's test
$ cd tests && python -m pytest -v -m cpu_test v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -k role_follows_children
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[loading-child] FAILED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[pure-producers] PASSED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[saving-child] FAILED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[no-loading-child] FAILED

[loading-child]
>       assert config.is_kv_consumer is consumer
E       AssertionError: assert False is True
[saving-child]
>       assert config.is_kv_producer is producer
E       AssertionError: assert False is True
[no-loading-child]
>       assert config.is_kv_consumer is consumer
E       AssertionError: assert True is False

3 failed, 1 passed, 32 deselected in 2.06s

# this PR (1167d0cfa7), same command
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[loading-child] PASSED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[pure-producers] PASSED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[saving-child] PASSED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[no-loading-child] PASSED

4 passed, 32 deselected in 2.37s
```

</details>

**Effect on the documented configs.** For each config, I built a real `VllmConfig` (Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct) and a `PrometheusStatLogger` on main and with this PR. Changed values are shown as main → this PR.

| Config | `is_kv_consumer` | `is_kv_producer` | KV fetch metric | Requests may omit multimodal embeddings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prefiller: top-level `kv_producer`; MooncakeConnector `kv_producer` + MooncakeStore `kv_both` | False → True | True | missing → present | no → yes |
| Decoder: everything `kv_consumer` | True | False | present | yes |
| Top-level `kv_consumer`; MooncakeConnector `kv_consumer` + MooncakeStore `kv_both` | True | False → True | present | yes |

`is_kv_consumer` also decides whether the scheduler defers freeing blocks (only with async scheduling or PP), and `is_kv_producer` decides whether `finalize_partial_tail_offloads` runs when a request finishes.

**End to end.** The prefiller config on B300, PP=4, Model Runner V2, async scheduling, MooncakeStore over RDMA with `load_async`. Four concurrent loops each abort a request, then send a request whose prefix is loaded from MooncakeStore into the blocks just freed. Every loaded block is checksummed when its load completes and again before the request's first forward pass; a mismatch means the KV was overwritten in between.

| Model / setting | Top-level `kv_producer`, no deferred freeing | With deferred freeing | How deferred freeing was enabled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-32B, 1 s sleep added to the aborted request's steps | 13/24 loads overwritten | 0/24 | This PR |
| Qwen3-32B, no added sleep | 0/298 | 0/598 | This PR |
| Qwen2.5-7B, no added sleep (`70d67f19d`) | 0/300, 3/300, 3/300, 4/300 by PP rank | 0/303 on every rank | Top-level `kv_both` |

The added sleep runs on the compute stream in steps that contain the aborted request, so its writes land after the load and the overwrite shows up often.

## Details

**Root cause.** `Scheduler.__init__` sets `defer_block_free` from `kv_transfer_config.is_kv_consumer`. Deferring keeps a finished request's blocks out of the free pool until its in-flight steps are done. With the documented prefiller config:

1. Request A is aborted while one of its steps is still queued on the GPU.
2. The top-level role is `kv_producer`, so A's blocks go back to the free pool at once.
3. Request B finds its prefix in MooncakeStore and is given those blocks. The `kv_both` child loads B's KV into them over RDMA, which is not ordered with the GPU compute stream.
4. A's queued step runs and writes A's KV into the same blocks. B then computes on that KV without any error.

**Change.** For a `MultiConnector`, `is_kv_producer` and `is_kv_consumer` read each child's `kv_role` from `kv_connector_extra_config["connectors"]`, the same way `has_connector()` and `uses_custom_mem_pool()` read the children. Behavior only changes when the top-level role disagrees with the children, as in the three test cases that fail on main: a top-level `kv_producer` with a child that loads KV (the documented prefiller) becomes a consumer; a top-level `kv_consumer` with a `kv_both` child becomes a producer; and a top-level `kv_both` with only `kv_producer` children is no longer a consumer, so it frees blocks immediately, since nothing loads into them.

AI assistance: Claude Code for implementation, tests, and experiments; Claude Code and ChatGPT for this description. I reviewed the changes and ran the validation above.

title: [KVConnector][Mooncake] Add per-GPU device names for MooncakeStoreConnector
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in `device_name_per_gpu` key to the Mooncake Store config: RDMA device names indexed by physical GPU ID, of which each rank's store client gets only its own GPU's entry. `device_name` keeps the all-HCAs behaviour from #43799. Companion to kvcache-ai/Mooncake#5151.

## Claims

- `setup_mooncake_store` passes the current GPU's entry when the key is set, else `device_name` as before. This covers MooncakeStoreConnector and the Mooncake EC connector's embedding store, both built in GPU workers.
- The two keys are mutually exclusive. An empty list, a blank entry or a GPU with no entry raises `ValueError`. Sleep mode accepts either key.
- An entry may list several devices, so a B300 host can give each GPU its two HCAs.

## Validation

- `whx/mooncake-store-per-gpu-nic @ b74843e87`: `test_mooncake_store_worker.py` 254 passed, including the new selection and invalid-config tests; 1 setup error because I ran without `tests/conftest.py` (the `caplog_vllm` fixture). pre-commit clean.
- Not from this branch: Kimi-K3 1P1D on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X with an equivalent runtime patch (each rank limited to `rdma<physical GPU>`). The prefill Store registered 209 GiB per rank and the benchmark passed. Without it, every rank tried all 8 NICs and Store init failed (details below).

## Details

Why not all NICs: when a rank's NICs span NUMA nodes, Mooncake maps the global segment with 4KB pages, and on MI355X `ibv_reg_mr` failed with EINVAL within each rank's first 2 GiB. kvcache-ai/Mooncake#5151 fixes the allocation; whether 8 ranks then fit on every NIC is untested, and one NIC per GPU is the setup measured here.

#42689 picked one CSV entry by GPU index, which #43799 removed for B300 (8 GPUs, 16 HCAs). An explicit list keeps that case expressible and changes no default. AI-assisted (Claude in Cursor).

<details><summary>Failing run without per-GPU NICs</summary>

```
real_client.cpp:1162] NUMA-segmented mode: NIC NUMA nodes=[0,1]
mmap_buffer.cpp:355] Allocated NUMA-segmented buffer: 224873414656 bytes, 2 regions, page_size=4096, nodes=[0,1]
rdma_context.cpp:803] Failed to register memory 0x74c143200000 length 67108864 dmabuf_offset 0 on rdma5 MC_RDMA_DATA_DIRECT=0: Invalid argument [22]
```

92 such failures, all on rdma5, across all 8 ranks. Store-process AnonHugePages per rank: 2,967,552 kB here, 222,558,208 kB with one NIC per GPU on the same node.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Keep numeric-string prompts as strings in CustomDataset
author: Vegetog
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65071. `CustomDataset.load_data()` lets `pd.read_json` infer the `prompt` column's dtype, so a JSONL file whose prompts are all numeric strings (`"00123"`, `"00456"`) is loaded as integers. Leading zeros are lost and `sample()` then fails in the tokenizer.

## Claims

- JSON string prompts are kept exactly as written, regardless of what other rows contain.
- `output_tokens` and other columns are unaffected.

## Validation

New regression test `test_custom_dataset_keeps_numeric_string_prompts` (CPU-only, local `WordLevel` tokenizer, no download) builds a real `CustomDataset` and calls `sample()`.

Before the fix (source reverted to `origin/main`):

```text
$ pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py -k numeric_string
E   ValueError: text input must be of type `str` (single example), `list[str]` ...
1 failed, 2 deselected
```

With the fix:

```text
$ pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py
3 passed
```

Lint: `pre-commit` hooks pass on the commit (ruff check/format, mypy, forbidden imports, test tethering). The test is picked up by the existing "Benchmarks CLI" step (`pytest -v -s benchmarks/`).

## Details

Root cause: pandas' default `dtype=True` coerces string columns that all parse as numbers. Passing `dtype={"prompt": str}` keeps the column as-is; other columns keep their current inference, so `output_tokens` behaviour is unchanged.

The other two `pd.read_json` callers in `datasets.py` read list-valued columns (`turns` / `messages`), which pandas does not coerce, so they are left alone.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #65071. #60506 and #61776 also touch `CustomDataset` but address output lengths / audio without a tokenizer in `sample()`, not the `read_json` dtype.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3.1] Four-wave decode top-k for the NVFP4 indexer
author: chao-xu-spec
body:
## Overview

On gfx950, the MiniMax-M3.1 NVFP4 indexer picks the 16 best blocks of every decode row with one wave per row. This PR gives each decode row four waves and merges their top-16 lists exactly, so the ordered block ids are unchanged. No other kernel, flag or call site changes.

## Claims

- Decode top-k is 4.1x faster over the decode shapes of a served MiniMax-M3.1 AgentX run (18.9 -> 4.65 us per call, weighted by how often each shape occurs, real index scores); 4.07x in the live server (21.2 -> 5.2 us per call). With random scores the same shapes give 1.26x: the old kernel is much slower on real scores (see Details).
- End to end (TP4, 2 runs per arm): c16 +1.34% and c32 +2.47% tok/s/GPU, TPOT p50 -12.2% / -12.0%, p90 -8.3% / -8.2% (interactivity p50 +13.9% / +13.6%, p90 +9.0% / +8.9%).
- Same output as before: bit-for-bit equal to AITER's `pa_sparse_block_topk` and to the old kernel in 4,500 sweep cases (772,650 rows); eager and CUDA-graph replay agree. In a replay of the real served calls 1 of 2,816 decode rows differs, in a call with duplicate page ids where the old kernel's own output changes from run to run. GSM8K and spec-decode accept length are unchanged.
- **Costs:** With random scores a call is up to 12% slower when every row is under about 213k tokens; with real scores that only shows for calls in which no row triggers the old kernel's slow path. See Limits.

## Validation

**Microbench.** MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash` with the two top-k files of this PR on top of main (7b77ed581d; the files are unchanged on main at 76c6f3f2a9, where the test file was re-run); stock = main's files. CUDA-graph replay of 16 back-to-back calls on distinct score buffers, 1 GiB memset (cold L2) before every replay, median of 20 replays per process, 6 fresh processes per arm; per-call us, median of the 6 (process-to-process range at most 0.07 us ours, 0.21 us stock). 1 index head, 4 rows per request, output equal in every process. Scores are the real output of the unchanged scorer on captured queries and index-K pages of a served run (grid cells: re-scored captured requests clipped to the cell's lengths; live lengths uniform in [max/2, max]). Rows = requests, columns = max sequence length (graph width). Not a repo benchmark (none exists for this op); the method is in the details block.

Stock / ours, us (speedup), real scores:

| Requests | 64k | 128k | 256k | 512k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10.5 / 4.00 (2.6x) | 11.4 / 4.00 (2.9x) | 12.2 / 4.44 (2.8x) | 20.8 / 4.71 (4.4x) |
| 2 | 8.7 / 4.05 (2.1x) | 15.0 / 4.05 (3.7x) | 18.5 / 4.51 (4.1x) | 20.6 / 4.64 (4.4x) |
| 4 | 16.5 / 4.10 (4.0x) | 17.4 / 4.10 (4.3x) | 18.3 / 4.54 (4.0x) | 35.3 / 4.68 (7.6x) |
| 8 | 18.3 / 4.11 (4.4x) | 18.3 / 4.12 (4.4x) | 20.4 / 4.64 (4.4x) | 35.9 / 4.74 (7.6x) |
| 16 | 18.3 / 4.15 (4.4x) | 18.4 / 4.23 (4.3x) | 20.1 / 4.69 (4.3x) | 36.5 / 4.86 (7.5x) |
| 32 | 18.4 / 4.23 (4.3x) | 18.5 / 4.34 (4.3x) | 20.6 / 4.84 (4.2x) | 36.8 / 5.18 (7.1x) |
| 64 | 18.5 / 4.35 (4.2x) | 18.6 / 4.45 (4.2x) | 20.7 / 5.16 (4.0x) | 36.8 / 5.83 (6.3x) |
| 100 | 18.6 / 4.77 (3.9x) | 18.8 / 4.95 (3.8x) | 21.0 / 5.81 (3.6x) | 37.4 / 6.90 (5.4x) |

Served shapes (20 decode graph calls of a TP4 AgentX c16 run: real lengths, padded batch, max length 1M, 1-14 requests), weighted by call count: stock 18.91 us (18.91-18.92), ours 4.65 us (4.65-4.66) per call, 4.06x (per process 4.06-4.07x); per call 1.04x to 7.4x. The same shapes with random scores: 5.79 / 4.61 us, 1.255x (table and per-call numbers in the details block).

**E2E.** amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 (MXFP4 experts, MXFP8 dense linears), TP4 EP1 on 4x MI355X, nvfp4 KV and indexer cache, DSpark with 3 draft tokens (synthetic acceptance 2.88), DBO, max-model-len 1M, `--max-num-seqs` 32 (c16) / 64 (c32). CI image plus an overlay of the two changed files (the four files of the decode top-k and its scorer are byte-identical to main's); stock = the image as is. InferenceX AgentX replay (agentx-harness 1.0.12, cc-traces-weka-062126), 3600 s per run, the CI client flags; 2 runs per arm in ABBA order (stock, ours, ours, stock), server restarted per run; ranges are min-max of the 2 runs. Noise floor = the larger of the stock-vs-stock range and the spread of 5 (c16) / 2 (c32) earlier stock runs; a change counts if it exceeds 2x the floor, has the same sign in both adjacent ABBA pairs and the runs do not overlap.

| Concurrency | Stock (tok/s/GPU) | Ours (tok/s/GPU) | Change | Stock TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | Ours TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | Change p50 / p90 | Noise floor (tok/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 168.70 (168.48-168.91) | 170.95 (170.92-170.98) | +1.34% | 5.285 (5.270-5.300) / 7.295 (7.290-7.300) | 4.640 (4.630-4.650) / 6.690 (6.650-6.730) | -12.2% / -8.3% | +-0.26% |
| 32 | 304.06 (304.03-304.08) | 311.57 (311.56-311.57) | +2.47% | 7.390 (7.390-7.390) / 10.535 (10.520-10.550) | 6.505 (6.490-6.520) / 9.675 (9.600-9.750) | -12.0% / -8.2% | +-0.09% |

| Concurrency | Metric | Stock | Ours | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | interactivity p50 / p90 | 189.2 (188.6-189.8) / 137.08 (136.94-137.23) | 215.5 (215.2-215.8) / 149.46 (148.49-150.44) | +13.9% / +9.0% |
| 32 | interactivity p50 / p90 | 135.3 (135.3-135.4) / 94.93 (94.80-95.07) | 153.7 (153.4-154.1) / 103.36 (102.61-104.12) | +13.6% / +8.9% |

Throughput, TPOT and interactivity gains (p50 and p90) are above the floor at both concurrencies (both ours runs above both stock runs). Mean output length is 975 (c16) / 1027 (c32); tok/s per mean output length gives +1.48% / +2.04%. In a kernel trace of the c16 server (profiler on, 12 windows of 64 steps per arm, rank 0) the decode top-k takes 21.2 us per call stock and 5.2 us ours (60 calls per decode step, 1.27 -> 0.31 ms of an 18 ms step); the scorer is unchanged (17.0 us per call at matched context in both). import sys, json, math, statistics, torch
from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.index_topk_decode.host import minimax_m3_index_topk_decode_indices as topk
K, QL = 16, 4
width = lambda msl: (1 << (math.ceil(math.ceil(msl / 128) / 64) - 1).bit_length()) * 64
flush = torch.empty(1 << 30, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"); res = {}
for msl in [65536, 131072, 262144, 524288, 1 << 20]:
    for nr in [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 32, 64, 100]:
        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(nr * 1000003 + msl)
        seq = torch.randint(msl // 2, msl + 1, (nr,), generator=gen).int().cuda()
        scores = []
        for _ in range(K):
            s = torch.randn(1, nr * QL, width(msl), generator=gen)
            s = torch.where(torch.rand(s.shape, generator=gen) < 4.0 / s.shape[-1], s + 6, s)
            s[:, :, 0] = 1e30; scores.append(s.cuda())
        outs = [torch.empty(1, nr * QL, 16, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") for _ in range(K)]
        def fn():
            for i in range(K): topk(scores[i], outs[i], seq, max_seq_len=msl, query_len=QL)
        fn(); torch.accelerator.synchronize()
        g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
        with torch.cuda.graph(g): fn()
        ts = []
        for _ in range(20):
            flush.zero_(); a, b = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
            a.record(); g.replay(); b.record(); torch.accelerator.synchronize(); ts.append(a.elapsed_time(b) * 1000 / K)
        res[f"{nr}x{msl}"] = statistics.median(ts)
json.dump(res, open(sys.argv[1], "w"))

## Details

Each decode row is one workgroup that walks the row's block scores in windows, keeps a running top 16 and ranks the candidates. The old kernel did this with a single wave over windows of 1,664 blocks (213k tokens); rows longer than that serialize on the one wave. Now the workgroup has four waves, each walking every fourth window of 1,024 blocks with its own candidates and running top 16, and the lists are merged by an exact rank over (score, block id), which reproduces AITER's order including ties, NaN and infinities. A wave with no live window pads its list with dead entries, and a row of at most one window skips the merge. The lane-bound threshold uses 16 bits instead of 12 and falls back to all 32 bits when too many keys pass. Prefill compiles to the same code as before. The kernel name for decode changes from `..._w26` to `..._w16`.

Why real scores matter: the old kernel keeps the keys above a bound and ranks at most 64 of them per window; when more pass, it rebuilds the candidates, and with many near-ties it runs an exact bit search on one wave. Random scores never reach that. Real index scores sit in a narrow range, so the 12-bit bound lets more than 64 keys through in about a third of the rows (emulated on the captured rows: 33% of rows with the old bound and window size, 6% with the 16-bit bound), and a call takes as long as its slowest row. Calls in which no row overflows run at the random-score time. I did not build a 16-bit-bound-only or four-wave-only variant, so I cannot say how much of the 4x comes from each.

Limits:
- Slower in some calls: when every row is under about 213k tokens and no row overflows the old kernel's candidate buffer, a call is up to 12% slower (about 0.5 us on a 4 us call; random-score table, and the 0.88x-0.92x served calls there) and 8-9% slower at 100 requests under 131k tokens. In my real-score runs no cell (20 served calls, 32 grid cells, 6 cells of 131k-213k rows) is slower than stock (lowest 1.04x), but about 30% of single-request calls with 131k-213k rows have no overflowing row (emulation). The launch only sees the graph's `max_seq_len` (1M in serving), not the row lengths, so the host cannot choose between the two kernels.
- The real-score grid cells are re-scored captured requests, not replays of served calls; the max length 1M column is random-score only.
- E2E was run on the published ROCm image with the two files overlaid, not on a build of current main: the CI recipe (DBO with this multimodal model) does not start on main under Model Runner V2, and I did not change the recipe. The kernel files are identical to main's; other kernels' shares differ on main (for example the MXFP8 fusions), so the gain on main may differ.
- c16 and c32 only (c1-c8 do not use this indexer path; c64 not run); one model, TP4, DSpark, DBO on; 2 runs per arm.
- Validation is gfx950 only, and no Buildkite step runs the test file on gfx950 (I ran it on MI355X). The microbench is not in `benchmarks/kernels/`.
- A 2-way merge for rows up to 2,048 blocks would halve the 131k-213k regression (+8 lines); it is not in this PR.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the top-k files or their test file (checked against main at 76c6f3f2a9). #64198 (MXFP4 K/V and index cache) does not touch them. #64264 (NVFP4 kernel warmup at startup) and #64273 (monokernel decode on M3.1) are closed drafts that only carried the same bytes of these files as main. #64448 (decode CP for DSpark 7) is open and edits the indexer module and the CP push kernel, not the top-k kernel, so it is complementary.

**AI assistance:** AI assistance was used in this PR, for the kernel change, the added tests and benchmark scripts, the measurements and this description; the models are listed as `Co-authored-by` on the commit. The numbers in this description come from the runs described above.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Skip vocab blocks with no target token in the resample kernel
author: zyongye
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

In Model Runner V2 verification, `_resample_kernel` now returns early for a vocab block whose target logits are all `-inf` (masked by top-k/top-p or a logits processor): the residual there is `-inf` too, so the draft-logit load and the Gumbel draw are skipped. Sampled tokens are bitwise identical. Part of the rejection-sampling work tracked in #61024; first of a stack (see the end of this description).

## Claims

- Resample kernel on top-p-masked verify rows (K = 3, top-p 0.95, Qwen3-0.6B logits, V = 151,936, GB300): **165.9 → 55.4 µs** (creative-writing rows) and **149.5 → 42.2 µs** (math rows) at 256 requests; 13.7 → 6.8 µs at 16 requests.
- No cost on unmasked rows: the check runs only when some request in the chunk may have masked logits (top-p = 1 rows stay at 165.1 µs; forcing the check on them would cost 173.7 µs, +5%).
- Output is bitwise identical with the skip on or off.

## Validation

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py -q
# 127 passed (GB300). Unmodified main, first two files: 111 passed; this adds 4 parametrizations.
```

- `test_skip_masked_vocab_blocks_is_bitwise_identical`: two whole vocab blocks and most of a third masked, with and without draft logits, fp32 and fp64 Gumbel; skip on vs off must match bitwise.
- `test_logits_processing_cache_matches_request_features` gains the expected `may_mask_logits` per request feature; temperature-only is the case that needs processing but never masks.

Kernel times: `_resample_kernel` device time from the torch profiler (10 calls after 3 warm-up), the same inputs through upstream `main` and this branch, loaded side by side; outputs compared on the valid positions only.

| rows (requests × 4) | profile | top-p | main µs | skip on µs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | creative | 0.95 | 13.7 | 6.8 |
| 1,024 | creative | 0.95 | 165.9 | 55.4 |
| 1,024 | math | 0.95 | 149.5 | 42.2 |
| 1,024 | creative | 1.0 | 165.1 | 165.1 (gated off) |

Not measured: end-to-end serving throughput. In a verify-step harness with vLLM's own chain (fp32 copy, temperature, Triton top-p mask, rejection sampling) the same kernel change took a 256-request step from 2,086 to 1,976 µs.

## Details

- **Gate.** The block max costs about 5% of the kernel when nothing is masked, so `rejection_sample` takes `skip_masked_vocab_blocks` (default off) and `RejectionSampler._verify` turns it on when any request in the chunk may have masked logits. `Sampler` records that per request in `may_mask_logits`: min-p, top-k or top-p active, or thinking-budget forcing or a logits processor (counted conservatively, e.g. logit bias). Temperature alone only scales and never sets the flag. No host/device sync: the flag is a NumPy lookup.
- **Why it is exact.** The residual is a subset of the target's support, so an all-`-inf` target block yields an all-`-inf` residual. Such a block never wins the global argmax unless every block is `-inf`, and in that case it reports index 0, which is what the argmax of an all-`-inf` block returns.
- **Not duplicating.** Searched open PRs for "resample kernel skip", "rejection sampler resample", "top-p rejection sampling" and #61024: #41258 (lazy recovery) changes the V1 sampler, #48928 (FlashInfer AIR top-p) replaces the mask itself; neither touches the MRV2 resample kernel.
- **With the on-load path.** #65102 and #65103 carry this commit. There the kernels apply the top-p cutoff to raw logits as they load them, so the raw block is never all `-inf`; their next commit tests the block after the cutoff instead, which is the same tensor on this PR's path.
- **Stack.** 1/4, independent of the rest: (2) #65101 `topp_cutoffs_lse` op, (3) #65102 top-p applied as target logits load, (4) #65103 target log-sum-exp from that op. #65104 (draft log-sum-exp from the drafter) closed: a net loss once the drafter's cost is counted.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and its tests; the submitter is reviewing every line.

title: [CI] Bake hash-locked KV connectors into the CI image and re-enable their jobs
