<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Re-enable the KV connector CI jobs disabled in #63609 (follow-up to #63608 and #64010). Instead of installing NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake and CuPy at job time, the CUDA 13 CI image now bakes them from a hash-pinned lock.

## Claims

- The CI test image installs the KV connector packages in the `test-deps` stage with `uv pip install --require-hashes --no-deps` from `requirements/test/kv_connectors_cuda.txt`. That lock is compiled against `requirements/cuda.txt` and `requirements/test/cuda.txt` and regenerated by a new `pip-compile-kv-connectors` pre-commit hook; a `check-kv-connector-lock` hook fails if it stops satisfying `requirements/kv_connectors.txt`. At build time it adds 16 packages and changes none already in the image.
- `install-kv-connectors.sh` becomes `check-kv-connectors.sh`. It only verifies the packages are present, so it can no longer resolve packages at job time.
- **ROCm needs no image change.** `kv_connectors_rocm.txt` (`tblib`, `lm_eval[api]`) is fully covered by `requirements/test/rocm.txt`, so the runtime installs were no-ops. They and the file are removed.
- **26 job blocks re-enabled.** The CUDA and AMD jobs are listed in the build below.
- **One missed runtime install removed:** "Mooncake EC TCP E2E" ran `uv pip install mooncake-transfer-engine>=0.3.12` into a venv. It now uses the image's Mooncake through `--system-site-packages`.
- 6 tethering-allowlist entries removed.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` on all changed files passed: pip-compile-kv-connectors, shellcheck, step keys, test tethering (`--all` reports nothing stale) and Dockerfile graph.
- All Buildkite YAML parses. Each restored block matches its pre-#63609 definition except for the script rename and the dropped ROCm install line.
- Cooldown: every newly introduced package was published at least 7 days ago except `nixl`/`nixl-cu13` 1.5.2 (PyPI Oct 29). Main already pins it in `requirements/kv_connectors.txt` since #64585. **Please don't merge before Nov 5** if we hold to the 7-day rule.
- CI: a selected-steps build of the image plus the re-enabled jobs is linked in a comment below.

## Details

- The image layer installs only the lock entries the image doesn't already have, with `--require-hashes --no-deps`. It fails the build if the install changed any preinstalled package. After the vLLM and EP kernel wheels are installed, `tools/kv_connector_lock.py verify` fails the build if any locked package differs from its locked version or has unmet requirements. Its exceptions are named in the script: `cuda-pathfinder`, which the vLLM install upgrades; `nixl` → `nixl-cu12`; and `torch` → the image-pinned NCCL. `check-kv-connectors.sh` reruns the same `verify` at job start. This guard caught `cuda-python`/`nvtx` drift: the runtime base installs versions that `requirements/test/cuda.txt` doesn't pin. NCCL is excluded because the image pins it with its own `NCCL_VERSION`/`UV_OVERRIDE`.
- **Scope:** only the stable x86_64 CUDA 13 image. Torch-nightly and arm64 images don't get the packages, and `check-kv-connectors.sh` fails fast there with a clear message. The KV jobs only run on x86 L4/H100/H200/B200 pools.
- **Still disabled:**
  - A100 "NixlConnector PD + Spec Decode acceptance": the A100 queue was retired in #64602. Its MI355 mirror needs a standalone conversion.
  - The two Intel jobs that `pip install -r requirements/kv_connectors.txt` on the XPU image. They need an Intel image change.
- The release images (`INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true`) are unchanged.

title: [Feature][MooncakeStore] Add automatic deployment cache prefixes
author: hj-mistral
body:
## Overview

Add opt-in `cache_prefix="auto"` to MooncakeStoreConnector so image/model/configuration changes can select a new shared KV namespace without manually calculating a prefix.

## Claims

- Derive a SHA-256 prefix from image identity (falling back to build commit), existing model/cache configuration hashes, and the resolved HF commit.
- Preserve the empty default and literal custom prefixes; scheduler capacities do not affect the automatic prefix.
- Keep the implementation in the Store worker, reusing maintained configuration hashes. The net diff against main is 3 files, +156/−6.

## Validation

- 9 focused CPU tests passed on the merged branch: `python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_cache_prefix.py -q` in a uv-managed Python 3.12 environment.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed against upstream main, including Ruff, mypy, markdown lint and test tethering.
- Real GPU startup and Mooncake transfers have not been validated locally. This remains a draft starting point; no accuracy or performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

Updated to incorporate Nicolò Lucchesi's simplification from https://github.com/hj-mistral/vllm/pull/3. This removes the parallel config exclusion lists, environment scan, quantization object serializer and dedicated GPU CI step from the original version. Existing CPU CI collects the focused tests.

Automatic mode requires an immutable image identity or known build commit and an immutable model identity. Environment flags and live/overwritten weight files are outside this first pass; use a custom prefix when they change without a corresponding identity change. The image tag takes precedence over the commit.

This namespace is not a complete payload-compatibility validator: deployments sharing it must still use compatible Store layouts and parallel topologies. In particular, rank numbers alone do not distinguish TP/PP sizes in the default rank-local layout. The resolved payload fingerprint proposed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56971 is complementary work.

title: [Perf][Frontend] Validate plain embedding inputs before the full union
author: davidteather
body:
## Overview

`EmbeddingRequest` is a five-member pydantic union with no discriminator, so every `/v1/embeddings` body is validated against all five. The chat-input members (#45173) check each input item against every chat message type, so a 256×64 token-id batch spends ~66 ms in validation on the API server's event loop. This tries `EmbeddingCompletionRequest` first when `input` is not chat-shaped and the body has no chat-only field, and otherwise (or on any error) falls back to the original union.

## Claims

- Validation of plain inputs: 256×64 token ids ~66 ms → 0.28 ms, 256 strings 818 → 44 µs, 1 string 20 → 4.8 µs.
- Parsed requests, `errors()` and HTTP 400 bodies are unchanged; chat bodies take the original path (+~0.4 µs for the check).
- Reach: `/v1/embeddings` (and `run_batch`) with string or token-id input. The Rust frontend has no embeddings route.

## Validation

A/B, 15 alternated rounds, fresh process per run, validation through the route's FastAPI body field; macOS arm64, Python 3.12.7, pydantic 2.14.1:

| body | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 256×64 token ids | 65.6 ms | 0.28 ms |
| 32×512 token ids | 64.9 ms | 0.15 ms |
| 256 strings | 818 µs | 44 µs |
| 1 chat conversation | 32.3 µs | 32.7 µs |
| ScoreRequest (control) | 15.6 µs | 15.7 µs |

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
import time
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.embed.protocol import EmbeddingRequest

ta = TypeAdapter(EmbeddingRequest)
body = {"model": "m", "input": [list(range(64)) for _ in range(256)]}
ta.validate_python(body)
t = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(20):
    ta.validate_python(body)
print(f"{(time.perf_counter() - t) / 20 * 1e3:.2f} ms")  # main 68.3, PR 0.26
```
</details>

Identity vs main: 55 valid bodies (every input shape and option, chat/batched/chat-as-input variants, both `input` and `messages`) parse to the same class and `model_dump()` over HTTP and through `run_batch`; 35 invalid bodies give the same status and errors.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_io_processor.py
# 64 passed
```

The new tests compare against the plain union for 11 valid and 4 invalid bodies; the invalid set fails if the chat-only-field check is removed. Evals: N/A, model inputs are unchanged. End-to-end server latency was not measured; numbers are the validation step only.

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR touches this union (`EmbeddingRequest`, `embeddings discriminator`, `pooling protocol union`).

## Details

Only the completion member can accept a non-chat `input` without `messages`, so when it validates, the result matches the union. Bodies with a chat-only field (`_CHAT_ONLY_FIELDS`, derived from `EmbeddingChatRequest.model_fields`) skip the fast path, because chat-member validators can reject them with a non-`ValidationError` (e.g. `continue_final_message` + `add_generation_prompt`). A `WrapValidator` is used instead of a `Discriminator`, which would change error `loc`s and the OpenAPI schema (`anyOf` → `oneOf`). Only cosmetic difference: `ValidationError.title` names the wrapper, visible in the first line of `run_batch` error strings.

AI assistance (Claude Opus 5.5) was used to find this target, draft the patch, and build the benchmark and identity check. I reviewed every line, re-ran the tests, and benchmarks above myself, and can answer for the change and where the perf wins come from.

title: [Spec Decode] Support XPress + Acceptance Estimator
author: tomasruizt
body:
## Overview

Adaptive verification does nothing for XPress today. The acceptance estimator is created, but XPress never feeds it, so the AV budget reads an uninitialised confidence buffer and prunes every draft after the first. Turning AV on makes XPress about 3x slower than leaving it off.

This wires XPress to the estimator, using the logits the draft tokens are sampled from.

## Performance

One H100, Qwen3-8B with the XPress b16 draft, 15 draft tokens, greedy, prefix caching off, SPEED-Bench throughput_1K shuffled with seed 42. AIPerf runs a concurrency grid of 1, 8, 32, 64 and 128 with 30 s cells and 3 trials. Throughput is output tokens in the steady window of each cell, median over the trials.

![Throughput-interactivity pareto](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomasruizt/vllm/assets/xpress-av/xpress-av-pareto.png)

AV off is the same curve on both commits, within 1%, which is also the spread between trials. On main, AV on verifies one token per step and loses 26% to 71% of throughput. Here it costs 8% at c1 and c8, and from c32 up it is faster than AV off: the budget verifies fewer drafts (AL 3.0 to 3.3 against 3.5 to 3.7), which makes each target step cheaper and more than pays for the shorter accept run.

<details>
<summary>Per-cell results</summary>

| c | AV off tok/s | AV on, main | AV on, this PR | AL off | AL on, main | AL on, this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 408 | 118 | 375 | 3.78 | 1.00 | 3.50 |
| 8 | 2,494 | 812 | 2,291 | 3.54 | 1.01 | 3.17 |
| 32 | 4,468 | 2,227 | 5,389 | 3.67 | 1.01 | 3.04 |
| 64 | 4,471 | 2,856 | 6,242 | 3.58 | 1.01 | 3.19 |
| 128 | 4,967 | 3,665 | 6,810 | 3.68 | 1.00 | 3.32 |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server and client commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=2048 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --served-model-name qwen \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8640 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

```yaml
# aiperf profile --config sweep.yaml, one invocation per AV mode
sweep: {type: grid, parameters: {phases.profiling.concurrency: [1, 8, 32, 64, 128]}}
multi_run: {num_runs: 3, cooldown_seconds: 5}
benchmark:
  endpoint:
    url: http://127.0.0.1:8640
    type: chat
    streaming: true
    use_server_token_count: true
    extra: {temperature: 0, max_completion_tokens: 1024, chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}}
  datasets:
    - {name: main, type: file, format: speed_bench_throughput_1k, path: throughput_1k.jsonl, sampling: shuffle, random_seed: 42}
  phases:
    - {name: profiling, type: concurrency, duration: 30, grace_period: 30, concurrency: 1}
```

</details>

## Claims

- AV on no longer collapses: acceptance length 1.08 to 7.26 on the e2e case (7.39 with AV off), acceptance rate 0.005 to 0.42.
- Throughput goes from a 26-71% loss on main to an 8% cost at c1 and c8, and a 21-40% gain from c32 up, because the budget spends fewer verified drafts per step.
- Accuracy is unchanged: GSM8K 0.885 with AV on and off, 1,319 questions.
- AV off is untouched. The draft is bit-identical, and both commits measure within 1% in every cell.

## Validation

The existing Qwen3-8B + XPress b16 case gets an `enable_adaptive_verification` variant in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/xpress/test_xpress.py`. It runs in the nightly XPress job, so no buildkite change is needed.

| commit | result |
|---|---|
| main `f9db1756e9` | `1 failed in 647.96s`, `acceptance_rate=0.005`, `acceptance_len=1.078` |
| this PR | `2 passed in 113.91s`, AV off `0.43 / 7.39`, AV on `0.42 / 7.26`, GSM8K `0.885` both |

<details>
<summary>Failure on main</summary>

```
E  AssertionError: method=dflash target=Qwen/Qwen3-8B, draft=UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16, eager=False,
   acceptance_rate=0.005, acceptance_len=1.078; expected acceptance_rate >= 0.375
E  assert 0.005191845631765376 >= 0.375
```

</details>

Unit: `pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_xpress_head.py` gives 4 passed. It covers both `xpress_topc` paths and asserts the draft is unchanged when no logits are requested.

## Details

`draft_token_confidence_probs` is allocated with `torch.empty` and only written by `_maybe_predict_acceptance`. DFlash and DSpark call it, XPress did not, so the AV budget read uninitialised survivals and the estimator never saw a single feature or verdict.

`jacobi_refine_greedy` now returns the logits of its last pass next to the draft ids, and `XPressSpeculator` hands them to the estimator. Both paths return exactly the logits the argmax ran on, the summed bias over the vocabulary or the top-C candidate scores when `xpress_topc` is set. Nothing is computed when AV is off.

The draft is unchanged, so AV now only decides how many draft tokens to verify, which is what it was meant to do.

title: [Perf][DCP] Sparse indexer: read the rank-major DCP top-k gather in place
author: mickaelseznec
body:
## Overview

The DCP sparse-indexer top-k merge (`_merge_dcp_topk_global`) all-gathers each rank's packed `(score, global_id)` candidates along dim 1. Since NCCL gathers along dim 0, `GroupCoordinator.all_gather` then reorders the result into `[rows, world_size * topk, 2]`: a full extra copy of every candidate. This PR gathers along dim 0 and lets the CuTeDSL selector read the rank-major `[world_size, rows, topk, 2]` buffer in place. The selected set is unchanged.

With `W` ranks, `R` rows and `K = topk` candidates per rank:

```python
# Before
packed = pack(local_topk)                    # [R, K, 2]  (score, global_id)
buf = nccl_all_gather(packed)                # [W*R, K, 2]  rank-major
gathered = buf.view(W, R, K, 2)              #              (free view)
           .movedim(0, 1)                    # [R, W, K, 2]
           .reshape(R, W*K, 2)               # [R, W*K, 2]  <-- full copy
selector(gathered)                           # one CTA per row r:
    for key_idx in range(W*K // 512):
        col = tid + key_idx * 512
        key = gathered[r, col]

# After
packed = pack(local_topk)                    # [R, K, 2]
buf = nccl_all_gather(packed)                # [W*R, K, 2]  rank-major
gathered = buf.view(W, R, K, 2)              # free view, read in place
selector(gathered)                           # one CTA per row r:
    for key_idx in range(W*K // 512):        # same loop, same keys
        rank = (key_idx * 512) // K          # compile-time constant (K % 512 == 0)
        cand = tid + (key_idx * 512) % K     # compile-time constant + tid
        key = gathered[rank, r, cand]
```

## Claims

- Removes the reorder copy from every DCP top-k merge (prefill and decode) of DSA models with a sparse indexer under DCP (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x).
- Kernel level on B200 (6710 rows, DCP8, top-2048): the merge's gather-side work drops from 1438 µs (reorder copy + selector) to 839 µs (selector on the rank-major input; 838 µs on the row-major input, so reading in place costs nothing).
- End to end, in a downstream fork (internal DSA model, 8×B200, TP8 × DCP8, top-2048): prefill throughput +5–6% (TTFT −5 to −6%) over 5k–100k-token prompts.

## Validation

- `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py`: 114 passed on B200. The selector test now feeds the rank-major layout and compares it with an fp64 reference over all candidates. The faked-gather merge tests follow the dim-0 gather.
- Downstream end-to-end benchmark (same container for both runs, 64 generated tokens, 3 iterations):

  | prompt | batch | prefill tok/s before | after | ratio |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 5k | 1 | 12,746 | 13,411 | 1.05× |
  | 5k | 16 | 12,677 | 13,312 | 1.05× |
  | 20k | 1 | 14,356 | 15,218 | 1.06× |
  | 20k | 16 | 14,153 | 15,011 | 1.06× |
  | 50k | 4 | 13,554 | 14,334 | 1.06× |
  | 100k | 16 | 13,391 | 14,148 | 1.06× |

  Decode was unchanged there, but that fork serves decode-sized batches through a separate symmetric-memory exchange. Upstream's decode path goes through this merge too, and is not measured here.
- No public-model end-to-end run yet (e.g. DeepSeek-V3.2 or GLM-5.x with DCP).

## Details

- The selector's only caller is `_merge_dcp_topk_global`, which already requires `topk ∈ (512, 1024, 2048)`. So each rank contributes `topk` candidates, a multiple of the 512-thread block, and every 512-wide slice of a row's candidates falls inside one rank. Each thread key's `(rank, candidate)` is then a compile-time constant plus the thread index: no runtime division. The `CompileKey(topk, num_candidates)` and the selector's radix passes are unchanged.
- `stable_topk_from_gathered_candidates_cutedsl` now takes only the rank-major layout, asserting its shape.
- `get_warmup_keys` skips a pooled top-k (kpool indexers) that isn't a multiple of 512. The merge rejects such a top-k at runtime anyway, so warmup no longer compiles a kernel that can never run.
- Related open PRs touching the same code:
  - #59367 gathers into a rank-major buffer, then copies it to row-major for the selector. With this PR the selector could read that buffer directly and drop the copy.
  - #64129 changes the selector's key bits in the same kernel and merge function; whichever lands second will need a small rebase.

title: [ROCm][CI] Gate MoRI EPv2 modular-kernel cases on the production EPv2 checks
author: djramic
body:
## Overview

Since #61361, `:amd: (MI300) MoE Kernels Multi-GPU` fails on main ([amd-ci#15761](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15761)): all 3 `MoriEPv2PrepareAndFinalize` cases hit a MoRI assertion on MI300X. This test-only PR registers MoRI EPv2 in the modular-kernel harness only where production would select it.

## Claims

- The MI300 Multi-GPU step passes again. The MoRI EPv1 and DeepEP cases are unchanged.
- MoRI EPv2 cases are generated only on gfx950/gfx1250 with MoRI >= 1.2.4, the conditions `RocmPlatform.check_and_update_config` uses.

## Validation

MI300X, `rocm/vllm-dev:ci_base` with MoRI 1.2.3.post1 (as in CI), 2 GPUs:

```bash
cd tests
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -v -s kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k multigpu
```

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Collected | 33 | 30 |
| MoRI EPv2 / EPv1 cases | 3 / 8 | 0 / 8 |
| Result | 3 failed, 30 passed | 30 passed |

On main, the EPv2 cases fail locally with the CI error: `AssertionError: combine block_num 304 exceeds xdb_flag_slots 256`.

## Details

The harness sets `mori_ep_v2=True` for the `"mori"` backend. That skips the EPv1 fallback production uses unless MoRI >= 1.2.4 is installed and the GPU is gfx950/gfx1250. On MI300X, MoRI's untuned EPv2 path uses one combine block per CU (304), above its fixed limit of 256. [ROCm/mori#876](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/pull/876) fixes this, but no MoRI release includes it yet.

AI-assisted tooling was used to analyze the CI logs, write the change, and run the validation. The change and the results were manually reviewed.

title: [GLM 5.3 Perf] Align draft model kv cache dtype align with target, 50% GPU Memory saved for each draft model
author: yewentao256

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Avoid the MNNVL FlashInfer all-reduce with HiSparse
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #64327. Unblocks #63801.

FlashInfer's MNNVL fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm has a cluster-barrier race (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782). The vLLM default single-node backend has been MNNVL since #61989. With HiSparse running host-memory gathers on its copy stream, the race fires and the engine dies with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (Xid 13 `CTA Not Present`).

With HiSparse enabled and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=auto`, backend selection now:
- single node: uses `trtllm`;
- multi-node: disables FlashInfer all-reduce, since `trtllm` doesn't support multi-node groups.

An explicit `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` setting is still respected. This is temporary: the check should be removed once vLLM picks up a FlashInfer release with #7782.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer_auto_backend or workspace_failure or standalone_workspace"
```

## Test Result

Server check that the new path runs: 4× H100 (driver 580.126.09), `main` + #63801 (Python side; kernels from the `main` precompiled wheel) + this PR, GLM-5.3 config with dummy weights cut to 5 layers, HiSparse with spec decode. Same build, same load; the only difference is the backend env var.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND={mnnvl,auto} \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 -tp 4 --enforce-eager --load-format dummy \
  --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 5, "first_k_dense_replace": 5, "indexer_types": ["full", "full", "full", "shared", "shared"]}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G \
  --max-model-len 67584 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":16}}'

# 6 waves, seeds 1..6
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 52000 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --seed $seed
```

| `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` | Fused AR workspace | Result | Output tok/s (mean of 6 waves) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mnnvl` (stock behavior) | `backend=mnnvl` | 6/6 waves, 0 failed requests | 499 |
| `auto` (this PR) | `backend=trtllm`, logs `Using flashinfer allreduce backend trtllm: ...` | 6/6 waves, 0 failed requests | 552 |

HiSparse was reading heavily from host memory (8.9 TB host-to-device, ~50% hot-buffer miss rate), but this reduced server didn't hit the race on H100 even with `mnnvl`. The crash evidence is the B200 result below and the standalone repro in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782, which faults within seconds on this same box.


10 passed. The two new HiSparse cases fail without the change.

Server-level evidence that `trtllm` avoids the crash (from #64327 / flashinfer#7782, set by hand via `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm`): GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP8 on 8× B200 with HiSparse went from a crash on wave 1 in 7/7 runs (MNNVL) to clean for 4/4 waves (TRTLLM), at about 3% lower decode throughput.

title: [HiSparse] Support the extensible KV cache
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Lets HiSparse run on the extensible KV cache (#56492), which previously excluded it. HiSparse's device pool is reserved and grown like any other KV cache. Its host pool stays outside it.

## Claims

- HiSparse uses the extensible KV cache by default.
- At default flags, GPU+host KV capacity grows by 16% and throughput matches `main`. GSM8K under heavy host offload also matches `main`.
- HiSparse with NIXL P/D and with the Mooncake store connector works on the extensible cache.
- Fixes two warmup crashes that removing the gate exposed:
  - the FlashInfer HiSparse autotune read hot blocks that had not been committed;
  - context-prefill warmup overflowed the hot group's fixed-size block-table rows.

## Validation

All runs on B200 with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, against base 3b6eeb0606.

**Default flags.** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, no `--gpu-memory-utilization`. Two runs each, server restarted for every point.
```
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-model-len 17408 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}'
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 2c --max-concurrency c --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

| | GPU+host KV tokens | c=16 tok/s | c=16 TPOT | c=64 tok/s | c=64 TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 1,313,935 | 661 / 666 | 20.3 / 20.1 ms | 949 / 944 | 54.3 / 54.7 ms |
| PR | 1,529,536 | 668 / 664 | 20.1 / 20.2 ms | 956 / 962 | 53.9 / 53.5 ms |

- The PR's log shows `Extended KV cache to 367616 blocks (63.11 GiB)`.
- At c=64, HiSparse stats show heavy host traffic in both variants.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 32. The same server at `--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.625` and `host_pool_gib` 32.
- PR: `Extended KV cache to 6208 blocks`, scores 0.904 and 0.912.
- `main` with `--num-gpu-blocks-override 6208`: 0.923 and 0.914.
- Both ran with 12.8k tokens of KV capacity against about 48k demanded, with about 14M hot-buffer misses and 61–65 GB H2D per stats interval.

**P/D.** Tiny DeepSeek-V3.2 with dummy weights, one prefiller and one decoder. The decoder is sized only by `--gpu-memory-utilization`.
- **NIXL:** the decoder runs `MultiConnector[HiSparseConnector, NixlConnector]`. Greedy outputs match HiSparse without P/D (5/5 prompts, 48/48 tokens) with a 1.26M-block pool and with a 768-block pool, where imports land in host memory. Without the post-extend cache-dict fix, the handshake fails: `RuntimeError: Engine ... holds KV layer 'model.layers.0.self_attn.attn', which has no counterpart here.`
- **Mooncake store:** `MultiConnector[HiSparseConnector, MooncakeStoreConnector]` starts and serves requests. Without the fix, startup fails: `ValueError: Missing transferable KV caches for layers: [...]`.

**Warmup crashes on `main`.** Run the GSM8K command on `main` with only the gate removed:
- `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in `FlashInferMLASparseImpl.autotune_hisparse_decode`;
- with autotune disabled, `Block table write ... exceeds row capacity (128 > 64)`.

**Tests**, all passing:

| File | Passed |
|---|---|
| `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` | 6/6 |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py` | 20/20 |
| `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py` | 66/66 |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py` | 36/36 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py` | 248/248 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` | 98/98 |

One more NIXL HMA case needs a gated checkpoint that could not be downloaded.

New tests:
- **`test_hisparse_extensible_kv_cache`:** greedy outputs and the post-extend `kv_caches_by_layer` (layers, dtypes, devices, shapes, storage sizes) must equal a fixed-size cache of the same block count. It fails with either warmup fix reverted, and before the resident/hot rebind (resident entries spanned the whole reservation). CI runs it on H200, which does not use the FlashInfer autotune, so only SM100 guards the autotune fix.
- **`test_shrink_kv_cache_configs_leaves_host_resident_tensors`:** fails on `main`, where the measured shrink rescales the host pool's tensor.

The NIXL/Mooncake registration itself has no permanent test: there is no HiSparse P/D CI job.

## Details

- **Host-resident tensors stay out of the extensible paths.** `ExtensibleKVCache`, `committed_views`/`committed_kv_cache_tensors` and `shrink_kv_cache_configs` skip `host_resident` tensors. `host_resident` is an existing generic field.
- **The post-extend cache dict matches the fixed path's.** The runner keeps the dict `init_kv_cache` returned (`kv_caches_by_layer`); `extend_kv_cache` swaps in the committed views and passes it to `runner.kv_caches` and the connectors. Host layers keep their views and HiSparse's hot slabs stay out. `committed_views` gives layers laid out over the raw buffer (`has_layer_views=False`) the committed prefix, and `rebind_hisparse_device_caches` rebinds HiSparse's resident and hot views over it, so they span the committed blocks rather than the reservation. CUDA graphs captured before extend stay valid: the base address does not move.
- **Autotune:** the HiSparse autotune commits `cdiv(topk, hot_block_size)` blocks before tuning.
- **Warmup:** clamps reservations to the spec's block-table row length (`max_num_blocks_per_req`), which bounds HiSparse's fixed-size hot rows. Mamba is exempt: in non-align modes `MambaManager` can hold more blocks than its row length.
- **Considered:** feature-owned `if hisparse:` branches in the model runner and `extend_kv_cache`. That is more code, and it still needs the same planning changes.
- **Not covered:** sleep/wake with HiSparse on the extensible cache.

title: [Bugfix] Pad extensible KV cache segments instead of rounding the block count
author: njhill
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65204. Supersedes #65210 (carries over its connector gating, with Vegetog as co-author).

With the extensible KV cache (#56492), any KV connector made the engine round the KV block count down to a multiple of `granule / gcd(granule, block_stride)`. For awkward strides that multiple is huge, so engines with `--kv-offloading-size` could fail to start. This PR pads segment placement instead, and applies it (and the defragmenting commit) only for connectors that register the KV cache for RDMA.

## Claims

- `--kv-offloading-size` (and any connector that doesn't register the device KV cache) keeps its measured block count: no rounding, no padding, no defragmenting commit.
- NIXL / Mooncake / MoRIIO / UMBP keep one physical chunk per committed segment for RDMA registration at **any** block count, instead of losing up to one alignment unit (2048 blocks, ~11.6 GB, for the stride in #65204) or failing to start below it.
- `UMBPStoreConnector` is added to `registers_kv_cache_memory()`: it registers GPU KV storage through MORI. This also turns the extensible cache off for it on ROCm, as for MoRIIO.

## Validation

GB200, all on this branch unless noted.

**Reproducer**: `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct` (20 KiB page = 2¹²·5, so main needs a multiple of 512 blocks), `kv_offloading_size=1`, `block_size=16`, `max_model_len=1024`, `enforce_eager=True`. Baseline = `origin/main` versions of the changed files over the same build.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 0.014 | fails at startup: "No available memory for the cache blocks … decrease `max_model_len`" (102 blocks rounded to 0) | starts, 102 blocks, correct greedy output |
| 0.018 | 1024 blocks | 1331 blocks, same output |

**NIXL P/D**: `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh` with `PREFILL_BLOCK_SIZE=16 DECODE_BLOCK_SIZE=16` (Qwen3-0.6B, 1P1D): passes for the default layer-outermost layout (padded) and with `--enable-cross-layers` (block-outermost, single segment), 0 failed transfers. A separate DEBUG run with `NixlConnector` confirmed the padded path ran: capacity 19254 blocks (main would have rounded to 19232), NIXL registered the padded segments, and the final 18624 blocks committed exactly the nominal 31.83 GiB.

**Unit tests**: `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py`, `tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py`, `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py` all pass. New/changed coverage:
- `test_pad_kv_cache_segments` (CPU): uniform and mixed block strides, block-outermost no-op.
- `test_defragmenting_commit_backs_each_segment_with_one_allocation[padded]`: unpadded segments still share chunks after a defragmenting commit; padded ones get one chunk each at an unaligned count.
- `test_padded_config_allocates_and_defragments` (LBNHC, BLNHC, mixed strides): views, committed views and connector placements agree on a padded reservation.
- `test_extensible_extend_asks_connector_for_its_memory_pool`: a registering connector gets `defragment=True`.

## Details

**Root cause.** A connector that registers each committed segment for RDMA needs that segment backed by one physical chunk. Segments were placed at multiples of `capacity × block_stride`, so they only started on commit granules when the block count was a granule multiple; the engine forced that by rounding the reserved capacity and the post-warmup count for *every* connector. CPU offloading only copies blocks and needs none of it.

**Fix.**
- When `registers_kv_cache_memory()`, each worker pads its own copy of the KV cache config in `initialize_from_config` (`pad_kv_cache_segments`): each layer region of a block-compact layer-outermost layout starts on that device's commit granule. This costs address space only; commits already map whole granules per segment (`physical_bytes_for`), so a defragmenting commit of any count backs each segment with exactly one chunk. Block-outermost layouts have one segment at offset 0 and are untouched. KV connectors with the extensible cache are already restricted to block-compact layouts.
- Padding is worker-local so the engine/scheduler configs keep unpadded placements: `shrink_kv_cache_configs` scales `size` by block count and scheduler-side connectors read `size // num_blocks`.
- `ExtensibleKVCache` takes the layout to derive one segment per layer region (gaps allowed) rather than inferring segments from a single stride, which can't tell padding from LHBNC head groups for small caches.
- Removed: engine-side `align_extensible_kv_cache_capacity` / `granule_aligned_kv_cache_blocks`, the `kv_cache_commit_granule` RPC, `granule_aligned_blocks` / `granule_block_alignment`, `blocks_within(aligned=)`.
- The defragmenting commit is gated on `registers_kv_cache_memory()` (#65210).

**Tradeoff/limitation.** `registers_kv_cache_memory()` is a name-based allowlist, so out-of-tree connectors loaded via `kv_connector_module_path` that register device memory no longer get one-chunk segments by default (previously any connector did). Unpadded configs (no registering connector) behave as before.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid catastrophic cancellation in the acceptance estimator
author: fuscof-ibm
body:
## Overview Follow-up to #52228, which added the estimator to do adaptive verification without a confidence head. The adaptive-verification acceptance feature loses its entire signal to catastrophic cancellation whenever the drafter is confident. Every draft row more confident than `1 - 6e-8` reports the same acceptance feature, `40.0`, whatever its true confidence is. The feature is specified as a log-odds, `logit(q(m*))`, but it recovers the complement mass by subtracting 1 from a sum that includes the max's own unit term, which in fp32 destroys the quantity being measured — no NaN, no warning, just the clamp. **Headline:** at temperature 0.5 on source code, **11.5% of draft positions** had their confidence score destroyed and replaced with a constant. The failing positions are not exotic or adversarial — the single worst case in the sample is completing `tl.int64` from `tl.int6` (see the `Details` section for the error analysis). This PR computes the complement directly instead fixing completely the numerical issue. ## Claims - The feature is accurate to fp32 relative precision across the full range it is clamped to. Previously it saturated to the `_MAX_LOG_ODDS` clamp for any row more confident than `1 - 6e-8`, collapsing a ~23-nat span of distinct confidences onto a single value. - No change to the feature's definition, the fit, the trimming policy, or any buffer layout the rest of adaptive verification reads. - One extra fp32 partial per (token, vocab block): 0.1% of the kernel's memory traffic (311 KiB against 311 MiB of logit reads at 1024 tokens and a 152k vocab). No extra kernel launch. ## Validation `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py` — **18 passed in 7.08s** on an NVIDIA H100 GPU, covering the pre-existing tests plus three new ones: - `test_feature_resolves_a_tiny_complement_mass` — δ ∈ {1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-12} against an fp64 reference computed without ever forming `1 + δ`. Fails at 1e-6 and 1e-12 on `main`. - `test_feature_combines_blocks_around_the_global_max` — parametrized over which of three vocabulary blocks holds the top token. Every pre-existing test used a 2048-token vocabulary, narrower than the kernel's 4096-wide block, so `num_blocks` was always 1 and the cross-block combine was dead code in the suite. - `test_feature_drops_exactly_one_tied_maximum` — k tied maxima must leave k-1 in the complement, giving `-log(k-1)`. Parametrized over ties within one block and across blocks, which catch different mistakes and are each blind to the other's. ## Details The estimator introduced in #52228 basically trains a logistic regression using as a feature the probability of the most likely draft token, $qmax$ , to construct a feature: ```math f={logit}(qmax) =\log\!\left(\frac{qmax}{1-qmax}\right) ``` Let the temperature-scaled logits be $x_1 \ldots x_V$, and let $m=max_i x_i$, then #### ```math qmax=q_{i^*}=\frac{e^m}{\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^V e^{x_j}}=\frac{1}{1+\sum_{j\ne i^*}e^{x_j-m}} ``` Let's define ```math S=\sum_{j\ne i^*}e^{x_j-m} ``` Then : ```math \begin{aligned} q_{\max} &= \frac{1}{1+S} \\[6pt] 1-q_{\max} &= 1-\frac{1}{1+S} = \frac{1+S}{1+S}-\frac{1}{1+S}= \frac{S}{1+S} \end{aligned} ``` We can rewrite as: ```math f=\log\left(\frac{qmax}{1-qmax}\right)=\log\left(\frac{1}{S}\right)=-\log S. ``` The computation of $S$ is what makes the current code in `main` exposed to catastrophic cancellation. The previous approach (in `main`) computes $S$ (see the logic in the `_predict_kernel`) by summing the totals (`total_sumexp` in the code, $A$ in what follows) and then subtracting `1`: ```math A = \sum_{j=1}^V e^{x_j-m} = 1 +S ``` ```math S = A - 1 = \left(\sum_{j=1}^V e^{x_j-m}\right)-1 ``` The problem is that when there is a confident prediction (i.e. $qmax$ is high) $S$ must be small as $qmax=\frac{1}{1+S}$. The result is that for a small $S$ (e.g. $S= 10^{-12}$) $A = 1.0 + S = 1.0 $. Therefore, $1.0 - 1.0 = 0.0$, and the final feature becomes $+\inf$, leading to a clamped value of $40.0$. The real value for the feature when $S= 10^{-12}$ would be instead $f = -\log(10^{-12}) \approx 27.63 \ldots$. This PR introduced a block based algorithm to compute $S$ as a sum of positive quantities: ```math S = \sum_{j\ne i^*}e^{x_j-M} ``` We introduce the function `_max_and_sumexps` which returns three quantities for each vocabulary block: its maximum logit, its full exponential sum, and its sum excluding *one* maximum position. For one block $b$, let $m_b$ denote its maximum, and $j_b$ a single index where that maximum occurs, the routines compute: ```math $$ \begin{aligned} m_b &= \max_{j\in b} x_j,\\ A_b &= \sum_{j\in b} e^{x_j-m_b},\\ E_b &= \sum_{\substack{j\in b\\j\ne j_b}} e^{x_j-m_b}. \end{aligned} $$ ``` The vocabulary is split into blocks (the new tests identify a width of \(4096\) elements). Each block has a different $m_b$, so its local $A_b$ and $E_b$ are expressed in a different exponential scale. They cannot be added without rescaling. Let's the global maximum and one selected winning block as: ```math $$ M = \max_b m_b,\qquad b^* \in {argmax}_b m_b. $$ ``` For any token in block $b$, the identity $e^{x_j-M} = e^{x_j-m_b}\,e^{m_b-M}$ shows how to convert the block's local exponential sum to the global scale. Its factor is $e^{m_b-M}$. This allows to perform the sum in blocks. What want to achieve is that the block that contains the actual max provides the sum omitting exactly one index, while the other blocks provide the full sum. This formula is simply a partition of $\sum_{j\ne i^*}e^{x_j-M}$ into blocks. ```math S=\sum_b e^{m_b-M} \begin{cases} E_b,&b=b^*,\\ A_b,&b\ne b^*. \end{cases} ``` - If $ b = b^* $, one globally maximal token must be left out, so use $E_{b^*}$. - If $b \neq b^*$, every token in block $b$ belongs in the complement and the contribution is $e^{m_b-M}A_b$. #### Error analysis setup To simplify the analysis/data collection we use CPU code in python. The Triton path on the GPU (before the fix) has the same cancellation problem. **Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`**, loaded from the local Hugging Face cache in fp32 on CPU via `transformers`: ```python tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B") model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", dtype=torch.float32).eval() ids = tok(text, return_tensors="pt").input_ids[:, :512] logits = model(ids).logits[0][:-1] # drop the last row: no next token follows it ``` Chosen for three reasons: 1. **Plausible drafter size.** 0.6B is in the range actually used for draft models 2. **Production-scale vocabulary — 151,936 tokens.** The complement sums over the *whole* tail, so a large vocabulary adds roughly `log(V)` to δ and makes saturation **harder**. Measuring on a large vocabulary is therefore the `conservative choice`; a smaller-vocabulary drafter would saturate more often, not less. 3. **It spans three vocabulary blocks.** The kernel reduces in 4096-wide blocks, so 151,936 tokens exercise the cross-block combine rather than the single-block degenerate case. We compute the `new` and `old` values as follows: ```python # old: everything, then subtract the top token's own unit term total = (sumexps * rescale).sum(dim=1) old = (total - 1.0).clamp(min=0.0) # new: the max's own block contributes its excluding sum, so nothing cancels use = sumexps.scatter(1, best_block[:, None], excl.gather(1, best_block[:, None])) new = (use * rescale).sum(dim=1) ``` **Inputs.** Two files from the vllm repo representing two different language distributions (code and prose): - code: [acceptance_estimator.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/acceptance_estimator.py) - prose:[README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/README.md) **thresholds**: Two thresholds are used: | name | condition | meaning | |---|---|---| | **degraded** | δ < 1e-5 | the subtraction is shedding digits; ≥1% error in the feature | | **saturated** | δ < 2^-24 ≈ 5.96e-8 | the value is gone; the feature pins to 40.0 | **Scripts, all CPU-only** to inspect the failure modes: | script | purpose | |---|---| | `measure_feature_distribution.py` | degraded/saturated rates by temperature | | `find_saturating_tokens.py` | decodes the failing positions | | `plot_feature_histogram.py` | the old-vs-new distribution figure | | `emulate_feature_error.py` | synthetic δ sweep, no model needed | Environment: `torch 2.11.0`, `transformers 5.13.0`, CPU, fp32. #### Acceptance feature distribution(s) The following plot highlights the acceptance feature distributions, original vs fixed. **logit(q_max)** is computed twice from identical logits in fp32 with the kernel's 4096-wide vocabulary blocking (Qwen3-0.6B, temp 0.5, 1022 code and prose positions), histogrammed on a log y-axis. _The original Σe^(z−m*) − 1 path cannot represent anything between 15.94 — one fp32 ulp of 1.0 — and the ±40 clamp, so 14% of positions with true features spanning 16–35 collapse to a single spike at 40, while the excluding-sum fix tracks the fp64 reference continuously to 34.86._ Analysis code: [plot_feature_histogram.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34314874/plot_feature_histogram.py) Command `python3 plot_feature_histogram.py ` #### Temperature dependence Analysis code: [measure_feature_distribution.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34315254/measure_feature_distribution.py) Command: `python3 PR_numerical_stability/measure_feature_distribution.py --temperatures 1.0 0.9 0.8 0.7 0.6 0.5 0.4 0.3 0.2 0.1 ` Temperature is applied *before* the feature is computed, in `_local_max_sumexp_kernel` (the `temp = tl.where(temp > 0.0, temp, 1.0)` guard and the division just below it), dividing the logit gap and multiplying the feature by `1/temp`. So lowering temperature pushes rows over the fp32 wall mechanically. Measured rates: | temp | code degraded | code **saturated** | prose degraded | prose **saturated** | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1.0 | 2.0% | **0.2%** | 2.9% | **0.0%** | | 0.9 | 3.7% | **0.6%** | 6.1% | **0.2%** | | 0.8 | 7.8% | **1.2%** | 11.0% | **1.8%** | | 0.7 | 11.5% | **2.3%** | 15.7% | **3.7%** | | 0.6 | 15.5% | **6.3%** | 22.3% | **8.2%** | | 0.5 | 22.1% | **11.5%** | 28.0% | **15.3%** | | 0.4 | 28.0% | **17.0%** | 35.6% | **24.5%** | | 0.3 | 35.2% | **25.8%** | 42.1% | **33.1%** | | 0.2 | 46.6% | **36.0%** | 49.3% | **43.1%** | | 0.1 | 67.7% | **56.2%** | 65.8% | **57.7%** | Reading this: - **At temp 1.0 the bug is nearly invisible** — 0.2% of code rows, 0% of prose. A benchmark run at temperature 1.0 will show nothing, on any metric. This is worth stating plainly because it means "we A/B tested and saw no difference" is the *expected* result at that setting, not evidence the bug is benign. - **The knee is between 0.8 and 0.5.** Saturation roughly doubles per 0.1 step of temperature through that range: 1.2% → 2.3% → 6.3% → 11.5%. - **Greedy decoding (temp = 0) is a separate case.** `temp == 0` is mapped to `1.0` rather than dividing by zero, so greedy rows land in the temp-1.0 row of this table. They also mix an unscaled feature into the same shared slope as temperature-scaled rows, which is its own modelling issue and out of scope here. - **Prose saturates slightly *more* than code below 0.6.** That surprised me; I had expected code to dominate throughout. Natural language has plenty of near-deterministic continuations too (fixed phrases, inflections, markup), and at low temperature those cross the wall just as easily. **The failure is not code-specific — code is simply where low temperatures are _*conventional*_.** The practical reading: **temp ≤ 0.7 is where this starts to matter, and temp ≤ 0.5 is where it is common. ** Both are ordinary settings for code completion and structured-output serving. #### Real examples All from this repository's own source, Qwen3-0.6B. `true` is the fp64 value;`old` is what the original fp32 path produced; `gap` is the *raw* pre-temperature top-2 logit gap. Analysis code: [find_saturating_tokens.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34315054/find_saturating_tokens.py) ##### At temp 0.5 — `acceptance_estimator.py`, 59/511 positions saturate (11.5%) Command: `python3 find_saturating_tokens.py`: ``` true 34.86 | old 40.0 | δ 7.3e-16 | gap 17.51 ...' other=0).to(\n tl.int6' -> '4' (runner-up '3') true 32.22 | old 40.0 | δ 1.0e-14 | gap 16.54 ...'.0,\n ).to(tl.float3' -> '2' (runner-up 'b') true 30.19 | old 40.0 | δ 7.8e-14 | gap 15.10 ...' num_accepted = tl.maximum(num_sample' -> 'd' (runner-up 'ded') true 28.63 | old 40.0 | δ 3.7e-13 | gap 14.60 ...'.program_id(0).to(tl.int6' -> '4' (runner-up '5') ``` `tl.int6` → `4`. The model has to complete `tl.int64`, and `tl.int63` is not a type. It is right to be certain. The feature that exists to express certainty reports the same number it would for a coin flip between two tokens 17 nats apart — because both exceed what fp32 can represent. ##### At temp 0.7 — same file, 12/511 saturate (2.3%) Command: `python3 find_saturating_tokens.py --temperature 0.7` The rate drops but the character does not; the same tokens are simply closer to the wall: ``` true 24.69 | old 40.0 | ...'tl.int6' -> '4' true 22.55 | old 40.0 | ...').to(tl.float3' -> '2' true 18.56 | old 40.0 | ...'pred_ptr + req_state' -> '_block' (runner-up '_blocks') ``` That last one is interesting: the runner-up `'_blocks'` is a *plausible* alternative, and the true feature of 18.56 says "confident, not certain." The old path reports 40.0 — maximal certainty — for a row where the model itself left room for doubt. ---

title: [Quantization] Remove QuTLASS and fp_quant, run QuIP NVFP4 on Humming
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Removes QuTLASS and the deprecated `fp_quant` method, and runs compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints with a Hadamard input transform (QuIP) on Humming. Supersedes #61671, and makes #51112 moot.

## Claims

- QuIP NVFP4 checkpoints load and generate again. At `main` they crash at startup on SM100+.
- The checkpoint's declared FP4 activation is honored, with no fallback to A16 on this path.
- Input transforms always receive unquantized activations, which also fixes the generic transform path.
- The `_qutlass_C` build dependency, the `fp_quant` method, and about 1,800 lines of code are gone.

**Breaking:** `fp_quant` checkpoints no longer load. They already failed to load on `main`, and the method has been deprecated since #31688.

## Validation

B300 (SM103), humming-kernels 0.1.18. FP-Quant numbers below are from a scratch prototype, since that path is removed here; the QuIP row was re-run on this branch.

**Tests**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/quantization/test_nvfp4.py -k 'quip or hadamard_fp4_routing'` | 8 passed |
| `pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k transforms_perplexity` | 3 passed |
| QuIP generation with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | clean |
| `pre-commit` on changed files | passed |

Reproducer on `main`: `LLM(model="nm-testing/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-quipv16-nvfp4")` fails during startup with `'QuantizedActivation' object has no attribute 'shape'`.

**GSM8K** (600 questions, 5-shot, greedy, %)

| Checkpoint | QuTLASS* | Humming A4 | Humming A16 + Hadamard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.2-1B QuIP NVFP4 (float: 32.3) | 18.8 | 17.3–20.5 (this branch) | 22.8 |
| Qwen3-1.7B FP-Quant RTN NVFP4 (float: 66.8) | 23.5 | 21.3 | 45.2 |
| Qwen3-1.7B FP-Quant QAT NVFP4 | 55.0 | 52.0 | 62.0 |
| Qwen3-1.7B FP-Quant RTN MXFP4 | 16.3 | 15.3 | 26.7 |

\* `main` cannot run these, so the baseline needed small harness patches for the two root causes below. FP-Quant rows ran in eager mode.

A4 vs QuTLASS is a statistical tie (paired p = 0.13–0.93), though lower in every prototype row. Run-to-run noise is large: two passes in one process scored 17.3 and 20.5, with 196/600 identical outputs.

**GEMM GPU time** (µs, graph replay, real `down_proj` weights, N=2048, K=6144, warm L2, not hand-tuned)

| M | QuTLASS + cutlass | QuTLASS + FlashInfer | Humming A4 | Humming A16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 17.9 | 7.7 | 9.7 | 9.8 |
| 1024 | 36.8 | 24.1 | 15.9 | 41.4 |
| 8192 | 164.9 | 146.4 | 75.8 | 240.6 |

NVFP4 shown. Graph replay was used because CUPTI failed in this environment (`cupti-python` 13.3.1).

## Details

**Root causes on `main`**
- `fp_quant`: checkpoints contain `backward_hadamard_matrix`, which `FPQuantLinearMethod` never registers, so loading fails.
- QuIP: since #44260 NVFP4 layers expose `input_quant_key`, so producers pass a `QuantizedActivation`, which the transform methods cannot handle. Per #61671, SM12x also fails because QuTLASS wheels contain only `sm_100` code.
- Neither was caught because the job holding the QuIP perplexity test is commented out. The new tests are in `test_nvfp4.py`, whose Blackwell job does run.

**Routing:** Humming is used for W4A4, SM100+, a `hadamard` input transform with `head_dim` in 16–128, no output transform, and backend `auto` or `humming`. Everything else uses the generic transform path. Humming's block size 16–256 output matched the dense Sylvester matrix to bf16 rounding.

**What is lost**
- QuEST for MXFP4. None of the 36 public `fp_quant` models use it.
- Bit-exact output against QuTLASS, since scale rounding differs.
- Fused handling of non-Sylvester dense transforms. They use the generic path, which is slower and was not tested here.
- About 2 µs at M=1–16 versus the CT FlashInfer path.

**Not validated:** SM120, and TP>1 (`HadamardTransform` still raises `NotImplementedError`). `Humming float4e2m1 activation is slow on SM103` still logs, though A4 was the fastest option at M ≥ 1024. Plain NVFP4 on `--linear-backend humming` still falls back to A16 on SM10x and is unchanged here.

Not a duplicate: open PRs #61671 and #51112 fix QuTLASS rather than remove it.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Keep lazy SimpleCPUOffload stores at the GPU eviction end
author: Juntian777
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Lazy SimpleCPUOffload should offload the blocks the allocator will evict next, but two behaviors move it away from them. This PR fixes both: stored blocks go back to the front of the GPU free queue, and every walk starts from the head of the queue instead of a saved cursor.

Includes the two commits of #59383 by @obendidi, rebased onto main with authorship kept, plus the walk change. Builds on #64229.

## Claims

- Lazy stores return GPU blocks to the eviction end (from #59383).
- The lazy walk starts at the head of the free queue on every step, so it no longer offloads blocks far from eviction.
- With sliding-window groups that are not prefix-cacheable (DeepSeek-V4.1) and a contended CPU tier, the walk change is what lowers recomputed blocks; #59383 alone does not help there. The simulation below went from 67.5% to 59.7% recomputed blocks with 32 such blocks per cached block.
- No change to eager mode. Net -3 lines outside tests (+17/-20).

## Validation

Tests, on CPU:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py
```

Result: 152 passed. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

`test_lazy_walk_does_not_offload_past_eviction_window` fails before the walk change: the second walk offloads the blocks past `target_free`. `test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end` comes from #59383.

Simulation: the real `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` and `BlockPool` replaying one multi-turn session trace per row, with only the requests and store completions simulated. Each cell is the share of prompt blocks recomputed, averaged over 2 seeds (lower is better). The CPU tier is 2x the GPU pool and the working set is about 2.7x the CPU tier. SWA blocks are taken from the same free queue and freed on the next step. The 32 row uses twice the pool and half the per-step budget of the others, so that the SWA blocks fit, and runs long enough to reach steady state.

| Uncached SWA blocks per cached block | main | #59383 only | walk from head only | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 74.8% | 55.8% | 74.5% | 55.7% |
| 8 | 64.7% | 66.5% | 60.0% | 57.6% |
| 32 | 67.5% | 70.5% | 62.6% | 59.7% |

Per request, #59383 alone also writes 1.8x (8 SWA) to 2.1x (32 SWA) as many blocks to the CPU tier as this PR. When the CPU tier holds the whole working set (8 SWA), all four variants recompute 4.0%.

Not validated:

- No E2E serving run was done for this PR, so these are block-level hit rates and not a throughput measurement. The pool sizes and session shape are assumptions.
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_integration.py` has no passing result: its 2 non-optional tests need a GPU. They failed at engine startup on a GPU without enough free memory, and also fail without a GPU, as `test_chunked_local_partial_gpu_hit` does on main. They need a run in CI or on a free GPU.

## Details

Root cause: the cursor is only reset when its block leaves the free queue. Uncached SWA blocks are freed to the front of the queue and reused there, so the block under the cursor is often neither stored nor reallocated, and the walk resumes past it. In the simulation with SWA groups, about 99% of walks with only #59383 applied resumed from the cursor, against 72% without SWA. The walk then misses the blocks #59383 returned to the front and keeps offloading fresher blocks, which turns over the CPU tier.

Why not just #59383: it is sufficient without such groups (first row), but on DeepSeek-V4.1-style configurations it needs the walk change. The two are combined here so they can be reviewed and merged together. If #59383 merges first, this PR reduces to the walk commit.

Tradeoffs: a walk now revisits blocks already on CPU near the head, but it is still bounded by `target_free`, the same bound as before. One simulated case favors #59383 alone: without SWA groups and with an 8-step store latency, it recomputes 67.2% against 70.8% here. With 8 SWA blocks and the same latency, this PR is better (65.6% against 58.7%).

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Skip the client-side chat template on chat backends
author: dilberx
body:
The `custom`, `hf`, `spec_bench` and `speed_bench` datasets apply the tokenizer's chat template to each prompt unless `--skip-chat-template` is passed. With `--backend openai-chat`, `openai-responses` or `vllm-chat`, that already-templated prompt is sent as the content of a user message, and the server (or `LLM.chat` for `vllm bench throughput`) applies the template a second time. The model sees two nested templates, and input token counts are inflated.

`get_samples` now treats chat backends as `--skip-chat-template`. Completion backends (`openai`, `vllm`) keep the client-side template, since their endpoint takes raw text.

On Qwen2.5-1.5B with 8 custom-dataset prompts and `--backend openai-chat`, using server-reported usage:

| client | total input tokens | per request |
|---|---|---|
| main | 384 | 48 |
| this PR | 232 | 29 |

232 matches the same prompts sent through `--backend openai` with the client template, so the chat path now sends one template.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_chat_template_kwargs.py`: 7 passed. On main, the three new chat-backend cases fail and the two completion-backend cases pass.
- `pytest tests/benchmarks` (excluding the serve/throughput/latency CLI tests): the same 9 tests fail on main and on this branch (`test_bench_startup`, `test_forward_cli`, `test_mm_processor_cli`), all `FileNotFoundError: 'vllm'` from the `vllm` CLI not being on PATH in my environment.
- GPU check above on an RTX 3080.

## Duplicate check

Searched open PRs and issues for skip-chat-template / chat template applied twice in the bench client; found none.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the commands above.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Enable prefix-cache SWA replay on gfx942
author: frida-andersson
body:
## Overview

Enable prefix-cache SWA replay on CDNA3 (gfx942). #64094 enabled it on CDNA4 only. The change is the CDNA check in the DSv4.1 attention layer and the comment in `amd/model.py` that describes it.

`--swa-bounded-replay` is on by default, so after this PR every gfx942 DSv4.1 server with model runner V2 and prefix caching replays the window on hits. `--no-swa-bounded-replay` turns it off.

## Claims

- gfx942 runs the same bounded replay as gfx950: the scheduler rewinds a hit by the 128-token window, and the shared metadata and `combine_topk_swa_indices` kernels bound each gather at `replay_start`. None of that is arch-specific; only the CDNA check kept it off.
- Prefix hits recall planted codes as well as cold misses, and a per-layer log shows every hit gathering from `replay_start`.
- With prefix caching on in both arms, this PR serves a shared-prefix workload at 1.6–1.7× the request throughput of main, with 4–5× lower median TTFT. A single repeated prompt hits 5–9 ms slower, which is the window being recomputed.
- RULER NIAH at 131072 and GSM8K are unchanged.

## Validation

MI325X TP4, `--monokernel` unless noted, prefix caching on in both arms. "main" is image `0.33.0rc1.dev484+g76c6f3f2a`; "this PR" is the same image with only this PR's gate change applied to its `attention.py`. Both arms ran side by side with the same KV cache size. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA` is gfx950-only and ignored on gfx942, so it plays no part here.

### Throughput with shared prefixes

Many requests that start with the same long prefix. Both arms are MI325X TP4 with prefix caching on and the same KV cache size. Stock is the image on GPUs 0–3, port 8003. This PR is that image plus the gate, `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ov64094_gate`, on GPUs 4–7, port 8002.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_USE_FLYDSL=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8002 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 266240 --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --language-model-only --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-log-requests --monokernel
```

256 prefixes of 32768 tokens, each used 4 times with a different 256-token suffix, 1024 prompts. Concurrency 8, 32 and 64 use seeds 11, 12 and 13. The stock arm is the same command against port 8003.

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm --dataset-name prefix_repetition --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8002 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 32768 --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 256 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 256 --prefix-repetition-output-len 128 \
  --num-prompts 1024 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 11 \
  --ignore-eos --trust-remote-code --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

| concurrency | req/s, main / this PR | median TTFT, main / this PR | median TPOT, main / this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 1.49 / 2.39 | 2489 / 572 ms | 16.2 / 9.1 ms |
| 32 | 1.67 / 2.90 | 3608 / 765 ms | 114 / 45 ms |
| 64 | 1.72 / 2.99 | 2181 / 437 ms | 244 / 88 ms |

TPOT is not flat because decode shares each step with prefill chunks, and main prefills about twice as many prompt tokens (below). The decode kernels are the same in both arms.

Both gains come from hits. The prefix cache hit rate is about 50% on main and 76% with this PR. Main misses the second use of each prefix: one 32768-token prefix sent four times in a row, each with a new 256-token suffix, hits 0, 0, 32768 and 32768 tokens on main, and 0, 32768, 32768 and 32768 with this PR. Two hits out of four uses on main and three with this PR give the 50% and 76%. With a suffix shorter than the window (64 tokens), main also hits from the second use.

### Cost on a single repeated prompt

TTFT of an exact repeat, served from the prefix cache. This PR recomputes the 128-token window on every hit; main does not.

| prompt | hit TTFT, main / this PR |
| --- | --- |
| 4096 | 28 / 37 ms |
| 32768 | 40 / 49 ms |
| 65536 | 54 / 59 ms |

### Recall on cache hits

Checks that a hit gives the same answers as a cold run. The prompt hides three codes (23, 320 and 2400 tokens from the end) and asks for them back. Each case runs cold, then again so it hits the cache. gfx942 prefill is not bit-stable above 512 tokens, so cold runs also miss codes sometimes; each case is 8 trials, each under its own `cache_salt`, and the two columns should match, not be 8/8.

| prompt | tokens from cache | cold, all 3 codes | cache hit, all 3 codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4096, repeated | 4032 | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| 4096 cached, then sent with 512 more | 4096 | 4/8 | 7/8 |
| 16384 cached, then 4096 more, across a prefill chunk | 16384 | 3/8 | 3/8 |
| 32768 cached, then 1 more | 32768 | 6/8 | 8/8 |
| 65536 cached, then 1 more | 65536 | 7/8 | 6/8 |
| 8 different 8191-token prompts, sent all at once, cold and then as hits | — | 6/8 | 6/8 |
| multi-turn: a 16000-token turn 1, then turn 2 adds its 256 generated tokens | 16192 | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| same, with DSpark k=6 | 16192 | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| 4096, repeated, without `--monokernel` | 4032 | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| 32768 cached, then 1 more, without `--monokernel` | 32768 | 5/8 | 5/8 |
| control: 4064, repeated, with the window not rebuilt | 4032 | 8/8 | 1/8 |
| 4096 / 8191 / 16384 / 32768, repeated, on a full cache (below) | 4032–32704 | 31/32 | 32/32 |

The control row breaks the replay on purpose, and the hits fail, so the probe catches a broken replay. With 8 trials it cannot show that hits are exactly as good as cold runs; small differences would not show up.

The full-cache row ran with the KV cache cut to 701,257 tokens (`--kv-cache-memory-bytes 3500000000`) while 9–10 random 16384-token requests ran in the background. About 7.5M prompt tokens went through the cache during the probe, and every hit was still served from it.

### Accuracy

| task | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RULER niah_single_1, 131072 tokens | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| RULER niah_single_2, 131072 tokens | 1.0 | 1.0 |

title: [Perf][ROCm][MiniMax-M3.1] Add opt-in parallel decode top-k
author: jiacao-amd
body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in parallel decode top-16 selector for MiniMax-M3.1 on gfx950, replacing the fixed FlyDSL w26 selector in the NVFP4 indexer.

Supersedes #65032 and targets `main`. The parallel top-k tests extend the existing MI355 NVFP4 indexer suite; no CI configuration changes are included.

## Claims

- Preserve selected block IDs, ordering, tie handling and causal boundaries.
- Use runtime shape metadata to avoid new row/stride specializations during mixed-batch serving.
- Enable with `VLLM_ROCM_PARALLEL_INDEX_TOPK=1`; default off. FP8 indexers, including C4 mono decode, bypass this path.

### 900 s AgentX: baseline vs top-k only

title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Fix mixed draft-model warmup token budget
author: wxsIcey
body:
## Overview
Draft-model initialization with speculative decoding can fail during mixed prefill/decode warmup:
```
AssertionError: Shape: 2050 out of considered ranges: [(1, 2048)]
```

The warmup creates one synthetic decode request and one synthetic prefill request, but builds the scheduler inputs directly and bypasses the scheduler's correction-slot reservation. The extra query slots for these requests were missing from the warmup token budget, allowing the resulting shape to exceed max_num_tokens.

When a speculator is enabled, cap the warmup token count at max_num_tokens - num_warmup_reqs * num_extra_query_per_req. Skip the warmup if the adjusted budget is too small for a mixed step.

This fixes a regression in the mixed warmup path added by [#56492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492).

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Don't split a multimodal item when a prefix cache hit ends inside it
author: Anieca
body:
## Overview

With `disable_chunked_mm_input`, the scheduler still splits a multimodal item when a prefix cache hit ends inside it and the step has no room for the rest of the item. Models with bidirectional attention over the item then prefill its first part without seeing the rest.

#52306 reported these splits and #52412 and #59721 fixed them, but this path remained.

## Claims

- When a cache hit ends inside a multimodal item, the request waits for a step that can schedule the rest of the item.
- Adds tests for a cache hit inside an image, at the scheduler and end to end.

## Validation

On base `51c6dfd8c`:

```text
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k mm_input_chunking                                   # CPU
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py -k cache_hit_inside_image      # L4
```

With the original `scheduler.py`, three of the new checks fail: the request that hit the cache is scheduled 39 tokens into the image, the guard returns 500 tokens for a chunk that starts inside the item, and end to end the 40 image tokens prefilled first differ from the request run alone (320 / 800 elements, max abs diff 8.5e-3). With the fix, all pass.

## Details

Root cause: the guard assumes a chunk never starts inside an item, which does not hold in these cases:

- The same image is followed by a different question. The last block of the image also holds the start of the question, so that block misses and the hit stops inside the image.
- The KV cache runs short. Blocks are reused tail first, so the hit can stop early in the image, leaving most of it.

With the flag on, startup checks that one item fits in a step (`max_num_batched_tokens`), so the request is not starved. A `long_prefill_token_threshold` smaller than the item stalls it, as it already does on main (#62031, #62030).

#62782 changes the same lines; the two combine in either merge order.

No open issue or PR covers this case (checked 2026-11-02).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve SWA null-page offsets after store retry
author: waizuichougou
body:
## Overview

When a CPU offload store is retried after capacity exhaustion, SWA can release a GPU block and reallocate it for another logical position. The offloading scheduler marks the old position as `NULL_BLOCK_ID` but removes it from the source spec, so later pages shift into the wrong positions in the destination CPU chunk and can be loaded back as incorrect KV data.

## Claims

- Preserve the logical page layout of every full SWA chunk in the GPU-to-CPU store spec, including null blocks as placeholders for unreachable pages.
- Prevent store retries from corrupting the mapping between GPU source pages and CPU chunk offsets.
- Add a scheduler regression test with a mocked store failure and SWA block reuse.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Test command</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k test_swa_retry_keeps_internal_null_block_in_store_spec -q
```

With the fix:

```text
1 passed, 484 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.94s
```

With the regression test applied to the parent revision:

```text
At index 6 diff: 8 != 0
Right contains one more item: 9
1 failed, 484 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.90s
```

</details>

Without the fix, the generated store spec contains only 8 source pages and skips the internal null page. With the fix, it contains all 9 logical pages with `group_sizes=[9]` and `block_indices=[0]`.

A separate validation with the real `CPUOffloadingManager`, scheduler, offloading handler, and CUDA transfers reproduced the data error before the fix: loading logical pages 7 and 8 returned `[9, -99]` instead of `[8, 9]`. After the fix, the stored chunk was `[0, 8, 9]` and loading logical pages 7 and 8 returned `[8, 9]`.

No model-level evaluation was performed. The V1 KV Connectors GPU CI job is currently disabled, so the regression test was run manually.

## Details

`prepare_store()` can return `None` when all CPU chunks are held by in-flight loads and no chunk is free or evictable. During the retry window, SWA may release a GPU block and reallocate it for another position. The offloading scheduler then marks the old logical position as `NULL_BLOCK_ID`. `_build_store_jobs()` previously dropped that null block when building `GPULoadStoreSpec.block_ids`. The remaining pages were then packed without their original logical offset, although the destination CPU chunk still reserved a slot for every page in the full chunk.

The fix keeps null blocks as placeholders for unreachable pages in the source spec so source and destination chunk offsets remain aligned. Null blocks are excluded from the fence set because block 0 is the permanently reserved GPU null block and is not a live allocation.

Unlike #62932, which bounds secondary-tier loads by CPU capacity, this fixes GPU-to-CPU store page alignment after a retry.

The change is limited to source-spec construction in `OffloadingConnectorScheduler` and one focused regression test. It does not change admission, eviction, retry, or partial-tail behavior.

title: [Perf][Core] Cache parked async KV loads' admission reservations
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview Async KV load admission (#44560) checks each new load against the blocks every in-flight prefill still needs. To get that total it calls `_request_remaining_blocks` for every in-flight request, and it does so again on every admission. A P/D decode instance under a burst parks thousands of loads, so one `schedule()` makes (loads admitted) × (loads parked) calls. This PR caches each parked load's reservation and keeps a running total, so an admission computes only its own. ## Claims - For one `schedule()` that admits k async loads while M are parked, `_request_remaining_blocks` is called about k·M times on main and about M + k times with #64379. With this PR it is called k + p + k·s times, where p loads are promoted and s of them are scheduled in that step. It no longer depends on M. - With 4096 loads parked, a `schedule()` that admits 8 more takes 47.2 ms on main, 12.7 ms with #64379 and 5.4 ms with this PR. A per-step cap (#61725) turns a burst into many steps like this one. A single uncapped burst of 4096 loads takes 8.05 s on main, 77 ms with #64379 and 63 ms with this PR. - Admission decisions do not change. A load that is scheduled stays counted until the step ends, as on main. The stress test below compares every step with main and found no difference. - A cached reservation only needs refreshing at promotion. A parked load keeps its blocks until then, and the count follows the blocks it holds, not `num_computed_tokens`. So a failed load or invalid blocks do not change it until promotion frees the blocks. The stress test below checks cached == recomputed after every such event. - HiSparse loads are not cached, because HiSparse's count depends on the host pool's free blocks. They are still summed on demand, as on main. ## Validation ### Stress and burst CPU only, about 2 minutes (script and full output below). It runs 12 KV cache configs × 6 scheduler cases × 30 seeds with random arrivals, receives, failed loads, invalid blocks and aborts. `no_promote` is this PR without the promotion refresh, as a check that the test can fail. | | result | |---|---| | Stale or inconsistent reservation in this PR | 0 of 2160 runs | | Decisions differ from main | 0 of 2160 runs | | `no_promote` caught, per config and case | 6 to 24 of 30 runs | Failed loads run only under the `recompute` policy. The 6 seeds in 30 that use `fail` cannot catch `no_promote`, so 24 is the maximum. Burst: a prefill peer dies with 4096 loads parked, so every load fails and frees its blocks at promotion, and each retry waits on a deferred connector lookup. New loads then arrive. Each cell is new loads admitted / blocks overcommitted: | KV config | main | this PR | `no_promote` | |---|---|---|---| | Full attention | 6 / 0 | 6 / 0 | 2464 / 24577 | | Sliding window | 8 / 1 | 8 / 1 | 3080 / 24577 | | Chunked local | 16 / 1 | 16 / 1 | 4096 / 16321 | | Full + sliding window | 3 / 0 | 3 / 0 | 2734 / 49149 | A larger one-off sweep also parked 1167 (num_tokens, matched) cases on each of 26 KV configs, adding sink, cross-attention and more window sizes, and lowered `num_computed_tokens`. No count moved. As a control, the same comparison on a load holding no blocks did move for windowed managers.
Stress and burst script (run from the repo root: VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python repro.py) ```python """#65285 repro: VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python repro.py (from the repo root). Modes: pr (this branch), main (on-demand sum, as on main), no_promote (no refresh at promotion). burst: a prefill peer dies with thousands of loads parked. stress: random arrivals, receives, failed loads, invalid blocks and aborts per KV manager and scheduler case; after every step pr must have cached == recomputed, and its decisions are compared with main. """ import logging import multiprocessing import random import torch from tests.v1.core.utils import create_requests, create_scheduler, mock_kv from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base import SupportsHMA from vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler import Scheduler from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import ( ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec, CircularBufferSpec, FullAttentionSpec, KVCacheConfig, KVCacheGroupSpec, MambaSpec, MLAAttentionSpec, RSWASpec, SlidingWindowSpec, ) from vllm.v1.outputs import KVConnectorOutput, ModelRunnerOutput from vllm.v1.request import RequestStatus as Status logging.disable(logging.WARNING) B = 16 K = dict(block_size=B, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=1, dtype=torch.float32) MAMBA = dict(block_size=B, shapes=((1, 1),), dtypes=(torch.float32,)) FULL = FullAttentionSpec(**K) SWA = SlidingWindowSpec(**K, sliding_window=64) CHUNKED = ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec(**K, attention_chunk_size=32) ALIGNED = MambaSpec(**MAMBA, mamba_cache_mode="align") CHECKPOINT = MambaSpec( **MAMBA, mamba_cache_mode="align", num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks=1, prefill_checkpoint_alignment=1, ) SPECS = { "full": [FULL], "mla": [MLAAttentionSpec(**K)], "rswa":
