title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoE] Fix tkw1 rejecting count-free expert metadata, rename AITER QuantMethod
author: divakar-amd
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #63204 (part of #54966 item 5), addressing its post-merge review comments.

## Claims

- **Fix:** `AiterFp8ChannelExperts` again accepts expert-token metadata without token counts on the tkw1 route (e.g. DeepEP v2 under CUDA graphs). #63204 made the check reject *any* metadata; it now rejects only metadata that carries counts, as before. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447566182))
- **Rename:** `QuantMethod` → `AiterQuantType` (plus `_AITER_QUANT_TYPE`, `quant_type=`, `derive_aiter_quant_type()`), since "quant method" means the weight-loading quantization classes in vLLM. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447852851))
- **Removal:** `ActivationMethod`. It only named SILU/GELU; every activation now resolves via `rocm_aiter_ops.get_aiter_activation_type()`, as SWIGLU/SITU already did. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447841385))
- **Guard:** assert `a1q_scale is None` on the tkw1 branch. tkw1 quantizes the activation itself, so a dispatch-side scale would be silently dropped where the generic route forwards it.
- No numerical change intended.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` | 88 passed |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k aiter` | 67 passed, 14 skipped |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py` | 53 passed |

The new regression test was mutation-checked against both ways the fix can regress:

| Mutation | Failure |
|---|---|
| revert the fix (reject any metadata) | `AssertionError: AITER tkw1 kernel does not support num_local_tokens` |
| let count-free metadata fall through to the generic route | `count-free metadata did not reach the tkw1 kernel` |

The second is why the test spies on `rocm_aiter_ops.asm_moe_tkw1` rather than only comparing outputs: `asm_moe_tkw1` is `fused_moe(quant_type=per_Token, doweight_stage1=True)`, so the generic route is numerically equivalent and an output-only check passes through a fall-through.

## Details

- Output comparison uses `rtol=atol=1e-2`: tkw1 differs by ~1 bf16 ulp run to run. The test is gated on gfx942/gfx950, like the other asm/FP8 tests in the file.
- The enum-value test now checks `AiterQuantType` against `aiter.QuantType` rather than literals, so drift from AITER is caught.
- The mirror enum is kept because subclasses declare `_AITER_QUANT_TYPE` at class definition, in a module imported where AITER isn't installed.
- Raw custom-op tests now pass AITER's own `ActivationType`/`QuantType`.
- `rocm_aiter_ops` custom-op argument names (`quant_method: int`, `activation_method: int`) are unchanged: they are `torch.ops.vllm.*` schema names, so renaming them is a schema change rather than a Python rename. Out-of-tree callers of `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` must rename `quant_method=` to `quant_type=`.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these names or the tkw1 check.

title: [Bugfix] Keep the HiSparse FlashInfer all-reduce backend on lazy workspace creation
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Overview

#65201 forces the `trtllm` FlashInfer all-reduce backend under HiSparse to avoid the MNNVL fused AR+RMSNorm race (#64327). The override was skipped when the shared workspace was created lazily outside the vLLM config context. HiSparse servers then still came up on `mnnvl` and crashed with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`. Related: #56699.

## Claims

- HiSparse servers on main now get the `trtllm` all-reduce workspace without needing `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND`.
- Fixes the asynchronous `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (driver 719) under HiSparse multi-turn agentic load. It surfaces at the next event sync, e.g. `_finish_mirror_phase` or `async_utils.get_output`.

## Validation

Hardware: 4×B200, TP4. Main = 70eaf457c3. PR = 70eaf457c3 + this diff (since merged with current main; the touched file is unchanged there). Both arms ran an identical environment shim on `PYTHONPATH`: the kernel fix from #61463 (merged since), an `os.memfd_create` polyfill for the container's Python build, and logging probes. ## Details

`FlashInferAllReduce.__init__` resolves its backend while the config is current, which yields `trtllm` under HiSparse. It then called `_resolve_fi_ar_backend` again when it created the global workspace on the first all-reduce. With the V2 runner, that first all-reduce happens in `_profile_cudagraph_memory` → `capture_model(profile_only=True)`, which runs outside `set_current_vllm_config`. `get_current_vllm_config_or_none()` returns `None` there, so the HiSparse guard is skipped and `mnnvl` is auto-selected. The workspace is a process-wide singleton, so the fused AR+RMSNorm ops reuse the `mnnvl` workspace. Instrumentation confirmed `config is None` at workspace creation, with that stack.

The fix passes the backend resolved at init into `get_fi_ar_workspace`. The fusion pass already resolves within the config context and is unchanged.

The HiSparse guard can be dropped once FlashInfer ships flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782; this fix goes with it.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3.1] Retune the MXFP8 dot_scaled GEMM tiles for M=17-256
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## What

`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` (Triton `tl.dot_scaled`) picks its tile in `_select_cfg`. For the MiniMax-M3.1 TP4 linears on gfx950, M=17-64 used a single narrow 16x16 tile and M=65-256 a 64x64 / 8-warp tile. This adds a shape-scoped tile table (`_M31_TP4_TILES`, keyed by the local `(N, K)`) for M <= 256 covering the fused qkv, o_proj, shared-expert gate_up / down, dense gate_up / down and the DSpark qkv. Decode and verify batches are M = 8 x requests, so M = 8..256 spans c1..c32.

Everything else is unchanged: M <= 16 for qkv / gate_up / shared down keeps its tile, M > 256 and every other shape use the existing selection, every other arch is untouched (the tile table is gated on CDNA4, `get_cdna_version() == 4`, i.e. gfx95x where it was tuned).

## Why

These GEMMs read each weight byte once and are weight-bandwidth bound (FLOPs are under 10% of the time at M=32, about 40% at M=128). What matters is how many M tiles re-read the same weights and how many programs fill the 256 CUs. A BLOCK_M that follows M, three pipeline stages for the shorter K tiles, and 4 warps for the 64x64 tiles remove most of the gap: for example fused qkv at M=64 goes from 4 M tiles of 16 to 2 tiles of 32.

## Results

MI355X, one GPU, HIP-graph replay over rotating weights (400 MiB of weights so they come from HBM, as in the model); worst of two interleaved rounds. A warm-weights (8 copies) check agrees (not shown). "Floor" is max(bytes / 8 TB/s, FLOPs / 5 PF) with bytes = fp8 weight + e8m0 scales + activation + bf16 output.

## Correctness

Only the launch configuration changes. For every shape and M above the output is bit-identical to the current kernel (0 elements differ) and the error against the dequantized reference is unchanged (relative error 1.7e-3, below the 0.5% bound used in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mxfp8_tp4.py`). The TP2 qkv and dense gate_up rows and the dense-down M=65-128 tile come from a head-to-head against #62509 by @jiacao-amd, whose tile results were folded into the shape-keyed table (credited as co-author on the commit).

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Fix PP rank derivation when prefill context parallelism is enabled
author: xsxszab
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix PP rank calculation when pipeline parallelism (PP) and prefill context parallelism (PCP) are enabled together. The current calculation ignores the PCP dimension, causing incorrect MooncakeStoreConnector keys, model layer metadata, and Ray actor names.

Workers follow a PP × PCP × TP layout, so each PP stage contains `tp_size * pcp_size` workers. This PR replaces `rank // tp_size % pp_size` with `rank // (tp_size * pcp_size) % pp_size` in all three affected locations.

This PR also includes a small PP fix that I don't think warrants a separate PR: rejecting negative layer counts in VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION, such as "-1,5", instead of allowing invalid layer ranges.

## Claims

- MooncakeStoreConnector uses the correct PP stage in store keys, restoring external prefix cache hits in the tested PP2 × PCP2 configuration.
- `ModelConfig.get_layers_start_end_indices` returns the correct stage's layer range, including the layer count used by KV connectors and EAGLE drafters for uneven partitions.
- Ray actor names report the correct PP and PCP indices.
- Negative custom layer counts fail validation at startup. PP rank calculation is unchanged when PCP = 1.

## Validation

### End-to-end

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (MLA, 27 layers, split 14/13).
- Hardware and parallelism: 4 × B300, PP2 × PCP2 × TP1.
- Connector: `MooncakeStoreConnector`, `kv_both`, standalone store, asynchronous loading.
- Workload: GSM8K 5-shot, run twice against the same server so the second pass can reuse stored prompt KV. Local prefix caching is disabled.

| Metric | main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| External prefix cache hit rate, pass 2 | 0.0% | 97.7% |
| GSM8K accuracy, pass 1 / pass 2 | 0.644 / 0.643 | 0.654 / 0.636 |

Accuracy remains within the observed evaluation noise (SE ≈ 0.013). Reference runs on main without the connector score 0.635 at PP2 × PCP2, 0.644 at PP1 × PCP2, and 0.635 at PP2 × PCP1.

Start the server with a standalone Mooncake store available:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 8192 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"load_async":true}}'
```

Run the evaluation twice:

```bash
for pass in 1 2; do
  python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
done
```

Both main and this PR use `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`: MooncakeStoreConnector did not support extensible KV cache at the base revision used for these runs.

### Regression tests and CI

All four regression tests fail on main and pass with this PR; the remaining 272 tests in their files also pass.

```bash
pytest tests/test_config.py::test_layer_range_with_prefill_context_parallel \
  tests/distributed/test_pipeline_partition.py::test_custom_layer_partition \
  tests/utils_/test_ray_utils.py::test_build_actor_name_follows_pp_pcp_tp_layout \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py::test_pp_stages_write_distinct_keys_with_pcp
```

This PR adds `test_pipeline_partition.py` to the **Distributed Comm Ops** CI step and marks the Mooncake regression test `cpu_test` so it runs in the KV connector unit-test job. The end-to-end validation above was run outside CI; no existing job combines an MLA model with PCP, four GPUs, and a Mooncake store.

## Details

At PP2 × PCP2 × TP1, ranks 0–3 belong to PP stages `[0, 0, 1, 1]`, but the old formula returns `[0, 1, 0, 1]`. In MooncakeStoreConnector, this makes the computed PP rank equal the PCP rank: only `(PP, PCP)` key combinations `(0, 0)` and `(1, 1)` are written. Each stage's lookup requires all PCP shards, but `(0, 1)` and `(1, 0)` are missing, preventing cache hits.

Model layer construction already uses the PP process group through `make_layers`. The model-config fix aligns the reported layer ranges and counts with that existing assignment.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, and tests, with AI assistance also used to edit this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Kernel] Marlin: remove 8-bit (INT8/FP8) activation support, rely on Humming
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Part of #65560.

Remove INT8 and FP8 activation support (W4A8) from the dense and MoE Marlin kernels. Marlin becomes a 16-bit-activation kernel, and Humming covers 8-bit activations. Independent of #65540 (Marlin PTX-only build); this PR leaves the fp16/bf16 Marlin arch lists alone.

## Claims

- Removes Marlin's W4A8-INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ INT4) and W4A8-FP8 (GPTQ/AWQ INT4, MXFP4) paths: the sm89 FP8-activation kernels and their SM89/SM12x build targets, the INT8-activation instantiations, the 8-bit paths in both templates, the `marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess` op, `a_scales` on `marlin_gemm`/`moe_wna16_marlin_gemm`, and `is_a_8bit` on the repack ops. Net −2039 lines.
- `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` is removed, and setting it raises an error with a migration hint. The replacement is `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}'` (or `float8e4m3`), documented in `docs/features/quantization/README.md`.
- Compressed-tensors W4A8-FP8 checkpoints on SM89/SM12x, which previously fell back to Marlin, now select `HummingLinearKernel`.
- No change for FP8-weight Marlin (W8A16, MXFP8) or any 16-bit-activation format.

## Validation

DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), CUDA 13.0, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1` source build of this branch (kernel tests rerun after rebasing onto main without #65540, with native sm_120f Marlin cubins).

Kernel tests: `test_marlin_gemm.py` 254 passed, `test_moe.py -k marlin` 189 passed / 6 skipped, `test_marlin_tile_padding.py` 98 passed, `test_reload.py -k marlin` 6 passed, `test_marlin_vs_trtllm_mxint4.py` 1 passed. The counts dropped because the 8-bit-activation cases were removed. pre-commit (incl. mypy) passes.

GSM8K, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4`, 100 questions, 5-shot:

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| default (Marlin W4A16) | 0.62, 3348 tok/s | 0.60 / 0.62 (2 runs), 3364 tok/s |
| W4A8-INT8 (main: `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=int8`; PR: `--quantization humming` + `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}'`) | 0.68, 3413 tok/s | 0.63, 4008 tok/s |
| W4A8-FP8 (same, `fp8` / `float8e4m3`) | 0.69, 3554 tok/s | 0.62, 3842 tok/s |

The 100-question accuracy gaps are within noise. On the full set (1319 questions, accuracy only):

| Config | main (Marlin) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| W4A16 | 0.622 | 0.622 (Marlin) |
| W4A8-INT8 | 0.625 | 0.644 (Humming) |
| W4A8-FP8 | 0.591 | 0.603 (Humming) |

I checked that the Humming runs actually quantize activations by reading the loaded layer config: `a_dtype=int8, as_dtype=float32`. Note that `--linear-backend humming` with the same env var does **not** quantize activations for GPTQ/AWQ (`a_dtype=float16`), which is why the docs point to `--quantization humming`. Setting `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` now fails at startup with: `ValueError: VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE has been removed. Marlin no longer supports 8-bit activations. Use --quantization humming and set the activation dtype with VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG, e.g. '{"dtype":"int8"}'.`

```bash
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}' vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4 --quantization humming --max-model-len 8192
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 100
```

## Details

- On main, the Marlin 8-bit path was already narrow. For linear layers it only worked with GPTQ symmetric INT4: AWQ + `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=int8` fails at load with "W8A8 is not supported by marlin kernel". FP8-weight + FP8-activation was plumbed in Python but never instantiated.
- Template changes are constant folding of `is_a_8bit == false`, so the 16-bit kernels compile to the same code. The `mma` helpers lose the k=32 path and the `k_size`/`idx` params, and the repack kernels lose their `is_a_8bit` template param.
- `MarlinLinearKernel.can_implement` rejects 1-byte activation types, so selection falls through to Humming. `ConchLinearKernel` now also rejects non-16-bit activations; it had no activation check and sits between Marlin and Humming in the CUDA list.
- `int_wna16` MoE conversion returns 8 entries instead of 10 (the INT8 input global scales are gone). Every in-tree caller is updated.
- Not validated: Humming W4A8 MoE end to end. Marlin MoE W4A8 was only reachable through the removed env var.
- Deprecation: `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` is removed without a deprecation cycle. Setting it is now a hard error, raised from `validate_environ` via a new `envs.removed_environment_variables` map, and the message points to `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG`. Without the error, a user who set it would silently fall back to W4A16. Covered in `tests/config/test_config_generation.py::test_unrecognized_env`.

Superseded open PRs that extend Marlin W4A8: #58326, #48926, #38066, #50096, #59895, #61405, #49039, #57091. No open PR removes these paths (searched "VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE", "marlin w4a8", "marlin int8/fp8 activation", "remove marlin").

title: [CI] Run H100 fusion config sweeps and batch invariance nightly only
author: khluu
body:
## Overview

Make three H100 steps nightly-only (`optional: true`) to relieve the saturated `mithril-h100-pool` queue: `fusion-e2e-config-sweep-h100`, `fusion-e2e-tp2-ar-rms-config-sweep-h100` and `batch-invariance-h100`. Their AMD mirrors keep running on PRs (`optional: false`, same pattern as `distributed.yaml` / `lora.yaml`).

## Claims

- Frees ~465 of the ~483 GPU-hours/week these steps used on the H100 pool (~10% of `ci`'s H100 GPU-hours). They now run once per nightly instead of on every selected PR and main build.
- No loss of per-PR coverage in either area apart from the H100-specific runs listed under Details.
- No change to AMD scheduling.

## Validation

Data from Oct 27 – Nov 3 2026, collected through the Buildkite REST API for the `ci` pipeline:

| step | GPUs | GPU-h / week | PR jobs passed | PR jobs failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch-invariance-h100` | 1 | 226 | 585 | 0 |
| `fusion-e2e-tp2-ar-rms-config-sweep-h100` | 2 | 207 | 360 | 0 |
| `fusion-e2e-config-sweep-h100` | 1 | 50 | 360 | 0 |

The PR jobs that didn't pass were canceled or `waiting_failed`; none failed.

Generator behavior was checked locally against ci-infra `main` (`eb2d628f`) by loading the edited yaml with `step.parse_steps_from_yaml`, then evaluating `_step_should_run` and `_get_amd_mirror_effective_step` on a PR diff touching `vllm/compilation/` and `vllm/model_executor/determinism/`:
- NVIDIA steps: `optional=True`, so they don't run on a PR and do run with `NIGHTLY=1`.
- AMD mirrors: `optional=False`, so they still run on the PR.

When `ci-selector` is on, `pipeline_generator._selector_decision` removes optional keys from the selector's choice, as on every PR build today; recent decisions show `selector_optional_dropped` of ~148 keys per build. AMD keys stay on the path rules.

`pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/compile.yaml .buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` passes.

## Details

Why these steps:
- The H100 pool's p90 queue wait was 46 min that week (p99 115 min), compared with 5–14 min on the H200-slice and B200 queues.
- Each of the three steps had 0 PR failures and has a sibling that still runs per-PR:
  - The fusion sweeps run the full config grid. `fusion-e2e-quick-h100` and `fusion-e2e-tp2-quick-h100` (plus `fusion-e2e-tp2-b200`) still cover fusion on PRs. The B200 sweep (`fusion-e2e-config-sweep-b200`) is already nightly.
  - `batch-invariance-b200` runs on PRs and its commands are a superset of the H100 step's.

What moves to nightly-only:
- **Hopper batch invariance.** The Qwen3-FP8 `FLASH_ATTN` needle test on H100 exercises FA3; on B200 the same test takes a different FlashAttention path.
- **Full H100 fusion sweeps.** Only the quick subsets keep running on H100 per PR.
- PRs can still run these steps through "Run more jobs" or a `ready-run-all-tests` label.
- A PR that edits one of these step definitions still runs it, through the selector's changed-steps rule.

Not in this PR: `replayssm-e2e` is 26.5% of `ci`'s H100 GPU-hours. Narrowing its `source_file_dependencies` would not help, because on 22 of 30 recent PR builds that ran it, `ci-selector` chose it itself (`added-by-coverage`). The remaining 8 were run-all, nightly or explicit builds. Reducing it needs a selector or test-size change, which will be a separate discussion.

Duplicate check: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` on "batch invariance nightly", "config sweep nightly", "fusion e2e sweep", "H100 nightly" and "batch-invariance-h100" returned no PR that changes these steps' scheduling.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep FlashInfer TRTLLM prefill query offsets in a persistent buffer
author: Pb314314
body:
## Purpose

Fix an illegal memory access / segfault during CUDA graph replay of the standalone draft-model prefill on Blackwell (SM100), reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60989#issuecomment-6620438731.

Since #60989, the standalone draft model (`method: "draft_model"`) captures FULL CUDA graphs for its prefill. That prefill is a uniform batch of `num_speculative_tokens + 2` tokens per request, because it adds a correction token. That is one token more than FlashInfer's `reorder_batch_threshold` (`1 + num_speculative_tokens`). The builder therefore classifies every request as a prefill and, on SM100, takes the TRTLLM prefill path.

On that path, `build()` allocated `cum_seq_lens_q` as a new tensor (`qo_indptr[prefill_start:] - qo_indptr[prefill_start]`). Attention metadata is built outside the graph, so a FULL graph keeps the address that tensor had at capture time. The tensor is freed after capture and its memory is reused. At replay, the attention kernel reads query offsets from that reused memory. The result is wrong drafts or, for large batches, `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` or a segfault in `cuGraphLaunch`.

This PR writes the offsets into a persistent buffer owned by the builder, the same way `paged_kv_indptr` already works, so every build updates the memory the graph reads. The other tensors on this path (`seq_lens`, `block_tables`, `cum_seq_lens_kv`) are already views of persistent buffers.

Not covered here: with an FP8 KV cache and a non-FP8 query, the same path also makes a contiguous copy of `block_tables` on each build, which would have the same problem under a FULL graph. That configuration was not tested, so this PR leaves it alone.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_prefill_cudagraph.py`. It builds TRTLLM prefill metadata twice, for uniform batches wider than the reorder threshold, and checks that `cum_seq_lens_q` holds the right offsets and stays at the same address.
- End to end on 1x GB200 with model runner V2:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 \
  --max-concurrency 256 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0 --seed 0
# and again with --max-concurrency 32
```

## Test Result

- Unit test: passes with this PR. On main it fails with `cum_seq_lens_q moved between builds`.
- GSM8K end to end (1319 questions, greedy decoding; target Qwen/Qwen3-8B, draft Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, K=3):

| Setup | C256 | C32 | Mean accepted tokens per draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform decode graphs up to 256 requests (as in #63406), without this fix | crash (illegal memory access) | n/a | n/a |
| Same, with this fix | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |
| `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, attention runs eagerly (reference) | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |
| main, with this fix | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |

On main without this fix, the crash is intermittent: graphs there stop at about 200 requests, so a crash depends on what the freed memory holds. With the fix, accuracy and acceptance match the PIECEWISE reference, which shows the replayed draft prefill now reads the correct query offsets.

title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Share the QSA top-k buffer across layers
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Overview

Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) allocated one QSA top-k selection buffer per QSA layer (`max_num_batched_tokens x (indexer_budget + compress_ratio)` int32 each). This PR allocates one buffer on `Qwen4ExpModel` and passes it to every QSA layer, as DeepSeek V3.2/V4, GLM-5.3-Flash and MiniMax-M3 already do. The MTP drafter now reuses the target buffer through the existing proposer sharing (`load_eagle_model` / `llm_base_proposer`).

## Claims

- Removes 12 of the 13 per-layer buffers on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (12 QSA layers + 1 MTP layer). With the default `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` each buffer is 128 MiB, so about 1.5 GiB/GPU moves to the KV cache (measured +1.52 GiB). The saving scales with `max_num_batched_tokens`, so large-chunk prefill deployments gain more.
- No accuracy or MTP acceptance change.

## Validation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 on 1x GB200 node, `-tp 4 -ep --enable-prefix-caching --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'`, default `max_num_batched_tokens` (16384). Baseline is `main` at 5225a1f17f; same node type, same command.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Available KV cache memory (per GPU) | 143.60 GiB | 145.12 GiB (+1.52 GiB) |
| GPU KV cache size | 9,044,352 tokens | 9,151,208 tokens (+1.2%) |
| gsm8k (20-shot, chat, 1319 q) | 0.966 | 0.964 |
| MTP draft acceptance (whole gsm8k run) | 82.68% | 82.69% |

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 -tp 4 -ep --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 20 --num-questions 1319 \
  --use-chat-completions --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --max-tokens 1024 --max-concurrency 64
```

Unit tests (GB200): `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_tpsp.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py` -> 15 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only).

## Details

- Sharing is safe because each QSA layer writes its selection and the sparse attention reads it within the same layer call, and Qwen4Exp QSA already rejects DBO/microbatching, so layers never interleave.
- MTP: the drafter allocates its own buffer at construction (like the other sparse MTP models) and the proposer replaces it with the target's. The target does not run between draft steps, and the drafter runs one layer per step, so `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` (step-0 rows reused by later steps) keeps working.
- Only the NVIDIA implementation is changed. The ROCm implementation (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/`) has the same per-layer buffer; I'll follow up there once I can validate on ROCm.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR shares this buffer. #59279/#61242/#61728 (QSA DCP) only touch the comment next to it.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Keep whole-chunk max_load_tokens caps with sliding window groups
author: albertoperdomo2
body:
## Overview

With sliding window groups, the OffloadingConnector applied its prompt-end `-1` after the `max_load_tokens` / `max_num_new_tokens` caps, so a whole-chunk cap lost a chunk (a one-chunk cap loaded nothing). Follow-up to #55885.

## Claims

- With sliding window groups (and no partial-tail support, e.g. gpt-oss, Gemma 2/3), `max_load_tokens = k * tokens_per_chunk` now loads `k` chunks instead of `k - 1`.
- The same lost chunk is fixed for `max_num_new_tokens` (the bound from groups the connector does not offload).
- No change when there is no cap: the hit still stops before the last prompt token.

## Validation

New test `test_max_load_tokens_preserves_aligned_sliding_window_chunk` (16-token chunks, 65-token prompt, mixed full/sliding-window groups):

| Cap | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 16 tokens | 0 | 16 |
| 32 tokens | 16 | 32 |
| none | 64 | 64 |

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "max_load_tokens or sliding"   # 132 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
```

## Details

`_lookup_complete_chunks` computed `min(num_tokens, computed + cap) - 1`. The `-1` exists so a sliding-window hit stops before the last prompt token, which must be recomputed. When a cap ends earlier, it is already a supported boundary, but the `-1` moved it one token below, and the per-group `round_down` then dropped a whole chunk. The fix applies the `-1` to the prompt-end ceiling only: `min(num_tokens - 1, computed + cap)`. This matches the partial-tail path, which already uses `num_prompt_tokens - 1` with uncapped limits. Mamba alignment is unchanged.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `max_load_tokens`, `max_hit_size_tokens`, sliding window + offloading). Draft #62932 edits nearby lines for a different purpose (capacity-bounded loads); expect a trivial rebase for whichever lands second.

Test creation and validation assisted by Claude Code.

title: [torch.compile] Replace config `compute_hash` with `compile_factors`
author: hmellor
body:
## Overview

Replaces every config's `compute_hash() -> str` with `compile_factors() -> dict`, covering the remaining TODOs in #39479.

Closes #39479 It revives #40246, which was approved but closed when its branch was deleted, rebased onto current main.

## Claims

- Configs return their compile factors; `normalize_value` uses a nested config's `compile_factors()`, so `CompilationConfig` and `KernelConfig` no longer special-case `pass_config`, `dynamic_shapes_config` or `ir_op_priority`.
- `hash_config()` / `hash_config_cached()` replace `compute_hash()` / `compute_hash_cached()` for callers that need a string (EPLB, DP validation, serve fingerprint, startup plan, FlashInfer autotune cache).
- `cache_key_factors.json` now records the full env, config, code and compiler factors, not just env factors and hashes.
- JIT (`VllmBackend`) and AOT (`aot_compile_hash_factors`) share one env/config hash helper, and the JIT cache key and AOT source check share one code hashing helper. `CompilationConfig.traced_files` is now `set[Path]`.
- Every config that affects the graph is now opt-out: it hashes all fields except an explicit `ignored_factors` set, so new fields are hashed by default. Configs that don't affect the graph return `{}` and say how to switch if that changes.
- `get_compile_factors` raises on unknown `ignored_factors`, so a typo can't silently leave a field hashed.
- The set of hashed fields is unchanged, but hash values change, so existing compile caches miss once.
- **Breaking for out-of-tree code:** `additional_config` objects and `CompilerInterface` subclasses must implement `compile_factors()` instead of `compute_hash()`. A `CompilerInterface` subclass still defining `compute_hash` raises `TypeError`, since it would otherwise silently drop out of the cache key (for example `AscendCompiler` in vllm-ascend).
- The worker sentinel now uses `hash_config_cached`, like every other EPLB `model_states` lookup, avoiding a `KeyError` after `max_model_len` auto-fit.
- Supersedes #62458, #61885 and #62628.

## Validation

B200, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` loaded twice with an empty `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`:

| | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| Warm start loads compiled artifacts | yes | yes |
| Greedy output | `' Paris. The capital of France is also…'` | identical |
| `cache_key_factors.json` keys | `env` + 3 hashes | `env`, `config` (per sub-config), `code`, `compiler` + 3 hashes |
| Compile and config tests (989) | 21 fail | the same 21 fail |

The 21 failures are all in `tests/compile/test_config.py` and also fail on main on this host: cudagraph capture-size defaults for B200, plus a forked `test_VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE[1]` subprocess exiting with status 3.

```bash
python cache_run.py Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B $VLLM_CACHE_ROOT  # LLM(...).generate twice, then read cache_key_factors.json
pytest tests/compile/test_config.py tests/compile/fullgraph/test_toy_llama.py tests/compile/fullgraph/test_simple.py \
  tests/compile/fullgraph/test_multiple_graphs.py tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py \
  tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py tests/compile/test_decorator.py tests/config tests/test_config.py
```

```bash
pytest tests/config tests/test_config.py tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_fingerprint.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py tests/utils_/test_numa_utils.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/compile/test_config.py
```

Tests: main and branch give identical results on these suites on macOS (1105 passed; the same 63 fail on both for environment reasons). New tests in `tests/config/test_config_utils.py` cover nested-config hashing and unknown `ignored_factors`.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2]  Read routed experts from unkeyed full blocks
author: chenjr97
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix routed-expert output reconstruction after a prefix-cache hit when EAGLE/MTP lookahead hashing leaves a complete block without a key. Read request-local pending blocks alongside the incomplete tail.

Related: [[#61589 — Lookahead block hashes for EAGLE prefix caching](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61589)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61589).

## Claims

- Handle output ranges spanning published blocks, pending full blocks, and an incomplete tail.
- Return an independent array that remains valid after buffer reuse.
- Add buffer, worker, and `LLM` regression coverage, with auxiliary-output changes triggering the existing speculative-decoding CI jobs.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py -q
```
**81 passed, 14 warnings in 13.82s.**

## Details

Lookahead hashing requires the token after a block before its hash can be generated. Routing rows can therefore form a complete block while still waiting in `pending_blocks`.

For a 48-token prompt with block size 16:

1. A cold request computes `[0,48)` and returns its current rows directly.
2. A subsequent request reuses `[0,32)` and recomputes `[32,48)`.
3. The recomputed block is complete, but its hash depends on the new request's first generated token at position 48.
4. Output reconstruction reads `[0,32)` from the store, then needs the pending `[32,48)` block. The old `read()` only checked the incomplete tail, which does not exist here, and asserted.

The fix passes pending blocks to `RoutedExpertsBuffer.read()` and combines them with the tail to cover the requested interval. It retains the coverage assertion and copies the output. Reading leaves pending blocks available for publication when their hashes arrive.

title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Route the PLE shard copy through copy_weight_
author: JimmyToluene
body:
## Overview

Routes the Qwen4Exp PLE shard copy through `copy_weight_`, the follow-up named in #58868. Fixes #58726.

@Willian-Zhang, as you asked in #58868.

**Not a duplicate:** when this was opened, no other open PR mentioned #58726 or changed `ple.py`. #65713 now applies the same swap to other loaders and doesn't touch this file. The open PLE storage PRs (#58439, #58815, #62847) avoid or stage this copy for offloaded tables; this one speeds up the existing device-resident path.

## Claims

- On a DGX Spark serving a device-resident packed-NVFP4 PLE table (`cpu_offload: false`), main `Loading weights took` falls from about 213 s to about 76 s from a cold page cache, and start to `/health` from about 320 s to about 184 s.
- Output is unchanged: logprobs and greedy text were exactly equal to the old line in every run.
- Off integrated GPUs `copy_weight_` is a plain `copy_`. A dtype-converting copy skips the touch.
- The old line also created a temporary GPU tensor through `.to(device=…)` before copying. This drops it, with or without a dtype conversion: in a small GB10 test, extra peak GPU memory went from the target's size to 0. I did not measure discrete GPUs.

## Validation

**End to end, this branch.** `vllm serve` on one GB10, `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-LIL-qad5500`, local NVMe, TP=1, four boots in the order old, new, new, old. Only `ple.py` differed. The checkpoint was evicted with `posix_fadvise` before each boot, and `mincore` reported 0% resident.

| Run | Main `Loading weights took` | Start to `/health` | Output tok/s | Mean ITL |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| old line, run 1 | 212.12 s | 318 s | 50.41 | 67.11 ms |
| `copy_weight_`, run 1 | 74.66 s | 179 s | 50.53 | 67.39 ms |
| `copy_weight_`, run 2 | 77.50 s | 188 s | 50.96 | 67.17 ms |
| old line, run 2 | 213.11 s | 322 s | 48.57 | 67.44 ms |

**Output.** Against the code it replaces, per `tests/AGENTS.md`: 16 fixed prompts with `temperature=0` and `seed=0`. All 566 prompt-token logprobs and all 16 48-token greedy completions were exactly equal across all four boots.

**Model evaluation not run.** `tests/evals/qwen4_exp` targets Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 with `--tensor-parallel-size 4` on H200/B200, which I don't have. This change does not alter the loaded weights, as the exact comparison above and the table check below show.

**Table copy alone, this branch.** The 128 `weight` and 128 `weight_scale` shards (28.8 GB), each copied by the real `_copy_embedding_shard_` into a GPU tensor of the shard's dtype, cold cache, two runs per arm. The old line took 176.8 s and 178.9 s; `copy_weight_` took 11.4 s and 10.2 s. Both tables compared equal with `torch.equal` after every run.

**Rebase.** The boots and table copy above ran just before a final rebase onto current `main`, which changed neither `ple.py` nor `model_executor/utils.py`. The tests below were rerun after it.

**Earlier result.** The 160 s → 14 s figure for the table within a stock nightly boot is in [this comment on #58868](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-6349449742).

**Tests**, from `.venv` per `AGENTS.md`, on the GB10 with its GPU:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_utils.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/ple.py
```

- `test_ple.py`: 127 passed, 2 skipped.
- `test_utils.py`: 32 passed.
- `pre-commit`: passed.

<details>
<summary>Serve command and environment</summary>

The host has no `nvcc`, so serving ran in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e4a5b5537344` (torch 2.14.0+cu130) with this tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The baseline bind-mounted the previous `ple.py` over it.

```bash
vllm serve <checkpoint> --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' --disable-flashinfer-autotune

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 \
  --random-output-len 64 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 4 --seed 0
```

Autotune was off because, with the model loaded, it took this machine down to 1 GiB available.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause:** `_copy_embedding_shard_` copied each shard with `target.copy_(source.to(device=target.device, dtype=target.dtype))`, straight from the safetensors mmap view. For a same-dtype source, the page faults land inside the driver copy, which #58726 measured as several times slower than faulting on the CPU.

**Scope:** `load_weights` in `nvidia/ngram_embedding.py` sends split table shards through `weight_loader` to this copy. Disk-offloaded tables take `accept_checkpoint_shard` instead. The `buffer.copy_` in the same function only handles the small hash buffers, so I left it alone.

**Other backends:** `amd/ple_layer.py` reaches the same copy. `copy_weight_` only touches pages when `is_integrated_gpu` is true, and otherwise runs a plain `copy_`. I only ran this on a GB10.

**Tradeoffs:** this is load-time only, so steady-state inference and CPU/GPU synchronization are untouched. The touch reads the pages it is about to copy, and the lowest available memory during boot was 4–5 GiB in both arms.

**CI coverage:** CI has no integrated GPU, so it can't exercise the touch path here. `test_ple.py` runs on H200 and MI355 through `models_basic.yaml`, and #58868 tests the helper with the gate forced on. I added no test because this is one line of wiring. Validation outside CI is above.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the measurements and this write-up; I reviewed the change and the results.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Handle EOS in speculative Guidance batches
author: sragrawal
body:
## Overview

Fix Guidance rejecting committed speculative token batches that contain EOS followed by more tokens when `ignore_eos=True`.

## Claims

- Validate the grammar only through the first primary EOS, preserving the caller's generated token list.
- Keep invalid-prefix rejection atomic and preserve normal EOS stopping and speculative rollback.

## Validation

CPU, PR head `055ccc9fb` plus the test correction: **81 passed, 2 existing xfails** across the Guidance, grammar-backend and structured-output-manager suites. The two new regression cases fail on the unmodified base. Changed-file pre-commit passes, including mypy and CI selection.

H200 ×1, OPT-125M, using the CI image built from `055ccc9fb`: the revised regression test fails with the unpatched backend—grammar rejection stops generation after 5 of 8 tokens—and passes with the fix, producing all eight tokens with a length finish reason and nonzero speculative acceptance. The test forces the `a → EOS` prefix through grammar masking and allowed token IDs, without the unsupported `logit_bias` setting.

GPU, vLLM 0.32.0 with the equivalent fix backported: H200 ×8 / TP8, Mistral Medium 3.5 FP8 with its [EAGLE draft](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-EAGLE), k=3, context 262144, concurrency 8, `ignore_eos=True`. Actual request payloads were identical between runs.

| Streaming check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completed requests | 10/16 | 16/16 |
| Grammar-related SSE500 errors | 6 | 0 |
| Exact requested output lengths | 10/10 successful requests | 16/16; 41,660 output tokens |

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q

# H200, from the repository root:
pytest -v -s \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py::test_guidance_ignore_eos_with_speculative_decoding

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py
```

</details>

## Details

Guidance already accepts further tokens after grammar termination. However, it rejects a batch containing EOS and a suffix before checking that state. The same tokens can therefore succeed one at a time and fail when committed together. The older bulk-consumption implementation can also leave the matcher in an invalid state after consuming past EOS.

Pass only the prefix through EOS to the matcher. The existing atomic acceptance and rollback from [#61557](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61557) remain intact. Normal EOS stopping trims the generated batch before grammar acceptance; temporary draft-mask advancement uses singleton tokens.

Related open [#65608](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65608) handles additional request/model stop tokens. This change concerns the tokenizer's primary EOS and does not add stop-token mapping. When combining the changes, primary-EOS prefix handling should precede additional-stop mapping.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft NoPE layer rotated (main) | 4.98 | .86 | .71 | .58 | .47 | .39 | .31 | .15 | .07 | .03 | .01 |
| `no_rope_layers` honored (this PR) | 7.34 | .91 | .82 | .73 | .65 | .58 | .52 | .38 | .26 | .17 | .09 |

- `tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Ricursive`, `tests/models/test_registry.py -k Ricursive`: pass.
- `tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning` (CPU): 9771 passed.
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py test_dflash_causality.py test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/models/test_qwen3_dflash_mxfp8_context_kv.py tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py`: 160 passed.
- New: `tests/parser/engine/test_ripple.py` and the Ripple trace-builder samples; `test_ripple_draft_skips_context_rope_on_nope_layers` in `test_dflash2.py` (draft routing, and NoPE layers keep unrotated context keys).

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
vllm serve ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4 --max-model-len 32768
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000

vllm serve ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser ripple --reasoning-parser ripple \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2", "num_speculative_tokens": 15}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 8192 --temperature 0
```
</details>

## Details

- **Model.** Dense 80 layers. Repeating pattern of 4 sliding-window (1024, RoPE) layers and 1 full-attention NoPE layer; PeriNorm (Gemma 3 style pre/post norms); per-head Q/K RMSNorm; fp32 sigmoid output gate; value residuals (`v_proj(lerp(x0, h, sigmoid(λ)))` with `x0` the scaled embeddings); clamped SwiGLU via the existing `SiluAndMulWithClamp`. Q/K/G share one `MergedColumnParallelLinear`; V stays separate because it reads the value-residual blend. The value-residual source is cloned, because the fused add+RMSNorm updates the layer-0 residual in place and would otherwise overwrite it. It travels through PP intermediate tensors, and the model exposes EAGLE-3 aux hidden states for the draft.
- **Parser.** A declarative `ParserEngine` grammar starting in CONTENT. The template's framing newlines (`<think>\n…\n</think>\n`, `\n<tool_call>\n…\n</tool_call>`) are folded into the marker spellings, so they reach neither reasoning nor content. Reasoning is optional, so structured outputs apply from the first token and constrained requests answer directly; this matches the authors' SGLang parser. The markers are multi-token plain text, so the parser is skipped in the single-token replay harness, as PLaMo3 already is.
- **DFlash NoPE.** Ripple's drafter lives in its own subclass (`ricursive_dflash2.py`): a `DFlash2DraftModel` draft that declares `no_rope_layers` is routed to `DFlash2RicursiveDraftModel` in `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`. Its NoPE layers skip the query rotation and restore their unrotated context keys after the shared fused RoPE call. The only shared-code change is moving that fused call into an overridable `DFlashQwen3Model._apply_context_rope`, with no behavior change for other drafts.
- **Reasoning-only streaming.** Without a tool parser (no `--enable-auto-tool-choice`), `parse_delta` passed deltas through raw once the prompt closed reasoning. Ripple's grammar starts in content, so that is always the case. An engine whose grammar can open reasoning from content now parses the whole stream, matching the non-streaming path (`abstract_parser.py`, `adapters.py`). The full `tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning` suite still passes (9771).
- **CI coverage.** The full-size checkpoints are too large for CI, so the parity and GSM8K numbers above were measured locally. `test_ripple.py` joins the other `tests/parser` files on the tethering allowlist while that CI job is disabled.
- **Limitations.** Not tested: ROCm, LoRA, the BF16 checkpoint at TP>1.

title: [GLM 5.3 Perf] Expand fp8 moe tma for sm100, 1.03~1.60x kernel performance improvement
author: yewentao256
body:
## Overview

Follow up for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63820

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
"""Compare Triton pointer and B-TMA loads for a GLM-5.3 local FP8 MoE shard.

Run from the repository root with ``PYTHONPATH=.``. Routing is precomputed;
the timings cover the local MoE kernels, not model serving.
"""

import argparse
from dataclasses import replace
from functools import partial
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
import triton.testing
from triton.tools.tensor_descriptor import TensorDescriptor

from tests.kernels.moe.utils import (
    make_dummy_moe_config,
    make_test_quant_config,
    modular_triton_fused_moe,
)
from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import override_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe import try_get_optimal_moe_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.fused_topk_bias_router import (
    fused_topk_bias,
)
from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager, reset_workspace_manager

TOKENS = (1, 8, 32, 128, 512, 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, 8192)
EXPERTS, HIDDEN, INTERMEDIATE, TOPK = 256, 6144, 2048, 8


def run(kernel, config, x, w1, w2, weights, ids, use_tma):
    with override_config({**config, "USE_TMA": use_tma}):
        return kernel.apply(
            x,
            w1,
            w2,
            weights,
            ids,
            activation=MoEActivation.SILU,
            global_num_experts=EXPERTS,
            expert_map=None,
            apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
        )


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--tp", type=int, choices=(4, 8), default=4)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    n = INTERMEDIATE // args.tp

    torch.set_default_device("cuda")
    torch.manual_seed(123)
    init_workspace_manager(torch.device(0))
    try:
        with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()), torch.inference_mode():
            w1, w2, quant = make_test_quant_config(
                EXPERTS,
                n,
                HIDDEN,
                torch.bfloat16,
                torch.float8_e4m3fn,
                block_shape=[128, 128],
            )
            print(f"{torch.cuda.get_device_name()} GLM-5.3 TP={args.tp}")
            print("tokens pointer_us b_tma_us speedup", flush=True)
            for m in TOKENS:
                x = (torch.randn(m, HIDDEN) / 10).to(torch.bfloat16)
                logits = torch.randn(m, EXPERTS, dtype=torch.float32)
                bias = torch.randn(EXPERTS, dtype=torch.float32) / 10
                weights, ids = fused_topk_bias(
                    x,
                    logits,
                    "sigmoid",
                    bias,
                    TOPK,
                    True,
                    routed_scaling_factor=2.5,
                )
                moe = make_dummy_moe_config(
                    num_experts=EXPERTS,
                    experts_per_token=TOPK,
                    hidden_dim=HIDDEN,
                    intermediate_size=INTERMEDIATE,
                    max_num_tokens=m,
                )
                moe.moe_parallel_config = replace(
                    moe.moe_parallel_config, tp_size=args.tp
                )
                moe.intermediate_size_per_partition = n
                kernel = modular_triton_fused_moe(moe, quant)
                config = try_get_optimal_moe_config(
                    w1.shape,
                    w2.shape,
                    TOPK,
                    "fp8_w8a8",
                    m,
                    block_shape=[128, 128],
                )
                call = partial(run, kernel, config, x, w1, w2, weights, ids)

                pointer = call(False)
                with patch.object(
                    TensorDescriptor, "from_tensor", wraps=TensorDescriptor.from_tensor
                ) as descriptors:
                    tma = call(True)
                assert len(descriptors.call_args_list) == 2
                assert all(c.args[0].ndim == 3 for c in descriptors.call_args_list)
                torch.testing.assert_close(pointer, tma, atol=0, rtol=0)

                pointer_us = 1000 * triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(
                    partial(call, False), rep=100
                )
                tma_us = 1000 * triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(
                    partial(call, True), rep=100
                )
                print(
                    f"{m:>6} {pointer_us:>10.1f} {tma_us:>8.1f} "
                    f"{pointer_us / tma_us:>7.2f}x",
                    flush=True,
                )
    finally:
        reset_workspace_manager()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Encoder CUDA graph: cap each graph's frame slots at its token budget
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview

When encoder CUDA graphs are on and the model accepts video, every captured graph is sized for `max_batch_size x max_frames_per_video` frames, including the graphs for small token budgets. For GLM-4.1V that is 64 x 600 = 38,400 frames, so even the smallest graph computes at least 38,400 tokens, and every image or video request replays a graph far larger than its input.

This PR caps each graph's frame slots at its token budget.

## Claims

- **GLM-4.1V** (encoder graph on, video allowed, which is the default):
  - Median image request: 470–481 ms → 31–32 ms.
  - Median video request: 475–484 ms → 35–36 ms.
  - Eager takes 57 ms (image) and 61 ms (video). Before this PR the graph path was ~8x slower than eager; after it, it is faster.
- **Qwen2.5-VL-7B at 128k context:**
  - Median image request: 30–33 ms → 27 ms.
  - Median video request: 32–33 ms → 30–31 ms.
- **Video outputs are unchanged:**
  - GLM-4.1V: graph outputs match eager bit for bit.
  - Qwen2.5-VL: graph outputs match main's graph outputs token for token.
  - Both hold for single videos and for 4-video batches replayed as one graph.
- **No effect** when video is disabled, or when `max_frames_per_batch` is at most the budget.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GB200, bf16, default ViT attention backend.
- Baseline is main at 2a777ce26e; this PR is the same commit plus the change.

**Latency.**
- One engine per run with `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 1}`, so image and video requests share the same graphs.
- Each run sends 24 image requests and 24 video requests one at a time, with `max_tokens=1`.
- Images and videos are fresh random inputs, so there are no encoder-cache hits:
  - images cycle through 6 sizes from 224x224 to 896x672;
  - videos have 4–16 frames at 224–448 px.
- Each graph-on request replays exactly one graph, counted via `EncoderCudaGraphManager.execute` calls.
- Runs were in the order baseline, this PR, this PR, baseline. The two values per cell are pass 1 / pass 2, each the median request latency.

| Model (`max_model_len`) | Requests | Baseline, graph on | This PR, graph on | Eager |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V-9B (8192) | image | 469.8 / 480.6 ms | 31.9 / 31.2 ms | 56.8 ms |
| GLM-4.1V-9B (8192) | video | 475.4 / 484.2 ms | 35.9 / 35.2 ms | 60.7 ms |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (128000) | image | 32.6 / 30.3 ms | 27.2 / 27.1 ms | 56.9 ms |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (128000) | video | 32.1 / 31.9 ms | 30.8 / 29.7 ms | 55.7 ms |

**Video correctness.** Greedy decoding with `logprobs=2`; each comparison is graph vs eager on the same tree, and every video is fresh.

| Model | Inputs | Graph replays | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V (`max_model_len=8192`, 38,400 → budget frame slots on every graph) | 4 single videos (48 tokens each) + 2 batches of 4 videos (32 tokens each) | each 4-video batch is one replay | tokens identical, logprob diff 0 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (`max_model_len=128000`, 896 → budget frame slots on graphs ≤ 512) | 4 single videos + 2 batches of 4 videos (32 tokens each) | 4 single replays, and each 4-video batch is one replay | identical to main's graph: 12/12 token sequences |

On Qwen2.5-VL, both main and this PR match eager on 10 of 12 sequences. The 2 that diverge are the same on both. Each divergence happens at a step where eager's top-2 logprobs are exactly tied, after bf16 differences of up to 0.24 in logprob. That drift between graph and eager already exists on main and is unrelated to this change.

On GLM-4.1V, the encoder outputs for videos were also compared directly:
- Graph vs eager has a relative L2 error of ≤ 0.2%, the same as eager vs eager in a different batch.
- Replaying after other inputs have dirtied the capture buffers gives identical outputs.

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: 79 passed. The new test captures with `max_frames_per_batch=1000` and checks two things: each graph keeps `min(1000, budget)` frame slots, and a video batch still replays. `pre-commit` passes.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
# Image latency (square images only); run with cudagraph_mm_encoder True and False.
import time, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
llm = LLM("zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking", max_model_len=8192, max_num_seqs=8,
          enable_prefix_caching=False, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 1},
          compilation_config={"cudagraph_mm_encoder": True})
P = ("[gMASK]<sop><|user|>\n<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>"
     "Describe the image.<|assistant|>assistant\n")
rng, sp, ts = np.random.default_rng(0), SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1), []
for _ in range(6):
    for s in (224, 336, 448, 672):
        im = Image.fromarray(rng.integers(0, 255, (s, s, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
        t = time.time(); llm.generate([{"prompt": P, "multi_modal_data": {"image": im}}], sp)
        ts.append(time.time() - t)
print(f"median {1e3 * sorted(ts)[len(ts) // 2]:.1f} ms")
```

The video runs use the same setup with synthetic videos (4–16 frames, 224–448 px). For correctness they use `temperature=0` and `logprobs=2`, run once with `cudagraph_mm_encoder` on and once off, and compare tokens and logprobs. For batches, 4 fresh videos are submitted in one `generate` call.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `EncoderCudaGraphManager` passes one `max_frames_per_batch` to every budget's capture. That value is `max_batch_size * max_frames_per_video`, which became the default in #40445.

Qwen2/2.5/3-VL and GLM-4.1V build their capture layout from it: each item gets `frames_per_item = max_frames_per_batch // max_batch_size` frames, and each frame has at least one token. The captured size is therefore at least `max_frames_per_batch` tokens, whatever the budget.

How badly a model is affected depends on where its frame limit comes from:
- **GLM-4.1V:** the limit is a constant 600 frames per video, so every budget captures at least 38,400 tokens.
- **Qwen:** the limit is derived from `max_model_len` and the video limit, so the graphs grow only with long contexts. For example, Qwen2.5-VL at 128k context gets 896 frame slots, which inflates the 64–512 budgets.

**Fix.** Every frame yields at least one output token, so a batch that fits budget `B` has at most `B` frames. Concretely:
- Each graph is captured with `min(max_frames_per_batch, B)` frame slots.
- That value is stored in `BudgetGraphMetadata`.
- Replay pads `cu_seqlens` to the same per-graph value.

The model capture layouts are unchanged; they shrink because they derive from the value passed in.

Every auto or validated configuration keeps `B >= max_batch_size`, so a graph never gets fewer frame slots than `max_batch_size`, and image replays are unaffected.

`EncoderCudaGraphManager` is shared by Model Runner V1 and V2 (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py`), so both get the fix. The change adds no host sync.

**Related: GLM-4.1V image outputs (not changed by this PR).**
- On main, with video enabled, GLM-4.1V image replays are numerically wrong. GLM registers no `cu_seqlens` padding, so the replay buffer's tail is filled with zeros.
- Measured at the encoder output on main, graph vs eager has a relative L2 error of up to 169% for a 576-token image. Eager vs eager in a different batch varies by only 0.2–2.7%.
- This PR does not fix that: 576-token images are still wrong with it. #65453 registers the padding and fixes it; with both applied, the error is back within the eager variation.

**Not a duplicate:**
- #60112 (open) falls back to eager when a replay exceeds a capture buffer.
- #43403 (closed draft) proposed an eager fallback for `T > frames_per_item`.
- #65453 (open) registers `cu_seqlens` padding for GLM-4.1V and Kimi-K2.5.

None of these changes the capture size. #65453 touches the same padding path but no lines in common; with this PR, capture and replay still use the same per-graph frame count.

title: [CI][Kernels] Make the MiniMax-M3 decode top-k test deterministic
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fix the flaky `(L4) Attention Kernels` failure on main: `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py::test_decode_index_topk_correctness[0-4-4]` fails with `assert {0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 7} == {0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7}`. It has failed 17 times since build [99886](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99886), with no related kernel or test change.

**Root cause.** The decode indexer computes scores with `tl.dot` on fp32 inputs, which runs at TF32 precision on L4. The reference uses a true-FP32 `einsum`. The test draws unseeded `randn` inputs, so whenever two blocks score within TF32 rounding of each other at the top-6 boundary, the two sides pick different blocks. The `[2-4-4]` sibling case, which takes the same `q_len=4` path, passes, so this isn't a kernel bug. The test just picks up whatever RNG state earlier tests in the shard left behind.

**Fix.**
- Draw the test's inputs from a local `torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)`, so they no longer depend on the global RNG state that earlier tests in the shard leave behind.
- Round `idx_q` and `index_kv_cache` to bf16-representable values. A product of two such values is exact in TF32, so the kernel and the reference compute identical products; the only remaining difference is fp32 accumulation order. The assertion stays a strict set-equality check.

Not a duplicate: there are no open PRs for this test. #52847 changes the decode index tile, not this test.

## Test Plan

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `py_compile` pass locally.
- I have no GPU locally, so the test hasn't been run on GPU yet. The step should go green on this PR's L4 CI.

## Test Result

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix FlashInfer ViT attention for GLM-4.1V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview

With `--mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASHINFER`, the GLM-4.1V/4.5V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash vision encoders fail on main, in eager mode and with encoder CUDA graphs alike.

This PR fixes their attention so FlashInfer runs and matches the other ViT backends. The default backend's output does not change.

## Claims

- **FlashInfer now works on all three models.** On main, every forward asserts `sequence_lengths is not None`. With this PR, FlashInfer's output differs from FlashAttention's by the same amount as `TORCH_SDPA`'s does.
- **Batching is now correct.** With only the assert fixed, every sequence after the first in a batch read the wrong `v`:
  - outputs were off by 166% relative L2, or NaN;
  - capturing a 1024-token encoder graph hit an illegal memory access.
  
  With this PR, an image's output in a batch matches its output alone within 0.2%, in either batch order.
- **Default backend unchanged.** FlashAttention outputs are bitwise identical to main. Encoder latency is 1.5% lower, since `v` is no longer copied.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GB200, bf16, TP1.
- Baseline is main at 2a777ce26e; this PR is the same commit plus the change.

**Method.**
- Each image is a fresh random image of 224x224 to 896x672.
- Every value is the relative L2 error `‖a − b‖ / ‖b‖` of the vision encoder output.

**Backend agreement (eager).** In the cross-backend columns below, FlashInfer is this PR; FlashAttention and SDPA are main. "Batched" is the largest error of an image's output in a 5-image batch against its output alone, over both batch orders.

| Model | Weights | FlashInfer, main | FlashInfer vs FlashAttention | SDPA vs FlashAttention | FlashInfer, batched vs alone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking | real | AssertionError | 2.55–2.82% | 2.42–2.88% | ≤ 0.21% |
| GLM-OCR | real | AssertionError | 4.20–5.72% | 3.93–6.72% | ≤ 0.26% |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (vision tower only) | random, seeded | AssertionError | 2.81–2.94% | 2.81–2.91% | ≤ 0.34% |

GLM-5.3-Flash uses the real `config.json` and processor with seeded random vision weights, because the full checkpoint was not available.

**Encoder CUDA graphs with FlashInfer (GLM-4.1V, `max_model_len=8192`, video enabled).**
- Graph vs eager is ≤ 0.20% for 6 single images (64–576 tokens) and 4 videos (256–768 tokens).
- Replaying after a larger batch has dirtied the capture buffers gives identical output.
- This holds with and without #65453.
- On main, capture fails.

**Default backend.**
- GLM-4.1V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash FlashAttention outputs are bitwise identical to main: single images, batches in both orders, and GLM-4.1V graph replays.
- GLM-4.1V encoder latency was measured over 34 batches of 1–200 images (64–13,800 tokens). Each value is the median of 15 runs. Runs went baseline, this PR, this PR, baseline, and each batch keeps the faster pass.

| | This PR / baseline (geomean) | Slowest batch | Batches > 2% slower | Baseline pass-to-pass spread (median) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph replay | 0.985 | 0.996 | 0 / 34 | 0.13% |
| Eager | 0.984 | 1.001 | 0 / 34 | 0.35% |

**FlashInfer vs FlashAttention latency (GLM-4.1V, with this PR).**
- This PR is a correctness fix; it does not make FlashInfer faster. FlashAttention (FA4) stays the default backend.
- Measured over the same 34 batches as above, alternating FlashAttention, FlashInfer, FlashInfer, FlashAttention, keeping the faster pass per batch.
- Every FlashInfer batch matched eager within the graph-vs-eager tolerance.

| | FlashInfer / FlashAttention (geomean) | Range | Batches > 2% slower |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph replay | 1.003 | 0.989–1.032 | 2 / 34 |
| Eager | 1.041 | 0.999–1.159 | 10 / 34 |

- **With graphs:** the two backends are within 1.1% for batches above 1,300 tokens. Smaller batches are up to 3.2% slower with FlashInfer.
- **In eager mode:** most batches up to 1,100 tokens are 12–16% slower with FlashInfer, where per-call host overhead dominates. Above 1,300 tokens they are within 2%.

**Tests.**
- This PR adds GLM-4.1V to `test_eonly_vit_cudagraph_outputs`, which runs FlashInfer with encoder CUDA graphs on image and video batches. It fails on main (`assert sequence_lengths is not None`) and passes with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: 78 passed.
- `pre-commit` passes.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
# Fails on main with AssertionError; runs with this PR.
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

llm = LLM("zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking", max_model_len=8192,
          mm_encoder_attn_backend="FLASHINFER", limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 2})
P = ("[gMASK]<sop><|user|>\n<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>"
     "Describe the image.<|assistant|>assistant\n")
im = Image.fromarray(np.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 255, (448, 448, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
print(llm.generate([{"prompt": P, "multi_modal_data": {"image": im}}],
                   SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8))[0].outputs[0].text)
```

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_eonly_vit_cudagraph_outputs -k glm4_1v
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The FlashInfer ViT path, `flashinfer_wrapper` (cuDNN batch prefill), needs two things these models did not provide.

1. **`sequence_lengths`.**
   - GLM-4.1V's `prepare_encoder_metadata` already computes it, but the vision transformer never passes it to its blocks.
   - GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash do not compute it in eager mode either. They also build plain `cu_seqlens` there, rather than FlashInfer's offset layout from `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`.
2. **The `v` layout.**
   - `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens` gives q/k token offsets of `hidden_size` and v offsets of `3 * hidden_size`. It expects `v` to be a view into the fused qkv output, as in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL.
   - The GLM attention made `v` contiguous, so its token stride was `hidden_size`. Every sequence after the first then read `v` at three times its real offset.

**Fix.**
- Thread `sequence_lengths` through the GLM vision attention and blocks.
- Keep `v` as a view: `.contiguous()` now applies only to `q` and `k`, which RoPE copies anyway.
- On the eager paths, build FlashInfer's metadata when FlashInfer is selected:
  - GLM-5.3-Flash reuses its existing `prepare_encoder_metadata`;
  - GLM-OCR calls the same `MMEncoderAttention` helpers inline, because its inherited `prepare_encoder_metadata` needs position embeddings that GLM-OCR removes.
- Other backends keep their existing code paths.

**Not covered.** GLM-5.3-Flash with encoder CUDA graphs was not run end to end: the full checkpoint was not available. Its graph path uses the same metadata keys as GLM-4.1V, which was tested.

**Related.** #65453 aligns FlashInfer's `cu_seqlens` between capture and replay for GLM and Kimi-K2.5. It touches different lines and composes with this PR; the graph results above hold with and without it.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds FlashInfer ViT support for the GLM vision encoders. #65453 assumes FlashInfer already runs on these models.

title: [Perf] Vectorize silu_and_mul_per_block_quant for large inputs
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` launches one 128-thread block per (token, group). Each thread issues one 2-byte load, and the group max is a shared-memory tree reduction. At prefill sizes the kernel runs at ~0.9 TB/s on H200. It is therefore 1.3-2.2x *slower* than the unfused `silu_and_mul` + `per_token_group_quant_fp8` pair it replaces.

This PR adds a vectorized variant (16B loads, warp-shuffle reduction, 8B stores) for large inputs. The existing kernel stays for small inputs, where it has lower latency. Both produce bitwise-identical results.

## Claims

- At >= 16k rows the fused kernel is 2.0-2.45x faster than before, and now 8-53% faster than the unfused pair. At <= 64 rows (decode) it is unchanged. See the table below.
- Paths that use the fused kernel today get faster prefill:
  - the Triton FP8 MoE with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0`;
  - the `SiluMul+BlockQuant` compile fusion, where it matches.
- Prerequisite for #65794, which enables the fused path by default (superseding #64906 and #43399). With the old kernel, that change costs -3.8% prefill on Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8.

## Validation

**Kernel:** H200, bf16 in, fp8 out, group 128, CUDA-graph timed, p10 µs.

| 2I | rows | unfused (silu_and_mul + group quant) | fused, main | fused, this PR | vs main |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 8 | 3.80 | 1.87 | **1.84** | 1.02x |
| 512 | 64 | 4.02 | 2.17 | **2.00** | 1.08x |
| 512 | 512 | 4.51 | 2.70 | **2.53** | 1.07x |
| 512 | 4096 | 7.49 | 7.54 | **4.63** | 1.63x |
| 512 | 16384 | 18.77 | 23.88 | **12.04** | 1.98x |
| 512 | 65536 | 64.88 | 98.58 | **42.49** | 2.32x |
| 1536 | 8 | 3.88 | 1.88 | **1.91** | 0.98x |
| 1536 | 64 | 4.05 | 2.07 | **2.07** | 1.00x |
| 1536 | 512 | 4.59 | 3.94 | **3.29** | 1.20x |
| 1536 | 4096 | 10.98 | 18.25 | **9.48** | 1.93x |
| 1536 | 16384 | 36.93 | 74.68 | **32.52** | 2.30x |
| 1536 | 65536 | 133.29 | 292.75 | **121.94** | 2.40x |
| 4096 | 8 | 3.97 | 1.98 | **1.97** | 1.01x |
| 4096 | 64 | 4.18 | 2.54 | **2.53** | 1.00x |
| 4096 | 512 | 5.95 | 7.38 | **4.60** | 1.60x |
| 4096 | 4096 | 25.55 | 48.17 | **22.28** | 2.16x |
| 4096 | 16384 | 91.15 | 197.16 | **82.37** | 2.39x |
| 4096 | 65536 | 349.48 | 783.51 | **320.24** | 2.45x |
| 24576 | 8 | 5.73 | 2.32 | **2.31** | 1.00x |
| 24576 | 64 | 6.37 | 5.98 | **3.95** | 1.51x |
| 24576 | 512 | 20.94 | 34.80 | **17.11** | 2.03x |
| 24576 | 4096 | 144.98 | 293.35 | **121.90** | 2.41x |
| 24576 | 16384 | 560.98 | 1166.89 | **478.78** | 2.44x |

**End to end:** `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8`, H200 TP1, `--moe-backend auto` (Triton), `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0` (the configuration where main already uses the fused kernel). Two runs per arm, interleaved.

| | prefill in tok/s | mixed out tok/s | TPOT c1 | TPOT c8 | TPOT c32 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main (run 1 / run 2) | 65,752 / 64,061 | 7,630 / 7,781 | 3.92 / 3.90 | 5.86 / 5.85 | 8.33 / 8.54 |
| this PR (run 1 / run 2) | **67,634 / 69,375** | 7,855 / 7,829 | 3.92 / 3.90 | 5.89 / 5.87 | 8.45 / 8.24 |

Prefill is +5.6% (mean of two), mixed +1.7%, and decode unchanged. Workloads, all `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`:
- prefill: 4096 in / 1 out, concurrency 64, 256 prompts
- mixed: 1024 / 512, concurrency 128
- decode: 1024 / 256 at concurrency 1/8/32

With the default `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1` the Triton MoE path does not use the fused kernel on main, so this PR is a no-op there today.

**Tests:**
- New `test_silu_and_mul_per_block_quant_vec_matches_scalar`: the vectorized path vs the scalar path, forced by a 2-byte-misaligned view of the same input. It asserts bitwise equality over bf16/fp16, fp8/int8, group sizes 64/128, and both scale layouts.
- The existing reference tests already hit the vectorized path through their large shapes (512x5120, 256x14336, and the int32-offset-overflow case).
- `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_silu_mul_block_quant.py`: 347 passed (331 on main, plus the 16 new cases).
- `tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_{,manual_}fusion.py`: 126 passed, the same as main.

## Details

**Mapping:** each group is handled by `group_size / 8` lanes (16 for group 128), each owning 8 contiguous elements of gate and up. The max is reduced with `__shfl_xor_sync` over those lanes, and lane 0 writes the scale.

**Dispatch:** the vectorized kernel is used for 16-bit inputs with 16B-aligned input and 8B-aligned output, when `num_tokens * num_groups >= 3072`. The threshold is measured: at <= 2048 groups the one-block-per-group kernel is ~0.4-0.9 µs faster, and above ~3072 groups the vectorized one wins. Misaligned views fall back to the existing kernel.

**Arithmetic:** identical to the existing kernel (`gate * (1 / (1 + exp(-gate))) * up`, `max(amax / qmax, min_scale)`, `x / scale`). The file is not built with `--use_fast_math`.

**Overlaps:**
- #62386 edits the same file (TMA-aligned scale stride). The changes are orthogonal, but whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- #43399 (UE8M0 option) also touches this kernel; the vectorized variant takes the same template flags if both land.

**Duplicate check:** no open PR changes this kernel's performance.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek-V4] Share the target embedding with the MTP drafter under PP
author: xsxszab
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix low draft acceptance with DeepSeek-V4 MTP under pipeline parallelism by sharing the target's input embedding with the drafter. This uses the existing embedding-sharing mechanism, as in [#58648](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58648).

## Claims

- Restores PP2 draft acceptance from 0.030 to 0.820, matching the PP1 baseline.
- Maintains comparable GSM8K accuracy: 0.949 with the fix versus 0.948 on main.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on B300, TP2 + EP, MegaMoE, MRV2, and MTP with 2 speculative tokens.

| Configuration | GSM8K accuracy | Draft acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| PP1, main | 0.947 | 0.820 |
| PP2, main | 0.948 | 0.030 |
| PP2, this PR | 0.949 | 0.820 |

GSM8K: 1,319 questions, 5-shot. Draft acceptance is total accepted tokens divided by total drafted tokens over the evaluation.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative_config.method=mtp \
  --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens=2

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
```

Use `--pipeline-parallel-size 1` for the PP1 baseline.

`pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k may_use_target_embed`: **2 passed**. Without the fix, the DeepSeek-V4 case fails because `may_use_target_embed` is `False`; the OPT control passes in both versions.

## Details

The checkpoint contains no separate MTP embedding. Under PP, the NVIDIA `DeepSeekV4MTP` does not declare `has_own_embed_tokens`, so the target's last stage omits its embedding and `maybe_share_target_embed` returns early. The drafter uses an unloaded embedding, causing almost every draft token to be rejected.

Setting `has_own_embed_tokens = False` enables both parts of the existing mechanism: the registry marks the drafter as `may_use_target_embed`, causing the target's last PP stage to load the embedding, and the drafter then shares that module. The retained embedding is TP-sharded (0.49 GiB per GPU at TP2 in this setup).

The change and registry regression test cover the NVIDIA implementation. Related PRs address other models: [#63141](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63141) adds an error for DeepSeek-V3/V3.2 MTP, and [#62903](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62903) fixes Inkling MTP.
