title: [Perf][Core] Reduce per-block CPU cost of KV block allocation and caching
author: njhill
body:
## Overview

Reduces the per-block Python work on the scheduler's main thread when an async KV load starts, is promoted to running, and finishes. These costs grow linearly with prompt length, and on a DP decode instance a slow `schedule()` on one rank holds up the per-step all-reduce.

Related: #61725 limits load starts per step to contain this cost; this makes each load cheaper. #64379 and #65285 target the repeated reservation sum, which is a separate cost.

## Claims

- For a 140K-token request, start + promote + finish CPU time drops about 50% on a DeepSeek-V4.1-shaped KV layout (2.66 to 1.34 ms) and about 45% with one group at block size 16 (10.55 to 5.79 ms).
- Source changes are net neutral in size (+51/-49 lines), and two properties are removed.
- No behaviour change intended. These paths are shared by all requests, so non-P/D traffic benefits too.

**Not yet shown:** an end-to-end improvement. These are scheduler-only numbers, with no real P/D run, so the effect on `schedule()` time and GPU wait in serving is unmeasured.

## Validation

### Timing

Real `Scheduler` and NIXL scheduler connector, with no GPU or transfer. GB200 host (aarch64), Python 3.12, 32 requests per run. Each value is the median of 3 rounds, each round being the median of 5 runs, interleaved with the baseline on one node. Spread between rounds was about 1-5%. ms per request, 140K tokens:

| Phase | DSv4.1 layout, before | After | Change | One group, block size 16, before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Start, fresh blocks | 0.71 | 0.33 | -54% | 2.60 | 1.03 | -60% |
| Promote to running | 1.01 | 0.65 | -36% | 5.97 | 3.76 | -37% |
| Finish | 0.95 | 0.36 | -62% | 1.98 | 1.00 | -50% |
| **Start + promote + finish** | **2.66** | **1.34** | **-50%** | **10.55** | **5.79** | **-45%** |
| Start, evicting cached blocks | 0.99 | 0.72 | -27% | 5.43 | 4.51 | -17% |

The "DSv4.1 layout" is a hand-built model of the KV groups read from the code: compressed MLA at 128 (SM10x), MLA sliding window at 32, one ring block at 8, hash block size 32. **The 128-token window and single compressed group are assumptions**, not confirmed from a real startup log.

These numbers predate the final `get_new_blocks` loop split, which was only measured in isolation: 8,750 fresh blocks, caching on and metrics off, 2.75 to 1.98 ms (-28%), faster in 6 of 6 paired rounds on a noisy x86 laptop with Python 3.13. Treat that size as approximate. The table above is therefore, if anything, slightly conservative for fresh starts.

### Tests

Run on the GB200 cluster against `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`, `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache`, `test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `test_deferred_block_free.py`, `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`, `test_contiguous_kv_packing.py`, `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit`.

- 19 tests fail on both this change and the baseline when run serially, with none unique to either. The errors sampled were gated models, engine startup and environment problems. **They give no signal here**, and some exercise the block pool (for example `test_cpu_offloading`, `test_tiering_offloading`), so CI results for them matter.
- There was no single clean full run. The full set ran once with the GPU hidden and an incomplete tree (4,048 passed), and failures were then re-run with a GPU and compared against baseline.
- **These runs predate the final `get_new_blocks` loop split**, which has not been through the tests yet. It reads as behaviour-preserving, and CI on this PR will be its first test run.
- The new `test_estimate_cached_tokens_tracks_hashed_prefix_of_each_group` uses a real `KVCacheManager` and passes on both this change and the baseline, as expected for a change that shouldn't alter results.

`ruff` passes. `mypy` was run on the changed files with imports skipped, which is weaker than the repo's hook.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script and commands</summary>

Run from outside the repo root, with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at the checkout:

```bash
# DSv4.1 layout
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= PROF_BLOCK_SIZE=128 PYTHONPATH=<checkout> python prof.py timing dsv41 32 140000
# One group, block size 16
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= PYTHONPATH=<checkout> python prof.py timing one 32 140000
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Async KV load CPU cost: real Scheduler + NIXL scheduler connector, no GPU/transfer.
usage: prof.py timing <config> <n> <tokens> | prof.py cprofile <config> <n> <tokens>
Prints one JSON line of ms/request per phase in timing mode."""
import cProfile, gc, json, logging, os, pstats, sys, time
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS", "1")
import torch
from tests.v1.kv_connector.unit.utils import (create_model_runner_output, create_request,
    create_scheduler, create_vllm_config)
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (CircularBufferSpec, FullAttentionSpec, KVCacheConfig,
    KVCacheGroupSpec, MLAAttentionSpec, SlidingWindowMLASpec, SlidingWindowSpec)
logging.disable(logging.WARNING)
BS = int(os.environ.get("PROF_BLOCK_SIZE", "16"))

SWA_BS = 32; RING_BS = 8; WINDOW = 128  # DSv4.1 layout; WINDOW is an assumption

def build_dsv41(n, tokens):
    """DeepSeek-V4.1 KV layout: compressed MLA at BS (backend-chosen), MLA SWA fixed at 32, one ring block."""
    c = create_vllm_config(max_num_seqs=128, max_num_batched_tokens=1280, block_size=BS, max_model_len=tokens+1000)
    common = dict(num_kv_heads=1, head_size=512, dtype=torch.uint8)
    num_blocks = (n+1)*(tokens//BS + 2 + WINDOW//SWA_BS + 4)
    kcc = KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=num_blocks, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=[
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["mla"], MLAAttentionSpec(block_size=BS, **common)),
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["swa"], SlidingWindowMLASpec(block_size=SWA_BS, sliding_window=WINDOW, **common)),
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["ring"], CircularBufferSpec(block_size=RING_BS, head_size_v=0, **common)),
    ])
    assert [g.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable for g in kcc.kv_cache_groups][:2] == [True, True]
    return create_scheduler(c, num_blocks=num_blocks, kv_cache_config=kcc, hash_block_size=SWA_BS)

def build(config, n, tokens):
    if config == "dsv41":
        return build_dsv41(n, tokens)
    c = create_vllm_config(max_num_seqs=128, max_num_batched_tokens=1280, block_size=BS, max_model_len=tokens+1000)
    per_req = tokens // BS + 2
    if config == "one":
        return create_scheduler(c, num_blocks=(n+1)*per_req)
    assert config == "swa"
    # Full attention + a sliding window group: the multi-group shape.
    num_blocks = 2*(n+1)*per_req
    kw = dict(block_size=BS, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=1, dtype=torch.float32)
    kcc = KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=num_blocks, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=[
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["full"], FullAttentionSpec(**kw)),
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["swa"], SlidingWindowSpec(sliding_window=128*BS, **kw)),
    ])
    return create_scheduler(c, num_blocks=num_blocks, kv_cache_config=kcc)

def reqs(n, tokens, hash_bs=None):
    return [create_request(block_size=hash_bs or BS, num_tokens=tokens, max_tokens=1, do_remote_prefill=True,
                           num_remote_blocks=tokens//BS) for _ in range(n)]

class Phases:
    """Runs start -> promote -> finish -> start-over-evictable, each via `run(name, fn)`."""
    def __init__(self, run, config, n, tokens):
        r = build(config, n, tokens)
        hb = SWA_BS if config == "dsv41" else None
        rs = reqs(n, tokens, hb); rs2 = reqs(n, tokens, hb)
        gc.collect(); gc.freeze()  # as the engine does at startup
        for q in rs: r.add_request(q)
        out = run("start_fresh", r.schedule)
        assert len(r.running) == 0 and sum(q.status.name == "WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS" for q in rs) == n, "not all started"
        r.update_from_output(out, create_model_runner_output([], finished_recving={q.request_id for q in rs}))
        out = run("promote", r.schedule)
        assert len(r.running) == n
        run("finish", lambda: r.update_from_output(out, create_model_runner_output(list(r.running))))
        for q in rs2: r.add_request(q)
        run("start_evict", r.schedule)
        started = sum(q.status.name == "WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS" for q in rs2)
        assert started == n, f"started {started}"

def timing(config, n, tokens, reps=5):
    res = {}
    for _ in range(reps):
        def run(name, fn):
            gc.disable()
            t = time.perf_counter(); o = fn(); d = time.perf_counter()-t
            gc.enable()
            res.setdefault(name, []).append(d*1e3/n)
            return o
        Phases(run, config, n, tokens); gc.unfreeze()
    print(json.dumps({"config": config, "n": n, "tokens": tokens, **{k: round(sorted(v)[len(v)//2], 3) for k, v in res.items()}}))

def prof(config, n, tokens):
    def run(name, fn):
        p = cProfile.Profile(); p.enable(); o = fn(); p.disable()
        print(f"\n## cProfile {config} {name} (n={n}, overhead inflates Python calls)")
        st = pstats.Stats(p, stream=sys.stdout); st.sort_stats("tottime").print_stats(14)
        return o
    Phases(run, config, n, tokens)

mode, config, n, tokens = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
(timing if mode == "timing" else prof)(config, n, tokens)
```

</details>

## Details

| Change | Why it's cheaper | Relies on |
|---|---|---|
| `block_hash` and `block_hash_num_tokens` become plain fields | No Python call per read in hot loops | Fields are now publicly writable. In `vllm/`, they are set through `set_block_hash`, `reset_hash` and one constructor call in the UMBP connector |
| Skip eviction for unhashed blocks in `get_new_blocks`; early return in `_remove_cached_block_hashes` | Most allocated blocks were never cached | A block only has secondary hashes alongside a primary one |
| Separate loops per mode in `get_new_blocks` | No per-block metrics check on the default path | |
| `_insert_block_hash` only checks `contain` when the block already has a hash | One dict lookup instead of two in the common case | A block with no hash has no cache entries |
| Pack the group id once per `cache_full_blocks` call | No `to_bytes` and helper call per block | |
| Reverse scan in `estimate_cached_tokens` | Stops at the last hashed block instead of visiting them all | Hash coverage never decreases along a block table, including partial and Mamba entries |
| `len([...])` instead of `sum(<genexpr>)` in the NIXL pull scheduler | No generator resume per block | |

**Tradeoffs:**
- With `kv_cache_metrics` on (off by default), every block still takes the eviction call so `on_block_evicted` can run, so that path gains less. That mode wasn't measured in the full benchmark, and the isolated measurement above was inconclusive for it.
- `get_new_blocks` now has three near-identical loops.

**The block size assumption matters for evaluating this work.** The 8,750-blocks-per-request figure comes from a block size 16, single-group setup, including part 1 of #61725. By my reading of the code, DSv4.1 on NVIDIA uses 128 or 64 for its main group, chosen by the backend, so a real load costs about a quarter of the block-size-16 figure before this change. For the same reason, changing the default in #63231 shouldn't affect DSv4.1 on NVIDIA. At block size 64 with one group, this change still gives about -42% (3.04 to 1.75 ms).

title: [Perf][Frontend] Write run-batch JSON responses without parsing them back
author: inc-jeong
body:
## Overview `vllm run-batch` parses every buffered JSON response body (`/v1/embeddings`, `/score`, `/rerank`) back into the response union and dumps it again to write the output line. This PR writes a successful JSON body as is instead. Follow-up to #63189, which made run-batch accept these buffered bodies. ## Claims - Writing one `/v1/embeddings` output line takes 4.8× less event-loop time for 128-dim embeddings (85.3 → 17.9 µs) and 6.4× less for 512-dim ones (188.1 → 29.4 µs), measured on main. - Embedding batches are bound by the frontend event loop, so this shows up end to end. On one H100 with a batch of 864,891 short inputs, the same change on v0.33.0 cut the wall time by 12.5% (a 128-dim embedding model) and 18% (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 512 dims). - Output values do not change. Only the number formatting can differ, because the line now keeps the handler's formatting instead of pydantic's: orjson for embeddings (e.g. `0.000007177709` instead of `7.177709e-6`), `json.dumps` for score and rerank (e.g. `1e-06` instead of `1e-6`). - Behavior changes: - A NaN or Inf embedding, which orjson writes as `null`, is now written as is with status 200, as the online `/v1/embeddings` server returns it. On main it became a "Request must not be sent in stream mode" error line. - A `Response` with a status other than 200 or a media type other than JSON, or a return value of any other type, now gets an error line that says so ("Unexpected response status code: …", "Unsupported response media type: …", "Unsupported response type") instead of the stream mode error. No run-batch handler returns these today. ## Validation **Tests.** - `test_batch_embedding_json_body_is_written_as_is` builds the body the way `EmbeddingServing` does (a float32 array written by orjson, with a NaN) and checks that the line carries it verbatim with no error. The parsing path would rewrite `0.000007177709` as `7.177709e-6` and reject the `null`. - `test_batch_json_responses` checks the written line for embedding and score bodies, from both `JSONResponse` and `create_json_response`. - `test_batch_rejects_unsupported_responses` covers the error lines: `StreamingResponse`, async generator, non-200 status, non-JSON media type, other types. - `test_requests_and_responses_reuse_type_adapters` returns a 400 `JSONResponse`, so it now expects the status code error. ``` # main (d8588b71ff), this PR's tests with the fix reverted $ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k "json_body or unsupported_responses" FAILED ...::test_batch_embedding_json_body_is_written_as_is FAILED ...::test_batch_rejects_unsupported_responses[status] FAILED ...::test_batch_rejects_unsupported_responses[media_type] FAILED ...::test_batch_rejects_unsupported_responses[other] 4 failed, 2 passed # this PR $ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k "json_response or json_body or unsupported_responses or type_adapters" 11 passed, 62 deselected ``` The whole file gives 61 passed and 12 failed locally, against 54 passed and 12 failed on main. The same 12 tests fail on both. They launch `vllm run-batch` with a model, which needs a vLLM build I don't have on macOS, so they are left to the Entrypoints Unit CI step. **Microbenchmark.** Apple M1 Pro, CPU only. `run_request` and the output line write for 3,000 responses per round, 7 alternating rounds, median with the range in brackets. The handler returns what `EmbeddingServing._openai_json_response` builds for `encoding_format=float`: `create_json_response()` of a dict with a float32 ndarray embedding, so both columns include that serialization. All 3,000 lines parse to the same values (ids aside) before and after, with no error lines. | embedding dims | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | 128 | 85.3 µs [83.5–103.6] | 17.9 µs [17.7–22.4] | | 512 | 188.1 µs [184.9–192.0] | 29.4 µs [28.9–32.7] | **End to end.** I have not run end to end on main. On v0.33.0 (before #63189, so both arms carry a small patch that parses these bodies with `json.loads` + `validate_python`), I applied an equivalent write-as-is patch and ran one embeddings batch file: 864,891 lines, averaging 15–21 prompt tokens depending on the tokenizer, `max_inflight` default. One H100 per run, 3 runs per arm on the same node. | model | v0.33.0 | write as is | output check | |---|---|---|---| | 128-dim embedding model | 680 s [671–686] | 595 s [588–606] (−12.5%) | values identical on the first 2,000 lines | | Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (512 dims) | 751 s [747–757] | 616 s [611–622] (−18%) | values identical on the first 2,000 lines | Event-loop CPU per request fell from 0.61 to 0.51 ms and from 0.68 to 0.53 ms. GPU utilization was 5–10%, so the loop was the bottleneck. On main the response path is a bit heavier than on v0.33.0. `validate_json` is slower than `json.loads` + `validate_python` for these float-heavy bodies, and the union has gained `CompletionResponse`. So the gain on main should be at least as large.
Benchmark script (python bench_run_batch_response.py before/run_batch.py after/run_batch.py) ```python """Per-response cost of writing a /v1/embeddings output line in run-batch. Usage (from the vLLM repo root): python bench_run_batch_response.py The handler returns the body the embeddings server builds for encoding_format=float: create_json_response() of a dict whose embedding is a float32 ndarray (EmbeddingServing._openai_json_response). """ import asyncio import importlib.util import json import statistics import sys import time import numpy as np import vllm.entrypoints.launchers # noqa: F401 (parent package) from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.embed.protocol import ( EmbeddingResponse, EmbeddingResponseData, ) from vllm.entrypoints.serve.engine.protocol import UsageInfo from vllm.entrypoints.serve.utils.api_utils import create_json_response def load(name, path): spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( f"vllm.entrypoints.launchers.{name}", path ) mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) spec.loader.exec_module(mod) return mod def body_dict(dim, rng): v = rng.standard_normal(dim).astype(np.float32) v /= np.linalg.norm(v) item = EmbeddingResponseData(index=0, embedding=[]).model_dump() item["embedding"] = v resp = EmbeddingResponse( id="embd-x", created=0, model="vllm", data=[], usage=UsageInfo(prompt_tokens=16, total_tokens=16), ).model_dump() resp["data"] = [item] return resp def write_line(output): to_line = getattr(output, "to_json_line", None) return to_line() if to_line is not None else output.model_dump_json() async def run(rb, payloads, request): it = iter(payloads) async def handler(_body): return create_json_response(next(it)) t0 = time.perf_counter() lines = [write_line(await rb.run_request(handler, request)) for _ in payloads] return lines, (time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(payloads) * 1e6 def main(): mods = {"before": load("rb_before", sys.argv[1]), "after": load("rb_after", sys.argv[2])} n, rounds = 3000, 7 for dim in (128, 512): rng = np.random.default_rng(0) payloads = [body_dict(dim, rng) for _ in range(n)] times = {k: [] for k in mods} lines = {} for r in range(rounds): for name, rb in (mods.items() if r % 2 == 0 else reversed(mods.items())): request = rb.BatchRequestInput.model_validate_json( json.dumps( { "custom_id": "k", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "vllm", "input": "x", "dimensions": dim}, } ) ) out, per = asyncio.run(run(rb, payloads, request)) times[name].append(per) lines[name] = out def values(line): d = json.loads(line) d.pop("id") d["response"].pop("request_id") return d same = sum(values(a) == values(b) for a, b in zip(lines["before"], lines["after"])) errors = {k: sum(json.loads(x)["error"] is not None for x in v) for k, v in lines.items()} med = {k: statistics.median(v) for k, v in times.items()} rng_ = {k: (min(v), max(v)) for k, v in times.items()} print( f"dim={dim} before={med['before']:.1f}us [{rng_['before'][0]:.1f}-{rng_['before'][1]:.1f}] " f"after={med['after']:.1f}us [{rng_['after'][0]:.1f}-{rng_['after'][1]:.1f}] " f"speedup={med['before'] / med['after']:.1f}x same_values={same}/{n} errors={errors}" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
## Details **Root cause.** Since #58660, the embeddings server returns a buffered orjson `Response`, and #63189 made `run_request` parse it with `_ALL_RESPONSE_ADAPTER.validate_json` so the line is not reported as an error. Score and rerank `JSONResponse` bodies took the same parse. Parsing validates every float of every embedding against the response union, and `model_dump_json` writes them all again. In an embeddings batch this runs on the event loop for every line. **Why skipping the parse is safe.** No run-batch handler needs it, as found in review: - Chat, completions, transcriptions and translations return the response models or `ErrorResponse`, which are written as before. - Embeddings (`float`, `base64`) returns an orjson `Response`, and `bytes` returns a `StreamingResponse`, which stays an error line. - Score and rerank return `JSONResponse(content=response.model_dump())`. - Pooling handlers raise on errors, and `run_request` turns the exception into an `ErrorResponse`, so no handler returns a non-200 JSON body. A 200 JSON body is built from the response models, so parsing it back only re-checks what was just serialized. The parse only fails for a non-finite embedding: orjson writes NaN and Inf as `null`, which the models reject. That failure was not handled on purpose. The line fell through to the "Request must not be sent in stream mode" error, while the online server returns the same body with status 200, and run-batch also wrote `null` when the handler returned `EmbeddingResponse` objects (pydantic writes NaN as `null` too). This PR writes these bodies as the online server returns them. **Shape of the result.** `run_request` returns early for each response type, as suggested in review. For a JSON body line, `BatchRequestOutput.response.body` is `None`. The handler's bytes are kept in a private attribute and spliced in by `BatchRequestOutput.to_json_line()`, which the writer now calls instead of `model_dump_json()`. Lines without a raw body are serialized exactly as before. `run_request` is internal to run-batch, and the output file is the contract, which the tests check. `_ALL_RESPONSE_ADAPTER` is removed. **Scope.** I measured `/v1/embeddings` only. Score and rerank bodies take the same path now, with one float per document, so I expect a smaller gain there. **Overlap.** #65670 (completion-order output) touches the same `model_dump_json()` write line in `dispatch_batch`, so whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase. **Duplicate check.** As of 2026-11-05, open PR searches for `run_batch orjson`, `run-batch validate_json`, `run-batch embeddings response` and `run-batch output line` return nothing that changes this path. Among open PRs touching run-batch, #65670, #65029, #64102, #63848, #62895, #61145 and #51859 do not change the response conversion. ---

title: [Kernel][Perf] Fused GDN MTP: Support DSpark K=8 and use idle SMs at small batch sizes
author: tomasruizt
body:
## Overview This PR makes two changes to the fused GDN MTP decode kernel: 1. **K=8 support:** DSpark K=8 (9 tokens per request) fell back to the slower Triton path. The kernel now handles 9 tokens. Overlaps with #53070. 2. **Split-V:** at small batch sizes, each value head is split over a cluster of 2 or 4 thread blocks to use idle SMs (SM90+). With Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and DSpark K=8, this PR increases output throughput over main by 18% on B300 and 13% on H100 with a single request. With 8 or more concurrent requests, the gain is 6% to 9% on B300 (measured up to 128 requests) and 2% to 6% on H100 (measured up to 32 requests). ## Claims - DSpark K=8 decode steps now use the fused kernel. On main they silently fall back to the Triton delta-rule + gated RMSNorm path in every GDN layer, because the kernel accepts at most 8 tokens. - The cluster split (SM90+) cuts the fused kernel time at 1 request from 22.3µs to 10.2µs on B300 and from 26.2µs to 14.3µs on H100. From 8 requests on, where it does not split, the kernel is 0.4% to 0.9% faster. It also speeds up K=7 by 8% at c1, which already used the fused kernel. - MTP3 does not regress: output throughput rises 2% to 3% at c1 and c2, and matches main from c4 on. - Outputs unchanged: GSM8K and acceptance length match main. ## E2E Benchmarks Serving benchmark. main is `5225a1f17f` (main on 2026-11-04), and this PR is based on it. B300 uses the bf16 model, H100 uses `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (bf16 does not fit): ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --language-model-only \ --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8}' ``` Client: AIPerf 0.13, config and command below. Output tok/s is measured over the steady window, which opens once the first c requests complete. Every reported point passed the validity checks (no errors, preemptions or queueing, server saturated).
AIPerf config and command One run per (repeat, concurrency) cell against the same server. The second repeat goes through the concurrencies in reverse order. `throughput_1k.jsonl` is the SPEED-Bench throughput 1k split. On H100, `model` is `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`. ```yaml schemaVersion: "2.0" randomSeed: 42 benchmark: model: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B endpoint: url: http://127.0.0.1:8000 type: chat streaming: true use_server_token_count: true timeout: 120 extra: temperature: 0 max_completion_tokens: 1024 chat_template_kwargs: enable_thinking: false tokenizer: name: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B datasets: - name: main type: file path: throughput_1k.jsonl format: speed_bench_throughput_1k sampling: shuffle random_seed: 42 phases: - name: profiling type: concurrency concurrency: C duration: D grace_period: 120 server_metrics: enabled: true urls: [http://127.0.0.1:8000/metrics] formats: [json] artifacts: dir: artifacts/rR-cC summary: [json] records: [jsonl] runtime: ui: none ``` ```bash duration() { d=30; l=32; while [ $1 -gt $l ]; do d=$((d + 10)); l=$((l * 2)); done; echo $d; } for R in 1 2 3; do CS="1 2 4 8 16 32 64 128 256"; [ $R = 2 ] && CS="256 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1" for C in $CS; do sed "s/concurrency: C/concurrency: $C/; s/duration: D/duration: $(duration $C)/; s|artifacts/rR-cC|artifacts/r$R-c$C|" aiperf.yaml > cell.yaml aiperf profile --config cell.yaml done done ```

B300 table, output tok/s and mean TPOT B300, K=8, median of 6 runs per variant (2 server sessions × 3 repeats, each session on a different GPU). c256 is not reported: at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` the server holds only ~180 concurrent requests, so c256 queues and preempts for both main and this PR. Our estimate is that the GDN state, kept for all 9 tokens of each request at K=8, dominates the per-request memory. | K | Concurrency | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | Change | main TPOT ms | this PR TPOT ms | Change | Speedup drivers | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | 8 | 1 | 476.0 | 561.5 | +18.0% | 2.01 | 1.72 | -14.3% | K=8 support + Split-V | | 8 | 2 | 832.6 | 972.2 | +16.8% | 2.29 | 1.93 | -15.8% | K=8 support + Split-V | | 8 | 4 | 1380.3 | 1492.7 | +8.1% | 2.74 | 2.56 | -6.5% | K=8 support + Split-V | | 8 | 8 | 2052.2 | 2226.3 | +8.5% | 3.72 | 3.39 | -8.7% | K=8 support | | 8 | 16 | 3154.2 | 3357.7 | +6.5% | 4.66 | 4.41 | -5.4% | K=8 support | | 8 | 32 | 4465.0 | 4751.9 | +6.4% | 6.70 | 6.25 | -6.6% | K=8 support | | 8 | 64 | 6223.5 | 6754.9 | +8.5% | 9.34 | 8.57 | -8.2% | K=8 support | | 8 | 128 | 8029.2 | 8641.2 | +7.6% | 13.90 | 12.98 | -6.6% | K=8 support | B300, K=7, median of 3 repeats per variant. At K=7 main already uses the fused kernel, so only Split-V can change the result. c256 is not reported, for the same reason as K=8. | K | Concurrency | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | Change | main TPOT ms | this PR TPOT ms | Change | Speedup drivers | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | 7 | 1 | 542.6 | 585.5 | +7.9% | 1.78 | 1.65 | -7.5% | Split-V | | 7 | 2 | 937.2 | 985.7 | +5.2% | 2.03 | 1.90 | -6.1% | Split-V | | 7 | 4 | 1576.7 | 1597.8 | +1.3% | 2.43 | 2.38 | -2.1% | Split-V | | 7 | 8 | 2327.6 | 2309.4 | -0.8% | 3.23 | 3.26 | +0.8% | - | | 7 | 16 | 3489.6 | 3479.5 | -0.3% | 4.28 | 4.27 | -0.3% | - | | 7 | 32 | 4997.1 | 4978.5 | -0.4% | 5.92 | 5.93 | +0.3% | - | | 7 | 64 | 7022.4 | 6982.8 | -0.6% | 8.25 | 8.27 | +0.3% | - | | 7 | 128 | 9164.1 | 9064.6 | -1.1% | 12.32 | 12.43 | +0.8% | - |
H100 table, output tok/s and mean TPOT H100, median of 6 runs per variant (2 server sessions × 3 repeats, main and this PR each ran once on each of two GPUs, in opposite order). c64 and above are not reported: the server holds only ~44 concurrent requests at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, so those points queue and preempt for both main and this PR. | K | Concurrency | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | Change | main TPOT ms | this PR TPOT ms | Change | Speedup drivers | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | 8 | 1 | 363.9 | 410.1 | +12.7% | 2.49 | 2.25 | -9.6% | K=8 support + Split-V | | 8 | 2 | 606.8 | 650.3 | +7.2% | 3.00 | 2.80 | -6.7% | K=8 support + Split-V | | 8 | 4 | 972.4 | 1041.0 | +7.0% | 3.73 | 3.54 | -4.9% | K=8 support + Split-V | | 8 | 8 | 1366.3 | 1446.5 | +5.9% | 5.52 | 5.17 | -6.4% | K=8 support | | 8 | 16 | 1934.0 | 1981.7 | +2.5% | 7.50 | 7.29 | -2.7% | K=8 support | | 8 | 32 | 2606.1 | 2656.7 | +1.9% | 10.37 | 10.17 | -1.9% | K=8 support |
## Split-V Microbenchmarks Both columns time the fused kernel `gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp_kernel`. Main rejects 9 tokens, so the main column uses main's kernel with only the 9-token support of `2a9f894eab`, and the PR column is the PR head `d756458d61`. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B TP1 shapes, 9 tokens per request, fp32 state read from HBM, CUDA graph replay, median of 3 repeats. | GPU | Requests | Tokens | main + K=8 support | this PR | Delta µs | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | B300 | 1 | 9 | 22.3µs | 10.2µs | -12.1µs | -54.2% | | B300 | 2 | 18 | 22.6µs | 13.5µs | -9.1µs | -40.1% | | B300 | 4 | 36 | 24.1µs | 21.4µs | -2.6µs | -11.0% | | B300 | 8 | 72 | 36.2µs | 36.1µs | -0.2µs | -0.4% | | B300 | 32 | 288 | 123.9µs | 123.3µs | -0.6µs | -0.5% | | H100 | 1 | 9 | 26.2µs | 14.3µs | -11.9µs | -45.3% | | H100 | 2 | 18 | 28.0µs | 23.6µs | -4.5µs | -15.9% | | H100 | 4 | 36 | 36.3µs | 34.8µs | -1.4µs | -3.9% | | H100 | 8 | 72 | 67.0µs | 66.4µs | -0.6µs | -0.9% | | H100 | 32 | 288 | 260.5µs | 259.3µs | -1.2µs | -0.5% | From 8 requests on, neither splits. The PR's unsplit kernel is slightly faster there, because `d756458d61` unrolls its token loops. ## MTP3 Benchmarks Main already runs MTP3 (4 tokens per request) through the fused kernel, so this section checks for regressions. Same server command and AIPerf setup as above, with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`. main is `5225a1f17f`, this PR is `d756458d61`.

B300 and H100 tables, output tok/s and mean TPOT Median of 3 repeats per variant, one server session each. c1 and c2 gain from Split-V. The new 4- and 16-request cases cover the split=2 and split=1 paths. The existing cases have at most 3 requests, so they always split on B300 and H100. In CI, `kernels/fla` runs on B200 and `kernels/mamba` on H200 MIG, so both exercise the split path. ## Details **9 tokens.** DSpark K=8 verifies 8 drafts plus the bonus token, so `state_indices` has width 9 and `_can_use_fused_gdn_mtp_decode` rejected it. Raising `kMaxMtpTokens` alone is not enough: the kernel assigned one warp per token and has 8 warps, so the 9th token was skipped. Warps now stride over tokens. Static shared memory at 9 tokens with fp32 state is ~45.6KB, under the 48KB static limit. **Related work.** - #53070 adds the same 9-token support as a separate width-9 template specialization next to the width-8 one. It has had no activity since Aug 31 and predates the move of the kernel to `csrc/gdn/`. This PR raises the cap in place instead (one kernel, warps stride over tokens). The cluster split does not depend on how the 9-token support lands, so it can be rebased onto #53070 if that one is preferred. - benchislett/vllm#8 (draft) extends fused GDN verification to 12 and 16 tokens (K=11 and K=15) on SM107, with a separate wide kernel that is used when the width exceeds `kMaxMtpTokens`. It complements this PR: with both, 9 tokens would use the kernel changed here and 12 or 16 tokens the wide kernel. - #54612 speeds up the Triton spec-decode recurrence for Qwen3-Next, which is the path that DSpark K=8 falls back to on main. This PR moves K=8 off that path to the fused CUDA kernel. **Cluster split.** At small batch sizes the kernel launches one CTA per (request, value head), e.g. 32 CTAs on 148 SMs at batch size 1. On SM90+, each head's V rows are split over a cluster of 2 or 4 CTAs (`blockIdx.z`) while the grid still fits in one wave at 2 CTAs per SM. Each CTA loads and updates its slice of the state. The gated RMSNorm sums the partial sums of squares of the cluster through distributed shared memory, with a final cluster barrier so no CTA exits while others read its shared memory. Without a split, the kernel keeps its single-pass epilogue, so batch sizes of 8 and more are unchanged. On B300 and H100 (HV=32) the split is 4 up to 2 requests, 2 at 4 requests, 1 from 8 requests. **Tradeoffs and limitations.** - The split choice is a host-side heuristic from the SM count, no tuning table. It queries two device attributes on the host per launch, with no GPU sync. - SM80 to SM89 never split. There, the split kernels compile to a trap stub to keep them out of the binary. - Validated on B300 and H100 only. SM100 and SM120 take the same path but were not tested. - Each kernel instantiation now has three split variants. Compiling this file for all 7 target archs (one nvcc 13.0 call with `--compress-mode=size`) takes 71s instead of 36s, and the object grows from 0.41MB to 0.90MB. - Mixed prefill and decode batches still use the unfused path, as before. They are CUDA graphed on main. CC @Jie-Fang @ZJY0516 @gau-nernst @vadiklyutiy @benchislett @BabyDrangoner 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Don't sync when building sparse-attention prefill metadata
author: MrGeva
body:
## Overview

`MiniMaxM3SparseMetadataBuilder.build` zeroes the first prefill `cu_seqlens_k` entry with `prefill_cu_seqlens_k[0] = 0` on CUDA. Assigning a Python scalar to an element of a CUDA tensor is a pageable host-to-device copy, so the host waits for all queued GPU work. The metadata is built while the previous step is still running on the GPU, so every step that contains a prefill stalls the host until the GPU drains. This PR zeroes the element with `prefill_cu_seqlens_k[:1].zero_()`, which ROCm already uses.

## Claims

- **No host sync when building MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention metadata.** Before this PR it is the only synchronizing call in a MiniMax-M3.1 Flash step (torch sync-debug mode, GB300, TP4). It is also why M3.1 cannot run under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on `main`: every request fails at this line.
- **The stall is gone.** Host time of the metadata build with GPU work still queued (GB300):

  | queued GPU work | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | 5 ms | 5.41 ms | 1.34 ms |
  | 20 ms | 20.48 ms | 1.31 ms |
  | 60 ms | 60.43 ms | 1.16 ms |

  With no queued work both take about 1.3 ms, so the difference is the wait.
- **In serving** (MiniMax-M3.1 Flash, GB300, TP4, DSpark K=7, AgentX agentic workload, 1 h per run, 2 runs per arm): host time of the attention-metadata build on steps with a prefill, p90, goes from 3.9–4.2 to about 1.5 ms at concurrency 16 and from 4.5–4.8 to 1.6–1.7 ms at concurrency 32. That serving A/B ran this change together with six other host-overhead changes (#65884, #65885); end-to-end throughput was not measured for this change alone.
- Outputs are unchanged: the tensor gets the same values.

## Validation

- New test `test_sparse_metadata_build_does_not_sync` in `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` builds prefill + decode metadata under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")` and checks `cu_seqlens_k` and the KV block count. It fails on `main` (the sync raises) and passes with this PR. The file already runs in CI.
- **On a `main` build** (nightly wheel for 7871c62b61 plus the Python files of `main` 75f6761497 and this branch, GB300): `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` passed 152 with 49 skipped (all skips are ROCm-only). `main` gives 151 passed / 49 skipped; the new test fails there. A 12-request M3.1 Flash smoke serve (TP4, DSpark K=7, NVFP4 KV cache) completed 12/12. Full GSM8K (1319 questions, c64, greedy, one node, 0 request errors): 0.9636 vs `main` 0.9682. The standard error is about 0.005 per run, and earlier `main` runs of the same configuration scored 0.9651–0.9689. The change does not alter the metadata values.
  - `main` currently fails to load M3.1 (`AttributeError: 'MinimaxM3QKVParallelLinearWithIndexer' object has no attribute 'loaded_shard_ids'`, from #63752). For these serves, both arms got a one-line workaround, `self.loaded_shard_ids = {}` after that layer's `ColumnParallelLinear.__init__`. The workaround is not part of this PR.
- Sync check: an M3.1 Flash serve with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed 12/12 smoke requests with this PR. On `main` it completed 0/12; every request raised at the `prefill_cu_seqlens_k[0] = 0` line.

## Details

- `torch.cumsum(..., out=prefill_cu_seqlens_k[1:])` fills the rest of the tensor, so only element 0 needs zeroing. `[:1].zero_()` launches a fill kernel and does not touch host memory.
- The ROCm branch already did this. The CUDA-only `[0] = 0` branch is removed, so both platforms run the same line.
- Found with torch's sync-debug mode on the eager mixed (prefill + decode) step of M3.1 Flash. That step is not CUDA-graphed, and its host time is on the critical path.
- Size: +3 / −4 source lines in 1 file, plus +38 test lines.

title: [Dependency] Upgrade FlashInfer to 0.7.3
author: lesj0610
body:
## Overview

Upgrade FlashInfer from `0.7.2.post1` to `0.7.3`, with the compatibility fixes the upgrade needs.

## Claims

- Update the `flashinfer-python` pin in `requirements/cuda.txt` to `0.7.3`, keeping the `flashinfer download-kernels` flow that installs the matching `flashinfer-cubin` and `flashinfer-jit-cache` in the Docker image.
- FlashInfer 0.7.3 requires `nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.32.0` and `nvidia-cutlass-dsl>=4.8.0`. The existing `nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.31.0` floor and `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.8.0` pin already allow both, so no other requirement changes.
- FlashInfer 0.7.3 removes `flashinfer.comm.trtllm_alltoall`, which the NVLink two-sided backend used. Without a fix, `has_flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided()` returns `False`, selecting the backend fails the manager's assert, and `test_moe_layer.py` silently drops it. The backend now uses the `NVLinkTwoSidedAlltoAll` wrapper in `flashinfer.moe_ep`, which runs the same prepare, all-to-all-v, and combine kernels.
- The 0.7.3 two-sided combine cannot reshape an empty local batch, which the old combine handled. A rank with no tokens now dispatches one row whose expert id `num_experts` maps to no rank, so it still joins both collectives, and drops that row's result after combine.
- The one-sided dispatch argument `max_tokens_per_rank` is now `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank`; the old keyword raises `TypeError` on 0.7.3.
- 0.7.3 turns on the CFT or Lamport one-sided transport where the platform supports them. The one-sided manager passes `cft=False` and `lamport=False` to keep the current fence transport.
- Supported backends and quantization combinations do not change. The two-sided wrapper takes a per-rank capacity at construction, set to `max_num_batched_tokens` as in one-sided; dispatch still sizes the received rows by the runtime token count.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` on the changed files.
- Imported the changed modules with FlashInfer 0.7.3 and checked the new dispatch, combine, and config signatures.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py` covers both NVLink backends, and `tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py` covers the two-sided manager lifecycle and dispatch/combine, now including an empty rank.

## Details

Based on upstream main `5b62a2853d`. Test updates follow the API changes: the two-sided lifecycle and data tests use the new communication object, the two-sided data test adds an empty-rank case, the one-sided calls pass the renamed argument, the one-sided zero-copy check compares the combine input with the workspace buffer, and `test_moe_layer.py` drops the cleanup of the removed `MoeAlltoAll` cache. No other open PR upgrades FlashInfer to 0.7.3. No associated issue.

title: [Quantization] Avoid importing humming when resolving quantization configs
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Resolving any quantized model's config imports `humming` in the front-end process, even for checkpoints that never use it (e.g. plain FP8). Importing `humming` starts two background build helper processes. This PR makes `utils/humming/schema.py` build its dtype tables lazily, so nothing imports `humming` until a Humming layer actually needs it.

Related: vllm-project/humming#184 skips those helpers when precompiled wheel artifacts are present. This change keeps vLLM from importing `humming` at all in processes that don't use it.

## Claims

- `get_quantization_config(...)` no longer imports `humming` for any quantization method. On current main it does for all of them, leaving 2 helper processes running in the importing process.
- No behavior change on Humming paths: the same dtype tables are built on first use and cached.

## Validation

Before vs. after, resolving `fp8`, `gptq`, `awq`, `compressed-tensors`, `modelopt_fp4`, and `mxfp4` configs:

| | `humming` in `sys.modules` | Humming helper child processes |
|---|---|---|
| main | True | 2 |
| this PR | False | 0 |

Reproduce:
```python
import sys
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import get_quantization_config
get_quantization_config("fp8")
print("humming" in sys.modules)  # main: True, this PR: False
```

Tests on H200 with humming installed:
```
pytest tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_compile.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py tests/config/test_config_generation.py
84 passed, 4 skipped
```

I also directly exercised all four rewritten functions (`weight_schema_to_quant_key`, `input_schema_to_quant_key`, `quant_key_to_input_schema`, `check_and_fallback_input_schema`) and the `moe.py` caller.

I did not add a regression test. It would belong in `tests/quantization`, whose CI job is currently disabled pending the torchao pin; the snippet above checks it.

## Details

The import chain is:

1. `get_quantization_config()` imports every quantization config.
2. Quark's MoE config imports `fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py`, which imports the `utils/humming` package.
3. That package imports `schema.py`, which calls `if has_humming():` at module level.
4. `has_humming()` trial-imports the package rather than only checking `find_spec`.

The two module-level tables become `functools.cache` getters. The two functions that used the module-global `humming_dtypes` now import it locally, next to the `vllm.utils.humming` imports they already had. Workers that actually run Humming layers still import it (and its helpers) as before.

This was found while profiling Humming JIT compile time during vLLM startup.

title: [ROCm][Kernel] Follow-ups to the gfx942 MLA Triton verify kernel
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Run `test_decode_attention_fwd_verify_int64_page_offset` at 128 heads too, so the 64-row QSPLIT path is checked past 2 GiB, and free cached memory before its free-memory gate.
- `verify_num_kv_splits` takes the launch config from `select_verify_config` itself instead of from the caller.
- Replace `VERIFY_DEFAULT_CONFIG` with a private base config that holds only the values both launch configs share.
- Cite ROCm/aiter#6732 in the FP8 V-scale probe and use `_ASM_PADDED_MAX_PS_QLEN` for its qlen bound.
- Fix the `_forward_triton_verify` docstring (only a varlen tail comes back as zeros) and a stale test comment.

These are the non-blocking follow-ups from the review of #62725, plus a few cleanups found by re-reading the merged code. The int64 test used to run only at 16 heads, which always picks the small-tile config, so the QSPLIT path's own page loads were never tested past 2 GiB. With the 128-head case, truncating one QSPLIT page offset to int32 causes an illegal memory access, while the 16-head case still passes. The test's memory gate also counted memory held by the caching allocator as used, so it could skip silently on a busy shard. On the kernel side, `VERIFY_DEFAULT_CONFIG`'s `BLOCK_H`, `BLOCK_N`, `num_warps` and `MIN_SPLIT_LEN` were always overridden, and `verify_num_kv_splits` defaulted to a split length the kernel never uses. Having it read the real launch config means the workspace reservation can't drift from the launch. The launch configs and split counts are identical to `main` over 476,280 shapes (batch, qlen, heads, max length and CU count), so there is no perf or accuracy change.

Tests on MI300X: `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py -k verify` passed 10/10 runs (146 passed each, the int64 cases ran rather than skipped), and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` gave 724 passed, 641 skipped, 0 failed.

title: [CI][KV Offload] Pin GPU block size in test_p2p_cache_reset_with_absent_decoder
author: zhenwei-intel
body:
## Overview

Pin the GPU KV block size to 16 in `test_p2p_cache_reset_with_absent_decoder`. #63231 changed the default `--block-size` from 16 to 64, so this test now fails deterministically at engine startup. Seen on Intel CI "(BMG) CPU Offload" builds 16800, 16804, 16806 and 16810.

## Claims

- Fixes `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py::test_p2p_cache_reset_with_absent_decoder`, which fails with:
  `ValueError: 'block_size'=16 in kv_connector_extra_config must be a multiple of the GPU KV cache block size (64 tokens).`
- Test-only change (+1 line). No production code is touched.

## Validation

Run in the exact CI image `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-test-repo:3199780ac6aff537b1cd7dbab9aec3ae030fc490-xpu` (torch 2.15.0+xpu, triton-xpu 3.9.0, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.16.3) on an Intel Arc Pro B60:

```bash
cd tests && pytest -v -s v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py
```

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_p2p_cache_reset_with_absent_decoder` | FAILED (same ValueError as CI) | PASSED (3/3 repeated runs) |
| Rest of the file | identical | identical |

The rest of the file gave the same results before and after. Locally, 4 `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` tests failed in both runs only because the host has no HF token for that gated repo; they pass in CI.

## Details

- Root cause: #63231 updated other offloading tests (`CPU_BLOCK_SIZES`, the mamba boundary test) and pinned `block_size=16` in `test_example_connector`, but missed this test. The test sets the offloaded chunk to `"block_size": 16`. GPU blocks now default to 64 tokens, and `build_offloading_config` requires the chunk to be a multiple of the GPU block size.
- This is not XPU-specific: TRITON_ATTN resolves to the 64-token default on CUDA too. It only shows up on Intel CI because that is where this file currently runs.
- Why pin the GPU block size instead of using `CPU_BLOCK_SIZES`: the prompt is 65 tokens. A 192-token chunk (the CUDA value) would never fill, so no P2P store would be parked and the test would time out. Pinning `block_size=16` keeps the test's original intent and matches what #63231 did for `test_example_connector`.
- Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs and issues for the test name, `absent_decoder`, and offloading/block-size keywords and found no existing fix.

title: [Model] Kimi K3.1: model files and NVIDIA specialized decode (Kimi K3.1 split 1/5)
author: ZJY0516
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Split 1/5 of Kimi K3.1 (#65685): the model files.** Adds Kimi K3.1 (`KimiK31ForConditionalGeneration`) and its NVIDIA specialized decode under `vllm/models/kimi_k3`, plus the registry and renderer entries. Its `VerifyAndUpdateConfig` entry (the DSA kv-cache dtype defaults and dense drafts) comes with split 3/5.

This PR does not touch `vllm/v1/attention`. The KV cache and attention changes that K3.1 needs to serve come in split 3/5 (#66037). Until that lands, K3.1 imports but does not serve; Kimi-K3 keeps working.

| Split | PR | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 1/5 | this PR | Model files |
| 2/5 | #66028 | Rust renderer |
| 3/5 | #66037 | KV cache and attention changes to serve K3.1 at TP8 |
| 4/5 | #65685 | ROCm, P/D, indexer top-k backends |
| 5/5 | #66027 | DCP optimizations (opt-in), merged last |

## Claims

- **Kimi K3.1**:
  - Kimi-K3 with DSA (DeepSeek sparse attention) on every MLA layer (`dsa_config` in `KimiLinearConfig`).
  - DSA indexer kernels (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops`).
  - Packed KDA/DSA hybrid caches (`get_packed_hybrid_block_size`).
- **Drafts**: dense and GQA drafts for K3.1. Kimi-K3's `KimiK3MTPModel` stays.
- **Specialized decode** (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode`):
  - CuTe DSL DSA (indexer, top-k exchange, sparse attention, DCP stage), KDA, MLA, MoE and GEMM kernels.
  - The drafter and recoverSSM.
  - Its DCP stage uses the packed top-k merge kernels, which live in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/dcp_topk_merge` here. Split 5/5 moves them to `vllm/v1/attention/ops` when the stock indexer uses them too.
  - It runs FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE through trtllm-gen only: the prims_ts, head padding and KV counter changes to that backend come with split 3/5 (#66037).
- **Python renderer**: K3.1 thinking efforts (low, medium, high, max).

## Validation

- Every NVIDIA/common module under `vllm.models.kimi_k3` imports on top of `main`'s shared code.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` hooks and the manual mypy hook pass on the changed files.
- Model tests and TP8 serving run on split 3/5, which adds the engine changes.

## Details

- `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration.process_weights_after_loading` was defined twice on the source branch, a merge leftover. The second definition hid the first, so the fused DSA projections were never packed. This PR merges the two, and `pack_projections` is now a no-op when it reruns after a reload.
- The specialized decode's DCP indexer merge was stale against main's #64580: `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` now needs `logits_dtype`, and the paged MQA logits default to FP32. It now asks for BF16, which its DeepSelect input requires.
- The specialized decode tests that need the FlashInfer sparse MLA changes move to split 3/5 with them.
- The model's DCP ShardQ hooks and the stock indexer's packed-merge argument come back in split 5/5.

title: [BugFix] Fix/spec decode insert resampled race
author: shustovTE
body:
## Overview

Run `_insert_resampled_kernel` with `num_warps=1` to avoid a race when reading and updating `num_sampled` in place. The race can cause an out-of-range lookup during speculative decoding and a fatal CUDA exception.

## Claims

- Removes the cross-warp read/write race in `_insert_resampled_kernel` by restricting its execution to one warp.
- Changes only this kernel's launch configuration.
- Makes no performance or model-quality claims.

## Validation

Two CUDA core dumps from separate crashes on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell show the same failure mechanism:

| Incident | Threads reading `num_sampled = 4` | Threads reading `num_sampled = 5` |
|---|---|---|
| First | 0, 32 | 64, 96 |
| Second | 0, 32, 64 | 96 |

The listed threads represent different warps within the same block. Disassembly maps these values to the load of `num_sampled`; the corresponding resampling indices are 4 and 5, with an exclusive end index of 5.

Both dumps report `Warp Out of range Address` at `_insert_resampled_kernel+384`, corresponding to:

    temp = tl.load(temp_ptr + req_state_idx).to(tl.float32)

The failing environment used vLLM 0.32.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, and Gemma 4 MTP with four speculative tokens. The same read/update pattern remains in the main-branch code patched here.

Local validation:
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, typos, and repository Python checks.
- Python syntax validation and `git diff --check` passed.

The dumps establish the original failure mechanism.

## Details

The kernel loads `num_sampled`, uses it to compute a resampling index, and increments the same counter in global memory. In the captured machine code, there is no inter-warp barrier between the load and the store.

A delayed warp can therefore read the incremented value after another warp has performed the update. In both incidents, this changes the resampling index from 4 to 5, outside the request's logits range. The subsequent mapping lookup supplies an invalid request-state index, causing the temperature load to fault.

Using one warp removes this inter-warp dependency without changing the sampling algorithm or introducing another kernel launch.

This failure occurs before the NaN/argmax handling addressed by #50183.

title: [Perf][GDN] Fuse prefill state gather/scatter with the shared Triton kernels
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Overview

Replace eager GDN prefill state gather/scatter with the existing shared Triton `gather_initial_states` / `scatter_states` kernels for Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 linear attention and Kimi KDA. Supersedes [#64498](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64498); see comparison below with [#50372](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50372). (Replaces #66058, which a branch rename auto-closed.)

## Claims

- Reduce prefill state gather/scatter from 4–5 eager kernels per layer per batch to one bandwidth-bound kernel per direction, covering every GDN prefill backend. Decode is unchanged.
- Improve the measured per-layer full prefill chain by 1.16–1.50x on a B300 GPU; isolated gather/scatter improves 4–30x.
- Preserve bitwise parity with the eager ops, including fresh-row zeroing and mixed-dtype scatter.

## Validation

Microbenchmarks on a B300 GPU: FlashInfer CUPTI timing, cold L2, CUDA-graph replayed chains, alternating arm order, medians of 5 rounds. Outputs are bitwise equal.

Per-layer full prefill chain (state gather/scatter + FlashInfer chunk kernel + write-back), fp32 pool, Qwen3.5-0.8B GDN dimensions. `B` is sequence count, `T` is tokens per sequence; mode is initial-state availability (`none`, `all`, or `mixed`).

| case | mode | main (µs) | PR (µs) | speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B=1 T=8192 | none | 139.5 | 119.6 | 1.17x |
| B=1 T=8192 | all | 139.2 | 119.7 | 1.16x |
| B=1 T=8192 | mixed | 138.8 | 120.2 | 1.16x |
| B=4 T=2048 | none | 93.2 | 75.4 | 1.24x |
| B=4 T=2048 | all | 93.2 | 77.0 | 1.21x |
| B=4 T=2048 | mixed | 93.3 | 76.5 | 1.22x |
| B=16 T=512 | none | 107.3 | 71.4 | 1.50x |
| B=16 T=512 | all | 107.3 | 74.5 | 1.43x |
| B=16 T=512 | mixed | 106.8 | 73.3 | 1.46x |

Isolated gather/scatter, same methodology: eager 83–714 µs versus fused 3.8–140 µs per layer across B=1..256 and fp32/bf16 pools (4–30x). At B=4 with an fp32 pool, eager gather takes 20.8 µs and bool-mask fill 32.0 µs; the fp32 cast is a no-op.

E2E forward benchmark: Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B, dummy weights, seeded, jitter 0; 2 alternating runs per arm, medians of each run's samples below (run-to-run spread <0.1% on every case):

| case (forward) | main (µs) | PR (µs) | delta |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| prefill 8192 | 11777.2 | 11461.8 | −2.7% |
| chunked prefill 2048@10240 | 4641.0 | 4355.8 | −6.1% |
| mix (64 decode + 4096 fresh prefill) | 8757.9 | 8436.8 | −3.7% |
| mixed-context prefill (2048 fresh + 2048 continuation) | 6936.3 | 6705.9 | −3.3% |
| decode 256×1@8192 | 6405.1 | 6409.2 | ~0 |

For reference, the closed pool-route PR measured −2.7% / −7.6% / −4.9% on the first three cases with the same tool; this PR is within ~1.5 points of it there, and additionally speeds up mixed fresh/cached batches, which the pool route could not.

E2E reproduction command:

```bash
vllm bench forward --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --kv-len-jitter 0 --seed 0 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --case prefill=8192 --case chunked=2048@10240c --case mix=64*1@8192,4096 \
  --case mixcached=2048,2048@8192c --case decode=256*1@8192
```

Tests run with the swaps in place:

- `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gather_scatter_states.py`: **40 passed** on a B300 GPU. Absorbs the gather test previously in `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py` (subsumed by the parametrized matrix). Covers 2 pool dtypes × B in {1, 3, 64, 256} × contiguous/strided indices, padded pool row strides, and mixed-dtype scatter; assertions are bitwise against eager operations.
- `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`: **78 passed**.
- CI: the H200-MIG mamba step collects `tests/kernels/mamba` by directory and already depends on the touched sources. The extended `tests/model_executor/test_qwen_triton_warmup.py` runs on the AMD Model Executor step (its deps cover `vllm/model_executor/warmup/` and `tests/model_executor`); the NVIDIA Model Executor step is disabled on main and returns with #65145. The JIT-monitor e2e step depends on `vllm/model_executor/warmup/` and fails on any post-warmup in-serving compile.

## Details

Eager prefill gathers `ssm[idx]`, zeros fresh rows through bool-mask `index_put`, casts, and scatters final states back into the cache pool. These 4–5 kernels per layer per batch run far below the bandwidth roofline. The replacement kernels already exist under `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/`, introduced with Kimi K3 KDA. They perform pure copies with cast-on-store only; bitwise parity with the eager operations follows from the copy semantics and is asserted in tests.

- **Qwen:** replace both gather sites (FlashInfer and non-FlashInfer `_forward_core`) and the shared scatter site. Extend the JIT-monitor-driven `qwen_triton_warmup` startup pass to compile both kernels for the variants serving reaches: fp32 (FlashInfer/FLA) and pool-dtype (CuteDSL/AITER) scatter sources, the unaligned index/mask pointers that mixed-batch slicing at `num_decodes` produces (Triton specializes on 16-byte pointer alignment), and strided index views from spec-decode block tables.
- **Kimi:** retain the existing fused gather and replace eager scatter. Register `scatter_states.register_warmup` at initialization, following glm5next. Add optional `src_dtype` to the scatter warmup spec for fp32 final states written into a bf16 pool.
- **XPU:** allow `scatter_states` on XPU, matching gather; the XPU Triton path reaches `_forward_core`.

Prior approaches: [#64498](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64498) (closed) routed through the pool, eliminating this gather/scatter only for homogeneous batches and coupling to FlashInfer's `state_indices` semantics. [#50372](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50372) (open, stalled) fuses the same gather/scatter with a 1-D div/mod indexing kernel limited to the FlashInfer path. This PR reuses kernels already in the tree and covers every GDN prefill backend.

Limitations: kernels retain their shipped configuration without further tuning. Measurements are on B300 (SM103); ROCm was not re-measured, though these kernels already run there through KDA.

title: [Recipe][ROCm] MiniMax-M3.1-Flash MI355X AgentX: nightly image and the opt-in optimizations
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## Overview

Update the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash MI355X AgentX preset (`mi355x_agentx`) to the lane that passed InferenceX CI on the latest ROCm nightly, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4866](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4866) (open; it replaces #4671, which the preset cites today). Recipe YAML only.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this preset. #65400 and #63547 also edit this file, but I found no hunk touching this preset.

## Claims

- Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-4fab5a07475822c6eaa971dceb2e2220d0446808@sha256:6f126f27…` (vLLM main of 2026-11-05) replaces the day-zero `minimax-m31-flash` image, so the MiniMax-M3.1 ROCm kernels merged since (#64448, #63637, #65087, #65432, #65478, #65481, #65530, #65386, #65267) are in the recipe's image.
- Switches that default off are now set at every point: `VLLM_ROCM_PARALLEL_INDEX_TOPK=1`, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=0` (alongside the existing `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO_DRAFTER=1`).
- Concurrency 16 and 32 run breakable CUDA graphs (`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, multiple-of-8 capture list); dual-batch overlap is removed from the 16-64 points.
- Runbook table and notes refreshed from the new run. InferenceX run 42224368840 at `ce4079c48`: p90 interactivity +8-22% at concurrency 1-8, +22% at 16, +16% at 32, +26% at 64 against the previous revision's run 41003224750; total tokens/s per GPU +2-20% at every point; GSM8K strict 0.961 / 0.963 / 0.960 at concurrency 8 / 32 / 64.

## Validation

Validated with the recipes repository's own checks (the `Recipes` PR check runs the first one):

```bash
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes   # valid against the renderer
```

and by rendering all seven points with the renderer's `renderCommand` (the function that builds the site's commands) for the old and new file. The delta per point is exactly what InferenceX #4866 changed and nothing else: new image at every point; `+VLLM_ROCM_PARALLEL_INDEX_TOPK`, `+VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND`, `+VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM` at every point; at concurrency 16 and 32 additionally `+VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH`, `+--compilation-config` and `-` the three DBO flags; at 64 `-` the DBO flags. Concurrency 1-8 render unchanged otherwise.

| Concurrency | p50 / p90 interactivity (tokens/s/user) | total tokens/s per GPU | previous revision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 604.4 / 590.1 | 7,617 | 551.0 / 515.7, 6,766 |
| 2 | 608.4 / 446.2 | 7,588 | 548.9 / 410.4, 6,918 |
| 4 | 610.2 / 428.3 | 9,698 | 546.3 / 395.6, 9,494 |
| 8 | 450.2 / 292.2 | 16,104 | 407.4 / 240.0, 15,411 |
| 16 | 313.5 / 204.6 | 28,686 | 228.6 / 168.3, 27,275 |
| 32 | 220.9 / 133.7 | 58,024 | 172.3 / 115.1, 54,158 |
| 64 | 95.1 / 59.7 | 90,495 | 71.4 / 47.3, 75,434 |

All numbers are single runs; no end-to-end run of this recipe's commands was done outside InferenceX.

## Details

- **Why the validator alone is not enough.** My first version passed validation but rendered concurrency 16 and 32 without `--compilation-config`: a preset's `json_args` can only edit a flag, and `--compilation-config` belongs to the `mono_decode` feature, so it was silently dropped where mono is not selected. It is now a plain argument.
- **Concurrency 16 first attempt was an outlier** (ITL p50 5.64 ms, slower than concurrency 32, GPU power 9% down, on one node); the rerun on another node gave the figures above (ITL p50 3.19 ms). The cause was not isolated, so treat 16 as one good run. This is stated in the runbook.
- **DBO and the graphs changed together.** DBO was on at 16-64 before; the gain at those points is the combined effect, not DBO alone. Also stated in the runbook.
- **INT4 quick all-reduce is not enabled.** The AITER in this image has no `QuickAllReduceInt4.compile`, which the nightly's FlyDSL INT4 path calls, so workers fail at startup with it (this is what failed the first InferenceX CI run).
- **`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO` is kept.** #66184 would replace it with `--monokernel`, but it is not merged and the pinned image still reads the env var.
- **Source pin.** `source.revision` is the InferenceX head `ce4079c48`; if #4866 changes before it merges, the revision, table and notes need a refresh. Concurrency 64 uses the host KV tier and was not rerun (the previous revision's first attempt hung at the first host-tier load).
